11100614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100614.value: Halogenated flame retardants (HFRs) are emerging contaminants of concern because most of them are persistent, toxic, and bioaccumulative. Despite their potential ecological and public health impacts, environmental data on these compounds, especially as alternatives for polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), are still very limited. PBDE levels in mussels and cetaceans in south China, including Hong Kong, have been found to be the highest among many Asian sites. High occurrence of these toxic and recalcitrant pollutants may be attributed to the heavy industrialization and urbanization in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) over the past decades. A recent study identified two new HFRs in Hong Kong cetaceans, and this finding lends support to the idea that a wide range of HFRs are in use in the region and are continuously being released into the coastal environment of south China. In addition, significantly higher levels of HFRs, including HFRs being used as PBDE alternatives, have been recorded in dolphins in comparison to porpoises inhabiting the northwestern and eastern waters, respectively. There is also an increasing usage of PBDE alternatives following the restriction/voluntary withdrawal of the production and use of PBDE commercial mixtures, namely pentabromodiphenyl ether (Penta-BDE) and octabromodiphenyl ether (Octa-BDE). Although some information on the distribution pattern and dietary preferences of local cetaceans is available, the sources of HFRs and how these emerging contaminants of concern accumulate in top predators are still unclear. Discerning the sources (e.g. point and non-point sources) and accumulation dynamics of HFRs in the cetaceans is both challenging and instructive. Compound-specific stable isotope analysis (CSIA) has been used to infer sources and fate of contaminants in the environment by measuring the ratio of stable isotopes in specific organic compounds. Recently, hyphenation with two-dimensional gas chromatography (2DGC) for CSIA has been proposed for use to characterize the source and fate of persistent organic pollutants due to its improved specificity and sensitivity. With the potential differences in isotopic fractionations in HFR sources from the respective habitats of the dolphins and porpoises, this project aims to test the hypothesis that the sources of HFRs in the PRD (northwestern waters of Hong Kong) are significantly different from those of the eastern waters of Hong Kong, and that these differences are reflected in the accumulation levels and profiles of target HFRs in dolphin and porpoise, respectively.

11100614.label: Realisation of objectives
11100614.value: During the first year of the project, a review was conducted on the occurrence and ecological risks of halogenated flame retardants (HFRs) in coastal zones. Special attention was given to emerging HFRs which have been produced as replacements for conventional HFRs, such as polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), as a result of the global ban on a number of PBDE congeners – Publication 1. During the same period, analytical methods were developed and validated for HFRs, and environmental samples (sediment, biota, sewage and cetacean blubber) were collected and analyzed for emerging chemicals of concern, including HFRs and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) – Publication 4. Levels of HFRs, including emerging HFRs such as hexabromocyclododecanes (HBCDs), 1,2-dibromo-4-(1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclohexane (TBECH) and Dechlorane Plus (DP), were measured in the blubber samples of local cetaceans – Publication 1. During the second and third year of the project, risks of HFRs to the local marine ecosystem were assessed. Data on the toxicological effects of HFRs on common organisms of marine food webs were collated from various sources, based on which Critical Effects Levels of concern were estimated. Over and above this, the toxicological effects of organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) were also investigated using zebrafish as a model vertebrate – Publication 2. In a preliminary risk evaluation of HBCDs, our results revealed that all Hazard Quotient (HQ) values were generally below unity for cetaceans. However, HQ under worst case scenario for white-sided dolphin from the eastern coast of the US, harbor porpoise from the UK and the North Sea Basin, striped dolphins from Japan, as well as the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin (Sousa chinensis) from the South China Sea exceeded unity, suggesting that blubber concentrations of HBCDs may pose risks to these marine mammals. Further to the widely used HBCDs, another important group of flame retardants collectively referred to as chlorinated paraffins (CPs), which are subdivided into short chain CPs (SCCPs, C10–13), and medium chain CPs (MCCPs, C14–17) according to their carbon chain length, were investigated in the blubber samples of finless porpoises (Neophocaena phocaenoides) and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins from South China – Publication 3. There is a scarcity of information on CPs, especially MCCPs, in marine mammals in the world. Our data showed an elevated temporal trend of SCCPs and MCCPs in all blubber samples of both cetacean species in Hong Kong over the past decade. Specifically, concentrations of SCCPs ranged from 280 to 3900 ng/g dry weight (dw) in porpoises and from 430 to 9100 ng/g dw in dolphins, while concentrations of MCCPs ranged from 320 to 8600 ng/g dw in porpoises and from 530 to 23 000 ng/g dw in dolphins. Significantly higher concentrations were present in dolphins than porpoises due to their exposure levels in their living habitats. These results confirm the difference in levels of persistent toxic substances, HFRs in this case, in the western and eastern marine environments of Hong Kong. Our project also revealed an elevated accumulation of SCCPs and MCCPs in marine mammals from Hong Kong waters. One of the two objectives of the current study was to examine the bioaccumulation and biomagnification of flame retardants in these apex predators. To achieve this goal, we sampled the dietary items of local marine mammals and tracked the sources of SCCPs and MCCPs through a marine food web study in this region. Sixteen fish species, seven crustacean species, and four mollusk species were collected, and the main prey species were identified for the two species of marine mammals. The specimens were analyzed for CPs using the methods developed and validated in this project. Based on the concentrations of total SCCPs and total MCCPs in these collected species, our data suggest a moderate pollution level in Hong Kong waters compared to the global range. Furthermore, lipid content was found to mediate congener-specific bioaccumulation in these marine species. Significantly positive correlations were observed between trophic levels and concentrations of total SCCPs or total MCCPs. Trophic magnification factors for total SCCPs and total MCCPs were 4.29 and 4.79, indicating that both SCCPs and MCCPs have trophic magnification potentials. Indeed, elevated biomagnification of SCCPs and MCCPs from prey species to marine mammals was observed. This study reports, for the first time, the dietary source tracking of SCCPs and MCCPs in marine mammals – Publication 6. The elevated biomagnification between prey and marine mammals raises environmental concerns about CPs in particular, and HFRs in general. To further understand the status and trends of chlorinated paraffins (CPs) in Hong Kong and its nearby region, and to assess the impacts on the coastal environment due to CP contamination, surface and core sediments were sampled from the urbanized coastal zones in China [Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta (PRD)] and Japan (Tokyo Bay) and analyzed for SCCPs and MCCPs. Much higher concentrations of CPs were found in the industrialized PRD compared to samples from adjacent Hong Kong waters. Significant correlation between CP concentration and population density in the coastal districts of Hong Kong was observed, highlighting the relationship between urban development and CP contamination. By contrast, a relatively lower levels of CPs were detected in Tokyo Bay. As well, the occurrence of more long-chain groups within SCCPs in the PRD than in Hong Kong waters and Tokyo Bay implied a stronger impact of industrialization in the PRD compared to Hong Kong and Tokyo Bay. A comparison of temporal trends between Hong Kong and Tokyo Bay also shows the striking difference in historical deposition of CPs under different regulatory regimes in Hong Kong/China and Japan. For the first time, the declining CP concentrations in Tokyo Bay, Japan, attests to the effectiveness of emissions controls – Publication 5. This sheds light on possible management measures for HFRs that can be taken in Hong Kong and its nearby region. Nearly all the tasks set out in the proposal have been completed. The use of compound-specific stable isotope analysis to infer sources and fate of HFRs in the environment turned out to be very challenging and this task has not been fully accomplished. This aspect of the work is still on-going. Publications listed in Part C Publication 1: Lam, J.C.W. and Lam, P.K.S. 2015. Pp. 389-409. (Ed. E. Zeng). 11100614.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100614.value: Levels of HFRs, including emerging HFRs such as hexabromocyclododecanes (HBCDs), were measured in the blubber samples of local finless porpoises and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins. HBCDs could pose risks to the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin from the South China Sea. Other flame retardants, short and medium-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs and MCCPs), were investigated in the blubber samples of porpoises and dolphins from South China. There is little information on chlorinated paraffins, especially MCCPs, in top predators of marine food chains (e.g. marine mammals) in the world. Our data showed an increasing temporal trend of SCCPs and MCCPs in blubber samples of Hong Kong cetaceans over the past decade. Dietary items of local marine mammals (e.g. fish, crustacean, and mollusk) were collected and analyzed for SCCPs and MCCPs. Sources of SCCPs and MCCPs were tracked through a marine food web study. Lipid content was found to mediate congener-specific bioaccumulation in these marine species. Based on the concentrations of total SCCPs and total MCCPs in these collected species, our data suggest a moderate pollution level in Hong Kong waters compared to the global range. Positive correlations were observed between trophic levels and concentrations of total SCCPs or total MCCPs. Trophic magnification factors for total SCCPs and total MCCPs were 4.29 and 4.79, indicating that both SCCPs and MCCPs have trophic magnification potentials. Indeed, elevated biomagnification of SCCPs and MCCPs from prey species to marine mammals was observed. This study reports, for the first time, the dietary source tracking of SCCPs and MCCPs in marine mammals. Sediment samples from urbanized coastal zones in China [Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta (PRD)] and Japan (Tokyo Bay) were analyzed for SCCPs and MCCPs. Much higher concentrations of chlorinated paraffins were found in the industrialized PRD compared to samples from adjacent Hong Kong waters. There was a significant correlation between chlorinated paraffin concentration and population density in the coastal districts of Hong Kong, highlighting the relationship between urban development and chlorinated paraffin contamination. A comparison of temporal trends between Hong Kong and Tokyo Bay also shows the striking difference in historical deposition of CPs under different regulatory regimes in Hong Kong/China and Japan. For the first time, the declining CP concentrations in Tokyo Bay, Japan, attests to the effectiveness of emissions controls. This sheds light on possible management measures for HFRs that can be taken in Hong Kong and its nearby region.

11100614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100614.value: As some HFRs are chiral and can exist in different isomeric forms, it would be instructive to assess the environmental and ecological risks posed by different HFR isomers. To this end, a more refined risk assessment on different isomers of HBCD as well as other emerging HFRs will be conducted. Chemical analyses will be performed on the biota samples collected from Hong Kong and the nearby South China area (as part of the current investigation) to determine the concentration of different isomers of HFRs commonly found in waters of Hong Kong and its neighbouring regions. In addition, laboratory-based investigations will be undertaken to examine the toxicological effects of different isomers of HFRs on marine organisms that are important in maintaining the structure and function of the ecosystems that are exposed to these contaminants.

11100614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100614.value: Halogenated flame retardants (HFRs) are emerging contaminants of concern because most of them are persistent, toxic, and bioaccumulative. Due to their potential ecological and public health impacts, many conventional HFRs have been banned and, consequently, new HFRs are being produced as replacements. Information on new HFRs is limited. Our results revealed that both conventional and new HFRs may pose risks to the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins in Hong Kong waters. Apart from conventional HFRs, another group of flame retardants [short and medium-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs and MCCPs)] showed an increasing temporal trend in blubber samples of finless porpoises and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins in Hong Kong over the past decade. The bioaccumulation and biomagnification of SCCPs and MCCPs in the local marine food webs were investigated. Fish, crustacean, and mollusk samples were collected, and the main prey species for the porpoises and dolphins were identified. The specimens were analyzed for SCCPs and MCCPs. Significantly positive correlations were observed between trophic levels and concentrations of SCCPs or MCCPs. Trophic magnification factors for SCCPs and MCCPs were 4.29 and 4.79, indicating that these compounds have high trophic magnification potentials. Overall, results of the present study raise environmental concerns about HFRs and chlorinated paraffins.

11100914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100914.value: The clinical connection between pain and the increases in levels of anxiety, depression as well as cognitive disorders has long been recognized, but the biological basis of the affective and cognitive changes in visceral pain remains badly understood. Using a viscerally hypersensitive (VH) rat mole, we have demonstrated sensitization of anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) neurons. Further, ACC activation is critical for memory processing involved in long-term visceral negative affective state. Recently, we characterized long-lasting potentiation of local field potential in the medial thalamus (MT)−ACC synapses in VH rats. Higher frequency stimulation in the MT reliably induced canonical long-term potentiation (LTP) in normal rat, however, induction of LTP were impaired in VH states implying chronic visceral pain disrupts emotional and cognitive functions (e.g.decision making) that are associated with ACC. In the current proposal behavioral studies will be performed to clarify the emotional disorders and cognitive deficits in the visceral pain. We hypothesize that the mechanisms of ACC synaptic metaplasticity are involved in modifying aversive responses to pain, and affect the processing learning and memory associated with chronic pain. Proportionately more brain neuronal theta activity (3–8Hz) predicts faster and better learning, and learning itself induces the theta activity during training. We will perform multiple-channel recordings to test our hypotheses that a disruption in the theta activity in MT-ACC circuitry may prevent interregional communication, leading to deficits in learning (gambling task) in later stage of visceral pain. There is now a growing body of evidence indicating that glial cells, particularly astrocytes, contribute actively to synaptic transmission, neuronal excitability and depressive and memory behavior. The nature of astrocytic modification dynamically varies with time after the noxious challenge. We will demonstrate that reactive astrogliosis modify the ACC glutamatergic excitation and contribute to synaptic plasticity in visceral pain. On the other hand, astrocytic and neuronal apoptosis related to degeneration occurs in the chronic visceral pain state. Byproducts of glycogen metabolism are critical for memory formation, astrocytes, but not neurons, store glycogen, in the last phase of this proposal we will characterize that an astrocytes-neuron metabolic coupling (e.g. lactate transport) plays a key role in memory formation, lactate transport is essential for rescue the memory loss, long-term synaptic plasticity in the chronic visceral pain. These observations would suggest that the visceral pain experience may be better explained as a biopsychosocial model of pain. Astrocytes play a vital role in the pain-emotional and cognition interactions.

11100914.label: Realisation of objectives
11100914.value: Visceral hypersensitivity induced behavioral changes in decision-making as revealed by the rat gambling task Visceral hypersensitivity in rats was induced by colonic anaphylaxis. The RGT has been developed to test the decision-making capacities in rats via a conflict between immediate and long-term gratification (food reward). Based on the percentage of advantageous choices made during the testing session, good, undecided, and poor decision-makers were identified in both control and VH rats. At the end of the testing, good decision-makers earned significantly more food pellets. The proportion of good decision-makers was reduced, 46% in VH compared to 71% in controls. The proportion of poor performers in the VH group was similar to that observed in controls. There was a greater proportion of undecided decision-makers in the VH group than in the control group. The difference in the proportions of the subgroups between the control and VH groups was significant suggesting that visceral hypersensitivity affects decision-making ability in rats. Basolateral amygdala (BLA) neuronal activity in response to colorectal distension in control and viscerally hypersensitive rats. The basal firing rate recorded of the CRD-excitatory neurons in VH rats was significantly higher than that in control rats. The BLA neuronal responses to 50 mm Hg CRD increased from baseline to 2.10 ± 0.07 and 2.96 ± 0.06 spikes/s in control and VH rats. These observations demonstrate that VH rats have an increased BLA neuronal excitability Synaptic transmission in BLA-ACC pathway In all rats, various stimuli (200 μA to 1000 μA) in the BLA elicited gradually increased ACC evoked LFP. I-O curve changed significantly between control and VH rats. In control rats (n = 6), after three trains of TBS delivered to the BLA, a 150.5±7.3% enhancement in LFP amplitude in response to BLA stimuli was observed compared to the baseline level (pre-TBS). In contrast, TBS failed to induce LTP in VH rats. These results indicated that the TBS induced. LTP in the BLA-ACC synapses was impaired by chronic visceral hypersensitivity. Augmented theta activities in the BLA and ACC of VH rats Significant alterations were detected both in BLA and ACC t-test analysis revealed that the BLA theta band power was increased from 4.38 × 10−4 ± 0.35 × 10−4 mV2 in control rats to 5.60 × 10−4 ± 0.33 × 10−4 mV2 in VH rats (p b 0.05, Fig. 4B). The theta band power of ACC was increased from 4.50 × 10−4 ± 0.22 × 10−4 mV2 in the control rats to 5.56 × 10−4 ± 0.23 × 10−4 mV2 in the VH rats. Visceral hypersensitivity reduced SFC between BLA and ACC We recorded single unit neuronal activity in the ACC as well as LFPs in the BLA simultaneously at quiet waking state for 120 s. Our results suggested that the accurate phase relation between spike firing in the ACC and LFP oscillation in BLA was impaired in VH rats. Visceral hypersensitivity disrupted spikes phase-locking to theta oscillation between BLA and ACC. Rayleigh test as a test of significance of phase-locking shown phase-locked neuron in the control rat exhibited maximal phase-locking at 8.0 Hz while the other un-phase-locked neuron in the VH rat showed no significant phase locking in theta-band frequencies. Reactive astrogliosis in the ACC in the chronic visceral pain. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) was the first molecular marker to be robustly associated with astrocytes. Upregulation of GFAP is a sensitive and reliable marker of astrocytes that are responding to CNS insults. The astrocytes also can be detected by ultrastructural evaluation or by other markers such as S100β, glutamine synthetase or Aldh1L1. We confirm our previous observations and clarify the up-regulation of GFAP and S100β immunoreactivity in the ACC suggesting development of reactive astrogliosis in the chronic VH rat model. Exogenous l-lactate supply into the ACC facilitates decision-making performance in rats Post hoc analysis revealed that the proportions of the three subgroups of decision makers were significant different in both lactate-treated control, and VH rats compared with those with artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) infusions. The final mean pellets rewarded during the RGT test were increased in lactate-treated control and VH rats. Lactate infusion rescues ACC LTP and repairs impaired spike phase locking in VH rats We found that, in control rats, a robust LTP was induced by TBS to the BLA. The local field potential (LFP) amplitude was increased up to 136.3% ± 5.7% 30 min after TBS compared with the baseline level. In VH rats, after ACSF infusion. In contrast, in another group of VH rats, after infusion of L-lactate (10 nmol) into the ACC, a 129.0% ± 6.1% potentiation was observed in response to the BLA stimulus. These observations suggest that the induction of LTP-like plasticity in BLA-ACC synapses was restored by L-lactate infusion into the ACC. Further, we found that, in VH rats, lactate infusion tremendously increased SFC values in the low-frequency range. Moreover, the percentage of phase-locked neurons increased from 27.35% ± 8.02% to 59.27% ± 9.89% following lactate infusion, and prior 4-CIN infusion reduced that to 19.65% ± 7.16%. Optogenetic activation of astrocytes induces L-lactate release in VH rats and rescues VH related decision-making deficit via the l-lactate pathway. Light stimulation induced an increase in L-lactate concentration in ChR2-expressing rats but not in enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP)-expressing rats. We found that light stimulation induced a marked increase in lactate level in the ACC of conscious VH rats. These results indicate that daily optogenetic activation of ACC astrocytes induced a repeatable increase of local L-lactate concentration in chronic VH rats. Next, we conducted RGT experiments in VH rats with ChR2-eYFP or eYFP expression in bilateral ACC regions. Three types of decision makers were identified in eYFP, ChR2, and ChR2+4-CIN (n = 19) rats. Post hoc analysis revealed a significant difference between the eYFP and ChR2 rats. Blocking the uptake of lactate from the extracellular space to neurons by prior 4-CIN administration abolished the action of light stimulation. The final reward obtained was also different in the three treated groups. These results suggest that manipulation of intrinsic astrocytes in the ACC regions rescues the decision-making deficit of VH rats through lactate signaling. Poor decision makers are characterized by disrupted ACC phase locking. Light stimulation facilitates ACC spike field coherence and phase locking in a quiet waking state and during the RGT. We found that, during the RGT, the ACC spike phase locking to BLA theta was also lower in undecided and poor decision makers compared with good subjects. These results suggest that the strength of ACC phase-locking in the theta range can closely track good decision performance; however, undecided and poor decision makers failed to increase phase locking during the RGT. Electrophysiological data showed that, during the RGT, light stimulation increased the percentage of within-ACC phase locked neurons to 52.56%±3.20%. In parallel, the percentage of ACC to BLA theta phase locked neurons was increased to 47.67%±4.90% with light stimulation. Overall, ACC astrogliosis in VH rats dampened ACC L-lactate release under high activity demand conditions such as decision making, which then suppressed ACC neuronal spike-theta synchrony. Moreover, optogenetic stimulation of astrocytes could release lactate, which is able to promote neuronal spike-field synchrony under physiological conditions and repair neuronal net work functions and rescue decision-making performance under chronic visceral pain.

11100914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100914.value: Astrocytes are characteristic star-shaped cells that permeate throughout the central nervous system. Although astrocytes have long been considered to have mainly a supportive function for neurons, a growing body of evidence suggests that they fulfill other active roles, including signal transmission and regulation of neural and synaptic plasticity. In recent study we revealed that astrocytes can release an important energy substrate called L-lactate upon various stimuli and that L-lactate may affect neuronal function to facilitate decision making. Human brain imaging studies have revealed the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) as a key brain region for mediating visceral-pain-cognitive interactions. Recently, we characterized impairments of long term potentiation and spike-field coherence in the basolateral amygdala (BLA)-ACC network in association with a decision-making deficit in rats with visceral hypersensitivity (VH chronic abdominal pain). Now, by combining integrative neurobiological approaches, we show that ACC-reactive astrogliosis and activity-dependent impairment of lactate release occur in VH rats. Exogenous lactate supply rescues chronic-visceral pain-caused impairments of ACC phase locking and decision making, which can be mimicked by optogenetic activation of ACC astrocytes. Largescale electrophysiological recordings in free-moving animals during a decision-making task indicate that optogenetic astrocytic activation improves decision-making performance and engages ACC phase. The truly novel message of these studies is the roles of lactate in neuronal plasticity and neuronal network synchrony. The current report reveals that lactate should no longer be considered sim¬ply as an energy substrate for neurons, but rather as an important signalling molecule that can regulate cellular processes independent of its metabolic effects. Collectively, these observations support the idea of an ‘‘astrocyte–neuron– L-lactate shuttle’’ and suggest that targeting astrocytes in abnormal neural circuits may help with cognitive dysfunctions under chronic pain. The clinical connection between pain and increases in levels of anxiety, depression, and cognitive disorders has long been recognized. It is possible that there are pathological decision-making deficits in other disease conditions, such as brain injury, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer's disease. The mechanism responsible for decision-making deficits in specific pathological conditions is an important but complicated area of research. In the future, we will explore whether L-lactate generated by moderate physical activity can enter the cerebrum through the blood-brain barrier to improve cognitive functions.

11100914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100914.value: We conducted lab tests on rat models to investigate the effect of chronic pain on cognitive disorders and how it can be mitigated. The research reveals that an important energy substrate called L-lactate can facilitate decision making. The findings provide new insight into cognitive treatment. The clinical connection between pain and increases in levels of anxiety, depression, and cognitive disorders, such as impaired decision making, has long been recognized. The published data from their research shows that impaired L-lactate release may be one of the factors in cognitive deficit in chronic visceral pain. It is possible that there are pathological decision-making deficits in other disease conditions, such as brain injury, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer's disease. The mechanism responsible for decision-making deficits in specific pathological conditions is an important but complicated area of research. In the future, my team will conduct experiments using the ‘rat gambling task’ to investigate whether the activation of astrocytes can rescue the decision-making deficits in rats with Alzheimer's disease and to study the role of L-lactate in this process.

11100914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100914.value: A research team led by City University of Hong Kong (CityU) has recently discovered a brain signalling molecule that can improve decision-making performance. “The truly novel discovery of our studies is the roles of L-lactate in neuronal plasticity and neuronal network synchrony. A daily L-lactate infusion into the anterior cingulate cortex in the brain increases the percentage of good decision making in both rats with chronic visceral pain and normal rats,” said Professor Li. In one of the tests, infusion of lactate into the brain increased the percentage of good-decision makers by 48% in normal subjects. “The findings reveal that L-lactate should no longer be considered sim¬ply an energy substrate for neurons, but rather as an important signalling molecule that can regulate cellular processes, and suggest that targeting astrocytes in abnormal neural circuits may help with cognitive dysfunction under chronic pain”. The article, titled “Astrocytic l-Lactate Signaling Facilitates Amygdala-Anterior Cingulate Cortex Synchrony and Decision Making in Rats”, was published recently in Cell Report, a prestigious international life sciences journal covering entire areas of molecular and cell biology.

11200314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200314.value: 在过去的几十年里，日本漫画在全世界范围内逐渐盛行。因此越来越多的人开始阅读漫画，同时也有更多的业余艺术家投入到漫画的创作中去。漫画的成功很大程度上归功于漫画家使用独特的叙事技术来增强读者的带入感。在这些技术当中，前景人物和对话框的构图在为读者提供流畅的阅读体验中起到了十分重要的作用。有效的构图可以通过连续和一致地引导读者以一定的顺序来阅读人物和对话框，从而增强对故事的描述并带给读者强烈的带入感。然而创作高质量的漫画构图通常需要专业的技术和独特的艺术天赋， 这使得业余艺术家很难完成有效的漫画构图。与使用固定规则来构图（例如把对话框统一放在人物顶部）的西方漫画不同，日本漫画的构图更加灵活并通常不使用固定的规则。然而，如果人物和对话框的构图不能有效地反应它们的阅读顺序，读者将很难理解漫画中的故事。日本漫画家主要依靠他们的直觉和理解来进行有效的布局和构图。换句话说，他们遵循一些隐式的规则进行创作并在作品中引入自己特定的风格。然而，当前并不存在能够描述日本漫画家如何使用人物，对话框以及背景的构图来引导读者注意力的计算模型。因此，这个项目的目的是开发数据驱动的漫画计算模型。该模型可以描述读者如何与漫画进行交互并且可以用于自动的漫画构图和移动设备上漫画阅读。具体来说，我们的目标是开发一个能够同时表示漫画元素（即人物，对话框和背景）的构图和它对读者注意力（通过人眼移动模式来表示）影响的模型。为此我们使用一种数据驱动的方法。首先，我们使用人眼跟踪技术来收集一些读者阅读漫画时的阅读行为数据。然后，使用该数据集来训练一个表示漫画元素和读者注意力关系的概率图模型。当使用移动设备来阅读漫画时，移动设备的屏幕可以看做是读者注意力的视口（例如平移等同于移动注意力的焦点）。我们扩展我们的构图-注意力模型来集成读者在移动设备上阅读漫画时的交互过程。为此我们使用一组从使用移动设备进行漫画阅读的读者处收集的数据（通过记录一些基于触摸的交互，平移，放大和缩小）来训练我们的扩展模型。最后，我们将我们的计算模型应用到两个与漫画相关的任务中：1）自动摆放漫画元素以便让业余艺术家创作出专业的漫画；2）一个可以使读者通过交互动画来获得流畅阅读体验的移动漫画浏览器。例外，我们的计算模型也可以应用到其他领域，例如杂志设计，个性化广告和移动设备上网站设计的评估。

11200314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200314.value: 1) graphical model for composing manga elements that can direct attention of the reader. The idea was extended to webpages by explicitly modeling eye gaze patterns on a webpages, and then directly optimizing the placement of the web page elements to manipulate the user's eye gaze. 2) the reading behavior of users is simulated in manga by extracting semantics from the manga, and then simulating camera movements such as panning, zooming, and special effects, which simulate user interactions when progressing through the story. Furthermore, on webpages, an interaction technique is developed to effectively suggest and place web buttons on existing web pages. 3) a prototype interface was designed for the models in (1). 4) a prototype mobile app / desktop app was designed for the models in (2). 5) in addition to the core research ideas, other research works that supported this project were also conducted, such as figure/background segmentation, manga panel extraction, visual tracking, and statistical regression models.

11200314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200314.value: The projects conducts research on how reader's attention is affected by the layout of a manga/webpage, and proposes methods for effectively guiding reader attention on manga/webpages. These methods could be used to make webpages more effective and efficient at conveying information. The project has also considered how to effectively place buttons (interactive elements) on a webpage, and has developed an effective interface for this.

11200514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200514.value: Due to demands from consumer markets in personal communications, security and automotive safety at millimeter waves on the one hand and new promising applications of Terahertz in explosive detection, tomographic imaging of transdermal drug delivery, and cultural heritage conservation, etc., on the other, we embark on investigating a key system component in millimeter-wave and terahertz antennas. At these frequencies, the low power available necessitates the use of high-gain antennas such as Fresnel zone plate (FZP) lens antennas. Albeit their large electrical size, FZP lens antennas have been investigated for many years due to their planar geometry and ease of fabrication at microwave frequencies. While the physical size of the FZP lens antennas is small at millimeter waves and terahertz, simple frequency scaling alone would not lead to cost-effective designs as standardized fabrication processes have tolerance limitations and substrate materials are only commercially available for specific electrical properties and thicknesses. Working with these two constraints, we have successfully completed a GRF project entitled “An Investigation of High-Order Mode Microstrip Antennas for 60 GHz Short-Range Wireless Communications,” in which low-cost 60 GHz magneto-electric dipole antennas were fabricated with 0.787mm Duroid 5880 substrate using plated through hole (PTH) and printed circuit board (PCB) techniques. In this project, we propose to investigate the applicability of these low-cost fabrication techniques for FZP lens antennas with equal E- and H-plane radiation patterns and enhanced gain. The former is realized by an innovative PCB feed design based on the complementary source approach while the latter is achieved by removing part of the substrate materials in the in-phase regions and/or applying periodic slot patterning on the out-of-phase printed ring regions. Our preliminary results, using 0.254mm Duroid 5880 substrates and mechanically drilled PTH vias with a diameter of 0.1mm, achieved 26dBi for a 10-ring FZP lens at 0.3 THz. Simulation, fabrication and testing of the preliminary designs were all conducted in house in the State Key Laboratory of Millimeter Waves (Hong Kong). We will investigate the frequency limit of the proposed low-cost approach before we resort to other conventional lithographical techniques for our quest of high-gain FZP lens antennas up to 1 THz which is limited by our measurement facilities. We strongly believe that the proposed research will contribute to the development of critical components for THz technology using low-cost materials and PCB and PTH technologies that Hong Kong electronic industry has mastered and perfected. 考虑到毫米波段的个人通讯与安全、汽车安全，以及新的应用于太赫兹波段的爆炸探测、透皮给药的层析成像、文化遗产保护等消费市场的需求，我们着手于开发一种新的关于毫米波太赫兹天线的关键系统部件。在这些频率，较低的可用功率使得高增益天线（例如菲涅尔天线）的使用成为必然。 虽然菲涅尔天线（FZP）具有较大的电尺寸，但是由于其平面结构以及在毫米波段易加工的特性，这种天线已经被研究了很多年。考虑到毫米波太赫兹FZP的物理尺寸较小，受普通加工工艺误差以及商用基片材料电特性和厚度的限制，简单的频率尺寸缩放不会带来有效的设计。致力于以上两个限制条件，我们成功地完成了一个名为“用于60GHz短距离无线通讯的高阶模贴片天线研究”的政府研究基金。在这个项目中，我们使用电镀通孔（PTH）和印刷电路板技术（PCB），成功地把60GHz的磁电偶极子加工在了0.787mm的Duroid 5880介质基板上。同时，我们提出了关于使用这种低成本加工技术来实现相等E面和H面辐射方向图以及增益增强的可行性研究。它们分别可以通过使用互补源技术的创新性PCB激励方法，以及去掉同相位区的介质材料和/或在反向位的印刷环区添加周期开槽结构来实现。 我们使用0.254mm Duroid5880介质基板和机械加工的0.1mm直径PTH的初步成果实现了在0.3THz频率的十环FZP达到26dBi的增益。所有关于初步设计的仿真、加工和测试工作都由毫米波国家重点实验室（香港城市大學夥伴實验室）来主导完成。受测试设备限制，在采用其它传统印刷平板技术来实现1THz高增益FZP前，我们将继续探索所提出的低成本方案的频率限制。我们非常肯定地相信所提出的研究方案将大大推动使用低成本材料、PCB和PTH技术的太赫兹关键部件的发展。这些技术也正是香港电子工业界所擅长的。

11200814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200814.value: A wide range of health problems can be treated by stimulation of the nervous system, including hearing loss, chronic pain, and Parkinson’s disease. Recently, an implantable device (Argus II Retinal Prosthesis System) has been clinically approved, in US and in Europe, to treat blindness due to retinal degeneration. The major blinding disease such as retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is caused by the degeneration of photoreceptors, affecting 1 in 1000 for a total of 1.3 million individuals in China (Xu et al 2006). Vision could be partially restored by electrically stimulating the remaining intact cells with neural electrodes, in a way that resemble the signals that a healthy retina would transmit to the brain. The development of neural prosthetic devices for recording and stimulation is inevitably advanced by micro or nano scale electronics technology. Neural electrodes are a rapidly growing field in neural interfacing and have significantly improved the quality of life for people suffered from neurological disorders and injuries. Safe stimulation is a critical consideration in successful neural electrodes design. Platinum, iridium oxide, and alloys of these metals are commonly used materials for neural stimulation. Recently, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) become excellent candidates for interfacing with neural systems due to their extraordinary strength, electrical conductivity and large surface area. The early studies focused on fabricating CNT-based electrodes on rigid silicon substrate for neuronal recording and stimulation. Recent reports indicate the possibility to fabricate CNT-based electrodes on a flexible polymer substrate for neuronal recording. Few studies have focused on neural stimulation using CNT-based electrodes on a polymer substrate. We propose a novel study to develop a CNT-based microelectrode array on a flexible substrate for stimulation of retinal tissue followed by electrophysiological measurements in a rodent model. In the first part of the study, we will fabricate a CNT-based microelectrode array on a polymer substrate. Characterization of the electrodes will be conducted to evaluate the electrical properties by electrochemical methods. In the second part of the study, biocompatibility and safe limits for stimulation will be studied by implanting the CNT-based microelectrode array in a rodent model’s visual system. This study will provide information on using CNTs as electrode materials for stimulation of retinal tissue and other biological tissues. Electrode efficiency and biocompatible stimulation will lead to an overall more efficient and safe neural prosthetic device. 用激励神经系统的方法可以治疗很多种疾病，包括耳聋、慢性疼痛、以及帕金森病。最近，一种可植入设备（Argus II视网膜义体系统）在美国和欧洲获准用于临床治疗因视网膜退化引起的失明。视网膜色素变性作为一种主要的因感光细胞退化致盲的疾病，在中国范围内影响着130万人，即每一千人中就有一人患此疾病(Xu et al 2006)。用神经电极激励余下没有改性的细胞的方式，可以模拟正常视网膜传递给大脑的信号来部分恢复视觉。微纳尺度电极制造技术极大促进了用于记录和激励的神经义体设备的发展。神经电极在神经接口领域发展迅速，并且极大提高了受神经逻辑错位与伤害影响的患者的生活质量。在考察神经电极是否成功时，安全的激励是很重要的一项。通常用来制作神经电极的材料有铂、氧化铱以及这些金属的合金。最近，碳纳米管以其极高的强度、导电性、和很大的表面积成为制作神经系统接口极好的备选材料。早期研究的重点是在刚性硅衬底上制作用来记录和激励的碳纳米管电极。最近有报告显示可以在柔性聚合物衬底上制作用来记录和激励的碳纳米管电极。很少有研究关注在聚合物衬底上制作用来激励神经的基于碳纳米管的电极。我们对于在柔性衬底上制作一种用来激励视网膜组织的基于碳纳米管的新式微电极阵列开展了研究，并在啮齿动物模型上进行了电学测量。在研究的第一部分，我们将会在聚合物衬底上制作一个基于碳纳米管的电极阵列，通过电化学方式测量并评价电极的电学特性。研究的第二部分将通过把基于碳纳米管的微电极阵列植入啮齿动物模型的视觉系统，研究其生物相容性以及激励的安全限值。这项研究将会为用碳纳米管作为激励视网膜组织以及其他生物组织的电极材料提供信息。在电极效率及其激励的生物相容性的引导下，将会产生更加高效、安全的神经义体设备。

11200814.label: Realisation of objectives
11200814.value: Summary – The first phase of the project was to fabricate carbon nanotubes (CNTs) microelectrodes on a silicon substrate. The electrochemical properties of the CNT microelectrodes were successfully measured. The electrochemical impedance of the CNT microelectrodes was reduced significantly using a new synthesis protocol. During the second phase of the project, we have successfully fabricated CNT microelectrode on a flexible substrate. The CNT electrodes synthesized facing down shows impedance improvement of about 90 times comparing with the normal facing up synthesized samples. Methodology Carbon nanotube fabrication on flexible substrate Silicon dioxide was grown on initial cleaned silicon substrate. This was the isolation layer when etching the rigid silicon by xenon difluoride. Then, 100 nm titanium was sputtered on SiO2, and patterned to form the interconnection. Another layer of silicon dioxide was deposited to avoid the cross talk during stimulation and it was etched in a special designed procedure. Firstly, the region of Ti pads were exposed. Photoresist was patterned to expose the electrode region. Subsequently, the exposed SiO2 was etched to expose the conducting layer of titanium beneath with the patterned photoresist. With the same patterned photoresist, 2 nm Fe catalyst was evaporated to act as catalyst for carbon nanotube synthesis and lift off to leave catalyst only in the electrode region. The holder of plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition equipment used to synthesis carbon nanotube was 2 inch, so the samples were diced and then deposited in the chamber, the synthesis temperature was 800C, pressure was 11.3 Torr, gas flow rate of CH4 : H2 : N2 was 35 sccm : 30 sccm : 10 sccm, the reaction time was 4 min. The electrodes were synthesized in face-up method and face-down method. Synthesized carbon nanotube electrodes were observed through scanning electron microscope. The steps to embed carbon nanotube electrodes into flexible substrate include front side parylene patterning and backside substrate substitution. Immediately after the synthesis of carbon nanotube, a layer of silicon dioxide with the thickness of 250 nm was deposited over the samples. This is a protection layer for carbon nanotube when etching parylene with O2 plasma. 1 um parylene C was deposited on the front side of sample. For the purpose of patterning parylene C, another layer of titanium was deposited on the surface and the region of pads and electrodes were exposed. Parylene C was opened by O2 plasma etching and was checked by Tencor P-10 Surface Profiler. Then, titanium mask was etched with the solution of HF : H2O 1:100. When substituting the substrate, the thinnest region of device was less than 2 μm. The structure layer will be too weak to handle, and hence a dummy glass protector was applied. The samples were adhered on a thick glass with photoresist, and put in XeF2 environment to etch away the silicon. A layer of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) was then spin coated on the backside and put into vacuum chamber to release the bubbles. After the membrane was solidified, the flexible sample was released and SiO2 protect layer was etched with buffered oxide etch (BOE). Finally, the possible exposed iron catalyst was etched by hydrochloric acid. Electrochemical measurements of carbon nanotube electrodes on flexible substrate The co-fabrication of synthesized and embedded carbon nanotube electrodes were measured in electrochemical station. Three-probe station (Reference 600, Gamry Instruments, US) were used to characterize the electrochemical performance of electrodes in phosphate buffered saline (PBS), including electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and cyclic voltammetry (CV). The reference electrode was a Ag/AgCl electrode, the counter was a platinum wire, and working electrode was carbon nanotube electrode, which was connected through titanium routing and spring probes weld on printed circuit boards. Connecting spring probe directly with the sample not only prevents the abrasion between pad and probe, but also ensures the attachment between them. Meanwhile, this method does not require wire bonding, so that the uncertainty of bonding was avoided. It is noticed that the impedance will increase with the decrease of the electrode size. In order to obtain the efficiency of sacrificing electrode area to decrease the impedance of the electrodes, section impedance is defined as the product of geometrical area of electrode and its impedance at 1 kHz. As it takes geometrical surface area into consideration, it shows the area efficiency of electrode, and makes comparisons between electrodes with different sizes consistent. Potential transient measurements (PTM) was measured according to the potential window which is the voltage limits for hydrogen and oxygen evolution from the cyclic voltammetry curve. Cathodic first, balanced current pulse was generated from the stimulator, platinum wire act as ground and carbon nanotube electrodes was connected to the positive output of the stimulator, electronic oscilloscope was used to monitor the voltage accumulation through the electrode to find the largest current pulse allowed for charge injection. Results The result shows that the surface of downward synthesized samples are rougher which may due to the local electric field affected by the rough holder surface. The bode plots of synthesized CNTs, and the impedance at 1 kHz improved about 90 times when flipping the catalyst side from upward to downward. According to the phase value, downward synthesized electrode shows better capacitive performance, which will contribute to the double layer capacitance. Charge Storage Capacity (CSC) is calculated to characterize the double layer capacity. Potential window is defined as the potential range, among which the reaction is still reversible. The solution will be electrolyzed when applied voltage extends potential window. The potential window is about -0.2 V to 0.9 V, and through calculation, the CSC is 3 mC/cm2. The current pulse used in PTM is 1 ms cathodic pulse, 0.2 ms without current pulse, 1 ms positive pulse and 7.8 ms without current pulse, while the amplitude of cathodic pulse and anodic pulse are the same. There is a sharp decrease and increase in the cyclic voltammetry which is related to the impedance of electrode. The slow accumulation reflects the charge stored on the double layer capacitance, according to the potential window. Charge injection limit (CIL) of electrodes indicates an upper limit of current pulse. The calculated CIL of downward synthesized CNT is 2.42 mC/cm2. From the PTM voltage pulse, the sharp slope reflects the impedance and the slow slope reflects the charge accumulation. The impedance and section impedance of electrodes with different sizes were compared. It is shown that the section impedance is smaller with smaller electrode sizes in groups of platinum TiN, and parylene embedded CNT electrodes in Musa et al. 2012. This means the smaller electrodes are more area efficient even their impedance is larger. The section impedance of downward synthesized CNT in this paper is the smallest comparing with other untreated CNTs, which means it has the highest area efficiency. The silicon dioxide deposited after carbon nanotubes’ synthesis act as the barrier layer to protect carbon nanotubes while patterning the parylene. It also enhances the adhesion between carbon nanotubes. Meanwhile, by etching silicon dioxide above carbon nanotube with buffered oxide etching, the untreated carbon nanotubes’ rough and hydrophobic surface becomes rough and hydrophilic, which is desirable in this application, rough surface attracts neuron growth, and hydrophilic surface decreases the stimulate impedance. Hence the CNTs embedded inside parylene show better performance.

11200814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200814.value: The present study focused on the fabrication and characterization of a carbon nanotube (CNT)-based microelectrode array on a non-flexible substrate and on a flexible substrate. Noble metals such as platinum, platinum alloys, iridium oxide, and titanium nitride, have been used as neural electrodes for a long time. In recent years, conducting polymers and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have emerged as alternative materials. Among all emerging materials, CNTs is an ideal material to meet the requirements for small electrode size yet with low impedance, superior electrical and mechanical properties, as well as good affinity to cell adhesion. The conventional MEAs are planar electrodes. Planar electrodes exhibit large distance between electrode and target neurons, resulting in elevation of stimulus threshold that leads to limitation on electrode size and more power consumption. A three-dimensional protruding structure of CNTs has shown a better affinity to neuronal cells, resulting in reduction of electrode-tissue distance and stimulus threshold. We fabricated a high-density carbon nanotube microelectrode array (MEA) chip. Vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) were synthesized by microwave plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition and thermal chemical vapor deposition. The device was characterized using electrochemical experiments such as cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy and potential transient measurements. Through-silicon vias (TSVs) were fabricated and partially filled with polycrystalline silicon to allow electrical connection from the high-density electrodes to a stimulator microchip. We have completed this work and published in a journal, Sensing and Bio-Sensing Research. Next, we fabricated a high-resolution flexible electrodes. Among the steps, the carbon nanotube (CNT) electrodes synthesized facing down shows impedance improvement of about 90 times comparing with the normal facing up synthesized samples. Meanwhile, section impedance of electrodes is also defined in this paper to compare the area efficiency of impedance between electrodes with different sizes. In addition and to the best of our knowledge, high performance electrodes embedded inside parylene is reported for the first time taking into consideration the hydrophobicity change of the CNT surface. We have completed this work and published in an IEEE international conference, 38th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. [Note: The acknowledged of the support of RGC is CityU 11200814, not 1200814. It is due to a typo made before publication.] In addition, we also successfully fabricated silicon nanowires with length closed to 60 um using different etchant compositions. We have reported this work in a journal, Nanoscale Research Letters.

11200814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200814.value: There are two suggested future developments of the present study. First, an extension could include a reliability test of the electrode. Delamination caused by mechanical instability and/or poor adhesion between electrode and substrate would be intensified by sustained current pulsing. It is important to evaluate the durability of the CNT MEA over the time course of sustained current pulse testing. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements could be performed at various time points (e.g. 100 days, 200 days, 300 days) in PBS at room temperature. Second, safety and efficacy studies using the CNT microelectrode array to retinal tissue could be further explored in the in vitro and in vivo settings using animal models with retinal degeneration.

11200814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200814.value: Clinicians and engineers have been working together to restore lost functions to individuals suffered from neurological disorders by electronic means for over 100 years. Neural interface technologies have been studied extensively to encode information as ensembles of the electrical activity of neurons and decode information as electric pulses to reactivate intact neurons in the damaged brain. There is an increasing need for high electrode density implants. While the electrode size continues to scale down, the stimulating neural microelectrode array has to remain efficient and safe. The present study has systematically fabricated and characterized a carbon nanotube (CNT)-based microelectrode array on a non-flexible substrate and on a flexible substrate. We successfully fabricated and tested a microelectrode chip using CNTs as the electrode material. Novel designs of interconnects were employed to solve the problem of routing for large microelectrode arrays. With the novel face down synthesis, the electrochemical performance of untreated CNT is improved about 90 times when comparing with face up synthesized samples, These results suggest that the next generation of neural implants could likely incorporate at least 1000 microelectrodes with the use of CNTs, interconnects and Flip-Chip technology and the novel synthesis of CNT.

11201014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201014.value: Semiconductor lasers under nonlinear dynamics are unique photonic sources for generating a variety of microwave or millimeter-wave waveforms. Without any external modulations, the nonlinear dynamics can be invoked by simple perturbation schemes such as the optical injection scheme. Over the past couple of years, the nonlinear dynamical period-one (P1) oscillation state invoked by optical injection has attracted new attentions for tunable, single-tone photonic millimeter-wave generation. The emission from a laser in P1 oscillation exhibits intensity oscillation at frequencies tunable from the microwave range to the millimeter-wave range. Different research groups, including our own, have experimentally demonstrated a number of applications of the P1 oscillation, which include photonic microwave signal amplification, radio-over-fiber communication, and millimeter-wave generation with phase noise reduction. Compared to the experimental works, theoretical analysis of the P1 oscillation remains much less explored. In this proposal, we consider analytical investigations on the P1 oscillation state. Modeling of the laser first follows the standard rate equations that express the optical field by its envelope at the optical frequency. Confining the attention to P1 oscillations allows one to simplify the envelope to individual oscillation frequency components, which vary much slower than the P1 oscillation frequencies in the microwave range. However, these very slowly varying frequency components contain the most important information for understanding the P1 oscillation state. Firstly, the proposed research will analytically investigate the modulation characteristics of the P1 oscillation frequency components. Through generalizing a steady-state analysis of the P1 frequency components, a time-varying analysis will be explored to reveal the mechanisms of modulating P1 oscillations in radio-over-fiber and optical communication applications. Secondly, the proposed research will focus on arriving analytical results on the noise contained in the P1 oscillation frequency components. Reduction of the phase noise through schemes such as coherent feedback and incoherent feedback will be investigated analytically. Thirdly, the proposed research will consider analytically the enhancement of the harmonics of the P1 oscillation states. The beat signals of the higher harmonics are at multiples of the fundamental P1 oscillation frequency. Enhancing these harmonics enables multiplication of the microwave or millimeter-wave frequencies generated from P1 oscillations. Harmonics enhancement through optical feedbacks from nonlinear optical media will be considered analytically. The proposed analytical investigations on the P1 oscillation are expected to deepen the understanding of the nonlinear laser dynamics for photonic microwave applications. 處於非線性動態的半導體激光器是可以產生各種微波及毫米波波形的獨特的光子發生器。在沒有外部調制的條件下，利用像光注入這樣的簡單微擾就可以產生各種非線性動態。在過去的幾年裏，利用光注入而產生的非線性單周期振蕩動態激起了人們新的研究興趣，並將其用於可調的、單頻的光子毫米波的產生。處於單周期振蕩的激光器，其發射的光波的強度以一定的頻率振蕩，並且該頻率在微波甚至於毫米波範圍內連續可調。包括我們在內的諸多研究小組已經在實驗上證實了單周期振蕩的一些應用，其中包括信號的放大和相位噪聲的壓制。相對於實驗研究而言，單周期振蕩的理論分析依然很少被探究。在這份研究計劃中，我們將要解析研究單周期振蕩的動力學態。激光器的建模首先采用了前人建立的標準的速率方程，其中他們使用光頻上的包絡來描述光場。著眼於單周期振蕩的研究，可以將包絡簡化為個別的振蕩場的幅度，而這些幅度隨時間演化的速度遠慢於以微波頻率振蕩的單周期振蕩的速度。然而，這些緩慢演化的光場幅度包含了理解單周期振蕩動力學態的最重要的信息。首先，擬定的研究將解析研究振蕩幅度的調制特性。利用對注入參數的調制，單周期振蕩已經被用於光載無線通信和光通信。但是通過將一個已建立的穩態分析擴展到時變分析來完善這種參數調制的分析模型還是必要的。其次，擬定的研究將著重於對單周期振蕩幅度中包含的噪聲影響獲得解析的成果。相位噪聲的壓制機制，比如相干反饋，非相干反饋和雙重鎖定，將被解析研究。第三，擬定的研究將解析單周期振蕩動力學態的諧波加強的效應。高次諧波的拍頻信號的頻率是單周期振蕩基頻的整數倍。這些諧波加強的效應使得單周期振蕩產生的微波或毫米波的頻率倍增成為可能。利用非線性光學媒介的光反饋的諧波加強效應將被考量。擬定的對單周期振蕩的解析研究有望加深對非線性激光系統動力學的理解，有利於其在微波光子學中的應用。

11201014.label: Realisation of objectives
11201014.value: The project aims to investigate the limit-cycle dynamics of optically injected semiconductor lasers. The oscillatory period-one (P1) dynamics is utilized for widely tunable and optically controllable photonic microwave generation. Based on the rate equations of different lasers, the oscillatory behaviors have been analyzed for a variety of photonic microwave signals. The investigation has led to the numerical and experimental demonstration of photonic microwave generation with frequency modulation of fast sweep rate, square-wave modulation via optical feedback, frequency stability in quantum-dot lasers. The investigation was extended to characterize noise in semiconductor ring lasers (SRLs), where up to 30 dB improvements on feedback insensitivity was found. The objectives of the project have been addressed over the duration of the project as detailed below. Objective 1 was about the modulation characteristics of the P1 oscillation in an optically injected semiconductor laser. Support by a rate-equation analysis, the oscillatory dynamics realized the generation of frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) microwave signals. A modulated optical injection drives the laser into P1 oscillation with a modulated microwave frequency, while adding feedback to the injection reduces the microwave phase noise. Compared to other alternative schemes, a very fast sweep rate of 0.42 GHz/ns was achieved in illustrating the unique properties of the use of P1 oscillation in photonic microwave generation. The sweep range covers a wide bandwidth of the same order of magnitude as the relaxation resonance frequency. The experimental observations were consistent with the results from small-signal analysis based on the rate equations of the lasers. Besides FMCW, square-wave (SW) switching of the lasing direction in a SRL was also investigated. Biased to a regime that supports lasing in either counter-clockwise (CCW) or clockwise (CW) direction, counter-directional mutual feedback was investigated using various combinations of feedback delay times. Symmetric SWs exceeding the tenth order was found to be supported by the nonlinear dynamics for fast periodic switching. Objective 2 was about investigating the phase noise of the P1 oscillation for generating signals of high spectral purity. Phase diffusion was analyzed through state-space reconstruction. The reconstruction of the stable attractor requires only the emission intensity time series, allowing both experimental and numerical evaluations with good qualitative agreement. By evaluating the divergence of neighboring states, the time-dependent exponents were monitored. Such exponents indicated that the divergence of the state-space trajectory in general does not saturate until after a long evolution time. A strong contrast of the P1 states was obtained in comparison to the chaotic states. Although experimental noise enables the generation of entropy, the P1 dynamics is periodic in providing no fast mixing of states. Also, through varying the linewidths of both the master and slave lasers, the phase noise of the P1 oscillation was found to be minimized when injected near the relaxation resonance frequency, where dual-loop feedback can reduce the phase noise to the level of −94 dBc/Hz without using any high-speed electronics. Additionally, based on self-mixing considerations, the spectral purity of the laser emission under coherent and incoherent feedback was examined through a direct comparison of lasers with linear and ring geometries. An analysis of the optical spectra reveals that the SRL remains nearly unaffected for an optical feedback level of as strong as −23 dB, which is indicative of an improvement of up to 30 dB in terms of insensitivity to feedback induced noise. Objective 3 was about extending the range of frequency generation. Feedback was introduced to the laser with a relatively long round-trip time delay in comparison to the laser dynamical oscillation. A new dynamical regime was unveiled both numerically and experimentally for switching between two nonlinear dynamical states. The P1 oscillation frequency is locked by the feedback in generating harmonics separated by the reciprocal of the feedback delay time. Additionally, for InAs/GaAs quantum dot lasers, the P1 oscillation with low sensitivity to the frequency detuning were found close to the Hopf bifurcation line. The second-harmonic distortion of the electrical signal can be much reduced by varying the detuning frequency. Through addressing these objectives, the project successfully demonstrated the variation of the P1 oscillation in the application for photonic microwave generation using different semiconductor lasers. Based on the experiments and the rate-equation models, the P1 oscillation was shown to be quickly tunable in yielding FMCW signals. The inherent laser dynamics has allowed for the SW modulation via optical feedback. The unique mechanisms in quantum dot lasers led to the demonstration of P1 with low sensitivity to perturbation. The extension to SRL realized periodic SW switching. Also, interestingly, self-mixing measurements revealed the 30 dB improvements on feedback insensitivity for SRLs.

11201014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201014.value: The research contributed to 7 journal publications and 6 conference papers. It also partially supported the training of 1 Ph.D. student on his work on the ring lasers. The project enabled collaborations with different overseas experts. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows. From rate-equation modeling as well as experiments, modulated P1 oscillations were used for generating FMCW signals with a fast sweep range reaching 7.7 GHz with a sweep rate of 0.42 GHz/ns. Through collaboration with Prof. Marc Sorel of Glasgow University, a different form of periodic oscillation was found via the dynamics of directional switching in SRLs. When CCW and CW modes in a SRL are coupled by feedback, periodic SWs were yielded with the switching time and electrical linewidth reduced to 1.4 ns and 1.1 kHz, respectively. High-order symmetric SWs with a reduced period were also found potentially for clock signal generation. The results were documented in journal publications [2, 5] and conference publication [1] in Part C. As for the noise characteristics associated with the P1 dynamics, analysis through state-space reconstruction was conducted using optimal choices of the embedding delay and dimension. In addition, the insensitivity to optical feedback was experimentally measured for a SRL as compared to a conventional FPL. Both optical noise and self-mixing measurement showed that the tolerance to feedback in SRLs is 25–30 dB stronger than in FPLs. Similarly, by analyzing quantum dot lasers, phase noise was found to be clearly affected by the excited and ground states, but not the carrier reservoir states. The results were documented in journal publications [3, 4, 7] and conference publications [2-4, 6] in Part C. Furthermore, using optical feedback in the long-cavity regime, spontaneous switching from a stable state to a periodic state was found. Predicted numerically and then verified experimentally, the resultant intensity time series was confirmed as comprising of a SW envelope, where harmonics with microwave linewidths reduced to the order of 10 kHz was yielded without any electrical modulation. Extension to InAs/GaAs quantum dot lasers was carried out with the P1 oscillations being relatively insensitive to the fluctuations of injection. The microwave power is enhanced by strengthening the injection when operating away from the Hopf bifurcation, whereas the second-harmonic distortion of the electrical signal is well reduced by increasing the detuning frequency. The results were documented in journal publications [1, 6] and conference publication [5] in Part C.

11201014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201014.value: With the demonstration of the different variants of P1 oscillations, a number of extensions for photonic microwave signal generation and processing can be explored. Firstly, the FMCW signal can be further developed for ranging applications with proper choices of the wideband antennas. Secondly, the periodic SW generation using the SRLs can be further investigated for increasing the switching speed for optical clock signals. Thirdly, the SW-modulated microwave signals can be applied in connection with wireless communications for distributing timing information. Additionally, the quantum dot and ring lasers with reduced sensitivities to perturbations can be applied for developing feedback insensitive sources. Some of these extensions are being pursued at the moment based on the results of this project.

11201014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201014.value: Semiconductor lasers are interesting nonlinear devices that are unique photonic sources for generating a variety of microwave waveforms. Without using any electronic modulations, the nonlinear dynamics can be invoked by simple perturbation schemes such as the optical injection scheme. The P1 oscillation of a semiconductor laser is essentially an undamped oscillation originating from the relaxation resonance. This project analyzed a number of modulation schemes on the P1 oscillation for generating microwave signals in the forms of FMCW for fast frequency modulation, SW oscillations as digital signals, and spontaneous switching for clock signals, which are applicable for radio-over-fiber communication and ranging. Moreover, through collaboration, special lasers in ring geometries and quantum dot materials have been found to exhibit unique insensitivities to perturbations. These sources can be further developed as stable sources for communication systems in the future.

11201114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201114.value: Program testing is widely practiced in the industry to assure the quality of programs and detect failures from them. Nowadays, many multithreaded programs are being developed. Critical failures such as memory corruption due to inconsistent concurrent accesses, deadlocks, and crashes are occasionally reported by the users of many important multithreaded programs such as MySQL and Tomcat. They show that the testing methods applied to these programs still fail to deal with the real-world challenges. These failures are major threats when users perform their activities that rely on such multithreaded programs. All such critical failures are originated from unexpected program states. Triggering these failures must firstly lead program executions into unexpected program states, which further require a reliable mechanism to determine whether a program state is unexpected. Static analysis or model checking techniques are inherently imprecise to identify unexpected program states from programs. Testing is an approach that executes programs and can precisely report the presence of such critical concurrency bugs. To determine whether a program may result in an unexpected state, linearizability testing aims to check whether a concurrent trace follows the behavior of some sequential trace of the same program over the same input. Existing state-of-the-art automated linearizability testing techniques check the responses from methods, outputs from the traces or assertion statements. Nonetheless, our preliminary experiment shows that these techniques miss to identify objects having states inconsistent with the states of the corresponding objects in the sequential trace counterparts. We have also found that objects in such unexpected states may lead the corresponding programs to crash or become deadlocking in some trace scenarios. New, precise, and automated techniques that effectively check and report unexpected states from execution traces of large-scale programs should be developed. This project aims at developing a novel LATTE framework to support object-state linearizability testing to address all the above challenges in testing object-oriented multithreaded programs. It formulates novel object-state models and conformance relations to support the checking between objects in concurrent traces against objects in their sequential trace counterparts. It systematically and recursively generates linearizable traces, and exploits this characteristic to formulate novel strategies to select objects for object-state linearizability testing. It validates whether the trace prefixes having objects confirmed with object-state linearizability violations can trigger critical failures via randomized active testing. This project will also educate research students so that they can effectively contribute to the growth of the software industry after graduation. 工業界廣泛採用程序測試來檢測程序失效，並保證程序的質量。現如今，許多軟件開發項目已致力於開發多線程程序。本項目針對的是面向對象的多線程程序。 對於許多重要的多線程程序，例如MySQL、Apache服務器和Eclipse，用戶在使用的過程中，仍不時的會提交嚴重的軟件失效報告，諸如由不一致的並發存取產生的內存破壞、死鎖以及程序崩潰。這表明當前使用的測試技術依舊無法充分解決實際工作中所遇到的難題。當用戶在進行依賴於多線程程序的活動時，軟件失效是其中主要的威脅。這些軟件失效都是源於非預期的程序狀態。程序需首先處於非預期的狀態中，才能觸發這些軟件失效。為此工業界需要一個可靠的機制來決定一個程序狀態是否是非預期的。 靜態分析或者模型檢測技術在識別非預期的程序狀態上有著內在的不准確性。程序測試是通過執行程序來準確報告存在的並發錯誤和非預期的程序狀態的一種手段。可線性化測試通過檢查程序的並行執行軌跡能否等同於同一輸入下的某些順序執行軌跡來判定該程序是否會引發非預期的狀態。現有的自動可線性化測試技術檢查函數的響應、程序執行的結果或者程序斷言。然而，我們的初步實驗表明這些技術無法識別跟順序執行軌跡中有著不一致狀態的程序對象。我們還進一步發現，這些處於非預期程序狀態中的對象，會導致程序在其他執行過程中崩潰或者死鎖。因此，開發新型的、準確的、自動化的技術，來有效地從大型程序的執行軌跡中檢測和識別非預期狀態是必要的。 為解決上述的難題，本項目旨在開發一款名為LATTE的新型的基於對象狀態的可線性化測試框架。此框架提出了新的程序對象狀態模型，以及用以比較並行執行軌跡與順序執行軌跡中對象相關性的一致性關係。它系統性地、遞歸地從順序執行軌跡中生成可線性化的軌跡，並且利用這一點去構造新的對象選擇策略，來選擇合適的程序對象進行可線性化測試。此框架還通過隨機性的主動測試，來驗證含有不一致對象狀態的執行軌跡是否會引發嚴重的軟件失效

11201114.label: Realisation of objectives
11201114.value: This project aimed to study and develop a testing framework to test against a kind of concurrency errors known as linearizability errors occurring in the executions of object-oriented multithreaded programs. This kind of concurrency error is raised due to improper usages of memory accesses on various objects among function calls in a program execution, which further makes developers difficult to understand, reason, and analyze the program code. Wrong usage of objects in the program due to concurrency issues will lead to the integrity issue in program states, which may further make the program to behave unintendedly. We conducted a series of exploratory study to achieve the objective one [J2-J5, J7, C1, C3, C7-C8, C10, C13, C15]. We examined the source code of selected programs and ran these programs to collect the execution statistics on the usages of individual memory locations and those function calls in relation to these memory locations and objects therein. To ensure the exploratory study representative, we studied those smaller benchmark programs that were widely used in concurrency bugs detection research published in their-party publications published conferences and journals as well as real-world multithreaded programs. When running these programs over test cases, we manipulated the thread executions to check whether the observed function calls can be rearranged in some other alternative schedules of the current runs and check whether the outputs of these program runs were the same. We applied existing methods in the area of active testing to support the fine-grained examinations over multiple program runs. We also manually inspected the source code of these programs around the bug locations of these concurrency errors and examined why some test cases can manifest these errors. We computed the statistics using various metrics that quantified complexity such as number of memory accesses on shared memory locations per function call, the number of function calls, how many lock acquisition and lock release operations performed to gain insights on the program executions. We also applied different active testing strategies as well as native or random strategies to examine the chances to observe these linearizability errors or the associated lower level concurrency bugs. We found that there are many factors affecting the detection of bugs from programs. Random inputs can be used as the baseline to generate test cases, but special designs to handle different unique input features should be considered in the test case generation process so as to reach some buggy code [J2, C7]. We also found that buggy memory locations are clustered [J3, J7, C3, C8, C10, C13] and many threads execute similar code fragments / function call sequences [J4] and yet reproduce the same program execution sequence is difficult [C14], which means that there should be a holistic support of testing and debugging [C5, C14]. By compiling the code using different compiler optimization, the detection of the same bug can become significantly easier [J5, C1]. To realize the second and the third objectives, we examined the existing methods in the same area and applied them to the cases identified in the above exploratory study and designed the use of classical and our designed test oracles and test selection approaches [J1-J3, J5-J7, C1-C3, C6, C8-C18]. There are many kinds of objects in a program execution. We finally chose function code block as the unit of object as the focal area studied in this project. The rationale behind this decision was that a precise set of operations affecting an object in a program execution cannot be extracted from the code. Prior arts checking this kind of objects rely on a strong assumption of availability of a specification stating the full set of functions involved. This kind of specification is generally unavailable in practice and objects without such a well-defined function interfaces cannot be checked by these methods. We also formulated methods to diversify the selection of objects. More specifically, we formulated a new strategy that measure the distances among intermediate objects in multiple executions in figuring out which objects and which executions to be explored [J1, C2] and under which sets of compiler configuration parameters [J5, C1]. We also formulated iterative approaches based on code refactoring to strengthen test oracles [J2] or on sharing of common patterns to reduce the amount of oracle checks with functional contexts [J7, C8, C13] or on metamorphic testing as an alternative to the classical test oracle to address the test oracle problem [C9] . We also formulated test oracles while monitoring function calls and changes in program states therein [C17, C18]. During the program execution, we selected objects based on execution contexts of objects and project them into various dimensions to reveal suspiciousness object usage patterns [J3, C3, C10]. When there were insufficient failing samples, we enriched the set of collected samples via cloning of failing test cases in the same set [J6], and when there are too many operations, we attempted to remove some non-essential ones [C12]. In debugging, when needed, we attempted to locate the targets by using the execution spectra from multiple code abstraction levels [C6]. Since there are many dimensions, we also developed a series of selection frameworks to support them [C11, C14-C18]. To realize the fourth objective and to make the comparison trustworthy, we carefully reviewed the potential threats to (internal, external, construct) validity and theoretical reliability that our evaluation may incur. We implemented all the techniques on the same platform. We followed the common practices used in the research community to evaluate our various formulated strategies and algorithms. For each kind of formulation, we strived to compare to baseline, classic and state-of-the-art techniques on the same framework whenever possible. To reduce risks, we reused the existing code of the prior arts if they were available. We used statistical tests to determine to what extent the observations in the experiment cannot be explained by random. We summarized the comparisons in various dimensions, also discussed and present them in meetings, conferences and journals to gain feedbacks from the experts [J1-J7, C1-C18]. Through this project, one PhD student is trained.
