11201114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201114.value: We have developed a set of new object selection [J2, J5, C1, C7, C11, C12, C15] and sampling strategies [J1, J3, J5, C1, C2, C3, C10, C13, C15] and a set of new test oracle formulations [C2, C9, C17-C18], implemented a set of new research supportive tools for selection strategies and test oracle check [J2, J4-J5, J7, C1, C4-C8, C11-C12, C14-18], and conducted empirical studies to understand the design factors and evaluate various components of this project [J2-J3, J5-J6, C3, C6, C11, C13-C18]. We found that there could be a huge number of objects in a program execution to be considered, and projection and abstraction, no matter using simple strategies or compositional strategies can make the overall process of checking significantly more efficient in object selection [J3-J4, J7, C3, C8, C10, C13, C16]. In particular, our strategy to compose threads into the same representation [J4] is particularly novel as it allows client techniques to extract conflow flow facts that could be intractable to existing techniques. Moreover, although randomized testing is an essential art in detecting these errors (as no one can precisely predict the locations of them in advance), sometimes, it would be useful to test randomly a set of these codes rather than one by one [C18]. Test oracles are proven to be difficult to be formulated, and we have to address this issues (test oracle problem) in quite a few dimensions, within a virtual machine [C17-C18], along a program execution [J7], over program outputs [J2-J3, C3, C9, C15] or relying on generic oracle information such as crashes [C7], which also shows that there is still a lacking in a general approach to solve the problem, which in turn warrants more research.

11201114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201114.value: We believe that the combination of a large number of objects in a program and the need to precisely check out the errors is still the main challenge in the roads ahead. One possible research direction to address this challenge is to consider a two-phase strategy. In the first phase, one may investigate an effective learning method, such as a deep learning architecture, to acquire the relations among objects and let the method to suggest candidates. In the second phase, a precise detection technique can be used to check these candidates for errors using the techniques we developed for object selection and error check. Another research dimension is that as there are many objects, and one may currently need an offline approach to analyze the same program execution multiple times but with different focuses on each time to manage the memory overhead problems. It would be interesting to consider an online approach with the ability to rollback the program executions in part and/or deterministically replay a sub-sequence of operations from the current execution point with very light overheads.

11201114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201114.value: The production process of software applications is still far from perfect. This makes critical latent bugs remained in the code even after intensive testing and user evaluation. Figuring out effective and efficient methods to find out these bugs is essential so as to make the current program testing process used by software developers more scalable and end users can use higher quality software applications at a lower cost. This project studies a kind of software applications known as multithreaded programs and focuses on the aspects of selecting objects for error checking and formulation of error checking conditions. To the best of our knowledge, we have invented the first hierarchical and compositional representation for clients to analyze program traces and demonstrated a new approach to formulate precise error checking conditions (which are known as test oracles) and figured out new test selection strategies to handle a large sample dataset extracted from running these programs for the purpose of error checking. This project also trained a PhD student, who is working in the ICT industry in Hong Kong.

11201414.value: 異質線性動力節點有向演化網絡的能控性與能觀性研究

11201414.label: Project Objectives
11201414.value: Derive some precise graphic-algebraic controllability conditions through theoretical analysis for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics, subject to one single pinning controller, and study the effects of various network parameters such as the coupling strength and node-node correlation on the controllability via extensive computer simulations. Derive some precise graphic-algebraic controllability conditions through theoretical analysis for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics, subject to multiple pinning controllers, and study the effects of the community structure on the controllability via extensive computer simulations. Derive some precise graphic-algebraic observability conditions through theoretical analysis for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics, and investigate the practical case with noisy measurements via a modified Kalman filtering approach for estimations.

Derive some precise graphic-algebraic controllability conditions through theoretical analysis for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics, subject to multiple pinning controllers, and study the effects of the community structure on the controllability via extensive computer simulations.

11201414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201414.value: This proposal aims to study the controllability of evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics and to derive some precise graph-theoretic controllability conditions and criteria for such networks. The associated network observability property will also be investigated. Several basic settings and typical scenarios will be considered, including pinning control with one single controller (if it is sufficient) and with multiple controllers (if it can be more effective), respectively, for various topologies such as regular, random, small-world and scale-free networks. The effects of key parameters and network structures on the network controllability and observability will be explored and analyzed. Three research objectives are proposed to achieve: (1) for complex networks with one single pinning controller, derive some precise graphic-algebraic controllability conditions and examine the effects of various network parameters on the controllability; (2) for complex networks with multiple pinning controllers, derive some precise graphic-algebraic controllability conditions and investigate the effects of community structures on the controllability; and (3) similarly as above, derive some precise graphic-algebraic observability conditions and investigate the practical case with noisy measurements. 摘要 本項目研究異質線性動力節點有向演化網絡的能控性與能觀性條件及相關特性，其中網絡包括正規、隨機、小世界和無標度類型，控制機制為牽制式。研究目標包括：（1）當只使用一個控制器時的圖論-代數能控性條件及網絡參數之影響；（2）當只使用多個控制器時的圖論-代數能控性條件及網絡結構之影響；（3）上述兩種情形網絡的能觀性條件，及有噪音環境下的相關研究。 English Abstract has no changes

11201414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201414.value: (1) A complete and precise graphic-algebraic controllability condition had been derived for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics, subject to one single pinning controller. Some effects of the key network parameters (coupling strength and node-node correlation) on the controllability have been analyzed based on simulations. (2) Two necessary and/or sufficient controllability conditions have been obtained for evolving directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics. The effects of the community structure on the controllability have been analyzed numerically. (3) A practical case with noisy measurements has been investigated based on a modified Kalman filter in a distributed manner.

11201414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201414.value: Similar research topics can be extended to sampled-data design of controllers and filters for the same type of complex networks. A new proposal will be submitted based on this approach, so as to develop more and deeper research in the same direction persistently.

11201414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201414.value: This research project has established some practical and precise conditions for the controllability of complex networks, which non-identical linear dynamical node systems, using one single pinning controller. Some effects of the key network parameters (such as coupling strength and node-node correlation) on the controllability have been analyzed based on computer simulations. Moreover, the same have been completed for evolutionary complex networks and complex networks in noisy environments. All these will be useful for designing controllers for various complex networks in industry and even society.

11201514.value: To provide computationally efficient estimates on the delay margins and delay domains that guarantee the stabilization of SISO and MIMO systems, respectively; To develop bounds on the guaranteed range of delays for systems subject to time-varying delays; To develop bounds on the guaranteed range of delays for mean-square stabilization of systems subject to random delays.

11201514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201514.value: This project sets out to develop a computational approach with the aim to provide computationally efficient estimates on the delay ranges within which a delay system or network can be stabilized via feedback control. The fundamental problem to be addressed and duly answered in this project concerns the question: What is the largest range of delay such that there exists a feedback controller that can stabilize all the systems subject to the delay within the range? Time delays are a prevailing scene in natural and engineered systems, which may arise from a variety of sources and can play especially a dominating role in the newly emerged interconnected systems and networks, including communication networks, sensor networks, cyber-physical systems, biological systems, and networked control systems, to name a few. Except on rare instances, time delays are likely to result in degraded performance, poor robustness, and even instability, which may translate into interrupted services and in the extreme, system failures. This project addresses some of the key, emerging needs facing today’s large-scale, complex engineering and social systems and networks, which exhibit typically time-varying, random delays on widely varied scales. Built on robust control theory and unified under small gain stability criteria, our approach draws upon a variety of techniques and tools found in analytic interpolation and rational approximation theories. Preliminary studies show that the approach is highly feasible and has the potential to deliver highly efficient solutions to a broad class of system and network delay problems, which the existing theory fails to cope with. The approach is broadly applicable to systems and networks containing large-scale, random, and time-varying delays, thus rendering it to be practically relevant to systems and networks of engineering significance. 本項目旨在發展一種高效計算方法，用於計算時間滯後系統的 最大時滯範圍，使得在該範圍之內，考慮的時滯系統或時滯網 絡可通過反饋機制鎮定。項目試圖回答下述具有本質性意義的 問題：對於一個時間滯後系統，存在一個單一反饋控制器使得 在整個時滯範圍內系統都可被鎮定的最大時滯範圍為何？基於 多種原因，時間滯後廣泛見於自然及工程系統之中，尤其在新 型互聯系統及網絡，譬如通訊網絡、傳感器網絡、物聯網、生 物系統、網絡化控制系統中起著顯著的作用。幾乎在所有情況 下，時滯都可能導致性能弱化，魯棒性變差， 甚至穩定性的喪 失，鮮有例外，並由此導致服務中斷，以至於系統崩潰。鑒於 此，本項目著重考慮當前大規模複雜工程及社會系統和網絡中 的關鍵時滯現象，具體表現為大尺度上的時變滯後。項目以魯 棒控制理論為基礎，以小增益穩定性判據為統一框架，擬採用 一系列可析函數插值及有理函數逼近的工具。初始成果顯示該 方法頗為可行，可潛在用於目前尚不能有效處理之廣泛類別的 系統和網絡時滯問題，即包含大尺度、隨機、時變滯後的系統 與網絡。為此，本方法對具工程背景及重要性的此類系統和網 絡有相當的參考意義。

11201514.label: Realisation of objectives
11201514.value: We believe that this project has been highly successful. All objectives (Objective 1-Ocjective 3) are completed, resulting in seven journal publications, nine conference papers, and one research monograph (J. Zhu, T. Qi, D. Ma, and J. Chen, Limits of Stability and Stabilization of Time-Delay Systems: A small Gain Approach, Springer, 2018). All seven journal papers, including four full-length papers, are published by the leading journals in the field of systems and control, of which the IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control and Automatica are the top 1 and top 2 journals. This outcome represents a high, and indeed rather extraordinary level of scholarship, both in quality and productivity. The project tackled and solved a number of challenging delay robustness problems for systems subject to (1) constant, unknown and uncertain delays, as reported in Journal Papers [1, 2], (2) uncertain time-varying delays, reported in Journal Papers [1, 6], and (3) stochastic delays, reported in Conference Paper [5]. The project also went beyond significantly the original scope of the proposal, leading to major results and findings on delay consensus robustness of multi-agent systems (Journal Papers [3, 7]), simultaneous stabilization of multiple discrete-time delay systems (Journal Paper [5]), and additionally PID control of delay systems (Journal Papers [4, 5, 6, 7]). Major results and findings are summarized in Section 6.1-Major Findings and Outcomes. In the due course, three Ph.D. students were supported by the project for different periods and lengths of duration. Dr. Jing Zhu received her Ph.D. in 2015 and went on to become a Lecturer at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics. She published several high quality papers and one research monograph which acknowledge the support of this project. Dr. Adil Zulfiqar received his Ph.D. in 2018 and has worked as a research staff at Chinese University of Hong Kong. He too published a number of papers based on the work generated from this project. Mr. Jianqi Chen continued to work on this project and is expected to to complete his degree in August 2019.

11201514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201514.value: The project solved a number of important problems concerning the stability and stabilization of time-delay systems and contributed in a major way to this area of research. In Journal Paper [1], we obtained fundamental bounds on the delay margin, within which a delay plant is guaranteed to be stabilizable by a certain LTI output feedback controller. The explicit, computationally efficient bounds can be computed readily and efficiently, requiring only the computation of the largest real eigenvalue of a constant matrix. Extensions are made to MIMO systems. In doing so, we introduced a new concept termed delay radius. We show that estimates on the variation ranges of multiple delays can be obtained by solving efficiently certain convex programs. Moreover, bounds and sufficient conditions are given for robust stabilization of systems with time-varying delays. Appealing results of this kind are believed to be made available the first time by this project. Another important development is the determination of the delay margin achievable by PID controllers (Journal Papers [6, 4]). PID controllers are the most widely used controllers in industry, accounting for over 90% practical control applications. In Journal Paper [6], we obtained tight, explicit bounds on the delay margin achievable by PID controllers. The results show that for first-order systems, PID controllers are among the optimal controllers that achieve the largest delay margin. Conceptually, the results also demonstrate that the integral control in fact undermines the delay robustness, the proportional control has no effect, and the derivative control is the sole means to compensate the destabilization effect of time delays. The third major outcome is the investigation of delay consensus margin and more generally performance issues for multi-agent systems subject to inter-agent communication delays. These findings are reported in Papers [3, 7, 8]. The work goes significantly beyond that for single-loop feedback systems and it requires overcoming difficulties imposed by communication network topologies. In Papers [3, 7], we gave bounds on the delay consensus margin, which demonstrate explicitly the constraints on the system's consensus imposed by the network topology. Finally, the development on random delays, other than providing significant stability results, established a generalized mean-square small gain theorem that can be applied to a broad class of estimation, control and security problems, as summarized in Section 6.2.

11201514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201514.value: The project has motivated and inspired further expansion and outgrowth. One problem of great importance is the estimation, control, and security of networked cyber physical control systems. The framework and analysis methods developed in this project will provide the foundation. In particular, the mean-square small gain theorem and its application to systems with random delays will serve as an enabler, allowing us to tackle the estimation, control, and cyber security issues in a framework of stochastic uncertainties and perturbations.

11201514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201514.value: Time delays pose significant challenges to scientists and engineers in a wide variety of fields. Driven by the considerable gap between the existing theory and emerging challenges, this project addresses some of the key, emerging needs facing large-scale, complex engineering and social systems and networks. The problem under investigation is to estimate and compute the margins or domains of delays allowable so that a complex system and network can be stabilized robustly via feedback. Built on robust control theory and unified under small gain stability criteria, this project developed a computationally efficient approach that can be used to compute bounds on the delay margin in general and exact solutions in particular for several more specialized yet still meaningful classes of systems. The approach is broadly applicable to systems and networks containing large-scale, random, spatially varying and time-varying delays, thus making it practically relevant to systems and networks of engineering significance, including, e.g., communication networks, sensor networks, cyber-physical systems, biological systems, and networked control systems.

11201914.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201914.value: 新競爭規範对建造業的影響

11201914.label: Project Objectives
11201914.value: The main purpose of the project is to assist the Hong Kong Construction Industry to prepare for the coming into force of the ‘new’ competition regime. The operating objectives and the respective research tasks are as follow: I. Study the application of a competition regime to the construction industry: I.1 studying the theoretical underpinnings of having a competition regime. I.2 comparing the competition legislations of other developed economies. II. Prepare for the challenges by: II.1 examining the minefields against the First and Second Conduct Rules. II.2 exploring arrangements/conducts for block exemption. II.3 suggesting compliance measures; III. Explore implications on the business models in construction Research plan for the fulfillment of the aim and operating objectives is elaborated in section 3 of this proposal. The significance of the project can be illustrated from: i) A policy perspective - Some critics object to the implementation of the Ordinance because of its departure from the “small government, big market” framework. As such, the research project probes into a more pragmatic view of the fundamental issues underpinning this policy move in relation to the construction industry. ii) An academic perspective – notwithstanding the generally accepted positive relation between competition and economic efficiency, the underlying assumptions will be examined if construction industry fits into this consumer welfare oriented paradigm. These are new as far as the Hong Kong construction industry is concerned, Furthermore, the market analysis for the application of the 2nd conduct rule is an almost uncharted area in construction research in Hong Kong. iii) A practice perspective – Almost all the industrial collaborators we have contacted in preparing this proposal indicated that they know very little about the Competition Ordinance, not to say how to prepare for it. The industrial collaborators have expressed strong interest in the proposed study. The findings may also point to long-term market structural reform.

11201914.label: Realisation of objectives
11201914.value: Objective I: Study the application of a competition regime to the construction industry: I.1 studying the theoretical underpinnings of having a competition regime. I.2 comparing the competition legislations of other developed economies. Desktop analyses provided invaluable input for the accomplishment of Objective I. The findings for objective 1.1 and 1.2 are reported in the following papers: Zhao X. J., Cheung S.O. and Guo Y.S. (2014) “The Impact of the Hong Kong first ever Competition Law on construction contracting”, ASCE Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction. Vol. 6(2). Cheung S.O. (2017) “Review of construction practices in the light of the Hong Kong first-ever Competition Ordinance”, Proceedings of the CIB International Research Conference, 11-12 September 2017, University of Salford, UK., pp 129-138. Objective II: Prepare for the challenges by: II.1 examining the minefields against the First and Second Conduct Rules. II.2 exploring arrangements/conducts for block exemption. II.3 suggesting compliance measures. For II.1, the potential minefields against the First Conduct Rule include: 1. Agreement not to compete 2. Joint venture arrangements 3. Tradesman wages agreements The studies conducted for the captioned are mainly derived from interviews with industry experts and desktop analyses. The activities conducted for the study and the findings therefrom are disseminated through the following publications: Shen Lu and Cheung S.O. (2017) “How forming Joint Ventures may affect Market Concentration?”, The International Journal of Construction Management (published on line 10th April 2017). Cheung S.O. (2016) “Are Agreements not to Compete Anti-competition?”, The ASCE Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering Construction. Vol. 8(2) May 2016 (doi:10.1061/(ASCE)LA.1943-4170.0000181). Shen Lu and Cheung S.O. (2016) “Would Joint Ventures affect Competition?”, Project Management Symposium, University of Maryland, 12-14 May 2016. Cheung S.O. (2016) “Would Tradesman Collective Wage Agreement be exempted from the Hong Kong Competition Ordinance?”, The Third Australasia and South-East Asia Structural Engineering and Construction Conference, Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia, Oct 31-Nov 4, 2016. For II.2, the criteria for block exemption have been studied, in particular to investigate the application to tradesmen wages agreement and joint venture agreements. The research findings suggest that these agreements are likely to be granted for exemption for the social benefits these derive. The said discussions are reported in the following publication: Cheung S.O. (2016) “Would Tradesman Collective Wage Agreement be exempted from the Hong Kong Competition Ordinance?”, The Third Australasia and South-East Asia Structural Engineering and Construction Conference, Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia, Oct 31-Nov 4, 2016. For II.3, interviews with the construction community suggest that the current practices of the construction industry have been designed to guard against corruptions and not so much for anti-competition. Nonetheless, the former has offer a good screen for anti-competition behaviours. The research team aims to further explore this in the remaining project duration. Objective III: Explore implications on the business models in construction The studies on joint venture and collective tradesman wage agreements also serve this objective. Although the industry does not think that the two aforementioned practices are having competition issue. The research team suggested that collective tradesman wage agreements should apply for block exemption under Section 15 of the Competition Ordinance. To further investigate the application of the Second Conduct rule, two markets studies have been conducted to exemplify the application of the guidelines of the Second Conduct Rule: i) ten mega- project market; and ii) the private residential unit supply market. These two markets have been identified by the Consumer Council that there may be issues of competition. The ten mega-projects currently being constructed in Hong Kong is an economy boosting program after the 2008 financial turmoil. The projects are of high value and would provide the needed transportation network for economic development as well as integration with the transportation network of PRC. These projects are of high value and thus usually being undertaken by Joint-ventures. With secondary data obtained from the public domains, a market concentration analysis was conducted. It is found that the market is fairly concentrated yet no particular strong and dominating participants were found. The study and its findings are reported in: Shen Lu and Cheung S.O. (2017) “How forming Joint Ventures may affect Market Concentration?”, The International Journal of Construction Management (published on line 10th April 2017). Cheung S.O. and Shen Lu “Concentration Analysis to measure Competition in Mega projects”, The ASCE Journal of Management in Engineering, (Published on line 11th July 2016). Shen Lu and Cheung S.O. (2016) “Would Joint Ventures affect Competition?”, Project Management Symposium, University of Maryland, 12-14 May 2016. The concentration of the private residential unit supply market is more difficult to measure. A preliminary analysis was conducted and reported in the following papers: Cheung S.O., Levina Brigitta and Niu Yuhan (2017) “Concentration Analysis of New Private Residential Units Market in Hong Kong”, The Journal of Construction Economics and Building, Vol. 17(2): 1-23 (June 2017). Cheung S.O. and Niu Yuhan (2016) “A Concentration Analysis of residential property unit in Hong Kong”, The Third Australasia and South-East Asia Structural Engineering and Construction Conference, Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia, Oct 31-Nov 4, 2016. It is also found that sharing with the construction community should be extended both locally and overseas. As such a keynote on competition issues in Housing and mega projects was presented in Melbourne in July 2017: Cheung S.O. (2017) “Housing Supply and Major Infrastructure Projects in Hong Kong”, 41st AUBEA. 3-5 July 2017, RMIT, Australia.

11201914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201914.value: The study has reviewed the current construction practices and offers the following key finings: 1. Tradesmen wage agreement should apply for block exemption under the Competition ordinance. 2. Although there is no concrete evidence of competition issues in the mega project market and the private residential unit market, the limited number of participant is conducive for issues of competition. 3. Joint-venturing is common for construction contracting, there is no guideline on the implications on market competition. 4. The completion ordinance offers administrative remedies to guard against agreement not to compete that is not illegal in Common law. 5. Market analysis is very difficult to conduct as market share informations are typical commercial secret. 11201914.value: Notable issues of competition have identified in the building maintenance and renovation market. Moreover, little has been done in this regard. 11201914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201914.value: Hong Kong enacted her first-ever Competition Ordinance (HKCO) which came into full effect on 14th December 2015. Among the rules under the HKCO, the First Conduct Rule (FCR) and Second Conduct Rule (SCR) are considered as having greater impacts on the construction industry. FCR seeks to curb agreements among undertakings that would prevent, restrict or distort competition in Hong Kong. SCR enables governmental administrative interventions should a market player having substantial market power abuse their power and carry out activities that would prevent, restrict or distort competition in Hong Kong. For the construction industry, the immediate impact can be noted from the abolishment of professional fee scales that have to be abolished. Bidding arrangement, tradesmen daily wage and forming joint venture also appear vulnerable. It is found that agreement not to compete in bidding is vulnerable under the FCR although it is not illegal in common law. Daily wage agreements of construction tradesmen should apply for block exemption. Joint venture agreements are not per se anti-competition. Moreover, these may present a competition issue should the market be very discrete and only has only a few firms participating as in the market of ten mega projects and private residential unit.

11202014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202014.value: 基於長週期光柵結構的石墨烯光學器件

11202014.label: Project Objectives
11202014.value: The first objective is to develop a theoretical model to calculate the transmission characteristics of a long-period fiber grating (LPFG) attached onto a graphene-deposited substrate, in particular, how the resonance bands of the LPFG are modulated by the absorption in the graphene layer. The model can facilitate the understanding of the operation principles of graphene-attached LPFGs and the design of LPFGs to optimize various modulation effects. The second objective is to experimentally investigate the transmission characteristics of graphene-attached LPFGs. The third objective is to investigate the feasibility of using a graphene-attached LPFG as a platform for the realization of fiber sensors, such as magnetic-field and gas sensors. The fourth objective is to develop a theoretical model to analyze long-period waveguide grating (LPWG) structures that incorporate graphene layers. The model can facilitate the design of various graphene-incorporated LPWG structures to best harness the optical properties of graphene. The fifth objective is to experimentally investigate the transmission characteristics of a properly designed graphene-incorporated LPWG and its response to the modulation of the optical absorption of graphene, where the LPWG is fabricated with polymer materials. The study can provide data to verify the theoretical model and help access the practicality of the structure. The sixth objective is to experimentally investigate the feasibility of using a graphene-incorporated LPWG as a platform for the realization of optical sensors, such as magnetic-field and gas sensors.

11202014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202014.value: Graphene, a two-dimensional single layer of carbon atoms, has found numerous applications in electronic devices. The unique optical properties of the material, such as electrically tunable absorption, exceptionally strong nonlinearity, saturable absorption, efficient luminescence, etc., have also promised a wide range of applications in the realization of photonic and optoelectronic devices, such as smart displays, touch screens, ultrafast lasers, photovoltaic devices, light-emitting devices, photodetectors, sensors, polarizers, and modulators. There is a growing interest world-wide in exploring the optical properties of graphene for various applications. Graphene photonic devices can be divided into two types: (i) waveguide devices and (ii) non-waveguide devices. Waveguide devices, where the light wave propagates along the graphene surface, are suitable for applications that require a long light-graphene interaction length. Devices like polarizers and modulators, and some sensors are waveguide devices. Non-waveguide devices, where light passes through the graphene layer vertically, are suitable for applications like smart displays and touch screens. The project investigates a versatile platform for the implementation of graphene-based waveguide devices. The waveguide structure considered in the project consists of a long-period grating (LPG) coupled optically to a graphene layer. An LPG is a periodic structure formed in an optical fiber or a planar waveguide to enables light coupling from the core into the cladding of the fiber/waveguide at specific wavelengths. When the light wave propagating in the cladding is in contact with the graphene layer, any absorption modulation in graphene can affect the light propagation and hence the transmission of the LPG. This graphene-incorporated LPG structure can be explored for the development of many devices, such as optical modulators, wavelength filters, polarization-dependent loss compensators, and various kinds of sensors. The PI has more than 15 year experience in LPG research and a much longer experience in waveguide design. CityU is equipped with the facility necessary for the fabrication of planar waveguides and LPGs (in fibers and waveguides). The availability of the new material – graphene – offers new application possibilities for LPGs. The project will investigate the light-graphene interaction in LPGs and experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of realizing graphene-incorporated LPG devices. The project will lead to a new class of graphene photonic devices based on LPG structures, which could be further developed into practical devices for application in optical communication, optical signal processing, and sensing. 石墨烯是由單層碳原子構成的二維材料，在電子器件方面已取得普遍應用。其特殊的光學特性，如電調諧吸收、極強的非線性、飽和吸收、高效螢光性等等，也使其在製作光子和光電子器件，如智能顯示器、觸屏、超高速激光器、光伏器件、發光器件、光探測器、光傳感器、光偏振器、光調制器等有望得到廣泛應用。探索石墨烯光學特性的各種應用已引起全世界的關注。 石墨烯光學器件可分為兩類：（1）波導器件 和 （2）非波導器件。在波導器件中，光沿著石墨烯的表面傳播，使光和石墨烯能夠在長距離相互作用。光偏振器、光調制器，以及一些光傳感器便是波導器件。而在非波導器件中，光垂直入射石墨烯，更有利於製作智慧顯示器和觸屏之類的器件。本項目致力於研究一個普遍適用於石墨烯波導器件設計的平臺。 本項目所研究的波導結構主要是由一個可以耦合到石墨烯層的長週期光柵組成。長週期光柵是一種寫於光纖或平板波導的週期性結構，它可以使特定波長的光從光纖或波導的芯層耦合到包層。當在包層傳播的光接觸到石墨烯時，任何調制石墨烯吸收的機制都會影響到光的傳播，從而影響到光柵的傳輸特性。這種帶石墨烯的長週期光柵結構可以用於設計各種器件，如光調制器、濾波器、偏振選擇損耗補償器、以及各式各樣的傳感器。 項目負責人擁有超過15年的長週期光柵的研究經驗，以及更長時間的波導設計經驗。香港城市大學已具有平面波導和長週期光柵（在光纖和波導上）的製備條件。石墨烯作爲新材料將賦予長週期光柵新的應用。本項目將會研究光與石墨烯通過長週期光柵的相互作用，並用實驗演示帶石墨烯的長週期光柵結構作爲器件設計平臺的可行性。本項目將會開拓一系列基於長週期光柵結構的石墨烯光學器，而這些器件經過進一步開發後有望在光通信、光信號處理和光傳感等領域得到實際應用。

11202014.label: Realisation of objectives
11202014.value: All the project objectives have been addressed and achieved. The studies involved can be grouped into the following four topics: (1) Study of the optical models of graphene (Objectives 1 and 4) We compared the three optical models of graphene found in the literature (the isotropic model, the anisotropic model, and the interface model) and provided measurement data based on our graphene-embedded multimode slab waveguides to verify their accuracies. Our results confirm that the interface model is the preferred model, which is not only accurate but also computationally efficient. Since then, we have applied this model to the design of all the graphene-incorporated fiber and waveguide structures studied in this project, whether the structures contain LPFGs or LPWGs. (2) Study of graphene-based optical fiber devices (Objectives 1, 2, and 3) Equipped with the correct model of graphene, we carried out a series of theoretical studies on graphene-based fiber structures, which included graphene-attached microfibers, graphene-wrapped microfibers, and graphene-covered D-shaped fibers. In particular, we studied the effects of graphene on the cladding modes of a graphene-wrapped fiber for the development of LPFG devices and sensors. On the experiment side, we developed the technique of wrapping graphene onto a fiber and characterized graphene-induced losses to the cladding modes excited by LPFGs. We demonstrated a sensitive and robust graphene-coated LPFG interferometer for the sensing of ammonia gas. Our proposed structure can serve as a generic platform for the development of new fiber sensors and devices that incorporate 2D materials. The operation principle based on the interaction of the cladding modes of a fiber with 2D material could be explored for various bio-chemical sensing applications. More recently, we successfully demonstrated an efficient low-loss externally pumped all-optical switch with a graphene-wrapped fiber interferometer based on the photothermal effect of graphene. Our switch offers many distinct advantages compared with those based on the same principle reported by others. (3) Study of graphene-based optical waveguide devices (Objectives 4, 5, and 6) We successfully developed a skill of embedding graphene into a polymer optical waveguide. With our understanding of the optical properties of graphene, we proposed and demonstrated several highly effective mode filters with graphene-embedded optical waveguides, which could find applications in mode-division multiplexing systems. Recently, we demonstrated a thermo-optic switch based on a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with buried graphene electrode heaters. Our fabricated devices show that the switching power obtained with graphene electrodes is almost four times lower than that obtained with aluminum electrodes, and the response of the device that uses graphene electrodes is also faster. We also proposed an electro-optic lithium-niobate LPWG mode converter using patterned graphene electrodes. The use of graphene electrodes can do away with the buffer layer and, thus, reduce the driving voltage of the device. For our experimental device, the driving voltage achieved with the graphene electrodes is lower than that achieved with the conventional aluminum electrodes by almost three times. The use of graphene electrodes can significantly enhance the efficiency of electro-optic devices and potentially reduce their fabrication cost. We also made an attempt to realize a graphene-covered LPWG for the sensing of ammonia gas. Because of the short length of the graphene coating on a waveguide, however, the sensitivity of the device is far lower than that achieved with our fiber ammonia-gas sensor mentioned in (2). In addition, we demonstrated all-optical control of the graphene-induced absorption loss based on the Pauli blocking effect with graphene-buried polymer waveguides and clarified the polarization dependence of the Pauli blocking effect. Our findings are important for the future development of all-optical modulators. (4) Other related studies We experimentally demonstrated an LPFG sensor coated with hydrogel for the measurement of the pH value of a solution and an LPFG sensor coated with enzyme-entrapped gel for phenol detection in liquid. This sensor configuration can be further developed by incorporating graphene into the structure. In addition, we designed and fabricated a Cu-coated surface-plasma-resonance (SPR) waveguide for the measurement of refractive index. This SPR structure could serve as a platform for the design of graphene-based waveguide sensors. In collaboration with Hong Kong Baptist University, we demonstrated a nano-functionalized LPFG sensor for rapid label-free detection of the carbonic anhydrase-IX (CA9) monoclonal antibody, a diagnostic biomarker in hypoxia condition cultured carcinoma cells. These studies can be considered as extensions of the original ideas proposed in the project.

11202014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202014.value: This project has generated many fruitful results. The major findings and research outcome are listed below: (1) We have compared three optical models of graphene (the isotropic model, the anisotropic model, and the interface model) with experimental data obtained from multimode slab waveguides and confirmed that the interface model is the preferred model [J1]. We have applied the interface model to the analysis of graphene-incorporated waveguides [J4],[J7],[J9] and microfibers/D-shaped fibers [J10]. (2) We have proposed the idea of exploring the cladding modes of a graphene-wrapped fiber for sensing application, where the cladding modes are excited by LPFGs [C5]. With this idea, we have demonstrated a sensitive ammonia-gas sensor built with an in-fiber LPFG Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated with graphene [J5],[C6]. (3) We have demonstrated a highly efficient low-loss all-optical switch based on an externally pumped graphene-coated fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer [J8]. This switch offers many distinct advantages, compared with reported switches based on the same principle. (4) We have demonstrated effective ultra-broadband mode filters with graphene-embedded waveguides [J4],[C2]. Such mode filters could find wide applications in mode-division-multiplexing systems. (5) We have proposed the idea of using graphene electrodes to reduce the driving voltage of electro-optic devices and experimentally verified our idea with lithium-niobate LPWG mode converters [J7]. Our experimental device shows a reduction of the driving voltage by almost three times. (6) We have proposed the idea of using buried graphene electrodes to reduce the power consumption of thermo-optic waveguide devices and experimentally verified our idea with polymer waveguide mode switches [J9]. Our experimental device shows a reduction of the power consumption by almost four times. (7) We have demonstrated all-optical modulation of the graphene-induced loss in a graphene-embedded polymer waveguide based on the Pauli blocking effect and clarified the polarization dependence of the effect [C7]. The findings are important for the development of all-optical control devices. (8) We have demonstrated several LPFG sensors for biosensing applications. Depending on the material coated on the LPFG, the fiber sensor can be used to measure the pH value [J3],[C3], the phenol concentration [C4], and specific proteins [J6]. Our fiber pH sensor offers the widest dynamic pH range ever reported. (9) We have designed and fabricated a Cu-coated surface-plasma-resonance (SPR) waveguide for the measurement of refractive index [J2],[C1]. This SPR structure could serve as a platform for the design of graphene-based waveguide sensors. (10) The main results in the project are summarized in a keynote talk at an international conference [C8].

11202014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202014.value: We have gained much new physical insight into the optical properties of grapheme from the projet, which can help us develop more powerful devices and sensors with graphene-incorporated fiber and waveguide structures in the future. We are the first to propose and demonstrate the idea of burying graphene into a waveguide to increase light-graphene interaction. Our in-house polymer-waveguide fabrication technology allows a graphene film with controllable length and width to be embedded at any location inside a waveguide. Such a graphene-embedded waveguide structure could be further explored for the realization of devices with enhanced performance, such as ultra-broadband optical modulators and all-optical switches. The excellent adsorption property of graphene also promises many potential sensor applications. New sensors with enhanced functionality could be developed by incorporating graphene into surface-plasmon-resonance waveguide and fiber structures. Our initial results along this direction are quite promising. Our pioneering studies on the use of graphene electrodes in electro-optic and thermo-optic devices could revolutionize the way of realizing such devices that traditionally rely on metal electrodes.

11202014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202014.value: Being a single layer of carbon atoms, graphene has found numerous applications in electronic devices. The unique optical properties of the material have also promised a wide range of applications in the realization of photonic devices. There is world-wide interest in exploring the optical properties of graphene for various applications. The primary objective of the project is to explore the optical properties of graphene to form graphene-based fiber and waveguide devices and sensors, with particular emphasis on the use of long-period fiber grating (LPFG) and long-period waveguide grating (LPWG) structures. By carrying out a detailed study of the optical models of graphene, new insight into the optical properties of graphene has been gained, which has led to the proposal of a number of novel fiber and waveguide devices and sensors. The graphene-based devices demonstrated in the project include a robust LPFG-based ammonia-gas sensor, a low-loss externally pumped all-optical fiber switch, several ultra-broadband mode filters, an efficient electro-optic LPWG-based mode converter, an efficient thermo-optic mode switch, and an all-optical waveguide loss modulator. Many of the ideas demonstrated in the project have the potential to be further developed for the realization of new devices and sensors with enhanced performance and functionality.

11202314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202314.value: Frameless (bolt-type) glass systems are widely used in modern workplaces to provide better work environments, but the fire hazard they pose is a deep concern. There are at least three problems that have not been addressed. The first is the thermal response of the glass panes, including the possibility of ignition under the non-uniform high radiative heat fluxes present in big fires. The upper parts of the vertical glass panes will be exposed to higher heat fluxes in a fire, creating different thermal stresses. The second problem is the thermal performance of the entire system including the glass panes, gel, framework edges and accessories. The third problem is the possibility of a glass pane falling and creating a larger opening, allowing air from adjacent areas among stored combustibles to fuel a bigger fire and allow more smoke and fire to spread to nearby areas. In the proposed project, these fire hazard problems will be investigated using normal and fire-resistant glass. Samples of two common normal glass panes and two fire-resistant glass panes with intumescent interlayers will be selected for in-depth exploration. Thermal response, including the mechanical performance of the glass panes and other parts of the glass systems, will be investigated experimentally and through mathematical modelling. Small samples will be tested under different radiative heat fluxes in a cone calorimeter in both horizontal and vertical directions to obtain the surface temperatures and stress distributions, facilitating an assessment of the possibility of igniting the glass pane sample and to identify the possible cracking mechanisms. Medium-scale experiments on a typical glass pane (1 m by 0.5 m) will be carried out with a thermal radiator developed to emit higher heat fluxes at the upper level of the glass pane. The effects of changes in items such as the thermal decomposition of glazing gels on glass surface temperature and hence the resulting thermal stress will be studied. Full-scale burning tests on part of a typical modern glass workplace will be conducted. Mathematical models of heat transfer in glass exposed to fire and changes in mechanical states, including thermal stress, will be combined with the experimental results to arrive at an integrated understanding of the fire hazards of frameless glass systems in modern workplaces. Finally, the heat removal rate achieved by applying water in protecting the glass panes through spray cooling will also be investigated. 为了提供更理想的工作环境，现代工作场逐渐广泛采用无框（螺栓型）玻璃系统。但这种系统带来了值得深切关注的火灾隐患，其中有三个问题并未引起足够重视。第一个是玻璃板的热响应，包括玻璃暴露在大火灾引起的不均匀高辐射热通量及点燃其他包含可燃物的可能性。垂直玻璃板的上部暴露在更高的热通量辐射下将会在整个玻璃板上产生热应力差。第二个问题是整个系统包括玻璃板。凝胶的热性能，框架的边缘和配件等的热工性能。第三个问题是火灾中玻璃窗格可能脱落而产生一个更大的分裂开口。通过开口的空气流通增大而燃烧更多可燃物，从而导致更大的火。同时，烟气和火焰也可通过开口蔓延到附近的其他区域。 本项目将分别使用普通型和防火型玻璃研究上列的这些火灾问题。研究用样品分别选用两种常见的普通玻璃板和两种带膨胀夹层的防火玻璃板。通过实验和数学建模，对玻璃板和玻璃系统的热响应，包括机械性能等进行研究。使用锥形量热仪对小型样本进行检测。在水平和垂直方向上赋予不同的辐射热通量条件，分析样本的表面温度和应力分布。根据结果评估得出玻璃板可能的点火温度及裂解机。对于典型的玻璃窗格（1.0米乘0.5米），将通过中尺度试验进行研究。将玻璃板上部暴露在利用热辐射器产生的较高的热通量中，研究凝胶的热分解玻璃表面温度的影响，以及由此而产生的热应力影响。在一个典型的玻璃结构现代工作场所中的一个区域内，将开展全尺寸燃烧试验研究。结合实验结果和玻璃暴露在火中的热传导数学模型以及包括热应力变化在内的机械力学变化数学模型，可以对现代工作场所无框玻璃系统的火灾危险性有一个整体认识。最后，本项目将考察用于冷却保护玻璃的水喷淋系统的除热率。

11202314.label: Realisation of objectives
11202314.value: Glass panes are commonly installed as walls, floors and ceilings in modern workplaces. As dense urban areas in the Asia-Oceania areas have offices storing a high amount of combustibles, big fires of long duration have been reported. The big fire hazards associated with this type of glass system was studied in this project conforming to the three objectives stated in the GRF proposal. In objective 1: To study the cracking of glass panes whose surfaces are exposed to different heat fluxes, and whether the glass can be ignited under high radiative heat fluxes due to big fires. The effect of temperature gradient components on the cracking behavior of glass panes under thermal radiation was studied first. A series of experiments and ANSYS finite-element simulations were performed for float glass panes with one side exposed to heat. The thermal boundary conditions of the unexposed side of the glass pane were varied by putting different materials, including brass, steel or tempered glass behind it. Temperature development, temperature gradient components across the thickness and in planar directions, cracking behavior and stress were comprehensively investigated. The temperature gradient component across the glass thickness was found to be much larger than those in planar directions and would change with the thermal conditions of the unexposed side. However, the increase of stress and hence the cracking behavior of glass panes is mainly determined by temperature gradient components in planar directions under thermal conditions similar to those in the present study. The transient temperature fields and the corresponding stress fields in glazing of different thicknesses with one side exposed to heat radiation was then studied. Based on the results of investigation, the criterion of critical temperature difference in cracking prediction was formulated. Glass samples of different thicknesses were tested under the same radiation exposure. Besides, a transient two-dimensional heat transfer model was proposed to obtain the transient temperature fields in the glass samples. In addition, the temperature fields were input to ANSYS for calculating the thermal stress fields. It is found that in the initial heating period, the maximum stress was mainly caused by the temperature gradient component across thickness and the stress value was larger for thicker glazing. As time evolved, the maximum stress was gradually dominated by the temperature gradient component along the planar direction. Thus, for thick glazing under strong heat flux of big fires as encountered in this part of the world, thermal bending stress caused by temperature gradient across thickness should be calculated to evaluate the cracking time. For other conditions, cracks will result from the stress caused by the temperature gradient along the planar direction, and the criterion of critical temperature difference is applicable for cracking prediction of glazing in any thickness. In objective 2: To study the thermal performance of the entire frameless glass system including the glass panes, gel and accessories for modern glass workplaces. Radiative heat transfer in a rectangular enclosure with a two-layer thermal structure was analyzed using a neural network based approach. Results show that the heat transfer depends sensitively on the three-dimensional geometry, the inhomogeneous and non-isothermal mixture condition within the enclosure, and the non-grey spectroscopic properties of the medium. The effect of the system parameters such as geometric dimensions, mixture concentration, and temperature are nonlinear and cannot be readily correlated by simple closed form analytical models. The engineering correlations commonly used are shown to be not so effective. Based on the aforementioned work, measured data was compared with modelling predictions and with other results of the mechanical or thermal performances of glass reported in the updated literature. The integrity of glazing elements exposed to big room fires was then studied using the new method. A new expression to determine the location and time of thermal cracking of frameless glazing was derived. Thermal stress was calculated based on typical temperature distributions of glazing exposed to big room fires. Simple expressions of the maximum stress were derived. Experiments of frameless glazing exposed to heat radiation were carried out to verify the applicability and accuracy of the obtained expressions. Furthermore, the concept was applied to study fire attack on composite structures with fiber reinforced polymer composites. In objective 3: To study the heat removed by water applied to cool the glass panes. Cooling one side of a glass pane by a water curtain can protect frameless glass systems in modern workplaces. The water curtain was discharged from a sprinkler system during a big room fire. The water layer acts as a thermal barrier to insulate thermal radiation against both outdoor fires and indoor fires, and to carry away heat so as to lower glass temperature. Rate of heat removal by water was studied. It is observed that glazing of a frameless glass system can be protected under appropriate water flow rate and pressure of the sprinkler system. Activation time of sprinkler is also an important parameter. Based on the study, two other points are proposed to be investigated: 1. As glass panes can be protected by applying a water curtain, integrating it with the thermal storage water wall system (WWS) can protect the glass panes of modern workplace against big fires. In addition, the water stored in the WWS can act on the fire or prewet the floor and walls upon breakage of the glass pane exposed to fire with higher temperature. This idea was put in drafting another project on the possibility of integrating the WWS in protecting glass panes under big fires. 2. Glass panes integrated with green plants can provide a better indoor environment with lower energy use. Green feature can reduce exterior surface temperature of building glass facades. The annual cooling energy consumption is also reduced. More importantly, this design would facilitate better heat removal by spraying water to give a wet porous medium with appropriate plants. The fire protection concept can be achieved by integrating glass panes with vertical greenery system.

11202314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202314.value: The fire hazards of frameless glass systems under big fires in modern workplaces were studied. The flashover room fire scenario in the room-corridor structure of a typical modern glass workplace was studied. The hot smoke and flames acting on the glass wall were simulated by fire models. Thermal radiation in flashover fires was investigated thoroughly. Radiative heat transfer in a rectangular enclosure with a two-layer thermal structure was studied by the neural network approach. The heat transfer was found to depend strongly on the three-dimensional geometry, the inhomogeneous and nonisothermal mixture condition within the enclosure, and the non-grey spectroscopic properties of the medium. Thermal performance of glass pane under fire was also studied. As reviewed on glass and associated fracture, glass temperature profiles on the glass pane were identified to have three stages. The first stage is rapid heating up, the second stage is steady heating up and the third stage is removing a certain amount of heat. Different glass temperature variations at the surface for these three stages were obtained by experimental measurements in a cone calorimeter. Three sets of partial differential equations on heat balance were set up. These three equations were then applied to study the heating up of glass in the modern workplace under big fires. Furthermore, the heat removal rate achieved by applying water in protecting the glass panes through spray cooling generated by a sprinkler system was investigated. A new fire protection design for modern workplace with glass was proposed by integrating with water wall system, and vertical greenery system. A total number of 5 journal papers were published, 1 journal paper was submitted for consideration to publish and another journal paper on water cooling is being drafted. Four of the journal papers appeared in journals in the first quartile (Q1) in Science Citation Index (SCI). These are Applied Thermal Engineering, Construction and Building Materials, and Energy and Buildings. The other two journals are in SCI Q3, they are AIAA-Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer, and Fire and Materials. All of the results of the three objectives were also compiled to draft practical design guides on achieving fire-safe frameless glass for modern workplaces, in consultation with the Authority.

11202314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202314.value: Architectural features with large glass panes for facades, partition walls, floorings and ceilings would be very hazardous under big fires with long duration. Based on the achieved results on studying fire behaviour of glass panes, different fire protection measures for modern glass workplaces can be evaluated. Practical design guides will then be drafted on the provision of fire-safe frameless glass for modern workplaces. Water cooling of glass panes by sprinkler is confirmed to be feasible to protect the glass system. Applying a water layer would give a thermal barrier to insulate thermal radiation against both outdoor fires and indoor fires. This concept would be further extended to integrate with the thermal storage water wall system to protect the glass panes. A project “A Study on Fire Protection Scheme of Glass Panes with Water Wall System” was drafted and funded by Research Grants Council – General Research Fund using the results on water cooling of this project. Integrating green façade with glass panes would be another feasible fire protection scheme for further development.

11202314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202314.value: The present project focuses on the fire hazards of glass panes used in buildings. Fire hazards of frameless glass systems in modern workplaces were studied in three areas. The first is the thermal response of the glass panes itself. The second is the thermal performance of the entire system including the glass panes, gel, framework edges and accessories. The third is the heat removal rate achieved by applying water layer on the glass panes. Thermal response, including the mechanical performance of the glass panes and other parts of the glass systems, was investigated experimentally and through mathematical modelling. The surface temperatures and stress distributions of glass panes were obtained. Possible cracking mechanisms of the glass system were then studied. Burning tests on part of a typical modern glass workplace were conducted. Mathematical models of heat transfer in glass exposed to fire and changes in mechanical states were combined with the experimental results to arrive at an integrated understanding of the fire hazards of the glass systems. The efficacy of protecting glass panes against fire via employing a water layer supplied by a sprinkler system was also investigated. These results are important in drafting guidelines for using glass panes in buildings.

11203714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203714.value: A networked dynamic system, which consists of a group of subsystems connected via a communication network, can be used to describe many practical control systems such as networked mobile robots, networked micro-satellites, teams of unmanned aerial or underwater vehicles, and so on. A key advantage of networked dynamic systems is that they are scalable, robust to local subsystem failure or communication failure, and able to carry out much more complex tasks than a single subsystem. Due to this advantage and their great potential in military and industrial applications, cooperative control of networked dynamic systems has attracted increasing attention in control community. Lots of efforts have been devoted to study on cooperative control of networked dynamic systems and significant progress has been made. However, the recent literature review reveals that there are still many issues to be addressed. For example, one issue is how to deal with cooperative control of heterogeneous networked systems with more general subsystem dynamics which might be subject to different disturbances and/or uncertainties, as most of existing works consider homogeneous networked systems with simple subsystem dynamics subject to neither disturbance nor uncertainty, which might not be the case for many practical applications. Another issue is how to deal with various communication constraints of networks such as packet dropouts and time-delays which would naturally arise in networked dynamic systems and are known to have great adverse impact on their performance. This project, by addressing those issues, will investigate and develop novel approaches and methodologies for cooperative control of heterogeneous networked dynamic systems subject to disturbances and/or uncertainties with communication constraints. The outcomes of this project are expected to provide more design tools for cooperative control of networked dynamic systems with high potential in real applications. 网络化动态系统由一群通过网络实现相互通信的子系统组成，它可用于描述许多实际的控制系统，例如：网络化的移动机器人和微型卫星；编队无人机以及无人潜水器。网络化动态系统的主要优点有：系统是可扩展的；对于局部子系统故障或通信故障具有鲁棒性；可以完成一些单个子系统无法完成的复杂任务。正是由于以上优点以及它们在军事和工业界的巨大应用前景，网络化动态系统的协同控制在控制界开始受到越来越多的关注。经过许多人的努力，网络化动态系统的协同控制研究取得了巨大进展。然而，回顾已有文献我们发现仍有许多问题有待解决。例如，如何处理由具有更一般动力学行为的子系统组成的异构网络化动态系统的协同控制问题，且考虑系统可能存在不同扰动或者不确定性。目前大多数的研究主要基于同构的网络化动态系统，系统中的子系统动力学行为一般比较简单，且大多未考虑系统存在的扰动或者不确定性，这样的系统可能无法符合实际应用。另一方面，如何处理网络通信中存在的诸如丢包和时延等许多约束条件，这类约束条件通常会出现在网络化动态系统中且常给系统性能带来不利影响。通过解决以上问题，本研究项目将提出新的方法以解决通信约束条件下存在各种扰动和不确定性的一般异构网络化动态系统的协同控制问题。研究成果有望为网络化动态系统的协同控制提供更多的解决方法，并具有极高的潜在应用价值。

11203714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203714.value: We have investigated cooperative control of heterogeneous networked dynamic systems subject to different disturbances, uncertainties, and/or communication constraints. We have developed a number of novel approaches. The key idea is to embed an internal model for each agent such that the embedded internal models achieve consensus for the leaderless case or track the leader for the leader-following case respectively. Then with the help of output regulation theory, distributed cooperative control schemes are designed such that the output consensus of heterogeneous networked dynamic systems subject to disturbances and uncertainties can be achieved. We have considered both fixed and time-varying topologies. Furthermore, we have investigated cooperative control of heterogeneous networked dynamic systems subject to different communication constraints. A number of novel distributed control schemes have been developed. The proposed approaches have been applied to typical mobile robotic systems and the simulation results have demonstrated their advantages over the existing approaches.

11203714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203714.value: It has been found that structured disturbances can be rejected with the help of output regulation theory and that unstructured disturbances would result in practical consensus in the sense that some tracking errors would exist when time goes to infinity. It would be interesting and desirable to investigate whether it is possible to achieve perfect consensus in the presence of unstructured disturbances and how to achieve it if possible. This could be one future research topic.

11203714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203714.value: A networked dynamic system can often be used to describe many practical control systems such as networked mobile robots, networked micro-satellites, teams of unmanned aerial or underwater vehicles. Due to their advantages over single systems and great potential in military and industrial applications, cooperative control of networked dynamic systems has attracted increasing attention in control community. This project has investigated cooperative control of heterogeneous networked systems subject to different disturbances, and/or uncertainties, and/or communication constraints which often arise in practical applications. A number of novel distributed control approaches have been developed. The outcome of this project is expected to enrich theoretical foundation on analysis and synthesis of networked dynamic control systems, and, in turn, the proposed approaches will provide control engineers in practice with more and/or better analysis and controller design tools. These approaches are also expected to have wide application in practical networked dynamic systems such as formation control of multiple mobile robots, attitude synchronization of multiple micro-satellites, flying control of unmanned air vehicles, and so on.

11204014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204014.value: 對手繪圖進行基於數據驅動的三維理解方法

11204014.label: Project Objectives
11204014.value: To design a new data-driven technique for inferring 3D shapes and structures from freehand drawings which possibly express an object with multiple parts or a scene with multiple objects, with minimal user intervention. To segment input drawings into multiple components that represent semantically meaningful parts or objects (sketch segmentation). To recognize the classes of the segmented components (sketch recognition). To reconstruct the 3D shapes and structures, which faithfully respect the input drawings (reconstruction). To apply our technique to various applications such as sketch-based retrieval and sketch-based 3D modeling.

To recognize the classes of the segmented components (sketch recognition).

11204014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204014.value: Sketching provides a natural way to depict complex shapes and express ideas. Various techniques have been proposed to support sketch-based 3D modeling, which has rich applications for example in the fields of education, engineering and design. It is well known that human perception relies on both visual rules and visual memory for sketch understanding. However, to date, sketch-based interfaces based on the concept of visual memory has been largely unexplored, though it has a unique ability to infer highly detailed models from simple, rough sketches. The very few existing solutions simply use a database of part or models, akin to visual memory, and pose the problem as sketch-based shape retrieval. A user needs to sketch individual components one by one, which are integrated into final models or scenes. Such approaches require either explicit or implicit sketch segmentation, enforcing artificial restrictions on the user and thus disallowing the same freedom provided by pencil and paper. A considerable amount of user effort is thus required to create models with complex structures. In addition, since they independently process individual sketched parts or objects, their performance is highly sensitive to the quality of individual strokes, demanding frequent user intervention and disallowing a seamless sketching experience. In this project we will explore a new data-driven approach to semantic 3D interpretation of freehand drawings. We aim at an automatic part-assembly process with respect to input hasty sketches, which depict a 3D object or a 3D scene of objects. We intend to place as few constraints as possible on the way a user draws, for example, no restrictions on the drawing order of strokes or the segmentation of sketched objects. This requires us to solve three challenging problems: segmenting freehand drawings into semantically meaningful components, recognizing the classes of individual components, and reconstructing the underlying shapes and structures. To address the significantly increased ambiguity level, we propose to use a repository of shapes composed of semantically segmented components with labels as visual memory, and solve these interdependent problems by heavily exploiting not only local shapes of individual parts but also their relative geometric configurations exhibited in the shape repository. We will show that our technique will benefit various applications, which rely on sketch-based shape retrieval and/or modeling. We believe that our work will take an important step towards human-like understanding of 3D shapes and structures in freehand drawings or images. 草圖繪製提供了一種很自然的方式來描述複雜形體或表述想法。基於草圖的三維建模已經有多種方法，並且已被運用到教育、工程、設計等領域中。眾所周知，一般人是通過視覺規律以及視覺記憶來詮釋草圖。然而，儘管視覺記憶能使得從粗略的草圖中恢復出具有較多細節的模型，迄今為止很少有基於草圖的界面使用到了視覺記憶。 僅有的幾個與視覺記憶相關的方法簡單地使用一個部件庫或者模型庫，然後把問題轉化為基於草圖的形狀檢索問題。這些方法要求用戶對需要的部件進行一個接著一個的草圖繪製，然後把它們合成成為最終的模型或場景。所以這些方法需要顯式或者隱式的草圖分割，這個對草圖繪製強加了一些本不必要的約束，使得用戶不能自由地進行草圖繪製。用戶需要不少的額外交互來創建具有複雜結構的模型。另外，由於各個部件或者物體是被獨立處理的，這些方法的成效就很取決於草圖中各個線條的質量。 在這個項目中我們會探索一個全新的基於視覺記憶的方法來理解手繪圖中隱含的三維信息。 我們的基本想法是通過一種部件組合的過程而不是直接使用單個部件本身來逼近輸入的草圖。我們的目標是對草圖繪製過程加盡可能少的約束。比如，我們不想限制筆劃的繪製順序，也不需要對草圖進行預分割。這就要求我們需要解決至少三個有挑戰性的問題：把手繪圖分割成有語義的部分，識別出每個部分的類別，重建出對應的幾何和結構。相對於以前的相關問題，我們要解決的問題的歧義性更加嚴重。為此，我們會不單只使用一個模型庫，而會同時假定模型庫中的模型已經有語義的分割，並且有已知的部件類別。使用這樣的數據庫來作為視覺記憶可以幫助我們有效地解決相互依賴的幾個問題。我們不僅會利用模型庫各個部件本身的形狀信息，更會去挖掘部件之間的幾何和結構關係。 在完成基本方法的實現後，我們會把它用到不同的應用中，比如基於草圖的形狀檢索和建模。我們相信這個工作會對做到像人一樣進行手繪圖的三維理解邁出重要的一步。

11204014.label: Realisation of objectives
11204014.value: We have achieved all the objectives. We started the project by preparing a database of 3D models with pre-segmented parts and their labels. Given a freehand sketch depicting an object with the same class as the 3D models, we developed a data-driven approach for segmenting the sketch into semantic components and inferring their labels (Objects 1 – 3). Our first attempt ([Journal 1] in Part C) was a fully geometric data-driven approach based on the idea of part assembly. This approach was the first to deal with part-level segmentation and labeling of freehand sketches, and achieved reasonably good segmentation and labeling accuracies. However, it takes several minutes to segment a single sketch, and is thus not suitable for interactive applications. Inspired by the success of deep learning technologies for various applications, we revisited the same problem by successfully developing a fast solution based convolutional neural networks [Journal 5]. Our segmentation and labeling algorithms assume the category of an input sketch is given and is the same as the pre-segmented 3D models in the training data. While the problem of sketch recognition has been well studied, existing solutions have focused on the recognition of individual sketches, which are often ambiguous to recognize. We proposed to recognize a sketched object in context of other objects, and presented a novel context-based approach [Conference 5] for sketch classification (Objective 3). The contextual information was extracted from a large-scale image dataset due to the lack of a large-scale collection of sketched scenes. Reconstructing 3D shapes and structures from input drawings (Objective 4) is challenging due to its ill-posed nature. We addressed this challenge in the following perspectives. In [Journal 2], based on line drawing decomposition (a problem similar to sketch segmentation (Objective 2)), we presented a progressive 3D reconstruction algorithm for planar-faced manifold objects. In [Journal 6], we explored how to anchor 2D strokes in 3D by exploiting the linear or planar structures of a reference 3D model on and around which 2D strokes are drawn. We showed such reference 3D models could be obtained by structure-oriented shape retrieval with the input 2D sketch as the query [Conference 1]. We also successfully demonstrated how to use the planar structures of a real-world scene to facilitate 3D sketching in mobile Augmented Reality [Conference 6]. The idea in [Journal 6] has been further extended to use an RGB-D image acquired by a consumer-level depth sensor as the reference to lift 2D sketches into 3D for sketch-based 3D prototyping. Finally, by using a richer set of 3D models and their corresponding line drawings as the training data, we successfully trained a deep learning network to infer plausible normal maps from single sketches [Conference 3]. Such normal maps can be used for 3D shape reconstruction. We applied the above developed techniques to various applications. Once an input sketch is segmented into semantic parts, we may easily achieve sketch-based part assembly. The proof of concept was given in [Journal 1]. With the efficient deep learning based solution, we showed it is possible to first segmenting a sketch into semantic components and then constructing a 3D model by assembly-based modeling in real time [Journal 5]. The part-assembly approach used in [Journal 1] was successfully adapted to address data-driven typeface synthesis [Journal 3] and cross-class 3D object synthesis [Journal 4]. Following our successful solutions for 3D interpretation of 2D sketches by using 3D models, we extended this idea to use videos for bringing motion into 2D sketches and presented a video-driven dynamic deformation of static drawings [Conference 4].

11204014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204014.value: Semantic understanding of freehand drawings is a challenging problem due to the limited information in drawings, different levels of abstraction, and their various drawing styles. In this project we showed data-driven approaches provide a promising solution to this problem. We focused on specific tasks and demonstrated the effectiveness of data-driven approaches for sketch segmentation [Journals 1, 2, and 5], sketch recognition/classification [Conference 5], and sketch reconstruction [Journal 2; Conference 1]. We showed that a single 3D model or a single raw RGB-D image already contains rich 3D information, which can be exploited for anchoring 2D strokes in 3D [Journal 6; Conference 1] and sketch-based modeling of swept surfaces [Conference 2]. When a similar idea is adopted in the temporal domain, we are able to extract and transfer motion in videos to static drawings [Conference 4]. By using more data, we are able to develop algorithms with better generalization ability for sketch segmentation and labeling [Journals 1 and 5] and sketch-based normal map generation [Conference 3]. In the middle of the project, deep learning technologies were proved effective for various image understanding problems. We successfully adopted well-known deep learning models including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) and demonstrated their effectiveness for sketch segmentation [Journal 5] and normal map recovery from sketches [Conference 3]. The project led to in total 12 publications, including 6 journal papers and 6 conference papers. The following papers were presented at the top conferences and/or published in the top journals in the fields of computer graphics and human-computer interaction (the rankings below are based on Google Scholar Metrics; as of 31 March, 2019): - Journal 1: in ACM Transactions on Graphics (the best journal in the graphics field); presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2014 (SIGGRAPH and SIGGRAPH Asia are considered as the best graphics conferences); - Journals 2 and 6: in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (No. 2 in graphics); - Journal 3: in Computer Graphics Forum (No. 3 in graphics); - Conference 2: in ACM UIST (No. 4 in HCI); - Conferences 4 and 6: in ACM CHI (the best HCI conference).

11204014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204014.value: For our data-driven sketch segmentation and labeling techniques [Journals 1 and 5] and normal map generation algorithm [Conference 3], we assume the category of an input sketch is known. Although we successfully improved the accuracy of sketch classification by using a context-based approach [Conference 5], how to more accurately recognize individual sketches is still an important but challenging problem to tackle. Existing deep learning solutions for sketch recognition have achieved impressive performance and outperformed techniques based on hand-crafted features. However, they mainly extended classification algorithms from the image domain to the sketch domain, and simply considered input sketches as binary images. We suspect exploiting the unique information, e.g., the temporal information of strokes using Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), can further improve the recognition accuracy.

11204014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204014.value: Sketching provides an efficient way to communicate complex ideas between people. Teaching machines to understand sketches as human beings do benefits various applications based on sketch-based interfaces. However, due to the limited information in an input sketch, semantic understanding of freehand sketches is often challenging. In this project we explored novel solutions for high-level sketch interpretation by extracting and using prior knowledge in existing data, which can be a single 3D model, a RGB-D image, a video, or a collection of 3D models. We successfully developed multiple data-driven solutions for the tasks including sketch segmentation and labeling, sketch classification, sketch reconstruction, sketch animation, and sketch-based 3D modeling. Our data-driven solutions are either purely geometric or based on the recent development of deep learning. The major findings of this project have been published in top venues of computer graphics and human-computer interaction. We believe that we have taken an important step towards semantic interpretation of freehand sketches and that our findings will be inspiring for the follow-up works in this area.
