11204114.value: 大型項目的發展正日益變得非常複雜。施工的成本是大型項目的最顯著的屬性。超大型項目是有超過十億美元造價,表示在實現項目目標時有更多的風險: 一般較長工期（超過三年），顯示更多的社會，技術，經濟，環境和政治上的挑戰和性能的各種風險。他們的特點是複雜的收購策略和配送方式，如合同類型，定價，招標，評估和補償的方法分配締約雙方之間的風險等等. 儘管發展過程中所面臨的挑戰，項目業主和金融機構繼續投資是冒著被超過進度和預算的高風險項目等款項。隨著全球化的迅速增加，面臨的共同挑戰是如何整合社會，技術，經濟，環境和政治不確定性，為管理決策貫穿於如此大的生命週期項目。雖然一定程度的成本和進度的不確定性是非常複雜的，問題就變成怎麼能預測，這些不確定性的金融和進度的影響，並採用緩解策略，以限制其影響。 在今天的追求，實現更強的項目績效，有需要有“新東西”而有效的工具和技術來準確地預測和管理從外部項目宏觀風險環境的觀點。因此，本研究旨在開發一種新的方法來管理風險對於大型項目的開發，在基礎上，英國標準風險管理施工階段實務守則（BS31100：2008執業風險管理 - 規範; BS ISO31000：2009風險管理 - 原則和指導方針和BS EN31010：2010風險管理，風險評估技術）。 在過去的6年中，我們的研究團隊完成了5資助項目*這創造了大量的數據集施工安全與風險評估大型建設項目。基於再過1年的試驗通過訪談研究**的這個建議，定性數據來自個案研究收集進行了電車網絡項目@愛丁堡（2012-13）。主要調查結果和分析在這種情況下，會出現為啟動政府和當地合作夥伴的重要數據有一個深入的了解的風險環境建設大型項目。這樣的理解是進一步貫徹落實至關重要有效的措施，以確保未來的發展方向是正確地創建一個更具吸引力環境，所有利益相關者，以避免項目延期和成本超支。 進一步改善現行的風險管理過程的性能，它被證明的分析網絡法（ANP）和系統動力學（SD）的方式方法是利用在研究以支持風險-英國標準的30風險管理技術管理。 ANP和統計處會在年底的援助項目中所提出的新的綜合方法管理人員加強主動風險評估，決定建設過程中制定過程大型項目。這種新方法將涵蓋廣泛的項目管理需求，通過解決系統性問題的影響力和主導大型項目的結果。這將保證正確的風險管理以及項目的最高價值回歸。

11204114.label: Realisation of objectives
11204114.value: Policy 1 – Improve Training As part of the basic skills requirement in the construction industry, Training is identified to be a major contributing factor to a decent worker environment on construction site. According to Marín and Vargas-Malpica (Marín and Vargas-Malpica 2014), training is a tool to securing improvement in occupational safety and health. Usually, a large proportion of unskilled workers are prone to unsafe deeds and conditions compared to their skilled counterparts. As the construction project proceeds, proper and effective training will exposure acts and conditions that are hazardous to health so that they can be reduced. Therefore, formal training and skills testing would be very important in improving behaviours on construction sites and as well as creating awareness of the dangers involve in unsafe acts and conditions on sites (Ludhra 2014). The International Labour Organization (ILO 2001) recommended that companies could initiate joint training schemes with social partners to inject additional skills into the informal training system and to streamline apprentice training to enable added solution to safe site training problem. According to ILO (2001), such training could be short courses and other programmes relevant to new techniques that could help to upgrade the skills of workers in general. Policy 2 – Improve Supervision The second policy is to improve the supervision on site. With better supervision and regular inspections, safety hazards can easily be identified on the project sites. Also proper monitoring can be used to promote safe work practices when all protection and safety systems are in place. These practices will help to enact prompt remedial actions and as well as to improve site safety conditions and effective worker commitment to lessen unsafe acts. Also, supervisors who occupy positions in construction operations and serve critical link between management and the workforce can plan, define work, manage, resolve conflicts between crew members, communicate with and motivate workers to perform within acceptable levels to improve productivity on site (Orando 2013). Therefore, it is the responsibility of the supervisor to ensure that good construction practices are enforced within specifications and standards. This requires clear thinking and quick onsite decision making strategies. Based on the outputs of the safety model simulation, the dynamic simulated pattern indicated in Figure 6 reveals that a rise in effective supervision will enhance understanding of all parties involve on the job site and eventually will reduce unsafe acts and conditions on site. Policy 3 – Combination of Policies 1 and 2 Policy 3 is a combination of policies 1 and 2. In order to check the effectiveness of implementing these two policies, the effectiveness of safety training and supervision need to be raised by a certain percentage. The reason behind this is that, improvement of knowledge flow will positively affect safety understanding of employees and at the same time increase supervision. In addition, better supervision will also improve site condition for all parties.

11204114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204114.value: Increase in unsafe acts and conditions on construction sites increases accidents and worker injuries. This study using the system dynamics approach to identify the factors which affect safety performance and describe their impact. At the end, to evaluate safety policies based on the result of the system dynamics model. The model was developed based on the assumption that the provisions for good health and safety conditions through effective management actions such as safety budget allocation, effective coordination and communication will sum up to increase understanding, commitment to safety practices and enhanced supervision to reduce unsafe practices on site. Additionally, goal discrepancies as a result of unsafe act and conditions on site will be reduced when safety training increases to create awareness and understanding of the challenges of negative acts on site. Increasingly, the study revealed that large proportions of the workers who are unskilled are prone to unsafe acts and unsafe conditions compared to skilled workers. As such, provisions of welfare facilities and occupational health and safety measures will have significant impact on workers‟ outputs and project goals. If safety facilities are improved, full realisation of workers attitude to work in construction will increase to achieve accelerated progress. The commitment resulting from project managers to safety conditions coupled with workers‟ understanding of the company’s policy and site safety practices can optimise fraction to maximise productivity and project’s desired goals. Although provision of safety training for workers is unlikely to happen in a highly casualized labour system, training schemes such as short courses for all operatives can eventually reduce unsafe acts and practices in order to minimise accidents and injuries. Alternative policies could be formulated and defined so as to implement an optimum ratio for employees and subcontractors’ commitment to safety practices on site. This will underpin management desired goals on safety and maximise workers health and conditions. With the application of system dynamics model for analysis and formulate preventive policies, the adopted safety management approach can regard as resilience system and ultimately achieve a higher standard of site safety via earning the benefit of resilience engineering. This study also proved that the concept of resilience engineering can further develop in the construction safety aspect via the use of system dynamics technology. Resilience engineering provides a new direction for construction safety improvement which will have positive contribution for the whole safety management system.

11204114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204114.value: Given the exploratory nature of this research, a qualitative approach was used in data gathering followed by dynamic modelling. In order to accomplish the objectives of this study, relevant academic journals and literature on construction safety published by the Health and Safety Executive were first reviewed to identify the factors which affect safety performance in construction site. Thereafter, an exploratory interview was conducted with experienced construction professionals on the attitude of workers toward safety on sites. The personnel contacted were project managers, site managers and project engineers and were asked to describe safety behaviours of workers in various site activities they were involved in. More names and addresses of interviewees can be obtained through personal contacts and others through published materials, such as list of Top Building Contractors disseminated by the Chartered Institute of Building, UK or HK. Based on the safety information obtained from the interviewees, a system dynamics model based on resilience engineering will be built with Vensim DSS software to describe the impact of the identified factors on safety performance.

11204114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204114.value: The construction industry is noted for its poor safety record when compared with other industries. Factors such as unsafe design, perilous acts and bad site practices can cause safety related issues and accidents in many construction sites. Where the project is a commercial asset, these accidents usually have significant impact on the completion time of the project as well as the estimated returns on investment over the operational phase of the project. Understanding the dynamics of specific factors that affect safety performance from the perspective of Resilience Engineering (RE) can thus be very crucial in designing containment measures to deal with their likely impact on construction projects. RE is a new approach to provide tools for proactive safety management (Woods 2006). RE can help the adopted site management better detect where hazards may be released, better handle the boundary beyond which work is no longer safe, recover if control is lost, and finally to minimize the effects if loss of control is irreversible (Schafer et al. 2009). Through the combination of literature review and interviews, different factors of unsafe acts and practices on construction sites were first identified. The identified factors were then modelled with a System Dynamics (SD) framework to appraise their measured impact on construction projects. The aim of the paper is to investigate the dynamics of the factors that affect safety performance and to formulate practical policies needed to improve such performances on construction sites. Some of these factors include ‘project goal discrepancy’, ‘safety attitude & behaviour’ as well as ‘company safety policies’. The result discloses that the need for robust safety culture, effective training program and proactive safety awareness are the most effective policies for improving exiting safe site conditions.

11204414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204414.value: Shape memory gel (SMG) is one of the most interesting hydrogels which can remember its original shape, keep the temporary deformed shape at low temperature and recovers to the original shape spontaneously by heating. Many thermo-mechanical models have been proposed to describe the shape memory behavior of SMGs in dry state. However, very little work has been done on SMGs in wet environment in which SMGs are soft with predominant water, and a thermo-chemo-mechanical coupled large-deformation commonly occurs. Hence, the proposed project aims to develop a constitutive theory for the thermo-chemo-mechanical coupled large-deformation and a meshless numerical technique for modelling the response of SMGs in wet environment. In order to provide a comprehensive insight into the mechanism for shape memory effect, this research will conduct experimental, theoretical and numerical investigations on the multi-field coupling behaviours of SMGs. First, a series of experiments on a representative SMG will be conducted at different temperatures and chemical environments for the quantitative characterization of the multi-field responses. Secondly, based on the experimental data, a coupled thermo-chemo-mechanical constitutive theory for large deformations will be formulated to characterize the response of thermally actuated SMGs within the framework of thermodynamics; the material parameters appearing in our constitutive model will be calibrated using the stress-strain data from the compression experiments. Thirdly, a numerical technique which is suitable for the large deformation analysis will be developed by implementing the developed constitutive model into the meshless method. Finally, representative experiments will be conducted to validate the predictive capability of the proposed theoretical model and its numerical implementation in complex three-dimensional geometries of SMGs. It is worth noting that, so far, relatively little work on the constitutive theory and numerical simulation of hydrogels with shape memory effect was reported in literature, and the proposed research will result in a constitutive model for the thermo-chemo-mechanically coupled large-deformation and a mesh-free numerical technique for the design of more complicated SMG-based structures and devices. 形状记忆凝胶能记住它的原始形状。在低温环境下能保持临时的变形性状，加热后又可恢复初始形状。目前，已有许多热-机模型用来描叙记忆凝胶在干躁环境下的形状记忆特征，但却很少见到在潮湿环境下的相关研究。在潮湿环境下，由于水的作用，形状记忆凝胶会变软，从而在热-机-化学耦合作用下产生大变形。 因此，本项目拟建立一个本构理论用来描叙形状记忆凝胶的热-机-化学耦合大变形，并应用无网格数值模拟方法模拟状记忆凝胶在潮湿环境下的响应。首先，在不同的温度和化学环境下，通过一系列的实验获得多场作用下的量化特征。其次，在实验数据的基础上提出一个耦合的热-机-化学本构理论描叙热激励下的响应，其中的材料常数将通过应力-应变压缩试验来确定。第三，在本构分析的基础上，建立一个适合于大变形分析的无网格方法。最后，通过实验验证所提出的理论模型，并用该理论模型分析形状记忆凝胶的大变形。

11204414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204414.value: 1. An effective meshless method is obtained, and the final discrete equilibrium equation is achieved for the large deformation analysis of hydrogels. In contrast to the non-interpolating meshless methods, the shape function in the meshless method satisfies the property of Kronecker function, and thus the proposed meshless method can apply the essential boundary conditions directly. Therefore, the expressions of matrices in the meshless method are more concise, resulting in a higher accuracy and efficiency. 2. A constitutive relation of ordinary state-based peridynamics is developed by incorporating cohesive effect into the original constitutive relation of quasi-brittle materials. Thus, an effective peridynamics model, which is a meshless method, is obtained for the investigation of crack growth in quasi-brittle materials. Using the proposed peridynamics model, the damage and arbitrary crack propagation in quasi-brittle materials can be spontaneously predicted without re-meshing or crack- tracking approach. 3. An experimental technique is obtained to build soft material and metallic bistable disks with high load-bearing capabilities. The stable configurations of the proposed bistable disks can be conveniently designed using a conventional nanotechnique for improving material properties. Mechanical tests are carried out to validate the proposed experimental technique.

11204414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204414.value: An effective interpolating complex variable meshless method is proposed for the large deformation analysis of shape memory hydrogels (SMG), in which the essential boundary conditions can be applied directly with higher accuracy and efficiency. Through analyzing the transformation of nine samples of a square hydrogel, the samples with different shapes and initial sizes of holes have diverse deformation patterns with the increase of chemical potential. The study of this project is highly significant for the design of multistable devices through extending to the bistable analysis of soft materials. Currently, we are extending the project to the broadband energy harvesting by using bistable SMG plates with integrated piezoelectric layers.

11204414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204414.value: As a new type of emerging soft active materials, shape memory (SM) hydrogels are stimuli-responsive materials that can be deformed and fixed into a temporary shape and have the ability to recover the original shape in response to external changes. This phenomenon is known as the SM effect. SM hydrogels have many biomedical or sensory applications, such as smart medical devices, implants for minimally invasive surgery, or heat shrinkable tubing and films. Despite the potential applications of such smart structures, a comprehensive understanding of their coupled thermo-chemo-mechanical behaviors is still in its infancy. An effective meshless method is proposed for the large deformation analysis of SM hydrogels. Based on the developed meshless method, different samples with elliptical, circular and square holes in a square hydrogel are simulated for the pattern transformation. The numerical results indicate that the shapes and initial sizes of holes in hydrogels lead to different pattern transformation rules, actuating behaviors and area reductions of holes. By utilizing above findings, the hydrogel has the potential to actuate the soft machines, control the flow as a soft valve and make a transparency adjustable window if researchers design reasonable shapes and izes of holes in a square hydrogel.

11204514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204514.value: A networked system (NS) is a system consisting of spatially distributed intelligent agents to monitor physical or environmental conditions, such as temperature, sound, pressure, etc. and to cooperatively transmit their data through the network. Each agent is small, inexpensive and can be easily deployed over a vast region. The application of NSs has been widely seen in many real-world engineering systems including wireless sensor networks, and distributed robotic systems. Efficient communication among agents is the key for NSs to strive the whole system towards a common goal in a collaborative fashion. However, in most cases, agents are equipped with limited batteries (or energy resources) supply. In particular, when NSs are used for critical tasks such as military or power system applications, it is unfeasible to recharge or replace the battery due to the hostile environment. Therefore, avoiding unnecessary energy consumption becomes more of a concern. It is highly desirable to exploit effective protocols to save the communication cost as much as possible. Recently, event-triggered control has been proposed as an alternative approach to the more traditional periodic execution of control tasks. On the premise of guaranteeing desired levels of performance, event-based schedule aims at decreasing the system's unnecessary execution behaviour and therefore saves cost as well as resources. Hence, this makes event-triggered control particularly useful in the collaborative framework. Although event-triggered control has already stirred quite a lot research attention, the distributed behaviour of the networked systems does bring some essential difficulties in controlling performance and reliability issues. The open problems include the development of a set of distributed event-triggered control techniques, establishment of a quantified relation between energy consumption and system performance, as well as the design of a cooperative framework for estimation or control in networked systems with distributed event-triggered communication protocol. This proposal has set up three new, challenging yet achievable objects to the theoretical investigation, algorithm development and practical applications of networked systems using event-triggered control strategies. The proposed research would have both theoretical and practical significance in advancing analysis technologies of networked complex systems. 分布式网络系统是由多个智能个体所组成的，用以协作收集信 息与监测温度、音量、压强等物理环境。由于组成分布式网络系统的的智能个体都能被应用到很广泛的领域，因此，分布式网络系统已经频繁出现在很多工程实际中，比如无线传感网络、分布式智能系统。众所周知，智能个体之间通信的有效性在利用分布式网络系统的实现协作目标时极其关键。然而，在多数情形下，智能个体都是由有限容量的电池驱动，特别是当网络系统被应用到军事或是能源领域时，在恶劣环境下，替智能体重新充电或是更换电池变得不可行。所以，如何减少电源的消 耗以及探求有效的通信方式变得尤为重要。 最近，网络系统中的事件驱动控制已经被证明是一种有效的替代控制方式。这是 由于在保证需求性态的前提下，采用事件驱动的控制方式能减少系统的不必要的运行姿态，也能节省资源的消耗。因此，基于事件驱动的控制在协作控制中变得特别愈加有效。尽管事件驱动控制已经吸引了众多的研究目光，然而在性态控制以及稳定性需求方面，如何在分布式网络系统中有效的使用事件驱动控制来达到协作目标依然存在很多困难，比如：如何设计分布式事件驱动控制，如何平衡资源消耗以及系统性能需求，同时还有如何采用分布式事件驱动控制进行网络系统估计？在这个提案中，三种新的极具挑战的目标被提出来用以完善事件驱动控制策略的理论研究、算法设计以及实际应用。这意味着，这个提案中的研究在网络复杂系统的分析中更具理论和实际使用价值。

11204514.label: Realisation of objectives
11204514.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: Several event-triggered schemes have been investigated in this project and significant results are summarized as follows : (i) Various event-triggered schemes for networks with different structures In [1], it investigates the leader-following consensus for multi-agent systems with general linear dynamics by means of event-triggered scheme (ETS). We propose three types of schemes, namely, distributed ETS (distributed-ETS), centralized ETS (centralized-ETS), and clustered ETS (clustered-ETS) for different network topologies. All these schemes guarantee that all followers can track the leader eventually. It should be emphasized that all event-triggered protocols in this paper depend on local information and their executions are distributed. Moreover, it is shown that such event-triggered mechanism can significantly reduce the frequency of control’s update [1]. (ii) Distributed edge event-triggered scheme A new distributed edge event-triggered (DEET) scheme of multi-agent systems via a common buffer to reduce unnecessary update of controllers induced by fast information transmission. The edge scheme avoids a synchronous phenomenon in previous node event triggered (NET) mechanism, in which the triggering of one agent activates information transmission of all edges linked with this agent. Hence, the NET scheme leads to unnecessary update of control algorithm while the DEET provides a new approach without sending out information synchronously, that is each edge sends out information independent from the other nodes [2]. (iii) Event-triggered schemes for networks with different layers A Layered Event Triggered scheme (LETS) is developed for a multi-layered system. A two-layered multi-agent system is served as an example for investigation and the scheme can be extended to multi-layered hierarchical systems. The LETS emphasizes on synchronous information transmission in the same layer but asynchronous message update between different layers [3]. (2) Realization of Objective 2: (i) Investigation on the balance of energy consumption and system performance. As discussed in the first objective, in [1], three types of schemes, namely, distributed ETS (distributed-ETS), centralized ETS (centralized-ETS), and clustered ETS (clustered-ETS) for different network topologies. The Characteristics of each ETS are compared with the Network Toplogy, Network size and detector cost (see Table II in [1]). (ii) Performance of the system under event-triggering with disturbance [4] This work proposes an impulsive framework to analyze the effect of the clustered event-triggered information transmission on the dynamics of multiagent systems. Under this framework, we study three cases and propose different types of event-triggered protocols. (a) If agents’ states are available, a clustered event-triggered protocol based on agents’ states is designed, which guarantees all followers to track the leader eventually. (b) The above case in (a) is further investigated when the agents’ states are under disturbance. A modified event-triggered protocol is introduced to reach L∞ leader-following consensus. (c) For the case where agents’ states are not available, a clustered event-triggered observer-type protocol is developed based on the agents’ outputs. It is worth noting that Zeno behavior is excluded in these cases [4]. (3) Realization of Objective 3: (i) Applications: Sensor networks with lossy data and cyber-attacks An observer-based event-triggering consensus control problem is investigated for a class of discrete time multiagent systems with lossy sensors and cyber-attacks. The purpose of the address problem in [5] is to design an observer-based distributed controller such that the closed-loop multiagent system achieves the prescribed consensus in spite of the lossy sensors and cyber-attacks. The detail design for the distributed observers is to estimate the relative full states and the estimated states are then used in the feedback protocol in order to achieve the overall consensus. An event-triggered mechanism with state-independent threshold is adopted to update the control input signals so as to reduce unnecessary data communications. The success ratio of the launched attacks is taken into account to reflect the probabilistic failures of the attacks passing through the protection devices subject to limited resources and network fluctuations. By making use of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Laplacian matrix, the closed-loop system is transformed into an easy-to-analyze setting and then a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee the desired consensus. Furthermore, the controller gain is obtained in terms of the solution to certain matrix inequality which is independent of the number of agents. An algorithm is provided to optimize the consensus bound. (ii) Applications to synchronization in an array coupled neural networks In [6], under event-based mechanism, pinning cluster synchronization in an array of coupled neural networks is studied. A new event-triggered sampled-data transmission strategy, where only local and event-triggering states are utilized to update the broadcasting state of each agent, is proposed to realize cluster synchronization of the coupled neural networks. Furthermore, a self-triggered pinning cluster synchronization algorithm is proposed, and a set of iterative procedures is given to compute the event-triggered time instants. Hence, this will reduce the computational load significantly. (iii) Switched-based system with disturbances and delays This paper in [7] investigates the finite-time and fixed-time stabilization (FFTS) of switched systems with discontinuous dynamics, external disturbances and delays. Firstly, a new parameterized discontinuous stabilizer is designed to ensure the FFTS of switched discontinuous systems in the sense of Filippov solutions. Secondly, a detailed analysis is provided on how to regulate the power parameters to determine the settling time is finite or fixed. Thirdly, a new adaptive controller is further designed to stabilize the considered system in a finite time, and the corresponding settling time is estimated as well. This work provides a fundamental approach on a finite/fixed-time of switched discontinuous systems. Although the finite/fix time approach are different from the event-triggered concept, they have the same goal to reduce the information transfer to achieve the objectives. This work provides some insight from a different aspect to the event-triggering project and proposes an alternative way to study triggering system in a switching sense to save energy. (iv) Fast sampling for multiple delta operator systems This paper in [8] considers the consensus problem for multiple delta operator systems. The delta operator system is used for describing continuous time processes at rapid rate sampling. Moreover, it has been known to have a better model description than that of shift-operator-based approach. Here, the consensus problem is first solved for multiple delta operator systems by using a distributed protocol. To achieve consensus, several important sufficient conditions are proposed for the fast sampling systems based on the parameters of sampling period and consensus strength. (v) Economic Power Dispatch in Smart Grids This paper [9] has investigated two second-order algorithms to solve the economic power dispatch problem in smart grids. Simulation results based on five-unit system, IEEE 30-bus system. This model will be used for event-triggered applications. (4) Overall Research Achievement: A total nine papers have been published to fulfill the objectives of the projects. During the research period, the PI worked with more than ten researchers from different institutes to complete the tasks. Different research ideas have been generated from different groups through discussions when they visited Hong Kong. The project is considered to be successful to realize all the objectives. In addition, one PhD student, Dr Wenying Xu, has been trained and she graduated in July 2016. Dr. Xu received the Chow Yei Ching School of Graduate Studies Scholarship from CityU in 2015. This award recognizes excellence in student research, intellectual creativity, originality, and quality of writing for research students. It is indeed a strong recognition for Dr. Xu outstanding performance in research through the support of this project.

11204514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204514.value: The project is completed smoothly and fruitful results are obtained. The above new results have been presented in different conferences. Eight papers have been published in journals. Most of them are considered as top rank journals including four papers in IEEE Trans on Cybernetic ([1],[3],[5]), one is published in IEEE Industrial Electronics [4], International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control [2], Neural Networks [6], Nonlinear Dynamics [7], System& Control Letters[8], IEEE Systems, Man and Cybernetics: Systems[9], respectively. The work related to communication delays, disturbances and zeno effects were investigated. The above work in [1-9] built up a strong foundation for studying various issues in multi-agent systems. Several event-triggered schemes(ETS) have been investigated in this project and some significant results are summarized as follows : (i) Various event-triggered schemes for networks with different structures are discussed in [1]. This is the first paper to compare distributed ETS and centralized ETS. A new model of integrating event-triggering with switching topology is also discussed. In addition, a new clustering ETS is also introduced. This leads to a new idea of layered event-triggered technique [3] which to be used in many multi-layered networks. (ii) It is known that node event-triggered (NET) scheme leads to unnecessary update of algorithm. The distributed edge event-triggered (DEET) developed in [2] has the advantage to avoid a synchronous phenomenon of sending out information. The DEET scheme of multi-agent systems is constructed via a common buffer to reduce unnecessary update of controllers induced by fast information transmission. Hence, the DEET provides a new approach without sending out information synchronously, that is each edge sends out information independent from the other nodes. This is the first paper to deal with edge event-triggered via using the a practical buffer along each edge. (iii) In [4], based in [1], an impulsive framework is developed to deal with disturbances issues. This is the first paper to introduce clustering ETS under the new framework. This leads to a new approach to solve the event-based networks with disturbances. (iv) Application/Extension of event-triggered schemes: (a) Observer-Based Event-Triggering Consensus Control for Multiagent Systems with lossy sensors and cyber-attacks Sensor networks [5]; (b) Pinning cluster synchronization in an array of coupled neural networks [6]; (c) Robust Stabilization switched-based network consensus with disturbances [7] have been investigated for finite/fixed-time cases. (d) Fast sampling protocol for multiple delta operator systems[8]. (e) The economic power dispatch problem in smart grids[9].

11204514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204514.value: The work can be further extended to safety issue when the multi-agent systems are under attacks. A new proposal has been approved on the secure estimation and control problems in 2017, and the project is in good progress. Another proposal has been submitted to UGC in 2017 Oct. The title is "Analysis of self-triggered estimation, control and optimization in distributed network systems". The proposal is further extended to self-triggered techniques which have not been fully investigated in this project. Further investigation on applications can be extended to cases on Event-based networks with communication delays and to design observer type event-triggered schemes. In addition, further new self-triggered schemes will be developed in our future work. To conclude, this project leads us in a great potential for further development of the research of event-based control and filtering design for NSs.

11204614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204614.value: 基于全纳米线电路的机械柔性和多谱段的红外中段光探测器阵列

11204614.label: Project Objectives
11204614.value: Develop the cost-effective synthesis technique to obtain composition- and bandgap-tunable InxGa1-xSb nanowires with the controlled crystal quality, diameters and length, surface morphology, structural and electronic properties. Fabricate and characterize single InxGa1-xSb nanowire field-effect-transistors, with different channel composition and dimension, as photoconductors for the high-performance, multispectral mid-infrared detection. This would provide the optimal nanowire condition as well as the corresponding spectral and dynamic responses for the photodetection of each infrared waveband. Utilize the nanowire contact printing scheme to heterogeneously integrate highly ordered and parallel arrays of optimized infrared active InxGa1-xSb nanowires and well-developed high-mobility In2O3 nanowires on plastics. This would interface the photodetector and electronic devices together to enable an all-nanowire circuitry with the on-chip integration, capable of detecting and amplifying infrared signals at each waveband with high sensitivity and precision. Construct and evaluate the ultimate performance limits as well as reliabilities of large arrays of nanowire photodetector circuitry with infrared imaging functionality. The aim is to achieve a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to realize the mechanically flexible and multispectral mid-infrared photodetector arrays based on multifunctional all-nanowire circuitry.

11204614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204614.value: 在过去的几十年里，红外探测器被广泛研究用于军事、通讯、分子光谱以及生物医学成像等科技领域。然而，由于高度透明的大气窗口（2到2.3微米）以及众多化学分子的强吸收（2.3到5微米），现有的研究集中在使这些探测器在红外中段（2-5 微米）具有更出色的性能、低耗、常温工作、机械柔性以及多谱段等特性。同时，纳米技术的发展也使得半导体纳米管、纳米线及纳米颗粒等具有独特的物理性质，比如，卓越的化学组分、带宽可调、机械弹性及稳健等性质，如此，就让开发应用于柔性和多谱段红外探测器的理想活性材料变得可能。举个例子，最近的研究表明锑基纳米线就可以用于红外中段探测器。这些探测器在室温下就展示出了优越的光导性能、好的稳定性、高的重复性以及让人印象深刻的光响应和量子效应等特性。然而，在纳米线可控合成、理解纳米线的基础性质、整合多功能纳米线阵列以及制造和确定光感应器电路矩阵的性能极限等方面上还存在重大的挑战。在这份计划书中，我们将着重尝试InxGa1-xSb纳米线体系为起作用的光导材料。这不仅由于InxGa1-xSb体系具有超群的电子输运性质，还由于在室温下，其带宽从0.17eV到0.72eV可调，也就是说，他们的对应波段从1.7到7.3微米连续可调，这就正好覆盖了整个红外中段区域。这样，我们的目的就是在塑胶上，利用最优红外活性的InxGa1-xSb和发展良好的高迁移率In2O3纳米线异质整合出高度有序和平行的阵列。使光探测器和电子器件链接在一起，实现全纳米线积分电路芯片，在每个波段上高灵敏和高准确的探测和放大红外信号。最后，我们将构建出大规模的纳米线光探测器电路阵列，同时评估他们的性能极限，从而得到多功能、低耗以及强有力的平台来实现基于全纳米线电路的机械柔性和多谱段的红外中段光电测器阵列。

11204614.label: Realisation of objectives
11204614.value: In this project, we have successfully accomplished all the objectives with 100% of completion. To be specific, we have achieved a new synthesis technique, known as solid-source chemical vapor deposition, to synthesize single-crystalline ternary InxGa1-xSb nanowires (NWs) with well-controlled chemical stoichiometry, geometries, surface morphologies, electrical and optoelectronic properties (Objective 1). For example, in order to synthesize InxGa1-xSb NWs with different chemical stoichiometry of In and Ga, InSb and GaSb powders in various mixture ratios (e.g. 10:1, 20:1, 30:1 and 40:1 in wt.%) are used as the precursor source. The chemical composition of the obtained NWs could then be evaluated by using energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), where they are found to be In0.15Ga0.85Sb, In0.22Ga0.78Sb, In0.09Ga0.91Sb, and In0.28Ga0.72Sb for the source mixture ratio (InSb:GaSb in wt.%) of 10:1, 20:1, 30:1, and 40:1, respectively. This slender variation of the NW composition indicates the robustness of the present CVD method in controlling the NW chemical stoichiometry, which is beneficial for assessing the NW composition dependent properties. Based on the transmission electron microscope (TEM) characterization, the average diameter of In0.15Ga0.85Sb, In0.22Ga0.78Sb, In0.09Ga0.91Sb, and In0.28Ga0.72Sb NWs are found to be very similar, with the values of 60 ± 10, 45 ± 10, 60 ± 5, and 57 ± 10 nm, accordingly, extracted from the statistics of more than 20 NWs for each sample group. Simultaneously, elemental mapping of the NW is also performed. It is obvious that the chemical constituents of In, Ga and Sb are distributed uniformly along both axial and radial directions of the NW, indicating the excellent NW composition homogeneity obtained in this simple growth. Notably, Au is only detected in the spherical tip region of the NW, which further confirms the catalytic vapor-liquid-solid mechanism employed here. At the same time, global back-gated NW FETs were fabricated with Ni as the source-drain electrodes. From the transfer (Ids–Vgs) and output (Ids–Vds) characteristic curves of a representative single In0.28Ga0.72Sb NW FET, respectively, it is clear that the drain-source current (Ids) decreases with the increase of gate voltage (Vgs), indicating the typical p-type conducting behavior of the NW. Importantly, the device also exhibits an impressive ON/OFF current ratio of 105 for Vds = 0.4 V. For a typical In0.09Ga0.91Sb NW transistor, when L is 4.2 um, NW diameter is 41 nm, gate capacitance is determined to be 0.26 fF for 50 nm SiO2 dielectric layer from COMSOL and peak transconductance is found to be 7 × 10-8 S for Vds = 0.1 V, then the peak mobility of the NW device can be calculated as high as 463 cm2V-1s-1. This mobility value is higher than the one of pure GaSb NWs, indicating the superior electrical properties of ternary III-V NWs, consisting with the behavior observed in bulk materials. It is also demonstrated that the mobility values of our In0.09Ga0.91Sb NW devices, regardless of the maximum and average values, are the highest among many others of III-V NW devices reported to date (Objective 2). Moreover, for the first time, our InxGa1-xSb NW photodetectors are demonstrated with the impressive photoresponse characteristics towards the near to mid-infrared, such as optical communication region at 1550 nm. As shown in the typical output characteristic with different illumination intensities of 1550 nm, the single In0.28Ga0.72Sb NW photodetector exhibits the increase of photocurrent with the increase of the illumination intensity at Vds = 2 V and Vgs = 0 V. Interestingly, it is observed that the IR response of those NW devices would enhance substantially when the In concentration of the NW device channel is increased accordingly, which can probably be attributed to the reduced bandgap as well as the enhanced absorption coefficient towards 1550 nm irradiation To further understand the photosensing characteristic of these NW detectors, the dependence of device photocurrent on different illumination intensities is measured. Similarly, several other key performance parameters, such as external quantum efficiency (EQE) and specific detectivity (D*), of the NW device can also be assessed. In this case, at a low incident intensity of 0.05 mW mm−2 and Vds = 2 V, the values of R, EQE and D* are determined to be 6000 A W−1, 4.8×106% and 3.7×109 Jones, respectively. These measured performance parameters are already comparable to those of the state-of-the-art III-V NW photodetectors (Objective 3). The good repeatability and fast response speed are also two important requirements for advanced photodetectors. It is obvious that the device on- and off-state can be effectively modulated by the chopped illumination, indicating the robustness and excellent stability of the device. A high resolution transient curve is measured to precisely determine the rise and decay time constants of the studied device. Here, the rise and decay time constants can be identiﬁed as 38 and 53 us, accordingly. In order to further demonstrate the feasibility of utilizing these NW photodetectors for the large-scale device integration, we employed the well-established NW contact printing and the same device fabrication procedure to achieve InxGa1-xSb NW parallel array FETs with impressive photoresponse characteristics in the 1550 nm regime, heterogeneously integrated with previously developed high-mobility In2O3 NW parallel arrays on plastics (Objective 3). When all these nanowires were fabricated into the photodetector circuitry with infrared imaging functionality, in particular, at a low incident light intensity of 0.05 mW mm−2 and Vds = 2 V, the values of R and D* are found to be about 4500 A W−1 and 5×108 Jones, respectively. As compared with the single NW photodetector, these R and D* values give a slight reduction, which is probably due to the improper alignment of the NW arrays, NW-to-NW variations, breakage of NWs as well as non-optimized electrical contact between NWs and electrodes. Anyway, ultra-fast response times, ranging between 30 to 50 s, are still observed for these integrated NW parallel array devices with significant output signal amplification. More importantly, while these flexible devices were performed with the bending test for 700 cycles with the radius of curvature down to 2.5 mm, the photocurrent still maintained over 90 %, indicating the excellent mechanical stability of these flexible devices (Objective 4). In the future, the photodetector performance can be further improved through the optimization of the NW parallel array density, alignment and channel length scaling, etc. In summary, we have developed a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to realize the mechanically flexible and multispectral mid-infrared photodetector arrays based on multifunctional all-nanowire circuitry.

11204614.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204614.value: In this project, there are several key findings, which lead to 9 high-impact journal publications (1 Nature Communications [under review], 2 ACS Nano, 1 Nano Energy, 1 Scientific Reports, 1 Advanced Materials Interfaces and 1 Nanotechnology, etc) as well as 8 invited presentations at different international conferences. In specific, as reported in ACS Nano 2017, using CMOS-compatible Pd catalysts, we demonstrated the formation of high-mobility ⟨111⟩-oriented III-V nanowires (like GaSb NWs) via vapor−solid−solid (VSS) growth through a complementary experimental and theoretical approach. In contrast to NWs formed by the conventional vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) mechanism, cylindrical-shaped Pd5Ga4 catalytic seeds were present in our Pd-catalyzed VSS-NWs. As solid catalysts, stoichiometric Pd5Ga4 was found to have the lowest crystal surface energy at the seed/NW interface for efficient epitaxial NW nucleation. These VSS characteristics led to the growth of slender NWs with superior electrical and optoelectronic device performances Once the high-quality III-V NWs are obtained, as reported in Advanced Materials Interfaces 2017, we developed a simple metal-oxide nanoparticle (NP) surface decoration approach onto the device channel in order to manipulate electrical and optoelectronic characteristics of III–V NWFETs. This was done through the manipulation of free electrons in the NW channel (i.e., InAs, InP, and ternary III-V) via depositing various metal-oxide NPs with different work functions. The versatility of our decoration scheme has also been illustrated through the realization of high-performance enhancement-mode NW-paralleled-arrayed devices as well as the configuration of highly efficient NW NMOS inverters. For the first time, we also obtained high-quality InxGa1-xSb NWs with high hole mobility and impressive photosensing characteristics in both visible and infrared regimes (Nature Communications, under review). For example, the NWs show impressive photodetection performance in the IR optical communication region (1550 nm). For the optimized In0.28Ga0.72Sb NW devices, they show excellent broadband photodetection performance in room temperature, especially with the excellent responsivity of 6000 AW-1, high external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 4.8×106 % and short response time of 38 μs under IR illumination (1550 nm) at a bias voltage of 2 V. This efficient response represents one of the fastest responses among all NW IR photodetectors reported in the literature. These NWs can as well be fabricated into NW parallel arrays based sensor devices for next-generation, ultrafast and efficient room-temperature IR photodetectors. In summary, all these major findings are significant, which would bring forward the deployment of ternary InGaSb NWs for high-performance next-generation IR imaging detectors.

11204614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204614.value: Although there are many significant findings produced from this work, there are still several major areas required for the further study of these mechanically flexible InGaSb NW mid-IR photodetector arrays. For example, the quantum efficiency of fabricated detectors is known to be far smaller than 1 because of the reflectance of light, insufficient absorption of light attributable to the finite thickness of NW and anisotropic absorption of light arising from the one-dimensional geometry, etc. Also there are many carrier traps for NWs due to the large surface-to-volume ratio of NWs. All these would dictate the performance limit of detectors. Therefore, it is necessary to enhance their quantum efficiencies and to adopt any effective surface passivation scheme to minimize all the trap states on the device channels. Another one is to further explore the operation of these flexible devices in extreme conditions, such as high-temperature, high humidity and others, since there will be lots of advanced applications like Internet of Things (IoT) requiring high-performance and cost-effective IR photodetector arrays operated in the non-conventional manner. All these further works would push forward the substantial technological development of InGaSb NW IR photodetector arrays for practical utilizations.

11204614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204614.value: In the past decade, high-performance, cost-effective and mechanically flexible room-temperature mid-infrared photodetectors have been urgently required for various advanced technological applications. Nevertheless, the current infrared detector design and processing schemes all require high-temperature epitaxial and extreme chemical processing conditions, which are not compatible with flexible substrates. Fortunately, the advent of nanotechnology has facilitated unique properties of semiconducting nanowires contributing ideal active materials for the flexible photodetectors. In this project, we have successfully developed a hybrid and low-cost approach utilizing the bottom-up high-performance multifunctional InGaSb nanowire arrays with the conventional top-down device fabrication processes to achieve large-scale, heterogeneously integrated nanowire circuitry with the on-chip integration, capable of detecting and amplifying infrared signals at each waveband with high sensitivity and precision. For example, we have obtained the detector response speed down to microseconds, being one of the best records in the scientific community. Ultimately, we established a versatile and powerful technology platform to realize the mechanically flexible and multispectral mid-infrared photodetector arrays based on multifunctional all-nanowire circuitry.

11205014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205014.value: Due to ever increasing data size, many data owners choose to host their data in the cloud. Since the cloud server is not fully trusted, the privacy of the data becomes a major concern when outsourcing data mining services to the cloud. In traditional data mining systems, the data owner itself provides data mining services to the users and its privacy-preserving is only against the users. In the outsourced data mining, the cloud server plays the role of data miner, while it is not fully trusted. Therefore, the data owner needs to preserve privacy against both the cloud server and the users. Existing techniques for privacy-preservation, such as differential privacy, bucketization and result auditing, are based on mechanisms of adding quantized noise to the raw data or mining results. However, they are not strong enough to protect the privacy against the cloud server. The principal goal of this project is to investigate privacy-preserving issues in outsourced data mining. This project has three major tasks: 1) Design privacy-preserving algorithms for outsourced data mining in cloud. 2) Develop a measurement model to quantify privacy and utility of data mining algorithms. To protect data privacy, sensitive information is often removed or hidden from the raw data, which leads to the loss of data utility for data mining. There is no common model to measure the privacy or the utility of data mining algorithms. We plan to develop a measurement model that can provide quantitative analysis of privacy and utility for data mining algorithms. 3) Design tradeoff mechanisms between privacy and utility. Privacy and utility are the two contradictory metrics of data mining algorithms. It is important to strike the balance between privacy and utility. We plan to develop tradeoff mechanisms between privacy and utility for different data mining applications. 随着数据大小的日益递增，越来越多的数据属主选择将其数据寄存在云服务器上，同时通过云服务器提供对数据的挖掘服务。然而，由于云服务器不能完全被用户所信任，数据的隐私性将成为外包数据挖掘服务时所需考虑的主要问题。在传统的数据挖掘系统中，由数据属主亲自向用户提供数据挖掘服务，数据的隐私保护主要针对于用户；而在外包数据挖掘中，不可信的云服务器成为数据挖掘的执行方，因此，数据的隐私保护需同时针对于云服务器和用户。现有的隐私保护技术，如differential privacy， bucketization和result auditing， 都基于向源数据或者数据挖掘结果中加入适量的噪音，而这些技术都无法实现针对于云服务器的数据保护。本项目旨在研究外包数据挖掘中的隐私保护问题，包括如下三个主要研究任务：1）为外包数据挖掘服务设计隐私保护的算法；2）提出一个测量模型用以量化数据挖掘算法的隐私性和可用性。为了保护数据隐私，往往从源数据中将敏感信息删除或者隐藏，而这样会降低数据的可用性。目前尚未有一个普遍的模型来衡量数据挖掘算法的隐私性和可用性，本项目计划提出一个新的测量模型用以量化数据挖掘算法的隐私性和可用性；3）提出一个针对数据隐私性和可用性的折衷机制。数据的隐私性和可用性是数据挖掘算法的两个对立的指标，本项目将针对不同的数据挖掘算法研究这两个指标之间的权衡机制。

11205014.label: Realisation of objectives
11205014.value: This is a fruitful project. All three major objectives are fully achieved. We started with the investigation of general security requirements in smart homes and cloud computing environment. We studied the security threats of home network routers and proposed a bloom-filter based analytic framework to capture persistent threats towards the home routers and distributed home networks. This work is essential for the development of secured home networking systems. We also studies of the wireless SDN and Cloud Computing structures (which led two publications in IEEE Trans on Cloud Computing 2015 and IEEE Globecom 2016). Then, we focused on search over encrypted data, and operations on encrypted data. We first proposed a framework for similarity search on encrypted data by using generalized pattern matching method. Similarity search over encrypted data is a very difficult task, as two similar keywords in plaintext will produce totally different cypher-text. We developed a hash function that can hash similar plaintext keywords to the same bucket. This work was published in IEEE Infocom 2015. We further extended this thread of work to the privacy-preserving task matching for multiple task-publishers and multiple task-subscribers. One application for this problem is privacy preserving task-matching in CrowdSourcing systems, where task publishers encrypt the task specifications and the workers also encrypt their interests, and the system is required to match the tasks to the workers on encrypted data. We developed a privacy preserving task matching algorithm, which was published in IEEE Trans on Service Computing. We also developed a general framework for privacy preserving keyword based publish-subscribe services, which is published in Information Science in 2017. We also studied general operations over encrypted data. Distributed key-value stores have been widely adopted for search over encrypted data. However, they do not guarantee to provide strong protection of data confidentiality. We proposed an encrypted key-value store with secure rich query support, which encrypts data records with multiple secondary attributes in the form of encrypted key-value pairs, such that rich queries over encrypted data can be supported. This work was published in AsiaCCS 2017.

Existing techniques for privacy-preservation, such as differential privacy, bucketization and result auditing, are based on mechanisms of adding quantized noise to the raw data or mining results. However, they are not strong enough to protect the privacy against the cloud server. The principal goal of this project is to investigate privacy-preserving issues in outsourced data mining. This pro-ject has three major tasks: 1) Design privacy-preserving algorithms for outsourced data mining in cloud. 2) Develop a measurement model to quantify privacy and utility of data mining algorithms. To protect data privacy, sensitive information is often removed or hidden from the raw data, which leads to the loss of data utility for data mining. There is no common model to measure the privacy or the utility of data mining algorithms. We plan to develop a measurement model that can provide quantitative analysis of privacy and utility for data mining algorithms. 3) Design tradeoff mecha-nisms between privacy and utility. Privacy and utility are the two contradictory metrics of data mining algorithms. It is important to strike the balance between privacy and utility. We plan to de-velop tradeoff mechanisms between privacy and utility for different data mining applications.

11205314.label: Project Objectives
11205314.value: To develop and investigate effective selection strategy based on stable marriage model. In MOEA/D, subproblems and solutions can be regarded as two sets of agents. Selection of promising solutions for subproblems is thus to find a matching between subproblems and solutions. As discussed in [2], different preference setting methods can lead to different ways for balancing convergence and diversity. As a first and critical step, we will develop appropriate indicators to measure the convergence and diversity from both subproblem and solution sides. The classic marriage model used in [2] is likely to produce a matching that greatly favors the agents who make proposals. To maximize the profits of both subproblems and solutions, we will investigate and develop appropriate models to achieve an optimal stable matching that is unbiased to neither side. Furthermore, we will theoretically analyze the behavior and effectiveness of the proposed selection strategy. To develop and investigate effective methods to accommodate DM’s preferences. To assist DMs to select their preferred solutions, we will develop and investigate a reference point-based technique to accommodate DM’s preferences. DMs usually provide only a very limited number of reference points to represent their preferences. Therefore, the matching model, used for selection strategy, should be extended from a one-to-one matching to a many-to-one matching. At first, we will define metrics to measure the attractions between reference points and solutions, by incorporating DM’s preferences. Then, we will investigate and develop methods to find a stable matching, which fulfill some fairness criteria, between reference points and solutions. To develop and investigate effective mating scheme based on group matching model. We will develop a novel mating scheme to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation of the evolutionary search. Unlike the unisexual population used in the classic evolutionary computation, we will model the mating process in a bisexual style. It is to match each male solution with its preferred female solutions. At first, we will develop mechanisms to assign solutions with different genders (i.e., male and female). Then, we will define indicators to set the preferences of one gender over the opposite. These indicators should be able to measure the exploration and exploitation. Finally, we will investigate and develop appropriate group matching models (i.e., many-to-many matching) to find the mating pairs among the population.

11205314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205314.value: Evolutionary multiobjective optimization (EMO) is one of the most active research areas in evolutionary computation and multiple criteria decision making. Multiobjective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition (MOEA/D), which bridges the traditional techniques and population-based methods, has been widely accepted as one of the three major EMO frameworks and been successfully applied in various domains. However, a number of fundamental issues, such as 1) how to select solution for each subproblem, 2) how to handle decision maker (DM)’s preferences, and 3) how to mate parents for offspring generation, still need to be addressed before this approach can be widely accepted and used in industry. In principle, all these three issues can be regarded as matching problems, which are subproblem-solution, preference-solution and solution-solution matching, respectively. Stable matching theory, first proposed and studied in a Nobel Prize winning paper, can effectively resolve conflicts of interests among selfish agents in the market. In this research, focusing on the aforementioned three issues, we will develop and investigate EMO methodologies from the perspective of stable matching theory. Specifically, we will first develop a novel selection strategy, which assigns each subproblem with its appropriate solution, based on a stable marriage model (one-to-one matching) under certain fairness criteria. Then, we will extend the stable marriage model, used for selection strategy, from a one-to-one matching to a many-to-one matching, and apply it to accommodate DM’s preferences. Finally, we will develop a novel mating scheme, which can balance the exploration and exploitation of the evolutionary search, based on a many-to-many matching model. It is more general than the one-to-one and many-to-one matchings. In the long run, this research will bring a completely new approach for designing and analyzing EMO methodologies in a systematic and rational manner. Moreover, its significant impacts are not only limited to the developments of EMO, but also to the design and analysis of other evolutionary search methods, metaheuristics and even traditional optimization. In the meanwhile, its outputs will provide more powerful tools for real-life optimization problems. 进化多目标优化（EMO）是当今进化计算和多目标决策的最活跃的研究方向。 基于分解的多目标进化算法（MOEA/D）是一种被广泛采纳的三大主流EMO框架之一。 它将基于种群的方法和传统优化技术相结合，并被广泛应用于多个领域。然而MOEA/D本身仍有一些基础的问题有待解决。 例如，1）怎样为每个子问题挑选解；2） 怎样处理决策者的偏好信息；3）怎样选择交配个体产生下一代种群。从本质上说，所有的这三点均可被视为匹配问题，它们分别为子问题与解的匹配，偏好信息与解的匹配，解与解的匹配。2012年经济学诺贝尔奖所授予的稳定匹配理论能有效地协调市场中个体的冲突的兴趣取向。在本项研究中，我们将从稳定匹配的角度出发设计和研究EMO算法用于解决前面所提出的三个基础问题。具体而言，我们将首先设计一种新颖的基于稳定婚姻模型（一对一匹配）的选择策略为每一个子问题分配一个合适的解。然后，我们将这个稳定婚姻模型进行扩展，即从一对一匹配扩展成为多对一匹配，并将其应用于处理决策者的偏好信息。最后，我们将设计一种新颖的基于多对多的配对机制。它能有效的平衡进化搜索中的开采与勘探之间的平衡。这样的一种多对多模型将比一对一和多对一模型更加泛化。从长远来看，该项研究将为设计和分析EMO算法提供全新的系统方法。另外，它的深远影响不仅限于EMO的发展，更为设计和分析进化搜索方法，启发式方法，甚至传统优化方法提供了新思路。与此同时，该项研究成果将为实际优化问题提供更为强有力的工具

11205314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205314.value: We developed a unified paradigm, which combines dominance and decomposition-based approaches, for many-objective optimization. Our major purpose is to exploit the merits of both dominance- and decomposition-based approaches to balance the convergence and diversity of the evolutionary process which is related to objective 1 of this proposal. The performance of our proposed method is validated and compared with four state-of-the-art algorithms on a number of unconstrained benchmark problems with up to 15 objectives. Empirical results fully demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method on all considered test instances. In addition, we extend this method to solve constrained problems having a large number of objectives. Compared to two other recently proposed constrained optimizers, our proposed method shows highly competitive performance on all the constrained optimization problems.

11205314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205314.value: This work could further extended to many other evolutionary algorithm in the selection process such as NSGA and PSO. Further, more applications based on evolutionary algorithms could be beneficial to the outcome this work.

11205314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205314.value: The ideas of apply stable matching algorithms for evolutionary algorithm has been successfully explored in this project and the results are exciting. In fact, there are many real world problems are based on matching, thus, the use of stable matching to other applications can be further investigated. To the best of our knowledge, this is the pioneer work in applying stable matching in evolutionary algorithms and achieved good results. This is hope that the work could be continued in the future for further exploring the foundation of the theory as well as applications to other domains.

11205514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205514.value: 近年來，在醫療保健、醫藥開發（例如化驗和篩查）、環境監測、食品檢測、安保及其他領域， 對於可靠、快速生物探測器的需求正逐年增加。生物傳感器是一種利用生化受體（例如抗體、酶及DNA等）檢測特定物質的裝置。通過被檢測物與傳感器的交互反應，生化信息（例如濃度及物質種類等）被轉化為可測量的電信號。最近興起的碳基納米材料，如石墨烯，由於其比表面積大和極高的電子遷移率等優異特性而被廣泛的應用於生物傳感器中。石墨烯的優異性能對某些物的質檢測更快速及更靈敏。然而由於石墨烯在納米尺度和極其穩定碳碳鍵連接，大批量生產具有特定電學性質的石墨烯和在石墨烯特定位置上安裝生化接收分子變得極其困難。解決這些技術難題對於開發基於石墨烯的可靠、高靈敏度生物傳感器至關重要。 本項研究致力於研發一種新型的納米機器人操作系統來提高當前高靈敏度石墨烯生物傳感器的製造效率。實現這目標的方法包含三個核心技術：1）通過電泳技術方法選擇適合具有特定電學性質的石墨烯製造生物傳感器；2）利用基於納米探針的局部氧化技術在石墨烯特定位置製造缺陷點使加強生化接收分子與石墨烯連接；3）針對納米機器人操作平台，設計能夠精確控制缺陷點在石墨烯中位置的控制算法。 本項目提出的納米機器人操作系統可以在石墨烯表面直接實現納米尺度局部功能化。這些功能化的位點能提高生化受體與石墨烯之間的連接。更加重要的是，本操控系統使得在納米尺度精確控制生化接收分子在石墨烯表面的位置成為可能，從而提高了生物傳感器的靈敏度和選擇性。通過納米操控平台，基於功能化石墨烯的生物傳感器可以被高效製造。本項研究為未來實現基於微流體技術，進行多種物質實時、快速檢測的納米生物傳感器陣列平台提供了堅實的研究基礎。

11205514.label: Realisation of objectives
11205514.value: 1 The study on the binding of the linker molecules and graphene have been achieved. The surface functionalization of graphene with the aromatic molecule and organic solvents were systematically studied. The doping effects of these different chemicals on graphene are investigated carefully by monitoring the changes in Raman spectrum and the shift of Dirac point voltage of the G-FETs during the chemical functionalization process. The Fermi level shift of graphene is also estimated by these two methods. The results indicate that the PBASE imposes a p-doping effect on graphene because of its electron-withdrawing property while DMF and CH3OH impose an n-doping effect. Besides, CH3OH causes a smaller reduction in carrier mobility of G-FETs than DMF. This work provides a two-in-one method to explore the effect of both the solvent and aromatic molecule on graphene. 2 The study on the further functionalization of graphene with the bioreceptors have been achieved. Two different bioreceptors such as antibody and aptamer were employed to functionalize graphene. The functionalization processes were studied by electrical and atomic force microscopy measurements. Both antibody and aptamer imposed slightly n-doping effects on graphene. Moreover, the sizes of the two different bioreceptors were characterized by atomic force microscopy measurements, in which the sizes were about 5 nm for antibody and 3.6 nm for aptamer, respectively. 3 The study on developing the protocol for functionalization of graphene via LAO cutting for efficient immobilization between the bioreceptor and graphene and developing the control scheme for using the customized nanorobot to functionalize graphene and pattern the bioreceptor molecules on graphene precisely have been achieved. The LAO cutting was performed with AFM tip, on which the bias of -12 V was applied. The cutting directions includes horizontal and vertical directions. The average with of the created trench was about 200 nm. The influence of LAO cutting on graphene electric properties were carefully studied. Both horizontal and vertical cutting imposed n-doping effect on graphene due to the resultant negatively charged COO- group. For horizontal cutting, the hole carrier mobility increased due to the PMMA removal and the oxidation of graphene. For vertical cutting, the electric current decreased due to the lower efficiency of carrier transportation and collection. Finally, the linker and antibody were used to functionalize LAO cutting graphene for bacterial detection. The average response of horizontal cutting graphene was about 9.38 % which was larger than that of vertical cutting (5.56 %). 4 The investigation on the sensing capability of the functionalized graphene biosensors for detection of bacteria based on Bio-field-effect-transistor (Bio-FET) have been achieved. Antibody and aptamer were employed as the bioreceptors due to their advantages such as high stability and high affinity bacterial cells. The change of the carrier density in the probe-modified graphene due to the attachment of E. coli is discussed theoretically for the first time and verified experimentally. The binding of E. coli brings the negatively charged E. coli close to the graphene surface, increasing the hole carrier density efficiently in graphene and achieving electrical detection. The detection mechanism is ascribed to the E. coli induced electrostatic gating. The binding of negatively charged E. coli induces holes in graphene, which are pumped into the graphene channel from the contact electrodes. The devices showed a detection limit of about 102 CFU/mL of E. coli and exhibits good affinity towards E. coli (KD = 700 CFU/mL). Besides, the experimental results also indicated that either the antibody-modified G-FETs (ABG-FETs) or the aptamer-modified G-FETs (APG-FETs) exhibited excellent selectivity for E. coli over other bacteria strains. 5 The study on the optimization of the operation of Bio-FET for detection of bacteria has been achieved. The ionic strength of electrolyte and the gate voltage are regarded as two key parameters to affect the sensing performance of graphene biosensors. First, phosphate buffered saline (PBS) was used as the electrolyte to provide a liquid environment for the detection of E. coli. The concentration of the PBS affected the ionic strength which was related to the Debye length, which was identified as an important factor to affect the number of E. coli-induced carriers. High concentration of PBS (10 mM PBS) yielded a Debye length of 0.7 nm. When the Debye length was smaller than the height of sensing probes, no carriers were induced in G-FETs due to the electric-field screening effect. Systematic studies were conducted and the results demonstrated that the optimal concentration of PBS was 0.1 mM PBS. Enhanced efficiency was found in the shorter height of the aptamer, which facilitated the carrier generation process in G-FETs. Quantitative analysis of the carrier density induced by the bacteria was also explored. For antibody-modified G-FETs (ABG-FETs), the average estimated number of holes induced by per E. coli K12 was 1488. While for aptamer-modified G-FETs (APG-FETs), the average estimated number of holes induced by per E. coli 8739 was 2042. Second, the gate voltage-dependent carrier mobility of G-FETs was correlated to the bio-detection signal to provide better electrical response and lower detection limit. Higher carrier mobility suggests that the E. coli induced-carriers in graphene can be collected efficiently. The carrier mobility of G-FETs can be tuned by the gate voltage. Therefore, by optimizing the gate voltage, the carrier mobility can be maximized accordingly. For both ABG-FETs and APG-FETs biosensors, we experimentally demonstrated that the lowest detection limit was obtained at the optimized gate voltage that resulted in highest carrier mobility. The detection limit of 102 CFU/mL was achieved at the gate voltage of 75 mV by using the ABG-FETs and 40 mV by using the APG-FETs. 6 The theoretically study on the sensing mechanism of G-FET biosensors were modeled and simulated with COMSOL Multiphysics. The motion of the negatively charged E. coli particles in solution at different time, and the surface charge of graphene induced by charged E. coli were systematically studied. The relationship between source-drain current, graphene-bacteria distance, and bacterial concentration are established, in which the graphene-bacteria distance may play a key role in improving the sensing performance of the G-FET biosensors. We believe that the simulation of the G-FET biosensors could serve as a guideline for the design and optimization of G-FETs biosensors in various applications.

11205514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205514.value: 1. First, the functionalization of graphene via DEP and cutting for efficient immobilization between the bioreceptor and graphene and attaching the bioreceptor molecules on graphene precisely have been explored. The functionalization processes and their influence on carrier mobility of G-FETs were investigated [J2, C1]. Aromatic molecule (1-pyrenebutanoic acid succinimidyl ester, PBASE) acting as a linker was used to anchor sensing probes onto graphene surface. The cutting direction was found to affect the electric properties of graphene devices. For horizontal cutting graphene, the hole carrier mobility increased because of the graphene oxidation and PMMA removal during cutting process. For vertical cutting graphene, the electric current decreased because of the graphene oxidation. For bacterial detection using LAO cutting graphene, the horizontal cutting graphene exhibited better performance than vertical cutting graphene. 2. Second, two types of sensing probes, namely antibody and aptamer, were employed to achieve specific detection of E. coli [J1, C2] The ionic strength of electrolyte (phosphate buffered saline, PBS) and gate voltage were proven to be two important factors to affect the sensing performance. The ionic strength was affected by the concentration of the PBS, which was related to the Debye length. When the Debye length was smaller than the height of sensing probes, no carriers were induced in G-FETs due to the electric-field screening effect. Systematic studies demonstrated that the optimal concentration of PBS was 0.1 mM PBS [C3]. The carrier mobility of G-FETs can be tuned by the gate voltage to provide better electrical response and lower detection limit. Higher carrier mobility suggests that the E. coli induced-carriers in graphene can be collected efficiently. Therefore, by optimizing the gate voltage, the carrier mobility can be maximized accordingly. For both ABG-FETs and APG-FETs biosensors, the lowest detection limit was obtained at the optimized gate voltage that resulted in highest carrier mobility. The detection limit of 102 CFU/mL was achieved at the gate voltage of 75 mV [J2] by using the APG-FETs and 40 mV by using the APG-FETs. 3 Third, the operation of G-FET biosensors was modeled and simulated with COMSOL Multiphysics [J3]. The motion of the negatively charged E. coli particles and the surface charge of graphene induced by charged E. coli were systematically studied. The relationship between source-drain current, the size of sensing probe, and bacterial concentration are established, in which the size of sensing probe and the bacterial concentration affect the sensing performance of the G-FET biosensors.

11205514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205514.value: 1. The accurately controlling the functionalization sites on the graphene surface is needed, which can gain a better understanding on the interaction between graphene, aromatic molecules and solvent molecule. 2. More studies such as different cutting bias voltage, number of the created trench, length of the trench, and other cutting directions are needed to further investigate the influence on the electric properties on graphene. Precisely controlling the functionalization position to improve the sensing performance is another challenging topic. 3. Both antibody and aptamer have been proven to be the effective sensing probes for E. coli detection. However, the detection limit is still not good enough in the consideration of “zero tolerance” concept in clinical diagnosis and food testing, and the change of the electrical response caused by the binding of E. coli was still small. More efforts are required to furtherly optimize the operation of G-FETs to achieve larger response and single-bacterial detection. 4. More experiments are needed to explore the functional sequence in the aptamer and the binding sites on bacterial surface. Furthermore, all graphene devices for E. coli detection in this project were not reusable, which becomes a big barrier on the way to commercialization. Hence, developing reusable devices in bio-sensing is another challenge in the future works.

11205514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205514.value: To date, the most common approach method relies on culturing and counting method. Although it is reliable and accurate, the detection process is time-consuming and complicated which usually requires several hours to several days to obtain the results. New strategies for rapid pathogen detection such as bacteria are in urgent for food and water safety monitoring and early diagnosis of pathogen infections. This project focuses on graphene field-effect transistors (G-FETs) for rapid and electrical bacterial detection. Graphene, recently discovered nanomaterial, has many extraordinary properties such as high carrier mobility, large specific surface area and outstanding electric conductivity, which equips graphene with great possibilities in biosensors applications. The graphene channel is functionalized by the sensing probes (antibody and single-strained DNA), which is inspired by the high specificity and strong affinity between bacteria and sensing probe. Moreover, the sensing performance was optimized by analyzing ionic strength of electrolyte and gate voltage, which can affect the carrier collection efficiency in graphene and the signal output. Finally, modeling and simulation were performed to theoretically understand the operation of graphene biosensors for bacterial detection.

11206014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206014.value: Metastasis is closely related to 90 % of cancer-related deaths, which is well-known as a leading cause of death worldwide for decades. Metastasis includes multiple stages of the cancer spreading processes from a primary cancer region to non-adjacent parts in the patient’s body. While many of these metastatic stages such as invasion, intravasation and post-colonization have been studied extensively, a comprehensive understanding of the extravasation mechanism of the metastatic circulating tumor cells remains elusive. Extravasation is the metastatic process related to transendothelial migration of the circulating tumor cells into distant tissues/organs, and formation of angiogenesis/cell proliferation at the secondary sites. Up to date, there is still lack of representative models for emulating the extravasation in vitro. A major technical challenge is extraction of extravasated cells from the in vitro models, after the cells migrate to the matrix on the other side of the endothelium. These extravasative cells are widely believed to be more metastatic, yet this technical challenge has caused a hurdle for further studying of the extravasative cancer cells, on their spatial and transient cell responses and the molecular mechanisms involved. In this proposed research, we plan to develop a microfluidic device based on a unique fabrication process we recently developed for micro-patterning of biocompatible polymer (polydimethylsiloxane) membranes. This device facilitates the growth of well-aligned vascular endothelial layer on a highly porous membrane in a microchannel, and at the same time allows the migration of cancer cells under the necessary vessel microenvironment (e.g. extracellular matrix and shear stress under blood flow). A unique capability of this device is isolation of the extravasated cancer cells from the device outlets and hence a board range of cell analysis techniques can be applied subsequently for the detailed study on the cell characteristics. Given the vast majority of breast cancer-related deaths resulted from metastases, in this research we choose metastatic breast tumor cells to study for their extravasation. We examine for their in vitro transendothelial migration using our proposed device. We also characterize dynamics of their cell cytoskeletal components, cell-cell specific interactions and molecule secretion by the extravasative cancer cells. Overall, we expect that this research can identify more specific characteristics of the extravasative cells and help elucidate the extravasation mechanism with detailed spatiotemporal information on the cell responses. This work may provide further important insights for our comprehensive understanding of extravasation mechanism as well as for discovering effective treatments for cancer metastasis. 腫瘤轉移涉及高達90％由癌症所造成的死亡人數。其轉移過程包括癌症在患者原發腫瘤區域擴散至非相鄰組織的多個階段。一些轉移階段如癌細胞入侵、血管內滲和其後的再度擴散已被廣泛研究。然而，學者對轉移性腫瘤細胞從循環系統滲出的機制還有待全面了解。『外滲』是轉移的一個過程，當中關係到以跨內皮的循環腫瘤細胞遷移到遠處的組織或器官繼而形成生長和血管生成的新據點。現時，學界仍然缺乏相對的體外仿真器件用作更深入研究。當中的技術難題是如何提取外滲遷移後於內皮的另一側的細胞。這些可以外滲的細胞被普遍認為是更具轉移性。因此，我們打算對外滲癌細胞的動態反應及其分子機制作進一步研究。 我們計劃開發基於生物相容聚合物（聚二甲基矽氧烷）的微加工薄膜所造成了微流體器件。此器件可模擬血管內皮層上的多孔薄膜以及腫瘤細胞面對的微環境（例如：細胞外基質和血液的剪應力）。外滲的癌細胞可以從器件出口導出，因此我們隨後可以利用現存的一系列細胞分析技術作進一步研究。有鑑於乳腺癌佔大多數由轉移造成的死亡，我們在此選擇了轉移性的乳腺癌腫瘤細胞的外滲過程作為重點研究；其中分括細胞移動、細胞骨架的成分、分泌物和細胞與細胞之間的相互作用。 總括而言，我們預計這器件可以識別外滲細胞的具體特性。研究結果將有助於了解其細胞反應的詳細信息和外滲機制，以望有助開發有效治療癌症轉移的新技術。

11206014.label: Realisation of objectives
11206014.value: Transendothelial migration of cancer cells is a critical stage in cancer, including breast cancer, as the migrating cells are generally believed to be highly metastatic. However, it is still challenging for many existing platforms to achieve a fully covering endothelium and to ensure transendothelial migration capability of the extracted cancer cells for analyses with high specificity. Here, we report a microfluidic device containing multiple independent cell collection microchambers underneath an embedded endothelium such that the transendothelial-migrated cells can be selectively collected from only the microchambers with full coverage of an endothelial layer. In this work, we first optimize the pore size of a microfabricated supporting membrane for the endothelium formation. We quantify transendothelial migration rates of a malignant human breast cell type (MDA-MB-231) under different shear stress levels. We investigate characteristics of the migrating cells including morphology, cytoskeletal structures, and migration (speed and persistence). Further implementation of this endothelium-embedded microfluidic device can provide important insights into migration and intracellular characteristics related to cancer metastasis and strategies for effective cancer therapy.
