11206014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206014.value: We report a microfluidic device to isolate and investigate the transendothelial migrating cancer cells, with a unique advantage of isolating cells migrated through a fully covering endothelium for high collection specificity. We have optimized the pore diameter of the microstructured supporting membrane to be 24 μm in order to facilitate the endothelium formation and exclude cell changes caused by physical constriction of the pores. This device can isolate migrating cancer cells and reveal the cell characteristics related to the transendothelial migration capability of a malignant human breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231). In essence, we have applied this device to isolate the migrating MDA-MB-213 cells and reveal their properties of a higher body aspect ratio, faster planar migration, less consistent stress fiber alignment, and a higher nuclear palladin expression, compared to the non-migrating ones.

11206014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206014.value: Notably, our platform can be configured with an optimized pore size on the microfabricated membrane to investigate the transmigration capability of other cancer cells such as prostate cancer cells and brain cancer cells. The platform has a high potential to flow with biofluids such as the human serum or the whole blood for more realistic biophysical conditions, with improvements such as a larger membrane region. Future applications of this integrated microfluidic transendothelial migration assay can include investigation for the biochemical factors, e.g., chemokines, inflammatory molecules, and pharmacological drugs, affecting cancer cells on their transendothelial migration as well as invasion (intravasation and extravasation) characteristics for more effective cancer research and drug development.

11206414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206414.value: 機械諧振是一種長久之前即被人們觀察到的物理現象，描述了振動的機械系統在特徵頻率下振幅放大的特性。此特徵頻率也被稱為諧振頻率。振動機械系統所加載質量的改變可通過諧振頻率的偏移來測得。這種測重式測量方式的靈敏度將隨著機械系統尺寸的縮小而顯著提高。近20年來，微納加工技術的迅速發展讓人們能夠制成微米甚至納米尺度的機械系統，從而使得測量的靈敏度顯著提高。雖然測重式測量的優越性在真空和空氣中振動的微納機械系統已經被許多研究所驗證，但生物傳感應用所需要的液體環境，對這些器件的正常工作仍然是一項的巨大的挑戰。 當浸沒在液體中，原本在空氣中的強烈振動將被周圍的流體顯著降低。因為本項目所研究的器件將最終將與集成電路結合起來，從而彰顯微納器件的優勢，因此，利用電氣接口來進行驅動和檢測機械振動式非常重要的。但在液體中實現有效的電氣換能非常困難。例如，對於液體環境中的傳統電容式換能器而言，液體的電解就是一個最常見的問題。爲了解決這些問題，有研究人員利用先進加工技術將流體限制在諧振器上的一個特定通道中。但對於低成本可拋棄式生物檢測的應用而言，這種器件的加工複雜性將大大提高其成本。 本項目旨在設計實現一種能夠承受流體阻尼并具有較高換能效率的新型諧振器。我們的創新點在於設計一種非釋放式的，在流體中進行厚度剪切模態振動的硅基諧振器。利用厚度剪切模態，我們能有效的降低器件在流體中的阻尼，增強能量存儲能力，從而提高品質因數（Q值）。器件的電氣接口將利用氮化鋁壓電材料來實現，從而保證高效的換能。我們的目標在於展示一種浸沒在液體中工作，並且Q值高於250的100MHz硅基氮化鋁諧振器。我們的目標Q值遠遠高於目前文獻中所報導的流體中工作的諧振器（約10-90）。最後，我們打算將此突破性的技術應用於單個細胞質量的測量，從而展示一種具有里程碑意義的生物檢測技術。 我們已經組建了一隻具有交叉學科背景的研究團隊，團隊中具有微機械諧振器設計和特性測試的專業人士以及生物醫學儀器和細胞生物學的專家。根據初步的模擬計算結果以及專業知識，我們有信心完成所提出的研究計劃并實現所有預定的研究目標。本項目的預期成果不僅將帶來應用於振動式傳感的微納科技的突破，也將推動生物醫學儀器以及細胞生物學的發展。

11206414.label: Realisation of objectives
11206414.value: Objective 1: We have implemented and electrically characterized various piezoelectric resonators of different modes (and different harmonics) and sizes in air, including the TS mode that was initially proposed. In air, some of the resonators we have developed are able to deliver insertion losses of less than 10dB. The reproducibilty of the results was excellent as we were able to obtain consistent results from sample to sample over hundreds of device tested. Objective 2: We have demonstrated electrically measurable electromechanical resonance in fluid-damped media like de-ionized water for the various piezoelectric resonators developed and studies in this project. This includes demonstrating feedthrough cancellation techniques that deliver peak-to-feedthrough ratios (PFRs) of 35dB. Compared to the state-of-art, most resonators measured in water would have of only a few dBs at best. Such high PFRs are the result of enhancing Q in water, designing for efficient electromechanical coupling, and feedthrough cancellation. Objective 3: We have experimentally verified our proposed equivalent circuit model, which has been described in multiple publications. We have shown that the same circuit model is applicable to a large range of piezoelectric resonator we have experimented over the course of the project. Objective 4: We have monitored the electrical response of our resonators of over and tested in range of different liquids, and found that the devices we have developed remain robust after being tested over periods of weeks.

11206414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206414.value: 1) We have found that with the various extensional type vibration modes that we studied, the Q factors of the resonators typically do not exceed a value of 200. This conclusion was reached after testing various devices spanning a range of frequencies by over an order of magnitude (14 MHz to 140 MHz). On this note, we have found that the AlN-on-Si technology we have used in the project yields higher Q factors in water than what has been reported for AlN-body resonators based on the same family of vibration modes. 2) The novel resonators we have developed in this project deliver what we have found to be one of the highest Q factors found in the existing literature. We tested our devices repeatedly to ensure that the experimental variations from one test to another were minimal. If the conditions from one test to another were different, the results could be very different. In the experimental results we have published, all our values were highly consistent such that variations from one test to another was minimal. The best Q factor reported in the literature is about 300, though this value is based on the highest value found. For the devices we have developed in this project, we were able to exceed 400 as an average value of multiple tests. The resonant peaks we have reported are also among cleanest found in the literature towards practical application of resonators for liquid-phase sensing. 3) We have found there is much that we still do not understand about the piezoelectric resonators operating in liquid. For example, we have found that the features around the resonator have an effect on Q factor when others have not even standardized their testing protocols. These interesting results have been published.

11206414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206414.value: Through the funding provided in this project, we have developed a set of very promising devices that we plan to take to the next level, which is to use them for sensing. In the last year, we have formed a collaboration with Prof Vittorio Ferrari of the University of Brescia in Italy who is an expert on control circuits for resonant sensors. Using our state-of-art devices as the key element, our newfound collaborators will apply their circuits with the goal of demonstrating a system that can track the frequency and Q factor of the resonator in real-time.

11206414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206414.value: Micro-scale mechanical resonators provide a highly interesting platform for sensing miniscule quantities of mass for a range of applications, as downscaling enhances sensitivity. The most interesting and challenging of these applications occur in the liquid-phase, where the oscillations of the device are heavily damped. This makes even measuring these devices in liquid a challenge. In this project, we have considered and created novel modes that surpass the current bottleneck on quality factor, delivering devices offering the higher quality factor reported in the literature. We have also formulated characterization techniques that yield one of the cleanest frequency spectra found in the literature. The work we have done in this project has put us in a strong position to apply these concepts and devices to applications, some of which will open up new questions across different science and engineering disciplines.

11206514.label: Realisation of objectives
11206514.value: The main objective of this project is to investigate the physiological and molecular responses of microbial communities performing anaerobic digestion of cellulosic biomass with state-of-the-art meta-omics methods (i.e., amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics and metaproteomics). All objectives in this proposal have been achieved. Specifically, in Objective 1, we elucidated the physiology and assembly of the microbial communities when the substrate switched from waste activated sludge or beverage wastewater to different cellulosic biomass and during the long-term enrichment process on cellulosic biomass. Subsequently, in Objective 2, the metagenomes of the enrichment cultures were sequenced with binning of the sequencing data to reconstruct genomes. Based on the metagenomics sequences, metatranscriptomics and metaproteomics were further applied to study the metabolism of different microbial community members during time course experiments of anaerobic digestion of cellulosic biomass. A conceptual model was developed by integrating the meta-omics data to describe the functional role of community members during the anaerobic digestion process. Besides studying complex microbial communities, artificial co-cultures were constructed so that detailed experiments could be performed to understand the interactions in a community. Metatranscriptomics technique was applied to study the interactions between the two microbial players in the co-cultures. Overall, through this study, we have gained insights into the composition and metabolism of anaerobic digestion communities. As part of the education plan of this study, we have trained a number of undergraduate students on microbiology and molecular techniques, bioinformatics and the application of anaerobic digestion as a renewable energy source.

11206514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206514.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of journal publications (Part C). Part of the goal of Objective 1 is to examine how the composition and physiology of the microbial communities from two different full-scale digesters that was digesting waste activated sludge or beverage wastewater would change when given the model cellulosic biomass cellulose or xylan. As described in the manuscript of Jia et al. (2016), we found using amplicon sequencing that even though the microbial communities originated from two different sources and were originally digesting different substrates, the composition of the microbial communities converged when the inocula were enriched on the same substrate and both communities produced methane. Furthermore, some similarities were observed in the communities digesting cellulose and xylan. As further illustrated in Wilkins et al. (2015), we determined that complete and efficient methane-producing communities could be assembled from different inocula and low abundance members in a microbial community could play key roles when perturbations occurred. We also showed in Jia et al. (2018) that the rare taxa in anaerobic digestion microbial communities exhibited disproportionate cell-level metabolic activity. The goal of Objective 2 is to study the metabolic functions of the microbial communities enriched in Objective 1. Metagenomics analysis of the inocula illustrated that the seed microbial communities possessed a high level of functional redundancy, but each community carried specific metabolic functions according to the substrate that was fed to the full-scale digester (Cai et al., 2016). In order to understand the functional role of the microbial community members, metatranscriptomics and metaproteomics analyses were applied. In the manuscript of Jia et al. (2018), using metagenomics and metatranscriptomics data in concert, we built a conceptual model illustrating the metabolism of key primary and secondary fermenters as well as methanogens during the anaerobic digestion of cellulosic biomass in time course experiments. We subsequently built a more sophisticated conceptual model of the metabolism of the microbial communities by integrating the metaproteomics data with the metagenomics and metatranscriptomics results (Jia et al., in preparation). In order to further understand the mechanisms of how members in a microbial community interact with each other, we carried out co-culture experiments and used metatranscriptomics sequencing to query the gene expression of the two bacteria in the model systems. As detailed in Lu et al. (2016) and Lu et al. (2017), we observed that the presence of the co-culturing partner could trigger physiology that was not possible in monocultures and the expression of key metabolic pathways when compared against the respective monocultures. These results suggest that members within a microbial community tend to regulate their functions according to environmental conditions and who are in the microbial community. The metabolic interactions in a constructed community could be further harnessed as biotechnology for the production of biobased chemicals as described in Lu et al. (2018). Overall, the findings from this project enhanced our fundamental understanding of the composition and metabolic functions of microbial communities performing anaerobic digestion.

11206514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206514.value: Sustainable development is a goal the international community is striving to achieve in this century. Methane derived from anaerobic digestion of biomass is a key renewable energy source. However, besides combusting the methane from anaerobic digestion for energy and power, it is also possible to derive renewable chemicals from methane. We are currently conducting a project where we are applying biotechnology to convert methane to value-added renewable chemicals. This work has received some internal seed funding. Our goal is to be able to couple methanogenesis and methane oxidation in one system so that the methane produced by anaerobic digestion has multiple applications.

11206514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206514.value: Methane derived from anaerobic digestion of renewable biomass plays an important role in our efforts to replace fossil fuels and combat climate change. Anaerobic digestion is a biological process that involves a group of microorganisms working closely together to hydrolyze the biomass and subsequently producing methane. Given the large number of microorganisms involved in anaerobic digestion, the composition and functions of the members in the microbial community are poorly understood. In this study, advanced meta-omics techniques (i.e., amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metaproteomics) were applied to examine the physiology and molecular responses of the microbial communities carrying out anaerobic digestion. In this research, we gained insights into how the microbial communities were assembled when given different substrates, the role of community members that were present in low abundance, and the metabolic functions of different community members. In addition to studying complex microbial communities, artificially constructed co-cultures were used as models to demonstrate that robust interactions occurred during anaerobic digestion. Overall, the results in this study are useful to engineers and operators in real-life applications so that the performance, stability and robustness of anaerobic digestion systems can be enhanced to provide a reliable source of renewable energy.

11206714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206714.value: Pedestrian movement inside a building is an important issue in today’s mega buildings. The improper spatial design of a building can cause overcrowding or even catastrophic stampedes. It can also cause fatalities when evacuating the building during a fire. Pedestrian movement in a building can be analysed using computer simulations during building design. Currently, discrete models (the cellular automata (CA) model) and continuous models (the social force model and its variants) are the two main approaches taken in modelling microscopic pedestrian movement. Both can be considered as agent-based models. Each pedestrian is an agent who changes his or her movement according to the physical changes in the neighbouring environment. The behaviour of each agent is governed by a set of rules developed from different theories in mathematics and physics. The parameters of these simulation models must be calibrated using real pedestrian movement records. Pedestrian movement is a kind of human behaviour. A pedestrian receives information through his or her vision and makes decisions accordingly. However, the decisions may not only depend on the physical information about the surrounding environment, they may also be governed by many psychological factors in response to what is seen. The sufficiency of the current mathematical models used to simulate pedestrian movement is debatable. This project proposes to model pedestrian movement inversely. Instead of developing mathematical models to describe the movement behaviour, we will train a statistical learning model with actual pedestrian movement and information about the pedestrians’ surrounding environment, such as the movement of neighbouring pedestrians and the geometrical relationships between pedestrians and neighbouring obstacles and exits. The model will learn the highly nonlinear correlations between the movement of a pedestrian and his or her neighbouring environment from the collected real data. Once the model has been trained, it will be used as the agent of the pedestrian in a CA framework to establish a complete agent-based collective behaviour model for simulating pedestrian movement. This model will be verified using different real pedestrian movement records. This approach inversely develops a pedestrian movement simulation model and circumvents the difficulties in traditional mathematical modelling of pedestrian movement. 建筑物内的人流情况是当今大型建筑中的一个重要问题。建筑物不正当的空间设计可能会导致过度人流拥挤甚至是灾难性的互相踩踏。它也可能在大楼火灾疏散时造成死亡。在建筑物的人流可通过计算机模拟结果作分析。目前，离散模型（元胞自动机（CA）模型）和连续模式（社会力模型及其变种）是两种主要的方法在模拟微观人流情况。它们也可以视为一种个体为本模型。每个步行者是谁改变了他或她的根据移动代理在相邻环境的物理变化。每个个体的行为是由一组来自于数学和物理学的理论发展规则所操控。这些仿真模型的参数必须使用真实的人流运动记录进行校准。人流运动是一种人类行为。步行者通过他的视觉接收的信息，并据此作出决定。然而，决策可能不仅依赖于周围环境有关的物理信息，它们也可以由许多从视觉接收所引起的心理因素支配。 当今用于模拟人流运动的数学模型是值得商榷的。本项目以逆向方式建立模型来模拟人流运动。不同于发展数学模型来描述人流运动，我们会利用统计学习模型通过训练去培养出具有真实人流行为与周围环境的相互模型。该模型将学习当中之高度非线性关系。模型被训练后，它将被放入CA的框架，建立了完整的个体为本的集体行为模型模拟人流的运动。此模型这将以实际人流记录验证。这种用逆向方法发展出来的人流运动仿真模型能绕过传统人流运动数学建模的困难。

11206714.label: Realisation of objectives
11206714.value: 1. We successfully captured video clips of the pedestrian movements in road crossing. The dynamic movement of each pedestrian was extracted from the video clips by our proposed semi-automatic approach. It is the most time consuming task of this project. 2. We investigated different machine learning tools including MLP, SVM, CNN, etc. Eventually, it was found that the success of the machine learning depended very much on quality of data. All investigated model performed similar and gave good results. Therefore, the most simple MLP model was selected to be used in this project. 3. The MLP model was trained by the pedestrian movement data extracted from the video clips. The accuracy of prediction (i.e. r-square > 0.8) was very encouraging. The trained MLP model was implemented into the agent based platform to simulate the movement and interactions between the agents (i.e. pedestrian) in road crossing. 4. The performance of the trained MLP model was benchmarked with other models available in the market. It shows the the results were comparable to the other models. However, the MLP could capture the overtaking behavior and give-way behavior which were not explicitly presented to the model but implicitly embedded in the training data extracted from the video clips of the pedestrian movements.

11206714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206714.value: We successfully captured the pedestrian movement behavior in road crossing by machine learning approach. Artificial neural network was adopted in the project. It was trained and implemented into an agent-based platform forming a pedestrian movement model. The major finding of this project is that it is not really necessary to assume the pedestrian movement behavior in the model and calibrate the model parameters. Instead, building the model based on the observations on pedestrian movement is also a possible way which explores opportunities to capture the pedestrian movement behaviors from observations.

11206714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206714.value: Currently, we assumed only one agent in the model. In future, agents of different age groups, genders and disability will also be built. The interactions between these agent may give a more realistic result. Also, road crossing is a bidirectional flow condition. In future, we can also capture video from fire drills to simulate the movements of the evacuees in fire engineering study. This project generates a large set of very useful data of pedestrian movement which can be used to benchmark the performances of other pedestrian movement models in future.

11206714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206714.value: Currently, scientists developed different mathematical models to simulate the human behavior in pedestrian movement. They usually require experimental data to tune the parameters of the models so that the models can reproduced similar behavior. However, the behaviors of these models are presumed which are based on the observations of the movement. This project model the human behavior inversely. The model is built from the observation. There is no assumption in the model development. The model autonomous adjusts itself based on the observations. It is the novelty of this project. This project shows that the model not only can reproduce the pedestrian movement but also their behaviors in overtaking and giving way to others which is not assumed in the model development.

11207414.label: Project Objectives
11207414.value: To develop novel artificial alveolus for multiphase catalytic reaction; To gain knowledge of artificial alveolar mechanics and multiphase microfluidic transport-reaction interactions; To devise principles for high-performance artificial alveolar reactors.
rows: To develop novel artificial alveolus for multiphase catalytic reaction;
To gain knowledge of artificial alveolar mechanics and multiphase microfluidic transport-reaction interactions;
To devise principles for high-performance artificial alveolar reactors.

11207414.label: Realisation of objectives
11207414.value: In this project, we conducted computational modeling and experimental studies to evaluate the mass transport and electrochemical activity of the artificial alveolus microfluidic system. We have gained insights into the use of microfluidics to manipulate the kinetics of electrocatalytic reactors. Our research on microfluidic photocatalytic fuel cell was particularly successful. Our recent research on computational analysis and experimental testing of a vanadium microfluidic fuel cell led to the development of a novel configuration of multi-layer flow-through porous carbon paper electrodes. A priori modeling and simulation revealed that these porous substrates operated with non-uniform reaction rate and the reaction rate distribution is highly sensitive to the flow rate condition. Comparable cell performance was witnessed for electrodes partly modified in the high reaction rate region and electrodes modified in all parts. Therefore, multi-layer stacking of single-layer electrodes was proposed and implemented to facilitate selection of appropriate materials to accommodate the requirements of the different layers of the electrodes. Here, the electrode materials studied were pristine carbon paper and electrochemically superior platinum coated carbon paper. The results stemmed from modeling and experiments consistently revealed that the highest peak power densities were obtained in the case with electrode modification in the high reaction rate region. This study highlights the significance of the multi-layer electrode configuration associated with the balance between performance and cost of this energy system. Moreover, the multi-layer electrode configuration offers flexibility in terms of changing layer arrangement to cope with the operating condition leading to superior cell performance. Successful completion of the proposed research will open up a new direction to achieve highly reactive gas-liquid-solid multiphase microfluidic catalytic reactors, which can perform functions and high reaction rates that are not obtainable by conventional reactors. The findings can be applied to enhance the performance and efficiency of various energy and environmental chemical processes, resulting in a higher degree of sustainability.

11207414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207414.value: The artificial alveolar configurations are effectively adopted to design and fabricate porous materials with strong electrochemical and photocatalytic reactivities. The microfluidic mass transport behaviors can enhance the reactor performance due to proper manipulation of the reactant flows, mechanisms involved and kinetics. Based on the new knowledge gained, novel reactors and electrodes were developed for fuel cells and photocatalytic reactors for improved energy conversion efficiency and system effectiveness.

11207414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207414.value: In this research, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of a novel high performance multi-layer porous electrode configuration for artificial alveolus system by computational modeling and experiment. Our studies cover various scales from porous nanomaterials to microfluidic reactors. The cell of multi-layer electrodes with partial electrode modification in the high reaction rate region can realize performances comparable to that of conventional full electrode modification, offering a promising alternative to achieve cost-effective energy system. Overall, the present study concludes that the proposed multi-layer porous electrode is effective in achieving the balance between performance and cost of this energy system, and providing the flexibility in terms of changing layer arrangement to cope with the operating condition so as to boost the cell performance. These findings could provide guidance for the future development of not only the present energy system but also potentially a wider range of fuel cell technologies. In the future, we will study the relationship between the artificial alveolus configurations and advanced electrocatalysts, e.g. co-doped materials. The methodology developed, including both computational modeling analysis and laboratory works, can be employed for further research.

11207414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207414.value: Biological respiration is a multiphase phenomenon, in which numerous alveoli and capillary vessels effectively deliver large amount of oxygen and blood, respectively, to the alveolar sac surfaces, where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffusions and their exchange with red blood cells occur. The mechanisms are similar to some photo-electro-chemical reactors, such as fuel cells and photocatalytic reactors. We have investigated novel biomimic artificial alveolar mechanics for increasing the reactivity of gas-liquid-solid multiphase catalytic reactors. We successfully completed the research with new knowledge gained in the interactions between nano-catalysts and microfluidic kinetics.

11207714.value: 电子封装喷胶系统的设计与控制

Objective 3 - Hybrid model based dispensing control (slow-scale) • Modeling of controllable variables • SPC/model based decoupling control • Temperature control for viscosity compensation

11207714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207714.value: 用于微电子封装的喷射式点胶被认为是新一代的点胶技术。目前在点胶过程中难以对所喷射的硅胶进行在线测量及调控。该项目主要是建立一种混合方法来集成喷射式点胶的离线设计和在线调控。首先对点胶的物理机理进行仿真，再通过实验采验数据对模型进行校正，由此导出用于在线调控的简化模型。最后，设计出基于模型的一致性控制算法。

11207714.label: Realisation of objectives
11207714.value: As the manufacturing system is a multi-scale dynamic process, it would be extremely difficult for this kind of system to achieve high quality performance. A 3-phase integrated design methodology is proposed for control in manufacturing [10], which includes 1) real-time experiment for data collection and performance verification, 2) physics-based simulation for system design, 3) analytical modeling for system control. Guided by this methodology, the project are successfully completed with some details presented below. Objective 1 - Development of multi-sensing based dispensing experiment A dispensing system with multi-sensing capability has been established for dispensing experiment, which consists of following basic components. • First, the dispensing platform is built to include one x-y motion platform and one jet dispenser that can be adjusted vertically. The motion precision for x-y can reach±10m, and ±3m for vertical motion. The dispensing speed can reach 26 dots/sec. • Second, different measurement devices have been added to work with the dispensing platform, such as, the high-precision balance for weight measurement, the high-speed camera for measuring the volume dispensed, etc. The system will be controlled by PC and is open for re-programming. All the motions, the pneumatic pressure and temperature are open for online control. After doing extensive experiment, we have studied the breakup behavior of the jet dispensing both theoretically and experimentally [1]. The major discovery are summarized as follows: • The breakup process will go through 3 stages: bridging, thinning, and breakup in about 50ms. • The amplitude of the initial disturbance will significantly affect the droplet consistency. Thus, the nozzle motion should be prevented for the high precision dispensing. • The disturbance wavelength will have a more complicated influence to the dispensing. The wavelength between 0.3 and 0.6 might be suitable to the breakup in high-speed dispensing. • A low dispensing distance about 2mm is better for high speed dispensing. In summary, the dispensing performance are influenced by many factors, both externally and internally, some of them cannot be observed in experiment. Simulation are needed to disclose the details. Objective 2 - Simulation based dispensing design The physical model of the fluid dispensing has been established for the physical simulation using the commercial software package, after considering all the necessary information, such as, the constitutive equations, viscosity model, boundary conditions, and needle kinematic models, etc. Objective 2.1 - Physics-based modeling of fluid dispensing It is extremely difficult and has no mature solution to calibrate the simulation model with the experimental data. In theory, we have developed one method for parameter optimization using evolutionary computation [4]. In practice, this method is approximately applied in simulation based optimization. After extensive simulation trials, the parameters of the model can match reasonably well with the experiment. Then, this physical model can properly simulate the behavior of the fluid dispensing. Through extensive simulations, man dispensing details and mechanism can be disclosed, which are unable to observe in real experiment. Objective 2.2 - Design of uncontrollable variables Both experiment and simulation disclose that many factors, affecting the dispensing quality, cannot be controlled directly. Through studies, two following uncontrollable variables are discovered to greatly influence the performance. • If the viscosity of the fluid can be lowered, then the fluid will be easier to dispense. • The needle may swing under disturbance, which will affect dispensing quality. Since these variables cannot be controlled, their influences have to be minimized through effective design. A novel method is proposed to reduce the viscoelasticity of epoxy using ultrasound [2]. The viscoelasticity and molecular structures of the epoxies were compared and analyzed before and after using ultrasound. It is found that elasticity is more sensitive to ultrasonic processing while viscosity is little affected. Further, large power and long processing time can minimize the viscoelasticity. Due to the reduced loss modulus and storage modulus after ultrasonic processing, smooth dispensing is demonstrated for the processed epoxy. The subsequently color temperature experiments show that ultrasonic processing will not affect property of the epoxy. Thus, this ultrasonic processing will have a good potential to improve dispensing of high viscoelastic epoxy in electronic industry. To minimize the needle swing, both the chamber bottom and the needle head should be designed to have sphere shape [13]. Under this sphere design, the needle swing will be minimized when hitting the chamber bottom. Due to the difficult implementation, the approximate design is also proposed for the optimal performance under the certain constraints. Objective 3 - Hybrid model based dispensing control In the slow scale, thousands of dots will be dispensed in about 30 min. Any disturbance appearing in this process should be suppressed to maintain a good dispensing consistency. The measurement system developed in the lab are for offline measurement. However, in the current market, all the dispensing systems do not have real-time measurement function for each single dispensing dot. Without real-time measurement, it would be impossible to have the precise dispensing control. Objective 3.1 - Modeling of controllable variables The novel design is conducted to add the motion sensor on the top of the dispensing valve. This sensor can measure the real-time motion of the needle that is the critical controllable variable to dispensing. Integrated with the motion data and the fluid model developed in objective 2, the integrated sensing/model method has been developed to provide an effective estimation of the dispensing volume [12]. This work is novel in academia and also possesses the commercial value. Additionally, an effective detection method should be developed to monitoring the dispensing process. The least squares support vector regression (LS-SVR) is a popular modeling method under stochastic variation. We have developed a multi-support vector regression (M-SVR) that can perform more reliable measurement than LS-SVR under the stochastic variation [3][6]. Objective 3.2 - SPC/model based decoupling control With the process model developed above, the distance rejection control can be designed to suppress any disturbance appearing in the operation [9]. Since the dispensing is extremely fast, any delay may generate long dead-time effect. Then the control should be upgraded to have robustness to the long dead-time effects [11]. This novel process control method is applied to the dispensing process. This is the first-of-kind real-time measurement and control system developed for the dispensing system. Objective 3.3 - Temperature control for viscosity compensation Temperature is one of important factors that can gradually influence the viscosity of the fluid to be dispensed. In academia, the fluid dispensing is a highly nonlinear and spatiotemporal process with its dynamics varying during the dispensing process. Thus, it is extremely difficult to estimate the temperature profile over space, not alone a uniform temperature control across the space. Deep learning is applied in first time for spatiotemporal modeling for temperature field prediction [7]. Fuzzy control is one of good approaches to control the unknown process when the process model is not available. The fluid process can be assumed approximately a coupled ODE-PDE cascaded system due to its inherent configuration. Since the sampling between measurement and actuation may not match well, the delay technique is used to synchronize these mismatch. The theoretical results are successfully derived [5][8]. The practical implementation will need lots of effort in future.

11207714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207714.value: The further development should be placed on the practical realization for the commercial merit. Lowering the cost is one of the key work while maintaining the same quality dispensing.

11207714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207714.value: The dispensing system is one of the critical machines in the electronics packaging industry. The difficulty for a consistent dispensing is a long-standing problem that affects the quality of packaging. The dispensing process is of multi-scale dynamics, involving knowledge from multi-disciplines from material science, mechatronics, computer engineering, and mechanical engineering, etc.. This project aims to develop a systematic approach to solve this difficult multi-scale problem. A 3-stage integration design methodology has been successfully developed through the study of the dispensing process. Under this methodology, experiment, simulation, and design/control can be properly conducted in different stages and integrated to achieve the final goal. The methodology can also be applied for a wide range of other manufacturing processes that have multi-scale properties.

11208114.label: Project Objectives
11208114.value: We will study randomized power control (RPC) schemes for general random access systems in which collisions involving up to K users can be potentially resolved, provided that some constraints on the power profile of these K users are met. Our aim is to maximize the probability to meet these constraints at minimum average power cost. The problem is very complicated, but the potential gain is attractive. We will look for efficient design techniques that may be sub-optimal but can nonetheless provide attractive gains. We will develop techniques to improve quality of service based on RPC. This is to exploit the capability of RPC in resolving collisions. The new scheme offers the possibility to reduce delay and packet loss rate for individual users without changing modulation format. It should be more flexible and theoretically more power efficient than the conventional adaptive modulation method. We will focus on practical algorithms that can realize these potential benefits. We will study the applications of spatially-coupled LDPC codes in RPC systems. It has been demonstrated that a spatially-coupled system can outperform SIC when centralized control is available. We will remove the constraint of centralized control and develop decentralized schemes based on RPC. We will also investigate the theoretical limits of such systems.

11208114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208114.value: 多个用户的无线通信系统可大致分为两类：集中式接入系统和随机接入系统。前者一般用于在蜂窝系统，后来一般用于无线局域网。此外，在AD HOC和认知无线电应用中，信道环境变化迅速以致没有足够的时间来实现集中控制。这时就只能采用随机接入。 传统的随机接入协议，如时分ALOHA，允许多个用户同时传输，这时有可能发生碰撞。传统的假设是参与碰撞的数据包不可恢复并被丢弃。这时的吞吐量（平均每次使用信道能成功地检测的数据包数目）在用户数很大时趋于1/e =36.8％。多包接收技术可以提高随机接入的接收成功概率。现有的多包接收技术一般采用传统的单用户检测技术而只能取得有限的性能改进。 在这个项目中，我们将研究可以显著提高吞吐量的随机接入技术。我们的基本手段是串性干扰消除（SIC）。 SIC是一个非常简单的多用户信号检测方法。现有的SIC技术需要复杂的集中功率控制。否则不同用户的到达信号功率分布不当会导致SIC失败， 或导致不必要地增加平均发送功率。如何在SIC中避免无集中控制是一个尚未解决的问题。 在前期研究中，我们设计了一个基于SIC的随机功率控制（RPC）技术。RPC能够最大化两个用户碰撞时可解概率，从而增加吞吐量。在这个项目中，我们将把RPC技术推广到更一般的场合，并研究新的RPC机制以及更先进的RPC编码技术，以提高服务质量。由于问题的复杂性，我们将专注于低复杂度的解决方法。尽管这些方法可能不是最佳的，但仍然可以提供有用的收益。 随机接入是未来小区通信系统的一个重要技术。碰撞问题一直是一个具有挑战性的研究课题，这问题在高负载应用中尤为严峻。这个项目的目的是寻求这个由来已久的问题有效解决方法。

11208114.label: Realisation of objectives
11208114.value: The work related to objective 1 can be divided several parts. The first part involves optimization of randomly selecting multiple transmission power levels. The second part involves joint detection algorithm based on successive interference cancelation and iterative detection. The third part involves performance analysis. We have completed these three parts in an integrated framework, in which the optimization techniques form the core of the random access scheme, The analysis technique provides a useful tool for solving the optimization problem of determining the optimal probability distribution, and the receiver technique helps to enhance the overall performance. Our focus is on an analytical model based on the IEEE 802.11 standard with additional multiple-packet reception capability. Our research showed that the new scheme can provide significantly enhanced throughput than the conventional ALOHA or CSMA technique. This finding has important practical implications as the IEEE 802.11 standard underpinning the practical WIFI systems. Regarding to objective 2, we approached the problem using the assumption that the network is operating in one of two modes, namely, infrastructure mode or ad hoc modes. In the infrastructure mode, the problem is formulated as an optimization problem with a solution to be broadcast to all the nodes by the access point. In the ad hoc mode, the same problem is formulated as a mixed-strategy game, where individual nodes strategically choose the probability distribution of the transmitting power levels to maximize its own throughput. We showed that the Nash equilibrium of this game is Pareto optimal and fair. We observed that the resulting throughput of the distributed approach is close to the optimal performance of the infrastructure mode. We studied techniques to determine back-off time to offer optimized compromise between the throughput constraint and delay constraint. The advantages of the randomized power control scheme have been confirmed in terms of average delay and average throughputs. Regarding objective 3, we applied spatially-coupled low-density parity-check (LDPC) coding to a randomized power control scheme. We studied a randomized power control technique in a coded ALOHA environment with multiuser detection based multiple packet reception. Our focus is for medium and high rate applications. Using both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, we observed significant throughput improvement. This improvement is more significant in the cases of fading channels. Compared the work reported above for IEEE 802.11 systems, the new spatially-coupled LDPC coded scheme is more flexible. It offers the possibility to reduce delay and packet loss rate for individual users without changing modulation format. Simulation results showed that the performance of the new scheme is indeed close to the capacity region predicted by information theoretic analyses. Exhaustive searching was used to determiner power levels in the spatially couple scheme. This is due to the fact that the problem is no longer complex. We are still working towards a low cost solution using approximation techniques. Encouraged by our findings in conventional settings, we also studied the extension of decentralized power control to a wider range of applications. We propose a semi random access scheme to achieve the coexistence of users with different control modes: centralized control for local users and decentralized control for visiting users. We adopt randomized power control and successive interference cancellation techniques to optimize the system within a quality of service (QoS) constraint of local users. Simulation results show that noticeable throughput gain of visiting users can be achieved at a marginal cost of the performance of local users. The two types of users can well coexist under a proper quality of service constraint, bringing about increased total throughput. We also investigated a system model in which some users serving as parallel relays for other users. The scheme is referred to as parallel two-way relaying orthogonal frequency division multiple access (PTWR-OFDMA). It is based on analog network coding in which users are divided into near-nodes and far-nodes. A near-node communicates with the base station directly while a far-node communicates indirectly via the assistance of near nodes. We study the design and analysis issues for PTWR-OFDMA. PTWR-OFDMA has some noticeable advantages. First, the power control is decentralized, which reduces the overhead of a centralized control mechanism. Second, the throughput of PTWR-OFDMA increases in a speed much higher than that of in conventional OFDMA. Third, PTWR-OFDMA can provide much better fairness than conventional OFDMA. Fourth, the power overhead per user reduces quickly when increases if there is a peak rate limitation, implying that there is no strong incentive for some users to avoid providing relaying. We also worked on detection problems with or without joint forward error control (FEC) coding. We devised techniques to improve convergence in iterative processing. The technique leads to later works on approximate message passing detection.

11208114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208114.value: One of the most interesting findings of this project is that the new decentralized power control strategy with multiple power levels can indeed offer significantly enhanced throughput in an IEEE 802.11 model. This finding is of important practical implications as the IEEE 802.11 standard has been widely used in practical WIFI systems. This finding is reported in journal attachment 1. Our work has attracted the attention of the research community. We were invited to report the above work in 2018 IEEE Vehicular Technology Conference as reported in conference attachment 1. A second finding of this project is a randomized power control scheme based on spatially-coupled low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. This finding is of theoretical importance since it demonstrate that the new random access scheme can operate close to the information theoretic limit specified by capacity regions. This finding is reported in journal attachment 3. We also extended the decentralized power control technique to more general environments, including small cell systems, relay systems and MIMO systems. We demonstrated that the decentralized power control technique is very versatile and can be modified to a wide range of applications with significantly enhanced gains. The work on small cell systems is reported in journal attachments 4. The work on relay systems is reported in journal attachments 2. The work on relay systems is reported in conference attachments 2.

11208114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208114.value: Our work was carried out mainly based on the IEEE 802-11 standard that defines the current WIFI network. The basic principles can be extended to other applications. In particular, the 5th generation (5G) cellular system will also adopt random access functions for machine-to-machine services. The randomized power control scheme offers a practical option for the 5G system. There are many interesting implementation issues. These include user activity detection, channel estimation, low-cost detection algorithms and efficient power control algorithms. We are currently working on these issues together with industrial partners.

11208114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208114.value: We carried out extensive research activities on randomized power control for random access systems with decentralized power control and multiple packet reception capability. The work is of important practical implications. In particular, we showed that the new scheme can be applied to IEEE 802.11 systems with significantly enhanced performance. The IEEE 802.11 standard is widely applied in the current WIFI systems. Therefore the outcomes of this project have high practical values. This fact is summarized in an invited paper presented in 2018 IEEE Vehicular Technology Conference. This project provides strong evidences that the random access networks can be improved by introducing decentralized power control. We also developed practical randomized power control algorithms and advanced receiver design. We are working with industrial partners to turn these findings into application.

11208914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208914.value: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have been found to reduce the heat release rate of materials by forming a low permeable char that contains graphitic carbon. They also reduce the number of surface cracks in chars, which increases barrier resistance to the evolution of flammable volatiles and the ingress of oxygen during the condensed phase. This project will explore how these processes affect the fire resistance and mechanical properties of composite structures strengthened with CNTs. Composite structures reinforced with CNTs are expected to have the superior properties of CNTs. Cement is a widely used construction material in modern concrete structures. A detailed investigation of the mechanical behavior and post-fire properties of CNT-reinforced concrete structures is of paramount importance for civil infrastructure, especially in Hong Kong, which has many tall or super-tall buildings. Concrete is brittle, has much lower strength, and thus cracks easily under tension, and it is common to find serious cracks in tension areas of reinforced concrete structures. Serious spalling can also occur on the surface of concrete structures after exposure to high temperature. Since the early use of cementitious composites, continuous efforts have been made to control the size and the growth of cracks, improving the ductility of concrete structure components and preventing serious spalling. However, obstacles and problems still exist and remain unsolved. This project will examine the potential of CNT-cement matrix composite (CCMC) to resist spalling and improve fire resistance. Fiber-reinforced cement has been used in construction for centuries; considerable research has focused on reinforcing cement with steel fiber, glass fiber, carbon fiber, polypropylene fiber, and synthetic materials. In the proposed project, CNTs will be added to the cement matrix to improve its mechanical behavior and post-fire properties. Previous studies of CNT composites suggest that the addition of CNTs to concrete can refine the pore size distribution, greatly decrease the porosity, and improve the bonding strength, compressive strength, flexural strength, and failure strain; CNTs can also act as bridges across cracks and voids, thus reducing crack size and guaranteeing load transfers under tension. Ideally, CCMC would have all the superior features of CNTs. In recent years, many tragic fires have occurred in Hong Kong, and fire safety has become a major concern of the government, building designers, and the general public. Thus, given its potential to improve the fire resistance and mechanical properties of concrete, a detailed investigation of CCMC is necessary.

11208914.label: Realisation of objectives
11208914.value: In this proposed research project, all objectives have been realized. We have completed fire field modeling and temperature field calculation. Heat transfer within the body of element, and thermal radiation and convection was considered. Assuming the material is isotropic, a partial differential equation (PDE) of heat conduction was derived from the Fourier theorem and conservation principal. Together with three typical thermal radiation and convection boundary conditions, the PDE equation was elaborated as a parabolic equation. Numerical approaches such as the mesh-free method and finite difference method were applied to simulate the structural problems. To determine the heat transfer process, the mesh-free method was adopted in the spatial-domain, while the finite different method is simultaneously adopted in the time-domain. The pyrolysis of CNT-cement matrix composites (CCMC), which was modeled using a three-dimensional pyrolysis model which incorporated the properties of CCMC, describes the migration of gases through the solid and volatile phases to the surface and their emission. This model represented a complex combination of chemical and physical processes in both solid and volatile phases. The pyrolysis process of CCMC was modeled using an Arrhenius expression. This energy conservation equation conforms to Fourier’s law for heat conduction. The formulation for internal migration of heat due to the movement of volatile gases was fully accounted for changes in the densities of CCMC, heat from the conversion from solid to volatile phases, mass losses of CCMC, heat of pyrolysis, internal heat transfer between the solid and volatile phases, emission of the volatile gases at the surface, etc. The thermal properties of pyrolysis CCMC, such as thermal conductivities and heat capacities, were represented by functions of the solid and volatile phases and char densities and temperature. Convection and radiation heat transfer at the interface of CCMC and gaseous combustion domains were considered. The migration of pyrolysis gaseous products (i.e., volatiles) to the surface of CCMC was assumed to be instantaneous and obtained by integrating local quantities over the pyrolysis zone. The resistance to the migration of gases through the pyrolysis solid phases was assumed to be negligible. The surface regression of CCMC as a result of mass loss due to pyrolysis was tracked. The physical, theoretical and mathematical pyrolysis and gaseous combustion models were combined to form a fire model of CCMC. The pyrolysis model was discretized with the finite volume techniques to give a set of simultaneous linear discretized equations. A computational code for the coupled pyrolysis and gaseous combustion models was solved numerically using the Linux-based high-performance computer clusters. We then develop a fractal mesh-free method for CCMC. The damage constitutive model predicted the transverse tensile stress responsible for cracks by considering the interaction between the dispersed reinforcement and cement matrix, and the development of damage in the latter. We treated a CNT as a two-phase material consisting cement matrix and fiber aggregates with volume fractions. To accurately model the crack propagation, ultimate chemical evolution, and micro-voids, we have incorporated the failure, strength degradation, stiffness, and other aspects of the mechanical and materials properties into the overall stress tensor. In the present theoretical framework, the overall stress tensor in the damaged material, was schematically related to the stress tensor in the undamaged material. To improve the prediction of the stresses involved in this failure pattern, the model was extended to account for the effects of CNT reinforcement. Temperature-dependent parameter values were used during the incremental numerical analysis. The experimental results from the mechanical strength tests after exposure to high temperatures were used to calibrate the temperature dependence of some of the material properties. The transient creep strain was accounted for by modifying the constrained thermal strain. The stress analysis was coupled with the hygro-thermal analysis of heat, mass transfer, and pore pressure build-up. The derived constitutive model was implemented, and validated using the experimental data. We have conducted numerical case studies. As the problem cannot be solved analytically, the coupled nonlinear partial differential equations were discretized using a control volume technique to derive a set of simultaneous discretization equations. The simultaneous discretization equations were solved using the strongly implicit procedure. The computation code for the hygro-thermal model was coupled with a fractal mesh-free method. Through such coupling, temperature and pressure fields were passed to the mesh-free interactively and simultaneously for stress and strain analysis at each time step. In the computational procedure, the system of equations was solved using the fractal mesh-free techniques which predicted crack progression. Spalling was considered to occur when a continuous crack has formed that separates a portion of cement matrix from the initial element. A computational code was developed for performing the simulations using the DEC Alpha UNIX based workstations. The computed temperature and pore pressure histories and distributions were used for further stress analyses of CCMC exposed to fire. Sensitivity analyses with various thermo-physical parameters including permeability and kinetic data were performed. We have conducted fire tests and verified the numerical results with experimental results. Experimental data obtained from the following experiments were used to validate the numerical studies. This research used Portland cement, single and double-wall CNTs ranging from 70 to 200 nm in diameter and 30 to 100 nm in length and other auxiliary materials and experimental apparatus. We have recognized that achieving a uniform dispersion of CNTs in a cement matrix and efficient CNT-matrix bonding properties are two obstacles in using CNTs as excellent reinforcements. The CNTs tend to adhere together during pouring, as a result of the van der Waals force between sidewalls, which makes the uniform distribution of CNTs very difficult. The CNTs were treated with chemical solutions such as sulfuric acid and hydrogen nitrate, which caused a series of chemical reactions on the interfaces that increased the reinforcement efficiency and the bond strength between the CNTs and cement pastes. The solution was stirred until the fibers were scattered. The original mixes for the specimens were poured into oiled molds, and an electric vibrator was used to ensure homogeneity and compaction. The experimental tests in the project included a microstructure morphology study, fire tests, and mechanical tests. The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM) were used to observe the morphology, micro structure, composition, and detailed characterizations of CMCC. High-resolution measurements and a strong executive force were used for the quantitative evaluation of interfacial properties. A specimen with a crack propagated across fibers was chosen for the pullout test. The selected fiber has one end plugged into the cement matrix and the other end protruded for the nano-manipulator. The pullout test was performed on specimens at both room temperature and after the structure has been exposed to elevated temperatures. These tests determined the influence of temperature on the bonding efficiency between the CNTs and cement matrix. The whole experimental investigation strategy is finished and compared with numerical results.

11208914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208914.value: In this research, we have found that the superior qualities exhibited by CNTs can improve the mechanical behavior and fire resistance of CNT-reinforced composites, which provide great theoretical values and practical applications in nanocomposite studies. This project has taken the advantage of the superior properties of CNTs to enhance the overall performance of CCMC. We have found that the pore structure and temperature gradient are the main reasons for spalling. Although by adding polypropylene fiber to cement matrix composites (CMC) decreases the possibility of spalling, it has an adverse effect on residual strength. We have also found that CNTs are naturally good fillers for porous materials and improve the mechanical properties in different ways than other materials. The addition of CNTs can significantly improve the mechanical behavior and ductility of nanocomposites. A detailed understanding of the reinforcement mechanism of CCMC and an efficient way of preventing spalling and enhancing the post-high-temperature residual strength of CCMC are important for engineering applications. Due to the high strength and nanoscale structure of CNTs, CNT-reinforced nanocomposites are more compact and better able to resist crack propagation. In this research, we have employed the pyrolysis model to describe volatile gases remains in the development of the fire field model for CCMC. Translation of hygro-thermal field information that can facilitate the fractal mesh-free analysis for predicting cracks in CCMC has been realized. The research modeled the crack initiation and spalling. The mechanism that causes crack initiation and spalling in CCMC has been identified through a detailed comparison of numerical simulations and fire tests on specimens. This research developed a pyrolysis model for CCMC which considers phase conversion, pyrolysis, and char formation. This research also developed a robust fire field model comprised of pyrolysis and gas-phase combustion models and a constitutive relationship for mechanical analysis. A fractal mesh-free method which incorporates the coupled heat and mass transfer model was completed, which can predict crack development, propagation, and spalling. This research further conducted experimental studies on the microscale structures, interfacial properties, and bond properties of CNTs and the cement matrix and performed fire tests for CCMC samples using various fire scenarios. Besides, we have validated the fractal mesh-free method and fire field model for CCMC with experimental results. The above mentioned points are the major findings and research outcome of this project.

11208914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208914.value: The developed mesh-free modeling framework and experimental facilities will have the potential to be used in further investigations in fire research of glass facades. The project can help to develop a valuable framework for predicting the thermomechanical behavior of glass building facades and improving their fire resistance. The project has involved full-scale experiments designed to investigate the breakage behavior of glass facades. Real experimental models can be created with the characteristics of a variety of installations to simulate compartment fires and assess the breakage behavior of glass facades. The effects of different fixing formats on fire resistance can be determined based on the outcome of this research. A series of bending and static stretching tests can be designed and conducted at various temperatures to explore the basic mechanical properties of different kinds of glasses. Moreover, based on this research, an in-house computational code based on the mesh-free method can be developed to predict stress distribution, breakage time, and crack initiation and propagation. Simulations will lead to the development of effective ways of predicting glass facade breakage.

This project explored how these processes affect the fire resistance and mechanical properties of composite structures strengthened with CNTs. In this project, CNTs have been added to the cement matrix to improve its mechanical behavior and post-fire properties. Studies of CNT composites proved that the addition of CNTs to concrete can refine the pore size distribution, greatly decrease the porosity, and improve the bonding strength, compressive strength, flexural strength, and failure strain. CNTs can also act as bridges across cracks and voids, thus reducing crack size and guaranteeing load transfers under tension. CCMC has all the superior features of CNTs. A detailed investigation into CCMC has been completed to improve the fire resistance and mechanical properties of concrete.

11209314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209314.value: Radically different from conventional solid-solution alloys with a well-defined base, multi-component alloy (MCA) systems with equiatomic compositions constitute a novel class of so-called high-entropy alloys (HEAs). At present, considerable work has devoted to screen HEAs for mapping their alloy compositions and properties. However, the scientific effort on understanding their physical metallurgy and mechanical behavior is still limited. Based on the recent studies, most HEAs are brittle and lack of room-temperature ductility in tension; on the other hand, those HEAs with fcc solid-solution structures have sufficient ductility but relative low strengths. In view of these findings, this proposal will focus on three basic aspects for fundamentally understanding the solid-solution effect and hardening in these fcc MCAs: 1) lattice distortions by alloying elements with large size difference, 2) solid solubility of these alloying elements, and 3) scientific principles for design of these novel MCAs with desirable strength and ductility. Firstly, we plan to understand the lattice distortions in these MCAs containing atoms with different sizes. The line broadening in traditional x-ray diffraction and pair distribution functions obtained from neutron scattering will be used to reveal the intrinsic lattice distortion due to the atomic-size effects. The advanced methods based on nano-beam electron diffraction (NBED) and neutron total scattering will be employed to characterize local atomic orders, and the results so obtained will be compared with those calculated from first-principles simulations. Secondly, we need to understand the solid solubility in these MCAs. Our studies will aim at establishing the correlation of the solid solubility with the fundamental properties of atomic-size difference, mixing entropy, mixing enthalpy, electronegativity, and electron concentration of solute atoms. Experimental verification will be conducted in the fcc transition-element alloy systems of (NiCoFe), (NiCoCr) and (NiCoFeCr) with additions of Ti and Nb having large atomic sizes. Finally, we intent to develop scientific principles for strengthening these fcc MCAs. By considering the intrinsic lattice distortion, short-range order and solid solubility, the strengthening behavior of these MCAs will be evaluated and predicted. Scientifically, a successful completion of this proposed research will lead to a fundamental understanding of the solute effects and hardening of these novel MCAs. Technically, our ultimate goal is to design the strong and ductile MCAs for structural applications. 傳統的固溶強化合金都基於某一主要元素設計而成。不同于傳統合金，以多個主要元素等比例混合得到的新型多主元合金，通常稱為高熵合金。目前，高熵合金的主要研究方向集中於探索合金的成分和性能，從而篩選出具有優異性能的合金種類。然而，從物理冶金以及力學行為角度深入理解高熵合金的嘗試仍然缺乏。從現有的研究來看，一方面多數高熵合金強度很高但比較脆缺少室溫塑性；另一方面具有面心立方(fcc)固溶體結構的高熵合金具有足夠的塑性但是強度相對較低。基於目前高熵合金的研究現狀，本專案將集中考慮三個方面，以期從根本上理解fcc高熵合金的固溶強化效應：1、原子尺寸效應引起的晶格畸變；2、合金元素的固溶度；3、固溶強化高熵合金的設計原則。 首先，嘗試揭示高熵合金的晶格畸變。我們將結合傳統X射線衍射峰的寬化效應以及中子散射得到的對分佈函數揭示原子尺寸效應引起的晶格畸變；基於納米電子束散射和中子全散射的最新技術表徵晶格中的原子占位；實驗的結果也將于第一性原理的計算進行定量對比。其次，進一步理解元素在等主元高熵合金中的固溶度。我們將致力於從原子尺寸差異、混合熵、混合焓、電負性和電子濃度等基本物理性質揭示溶質原子的固溶度。實驗驗證將通過在(NiCoFe), (NiCoCr)以及(NiCoFeCr)等多主元基體中添加較大原子尺寸的Ti和Nb開展。 最終，我們將提出強化fcc高熵合金的設計原則。通過綜合考慮固有的晶格畸變、局部原子占位元以及固溶度，揭示fcc高熵合金的固溶強化機制，進一步評估預測fcc高熵合金的力學行為。從科學角度，本項目的完成將促進深入理解高熵合金的晶格畸變及固溶行為。從技術層面，我們的最終目標是設計具有足夠強度和韌性的高熵合金，做為結構材料應用。

11209314.label: Realisation of objectives
11209314.value: 1. To characterize lattice distortions in the fcc multi-component alloys (MCAs) with equiatomic compositions. (Object 1) Multi-component alloys, also referred to as High-entropy alloys (HEAs), have emerged as an exciting new class of metallic materials due to their unique microstructure and outstanding mechanical properties as ultrahigh strength and outstanding fracture toughness at ambient and cryogenic temperatures. These alloys are, in principle, single-phased crystalline solid solutions comprising multiple principle elements, typically in equal molar ratios. The unique properties of MCAs mainly originate from their multiple components and special chemical structural characteristic (e.g. severe lattice distortion), as compared with conventional crystalline alloys. However, a clear physical description of the lattice distortions in these advanced alloys containing different atomic sizes is still lacking at the present time. As a result, we try to propose a new model to address the lattice distortion based on the comparison between the distorted lattice and its ideal counterpart. By defining the dimensionless displacement between an atomic pair and its counterpart pair, an optimal parameter representing a local atomic distortion was obtained. With this new parameter, the terms of lattice distortion, the strain energy of the valence field model, and excess entropy have been well explained and connected. The results summarized above have been published: Z. Wang, W. Qiu, Y. Yang and C.T. Liu, Atomic-size and lattice-distortion effects in newly developed high-entropy alloys with multiple principal elements. Intermetallics, 64, 63-69, 2015. 2. To predict the solid solubility of solute atoms in these MCAs based on fundamental properties of alloying elements. (Object 2) In physical metallurgy, it is well proved that solid solubility of alloys plays a vital role in determining their physical/mechanical properties. Hume–Rothery rules define the effect of the size difference between solvent and solute atoms on the solid solubility of binary alloys. Nevertheless, multi-component alloys defy the classic atomic size effect due to the absence of solvent and/or solute atoms. Therefore, we propose an effective atomic size parameter by considering atomic packing misfitting in multicomponent systems. We chose the ratio between the solid angles of the smallest (rS) and largest atoms(rL): γ=ω_L⁄ω_S, as an indicator to reveal the atom packing misfit and topological instability. The multicomponent alloys tend to form solid solutions when their atomic packing parameter γ is smaller than 1.175, which is consistent to the 15% limit of Hume–Rothery rules commonly used in binary alloys corresponding to a critical value of packing misfitting of γ=1.167. In other words, the proposed parameter has a clear physical meaning in determining the solubility of these multicomponent alloys, it should be noted that γ<1.175 is one of the necessary conditions for determining the solubility of multicomponent alloys but not enough one, and that the mixing enthalpy, electronegativity and electron concentration should also be considered in order to confirm the solubility of multicomponent alloys. The results summarized above have been published: Z. Wang, Y. Huang, Y. Yang, J. Wang and C.T. Liu, Atomic-size effect and solid solubility of multicomponent alloys. Scripta Materialia, 94, 28-31, 2015. 3 To establish the scientific principles for the strengthening of these multi-component alloys (Object 3) In previous tasks, we have theoretically defined the lattice distortion and solid solution ability of multi-component alloys. here, we aim at evaluating the effects of lattice distortion on solid solution strengthening. First, the previous characterization of the lattice distortion in multi-component alloys was based on the diffraction intensity decrease of alloys prepared by casting. However, cast alloys usually have serious preferred orientation effects, which would greatly affect the diffraction distributions of individual crystal planes. In our studies, the powders diffraction without preferred orientation effects was utilized and the findings of large atom Mo additions on lattice distortion of the CoCrFeNi alloy were characterized carefully. The lattice distortion was calculated using the formula: Γ_hkl=4*tanθ*ε_str, where, Γ_hkl is the breadth of a reflection located at 2θ and ε_str is the weighted average strain. The solution of Mo results in a lattice dilation, and the lattice parameter increases continuously with the increased Mo concentration indicating a steadily growing uniform lattice strain. The micro-strain ε_str indeed exists in the powder and it increases steadily with the Mo concentration. For HEAs, the terms “solute” and “solvent” lose their conventional meanings, thus the precise contribution of solid-solution strengthening in multi-components remains to be a challenge. Fortunately, Fe, Cr, Ni, Co elements have nearly the same atomic sizes and the mixing enthalpies of different atom-pairs of these four elements are nearly equal to zero. When incorporating Mo elements at a low level to the CoCrFeNi matrix, the element will act as the solute atoms, and Fleisher's theory, a standard model for substitutional solid solution strengthening based on dislocation-solute elastic interactions, could be directly applied to evaluate the potency of solution strengthening caused by the solute atom of Mo. Clearly, the experimental data is much higher than those of the theoretical value, suggesting an extra hardening besides the solid solution strengthening. Besides, the modulation of defect structures was proved to be effective on the strength enhancement of the multi-component CoCrFeNiNbx alloys.

11209314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209314.value: The multi-component alloy (MCA) systems with equiatomic compositions have attracted a great deal of attention due to their unique microstructure and outing mechanical properties as ultrahigh strength and outstanding fracture toughness at cryogenic temperature. Such unique properties of MCAs mainly originate from their multiple components and special chemical structure, compared with conventional alloys. With the aid of theoretical and experimental methods, we have made an impressive achievement, which put some new insights into the fundamental understanding of the structural features and strengthening mechanism of the MCAs. New optimized parameters with more clear physical meanings have been proposed, by which we can determine the lattice distortion and solid solubility of MCAs more accurately. These findings allow us to well predict the alloying behaviors of MCAs and also control their mechanical properties and associated deformation mechanisms.

11209314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209314.value: A great number of studies indicate that the single-phase fcc structure, is insufficiently strong for practical applications and thus, other strengthening mechanisms are needed so that desirable mechanical properties can be obtained, especially the higher yield strengths. Based on the lattice distortion and solid solubility behaviors discovered in the current proposal, precipitation of hard intermetallic particles, which has been recognized as a potential method for strengthening steels and alloys because of their resistance to gliding dislocations, can be also employed to further enhance the fcc-type MCAs towards superior strength-ductility combinations. Alloying additions and associated microstructural control will be conducted in the future.

11209314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209314.value: Lattice distortion and solid solubility have been regarded as two crucial issues in the multi-component alloy (MCA) systems with the single fcc structure. In this project, we proposed new physical parameters and models to define the lattice distortion and solid solubility behaviors of MCAs. These innovative efforts are not only essential for an enhanced fundamental understanding of the MCAs, but also provide a practical guidance to greatly accelerate the alloy design of MCAs for advanced structural applications.

11209514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209514.value: A multi-agent dynamic system is a dynamic system consisting of a number of subsystems named agents. Coordinated control of multi-agent systems has attracted great attention in the past few years because these systems have advantages such as high efficiency and great flexibility. Typical application examples include removal of a large amount of hazardous material by a team of mobile robots and surveillance of an enormous area by a group of artificial satellites. In practice it is common for simple embedded microprocessors and low-cost communication and actuation modules to be used in implementation of multi-agent control systems. They are responsible for communicating with neighbors, processing the information, computing control algorithm, and driving the agent. Normally such low-cost on board hardware would lead to limited communication capacity and limited onboard energy resource. Unfortunately, most of the existing results focus on control algorithm development in a continuous-time setting without considering these practical constraints. More recently, some efforts are devoted to addressing those constraints by adopting sampled-data algorithms. However, they only consider multi-agent systems with single integrator or double integrator agent dynamics, which are not the case for many engineering systems in practice. The objective of this project is to investigate several fundamental problems in coordinated control and implementation of multi-agent systems in more practical settings. We aim to develop a distributed non-uniformly sampled control methodology for coordination of multi-agent systems. This includes non-uniform sampling algorithm design, sampled controller synthesis, and stability analysis for multi-agent systems with more general agent dynamics, time-varying communication topologies, parameter variation and environmental disturbances. The theoretical results will also be applied to several practical engineering problems such as formation of mobile robots and coordination of micro air vehicles. The existing continuous and periodic sampling methods are inherently demanding for communication bandwidth and capacity. To aim for a wider range of applications with more flexibility, a non-uniformly sampled control strategy will be developed. This approach only requires information exchange and control execution when certain condition is satisfied. With such a mechanism, the number of communications, controller computations, and actuator updates could be significantly reduced. The success of this research project will enable us to address a number of critical and fundamental problems in coordinated control and implementation of multi-agent systems. The anticipated theoretic results will facilitate the applications of multi-agent systems in more practical situations. This project thus holds both significant academic interest and practical importance. 多智能体系统是一种由多个子系统组成的动态系统，每个子系统又被称作智能体。由于多智能体系统具有效率高、灵活性强等优点，近年来多智能体系统的协同控制研究受到越来越多的关注并取得极大进展。在实际应用中，多智能体控制系统通常通过一些简单的嵌入式处理器、低成本的通讯和驱动模块来实现多种功能，比如，与邻居节点通信，处理信息，演算控制算法，以及驱动智能体。通常情况下，这些低成本的机载硬件只能保证有限的通信能力和有限的动力能源。目前已有的大多数结果主要在连续时间的背景下提出控制算法而忽略了这些实际的约束条件。考虑这些约束条件，最近开始有研究使用采样算法，但这些研究仍局限于仅具有一重或二重积分器动力学特征的多智能体系统，它们并不适用于许多实际的控制系统。现有的连续性和周期性采样机制对通信带宽和通信能力有着极高的要求。为了更广泛和灵活地应用多智能体系统，本项目拟提出一套分布式的非一致采样下的控制方法论来解决多智能体系统的协同问题。该方法具有只在某些特定条件满足时才会执行信息的交换和控制的运行等操作的特点。通过这样的机制，整个系统中通信的次数、控制器的计算量、驱动器的更新次数都会大幅减少。本项目包含了非一致采样的算法设计、采样控制器的生成以及稳定性分析，研究的多智能体系统将包含更一般动力学特征、时变的通信拓扑图、系统参数的变化以及外界的扰动。这些理论成果亦将被应用于解决一些实际控制问题，例如移动机器人的编队和微型飞行器的协作。本研究项目的成功将大大促进多智能体系统在更多实际情况下的应用。
