11209514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209514.value: A number of important and fundamental issues in coordinated control of multi-agent systems have been investigated. In particular, the coordinated control problems for multi-agent systems with non-uniformly sampled control strategies have been studied. Effective control strategies have been developed to handle multi-agent systems in more practical settings. Consensus of linear multi-agent systems by distributed event-triggered strategy is first studied. Then the output consensus of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems has been considered with distributed event-triggered and self-triggered strategies. At the same time, a more complicated problem, the so-called cooperative output regulation problem, of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems by event-triggered control is investigated. Both the consensus and the output regulation problems are the most fundamental and important problems in this area. Because various coordinated control problems can be formulated into the special cases or applications of these two problems. Same problems for some nonlinear systems have also been studied. It is worth mentioning that a unified framework of time- and event-triggering strategies for the cooperative control problems of linear multi-agent systems by intermittent communication is developed. With this framework, the relationship between the conventional periodic sampling control and the new non-uniformly sampling control can be better understood. The comparison between these two control methods can also be easily carried out. Finally, the application of the developed control strategies to coordination of multiple mobile robots has also been investigated. It is obvious that with the newly developed framework and control approach, more flexibility will be provided for a wide range of applications in real life.

11209514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209514.value: A number of results have been obtained and published regarding the coordinated control of multi-agent systems with non-uniformly sampled control strategies. Nevertheless, many intriguing problems in coordinated control of multi-agent systems are still worth investigating. For example, so far we have assumed the communication network is time invariant to develop non-uniformly sampled control strategies, while in many real scenarios the network might be time varying due to external environmental changes. This is interesting considering the application of the developed control methods. It has been one of our recent interests and could be one of the future research focuses.

11209514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209514.value: It is of great theoretical and practical significance to develop the non-uniformly sampled control strategies in coordinated control of multi-agent systems. The previously developed continuous and periodic sampling methods can be viewed as scheduling algorithms in a time-triggered manner. It is known that periodic sampling methods usually require a high sampling rate to guarantee desired performance. However, frequent communication and control execution will inevitably raise hardware requirement, increase energy consumption and shorten operation life span. To aim for a wider range of applications in real life with more flexibility, especially for systems operating with limited communication bandwidth and energy resource, this research project has developed non-uniformly sampled control strategies. These control strategies have the feature that the information exchange and control execution only happens when certain condition is satisfied. With such a mechanism, the number of communications, controller computations, and actuator updates could be significantly reduced. The outcome of this research project will provide more powerful tools with less energy consumption and reduced cost for more practical situations.

11209614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209614.value: The Hong Kong Kai Tak Cruise Terminal was opened in early 2013 and is a hub for cruise ships providing a gateway from Hong Kong to many Asia cities. With the rapid growth of economy and cruise ship travel, there will have a great many large passenger and cruise ships traveling to and from Hong Kong and in the Asia region. In view of the demand for pleasure voyages, larger and larger vessels are now sailing on the sea. It is not uncommon to have ships over two hundred thousand tons accommodating several thousand passengers. On the other hands, we cannot assure a zero risk situation and cruise ship accident, such as the Costa Concordia causing over 50 fatalities, has happened in recent years. In order to mitigate the ill effect of an emergency, evacuating the passengers from the ships will be necessary. The Costa Concordia accident required total evacuation of over 4,000 passengers from the ship. Studying the evacuation process and establishing appropriate strategies will be important to ship manufacturers, management companies as well as the government. Escaping from a large cruise and passenger ship may not be the same as in a building. Evacuting in confined space, narrower exits, listing, heeling and unlevelled routes, upward escape or even swinging escape routes and lifeboat operation may need to be considered for ship evacuation. The project aims at developing an integrated model incorporating agent-based and network sub-models to simulate the evacuation process in ships. Simulated experiments will be performed to study the gait patterns of evacuees in confined space, listing, heeling and swinging routes. As there may have a large number of aged and retired people to travel in cruise ships, the movement and safety of individuals with mobility impairments is something we are very much interested in studying as well. The information gathered will serve to calibrate the computer model and various ship evacuation strategies will be studied and to provide insights to cruise ship management as well as relevant government authorities. 香港启德邮轮码头于2013年初开放使用，它是一个连接香港和许多亚洲城市的轮渡枢纽。随着经济的快速增长和轮渡交通的流行，越来越多的乘客开始选择轮渡作为去其他亚洲城市旅行的交通工具。由于乘客对邮轮舒适度的需求的提高，邮轮的尺寸规模也越来越大，荷载数千人，排水量20万吨以上的邮轮已是很常见的规格。而另一方面，人数的增加意味着对邮轮的安全性要求的增加。而现在的技术并不能确保邮轮的零风险与绝对安全。如2012年发生在意大利的造成超过50人遇难的歌诗达协和号邮轮触礁事故。为了降低突发事故造成的损失，最重要的是如何让乘客从邮轮逃生。上述的歌诗达协和号邮轮就需要让4000名乘客及时从邮轮中逃生，因此对逃生过程的研究以及建立一个合适有效的逃生策略与路线对于邮轮的生产厂商、运营商以至政府部门都显得尤为重要。邮轮逃生与高层建筑逃生不同，邮轮逃生空间有限，出口狭窄，船体倾斜导致逃生通道倾斜不平，同时船体不稳，易晃动，邮轮逃生方向为所有逃生者向上而不是如高层建筑般向下逃离，且抵达甲板后还需要搭乘救生艇逃离。本研究旨在建立一套整合了个人为本模型（Agent-based Model）和网络模型（Network Model）的计算机模型，用于模拟邮轮的逃生过程。模拟实验将会为本研究提供逃生者在狭窄、倾斜、高低不平并摇晃的逃生通道内行走逃生的步态模式。由于越来越多的老年退休人士选择搭乘邮轮，对行动障碍者的逃生过程的研究也非常有意义。这些信息在用于改良计算机模型的演算过程，让模拟结果更接近客观现实的同时，也为邮轮管理及相关政府部门在船只的逃生策略方面提供更多的方案及建议。

11209614.label: Realisation of objectives
11209614.value: It is reported that there are 24.2 million passengers cruising globally in 2016 and 4-5% increase has been recorded for the year 2017. With the rapid growth of sea and river traveling, a large number of huge and complex setting cruise ships are now sailing on the sea and rivers. The Eastern Star Cruise Ship sank in June 2015 in China's Yangtze River killing more than 400 people. The accident and many other cruise ship accidents have aroused the concern of people on the safety of cruise ships around the world, in particular, people may question if the passengers can effectively leave the ship in a short period of time. Modern cruise ships are designed to be a recreation and amusing center with complex setting. In view of the limited space and the complex setting, in case of emergency, it may be difficult for the passengers to evacuate in a short period of time. Moreover, passenger ship evacuation can be very different from building evacuation because of the special environmental factors including the motion, heeling, listing and rolling of the vessel, confined space and the complexity of ships' geometrical structure. Safe and efficient evacuation has received more and more attention and International Conventions for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) requires that cruise/ passenger ships satisfying the specified criteria given in the International Maritime Organization (IMO) guide-lines should be evaluated by evacuation analyses in the early design stage. To investigate the movement pattern of passengers by considering the effect of ship heeling and trim, experimental and theoretical studies on individual walking speed, individual spatiotemporal step characteristics, as well as single file moving characteristics, influenced by the heeling and trim angles have been performed in this study. The team has collaborated with researchers in the State Key Laboratory of Fire Science at the University of Science and Technology, China (USTC) to set up experiments in USTC campus. A ship corridor simulator with a size of 10.0m (L) ×1.8m (W) ×2.2m (H) was built, which could simulate the ship corridor environment in heeling conditions, trimming conditions and a combination of both by hydraulic device, so as to provide the ship heeling and trim environments for investigating the movement of people. Experimental results were reported and published in refereed conference and journal articles. One of the PI’s PhD student, JL Sun, has participated in the experimental studies and the results have been presented in her thesis. She has successfully defensed in May 2018. In addition to experimental studies, detailed passenger/ pedestrian movement dynamics have also been studied. Two PI’s PhD students have carried out detailed studies on people’s movement with spatial constraints. A pedestrian step model has been proposed and can be adopted for “unstable” ground such as ground moving or tilting aboard ships. When compared with general buildings, it has been noticed that ship evacuation is unique because ships display a six-degree-of-freedom motion feature due to the periodical water movement and wind influence. As a result, constrained by the kinetic motion of the ground, pedestrian agents in the model could adapt its own gait according to the motion-induced stability conditions. Simulation results indicate the model can capture well-known empirical pedestrian features. Then, detailed influence of ship motion on people movement features was investigated. From the simulation results we can see the effect of ship motion on pedestrian movement feature is very complex, and should be included in simulation model. An improved agent-based model based on PI’s previous model, CityFlow, has been established to simulate evacuation process in cruise ships with complex setting. The simulation results were found to be in reasonable agreement with the experimental measured data.

11209914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209914.value: As the critical feature sizes of modern electronic devices continue to shrink, extensive research has been focused on the development and implementation of next-generation interconnects in order to incorporate increasingly small feature sizes with high performance and reliability in a cost-effective manner. Existing top-down fabrication techniques (e.g. photolithography) will expect to encounter a barrier for characteristic lengths below 14 nanometers (nm). Ultrathin metallic nanowires, on the other hand, which made by bottom-up chemical synthesis, as a new kind of one-dimensional (1-D) metallic nanostructures with diameters less than 10nm, have recently emerged as ideal candidates for future nanoelectronics applications at sub-10nm level. Since the first reports on rational synthesis of ultrathin gold (Au) nanowires in 2008, more and more ultrathin metallic nanowires (Pt, Pd, AuAg, FePtPd…) with well-controlled crystalline structure and morphology have been recently fabricated and reported, which could have great potential not only for integrated-circuits (IC) industry, but also in many other fields such as energy conversion, catalyst, and bio-sensors because of their unique physical properties. Nevertheless, all these attractive applications requires a comprehensive understanding of their mechanical performance and reliability, as both theoretical predictions and our preliminary experimental study on ultrathin Au nanowires indicated that the deformation mechanisms will be radically different to those larger nanowires with hundreds of nanometers. So in this project, we will develop and use our customized in situ SEM/TEM platforms for quantitative nanomechanical characterization of various ultrathin metallic nanowires. Furthermore, we will study their electro- and thermo-mechanical responses under charging and heating, respectively, to simulate how these 1-D building blocks degrade in realistic serving conditions. Another major challenge that hinders the industrial application of ultrathin metallic nanowires is bottom-up assembly. Despite that significant progresses had been made in hierarchical assembly and joining of traditional nanowires, the nature of ultrathin nanowires determines that they require special handling techniques on alignment and integration, to prevent any potential damage. Therefore in this project, we propose to adopt pure mechanical alignment approaches based on the “Langmuir−Blodgett”, “strain releasing” and “nano-combing” methods, assisted with our earlier discovered “cold welding” integration technique, for the scalable assembly of ultrathin metallic nanowires. The successful implementation of this project will not only provide comprehensive understanding of the intrinsic mechanical properties of ultrathin metallic nanowires as well as their mechanical responses under service conditions, but also provide a feasible assembly technique for scalable integration of ultrathin metallic nanowires for future nanoelectronics and many other applications. 隨著現代電子器件的特征尺寸持續減小，目前有大量的研究集中在發展和應用下一代集成電路中的金屬互聯技術，以期實現在縮小的芯片尺寸上達到更高的性能和可靠性。而目前廣泛應用的自上而下的芯片制造加工技術（例如光刻技術）預期將在特征尺寸達到14納米以下時遇到瓶頸；另一方面，采用自下而上方法制備的超細金屬納米線（一種新型的直徑在10納米以下的一維納米結構）在近期嶄露頭角，作為未來納米電子學在10納米尺度以下互聯應用的有力競爭者而引起了廣泛關註。自從2008年關於超細金納米線的可控制備被首次報道以來，陸續有更多的超細金屬納米線（包括鉑，鈀，金銀，鐵鉑鈀…等）被相繼制造成功並廣泛報道。他們不僅被認為是對未來集成電路產業有巨大潛力，而且由於其獨特的物理性能，在很多其他應用方面，諸如能量轉化，催化和生物感測等，也有巨大的前景。然而，所有的這些關於超細金屬納米線的潛在應用都需要對這類新材料的機械性能及其可靠性有一個全面的了解－因為已有的理論預測以及（關於超細金納米線的）前期試驗觀測均表明在這個尺度下（直徑小於10納米），金屬的力學特性和形變機制和他們在宏觀尺寸以及幾百納米下都有很大的區別。因此，在這個研究項目中，我們將發展一套獨特的原位電鏡納米力學測試平臺並用於對各種超細金屬納米線進行系統的，定量的，力學性質和本構關系的研究。此外，困擾超細金屬納米線的工業應用的另一大阻礙則是其自下而上的組裝—盡管最近數年對於傳統納米線的多級組裝和銜接有了多項重大進展，但超細納米線的尺寸和特性決定了對於其操作（包括排列和組裝等）的手段需要格外的考慮，以防造成任何潛在的破壞。因此在本項目裏我們將提出一種純機械的，基於“Langmuir−Blodgett”, “應變釋放” 和 “納米梳理”方法的納米線排列技術，輔以我們早前發現的“冷焊（cold welding）”原理，用於實現對超細金屬納米線進行可擴展組裝。本項目的成功執行不僅可以對超細金屬納米線的本征力學屬性有一個全面的理解，還將提供一套可行的對超細金屬納米線可擴展組裝的方案，用於未來的納米電子器件以及其他多種工業應用。

11209914.label: Realisation of objectives
11209914.value: 1. We have studied size-dependent and rate-dependent mechanical properties of various metallic nanowires through quantitative in situ tensile/torsion testing inside high-resolution electron microscopes: By using the in situ TEM technique, we studied the mechanical properties and discovered that Rayleigh instability phenomenon clearly exists in ultrathin gold nanowires both FCC and 4H phase upon moderate heating. We have demonstrated the size effect on the Rayleigh instability of 4H gold nanoribbons, a new type of ultrathin gold nanostructures. As the width decrease，the expansion or shrinkage degree of ultrathin 4H Au NRBs increases approximately linearly. The detailed achievement can be found in our Nano Research 2018 paper and another paper we are preparing for submission. In addition to sub 10nm nanowires, we have also established multi-scale testing platform to study the mechanical properties of larger nano-/micro-wires. For nanowires, we used nanoindentation of a push-to-pull device by Hysitron Pico-indentation 85 (PI85) inside SEM or 95 (PI95) inside TEM to do quantitative tensile tests of individual nanowires. By in situ tensile tests, it can clearly reveal the mechanical properties of nanowires at different size and loading rate. For microwires, in situ tensile mechanical studies are carried out through GatanTM Deben Microtest 200 micro-tensile-test system mounted under a high-resolution optical camera or a SEM to record the real time deformation process. For example, size effect of Ag nanowires were studied by the first method (Nanotechnology 2018). Besides, we also investigated the mechanical properties of other metallic microwires by the second method, including novel metallic glass microwires, Au microwires and Cu microwires. These works have been published on Journal of Applied Physics 2016, Journal of Materials Science & Technology 2019 and Metallurgical and Materials Transactions A 2019. Beside tensile tests, we also developed an in situ SEM torsion testing platform to study metallic glass microwires based on a micro robotic mechanical system (Scanning 2016; Experimental Mechanics 2019). 2. Combined with in situ HRTEM studies and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on ultrathin metallic nanowires, we have elucidated the crystal plasticity for metals at sub-10nm length scale and their failure mechanisms: We systematically investigated the thermal responses in geometry and crystal phase of 4H Au NRBs under controlled in situ heating processes using either electron beam (E-beam) irradiation or microelectromechanical system (MEMS)-type heating chip. Under E-beam irradiation heating, Rayleigh instability has been clearly observed and the geometry of the ultrathin 4H Au NRBs varies as the overall width decreasing while thickness increasing. On the other hand, the 4H phase remains quite stable on the dedicated MEMS heating chip up to ~600 K, suggesting the metastable 4H polytype can sustain moderate temperature. However, phase transition from 4H to FCC occurred when approaching 800 K and completed at ~900 K, which agrees well with the results of MD simulations.‘Unzipping’ of twin lamella was achieved by gradually increasing twin spacing along the wire axis via a layer-by-layer twin boundary migration process. MD simulations suggest that partial dislocation slip is responsible for activating the ‘unzipping’, with a multi-step-process involving dislocation loop initiation, expansion and partially annihilation. (Materials Research Letters 2017) For metal wire bonding applications, Au-Al intermetallic compounds regarded as damage sources within wire bonding interfaces were investigated to illustrate their intrinsic mechanical properties by in situ bending tests (J Mater Sci: Mater Electron 2018). 3. We have further investigated "cold welding" phenomenon and its underlying mechanisms to be used for bottom-up assembly and nano-fabrication: We have found that “dumbbell” shaped ultrathin gold nanorods can be cold welded in the side-to-side mode in a highly controllable manner and can form an extremely small nanogap via a slow welding process. By combining in situ HRTEM analysis and MD simulations, we further reveal the underlying mechanism for this side-to-side welding process as being dominated by atom kinetics, which provides critical insights into nano-system integration of functional nanodevices. (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2016) Through the controlled electron beam irradiation-induced heating mechanism, we further quantified the effect of electron beam intensity and its dependence on Rayleigh instability in altering the geometry of the ultrathin gold nanowires. Moreover, in situ HRTEM observations revealed surface atomic diffusion process to be the dominating mechanism for the morphology evolution processes. Our in situ characterization of ultrathin gold nanowires on their thermal/structural stability upon heating could offer critical insights toward reliable applications of ultrathin gold nanostructures, as well as other emerging ultrathin metallic nanowires in nanoscale electronics and mechatronics systems. (Nano Research 2018) Furthermore, mechanically assisted self-healing process of damaged ultrathin gold nanowires has been investigated and eludicated with in situ HRTEM experiments and MD&DFT experiments, and surface atom diffusion has been considered as one of the major mechanisms in such processes. 4. We have demonstrated the scalable assembly of ultrathin metallic nanowires based on the mechanical assisted strategy and explore the functional (device) applications of ultrathin metallic nanostructures and their hierarchical structures: Upon mechanical perturbations, predamaged, nonuniform ultrathin gold nanowires can quickly recover into uniform diameters and restore their smooth surfaces, via a simple mechanically assisted self-healing process. We showed that mechanical manipulation can assist the atoms to overcome the diffusion barriers, as suggested by ab initio calculations, to activate more surface adatoms to diffuse and consequently speed up the self-healing process. This self-healing could be done simply by applying global mechanical perturbations on the whole nanowire devices, without the need of precise controlling mechanisms. This part of the work has been published in Small 2018. We further demonstrate a controllable fabrication of porous gold nanorods by in situ fragmentation of Au–Ag alloy nanowires associated with Rayleigh instability. Together with a one-step dealloying finishing process, our method could facilitate the mass production for low-cost, high-throughput fabrication of low-aspect-ratio porous metallic nanorods for biomedical (such as drug delivery) and other applications (RSC Advances 2016). Other applications of metal size effect in strengthening real devices/structures have also been demonstrated, such as 3D-printing assisted metal-coated micro/nano-lattice composites (Composite Structures 2018). Recently, combined the merits of silver nanowires and graphene, we fabricated transparent electrode of silver nanowire array/network supported by few-layer graphene. By taking advantages of scalable assembly of silver nanowire arrays via cold welding, we can expect a high efficient, low cost manufacturing method of such flexible metallic conductive films. This part of the work is in preparation for a paper submission as well as patent application.

11209914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209914.value: By using the in situ TEM technique, we discovered that the Rayleigh instability phenomenon exists in ultrathin gold nanowires both fcc and 4H phase upon moderate heating. (Nano Research 2018) We have demonstrated size effect of ultrathin 4H gold nanowires (a new type of ultrathin gold nanostructures) and systematically investigated thermal responses in geometry and crystal phase of 4H Au NRBs under the controlled in situ heating processes. Based on similar mechanism with cold welding, upon mechanical assistance, gold nanowires can recover uniform diameters (including Rayleigh instability) and restore their smooth surfaces via self-healing process. (Small 2018) With the assistance of Rayleigh instability, we demonstrate a controllable fabrication of porous gold nanorods by a novel template-assisted electrodeposition and in situ fragmentation of Au–Ag alloy nanowires, followed by a dealloying process to convert the resulting Au–Ag nanorods into desired NPG nanorods. (RSC Advances 2016) In addition to nanowires around 10nm, we have also established multi-scale tensile testing platform. This tensile platform contains nanowires testing system based on Hysitron PI85 picoindenter inside SEM or PI95 inside TEM and microwires testing system based on GatanTM Microtest system mounted under an optical camera or SEM. Based on these platforms, we demonstrated size-dependent and rate-dependent mechanical properties of various metallic nanowires. (Nanotechnology 2018, Journal of Applied Physics 2016 and Journal of Materials Science & Technology 2019) In addition to tensile tests, we established a self-developed micro robotic mechanical testing system to implement the in situ SEM torsion tests of microwires. (Experimental Mechanics 2019) Combined with in situ HRTEM studies and molecular dynamics (MD)/DFT simulations on metallic micro-/nanowires, 'unzipping' of twin lamella was achieved by gradually increasing twin spacing along the wire axis via a layer-by-layer twin boundary migration process. (Materials Research Letters 2017) And we have further investigated “cold welding” phenomenon and found that “dumbbell” shaped ultrathin gold nanorods can be cold welded in the side-to-side mode in a highly controllable manner and can form an extremely small nanogap via a relatively slow welding process. (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2016) Scalable assembly of ultrathin metallic nanowires were thus achieved. Combined the merits of silver nanowires and graphene, we fabricated transparent electrode of silver nanowires network supported by few layers’ graphene for flexible electronics applications.

11209914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209914.value: The further development regarding to this project is the development of study the mechanical behavior of hierarchical structure containing nanowire building blocks, as well as the investigation on the scalable cold welding for flexible electronics. Our multi-scale platform is applicable for testing of hierarchical structural and uncover the mechanical behaviors that utilizing the metal size effects to strengthening the structures, such as 3D-printed metal-coated hybrid micro/nano-lattice composites. (Composite Structures 2018). Besides, study the electro-mechanical response of metallic nanostructures upon mechanical straining for their electronic/functional device applications (RSC Advances 2015 and Journal of Nanoparticle Research 2016). Based on our recent developed electro-mechanical testing platform, the electro-mechanical coupling/responses of ultrathin metallic structures will be studied for better understanding and design their hierarchically assembled flexible devices.

11209914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209914.value: Metallic (such as gold) wires with diameter ranging from hundreds nanometers down to sub 10 nanometers are promising ideal candidates for future electronics and electromechanical applications. To study their properties is not only important for future integrated-circuits (IC) industry, but also valuable in many other fields such as sensor, energy conversion, catalyst. Nevertheless, all these attractive applications require a comprehensive understanding of their mechanical performance and structure reliability. In this project, we developed multi-scale in situ SEM/TEM platforms for quantitative nanomechanical characterization of various ultrathin metallic nanowires down to sub 10 nanometer level. Combined with in situ HRTEM studies and atomic simulations on ultrathin metallic nanowires and nanoribbons, we quantified their mechanical properties and discovered obvious Rayleigh instability in ultrathin gold nanostructures. We systematically investigated the thermal responses in the geometry and crystal phase of those sub-10nm gold nanostructures. In addition, we showed that self-healing process upon mechanical stimulation can help to quickly recover pre-damaged ultrathin gold nanowires, even in functional devices. We also further investigated“cold welding”phenomenon and found side-to-side "cold welding" for controllable nanogap formation from ultrathin gold nanorods, useful for chemical/bio sensing. Besides, we worked on the scalable assembly of metallic nanowires and demonstrate the possibility of integration of silver nanowire arrays with graphene membrane, which can be a low-cost alternative for flexible conductive film/membrane fabrication/manufacturing. The study in this project not only provides critical insights in understanding the intrinsic mechanical properties of ultrathin metallic nanowires as well as their practical mechanical reliability/responses under service conditions, but also provides a feasible technique for scalable integration and application of ultrathin metallic nanowires and their networks for future device applications.

11210014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210014.value: With the advancement of technology and the support of regulatory policy, the millimeter wave technology has been viable for commercialization. Existing and new applications are very diverse, including satellite broadband Internet access, broadband media transfer at home, point-to-point data links, automotive radar, security imaging in businesses and at airports, body measurements in retail clothing shops, Doppler radar sensors for healthcare monitoring, and many others. Atmospheric absorption is very strong at millimeter waves. The output power of millimeter wave solid-state sources cannot be too high. This requires the use of medium or high gain millimeter wave antennas to develop millimeter wave systems with acceptable performance. Many planar antenna arrays with good directional property were developed recently for the unlicensed 57-64 GHz frequency band. These antenna arrays are complex in structures which are costly in fabrication. Recently, we demonstrated that by integrating two trapezoidal shape microstrip antennas with a biquad type antenna together, a low-profile printed antenna element with unidirectional radiation pattern, high gain and reasonably wide bandwidth can be achieved. Preliminary results indicate that the antenna element can be used to construct 60 GHz high gain printed antenna arrays with high efficiency. In this project, we will develop a new series of antenna arrays for various millimeter wave applications operated between 60 – 140 GHz based on this new antenna element. 隨著科技的進步與政策的支持，毫米波技術已成功實現了商業化。已有的毫米波應用和新型毫米波應用也呈現多樣化，這包括衛星寬頻英特網連接、家用寬頻多媒體傳輸、點對點信息傳輸、汽車雷達、商用及機場安檢成像、零售服裝商店的顧客身形測量、個人健康檢測的多普勒雷達傳感器等很多應用技術。但是，在毫米波頻段的大氣吸收十分顯著，加之毫米波的電晶體信號源輸出功率不可能很高，於是，在這種情況下為了實現合理的性能，就需要在毫米波系統中採用中高增益的天線。到目前為止，許多具有強方向性的平面天線陣列已被設計在57-64GHz免費頻段。這些天線陣列結構複雜，從而增高了生產成本。近期我們發明了一種新的低剖面印製天線陣子，它通過集成兩個梯形微帶天線和一個雙四邊形天線，同時實現了單向輻射方向圖、高增益和合理的阻抗頻寬。初步結果證實這種天線陣子能被應用於構建60GHz高增益高效率印製天線陣列。因此，此項目中，我們將基於這種天線陣子，設計一系列新的天線陣列來滿足工作在60-140GHz的毫米波段的各型應用。

11210014.label: Realisation of objectives
11210014.value: The aim of the project is to develop low-profile low-cost printed millimeter-wave antennas with wideband performance for future wireless applications. A novel antenna element was proposed for achieving four objectives. The research plan was carried out with the assistance from two Ph.D. students. The proposed printed antenna structure is basically a direct dipole loaded with two parallel loops. It is low in profile while having wide bandwidth due to the multi-resonance behavior. It is a single-layered structure, which makes it attractive for millimeter wave applications, as the fabrication costs are not expensive owing to its simple configuration. The antenna structure was optimized with wider bandwidth, through detailed parametric study. For array applications, it is preferable to reduce the size of the antenna element, while maintaining reasonable bandwidth. Two approaches have been investigated, including the use of etching slots on the dipoles and the use of high dielectric-constant substrates. For producing circularly-polarized radiation, a few methods have been employed. The first method is to remove a few portions of the metallic dipole surfaces, which however is not very effective. Another method is to follow the conventional cross-dipole concept to produce circular polarization. The antenna structure is more complex using this method. Related to this study, novel feed networks for producing dual circular polarizations were investigated. For developing antenna arrays at different millimeter-wave frequencies with high gain, different feed networks based on microstrip lines were investigated, including parallel feed, series feed and a combination of parallel and series feed. A combination of microstrip lines and waveguides for achieving higher gain was also investigated. Great effort has been tried to realize the objectives and achieve the aim. The major objectives have been achieved and some related investigations were carried out with the help of the two Ph.D. students.

11210014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210014.value: The investigation of the project was started with the support of my Ph.D. students before the funding was approved. This explains why the first journal paper [Journal paper 1] was published before the beginning of this project. It was reported that based on the new antenna element, a number of 2-dimensional antennas arrays with 4-elements, 14-elements and 50-elements were successfully realized with 15 dBi, 19 dBi and 24 dBi gains, respectively, covering the 57-64 GHz unlicensed frequency band. These antenna arrays are single-layered structure as they are excited by series and parallel microstrip line networks. To achieve higher gain, more elements are required. Then the corresponding microstrip line feed network will be very lengthy, resulting in very high feedline loss. It was found that by combining four sub-arrays of 4 by 4 elements through aperture coupling of the microstrip-line feed network for the sub-array to a rectangular waveguide parallel feed network, a highly-efficient high-gain antenna array of 16 by 16 elements with 32.7 dBi gain can be achieved, with low fabrication costs [Conference paper 1]. This work was accomplished with the assistance of one of my Ph.D. student, Dr Yue Zhao. The significance of this work is that antenna arrays with very high gain and large number of elements can be designed using this method. In the course to investigate how to modify the new antenna element with circularly polarized radiation, a new single SIW feed network for generating dual circularly-polarized radiations was invented [Journal paper 3]. In the design, the two polarizations share the common radiating element and feed network so that the two polarizations exhibit almost identical performance in bandwidth, gain and radiation patterns. A prototype of 8 by 8 elements operated at 60 GHz was constructed and tested successfully. The feed network can provide over 20% bandwidth which is sufficient for many applications. The isolation between the two ports is about 14 dB which needs to be improved in the future. Another Ph.D. student supporting this project, Dr Fan Wu, also worked on reconfigurable antennas. He has successfully developed several reconfigurable magneto-electric dipole antennas operated at microwave frequencies [Journal papers 4 and 5]. The knowledge obtained will be useful for designing millimeter-wave printed antennas and arrays in the future. The most important contribution of this study is that it reveals the basic principle to design wideband low profile printed antenna using the multi-mode approach. Each mode can be coming from different antenna structure. The proposed antenna element is just one example, which consists of a bowtie dipole and two loop antennas supported by a grounded dielectric substrate. It is believed that many other combinations with better performance can be found.

11210014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210014.value: The designs with linearly polarized radiation are excellent in performance and attractive for many future wireless applications. We have difficulty to enhance the design with circularly polarized radiation. Further effort is still required, which is worthwhile as it is expected that more future wireless systems will be operated with circular polarization for enhancing the reception quality. We have obtained simulation results for similar designs operated at 120 GHz, reasonable good performance was found. However, due to high fabrication costs, prototypes were not fabricated. We believe that the designs are still effective up to 300 GHz, providing that low-cost 3D printing technique is available in the near future.

11210014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210014.value: The project is to investigate low-cost low-profile millimeter-wave printed antennas and arrays for various wireless applications, including communications, radars and sensors. As the output power of millimeter wave solid state sources are quite low, high gain antenna arrays are required to achieve high system performance. Traditional designs based on bulky antenna structure such as horn antennas are available, but not suitable for portable devices. In this project, we have successfully developed a new series of printed antenna arrays which is low in profile and wide in bandwidth. It can be fabricated by low cost printed-circuit-board techniques. When this project was proposed, we did not know that the 5G mobile communications would include the millimeter wave frequency channels. The new printed antenna arrays will be applicable to base stations, routers, hubs and portable devices for 5G and beyond.

11210314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210314.value: Microfluidics, microfabrication, and biochemical molecular diagnostics have many requirements and constraints that are in conflict with each other. A major issue in the development of any practically protocol integrating these technologies has always been preserving the downstream viability of the cell sample. For a lab-on-a-chip (LOC) to be clinically practical, a fabrication platform must be developed that can reconcile the low cost and rapid fabrication advantages of soft (polymer) lithography with the versatility of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) integration. Specifically, standard lithography processes require an expensive mask or mold to create micro-channels and other functional structures. The research team in this proposal has recently demonstrated a “virtual mask” system that uses computer-generated, digitally projected images to rapidly pattern regular arrays of polymer structures. We have named the principle behind this assembly mechanism as optically-induced electrohydrodynamic instability (OEHI). In this project, we will characterize and extend the patterning capabilities of OEHI to dynamically fabricate all the structures for common microfluidic functions: particle or cell sorting, concentrating, filtering, mixing, incubating and detection. Having recently demonstrated results of controlled OEHI-based pillar growth in a microchannel, this project will explore the capability of OEHI to dynamically generate other basic microfluidic components such as walls, mixing chambers, sorters, and concentrators using non-ultraviolet optical images projected into a microchannel. As a proof-of-concept of this OEHI platform, we will develop a LOC system targeted at the sorting and detection of circulating cancer cells (e.g. spiked MCF-7 human breast cancer cells in a red blood cell sample). An important advantage of the LOC created using OEHI will be demonstrated by maintaining the viability of these cells for subsequent downstream incubation or assays. By switching from the DC power source required for OEHI patterning to a millimeter-wave (GHz) source, it is possible to use localized inductive heating by seeding conductive particles into the PDMS and controlling the penetration skin depth of electron transport. We will demonstrate the capability to release the captured, live, cancer cells from our polymer-filter structures. The assembled team has successful worked together recently to introduce OEHI to the world. Furthermore, we bring considerable experience in integrated microfluidic devices for clinical applications (Mai and Lee), control of optoelectrokinetic (OEK) phenomena (Li and Lee), and localized inductive heating of polymers for MEMS and biomedical applications (Mai and Lee). The success of this project will deliver new insight into OEHI-based, rapid patterning techniques and localized heating techniques to release captured rare cells. N/A

11210514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210514.value: The existing search techniques are mostly relevancy driven. Specifically, given a query, the underlying engine seeks to sort the documents in descending order of relevancy to the query, followed by list-wise presentation of the results. Such strategy is deemed to be effective, if the user has a clear search goal (e.g., top-100 kindergartens in Hong Kong) and expects an answer in the first page of results. For a complex query (e.g., Hong Kong education reform since 1997), however, it becomes the user’s responsibility to explore the rank list to reveal the multi-faceted information underneath the query. The exploration of search results can be highly difficult for users whose purpose are to learn and investigate. In practice, the exploration of search results is more complicated because of two facts: the search intent is not static but may switch gradually when more information is exposed; the search results are not purely text-based but mixed with a variety of multimedia information such as videos and images. This project targets for a multimedia-based exploratory search system beyond relevancy seeking and list-wise presentation. The focus of studies will be on addressing four research problems in exploratory search. First, the search is recall-oriented. The presented information in the first page of results should be as complete, relevant and less redundant as possible, for an overview of multiple facets in a query before navigating the results in the next page. Second, the relationship among search results of different media should be exposed for efficient comprehension of information. Third, the index engine should continuously capture the time-evolving nature of potential search topics for displaying of up-to-date event relationship without information delay. Finally, there is no absolute measure of relevancy ranking among the search results. The selection of results to display is not only based on content relevancy, but also contexts such as user interaction to make sense of the presented results. This project will contribute by researching a solution that integrates user (through modeling search behavior), data (through multimedia analysis) and space (through analytical presentation) for exploratory search of Internet videos. The solution aims for recall-oriented techniques in providing multi-perspective information access and navigation; and utility-driven strategies that emphasize of how the result of multimedia analysis could be utilized by users (e.g., through visualization and recommendation) for subsequence search. These two peculiarities basically mark the difference between the proposed works in this project and the conventional goal-driven precision-oriented search techniques. 現有的搜索技術大多是由相關性驅動的。比如，給定一個查詢，搜索引擎會根據文檔與查詢的相關性對結果排序，隨後以列表的形式展現。這種策略在用戶有明確搜索目標/意圖（例如，香港頂級的100所幼兒園），並期望在第一頁找到答案的情況下是有效的。然而，對於一個復雜查詢（例如，1997年以來香港的教育制度改革），用戶只能通過瀏覽搜索結果的方式尋找隱藏在查詢語句中多方面的信息。對搜索目標不明確（需要學習和調查）的用戶而言，瀏覽搜索結果列表的方式變得非常困難。在實踐中，瀏覽搜索結果更加復雜，因為（1）用戶的搜索意圖通常不是靜態的，而是隨著時間逐步清晰;（2）搜索結果通常也不是純文本的，而是混合了各種媒體信息，比如視頻和圖像。 該項目研究搜索相關性和列表展示之外的多媒體探索性搜索。研究重點是搜索四個主要問題。首先，搜索結果側重召回率。第一頁的搜索結果應盡可能得完整，相關，並盡可能少得冗余。這些結果需能在用戶查看下一頁前概括查詢的各個方面。其次，如何展現不同媒體搜索結果之間的聯系以幫助用戶快速理解搜索結果。第三，索引需要不間斷地捕捉隨時間變化的事件關系，無延遲地顯示最新事件關系。最後，搜索結果中相關性沒有絕對的排名。搜索結果顯示的選擇不僅要基於內容相關性，而且要基於語境信息（諸如用戶交互），使所呈現的結果更容易理解。 本項目提出一個解決方案，用來集成用戶（用戶行為建模），數據（多媒體內容分析），和空間（搜索結果解析式展現），從而進行互聯網視頻的探索式搜索。本研究方案側重以召回率為導向的技術來支持多視角信息接入與導航；此外，以效用為驅動的策略能夠強調多媒體分析結果是如何被用戶利用的（例如，通過可視化或者推薦系統）。這兩個特點區別了本項目與傳統的以目標驅動，以準確率為導向的方法。

11210514.label: Realisation of objectives
11210514.value: Objective-1: Knowledge construction and adaptation The objective is realized by studying of algorithm for topic tree construction and its utilization for video navigation. We consider the construction of topic tree from a predefined hierarchy prototype and then the hierarchy is adapted by topic tracking. Initially, the hierarchy is constructed automatically from Wikipedia pages. Web videos are continuously processed and matched to the hierarchy, while adaptation of the hierarchy is performed when new topic facets are mined from the videos. The main issue being addressed is how to mine salient phrases for video clusters so as to match with topics predefined under a given hierarchy. The problem is formulated as the ranking of salient phrases. Each candidate phrase is represented with five properties derived from the video cluster attached to the phrase. A regression model is employed to fuse these properties and eventually output a saliency score for ranking. Only top-ranked phrases are considered as salient for matching with hierarchy. During matching, the initial hierarchy will be transformed to align with salient phrases, which includes removal of nodes that are without compatible videos for assignment, and possibly addition of nodes to accommodate new clusters of videos missing from the existing nodes. The matching between videos and hierarchy is performed with a greedy algorithm that integrates three criteria: relevance, uniqueness and diversity. Relevancy measures the semantic relatedness between videos and nodes in hierarchy. Uniqueness biases the videos that are related to one node only rather than multiple nodes. Diversity ensures that there is no content redundancy among the videos attached to a node. The greedy algorithm sequentially searches for the node that best matches with a salient phrase, and then identifies a video from the corresponding cluster for insertion. Adaptation of the hierarchy with new facets mined from videos without semantically distorting the already well-organized hierarchy is challenging. A conservative but safer strategy in order not to frustrate browsing experience is by listing important facets alongside with hierarchy. As videos of newly mined facets may lack of text description, latent semantic indexing is performed for the selection of representative videos for these facets. Objective-2: Cross-modal and cross-source hyper-linking The objective is realized by researching of algorithms for cross-media and cross-modal analysis of person and opinion facets. For person facet, a multi-cue approach based on conditional random field (CRF) has been proposed for name-face association. The cues considered are face similarity (via handcrafted and deep-based facial features), spatio-temporal constraints and face models trained based on weakly-tagged web images. The problem is considered for within-video and between-video face naming scenarios. Basically within-video only assigns names mentioned in the metadata to a video, while between-video leverages social network to connect videos and models celebrity relationships for joint inference of names across videos. The latter is powerful in way that persons whose names are not mentioned in the metadata could also be inferred, but suffers from the computational issues due to high memory consumption of CRF. We have hence also proposed a memory-efficient algorithm for between-video name-face association. The algorithm is able to reduce the memory consumption from 5G bytes to 0.04G bytes for around 280 videos involving 13 celebrities. For opinion facet, the research focuses on the localization of video answers for efficient video browsing. The problem was addressed by multi-modal sentiment analysis and opinion clip localization. The former takes speech, caption and metadata as input to a naïve Bayes classifier that is trained using SentiWordNet ontology to locate talking tracks with sentiment content. The latter further extracts eleven features based on audio-visual cues to locate opinion clips. With these, our developed system can index all the extracted opinion clips for matching against text questions. As emotion and sentiment content is generally difficult to be analyzed based on a single modal only, investigation has also been carried out on affective analysis for multi-modal retrieval, i.e., phrase-to-video retrieval and vice versa. A multi-modal deep Boltzmann machine (DBM) with three pathways (visual, auditory and text) is proposed for learning joint representation for cross-modal retrieval. The learning is conducted in unsupervised manner, specifically DBM is learnt from user-generated-content without expert data labeling. Based on this model, problems such as video emotion detection, sentiment analysis of twitter messages and affective based video retrieval are also investigated. Objective-3: Interactive context-aware visualization The objective is realized by studying the scenario of video recommendation in the context of celebrity network. Specifically, the scenario is that a user wants to know more about the social circle of a celebrity when browsing videos. The solution is by providing recommendation with sufficient coverage that allows user to quickly grasp the basic knowledge for further exploration of video collection. To do so, the proposed approach probabilistically encodes the topics and labels the faces of videos for indexing, based on topic modeling and name-face association algorithms studied in the objective-2. When a celebrity in a video is selected for browsing, new set of videos is recommended based on topic diversity and celebrity social network. The recommendation is based on maximal marginal relevancy greed search algorithm that suggests as diverse as possible videos among the relevant videos up to at most five recommendations. User can interact with video content by mouse hovering over faces to show names, and further clicking of faces can trigger new video recommendation. Throughout the process, serendipitous-based browsing is achieved by diversity-based video recommendation. The problem is also investigated by studying suitable algorithms and network architectures to establish inter-video relationship for interactive browsing. In this study, name entities extracted from ASR (automatic speech recognition) are used for video linking. We compare the performance between traditional tf-idf and neural-based word2vec (w2v) representations for this task. The w2v can represent 3 million of words and phrases in high dimensional space, and is trained using skip-gram architecture with hierarchical softmax. The work is later extended to also consider semantic features extracted from video content, and a neural network composed of LSTM (long short term memory) and holographic layer is developed for empirical studies. Objective-4: Development of exploratory video search system This objective is realized by development of an interactive system that supports exploratory search by indexing a large number of semantic concepts and name entities extracted from the video metadata and captions. Videos are organized hierarchically for fast browsing, while user can issue complex queries by text and sketch. A large number of techniques are explored, including concept screening, video re-ranking by highlighted concepts, relevance feedback and color sketch, for interactive search. A particular study conducted is to understand user behavior and data distribution in influencing search effectiveness. As a retrieval model usually has many parameters to fine-tune, an experiment with real user interaction is not possible and therefore the study is based on simulation. Under the context of color sketching, five types of user errors are studied to investigate the recommendation strategies that should cope with both user behavior and data distribution. The study results in a design of new query interface, where user can visualize the distribution of search results after placing the first query. The visualization gives clue to user of where to explore in the feature space by placing a proper second query to efficiently navigate the search space.

11210514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210514.value: This project addresses video exploration beyond relevancy-seeking and list-wise presentation of search result. To enable recall-oriented search, a number of fundamental issues are studied, including topic construction [TMM 2016], cross-modal linking by name-face association [TMM 2015], sentiment analysis and opinion clip localization [TOMM 2015], affective-based cross-modal retrieval [TMM 2015], and video linking [TRECVid 2015, ICMR 2016, TRECVid 2017]. The results of studies are leveraged for efficient browsing in large video dataset. To verify the merit of exploratory search, different interfaces are developed for user studies in different vertical domain, including topic construction, exploratory search, opinion-based text-to-video retrieval, and celebrity video recommendation. In the study of topic construction, the experiment covers four major topics (celebrity, city, company, event) and a dataset of 1,300 YouTube videos for each topic. User studies confirm that interactive hierarchical browsing is preferred than list-wise presentation, and the transformation of hierarchy by node removal and addition of new topic facets are helpful in browsing. The study of name-face association also results in a memory efficient algorithm for inter-video linking, which is explored for video recommendation in the case study of celebrity browsing. When integrating with other techniques such as topic modeling and maximal marginal relevancy, the algorithm is verified to be effective in recommending serendipitous videos. For opinion and affective analysis, due to rapid advancement of deep learning techniques, the studies are focused on network architecture design to enable cross-modal retrieval and boost the performance of classification. The experiments on eight opinion-oriented topics and 800 hours of web videos show the challenge of localizing opinion clips, with accuracy around 0.5, for video answer retrieval. To study the relationship of different factors (user behavior, robustness of multimedia analysis, data distribution and space of exploration) that affect browsing experience, a video search system is also developed. In the design, user interacts by consecutive action of querying and browsing, while the system makes recommendation by visualizing the distribution of search result to user as guidance for navigation of search space. In the study, efficient video browsing is found to play a critical role in searching, where user can quickly modify a query when navigating to a cluster of videos of interest or switch to a new topic or query whenever the search result is sub-optimal. The system has also been showcased in the video browser showdown (VBS) for real-time evaluation by experts and novice users [MMM 2017, MMM 2018].

11210514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210514.value: This project has studied a variety of issues in enabling recall-oriented search. A number of issues are worth further research from the perspectives of system robustness and user experience. Feature learning: Some features are engineered for performance optimization, which limit the robustness of multimedia analysis. With the progress in deep learning, embedding methods based on neural networks can be explored. For example, the list of ad-hoc features hand-crafted for opinion clip localization can possibly be learnt by neural network using training videos. Video fragmentation: The retrieval algorithm assumes that the length of a fragment is predefined and does not adapt to user query. However, browsing experience can be impacted as the context of a fragment may change due to inclusion of query irrelevant content. Future research should investigate query-adaptive fragmentation, such as multi-scale video analysis so that fragment length can be determined on-the-fly during query time. System optimization: In exploratory search, user starts by trial-n-error querying before video navigation. Real-time performance between the time that a query is issued and the results are displayed significantly impacts user experience. Hence, future research should study optimization of different system parameters, for example the tradeoff between the complexity of recommendation algorithm and system response time.

11210514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210514.value: This project investigates algorithms and techniques to enhance video search system by providing multi-perspective information access and navigation. Analysis of different information facets, including topic, person, opinion, sentiment, is studied. In topic analysis, a hierarchy tree for browsing different aspects of a topic is constructed, by mapping the most suitable set of videos to nodes in the tree. The prototype of tree is initially constructed from Wikipedia pages, and then sequentially refined based on the facets mined from video content. In person analysis, the faces in videos are first named and then leveraged to create links within and between videos for fast navigation. In opinion and sentiment analysis, multi-modal and cross-modal analysis, based on audio-visual signal, video metadata and face information, is studied for clip segmentation and emotion analysis. Based on these multimedia analyses, user studies have been designed to compare different techniques, including list-wise, hierarchy and recommendation based presentation, for browsing and navigation. Experimental results are favorable to the cases where user can efficiently explore the search space with cues that provide possible navigation paths. Examples include the use of topical tree to navigate search results, and visualization of search result distribution in feature space as recommendation for next possible query.

11210814.label: Realisation of objectives
11210814.value: Understanding cell migration in a three-dimensional (3D) microenvironment is essential as most cells encounter complex 3D extra-cellular matrix (ECM) in vivo. Although interactions between cells and ECM have been studied previously on two dimensional (2D) surfaces, cell migration studies in 3D environment are still limited. To investigate cell migration under various degrees of confinements and coating conditions, 3D platforms with micropost arrays and controlled fibronectin (FN) protein coating were developed. MC3T3-E1 cells spread and contacted the top surface of microposts if FN was coated on top. When FN was coated all over the microposts, cells were trapped between microposts with 3 μm spacing and barely moved. As the spacing between microposts increased from 3 to 5 μm, cells became elongated with limited cell movement of 0.18 μm/min, slower than the cell migration speed of 0.40 μm/min when cells moved on top. When cells were trapped in between the microposts, cell nuclei were distorted and actin-filaments formed along the sidewalls of microposts. With the addition of a top cover to introduce cell confinement, the cell migration speed was 0.23 and 0.84 μm/min when the channel height was reduced from 20 to 10 μm, respectively. Cell traction force was monitored at on the top and bottom microposts with 10 μm channel height. These results show that the MC3T3-E1 cell morphology, migration speed, and movement position were affected by surface coating and physical confinement, which will provide significant insights for in vivo cell migration within a 3D ECM. MC3T3-E1 osteoblastic cell migration was tracked in between opposing flat surfaces and double-sided micropost arrays with different separating distances. Cells with 10 μm separation between flat surfaces migrated in a larger range with a higher speed of 0.69±0.03 μm/min compared with cells with 15 μm separation between flat surfaces (0.50±0.04 μm/min). Similarly, the cell migration speed in between double-sided micropost arrays with 10 μm separation was 0.61±0.07 μm/min and was higher than that in between 15 μm-separated micropost arrays with a speed of 0.47±0.05 μm/min. To correlate cell traction force development during cell migration under confinement, the cell traction force on the top and bottom micropost layers was measured during forward cell migration in between opposing surfaces with the separating distance changed from 10 to 15 μm. Similar to 2D lamellipodial migration in the forward direction, the cyclic development of cell traction force in the leading, middle, and trailing regions was observed at the bottom micropost layer. Cell adhesion and traction force on the top surface became weaker when the separation was 15 μm. By decreasing the separation distance from 15 to 10 μm, the traction force on the top micropost layer showed correlation with cell shape and speed during forward cell migration. As a cell protruded its leading lamella and became elongated, the traction force in the leading region increased and showed a larger difference compared with that in the trailing region. The total traction force in the leading region generated on both surfaces with 10 and 15 μm separation was 66.1±4.5 and 44.1±3.1 nN, respectively. In the trailing region, the total traction force with 10 and 15 μm separation were 36.0±2.3 and 34.0±5.1 nN, respectively. The contact effect in 3D ECM was also investigated by modifying the micropost density on top. The spacing between microposts on top was increased from 3 to 5 μm, whereas the spacing between microposts at the bottom remained at 3 μm. As the spacing on the top microposts increased from 3 to 5 μm with 10 μm separation, the migration speed decreased from 0.61±0.07 to 0.50±0.08 μm/min, and the leading region traction force decreased from 28.6±2.5 to 17.8±4.0 nN on top micropost layer. When the separation distance was increased from 10 to 15 μm, the cell migration speed and leading traction force on top further decreased.

11210814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210814.value: Real time monitoring of cell traction force was carried out for cell migration in forward and reversed directions. Dynamic traction force development under guided, directional cell migration was studied for the first time. The results showed that cell–ECM interactions are regulated by topographical guidance that could influence cell migration speed and direction. MC3T3-E1 osteoblast cell migration within 3D microenvironments with various degrees of confinement was investigated. To acquire insights in cell migration within confined structures, the fluorescent distributions of cell nucleus, actin-filament, and vinculin were investigated. The morphologies of cell spreading within 3D matrix were obtained using SEM. The cell migration trajectories and speed were compared during cell migration on micropost platforms with various confinements. To create the 3D platforms, covers were placed at different separation distance above the micropost arrays. The traction force generated in the leading region was primarily determined by the separating distance and was also affected by the density of microposts. Higher traction force produced at the leading region of cells during migration in 3D ECM created a larger force imbalance from the leading to trailing regions, which resulted in higher cell migration speed. To our best knowledge, this is the first study to map the dynamic development of cell traction force on top and bottom surfaces cell contacted in a 3D microenvironment. These results will provide better understanding of adherent cell migration in 3D ECM in vivo. Other cellular types with different migration modes and cellular states, such as tumour cells with the ability to switch between amoeboid-mesenchymal movements when activated, can be seeded on similar platforms to investigate the physical mechanisms of cell migration. Hence, these double-sided micropost sensing arrays provided broad applications and the results of 3D cell traction force are useful for designing platforms to control cell migration.

11211014.label: Realisation of objectives
11211014.value: We have extended and developed further our near stoichiometric (NS) lithium niobate (LiNbO3 or LN) optical waveguide fabrication process based on diffusion process and vapour transport equilibrium (VTE) treatment. We have studied shallow NS shallow Mg:LN and lithium tantalate (LT) waveguides doped with scandium (Sc), zirconium (Zr), and gallium (Ga), and have observed a new physical phenomenon: diffusion control of an ion by another. The electro-optic properties of these waveguides have also been studied. The fabricated waveguides exhibit interesting properties and are optical-damage resistant, which is important for Difference Frequency Generation (DFG) application where high power pumping is required. The results of these work have been published. To demonstrate the grating effect, a tunable electro-optic broadband filter based on long period grating in Ti:LN waveguide has been fabricated. The filter has a stop-band in the 1.1–1.3 (1.4–1.6) μm spectral region for a grating pitch of 675 (880) μm, and a contrast that increases linearly to ∼30 dB as the voltage is increased to 300 V. Periodically poling of LN waveguide has also been started, but unfortunately the high voltage source was damaged and could not be replaced. To overcome this, we have contacted other researchers, and in December 2016 Dr Sakellaris Mailis (Associate Professor) from Southampton University (England) agreed to help. After some discussions through emails an agreement was reached, and we were informed to contact Dr Corin Gawith from Covesion (who stock the photolithographic resources) with regards to the grating photolithographic process, and unfortunately the exact grating periodicity we wanted was not available. We have then designed the DFG device, and fabricated some samples based on our NS shallow waveguide work. The samples were sent to Dr Sakellaris in early 2018. Latest news is that the cleanroom in Southampton was closed for maintenance for most of April, and there is a large backlog of jobs that need to be done. The samples will not be poled before the end of June 2018, and we have to wait.

11211014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211014.value: Other than LN material we have also investigated LT material (less developed due to the lower Ti diffusivity and higher waveguide loss), because most properties of LT are as favourable as those of LN, and some are even advantageous, such as smaller birefringence, two orders of magnitude higher resistance to optical damage, higher quasi-phase-match (QPM) frequency conversion efficiency, and being an attractive candidate for UV radiation generation based on periodically poled PPLT. A polarization-insensitive shallow NS LT waveguide has been demonstrated (the waveguide loss is 0.2/0.3 dB/cm for the TE/TM mode and the waveguide is promising for developing an optical-damage-resistant device that requires a shallow mode field profile). Interesting results have been achieved, especially on the realization of near-stoichiometric (NS) LN and LT strip waveguides form by metal (Ti, Zr, Ga, Sc) diffusion followed by Li-rich vapor transport equilibration. The waveguides exhibit low loss and are optical damage resistant, making them attractive for passive devices which require a shallow waveguide, such as photonic crystal, electro-optic, and periodic poled waveguide devices. We demonstrated that the EO property of Mg doped LN depends strongly on the Mg concentration, and there are two concentration thresholds (CMg~1.2 – 2 mol% and 4.5-5 mol%) of photorefractive damage. Also, a new physical phenomenon: diffusion control of an ion by another, has been observed and reported. The results have been published in international refereed journals. Although periodic poling was not carried out at CityU due to the damage of the high voltage source, we have established contact and collaboration with Southampton University who will do the poling. We have also designed the periodic poled DFG waveguide, and are waiting for the return of the samples.

11211014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211014.value: Once the samples are sent back from Southampton University we shall try and characterize the devices. The DFG uses a commercially available high-power 780nm wavelength laser diode as the pump source, and an external cavity laser with 1500-1558nm output wavelength range as the signal source. The device functions simultaneously as two coherent radiation sources, generating tunable, narrowband near-infrared (NIR) waves and THz waves. The periodically poled strip waveguide device combines a number of merits, and there are strong commercial interests on THz sources.

11211014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211014.value: The excellent electro-optic, acousto-optic, and nonlinear optical properties of congruent ([Li]/[Nb]~0.945) lithium niobate (LiNbO3 or LN) and lithium tantalite (LT) optical waveguides have led to the development of high functionality devices and optical integrated circuits. However, serious photorefractive damage in both visible and near infrared wavelength regions limits the applications of these devices. In this project, we have further developed our novel fabrication process based on diffusion process and vapor transport equilibration (VTE) treatment, and realized near-stoichiometric (NS, [Li]/[Nb]>0.98) metal diffused LN/LT and magnesium oxide (MgO) doped LN/LT waveguides. The NS waveguide exhibits similar bulk NS material properties and has a number of advantages over congruent material. Most importantly, the NS waveguide exhibits lower photorefractive damage susceptibility, enabling the device to operate in the visible and near infrared wavelength region. We have studied and characterized the diffusion of different metal ions (such as titanium, scandium, zirconium, and gallium) their effects on the formation of the optical waveguides, and have demonstrated an optical filter. We have also designed a quasi-phase-matched (QPM) difference frequency generator (DFG) utilizing periodically poled NS Ti:Mg:LN strip waveguide

11211114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211114.value: 大塊金屬玻璃擁有異於一般金屬材料的性能組合，可以成為一些特殊應用的理想材料。再加上可透過鑄造或熱塑性加工而直接成型複雜細緻的產品，大塊金屬玻璃已應用於傳感器，微機械等。熱塑性加工需要將金屬玻璃加熱到玻璃轉變溫度以上，令材料變成像高黏度流體狀態以便成形。此計劃研究人員提出以脈沖電流加熱材料以改善加工流程。研究組以往已成功利用脈沖電流處理鎂合金等難加工物料，確定這方法加工時間短及節省能源等優點。所以研究組希望以這相對未獲廣泛應用的技術去提昇金屬玻璃加工的水平。假若計劃進展順利，研究組預計可以確立脈沖電流處理金屬玻璃的加工流程及可行的相關參數範圍。這技術將會有極大應用前景，並能令金屬玻璃有更廣的應用。此外，通過詳細的微結構研究，可加深對金屬玻璃變形機理及脈沖電流對微結構影響的了解。

11211114.label: Realisation of objectives
11211114.value: The project team carried out investigations on the pulse-current assisted plastic deformation of metallic glass to address Objectives 1 and 2. A commercially available iron-based metallic glass ribbon was used for investigating the effects of large current pulses on the relaxation and deformation behaviour of a glassy alloy. Current pulses with peak current density of 400 – 520 A/cm^2 were applied to the glassy ribbons of dimensions 10mm x 80mm x 0.025mm. Various frequencies of the current pulses were used and the total treatment time was fixed at 30 seconds. In one set of the experiments, the glassy ribbons were bent to different curvature before the current pulses were applied. The bending stress was well below the yield stress or failure stress of the metallic glass so that only elastic strain was observed before the pulsed-current treatment. After the treatments, all the ribbons exhibited permanent deformation, while remaining amorphous as indicated by the XRD and DSC results. The permanent deformation of the metallic glass ribbons was explained in terms of structural relaxation of the glassy structure under the combined effects of thermal and athermal factors. Since the temperatures of the ribbons were well below the glass transition temperature of the metallic glass during the treatment, as monitored by a infrared thermoscope, therefore the joule-heating effect alone was not sufficient to cause the relaxation. It was proposed that the ‘electron wind’ arising from the large current density during the treatment can transfer momentum to the atoms or clusters in the metallic glass. This ‘force’ can assist atomic diffusion and reduce the energy barrier for structural relaxation. In another set of experiments, instead of pre-stressing the metallic glass and allow structural relaxation to proceed during electropulsing treatment, mechanical stress was applied to the glassy ribbons through a copper punch attached to a tensile testing machine while current pulses passed through the ribbons. The current pulses parameters were more or less that same as those used in the first set of experiments described above. The temperatures of the ribbons during treatment measured with IR thermoscope were all well below the glass transition temperature. If no current was passed through the glassy ribbon, there was no observable plastic deformation after punching. However, with the simultaneous application of current pulses and stress, obvious drawing marks, viz. plastic deformation, could be seen in the glassy ribbons. The ribbons remained amorphous after the current pulse treatment as confirmed by XRD and wide-angle x-ray scattering. The load in the ribbons during the treatment exhibited periodic variations with the same frequency as the applied current pulses. These observations indirectly indicated that the large current density pulses might exert an ‘electron wind force’ on the atoms or clusters in the ribbon. This athermal effect was expected to work in conjunction with the joule heating effect of the electric current to promote atomic diffusion and made plastic deformation of the metallic glass at temperatures significantly lower than the glass transition. In order to address Objective 3, series of ternary RE-Al-Ge alloys were prepared and characterized to investigate the atomic scale structures, including short-range and long-range order, of the alloys. By detailed analysis of the x-ray diffraction and selected area electron diffraction results, the crystal symmetry of the alloy phases as well as the local atomic environments were determined. The electronic structure of the alloys determined with the structural results from XRD and SAED. From the experimental results, It is apparent that the structural modulations in the ternary alloys are dependent on the nature of the rare-earth metals and the amount of vacancies at the aluminum sites. With all these experimental findings, which had been published in international refereed journals, all the three objectives were considered achieved satisfactorily.
