11211114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211114.value: In this study, the PI and his team carried out systematic experiments on electric current assisted plastic deformation of Fe78B13Si9 metallic glass ribbons. The detailed atomic scale structure of a family of ternary RE-Al-Ge alloys were determined, the experience of which may help the understanding of the cluster structures of metallic glasses. In the first set of current assisted deformation experiment, the metallic glass ribbons were bent into a U-shape between a pair of copper electrodes to different curvature before the current pulses were applied. The bending stress was well below the yield stress or failure stress of the metallic glass so that only elastic strain was observed before the current pulses treatment. The ribbons were subjected to electropulsing with peak current density of 400 – 520 A/cm^2 for 30 s. The temperature of the ribbon did not exceed the glass transition temperature under the electropulsing treatment. The ribbons were permanently deformed after electropulsing and remained amorphous. By varying the electrode separation, current and pulsing frequency, the extent of permanent bending could be controlled. It was concluded that momentum transfer by electron led to enhancement of free volume motion in the sample. This is more effective than softening by conventional heating. This work revealed a faster and easier novel way of shaping metallic glasses of limited plasticity, while evading embrittlement and crystallization. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 1 in Part C, Section 8). The process described above required pre-stressing prior to electropulsing and large elastic recovery limited the dimensional accuracy of the forming process. In the second set of experiment, metallic glass ribbons were subjected to punching with electropulsing applied simultaneously in various combinations of frequency and punching speed. Process temperature was measured to be significantly below the glass transition temperature and the process only takes 20-30 s. Lower load was required to punch the ribbon with electrical pulses applied. All the ribbons were fully deformed without spring back after the punch was retracted. The ribbons were essentially amorphous after the treatment, with only some rare cases suffering from embrittlement. The electric current provided a directional force acting as an aid to overcome the activation barrier of shear transformation zones. However, as a side effect joule heating also accelerated beta relaxation causing the embrittlement. This study revealed a novel way of shaping metallic glasses with the potential of industrial scale application. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 2 in Part C, Section 8). Ternary alloys with general formulae REAl(1–x)Ge3 (RE = Nd, Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, and Ho; 0.6 < x < 0.9) were prepared for glass-forming ability and atomic scale structure investigations. The structures have been characterized by X-ray diffraction and selected area electron diffraction. The average structure represents a variant of the orthorhombic SmNiGe3-type structure, where the Al atoms are found at the Ni site, and the deep off-stoichiometry is due to statistical vacancies at this position. Electron diffraction suggests the existence of two different short-range ordered structures depending on the nature of the rare-earth metals: a monoclinic structure for the Nd and Sm analogs, and an orthorhombic structure for members based on the heavier rare-earth metals. Longer-range commensurate and incommensurate structural modulations based on these parent structures are also observed, attesting to the structural complexity arising from the existence of aluminum vacancies. Magnetic susceptibility measurements of these compounds are presented and discussed, as well as the results from electronic band-structure calculations. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 3 in Part C, Section 8).

11211114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211114.value: It was demonstrated by our experimental results that large amplitude current pulses applied through metallic glass samples during plastic loading can reduce the load and time required for deforming metallic glass. The structures remain glassy after the current-assisted plastic deformation when the process parameters were selected correctly. These findings open the possibility of rapid plastic forming of metallic glass without the need to pre-heat the sample and the risk of embrittlement due to partial crystallization. Such processing technology can broaden the range of application of metallic glass by lowering the processing cost because complex shaped components can be produced by high precision forming of pre-cast blanks with the help of pulsed-current. Furthermore, the controlling factors of formation of short-range and long-range order in ternary RE-Al-Ge and RE-Al-Si alloys are not yet fully understood. This can be a meaningful direction for further pursuit.

11211114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211114.value: Metallic glasses possess interesting combinations of properties which are peculiar to this family of materials. However, their applications are usually limited by the difficulties in forming the materials in the desired geometry at a low processing cost. The current-assisted plastic deformation processes investigated in this project is a novel way of shaping metallic glass with much lower risk of embrittlement, mainly due to partial crystallization, compared with the well-known thermoplastic forming process. When the processing parameters are properly chosen, the metallic glass can be shaped at a temperature significantly lower than its glass transition temperature and therefore evading crystallization, or even structural relaxation. The desirable combination of properties of the glassy state can therefore be retained after plastic forming. On the scientific side, the mechanism of the interactions of the current, viz. rapidly moving electrons, and the atoms or atomic clusters in metallic glass is still not well understood. Our experimental results can potentially lead to insights for more thorough understanding of the interactions involved in the pulse-current treatment.

11211314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211314.value: 儘管市場对有效治療許多中樞神經系統疾病的藥物有著巨大需求，只有僅僅7％的針對神經系統開發的藥物能夠發展到臨床終端。造成這樣低的成功率的原因主要有兩個：第一是人腦具有獨特而顯著的複雜性; 第二是因為缺乏能夠快速在活體動物的大腦器官層面快速評估大量藥物前導物的的關鍵技術。理想情況下，評估潛在藥物的在大腦中的作用需要在用藥的情況下關聯特定的神經元的活動與特定行為活動，也就是通常所說的大腦活動映射。用於全腦活動監測與映射的高通量技術對于基礎和轉化神經科學的研究將是非常寶貴的。為了實現這一目標，本計畫將利用轉基因斑馬魚作為脊椎動物模型，通過應用不同的電子和生物醫學工程方法解決幾個觀測斑馬魚全腦活動的關鍵問題，開發一個自動化系統具備在未麻醉的斑馬魚活體中進行大腦性活動的高通量映射的能力，并初步驗證其在篩選神經系統藥物的潛在用途。

11211314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211314.value: The reconstruction of neural activity across complete neural circuits, or brain activity mapping, has great potential in both fundamental and translational neuroscience research. Larval zebrafish, a vertebrate model, has recently been demonstrated to be amenable for whole brain activity mapping in behaving animals. In project, we develop system enabled high-throughput, gel-free, and anesthetic-free manipulation of larvae, and thus allowed real-time observation of behavioral responses, and associated physiological changes at cellular resolution within specific organs in response to acute ethanol stimuli, which would otherwise be impossible by using traditional methods for larva immobilization and orientation. Specifically, three types of chips (“motion”, “lateral” and “dorsal”), based on a simple hydrodynamic design, were used to perform analysis in animal behavior, cardiac and brain physiology respectively. This versatile Fish-on-Chip platform could potentially be adopted for systematic cross-organ investigations involving chemical or genetic manipulations in zebrafish model. We further develop demonstrate the use of the microfluidic array system (″Fish-Trap″) to enable high-throughput mapping of brain-wide activity in awake larval zebrafish. Unlike the commonly practiced larva-processing methods using rigid gel or capillary tube, which are laborious and time-consuming, the hydrodynamic design of our microfluidic chip allows automatic, gel-free, and anesthetic-free processing of tens of larvae for microscopic imaging with single cell resolution. Notably, this system provides the capability to directly couple pharmaceutical stimuli with real-time recording of neural activity in a large number of animals; and the local and global effects of pharmacoactive drugs on the nervous system can be directly visualized and evaluated by analyzing drug-induced functional perturbation within or across different brain regions. Using this technology, we tested a set of neurotoxin peptides, and obtained new insights about how to exploit neurotoxin derivatives as therapeutic agents. The novel and versatile ″Fish-Trap″ technology can be readily unitized to study other stimuli (optical, acoustic, or physical) associated functional brain circuits using similar experimental strategies.

11211314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211314.value: For potential further development, the technology for in vivo high-throughput brain activity mapping can be exploited for drug screening. Specifically, the evaluation of drug leads would preferably need to correlate the activation of specific neurons with the execution of certain behaviours under normal or drug treated conditions, which is commonly referred as Brain Activity Map (BAM). Future study could develop a completely novel screen system that is capable of evaluating and predicting the neuropharmacological property of various compounds using functional data acquired by in vivo high-throughput mapping of brain-wide activities in live and awake vertebrate animals. If we can acquire a sufficiently large library of BAMs for many compounds, we can apply bioinformatic approaches to analyze and cluster the compound-specific signatures based upon their brain activity map, and to make association of such clusters with the chemical/molecular properties of testing compounds. So that we can create a functional classifier that can be used for predicting neuropharmacology of specific compounds by using their readily achievable brain activity map. In addition, this strategy also to provide an exciting alternative for elucidating the molecular targets to assist in the development of improved analogs with enhanced efficacy.

11211314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211314.value: In this study, we developed a versatile technology, namely ″Fish-Trap″, for high-throughput immobilization and orientation of live and awake larval zebrafish. It also enables single-cell-resolution imaging of specific organs in behaving and drug-responsive larvae. Using the system, we mapped the brain-wide activity in tens of vertebrate animals while in situ drug treatment. Zebrafish has become an increasingly important preclinical model for drug discoveries and development of new diagnostic tools. This model combines the scale and throughput of cell-based assays with the physiological complexity of animal studies, rendering it well suited for in vivo screening, especially for the development of biologic pharmaceuticals, many of which are currently under active investigation as therapeutics for neurological diseases. In contrast to chemically synthesized small molecules with enhanced solubility and permeability, biologic molecules have structures that are generally much larger and far more complex, and therefore require a new paradigm in the screening and evaluation of their in vivo properties, such as efficacy, toxicity, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics and tissue specificity.

11211714.label: Project Objectives
11211714.value: To develop a direct sensing methodology for quantitatively measuring cell protrusion force and the protrusion force distribution at the cell leading edge using a robot-aided cell manipulation system equipped with optical tweezers. To develop a dynamic modeling approach for determining the relationship amongst the protrusion force, the chemoattractant gradient, and the cell motion, particularly the influence of the chemoattractant gradient and concentration on cell migration. To develop an automated control approach that will direct migrating cells to follow robotically controlled chemoattractant-loaded microbeads. A leader–follower control strategy will be incorporated into a potential field function to develop a controller that will drive the cell–bead complexes to desired positions while avoiding collisions with other obstacles in the environment.

11211714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211714.value: Cell migration is directional cell movement in response to a chemoattractant gradient, a process that occurs in a wide variety of biological phenomena and has recently attracted increased attention. However, the mechanism by which a chemoattractant gradient induces cell migration remains unknown, inhibiting further advances in cell motility research. To fill in this knowledge gap, we propose the use of a robot-aided cell manipulation system equipped with optical tweezers to probe the mechanism of cell migration and to control cell migration by following optically trapped chemoattractant-loaded microsources. We proposed to conduct this research from three different perspectives: sensing, modeling, and control. In sensing, we will develop a new method that allows direct measurement of the cell protrusion force, which is generated by actin polymerization and drives the cell to move toward the stimulus as induced by the chemoattractant gradient. Through this study, we will understand the range of the protrusion force of live cells as well as the force distribution at the cell leading edge. In modeling, we will establish a dynamic cell migration model that will, for the first time, quantitatively describe the relationship amongst the cell protrusion force, the chemoattractant gradient, and cell movement velocity. This study will lay a solid foundation for controlling cell migration, which will be conducted in the next step. In control, we will focus on the automated transportation of cells to desired positions led by chemoattractant-loaded microbeads. We will use the leader–follower control strategy and potential field functions to design a controller that will drive the cell–bead coalition to the desired position while avoiding collisions with other obstacles in the environment. Upon completion of this project, proof-of-concept demonstrations with a complete set of quantitative data will be produced. These data will help probe the mechanism of cell migration and provide a new opportunity to control cell migration behavior. The success of this research will benefit many biomedical applications, such as the probing of the regulatory mechanism that directs the migration of hematopoietic stem cells and acute myeloid leukemia cells to and from the bone marrow niche. Another benefit is facilitating the native sensing of live cells treated with potential drugs for drug discovery. Immediate observation of the cellular responses to specific drugs using the proposed method will significantly help to reduce both the time cycle and the cost of drug development. 本項目旨在研究用於探索細胞趨化遷移機理的測量，建模和控制方法。首先，利用可以控制細胞運動的機器人輔助光鑷捕獲平臺，通過光鑷捕獲和機器人控制的特殊微粒（例如PLGA微珠）釋放趨化因數來刺激和控制細胞的運動。重點研究如何利用該平臺測量細胞的遷移力。其次，將研究細胞趨化遷移的動力學模型，找出影響細胞遷移的重要參數。在以上兩項研究的基礎上，最後將探索影響細胞遷移過程的控制演算法。

11211714.label: Realisation of objectives
11211714.value: To achieve the first objective of developing a direct sensing methodology for quantitatively measuring cell protrusion force and the protrusion force distribution, we have developed a new methodology for the direct measurement of cell protrusion force utilizing a robot-aided optical tweezer system. The functionalized beads that are robotically trapped and placed near the cell serve as both cell migration stimulators and protrusion force probes. The force generated by the actin polymerization of the cell propels the bead to move away from the trapping center when the cell comes in contact with the bead. Such a deviation can be determined and used to calculate the trapping force, which is equal to the protrusion force at a balanced position. With the quantitative measurement of the protrusion, we find that the protrusion force of a live cell in response to a chemoattractant within the range of hundreds of piconewtons. We further probe the protrusion force distribution at the cell leading edge and find that the highest protrusion force appears at the cell migration direction. These measurements can help characterize the mechanism of cell migration and lay a solid foundation for further proactive control of cell movement. To achieve the second objective of developing a dynamic modeling approach for determining the relationship amongst the protrusion force, the chemoattractant gradient, and the cell motion, we have developed a cell-migration model by mimicking in vivo migration using optically manipulated chemoattractant-loaded microsources. The model facilitates a quantitative characterization of the relationship among the protrusion force, cell motility, and chemoattractant gradient for the first time. Chemoattractant-loaded microsource beads trapped by robotically controlled optical tweezers are used to release the stimuli and consequently induce target cells to migrate into a desired region. Cell-movement dynamics under optical tweezer manipulation is analyzed. A new geometric model that confined microsource beads within the effective trapping area of the optical tweezers and the high-motility area of the cell under study is established. This model lays a solid foundation to the development of a potential field function-based controller that handled the optical tweezers in manipulating the microsource beads, thereby stimulating cells to migrate into desired regions. Simulations and experiments are further performed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. To achieve the third objective of developing an automated control approach for cell migration and transportation control, we have investigated the control of a single cell to in migration to a desired region with a unified controller. A potential field function based controller is developed to migrate the cell to a desired region. Based on a switching geometrical model for achieving automatic cell trapping, maintenance of optical trapping, and obstacle avoidance, a controller for high speed cell transportation is also proposed to transfer the target cell to the destination efficiently. A dual closed-loop control strategy is further developed, which includes an inner tweezers-bead control loop with proportional-integral feedback plus feedforward controller, and an outer bead-cell control loop with an active disturbance rejection controller. Simulation and experiments results are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. In summary, all the proposed three objectives have been accomplished successfully.

11211714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211714.value: Cell migration plays an essential role in cancer cell study. Investigation of a novel method for characterizing and controlling cell migration movement can help develop new therapeutic strategies. In this project, we have addressed the cell migration problem from three perspectives of sensing, modeling and control. In sensing, we have developed a new measurement methodology to detect cell protrusion force by utilizing a robot-aided optical tweezer system. We have also proposed on-chip cell migration assays to characterise the migration property of cancer cells, which benefits the development of new therapeutic strategies for metastasis. In modeling, we have proposed several modeling methods including a cell-migration model that mimicks in vivo migration using optically manipulated chemoattractant-loaded microsources, a geometric model that confines microsource beads within the effective trapping area of the optical tweezers and the high-motility area of the cell under study, as well as a switching geometrical model that considers cell trapping, maintenance of optical trapping, and obstacle avoidance simultaneously. Finally, various control schemes have been developed based on different models and verified by simulation and experimental studies.

11211714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211714.value: Sufficient fundamental research has been done through this project. Further development of this research should focus on application of these developments to real biomedical applications. A number of patents are to be generated through this research. Successful technology transfer is expected in the near future.

11211714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211714.value: Cell migration is directional cell movement in response to a chemoattractant gradient, a process that occurs in a wide variety of biological phenomena but its mechanism by which a chemoattractant gradient induces cell migration remains unknown. In this project, we propose the use of a robot-aided cell manipulation system equipped with optical tweezers to probe the mechanism of cell migration and to control cell migration. The research is performed from three aspects of sensing, modeling and control. In sensing, we have developed new methods to measure the cell protrusion force directly and to understand the range of the protrusion force of live cells as well as the force distribution at the cell leading edge. In modeling, we have established a dynamic cell migration model that can quantitatively describe the relationship amongst the cell protrusion force, the chemoattractant gradient, and cell movement velocity. In control, we have developed a number of automated control schemes to transport cells to desired positions while avoiding collisions with other obstacles in the environment. The success of this research will greatly benefit many biomedical applications as well as facilitate the native sensing of live cells treated with potential drugs for drug discovery.

11212114.label: Project Objectives
11212114.value: Develop theories and algorithms for maximum likelihood estimation of cascading failure source in the Internet of Things (IoT) with multiple observations. Study the performance tradeoff between the number of observations and the speed of detection. Develop computationally efficient algorithms for networks with general graph topology using diffusion tree approximations for failure source identification. Develop data analytics to study cascading failures in networks and develop network centrality to quantify network resilience. Implement cyber security protocols based on the theories and algorithms in Objectives 1 to 3 to identify the cascading failure source and enhance network resilience in a Smart Grid.

11212114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212114.value: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a novel paradigm in networking that is increasingly important with the advent of sensors that can be embedded into “things” as diverse as household appliances to the Internet and mission-critical systems such as the Smart Grid (next-generation power networks). The majority of things are imbued with the ability to communicate and network. Thus, the IoT is a network of networks with many unique characteristics that requires new fundamental understanding of the interactions and inter-dependencies. Where simple connectivity rules between “things” can lead to almost limitless possibilities – the complexity of IoT interconnections rapidly outstrips our ability to unravel them. The IoT networks could mash together introducing or accelerating black swan events: catastrophic cascading failures that are unexpected but obvious in hindsight. As IoT devices collect data, relay information to one another and process information collaboratively, it is important to understand the cascading prowess of IoT. An action triggered by one device, e.g., failure, could lead to a cascade of other state changes and messages being exchanged with the other devices. Understanding this embedded interaction and cascading failure effect is important to guarantee security and reliability in IoT. Detection and identification of cascading failure sources in the IoT allows timely quarantine of the failure. For example, law enforcement agencies want to identify the perpetrators who attack the Smart Grid sensors that leads to widespread power blackout. How to identify the source of the cascading failure remains a rather unexplored and challenging problem, which is complicated by the size of the network that can lead to computational intractability. There are no existing work on this problem for a general network topology. The goal of this project is to develop new mathematical theories and algorithms to identify cascading failure sources in IoT. In particular, the project aims to develop inference with multiple observations to detect failure source as quickly as possible, and to quantify the detection performance based on cascading models that well represent IoT applications. The novelty in our research is to utilize novel links between probability theory and statistical inference on graph to quantify the detection performance for networks of finite as well as asymptotically large size, and analyze the tradeoff between reliability, security and speed of detection. The result is a new cyber-security protocol design to enhance the network resilience of IoT in a Smart Grid by identifying risks before attackers do. 物聯網（Internet of Things）是一個新的網絡模式，是因傳感器可以嵌入到不同的家電互聯網和關鍵任務系統，如智能電網（下一代發電電力網絡）並發展成“物聯網”。大部分的物器擁有網絡溝通的能力，並需要相互依賴。因此，物聯網具有許多獨特的網絡數據收集和處理信息的特徵。“物”與“物”之間的簡單連接規則可以導致幾乎無限的可能性，並增大物聯網互連的複雜性。這種網絡複雜性可以造成災難性的連鎖故障意外。一台物器設備的失效，可能導致其他狀態改變和消息的級聯被交換等後果。成功檢測連鎖故障源可以及時隔離故障。因此，了解這種嵌入式的互動和網絡連鎖故障是很重要的，以確保物聯網的安全性和可靠性。例如，當大規模的停電發生時，執法機構要確定誰攻擊了智能電網的傳感器，根除肇事者。如何識別連鎖故障的來源是一個富有挑戰性和計算規模複雜的網絡問題。這個問題涉及信息傳播和網絡拓撲結構。該項目的目標是開發新的數學理論和算法，以確定物聯網連鎖故障源，尤其是開發推理與多個觀測來快速檢測故障源，並研究基礎的量化級聯模式，以及物聯網應用的檢測性能。該項目研究中的新穎之處在於，利用概率論和統計推斷之間新的鏈接圖形可以量化為有限網絡以及漸近大尺寸的檢測性能來分析網絡可靠性，安全性和檢測的速度之間的權衡。研究結果是一個新的網絡安全協議設計，準確識別風險，以提高物聯網在智能電網的網絡彈性。

11212114.label: Realisation of objectives
11212114.value: All the four objectives have been realized through the publication in top-tiered conferences and journals. We have developed theories and algorithms for maximum likelihood estimation problems in Smart Grid and the Internet of Things (IoT). We have developed computationally efficient algorithms for wireless networks with general graph topology. We have developed data analytics in cyberspace networks and develop network centrality to quantify network resilience. We have implemented cyber security protocols based on the theories and algorithms to enhance network resilience in a Smart Grid. In particular, we have developed a network centrality measure to solve maximum-likelihood estimation problems in large networks. Our work in this project is best summarized in a top-tiered journal publication "Averting Cascading Failures in Networked Infrastructures: Poset-constrained Graph Algorithms," to be published in August 2018 in the IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, which runs a Special Issue on Signal and Information Processing for Critical Infrastructures. This work has led to rigorous theories and computationally-fast algorithm design to analyze cascading failure source in the Internet of Things (IoT) and to enhance network resilience in smart grids and many critical infrastructures.

11213114.label: Project Objectives
11213114.value: To study the optimal group buying strategy for on-demand VM instances. Given a set of users with arbitrary VM instance demands, we study the optimal strategy to buy resource so as to minimize the total cost of all users in a group, which is achieved by leveraging the pricing model that renting a dedicated server is cheaper than renting a set of VM instances with the same total capacity. To study the optimal group-buying strategy with time-varying demands and long-term reservation. Considering the time-multiplexing of VM instances among different users in a group and the discount for long-term reservations, we study the optimal group-buying strategy on long-term reservations and on-demand instances as well as the scheduling of VMs on long-term reserved instances. To study a fair cost sharing among a group of users. To ensure that each user pays less after joining group buying, we will build up cooperative game and study the cost sharing for each user so that no users have any incentive to leave the grand coalition to form their own small coalition. To study the implication and possible responding pricing strategy for cloud service providers when group buying becomes a new pricing model. To this end, we will study a two-stage game, where the cloud provider makes the pricing decision in the first stage, and group buying is formed in the second stage upon the first-stage pricing decision. By predicting the second-stage decision, the cloud provider can optimize the pricing decision to maximize its profit.

11213114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213114.value: Low cost is the biggest slogan of cloud computing, serving as the major incentive for users to adopt cloud services. There is no doubt that further lowering cost will accelerate the adoption rate of cloud computing. While cloud providers can optimize their resource provisioning and scheduling to offer low-cost services to users, users can also take some actions to reduce cost by themselves, for example, via group buying. Group buying, where multiple buyers jointly make a large-volume order for a better deal, has recently become prevalent in e-commerce. In cloud computing, people have also started to raise the possibility of group buying. Group buying for cloud computing, however, is more complicated than group buying for conventional products because cloud computing demands are multi-attribute and time varying, and involve virtual machine assignment and even communication inside the cloud. Therefore, we see a timely need to understand group buying for cloud computing. Roughly speaking, the benefit of group buying for cloud resources comes directly from the different pricing schemes on the current cloud market, e.g., lower unit price for a bigger volume (or dedicated servers) and lower hourly cost for long-term reserved instances. Hence multiple users can pool their demands together and leverage those pricing schemes to reduce their cost. To implement group buying, we need to tackle several challenges. First, given multiple users, each of which has an arbitrary resource demand, we need an optimal purchasing decision to minimize the total cost for all users. Second, we need to design a fair cost sharing scheme for the users to share the total cost so that every user has an incentive to join group buying. The former issue is a hard optimization problem. While it may look similar to the cloud provider's resource provisioning problem, it is more challenging due to the intricacy of different pricing schemes such as on-demand instances and long-term reservation. The latter issue involves cooperative game theory, which will provide a theoretical foundation to ensure the stability of group buying. At last, based on the research on users’ group buying behaviors, the cloud provider may also manipulate the pricing schemes to retrieve a higher profit. This project aims to address the aforementioned challenges in group buying of cloud resources. The results will certainly provide firm answers on whether group-buying is the future pricing model in cloud computing and how to practice it if the answer is yes. 低成本一直是云计算吸引用户的口号。毫无疑问， 进一步地降低费用会加速云计算的使用率。 除了云提供商能优化他们的资源分配与调度以降低收费外， 云使用者也能通过团购来降低他们的使用费用。 团购是电子商务里一个很流行的商业模式， 主要是通过多个买家联手买下一个单位成本低的大的订单以减低每个用户的费用。 云计算里的团购， 比传统的团购其他的商品更复杂， 因为云计算的需求是多维， 随时间变化的， 并且涉及虚机的分配， 甚至云内的通讯。 这些特殊的属性使得研究云计算的团购变得很必要。 简单地说， 云计算的团购的利益直接来源于当前的云市场上的不同的定价机制， 比如， 量大， 单位价格就低， 长期租户， 每小时的费用就低。 因此多个用户可以将他们的需求集合起来， 利用这些价格机制来降低他们的使用成本。 实现云计算的团购， 我们需要解决一下的挑战。 首先， 给定多个用户， 每个有自己任意的资源需求， 我们需要设计一个最优的购买决策以最小化所有用户的总费用。这个问题虽然与云计算的资源分配问题有相似性， 因为要考虑不同的定价机制， 这个问题比传统的资源分配问题更为复杂。 其次， 我们需要设计一个公平的费用分摊的机制使得每个用户都有动力加入团购。 这个问题涉及协作博弈论， 其决策将对提供团购的稳定性提供理论支持。 最后， 基于用户的团购行为， 云提供商业可以设计新的更有吸引力的定价以提高他们的收益。 本项目拟解决以上提到的云计算中的团购问题的一些挑战。

11213114.label: Realisation of objectives
11213114.value: There are four objectives in this project. In simple words, Objectives 1 to 3 are concerned with a group of cloud users making joint decision on how to acquire cloud resource for online demand, for offline demand, and for cost sharing, respectively. Objective 4 focuses on issues of cloud providers. Our achievement of Objective 1 is reported in a paper published on TPDS (Part C, Section 8, No. 1). We observe that most cloud service providers offer volume discount where users pay when they request more. By leveraging the volume discount policy, cloud brokers become viable players in the cloud market. We studied how a broker can schedule on-line arrived jobs from a group of users to achieve the maximum cost reduction. We started from three special cases with all known jobs and derive optimal algorithms accordingly. Using such results as building blocks, we designed a randomized algorithm for the online problem where the demands of users arrive dynamically. We proved the lower bound of the competitive ratio of the proposed algorithm under generic concaving cost function. Objectives 2 and 3 are achieved by the papers in an INFOCOM paper (Part C, Section 9, No. 1) and an IEEE Access paper (Part C, Section 8, No. 4). In the INFOCOM paper, we consider a group of users who would like to form a coalition so that the maximum cost reduction can be enjoyed. What we are interested are how they can form stable coalitions for group buying, meaning that no one has incentive to leave the coalition for further cost reduction. We found out that no stable coalitions are sustainable under commonly used stability concepts. We then proposed a new solution concept, namely, contractually group stable, where no one can migrate from one coalition to another if its migration will cause high cost to others in either coalition. We show that stable coalitions exist in group-buying under the new stability concept. A heuristic algorithm is developed to derive individual user’s purchasing strategy in forming contractually group stable coalitions. Simulation results show that the solution can achieve significant cost reduction for cloud users. In the Access paper, we study a new application, private cloud, which needs a different solution because of the lack of money transfer. To ensure that each user can honestly tell its demand and meanwhile maximize the social welfare, we design resource allocation mechanisms and show that the proposed mechanisms are truthful for general monotonic profit functions. Theoretical analysis shows that the worst-case performance on the social welfare is bounded by a constant factor of the optimal solution for linear profit functions. Our achievement of Objective 4 is published in IEEE TSC (Part C, Section 8, No. 5). In the paper we consider mobile cloud computing, where a cloud operator can exploit the idle resources of the nearby mobile devices, making them usable for task execution. We use an auction scheme to encourage mobile devices to share their resources, and allow users to bid for the resources at mobile devices. Our major results include two parts. First, we design a distributed auction mechanism to fairly allocate the tasks and determine the trading prices of the resources. Second, we designed an efficient payment evaluation process which, through the collaboration of the buyers, eliminates possible dishonest activity of the sellers. We prove that the auction mechanism can achieve computational efficiency, individual rationality, and budget balance. Simulation results confirm the validity of the proposed auction mechanism. We have also studied service providers’ collaboration, an extended achievement of Objective 4, in a JASC paper (Part C, Section 8, No. 3). The work is motivated by one business solution, implemented in the Chinese telecom industry, of forming a joint venture responsible for building and maintaining common infrastructures. The novelty of this practice is the role of operators in that they have shares of the joint venture, and also pay to the joint venture for using the infrastructures. We study this business model from a game theoretic approach. Our results show that, if we have proper regulation on the joint venture, the market can converge to equilibria with desirable properties which cannot be achieved without the joint venture. Furthermore, we also study how the joint venture reduces the investment of the operators. It shows that a moderate user density will significantly reduce the total investment on the infrastructures.

11213114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213114.value: This project studies how multiple cloud users can purchase cloud services economically through group buying. We first consider how a broker can pool and schedule the demands of multiple users together so that the total cost of resource demands for users can be minimized by leveraging the volume discount pricing policy offered by the cloud service provider. The work is presented in the paper reported in Part C, Section 8, No. 1. The results provide mechanisms to maximize the benefits of group buying for a group of users under given pricing policies. Next we study how the cost, or equivalently, the benefits of group buying, should be shared among cloud users, which ensures the sustainability of group buying. Using the cooperative game theory, we found that many existing game theory solutions cannot provide stable coalitions. In order to sustain group-buying for cloud services, we propose a new solution concept, contractually group stable, where a user can migrate from one coalition to another if and only if its migration will not cause the higher cost of other users in either coalition. We show that this new solution concept can guarantee the existence of stable coalitions, making group-buying always possible on the cloud market. The work is presented in the paper reported in Part C, Section 9, No. 1. For the case of private clouds where there is no transfer payment among users, we designed a mechanism to ensure the truth-telling of users. The work is presented in the paper reported in Part C, Section 8, No. 4. We then study the resource management problem of cloud service providers. Specifically, we study how a mobile cloud service provider can exploit the unused resources of the nearby mobile devices, to efficiently execute the tasks from different customers. The work is presented in the paper reported in Part C, Section 8, No. 5. Furthermore, we extend the concept of group collaboration to service providers. We study the recent practice for major Chinese telecom companies to jointly build shared infrastructure, and study the potential benefit and risk. The work is presented in the paper reported in Part C, Section 8, No. 3.

11213114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213114.value: We plan to extend the work to the virtual network service provider market where multiple virtual network service providers rent resources as a group from a physical service provider. Due to the multiplexing gain of traffic, the total resource demands will be reduced when multiple virtual network service providers rent resources as group. The main challenges when applying group buying to virtual networks are 1) how to quantify the multiplexing gain of traffic; 2) how to shape and admit traffic so that fairness can be achieved for traffic from different virtual service providers so that sustainable coalition can be formed. These new challenges are similar to the problems encountered when group buying is applied to cloud computing. However, in the new domain, we will mainly consider stochastic traffic demands and delay requirements, which will make such problems new and challenging.

11213114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213114.value: Cloud computing allows users to purchase computing resource based on their need, which reduces the users’ investment on IT infrastructure. To further take advantage of economy of scale, multiple users can take the concept of “group buying“, i.e., pooling their needs together to buy cloud services as a group, to fit the pricing policies of the cloud provider. This project investigates the implementation feasibility and potential benefit of group buying for cloud computing. We have used optimization techniques to design algorithms to schedule jobs among a group of users so that they can enjoy the maximum benefits of group buying. We have designed incentive mechanisms using cooperative game theory techniques under the proposed contractual group stability concept to provide the sustainability of group buying. We have studied cooperative resource buying/sharing in not only public cloud, but also private cloud. We have extended the work to cooperative investment of joint infrastructure and pricing among multiple service providers. The project provides insightful guideline among a group of individual cloud users or service providers when they would like to cooperate for cost reduction.

11213414.label: Realisation of objectives
11213414.value: Ober the past several years, we have successfully implemented the proposed project and realized all the objectives proposed in our proposal. This project also has led to several important publications such as in Nature Physics, Nature Communications, Small, and cultivation of three PHD graduates. The success of this project is also evidenced by the receipt of many prestigious awards by our PHD graduates including the Materials Research Society (MRS) Graduate Student Gold Award (2016), MRS Graduate Student Silver Award (2015), Hong Kong Young Scientist Award (2015). Specifically, Objective 1: Elucidate the basic mechanism governing the occurrence of pancake bouncing by using analytical and numerical models. Timescale and energy criteria will be proposed. Based on the timescale and energy analysis, the strategy to achieve enhanced pancake bouncing will be proposed. Under the support of this GRF project (CityU 11213414), the PI had made exciting progress in the development of bio-inspired interfacial materials with enhanced droplet mobility as well as the elucidation of the fundamental mechanisms underpinning the peculiar phenomenon. We found that the impinging droplet directly jumps from the substrate at the end of the spreading stage in a pancake shape without undergoing significant lateral retraction. This allows for a fourfold reduction in contact time compared with conventional complete rebound (Nature Physics, 2014). Based on the Lattice Boltzmann simulation (Langmuir, 2014), as well as the theoretical interfacial energy analysis (Applied Physics Letters, 2015), we demonstrated that the pancake bouncing results from the rectification of capillary energy stored in the penetrated liquid into upward motion adequate to lift the drop. Moreover, the timescales for lateral drop spreading over the surface and for vertical motion must be comparable. Based on the energy and timescale arguments, we also formulated a general phase diagram which gives a general guideline for the design of structured surfaces which can significantly enhance the mobility of impinging droplets. The insights learned from this fundamental understanding allow us to rationally design various surfaces for many practical applications. Objective 2: Perform drop impact experiments on various surfaces with uniform spacing under different Weber numbers to validate the timescale and energy criteria. A universal parameter consisting of key topographical features, surface chemistry and drop size will be formulated and determined to provide insights for the prediction of impact scenario on different surfaces. Drop impact dynamics on multi-layered surfaces with graded spacing will be investigated to validate the hypothesis on promoting pancake bouncing through decoupling the timescale and energy requirements. We systematically fabricated various surfaces including the macrotextured tapered structures and straight post arrays, with different aspect ratios and apex angles. Conventional wisdom suggests the use of nanoscale posts with small inter-post spacings because the smaller the inter-post spacings, the greater the impact velocity the small inter-post can withstand. We demonstrate that by designing a surface with macrostructures—tapered sub-millimeter post arrays with a wide spacing, a droplet will shed from it much faster than any previously engineered materials. Moreover, under the same centre-to-centre post spacing, surfaces with a larger apex angle could give rise to more robust pancake bouncing (Applied Physics Letters, 2015). Remarkably, we found that asymmetric surfaces with a broad of architectures (concave, convex or corrugated) and millimeter-scale feature size also achieve robust contact time reduction. We show that the physical mechanism responsible for the contact time reduction does not require drop break-up. Instead, the key roles of momentum anisotropy and preferential flow around the rim of the drop are not considered. It is these that lead to the fast axial retraction on our asymmetric surfaces. Also, the drop retraction in the curved direction includes a vertical momentum component which makes it easier to lift the drop off the surface (Nature Communications, 2015). 3: Investigate the feasibility of enhancing anti-icing by pancake bouncing. De-icing properties of as-proposed surfaces will also be investigated. Preventing the formation/accumulation of ice on solid surfaces as well as promoting its easy detachment without energy input is of importance for a wide range of applications including in transportation, energy system, telecommunications and aerospace. The state of the art active ice mitigation approaches require substantial energy input and pose detrimental environmental impacts. Alternatively, passive approaches leveraging the surface wettability for anti-icing offer tremendous promises. Previously, it has shown that in contrast to the normal droplets at ambient conditions, supercooled droplets will become frozen on superhydrophobic surfaces once impact due to the increased viscosity at low temperature. Our result indicates that owing to the manifestation of reduced contact time, the droplet of room temperature can detach from the cold surface before its freezing. Currently, we are setting up a chamber which allows us to achieve an extremely low temperature, say, -50 degrees and it will be interesting to explore whether the anti-icing property will sustain at extreme environments. Similar to pancake bouncing, we also studied how the self-jumping of droplet will can be used to inhibit liquid freezing without compromising the condensation heat transfer. By creating a varying interfacial thermal barrier underneath the supercooled condensate, the biphilic structures tune the nucleation rates of water and ice in the sequential condensation-to-freezing process.

11213414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213414.value: In this project, we developed a novel surface made from tapered macrotexture arrays that enables an impinging droplet to bounce off in a pancake-like shape without undergoing the conventional retraction stage, leading to ~80% reduction in contact time. As commented by Prof. Doris Vollmer & Hans-Jürgen Butt in Nature Physics in 2014, “Zuankai’s work is especially intriguing and signifies a new direction in the field of drop impact. Their study also introduces a novel method for reducing the contact time of millimeter sized drops to values that had previously been considered impossible.” This pancake bouncing result was published in Nature Physics, and solved the 130 years’ puzzle of what is the shortest solid-liquid contact time that underlies many important technological applications. Notably, the related publications garnered from this project has already garnered over 400 citations in just three years and has been recognized by the Guinness World Records.

11213514.value: Extend the lane-based optimization method for total intersection delay minimization by incorporating a cell transmission model that can encapsulate the spatial queue propagation across upstream and downstream intersections; and Formulate the design problem into a Binary-Mixed-Integer-Non-Linear-Program (BMINLP) and solve the problem by cutting plane algorithms with improved stopping criteria to generate reliable lane markings and compatible signal timings for all involved intersections.
rows: Extend the lane-based optimization method for total intersection delay minimization by incorporating a cell transmission model that can encapsulate the spatial queue propagation across upstream and downstream intersections; and

Formulate the design problem into a Binary-Mixed-Integer-Non-Linear-Program (BMINLP) and solve the problem by cutting plane algorithms with improved stopping criteria to generate reliable lane markings and compatible signal timings for all involved intersections.

11213514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213514.value: Lane-based optimization method was developed by the principal investigator for designing signal-controlled intersections. Lane markings are directional arrows painted on ground to guide road users for making turns at signal-controlled intersections and are defined as binary variables which are then optimized with signal timings to optimize the entire intersection performance for best utilizing all available traffic lanes. Conventional lane-based optimization method for designing signal-controlled intersections adopted an unrealistic point queue system for maximizing the entire intersection capacity to let through as much traffic as possible within a signal cycle. The optimization result is always binding at the maximum allowable cycle length generating long vehicle queues along short links. This potential defect should be repaired. This proposed project will extend the lane-based optimization concept to deal with spatial queue propagation in a signal-controlled system (involving_traffic_moving_from_upstream_to downstream_intersections). Spatial vehicle queue formation and dissipation along a physical road link is much more realistic than the point (or vertical) queue. A cell transmission model divides single road link into series of cells with holding capacities that can model vehicle queue development and even spillback of physical vehicle queues (from_downstream_road_links through_upstream_intersections). The proposed study is to develop a signalized cell transmission model that is able to design lane markings and signal settings by optimizing the total delay incurred by vehicle queues. Delay and vehicle queuing minimization using traditional stage- or group- (or phase-) based methods are nonlinear but “convex” mathematical programming problem with lane markings and lane flows being fixed given parameters. Since the lane-based approach relaxes the lane markings as binary variables, the corresponding assigned lane flows are no longer fixed parameters but turned to be continuous control variables. All of these simply change the problem nature into a nonlinear and “non-convex” one. The lane-based delay and vehicle queue minimization problem becomes a “non-convex” type binary-mixed-integer-non-linear-programming problem (BMINLP). Piecewise linearization technique, that works well for convex problems, therefore becomes ineffective and inefficient to tackle non-convex problems. To solve such kind of high dimensional nonlinear non-convex mathematical programming, a cutting plane method could be applied in which series of linear hyper planes should be added until sufficient number of linear planes is created to replicate the original nonlinear solution space. The more the hyper planes added, the better the solution resolution and quality. Some new reliable stopping criteria are established to terminate adding hyper planes during the solution process making the algorithm attractive and efficient.

11213514.label: Realisation of objectives
11213514.value: For Objective 1, the lane-based optimization method has been extended in several ways (I-III). (I) The lane-based model has been extended to deal with coordinated traffic signal designs in which the original lane-based model could only be optimized for individual signal-controlled intersections without considering the important signal-coordination effects. Journal paper reviewers did concern this weakness very much. For this, while attending the international conferences during the study period, participants proposed that “MAXBAND” method could be considered. After reviewing relevant references, it is found that MAXBAND concept is to optimize the green signals to maximize the widths of a green time corridor along the major paths across all involved intersections. Journal No. 1 then optimizes the traffic signal coordination by maximizing the green bands to the selected major paths. Relevant modeling results are found in Figures 9-10 in Pages 22-23. It is found that the total network travel times including the total intersection delays are reduced by applying the proposed optimization method and results could be referred to Tables 7-8 on Page 31. (II) Concerns of the total delay evaluations are other critical comments from reviewers. In Journal No. 1, a linearized end-of-lane delay function has been proposed to predict the average delays. The quality and accuracy of it are queried although the performance of the calibrated delay function in the studied hypothetical network has been compared with the (uniform + sheared) delays by another well-calibrated equation using previously in a real network with real traffic data in Sha Tin. To respond this comment, Journal No. 2 develops a new delay prediction function taking 7 lane-based model variables as predictors including total lane flows along and not along green bands, green bandwidths, lane flow factors, lane saturation flows, effective green times, and cycle time. To execute this in the solution process, the whole formulation grows from 31 to 101 sets of governing constraints. The reason of enlarging the problem size is that many specific conditions and criteria have to be matched in the selection process so that the proper optimization outcomes from the lane-based framework can be input to the new delay prediction function properly. They are indeed a complex process in programming framework. Still, the delay prediction function could be improved by introducing more lane-based model outputs to capture more upstream, downstream, or even further downstream traffic conditions into accounts. This may be regarded as the under-achievement in the report and the attempts for improving the delay function quality have been outlined in Journal No. 2, Lines 1017-1329 in Pages 38-48. (III) As for applying the cell transmission model to model spatial queue propagation across upstream and downstream intersections, Journal Nos. 2 and 5 have applied the latest TRANSYT 15 CTM package to simulate and verify the study findings and to ensure that the spatial queue development and the total delay are not deviating from the simulation patterns. The enhanced delay prediction function in Journal No. 2 has been calibrated using the TRANSYT 15 model outputs as observed (true) figures. Figure 12 on Page 67 gives the general model calibration results and the R-square is found to be 0.884 between the predicted total delays and the TRANSYT 15 model delays. In Journal No. 5, the TRANSYT CTM package has been applied to simulate for the study intersection with short lanes. It is found that severe overflowing and queue spillback exist in operating the observed traffic signal and lane marking settings. Figure 10 in Pages 26-28 shows the queue development patterns in one signal cycle with 5s resolution for the optimized lane marking and traffic signal settings. All traffic lanes including the short lanes have no overflowing found by operating the optimized traffic signal settings. As for the under-achievement in the report, the lane-based model is now in a linear formulation and the signalized cell transmission model can also be modeled linearly. Intuitively, both could be integrate together to form a lane-based Cell Transmission Model. To model the flow dynamics across cells, the signalized cells should be controlled by traffic signal settings implying that the exit flows (=0 when red or = full saturation flow when green) are key variables. In the lane-based framework, lane markings would control the assigned flow patterns. Without the existence of a lane marking arrow for a specific turn, the associated lane turning flow must be forced to be zero. If shared lane markings are given, then different turning flows could be assigned associating with different turning proportions. In Journal No. 5, Lines 153-172 in Pages 5-6 together with Figure 2, it explains that the sent flow variables in CTM depends on cell exit flows (= saturation flow variable values in the lane-based model output) and the sent flow proportions (= turning proportion depending on turning flow variable values in the lane-based model output). Sent flows become non-linear variables when these two model variables are multiplied together. Further investigations should be conducted to overcome this modeling difficulty. For Objective 2, the BMINLP is formulated and solved by cutting plane algorithms. The proposed lane-based problem to generate reliable lane markings and compatible signal timings for intersections to avoid spatial overflowing in Journal No. 5 relies on controlling the lengths of effective red times (or durations). Non-linearity in the 2 new constraint sets in Eqs. (1-2) is due to the multiplications of two model variables in the lane-based framework. The first non-linearity is due to the multiplication of total lane flows and effective red times that should be equal to cycle time minus effective green times. The second non-linearity is due to the multiplication of the effective red times (in seconds) and reciprocal of cycle time. Direct including them as the governing constraint sets for optimization, the new lane-based design problem becomes a Binary-Mixed-Integer-Non-Linear-Program (BMINLP). The original idea of cutting plane algorithms is to add adequate linear hyper-planes to replace the original non-linear constraints in the solution process. The problem has to be solved as a Binary-Mix-Integer-Linear-Program (BMILP) by a standard CPLEX solver for optimized solutions. Following the idea of applying cutting plane algorithms, the non-linear constraint sets that have to be included to control the lengths of effective red times and effective red durations are then replaced by 4 new linear constraint sets as given in Journal No. 5 in Eqs. (3-7) for replicating the high-dimension solution space. The entire problem for solving the case study of a 4-arm intersection with a full set of 12 movement turns (3 turns from each arm x 4 arms) on 12 approach lanes requires 6,407 linear constraints, 1,520 binary variables, and 86 continuous variables. Among them, 5,556 linear constraints are the hyper planes being added by Eq. (3) [2,760 planes], Eq. (4) [24 planes], Eq. (5) [2,736 planes], Eq. (6) [12 planes], and Eq. (7) [24 planes] to simulate the original 24 non-linear constraints in Eqs. (1-2) for discretizing the maximum cycle time of 120 seconds into 120 segments. As for the solution quality, the solver has reached less than 1.0% convergence intervals to stop the solution process in 10,372 iterations. It is found that the settings are able to generate reliable lane marking and traffic signal setting patterns as reported in Journal No. 5.

11213514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213514.value: 1. The enhanced lane-based modeling framework can now be applied to optimize lane markings to establish optimized link connections for configuring signalized networks. Turns and flows at intersections can be optimized simultaneously. Still, approach and exit lanes have to be defined by users as fixed inputs. As a future development, traffic lanes from different arms could be defined either to be approach or exit lanes. Then, lane markings can then be optimized on approach lanes. This lane usage relaxation may alter the intersection and network designs significantly. Asymmetric lane arrangements could be expected. 2. Lane markings, once painted on the ground showing road users guidance to turn at intersections, are unable to be changed in daily operations irrespective to the very different demand flow patterns across the day in morning-, off-, and evening-peak periods. The enhanced lane marking optimization framework could be further extended to multi-period designs taking different demand flow patterns as inputs. Traffic signal timings could be varied with respect to one optimized set of lane marking patterns. Some trade-offs in the performances in some periods could be expected for optimizing the signalized system as a whole to control time-varying demand patterns more effectively to avoid very unbalanced designs.

11213514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213514.value: Lane-based method is the latest method for designing signal-controlled systems. Lane markings in the form of directional arrows, showing on the ground to guide drivers to turn at intersections, can be designed with signal timings. Completed works extend the designs for signal-controlled networks consisting of multiple intersections. Linked signal timings are designed to allow users traveling faster through major paths. The works are significant as the network link connections can be improved to enable smooth traffic flowing and lesser delays in the network. Red signals from signal heads would stop traffic movements at intersections. If red times are too long, long vehicle queues would be developed. Without proper control, the original lane-based method would design unreliable signal timings. Overflowing occurs. New mathematical constraints have also been developed to refine the designs by giving shorter red times especially to short lanes with limited capacities. Enhanced safety considerations are also included in the completed study to enhance the designs such as shared lane markings should not permit more than two movement turns and shared lane markings should be established on middle lanes. Pedestrian crossings should be relocated to underground or flyovers. These new requirements alter the intersection designs. New results are promising.

11213914.value: To further develop our existing solution technique for elastic quarter space in terms of generalization of its application to geometrical structures with a free surface of arbitrary tilted angles (wedge shapes). To validate the solution technique by comparison with results from FEM and experiments. To realize EHL analyses for quarter-space problems by considering firstly the classical geometry of vertical free surface, and then the general wedge structure with arbitrary tilted angles. In reality, machine elements like roller bearings, cam-followers are with axially crowned surfaces or chamfered edges to minimise the edge stress concentration. The end surface in a wedge shape is closer to the practical conditions. 11213914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213914.value: 本項目建議的研究工作涉及1/4空間接觸下的彈性流體動力潤滑研究(EHL)，該項研究目前是一個相對空白的領域。許多實際工程零部件工作接觸區接近自由端面，如滾子軸承、齒輪和鐵路輪軌接觸，這些零部件的接觸都存在沒有接觸應力的自由端面，這種結構的接觸稱為1/4空間接觸。當前所有的EHL理論和數值計算研究都是採用彈性半無限體模型，因此非常有需要清晰地研究非承載的自由端面如何影響表面變形、接觸應力和油膜壓力分佈，以及和半無限體模型計算結果之間的區別。 EHL數值分析一般都需要進行反覆運算從而獲得符合彈性變形和動力潤滑公式的計算收斂結果，對於半無限體模型，彈性變形可以直接採用Boussinesq公式進入反覆運算。但對於1/4空間的彈性變形計算，現有的一些計算理論和方法非常複雜和難解，很難應用到EHL反覆運算中，因此雖然1/4空間接觸模型更接近於實際工程接觸，在EHL分析中仍沒有應用。 對於穩態的彈流理論方面，無論實驗和理論研究，都已非常成熟，特別是20世紀60年代到80年代出了很多代表性成果。當前彈流的研究逐漸轉向更接近於實際工程工況的研究,如瞬態研究、乏油工況、熱影響、有限長模型、邊界滑移、表面粗糙度和表面結構影響等。本項研究首次對1/4空間接觸下的彈流模型進行工作，在此方面已在1/4空間接觸模型方面獲得了一種快速解法，這一方法採用矩陣方法實現了1/4空間問題的直接解析解，並實現了計算彈性變形的柔度矩陣計算方法，而該柔度矩陣方法獨立于外界載荷，對於不同載荷工況，可以採用同一柔道矩陣。因此這一種基於矩陣方法的1/4空間的解析解方法非常適合應用於需反覆運算的EHL分析，使1/4空間模型下的EHL研究成為可能，而這一方法的正確性已與現有的1/4空間彈性計算結果進行了對比驗證。 本項研究的主要目的有：1.進一步拓展矩陣解析解於一般的工況，包括契面自由端面。2.應用新的1/4彈性空間矩陣解析解法應用於EHL分析，研究工作的原創性在於首次應用1/4空間的矩陣快速解法於1/4空間和契面問題，並應用這一方法於有限長潤滑研究。 項目研究的成功，將實現1/4空間彈流問題的快速解法，通過與傳統採用半無限體模型計算結果對比，可以有效地評價自由端面的影響，並可能對現有的彈流計算公式進行修正，使其更適合應用於實際工程工況。

11213914.label: Realisation of objectives
11213914.value: (Objective 1) The first objective of the project is to extend the original solution technique, such that it is not limited to elastic quarter space problems, in which the loaded surface and the free surface is restricted to orthogonal (90 deg.). The general wedge shape of any wedge angle less than or equal to 180o is solved by the extension of the technique. We have derived an explicit matrix algorithm for solving 3D wedge problems under general surface loads: arbitrarily distributed normal and shear loads. The methodology is based on the concept of overlapping two half-spaces formed by the surfaces of a wedge and all calculations are based on half-space equivalent loads. We show that the equivalent loads on the two half-spaces are directly related to the product of the original loads on the wedge and transformation matrices. The transformation matrices are functions of wedge angle, mesh structure, and Poisson’s ratio, but not the applied load. Hence, a 3D wedge problem can be solved using those classical solutions for half-spaces once the equivalent loads are obtained. We have conducted stress analyses of elastic wedge with different wedge angles. The new algorithm was validated by comparing results of three special cases: wedge angle of 170 deg., 90 deg. and 60 deg. with half-space results, the published data of quarter-space and FEM, respectively. The comparison shows good correlation. We have demonstrated the value of the new algorithm by a study on the effect of wedge angle on internal stresses. The original objective aims at extending the technique to solve 3D wedge problems with one surface to be load-free, i.e. only one of the plane is loaded. The current development enables the technique to solve 3D wedge problems that have general loads on both surfaces. (Journal Paper #3) (Objective 2) Our solution methods were validated with results by FEM and experiments. We have used FEM packages: ANSYS and COMSOL to do the jobs. The first one was to validate our quarter-space algorithm for the calculation of surface deformation. ANSYS was used (Journal Paper #1) Second, the solution method for roller contacts (finite line contact) was validated with experimental data (Wymer D.G. and Cameron A., Proc. I.Mech.E., 188, 221-238, 1974). (Journal Paper #2) Third, solutions for cylindrical and tapered roller contacts (consideration of combined effects of two end surfaces) were verified with some cases obtained by COMSOL (Journal Paper #4). (Objective 3) The developed algorithm was used in elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) analyses. The model of cylindrical (line) contact resembles a quarter-space contact. The value of the new development for wedge shape solutions (Objective 1) is shown in the EHL analyses of contacts with different end profiles. (Journal Paper #2). (Objective 4) The new solution technique was used in EHL analyses. We examined the free edge effect on finite line contact EHL and analysed the lubrication behaviours with different roller profiles. We have found that the free end surface does not play a significant role in determining the lubrication behaviour in the centre of the line contact. If the free end is not taken into consideration (the half-space model) for the finite line contact EHL analysis, the magnitude of pressure spikes near the edge will be overestimated. The free surface can reduce pressure concentration through larger deformation, which is beneficial to lubrication behavior. We have also analyzed the Lundberg profile. The pressure distribution with the Lundberg profile is even along the axial direction, which is good for bearing applications. Apparent pressure spike is not observed near the edge, which contradicts the previous analyses that adopted the half-space model. The minimum film thickness appears near the free edge surface even when the free surface effect is considered. (Journal Paper #2) We have used the new technique to study the effect of free surface on the maximum stress (von Mises stress) in the contacting bodies. Results are being analyzed and will be published. (Objective 5) The effect of the free side surface is apparent when the applied load is close to the edge, but it will diminish when the load is far away. Typical results of an infinite block of finite width, under a Hertzian point load at its mid-span were obtained and compared with the corresponding half-space results. Similar calculations for a quarter space were also performed. The ratio of deformation at the edge and at the load centre of a block and a quarter space to that of a half space were acquired. The deformation of a block and a quarter space is bigger than that of the half space due to the effect of the free side surface. There exists no free side surface in the half space and its structure is thus stronger than the other two. Such differences become increasingly obvious as the load centre approaches the side edge. All the data points are best fitted with exponential formula with appropriate coefficients. Correction factors for the deformation at the edge and the centre of Hertzian point load for different distance of the load from the free edge are expressed with empirical formulae. The correction factors are independent of the elastic modulus of material and the load. Therefore, deformation solutions of finite block and quarter space can be readily obtained based on the half-space solutions and the corresponding correction factors. Empirical formulae for correction factors for the calculation of block or quarter-space deformation based on half-space solutions are presented (Journal Paper #4).

11213914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213914.value: Three dimensional wedge problem is still unresolved analytically. Its solutions rely on approximation techniques such as FEM. The major contribution of the project to the field is the development of a semi-analytical technique to solve the general wedge problem using an efficient matrix approach (Journal Paper #3). Our technique is based on the concept of transformation matrix which converts the original applied loads to equivalent loads in half-space. Hence, the solutions of a wedge problem can be analytically calculated using the half-space equivalent loads. This fast solution method is demonstrated to be good for elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) analysis which requires repetitive or iterative calculation for deformation (Journal Papers #2 and #3). The technique has been further developed for considering the combined effect of two end surfaces of a roller or a block with finite length (Journal Paper #4). It was found that if the distance between the two end surfaces of an infinite block is less than five times of the radius of the Hertzian point loaded zone, the effect of the other end surface cannot be ignored. Correct factors have been devised such that surface deformations of a quarter space can be obtained from the analytical half-space calculated results (Journal Paper #4).

11213914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213914.value: The technique developed in this project is only able to deal with wedge angles less than 180 degree. Engineering components or parts may have features of wedge angle greater than that, such as cutting tools and chisel tools. The current algorithm can be further developed to solve such problems, so the internal stress and deformation of cutting tools can be obtained directly. There are two types of contact problem. The current development of the technique has focused on the one in which the pressure distribution on the surface of wedge structure is predefined. There is another perspective of contact problems by considering the contact with a rigid body. For the second contact problem, the deformation on the surface of a wedge structure can be taken as the boundary condition. Further development of the current algorithm with the complementary potential energy equation can lead to the solutions of the contact of an elastic wedge structure and a rig body. The current project has devised correction factors for surface deformation of a quarter space upon the application of Hertzian point contact load. Similar works can be done with Hertzian line contact load, considering that both Hertzian load types are common in contact problems.

11213914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213914.value: Engineering design requires the knowledge of stress and deformation of loaded objects. The surface deformation and stress of a ‘large’ body with a ‘large’ flat surface under external loads can be obtained by classical theories in contact mechanics (‘large’ body or surface is relative to the dimension of the loaded zone). However, no existing theory is available for problems with the applied load located close to an edge surface of a body. This project has addressed this problem by devising a semi-analytical technique using an efficient matrix approach. The new technique has been successfully developed, and it enables the study of the free edge surface effect on the surface deformation and stress of loaded object. The project has further developed the technique for more general situations such as the free edge surface can be of any angle with the loaded plane surface (general wedge structure). Thus, the technique can now be used for the lubrication analysis of tapered roller bearings. A taper roller has two wedge shapes at its ends. Furthermore, the developed technique can deal with a wedge structure having loads on both of its surfaces. As such, it can be used for the design of cutting tools.

11214114.label: Realisation of objectives
11214114.value: Impact of quantum statistics on the many-body dynamics of a crystalline solid at finite temperatures containing an interstitial solute atom (ISA) is investigated. Treating the difference between the Ehrenfest and Newtonian forces in the many-body equations of motion of the atoms as a stochastic perturbation, the corresponding fluctuation-dissipation relation (FDR) is formally related to the phonon and magnon densities of states. The many-body dynamics can then be directly solved numerically by following the MD approach with a Langevin heat bath based on the quantum FDR. At the same time, the Mori-Zwanzig theory also allows the many-body dynamics of the crystal to be formulated and solved analytically within a pseudo-one-particle approach using the Langevin equation using a phonon DOS based on the Debye model. Quantum statistics in the thermodynamics, vacancy formation and migration, self-diffusion of bcc iron, Helium diffusion in bcc tungsten via the vacancy and interstitial mechanisms are investigated. Significant and fundamental impacts are revealed which explains a number of anomalous behaviors. Thus, below the Debye temperature of the host lattice, quantum statistics is found to significantly impact the ISA transport properties in both approaches, resulting in major departures from both the Arrhenius law of diffusion and the Einstein-Smoluchowski relation between the mobility and diffusivity. Indeed, we found that below a third of the Debye temperature, quantum mobility and diffusivity are both orders-of-magnitude larger and practically temperature independent. These quantum effects have their physical origin in the zero-point lattice vibrations which can be traced to the non-commutative relation between position and momenta of the lattice atoms. In the quantum molecular-dynamics calculation of mobility and diffusivity of interstitial helium in BCC W. In this case, the Arrhenius law is only valid in a narrow range between ~300K and ~700K. The diffusivity becomes temperature independent on the low-temperature side while increasing linearly with temperature on the high-temperature side.

11214114.value: Treating the difference between the Ehrenfest and Newtonian forces in the many-body equations of motion of the atoms as a stochastic perturbation, the corresponding fluctuation-dissipation relation (FDR) is formally related to the phonon and magnon densities of states. The many-body dynamics can then be directly solved numerically by following the MD approach with a Langevin heat bath based on the quantum FDR. At the same time, the Mori-Zwanzig theory also allows the many-body dynamics of the crystal to be formulated and solved analytically within a pseudo-one-particle approach using the Langevin equation using a phonon DOS based on the Debye model. The average energy needed to create a magnon is high in ferromagnetic metals due to the high-strength spin stiffness, which results in strong quantization effects that could be important even at thousands of degrees. To take into account quantum statistics at such high temperatures, the associated effects of anharmonicity of the spin vibrations must be taken into account. In addition to the complex nature of such effects, anharmonicity also affects the occupation of the density of state of the vibration states in the context of quantum statistics. Thus, an unoccupied vibration state might become occupied when its spring stiffness is substantially reduced with anharmonicity. Combined effects of quantum statistics and anharmonicity are expected. In this regard, the thermodynamics of ferromagnetic metals are investigated in this paper through the example of bcc iron between 10 and 1400 K. Theoretical analysis and spin-lattice dynamic simulations are performed, through which the physics behind the complex and dramatic temperature dependence of the thermodynamic functions of bcc iron is understood. Noting the congruence between the dynamics of the many-body and stochastic systems within the Mori-Zwanzig theory, we analyzed the dynamics of a model particle subjected to a saw-tooth potential in a noisy medium. Impurity mobility is found to be governed by two sources of dissipative friction: that which is produced by the scattering of lattice waves (phonon wind), and that which is derived from the energy dissipation associated with overcoming the migration barrier screened by phonons. The many-body effect in both cases increases with temperature, so that the first component of the friction is important at high temperatures and the second component is important at low temperatures.
