11216214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216214.value: Cloud service providers (CSP), such as Google and Facebook, replicate and transport their content between geographically distributed datacenters using inter-datacenter wide area networks. Total inter-datacenter traffic volume is over 0.6 Exabyte per day, and is growing at a rate of over 25% per annum. Therefore, its transport consumes a significant amount of energy and represents a substantial cost burden on CSPs. This project will develop a new network design methodology to achieve cost effective and energy conserving operations that meet the performance and reliability requirements of future inter-datacenter networks. For the first time, network design methodologies based on integrating flexi-grid communications, protection, disaster survivability, and light-tree assignment will be provided. Flexi-grid communications technology has the potential to increase efficiency and flexibility. Protection guarantees sufficient capacity on alternative routes when links fail; disaster survivability guarantees high probability of connectivity in case of major disasters, and light-trees provide cost effective all-optical data transport especially for multicasting traffic. The project will provide an assessment of the extent to which energy and cost savings are achieved using flexi-grid communications and light-trees in inter-datacenter networks. Inter-datacenter networks have the following unique features: (1) inter-datacenter traffic involves replications that require significant multicasting - this justifies the use of light-trees; (2) datacenters may have advance information on the volume of data per connection - this enables efficient utilization of the flexible network resources considered in this project (i.e. flexi-grid based light-trees and lightpaths) and justifies their applicability, and (3) the number of nodes of an inter-datacenter network is not large. The proposed solution methods exploit these features; they are based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP), and on accurate and efficient heuristics. An ILP formulation provides a rigorous description of the engineering and economic considerations of the relevant optimization problem. ILP can also provide an optimal solution for small CSPs, and serves as a benchmark for other suboptimal solutions. Although the proposed methodologies are well adapted to inter-datacenter networks, the results and conclusions of the project can also apply to some extent to other optical networks. The project will address both legacy and greenfield scenarios. Under the legacy scenario, we will optimize the traffic routing and wavelength/spectrum assignment of lightpaths and light-trees for a given topology. In the greenfield scenario, the topology is optimally designed by minimizing cost subject to meeting disaster survivability requirements with special attention given to cable shapes that may not be in straight lines. 雲服務供應商，如Google、Facebook，採用廣域網絡實現了分佈於各地的數據中心間數據的複製和傳輸。如今，數據中心之間的業務量日超0.6艾字節（Exabyte），並正以每年超過25%的速度增長。由此將產生巨大的能源消耗，同時給雲服務供應商帶來沉重的經濟負擔。該研究項目將開發一種新的網絡設計方案，在滿足未來跨數據中心網絡的性能和可靠性要求下，實現低成本和低能耗的目標。 該項目將首次提出基於靈活柵格通信、保護、抗災能力以及光樹（Light-Tree）機制的網絡設計方案。靈活柵格通信技術在提高效率和靈活性方面極具潛力。保護機制能確保在鏈路失效時保護路徑上具備足夠的頻寬，抗災機制能保證在發生重大災難時網絡的高連通率，同時光樹能降低全光數據，尤其是多播業務的傳輸成本。該項目將評估基於靈活柵格通信和光樹機制的跨數據中心網絡所能夠獲得的能源和成本效率。 跨數據中心網絡具有以下特性：（1）數據中心間的業務涉及大量的組播複製--顯示出光樹的利用價值。（2）基於靈活柵格的跨數據中心網絡頻譜分配靈活、資源利用率高。在傳統網絡中，不同連接之間的頻寬按照其業務請求的峰值分配，並且建立後固定不可拆除，導致極大的資源浪費。與之相比，基於靈活柵格的跨數據中心網絡能更加準確地獲得數據流量的詳細信息，並根據業務請求動態地建立和拆除連接，按需分配頻譜資源，提高資源利用率。（3）跨數據中心網絡的節點較少。針對這些特性提出基於整數線性規劃（ILP）的解決方案，以及準確、高效的啟發式演算法。ILP模型提供了相關優化問題的工程及經濟方面的嚴格控制。同時，ILP可以為小型電信運營商提供最優解決方案，並可以作為其他次優解決方案的基準。該研究項目所提出的方法不僅能很好地應用於跨數據中心的網絡，其結果和結論在一定程度上也適用於其他光網絡。 該研究項目將統籌考慮傳統的和新興的兩種網絡場景。在傳統場景下，對於已知的拓撲結構，我們將優化光路和光樹的路由和波長/頻譜分配。在新興場景下，設計最優化拓撲使得在達到抗災能力要求的前提下降低成本。為此，需要特別指出的是直線鋪設光纜並非為最佳方案。

11216214.label: Realisation of objectives
11216214.value: To address the first two objectives, we have formulated Mixed ILP (MILP) models and developed efficient heuristic algorithms for survivable multicast routing and spectrum assignment in light-tree based elastic optical networks considering distance adaptive resource allocation. Numerical results have demonstrated that our heuristic algorithms perform close to the optimal solutions. Our objective function has been to minimize spectral usage. One important focus of this project has been on flexi-grid networks, as this is the new field. We also addressed the third objective by comparing cases of light-trees versus only lightpaths and quantitatively demonstrated the benefit of implementing light-trees. In addition to light-trees and lightpaths mentioned in the third objective, we have considered using light-trails to accommodate multicast demands. In particular, we have considered a light-tree-based elastic all-optical network, where each node is multicast-capable and does not support spectrum conversion. In such a network, for a given set of static multicast demands and considering distance-adaptive resource allocation, our aim has been to optimize multicast routing and spectrum assignment (MC-RSA) in order to minimize the maximum required spectrum for all network links. For this MC-RSA problem, we have considered three cases: (1) a case without protection, (2) a case with 1+1 dedicated protection allowing self-sharing where the spectrum on the primary link of a source-destination (SD) pair could be used to protect another SD pair of the same multicast connection, and (3) a case with shared protection allowing self-sharing and also cross-sharing, where the spectrum on a link used only as backup can be shared among different connections. In dedicated protection, resources are reserved exclusively to connections for protection in case of failures and cannot be utilized for other connections. To improve spectrum utilization, sophisticated algorithms have been introduced in shared protection to make use of reserved resources to protect different connections. For each case, we have formulated a node-arc MILP model. We have also developed a scalable greedy algorithm that is applicable to large networks. Numerical results for small problems have shown that the heuristic algorithms perform close to the optimal MILP models. We have also demonstrated that MC-RSA with 1+1 dedicated protection and shared protection requires significantly more spectra compared to the case without protection, which is especially true when the network has a low average nodal degree. We have provided further numerical results based on the MILP models and the heuristic algorithms for the important special case of MC-RSA, namely, the unicast routing and spectrum assignment. Note that in this research field, the issue of distance adaptive resource allocation has been recently introduced and it is considered important. Therefore, we have extended out modelling to include distance adaptive resource allocation, and since distance is normally measured in continuous variables, we provide MILP models and not merely ILP models. The studies on Objectives 1 and 2 have led to a journal publication in JLT (IEEE/OSA Journal on Lightwave Technology) and a conference publication in ACP (Asia Communications and Photonics Conference) 2015. The work on Objective 3 has led to a publication in JOCN (Journal of Optical Communications and Networking). In the work published in JOCN, we have evaluated the efficiency benefit of flexi-grid EONs over traditional fixed-grid WDM networks through a range of cases. We have considered a network case with dedicated protection allowing the above-mentioned self-sharing. We have assumed a general case where distance-adaptive transmission is relaxed. We have provided an ILP formulation and proposed a heuristic algorithm. Numerical results show that for small problems, the proposed algorithm performs close to the optimal ILP while for large instances, it achieves a comparable performance to the state-of-the-art algorithm but at the cost of a lower computational complexity. As Optical Burst Switching (OBS) is a potential technology for future datacenter networking, we contributed to efficient design of OBS networks in (S. Li et al. 2015a). Their protection has been studied also for unicast, a special case of multicast, which has led to two journal publications in IEEE Photonics Technology Letters (S. Li, et al. 2015b and S. Li et al., 2016). Further, we extensively investigated approaches for multicast provisioning in EONs. This has led to a paper in ICTON (International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks) 2018. Different approaches of multicast provisioning yield varied results. Also, when compared to fixed-grid WDM networks, EONs could present different performances of the approaches because of various additional degrees of flexibility. In this work, we have considered many multicast approaches based on technologies, namely, lightpath, light-tree, and light-trail, in EONs. These approaches include one lightpath approach, two light-tree approaches, and two light-trail approaches. To accommodate a multicast, the lightpath approach provides a lightpath from the source to each destination. Different from lightpaths where signals are transmitted to a sole destination, light-trees/light-trails inherently support optical multicasting where signals are transmitted to multiple destinations through a single light-tree/light-trail. The light-tree approaches either use a single light-tree to cover all the destinations or a variable number of light-trees each covering a part of the destinations, so do the light-trail approaches. The optimal number of light-trees/light-trails for a multicast is not deterministic, e.g., neither one nor the destination count, and finding this optimal light-tree/light-trail count is an NP-complete problem. In this work, we have considered the following problem. Given a multicast demand, a network topology, and a multicast approach, the objective is to minimize resource usage in terms of transmitter usage (i.e., the number of lightpaths/light-trees/light-trails used) and spectrum consumption to accommodate the multicast demand in the context of EONs. For all these multicast approaches, we have formulated the problem by MILP and have made a comprehensive comparison of their effectiveness in multicast provisioning. In particular, it is the first time that the problem of using light-trails for multicast provisioning in EONs is formulated by MILP. Numerical results demonstrate their performance for a range of cases. We have also evaluated the benefit of the flexibility, i.e., distance-adaptive transmission, provided by EONs for all the multicast approaches. An additional paper was published in JLT (IEEE/OSA Journal on Lightwave Technology) on design of Virtual Network Embedding (VNE) for flexi-grid optical networks. Demands of virtual networks (VNs) can be viewed as a generalization of unicast or multicast demands, therefore VNE is an important generalization and a natural extension of the present project. Although the work on VNE goes somewhat beyond the original objectives of the project in terms of applications, it is strongly related to this project by considering a more general problem and using methodologies that apply also to the special cases described by the project objectives.

11216214.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216214.value: Internet traffic is experiencing an enormous growth and increased demand for new services. To enhance flexibility and improved spectral efficiency of traditional WDM optical networks that use ITU-T fixed frequency grid, EONs have been proposed. Moreover, multicast services, including live Internet video delivery and inter-datacenter database synchronization, gain popularity, and they usually generate large volume of traffic. This calls for efficient multicast accommodation for bandwidth savings. To investigate the efficiency benefit of flexible grids of EONs over fixed grids of WDM networks for multicast service provisioning, we have formulated ILP models and proposed efficient heuristic algorithms. The work has led to a journal publication (A. Cai, et al. 2017). Moreover, we have compared various approaches based on technologies, namely, lightpath, light-tree, and light-trail, to provision multicast services in EONs. We have developed MILP models for these multicast approaches and compared their effectiveness in terms of spectrum consumption and transmitter usage. Also, the benefit of having distance-adaptive transmission in EONs has been assessed. The work has led to a conference publication (A. Cai, et al. 2018). Fiber cuts often occur to optical networks. Therefore, adequate protection should be preplanned for optical networks so that they can continue to operate under failures. This is especially true when a trunk of the multicast tree fails, in which case multiple destinations are affected and could not receive data from the source. Different protection methods provide different levels of quality of service. Dedicated protection provides a faster recovery speed while shared protection achieves better spectral efficiency. We have considered EONs with shared protection and dedicated protection for multicast provisioning. To compare the spectrum efficiency of both protection methods, we have further compared them with the case of unprotected EONs. We have provided MILP formulations that produce optimal solutions for small networks; for scalability to large problem instances, we have proposed efficient polynomial algorithms. Numerical results show that dedicated protection requires significantly more spectrum than shared protection. The work has led to three journal and one conference publications (A. Cai, et al. 2015, 2016, 2017a,b). We have also introduced new methods for efficiency improvement of OBS networks and studies involving 1+1 and 1+X protection (S. Li, et al. 2015a,b, 2016). Additionally, VNE has been considered in the design of flexi-grid optical networks, which has led to a journal publication (R. Lin, et al. 2017).

11216214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216214.value: The focus in the present project was mainly on designing optical networks with unicast and multicast demands. Additionally, we have published work on VNE for VN demands which are a generalization of the aforementioned demands. This has potential for further research development focusing on efficient design of elastic and WDM optical networks meeting VN demands and their service requirements. Another important research direction is developments of scalable heuristics that the tightness of their solutions can be guaranteed in terms of how close they are to the optimal solutions by provable bounds. This research direction is important for the entire field of network design, in particular for efficient design of VNE in optical networks. Course of action will include developments of new rigorous approaches to iterative LP relaxation with column generation algorithms that will lead to derivation of provable bounds on the quality of solutions. In addition to legacy scenarios where the topology is given, greenfield scenarios will also be considered, where the topology is also optimized by minimizing cost subject to meeting VN service requirements. Other potential directions include using machine learning for VNE, and applications to flexi-grid filterless optical networks which inherently provide optical multicasting but require unique constraints.

11216214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216214.value: Cloud service providers (CSPs), such as Google and Facebook, replicate and transport their content between geographically distributed datacenters using inter-datacenter wide area networks. Total inter-datacenter traffic volume is over 0.6 Exabyte per day, and is growing at a rate of over 25% per annum. Therefore, its transport consumes a significant amount of energy and represents a substantial cost burden on CSPs. Inter-datacenter traffic involves replications that require significant multicasting. This project develops new methodologies to achieve cost effective network designs that meet the performance and reliability requirements of future inter-datacenter networks. We compared various different approaches to accommodate multicast traffic in flexi-grid networks. In particular, for one of the approaches, i.e., light-tree, we evaluated the benefit of flexi-grid communications as compared to fixed-grid communications. Furthermore, to ensure survivability in case of failure occurrence, protection methods, namely, shared protection, dedicated protection, and no protection, have been compared through a range of cases in flexi-grid networks. The proposed solution methods include integer linear programming formulations, which provide optimal solutions for small-size problems, and efficient heuristics that scale to large instances.

11300114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300114.value: Particles are a key driver of health effects in urban air. In Hong Kong, the crowded urban environment makes it likely that people receive a significant burden from particles that are generated by road vehicles. These particles are extremely small in size and although regulated it has been assumed that all particles of a given size are equally toxic. The composition of particles is both variable and complex, so it is not easy to analyse particles in an attempt to identify the components that affect urban health. Increasingly health impact has been related to those compounds that can induce oxidative stress in the lung, especially through the production the superoxide radical (˙O2-), the hydroxyl radical (˙OH) and hydrogen peroxide H2O2). Such reactive oxygen specials can be estimated from chemical reactions in extracts from collected particles. Reactive oxygen species have been found to be concentrated on particles near the roadside and other urban environments, but also at higher concentrations in the summer. They also appear to be produced in particles containing copper. The proposed research will examine the potential for reactive oxygen species to form on airborne particles as they are transported away from the roadside in Hong Kong, by collection and analysing these at various distances from the roadway. Laboratory experiments will attempt to see if ozone or light can alter the concentration of reactive oxygen species on particles. Additional experiments will determine the distribution of reactive oxygen species in a number of sitting out areas as these are locations where elderly people (often the most sensitive to particulate air pollution) spend their days at locations that are frequently close to busy roads. The current project is novel not simply because it looks at reactive oxygen species at the roadside in Hong Kong and considers unique Hong Kong environments such as sitting out areas, but it attempts to examine transformations that might influence particle toxicity. It will hopefully encourage thought to be given to particle toxicity when framing air pollution legislation. Additionally it might help shift air pollution control in Hong Kong away from a focus on reducing emissions to a broader consideration how we might reduce our exposure to the most harmful air pollutants. 在城市空氣污染中固體顆粒物對人類的健康有著重大的影響。特別是在香港這個擁擠的 城市中，人們正因路邊產生大量的固體顆粒物而承受著巨大的負擔。這些固體粒子的尺 寸都相當的小，盡管在控制它們時我們假設所有尺寸的顆粒物的毒性是均等的，但是這 些粒子中所包含的組份卻是相當復雜與多變的。所以我們想要試圖去分析城市環境中顆 粒物組份對人類健康的影響並不是那麼的簡單。現在越來越多的健康問題都與某些化學 物質有關，而這些化學物質在人的肺部中會發生氧化應激反應，特別是反應中所衍生出 的超氧自由基陰離子, 羥基自由基和過氧化氫會對人類健康有著巨大的影響。而這些活 性氧化物是可以通過采集顆粒物並制作提取液，而後用化學反應的方式來鑒定的。我們 在路邊及其他城市環境的空氣固體物中已發現含有高濃度的活性氧化物。所以未來的研 究工作將對香港路邊及其他區域的空氣顆粒物中所形成的活性氧化物質的潛在危害進行 檢測。這是一個新奇但並不簡單的課題，因為它將會涉及路邊空氣固體粒子中的活性氧 化物並且是針對香港某些特定的環境比如休息場所進行研究，我們將會試圖去發現這些 活性氧化物的轉化以及對顆粒物毒性的影響。我們希望這樣的檢測可以推動人們在制定 空氣污染法規時增加對固體顆粒物的毒性的考慮。此外它可以幫助我們將香港空氣污染 控制的重心從減少污染排放轉移到更多的去考慮如何能減低我們曝露在危害性最強的空 氣污染物中的概率。

11300114.label: Realisation of objectives
11300114.value: Earlier studies have revealed that reactive oxygen species are concentrated on particles near the roadside and present at higher concentrations in the summer. They also appear to be produced in particles containing copper. Transformations in the near roadside environment potentially alter particle toxicity. The postdoctoral researcher Dr. Nirmal Gali, who was employed on the GRF was key in developing the outputs to this research. 1. Investigate the evolution of ROS in the near roadside environment: A time-integrated PM sampling at two sites, representing roadside and urban background, collected particulate PM2.5 (Solid-PM) and gaseous semi-volatile PM (SV-PM) separately from September 2016 to January 2017 and spanned summer and winter seasons. Each sampling day was divided into three sampling intervals of 6 h each – 04:00 -10:00, 12:00 – 18:00 and 20:00 – 02:00 h, representing morning rush hours, afternoon and late evening to night periods. Water-soluble and -insoluble PM extracts were exposed to two cell lines: namely RAW264.7 macrophages and A549 epithelial cells. In summary, the filter-based PM sampling was employed in the analysis of in vitro cellular toxicity of particulate solid PM and semi-volatile PM. From the data, it was noted that the RAW264.7 macrophages are more susceptible to PM compared to A549 epithelial cells. The SV-PM fraction is capable of inducing oxidative stress in cells compared to its counterpart Solid-PM considering the quantity of PM available, especially during summer season. The roadside site causes a significant increase in oxidative stress compared to the background site. While the high oxidative stress is found during afternoons at the roadside, background site surprisingly shows night times a more influential period. 2. Examine the potential for ROS to form on freshly collected particulate material: The evolution of particle physicochemical and optical properties in typical urban atmospheres of Hong Kong was examined through the collection of chemically-resolved PM2.5 data and PM2.5 size distribution at a roadside and an ambient site. Roadside particle size distribution showed typical peaks in the nuclei mode (30–40 nm) while ambient measurements peaked in the Aitken mode (50–70 nm), revealing possible condensation and coagulation growth of freshly emitted particles during aging processes. By contrast, PM2.5 UV light absorption coefficients (babs-BrC,370nm) at the ambient site (4.2 Mm-1) and at the roadside site (4.1 Mm-1) were similar, emphasizing that particle aging processes enhanced UV light-absorbing properties, a conclusion that was also supported by the finding that the Absorption Ångström coefficient (AAC) value at UV wavelengths (AAC_UV band) at the ambient site were ~1.7 times higher than that at the roadside. Both aqueous reaction and photochemically produced secondary organic aerosol (SOA) for ambient aerosols contributed to the peak values of babs-BrC,370nm in ambient particles at midnight and around noon, highlighting that secondary BrC had different sources and particle aging in the atmosphere affected BrC and BC properties and related aerosol light absorption. The transformations of ambient black carbon (BC) under photochemical oxidation leads to oxidized forms which lead to increased intercellular reactive oxygen species (e.g. most recently An, et al., (2019) Interactions between oxidative stress, autophagy and apoptosis in A549 cells treated with aged black carbon, Toxicology in Vitro, 54, pp. 67-74.) . 3. Assess the exposure to ROS at typical near roadside locations such as sitting out areas: We did not complete the work on exposure in parks and sitting-out areas in the duration of the current project, but it is now close to completion and is the subject of a number of papers that have been produced from work under a subsequent GRF (9042244) which assessed potential exposure in typical near roadside locations was continued as part of a subsequent GRF project "Air pollution in sitting-out areas and playgrounds in the urban roadside environment" - a number of papers have emerged from this and most pertinently a MS "Urban Park Layout and Exposure to Air Pollutants" submitted this month focusses on exposure directly. 4. Consider the likely health impacts of ROS in Hong Kong’s near roadside environments: The contribution of solid-PM and SV-PM to the total PM2.5 mass concentration was 9:1, with SV-PM dominating at roadside over urban background (p<0.001, n=36). Also, the SV-PM mass concentration increased by 10-20% during 20:00 – 02:00 h compared to the other two sampling periods, supplemented by ECOC ratio. The water-insoluble PM has caused 23-29% higher cell death compared to water-soluble PM, which is complemented with increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in both cell lines. The cellular damage caused by oxidative stress was determined from increased HO-1 and TNF-alpha expression in RAW264.7 macrophages was high compared to the A549 cell line, which demonstrated the greater induction of toxicity from water-insoluble PM over soluble PM. Similarly, the SV-PM induced many-fold higher ROS generation in cells compared to solid-PM. The lack of phagocytic action in A549 cells compared to RAW264.7 helped us to postulate novel toxicity mechanisms for water-soluble and -insoluble PM, which can also be assumed to occur at the level of human PM inhalation and bronchi alveolar exposure. Adverse health effects are associated with exposure to atmospheric particulate matter (PM), especially reactive oxygen species (ROS) which and induce both exogenous and endogenous oxidative stress. We investigated the spatial and seasonal variability of PM-induced ROS at four sites with different characteristics in Hong Kong. Metals such as Fe, Cr, Mo, Pb, Ni, and V from UG, AG, and BUS routes exhibited much lower solubility compared with ambient PM. The cell toxicity of PM in these transport microenvironments was also analyzed in vitro and compared with urban ambient environments. Strong positive associations were observed for reactive oxygen species (ROS) with water-soluble metals (Cr, Cu, Fe, Mn, Ni, V, Mo; R > 0.70) and organic and elemental carbon (OCEC) (R > 0.85) for UG and AG routes. In addition, PM from UG and AG routes generated 3–4-fold (in PM2.5) and 40–50-fold (in coarse PM) less ROS compared to urban sites, suggesting PM in these public transport microenvironments may not be intrinsically redox active than in urban ambient, and water solubility of metals seems to have played an important role in it.

11300114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300114.value: A novel profluorescent probe BPEAnit was employed to measure total PM2.5 - and gas phase-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) in real time using PILS. The contribution of particulate PM2.5 to total ROS was calculated showing that the oxidative potential measured at the roadside is significantly higher than in the background over 24 h sampling especially with respect to total ROS. While volumetric data showed high ROS generation during morning to late evening periods, the PM normalized data showed increased ROS production during night times, which could be mainly due to gaseous pollutant-mediated secondary aerosol formation, suggesting the gas phase PM can’t be neglected. The observation of higher oxidative potential during mornings to late evening periods in weekdays, and during late nights in weekends was a notable feature. The PM mass concentration, p-PAHs and BC are in good agreement with total- and gas phase-induced oxidative potential suggestive of possible surrogates, but its contradictory with respect to particulate PM2.5-induced ROS changes. The spatial and seasonal variability of PM-induced ROS at four sites with different characteristics in Hong Kong, examining cytotoxicity, exogenous and endogenous ROS was determined on a dose and time dependent analysis. Large spatial variation of ROS was observed with fine PM at the urban site showing highest ROS levels. The coarse PM at traffic site ranks highest. Somewhat surprisingly no consistent seasonal difference was observed for ROS levels among all sites, as we had expected summer to produce more. The highly heterogeneous distribution of PM-induced ROS demonstrates the differential capability of PM to produce oxidative stress, and the need to use appropriate metrics as surrogates of exposure instead of PM mass in epidemiologic studies. Transition metals were found associated with ROS ro by different degrees illustrating the complexity of mechanisms involved which is an extension of earlier postulates which suggested copper might be important in ROS production and observations that particle toxicity was enhanced though the presence of iron and vanadium. The oxidative potential and role of aerosol carbon and water-soluble metals in fine (dp < 2.5 µm) and coarse PM (2.5 0.70) and organic and elemental carbon (OCEC) (R > 0.85). Along mass transit routes routes there was 3–4-fold (in PM2.5) and 40–50-fold (in coarse PM) less ROS compared to general urban sites, suggesting PM in these public transport microenvironments may be less redox active than in urban ambient and the water solubility of metals seems to have played an important role in ROS formation.

11300114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300114.value: The project has developed a number of innovative techniques for distinguishing the ROS in water-soluble and -insoluble PM (determined from increased HO-1 and TNF-alpha expression in RAW264.7 macrophages and comparison to the A549 cell line). It prompts further research on contribution of particulate PM2.5-induced ROS to total ROS in the presence and absence of gas phase and we have been able to postulate novel toxicity mechanisms, which are the subject of ongoing work (which has now move with D. Zhi NING's group to UST). The near-roadside environment is a matter of increasing study as we have begun to examine the air pollution exposure of individuals in sitting out areas and parks (GRF 9042244), overhead walkways (GRF 13291116) and more recently bus stops (GRF 9042244). The role of trace metals in aerosol remains a focus, especially in our work in parks and sitting out areas. This work continues under the two GRFs and although some work on bus stops has been completed a proposal has currently be lodged under the present round of GRF applications.

11300114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300114.value: Airborne particulate matter causes adverse pulmonary and cardiovascular health effects. In densely populated Hong Kong ~7 million people are exposed to different levels of PM. It is not simply concentrations that are important, but the composition of respirable particles affects their toxicity. This project examined a particular marker of toxicity the Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS). Large spatial variation of ROS was observed with finer particles at urban sites showing the highest ROS levels, while particles at a site with busy traffic ranks the top for coarse particles. There was no consistent seasonal difference in ROS levels any of the sites. The presence of some metals (chromium, copper iron manganese nickel vanadium and molybdenum) in the particles was associated with ROS and hints that these are likely to be involved in the production. The mechanisms of ROS production are also dependent on the amount of water soluble materials associated with the atmospheric particles.

11300214.value: The following results have been obtained in this study: 1. Establishment of two climatologies of TC size, one using the QuikScat data and one using the reanalyses. Both climatologies are found to be consistent with each other, thus establishing a methodology to create such climatologies. 2. Identified the effect of different microphysics schemes on simulating TC size. 3. Demonstrated that vortices at different latitudes can have different movement even with the same size. 4. Increased vertical motion has been identified in TCs with a size increase, which leads to an increase in radial winds, and hence angular momentum imports. This result is found from both reanalyses and NWP model outputs. 5. Prediction of TC size changes by NWP model apparently is only successful about 50% of the time.

11300214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300214.value: The potential of NWP model in correctly predicting size has not been thoroughly examined due to the lack of data. One future direction would be to collaborate with an NWP centre to perform a systematic evaluation of the model performance. So far, all studies of size focused on the azimuthal average. However, it is well known that large asymmetries occur. The question of the mechanism responsible for such asymmetries and whether NWP models can predict such asymmetries should also be addressed.

11300214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300214.value: In addition to the maximum winds, the extent of damaging winds in a tropical cyclone is also important in forecasting. This project addresses this question from both an observational and modeling perspective. The results will provide useful information for forecasters in real-time situations as to what features of the tropical cyclone and the environment should be examined when predicting changes in the size.

11300414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300414.value: 金屬和配體，以及多個金屬中心之間的協同效應可以產生新的反應活性。互助配體和相關金屬中心在可逆反應和鍵活化反應中起到積極的協同作用。具有協同作用的配體的一個顯著特性是它們非特定性氧化還原性質，通過改變金屬中心的電性便可以穩定多種氧化態以及提高反應性。關於雙金屬的協同效應，金屬中心必須在接近的位置才能使得協同反應發生，從而得到優良的活性和選擇性。該課題旨在透過簡單的二聚化過程所形成的雙核配合物去開發一種新的多齒配體雙核配合物，它具有一個獨特四碳的離域部分作為橋接。逆夾芯式M-C4-M是一個很有趣的結構，因為從晶體結構可得知配位模式是可轉變的。該金屬離子之間足夠地接近使得協同效應變得可行，並且離域四碳部分可用於非特定性的氧化還原反應。通過分析和光譜研究，可以了解非傳統式有機金屬的鏈合和它形成的機制。主要目標是開發新型附有獨特性能的催化劑體系，並研究潛在的協同效應對反應的影響。

11300414.label: Realisation of objectives
11300414.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. In addition, two research students have been trained under this project, and keynote talks and oral presentations have been given. Objective 1: In this project, several new families of binuclear complexes supported by multidentate ligands bearing various delocalized C-based bridging cores have been prepared. The delocalized C-based bridging groups successfully developed include the unusual mu-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] moiety (generated by regioselective, redox-neutral vinylic dimerization reaction), meta- and para-di(methine)phenylene (CH-C6H4-CH), and the bridging naphthyl unit. Combined with bis-[pyridine-phenolate]-chelating groups, these C-based bridging structures have been designed to afford binuclear complexes displaying variable and adjustable intermetallic distances and geometry. The mu-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] structure is intriguing because hapticity is tunable and different metal sizes can be readily accommodated. Importantly, for all delocalized C-based bridging groups, the metal ions are in sufficiently close proximity so that synergistic and cooperative effects (e.g. bimetallic enchainment interactions) between metal centers become feasible. Objective 2: All new classes of complexes have been characterization by multinuclear NMR and a variety of spectroscopic methods, investigated using DFT calculations, and in some cases structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography. The molecular structures of binuclear complexes of Ti, Zr and Hf bearing the bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] moiety, determined by X-ray crystallography, show a bis-[O,N]-chelating mu-(eta(3):eta(3)-antifacial)-(cis-C4R2H2) framework that coils around and binds the two metal centers on opposite faces of the delocalized C4 moiety. While the M–C(eta-3) bond lengths are different (signifying variation in ligand hapticity), it is striking that the M-C4-M coordination is dissimilar for different metals, but conversely, the geometry of the C4 core is consistent and relatively independent of the metal. Although the bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] moiety can exist as cis or trans as well as syn or anti (R groups on same or opposite sides) isomers, only the cis-syn structure was isolated and characterized in each case, and hence investigations by DFT calculations have been performed to examine the possibility of a concerted, associative dimerization mechanism. It was found that the barrier for the formation of the cis-syn dimer is substantially lower than that for the cis-anti isomer, thus indicating that the former is kinetically favored. For all complexes, the pathway to the cis-syn dimer requires significantly lower activation energy than the cis-anti form (considerations were also given to trans-syn and -anti pathways but even higher barriers were predicted), consistent with the observed strong preference for cis-syn structures. Molecular orbital (MO) interactions have also been analyzed by DFT calculations, which confirm the covalency of the M-C4-M interaction. The binuclear complexes of Zr and Hf bearing the bridging-[C(Me)CHCHC(Me)] moiety are highly colored and display intense charge transfer absorption bands at 600 and 578 nm. An admixture of (C4)ligand-to-metal and intraligand charge transfer (LMCT and ILCT) is tentatively assigned, in agreement with the calculated MOs, and the blue shift from Zr to Hf is consistent with a LMCT transition for d(0) centers. The Zr and Hf derivatives bearing the bridging-[C(H)CHCHC(H)] moiety exhibit absorption shoulders at 400–500 nm that are tentatively assigned to ILCT with minor (C4)ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) character. Objective 3: Studies into the olefin polymerization reactivity of the newly developed catalysts have been undertaken. First, the stability of the bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] moiety was investigated to determine if it would be sufficiently robust to support catalytic reactivity. The reaction of the binuclear complexes with trityl borate proceeded cleanly to generate the corresponding dicationic species, thus demonstrating that electrophilic attack by trityl does not occur at the bridging C4 moiety and leads to benzyl abstraction from the metal sites. Next, by exploiting the chelate effect and attendant steric protection, the bis-(phenolate-pyridine)-[mu-C(R)CHCHC(R)] framework was shown to support interesting catalytic reactivity at the bimetallic sites. Interesting olefin copolymerization behavior was evident for the di-Ti catalysts, and the possibility of bimetallic cooperativity was investigated. High catalytic efficiencies, production of high molecular-weight polymers and well-defined catalytic behavior have been observed. Regarding the bimetallic bis-[(pyridine-2-phenolate-6-methine)M] (M = Ti, Zr, Hf) derivatives bearing meta- and para-phenylene bridging groups, the di-Ti catalysts display superior olefin homo- and copolymerization activities. For ethylene/1-octene copolymerizations, the degrees of 1-octene incorporation and molecular weights of the polymer produced by the di-Ti catalysts are significantly higher than for the mononuclear control, indicating comonomer enchainment and hence cooperative reactivity between the Ti centers. The binuclear bis-[(pyridine-phenolate)M] (M = Ti, Zr, Hf) complexes supported by a bridging naphthyl moiety have also been evaluated as olefin copolymerization catalysts in conjunction with trityl borate, and comparisons with mononuclear controls have been made. Importantly, the di-Ti catalysts produced high molecular-weight copolymers with elevated levels of comonomer incorporation, indicative of bimetallic enchainment and cooperative reactivity.

11300414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300414.value: Binuclear group 4 complexes supported by a bis-[pyridine-phenolate]-chelating bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] ligand system have been prepared by a regioselective, redox-neutral vinylic dimerization reaction. Investigations by X-ray crystallography, various spectroscopic methods and DFT calculations have been undertaken to probe the nature of the unusual delocalized bridging-C4 moiety and its mechanism of formation. The bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] core structure is intriguing because hapticity is readily malleable and different metal sizes can be accommodated, and stability against electrophilic attack is conferred by the chelate effect and the associated steric protection, so that these complexes can mediate catalytic reactivity at the bimetallic sites. Interesting olefin copolymerization behavior has been observed for the di-Ti catalysts, and the possibility of bimetallic cooperativity has been examined. [Publications 1 and 4] A series of (pyridine-phenolate)-based group 4 bis(benzyl) complexes, featuring a flexible O,N-donor chelate, have been synthesized and characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. Variable-temperature 1H NMR experiments indicate a fluxional process involving inversion of the seven-membered chelate ring accompanied by conformational changes for the benzyl groups. Examination of the molecular structure, determined by X-ray crystallography, revealed severely distorted ‘quasi-meridional’ coordination for the tridentate ligand and atypical (virtually perpendicular) orientation of the benzyl moieties. High catalytic efficiencies for olefin polymerization have been observed in conjunction with MAO and trityl borate. [Publication 2] Bimetallic bis-[(pyridine-2-phenolate-6-methine)M] (M = Ti, Zr, Hf) complexes bearing meta- and para-phenylene bridging groups have been prepared and characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. Studies have been undertaken to assess their olefin polymerization reactivity in conjunction with various cocatalysts. DFT calculations have been performed to investigate the nature of the active species. The di-Ti catalysts display superior olefin homo- and copolymerization activities in conjunction with trityl borate. For ethylene/1-octene copolymerizations, the degrees of 1-octene incorporation for the di-Ti catalysts are higher than for the mononuclear control, indicating 1-octene enchainment and hence cooperative reactivity between the Ti centers. [Publication 3] Using a bis-[pyridine-phenolate]-chelating ligand containing a bridging naphthyl moiety, a series of bimetallic bis-/tris(benzyl) group 4 complexes has been prepared, which readily convert into the desired bis-/bis(benzyl) derivatives upon heating in toluene. DFT calculations show energy-minimized structures with relatively short M···M separations (in the 6–7 angstrom range). The complexes have been evaluated as olefin copolymerization catalysts in conjunction with trityl borate, and comparisons with mononuclear controls have been made. The di-Ti catalysts produced copolymers exhibiting elevated levels of comonomer incorporation and high molecular weights, indicative of bimetallic enchainment and cooperative reactivity. [Publication 5]

11300414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300414.value: New families of bimetallic complexes supported by multidentate ligands bearing various delocalized C-based bridging units have been prepared, and their ability to catalyze olefin polymerization reactions and support synergistic and cooperative reactivity have been investigated. Further work to design and synthesize new and modified C-based bridging groups may be undertaken. Regarding the bridging-[C(R)CHCHC(R)] moiety, further studies may be performed to probe its potential redox non-innocent properties, and its ability to remain resistant to M–C cleavage. Additional studies by X-ray crystallography, various spectroscopic methods and DFT calculations can provide greater insights. Synthetic work to extend to other metal systems, as well as heteroatom analogues, are proposed. Further investigations to broaden the scope of catalytic applications and probe the bimetallic cooperativity are suggested. Moreover, the consequences of unusual or distorted ligand coordination geometries upon catalytic reactivity and polymerization behavior remains unclear, and additional studies are justified. In general, the design and development of new ligand structures and frameworks that can support novel catalytic processes, as well as cooperative reactivity, is warranted.

11300414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300414.value: In metal-metal cooperativity, adjacent metal sites can react synergistically to achieve activity and selectivity that are superior to their mononuclear analogues. This project focused on the synthesis, characterization and catalytic reactivity of binuclear complexes bearing suitably positioned metal centers. New classes of bimetallic complexes supported by multidentate ligands that contain a delocalized bridging (cis-butadiene)-like or related carbon-based core structures have been developed. Detailed investigations by a variety of spectroscopic methods (including multinuclear NMR spectroscopy) and DFT calculations, and structural characterizations by X-ray crystallography, have been undertaken. The M-C4-M structure is intriguing because variable coordination modes are evident from the crystal structures and different metal sizes can be accommodated. It is important to note that previously reported non-chelating relatives of such carbon-based bridging ligands are insufficiently robust, as reflected by a dearth of catalytic applications. Here, by exploiting the chelate effect and the attendant steric protection, the increased stability of the bridging (cis-butadiene)-like and related core structures and their capacity to mediate catalytic reactivity at the bimetallic sites have been demonstrated. The ability of the binuclear complexes to function as olefin polymerization catalysts have been investigated. Interesting copolymerization results and evidence indicative of bimetallic cooperative reactivity have been obtained.

11300614.label: Summary of objectives addressed
11300614.value: Objectives Addressed Percentage achieved 1.We study the intrinsic approach applied to the displacement traction-problem for a linearly elastic plate. To this end, we first explicitly compute the intrinsic three-dimensional boundary condition of place in terms of the Cartesian components of the linearized strain tensor field, thus avoiding the recourse to covariant components in curvilinear coordinates and providing an interesting example of actual computation of an intrinsic boundary condition of place in three-dimensional elasticity. Second, we perform a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the three-dimensional equations as the thickness of the plate approaches zero. As a result, we identify the intrinsic two-dimensional equations of a linearly elastic plate modeled by the Kirchhoff-Love theory, with the linearized change of metric and change of curvature tensor fields of the middle surface of the plate as the new unknowns. This paper has been accepted in 2018 for publication in the high-ranking journal “Mathematics and Mechanics of Solids”.Yes100% 2.We recast the displacement-traction problem of the Kirchhoff - Love theory of linearly elastic plates as a boundary value problem with the bending moments and stress resultants inside the middle section of the plate as the sole unknowns, instead of the displacement field in the classical formulation. To this end, we show in particular how to recast the Dirichlet boundary conditions satisfied by the displacement field of the middle surface of a plate as boundary conditions satisfied by the bending moments and stress resultants. To this end, we first explicitly compute the intrinsic three-dimensional boundary condition of place in terms of the Cartesian components of the linearized strain tensor field, thus avoiding the recourse to covariant components in curvilinear coordinates and providing an interesting example of actual computation of an intrinsic boundary condition of place in three-dimensional elasticity. Second, we perform a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the three-dimensional equations as the thickness of the plate approaches zero. This paper has been accepted in 2018 for publication in the high-ranking journal “Mathematics and Mechanics of Solids”.

We recast the displacement-traction problem of the Kirchhoff - Love theory of linearly elastic plates as a boundary value problem with the bending moments and stress resultants inside the middle section of the plate as the sole unknowns, instead of the displacement field in the classical formulation. To this end, we show in particular how to recast the Dirichlet boundary conditions satisfied by the displacement field of the middle surface of a plate as boundary conditions satisfied by the bending moments and stress resultants. This paper has been published in the high-ranking journal “Analysis and Applications” in 2018.

We recast the Dirichlet boundary conditions satisfied by the displacement field of the middle surface of a linearly elastic shell as boundary conditions satisfied by the corresponding linearized change of metric and of curvature tensor fields. This in turn allows us to give an intrinsic formulation of the linear shell model of W.T. Koiter with these two tensor fields as the sole unknowns. This paper has been accepted for publication in 2018 in Comptes Rendus de l’Academie des Sciences de Paris.

We show that the intrinsic equations of Koiter's model of a linearly elastic shell can be derived from the intrinsic formulation of the three-dimensional equations of a linearly elastic shell, by using an appropriate a priori assumption regarding the three-dimensional strain tensor fields appearing in these equations. To this end, we recast in particular the Dirichlet boundary conditions satisfied by any admissible displacement field as boundary conditions satisfied by the covariant components of the corresponding strain tensor field expressed in the natural curvilinear coordinates of the shell. Then we show that, when restricted to strain tensor fields satisfying a specific a priori assumption, these new boundary conditions reduce to those of the intrinsic equations of Koiter's model of a linearly elastic shell. This paper has been accepted in 2018 for publication in Comptes Rendus de l’Academie des Sciences de Paris.

11300614.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300614.value: This research has laid down the mathematical foundations of the intrinsic approach to linearly plates and shells. More precisely, the boundary value problems of this intrinsic approach, i.e., the corresponding partial differential equations and boundary conditions, have been identified, and fully justified by means of a rigorous asymptotic analysis. It is to be emphasized that these identifications and justifications have been carried out in the realistic case where both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions are applied along the lateral face of the plate or shell. As a result, the proofs are often quite delicate, and involve interesting new mathematical techniques.

11300614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300614.value: First, this research paves the way for developing new numerical methods for directly approximating the strains, and consequently the stresses by means of the constitutive equation, that arise in elastic thin structures, such as cooling towers, roofs, blades, wings of an airplane, etc. Second, it also paves the way for extending the intrinsic approach to nonlinearly elastic plates and shells. A research proposal has been recently prepared in this direction.

11300614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300614.value: When an elastic structure is subjected to applied forces, stresses are generated inside the structure, which may eventually provoke its collapse. In the “classical” approach to elasticity, however, it is not the stresses that are computed, but rather the displacements, which do not necessarily endanger a structure, even if they are large (think of a bow, for instance). It is therefore of paramount importance to compute the stresses with a good accuracy. An “intrinsic” approach provides a way to do so, without having to compute the displacements. This proposal lays down the theoretical foundations of the intrinsic approach applied to plates and shells, which are among the most common elastic bodies found in contemporary structures, such as cooling towers, roofs, blades, wings of an airplane, etc..

11300714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11300714.value: 基于复杂度，条件，和逼近的理论

11300714.label: Project Objectives
11300714.value: The only objective of this project is to develop a complexity theory over the reals, extending the BSS theory, that will incorporate round-off errors and complexity of iterative algorithms. This general goal implies a definition of "decision problem" --that will include the condition of the input data--, an appropriate measurement of cost --that will explain the behavior of iterative algorithms--, a version of nondeterminism --to define the corresponding class NP--, and a suitable notion of reduction --to define hardness and, eventually, exhibit NP-complete problems. Once the above is done, the doors are open to consider further complexity resources (parallelism, alternation, . . . ) and the theoretical problems related to them. I intend to do so in the measure that I have time and resources.

11300714.label: Realisation of objectives
11300714.value: The objective of the proposal has been fully achieved. A complexity theory over the reals incorporating round-off errors and complexity of iterative algorithms was developed. This theory defines three versions of the class P (of problems decidable in polynomial time). One of them is general and the other two are subclasses of the first that capture problems for which the polynomial-time algorithm solving them has some additional feature. Natural examples of problems in these three classes are exhibited. Two forms of nondeterminism are studied as well and the corresponding NP classes defined. Complete problems for these classes are shown to exist. The theory makes the subject of a 50-pages article. As an application of the theory, two more articles have been published, both dealing with the problem of computing eigenpairs of complex matrices (and in both cases, under the viewpoint above, i.e., iterative algorithms working in the presence of round-off errors). One of them (published in the J. European Math. Soc.) is a 63-pages long paper solving a long-standing problem: to prove the existence of a numerically stable algorithm computing eigenpairs of complex matrices in polynomial time on the average. The other one shows that zeros of the characteristic polynomial of Gaussian matrices are ill-conditioned on average. This is consistent with (and could be a theoretical explanation of) the fact that computing eigenvalues via computing the zeros of the characteristic polynomial is typically unstable.

11300714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300714.value: The main outcome of the proposal is the development of a new theory of complexity that takes into consideration finite precision, iterative algorithms and data condition. The theory defines versions of the classes P, NP, and EXP within this context and exhibits natural examples of problems in these classes, NP-complete problems, and an inclusion of NP in EXP. In addition, we have tackled the problem of computing eigenpairs of complex matrices and solved a long standing problem, namely, to prove the existence of a numerically stable algorithm computing eigenpairs of complex matrices in polynomial time on the average. On a third paper we have proved that zeros of the characteristic polynomial of Gaussian matrices are ill-conditioned on average. This is consistent with (and could be a theoretical explanation of) the fact that computing eigenvalues via computing the zeros of the characteristic polynomial is typically unstable.

11300714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300714.value: There is no doubt potential for further development as any new theory, rather than closing avenues of thought, opens up problems and allows old problems to be reconsidered under a new light. My current research is focusing on one such problem (the computation of homology groups for semialgebraic sets) within the context of finite precision, iterative algorithms and data condition.

11300714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300714.value: Computer algorithms have changed the way we live. A fundamental aspect of these algorithms is their complexity which, broadly speaking, divides algorithms in efficient and inefficient. For a given computational problem, the first question one considers is whether efficient algorithms do exist. To tackle this question, a theory of complexity has developed over the last fifty years. But this theory deals only with discrete problems. To deal instead with continuous problems, a tailor made theory was proposed in the late 80s by Blum, Shub and Smale. At the end of their 1989 paper they mention as an open problem to extend their theory so that it can consider iterative algorithms and finite precision. This is what, about a quarter of a century later, we have done in this project.

11300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300814.value: In this project, we plan to study asymptotics of orthogonal polynomials when their degree n tends to infinity. We will investigate complex Hermite polynomials, some hypergeometric polynomials in the Askey-scheme and the corresponding q-orthogonal polynomials. The Plancherel-Rotach asymptotic expansions of these polynomials will be derived by using the difference equation method and the integral method. Important improvements of these methods will also be achieved when solving our problems. 在本研究項目中，我們計划探討正交多項式在其階n趨於無窮大時的漸近行為。我們準備研究复埃爾米特（Hermite）多項式，一些在阿斯基類（Askey-scheme）中的超幾何多項式，以及它們的q模擬。我們預計會運用差分方程以及積分的方法來推導這些多項式的Plancherel-Rotach型漸近展開式。在解決問題的過程中，我們需要對這些方法進行重要的改進。

11300814.label: Realisation of objectives
11300814.value: The main objective of this project is to investigate asymptotic properties of various orthogonal polynomials and their q-analogues. We first study the perturbed Laguerre polynomials, where an additional exp(-t/x) type singularity is introduced in the weight function. Note that the term -t/x in the exponent can be generalized to that possessing a higher order pole at the origin as well. When t=0, this is simply the classical Laguerre polynomials, whose properties are well-known in the literature. When t is a small positive constant, although the perturbation term does not change properties of the polynomials significantly in the macroscopic level (for example, the limiting zero distribution remains the same), it changes the behavior of the polynomials near the origin in the microscopic level. From the viewpoint of asymptotics, the Bessel-type expansion is replaced by new Painleve-type ones in the neighborhood of the origin. This property is successfully applied to Random Matrix Theory and statistical mechanics, which describes a new universality class and phase transition, respectively. In the technique part, a new model Riemann-Hilbert problem is constructed in the Deift-Zhou steepest descent analysis. It is also noting that, when the degree of the polynomial is fixed, such kind of perturbed Laguerre polynomials are closely related to a class of special solutions to some partial differential equations in integrable system, namely the peakon solutions. Next, we consider a class of orthogonal polynomials which arises from nonlinear coherent states in quantum optics. These polynomials are defined via a three-term recurrence relation. As a consequence, we adopt Wang-Wong difference equation method to study their asymptotic properties. Note that the Wang and Wong’s method can be applied to study not only orthogonal polynomials, but also solutions to general second order linear difference equations. There are some interesting features about the polynomials we considered in the present project. The three-term recurrence coefficients are very simple rational functions in terms of n, the polynomial degree. Moreover, they are similar to the associated Hermite polynomials in the literature. Nevertheless, they don’t belong to any members in the well-known Askey scheme. In fact, their asymptotics suggest that the orthogonality density function possesses an unusual singularity near the origin. This also indicates that it is difficult to make use of other methods to derive their asymptotic properties. Using the difference equation method, we successfully obtained the uniform asymptotics, which also implies the explicit form of the orthogonal weight function. We also develop the difference equation method to study the two-sided case. This means the parameter n in the difference equation is no longer non-negative integers, but all of them in Z. It is interesting to note that, no matter n is positive or not, one may always get polynomials from the recurrence relation, whose order depends on |n|. In the literature, such kind of difference equation is closely related to double-infinite Toda lattice in mathematical physics. Similar to the one-sided case, the polynomials generated by the recurrence relation can be considered as eigenfunctions of a doubly infinite Jacobi matrix. We carefully investigate the properties of the doubly infinite Jacobi matrices corresponding to different polynomials, such as Lommel polynomials, associated ultraspherical polynomials, and Al-Salam-Ismail polynomials, etc.. By finding the minimal (or subdominant) solutions or calculating the continued fractions for the difference equations, we derive explicit formulas for the matrix entries of resolvent. As a consequence, the spectral measures are derived explicitly by inverting Stieltjes transformations. Note that, the polynomials we studied are comprehensive in the sense that they cover continuous, discrete as well as q-cases. Regarding the complex Hermite polynomials, continuous dual Hahn polynomials, the Wilson polynomials, we successfully applied the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems to obtain their asymptotics. For the complex Hermite polynomials, it is crucial to discover their relations with classical Laguerre polynomials with certain varying parameters. For the continuous dual Hahn polynomials and the Wilson polynomials, we need to construct a new local parametrix near the origin. Note that, the weight functions of these two polynomials are given as quotients of Gamma functions. As a consequence, the weight functions possess infinitely many zeros and poles in the complex plane. After the rescaling (which makes the zeros in a bounded interval), the origin becomes a limiting point of the possible singularities. To handle the behavior near the origin, we need to carry on the Riemann-Hilbert analysis carefully near the origin and construct a new parametrix. Finally, we successfully obtained the asymptotics including the origin, which can also be matched with other existing results in the literature. Note that, the existing method can only achieve asymptotic results when the variable x is fixed, and no uniform asymptotic results are available before our work. Finally, we apply the asymptotics of the Stieltjes-Wigert polynomials to study the thermal partition function of a model of quantum mechanical fermions with matrix-like index structure and quartic interactions. We further develop a discrete analogue of Laplace’s approximation to obtain the asymptotics of the Stieltjes-Wigert polynomials, which are given in terms of theta functions. Our approach can be easily extended to handle general q-polynomials. These results help us to understand the physics of a large number of fermionic degrees of freedom subject to non-local interactions.

11300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300814.value: In this research project, we first thoroughly understand the influence of the singular term exp(-t/x) appearing in the weight function of orthogonal polynomials. When t is a small parameter depending on the polynomials degree n, we show that the local asymptotic behavior of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials near the origin is given in terms of certain Painleve functions. Due to the close relation between orthogonal polynomials and random unitary ensembles, these asymptotic results give us novel eigenvalue correlation kernels involving Painleve functions. It is well-known that unitary ensembles are determinantal point possess, where all the important information is contained in the correlation kernels. Therefore, our findings make it possible to investigate several crucial quantities in random unitary ensembles, such as gap probability and its asymptotics. Next, we develop the difference equation method to study orthogonal polynomials and their q-analogues. Uniform asymptotics for various polynomials have been obtained, such as the continuous dual Hahn polynomials, the Wilson polynomials, as well as orthogonal polynomials arising from nonlinear coherent states in quantum optics. We also consider some q-orthogonal polynomials. Instead of the usual Airy, Bessel or trigonometric type expansions, their asymptotics are given in terms of q-Airy function or the theta functions. These results are crucial to understand the physics of a large number of fermionic degrees of freedom subject to non-local interactions. The difference equation method has also been developed to two-sided case. In this situation, we have doubly infinite Jacobi matrices. Although there are some similarities between the one-sided and two-sided cases, the resolvent and spectral measure have some unique features. By finding the minimal (or subdominant) solutions or calculating the continued fractions for the difference equations, we derive explicit formulas for the matrix entries of resolvent of doubly infinite Jacobi matrices corresponding to various polynomials, such as Lommel polynomials, associated ultraspherical polynomials, and Al-Salam-Ismail polynomials, etc.. We also investigate the complex Hermite polynomials. After discovering their relation with the classical Laguerre polynomials with varying parameters, we successfully apply the Riemann-Hilbert method to derive their asymptotic expansion. Comparing with the existing results in the literature, the accuracy of our results has been significantly improved.

11300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300814.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: 1. Further develop the asymptotic methods for difference equations. At present stage, researchers handle difference equations whose coefficients grow in algebraic orders. It will be very interesting to generalize the existing method, such that it can solve difference equations with exponential growth coefficients. On the other hand, most of asymptotic study on difference equation relies on the fact that the equation is of order two. In the literature, there has been some work on higher order difference equations. However, the theory is not complete in the sense that quite a few extra conditions have been assumed. We believe these conditions are not necessary and some developments can be made. 2. Apply the asymptotic results to random matrix theory. Through the asymptotic study of orthogonal polynomials in this project, we understood several new universality classes and obtained the related new correlation kernels. Based on these results, it is possible to answer some important questions in random matrix theory, such as the gap probability where there is no eigenvalue in certain intervals. Moreover, the large gap asymptotics can also be derived.

11300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300814.value: Special functions are certain mathematical functions which are wildly used in applied mathematics, physics and engineering. Orthogonal polynomials and Painleve functions are important topics in this research field. In particular, the Painleve functions are viewed as the special functions in the 21st century due to their significant applications in nonlinear mathematical physics discovered in the past a few decades. Q-orthogonal polynomials and q-Painleve functions are their extensions related to quantum mechanics. Many applications of these special functions rely on their asymptotic properties. In this project, we have developed various asymptotic methods, and then applied them to study asymptotic properties of these special functions. Some significant new phenomena have been observed and understood. The relations and applications of our new results have also been discovered and discussed, which points out several possible research developments in mathematics, as well as other fields in mathematical physics, such as random matrix theory, statistical mechanics, etc..
