11301014.label: Project Objectives
11301014.value: A numerically more stable proper refinement of Nash equilibrium: To address numerical instability arising in the computation of proper equilibrium with Myerson’s concept, we will formulate the notion of perfect d-proper equilibrium, whose degree of properness is controllable by d strictly between zero and one. To ensure existence of such an equilibrium, we will form a perturbed game depending on the perturbing probability functions of t and d and apply linear programming to obtain a t-perfect d-proper equilibrium. The key technical issue to tackle is the assurance of full properness of perfect d-proper equilibrium under a sufficiently small d. A smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium: Every Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game yields a t-perfect d-proper equilibrium. This property, together with multilinear form of the payoff function, will be fully exploited in the formulation of the path. We will first apply t as an extra variable to obtain a barrier payoff function from an appropriate convex combination of a barrier term with the payoff function. Then, we will form a barrier game that deforms from a trivial game to the original game as t varies from one to zero. The barrier term will force Nash equilibrium of the barrier game to stay in the interior of the perturbed strategy space. For any given sufficiently small t, the corresponding coefficient of the barrier term satisfies that Nash equilibrium of the barrier game closely approximates some Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game. To ensure the existence of a smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium, a perturbing term will be subtracted and Sard’s and implicit function theorems will be applied. The key technical issues to address are the convergence of the path to a perfect d-proper equilibrium and finiteness of the entire path length. An efficient predictor-corrector method to numerically follow the smooth path: To numerically follow the smooth path to a perfect d-proper equilibrium, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be formulated to characterize the path. To solve the system, a predictor-corrector method will be proposed by taking advantage of the special structures of the problem. The emphasis will be on numerical stability and efficiency. The sparsity of the problem will be exploited in the Cholesky factorization. When t is sufficiently small, the numerical instability may occur. To deal with this problem, we will utilize the preconditioning techniques as in interior-point methods. The key technical issue to tackle is the estimation of step length in the predictor step. A simplicial path-following method for computing a perfect d-proper equilibrium: Nash equilibrium can be formulated as a stationary point problem. Based on the stationary point formulation of the perturbed game, a continuous mapping can be defined on the perturbed strategy space such that a strategy profile is Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game if and only if it is a fixed point of the mapping. By employing t as the homotopy parameter, a homotopy function can be defined to deform from a trivial game to the original game as t varies from one to zero. When zero is a regular value of the homotopy function, a connected component of zero points of the homotopy function constitutes a piecewise smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium. To numerically follow this path, a triangulation of continuous refinement of grid size will be constructed to define a piecewise linear path and a simplicial method will be adapted for numerically following the path. The key technical issue to address is how to refine the grid size so that the piecewise linear path leads to a perfect d-proper equilibrium. Numerical implementations: When the methods are successfully developed in the proposed research, we will code them in both MATLAB and C++. Extensive numerical tests will be systematically carried out. A software package of the methods will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for applications. The key technical issue to tackle is the reduction of computational amount of the expected payoff for games with many players and each player having a large number of pure strategies.
rows: A numerically more stable proper refinement of Nash equilibrium: To address numerical instability arising in the computation of proper equilibrium with Myerson’s concept, we will formulate the notion of perfect d-proper equilibrium, whose degree of properness is controllable by d strictly between zero and one. To ensure existence of such an equilibrium, we will form a perturbed game depending on the perturbing probability functions of t and d and apply linear programming to obtain a t-perfect d-proper equilibrium. The key technical issue to tackle is the assurance of full properness of perfect d-proper equilibrium under a sufficiently small d.

A smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium: Every Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game yields a t-perfect d-proper equilibrium. This property, together with multilinear form of the payoff function, will be fully exploited in the formulation of the path. We will first apply t as an extra variable to obtain a barrier payoff function from an appropriate convex combination of a barrier term with the payoff function. Then, we will form a barrier game that deforms from a trivial game to the original game as t varies from one to zero. The barrier term will force Nash equilibrium of the barrier game to stay in the interior of the perturbed strategy space. For any given sufficiently small t, the corresponding coefficient of the barrier term satisfies that Nash equilibrium of the barrier game closely approximates some Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game. To ensure the existence of a smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium, a perturbing term will be subtracted and Sard’s and implicit function theorems will be applied. The key technical issues to address are the convergence of the path to a perfect d-proper equilibrium and finiteness of the entire path length.

An efficient predictor-corrector method to numerically follow the smooth path: To numerically follow the smooth path to a perfect d-proper equilibrium, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be formulated to characterize the path. To solve the system, a predictor-corrector method will be proposed by taking advantage of the special structures of the problem. The emphasis will be on numerical stability and efficiency. The sparsity of the problem will be exploited in the Cholesky factorization. When t is sufficiently small, the numerical instability may occur. To deal with this problem, we will utilize the preconditioning techniques as in interior-point methods. The key technical issue to tackle is the estimation of step length in the predictor step.

A simplicial path-following method for computing a perfect d-proper equilibrium: Nash equilibrium can be formulated as a stationary point problem. Based on the stationary point formulation of the perturbed game, a continuous mapping can be defined on the perturbed strategy space such that a strategy profile is Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game if and only if it is a fixed point of the mapping. By employing t as the homotopy parameter, a homotopy function can be defined to deform from a trivial game to the original game as t varies from one to zero. When zero is a regular value of the homotopy function, a connected component of zero points of the homotopy function constitutes a piecewise smooth path leading to a perfect d-proper equilibrium. To numerically follow this path, a triangulation of continuous refinement of grid size will be constructed to define a piecewise linear path and a simplicial method will be adapted for numerically following the path. The key technical issue to address is how to refine the grid size so that the piecewise linear path leads to a perfect d-proper equilibrium.

Numerical implementations: When the methods are successfully developed in the proposed research, we will code them in both MATLAB and C++. Extensive numerical tests will be systematically carried out. A software package of the methods will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for applications. The key technical issue to tackle is the reduction of computational amount of the expected payoff for games with many players and each player having a large number of pure strategies.

11301014.label: Realisation of objectives
11301014.value: To overcome the numerical difficulty caused by the notion of proper equilibrium, we introduce a parameter d with a given value between zero and one to control the degree of properness and define an epsilon-perfect d-proper equilibrium. As a result of this epsilon-perfect d-proepr equilibrium, we establish the concept of perfect d-proper equilibrium by taking the limit of a sequence of epsilon-perfect d-proper equilibria as epsilon descends to zero. To prove the existence of such an equilibrium, we constitute a perturbed game such that every Nash equilibrium of this perturbed game is an epsilon-perfect d-proper equilibrium. With this perturbed game, we attain the existence of a perfect d-proper equilibrium. For any given game, one can derive that a perfect d-proper equilibrium is a proper equilibrium provided that d is sufficiently small. Examples show that a perfect d-proper equilibrium is a proper equilibrium even when d is rather large. This equilibrium concept effectively solves the numerical difficulty with the notion of proper equilibrium. By exploiting an extra variable ranging between zero and one, we define a smooth increasing function such that it becomes zero before the extra variable vanishes. With this increasing function, we incorporate a logarithmic barrier term into each player’s payoff function to constitute a barrier game. In this barrier game, each player solves against any given strategy profile of other players a convex optimization problem. This barrier game has a desired property that it becomes identical to the perturbed game before the extra variable descends to zero. An application of the optimality conditions to the optimization problem for each player and a fixed-point argument together yield an equilibrium system. By capitalizing on the equilibrium system and the property, we establish the existence of a smooth path that leads to a perfect d-proper equilibrium under the assumption that zero is a regular value of the equilibrium system. To get rid of the assumption, we add to the system a perturbation term that becomes zero when the extra variable equals one and zero. We show that the path always ends at a Nash equilibrium that approximates some perfect d-proper equilibrium provided that the normal of the perturbation vector is sufficiently small. When Jacobian matrix at the Nash equilibrium the path ends at is nonsingular, the path has finite length. To numerically follow this smooth path, we develop a predictor-corrector method by fully exploiting the special structures of the system. By exploiting the perturbed game, we form an equilibrium system. With the system, we construct a piecewise smooth path that leads to a perfect d-proper equilibrium. To numerically follow this nonsmooth path, we formulate a piecewise linear system. With this system and an existing triangulation of continuous refinement of gird size, we develop a simplicial homotopy method to compute a perfect d-proper equilibrium. Software packages of two proposed methods have been made available for computing perfect d-proper equilibria.

11301014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301014.value: The computation of proper equilibrium plays a significant role in the applications of game theory. Nevertheless, it is numerically very time-consuming to find a proper equilibrium since one has to use very high precision computation to ensure numerical stability. The concept of perfect d-proper equilibrium effectively solves the numerical difficulty with the notion of proper equilibrium. This concept has been generalized to market equilibrium and a smooth path-following method has bee obtained to find market equilibria in [1]. Tarski’s fixed-point problem under componentwise ordering is a very powerful tool in economic analysis. The simplicial homotopy idea developed in this project has been successfully exploited in the computation of Tarski’s fixed point. As a result, we are able to show that the problem is in the class PPAD in [2], which is the first complexity result for the problem. The metric learning can be formulated as an equilibrium problem. It has many applications in image processing. The path-following idea developed in the project has been employed in the metric learning. As a result, a weighted graph embedding-based metric learning method has been proposed for kinship verification in [3] and a clustering ensemble selection has been derived for categorical data in [4]. One of the main ideas in the project is an application of a fixed-point argument in the formulation of an equilibrium system. This idea has been successfully capitalized on to solve some practical problems in [5, 6, 7]. To study drug pricing patterns in china, game theory has been applied to derive some useful models and the methods developed in the project have been employed to find some equilibrium strategies in [8].

11301014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301014.value: The idea developed in this project can be generalized to stochastic game to formulate the concept of perfect d-proper stationary equilibrium. To compute such a stationary equilibrium, one can formulate a perturbed stochastic game and constitute a barrier stochastic game such that there exists a smooth path of stationary equilibria, which starts from a unique stationary equilibrium on the level one and leads to a perfect d-proper stationary equilibrium on the level zero. With this path, a predictor-corrector method can be adapted for numerically tracing the path to a perfect d-proper stationary equilibrium in stochastic game.

11301014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301014.value: As an effective mechanism for strategic decision making, game theory has been successfully applied in a variety of fields including business, economics, and social science. To further promote the applications of game theory, this project formulates the concept of perfect d-proper equilibrium, which is a refinement of perfect equilibrium and is much easier to compute than proper equilibrium. The computation of Nash equilibrium and its refinements plays an important role in the applications of game theory. The project develops a smooth path-following method for computing a perfect d-proper equilibrium for a finite n-person game in normal form. The method forms a barrier game by incorporating a logarithmic barrier term into a player’s payoff function with an appropriate convex combination and fully exploits differentiability of the problem. The existence of a smooth path is ensured from the subtraction of a perturbation term and an application of Sard’s and implicit function theorems. Extensive numerical tests have been carried out. The research of this project will further enhance the applications of game theory.

11301414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301414.value: The use light to control the course of a chemical/biochemical reaction is an attractive idea because this control can be easily administered with high precision and very fine spatial resolution. Indeed, photo-regulated processes have already found many applications in materials and microelectronic fabrication. The rapidly growing fields of chemical biology and cell biology are also beginning to recognize the advantage of photo-regulation, and are trying to realize the photo-control of bioconjugation for bio-labeling and bio-imaging purposes. Two of the most commonly adopted bioconjugation processes are the “Click” reaction and the Staudinger ligation reaction. The former is a [3+2] cycloaddition reaction between an azide and an alkyne, that may require the use of Cu(I) catalysts. The latter is a spontaneous and clean reaction between azides and triarylphosphines to form iminophosphoranes, which can further be hydrolyzed to stable amides. There is already one recent report on photo-regulated “Click” reaction, but, to the best of our knowledge, there is no report on any photo-triggered Staudinger ligation reaction. While there were several previous studies on the photolysis of phosphonium compounds, most of them have focused on the photolytic generation of carbocations rather than paying attention to the possible co-generation of the phosphines. With this view, we designed a thioester-bearing anthracenylmethyl dipehnylphosphonium compound that showed very promising Staudinger ligation properties upon photo-excitation. The aim of this project is to further develop this anthracenylmethyl phosphonium system for photo-triggered traceless Staudinger ligation. A series of new phosphonium compounds will be designed, synthesized and evaluated for their efficiency in the photo-induction of Staudinger ligation reactions. Bio-imaging probes based on these new compounds will also be developed for the fluoro-tagging of selected biomolecules in live cells. Surface-modifying photo-triggered traceless Staudinger ligation reagents will also be developed to demonstrate the possibility of patterned immobilization of biomolecules on inert substrate using such a photo-regulated approach for biosensing and other biomedical applications. 利用光來控制化學/生化反應過程是一個有吸引力的想法。事實上，光化學控制已大幅度地應用於微電子製造上。化學生物學和細胞生物學領域也開始認識到光調控的優勢，並試圖實現光控生物耦合和生物成像。”Click”耦合以及施陶丁格連接反應是目前最普遍被採用的兩個生物耦合反應。前者是一個經Cu（I）催化的疊氮化物和炔烴之間的[3+2] cyclic addition反應。後者則是酰胺疊氮化物和三芳基膦之間自發的反應。最近已有關於光控”Click”反應的報告，但盡我們所知，目前還未有任何關於光控施陶丁格連接反應的報導。以往有關磷化合物光解的研究，大部分都集中在光解產生的碳正離子上，而忽略了所產生的磷化合物可能有用於施陶丁格連接反應。基於這個假設，我們設計一種anthracenylmethyldiphenylphosphonium的化合物，並發現它擁有光觸發施陶丁格反應的特性。這一項目的目標是進一步開發這一個光觸發無痕施陶丁格連接系統。一系列新的鏻化合物會被合成，而它們的光觸發施陶丁格反應效率會被仔細評價。我們也會利用這個光觸發無痕施陶丁格連接系統來開發新的生物成像探針，以及能用於將生化分子固定在惰性底材上的光控表面處理方案。

11301414.label: Realisation of objectives
11301414.value: In this project, we have successfully developed an approach for the photo-triggering of traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reaction via the photocaging of phosphinothioesters by substituted anthracenylmethyl moieties. Photo-uncaging of the phosphonium salts induces heterolytic cleavage of their anthracenylmethyl-phosphorus bond, releasing the diphenylphosphinothioesters as efficient traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reagents. The phosphonium salts also possess considerable solubility in aqueous organic solvents. This facilitates the photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reactions to be carried out in more compatible solvent systems for bioconjugation purposes. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first research group to report the photo-regulation of traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation [1]. Our substituted anthraceneylmethyl photocages are responsive to broadband photolysis from 360 – 425 nm in aqueous organic solvents. The quantum yield of the photo-uncaging process at their optimal wavelengths of photolysis at room temperature is ranged from 2.5% to >= 7%. It has to mention that the research group leads by Prof. Isaac S. Carrico of the State University of New York Stony Brook has reported another photocaging strategy for photo-activated non-traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation a few months before our first publication of our approach [2]. Our two research articles are the only literature for the light-activated Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation at the moment. In this project, we have also demonstrated the capability of photo-triggered bioconjugation of amino acids and oligopeptides with our phosphonium Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reagent [3]. Yields of those oligopeptides are ranged from 31 to 43%, which are consistent with those obtained with traditional traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation processes [4-6]. As demonstrated by our work, the photo-triggered Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process is ideal for the photo-regulated assembly of peptides via the conjugation of smaller oligopeptides and/or amino acids. Unlike other photo-click reactions, our process is able to conjugate molecule units by a simple peptide bond without any other residue atoms at the conjugation. Towards the last 12 months of the project, our main effort has been focused on the use of our photo-triggered Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process for the generation of functional peptides/proteins from non-functional peptide fragments. We worked on the light-activated generation of Angiotensin II (DRVYIHPF), an oligopeptide hormone containing 8 amino acids which regulates our blood pressure by stimulating vasopressin production in the brain and by directly constricting blood vessel wall [7]. It also regulates steroidogenesis by up-regulating the expression level of early transcription factors NR4A1 (NGFIB) and NR4A2 (Nurr1), a process that can be demonstrated in human adrenocortical tumor cells H295R [8]. Hence, the biological activity of Angiotensin II can be verified by its effect on the expression of these two genes in H295R cells. We synthesized the full-length Angiotensin II (DRVYIHPF), and its truncation fragments F1 (DRVY) and F2 (IHPF). The C-terminus of the DRVY fragment was derivatized by (diphenylphosphaneyl)methanethiol to produce the diphenylphosphinothioester derivative of the oligopeptide fragment (denoted as P1). The N-terminus of the IHPF fragment was derivatized into a terminal azido functionality (denoted as P3). H295R cells were serum-starved for 24 hours (to ensure the endogenous Angiotensin II present in the serum was metabolised) prior to the treatment with these peptides at 1uM for one hour. RNAs were then isolated from the treated cells and the expression levels of NR4A1 and NR4A2 were examined. Full-length Angiotensin II induced the expression of both NR4A1 and NR4A2, relative to the housekeeping gene GAPDH, in consistent with previous observations [5]. Neither F1 and F2 caused any significant changes in NR4A1 and NR4A2 expression. This indicates that the biological function of Angiotensin II was eradicated by the truncation. We then treated serum-starved H295R cells with the full-length Angiotensin II, P1, P3 and the conjugation product, R1, for one hour. Previous experiments showed that P1, P3 and R1 did not exert any observable cytotoxicity on H295R cells even after 4-hour incubation (data not shown). Whereas P1 and P3 did not significantly change the expression level of NR4A1 and NR4A2, the ligation product R1 could up-regulate these two genes to a similar extent as the full-length Angiotensin II. This suggests that our Staudinger reaction could traceless ligate two peptides in the correct order, generating a longer peptide that was functionally indistinguishable from the naturally occurring counterpart. From these experimental results, we can conclude that our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process can achieve on-demand assembly of functional peptides, from non-functional oligopeptide fragments, for the regulation of cellular and systemic metabolisms. Works alone this strategy are still on-going despite the completion of this project. Finally, throughout the project period, we have repeatedly attempted to immobilize oligopeptides or single-strand DNAs onto glass substrates using our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process. Our strategy was to immobilize the phosphonium-based photo-triggerable traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation onto the glass substrate. Upon photo-excitation, the reagent will be photo-uncaged to generate the immobilized phosphinothioesters for conjugation with azidylated oligopeptides or proteins. However, we encountered issues of oxidation of the photo-uncaged phosphinothioesters to their corresponding phosphine oxides. Apparently, this oxidation process for the monolayer of immobilized phosphinothioesters is very rapid under ambient conditions, even with thoroughly degassed solvents by argon bubbling. Our results reveal that our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process may not be applicable to photolithography or the photo-patterning of biomolecules on solid substrates. 11301414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301414.value: (1) Anthracenylmethyl moiety is found to be an efficient photocage for phosphine for the realisation of photo-triggered Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation. Phosphinothioesters, known traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligand reagents, can be conveniently caged by reaction with 9-(chloromethyl)anthracene to generate the corresponding phosphonium salts, which possess considerable solubility in aqueous organic solvents. These phosphonium salts can be photolyzed efficiently via broad band irradiation from 360 to 425 nm to release the phosphinothioesters. Quantum yields of such a photo-uncaging process at optimal photo-excitation wavelengths range from 2.5% to >= 7%. (2) Unlike other photo-click reactions, traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation is able to conjugate molecule units by a simple peptide bond without any other residue atoms at the conjugation. Thus, it is ideal for peptide synthesis. Our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process enables the photo-regulation of such a peptide synthesis strategy. We demonstrated this by the conjugation of various amino acids and oligopeptide fragments.Yields of the resulting oligopeptides are ranged from 31 to 43%, which are consistent with those obtained with traditional traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation processes. (3) We have also make use of the photo-regulated peptide synthesis strategy outlined in (2) to generate functional peptide from non-functional oligopeptide fragments. We worked on the light-activated generation of Angiotensin II (DRVYIHPF), an oligopeptide hormone containing 8 amino acids which regulates our blood pressure by stimulating vasopressin production in the brain and by directly constricting blood vessel wall, from its truncated fragments, DRVY and IHPF. The former fragment was derivatized into a phosphinothioester-conjugated oligopeptide, while the latter fragment was azidylated at its N-terminus. We demonstrated that photo-excitation caused the conjugation of those two derivatized fragments into Angiotensin II. We used the H295R human adrenocortical tumour cell line to reveal the outcome of this photo-regulated generation of functional peptides. In the absence of photo-excitation, neither the truncated fragments nor their phosphinothioester/azidylation derivatives were able to induce the expression of early transcription factors NR4A1 (NGFIB) and NR4A2 (Nurr1). After broad band irradiation, significant up-regulation of expression of those transcription factors in H295R was observed. This illustrates the successful conjugation of non-functional peptide fragments into functional Angiotensin II which regulates cellular metabolism. (4) Immobilization phosphonium-based photo-triggerable traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reagents onto glass substrates for the photolithographic patterning of selected biomolecules on solid substrates have been attempted, but failed. The monolayer of immobilized phosphinothioesters generated after photolysis is found to be very susceptible to oxidation which hinders any subsequent traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process to take place.

11301414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301414.value: (1) The capability of our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process to control the in-situ generation of functional peptides/proteins that can regulate metabolism in vitro and in vivo is worthy of further exploration. This process can be developed into a new form of phototherapy for cancers and other systemic diseases. (2) The development of other photocages for phosphinothioesters that allow the photo-uncaging process to take place at lower photo-excitation energy is worthy of further exploration. This enables our photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process to be even more compatible with live cells and in vivo studies.

11301414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301414.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a new, bio-compatible photo-click process known as the photo-triggerable traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reaction. We are the first research group in the world to report such a process. Our process is capable for effecting the conjugation of two molecular units by a simple peptide bond, upon photo-excitation. This process is ideal for the photo-controlled generation of functional peptides/proteins, from non-functional oligopeptide fragments, for the regulation of cellular and systems metabolism. We demonstrated this capability by the conjugation of a serious of amino acids and small oligopeptides, as well as the photo-regulated generation of a peptide hormone, Angiotensin II. We envision that our process can eventually be developed into a new form of phototherapy for cancers and other systemic diseases.

11301514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301514.value: This project is focused on theoretical studies of the oxidation of various organic substrates by ferrate(VI), FeO42- and ferrate(V), FeO43-. These species are very strong oxidants that can oxidize a variety of organic substrates and the mechanisms of these oxidation reactions are of fundamental interest. Ferrate(VI) has been used as an environmentally friendly oxidant for water treatment because it can be readily prepared and it gives nontoxic Fe(III) product. Nature also makes use of a number of heme and non-heme enzymes such as cytochrome P-450 and methane monooxygenase to perform various oxidation reactions via high-valent iron oxo intermediates. The kinetics and mechanisms of the oxidation of various organic substrates by ferrate(VI) have been extensively studied but in some cases contradicting mechanisms were proposed. The theoretical aspects on the oxidations of organic compounds by ferrate species are largely unexplored. In this project, we plan to study the oxidation of alkanes, aliphatic amines, anilines, phenols and organosulfur compounds by ferrate(VI) and ferrate(V) using density functional theory and polarization continuum model methods. We explore the potential energy surfaces of these reactions and evaluate the activation barrier of rate-determining step. In general, there are several possible pathways for the oxidation of an organic compound by a metal oxo species: (a) 1e- transfer, (b) H-atom transfer/proton-coupled 1e- transfer, (c) hydride transfer/proton-coupled 2e- transfer (d) O-atom transfer. Depending on the pH, the ferrate(VI) species can exist in various protonated forms: H3FeO4+, H2FeO4, HFeO4- and FeO42-. Thus, we investigate the reaction mechanisms for each possible pathway by ferrate(VI) species and its protonated forms. In particular, we examine the spin/electron density from reactants to transition state structure to products in order to elucidate the detailed mechanisms. The 1e- reduction of FeO42- by various substrates would generate FeO43-, which is known to be a stronger oxidant and would react faster than FeO42-. However, very few kinetic information on oxidation by ferrate(V) species is known. Hence, we also perform theoretical calculations on oxidation by FeO43- and its protonated forms. The predicted mechanisms and activation barriers will be correlated with the experimental results from the literature. Additional experimental studies, including deuterium isotope effects and 18O-labeling experiments, will be performed by Co-I’s team in order to clarify the mechanisms. Our proposed work should provide valuable insights into the detailed mechanisms of oxidation of organic functional groups by ferrate(V) and ferrate(VI). It makes an important contribution to the reactivity of iron oxo species in general. 本項目著重于六價(FeO42-)及五價(FeO43-)高鐵酸根對各種有機基質氧化作用的理論研究。這兩種高鐵酸根是強氧化劑，可以氧化各種有機基質，氧化反應的機理也值得深入探討。因為六價高鐵酸根容易製備且會生成無毒的三價鐵化合物，其在水處理過程中被視為一種對環境無害的氧化劑。在自然界中，血紅素和非血紅素酶(例如細胞色素 P-450和甲烷單加氧酶)则常會通過高價氧絡鐵中間體進行各種氧化反應。 六價高鐵酸根對各種有機基質氧化作用的動力學及反應機理在實驗上已經得到了廣泛的研究，但在某些例子中存在著相互矛盾的觀點和解釋。另一方面，各種高鐵酸根對有機化合物氧化作用的理論研究卻很少。于此項目中，我們計劃使用密度泛函理論和極化連續介質模型方法對六價及五價高鐵酸根氧化烷烴，脂肪胺，苯胺，酚和有機硫化合物的反應進行研究。我們將探討這些反應的勢能面以及決速步的活化能壘。 通常來說，金屬氧絡物對有機化合物的氧化有如下幾種可能的反應途徑：(a) 單電子轉移， (b) 氫原子轉移或單質子單電子轉移，(c)負氫離子轉移或單質子雙電子轉移，(d)氧原子轉移。根據pH值的不同，六價高鐵酸根化合物能以不同質子化形式存在，如H3FeO4+，H2FeO4， HFeO4- 和FeO42-等。因此，我們將研究六價高鐵酸根化合物及其質子化形式每一種可能反應途徑的機理。對反應物到過渡態再到產物的電子自旋密度，我們將特別進行探討并用以闡明反應機理的細節。 FeO42-經很多基質的電子還原作用可以生成FeO43-. FeO43-是一種強氧化劑并且比FeO42-反應速度更快。但，五價高鐵酸根化合物氧化作用的動力學信息非常少。因此，我們也將對FeO43-及其質子化形式進行理論計算。我們將把預測得到的機理和活化能壘與文獻記載的實驗值進行對比。與此同時，為了更好的說明機理，額外的實驗(例如氘同位素作用和18O標記實驗)會在合作者的研究小組進行。 我們這項工作將對六價及五價高鐵酸根氧化有機功能團的詳細反應機理提供有價值的見解，同時也將會對氧絡鐵化合物活性研究做出重要貢獻。

11301514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301514.value: We have carried theoretical calculations and experimental studies to investigate the activation of ferrate(VI) by Ca2+ at pH 9-10 for the oxidization of water and generation of O2. The reaction has the following rate law: d[O2]/dt = kCa[Ca2+][FeO42-]2. 18O-labelingexperiments show that both O atoms in O2 come from FeO42-. These results together with DFT calculations suggest that the function of Ca2+ is to facilitate intermolecular O-O coupling by bridging two FeO42-. Similar activating effects are also observed with Mg2+ andSr2+. The results were published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 3012 –3016. We have performed theoretical calculations to examine the hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) mechanism in the oxidation of alcohols by [FeO4]2− in aqueous solution. The ferrate(VI) ion, [FeO4]2−, has attracted much interest in recent years because of its potential use as a green oxidant in organic synthesis and water treatment. Although there have been several reports on the use of ferrate(VI) for the oxidation of alcohols to the corresponding carbonyl compounds, the mechanism remains unclear. Two mechanistic steps are considered: the first step is HAT from α-C–H of CH3OH to [FeO4]2− to generate •CH2OH and FeO3(OH)2−. This is followed by either (a) a second HAT to generate HCHO and Fe(IV), or (b) the formation of an organometallic intermediate [Fe(O)3(OH)(CH2OH)]2− which then undergoes a second HAT to form HCHO and Fe(IV). The barrier height in step (a) is much lower than that in step (b). The calculated mechanism is consistent with the kinetic measurements and deuterium isotopic effect. A linear correlation is found between the second-order rate constants and the α-C–H bond dissociation energies (BDEs), ranging from 81 to 95 kcal mol−1, of the alcohols, in agreement with a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) mechanism. The results were published in Dalton Trans., 2018, 47, 240-245. The kinetics and mechanism of the reaction of S(IV) (SO32- + HSO3-) with a ruthenium(VI) nitrido complex, [(L)RuVI(N)(OH2)]+ (RuVIN, L=N,N’-bis(salicylidene)-o-cyclohexyldiamine dianion), in aqueous acidic solutions are reported. The kinetic results are consistent with parallel pathways involving oxidation of HSO3- and SO32- by RuVIN. A deuterium isotope effect of 4.7 is observed in the HSO3- pathway. Based on experimental results and DFT calculations the proposed mechanism involves concerted N-S bond formation (partial N-atom transfer) between RuVIN and HSO3- and H+ transfer from HSO3- to a H2O molecule. The results were published in Chem. Eur. J. 2016, 22, 10754 – 10758. We have employed DFT to investigate the oxidation of HSO3− by a trans-dioxoruthenium-(VI) complex, [RuVI(TMC)(O)2)]2+ (RuVI; TMC = 1,4,8,11-tetramethyl-1,4,8,11-traazcyclotetradecane) in aqueous solutions. The concerted and stepwise proton-coupled O-atom transfer mechanisms are considered. The theoretical calculations suggested that O−H bond breaking occurs in the rate-limiting step and this agrees with the deuterium isotope effect of 17.4 for HSO3− . The results were published in Inorg. Chem. 2017, 56, 12699−12702.

11301914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301914.value: Numerical methods play an important role in the design and optimization of photonic structures and devices. General numerical methods for solving the Maxwell's equations are applicable to most photonics problems, but special methods developed for a class of structures are often much more efficient. Many photonic devices are multiply layered, in the sense that the structure consists of a few parts where each part is a layered structure (i.e., the material properties depend only on one spatial variable z). In this project, we develop an efficient numerical method for three-dimensional (3D) multiply layered structures by coupling one-dimensional (1D) mode expansions and boundary integral equations for two-dimensional (2D) Helmholtz equations. Our method effectively reduces the original 3D problems to 2D problems. Compared with the classical mode matching method (also called eigenmode expansion method or modal method), our method is much more efficient, since it avoids the expensive step of solving 2D eigenvalue problems. The method developed in this project will be used to analyze practical 3D photonic structures. 在設計和優化光子結構及原件的過程中，計算方法起著很重要的作用。雖然解 Maxwell 方程的通用方法也適用於光子學中的問題，但對特殊結構所設計的特殊方法會更有效。很多光子原件是多區分層結構，也就是說，原件有幾個部分組成，每個部分是分層結構。本研究計劃的目的是對多區分層結構開發新的快速計算方法。我們的設想是通過結合一維的模展開和二維的邊界積分方程方法，將三維問題演化為二維問題來求解。同現有的模張開方法相比，我們的方法避免了解二維特徵值問題的困難，可以更加有效。我們的方法會被用來分析一些實用的三維光子結構。

11301914.label: Realisation of objectives
11301914.value: The objectives of this research project is to develop fast computational methods for analyzing the scattering of light by the so-called multiply-layered structures. In the field of photonics, especially plasmonics, many nano-structures consist of tiny cylindrical objects, and they are multiply-layered structures. In principle, to analyze the scattering and resonance of light, it is necessary to solve the three-dimensional Maxwell's equations. However, existing numerical methods are too expensive to use for some problems with large and complicated structures. In this project, we develop the so-called Vertical Mode Expansion Method (VMEM) for multiply-layered structures. The efficiency and accuracy of our method are demonstrated by the examples in our publications. We expect VMEM to be useful in engineering design processes. Four specific objectives are listed below. The first objective is about multiply-layered structures with finite number of circular cylindrical objects and it is addressed in paper [5]. The second objective is related to periodic structures with circular cylindrical objects, and it is addressed in paper [6]. Major progress is made in our paper [2], where a VMEM for arbitrary cylindrical structure is first developed. It relies on a combination of 2D boundary integral equation (BIE) method with 1D (vertical) mode matching technique, and allows us to achieve the third objective. In papers [4] and [14], we apply the VMEM to two special structures which are extremely difficult to analyze by any existing methods. Objective 4 is addressed in papers [11] and [13], where efficient methods for computing resonant modes (also special resonant modes with real frequencies, the so-called bound states in the continuum) are described. We further analyze nonlinear problems related to resonance and scattering in papers [3], [7], [8] and [10]. Note that the BIE method is an important component in our VMEM for general cylindrical objects. In papers [9] and [12], we develop BIE methods for structures with sharp corners and with interfaces extending to infinity.

11301914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301914.value: A multiply-layered structure has its material parameters depending only on one spatial variable (assumed to be the vertical variable) in a number of separating cylindrical regions. Due to the existing nano-fabrication techniques, many multiply-layered structures appear in photonics applications (especially in plasmonics). Existing methods for analyzing such structures by solving 3D Maxwell's equations directly are not efficient and too expensive to use in optimal design processes. We developed an efficient special method, called Vertical Mode Expansion Method (VMEM), for multiply-layered structures. Different versions of VMEM and their applications are described in our publications [1], [2], [4], [5], [6] and [14]. In particular, the VMEM versions given in papers [5], [6] and [2] correspond to our fist, second and third research objectives. Papers [4] and [14] are concerned with two applications of the VMEM. The structures studied in [4] and [14] are extremely difficult to analyze using existing numerical methods. The fourth objective is about numerical method for computing resonant modes, which are eigenstates of the structure with complex frequencies. Special resonant states with real frequencies (and infinite quality factors) are the so-called bound states in the continuum (BICs), and they are particularly interesting and difficult to calculate. In papers [11] and [13], we present a method for computing resonant modes and BICs in different periodic structures. The problem becomes more interesting and more difficult when the media are nonlinear. We study non-linear scattering and resonance problems in papers [3], [7], [8] and [10]. Another difficulty is related to field singularities at corners and edges. We present a highly accurate boundary integral equation method for structures with sharp corners in papers [9] and [12].

11301914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301914.value: Related to the fourth objective, we have developed a VMEM for computing resonant modes of 3D multiply-layered structures. The method requires the use of perfectly matched layers (PMLs). The PML technique is widely used for truncating unbounded domains for numerical simulations of waves. When PML is used for computing resonant modes, it produces errors in the complex resonant frequencies. This error is known to be small, indeed exponentially small with respect to PML parameters, but the relative error for the imaginary part of the complex resonant frequency may be not small. Since resonant modes with a small imaginary part in the complex frequency are very important (they are the resonant modes with high quality factors), we would like to develop numerical (or semi-analytic) methods that can find the imaginary part of the complex resonant frequency with high relative accuracy.

11301914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301914.value: In photonics, especially in the field of plasmonics, it is often necessary to analyze the scattering and resonance of light by nano-structures. Due to the existing fabrication techniques, the nano-structures are often tiny cylindrical objects. In principle, we need to solve the 3D Maxwell's equations if the size of the structure is at least a few nanometers. However, for some complicated structures, solving Maxwell's equations directly is time consuming. Therefore, it is difficult to optimize the designs for these nano-structures. In this project, we developed a new method for analyzing nano-structures involving cylindrical objects. Our method, the so-called vertical mode expansion method (VMEM), is more efficient than existing numerical or semi-analytic methods, since it takes advantage of the special geometric features. The method can be used to optimize nano-structures in photonics and should have many other applications.

11302014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302014.value: The long-term goal of the P.I. is to develop and study, theoretically as well as computationally, efficient, robust and superconvergent numerical methods for solving partial differential equations arising in fluid dynamics and continuum mechanics. In this proposal, the P.I. will concentrate on the study and development of a new, emerging numerical scheme - hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods. HDG methods are characterized by being easier to implement, having enhanced stability, convergence properties and robustness, and by displaying an improved flexibility for handling arbitrarily-shaped domains. The only globally coupled degrees of freedom of HDG mehtods are those of a numerical approximation defined on the boundaries of the elements. Compared with convectional DG methods, HDG methods significantly reduce the degrees of freedom and can be more efficiently implemented. On the other hand, HDG methods use stabilization functions along interfaces of meshes to obtain extra stability, such that they have better stability than mixed finite element methods (HDG methods can be considered as stabilized mixed finite element methods). In addition, post-processed solution of HDG methods achieves one order higher convergence rate for primary variable (like displacement in linear elasticity problem) than mixed finite element methods. These features make HDG methods suitable for solving partial differential equations arising in fluid dynamics and continuum mechanics. The P.I. is interested in studying and developing a new class of HDG methods, which is robust, efficient and superconvergent without post-processing, for a variety of equations arising in fluid dynamics and continuum mechanics. 该P.I.的长期目标是开发和研究，从理论上以及为解决流体动力学和连续介质力学所产生的偏微分方程计算，高效，严谨，超收敛数值方法。在这个方案中，P.I.将集中在一个新的，新兴的数值方法的研究与发展 - 杂交间断有限元（HDG）的方法。 HDG方法的特点是易于实现，具有增强的稳定性，收敛性和鲁棒性，并通过显示处理任意形状域改进的灵活性。唯一的全局耦合度HDG自由度的是那些对元素的边界所限定的数值近似。与对流DG方法相比，HDG方法显著减少的自由度，并且可以更有效地实现。在另一方面，HDG方法使用稳定功能以及网格接口，以获得额外的稳定性，使得他们比混合有限元法（HDG方法可视为稳定的混合有限元方法），更好的稳定性。此外，HDG方法后处理解决方案，实现了高一阶收敛速度主要变量（如位移线弹性问题）比混合有限元方法。这些特性使得HDG方法适用于解决出现的偏微分方程 在流体动力学和连续介质力学。 该P.I.有兴趣研究和开发一类新的HDG方法，这是强大的，高效的和超收敛无后处理，用于各种流体动力学和连续介质力学所产生的方程。

11302114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302114.value: When a semiconductor quantum dot (QD) absorbs a photon of light a pair of charged carriers (a hole and an electron) are created, as an exciton within the nanoparticle. Depending on the particular application, we may want the two geminate carriers to recombine some time later and re-emit a photon of light. Alternatively we may want to dissociate the charges and extract them from the material as a photocurrent (e.g. in an optical detector or a photovoltaic solar cell). In most cases it is unhelpful if one or both of the photoinduced charges becomes localized and trapped, within the QD or elsewhere outside the QD in the device structure. Additional energy is required to de-trap carriers, and they may be trapped and unable to recombine for much longer than the normal timescale for band edge recombination. Where recombination involving de-trapped carriers does occur, and where the trap state energy lies between the conduction and valence band energy levels of the QD, the recombination is red shifted. Depending on the trap energy level and the depth of the trap, carriers may not necessarily re-combine radiatively. In such cases a charge other than the original geminate photocharge combines with the trapped carrier, or the trapped carrier may be involved in a chemical reaction at the site and that might have implications for the stability of the material. In photovoltaic devices especially, traps within the QDs, at their surfaces or within the material surrounding the QDs can have a very limiting impact on the efficiency and service lifetime of the solar cell. In other devices (photoconductive detectors) however, it can be beneficial to have a limited number of shallow traps, provided the trapped carriers do not undergo any deleterious chemical reactions whilst localized. There are many different types of potential trap sites in QDs and in composite devices with QDs embedded in dielectric solids. The energetics and carrier dynamics can span a wide range (from the fs to over seconds timescale). We propose to study and understand the formation of charge traps in low bandgap QD materials and composites by correlating a range of electrical, electro-optic and optical measurement techniques and physical characterization of the QDs, with the synthetic methods used in their preparation. In this way we aim to improve the performance of our QD materials by engineering traps in a controlled manner. 當半導體量子點納米晶吸收一個光子，將會產生一對荷電載流子（即電子-空穴，是為激子）。根據具體的應用領域不同，我們可能希望延緩這對激子的復合并重新發射光子。或者期望電荷分離並將電荷導出形成光電流（如光探測或者光伏太陽能電池應用）。然而，大多數情況下，光生電子或/和空穴易被量子點內部或者器件結構中的陷阱捕獲，這一情況是不利的，需要額外的能量來釋放被陷阱捕獲的載流子。載流子被捕獲后，其復合需要的時間要遠長於常規帶間復合時間。如果脫離陷阱的載流子要發生復合，且其陷阱能級位於量子點的導帶和價帶之間，該復合將會發生紅移。根據陷阱能級的位置和深度，載流子亦可能發生無放射復合。在這種情況下，電荷而非原始的光電荷與被捕獲的載流子結合，或者被捕獲的載流子參與化學反應，這關乎到材料的穩定性。特別是在光伏器件中，量子點內部、表面或者周邊物質中的陷阱嚴重影響對太陽能電池的效率和服務壽命。然而，在其他器件如光敏探測器中，如果陷阱載流子不發生不利的化學反應同時局限化，一定數量的淺態陷阱是有益的。在量子點及電介質包覆量子點復合器件中，存在大量不同類型的潛在陷阱，其動能學和載流子動力學特征差異很大，時間尺度跨越飛秒到秒級。我們計劃通過系統的電學、電-光和光學性能測試技術和物理表征手段，并結合合成方法和製備技術的應用，來研究和理解電荷陷阱在窄禁帶量子點及其復合材料的形成過程和機理，以期通過有效的陷阱調控提高量子點材料的綜合性能。

11302114.label: Realisation of objectives
11302114.value: All the objectives of this projects have been successfully achieved. Synthesis of CdTe, alloyed CdHgTe, and HgTe quantum dots (QDs) under different growth conditions has been performed. Narrowing of the photoluminescence of aqueous CdTe QDs via Ostwald Ripening suppression was realized by programmed dropwise precursor addition. Enhancement of the fluorescence quantum yield of thiol-stabilized CdTe QDs through surface passivation with sodium chloride and bicarbonate has been achieved. Exchange kinetics and surface recovery of alloyed CdgTe QDs during cation exchange has been revealed using a microfluidic flow reactor. Room temperature synthesis of HgTe QDs in an aprotic solvent has been developed, leading to high photoluminescence quantum yields in the infrared. Ultrafast spectroscopy on these materials (fluorescence, and transient absorption) at wavelengths extending from the visible to the near infrared has been performed to study the initial stages of carrier trapping, and to identify trap sites. Dielectric functions of CdHgTe QD films have been evaluated by spectroscopic ellipsometry. FET measurements have been performed on film samples to further probe carrier dynamics and to determine recombination mechanisms, trap densities, and lifetimes. Polaron and energy transfer effects have been studied experimentally and theoretically on a system where D2O/H2O solvent exchange has been applied to influence on the emission of HgTe and CdTe QDs. In collaboration with theory group from the University of Hamburg, Germany, a model has been developed which provided important insights into strain effects on band alignment shifts, carrier localization and recombination kinetics in CdTe/CdS core/shell QDs. In collaboration with another theory group from NTU Singapore, excitonic character in optical properties of tetrahedral CdX (X=S, Se, Te) clusters has been demonstrated. Based on the developed methodology to identify and control trap characteristics and densities to allow material engineering via synthesis and fabrication processes for different types of optoelectronic devices, HgTe QD phototransistors enabling high-sensitivity room-temperature photodetection at 2000 nm have been fabricated. Temperature dependence of exciton and trap-related photoluminescence of CdTe and CdHgTe QDs embedded in a NaCl matrix has been used to demonstrate the possibilities of a nanoscale optical thermometry. Basics of the aqueous chemical synthesis of semicondcutor QDs have been summarized in a comprehensive review publishe din Chemical Reviews. Materials aspects of semiconductor QDs used in a variety of optoelectronic applications have been summarized in a review published in Materials Horizons. Carrier multiplication mechanisms and competing processes in colloidal semiconductor nanostructures have been analyzed in relation to traps in a review paper in Materials. Waveguide and optoelectronic devices utilizing narrow band infrared HgTe QDs have been considered in a review published in Z. Phys. Chem.

11302114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302114.value: Major findings of this project constitute new chemical syntheses of narrow-bandgap semiconductor quantum dots (QDs): CdTe based materials emititng in the red and near-infrared; alloyed CdHgTe QDs emitting in the near-infrared; and HgTe QDs emitting in the near-to-mid infrared spectral ranges. The nature of optical traps in these materials has been identified using a range of optical (photoluminescense; transient absorption) and electrical (FET) measurements. The obtained knowledge has been used to optimize several kind of optoelectronic devices based on these QD materials, such as HgTE phototransistors enabling high-sensitivity room-temperature photodetection at 2000 nm, and optical nanothermometry approaches utilizing exciton and trap-related photoluminescence of CdT and CdHgTe QDs. In collaboration with theory group from the University of Hamburg, Germany, a model has been developed which provided important insights into strain effects on band alignment shifts, carrier localization and recombination kinetics in CdTe/CdS core/shell QDs. In collaboration with another theory group from NTU Singapore, excitonic character in optical properties of tetrahedral CdX (X=S, Se, Te) clusters has been demonstrated. The results of this project have bene published in 10 original research papers, and in 4 review articles, some of them in very high impact journals such as Chemistry of Materials, ACS Nano, and Chemical Reviews. They have also been disseminated at 9 international research conferences, where the PIs of this project delivered invited talks. PhD by Nema Abdelazim (City University of Hong Kong) has been obtained on the research topic of this project.

11302114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302114.value: Further development of this project may include a focused effort on the further improvement of optical characteristics of mid-infrared emitting HgTe quantum dots. The aim will be to significantly extend their emission further in to nid-infrared range (up to 4000 nm), and to improve their photoluminescence quantum yield up to 10-15%. In collaboration with a device engineering group at CUHK, photodetector devices utilizing these QDs will be fabricated and tested.

11302114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302114.value: When a semiconductor quantum dot (QD) absorbs a photon of light a pair of charged carriers is created. In most cases it is detrimental if the photoinduced charges becomes trapped, within the QD or in the device structure. In some devices however, such as photoconductive detectors, it can be beneficial to have a limited number of shallow traps. There are many different types of potential trap sites in QDs and in composite devices with QDs embedded in dielectric solids, and their energetics and carrier dynamics can span a wide range. In this project, we studied and understood the formation of charge traps in narrow bandgap QD materials and composites by correlating a range of electrical, electro-optic and optical measurement techniques and physical characterization of the QDs, with the synthetic methods used in their preparation. In this way we were able to develop several kind of light-emitting QD materials, such as CdTE, CdHgTe and HgTe QDs with favorable optical characteristics, where performance has been improved by engineering traps in a controlled manner. These improved QD materials were used to produce a range of optoelectronic devices, such as photodetectors for infra-red spectral range, and optical thermometers.

11302314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302314.value: 可靠性的数学方法：诊断，维修和耐久度

11302314.label: Project Objectives
11302314.value: To advance the mathematical science base of the assurance sciences that comprise the topics of reliability theory and risk analysis.
rows: To advance the mathematical science base of the assurance sciences that comprise the topics of reliability theory and risk analysis.

11302314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302314.value: 为了开展关于系统诊断，可靠性和可维修性的随机建模的研究，特此申请为期三年的研究经费。研究工作分有三个方面，每个部分都有各自独立的研究计划。但因为每个方面都致力于发展一套理论与方法以深入刻画可靠性与风险之科学基础，所以所有的研究计划都在这里列出。 1） 第一个研究方向是一套关于工程与医学中诊断与侦测检验之随机性的理论。整个理论建立于信息论和决策理论的基础上。这项工作首要的目标是发展可以最小化误诊率的高效的方法。这套方法不仅可以直接应用于医学中，而且与信号处理，威胁侦测，科学发现有着紧密的联系。 2） 可靠性与可维修性一直被视为分立的两个课题。他们所使用的模型，和具体的应用方法都有着很大的不同。最近关于抗风险潜力（Hazard Potential）的工作为可靠性与可维修性的研究提供了一个整体的框架。具体而言，衰老，磨损和疲劳可以被认为是消耗了抗风险潜力，而维修的行为会重新补充抗风险潜力。这种情形可以与筑坝蓄水以及库存的理论进行对比，这样的类比本质在于从统一的视角看待两者。如此，我们就有了一类全新的研究问题，首先使用一个抗风险潜力的命中时间即使失效时间的随机过程来建模退化数据。然后是建立库存式模型来更新抗风险潜力，以之诠释维修的概念。 3） 目前，可靠性（几率）已经成为了评估一个事物可信赖度的唯一度量。这一度量的本质缺陷在与几率是一个无法观测的项，所以缺乏操作性。我们认为是从实用主义的角度出发，一个可操作的度量是事物的耐久度（Survivability）。这一观点等同于这样一个主题，即评估事物的可信赖度的基本方法需要被重新诠释。使得可靠性可以被视为Popper所云的倾向性（Propensity），或是Kolmogorov所云的未定义的朴素概率（Primitive），而耐久度则是一个人关于倾向性的主观概率（如de Finite所云）这个观点引出了诸多哲学议题，而解决这些问题可以带来可靠性理论和风险分析之数学基础的根本改变。解释这些思路并将他们付诸实用的工具则是滤波理论的本质与追踪可靠性随着时间与阶段发展的演化

11302314.label: Realisation of objectives
11302314.value: The mathematical theory of reliability, as it has evolved for a long time and up until today, is based on a paradigm of the World War II era. Reliability has been viewed as an objective feature of items, individuals, and systems. This paradigm has been dictated by an interpretation of probability that has been under much debate and discussion since the times of Bernoulli, Bayes, and La Place. We challenge this concept vis a vis the notion of reliability, and make the case that whereas reliability may be an objective feature of items and systems, ones inability too see it and to measure it reduces the notion of reliability to an abstraction. We advocate the view that reliability is not the correct metric for assessing a system's ability to function, but that our perception of reliability, which we call survivability is the correct metric. Our papers makes the case for our view in two scenarios, one pertaining to testing and detection and the other pertaining to the evolution of a system under development, such a complex engineering entity of a software system. This view of ours has been challenged by a few as well as endorsed by some. The discussants of our main contribution, namely the paper on tracking for survivability, state their positions. Based on our work in reliability we venture beyond it to make the case that our perception is also relevant to one of the most widely used mathematical and engineering methodologies in data science, namely, filtering and control, and make the case that despite its phenomenal success the current practice therein lacks a foundation. We provide this foundation. The three documents under preparation pertain to miscellaneous issues, such as some hidden caveats in using Bayes' Law (very commonly used in reliability), the resolution of a long standing open problem in reliability, namely assessing the efficacy of diagnostic tests using Information Theoretic ideas, and the decomposition of a survival function to yield a spectrum of inequalities, leading to a new characterization of distributions. The article on "Seeking Relationships in Big Data" is motivated by a widely referenced and discussed paper in Science,and comments on the fact that observed correlations do not imply causality and that the former are merely manifestations of a subjectively chosen probability model. One document, accepted for publication, leads on Popper's notion of what is a science, and comes to the conclusion that reliability, like mathematics and statistics is not a science. The GRF has helped support the work of a doctoral student, whose general topic pertains to contributions to data science an his has been recorded.

11302314.value: 1. A clearer and cleaner articulation as to what reliability means and how to track its evolution over time. 2. The resolution of a long standing problem in detection and diagnostic testing. 3. A new decomposition and characterization of probability distributions. 4. Letting those who routinely use Bayes' law to address reliability and survival analysis problems as to what underlies the mechanics of their mathematical processes. 5. Pointing out to fallacies about identifying causality based on an analysis of observed data alone.

11302314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302314.value: A more defensible and more realistic way to think about a commonly used concept in engineering reliability and medical survival analysis by making a distinction between an item's propensity to fail and our ability to assess and track this propensity. This boils down to a change in a paradigm that has been in vogue for almost 75 years, despite criticisms about it.

11302514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302514.value: 關於非綫性拋物方程特徵綫型數值方法的新分析

11302514.label: Project Objectives
11302514.value: With the new approach, we first investigate a typical characteristic method, the modified method of characteristics, for two popular physical equations, incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and incompressible miscible displacement in porous media. We will introduce a new auxiliary characteristic time-discrete system for each model. The error analysis and regularity analysis of the solution of the time-discrete system will be studied. More attention will be paid to $tau$-independent error estimates of the modified method of characteristics for the time-discrete system. With these estimates, we may establish the boundedness of numerical solution in $W^{1,infty}$-norm, with which optimal error estimates can be obtained unconditionally or almost unconditionally (i.e., when time stepsize $tau$ and spatial stepsize $h$ are small than a given positive constant) in a usual way. We will extend the temporal-spatial error splitting argument to some other type characteristic methods, such as CMFEM, ELLAM and MMOCAA, which have certain advanatges on implementation and boundary conditions. However, these methods may have a stronger coupling of the temporal error and the spatial error. Analysis for the corresponding characteristic time-discrete system may not be straightforward and some modified temporal-spatial error splittings are needed. A systematic numerical simulation for several practical models with different characteristic temporal discrete schemes and different spatial approximations will be presented to confirm our theoretical analysis. Effective implementation and applicability to more general boundary conditions will be studied. Some other physical applications, such as a compressible sweat flow through porous textile materials, will also be investigated.

11302514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302514.value: The convection and diffusion play an important role in many physical phenomena. In some applications, the convection may dominate in the fluid transport process and the diffusion is weak. In such a case, the model is often described by a parabolic equation (or system) with a strong hyperbolic feature. This festure should be considered in developing numerical methods. The method of characteristic type, which is based on a hyperbolic tracking, is especially effective for convection-dominated diffusion equations and numerical simulations show that the method is stable for a large time step. However, existing theoretical analyses may not match such observations well since optimal error estimates were always obtained under certain time stepsize restrictions. In this project, we intend to investigate further characteristic type methods for a large class of nonlinear convection-dominated diffusion equations and to provide unconditional error analysis. 在許多流體運動問題中，對流常常是佔優的。這樣的問題可以被描述為帶着雙曲特徵的抛物方程。特徵綫型方法是基於雙曲特徵而發展出的有效的數值方法。數值實驗顥示該方法允許使用更大時間步長。然而，存在的理論分析常常要求時間步長滿足若干強的限制性條件。在該研究計劃中，我們將進一步研究特徵綫型數值方法並給出無步長限制的理論分析。

11302714.value: 随着能源需求不断上升，全球变暖和能源经济等相关问题变得日益严峻，二氧化碳的回收及再利用将成为解决矿物能源利用的关键技术。这场较量在于发展绿色的二氧化碳还原技术，使之成为化石燃料运用中的不可分割的技术。 该项目申请旨在通过半导体催化剂组装得到Z型光催化剂，开发人工光合作用体系，以达到仅利用水和太阳光化学还原二氧化碳的目的。这涉及到将价带足够正以氧化水的金属氧化物与导带足够负以还原CO2的量子点耦合在一起。这样的Z型光催化剂的最大优势在于，不再是一个单一的光催化剂结构，而是一个可以结合多种光催化剂材料特点来满足对催化剂的两个能带中任何一个的要求。 Z型光催化反应中有5个核心组成部分，即析氧催化剂（OEC），金属氧化物的光催化剂，电子介体，量子点的光催化剂，和CO2还原催化剂（CRC）。除了设计OEC，这个被认为是最近的发现高效的磷酸钴和二氧化铱已经解决难题，该项目着重于其它组成部分的系统开发。在这里，我们选择TiO2，ZnO，SnO2，SrTiO3, WO3, Fe2O3和BiVO4等典型金属氧化物催化及它们的掺杂形式。同样，量子点光催化剂的选择范围包括CdX，PbX（X = S，Se，Te）和CuInS2，其中量子点的导带电位和能隙可以通过控制晶体的尺寸进行精确调控。我们将研究各种不同的电子传导策略，包括物理耦合，石墨稀辅助，重金属以及水溶性的离子媒介。一种新型的基于碱金属氧化物的，能够高效并选择性地还原CO2的CRC也是本项目研究的对象之一。 Z型光催化剂将在模拟太阳照射下进行评估，而其中基础的电荷传输和还原二氧化碳的机理将被揭示出来。该项目的研究成功将产生一个类新的利用太阳能活化和选择性还原CO2的光催化剂。

11302714.label: Realisation of objectives
11302714.value: All the objectives as laid out in this Project have been fully met. Under Objective 1, we developed a number of Z-scheme photocatalysts and their individual components for CO2 reduction and the water oxidation as the conjugate reaction. These photocatalysts are composed of the combination of wide and narrow/mid-bandgap semiconductors, which in these particular cases provide oxidative and reductive sites, respectively. Under Objective 2, we have elucidated the electron transport phenomena across interfaces. We found that depending on the combination of semiconductor materials, the photoelectrons across interface is dominated by the effect of shuttling between the two semiconductors. We devised strategies to overcome these shortcomings. Under Objective 3, we assessed the durability of the photocatalysts over a long period of assessment (more than 18 h). While the oxide-based photocatalysts show extremely high stability in photocatalytic activity, the chalcogenide series show low stability, but can be overcome with the design of capping agent.

11302714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302714.value: Through this project, we developed composite Z-scheme photocatalysts with suitable energy potentials for the reduction of CO2 and the oxidation of water. We found that the Bi2O3 photocatalyst, when coupled with a suitable water oxidation photocatalysts such as TiO2, Ag@AgCl and BaLaTi4O15, was capable of reducing CO2 to form CO, formic acid and methanol (Output 10.1, and 10.7). The deposition of electron sink, e.g., Pt-rGO, was found to minimize the electron shuttling and hence improved the photoconversion efficiency (Output 8.1, 8.5, and 9.2). The ionic conductivity of Bi2O3 is one of the key parameters that govern its surface catalytic activity as we have reported in Output 8.2. We tested the reusability of the photocatalyst over an 18 h irradiation, and found highly stable photocatalytic activity in the reduction of CO2 and water oxidation. The addition of Ru deposits renders high selectivity towards methane formation due to the strong hydrogenation activity (Output 8.3). To cover a wider spectrum of the solar irradiation, we also explored the Z-scheme photocatalyst based on chalcogenide quantum dots (QDs), which include CdS and CdTe on TiO2 nanotubes. To optimize the synthesis of the QDs, we performed the first in situ studies using a microfluidic device to follow their formation mechanism and optical properties (Output 8.4). We further found that the doping of Mn in CdS improved the charge separation efficiency due to the enhanced electron lifetime of the CdS (Output 8.6). An inherent disadvantage of chalcogenide QDs is the low stability but this can be minimized by optimizing the design of capping ligands. For a C3 molecule such as mercaptopropinic acid capping ligand, we showed a decrease of ~30% in activity after an equivalent of 1.5 months of continuous solar irradiation (Output 9.3-9.6, 9.12, 10.2). Besides using TiO2 nanotube as the water oxidation photocatalyst, we also developed the highly stable Sn-doped hematite (rust!) using a novel modulated anodization synthesis as alternative (Output 8.7). Lastly, we explored the use of a series of Rh-complexes as the CO2 reduction photocatalyst anchored onto BaLaTi4O15 and TiO2 as the water oxidation photocatalyst (Output 9.7, 10.4). Unlike heterogeneous photocatalysts, Rh-complexes are highly selective towards the reduction of CO2 to CO. Turnover number as high as 8.9 for CO evolution was measured under simulated solar irradiation. The competing minor reaction is H2 evolution, which we identified as due to the back electron injection (as opposed to the Z-scheme transport for CO evolution) to the oxide photocatalyst.

11302714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302714.value: Through the project, we developed Z-scheme photocatalysts and their photocatalytic components for the reduction of CO2 using sunlight and water (i.e., water oxidation). The work laid out the interfacial charge transport mechanisms for these different classes of photocatalysts, as well as the stability. Such knowledge serves as the fundamental basis for the design of more efficient photocatalyst combinations in the near future. To this end, it is fair to claim that the design of the photocatalytic component for the CO2 reduction is more sophisticated than the water oxidation component, given the low photostability of the former. As such, the exploration of more recently reported stable photocatalysts with high conduction band edges, e.g., pristine and doped g-C3N4, can be further coupled to the highly stable water oxidation photocatalysts developed in this work. Such effort is currently underway, while also looking into the potential of N2 fixation (NH3 evolution) using the developed Z-scheme photocatalysts. Because the products of CO2 reduction are normally of low values, e.g., CO, methanol, formic acid, we developing further downstream techniques for upgrading the value of the products by further converting them to usable fuels and valuable chemicals. These upgraded products include methane, dimethyl ether, levulinic acid (Output 9.1, 9.7-9.10). We believe they are part of an integrated process for CO2 capture and reduction.

11302714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302714.value: A number of composite photocatalysts that carries out the simultaneous reduction of CO2 and water oxidation under solar irradiation has been developed in this project. These photocatalysts can be categorized into bismuth oxide-series, quantum dots-series, and the Rh-complexes series. By applying the charge transport engineering, we were able to overcome a number of reaction bottlenecks that limited the overall photocatalytic efficiencies and photostability. As a result, these photocatalysts are capable of producing CO2 valorization products such as carbon monoxide, methanol and formic acid, which can be further upgraded to usable fuels and valuable chemicals. The development of such technologies are highly critical as part of the wider effort in combating climate change, especially in the region of the Greater China. The project has contributed to the training of 5 PhD students and 2 undergraduate students in this field.

11302914.value: quantile回歸分析與失蹤和長度偏見數據

11302914.label: Project Objectives
11302914.value: Part 1 of the project considers quantile regression with data missing from the covariates and/or response. The specific objectives are as follows: a) Develop methods for handling missing data in a quantile regression context based on the approaches of non-parametric inverse probability weighting, estimating equation projection and a combination of both; b) Derive asymptotic results in relation to the properties of the quantile regression estimators obtained after adjusting for missing data; in particular, evaluate the asymptotic efficiency of the estimators against the semiparametric efficiency bound; c) Adapt the majorize/minimize (MM) algorithm for finding optimal estimates to the current context of analysis, and consider any necessary modification to the algorithm; d) Develop a resampling method for computing the variance-covariance matrix of the estimators in practical implementation; e) Conduct an extensive Monte-Carlo study to investigate the finite-sample properties of the proposed estimators, and f) Apply the method to real data. Part 2 of the project considers quantile regression with length-biased survival data with the following objectives: a) Develop a varying-coefficient quantile regression approach to model length-biased survival data; b) Derive the asymptotic properties of the quantile regression estimators obtained by the approach of local inverse probability weighting; c) Adapt the majorize/minimize (MM) algorithm for finding optimal estimates to the current context of analysis, and consider any necessary modification to the algorithm; d) Conduct an extensive Monte-Carlo study to investigate the finite-sample properties of the proposed estimators, and e) Apply the method to real data.
