11302914.value: 在統計模型,數據往往不足以各種方式。 一個主要的缺陷時出現某些意見是完全不可用。 另一個缺陷常遇到的做法,特別是與生存的數據示例數據,是的,長度偏見的可能性,也就是說,選擇一個觀察從人口的比例,是從開始的時候,沒有發生事件。 主要的利益,這項工程計劃,結合quantile回歸(QR)分析與上述形式的數據不足。 這些主題是不發達,現有的文獻。 盡管這些武器的工具,可用於減輕的影響,缺少的數據,主要要素,這些工具強調有條件意味著估計。 與此相反,有幾項研究審查時的情況下的目標是,估計quantiles有條件。 這是不幸的,因為現在是一個必不可少的工具QR統計研究。 引人注目的是,一小撮的方法可用於處理失蹤QR所有數據,也有著共同的弱點是無法治療沒有反應,同時covariates。 大多數這些方法還依靠強有力的假設完全相同的方式分發錯誤,很多人也不會有健全的理論基礎。 顯然,這些缺點造成嚴重限制的方法的效用。 一個重要原因,沒有一個“quantile對應”的許多技術發展的條件意味著模型qrs丟失的數據是基於非順利標准職能。 這後一種功能構成了重大的技術挑戰之一,試圖建立optimality屬性的方法,在quantile設置。 擬議的研究認為作為一個主要重點為三個方法處理數據的一個失蹤QR設置。 這些包括反向的概率相對比重(國際)方法,估計方程式預測(通行証)方法和一個兩者結合。 其中一些辦法已制訂模型隻是最近才有條件意味著,它是由不當作一回事,延長他們QR背景下,由於上述技術上的挑戰。 我們已花了相當多的時間和努力探討這些技術問題和發現,他們可能是克服使用技術,利用成果過程中的經驗。 此外,我們建議的方法可以處理丟失數據的反應和/或covariates,和他們具備最佳性能甚至在非相同錯誤的。 我們認為,這些結果是相當重要的進展和決定,申請撥款,完成這項工作。 還有一個需要發展一個調整的方法來獲得越差額的估測指標。 所要求的金額是主要的征聘一名研究助理,進行模擬和真實的數據分析。 第二個重點領域,這項研究是關於如何對待長度偏見數據在QR模型。 該研究對模擬有條件quantiles生存的時代已經擴展到在最近幾年,但很少研究考慮數據長度-biasedness聯和那些不承擔所有的線性功能之間關系的生存時間和covariates。 我們建議使用一種不同的系數QR辦法。 一個重要力量,我們的慣常做法,除了提供靈活的系數的不同,是我們不需要承擔的封殺變量正在分發的獨立covariates或失敗的時代。 我們已經制訂了一些關鍵性的理論屬性的方法,但尚未完成的數值分析。 我們把這第二個題目的第一個關於失蹤的數據在一個單一項目,因為他們兩個構成一個有凝聚力的小組,我們可以從中得到的物業的QR估測指標使用類似的分析和計算技術。

11302914.label: Realisation of objectives
11302914.value: Both objectives 1. and 2. listed above have been fully achieved without any issue. In addition, the project has considered two other research problems related to missing and censored data in statistics. In this regard, the project objectives have been over-achieved. At the initial stage of the project, the P.I. and Co-I.’s work focused on Part 2 of the project on developing a varying-coefficient quantile regression approach to model length-biased survival data. On the theoretical side, they worked out the asymptotic theoretical properties of the estimator. They also developed a MM algorithm for computing the estimates and carried out extensive Monte Carlo studies. This resulted in a paper published in the Electronic Journal of Statistics. During the second stage of the project, the P.I. and Co-I. worked on aspects relating to the Part 1 of the project. They considered the three missing data handling approaches as stated in the original proposal, namely, inverse probability weighting, estimating equation projection and the amalgamation of the two, in the context of quantile regression context, and derived the asymptotic properties of the resultant estimators. This was quite significant as few studies had considered missing data handling procedures in quantile regression in spite of quantile regression’s being a useful and popular statistical tool. The P.I. and Co-I. also developed an algorithm and a bootstrap method for computing the estimates. This resulted in a paper published in the Journal of the American Statistical Association. During the course of their investigation, the P.I. and Co-I. found that the theoretical tools and numerical algorithms developed under Parts 1 and 2 of the project can be applied to other related research problems. In particular, they considered the case of censored data that was closely related to length-biased data, and that of the accelerated failure time competing risks model with causes of failure missing at random. Investigations on aspects similar to those considered under Parts 1 and 2 but with the focus changed to censored data were carried out. The outcome was fruitful and led to a publication in the Computational Statistics and Data Analysis. For the research work on the accelerated failure time model with missing failure cause, the P.I. and Co-I. were able to collaborate with Prof. Peter Gilbert, a well-known biostatistician from the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center of the University of Washington, who supplied the P.I. and Co-I. an HIV vaccine efficacy trial data set for illustrating the technical methods developed. The P.I. considered this a significant development because it has paved the way for further collaboration with the Fred Hutchinson Institute. The joint paper with Dr. Gilbert has recently accepted for publication in Statistica Sinica. The P.I. and Co-I have also generalised the analysis considered in Part 1 of the project to the case where the underlying estimating equation is non-smooth. The quantile regression case considered under Part 1 is a special case of non-smooth estimating equations. The paper containing the results is currently under submission.

11302914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302914.value: Major findings and research outcomes include the following: 1) An important feature of the methods developed under Part 1 of the project is their ability to handle missing response and/or partially missing covariates, whereas existing techniques can handle only one or the other, but not both. We have proved that our methods yield asymptotically equivalent estimators that achieve the desirable asymptotic properties of unbiasedness, normality, and root-n consistency. We have also found that under the special case of identical error distributions, all of our proposed estimators achieve the semiparametric efficiency bound. In addition, we have developed an iterative method based on the majorize/minimize algorithm for computing the quantile regression estimates, 2) Under Part 2 of the project, a varying-coefficient quantile regression approach to model length-biased data is developed. This new approach does not only allow the direct estimation of the conditional quantiles of survival times based on a flexible model structure, but also has the important appeal of permitting dependence between the censoring variable and the covariates. We have developed local linear estimators of the coefficients using a local inverse probability weighted estimating equation approach, and established these estimators’ asymptotic properties. 3) We have also developed a varying-coefficient approach to the estimation of regression quantiles under random data censoring. We have used a weighted inverse probability approach to account for censoring, and proposed a majorize–minimize type algorithm to optimize the non-smooth objective function. An important aspect of this work is that the method allows the censoring time to depend on the covariates. 4) We have also examined the accelerated failure time competing risks model with missing cause of failure using the monotone class rank-based estimating equations approach. We handle the non-smoothness of the rank-based estimating equations using a kernel smoothed estimation method. Under this setup, we estimate the unknown regression parameters based on missing data handling mechanism developed under Part 1 of the project. We have also obtained the associated asymptotic theories of the proposed estimators. A real data application based on a HIV vaccine efficacy trial study has been considered.

11302914.value: The techniques developed have application potential for a lot of medical data analysis problems, where observations are frequently missing, length-biased or censored.

11302914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302914.value: In statistical modelling, data are frequently deficient. One major deficiency arises when certain observations are completely missing. Another deficiency commonly encountered in practice is the data sample is length-biased, meaning that the probability of selecting an observation from the population is proportional to the time from the initiation event to the failure event. The main interest of this project is to combine quantile regression (QR) analysis with the above mentioned forms of deficient data. The study has considered three methods for handling missing data in a QR setting. These include the inverse probability weighting (IPW) method, estimating equation projection (EEP) method and a combination of both. Some of these approaches have been developed for conditional mean modelling but extension to QR contexts is non-trivial. As well, few studies have consider data length-biasedness in conjunction with modeling conditional quantiles. Our study has used a varying-coefficient QR approach. One remarkable strength of our approach is that it has very flexible because we do not assume the censoring variable being distributed independently of the failure times. We have established the theoretical properties of the proposed techniques and demonstrated that they work well for practical real data problems where observations are missing or length-biased.

11303314.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11303314.value: Prof Huang, Huaxiong Prof Miura, Robert

11303314.label: Project Objectives
11303314.value: We will develop a framework to determine the electrodiffusive transport of ions across a membrane. We will adopt the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations (that represent a simple self-consistent description of electrodiffusion) for arbitrary ions across a membrane that is much wider than the Debye length and does not contain fixed charge. We will then obtain solutions to the PNP system and develop theoretical tools to consider existence and uniqueness of the solutions. We will then adapt the above method to include the effects of fixed charge in the membrane and determine how the fixed charge can affect the ion transport. We will pay particular attention to issues of non-uniqueness that are known to be important for cases in which fixed charge is present. We will use the solutions to the Poisson-Nernst-Planck system to develop expressions for the ion fluxes across a membrane that can be applied to models for CSD. Using these expressions, we will implement the ion fluxes into the CSD model of Chang et al. (2013) that used an empirical model for ion fluxes. We will then numerically solve the CSD model for physiologically relevant parameters and determine how electrodiffusion affects the wave speed and instigation threshold for CSD waves. We will also develop a model to describe electrodiffusion in the extra-cellular space. Using asymptotic techniques based on the smallness of the Debye length, we will solve the model equations and obtain expressions for the ion flux in the extra-cellular space. We will then use this expression for the ionic flux in the CSD model of Chang et al. (2013) that previously approximated ion transport as simple diffusion. Again, by numerically solving the CSD model, we will determine the importance of electrodiffusion in affecting the wave speed and instigation threshold. Finally, we will include both the electrodiffusion model for cross-membrane transport with the electrodiffusion model for ion fluxes in the extra-cellular space into the CSD model and determine the combined effect.

11303314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303314.value: 儘管皮層擴散性抑制 (CSD)一直是近七十年來大量實驗研究關注的焦點，現在仍有很多CSD背後的機制間互動原理問題仍未解決。現有研究提出CSD傳播涉及各種物理和化學過程，包括離子的電擴散、細胞膜的離子電流、細胞膜內部固定電荷、滲透作用、空間緩衝、神經遞質物質、間隙連接、代謝泵和突觸連接。除了關於CSD的實驗研究外，還有一些數學建模研究，包括CSD連續模型，由離子通過細胞膜上的離子通道時産生的離子流耦合的離子濃度非線性微分方程組成。在以前的這些研究中，通過離子通道的通量模型往往與電擴散不一致，基本是經驗逼近而不能正式證明。此外，以前的模型並未考慮細胞外空間中電擴散離子遷移的影響，把離子遷移當作簡單擴散過程而忽略其固有電擴散的電力。本計劃將介紹如何使用漸進方法來獲得一個可以跨細胞膜和細胞外空間的離子傳輸系統，並與電擴散的Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) 模型一致。我們還將建立一個理論，可一致地處理細胞膜中的固定電荷，以及固定電荷如何影響離子轉運的動力學研究。從數學角度看，跨細胞膜和細胞外空間這兩種類型的離子轉運有很大的不同，需要不同的漸近方法。我們的初步結果表明，一般而言，電擴散不能通過簡單擴散來達到良好近似，CSD傳播在電擴散中的影響可以是非常重要的。

11303314.label: Realisation of objectives
11303314.value: In completing this proposal we faced a number of challenges. This is most acutely seen in the vast difference in scales between the macro-scale, the scale of the Debye layers and the scale over which van der Waals forces operate. This poses a number of distinct numerical challenges. We were able to overcome these challenges by using a numerical method that separately treats the Nernst-Planck component of the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations. We also used an integral formulation to determine the total pairwise interaction between two molecules. These components could then be readily pieced together to generate a highly efficient, accurate and robust numerical method that formed the basis for the majority of the work in this proposal. This numerical method is non-trivial to develop, but once it was in place, it was relatively easy to incorporate the effects of fixed charge. The ion fluxes and other important quantities could also be readily obtained. This also allowed us to readily study the effects of electro-diffusion in determining ion fluxes both near to the boundaries and in the regions far from the boundaries. This mean-field approach to investigating the ion transport and storage pattern was applied to both biological channels and also to the storage of lithium ions between double-layer graphene. In our research, we captured the effects of the nanoscale mechanics so that the forces between ions and the fixed charges embedded in boundaries were incorporated. Even more importantly, we were able to capture steric effects between ions and understand how finite size effects modify ion fluxes and storage patterns. Fluid flow, charge conductivity and thermal effects were all also included. We showed that, under certain electric fields, multi-layers can occur and related storage phenomenon was investigated. This has important potential applications in biological settings and also in lithium ion batteries. The inclusion of fluid effects was also fully implemented into the numerical method. Using some of the numerical techniques that we developed, we were also able to solve a related problem in fluid mechanics. This involved the evolution of complicated non-connected boundaries driven by externally imposed forces.

11303314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303314.value: We investigated the formation of thin ionic layers driven by electro-osmotic forces, that are commonly found in micro- and nano-channels. We used a continuum approach to investigate the flow of ions that experience electrodiffusive transport. The effects of fluid flow, charge conductivity and thermal stability were all carefully investigated. We used this to determine the topology of the ionic layers that occur near boundaries. This work was published in Scientific Reports. We also made use of a continuum approach that used the Poisson equation and mean-field theory to investigate the ion transport and storage. This allowed us to capture the effects of the nanoscale mechanics in determining the bulk ion flux mechanics. Forces between ions and fixed charges and steric effects were also incorporated. We showed that multi-layers could occur and carefully discussed some issues related to storage phenomenon in lithium ion batteries. Our analysis also allowed us to better understand ion fluxes in biological channels. This work was published in Europhysics Letters. Using related techniques, we were also able to solve a fluid mechanics problem in which an arbitrary number of internal holes of arbitrary shape evolve when an external force is applied. The framework is quite general and allowed the inclusion of thermal effects. This work was published in Journal of Fluid Mechanics.

11303314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303314.value: The numerical method that we have developed is quite general and can be used to study how the geometry of the fixed charges affect ion fluxes and layer formation. In particular, a natural study would be to include the effects of curvature of the boundaries. There are also a number of interesting studies that can be undertaken to determine the speed at which discharge can occur and how storage patterns affect the discharge rate. This has a number of important applications. Another important issue involves the general stability of the solutions found in this study. Although this requires some additional ideas, the main concepts nevertheless allow one to readily study these issues.

11303314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303314.value: We have investigated the formation of thin ionic layers driven by electrodiffusive forces that are found in micro- and nano-channels and are important to the ionic flux transport in Cortical Spreading Depression. We used a continuum approach to investigate the flow of ions and the formation of ionic layers. This approach directly modelled the effects of ionic diffusion, osmotic drift, externally applied electrical forces and inter-ion van der Waals forces. Fluid flow, charge conductivity and thermal effects were all also included. We found that the separation and strength of forces between the fixed charges, the external electric field and thermal effects interact in a complicated way to determine the topology of the ionic layers. By understanding how the ion fluxes are established and how ion layering affects the storage of ions near boundaries we were also to understand a number of important phenomena in biological channels and in batteries.

11303414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303414.value: This synthetic project aims for robust covalent solids combining porous structures and highly electroactive metal-thiolate functions (i.e., the metal-dithiolene hybrid motif), in order to fundamentally impact the wide-ranging technologies of sensors, heterogeneous catalysis, and photoelectrochemical cells and batteries. The metal-dithiolene unit is famous for its strength, well-defined geometry, and versatile electroactive properties. However, the integration of this motif into stable porous solids remains a challenge because of the apparent dilemma traditionally believed to be existent between bond strength and crystallinity: namely, the very strong metal-thiolate bonds often form too fast and irreversibly, and the resultant framework solids tend to be ill-ordered and non-porous. Combining the recent advances in the making of porous framework materials and our unique specialty in molecular design/synthesis, we plan to synthesize rigid, multidentate dithiolene building blocks that will bind metal ions in well-defined local geometry, thus enforcing substantial porosity throughout the resultant frameworks: i.e., even in an amorphous or semi-crystalline state, the highly rigid and open framework product will be constraint to yield the desired porous properties. 本項目致力於合成具有多孔结構和高電活性金屬-硫化官能團的共價固體材料(例如金屬-二巰烯雜化結構)，從而根本性地促進傳感器，多相催化和光電化學電池等一系列技術的發展。金屬-二巰烯單元以其強度、規則的幾何構形及多用途的電活性能而為研究者熟知。然而，把這個結構融入到穩定的多孔固體材料中仍然是一項挑戰，因為傳統上認為鍵強和結晶性之間存在着明顯的矛盾，如這種非常強的金屬-硫鍵往往形成得過快而且不可逆轉，以致得到無序和非孔的框架材料。基於我們在製備多孔框架材料的最新進展和在有機分子的設計合成上的特有理念，我們計劃合成剛性，多齒的二巰烯構建單元，固定金屬離子於有序的幾何構形中，從而大大增加所得配合物的多孔性。即使在無定形態或半晶態下，這種高剛性和開放的框架材料仍然能夠產生預期的多孔性。

11303414.label: Realisation of objectives
11303414.value: The realization of objects 1 and 2, regarding the synthesis of aromatic molecular building blocks and the construction of porous frameworks, was highlighted by papers No. 2 and 4 attached. In particular, Paper 2, in the title of “Synthesis of a Thiol Building Block for the Crystallization of a Semiconducting Gyroidal Metal-sulfur Framework”, was published in The Journal of Visualized Experiments (styled JoVE), a peer-reviewed scientific journal that publishes experimental methods in video format. The video format is especially fitting for this project, because the proposed polythiol organic linkers had remained notoriously challenging to synthesize prior to our work. Such experiments can be difficult to replicate as they involve the handling of air sensitive reagents, and the traditional written description of the original scientific methods might not be sufficient. In this JoVE video publication, we disclosed a step-by-step visual guide of the actual experiment so that the detailed manipulations necessary to perform the experiment successfully can be seen. By showcasing our efficient synthetic method for thioesters/thiols and their use for facilitating the crystallization of metal-sulfur networks, we are hopeful that our synthetic objectives, thus fully realized and publicized, will promote further efforts to bridge the intellectual and practical divide between synthetic organic chemistry and solid state chemistry, so as to help the speedy and healthy development of porous frameworks. The realization of objective 3 can also be illustrated in a large and diverse body of research results. For example, electroactive and conductivity property studies were highlighted in paper No 4, in the title of “A semiconducting gyroidal metal-sulfur framework for chemiresistive sensing”. In this important breakthrough, we succeeded in obtaining single crystals a semiconducting gyroidal net (denoted as HTT–Pb) that derives its rich electronic properties fromthe large organic p-electron system of a triphenylene core, highly polarizable Pb-dithiolene links, and robust Pb-oxo connections. In fact, this is the first time a single crystal of open framework metla-dithiolene system was achieved. That is to say, in contrast to the generally encountered difficulty in crystallizing metalthiolate networks, single crystals of HTT–Pb amenable to X-ray studies can be reliably obtained by regular solvothermal synthesis. The electronic conductivity of the framework solid is highly responsive to the water content in air, demonstrating potential use in chemiresistive sensing of humidity. In addition, Paper No. 3 represents a tour de force of materials properties studies of porous conjugated aromatic framework systems. Therein, we report a highly recyclable, 2D aromatic framework that offers a unique and versatile combination of photocatalytic activity and heavy metal uptake capability, as well as other attributes crucial for green and sustainable development technologies. Firstly, the semiconductive nature of the framework, built on fused donor–acceptor aromatic p-systems, enables optical absorption properties for environmentally friendly photoredox catalysis (PRC) utilizing the safe and abundant visible light (and we also implemented this application in a commercial flow reactor). The graphene-like open structure can be assembled from economical building blocks without the need for transition metal catalysts, and proves additionally interesting for environmental remediation applications in its fast and strong binding for Pb(II) ions (e.g., removing aqueous Pb ions below the drinkable limit within minutes). Moreover, the alkaline N-heterocycle units of the robust and porous host are able to quantitatively catalyse Knoevenagel reactions in water. Also discussed in this work is a new metric for benchmarking the kinetic performance of sorbents in the context of heavy metal removal from drinking water.

11303414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303414.value: As stated above, one major discovery from this GRF project lies a fundamental breakthrough in the synthetic strategy for open framework materials. Specifically, Metal-thiolate frameworks are notoriously difficult to crystallize because of the strong, intractable metal-sulfur bonds, as well as the reactive, unstable nature of the thiol building blocks. In stark contrast to the countless metal-carboxylate nets (e.g., MOFs), very few metal-thiolate networks have been crystallized, in spite of keen interests in their electronic properties. The breakthrough therefore is epitomized in the single crystal of dithiolene-metal net of this GRF project. Besides the crystallization of the metal-dithiolene network, the one-pot, transition-metal-free synthesis of thiols and thioesters from aromatic halides and sodium thiomethoxide is of strong practical interest, because of the safer and potentially wide-scope application of this synthetic method. Building on this synthetic breakthrough, we also expand our effort onto installing a powerful donor-acceptor couple within a fully conjugated 2-D porous material, leading to a multifunctional semiconductive network that spawns broad-sweeping capabilities crucial for advancing green technologies. Indeed, the breadth of green credentials is unprecedented: 1) Fastest rate of removing Pb(II) ions from water by framework materials; 2) Harvesting the safe and abundant visible-light for driving organic reactions, and the integration into a commercial flow reactor for recyclable, continuous catalysis; 3) Enabling water as a green medium for organic reactions (e.g., the industrially important Knoevenagel reaction).

11303414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303414.value: With the improvement in linker synthesis and crystallization, we foresee a broad horizon for exploring the unique functionality of similar open frameworks in the context of the technological applications of electroactive and photoactive porous semiconductive materials. Specifically, wider-ranging applications regarding catalysis, sensing and charge/energy storage properties can be envisioned, especially with more robust systems based on softer metal ions such as the Pd(II)-based systems should offer the crucial advantages in stability and functionality. Indeed, the improvement in linker synthesis and crystallization have led to the accomplishment of the proposed objects in an unexpectedly efficient manner. In other words, the well-defined crystalline porous network can serve as starting materials for post-synthetic modification, e.g., by alkylating the sulfur atoms, in order to dial in further chemical functions and to fine tune the electroactive, photoactive and conductive properties.

11303414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303414.value: This synthetic project constructs robust covalent solids combining porous structures and highly electroactive metal-thiolate functions (i.e., the metal-dithiolene hybrid motif), in order to fundamentally impact the wide-ranging technologies of sensors, heterogeneous catalysis, and photoelectrochemical cells and batteries. The metal-dithiolene unit is famous for its strength, well-defined geometry, and versatile electroactive properties. However, the integration of this motif into stable porous solids has remained a challenge, because of the apparent dilemma traditionally believed to be existent between bond strength and crystallinity: namely, the very strong metal-thiolate bonds often form too fast and irreversibly, and the resultant framework solids tend to be ill-ordered and non-porous. Combining the recent advances in the making of porous framework materials and our unique specialty in molecular design/synthesis, we have synthesized rigid, multidentate dithiolene building blocks and analogs that bind metal ions in well-defined local geometry, thus enforcing substantial porosity throughout the resultant frameworks for yielding the desired porous properties.

11303614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303614.value: 在十九世紀九十年代或以前的一些研究人員的工作的基礎上，近年來關於不帶角截斷假設的波爾茲曼方程數學理論的研究取得了許多進展。是否帶角截斷假設的波爾茲曼方程之間的一個主要差別在於由於角奇性而導致的對解的正則性的影響。到目前為止這種正則性效應已得到公認並在波爾茲曼方程的解具有一定的初始正則性，例如某些加權的Sobolev空間中，的框架中得到了廣泛的研究。另一方面，由於波爾茲曼方程描述的是粒子分佈函數隨時間的演化，一個自然的函數空間是帶有一些矩限制（例如動量、能量等）的概率測度。 對空間齊次的Maxwell分子模型的波爾茲曼方程，Tanaka在1978年首先利用概率論研究了這類解的存在性和大時間性態，隨後Toscani-Villani和Pulvirenti-Toscani利用Wasserstein度量給出了Tanaka結果的一個偏微分方程證明。還有最近Cannone-Karch和Morimoto在Cercignani-Toscani所構造的自相似解基礎上的關於無限能量解的工作。在這些工作中即使對初始值的正則性要求很低，在我們和Morimoto的最近合作的工作中我們證明了只要初值不是單個Dirac 函數，只要時間大於零，這些解就會變得無窮光滑。這正是Villani關於這一問題的一個猜想。這些研究工作導致了本研究項目中所擬定的研究目標：進一步發展這一有趣現象的數學理論。值得指出的是，Lu-Mouhot最近對硬勢情形研究了測度值解的存在性，但是相應的正則性分析還是未知的。 在本項目中，我們擬研究如下問題：由於對測度值解的Villani猜想僅僅在空間齊次的情形下對Maxwell分子模型得到了證實，而這一證明強烈的依賴於Bobylev公式，首先一個自然的問題是對具有一般的碰撞核，例如硬勢和軟勢，的空間齊次的情形，相應的結論是否成立？在這些情況下，由於碰撞算子的複雜結構，關於Villani猜想到目前為止還沒有任何進展。第二個問題是關於解的大時間性態分析。即使有多位研究人員研究了整體解收斂到Maxwell分佈或自相似解的情形，但是，正如我們下面將要提及的， 有許多事情需要進一步研究。事實上，這種由於解在任何正的時間裡是無窮次可微的，這種收斂應該也是在某種意義下是“強的”。如果能得到在某種“強”意義下收斂到Maxwell分佈的結果，我們就能進一步研究空間非其次波爾茲曼方程的適定性理論。最後我們擬研究空間非齊次波爾茲曼方程相應的正則性效應。

11303614.label: Realisation of objectives
11303614.value: The objectives of this project have been fully addressed. The research results have been written into five research papers, among them, three have been published in international refereed journals. The other two papers will be submitted soon. Some details of the research are presented as follows. First of all, the Boltzmann equation is a fundamental equation in statistical physics that describes the time evolution of the distribution function of particles of a dilute gas. Besides its physical background and applications in engineering, biology and even in social science, it provides a lot of challenging mathematical problems that form the foundation of kinetic theory. For the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation, under the angular cutoff assumption, the first existence result was given in the seminal paper by Carleman in 1933, and was developed by Arkeryd in 1970s, and then more recently by Mischler-Wennberg and many others. Without the angular cutoff assumption, there is an important work by Villani on the weighted L1 weak solutions. For the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation, there have been extensive studies under the Grad's angular cutoff assumption. On the other hand, there are also a lot of important results on the non-angular cutoff Boltzmann equation, such as Alexandre-Villani’s work on the renormalized solution; and the recent progress made by two research groups, Gressman-Strain and Alexandre-Morimoto-Ukai-Xu-Yang on the well-posedness theories in Sobolev spaces for perturbative solutions around a global Maxwellian. The purpose of this project is to explore a rigorous proof of the Villani conjecture on the regularizing effect for the Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff. Precisely, Villani conjecture says that the solution become arbitrarily smooth in any positive time as long as the initial datum is not a single Dirac mass, in particular, in the spatially homogeneous setting. This conjecture is proved for the Maxwellian molecule cross-section for the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation where the cross section is only a function of interaction angle in our previous work. How to show that it also holds for the hard and soft potentials, and also the spatially inhomogeneous problem in different setting is difficult because of the lack of precise estimations on the coercivity of the collision operator for the measure valued solution, and the interaction of the collision and the convection operators. To achieve the objectives in the project, by precisely classify the Fourier transform of the measure valued functions with moment bounds, we introduce a uniform approach to study the existence and regularity theories on the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with measure valued initial data. In addition, for the spatially inhomogeneous problem, the well-posedness and regularity have been studied for the algebraic decayed initial data. Some detail of the research results is given as follows. In the first paper, we introduce a precise classification of characteristic functions in the Fourier space according to the moment constraint in the physical space of any order. Based on this, we construct measure valued solutions to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with the exact moment condition as the initial data. In the second paper, we characterize the class of probability measures possessing finite moments of an arbitrary positive order in terms of the symmetric difference operators of their Fourier transforms. As an application, we prove the continuity of probability densities associated with measure-valued solutions to the Cauchy problem for the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with Maxwellian molecules. Then a uniform approach is introduced in the third paper to study the existence of measure valued solutions to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation for both the hard potential with finite energy, and the soft potential with finite or infinite energy, by using Toscani metric. Under the non-angular cutoff assumption on the cross-section, the solutions obtained are shown to be in the Schwartz space in the velocity variable as long as the initial data is not a single Dirac mass without any extra moment condition for the hard potential, and with the boundedness on moments of any order for the soft potential. In the fourth paper, we consider the measure valued solution to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with two models of Debye-Yukawa type. For the first one that is related to the true Debye-Yukawa potential, we obtain the existence of the solution and obtain some important properties of the solution. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first rigorous mathematical discussion on such collision kernel. For the second one which is a Maxwellian molecule type of Deybe-Yukawa potential, we introduce a new coercivity estimate and proved the solution becomes smooth for any positive time as long as the initial data is not a Dirac mass. In the last paper, the Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff is considered when the initial data is a perturbation of a global Maxwellian with algebraic decay in the velocity variable. Global solution is proved by combining the analysis in moment propagation, spectrum of the linearized operator and the smoothing effect of the linearized operator when initial data in Sobolev space with negative index. In addition, the non-negativity and uniqueness of the solution are also considered. In summary, we develop some new analytic techniques in justifying Villani conjecture on the regularity of solutions to the Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff. The results cover both the hard and soft potentials with algebraic order of angular singularity, the Debye-Yukawa potential with logarithm order of angular singularity. We believe that the results enrich the mathematical theories on this topic and also have applications to other mathematical problems.

11303614.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303614.value: By precisely classify the Fourier transform of measure valued functions with moments, we introduce a uniform approach to study the mathematical theory on the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with measure valued initial data. Furthermore, for the spatially inhomogeneous problem, well-posedness and regularity are also studied for the algebraic decayed initial data. Precisely, we introduce a precise classification of characteristic functions in the Fourier space according to the moment constraint in the physical space of any order. Based on this, we construct measure valued solutions to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with the exact moment condition as the initial data. Furthermore, we characterize the class of probability measures possessing finite moments of an arbitrary positive order in terms of the symmetric difference operators of their Fourier transforms. As an application, we prove the continuity of probability densities associated with measure-valued solutions to the Cauchy problem for the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with Maxwellian molecules. Then a uniform approach is introduced to study the existence of measure valued solutions to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation for both the hard potential with finite energy, and the soft potential with finite or infinite energy, by using the Toscani metric. Under the non-angular cutoff assumption on the cross-section, the solutions obtained are shown to be in the Schwartz space in the velocity variable as long as the initial data is not a single Dirac mass without any extra moment condition for the hard potential, and with the boundedness on moments of any order for the soft potential. In addition, we consider the measure valued solution to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation with two models of Debye-Yukawa type. For the first one that is related to the true Debye-Yukawa potential, we obtain the existence of the solution and some important properties of the solution, and it firstly gives a rigorously mathematical theory on this physical model. For the second one which is the Maxwellian molecule type Deybe-Yukawa potential, we introduce a new coercivity estimate and proved the solution becomes smooth for any positive time as long as the initial data is not a Dirac mass. Finally, spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff is considered when the initial data is a perturbation of a global Maxwellian with algebraic decay in the velocity variable. Global existence is proved by studying moment propagation, spectrum of the linearized operator and the smoothing effect of the linearized operator in Sobolev space with negative index.

11303614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303614.value: Firstly, the newly classification of the characteristic functions for the probability measures possessing finite moments of an arbitrary positive order in terms of the symmetric difference operators of their Fourier transforms is of interest in its own. One application is given to the study on the Boltzmann equation with measure valued initial data in this project, and we believe that it can be useful in other research topics. Secondly, even though a satisfactory mathematical theory on the Boltzmann equation with measure valued data has been established for existence and regularity, the uniqueness basically has only been proved so far for the Maxwellian molecules without any extra conditions. How to prove uniqueness under suitably physical condition remains a challenging problem for other cross-sections. In addition, the large time behavior of solutions with initial data of infinite energy has only to be shown for the Maxwellian molecules. The justification of the convergence to the self-similar solutions obtained by Bobylev for the soft potential is feasible, but how to investigate the property of the immediate gain of moment for the hard potential on large time behavior remains unknown. Therefore, there are many potential problems to be considered in this direction.

11303614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303614.value: Boltzmann equation is about the time evolution of particle distribution function of dilute gases, one natural function space is the space of probability measure with some moment constraint that corresponds to, for example, the momentum and energy. For the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation with the Maxwellian molecule type cross section, the existence and large time behavior of this kind of solution were studied in the early work by Tanada in 1978 using probability theory, and then Toscani-Villani, Pulvirenti-Toscani using Wasserstein metrics, the works on solutions with infinite energy by Cannone-Karch and Morimoto motivated by the self-similar solutions constructed by Cercignani-Toscani. Furthermore, it was shown in my recent work with Morimoto that these solutions become arbitrarily smooth in any positive time as long as the initial datum is not a single Dirac mass which is exactly the Villani conjecture in this setting. These works lead to the study on the problems proposed in this project that aim to develop the mathematical theories on this phenomenon, that is, to justify the Villani conjecture for the general cross sections, for example, the hard and soft potentials and the Debye-Yukawa potential, and the corresponding regularizing effect problems for the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation.

11303714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303714.value: Interfacial fluid mixing is a common phenomenon that occurs frequently in basic science research and in engineering applications. Very often, the involved interface is unstable and small disturbances at the interface grow and form nonlinear structures, such as fingers and chaotic mixing layers. It is important to understand the growth of such nonlinear structures. However, many physical parameters can affect the dynamics of these nonlinear structures. One needs to perform large numbers of simulations or experiments to explore the effects of any physical parameter, which can be very time-consuming and financially expensive. Therefore, it is extremely desirable and important to study the universal behavior in the dynamics of these nonlinear structures. The property of universality allows us to determine the dominant behavior for a whole class of unstable interfacial mixing problems from a single numerical simulation or a single experiment. However, due to the complicated dynamics and nonlinear nature of the phenomena, even performing numerical simulations and experiments for a given parameter set represents a significant challenge. Therefore, to a large extent, the universal behavior in unstable interfacial mixing has not been examined. In this proposal, we will study universality in the behavior of nonlinear structures at unstable interfaces. We will focus on a well-known class of unstable interfacial mixing problems: the nonlinear structures in a shock-driven interfacial instability. This unstable system is challenging to study due to several complications, including fluid compressibility and the presence of shock and rarefaction waves. For this reason, the issue of universality in the dynamics of a shock-driven interfacial instability has not been analyzed. We will conduct such a study in this project. 流體界面的混合現象普遍存在於基礎科學研究中，同時具有廣泛的工程應用。然而，在許多情況下，所涉及的界面是不穩定的。界面處的微小擾動將隨時間不斷增長而形成非線性結構。因此，瞭解這些非線性結構的動力學機制是非常重要的。然而，許多物理參數可以影響這些非線性結構的動力學行爲。要瞭解這些參數的影響，需要進行大量的數值模擬或實驗。這不僅非常費時，而且在經濟上是昂貴的。因此，對這些非線性結構的動力學行爲中的共性的研究顯得格外重要和迫切。這種共性讓我們能夠從一個數值模擬或一個實驗中得到的結果來確定一類非穩定界面混合問題的行爲。然而，由於非線性動力系統的複雜性，即使對給定體系的數值模擬和實驗都具有極大的挑戰性，更不用說對一般體系的共性的研究 。因此，在相當程度上，人們對非穩定的混合界面的動力學行為的共性瞭解得極少。在本計劃中，我們將研究非穩定界面上的非線性結構的動力學行為的共性。我們將專注於一類經典的非穩定界面的混合問題：由激波產生的非穩定界面上的非線性結構。對這類非穩定系統的研究極具挑戰性，其中包括流體的可壓縮性以及激波和稀疏波的複雜性。由於這些原因，人們缺乏對由激波驅動的非穩定界面的非線性結構的共性的研究。在本項目中，我們將進行這樣的研究。

11303714.label: Realisation of objectives
11303714.value: The goal of this project is to study the dynamics of unstable interfacial mixing driven by shock waves, known as the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability (RMI) in the literature. Since the pioneering works of Richtmyer, the study of this classical problem has been carried out for more than half a century among mathematicians, physicists and engineers. Due to the unstable nature of this system, when an incident shock hits a material interface between two fluids of different densities, the interface becomes unstable. Small disturbances at the material interface grow in size to form nonlinear structures. The fluid in one phase penetrates into the fluid in the other phase. The portion of the light fluid penetrating into the heavy fluid is called bubbles, and the portion of the heavy fluid penetrating into the light fluid is called spikes. The growth rates of the fingers, namely how fast the amplitude of the spikes and that of the bubbles grow with time, represent the dominant features of the interfacial mixing at the Richtmyer-Meshkov unstable interface. For decades, researchers have been searching for an accurate theoretical formula to predict the growth rates and amplitudes of the fingers in the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability in compressible fluids and over the entire time domain from early to late times. The difficulties in deriving theoretical formulas lie in the fact that the system is both compressible and nonlinear. In this project, we have successfully achieved our goal of developing accurate quantitative theories for compressible fluids and over the entire time domain. We have established a surprising universality property for the dominant behavior for the fingers in systems with different physical parameters and for fingers of different types (spikes and bubbles) in two dimensions. To construct our analytical formulas for the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability in compressible fluids over the entire time domain, we identify the dominant behavior in complicated dynamics of the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability in different time domain. Compressibility and nonlinearity are two major obstacles to developing an accurate quantitative theory for the compressible RMI. Our theoretical study is based on the following physical understanding. By definition, compressibility measures the changes in density resulting from changes in pressure. For the RMI, the large changes in pressure occur in the vicinity of shocks. At early times, the incident shock, the transmitted shock and the reflected wave interact with the material interface and the compressibility effects are important. Thus, for an RM interface with a small initial perturbation, the dynamics is governed by the compressible linear theory. However, after the transmitted shock and the reflected wave have propagated away from the material interface, there are no large changes in pressure in the vicinity of fingers. Thus, the compressibility effects become less important. This is because, although the fluids are compressible, the system does not provide an environment to reveal the compressibility. The compressibility effects are progressively decreasing with time and the nonlinearity effects are progressively increasing. Thus, the system gradually changes from a linear and compressible stage at early times to a nonlinear and incompressible stage at late times. With this understanding, our theoretical approach consists of two steps: (1) Since the dynamics at late times is different from that at early times, we treat the former separately from the latter and develop an approximate solution for the nonlinear incompressible system; (2) By applying an asymptotic matching technique, we match the compressible linear theory at early times and the incompressible nonlinear theory at late times to obtain an approximate solution for the compressible system with any density ratio and over all time. It is an extremely difficult task to derive the behavior of fingers in the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at asymptotically large times. We have carried out this difficult task in this project. We analyzed the curvature at the tip of the fingers for systems with a very large density ratio. We showed that, instead of using regular expansions based on Taylor series, one must use singular expansions based on Laurent series. The singular expansion allows us to determine the curvatures of the fingers, and consequently the growth rates and the amplitudes of the fingers, for systems with arbitrary density ratio and for both finger types (spikes and bubbles). From the asymptotic solution obtained, we discover a surprising universality phenomenon among fingers of different density ratios and of different types in two dimensions. The property of universality allows us to determine the dominant behavior of fingers for a whole class of shock-driven unstable interfacial mixing problems from a single numerical simulation or a single experiment. We applied a two-point Pade approximant method to the small time and large time solutions to construct theoretical formulas for the growth rates and amplitudes of fingers in incompressible systems from early to late times. To our knowledge, this is the first time that the method of two-point Pade approximant is applied to a problem in fluid dynamics. Finally, we applied the method of Prandtl asymptotic matching to the solutions of the linear compressible theory and the results for the incompressible nonlinear theory derived from the asymptotic analysis and the two-point Pade approximant to obtain explicit formulas for the growth rates and the amplitudes of fingers in compressible systems with arbitrary density ratios and over the entire time domain. The theoretical predictions are in surprisingly good agreement with experimental results and numerical data. We have successfully reached all goals set in this project.

11303714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303714.value: We discovered a surprising universality phenomenon for a class of systems in RMI and developed explicit formulas that provide accurate theoretical predictions for the growth rates and amplitudes of fingers. This represents an important advance in the studies of RMI. It is well known that the growth rates of fingers depend on physical parameters such as the density ratio of the two fluids, the material properties of the fluids, the incident-shock strength. Furthermore, the growth rates of spikes are different from the growth rates of bubbles. Therefore, for each set of physical parameters, one has to conduct a separate experiment or numerical simulation. In this project, we have established a surprising scaling relation between systems with different physical parameters and even between fingers of different types, namely between spikes and bubbles. This means that the dominant behavior of all fingers with any physical parameters and of any finger type satisfies a universality property. Universality is an intrinsic property of a physical system. It represents the invariance of certain appropriately-scaled physical quantities when the physical parameter changes. Therefore, once one discovers the universality property for a class of physical systems, one only needs to perform one numerical simulation or one experiment with given physical parameter values to determine the behavior of the whole class. The results for any other value of the physical parameters can be obtained by scaling the results from the system which has been studied. Therefore, the universality relation that we have discovered in this project is very important for the studies of RMI. We have shown that the numerical results from simulations for systems with different density ratios and for spikes and bubbles all coincide very well with our theoretically predicted universal curve. This surprising result is published in JFM (attached). We have developed a quantitative theory for the growth rates and amplitudes of fingers in the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability. The theory is valid: (1) for compressible fluids, (2) for systems with arbitrary density ratio between two fluids, (3) over the entire time domain from early to late times, and (4) for both cases of reflected shocks and reflected rarefaction waves. The theory contains no fitting parameters. Our theoretical predictions are in remarkably good agreement with results from numerical simulations and data from experiments. Therefore, we have developed theoretical formulas that the researchers have been searching for. These important results are published in PRL (attached).

11303714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303714.value: In this proposal, we have studied the shock-induced interfacial instability. We have developed accurate theoretical formulas and discovered an important universality phenomenon. The systems that we have studied are in two-dimensional planar geometry. In nature phenomenon, the shock-induced interfacial instability also occurs in three dimensions. Conducting numerical simulations in three dimensions for shock-induced interfacial instability is extremely time-consuming. Furthermore, the design and implementation of numerical methods for conducting numerical simulations of shock-induced interfacial instability in three dimensions are very challenging tasks. Therefore, it is extremely desirable to explore the possibility of scaling behavior between fingers in three-dimensional systems and those in two-dimensional systems. If one can establish such a scaling relation, it will provide an extremely helpful tool to understand shock-induced interfacial instability in three dimensions. In addition, experimental studies of shock-induced interfacial instability are often carried out in cylindrical tubes. Shock-induced interfacial instability in cylindrical tubes are dramatically more complicated than that in two-dimensional planar geometry. It contains perturbations in the radial dimension and perturbations in the angular dimension. Conducting theoretical studies and exploring the possible scaling laws in the complicated setting of cylindrical tubes are also very important, although extremely challenging.

11303714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303714.value: The shock-induced interfacial instability is a classical problem in mathematics, physics and engineering. How to predict the dynamic behavior of unstable nonlinear structures at the unstable interface is one of the key issues in the studies of this instability. Unfortunately, due to the complicated nature of the dynamics in this difficult problem, no quantitative theories have been found. In this project, we have, for the first time, derived theoretical formulas to provide accurate prediction for the dynamic behavior of nonlinear structures at the unstable material interface from early to late times. The theoretical predictions are in excellent agreement with results from experiments and data from numerical simulations. Furthermore, we have shown a surprising universality phenomenon: By properly presenting physical quantities in terms of scaled dimensionless variables, all unstable nonlinear structures in systems with different physical parameters have the same universal dominant behavior. This means that a single curve represents the dominant behavior for all systems even though these systems have very different physical parameters. This universality property represents a very important advance in the studies of unstable interfacial mixing problems.

11303914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303914.value: Most problems that we encounter in nature share the common feature of possessing multiple scales. In order to modeling and approximate these problems with limited computational resources, effective multiscale modeling and numerical methods are essential. Multiscale finite element method (MsFEM) and finite element heterogeneous multiscale method (FE-HMM) are two examples of successful numerical methods based on the homogenization theory for multiscale problems. They have been applied to many multiscale problems successfully. For many practical problems, it is still a very challenging task to modify these algorithms or design new algorithms to solve the multiscale problems accurately and effectively. For example, in classical MsFEM and FE-HMM, oversampling methods are often used to reduce the resonance effect. This will heavily increase the computational cost. Also, problems other than well-studied model problems need careful analysis and problem specific numerical multiscale methods. The long-term goal of the P.I. is to develop and study, theoretically as well as computationally, accurate and efficient numerical methods for solving problems with multiscale features. In this proposal, the P.I. will concentrate on applications of ideas of adaptive finite element methods in numerical multiscale methods including MsFEM and FE-HMM. With accurate a posteriori error estimators and carefully designed adaptive algorithms, adaptive finite element methods solve the partial differential equations with a problem-adapted mesh, thus can achieve optimal computational complexity.This feature makes adaptive algorithms ideal for numerical methods for multiscale problems. In this proposed research, the P.I. will develop all-levele adaptive numerical multiscale methods. The adaptivity will be performed on every level of the computation, including local computations of oscillating functions, deciding the size of oversampling domain, and global contributions due to geometric singularities. The P.I. will also extend the methods to other interesting problems other than standard model elliptic equations. The proposed research will also develop new methods to combine best features of adaptive methods and numerical multiscale methods by applying the former on non-scale-separated regions and the latter on scale-separated regions. The P.I. is interested in studying practical and effective algorithms and mathematical foundations for applications of adaptive methods in numerical musicale methods. The methodology developed in the project will shed light on how to design adaptive algorithms on the every levels of numerical multiscale methods. The results of the pro- posed research will provide powerful computational tools for industrial and engineering multiscale computation, and has wide applications in areas of complex physics, biology, and chemistry. 自然界中的很多問題具有多重尺度, 為了在有限的計算資源下模擬和逼近這些問題, 我們有必要提出有效的多尺度建模和數值方法. 多尺度有限元方法和有限元異質多尺度方法是兩個基於多尺度方法均質化理論的成功數值方法. 他們已經成功應用於很多問題. 對很多實際問題, 修改這些方法或者設計新的算法來精確和高效的求解多尺度問題還是一個非常困難的問題. 例如, 在經典的多尺度有限元方法和有限元異質多尺度方法中, 擴大取樣方法經常被用來減少共振效應. 這回大大增加計算量, 並且, 除了那些已經仔細研究過了問題之外, 其他問題也需要仔細的問題和基於問題的數值多尺度方法. 本研究計劃主持人的長期目標是在理論上和計算上發展和研究精確和高效的多尺度問題求解方法. 在這個研究計劃中, 將會集中將自適應有限元的想法應用於包括多尺度有限元方法和有限元異質多尺度方法在內的數值多尺度方法. 基於精確的后驗估計和仔細設計的自適應算法, 自適應有限元方法可以對偏微分方程在一個和問題適應的網格上求解, 從而獲得最優的計算複雜度. 這個特點使得自適應伏算法對於多尺度問題的數值方法是理想的. 在這個計劃的研究中, 我們會提出全層次的自適應數值多尺度方法. 在每個層次的計算上, 包括震動函數的計算, 擴大取樣區域的大小, 和因為幾何奇異性導致的整體效應, 自適應方法都會應用到. 我們也會把這些方法擴展到除了標準的橢圓問題之外的另外的感興趣的問題, 本研究計劃也會設計一個把自適應方法和數值多尺度方法結合起來的方法, 使得在沒有尺度分離的區域使用自適應方法和在尺度分離的區域使用數值多尺度方法. 我們關心自適應算法在數值多尺度方法中得實用和有效的算法和數學基礎. 本研究計劃中的提出的方法會對怎樣在數值多尺度方法的每個層次上設計自適應方法提供新想法. 本研究計劃的結果會對工業和工程上的多尺度計算提供有力的工具, 也會在複雜物理, 生物, 和化學中的各領域有廣泛應用.

11303914.label: Realisation of objectives
11303914.value: In this project, we first propose reduced basis multiscale finite element methods (RB- MsFEMs) for elliptic problems with highly oscillating coefficients. The method is based on MsFEMs with local test functions that encode the oscillatory behavior. For uniform rectangular meshes, the local oscillating test functions are represented by a reduced basis method (RBM), parameterizing the center of the elements. For triangular elements, we introduce a slightly different approach. By exploring oversampling of the oscillating test functions, initially introduced to recover a better approximation of the global harmonic coordinate map, we first build the reduced basis on uniform rectangular elements containing the original triangular elements and then restrict the oscillating test function to the triangular elements. These techniques are also generalized to the case where the coefficients dependent on additional independent parameters. The analysis of the proposed methods is supported by various numerical results, obtained on regular and unstructured grids. To study the adaptive methods, the first-order system LL* (FOSLL*) approach for general second-order elliptic partial differential equations was proposed and analyzed in [Z. Cai et al., SIAM J. Numer. Anal., 39 (2001), pp. 1418–1445], in order to retain the full efficiency of the L2 norm first-order system least- squares (FOSLS) approach while exhibiting the generality of the inverse-norm FOSLS approach. The FOSLL* approach of Cai et al. was applied to the div-curl system with added slack variables, and hence it is quite complicated. In this paper, we apply the FOSLL* approach to the div system and establish its well-posedness. For the corresponding finite element approximation, we obtain a quasi-optimal a priori error bound under the same regularity assumption as the standard Galerkin method, but without the restriction to sufficiently small mesh size. Unlike the FOSLS approach, the FOSLL* approach does not have a free a posteriori error estimator. We then propose an explicit residual error estimator and establish its reliability and efficiency bounds. We also propose two different improvements of reduced basis(RB) methods to enable the efficient and accurate evaluation of an output functional based on the numerical solution of parametrized partial differential equations with a possibly high-dimensional parameter space. The element that combines these two techniques is that they both utilize analysis of variance (ANOVA) expansions to enable the improvements. The first method is a three-step RB–ANOVA–RB method, which aims to use a combination of RB methods and ANOVA expansions to effectively compress the parameter space with minimal impact on the accuracy of the output of interest under the assumption that only a selection of parameters are very important for the problem. This is achieved by first building a low-accuracy reduced model for the full high-dimensional parametric problem. This is used to recover an approximate ANOVA expansion for the output functional at marginal cost, allowing the estimation of the sensitivity of the output functional to parameter variation and enabling a subsequent compression of the parameter space. A new accurate reduced model can then be constructed for the compressed parametric problem at a substantially reduced computational cost as for the full problem. In the second approach we explore the ANOVA expansion to drive an hp RB method. This is initiated considering a RB as accurate as can be afforded during the online stage. If the offline greedy procedure for a given parameter domain converges with equal or less than the maximum basis functions, the offline algorithm stops. Otherwise, an approximate ANOVA expansion is performed for the output functional. The parameter domain is decomposed into several subdomains where the most important parameters according to the ANOVA expansion are split. The offline greedy algorithms are performed in these parameter subdomains. The algorithm is applied recursively until the offline greedy algorithm converges across all parameter subdomains. We also we study a modified residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the nonconforming linear finite element approximation to the interface problem. The reliability of the estimator is analyzed by a new and direct approach without using the Helmholtz decomposition. It is proved that the estimator is reliable with constant independent of the jump of diffusion coefficients across the interfaces, without the assumption that the diffusion coefficient is quasi-monotone. We extend the results of Cai and Zhang (2009) to diffusion problems with full diffusion tensor and to the flux recovery both in piecewise constant and piecewise linear H (div) space. Also For elliptic interface problems in two and three dimensions, this paper studies a priori and residual-based a posteriori error estimations for the Crouzeix–Raviart nonconforming and the discontinuous Galerkin finite element approximations. It is shown that both the a priori and the a posteriori error estimates are robust with respect to the diffusion coefficient, i.e., constants in the error bounds are independent of the jump of the diffusion coefficient. The a priori estimates are also optimal with respect to local regularity of the solution. Moreover, we obtained these estimates with no assumption on the distribution of the diffusion coefficient. We also developed and analyzed balanced, efficient, and accurate all-level adaptive Ms- FEM and FE-HMM and developed relevant computer codes of all-level adaptive MsFEM and FE-HMM for various problems.

11303914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303914.value: In this project, we first developed an RB-MSFEM method. In the method, we combined the adaptive methods and the reduced basis methods and the multiscale method. Then we developed a series of theoretical analysis of the robust a posteriori analysis for the adaptive methods, specially, we resolved an open problem in the a posteriori error estimator for diffusion problems with discontinuous coefficients. The famous quasi-monotonicity condition is removed for the first time in the analysis since the condition appeared in such analysis in 1980s. An explicit version of robust ZZ error estimators is developed. A unified analysis combined the MsFEM and HMM method and adaptivity is developed. We also developed ANOVA based RBM. The method uses adaptivity techniques based on ANOVA, and can be applied to complicated physical problems with multiscale features.

11304114.label: Project Objectives
11304114.value: Approximation theory of incremental kernel PCA and related algorithms. Approximation analysis for the classical incremental PCA with satisfactory learning rates will be completed by removing a special assumption imposed in the classical literature for almost sure convergence. For an online classification algorithm associated with a Mercer kernel and a convex loss function, we shall obtain confidence-based error bounds to prove the almost sure convergence. Approximation theory of some kernel-based regularization schemes for learning. We shall first establish approximation theory for SVM type regularization schemes with additive kernels in additive models. Learning rates will be derived by methods from approximation theory, and an interesting approximation theory question concerning Gaussian kernels arising from this study will be considered. Coefficient-based regularization schemes in minimum error entropy principle will be investigated by error decomposition and the scaling operator. Robustness of such regularization schemes will be studied by influence functions. Error analysis for early stopping methods in the classification setting will be done. Some bioinformatics problems such as the one on reassortment of segmented viruses will be discussed by methods and ideas from learning theory and approximation theory.

11304114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304114.value: Learning theory provides mathematical foundations of machine learning which studies efficient learning algorithms for analyzing and processing large data in science and technology. Methods and ideas from approximation theory play an important role in learning theory. The goal of this project is approximation theory of incremental principal component analysis and some kernel-based regularization schemes for learning. We shall first carry out error analysis and derive learning rates for the classical incremental principal component analysis. We shall then get confidence-based error bounds for online classification algorithms associated with convex loss functions and prove the almost sure convergence. Approximation analysis for SVM type regularization schemes with additive kernels in additive models will be conducted by means of approximation by integral operators. An interesting approximation theory question concerning Gaussian kernels arising from this study will also be considered. Coefficient-based schemes and robustness of minimum error entropy regularization will be investigated by the scaling operator in wavelet analysis and by the concepts of influence functions. Finally some data analysis problems from bioinformatics will be considered by ideas from learning theory and approximation theory. 機器學習研究用於分析和處理科學技術大數據的學習算法,學習理論為其提供數學基礎.逼近論的方法和想法在學習理論中起著重要作用.本項目旨在研究在線主成分分析和一些基於核的正則化學習算法的逼近理論.首先我們將對經典的在線主成分分析進行誤差分析並得到學習率.然後我們將給由凸損失函數導出的在線分類算法提供置信度誤差界,並證明幾乎必然收斂性.利用積分算子逼近,我們將對在可加模型中可加核產生的支持向量機型的正則化算法作逼近分析.在此研究中產生的一個關於高斯核的逼近問題將予以考慮.我們將利用小波分析中的尺度算子和影響函數概念來研究最小誤差熵的係數正則化和魯棒性.最後,對一些生物信息學中的數據分析問題將用學習理論和逼近論想法進行研究.

11304114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304114.value: We have studied approximation analysis of some kernel-based online or off-line learning algorithms. In [1] learning with least squares regularization in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces by a divide-and-conquer approach is considered where error bounds in expectation are derived. Our error bounds are sharp and stated in a general setting without any eigenfunction assumption. The analysis is achieved by a novel second order decomposition of operator differences in our integral operator approach. In [2] we propose an online learning algorithm, a general randomized sparse Kaczmarz method, for generating sparse approximations. This algorithm in a general form may cover some other online or incremental methods such as randomized sparse Kaczmarz and incremental PCA. We present an approximation theory of this learning algorithm and study its convergence. Under a mild assumption covering the case of noisy random measurements in the sampling process or nonlinear regression function, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the convergence in expectation by means of the step size sequence. Convergence rates and a sufficient condition for almost sure convergence are also obtained. In [3] we introduce a semi-supervised learning algorithm, distributed semi-supervised learning with kernel ridge regression (DSKRR), based on a divide-and-conquer strategy. Using a novel error decomposition which divides the generalization error of DSKRR into the approximation error, sample error and distributed error, we provides error analysis for DSKRR and find that the sample error and distributed error reflect the power and limitation of DSKRR, compared with kernel ridge regression. Our results show that unlabeled data play important roles in reducing the distributed error and enlarging the number of data subsets in DSKRR. In [4] we study the approximation of functions by linear integral operators on variable exponent spaces. Under a log-Holder continuity assumption of the exponent function, we present quantitative estimates for the approximation and solve an open problem. As applications of our key estimates, we provide high orders of approximation by some linear operators on variable exponent spaces, and consider connections of this approximation theory to some applications to kernel methods in learning theory. In [5] we consider robustness of SVM type kernel-based regularization schemes and give conditions under which such schemes based on a convex Lipschitz loss function and on a bounded and smooth kernel are stable. Robustness results are also given for pairwise learning. The topic studied in this paper is more general than that in the classical robust statistics.

11304114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304114.value: Research problems studied and ideas developed in this project lead to some related questions on distributed learning and online learning with pairwise loss functions. We shall consider these questions in our further study.

11304114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304114.value: Learning theory provides mathematical foundations of machine learning which studies efficient learning algorithms for analyzing and processing large data in science and technology. Methods and ideas from approximation theory play an important role in learning theory. This project provides approximation analysis of some kernel-based online or off-line learning algorithms. We propose a general randomized sparse Kaczmarz method for generating sparse approximations and study its convergence and connections to incremental principal component analysis. Regularization schemes in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces in distributed learning for dealing with big data by a divide-and- conquer approach are studied when least squares regularization and semi-supervised learning with kernel ridge regression are used. Robustness of kernel-based regularization schemes is considered and conditions for total stability are presented. Some related problems on approximation from variable exponent spaces and connections to kernel methods in learning theory are also investigated.

11304314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304314.value: 能量面的过渡态的研究：数值分析和算法发展

11304314.label: Project Objectives
11304314.value: Analysis work. We address the convergence property of a dynamical system for saddle point search. We then mainly focus on a new formulation of iterative minimization scheme by establishing its quadratic convergence rate. Algorithmic development. We shall investigate a key issue of developing efficient solvers for our proposed iterative minimization scheme. We test the performance on benchmark problems. Solving issues related to applications. We study the extension of our work to the free energy surface which has its own special features as well as how to leave a local minimum at initial stage.

11304314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304314.value: 许多重要的物理或化学事件，如相变，蛋白质折叠或大分子构象变化，是在非常高维的势能面的亚稳态（局部最小值）之间跃迁的典型例子。在低温条件下，这些跃迁很少发生，但一旦发生，就通过穿越相关过渡态的方法跨越势垒障碍。这些过渡态提供诸如关于能量壁垒和可以从过渡态理论计算的迁移速率的关键化学和物理信息。当系统极其复杂，有一个非常粗糙的势能面，通过某些降维方法系统可能会表现出更平滑的自由能面。在这个自由能面上的过渡态，而不是那些在原有的能源面，将提供这些复杂的系统的迁移过程的更清晰的见解。 在数学上，这些过渡态是在R^3N空间的能量表面的指数-1的鞍点，其中N为原子数。这样的高维问题给这些指数-1鞍点的数值搜索带来了挑战。标准牛顿迭代方法求根可能会受制于非凡的计算代价。系统自身的松弛过程，如常规的分子动力学模拟，是有助于寻找局部的亚稳状态，但不可能定位鞍点。项目主持人提出了新的动力系统，“温和的上升动力”（GAD），该动力学收敛到指数-1的鞍点。这种新的动力学是基于最小模式跟踪的方法论，其中仅仅需要海瑟矩阵的最小特征值对应的特征向量。 在这个项目中，我们的主要目标是提出一种新的算法框架来搜索指数-1鞍点，该框架能够加速线性收敛的现有数值方法达到二次或超线性收敛的，而维持同样的计算成本不变。我们的框架是一种具有二次迭代速度的迭代最小化方案，该方案的一般广泛性使得能够从传统的数值分析角度来重新解释和分析很多现有的算法。此项目研究该框架的最佳的数值实现，并应用到潜在的能源面（无降维）和自由能面（带降维）。我们还解决有关实际应用，如初始化一些重要的问题。

11304314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304314.value: We proposed the framework of iterative minimization for the saddle point problem and proved the quadratic convergence for the iterative scheme. This result reveals the hidden math structure behind the mainstream algorithms. With this math understanding, we constructed the new algorithm which significantly outperforms the mainstream algorithms. Our algorithm to the multi-scale problem is also quite efficient due to this new formulation.

11304314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304314.value: There are quite a few points for further developments, most of which are from the communication with the experts in other fields (control, optimization, material science, training neural networks, etc) 1) The connection to the proximal method in optimization for min-max problem 2) The variational structure of our GAD: the connection to the Zermelo's navigation problem (one classic problem in optimal control) and Finsler geometry 3) The acceleration of our Multi-Scale GAD with the aid of ADAM idea used in training the neural network as a most p opular acceleration technique of the stochastic gradient descient.

11304314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304314.value: Optimization is an old and well-established subject which concerns the minimization of a function. Most of the problems are not convex and there are multiple local minimizers. Then in this case, the saddle point connecting local minimizers is then of particular interest: not only in the area of rare events associated with the stochastic system but also in the understanding of high dimensional non-convex function -- the energy landscape problem. The outputs of this project offer a very powerful and efficient tool of numerical technique to explore such an energy landscape.

11304414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304414.value: 關於多維細分法與方向FIR濾波器組的設計與應用

11304414.label: Project Objectives
11304414.value: Characterization and Construction of Multidimensional Subdivision Schemes: The main objective of this project is to construction new multidimensional subdivision schemes. Based on suitable analysis and characterization of multidimensional subdivision schemes in terms of their associated subdivision masks, our focus will be on subdivision schemes associated with multidimensional quincunx lattices or other commonly used lattices, for example, lattices associated with root-p subdivision schemes for p=2, 3, 5, ..., in dimension 2, as well as on subdivision schemes having many desired properties including symmetry properties (symmetric with respect to certain symmetry groups in high dimensions), high orders of sum rule, linear phase moments, and so on. We shall study interpolatory subdivision schemes in the point of view of sum rules and linear phase moments, and provide new insight on the construction of interpolatory subdivision schemes in high dimensions. Special attention will be given on proposing new multidimensional subdivision schemes whose associated masks have the properties of short support, high order of linear phase moments, high order of sum rules, symmetry, and good Sobolev smoothness. Multivariate Symmetric Compactly Supported Wavelet Tight (Dual) Frames and Directional FIR Filter Banks: Once we obtain subdivision masks for the multidimensional subdivision schemes with those desirable properties, our another objective of this project is to further investigate the construction of multivariate wavelet tight (dual) frames from those subdivision masks. We shall focus on the development of extension algorithms for the construction of the framelet masks (high-pass filters) from the scaling masks (low-pass filters) for our constructed subdivision schemes, and also on the construction of framelet generators having symmetry properties with respect to some commonly used symmetry group in CAGD, e.g, full-axial symmetry group, the quadrilateral symmetry group D4, and the hexagonal symmetry group D6. Motivated by the diamond-shape filters associated with the quincunx subdivision schemes, we shall also investigate the design of FIR filter banks having directional sensitivity, for example, using the Laplacian pyramid scheme. Applications of our wavelet tight (dual) frames and directional FIR filter banks in high-dimensional data analysis such as image/signal denoising shall be considered. In the spirit of reproducible research, we shall provide a publicly available software package of the implemented fast algorithms of our directional filter banks systems with testing experimental results for many suitable applications.
