11409214.label: Major findings and research outcome
11409214.value: In recent decades, restorative justice (RJ) has provided an alternative means for dealing with criminal matters worldwide. Among scholars, lawyers, and government officials in Taiwan and mainland China, there is growing interest in RJ such as mediation, criminal reconciliation, alternative measures to prosecution, and community correction programmes. In mainland China, amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law that were enforced in 2012 appear to have consolidated existing RJ practices and facilitated the future development of RJ. In Taiwan, the Ministry of Justice has adopted RJ as its priority policy of criminal justice reform. In 2010, the Government launched a pioneering programme entitled the ‘Restorative Justice Initiative’, which was conducted at the District Prosecutor’s Office. Unlike Taiwan and mainland China, no statutory restorative measures have yet been incorporated into the mainstream criminal justice system in Hong Kong. Some non-governmental organizations endeavour to develop innovative strategies to prevent misbehaving adolescents from delinquency. The present study have investigated the laws, mechanisms and conditions that allow RJ to be used for treating delinquents in Hong Kong, Taiwan and mainland China over the past two decades. Drawing upon existing research data from three jurisdictions, we have constructed a framework for analyzing the uses of RJ in three Chinese communities. Over the past three years, the research team has completed 70 individual interviews and 16 focus groups with mediators, social workers, criminal justice personnel, and service users of RJ in Hong Kong, Taiwan and mainland China. In other words, all field works were successfully completed. In sum, the research team had identified the definitions and characteristics of RJ, delineated the similarities and differences between Chinese mediation and RJ, and identified factors affecting RJ’s evolution in the region. The analysis had examined the compatibility of Western RJ with Chinese RJ practices. In total, 14 pieces of research output have been generated by the research grant thus far. These include 10 papers presented at international conferences in Australia, China, Hong Kong, Iran, Norway, and Singapore; and one book chapter published by Routledge, one book chapter to be published by Routledge (in press), and two articles published in international refereed journals. So far, we have documented the rapid development of RJ over the past two decades and developed a better understanding of how RJ is connected to the current CJ system in three Chinese jurisdictions.

11409214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11409214.value: Over the past two decades, RJ processes have been implemented in several countries in the Asia-pacific, North America, and Europe. The scope of RJ has been expanded, from dealing with minor crimes to more serious offences such as school violence, sexual offences, domestic violence, and murder. The emphasis remains on reducing crime and transforming the behaviour of offenders, rather than empowering victims towards healing. Different handbooks have been produced to guide conference facilitators or mediation practitioners to conduct various restorative practices. Nevertheless, no statutory restorative measures have yet been incorporated into the conventional criminal justice system in Hong Kong. It is therefore essential to study the lessons from Taiwan, mainland China and overseas, to investigate how RJ can be incorporated into the mainstream CJ system in Hong Kong. Based on the current GRF, we have applied for a new GRF grant to further our study in this aspect. I am pleased to report that RGC has approved our application for extending our research on RJ. A project titled "Restorative justice for delinquents in Hong Kong: The way forward" has just been approved, allowing our team to continue our study from January 1, 2019 to Dec 31, 2020.

11409214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11409214.value: In recent decades, restorative justice (RJ) has provided an alternative means for dealing with criminal matters worldwide, including the Greater China region. In mainland China, amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law that were enforced in 2012 appear to have consolidated existing RJ practices and facilitated the future development of RJ. In Taiwan, the Ministry of Justice has adopted RJ as its priority policy of criminal justice reform. In 2010, the Government launched a pioneering program entitled the ‘RJ Initiative’, which was conducted at the District Prosecutor’s Office. Unlike Taiwan and mainland China, no statutory restorative measures have yet been incorporated into the mainstream criminal justice system in Hong Kong. The present study have investigated the laws, mechanisms and conditions that allow RJ to be used for treating delinquents in Hong Kong, Taiwan and mainland China. In this study, we have identified the definitions and characteristics of RJ, delineated the similarities and differences between Chinese mediation and RJ, and identified factors affecting RJ’s evolution in the region. In sum, we have documented the development of RJ over the past years and developed a better understanding of how RJ is connected to the criminal justice system in the three Chinese jurisdictions.

11409314.label: Project Objectives

Compile a data-base of the spatial layouts, internal street patterns and location of key features of different shopping centre types in Hong Kong. 11409314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11409314.value: 大型商場已發展成世界各地主要都市的重要部分。作為城市組織往室內重要延伸，它們巳發展成一種新形式的公共娛樂休閒空間。毫無疑問，在主要現代城市裏市民和遊客們正花越來越多時間於的商場內。 本研究主要以凱文·林奇 （Kevin Lynch) 的經典城市理論內五大元素 − 通道（Path）、區域（Districts）、邊緣（Edge）、節點（Node）、地標（Landmark）− 作為基本，運用視覺和網絡圖分析方法探討香港主要商場作為城市空間的不同範疇。現有商場規劃策略大多以離商場“中心點”實際距離為出發點計算的基礎。除了空間的實際分佈及連接外，能見度及視線連接度也是影響用家動作和行為的關鍵。 具體而言，本研究主要集中研究商場空間三大方面：1）通道空間視線場特性，2）個別主要空間能見度，以及 3）空間與空間視線連接度，調查五大元素於商場的應用。利用能見度圖表分析（Visibility Graph Analysis [VGA]）衍生的電腦軟件，此研究分析20不同大小商場案例視線場特性，如連接度、結合度、可懂度、複雜性、集結性、等等，以作歸類。原用於社會網絡分析（Social Network Analysis [SNA]）的方法將被採用來建立互望度網絡（Inter-visibility Network [IVN]），加深對關鍵空間和其他焦點視覺網絡上分佈的理解。最後，將在選定商場內進行現場調查和實地觀察用者活動和行為模式，核實所得出的結果。 本研究的結果可用來優化商場設計的視線網和空間網絡性能。這將是一個雙贏的局面：不但用家可以享受更好的城市空間，而且可以吸引更多的遊客到商場，並同時提高零售商業務從而為商場經營者增加銷售衍生租金收入。此外，這項研究的結果可向研究人員、業界、發展商和管理層進一步説明商場視線網和空間網絡性能對用戶行為的深層影響，以及其對城市規劃研究更廣泛的應用。

11409714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11409714.value: 佛教源於印度，廣被東亞等地，流傳下來的漢譯佛典的種類和數量繁多，為研究佛教歷史和教理的珍貴材料；其中《雜阿含》更是最原始的佛典之一，日益受到國際佛學界的重視。學界使用漢譯佛典時，多依據《大正新脩大藏經》，但這版藏經訛誤、錯漏甚多；《雜阿含》近年雖有重編本，仍未及參校《磧砂藏》、《金藏》等，也未能吸收近年方興未艾的「佛典語言學」的研究方法和成果。本計劃擬重新校勘、標點《雜阿含》全本，並選擇代表性的篇章，進行白話譯寫和主題研究，冀通過版本校勘、漢巴梵文本對讀，解決經文的難點，除有助更清晰和全面理解《雜阿含》外，也可為漢譯佛典的校讀和譯寫，積累經驗，制訂範例。 Saṃyuktāgama: Collation, Translation into Modern Chinese and Thematic Studies Buddhism originated in India and disseminated into East Asia. Considerable quantities of Buddhist scriptures were translated into Chinese and they are precious resources for the Buddhist studies. Being one of the most primitive scriptures of Buddhism, Saṃyuktāgama(Za-A-Nan-Jing) has been catching more attention from the academia. Scholars, in general, consult Taishō Tripiṭaka when they are looking for the Saṃyuktāgama. This version, however, is full of errors. Recently, there is a re-edited version of Saṃyuktāgama, but it was not emended by making references to Qìshā Edition and Jin Edition, let alone new methodologies and recent achievements in linguistic research of Chinese Buddhist translations. This project aims at re-collating and re-punctuating the Saṃyuktāgama, as well as translating and carrying out thematic studies on selected passages. By comparing and analyzing Saṃyuktāgama from different versions and different languages, problematic interpretations in the scripture can be overcome. It is hoped that this project can help to improve the interpretation and understanding of Saṃyuktāgama, as well as setting up a fine example for the collation and translation of Chinese Buddhist translations in the future.

11410214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11410214.value: 香港及澳門業權分散住宅的管治︰三元效能感、機構設計及集體主義

11410214.label: Project Objectives
11410214.value: To provide an overview of the governance process of MOH in Asian cities, particularly regarding difficulties encountered in the processes of collective action and its consequences; To adapt the collective interest model by incorporating the concept of proxy efficacy and other relevant social theories; To investigate the participation levels of homeowners in housing governance in selected housing projects in Hong Kong and Macau; To empirically test the applicability of the adapted collective interest model in explaining the participation behaviour of the homeowners in housing governance in Hong Kong and Macau, and to explore the determinants of the homeowner participation; To elucidate how differences in the institutional settings of housing governance affect collective action in the governance of the selected housing developments; and To explore possible ways of improving private housing governance in Hong Kong and Macau to improve socially responsible decision-making by the local authorities.

To adapt the collective interest model by incorporating the concept of proxy efficacy and other relevant social theories;

To empirically test the applicability of the adapted collective interest model in explaining the participation behaviour of the homeowners in housing governance in Hong Kong and Macau, and to explore the determinants of the homeowner participation;

11410214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11410214.value: The ownership arrangement of multi-owned housing (MOH) necessitates collective actions of homeowners for proper governance of this type of housing (e.g. for housing maintenance and rights protection). Yet, given the collective-good nature of the outcomes of MOH governance, the classic collective-action dilemma suggests that rationality drives homeowners to free-ride on others’ efforts, and that no collective action will take place eventually. However, not all MOH developments are unmanaged actually. Some homeowners do actively participate in MOH governance, and it is worthwhile to examine why some participate whereas others do not. Such inquiry helps to illuminate ways to facilitate collective actions in MOH governance, which is essential for the sustainable management of housing stock and nurturing of civil society. While other scholars and the investigators have identified a list of determinants of homeowner participation, little work has been done on the effects of perceived efficacies of governance proxies (e.g. property management companies and owners’ associations) and institutional settings on collective actions in MOH governance. To fill these gaps, this study aims to explore the impacts of proxy efficacy beliefs and institutional settings on homeowner participation in Hong Kong and Macau using both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Given their similar social and cultural contexts but different institutional settings, these two cities are chosen for a meaningful comparison of the findings. To evaluate the effects of proxy efficacy beliefs, an analytical model built upon the widely-used collective interest model and supplemented by other profound social theories like normative conformity and social identity theories is developed. Quantities analyses are conducted the data obtained from structured household surveys. On the qualitative side, in-depth case studies through contextual analyses and interviews with various stakeholders involved in MOH governance are conducted. The information collected is analysed with the institutional analysis and development framework. The findings of the qualitative study depict how the effects of efficacy beliefs, including perceived self, group and proxy efficacies, on participation behaviour are moderated by institutional design. This research will provide valuable insights into homeowner participation in MOH governance in Hong Kong and Macau. The findings will assist policy-makers to make more informed decisions on the governance of MOH. In addition, this study will propose recommendations for improvements in the structure of contemporary housing governance. It will also serve as a cornerstone for wider comparative research with other Asian cities where MOH is predominant such as Shanghai, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore. 因為業權分散住宅的所有權安排，在適當管治這種類型住宅時，集體行動（如房屋維修和維權）是必須的。然而，鑑於業權分散住宅的管治成果屬於集體利益的一種，個別業主會受理性驅使，選擇不參與，反而去坐享別人努力的成果，集體行動因而不會出現，這個情況是典型的集體行動困局。話雖如此，事實上，並非所有的業權分散住宅都管理失當，一些業主確實積極參與住宅管治。因此，為什麼有些業主參與，而有些則不參與？這個問題值得我們深入研究。這種研究有助我們瞭解如何促進在業權分散住宅的集體行動，這樣的知識對住宅的可持續管理及培育公民社會十分重要。雖然，其他學者和研究人員已經找出了一些決定業主參與屋苑管理的因素，但管治代理（如物業管理公司及業主組織）的效能及制度安排等方面的影響，仍未有足夠的研究。為了彌補這些不足，本研究採用定量和定性方法，探討代理效能信念及制度安排如何影響香港及澳門的業主參與住宅管治。選擇這兩個城市作研究對象，是因為它們有類似的社會和文化背景，同時有不同的制度安排。 研究團隊為了評估代理效能感對業主參與住宅管治的影響，在已獲廣泛使用的「集體利益模型」及其他經典理論（如從眾理論及社會認同理論）的基礎上，構建一個分析模型。研究團隊會通過問卷調查向住戶收集數據，進行定量分析。另一方面，研究團隊亦牽通過案例研究及訪談各利益相關者，進行定性分析。研究團隊將收集得來的資料，以制度分析與發展框架進行分析。定性研究的結果將說明效能感（包括自我效能感、集體效能感及代理效能感）對業主的參與行為，如何受到制度設計的影響。這項研究將就香港和澳門業權分散住宅業主參與屋苑管治的課題上，提供有價值的見解。這些研究成果將有助於決策者對業權分散住宅業的管治做出更明智的決策。此外，本研究將提出改善在當代房屋管治的建議，它也將作為與其他亞洲城市（如上海、台北、吉隆坡和新加坡）比較研究的基礎。

11410214.label: Realisation of objectives
11410214.value: To realize the project objectives, the research team has undertaken or completed the following activities: (1) Overviewing the frameworks and processes of multi-owned housing (MOH) governance in Asian cities through a background study - Problems and difficulties encountered in initiating and maintaining collective actions in MOH governance were studied; (2) Conducting a comprehensive literature review on the collective interest model and concepts of efficacy beliefs - Based on the findings of the literature review, an analytical model which integrates the collective interest model with social cognitive theory and other social theories was constructed; (3) Compiling rosters of medium- and large-scale of private housing developments in Hong Kong and Macau based on the information from the governmental sources and publicly accessible geographical information systems - These rosters formed the sampling frameworks for the questionnaire surveys in the two study cities; (4) Designing, pretesting and fine-tuning a questionnaire set for obtaining the data for the empirical research; (5) Carrying out questionnaire surveys in 15 selected private housing developments in Hong Kong and 12 selected private housing developments in Macau; (6) Performing statistical analyses performed on the dataset obtainable from the surveys to identify determinants of the participation behaviour of homeowners in MOH governance in the two cities; (7) Comparing the survey findings and analysis results obtained from the two cities; (8) Conducting case studies on two private housing developments in Hong Kong and one in Macau to investigate how institutional settings of housing governance affect collective actions in MOH governance - In-depth interviews were held with the representatives of the resident associations, individual homeowners and staff of property management agents of these three housing developments. Documentary review was performed on the deeds of mutual covenant, house rules and minutes of resident association meetings. Contextual analyses were conducted on the materials posted on the online resident forums of these housing developments; (9) Carrying out analyses based on the institutional analysis and development (IAD) framework to compare the influences of different institutional settings of housing governance (e.g. formation of owners’ association and legislation supporting housing governance) on homeowner participation in MOH governance; and (10) Drawing practical and policy implications and recommendations regarding how to improve MOH governance in Hong Kong and Macau. Overall speaking, the six project objectives as per original application have been substantially achieved.

11410214.label: Major findings and research outcome
11410214.value: The results of the quantitative analysis generally confirm the applicability of the collective interest model (CIM) in explaining collective-action behaviour in multi-owned housing (MOH) governance even though the model is extended by inclusion of the new factor - proxy efficacy belief. The analysis results reveal that self and group efficacy beliefs correlated significantly and positively with the level of homeowner participation in MOH governance. Efficacies of property management agents perceived by homeowners are found to bear a significant but negative effect on participation level. On the other hand, no significant correlation is found between perceived efficacy of owners’ association and participation level. Other significant determinants of participation level identified in this research include level of discontent towards MOH governance outcomes, residential attachment, social norm, membership of owners' association committee and development scale. Among all factors in the extended CIM, collective efficacy belief was the most influential predictor of homeowner participation level in the sampled housing developments in Hong Kong and Macau. Although the qualitative investigation based on the institutional analysis and development (IAD) framework found that there were noticeable dissimilarities in the institutional settings of MOH governance between Hong Kong and Macau (e.g. legal framework and power of owners' association), the quantitative analysis did not spot any significant difference in participation level between Hong Kong and Macau homeowners, paribus ceteris. With reference to the findings of the research, the following recommendations for promoting homeowner participation in MOH governance in the two cities were drawn: (1) launching community education programme which equips homeowners with the skills and knowledge necessary for MOH governance and reminds homeowners that housing governance is their own responsibilities; (2) fostering a cooperative climate within a MOH community through a multi-pronged community-building approach (e.g. better housing design with more communal facilities for social interactions, activities organized for social networking, induction program for new residents and amicable dispute resolution); (3) fortifying residential attachment of homeowners through various means (e.g. better housing design and devising a logo and song for the housing estate); and (4) institutionalizing clear rules and formal procedures for homeowners to terminate services of poorly-performing property management companies.

11410214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11410214.value: Currently, the principal investigator is writing two papers, one on the socio-economic and contextual determinants of the three efficacy beliefs of individual homeowners in multi-owned housing (MOH) developments in Hong Kong and Macau and the other on the comparative analysis of the formal and informal institutions guiding MOH governance in the two cities. The first paper will target at City & Community and the second one at Urban Policy and Research. Moreover, the research team plans to study the dynamic relationships among the three types of efficacy belief (i.e. self efficacy, group efficacy and proxy efficacy) and their impacts (both direct and indirect impacts) on homeowner participation using a path analytic approach. Drawing on the findings of this inquiry, a manuscript targeting at Housing Studies will be prepared and submitted. The current research can be further extended in at least two ways. First, the analytical framework and research design of this empirical study can be rolled out and applied to other Asian cities with large numbers of MOH developments (e.g. Singapore, Taipei and Kuala Lumpur). Second, using the institutional analysis and development framework adopted in the current study, a comparative study on the institutional arrangements for MOH governance can be conducted on Hong Kong, Macau, Taipei, Shanghai, Beijing and other big cities in Greater China.

11410214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11410214.value: While classical collective-action theories postulate that rationality drives homeowners to free-ride on others’ efforts in the governance of multi-owned housing (MOH), not all MOH developments are unmanaged actually. Some homeowners do actively participate in MOH governance, and the reasons why some participate whereas others do not is worthwhile examining. Such inquiry helps to illuminate ways to promote collective actions in MOH governance, which is essential for sustainable management of housing stock and nurturing of civil society. Previous studies identified a list of determinants of homeowner participation but little work has been done on the effects of perceived efficacies of governance proxies like the property management companies and institutional settings on collective actions in MOH governance. To fill these gaps, this study aims to explore the impacts of proxy efficacy beliefs and institutional settings on homeowner participation in Hong Kong and Macau. The findings of the study provide valuable insights into homeowner participation in MOH governance in the two cities. They assist policy-makers to make more informed decisions on the governance of MOH. The current research also serves as a cornerstone for wider comparative research with other Asian cities where MOH is predominant such as Shanghai, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore.

11410314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11410314.value: Schwartz(1992)認為人的價值觀可以形成一個環狀結構，在該結構中相鄰的價值觀是相容的，而在對立面的價值觀則是相反的。一種價值觀的變化通常也會導致其相容或者相反的價值觀發生改變(Bardi & Goodwin, 2011)。由於該結構反映的是各種價值觀的相對重要性，改變可以通過增加一種價值觀的重要性或者降低其相反價值觀的重要性來達成。 然而，目前文獻對於這兩種改變途徑及其對主觀幸福感的影響所知甚少。以往研究表明人有兩種生物系統：行為抑制(BIS)和行為激活(BAS)。前者與懲罰和回避型行為有關，而後者則與獎賞和趨向型行為有關(Gray & McNaughton, 2000)。儘管已有研究表明主觀幸福感與BIS/BAS(Erdle & Rushton, 2010)和價值觀(Bobowik, Basabe, Paez, Jimenez, & Bilbao, 2011)均有關聯，對於BIS/BAS如何影響價值觀的改變途徑並最終影響主觀幸福感仍所知有限。本計劃設計兩項研究對此進行探討。 研究一採用文化啟動方法在實驗環境中探討此問題。根據文化身份理論(Oyserman & Lee, 2008)，人們對於文化啟動的反應可以是同化或者對比。在這兩種情形下，人的價值觀均有可能經過兩種改變途徑而發生改變。本實驗將探討文化啟動所導致的價值觀改變以及該等改變在BIS/BAS與主觀幸福感之間的中介作用。 研究二採用追蹤設計在自然生活環境中探討此問題。研究表明大學教育可帶來明顯的價值觀轉變(Schwartz, 2007)。而BIS/BAS有可能影響價值觀轉變是通過哪種途徑發生，例如是提升與大學教育相容的價值觀（如開放性），或是降低與大學教育不相容的價值觀（如保守性）。本追蹤研究將運用潛增長模型探討價值觀及主觀幸福感的發展軌跡是如何互相聯繫以及受BIS/BAS的影響。

11410314.label: Realisation of objectives
11410314.value: To achieve the above objectives, two studies have been conducted this proposed successfully. Study I examines the mechanism in a laboratory setting using cultural priming procedures. According to cultural identity theories (Oyserman & Lee, 2008), people respond to cultural priming by either assimilating to or contrasting against the primed culture. The assimilation and contrast effects can lead to value changes, through either increasing values that are compatible with cultural identities or decreasing the incompatible values, before further contributing to subjective well-being. For this study, we have successfully completed data collection, statistical analysis, and published the findings on a major international conference and leading journal in the field. The total number of participants who joined our experiments was 228, which is more than the sample size planned in the proposal (i.e., 186). The findings were presented on a symposium of The 23rd Congress of the International Association for Cross-Cultural Psychology (IACCP2016) and published in International Journal of Intercultural Relations (attached). Study II employs a longitudinal design to examine the mechanism in a natural life setting. Research has shown that university education can result in significant value changes (Schwartz, 2007). Students with different levels of BIS/BAS may experience different ways of value change by either increasing values compatible with university education (e.g., openness to change) or decreasing values incompatible with university education (e.g., conservation). Using latent growth modeling, the study examines how the developmental trajectories of values and SWB are related to each other and affected by BIS/BAS. For this second study, we have also successfully completed four waves of the longitudinal data. The sample sizes for the four waves collected were 330, 302, 275, and 252, respectively. Same as in Study I, the total number of valid cases is more than what was originally planned in the proposal (i.e., 216). In collaboration with our team members, we have put together the findings from the current study with two other longitudinal studies conducted in the Mainland and the UK to prepare a high-quality manuscript, which is to be submitted to a top journal in our field (i.e., Journal of Personality and Social Psychology). The manuscript is also attached in this report.

11410314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11410314.value: Below are the findings reported in the paper published in IJIR and manuscript to be submitted to JPSP. 1. Cross-cultural experiences are increasingly common in people’s daily lives. To better understand the process of acculturation, this study examined how people with different cultural identities changed their personal values under different culturally primed contexts and the impact on their subjective well-being. A sample of Hong Kong university students (n = 179) who varied in their bicultural selves were randomly assigned to one of two culture priming conditions (i.e., Chinese and Western), before and after which their personal values and subjective well-being were assessed. Results showed that the values of Biculturals assimilated to both Chinese and Western culture primes, whereas the values of monoculturals became more in line with their own cultural identities by either assimilating to the primed culture that they identified with or contrasting against the primed culture that they did not. Consistent with our hypotheses, the value changes based on cultural identities were significantly related to the changes in subjective well-being. The implications of the findings for research on personal values and cross-cultural psychology are discussed. 2. Past research has shown personal values and well-being are somewhat related. Different perspectives have been proposed to account for the pathways from values to well-being. The effects of well-being on values, however, have not yet been elaborated in theorizing or investigated in empirical research. In this research, we offered three alternative theoretical perspectives to illustrate how well-being may contribute to values. To disentangle the directionality of the relationships between values and well-being, three longitudinal studies within the same life transition to undergraduate studies were conducted among different cultural samples in the East and the West (Mainland China: N = 218; Hong Kong: N = 252, and the United Kingdom: N = 196), using different measures of well-being and personal values. Across three studies, we showed that the initial levels of well-being predicted subsequent value change, but not the reverse. The findings highlight the importance to reconsider the role of well-being, not only as a desired outcome, but as a facilitator for value change in the process of adaptation to different social environments.

11410314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11410314.value: The findings from this project has encouraged us to further investigate the issue of value change among different samples and settings. First, in a subsequent GRF project, we attempt to investigate how the similarity in personal values among dating couples is related to their relationship quality. In this project, we conduct an experimental study in laboratory settings to examine how couple similarity affect relationship satisfaction. A longitudinal study is being conducted to test the research question in a real-life setting. Second, in our GRF proposal submitted last year, we extend the study of value similarity by incorporating the framework of implicit theories. In this project, we attempt to develop innovative implicit measures of personal values and romantic attraction to further examine how explicit and implicit measures may differ in revealing the answers. With all the above funding, we are able to build up a consistent line of research to address issues that are both theoretically and practically meaningful.

11410314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11410314.value: According to Schwartz’s (1992) theory, basic human values form a circular structure, with neighboring values being compatible with each other and values at opposite positions being conflicting ones. When value change occurs, the increase in the importance of one value is accompanied by the increases in the importance of compatible values and by the decreases in the importance of conflicting values (Bardi & Goodwin, 2011). Since values are reflected in relative importance and priorities, similar value changes can be achieved by either increasing the importance of compatible values or decreasing the importance of conflicting ones. However, little is known about the mechanism underlying these two ways of value change and the effects on subjective well-being (SWB). Findings from this project contribute to the existing literature by showing how personal values may change under different situations and how such changes further lead to changes in subjective well-being. The understanding about such as a mechanism is important not only for value theories, but also the practices (e.g., social adaptation) under different contexts, in which personal values may greatly differ (e.g., cross-cultural settings).

11500014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500014.value: 全国性选举，政治不确定性，与企业融资活动

11500014.label: Project Objectives
11500014.value: The first objective of this project is to examine whether the variation in political uncertainty brought about by national elections affects the firms’ ability to raise external funds, as measured by the likelihood of raising public and private debt and equity and the quantity of raised funds. A number of theoretical and empirical studies suggest that the uncertainty about government’s fiscal, monetary and regulatory policy affects economic behavior of private enterprises and individuals. We build upon those studies and propose that variation in political uncertainty will also impact firms’ financing activities. However, it is not clear a priori whether political uncertainty will have positive or negative effect on capital raising. On one hand, elevated political uncertainty can increase risk premia that investors require to hold financial assets (Pastor and Veronesi, 2012) and thus increase the cost of external financing and potentially decrease the supply of capital to corporations. This (supply side) view thus predicts that political uncertainty will dampen capital raising. On the other hand, if elevated political uncertainty, increases the need for precautionary savings of liquid assets, then we would observe that the periods of greater political uncertainty are associated with an increase in capital raising (demand side view). The second objective is to examine whether, conditional on a firm accessing capital markets, political uncertainty also affects the method of capital raising. Erel et al. (2011) and other studies, show that changes in economic conditions affect firms’ security issuance choices. Building on these studies, we examine the impact of uncertainty on the chosen form of capital raising: public or private equity placement, public debt, bank loan, or convertible debt. The third objective is to examine whether political uncertainty affects the use of raised funds. This investigation will help us distinguish between supply and demand explanations for the impact of political uncertainty on capital raising. The fourth objective is to examine heterogeneity in the effect of political uncertainty on financing activities of firms within the same country. Building on prior literature (e.g. Julio and Yook, 2012), we study whether the impact of political uncertainty on firms’ capital raising varies systematically with firms’ sensitivity to policy change, the political orientation of the incumbent government, and the unpredictability or closeness of the election outcome. These results would provide additional evidence on the political risk channel effect of electoral uncertainty on corporate financing activities.

11500014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500014.value: Does political uncertainty influence the ability of firms to raise external funds as well as the manner in which firms raise funds? If so, how? The goal of this proposed research is to answer these questions by examining the response of firms’ financing activities to political uncertainty surrounding national elections around the world. We focus our attention on national elections to study the effects of political uncertainty because the outcomes of such elections often have a profound impact on the future path of government economic policy. Therefore, the uncertainty related to the timing and outcome of national elections can have an important impact on corporate financing choices. Our paper contributes to a rapidly growing literature that argues that political uncertainty has real implications for corporate investment behavior (e.g. Bernanke 1983; Julio and Yook, 2012). However, we know very little about the impact of political uncertainty on the ability of firms around the world to raise debt and equity capital. Better understanding of the impact of political uncertainty on corporate financing is of great economic significance because the ability to raise needed capital is crucial for firms’ performance and investment and thus overall country economic growth. To examine the impact of political uncertainty on corporate financing, we plan to create a large data set on the capital raising activities of publicly traded firms in 48 countries in the period from 1990 to 2010. We follow Julio and Yook (2012) and use the timing of national elections as a source of exogenous variation in political uncertainty. The advantage of using an international setting is that it allows us to utilize significant cross-country and time-series variation in the timing and importance of elections as well as the capital raising activity of firms. We examine how the variations in political uncertainty brought about by national elections affects various aspects of firms' capital raising activities, including: (a) the likelihood that a firm raises external funds, b) the method of raising capital, c) the amount of raised funds, and (d) the uses of the raised funds. We also examine heterogeneity in the effect of political uncertainty on financing activities of firms within the same country. We believe that the findings of this study will provide new insights into the economic consequences of political uncertainty and therefore be useful for researchers, practitioners, investors, and policy makers. 政治不确定性是否会影响企业的融资能力？本研究通过检验企业融资活动对由全国性选举所带来的政治不确定性的反应来回答这个问题。我们专注于全国性选举是因为这类选举普遍对政府未来的经济政策有显著影响。因此企业融资方面的决定会受到全国性选举时间、结果不确定性的重要影响。政治不确定性的实质影响是目前正在快速推进的一个研究领域，但我们对全球层面企业通过债务或股权融资能力受政治不确定性的影响仍然所知甚少。对此问题的更深层理解有助于企业获得更好的业绩、做出更好的投资决定，进而有助于经济增长，因此有重大的实际价值。 我们收集了包括全球四十八个国家、时间跨度超过二十年的企业融资活动大数据。我们利用全国性大选的时间作为政治不确定性变化的外生变量。而跨国数据使我们可以利用国家间关于大选时间、大选重要性、以及企业融资活动的差别。我们检验了政治不确定性的变化对下列融资行为的影响：（1）企业外部融资的可能性，（2）企业融资的渠道，（3）企业融资的额度，（4）募集所得资金的用途。我们同时检验了政治不确定性对单个国家内部融资行为的影响。我们相信对政治不确定性之经济后果的研究将为研究人员、从业人员、投资者以及政策制定者提供新的启示。

11500014.label: Realisation of objectives
11500014.value: We have largely completed all the project objectives. As the attached paper shows, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the effect of political uncertainty on the capital raising activity of firms for firms from 46 countries over the 1992 to 2014 period. Specifically we exploit plausibly exogenous time-series variation in political uncertainty induced by national elections over that period. We gathered information on national elections from the World Bank Database of Political Institutions (DPI), which provides information about the timing of national around the world. Given that the national elections occur at the country level, policy uncertainty brought about by the elections should be largely exogenous for the individual firm. We collected data for all public and private debt issued by private and public companies in 46 countries during the period from January 1992 to December 2014. Finally, we linked the security issuance data to the firm accounting information from the Compustat Global and Compustat North America databases. Our empirical strategy aims to uncover whether shifts in the level of political uncertainty, as captured by the timing of national elections, are an important determinant of firms’ ability to raise external funds when needed (and investors willingness to provide capital). To realize our objectives, we estimated a series of firm-year level multivariate regressions in which we modeled various aspects of firm capital raising activity as a function of a dummy variable for the election years (our measure of increased policy uncertainty), country GDP growth rate and firm-specific characteristics. All regressions also include country and year dummy variables to remove the influence of any time-invariant country characteristics and time-varying global macroeconomic shocks that could affect firm financing activities in a given country and year. To realize our first and second objectives, we estimated a series of logit models to examine the effect of political uncertainty on the likelihood of firms’ capital raising as a function of the timing of national elections and controls for changes in country-level economic conditions and firm-specific characteristics. We also examined the effect of elections-induced political uncertainty on the firms’ choice of security that they could possibly issue. Specifically, we tested whether, conditional on a firm’s decision to raise capital, increased policy uncertainty due to a national election affects the firm’s choice of a specific security, namely seasoned equity offering, private debt (bank loan), or public debt (bonds). We also examined whether political uncertainty affects not only the firm’s decision to obtain capital but also the quantity of raised capital when the firm decides to issue either seasoned equity offering, bank loan, or bonds. In these regressions, our question is whether, given the firm’s decision to issue a particular security in a given year, increased policy uncertainty due to an election affects the size of the issue? To realize our third objective, we examine the differences in how firms use the raised external funds in the election and non-election years (i.e. over the election cycle). If the change in a typical firm’s capital-raising activity in the election periods (if any) is indeed driven by the firm’s demand for precautionary savings of liquid assets, then we expect firms to save cash raised from the external sources, rather than spend it on investment projects. To realize our forth objective, we study cross-sectional heterogeneity in the effect of political uncertainty on financing activities of firms across countries as well as time-series heterogeneity within the same country. Specifically, we examine whether the effects of political uncertainty vary with cross-country differences in the quality of various country legal institutions and country political/electoral system, the differences in the political orientation of the incumbent and newly elected government, the closeness of the election outcome, and firms’ sensitivity to potential change in government policy. To parsimoniously test the incremental role of cross-country, election and firm characteristics, we estimated a series of regressions which include an interactive variable of our main independent variable – Election Year - with country, election and firm characteristics that could incrementally affect the response of corporate financing decisions to elevated policy uncertainty caused by national elections. Currently, we are estimating additional tests to further sharpen our results and delve deeper into mechanisms for the observed impact of elections (and elevated political uncertainty) on firm financing activity.

11500014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500014.value: Overall, our results uncover some evidence that the variation in policy uncertainty affects corporate capital raising by influencing firms’ decisions to access capital market, the types of securities issued by firms, the size of the issues and how firms use their issuance proceeds. First, we find that the likelihood of firms raising new capital increases in election years on average and that the increase in capital raising likelihood is driven primarily by increased seasoned equity issuance. In contrast, political uncertainty does not significantly affect the issuance of public and private debt securities on average. After establishing the positive effect of political uncertainty on capital raising activity, in the next two sets of tests we attempt to distinguish between the supply and demand (precautionary issuance) explanations for this effect. Specifically, we examine whether, conditional on issuance, increased political uncertainty in election years also affects the quantity of raised funds. We find that issuing firms indeed on average raise more funds when they issue bonds, loan or seasoned equity in election years. We then examine whether shifts in political uncertainty also relate to how firms use the proceeds from the security issuance. We find that the amount of issuance proceeds raised by firms in election years is positively associated with a contemporaneous increase in cash balance but not with investment in capital expenditure or research and development. These results therefore suggest that precautionary issuance motive seems to be the primary motive for increased capital raising in the election years because firms appear to want to have more liquid funds on hand in uncertain times. Given that the US firms dominate our sample, we show that all these results hold for the full sample and for the non-US sample. Finally, we studied whether the impact of political uncertainty on firms’ capital raising varies systematically with the strength of country legal institutions, differences in electoral system, strength of country checks and balances, political stability and risk, firms’ sensitivity to policy change, whether an election results in a change in government, and the unpredictability or closeness of the election outcome. We find some evidence that the effect of election years on firm debt and equity issuance decisions appears to vary with the country electoral system (presidential versus parliamentary) and closeness of the election outcome. Taken together, the results show that shifts in political uncertainty can influence firms’ incentives (and ability) to raise needed external funds.

11500014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500014.value: We are currently expanding the scope of our initial investigation by using alternative settings (“quasi-natural experiments”) which significantly (and unexpectedly) increased the level of political uncertainty faced by firms, such as the decision of the United Kingdom citizens to leave the European Union in the June 2016 “Brexit” referendum. To investigate the impact of “Brexit” on financing activity and cost of capital of firms, we extended our data through June 2017. In this project, we employ the difference-in-difference approach to identify the impact of a shock to policy uncertainty caused by the Brexit on the capital raising activity of firms around the world. This project is currently in progress.

11500014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500014.value: This research studies how shifts in political uncertainty due to the timing of national elections impact financing decisions of firms in 46 countries over the 1992-2014 period. Our evidence suggesting that political uncertainty affects firms’ decisions to access capital markets, the types of securities they issue, the size of the issues and how firms use their issuance proceeds. We find that the likelihood of raising new capital, especially new equity capital, increases in election years on average. Issuing firms raise more funds when they issue bonds, loans or seasoned equity in election years. We also find that firms increase their financing activity in election years mainly to increase their precautionary cash balances. We find some evidence that the effect of elections on firm financing activity varies with the country electoral system (presidential versus parliamentary) and closeness of the election outcome. We believe that our results should provide important evidence on a specific channel through which political uncertainty affects firms’ decisions and performance. Because the availability of financing to businesses is crucial for firms’ performance and countries’ economic growth, understanding the effects of political uncertainty on corporate financing should be important for scholars, practitioners, investors, and policy makers.

11500114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500114.value: 利用语意搜寻及可重用性指引架构 建立协同建模及企业信息系统整合需求分析

11500114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500114.value: Enterprise systems integration is an important ongoing activity in organizations with large and complex IT infrastructures, which require solid integration architecture to enhance business flexibility and agility. To establish such architectures, it is necessary to identify, model and analyze the integration requirements of numerous stakeholders. The entire process needs elaborate collaboration, coordination, and negotiation among the various stakeholders from both business and technical groups. The Principal Investigator recently completed a GRF project that included the development and evaluation of a conceptual modeling technique for identifying and specifying the services and events required by each system as individual model fragments, and then synthesizing those fragments to obtain enterprise-wide integration requirements. The final evaluation of this modeling technique highlighted certain challenges that need to be addressed. In particular, it identified the need to support collaboration among stakeholders who cannot be co-located, and to deal with the evolving nature of the integration requirements identified by those stakeholders; to address the scalability problems related to the technique especially with respect to collaboration and negotiation; and to improve the identification and specification of reusable services and events. The project will build upon the developed modeling technique, following a design science research methodology for building and evaluation of key components of the proposed framework environment. The framework will include a semantic search and matching algorithm for finding services and events, and an algorithm for technical group members to identify similar services and events to enhance reusability. This project will develop a prototype system to help stakeholders from business and technical groups in modeling and resolving differences through an iterative and incremental process performed in an asynchronous and distributed mode. These algorithms and the prototype system will be evaluated by using it in a graduate systems integration course that has a typical enrolment of about 100 students. This applied research will contribute to the development of two algorithms to address the challenging problems of identifying integration requirements around the proposed framework. The requirement specifications produced by several stakeholders in an organization using such a system can be effectively and efficiently used to determine the enterprise integration architectures and the subsequent selection of suitable integration technologies. Finally, the design principles and framework used in this project can be adapted for other types of environments, such as large-scale software systems development, and one-of-a-kind complex systems that inherently necessitate the specification of requirements by several stakeholders.

11500414.value: 關於存在前置期的隨機收益問題研究

11500414.label: Project Objectives
11500414.value: To partially characterize the optimal replenishment policy structure for the periodic-review inventory system with random yield and positive leadtimes. To develop heuristics and bounds that perform well and are easily implementable. To publish high quality research papers.

To develop heuristics and bounds that perform well and are easily implementable.
To publish high quality research papers.

11500414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500414.value: The proposed project has arisen from recent experiences with a pharmaceutical firm at which arriving materials must be sample-tested for microbial contamination control. If a sample test fails, the entire shipment of a material is disposed of or returned. That is, each order shipment is subject to so-called all-or-nothing random yield. A sample test usually takes a significant amount of time to run, in the range of multiple weeks, which may be much longer than the order delivery time. The firm needs to implement a decision-support system to guide its inventory replenishment of such materials. We will consider a single-item multi-period periodic-review inventory system in which the firm conducts a sample-test immediately upon the arrival of each order shipment. The total time taken by the supplier to fulfill an order and by the firm's sample test is significant, and we refer to it as the (order) leadtime. If the arriving order fails the sample test, the entire shipment is defective and is disposed of or returned. Demand occurs randomly in each period. The firm's objective is to minimize its expected total discounted cost, which includes purchasing, inventory-holding and shortage costs, by optimizing its inventory replenishment policy. In the extensive literature on inventory management in the presence of random yield and/or supply disruption, there are only a few reported results for problems with positive leadtimes. The structure of an optimal inventory control policy is an open area of research due to the challenge intrinsic to problems with random yield. Furthermore, an optimal policy structure will not be easy to implement, even if it can be fully characterized, and hence developing easily implementable heuristics and bounds is inevitable. However, characterizing the optimal policy structure will provide not only a benchmark for evaluating heuristics and bounds, but also insights into heuristic development and bound construction. Although a number of heuristics have been proposed and tested under a general form of yield randomness, little is known for the problem with an all-or-nothing yield pattern. The proposed project will aim to fill these two gaps. Preliminary analytical results are presented in this proposal, and a set of tasks for achieving the research goals are described. Our recent work on related problems and the techniques learned during those experiences have encouraged us to take up the challenge described here. 該項目基於近期與制藥企業調查中發現的問題。 該企業的來料在投入使用前，大都需要經過抽驗， 以防微生物及細菌污染。如果抽驗不合格，整批來料就會作廢或退還給供應商。具體地講, 每批訂貨會呈現所謂 “全部或零” 的隨機收益。 樣檢一般需用相當長的時間來完成, 如數個星期, 從而可能比訂單送達前置期還要長。企業需要決策支援系統進行該類物料的補貨管理。 我們將考慮單貨品週期定貨系統; 該系統要求貨品到達之時進行樣檢 而且樣檢需時較長。訂單送達時間與檢測時間總和在此稱為訂單前置期。如果到達的貨品不能通過檢驗 整批貨品將被視為不合格 被消毀或退還。需求在每期到達, 其量屬於隨機變數。企業的目標是通過補貨策略達成折現總成本最小化; 成本包括採購, 庫存和缺貨成本。 在豐富的隨機收益文獻中, 只有少數文章渉及有前置期的庫存問題。針對最優定貨策略的結構是怎麼樣的問題的研究文獻中屬空白。一方面, 即使該結構可以刻劃, 其實施也會不易, 因而有必要開發易於實施的經驗演算法及上下界。另一方面, 最優結構的分析不僅為評估經驗演算法提供依據, 也為設計後者提供思路。儘管已有若干經驗演算法面世, 但它們主要針對一般隨機收益模式, 而對於我們的研究的特殊收益 ˗ 全部或零 – 模式指導意義不大。本研究專案旨在填補該項空白。 前期初步研究在此做了介紹, 一組任務也進行了描述。我們在相關問題研究中累積的經驗以及在這些過程中掌握的工具增強了我們的開展該項目的信心。

11500414.label: Realisation of objectives
11500414.value: We have established a well performing heuristic, and partial results appeared in a conference paper (published). As the conference paper has shown, the problem possesses certain structural properties; however, they do not change the problem nature -- multi-dimensionality. This remains a computational challenge. A PhD student is exploring new ways by combining Deep Learning with optimisation, which can take advantage of structural properties. We hope such effort will lead to more promising results. Note that the Deep Learning methodology does not generally utilize structural properties of the problem in concern. Although two papers related to random yield are still under review after revisions by International Journal of Production Economics and Annals of Oper. Research, I believe they will be accepted within one year. Another major paper we prepared earlier is still under revision (initially submitted to Oper. Research).

11500414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500414.value: 1. In the first project, we studied a single-item, periodic-review inventory system with stochastic demand, delivery lead times and all-or-nothing production yields: whenever a shipment (of an order) arrives, the firm conducts a sample test to confirm the quality; if the sample test fails, the entire shipment is returned or destroyed. Although the problem is impossible to solve exactly except in special cases, we utilize properties of the problem to develop a heuristic that, in numerical tests, performs well in comparison to a popular heuristic and in comparison to the optimal policy. 2. In the second project, we investigated the implications of yield uncertainty in firms' mergers and acquisitions, which interfaces between economics and production management. We demonstrate a threshold structure with respect to yield uncertainty to evaluate the merger profitability. Moreover, we find that the yield uncertainty effect complements the cost synergy effect (i.e., marginal cost reduction), and both have opposite impacts on the post-merger outcomes compared to the competition effect. This relationship reveals some novel insights into the aggregate merger effects on the firms' performance, total output, consumer surplus, and social welfare. For example, we show that the post-merger price might decrease even when the marginal cost reduction is not substantial. 3. In the third project, we considered a multi-component assembly system that produces a single end product in order to satisfy the one-time demand at a (known) future time with an exogenous selling price. Components can be outsourced from outside suppliers with positive leadtimes under either time-inflexible or time-flexible contracts. One of these components, say component 1, faces an uncertainty in its procurement price, depending on the spot market price, and its leadtime is uncertain too (a kind of yield uncertainty). Given supply contracts, the assembler needs to determine the procurement strategy to maximize the total expected profit that equals the expected revenue minus procurement cost, holding cost and tardiness penalty cost. After establishing a number of structural properties for each contract type, we conduct numerical studies which reveal several interesting insights; e.g., both procurement quantity and profit are non-monotone in the leadtime length, and the value of time-flexible contracts compared to time-inflexible contracts is close to zero if the price of component 1 has a decreasing trend, but otherwise significant. The research outcome has partially been described in 5.3.

11500414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500414.value: The random yield problems with lead-time remain computationally challenging because of their multi-dimensionality nature. Heuristics may work well but they can be problem-setting dependent. Thanks to recent advancement in Depp Learning, we believe the computational challenge may be overcome by combining structural properties of random yield problems with the Deep Learning approach. I will continue working with PhD students and collaborators to explore in this direction which we believe to be a fruitful endeavour. On the another front, we have encountered a technical difficulty to fix a problem pointed out by a referee in the earlier submission to Operations Research. As a result, the manuscript is currently still under revision.

11500814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500814.value: 基與消費者風險態度異質性的新產品動態定價策略研究

11500814.label: Project Objectives
11500814.value: To propose and identify pricing strategies to reduce market inefficiency due to bilateral product uncertainty faced by the monopolist seller and consumers when a new product is launched, especially in the presence of risk-averse consumers and the opportunity for social learning over time; To offer a new explanation of the pattern of introductory prices based on the notion of consumer risk attitudes; To discuss the implications of product valuation uncertainty and risk attitudes on social welfare.
rows: To propose and identify pricing strategies to reduce market inefficiency due to bilateral product uncertainty faced by the monopolist seller and consumers when a new product is launched, especially in the presence of risk-averse consumers and the opportunity for social learning over time;
To offer a new explanation of the pattern of introductory prices based on the notion of consumer risk attitudes;
To discuss the implications of product valuation uncertainty and risk attitudes on social welfare.

11500814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500814.value: While a new product is introduced into the market, consumers are typically ex ante uncertain about how much they are willing to pay for it. To resolve this uncertainty before purchasing, they may engage in a costly evaluation to learn their product valuation. The proposed research aims to investigate the firm’s strategic intertemporal pricing with regard to whether to induce or prevent the consumers to evaluate by taking into consideration their various risk attitudes. Specifically, we propose a two-period model where a monopolistic firm launches its product at the beginning of the first period and sells it over two periods. In each period, the firm determines whether to induce or prevent evaluation by setting a price for this period that maximizes its expected profits. All consumers arrive at the outset and after observing the price in the first period, they strategically make trade-offs between the expected utility from evaluation versus that from purchasing with no information. While consumers differ in their risk attitudes, they may act in different ways. If some consumers discover their true valuations in the first period through evaluation or purchase, they will reveal their information to the market. As a result, the consumers who have neither evaluated nor purchased in the first period may learn from the early adopters and make their purchase decisions accordingly in the second period. We plan to investigate how the consumers’ risk attitudes influence their evaluation decisions and the firm’s intertemporal pricing strategies. In addition, we will explore whether the consumer heterogeneity in risk attitudes benefits or hurts the firm’s profitability as well as the social welfare. 當新產品上市時，消費者通常不能確定他們對產品的支付意願如何。為解決這一不確定性，消費者在購買前可能會花費時間或金錢來對產品的價值進行評估。本研究旨在探討當消費者對購買風險的態度存在差異性時，公司如何制定其動態定價策略以引發或阻止消費者的購買前評估行為。具體來講，我們構建了一個兩階段模型。公司在第一階段推出新產品并在其後的兩階段內進行銷售。在每一階段，公司會決定是否引發或阻止消費者進行產品評估，并制定相應的價格以最大化其預期收益。所有消費者都已在最初即存在於市場，通過觀察第一階段的產品價格，他們會策略性的權衡評估與否所帶來的不同預期效用。由於消費者對風險的態度不同，他們所作出的決策也可能會有所不同。當一部分消費者在第一階段通過評估或購買發現了產品的真正價值時，他們會將信息傳遞到市場上。繼而，使第一階段未進行評估或購買的消費者得以了解，并據此做出第二階段的購買決定。本研究計劃探討消費者風險態度的差異性如何影響其購買前的評估決策和公司的動態定價策略。另外，我們還會探究消費者風險態度差異性的存在是否會有益于或傷害公司的利潤以及社會福利。

11500814.label: Realisation of objectives
11500814.value: To achieve the proposed objectives, we build a dynamic model where a monopolist sells a radically new product and use prices to induce adoption at different times. Prices are an important marketing strategy to induce adoption because in face of great product value uncertainty, consumers are not easily convinced by the seller’s marketing messages. By setting dynamic prices and inducing early purchases, the seller can influence consumer informedness and adoption decisions. Unlike many previous social learning models which treat the adoption sequentiality as given, we model the different timing in adopting the new products as a result of inherent consumer differences in risk preferences and seller pricing strategies. With everything else being equal, consumers who are less sensitive to risks will adopt the product earlier; they serve as the information source about product value and enable the process of social learning. Late adopters benefit from information externality since over time the valuation uncertainty is reduced. The dynamic model here captures consumer social learning process over time in which individuals update their product value judgment imperfectly, and allows the firm to sell its product at a different price after sufficient product information is obtained. In the absence of social learning, the firm’s pricing strategy follows a typical intertemporal price discrimination scheme that the firm initially sets a high price to target the risk-neutral consumers and then lower down its price in the later period to target the risk-averse consumers. However, if social learning is possible, the risk-averse consumers may adjust their willingness to pay according after learning about the product valuation from early adopters. As such, the firm’s pricing strategy depends on the size of risk-averse consumers as well as the intensity of social learning in the market. Essentially, risk aversion and social learning are two forces that affect the adoption decisions in opposite directions. On the one hand, the presence of risk-averse consumers prevents them from adopting innovative products early on for fear of possible negative outcomes. Even if they buy, their willingness-to-pay is low and the seller has to compensate for their risk premium. On the other hand, social learning from early adopters allows information about product usefulness to spread so that consumers who have not yet adopted can learn from early adopters by, for example, reading their product reviews, engaging in conversations with them and observing the their responses. Information externality arises as a consequence of early consumer adoptions and can potentially adjust risk-averse consumers’ adoption decision and willingness-to-pay. As a result, to decide on the optimal prices, the seller has to make a tradeoff between extracting rent from uninformed consumers in the first period and allowing the informational externality to increase the late adopters’ willingness to pay at a later period. In a dynamic model, the firm can choose to sell to all consumers by adopting a single static price (termed “uniform pricing strategy”) or to price-discriminate intertemporatlly with different prices (termed “dynamic pricing strategy”). While the firm does not have to commit to a static price, it can take advantage of its knowledge about the market potential in making pricing decisions. Our results show that the uniform pricing strategy is optimal when the true market potential is low and the size of risk-averse segment is large whereas the dynamic pricing strategy is optimal otherwise. Under the dynamic pricing strategy, we find that different price patterns, such as penetration and skim pricing, emerge as a result of the combined effects of social learning intensity and true product usefulness. The seller can use penetration pricing when social learning intensity is high and market potential information is freely spread from early adopters to the rest of the market. In contrast, skim pricing happens when social learning is scarce even if the true market potential is high. These results highlight the positive effect of social learning in spreading good news and updating nonadopters’ beliefs favorably.

11500814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500814.value: This research offers an alternative explanation for various pattern of introductory prices based on the notions of consumer risk preferences and social learning. Though the seller lacks the capability to persuade the market immediately of the usefulness of its innovation, the opportunity to dynamically adjust the prices allows the firm to wait for consumers to gradually understand the value. Initially uninformed consumers later become willing to pay a higher price and bring higher profit margin to the seller. The risk-averse consumers represent the best source for incremental profits as a result of the social learning process especially when the true market potential is higher than their uninformed speculation. That also explains our finding that when social learning intensity is sufficiently high the firm with perfect market information may gain more profits from an increase in the size of risk-averse consumers, which is impossible in a static model. Furthermore, by comparing the results with that when all consumers are risk-neutral, we find that the firm might be more profitable in the presence of risk-averse consumers. The intuition behind is that the heterogeneity in consumer risk preferences enables social learning in the market which may help in credibly transferring favorable product information among consumers. Due to the information externality early adopters exert on the rest of the market, the firm’s inefficient pricing problem then could be partially eliminated. We also find that for the risk-neutral consumers, the total surplus is positive if the firm adopts the uniform pricing strategy but zero if the firm adopts the dynamic pricing strategy. For the risk-averse consumers, the uniform pricing strategy leaves them zero surplus. But under the dynamic pricing strategy, consumer surplus depends on if their updated product valuation is higher or lower than the ex-ante expected level. Specifically, if the updated valuation is higher than the ex-ante expectation, an informed consumer may have a positive surplus whereas an uninformed consumer can have zero surplus only; but if the updated valuation is lower than the ex-ante expectation, an informed consumer gains a zero surplus but the uninformed consumers may gain a positive surplus. The ex-ante consumer surplus is always nonnegative when they have heterogeneous risk attitudes. As a result, the ex-ante consumer surplus when consumers are heterogeneous is always greater than when they are homogeneous.

11500814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500814.value: Further research could extend the results presented here to incorporate other considerations. In the present research, we have assumed that the product has the properties of an experience good, which implies that consumers can discover the true product value through purchasing or social learning. However, given the multimedia technology it might be possible that a consumer could also learn about the product through a thorough (and possibly costly) evaluation process. The literature suggests that the distinction between search and experience goods is more blurred than ever due to the omnipotence of the Internet. A natural question is how the availability of such information should affect consumers purchase decision. Further, if the monopolist seller can provide such “near-experience” product usefulness information at a cost, then the next questions are how much the firm should invest in providing it and what the firm’s optimal pricing strategies would be. Finally, because our study focuses on the information from early adopter experience, further research could discuss how the product information provided by the seller and by the early adopters would affect consumer adoption and if the two information sources interact in the process.

11500814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500814.value: When a new product is introduced to the market, consumers are typically uncertain about how much they are willing to pay for it. With valuation uncertainty, whether to adopt the product is a risky decision for consumers. This research project proposes a dynamic model to investigate the optimal intertemporal pricing strategies for a monopolist selling an innovative product to a market where consumers differ in their attitudes towards consumption risk. In contrast to herding models with a fixed price, the seller in our model is free to adjust the price over time to induce the heterogeneous consumers to adopt the product at different points in time. Given that the potential customers can learn about their product valuation from the early adopters and make their purchase decisions accordingly at a later period, we explain how the consumer heterogeneity and social learning provide a rationale for the use of dynamic pricing. We also show that the consumer heterogeneity in risk attitudes can possibly benefit both the seller and the consumers.

11501114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501114.value: Fast decision-making is a subset of decision making research and typical in flora auctions, where bidding time windows are usually a few seconds, bidders make hundreds of decisions continuously for several hours, and the processes repeat on a daily basis. Such auctions provide an ideal environment to explore several under-studied issues on bidders in fast decision-making contexts, such as decision quality, levels of performance, learning styles, and job satisfaction, as well as mediating variables such as competitive arousal, number of rivalries, and demand urgency. Based on a pilot study of one of the largest flora auctions in Asia, we propose a hierarchical Bayesian model of the antecedents and consequences of fast decision-makings and plan to test it with a set of rich, big data. The data we plan to collect will consist of real-time tracking data of million bids over six months, daily in-depth interviews of a panel of bidders for one month, and observational data of these bidders’ facial and emotional responses in the bidding processes. These structured and unstructured data will be integrated and subject to a series of Markov-Chain Monte Carlo analyses to test the validity and reliability of our theoretical model. The findings should be able to contribute to the literature of fast decision-makings and offer implications for auction operators and participants.

11501314.label: Realisation of objectives
11501314.value: All the objectives have been effectively achieved. The first four objectives have been achieved by completing the project that examines how mindfulness in technology adoption (together with herding) affects soundness of technology adoption in the form of user post-adoption regret and satisfaction. Faced with multiple technology alternatives, users often make an adoption decision under uncertainty, which may affect their perception of soundness of technology adoption decision at the post-adoption stage. Specifically, they may later regret and/or dissatisfied with the choice (hence poor soundness of technology adoption) and subsequently even switch to a foregone technology at the post-adoption stage. The extant research focuses on a chosen technology and accordingly does not sufficiently explain such regret experience resulting from foregone technologies. To fill this void, we develop a research model that systematically conceptualizes and examine how mindfulness and herding, two uncertainty-mitigation adoption strategy, affects post-adoption regret and satisfaction in a technology adoption situation. We argue that Mindfulness in Technology Adoption and Herding will play different roles in affecting regret through two routes: undesirable post-adoption outcomes and unjustified adoption process. The research model was supported by a longitudinal study of 175 technology users who chose between two technologies. This research provides implications for both research and practices and make important contributions to the field. This empirical study has resulted in a conference paper published at International Conference on Information Systems in 2016. We submitted the paper to MIS Quarterly subsequently. However, despite quite constructive review comments from the review team, our paper was rejected and encouraged to resubmit. We then revised the mindfulness and regret paper based on the reviewers' comments collected from the last round of review and submitted to Information Systems Research. Unfortunately, our submission of the study to Information Systems Research journal was also rejected from further consideration at the journal. However, we received a rich set of useful comments which we spent time carefully digesting and addressing. As a result, we have made necessary revisions on the paper and are now preparing it for re-submission to MIS Quarterly. The fifth and sixth objectives represent a meaningful extension from the first four objectives by examining what are the user voluntary contribution behaviors are when users keep using a technology at the adoption stage. Specifically, involving in more interactions with an IT service at the post-adoption stage, users may develop a relationship with the IT artifact and even voluntarily contribute to it. In this research, we propose a set of new consequences of human-IT relationship, technology extra-role behavior (TERB), to denote such voluntary contributions from the users. Drawing on extra-role behavior literature, we develop a comprehensive typology of TERB and conceive of it as having three broad dimensions: feedback, voice and cooperation; recommendation and endorsement; and helping users, governance, and endorsement, among others. Then, we explore the connection between human-IT relationship at the post-adoption stage and TERB by drawing on the psychological ownership (PO) perspective. Referring to PO studies, we construct a research model to depict why users are willing to contribute voluntarily with the perceived psychological possession of a general IT service and how to design IT affordances to incubate this perception. Moreover, we also collected the necessary survey data to empirically test the research model. Two wave survey data from 200 valid respondents were collected to test the model. The empirical results lend general support to our research model. To substantiate these research pursuits, we first developed a conceptual paper titled “Engaging in Technology Extra-Role Behavior in a Human-IT Relationship: A Psychological Ownership Perspective “that more completely develops the research model by drawing on the extra-role literature and the psychological ownership theory. This conceptual paper was submitted to International Conference on Information Systems (ICIS) in May 2017 and subsequently got accepted. We presented the paper at the conference and received helpful comments. The full manuscript is also enclosed in this progress report. Then, we developed another conceptual paper to provide more details on how to conceptualize user voluntary contribution behavior from the extra-role behavior perspective, and submitted to ICIS 2018. The paper was just accepted for presentation at ICIS in San Francisco in December 2018. We are planning to prepare this conceptual paper to a special issue at MIS Quarterly on theory development and have submitted an extended abstract to the journal for the first round of review. As to the empirical study that examines user voluntary contribution behavior from psychological ownership perspective, we have been preparing a full manuscript and plan to submit in 2019. Last but not the least, the PhD student involved in this particular project has successfully graduated and joined University of Warwick as an Assistant Professor, fulfilling the mission of developing both research and research scholars. To summarize, the objectives of the research project have been realized through the joint and persistent efforts throughout the funding period. We are now well positioned to turn the research results that are well documented in the leading conferences in the IS field to premium journal papers. We greatly appreciate this GRF funding for supporting our initiative.
