11501314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501314.value: Our research contributes to the field of IS in several ways. First, we have developed a longitudinal research model which delineates how post-adoption regret about IT, a new concept underpinning users’ perception of soundness of information technology adoption, is formed and explain how mindfulness in technology adoption can alleviate (and herding can enhance) regret and enhance (reduce) user satisfaction. The model is the first to integrate the mindfulness perspective into regret research. It enriches our understanding of the pros and cons of the two adoption strategies (mindfulness and herding) by explaining the consequences of adoption (ICIS 2016). Specifically, our study finds that mindfulness in technology adoption helps reduce the tendency to discount one’s own information and disconfirmation, by considering the user’s local context, providing product-specific information, and justifying the decision process. Meanwhile, we find that herding leads to regret through two routes: undesirable outcome and unjustified process. In doing so, mindfulness in technology adoption can reduce post-adoption regret and subsequently enhance user satisfaction and reduce the chance to switch out (ICIS 2016). Second, although earlier studies have mentioned the influence of other technologies on the staying power (i.e., soundness) of adopted technology to the best of our knowledge, our research is one of only a few to systematically consider both internal (satisfaction) and external (regret) comparisons in post-adoptive technology evaluation that verifies user perception of soundness of technology adoption. By introducing external comparison, we complement the existing research which concentrates heavily on a single focal technology. We holistically consider other foregone technologies, which accounts for a large proportion of the variance in post-adoption evaluations. In addition, we are able to explain why users can be both satisfied and regretful at the same time by understanding that users may employ multiple reference points in these two parallel comparisons, and both perceptions are influenced by mindfulness (ICIS 2016; MISQ under preparation). Our subsequent study focuses on explaining user voluntary contribution behavior during continued technology usage. Our study first conceptualizes and develop a typology of user voluntary contribution by synthesizing the existing related literature. This leads to a classification of eight contribution behaviors, which can take various forms including helping users, knowledge contribution, feedback, tolerance, governance, recommendation, justification, and endorsement (ICIS 2018; MISQ under review). Then, we put forward that psychological ownership of IT, as a type of user-artifact relationship, is positively related to user voluntary contribution, with varying effects (ICIS 2017; MISQ under preparation).

11501314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11501314.value: Further development of the research could focus on addressing the following issues. First, both empirical studies use student samples. While this may enhance the feasibility of collecting longitudinal data (which we did), this design may threaten the generalizability of this research. This is perhaps quite important when we submit the papers to premier journals such as MIS Quarterly and Information Systems Research. Therefore, future research could take the action of collecting user data from real organizations with a longitudinal design. Second, the question of switching cost is worth attention. Today, it is common for users to possess multiple technologies with similar functionalities (partial switching). However, in our study context, users must devote time to developing a digital library (i.e., wiki, blog, notes, citation management software), and are thus less likely to have another simultaneous library. Future research can more explicitly consider the switching cost issue. Third, extant research has tended to overlook the notion that an unjustified process will lead to regret. In this study, we distinguished the two routes of regret and we found that mindfulness showed their separate influences on post-adoption behavior. Future research can leverage this nuanced understanding of how regret can be induced.

11501314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501314.value: Soundness of information technology adoption is manifested through user satisfaction with the adopted technology and subsequent voluntary contribution back to its development. This research projects examines how mindfulness reduces post-adoption regret and enhance user satisfaction of the technology, and what voluntary contribution behavior by users when they continue use the technology. We develop a research model that systematically conceptualizes mindfulness and post-adoption regret and examines their impacts on user satisfaction and continuance behavior, and another model that examines factors leading to user voluntary contribution behavior. Through multiple-wave longitudinal survey, we find that mindfulness can reduces post-adoption regret and subsequently enhance user satisfaction. We also find that existing users who contribute voluntarily to the technology exhibit strong psychological ownership orientation that goes beyond satisfaction. The practical implications to technology designers are that it is important to ensure that users are mindful when making choices between competing technologies. This includes being engaged with the focal technology, aware of local context, seeking novel solutions, being aware of alternative technologies. In addition, our findings also suggest to technology designers that it is important to enhance user psychological ownership, even when users are satisfied, in order for the users to make voluntary contributions.

11501414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501414.value: 灰色市场条件下的多市场定价：理论模型与实证分析

11501414.label: Project Objectives
11501414.value: Understand the nature of grey market and the impact of a grey market on the profit of a firm. Many firms claim profit loss due to grey market sales, which is intuitive because some consumers pay a low price now. However, a grey market may also attract consumers who originally would not have purchased the product at the high price. So it may also help the firm to expand its market. We build a theoretical model to study this tradeoff and examine under what conditions a grey market may be even beneficial to a firm. We will also examine the impact of a grey market on the social welfare, including the welfare of the firm and the welfare of consumers. Examine measures to regulate grey markets, such as information barrier, government regulations (such as quota and taxes), as well as prices, on the existence of a grey market. For example, for some sensitive products such as baby formula, the HK government implements a quota policy on the amount of baby formula that each person can carry through the border. For those less sensitive products, will economic measures be more efficient? How to design a good price coordination strategy in the presence of a grey market? Will such price coordination strategy more efficient to luxury good (where it is less likely to have over demand) than to ordinary popular good? Propose methods to empirically detect the existence of a grey market, and to empirically measure the size of the grey market. It is difficult to tell whether a sale is generated through genuine buyers, or a buyer who acts as an agent on behalf of another buyer in a different channel with higher prices. Panel data needs to be employed to monitor each specific buyer in a relatively long time in order to detect irregular buying activities. And changes in the sales in one channel need to be coordinated with the changes in the sales of other channels. Compare the different nature of grey markets in industrial good and luxury consumption goods by utilizing two different data sets, one from a multi-product, multi-channel and multi-nation company, and one from one of the biggest online market place in China where some of the “grey market” products are sold.

11501414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501414.value: The sale of genuine branded products through unauthorized channels (also known as gray market) is a growing problem for many firms that operate in multiple markets. Though it is hard to measure the exact size of grey market, it is generally believed that the existence of such unauthorized sales will cannibalize the profits of brand owners and measures need to be developed to counter the gray market threat. In this paper, we develop a pricing model where a firm tacitly coordinates prices across different channels so as to maximize total profits. We demonstrate that while a firm needs to reduce the price gap between markets thus leaving little room for arbitrage, the firm can sometimes benefit from the emergence of gray market activities. We also propose methods to empirically measure and examine grey markets, using two data sets: one from a multi-product, multi-channel and multi-nation company, and one from one of the biggest online market place in China where some of the “grey market” products are sold. 通过非授权渠道销售正品品牌产品 (也称为灰色市场）对于许多运行于多个市场的企业带来日益严重的问题。 虽然很难测量灰色市场的确切规模，通常认为 灰色市场的存在会蚕食的品牌拥有者的利润，所以需要制定应对灰色市场威胁的措施。在本文中，我们 制定一个定价模型，研究厂商在灰色市场存在条件下如何调节不同市场的价格。本研究发现，厂商固然需要减少不同市场之间的价格差距从而留下小套利空间，但也有可能 受益于灰色市场活动。此外，本研究也应用两组数据建议实证衡量和检验的灰色市场的方法。

11501414.label: Realisation of objectives
11501414.value: All the objectives are achieved. We have built a theoretical model to understand the the phenomenon of gray market. It is a natural outcome due to firm's profit seeking behavior. It may harm the firm under certain consequences, but surprisingly, it may also benefit the manufacturer. We also examine the effectiveness of a price coordination strategy to help regulate the gray market, and also use empirical data to demonstrate whether the observed pricing strategies in practice is effective. In addition, we also use our empirical data to verify the existence of a gray market, and measure the size of the gray market. We also compare gray markets in different product categories.

11501414.value: We find that price can be used to effectively control the size of the gray market. However, the existence of gray market is not always detrimental. Under certain conditions it helps the producer to expand market, and reach consumers who previously had not change/would not buy the product. Empirical evidence also show the existence of grey market in different segments. Firms need to take this into consideration while they make pricing decisions. 11501414.value: Grey markets are omniscient in today's business world. Different market has different properties. We wish to seek more empirical data to understand the different nature of grey markets, and explore possible measures to control/manage it.

11501414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501414.value: The sale of genuinely branded products through unauthorized channels (also known as gray markets) is a growing problem for many firms that operate in separate markets. It is generally believed that the existence of such unauthorized sales hurt the profits of brand owners. We develop a pricing model for a firm that sells an identical product in two distinct markets but faces the threat of potential gray market sales. The firm chooses prices in each market. A consumer chooses whether to buy the product from one of the markets including a gray market. We derive the optimal prices in the two markets and examine their effects on consumer demand and the total profit. We show that the higher price in one market transfers part of its demand into the gray market, thus influencing the consumer demand in the low-priced market as well. Additionally, the price gap between the two separate markets positively influences gray market sales and, under certain conditions, can lead to an increase in firm profit. Using authorized sales data from a Fortune 100 company and a separate data set on online gray market sales, we find empirical evidence in support of our model results.

11502014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502014.value: Firms competing in the same market often subcontract production of some components of their final products to their rivals. This so-called horizontal outsourcing phenomenon is common, especially in some major industries such as automobiles, computers, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. It often involves firms that have the technology know-how to produce key intermediate components in-house outsource from a rival who competes against them in the downstream market. Since horizontal outsourcing occurs between rivals, executives should look beyond cost reduction as a tool to improve their firms’ competitiveness. Otherwise, they may outsource for a wrong reason and misalign the outsourcing strategy with firms’ business strategy. Yet, in practice, according to a survey of over 300 business and IT executives conducted in 2008 by Deloitte consulting, cost reduction is considered the primary factor motivating most outsourcing decisions. Only 27% of the firms selected gaining competitive advantage as motivation for outsourcing, and a merely 15% of the firms include increasing shareholder value as one of the motivations. Our research attempts to uncover the role of strategic consideration on horizontal outsourcing. Specifically, in this project, we attempt to address several under-studied issues that could be critical for firms to make a sound decision on horizontal outsourcing. Is cost reduction still a right motivation? What are the implications of horizontal outsourcing on the final product market competition? Under what conditions are firms better off with horizontal outsourcing than producing in-house or sourcing from a non-competitor? How does the degree of substitutability of rivals' end products affect outsourcing decision? And, how does market uncertainty affect horizontal outsourcing? Our initial results show that focusing only on cost reduction but ignoring the strategic implication of outsourcing in the end product market competition, firms may lose opportunities to make greater profits. Under some conditions, a firm could make greater profit by sourcing from a rival at a price higher than in-house production cost! We expect this research will generate managerial insights to guide mid-and-high level managers whether to source components from a competitor or to produce in-house. Our initial results can be a wake-up call for many companies that primarily use outsourcing as cost reduction strategy. After completion of this project, we expect to obtain more insights on how other important factors such as demand uncertainty and contracting terms affect horizontal outsourcing. 据由德勤咨询公司进行的 对超过300的业务和IT管理人员调查(2008)，对外包的主要驱动力是降低成本和获取技术知识。水平外包往往涉及具有关键零件内部生产能力的公司把此零件的生产外包给自下游市场竞争对手。因此，第二个动机，获取技术知识作为一个激励因素可以被排除。这使得成本降低成为对外包的主要动机。但是，为什么外包给下游直接竞争对手，而不从具有此生产能力的非竞争对手公司购买呢？从供应企业的角度去看，降低其竞争对手的成本 会提高在随后的终端市场的竞争对手的竞争优势。对于买方来说，外包可以使竞争对手从出售零件获利，因此可能使竞争对手在终端产品市场的竞争能力。因此，外包给非竞争对手或内部生产好像更为合理。此外，如果组件的生产具有规模经济，外包有助于降低供应厂商的边际生产成本，从而进一步提高供应厂商在终端市场的竞争力。总之，用节约成本来解释水平外包成本的动机似乎并不够合理或全面。我们相信探讨水平外包对下游市场竞争的战略意义及识别一些额外的研究问题 非常重要。本研究的结果预计将有助于增进学术界和工业界对水平外包的理解。研究结果将为那些需要决定是否外包部件和从什么样的公司，盟友还是对手，购买源提供战略指导。 总之，我们试图揭开除节约成本以外的支持水平外包的基础。具体地说，我们有以下目标： 1。探讨企业生产效率的差距 和他们的最终产品的替代程度如何影响采购决策。 2。研究水平外包对最终产品市场竞争的战略影响。 3。了解市场的不确定性对企业外包决策的影响。 4。研究外包合同条款对公司决策的影响。

11502014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502014.value: Objectives 1,2, and 4 are completed with interesting results. However, objective 3 does not lead to publishable results because once uncertainty is considered in the competition, the analysis becomes untractable. Unless the modeling methods change dramatically, the effect of uncertainty cannot be distilled theoretically. Hence, we focus on deterministic models. Below we summarize the major findings. Focusing on cost consideration, previous studies on horizontal outsourcing have neglected the role of sole sourcing commitment and competition form on rms' sourcing decisions, which we analyze through a multi-stage game with a duopoly: an incumbent with technology know-how to make a key component in-house, and an entrant who can source the component either from a supplier who does not participate in the end product market or from the incumbent who has the technology know-how and engages in either Bertrand or Cournot competition with the incumbent in the end product market. We nd that when they engage in Bertrand competition, if the entrant commits to sole sourcing, then it will source from the incumbent whether or not the latter has a cost advantage over the non-competitive supplier because doing so, i.e., horizontal outsourcing, softens downstream market competition, or leads to market expansion when the degree of product substitutability is high and therefore, benets both rms. Without sole sourcing commitment, however, the entrant will source from its rival only if the rival enjoys a cost advantage over the non-competitive supplier. In this case, horizontal outsourcing leads to market expansion, which benets the rms and improves consumer surplus. In contrast, if the firms engage in Cournot competition, sole sourcing commitment is irrelevant: the entrant will source from its rival only if the incumbent enjoys a signicant cost advantage over the non-competitive supply source. Based on these results, we have written a paper and submitted it for peer review. Please refer to Part C.

11502014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502014.value: The potential for further development of the research includes changing the form of competition to Hotelling line competition and perhaps adding a capacity constraint in the model in the future. Some analysis has been done when the firms compete via the Hotelling line. In the future, we may consider capacity constraint. When outsourcing occurs, the efficient firm has to ration its capacity and this may change the equilibrium of the multi-stage game drastically.

11502014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502014.value: Our result shows that when firms source from a rival instead of making-in-house, they may be driven not by cost considerations, but rather on strategic reasons. In addition, whether to retain in-house capacity and thus not to commit to sole sourcing has implications for the ensuing competition if the firms sell differentiated products and compete on prices. Surprisingly, when the firms compete on prices, for the firm that will source from its rival, it is better to commit to sole sourcing because in response to this commitment, the rival firm will price higher in the end product market. Consequently, horizontal outsourcing (buying from a rival firm) does not require that the buying firm has a cost disadvantage. The main driver of horizontal outsourcing is the strategic reason: soften ensuing downstream price competition. If the buying firm does not commit to sole sourcing, t hen horizontal outsourcing occurs only if the buyer has a cost disadvantage. In contrast, when the firms compete through quantity, then the sole sourcing commitment has no effect on the firms' downstream competition.

11502114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502114.value: In this study, we investigate how the use of extended tags in eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) filings are associated with financial analysts’ information. XBRL allows firms to tag financial data and file that data with SEC or any other regulatory body. This data is then machine readable and searchable, which reduces cost of accessing and using that data (i.e. information processing costs). Prior research suggests that XBRL in general reduces information processing costs, especially for institutional investors resulting in lower cost of capital and more firm-specific information reflected in prices. However, the SEC allows firms to provide customize tags in their XBRL filings which, on the one hand, may allow firms to voluntarily customize financial statements to provide more firms specific information by highlighting concepts that are not included in the standard set of tags. On the other hand, customized tag may inhibit information search, obfuscate financial statement numbers, and ultimately reduce the usefulness of XBRL data. There is anecdotal and empirical evidence of the negative effects of the use of extended tags, including increased error rates and earnings management. We address the question of how the use of firm-specific (extended) tags is associated with the firm’s information environment. We consider the extension rate at the document level, within the disclosure related sections of the XBRL filing, within the financial statement, and for particular items that are common to many firms. We use financial analysts’ forecast error and dispersion as proxies for investors' information. We contend that extensions in the disclosure section of the XBRL filing is more likely intended to provide firm-specific information whereas extensions on items that are common across many firms are the result of the misuse of taxonomy extensions. As such, we expect the former (latter) to reduce (increase) analysts forecast error and forecast dispersion. Our study is relevant to regulators creating policies about XBRL, both in the US and around the world. Our study also addresses the broader question of how voluntary disclosure choices affect analyst information. 在這項研究中，我們研究如何以可擴展商業使用擴展標籤 報告語言（ XBRL ）申報與財務分析師的信息相關聯。 XBRL使公司標記的財務數據和文件數據與美國證券交易委員會或任何其他 監管機構。然後，這些數據的機器可讀和可搜索，可降低成本 的訪問和使用這些數據（即信息處理成本）。以前的研究 表明XBRL一般降低信息處理成本，特別是對 導致資本和更多的企業特有的成本較低的機構投資者 信息反映在價格上。不過，美國證券交易委員會允許公司提供定制的標籤 在他們的XBRL報告的，一方面，可以讓企業自願定制 財務報表，突出概念，以提供更多的公司具體信息 那些不包括在標準的標籤集。在另一方面，定制標籤可 抑制信息搜索，模糊的財務報表數字，並最終 減少XBRL數據的有用性。還有的軼事和經驗證據 使用擴展標籤的負面影響，包括增加錯誤率和收益 管理。我們討論如何利用公司特有的（擴展）標籤是個問題 與該公司的信息環境有關。我們認為，在延伸率 文檔級別的XBRL報送的信息披露相關的部分中，內 財務報表，以及共有的許多企業特定項目。我們使用 金融分析師的預測誤差和分散的代理的投資者的信息。我們 主張在XBRL報送的信息披露部分的擴展更容易 旨在提供有關該項目是企業特有的，而擴展的信息 通用的許多公司都擴展分類標準的誤用的結果。因此， 我們預計前者（後者）減少（增加）分析師預測誤差與預測 分散。我們的研究是有關監管部門建立有關XBRL的政策，無論是在 美國和世界各地。我們的研究還解決了如何更廣泛的問題 自願性信息披露的選擇會影響分析師的信息。

11502114.label: Realisation of objectives
11502114.value: This study examines the how XBRL extensions are related to financial analysts information. I find that, after controlling for potential endogeneity, more extensions are associated with lower analysts forecast error and dispersion. This suggests that extensions are related to better informed forecasts by analysts. I also examine how this association varies with earnings management, information uncertainty, errors in XBRL filings, and earnings comparability. I find that the association between extension rate and analysts information does not vary with earnings management variables but is stronger for firm with more uncertain information environments and for firms that are more comparable to their industry peers. Furthermore, extension rate and analysts’ information is insignificant for filings with technical errors. This suggests that the association between XBRL extensions and analysts forecasts is due to informational needs rather then managerial opportunism.

11502414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502414.value: Information security has long been a concern in the healthcare sector, but it has become a growing public interest as healthcare providers increasingly move sensitive healthcare information into electronic healthcare records (EHRs). While the move towards EHRs is believed to produce many benefits for healthcare providers as well as patients, EHRs-supported processes have made healthcare providers progressively more vulnerable to security attacks and breaches. Within this environment, healthcare providers must adopt EHRs as well as protects patient information. Federal regulations like the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (HITECH), as well as individual state regulations, have required healthcare providers to follow various notification guidelines to disclose breaches. Further, the government has required healthcare providers to qualify as a meaningful user of EHRs. Thus healthcare providers must move beyond purchasing and even implementing EHRs. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) outlined the criteria for meaningful use of EHRs. To qualify for federal EHR incentives, healthcare providers must attest to the specific “meaningful use” criteria. The criteria are grouped into stages, with stage 1 (2011 meaningful use criteria) being the first hurdle required for funding. Coupled with large financial incentives, meaningful use attestation requires a measure for protecting EHRs and a security risk management process. Securing electronic health information is one of the meaningful use core objectives. Therefore, this project attempts to identify the relationships among the adoption of EHRs, meaningful use attestation, and healthcare data breaches. We develop an econometric model of meaningful use attestation as a function of the adoption of EHRs and healthcare data breaches, and also develop a model of healthcare security as a function of meaningful use attestation and adoption of EHRs. We further investigate whether EHRs adoption can improve meaningful use attestation and the interaction with breaches on meaningful use attestation. This project can provide a deeper understanding of effective security programs and the effect of meaningful use on healthcare security. 长久以来，资讯安全一直是医疗行业的重要考量，而随着医疗服务提供者越来越多地将敏感的医疗资讯转成电子病历（EHRs）,该项议题也就越来越吸引了公众的关注。虽然相信朝EHRs的转化会对医疗服务提供者和患者都带来许多好处，然而基于电子病历的医疗流程，使得医疗服务提供者越来越容易成为安全攻击和数据泄露的受害者。在这样的环境下，医疗服务提供者必须在采用EHRs的同时保护患者的信息。诸如《健康保险携带和责任法案》（HIPAA）和《经济与临床医疗信息技术法案》这样的联邦规章，以及一些州立规章，都已要求医疗服务提供者按多项通告原则来披露信息泄露。而且，政府已要求医疗服务提供者满足EHRs的“有效使用”用户条件。这样医疗服务提供者就必须不仅仅是购买和配置EHRs这么简单了。聯邦醫療保險和聯邦醫療輔助計劃服務中心列出了一些对EHRs有效使用的准则。如果要符合联邦EHR激励的资格，医疗服务提供者必须证明其满足特定的“有效使用”准则。该准则被分为几个阶段，第一阶段（2011有效使用准则）是要求拨款的第一个门槛。与大量的财政激励相挂钩，有效使用验证要求对电子病历保护和安全风险管理流程进行度量。保障电子医疗资讯安全是有效使用的一个核心目标。因而，本研究计划试图找到对EHRs的使用、有效使用验证系统和医疗数据泄露这三者之间的关系。我们研究出一个计量经济学模型，该模型将医疗信息安全视为有效使用验证和医疗数据泄露这两者的方程，同时研究出将医疗信息安全看作有效使用验证和对EHRs采用的方程的模型。我们更进一步地研究了对EHRs的采用，是否会提高有效使用验证，以及资讯泄露和有效使用验证之间的关系。本项目可以对有效安全程序，和对医疗安全资讯的有效使用提供更深的理解。

11502414.label: Realisation of objectives
11502414.value: In order to achieve our objectives, we have strengthened hypothesis development and provided additional new analyses. We summarized our attempts to overcome research issues: (1) We have strengthened the theoretical basis for our hypotheses by extending the literature review. Building on organizational learning theory (used by certification studies in operations management), we have provided specific mechanisms for our hypothesis development along with the unique characteristics of security management. (2) We have enhanced our empirical analyses as following: ▪ In addition to our core analysis, we estimate a series of alternative models. While Model (1) and (2) identify the effects of all DID dummies without fixed effects, Model (3) and (4) include fixed effects. Model (1) and (3) eliminate the lagged dependent variables, only having control variables in hospital information and healthcare IT. Model (2) and (4) contain all variables. Model (1) ~ (4) cluster standard errors by hospital to account for heteroscedasticity and non-independence among observations from hospitals across years. Model (5) presents a logistic model as a robustness test for non-linear cases. The results are consistent with our earlier findings, illustrating the robustness of our results. ▪ In order to handle the concern on the matched DID sample, we created a new set of matched samples that were limited to those having at least three-years of consecutive observations with a 0.003 matching threshold (the previous version had two consecutively reported years and 0.001 as the matching threshold yielding 3,626 observations). ▪ To analyze the effect of attestation over time, we have separately tested the effect of meaningful-use attestation in the first 12-months (short term, within 12 months after attestation) and the next 12-month term (long-term, from 13 to 24 months after attestation). ‒ For the short-term analysis, we were able to satisfactorily match 850 treatment hospitals to equivalent control hospitals, yielding a matched sample of 6,028 observations. In this matched sample, 161 hospitals attested in 2011, 458 in 2012, and 231 in 2013. ‒ For the long-term analysis, we limited the sample to pairs whose treatment hospitals attested in 2011 and 2012 to ensure the long-term period (24 months) of post-treatment data. The resulting matched sample for the long-term effect includes 4,424 observations having 619 treatment hospitals with their controls. ▪ We further analyzed the effect for the cumulative period combining the short- and long-term periods. We have clearly provided changes in three types of breaches over the cumulative period. (3) In order to resolve some issues on the “incentive vs. penalty” analysis, we have removed that analysis, focusing the paper on the differential impact of attestation across breach types.

11502414.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502414.value: This study examined the effects of a certification regime on information security. Given the diverse trends and traits of data breaches, we proposed hypotheses explicating the temporal effects of meaningful-use attestation on data breaches. Our empirical models demonstrated that the effect of meaningful-use attestation varies with the nature of a breach and the effect changes over time. Our study shows that attesting hospitals observed decreases in external breaches in the year after attestation. However, they did not see any further reductions in the subsequent year. The extent to which the guidance and standards of meaningful use are sufficiently effective in reducing external breaches seems to be unclear, particularly in light of new technologies and evolving security threats. For compliance assessment, security practices required by meaningful-use attestation are grounded in well-known security vulnerabilities. However, the unpredictable and changing nature of external attacks erodes the year-over-year improvement achieved. Our finding suggests that continued progress toward preventing external breaches requires ongoing effort beyond achieving Stage-1 meaningful use. On the other hand, we found that hospitals discovered and reported more accidental breaches in the year following attestation; however, these reported breaches decreased in the long term. Organizations often do not realize an inadvertent disclosure without standardized and systematic detection procedures. Prior to meaningful use, these breaches often went unreported. Through attestation processes, hospitals discover their vulnerabilities and monitor them through periodic audits (i.e., access and incident tracking reports). As noted earlier, whereas external breaches are attributed to a lack of technical solutions (e.g., anti-virus, encryption, firewall, intrusion detection, spam/spyware filter, user authentication), accidental breaches are typically the result of "human factor" errors (Verizon 2013). Given that one of the goals of the meaningful-use program is to encourage the implementation of appropriate security mechanisms, the systematic and standardized approach of meaningful-use attestation enables identification of inadvertent breaches by tracking human errors. This tracking ability ultimately leads to actual data protection over time, because hospitals learn their vulnerable points through ongoing tracking (and more so than from any particular prior breach). Moreover, meaningful-use standards help hospitals integrate EHRs into their workflow more effectively, thus reducing the need to move data into unsecure formats like spreadsheets that are easily copied onto vulnerable storage devices – leading to the reduction of “low-tech” incidents. Unsurprisingly, we did not find an association between meaningful-use attestation and malicious internal breaches. This makes sense because the security provisions required for meaningful-use attestation focus on implementing security safeguards but do not address other issues beyond security. While external and accidental breaches are linked to security issues that can be addressed by meaningful use, malicious insider threats are often more closely associated with organizational and personnel issues. Malicious insiders are motivated by many factors, from greed to personnel actions like being passed over for a promotion, not getting an expected bonus, or the threat of being fired. Such human resource factors and surrounding social issues beyond security are likely larger drivers of insider attacks. To approach the malicious insider problem, organizations must address psychological as well as diverse organizational and contextual factors.

11502414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502414.value: While this study provides theoretical and practical insights on security programs, it also has some room for further development. First, our sample is limited to hospitals with complete data from the HIMSS database. The HIMSS database is extensive, but the data are self-reported and missing for some periods. If we add other healthcare providers such as business associates, the results can include the impact on more diverse breaches. Second, our analysis focused on the effects in the first and second year after attestation. However, our results address the core effect of Stage-1 meaningful use and the analysis is not compromised by the adoption of Stage 2 (that started in 2014). Nonetheless, data covering longer periods and advanced stages would provide more insights and offer an opportunity for future research.

11502414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502414.value: Meaningful-use attestation helps healthcare providers establish technical and administrative safeguards. However, without continued security investment and rolling updates, static security certification mechanisms will become less effective due to a dynamic security landscape. A certification regime is a useful strategy for laggards, who have fallen behind standard practice. Maintaining top security requires addressing a complex combination of human and organizational factors along with the most recent hardware and software. Thus, policy makers should encourage holistic tactics.

11502914.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502914.value: 雙文化身份整合的前因及其對中國雙文化員工的創意的影響

11502914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502914.value: Creativity is critical to the competitiveness of firms, and many antecedents of creativity have been studied. A recent stream of research has investigated a novel antecedent, exposure to a second societal culture, and shown that bicultural individuals exhibit higher creativity. Prior research has shown that only some individuals identify with two cultures that they are exposed to, and that biculturals vary in the perceived compatibility of their two cultural identities, known as bicultural identity integration (BII). BII is found to be positively related to creativity, but not much is known about the antecedents of BII and the mechanisms underlying its positive effects. Most prior studies were conducted with Asian Americans, but we focus on Chinese people who have been exposed to Western culture. This group is rising in number because many have studied in the West, and/or have contact with Westerners at work. One objective of this research project is to explore the factors that facilitate Chinese biculturals to develop high BII, namely, perceiving Chinese and Western cultures as compatible. This question is important because to reap the benefit of exposure to Western culture for enhancing creativity, we need to know when and how BII is developed. The second objective is to examine the processes underlying the beneficial effect of BII on creativity to find out when and how BII is conducive to creativity. Three studies are proposed, with the first two focusing on two antecedents of BII: cultural adjustment during a sojourn in the West and intercultural experience at work. Cultural adjustment and intercultural work experience are posited to positively relate to BII through intercultural learning, and these relationships are influenced by moderators. The first study will be a survey with employees, and the second study will employ an experimental design with students to provide causal evidence for our theorizing. The third study will examine the relationship between BII and employee creativity and the mediating mechanisms involved, as well as moderating variables that influence the effects of BII. Our proposal aims to establish the usefulness of BII in the Chinese context and contributes to the development of a theory of BII. It also aims to establish BII as a novel antecedent of employee creativity and shed light on the dynamics involved. The proposed research will provide guidance to organizations to leverage exposure to a foreign culture to increase employee creativity. 創意對企業的競爭力至為關鍵，因此過去的研究檢視了不少影響員工創意的因素，近年來一系列的研究探討了一個新穎的前置變量：跟外國文化的接觸，發現雙文化的人有較高創意，研究更顯示，只有部份接觸兩個文化的人會同時認同他們，而且這些人對這兩個文化的匹配性可能有不同的認知，這概念稱之為＂雙文化身份整合＂（簡稱為＂雙份整合＂），雙份整合跟創意有正向關係，但我們對雙份整合的前因及其提高創意的機制了解不多。過去的研究針對亞裔美國人為主，我們的研究針對跟西方文化有接解的中國人，這類人的數目不斷增加，因為曾在西方生活或在工作上與西方人有接觸的中國人愈來愈多。這個研究項目的一個目標是研究提高雙文化中國人的雙份整合的因素，這是重要的研究目標，因為雙份整合對創意有幫助。第二個目標是檢視雙份整合提高創意的機制，探討雙份整合為甚麼及何時對創意有幫助。 我們提出三個研究，兩個研究探討雙份整合的兩個前因：在西方生活的適應及在工作上的跨文化經驗，我們認為這兩個前因是通過跨文化學習提高雙份整合的水平，這中介關係同時受到調節變量的影響，第一個研究以問卷調查企業員工，第二個研究以大學生為樣本，用實驗方法探討變量之間的因果關係。第三個研究聚焦於雙份整合與員工創意的關係，探討牽涉其中的中介及調節效應。 這研究項目希望確立雙文化身份整合在中國社會的重要性，對建立雙份整合的理論作出貢獻，並証明雙份整合是員工創意的一個新穎前因，釐清牽涉其中的機制，這研究項目更可以為企業如何利用與外國文化的接觸來提高員工創意作出指引。

11503014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503014.value: This project will examine the extent of the tax-sheltering activity (aggressive transfer-pricing activity and tax haven utilization) of Chinese listed firms over the 2006–2010 period, surrounding the introduction of the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in January 2008 and determine whether any significant changes in these tax-sheltering activities follow the GAAR implementation. Although prior studies have examined the effect of stricter tax enforcement on tax sheltering in developed (rule-based) economies (e.g., Hoopes et al. 2012), little is known about whether anti-avoidance rules are effective in deterring tax sheltering in developing (relation-based) economies such as China. This project will provide important insights into whether stricter anti-avoidance tax rules actually constrain tax sheltering in relation-based economies such as China. Further, prior research provides evidence that state ownership and institutional setting (including political connections) impact economic and financial activities of Chinese firms. We extend prior research to determine if ownership structure, political connections, and corporate governance structures impede or exacerbate the effects of the GAAR on the tax-sheltering activities of Chinese listed firms. Our project is timely and important given the rapid increase in foreign investment and trade of Chinese multinational firms, the increased importance placed on resourcing the audits of tax sheltering activities by the State Administration of Taxation in China, and the global recognition that transfer pricing and tax haven utilization have been the primary mechanisms for multinational firms to reduce corporate tax liabilities. Overall, the findings of this project will provide important insights into the nature and extent of international corporate tax sheltering activities adopted by Chinese firms, and changes in these tax-sheltering activities as a direct result of implementation of GAAR.

11503014.label: Realisation of objectives
11503014.value: We have completely achieved our stated research objectives. Regarding the first objective "To assess the tax-sheltering activity (aggressive transfer pricing activity and tax haven utilization) of Chinese listed firms over the 2006–2010 period surrounding the GAAR’s adoption in January 2008, and determine whether any significant changes in tax-sheltering activity by Chinese listed firms follow the GAAR implementation", We examined a sample of 517 Chinese firms over the 2006–2010 period (2,585 firm-year observations) and we find that the GAAR has been effective in deterring tax avoidance in China. The significant reduction in corporate tax avoidance post implementation of the GAAR appears to be a response to the new and stringent tax legislation, and the consolidation of Chinese tax law. Regarding the second research objective "To examine whether ownership structure, political connections and corporate governance structure impede or exacerbate the effect of the GAAR on the tax-sheltering activities of Chinese listed firms", we also observe that the effects of state-ownership, engagement of a Big 4 auditor, and directors with tax expertise on inhibiting corporate tax avoidance were significantly reduced post implementation of the GAAR. To all intents and purposes, the GAAR has created a level playing field in China by moderating the effects of, and substituting for, these various control, monitoring and disciplining mechanisms.

11503014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503014.value: This study examines the effect of the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR), introduced on January 1, 2008, on corporate tax avoidance in China. Based on a sample of 517 Chinese firms over the 2006–2010 period (2,585 firm-year observations), we find that the GAAR has been effective in deterring tax avoidance in China. The significant reduction in corporate tax avoidance post implementation of the GAAR appears to be a response to the new and stringent tax legislation, and the consolidation of Chinese tax law. We also observe that the effects of state-ownership, engagement of a Big 4 auditor, and directors with tax expertise on inhibiting corporate tax avoidance were significantly reduced post implementation of the GAAR. To all intents and purposes, the GAAR has created a level playing field in China by moderating the effects of, and substituting for, these various control, monitoring and disciplining mechanisms.

11503014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503014.value: Future research should consider whether Chinese firms are more active in using tax havens after the General Anti-Avoidance Rule as a tax avoidance strategy. Another potential research avenue is to examine how the Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong responds to the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.

11503014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503014.value: The purpose of this study is to examine the corporate tax avoidance1 activities of Chinese firms to determine whether there were any significant changes in those activities following the implementation of the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in China on January 1, 2008. Although prior research has examined the effect of stricter tax enforcement regulations on corporate tax avoidance in developed (rule-based) economies such as the U.S., little is known about whether anti-avoidance rules are effective in deterring tax avoidance schemes in developing (relation-based) economies such as China. By examining how Chinese firms respond to the implementation of the GAAR in China, this study extends prior research to consider the issue of whether stricter anti-avoidance tax rules constrain corporate tax avoidance in a major relation-based economy. Our findings provide valuable feedback to both government and the tax authorities in China on whether the GAAR achieved its intended purpose in effectively curbing the tax avoidance behavior of Chinese firms and should also be of interest to policy-makers and regulators in other developing (relation-based) economies who are contemplating tax reform in the area of corporate tax avoidance.

11503114.value: 信用違約互換對同行企業的外在性

11503114.label: Project Objectives
11503114.value: Further our understanding of how financial innovations, CDS in particular, affect corporate financial policies. Provide insights on how product market interactions mediate a spillover effect of CDS on non-CDS peer firms.
rows: Further our understanding of how financial innovations, CDS in particular, affect corporate financial policies.
Provide insights on how product market interactions mediate a spillover effect of CDS on non-CDS peer firms.

11503114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503114.value: Credit default swaps (CDS) are among the most influential and controversial financial innovations in the recent decades. As an insurance-type of contract, they facilitate credit risk transfer, thus enhancing the opportunities for both risk-sharing and risk-taking. However, among industrial firms, only a handful of large corporations are referenced by CDS. Is the influence of CDS limited to those CDS-referenced firms only? In the proposed project, we study how CDS written on peer firms affect other non CDS-referenced firms in the same industry. Competing with each other in the product market, peer firms play a prominent role in shaping corporate financial decisions. Because CDS can affect or reflect underlying firms’ actions and characteristics, the trading of CDS on peer firms should have important impact on a firm’s financial policies. First, as a new facility for price discovery, CDS can convey new information about the risk outlook of the peer firms and the industry, which can be useful to guide the firm’s own financial policy. Second, as a new approach to hedging credit risk, CDS can facilitate credit supply to the peer firms, and may therefore affect the firm’s own access to credit. The proposed project investigates the empirical effect of peer CDS on firm leverage and examines the mechanisms that may lead to this effect. Understanding this effect will broaden our view on the interactions between product market competition, financial innovation, and corporate financial policies. It will also contribute to a growing strand of literature that analyzing individual firms’ capital structure decisions no longer in isolation but with connection to its business environment such as product market stake holders and competitors.

11503114.label: Realisation of objectives
11503114.value: I find CDS trading improves firms' product market outcomes because CDS alleviate the agency costs of debt that hinders competitiveness against product market rivals. This main finding furthers our understanding of how financial innovations, CDS in particular, affect corporate performance and strategies. CDS firms are able to compete more aggressively against non-CDS rivals using price cuts and R&D investment. The CDS effect therefore affect the structure of the industry as a whole, in terms of both market share distribution and product prices.

11503114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503114.value: Creditors are less stringent on their borrowers’ near-term profitability when they can buy credit protection from the financial market, freeing borrowers for more aggressive strategies in the product market. We find that, after the inception of credit default swaps (CDS) trading, the reference firms gain product market share from their non-CDS industry rivals. This CDS effect on industry structure is more pronounced for more opaque and financially constrained sectors. CDS firms gain market share by cutting product prices and increasing R&D. This is the first study showing that derivatives trading in the financial market can affect the product market.

11503114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503114.value: If data are available, it is interesting to look at how consumers of firms' products react to CDS firms' market share gains and price cuts.

11503114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503114.value: This research advances our understanding of how financial markets can affect the real economy. The finding that derivatives trading can affect real economic outcomes in the product market, i.e., the producers and consumers, reveals the significance of financial markets. From this research, we can have a more balanced understanding about the pros and cons of the financial market.

11503214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503214.value: 眾籌代表了一種新穎而有效的籌資方式。它是一個基於互聯網的開放式平台幫助小企業與大集團連接網上的個人資助者招募資金（Mollick2013）的方式。因為能夠充分利用大眾在集體評估，選擇，社會和資金籌資的優勢，眾籌從根本上轉變了創業者資金籌集的方式。在2012年眾籌網站已成功在全球籌集了27億美元，並資助了超過一百萬個眾籌項目。籌資總數在2013年也將翻番（Massolution2013）。基於眾籌在經濟增長和社會的顯著貢獻，美國政府最近合法化眾籌，為它的進一步發展鋪平道路。可以預見在某些擁有令人興奮的機遇以及能夠動員龐大人才和創新資源的地區如中國大陸和香港，眾籌將會進一步發展。 關於於眾籌的研究現在仍保持在初級階段。大部分的研究主要是描述性的個案研究和正在撰寫而尚未發別的論文。儘管如此，目前兩個新興的研究主題為未來的眾籌和眾包研究提供了寶貴的資料及參考。第一個研究主題主要採用經濟理論（例如，價格歧視和預購）比較眾籌與傳統籌資方式的有效性（Bellefamme等，2012）。第二個研究主題使用社會心理學（例如，責任擴散效應）和公共產品（例如，替代效應）來解釋資助者的動機和捐款方式如何影響眾籌結果（(Burtch, Ghose, and Wattal 2013; Kuppuswamy and Bayus 2013). 但是，大多數現有的研究只集中於個別資助者和他人的資助行為對他們的資助決定的影響。根據社會影響力，眾包，以及幫助行為的研究文獻，我們的項目旨在建立以及測試一個新的研究框架，並從項目創建者和出資者的角度來看回報眾籌的社會影響和動態過程。我們建議，創業者可以通過獨特的獎勵設計和信息發布策略積極影響出資者的動機，行為和社會交往。重要的是，該項目創建者和資助者之間的社會互動大大影響眾籌策略的有效性，也影響參與者的資助模式，決策，以及當前和後續項目的籌資和社會後果。 該項目將綜合每天從特定的眾籌網站所長期收集的網絡數據和與創業者和資助者的多輪深入的採訪和調查。我們對於眾籌過程所進行的系統而全面的調查結果將有助於眾籌方面的研究文獻，同時也為眾籌項目創建者促進和改善眾籌的效率提供可行的策略。

11503214.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503214.value: One major finding is derived from the recent publciation, which is upported by the GRF. Crowdsourcing and crowdfunding -based new product development (NPD) involves consumers in contributing ideas as ideators in the ideation phase, and providing inputs as cocreators in self-selected subtasks in the product development phase. The novelty of this NPD approach furnishes little understanding about the effect of crowds’ self-select participation into ideation and development subtasks, and this study aims to bridge this gap. This article draws on the attention allocation perspective of online knowledge sharing to identify the domains of ideator expertise based on the types of development subtasks they self-selected to perform as cocreators in prior projects. It separately examines the impact of different domains of ideator expertise (marketing and engineering) and the interaction between ideators’ expertise and cocreators’ inputs on crowdsourcing-based NPD outcomes. Large-scale, longitudinal data from a crowdsourcingbased NPD platform reveal that ideators’ engineering expertise helps convert ideas into final products more than ideators’ marketing expertise. In contrast, ideators’ marketing expertise helps these products achieve more sales than ideators’ engineering expertise. Moreover, final products achieve more sales if ideators’ marketing expertise embedded in initial product ideas is later augmented with either marketing or engineering-related development inputs by crowd cocreators. However, ideas generated by ideators with engineering expertise achieve fewer product sales when those ideas are complemented by more marketing-related development inputs by cocreators. These findings extend crowdsourcing-based NPD theory and furnish insight on managing crowdsourcing-based NPD platforms.

11503214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503214.value: Crowdfunding is still an emerging phenomenon. 11503214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503214.value: Crowdfunding has fundamentally transformed fundraising for entrepreneurs by allowing them harness the power of the crowd in collective evaluation, selection, social, and financial support. There are exciting opportunities to mobilize huge talent pool and innovations resources, will be promising crowd-markets for the further growth and development of crowdfunding. Research with respect to crowdfunding remains in the nascent stage and is composed primarily of descriptive case studies and working papers. Grounded in the literature concerning social influence, crowdsourcing, and helping behaviors, our project develop and examine a framework that captures the social and dynamic process of reward-based crowdfunding from the project creator and funder perspective. We find that entrepreneurs can proactively influence funder motives, behaviors, and social engagement through a unique reward design and information release strategy. Crucially, social interactions between the project creators and funders influence the effectiveness of the strategy and affect participant funding patterns, decisions, and the financial and social outcomes of current and subsequent projects. This project incorporates longitudinal web data retrieved daily from selected crowdfunding sites and manual coding of the collected web data. We provide systematic and holistic investigation of crowdfunding and feasible strategies for project creators to stimulate and improve the process.

11503714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503714.value: For more than a decade, we have been working with large companies such as Philips to manage their worldwide transportation procurement contracts. Due to the recent changes in the shipping environment, we would like to study the optimization problem of assigning lanes and quantities to service providers with total quantity discounts. We named this problem, transportation service procurement with total quantity discount. Existing work includes investigations on different practical business constraints such as limiting the number of winner carriers, committing a minimum quantity of freight to each winner carrier and requiring a minimum number of carriers to provide transportation service. There is a lack of literature on transportation service procurement problem with the total quantity discounts. While there is a growing body of research work on optimization problems with total quantity discounts, none of these are on the transportation service procurement problem that includes the practical business constraints. This work attempts to combine the total quantity discounts in the context of practical business constraints. We will develop an optimization model to characterize the impact of total quantity discount factors, integrating transportation service procurement with practical business constraints, so as to minimize the total cost. To express the total quantity discounts, the model becomes more complex by introducing additional decision variables and constraints. In our research plan, we will develop new solution methods for this problem, including exact methods and heuristics, by applying a suite of optimization techniques with sophisticated analysis on the nature of the model. Extensive experiments on a set of data generated from practice will be carried out to test the different methods. Effective methods will be identified and extended for applications in practice. The contribution of this project is two-fold. First, formulating and solving the transportation service procurement problem that integrates the total quantity discount structure and a set of practical business constraints will produce new analytical tools that enhance best practices in transportation service procurement. The results will be of a great impact to the industry practice. Second, progresses on development of effective solution methods for the model can provide intelligent methods for handling the different business constraints, and identify strong valid inequalities and dedicated procedures for solving problems under a total quantity discount structure, thus contributing to the academic literature in this and related areas. 過去十年以來，我們一直與很多國際大公司如飛利浦進行合作研究，致力於解決如何管理運輸服務採購的優化問題。由於近年來航運環境的變化，我們希望能研究如何在考慮總量折扣的情況下為運輸服務提供商最優化地分配航線和貨物量的問題，即考慮總量折扣的運輸服務採購優化問題。 學術上已知的相關研究成果主要包括研究運輸服務採購問題在不同約束條件如限定運輸服務商的數量、允許最小配額等等下的優化問題。對於考慮總量折扣下如何優化求解，已知文獻中少有全面的解決方案。總量折扣在很多實際採購中有著重要的應用背景，但其在運輸服務採購方面少有人研究。 我們將在研究中同時考慮總量折扣和實際應用中的不同約束條件。我們將對問題建立數學模型，分析總量折扣對研究問題帶來的複雜性，基於考慮不同的應用與商業環境的約束條件，提出有效的算法來求解問題以達到最小化採購成本的目標。為了對總量折扣建模，就必須引入額外的數學變量和約束條件，這將使得研究問題變得更加複雜。依據研究計劃，通過研究該問題的數學模型的特點和應用科學的研究方法，我們將對求解該問題的最優解提出兩種以上的新算法，包括精確算法和啟發式算法。基於來自實際公司的採購數據，我們將通過大量的科學實驗來驗證算法的有效性。最有效的算法和相關的解決方案將會被應用到實際中去。 該項目的貢獻主要集中于兩個方面。第一，在考慮總量折扣和實際約束條件下對該運輸服務採購問題的建模和求解中，依據經驗和成果，一系列有效的分析工具將會被研發和應用，他們能夠為企業在實際中的運輸服務採購中帶來方便，并產生深遠的影響。第二，研究中的階段性成果，包括對各種不同約束條件的建模、減小可行域的有效不等式和對帶有總量折扣結構的一類問題的快速有效的解法等等，將擴充理論體系，為方便以後的學者和研究工作帶來學術貢獻。

11503714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503714.value: In this research, we study a transportation service procurement problem that allows total quantity discounts. The total quantity discounts introduce possibilities to activate more discounts by purchasing more freight volume than demand to achieve cost reduction. An optimization model is developed to characterize the total quantity discount structure and formulate the problem. To express the total quantity discounts, the model introduces additional decision variables and a set of generalized upper bound (GUB) constraints. With sophisticated analysis on the nature of the model, we propose two sets of GUB flow cover inequalities that are effective to the structure consisting of the "more-than-demand'' constraints, capacities, and GUB constraints. Besides, a set-covering integer programming formulation for the problem is also derived and an exact algorithm involving column generation and separating valid inequalities are developed. Extensive experiments on a set of data generated from practice are carried out to evaluate the methods. The results indicate that the new valid inequalities are effective and the exact algorithm is competent to solve problem instances of practical sizes.

11503814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503814.value: Despite numerous studies on technology adoption behavior at the individual level, the underlying mechanisms of technology adoption at the organizational level are still insufficiently researched. Prior literature has identified several exogenous factors, such as technological, organizational, and environmental factors (i.e., the TOE framework), affecting organizational technology adoption. However, it is still not clear how these exogenous factors can evoke internal organizational responses, which in turn enable technology adoption. Furthermore, most of the prior studies on organizational technology adoption are built on the assumption that organizations adopt a new technology with the purpose of improving performance. This assumption may not be universally true as anecdotal evidence suggests that some organizations simply try to demonstrate symbols which convey meanings beyond functional usage, such as peer recognition and image, through technology adoption behavior. To address these two issues, this proposal draws on the upper echelons theory and symbolic action theory to understand the mediating and moderating mechanisms behind organizational technology adoption decision. Specifically, based on the TOE framework, we uncover the mediating mechanism of upper management disposition or overall attitude towards the technology in question by identifying an endogenous factor (i.e. top management support). We also classify technology adoptions into two categories, namely functional and symbolic adoptions, in order to explain their moderating mechanism. The proposed model attempts to extend the original TOE framework and to enhance its applicability and predictive power. A field survey of organizations will be conducted to test the proposed model and hypotheses. To this end, we have gained consent from the senior management of 30 medium and large companies for their participation in our study as pilot sites. We will use the data collected from these companies to refine our survey instrument. We plan to test the model through a survey of users from 300 firms which are considering whether or not to adopt a new IT system. Data will be analyzed using the Partial Least Square technique. By introducing the upper echelons theory and symbolic action theory into the TOE framework, this study will extend the organizational technology adoption literature by shifting the analytic logic from the structuralist perspective to the behaviorist perspective. This paradigm shift will provide a new perspective for organizational technology adoption research. The proposed study will also generate fresh managerial insights to guide future system implementation efforts. 雖然個人層面的技術採用已經有了大量的研究，但組織層面的技術採用機制還沒有被充分的研究。前人的研究指出了幾個影響組織技術採用的外部因素，如技術，組織，和環境因素（即TOE框架）。然而，目前還不清楚這些外在因素如何引起組織內部的反應，繼而影響技術採用。此外，大多數組織技術採用研究是建立在企業採用新技術以提高組織效能為目的這一假設之上的。然而，這個假設可能並不普遍適用。例如，一些組織只是簡單的想通過技術採用來傳達一些象徵意義，比如同行的認可，而非使用其具體的功能。為了解決這兩個問題，本文借鑒了高層梯隊理論（upper echelons theory）和象徵性行為理論(symbolic action theory) 去發掘組織技術採用決策背後的仲介和調節機制。具體而言，基於TOE框架，我們用一個內源性因素（即高級管理層的支持）來反映高層管理人員意向，或者對其正在考慮中的技術的態度。為了揭示它們的調控機制，我們還將技術採用分為兩類，即功能性採用和象徵性採用。我們的模型試圖擴展原有的TOE框架，增強它的適用性和預測能力。我們將會組織一次實地調查來測試提出的模型和假設。 為此，我們已獲得30家中型和大型公司的高級管理人員的認可。他們將作為試點參加我們的研究。我們將使用收集來的資料優化調查問卷。我們計畫調查300家正在考慮採用新的IT系統的公司來驗證我們的模型。數據將採用偏最小二乘法（PLS）分析。通過將高層梯隊理論和象徵性行為理論引入TOE框架，本研究擬通過將分析邏輯從結構主義轉換到行為主義，從而擴展原有的組織技術採用文獻。這一轉變將為組織技術採用研究提供新的視角。該研究還將產生新的管理理念，指導未來的系統實施工作。

11503814.label: Realisation of objectives
11503814.value: The objectives of the project, as stated above, have been fully achieved. In relation to the first objective, the research team reviewed prior literature on organizational technology adoption and theorized based on upper echelons theory to examine the mediating mechanism between the external Technology-Organizational-Environment (TOE) factors and the internal organizational technology acceptance behaviors. Specifically, according to the upper echelons theory, organizational outcomes (in our case, the decision to adopt a technology) are reflections of the top executive’s selective perceptions and interpretations of external cues. We theorized that the exogenous factors under the TOE framework may not necessarily lead to adoption of technology unless these factors are internalized by the top managers who are in charge of the adoption decision. In relation to the second objective, drawing upon symbolic action theory, we examined the moderating mechanism between the external TOE factors and the internal organizational technology acceptance behavior. In particular, beyond the performance-dominant viewpoint, we identified symbolic goals as another purpose that drives organizational technology adoption behavior. Symbolic purpose means that an organization may adopt a technological innovation because the technology adoption behavior can demonstrate certain symbols or signals to the stakeholders of the organization. This signaling effect, in turn, helps the organization to boost legitimacy and obtain access to more resources. We argue that top management’s orientation toward technology adoption (functional vs. symbolic orientation) guides them to respond to the external stimuli differently. We proposed an integrative model that we called Model for Organizational Adoption of Technology (i.e., MOAT). MOAT advances the theoretical understanding on organizational technology adoption in two major ways. First, MOAT extends the TOE framework and its scope of application by opening the ‘black box’ connecting TOE factors and organizational technology adoption, thus improving the explanatory power of the original TOE framework. Specially, the mediating effect can provide a better understanding of why identical firms faced with identical sets of external forces (technological, organizational, and environmental) may produce very different adoption decisions. Second, MOAT identifies how TOE factors demonstrate different roles under the two types of technology adoption orientation, and further articulates the boundary conditions of the TOE framework by taking into consideration the functional vs. symbolic orientation of technology adoption. The model was tested through a field survey of 218 organizations. Overall, the results provide strong support for MOAT and advances the literature on organizational technology adoption. The results also generate interesting insights and useful guidelines for practitioners.

11503814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503814.value: This project yields three important findings and enriches our understanding on organizational technology adoption. First, the model that we developed (called MOAT) extends the Technology-Organizational-Environment (TOE) framework by shifting the analytical logic from structuralist perspective to behaviorist perspective by introducing the upper echelons theory into the organizational technology adoption research. Previous TOE studies focus on the direct effects of TOE factors on technology use by assuming that organizations facing the same external situations should behave similarly. However, prior studies have provided evidence to suggest that external forces have mixed effect on the behavior of organizations. This prompted us to believe that there is a need for a paradigm shift from the structrualist perspective to the behaviorist perspective. Drawing upon the upper echelons theory, we identify the managerial perceptions as the missing link between TOE factors and organizational adoption behavior. Future research on organizational technology adoption should not only explore the context-specific factors in terms of the TOE framework, but also uncover the black box between TOE factors and technology adoption behavior, paying attention to the pivotal role of internal human agents. Second, our study identifies and empirical verifies the mediating role of top management support between the TOE factors and organizational technology adoption. Drawing upon the upper echelons theory, we argue that top management support should be treated as an endogenous variable rather than an exogenous variable. This suggests that future research should reconsider the role of top management support by distinguishing top management support from TOE factors (organizational factors in particular) and by examining its mediating effects between TOE factors and organizational behavior. Third, MOAT articulates the boundary conditions under which different TOE factors work. A premise for previous studies on organizational technology adoption is that organizations adopt technologies to boost their business performance. However, recent studies suggest that organizations may adopt a technology for its symbolic value (e.g., reputation, image, or legitimacy) rather than for its functional value (e.g., performance improvement). Arguably, the previous performance-centric analysis may lose its explanation and predictive power. Drawing upon the symbolic action theory, this study asserts symbolic orientation and functional orientation as two strategic orientations toward adopting a new technology. Therefore, our study serves as a foundation for future research: future organizational technology acceptance research should explicitly recognize the differences in strategic orientations of top managers and explore how these differences can change the decision making mechanisms.

11503814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503814.value: As with any study, this study has several limitations that need to be taken into consideration when interpreting the results. With that, there are also several opportunities for further development of this research. First, our research model was tested using cross-sectional data rather than longitudinal data. Use of cross-sectional data has usually been criticized for unable to firmly establish causality of relationships. We encourage future research to further examine MOAT and the proposed causal relationships using a longitudinal design. Second, the demographics of our sample show that the companies in the manufacturing industry account for about 40% of the entire sample. This may bias our conclusions toward manufacturing companies. Therefore, one possible future development is to conduct another study with more diversified industry sectors. Third, choosing Taiwan as the location for data collection and three special technologies (e.g., social networking, cloud computing and RFID) as the focal technologies, we may limit the generalizability of the conclusions. Validating or extending our research model to a different country and culture may be a potential future research direction. It is also interesting to compare and contrast the technology adoption mechanisms for well-established and used technologies with emerging technologies.

11503814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503814.value: Our results provided several guidelines for managers and policy makers. First, we provides a useful framework for managers to guide their technology adoption decisions. In particular, top management should begin by evaluating the technological context and considering the extent to which a new technology can satisfy the needs for data, collaboration, mobility and timeliness. Second, to ensure the successful implementation of new technologies, IT managers should use different persuasion strategies to gain support from top management. Specifically, technological factors should be stressed for top managements with functional orientation, while environmental factors should be emphasized for top managements with symbolic orientation. However, regardless of the top managements’ technology adoption orientation, the organizational context must be clearly described and outlined to help top managements to understand the organizational readiness for technology adoption. Finally, top managements may decide to adopt a new technology when they are forced to do so or when they find that their competitors do obtain certain benefits after adopting the technology. However, this strategy is not a silver bullet; government agencies and trade associations should recognize that institutional pressures can exert impact on organizational technology adoption only for top managers with symbolic orientation.

11504014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504014.value: Portfolio risk measurement under nested setting has received increasing attention among simulation researchers and practitioners in recent years. Under nested setting, simulation is required to re-evaluate the portfolio value at a future date, making the problem extremely computationally challenging. Portfolio risk measurement under such setting often involves a two-level simulation procedure, in which one first simulates a number of possible scenarios of risk factors up to a future time horizon in the outer level, and then in the inner level evaluates the mark-to-market loss of the portfolio for each outer-level scenario. In this project, we propose an optimal stopping approach in which only one observation is required in the inner-level simulation for each outer-level scenario, thus reducing the computational burden arising from the two-level simulation procedure. In particular, we show that conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of the portfolio can be represented as the optimal value of a stochastic program which involves an appropriately constructed optimal stopping problem. Then various methods in the literature of optimal stopping can be borrowed to estimate CVaR. As a by-product, the approach also leads to an estimate of value-at-risk (VaR). We expect that the optimal stopping approach will serve as a viable tool for portfolio risk measurement problems in practice. In addition to estimation of VaR and CVaR, we plan to investigate its use in portfolio optimization, including mean-CVaR optimization under nested setting, and multistage risk adverse portfolio optimization. It is expected that outputs of this project will provide useful simulation techniques to portfolio optimization. 投資組合風險測量近幾年獲得越來越多的關注，尤其當組合里包含金融衍生品的情況下。在這種嵌套情形下，投資組合在未來一個時間的價值需要被重新模擬，使得這個問題計算上變得極為複雜。一般來說，解決這個問題需要兩層的隨機模擬。外面一層先模擬未來可能的風險因素，然後裡面一層模擬在給定風險因素下去估计投資組合的損失。 在這個研究項目里，我們提出一種最優停時的方法，使得做裡面一層模擬的時候只需要生成一個樣本，從而大大降低計算的難度。我們考慮投資組合的條件風險價值，并證明條件風險價值能夠寫成一個優化問題的最優值，其中這個優化問題是由一個最優停時問題所構造出來的。 我們期望項目所提出的新方法有助於解決現實中的投資組合風險度量問題。此外，作為這個問題的延伸，我們還將考慮在嵌套情形下如何選擇最好的投資組合，以及多階段設定下如何度量投資組合風險。這一系列的問題都將有助於人們更好理解投資組合優化與決策。

11504014.label: Realisation of objectives
11504014.value: We have successfully achieved all the project objectives. We have proposed both lower- and upper-bound algorithms for CVaR estimation under the nested setting. We have provided theoretical supports for the algorithms, in particular, their strong consistency and central limit theorems. Furthermore, we have established a linkage between the CVaR estimation problem and the optimal stopping problem. Implementation issues have also been studied carefully, where we propose different approaches, including least-squares regression, stochastic kriging, and nested simulation, to the construction of the approximating function that serves as an important part of the proposed algorithms. Numerical results show that both the least-squares regression and stochastic kriging may lead to very tight lower and upper bounds. Use of the proposed method in mean-CVaR portfolio optimisation has also been discussed, where the message is mixed. While the drawback is that the lower-bound based mean-CVaR formulation is not convex, the bright side is that it can produce a fast local optimal solution which turns out to be quite close to the global optimal one. We have also studied the estimation of average value-at-risk (AVaR), a multistage extension of CVaR that is time consistent. We have proposed estimators based on a combination of least-squares regression and quantile regression, and analysed the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimator. This is the first work to study computational methods of multistage risk measures, and numerical experiments show that the proposed method works quite well.

11504014.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504014.value: We successfully fulfill all the project objectives. The outcome of the research is summarized as follows. 1. We have developed a simulation method to estimate CVaR efficiently, in which a VaR estimator comes as a by-product. In particular, we develop both lower and upper bounds for CVaR, and provide the theoretical supports. These results are major parts of our working paper "Simulating bounds for conditional Value-at-Risk". An earlier version of this paper gone through two rounds of reviews with Management Science, but unfortunately got rejected. However, the review team gave very positive feedback on the novelty of the method. We are currently revising the paper, and will submit it to Operations Research soon. 2. We have developed a simulation method to estimate conditional average value-at-risk, which is a popular multistage risk measure, and analyzed the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimator. These results are major parts of our working paper titled "Simulating conditional average Value-at-Risk", which is currently under review with INFORMS Journal on Computing. 3. In addition to the above working papers, the project produces two conference papers, titled "Portfolio risk measurement via stochastic mesh" and "A misspecification test for simulation metamodels", respectively, published by the peer-reviewed proceedings of the 2017 Winter Simulation Conference.

11504014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504014.value: We believe that the proposed method can also be extended to deal with convex risk measures, which is a very broad class of risk measures in financial engineering. It is not a trivial extension, as convex risk measures in many cases are solutions to certain stochastic programs. Such cases require much more elaborate analysis. We are currently working on it.

11504014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504014.value: In this project we have studied the estimation via simulation of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), a risk measure widely used in financial industry, in a context when portfolio value reevaluation requires time consuming simulations. We have proposed an efficient method which leads to fast and tight lower and upper bounds for CVaR, which helps to assess the risk within a small time frame for large-scale financial portfolios. This provides an effective tool for daily risk assessment for portfolio managers. We have also proposed efficient simulation methods for estimating conditional average value-at-risk, which is a multistage extension of CVaR. This is the first work that focuses on computational aspects of time consistent risk measures.

11504414.label: Project Objectives
11504414.value: We plan to find the fundamental economic risk(s) that underlie the explanation of the finding of Savor and Wilson (2013) that the overall stock market returns on days with macroeconomic news announcements (henceforth called macro-news days) are much higher than on other days (henceforth called macro-news days). Once these risk(s) have been identified, we aim to use this information to derive novel implications for the variation in the cross section of stock returns between macro-news days and non-macro-news days. We plan to then study whether such implications are supported in the data. If they are supported, we would then have achieved a greater understanding of the link between macroeconomic news releases and asset returns. We also aim to then understand the significance and importance of the identified economic risk(s) in relation to well known, stylized facts regarding the cross section of stock returns such as the value premium and momentum and reversal patterns. We also aim to understand these factors from a production based view in order to understand the identified macroeconomic risk(s) from a different perspective.
