11504414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504414.value: We propose to study the impact of the presence of news release regarding the macro-economy (specifically unemployment, inflation and central bank policy) on stock returns. Most prior research in this area has focused on the study of the impact of the content of such news releases on asset returns. Recent research by Savor and Wilson has shifted the focus to the mere presence of such news releases by showing that the overall stock market returns are much higher on days when such news is released in comparison to other days. The magnitude of this difference in returns is large (approximately 0.10% on a daily basis or nearly 25% on a yearly basis) and both economically and statistically significant. This result is particularly interesting as the release of such news is scheduled months or even years in advance and so investors know whether very much in advance whether such news is going to be released on any particular day. The high level of returns must therefore compensate some important risk as investors would otherwise take advantage of this pattern. In the first part of this project, we therefore aim to study the specific nature of the underlying macro-economic risk that is being compensated by these relatively large returns. This question is of fundamental importance as the specific nature of this risk has not yet been identified in the literature. The identification of this underlying risk(s) will enable us to derive novel implications regarding the structure of stock market returns and its temporal variation with regard to macroeconomic news releases. Such novel implications can then be tested using the data and will thus thus enable a significant advance in the theoretical and empirical understanding of the link between the presence of macroeconomic news and stock returns in general. Preliminary results obtained by us indicate that the consumption risk of stockholders is an important risk that is being compensated on such days. We also derive some novel implications regarding the variation of the cross section of stock returns between such days and other days using this preliminary analysis and verify that they are indeed satisfied in the data. In the second phase of this project, we aim to study this link from the firm's point of view by concentrating on it's production function and constructing a production based macroeconomic asset pricing model using the results of the first part of the project. 我們建議研究宏觀經濟新聞發布（特別是失業率，通脹和央行政策）對股票收益的影響。大多數這方面已有的研究主要集中在新聞的内容對資產收益的影響。Savor and Wilson最近的研究表明有宏观经济新闻发布日子里，股市回報要比没有宏观经济新闻发布的日子要高得多。这种回報差異很大（每天大约0.10%，每年大约25％），並且在經濟上和統計上都非常顯著。因為這樣的消息發布早在數月甚至數年之前就已经安排好了，投资者非常清楚什么时间什么样的宏观经济新闻会被发布，這一差异回报就显得特別有趣。因此，这种高回報一定是賠償一些重要的投资風險，否則投资者就会利用這種模式来套取超额回报。 因此在這個項目的第一部分，我們的目標是研究這些比較大的收益所要彌補的宏觀經濟新闻的風險的具體性質。這種風險的具體性質尚未在文獻中被識別，這個問題是極其重要的。這種風險的識別将使我們能夠推导關於股市回報及其随宏觀經濟新聞的發布而變化的新颖的观点。我们可以随后用市场数据来验证這種新穎的观点。这将会把宏觀經濟新聞和股票收益的關係从理論上和實證上显著向前推进一步。我們所獲得的初步結果表明，股市投资者的消費風險是在這些日子被補償的一個重要風險。基于这些初步的分析，我們也得到并验证了一些關於股票收益在有宏观经济新闻公布的日子和其他日子的变化的一些推论。 在這個項目的第二階段，我們的目標是从企業的角度來研究这种关系。基于該項目第一部分的結果，我们将專注於它的生產函數，構建一个基於产品的宏觀經濟的資本定價模型

11504714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504714.value: A considerable amount of research has been devoted to unit root testing in economic and financial time series. It is generally believed that economic and financial time series such as logarithmic real GDP and exchange rates are non-stationary, with time-varying mean and variance. In economics and finance, the general consensus seems to be that a combination of stochastic and deterministic trends is likely to describe the data well. However, distinguishing between these different types of trends (deterministic, stochastic) is difficult in practice. Recent research has primarily focused on stochastic trends caused by unit roots, and how to distinguish these from deterministic trends. One reason for this is that stochastic trends may have important implications for the formulation of economic models. Another reason is that stochastic trends can result in spurious inference, and hence need to be properly accounted for in order to make valid inference when analyzing multivariate time series. From a practitioner's perspective, standard tests for unit root, such as modifications of the augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test, may be hard to fully comprehend with their unknown finite-sample distributions and complicated limiting distributions. In addition, standard unit root tests are known to be sensitive to the initial condition of the data generating process, and to model misspecifications such as serially correlated (autocorrelated) disturbances, with low power and severe size distortions in finite-samples. This project aims to develop simple (easy to implement, easy to use), parametric and non-parametric (distribution-free), initial condition and autocorrelation robust tests for unit root, whose exact finite-sample distributions can be expressed using standard results from order statistics and non-parametric statistics. In addition, some of the proposed tests are, by design, robust to heavy-tailed samples (or outliers) and to certain forms of heteroskedasticity.

11505114.label: Project Objectives
11505114.value: To study the effects of cost uncertainty and strategic customer behavior on a firm's pricing and production/inventory decisions under different pricing policies. 11505114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505114.value: Just-in-time operations strategy has received a lot of attention in practice and in academia. It allows a firm to reduce inventory holding cost and to capture more savings from learning by doing. However, since customers who expect a cost reduction and hence a future price reduction may wait for a lower price, this kind of strategic waiting directly reduces the firm's initial production quantity and hence the firm's cost saving from learning by doing. This brings doubt to the performance of just-in-time policy in the presence of strategic customers. While pricing strategies such as price commitment have been proposed to alleviate strategic waiting of customers, these strategies usually reduces the firm’s flexibility to respond to updated information about uncertainty. In particular, when future cost is uncertain, a firm may want to have the flexibility to adjust price and production quantity based on the latest cost information. We propose to consider the pricing and production decisions of a firm facing cost uncertainty and strategic customers. In particular, the production cost of a firm decreases in its cumulative production quantity, but the actual cost reduction is uncertain. We first study the case when the firm adopts just-in-time policy and carries no inventory. Our preliminary results suggest that the firm may suffer when the average cost reduction is higher but the firm may benefit when uncertainty is higher. These results are driven by the existence of strategic waiting. In this project, we plan to study the effectiveness of just-in-time policy by analyzing the case when the firm carries inventory. We will further compare different types of cost reduction (external cost reduction in the whole industry vs. internal cost reduction from learning by doing). We will look at the social impact of strategic waiting in the presence of production learning and the role of government intervention. Finally, we will look at the impact on retail competition. The successful completion of the project will contribute to the interface of customer behavior and production/inventory management. Particularly, it will improve our understanding of how strategic waiting affects pricing and inventory strategy. 只是即時操作策略已經收到了很多關注實踐和學術界。它允許企業減少庫存持有成本，並通過做來捕獲學習更多的儲蓄。然而，由於誰想到降低成本，因此未來降價的消費者可能會等待更低的價格，這種直接的戰略等待從做中學降低企業的初始生產量，因此該公司的成本節約。這對於剛剛在一次政策的戰略客戶存在的性能帶來了疑問。雖然定價策略，如價格承諾已經提出來減輕客戶的戰略等待，這些策略通常會減少企業的靈活性，以約不確定性的更新信息作出反應。特別是，當未來的成本是不確定的，企業可能需要有靈活調整基於最新的成本信息，價格和生產數量。 我們建議要考慮的一個公司面臨的成本的不確定性和戰略客戶的定價和生產決策。特別是，企業的生產成本在其累計生產數量減少，但實際降低成本是不確定的。我們首先研究的情況下，當企業採用了剛剛在時間的政策，並進行無庫存。我們的初步結果表明，該公司可能會因為降低平均成本較高，但在不確定性較高的企業可能受益。這些結果是由戰略等候的存在驅動。在這個項目中，我們計劃通過分析情況下，當企業進行清查，研究剛剛在一次政策的有效性。我們將進一步比較不同類型的成本降低（整個行業的外部成本降低與學習，從內部降低成本做）的。我們將著眼於戰略性的等待社會影響的生產學習的存在和政府干預的作用。最後，我們將看看在零售競爭的影響。該項目順利完成，將有助於客戶行為和生產/庫存管理的接口。特別是，這將提高我們的等待是如何的戰略影響定價和庫存策略的理解。

11505114.label: Realisation of objectives
11505114.value: All the objectives have been achieved. First, we have considered the effect of uncertainty and strategic customer behaviour on the firm's pricing and inventory decisions. Our results indicate that, with a higher uncertainty, it is better for the firm not to markdown more leftover inventories to reduce future demand uncertainty. This insight is novel to the existing literatures. Our results also indicate that, when customers are more strategic, it is less likely for the firm to offer discounted sales. The firm will order more when it does not offer discounted sales, and the firm will order less when it offers discounted sales. These results provide answers to the effect of uncertainty and strategic customer behaviour on the firm's pricing and inventory decisions. We have developed a theoretical framework to study the influence of uncertainty on customers' strategic behaviour. Thought theoretical analysis, we obtain the optimal policy of the firm. In particular, we show that the firm should either put all of the leftover inventory on discount or dispose all of it, and the choice depends on the amount of the leftover inventory. In particular, the firm should introduce markdown when the amount of leftover inventory is higher than a certain threshold, and dispose all otherwise. These results provide recommendations to the firm to design its pricing and inventory policies. Due to the final model setup, it is more appropriate to compare static and dynamic policy rather than studying the effectiveness of just-in-time strategy. As such, we compared the static and dynamic policy. Our results indicate that the firm incurs substantial loss by adopting the static policies. Specifically, the average loss of efficiency across the 4000 testes instances is 1.7% and 12.4% respectively for two different types of static policies. In the worst case scenario, the loss of efficiency can be as high as 77.9%.

11505114.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505114.value: In Hu, Shum and Yu, we formulate and analyze a novel model on a firm’s dynamic inventory and markdown decisions for perishable goods. We consider a dynamic stochastic setting, where every period consists of two phases, clearance phase and regular-sales phase. In the clearance phase, the firm decides how much to order for regular sales, as well as whether to markdown some (or all) of the leftover inventory from the previous period that will be disposed otherwise. Since strategic consumers may buy the product during clearance sales for future consumption, markdown may cannibalize future sales at regular price. Hence, the firm needs to make a trade-off between product spoilage and intertemporal demand substitution. We show that the firm should either put all of the leftover inventory on discount or dispose all of it, and the choice depends on the amount of leftover inventory from the previous period. In particular, the firm should introduce markdown when the amount of leftover inventory is higher than a certain threshold, and dispose all otherwise. We also conduct numerical studies to further characterise the optimal policy, and to evaluate the loss of efficiency under static policies when compared to the optimal dynamic policy. In Lu et al., we study the value of information sharing in the presence of either or two types of information errors, source error and transmission error. In particular, when information is shared, the manufacturer may use both the shared demand information and the retailer's order quantity to make decisions, or she may rely solely on the shared demand information and disregard the retailer's order quantity when doing forecasting. We analyze the values of information sharing for both settings, and characterize the lowest-cost information sharing strategy for the manufacturer. Our results suggest that transmission error and source error have signicantly dierent impacts on the value of information sharing and the manufacturer's optimal strategy.

11505114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505114.value: In this project, we only consider products with short lifetime. In particular, we assume that the lifetime of the product is only one period. Although this is true for bakery products and certain products in the grocery stores, there are other products that are perishable but yet have longer lifetimes. To extend our model to the products with lifetimes of more than one period, the dimension of state space has to be increased to specify the amounts of inventory that are going to expire at different points of time in the future. This definitely creates a technical challenge for the extension. Another possible extension is to incorporate a fixed operating cost for markdown sales. It is straightforward to see that the bang-bang policy remains optimal with such a fixed cost in the single-period setting. Incorporating the fixed cost in the dynamic model, however, will introduce additional technical complexity to the dynamic program, and is potential direction for further development.

11505114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505114.value: We examine a firm’s dynamic inventory and markdown policy for perishable products when consumers are strategic. Thus, sales at the discount price may cannibalise future demand at the full price. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first stochastic and dynamic inventory model facing strategic customer behavior with joint ordering and discounting decisions. The technical challenge is that the single-period profit is neither concave nor convex, but quasiconvex in the amount of leftover inventory to mark down. Despite the lack of existing results on the preservation of this kind of property in dynamic programming, we are able to characterize the firm’s optimal policy with the use of a transformation technique. Our results suggest that, the firm should either put all leftover inventory on discount or dispose all leftover inventory without introducing any discount. In particular, the firm should introduce markdown if and only if the amount of leftover inventory is high. Furthermore, the firm should reduce the quantity ordered for sales at the full price, whenever it offers a discount. In addition, the loss of efficiency from adopting static policies in comparison to a dynamic policy can be very significant.

11505314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11505314.value: 组织间关系中的信任困境与复杂管制

11505314.label: Project Objectives
11505314.value: We explore dependence imbalance as the main driving factor of firm trust ambivalence. We argue that as dependence deepens, the more dependent organization becomes less concerned about its partner’s competence as the partner possesses the capabilities and resources it is dependent upon for its desired goals (Emerson, 1962; Pfeffer & Salancik, 1978); the firm becomes more concerned about its partner’s goodwill as the partner’s power and behavior are outside its purview and control (Lieberman, 1981; Sheppard & Sherman, 1998). Thus, trust ambivalence arises from such dependence imbalance. We theorize that firm governance complexity is a function of trust ambivalence. Drawing on Lewicki et al.’s (1998) classification of trust ambivalence, we develop a corresponding classification of firm governance complexity that distinguishes between trust-enabling governance and distrust-mitigating governance and argue that a higher level of trust ambivalence gives rise to a more complex governance combination to ensure the full production of trust between organizations. To add richness to our theory, we also look at trust ambivalence beyond the dyadic perspective to explore whether the network embeddedness would moderate the relationship between trust ambivalence and governance complexity. We aim to publish our research in top-tiered marketing/management journals such as Journal of Marketing, Academy of Management Journal or Strategic Management Journal.

11505314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505314.value: 尽管信任是组织合作的重要前提，但组织间信任的产生是很困难的。这不仅因为信任产生成本高昂，更因为可信任因素的不完整性。譬如，中方经理信任其西方合作者的技术能力，但不信任他们转让技术的善意。西方经理信任其中方合作者的社会资本但不信任他们分享关系的善意。在这种信任困境下，经理人能信任他们的合作伙伴吗？不能。因为某些可信任因素缺失并导致高感知信任风险。那么，经理人如何才能信任他们的合作伙伴呢？或者说，他们如何才会愿意承担信任风险呢？ 本项研究致力于探索组织间合作中在信任因素缺失条件下信任产生机制。具体而言，我们探索以下研究问题：1）什么导致组织间信任困境？2）在某些信任因素缺失条件下，如何设计组织间管制机制以便克服由于信任因素缺失导致的感知风险。为此，我们定义组织间信任困境为在信任因素维度上信任与不信任并存。信任是指基于人们对其合作伙伴可信任因素正面预期之上愿意承担风险的意愿；不信任是指基于人们对其合作伙伴可信任因素负面预期之上进行戒备的倾向。我们认为，组织间依赖的不平衡，是组织间信任困境产生的主要驱动因素。我们区分两类组织管制机制：不信任减轻管制与信任促进管制。我们认为，为了保证组织信任产生，两种管制机制必须合并使用形成复杂管制机制形态。

11505314.label: Realisation of objectives
11505314.value: We set four major goals for this project: We explore dependence imbalance as the main driving factor of firm trust ambivalence; we theorize that firm governance complexity is a function of trust ambivalence; we explore whether the network embeddedness would moderate the relationship between trust ambivalence and governance complexity; we aim to publish our research findings in top-tier marketing/management journals. We believe we have achieved our first three objectives in a satisfactory way. Through reorganizing several bodies of literature, we deduced our conceptual model that specified that dependence imbalance function to result in trust ambivalence between firms in business cooperation, trust ambivalence affect the degree firms choose complex governance modes, and network embeddedbess moderates the relationships between dependence imbalance and trust ambivalence, and between trust ambivalence and governance complexity. Our data drawn from 238 usable matched channel dyads between US supplier and Chinese distributors supported our research hypotheses. We are currently revising our manuscript to be submitted to Journal of Marketing, one of the top-tier journals in marketing, for possible publication.

11505314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505314.value: Trust between firm is difficult to produce because of missing trustworthiness such as goodwill and/or competence, leading to trust ambivalence. This study examines the major driving force of trust ambivalence between firms for the first time and proposes that a combination of different governance modes should be used to address trust ambivalence. We find that dependence imbalance between firms determines the degree to which firms may use complex governance because of trust ambivalence. Cross-dimensional trust ambivalence functions as the mediating mechanism between dependence imbalance and governance complexity. Specifically, he higher the level of unilateral dependence, the higher the level of governance complexity; the higher the level of unilateral dependence, the higher the level of cross-dimensional trust ambivalence; the higher the level of cross-dimensional trust ambivalence, the higher the level of governance complexity; cross-dimensional trust ambivalence mediates the relationship between dependence and governance complexity. We also find that network embeddedness weakens the mediating relationship among dependence, cross-dimensional trust ambivalence, and governance complexity.

11505314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505314.value: Future studies may further explore trust ambivalence from a dyadic perspective. Because of the difference between firms in terms of their values, business environments, and boundary spanners, trust perception may vary from each side, which leads to asymmetric trust perceptions. Such perception asymmetry may in turn leads to asymmetric ambivalence, resulting in governance mismatch between firms. Future studies may also explore additional boundary conditions of trust ambivalence. Dependence may be further classified into resource dependence and lock-in dependence and examine their effect on trust ambivalence respectively.

11505314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505314.value: Firms cooperate to gain business success. In order to cooperate effectively, firm must trust each other. However, firms are challenged by being hard to find a good cooperative partner because no firm exists with both goodwill and competence. Typically, firms find their partner to be either lacking goodwill or competence; so they are struggling with imperfect partners in business cooperation. Without trust, firm are unwilling to take full risk in business cooperation. This study investigate such trust ambivalence in firms' choice of governance strategies. We find that dependence imbalance between firms is one of the major factors that result in firms' trust ambivalence, which in turn determines firms' governance choice. We also find, doing business in a network can mitigate firms' trust ambivalence.

11505714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11505714.value: 關係，知識獲取，和制度環境

11505714.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11505714.value: Prof Yang, Haibin Mr Zhong, Weiguo

11505714.label: Project Objectives
11505714.value: We distinguish between business ties and political ties because they have differing impacts on a firm’s performance. This study compares and contrasts these two types of managerial ties and examines their respective impacts on knowledge acquisition. We argue that it is not the managerial ties per se but the knowledge acquisition through utilization of managerial ties that affects firm performance. We bridge the micro-macro link by testing a mediation model. Specifically, knowledge depth and knowledge breadth serve as mediators that underlie the intervening process between managerial ties and firm performance. We surmise that the effects of managerial ties on knowledge acquisition are contingent upon the institutional environment, and we examine two important institutional factors—legal system ineffectiveness and official arbitrariness—that may moderate a firm’s strategies for using managerial ties and affect the outcome of knowledge acquisition. This research provides implications for doing business in transition markets such as China. It aims to show what specific resources (e.g. knowledge) firms can acquire by using their business or political ties and how they can use their ties more effectively given China’s institutional environment.

11505714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505714.value: Managers cultivate interpersonal ties to facilitate inter-firm resource acquisition and collaboration. Managerial ties in China— both business ties (ties with partner firm managers) and political ties (ties with government officials)—help firms in various ways. A firm’s managerial ties reflect a micro-macro link in which personal connections serve as an alternate mechanism that complement weak market institutions and exert a powerful influence on firm outcomes. One unresolved puzzle is how managerial ties, a micro-level construct, contribute to performance, a macro-level phenomenon. Specifically, what benefits accrue from business and political ties? Does the institutional environment alter the impact of managerial ties on resource acquisition? How do the different types of resources obtained by the firm affect its performance? This research aims to address three theoretical gaps in the literature. First, a fine-grained approach to examining different types of managerial ties is critically needed. Business ties and political ties are fundamentally different and thus offer firms distinctly different resources. Drawing on a knowledge-based view, this study proposes that business ties are used quite differently from political ties in the acquisition of external knowledge. In addition, a firm’s institutional environment, as reflected in legal system ineffectiveness and official arbitrariness, moderates the impact of managerial ties on knowledge acquisition. Second, it is still unclear how firms utilize managerial ties to achieve desired outcomes. We propose that knowledge acquired through managerial ties—particularly knowledge depth and knowledge breadth—mediates the influence of managerial ties on performance. Third, prior research has mainly adopted a focal firm approach to investigating the role of managerial ties. We integrate the dyadic nature of managerial ties, looking at interactions between partners in a dyad. This study will examine dyadic supplier-distributor relationships in China. Chinese suppliers and distributors have deeply embedded interpersonal relationships, and firms rely on these managerial ties for external knowledge and resources. China’s changing market and evolving institutional environment provide an ideal context to examine our theories. We will collect dyadic survey data (i.e., from both suppliers and distributors in dyadic relationships) and additional secondary data to test the hypotheses. 經理人培養人際關係是為促進企業間的資源獲取和協作。在中國，關係--包括商務關係（與夥伴公司經理的關係）和政治關係（與政府官員的關係）--在以各種方式幫助公司。一個企業的關係反映微觀與宏觀的對接，其中的人脈關係作為可選擇的機制補充了薄弱的市場制度，對企業的業績發揮著巨大影響。 一個尚未解決的問題是，關係這個微觀層面的因素，如何貢獻業績，這個宏觀層面的現象。具體而言，在商業和政治的關係中可以汲取什麼樣的好處？制度環境能否改變關係對資源獲取的影響？企業獲得的不同類型的資源如何影響其業績？ 本研究旨在解決文獻理論中的三個不足。首先，我們迫切需要使用一種精細的方法來研究不同類型的關係。商業關係和政治關係存在著根本上的不同，因而也為企業提供明顯不同的資源。從知識型的角度來看，本研究提出：商業關係在從外部獲取知識的使用中與政治關係有著很大不同。此外，企業的制度環境的弊端，體現在法律制度的無效性和官員的隨意性上，削弱了關係對知識獲取的影響。其次，企業如何利用關係實現預期效果目前尚不明晰。我們認為通過關係獲得的知識，尤其是知識深度和知識廣度，傳導著關係在業績上的影響。第三，以往的研究主要根據核心企業來研究關係的作用。我們整合關係的二元性，著眼於兩個合作夥伴之間的互動。 本研究將探討在中國的供應商 - 分銷商二元關係。中國的供應商和分銷商已深嵌入人際關係當中，公司依賴於這些關係的外部知識和資源。中國不斷變化的市場和不斷發展的制度環境為我們研究理論提供了理想的背景。我們將收集雙向的調查數據（即供應商和分銷商的二元關係）和額外的輔助數據來測試該假設。

11505714.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505714.value: Our findings suggest that the different resources and information accessed via business versus political ties distinctively influence firm innovation behaviors within a transition economy. These findings seem to be consistent with the marketing discipline research where scholars have recognized that firms with a market orientation will become more attentive to changes in customers and competitors by introducing new products (Jaworski and Kohli, 1993; Slater and Narver, 1999). In contrast, strong political ties may motivate firms to exploit the fleeting benefits of institutional resources and sacrifice their exploration in market and technologies. This finding echoes the work of Sun et al. (2010), which finds that political embeddedness may generate a negative effect as the market becomes increasingly liberalized in transition economies, significantly decreasing firms’ abilities to engage in exploratory initiatives. Second, our mediation model represents a new angle examining the relationship between relational ties and firm performance. Prior research has primarily focused on the direct effects of relational ties (e.g., Sheng et al., 2011), falling short of revealing the underlying mechanisms that must be explicitly modeled rather than taken for granted in network research (Lee, 2010). Although some studies have contributed to a moderation model of this relationship, a mediation model is critically needed in order to disentangle these internal mechanisms rather than only investigating contextual variables. Our focus on the types of innovation as key mediators has profound ramifications for the organizational innovation literature, highlighting the antecedents and consequences of different innovation activities Third, our study also contributes to the prior literature’s debate on whether or not the value of relational ties increases with the degree of market competition (Boisot and Child, 1996; Peng, 2003; Danis, Chiaburu, and Lyles, 2010). Our moderated mediation approach suggests that competitive industry intensity will increase the value of business ties, while decreasing the value of political ties in a transition economy like China. Competitive intensity differentially affects the mechanisms from business or political ties to firm performance via certain intervening factors. This approach further clarifies the conditions under which certain mediation effects hold, and highlights the relative importance of resources under different external environments (Priem and Butler, 2001). It also indicates that the relationship between relational ties and performance is much more subtle and complex than previously thought.

11505714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505714.value: Since many large and complex transition economies (notably Brazil, Russia, India, and China) demonstrate a high degree of heterogeneous national environments (Chan, Makino, and Isobe, 2010), it will be interesting to examine this theoretical model within different national settings with varying cultures, norms, and institutional developments. In addition, different transition economies may follow different paths when transitioning into market economies. For example, in some countries such as the Ukraine and Russia where regime changes occurred via a rapid collapse of the political system or the defeat of the dominant political party in elections, connections with pre-reform officials or institutions may actually backfire rather than enhance the competitive advantages of local firms (Siegel, 2007). Our arguments can be applied reasonably well in contexts where the regime change has a low intensity (Walder, 2003).

11505714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505714.value: This study explores how relational ties affect firm performance via an intervening process of innovation. Drawing on the relational ties literature and the resource-based view, we differentiate between two types of relational ties (business versus political ties) and investigate how firm innovation (exploration versus exploitation) mediates relational ties and firm performance in two unique pathways. Survey data from two industries (semiconductor and pharmaceuticals) in China suggest that a firm’s business ties with buyers, suppliers and competitors are more related to exploratory innovation, while its political ties with government agencies are more related to exploitative innovation. Interestingly, competitive intensity demonstrates distinct moderating effects on the above mediation models.

11506914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506914.value: This project investigates how client political connections affect auditor reporting decisions in the United States. Following Goldman et al. (2009), we define a firm as politically connected if one or more of its directors had held a political position. We posit that auditors may be more likely to issue going-concern opinions to politically connected clients, for two reasons. First, politically connected firms may receive more media coverage, which may cause auditors to be more conservative in their audit reporting decisions for such clients (the visibility argument). Second, political connections may increase connected firms’ business risk, which in turn may increase the litigation risk faced by auditors (the risk argument). While these two arguments have similar predictions, their implications for audit quality differ. The visibility argument suggests that auditors are unduly affected by press coverage on client firms and therefore are over-conservative in auditing politically connected clients. As such, a higher likelihood of issuing going-concern opinions to such clients may not suggest higher quality audits. In contrast, the risk argument suggests that auditors recognize that politically connected firms have higher failure risk, and are therefore more likely to issue warning signals, i.e., going-concern opinions to investors. In the latter case, higher probability of going-concern opinion issuance represents higher audit quality. We design four additional tests to evaluate the relative importance of the two arguments discussed above. First, we examine whether political connection effects on audit opinions vary between election and non-election years. Second, we examine whether auditors are more likely to issue going-concern opinions to politically connected firms when events such as delisting, bankruptcy, or shareholder lawsuits are absent in the near future. Third, we directly compare press coverage between politically connected and matched, non-connected firms to determine whether politically connected firms indeed receive more attention from the media. Finally, we investigate whether politically connected firms are more likely to go bankrupt, be delisted, or be sued by shareholders in the near future. The findings from this work will help to explain how political factors and public attention on client firms affect auditor judgment and decision making in the U.S. The auditing literature mostly examines how political factors shape auditor behavior in international settings (e.g., Guedhami et al., 2013) or developing countries (e.g., Wang et al. (2008) and Chan et al. (2006) for the Chinese case). Our work extends this literature by providing U.S. evidence. 本项目主要研究在美国审计客户的政治关系对审计师发表审计意见的影响。如果一个审计客户有任何董事之前担任政治职务，我们则定义这个客户拥有政治关系。 我们认为审计客户有政治关系时，审计师更可能发表有保留审计意见。原因有两个。第一，有政治关系的公司会受到更多的媒体关注，而媒体关注会导致审计师更加保守谨慎。第二，政治关系可能增加公司的商业风险，从而加大审计师的诉讼风险。 虽然上述两个原因都会导致审计师倾向于发表有保留审计意见，它们对审计质量的影响是不一样的。如果审计师是因为有政治关系的客户有更高的媒体曝光度而发表有保留审计意见，那么审计师就是过度保守；他们发表有保留意见也就不等于说他们提供了高质量的审计。如果审计师是因为觉察到有政治关系的客户有更高的商业风险从而发表有保留意见，那么他们发表的有保留意见就是给投资者提供了一个有用的警告信号。从这个意义上说，他们提供了高质量的审计。 我们设计了四个检验来评估每种解释的可能性。第一，我们把样本期分为选举年和非选举年，然后比较审计师发表有保留意见的倾向是否有差异。第二，我们根据审计后一年公司是否发生退市、破产或股东诉讼把样本分为两部分，然后分别比较有政治关系和没有政治关客户收到有保留意见的概率。第三，我们也直接比较有政治关系和没有政治关系客户的媒体关注度。第四，我们直接比较有政治关系和没有政治关系客户未来破产，退市，或被股东起诉的概率。 这个研究项目的发现将有助于人们理解在美国政治因素和公众关注度受否对审计师的判断和审计意见产生影响。现有文献主要是利用发展中国家的数据来研究政治因素对审计师的影响。我们的项目提供了美国的证据，从而拓展了审计文献。

11507214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507214.value: Using audit firms’ transparency reports in Korea, the proposed research investigates whether and how audit firm characteristics influence audit firm client portfolio management decisions. More specifically, the study examines the following two research questions: (1) do audit firms’ financial performance, governance, and human resource quality affect risk avoidance behavior in audit firms’ portfolio management; and (2) if so, what are the types of risk that is affected? Effective risk control and management are essential to the success and sustainability of audit firms. A study of audit firm portfolio management decisions is also important to regulators and investors because audit firms’ effective quality control increases the confidence of investors in using financial statements. This proposed research examines how partner experience, audit firm profitability, and audit firm board size moderate the effect of different types of risk facing audit firms on client acceptance and retention decisions and makes the following contributions: First, it enhances our understanding of audit firm client portfolio decisions. Although prior research examines the risk profiles of client portfolios between large versus small audit firms, little is known for the effect of audit firm characteristics other than audit firm size on client portfolio decisions. The proposed research takes advantage of the availability of detailed data from the transparency reports of audit firms to provide new insight into audit firm client portfolio decisions. Second, the data of the study include privately held client firms as well as publicly traded firms and enable us to analyze audit firm portfolio management in a more comprehensive manner. The results of the study will be useful in helping regulators, audit committee members, and investors better understand audit firms’ risk control and monitoring. 本研究计划使用韩国审计事务所的透明性报告，对审计事务所的特征是否影响以及如何影响审计事务所的客户组合管理决策进行研究。具体而言，本研究将探讨以下两个问题：（1）审计事务所的财务业绩、治理情况和人力资源的质量是否影响审计事务所的组合管理；以及（2）如果是，受到影响的风险类型有哪些？有效的风险控制及管理对于审计事务所的成功及可持续发展至关重要。由于审计事务所有效的质量控制能提高投资者使用财务报表的信心，因此研究审计事务所的组合管理决策对于监管机构和投资者而言也相当重要。本研究将探讨合伙人的经验、审计事务所的盈利能力和审计事务所的董事会规模如何缓和审计事务所面临的不同类型的风险对于其客户接受与保留决策的影响，并且将有以下贡献：首先，加深我们对于审计事务所的客户组合决策的理解。虽然以往的研究对于大事务所和小事务所的客户组合的风险情况已有探讨，但对于审计事务所规模大小之外的其他特征对于客户组合决策的影响却少有涉及。本研究将充分利用审计事务所透明性报告中的详细数据为审计事务所客户组合决策提供新的解读。其次，本研究的数据包括上市以及非上市的客户公司，使得我们能够从更全面的视角分析审计事务所的组合管理。我们的研究结果将能帮助监管机构、审计委员会成员和投资者进一步了解审计事务所的风险控制和监督。

11507214.label: Realisation of objectives
11507214.value: My project was to examine the effects of audit firm characteristics on audit firms' client portfolio management decisions. Specifically, the project was to investigate the effects of the following audit firm characteristics---the quality of human resource, financial performance, and audit firm governance on audit firms' client acceptance and retention decisions. In implementing the project, I have changed the framework in which my research questions are examined. Rather than investigating audit firms' client portfolio management decisions, I have focused on audit firms' organizational performance. The logic is that the outcome of client portfolio decisions will be ultimately reflected in audit firms' performance. A primary reason for this change is because I couldn't find meaningful and consistent relationships between audit firm characteristics and client portfolio management decisions. In so doing, I have focused on one of audit firm characteristics, employee turnover, and its effect on various aspects of audit firms' organizational performance. Because of this change, I cannot directly address the extent to which project objectives have been achieved. Instead, I have explored the following three research questions: 1) Is employee turnover related to organizational performance in public accounting firms?; 2) Does partner turnover have a greater impact on organizational performance than professional staff turnover?; 3) Does the turnover-performance relationship differ between larger audit firms and smaller audit firms? Using a unique dataset of audit firm transparency reports, I find that 1) employee turnover negatively affects the organizational performance of accounting firms; 2) partner departures have a greater impact on audit firm performance than professional staff turnover; and 3) the negative turnover-performance relationship is found only for non-Big audit firms.

11507214.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507214.value: We examine the effect of employee turnover on organizational performance in public accounting firms. We find that the overall turnover rates are negatively associated with various measures of organizational performance of audit firms. When we separate the overall turnover into partner turnover and professional staff turnover, we find that partner turnover has a stronger impact on organizational performance. When we analyze the moderating effect of audit firm size in the turnover-performance relationship, we find that employee turnover impacts negatively organizational performance for Non-Big 4 audit firms, while there is no association between turnover and audit firm performance for Big 4 audit firms. In addition, we find that partner turnover at the audit firm level reduces audit effort and audit quality at the engagement level.

11507214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507214.value: There is room for further developing our research. For example, we may incorporate audit partner characteristics into our analyses. For this, we are going to collect data on audit partner characteristics and engagement resource (i.e., time and human resources) allocations to examine whether audit partner characteristics such as experience and ownership units moderate the turnover-performance relationship.

11507214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507214.value: Employee turnover is a concern for any organization. We examine the effect of employee turnover on organizational performance in public accounting firms. Our findings are summarized as follows: 1) employee turnover adversely affects productivity and financial performance of accounting firms; (2) partner turnover has a greater impact on audit firms' performance than professional staff; and (3) the negative relationship between employee turnover and performance is found in non-Big 4 audit firms. To our knowledge, our study is the first to examine the consequences of employee turnover in public accounting firms using archival data. Our findings are of interest to audit firms and regulators. Our study highlights the importance of managing employee turnover effectively since audit firms' performance is adversely affected by employee turnover. Our study is also relevant to the ongoing discussions on audit quality indicators (AQIs). Our study provides evidence that a firm-level AQI influences engagement-level audit outcomes---audit effort and audit quality.

11507314.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507314.value: In this project, we study production control of the food processing supply chain. We consider the type of supply chains where the raw materials are perishable while the end product is non-perishable. To investigate the optimal production policy to avoid perishability. We formulate the problem as a dynamic programming problem. By adopt the L-convexity and its preservation under the minimization operator tailored for our problem, we are able to show various monotone properties of the optimal production quantity with respect to the state variables. In general, based on the L-convexity we find that the optimal production quantity is more sensitive to sooner to expire items. However, when the expiration cost is high, then a simple nested echelon base stock policy is optimal: there is an echelon base stock level for items with each age, then the age is larger, then the echelon base stock level is higher. We are able to do so by show a new preservation property of decomposition under the minimization operator. We also numerically test some of the proposed heuristics. We also investigate the dynamic pricing and ordering strategies in the presence of advertisements (the related paper is accepted by JSSSE). Our findings shed light on how to manage perishable food processing supply chains to avoid too much costly and environmentally detrimental waste.

11507314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507314.value: We only consider two-echelon supply chains. It is interesting to consider multiple stage supply chains. We also need additional efforts to complete the numerical studies for the effectiveness of the proposed heuristics.

11507314.value: In this project, we study production control of the food processing supply chain. We consider the type of supply chains where the raw materials are perishable while the end product is non-perishable. We investigate the optimal production policy to avoid perishability. In general, we find that the optimal production quantity is more sensitive to sooner to expire items. However, when the expiration cost is high, then a simple nested echelon base stock policy is optimal: there is an echelon base stock level for items with each age, then the age is larger, then the echelon base stock level is higher. When the product is still perishable, we also explore the optimal dynamic pricing and production strategy in the presence of advertisement.

11507514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507514.value: 社会互动包含正向的和负向的互动。这些互动是否影响以及如何影响人们的行为，成了重要的研究课题。我们的研究特别关注对个人消费行为的影响，比如说当两人建立了正向的或负向的关系后，他们是否会买更相同的产品还是更不同的产品。 虽然很多研究已经探讨了正向的关系（例如朋友，粉丝，合作者等），但是很少有人研究负向的关系（例如敌人，对手，竞争者）。在营销领域，一个普遍的发现是，当两人建立正向的关系后，他们会选择更加相似的产品和服务。至于负向关系的影响，就不那么清楚。有可能负向互动的人们（比如对手）会选择不同而非相同的产品。或者，消费模式会更复杂，互动的影响可以受到产品类型的影响。即便是正向的关系，也不一定总是导致消费相同的产品。比如，合作者可能会选择不同的功能性产品进行互补，或者选择不同的享乐性产品来保持他们的独特性。类似的，负向关系的人可能选择同样的功能性产品但是质量上比他们的竞争对手更高。 我们的研究试图在理论和实证上填补文献中的这个缺口。对于负向关系，最近在别的领域有些研究（比如组织行为学），但是定义和测量有很多种方法。很多概念曾被用来代表负向关系（敌人，竞争者）但他们在本质上有不同，也会导致不同的结果。我们希望对负向关系这一概念能进行更准确的描述，并区分不同类型的该关系的效果。 实证方面，我们将采用一套新颖的数据来研究我们的问题，数据来自一款大型的多人在线角色扮演游戏。这是因为传统的调查方法在收集负向关系的数据时会有实际的困难。对一般受访者，报告他们的负向关系可能是一个敏感的话题。在我们的游戏数据中，玩家以多种方式互动（交友，任务合作，战斗，竞争，交易），提供了大量的正向和负向关系。所有这些关系和他们导致的结果（比如消费）都被系统客观的测量和记录，使得我们能更准确的评估各种社会影响。另外，游戏中不仅含有功能性产品（比如装备，药），也有享乐性物品（如服装和装饰品），让我们能够比较不同类型产品的消费模式。此项研究的结果将有助于营销人员改进他们的产品推广策略，确定为客户定制的最佳程度，以及优化产品的多样性。

11507514.label: Realisation of objectives
11507514.value: For objective 1: We have conducted a comprehensive literature review and clarified the concepts of various negative relationships. For objective 2: We have prepared a working paper. In this paper, we focus on one type of negative relationship (i.e., competitive relationship). In particular, we examine the scenario in which male consumers compete with female consumers. The competitive relationship may have differentiate effects on the behavior of male and female, such that male may become more aggressive while female may become more submissive. We discuss how these effects may affect people’s competition performance and the corresponding marketing implications. For objective 3: We have examined the effects of some moderating factors. For example, in many economic and business interactions, consumers may create their own virtual identity which may or may not be consistent with their true identity. We examine how the virtual and true identity jointly affect the ways by which people interact. For objective 4: We have written a paper regarding how people perform in a positive relationship (i.e., group work). This paper is just accepted by the Journal of Business Research. In addition, we have also published a paper regarding the temporal pattern of consumers’ propensity to build positive relationship (i.e., friendship) with strangers. We originally planned to also include product type as a moderating factor, but we were not able to do so because of the difficulty to obtain product-related data from the company.

11507514.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507514.value: We generated three papers from this project. First, we have reviewed the literature and clarified the concepts of various negative relationships. We then prepared a working paper that focuses on one type of negative relationship, namely competitive relationship. We examine the scenario in which male consumers compete with female consumers. Our findings show that the competitive relationship has differential effects on the behavior of male and female. In particular, males become more aggressive while females become more submissive. We discuss how these effects affect people’s competition performance and the marketing implications. We have examined the effects of some moderating factors. For example, in many economic and business interactions, consumers may create their own virtual identity which may or may not be consistent with their true identity. We examine how the virtual and true identity jointly affects the ways in which people interact. We find that both true identity and virtual identity can lead to stereotype effects and virtual identity does not have a priming effect as suggested. Second, we have published a paper regarding how people perform in a positive relationship (i.e., group work). Third, we have published a paper regarding the temporal pattern of consumers’ propensity to build the positive relationship (i.e., friendship) with strangers. The findings show that people have higher propensity to establish the positive relationship at night than during daytime. This result has implications for marketers to determine the timing of socializing activities among consumers.

11507514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507514.value: We originally planned to include product purchase into the analysis, but we were not able to do so because of the difficulty to obtain product-related data from the company. Future research can explore this direction if the data are available.

11507514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507514.value: Social interactions have both positive and negative aspects. Prior research has focused on positive relationships (e.g., friendship) but paid little attention to negative relationships between individuals (e.g., competitors). In this project, we first prepared a working paper that focuses on one type of negative relationship, namely competitive relationship. We examine the scenario in which male consumers compete with female consumers. Our findings show that the competitive relationship has differential effects on the behavior of male and female. In particular, males become more aggressive while females become more submissive. We discuss how these effects affect people’s competition performance and the marketing implications. We have examined the moderating effects of virtual identity (e.g., consumers may create their own virtual identity which may or may not be consistent with their true identity). We find that both true identity and virtual identity can lead to stereotype effects in a mixed-gender competition. As for the positive relationship, we have published a paper regarding how people perform in a positive relationship (i.e., group work). We have also published a paper regarding the temporal pattern of consumers’ propensity to build the positive relationship. We find that people are more likely to add new friends at night than during daytime.

11507814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507814.value: 期权交易对股票价格在高管薪酬契约及解聘决定中使用程度的影响

11507814.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11507814.value: Prof Kim, Jeong Bon Dr Zhang, Liandong

11507814.label: Project Objectives
11507814.value: We intend to provide empirical evidence of the role of options trading on the use of stock price in CEO compensation design. In doing so, we extend the executive compensation literature in understanding how stock market microstructure (or the process of stock price formation) affects the use of (and the recent trend of using) stock-based equity in CEO compensation design. In a similar vein, as stock price incorporates more information of managers’ actions via option trading, the board may rely more on stock price performance relative to other performance measure when evaluating poorly performing CEOs and making their replacement decisions. We intend to provide empirical evidence of the role of options trading on CEO replacement decisions. As our hypotheses are developed from an efficient contracting perspective, we further expect that the hypothesized impact of option trading on CEO compensation and replacement decisions is more pronounced when corporate governance is more effective or managers are less entrenched. We will provide empirical tests to see whether this expectation holds.

11507814.label: Realisation of objectives
11507814.value: A growing literature has shown that option trading improves stock price informativeness by facilitating informed trading. Bond, Edmans, and Goldstein (2012) suggest that the manager’s incentives to take real actions will depend on the extent to which they will be reflected in the stock price. If the stock price is not closely tied to firm value, the manager has weak incentives to exert costly effort to improve the firm’s fundamental value. In the proposal, we intent to examine how option trading, which help impounds into prices the impact CEOs’ action on firm fundamental, makes stock price information more useful in contracting setting. More specifically, we examine how the sensitivity of CEO’s compensation to stock price and the sensitivity of CEO’s replacement decision to stock price increases in the volume of option trading. Though we are able to generate empirical evidence consistent with our predictions, two major concerns raised by reviewers make the paper difficult to be published in the top-tier journal. First, Gao (2010) has already shown a positive association between option trading and pay-for-performance sensitivity. Gao (2010) argues that the access to the hedging market increases the manager’s ability to bear risk hence decreases her incentive to exert effort. In equilibrium, shareholders should provide a higher-power contract so that the manager’s after-hedging incentive is closer to the optimal level. Though we have a different interpretation of the finding, it is difficult to empirically differentiate. Second, reviewers raised concerns that option trading are endogenous in nature and it is difficult to find a way to address the endogeneity concerns. Given the difficulties in publishing the findings from the original proposal, we changed our research directions to some extent. To overcome the first concern, we broaden our research question by examining how option trading affects managers’ real decisions (more specifically innovation) and the initial proposed compensation mechanism is one of the channels through which option trading affects managers’ innovation decisions. The other channel is the learning channel (i.e., the trading of options can enhance the incorporation of decision-useful, private information in market prices). Compared to the original proposal, we feel the broader question is more interesting. The paper titled “The Real Effects of Derivative Markets: The Impact of Options Trading Activity on Corporate Innovation” is now under the review of Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. Part of the RGC fund has been used to support a Ph.D. student. During our discussion regarding the endogeneity issue, our Ph.D. student identified an interesting exogenous shock, i.e., the 1999 ruling of the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, we eventually utilize the shock which impose a weakened litigation environment and examine how it affects CEO’ compensation design. We recently finished a paper titled “The Impact of Shareholder Litigation Risk on Equity Incentives: Evidence from a Natural Experiment”, which is currently under review of The Accounting Review. Although the second paper is not exactly what we set off to investigate in the proposal, we feel that it is also in line with the initial broad idea. Given that training Ph.D. student is one of the objectives of RGC funding, we attribute this paper as another output of the RGC funding. We acknowledged the generous support of RGC in both papers.

11507814.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507814.value: Summary of main findings: Our study shows that firms with greater levels of options trading generate both more patents and patent citations. Interpreting these results, we argue that options markets enhance stock price efficiency, which, in turn, increases both managerial incentives and ability to innovate. Our split-sample results confirm these arguments. Most research in the asset pricing and microstructure literature has focused on how options markets contribute to price discovery and stock market efficiency, while our study focuses on the impact of options markets on corporate real actions such as innovation. Research outcome: Our paper titled “The Real Effects of Derivative Markets: The Impact of Options Trading Activity on Corporate Innovation” is now under the review of Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis.

11507814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507814.value: We generated two papers from the RGC funding, which are currently under review. We will try to get the papers published in the near future.

11507814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507814.value: An extensive literature has shown that the features of options markets facilitate informed trading, which, in turn, enhances the price efficiency of equity markets. However, few studies have directly examined how trading in secondary financial markets affect real economic activity. To fill the void, our research investigates the effects of options trading on corporate innovation. We find that firms with greater levels of options trading generate both more patents and patent citations. In terms of the mechanisms through which options trading fosters innovation, our findings suggest that both the incentive channel and learning channel play important roles. The learning channel suggests that managers can learn new information from secondary market prices and use this information to guide their investment decisions. The incentive channel suggests that options trading mitigates managerial myopia by impounding its long-run value into market prices. Our research complements a recent study by Roll et al. (2009), which finds that options trading increases firm value. We show that innovation is an important channel through which options trading activity enhances firm value. Our research extends the existing financial market literature on the benefits of options markets.

11507914.label: Realisation of objectives
11507914.value: The original objective of this study is to employ a design that combines survey-based data together with archival data in China to examine the role of auditors' judgment-related traits on audit quality. With the support of RGC, our research team made the following achievements: (1) we manually collect all Chinese listed firms' auditing team members' characteristics for the recent twenty years, including name, age, position, degree, major, gender, qualification, political status, affiliation, graduating university, and working city, etc. These information are not only useful for this project, also could be used for many other projects related to Chinese auditors; (2) we make surveys to all individual auditors we could find addresses and get some feedbacks from these auditors. These feedbacks are also quite useful for any projects related to Chinese auditors' trait-related characteristics; (3) we also make some pilot surveys to a big number of business school students from six famous Chinese universities, including Fudan University, Renmin University of China, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, etc. Although these students are not auditors yet, the feedback to these surveys is able to lend support to many relevant research as the larger number of feedback (compared to those feedback from individual auditors) can enhance the statistical power; and (4) using the available data, the principal investigator finished a working paper which is relevant to this project, although not perfectly matching. The working paper has now been revised and resubmitted to one of the good accounting journals - Accounting Horizons. However, the objectives of this project are not fully achieved as we did not find a significant association between individual auditors' judgment-related traits and audit quality. Given the small sample size, low statistical power, limited generalization possibility, and rigid research spirit, we hesitate to jump to a conclusion and hence are not table to finish a working paper with the exactly the same research question as our original plan. The potential reasons for the insignificant results could be (1) Due to low statistical power due to the low response rate of individual auditors and thus small sample size. In more details, from the 2698 Chinese listed firms from 2011 to 2014, we identify 3914 individual auditor names. Among them, 30.79% individual auditors' working firms are located in Beijing, and 10.40% are in Shanghai. We attempted to approach around 320 individual auditors in Beijing and 130 auditors in Shanghai, whose working address could be clearly identified by post, email or asking friends to collect survey results directly. However, we received very few feedback from these individual auditors. In total, less than 30 responses are received, leads to a very low response rate (6.7%). As a consequence, the sample size of our test sample is very small. (2) Due to biased or untrustworthy feedback from individual auditors. The special design in our survey questions is that we ask the individual auditors to indicate their names in the answers. It turns out that those auditors are unwilling to disclose their names, probably because some questions are sensitive such as ethical or morale issues or risk attitude. Moreover, (3) due to other omitted characteristics which could affect the association. Nevertheless, we are still making attempts to overcome these problems by (1) keeping in contact with those individual auditor and expect them to finish more refined surveys and try to increase the number of sample observations; (2) trying to find Chinese administrative bureau which is responsible to manage individual auditors to distribute survey questions for us. Actually we already find a potential coauthor from Renmin University of China, Professor Kangtao Ye. He agrees to find his friend, a high level officer in CICPA, to distribute the survey questions to some individual auditors in Beijing. Although we didn't have a working paper with the exactly the same research questions as previously proposed, we still make some progress on this project as (1) we have come up with a related working paper which is under revision for resubmission to Accounting Horizons; (2) using the archival data we have collected so far, we could come up with another working paper, potentially titled as "The role of individual auditors' characteristics on audit quality: Chinese evidence." Now it's in the preliminary data analyses stage; and (3) we have plenty of feedbacks from business school students from six mainland universities, so we could test the same research questions as proposed in this project, using experimental research methodology. We believe that this experimental research design will also lend support to the proposed research question and contribute to relevant literature.

11507914.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507914.value: Using the available data, the principal investigator finished a working paper which is relevant to this project, although not perfectly matching. In detail, we investigate whether individual Chinese auditors are associated with the comparability of their clients’ financial statements, based on a sample of Chinese companies audited by 10 large audit firms. We first confirm the existence of office-level effect on clients’ financial statement comparability in China. More importantly, we demonstrate that individual auditors have an incremental effect on comparability, beyond the office-level effect. We also find that individual auditor’s characteristics such as age, position, and academic degree could affect auditors’ abilities to exert influence. The working paper has now been revised and resubmitted to one of the good accounting journals - Accounting Horizons. Although we didn't have a working paper with the exactly the same research questions as previously proposed, we still make some progress on this project as (1) we have come up with a related working paper which is under revision for resubmission to Accounting Horizons; (2) using the archival data we have collected so far, we could come up with another working paper, potentially titled as "The role of individual auditors' characteristics on audit quality: Chinese evidence." Now it's in the preliminary data analyses stage; and (3) we have plenty of feedbacks from business school students from six mainland universities, so we could test the same research questions as proposed in this project, using experimental research methodology. We believe that this experimental research design will also lend support to the proposed research question and contribute to relevant literature.

11507914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507914.value: We attempt to test other related research questions, such as individual auditors' judgment-related traits and other audit outcomes, such as audit style, audit lag, auditor independence etc. We could come up with another working paper, potentially titled as "The role of individual auditors' characteristics on audit quality: Chinese evidence." We have plenty of feedbacks from business school students from six mainland universities, so we could test the same research questions as proposed in this project, using experimental research methodology, potentially titled as "The role of auditors' judgment-related traits on audit quality: experimental evidence".

11507914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507914.value: The paper which has been resubmitted to Accounting Horizons can make several contributions. First, it extends the prior literature and provides evidence of individual auditor style based on large-scale archival data. Our study suggests that both in-house knowledge and working rules at firm, office, and auditor levels are important factors in determining firms’ financial statement comparability. Second, the study advances our understanding of the role of the micro-level institution in promoting comparability and therefore has implications for regulators. The accounting standards set emphasize comparability as an important quality characteristic, and thus efforts have been made to promote comparability by converging accounting standards worldwide, but previous studies suggest that the lack of supporting institutions results in limited success in enforcing comparability. Finally, this study has valuable implications for practitioners. Various financial market participants have a strong interest in understanding financial statement comparability because comparability improves multiplying valuation performance and is associated with several financial consequences. Our study is informative for investors and financial analysts because it suggests that individual auditors can be a source of reference in identifying comparable stocks for conducting financial statement analysis. Other financial market participants, such as creditors and fund managers, can also benefit from our study.

12100914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100914.value: 柏金遜症（PD）是世界第二常見神經退行性疾病，中國大陸約200萬PD患者，香港55歲以上人口發病率約0.5％。到2030年PD在中國的發病率預計將增加至4.94％。PD對人類的生活質量造成嚴重的影響，給衛生保健系統帶來越來越重的負擔。開發一種有效治療藥物將為數百萬患者帶來福音。多巴胺能神經元中由α-突觸核蛋白（α-syn）蛋白形成的路易小體的累積是PD的一個主要病理特徵，α-syn水平異常增高具有致病性。自噬是細胞降解內容物包括蛋白聚集體和受損細胞器，以維持細胞穩態的一種進化上保守的細胞過程。越來越多的證據表明，自噬對疾病相關蛋白（包括α-syn突變體）的清除發揮關鍵作用，自噬功能的失調可加重PD患者及PD模型動物腦內病理特徵。促進自噬以清除神經毒性蛋白聚集體可以提供緩解PD病程的治療方法。 自噬基因Beclin1在自噬調控中發揮核心作用。它與PI3K III複合物中多種蛋白相互作用以控制自噬活性。高遷移率族蛋白B1（HMGB1）是一種核蛋白，其轉運到細胞質中，與Beclin1相互作用可正向調控自噬。在前期研究中，項目申請人確定了Beclin1-VPS34蛋白複合物中新的組分，揭示了其調控自噬的獨特作用並解析出Beclin1蛋白複合物的晶體結構（Zhong Y, et al., Nature Cell Biology 2009; Li X, et al., Nature Communications 2012）。 最近我们从具有神经保護活性的中药钩藤中篩選出依賴於Beclin1的细胞自噬诱导剂柯諾辛B（Cory B），在多種PD細胞模型中，Cory B顯著促进α-syn蛋白的清除（Lu JH, et al. Autophagy 2012; Patent No.: US 13/420,628）（基金資助RGC-NSFC/11-12）。其次，我们的研究表明：在PD細胞模型中，α-syn蛋白的過度表达損傷了HMGB1/Beclin 1介導的自噬，而Cory B可能通過調節HMGB1-Beclin 1通路恢復細胞自噬功能（Song JX, et al., Autophagy 2014）。 此外，我们获得的一系列初步数据显示：（1）Cory B直接结合HMGB1；（2）Cory B促进HMGB1-Beclin1的相互作用；（3）Cory B在果蝇和小鼠中诱导自噬和防止神经退行病變。根據这些令人鼓舞的结果，我们推测：Cory B通過增强HMGB1-Beclin1的相互作用，促进自噬而发挥神经保护作用。为了驗證这一假设，我们將進行以下實驗研究：（1）验证HMGB1- Beclin1相互作用为Cory B诱导自噬的主要分子靶標;（2）解析Cory B- HMGB1/ Beclin1複合物的結構；（3）在腺相关病毒（AAV）介導的α-syn蛋白過表達大鼠模型中评估Cory B作用於HMGB1-Beclin1複合物调控自噬和神經保護作用機制。 本項目将揭示Cory B誘導自噬的直接分子靶標并进一步推動预防/治疗PD的新藥開發研究。

12100914.label: Realisation of objectives
12100914.value: Objective 1. To validate and dissect HMGB1-Beclin 1 interaction as the primary target of Cory B to induce autophagy. We have conducted a series of experiments and found that Cory B induces autophagy in multiple neuronal cells and in animals. Our study further revealed that Cory B induces autophagy in a Beclin 1-dependent but mTOR-independent manner. Interestingly, Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) assay showed a stable binding between HMGB1 and Cory B, thus confirming that HMGB1 is a direct binding partner of Cory B. Moreover, we developed a novel network-based algorithm of in silico Kinome Activity Profiling (iKAP) to computationally infer potentially important protein kinases from phosphorylation networks. Using this algorithm, we identifed the molecular targets/pathways regulated by Cory B and compared the difference of Cory B and its isomer Cory. For Objective 2. To examine the role of HMGB1-Beclin 1 interaction in Cory B-mediated autophagy regulation and neuroprotection in the adeno-associated viral (AAV)-α-synuclein model of Parkinson's disease. Since the AAV-α-synuclein vector was not effective in our model we selected a commonly used α-synuclein transgenic mice and the rotenone model of PD. In α-synuclein mice, we found that Cory B promotes α-synuclein degradation in animal brains. In the rotenone model α-synuclein is significantly increased, which is similar to α-synuclein overexpression. We found significant neuroprotective effects of Cory B via autophagy enhancement in the rotenone model. Moreover, in transgenic PD drosophila model, we found that Cory B induces autophagy and effectively promotes the degradation of α-synuclein and improved survival rate, alleviated impaired locomotor function, further confirmed that Cory B has good neuroprotective effects in animal models of PD.

12100914.label: Major findings and research outcome
12100914.value: The major objectives of the proposal are to determine the potential of neuroprotective effects of Cory B, a natural autophagy enhancer, in PD disease animal models and the underlying mechanism of Cory B in the induction of autophagy. Our hypothesis is that by promoting autophagy by Cory B, could remove the toxic protein aggregates (such as α-synuclein) may provide disease-modifying therapies for PD. In mice, rat and Drosophila PD models, we conducted a series of experiments to study the neuroprotective effect of Cory B, an autophagy enhancer. In α-synuclein trangenic micem we found that Cory B promotes the degradation of α-synuclein in mice brains. In a rat model of PD, we found that Cory B effective induces autophagy, promotes the degradation of α-synuclein, prevents neuronal loss, and improves apomorphine-induced rotational behavior impairment. In Drosophila model of PD, we found that Cory B reduced the level of α-synuclein and prevented degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in α-synuclein transgenic Drosophila. Further elucidation of the therapeutic mechanism revealed that Cory B protected neuronal loss may inducing autophagy in animal. Interestingly, we found that Cory B induces autophagy in a mTOR-independent but Beclin 1-dependent manner. We also showed that Cory B directly binding with HMGB1, the HMGB1-Beclin 1 interaction may contribute to the role of Cory B in inducing autophagy. Finally, we developed a novel network-based algorithm of in silico Kinome Activity Profiling (iKAP) to computationally infer potentially important protein kinases from phosphorylation networks. Using this algorithm, we observed that Cory B potentially regulated several kinases to induces autophagy. Collectively, we not only demonstrated the neuroprotective effects of Cory B in animal models of PD, but also elucidated the possible mechanisms.

12100914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12100914.value: Our results have confirmed the efficacy of Cory B in animal models of PD, which can protect dopaminergic neurons known to degenerate in Parkinson's disease, achieving the therapeutic effect. Based on these findings, follow-up work can be adopted to 1) to further study the toxicity and PK of Cory B in animal models, to obtain more evidence for conduct future clinical experiments. and 2) find strategies to facilitate translation of the findings to clinical setting. 12100914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12100914.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder, affecting nearly 2 million people in mainland China and about 0.5% of the population aged over 55 in Hong Kong. The prevalence of PD in China is predicted to increase to 4.94% by 2030. Accumulation of alpha-synuclein (α-syn) protein in Lewy bodies (LB) in dopaminergic neurons is a hallmark of PD and thus increased α-syn level is pathogenic. Autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved cellular process for degradation of cellular contents, including protein aggregates and damaged cellular organelles to maintain cellular homeostasis. Increasing evidence suggests that autophagy plays a role in the clearance of disease-associated proteins (including mutant α-syn) and the deregulation of the autophagy pathway may promote PD-related pathologies in the brains of PD patients and in animal models of PD. Promoting autophagy to remove the toxic protein aggregates may provide disease-modifying therapies for PD. Our study has shown that Cory B, from Chinese herb Gouteng (鉤藤), induces autophagy, promotes the degradation of α-synuclein, and prevents neurodegeneration in animal models of PD. We have also elucidated the mechanism of action. Our results have the potential to be translated to clinics helping the rapidly increasing population of Parkinson's disease patients.
