12101314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101314.value: In plants, microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as important regulators in various aspects of growth and development. miR163, a recently evolved miRNA, is highly accumulated in Arabidopsis thaliana but is nearly undetectable in its related outcrossing relative, Arabidopsis arenosa. It has been showed that miR163 plays a role in conferring natural variation of secondary metabolites accumulation in Arabidopsis polyploids. miR163 and its targets expression can be induced by alamethicin (fungal elicitor) treatment. In addition, one of the miR163 targets, farnesoic acid methyltransferase (FAMT) can convert farnesoic acid (FA) to methyl farnesoate (MeFA) to which MeFA is a precursor of insect juvenile hormone III (JHIII). Therefore, these data suggested a role of miR163 and its target in plant defense. However, their physiological relevance in plant defense against biotic stresses is still unclear. The goal of this study is to elucidate the functional roles of Arabidopsis miR163 and its targets in plant defense against bacterial pathogens. We will first evaluate the dynamic and epigenetic regulation of miR163 and its targets under biotic stresses by using wild type A. thaliana, the mir163 mutant and an established MIR163 promoter-GUS reporter transgenic lines. In addition, by overexpressing miR163 or its targets in transgenic A. thaliana, we will examine their direct functional roles in defense against Pseudomonas syringae (Pst). At a biochemical level, alteration of metabolite profiles mediated by miR163 will be characterized using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and mass spectrometry (MS) analyses. Potential gene regulatory network and transcriptome changes mediated by miR163 and its target genes in response to Pst infection will be evaluated using mRNA-seq on genome-wide scale. It is expected that results will shed light on the role of miR163 in plant defenses. Moreover, data obtained will provide a foundation for further investigation on the role of miR163 and its targets in the related Arabidopsis autotetraploids and their tetraploid hybrids, as well as providing insights to the evolutionary significance of miRNA in mediating plant defense pathways in different plant species or hybrids. microRNAs(miRNAs)在植物成長和發展方面擔當重要的監管角色。miR163為一種最近演變的miRNA，在擬南芥(Arabidopsis thaliana)中高度累積，但近乎不能在其相屬異交品種(Arabidopsis arenosa)中探測。miR163 在擬南芥多倍體中的自然變異所衍生的代謝物積累已被展示。一種真菌誘導物(alamethicin)可誘發miR163和其目標的表達。此外，該miR163目標之一，FAMT 可轉換farnesoic acid (FA)為methyl farnesoate (MeFA), 成為昆蟲幼激素III（JHIII）的前體。因此，這些數據展示了miR163及其目標在植物防禦中的角色。然而目前，它們對植物在生物脅迫下的防禦生理意義還不確定。本研究的目的是闡明擬南芥miR163與其目標在對抗細菌病原體的功能。我們將先用野生型(wild type)擬南芥, mir163突變體及已建立的MIR163啟動子-GUS報告基因系統來評估miR163及其目標在生物脅迫的動態性和表觀遺傳調控。此外，通過過表達(overexpressing) miR163或其目標在轉基因擬南芥，我們將研究它們在Pseudomonas syringae（Pst）的直接功能作用。在生化水平上，由miR163引導改變的代謝水平將使用高效液相色譜（HPLC）和質譜（MS）來進行分析。由miR163及其目標基因在Pst感染所導致的潛在基因調控網絡和轉錄改變將使用的mRNA-seq於基因組內進行評價。結果將闡明miR163在植物防禦中的作用。此外，獲得的數據將提供有關miR163和其目標在相關在擬南芥同源四倍體和四倍雜交體中的作用作進一步調查，並提供miRNA在不同的植物物種和雜種植物中的防禦途徑和進化意義。

12101314.label: Realisation of objectives
12101314.value: The overall goal of this project is to study a recently evolved miRNA (miR163) and its targets (PXMT1 and FAMT) in defense against the bacterial pathogen, Pseudomonas syringe. In the original proposed research, panel members and reviewers have concerns that the objectives are too ambitious and complicated. Therefore, the original objectives were revised and more focuses are put into elucidating miR163 and its targets regulations through specific biological experiments. The two specific objectives are (1) Regulation of miR163 and its targets under biotic stresses; and (2) Direct functional analyses of two selected miR163 targets. Both objectives of the project have been achieved for the project period. During the project period, we found that miR163 mutation has led to enhanced resistance against P. syringae infection. In elucidating the regulatory relationship between miR163 and PXMT1 or FAMT, we further found that both the miRNA and the targets are inducible by Pst treatment. However, differential targeting efficiency by miR163 was observed between miR163-PXMT1 and miR163-FAMT pairs. Furthermore, we also showed that histone deacetylase (HDA19) act cooperatively with miR163 in mediating the defense against Pst. Direct functional analyses of PXMT1 and FAMT showed that PXMT1 plays a lesser role in plant defense. In contrast, altered FAMT expression (in the famt mutant or FAMT overexpressors) showed altered level of sensitivities against Pst infection. Therefore, our findings further suggested that miR163 play a modulatory role in controlling the threshold of target genes expression so as to balance the cost for establishing disease resistance while maintaining the growth of plants. In conclusion, our study has provided an example that non-conversed miRNA is induced as a part of defense response and represses its target gene expression to achieve appropriate levels of gene expression, revealing one of the evolutionary significances upon the formation and selection of new miRNA genes in plants. Achievements of project objectives Objective 1: Regulation of miR163 and its targets under biotic stresses In the previous mid-term progress report (1-1-2015 to 31-3-2016), we have reported in detail the achievement of objective 1 (70%) in understanding the dynamic regulation of miR163 and its targets (PXMT1 and FAMT) in response to Pseudomonas syringae challenge. Overall, we have demonstrated a modulating relationship between miR163 and its targets in responses to pathogen stress. To further investigate their regulation at the epigenetic level, we have characterized if genetic interaction exists between miR163 and histone deacetylation in defense signaling. To achieve this, we crossed the mir163 with the hda19 mutants, and selected a homozygous mir163 hda19 double mutant (DM) line for subsequent analyses. Like the mir163 mutant, the hda19 mutant showed increased resistance against Pst DC3000. In addition, a slight increase in resistance against Pst DC3000 was also detected in the DM line when compared to either of the single mutant. In the hda19 mutant, a decreased basal miR163 accumulation and a lower accumulation of miR163 by Pst DC3000 were evident when compared to Col-0, which is consistent with the observed disease resistance in the mir163 mutant. At the transcript level, basal accumulation of FAMT was increased in the hda19 mutant and was further enhanced in the DM compared to either of the single mutant, suggesting HDA19 act to repress FAMT expression. However, similar induction of FAMT upon Pst DC3000 treatment was observed in the wild-type, single mutants and the DM lines. Overall, these data suggested a cooperative interaction between miR163 and histone deacetylase in modulating FAMT induction during Pst infection and that histone deacetylation contributed as a part of negative regulation of FAMT expression. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation, we aimed to further understand the regulation and histone modification changes at the MIR163 and its target loci under biotic stresses. At the MIR163 locus, enrichments of H3K9ac and H3K4me3 (permissive histone marks) were detected at the proximal region when compared to the distal region of the promoter under normal condition. Upon Pst DC3000 infection, H3K9ac level was enhanced (~4.9 folds) at the MIR163 proximal upstream region while no further enrichment of H3K4me3 was detected. Using antibodies against the C-terminus of histone H3 (H3 C-ter), histone H3 occupancy at both the proximal and distal regions showed a lower level but insignificant enrichment at 6 hpi than that at 0 hpi. In contrast to the MIR163 locus, significant enrichment of H3K4me3 at the proximal region of PXMT1 (~8 folds) and FAMT (~5.5 folds) were detected upon Pst infection while H3K9ac levels remained unchanged. Therefore, the increase in H3K4me3 at the PXMT1 and FAMT loci correlates with their active expression upon pathogen attacks. Objective 2: Direct functional analyses of two selected miR163 targets To further characterize the direct functional roles of PXMT1 and FAMT in plant defense, silent mutations were introduced at the miR163 complementary site in PXMT1 and FAMT, generating the c-myc-tagged mPXMT1 and mFAMT for 35S-driven overexpression in A. thaliana, respectively. Overexpression of the corresponding target cDNA without the mutagenized cleavage site was used as a control. When plants were inoculated with Pst DC3000, expression of PXMT1 was significantly induced at 24 hpi in the empty vector control line but not in the overexpressors. Nevertheless, all lines tested showed similar sensitivities to Pst DC3000 infection, suggesting a less direct correlation between the altered PXMT1 expression and the increased resistance against Pst DC3000 in the mir163 mutant. In the famt mutant, an increased sensitivity to the pathogen infection was detected when compared to the Col-0. This result agrees with the defense response observed in the mir163 mutant to which the mir163 mutant showed enhanced resistance against Pst. In the reciprocal experiment, overexpression of FAMT is expected to confer improved resistance in the overexpressors. To our surprise, increased sensitivity to Pst DC3000 was also observed in the 35S-FAMT and 35S-mFAMT lines. Therefore, this suggested that the ectopic over-accumulation of FAMT could adversely affect the level of plant defense. In Arabidopsis, constitutive expression of inducible SAR resistance pathways involving the PR1 and NPR1 genes was found to incur costs in terms of plant size and seed yields. Since the FAMT overexpressors exhibited similar increased disease sensitivity as the famt mutant, it is possible that high level of FAMT expression over activates the secondary metabolite production, increasing the cost burden on plant development, rendering the plant more sensitive to Pst infection. At the transcript level, a 1.4-fold expression difference was found between the 35S-FAMT and 35S-mFAMT lines at 0 and 24 hpi, confirming mutation at the miR163 target site had an effect in the Myc-mFAMT transcript accumulation. Therefore, these data suggested that FAMT contributes in stress responses against Pst infection. However, the involvement of FAMT in plant defense is more complicated than a simple direct correlation between the miRNA and the target. Conclusions In summary, we have achieved the project aims outlined in both project objectives and have elucidated the regulatory role of miR163 and its targets in plant defense signaling. In the future, a more focus high-throughput and comprehensive approach could be applied to further the findings from our study. In addition to presentations at various local and international conferences, a manuscript is published to conclude the findings from the funded project.

12101314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12101314.value: To further elucidate the regulatory role of miR163 and FAMT in plant defense, mRNA-seq was used recently to evaluate the affected gene regulatory networks in the mir163 and the famt mutants, respectively. Initial transcriptome comparisons among the wild type (Col-0), mir163 and famt mutants revealed some differentially expressed genes that are involved in the defense and secondary metabolite production. Further transcriptome profiling of these genotypes under Pst-induced stresses will provide additional insights into the potential roles of miR163 and its targets in plant defense. It is expected that data obtained will provide a foundation for further investigation on the role of miR163 and its targets in the related Arabidopsis autotetraploids and their tetraploid hybrids, as well as providing insights to the evolutionary significance of miRNA in mediating plant defense pathways in different plant species or hybrids.

12101514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101514.value: Natural Killer (NK) cell, a crucial player of the human immune defense system, detects and kills virus-infected cells and cancer cells. Although the relevant molecular machineries involved in NK cell activation and NK-target cell interactions are largely known, how their collected dynamics regulate fast yet highly selective target cell killing in the complex environment of tissues is poorly understood. In traditional bulk killing assays, heterogeneity and kinetic details of individual NK-target cell interactions are masked, seriously limiting analysis of the underlying dynamic mechanism(s). Therefore, in this proposed study we will develop quantitative single-cell microscopy assays in chemically and physically defined environments using microfluidic platform, to investigate the real-time killing dynamics of epithelial cancer cells by primary NK cells purified from human blood. Our goal is to determine rate-limiting steps in NK-cancer cell interaction, identify mechanistically relevant heterogeneity in the process, and relate the observed kinetics and heterogeneity to key molecular events and regulatory components of the NK cell machinery in a quantitative manner. The interdisciplinary approach that we employ will integrate complementary experimental and theoretical methodologies in live-cell imaging, microfluidics engineering, systemic profiling and computational modeling. The resulting fundamental knowledge will significantly improve our understanding of the cytotoxic mechanism of primary NK cell, in particular regarding how NK cell killing varies between different cancer targets. NK cells are considered promising candidate for cancer treatment, especially for eliminating residual cancer cells after conventional therapy. Results from our proposed study will provide new mechanistic insight to develop this treatment strategy. The integrative platform that we develop will also be readily extendable to analysis of other cell-cell interaction dynamics, e.g. in macrophage and T cell function. 自然殺傷（NK）細胞是人類免疫系統的一個重要組成部分，具有檢測並殺死被病毒感染的細胞和癌變細胞的作用。儘管NK細胞的激活以及其促進受感染和癌變細胞凋亡的分子機制在很大程度上已知，但對於這一過程的動力學特徵及其調控，例如NK細胞如何在複雜的組織環境中快速而有選擇性的殺死目標細胞，我們還知之甚少。傳統測量NK細胞殺傷性的實驗都只能觀測NK細胞與靶細胞在整體水平的相互作用，因而無法研究NK細胞與靶細胞相互作用的瞬態動力學及這一過程的特異性，嚴重限制了研究NK細胞作用的定量動態機制。基於以上考慮，我們將通過本研究項目，建立微流體單細胞實驗平台，並結合單細胞顯微成像技術，定量測定與分析體原NK細胞（從人體血液中純化）在特定環境下殺死上皮癌細胞的動力學特徵與機制。我們的研究目標是確定NK細胞與目標癌細胞相互作用的關鍵動態步驟，以及與此過程相關的單細胞多樣性，並且找出與所觀察到的動力學和多樣性特徵相關的關鍵細胞調控分子和調控通路。本研究項目將利用跨學科的實驗和理論分析方法，包括活體細胞顯微成像，微流體芯片控制，整體系統表型測定以及理論模型計算。本研究項目的結果將顯著提升我們對NK細胞殺滅癌細胞機理的認識，特別是關於NK細胞的殺傷性是如何因應腫瘤細胞的不同而變化的重要機制性問題。 此外，NK細胞對癌細胞的自然殺傷性可被利用於免疫抗癌治療，特別是應用於去除常規治療後殘存的癌細胞。所以我們的研究結果也將為進一步發展這一免疫抗癌治療方法提供新的、重要的細胞機理基礎。我們所發展的實驗及理論相結合的綜合研究手段也將適用於研究其它細胞相互作用的定量動力學機制，例如分析巨噬細胞和T細胞的動態功能。

12101514.label: Realisation of objectives
12101514.value: Objective 1: This objective is fully realized. Specifically, by using unique fluorescent reporters and live-cell imaging, we identified and quantified the differential control of NK-cancer cell interaction by three distinct signaling pathways, including lytic granule-mediated apoptosis, death ligand-mediated apoptosis and necrosis. We found cytotoxic dynamics of primary NK cell was mediated substantially by non-lytic granule mechanism; and the transient nature of NK-cancer cell conjugation that activates FasL signaling is significantly different from the sustained conjugation that activates the lytic granule and necrotic pathway, pointing to differential target recognition by primary NK cell. The above results have been published (Zhu et al, Oncotarget, 2016; 7(30): 47163-47172). Objective 2: This objective is fully realized. Based on the live-cell imaging data, we pinpointed specific cytotoxic pathways for further investigation of the molecular regulators underlying NK-cancer cell interaction. Flow cytometry analysis revealed up-regulation of the activating receptor, NKG2D, but not NKp46, and down-regulation of inhibitory receptor, KIR2D, during the NK-cancer cell interaction process. Moreover, cytokine/chemokine array analysis identified that NK-cancer cell interaction mainly induced secretion of key chemokines, such as CCL3, CCL4 and CCL5, indicating NK-cancer cell interaction likely enhanced NK cell cytotoxic activity by promoting NK cell motility towards the cancer target. Objective 3: This objective is fully realized. By combining live-cell imaging, antibody blocking of distinct NK cell receptors and flow cytometry analysis of corresponding NK cell ligand expression on the target cell surface, we investigated target specificity of NK cell cytotoxic dynamics against four cancer (U-2 OS, HeLa, MCF7 and SMMC) and one normal (LOX2) cell lines. We found sensitivity to primary NK cell killing mainly depended on expression of MHCI molecules on the target cell surface for both normal and cancer targets, indicating the inhibitory strength between KIRs on NK cell and MHCI on the target cell plays a key regulatory role in the interaction dynamics. Moreover, the NK cell activating ligand, MICB, was found to contribute specifically to the necrotic mode of NK cell cytotoxicity. These results constituted a main part of the PhD thesis of Yanting Zhu (refer to part C). We are converting the thesis to manuscript form and aim to submit it in 3-6 months. Objective 4: This objective is fully realized. Based on the extensive experimental data, we performed mathematical modeling in collaboration with Prof. Zhibin Li (School of Physics, Sun Yat Sen University). Briefly, statistical analysis and kinetic modeling showed directed motion of primary NK cells, i.e., non-random diffusion, when NK cells were in close proximity of about 40-50 um to the cancer target, indicating the polarized NK cells can sense a signaling gradient secreted by the cancer target at the spatial scale of about 40-50 um. Moreover, this directed motility was found to be modulated by the polarization state of NK cell, with polarized NK cells exhibiting longer correlated motion and 10-fold larger diffusion coefficient than the non-polarized NK cells, which enhanced their targeted motion and subsequent cytotoxicity. The modeling results were summarized in the MPhil thesis of Yiwen Tang (Supervisor: Prof. Zhibin Li). A manuscript based on the MPhil thesis is near completion for submission.

12101514.label: Major findings and research outcome
12101514.value: Using novel quantitative microscopy assays and mathematical modeling, we elucidated, at the single cell level, real-time killing dynamics of epithelial cells by primary human NK cells. Our results revealed differential kinetics of three distinct cytotoxic modes of primary NK cells and their relative contributions to the killing of different target cell types, which accounted for the significant heterogeneity observed in the NK cell cytotoxic activity. We found sensitivity of both normal and cancer targets to primary NK cell killing was mainly regulated by expression level of target MHCI molecules, and to a lesser extent by expression of NKG2D ligands. And the NKG2D ligand, MICB, exerted strong effect specifically on triggering the necrotic mode of NK cell cytotoxicity. Moreover, target-oriented motion of primary NK cells appeared to be driven by chemokine gradient spanning 40-50 um around the target cells, and this directed motion depended also on the polarization state of the NK cells. Our findings have resulted in one journal publication (Zhu et al, Oncotarget, 2016; 7(30): 47163-47172), one PhD thesis (Yanting Zhu, 2018), one MPhil thesis (Yiwen Tang, 2018) and two manuscripts currently under preparation, which we aim to submit in the coming 3-6 months (please refer to Part C for details).

12101514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12101514.value: Our results revealed intriguing target specificity of primary NK cell activity and directed motion of NK cells towards the cancer target. One immediate follow-up question is how the directed motion of primary NK cells varies depending on the target cell type and how such target-dependent motility contributes to differential target recognition as well as variable NK cell cytotoxic activity. For instance, we can use insert to seed two different target cell types, e.g., cancer vs. normal, onto two sides of the imaging plate and then study how NK cells move towards the competing targets. We plan to further collaborate with Prof. Zhibin Li to pursue a more in-depth understanding of NK cell motility as a function of target cell types and determine how motility quantitatively affects NK cell cytotoxic activity. To this end, we will develop automatic cell tracking algorithm based on machine learning to quantify NK cell motility, perform co-culture experiments with multiple target cell types and construct more advanced mathematical models that consider target-specific parameters.

12101514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12101514.value: Natural Killer (NK) cell, a crucial player of the human immune defense system, detects and kills virus-infected cells and cancer cells. In this research project, by combining novel single cell microscopy assays and mathematical modeling, we quantified the rate-limiting kinetics underlying NK-cancer cell interaction via three distinct cytotoxic signaling pathways and identified mechanism that governs variability in the cytotoxic dynamics of primary NK cells against different target cell types. We found sensitivity of different target cell types to NK cell killing mainly depended on the inhibitory interaction between KIR receptors on primary NK cell surface and MHCI molecules on the target cell surface; and directed motion of polarized NK cells towards target cancer cells significantly enhanced NK cell cytotoxicity. NK cells are considered promising candidate for cancer treatment, especially for eliminating residual cancer cells after conventional therapy. Results from our study elucidated the quantitative mechanism underlying cytotoxic dynamics of primary human NK cell at the single cell level, providing new insight for further developing NK cell therapy. The live-cell imaging assays that we developed are also readily extendable to analysis of other cell-cell interaction dynamics, e.g. in macrophage and T cell function.

12102314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12102314.value: Redox signaling occurs when cellular redox homeostasis is perturbed. Redox signaling has increasingly been recognized as an important mechanism in regulating a variety of biological processes. Adverse environmental conditions often cause overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which can act as signals in activating the oxidative stress response. Redox signaling is largely mediated by redox-sensitive proteins that undergo oxidative modifications in response to environmental and internal cues that alter cellular redox homeostasis. Some transcription factors have been found to undergo oxidative modification under oxidative stress which alters their activity and/or subcellular localization, leading to activation of stress-responsive genes. The mechanism that regulates the oxidative stress response in plants remains largely unknown. Through redox proteomics analysis, we recently found that the Arabidopsis basic region/leucine zipper transcription factor AtbZIP68 underwent reversible oxidation at its Cys320 residue in Arabidopsis cells under oxidative stress. We found that bZIP68 is localized in the nucleus under normal conditions but translocates to the cytosol under oxidative stress. We hypothesize that bZIP68 might act as a transcriptional repressor to suppress oxidative stress-responsive genes under normal conditions. Under oxidative stress, it undergoes oxidation which causes its translocation from the nucleus to the cytosol, thereby leading to activation of oxidative stress-responsive genes. In this study, we will use molecular, genetic, and functional genomics approaches to define the molecular mechanism that controls nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of bZIP68 and its transcriptional regulation. We will identify bZIP68’s target genes through chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high throughput sequencing (ChIP-seq) and by comparison of transcriptomes between the bzip68 mutant and wildtype plants. Additional mutational analysis and the target gene identification will allow us to define biological pathways regulated by bZIP68. The study will reveal whether bZIP68 acts as a redox sensor in regulating the stress response and provide novel insights into the molecular mechanism governing the stress response in plants.

12102314.label: Realisation of objectives
12102314.value: Objective 1: Determine redox states of bZIP68 under various redox-perturbing conditions. Dynamic profiles of redox states at Cys320 under stress treatments will be generated. To determine whether bZIP68 undergoes oxidative modifications in plants in response to oxidative stress, we generated transgenic lines expression bZIP68-FLAG and used it in Western. H2O2 treatment of the seedlings caused formation of an oxidized form of bZIP68-FLAG and this oxidized form was reducible by DTT. The oxidized form is likely a homo- or hetero-multimer (with a size of about 150 kD). The oxidized form is likely formed through a disulfide bond with the redox-sensitive Cys320 residue as the C320S mutation abolished the formation of the oxidized form. Similar oxidation of bZIP68 also occurred when protein extracts were treated with H2O2 in vitro. These results suggest that bZIP68 might directly sense cellular H2O2 and/or other ROS. Objective 2. Reveal the mechanism that controls nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of bZIP68. The roles of redox regulation and the nuclear export signal of bZIP68 in nucleocytoplasmic shuttling will be defined. bZIP68 was found to be localized in the nucleus in seedlings under normal conditions but oxidative stress led to its accumulation in the cytosol in some cells. The mutation of C320 to serine was found to block nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of bZIP68 under oxidative stress. In addition, altering two leucine residues in the putative NES sequence of bZIP68 also affects the shuttling process. These results suggest that C320 oxidation causes a conformational change of the protein which might expose its NES, leading to export of bZIP68 to the cytosol by exportin. The alteration of subcellular localization pattern of bZIP68-GFP was also observed in seedlings subjected to cold treatment. Objective 3. Identify target genes whose expression is directly regulated by bZIP68. Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high throughput DNA sequencing (ChIP-seq) and transcriptome comparison between wildtype and bzip68 mutant plants will be used to identify genes that are directly activated or suppressed by bZIP68. Transcriptome profiles of two bZIP68 mutants and wildtype plants have been generated through RNA-seq. Besides, RNA samples from the WT and bzip68-1 mutant under hydrogen peroxide treatment have also been sequenced. The results shows that the transcriptome of the bzip68 mutant resembles that of a wildtype plant that is under ROS stress. Enriched GO terms for the genes expressed at higher levels in bzip68 include those involved in abiotic and biotic stress responses, whereas the genes expressed at lower levels in the mutant include those involved in promoting growth such as auxin pathway genes and response to karrikin. To further identify direct targets of bZIP68, the ChIP-seq experiment was carried out using transgenic lines expressing bZIP68-FLAG and the control line (expressing GFP-FLAG). Over 5,000 bZIP68 binding peaks were identified that are linked to over 1,000 genes. Over 80% of the peaks are located in the promoter regions of these genes. De novo motif analysis revealed that the mostly enriched motifs of the bZIP68 binding peaks are the G-box and G-box-like motifs, which is consistent with the previous findings that bZIP68 is a G-box binding protein. GO analysis of these putative target genes showed that they are involved in responses to abiotic or biotic stresses, ABA, and light and in photosynthesis, protein/RNA metabolism, and transcriptional regulation. Objective 4. Understand the biological function of bZIP68. Mutational analysis, in combination of target gene identification, will be used to reveal the pathways that are regulated by bZIP68. Two loss-of-function mutants of bZIP68 (bzip68-1 and bzip68-2) were obtained and subjected to phenotypic analysis to understand bZIP68 biological functions. bzip68-1 is likely a knockout mutant whereas the other one might be a weak allele (which leads to a truncated protein). The bzip68-1 showed slower growth that wildtype under normal conditions, particularly in presence of exogenous sugar in the growth medium. The mutant also showed more severe growth inhibition under cold and low light conditions. However, the mutant exhibited enhanced tolerance to oxidative stress (induced by paraquat/MV). Transgenic plants expressing the mutants of bZIP68 generated through site-directed mutagenesis (such as C320S) and bZIP68 overexpressing lines have also been generated and analyzed for any discernible phenotypes. bZIP68 overexpression lines exhibited an opposite phenotype to that of the bzip68 knockout mutant.

12102314.label: Major findings and research outcome
12102314.value: 1. bZIP68 undergoes oxidative modifications in plants in response to oxidative stress. Its oxidation is dependent on its Cys320 residue. bZIP68 could be a redox sensor to regulate the oxidative stress response. 2. bZIP68 alters its subcellular localization under oxidative stress in a C320-dependent manner. It is localized in the nucleus in seedlings under normal conditions but oxidative stress led to its accumulation in the cytosol in some cells. 3. Under normal growth conditions, the loss of function of bZIP68 causes slower growth and enhanced expression of the genes functioning in stress tolerance. The reduced growth is likely a cost of unnecessary expression of many stress tolerance genes under normal conditions. Under the oxidative stress caused by MV, the mutant displayed better growth than wildtype, likely due to its enhanced expression of stress tolerance genes. 4. The phenotypic analysis, transcriptome profiling, and ChIP-seq analysis indicate that bZIP68 normally suppresses genes that function in stress tolerance but acts as an activator of genes involved in growth promotion. Under oxidative stress, bZIP68 undergoes oxidation which likely leads to its inactivation, resulting in de-repression of defense-related genes and inactivation of growth-related genes. Therefore, bZIP68 functions in sensing stress conditions to mediate the stress response pathway through its redox regulation. A manuscript (attached) including some of the major findings is under review by Plant Physiology. The work was presented in a Gordon Conference (oral) and two Plant Biology conferences (Poster).

12102314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12102314.value: Redox sensing and signaling mechanisms in plants remain largely unknown. bZIP68 could be an important redox sensor that modulates plant responses to environments. In addition to bZIP68, two of its close homologs, GBF1 and bZIP16, are also redox-sensitive. These transcription factors, together with other transcription factors such as PIFs, BZR1, etc, likely form complex signaling and transcriptional networks to fine-tune plant stress responses according to encountered environmental conditions. Unraveling the networks is a big task for further understanding of plant responses to ever-changing environments and the knowledge will be helpful for improving crop production.

12102314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12102314.value: Plants are exposed to ever-changing environments and often encounter adverse conditions for their growth and development. Plants need to protect themselves from damage by stress environments. However, unnecessary activation of stress tolerance mechanisms could have detrimental effects on normal growth. Therefore, plants need to have complex mechanisms to sense environmental conditions to balance growth and stress responses. Stress often causes perturbation of the cellular redox state which is sensed by redox-sensitive proteins so that the cell can physiologically respond to stressors; however, the mechanisms linking sensing to response remain poorly understood in plants. Here we report that the transcription factor bZIP68 plays an important role in regulating plant growth and stress tolerance. Under normal conditions, bZIP68 suppresses expression of stress tolerance genes but promotes expression of growth related genes. Under oxidative stress, it becomes oxidized and inactivation, resulting in expression of stress-related genes and enhanced stress tolerance. bZIP68 might balance stress tolerance with growth through the extent of its oxidative inactivation according to the environment.

12102514.value: To optimize and characterize a novel immunoliposome-based drug delivery system targeting the tumor-associated cell surface antigen CA9. 12102514.label: Realisation of objectives
12102514.value: In this study, we have investigated the targeting capability of Carbonic Anhydrase IX(CA9), a cell surface antigen characterized by high expression in a variety of solid tumors and restricted expression in normal tissues. In the lung cancer, CA9 has been confirmed the present in malignant tumors, whereas all other normal lung specimens sampled at a distance from the tumor are negative. We have developed an immunoliposome by conjugating CA9 antibody as the drug carrier system targeting CA9, and integrate the technology of liposome with triptolid for lung cancer therapy. We have investigated the in vitro binding activity and cytotoxicity effect of this immunoliposome in human lung cancer cells. We have also investigated its biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy using a mouse lung cancer model. This study has been ultimately bring us closer to the realization of targeted cancer therapy through the use of immunoliposomes.

12102914.label: Realisation of objectives
12102914.value: 100% of the 6 objectives have been completed in this project. L6 aptamer has been renamed as CH6 aptamer based on our updated results. To test the CH6-mediated changes in cellular-level distribution and gene silencing efficiency for the osteogenic siRNA (objective 1), we examined the co-localization of Cy3-labeled siRNA and specific markers of different cells after the administration of siRNA delivered by LNPs, Rd-LNPs or CH6-LNPs in 6-month-old female Sprague-Dawley rats. Our results showed that CH6 facilitated specifically targeting osteoblasts and reducing exposure to osteoclasts, osteocytes, osteoclasts, macrophages, adipocytes endothelial cells and hepatocytes for siRNA (encapsulated in LNPs) in vivo. Plekho1 mRNA expression in rat bone marrow cells was examined after fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), the gene knockdown efficiency of Plekho1 siRNA delivered by CH6-LNPs was significantly higher in osteoblasts than that delivered by Rd-LNPs or LNPs. In contrast, there was no significant difference in the Plekho1 gene knockdown efficiency in non-osteoblasts after the administration of CH6-LNPs-siRNA, Rd-LNPs-siRNA or LNPs-siRNA. To test the CH6-mediated changes in dose-response pattern and persistence of gene silencing (objective 2), we used laser capture microdissection (LCM) in combination with real-time PCR to assess the expression of Plekho1 (CKIP-1) mRNA in osteoblasts after the admin¬istration of CH6-LNPs-siRNA, LNPs-siRNA or Rd-LNPs-siRNA. The Plekho1 gene knockdown efficiency increased in a dose-dependent manner at the siRNA dose ranging from 0.1 mg kg–1 to 1.0 mg kg–1 and almost 80% gene knockdown efficiency was achieved at an siRNA dose of 1.0 mg kg–1 in CH6-LNPs-siRNA group. After a single injection of siRNA formulations at an siRNA dose of 1.0 mg kg−1, our results showed that CH6-LNPs-siRNA maintained a low Plekho1 mRNA level (<50% of the Plekho1 mRNA level at baseline) for a longer time (~12 d) when compared to the other LNPs-based siRNA formulations or to (AspSerSer)6-liposome-siRNA (~7 d). To test the CH6-mediated changes in bone histomorphometric parameters/bone architecture/bone mass/bone mechanical properties (objective 3), we administered six periodic injections of Plekho1 siRNA (1.0 mg kg–1) encapsulated in LNPs with or without the linkage of CH6 aptamer to ovariectomized rats at an interval of one week. After treatment, all the in vivo microCT param¬eters, including bone mineral density (BMD), relative bone volume (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), trabecular separation (Tb.Sp), trabecular number (Tb.N) and structural model index (SMI), were obviously improved and were nearly restored to the pre-surgery levels in the OVX + CH6-LNPs-siRNA group when compared to the OVX + Rd-LNPs-siRNA group. Better-organized microarchitecture and higher bone mass were consistently found in trabecular bone from the OVX rats treated with CH6-LNPs-siRNA when compared to Rd-LNPs-siRNA. Histomorphometric analysis further demonstrated that the mineral apposition rate (MAR), bone formation rate (BFR/BS), osteoblast sur¬face (Ob.S/BS) and osteoblast number (Ob.N/B.Pm) were significantly increased from baseline and were obviously higher in the OVX + CH6-LNPs-siRNA group when compared to the OVX + Rd-LNPs-siRNA group after 6 weeks of siRNA treatment. A larger width between the xylenol and the calcein labeling bands was consistently found in the OVX rats treated with CH6-LNPs-siRNA compared to Rd-LNPs-siRNA. No significant difference between Oc.S/BS and Oc.N/B.Pm was found among the siRNA groups. Results from mechanical testing, bone turnover marker assays and microCT examination of cortical bone and fifth vertebrae also evidenced that CH6-LNPs-siRNA achieved a better therapeutic effect when com¬pared to the other siRNA groups. To detect the CH6-mediated changes in liver-related toxicity (objective 4), Liver function indicators (ATL and AST) in serum were determined in OVX rats administrated with CH6-LNPs-CKIP-1 siRNA. No obvious toxicity and immune response were found in rats after either a single dose or multiple doses of CH6-LNPs-siRNA. To investigate the mechanism of the L6-mediated siRNA cellular uptake and sub-cellular trafficking (objective 5), we labeled Plekho1 siRNA with Cy3 and incubated osteoblasts with different siRNA formula¬tions in the presence of Alexa Fluor 488–labeled endocytic markers. We detected by confocal microscopy numerous instances of co-localization of siRNA with transferrin (a marker for clathrin-mediated endocytosis) and dextran (a marker for macropinocytosis), but not with choleratoxin (a marker for caveolae-mediated endocytosis) in osteoblasts incubated with CH6-LNPs-siRNA, indicating that CH6-LNPs-siRNA can be taken up via clathrin-mediated endo¬cytosis as well as by macropinocytosis. In contrast, Rd-LNPs-siRNA and LNPs-siRNA were found to enter osteoblasts only via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Chemical inhibition experiments confirmed these findings from the confocal imaging. Additionally, confocal images showed that CH6-LNPs-siRNA induced membrane ruffling and lysosome escape of siRNA (attributes of macropinocytosis) in osteoblasts, but we did not observe this for either LNP-siRNA or Rd-LNP-siRNA. To identify the L6-specific target proteins on surface of osteoblasts (objective 6), we coupled Biotin-labeled CH6 aptamer with streptavidin-coated magnetic beads and incubated it with lysates of rat primary osteoblasts. The binding proteins of CH6 were extracted and subjected to subsequent silver staining. The specific band in CH6 extraction were excised and analyzed by MS. However, most of the high-ranked candidates remained unexplored and had unknown functions after searching in PubMed database, implying unknown characteristic receptors on surface of osteoblasts.

12102914.label: Major findings and research outcome
12102914.value: Metabolic skeletal disorders associated with impaired bone formation are major clinical challenges. RNA interference (RNAi) for promoting osteoblastic bone formation is a promising approach to the challenges. The bottleneck for translating RNAi with efficiency and safety to clinical bone anabolic strategy is to seek targeted delivery systems for osteogenic siRNAs. The applicants have identified (AspSerSer)6 as a target moiety specifically approaching bone formation surface and further validated that (AspSerSer)6 could facilitate osteogenic siRNAs targeting osteogenic cells to promote bone formation in rodents. However, the limitation of the specificity of the targeted delivery by (AspSerSer)6-liposome is not at cellular level but at tissue level, i.e. bone formation surface, which still cannot substantiality release concerns on efficacy and safety. Using cell-SELEX technology, the applicants obtained an aptamers CH6, which could target osteoblasts but not hepatocytes and PBCs in vitro. Thereafter, the applicants linked CH6 aptamer to the surface of the PEG-modified LNPs encapsulating osteogenic siRNA, i.e., CH6-LNPs-siRNA. CH6 aptamer facilitated the distribution of the siRNAs in bone and reducing their accumulation in liver in normal rats. We aimed to examine whether the CH6 aptamer could facilitate selectively targeting osteoblast for osteogenic siRNAs and subsequently promoting bone formation in established osteoporotic rodents. Our results showed that the osteoblast-specific accumulation of the osteogenic siRNA and gene knockdown efficiency was significant higher in rats treated with CH6-LNPs-siRNA when compared to rats treated with other siRNA formulations. Almost 80% gene knockdown efficiency was achieved at an siRNA dose of 1.0 mg kg–1 for CH6-LNPs-siRNA. CH6-LNPs-siRNA maintained a low Plekho1 mRNA level (<50% of the Plekho1 mRNA level at baseline) for a longer time (~12 d) when compared to the other LNPs-based siRNA formulations or to (AspSerSer)6-liposome-siRNA (~7 d). Bone formation and bone mass was dramatically improved in rats treated with CH6-LNPs-siRNA. No toxicity of CH6-LNPs-siRNA was detected in rats. Mechanistically, we found that the CH6 aptamer specifically induced macropinocytosis and facilitated siRNA entry in osteoblasts.

12102914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12102914.value: This study provides a novel aptamer-functionalized osteoblast-targeting delivery system for osteogenic siRNAs to advance the targeted delivery from tissue level toward cellular level. In future, we will validate the bone anabolic action of CH6-LNPs-siRNA in other osteoporotic animal models and facilitate the translation of RNAi-based clinical bone anabolic strategy in treating metabolic skeletal disorders associated with impaired bone formation.

12102914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12102914.value: Currently, major concerns about the safety and efficacy of RNA interference (RNAi)-based bone anabolic strategies still exist because of the lack of direct osteoblast-specific delivery systems for osteogenic siRNAs. Here we screened the aptamer CH6 by cell-SELEX, specifically targeting both rat and human osteoblasts, and then we developed CH6 aptamer–functionalized lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) encapsulating osteogenic pleckstrin homology domain-containing family O member 1 (Plekho1) siRNA (CH6-LNPs-siRNA). Our results showed that CH6 facilitated in vitro osteoblast-selective uptake of Plekho1 siRNA, mainly via macropinocytosis, and boosted in vivo osteoblast-specific Plekho1 gene silencing, which promoted bone formation, improved bone microarchitecture, increased bone mass and enhanced mechanical properties in both osteopenic and healthy rodents. These results indicate that osteoblast-specific aptamer-functionalized LNPs could act as a new RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy, advancing the targeted delivery selectivity of osteogenic siRNAs from the tissue level to the cellular level.

12103014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103014.value: Cancer, a leading cause of death in the world, has become the most onerous health problem that afflicts the world public. Many anticancer drugs have been developed in the last few decades, but all of them are limited in use due to their narrow therapeutic indices and severe side effects, and almost all of them will eventually encounter resistance from cancer cells. The search and discovery of novel anticancer agents are therefore imperative. Natural products have proven to be a rich source of anticancer compounds with more than half of the current agents in clinical use being such molecules. In our ongoing search for novel anticancer active compounds from plant resources, a cluster of novel compounds with a rare C-18 skeleton, designated as the miliusanes, were discovered from Miliusa sinensis. These plant natural compounds displayed potent activity against a panel of human cancer cell lines in in vitro, as well as, in in vivo studies. In a hollow fiber in vivo mouse model study, two miliusanes showed potent inhibition against cancer cell growth. Xenograft mouse model experiment using HCT116 human colon cancer cell line further revealed that one of the miliusane compounds showed significant tumor inhibition response at the doses of 20 and 30 mg/kg. Further, three miliusanes (miliusol, miliusate and miliusane I) were evaluated in the NCI 60 cell line panel, and the NCI 60 cell line COMPARE analysis revealed that this group of compounds may possess a potentially novel anticancer mechanism of action. Thus, considering their anticancer potency and structural novelty, this type of molecules are deemed worthy of in-depth chemical and biological studies. The current project is our continuing efforts to discover novel and potent anticancer agents in order to develop new chemical entity drugs amenable to the treatment of cancer. To achieve this goal, the following objectives and tasks are proposed: 1) to elucidate anticancer effects of the miliusanes through different approaches including characterization of transforming phenotype and cDNA gene analysis; 2) to synthesize structurally novel miliusane derivatives to optimize their anticancer activities and therapeutic potentials; 3) to assess the anticancer efficacy of the newly synthesized miliusanes through in vitro and in vivo studies as well as to determine the pharmacokinetic effects of the selected miliusanes in animals. It is our expectation that anticancer candidates with strong therapeutic efficacy will emerge upon the completion of the proposed studies.

12103014.label: Realisation of objectives
12103014.value: A.1. Isolation of Miliusanes from Miliusa balansa (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.2) We identified the anticancer miliusane compounds including miliusol and miliusate from Miliusa sinensis (please see the attached our publication: Zhang et al., 2016). In our attempt to accumulate sufficient amounts of miliusol (1) and miliusate (2), the starting compounds for synthesis of miliusane analogs, we isolated additional 17 miliusanes (3-19) including 11 novel ones (5 and 10-19) from M. balansae [the numbering of the compounds is based on Figure 1 of our attached manuscript that was submitted to Journal of Medicnal Chemistry and is now under revision: Xu et al., 2018 (the manuscript is coded as JMC2018 for the subsequent reporting)]. A.2. Synthesis of Miliusane Analogs (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.3) We synthesized 17 miliusane analogs (20-36) (please see their structures in Scheme 1 of JMC2018; compounds 33-36 are included in the two attached patents). They were synthesized via modification of the functional groups of the naturally abundant miliusol (1) and miliusate (2). These compounds were also included in our granted US patent 9,695,141B2 (attached: Zhang & Guan, 2017). In this patent, we included two other new miliusane analogs: 5-(p-trimethylammonio-benzoyl)miliusol iodide (33) in Scheme 11 and 5-(p-dimethyl-aalyl-ammonio-benzoyl)miliusol bromide (34) in Scheme 12). Miliusanes 33 and 34 are two miliusane ammonium salts, which are soluble in water. In another granted US patent US9,822,071B2 (attached: Zhang, 2017), we patented miliusane lactams, exemplified by N-(n-butyl)-miliusol lactam (35) and N-phenyl-miliusol lactam (36). A.3. Assessment of Cancer Cell Killing Activity of Miliusanes In Vitro (to fulfill Objective 3: b.3.2) The cytotoxicity of the isolated miliusanes were evaluated against HCT116, A375 and A549 cells. Among the 19 natural miliusanes, 1-3, 7-9 and 16 were the most active ones with IC50 values ranging from 1-5 µM (see Table 4 in JMC2018). According to the NCI-60 cell line data (see Figures S102-S105 of JMC2018 supporting information), the evaluated natural miliusanes 1-3 were very susceptible to the colorectal cancer cells with GI50 values in the range of 0.21-2.24 µM; thus, HCT116 cell line was used as the cellular platform to evaluate the cytotoxicity of the synthesized miliusane analogs. From the data shown in Table 5 of JMC2018, four synthetics, 20 (p-dimethylamino-benzoyl-miliusol) and 25-27, displayed anti-proliferative effect on HCT116 cells equivalent to the natural miliusanes 1 and 2. Compounds 20, 26 and 27 are nitrogen containing miliusanes, which can be made as water soluble salts. A.4. Elucidation of Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) of Miliusanes (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.3) The isolated and synthetic miliusanes (1-32) were evaluated for their cancer cell killing activity against HCT116. By analyzing the SAR of these compounds, we concluded some important SAR information summarized in Figure 6 of JMC2018. In particular, we found that the functional groups at C-4 appear the key binding site for particular molecular target(s) whilst the presence of an α,β-conjugated system is not critical to the enhancement of anticancer activity. A.5. Characterization of Transforming Phenotypes of Miliusanes Treated Cancer Cells (to fulfill Objective 1: b.1.2) To investigate the impact of miliusanes on cell transformation, division and migration, we examined if miliusanes might be effective against reproductive integrity, tumorigenicity and metastasis of HCT116 cancer cells, and further determine their cell cycle and apoptosis effects. The natural miliusanes 1-3 and the synthetic analogs 20 and 27 were selected for these tests. In colony formation assays, 20 is among the best to inhibit the formation of HCT116 colonies (see Figure 7 of JMC2018). In cell cycle control assays, 1 and 2 were shown to target cell cycle transition from G1 phase into S phase (see Figure 12 of JMC2018 as well as Figures 4 and 5 of the Mid-Term Progress Report). However, the miliusanes showed no cell motility reduction effects in wound-healing assays, nor did they show apoptotic effects up to IC50 concentrations. We further examined them in senescence assays. As shown in Figure 13 of JMC2018, the treatment with miliusanes caused discernible senescence in the HCT-116 cells. Backed up by the significant cell cycle arrest at G1 and the positive signals of SA-β-gal staining, we suggest that miliusanes are potential cellular senescence inducers. A.6. Miliusanes Targeted Signaling Pathways Identified (to fulfill Objective 1: b.1.3) Since we have already determined the anticancer effect of miliusanes might be correlated with their induction of senescence (see section A.5), it has no need to carry out the global gene expression experiments using cDNA microarray analysis. We then focused on the pathways caused by miliusane induced senescence. We examined the expression levels of a panel of senescence-related genes by means of qPCR array profiling. Among the 84 testing genes, at least 30 were significantly altered in the HCT-116 cells upon the treatment with 1 or 20 (see Figures 14A and 14B of JMC2018). In particular, we noticed that 20 up-regulated the transcript levels of TP53 (p53) and CDKN1A (p21). At the translational level, the expression of p21 was prominently elevated in the HCT-116 cells after the 48 h treatment of 1, 2 or 20 whilst the increase of p53 was subtler (see Figure 14C of JMC2018). Based on our qPCR and immunoblotting results, the molecular mechanism of miliusanes in the HCT-116 cells involved the activation of the p53-p21 axis. In parallel with the p53-p21 axis, the p16/RB cascade has also been suggested a major regulatory mechanism of cellular senescence, as well as a tumor suppressor pathway. In our study, the application of 20 indeed enhanced the expression of p16 (see Figures 14D of JMC2018). The expression alteration of p21 and p16 was also observed in the miliusane-treated tumors (see Figure 15 of JMC2018). Our results suggest that the anti-proliferative effect of miliusanes is conceivably derived from the p21-dependent and p16-associated execution of senescence. A.7. Assessment of Antitumor Activity of Miliusanes In Vivo (to fulfill Objective 3: b.3.3) Since 1, 20, 26 and 27 showed cancer cell killing activities in vitro, their in vivo efficacies were subsequently validated in the tumor xenograft-bearing mice. Our previous animal data showed that 1 could significantly restricted the tumor growth [see Figure 8 (A-1-A4) of JMC2018]. In a further trial, we evaluated the tumor inhibitory effect of 1 (7.5 mg/kg), 20 (10/20 mg/kg) and the clinical drug paclitaxel (7.5 mg/kg). In this trial, the growth of the HCT116 xenograft tumors was significantly reduced by treatment of 20 and 1 [see Figure 8 (B-1-B4) of JMC2018]. However, all mice of the paclitaxel group died in the treatment period, indicating that 20 and 1 have lower in vivo toxicity than paclitaxel, which was also confirmed by our toxicity study (see Figure 10 of JMC2018). In two other trials, 26 (20/40 mg/kg) and 27 (20/40 mg/kg) were also tested against the xengraft HCT116 tumor growth in comparision with 20 (20 mg/kg), paclitaxel (10 mg/kg) or another clinical used drug 5-FU (fluorouracil) (25 mg/kg). The tumor inhibitory activity of 26 and 27 was less potent than that of 20, though 27 caused a restriction of HCT116 xenograft similar to 5-FU [see Figures 8 (C-1-C4 and D1-D4) of JMC2018]. Since 1 and 20 effectively restricted the growth of HCT116 xenograft tumors, their antitumor efficacies were further validated in nude mice bearing xenografts of HeLa human cervical carcinoma and A375 human melanoma (see Figure 9 of JMC2018). Taken together, miliusanes appear a unique type of antitumor agents with low toxicity profile when compared to paclitaxel.

12103014.label: Major findings and research outcome
12103014.value: 1) We isolated 19 natural miliusanes including 11 new ones (Xu et al., 2018). 2) We further synthesized 17 new miliusane analogs including 9 nitrogen containing miliusanes (Xe et al., 2018; Zhang & Guan, patent 2015; Zhang, patent, 2017). 3) The isolated and synthetic miliusanes were evaluated for their cell killing activity in vitro, and most of them showed inhibitory activity against a panel of cancer cell lines. Several of them displayed comparable activities as those of miliusol and miliusate, the anticancer active lead compounds identified in our previous study (Xu et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2016). 4) Based on the Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) analysis of the miliusanes, we found that the functional groups at C-4 appear the key binding site for particular molecular target(s) whilst the presence of an α,β-conjugated system is not critical to the enhancement of anticancer activity (Xu et al., 2018). 5) We then investigateed the impact of miliusanes on cell transformation, cell division and cell migration, and found that the miliusanes are regulators of cell cycle transition from G1 phase to S phase and were potential cellular senescence inducers (Xu et al., 2018). 6) Using several techniques such as qPCR array filing and immunoblotting assays, we determined that the anti-proliferative effect of miliusanes is conceivably derived from the p21-dependent and p16-associated execution of senescence (Xu et al., 2018). 7) Since several miliusanes including three synthetic analogs displayed potent cancer cell killing activities in vitro, these compounds were further evaluated for their antitumor efficacy in xenograft mouse models using human HCT116 (colorectal), Hela (cervical) and A375 (melanoma) cancer cell lines. All the tested miliusanes demonstrated restriction of tumor growth comparable or even superior to the mainstay chemotherapeutics paclitaxel or fluorouracil (5-FU). Our animal trials and toxicity study also indicated that these miliusanes had much lower in vivo toxicity than paclitaxel. The miliusanes are considered as (Xu et al., 2018). 8) Four research papers have been published (Li et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2016; Guo et al., 2017), and one is under revision (Xue et al., 2018). 9) Two US patents were granted. 10) The study results have been presented in 11 conferences including 10 international ones. 11) In conclusion, our data showed strong evidences to support miliusanes as putative chemotherapeutic alternatives to the conventional apoptosis-inducing molecules in overcoming drug resistance.

12103014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103014.value: In the present study, we have determined miliusanes as potential novel therapeutic leads for cancer. Unlike many mainstay anticancer drugs, which cause cancer cell death through apoptotic induction, the anti-proliferative effect of miliusanes is positively correclated with induction of senescence. As senescence has been suggested as a tumor suppressive mechanism alternative to apoptosis, to develop miliusanes as senescence-inducing drug candidates appears beneficial and complementary to the clinical management of cancer malignancies. To achieve this goal, we will further synthesize other structurally novel miliusane analogs, particularly the C-4 nitrogen substituted analogs as our present studies have demonstrated the removal of the ,-unsaturated conjugate system can significantly lower toxicity while retain the antitumor activity. At the same time, we will develop an efficient total synthetic route to produce adequate amounts of miliusane compounds, which will relieve our burden to depend on the natural sources. On the other hand, we will implement different approaches such as affinity pull-down assays to determine the anticancer molecular target(s) of miliusanes, which, in turn can facilitate our rational synthetic design to optimize the drug properties of miliusanes. Upon implementation of the further proposed studies, we hope to identify suitable drug candidate(s) amenable to further preclinical/clinical studies.

12103014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103014.value: Cancer is a major public health burden in both developed and developing countries. In fact, cancer is one of the commonest causes of death worldwide, and the number of cancer patients continues to rise. The current therapies for cancer are not perfect and may cause serious undesirable side effects and rapid development of drug resistance in the cancer cells. In the present studies, we have obtained 36 miliusanes via isolation and structure modification, and further evaluated their anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. A number of these compounds were found to potently inhibit tumor growth in animal studies against colorectal, cervical and melanoma cancer cells. The antitumor potencies of the tested miliusanes are comparable or even superior to the mainstay drugs paclitaxel or fluorouracil (5-FU). Above all, these miliusanes showed minimal toxicity in vivo. Our further mechanism of action studies determined the antitumor activities of miliusanes are highly associated with the p21-dependent induction of cellular senescence. The results of our extensive studies suggest miliusanes are a new class of anti-proliferative remedies alternative to the mainstay apoptotic inducing agents, which are deemed to be potential antitumor candidates for further development as clinical therapeutics in the management of cancerous pathologies.

12103314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103314.value: 近緣種之間雜交產生的後代通常會表現出不育、發育缺陷甚至死亡等性狀，稱爲合子後的雜交不親和性。雜交不親和性在維持生物的遺傳穩定性方面有着重要的生物學意義，對其機理的探索在模式生物中一直是研究的熱點。以果蠅（Drosophila）爲例，由於許多果蠅近緣種之間可以交配並且產生少量可育的雜交後代，成爲研究雜交不親和性機理的重要模型。但該研究在其他生物當中則較爲罕見。秀麗隱杆線蟲（C. elegans）作爲一種較爲完善的模式生物，由於缺乏可與之交配並且產生可育後代的近緣種，而一直無法被應用於該項研究當中。這樣的近緣物種近期在另外一對線蟲中被發現，即C. briggsae和C.sp.9，使得在線蟲中研究雜交不親和性的遺傳與分子機理成爲可能。爲在線蟲中建立雜交不親和性的研究模型，本實驗室在C. briggsae染色體上隨機插入綠色熒光蛋白（GFP）標記，以雜交的方式將其引入到C.sp.9的基因組中。經過與C.sp.9的多次回交，雜交後代的基因組大部分來自C.sp.9，同時保留一小部分與GFP標記連鎖的C. briggsae基因組片段。通過鑑定C. briggsae基因組片段在染色體中的邊界，我們發現由於外源基因組片段的存在導致雜交後代表現出特定的雜交不親和性狀，比如雄性不育或死亡。進一步的研究表明導致雜交後代雄性不育或不活的位點主要分佈在線蟲X染色體的中部和右臂部分。該項工作爲種間雜交後代雄性不育或致死的分子機理研究提供了重要的試驗平臺，在線蟲研究領域中尚屬首例。在此次研究計劃中，我們將首先採用二代測序技術對C. briggsae和C. sp.9的基因組重新組裝，並進行相關的比較基因組學研究。接下來我們將採用轉錄組測序的手段，對雜交後代不育的雄性線蟲和親本可育的雄性線蟲的轉錄組進行比較分析，尋找在雜交後代性腺中異常表達的基因。我們將採用Southern blot和二代測序技術，進一步檢測雜交後代在C.sp.9的基因組背景下，外源的C. briggsae基因組片段中特有的轉座因子是否被激活。我們之前的研究結果顯示，在C. sp.9的X染色體上存在一個長約490-Kb的位點，在雜交後代中如果該位點被C. briggsae基因組片段所取代，將導致雜交後代雄性死亡。因此我們將對該位點做進一步的分析與鑑定。該研究工作將在分子水平上闡述線蟲近緣種之間雜交後代雄性不育或致死的調控機理。

12103314.label: Realisation of objectives
12103314.value: Realization of objectives for the project HKBU12103314 Prepared by Dr. ZHAO Zhongying Department of Biology, HKBU All the objectives of this proposal have been achieved, and the major finding of the project was published in Genome research, 2016 Sep;26(9):1219-32. doi: 10.1101/gr.204479.116. The details on the objective realization are elaborated below. Objective 1. To determine the differential expression of both mRNAs and non-coding small RNA genes between the hybrid sterile males and those of C. briggsae or C. sp.9 with RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq). We have performed RNA-seq experiments for both mRNAs and small RNAs in both parental males and their hybrid males between C. briggsae and C. sp.9, now renamed as C. nigoni, to understand the molecular mechanisms of hybrid male sterility. We found dysregulation of one subclass of small RNA, i.e., 22G RNAs, is responsible for specific downregulation of spermatogenesis genes in the sterile hybrid carrying an introgression. The findings were published in Genome research, 2016 Sep;26(9):1219-32. doi: 10.1101/gr.204479.116 and in, PLoS Genetics, 2015 Feb 18;11(2):e1004993. doi: 10.1371/journal.pgen.1004993. Objective 2. To examine the potential activation of C. briggsae specific transposable elements in an otherwise C. sp.9 background of hybrid sterile males using Southern blot and NGS. By contrasting the expression profiles of both mRNAs and small RNAs, we identified no significant activation of C. briggsae specific transposable elements in an otherwise C. sp.9 background of hybrid sterile males. However, we observed unexpected dysregulation of 22G RNAs, which appeared to be mis-routed to target male-specific genes for downregulation rather than upregulation as they usually do. We performed NGS and PCR to quantify the copy number for the C. briggsae specific transposable elements, and again, we found no significant increase in their copy number, indicating that the transposable elements are not activated in the hybrid background. Objective 3. To attempt to further narrow down the interval of male inviable or sterile loci mapped onto the X chromosome by repeated back-crossing followed by PCR-based genotyping. We performed additional backcross from 15 generations to 50 generations for all the introgressions that produce hybrid male sterility or invialibity. Unfortunately, we achieve few more recombination after the intensive backcrossing. To unravel the mechanism of the underlying resistance in recombination, we recently produced a novel genome assembly of C. nigoni with chromosome level of continuity. Comparison of genomes between C. briggsae and C. nigoni, we found wide-spread of genome rearrangements and insertions and deletions (indels) in addition to the high divergence of genomic sequences (with an overall of less than 80% at DNA sequence level). We postulate that the divergence in genomes and chromosome rearrangements contribute to the recombination resistance.

12103314.label: Major findings and research outcome
12103314.value: It is well known that closely related species are able to mate with each other, but their hybrid offspring are frequently sterile or inviable. This is particularly the case for male progeny, a phenomenon called post-zygotic hybrid incompatibility (HI). Mechanistic research into HI lies at the heart of biology because it limits gene exchanges between species, leading to relative genetic stability of a living species. The genetics of HI have been intensively studied in Drosophila species, but remains poorly defined in other species. Nematode C. elegans as a well-established genetic model organism lags far behind Drosophila species in HI study primarily because of the lack of a sister species with which C. elegans can mate and produce viable progeny. The recent discovery of C. briggsae sister species, C. sp.9, now renamed as C. nigoni, opens the possibility of investigating genetic and molecular mechanism in nematode species. To empower the nematode species pair as a model for HI study, we previously generated 96 chromosomally integrated green fluorescent protein (GFP) insertions as the dominant markers in C. briggsae and physically mapped them into defined genomic regions. Aided by the introgression, we dissected the genome-wide patterns of HI between the two nematode species. Intriguingly, we observed that multiple hybrid male sterile or inviable loci are predominantly located on the X chromosome, which provides a framework for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of interspecific HI phenotypes in nematode species for the first time. To characterize the molecular mechanisms of hybrid male sterility and inviability produced by X-linked C. briggsae introgression in an otherwise C. nigoni background, we performed RNA-seq analyses for both mRNAs and small RNAs in both parental males and their hybrid males between C. briggsae and C. nigoni. We found unexpected dysregulation of one subclass of small RNA, i.e., 22G RNAs, is responsible for the specific downregulation of spermatogenesis genes in the sterile hybrid carrying an introgression. However, we identified no significant activation of C. briggsae specific transposable elements in an otherwise C. nigoni background of hybrid sterile males. The findings were published in Genome research, 2016 Sep;26(9):1219-32. doi: 10.1101/gr.204479.116 and in PLoS Genetics, 2015 Feb 18;11(2):e1004993. doi: 10.1371/journal.pgen.1004993. There are total of 6 journal publications that were completely or partially supported by the grant. The funding also supported one PhD and one Mphil student. It also supported attendance of four international conferences (See Research output).

12103314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103314.value: This project established the unexpected role of small RNAs in regulation of hybrid male fertility. Given the functional roles of small RNAs in manipulating chromatin architecture and epigenetic landscape, the results have laid down a framework for further characterization of chromatin architecture and epigenetic landscape in the parental males and hybrid sterile males, which could provide further insights into the mechanism of hybrid male sterility.

12103314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103314.value: Hybrid incompatibility (HI) prevents gene flow between species, thus lying at the heart of speciation genetics. One of the most common HIs is male sterility. Analysis of gene expression in Drosophila hybrids suggests a genetic interaction between the X Chromosome and autosomes that is essential for male fertility. However, the prevalence of such an interaction and its underlying mechanism remain largely unknown. In this funded project, we examined the interaction in nematode species by contrasting the expression of both coding genes and transposable elements (TEs) between hybrid sterile males and its parental nematode males. We used two lines of hybrid sterile males, each carrying an independent introgression fragment from Caenorhabditis briggsae X Chromosome in an otherwise Caenorhabditis nigoni background. We observed a similar pattern of down-regulated genes that are specific for spermatogenesis between the two hybrids. Importantly, the down-regulated genes caused by the X Chromosome introgressions show a significant enrichment on the autosomes, supporting an epistatic interaction between the X Chromosome and autosomes. We investigated the underlying mechanism of the interaction by measuring small RNAs and found that a subset of 22G RNAs specifically targeting the down-regulated spermatogenesis genes was significantly up-regulated in hybrids, suggesting that perturbation of small RNA-mediated regulation may contribute to the X-autosome interaction.

12200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200114.value: 近年來，各種信息網絡的快速發展已經產生大量網絡數據。網絡數據可被廣泛用於各種數據分析任務，但也使得個人隱私安全變得愈加嚴峻。以往的經驗表明僅僅依靠政策法規既不能提供有效的隱私保護，也不能保證數據分析的效用。技術手段對於同時保證所發布網絡數據的隱私和有用性具有不可或缺的作用。早期的網絡數據發布研究通常針對特定類型的隱私攻擊，使得相應隱私保護方法無法防範具有較強背景知識的攻擊者。因此開發具有可靠隱私保證的新型隱私保護技術顯得日益重要。本項目基於最新提出的差分隱私模型來獲得不依賴於攻擊者所擁有背景知識的隱私保證。其中，差分隱私要求數據庫的所有分析結果不過分依賴一個特定用戶，從而保證加入數據庫不會帶來隱私泄漏。差分隱私下的網絡數據發布具有很大挑戰性。這不僅僅因為網絡數據拓撲結構的固有復雜性，也因為網絡對細微結構變化的高度敏感性。在本項目中，我們將探索新穎實用的滿足差分隱私的網絡數據發布技術。核心是把該問題轉化為對輸入網絡數據對應的鄰接矩陣進行基於密度的探索和重構。這一轉變能有效解決網絡數據發布中的技術難點。為此，我們將研究以下問題：(1) 尋找能使鄰接矩陣形成稠密區域的節點標簽方案；(2) 設計自上而下的自適應切割過程以探索稠密區域；(3) 開發基於雙聚類的稠密區域提取框架；(4) 設計效用損失最小化的高效稠密區域重構算法。最後，我們將開發一個通用的保護隱私的網絡數據發布框架，並通過大量真實海量數據和不同數據分析任務來驗證該框架的有效性。我們希望此研究成果成為第一個能在差分隱私下有效處理海量網絡數據的框架，並有效緩解公眾因網絡數據分享所帶來的隱私顧慮。

12200114.label: Realisation of objectives
12200114.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have defined quality metrics for a vertex labeling scheme that exploits the final utility of the entire solution. A general swap-based differentially private algorithm has been designed for finding the best vertex labeling. Using the vertex labeling identified, we can construct an adjacency matrix of the input network dataset. Based on that, we have designed a top-down partitioning process guided by density to identify dense regions of the graph for efficient sanitization. To make this top-down partitioning process effective, we have conducted a thorough investigation on the impact of different space-partitioning structures and designed a concrete formulation of density contrast to guide the partitioning process. Moreover, we have studied to find denser areas via biclustering. As the biclustering problem are NP-complete, we have developed an efficient biclustering framework that suits sparse adjacency matrices while satisfying differential privacy. We have further designed new efficient edge arrangement schemes that achieve better accuracy and are more stable to different vertex labelings. A group-and-conquer strategy has also been proposed to reconstruct the dense regions so as to generate the sanitized network graph under differential privacy.

12200114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200114.value: To address the privacy issue in data publication, we have considered the problem of releasing high-dimensional data with differential privacy guarantees. We proposed a novel solution to preserve the joint distribution of a high-dimensional dataset. We first developed a robust sampling-based framework to systematically explore the dependencies among all attributes and subsequently build a dependency graph. This framework is coupled with a generic threshold mechanism to significantly improve accuracy. We then identified a set of marginal tables from the dependency graph to approximate the joint distribution based on the solid inference foundation of the junction tree algorithm while minimizing the resultant error. We have proved that selecting the optimal marginal with the goal of minimizing error is NP-hard and, thus, designed an approximation algorithm using an integer programming relaxation and the constrained concave-convex procedure. Extensive experiments on real datasets show that our solution substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors. We have also studied the problem of publishing high-dimensional data in a distributed multiparty environment under differential privacy. In particular, with the assistance of a semi-trusted curator, the involved parties (i.e., local data owners) collectively generate a synthetic integrated dataset while satisfying ε-differential privacy for any local dataset. To solve this problem, we have presented a differentially private sequential update of Bayesian network (DP-SUBN) solution. In DP-SUBN, the parties and the curator collaboratively identify the Bayesian network N that best fits the integrated dataset D in a sequential manner, from which a synthetic dataset can then be generated. The core of DP-SUBN is the construction of the search frontier, which can be seen as a priori knowledge to guide the parties to update N. To improve the fitness of N and reduce the communication cost, we introduced a correlation-aware search frontier construction (CSFC) approach, where attribute pairs with strong correlations are used to construct the search frontier. Extensive experiments on a real dataset demonstrate that DP-SUBN offers desirable data utility with low communication cost. In addition, we have investigated private approaches for subgraph query services on outsourced network data and probabilistic queries on uncertain graph networks.

12200114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200114.value: As for further development, we plan to extend the proposed techniques for differentially private network data publication in two directions. First, we are going to study the scenario of continuous data release, where the temporal correlation among continuously generated network data can be learned by adversaries. As such, a traditional differential private mechanism may suffer from potential privacy loss under temporal correlations. Therefore, it calls for more sophisticated solutions to coping with temporal privacy leakage. Second, we will investigate differential privacy techniques to local settings. Local differential privacy techniques enable the gathering of statistics while preserving privacy of individual users. We are going to design efficient protocols for estimating frequencies and distributions of statistical values under local differential privacy.

12200114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200114.value: The recent rapid rise of information networks in various application domains has generated enormous network data, which are typically represented as graphs with nodes corresponding to a set of individuals and edges corresponding to connections between them. While network data have flourished a wide spectrum of data analysis tasks, it makes individual privacy more subject to intrusions than ever before. For example, the privacy breach of the social networking site LivingSocial this year affected more than 50 million users. As a precaution, the Hong Kong Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data has organized liberal studies of personal privacy on social networking sites. Unfortunately, past experience has shown that policies and guidelines alone are unable to provide either adequate privacy protection or meaningful utility for data analysis. Technical efforts are indispensable to make published network data both private and useful. In this project, we have investigated novel practical techniques for non-interactive network data publication under differential privacy. Being the first framework that is capable of sanitizing large-scale real-life network data under differential privacy, our research findings can facilitate the dissemination of network data by easing different stakeholders’ anxieties concerning privacy risks.
