12200714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200714.value: Environmental contamination by pharmaceutical residues (PRs) represents an emerging concern for sustainability of public health and the environment, particularly in rapidly urbanizing areas. Recent studies have confirmed that risks to ecosystems and human populations must be examined more thoroughly and high priority research needs are identified. Documented ecological impacts from PRs include but do not limit to extensive mortality of vultures on Indian subcontinent and feminization of gudgeon. This problem has not been contained despite initial actions from Europe and the USA. One reason is that world’s drug demand has been increasing due to ageing and increasing population. Important information, e.g. how much and what type of PRs are being added to the environment every year, where in the built environment is the best place to remove them from entering the environment and what schemes are most effective in collecting unused pharmaceuticals, are largely unknown for Asian countries including China. Although environmental information in general are more complete and readily available in Hong Kong, a Special Administrative Region of China, than other Chinese cities, the sources and the environmental effect of PRs in Hong Kong are similarly unknown. Further, available information collected using robust analytical methods and QAQC programs are largely lacking from this region. Thus, it is imminent to initiate a surveillance program and develop an effective reverse logistics scheme to arrest the growing problem in such a fragile and stressed environment before irreversible damages are inflicted. There are two main sources of environmental PRs. One is discharges from drug manufacturing plants and another, which is also believed to be the main source, is through routine domestic application and consumption. This study focuses on the management of the latter. A comprehensive survey on the general public will be conducted to find out the estimated amount of unwanted pharmaceuticals generated from Hong Kong. A series of interviews with primary stakeholders such as pharmacy operators and (outpatient) clinics will be conducted to examine the possibility of setting up a return programme within this network. A parallel workstream is to measure the environmental concentrations of targeted pharmaceuticals, including antibiotics, and other effluent tracer in the wastewater system and aquatic ecosystems in Southern China. This information will then be translated using a novel modeling approach to estimate surface water quality hazards. The feasibility of a setting up the take-back logistics of unwanted pharmaceutical will be examined to conclude this study. 近些年來, 藥物殘留(PRs)所造成的環境污染越發被人們所關注。尤其在快速城市化的發展區域，PRs的存在逐漸成為危害公眾健康的新威脅, 因此, 我們迫切需要就PRs對生態系統和人類的危害進行有系統的研究。目前的研究表明，環境中的PRs可能是導致印第安大陸禿鷹大量死亡，以及淡水環境中白楊魚(gudgeon)雌性化的原因之一。隨著世界性的人口增長和老齡化加劇，藥物的需求也在不斷的增加。儘管歐美國家已經有所行動，但隨PRs而來的環境問題並未得到足夠的重視。 目前，亞洲國家(包括中國)對有關PRs的重要訊息, 如PRs的年均排放量及種類、如何有效地阻止PRs的擴散、如何高效地收集剩餘藥物等所知極為有限。儘管香港特別行政區相比部分中國大陸地區有著更為完善的環境保護體系，但我們依然對PRs的具體來源，以及其對環境的影響缺乏足夠了解。因此，現階段我們並沒有足夠的資料與數據就香港地區的PRs作準確及高質量的分析。由於我們賴以生存的環境是非常脆弱，在污染對其造成不可逆轉的傷害之前, 我們迫切需要建立起有效的PRs污染監視系統和藥物回收渠道。 研究顯示，環境中PRs有兩個主要來源，一是藥廠的排放，二是市民的藥物使用與消費，而我們的研究主要集中在後者。我們將會向公眾作問卷調查，並與藥房和門診所等直接相關方溝通，用以了解在香港地區設立藥物回收系統的可能性。與此同時，我們的研究團隊會測量目標藥物(包含抗生素以及排放物指標)在廢水處理系統和中國南海海洋生態系統中的環境濃度。以上的數據將會被應用在檢測表層水體PRs污染的前沿科學模型里以估算PRs對地表水體的危害; 最後我們會為剩餘藥物回收系統作可行性評估。

12200714.label: Realisation of objectives
12200714.value: Objective 1 - This objective is 100% achieved. By conducting a fully supervised questionnaire survey in 7 samples points covering the three major regions (Hong Kong Island, Kowloon & the New Territories) in Hong Kong, with 1835 usable datasets obtained, it is found that each respondent is keeping 138.4 gm of drugs at home. With a population of 7.35 million in mid-2016, it is equivalent to 1017 tonnes of stored up medicine just in the domestic sector. The predominant majority of these 1017 tonnes of drugs found at home are in tablet, capsule or powder forms. Cold drugs are the major type of medicine being stocked up by respondents, followed by anti-inflammatory and painkilling drugs and drugs for stomach. This can be explained by the easy availability of most common cold drugs in Hong Kong and the relatively high prevalence of common cold (among communicable diseases found in Hong Kong) in such a densely populated city. Objective 2 - This objective is 100% achieved. Results showed that the degree of support from the general public in Hong Kong for a waste medicine take back scheme was not high, with only less than 40% were wholehearted supporters and another 8.1% in Hong Kong professed that they would rather return some but not all medicine through this scheme (partial supporters). At the same time, 23.3% of the respondents would not participate in such a take-back scheme and another 28.8% would consider but undecided at the time of survey while others would participate with conditions. As a result, it appears that there is not even a clear majority support for an unused drug take-back scheme in Hong Kong. For the (wholehearted & partial) supporters of such scheme, they were asked to indicate their top three preferred take back locations/approaches out of the nine options set out in the questionnaire. Respondents were also given the option to provide their own suggestions beyond the nine stated. The top three most preferred take back locations are in the order of popularity, Western out-patient clinics, convenient stores that sell over the counter medicines and licensed pharmacies. A reason for hospitals to fall out of the top three choices is likely due to the fewer number of hospitals in the city when compared to Western out-patient clinics and licensed pharmacies. The fact that respondents prefer to return unused drugs at certain convenience stores indicate that just like other product take-back schemes, convenience is an important consideration for drug return. However, if unused drug return boxes are to set up in convenience stores, statutory exemptions to allow these stores to keep prescribed drug will need to be granted. This will involve amendment of current laws. Giving reminders (e.g. “Please support drug return”) when acquiring medicine can be an effective means to boost the participation rate of a drug take back scheme with 55.1 – 60.6% of respondents indicating support. Since this is 7-12% higher than there the aggregate of wholehearted and partial supporters (39.8%+8.1%), thus, it may be inferred that if a drug take-back programme is really launched, it is possible that some of the undeciders and even non-supporters may also take the advantage to drop off their unwanted medicines. In general, reminders (in the form of packaging label or additional information statement) relating to encouraging return of unused drugs and the harmful effects of improper drug disposal are effective in rendering 63.1% to 74.9% of the respondents to either more carefully disposing unwanted medicines or to take part in the unused drug return scheme. Objective 3 - This objective is 100% achieved. We selected the following facilities in Hong Kong and Taipei for an initial study to determine whether commonly used human antibiotics (cephalexin [CLX], chloramphenicol [CAP negative], ciprofloxacin [CIP], erythromycin [ERY], roxithromycin [ROX], trimethoprim [TMP], and sulfamethoxazole [SMX]) were present in the leachate and wastewater of these facilities: Hong Kong - Shuen Wan (SW), Pillar Point Valley (PPV) closed landfills and WENT (active) landfill Stonecutter Island Sewage Treatment Work North West Kowloon Primary Treatment Work (PTW) Kwai Chung PTW Tsing Yi PTW Chai Wan PTW Shau Kei Wan PTW Tseung Kwan O PTW Kwun Tong PTW To Kwa Wan PTW Taiwan - Dihua Wastewater treatment work (DHWWTW) Bali Wastewater Treatment Work (BLWWTW) For landfills, we analyzed the concentration of the 7 antibiotics in the raw and treated leachate of the 3 landfills mentioned for two times a year. For the 8 PTWs, we also analyzed the concentrations of the 7 antibiotics in the effluent of the 8 plants two times a year. For the Stonecutter Island Sewage Treatment Work, both the influent and effluent of the Plant were analyzed for the 7 antibiotics. This is similarly the case with DHWWTW and BLWWTW. Observations of each antibiotic were then compared diagnostically to minimal inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and predicted no effect concentrations (PNEC, or minimal selective concentrations) for the development of antibiotic resistance.

12200714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200714.value: In this study, it is found that 75% of the population has unwanted drugs at home and on average, each is storing up 182.4 gm with the major drug type being cold medicine. This phenomenon poses risk to the health of the householders (especially children) and the environment. In addition, undesirable phenomena, such as hoarding unused medicines beyond the originally prescribed time period and self-medication are common practices. Children’s accessibility to surplus medicine at home is still greater than desirable and most surplus medicine is improperly disposed. The general public’s support on a drug return scheme is lukewarm and their knowledge and awareness on proper drug handling still has rooms for improvement. With elevated levels of certain antibiotics found in the leachate of both currently active and those that have closed for 20 years in Hong Kong, there is good reason to believe that some of the antibiotics are not so environmentally recalcitrant under methanogenic conditions. Similarly, elevated levels of antibiotics were observed in all PTWs exceeding PNECs for TMP, CIP and ERY. PNEC values for development of antibiotic resistance were also observed for TMP and CIP in effluent discharges from Stonecutters Island of Hong Kong and BLWWTW and DHWWTW in Taiwan. In view of the extent of PNEC exceedance of CIP and to a lesser extent ERY and TMP for antibiotic resistance selection, policy intervention (e.g., tightening the enforcement of the chemical waste regulation and introduction of a drug take-back scheme for households to return their unused drugs, including but not limiting to antimicrobials) and further studies on the leachate plumes of other landfills and effluent discharges in Asia are much warranted.

12200714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200714.value: We plan on submitting future funding proposals to understanding temporal variability and subpopulation characteristics associated with medicine use and management in Asia.

12200714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200714.value: Households are storing >1200 tonnes of pharmaceutical products at any one time in Hong Kong. The majority of them will eventually be disposed with normal waste. As a result, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) are introduced into the leachate (wastewater from the landfill). In addition, wastewater is another source of APIs in the aquatic environment. This study confirms these two phenomena. It was found that all the seven antibiotics are present in both the raw and treated leachate of current and closed landfills as well as the influent and effluent of 8 urban sewage treatment plants in Hong Kong. Among the seven antibiotics tested, ciprofloxacin (CIP), a commonly used antibiotic to treat various infections (e.g.urinary tract infection), is found to reach levels far exceeding it predicted no effect concentration (PNEC) for the development of antibiotic resistance, meaning that the environments for the development of pathogens resistant to CIP do exist. This is similarly the case with the two urban wastewater treatment plants in Taipei. In view of the extent of PNEC exceedances, policy intervention (e.g., tightening the enforcement of the chemical waste regulation and introduction of a drug take-back scheme for households to return their unused drugs) are much warranted.

12200914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200914.value: 在各類基於地理位置服務中,地圖服務是核心。然而，最近有報導指出地圖服務商記錄及跟踪用戶瀏覽的地圖位置。這些記錄關乎用戶在醫療、金融及其他方面的個人隱私，因此受到了廣泛的關注。在本項目中，我們提出“隱身地圖瀏覽”的概念，即伺服器在提供用戶地圖上的興趣點（POI）資訊的同時，無法得知任何關於哪些興趣點被用戶訪問的資訊，從而使用戶得以“隱身”。 本項目的最大挑戰，是提供一種可驗證的隱私保護，使用戶在沒有可信第三方的前提下得到“隱身”，無論是進行興趣點查詢或是利用手勢在地圖上瀏覽。傳統隱私保護技術無法解決上述挑戰，因此我們將研究如何使用基於計算的私密資訊檢索（PIR）。雖然它曾被應用於時空數據庫中的若干問題，但所提出的解決方案都較特殊，無法應用於本項目。 為了解決私密資訊檢索的計算及通訊代價過大的問題，我們將改造經典的PIR方案，使其支持地圖中普遍使用的空間索引。除此之外，我們也會設計緩存及預取方案，進一步降低代價。 在隱私保護日益受關注的今天，本項目的實施對IT產業，尤其是地理位置服務，以及普羅大眾均大有裨益。

12200914.label: Realisation of objectives
12200914.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, we report that most objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have fully achieved objectives 1 and 2 by the end of year 2016, and objectives 3 and 4 by the end of year 2017, and mid 2018, respectively. For objective 1, our outcome is a computational PIR scheme with indexing support for the incognito browsing problem on spatial-temporal data. The first result focused on bichromatic reverse nearest neighbor query, which has been published in DASFAA 2015. We chose this query because it is a good abstraction of distance-based queries that we target on for this project. After that, we have put our efforts on generalizing this solution to the spatio-temporal data storage, authentication, and fast access on mobile devices. Based on computational PIR, this work further designed privacy-preserving access mechanism for both spatio-temporal data and their integrity checksum (namely, the prefix MAC, or PMAC). We also employed both R-tree and grid-file based indexes to speed up the private access. The result has been published in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing (TMC) in 2017. For objective 2, our TMC'17 work in the above also addressed the multi-object/node and continuous insertion and browsing problem by designing an aggregate scheme for the PMAC and associated index (either R-tree or grid-file). Our experiments showed that this approach, together with the proactive prefetching mechanism, can significantly reduce the access latency for continuous spatio-temporal data access and queries. As sometimes the spatial data can be symbolic (i.e., set-valued), we also set out to investigate the effect of aggregation on set-valued data. Our study showed that by employing suitable cryptographic tools such as bilinear paring and attribute-based encryption, the aggregation scheme can be efficiently extended to set-valued data. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE) in 2018. And an extended version that supports access control has been published in ACM SIGMOD conference in 2018. For objective 3, we have designed several techniques to ensure the privacy of spatial-temporal objects during incognito browsing. Our first work studied the problem of indoor location tracking and visualization. As the user movement is highly dynamic, we have adopted some alternative solutions without the use of a global index, as indicated in this objective. This work has been published in the 11th IEEE International Conference on Mobile Adhoc and Sensor Networks (MSN 2015). Our second work studied privacy-preserving spatio-temporal object sensing using oblivious RAM (ORAM), which is deemed as the dual technique of PIR with similar strong security guarantee. The application scenario is for mobile users to not only view the contents of neighboring POIs, but also modify or update (insert/delete) them without disclosing their location. We have integrated both ORAM and homomorphic encryption (HE), the enabling cryptographic tool for PIR to strike a balance between parallelism and POI group size. To further enhance the efficiency, we also designed a grid-file index and a comprehensive cost model to derive the optimal partition between ORAM and HE. The work is under the second round submission to IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC). Thirdly, we have also investigated the privacy-preserving release of spatial-temporal data trajectories for browsing. The work is based on l-diversity with enhanced privacy features on sensitive data attributes. The paper has been published and awarded the best paper in IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM) in 2019. For objective 4, we studied and addressed the computational efficiency problem of PIR and related approaches in the following directions. First, in our TDSC submission, we have investigated parallel homomorphic computation by dividing the whole space into grid cells and exploiting multi-core and multi/hyper-thread CPU architecture to speed up the cryptographic computation. Second, we have also designed a proactive prefetching mechanism in our TMC'17 paper to preload index snippets before any browsing/access request in the corresponding space of these snippets. Third, we have also explored several alternative mechanisms to PIR that can further reduce the computational overhead. For example, in SP'19 and ICDE'19, we attempted to leverage on local differential privacy and secret sharing respectively to hide the user's location or other spatial intents. Local differential privacy adds controllable noise, instead of applying encryption, onto the local requests/data. Normally, it is only suitable for statistical estimation on simple data types, such as categorical or binary values. Our work in IEEE S&P' 19 showed that by combining with prefetching and calibration techniques, set-valued and key-valued data of user intentions that originate from spatio-temporal data can be protected with similar theoretical guarantee as PIR (i.e., close to indistinguishability). Our work in ICDE'19 showed that if we assume the spatial data requested by users originate from two or more cloud sources, applying secret sharing techniques can significantly eliminate most of the heavy cryptographic computation and thus improve the efficiency of privacy-preserving spatial data access/browsing gestures as those supported by PIR. As another example, we have also explored the possibility of pre-compute and index spatial query results for fast access by private-preserving techniques such as PIR. In our VLDBJ'17 paper, we demonstrate the result of a complicate geo-social query can be efficiently pre-computed and indexed with moderate cost of update.

12200914.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200914.value: Our major research findings and outcome are listed as below. Due to space limitation, more technical details are presented in Section 5.3 as above. 1. A computational PIR scheme with indexing support for the incognito browsing problem on spatial-temporal data. The results are published in DASFAA 2015 and IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing (TMC) 2017. 2. An aggregate scheme and a prefetching scheme for MAC and index to support multi-object, multi-node browsing. The results are published in TMC17, IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE) 2018, and ACM SIGMOD conference 2018. 3. A privacy-preserving indoor location tracking and visualization system without a global index. The results are published in the 11th IEEE International Conference on Mobile Adhoc and Sensor Networks (MSN 2015) . 4. A privacy-preserving spatio-temporal object sensing mechanism using oblivious RAM (ORAM) and homomorphic encryption (HE). The results are submitted to IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC), under 2nd round review. 5. A privacy-preserving release of spatial-temporal data trajectories for browsing. The paper has been published and awarded the best paper in IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM) in 2019. 6. Local differential privacy technique for set-valued location data release for browsing. The results are published in the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 2019. 7. Secret sharing-based techniques that can eliminate most of the heavy cryptographic computation and thus improve the efficiency of privacy-preserving data access. The results are published in ICDE 2019. We have also been granted two US patents in this project. 1. H. Hu, Z. Chen, and J. Yu. "Privacy-Preserving Large-Scale Location Monitoring." US Patent No. 9,756,461, Sept 2017. 2. H. Hu, Q. Chen, and J. Xu. "Method and Apparatus for Assuring Location Data Integrity with Minimum Location Disclosure." US Patent No. 9,973,514 B2, May 2018.

12200914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200914.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our existing prototype system to make it suitable for commercial demonstration and knowledge transfer. We believe that the promotion of this prototype system will further make an impact on both research and industry community regarding our privacy-preserving spatial-temporal browsing and accessing maps for location-based services.

12200914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200914.value: Maps and location-based services (LBS) are popular mobile services for every walk of life. However, there has been growing concern about map service providers keeping track of user's browsing requests. In this project, we address the privacy requirement in map service and propose “incognito browsing”, where a user browses the map contents, such as points of interest (POI), without the server learning any information from his/her browsing request. Incognito browsing lays the foundation for privacy-preserving map service and has great potential in business planning, finance, marketing, and other sectors where privacy is essential. Despite the extensive literature on privacy protection, conventional techniques such as identity anonymizing do not work for incognito browsing. In this project, we investigate novel solutions based on modern cryptography, namely, computational private information retrieval (cPIR) and homomorphic encryption (HE), where a user can retrieve an item from a database of n items without revealing it. This project has designed a comprehensive set of spatial-temporal database techniques for incognito browsing. In particular, we have redesigned classic cPIR schemes to support spatial indexes, and devising prefetching techniques for consecutive browsing. The research outcomes can benefit the research community, the IT industry, and the public in Hong Kong.

12201214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201214.value: 浮遊植物細胞的識別與分析對水生態學和水環境監測具有重要意義。裸眼光學顯微鏡檢壹直是實驗室裏常規的識別與分析方法。然而，這種方法速度緩慢，在實踐中十分單調。此外，浮遊植物種類的鏡檢判別需要操作人員具有非常專業的技能和經驗，其準確性和效率會受到操作人員主觀差異的嚴重影響。 在信息時代，數字成像和計算機圖像處理技術的結合被人們公認為是壹種有可能替代人工操作，實現更可重復、更客觀、更高效的浮遊植物細胞群落分析的方法, 具有廣闊的應用前景。顯然，這壹策略的成功首先需要對浮遊植物細胞的成像具有高保真度和速度。針對這壹要求，兩種主流方法在對納米和微米尺度浮遊植物細胞成像應用中得到了長足的發展，分別是的自動化數字光學顯微鏡和成像流式細胞儀。自動化數字光學顯微可以獲得最佳的圖像質量，但它需要固定樣品，在實際應用中速度仍然太慢；成像流式細胞儀可以在浮遊植物細胞流動中對其進行成像，它在實驗室、現場、甚至水下原位等場合已經取得成功的應用，顯示出廣闊的前景。然而，橫向運動模糊和散焦是困擾現代成像流式細胞儀的兩大難題，會降低成像的速度和質量。此外，目前所有的成像流式細胞儀所獲取的都是浮遊植物細胞的二維圖像，而實際上浮遊植物細胞是具有復雜三維形態結構的，三維到二維信息的損失必然會阻礙後續圖像處理分析準確性的提升。 香港擁有很長的海岸線和許多淡水水體，但是卻缺乏用於諸如赤潮監測和水質評價等應用的浮遊植物自動化分析手段，大部分的水樣目前仍依賴緩慢的人工檢查分析。本項目旨在建立壹種新型的流式顯微技術，可以同時實現浮遊植物細胞顆粒（大於5微米）的暗場和熒光流式二維/三維成像，從而專門用於高通量浮遊植物細胞分析。除了高通量的優勢，這壹項目研究的方法還具有無橫向運動模糊和散焦的特點，可以實現對浮遊植物細胞顆粒內部葉綠體或全細胞的二維疊焦成像、三維輪廓和體成像。這壹新方法預計將能夠對浮遊植物細胞群落進行更快速、更準確的分析，不僅對本地水質監測十分有益，而且對藻類分類學、水生生態學、生物多樣性調查等科學研究具有十分重要的意義。

12201414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201414.value: Biometric security has been a serious concern ever since biometrics began to be widely used as a means of identity verification. Ranging from computer networks to a single datum, access is granted to a biometric user only after the user is authenticated by a biometric recognition system. High biometric system security is desirable to prevent illegitimate access by imposters. Otherwise, a security compromise could be devastating to the users, causing financial loss, identity abuse or even worse consequences. Biometric systems are designed to accept multiple similar biometric measurements per user due to inherent intra-class variations in the biometric data. This is important to preserve the acceptance rate of genuine queries and the overall feasibility of the recognition system. Compared to systems that only accept the same representation as the enrolled representation, maintaining equivalent genuine acceptance rate for systems accepting multiple measurements increases the chance for an imposter to obtain a system-acceptable measurement. Such deteriorated security of the system has to be measurable to provide truthful assurance of security to the users. Reliable security measures for biometric systems are essential to ensure the robustness of a system to adversarial attack. Entropy is a standard measure of security. However, the entropy formula is only applicable when the system accepts exactly the enrolled measurement. Applying this formula to the case of multiple system-acceptable biometrics would lead to an over-estimation of system entropy. To date, there is no appropriate measurement technique to evaluate system entropy. Although a few approaches estimate biometric security based on the hardness of adversarial guessing, none are directed at solving the problem of system entropy measurement. In this project, we work towards developing the first entropy-measuring model for a biometric system when multiple similar measurements are acceptable. We develop an entropy-measuring approach based on the notion of guessing entropy to quantify biometric system security in terms of adversarial guessing effort. We analyse and differentiate between two different attack scenarios where the adversarial guessing strategy may vary. For each scenario, we aim to seek an optimal guessing strategy such that the reflected entropy measure corresponds to the actual hardness (actual number of required attempts) of adversarial guessing in the real world. 自從生物特徵識別作為一種身份認證技術被廣泛使用後，系統安全已經成為一個關鍵問題。從大型網絡到個人計算機系統，用戶只需通過生物特徵識別系統的身份認證，即有訪問權限。為防止入侵者的非法訪問，生物特徵識別系統需要極高的安全性能。否則，系統一旦被入侵可能會招致用戶經濟損失、身份濫用或其它災難性的後果。 捕獲生物特徵數據時，由於無法控制的外部因素（如光照、用戶配合度等）的影響，同一用戶同一生物特徵，仍然會有一定程度的類內偏差。因此，生物特徵識別系統可以接受同一用戶的高度相似生物特徵以保證真實用戶接受率及系統可用性。相對僅接受完全相同數據的傳統密碼系統，該類系統通過接受多個相似的生物特徵以保證一定的真實用戶接受率的同時亦增加了入侵者獲取系統可接受的生物特徵的風險。為確保該類系統能給用戶提供可靠的安全性能，這種風險的增加必須是可以測量的。 可靠的安全性測量對於保證系統遭受攻擊時的魯棒性是至關重要的。熵是安全性的標準度量，但現時的熵測量方法僅適用於接受完全相同數據的傳統密碼系統的安全性測量，應用於接受多個相似生物特徵的系統時會導致偏高的熵測量值。迄今為止，對於生物特徵識別系統，尚未有合適的熵測量方法，儘管已有幾種基於攻擊困難度的系統安全測量技術，但沒有直接測量該類系統熵的方法。 本項目致力於針對可接受多個相似生物特徵的系統開發第一個熵測量模型。我們希望開發一個基於猜測熵的熵測量方法，該方法主要通過攻擊过程中的猜測難度來量化系統的安全性。由於攻擊過程中可能會有多種猜測策略，我們亦針對兩種不同的攻擊場景進行了區分以及分析。對於每一種攻擊場景，我們均致力於尋找最佳猜測策略以使所測量的熵能準確反映實際攻擊難度，即攻擊者在攻擊過程需要嘗試的實際次數。

12201414.label: Realisation of objectives
12201414.value: The original PI of this project was Dr. M H Lim. Since he left the university in 2016, Prof. Yuen (original Co-I) picked up the project. The three listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily along three main directions. Details are discussed as follows. First Objective: We have studied three guessing/attacking strategies for three attacking scenarios to evaluate the security strength of biometric systems from different perspectives. In the first scenario (sensor attack), we consider the whole biometric system as a “black-box” and the adversary could only attack the system by inputting the biometric data (e.g., face images and fingerprints). Since the adversary can only observe the final decision whether the input biometric is accepted or not, there is no attacking strategy that is better than the brute force. Note that the brute force here implies that the adversary tries the input biometric data one by one from a large collection of dataset. Besides, as the adversary could not observe the representation of the input biometric and therefore do not know which representation was guessed before. Therefore, we model the guessing strategy in this scenario as a sampling with replacement. In the second scenario (discretizer attack), we assume that the transmission between the client (senor and feature extractor) and server (remaining components) has been tapped by the adversary. The adversary can directly submit a biometric representation to the system and then observe the corresponding decision (accept or reject). In addition to the capabilities of the system, we also assume that the adversary has some knowledge (i.e., impostor distance distribution and matching threshold) about the target system. In this scenario, the optimal strategy for the adversary is to try the biometric representation of highest success probability at each trial. Different from the first scenario that previously rejected representations are not known, the adversary in this scenario can record the rejected representations. Therefore, we model the guessing strategy in this scenario as a sampling without replacement. In the third scenario (reconstruction attack), we consider the whole biometric system as a “black-box”, as in the first scenario. Beyond that, we have assumed that the representation (template) of the target user has been leaked and the adversary is able to obtain a “black-box” feature extractor of the target system. Under this scenario, the optimal strategy for the adversary is to learn a reconstruction model to reconstruct the raw biometric data from the leaked templates and then use the reconstructed data to access the target biometric system. In this project, we have attempted to reconstruct the face images from the state-of-the-art deep representations which are extracted using deep convolutional neural networks. A straightforward method is to design a de-convolutional neural network (D-CNN) with a large number of output channels (filters) in each de-convolution layer. However, it may result noisy and repeated channels. To address these issues, we have proposed a neighborly de-convolutional network framework (NbNet). To train such framework, a large number of face images are required. To do that, we have trained a face image generator to augment available public domain face datasets. We have also explored perceptual loss for training the NbNets, to further enhance the quality of reconstructed images. We have conducted comprehensive experiments to evaluate the proposed method. Second Objective: We have formulated the probability of adversarial success in obtaining one of the multiple system-acceptable binary representations at all possible trials for the first two attack scenarios (sensor and discretizer attacks) described in the realisation of the first objective. Note that the reconstruction attack of the third scenario is not iterative and therefore such probability formulations are not needed. For the first scenario, we have modeled the optimal attacking strategy as a sampling with replacement. Therefore, the attacking success rate of each trial remains the same. With our analysis, such success rate is the FAR of the target biometric system. Based on these analyses, we have formulated the guessing entropy of the target system as a function of the FAR. We have validated our formulation of guessing entropy under this scenario using attack simulation based on synthetic datasets. The reason why we use synthetic datasets is that generating binary representations of n-bit require at least 2^n samples. In practices, we are not able to have such a large-scale dataset even n is 64 or smaller because of the limitation of computation and storage. We have performed comprehensive experiments to support our theory. For the second scenario, we have modeled the optimal attacking strategy as a sampling without replacement. The most straightforward method for estimating the adversarial success probability is to estimate the occurrence probability of each representation by collecting a large-scale dataset. However, due to the large representation space (2^n possible representations for bit length n), there are often insufficient collected samples and insufficient memory for storing these estimated probabilities. Alternatively, we propose a new method for estimating the adversarial success probability, where the guessing strategy are revised accordingly. Note that the adversarial success probability and guessing strategy are closely related. The proposed probability estimation method is a function of impostor distance distribution and matching threshold. The basic idea is that, given an impostor (adversarial) representation, for each trial, we estimate the highest success probability of the representation modified from the given representation and then use it as the success probability of this trial. Since the previous unsuccessful trial would give information about the success of the incoming guesses, the success probability has to be updated after each trial. This causes the expensive computation cost of the probability estimation. In this project, in the first stage, we have formulated the probability term and justify its correctness by numerical analysis on the FERET face dataset using five different binary representations. Due to the expensive computational cost, we can only launch experiments on binary representations with bit length no greater than 18-bits. In the second stage, we have analyzed the probability terms of successive trials and then reformulate the probability term so that the calculations for the current trial can be reused by the forthcoming trials. We have justified the correctness of the re-formulated probability terms by numerically comparing the results. Furthermore, the re-formulated terms have partially helped us to estimate the guessing entropy of binary representations with up to 64 bits. Third Objective: We have formulated the upper bound as the average number of adversarial guesses required to obtain the first success for the scenarios as stated in the realization of the second objective (i.e., sensor attack and discretizer attack). This is an upper bound of the system security as the representations are assumed to be equal-probable. The lower bound of system security for the sensor attack scenario is found to be the same as the upper bound because both these bounds correspond to the brute force strategy. For the scenario of discretizer attack, we have also derived an upper and a lower bound of the system security after T-th guessing trials. Specifically, the expected number of guessing trials is a non-decreasing function of T, while T is also increasing. Therefore, the lower bound can be calculated by the expected number of guessing trials estimated based on the first T trials. We have conducted numerical analysis to justify the derived bounds.

12201414.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201414.value: To achieve the objectives stated above, we have investigated and studied different approaches for developing security evaluation methods to quantify the security of biometric recognition systems. The security strength of a biometric system varies from attacking scenarios and adversary’s strategy. In this project, we have addressed these issues from defining the practical scenarios, proposing optimal strategies, to studying the system security strength. Overall, we have studied the biometric system security strength in three different scenarios. For the first and second attack scenarios, we firstly model them as sampling with replacement and sampling without replacement, respectively. Secondly, we derive the upper bound of system security strength corresponding to these scenarios. The upper bound is derived with the ideal system assumption, where all the biometric representations are equally probable. Third, we propose the guessing strategy for both scenarios and formulate the corresponding probability of adversarial success with a different number of guessing trials. Finally, we justify our formulation with the numerical experiments on both synthetic and real datasets. These research findings have been reported in IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics [1]. The security evaluation method for the second attacking scenario (discretizer attack) is proven to be accurate but far from practical because of its expensive computational cost. To evaluate the system security strength under the discretizer attack, we have firstly studied the probability formulation of the adversarial success at different guessing trials and figured out the reusable computations for successive trials. Secondly, we have reformulated the probability terms such that the computations can be used. Third, we have also derived the error bound which guarantees to accurately estimate the security strength without computational expensively to launch all the guessing trials. Finally, we have empirically demonstrated that the numerical results are consistent, and the acceleration can be up to 200 times. These research findings have been reported in IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics [2]. For the third attacking scenario (reconstruction attack), we have proposed a neighborly de-convolutional neural network (NbNet) for reconstructing the face images from deep face templates. To train the NbNet, we have proposed a face image generating based training strategy and adopt the perceptual loss for maintaining the discriminative information in the reconstructed face images. Lastly, we have empirically demonstrated that the face images can be reconstructed from their corresponding deep templates. These research findings have been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence [3].

12201414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201414.value: For the security measurement under discretizer attack, we have accelerated it and made it can only be applied on 18 bits binary representations in our first version and become 64 bits in our second version. However, the size of the representations in practical systems can be hundreds or even thousands. One of the future studies along this direction is to further accelerate the security estimation by searching a tighter error bound or developing algorithms can be paralleled by GPU, FPGA, or even quantum computers. For the security evaluation under reconstruction attack, our current study is limited on the intra-system attack. The further research along this direction can be a cross-system attack. Moreover, we have only studied the attack on face recognition systems. The further studied can also be launched on other modalities such as fingerprint and iris.

12201414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201414.value: It is critical to evaluate the biometric system security to various potential attacks to serve as a criterion for selecting the systems with various security requirements. The performance of existing methods are not satisfactory because they are suffering from either inappropriate assumption about the biometric system or impractical assumptions about the attacking scenarios. To overcome these limitations, this project has developed new methods to properly evaluate the security strength of biometric systems with appropriate and practical assumptions. We have contributed to the biometric system security evaluation: for the sensor and the discretizer attack, we have introduced the guessing entropy for measuring the system security strength, where the proposed guessing entropy reflects the expected number of guessing trials in attacking the target biometric systems. Furthermore, different from existing methods work with the assumption that the biometric system is a single-acceptable-input system, our evaluation method considers biometric systems accept multiple inputs for a given subject. This is the nature of a biometric system to allow intra-subject variations. For the reconstruction attack, we have developed a face image reconstruction method to demonstrate the vulnerabilities of a biometric system in which the templates of the target users are leaked.

12201814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201814.value: This proposal of automatic incident classification (AIC) for large-scale traffic data is mainly to contribute to the development of traffic monitoring and managing for Traffic Control and Surveillance System (TCSS). An effective AIC method enhances the response time to traffic incidents and reduces massive human operators in operation. It should be capable to detect and classify a traffic incident from massive data and prevent the result from any corruption of data errors. Over decades, most previous research has mainly focused on the automatic incident detection (AID), with or without incident only. This means no detailed classification of traffic incidents was given. Also, they rarely dealed with data errors embedded on the dataset. Therefore, it is increasing a demand to develop a technology to improve the data quality and strengthen the discriminative power to detect and classify traffic incident. First, it is not straightforward to separate traffic incident and data errors. This proposal offers a new perspective to treat this problem from outlier detection and classification. Outliers are those inconsistent to the majority of data. Data errors and traffic incidents embedded in traffic datasets are outliers while others are regarded as inliers. Hence, this project will develop the AIC based on a framework of outlier detection and classification method. Second, traffic incident classification requires more advanced techniques and strong support of an accurate traffic incident detection result. Therefore, in this proposal, our AIC would firstly screen outliers (traffic incidents and data errors) and inliers (incident-free events) from massive traffic data by an outlier detection method with high detection rate. Then, our AIC will perform a finer outlier classification of detected anomalies for 7 outlier types, in which two types belong to data errors and five types belong to traffic incidents. This would contribute to the state-of-the-art TCSS with automatic and accurate traffic incident detection, and fine classification of traffic incidents. 這研究計劃主要是開發關於大量交通數據之自動化事件分類法，從而促進交通控制及監控中心(簡稱交控中心)在交通監察與管理的發展。一個有效之自動事件分類法，不單能加快交控中心對交通事故之反應，亦能減少大量人手操作的需求。這個交通數據自動化事件分類法之研究，會覆蓋兩個層面：一是從大數據中檢測及分類交通事件，二是能避免在數據傳送或儲存中的錯誤引起之數據失真。這方面有很多相類似的研究超過十年，可是都只作出簡單的自動化交通事件檢測，並沒有作出深入分類，這意味著其應用範圍十分有限。由於巳進入大數據年代，因此對技術上有關數據質量的保存、強化檢測及分類的能力，日益需求開發新理論和技術來應付。在這研究計劃的第一部份，首先會提供一個全新的角度去處理問題：分離體的檢測及分類。理論上，所有數據都包含著分離體及內層體。內層體是指數據內之正常部份及佔大多數，分離體是指與內層體相反的少數族群。在交通數據內，分離體是指數據錯誤和交通事件兩大類，內層體則包括所有正常的交通狀況下之數據。是故這研究提供了一個全新的框架，去作自動化交通數據的事件分類。在這研究的第二部份，是正式進入開發交通數據自動化事件分類法，為求發展尖端的理論和技術，這必要建基於精準的交通事件檢測結果。因此，在這研究計劃內的自動事件分類法之開發，第一步是把分離體(指數據錯誤和交通事件)及內層體(指正常的交通狀況數據)從大量交通數據中分辨出來，第二步是開發一個細微的七種分離體之分類法，把兩種的數據錯誤及五種的交通事件分門別類出來。這研究會在自動化精準交通事件檢測及細微分類法之研究中，對交控中心之高端技術發展作出長久的貢獻。

12201814.label: Realisation of objectives
12201814.value: 1. We have successfully characterized three meaningful feature sets, traffic dynamics, ST signal static and detected inlier-outlier features, in progressive steps. The ST signals have been converted to be multi-dimensional principal component analysis (PCA) data points for outlier detection (OD) and classification. 2. We have successfully developed an adaptive multi-resolution OD method, with enhanced discriminate capability to separate inliers (incident-free events) and outliers (traffic incidents and data errors) by various traffic dynamics. The multi-solution OD was performed based on a finer granularity of the ST signal, which was divided into three 1-hour sessions (Level 0) from the original one 3-hour session. These 1-hour session is called Level 1 resolution. Furthermore, the 1-hour session of a ST signal has been further divided into a finer 0.5-hour session of a ST signal as Level 2. 3. We have successfully developed an outlier classification method to classify outliers, including but not limited to (a) data errors and noise, (b) traffic incident events namely congestion, vehicle blocking, low speed vehicles, fallen objects and accidents, to achieve AIC ultimately. We have developed the AIC methods including adaptive boosting SVM (AB-SVM), node-based modulo-k (MK) clustering, etc.

12201814.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201814.value: In this project, we have produced 3 international journals [J1, J2, J3] and 8 international conference proceedings [C1-C8]. Please refer to the Research Output in Part C at this final report. There are two main phases in the AIC for large-scale traffic data : (1) outlier detection (OD) by adaptive wavelet-based multi-resolution technique; (2) outlier classification by a RNN classifier. For the first phase, we have firstly further developed some OD methods including one-class SVM (9.61% accuracy) [C2], kernel density estimation (95.20% accuracy) [C2], k-nearest neighbours (96.19% accuracy) [C1], kernel smoothing naïve Bayes method (93.78% accuracy) [C4], Gaussian mixture model (94.50% accuracy) [C4], modulo-k clustering (97.94% accuracy) [6], density-based local outlier factor (LOF) (93.5% accuracy) [C2], bounded LOF (96% accuracy) [J2], quaternion-valued function (97.83% accuracy) [C5], regression analysis (97.37% accuracy) [C7] and accumulated relative density (95% accuracy) [C8]. Next, we have re-produced the large-scale traffic database into a new database of multi-granularity levels. The original traffic database is in term of spatial-temporal (ST) signals of traffic flow dynamics representing a 3-hour session (as Level 1 data). The new database is composed of three finer ST signals with each one in a 1-hour length [C7] denoted as Level 2 data. The regression analysis with cook’s distance criterion has been applied in [C7] for Level 2 data with 94.44% accuracy (whilst 94.28% accuracy for Level 1 data). For the second phase, we chose an adaptive boost (AB) classifier [J1] as the machine learning tool. This AB classifier was to train the ST signals and then classified three kinds of outliers, namely hardware failure, slight traffic jams and serious traffic jam, by a SVM classifier with linear kernel [J1]. This AIC approach achieves an average 92% accuracy in classification for a much larger database of 15-time real and synthetic data. Later on, a novel node-based modulo-k (MK) clustering tree classification method [J3] has been developed for the AIC and achieved 94.29% accuracy.

12201814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201814.value: The AIC research can be further developed in the techniques for machine learning and for more modality of traffic data such as loop data, video data, etc. The AIC research is a very important foundation for the automatic incident prediction for large-scale traffic data in future. This can complete the whole picture from automatic outlier detection, classification to prediction for traffic control and surveillance systems (TCSS) for modern cities.

12201814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201814.value: This research have contributed to develop very practical techniques for automatic incident classification of large-scale traffic data. During the project period, several techniques have been investigated such as methods of AB-SVM, MK, etc. We have produced at least 3 international journals and 8 international conference proceedings, for which some more publications may be produced if the PI have time or have a long-term position in academia. The PI has trained up 1 research fellow, 9 local/non-local undergraduate students and 2 master students for those 12 publications. The undergraduate students at Hong Kong Baptist University have very good potential to acquire the research ability and strive for excellence in research. The GRF grant can be considered to support undergraduate student research training, especially for building up a good atmosphere for innovative technology. We have contributed a good foundation of automatic traffic incident classification that can be further developed as automatic traffic incident prediction in need indeed.

12201914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201914.value: Organic semiconductors are finding widespread applications in modern optoelectronic devices. So far, organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), lighting and display applications have captured the most attention. In these devices, organic semiconductors are usually present in the form of amorphous films. Thus, there are numerous endeavors to develop new amorphous materials for OLED applications, and improving their intrinsic conductivities is of vital importance for the reduction of power consumption and device optimization.[1] We propose here to use organic thin film transistor (TFT) technique as a low-sample-demand tool for probing bulk transport properties of these amorphous organic semiconductors. To do this, the gate dielectric layer for the TFT structure needs to be non-polar. The non-polar surface can be realized through deposition of suitable non-polar polymers or organic insulators. On such a surface, we suggest that bulk-like behaviors can be realized for amorphous organic semiconductors. We highlight that only a thin film down to ~10 nm is sufficient for TFT measurements. Thus our approach will be of special relevance to the evaluation of transport properties of newly synthesized materials in which the yield is yet to be optimized. We also point out that the TFT can serve as a tool to study gate dielectric / organic interaction. Through temperature dependent measurements, interfacial energetic disorder can be evaluated. The outcome of this project should signify a key advance in the transport characterization of organic semiconductors and is of general interest to the research community of organic electronics. 有機半導體已被廣泛應用於光電器件。到目前為止，有機發光二極管（OLED）、照明和顯示器技術最為成熟。在這些器件中，有機半導體通常形成非晶薄膜。因此，新式非晶有機材料是一個清晰的研究方向，而新材料的電導率是非常重要的參考數據。在此建議書內，我們提出使用有機薄膜晶體管（TFT）的技術，作為探測工具，檢查非晶有機半導體的載流子運輸性質。要做到這一點，柵極介質層的結構必須要是非極性的，例如非極性聚合物或有機絕緣體。在這樣的表面上，我們認為可探測到非晶有機半導體的載流子遷移率。利用TFT方法，10nm材料已足夠使用。我們的方法特別適於產量低，但有待優化的新材料。我們還指出，TFT技術是可用於探測柵介質/有機相互作用的工具。通過不同溫度的測試，可提取界面相互作用的能量紋亂度。這個項目的成果會推進有機半導體的電荷傳輸表征和研究。

12201914.label: Realisation of objectives
12201914.value: Most objectives outline in 5.1 have been achieved. We have successfully employed thin film transistor (TFT) method as a low-sample-demand tool to probe bulk-like transport behaviors in amorphous organic semiconductors. (See e.g. Refs. 1 and 2 below). The essential criterion is the choice of a non-polar gate dielectric layer such as polystyrene. Furthermore, we use a trap-free hole transporter to reverse-probe the disorder induced by the gate dielectric layer when the layer itself is polar. Polar gate dielectric induces energetic disorder which can be probed by temperature dependent mobility measurements (e.g. Ref. 2). The insights obtained from Refs 1 and 2 allows us to further identify suitable gate dielectric materials for charge transport characterization in hybrid organic/inorganic semiconductors such as perovskite compounds (Ref. 3). 12201914.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201914.value: 1. We employed thin film transistor (TFT) as a probe and study the hole conduction properties of a series of iridium-based molecules in neat films and as dopants in a CBP (carbazol). The compounds were only available in small quantities provided by our collaborators. With the TFTs, we were able to evaluate their hole mobilties in line with Objective (1). All Ir compounds bearing phenylpyridine, carbazole, and amine moieties show significant hole mobilities of ~1x10-5 cm2 V-1s-1, comparable to CBP or NPB. FIrpic is non-conducting. In doped films of CBP:Ir(ppy)3 and CBP:Ir(piq)3, dopants act as deep trapping sites. Conduction in phosphorescent dyes appears to be a general phenomenon, and should be fully explored to simplify OLED structures [Ref. 1: Organic Electronics 24, 7-11 (2015)] 2. We used TFT to probe how interfacial disorders affect molecular orientations and hence charge transport. Our key findings are: (1) TFT can be used as a tool of metrology for probing bulk transport properties of organic semiconductors. To do this, the gate dielectric layer for the TFT structure needs to be non-polar. We observe bulk-like transport behaviors for amorphous organic semiconductors. The thickness of the organic layer required is down to about 10 nm — less than 1% of the TOF consumption. (2) TFT can study gate dielectric / organic interactions using temperature dependent mobility measurements. (3) The high temperature limits of the carrier mobilities can be correlated with the orientations of the molecules with a planar conformation. [Ref. 2: Adv. Electr. Mater. Adv. Electron. Mater. 2(3), 1500273 (2016)] 3. We studied the impacts of surface polarity /hydrophobicity on the growth of hydrid organic/inorganic perovskite TFTs. We found that the ﬁlm growth of CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite is a competition between ﬁlm adhesion and crystal size. A less hydrophobic surfaces favors ﬁlm formation but results in ﬁlms with small crystallites. More hydrophobic polymers potentially result in much larger crystals but non-adhering crystals. Among the tested dielectric materials, a methacrylate-based polymer, PPhMA, offers the best compromise. Using perovskites on PPhMA as the active layer for TFT, an impressive TFT mobility of 0.40 cm2 V−1 s−1 can be achieved. The ﬁndings suggests that polar polymers can assist or promote perovskite crystal growth for device applications. [Ref. 3: RSC Advances 7 (78), 49353-49360 (2017).]

12201914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201914.value: We clearly show in Refs. 1 and 2 that TFT can be used to probe bulk-like carrier mobilities for amorphous organic semiconductors. To do this properly, the gate dielectric layer should be non-polar. With this condition, TFT can be used as a low-sample-demand tool for charge transport evaluation and should have broad applications in organic electronics.

12201914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201914.value: Organic or hybrid organic/inorganic materials are being developed for applications in light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and photovoltaic (OPV) cells. Irrespective of their detailed chemical structures, their electrical conductivities are critical parameters for the initial device performance and evaluation. Yet, very often, newly synthesized materials are only available in small quantities for assessment. To circumvent this need, we use thin film transistor (TFT) as a low-sample-demand tool to probe the intrinsic conductivities of these materials. The key step to realize the TFT technique is the use of a non-polar gate dielectric layer onto which the organic materials can be grown. In this way, the organic materials retain its intrinsic transport properties and remains free of disturbance from the underlying layer. (Refs. 1 and 2) We demonstrated the success of this technique using organic hole transporting and iridium phosphors for LED applications. Furthermore, insights obtained from identifying the gate dielectric layers let us identify more suitable gate dielectric materials for transport characterization in hybrid organic/inorganic compounds.(Ref. 3). Our results provide a key advance in transport characterization of organic semiconductors and should be of general interest to materials and device scientists.

12202114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202114.value: 縱觀人類社會的發展，流行傳染病一直持續不斷地威脅著人類的健康，每一次大爆發都給人類社會帶來巨大的損失。如何控制流行病的傳播是人類共同面臨的嚴峻挑戰之一。對流行病傳播規律的研究不可能採取實驗形式，因此，使用數學模型定量地研究流行病的傳播規律進而設計有效的預防與控制策略是當前流行病學領域的一個熱點研究問題。然而，此類研究需要同時考慮流行病在時間維度和空間維度傳播的相互作用及相互依賴，建模過程非常復雜並且具有很高的挑戰性。具體來說，本項目主要解決以下幾個關鍵問題：（1）如何在時空維度同時對傳染病的傳播建模。（2）如何確認流行病的傳播網絡結構。（3）如何基於流行病傳播網絡模型來估計流行病的全局擴散速度和局部擴散速度。 本項目基於過去多年的研究經驗，結合流行病動力學、人工智能和信息傳播學提出一個新的基於流行病監控數據的隨機網絡模型，突破目前這個領域的瓶頸。在我們提出的模型中，傳統的傳染病模型所研究的局部動態過程通過一個不均勻的泊鬆隨機過程體現。傳染病傳播網絡中的節點相互傳播由對應的多個隨機過程的相互作用來體現。基於我們提出的模型，我們可以有效的估計網絡結構及模型參數。本項目將會使用開發的新模型對兩個真實的流行病的監控數據進行分析，我們的研究成果將為制定並完善我國流行傳染病的控制策略提供理論與實証的支持，也將為相關領域的研究（網絡病毒傳播）提供新的理論依據。

12202114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202114.value: Infectious diseases such as SARS and H1N1 can significantly impact people’s lives and cause severe social and economic damages. Recent outbreaks have stressed the urgency of effective research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread. However, it is difficult to predict when and where outbreaks may emerge and how infectious diseases spread because many factors affect their transmission, and some of them may be unknown. One feasible means to promptly detect an outbreak and track the progress of disease spread is to implement surveillance systems in regional or national health and medical centres. The accumulated surveillance data, including temporal, spatial, clinical, and demographic information can provide valuable information that can be exploited to better understand and model the dynamics of infectious disease spread. In this project, we have developed and empirically evaluated a stochastic model that allows the investigation of transmission patterns of infectious diseases in heterogeneous populations. A few works have been published during the progress of this project.

12202114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202114.value: Geographic variations of an infectious disease characterize the spatial differentiation of disease incidences caused by various impact factors, such as environmental, demographic, and socioeconomic factors. Some factors may directly determine the force of infection of the disease (namely, explicit factors), while many other factors may indirectly affect the number of disease incidences via certain unmeasurable processes (namely, implicit factors). In the future, we will investigate the impact of heterogeneous factors on geographic variations of infectious diseases.

12202114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202114.value: We have applied the proposed model to the surveillance data from the 2009 H1N1 pandemic in Hong Kong. In terms of the forward prediction of case incidence, the mean absolute percentage error is 20.0 %. We believe that our model can provide valuable insights for public health authorities to predict the effect of disease spread and analyse its underlying factors and to guide new control efforts.

12202214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202214.value: Large-scale personal identification systems use multiple biometric traits (e.g. face, fingerprint, iris) from the same person, so-called multibiometrics, to increase the recognition accuracy and population coverage. Core to such systems is the search of multibiometric identities in large-scale databases. With ever-increasing data volume and access demand, it is necessary to develop efficient search methods subject to a certain accuracy level. This is particularly important for biometric identity management in critical national security applications that involve large scale computationally intensive tasks, such as identity de-duplication and secured identification. An efficient search method consists in narrowing down the search range and reducing the matching complexity. The basic idea of biometric indexing is to assign an index vector to every identity in the database, with the aim of retrieving a small number of candidate identities for matching. Earlier work in this area has been focused on single modality indexing schemes, which typically derive the index values by dimension reduction of the respective biometric features. Multibiometric indexing schemes are emerging, but existing techniques rely on modality-specific matchers and matching references that are data-dependent. Moreover, indexing methods based on real-valued index descriptors of high-dimension biometric features often require significant computational efforts and memory storage. Binary representations can ensure fast operations and low storage costs. However, biometric features are in general not represented in binary form. Known binarization schemes for biometric features were designed for one-to-one verification (e.g. in biometric cryptosystems) that requires accurate matching. The resulting binary templates typically have long bit-length, which is problematic for large scale searches. This project seeks to develop binary index codes for effective and efficient search of multibiometric features. Our approach is to leverage machine learning techniques to integrate binary embedding with nearest neighbour search procedures. We design learning objectives to obtain compact binary representations by exploiting the feature distribution in the original biometric feature space. The binary index codes learned from heterogeneous biometric features will be combined systematically into a compact form for indexing multibiometric identities in large-scale databases. The expected outcome of this project will directly contribute to the development of high-throughput and cost-effective solutions to large-scale biometric systems in critical national security applications such as border control and national identity management. The search problem being quite general, the underlying techniques may be adapted to search other biometric-like fuzzy data and should have a broader impact on related areas. 大規模生物特徵識別系統往往採用多模態特徵（如，人臉、指紋、虹膜等）以提高身份識別的準確度與人口覆蓋率。其核心技術在於多模態特徵的大型數據庫檢索問題。隨著數據量及訪問需求的不斷增加，有必要開發高效的搜尋引擎以利於相關應用。這對於基於生物特徵的身份管理問題尤為重要。因為大規模生物識別應用往往涉及一些高強度的運算作業，如，重複身份檢測等，需要準確而快速地提取身份特徵。 提高搜索效率的途徑主要包括縮小檢索範圍與簡化計算複雜度。檢索生物特徵的基本思路主要通過對數據庫中每一個體分配一個索引向量來實現。其主要目的是篩選出一小部份數最具可能的候選對象進行匹配。在這個研究領域中，早期工作集中於單模態生物索引特徵向量的提取及其相對應的降維方法等。關於多模態生物特徵索引的研究文獻開始出現。但是現有的技術大多基於融合特定單模態匹配結果，因而依賴於具體匹配參照物和數據庫。 基於實數型高維向量描述的索引方法往往需要消耗大量的計算量和記憶體存儲。二進制代碼表示方法可以確保快速操作和低存儲成本。然而，並不是所有生物特徵都是直接用二進制代碼表示的。 現有的生物特徵二進制化演算法大多針對需要高精度匹配的生物特徵加密系統所設計。其生成的二進位範本通常具有很長的位長，不利於對大規模生物特徵的檢索。 本項目致力於為快速有效地檢索多模態生物特徵開發有效的二進位索引代碼。我們的方法利用機器學習技術集成了二進制嵌入技術與近鄰搜索演算法。具體實現上，我們將根據生物特徵在原始表示空間中的分佈規律，設計機器學習目標函數，以獲取緊湊的二進制數據描述。我們將提出新的特徵層融合方法，整合從多模態生物特徵學習得來的二進制數據描述，系統地利用特徵編碼建立快速索引技術，實現基於多模態生物特徵的大規模身份識別演算法。 本項目的預期研究成果將有助與推動發展具備高效運作和成本效益的大規模生物特徵系統解決方案，有利於邊境管理、全民身份證管理等生物特徵在關鍵國家安全項目中的應用。基於檢索問題的普遍性和重要性，本項目中提出的一些基本技術思想可能轉換運用於類似的模糊數據，從而對生物特徵相關領域的研究產生更廣泛的影響。

12202214.label: Realisation of objectives
12202214.value: Dr. Yi Wang was the original PI of this project and left HKBU end of 2016. Prof. Yuen became the PI since then. The three objectives have been realized along three main directions and discussed as follows. Objective One: We have studied the spatial inhomogeneity of minutiae distribution with respect to the level-1 features of singular points and ridge orientation field. We have considered only the locations of minutiae and treat a set of minutiae in a fingerprint as a spatial point pattern and proposed a minutiae intensity function to measure the spatial inhomogeneity. Since intensity functions are widely used for statistics associated with spatial point patterns, a nonparametric regression model is used to explore the relationship between spatial inhomogeneity and level-1 features of fingerprint. Our statistical experiments on the NIST14 database show that singular points and orientation field partially explain the variations of minutiae intensity (about 20% ～ 40% according to R-Square). The findings of this work provide deeper insights to the experiential probability of a random correspondence and indicate the need of investigating additional explanatory variables for explaining the spatial inhomogeneity of minutiae distribution in fingerprints. Second, we have developed a theoretical framework for learning compact binary hash codes for fingerprint features based on modeling the correlation distribution of minutiae features. We have applied the theory of Markov random field (MRF) to model adjacent bit correlations in the binary representation of minutiae cylinder code (MCC). MCC uses hundreds of bits to represent a single minutiae feature in the minutiae point set of a fingerprint template and provides the best performance in terms of accuracy, even for cross-device matching. However, MCC code is long with far more zeros than ones. We have shown this property by analyzing over 100,000 MCC bit-based representations from 2000 fingerprints in a benchmark database in which the average bit value is 0.05. That is, about 95% of MCC bits are zeros on average. So, we have modeled the MCC as multiple MRFs. After modelling the bit correlations in MCC, we have learned hash bits from a generalized linear model (GLM) whose maximum likelihood estimates can be conveniently obtained using efficient algorithms. With 384-bit MCC representations, we have achieved a hash ratio of 4:1 by using a second-order MRF and 9:1 by using a third-order MRF, resulting in 96-bit and 24-bit binary codes, respectively. Finally, we have developed a Montgomery multiplication-based method to generate compact and privacy-persevering binary index codes. Popular binary index codes are learned from their corresponding biometric features with the distance-persevering constraints. This allows adversary who can access data structures to analyses the search indexes and glean critical similarity information of the dataset. To achieve a privacy-persevering search, one of the straightforward methods is to encrypt a popularly used binary index code with standard ciphers such as AES and RSA. However, the resultant cyphertexts of standard ciphers (e.g. 256 bits SHA-256) are too long to be efficiently indexed, where other researchers suggest that index codes of length longer than 32 bits are not suitable for indexing data structure. Therefore, we proposed to index in a randomized Montgomery domain. Objective Two: we have developed an effective nearest neighbor method for efficient fingerprint search in Hamming space. Specifically, a hierarchical indexing scheme is proposed to combine the merits of local sensitive hashing (LSH) and geometric hashing. The proposed Geo-LSH indexing approach can effectively achieve superior identification accuracy and is robust in the presence of noise and missing points. Moreover, it does not require any pre-processing steps such as image segmentation and pre-alignments for feature extraction. The LSH can distribute binary codes more evenly to buckets by random bit sampling. However, the LSH based on the MCC (MCC-LSH) used homogeneous features for both indexing points and approximating point similarities, which generally require high dimensional representations to generate key values. Our work on geometric hashing based on the MCC (Geo-MCC) can improve the retrieval accuracy over existing fingerprint indexing algorithms including the state-of-the-art MCC-LSH. However, Geo-MCC has two limitations. First, a few geometric hash bins contain a large number of entries. As the longest list dominates the search time, a more uniform distribution of the entries is desired. Second, the point matching is based on the MCC bit-based representation. Although this is done by fast bit operations in Hamming space, it is still desirable to reduce extensive comparisons of long binary codes. Therefore, we combine the advantages of both MCC-LSH and Geo-MCC and propose a hierarchical indexing scheme, Geo-LSH. Our indexing experiments showed that a Geo-LSH search based on the 24-bit hash code can maintain a comparable identification accuracy while achieving a significant speed-up of over four-fold in the average search time compared to that based on the 384-bit MCC representation. Furthermore, we have developed an inference-based framework for efficient privacy-preserving nearest neighbor search in Hamming space. Specifically, we have modeled the privacy-preserving Hamming-ball search problem as a binary channel estimation for which we derive the optimal decision rule based on the theory of binary hypothesis testing. This enables the design of an inference-based approach for detecting, with a high accuracy in the retrieval space, matching candidates within a predefined neighborhood of the query without knowing the actual distance values. Then, we present a distance obfuscation mechanism, as a key element of the binary channel, based on matching piecewise obfuscated binary codes for hash-based similarity search. We derive analytically the condition where it is guaranteed to have a substring collision for neighboring pairs and show how it gives rise to an obfuscated distance measure that conceals the Hamming distance in a dynamic interval. Finally, the inference-based approach for Hamming-ball search is extended to handle a test-based rank-ordered search that arranges the retrieved candidates in rank order without the need of comparing distance values. Objective Three: We have developed a binary feature fusion method to fuse the compact binary index codes of fingerprint, face and iris. Our proposed binary feature fusion analyzed the dependency among different bits of multi-biometric index codes and fused the index codes to produce more compact and informative index codes. As the properties for achieving both effective and informative criteria can be divided into multiple-bit-based (i.e., dependency among bits) and individual-bit-based (i.e., intra-subject variations, inter-subject variations and bit uniformity). The proposed fusion consists of two stages: (i) dependency-reductive bit-grouping and (ii) discriminative within-group fusion. In the first stage, we address the multiple-bit-based property: We extract a set of weakly dependent bit-groups from multiple sets of binary unimodal features, such that, if the bits in each group is fused into a single bit, these fused bits, upon concatenation, will be weakly interdependent. Then, in the second stage, we address the individual-bit-based properties: We fuse bits in each bit-group into a single bit with the objective of minimizing the intra-user variation, maximizing the inter-user variation and maximizing uniformity of the bits. As maximizing bit uniformity is equivalent to maximizing the inter-user variation of the corresponding bit, the fusion function is designed to only maximize discriminability (minimize intra-user variations and maximize inter-user variations). We have conducted experiments on WVU multi-modal database and two chimeric databases and the results have justified the proposed method in producing a more effective and informative fused binary indexes from multi-modal samples.

12202214.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202214.value: To achieve the objectives stated above, we have investigated and researched different approaches for developing compact binary index codes and effective binary embedding schemes for nearest neighbor search (NNS) methods in order to achieve effective and efficient search of biometric features, as stated in the proposal. At the core of biometric indexing is the NNS problem. Over the past two decades, the performance of NNS in multi-dimensional vector space is not yet satisfactory mainly due to the “curse of dimensionality”. To address this issue, for fingerprint indexing, we firstly study data characteristics of minutiae cylinder code (MCC) and observe that its binary representation is bit-correlated. Secondly, we propose a theoretical framework for systematically learning compact binary hash codes. Finally, we design a hierarchical fingerprint indexing scheme based on the proposed hash codes. Under the proposed framework, the binary search code length can be significantly reduced from 384 bits to 24 bits. This allows fewer hash functions and tables to be used for nearest neighbor search in Hamming space. These research findings have been reported in IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security [TIFS2015]. For the effective and efficient search of face and iris features with privacy-preserving, we propose an inference-based framework. The framework builds on an obfuscated distance measure that can conceal Hamming distance in a dynamic interval. Such a mechanism enables us to systematically design statistically reliable methods for retrieving most likely candidates without knowing the exact distance values. We further propose to apply Montgomery multiplication for generating search indexes that can withstand adversarial similarity analysis and show that information leakage in randomized Montgomery domains can be made negligibly small. These research findings have been reported in Chinese Conference on Biometrics Recognition [CCBR 2016] and IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence [TPAMI 2018]. For the effective and efficient search of multibiometric features (face, fingerprint, and iris), we propose a binary feature fusion method. Our binary feature fusion firstly analyzes the dependency among different bits of multi-biometric index codes and group the highly dependent bits together, while the less dependent bits are in different groups. Secondly, we fuse the bits in each group with maximizing the entropy and discriminability. These research findings have been reported in International Conference on Biometrics Theory, Applications and Systems [BTAS 2015] and Image and Vision Computing Journal [IVC 2017].

12202214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202214.value: Our current search system is mainly based on full images as the probe. In some forensic scenarios, partial images can be captured (e.g., latent fingerprint, occluded face images). A future work along this line is to design robust index codes so that the biometric features can be searched with features extracted from partial images. Furthermore, the proposed inference-based approach for privacy-preserving search can be operated for fixed-length binary features only. A future work along this direction is to extend the inference-based approach to other biometric modalities such as fingerprints that do not have a fixed-length binary string representation. Furthermore, it can be also extended to search problems with distance measures other than in Hamming space.

12202214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202214.value: The efficient and effective search of person identity using multibiometric modality is the core technology in large-scale biometrics systems. Most of the existing search methods are developed based on nearest neighbor search (NNS) in multi-dimensional vector space. However, they suffer from the “curse of dimensionality”. To overcome this issue, this project has developed compact binary index codes and effective binary embedding schemes for NNS. The results of this project have contributed to the research in multibiometric indexing in several aspects. First, we have developed a theoretical framework for systematically learning compact binary hash codes for fingerprint features and a Montgomery multiplication based method to generate compact and privacy-persevering binary index code for face and iris. Second, we have developed an effective method for efficient NNS in Hamming space. Third, we have developed an inference-based framework for efficient privacy-preserving NSS in Hamming space. Fourth, we have developed a binary feature fusion method to fuse the compact binary index codes of fingerprint, face, and iris to produce more compact and informative index codes. Such index codes can be used for efficient and effective NNS for practical multibiometric systems in future.

12202414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202414.value: 在雲輔助多源數據收集環境下，數據由分佈於不同位置的收集者收集後外包給雲服務商提供查詢服務。這種計算模式在商業營銷、智能交通、醫療保健、環境監測等領域有著廣泛的應用。比如，格價員們在不用區域的商店收集價格信息後報告給雲服務器，然後用戶就可以通過雲服務器查詢價格信息，如查找某項商品的最低價格。雖然這種計算模式在成本、性能及靈活性等方面有很多優勢，但同時也帶來了查詢結果完整性的問題。如果雲服務器是不可信的或者受到了外部攻擊，它有可能返回不正確或不完整的結果給用戶。因此，本項目將研究在雲輔助多源數據收集及查詢服務中，如何讓用戶可以驗證查詢結果的正確性和完整性。主要研究內容包括：1）可聚合的認證數據結構；2）查詢驗證處理及數據更新算法；3）支持隱私保護的查詢驗證技術；4）安全性分析與性能評估。

12202414.label: Realisation of objectives
12202414.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have identified and formulated the multi-source query authentication problem in a distributed data collection environment. We have developed new data structures and algorithms for efficient query authentication on both one-dimensional and multi-dimensional data, including range queries [Conference/1], spatial-keyword queries [Journal/1, Conference/3] and kNN queries [Conference/4]. Moreover, we have proposed techniques for authenticated aggregate queries over set-valued data that not only ensure the integrity of query results but also preserve the confidentiality of source data [Journal/2, Conference/2]. The problem of query authentication under fine-grained access control has also been investigated [Conference/5]. In addition, we have studied how to answer the why-not questions posed for query results [Conference/6, Conference/7]. In all the above studies, we have evaluated the security and efficiency of the proposed algorithms and techniques by combining theoretical analysis and empirical investigation. The research findings have been published in the top conferences and journals including ACM SIGMOD, IEEE TKDE and ICDE.
