12202414.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202414.value: To guarantee the integrity of query results, we have identified and formulated the multi-source query authentication problem in a cloud-assisted computing model. More specifically, the correctness of query results consists of two authenticity conditions: (i) soundness: the returned values are all genuine query results and are not tampered with; (ii) completeness: no genuine query results are missing. The main challenge lies in the design of a mechanism that can aggregate the inputs from all data sources faithfully by the untrusted server for future query authentication. To deal with this challenge, we have proposed homomorphic secret sharing seal (HS3) as the underlying authentication code for integrity assurance of distributed data [Conference/1]. Based on this, we have designed two indexing schemes, namely the HS3-G-tree and HS3-R-tree, for authenticating various types of queries on multidimensional data. Experimental results show that our seal design and authentication schemes are efficient and robust under various system settings. We have also developed authentication techniques for more advanced top-k spatial keyword (MkSK) queries [Journal/1]. We have proposed a new data structure for the authentication of MkSK queries, MIR-tree, that enables low computation and communication costs. We have designed a Verification Object (VO) for authenticating the top-k results and safe zones of MkSK queries. Algorithms for constructing the VO and verifying the top-k results and safe zones using the VO have been developed. Extensive empirical studies on real data sets demonstrate that the proposed approaches are capable of outperforming two baseline algorithms that utilize existing techniques by orders of magnitude. In addition, new authenticated indexes have been proposed for authenticating spatial-textual similarity joins [Conference/3] and k-nearest-neighbors (kNN) queries [Conference/4] in untrusted cloud environments. Regarding aggregate queries over set-valued data, as many of them are composed of multiset operations such as set union and subset, we have developed a family of privacy-preserving authentication protocols for primitive multiset operations. Using these protocols as building blocks, we have designed a privacy-preserving authentication framework for various aggregate queries and further optimized their authentication performance [Journal/2, Conference/2]. Whereas query authentication had been extensively studied, access control, another important security concern, is largely ignored by existing works. Notably, recent breakthroughs in cryptography have enabled fine-grained access control over outsourced data. Thus, we have taken the first step toward studying the problem of authenticating relational queries with fine-grained access control [Conference/5]. The key challenge is how to protect information confidentiality during query authentication, which is essential to many critical applications. To address this challenge, we have proposed a novel access-policy-preserving (APP) signature as the primitive authenticated data structure. A useful property of the APP signature is that it can be used to derive customized signatures for unauthorized users to prove the inaccessibility while achieving the zero-knowledge confidentiality. We have also proposed a grid-index-based tree structure that can aggregate APP signatures for efficient range and join query authentication. In addition to this, a number of optimization techniques have been proposed to further improve the authentication performance. Security analysis and performance evaluation substantiate the security and efficiency of the proposed solutions and techniques. In addition, we have studied how to answer the why-not questions posed for query results [Conference/6, Conference/7]. In case an object is unexpectedly missing from the query result, we offer users explanations of why such expected objects are missing. We have developed efficient techniques that allow the revision of the initial queries such that their results include one or more desired but missing objects.

12202414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202414.value: For future work, we plan to extend the proposed authentication schemes to more complex query types, especially those involve distance computation such as distance-based joins. As there are many applications that adopt distance metrics other than the Euclidean distance, designing a more general version of secret sharing seal in the metric space is worthy further investigation. We also plan to extend our study to blockchain systems. We are interested to study integrity-assured blockchain query services by utilizing authenticated query processing techniques. Specifically, we intend to study authenticated range and Boolean queries over blockchain databases. Various query modes, such as time window, sliding window and subscription queries, will be considered. Furthermore, blockchains offer a new way to execute trustworthy computation known as smart contract. Thus, we will also investigate how to leverage smart contract to enable authenticated query services, handle data updates on behalf of data owners, and enforce access control.

12202414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202414.value: The convergence of sensor technologies, crowdsourcing, and cloud computing has given rise to a brand-new paradigm for cloud-assisted multi-source data collection, where data is collected by physically distributed collectors and outsourced to the cloud (such as Amazon EC2 and Google App Engine) to provide query services. This paradigm has numerous potential applications across a wide variety of domains such as marketing, transport, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. While this model is appealing in terms of cost, performance, and flexibility, it raises the issue of query integrity. If the cloud server is untrustworthy or compromised, it may return incorrect or incomplete query results to clients and possibly mislead them, leading to wrong decisions being made. The consequences could be disastrous for many critical applications. Therefore, empowering clients to authenticate query results is imperative in such cloud-assisted multi-source data collection and query services. In this project, we have proposed a number of novel query authentication techniques and algorithms to ensure the integrity of query results. We believe that the outcomes of this project can benefit both users and service providers in the cloud/crowd computing industry.

12202514.label: Project Objectives
12202514.value: To investigate and develop a weakly supervised domain adaptation framework without positive labelled data in the target domain to solve the joint distribution mismatch problem in video surveillance applications in large-scale camera networks. To study and develop a method to find weakly positive information in the target domain using labelled data in the source domain and, negative labelled data and unlabelled data in the target domain. To examine and develop a weakly supervised domain adaptation algorithm to learn the target classification model using labelled data in the source domain, negative labelled data in the target domain and weakly positive information estimated by (2).

12202514.label: Realisation of objectives
12202514.value: The three listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily along three main directions. First Objective: We have developed three weakly supervised domain adaptation models to solve the joint distribution mismatch problem in video surveillance applications. One effective approach to solve the joint distribution mismatch problem is joint distribution alignment. The challenge of this approach is that the joint distribution in the target domain is hard to estimate without target labels. Instead of estimating the target-domain joint distribution, we have developed a domain-shared group-sparse dictionary learning model [C1][J5] to align joint distributions across domains. In this model, joint dictionaries between source domain and target domains are introduced to learn a domain-shared coefficient space. The joint distributions of coefficients are aligned with the constraint of domain-shared group sparsity on the source and target domains. The group sparsity in the target domain without labels is obtained by constraining the target coefficient exclude for two sub-dictionaries representing two different classes. With this criterion, each target sample automatically selects the optimal group of coefficients for representation so that the joint distributions of the source and target group-sparse coefficients are aligned. Experimental results show that domain-shared group-sparse coefficients improve the performance on cross-domain face and object recognition from 67.1% to 98.8% and from 84.7% to 92.5%, respectively. We have studied and analyzed the data distributions in different datasets. It is found that distribution structures could vary in different datasets. To handle the distribution mismatch caused by the difference of distribution structures, an unsupervised graph alignment model [C2] has been developed. In each domain data are linked to build a complete graph. Therefore, the structural information of feature distribution is contained in the edge of graph. The distribution alignment across domains can then be modeled as the alignment between the source graph and the target graph. To reduce the joint distribution mismatch between the source and target edges, edges are categorized as intra-class edges and inter-class edges according to the labels of each pair of features. But without target labels, this castigation cannot be applied in the target domain. Therefore, we have designed cross-domain unified criteria for edges in both source and target domains, to weakly supervise the adaption between source edges and target edges. The aligned features obtained by unsupervised graph alignment model [C2] has shown good performance in multiple applications. The average accuracies of cross-domain digit and object recognition increased by 6.4% and 16.9%, respectively. The graph-aligned features also show good generalizability in the task of cross-modality person re-identification, and achieved 13% increase in mean average precision (mAP). Third, we addressed the problems in person re-identification in large-scale camera networks. Since the number of unmatched image pairs are usually much larger than that of matched ones, the unlabeled target data are imbalanced. It makes the distribution alignment based domain adaptation method unreliable. To address the imbalanced data issue, we propose to estimate target positive information based on the labeled data from the source domain, target negative data and target unlabeled data [J1]. We propose to relax the discriminative constraint into a necessary condition to it, which only relies on the mean of positive pairs. Two positive mean estimations are then introduced. The first one is deviated from the assumption that the differences between positive mean and negative mean are invariant across domains. The second one is given by the mean of potential positive data, which is selected from the unlabeled data in the target domain by maximizing the positive joint distribution with properties and constraints in person re-identiﬁcation. To further reduce the estimation error, the two estimations of the target positive mean are combined to determine the optimal estimation by the training data. Second Objective: We have studied two strategies for two video surveillance applications, namely cross-quality human pose estimation [J3] and cross-domain person re-identification [J1][J2], to find weakly positive information in the target domain. Cross-quality Human Pose Estimation: Due to the large variations in appearance between the source and target poses with different image qualities, finding target-domain positive information (human poses) from an unlabeled target image is difficult. Therefore, we have proposed an Image Quality Translative Dictionary Learning method [J3] to synthesize target body parts as the target positive information. The human contours that are less sensitive to the image quality are used as the clues (domain-shared codes) to guide the synthesis of the target body parts. Experiments of feature distribution analysis have been done to evaluate the image quality of the synthesized target body parts. We found that the feature distribution of the synthesized body parts is more similar to that of the target body parts compared to the body parts from source images. This finding indicates that the image quality of the synthesized body parts is similar to the target domain. Cross-domain Person Re-identification: To obtain more positive information than positive mean, we explore target positive regions as target positive information, where target positive regions denote the region with non-zero positive conditional probability in target feature space [J1]. Since it is difficult to estimate the target positive data accurately from the imbalanced unlabeled data, we study positive region estimation and find that it can be approximated using positive neighbors instead of positive data. That avoids the unreliable positive sample estimation, and hence enhances the robustness of the domain adaptation model in challenging cases. Furthermore, we find that the positive neighbors can be estimated using labelled data in the source domain and, negative labelled data and unlabeled data in the target domain. Third Objective: Two adaptation algorithms have been proposed to learn the target classification model with the weakly positive information estimated by the above-mentioned strategies. Cross-quality Adaptation Model: For cross-quality pose estimation, we learned the target-domain pose estimator by refining the source pose estimator using the synthesized target body parts [J3]. As the weakly target positive information, the synthesized target body parts would have different reliability for the model refinement. Thus, we analyzed the confidence of each synthesized target body part. We then developed a cross-quality adaptation model by exploiting the confidence of synthesized target body parts to flexibly adapt the source pose estimator to the target domain. Experimental results show that further improvement can be obtained when the confidence analysis is used for model refinement. Cross-domain Person Re-identification: A region-based weakly supervised domain adaptation algorithm is proposed for person re-identification [J1]. Specifically, an optimization problem for positive neighbor estimation from unlabeled data is derived and solved by aligning the cross-person score distributions together with optimizing for multiple graphs based label propagation. To extract the positive information from the positive neighbors, we propose to construct multiple positive regions by the regularized afﬁne hull of positives neighbors. A region-to-point metric learning is derived subsequently to learn a discriminative model by maximizing the weighted distance from the positive regions to negatives.

12202514.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202514.value: In this project, we have investigated and developed different strategies to address the challenges caused by the lack of positive labelled data in the target domain. The first strategy is developing weakly supervised domain adaptation models to align joint distributions across domains without target labeled data. To achieve this purpose, we have designed two alignment criteria (domain-shared group sparsity [C1][J5] and unified edge criteria [C2]) for joint distribution alignment without using the label information in the target domain. Our studies indicated that the joint distributions in the source and target domains can be better aligned in the projected space with the relaxed alignment criteria. We have also found that the aligned features could be learned using both dictionary-learning model [C1][J5] and deep-learning model [C2]. Furthermore, we have developed a novel Adaptive Ranking Support Vector Machines (AdaRSVM) method to deal with the problem that label information of persons is not available under target cameras [J1]. Without positive image pairs generated by the label information of persons, we have found a necessary condition of the discriminative constraint, which only relies on the mean of positive pairs. We make use of the labeled data from the source domain, the negative and unlabeled data from the target domain to design two target positive mean estimations. An optimal combination strategy of the two estimations is also designed by the training data. The second strategy is estimating target-domain positive information using the labeled data in the source domain and unlabeled data in the target domain. This estimated target-domain positive information is then used to refine the source model to the target domain. Based on the image/video characteristics of different applications, we have proposed two estimation methods for two cross-domain surveillance applications. For cross-quality pose estimation, we have developed an Image Quality Translative Dictionary Learning model [J3] to synthesize target body parts as the target-domain positive information. For cross-domain person re-identification, the target-domain positive information is estimated using the positive region [J1] in the source and target domains. In addition, our studies have shown that the proposed methods could be applied and achieved promising results on various video surveillance applications, e.g., object recognition [J5][C1][C2], person re-identification [J1][J4] and human pose estimation [J3].

12202514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202514.value: With the growing interest of deep learning based applications, extracting label information from unlabeled data has been a very hot research topic in the past few years. This project has successful developed some new algorithms for video surveillance applications, including person re-identification and human pose estimation. The proposed methods could be further extended to other applications. Moreover, based on the results of this project, there is opportunity to develop novel video-based applications for large-scale camera network.

12202514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202514.value: With the advanced camera technology, CCTV system has been extended from a few cameras to thousands of camera networks. Many promising computer vision methods require labeled data for training. However, with such a large-scale camera network, it is almost impossible to collect labeled data from all cameras. It is because labeling is time consuming and expensive. As such, this project has investigated and developed new algorithms to automatically extract labeled information from unlabeled data, called weakly labeled information. With extracted information, existing computer vision methods can be applied. We have successfully demonstrated that the proposed methods can be applied to object recognition, person re-identification and human pose estimation.

12300014.label: Project Objectives
12300014.value: Identification of nonstandard integro-differential equations that arise as mathematical models in materials science and chemical engineering and for which there is a lack of efficient computational schemes. Extension of classical time-stepping techniques (e.g. collocation methods and discontinuous Galerkin methods) to the classes of nonstandard integro-differential equations of (i). Stability, convergence and error analysis for the numerical schemes introduced in (ii). Computational implementation of the above numerical methods for integro-differential equations with singular features (e.g. equations with unbounded spatial domains; solutions that blow up in finite time). This will necessitate the design of adaptive time-stepping techniques. Extensive practical numerical simulations, using the mathematical models identified in (i).

12300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300014.value: The mathematical modeling of physical or chemical processes where memory effects play an important role (for example heat conduction in materials with memory, rheology, turbulence, chemical combustion theory) leads to nonstandard ordinary or partial integro-differential equations in which the underlying nonlinear integral operators contain the unknown solution with different time arguments, or where the spatial domain is unbounded. While the theory of these nonlinear problems is quite well understood, there is still a distinct lack of efficient computational methods. This research proposal aims to fill this gap and thus make a significant contribution to the design, analysis, and computational implementation of efficient numerical methods for such nonstandard integro-differential equations, including singularly perturbed problems. The theoretical part of the proposal will be complemented by extensive numerical simulations for various model equations arising in the above-mentioned applications.

12300014.label: Realisation of objectives
12300014.value: As shown by the list of publications and list of international conference talks, the above project objectives have been largely attained, with the exception of the carrying out of extensive computer simulations of real-life integro-differential equations arising as mathematical models (see also the 2018 paper "Numerical analysis and computational solution of integer-differential equations" listed under Publications).

12300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300014.value: The following aspects of the numerical analysis and computational solution of Volterra-type integro-differential equations (VIDEs) were addressed during the duration of this project: (1) Theory and numerical analysis of VIDEs with highly oscillatory kernels. (2) Theory and numerical analysis of integer-differential algebraic VIDEs. Work crucial to this included the numerical analysis of auto-convolution Volterra integral equations, Galerkin-type methods for delay differential equations, collocation methods for weakly singular and third-kind Volterra integral equations. (3) Analysis and computational solution of semi linear parabolic VIDEs with blow-up solutions.

12300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300014.value: Numerical simulation of nonlinear (Volterra and Fredholm) integro-differential equations arising as mathematical models in physics, chemistry, and engineering, using the methods described in the various publications arising from this project.

12300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300014.value: Linear and nonlinear integro-differential equations (both of Volterra and Fredholm type) arise in the mathematical modelling of numerous physical or biological phenomena. Since the solutions of such equations are generally not known explicitly, insight into these problems can thus only obtained by reliable and highly accurate numerical methods. This project describes classes of such methods based mostly on collocation techniques and corresponding convergence and error analyses.

12300114.label: Project Objectives
12300114.value: To develop cell line models for studying endogenous metabolites in breast cancer cells exposed to PBDEs with various dosing levels and at different time points. To develop methods and conduct mass spectrometry-based metabolomics study on the cellular metabolism and to identify metabolites To construct metabolic network from the identified biomarkers and metabolic pathways and to initially investigate the mechanism of toxicological effects of PBDEs on cell metabolism.

12300114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300114.value: Major components of polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) have been included in the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants since May 2009. The chemicals are found to be accumulated in human milk, adipose and blood. Previous work also suggested that PBDEs may promote breast cancer proliferation. More importantly, it has been widely recognized that the origin of cancer is by means of metabolic selection. Therefore, we hypothesized that PBDEs may enhance breast cancer risk through metabolic reprogramming. To test this hypothesis, we will carry out mass spectrometry-based metabolomics in combination with isotope labeling technique. The endogenous metabolites are the amplified readout of cell pathogenesis, which would indicate altered metabolism in cells exposed to PBDEs. PBDEs exposure will be investigated not only in non-tumorigenic human breast cell lines (MCF-10A and Hs578Bst) for understanding the toxicological effects, but also with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7 and T47D) as well as estrogen receptor-negative breast cancer cell lines (MDA-MB-231 and Hs578T) for evaluating the promoting proliferative effects. Liquid chromatography and gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry will be employed for non-targeted and targeted metabolomics analysis. The feature selection from total ion chromatograms in mass spectra will be applied for searching potential biomarkers that will be proposed in the metabolic pathways. The metabolomics data analysis package MetaXCMS will then be used to detect the shared metabolites from multiple sample groups representing different models of the same phenotype. Moreover, regarding Warburg effect in cancer metabolism, targeted metabolomics in combination with isotope-labeling technique will be applied for quantitative analysis of the intermediate metabolites in glycolysis and citric acid cycle to reveal metabolic reprogramming induced by PBDEs exposure. The isotope-labeled glucose or glutamine will be used in cell culture for metabolite extraction, and metabolic switches will be unlocked. By taking the toxicological effects of PBDEs in normal breast cells into account, the disturbed metabolic pathways might be linked to breast cancer development for uncovering estrogen-dependent or –independent metabolic mechanisms. In summary, we will apply mass spectrometry-based metabolomics for studying metabolic phenotypes associated with the possible toxicological effects of PBDEs. The hypothesis on PBDEs exposure associated with breast cancer development will be tested.

12300114.label: Realisation of objectives
12300114.value: 1. The breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 as triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell model and MCF-7 cell line as ER-positive breast cancer cell model were applied in the exposure of PBDEs. It has been reported that BDE-47, BDE-99, BDE-153 and BDE-209 belongs to the major components of PBDEs and has been detected in multiple biota samples. Therefore, they were used to investigate the influence on breast cancer development. The PBDEs exposure levels (100 µM, 10 µM,1 µM, 100 nM, 10 nM, 1 nM, 100 pM, and 10 pM) and time points (24, 48, 72h) were examined to achieve the optimal cell viability for the metabolomics analysis. There was no noticeable toxicity in the exposure groups in three PBDEs species (BDE-99, BDE-153 and BDE-209) under the conditions applied. Therefore, BDE-47 at 5 µM as low dose and 10 µM as high dose of exposure for 72 h in 1% FBS medium were applied in the metabolomics study. Besides, we also did the exposure assay by using C57BL/6 mouse cell and preadipocyte cell line 3T3-L1, hoping to find possible linkage between the exposure and neuro toxicity and obesity. 2. We have conducted mass spectrometry-based metabolomics study by using LC-MS and GC-MS. Samples were prepared by liquid-liquid extraction. The Human Metabolome Database (http://www.hmdb.ca/) and METLIN Database (https://metlin.scripps.edu/index.php) were used for metabolite searching and tandem mass spectrometry searching. Parallel reaction monitor mode (PRM) of MS analysis was applied to obtain the tandem MS data. The accurate MS and tandem MS data were input into the HMDB and METLIN database for searching and matching. 19 significantly changed ions were identified in breast cancer cell line samples. Moreover, 24 significantly changed metabolites from serum and 42 from striatum were identified in the C57BL/6 mice experiment exposed with BDE-47. Most of the identified metabolites were verified by using authentic standards. 3. The identified metabolites were semi-quantified by using the chromatographic peak areas. Based on the comparison of the control and high-dose groups, fold changes of the identified metabolites were calculated. In the breast cancer cell line MCF-7 exposure assay, we found that the metabolites involved in the pyrimidine metabolism and purine metabolism were significantly downregulated. Besides, 6-phosphogluconic acid, which was involved in pentose phosphate pathway, was reduced significantly. In the C57BL/6 mice and 3T3-L1 cell exposure assay, the metabolites with fold change > 1.5 and p value < 0.05 were also quantified by relative intensity. 4. The metabolic network was constructed from the identified metabolites. In the breast cancer cell MCF-7 exposure assay, we found that pyrimidine metabolism, purine metabolism and pentose phosphate pathways (PPP) were the top three pathways that were impacted by the exposure of BDE-47. BDE-47 exposure inhibited the generation of NADPH in the PPP. The inhibition could lead to NADPH shortage because PPP is the main routine for cells to generate NADPH. Lack of NADPH could influence multiple pathways, in which the reactive oxygen species (ROS) elimination system was involved. Because antioxidases could not clear up the ROS timely without NADPH, oxidative stress occurred and eventually resulted in damage to cells. Thus, BDE-47 exposure on MCF-7 cells could induce oxidative stress through the inhibition of NADPH generation in the PPP. In the C57BL/6 mice exposure assay, we found that BDE-47 could induce oxidative stress, dysregulate neurotransmitters, and disturb dopaminergic system. The observed metabolic alterations induced by BDE-47 exposure have close relationship with Parkinson’s disease. The 3T3-L1 cell exposure assay revealed a new mechanism of how this environmental organic pollutant promotes adipocytes differentiation via the up-regulated purine metabolism pathway and augmented mitochondrial respiration capacity to induce differentiation of adipocytes. The promoting effects of BDE-47 on adipocyte differentiation may reveal how an environmental pollutant aggravate obesity.

12300114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300114.value: Among the four investigated PBDEs congeners (BDE-47, BDE-99, BDE-153 and BDE-209), BDE-47 was the most toxic congener to breast cancer cell line. The exposure of BDE-47 to breast cancer cell line MCF-7 significantly altered the cell metabolism. The pentose phosphate pathway, which was the major source of generating NADPH, was downregulated by the exposure. Because NADPH could assist to eliminate reactive oxygen species (ROS), the downregulation of NADPH induced oxidative stress since the antioxidases could not remove all ROS efficiently at the circumstance of lacking reduction ability. Moreover, insufficient NADPH could influence the cell metabolism through some other pathways such as fatty acid and lipid synthesis, because NADPH is the vital coenzyme in the metabolic procedures. BDE-47 might also inhibit the transcription of mRNA, leading to the downregulation of purine and pyrimidine metabolism. Thus, BDE-47 exposure on MCF-7 cells could induce oxidative stress through the inhibition of NADPH generation in the pentose phosphate pathway. This study provided useful information for the in vivo study to unveil the adverse health effect mechanism of BDE-47 to breast cancer in the future. The 3T3-L1 cell exposure assay suggested that BDE-47 might promote lipid accumulation during adipocyte differentiation via inducing ROS production and elevation of oxidative stress might play a key role in BDE-47-induced adipocyte differentiation. Therefore, BDE-47 probably was an environmental obesogen that produced an oxidative environment for inducing adipocyte differentiation. In the C57BL/6 mice exposure assay, the metabolic pathway variations were observed in purine, alanine, aspartate and glutamate, tryptophan, phenylalanine, and glutathione pathways. The obtained results suggested that BDE-47 could induce oxidative stress, dysregulate neurotransmitters, and disturb dopaminergic system. Moreover, the observed metabolic alterations induced by BDE-47 exposure involved in the pathways related to Parkinson’s Disease (PD). Thus, BDE-47 exposure might likely be a risk factor of the onset and progression of PD.

12300114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300114.value: 1. Animal study could be designed for further in-depth investigation based on the cell experiment results. Because cell surface receptors of different cell lines are diverse, we should use several breast cancer cell lines to construct breast cancer mouse model. Animal model will be applied for the PBDEs-associated metabolomics study, for the discovery of new potential biomarkers and mechanism of influence generated by PBDEs exposure. 2. The developed LC-MS method for the detection and quantification of targeted metabolites (such as free fatty acids, hydroxy short chain fatty acids) could be applied in future studies.

12300114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300114.value: According to previous reports, BDE-47 showed toxicity to liver cells and neuron cells, but the potential toxicity to breast cells and its underlying mechanism is scarce. We investigated the toxicity of BDE-47 to MCF-7 breast cancer cells by using mass spectrometry-based metabolomics strategy. The obtained results showed that BDE-47 exposure could alter multi metabolic pathways and hence disorder the entire cell metabolism. The disorder may contribute to the development of breast cancer in vivo. Therefore, this study could provide a potential mechanism for further study on the effect of BDE-47 on breast cancer development in vivo. Moreover, through the C57BL/6 mice exposure assay we found that the exposure could lead to neuro toxicity and hence might have relationship with Parkinson's Disease (PD). The 3T3-L1 cell exposure assay revealed that the exposure of BDE-47 could improve adipocytes differentiation and might aggravate obesity. These study supports the hypothesis that BDE-47 is a new risk factor for the development of breast cancer, PD and obesity. Hence, understanding the mechanism of how environmental pollutants influence the diseases will be useful for the development of comprehensive therapeutic strategies for the prevention and treatment of the diseases.

12300714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300714.value: The aim of this proposal is to increase the number of proteins for biological analysis by concentrating the proteins from the provided sample. Protein analysis, such as protein sequencing, protein detection and etc., is an important step in biological and medical diagnostics. To obtain the detectable signal, a certain number of proteins are needed. Since there is no chemical method available for protein amplification, protein concentration and trapping is the feasible way to increase the number of proteins being analyzed. Recent research shows that insulating dielectrophoresis (iDEP) is a promising enrichment technique for proteins, which refers to the movement of proteins towards the large or small electric field gradient in a non-uniform electric field. It is normally performed in a microfluidic channel, where an array of insulating posts are placed in the channel and two external electrodes submerged in the reservoirs. The electric field lines are squeezed between the insulating posts and the field gradient is created around them. The iDEP force exerted on proteins mainly depends on the protein size and polarizability, and magnitude of electric field gradient. To successful trap proteins, a large electric field gradient is required. This requirement comes from the fact that proteins have a small dimension (only a few nanometers) and low polarizability. To generate the large electric field gradient, a well-known way is to scale down the dimensions of insulating posts and the spacing between adjacent posts to nanometer range. Here we propose to employ oblique angle deposition (OAD) to fabricate nanostructures and integrate them into iDEP devices. OAD can overcome a few difficulties the current fabrication methods are facing, such as the limit of insulating posts dimensions, high cost, difficult process, etc. More significantly, our preliminary simulation shows that, with the dimensions of nanorods made by OAD, the field gradient generated by them is 10 - 10^6 larger than that produced by the reported smallest insulating posts. In this project, protein trapping capability of OAD-based nanostructures will be investigated; and further experiments on iDEP improved protein detection will be carried out. Most diagnostic centers in Hong Kong mainly focus on bioanalytical and medical applications. Our studies will lead to the development of a simple, low-cost, and highly effective protein concentration and trapping technique by taking advantages of versatile nanostructures made by OAD. We believe that the success of this proposal will facilitate the low-cost bio-analysis and bio-detection chips in the related industry. 本項目書旨在從樣品中收集蛋白質以增加被檢測蛋白質的數量，從而提高蛋白質分析的信號。 蛋白質序列分析，蛋白質檢測等都是生物和醫學診斷中的重要步驟。為了獲得可檢測信號，蛋白質需要達到一定的數量。然而，目前并沒有化學方法來進行蛋白質的複製，因此，將分析樣品中的蛋白質捕獲并收集起來，是增加蛋白質數量的可行方法。 介電泳是指在一個非均勻電場中，分析物被極化，并受到一個介電泳力沿著最大或者最小電場梯度的方向移動。近年來研究表明，利用絕緣體擠壓電力線形成的非均勻電場介電泳是一種收集蛋白質的有效方法。這種方法通常是在微流控通道中放置絕緣柱子，兩頭加電壓，電力線圍繞着絕緣柱子形成電場梯度，蛋白質被捕獲并收集在絕緣柱子邊緣。介電泳力主要取決於分析物的尺寸和極化能力，以及電場梯度的大小。由於蛋白質的尺寸只有几納米，極化能力低，所以成功收集蛋白質的關鍵在於建造一個極高的電場梯度。為此，其中一個方法是將絕緣柱子的尺寸以及相鄰柱子之間的距離減小到納米尺度。本項目書提出應用斜入射沉積方法，將納米結構整合到介電泳微流控器件中，以克服一些現有技術面臨的困難，例如絕緣柱的尺寸極限，高成本，製備方法複雜等。而且，我們前期的模擬計算顯示，基於斜入射沉積製備的納米結構尺寸，電場梯度比目前報道的最大電場梯度提高了10 - 10^6 倍。因此，本項目會探索基於斜入射沉積整合的介電泳器件對蛋白質的收集能力，以及對蛋白質檢測的信號提高效果。 香港有很多醫療中心都需要進行生物分析和醫療應用，本研究希望通過斜入射沉積方法製備納米結構，發展一種簡單，低成本和高效的蛋白質捕獲和收集方法，以造福相關行業。

12300714.label: Realisation of objectives
12300714.value: 1. Fabricate tilted, L-shaped and zigzag SiO2 nanorods for iDEP protein concentration and trapping A physical vapor deposition has been utilized for integration of nanostructures in iDEP devices to obtain the super large electric field gradient. The nanostructure growth mechanism is governed by the shadowing effect and surface diffusion of adatoms. In brief, a piece of substrate is tilted at a large deposition angle θ (θ = 85°), defined as the angle between incident vapor and surface normal of the substrate. At the beginning of the deposition, randomly nucleated islands are formed on the substrate surface. As the deposition continues, the small islands will be blocked from receiving more atoms and become the voids of submerged tilted nanorods (NDs). This process is called as oblique angle deposition (OAD). If the substrate rotates azimuthally, call as glancing angle deposition (GLAD), vertical NDs will form due to the cancellation of lateral incident vapor. The L-shaped NDs are accomplished by making 180° azimuthal substrate rotations between two segments. Instead of Ag NDs, Ag islands will form by GLAD since the diffusion ability of Ag atoms is very high. 2. Fabricate tilted, L-shaped and zigzag SiO2 coated Ag nanorods for iDEP protein concentration and trapping We have fabricated SiO2 film/Ag nanoparticles/SiO2 NDs for insulating dielectrophoresis (iDEP) experiments. 3. Tune the dimensional parameters to optimize the iDEP performance of the above nanostructures Before integration of NDs, a pattern of microelectrode arrays with 5-μm gaps is created on glass wafers via coarse photolithography. The patterned device is bonded with a slab of PDMS molded with reservoirs, which are aligned with individual electrode gap for DEP trapping of particles. As targets to be captured, fluorescent polystyrene nanospheres with sizes of 500 nm and 50 nm, and Alexa 488 labeled Bovine serum albumin (BSA) protein are diluted for use. DEP experiments are started with short SiO2 NDs (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 100 nm, GLAD). Since the actual height is only few nanometers, the squeezing effect of electric lines is not observed. While positive DEP (pDEP) and negative DEP (nDEP) are observed for 500 nm beads, which should be attributed to patterned microelectrodes. Then, longer SiO2 NDs (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 1000 nm, GLAD) has been tested for the above targets. pDEP of 50-nm beads has been demonstrated using 5 Vpp at 1 MHz, concentrated around oxide NDs at the gaps of both castellated and sawtooth electrode array. This is due to intensified field gradient around oxide NDs, which has been verified as 1×10^20 V^2/m^3 through COMSOL simulation. BSA proteins quickly concentrate around oxide NDs within 10 seconds from the onset of bias (5 Vpp at 1 MHz) (pDEP). nDEP is also witnessed at the increase of frequency to 10 MHz, where fluorescent labeled BSA is abruptly repelled from gaps between electrodes rather than diffused away from the trapping positions. This observation is in accordance with the prediction by the analysis of crossover frequency. According to the simulation result, Ag ND arrays will also produce the field gradient ( ∇E^2) as high as 1.0×10^20 v^2/m^3. However, we do not observe any DEP behavior for all the target samples from Ag NDs (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 1000 nm, OAD). Since DEP even does not work for 500 nm beads, we believe that short circuit occurs because of the initial Ag nucleus growth on the substrate. Thus, a layer of SiO2 NDs (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 1000 nm, OAD) is deposited prior to Ag NDs deposition. To enhance the adhesion between Ag and oxide, 50 nm Ti has been deposited on oxide via OAD. Same problem still exist due to the possible reason that Ag NDs collapse and connect each other. We have experienced the similar problem in other projects. Interestingly, it is found that there will be positive induced charges on the left surface of the oxide shell and negative charges on the right side from the simulation. Therefore, a very strong electric field will be produced within the thin layer of oxide, corresponding to a super high field gradient, i.e., 2.6×10^24 v^2/m^3. To consolidate the structure of Ag NDs and verify the higher field gradient from the simulation, after a layer of Ag islands (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 300 nm, GLAD) has been grown on the SiO2 NDs (θ = 85◦, nominal thickness = 200 nm, GLAD), a blank evaporation of 5-nm oxide (θ = 10◦, nominal thickness = 100 nm, GLAD) is deposited onto Ag islands to form the core-shell structure. As expected, both 50 nm beads’ and BSA proteins’ concentration are observed around the oxide coated Ag NDs at the same condition as for SiO2 NDs, with an evidently stronger fluorescent intensity. 4. Design the multilayer hetero-nanostructures to improve streptavidin protein detection by iDEP Instead of streptavidin protein detection, we choose the more practical immune detection. In brief, the goat anti-mouse IgG was first covalently immobilized on the NDs surface. After adding mouse IgG, an AC field of 5 V at 1 MHz is applied to implement pDEP enrichment of target antigens. To ensure the saturation of analyte, the duration of voltage lasts for 1 minute. At last, rabbit anti-mouse IgG conjugated with Alexa 488 is added to produce sandwich complex and the fluorescent identification of captured antigens is enabled. The Limit of Detection (LoD) of the device with oxide coated Ag NDs attains 275.3 fg/mL and the dynamic range is over 3 orders. In comparison, the LoD of assay performed on the reference glass plate was found to be 5.8 ng/mL. The 20000-fold increase in detection sensitivity results from highly effective DEP enrichment of target proteins induced by strong field gradient adjacent to oxide coatings of Ag NDs. On the other hand, a LoD of 15.1 pg/mL was reported here using DEP enrichment on the device with oxide NDs, still achieving a 55-fold increment with respect to the glass plate. To explore the clinical utility of our device, we further performed the assay to detect a cancer biomarker, prostate-specific antigen, diluted in human serum, which is crucial for diagnosis and prognosis of prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy. The LoD of 2.6 pg/mL was achieved using the device with oxide coated Ag NDs, compared with 7.5 ng/mL for assays conducted on glass plates.

12300714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300714.value: We have demonstrated highly effective enrichment of proteins by using insulator-based DEP integrated with ND arrays, which are easily achieved via OAD/GLAD without the requirement of advanced lithography tools. Through theoretical analysis and scientific simulation, these ND arrays are able to create a strong electric field of 1.0×10^8 V/m and a super high field gradient of 2.6×10^24 V^2/m^3. Thus, we achieved 1800-fold enrichment of BSA at average rate of 180-fold/s using oxide coated Ag NDs device pre-patterned with sawtooth electrodes. Leveraging on the platform, the immunoassay sensitivity of mouse IgG was significantly enhanced by 20000-fold, from 5.8 ng/mL down to 275.3 fg/mL, while the accuracy has been also confirmed by recovery rate measurement. A practical assay to detect a cancer biomarker PSA was also presented with a detection limit of 2.6 pg/mL, which is comparable to or better than state-of-the-art methods. The concentration of proteins also accelerates the binding kinetics and therefore greatly shortens the incubation time, reaching a steady signal level within one minute from the onset of DEP enrichment. Together with a simple fabrication method, easy operation and highly sensitive immunoassay performance, the platform poses great potentials in applications for bioanalysis and biosensors. Please refer to publication 1 in part C.

12300714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300714.value: We will continuously work on both practical and fundamental ideas. First, we are designing a multiplex assay using protein concentration by iDEP, which has great potential to be commercialized. Based on the simple fabrication technique and verified high sensitivity, the multiplex assay can be easily integrated into bio-analysis and bio-detection chips for convenient use and fast detection in diagnostic clinics or ports. Second, we have further designed and fabricated more versatile nanostructures such as rugate structure and multi-layer oxide coated Ag nanoparticles, targeting even higher field gradient for single-molecule detection. Our preliminary simulation has shown that the field gradient produced by rugate structure could reach 1.0×10^26 V^2/m^3. We believe that out studies will lead to the development of simple, low-cost, and highly effective protein and single-molecule analysis and detection.

12300714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300714.value: Protein analysis is an important step in biological and medical diagnostics. To obtain the detectable signal, a certain number of proteins are needed. Un-like cells and DNAs, there is no chemical method available for protein amplification. Therefore, protein concentration and trapping is the feasible way to increase the number of proteins being analyzed. Dielectrophoresis (DEP) is a promising manipulation technique, which exerts a force on particles and pulls them to some designated points on chips. Since DEP force is proportional to particle size, it becomes challenging to capture proteins with a typical diameter of 2~3 nm. In our study, we have successfully integrated versatile nanostructures into DEP devices and significantly increase the strength of DEP force for proteins concentration. By concentrating the proteins from the provided sample, our device is able to detect mouse immunoglobulin G with femtomolar sensitivity and a cancer biomarker, prostate-specific antigen, spiked in human serum with a detection limit of 2.6 pg/mL. We believe that this project will facilitate the low-cost bio-analysis and bio-detection chips in the related industry.

12300914.label: Realisation of objectives
12300914.value: Overall speaking, the project objectives have been well achieved. 1. We have developed and optimized a GC-MS based analytical method for the quantification of PM2.5-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), nitrated PAHs (NPAHs), and hydroxylated PAHs (OHPAHs) in 56 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a 1-year period. POA and SOA markers, such as levoglucosan, hopanes, tracers of isoprene, monoterpene and beta-caryophellen SOA, total and water-soluble metals, and major aerosol constituents, i.e. EC, OC, inorganic cations and anions, were quantified as well. 2. We have investigated the oxidative potential of PM2.5 using various bioanalytical techniques. a. We’ve applied both cell-free dithiothreitol (DTT) and terephthalate (TPT) assay to measure the DTT consumption rate and ∙OH generation ability of water-soluble PM2.5 collected in Hong Kong. The lipid-soluble extract of PM2.5 almost showed no response to DTT and TPT assay. b. We’ve applied the murine macrophage cell line RAW 264.7 to evaluate the expression of oxidative stress related cytokines induced upon exposure to water-soluble extracts of 49 Hong Kong PM2.5 samples. The level of tumor necrosis factor (TNF-α) was determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) with cell viabilities over 80%. MTT (Thiazolyl Blue Tetrazolium Bromide) was used to monitor the viability of exposed cells. The level of TNF-α induced by lipid-soluble extract of PM2.5 was much lower (~10 times lower) than that induced by the water-soluble extract. Since the lipid-soluble extract of PM2.5 showed nearly no response to DTT and TPT assay either, we then focused on the redox activity of water-soluble extract of PM2.5 in this project. c. To get a better understanding of the ROS activity of different components of PM2.5, we’ve also examined the DTT activity of water-soluble humic-like substances (HULIS) in 49 and 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong and Beijing, respectively. 3. We have applied positive matrix factorization (PMF) to apportion the pollution sources of waters-soluble PM2.5 associated DTT consumption and ∙OH generation. Sampled air volume-normalized DTT activity (DTTV) and ∙OH generation (∙OHV), together with various chemical source markers, were input into PMF, and six sources of water-soluble PM2.5 associated redox activity have been identified. All six sources, i.e. secondary sulfate (SS), biomass burning (BB), secondary organic aerosol (SOA), vehicle emissions, marine vessels and metals, were found to be DTT active. However, only three sources, i.e. metals, vehicle emissions, and SOA, showed contribution to ∙OH generation. Pearson’s R analysis between measured ROS activity and selected PM2.5 components have been conducted. We have also evaluated the intrinsic ROS generation ability of water soluble PM2.5 from each source. We have examined the correlation between measured DTTV and ∙OHV, and found no correlation. Nevertheless, both of them showed high values on days mainly influenced by regional pollution sources. TNF-α, on the other hand, showed remarkably different seasonal trend as those for DTT activity and ∙OH generation. It showed higher levels on local days than on LRT and regional days. Spearman correlation tests were conducted between TNF-α and all chemical species we measured in PM2.5. Overall, the relationship between TNF-α and the chemical composition of PM2.5 was quite complex, and could be a comprehensive effects from all emission sources in Hong Kong. Most organic constituents, particularly HULIS and levoglucosan, and some inorganic compounds, such as Mn, Fe, As, Cd and sulfate, showed negative correlations with TNF-α. We also examined the relationships between TNF-α and PMF-resolved PM2.5 sources of the same batch samples and further discussed the influence of PM sources on its oxidative potential. As an extension of my previously funded GRF grant HKBU201212, we have also apportioned HULIS-associated DTT activity in PM2.5 samples collected in both Hong Kong and Beijing using PMF. Biomass burning and secondary processes were found to be the top two contributors to HULIS-associated DTT activity in both megacities. Four manuscripts have been generated from results obtained in this project. One has been published, one is under review, one is ready to be submitted soon, and one is under preparation. The first three manuscripts have been uploaded in Part C. 1. In the past few years, the PI and PhD students involved in this project have participated several national and international conferences to present results related to this project. Details of the conference presentations were provided in Part C.

12300914.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300914.value: A comprehensive characterization and source apportionment of PM2.5-bound toxic compounds, i.e. PAHs, NPAHs and OHPAHs, were conducted for 56 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong. BaPeq-based PM2.5 toxicity was also evaluated. Based on the results, we’ve obtained a better understanding of the levels, atmospheric transformation, sources, and health implications of PM2.5-bound PAHs and their derivatives in the region (Ma et al. 2016 in Part C). ROS activity of water-soluble PM2.5 collected in Hong Kong during a one-year period was assessed in terms of DTT consumption and ∙OH generation using cell-free DTT and TPT assay. Both of them showed high values on days mainly influenced by regional pollution sources, indicating more ROS active PM2.5 components generated or transported to Hong Kong under this condition. Six sources of water-soluble PM2.5 associated redox activity were apportioned by PMF, i.e. secondary sulfate (SS), biomass burning (BB), secondary organic aerosol (SOA), vehicle emissions, marine vessels and metals. Primary sources accounted for 83.5% of DTT activity, with metals as the leading contributor on days under regional and long regional transport pollution, and marine vessels to be the most significant on the days under local pollution. Metals also made the predominant contribution (84.5%) to ∙OH generation throughout the year. All six sources were found to be DTT active, however, only three sources, i.e. metals, vehicle emissions, and SOA, showed contribution to ∙OH generation. Based on PMF results, we further evaluate the intrinsic ROS generation ability of water-soluble PM2.5 from each source. Marine vessels exhibited the highest intrinsic DTT activity; while metal factors was the most effective source in ∙OH generation (Cheng et al. in Part C). The level of TNF-α induced upon exposure of water extracts of PM2.5 was determined using ELISA with cell viabilities over 80%. For the 49 Hong Kong PM2.5 samples, expression levels of TNF-α ranged from 25.3 to 434.2 pg mL-1, with the annual average value of 70.9 pg mL-1. However, an inverse correlation was found between TNF-α and DTT-ROS activity. TNF-α exhibited higher levels on local days (average: 102.1 pg mL-1), than on LRT days (56.0 pg mL-1) and regional days (38.3 pg mL-1). Industrial exhaust, BB, SOA were found to have a suppression effect on TNF-α; yet marine vessels had a significant positive correlation with TNF-α, which explains the higher level of TNF-α expression on local days (Cheng et al. in Part C).

12300914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300914.value: Future study will be carried out to assess the ability of different chemical fractions of PM2.5 (i.e. total, lipid soluble, water-soluble, and water-soluble metals) to induce expression of cytokines and differential expression genes (DEGs) using both in vitro and in vivo models. We also plan to evaluate the synergistic and antagonistic effects of different PM2.5 components on PM toxicity.

12300914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300914.value: A comprehensive study on the concentrations, sources, atmospheric transformation and health implications of PM2.5-bound toxic compounds, i.e. PAHs, NPAHs and OHPAHs, has been conducted for PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong over a 1-yr period. We have assessed the DTT activity and ∙OH generation ability of water-soluble PM2.5 using cell-free DTT and TPT assays, and both showed higher values under regional pollution. PM2.5 from six sources, i.e. secondary sulfate (SS), biomass burning (BB), secondary organic aerosol (SOA), vehicle emissions, marine vessels and metals, were identified to be DTT-active using PMF. However, only three sources associated PM2.5, i.e. metals, vehicle emissions, and SOA, showed ∙OH generation ability. Most of the water-soluble PM2.5 associated redox activity come from primary sources. Particularly, marine vessels exhibited the highest intrinsic DTT activity; while metal factors was the most effective source in ∙OH generation. The level of TNF-α induced upon exposure of water extracts of PM2.5 showed an inverse correlation with DTT-ROS activity. Industrial exhaust, BB, SOA were found to have a suppression effect on TNF-α; yet marine vessels had a significant positive correlation with TNF-α, explaining the higher TNF-α expression level under local pollution.

12301214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301214.value: In last few decades, more and more anomalous diffusion phenomena have been found in the real world applications, which lead to fractional diffusion equations. The use of fractional diffusion equations was shown to provide an adequate and accurate description for these diffusion phenomena. One of the main characteristics of the fractional differential operator is non-local. Most numerical methods for fractional diffusion equations generate dense coefficient matrices which are different from sparse coefficient matrices arising from the standard second-order diffusion equations. However, such dense coefficient matrices have Toeplitz-like structure which can be written as the sum of the scaled identify matrix and two diagonal-times-Toeplitz matrices. Therefore, the storage requirement can be reduced to O(n) where n is the number of grid points. By using the fast Fourier transform, the matrix-vector multiplication of these dense coefficient matrices can be done in O(n log n) operations. The main aim of this proposal is to develop preconditioning techniques for such diagonal-times-Toeplitz matrices arising from the discretization scheme of fractional diffusion equations. Our idea is to construct a preconditioner by approximating the inverse of the sum of the scaled identify matrix and two diagonal-times-Toeplitz matrices. One of the interesting property of these Toeplitz matrices is that their diagonals are the Fourier coefficients of a function behaving like |x|^a, where a is the fractional order of the derivative in the fractional diffusion equation. The preconditioning techniques for this kind of Toeplitz matrices has not been studied in the literature. We would like to establish new theoretical results for circulant preconditioners for this kind of Toeplitz matrices. By using the new proposed results of circulant approximation, we will study and analyze the spectral properties of the approximate inverse preconditioned matrices. In particular, we would like to show the preconditioned matrices are the sum of a matrix of low rank and a matrix of small norm. The performance of the proposed preconditioners will be analyzed and evaluated by testing for a wide range of examples including three-dimensional fractional diffusion equations. 在過去的幾十年裡，越來越多的反常擴散現象已在現實世界中的應用程序，從而導致分數擴散方程的發現。利用分數階擴散方程的結果顯示，以提供足夠和準確的描述，這些擴散的現象。分數階微分算子的主要特點是非本地。大多數的分數階擴散方程的數值解法生成緻密係數矩陣這是從標準的二階擴散方程的稀疏係數矩陣不同。然而，這種緻密的係數矩陣具有托普利茲狀結構，它可以寫為經縮放的識別矩陣之和兩條對角線倍-Toeplitz矩陣。因此，存儲要求可以降低到O(n)，其中n為網格點的數量。通過使用快速傅立葉變換，這些稠密係數矩陣的矩陣 - 向量乘法可以在O(nlogn)的操作。 該方案的主要目的是發展預處理技術，從分數階擴散方程的離散格式所產生的這種對角線倍，Toeplitz矩陣。我們的想法是通過近似縮放的識別矩陣和兩個對角倍-Toeplitz矩陣的和的倒數來構造預處理器。其中一個Toeplitz矩陣的有趣特性是，其對角線功能的行為就像傅立葉係數| X | ^ a，其中a是在分數階擴散方程的導數的分數階。在預處理技術，對這種Toeplitz矩陣的尚未研究在文獻中。我們想建立新的理論成果為循環預條件對這種Toeplitz矩陣的。通過使用循環近似的新建議的結果，我們將研究和分析近似逆預處理矩陣的光譜特性。特別是，我們想展現的預處理矩陣是低級別的矩陣之和的小範數的矩陣。所提出的預處理器的性能進行分析，並通過測試，適用範圍廣的例子包括三維的分數階擴散方程的評估。

12301214.label: Realisation of objectives
12301214.value: The objectives of this project are achieved by developing new preconditioning techniques for diagonal-times-Toeplitz matrices arising from the discretization scheme of fractional diffusion equations. Both theoretical (the analysis of the Fourier coefficients) and experimental results are analyzed and reported in several publications to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. Under mild conditions on variable diffusion coeffcients, we have shown that the singular values of the preconditioned matrix are bounded above and below by positive constants which are independent of temporal and spatial discretization step-sizes. When the preconditioned conjugate gradient squared method is employed to solve such preconditioned linear systems, the method converges linearly within an iteration number independent of the discretization step-sizes.

12301214.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301214.value: In [Output #1], we develop approximate inverse preconditioners for such diagonal times-Toeplitz matrices. An approximate inverse preconditioner is constructed to approximate the inverses of weighted Toeplitz matrices by circulant matrices, and then combine them together row-by-row. Theoretically, we have shown that the spectra of the resulting preconditioned matrices are clustered around one. In [Output #2,3], we further study the linear systems arising from the discretization of time dependent space-fractional diffusion equations based on the finite volume discretization scheme for the space-fractional derivative. We have shown that the spectra of the corresponding preconditioned matrices are clustered around 1. In [Output #4,5], we tested the proposed methods for time-dependent and space-fractional diffusion equations and the experimental results have shown the proposed methods are better than the other existing methods. In [Output #6], we study Toeplitz-like linear systems arising from time-dependent one-dimensional and two-dimensional Riesz space-fractional diffusion equations with variable diffusion coefficients. The splitting method based on the approximate inverse preconditioning is introduced. We have shown that the singular values of the preconditioned matrix are bounded above and below by positive constants which are independent of temporal and spatial discretization step-sizes.

12301214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301214.value: In many practical applications, the source term in fractional diffusion equations is unknown. In the future research work, we are interested in solving this inverse source problem by employing additional measurement data. We study modified quasi-boundary value method and Tiknonov regularization method for solving this inverse source problem. The main challenge is to develop fast iterative solvers for such very large block linear systems arising from the modified quasi-boundary method and Tiknonov regularization method. We remark that the number of unknowns can be very large when the time and spatial discretization step-sizes are very small. It is interesting to develop new preconditioning methods for solving such very large linear systems. Our idea is to construct Schur complement preconditioners based on block-circulant-type approximation and divide-and-conquer technique. We will investigate the spectra analysis of the proposed preconditioned matrices and demonstrate the fast convergence of the preconditioned iterative method.

12301214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301214.value: The time fractional diffusion equation can be used to describe the anomalous diffusion phenomena instead of the classical diffusion process. The main idea is to replace the standard time derivative by the time fractional derivative (the Caputo derivative). In some applications, time-space fractional diffusion equation is employed by replacing the standard spatial derivative by the Riemann-Liouville derivative or the Riesz fractional derivative. Because of nonlocal nature of these derivatives, their discretized systems of equations involve dense coefficient matrices. In this project, we successfully study and analyze several preconditioning techniques for solving this kind of linear systems, and present interesting theoretical and experimental results for further mathematical development and applications in other areas such as inverse problems.

12301514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301514.value: The ability to monitor nutrient and other environmental conditions with high sensitivity is crucial for cell growth and survival. Sensory adaptation allows a cell to recover its sensitivity after a transient response to a shift in the strength of extracellular stimulus. The working principles of adaptation have been established previously based on rate equations which do not consider fluctuations in a thermal environment. A more complete approach to the problem requires a statistical mechanical reformulation in terms of discrete chemical states and transition rates governed by free energies. Recently, G. Lan et al. (Nature Phys., 8:422-8, 2012) performed a detailed analysis of a stochastic model for the E. coli sensory network. They showed that accurate adaptation is possible only when the system operates in a nonequilibrium steady-state. They further obtained a relation among energy dissipation, adaptation speed and adaptation error through model calculation and suggested that it may hold generally. However, adaptation is only one aspect of the bacterial chemo-sensing system. Its transient response to ligand concentration fluctuations with high gain is at least as important. Therefore, it would be quite surprising if the operational cost of the sensory network is solely for reducing the adaptation error. In fact, the energy dissipation is present even when there is no change in the extracelllar ligand concentration. We therefore propose to re-analyze the stochastic model of G. Lan et al. to gain a better understanding of the origin of the observed relationship. The simplicity of the model allows a rigorous treatment using methods of statistical mechanics. The model also possesses several desirable analytic properties which make it an attractive testing ground to demystify various general results on energy dissipation and linear response in nonequilibrium states in the literature. We believe the detailed model study will contribute to the “Hamiltonian formulation” of molecular network dynamics that goes beyond the rate equation approach, thereby bringing physics closer to biology. 對營養及其他環境因素的高度敏感是細胞生長和存活的關鍵要素。在對體外信號強度的變化做出瞬態響應後，受體的適應性可以讓細胞恢復其靈敏度。它的工作原理在過去基於速率方程的研究中已被確立，但此類討論忽略了熱環境中漲落的影響。更完整的處理需要從受體分子的離散化學狀態及其相互轉換的速率出發，運用統計力學的方法對問題做重新定義。最近，藍贛輝等研究者（《自然物理》8：422-8，2012）提出了一個大腸桿菌傳感網絡的隨機模型並對其做了詳細分析。他們發現精確適應只有當系統工作在非平衡態時才能被實現。他們還通過模型計算提出了一個能量消耗、適應速度及適應誤差之間的關係。 然而，適應性僅是細菌化學遷移系統的一個側面。維持系統對體外配體濃度變化的高增益瞬態響應至少是同樣重要的。因此，如果傳感網絡的能耗僅是為了減少適應誤差，這將是非常令人驚訝的。事實上，能量耗散即使在體外配體濃度不發生變化時也同樣存在。因此，我們建議重新分析藍贛輝等提出的隨機模型，更好地理解他們觀察到的關係的起源。該模型的簡單性允許用統計力學的方法對其進行嚴格處理。該模型還具有若干理想的解析特性，這使得它成為一個有趣的練習場，用來揭密文獻中大量非平衡系統的能量耗散、線性響應的一般性結論。我們相信，詳細的模型研究將促進建立分子網絡動態分析的“漢密爾頓方法”，超越目前常用的速率方程，讓物理學更走近生物學。

12301514.label: Realisation of objectives
12301514.value: During the course of the project, we have made good progress towards completing the objectives laid out in the original proposal, both with regard to the solution of a specific model of sensory adaptation and more generally modes of energy dissipation in driven Markov systems with adaptation. In the second half of the project, we applied the general theory to collective oscillations in adaptive cell populations, a natural extension of the original research program. We showed that, in addition to the heat dissipated to maintain an adaptive circuit in the nonequilibrium state, energy outflow in the form of work induced by a time-dependent stimulus in a frequency interval. This provides a physical mechanism to initiate cell-to-cell communication through oscillatory signaling, provided the local cell density exceeds certain threshold. Our approach shed new light on dynamical quorum sensing which is widely employed to coordinate multicellular developmental programs. Although the key theoretical results were derived more than two years ago, it took us much time to go through the vast biological literature to validate the model assumptions and to find evidence for the theoretical predictions in specific systems, including glycolytic oscillations in yeast cell suspensions and cAMP waves in social amoebae. With this hard-earned experience, we are more ready to tackle significant biological problems using ideas and methods from nonequilibrium statistical physics. Details are given below. 1) With regard to the two-node adaptation network proposed previously by Lan et al., we derived exact results on the nonequilibrium steady-state distribution, an expression for receptor activity with respect to external signal strength, energy dissipation of the circuit, and also frequency-resolved transient response. We have shown that the fluctuation-response relation is violated for both activity and methylation variables. As the system is driven out of equilibrium, the energy dissipation continues to increase. However, there is a limit to the "accuracy" of adaptation for a system with a finite methylation range. On the other hand, adaptation accuracy, as measured by insensitivity to a shift in external signal strength after a short time transient, can be arbitrarily high at a finite dissipation rate. These results do not agree with the relation proposed by Lan et al. in their 2012 paper, where adaptation error was defined in the nonequilibrium steady-state. We also showed that the system exhibits a nonequilibrium phase transition in the infinite methylation range limit, despite the fact that the model contains only two discrete variables. The phase transition also highlights adaptation as a property not just out of equilibrium, but sufficiently far from equilibrium. These results were published in J Stat Phys: Theory and Experiment, P07025 (2015). 2) The adaptation model has a property known as time-scale separation that greatly simplifies the theoretical analysis. Inspired by the successful analysis of the model, we studied a general class of Markov models with fast and slow variables. The driven motion of a colloidal particle in a fluid satisfies such a description. In the absence of the slow process, the system would stay in the reduced phase space spanned by the fast variables. Suppose the dynamics of the fast variables do not satisfy detailed balance, i.e., they are active instead of in thermal equilibrium. The question is whether one can detect or even determine the energy dissipated from time series measurements of the slow variable. A partial answer can be obtained from the Harada-Sasa equality, which expresses the work done by the slow variable against the dissipative medium as an integral of FDT violation in frequency space. By setting up a degenerate perturbation scheme in the master equation formulation, we showed that the FDT violation has a constant magnitude in the frequency regime delimited by the fast and slow time scales. As the magnitude is proportional to the ratio of the fast and slow time scales, the total energy dissipated is independent of the size of the frequency window. The dynamics of the slow variable on longer time scales may satisfy detailed balance, in which case its motion can be described by a Langevin equation with an effective potential and effective noise strength. These general results were reported in Phys Rev Lett 117, 070601 (2016) and in a preprint deposited online (arXiv:1610.00120). In the two-node adaptation model, receptor activity is fast while the methylation level change is slow. 3) Sensory adaptation can be realized in a stochastic linear model of two variables. Its response and correlation functions can be calculated exactly, both in real time and in frequencies. The so-called response spectral function has a real part and an imaginary part. For an equilibrium system, the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) requires the imaginary part to be positive at all frequencies. Our results show that this requirement is violated by the adaptive circuit at low frequencies. We have since constructed a general proof to link the negative imaginary part of the response function in a certain frequency interval to adaptation itself. The proof is a simple application of the Kramers-Kroenig relation from causality. Put it simply, sensory adaptation is able to anticipate recurrent stimuli by developing a phase lead over a periodic signal. The phase-leading behavior opens up a remarkable possibility: the nonequilibrium circuit is able to drive a passive signal source through stimulated energy release. In this scenario, the role of the signal and the receptor unit is reversed. This is one of the most original findings coming out of the current project. Part of this work can be found in the online preprint arXiv:1611.04089. 4) In the manuscript “Emergence of collective oscillations in adaptive cells” attached to the report (under review with Nature Communications), we reported three case studies to illustrate how the above general results could be applied to specific cellular systems with increasing biological complexity. The first is a high-level model where signal reception and release are integrated into the same activity node (e.g., a membrane protein or a molecular motor). Due to the weak nonlinearity of the intracellular circuit, many analytical results could be obtained, including the onset cell density and oscillation frequency. Much of these results carry over to the second example, a population of coupled excitable circuits described by the FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) model. Despite its highly nonlinear nature, the FHN model in the resting state shows adaptive response under weak stimulation. Our third example is glycolytic oscillation in yeast cell suspensions, whose origin is still disputed after fifty years of dedicated research. Despite the overwhelming complexity of the metabolic and regulatory network, our simulation studies yielded a relatively simple picture which is reproduced semi-quantitatively by a 3-variable model of ATP autocatalysis. Fast exchange of the metabolite acetaldehyde between cells gives rise to collective oscillations that span over both adaptive and oscillating regimes of individual cells. In this respect, our study unifies the two competing claims in the literature regarding the origin of glycolytic oscillations, i.e., autonomous or through mutual stimulation. The detailed model studies, which involve a great deal of work, establish adaptation as a unifying theme behind dynamical quorum sensing reported in the recent literature. We believe the high-level yet flexible modelling strategy based on response functions should have applications to a broad range of complex spatiotemporal phenomena.
