12301514.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301514.value: 1) Energy dissipation in an adaptive molecular circuit (JSTAT P07025). Analytic results on the NESS of a two-node adaptation model were obtained through a mapping to a one-dimensional birth-death process. An exact expression for the entropy production rate is also derived. Based on these results, we are able to discuss the "energy-speed-accuracy tradeoff" relation in a more general setting. Our study suggests that the adaptation error can be reduced exponentially as the methylation range increases. Finally, we show that a nonequilibrium phase transition exists in the infinite methylation range limit, despite the fact that the model contains only two discrete variables. 2) Entropy Production of Nanosystems with Time Scale Separation (PRL 117, 070601, arXiv:1601.04463). Experimental observations of energy transport and dissipation in biomolecular motors and machines are limited to a small subset of variables. Through a solvable Langevin model, we show that the seemingly hidden entropy production is measurable through the violation spectrum of the fluctuation-response relation of a slow observable. For general Markov systems with time scale separation, we prove that the violation spectrum exhibits a characteristic plateau in the intermediate frequency region. Despite its vanishing height, the plateau can account for energy dissipation over a broad time scale. Our findings suggest a general possibility to probe hidden entropy production in nanosystems without direct observation of fast variables. 3) Extracting energy from non-equilibrium fluctuations without using information (arXiv:1611.04089). We show that energy extraction from a body using a noisy signal demands a negative response spectrum in a certain frequency region, which is possible only when the body is out of equilibrium. Negative response is intrinsic to any system that adapts to a slow external operation. These are demonstrated through a solvable model. 4) Emergence of collective oscillations in adaptive cells (paper under review with Nature Communications). We establish here a fundamental link between adaptive cellular response in cell-to-cell communication and auto-induced collective oscillations. Through mathematical constructions, we show that adaptation translates into the precise notation of a phase lead that enables cells to anticipate recurrent stimuli. Thermodynamically, this opens an “active” frequency window for stimulated energy flow from cells to the signal. We present quantitative relations for the onset cell density and frequency of oscillations in terms of measured single-cell and signal response functions. Analysis of dynamical quorum sensing in several cellular systems with increasing biological complexity reaffirms the pivotal role of adaptation in sustaining oscillations in an otherwise dissipative communication channel.

12301514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301514.value: The work on collective oscillations took more than two years to complete. The general formalism, based on response functions of cells and the medium, can be applied to spatio-temporal pattern formation in other active systems, notably swarming bacterial suspensions. We are actively pursuing this avenue of research with the experimental group led by Yilin Wu at CUHK. Funding from the RGC to support the project would be highly desirable. Through the course of the project, we have generated many results, some of which have been announced as preprints deposited online. We will get them submitted in the near future.

12301514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301514.value: Sensory adaptation allows a cell to recover its sensitivity after a transient response to a shift in the strength of extracellular stimulus. In this project, we developed statistical mechanical formalisms to treat this and related phenomena beyond the traditional rate equations. With the help of response functions against the external stimuli, we quantify the system's performance and relate it to the underlying energy-driven processes. The response functions can be either measured directly in experiments, or calculated using models with various levels of approximation to the real system. Our results clarified some of the proposals in the literature with regard to the role played by nonequilibrium processes in enhancing the system's performance. We also obtained general expressions on how active processes on fast time scales affect the systems dynamics on slow time scales, in particular those with functional implications. The renewed understanding between adaptation and energy-driven processes led us to a fundamental link between adaptation and auto-induced collective oscillations in cell populations. Our results not only help to pinpoint the "core oscillator" in a given system through its response properties, but also shed light on other group behavior resulting from adaption of individuals to their local environment.

12301614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301614.value: The Allen-Cahn equation has been widely used to model various phenomena in nature. In particular it has become a basic model equation for the diffuse interface approach developed to study phase transitions and interfacial dynamics in materials science. As the exact solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation cannot be found, numerical methods have played an important role in various simulations. One of the important numerical aspects is about the discrete stability of the numerical schemes. This project is to carry out a systematic study on the numerical stability for the numerical solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation. The numerical approximations will involve finite difference, finite element and spectral method in space and implicit-explicit scheme in time. The goal is to identify some effective numerical schemes that provide high resolution in space and allow reasonably large time steps in time. Allen-Cahn方程在自然界很多現象中有廣泛的應用﹐其主要應用之一是材料科學中相變動力學的擴散界面的模型研究。由於Allen-Cahn方程的精確解不能夠給出﹐數值求解在很多實際模擬中變得非常重要。數值方法中一個很重要的概念就是計算方法的離散穩定性。這一研究項目將對Allen-Cahn方程提供系統的數值離散穩定性研究﹐包括對空間有限差分格式﹑有限元格式和譜方法,以及時間上的隱顯格式。我們的目的是確定一些空間高分辨時間大步長的高效數值方法。

12301614.label: Realisation of objectives
12301614.value: In this project, we emphasize the three research targets. The first one is to analyze semi-implicit finite-difference method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. We wish to understand the L^∞ -stability (i.e., the maximum principle) of the numerical solution. This is fully justified in the following paper: J. Shen, T. Tang, and J. Yang, On The Maximum Principle Preserving Schemes For The Generalized Allen-Cahn Equation, Commu. Math. Sci. 14(6) (2016), 1517-1534. This paper is concerned with the generalized Allen–Cahn equation with a nonlinear mobility that may be degenerate, which also includes an advection term appearing in many phasefield models for multi-component fluid flows. A class of maximum principle preserving schemes are studied for the generalized Allen–Cahn equation, with either the commonly used polynomial free energy or the logarithmic free energy, and with a nonlinear degenerate mobility. For time discretization, the standard semi-implicit scheme as well as the stabilized semi-implicit scheme are adopted, while for space discretization, the central finite difference is used for approximating the diffusion term and the upwind scheme is employed for the advection term. We establish the maximum principle for both semi-discrete (in time) and fully discretized schemes. We also provide an error estimate by using the established maximum principle which plays a key role in the analysis. Several numerical experiments are carried out to verify our theoretical results. The second target is to carry out theoretical study to the semi-implicit Fourier-spectral method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. The Fourier-spectral method whose convergence rate is exponential (for smooth functions) may lead to serious difficulty for stability analysis due to the nonlinearity of the governing equation. This will require us some careful study of the relevant numerical schemes. This target is realized by the following paper which provides some deep insight on the relevant methods: D. Li, Z. Qiao, and T. Tang, Characterizing the stabilization size for semi-implicit Fourier-spectral method to phase field equations, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 54(3) (2016), 1653-1681. Recent results in the literature provide computational evidence that the stabilized semi-implicit time-stepping method can efficiently simulate phase field problems involving fourth-order nonlinear diffusion, with typical examples like the Cahn-Hilliard equation and the thin film type equation. The up-to-date theoretical explanation of the numerical stability relies on the assumption that the derivative of the nonlinear potential function satisfies a Lipschitz-type condition, which in a rigorous sense, implies the boundedness of the numerical solution. In the above work we remove the Lipschitz assumption on the nonlinearity and prove unconditional energy stability for the stabilized semi-implicit time-stepping methods. It is shown that the size of the stabilization term depends on the initial energy and the perturbation parameter but is independent of the time step. The corresponding error analysis is also established under minimal nonlinearity and regularity assumptions. Fractional differential equations have been investigated extensively theoreticalland numerically in recent years. The third target is to study the case when fractional diffusion is used for Allen-Cahn reactions. It is new and challenging to analyze numerical stability for fractional-in-space equations. No papers have been published yet, but part of the results has been obtained in the thesis of my PhD student Huifang Yuan: Spectral Collocation Methods for the Fractional PDEs in Unbounded Domain, PhD Thesis, HKBU, July, 2018 In summary, the project objectives have been almost fully achieved, with some writing up for the third target.

12301614.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301614.value: The main findings are the two-folds. First, it is known that the Allen-Chan equations satisfy the maximum principle. Is this true for numerical schemes? To the best of our knowledge, the state-of-art stability framework is the nonlinear energy stability which has been studied extensively for the phase field type equations. In this project, we have shown that a stronger stability under the infinity norm can be established for the implicit-explicit discretization in time and central finite difference in space. In other words, this commonly used numerical method for the Allen-Cahn equation preserves the maximum principle. The second finding is about the stabilization size for semi-implicit Fourier-spectral method to phase field equations. The up-to-date theoretical explanation of the numerical stability relies on the assumption that the derivative of the nonlinear potential function satisfies a Lipschitz-type condition, which in a rigorous sense, implies the boundedness of the numerical solution. In this project we have successfully removed the Lipschitz assumption on the nonlinearity and prove unconditional energy stability for the stabilized semi-implicit time-stepping methods. It is shown that the size of the stabilization term depends on the initial energy and the perturbation parameter but is independent of the time step. The corresponding error analysis is also established under minimal nonlinearity and regularity assumptions.

12301614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301614.value: Fractional differential equations have been investigated extensively theoretically and numerically in recent years. The third target of this proposal is to study fractional Allen-Cahn reactions. In fact, it is a new and challenging direction to study fractional phase-field problems, including fractional Allen-Cahn equation and fractional Cahn-Hilliard equation. Some useful tools developed in the study of this proposal can be extended to study the fractional phase-field problems. Some new tools particularly suitable for the global framework must be developed.

12301614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301614.value: The main difficulty for developing a numerical method for phase field equations is a severe stability restriction on the time step due to nonlinearity and high order differential terms. It is known that the phase field models satisfy a nonlinear stability relationship called gradient stability, usually expressed as a time-decreasing free-energy functional. This property has been used recently to derive numerical schemes that inherit the gradient stability. The state-of-art schemes include implicit-explicit time discretizations which satisfy the energy stability. However, how to theoretically justify the well-posedness of the numerical approaches, such as stability and convergence, have to be understood from mathematical point of view. This is the main motivation of the present proposal. Some interesting theoretical results on stability and convergence are obtained in this project. We also developed some useful tools which can be used for studying some generalized models.

12301814.label: Realisation of objectives
12301814.value: The objectives have been successfully achieved as planned. The collaboration was very effective and has spawned new directions that are now still being investigated in an ongoing CRF project on "Cooperative Molecular Rotors" (C2014-15G) led by this GRF project’s PI. A central effort of this GRF project has been the development and systematic application of the concept of torque to examine the rotational behavior of rotational motor molecules: it is a general approach that we have shown to extend far beyond the initial focus of this project, namely far beyond light-driven molecular rotors at surfaces. Indeed, torque is also ubiquitous in a wide range of other dynamic molecular phenomena such as collisions, chemical reactions, vibrations and electronic excitations. We have utilized this concept of torque predictively, i.e. to predict whether a particular molecule prepared in a specific state (e.g. photoexcited or twisted in a collision) will internally rotate or not; also, the torque vector makes it possible to predict the dominant direction of rotation: around which axis and in what sense (clockwise vs. counterclockwise) it will rotate. Our approach is general in that it makes no a priori assumptions about the rotational properties of the molecule under study, and thus includes a wide variety of possible rotational behaviors. As an illustration of the power of the method, we have modeled a well-studied light-driven rotor molecule [9-(2,4,7-trimethyl-2,3-dihydro-1Hinden- 1-ylidene)-9H-fluorene] consisting of a rotator and a stator. It is known experimentally that this molecule presents a unidirectional motor behavior by appropriate chirality, radiationless decay and two stable equilibria. To reveal its underlying mechanism, theoretical studies were performed by other groups who extensively mapped the detailed geometry of the molecule during the rotation to determine its configurational trajectories in multidimensional space: this is computationally very demanding and even then cannot confidently predict the rotation direction due to the need to explore a very-high-dimensional structural space with exhaustive and computationally onerous search methods. In our work, we are able to obtain the rotational character much more easily by calculating the torque at a few selected geometries. This efficient study of the molecule’s global behavior very much reduces the need to explore large volumes of configuration space and thus can guide a subsequent detailed study more efficiently toward a full understanding of the rotational mechanism of the system. To efficiently use torque, we have developed a systematic formalism to analyze the complex motion of atoms inside large molecules by considering translation, rotation, and flexibility of corresponding molecular fragments; we have shown that it is possible and practical to apply classical mechanics based on Pulay forces on the atoms, in analogy with molecular dynamics. We have proposed a fragment motion analysis that provides a reliable qualitative understanding of the motion of the different molecular components. It can also help to describe or design simplified fragment motions, e.g. the rotation of a rotator with respect to its stator counterpart in a rotor molecule, despite the higher actual complexity due to flexibility of both rotator and stator or due to a variable rotation axis. We have demonstrated the utility and effectiveness of the fragment motion analysis with application to the rotational motion inside the BTP-BCO molecule (4’,4’’’’-(bicyclo[2,2,2]octane-1,4-diyldi-4,1-phenylene)-bis-2,2’:6’,2’’-terpyridine) and to rotational transitions between cis- and trans-isomers of stilbene (C14H12). We have also used the induced intramolecular torque to study the underlying rotational mechanism stimulated by an electron injection or extraction for the well-known rotor molecule 9-(2,4,7-trimethyl-2,3-dihydro-1H-inden-1-ylidene)-9H-fluorene; this work complements and clarifies the photoexcitation mechanism utilized in previous experiments with the same molecule. The results show in particular that the charged molecule in a quartet spin state can rotate internally, while that in the doublet state cannot. The torque on the rotator in the quartet state always maintains unidirectional rotation. In addition, the attachment/extraction of an electron leads to the reduction of the rotational energy barrier by about 18 kcal/mol, facilitating a more favorable molecular rotation than in the neutral singlet state. Here, vibrations play a significant role via changes in the potential barrier to rotation. The flexibility of a surface or stator has a minor influence unless steric interactions interfere with internal rotations. These findings provide a molecular-level understanding of various transformation pathways for experimental designs or rotor as well as motor molecules, and further demonstrates the effectiveness of the torque approach. Our project also addressed several other interesting molecules on metal surfaces: a molecular “hover board”, and a family of molecules – 5-, 10-, 15-, and 20-tetrakis-(4-bromophenyl)-porphyrin-Co (TBrPP-Co) – via low temperature ultrahigh vacuum scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The inelastic electron tunneling (IET)-STM manipulation switching scheme is used to explore the switching of a single molecule of TBrPP-Co. It was performed by locating the STM tip on one of the protruding pyrroline subunits of TBrPP-Co molecule. The tunneling current was recorded for a few ms to seconds while the voltage and current are at fixed values. An abrupt change in the recorded characteristics curve was observed as the indication of a change in the molecule. Tunneling electrons can induce the switching between tilt-up and tilt-down positions of these pyrroline subunits by increasing the bias voltage between tip and sample. The switching of these units thus gives rise to conformational changes of TBrPP-Co between two states. Some of the energy of the tunneling electrons injected from the STM tip converts to vibrational energy of the molecules which cause the conformational switching of the molecule. Furthermore, a comprehensive study of a molecular “hover board” was performed on different substrates: it consists of two molecular wheels on a molecular axle. To activate it, an electric field is applied by STM: we find that the hover board only moves on a gold surface. The molecular hover board is driven across the herringbone reconstruction of the reconstructed gold surface by using both a positive and a negative electric field of STM in a controlled manner. Detailed analysis reveals the threshold energy required to roll the wheels of nano hover board on gold by both schemes.

12301814.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301814.value: We have investigated rotation-inducing torque since it is a ubiquitous phenomenon in many molecular systems. We present a theoretical method based on forces acting on atoms and obtained from atomistic quantum mechanics calculations to quickly determine whether a molecule or sub-unit thereof has a tendency to rotate and, if so, around which axis and in which sense: clockwise or counterclockwise. The method also indicates which atoms, if any, are predominant in causing the rotation. Our computational approach can in general efficiently provide insights into the internal rotational degrees of freedom of all molecules and help to theoretically screen or modify them in advance of experiments, or to efficiently guide a detailed analysis of their rotational behavior with more extensive computations. As an example, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of the approach using a specific light-driven molecular rotary motor which was successfully synthesized and analyzed in prior experiments and simulations. These studies have paved the way for a new directions of research which this PI has undertaken in a later RGC/CRF-supported project on "Cooperative Molecular Rotors". Also, experimental STM studies were performed on “TBrPP-Co” molecules as well as on a “hover board” molecule that can roll on a gold surface.

12301814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301814.value: Our results have suggested many possibilities for further investigations. One direction has been pursued by this PI in a later CRF on "Cooperative Molecular Rotors" (C2014-15G), which is ongoing at the time of this report: it focuses on the transmission of rotation and other forms of motion from one molecule to another, e.g. along a chain of gear molecules. Another direction, which we are also pursuing, is switch molecules, such as those involved in transport of drugs to target sites within the living body (such molecules can “open up” or “close down” around a drug particle that needs to be brought as close as possible to a disease location). A further direction of interest is the collision process of one molecule against another or against a more solid piece of material such as a catalyst surface. In all these examples, the internal rotations of molecules can play very important roles in terms of energy transfer, bond breaking and bond formation, as well as recoil phenomena. More work is desirable on the role of vibrations and deformations of large amplitude, where significant non-linear and steric effects have the potential to significantly alter the behavior of rotational molecules.

12301814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301814.value: Molecules with internal rotations can play important roles in the development of artificial molecular motors, which hold much promise for sourcing sustainable energy, developing advanced medical devices, etc. We have studied the systematics of such internal molecular rotations, to enable the prediction of rotational behavior of such molecules after external excitations, in particular light excitations and related electronic excitations.

12302114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302114.value: Nanosheet materials have attracted significant attention because of their unique electronic and physical properties, which derive from their two-dimensional (2D) nature. Graphene and other 2D inorganic sheet assemblies of metal chalcogenides (e.g. TiO2, TiNbO5, MoS2, WS2, etc.) are prominent nanosheet materials which are widely exploited in electronics, photonics, and spintronics technologies, because 2D materials possess close affinity with those used in the silicon-based electronics. Most of these nanosheets have been synthesized via exfoliation of bulk layered materials, which is a top-down method. In contrast, “bottom-up” nanosheets are generally synthesized directly from organic compounds, ligands, and/or metal ion connectors. Such examples include surface metal-organic frameworks and covalent organic frameworks. Their composition, structure, and properties can be tuned at will by tailoring the constituent components used. This is a strong point of using bottom-up nanosheet against the top-down congener. However, application studies of the bottom-up 2D metal complex nanosheets are still very rare. In this project, we initiate a new programme of designing and synthesizing a new family of bis(dipyrrinato) metal complex 2D nanosheets by the facile bottom-up approach, which can be monometallic or bimetallic in nature. Both single-layer and multilayer 2D nanosheets will be developed depending on the fabrication method (i.e. gas-liquid or liquid-liquid interfacial synthesis). The ligand structure can be easily altered in terms of spacer lengths between dipyrrinato unit and central core as well as the number of arms. Bis(dipyrrinato) metal complexes can be modified to show significant π-conjugation and intense absorptions in the visible and near-infrared region, which will be useful for the construction of photoresponsive and semiconductive nanosheets. We can easily adjust the hole and electron mobilities of the compounds by using electron-rich and electron-poor chromophores in the ligands, respectively. Therefore, bottom-up nanosheets with different topological structures, pore sizes, surface areas and advanced functionalities (e.g. tunable optical and magnetic properties) will be prepared by different monomer combinations. With our strengths in synthetic chemistry, polymer and metal complex chemistry, the properties and device performance of these metal-organic nanosheets can be fine-tuned through chemical modulations of the ligand structures and metal ions. The present work fills in a relatively under-investigated area of bottom-up 2D metal complex nanosheets. It is anticipated that an attractive class of nanosheets with novel topological structures and advanced functional properties can be developed which can find high-tech applications in electronics and spintronics.

12302114.label: Realisation of objectives
12302114.value: The PI has recruited two Ph.D. students and one postdoc. (Qian Liu) to work on the project. So far, the PI has secured 9 publications from this project (including 1 paper in Chem. Soc. Rev., 1 paper Nat. Commun., 1 paper in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 1 paper in Nano Lett., 1 paper in Nanoscale and 1 paper in Chem. Commun., etc.). The graduate students have received good training in several areas of modern science and technology in Hong Kong. A new family of metallo-organic 2D nanosheets were prepared by the direct bottom-up approach. These new nanosheets are mainly made from the complexation between dipyrrinato or terpyridyl ligands and metal ions and they can be monometallic or bimetallic in nature. Both single-layer and multilayer 2D nanosheets were developed depending on the fabrication method (i.e. gas-liquid or liquid-liquid interfacial synthesis) used. The monomer structure can be easily altered in terms of the spacer length between dipyrrinato or terpyridyl unit and the central core as well as the number of arms. The prepared metal complex nanosheets were characterized using a variety of techniques, including, SEM, TEM, AFM, XPS, FTIR, absorption, fluorescence, etc. These 2D materials can be tuned to show significant π-conjugation and intense absorptions in the visible and near-infrared region, which will be useful for the construction of photoresponsive and semiconductive nanosheets. The structure-property relationships of these nanosheets were elucidated. These bottom-up nanosheets with different topological structures, pore sizes, surface areas and advanced functionalities (such as tunable optical and photoluminescence properties) can be prepared by different monomer combinations. The potential application studies of these nanosheets were also explored briefly. As far as the GRF is concerned, the PI considers that he has addressed in full all the issues relevant to the objectives concerned.

12302114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302114.value: A new bottom-up nanosheet featuring a photoactive bis(dipyrrinato)zinc(II) complex motif was synthesized. A liquid/liquid interfacial synthesis between a three-way dipyrrin ligand and zinc(II) ions results in a multi-layer nanosheet, whereas an air/liquid interfacial reaction produces a single-layer or few-layer nanosheet with domain sizes of larger than 10 micron on one side. Such nanosheet is easy to deposit on various substrates using the Langmuir Schafer process (paper 1). Another bis(dipyrrinato)zinc(II) complex micro- and nanosheets containing zinc(II) porphyrin was also synthesized. A liquid/liquid interface method between this dipyrrin porphyrin ligand and zinc acetate produces a new nanosheet with a large domain size. The photoresponse of this nanosheet covers the whole visible wavelength range (400–650 nm), with a maximum quantum efficiency of more than twice that of a bis(dipyrrinato)zinc(II) complex nanosheet without porphyrin (paper 2). We develop a facile chemical reaction route to modulate the crystallization process of luminescent zinc 8-hydroxyquinoline (Znq2) particles. Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-modified octahedral Znq2 micro- and nano-crystals were used as seeds to construct two distinct hybrid structures (paper 3). We also develop a simple single-step solution strategy for the realization of organic heterostructures comprising coronene and perylene (paper 4). Other metallopolymers can be employed as molecular precursors to make metal-based nanomaterials (i.e. nanoparticles) (papers 5-6). Composite materials, made of graphitic carbon nitride/gadolinium and nitrogen co-doped titanium dioxide (g- C3N4/Gd-N-TiO2), were prepared by a simple and reproducible in-situ synthetic method. Specific surface area, pore size, particle morphology, crystalline structure, energy band gap, and chemical bonding mode of the materials were characterized. The composites exhibit significantly enhanced photocatalytic activity (paper 7). The Pt diamine bis(acetylide) charge-transfer chromophore was also shown to be good for developing photosensitizing metal complex which can promote electron transfer and the light-driven generation of hydrogen. This forms the basis for the future development of photofunctional Pt-acetylide based nanosheets (paper 8). The results also contribute partly to the review article in Chem. Soc. Rev. (paper 9). A series of terpyridine-based Co(II) complex nanosheets and multi-hydroxy-based Cu(II) complex nanosheets were recently synthesized by the bottom-up approach. The produced nanosheets have different morphologies, pore sizes and functionalities (e.g. luminescence, electrochromism). The effects of the ligand concentration, the metal ion concentration and time on the growth of the nanosheet films were examined. These nanosheets were characterized and their potential applications, including batteries and electrochromic switching, were demonstrated. Manuscripts concerning these results are currently in progress.

12302114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302114.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to new metal complex nanosheets containing other functional metal cores and ligand groups. (2) Enhancement of the performance of the photoelectric conversion devices based on these nanosheets. (3) Evaluation of the potential applications of these bottom-up 2D metal complex nanosheets in electronics and spintronics technologies.

12302114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302114.value: A series of ligands containing bis(dipyrrinato), terpyridyl and multi-hydroxyl groups were synthesized and they are good synthons for supramolecular coordination chemistry with a number of transition metal ions. A new family of bottom-up photofunctional metal complex nanosheets were prepared. The spectroscopic and redox behavior of these new 2D materials were investigated. With our strengths in synthetic chemistry, polymer and metal complex chemistry, the functional properties of these metal-organic nanosheets can be fine-tuned through chemical modifications of the ligand structures and metal ion connectors. The present work fills in a relatively under-investigated area of “bottom-up” metallo-organic 2D nanosheets. These nanosheets which have been shown to have photofunctionality could lead to more research into creating useful and promising nanomaterials and they will in turn open up new areas where this type of two-dimensional nanomaterials can be applied. The nanosheet deposited on a transparent SnO2 electrode functions as a photoanode in a photoelectric conversion system and represents the first photofunctional bottom-up nanosheet. It is anticipated that we can develop a variety of nanosheets with novel topological structures and advanced functional properties from this project with high potentials for high-tech applications in electronics and spintronics technologies.

12302414.label: Project Objectives

rows: Stability analysis for one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation

12302414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302414.value: This project is about the stability analysis of local artificial boundary conditons for some nonlinear partial differential equations on unbounded domains. Artificial boundaries are introduced to seperate the unbounded domains, and local boundary conditions will be obtained on the artificial boundaries, which are in nonlinear forms. Then, the original problems are reduced to initial boundary value problems on bounded computational domains. The main task of this project is the stability analysis. We will first consider the one dimensional Schrodinger equation with a general nonlinear potential, perform the numerical tests for stability and stability analysis, and then consider the two dimensional Schrodinger equation with a general nonlinear potential. Finally, we will discuss the atability of local artificial boundary conditons for some other related problems.

12302414.label: Realisation of objectives
12302414.value: Stability analysis for one and two-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equations has been carried out. Using the unified approach technique we reduced the Schrodinger equations on unbounded domains to problems on bounded domains. Under some assumptions on the nonlinear term, we proved that the numerical schemes are stable for both one and two-dimensional problems. Also, some numerical experiments are given to verify the theoretical results[1]. Application to other problems has been discussed, some results have been obtained. More specifically, we considered the numerical solution to the one-dimensional fractional subdiffusion equation on unbounded domains. High order local artificial boundary conditions are constructed on the artificial boundaries, and a fully discrete implicit difference scheme is constructed to solve the reduced problem. Stability and convergence are obtaineded for the finite difference scheme. Then, the corresponding problem in two-dimensions is also discussed. Finally, numerical experiments are given to demonstrate the efficiency, stability, and accuracy of the numerical schemes. [2][3].

12302414.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302414.value: In this project, we carried out stability analysis of local artificial boundary conditions for some time dependent nonlinear partial differential equations. In the first step of the project, we discussed the stability issue for one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation on unbounded domains. By introducing artificial boundaries, we reduced the original problem to an initial-bpoundary value problem on a bound domain. Local boundary conditions are then applied on the artificial boundaries. Finite difference approximation is applied to both the equation in the interior domain and the local boundary conditions. we showed that the finite difference scheme has a unique solution, and the scheme is stable[1]. Then in the second step, the stability issue for two-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation on unbounded domains is discussed. Similarly, we also showed that the numerical scheme is stable. Some numerical tests are performed, which verified the stability and convergence results. Overall, both theoretical and numerical results showed that the proposed numerical schemes are very efficient for the one and two-dimensional heat equations on unbounded domains[1]. In the last step of the project, we discussed some other problems. The finite difference schemes are also applied to one and two-dimensional time-fractional sub-diffusion equations on unbounded domains. Some stability results are obtained, numerical experiments showed that artificial boundary conditions are efficient[2][3].

12302414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302414.value: Finite difference method is a simple and efficient method, especially for time dependent problems. In many engineering and physics applications, problems are governed by nonlinear partial differential equations on unbounded domains. In general, for nonlinear problems, both numerical and theoretical issues are complicated. We expect that the numerical schemes and the analysis tools used in this project can be applied to some other interesting application problems, and come up some new results.

12302414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302414.value: The objective of this project is to perform the stability analysis of local artificial boundary conditons for some nonlinear partial differential equations on unbounded domains. These problems are models of many physical applications. Finite difference method is a simple and efficient method, especially for time dependent problems and problems with structured geometry. The main difficulty for the numerical solution of these problems is the unboundedness of the computational domain. In this project, we first discussed one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation on unbounded domains, and then two-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation on unbounded domains. By introdocing artificial boundaries, we reduced the original problems to new problems on bounded domains, and designed numerical schemes for the new problems. We showed that the numerical schemes for these problems are stable, and gave some numerical experiments to verify the theoretical results. We also discussed one and two-dimensional time-fractional sub-diffusion equation on unbounded domains. Some stability results are obtained, and numerical examples showed that the numerical schemes also work well for these problems.

12302514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302514.value: The Douglas-Rachford splitting method (DRSM) and the Peaceman-Rachford splitting method (PRSM) are two fundamental operator splitting methods. The PRSM is known to be less numerically robust than the DRSM; and thus has received much less attention in the literature. This numerical difference between these two methods is reflected in the fact that the sequence generated by the DRSM is strictly contractive with respect to the solution set, while the PRSM's sequence does not have this property. In this project, we will systematically investigate how to apply contraction techniques to the PRSM for some canonical convex optimization models. A series of PRSM-based strictly contractive algorithms will be proposed. These new algorithms are expected to be very efficient; in particular, they could numerically outperform some of the existing benchmark DRSM-based algorithms in the literature. The numerical study of the PRSM will thus be reactivated, especially in the convex optimization context. For each algorithm to be proposed, we shall establish its global convergence, estimate its worst-case convergence rate measured by the iteration complexity, and examine its efficiency for solving some concrete applications arising in different areas. Douglas-Rachford分裂方法和Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法是兩類基本的算子分裂方法。總所周知，Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法在數值上沒有Douglas-Rachford分裂方法穩定，因此它並沒有像Douglas-Rachford分裂方法那樣受到學者太多的關注。兩者在數值上的差異事實上可以解釋為以下事實：Douglas-Rachford分裂方法產生的迭代點列對解集而言是嚴格收縮的，而Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法產生的迭代點列則沒有這個性質。本研究課題的重點是針對凸優化問題，系統地研究如何將收縮技術與Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法相結合。我們將提出一系列基於Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法的嚴格收縮算法。我們預計這些新算法將非常有效。具體而言，這些新算法可能在數值上比文獻中一些基於Douglas-Rachford分裂方法的方法還要有效。從這個意義上，我們將使得重新研究Peaceman-Rachford分裂方法變為可能，尤其是其針對凸優化問題的研究。對於每一個新算法，我們將證明其收斂性，并估計它的用迭代複雜性來刻畫的收斂速度。同時，我們還將通過一些具體的應用問題來檢驗新算法的有效性。

12302514.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302514.value: The major findings of this project are the framework of developing PRSM-based strictly contractive algorithms and the mathematical theory of analyzing the corresponding convergence. It seems to be the first time in the literature to systematically study the PRSM method from both algorithmic and theoretical perspectives. Research outcome of this project include several papers on the most prestigious journals in the areas of optimization and image processing.

12302514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302514.value: Potentially, the algorithms developed in this project and the analytical framework for establishing the convergence can be used to solve some challenging control problems with PDE constraints and other scientific computing problems. We shall attempt to follow up this trend.

12302514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302514.value: The focus of this project is investigating the so-called PRSM method, which is a classic method widely used in PDE area while its theoretical properties had not been well understood. We discovered some interesting properties that can explain the failure of the convergence of this method, and systematically study how to ensure the convergence if the PRSM method is appropriately adjusted. We proposed the so-called strictly contractive PRSM method and it variants for various convex programming cases, analyzed the convergence of this new series of algorithms, and studied their implementation to image processing problems. Through our study, the understanding of the PRSM method has been enhanced both theoretically and algorithmically, and the application range of this type of methods has been enlarged.

12302714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302714.value: Image segmentation is a central problem in image processing applications, which aims to distinguish objects in an image foreground from the background and to systematically select specific features from an image that has many features. This research proposal involves the development of image segmentation models from variational approaches, with particular efforts on real applications. Previously, there have been many segmentation algorithms designed under different conditions, mostly multiphase segmentation algorithms that are very complex and based on very strict conditions. In this project, the variational approaches will be based on the theory of image segmentation, image restoration, optimization and statistics to handle image segmentation. As in our previous research on image processing, we will concentrate on several aspects --- viz. efficient algorithms considering blurring effects, an extension to non-Gaussian noise, segmentation of the images with intensity inhomogeneity, motion segmentation, and selective segmentation. These are considered to represent the most important issues requiring substantial research for image segmentation problems. Apart from its academic interest, this research proposal will apply to important real-life applications such as medical imaging, biological imaging and Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery. 圖像分割是圖像應用處理中的中心問題, 其目的在於從複雜圖像中分離圖像前景後景中的目標并提取特定特徵. 本研究項目致力於變分法中的圖像分割模型發展与應用. 目前文獻中存在許多不同環境下的圖像分割算法, 大部分多態分割算法步驟繁複條件苛刻. 本項目中的變分法將建基于圖像分割、恢復、優化和統計理論. 和我們之前的圖像處理工作一致，我們將集中研究如下方向: 含模糊的有效算法、 非高斯噪音拓展、 非均勻強度的分割、 運動分割和選擇分割. 這些將作為圖像分割中需要細緻研究的課題. 除了學術價值, 本研究項目將對醫學成像、生物成像和雷達圖像有着重要的實際應用.

12302714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302714.value: 1. A variational image deblurring approach via total variation based structured sparse model selection. Numerical experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves competitive performance. 2. A new algorithm framework for image inpainting in transform domain. The numerical experiments and comparisons on various images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. 3. A low rank prior and total variation regularization method for image deblurring. Numerical experimental results illustratively clearly that the proposed algorithms achieve competitive performance. 4. A phase retrieval method from incomplete magnitude information via total variation regularization. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical finding and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in recovering objects from noisy and incomplete data. 5. A two-stage image segmentation model for multi-channel images. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method is very robust against noise and superior to other image segmentation approaches. 6. A variational multiplicative noise removal by DC programming. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has good performance. 7. A variational phase retrieval with globally convergent preconditioned proximal algorithm. Extensive experiments are conducted to show the effectiveness of the proposed methods. 8. A method for reducing spatially varying out-of-focus blur from natural image. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method performs better than the compared methods. 9. A method of low rank prior and total variation regularization for image deblurring. Numerical experimental results illustratively clearly that the proposed algorithms achieve competitive performance. 10. A multiplicative noise removal method based on unbiased Box-Cox transformation. The proposed method is superior to the existing methods for multiplicative noise removal in the literature. 11. A three-stage approach for segmenting degraded color images: Smoothing, Lifting and Thresholding (SLaT). Experiments demonstrate that our SLaT method gives excellent results in terms of segmentation quality and CPU time in comparison with other state-of-the-art segmentation methods. 12. A method of regularized non-local total variation with application in image restoration. We illustrate the ability of the model to restore relevant unknown edges from the neighboring edges on an image inpainting problem. 13. A weighted variational model for selective image segmentation with application to medical images. Numerical experiments and comparisons for some challenging medical images demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed method. 14. A convex blind image deconvolution method by inverse filtering. Numerical examples for blind image restoration are given to show that the proposed method outperforms some existing methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity (SSIM), visual quality and time consumption.

12303114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303114.value: Organic solar cells (OSCs) are a promising alternative photovoltaic technology to conventional inorganic solar cells due to their cost effectiveness and broad range of application. Despite their flexible design with small molecules, polymer/fullerene and hybrid small molecule/polymer blends, their performance is hampered by limited light absorption due to the mismatch between optical absorption length and charge transport scale, caused by the low charge mobility in organic materials. A key technical development to circumvent this hurdle is a device design to enhance light trapping. Various approaches have been reported including incorporating metal nanoparticles, surface plasmonic structures and a textured substrate template in OSCs to boost light absorption. However, each approach has its own technical limitation for a particular device design. In this application, we propose a unique approach to address this need. This approach is applicable to all OSC designs with broadband and omnidirectional light absorption enhancement. In this project, we propose a new type of transparent poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)/transparent conducting oxide (TCO) (with low/high dielectric constant) double layer two-dimensional photonic structures to achieve broadband and omnidirectional light absorption enhancement in OSCs, thereby improving short-circuit current density and efficiency. The broadband light absorption in nano-structured OSCs is dependent on the photonic structures and also the selection of the photoactive materials. The project includes theoretical simulation and experimental optimization, organic/electrode interfacial analysis and process integration. The primary focus is on realization of >20% light absorption enhancement in OSCs, compared to a state of the art planar control cell, through simultaneous excitation of horizontally propagating surface plasmon polaritons, localized surface plasmons, waveguide modes and their mutual coupling.

12303114.label: Realisation of objectives
12303114.value: Currently, there are intense research activities on organic solar cells (OSCs), for the obvious reason of searching for new and efficient renewable energy sources to reduce our dependence on fossil fuel. The aim of this project is to study broadband and omnidirectional light absorption enhancement in the organic photoactive layer for efficient operation of OSCs. The research work has been focused on three major tasks: (1) realizing broadband and omnidirectional light absorption enhancement in OSCs with photonic structures, (2) analyzing the effect of angular dependency on light absorption in OSCs, and examine photonic structures for absorption enhancement in OSCs, and (3) developing optimal device structure towards attaining efficient and durable OSCs. These tasks have been successfully accomplished by the team. The achievements of the project are highlighted below: (1) Realizing broadband and omnidirectional light absorption enhancement in OSCs with photonic structures A comprehensive study on inverted OSCs with a moth’s eye nanostructured (MEN) active layer has been carried out. Performance of the MEN-based OSCs and the corresponding control planar cells, fabricated with blend of PTB7: PC70BM was analyzed. The efficiency of the MEN-based OSCs was optimized by adjusting the height of MEN pattern in the active layer. Our experimental and theoretical results reveal that the MEN pattern enhances light absorption in the PTB7:PC70BM active layer, especially over the long wavelength region. The effect of oxide interlayer on the performance of OSCs has been carried out by a combination of optical simulation, interfacial exciton dissociation and charge collection analyses. It is found that a blend layer thickness optimized for maximum light absorption in OSCs does not generally give rise to the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE). OSCs can benefit from the oxide interlayer in two ways, (1) to enhance the built-in potential for reducing recombination loss of the photo-generated charge carriers, and (2) to improve charge collection by removal of unfavorable interfacial exciton dissociation. The combined effects result in ~20% improvement in PCE over an optimized control cell, having an identical layer configuration without an optimal oxide interlayer. (2) Analyzing the effect of angular dependency on light absorption in OSCs, and examine photonic structures for absorption enhancement in OSCs The effect of 2-D photonic-structures on omnidirectional and broadband light absorption enhancement in OSCs has been analyzed using a combination of theoretical simulation and experimental optimization. The photonic structures in the active layer, with a blend system of PTB7:PC70BM, were prepared by the nanoimprint method. It shows that the 2-D photonic structures enable not only broadband but also omnidirectional absorption enhancements in the PTB7:PC70BM-based OSCs over a broader angle range of the incident light, leading to >11 % increase in the power conversion efficiency, as compared to an optimal planar control cell. A weak angular dependency on light absorption is a unique feature of the photonic-structured OSCs, which is useful for different applications. (3) Developing optimal device structure towards attaining efficient and durable OSCs The charge carrier recombination/transfer processes at the organic/metal oxide and organic/electrode interfaces were analyzed. A number of techniques were adopted to study these recombination processes. Light intensity dependent measurements suggest that bimolecular recombination is the most prominent factor limiting the performance of OSCs. Transient photo current study indicted the use of an ultrathin oxide interlayer between the organic active layer and the contact helps to reduce the interfacial exciton dissociation, suppress the bimolecular recombination and hence improve the solar cell charge collection efficiency. With the progresses made in achieving the absorption enhancement in OSCs, we extended the work to study the origin of efficient operation of OSCs, e.g., based on different blend systems of PTB7-Th: ITIC, PBDBT:ITIC blend systems. The effects of buildup of space charges, charge extraction and bimolecular recombination processes on the performance and the stability of regular and reverse configuration OSCs were analyzed. It is found that the high performing inverted PTB7-Th:ITIC OSCs benefit from the combined effects of: (1) suppression of bimolecular recombination enabled by an augmented effective internal electric field, and (2) improvement of charge extraction by avoiding the holes passing through acceptor-rich region, which would otherwise occur in a regular configuration cell. The inverted PTB7-Th:ITIC OSCs possess a significant improvement in the cell stability, and a high PCE of 8.0%, which is >29% higher than that of an optimized regular configuration control cell (6.1%). This project has attracted three PhD students to do research in OSCs with partial financial support by this project. We have published 11 high impact journal publications in the field. This project completed successfully.

12303114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303114.value: Omnidirectional and broadband light absorption enhancement in photonic-structured OSCs with a pitch size of 350 nm has been demonstrated experimentally. The results reveal that increase in the short circuit current density of photonic-structured OSCs at the different angles of the incidence of light benefits from the combined effects of light scatting, excitation of surface plasmon polaritons, waveguide modes and their mutual coupling, caused by the photonic structures. A weak angular dependency on light absorption is a unique feature of the photonic-structured OSCs, which is useful for different applications [Part C, publications 1, 3, 5, 8]. The interfacial engineering, exciton dissociation and charge collection in OSCs with different cell configurations were analyzed [Part C, publications 4, 7, 9, 10]. The operational stability of the OSCs has been analyzed systematically. The operational stability of the OSCs has been analyzed systematically. It shows that a continuous vertical phase separation process occurred, forming a polymer-rich top surface and an acceptor-rich bottom surface in PBDB-T:ITIC BHJ during the aging [Part C, publications 2, 6, 11]. The stability of PBDB-T:ITIC-based OSCs has been analyzed systematically using a combination of transient photocurrent measurements, morphology characterization, photoelectron spectroscopy and aging studies. It shows that a continuous vertical phase separation process occurred, forming a polymer-rich top surface and an acceptor-rich bottom surface in PBDB-T:ITIC BHJ during the aging period. A gradual decrease in the built-in potential in the regular configuration OSCs, due to the interfacial reaction between PEDOT:PSS hole transporting layer and ITIC acceptor, is one of the reasons responsible for the performance deterioration. The reduction in built-in, caused by an inevitable reaction at the ITIC/PEDOT:PSS interface in the OSCs can be suppressed by introducing an MoO3 interfacial passivation layer. Retaining a stable and high built-in potential across BHJ through interfacial modification and device engineering, e.g., as seen in the inverted PBDB-T:ITIC OSCs, is a prerequisite for efficient and stable operation of OSCs [Part C, publications 6, 11].

12303114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303114.value: Remarkable progress has been made over the past decade in the development of solution-processable polymer/fullerene OSCs. However, fullerene acceptors have some limitations with respect to cell performance improvement because of poor light absorption, difficult energy level tuning, and challenging issues associated with the instable morphology of the polymer-fullerene BHJ. Compared to fullerene based acceptors with absorption mainly in the UV-visible region, the development of nonfullerene based acceptor molecules with excellent long wavelength sensitivity has drawn increasing attentions. Very recently, a PCE of 17.3% for solution-processed tandem OSCs with a long wavelength sensitive nonfullerene sub-cell unit has been reported, demonstrating the exciting potential of nonfullerene acceptor materials for the fabrication of efficient OSCs. Considerable research into the development of efficient and stable nonfullerene OSCs will be carried out through an improved understanding of the effects of the morphology and vertical stratification of a BHJ on charge transfer, recombination and stability of nonfullerene OSCs. The accomplishment of this project will help us to improve the understanding of the suppression of bimolecular recombination, improvement of charge collection probability, and optimal device design to enhance the performance and operational stability of nonfullerene OSCs.

12303114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303114.value: Remarkable progress has been observed in the development of solution-processable organic solar cells (OSCs) made with different organic semiconductor systems. The effects of photonic structures in the organic photoactive layer on efficient operation of OSCs has been systemically studied during the course of this research project. The photonic structures in the OSCs were created directed in the active layer by imprinting approach without require any additional post-annealing or post deposition treatment. The cell fabrication process developed in our work has the advantage of forming any desired photonic-structure at the organic/metal interface inside the cells without encountering progressive planarization of the nanostructures in the active layer. The effects of a build-up of space charges, charge extraction, and charge carrier recombination processes on the performance and the stability of photonic-structured OSCs has been analysed using space charge-limited current and photo-physics measurement techniques. Retaining a stable and high built-in potential across photoactive region through interfacial modification and device engineering is a prerequisite for efficient and stable operation of OSCs. The accomplishment of the proposed project has a profound impact on the development of highly efficient and stable OSCs that can be prepared by solution fabrication processes.

12303214.value: 回歸的自我調整模型檢驗

12303214.label: Project Objectives
12303214.value: To make test procedure adaptive to dimension reduction structure under the null, we first define two estimates for the number of convex combinations of predictors. The estimates could be consistent under both the null and the saturated alternative. Thus, it can automatically adapt the structures about predictors under the both hypotheses. Once we have this adaption, we can define locally smoothing test statistics by cooperating with the above estimates. It is expected that locally smoothing tests would have the convergence rate of $1/sqrt {nh^{q/2}}$ rather than $1/sqrt {nh^{p/2}}$ that is the classical optimal rate, where $n$ is the sample size, $q$ is the number of convex combinations and $p$ is the number of predictors. When $q$ is small, say equal to $1$ in linear, generalized linear and single-index models, the rate is much faster than the classical optimal rate. We also construct globally smoothing tests in the above way. We expect having tests with the convergence rate $1/sqrt n$. This rate cannot improve the classical ones. However, when $q=1$, the tests could have tractable limiting null distributions and could be still against the saturated alternatives because of the above adaption. For power study, we will prove that the tests are consistent with power $1$ asymptotically. To examine the sensitiveness of the tests to alternatives, we show that the locally smoothing tests would be sensitive to the alternatives converging to the null at the rate $1/sqrt {nh^{q/2}}$, rather than $1/sqrt {nh^{p/2}}$, and the globally smoothing tests to the alternatives distinct from the null at the rate as close to $1/sqrt {n}$ as possible. The above methodology will be applied to classical regression models, and models with censored data, missing data, longitudinal data, and random-effects models.

12303214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303214.value: 回歸分析中的模型檢驗是避免產生誤導性結論的重要步驟。文獻中已有一系列方法。兩類主要方法分別基於參數與非參數擬合的比較，和殘差經驗過程。這些方法定義了局部光滑和整體光滑檢驗。然而，已有的檢驗在零假設和被擇假設都涉及所有預測量，即便假設的模型具有降維結構。我們知道，線性，廣義線性，單指標模型都是典型例子。這個特性使得局部光滑檢驗收斂速度較慢，也只能探測偏離零假設速度較慢的被擇模型。 而儘管整體光滑可以有參數速度，其極限零分佈一般無法得到，因而需要重抽樣技術協助得到臨界值。為使得這些檢驗有更好的功效，我們提出一個自我調整方法，並且應用到不同的回歸問題中。通過數值分析，我們檢驗方法的有效性。這個研究旨在推動新的方法論，從而對模型檢驗有更深的理解。以期研究的影響超出古典方法的範疇。

12303214.label: Realisation of objectives
12303214.value: The objectives have been achieved. We have proposed a generic methodology to achieve the model adaptation in model checking for regressions. As this method can fully use dimension reduction structure and thus the curse of dimensionality can be greatly alleviated. The numerical studies and real data analysis have also demonstrated this. As the by-products, we have also obtained some other relevant results.

rows: To make test procedure adaptive to dimension reduction structure under the null, we first define two estimates for the number of convex combinations of predictors. The estimates could be consistent under both the null and the saturated alternative. Thus, it can automatically adapt the structures about predictors under the both hypotheses.

Once we have this adaption, we can define locally smoothing test statistics by cooperating with the above estimates. It is expected that locally smoothing tests would have the convergence rate of $1/sqrt {nh^{q/2}}$ rather than $1/sqrt {nh^{p/2}}$ that is the classical optimal rate, where $n$ is the sample size, $q$ is the number of convex combinations and $p$ is the number of predictors. When $q$ is small, say equal to $1$ in linear, generalized linear and single-index models, the rate is much faster than the classical optimal rate.

We also construct globally smoothing tests in the above way. We expect having tests with the convergence rate $1/sqrt n$. This rate cannot improve the classical ones. However, when $q=1$, the tests could have tractable limiting null distributions and could be still against the saturated alternatives because of the above adaption.

For power study, we will prove that the tests are consistent with power $1$ asymptotically. To examine the sensitiveness of the tests to alternatives, we show that the locally smoothing tests would be sensitive to the alternatives converging to the null at the rate $1/sqrt {nh^{q/2}}$, rather than $1/sqrt {nh^{p/2}}$, and the globally smoothing tests to the alternatives distinct from the null at the rate as close to $1/sqrt {n}$ as possible.
The above methodology will be applied to classical regression models, and models with censored data, missing data, longitudinal data, and random-effects models.

12303214.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303214.value: For the objectives we set in the proposal, we have fully achieved. The main findings are the following. First, we proposed a new concept in hypothesis testing for regressions: model adaptation of a test. This is pretty new as a referee said in his/her report: it is a substantial contribution. This is because the constructed tests can adapt to the underlying model so that it can maintain the significance level and enhance the test power. Particularly, when the null model has a dimension reduction structure, the test can fully use this piece of information and behaves like a test as if the covariate is one-dimensional although its original dimension is high. This generic methodology can be readily applied to many other model checking problems. The first result has been published in JRSS B.

12303214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303214.value: As this is a very generic methodology, and thus can be applied to many other regression problems when we consider hypothesis testing. We are working on this. More importantly, we are trying to advocate its concept, rather than only publishing papers.

12303214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303214.value: In this proposal, we propose a new concept in hypothesis testing for regressions: model adaptation. This methodology can make a test automatically adapt the underlying model such that it can maintain the significance level and greatly enhance the test power. Also when the null model is of a dimension reduction structure, the test behaves like a test with only one covariate even when there are many covariates.

12304114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12304114.value: 許多理學和工程學的問題需要通過求解偏微分方程來解決。無網格方法，包括徑向基函數(RBF)配置法或Kansa方法，是目前研究偏微分方程數值計算方面的一個重要領域，其研究重點大部分在對橢圓和拋物線型偏微分方程的研究上面。無網格方法的一個很大的優勢就在於，它不需要構建及操作網格。因此，即使無網格方法只有較短的發展歷史，它已經擁有了很多精準計算的應用實例。但同時，由于理論上的局限性，很多研究人員在Kansa方法的正確性方面都抱有懷疑態度。 有著更完整的理論支持，並能通過對（廣義）RBF插值使用一般誤差估計來得到求解偏微分方程的新的數值方法的RBF插值問題，為Kansa方法提供一些理論依據。這裡對RBF插值的一般誤差估計（類似於多項式插值）具體是指，RBF插值與方程間的($L^infty$)距離，是由再生核希爾伯特空間 (RKHS)和與方程無關的常數之間的乘積來界定的。而這個常數，通常被認作為冪函數，是可以進一步通過界定數據的分佈距離來完成誤差分析的。 在以下這個項目中，我們通過利用同時依賴於RKHS和數據分佈的冪函數來設計新的算法。一旦內核及RKHS被固定，函數或偏微分方程的解及其準則也會被指定。此外，通過利用重現標準索伯列夫(Sobolev)空間的Matern內核，我們也能夠在熟悉的索伯列夫空間上估算誤差（最多能夠估算解的範數的一個），而不是一些抽象的RKHS。基於從相應的冪函數中得到的信息，我們得以設計算法來最小化有著各種限制的冪函數（在某些索伯列夫範數下），以保證數值計算的效率；因此，我們的將這個項目命名為，最佳誤差算法。

12304114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304114.value: In our Annual Progress Report, we reported that a fast adaptive trial space selection algorithm [L, SISC 2016] was proposed. By exploiting the meshless property of kernel-based collocation methods, we further propose a fully automatic numerical recipe for solving interpolation/regression and boundary value problems adaptively [L & Chiu, IJNME 2018]. The proposed algorithm is built upon a least-squares collocation formulation on some quasi-random point sets with low discrepancy. To circumvent the potential problem of ill-conditioning due to extremely small separation distance in the point sets, we add an extra dimension to the data points for generating shape parameters such that nearby kernels are of distinctive shape. This effectively eliminates the needs of shape parameter identification. Resulting linear systems were then solved by the algorithm in [L, SISC 2016] to improve the robustness of the algorithm. To further eliminate the influence of user’s defined parameters, we propose a doubly stochastic radial basis function (DSRBF) method for function recoveries in [Yang, Yan & L, JCP 2018]. Instead of a constant, we treat the RBF shape parameters as stochastic variables whose distribution were determined by a stochastic leave-one-out cross validation estimation. A careful operation count is provided in order to determine the ranges of all the parameters in our methods. The overhead cost for setting up the proposed DSRBF method is O(n^2) for function recovery problems with n basis. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed method not only outperforms constant shape parameter formulation in terms of accuracy with comparable computational cost, but also the optimal LOOCV formulation in terms of both accuracy and computational cost. In [L&Ye, AA2018], we combine techniques in meshfree methods and Gaussian process regressions to construct kernel-based estimators for numerical derivatives from noisy data. Specially, we construct meshfree estimators from normal random variables, which are defined by kernel-based probability measures induced from symmetric positive definite kernels, to reconstruct the unknown partial derivatives from scattered noisy data. Our developed theories give rise to Tikhonov regularization methods with a priori parameter, but the shape parameters of the kernels remain tunable. For that, we propose an error measure that is computable without the exact values of the derivative. This allows users to obtain a quasi-optimal kernel-based estimator by comparing the approximation quality of kernel-based estimators. Numerical examples in two-dimensions and three-dimensions are included to demonstrate the convergence behavior and effectiveness of the proposed numerical differentiation scheme.

12304114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304114.value: After proving some rigorous convergence theories [Cheung, L & Schaback, SINUM 2018] and developing various stable meshfree algorithms, we have more theoretical and numerical tools in our machinery to target more challenging partial differential equations (PDEs) on surfaces, which appear in many applications throughout the natural and applied sciences. Image processing applications include the placement of an image on a surface, the restoration of a damaged pattern on a surface and the segmentation and the denoising of images on surfaces. In biology, applications include the formation of patterns on animal coats and the wound healing process. In computer graphics, applications are found on the topic of real time fluid visualization on surfaces. Some preliminary meshfree algorithms were carried out in [Cheung, L & Ruuth, JCP 2015] and our formal convergence proof were recently published in [Cheung & L, SISC 2018]. Both articles concern PDEs on static surfaces. Our future research will focus on evolving surfaces and domain-boundary coupled PDE systems.

12304114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304114.value: This project developed some novel algorithm for the unsymmetric radial basis function (RBF) collocation method, which is also known as the Kansa method in the community. This numerical approach requires no re-formulation of the PDE and no triangularization. As long as one knows how to program for an interpolation problem, it only takes minutes to understand and code up something for the Kansa method. Since invented, the Kansa method has been widely used in vast numbers of applications in physics and engineering. As Kansa methods gain popularity, this work also provides ways to stably solve the resulting severely ill-conditioned linear systems, tweaks to improve robustness of the methods, and algorithms to perform numerical differentiation.

12400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12400014.value: 認知語言學的隱喻研究以分析隱喻當中的概念模式為主。隱喻的概念模式是由來源域（由具體概念組成）和目標域（由抽象概念組成）這兩個概念領域組成，並以來源域來理解目標域。而這些研究大多假設隱喻在不同語言的表達方式都是一樣的，卻沒有提供充足的例子作證。所以，我希望借用語料庫的研究來檢查隱喻在不同語言的表達方式，從而測試來源域──目標域在不同語言的配對關聯，以完善概念隱喻理論。 香港有豐富的語言現象，同時使用兩文三語，是本研究最好的對象。在一九九七年前，由於香港是英國的殖民地，從英國來港的總督都以英文和香港市民溝通，所以當時流行於香港的政治語言大多以英文為主，附以中文的翻譯。而在一九九七年後，由於香港已經回歸中國，香港特別行政區行政長官大多以中文作為溝通的主要媒介。所以，香港的政治用語自九七後起了相當的變化，從英文為主，中文為輔；變成中文為主，英文為輔。本研究收集香港的政治用語（以施政報告為主）作研究，並從中指出隱喻的表達方法在中、英文的相同與不同之處。本研究所發現的隱喻，將會進一步整理，以作比較。 研究預期結果將包括不同時代漢英隱喻的分析。為強化本研究結果，本研究更進一步比較概念隱喻在不同地方的中文政治用語上的使用方法。透過分析香港行政長官的施政報告、中國總理的工作報告，以及台灣總統的元旦和國慶文告，本研究探討概念隱喻在過去的三十年中、在兩岸三地的不同表達方式。除了不同之處，本研究也強調隱喻在這三個地方的一致性，特別是這兩岸三地的政治語言使用者都有着差不多的文化背景、思考模式及信仰。他們都使用同一語言（中文）來表達概念隱喻。這樣的分析，可加深了解概念隱喻的普遍性，足以彌補現有理論的不足。 總的來說，透過收集這些政治用語和以上的分析，本研究可以深入分析香港政治用語與概念隱喻使用在不同時代的轉變，並試圖解釋這些詞彙選擇上的微妙轉變如何提供描素人類概念系統所需的證據。

12400014.label: Realisation of objectives
12400014.value: The overall goals of this project were achieved through the publication of 4 journal articles (1 accepted and 3 submitted), 4 book chapters and 10 conference papers. This project has four main objectives as listed in Section 5.1. 1. The first objective has been completed through the publication of 1 journal paper (submitted), 2 book chapters, and 5 conference papers. In addition, an online corpus was built with additional funding and is reported under Part C (Research Output). The English data of Hong Kong Policy Address has been thoroughly analyzed, with special attention on the source domains of JOURNEY, BUILDING, WAR, BOOK, OCEAN and PLANT (e.g., Ahrens, 2016a; Ahrens, 2016b; Ahrens, 2016c; Ahrens, 2016d; Ahrens, 2016e). The information of the five presentations given at different international conferences can be found in Part C. Two book chapters have been accepted. One chapter (Ahrens and Zeng, Accepted) examines the conceptualization of democracy in Hong Kong context (Ahrens and Zeng, Accepted), while the other one (Ahrens, Jiang and Zeng, Accepted) explores how BUILDING metaphors are used in Hong Kong Policy Addresses over a thirty-year period. The submitted journal article (Zeng, Tay and Ahrens, Submitted) looks at the gendered influence in Hong Kong political speeches. Note also that our data analysis extended beyond the year 2012 to include up to 2014. 2. We have achieved our second objective through the publication of 2 conference papers and the submission of 1 journal article. Analyses for the source domain of JOURNEY and BUILDING have been completed for the HK Policy Addresses written in Chinese (e.g., Ahrens and Chan, 2016; Ahrens and Jiang, Submitted). The journal article (Ahrens and Jiang, Submitted) aims at making proposals regarding the morphological issues in Source Domain Determination (Ahrens and Jiang, Submitted). In particular, we propose a method to identify which source domain a conceptual metaphor belongs to with the assistance of SUMO (Suggested Upper Merged Ontology), WordNet, collocational patterns and an online Chinese dictionary. Two conference presentations have been given to examine the translation changes in conceptual metaphors in Hong Kong political discourse (Ahrens and Chan, 2016), and to study how the conceptualization of HOUSING changes in Hong Kong Chief Executives’ Political Addresses (Chan and Ahrens, 2018). 3. Our third objective has been achieved as seen by the submission of 1 journal article and presentation of 3 conference papers. The comparison of metaphor use in political discourse in different regions has been conducted, with special regard to the target domain of EDUCATION (Ahrens and Zeng, 2017) and DEMOCRACY (Ahrens, 2017). Three conference presentations have been given related to this (Ahrens and Zeng, 2017a; Ahrens and Zeng, 2017b; Ahrens, 2017). In addition, one journal paper has been submitted aiming at investigating the differences of metaphors used in Chinese political rhetoric regarding “education” over the past thirty years, showing a comparison between Hong Kong and Mainland China (Ahrens and Zeng, Submitted). Moreover, a bottom-up analysis has also been conducted for both English and Chinese data, across different language regions. The first and the last speech for each speaker in different regions have been selected for annotation, making it possible for us to compare among different regions, speakers and time. The bottom-up analysis is mainly conducted at two levels. For the first level, metaphor usages have been identified by aligning with Group’s (2007) metaphor identification procedures. A variety of language resources (e.g., Chinese Wordnet, Chinese SUMO, and Handian – an on-line Contemporary Chinese Dictionary) have been utilized to help with the metaphor identification (to check if there is a contrast between the contextual meaning and the more basic meaning). Two annotators were involved and inter-rater reliability tests have shown that there is an almost perfect agreement between different annotators, which indicate the reliability and validity of our annotation schema. All the annotated texts have been published on Open Science Framework (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/75Q3V). 4. The fourth objective has been fulfilled by the publication of 1 journal paper and 2 book chapters. One of the book chapters (Ahrens and Chang (Accepted)) looks at the role of lexical frequency and collocation with respect to metaphor modeling based on an additional corpus of speeches given by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) government with three different audiences: people in Taiwan, the Taiwan government, and people in the PRC. The second book chapter, (Ahrens, 2019) examines to what extent politicians invoke a particular source domain in order to advance their political ideology by analyzing the WAR metaphors used by Hillary Clinton in her various political roles. A US corpus was also created in order to do a time series analysis, as a much longer timespan was needed to postulate an answer regarding changes seen over time. One journal article has been accepted by Applied Linguistics (A* SSCI journal) (Burgers and Ahrens (Accepted)) as a result of this extended inquiry.
