12400014.label: Major findings and research outcome
12400014.value: The analysis of conceptual metaphors of Hong Kong in Chinese and English has allowed for greater understanding of the rhetorical patterns of persuasion in Hong Kong political speeches over time, as well as provided insight into how lexical choice underlies and reflects subtleties in the human conceptual system. The various pairwise comparisons among speeches in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong has also advanced our understanding of variations within Chinese. In addition, a corpus-based statistical approach has been used to study the cross-linguistic variation in metaphor conceptualization. Our project has demonstrated that by building political corpora and the judicious use of computational/statistical analytical tools, it is now possible to identify the variations among speakers, regions and time, and to better describe the nature and motivation of these variations. In addition, an on-line corpus has been built, including sub-corpus of U.S. Presidential Speeches (1789-2015); sub-corpus of Hong Kong Policy Address in English (1984-2014); sub-corpus of Hong Kong Policy Address in Chinese (1985-2014); sub-corpus of PRC Premier Speeches in Chinese (1984-2013); sub-corpus of Taiwan Presidential Speeches in Chinese (1978-2014). This is an important resource for all those interested in the study of political rhetoric. In addition, students, teachers, researchers, and linguists may use this Corpus to conduct research on a range of linguistic issues, including research on morphology, semantics, syntax, pragmatics and discourse. The Corpus is available online at https://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/corpus/. Both English and Chinese data have been fully annotated with metaphor identification. Bottom-up analysis has been conducted for both English and Chinese political speeches, across different regions (i.e. Hong Kong, PRC, and Taiwan). The annotated data has been published on the Open Science Framework and will be helpful to researchers who are interested in the study of political rhetoric. In addition, the fully annotated data may also be used in the field of computational linguistics (i.e. to provide high quality training data for machine learning algorithms, e.g., automatic identification of metaphor).

12400014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12400014.value: By introducing the study of metaphors to research on political discourse in Hong Kong, our study has the potential to lead to more interdisciplinary investigations involving linguistics and other social sciences. In particular, we have developed a corpus-based statistical approach to study the cross-linguistic variation in metaphor conceptualization. In the future, with the availability of parsed political corpora and the assistance of computational/statistical analytical tools, it will be possible to effectively identify the variations among multiple language varieties so as to better describe the nature and motivation of language variations. In addition, by determining how variations are parameterized over speaker, language, region and time, our foray into examining which metaphors are used at which times may be extended to additional corpora to come to a deeper understanding of the degree of universality that languages share across and within conventionalized conceptual metaphors. In sum, our project has developed a framework that will be of value to both a synchronic and diachronic analysis of the rapidly shifting cultural and political landscapes throughout the region.

12400014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12400014.value: How people use language to get across their emotions and their point of view about the world is a long-standing issue in the field of linguistics. Conceptual metaphors (which are conventionalized expressions that use concrete concepts to describe more abstract concepts as in the case of TIME being understood in terms of MONEY, i.e., in “She spent a lot of time on the report”) are one way people get across their emotions or point of view about an issue. This project has demonstrated the political leaders in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and the US vary in their conceptual metaphor use. Sometimes this variation is seen as a result of the different political roles a speaker has taken over the course of their career; sometimes it is a result of groups of speakers having a different ideological background; other times it is a result of political leaders speaking to a different audience. In addition, it is important to recognize that these variations are not absolute; the variation is one of degree, not one of kind. In short, while metaphors are ubiquitous, a group of speakers may draw upon a particular metaphor more often than a different group of speakers and it is useful to examine these frequency preferences for insight into the worldview of a speaker or group of speakers.

12400314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12400314.value: A development of the PI’s previous GRF, this new research project aims at assessing the rise but also the limits of China’s influence in Sub-Saharan Africa in putting Sino-African relations in a global context. This research will be based on data collected in Hong Kong and mainland China as well as fieldwork conducted in Africa. It will adopt both a quantitative and a qualitative approach. Fieldwork will be conducted in a sample of eight countries selected because of their different size, historical background, spoken language, economic structure and resources and political orientations (South Africa, Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan, Mozambique, Rwanda, Uganda, Burkina Faso and Chad). Firstly, this research will attempt to measure China’s weight in the selected African countries’ economy, political system, society and external relations in a comparative manner. It will evaluate the “relation intensity” that has been reached between China and these African countries. Then it will compare this with the “relation intensity” between these nations and their other major partners, inside and outside of Africa. Secondly, this research will concentrate on evaluating China’s influence on African countries’ foreign policy. Here the working hypothesis is that while African countries can no longer ignore China’s diplomatic concerns, especially its so-called “core interests”, they can balance China’s growing influence in cultivating closer relations with their traditional partners, especially the ones providing security guarantees, or their new emerging partners. As a result, African countries’ foreign policy may not have fundamentally changed because of China’s growing economic, diplomatic or cultural presence on the continent. Thirdly, this research will explore the major limitations of China’s influence in Africa as well as identify the main reasons of these limits. It will in particular attempt to assess whether China’s difficulties are the result of African governments or elites’ own policy adjustments or the outcome of other big powers’ reactions and counteroffers. It will also try to evaluate African elites’ attitude vis-à-vis China’s authoritarian and state-centred economic success story as well as interest in Chinese culture and civilisation, or more generally the impact of China’s soft power on this continent, in comparison with other big powers’ respective soft power. Finally, it will check if the nature of the political system matters or if it remains a marginal factor in African countries’ relations with China. This new project is aimed at writing a single-author book on the rise and the limits of China’s influence in Africa.

12400314.label: Realisation of objectives
12400314.value: Objectives 2 and 3 have been fully realised. Objective 1 has been realised not in the form of a single-authored book but in a series of single-authored articles published in top-tier academic journals as well as policy-oriented journals. The reason for this change of format has been the large diversity of cases that I have researched on as well as the impact journal articles enjoy as opposed to books. Actually, out of these three objectives, the most important is the third one: better comprehend the rise and limits of China's influence in Africa in a global context. I think that I have fully met this target. Through the field work that I have completed in fourteen African countries as well as the research output that I have produced, I have been able to better comprehend and present to a large audience the rise and the limits of China's influence in Africa. On the rise side, I can mention first of all China's quasi-complete marginalisation of Taiwan in Africa. Today only one African country, Eswatini (ex-Swaziland), still holds diplomatic relations with Taiwan. In 2016, when I did some fieldwork in Burkina Faso, this nation still entertained official links with Taiwan: I then wrote an article on the content of Taiwan's cooperation with and public diplomacy in Burkina Faso but also on the fragility of this diplomatic relationship. China's increasing involvement in United Nations peacekeeping operations, particularly in sub-Sahara Africa, has also contributed to enhancing this country's influence in the black continent. The People's Liberation Army (PLA)'s participation in the MINUSMA, the UN peacekeeping mission in Mali where I conducted some fieldwork in 2016, is a good illustration, as well, of this growing involvement. Out of this fieldwork, I published two outputs: one scholarly article in the China Quarterly and a more policy-oriented piece as a Special Report for the United States Institute of Peace. The following year, I conducted some fieldwork in Niger and Chad, two countries where China has been increasingly involved, particularly in the oil sector. Similarities between China's growing engagement in Niger and Chad are striking. Since there have already been publications on China-Chad relations, I decided to concentrate on Niger: out of this research work, has come out a long article published in the prestigious Journal of Contemporary China in late 2018. The Niger case underscores how China, in investing in not necessarily profitable industries, as the oil and refinery industry, has managed to gain influence to the detriment of France, in this former French colony. In 2018, I did some fieldwork in Djibouti, one year after the PLA's military based had been opened. Out of this fieldwork and data assembled in Hong Kong, I was able to write a long scholarly article that has already been accepted for publication by the Journal of Contemporary China: it should be available on line at the end of 2019. I earlier published a shorter policy-oriented article on the issue in the Journal of Politik Risk, a US based specialised publication. This new and unprecedented development of China's presence in Africa underlines China's increasing interest in Africa's security as well as the security of its nationals and companies active on this continent. More generally, China's presence in Africa has been increasingly part of and influenced by Xi Jinping's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) launched in 2013. I have illustrated this point in my Niger-China article as well as, as far as BRI security is concerned, in my piece on the PLA base in Djibouti. But I have also analysed China's ambitions in a more recent article specifically on the BRI published in French in the prestigious Jesuits-managed journal Etudes in late 2019. These ambitions have enhanced Beijing's new hegemonic position in Africa and have long-term implications for China-Africa relations. On the downside, there are clear limits to China's influence in Africa. Firstly, in spite of its new military base in Djibouti, China does not contribute much to Africa's security. Its peacekeepers just represent 3% of the MINUSMA. Likewise, in spite of a growing bilateral military cooperation between China and Niger, Beijing has remained reluctant to get involved in Niger security: while it has accepted to symbolically contribute to G5 Sahel, the regional organisation aimed at fighting agains the terrorist threat in the Sahel and improving the security of the region's five countries, including Niger, China has left security matters and responsibilities to France and the US. Secondly, China's ambition to develop trilateral cooperation with developed countries in Africa has bumped into multiple difficulties. In a paper that I presented at a conference in Lagos, Nigeria, in 2016, I demonstrated that China's triangular cooperation with France in Africa has never really taken off ground because both countries are more prone to compete that cooperate. The paper is available on Thierry Pairault's webpage on China-Africa (https://www.pairault.fr/sinaf/) at the following link: https://www.pairault.fr/sinaf/index.php/les-afriques-et-la-chine/liste-des-categories/15-references/801-cooperations-tripartites-france-chine-afrique. Thirdly, Xi Jinping's BRI and China's new hegemonic ambitions in Africa have triggered some negative reactions that I had already analysed in a previous GRF in an article (co-authored with economist Jean-Raphaël Chaponnière) on China-Tanzania relations which was published as a book by Lambert in 2017. As a result, several African countries, including not only Tanzania but also Mozambique and, more recently, Angola, Ethiopia and Sudan, have tried to hedge against China in developing or trying to develop relations with other partners, including Japan, Brazil or the US. Fourthly, on the basis of the fieldwork that I have conducted in fourteen countries (Mozambique, Malawi, Burkina Faso, Mali, Congo Brazzaville, Democratic Republic of Congo, Niger, Chad, Sudan, Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda, Djibouti and South Africa), I have accumulated a rich data base that also contributes to demonstrating both the growing influence of China in Africa as well as the limits of this influence, all African countries visited trying to balance China's role in keeping close relations with other partners (as the US, the UK, Japan or France) and reaching out new partners (as India, Brazil, Turkey or Morocco). I have as a result fully reached the second objective listed below. However, the difficulty in front such a diverse African reality is to produce a single-authored book that can embrace fully the complex reality of China-Africa relations. Actually, in the last few years, it has become harder to write overviews on this topic as research has specialised so much in different directions. As a result, I have preferred to write single-authored articles on specific issues or case studies: while very focused, each of these articles or research output fully illustrates both the rising influence of China in Africa as well as the limits of this influence. I have therefore estimated that I have completely reached the first objective of this GRF project.

12400314.label: Major findings and research outcome
12400314.value: China's influence in Africa has clearly been rising since Beijing launched its "going out" policy in the late 1990s. This influence has intensified after President Xi Jinping launched the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2013. Since then, China has become most African countries' major trade and economic partner. It has been their top infrastructures and loans providers. It has finished marginalising Taiwan, normalising for example with Burkina Faso in 2017. It has deepened its role in UN peacekeeping operations, particularly in Mali and South Sudan. And it has intensified its cooperation with many countries, including poor nations, as Niger, where its investments for instance in the oil industry, are not necessarily productive. In other words, China has acquired a new hegemonic position in Africa which allows it to better protect its economic, diplomatic and security interests there. No African country now dares criticising China for its human rights records, or its policy in Xinjiang or vis-à-vis Taiwan. And equipped with a new military base in Djibouti, China can now pretend to better protect its nationals or companies active in Africa. Nonetheless, China's growing influence in Africa has met a number of limits. In spite of its new military base in Djibouti, China does not contribute much to Africa's security. Its peacekeepers just represent 3% of the MINUSMA in Mali. Likewise, in spite of a growing bilateral military cooperation between China and Niger, Beijing has remained reluctant to get involved in Niger security: while it has accepted to symbolically contribute to G5 Sahel, the regional organisation aimed at fighting against the terrorist threat in the Sahel and improving the security of the region's five countries, including Niger, China has left security matters to France and the US. China's ambition to develop trilateral cooperation with developed countries in Africa has bumped into multiple difficulties. For example, its triangular cooperation with France in Africa has never really taken off ground because both countries see themselves as competitors. Finally, Xi Jinping's BRI and new hegemonic ambitions in Africa have triggered some negative reactions. As a result, a growing number of African countries, including not only Tanzania but also Mozambique and more recently Angola, Sudan and Ethiopia, are trying to balance China's new hegemonic role on their continent in keeping close relations with other partners (as the US, the UK, Japan or France) and reaching out new partners (as India, Brazil, Turkey or Morocco).

12400314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12400314.value: This research project has allowed me to start diving into China-Africa security relations, the subject of the GRF that I obtained in 2018 and started to research on in January 2019. On the basis of this already-completed GRF on the rise and limits of China's influence in Africa, I can now look at and research on more specific cases of security cooperation between China and Africa, including the PLA's participation in the UN peacekeeping mission in South Sudan, a deeper and updated analysis of Djibouti PLA base in the security of the BRI and more broadly China's African policy, China's security assistance to the African Union aimed at empowering this regional organisation and better equip it to manage Africa's security challenges, as well as other aspects of China's security relation with Africa, including bilateral military cooperation and soft security, e.g. health security cooperation.

12400314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12400314.value: Based on fieldwork conducted in fourteen African countries over a period of four years, this research has demonstrated through several significant case studies (Burkina Faso, UN peacekeeping force in Mali, Niger, China-France cooperation in Africa, Djibouti military base) that China's influence in Africa has clearly been rising, particularly after President Xi Jinping launched the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2013, but at the same time that this influence is also facing clear limits. Today, China is many African countries' major trade and economic partner. It is also their top infrastructures and loans providers. It has quasi completely marginalised Taiwan. It has deepened its role in UN peacekeeping operations. In other words, China has acquired a new hegemonic position in Africa which allows it to better protect its economic, diplomatic and security interests there. Nonetheless, China's increasing influence in Africa has met a number of limits. Xi Jinping's new international ambitions have triggered some negative reactions, convincing a growing number of African countries to balance China's role in keeping or developing closer relations with other partners. Moreover, Beijing has remained reluctant to get involved in Africa' security in spite of its recent pledge to provide more assistance on that front.

12400914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12400914.value: Cross-border integration between mainland China and Hong Kong has moved beyond mutual economic benefits to socio-cultural, environmental and political arena. While much attention is still devoted to the impact of economic integration on migration and tourism, there is increasing public concern about its impact on the environment, land and communities on both sides of the border. On the heated debate about Hong Kong-mainland integration, we would like to explore a critical phenomenon that is completely ignored by scholars, journalists and the public, i.e. the stories of Hong Kong farmers moving across border, to the north, to open huge farms in mainland China, and then sell the fresh produce back to Hong Kong people. This phenomenon has been going on for 30 years, and yet, almost no research and policy studies has been done on these trans-border farming communities, who has contributed hugely to the supply of fresh produce to Hong Kong. How does this trans-border production network – created by Hong Kong farmers moving north – operate? How does this cross-border production impact both mainland and Hong Kong societies, in terms of socio-economic impact (i.e. creating jobs), land justice (how the land was obtained), and environmental impact? These research questions will be answered through the ethnographical fieldwork approach. Detailed interviews of key players in this cross-border production network will be carried out in three years. As for long-term impact and policy implication, this research will answer the questions: “Do we still need agricultural land in Hong Kong?”; “Should we turn all the abandoned agricultural land to development purposes?”; “Do we need food security and agricultural policy?”; and “Do we need technical, logistics and marketing support for our farmers?” Today, we are facing increasing concern for food safety and health, the popularity of organic produce and local farmers’ markets, the desire to decrease carbon footprint of our food consumption, and the revival of local farming practices (some are actually Hong Kong farmers returning from the mainland). We believe that the findings of this research will help us re-evaluate our existing development-oriented land use, and refocus on food security, genuine environmental protection and the revival of the farming industry as an alternative economy. 中國大陸和香港之間的跨界融合不限於經濟互惠而己，還包括社會，文化，環境和政治的面向。雖然經濟融合對移民及旅遊的衝擊得到最多注意，民眾也越來越來越關心融合對邊境兩側的環境，土地和社區的衝擊。 在香港與內地融合的激烈爭論脈絡中，我們想探討完全被學者、記者和公眾忽略了一個重要的現象，即香港農民跨邊界北移，在中國大陸開設大型農場，再把新鮮蔬菜賣回給香港人。這種現象已經持續了30年，然而，幾乎沒有針對這些提供大量新鮮蔬的跨境農業社群的學術及政策研究。 由香港農民北移創造的跨境生產網絡是如何運作？這個跨境生產如何影響大陸和香港兩地的社會，包括社會經濟(如創造就業機會）、土地正義（土地是如何獲得的），以及對環境衝擊？ 這些研究問題將通過民族志田野調查的方式來回答。我們計劃用三年時間，深入訪問跨境生產網絡的重要成員。 至於長期的影響和政策含義，本研究將回答以下問題：「香港還需要農地嗎？」; 「我們是否應該把所有的荒廢農地都拿來開發呢？」; 「我們是否需要糧食安全和農業政策嗎？」; 以及「我們需要為香港農民提供技術，物流和營銷支持嗎？」今天，我們正面臨著食品安全和健康、有機農產品和本地農墟普及、降地食物低碳足的期望，以及恢復本地農業生產方式（有些其實是香港農民從內地回港復耕）。我們認為本研究結果將有助於我們重新評估我們現有的以發展為導向的土地利用，並重新關注糧食安全，真正的環境保護，以及復耕作為替代經濟的可能性。

12401014.label: Realisation of objectives
12401014.value: This project aims to generate empirical findings that are useful for assessing the policy proposals of the HKSAR Government on the future fuel mix for electricity generation. The HKSAR Government proposed an aggressive target of a 50-60% reduction in carbon intensity, implying an absolute reduction of 19-33% in total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. A major task of the project is to estimate the willingness-to-pay (WTP) of Hong Kong residents by the contingent valuation method (CVM). It entails collecting consumer preference data via a telephone survey and analyzing the survey responses via a regression analysis. The project bears important policy implications because: o If the WTP estimate is large, a high target could be set without strong public objection. o If the WTP estimate is small, public support for the high target may require financial mitigation of the ensuing bill increase, possibly with taxpayer money or utility shareholders’ earnings. Alternatively, the high target policy may have to be revised to win public support. o The Fukushima disaster and its aftermath suggest that the WTP estimate for nuclear power could be substantially less than the WTP estimate for natural-gas-fired generation. As a result, a publicly acceptable fuel mix would contain less nuclear power. Knowing the WTP for nuclear power will enable us to formulate a fuel mix that can better match what Hong Kong residents want and support. However, the Government changed its energy strategy twice during the period of study of this project. As a response, the research delayed twice the implementation of the study plan to cope with the new developments. Specifically, when the proposal was prepared in 2013, the original plan of the study was to gauge the “willingness-to-pay” (WTP) of Hong Kong residents for various fuel mix proposals as laid out in HKSAR Government’s consultation paper published in 2010. Through econometric analysis of survey results, the project was designed to find out the consumers’ preference in paying higher price to enjoy better environment if more electricity is generated by natural gas and nuclear. In that proposal, nuclear power would account for as much as 50% of the total electricity consumption in Hong Kong in the future. However, the earthquake in northeastern Japan in 2011 has led to strong social resistance to the use of nuclear power around the world. The HKSAR Government therefore launched another consultation in March 2014, proposing new options for future’s fuel import strategy. One of the most debated issue is whether Hong Kong should import a vast amount of electricity by connecting to the grid of Mainland China (“grip import”) regardless of its fuel mix. In March 2015, the Government launched yet another public consultation on the future development of the electricity market. Importantly, the consultation document ruled out the option of “grip import”. It was proposed that coal-fired electricity generation would be replaced by a modest increase in nuclear import, a big increase in natural gas generation and an unspecified amount of renewable energy. The consultation ended in 30 June 2015, but the consultation report had not been released up to early 2016. In order to maintain the policy relevance of the project, the team delayed the implementation of the survey twice. The team finally conducted the survey in April 2016, taking into account the latest policy proposal. Data of 1460 residential households were collected, yielding dichotomous choice (DC) data based on the respondents’ answers to a set of closed-ended questions and direct elicitation (DE) date through open-ended questions. Econometric analysis was then conducted.

12401014.label: Major findings and research outcome
12401014.value: The major findings can be summarized as follows: o To achieve the target of reducing CO2 by 30% of the 2005 level in the year 2020 through a combination of natural gas and renewable generation, Hong Kong households’ WTP estimate is 48% - 51% (increase over the current bills). o If the same target is to be achieved with additional nuclear importation from China, the WTP estimate declines to 32% - 42% (increase over the current bills). o As the projected bill increase resulting from the target implementation is 40%, our WTP estimates support the government’s fuel mix policy of using natural gas generation and renewable energy to displace Hong Kong’s coal generation.

12401014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12401014.value: This project applies the contingent valuation method (CVM) to evaluate Hong Kong’s energy policy. The method is a useful tool to inform policy debates by soliciting objectively the preferences of citizens in terms of their valuation of a policy change. Citizens’ valuations can be contrasted with the views of interest groups and lobbyists and considered in making policies. In the future, application of this tool to other policy areas (such as land use and heritage preservation) can be explored.

12401014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12401014.value: Motivated by the government's proposed target of reducing CO2 emissions by 30% of the 2005 level in the year 2020, we estimate the residential willingness-to-pay (WTP) for deep decarbonization of Hong Kong's electricity supply, which is heavily dependent on coal-fired generation. Our contingent valuation survey conducted in 2016 of 1460 households yields dichotomous choice data based on the respondents' answers to a series of closed-ended questions. Such data are less susceptible to the strategic bias that often plagues self-stated WTP data obtained by direct elicitation via open-ended questions. Using binary choice models, we find that average WTP is 48% - 51%, relative to current bills, if the decarbonization target is achieved via natural gas generation and renewable energy. However, estimated WTP declines to 32% - 42% when decarbonization entails additional nuclear imports from China. As the projected bill increase caused by the target's implementation is 40%, our WTP estimates support the government's fuel mix policy of using natural gas and renewable energy to displace Hong Kong's coal generation.

12401714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12401714.value: The development of seventeenth-century French harpsichord music is enigmatic in several respects. Although little is known about the formation of this style before 1650 (we have names of composers, but no surviving music), the style has attained a high degree of refinement and sophistication in the music of the earliest known masters (e.g. Chambonnières, Louis Couperin, D’Anglebert). The creative processes behind how the seventeenth-century musicians taught and played remained steeped in mystery. A study of recently rediscovered manuscripts offers fresh opportunity for a reassessment of performance practice issues, as well as insight into how contemporary harpsichordists taught and played. By compiling a thematic catalogue of some 20 sources containing seventeenth-century French harpsichord music rediscovered since the publication of Bruce Gustafson’s catalogue of this repertory (1979, 1990), information on new sources, modern editions, scholarly publications, archival materials, and other items of relevance—some of which currently unavailable and some of which currently dispersed across many different locations—will be assembled, classified, catalogued and stored on one convenient site. This updated knowledge base will provide materials for revisiting key issues pertaining to this repertory: how to define the “work”, what could be possible variants (melodic, rhythmic, textural) between performances, what is the role of improvisation, among others. In particular, a comparative study of variant readings between concordant versions and related performance practice matters will inform the present-day performer on ways to maintain spontaneity in works that were composed, and on ways to be creative yet stay faithful to the original spirit of the music. An innovative feature of this project is that information of the sources will be digitally converted to modern terms and organized into databases, paving the way for an online publication which allows scholars worldwide to freely access and locate accurate and updated information using advanced search facilities. 十七世紀法國古鍵琴音樂的發展在好幾方面都是如謎一般的。雖然對於有關這種風格在1650年前形成的資料所知不多（只有作曲家名字，並無留傳下來的樂曲），但在最早期為人所知的大師（如Chambonnières, Louis Couperin, D’Anglebert）作品中，也能看出這種風格已達致頗高的精煉度與複雜度。十七世紀音樂家教學與演奏背後的創作過程卻依然是一個謎團。一個對近期重新發現的手稿之研究，為對演奏實踐有關問題的再評估，以及了解當代古鍵琴家如何教學與演奏提供了新的機遇。自Bruce Gustafson的目錄（1979, 1990）出版後，通過編製二十多個包括十七世紀法國古鍵琴音樂之資料來源的專題目錄，有關新資料來源、現化版本、學術刊物、檔案材料和其他有關材料（有些現時尚未取得，有些則分散於不同地方）將會被集合、分類、編目，並存儲在一個方便的地點。這更新的資料庫會可提供材料重新審視有關這類曲目的關鍵問題 ：如何定義這些作品、演奏中可能的變數（旋律、節奏、組織）、即興發揮的角色等等。具體地說，對同一版本的不同演譯以及有關演奏實踐問題的比較研究，會讓今天的演奏者得合該如何去維持作品的自發性，以及如何既有創意又能忠實地表達作品本來的精神。這個計劃一個創新的特點，是來源的資料會以數據化形式轉換為現代術語並整理成資料庫，開拓一個讓世界各地學者以先進搜尋設備自由存取與尋找準確而最新資料的線上媒介。

12401714.label: Realisation of objectives
12401714.value: The original objectives have been mostly achieved. With generous help from Bruce Gustafson, Denis Herlin and other scholars, I have been able to compile together a list of recently discovered sources. For manuscripts currently located in the UK, Belgium and France, I have travelled to libraries and examined in person the contents and collected source information relevant to this project. For manuscripts located in other countries, I have obtained digital copies from libraries and archives with the exception of several sources that are privately owned. Manuscripts in private ownership include Chambure, Selosse, Oldham and Hogwood-1471. For Chambure and Selosse, I have relied on information provided by Bruce Gustafson and Peter Leech. However, Hogwood-1471, is currently unavailable for research, since this manuscript, previously owned by Christopher Hogwood is being catalogued by the British Library following his decease. The Oldham collection is also unavailable for this research, since the owner is not reachable. In addition, Denis Herlin has alerted me that he has just discovered a new manuscript that contains a significant number of French pieces, including keyboard arrangements of Lully’s music. This manuscript is also privately owned and currently unavailable for research by the PI. I will continue my on-going efforts to access and examine sources not yet available and to share the updated information with the scholarly community at large. Except those few manuscripts that were not available for detailed examination, this research has largely fulfilled the objectives of compiling source information, engraving thematic incipits of identified French harpsichord music, and organizing relevant information into database records. Although information of these manuscripts is summarized in a recent article by Bruce Gustafson (‘Four decades after French Harpsichord Music of the Seventeenth Century: newly discovered sources,’ in: Rachelle Taylor and Hank Knox, Perspectives on Early Keyboard Music and Revival in the Twentieth Century, London and New York, Routledge, 2018, pp. 7-45), detailed source inventories are still lacking for the new sources. It is possible that my research on the new sources could integrate into Gustafson’s monumental catalogue at a later stage. For many sources in this project, the identities of the scribes are still unknown, and many pieces are not yet identified. One challenge relates to the fact that in the majority of manuscript sources, original music often rubs shoulder to shoulder with transcriptions, making the process of identification extremely tedious. In this project, I have made thematic incipits not only of identified music, but also of unidentified music. In addition, I have compiled a list of numeric incipits by adopting Gustafson’s existing system, making these themes searchable for a digitized thematic catalogue. Having examined all the newly discovered sources, I have also scrutinized each source for evidence of (1) performance practice, and (2) how the harpsichord was taught in the seventeenth. In addition, research into the creative processes behind how the seventeenth-century harpsichordists taught has shed new light on how musicians could expand a range of historically informed techniques of interpreting this music. This research has identified not only new pieces for the seventeenth century French harpsichord repertory, but also new versions of existing pieces. Significantly, some of the new versions were transmitted in sources by professional musicians (such as Couperin-Turin). My research into the performance practice and the creative process of French harpsichord teaching and performance has so far led to the publication of two scholarly articles, one online resource, and two paper presentations at international conferences. At least one more article is being prepared and will be submitted to a top-tier journal later this year. Main reason for under-achievements: a few manuscripts owned privately were not available for consultation (as explained above).

12401714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12401714.value: The development of seventeenth-century French harpsichord music is enigmatic in several respects. Although little is known about the formation of this style before 1650 the style has attained a high degree of sophistication in the music of the earliest known masters, including Chambonnières, Louis Couperin and D’Anglebert. The current study of about twenty recently-rediscovered manuscripts offers fresh opportunity for a reassessment of performance practice issues, as well as insight into how harpsichordists of the time taught and played. In particular, a comparative study of variant readings between concordant versions serves to inform the present-day performer on ways to maintain spontaneity in works that were composed, and on ways to be creative yet stay faithful to the original spirit of the music. Of even more significance, these new sources provide additional materials for revisiting key issues pertaining to this repertory: how to define the “work”, what could be the possible variants (melodic, rhythmic, textural) between performances, what is the role of improvisation, as well as the creativity processes of French keyboard performance during the seventeenth century. This study supports the prevailing view that the seventeenth-century French harpsichord repertory developed from a largely improvised art in which the notation served as an aide-mémoire to a form with highly sophisticated notation in which the details carefully marked by the composer were expected to be observed meticulously by the performer. Although some of the differences among the manuscript sources could be explained as the inevitable result of aural transmission, it is clear that seventeenth-century scribes did not restrict their role to that of a faithful or mechanical copyist. Instead, they felt quite ready to impose their copying habits, musical tastes and their personalities during the process of writing out ornaments, rhythms, cadences, and other effects. In this context, the notation serves sometimes as an example of what could be done and sometimes as what had been done, in which many elements of the notation are not at all binding on the performer. By identifying elements of the music that are decorative and those that are structural and integral to the musical fabric, modern performers can cultivate ways to be spontaneous yet stay faithful to the original spirit of the music through an increased awareness of the knowledge creatively embedded in the performance.

12401714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12401714.value: (1) This project has led to the publication of my online resource on keyboard arrangements of Lully’s music (http://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/OTCL/), the first digitized thematic catalogue of over 600 pieces from some 70 manuscript and printed sources that constitute the entire repertory of keyboard arrangements of Jean-Baptiste Lully’s music. OTCL provides a useful model for developing future online resources. Clearly, online thematic catalogues carry the obvious advantages of wider dissemination, reduced reproduction costs, and the opportunity to benefit from future technological innovations in which information may be flexibly browsed and searched. I am discussing with Prof. Bruce Gustafson, the leading scholar in my field, the feasibility of developing an electronic resource for the entire seventeenth-century French keyboard repertory. (2) This project has identified additional concordances for many existing pieces, and there is potential for preparing scholarly editions of pieces with multiple versions. To this end, I am compiling a list of pieces not yet published and developing new editorial procedures for these pieces, since the “Urtext” concept is particularly ill-suited to pieces where the original cannot be identified, as in the majority of seventeenth-century keyboard music.

12401714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12401714.value: This project has made a detailed examination of over 20 newly-rediscovered sources containing seventeenth-century French harpsichord music, and led to an enhanced understanding of the reception and transmission of this repertory outside France, since most the new sources are of non-French provenance. In addition to compiling and digitizing source information, this project re-evaluates the significance of the 17th-century French harpsichord music in a range of intellectual and musical issues and assesses the importance of the newly- discovered versions and variant readings for modern scholars, music editors and performers. By connecting ideas pertinent to source studies with ideas pertinent to performance practice studies, this project includes a full reappraisal of our attitudes to performing and teaching this music. Research outcome to date includes two scholarly articles (both peer-reviewed) and an online thematic catalogue of keyboard arrangements of Lully's music (OTCL), as well as two paper presentations delivered at international conferences. The online catalogue offers a useful model for future digital humanities projects. It is an open-ended resource in which data discovered in the future will be added to the catalogue.

12401814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12401814.value: The benefits of regular participation in physical activity (PA) to physical and psychological health throughout the lifespan are well recognized. However, previous studies reported that children’s participation in PA decreased significantly during their transition into adolescence (Nader et al., 2008). Recent evidence further reported that many adolescents were living in a physically inactive lifestyle (Hallal et al., 2012). In considering the participation of PA among adolescents, study suggested that the PA during Physical Education (PE) classes contributed considerably to students’ overall PA level (Alderman et al., 2012; U. Meyer et al., 2013). However, a local study found that a decrease of participation in moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) in secondary school PE classes in Hong Kong (Chow et al., 2009). This decline of PA level among adolescents may have a significant impact on their cardiovascular, skeletal, and psychological health (Biddle et al., 2004). Therefore, the factors that influence adolescents’ PA level in both PE classes and leisure time should be further studied. PE class is considered an important platform to promote PA in children and adolescents (Pate et al., 2006). Therefore, many studies were conducted to examine how social factors would influence students’ learning outcomes (i.e., PA level, competence, motivation) in relation to PE class. Previous studies suggested that PE teachers’ autonomy supportive behaviors significantly predicted students’ autonomous motivation towards PA in PE class and leisure-time (i.e., Standage et al., 2012). However, influences of other important need-supportive behaviors such as structure (viz., which consists of the provision of guidance, expectations, plans and goal setting) and involvement (i.g., the degree to which significant others devote time, energy and interests to others) were ignored. In another study, Chow et al. (2009) examined the PA level of secondary school students and the environmental influence on the PA during the PE classes. However, the influence of teachers’ teaching behaviors was not examined in this study. Furthermore, majority of previous studies used self-report measures to measure teachers’ need-supportive behaviors, which may not accurately reflect the true teaching behaviors (Haerens et al., 2013). This project aims to investigate the relationships between observed PE teachers’ need-supportive behaviors (autonomy support, structure, and involvement) and students’ objectively measured PA level and other motivational outcomes (motivation, effort, and subjective vitality) during PE classes in secondary schools in Hong Kong. The findings of the proposed study will complement the previous works on teachers’ need-supportive behaviors and students’ PA level during PE classes in secondary schools.

12401814.label: Realisation of objectives
12401814.value: Objective 1 was achieved. The relationships between observed PE teachers’ need supportive teaching styles and students’ perceived PE teachers’ need supportive teaching styles were examined among 90 secondary school PE teachers and their students (n=2287) using multilevel structural equation modeling. It was found that only one (structure support during activity) out of four observed need-supportive teaching styles (autonomy support, structure support during activity, structure support before activity, and involvement) was significantly associated with students’ perceived structure support. Surprisingly, these results are inconsistent with previous study, in which weak significant associations were reported. The present findings suggested that the observed need-supportive teaching styles might not be accurately reflected from students’ perception. One of the reasons may be that the students, not like the coders who had received systematic training on analyzing the videos with the purpose of objectively assess PE teachers’ teaching styles, did not have relevant knowledge to differentiate the specific supportive teaching styles they perceived from their teachers. They might perceive their teachers’ teaching styles solely based on their feelings in that particular moment or their previous experiences interacting with their teachers. This may explain the nonsignificant relationships between the two sets of data. Objective 2 was achieved. The relationships among observed PE teachers’ need-supportive teaching styles and students’ objectively measured physical activity and students perceived need satisfaction and motivation in PE classes were examined. It was found that only structure support before activity was associated with students’ moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPAP: percentage of class time; MVPAT: absolute time). It is worthy to note that students’ physical activity level in PE classes might predominately influenced by the sport activities taught in the classes, which may also be one of the reasons that caused insignificant associations. No significant associations were found among observed teachers’ need-supportive teaching styles and students’ need satisfaction and motivation. Interestingly, students’ perceived teachers’ structure support was found significantly associated with student’s MVPAT. Further, all students’ perceived need-supportive teaching styles were significantly associated with students’ perceived need satisfaction. Students’ perceived need-supportive teaching styles were significantly and positively associated with students’ autonomous motivations and negatively associated with students’ external regulation and amotivation. It is noteworthy that most of the aforementioned results at students’ level are consistent with previous findings in PE context. The present findings suggested that students’ perceived teachers’ teaching styles might have played a relatively more important role on influencing their behaviors and subjective feelings compared with the so-called objective measurement of teachers’ behaviors, which involved less “self-relevant information”. Therefore, the present findings further suggested that future study should consider the purpose of the study when selecting tools of measuring teachers’ teaching style in PE context. On one hand, for example, if the interest of the study is more related to assessing PE teachers’ teaching styles or investigating whether a particular program is effective or not in changing teachers’ need-supportive teaching styles, researchers may consider using observational approach. This is because the observational approach assesses teaching behaviors from a third party’s perspective that requires less or no self-relevant information and therefore the comparisons could be made based on the “same” standard and criterion. On the other hand, if the interest of the study is more related to students’ feelings and behaviors in PE context, researchers may consider using students’ self-reported instruments because compared with the objective outside reality, the perceived feelings of students and its relations with behaviors may provide more information.

12401814.label: Major findings and research outcome
12401814.value: Observed teachers’ structure support during activity was significantly associated with students’ perceived teachers’ structure support. Observed teachers’ structure support before activity was associated with students’ moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPAP: percentage of class time; MVPAT: absolute time). Observed teachers’ need-supportive teaching styles were not associated with students’ self-reported need satisfaction and motivation. In contrast, students’ perceived teachers’ structure support was significantly associated with student’s objectively measured MVPAT. Students’ perceived need-supportive teaching styles were significantly associated with students’ self-reported need satisfaction. Further, students’ perceived need-supportive teaching styles were significantly and positively associated with students’ autonomous motivations and negatively associated with students’ external regulation and amotivation.

12401814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12401814.value: To better understand the question that how teachers’ teaching behaviors may influence students’ behaviors and subjective feelings in PE classes, more works should be done to further investigate how the associations between objectively measured teachers’ teaching behaviors and students’ perceived teachers’ teaching behaviors could be established. The question of whether teachers’ teaching style could be changed or not has received a lot of attention in academic contexts, more study should be done on the evaluation of the development and effectiveness of these programs. Given the methodological limitations of existing studies that only one occasion measurement was used, future study may consider adopting multiple-occasion assessments approach to minimize the “situational effect” on the measurement of teachers’ teaching styles. Further, research has consistently suggested that although teachers are need supportive in class (e.g., Reeve et al., 2004; Tessier et al., 2010), not all students equally perceive these interactions as need supportive, and these differences in students’ perceptions of the same behavior might depend on students’ personal characteristics. Therefore, future study may pay more attention to the influence of personal characteristics such as personality, causality orientation and even gene on theirs perceptions of teachers’ teaching behaviors.

12401814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12401814.value: The influences of teachers’ teaching behaviors on students’ behaviors and feelings in school contexts have been widely evidenced. However, the associations between observed teachers’ teaching styles and students’ perceived teachers’ teaching styles have not been well investigated. Although previous studies in PE setting suggested significant associations between the two sets of data, the findings of the present study failed to support the relationships. Further, the present findings also failed to support the associations between observed teacher’s teaching styles and students’ MVPA in PE context. More studies should be done to further explore how the associations could be established because it is the fundamental question of how teachers’ teaching behavior may influence on their students’ experiences and learning outcomes in school contexts. Students’ perceived teachers’ teaching style plays a relative more important role in predicting their motivation and behaviors in PE classes. If the interests of the study are on students’ subjective feelings and behaviors, the study should pay more attention to students’ perceptions rather than the so call objective outside reality. Strategies and programs could be developed to increase students’ perceptions of need-supportive teaching styles, which will further result in students’ positive subjective feelings and adaptive behaviors in PE context.

12402314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12402314.value: In 1948, one year after India's independence, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Films Division (FD) to lead the production and distribution of documentary films, and participate in the project of nation building. Following the model of the Indian mixed economy, in which public and private sectors collaborated, 60% of FD films were produced internally, whilst 40% were commissioned from private companies, which also produced films outside of FD. These three areas of production (internal to, associated with and external to FD) made up the Indian documentary film sector of the 1950s. Whilst films made within that sector explored social issues, they were rarely able to do so from an overtly critical perspective. However, during the 1960s and early 1970s, this changed, as documentary films made in conjunction with, and outside of FD, began to question social inequality, and the role and actions of the state. At the same time, these films also began to explore film form more directly. However, this period of advance in Indian documentary film culture came to an end in 1975, when a government-decreed ‘State of Emergency’ imposed controls over the media, including the documentary film. The documentary film production of the period 1948-1975 was characterised by increasing formal experimentation and analytical social and political enquiry, and by a complex, mixed structure of state-sponsored monopoly and free-market operation. However, that production remains significantly under-researched. The project proposed here will be the first to investigate this under-researched area of the documentary film sector in India from 1948 to 1975. It will research the economic and organizational structure of that sector, the themes and stylistic features of films produced, and the role played by official, professional and creative factors in the development of the sector. The project builds on the PI's doctoral research on Indian film and television industries, and will combine archival research, interviews and film analysis, to arrive at conclusions on how the Indian documentary film sector developed against a context of national independence, consolidation of the commercial film, and the emergence of television and art cinema. The project will also aim to assess the significance of the films produced. This original project will thus make an important contribution to the field of documentary film studies and Indian film studies, and will also provide concrete research findings and a solid foundation for an envisioned later extension project, which will cover the longer, later period of 1975-2015. 1948年，即印度獨立後一年，當地總理尼赫魯(Jawaharlal Nehru)成立電影部門，用以率領印度紀錄片製作與發行，以及參與國家建設項目。電影部門依循印度公營與私營經濟並存的混合體制，60%的電影出品由內部製作，另外40%為政府委託私人公司製作；私人公司本身亦製作旗下的電影作品。上述三大製片源頭(電影部門製作、公私聯合製作及非電影部門製作)，構成了1950年代印度紀錄片領域的骨幹，作品探索社會問題，卻甚少以公然批判的角度拍攝。及至1960年代至1970年代初，這個情況卻有改變。不論公私聯合製作及非電影部門製作的紀錄片內容，皆開始質疑社會不均的現象，以至國家的角色與各種行動。作品亦更直接地探究電影的形式。然而，印度政府在1975年對媒體頒佈緊急狀態令，接管行業運作，紀錄片亦不能倖免，當地紀錄片文化的進步時期就此告終。在1948年至1975年間，可見印度紀錄片透過國家贊助全權製作與自由巿場運作的混合與複雜架構，正式地實行更多電影實驗，越加分析與質詢多種的社會與政治問題，成為當時印度紀錄片的一大特徵。只是這段時期仍欠深入與獨到的研究。 本建議項目將是首個調查1948年至1975年印度紀錄片發展的研究活動。本項目將探討這個領域的經濟與組織結構，作品的各種主題與風格特色，以及政府、專業與創意因素在促進印度紀錄片發展上的作用。 本項目以首席研究員的印度電影與電視行業博士研究為本，結合檔案研究、訪問與電影分析，總結印度紀錄片如何在國家獨立、商業電影整合及電視與藝術電影行業冒起的情況下，萌芽發展。本項目亦旨在評估當時作品的意義。這個原創研究項目將為紀錄片與印度電影研究帶來重大的貢獻，提供扎實的研究結果，同時為日後的延伸研究項目奠立牢固的基礎。延伸研究項目將剖析較後的年期，即1975年至2015年的印度紀錄片發展，涉獵的年期更廣。

12402314.label: Realisation of objectives
12402314.value: Objectives 1 to 7 have been achieved and appear in: A) The extended research report (36,333 words), which compiles research findings and includes an extensive bibliography and filmography. This report is structured around the historical context of the period from 1948 to 1975 and is based on an approach combining the critical analysis of primary (official papers from Indian archives, interviews, in-depth analysis of 100 films) and secondary research material. This report has been published on PI's research website at the following address: http://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/documentary-film/india.php B) The 24 interviews conducted in India and elsewhere between January 2015 and February 2016 with 24 important Indian documentary film scholars, filmmakers, and professionals working for public and private organisations involved in the production, distribution and exhibition of documentary films in India. Their first-hand and personal insights provide exclusive and rare oral testimonies on the lesser-known history of the documentary film in India. These interview transcripts are available on the PI's research website at the following address: http://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/documentary-film/interview.php C) The 100 in-depth textual analysis of significant Indian documentary films. Each individual analysis includes metadata (filmmaker, producer, company, duration, title, year), synopsis, detailed description and contextual analysis of the film. 12402314.label: Major findings and research outcome
12402314.value: The major findings of this project include reaching conclusions concerning the creation, organisation, development and governance of the documentary film sector in India from 1948 to 1975, including both Films Division - the state-sponsored institution launched in 1948 (one year after independence) - and private filmmakers and producers. This project also details the relationships that the documentary film developed with television (in its infancy over the period under study), art cinema (which more significantly developed in the late 1960s) and the mainstream film industry in general; and how the organisation, governance and development of these various film and TV sectors reflected the state project of nation building and national integration. The new online platform 'South and South-East Asia Documentary Film Research Website' has been designed in collaboration with HKBU library and co-I Prof. Ian Aitken to hold and disseminate primary and secondary research materials – including texts, images, video and audio files – pertaining to the subject of documentary film in South and South-East Asia and covering the colonial, late colonial and post-colonial periods. The digital archive presented in this website collects, electronically processes, preserves and disseminates primary and secondary research materials pertaining to the documentary film in colonial and post-colonial South and South-East Asia using web and database archiving techniques. In its initial phase of development, this website contained over 3,000 electronically-processed pages of official documents relating to the use of official films in South-East Asia, including Hong Kong, written between 1945 and 1973. As a result of the digitalisation process, these primary materials can now be cross-referenced in a number of ways using web search and retrieval tools that facilitate the open access and sharing of information worldwide. Related to the wider developing field of ‘digital humanities’, this website marks a major achievement for the advancement of academic research, as scholars are now able to freely access this material and contribute to further developments in the area of colonial, late colonial and post-colonial film studies in the South-East Asian region. A whole new set of materials on this topic, which includes 3,000 pages of official documents pertaining to PI's GRF project, has been analysed and digitalised over the academic year 2015-2016. This material will appear on the website in Spring 2016. 24 interviews and 100 analysis of individual documentary films pertaining to PI's GRF project are available on this website.

12402314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12402314.value: PI's employment contract with HKBU ends on April 30, 2016, after which PI will permanently return to her home country. Therefore, there is little potential for the further development of this research by PI in Hong Kong. However, it is hoped that the research website, and more specifically the online archive of the primary documents collected in India over the course of this 18-month project, as well as the collaboration started with Darthmouth College in the US, will encourage other scholars and post-graduate students to continue researching this lesser-known area of Indian film history.

12402314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12402314.value: This 18-month research project was the first to investigate the under-researched area of the documentary film sector in India from 1948 to 1975. It has researched the economic and organizational structure of that sector, the themes and stylistic features of the films produced, and the role played by official, professional and creative factors in the development of the sector. Combining first-hand archival research, interviews with important figures of the documentary film in India and in-depth analysis of 100 significant films of the period, this project has detailed how, over the first three decades of independence in India (1948–1975), the new independent state used the documentary film as the main audio-visual medium of mass communication and education, how the strict state governance of the documentary film sector was challenged inside and outside FD, as well as by the audience, and how this opposition more widely reflected the difficulty in reaching a consensual national identity in India. Finally, it has presented how Indian documentary films articulated both the state’s vision and its challenges and limitations in the area of nation building and national integration.

12403214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12403214.value: Originating in Europe in the 1970s, foreign/second language learner autonomy has become influential as an educational goal in many parts of the world, including “Confucian-heritage” (Biggs & Watkins, 1996) societies such as Mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong. In recent years, it has been well recognized that the development of language learner autonomy depends largely on language teacher autonomy. Therefore, the development of teacher autonomy in pre-service and in-service teachers has become a relevant and urgent issue if we aspire to support and nurture autonomy in language learners. It is against this social-educational background that the current study is proposed. After 30 years of research and practice, there is now a fair degree of consensus on what learner autonomy means in language education. However, since the notion of teacher autonomy has only come to the fore over the last decade, there is much less consensus on its meaning and its development processes. In a historical sense, the idea of teacher autonomy was introduced into language education by researchers who were primarily interested in the promotion of learner autonomy (Benson & Huang, 2008; Little, 1995; Smith, 2000). Therefore, what has been discussed so far in the literature is primarily about the interrelationship between language teachers’ autonomy and their students' autonomy (autonomy of different individuals). There has been, to date, very little published empirical research on the complex interaction between autonomy in language learning and autonomy in language teaching, for the same individual, over a prolonged period of time. This research seeks to examine the nature and kinds of transition from learner to teacher autonomy that might be expected in the development of the same individual moving from a language learner context to a language teacher context. Following an interpretative-qualitative research tradition and foregrounding insider perspectives, the study investigates and compares, in depth, the learning-teaching experiences of English learners-teachers, spanning their pre-service teacher education and their first year in school teaching, in the Mainland Chinese socio-institutional contexts. The research will contribute new knowledge to the long-term development of language learner and teacher autonomy and will generate insights into pre-service and in-service language teacher education. It will also project a direction for research on autonomy: A shift away from snapshot studies of classroom and out-of-class learning towards investigations of the development of autonomy over long periods of time and in the context of the lives of institutions and the individuals who pass through them. 外語/二語學習者自主性的概念起源於歐洲二十世紀七十年代，現已成為世界上很多地方包括受儒家傳統思想影響的社會如中國大陸、臺灣和香港的一個教育目標 (Biggs & Watkins, 1996)。近年來，人們意識到語言學習者自主性的發展在很大程度上取決於語言教師自主性。因此，如果我們要培養語言學習者之自主性，如何促進職前、職中教師之自主性就成為一個既相關又緊急的課題。本研究正是基於此社會、教育背景提出的。 經過三十年的研究和實踐，人們對語言教育中學習者自主性的理解已有相當程度的共識。然而，由於圍繞教師自主性的討論在過去的十年左右才嶄露頭角，關於教師自主性的含義及其發展過程就明顯缺乏一致看法。在歷史意義上，教師自主性的概念是被有志於促進學習者自主性的學者引進語言教育領域的（Benson & Huang, 2008; Little, 1995; Smith, 2000）。因此，迄今為止文獻所討論的主要是語言教師的自主性和他們所教學生的自主性之間的關係（即不同個體的自主性）。到目前為止，還沒有多少已發表的實證研究集中討論同一個體在長時間內其語言學習自主與其語言教學自主之間複雜的相互作用。 本研究旨在審視從學習者自主到教師自主過渡之性質和種類，而這種轉變是可以預料在同一個人身上因應從語言學習者環境到語言教授者環境的變遷而發生。本課題遵循詮釋性-質性研究傳統並把內部人視角置於顯著地位，深入地調查和比較在中國大陸社會-機構環境下既是英語學習者也是英語教授者的橫跨從職前教師教育到大學畢業後第一年在中小學從事教學的學習英語-教授英語的長期經歷。本課題將對語言學習者自主性和教師自主性的研究和實踐貢獻新的知識，並將對職前和職中語言教師教育產生新的見解。本課題也將給自主性的研究指明一個方向：即從對課堂及課外學習的“快照”式研究轉移到自主性長期發展的歷時考察。

12403214.label: Realisation of objectives
12403214.value: Objective 1 corresponds with research questions 1-2 (How do student teachers take control of their English learning over time? How do student teachers and later in-service novice teachers take control of their English teaching over time?). Broadly speaking, this objective is concerned with all aspects of learning-teaching experiences of the research participants. The project provides a thick description of pre-service and in-service teachers’ experiences in learning English as a foreign language (EFL); learning to teach EFL; and teaching EFL to pursue their personal and professional development, over time and across settings. The current study gave more attention to “autonomy in language teaching” (language teacher autonomy), which generated richer data and greater insights into the long-term development of language teacher autonomy. However, the enquiry into pre-service and in-service teachers’ own EFL learning experiences was also useful in providing a background to understand these participants’ pathways for autonomy (see objective 2). Shortly after the project started, the researcher realized that a comparison between the learning and teaching EFL experiences of these EFL teachers in mainland China (especially Shenzhen) and Hong Kong would generate insights into how autonomy might be afforded and constrained similarly and differently in two socio-educational contexts which are similar in some ways but different in other ways (see objective 4). The objective was fully achieved. Objective 2 corresponds with research question 3 (How does autonomy in foreign language learning affect autonomy in foreign language teaching?). To achieve this objective, data were collected with the research participants, same individuals, when they were student teachers in the final year in university; when they were conducting their teaching practicum in co-operating schools; and when they became real in-service teachers and were teaching in primary or secondary schools. When they were still student teachers, there was a direct focus on their perceptions of language learning and teaching, their perceptions and classroom behaviours in their teaching practicum. In their initial in-service teaching years, they were often invited to draw on their university and pre-university experiences to interpret their classroom practices. These data, collected at different times in different settings, in the form of interviews, teaching journals, school documents, and informal social media (WeChat) conversations, were compared closely to examine how their autonomous learning experiences affected their autonomous teaching experiences. The objective was fully achieved. Objective 3 corresponds with research question 4 (What roles do identity and agency play in the development of autonomy in foreign language learning and teaching?). Addressing this research question would contribute to autonomy theory and practice in the mainland Chinese and Hong Kong contexts. To achieve this objective, all the data collected at different stages were analysed closely and relevant literature was drawn on to develop arguments on the interrelatedness and the complex interaction among the three key constructs of autonomy, identity and agency that I have been conceptualizing in the past years. Although there is still much more to do to fully understand these complex ideas, the longitudinal research approach adopted and the great amount of data collected have facilitated the full achievement of this objective. Objective 4 corresponds with research question 5 (What influences the development of learner and teacher autonomy in the particular Chinese socio-institutional contexts?). To address this question, I had also collected data with student teachers (later in-service teachers) in Hong Kong to enable a comparison on how foreign language learner/teacher autonomy is afforded and constrained in two particular settings of Shenzhen and Hong Kong, which shared similarities in some aspects but differed in other aspects. This turned out to be a sensible decision to facilitate the achievement of the objective. These efforts have also contributed to the success of the GRF application for 2018/19 (Project Number: 12607418; Project title: “Identity, agency and autonomy in foreign and second language education: Case studies of in-service teachers in Shenzhen and Hong Kong”).

12403214.label: Major findings and research outcome
12403214.value: Student teachers in the BA TEFL (teaching English as a foreign language) degree programme in mainland China displayed more reactive autonomy rather than proactive autonomy in their first two years in university. However, when they moved to a more advanced stage (the last two years in university) they became more proactive in learning EFL and learning to teach EFL, displaying a high degree of individual agency triggered by a prospective teacher identity. In their initial in-service years, they were eager to enhance their capacity to take effective control over their teaching and professional development (teacher autonomy) through a range of strategies such as taking the initiative to upgrade their knowledge and skills in classroom teaching and management; adopting what they considered as a more “student-centred” approach in classroom instruction and meanwhile supporting enthusiastically students’ out-of-class learning; and, establishing a harmonious relationship with their mentors, colleagues, and “leaders” (e.g. principals and the middle management). In their first-year (particularly first-semester) teaching, their previous experiences as autonomous learners throughout school and university education over more than 10 years substantially mediated and shaped their autonomous teaching and autonomous development. In their initial years in school teaching, teacher identity provided a clear direction for the development of teacher autonomy because identity formation often gave rise to the exercise of teacher agency to overcome difficulties and constraints in their particular settings. In order to examine more closely the development pathways of novice English teachers in mainland China, particularly in Shenzhen, which, as a city, is geographical-economically similar to yet social-political-educationally different from Hong Kong, a few novice English teachers in primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong were invited to join the study. Initial findings indicate that in the two neighbouring cities, pre-service and novice English teachers’ perceptions of and responses to affordances for and constraints upon their autonomy in teaching and teacher-learning are influenced substantially by a range of differences between the two cities in areas such as pre-service teacher education (e.g., predominantly proficiency courses in Shenzhen vs a sufficient number of pedagogical courses in Hong Kong; loosely organized once-off six-week teaching practicum in Shenzhen vs rigorously implemented practicums in Hong Kong), teacher induction and staff development opportunities (much more school-supported professional learning activities in Shenzhen), teaching workload (much greater in Hong Kong) and working conditions, institutional structures and cultures, etc.

12403214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12403214.value: The GRF research process and major findings suggest that there is much potential for further development of the research. First, it would generate rich insights into teacher development through tracking these novice teachers beyond their survival stage, for example, the initial three years in their school teaching. It is recognized that autonomy is hard to gain but easy to lose. A long-term development view of autonomy coupled with a longitudinal approach in research would help us gain a deep understanding of the complex idea of autonomy and its complex interaction with related notions of identity and agency. Second, adding a comparative element to the teacher development project would be helpful to understand how autonomy is afforded and constrained, similarly and differently, in particular socio-educational settings. The researcher was lucky to be awarded a new GRF project for 2018/2019 (“Identity, agency and autonomy in foreign and second language education: Case studies of in-service teachers in Shenzhen and Hong Kong”) which is intended to integrate the above two elements in the research process.

12403214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12403214.value: Originating in Europe in the 1970s, foreign/second language learner autonomy has become an educational goal in many parts of the world, including Mainland China and Hong Kong. In recent years, it has been well recognized that language learner autonomy depends largely on language teacher autonomy. Therefore, the development of teacher autonomy in pre-service and in-service teachers has become a relevant issue if we aspire to support and nurture autonomy in language learners. There has been, to date, very little published empirical research on the complex interaction between autonomy in language learning and autonomy in language teaching, for the same individual, over a prolonged period of time. This research examined the nature and kinds of transition from learner to teacher autonomy in the development of the same individual moving from a language learner context to a language teacher context. The research has contributed new knowledge to the long-term development of language learner and teacher autonomy and generated insights into pre-service and in-service language teacher education. It has also projected a direction for research on autonomy: A shift away from snapshot studies of classroom and out-of-class learning towards investigations of the development of autonomy over long periods of time and across settings.
