12407814.value: 從風險社會視野看青年人由學校過渡到工作: 以四個不同學歷程度的香港青年組群為例

12407814.label: Project Objectives
12407814.value: To examine a diversity of young people’s perceptions and negotiations of risks and opportunities with reference to their school-to-work transition experience and their social positions To identify the relationship between youth aspiration pursuance and the context and experience of their transitions to work
rows: To examine a diversity of young people’s perceptions and negotiations of risks and opportunities with reference to their school-to-work transition experience and their social positions
To identify the relationship between youth aspiration pursuance and the context and experience of their transitions to work

12407814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12407814.value: This research is a qualitative study focused on examining and comparing the school-to-work transition experience of four groups of young people with different levels of educational qualifications in Hong Kong. The first group is early school leavers who failed to finish secondary school education. The second group refers to those who failed the public examination for Form 5 or Form 6 students. The third group refers to those who did not manage to pursue studying a sub-degree or degree programme subsidized by the government in spite of getting pass scores with the public examination. Finally, the more privileged degree holders are the fourth group. Informed by the risk society perspective, the study aims at 1) examining a diversity of young people’s perception and negotiation of risks and opportunities with reference to their school-to-work transition experience and their social positions; and 2) identifying the relationship between youth aspiration pursuance and the context and experience of their transitions to work. It is assumed that these young people’s navigation to work are characterized with risks and boundedness, which are constituted by the interlocking relations between agency and structure as illuminated in regards to stratification, commodification, individualized responsibility, and individual aspirations. Purposive sampling is deployed for the study to help maximize the discovery of young people’s perceptions and management of risks and opportunities and pursuing their own aspirations during this transition journey. In drawing samples for each of the four respondent groups, three sampling criteria are taken into account, namely, 1) gender: males vs. females; 2) class: relatively disadvantaged vs. relatively favorable background by using the median monthly domestic household income as the dividing line; and 3) social status: those who are not versus those who are in education, employment or training at the time of face-to-face interview. Against the backdrop of ongoing global economic crisis which has made ‘school-to-work’ pathway a major public policy in market economies, this research study would fill in a research gap leading to a more critical understanding of the diversity of young people’s perceiving and negotiating risks and opportunities and pursuing their aspirations on their transitions from school to work, which can help shed light on addressing the complexity of school-to-work transitions in a post-industrial service economy like Hong Kong, which is characterized by a shift from manual work to a mix of service and knowledge-intensive forms of labor. 這項質性研究旨在探討及比較四個不同學歷程度的香港青年組群從學校過渡到工作世界的經驗。第一個是沒有完成中學教育的組群。第二個組群是中五或中六公開考試的失敗者。第三個是中學公開考試及格，但卻未能攻讀由政府資助的副學士或學士課程的組群。最後，第四個是獲取學士學位的較優越組群。從風險社會視野出發，本研究旨在探討兩方面，首先檢視青年人在過渡至工作世界及其所身處的社會位置時如何理解風險及運用所面對的機會，以及探索他們在此過渡旅程中如何取捨或整合就職需要與個人志向及願望的達成。研究的背後假設是在過渡旅程上，青年人總遇上風險與障礙，而這種經驗又與其主體性及面對的社會結構結下不解之緣，並在不同經驗面向反映出來，如社會分層化、商品化、個人責任，與個人職志等。為了盡量展露青年在理解和管理風險與機會以及追夢的多樣性面貌，本研究會採用目的抽樣法。每一個青年組群，均會依據三個抽樣指標邀請受訪者，分別是(一):性別，即男性及女性; (二):社會階層，即入息中位數以上及以下; (三):受訪時的社會位置，即是在職、在學或受訓者，或三者皆不是。在彌漫著全球化社會風險的處境下，並在後工業社會的氛圍下，即由勞動力密集的工業生產階段過渡至以服務及知識為本的後工業時期，此項研究將有助理解不同青年組群從學校過渡至工作世界的旅途上所展露的殊異經驗。

12407814.label: Realisation of objectives
12407814.value: The project objectives have been achieved in a number of ways. In a general term, the research team was able to recruit all the 96 participants from each category as proposed under the framework of purposive sampling. Although we experienced some difficulties in recruiting the last few participants, the team was finally able to expand our direct and indirect social networks and seek referrals from new/existing affiliated helping professionals. In a specific term, having successfully recruited all required informants enable the team to carry out other essential research procedures including data compiling, transcribing, translating, coding, recoding, analyzing and research write-ups. With an in-depth face-to-face individual interview with the use of a semi-structured interview schedule, the team was able to delve into youth respondents’ individualized transition biographies and to identify their risk coping strategies and the risks confronted, who were characterized by four different levels of academic credentials. A web of shaping factors including class, gender, young parenthood, sole parenting, relationships, educational qualifications, agency and personal aspirations (serious leisure, career paths or individual interests) has all played a complex role in youth transitions to work/adulthood. The research objectives are further achieved by a detailed and an individual analysis of young people at each level. Four manuscripts are written to explicate the characteristic features of young people alongside the level of education they belong to. The manuscript titled “Untangling the complexity of the lost generation’s transitions to work: The case of Hong Kong” describes young people without the completion of public examinations (Level 1); “Negotiation and compromise in the midst of risks: A case study of academic underachievers in Hong Kong” highlights the transition journeys of holders of secondary school qualifications (Level 2); “Trapped in the middle: Hong Kong youth transitions from a risk society perspective” unfolds lives of pursuers/holders of sub-degree qualifications (Level 3) and “Juggle in a privileged position? Young people’s transitions to work in a risk society perspective” revisits the lived experiences of pursuers/ holders of degree qualifications (Level 4). An overall paper titled “Qualification stratification and risk management: Youth transitions to work in Hong Kong” is written to compare and contrast the young people with the four different levels of academic credentials. As such, a fuller picture of young people’s transitions to work can be drawn out.

12407814.label: Major findings and research outcome
12407814.value: Of the 24 lost-generation respondents who are the early school leavers (Level 1), there were two major risks facing them: 1) employment precarity and 2) young parenthood/sole parenting. To overcome the incurred difficulties, some respondents develop dreams to pursue their aspired leisure or career paths, while some female homemaker respondents made sacrifice for their children. Of the 24 academic underachievers who are holders of secondary school qualifications (Level 2), a majority of the informants was afflicted by precarity. Eight of them developed their serious leisure to cope with risks caused by low academic credentials; six pursued vocational qualifications to overcome the limited opportunities available to them and four struck to acquire tertiary (degree and sub-degree) academic qualifications. Unlike the young mothers from the lost-generation group, they tended to experience greater sense of dissatisfaction and inter-role conflict. Of the 24 trapped middles who are sub-degree students/graduates (Level 3), the acquisition of degrees was largely the prime concern for every respondent in this group when they finished their secondary education. They were also required to mediate risks related to student loans and debt particularly for those who were less well-off. It was interesting to note that informants who aspired to alternative pathways, either pursuing personal aspirations or simply being satisfied with sub-degree qualifications, seemed to experience less internal struggles and be more optimistic about their future. Of the 24 better qualified (Level 4), all degree students/graduates, regardless of whether the pathways are smooth or not, were facing the stratification of degree qualifications which was linked to the notion of tertiary institution hierarchies. Yet those with non-smooth pathways were more likely to be afflicted by debt especially for those who were from less fortunate backgrounds and chose to study self-financed programmes. The transition experience of all the 96 respondents across the four levels was stratified by academic qualifications and further reflected on their manner of occupation, whether being engaged in paid or unpaid work, in which the difference lays in the role of purpose. For those who had paid work, young people with sub-degree qualifications or above tended to have more standard and prospective employment while youth with a secondary school qualification or below tended to churn between precarious, casual and temporary jobs. Some respondents who are NEETs had no purpose or orientation: either did very little or suffered from psychological and physical health challenges which derailed individual future planning.

12407814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12407814.value: The shaping factors such as class, gender, ethnic background, level of educational qualifications, and enjoying a legitimate social status as a youth in education, employment or training or not can be further examined for highlighting the similarities and comparing the differences confronted by youth in their school-to-work transition journeys. Risk perception, risk avoidance, risk coping, and risk taking are arguably shaped and mediated by both personal agency and structural factors. One manuscript has already been published as a referred journal article which is focused on studying the trapped middles with sub-degree qualifications. Four manuscripts were already presented in different international conferences, among which three are to be further revised for consideration for publication in referred journals. These three are respectively focused on studying the school-to-work transitions of i) the lost generation, ii) the better qualified, and iii) overall comparison of 96 respondents with different levels of educational qualifications in regards to their transitions to the world of work and adulthood. A manuscript on the transition of underachievers is also under preparation. All this can empirically inform an in-depth analysis of the complexity and multiplicity of youth transitions to work and adulthood, and inspire policy advocacy and intervention practice.

12407814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12407814.value: This was a valuable piece of research in the way that it compared the transitions to work and adulthood of young people with four different levels of academic credentials in Hong Kong. With detailed analysis, overall transition patterns of each level and major risks confronted by all or by some were distinguished. Discussions on how diverse risk coping strategies were applied provided an insightful analysis of the complex interaction between structure (class, gender, ethnicity, etc.) and agency along with a web of other influential factors (levels of education, parenthood, social networks, aspiration pursuance, etc.) and confirmed Beck’s notion of the risk society that every member of society has to come to terms with the distribution of risk and dangers. All this academic work can help inform a more thorough understanding on the social context and social processes through which young people make a complex transition to the world of work and adulthood at large, which cannot go without confronting risks, making use of resources and networks, trying out opportunities, anticipating intended positive outcomes, and addressing unintended and undesirable outcomes following risk-coping and risk-taking. All this can help inform relevant policy advocacy and intervention practice for advancing youth welfare accordingly.

12408414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12408414.value: 英文報紙中的早期香港電影：1897-1925

12408414.label: Project Objectives
12408414.value: To discover new information relating to early Hong Kong film history.
rows: To discover new information relating to early Hong Kong film history.

12408414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12408414.value: This project will research early film scenes in Hong Kong by reading and collecting film coverage in the major English-language newspapers (The China Mail, South China Morning Post, and Hong Kong Telegraph) in the territory between 1897 (the initial film exhibitions) and 1925 (when the Hongkong/ Canton general strike broke out). This continues the 2010 GRF project “Chinese Film Industry Beyond Shanghai, 1900-1950” that uncovered primary source materials on film marketing, promotion, exhibition and reception in regional Chinese cities. In Hong Kong, one of the four cities surveyed, we found that English-language newspapers covered more film news than the Chinese press, both in quantity and quality. Furthermore, through the English-language materials, we discovered a number of errors in the standard history of Hong Kong film. These findings show the importance of reading English-language newspapers to survey a wider terrain of Hong Kong’s early cinema. Hence, we request a grant to research film coverage in English-language newspapers. We plan to collect and catalogue four sets of primary materials from local archives and libraries on: 1) distribution companies and their circuits, 2) movie theatres, 3) film advertisements, and 4) film reviews. These materials will provide a deeper knowledge of early film industry practices (distribution, marketing and exhibition) and reception that are currently missing in the standard literature. The English-language news investigated will supplement, modify and adjust the existing understanding of early Hong Kong film history. We will share our findings with the scholarly community by building an English database of film news, advertisements and reviews. The collected materials will be catalogued by the following indices: press, date of publication, personnel, company, film title, exhibition venue, tagline, keywords, synopsis, duration and size of advertisements. The database will serve as an essential reference for future research on Hong Kong film history. Further dissemination is planned by means of two to three peer-reviewed publications. 本項目計劃細讀和收集於1897年（電影於香港最早放映年份）至1925年（省港大罷工）期間刊登於香港英語報紙（如德臣西報、南華早報和士蔑報）的電影的新聞與廣告，藉此研究香港早期電影歷史。 本項目延續2010年優配研究金的項目「上海以外的中國電影工業，1900-1950」。該項目重建中國電影市場發行、推廣、映演和接收的一手資料，而香港則是該項目四個受研究城市之一。該研究發現，在香港的英語報紙對電影的報導比中文更廣泛。此外，憑藉這些英文的資料，我們陸續發現標準香港電影史的若干錯誤。這說明英語報紙是研究香港早期電影之重要資料。 本計劃會從本地資料庫和圖書館中收集四款一手資料，並予以編目。資料包括︰（1）發行公司及其發行網絡；（2）電影院；（3）電影廣告；和（4）電影評論。它們會為早期電影業的操作（發行、營銷和放映）和接收提供更深入的知識，而這正是現時一般香港早期電影研究的討論中忽略的面向。透過細緻閱讀英語新聞，本計劃會對現時香港早期電影史的理解予以補充和修改。

12408714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12408714.value: This research project aims to use a critical perspective to examine the characteristics of contemporary art in three Chinese cities; Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Hangzhou. The focus will be on investigating the ‘other aesthetic expressions’ revealed through works by artists who are non-natives living and working in the three respective places. The research project elects to bring Hong Kong together with Shanghai and Hangzhou for a study because the development of contemporary art in the three Chinese cities has been significant over the last decade. Moreover, the three cities share a common experience in their recent histories; they have been the places for people such as foreigners, exiles, and refugees to take shelter or migrate to. These non-natives, being called in this project ‘borrowed people’, nevertheless, make an important contribution to the art and cultural development of the places based on their unique experiences. A total of six artists will be invited to participate in the project, with two artists coming from each city. Artists will be chosen based on their own identities related to the concept of ‘borrowed people’ as well as their works relevant to ‘other aesthetic expressions’. The project intends to bring together places, artists, and artworks to study them. The research will be conducted with two tracks. The first track will comprise individual interviews at the artists’ studios in the cities they live. A series of qualitative and topical interviews will be conducted with an emphasis on analyzing a representative selection of their works. The second track will comprise an exhibition in Hong Kong organized concurrently with the project. The chosen artists will be invited to create a body of new works and present them together with a selection of existing works for a thematic exhibition in accordance with the research project. Although the research is conducted and based in Hong Kong, it will have a broader scope for comparing the art and culture of the three cities. It is expected to expand the understanding of contemporary art in China, acknowledging its distinguished pluralism and eclecticism which allows the contribution of ‘other aesthetic expressions’ brought forth by works from non-native artists with a variety of backgrounds.

12408714.label: Realisation of objectives
12408714.value: This research project is successfully realized with a curated exhibition. Seven artists have been invited to take part in this exhibition. The exhibition borrows from each artist paintings which are representative of his/her art making, including a new series completed in recent years and a selected earlier work. Interwoven with works across a number of years, the exhibition presents a total number of 30 paintings which explores the association between artists, paintings and places, and talks about the value of diversity and the many faces of contemporary painting. This project started in 2015. My curatorial team visited Hong Kong, Shanghai and Hangzhou a number of times, meeting the artists for interviews and selecting the works to be shown. We had the chance to know each artist’s exploration in their art pursuit. We saw in studios paintings to be completed, went through one by one sketches stored in an old suitcase, looked at collections carefully archived in warehouses of galleries and art museums, and came across graffiti still fresh as yesterday around a corner on our way to visit an artist. The participating artists come from different parts of the world. They speak different languages and have different cultural backgrounds. They have, however, settled down for some time in one of these three Chinese cities: Hong Kong, Shanghai and Hangzhou. With Hong Kong, all of them have direct or indirect connection, or they can somehow trace their paths back to the place. Some of them were born in Hong Kong and later moved to another city. Some came to Hong Kong to work many years ago and eventually built their home here. Some are living in another city but frequently return to Hong Kong to show their works. 12408714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12408714.value: Curating is a way to present these multi-layer connections and dialogue. In the process of looking for and contacting the artists, we have learned more about their stories, the paths they travelled, and what they think about life and their art. Emotional bond is never in a static state. Do places affect our feelings or is it what we feel that affects our way of seeing places and the people and things around us? It is quite clear that this exhibition wants to talk about people, about non-local people influencing a place or traces of a place’s influence on them (and their works). Artists, who handle images, materials and space, are the subject of such examination. Cheng Tsai-tung offers a myriad of colour combinations from his inner mind. Frank Vigneron adopts absolute lightness in writing about space. Toru Harada plays the role of “intruder” and brings about the “transformation” between ruins/communities. Cho Yeou-jui repeats on two-dimensional surfaces the weight of reality. Basmat Levin presents people in a lively and exciting way. The rhythm of Siuhak can be seen or heard. Tom O’dea criticises post-modern western paintings in the simplest and most humble way. The exhibition is formed by invited people and borrowed works. In it we can see a wider-than-expected connection between places, as well as the possible extensions and flexibility of painting in one’s inner mind and in the aspect of social aesthetics.

12408714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12408714.value: A new research proposal has been submitted to HKADC in early 2019 to apply for granting another exhibition to further develop the idea of borrowed people. The second exhibition will put focus on examining the art form of "Drawing". Thirteen artists have already agreed to present their drawing works and the exhibition is planned to be held in mid 2020. The artists being invited coming from Hong Kong as well as cities such as Shanghai and Taipei. The second exhibition is intended to further investigate the topic of artworks and artists in places.

12408714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12408714.value: The exhibition project intends to examine the connection between paintings, people and places. The exhibition entitled “Borrowed People” was organized to present the works from seven artists who came from different parts of the world: France, Israel, Japan, Ireland, Taiwan, Hong Kong, however, settled down for some time in one of these three Chinese cities: Hong Kong, Shanghai and Hangzhou. With Hong Kong, all of the seven artists have direct or indirect connection. A total of 30 paintings were displayed in the exhibition which included selected old works as well as new works completed in recent years. Throughout the project, numbers of interviews were conducted with the artists. During the exhibition opening, a forum was held and most artists came over to participate in the discussions. Apart from GRF support to conduct the research and organizing the exhibition, Hong Kong Art Development Council has provided funding for making a fully illustrated exhibition catalogue. The catalogue will feature all the exhibits and will comprise of reviews by scholars and writers. It will also include transcripts summarized from artist interviews and forum discussions. The catalogue will be published in June 2019.

12408914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12408914.value: Huiwen（回文） is an exclusive form of literature in Classical Chinese, to be specific, it may refer to a sentence, or a text, reading from the beginning to the end, or reversely, we both get a full sentence or text with explicit meaning and special aesthetic effect. In Classical Chinese Literature, there are mainly two kinds of Huiwen, the Huiwen shi（回文詩） and Huiwen ci, with the former appearing earlier than the latter. This project aims to study Huiwen ci in the Qing, which includes the following parts: Part one: it will review its first appearance in the Song dynasty（宋代）, studying the reasons of its appearance and the influences got from Huiwen shi. Part two: it will reveal the development scope of Huiwen ci from the Song to Qing dynasty. In the Song dynasty, there are only 50 or so Huiwen ci, while the amount is up to be more than 1000 in the Qing dynasty. Part three: it will study its relation to the family culture, group culture, as well as academic environment in the Qing. Part four: it will study its features of language structure in form of one sentence, double sentences, text as well as co-texts. Part five: it will study its exclusive aesthetic effect via vocabularies, images, rhythm etc. Ci meets a big opportunity for its revival in the Qing, when Huiwen ci has bloomed on the basis that ci writers show greater interests and passion in writing it. They pay efforts in digging out its language charm by deeply studying its word changes and further differentiating ci and poem in genre. Accordingly, this project will adopt the methodology of literary history, culture study as well as aesthetics. The previous research on Huiwen ci was mainly focus on the period of Song, with a small amount and a few achievements. As to the period of Qing, there was seldom any research on it. Comparably speaking, Huiwen ci in the Qing has the privilege of richness and variability both in content and form. Therefore, the significance of the study is to better understand how Huiwen ci creates its distinctive charm by changing the sequence of words order in the Classical Chinese Literature. What’s more, the study will greatly benefit the researchers in the areas of Classical Chinese Literature, Classical Chinese Aesthetics as well as Classical Chinese Culture. 回文（Huiwen）是一種非常獨特的文學形式，它充分運用了漢字的單音節以及注重語序的特點，經過回環變化，造成了獨特的審美效果，是中國文學的一個重要組成部分。本研究計畫擬對清代的回文詞進行研究，包括以下幾方面的內容：1、回文詞的出現與回文詩對它的影響；2、從宋代到明代回文詞的發展狀況；3、清代回文詞興盛的背景；4、清代回文詞在語言結構上的特點；5、清代回文詞所創造的獨特的審美情趣。清代是詞復興的時代，回文詞的繁榮發展，充分體現了清代詞人對詞創作的重視和熱情，他們對詞這種文體之中語言文字的變化表示出更大的興趣，試圖能夠進一步探討詩和詞這兩種文體的區別，也試圖更加充分地挖掘詞的語言魅力。本硏究計劃將把這一現象放在中國文化史和文學史的發展過程中，結合清代的學術背景和社會風氣，結合清代詞學的整體建構，去探討這一類作品的歷史意義、文化意義和文學意義。

12408914.label: Realisation of objectives
12408914.value: 本課題從文學史發展的角度，梳理了回文詞的源流，對宋代至明代的回文詞的創作加以回顧，論述了清代回文詞的發展演變，指出其對前代遺產的傳承，又有了新的突破。這一突破，和清代的社會文化背景密切相關，主要體現在遣詞、造句、謀篇等方面。本課題的主要切入點是清代的回文詞，但也將其視為清詞整體發展的一個組成部分，因此，由於回文詞是雜體詞的一種，從這個角度，發展出對同樣是雜體詞的清代檃栝詞的硏究；由於清代初年出現了非常有特色的顧長發的回文詞圖譜《詩餘圖譜》，從這個角度，發展出對田能村孝憲的《填詞圖譜》的硏究；由於回文詞在乾嘉年間的發展與學人化有一定的聯繫，從這個角度，發展出對乾嘉學派的重要代表人物之一的姚鼐詞學的硏究。這樣，對於回文詞的硏究就不是孤立的，而是和清詞復興的大背景密切結合起來。另外，由於清代回文詞從未有人涉及，分佈零散，查找不易，本課題就閱讀所及，將此類作品初步彙編起來。不過，清詞的文獻尚未得到充分整理，目前只能就已經出版的《全清詞》相關部分加以統計，這一部分以後尚待加強。

12408914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12408914.value: 回文是漢語所特有的一種詞序回環往復的修辭方法，有著獨特的藝術效果。回文詩在晉代以後很盛行，宋詞借鑒了這一方法，至清代，更受到重視。詞是長短句，比起齊言的詩，回文更為困難。清代詞人在這方面，有了更多的發揮。本硏究計劃即在這些方面進行探討，並多向發展，將清詞和清代詞學視為一個整體，涉及檃括詞、姚鼐的詞學觀念以及田能村孝憲的《填詞圖譜》等，在一個大的背景中，思考了清詞和清代詞學的獨特價値。

12500514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12500514.value: 服務型領導和主動性顧客服務表現的關係: 香港酒店業的研究

12500514.label: Project Objectives
12500514.value: to advance theory and practice by developing and empirically testing a new conceptual framework based on social learning theory and the model of proactive motivation - can do, reason to, and energized to - that underlies the relationship between servant leadership and PCSP in the hospitality industry, an important area that is currently absent from the literature; to extend theory on the impacts of servant leadership on service employees’ motivation and active service behavior; to investigate the mediating roles of self-efficacy, felt responsibility, and harmonious passion on the servant leadership-PCSP relationship; and to provide guidance to future research and practice in this important area of hospitality management.

to extend theory on the impacts of servant leadership on service employees’ motivation and active service behavior;
to investigate the mediating roles of self-efficacy, felt responsibility, and harmonious passion on the servant leadership-PCSP relationship; and

12500514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500514.value: Proactive customer service performance (PCSP) is critical to hospitality organizations, especially for hotels competing through customer service excellence strategies. The failure of front-line service employees to act proactively when serving customers may not only adversely affect the quality of service provided but, ultimately, the competitiveness of the organization. However, despite its importance, we know little about how and why front-line service employees may act proactively to satisfy customer service demands and expectations. The proposed study intends to draw on social learning theory and the model of proactive motivation to examine and better understand the implications of servant leadership on employee PCSP in the hotel industry and how such a relationship might be mediated by front-line service employees’ motivational pathways (i.e., self-efficacy, felt obligation, and harmonious passion). Several contributions to theory and practice are intended: (i) we intend to advance the proactive motivation and hospitality management literatures by examining a potentially important antecedent (servant leadership) of PCSP. Although servant leadership has been shown to be more relevant to customer service related behavior than other forms of leadership (Brownell, 2010), an over-emphasis in prior research on the influence of other forms of leadership (Rank et al., 2007) restricts our understanding of how employees might learn from and react to leader behaviors more conducive to the ‘service’ setting (i.e., the hospitality industry). (ii) whereas prior research on servant leadership is mainly based on social exchange and justice perspectives to explain its relational outcomes (e.g., trust, LMX, commitment), such as citizenship behavior (e.g., Liden et al., 2008; Mayer et al., 2008), we intend to add to the servant leadership literature by examining the under-researched area of motivational outcomes (e.g., PCSP) (c.f., van Dierendonck, 2011). (iii) by investigating the potential mediating effects of three motivational pathways, we also intend to shed new light on the mechanisms or underlying process through which servant leadership influences employees’ PCSP. (iv) since few, if any, studies have been conducted in the hospitality context (particularly in Asia), we intend to offer novel insights into a setting which because of its own unique characteristics and operational environment warrants greater attention. In sum, a better understanding of how and why front-line service employees may act proactively to satisfy customer service demands and expectations is therefore not only important to scholars of hospitality management but also to the long-term competitiveness of one of Hong Kong’s pillar industries – the hospitality industry. 主動性顧客服務表現對於酒店業機構非常重要，尤其現時各酒店都希望以出色的顧客服務策略於市場上競爭。若前線的服務員工未能主動地服務顧客，不但會負面地影響服務質素，最終甚至影響到機構的競爭力。即使它的重要性，我們對於員工如何能主動地滿足顧客對服務的需求和期望卻認識不多。本研究是透過主動性動機模型來探索和了解服務型領導行為對酒店業主動性顧客服務表現的影響及對前線員工三種動機相關的路徑 (自我效能，義務感，和熱情) 促成的關係。本研究對理論和實踐作出以下貢獻： 一) 透過探索主動性顧客服務表現的前因 (即服務型領導)，我們推進有關主動性動機模型和酒店業管理的文獻。即使服務型領導相比其他領導方式與顧客服務有相關的影响 (Brownell, 2010)，以往的研究都過分著重其他領導方式的影響，因而限制了我們對員工如何受益於服務型領導的行為的了解。 (二) 過往有關服務型領導的研究主要以交換埋論和公義的觀點來解釋有關人際關係的結果 (如信任、領導成員交換和忠誠)，如組織公民行為 (Liden et al., 2008; Mayer et al., 2008)，我們則嘗試透過探索較少被研究的動力性結果 (即主動性顧客服務表現) (互見參照: van Dierendonck, 2011) 來進一步推動服務型領導的文獻。 (三) 透過深入探討有關三種動力路徑的促進性影響，我們亦嘗試闡明服務型領導如何影響員工的主動性顧客服務表現的機制和過程。 (四) 環境因素是影响員工的顧客服務主動性行為其中重要的因素之一。以往甚少有關研究以酒店業作背景 (特別於亞洲)，本研究提供創新的觀點, 希望學者們逐步關注地方自身的特點和經營環境的重要。 總括來說, 透過深入地探討酒店服務業的前線員工如何主動地滿足顧客的需求和期望, 本研究不但對酒店管理界的學者重要，而且對於香港支柱行業的酒店業的長期競爭力有更深遠的意義。

12501014.value: 工作不安全感對於員工諫言、尋求反饋、政治行爲以及提升領導力等主動行爲的影響

12501014.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12501014.value: Prof Lee, Cynthia Dr Wellman, Ned

12501014.label: Project Objectives
12501014.value: To examine the impact of job insecurity on employee proactive behaviors at the workplace, including promotive and prohibitive voice, feedback seeking, political behavior, and leadership skill development. To examine the moderating effect of proactive personality on the relationships between JI and the four types of employee proactive behaviors.

To examine the moderating effect of proactive personality on the relationships between JI and the four types of employee proactive behaviors.

12501014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501014.value: Job insecurity (JI) has been an extremely relevant topic for academics and practitioners in the past two or three decades due to the fast changing economic situation and workplaces all over the world. Although there are many studies on the effect of JI on employee work attitudes and performances, existing research on how individual employees actively respond to JI is limited. In the proposed study, we aim to examine employees’ behavioral responses to JI and the boundary condition of such effects. We focus particularly on employees’ discretionary behaviors including feedback seeking, voice, political behaviors, and leadership skill development. Drawing on the theory of planned behavior and the research on proactivity, we suggest that JI has an inverted U-shaped curvilinear relationship with promotive voice, a negative relationship with prohibitive voice, a positive relationship with feedback seeking behaviors, a positive relationship with political behaviors, and a negative relationship with employees’ leadership skill development behaviors via individuals’ intention to do these behaviors. We further argue that these effects can be strengthened by individuals’ proactive personality. We conclude by describing a plan to test our model in Chinese organizations. 過去的二、三十年中，全球經濟和就業狀況的巨大變化令業界和學界都對“工作不安全感”這一現象愈來愈重視。現有文獻中儘管已有不少關於工作不安全感對員工態度與績效的影響的研究，但是很少有對於員工感到工作不安全時可能如何主動採取行動的研究。在我們提出的此項研究中，我們關注工作不安全感可能引起的行爲反應，包括員工在工作中的四種自發行爲：諫言、尋求反饋、政治行爲以及主動提升自身領導力的行爲。基於計劃行爲理論以及現有的對員工主動性的研究，我們提出工作不安全感會減少預防性的諫言而與促進性的諫言呈倒U的曲綫關係，會增加員工尋求反饋的行爲以及政治行爲，也會降低員工提升自身領導力的行爲。進一步的，我們認為員工的主動性人格越強，工作不安全感對以上提到的行爲反應的影響會越大。爲了檢驗這些理論假設，我們計劃在一些中國企業進行數據收集和調研。

12501014.label: Realisation of objectives
12501014.value: We have reported the following in the middle term report of this project: “We had focused on literature review, model development and identifying data collection opportunities in the first stage of this project. Based on the reviewers’ comments on our initial proposal and a more comprehensive literature review, we have revised our theorizing about the job insecurity impact proposed in the proposal. A major concern raised by the external reviewers is the overall theoretical framework (the theory of planned behavior) we used to theorize the impact of JI on all the four different types of behaviors. We agree with the comment and have decided to study the impact of job insecurity on the four behaviors separately and develop more specific arguments for the impact of job insecurity on each of the behaviors using more specific and focused theorization, instead of using one general theory (the theory of planned behavior). As a result of this revision and development, we focus on more specific mediating mechanisms and moderators instead of the proactive personality as the single moderator.” Due to the above reasons, this project has generated several studies with different collaborators who have expertise knowledge in the areas of the various proactive behaviors we study. In one study, we focused on the impact of job feature insecurity on employee voice behavior. Specifically, we propose that job insecurity affects voice through increasing employees’ desire for control in the workplace and such effect is conditioned on the individual job situation and supervisor support for voice in the workplace. We have surveyed employees and their managers in multiple companies in south and west China using a three wave longitudinal design. Results supported most of the hypothesized relationships—we found job feature insecurity measured at time 1 influences employees’ desire for control at time 2 which in turn leads to their voice behaviors. Further, the first link is strengthened by individual’s job embeddedness and the second link is strengthened by employee’s perceived supervisor positive response toward voice behaviors. We are now writing up the manuscript for submission to the Journal of Applied Psychology. In another study, we studied how job insecurity influences employee’s proactive behaviors toward their organization and their own career development. This study has been finished and submitted to the Human Resource Management journal. The abstract of our submission says “when people feel insecure in a job position, their attitudes toward the organization and their careers could be affected. To investigate such impacts, we study two different aspects of job insecurity perceptions—insecurity about losing the job and insecurity about losing desired features of the job—and contrast their impact on organization- and career-related outcomes. Borrowing from the research on different foci of employee commitment and proactivity, we propose job loss insecurity drives a psychological focus on the self and thus has a stronger impact on career commitment and pro-career behaviors than job feature insecurity, whereas job feature insecurity drives a focus on the organization and thus has a stronger impact on organizational commitment and proactive behavior toward the organization than job loss insecurity. We further suggest age as an important condition to these effects. Data from two samples in various organizations in China supported our hypotheses.” In the third study, we focused on how job insecurity influences the leadership development behaviors for these who are not in the formal leadership positions. Such informal leadership development behaviors are getting more and more attention in both the practical and the academic fields. We have developed a model in which job insecurity interacts with consideration of future consequences to influence employees’ motivation to lead which in turn determines their leadership development behaviors. We found support using survey data from another project which has measured all the variables in our model. The manuscript has been submitted to the Academy of Management Journal but unfortunately it was rejected after the first round submission. The major concerns raised by the editor and reviewers are related to the theoretical framework (the theory of planned behavior) and the data analysis approach we used. We are revising this study based on the comments we received and plan to submit our revision to the Journal of Applied Psychology. In addition to the above empirical studies, we have finished a review paper on job insecurity published at the Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior. It is a comprehensive review of the growing literature since 2003. In particular, we have highlighted the importance of understanding the role of the fast changing workplace today in influencing individuals’ experience of job insecurity. Studying the relationships between job insecurity and various types of proactive behaviors in the workplace has been emphasized as an important future research direction in the review article. In summary, we have achieved the two objectives proposed in the original proposal and have gone beyond that to conduct empirical studies using more refined theoretical arguments and more appropriate research designs for specific studies. We have also synthesized our knowledge in this area by conducting a literature review study.

12501014.value: Overall, we found support for the impact of job insecurity on employee proactive behaviors. When employees feel insecure in their jobs, they would have various behavioral responses under different conditions. Specifically, employees may voice out more because the sense of insecurity generates a desire to gain control in the workplace but such effects are conditioned on how embedded they are in their jobs and how they perceive their supervisors welcome voices; employees’ proactive behaviors toward the organizations and their own career development may be hurt when they feel their jobs or desired job features are threatened and the effects vary for the younger and older employees; employees’ motivation to develop their leadership potential can also be influenced by job insecurity feelings particularly for these who have a low consideration of future consequences. 12501114.label: Realisation of objectives
12501114.value: The proposed study contributed to the brand love literature by delineating a model of "Shift of Brand Love". It also empirically tested the model, providing evidence that the three proposed antecedents of brand transgression, reduction in brand appeal, and reduction in customer engagement are relevant factors that could reduce Chinese consumers' extent of brand love towards a local brand. 12501114.label: Major findings and research outcome
12501114.value: By examining the shift of brand love from local to foreign brands, the proposed study enriches the existing branding literature by identifying three brand-level factors (i.e., brand transgression, reduced brand appeal and brand engagement) that could exert significant effects on the focal brands' relationship with the consumer. The study also identified a consumer-level factor of self-affirmation that could moderate the proposed main effects though the effects were weak. Thus, future research is needed to examine this and other consumer-level moderating factors. Also, in the process of conducting this study, the researchers gained a better understanding of the consumers' brand love directed at foreign brands and the boundary conditions of that brand love. At the current time, the research has produced a published journal paper and a conference session. The research for the published journal paper does not represent the main findings of this research though the grant has assisted its completion, thus acknowledgement is due. The main findings are indicated in the conference session, a paper under review at Communication Research, and other works in progress. The grant has helped trained a PhD student who would be graduating towards the end of this summer. She has successfully landed a job in academia.

12501114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12501114.value: The study provided empirical evidence of the main effects of three brand-level antecedents to the "shift of brand love". However, the moderating effects of consumer-level factors are weak. Future research could extend further efforts in this area. Specifically, future research can reexamine self-affirmation, the factor examined in this study, but provide a stronger manipulation. Future research can also examine other consumer-level factors such as the consumers' changing-self (e.g., as a result of social-economic changes) that could moderate the effects of brand-level factors on shift of brand love. Though it is not an intended area of study, the proposed research did help the researchers gain a better understanding of the Chinese consumers' brand love towards foreign brands. This would be another area of potential future research.

12501114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12501114.value: Using Chinese consumers' views towards local and foreign brands, the proposed study provided a better understanding of the factors that could contribute to a shift in the consumers' love towards a local brand as well as the boundary conditions that could limit (and reduce) this emotive state. The factors that may reduce brand love include brand transgression (e.g., faulty products such as tainted milk), reduced brand appeal and reduced brand engagement, the latter of which may take place when a brand manager cuts back expenses. The study also identified that the consumers' value set has potential effects in changing this relationship. That is, if a consumer is using a local brand to affirm who he/she is, then changes in brand-level factors (e.g., brand transgression) has less of an adverse effect in reducing the consumer's love towards the brand.

12501414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501414.value: Stock returns are positively related to the ratio of a firm's book value of common equity to its market value. The well-known effect is pervasive in stock markets around the world. Investment strategies based on the phenomenon provide substantial profits, around 8% over the first year of holding and up to 30% over a three-year horizon. This has challenged the notion of market efficiency in traditional finance theory and has been under debate among financial economists for more than two decades. The current literature has provided various different and seemingly opposing arguments but individually supportive evidence to this phenomenon. We provide and examine a unified explanation, specifically a mechanism involving extrapolative corporate growth expectation and style investing focusing on growth, to address the main driving force of the book-to-market effect and simultaneously reconcile and synthesize the set of empirical findings being recently documented. We expect to document that (1) the book-to-market effect or the class of positive relations between stock returns and similar valuation ratios is strong (weak) when total asset growth subsequently reverses (persists); (2) firm attributes that have been shown to be related to the book-to-market equity or related valuation ratio and systematic risks essentially contain information about future asset growth (3) limits to arbitrage are endogenously associated with uncertainty in growth dynamics; and (4) the effect is stronger when growth is ex-ante predicted to subsequently reverse more. 股票收益率呈顯著正相關的一家公司的權益帳面價值的常用比例 對它的市場價值。知名的作用是在各地的股市無處不在 世界。基於這一現象的投資策略提供巨大的利潤， 在第一年的控股和達 8%左右三年地平線超過 30%。這 在傳統的金融理論中的市場效率的概念提出了挑戰和已 以上兩個幾十年已經下金融經濟學家之間的辯論。當前 文學提供了各種不同的、 看似對立論點，但 對這一現象的單獨支援性證據。我們提供和審查統一 具體涉及控制點的企業成長機制的解釋 期待與風格投資側重于經濟增長，要解決的主要驅動力 圖書市場影響和同時調和和合成的集 實證研究結果最近被記錄。我們期望文檔，（1） 用盡- 市場效應或任何類別的股票收益率與類似的積極關係 估值比率是強 （弱） 當總資產增長隨後逆轉 （存在） ；(2) 堅定的特性，已被證明與有關的圖書市場 股權或相關的估值比率和系統性風險本質上包含的資訊 關於未來資產增長 （3） 限制套利是與內在關聯 不確定性增長動力學 ；(4) 效果越強，當經濟增長是事前 預計隨後逆轉更多。

12502314.label: Project Objectives
12502314.value: To examine whether and how reputed non-CEO inside directors on the board affect the existence of internal control weaknesses (ICWs) under SOX Section 404; To examine whether the effect of reputed non-CEO inside directors is conditioned upon the type of ICWs, i.e., company-level versus account-level ICWs.

To examine whether the effect of reputed non-CEO inside directors is conditioned upon the type of ICWs, i.e., company-level versus account-level ICWs.

12502314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502314.value: The proposed research aims to provide systematic evidence on the impact of non-CEO inside directors on a company’s internal control over financial reporting. Internal control over financial reporting is “a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company's board of directors, management, and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with GAAP” (PCAOB 2007). Internal control effectiveness is an important indicator of financial reporting quality and has become a topical issue after a number of accounting scandals and the subsequent passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) of 2002. Inside directors are firm managers that sit on the board of directors. There are two conflicting views on the role of inside directors. Conventional agency theory suggests that inside directors are dependent on the CEO for their continued employment, compensation, and private benefits. In contrast, efficient contracting theory suggests that if properly motivated, non-CEO inside directors can use their valuable firm-specific information to improve the communication between firm management and outside investors and the monitoring of CEOs. Given the above conflicting views, the proposed research intends to provide evidence on two interrelated issues: (1) whether and how reputed non-CEO inside directors (RIDs) affect the existence of internal control weaknesses (ICWs); (2) whether the effect of RIDs is conditioned upon the type of ICWs, i.e., company-level versus account-level ICWs. The proposed research hopes to contribute to the literature in several ways. First, the proposed research will add to the studies examining the determinants of internal control effectiveness. As the reputation concern is an implicit incentive for board directors to effectively perform their duties, it is worthwhile to investigate whether and how RIDs can affect a company’s internal controls. Second, although theoretical research has explored the role of inside directors from several perspectives, there is sparse empirical evidence. The propose research thus contributes to the growing literature by providing new evidence in this area. Third, the proposed research will have policy implications for regulators. The governance reforms mandated by the SOX recommend greater outside representation on the board, but pay little attention to the value of inside directors. In this sense, the proposed research sheds light on the future governance reforms.

12502314.label: Realisation of objectives
12502314.value: The literature suggests two conflicting views on non-CEO inside directors who are also members of a firm’s management team. Conventional agency theory literature (Mace 1986; Warther 1998; Malmendier and Tate 2009) suggests that inside directors rely on the CEO for their continued employment and compensation, and are therefore less likely to challenge CEO decisions. Inside directors may actually prefer an ineffective internal control system, where they and other senior managers can exercise more discretion when pursuing self-utilities, due to the lack of formal and effective control policies and procedures (Hogan and Wilkins 2008). Inside directors can in this case be related to poor governance and ineffective internal control (Larcker et al. 2007). The efficient contracting theory (Kaplan and Reishus 1990; Fama and Jensen 1983; Holmstrom 1999; Raheja 2005; Adams and Ferreira 2007; Drymiotes 2007; Harris and Raviv 2008), however, suggests that properly motivated non-CEO inside directors can use their valuable firm-specific information to improve the communication between firm management and outside investors and strengthen monitoring the CEOs. Reputable inside directors can impact a firm’s internal control effectiveness in three related ways. First, directors may lose their board seats in their own and other companies after the firms experience financial distress, perform poorly, restate earnings, or are involved in financial fraud lawsuits (Gilson 1990; Yermack 2004; Fich and Shivdasani 2007; Ertimur et al. 2012). The reporting of ICWs under SOX 404 can act as a direct signal of problematic financial reporting and high information risk, and may hurt the reputation of directors in the managerial labor market and limit their future directorship opportunities. Therefore, reputable inside directors have the incentive to oversee a firm’s internal control system. Second, in firms with reputable inside directors, CEOs face stronger monitoring and replacement pressure. These directors are less likely to simply follow CEOs’ problematic decisions on financial reporting and are more willing to share information with other board members and outside investors (e.g., Raheja 2005; Harris and Raviv 2008; Masulis and Mobbs 2011). The CEOs then face more effective monitoring by the board and outside investors. The enhanced reputation increases the likelihood that inside directors will replace the current CEO (Masulis and Mobbs 2011; Mobbs 2012). This replacement pressure can reduce the entrenchment behavior of CEOs and motivate incumbent CEOs to improve overall firm performance, and particularly the internal controls over financial reporting. Third, compared to independent directors, inside directors usually hold significant operating positions (e.g., president, chief operating officer, or chief financial officer) and thus possess better operational knowledge and more firm-specific information (e.g., Masulis and Mobbs 2011; Mobbs 2013). Equipped with strong financial and operating management skills, inside directors are able to monitor and improve a firm’s internal control. To provide empirical evidence on this issue, we first test the following hypothesis on the positive effect of reputable inside directors: H1: Firms with reputable inside directors are less likely to have ICWs, all else being equal. Not all internal control weaknesses have the same nature and potential severity. Moody’s Investors Service (2004, 2006, and 2007) classifies internal control weaknesses into two categories, account-level weaknesses (Category A) and company-level weaknesses (Category B). Account-level ICWs refer to controls over specific account balances or transaction-level processes, while company-level ICWs relate to the overall control environment or financial reporting process (inadequate disclosure controls, ineffective audit committee or internal audit function, lack of senior management competency and philosophy, ineffective personnel policy, and conflict of duties. Moody’s Investors Service (2006 and 2007) argues that the inability to complete the Section 404 report itself is a company-level ICW. Thus, we view firms that do not finish ICW reports as having a company-level ICW. Internal control literature has shown that account-level and company-level ICWs have different impact. Kim et al. (2011) find that borrowers with company-level ICWs pay significantly higher loan interest rates than borrowers with account-level ICWs. Hoitash et al. (2012) report that account-specific ICWs, as opposed to company-wide ICWs, drive the effects of ICWs on CFO compensation, which highlights the importance of CFO-specific job responsibilities on account-level control issues. Since non-CEO inside directors (e.g., CFOs) are mainly responsible for corporate decisions involving more specialized judgment like account classification or related party transaction issues, we expect that reputable inside directors can more expertly monitor a company’s account-level internal control than company-level internal controls. This leads to the second hypothesis: H2: The association between inside director reputation and ICWs is more pronounced for account-level ICWs than for company-level ICWs. We construct the following model to empirically investigate the impact of inside director reputation on the effectiveness of internal control systems: ICW = α0 + α1RID + α2 Governance Controls+α5 Other Firm-specific Controls + Industry Indicators + Year Indicators + error The dependent variable ICW is an indicator variable that equals one if the external auditor’s annual SOX 404 report concludes that the company’s internal control over financial reporting is ineffective, and zero otherwise. The test variable RID is measured using the presence and the percentage of non-CEO inside directors holding at least one outside directorship. We include a large set of control variables in the model. First, we control for the following variables related to board strength: percentage of independent directors (Indep%), board size (BoardSize), board member age (BoardAge), an indicator for busy directors (Busy), independent director quality (IndepRepu), analyst following (Analyst), and an indicator for audit quality (Big4). Indep% is the percentage of independent directors on the board. BoardSize is the natural log of the number of directors on the board. BoardAge is the natural log of the average age of the directors. Busy equals one if the firm has a non-CEO inside director with three or more outside board appointments in unaffiliated firms, and zero otherwise. IndepRepu is the average number of outside board seats held by the independent directors. Analyst is the natural log of the number of financial analysts following a company, and Big4 is an indicator variable for audit quality that equals one if a company is audited by a Big 4 audit firm (Hoitash et al. 2009). Next, we include a series of firm-specific control variables that are considered to be the inducement of ICWs (e.g., Ashbaugh-Skaife et al. 2007; Doyle et al. 2007; Hoitash et al. 2009; Bedard et al. 2014): firm size (FirmSize), financial leverage (Leverage), foreign operations (Foreign), prior financial statement restatement (Restatement), profitability (Loss), sales growth (SaleGrowth), organizational change (Restructure), acquisition (Acquisition), and inventory level (Inventory). Industry and year indicators are included in the model to control for the potential difference in internal control effectiveness across industries and over years. We estimate Eq. (1) using the probit procedure. H1 predicts the estimated coefficient α1 to be negative, which supports the positive effect of inside director reputation. However, if the reputation effect of inside directors weakens board monitoring and increases executives’ entrenchment, as suggested in the conventional agency theory, the estimated coefficient α1 will be positive. To test H2, we estimate Eq. (1) using CompanyICW and AccountICW as the dependent variables, respectively. H2 can be supported if the estimation results show the inside director reputation has stronger incremental effect on AccountICW than CompanyICW.

12502314.label: Major findings and research outcome
12502314.value: Using a large sample of 7,352 firm-year observations from 2004 to 2012, our study shows that firms with more reputable inside directors (RIDs) are less likely to have reported internal control weaknesses (ICWs). Consistent with the efficient contracting theory (Fama and Jensen 1983) and the reputation formation theory (Holmstrom 1999), this finding suggests that reputation concerns can motivate inside directors to fulfill their responsibilities in maintaining effective internal controls and high quality financial reporting. We also find that RIDs help improve a firm’s internal control effectiveness only when they are not connected with the CEO. This reflects the view that directors’ connection to their CEO weakens their monitoring role on the board (Bruynseels and Cardinaels 2014; Coles et al. 2014; Fracassi and Tate 2012; Khanna et al. 2015; Krishnan et al. 2011). The study also finds that reputable inside directors have a more pervasive impact on account-level ICWs than company-level ICWs. This result is consistent with Hoitash et al. (2012)’s finding that inside executives are mainly responsible for corporate decisions involving more specialized judgment like account- or transaction-level issues. We further investigates the effect of cost of misreporting on the association between RIDs and ICWs, and find that it is more pronounced for firms with higher costs of misreporting. In another research paper, we examine the impact of reputable inside directors on bank loan contracting using a sample of 5,104 loans. After controlling for borrower-specific, loan-specific, and economy-wide characteristics, we find that loans to borrowers with RIDs have lower interest rates, include fewer restrictive covenants, and are less likely to be secured by collateral, compared to loans to borrower without RIDs. These findings suggest that RIDs help borrowers to reduce agency and information risk, thus leading to more favorable loan contracting terms. In light of growing literature on the important role played by CFOs (e.g., Chava and Purnanandam 2010; Jiang et al. 2010; Feng et al. 2011; Kim et al. 2011a; Mergenthaler et al. 2012), we separately examine the effect of reputable CFO directors (RCFOs) and other inside directors (ROTHERs) in bank loan contracting. Our results show that both RCFOs and ROTHERs have a favorable effect on loan spread and collateral requirements, while ROTHERs have a more significant effect on financial covenants than RCFOs. Our analysis also shows that the favorable effect of RIDs on various loan terms is more significant for borrowers without prior lending relationships with the lenders.

12502314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12502314.value: A stream of literature examines the connectedness (social ties) between board directors and CEOs/outside stakeholders. Fracassi and Tate (2012) identify external network connections between directors and CEOs, and find that firm value is reduced and value-destroying acquisitions increase in firms with CEO-director connectedness. Their findings suggest that directors’ network ties with CEOs weaken board monitoring. Coles et al. (2014) argue that CEO-nominated directors have stronger allegiances to the CEO, and thus are weak monitors. They find lower turnover-performance sensitivity and pay-performance sensitivity for firms with a higher proportion of directors appointed during the CEO’s tenure. Khanna et al. (2015) find that the connections CEO develop with senior executives and directors through appointment decisions increase the risk of corporate fraud. The above findings suggest that the connectedness between RIDs and the CEO may have an effect on whether and how RIDs monitor the CEO, advise the board on important firm decisions, and work for the shareholders’ best interests. Thus, we are trying to further our current study by investigating whether the effect of RIDs on ICWs is conditional on the connectedness between RIDs and the CEO.

12502314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12502314.value: Our research project investigates whether reputable non-CEO inside directors (RIDs) affect the effectiveness of a firm’s internal control over financial reporting. Internal control has become a topical issue after a number of accounting scandals (e.g., Enron, WorldCom, Qwest, etc.) and the subsequent passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (hereafter, SOX). Although previous studies emphasize the importance of outside or independent directors in corporate governance, little empirical evidence supports the role of non-CEO inside directors with respect to governance-related decisions and financial reporting. Using a large sample of 7,352 firm-year observations from 2004 to 2012, we find that firms with RIDs are less likely to report internal control weaknesses (ICWs). We also find that RIDs have a more pervasive impact on account-level ICWs than company-level ICWs. Empirical results also demonstrate that the association between RIDs and ICWs is more pronounced for firms with lower audit quality, higher CEO entrenchment, and higher cost of misreporting. This project contributes to the literature examining the determinants of internal control effectiveness, provides new insight into the value of inside directors, and has policy implications for governance reforms.

12502414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502414.value: The previous literature on bribery can be classified in three streams. The first stream has focused on measuring bribery at the country level, its determinants, and its impact on the country’s economic development. This literature measures bribery indirectly, by relying on questionnaires or indices of corruption perceptions at the country-level. The second stream analyzes firm-level data from surveys to determine how much firms pay as bribes, and what determines the size of bribes. Finally, the third - and smallest - stream of literature uses firm-level data derived from actual bribery incidents and focuses on the date of the revelation of the bribery. The current study belongs to the third stream. Although bribery is likely to be a manifestation of poor corporate governance, there is no study that has examined the relationship between corporate governance and bribery. Managers may actively pursue (or turn a blind eye to) bribery by their subordinates, in the hope that they may reap the benefits of better firm performance, without facing personal cost if the bribery is revealed. We plan to use data from real bribery incidents worldwide. Our research has three objectives. First, when the bribe was paid, we plan to compare the corporate governance of bribing firms with that of the remaining firms in the same market that have not been detected bribing. Corporate governance characteristics of interest are the composition of the board of directors, and the presence of large shareholders, especially institutional investors that may monitor managers. Second, and most importantly, we plan to examine whether there are changes in corporate governance following the revelation of the bribery. Do CEOs lose their jobs? Are there changes in the composition of the board of directors? Do institutional investors sell the shares of companies that have behaved unethically? If top management do not face penalties, it may be an optimal strategy for them to turn a blind eye on their subordinates who pay bribes. Finally, we will examine what determines whether there are such changes or not? Anecdotal evidence suggests that CEOs do not always lose their jobs following the revelation of bribery. For example, in the early 1990s, an Israeli general went to jail for receiving bribes by the U.S. firm General Electric (GE) for military jet aircraft engine contracts. The CEO of GE Jack Welch was not replaced. What determines whether the CEO loses the job or not? 對企業賄賂的故有研究可分為三類。第一類以地域(國家)作為研究層面，着重研究企業 賄賂的誘因及對整個國家(地域)經濟體系的影響。但由於該類研究通常以問卷形式或受訪者對國家(地域)的清廉之主觀評分作為基礎，所得出的賄賂測量與鑑定可謂間接；第二類則以企業作為研究層面，以調查所得的數據及其它資料估計企業已支付出的賄款，並分析影響賄款多寡的因素。第三類的研究(亦為本文所屬之類)比較少見：該類研究亦以企業作為研究層面，但樣本依據為發現賄賂案件後所得的企業資料，而且揭發賄賂案件的日期亦為重要的研究對象。 本文中心論點有二：第一，企業賄賂的出現是企業管治不善的結果；第二，管理層有機會主動與下屬合作行賄(或故意放縱下屬進行賄賂)，從而透過因行賄而衍生出來的正面財務業積(評價)而獲取私利，並且毋須忌諱一旦行賄被發現後之個人損失。 為證實論點，本文將由三大方向蒐集論據。第一，就世界各地已證實有涉及(進行)賄賂的企業中，本文將以其企業管治特點(例如：董事局架構、企業持股結構有否大股東或機構投資者)與相應市場上沒有行賄紀錄的企業進行比較：第二，本文將觀察企業一旦被證實有涉及(進行)賄賂後，該企業有否出現(相應的)企業管治變化(例如：行政總裁的人事變動、董事局的人事變動、機構投資者的持股量變動)。假如高級管理層沒有因企業涉及(進行)賄賂而備受處分，這或意味着高級管理層將會或經而放縱(姑息)行賄的下屬。第三，本文將分析上述企業管治變化之決定因素。有證據顯示，行政總裁或不會因企業證實出現賄賂案件而被辭退。例如在九十年代初 ，美國通用電氣公司 (General Electric)被揭發在有關軍用戰機引擎的合約中行賄。雖然收受賄款之以色列將令被判監禁，可是當時美國通用電氣公司的行政總裁 Jack Wekch 沒有被辭退。顯然，當中必定有某些因素影響企業賄賂與企業管治調整的關係。

12502514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502514.value: Does telling your customer that your product now contains fewer bad materials negatively affect their view of your product? In many situations, manufacturers cannot completely eliminate the perceived negative qualities of a product, due to the nature of the product, technical limitations, or time constraints in a highly competitive environment. Therefore, when manufacturers manage to partly improve a product by reducing its negative qualities, they might choose to advertise the new product as having “less of a negative attribute,”— this is called “partially reduced negativity” product information. For instance, in response to the widespread perception that a high sugar content adversely affects the healthiness of a product, many packaged lemon tea manufacturers in Hong Kong launched reduced sugar versions several years ago. For example, Vitasoy launched the VITA Low Sugar Lemon Tea in 2007. Communicating new information normally costs millions of dollars, but does telling consumers that the product is now “less bad” really benefit sales? One real market case suggests otherwise. In 2010, Coca-Cola marketers of Bonaqua water advertised in Hong Kong that the new 500 mL Bonaqua lightweight packaging could reduce plastic use by 34% (Coca-Cola Company 2010). However, when this message was communicated to consumers, many consumers have negative attitudes towards the product which finally negatively impact on Bonaqua sales. In this research, we examine whether a commonly used marketing strategy (i.e., communicating a “partially reduced negativity” product attribute) may reduce product sales in certain situations, but not in the others. According to the incremental-versus-entity theory of self-developed by Carol Dweck and her colleagues (1983; 1995), people have either an “incremental” or “entity” belief about changes in human nature, abilities, personalities, etc. We make an analogous distinction in people’s attitudes toward product performance. Specifically, we propose that incremental theorists will be attuned to incremental changes in a quality and will therefore react to the improved product positively, whereas entity theorists may see the partially reduced negativity information as a reminder of the immutable negative attribute and this will result in reduced willingness to purchase the produce. Moreover, we expect that processing fluency will mediate the effects of incremental-versus-entity belief on product evaluation. We will collect real market data to support our arguments in the pilot study, and four studies were further proposed to test our propositions. 當你告訴顧客你的產品現在包含更少不良原料時，會令他們對產品的看法產生負面影響嗎？由於受到產品本質局限、技術限制或因競爭激烈所致的時間限制，生產商在許多情況下根本無法完全消除產品的負面感知特質。因此，當生產商設法透過減少產品的負面特質來在一定程度上改進產品，他們可能選擇以「較少負屬性」來為新產品作宣傳，而這就是所謂的「部分減少的負面性」產品信息。舉例來說，有鑑於市場上廣泛流傳含糖量高的食品會對健康構成不良影響，多間香港包裝檸檬茶生產商在幾年前均開始推出低糖版本，如：維他奶國際集團有限公司於2007年推出了維他低糖檸檬茶。在市場上傳播新信息通常花費數百萬金錢，但告訴消費者該產品現在比以往較少「壞處」真正能令銷售受益嗎？一個真實的市場個案對此作出否定。可口可樂公司於2010年在香港營銷「飛雪」(Bonaqua) 礦物質水時，以全新500毫升「輕量樽」作宣傳，聲稱新包裝比之往節省34%塑膠原材料。然而，當這個消息傳達到消費者時，很多消費者都對「飛雪」持負面態度，而這亦最終為「飛雪」的銷售帶來了負面的影響 (可口可樂公司 2010)。 在這個研究中，我們研究一種常用的營銷策略(即傳達「部分減少的負面性」的產品特性)會否在某些特定的情況下減少產品的銷售。根據國外學者Dweck和她的研究團隊(1983;1995) 所提出的增長理論 (incremental theory) 和相對的固定理論(entity theory)，人對於本性、能力和性格的變化持有增長理論的看法或是固定理論的看法。而人對於產品性能的態度也有著類似的區分。具體而言，我們提出支持增長理論的人能理解增量變化的質量從而對已改進的產品作出正面的反應；而支持固定理論的人也許視「部分減少的負面性」的產品信息為一個提醒，令他們回憶永遠不變的負面特性，而導致降低購買產品的意欲。此外，我們預計在增長理論的看法與固定理論的看法相比所引致不同的產品評價，處理訊息的流暢度會有著中介效果。我們將從先導性研究收集實質的市場數據來支持我們的論點，然後進行4組實驗室研究來檢驗我們提出的論點。

12502514.label: Realisation of objectives
12502514.value: By focusing on the marketing communication strategies for products with partially reduced negative attributes, our findings offer novel evidence and provide plausible explanations for why consumers' implicit theory orientation determines their interpretations and reactions to these strategies. In this paper, we present converging evidence across five studies, showing that the communication of partially reduced negative product information leads to more (less) favorable product evaluations among incremental (entity) theorists. This effect held when implicit theories were manipulated or assessed and when the reduced negativity information was presented using absolute values, percentages, and general expressions. Using measurement-of-mediation and moderation-of-process designs, we further showed that the distinct interpretations of the reduced negative information among incremental and entity theorists contributed to the effect. In our field study, we generalized our findings from the product evaluations of a fictitious product to behavioral choice concerning a real product. Finally, we demonstrated the managerial significance of the effect by showing that marketers can situationally invoke consumers' implicit theory orientation and hence influence reactions towards reduced negativity communication. This paper contributes to the marketing communication literature by focusing on the communication of partially reduced negative product information, which is a pervasively used yet under-researched marketing strategy. The literature on the influence of changing negative product attributes focuses primarily on the complete removal or addition of a negative attribute (e.g., Houston and Sherman 1995). Unlike the previous work on such qualitative changes in undesirable attributes, our paper explores whether the partial removal of a negative attribute, a kind of quantitative change, influences consumers' responses through a quite different mechanism (Shaffer and Kipp 2014). We proposed and showed that the information on a partial reduction in a negative product attribute contains two conceptually distinct components (i.e., a trend component and an end state component) that may exert opposing influences on consumer evaluations. We hope that our conceptualization of partially reduced product negativity will encourage future research to further investigate the consequences of communicating the quantitative change in a product's attribute. We also enrich the repertoire of the cognitive consequences associated with implicit beliefs in the context of reduced product negativity by showing that incremental theorists and entity theorists interpret such communications differently. Specifically, while incremental theorists rely on trend-based interpretation (which stresses an improvement in the negative feature), entity theorists form end-state-based interpretation (which stresses the existence of the negative nature of the attribute) when responding to information containing reduced negativity. Thus, the current study advances our understanding of the mechanism by which partially reduced negativity communication of products can lead to consumers' contrasting interpretations and responses. In addition, although we differentiated and examined the trend versus end state information component in the context of partially reduced negativity communication, we believe that the two components can be applied to much broader contexts. From the perspective of Kahneman and Tversky's (1979) utility function, the trend component indicates the direction of the change in utility of an attribute, whereas the end state component represents the absolute utility value in the final state. Accordingly, any utility change that occurs at either the attribute-level or product-level will involve both a trend component and an end state component. Although we conducted a pioneering study of how people's perceptions of the two components differ under different implicit beliefs, future studies can extend this line of research by investigating whether the distinct processing styles aroused by incremental versus entity belief can be replicated under the various situations that involve utility changes. For example, the question remains as to whether incremental theorists and entity theorists interpret increased positivity communications differently. In this case, because both the trend-based and end-state-based interpretations have positive implications for such communications, entity theorists might respond positively. Because implicit theories are fundamental beliefs that affect various types of judgement and decision-making, we believe that this line of research will have extensive marketing implications. Our findings also contribute to the research on the attribute-framing effect (e.g., Cesario, Corker, and Jelinek 2013). The existing studies have defined attribute framing in either positive terms (e.g., % leanness of a food product; % correct in a test) or negative terms (e.g., % fat in a food product; % incorrect in a test). For example, Levin and Gaeth (1988) found that positive (negative) attribute framing tended to evoke positive (negative) associations, which resulted in more favorable responses to positive attribute framing. Our findings contribute to this line of research by identifying a novel framing effect for reduced negativity attributes. Specifically, we found that a key difference between the two types of verbal framing of a reduced negativity attribute (i.e., "reducing frame" and "remaining frame") is the emphasis of the trend of improvement in the reducing form but not in the remaining form. However, some boundary conditions must be acknowledged when applying our findings to marketing practices. For example, if McDonald's reduced the calories in a Big Mac from 563 to 400, incremental theorists could respond negatively due to concerns about taste. That is, the basic effect documented in this paper may not hold when the negative attribute is correlated with a positive benefit. Another boundary condition concerns the nature of the negative attributes, which may vary across different product categories. It may be the case that a company reduces the negativity of an attribute but the amount left either is still considerably large or even a small trace of the negativity has terrible consequences. In such cases, the mere presence of reduced negativity information may be sufficient to result in unfavorable evaluations, which may be true even for incremental theorists. Our findings reported herein are thought provoking in their own right. They suggest that, for example, when negative attributes (e.g., environmentally unfriendly materials in packaging) are only partially reduced, not all types of communication efforts lead to a better outcome as opposed to saying nothing. These implications are conceptually consistent with previous findings that although advertising benefits sales in general, marketing communications should effectively convey the key points (e.g., McAlister et al. 2016). Although incremental theorists are likely to embrace a product with a partially reduced negative attribute, entity theorists may view the reduced negativity communication as a reminder of that negative attribute, and thus are less likely to purchase the product. In other words, the relationship between a reduction in the degree of product negativity and consumers' willingness to purchase the product is non-linear. Given the very high cost of marketing campaigns, the current research has important managerial implications for marketing communication practices. For incremental theorists, marketers may wish to communicate the partially reduced negative attribute of a product. In contrast, entity theorists may embrace the reduced negativity product communication only when they have been situationally primed according to the incremental theory (e.g., through a marketing mix, such as the use of slogans in advertisements). In addition, research has suggested that individuals in Western cultures (e.g., American) typically hold entity beliefs, whereas those in Eastern cultures (e.g., Asian) typically hold incremental beliefs (Church et al. 2003, 2005). Thus, an important managerial implication of our findings is that the promotion strategies for products with partially reduced negative attributes need to be customized across cultures.

12502514.label: Major findings and research outcome
12502514.value: Across four experiments and one field study, the authors found that consumers' responses to such communications depend on their implicit theories regarding their general views of whether traits and abilities are fixed or malleable. Incremental theorists tend to interpret such communications based on the trend of improvement, resulting in more positive responses than no communication. Entity theorists, in contrast, interpret such communications based on the undesirable end state of the attribute (i.e., the negativity is not totally eliminated); thus, they evaluate the product less favorably than no communication. The proposed effect diminishes when "partially reducing negativity" is reframed as "partially remaining negativity," which makes the existence of negativity more salient than the trend of improvement. These findings advance understandings of the effects of partially reduced negativity communication among consumers with different implicit theories and provide marketing implications for managers concerning when, how, and to whom to convey such communications.
