12502714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502714.value: Family business groups play an important role in East Asian emerging markets. Controlling families are inclined to transfer resources among member firms to maximize their interests. However, their intragroup value transfers may normally impair the interests of the minority shareholders of member firms from which resources are siphoned off. Effective audits could credibly increase a firm’s information transparency and thus increase the likelihood of expropriations by insiders to be detected by outsiders. However, the controlling families could take a ‘divide and conquer’ strategy by hiring different auditors rather than a single auditor for different member firms to weaken the auditor’s disciplining role over their expropriation of member firms’ resources. First, the multiple-auditor appointment might deny each involved auditor from obtaining complete knowledge of intragroup connections and full understanding of resultant value implications for affected member firms, which would weaken the auditor’s ability to detect the controlling families’ endeavors to mask their opportunistic intragroup transactions. Second, the use of multiple auditors provides the controlling families an extra opportunity of opinion shopping for a favorable treatment, which might ex ant endanger auditor independence. Third, the multiple-auditor appointment might intensify competition pressures among auditors to retain clients, which may compromise auditor independence. Using a sample of family business groups from four East Asian markets (e.g., Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore, and Taiwan), this study attempts to investigate 1) whether the propensity of controlling families to hire multiple auditors grows with the agency problem inherent in their groups’ ownership structure, and 2) whether the multiple-auditor appointment is accompanied with a higher degree of intragroup value transfers. Following prior literature, this study will use two measures to capture the intragroup value transfers. One is related party transactions undertaken by a family business group. The other is the valuation implication of earnings news released by member firms for their non-announcing group peers. Earnings news released by member firms serves as a good indicator to signal resources available to be transferred to their group peers. This study will add to auditing literature by revealing the effect of multiple-auditor appointment by family business groups on the governance role of external auditors. Meanwhile, this study will contribute to family business group literature by providing evidence that controlling families could strategically use multiple-auditor appointment to facilitate their intragroup value transferring activities. This study will also provide implications for regulators to improve the protection of minority shareholders.

12502714.label: Realisation of objectives
12502714.value: With the financial support of the RGC fund, we collected a sample of family business groups (FBGs thereafter) that control at least two listed member firms in three East Asian economies: Hong Kong, Singapore, and Taiwan, during the period 2003-2012. Specifically, we identify FBGs and their listed member firms from Hong Kong and Singapore by manually collecting ownership data from annual reports of all firms listed on Hong Kong Stock Exchange (Main Board) and Singapore Exchange, and then grouping listed firms that share the same ultimate controlling owner. Regarding the sample of Taiwan FBGs and their listed firms, we initially obtain data from the Group Enterprises database maintained by China Credit Information Services (CCIS) and then verify the group membership by the ownership information that we manually collect from annual reports. Initially, we obtained 171 member firms affiliated to 59 FBGs in Hong Kong, 67 member firms affiliated to 24 FBGs in Singapore, and 142 member firms affiliated to 38 FBGs in Taiwan. We imposed different screening requirements upon final sample selection depending on the specific research questions and conducted respective empirical tests to achieve the proposed objectives (the detailed information please refer to the output manuscript of this research). We summarize as follows how and to what extent our research objectives have been achieved. 1. The objective: Examine whether market perceives family business groups with multiple auditors as undertaking more intragroup value transfers. To achieve this objective, we follow Bae, Cheon, and Kang (2008) and take advantage of stock price reactions of non-announcing member firms to earnings news released by other member firms within the same FBGs to capture market perception of intragroup value transfer potentials. Based on a sample of 966 earnings announcements involving 262 member firms affiliated to 87 FBGs from the three economies, our empirical tests show that the positive stock price reactions of non-announcing member firms to the earnings news released by their group peers are more pronounced when their FBGs hire multiple auditors (especially engaging non-Big auditor) rather than one single auditor. These results are consistent with the conjecture that the controlling families exploit the multiple-auditor appointment as ‘divide and conquer’ strategy to weaken auditor monitoring and facilitate undertaking more intragroup value transfers. 2. The objective: Examine whether the levels of related party transactions are higher within family business groups with multiple auditors versus one single auditor. To achieve this objective, we manually collect data on the related party transactions (RPTs thereafter) undertaken by FBGs in Hong Kong. We fail to access data on RPTs for the sample FBGs in Singapore and Taiwan because of no publicly available dataset in these two economies. Based on a final sample of 566 group-year observations involving 458 RPT announcements made by 131 member firms affiliated to 59 FBGs in Hong Kong, our empirical tests show that FBGs that hire multiple auditors (especially engaging non-Big auditor) tend to more frequently conduct RPTs than FBGs that hire a single common auditor. Further analyses reveal that the two consecutive RPTs undertaken by different two member firms within FBGs are more likely to be in opposite direction when the two member firms are audited by different auditors. In sum, our empirical analyses on RPTs support that FBGs with multiple auditors are inclined to conduct a higher level of RPTs to transfer value among their member firms than FBGs with a single common auditor. 3. The objective: Investigate the incentives of family business groups to hire multiple auditors. Our empirical analyses both on stock price reactions and on RPTs suggest that the multiple-auditor appointment undermines the effectiveness of auditor monitoring and facilitates the intragroup value transfers within FBGs. Extant theory posits that business groups with higher agency problems have greater incentives to undertake opportunistic value transfer activities. Following prior literature, we use the wedge between control rights and cash flow rights owned by the controlling families to capture the agency conflict between the controlling families and minority shareholders. Our empirical analyses show that FBGs with a larger wedge between control rights and cash flow rights owned by the controlling families are more likely to hire multiple auditors. These findings support that FBGs with higher agency problems have greater incentives to hire multiple auditors and reduce the auditor's monitoring over their opportunistic intragroup value transfer activities. 4. The objective: Provide implications for regulators and investors about corporate governance issues within family business groups Our empirical analyses, combined together, suggest that FBGs can exploit the multiple-auditor appointment as a ‘divide and conquer’ strategy to weaken the monitoring role of external auditors and thus facilitate their intragroup value transfers that could impair the interests of minority shareholders. The regulators with mission to protect outside investors should consider whether certain actions are necessary to address FBGs’ opportunistic auditor appointment strategy. For example, the regulators can list the single-auditor appointment by FBGs as one of recommended best practices in corporate governance codes and take the ‘comply or explain’ approach to ensure the governance role of external auditors in constraining the controlling families’ opportunistic intragroup value transfers. The average investors better take into account the auditor appointment strategy adopted by FBGs when evaluating corporate governance practices of their member firms. The average investors should pay special attention to the controlling families’ propensity to undertake intragroup value transfer if FBGs hire multiple auditors.

12502714.label: Major findings and research outcome
12502714.value: Based on a sample of firms affiliated to family business groups in three East Asian economies: Hong Kong, Singapore, and Taiwan, this research focuses on the auditor appointment strategy within family business groups and documents several findings as follows: (1) the stock market perceives that family business groups that hire different auditors (especially engaging non-Big 4 auditor) to audit different member firms are more likely to undertake intragroup value transfer activities, evidenced by the stronger stock price reactions of non-announcing member firms to earnings news released by their group peers when their family business groups hire multiple auditors rather than a single common auditor. (2) Family business groups with multiple auditors tend to more frequently conduct related party transactions that serve as direct ways to transfer value between member firms. (3) Family business groups with higher agency problems are more inclined to hire multiple auditors. Taken together, the findings in this research suggest that family business groups take advantage of the multiple-auditor appointment as a ‘divide and conquer’ strategy to undermine the disciplining role played by external auditors. This research produces outcomes in two aspects. Firstly, we complete an article to document the findings and contributions of this research. The article is now being under revision and resubmission at Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance, a quality journal in accounting and finance areas. To improve this research and promote the visibility of this research, the principal investigator attended two top tier conferences in the accounting academics and presented the findings of this research to the audience. The two conferences are the American Accounting Association 2018 Western Region Meeting in Vancouver, Washington, and the European Accounting Association 41st Annual Congress in Milan, Italy. In addition to these two conferences, the principal investigator was invited to present this research at other universities including Hohai University, Nanjing University, Shanghai University, Xiamen University, Zhejiang University, and Zhongnan University of Economics and Law. Secondly, this research produces a comprehensive sample of family business groups that control at least two listed member firms in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Taiwan. This dataset is much broader in scope than that used in prior literature and can be used for other related future research. Actually, the principal investigator has already shared the data with several colleagues for them to probe into the research questions related to family business groups.

12502714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12502714.value: The sample of family business groups manually constructed in this research can be utilized to investigate other important issues within family business groups. For example, whether do family business groups adopt different strategies for different member firms to engage in corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities? CSR investments made by one member firm may benefit a family business group as a whole. The controlling families have incentives to make certain member firms undertake more CSR investments to maximize their own private benefits. Another potential topic is the technological innovation strategy adopted by family business groups. Nowadays, both CSR and innovation investments are vital for a firm's long-term competitive advantage. Different allocation of the related expenditures among member firms might be associated with different consequences for the controlling families and minority shareholders in individual member firms. We are now focusing on the revisions of the output manuscript to address comments from the editor and reviewers at Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance. We will try our best to have the output manuscript accepted for publication in the end so that this research can bring higher impact on and greater contribution to practitioners as well as the academia.

12502714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12502714.value: Family business groups control two or more member firms and play an important role in East Asian economies. The controlling families tend to transfer resources between member firms to maximize the whole group value or their own private benefits. External auditing serves as a critical mechanism to constrain the opportunistic behaviors of the controlling families. This research investigates how the controlling families exploit the auditor appointment strategy within their groups to undermine the effectiveness of monitoring by external auditors. This research reveals that family business groups can hire different auditors rather than a single common auditor to audit their different member firms to facilitate their intragroup value transfers. Family business groups with higher agency problems are more likely to hire multiple auditors. The findings of this research improve our understanding of agency problems and corporate governance issues within family business groups. The outsiders such regulatory bodies and investors can take the auditor appoint strategies into account to evaluate corporate governance practices, agency problems, and intragroup group value transfer potentials within family business groups.

12502814.label: Project Objectives
12502814.value: To study the expected-utility maximization, hierarchy, and diversification properties, of stochastic dominance (SD) for risk averters and risk lovers to any order. We will also study the conditions in different orders of SD such that risk averters and risk lovers could have the same or reversed preferences. To study the diversification properties for risk averters, risk lovers, and other types of investors including investors with S-shaped and reversed S-shaped utility functions for the independent and dependent variables. To develop a theory of almost SD (ASD) for risk-loving investors, study the relationship between ASD for risk-lovers and that for risk averters, and study the expected-utility maximization, hierarchy, and diversification properties of ASD for risk averters and risk lovers to any order. We will also study the conditions in ASD to any order such that risk averters and risk lovers could have the same preferences or reversed preferences. In addition, we will study the relationship between any order of ASD for risk averters and risk lovers with the corresponding order of moment. To derive the limiting process of n-order SD and ASD statistics for risk averters and risk lovers by taking into consideration that the underlying processes are dependent as well as independent. To develop a bootstrap method to compute the critical values for the tests. In addition, we will include testing other conditions to test the true SD and ASD relationships among the prospects being compared. We will conduct simulation to compare the performance of the SD and ASD tests. To examine the preferences for risk averters and risk lovers on stocks and bonds by using the new theory and tests we plan to develop in this project.

12502814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502814.value: We first plan to extend Wong (2007) and others to study the expected-utility maximization, hierarchy, and diversification properties of stochastic dominance (SD) for risk-averse and risk-loving investors to any order. We will also study the conditions such that the preferences of risk-averse and risk-loving investors could be the same or reversed. We will construct examples to demonstrate the usefulness of our approach. We then plan to extend Egozcue and Wong (2010) and others to investigate the diversification preferences of risk-averse and risk-loving investors and other types of investors including investors with S-shaped and reversed S-shaped utility functions for the independent and identical distributed variables. In particular, we plan to examine whether these investors would prefer to invest in an individual asset, any convex combination portfolio, or the equally weighted portfolio. Thereafter, we will extend the theory to include the dependent cases. Thereafter, we plan to extend Levy and Levy (2002) and others to first develop a theory of almost SD (ASD) for risk-loving investors. We will study the expected-utility maximization, hierarchy, and diversification relationships in ASD for risk-lovers and risk averters to any order. We will also study the conditions such that different orders of almost SD for risk-averse and risk-loving investors could be the same or reversed. In addition, we will study the relationship between any order of ASD for risk averters and risk lovers with the corresponding moment. We will then extend Bai, Li, Liu, and Wong (2011) and others to derive the limiting process of n-order SD and ASD statistics for risk averters and risk lovers. We will take into consideration that the underlying processes are dependent as well as independent. We will also develop a bootstrap method to compute the critical values for the tests. In addition, we will include testing other conditions in the SD and ASD testing procedures to reveal the true SD and ASD relationships among the prospects being compared. For example, we will test whether the means of the assets are equal for the third order SD. We will also conduct simulation to compare the performance of the SD and ASD tests we plan to develop. At last, we readdress the issue analyzed by Levy (2009) to study the preferences of risk-averse and risk-loving investors on stocks and bonds by using the new SD and ASD theory and tests we plan to develop in this project.

12502814.value: All the theoretical objectives have been achieved by developing several new theories as shown in my output. Only 2 applications of the theories we developed have not completed and we are still working on it. We should be able to complete very soon.

12503114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503114.value: In the extensive political economy literature, the most heavily-examined issues related to political connection is whether firms benefit from political connections or suffer from lack of connections. However, the cost side of seeking or maintaining political connections by firms has been largely ignored. Seeking political connections is costly. In this study we will exam the costs (in the form of tax overpayment) firms have to incur in seeking political ties and the resultant benefits (economic rents) they obtain. We first describe why Chinese private firms have incentives to develop stronger political connections and how those incentives compare to U.S. settings. We then examine whether firms seeking political ties pay more taxes to help local governments make up their expenditure shortage. We then study whether, in return, connected firms get preferential access to government-controlled resources (licenses, subsidies and financing opportunities). Finally, we examine the legal institutions in which such a “gift exchange” between the government and the firm most likely exists. The results of the study will highlight the importance of understanding political economy when analyzing corporate operations and tax reporting behaviour. 在政治經濟學的文獻中，政治關聯是一個被廣泛研究的課題。大部份的研究集中於政治關聯為企業帶來的利益以及因為政治關聯的缺失企業所需承擔的額外成本問題。然而，對於如何建立政治關聯以及其所需的成本卻很少有學者問津。尋求政治關聯往往花費巨大。在中國，企業會向政府支付超額的稅款用以建立政治關聯。在這個研究項目中，我們將企業的超額賦稅作為企业尋求政治關聯的成本度量，并進一步研究企業在獲得政治關聯后通過尋租而獲得的相關利益。 我們将首先闡述中國民營企業建立政治關聯的動機，並且與美國企業建立政治關聯動機進行比較。然後我們將測試政治關聯缺失的公司是否會通過向財政短缺的地方政府繳付超額的稅款用以建議政治關聯。我们將进一步研究建立政治關聯的公司是否会优先获得政府控制的资源，如行业准入执照，政府补贴以及融资机会。最后，我们将研究这种利益交换行为在什么样的外部法律制度环境中较为普遍。課題的研究結果有助於加深理解政治經濟在企業運營和稅務報告行為方面的影響。

13400014.label: Project Objectives
13400014.value: First, the project shall go beyond the traditional studies of sentence formation and conduct syntactic analysis within the matrix of modern theories of syntax. In my view, Chinese poetic syntax is best understood in terms of two alternate ways of arranging words. The first is a linear arrangement that indicates a clear spatiotemporal and causal relationship; the second is a non-linear arrangement that reveals an abrupt break in the spatiotemporal and causal relationship. More often than not, the non-linear arrangement indicates a gap or break between what is being observed (the topic: an object, scene, or occurrence) and the observer’s emotional response to it (the comment). The construction of topic+comment sentences is made possible and facilitated by the absence of inflection in Chinese. Topic+comment sentences are used profusely in Chinese poetry as a primary means of expressing and amplifying emotion in ways that anticipate the use of juxtaposed images in modern Western poetry. Second, the project shall carefully investigate the dynamic, productive tension between rhythms and syntax in classical Chinese poetry. On the one hand, the established rhythm(s) of a genre or subgenre significantly impacts the range of syntactic choices. As a rule, it sets limits on what types of subject+predicate and topic+comment sentences can be fitted into a line, and what types cannot. On the other hand, poets continually seek to stretch these limits to accommodate more syntactic constructions, especially those taken from prose. When a breaking point is reached, a search for new poetic rhythms begins, heralding the birth of a new genre. Undoubtedly, the tension between rhythm and syntax is a primary driving force of generic evolution and transformation. Third, the project shall closely examine the evolution of Chinese poetic structures, a subject badly neglected in both traditional and modern scholarship, I make a bold attempt to conceptualize the structural principles as the syntactic principles writ large. As I examine the 100 selected poems, I demonstrate that some genres are typically linearly structured, while many other genres are presented in a far less linear manner reminiscent of topic+comment. Fourth, the project shall illuminate how the dynamic interplay of rhythms, syntax, and structure yields different kinds of poetic vision. Moreover, I engage the impressionistic comments of traditional Chinese critics in light of the formal features I have outlined. I believe this novel approach will help to explain the linguistic foundations of the making of poetic vision. If each chapter demonstrates the synchronic interconnectedness of rhythms, syntax, structure, and vision in a given genre, the totality of the fourteen chapters will reveal the diachronic interconnectedness of these four aspects of Chinese poetic art. To accentuate this diachronic interconnectedness, I will carefully trace the continual reconfiguration of these four aspects through all the major genres. By so doing, I aim to make manifest the inner dynamics of the evolution of Chinese poetic art.

13400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13400014.value: Chinese people have been engrossed by poetic art for more than two millennia; Western poets and scholars have been fascinated by Chinese poetry since the 19th century. The proposed project *Chinese Poetry as Art* will provide an account of Chinese poetic art that departs significantly from both Chinese and Western scholarship. If traditional Chinese impressionistic criticism reveals an intuitive grasp of the ineffable aesthetic qualities of a given work, the oeuvre of a poet, or even a given genre, *Chinese Poetry as Art* aims to go one step further: to provide an analytical explanation for these aesthetic qualities. It consistently applies modern linguistics to analyze both the synchronic and diachronic interconnectedness of four essential aspects of Chinese poetic art—rhythm, syntax, structure, and vision—in an effort to illuminate the inner dynamics of Chinese poetic evolution. This new narrative of Chinese poetic art marks the culmination of my longtime endeavors to pursue innovative scholarship and to promote and energize the learning and teaching of Chinese poetry. I believe that we scholars have an obligation to integrate research with teaching and make our scholarship meaningful to both undergraduates and the general reader. To make *Chinese Poetry as Art* readily accessible, I adopt a “beads-on-a-string” strategy. The “beads” are the 100 of the best-loved Chinese poems selected for close reading. Indeed, each poem is a gem of poetic beauty for delightful appreciation. What is more, it is a fine specimen of the Chinese language for reading aloud and recitation, accompanied by tone-marked romanization and sound recording in Chinese. The “string” is a well-wrought network of concise commentaries that highlight the features of each genre examined and depict the trajectory of cross-generic transformation of the four aspects of Chinese poetic art. So the general reader can choose: to just appreciate any poems that catch his fancy, or to study all the poems to gain a comprehensive understanding of the evolution of Chinese poetic art. With a UGC grant, I will be able to complete *Chinese Poetry as Art,* the culmination of my poetry studies series, and make a significant impact on learning, understanding, and teaching of Chinese poetry both in and beyond the academy. *中國詩歌藝術新解*試圖深入研究詩歌語法與詩境的内在關係。 詩歌語法主要涵蓋韻律、句法、結構三大方面；詩境則是這三者互動結合而產生的的審美體驗，其中最上乘者被認為可呈現主、客觀世界之實相，稱為「意境」、「意象」、「境界」。 語法為實，詩境為虛，但兩者很少放在一起討論。談詩歌語法的文章，以實見長，一板一眼，用實例數據說話。立論多可信，但時常讀來索然寡味。談詩境的則恰恰相反，熱衷於描述言外之意，象外之象，優美的讚語不絕於耳，而落實在文本之上的分析不多。這似乎是告訴讀者，好詩的境界只能神會，不可言傳，說詩人僅能以虛對虛，用詩一般的言語來傳達自己的審美感受。 作者認為，韻律、句法、結構、詩境實際上有著密不可分的關係。爲了揭示四者內在互聯的關係，作者將集中探究以下問題：各種主要詩體有什麼獨特的節奏？每種獨特節奏引入了什麼新句式？句式與篇章結構有無內在聯係？新節奏、新句法、新結構的結合又會產生什麼新的詩境？提供何種難以言傳的審美體驗呢？為了尋找這些問題的答案，作者將進行三方面的研究。一是參照傳統詩學句法論，兼用量化統計，較為精確地描述各種詩體的節奏。二是借鑒現代語言學句法論，仔細分析不同詩體節奏所催生的各種句式，在時間與空間、讀者與作者等深層關係上探研各種詩境的生成方式。三是用節奏、句式、結構分析的結果來闡釋古人對各種詩體境界的直觀描述，以求從感性的「知其然」邁向理性的「知其所以然」。這一研究也許能為古典詩歌傳統提出一種新的解讀。

13401114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13401114.value: The Project, “The Making of Hong Kong Modernism: Hong Kong Literature and Culture of the 1960s”, critically examines the formation and development of Hong Kong literary modernism in the context of the 1960s. It is a cross-disciplinary research project that situates literature in its cultural context of visual arts, translation, cinema, music, performance, media etc. The project puts forward the question: What is Hong Kong literary Modernism in the context of 1960s? With the advent of the first post-war generation growing up in the 1960s, a new form of expression became an urgent quest, as rendered in the work of diverse cultural sectors, as well as the translational quality therein. The 1960s Hong Kong in the background of the Cold War provided a unique social context among Chinese societies for writers to conduct experiments on literary work which at the same time challenged and adapted the tradition. The colonial culture also allowed the writers to receive foreign culture but the reception process was not without negotiation. The Hong Kong reality, in a way, with its agenda on popular culture, hindered the development of literary modernism but at the same time helped circulate the idea in popular media. Existing research and resources on the subject are meager compared to the studies of the decade in other areas of the Greater China. Therefore, it is urgent (1) to recover significant yet disappearing modernist work of Hong Kong literature of the 1960s, and (2) to organize the academics of various humanities disciplines to undertake cross-disciplinary critical studies on the topic, which are the purposes this proposed project aims to serve. Established in 2001, Lingnan University’s Centre for Humanities Research (thereafter CHR), formerly headed by Prof. Leung Ping-kwan and currently led by Dr. Wong Shuk-han, has been playing a leading role in the studies of Hong Kong literature and culture. CHR has devoted endeavours on the studies of Hong Kong literature of the 1930s, 1940s, and most recently 1950s supported by RGC. CHR has a name for introducing Hong Kong literature to the international academia through publishing the refereed journal, Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese and organizing more than ten reputable international academic conferences. Extending previous efforts, the proposed project aims to systematically pioneer both local and international academia into the uncharted territory of research on Hong Kong literature and culture of the 1960s. 「香港現代主義的發生：一九六○年代的香港文學與文化」研究計劃旨在考察香港現代主義在一九六○年代的形成和發展。一九六○年代的香港具有獨特的文化政治語境，一方面文學、視覺藝術、翻譯、電影、音樂、媒體等多個文化領域縱橫交雜，另一方面在左右兩派政治勢力的激烈交鋒下，文化藝術發展蓬勃。本計劃提出的研究問題是：「在香港一九六○年代的文化政治語境下，香港現代主義如何形成？有什麼特色？」。在一九六○年代的香港，文化冷戰愈演愈烈，戰後第一代香港本土作家開始崛起，他們亟需發出一種新的聲音。他們在此期間創作的實驗性文學作品，以及他們和其它文化界別的實驗性合作，對五四文學傳統既有承傳亦有轉化，為香港現代主義打下了堅實的基礎。雖然在香港這片殖民地上，現代主義作家能夠接觸到外國先鋒文化，但是他們並非對其毫無保留地全盤接受。這一批作家在一九六○年代的香港，必須處理嚴肅文學與流行文化之間的問題。流行文化一方面阻礙了現代主義文學的發展，另一方面又將現代主義文學傳播至流行文化的領域。香港現存的相關學術研究材料，相比中國大陸和台灣對於當地一九六○年代以及現代主義文學的研究成果，目前仍只能望其項背，因此本計劃亟需：（一）蒐集與發掘發表於一九六○年代各文學期刊和報紙副刊的香港現代主義文學作品；（二）組織研究香港一九六○年代文學與文化的專家，從跨學科的角度來討論本計劃的議題。

13401114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13401114.value: Hong Kong 1960s was a decade of change. From the comparatively silent 1950s, Hong Kong has turned into a city of youth and as well as disturbance. At the meantime, the youthquarke of the global 1960s had highly influenced Hong Kong writers and artists of the time. Culturally, Hong Kong was an active battlefield for the cold war. Both the US and Soviet power had their influence on Hong Kong culture. Domestically, both China and Taiwan had planted cultural companies and organizations in the colonial Hong Kong. By researching on Hong Kong literature/cinema and arts, the project traced the changing atmosphere of the decades which the south-bound literati gave way to the local writers and artists. The resesarch studied Hong Kong literture/arts against the local and global poliltical atmostphere. The research has high signaficance in the understanding of Hong Kong literature/arts in the relationship of the changing 1960s.

13500114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500114.value: Reactance is a common psychological condition. When individuals perceive a threat to a valued freedom, they are motivated to reestablish that freedom. Social psychologists have studied psychological reactance for more than four decades. Reactance has been found to trigger aggressive and restricted behaviors, which undermine employee productivity and, eventually, organizational performance. In spite of its significance for organizations, few studies have explored the effects of reactance in organizations. Knowledge of the effects of psychological reactance along with organizational variables on employee work outcomes is very limited. In addition, most previous studies have focused on documenting the negative outcomes of psychological reactance without attending to the mechanisms through which it influences individual outcomes and how it can be managed in such a way to reduce its negative effects. To fill in these gaps, the first objective of this project is to develop a model that explains how psychological reactance is related to employee counterproductive behavior. To this end, we draw on leader-member exchange (LMX) theory and posit that reactant employees tend to develop a low level of LMX, through which psychological reactance influences counterproductive behavior. LMX is a type of social exchange that is typically characterized by hierarchy and imbalance of power. In organizations, supervisors have the legitimate power to influence subordinates and are a major target of reactant responses. Reactant employees often perceive the influence of supervisors as negative and perceive themselves as in conflict with their supervisors. Thus reactance is associated with low LMX and more counterproductive behaviors. The second objective of this project is to identify moderators between reactance and LMX. Considerable research has suggested that it is not conflict itself, but approaches to conflict management that affect interaction, relationships, and outcomes. Accordingly, this project will investigate how conflict management approaches moderate the relationship between psychological reactance and counterproductive behavior via LMX. To form our hypotheses, we use the theory of cooperation and competition, which is a universal theory, and social face protection, which is a theory specific to Chinese culture. We hypothesize that cooperation, conflict avoidance, and face protection reduce the negative effects of psychological reactance, and competition intensifies its negative effects. Finally, this project seeks to integrate universal and culture-specific theories by comparing the dynamics of different conflict-management approaches in different cultures. To examine our hypothesized model, we will conduct multi-wave cross-cultural surveys in state-owned enterprises and private companies in China and in private companies in the United States. 本項目旨在跨文化的情境中，研究衝突管理及面子如何對叛逆行為的負面效應產生調節作用。

13500114.label: Realisation of objectives
13500114.value: Objective 1 was fully achieved. This projects developed a model that explains how psychological reactance is related to employee counterproductive behavior. We found that state reactance, as a novel explanatory mechanism, explains why employees that experience organization injustice display counterproductive work behavior (CWB) toward organization. Objective 2 was also achieved. We examined the mediating effect of LMX on the relationship between psychological reactance and counterproductive behavior and found that LMX works as a dual system as psychological reactance to mediate the relationship between organization injustice and employees' counter-productive work behavior (CWB) toward organization. Object 3, 4 and 5 was partially achieved. We investigated the moderating effects of conflict management and face protection on the relationship between LMX and CWB and found that they are not the boundary conditions of the relationship between LMX and CWB with no cross-cultural diferences. Instead, the data collected indicated, job autonomy is a strong moderator to buffer the negative effects between organization injustice and employees' CWB via LMX. Objective 6 was achieved. The findings of this project provide practical implications on how to manage reactant employees so that CWB could be better managed in organizations in different cultural contexts.

13500114.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500114.value: Empirical data funded by this project casts that, state reactance, as a novel explanatory mechanism, explains why employees that experience organization injustice display counterproductive work behavior (CWB) toward organization. Applying reactance theory, this study extends and complements the dominant job stress framework in which organizational CWB is a behavioral strain response, and negative emotion mediates the stressor–strain relationship. With data collected from a multi-wave-multi source survey study, we tested the research model with state reactance and LMX as dual mediators and job autonomy as a moderator. Results supported the hypothesis that job autonomy moderates the indirect relationship between organizational injustice and CWB via state reactance and LMX. The completed paper will be submitted to Journal of Applied Psychology. Although we didn't find cross-cultural difference on the moderating effects of conflict-management approaches and face protection, the data supported the argument that American managers working in a company embracing Western low power distance and Eastern collectivism values are able to manage conflict cooperatively with their Chinese employees. The research paper titled "Transforming cross-cultural conflict into collaboration: The integration of western and eastern values", was published on Cross Cultural & Strategic Management, 2018-Vol. 25 Issue: 1, pp.70-95, https://doi.org/10.1108/CCSM-10-2016-0187 Data collected for this project also indicated that being envied is associated with three types of discrete emotions, which then translates into different prosocial and antisocial behaviors. Being envied indirectly related to interpersonal helping between employees via authentic pride, while hubristic pride mediated the relationship between being envied and various types of counter-productive behaviors. The research paper titled “Get Along, Get Ahead, or Get Away? Affective and Behavioral Outcomes of Being Envied” is currently under review by Journal of Applied Psychology. Other related findings of this project were presented at the 2016 SIOP Annual Conference (paper titled “An Integration of Instrumental and Relational Approaches to Employee Help-Seeking”) and the 2017 Academy of International Business US Midwest Conference (paper titled “the Constructive Controversy for Team Support and Productivity in China”).

13500114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500114.value: There are two future directions of potential for further development of the research. First, although we didn't find cross-cultural difference on the moderating effects of conflict-management approaches and face protection, we did find job autonomy as a boundary condition to moderate the relationship between psychology reactance and CWB. In line with this finding, further research can explore whether some of the power related constructs (i.e. power distance, self-leadership) can buffer the negative relationship between psychological reactance and test whether their effects have cross-cultural differences. Second, although the findings were based on multi-source-multi-wave data, some constructs (i.e. LMX) are not static but changeable. To address this issue, future research can adopt change perceptive to examine the relationship between psychological reactance and CWB via LMX under dynamic situation.

13500114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500114.value: Psychological reactance, which refers to the motivation to restore a valued freedom when perceiving a threat to that freedom, has been found to trigger counter productive behaviors (CWBs). Adding to the literature that investigated the negative outcomes of psychological reactance, this research project studied the mechanisms through which employees’ CWB was triggered and how state reactance could be managed to reduce its negative effects. The major finding of this project indicated that state reactance works as a novel explanatory mechanism to explain why employees perceive organization injustice behave counter-productively toward the organization. In addition, the results also suggested that job autonomy could buffer the negative indirect relationship between organizational injustice and CWB via state reactance and LMX. The significance and value of this research are: first, this project found the mediating effect of state reactance shed light on the process through which psychological reactance is triggers and in turn leads to counterproductive behaviors. These results are important because they advance our understanding of the dynamics of psychological reactance in organizations. Second, the finding on the moderating effects of job autonomy provided practical guidelines for supervisors to manage and buffer the negative effects of state reactance to reduce employees’ CWB.

13500314.value: 企業往往要根據新產品概念測試的結果做出關鍵性的決策。概念測試一直被認為是用來評估新產品的市場需求和確定目標客戶的重要工具。概念測試收集消費者對新產品概念的反應，這些資料可以説明企業在眾多的新產品概念中選擇最有可能獲得成功的好概念，從而更有效地分配新產品開發的資源。因此無論是改進概念測試的方法設計還是加強對概念測試結果的解釋都可以提高新產品開發的有效性。 傳統的概念測試完全基於經典測驗理論（CTT; Lord & Novick, 1968），依賴簡單的統計量計算，如量表項目的總分或均值，來描述產品概念的優劣，但忽視了個別量表項目（或被試者的評估能力）對概念測試結果的影響。經典測驗理論通過信效度測量和驗證性因數分析來選擇有效的量表項目（Churchill, 1979; Gerbing & Anderson, 1988），但這種量表項目的選擇方法不區分測量誤差的各種類型，籠統歸於單一的誤差項，很可能會對概念測試的結果產生誤導，從而影響最終的選擇決策。因為為不同類型的概念測試選擇有效的量表項目和合格的被試者會對概念測試的結果產生顯著的影響，如果量表項目和被試者選擇不當，將會嚴重破壞概念測試的有效性和準確性。 為瞭解決基於經典測驗理論的測量方法所存在的誤差問題，我們的研究採用現代測驗理論中的項目反應模型（IRT），為不同類型的概念測試進行優化設計，包括選擇有效的量表項目和合適的被試者。我們通過效用差異分析（DIF），測量不同量表專案的辨析度和被試者的評估能力對概念測試結果的影響，作為選擇量表和被試者的有效依據。專案反應理論風靡教育心理學和心理測量學等領域，但在市場學中的應用還比較少見（e.g., de Jong et al., 2009; Paas & Sijtsma, 2008）。它用一系列數學模型來描述量表專案反應組型和被測變數之間的函數關係。模型所採用的專案參數(item parameters)（如：難度、鑑別度、猜測度等），不會因為所選出接受測試的被試者樣本的不同而不同。它能夠針對每位被試者，提供個別差異的測量誤差指標，而非單一相同的測量標準誤，因此能夠精確推估被試者的能力估計值，並對不同被試者的評估能力進行有意義的比較。據我們所知，IRT和DIF還沒有應用在新產品開發的區域。我們的兩項研究任務包括：（1）憑藉項目參數的估計值為不同類型的概念測試選擇有效的專案量表，（2）通過對被試者評估能力的估計為概念測試選擇合格有效的被試者。這些結果將有助於更好地理解概念測試的設計和結果解釋，為營銷人員設計和推廣新產品和制定目標市場營銷策略提供切實有力的幫助。

13500314.label: Realisation of objectives
13500314.value: To examine the performance of product from the item response theory perspective, we propose an item response theory (IRT) model of customer satisfaction and a multi-facet IRT (MFIRT) framework to simultaneously examine the effects of attributes, reviewer criticality, consumption situation, product type, and time. Analyses of field data suggest that product attributes differ in their discriminating and threshold characteristics and that reviewers emphasize different attributes when rating various products over time. The MFIRT estimates predict hotel performance more accurately than alternative methods by a significant, and uncover rich and novel insight to inform business strategies. Overall, this research furnishes strong evidence that IRT and MFIRT provides an integrative framework for assessing customer satisfaction by incorporating item characteristics, customer criticality and other relevant facets, and renders superior predictive performance over the conventional methods. The IRT approach clearly provides a more rigorous and in-depth examination of customer satisfaction and its sources of variance. The IRT models extract novel insight that cannot be obtained using conventional methods that assume equal weights of product attributes and measurement errors across different product and customer groups. Given the abundance of online product ratings, researchers can leverage the analytical power of IRT to examine customer satisfaction through a new multi-angled lens. This approach makes it possible to analyze the rich data of online reviews in a transparent, systematic and disciplined fashion, generates results that articulate the relations among variables, and offers actionable recommendations for managers. This researcg contributes to the literature and practice in several areas. First, we are the first to extend the current applications of IRT in business beyond measurement issues, adapt the IRT methodology as a set of analytical tools to address managerial and strategic issues. By examining the measurement characteristics of both product attributes and respondents (i.e., reviewers), the graded response model (GRM, a single-facet IRT model for polytomous response data) deduces the influence of attribute discrimination and threshold on consumer attitude, and thus provides rich and novel insight to inform business strategies for individual firms. Second, we propose the MFIRT framework as an analytical framework to simultaneously examine multiple key facets relevant to the formation of customer satisfaction, and thus overcomes the limitations of the CTT approach in accounting for the multiple sources of errors and unobserved heterogeneity. In so doing, we demonstrate the versatility and scalability of the IRT framework, which enables managers to produce more nuanced findings at different levels of facets and to refine their product and marketing strategies accordingly. Third, we elaborate the merit of the IRT and MFIRT models for mining intelligence, as they can identify the attributes important to customer satisfaction and how they interact with other facets to reveal the underlying problems. The estimated results predict product performance more accurately than competing methods by a substantial margin and produce rich insight that can enhance the effectiveness of product and marketing strategies. Lastly, we expect that IRT can not only improve the measures of constructs such as customer satisfaction, but more importantly enable rigorous analyses of consumer behaviors and business concepts in broader areas to address other theoretical, managerial and strategic issues, and fundamentally change how we derive knowledge from multi-faceted data and develop insight to inform business strategies. We have conducted several studies using various datas sets. To date, we have presented our research findings at three international conferneces. The preliminary results have been published in an international refereed journal. The final manuscript has been submitted to a top tier academic journal and is currently under review. The initial feedback from the reviewers support the innovativeness of our research and the significant implication for both resesearch and management. We expect that IRT perspective over time will have a profound impact on how we analyze consumer attitudes and help improve research as well as practice. Overall, we have satisfactorily achieved the objectives of the proposed research and expect that it will appear in a journal of high reputation and have a significant and long-term impact on marketing research.

13500314.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500314.value: In assessing customer satisfaction, the IRT results reveal many novel and interesting findings that cannot be unraveled by traditional methods. The findings suggest that attributes with high (or low) ratings might carry greater weights depending on their discrimination efficiency. For example, our GRM findings suggest that for luxury hotel A, reviewers accentuate good value (weight=0.297) even though value has a lowest rating (3.9) compared to other attributes. While location is a high-rating attribute for both hotel A and B, it carries the lowest weight in forming latent customer satisfaction. Therefore, without accounting for these attribute characteristics, a good overall rating or high scores for less important attributes may give managers a false sense of security and lead to misguided effort. Moreover, the interaction effects from our MFIRT results reveal that the weights of attributes vary across reviewer groups and hotel types, and they change over time. To answer the questions raised in the introduction, the IRT perspective points to the importance of improving performance only in those attributes that really matter to consumers who are particularly critical and influential in this respect.

13500314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500314.value: Additional research is needed to enhance the applicability of IRT and MFIRT to other platforms, products and attributes, and to other contexts in which researchers use multi-attribute measures to assess consumer perceptions and the effect of marketing stimuli. Our research serves as an initial effort to propose IRT as an analytical framework and methodology to address managerial and strategic problems in business. While our effort focuses on mining intelligence for firms, information intermediaries such as review websites, research firms and digital agencies may deploy the MFIRT approach to provide their clients with research designs and findings that are more relevant for their product types and customer segments. Future studies may consider adopting the MFIRT method to improve online review systems by developing ratings of products adjusted for attributes, reviewer and product segments. Researchers are encouraged to explore the advantages of MFIRT in other areas such as new product development, brand positioning, and product quality augmentation.

13500314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500314.value: The raw scores given by reviewers to rate the various dimensions of a product may not reveal why the product receives high or low ratings on certain attributes. The IRT results indicate that variations in ratings of attributes may be due to their attribute characteristics, reviewer criticality which differ depending on reviewer expertise and/or consumption situation, product type, and the dynamic effects. Such insight allows firms to uncover and define the problems more precisely, adapt their strategies, and devise effective solutions to address the deficiencies. As return on investment is a challenge for managers, the IRT model enables them to scale the effect of different facets and direct their efforts to target specific product attributes or customer groups. Such insight provides critical intelligence that can help firms devise actionable strategies to allocate precious resources in areas that will produce tangible improvement and result in a measurable impact on customer satisfaction and sales.

13500614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500614.value: In order “to promote the financial stability of the United States by improving accountability and transparency in the financial system”, in 2010 the U.S. congress passed the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (commonly referred to as “Dodd-Frank”), in which Section 165 requires a separate risk committee for publicly traded bank holding companies that have total consolidated assets of $10 billion or more. According to Dodd-Frank, a risk committee should include certain number of independent directors deemed as appropriate by the Federal Reserve Board, and also at least one member with risk management expertise. The risk committee, as a stand-alone board level committee, will be responsible for overseeing the firm-wide risk management practices. The objective of this project is to use the passage of Dodd-Frank as a quasi-experiment to identify and assess whether and how the establishment of a separate board level risk committee and its associated characteristics impact bank performance and firm value. Our first question is to directly examine the effect of a stand-alone risk committee on bank risk-taking. Our second question is to assess the effect of risk committee on CEO turnover and accounting quality, built upon the hypothesis that under more intensive monitoring and better oversight, CEOs are more likely to be replaced by the board and banks’ accounting quality should improve. Our last question is to examine the net effect of a separate risk committee on firm value. This research has important policy implications that should be of interest to not only U.S. regulators but also regulators of other countries who may wish to adopt similar policies to improve corporate internal governance. More importantly, this study may provide an empirical basis for recommendations of independent risk expert involvement in board oversight duties. For example, even though the Hong Kong Ordinances - Section 65 of the SFO (Securities and Futures Ordinance) – require an establishment of a risk management committee, the ordinance does not mandate or make recommendations on the experience and expertise required by the committee member. Our study will contribute to the regulation literature by identifying and evaluating the effect of Dodd-Frank Section 165. Our research will also contribute to the large literature on bank risk-taking and the small but growing literature on the role of corporate internal governance of financial institutions.

13500814.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500814.value: We extend the R–S definition to a background risk framework (see research outcome 4). We propose a method to construct uniform confidence band for expectation dependence (see research outcome 2). We identify new conditions ensuring risk aversion in the sense of Arrow–Pratt in a two-argument utility framework in which a financial risk is accompanied by a background risk (see research outcome 1). We examine on savings with general Selden/Kreps– Porteus preferences (see research outcome 5). We propose an alternative decomposition of the consumption-based capital asset pricing model (C-CAPM) in terms of higher-order risks. These theoretical results are linked to the equity premium and risk-free rate puzzles. The calibrated and estimated levels of risk aversion and prudence correspond to the theoretical values commonly discussed in the literature (see research outcome 3).

We investiagte how risk attitudes and background risks jointly affect our decisions. Our results can be applied to any security-bonds, options, and so on, - and to any uncertain cash flow.

13500814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500814.value: The main empirical failure of the traditional consumption-based capital asset pricing (C-CAPM) model is the equity premium puzzle. This puzzle has potentially serious consequences, because much of modern economics and finance is built on basically the same models that underlie the same principles. This project uses traditional C-CAPM model as a starting point and extends them by including fundamental modifications such as higher-order risk attitudes and background risks. The project helps us to better understand the relevant basic factors that determine asset prices.

13501214.label: Realisation of objectives
13501214.value: Using a uniquely matched rating dataset for a large sample of U.S. corporations, this paper investigates whether market-implied ratings (MIRs) derived from bond-, equity-, and credit-default-swap (CDS) market prices provide timelier information than do credit ratings (CRs). We also examine the firm characteristics that drive the divergence between CRs and MIRs and, more importantly, whether such divergence could provide incremental information to the market for anticipating defaults, rating changes, and early indicators of rating changes (such as outlooks and watchlists). Furthermore, we test how the 2008 financial crisis and the Dodd-Frank Act affect the predictive ability of the ratings gap between CRs and MIRs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the determinants and predictive ability of the discrepancy between actual credit ratings and market-price implied ratings. Market-based credit ratings, or market-implied ratings (MIRs), refer to credit ratings or assessments that use “the prices of traded assets to directly determine the credit ratings for publicly traded firms with a minimal amount of subjective input on a firm-by-firm basis” (Creal, Gramacy, and Tsay, 2014). MIRs are expressed on the same rating scale as the Moody’s CR scale, making them easier and more intuitive to comprehend than raw market prices for comparison and application purposes. Moreover, MIRs are better measures of credit risk than are raw market prices of equities, bonds, and CDSs. Although market prices can capture credit quality sentiment for a given company, this view is often blurred by the market’s general appetite for risk and is affected by liquidity risk and counterparty risk. For example, stock prices incorporate news of both cash flow and credit risk; bond prices are affected by bond features and liquidity risk (Blanco, Brennan, and Marsh, 2005); and CDS prices include liquidity and counterparty risk. In comparison, MIRs isolate idiosyncratic risk-spread movements from changes in the broad market and filter out non-credit risks. MIRs can incorporate subtle and fast-moving changes in borrower conditions and may respond faster to credit risk than CRs provided by CRAs. A case in point is a comparison between MIRs and CRs around the Lehman Brothers bankruptcy. Before Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on September 15, 2008, its Moody’s rating was A1 at the beginning of the year, A2 in early September, and B3 on the day of its bankruptcy. However, the MIRs provided warning signals prior to the bankruptcy. Figure 1 shows that the ratings implied from bond spreads, equity prices, and CDS spreads in early 2008 were around Baa2, Baa3, and Ba1, which are much lower than the CRs and indicate a higher chance of default. This example shows that MIRs lead credit rating changes and defaults by many months. If market participants had tracked the MIR and its divergence from the actual credit rating for Lehman, they may well have made better investment or risk-management decisions. To shed more light on the relevance and importance of MIRs for investment, risk management and regulatory decisions, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of four issues regarding MIRs and their divergence from CRs. First, we examine the timeliness of MIRs relative to CRs for 2002–2014, a period spanning pre-, during and post-financial crisis. A unique feature of our study is that the MIRs are based on Moody’s models, as opposed to other models (e.g., Kou and Varotto 2008; Creal, Gramacy, and Tsay 2014). We employ three versions of MIRs: bond-, CDS-, and equity-implied ratings. We find that all three MIRs lead CRs for U.S. corporate bond issuers by up to 12 months prior to a credit-rating change. Specifically, bond- and CDS-implied ratings predict rating changes more accurately than do equity-implied ratings. Second, we investigate the determinants of the discrepancy between CRs and MIRs. We find that the gap between Moody’s credit rating and bond-implied rating is positive, indicating that CRAs perceive a firm’s credit quality, on average, at a higher level than do bond investors. Conversely, the gap between Moody’s credit rating and equity-implied rating is, on average, negative. The same holds true for the gap between credit rating and CDS-implied rating. A negative gap means that CRAs perceive a firm’s credit quality at a lower level than do stock and CDS investors. Next, we seek to determine whether rating gaps are wider for firms with higher information opacity or uncertainty. If a firm has greater information opacity, CRAs may have more leeway to assign their ratings. For example, they may inflate ratings because they are paid by the firms they are rating. It is more difficult for investors to detect rating inflation for less transparent firms. In addition, if a firm has greater information uncertainty, CRAs may be more reluctant to revise credit ratings, because they adopt a through-the-cycle methodology and strive to maintain rating stability. Our results show that rating gaps are indeed larger when information opacity is more severe (measured by the number of analysts making earnings forecasts on the issuer and the dispersion of analyst forecasts) and when the issuer’s volatility is higher (measured by the issuer’s cash flow volatility and idiosyncratic risk). Third, and more importantly, we explore the predicative ability of the divergence between CRs and MIRs. We expect that tracking the divergence (that is, the gap between CRs and MIRs) can provide incremental and useful information to the market. Indeed, the divergence between CRs and MIRs does help predict corporate defaults and rating changes. The prediction power is stronger for downgrades than for upgrades. Credit rating agencies tend to narrow the gap by moving towards the rating implied by market prices. If the credit rating is greater than the MIR, the issuer is more likely to be downgraded; whereas, if the credit rating is lower than the MIR, the issuer is more likely to be upgraded. Furthermore, rating gaps between MIRs and CRs can predict outlooks and credit watches, which are early indicators of rating changes. In general, bond-implied and CDS-implied rating gaps have better predictive ability than do equity-implied rating gaps for negative credit events. Finally, we evaluate how the 2008 financial crisis and the Dodd-Frank Act affect the predictive ability of gaps between CRs and MIRs. Credit rating agencies were criticized as too slow to downgrade ratings during the crisis. We find that the bond-implied rating gap remained positive and slightly widened, the CDS-implied rating gap turned from negative to positive, while the equity-implied rating gap remained negative in the six months before the financial crisis. This interesting pattern of changes reveals that bond and CDS investors anticipated the crisis before credit-rating agencies and equity investors. In terms of predictive ability, our multivariate regression results show that the gap between credit rating and CDS-implied rating is a better predictor of issuer defaults during the crisis than during non-crisis periods. Moreover, each rating gap can better predict rating changes during the crisis. This supports the criticism that CRAs were slow to adjust credit ratings during the financial crisis.

13501214.label: Major findings and research outcome
13501214.value: Our results suggest that MIRs are timelier indicators of creditworthiness than are the typical CRs. We also find that MIRs lead CRs by up to 12 months prior to credit rating changes. In addition, we find that rating gaps are larger if information opacity is more severe, as reflected by the number of analysts providing earnings forecasts for the issuer and the dispersion of those forecasts. Rating gaps are also larger if the firm is more volatile, as measured by cash flow volatility and idiosyncratic volatility. Moreover, the divergence between CRs and MIRs provides important information to market participants, i.e., rating gaps help predict defaults as well as rating, outlook and watchlist changes. A positive rating gap (where the CR is higher than the MIR) is associated with a greater probability of default and downgrades in subsequent periods. A negative rating gap (where the CR is lower than the MIR) is associated with a higher likelihood of subsequent credit rating upgrades by CRAs. Among the three MIRs, bond-implied and CDS-implied ratings are better than equity-implied ratings at predicting defaults and subsequent rating changes. Furthermore, the predictive ability of rating gaps on subsequent rating changes was pronounced during the 2008 financial crisis but was mitigated in the post-Dodd-Frank period, supporting the view that credit rating agencies were slow to adjust ratings at the time of the crisis, but improved under regulatory pressure. This study adds to our understanding of market-implied ratings, which are better measures of credit risk than are raw market prices of bonds, stocks and credit default swaps. In practice, MIRs are easier and more intuitive to use for application purposes. Our results have important implications for market participants such as bond investors, risk managers, and portfolio managers regarding the use of credit ratings and their possible alternatives. Specifically, tracking the divergence between MIRs and CRs can exploit significant incremental information for predicting issuer defaults, rating changes, and even early signals of rating changes. It should also provide useful information for regulators in their efforts to oversee and restructure the credit rating industry.

13501214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13501214.value: Our results have important implications for market participants such as bond investors, risk managers, and portfolio managers regarding the use of market-based complementary sources of credit information. Future research could study more specifically how market participants apply and use the incremental information derived from the divergence between CRs and MIRs in enhancing their risk and portfolio management.

13501214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13501214.value: This study investigates the importance of market-implied ratings (MIRs) in predicting changes in credit ratings (CRs) and their relative divergence. The evidence portrays that MIR changes lead CR changes by up to 12 months. The rating divergence provides incremental information to the market regarding subsequent defaults, rating, outlook and watchlist changes and is more significant when information opacity or firm uncertainty is higher. This predictive ability of the rating divergence was more pronounced during the 2008 financial crisis but weakened in the post-Dodd-Frank period. This is consistent with the credit rating agencies’ efforts in improving their performance upon regulatory pressure.

13501414.label: Project Objectives
13501414.value: We will explore the impact of carbon labeling programs on the manufacturer’s wholesale pricing and the retailer’s retail margin decisions. We will examine whether the labeling program leads to an increase or a decrease in the retailer’s profit. We will study when the manufacturer can gain a higher profit from the labeling program by comparing his profit with and without labeling. We will examine how operational factors affect firm profits by conducting some sensitivity analysis. We plan to study the effectiveness of the carbon labeling program to reduce emissions by comparing the total emission reduction (or total emission, or unit emission rate) with and without labeling. We can hence understand when the labeling programs are most effective, and suggest the policy makers to provide economic incentive to stimulate such effective emission reduction. We will explore how operational factors affect the above effectiveness by doing some sensitivity analysis. We will explore how the competition between manufacturers affect the retailer’s labeling decisions.

13501414.label: Realisation of objectives
13501414.value: Our first objective is to examine the impact of carbon labeling programs on the manufacturer’s wholesale pricing and the retailer’s retail margin decisions. Our analysis shows that when without labeling, the low-type manufacturer always has an incentive to mimic the high-type manufacturer since the customers belief about emission reduction is based solely on price. Hence no separating equilibrium exists. However, we find that pooling equilibrium can survive, where the manufacturer will set a wholesale price independent its type. The retailer cannot infer the manufacturer’s type and set a retail margin based on the expected demand. When with labeling, the low-type manufacturer will set a low wholesale price and the high-type manufacturer will set a high wholesale price. The retailer will set a high retail margin when the manufacturer’s type is high but a low retail margin when the manufacturer’s type is low. Our second and third objectives are to examine the impact of carbon labeling programs on the manufacturer’s profit and the retailer’s profit, respectively. We have: If the retailer adopts carbon emission labeling, the manufacturer will be better off whereas the retailer can be worse off. This shows that the manufacturer will benefit from the retailer’s carbon emission labeling. This is because when without carbon emission labeling, the low-type manufacturer always has an incentive to mimic the high-type manufacturer. Hence the high-type manufacturer cannot reveal the high carbon reduction level to customers. However, under labeling, customers will know exactly the manufacturer’s type. Though the manufacturer will instead hurt from the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior, he can adjust the green technology investment intensity to moderate the negative impact of the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior. Intuitively, under carbon emission labeling, the retailer can benefit from improved pricing decision by observing the manufacturer’s real type. Our analysis shows that this is the case when the green technology is not efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, where the manufacturer does not invest less in green technology. However, interestingly, when the green technology is very efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, the result may be different if both the manufacturer’s and the retailer’s strategic decisions are also taken into account. In specific, when the green technology is very efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior will be much enhanced, and hence the manufacturer will invest much less in green technology. For the retailer, the hurt from reduced green technology investment can dominate the benefit from strategic pricing decision. Thus the retailer can be worse off under carbon emission labeling. Note that when the green technology is moderately efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, the manufacturer will also invest less (not too much) in green technology. Then for the retailer, the hurt from reduced green technology investment can be covered by the benefit from strategic pricing decision. In such cases, the retailer will be better off with carbon emission labeling. Our fourth objective is to examine how operational factors affect firm profits by conducting some sensitivity analysis. The results are nearly the same with and without carbon labeling. First, as the product’s basic valueincreases, both the manufacturer’s profit and the retailer’s profit will increase. Second, as the green technology investment cost decreases, the manufacturer will increase more in green technology. Meanwhile, both the manufacturer and the retailer will be better off. Third, as the green technology becomes more efficient in reducing carbon emission, both the manufacturer and the retailer will be better off. Our fifth objective is to examine the impact of carbon labeling programs on carbon emission reduction (i.e., green technology investment). We have: If the retailer adopts carbon emission labeling, the manufacturer will invest more in green technology if the green technology is not efficient in reducing the carbon emission level but invest less if the green technology is efficient in reducing the carbon emission level. One may intuit that carbon emission labeling will encourage the manufacturer to invest more in green technology. Because customers will be informed the real carbon reduction level and will be more likely to buy the product if the manufacturer’s green technology investment successes. Proposition 1 shows that such intuition can be wrong and the manufacturer may invest less under carbon emission labeling. The reason hinges on the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior. When with carbon emission labeling, the retailer will also know exactly the manufacturer’s type. If the manufacturer’s green technology investment successes, the retailer will increase her retail margin much because of the increased demand. Clearly, the high retail margin will reduce the manufacturer’s incentive to invest in green technology. When the green technology is not efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, the manufacturer’s benefit from revealing his real type to customers can cover the loss induced by the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior, and hence the manufacturer will invest more in green technology. However, when the green technology is efficient in reducing the carbon emission level, the retailer’s strategic pricing behavior is intensified and its hurt dominates the manufacturer’s benefit from revealing his real type to customers. Thus the manufacturer may invest less in green technology. Our sixth objective is to explore how operational factors affect the above effectiveness by doing some sensitivity analysis. In one-to-one supply chain, if a labeling strategy is adopted, the retailer knows the true carbon emission reduction and he will set a higher expected retail margin than that under no labeling strategy, which leads to a higher expected retail price under labeling. This will discourage the manufacturer to invest more green technology. So the manufacturer’s green technology investment under labeling is less than that under no labeling. We show that the manufacturer’s green technology investment is decreasing in the green technology development cost factor. The smaller the development cost factor is, the less cost it takes the manufacturer, so the manufacturer will invest more in the green technology and charge a higher retail price. However, a high retail price results in less demand. So the retailer doesn’t always benefit from a high green technology investment. Our last objective is to explore how the competition between manufacturers affect the retailer’s labeling decisions. With upstream manufacturer competition, each firm seeks to differentiate from the other. Otherwise, they will compete fiercely for market share, which hurts both manufacturers. Given that one manufacturer’s carbon emission reduction is low, the other manufacturer would invest more green technology to make differentiation. However, the more investment is spent on green technology, the higher expected retail margin the retailer would set and so does the retail price. The higher expected retail margin hurts the rival manufacturer’s incentive to invest green technology. The higher retail price results in less demand for the rival manufacturer’s product, the rival manufacturer still earns more profit due to less fierce competition. But the retailer is worse off since the demand loss for the rival manufacturer’s product dominates the increased retail margin. We find that the development cost factor plays an important role. When the development cost factor is sufficiently small, the rival manufacturer will invest more under labeling, henceforth he will charge a higher retail price, which hurts the retailer. So the retailer prefers no labeling if the development cost factor is sufficiently small. Otherwise, the retailer prefers labeling.

13501414.label: Major findings and research outcome
13501414.value: We show that in one-to-one supply chain, the manufacturer’s green technology investment under no labeling is higher than that under labeling. The labeling strategy hurts the manufacturer, but benefits both the retailer and supply chain. So the retailer will adopt labeling strategy. As to the carbon emission, it’s true that the total carbon emission reduction under no labeling is greater than that under labeling due to the higher green technology investment under no labeling. However, interestingly we find that labeling strategy does not always leads to less carbon emission. The total carbon emission depends on the original carbon emission in producing one unit. If the original carbon emission is low enough, the total carbon emission under labeling is less than that under no labeling. Otherwise, the total carbon emission under no labeling is less than that under labeling. When there exists upstream competition, given one manufacturer’s carbon emission reduction is low, the other manufacturer’s green technology investment depends on the development cost factor. When the development cost factor is less than a threshold, the green technology investment under labeling is greater than that under no labeling. Otherwise, the green technology investment under labeling is less than that under no labeling. The retailer prefers no labeling strategy when the development cost factor is small enough. Otherwise, the retailer prefers labeling strategy. Different from the case with no upstream competition, we find that both the total carbon emission and carbon emission reduction of the supply chain depend on the green technology development cost factor. When the development cost factor is greater than a threshold, the total carbon emission reduction (the total carbon emission) of the supply chain under no labeling is more (less) than that under labeling. Otherwise, the total carbon emission reduction (the total carbon emission) of the supply chain under no labeling is less (more) than that under labeling. This project has led to one paper published in Management Science, one working paper under review by MSOM, one conference paper. In addition, one postgraduate student is working on this project, and part of the project is one chapter of his thesis work.

13501414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13501414.value: An ideal model to investigate manufacturer competition should assume both manufacturers may adopt no labeling strategy. However, this will bring in some technical difficulties. Specifically, the problem of two firms simultaneously making decisions to signal their respective private information has not been investigated in the literature. As the belief of each other also depends on the strategy of the rival manufacturer, it is difficult to obtain an equilibrium which supports the equilibrium belief under competition. Hence, in our working paper, we assume one manufacturer always has labeling. This makes the problem tractable. In future, it is worthwhile to try the above more general competition model. Finding condition to ensure equilibria under manufacturer competition will contribute significantly to the literature.

13501414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13501414.value: Carbon emission labeling programme benefits the retailer and the whole supply chain and hurts the manufacturer. Interestingly, a manufacturer may have to reduce investment in environmental protection when the labeling programme is viable; the labeling programme may increase or reduce emision amount depending on the original emission level. The labeling programme is environmentally beneficial if and only if the original emission level is low. Otherwise, the labeling programme will lead to more emission. When there is upstream manufacturer competition, both the total carbon emission and carbon emission reduction of the supply chain depend on the green technology development cost factor, and the labeling programme may increase or decrease manufacturers' investment in green technology.
