14100114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100114.value: 幽門螺旋菌是消化性潰瘍的主要病因，和胃癌及胃腺癌的主要危險因素。運動的幽門螺旋桿菌定植在胃內是通過複雜的納米機器 - 鞭毛。鞭毛III型分泌系統能準確地控制各個鞭毛蛋白的輸出。在模型微生物中，大腸桿菌和沙門氏菌，分泌分子伴侶FlgN，FliS和FliT 作“衛兵”來保護他們的基體，防止基體在胞質中過早聚合，和攜帶他們到分泌系統。但是，遺傳學和鞭毛結構的研究已證明不同細菌的鞭毛系統存在差異。迄今為止，幽門螺旋菌鞭毛分泌的分子基礎幽還不是很清楚。 雖然FliS與鞭毛蛋白相互作用，但我們最近確定了幽門螺旋菌FliS有一些額外的相互分子。這結果表明，FliS可能有廣泛的基體和多種功能。具體地說，我們發現FliS與鞭毛絲帽FliD，鞭毛鉤絲結FlgK，和一個未表徵蛋白HP1076相互作用。 HP1076在細菌運動沒有作用，所以我們特別好奇FliS-HP1076的互動意義。我們已獲得FliS，HP1076及它們的二元複合物的結晶結構。FliS-HP1076相互作用不需要FliS的基體，例如鞭毛蛋白。 HP1076分佈在整個細菌細胞，而不是只在鞭毛極，這結果與HP1076不是鞭毛分泌系統的組成部分是一致的，而是HP1076涉及其他細胞功能。因此，我們假設FliS相互作用和分子伴侶蛋白的多樣化，有助於幽門螺旋菌生物學。為了進一步了解FliS的功能，我們應用分子微生物學和結構生物學，1）分離完整的FliS相互作用夥伴，2）測繪FliS與相互分子的作用表面，和 3) 描述FliS如何影響HP1076的表達和定位。這項計劃將加強我們對鞭毛III型分泌系統和幽門螺旋菌利用不同策略的認識。我們的研究結果將提供新的研究途徑於毒力因子。

14100114.label: Realisation of objectives
14100114.value: Objective 1: We applied pull-down assay to isolate FliS / FliS-HP1076 interacting partners. Together with mass spectrometry, H. pylori CtpA, a carboxyl-terminal processing protease, was found to interact with GST-FliS-HP1076 complex. Direct interaction between CtpA and HP1076 was validated. CtpA was also found to catalyze the cleavage of HP1076 at its C terminal in the absence of FliS. In some bacteria, CtpA is found to function in cell wall integrity and degradation of mis-folded proteins. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, CtpA is essential for the normal function of the type III secretion system. However, the biological function of H. pylori CtpA has never been characterized. In addition, we applied in vivo cross-linker DSSO and LC-MS for cross-linking study. We noted various cross-linked products but none of them are FliS or HP1076 related. We will test different concentrations and types of cross-linkers to optimized applying this approach in interactome study. Objective 2: The biophysical interactions of FliS with different flagella proteins were studied by making various truncated fragments. Interaction of FliS-FlaB was found to be the most stable when compared with FliS-FlaA. However, co-purification of FliS with FliD, FlgK was failed after affinity pull-down. The complex was dissociated during size exclusion chromatography, indicating the binding affinity of FliS with FliD and FlgK is rather low. The major difficulty to complete this objective is the solubility of these flagellar proteins. Unlike other bacteria, when these proteins are expressed and purified alone, they tend to aggregate. This hinders the work to characterize their binding kinetics. Therefore, major effort was on the structural study of FliS-FlaB as described below. Objective 3: We successfully purified FliS-FlaBc-HP1076 complex by mixing purified FliS-FlaBc and HP1076 followed by size exclusion chromatography. The crystallization was optimized and a complete x-ray data set was collected at NSRRC synchrotron source. The data was processed to 2.95A and the phase was solved by molecular replacement using FliS-HP1076 as a search model. This work together with some findings from Objective 4 was submitted to Frontiers in Microbiology and is under reviewed. Additionally, To understand the molecular basis of the catalytic mechanism of CtpA, the crystallographic study was applied on CtpA. Needle-like crystals obtained. The best resolution of the diffraction data so far is 3.5 Å. Model building is in progress. Based on the partially built model, CtpA was composed of three domains, the N-terminal domain, the PDZ domain and the protease domain. The N-terminal domain was responsible for the dimerization of CtpA. The limited data quality makes it difficult to build the model, optimization of crystallization will be carried out to obtain higher resolution of the structure. Objective 4: We successfully constructed fliS-null, hp1076-null and ctpA-null strains. Additionally, we applied cell fractionation, western blot and LC-MS to characterize the importance of HP1076 and CtpA. Our data indicated both HP1076 and CtpA are membrane-associated proteins in H. pylori. To unravel the mechanism of how CtpA cleaves HP1076, we analyzed the product of HP1076 after digestion by CtpA using mass spectrometry. In line with the other C-terminal proteases, multiple cleavage sites were detected. To understand the roles of HP1076 and CtpA in the flagella system, negative staining and transmission electron microscopy were applied on both H. pylori wild type and HP1076-null and ctpA-null strains. While HP1076-null strain did not impact on flagellation, ctpA-null strain was non-flagellated. Consistent with that, cell motility assay showed ctpA-null strain was immotile. These results indicating that CtpA is critical for flagellar system.

14100114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100114.value: In this study, we have resolved the molecular structure of export chaperone FliS in complex with flagellin and HP1076. Although the D0 domain of flagellins are well conserved, when compared with other known structures of FliS-FliC binary complexes, H. pylori flagellin adopts a different conformation when it is bound on FliS. Specifically, the first two helices are oriented like a hair-pin that occupy one face (helices α3-α4) of FliS. Given the relatively high structural and sequence homology of the D0 domain of FliC in other bacterial species, it is intriguing why FlaB adopts a different helical arrangement upon FliS interaction. We speculate that the fold is guided by the groove generated by variable residues Tyr79 and His86 of FliS. The insertion of Phe485 of FlaB into the hydrophobic pocket of FliS further promotes the binding of the hairpin to FliS. The orientation of FlaB revealed from our structure will provide insights to understand how the C-terminal D0 domain of flagellin can stabilize TLR5 for activation. In addition, HP1076 shares both structural similarity and FliS binding interface with the D1 domain of flagellin, suggesting it might be a substrate of FliS. On the other hand, through interaction studies, we isolated CtpA as an interacting partner of HP1076. We have also collected a 3.4A data from a CtpA co-crystallized with HP1076 peptides to investigate the molecular mechanism of substrate recogntion and cleavage. Molecular genetic studies indicated that CtpA is essential for flagellation and motility. To our understanding, this will be the first study to report the association of C_teminal protease to flagellar system.

14100114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100114.value: We will continue the model building and refinement of CtpA. In addition, since we have generated various knock-out mutant strains in H.pylori. We will applied cross-linking, fractionation studies and LC-MS to characterize the functional relationship of CtpA in flagellar system and beyond. We will also extend our work to identify other CtpA substrates in H.pylori.

14100114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100114.value: Formation of functional flagella plays a critical role in bacterial survival and host colonization, and is a wide-spread virulence factor. The flagellar synthesis is a complex but highly coordinated process. Flagellin also has an essential role in triggering the innate immunity throught toll-like receptors. Interestingly, H. pylori have evolved flagellins evades the TLR5 recognition. This project aims to study the molecular basis of substrate recognition by export chaperone FliS. Our studies have revealed the atomic details of FliS in complex with flagellin from H. pylori and also identified a novel protein CtpA associated to flagellar system. Our findings will strengthen our understanding of the distinct strategy exploited by H. pylori for its survival and infection and will provide new avenues for studying an important virulence factor secretion system.

14100514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100514.value: Oncogenes are critical for tumor progression and maintenance. Targeting oncoproteins with small molecule inhibitors holds great promises in many cancers. However, the acquisition of drug resistance poses significant challenges. Various mechanisms have been implicated. These include increase in drug efflux and the acquisition of new mutations that can subvert drug-binding. Thus, research aiming to preempt drug resistance will extend survival or reduce tumor relapse. This application studies a new paradigm of drug resistance whereby tumor generate supportive stromal cells to sustain a “chemoresistant niche” to promote survival of cancer cells. This is based on observations made in neuroblastoma (NB), an extracranial pediatric tumor of neural crest origin. NB have the highest incidence among infants. High risk NB are metastatic with a 5-year survival rate of 40% even with aggressive therapies. Genome-wide search for driver oncogenes in familial NB uncovered mutations in the Anaplastic Large cell Lymphoma Kinase gene (ALK). The incidence of ALK mutation in sporadic NB is 7% while 77% of advanced stage patients have more expression of ALK. Intense efforts are underway to develop kinase inhibitors that can eradicate ALK-positive tumors. Treatment of an ALK-positive neuroblastoma cell line with a kinase inhibitor, TAE684, led to the emergence of resistant cells comprising of a mixture of predominantly Schwann-like cells and a few neuroblastic tumor cells. As neural crest progenitors are cells of origin, this observation raises the possibility that tumor-derived Schwann-like cells confer survival to neuroblastic tumor cells. Indeed, co-culture experiments demonstrated the ability of Schwann-like cells to protect neuroblastic tumor cells from the apoptotic effects of TAE684. Mechanistically, this protective effect was mediated by cell-cell interactions and paracrine factors. Cell-cell interactions upregulated Stat3 signaling while heparin-binding growth factors (HBGFs) secreted by Schwann-like cells enhanced the survival of neuroblastic tumor cells through the PI3-K pathway. Attempts to isolate relevant HBGFs have identified a Wnt modulator, secreted Frizzled-Related Protein 1 (sFRP1). This proposal aims to achieve four major goals. First, whether this mechanism of chemoresistance is generally applicable will be tested. Second, the functional relevance of Stat3 and Akt signaling will be examined. Thirdly, the role of Wnt signaling in promoting tumor cell viability will be tested. Finally, animal models will test if targeted therapy can be enhanced by disrupting this chemoresistant niche. Results will have strong impact on understanding treatment resistance in targeted therapy of many cancer types. 原癌基因在腫瘤的形成以及維持過程中起關鍵作用。在多種癌症中，小分子抑製劑靶向原癌基因蛋白的治療方法大有前景。但是，隨之而來的耐藥性問題帶來顯著挑戰。耐藥性的產生涉及多種機制，包括增加藥物排出以及突變改變藥物作用靶點等。因此，研究機體的耐藥性有助於延長患者生存期或者減少復發。本項目研究產生耐藥性的一種新機制——腫瘤基質細胞包含的抵抗藥物的“壁龕”可以促進腫瘤細胞的存活。這一結論基於對成神經母細胞瘤（neuroblastoma, NB）的研究。 NB是一種發起於原始神經嵴細胞的兒童顱外腫瘤，最常見於嬰幼兒。高危組NB患者，即使使用各種強化的治療方法，五年的存活率也僅為40%。對家族型NB的基因組序列搜索發現間變淋巴瘤激酶（anaplastic lymphoma kinase，ALK）的突變驅動NB的發生。 NB患者中ALK突變的概率是7%。而有77%的NB晚期患者出現ALK過表達現象。針對ALK陽性腫瘤的癌症激酶抑製劑仍在不斷的研究中。TAE684是一種激酶抑製劑。用其處理ALK陽性的NB細胞株，SK-N-SH，存活的細胞為大量Schwann樣細胞和少量神經母細胞的混合。由於細胞均起源自神經嵴祖細胞，這一結果提供了一種假設，即NB中的Schwann樣細胞協助神經母細胞的存活。事實上，細胞共培養實驗證明Schwann細胞幫助神經母細胞免於TAE684的凋亡作用。這一保護機制由細胞間相互作用與旁分泌因子共同調控。細胞間相互作用上調Stat3信號通路。 Schwann細胞分泌的肝素結合生長因子（heparin-binding growth factors，HBGFs）通過PI3-K通路加強神經母細胞的存活。分離HBGFs得到一個Wnt調節因子，分泌型捲曲相關蛋白1（secreted Frizzled-Related Protein 1，sFRP1）。本研究旨在達成以下四個目標。一，檢測上文提及的耐藥性機制是否廣泛適用。二，研究Stat3和Akt信號通路的功能相關性。三，研究Wnt通路在增強腫瘤細胞活性中的作用。四，使用動物模型檢測去除這一耐藥機制可否增強靶向治療作用。研究結果將有助於理解在多種腫瘤靶向治療過程中出現的耐藥問題。

14100514.label: Realisation of objectives
14100514.value: Objective 1. We have completed this objective by characterizing two additional N-type (BE(2)-M17, IMR32), and S-type (EP1, SK-N-SH S1, S2, S3) cell lines. Of note, we utilized substantial amount of time to rederive S-type cells from SK-N-SH cell line since we realized there are considerable variations in the literature concerning this cell line. For that, the earliest possible passage (P35) was purchased from ATCC and clonal S-type sublines (S0, S1, S2, S3) were regenerated. We believe this will enhance the validity of our results by using cells that resemble to the original metastatic lesion. To our surprise, the early passage SK-N-SH cultures are composed predominantly of S-type rather than N-type cells. Comixing experiments with these S-type cells demonstrated the ability of heterologous N- and S-type pairings could synergistically activate downstream signalling events. For example, co-culturing N-type cells from SK-N-SH (NC3) and BE(2)-M17 synergistically stimulated the phosphorylation of STAT3 and AKT. However, coculturing S-type cells with IMR32 only stimulated STAT3 but not AKT. We have investigated two additional N-type cells proposed – KELLY and LA55N for apoptosis assays but the results were negative. However, we did observed an ~3-fold decrease in necrotic cell death in N-type cells when co-culturing with another independent S-type cell line, LA1-5S. Objective 2. We have completed this objective by performing co-culturing experiments using N- and S-type cells. In addition, we also tested conditioned medium (CM) derived from S-type cells. For co-culturing experiments, we have tested a total of 6 S-type cells in synergistic activation of STAT3 but not AKT. This is correlated with their abilities to promote survival of N-type cells against the anti-ALK inhibitor, TAE684. For CM treatment, we were able to show that CM from three S-type sublines, S1, S2, and S3 promoted cell proliferation as well as cell viability of N-type cells by cell counting and MTS-based biological assays. Unlike co-cultures, we found CM was able to stimulate not just STAT3 but also AKT and ALK. As ALK can stimulate both STAT3 and AKT signalling, we also investigated if the further activation of ALK by CM could lead to STAT or AKT activation. While ALK blockade eliminated AKT and ERK signalling, STAT3 activation was not completely blocked. This data suggest that ALK independent paracrine factor(s) in STAT3 activation. Objective 3. Based on our unexpected observation in Objective 1, it is cleared that tumor initiating cells (TIC) may first populate the bone marrow microenvironment and subsequently differentiating into N- and S-type cells. We initiate to isolate TIC using the well-established stem cell markers, CD133 and CD44. Four groups of cells were flow sorted: (i) CD133+CD44+ (stem cells), (ii) CD133+CD44- (stem cells), (iii) CD133-CD44+ (Schwann cells), (iv) CD133-CD44- (N-type cells), and the parental SK-N-SH were injected subcutaneously into immune-deficient nude mice. Subcutaneous injection was selected prior to injection into the bone marrow compartment. We found that both CD133+CD44+ and CD133+CD44- stem cell populations were able to induce tumors with a latency of 2 months. We have not completed the part of the study by directly injecting tumor stem cells into the bone marrow. Objective 4 We proposed to identify secreted factors from S-type cells that could confer chemoresistance to TAE684. We have first examined the expression of 18 cytokines and identified IL-6 being the only one that expressed in S-type cells. However, the concentration of IL-6 in CM was insufficient to promote STAT3 activation and cell viability. To identify novel factors, RNA-Seq analysis was used to compare N- and S-type cells. We identified 1460 down-regulated genes and 1334 up-regulated genes mostly enriched in TGF-b, Wnt, and inflammatory mediator pathways. By integrating DEGs upregulated in S-type cells with the human secretome database, we uncovered 336 genes. Next, CMs from S-and N-types cells were subjected to proteomic analysis using mass spectroscopy techniques. We identified 74 proteins that specifically expressed in S-type cells. Integrating the RNA-Seq and proteomic data narrowed down the candidate soluble factors to 53 genes, which were enriched in Fas and integrin signalling pathway. By literature search, 6 genes (POSTN, LEG1, PAI1, SPARC, GRN, and HSPA5) were shown to be linked to STAT3 signaling. Among those, we were successful in validating four (POSTN, LEG1, PAI1, SPARC) with RT-qPCR. We further confirmed their abilities in activating STAT3 and a clear positive pro-survival effect against TAE684 was demonstrated in one, POSTN. Therefore, this objective was rigorously pursued and yielded solid result. Objective 5. We proposed to investigate TAE684-treated sublines (TR1 to TR4) in regulating N-type cells functions. We also proposed to differentiate between tumor-derived Schwann cells with normal Schwann cells as well as mesenchymal stem cells (hMSC). For the first part and as indicated in objective 1, we uncovered that S-type cells are the predominant cell type in early passage SK-N-SH. The TR sublines proposed were derived from SK-N-SH that have been passaged for multiple rounds. For this reason, we redirected our experiments to focus more on the newly isolated S-type cells (S1, S2, S3, and S4), which is of more relevance. In addition, we also proposed to study sFRP1 secreted factor. We compared and confirmed the expression of sFRP1 in 6 S-type cell lines (S0, S1, S2, S3, EP1, and TRC4) and uncovered S3 cell line secreting the highest amount of sFRP1. We also consumed a vast amount of time in generating recombinant SFRP1 using the baculovirus system. However, we encountered considerable hurdles in having sufficient large quantity of the Histidine-tagged sFRP1 protein. While this was in progress, we were successful in identifying 4 novel factors that could stimulate STAT3 (see Objective 4). Therefore, we diverted our efforts instead to work on POSTN, LEG1, PAI1, and SPARC. As to the lineage plasticity experiments, we conducted two lines of research. First, 47 single cells were captured from early passage SK-N-SH cell line and qPCR analysis was carried out using 49 pairs of lineage- and pathway-specific primer pairs covering Schwann cells, sympathoadrenal, early neural crest, undifferentiated neural crest, neural progenitor, neuronal and migrating neural crest. Heat map and violin plot analysis revealed tremendous lineage diversity. In the second set of experiments, we compared the transcriptomes of two pairs of N-, S-, hMSC and normal human Schwann (hSC) cell cultures. Principal component analysis revealed closer but distinct relationship between S-type, N-type and hSC. Hierarchical clustering suggest closer relationship between S- and N-type cells probably due to their same origin. In contrast, hMSC is very distinct. The most interesting comparison is between normal (hSC) and tumor-derived (S-type) Schwann cells. There were 3839 genes up-regulated and 3015 genes down-regulated. Gene Ontology term revealed significant differences in glycosaminoglycan binding, calcium ion binding, and heparin binding. We plan to publish this in the near future. Objective 6. We made a modification in our original strategy in removing S-type cells from NB tumors. Based on overwhelming data suggesting the critical role of STAT3 in sustaining N-type cell proliferation and survival, we spent considerable efforts aimed at expressing a dominant negative STAT3 Y705F mutant in S-type cells for in vivo tumor assays. We have tried lentiviral-based vector but were unsuccessful. We were only recently successful in generating stable cell lines by retroviral-based vector and is currently characterizing the lines for their ability to promote tumor growth in vivo.

14100514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100514.value: There are three major findings. First, our results provide a glimpse into the tumor microenvironment of a metastatic lesions within the bone marrow of a neuroblastoma patient. Study of early passaged SK-N-SH revealed a predominantly Schwannian S-type cells with minimal neuroblastic N-type tumor cells. This is unexpected as the literature in the past few decades has almost exclusively focused on N-type cells and the authenticity of SK-N-SH cell line use should be carefully stated in future publications. We further demonstrated that S-type cells confer survival to N-type cells against the anti-ALK targeted therapeutics. This pro-survival function is closely linked to STAT3 activation through either cell-cell interaction or paracrine mode of action. Treatment with STAT3 inhibitor markedly blocked conditioned medium from S-type cells in promoting survival in N-type cells treated with anti-ALK targeted drug. This finding could be extended to additional S- and N-type cells suggesting that this symbiotic relationship is not restricted to a single cell line. We further conclude that Schwannian S-type cells may provide a favourable microenvironment for N-type tumor cells to thrive. The second finding is related to the molecular insight into the lineage specification of bone marrow metastatic lesions in neuroblastoma patients. By single cell qPCR analysis, we discovered diverse lineage specification of the Schwannian S-type cells with sympathoadrenal (GATA2/3), neural progenitor (PAX6), neuronal (MAP2), as well as early neural crest (SNAIL/SLUG) marker expression. We also provided a first analysis of the transcriptomes of tumor-derived Schwann cells, normal Schwann cells, mesenchymal stem cells and neuroblastic tumor cells. These analyses suggest that tumor-derived Schwann cells are very distinct from normal Schwann cells or mesenchymal stem cells. Cell sorting and in vivo tumorigenicity assay identified CD133+CD44+ as well as CD133+CD44- populations that may be the tumor-initiating populations in the initial seeding of the bone marrow site. Our third major finding is the finding that IL-6 is the major cytokine secreted by S-type cells but on its own is insufficient to confer STAT3 activation and survival. Instead, proteomics analysis revealed four secreted proteins, POSTN, LEG1, PAI1, SPARC with the capacity to stimulate STAT3 and with POSTN harbouring the ability to promote cell survival against anti-ALK inhibitor. We conclude that a combination of these secreted factors is necessary to mediate the symbiotic interaction between S- and N-type cells. Overall, we believe our results contribute new molecular insights into the cross talk between heterogeneous cell types in metastatic neuroblastoma.

14100514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100514.value: There are several areas for future research. First, we will confirm our findings using clinical specimens isolated from bone marrow metastases of neuroblastoma patients by initiating collaboration with Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Detailed histological and lineage specific marker expression will be examined. Second, we have identified paracrine factors involved in the cross talk between N- and S-type cells. However, we were unable to identify the surface molecules that mediate the cell-cell interaction. Based on our transcriptome data, we already identified surface integrin molecules and adhesion receptors that are differentially expressed in N- and S-type cells. Their functional relevance will be tested by siRNA-mediated gene silencing. Thirdly, we will further study the four paracrine factors (POSTN, LEG1, PAI1, SPARC) isolated by testing if their blockade by neutralizing antibodies can disrupt pro-survival crosstalk. Fourthly, we will finish our animal studies in testing the two CD133+ stem cell populations isolated as well as the STAT3 dominant negative mutant expressing S-type cells. We understand this deficiency in our output and aim to rectify this in the immediate future. Finally, we will further mine the differentially expressed genes in tumor-derived Schwann cells in order to identify novel therapeutic targets.

14100514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100514.value: Neuroblastoma is one of the most common childhood solid tumor. The overall survival is not ideal and the high risk form metastasizes frequently to the bone marrow and has poor outcome in general. Apart from conventional chemo- and radio-therapies, targeted therapy that aims to eliminate tumors based on specific gene mutations have gained considerable attention. However, how metastatic tumor cells within the bone marrow respond to targeted therapy is not fully understood. Our research made two critical findings. First, neuroblastoma tumor cells that migrated to the bone barrow are not monolithic in nature and are in fact composed of a variety of tumor cell types that provide nourishing factors for tumor cells to thrive. We found that this nourishing environment can reduce the effectiveness of targeted therapy. The second finding is that we have identified molecules produced by metastatic cells that act on surrounding tumor cells so that they survive better. Our research is highly translational. It is well-established that tumor cells treated with targeted therapy have mechanisms in subverting the drug actions. Our findings will lead to the development of combination therapy by combining targeted therapeutic drugs with other inhibitors in order to achieve greater tumor-killing potential.

14100614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100614.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is a very common sport injury resulting in an unstable knee. As a ruptured ACL does not heal, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) is the standard treatment to restore knee function. The surgical procedure of ACLR involves the use of a tendon graft to replace the ruptured ACL. Surgeons drill bone tunnels on distal femur and proximal tibia, insert the tendon graft through the bone tunnels and secure the graft in place. Poor graft healing is the major cause leading to ACLR failure and excessive knee laxity, because the graft tissue is weakened with decreased mechanical properties under hostile micro-environment at early healing phase, which never return to the original level. Glycyl-histidyl-lysine tripeptide copper complex (GHK-Cu) is a well-known activator of tissue remodeling, which is used in many skin products. In the 2011 GRF project, we found that GHK-Cu can enhance graft incorporation and improve restoration of knee laxity. However, repeated intra-articular injections of GHK-Cu at post inflammatory phase may bring unnecessary tissue responses. In 2013, we are supported by GRF to develop a controlled delivery system of GHK-Cu with a temperature-sensitive hydrogel for ease of coating on the graft. However, a timely dosing of GHK-Cu will need more information about how GHK-Cu acts at different stages of graft healing. In order to facilitate the clinical use of GHK-Cu to promote graft healing in ACLR, we propose to collect information about the cellular responses to GHK-Cu at early healing stage, proliferation stage and ligamentization stage of ACLR. The findings of this project will help to devise when and how much GHK-Cu is needed to promote graft healing, thus complementing the controlled delivery system for clinical use. As there are over 1200 ACLR in Hong Kong per year, with over 200,000 ACLR in US per year and probably millions in the world; our study will not just benefit the patients Hong Kong but worldwide. 前十字韌帶(ACL)撕裂是常見的運動損傷，令膝關節變得不穩定。由於ACL撕裂後不能復原，ACL重建手術(ACLR)是標準的治療方法以恢復膝關節功能。手術會利用肌腱移植物取代撕裂的ACL。外科醫生會在股骨遠端和脛骨近端鑽開骨隧道，把肌腱移植物穿過並固定於隧道內。不過移植物若癒合不好，移植物的力學性能在早期癒合時期惡劣的環境下會下降，並導致關節鬆弛，無法回復到受傷前的運動能力。 藍銅勝肽(GHK-Cu)是一種常用於皮膚產品的組織重構活化劑。在2011年的GRF 項目中，我們發現GHK-Cu能加強移植物與骨頭的癒合並改善膝關節鬆弛的問題，然而於發炎期後重覆注射GHK-Cu到關節內會引致不必要的組織反應。2013年我們獲得GRF的資助，發展在移植物上塗上含GHK-Cu的熱敏水凝膠藥物緩釋系統。不過，我們需要更多GHK-Cu於不同癒合時期的作用，以便調控GHK-Cu釋放。為了方便臨床使用GHK-Cu以促進ACLR治療，我們建議研究GHK-Cu在早期癒合階段、細胞增加階段和韌帶化階段對細胞的影響。研究結果將幫助制定釋放GHK-Cu的時間和分量來促進移植物癒合，從而幫助我們建立藥物緩釋系統供臨床應用。現時香港及美國每年有多於1200 及20,000宗 ACLR進行，全世界甚或有過百萬人需要進行ACLR; 我們的研究將會幫助香港以至全世界的病人。

14100614.label: Realisation of objectives
14100614.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. To achieve the first objective, anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) were perform in SD rats, at different ACLR healing stages, rats were sacrificed and healing cells were isolated from the graft and bone tunnels. Cells were cultured and the cellular activities in relation to cell repopulation and tissue remodeling in the healing cell cultures were measured by BrdU assay and quantitative gene expression of tissue remodeling related genes (Pro-collagen I and Pro-collagen II, MMP1, TIMP1). To achieve the second objective, healing cells isolated at different healing stages were treated with different dose of GHK-Cu. The effect of GHK-Cu on cell proliferation was measured by BrdU assay; the effect of GHK-Cu on tissue remodeling were measured by quantitative gene expression of tissue remodeling related genes. The above results have been reported in different international conferences (Orthopaedics Research Society Annual meeting 2016, ISL&T 2016, 2017, HKOA 2015) and 1 manuscript is under preparation.

14100614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100614.value: ACLR healing is a complicated process which involved graft remodeling and osteo-intergradation. The temporal changes in cellular responses in the tendon graft and the origin of these healing cells are largely unknown; therefore, the timing of treatment has not been optimized. The natural healing process of ACLR involves cell proliferation and cell recruitment in the early phase, cell repopulation and matrix synthesis and remodeling in the graft remodeling phase. By knowing the temporal changes in cellular response at different healing stages, biological modulation target to specific cellular response or healing phase could be performed and further enhance treatment outcome. In this study, we aim to investigate the cellular response of healing cells at different healing phase during ACLR graft healing. Histological study of ACLR healing graft was performed at week1, 2, 6, 12 and 24 post ACLR. From the hematoxylin and eosin staining, cellularity was increased at week 1 and reached highest at week2. Cellularity was reduced from week6 onwards. Consistence to histological result, total number of cell released from the graft was highest at week2 and reduced from week6, 12 and 24. Cell proliferation was measured by BrdU assay, cell proliferation rate was decreased as the time points post ACLR increased (p<0.05). Matrix remodeling genes (pro-col1A1, pro-col3, MMP1, TIMP1) expressions at different time points were measured by qRT-PCR. The mRNA expression of pro-col1A1, pro-col3, TIMP1 and MMP1 were up-regulated (p<0.05). At week12, cell proliferation was further decreased (p<0.05). In addition, pro-col1A1, pro-col3, TIMP1 mRNA expressions were also decreased (p<0.05) while MMP1 reached the highest mRNA expression level (p<0.05). At week24, cell proliferation and collagens mRNA expressions were stabilized (p<0.05). However, TIMP1 and MMP1 mRNA expressions were down-regulated (p<0.05). In response to GHK treatment, week1-healing-cells significantly increased pro-col1A1, MMP1, MMP13 and TIMP1 expression (p<0.05); MMP1 expression was increased while pro-col1A1 was decreased in week2-healing-cells (p<0.05); week12-healing-cells significantly reduced pro-col1A1, MMP1, MMP13 and TIMP1 expressions and increased pro-col3 expression (p<0.05); similarly, week24-healing-cells reduced pro-col1A1 , MMP1, MMP13, and increased pro-col3 expression (p<0.05). In conclusion, temporal changes of cellular activity in cell proliferation, matrix remodeling was observed in healing cells at different healing stages. In addition, the result of the effect of GHK-Cu on healing cells isolated from early phase was more responsive as compared with later time points. The results of this study provide a time reference for the suitable time of treatment and the biological modulation could be defined.

14100614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100614.value: In this study, we demonstrated the temporal differences in cellular activities of ACLR healing cells at different healing stages, these finding could provide a time reference for the suitable time of treatment and the biological modulation could be defined. In addition, in previous study, GHK-Cu enhanced ACLR healing with multiple intra-articular injections. In this study, we demonstrated GHK-Cu affected the cell proliferation and tissue remodeling related gene expression, especially in cells isolated at early stage as compared with later time points. Thus, the GHK-Cu injection should be performed at the early time point as healing cells isolated at later time points did not response well.

14100614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100614.value: ACL injury is common across different populations. ACLR is the standard treatment of ACL injury. However, the graft healing process is less characterized. Different biological studies have been attempted to promote graft healing in ACLR. However, the best time of treatment was not defined, as the temporal changes in cellular response in the healing graft are largely unknown. Previously, we demonstrated that multiple intra-articular injections of Glycyl-Histidyl-Lysine-copper complex (GHK-Cu), an activator of tissue remodeling, could transiently promote graft healing. The results of this study showed that cells isolated from different time post ACLR have different cell proliferation and graft remodeling genes expression. In addition, cell isolated from different time points also exhibited different responses to GHK-Cu. GHK-Cu increased collagens expression and MMPs expressions in cell isolated from early time points post ACLR (week 1 and 2); whereas, GHK-Cu reduced collagen and MMPs expressions in cell isolated from late time points. These results implicated that during ACLR healing, cellular activity of the healing cells is different across time and responded to treatment differently. With the current results, GHK-Cu targeted at the first 2 weeks post ACLR might be more effective in healing.

14100714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100714.value: 亨廷頓舞蹈症 （Huntington’s Disease， HD） 是由亨廷頓 （Huntingtin， Htt） 基因中編碼穀氨酰胺的CAG三核苷酸重複序列異常擴展所致。亨廷頓疾病蛋白富含多聚穀氨酰胺 （polyglutamine， polyQ）的結構域擴展引起了亨廷頓舞蹈症的毒性。亨廷頓疾病的發病機制極為複雜，近幾年的研究進展讓我們開始逐漸了解每一條獨立的分子致病通路是如何參與入亨廷頓疾病細胞和生理層面的致病機理中。通過之前在我們實驗室開展的遺傳修飾因子的篩選，我們發現一個在發育過程中參與建立平面細胞極性的被稱作fuzzy (fy) 的基因，在果蠅模型中有調控polyQ疾病毒性的功能。我們進一步發現fy的人類同源基因Fuz，同樣可以在人類細胞模型中調控亨廷頓疾病的毒性。基於我們前期的實驗數據，我們假設Fuz蛋白從兩方面影響亨廷頓舞蹈症的致病進程。在此實驗設計中，我們計劃闡明Fuz所在的誘導細胞死亡的信號通路，同時研究Fuz在亨廷頓舞蹈症中的作用。研究Fuz在亨廷頓疾病中的具體功能有助於我們更好地了解亨廷頓舞蹈症的發病機制。

14100714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100714.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP) signalling governs a range of cellular processes, including directional cell migration and the establishment of cytoskeletal structures. Mutations in the PCP-related gene Fuz have been associated with neural tube defects in humans. In this report, we demonstrate a novel proapoptotic function of Fuz and reveal the involvement of the Dvl-Rac1-MAPK-caspase signalling axis in Fuz-induced apoptosis. Interestingly, we found that Fuz transcription was upregulated in the context of polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases, a group of neurodegenerative diseases, including Huntington's Disease, caused by CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion. The suppression of Fuz expression rescued polyQ-induced neurodegeneration both in vitro and in vivo. We further identified Yin Yang 1 (YY1) as a transcriptional repressor of Fuz that binds to and facilitates CpG DNA methylation of the Fuz promoter. Meanwhile, we observed a reduced level of soluble YY1 protein in polyQ patient brain samples, such reduction compromises YY1 cellular function and transcriptionally derepresses Fuz. The consequent upregulation of Fuz expression leads to apoptosis via the Dvl-Rac1-MAPK-caspase signalling axis. In this study, we characterised a novel proapoptotic role for the PCP-related gene Fuz, and demonstrated a YY1-dependent transcriptional Fuz derepression mechanism in polyQ diseases. Our group is the first to demonstrate that expanded polyQ can trigger apoptosis by derepressing the expression of a proapoptotic gene. In summary, this report provides new insights into polyQ pathogenesis by unveiling a pathogenic pathway involving the transcriptional regulator YY1 and the previously undescribed pro-apoptotic function of Fuz. Targeting of this novel pathway might provide therapeutic benefits.

14100714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100714.value: We are now actively investigating the involvement of Fuz in other disease conditions, and finding compounds that can bring Fuz upregulation back down to a normal level. This will be a novel therapeutic direction toward polyQ (including Huntington's Disease) and Alzheimer’s diseases.

14100714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100714.value: In the past, scientists only considered Fuz as a player in neurodevelopment. We are the first to report this unnoticed cell death-inducing function of Fuz and unveil its role in polyglutamine diseases, including Huntington's Disease. Intriguingly, we also observed that in Alzheimer’s disease, the expression level of Fuz also increased. This unexpected and exciting research finding tells us the Fuz-mediated apoptosis pathway plays some common roles in neurological disorders in general.

14100914.label: Realisation of objectives
14100914.value: We have accomplished all the proposed research objectives in this project. Our major findings are summarized as follows. 1. Objective 1: As planned, we determined the expression patterns of ERRα and multiple key steroidogenic enzymes involved in androgen biosynthesis and their association in two xenograft tumor models of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), VCaP-CRPC and CWR22-AIM, established by us by qRT-PCR and immunoblot analyses. Our results showed that both the CRPC xenograft tumor models expressed significant higher levels of ERRα and several key androgen biosynthetic enzymes (including STAR, CYP11A1, HSD3B2, CYP17A1, AKR1C2, AKR1C3, HSD17B3 and SDR5A2), suggesting that ERRα was closely associated with the up-regulation of some key androgen biosynthetic enzymes. 2. Objective 2: As planned, we characterized and determined the functional roles of ERRα in the castration-resistant or androgen-insensitive growth of prostate cancer by both stable ERRα-overexpression and shRNA-mediated knockdown approaches in two androgen receptor (AR) –positive prostate cancer cell lines (LNCaP and VCaP) and one AR-negative line (DU145) by retroviral transduction and lentiviral infection. (a) Our results showed that ERRα overexpression (LNCaP/VCaP-ERRα transduced cells) could enhance in vitro resistance to culture condition with charcoal-stripped serum (CS-FBS, mimicking androgen-deprivation)and antiandrogen (enzalutamide) in AR-positive but not AR-negative prostate cancer cells, and also enhance the in vivo resistance to castration as demonstrated by xenograft tumors grown by LNCaP-ERRα cells in castrated host immunodeficient mice. (b) Conversely, knockdown of endogenous ERRα in LNCaP cells (LNCaP-shERRα) could enhance or potentiate the growth inhibition as induced by androgen-deprivation (CS-FBS) and antiandrogen in AR-positive LNCaP-shERRα cells as compared to control LNCaP-shScramble cells. (c) Moreover, pharmacological inhibition of ERRα activity by an ERRα-specific inverse agonist XCT790 could significantly sensitize or potentiate the growth inhibition as exerted by androgen-deprivation and antiandrogen in AR-positive VCaP cells but induce no changes in growth inhibition in AR-negative and ERRα-knockdowned DU145-shERRα transduced cells when they were cultured under the same conditions with CS-FBS and antiandrogen as for AR-positive LNCaP-shERRα transduced cells. 3. Objective 3: As planned, we characterized whether ERRα could directly target to some key androgen biosynthetic enzyme genes, which showed up-regulation in both xenograft tumor models of CRPC and also ERRα-overexpressed prostate cancer cells by gene promoter sequence analysis, reporter gene and ChIP assays, in order to determine the specific role of ERRα in transcriptional regulation of the identified steroidogenic enzyme genes. Our results characterized that ERRα could directly transactivate two androgen biosynthetic enzyme genes, CYP11A1 and AKR1C3, in prostate cancer cells. 4. Objective 4: As planned, we determined the intracellular and intratumoral androgen levels in both the cultured prostate cancer cells (LNCaP and VCaP) and CRPC xenograft tumors by ultra-high performance coupled with tandem-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). Our results showed that both the LNCaP-ERRα and VCaP-ERRα transduced cells and the castration-relapse VCaP-CRPC xenograft tumors contained significant higher intracellular and intratumoral levels of androgens (testosterone/T and dihydrotestosterone/DHT), indicating that ERRα could play a role in intratumoral androgen biosynthesis in CRPC. • Some of the results as revealed by the study Objectives 1-4 have been submitted for publication recently and the manuscript is currently being revised for resubmission (Theranostics manuscript no. 35589s). 5. Objective 5: As planned, we analyzed the genomics datasets obtained from the Cancer Genome Atlas-Cancer Genomics (TCGA) in order to identify the potential molecular targets or determinants associated with or responsible for the up-regulation of ERRα in primary prostate cancer or CRPC patients. Our analysis identified that ERRα exhibited a significant positive expression correlation with an oncogenic transcription factor ERG expressed by the fusion gene TMPRSS2:ERG expressed in clinical prostate cancer samples. Further expression analysis of the association between ERRα and ERG expression revealed that their increased co-expressions were closely associated with higher Gleason scores and metastasis in CRPC patients. Based on this finding, we further characterized and dissected in detail the functional relational relation between the nuclear receptor ERRα and transcription factor ERG and also their molecular link in prostate cancer cells. Our detailed functional and mechanistic analyses showed that ERRα and ERG could synergistically regulated each other at their promoters or regulatory regions and both form a reciprocal positive regulatory loop to promote the advanced growth of prostate cancer via their respective signaling pathways. • Our results as revealed by the study Objective 5 have been published recently (Xu et al., Oncogene 2018;37:6259-6274).

14100914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100914.value: Our major findings obtained by this GRF-funded study on the role of nuclear receptor ERRα in castration-resistant prostate cancer are summarized as follows: 1. Enhanced intratumoral androgen biosynthesis and persistent AR signaling are regarded as key factors responsible for the therapy-resistant growth of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Residual intraprostatic androgens can be derived from de novo synthesis of androgens from cholesterol or conversion from adrenal androgens by steroidogenic enzymes expressed in prostate cancer cells via different steroidogenic pathways. However, dysregulation of androgen biosynthetic enzymes in CRPC still remains poorly understood so far. One major finding of this study was that ERRα, which exhibited an up-regulation in clinical metastatic CRPC and experimental CRPC xenograft models, could act to promote castration-resistant growth capacity vis its direct transactivation of two key androgen biosynthetic enzymes CYP11A1 and AKR1C3, and hence enhance intraprostatic production of dihydrotestosterone (DHT) and reactivation of AR signaling in prostate cancer cells. Our findings also provides a novel insight that targeting ERRα could be a potential therapeutic strategy for CRPC management as pharmacological inhibition of its activity by inverse agonist could help to attenuate the intraprostatic androgen production and hence suppress AR signaling in prostate cancer cells. Some of these major findings have been submitted for publication and is currently being revised for resubmission (Theranostics). 2. Another major finding of this study is the identification of oncogenic transcription factor ERG expressed by the TMPRSS2:ERG (T:E) fusion gene that is responsible for the up-regulation of ERRα in advanced prostate cancer. Through genomics analysis of TCGA cancer genomics datasets, we revealed that up-regulation of ERRα was positively correlated with the ERG in clinical prostate cancer samples, and their increased co-expression patterns were closely associated with higher Gleason scores and shorter survival in patients. Through detailed molecular analyses, we showed that ERRα could directly transactivate T:E fusion gene in both AR-positive and –negative prostate cancer cells via both ERRE and ARE-dependent manners. Intriguingly, ERG could also conversely transactivate the ERRα (ESRRA) gene promoter. Hereby, ERRα and ERG could synergistically regulate each other at transcriptional level and both form a reciprocal loop to promote the advanced growth of prostate cancer. Our finding also provides an insight that targeting ERRα could be a potential therapeutic strategy for management of aggressive T:E-positive prostate cancer as ERRα activity could be suppressed by ERRα inverse agonist. Our findings have been published recently (Xu et al., Oncogene 2018;37:6259-6274).

14100914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100914.value: 1. In this GRF-supported study, we have elucidated the functional roles of ERRα on its contribution to enhanced intraprostatic androgen biosynthesis and incessant AR signaling in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) via its transcriptional control of multiple steroidogenic enzyme genes, and also ERRα and transcription factor ERG can synergistically regulate each other at transcriptional level formin a reciprocal regulatory loop to advance the growth of prostate cancer via their respective downstream pathways. 2. Besides these findings, we also demonstrated that pharmacological targeting ERRα could reduce the intracellular androgen production and thus suppress AR-axis signaling, and also suppress the expression of oncogenic fusion gene T:E in prostate cancer cells. These noteworthy findings provide a novel insight and also open a new research avenue that targeting ERRα could be of therapeutic value and beneficial to advanced prostate cancer patients. This potential therapeutic approach is different from the conventional approach in the hormone therapy for prostate cancer by merely targeting to the AR or its signaling via androgen-deprivation or suppression of AR by antiandrogen. It will be worthwhile to further evaluate the therapeutic significance of targeting ERRα in clinically relevant in vivo models of prostate cancer, such as patient-derived xenograft models and CRPC models.

14100914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100914.value: Prostate cancer is a common male cancer in Hong Kong, being ranked the 3rd common cancer in recent years. This cancer is unique in its initial slow growth and androgen-dependence, thus surgery and hormone-therapy are the two mainstream treatment options. Unfortunately, many hormone therapy-treated patients will inevitably relapse and progress to a lethal hormone-independent and metastatic disease (hormone-refractory or castration-resistant prostate cancer CRPC). Intratumoral androgen biosynthesis and persistent androgen receptor (AR) signaling are considered as key factors contributing to CRPC progression. In this study, we demonstrate that the nuclear receptor estrogen-related receptor alpha (ERRα) is an important biomarker of CRPC as it can function to promote intratumoral androgen biosynthesis and maintain persistent AR signaling in CRPC via its transcriptional control of key steroidogenic enzyme genes, and also to form a reciprocal regulatory loop with an oncogenic transcription factor ERG expressed by TMPRSS2:ERG fusion gene to advance the growth of prostate cancer. One noteworthy finding of this study is that ERRα could be a potential therapeutic target for prostate cancer as its targeting by pharmacological inhibition could help to reduce the intratumoral androgen production, and also to suppress the persistent AR signaling and expression of ERG in advanced prostate cancer.

14101114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101114.value: 精子沿着女性生殖道游向处于输卵管内的卵子是体内成功授精的前提。然而，精子是如何被引导游向授精发生地的问题尚不清晰。早期观察发现，精子在体外能向卵泡液定向游动。这一现象，又称作精子趋向性，提示了精子在女性生殖道游行过程中可能受到了某些趋化因子的指引。然而，目前这些趋化因子的分子构成，以及与其对应的、在精子上的受体的分子构成尚未被阐明。我们的近期研究发现，β-防御素1通过与精子上的趋化因子受体6（CCR6）相互作用，发挥了重要的提升精子活力的作用。有趣的是，配体与CCR6的结合在免疫细胞趋化性中的作用已被充分肯定。重要的是，CCR6还具有结合女性生殖道中表达的其它一些β-防御素的能力。我们的前期工作也显示，CCR6能与精子上的一种Ca2+通道（Catsper）结合并形成复合体，而Catsper已被报道在精子趋向性中发挥作用。这些证据促使我们提出以下工作假设：由颗粒细胞-卵子复合体、输卵管和子宫内膜上皮分泌的不同β-防御素，与精子上的CCR6-Catsper复合体相互结合，共同引导精子在女性生殖道中的迁移；即女性生殖道β-防御素与精子上CCR6-Catsper复合体相互作用可能是精子趋向卵子的分子机制。为了检验该假设，我们提出以下三个研究目标：1）检验β-防御素及其与精子上CCR6的相互作用对精子趋向性的重要性；2）研究β-防御素介导精子趋向性的分子机制；3）通过体内实验阐明β-防御素在女性生殖道参与精子趋向性。此项研究将揭示全新的女性生殖道β-防御素引导精子趋向卵子运动的分子机制，并将促进新型男性不育症诊断和治疗手段的发展。

14101314.label: Project Objectives
14101314.value: To compare and contrast binding patterns of norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) against native infectious viruses and inactivated viruses in vitro and ex vivo.
rows: To compare and contrast binding patterns of norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) against native infectious viruses and inactivated viruses in vitro and ex vivo.

14101314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101314.value: In this study, we primarily aim at comparing and contrasting binding patterns of norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) against native infectious viruses and inactivated viruses in vitro and ex vivo. Human norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis in both developed and developing countries, affecting all age groups. In otherwise healthy individuals norovirus infections are generally mild and self-limiting, however severe clinical outcomes may occur in the elderly and in the immunocompromised. Despite its public health importance, research on norovirus is severely hampered by the fact that the virus remains refractory to infection and productive replication in cell culture. To get around the hurdle, VLPs have been widely used as surrogates in norovirus studies addressing cell biology questions including virus binding, immunogenicity, and vaccine evaluation. VLPs are generally considered to be good surrogates because they are similar in size with and structurally resembling to native viruses. In addition, VLPs exhibit authentic conformation of important antigenic epitopes. Though widely used, direct side-by-side comparison of VLPs with and the relevance of them to native virions remains unexplored and deserves more attention. More importantly, growing evidence highlight discrepancies between findings using VLPs in vitro and native virions in vivo, especially in virus binding studies, raising questions over the biological relevance of VLPs. Binding studies to compare and contrast VLPs and native infectious viruses are urgently needed to support the current use of VLPs or, alternatively, to suggest the use of native virion is necessary. Here we propose a systematic and comprehensive laboratory study to address for the above-mentioned important question. Three forms of human norovirus will be evaluated: VLPs, native infectious viruses, and inactivated viruses. To evaluate virus binding patterns, we will use saliva and synthetic carbohydrate capture ELISA assays, in vitro virus-binding on various intestinal and hematopoietic cell lines and intestinal/immune tissue arrays, as well as ex vivo virus adsorption on duodenal and colonic biopsies. If our findings showed that binding patterns among different forms of noroviruses are highly comparable, this would provide strong support to the validity of VLPs-based analyses. Conversely, if our findings showed substantial differences in binding patterns, this would suggest that use of intact virion (either as native infectious or as inactivated form) are necessary in future binding analyses. More broadly, our findings may shed lights on factors governing virus-binding that may in turn have implications for tissue tropism of norovirus, the biggest known unknown in the field. 這項研究目的是比較諾如（前稱諾沃克）病毒樣顆粒、具感染性的原生諾如病毒和經過滅活的諾如病毒在試管內和體外的結合模式。 人類諾如病毒是急性腸胃炎的主要成因。健康人士如受到諾如病毒感染，病徵一般比較溫和。相反，若發生在長者或有免疫功能缺陷的病人身上，有機會出現嚴重病徵，甚至導致死亡。諾如病毒研究進展緩慢的其中一個主因是到目前為止仍未有一種細胞培養方法能大量複製原生諾如病毒。取以代之，科學界正利用病毒樣顆粒研究諾如病毒的結合模式、免疫原性和疫苗效能。病毒樣顆粒之所以被認為是合適的代替在於它們在大小、結構和重要抗原表位方面與具感染性的原生諾如病毒極為相似，但在其他方面並沒有作出仔細比較。最新證據顯示諾如病毒樣顆粒在試管內和體外的結合模式與原生病毒存在若干重大差異。固此，確實有迫切需要深入研究諾如病毒樣顆粒和原生病毒結合模式之相關性。 針對以上問題，我們提出一個全面性研究。研究對象包括三種形態的人類諾如病毒：病毒樣顆粒、原生病毒和滅活病毒。我們將採用由唾液和合成碳水化合物組成的捕獲酶聯免疫吸附試驗測定法、塗有腸道和造血免疫細胞之組織芯片和取自十二指腸和結腸的體外活檢組織，比較三種諾如病毒形態之間的結合模式。如果研究結果顯示不同形態諾如病毒之間的結合模式非常相似，這會為以病毒樣顆粒為基礎的研究有效性提供有力證據支持。相反，如果研究結果顯示彼此結合模式出現重大差別，就表示將來實驗有必要使用完整的諾如病毒（無論是原生或滅活形態）。長遠而言，研究成果對尋找影響諾如病毒組織嗜性之因素提供重要線索。

14101314.label: Realisation of objectives
14101314.value: We first expressed virus-like particles (VLPs) of a norovirus GII.Pe-GII.4 Sydney strain (CUHK-NS-141) in a baculovirus system as proposed. Complete genome sequence of this strain was available in GenBank with accession number KJ649705. Two forms of VLPs were expressed: one with only the major capsid protein VP1 (denoted as VLP1) and another with both major (VP1) and minor (VP2) capsid proteins (denoted as VLP1+2). Quantification of VLPs, native virus, and inactivated virus were performed by a commercially available and FDA-cleared ELISA-based assay called RIDASCREEN Norovirus 3rd Generation. All subsequent assays were performed using the same amount of virus (ELISA unit equivalent to an optical density of 3 at wavelength 450 nm [OD450nm]). Downstream binding assays included: 1. Saliva (secretor A, B, AB, and O and weak secretor) 2. Histo-blood group antigens (HBGAs A, B, H type 1, H type 2, and Lewis A, B, X, and Y) 3. Cell lines 4. Human intestinal and immune-related tissues. Major findings and research outcome are described in Section 6.1 below. One major unexpected technical difficulty during the study was the unstable performance of antibody-based detection of heat- and formalin-inactivated viruses. Despite of the use of same genome-equivalent amount of viruses per assay, we found substantial reduction (up to 90%) of OD450 in ELISA assay. In other words, all antibody-based detection assay would not be able to truly reflect binding profile of inactivated viruses because antibodies used simply could not detected any bound viruses. We tried to replace the antibody cocktail with different broadly-recognizing norovirus-specific antibodies, including clones P7G3, 17E11, 2002-G5, and SMV59; however performance did not improve. We speculated that virus inactivation process used irreversibly destroy key immunological epitopes on native virus capsid. As a consequence, we can only compare binding patterns of different VLPs with native virus but not with inactivated viruses.

14101314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101314.value: Overall, we found that VLP1+2 bound stronger than VLP1. However, binding patterns of VLPs do not necessarily reflect that of native viruses and the usefulness of VLPs as surrogates for native norovirus needs to be evaluated on an assay-specific basis before making any inference. Saliva binding assay: VLP1+2 bound strongly to secretors of blood groups A and AB and to a lesser extent to that of B; whereas native virus and VLP1 only bound weakly to secretor, or there was no binding at all. Neither VLP1, VLP1+2, nor native virus bound to weak secretor. We concluded that co-expression of VP2 is necessary to confer the saliva-binding ability of VLP1+2; however, this saliva-binding property may be an artifact. HBGAs binding assay: VLP1+2 bound strongly to A and H antigens and to a lesser extent to B antigen, a pattern in very well agreement with that of saliva binding assay. Notably, VLP1 also bound to A, B, and H antigens, but at an approximately 50% reduced intensity. Native virus only bound weakly to A antigen. We concluded that co-expression of VP2 can enhance HBGA-binding ability of norovirus VLPs. However, native virus does not have a high affinity to HBGAs. Human tissue binding assay: 1. Small intestine: VLP1+2, VLP1, and native virus bound in a microscopically indistinguishable pattern to a small subset of cells in lamina propria of duodenum. No binding to epithelial surface was observed. 2. Stomach: VLP1+2 bound strongly to lamina propria. No binding was observed for VLP1 and native virus. 3. Lymph node: VLP1+2 bound to a subset of cells. No binding was observed for VLP1 and native virus. Data interpretation of tissue binding assay was challenging. Generally, VLP1+2 bound to all tissues tested. However, native virus did not bind to stomach and lymph node, tissues that are unlikely primary sites of infection of human norovirus. The binding pattern of VLP1+2 in these tissues may be artefact. In duodenum, the proposed site of norovirus infections, we observed binding of VLPs and native virus. This infers the presence of authentic norovirus receptor in small intestine that can be recognized by VLPs and native virus alike, and VP2 is not necessary in such binding. In conclusion, norovirus VLPs are good surrogates for native norovirus only when used on small intestinal tissue. The ability that VLPs “can” bind to saliva and carbohydrates do not mean that native virus “will” bind to these so-called attachment factors.

14101314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101314.value: VLPs are generally considered to be good surrogates because they are similar in size with and structurally resembling to native viruses. Norovirus VLPs exhibit authentic conformation of antigenic epitopes and have been widely used in immunogenicity testing and vaccine development. However, direct side-by-side comparison of VLPs binding with that of native virus has been lacking. Our findings that norovirus VLPs behaved very differently with native virus raise serious concerns over the validity of a large volume of studies in the literature that used VLPs to study norovirus binding. We expect that our findings may not fare well in the field and may be subject to scrutiny and criticism. We are preparing to present our data at the upcoming Annual Meeting of the American Society for Virology to be held at the University of Maryland in College Park in July 2018 to collect peer comments. We may perform additional assays that will be necessary to address concerns. We will then prepare a manuscript for submission to an international journal.

14101314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101314.value: Human norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide in all age groups. Despite its public health importance, our understanding on norovirus pathogenesis has been severely hampered by the lack of a robust, cost-effective culture model. To get around the hurdle, laboratory-made virus-like particles (VLPs) have been widely used as they are structurally resembling to native virus; however, direct side-by-side performance comparison was absent. In this study, we compared binding patterns of VLPs and native norovirus collected from stool of diarrheal patients. We found that norovirus VLPs behaved very differently with native virus in saliva, histo-blood group antigen, and tissue binding assays. Our findings raise serious concerns over the validity of a large volume of studies in the literature that used VLPs to study norovirus binding and tropism. We conclude that VLPs are good surrogate for native norovirus only when used on small intestinal tissue. The ability that VLPs “can” bind to saliva and carbohydrates do not mean that native virus “will” bind to these so-called attachment factors. The usefulness of VLPs as surrogates for native norovirus in binding assay needs to be evaluated on a case-by-case basis before making any inference. Native norovirus should be used whenever feasible.

14101414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101414.value: The aim of this study is to determine the role of perioperative troponin monitoring for the detection of clinically important myocardial injury after adult cardiac surgery. Perioperative myocardial injury is a common complication after cardiac surgery that is associated with substantial short-term and long-term mortality. However, clinical diagnosis of myocardial injury is often difficult and delayed because there are a number of distracting factors (e.g. sternal wound pain, and non-specific ECG changes) that can mask the symptoms and signs. Troponin is a sensitive cardiac biomarker and hence perioperative troponin monitoring may facilitate early detection of significant myocardial injury and allow the attending physicians to initiate timely treatment, such as further coronary intervention, insertion of mechanical assist device and administration of antiplatelet, anticoagulant or other anti-anginal drugs. In a large prospective, observational cohort (VISION) study, we have recently reported the utility of perioperative troponin monitoring in noncardiac surgery. Our study showed that an elevated troponin measurement in the early postoperative period is the strongest independent predictor of 30-day mortality. Perioperative troponin monitoring is also cost effective in allowing physicians to avoid missing significant myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery. Using a similar study design, we propose conducting an international, multicenter, observational cohort study of 5,000 adult cardiac surgical patients to evaluate the relationship between postoperative troponin measurements and the 30-day risk of vascular death. Our primary aim is to determine the threshold troponin concentration that indicates clinically significant myocardial injury. Our secondary aim is to accurately document the adverse event profile within 12 months of undergoing contemporary cardiac surgery. The expected findings of this study will be of considerable clinical and research interest. If our study confirms the utility of troponin monitoring, this finding should instigate a fundamental change in the perioperative management of cardiac surgical patients around the world. Specifically, it should support the recommendation that troponin monitoring be incorporated into routine postoperative care. Finally, the threshold troponin value will become an important endpoint for future cardiac surgery trials. 本研究旨在通過監測成年心臟手術患者圍術期肌鈣蛋白(troponin)水平，探索其在診斷臨床嚴重心肌損傷中的作用。 心臟手術圍術期發生心肌損傷非常常見，關系到患者短期及長期生存率。但由於存在一系列的干擾因素掩蓋其症狀體徵（如胸骨上傷口疼痛，非特異性心電圖改變），臨床上診斷心肌損傷存在困難且常滯後。肌鈣蛋白(troponin)是敏感性強的心臟生物標誌，圍術期監測可發現早期嚴重心肌損傷，利於及時開始治療，如進一步冠脈干預、植入機械輔助循環裝置、抗血小板藥物治療、抗凝治療或其他緩解心絞痛藥物治療。 近年來，我們進行了大樣本前瞻性觀察性隊列(VISION)研究，報道了非心臟手術患者圍術期肌鈣蛋白監測的效用。研究証實術後早期肌鈣蛋白升高是30天死亡率的最強獨立預測指標。圍術期監測可以避免漏診嚴重心肌損傷，在非心臟手術病人中也是有成本效益的。 運用類似的研究設計模式，我們計劃對5,000名成年心臟手術病人進行國際性、多中心、觀察性隊列研究，以評估心臟手術後肌鈣蛋白水平與30天血管事件死亡率的關系，主要目的是尋找能預測臨床上嚴重心肌損傷的肌鈣蛋白濃度閾值，次要目的是精確記錄當代心臟外科術後12個月的不良事件概要。 本研究結果可能極具臨床實踐及科學研究意義。一旦確立了肌鈣蛋白監測的效用，就可能引起全世界范圍對心臟手術病人圍術期管理的重大變革。特別是，肌鈣蛋白監測應納入常規術後護理，本研究為這一臨床推薦提供了有力支持。最後，肌鈣蛋白效用閾值的確立，將會成為未來心臟手術臨床試驗的重要終點事件。

14101414.label: Realisation of objectives
14101414.value: We have completed the Vascular events In Surgery patIents cOhort evaluation (VISION) – Cardiac Surgery study – an international, multicenter, prospective cohort study to evaluate the clinical utility of perioperative cardiac tropoinin monitoring in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery. There has been some delay in patient enrollment among centers overseas, and recruitment has been extended for 10 months. Between January 2015 and October 2018, we have successfully recruited a total of 15,053 patients from 25 centres from 13 countries in North and South America, Africa, Asia, Australia, Russia and Europe. In Hong Kong, a total of 1,273 patients were enrolled to the study. In the study, we included a representative sample of patients, ≥ 45 years, undergoing cardiac surgery that required cardiopulmonary bypass. We recruited patients scheduled for elective, urgent/emergent surgery, day or night-time surgery over the weekday or weekend. Overall, 74% of all eligible patients were consented and included in the study. 30-day follow-up was completed in 99.8% of patients. In all patients, we measured plasma high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I concentrations during the first 3 days after surgery. Since 12-month follow-ups in many overseas centers have not been completed, the following analyses are restricted to patients enrolled in Hong Kong and should be considered as preliminary findings. Based on the local data in the study, the 30-day mortality was 3.4% [95% confidence intervals (CI): 2.5-4.5%]. All patients had a postoperative troponin value exceeded the 99% upper limit of normal (URL) of 16 ng/L. Myocardial infarction occurred in 6.8% of patients (95%CI: 5.6-8.4%), stroke in 1.9% (1.3-2.8%), acute renal failure in 7.2% (5.9-8.8%) and reoperation was required in 5.7% (4.6-7.2%) and pulmonary embolism 0.6%. The 12-month death rate was 6.2% (95%CI: 5.7-6.8). We have adopted the modified Mazumdar approach and determined the threshold cardiac troponin value that increase the risk of vascular death using the Cox regression model at 30-day after surgery.

14101414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101414.value: In the study, we found that all patients have elevated cardiac troponin levels and therefore a threshold based on 99th centile of the normal population would not be helpful. Based on the current Third Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction consensus guidelines, where troponin levels >10 times of URL was considered as significant, 81% of patients had biochemical evidence of myocardial injury. However, there was no association between elevated cardiac troponin and 30-day mortality of morbidity, p = 0.148. Therefore, we need to derive the threshold of postoperative cardiac troponin concentration that predicted vascular death at 30 days after surgery. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that peak cardiac troponin concentration 15 times of upper reference limit (URL) occurred in 58.2% (55.5-60.9%) of patients and was associated with higher 30-day mortality and major cardiac events. Specifically, the adjusted hazard ratio (95%CI) for patients with peak cardiac troponin concentration of >15 times of URL was 4.72 (2.13-10.64). p < 0.001. When the peak cardiac troponin level was higher than 20 times of URL, the hazard ratio increased to 6.54 (2.24-19.15), p < 0.001, (Objective 1). The proportion of patients with ischemic ECG or echocardiographic changes after surgery were few 6.8% (5.6-8.4%). These data suggested that a large number of patients (51.4%) were at risk of 30-day vascular mortality despite of no apparent ECG changes, and would be missed if no troponin monitoring was performed (Objective 2). At 12-month follow-up, cardiac troponin elevation ≥ 20 times of URL was associated higher mortality [adjusted hazard ratio (95%CI): 6.54 (2.24-19.12)], higher rate of stroke 2.85 (1.31-5.82) and renal failure 14.12 (2.86-47.58), Objective 3. These data suggested that elevation of cardiac troponin concentrations (≥ 20 times of URL) during the first 3 days after noncardiac surgery is strongly associated with 30-day and 12-month vascular mortality. The threshold is prognostic relevant and is an independent predictor of postoperative mortality. Perioperative troponin monitoring is also effective in allowing physicians to avoid missing significant myocardial injury after cardiac surgery. Monitoring of cardiac troponin after surgery should be considered in patients according to the updated universal definition of myocardial infarction after cardiac surgery.

14101414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101414.value: Elevated cardiac troponin > 20 times of URL is prognostic important and is an independent risk factor for vascular mortality at 30 days and 12 months after cardiac surgery. Although our findings are encouraging, they are derived from observational data. There is a need to conduct large definitive clinical trials to determine whether interventions (e.g. coronary intervention, insertion of mechanical assist device and administration of antiplatelet, anticoagulant or other anti-anginal drugs) that minimize postoperative cardiac troponin concentration will improve morbidity and mortality after cardiac surgery. The VISION Cardiac surgery also provides opportunity to study other outcomes from cardiac surgery. In this respect, we have also evaluated the incidence of chronic postsurgical pain after cardiac surgery (Br J Anaesth 2016; 117: 801-811). We found 12% of patients developed chronic pain over the sternal (or leg) wound after cardiac surgery. We have also collected data to determine the factors that predicted the chronic pain after cardiac surgery (BMJ Open 2018, accepted on 17th November 2018).

14101414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101414.value: Perioperative myocardial injury is a common complication after cardiac surgery that is associated with substantial short-term and long-term mortality. However, clinical diagnosis of myocardial injury is often difficult and delayed because there are a number of distracting factors (e.g. sternal wound pain, and non-specific ECG changes) that can mask the symptoms and signs. We investigated whether perioperative troponin monitoring may facilitate early detection of significant myocardial injury and allow the attending physicians to initiate timely treatment. VISION Cardiac Surgery Study was a large prospective, observational cohort study involving over 15,000 patients. In this study, we found that cardiac troponin level > 20 times of reference limit predicted deaths at 30 days and 12 months after cardiac surgery. At this level, cardiac troponin also predicted kidney injury and stroke after surgery. Our research showed that cardiac troponin is a sensitive biomarker and hence troponin monitoring will facilitate early detection of significant injury to the heart and allow the attending physicians and surgeons to initiate timely treatment. Based on our findings, routine monitoring of cardiac troponin should be incorporated to international guidelines for the management of patients after cardiac surgery.

14101514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101514.value: <背景>： 宮頸癌是在全球女性中第三常見的癌症，感染高危型人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV）是引起宮頸癌的主要原因。HPV52是高危型中的一種，並且不能通過現有的HPV疫苗預防。雖然HPV52只在世界上小部分宮頸癌（3.6%）中被發現，但在東亞地區它與超過15%的宮頸癌相關，且在中國、日本和韓國女性中特別普遍。 造成HPV52疾病負擔的這種種族/地域偏好性的原因未明。我們最近完成了一個國際性的HPV52研究，收集了橫跨美洲、非洲、歐洲和亞洲的14個地區的611個研究樣本。我們發現一個變異株（E6 K93R）與宮頸癌的高風險相關。同時我們也發現這種E6 K93R變異株在東亞比在世界其他地區更為常見。這些流行病學的觀察結果可以解釋為何HPV52在東亞有更高的疾病負擔，並對診斷化驗和疫苗開發有重要意義。在這些信息能應用於臨床治療之前，其風險相關性應通過體外實驗驗證。 <具體目標>： 我們將通過以下方法評估HPV52 E6 K93R變異株相對於樣本型和其他常見變異株的致癌性高低： 1. 闡明并比較HPV52 E6樣本型和不同變異株在角質細胞中引起永生化、惡性轉化和浸潤性的能力。 2. 描述并比較分別由樣本型和不同變異株編碼的E6蛋白的亞細胞定位及穩定性。 3. 描述并比較由HPV52樣本型和不同變異株編碼的E6蛋白與癌變相關的關鍵性細胞靶點（包括p53、Bak、hDlg和E6AP）之間的相互作用。 預期結果： 本研究將獲得現時缺失的HPV52 E6變異株致癌作用的一系列綜合數據。 <最終目標>： 我們的研究將驗證之前的流行病學觀察結果，即一種高危變異株在東亞地區相當常見。這是該觀察結果可以轉化為臨床應用的關鍵。本研究不僅有助於我們理解HPV52在東亞有更高疾病負擔的原因，也使我們對HPV E6介導的致癌機制有更深入認識。

14101514.label: Realisation of objectives
14101514.value: Objective 1: To elucidate and compare the oncogenicity of HPV52 E6 prototype and naturally occurring variants by assessing their immortalizing, transforming and pro-invasive abilities in keratinocytes. A. Proposed approaches: We proposed to address this objective using human keratinocytes expressing HPV-52 E6 prototype and natural variants, namely E6 V1 (K93R), V2 (N122K/K93R) and V3 (E14D/V92L), constitutively. The following oncogenic properties of these oncoproteins will be assessed: (i) Immortalization - We proposed to investigate this by evaluating the length of time for the cells to reach passage 65, doubling time, ability of cells to overcome replicative senescence and crisis. (ii) Transformation – This can be achieved by evaluating the ability of cells to resist anoikis, serum starvation and achieve anchorage independent growth. (iii) Pro-invasive abilities – Study cell proliferation and apoptosis, motility and invasion. B. Results achieved: (i) We have successfully expressed HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants in primary baby rat kidney (BRK) cells. The cells were also propagated under continuous G418 selection up to passage 30. Number of cells harvested and seeded for each passage was recorded to calculate population doubling level (PDL). In general, all the transformants showed a similar growth pattern and achieved double time of around 1 to 2 days at the 30th passage. The transformants also did not show any sign of replicative senescence and crisis. (ii) We performed soft agar assays using BRK cells expressing HPV-52 E6 prototypes and variants, in parallel with HeLa cells which serve as a positive control. After 17 days, we observed that among HPV-52 E6s, HPV-52 E6 V2 possesses a significantly higher ability in inducing anchorage independent growth compared to prototype and other variants (V1 and V3). (iii) Instead of the proposed MTT assay, we performed Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assays which serve a similar purpose. Our results showed that HPV-52 E6V2 stable cells attained a higher proliferative ability, followed by HPV-52 E6 V1, prototype and V3. We also performed wound healing and matrigel cell invasion assays. Intriguingly, we found that HPV-52 E6 V1 can migrate significantly faster than prototype and other variants (V2 and V3). However, HPV-52 E6 V2 exhibited a greater proliferative invasiveness power than prototype, V1 and V3. C. Problem encountered and solutions: We proposed to use human keratinocytes in this study. However, ectopic expression using human keratinocytes can be technically challenging. We tried various methods to introduce expression plasmids encoding for HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants into human keratinocytes, including cationic polymer polyethylenimine (PEI), TransIT (Mirus Bio), and commercially available liposome-mediate reagents, including Lipofectamine® LTX (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and Lipofectamine® 3000 (Thermo Fisher Scientific), FuGENE HD and ViaFect (Promega). Further attempts were made by electroporation using Amaxa® human keratinocyte nucleofector® Kit with the Nucleofector™ 2b Device (Lonza, Switzerland) and retroviral transduction system (kindly provided by Prof. John Doorbar, University of Cambridge). However, all these methods yielded less than 10% transfection efficiency. We faced obstacles in establishing stable cell lines which is supposed to be used for comparing oncogenic events mediated by HPV-52 E6s. Therefore, instead of human keratinocytes, we used primary cells extracted from 9‐day‐old Wistar Hannover rats. We chose this approach because on one hand, it offers a greater transfection efficiency; and on the hand, this method has been well-established and widely used in many laboratories worldwide to study oncogenic events mediated by HPV oncoproteins. Besides, we did not perform study to elucidate the ability of the HPV-52 E6s stable transformants to resist anoikis, serum starvation and undergoing apoptosis. During the entire experiments, we monitored the cell growth carefully and we did not see any sign of the cells in undergoing crisis. In addition, for each passages, we stained cells with trypan blue during cell counting, we did not observe any major change of number of apoptotic cells among the transformants. Objective 2: To delineate and compare the subcellular localization and stability of E6 proteins encoded by HPV52 E6 prototype and variants. A. Proposed approaches: We planned to overexpress HA-tagged HPV-52 E6 and variants in HaCaT cells and perform immunofluorescence assays to study subcellular localization of HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants. While steady-state levels of HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants was proposed to be assessed through cyclohexamide-chase assays. B. Results achieved: We overexpressed expression plasmids encoded for HA-tagged HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants in U-2 OS cells. Our immunofluorescence images showed that all HPV-52 E6 variants displayed similar nuclear and cytoplasmic distribution in an even manner as the prototype. In addition, all the three HPV-52 E6 variants shared similar half-life with prototype of approximately 45 min (ranging from 43.8 ± 7.3 to 47.8 ± 11.9 min). These results indicated that natural amino acid variation within HPV-52 E6s does not affect their protein localization and stability. C. Problem encountered and solutions: Due to low transfection efficiency of HaCaT (human keratinocytes), we used HPV-null U-2 OS cells (human osteosarcoma cells) for immunofluorescence assay. We were able to express HPV-52 E6s in U-2 OS cells at an appreciable levels and the results are in line with previous studies performed by Mesplède et al., 2011 using C-33A (cervical cancer cells). Objective 3: To characterize and compare specific key functions of E6 proteins encoded by HPV52 prototype and naturally occurring E6 variants by studying their interaction with host cellular targets related to oncogenic functions, including p53, hDlg, Bak and E6AP. A. Proposed approaches: We proposed to study the ability of HA-tagged HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants in degrading p53 using H1299 (HPV-null, p53-null lung adenocarcinoma cells), effect on p53 transcriptional activity, degrading hDlg, Bak and binding to E6AP using HEK293 (HPV-null human embryonic kidney) cells. B. Results achieved: From our in vitro binding assays, we observed that HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants bound to GST-E6AP and GST-p53 at a similar extent as HPV-16 E6AA. We next study the ability of HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants in degrading p53 in cells, as HPV-E6 requires binding with E6AP to degrade p53. Interestingly, we observed that HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants degraded p53 in H1299 (HPV- and p53-null) cells, at a greater extent than HPV-16 E6AA. Besides, we observed that HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants possess a weaker ability in degrading PDZ proteins. However, HPV-52 E6 prototype and variants showed a similar ability in targeting PDZ1 and PDZ2 domains of MAGI-1 and Dlg, respectively. C. Problem encountered and solutions: Instead of using HEK293 cells for the proposed degradation targets, we took the advice of our overseas collaborator to use H1299 because of its HPV- and p53-null background which is more preferred.
