14103014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103014.value: We have successfully established four single mutant zebrafish lines (lhb, lhr, fshb and fshr) and six double mutant lines (lhb;fshb, lhr;fshr, fshb;lhr, lhb;lhr, fshb;fshr and lhb;fshr). Homozygous lhb mutant females are infertile while homozygous fshb mutant females are fertile. Folliculogenesis is partially affected in the fshb mutant but not affected in the lhb mutant. Oocyte maturation and ovulation is disrupted in the lhb mutant, and differential expression of genes in the ovary involved in oocyte maturation and ovulation is evident, demonstrating the essential role of luteinizing hormone signaling in oocyte maturation and ovulation. Moreover, double knockout of fshb;lhb leads to all infertile male offsprings. These data provide in vivo evidence to substantiate the functions and molecular mechanisms of gonadotropin signaling in controlling ovary development in zebrafish (see Research Output 1). All lhb;lhr and fshb;fshr mutant males were fertile. Analysis on the gonadosomatic index and testicular histology in these lhb;lhr and fshb;fshr mutants demonstrated that Lh signaling and Fsh signaling could functionally compensate each other in the testis. Intriguingly, it was found that the lhb;fshr mutant male fish were also morphologically and histologically normal and functionally fertile, a phenomenon which could be explained by the cross-activation of Lhr by Fsh. Taken together, we conclude that the action of Lh signaling and Fsh signaling is redundant in that either alone can support zebrafish spermatogenesis (see Research Output 2). Using zebrafish, a teleost phylogenetically distant from mammals, we have genetically analysed the functions of gonadotropins and their receptors through gene knockout studies. Apart from revealing the complexity of gonadotropin signaling in controlling reproduction in zebrafish, our studies also shed light towards a better understanding on the evolution of gonadotropin signaling in vertebrates from fish to mammals. We have summarized our findings in a review (see Research Output 3). Using the knockout platform, we have also succeeded in probing into the regulation of ovulation by Lh signaling in zebrafish. Our findings provide robust in vivo evidence indicating that npr mediates the action of Lh signaling on ovulation possibly through ptger4b in zebrafish, thus elucidating the biochemical pathways that link the initial stimulation by Lh to the actualization of ovulation (see Research Output 4). The mechanistic studies using some of the mutant lines also reveal that zinc mediates the action of androgen in acting as a downstream effector of Lh on oocyte maturation in zebrafish (see Research Output 5).

14103014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103014.value: This project has succeeded in creating a large number of zebrafish lines with the Lh signalling systematically disrupted either at the ligand level and the receptor level. These fish lines provide a very valuable repertoire of biological resources for investigating into the mechanism of Lh signalling in vivo. Apart from values in basic mechanistic studies, there are immense implications in attempting to manipulate the reproduction of animals in the farming industry. Further studies in exploiting these resources are now underway.

14103014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103014.value: Animal reproduction is controlled by the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonad axis. Gonadotropins, viz. follicle-stimulating hormone (Fsh) and luteinizing hormone (Lh) bind to their receptors, i.e. Fsh receptor (Fshr) and Lh receptor (Lhr), located in the gonads to orchestrate gonadal growth and development. Gonadotropin signalling in fish has attracted many researchers’ attention in the past two decades. However, because of the lack of a suitable genetic model, direct evidence on the in vivo functions of gonadotropin signalling in fish ovary development is lacking. The results systematically obtained in this project provide definitive in vivo data to substantiate the functions and molecular mechanisms of gonadotropin signalling in controlling ovary development in fish. In addition, knowledge gained from this project will provide us the means of producing more food in animal farming through controlling their reproduction.

14103314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103314.value: Sarcopenia is an aging-induced loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, characterized with reduced fast-twitch skeletal muscle fiber type II. This is also associated with osteoporosis (odds ratio=1.80) and a major risk factor of fall-induced osteoporotic fracture. The prevalence was 12.3% in men and 7.6% in women aged >70 years in Hong Kong. Physical exercise is the only recommended intervention to retard sarcopenia but not effective due to low compliance. Therefore, there is a need to develop a good compliance and effective intervention to prevent and retard the progress of sarcopenia. Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) is a non-invasive biophysical intervention providing systemic cyclic mechanical stimulation on musculoskeletal system with good compliance. Our previous animal study on the LMHFV effect on 28day tail-suspension muscle disuse atrophy model, we found stimulatory effects predominantly on fast-twitch muscle fibers with type IIB fiber hypertrophy and increased number of type IIA activated satellite cells. A large-scale clinical trial involving 710 postmenopausal women also demonstrated a significantly reduced fall rate by 39% after 18-month LMHFV treatment, while quadriceps strength and balancing ability were significantly enhanced. Bone loss at femoral neck and spine were lower in high-compliance (>80%) group too. A few more animal studies also revealed a strong osteogenic effect of LMHFV on fractured rat model by increasing bone formation by 25-30% as well as increased blood flow velocity and volume in both normal and osteoporotic bones. All these encouraging findings support that LMHFV is effective to actively induce skeletal muscles and bone tissues to react, which should be beneficial to resist aging-induced deterioration of musculoskeletal functions. A recent in vitro study demonstrated that low-amplitude high-frequency vibration could suppress atrophy pathway and down-regulate myostatin level that is known to be a negative regulator of muscle growth and may be associated with bone metabolism too. Based on these, we hypothesize that LMHFV can retard the onset and progression of sarcopenia through increasing satellite cell proliferation, muscle fiber type II and also reduce the bone loss simultaneously, where myostatin may be a potential candidate in regulating both sarcopenia and low bone mass. In this study, we will use our established senescence accelerated mouse model (SAMP8) with confirmed sarcopenia onset on month 8 to evaluate changes of skeletal muscles and its relationship with bone quality in conjunction with myostatin. This will be the first study to investigate the efficacy and mechanism of LMHFV on sarcopenia and low bone mass.

14103314.label: Realisation of objectives
14103314.value: All objectives of this research project have been completely achieved. 1. Senescence accelerated mouse P8 (SAMP8) mice were used as sarcopenia animal model in this study, which sarcopenia was proven to onset at the age of month 8 [8.1]. SAMP8 mice were randomized to either control or vibration group, where vibration group was provided low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) 20min/day and 5days/week; control mice were placed on LMHFV platform with power off. At months 1, 2, 3, 4 post-treatment, the gastrocnemius muscles were harvested; their muscle mass and strength were measured by weighing and ex vivo functional test, respectively. Results indicated that at late stage, the mice in the vibration group showed significantly higher muscle strength (month 4, p=0.028) than control. Contractibility was significantly improved by LMHFV (contraction time, p=0.000; half-relaxation time, p=0.000). The fatigue rate in control group was generally higher than that in the vibration group (p=0.01, two-way ANOVA); at month 1, the difference was significant (p=0.001, independent sample t-test). However, no significant difference of muscle mass at all time points was observed [8.2, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3]. 2. Based on the study design as mentioned above, the gastrocnemius samples were subjected to cryo-sectioning. ATPase staining was performed to identify muscle typing and immunofluorescence (Pax7/laminin) to assess satellite cells. Results showed that vibration group had larger fiber cross-sectional area (FCSA) of muscle fiber type IIA than control group (p=0.000, two-way ANOVA) and the differences were significant at months 1, 2, 3 (p=0.000, 0.035, 0.003, respectively, independent t-test). Also, the FCSA of muscle fiber type I at months 1 and 4 was significantly larger than those at the corresponding time points in the control group (p=0.008 and p=0.042, respectively, independent sample t-test). These confirmed that LMHFV could induce structural improvement in sarcopenic muscle. For satellite cells (SC), the vibration group had a higher SC amount at months 3 and 4 than those at the corresponding time points in the control group (p=0.001 and p=0.001, respectively, independent sample t-test). Generally, the SC amount in vibration groups was higher than the control group (p=0.001, two-way ANOVA) [8.2, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3]. 3. Besides the muscle measurements, the SAMP8 mice were assessed bone mineral density (BMD). The BMD of SAMP8 dropped from month 8 to 10 (210.04±5.14 to 193.81±17.19 mgHA/ccm or 7.7%) [8.4, 9.4, 9.5, 9.6]. The mice underwent senile osteoporosis. However, after LMHFV treatment, there was no significant difference in BMD, as compared with control group at different time points [9.6]. 4. For all the mice before euthanasia, 3mL blood was taken for measuring serum levels of myostatin and IL-6 using ELISA kit. The absorbance was read at 450nm with a microplate spectrophotometer. Myostatin level decreased from month 0 to 2 and increased from month 2 to 4 in both control and vibration groups. The vibration group had a higher serum myostatin level than control and the difference was significant at month 2 (p=0.031, independent sample t-test). In contrast, a significantly lower expression of myostatin in vibration group was observed at month 4 when compared with control group (p=0.050, independent sample t-test) [8.2, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3]. In this part, we also add one more group (myostatin-vibration) for comparison, which the functional and structural changes induced by LMHFV became not different from control group at all. As myostatin is a myokine inhibiting myogenesis, the suppression of myostatin by LMHFV at late phase matched very well with the above data of enhanced muscle strength and satellite cell pool, which indicated myostatin may play an important role in sarcopenia, yet the relationship with bone quality is not remarkable. On the other hand, there was no detectable changes in IL-6 after LMHFV treatment [8.3].

14103314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103314.value: The skeletal muscles of SAMP8 mice were comprehensively characterized at the age of month 6-10. Muscle mass peaked at month 7 and the onset of contractility decline started from month 8. Most functional outcomes decreased significantly at month 10 than month 6. Structurally, fast-twitch muscle fiber type IIA peaked at month 8 and then decreased. Matching with the official definition of sarcopenia, SAMP8 showed the onset of sarcopenia at month 8 (pre-sarcopenia stage) and progressed to sarcopenia stage at month 10. These confirm that SAMP8 mice can be used in sarcopenia research with established time line. These animal characterization data generated an original journal article [8.1]. For the effect of LMHFV on sarcopenia in SAMP8, the mice showed significantly higher muscle strength (specific twitch force) after 4-month LMHFV (p=0.028). The contractibility was generally improved with significantly lower contraction time (p=0.000 at month 2; p=0.005 at month 4) and half-relaxation time (p=0.002 at month 1, p=0.001 at month 2). Structurally, cross-sectional area of muscle fiber type IIA was enlarged after LMHFV with significant differences at month 1 (p=0.000), month 2 (p=0.035) and month 3 (p=0.003). Biochemically, LMHFV could significantly increase the satellite cell pool at month 3 (p=0.001) and month 4 (p=0.001) than the control. Furthermore, the level of myostatin (a myokine known to inhibit myogenesis) was suppressed by LMHFV at month 4 (p=0.050). The biochemical findings could explain very well the functional improvement at late phase. However, there was no change of muscle mass between two groups at all time points. Overall, LMHFV could improve the sarcopenic skeletal muscle quality functionally, structurally and biochemically. These findings generated an original journal article [8.2] and 3 conference abstracts [9.1, 9.2, 9.3] (Note: 9.1 is supported by a previous GRF #469911 but related to this study). The change of bone mineral density (BMD) in the SAMP8 mice were also characterized. BMD of SAMP8 dropped from month 6 to 10 (235.85±16.83 to 193.81±17.19 mgHA/ccm or 17.8%) (Note: between month 8-10, BMD dropped by 7.7%). Therefore, SAMP8 underwent senile osteoporosis. This is the first report to show that SAMP8 had co-existing sarcopenia and osteoporosis. However, there was no detectable effect of LMHFV on the bone quality in this study. These data partially contributed to an original journal article [8.4] and 3 conference abstracts [9.4, 9.5, 9.6]. (Note: 9.4, 9.5 are also supported by another external grant, which acknowledge GRF #14103314 in ppt of 9.5)

14103314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103314.value: 1. We explore a new treatment for sarcopenia – combined effect of vibration and HMB [β-hydroxy β-methylbutyrate] and we verify this postulation in our established SAMP8 animal model again which shows a significant positive effect to enhance both muscle mass and muscle strength [9.6]. Bone mineral density was also enhanced with the combined treatment [unpublished]. With this evidence, we are going to conduct a randomized controlled trial to study the combined treatment on sarcopenia patients. 2. We make use of the developed animal model to study the relationship between sarcopenia and osteoporotic fracture healing [8.4], that is a highly prevalent condition clinically but their relationship is never reported before. Our latest findings showed that sarcopenia imposes negative effect on osteoporotic fracture healing, particularly in early phase of bone formation. Meanwhile, we identify a highly potential factor, myostatin, that may play a key role for this muscle-bone interaction, as myostatin is highly expressed in sarcopenic muscle and affects fracture healing simultaneously. The expression of myostatin in the fracture callus and sarcopenic muscle is highly correlated (R2=0.7837, p=0.0001). We are going to conduct a loss-of-function experiment to depict the direct relationship of myostatin in sarcopenia and osteoporotic fracture healing.

14103314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103314.value: Sarcopenia is an age-induced skeletal muscle atrophy and the diagnosis is newly defined based on both muscle mass and muscle performance. There is no promising intervention for sarcopenia. The current recommendations for treating sarcopenia are physical exercise and high-protein diet, yet the effect is not satisfactory mainly due to poor compliance. Therefore, there is a pressing need to search for an effective, non-invasive and good-compliance intervention for sarcopenia. This study is the first to investigate the effect of low-magnitude high-frequency vibration treatment on sarcopenia in a senescence-accelerated mouse model. The results showed that vibration could significantly increase the muscle strength after 4-month treatment with improved muscle contraction ability. Also, the cross-sectional area of fast-twitch muscle fibers was significantly increased. The muscle regeneration capacity was also enhanced by higher satellite cell pool and lower level of myostatin (a myokine inhibiting muscle formation) in vibration group. However, no significant change of muscle mass was observed. In summary, vibration treatment could improve biochemical, structural and functional outcomes of sarcopenic skeletal muscles, hence retarding the progression of sarcopenia. It would be a good recommendation for prevention of the diseases related to skeletal muscle atrophy.

14104314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14104314.value: SIRT3在腎病中的病理作用和調控

14104314.label: Project Objectives
14104314.value: To determine the role of Sirt3 in kidney diseases We will determine whether oxidative stress, renal fibrosis, and inflammation in diseased kidneys during Adriamycin nephropathy (AN) and obstructive nephropathy will be enhanced in Sirt3 knockout (KO) mice. Furthermore, we will determine whether restoration of Sirt3 expression will ameliorate renal injury in these KO mice. Moreover, we will validate the functional role of Sirt3 during TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in vitro by either overexpressing or inhibiting Sirt3 in mesangial and tubular epithelial cells. To investigate signalling mechanisms by which TGF-beta signaling regulates Sirt3 expression We will employ Smad2 knockdown (KD), Smad3 KD, and an inducible Smad7-expressing kidney cell lines to examine how TGF-beta/Smads regulate Sirt3 expression. We next will investigate how Smad3 regulates the transcription of the HIC1 transcriptional repressor. Finally, we will determine whether HIC1 is required for TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling-suppressed Sirt3 expression. To determine the therapeutic potential of Sirt3 in kidney diseases and investigate how Sirt3 prevents kidney injury By an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery system, we will deliver overexpression plasmids of Sirt3 into established diseased kidneys to determine whether restoration of Sirt3 expression in diseased kidneys has therapeutic potential to attenuate renal injury in mouse models of Adriamycin nephropathy (AN) and obstructive nephropathy. In addition, we will also explore whether suppressing TGF-beta-induced Id1 signaling is a possible mechanism for Sirt3-protected renal injury.

14104314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104314.value: 目的：為了確定如何在腎病中調節SIRT3的表達和功能 氧化應激在慢性腎臟疾病中扮演重要角色，越來越多的證據表明，氧化應激在腎病纖維化和炎症中起重要作用，包括調節細胞外基質的產生，間質白細胞的侵入和肌成纖維細胞的增殖。所以需要進一步開發新的治療策略來控制這些由氧化應激引發慢性腎病的病徵。 一個新的和重要的初步結論是，在阿黴素和梗阻性慢性腎病的小鼠模型中，腎臟的SIRT3(一個重要的III級脫乙酰基酶)的表達被下調。腎臟的SIRT3表達與腎病纖維化和炎症呈負相關係。利用敲除Sirt3基因的小鼠，發現敲除Sirt3基因更進一步增強腎纖維化和炎症反應，以及令到腎功能進一步惡化。體外研究還證實過度表達SIRT3能抑制在腎小管上皮細胞中TGF-β誘導的纖維化。相反，抑制在腎小管上皮細胞中SIRT3的表達卻增強TGF-β誘導的纖維化。此外，抑制TGF-β誘導的ID1可能是SIRT3保護腎損傷的機制。這些新的研究結果表明，SIRT3可以保護腎臟免受傷害。此外，SIRT3表達與TGF-β/ Smad3信號的激活和HIC1的表達呈負相關，提示TGF-β-Smad3-HIC1軸線可在疾病狀態抑制腎SIRT3表達。 基於這些發現，我們假設TGF-β/ Smad3蛋白通過上調HIC1的表達去抑制SIRT3表達，和SIRT3通過抑制氧化應激的作用能够防止由纖維化和炎症所導致腎損傷。我們提出了三個具體研究目標，以檢驗這些假設：1）我們將釐定SIRT3在腎損傷的功能作用；2）我們將研究TGF-β信號如何調節SIRT3表達和傳導機制；3）我們將研究SIRT3如何防止腎損傷和測定它的治療潛力。 確定SIRT3的腎損傷的作用和調控將會發現腎病發病的新機制。值得注意的是，SIRT3在腎臟的過度表達會抑制腎臟損傷。雖然最近的研究發現加深我們對腎病發病的了解，但目前還沒有成功的策略去抑制腎損傷。因此，我們迫切需要一種能抑制腎損傷的治療新策略。由這個提出的研究之結果可以對慢性腎病的發病的預防和治療方面提供的一個具體和有效的策略。

14104314.label: Realisation of objectives
14104314.value: 1. Specific Aim 1. To determine the role of Sirt3 in renal injury. We employed adriamycin nephropathy (AN) model of progressive kidney diseases and in vitro studies to examine the protective role of Sirt3 in renal injury. Firstly, we found that deletion of Sirt3 gene in mice with AN further impaired the renal function when comparing the urine albumin excretion and serum creatinine with wild type (WT) mice with AN. In addition, the expression levels of biomarkers for fibrosis (Col I, Col IV, α-SMA, and Fn), inflammation (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, MCP-1, and ICAM1), and TGF-beta signaling pathway (P-Smad2/3, and TGF-beta1) were further elevated in diseased kidneys of Sirt3 knockout (KO) mice, when compared with diseased kidneys of WT mice. Nitrotyrosine levels, a marker nitro-oxidative stress, were further elevated in diseased kidneys of Sirt3 KO mice, when compared with diseased kidneys of WT mice. In contrast, expression levels of biomarkers for oxidative stress (SOD2, and catalase) were further reduced in diseased kidneys of Sirt3 KO mice. When overexpression (OE) plasmids of Sirt3 were delivered into the kidneys of Sirt3 WT and KO mice by an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery technique not just restored the Sirt3 expression levels in kidneys, but also reduced the expression levels of biomarkers for fibrosis, inflammation, nitrotyrosine levels, and TGF-beta signaling pathway in diseased kidneys of Sirt3 KO mice, when compared with diseased kidneys of WT mice. These results were also confirmed by in vitro studies in kidney cells. Treatment with human TGF-β1 and oxidants reduced expression levels of Sirt3, biomarkers for oxidative stress (SOD2, catalase and FOXO1), but increased expression levels of HIC1, biomarkers for fibrosis (Col I, Col IV, alpha-SMA, and Fn), inflammation (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, MCP-1, and ICAM1), and TGF-beta signaling pathway (P-Smad2/3). However, knockdown of Sirt3 expression by Sirt3 shRNA aggravated these effects but restoration of Sirt3 expression by overexpressing Sirt3 diminished such effects. These findings show that Sirt3 deficiency further enhanced renal injury, renal fibrosis, and elevated the oxidative stress in diseased kidneys of AN model. Restoration of Sirt3 expression in kidneys suppressed renal injury. These results suggest that Sirt3 plays a protective role in renal fibrosis and inflammation during renal injury. 2. Specific Aim 2. To Investigate signaling mechanisms by which TGF-beta signaling regulates Sirt3 expression Our results demonstrated that TGF-beta suppressed Sirt3 expression in a Smad3-dependent manner. However, no Smad binding site was found in Sirt3 promoter. Then we found that a binding site of HIC1, a transcriptional repressor, is located in the Sirt3 promoter and knocking down of HIC1 expression restored Sirt3 expression. Then, we found that HIC1 was regulated positively by TGF-beta/Smad3 but negatively by Smad7 and Smad2. Activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is necessary for regulating HIC1 and Sirt3 expression. Furthermore, HIC1 expression reciprocally regulated Sirt3 expression and its effect on renal injury. Thus, HIC1 should be responsible for suppressing Sirt3 expression to enhance the renal injury in response to TGF-beta1. By chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and reporter assays, we found that HIC1 was a direct target of Smad3 and Sirt3 is a target of HIC1. By employing metabolomic study, we also found that deletion of Sirt3 genes in mesangial cells (MC) promoted the expression of oxidative stress, fibrotic and proinflammatory markers in MCs under diabetic condition. We demonstrated for the first time that deletion of Sirt3 genes in MCs altered amino acid biosynthesis, citrate cycle, and purine metabolism in MCs under diabetic condition. 13 intracellular metabolites were significantly changed by Sirt3 deficiency with high glucose (HG) condition compared with HG condition, including L-tyrosine, L-phenylalanine, L-arginine, L-glutamate, L-tryptophan, AMP, ADP, UMP, inosine, and hypoxanthine, which have been reported to be related to kidney injury. In addition, Sirt3 deficiency in MCs significantly altered the expression levels of key enzymes involved in the metabolism of these amino acids and purines. Supplement of L-tyrosine, L-phenylalanine, L-arginine, and L-tryptophan reduced the marker expression of fibrosis and inflammation induced by Sirt3 deficiency. In conclusion, our results suggest that under HG condition, Sirt3 deficiency promotes diabetic kidney injury by impairing metabolisms of amino acids and purines to induce more fibrosis and inflammation in MCs. 3. Specific Aim 3. To determine the therapeutic potential of Sirt3 in kidney diseases and investigate how Sirt3 prevents kidney injury In this aim, we investigated the therapeutic potential of Sirt3 for renal fibrosis by delivering Sirt3 overexpression plasmids into AN kidneys to study whether the progression of renal fibrosis was altered. Prevention and intervention experiments were included to determine whether the restoration of Sirt3 expression was able to inhibit renal fibrosis or affect the progression of renal fibrosis during established renal diseases. The ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene transfer of a Sirt3 overexpression plasmid in a mouse model of AN ameliorated renal fibrosis and inflammation, and this revealed a therapeutic potential for restoration of Sirt3 expression in renal injury. These results not only support the protective role of Sirt3 in renal injury, but also provide a feasible therapeutic approach to halt the progression of renal injury by restoring Sirt3 expression in established diseased kidneys.

14104314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104314.value: Oxidative stress plays a vital role in the pathophysiology of chronic kidney diseases (CKD). Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that oxidative stress plays an important role in kidney fibrosis and inflammation. TGF-beta signaling plays a critical role in chronic kidney disease. It is well known that Sirt3, an important class III deacetylase, plays a key role in regulating oxidative stress. However, the exact role of Sirt3 and the relationship between Sirt3 and TGF-beta signaling in renal diseases remain unclear. In this study, we tested a novel hypothesis that Sirt3 might play an essential role in regulating the renal injury in response to TGF-beta1 and that restoration of Sirt3 expression might represent an effective and novel therapy for CKD. Results from animal studies demonstrated that renal Sirt3 expression is negatively correlated with renal fibrosis and inflammation in the diseased kidneys of mice with adriamycin nephropathy (AN). Furthermore, deletion of Sirt3 gene in mice further enhanced renal injury, renal fibrosis, and elevated the oxidative stress during renal injury. Restoration of Sirt3 expression in kidneys suppressed renal injury. These results were also confirmed by in vitro studies in kidney cells. These findings suggest that Sirt3 plays a protective role in renal fibrosis and inflammation during renal injury. The functional studies of Sirt3 found that HIC1 was a direct target of Smad3 and Sirt3 is a target of HIC1. Activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is necessary for regulating HIC1 and Sirt3 expression. Furthermore, HIC1 expression reciprocally regulated Sirt3 expression and its effect on renal injury. In addition, our metabolomics results suggest that under diabetic condition, Sirt3 deficiency promotes diabetic kidney injury by impairing metabolisms of amino acids and purines to induce more fibrosis and inflammation in MCs. More importantly, the therapeutic potential of restoring Sirt3 expression in kidney disease was demonstrated in mouse models of AN by applying an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated anti-Sirt3 gene transfer technique. This gene transfer of Sirt3 overexpression plasmid into the diseased kidneys was able to halt the progression of renal fibrosis and inflammation. All these results revealed a therapeutic potential for restoring Sirt3 expression in chronic kidney disease. In conclusion, Sirt3 plays a protective role in the development of renal injury. Restoring Sirt3 expression may represent a novel and effective therapy to combat CKD. Currently, the manuscript is in preparation. The research work of this study resulted in 14 publications, 11 presentations in international conferences, 2 presentations in local conferences, and the training of 2 doctoral students.

14104314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104314.value: 1. To determine the mechanism of how Sirt3 protects renal injury. In this report, we found two mechanisms of how Sirt3 was involved in protecting renal injury. Firstly, activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is necessary for regulating HIC1 and Sirt3 expression. Furthermore, HIC1 expression reciprocally regulated Sirt3 expression and its effect on renal injury. Secondly, our metabolomics results suggest that under diabetic condition, Sirt3 deficiency promotes diabetic kidney injury by impairing metabolisms of amino acids and purines to induce more fibrosis and inflammation in mesangial cells. Thus, the next step is to study how these mechanisms are linked together for Sirt3 to regulate renal fibrosis and inflammation. 2. To develop a therapeutic strategy for renal injury by delivering overexpression plasmid of Sirt3 into diseased kidneys We should determine the therapeutic potential of restoring Sirt3 expression for renal injury in different mouse models of kidney diseases, including diabetic kidney disease. By an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery system, we can deliver overexpression plasmids of Sirt3 into diseased kidneys at every 4 weeks to determine whether restoring of expression of Sirt3 expression will attenuate renal injury.

14104314.value: Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that oxidative stress and TGF-beta signaling plays an important role in kidney fibrosis and inflammation during chronic kidney diseases (CKD). Sirt3, a deacetylase, regulates oxidative stress. However, the exact role of Sirt3 and the relationship between Sirt3 and TGF-beta signaling in renal diseases remain unclear. In this study, we tested novel hypotheses that Sirt3 might play a role in regulating the renal injury in response to TGF-beta1 and that restoration of Sirt3 expression might represent an effective and novel therapy for CKD. 14104614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104614.value: Directed differentiation of embryonic stem cells (ESC) or induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) into functional neural stem cells (NSC) can provide a renewable source of donor cells for the promising cell therapy in neurodegenerative diseases or brain/spinal injuries. However, current protocols for neural induction tend to differentiate ESCs/iPSCs into a heterogeneous cell population in culture. Thus, elucidation of the molecular mechanism underlying early neural induction as well as NSC generation is necessary for improving the efficiency of generating desired NSCs from ESCs/iPSCs. In our previous work, we have established a stepwise neural induction protocol and have depicted the molecular changes underlying critical cell fate transitions during early neural induction. More importantly, we have identified a coiled-coil domain containing gene Ccdc141 as a potential regulator of the neural induction based on its up-regulated expression at early stage of neural induction as well as the defective neural differentiation in the absence of Ccdc141 (Tsang et al., 2013; ref [11]). Since very few regulators of the early neural induction have been identified so far, further characterization of Ccdc141 will surely enrich our knowledge of this group of regulators. Currently, Ccdc141 is not well characterized yet and its functions remain largely unknown. However the coiled-coil domain motif in this protein implicates that Ccdc141 may play roles in directing transcription regulation as well as influencing other proteins through protein-protein interaction. Hence, study on Ccdc141 has a significant potential to reveal new insights into the early neural induction. In this project, we will systematically investigate the regulatory function of Ccdc141 in neural induction by applying various in vitro and in vivo approaches. First, we will analyze the gene expression changes caused by Ccdc141 depletion using time-course microarray analysis and examine its potential transcriptional regulatory function via Chromatin-immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay. Second, we will investigate the interactome of CCDC141 using a proteomics approaches. Finally, we will employ the established animal model Xenopus to assess the dynamic expression and function of Ccdc141 during in vivo neural induction. A cutting-edged gene targeting technique will be applied to generate knockout Xenopus for an authentic loss-of-function study. Collectively, the proposed work will produce insightful understanding on the function of Ccdc141 and further unravel the molecular mechanism underlying neural induction and NSC generation. The data obtained will provide important clue to improving the efficiency of in vitro neural induction as well as generating desired NSCs.

14104614.label: Realisation of objectives
14104614.value: Directed differentiation of embryonic stem cells (ESC) or induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) into functional neural stem cells (NSC) can provide a renewable source of donor cells for potential cell therapy in neurodegenerative diseases or brain/spinal injuries. However, current protocols for NSC induction are inefficient and could only differentiate ESCs/iPSCs into a heterogeneous cell population. In order to improve the efficiency and quality of NSC induction, in this project, we have employed multidisciplinary approaches to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying early neural induction and NSC generation, to study the regulatory roles of a potential regulator CCDC141, and to develop new molecular tools that could facilitate further mechanistic studies. In our previous work, we established stepwise neural induction process and have identified a coiled-coil domain containing gene Ccdc141 as a new regulator of the NSC induction (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013). Based on this finding, we first performed correlation analysis and confirmed that that Ccdc141 genes are conserved between multiple organisms, including human, mouse and Xenopus. Subsequently, we examined the dynamic expression and function of Ccdc141 during early development and neural induction using Xenopus model. We cloned the cDNA of Xenopus ccdc141gene and performed RNA in situ hybridization in developing embryos. Interestingly, our results showed predominant expression of ccdc141 in heart and somites at early stages. This is consistent with recent studies that Ccdc141 is involved in cardiac function in human, suggesting that the function of Ccdc141 in heart may related to its role in cardiac development (manuscript under preparation). Meanwhile, we also observed drastic up-regulation of Ccdc141 in early neural induction which suggests a novel function of this gene at an even earlier stage of stem cell commitment. We have performed integrated bioinformatics analysis to examine potential regulatory network in pluripotent stem cells and during early commitment, and identified regulatory modules related to Ccdc141 function (Wang et al., J Stem Cell Res Ther. 2015; and manuscript under preparation). We have performed proteomics analysis and examined the proteins interaction network of CCDC141 protein. We constructed the plasmid containing HA-Ccdc141 driven by CAG promoter, and performed the co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) using antibody against the HA tag. We analyzed proteins that were pulled down with CCDC141 in a complex using polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) followed by mass spectrometry (MS) analysis. Through this proteomics approach, we identified one interesting candidate T2 protein which interacts with CCDC141. We cloned both the human and mouse genes encoding the T2 proteins, and confirmed using co-IP assays that, indeed, the CCDC141 interacts with T2 proteins from both human and mouse, and could play important role together with CCDC141 (unpublished). Furthermore, we adopted the groundbreaking genome editing technology CRISPR/Cas9 and investigated its potentials as great tools to genetically modify embryonic stem cells (ESC) and Xenopus (He et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2016, and Liu et al., Cell Biosci 2016). Studies reported that CRISPR-induced site-specific DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) can be repaired by homology-directed repair (HDR) or non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathways. In our study, we found that NHEJ pathway can mediate more efficient rejoining following CRISPR/Cas9-induced DNA breaks between genome and plasmids. It promotes high-efficiency DNA integration in various human cell types. Our quantitative comparison further demonstrated that the NHEJ-based knock-in is more efficient than traditional HDR-mediated gene targeting in all human cell types examined (He et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2016). Subsequently, we showed that simultaneous knock-in of dual reporters through this homology-independent approach permits one-step generation of cells carrying complete gene disruption of multiple alleles (Zhang et al., BMC Biol 2018). With this new genome editing approach, we have generated Ccdc141-/- ESCs, which will offer a powerful tools for further elucidate the function of Ccdc141 and related molecules. The new development of the CRISPR-based high-efficiency knock-in approach has establish a new strength of our research. As technological advance, it permits efficient somatic gene editing which provide great potentials to study physiological functions of genes essential to early development under in vivo conditions. Meanwhile it holds promises to treat or even cure inherited genetic disorders (He et al., Stem Cells Int 2018, Ma et al., Zool Res 2018). Altogether, through this research, we have obtained new insights into the regulatory mechanisms related to the Ccdc141 and NSC induction, and established new technology and tool for further study.

14104614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104614.value: In our previous work, we have identified a coiled-coil domain containing gene Ccdc141 as a potential regulator of the neural induction (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013). We have confirmed that that Ccdc141 genes are conserved between human, mouse and Xenopus. Through RNA in situ hybridization analysis using DIG-labeled probe, we found that ccdc141 is predominantly expressed in developing heart and somites at early stages. This is consistent with recent studies that Ccdc141 is involved in cardiac function in human, suggesting that the function of Ccdc141 in heart may related to its role in cardiac development (manuscript under preparation). Meanwhile, our finding of drastic up-regulation of Ccdc141 in early neural induction suggests a novel function of this gene at an even earlier stage of stem cell commitment. We have performed integrated bioinformatics analysis and identified regulatory modules related to Ccdc141 function, through examining potential co-expressed genes among the regulatory network in pluripotent stem cells and during early commitment, (Wang et al., J Stem Cell Res Ther. 2015; and manuscript under preparation). In addition, we also performed proteomics analysis to examine the protein-protein interaction network of CCDC141. We identified one interesting candidate T2 protein which interacts with CCDC141 using co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) followed by mass spectrometry (MS) approach, and have confirmed that indeed the CCDC141 interact with T2 proteins cloned from both human and mouse (unpublished). This provide a new clue to investigate the role of CCDC141 in regulating stem cell differentiation. Furthermore, we have established a novel high-efficiency homology-independent knock-in approach, through adopting recent groundbreaking genome editing technology CRISPR/Cas9. This technology holds great potential to apply genome editing approach to a broad range of cell models and to study physiological functions of genes under in vivo conditions (He et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2016; He et al., Stem Cells Int 2018; Ma et al., Zool Res 2018). Using this approach, we have established Ccdc141-/- ESCs, which will offer a powerful tools for further elucidate the function of Ccdc141 and related molecules.

14104614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104614.value: Ccdc141 and its potential interaction with T2 protein might imply a new molecular module that regulates the commitment of pluripotent stem cells towards differentiation. Other than its function in NSC induction, our previous observation also suggested that Ccdc141 might be also involved in mesoendoderm (cardiac) differentiation. On one hand, we will continue with integrative bioinformatics approach to delineate their functions during lineage commitment, toward either NSC induction or mesoendoderm differentiation. On the other hand, our recent study on definitive endoderm (DE), which derives from mesoendoderm at early embryonic stages and gives rise to all endodermal tissues and organs, provides a suitable angle to study the function of Ccdc141 toward mesoendoderm differentiation. Our research recently revealed a previously unreported phenomenon that both canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling pathways are required for DE differentiation. This has been further supported by our experimental results, using both chemical approach and gene tic approach, including using the CTNNB1-/- hESCs generated through our recently established CRISPR-based knock-in approach. In future, we will investigate the expression changes of Ccdc141 and T2 gene during mesoendoderm or DE differentiation from hESCs., to delineate the potential regulations or interactions between these molecules and canonical or noncanonical Wnt pathways.

14104614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104614.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESC) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) undergo unlimited self-renewal, providing valuable tool and sources to in studying cell differentiation, modeling human diseases, and developing regenerative medicine. However, current methodologies are imperfect and can only induce partial or heterogeneous differentiation. In order to improve stem cell technology, efforts are needed to further elucidate the molecular mechanisms. We have identified a coiled-coil domain containing gene Ccdc141 as a new regulator of early differentiation. Here we further extended the knowledge by demonstrating the dynamic expression of Ccdc141 gene in developing embryos of Xenopus, and identifying its interacting partner protein T2. These findings have potential to unravel new insight into the early differentiation regulation, as well as to promote development of better protocol to control stem cell differentiation. In addition, through this research, we have also established a new genome editing approach which could support targeted knock-in of foreign genes at safe regions in genome. This technology has great potential to develop new therapeutic treatment for human inherited diseases.

14105214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105214.value: Aim The aim of this study is to conduct research investigating the molecular mechanisms of heat shock protein 27 (Hsp27) response to facilitate human Enterovirus 71 (EV71) infection. Project Background The recent repeated outbreaks of EV71 have infected over a million children and have caused hundreds to thousands deaths in China annually. To date, no effective therapy is available to prevent or treat EV71 infection. Little is known about the host responses to combat or facilitate EV71 infection. Brief Project Description Our team has investigated the host responses to EV71 infection by two-dimensional proteomics studies. After validation by RT-PCR and western blot assays, we have shown that Hsp27 is one of the most elevated proteins which respond to EV71 infection from fast replication to secretion phases. Further studies have revealed that Hsp27 and p38 MAPK signaling plays an important role in facilitating viral infection. In this study, we will investigate the underlying mechanisms of p38 MARK signaling on Hsp27 response to enhance virus infections. Particularly, we will knockdown p38 and generate series of phosphorylation-deficient and oligomerization-deficient Hsp27 mutants, and demonstrate how they affect EV71 life cycle. Significance of Project The results of this study will provide a new insight into the viral strategies used to facilitate its life cycle in the host cells and will promote the development of new antiviral drugs against EV 71. 自2009年以來，EV71病毒感染的 兒童數量在中國每年都超過百萬人，導致數百至千人死亡。 雖然EV71疫苗在三期臨床試驗結果比較良好，目前仍然沒有有效的疫苗或藥物治療EV71的感染。我們對宿主如何阻止或幫助EV71的感染的知識知之勝少。 我們通過蛋白組學的研究瞭解宿主如何對EV71感染作出反應。我們發現，HSP27是EV71感染後細胞內上升倍數最高的一個蛋白。進一步的研究發現HSP27和p38- MAPK信號通路在病毒感染過程中起著重要作用。我們將研究p38 MAPK信號通路將如何通過HSP27促進病毒感染。我們將沉默p38，構建系列磷酸化缺陷性或多聚化缺陷性HSP27並研究它們對病毒生活週期的影響。在此基礎上，我們將進一步評估p38 MARK抑制劑是否可作為潛在的抗EV71的藥物。

14105214.label: Realisation of objectives
14105214.value: Aim 1: We conducted proteomics study and identified heat shock proteins are most obvious host proteins responding to EV-A71 infection. The phosphorylation of Hsp27 is upregulated upon EV-A71 infection, possibly through p38. 1) We firstly designed specific siRNAs and constructed shRNA vectors to knock down Hsp27, p38α and p38β subunits. The effect of knockdown was examined by RT-qPCR and west blot assays. The expression level of Hsp27, p38α and/or p38β in knockdown cells were reduced by 70-80% compared with scramble siRNA/shRNA treated cells. 2) After knockdown of p38α and p38β, we examined the status of Hsp27 phosphorylation upon EV71 infection in RD cells. The viral titer was determined by the end-point dilution assay (TCID50) and plague assays. Knockdown of p38α reduced Hsp27 phosphorylation at Ser-78, but showed little effects on Ser-15 and Ser-82 phosphorylation. Knockdown of p38β siRNA obviously inhibited the phosphorylation of Hsp27 at sites Ser78 and Ser82. Knockdown of either p38α and/or p38β significantly inhibited viral RNA and protein synthesis. Simultaneous knockdown of p38α and p38β displayed synergistic antiviral effects. 3) We established Hsp27 knockout (Hsp27-KO) cells by CRISPR/Cas9/sgRNA mediated gene editing. To further confirm the role of p38 MAPK in EV71 replication, we overexpressed p38α and p38β in both the wild type RD cells and Hsp27-KO cells. Then the cells were infected with EV71 at a MOI of 1 for 12h. Overexpression of p38α and p38β markedly increased the viral RNA and protein levels. Moreover, p38-mediated enhancement of EV-A71 replication was significantly inhibited after knockout of Hsp27. However, there was no obvious change of the phosphorylate Hsp27 after overexpression of p38α and p38β in wild type HEK293 cells. We postulated that the basal level of p38α and p38β may be sufficient to support the phosphorylation of Hsp27. 4) p38 inhibitor SB203580 significantly inhibited Hsp27 phosphorylation upon virus infection, potently decreased EV-A71 yield. These results demonstrated that Hsp27 acts as a downstream factor of p38 MAPK to support EV71 infection (manuscript in preparation). Aim 2: 1) We constructed oligomerization-deficient Hsp27 expressing vectors. the WDPF-motif in the N-terminus and Ser135/Arg136 in the α-crystallin domain are important for Hsp27 oligomerization while Cys137 is the only residue that cross-link with other counterpart molecules. C137A mutant blocks Hsp27 to crosslink with its counterpart molecules to form large oligomers. Mutations of S135F and R136W would result in the dissociation of Hsp27 dimers without obvious effects on the structure of large oligomers. We chemically synthesized Hsp27 cDNAs with WDFP deletion and Ser135F/R136W or Ser135F/R136W/C137A (cross-link deficient) and cloned into a Lentiviral vector. We will restore the mutant Hsp27 in the Hsp27-KO cells and examine its effect on EV-A71 reproduction. After we finish the experiments, the results will be presented in the next manuscript. 2) TDP, a natural product isolated from a traditional Chinese medicinal herb Garcinia oblongifolia, has been proven an Hsp27 inhibitor. TDP directly interacts with Hsp27 and induces dissociation of Hsp27. We checked the effect of TDP on EV-A71 infection by CPE assay. The CPEs were observed under a phase-contrast microscope. The cells became round and detached from the dishes after EV-A71 infection. TDP treatment protected the cells from EV-A71 infection and dramatically reduced CPEs in a dose-dependent manner. Consistent with the CPE reduction, TDP significantly inhibited EV71 replication, decreased the levels of intracellular viral RNA and viral protein. Moreover, the viral yield in the supernatant significantly decreased after TDP treatment. 3) We set up a reporter system to measure reagents (including host factors) that may affect virus IRES activities (Oncotarget, 2016). We observed that the IRES activity was inhibited by TDP in a dose-dependent manner. 4) Virus-induced eIF4G cleavage was also inhibited by TDP. These results demonstrated that EV-A71 infection is inhibited by Hsp27dissociation (J. Virol., 2019). Aim 3: 1) We checked whether Hsp27 affected the expression of eIF4G by RT-qPCR and west blot assays. In normal condition, the total level of eIF4G was not affected by depleting or ectopic expressing Hsp27. 2)To determine whether Hsp27 affects eIF4G cleavage, plasmids for 2Apro and 2AC110A proteins were constructed and transformed into E. coli BL21. The recombinant proteins were purified by Ni-NTi beads. Hsp27 was knocked down in RD cells, forty-eight hours post-transfection, the cells were harvested and the cell lysate were incubated with purified 2Apro and 2AC110A at 37oC for 4 hours. We checked the status of eIF4G cleavage by western blot assays. However, our results showed that knockdown of Hsp27 expression did not show marked reduction of eIF4G cleavage in the cell lysate. We postulated that false-negative results may come from the high noise due to remaining endogenous Hsp27 which was still at high level after knockdown. 3) To get clear conclusion without such noise, we co-transfected pHsp27 and 2Apro-expressing plasmid into HEK293T cells, we found 2Apro promoted eIf4G cleavage in a dose-dependent manner. 4) After infection of RD and Hsp27-KO cells with EV-A71, we showed that the eIf4G cleavage significantly decreased in Hsp-27-KO cells. 5) Recombinant 2Apro expressed in Escherichia coli was incubated in vitro with the lysates from wild-type and Hsp27-KO cells at 37°C for 4 h, obviously the eIF4G cleavage deceased in the cell lysate with knockout of Hsp27. 6) The ectopic expression of 2Apro promoted viral VP1 expression in the wild-type RD cells, whereas the knockout of Hsp27 almost diminished viral VP1 expression with or without the promotion by 2Apro . These results have been summarized in the recent publication (J. Viol., 2019). In addition, we show that knockout of Hsp27 inhibited EV-A71-induced hnRNP A1 translocation. The hnRNP A1 and FBP1 play critical roles in enhancing IRES-dependent translation. After EV-A71 infection, hnRNP A1 translocates from nucleus to cytoplasm and interact with the EV-A71 5′ UTR. We postulated that Hsp27 may affect hnRNP A1 and FBP1 redistribution to regulate the IRES activity. The wild type and Hsp27-KO RD cells were infected with EV-A71 at MOI of 20 or 40 for 6h, and then we visualized the intracellular hnRNP A1 protein distribution via immunofluorescence staining. We showed that hnRNP A1 normally localized in the nucleus in the mock-infected cells and translocated from nucleus to cytoplasm after EV-A71 infection. However, the translocation of hnRNP A1 was almost completely blocked in the Hsp27-KO cells. We further conducted RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) assay to dissect the binding activity of hnRNP A1 to viral 5’-UTR. Knockout of Hsp27 resulted in significant reduction of viral RNA binding with hnRNP A1. Surprisingly, Hsp27 knockout didn’t block FBP1 translocation after EV-A71 infection, suggesting that Hsp27 differentially regulates only a portion of RNA binding proteins’ redistribution to cytosol (J. Viol., 2019).

14105214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105214.value: Based on GRF support and combined with CityU supported $543,859, we conducted additional research activities on how ERp57 (another member of heat shock protein (Hsp) family) as well as its inhibitor OM (another compound also isolated from Garcinia oblongifolia), in facilitating/inhibiting EV-A71 replication, and potential value of ERp57 for drug target (Oncotarget, 2016). We identified 24 differentially expressed proteins by proteomics studies after EV-A71 infection in RD cells. Chaperon proteins (Hsp27, GRp78, ERp57, HSPA9, PHB, hnRNP K) are the most upregulated/downregulated proteins responding to EV- A71 infection. (1) We confirmed that both the mRNA and protein levels on Hsp27 were significantly elevated upon EV-A71 infection. (2) Knockout of Hsp27 by CRISPR-Cas9/sgRNA mediated gene editing significantly reduced cytopathic effects caused by EV-A71 infection, inhibited viral protein synthesis and replication, and reduced viral titers >10 folds; while ectopic expression of Hsp27 markedly promoted viral protein synthesis and reproduction. (3) Hsp27 inhibitor TDP protected cells from EV-A71 infection and reduced virus titers by over 95% via inhibiting IRES-mediated viral protein translation in a dose-dependent manner. (4) Surprisingly, knockout of Hsp27 blocked the translocation of hnRNP A1 from nucleus to cytoplasm after EV-A71 infection. The interaction between hnRNP A1 and EV-A71 viral RNA was blocked after knockout of Hsp27. More interestingly, Hsp27 always locates in the cytosol whereas it translocates into nuclei upon infections (J.Virol., 2019; Patent file No. 201811294538.2). (5) EV-A71 infection does not only induce Hsp27 expression, but also stimulates the phosphorylation of Hsp27 on Ser-15, Ser-78 and Ser-82. p38 plays an important role in the process. (6) p38 inhibitor SB203580 significantly reduced Hsp27 phosphorylation and viral reproduction (manuscript in preparation). Publications (1) Wang M, Dong Q et al., Oncotarget. 2016; 23;7(8):8797-808. 14105214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105214.value: (1) we will continue the study on p38/Hsp27 signalling in EV-A71 infection, complete another manuscript which is in preparation. (2) The new findings from this study provide a very precious opportunity and platform to demonstrate the molecular mechanism of RNA binding protein translocation from nucleus to cytosol. We will further investigate how Hsp27 regulates hnRNP A1 translocation in the host cells upon EV-A71 infection. We have submitted another GRF proposal (2019/20) entitled “Mechanism of hnRNP A1 protein translocation regulated by Hsp27 upon enterovirus A71 infection” (Ref. 11103519). In this new proposal, we will investigate (i) the structural basis of Hsp27 essential for hnRNP A1 translocation, (ii) the interaction between hnRNP A1 and Hsp27, and (iii) viral components that cooperate with Hsp27 to regulate hnRNP A1 translocation.

14105214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105214.value: EV-A71 infection causes hand-foot-and-mouth disease and severe neurological disorders even deaths. However, there is no approved treatments available for EV-A71 infection. Hsp27 is one of the most upregulated proteins responding to EV-A71 infection. Depletion of Hsp27 by siRNA or CRISPR-Cas9 mediated knockout significantly inhibits viral replication, protein expression and reproduction; while restoration of Hsp27 rescores such virus activities. Furthermore, Hsp27 plays crucial role in regulating the viral internal ribosome entry site (IRES) activities by two different mechanisms. Hsp27 markedly promotes 2Apro-mediated eIF4G cleavage, an important process for selecting and initiating IRES-mediated translation. hnRNP A1 is a key IRES trans-acting factor (ITAF) for enhancing IRES-mediated translation. Surprisingly, knockout of Hsp27 differentially blocks hnRNP A1 but not FBP1 translocation from nucleus to cytoplasm, and therefore abolishes hnRNP A1 interaction with IRES. Most importantly, Hsp27 inhibitor TDP, a compound isolated from a traditional Chinese herb, significantly protects cytopathic effects and inhibits EV-A71 infection. p38 regulates the phosphorylation of Hsp27 to promote viral reproduction, while p38 inhibitor SB203580 potently inhibits viral activities. Collectively, our results demonstrate new functions of Hsp27 in facilitating virus infection and provides novel options for combating EV-A71 infection or other (+) RNA viruses by targeting Hsp27

14105714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105714.value: The aim of this project is to identify genetic determinants of lipid response to statins and plasma concentrations of statins in Chinese patients with hypercholesterolaemia by using a genome-wide genotyping approach. Statins are one of the most widely used classes of drugs to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. The beneficial effect of statins on cardiovascular event is clearly related to the on-treatment low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels. However, there are wide variations in the lipid response to statins between individuals. In addition, Chinese subjects have increased plasma concentration of rosuvastatin and increased risk of simvastatin-induced myopathy than that in Caucasians, but the underlying genetic factors contributing to the ethnic differences in the pharmacokinetics and safety of statins have not been identified. Early pharmacogenetic analyses of statin responses using the candidate gene approach have shown that genetic polymorphisms in genes related to the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of statins may influence lipid responses to statins, but the candidate gene studies explained only a small part of the observed variation and results have often been inconsistent. In recent years, several genome-wide association studies conducted in Caucasians have demonstrated that polymoprhisms in genes coding for drug transporters and other genes related to lipoprotein metabolism significantly influence the safety and lipid-lowering effect of statins. However, the genetic markers identified in one population cannot be generalized to other populations due to different frequencies of polymorphisms and different linkage disequilibrium patterns among ethnic groups. In the current project, we will attempt to perform the first genome-wide analysis of the lipid response to rosuvastatin and simvastatin and plasma concentrations of these statins in a homogeneous group of Han Chinese patients (n=360), who previously participated in our research project on the pharmacogenetics of statins using the candidate gene approach. Lipid profiles on no lipid-lowering treatment and on single lipid-lowering therapy of rosuvastatin and simvastatin were already obtained. Drug levels and other cardiovascular biomarkers were measured. This study holds great potential for identification of new genetic markers for the lipid-lowering effect and systemic exposure to the two commonly used statins in Chinese patients with hypercholesterolaemia. The results of the study will also be useful for future collaborative project on pharmacogenomics of statins with Chinese population or other ethnic groups and this is a step forward for our ultimate goal of optimization and personalization of statin therapy and to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease in the society. 本研究旨在通過全基因組基因型分析的方法確定影響他汀藥物對華裔高膽固醇病人降脂作用與血藥水平的遺傳決定因素。 他汀類降膽固醇藥物為降低心血管疾病風險的常用藥物之一。其降低心血管事件的作用與治療中病人的低密度膽固醇水平密切相關。但是，他汀藥物降膽固醇作用存在很大的個體差異。另外，華裔病人體內瑞舒伐他汀的血藥水平以及對辛伐他汀引起的肌肉毒副作用的發生機率均高於白種人，對於影響他汀類藥物這一種族差異的遺傳因素尚未明確。前期的對遺傳藥理學候選基因基因型分析研究顯示與他汀類藥物藥代學與藥效學相關的基因多態性可能會影響他汀藥物的降脂作用。可是候選基因基因型分析研究結果僅可以解釋他汀藥物反應個體差異中的一小部分且各研究結果常常不一致。近年來，幾項在白種人群中進行的全基因組基因型關聯研究顯示藥物轉運體以及與血脂代謝相關的基因多態性可顯著影響他汀藥物的安全性與降血脂作用。但是，由於基因多態性以及連鎖不平衡模式在不同種族發生的頻率不同，所以不能一概而論地認為在白種人群中發現的影響他汀藥物療效的遺傳因子會發生在其他種族內。 在本研究中，我們試圖首次通過全基因組基因型分析的方法確定影響華裔高膽固醇病人（n=360）對瑞舒伐他汀以及辛伐他汀的降脂作用與血藥水平的遺傳決定因素。這些病人參加了我們前期進行的他汀藥物遺傳藥理學候選基因基因型分析的研究。病人服用瑞舒伐他汀以及辛伐他汀前後的血脂水平，血藥水平以及其他心血管風險因素的生物標記已完成檢測。 本研究有望發現影響華裔高膽固醇病人對兩種常用他汀藥物降脂作用與血藥水平的新的遺傳因素。本研究結果亦可用於日後與其他華裔或其他種族人群他汀藥物基因組學研究進行合作，最終可以實現優化他汀藥物治療，實現他汀藥物個體化治療，從而減輕心血管疾病對社會的負擔的目標。

14105714.label: Realisation of objectives
14105714.value: The objectives of this study as indicated above have been fully (100%) achieved in this project. We planned to perform the genome-wide analysis of the lipid responses to rosuvastatin and simvastatin and plasma concentrations of these two statins in 360 Chinese patients with hypercholesterolaemia (familial or non-familial) who previously participated in our research project on the pharmacogenetics of statins. All subjects previously provided written consents for DNA analysis of lipid response to statins. The lipid profiles at baseline on no lipid-lowering treatment and after 4-6 week treatment of rosuvastatin 10 mg daily (n=370) and simvastatin 40 mg daily (n=275) were collected. Plasma concentrations of these two statins and their active metabolites about 12 hours after administration of statins were measured by LS-MS/MS. We have conducted the genome-wide genotyping in 400 patients using the Illumina infinium Human Omni ZhongHua-8 v1.1 BeadChip (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA), which contains 866,925 SNPs, at the Li Ka Shing Institute of Health Sciences, The Chinese University of Hong Kong as planned. The genome-wide genotyping data was obtained in April 2015. The genome-wide analysis was performed in the Department of Medicine of Therapeutics by Dr Claudia Tam and in the Division of Biostatistics, The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK, by Prof Maggie Wang and her PhD student Ms Rui Sun. A total of 785,365 SNPs passed quality-control and were examined for association with the lipid-lowering effect and the plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin and simvastatin. The genome-wide significance threshold was set at the Bonferroni limit of P<6×10-8. We have performed genome-wide analysis and found that SNPs located in or near ATP binding cassette subfamily G member 2 (ABCG2) on chromosome 12 were significantly associated with plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin and its active metabolite N-desmethyl rosuvastatin. We then resequenced the promoter and the 16 exons in ABCG2 in 40 patients with good LDL-C response and 40 patients with poor response in the Division of Genomics and Bioinformatics, CUHK-BGI Innovation Institute of Trans-omics, CUHK. The functional polymorphism rs2231142 and two SNPs in the promoter region (rs3841115 and rs4148162), which appeared to be associated with statin response, were further genotyped in all subjects by Taqman® SNP Genotyping Assay from Applied Biosystems (Foster City, CA). Further analysis confirmed the importance of the functional SNP 421C>A in determining the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of rosuvastatin. We did not find any other common variants in ABCG2 or other genes that would contribute to the variations in the plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin in Chinese patients receiving long-term statin therapy. No significant association between genetic variants and the plasma concentration and the lipid-lowering effect of simvastatin were observed.

14105714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105714.value: The study confirmed that ABCG2 polymorphisms are the most important determinant of the plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin and its lipid-lowering effect. The ABCG2 transporter is an efflux transporter expressed in the apical membrane of small intestinal enterocytes, hepatocytes and proximal tubule cells in the kidney (11, 12). ABCG2 contributes significantly to the disposition of a wide variety of endogenous and exogenous substrates, including some anti-cancer drugs and statins, by reducing intestinal absorption and/or promoting hepatic elimination. The nonsynonymous SNP 421C>A located in exon 5 of the ABCG2 gene results in reduced transport activity of ABCG2 in vitro. It has been shown that the ABCG2 421C>A polymorphism was associated with the pharmacokinetics of rosuvastatin in Chinese and European healthy volunteers. We have also shown that this polymorphism was associated with increased plasma concentrations and lipid-lowering effects of rosuvastatin in patients receiving long-term rosuvastatin therapy using a candidate gene approach In the current genome-wide analysis, we identified 3 completely linked intronic SNPs in ABCG2 (e.g. rs4148157) significantly associated with plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin and N-desmethyl rosuvastatin. The intronic SNP rs4148157 G>A is located in intron 11 of the ABCG2 gene and is in strong linkage disequilibrium with the functional 421C>A SNP. The association between these intronic SNPs and the phenotypes were no longer significant after adjustment for the ABCG2 421C>A variant. When including both the intronic SNPs and the 421C>A polymorphism in the linear regression model, only the 421C>A polymorphism was associated with plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin. The analysis suggested that these intronic SNPs and the other top SNPs identified only served as a surrogate for the ABCG2 421C>A polymorphism.

14105714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105714.value: The aim of this project is to identify genetic factors that may influence the safety and efficacy of statins. However, the genetic factors can only explain a small proportion in the interindividual variations in drug response. Epigenetics is a rapidly growth field and is a very promising area of research. Epigenetic factors may affect the expression of drug-metabolizing enzymes, drug transporters, and nuclear receptors that regulate the expression of various genes and ultimately affect the response to drugs. Pharmacoepigenetics will offer another layer of information that could help develop more personalized therapy.

14105714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105714.value: This first genome-wide analysis of statins in Chinese patients confirmed that ABCG2 polymorphisms are the most important determinant of the plasma concentrations of rosuvastatin and its lipid-lowering effect. The ABCG2 drug transporter can pump drugs out of intestine cells and liver cells or excretion. Rosuvastatin is a substrate of this transporter. About 50% of Chinese population carry at least one copy of the less functional variant allele of the ABCG2 polymorphism and these subjects may have a higher systemic and hepatic exposure to rosuvastatin and thus have a better response to the drug.

14105814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105814.value: 心血管代謝疾病是一種病理機制複雜的疾病，涉及多器官多病變的進程。內皮功能障礙參與了糖尿病和肥胖症誘導的心血管疾病的發生發展。越來越多的證據表明，骨形成蛋白4（BMP4）是引致心血管疾病的危險因素之一。多項研究已經揭示了BMP4在高血壓和動脈粥樣硬化的發展中所起的關鍵作用。當BMP與其受體結合可激活胞內Smad1/5/8信號，激活後的Smad1/5/8與共介導型Smad形成複合物並移位到細胞核內，從而調節靶基因的轉錄。然而，內皮BMP和Smad信號對代謝疾病相關血管功能障礙的機制仍然知之甚少。 我們以往的研究表明，BMP4是高血壓血管內皮功能障礙的重要發起者。然而，Smad蛋白的激活對代謝疾病相關血管內皮功能的損害及機制還有待探索。為此，通過採用轉基因小鼠模型，包括糖尿病和肥胖小鼠和內皮細胞特異性Smad4基因敲除的小鼠中，我們將具體研究探討，第一，Smad信號通路在糖尿病和肥胖症有關的血管炎症和功能障礙中的病理學作用；第二，內皮細胞特異性Smad4的缺失能否改善肥胖小鼠的血管功能和胰島素敏感性。

14105814.label: Realisation of objectives
14105814.value: We have completed this funded project with one publication in Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology in 2016, one of top journals in cardiovascular research and with another manuscript in preparation. We have achieved both objectives. Project one: Bone morphogenic protein 4-Smad induced up-regulation of platelet-derived growth factor AA Impairs endothelial function Bone morphogenic protein 4 (BMP4) is an important mediator of endothelial dysfunction in cardio-metabolic diseases while platelet-derived growth factors (PDGFs) are major angiogenic and pro-inflammatory mediator although the functional link between these two factors is unknown. The present study investigated whether PDGF mediates BMP4-induced endothelial dysfunction in diabetes. PDGF-AA was elevated in serum of both diabetic patients and diabetic db/db mice. Transfection with BMP4-shRNA or PDGF-A shRNA adenovirus in db/db mice reduced serum PDGF-AA concentration. In vitro treatment with BMP4 (10-40 ng/mL) up-regulated expression of PDGF-AA in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and this effect were reversed by BMP4 antagonist. Treatment (72 h) of SMAD4 shRNA lentivirus interrupted BMP4 signaling and normalized PDGF-AA levels in HUVECs. Furthermore, BMP4 failed to increase PDGF-AA expression in C57BL/6J mice transduced for one week with Ad-SMAD1/5 shRNA. PDGF-AA neutralizing antibody or transfection with Ad-PDGF-A shRNA improved endothelial dysfunction in db/db mouse aortas and small mesentery arteries as well as reversed the impaired endothelial function in BMP4- or Ad-BMP4-treated C57BL/6J mouse aortas. BMP4 is identified as a new risk factor in cardiovascular disease, particularly showing harmful effects on endothelial cell function, but the critical effector of BMP4 is still unclear. Our previous study has shown that BMP4 upregulates cyclooxygenase-2 expression and alters vascular reactivity (Wong et al., 2010). This study demonstrates that PDGF-AA mediates BMP4 signaling and its harmful effects on endothelial cells through the canonical Smad1/5 and Smad4 pathway. Importantly, PDGF-AA is upregulated in diabetes mellitus. Knockdown of PDGF-AA in vivo by Ad-Pdgfa-shRNA abolishes BMP4-induced endothelial dysfunction in nondiabetic mice, while also improved endothelial function in diabetic db/db mice, indicating PDGF-AA as a critical effector of BMP4 contributing to vascular dysfunction in diabetes mellitus. PDGF is believed to participate in SMC proliferation and arteriosclerosis. However, little is known whether and how PDGF-AA exhibits beneficial/harmful effect on endothelial cells. An early study showed that PDGF-BB can dilate rat aorta and mesenteric arteries (Cunningham et al., 1992). However, we found that PDGF-AA impairs endothelium-dependent vasodilation. The difference may be caused by the differential expressions of PDGFRα and PDGFRβ in different vascular bed and different downstream signaling pathways. BMP4 upregulates PDGF-AA, but not PDGF-BB, and PDGF-AA mediates the effect of BMP4 on endothelial function. Our previous study showed that BMP4 caused endothelial dysfunction in db/db mice (Zhang et al., 2014). Here we also found increase of plasma PDGF-AA in diabetic human and db/db mice. Importantly, antagonizing PDGF-AA improves endothelium-dependent vasodilation in db/db mice, indicating PDGF-AA as a new risk factor to cause vascular dysfunction. We also showed that inhibition of Smad1/5 and Smad4 abolished BMP4-induced PDGF-AA. Smads are intracellular proteins that transduce extracellular signals from TGF- and BMPs to the nucleus to activate target gene transcription. Studies have shown the role of TGF-/Smad3 in diabetes mellitus. Targeting TGF-/Smad3 and its downstream effectors can be an effective strategy for the treatment of renal fibrosis in diabetes mellitus. However, the role of BMP4/Smad is more complicated in diabetes mellitus. The present study provides novel evidence that BMP4-mediated impairment of endothelial function is partly mediated through elevated PDGF-AA production through Smad4/Smad1/5-dependent mechanisms. Targeting BMP4-Smad-PDGFs signaling cascade might offer another useful strategy for the amelioration of diabetic vasculopathy. References 1. Cunningham et al. J Clin Invest. 1992;89:878–882. 2. Tian et al. J Mol Cell Cardiol. 2012;52:237–244. 3. Wong et al. Circ Res. 2010;107:984–991. 4. Zhang et al. Arterioscler Thromb Vasc Biol. 2014;34:152–159. Significance of this study: This study elucidates that PDGF-AA is an important mediator in BMP4 signaling in endothelial cells. The inhibition of PDGF-AA by PDGF-AA neutralizing antibody or Ad-PDGF-A shRNA effectively improve endothelial-dependent relaxations in diabetic mice, revealing a critical pathological role of PDGF-AA in diabetic vasculopathy. On the other hand, this study provides evidence showing BMP-SMAD is a critical pathway in regulating PDGF-AA. This work was published by Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology 36(3):553-560 in March 2016. Other impacts: The PhD student, Mr. Hu Weining presented his new results at two international conferences (United Kingdom and Denmark) and at one local meeting in Hong Kong. He received two prizes for his presentations (2nd Prize of Oral Presentation for Young Investigator Awards, at the 19th Annual Scientific Meeting of the Institute of Cardiovascular Science and Medicine and the 10th Across the Strait Conference on Cardiovascular Science, Hong Kong (21 November 2015) and Young Investigator Award, International Conference on Endothelium-Dependent Hypolarizations (EDH 2015), Nyborg, Denmark, 14-17 2015). Hu Weining completed his PhD study in August 2016. Project two: Inhibition of endothelial Smad4 suppresses endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and atherosclerosis The key findings of our study include: (1) deletion of endothelial Smad4 attenuated vascular dysfunction and blood pressure increase in hypertensive mice after AngII infusion; (2) deletion of endothelial Smad4 reduced atherosclerotic plaque formation in mice on ApoE knockout background; and (3) Smad4 is involved in AngII induced increase of ROS production, followed by induction of ER stress signalling pathway, leading to vascular inflammation and diminished NO production in endothelial cells. In summary, we showed that endothelial Smad4 is required for vascular dysfunction and inflammation in both mouse models of hypertension and atherosclerosis. Smad4 activation is involved in ROS production, ER stress responses, and reduced NO production in endothelial cells. We generated Tie2-CreERT2, tomoxifen inducible Smad4 endothelial knock out (iEC-Smad4-/-) mice and cross-bred them to Apoe-/- background for atherosclerotic study. iEC-Smad4-/- mice were infused with angiotensin II to mimic human hypertension. We have shown that iEC-Smad4-/- mice attenuated blood pressure elevation induced by angiotensin II infusion and improved acetylcholine-induced endothelium-dependent relaxations in aortas from angiotensin II-induced hypertensive mice while sodium nitroprusside-induced endothelium-independent relaxations were comparable among the four groups, suggesting that endothelial cell Smad 4 plays a significant role in angiotensin II-induced hypertension and impairment of endothelial function. EC-specific Smad4 deletion also restored the reduced flow-mediated dilatations in resistance mesenteric arteries from angiotensin II-induced hypertensive mice. EC-specific Smad4 knockout suppressed ROS over-generation indicated by DHE fluorescence in aortic endothelial layer from angiotensin II-induced hypertensive mice. EC-specific Smad4 deficiency also decreases the expression of the pro-inflammatory marker VCAM-1 in disturbed flow region of the aorta from angiotensin II-induced hypertensive mice. In addition, SMAD4 knockdown in HUVECs reversed eNOS phosphorylation at S1177, but suppressed its phosphorylation at T494 following angiotensin II treatment. These novel results indicate that Smad 4 is important in vascular dysfunction and targeting this molecule may be an effective approach to reverse vascular dysfunction in cardio-metabolic diseases. We are now preparing a manuscript for submission. We believe that EC-specific Smad deletion and detailed analysis of RNA-sequencing data will provide more focused targets to study the pathogenesis involved in vascular dysfunction in relation to Smad signaling pathways in diabetes, obesity and hypertension. The following are the results we have obtained so far in this project.
