14108114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108114.value: The aim of this study is to investigate the associations between sleep/wake patterns and neurocognitive outcomes in local preschool children. Sleep plays an important role in normal childhood growth and development. Sleep/wake pattern evolves substantially throughout early childhood. Appropriate sleep quantity and quality is important for appropriate daytime functioning and physical and mental development. Inadequate sleep duration, a potentially modifiable aspect of sleep, has been suggested to be associated with increased long-term risk of adverse conditions such as obesity, dyslipidaemia, behavioural problems and neurocognitive dysfunction. Thus, insufficient sleep during the preschool years may have profound, long-lasting effects on health and developmental outcomes. Despite the importance of adequate sleep duration in children, research into factors that influence this important parameter in preschool children is sparse. Most studies in this area investigating neurocognitive performance have focused on school age children. Further, children in Hong Kong have been suggested to sleep significantly less than their predominantly Caucasian counterparts. Whether they are “natural short-sleepers” or are suffering from chronic sleep deprivation is unclear. We will recruit preschool children and their parents from a representative community-based study that was conducted in preparation for this project. Short sleepers (sleep duration <10th percentile) and “median” sleepers (40th to 60th percentile) will be recruited from this community-based cohort to undergo objective sleep duration measurement, by sleep diaries and actigraphy, and a panel of neurocognitive assessments. Multivariate analyses will be used to assess the associations between sleep duration and childhood neurocognitive performance. Increasing understanding of the factors that influence sleep/wake patterns and the degree to which abnormal sleep duration is associated with adverse effects such as neurocognitive impairment is crucial for clinicians to formulate evidence-based interventions that can be further investigated and tested. Ultimately, such research could improve measures that ensure appropriate amounts of sleep from an early age and reduce the far reaching adverse public health consequences of inadequate sleep in children. 本研究是一項前瞻性研究，目的是制定香港兒童睡眠時間標準、了解影響有關兒童睡眠的因素及睡眠模式對兒童認知發展的影響。有不少研究和證據顯示在兒童睡眠不足情況對遠期的身體健康和認知發展有負面影響。是次研究計劃探討本地兒童的睡眠模式，並通過問卷採集、睡眠日記記錄、移動探測錶(actigraphy)及認知測試形式調查有關兒童作息起居情況等因素及其認知發展情況，從而了解兒童的睡眠模式並探尋其影響因素及對認知力發展的影響。

14108114.label: Realisation of objectives
14108114.value: Before commencing this grant project, we had commenced recruiting a population-representative cohort of children from 3 to 5 years of age from all four geographic regions in Hong Kong. The sleep/wake patterns of these preschoolers were determined by sleep questionnaire. Subject night-time awakenings, length of naps, bedtime, sleep environment/hygiene factors including co-sleeping (bed sharing), room sharing, bedtime routines, usual activities in the hour preceding bedtime and features of bedtime resistance were recorded. In addition, subject and demographic characteristics such as gender, birth weight, gestational age, parental occupation, living conditions, family income, parental education level, time living in HK, medical history of the child, parental smoking and alcohol consumption were also included. A total of 2748 questionnaires were completed. This was much higher than the original sample size of 723 subjects minimum requirement for this preparatory phase. Objective 1 (a) was to determine the associations between sleep/wake patterns of the preschooler and the other household members. We were able to determine that sleep/wake patterns of siblings (if present) were most closely associated with preschooler sleep/wake pattern, followed by mothers and then fathers. Originally, we planned to use structural equation modelling to analyse these associations, but found that quantile regression analysis was more appropriate in order to handle the sibling data. Objective 1 (b) was to determine the environmental and behavioural factors associated with childhoold sleep/wake patterns. The analyses of this showed that electronic device use before bedtime to be the factor most strongly associated with night time sleep duration. Objective 2 was to determine the associations between short sleep duration and neurocognitive outcomes in preschoolers. From the population-representative cohort, we calculated the percentiles of sleep duration for HK preschoolers using the information from the preparatory phase. Children with the shortest sleep duration (=/< 10th percentile of cohort, and children with average sleep duration (25-75th percentile) and their parents were invited to undergo (1) 14 consecutive days actigraphy (to include weekdays and a full weekend with the preceding and following weekdays) and concurrent sleep diary to record bedtimes, waking times, and nap times; (2) neurocognitive assessment: Beery-Buktenica Developmental Test of Visual-Motor Integration, 6th Edition (VMI) for both parents and children, and Connor’s Kiddie Continuous Performance Test (K-CPT) for children and Connor’s Continuous Performance Test (CPT) for parents. The 10th percentile of total sleep duration was found to be 9.75 and 9.5 h for 4 and 5 years children, respectively; 25-75th percentile was 10.5-11.5 h and 10-11.25h for 4 and 5 years children, respectively. Children who snores >3 times per week were excluded since obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is a major confounder for sleep duration and neurocognitive assessment. We originally planned to recruit 27 and 32 short sleepers for the 4 and 5-year-old strata per group respectively to achieve 80% power and P of 0.05; with 1:1 ratio of subjects to controls, i.e., a total of 118 children. We initially planned to recruit children sleeping between 40th to 60th percentiles as controls, but encountered difficulties in case recruitment in view of the discrepancy between the sleep questionnaire and the final sleep diary measurements when the children were invited back for assessment. We thus expanded the sleep duration range for controls to 25-75th percentile and extended the recruitment period. Finally, we recruited 80 subjects (4-year: 32 subjects; 5-years: 48 subjects) with short sleep duration and 119 (4-year: 65 subjects; 5-years: 54 subjects) with median sleep duration, which exceeded our initial aims. The two groups (short sleepers versus controls) were compared against each other by Student t test. In addition, for the associations between sleep duration and neurocognitive outcomes, multivariate linear regression analyses were performed adjusting for confounding variables (child's age, sex, birth weight, gestation week, BMI z-score, mother and father's education level, drinking habit, smoking habit, the National Statistics Socioeconomic Classification, and parents’ CPT and VMI). SPSS software version 21.0 for Windows (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, US) will be used for the t tests, correlation analysis and regression. All the objectives were thus fully achieved after study period extension.

14108114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108114.value: In the preparatory phase, a total number of 2748 questionnaires were eligible for analysis. Quantile regression analysis was conducted to analyse the association between children’s nighttime sleep duration/nap duration/total sleep duration and parents’ or siblings’ nighttime sleep duration/nap duration/total sleep duration, number of siblings, inversed age gap between the subject and siblings, and siblings’ gender in weekdays and weekends at 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile, respectively. According to the quantile regression analysis, mother and sibling sleep/wake patterns were most significantly associated with pre-schooler sleep/wake patterns, while father sleep/wake pattern showed less impact on nap duration/night sleep duration/total sleep duration since the results were inconsistent. The gender of the sibling was not found to have consistent impact on the sleep parameters of preschool children. By multivariate linear regression we found that kindergarten start time was significantly associated with sleep/wake patterns, with early start kindergartens being associated with shorter night sleep duration (Beta -1.1, P < 0.001), but longer nap duration (Beta 1.1, P < 0.001). However, early start time of kindergarten classes was not associated with shorter total sleep duration as the night sleep duration and nap duration balanced each other out. Another significant factor was use of electronic devices before bedtime, which was associated with later bedtime (Beta 0.4, P < 0.001) and shorter night sleep duration (Beta -0.2, P = 0.012), however, again, total sleep duration was not affected as nap duration was increased (Beta 0.2, P = 0.004). This suggested that unlike older children, pre-schoolers were able to compensate for short night sleep duration by increasing nap duration. For objective 2 we recruited 80 short sleepers and 119 median sleepers. Significant difference was observed in nap duration, nighttime sleep duration, total sleep duration between short and median sleepers. K-CPT and VMI scores showed that most preschoolers were within the normal range; 10 children (5.23%) are found to have higher ADHD confidence index (t score>67) in K-CPT, indicating a chance of significant attention problem. Median sleepers were found to present a higher score than short sleepers in Perseverations which was the only one sub-item in K-CPT showing significant difference between the two arms. Usually in K-CPT lower t-score indicates a better performance, but higher score in Perseverations would indicate impulsivity. For other sub-items in K-CPT and VMI, no significant difference was observed, and median sleepers did not necessarily perform better than short sleepers.

14108114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108114.value: Our major findings include the relative short sleep duration of children in Hong Kong even at preschool age, that significant associations with sleep duration included electronic device use before sleep, kindergarten class start time, sibling sleep/wake patterns and maternal sleep/wake patterns. In addition, the neurocognitive tests did not reveal any decreased performance in short sleepers. Our grant project did not further explore the issue of electronic devices, and this is something that is potentially modifiable and may impact on night sleep duration in the long-term. Intervention studies incorporating restrictions on electronic device use, family sleep hygiene intervention may be warranted in our population based on our results. We found that mother and siblings’ sleep duration showed major impact on that of preschool children, but father did not necessarily affect preschool children. These differential associations between family members may allow further analysis to be performed in terms of heritability of sleep duration. This may be useful as a basis upon which to perform genetic analyses to determine whether Hong Kong children are genetically predisposed to short sleep duration.

14108114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108114.value: Our study shows that Hong Kong pre-schoolers, like their school-aged counterparts sleep much less than children from Western regions. Significant effects of electronic device use and kindergarten class start time were found for night sleep duration, with use before bedtime and early kindergarten start time both reducing night sleep duration. However, for most effects reductions in night sleep duration, pre-schoolers could compensate by increasing nap duration. Minimal impact on total sleep duration was found for any of the factors. Of household members, sibling and maternal short sleep duration were both associated with short sleep duration in pre-schoolers. Despite short sleep duration in pre-schoolers in Hong Kong, neurocognitive performance did not show consistent differences from those who slept average amounts. Further studies are required to determine whether pre-schoolers in Hong Kong are natural short sleepers or are sleep restricted and at risk of long-term complications.

14108214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108214.value: Background: There has been longstanding interesting in cognitive training for people with dementia. In the past few years, promising results suggested that working memory training might help to enhance fluid intelligence. However, earlier success has not been well replicated. It would be of interests to further investigate the benefits of working memory training in older adults at risk of cognitive decline, and explore augmentation strategies that could possibly consolidate the effects. A form of non-invasive brain stimulation, the transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) had been demonstrated to affect the neuronal excitability, and reported to enhance memory performance. tDCS may also modulate cognitive function through changes in neuroplastic response. Objectives: Working memory training may lead to cognitive benefits, and tDCS could affect neuroplastic response to cognitive stimulation. The current proposal aims to 1) examine the short term and sustained cognitive benefits of tDCS and working memory training in older adults with mild neurocogntiive disorder due to Alzheimer’s disease, and 2) compare the cognitive effects of co-administration of tDCS and working memory training with single modality intervention. Design: A 4-week intervention (12 week observation) double blind Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) of tDCS. Methods: Chinese older adults (aged 60 to 90 years) with mild neurocognitive disorder due to Alzheimer’s disease (DSM-5 criteria) would be randomized into a 4 week intervention of either tDCS-working memory (DCS-WM), tDCS-control cognitive training(DCS-CC), and sham tDCS-working memory (WM-CD) groups with 64 subjects per arm. Cognitive performance would be assessed at the baseline, and at 4th, 8th and 12th weeks. Program adherence and adverse effects would be monitored throughout intervention. Data Analysis: The primary outcome would be changes in global cognitive function scores with the two single modality interventions (DCS-CC, WM-CD) and tDCS-working memory (DCS-WM) training, and comparisons of group differences with time. Secondary outcomes would be test performance of specific cognitive domains and mood status. Intention–to-treat analysis would be carried out. Changes of efficacy indicators from baseline to each follow up point and intervention differences would be tested with mixed effect model. Significance: The proposed study adopts the theory of neuroplasticity to evaluate the potential cognitive benefits of non-invasive electrical brain stimulation, working memory training and dual stimulation in older adults at risk of cognitive decline. It would also examine the tolerability, program adherence and adverse effects of this novel intervention. Information would be helpful for further research of dementia prevention studies.

14108214.label: Realisation of objectives
14108214.value: The study aimed to achieve the following 3 objectives. 1. To examine the short term (post-intervention) and long term (8 weeks post intervention) cognitive effects of 4 week tDCS- control cognitive training, sham tDCS-working memory training and combined tDCS-working memory training in older adults with mild neurocognitive disorder due to AD. 2. To compare the short term (post-intervention) and long term (8 weeks post intervention) cognitive effects of 4 week tDCS- control cognitive training, sham tDCS-working memory training and combined tDCS-working memory training in older adults with mild neurocognitive disorder due to AD. 3. To examine the acceptability and adherence of the proposed intervention. We have screened over 600 potential subjects and recruited 201participants with mild neurocognitive disorder due to AD (mild NCD-AD). 173 subjects completed intervention and all observations (86% completion rate), reaching the estimated sample size requirements for 51 subjects per arm. Throughout the intervention, there have been no major adverse events. Three subjects had mild skin abrasions over cathodal electrode (reference site) over the right deltoid area. The skin lesions healed uneventfully after a few days. Apart from these adverse events, acceptability and adherence was satisfactory as reflected by the high completion rate.

14108214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108214.value: 69 participants with mild neurocognitive disorder due to AD (Mild NCD-AD) were assigned to dual intervention with tDCS-working memory training (tDCS-WMT), 64 to sham tDCS-WMT, and 68 to tDCS control cognitive training (tDCS-CC) groups respectively. Baseline characteristics are comparable. 28 cases dropped out from this study (dropout rate: 14%). The participants who dropped out did not differ from completers on baseline demographics or cognitive performance. Improvements in global cognitive performance were found after intervention at T1 (4th week) in all 3 groups. At post-intervention assessments (T2 and T3, 8th and 12th weeks), global cognition showed a trend for reverting towards the baseline. At T3, ADAS-Cog was higher than baseline with no group differences observed (paired t-tests, p < 0.01). As for performance of N-back task, the mean reaction time RT and intra-individual variability of reaction time (IIV of RT) decreased with the time across all group (paired t-tests, p ≤ 0.001). Improvement persisted at T3 (paired t-tests, p<0.01), with no group differences observed through T1 to T3. After intervention, all groups showed improvement in delay recall of episodic memory test (T0 versus T1, paired t-test, p < 0,001). The tDCS-WMT group had greater improvement over single modality intervention (linear mixed effects model, group effect, p = 0.043). At 8th week post-intervention, only the tDCS-WMT group showed higher delay recall score over baseline (paired t-test, t = 2.79, p = 0.007). All groups had an improvement in working memory capacity (WMC) at T1 (paired t-test, p < 0.05). The tDCS-WMT group showed higher WMC compared with either sham tDCS-WMT or tDCS-CC at 4th week (T1)(linear mixed effects model, group effect, p = 0.04) and better performance of logical memory at 12th week (linear mixed effects model, group effect, p = 0.042). To the best of our knowledge, this is one of largest sham-controlled RCT on tDCS and working memory training for cognitively at risk older adults. Through scheduled interventions, participants with mild NCD-AD demonstrated cognitive gains. As compared with single modality intervention, dual modality showed greater enhancement on both working memory and memory functions after a 4-week intervention, and residual benefits appeared to retain 8 weeks after the intervention.

14108214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108214.value: This 4 week non-invasive brain intervention, either single or dual modality, enhanced the core domains of cognitive functions in people with mild NCD with relatively low incidence of adverse events. The findings provide evidence that combined modality intervention could be considered and adapted for further translation into clinical cognitive interventions for the individuals at risk of decline. Considering further research, different stimulation schedules as applicable in different neurocognitive disorders should be of interests to clinicians. It is also interesting to explore the physiological underpinnings of non-invasive brain stimulation through the use of electrophysiological or neuroimaging tools in future studies.

14108214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108214.value: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is increasingly recognized for its potential impact on cognition in late life neurocognitive disorders. Working memory training (WMT) has also been proposed as a target for cognitive training. This study examined the combined effects of tDCS and WMT on memory capacity in individuals with mild neurocognitive disorder due to Alzheimer’s disease (mild NCD-AD). Two hundred and one older Chinese adults with mild NCD-AD were randomised into 3 groups for a 4-week intervention of either tDCS-working memory training (tDCS-WMT), sham tDCS-working memory training (Sham tDCS-WMT), or tDCS-control cognitive training (tDCS-CC). The demographics and cognitive performance were comparable across 3 groups at baseline. Within each group, global cognitive function and memory improved after 4 week intervention. Combined tDCS-WMT group had better performance in episodic and working memory after intervention at 4th week. This modality-driven, non-invasive brain stimulation intervention is safe and effective for older adults with mild NCD-AD. Single modality, either tDCS or WMT, has positive cognitive effects with intervention. A combination of tDCS and WMT demonstrated more enhancements than single modality, particularly on the capacity- and speed-based memory performance. (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: ChiCTR-TRC-14005036)

14109414.label: Realisation of objectives
14109414.value: We demonstrated that the fasting-induced mL-STL gene is a male-dominant liver-specific cytosolic sulfotransferase which is required for sulfonation of 7α-hydroxyl bile acids [J Lipid Res 58 (2017): 1114-1131]. The mL-STL is formally renamed as Sult2a8 which is assigned by the International Nomenclature Committee for Sulfotransferases. To probe how Sult2a8 (mL-STL) regulates energy metabolism, we constructed a transgenic Sult2a8-knockout (KO) mouse model. Specifically, Objective 1: Produce a Sult2a8-deficient transgenic mouse model by target-disruption of the Sult2a8 gene. A KO vector was designed to target the disruption of exon 3 of the mouse Sult2a8 gene. To achieve homogenous C57BL/6 genetic background, a congenic C57BL/6 embryonic stem (ES) cell line Bruce4 was used for transgenic mouse production. Following injection into blastocysts, several chimera mice were obtained, and finally one transgenic line was established. Unexpectedly, no homozygous KO mice was obtained. More surprising, number of wide-type (WT) mice (derived from heterozygous intercourses) decreased with the advance in progeny generations, suggesting lethality in WT mice too! Nevertheless, the heterozygous (HT) mice is viable and fertile. To answer whether the WT and KO lethality were resulted from Sult2a8 gene disruption, pre-implantation (2-cell stages to blastocysts) and post-implantation (E6.5 to E18.5) embryos were collected for extensive Sult2a8 gene expression analysis. Phenotypic and expression analyses indicated that lethality occurred at early pre-implantation stages, well before expression of Sult2a8 gene detected, suggesting embryonic lethality is NOT resulted from Sult2a8 gene disruption. Instead, backcrossing study indicated that the embryonic lethality was most likely resulted from unstable genetic background contributed by the congenic background of the Bruce4 ES cells. These expression studies were not planned in our original proposal. As for the studies were essential to characterize the Sult2a8-KO mice model, we sought extra funding from University and worked extra 8 months to complete the studies. Objective 2: Initiate phenotypic and functional characterization of the Sult2a8-deficient transgenic mice to evidence sulfonation plays an essential role in regulating bile acid homeostasis. The HT mice were adopted as a Sult2a8-deficient mice model for further functional characterization. Firstly, we examined the relationship between genotype and phenotype. As for the disruption of one Sult2a8 allele, a reduction of the total sulfotransferase activity toward 7α-hydroxyl bile acids was expected. The hepatic sulfotransferase activity of WT and HT mice were compared using a series of 7α-hydroxyl bile acids as substrates. Enzymatic assay clearly indicated that sulfotransferase activity of male HT mice was about 50% that of male WT mice, but there was no significant difference between WT and HT female mice. The results suggest phenotype agreed well with genotype, and affirmed the HT mice being a Sult2a8-deficient mice model. Importantly, the results also confirm our previous conclusion that Sult2a8 is a male-dominant liver-specific sulfotransferase with 7α-hydroxyl bile acids as the preferred substrates. No abnormality in the liver gross tissue structure nor in the hepatocyte morphology were found, suggesting the HT mice developed and grew normally. To further access the hepatic functions, the composition of bile acid pool in WT and HT mice was compared using a LC-MS/MS-based methodology. Consistent with previous reports, taurine-conjugated cholic (T-CA) and muricholic acids (T-MCA) were predominant contributing more than 90% of the total bile acids in both WT and HT mice. Importantly, there was no noticeable difference in the composition as well as spectrum of bile acid between WT and HT mice, suggesting the HT mice carried out normal cholesterol and bile acid metabolism under normal fed condition. In agreement with the previous findings that sulfonation is a minor pathway in mice, sulfonated cholic acid (CA-S) was found to be about 20% and 1% of the hepatic cholic acid (CA) and total bile acids, respectively. Among the predominant bile acids, only taurine-conjugated cholic acid was the preferred substrate of Sult2a8. Therefore, majority of sulfonated bile acids were CA and T-CA, which were estimated to be about 10% of total bile acids at most. The plasma CA-S level of HT mice was consistently and significantly lower than that of WT mice. Furthermore, a noticeable lower level of CA-S was also found in liver, gallbladder and urine thought it was not statistically significant. These results suggest that although sulfonated bile acids were only a minor component, the 50% reduction of hepatic Sult2a8 activity in HT mice significantly lowered CA-S formation, confirming that Sult2a8 played a regulatory role on bile acids homeostasis physiologically. Objective 3: Determine the effect of Sult2a8 deficiency in energy balance in the Sult2a8-deficient transgenic mouse model Initially, we examined whether Sult2a8 deficiency impacted on regular energy metabolism by measuring the plasma levels of various metabolites. Results of blood chemistry analyses indicated that both WT and HT mice exhibited a similar value on blood glucose, triglyceride, glycerol, free fatty acids, ketone bodies and cholesterol levels without any significant difference. In addition, the plasma levels of insulin and leptin were also indistinguishable between WT and HT mice. Next the WT and HT mice were subject to 48-hr starvation. There was a significant decrease in blood glucose levels and an obvious increase in the plasma level of ketone bodies. However, there was no significant changes in the plasma levels of triglycerides, glycerol and free fatty acids. Fasting also induced a significant decrease in the plasma levels of insulin and leptin hormones. Importantly, both WT and HT mice in either sex displayed similar responses, and no detectable difference was found. These results suggest both the WT and HT mice conducted normal energy metabolism and exhibited normal hormonal regulatory responses to energy deprivation. Despite no significant difference was found in most of energy metabolites between WT and HT mice, it is of interest to note that there was a drastic decrease in the plasma cholesterol level in male HT mice following fasting, but not in the female HT mice, nor in the WT mice. Furthermore, a significant increase in hepatic T-CA level were found in male HT mice following 48-hr fasting. These results indicated that in the deficiency of Sult2a8, hepatic cholesterol metabolism in male mice was disrupted. Given that sulfonated bile acids are more water soluble, but is less able to be re-absorbed into liver via the enterohepatic recirculation. Lines of evidences also showed that there is a decrease in the plasma LDL and HDL lipoproteins if the bile acid receptor FXR is activated. A possibility arises that there is an increase of hepatic cholesterol breakdown into bile acid and forming the T-CA during energy deprivation. In the Sult2a8 deficient HT mice, most of T-CA is non-sulfonated, and therefore most of the excreted T-CA will be recirculated back to liver when compare with WT control mice. With the elevated hepatic T-CA level, activity of bile acid receptor FXR probably up-regulated and resulted in reducing plasma LDL and HDL lipoproteins. Subsequently, the plasma cholesterol level in male HT mice was drastically reduced following the 48-hr fasting. In brief, results of current study clearly indicates a regulatory role of sulfotransferase in bile acid homeostasis and cholesterol metabolism, suggesting sulfotransferase is a therapeutic target for metabolic syndrome. In addition, as the cholesterol lowering effect was observed only after fasting, our study also reverberates the physiological significance of caloric restriction on modulating energy metabolism.

14109414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109414.value: Major findings 1. Sult2a8 gene encodes a cytosolic sulfotransferase which is male-dominant and liver-specific, and 7α-hydroxyl bile acids are the preferred substrates for Sult2a8. 2. Sult2a8-deficient heterozygous mice can serve as a mice model for examining the physiological roles of sulfotransferase. However, the use of congenic C57BL/6 Bruce4 ES cells for transgenic mice construction should be carefully evaluated. 3. Sult2a8 is a physiological regulator of bile acid homeostasis and cholesterol metabolism. 4. With its ability to modulate blood cholesterol levels, Sult2a8 / sulfotransferase is a therapeutic target for treating metabolic syndrome. 5, The beneficiary effects of caloric restriction on energy metabolism might be partly acting via modulation of bile acids homeostasis. Research outcome 1. One research paper was published in a high impact journal (J Lipid Res) which also accompanied with an editorial comment, three conference papers were published, and one manuscript is under preparation / submitted. 2. The project was honoured with two distinguish awards during conference presentation. 3. Two PhD students (Mr. Kai Wong and Mr. Jian Xu), two research assistants (Mr. Martin Chan and Dr. Xing Liu) and one technical staff (Ms Pik-Shan Li) were trained in the project with all the technical ability to construct and maintain transgenic mice, LC-MS/MS metabolomics analysis, and various key biochemical analytic assays.

14109414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109414.value: Results of the present study imply sulfotransferase could be a therapeutic target for metabolic syndrome, and bile acids might be a key mediator for the beneficiary effects of caloric restriction. These two implications open a new perspective in the field and many questions have yet to be answered. With the limitations of our mouse model being heterozygous in nature and the Sult2a8 gene was knocked down in all the tissues, the off-target effects, such as the sulfonation of steroid hormones in adrenal glands, could not be fully assessed. Hence, it is important to construct a hepatic-specific conditional Sult2a8 KO mice model for further evaluation. Once the homozygous hepatic Sult2a8 KO mice are available, the mice can be subject to fasting to re-examine the changes in energy metabolism. On the other hand, hepatic bile acid pool can be manipulated with supplementary supply of bile acids for evaluating the effect of bile acids in regulation of energy metabolism.

14109414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109414.value: Bile acids are synthesized from cholesterol in liver, and lines of evidence show that bile acids regulate energy metabolism. Sult2a8 is a male-predominant and liver-specific mouse cytosolic sulfotransferase which transfers a sulfonate group (SO3) to bile acids. Sulfonation increases the water solubility of bile acids and facilitates bile acid elimination, and thus maintains the balance of bile acid pool. We created a global Sult2a8 knockout (KO) mouse model by targeted gene disruption. The heterozygous (HT) mutant was viable and fertile, but embryonic lethality was unexpectedly found in homozygous Sult2a8 KO animal as well as in wide-type (WT) mice. A ~50% decrease in the hepatic sulfonation activity was found in the male, but not female, Sult2a8 HT mutants, confirming that Sult2a8 is the major cytosolic sulfotransferase in male mice. Both WT and HT mice were found to conduct similar energy metabolism, fasting induced accumulation of hepatic conjugated bile acids, which results in lowering plasma cholesterol level in Sult2a8 deficient male HT mice. The ability to lower blood cholesterol level in Sult2a8-deficient mice during energy deprivation suggests that sulfotransferase is a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases, and balance of bile acid pool might mediate the beneficiary effects of restricting food-intakes.

14109814.value: To establish a new paradigm to study dendritic regeneration in mammalian central nervous system neurons with time-lapse in vivo imaging. To investigate the impact of PTEN and/or SOCS3 deletion on dendritic regeneration following optic nerve crush via (1) determining the time window in which dendritic regeneration would still be possible following optic nerve injury, (2) measuring the rate of change of dendritic regeneration, and (3) examining the association between dendritic and axonal regeneration and the corresponding functional recovery.

14109814.label: Realisation of objectives
14109814.value: (A) Objective 1 – A new paradigm to study neuroprotection and neuroregeneration - We have successfully established a new paradigm for evaluation of neuroprotective and neuroregeneration interventions through demonstrating the feasibility of using time-lapse, in vivo imaging to measure dendritic and axonal changes of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) over 6 months of follow-up following modification of signaling pathways for cell growth and protein synthesis via deletion of PTEN/SOCS3 in eyes with optic nerve injury. - Evaluation of the effectiveness of a neuroprotective or neuroregenerative treatment for RGCs has been predicated on histological analysis of the number of RGCs in the retina and the number of axons in the optic nerve. The dendrites of RGCs are rarely examined in neuroprotection/neuroregeneration studies because the dendritic arborization is difficult to demarcate and analyze, which is largely related to the complexity of axonal and dendritic processes at different layers of the retina. As the Thy-1 YFP transgenic line expresses florescence protein only in a small fraction of RGCs in the retina, the dendritic arborization and the axon of an individual RGC can be traced and measured. The cross-breeding of the Thy-1-YFP line with the PTENf/f and SOCS3f/f lines in this study has provided a unique model to investigate the neuroprotective and neuroregenerative effect of PTEN/SOCS3 deletion on the structural integrity of the axons and dendrites of RGCs. Whereas deletion of PTEN/SOCS3 has been shown to promote axon regeneration of the RGCs, our data are the first to demonstrate that prevention of dendritic shrinkage is feasible after downregulating PTEN in the RGCs following optic nerve injury. Functional recovery of vision requires preservation of both axonal and dendritic connections. Our study may prove transformative for screening, testing, and development of therapies for neuroprotection or neuroregeneration. (B) Objective 2 – Impact of PTEN/SOCS3 deletion on dendritic and axonal arborizations of RGCs - In the original proposal, we hypothesized that dendritic regeneration would follow dendritic shrinkage in mice with deletion of PTEN/SOCS3 following optic nerve injury. However, neither dendritic shrinkage nor dendritic regeneration was observed in most RGCs in mice with PTEN deletion, and in mice with both PTEN and SOCS3 deletion. Unexpectedly, robust aberrant axon regeneration was evidenced in the retina in these mutants. This is in contrast to mice with deletion of SOCS3 and control mice in which dendritic shrinkage, loss of the axon and the soma were detected following optic nerve injury. Nevertheless, axon regeneration was detected in the optic nerve in the three mutants. Our finding suggests that while deleting PTEN or deleting SOCS3 can promote axon regeneration after optic nerve injury, only the former prevents dendritic shrinkage in the RGCs. - We have shown that the effectiveness of a neuroprotective/neuroregenerative strategy can be evaluated by measuring the rate of change of total dendritic length and the rate of change of dendritic complexity (Sholl analysis). The rates of change of total dendritic length and dendritic complexity were –81.27 µm/day (95% CI: –100.78 to –61.77 µm/day) and –7.11 %/day (95% CI: –8.66 to –5.57 %/day), respectively, for the control mice; and –77.06 µm/day (95% CI: –132.96 to –21.15 µm/day) and –7.02 %/day (95% CI: –12.27 to –1.78 %/day), respectively, for the Thy-1-YFP-SCOS3 mice. By contrast, the rates of change of total dendritic length and dendritic complexity were -2.08 µm/day (95% CI: –5.94 to 1.77 µm/day) and –0.21 %/day (95% CI: –0.47 to 0.05 %/day), respectively, for the Thy-1-YFP/PTEN-/- mice; and -0.98 µm/day (95% CI: –4.24 to 2.29 µm/day) and –0.13 %/day (95% CI: –0.33 to 0.08 %/day), respectively, for the Thy-1-YFP/PTEN-/-SOCS3-/- mice following optic nerve crush. The comparisons of the rates of dendritic shrinkage support that deletion of PTEN alone is effective to prevent dendritic shrinkage. (C) Additional objectives achieved Since our finding indicates deletion of PTEN to be critical to both axon regeneration and prevention of dendritic shrinkage following optic nerve injury, we then performed additional experiments to identify potential upstream regulators of PTEN and investigate if therapeutic intervention can be devised to downregulate the expression of PTEN for treatment of optic nerve injury or optic neuropathies. Important findings from these additional studies are that the expression of PTEN is developmentally regulated in RGCs, with increasing expression of PTEN with age; and that the developmental upregulation of PTEN expression is connected to a corresponding downregulation of microRNA-19a in the RGCs. The developmental upregulation of PTEN likely attributes in part to the loss of intrinsic regenerative capacity in mature RGCs. Our data uncover a previously unrecognized involvement of the microRNA-19a-PTEN axis in regulating the developmental decline in axon regenerative capacity of RGCs, and underscore the potential therapeutic application of intravitreal injection of microRNAs to downregulate PTEN for treatment of optic neuropathies. (II) Objectives not achieved We have not examined the association between dendritic and axonal regeneration and the corresponding functional recovery because there are studies recently published suggesting that functional recovery may not be attainable after PTEN deletion as most of the regenerated axons would not reinnervate the thalamus and midbrain and axon misguidance is common (e.g. Luo X, et al. Three-dimensional evaluation of retinal ganglion cell axon regeneration and pathfinding in whole mouse tissue after injury. Exp Neurol. 2013;247:653-62). Further investigation on axon guidance and pathfinding is critical to direct axon growth to reinnervate the appropriate targets for recovery of visual function.

14109814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109814.value: 1. We have demonstrated a new paradigm of evaluating the effectiveness of a neuroprotective or neuroregenerative intervention through interrogating and following the changes of the structural integrity of the dendrites and axons of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) in the retina using time-lapse, in vivo confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy. 2. While deletion of PTEN and/or SOCS3 has been shown to be effective to promote axon regeneration after optic nerve injury in previous studies, we show that deletion of PTEN, but not deletion of SOCS3, prevents dendritic shrinkage of RGCs (Part C8, No.1, Figure 4). The rate of dendritic shrinkage is rapid following optic nerve crush in mice with SOCS3 deletion and control mice whereas the rates of change of total dendritic length and dendritic complexity (Sholl analysis) were insignificant in mice with PTEN and SOCS3 deletion and in mice with PTEN deletion. Further, new axons sprouting was evidenced in the retinas in these mutants (Part C8, No.1, Figure 5). Regenerating axons were tortuous, traversing in different layers of the retina (Part C8, No.1, Figure 6). Remarkably, aberrant axon regeneration could be detected in the retina as early as within one week following the optic nerve crush and the regeneration sustained over 6 months (Part C8, No.1, Figure 5). Our data are the first to demonstrate that prevention of dendritic shrinkage in the RGCs is possible after optic nerve crush. Targeting PTEN or its downstream target mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) would be relevant to the development of neuroprotective and neuroregenerative therapies for patients with optic neuropathies. 3. We show that the loss of axon regenerative capacity in mature RGCs is partially attributed to an upregulation of PTEN during development consequential to a drastic decline of microRNA-19a (Part C8, No.2, Figure 1). Intravitreal injection of miR-19a delivered by adeno-associated virus increases miR-19a levels in the RGCs, downregulates the expression PTEN, and improves axon regeneration in vivo after optic nerve crush in adult rodents (Part C8, No.2, Figure 2). Remarkably, upregulation of miR-19a expression also increases axon extension in RGCs isolated from aged human donors (Part C8, No.2, Figure 3). Our data uncover a previously unrecognized involvement of the microRNA-19a-PTEN axis in regulating the developmental decline in axon regenerative capacity of RGCs, and underscore the potential therapeutic application of intravitreal injection of microRNAs to rejuvenate aged RGCs for axon regeneration in the treatment of optic neuropathies. Two original articles have been prepared for submission (Part C8).

14109814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109814.value: As deletion of PTEN, even with combination of other interventions including intraocular injection of cAMP and zymosan, may not attain a sufficient number of regenerating axons to reach the thalamus and mid brain (Luo X, et al. Three-dimensional evaluation of retinal ganglion cell axon regeneration and pathfinding in whole mouse tissue after injury. Exp Neurol. 2013;247:653-62), identifying other regulators that can further promote axon regeneration and prevent dendritic shrinkage would be the next stage of development of the research. Our studies on developmental changes of microRNAs expression in RGCs have provided a new perspective to identify relevant microRNAs for restoration of the intrinsic regenerative capacity of RGCs. MicroRNA-19a is only one of the regulators of axon regeneration identified from our microarray analysis. We plan to identify and validate other microRNAs that have the potential to create a molecular environment conducive to robust axon regeneration and preservation of dendritic arborization.

14109814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109814.value: The optic nerve is composed of the fibers extended from the retinal neurons, relaying visual information from the retina to the brain for interpretation of vision. Diseases affecting the optic nerve, such as glaucoma, often lead to permanent loss in vision because degeneration of retinal neurons is an irreversible process. In this study, we developed an experimental model to investigate the degenerative and regenerative processes of optic nerve injury by imaging the retinal neurons in rodents non-invasively and longitudinally. We demonstrated that by genetically manipulating the signaling pathways responsible for cell growth and protein synthesis, we were able to preserve the structural integrity of these retinal neurons. Our study has provided an efficient approach to test and develop strategies for protection and regeneration of the optic nerve in patients with optic nerve diseases.

14109814.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
14109814.value: We collaborated with Professor Sabel Bernhard, director of the Institute of Medical Psychology at the Otto-von-Guericke University of Magdeburg in Magdeburg, Germany, between 2013 and 2016 on a research project investigating if electrical stimulation is effective to preserve the dendritic and axonal arborizations of retinal ganglion cells. Unexpectedly, we found electrical stimulation induced more dendritic shrinkage compared with control mice after optic nerve crush but improved the survival of retinal ganglion cell soma. The finding that there was complete loss of visual evoked potential in mice receiving electrical stimulation supports the notion that preservation of the dendrites is critical to functional recovery of retinal ganglion cells after optic nerve injury. This study was published in Scientific Reports in 2017. Henrich-Noack P, Sergeeva EG, Eber T, You Q, Voigt N, Köhler J, Wagner S, Lazik S, Mawrin C, Xu G, Biswas S, Sabel BA, Leung CK. Electrical brain stimulation induces dendritic stripping but improves survival of silent neurons after optic nerve damage. Sci Rep. 2017;7:627.

14109914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109914.value: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder and a third of patients with epilepsy remain unresponsive to drug treatment. The only realistic hope for these patients is to find out the seizure focus with a view to resection. Surface electroencephalography(EEG) is the most important and least invasive form of investigation. It can record brain waves at the time of seizure or in between attacks. Signal artifacts and suboptimal spatial localization are the major drawbacks of standard EEG. Study aims: High-density surface EEG is a novel research tool with potential clinical application. With advancing techniques of high-density EEG for brain signals we test the hypothesis that high-density EEG may pinpoint EEG generators with respect to the surgical area determined by multidisciplinary conferences. The proportion of patients who ultimately achieve seizure-freedom after epilepsy surgery may serve as the "ground truth" to gauge the accuracy of high-density EEG. Methods: We will prospectively recruit 150 patients who suffer from epilepsy that is not responsive to medications. These patients must have magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) or a booking-appointment within 3 years. 75 patients will be assigned to high-density EEG(128 electrodes) and 75 patients to standard EEG(16 channels) with 1:1 randomization and stratification for brain lesion, location and previous EEG information. Electrodes will be applied to the head of each patient using international 10-5 system/Geodesic Sensor Net during a monitoring-period of between 5-7 days to capture their seizure-attacks. For high-density EEG, the configuration of the surface electrodes may be tailored after the first seizure to provide high-density seizure-map around the suspected focus. Discrete recording sessions are run in 2-hourly time-slots to ensure patient comfort. The electrical signals at the time of seizure will be analyzed by wavelet-denoising coupled with absolute-slope method(WT+ASM), an analytic tool developed by our group. The electrical signals in between attacks will be analyzed by Matlab-based, dipolar and distributed source models(e-Connectome, Field-trip, Brainstorm, Geodesic). The primary outcome is sensitivity/specificity of localization according to resection margin. The secondary outcome is sensitivity/specificity with respect to surgical location among patients achieving seizure-freedom. Significance: This study may increase the sensitivity/specificity of EEG localization by 20%. Ultimately, it helps patients who have multiple lesions or no lesion to achieve epilepsy surgery, who may otherwise be denied surgical therapy. N/A

14110314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110314.value: 肝臟是一個中央葡萄糖代謝的重要器官，同時也是胰島素作用的主要目標。胰島素對於肝臟有兩個主要作用，一是控制脂肪酸和甘油三酯的合成（脂肪生成），二是下調肝臟的葡萄糖產生（糖質新生）。因此在肝細胞功能缺陷的情況下， 二型糖尿病（T2DM）風險也會相應的增加。與此同時，由於维生素D是眾所周知的調節钙和骨質的平衡素， 所以缺乏維生素D（維生素D缺乏癥）也相對的會增強胰島素抵抗，削弱胰岛素的分泌，并會間接地影響許多其它與二型糖尿病相關的代謝綜合癥疾病。越來越多的研究發現表明，二型糖尿病糖與肝功能障礙有著密切相關的關係，包括脂質代謝異常和缺乏維生素D，更重要的是對於在肝臟胰島素抵抗的發病機制里的肝臟糖異生起著關鍵作用。鑒於這些研究結果，我們推測維生素D藉由局部肝內維生素D與肝脂肪和糖質新生的直接調製信號來調節胰島素的敏感性，從而降低肝臟胰島素抵抗。 爲了驗證以上這個推測，我們將運用體內，離體和體外實驗模式，在正常或者胰島素獨立的糖尿病狀態下，透過刺激維生素D缺乏或消耗的方法來比較 對肝脂質的生成和對肝葡萄糖的生成的影響。我們的目標是希望研究出在肝臟里，是否維護正常的維他命D的功能有助於在正常血糖情況下維持正常胰島素敏感性下或在高血糖的情況下能夠改善胰島素的抵抗，從而促進正常的葡萄糖代謝。我們也將進一步測定在調節正常葡萄糖代謝的作用里，是否肝臟里的AMPK和鈣之間的信號，內質網應激，胰島素信息路徑，局部腎素-血管緊張素系統的活性，有否Notch信號都有提供保護功能。 該項目的研究結果可能有助于對非胰島素依賴性糖尿病的治療的標靶發展和調節營養因素。這項研究方案所能提供的機制學證據有助於對維他命D缺乏癥的臨床研究設計而達到控制非酒精性脂肪肝病以及血糖穩態水平，同時也進一步爲了保持充足的维生素D状态而帶來的潛在益處提供了有力證據。

14110314.label: Realisation of objectives
14110314.value: The stated three objectives have now been basically addressed and achieved in this completion report. Briefly, we employed in vitro and in vivo experimental approaches to investigate into the protective effects of calcitriol (an active form of vitamin D) on hepatic dysfunction in type 2 diabetes. To address these issues, T2DM db/db mouse model was selected to examine the effects of calcitriol on hepatic and systemic metabolic abnormalities. In conjugation with in vivo studies, we also employed in vitro HepG2 cells (a hepatocellular carcinoma cell line) that were cultured and exposed to high-glucose and insulin conditions, mimicking insulin resistant state, in order to further explore the mechanism-of-action whereby vitamin D signalling is involved in the determination of hepatic insulin resistance. Our study findings indicate that vitamin D/calcitriol is able to ameliorate hepatic triglyceride accumulation and glucose output, at least in part, via the mediation of Ca2+/CaMKKbeta/AMPK signaling pathway under insulin-resistant conditions. Please refer to the detailed descriptions of Section 6.1. "Major findings and research outcome" as well as "Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action" of Section 6. Please also refer to the publication and conference list in Section 8 and 9 of "Research Output" in this completion report.

14110314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110314.value: Given calcitriol/hormonal vitamin D being recognised to regulate calcium and phosphate metabolism and to promote bone health, our major study findings have shown that vitamin D has beneficial action on ameliorating abnormalities in hepatic lipid and glucose metabolism under the insulin-resistant state, without any appreciable toxic effects. These demonstrated effects were, at least partly, regulated via the mediation of Ca2+/CaMKKbeta/AMPK pathway, given higher dosages we used (i.e. 0.5-2.5 ug/kg/2 days in mice and 1-10 nM in HepG2 cells). Our data obtained suggest a potentially useful option for the adjuvant treatment of vitamin D in patients with T2DM. This extension of therapeutic usage of calcitriol may prove as meaningful as other clinical measures for diabetic medicine, in the same way that new pharmacological benefits have been identified at different dosages of well-known therapeutic agents, including aspirin, dopamine and glucocorticoids. It is noticeable, however, that many studies have shown no meaningful benefits of vitamin D supplementation in established T2DM. The reasons for these observations might rest on inadequate doses of intact vitamin D, especially if defective vitamin D activation arises from hepatic defects due to T2DM or NAFLD. Simply using larger doses of intact vitamin D may prove helpful, but might induce toxicity, which would be slow to resolve. On the other hand, calcitriol does not accumulate in adipose tissue,with its short half-life and its effects are rapid in both onset and off-set manner, which might make it easier to avoid toxicity. Because of individual differences in sensitivity to calcitriol in humans as well as between species difference, the selected dosages for human use cannot be extrapolated from experimental data. Despite this fact, our study findings point toward the potential value of calcitriol being as an adjunctive therapy for obesity-related T2DM and NAFLD, which warrants to be further investigated in the future. Please also refer to our publication and reference list in Section 8 and Section 9 of "Research Output".

14110314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110314.value: As stated in the last report, we have also started on exploring the potential interaction between the RAS and vitamin D in the modulation of hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism. As expected, our preliminary results showed that major RAS components (e.g. angiotensinogen, AT1/AT2/Mas receptors, and ACE/ACE2) were expressed in the HepG2 cells and isolated hepatocyte cells. Interestingly, our preliminary data also showed that high-glucose plus high-insulin culture conditions significantly upregulated the expression of the key RAS components, notably the AT1 receptor in HepG2 cells. More interestingly, treatment with different concentrations of calcitriol (0.01-10nM) significantly suppressed the inappropriate activation of the AT1 receptor expression under insulin-resistant conditions in a dose dependent manner; these inhibitory effects on AT1 receptor were observed from 4 to 6 hours after calcitriol treatment. In corroboration with the HepG2 cells, similar results on the protective effects of calcitriol were also observed in the isolated hepatocytes. These data indicate that calcitriol (an active form of vitamin D) has modulatory action on the inappropriate activation of the hepatic RAS under insulin-resistant conditions in HepG2 cells, and that potential vitamin D supplementation might provide a cost-effective measure for improving hepatic metabolic dysfunction in T2DM and related NAFLD. Please also refer to the abstract of EASD in Section 9 of the completion report.

14110314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110314.value: Vitamin D deficiency, or insufficiency, is commonly observed in many countries. Its deficiency is known to be closely associated with increased insulin resistance, impaired insulin secretion, and poorly controlled glucose homeostasis, and thus is correlated with the risk of metabolic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Meanwhile, the liver plays key roles in glucose and lipid metabolism, and its deregulation leads to abnormalities in hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism. The present study provides a scientific basis for the protective effects of vitamin D on hepatic insulin resistance, particularly in the context of type 2 diabetes and related diseases. Our results would be important for informing healthcare providers and patients about the potential benefits of vitamin D supplementation, as a food additive or nutraceutical. In short, the significance of this work points toward the potential use of vitamin D supplementation to oppose the development or worsening of obesity-related metabolic diseases, such as T2DM and NAFLD. In view of this, the results obtained provide a cost-effective measure for improving and preventing hepatic dysfunction as seen in metabolic diseases.

14110614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110614.value: Our research question is: Does surgical intervention for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) in children improve blood pressure (BP) profile? Childhood OSA is common and it is associated with important morbidities, namely cardiovascular abnormalities as well as neurocognitive and metabolic disturbances. Elevated BP and hypertension have been documented in children with OSA, and especially those with moderate-to-severe disease (obstructive apnoea-hypopnoea index [OAHI] >5). Childhood BP abnormalities are risk factors for adulthood hypertension, atherosclerosis and metabolic syndrome. There is ample robust evidence to suggest that elevated BP and hypertension in children should be recognized and tackled early in order to prevent adulthood adverse complications. The first-line treatment for childhood OSA is adenotonsillectomy. However, there has been no controlled study to evaluate the usefulness of adenotonsillectomy in ameliorating cardiovascular disturbances in children with OSA. Few paediatric cohort studies with flawed methodology provided conflicting findings on whether BP abnormalities are potentially reversible following treatment. In our locality, parents are often reluctant for their children to undergo surgery, thus uptake for this procedure is low. It is usual practice for children with OSA whose parents have consented for surgery to have to wait for 5-6 months before the operation. In this study we will randomly assign pre-pubertal non-obese children, aged 5 to 11 years with moderate-to-severe OSA to surgical intervention or watchful waiting. The surgical intervention includes adentonsillectomy +/- turbinate reduction if latter is deemed necessary according to predefined criteria, to be carried out within 4-6 weeks after ENT assessment. Both groups will undergo nocturnal polysomnography, ambulatory 24-hr blood pressure (24-hr ABP) monitoring and assessment by an ENT surgeon before and after a 6-month intervention period. The primary outcome is change in 24-hr ABP parameters (daytime and nighttime systolic and diastolic BP, 24-hr mean BP and nocturnal dipping) in the two study groups over the intervention period. Secondary outcomes will include changes in indexes of OSA severity (OAHI and respiratory disturbance index [RDI]) and symptoms of OSA. We hypothesize that surgical intervention will lead to significant improvements in ambulatory blood pressure parameters. If this study confirms BP abnormalities in children with OSA are amendable following treatment, such important information will be useful in parents counseling in order to increase their acceptance for surgery. The result will also be an important catalyst for change in our current management approach for this prevalent and important condition. 我們的研究問題是：手術治療能否改善阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停（OSA）患兒的血壓？ 兒童OSA是十分常見的睡眠問題，其併發症可能包括心血管異常，神經認知功能受損及代謝紊亂。臨床研究指出OSA患兒的血壓較非患者為高，尤其是那些有中度至嚴重疾病的（阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停低通氣指數[OAHI]>5/h）。兒童血壓升高是成年後高血壓、動脈粥樣硬化和代謝綜合症的危險因素。有充分有力的證據表明，有血壓升高或高血壓的孩子應及早被診斷及接受治療以防止成年後出現不良的併發症。 扁桃體增殖體切除術是兒童OSA的第一線治療。然而，一直沒有任何對照研究以評估該手術對改善OSA患兒的心血管異常的成效。只有少數群組研究探討OSA患兒的血壓異常是否可憑藉治療得以回復正常，但始終未有一致的結論。 在本港，家長往往不願意讓子女接受手術，對該手術的需求偏低，所以相關的資源也較少，輪候時間一般需要5至6個月。 在這項研究中，研究對象為5至11歲確診患有中度至重度OSA的青春期前非肥胖兒童，我們將隨機分配參加者至手術干預組或觀察等待組。手術干預組的參加者將接受增殖體扁桃體切除術。如果患兒同時患有過敏性鼻炎，並在耳鼻喉檢查中發現鼻甲肥大，患兒將同時接受鼻甲減容術。手術將在耳鼻喉科檢查後4至6週內進行。兩組的參加者均會在干預前及干預後6個月進行夜間多導睡眠監測，24小時動態血壓監測及耳鼻喉檢查。此研究的主要結果指標是24小時動態血壓參數（白天和夜間的收縮壓和舒張壓，24小時平均血壓和夜間血壓下降）干預期前後的改變。次要結果指標包括OSA嚴重程度（OAHI和呼吸紊亂指數[RDI]）和徵狀的改變。 我們假設手術干預可使動態血壓參數顯著改善。如果這個研究證實OSA兒童的血壓異常經治療後可改善，此重要信息將可作為說服家長接受子女進行該手術的理據。研究結果也將促使我們改變目前針對這普遍而重要的疾病的管理方法。

14110614.label: Realisation of objectives
14110614.value: A total of 150 pre-pubertal children diagnosed to have moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea (MS-OSA, defined as apnoea hypopnoea index (AHI) ≥3/h) were recruited. Eight of them were excluded because of obesity. One hundred and forty-two non-obese children were enrolled and randomly allocated to early adenotonsillectomy (AT) or watchful waiting (WW) groups. Subjects allocated to the AT group were arranged for early AT and repeat assessment was conducted 6 months after AT. Those allocated to the WW group were put on the waitlist of AT and reevaluated 9-10 months after the baseline visit. Twenty-one of them are still pending for the follow-up visit. Among the remaining 121 subjects, 81 successfully completed the study protocol whereas 40 were excluded or drop-out. Their group allocations were disclosed upon completion or termination of the study. A total of 66 subjects were allocated to the AT group, of whom 41 completed the study protocol. Twenty-five (38%) were excluded due to refusal of follow-up (n=9, 14%), refusal of surgery (n=12, 18%), or insufficient ambulatory blood pressure readings (n=4, 6%). Fifty-five subjects were allocated to the WW group, of whom 40 completed the study protocol. Fifteen (27%) were excluded due to refusal of follow-up (n=12, 22%) or insufficient ambulatory blood pressure readings (n=3, 5%). According to our initial sample size estimation, a total of 116 subjects were required for this study. Taking into account the 21 subjects who are expected to complete all assessments in the coming months, we still need to recruit at least 14 more participants. We are hopeful that this can be done in the coming summer months. The study has taken a longer time than expected to recruit and complete all necessary baseline and repeat assessments due to the following reasons: - High rate of drop-out and refusal of treatment, resulting in a total incomplete rate of 24%, i.e. 14% higher than what we expected. - The recruitment rate is also slower than expected. Many of the potential subjects were found to have mild instead of moderate-to-severe OSA. - Our sleep research service was stopped during the peak flu period which lasted from January to April each year, and in 2018 the period was unexpectedly prolonged. - Cases allocated to the treatment group were expected to undergo surgery within a short timeframe, 6-8 weeks after seeing our ENT colleagues but unfortunately in many instances this did not happen as a result of operation list being cancelled, cases with more urgent illnesses taking up the operation slot. This has led to delay in the repeat assessment. Attempts to overcome problems: - we have offered to carry out sleep study assessment at weekends but once again it depends on bed availability and whether parents / carers are able to accompany their children for hospital admission at weekends. - we have liaised with ward manager and nursing colleagues regarding the use of our day ward for sleep study assessment. Usage of our day ward is less affected by acute emergency admissions. Liaison work involves providing extra manpower to cover for the day ward, generation of a new admission code and approval by hospital hierarchy and our application has recently been approved. This initiative can begin this coming summer. At both baseline and follow-up visits, all participants underwent nocturnal polysomnography (PSG), 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) and upper airway examination. Their parents completed a set of questionnaires including an OSA symptom questionnaire (HKCSQ), modified Epworth sleepiness scale (ESS), paediatric daytime sleepiness scale (PDSS), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) rating scale and child behaviour checklist (CBCL). The complete dataset of 81 subjects who have completed the study is ready for preliminary statistical analysis. General linear models and generalized estimating equations were used to test the group, time and group*time effects on continuous and categorical outcomes, respectively. All statistical analyses were performed on a per-protocol basis.

14110614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110614.value: After AT, the severity of OSA significantly improved, accompanied by an increase in body mass index (BMI) z score. No significant improvement was observed in any blood pressure parameters including daytime and nighttime systolic and diastolic BP and BP z score, and nocturnal BP dipping. Daytime systolic blood pressure (SBP) and 24-hour average SBP increased after AT, probably attributed to the increase in BMI. The WW group did not show any significant change in OSA severity, BMI z score and BP. On the other hand, the AT group had significant improvements in OSA-related symptoms and behavioural problems over the WW group. Daytime sleepiness scales and ADHD-rating scales were significantly reduced after AT. Moreover, both daytime and nighttime symptoms were significantly reduced after AT. Improved nighttime symptoms included snoring, night sweating, laboured breathing, oral breathing, witnessed apnoea, frequent body movement. Improved daytime symptoms included daytime fatigue, waking up unrefreshed after sleep, and morning dry mouth. In contrast, the WW group did not show any significant improvement except for a reduction in the hyperactivity score of the ADHD-rating scale. In addition, significant improvements in behavioural problems were demonstrated after AT. The total problem score derived from CBCL was significantly reduced. Both internalizing and externalizing problems were significantly improved. More specifically, the following subscales were improved: Somatic complaints, thought problems, attention problems, depressive problems, attention deficit hyperactivity problems, sluggish cognitive tempo, obsessive/compulsive problems and stress problems. No significant change was found in any subscale or total problem scores in the WW group. In summary, the results of this randomised controlled trial supported that AT can effectively reduce OSA severity indexes obtained from nocturnal polysomnography. AT can also improve OSA-related daytime and nocturnal symptoms, and behavioural problems subjectively reported by parents. However, no significant change in ambulatory blood pressure could be observed after AT.

14110614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110614.value: Data of this randomised controlled trial provide high-quality evidence to disprove the causal relationship between childhood OSA and elevated blood pressure in a group of non-obese prepubertal children. However, there are still a number of unanswered questions related to the association between childhood OSA and blood pressure. Compared to our previously published study, the BP levels of the subjects of this current trial were lower. Moreover, the BP levels of most of the subjects participated in this trial were within normal range. Elevated BP may only be found in some of the children with OSA but not the others. We shall try to investigate if there is any predictor of elevated BP in children with OSA by a case-control study comparing OSA children with and without elevated BP. A further research question is whether surgical treatment can improve BP levels in OSA children with elevated BP. This will need another randomised controlled trial to provide the answer.

14110614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110614.value: Accumulating evidence suggested that childhood OSA is associated with elevated blood pressure which can be reversed after OSA treatment. However, none of these data were obtained from randomised controlled trial. Our study was the first randomised controlled trial to investigate the effects of surgical removal of tonsils and/or adenoid on blood pressure in children with OSA. The study was based on a group of non-obese prepubertal children with moderate-to-severe OSA with adenotonsillar hypertrophy who are typically seen in clinical settings. The results revealed that although the surgical procedure can effectively ameliorate the severity of OSA objectively measured by nocturnal sleep study and also improve OSA-related symptoms and behavioural problems subjectively reported by parents, blood pressure did not change significantly after the surgery. The findings disproved the causal link between childhood OSA and elevated blood pressure, but on the other hand supported the causal relationship between OSA and bebavioural problems in children.
