14113214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113214.value: Vascular dementia (VaD) is considered as the second commonest type of dementia next to Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) is proposed to encompass the full spectrum of cerebrovascular related cognitive impairment, ranging from mild VCI (mVCI) to VaD. mVCI, lying on a continuum between normal cognition and dementia, is the best stage to discover, prevent and intervene its progression. However, consensus is still lacking on the criteria for differentiating different subtypes of mVCI, which will develop to VaD or mixed dementia, remain stable mVCI, or improve to normal cognition, at the early stage. Recent studies reported that patients with dementia could have abnormal functional brain connectivity and altered brain network, which may provide a new perspective to investigate the pathogenesis of VCI and reveal the reorganization of the functional brain network of VCI at early stage. The EEG-informed fMRI analysis could provide complementary information of functional brain network and is potentially an effective way to enhance our understanding of altered functional brain connectivity of VCI. It is thus timely to develop an effective method to intelligently analyze the EEG-informed MRI data and further investigate its potential value in facilitating early differential diagnosis of VCI. The main objective of this project is to establish an effective EEG-informed fMRI analysis framework to investigate the altered functional brain network of VCI in a longitudinal study and detecting the distinctive neuro-connectivity biomarkers for early diagnosis of VCI. The directed functional connectivity of the brain will be evaluated based on graph theory. The reorganized functional brain network of mVCI will be revealed on a group level and the factors influence the progression of VCI will be identified in the longitudinal study by using the EEG-informed fMRI analysis. Then, the multi-modal network metrics contributing to different subtypes of VCI will be selected by using a multi-modal feature selection method and a structured multi-class support vector machine (s-SVM) will be developed for VCI subtype classification. Moreover, a user-friendly open source GUI toolbox will be developed to implement the framework proposed and to enable convenient EEG-informed fMRI analysis for other researchers worldwide. This will be the first study to investigate the functional brain network of VCI based on the complementary information from EEG and fMRI. The results will shed light on revealing the abnormalities of the functional brain network of VCI and provide evidence-based neuro-connectivity biomarkers for the early diagnosis of different subtypes of VCI.

14113214.label: Realisation of objectives
14113214.value: (1) To establish an effective EEG-informed fMRI framework for evaluating the functional brain network. To eliminate the ethnic-related brain difference in brain network analysis, a statistical brain atlas based on a multi-center high quality MRI dataset of 2020 Chinese adults was constructed [1], which has been demonstrated to improve the performance of brain analysis in Chinese populations [2]. To eliminate the variation of different acquisitions in brain analysis, a histogram-based intensity normalization approach was proposed to reduce the intensity variation of MRI images from different acquisitions[3]. To investigate the cognitive state of subjects with cognitive impairment during task state, a background functional connectivity analysis approach was introduced [4]. A date-driven approach based on K-means clustering and two-step singular value decomposition was also proposed to investigate the dynamic functional connectivity of the brain[5]. We also evaluated effects of different preprocessing procedures on EEG-informed fMRI analysis, and proposed an optimal pipeline for the data preprocessing. With the proposed data preprocessing and regressors design such as alpha power time series and peaks, fMRI analysis guided by the denoised EEG signal was able to improve the identify brain areas with significant activations. (2) To reveal the reorganization of the brain network of different subtypes of VCI on group level. Based on activation likelihood estimation, we identified the high-level visual cortices processing “what” and “where” visual perceptions, and the altered structural [6] as well as functional network[7] of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s dementia were investigated . The altered whole brain network patterns in progressive cognitive impairment and stable cognitive impairment were also investigated[8]. We also explored the changes of cerebral perfusion and functional brain network in patients with cognitive impairment, and found the deficits of cerebral blood flow and functional connectivity in the default mode network[9]. To reveal the reorganization of the structural brain network, a new DTI statistical analysis method—tractography atlas-based spatial statistics (TABSS) was proposed. The results showed this method could better interpreter the white matter tracts, and showed age-related FA alternation patterns in elderly[10]. We also proposed a fiber connectivity density (FiCD) method to evaluate the structural connectivity on vertex-wise[11, 12]. Group comparison between post-stroke patients and healthy controls revealed this method could accurately reflect the affected cortical regions due to subcortical lesions [13]. (3) To identify the factors that influence the conversion process from mVCI to VCI no dementia, vascular dementia and mixed dementia. Based on state-of-art deep learning approach, we have proposed several novel approaches to automatically detect/segment the neuroimaging biomarkers of cerebrovascular and cognitive impairment diseases [14, 15]. Then, a multivariate lesion-symptom mapping model based on support vector regression was proposed to investigate the contribution of white matter hyperinternsity location[16], infarct location[17], as well as the joint contribution and distribution patterns of multiple types of small vessel disease imaging features[18] to cognitive impairment. In addition, we also investigated the possible spatial correlation of white matter hyperintensities on cerebral blood flow and spontaneous activities of the brain[19], which would provide a new perspective to reveal the mechanism of cognitive impairment related to white matter change. (4) To classify different subtypes of VCI on individual level by using the multi-modal network metrics. Based on the effective biomarkers derived from functional connectivity/brain network analysis, the support vector machine approach was used to classify the vascular impairment and healthy elderly, the results should a high good performance for the VCI clarification with an accuracy around 80% [20]. (5) To develop a user-friendly toolbox to implement the framework proposed in this project. The Background Network Analysis Toolbox (BNAT) has been developed based on SPM12 under the MATLAB environment. This BNAT toolbox provides a user-friendly pipeline for background network analysis, EEG-informed fMRI analysis, and graph theory analysis. We believe this toolbox will not only implement the framework we proposed, but also enable more clinically-oriented studies related to EEG-informed fMRI, functional connectivity analysis, network analysis, and the diagnosis of different types of cognitive impairment diseases.

14113214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113214.value: In this project, an effective EEG-informed fMRI network analysis pipeline was proposed. A Chinese specific brain template was firstly constructed based on a multi-center high quality MRI dataset of 2020 Chinese adults to eliminate the ethnic-related brain differences during coregistration for brain network analysis [1, 2]. In addition, optimization approach for image reconstruction and noise reductions [21-24] were proposed, which provided effective tools for our template construction. A series of novel segmentation/detection approaches were proposed[25-29], and used to automatically detect/segment the neuroimaing biomarkers (such as cerebral microbleeds, white matter lesion) of elderly [14, 15]. Several novel approaches/pipelines were proposed to investigate the structural and functional brain network. A novel TABSS approach was proposed to investigate the diffusion tensor image along fiber pathways [10] and a new measure (FiCD) was proposed to measure the structural connectivity of the brain on the cerebral cortex[11-13]. The background connectivity[4] and dynamic functional connectivity[5] was proposed to investigate the functional brain network of cognitive impairment and healthy elderly. In addition, these cutting-edge brain network analysis techniques were also applied in other diseases [30-32]. We also proposed a multivariate lesion-symptom mapping approach to mapping the contribution and strategic distribution patterns of neuroimaging features of small vessel disease in cognitive impairment based on the big data derived from thousands of stroke patients in Hong Kong[16-18].

14113214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113214.value: This project focused on the functional and structural network analysis of the patients with VCI. Automatically identify the major manifestations of cerebral small vessel disease would significantly improve the VCI diagnosis as well as prediction. In the further study, we will focus on proposing a novel deep learning approach to automatically identify cerebral small vessel disease biomarkers and explore the potential risk factors of cognitive decline in cognitively healthy elderly.

14113214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113214.value: In this project, we proposed an effective EEG-informed fMRI analysis pipeline and revealed the altered functional/structural network of subjects with cognitive impairment. A series of novel neuroimaging computing approaches were also proposed to support this pipeline. The contributions of small vessel disease on post-stroke cognitive impairment were also explored. The results of this project would improve our understanding of the mechanism of VD/VCI and benefit the clinical diagnosis/prediction of VD/VCI.

14113314.label: Project Objectives
14113314.value: To determine if there is a causal relationship between oxidative stress and atRA homeostasis, our first objective is to test whether induction of oxidative stress in mouse embryos will lead to a change in atRA synthesis/degradation and concentrations, and the expression of target genes of atRA signaling, thereby leading to specific malformations. To determine if excess atRA-induced atRA deficiency is mediated via an increase in oxidative stress, our second objective is to test whether alleviating oxidative stress in atRA-overexposed mouse embryos can normalize atRA synthesis/degradation and concentrations, and the expression of target genes of atRA signaling, thereby reducing the incidence of specific malformations induced by a teratogenic dose of atRA. To determine if disturbance of atRA homeostasis in embryos of diabetic pregnancy is mediated via an increase in oxidative stress, our third objective is to test whether alleviating oxidative stress in embryos of diabetic mice can normalize atRA synthesis/degradation and concentrations, and the expression of target genes of atRA signaling, thereby reducing their susceptibility to specific malformations.

14113314.label: Realisation of objectives
14113314.value: Problems encountered: Due to an outbreak of Mouse Hepatitis Virus in the Animal Holding Core facility, mice were depopulated and no breeding was allowed for several months. Research progress was severely interrupted as majority of experiments in this project required breeding of mice for embryo collection. An extension of project completion date for 4 months was approved by the Research Committee of CUHK in Aug 2017. This study aims to investigate our hypothesis that an increase in oxidative stress in the embryo disturbs retinoic acid (RA) homeostasis and leads to RA deficiency, thereby increasing the propensity to malformations. Three objectives were set up to decipher this proposed linkage between oxidative stress and RA homeostasis in the mouse embryo, which have been achieved as follow: (Objective 3) Oxidative stress is well-documented to be associated with diabetic embryopathy. However the underlying mechanism remains far from clear. We find that mouse embryos exposed to diabetes in utero exhibit significant reduction in RA synthesis and RA concentrations. To test our hypothesis that disruption of RA homeostasis in embryos of diabetic pregnancy is mediated via an increase in oxidative stress, we have employed an in vivo approach to alleviate oxidative stress in embryos of streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, with the prediction that this would restore RA homeostasis and reduce their susceptibility to malformations. Following the original plan as proposed, we attempted to reduce oxidative stress via maternal dietary supplementation with vitamin E, which is a well-employed antioxidant. Vitamin E (VitE) was added to the rodent chow starting from the first day of pregnancy. At mid-gestation [gestational day (GD) 9], and embryos were collected for measurement of the oxidative stress biomarker 8-isoprostane. After confirming the effectiveness of VitE in alleviating oxidative stress, we then examined RA homeostasis by measuring the activity of the enzyme retinal dehydrogenase (Raldh) responsible for synthesis of RA in the GD9 embryo. We have established an in vitro assay to determine the amount of all-trans retinal (substrate of Raldh) being converted into all-trans retinoic acid (RA), which was quantified using a RA reporter cell line that has sensitivity as low as 10-10M RA and can detect trace amount of RA. Next, we measured endogenous concentrations of RA in GD9 embryos using the RA reporter cell line. Moreover, GD9 embryos were subjected to analysis of the expression of several target genes of RA signaling using real-time qRT-PCR. To test whether alleviation of oxidative stress in embryos of diabetic mice could abolish their increased susceptibility to malformations caused by RA deficiency, embryos were maternally challenged at GD9 with bisdiamine, a potent Raldh inhibitor, to lower endogenous RA levels. Embryos were collected at GD10 for determination of RA concentrations using HPLC. Fetuses were examined at near-term (GD18) for malformations. After achieving objective 3, we have extended the study to decipher whether a decrease in RA concentrations in embryos of diabetic mice indeed increases their malformation risk, by testing the effect of correcting RA deficiency with direct replenishment of RA. To this end, diabetic and non-diabetic pregnant mice were fed a diet supplemented with various dosages of RA starting from GD7. Embryos were collected at GD9 for measurement of RA concentrations and the expressions of several genes as molecular readout of RA signaling. Moreover, maternal blood glucose and embryonic 8-isoprostane concentrations were determined. After finding out the optimal dose of RA diet to raise RA concentrations in embryos of diabetic mice to a level similar to embryos of non-diabetic mice, pregnant mice were challenged at GD9 with bisdiamine to lower the RA level. Fetuses were examined at near-term (GD18) for malformations. Besides embryopathy, oxidative stress is associated with other diabetic complications. To determine whether the phenomenon that oxidative stress dysregulates RA homeostasis may also occur in adult tissues, we extended the study to measure RA concentrations in the uterus of diabetic mice and found a significant reduction. We then examine whether alleviation of oxidative stress with Vitamin E could correct RA deficiency in the uterus of diabetic mice. After establishing a causal link between oxidative stress and dysregulation of RA homeostasis in diabetic conditions, we then addressed whether such linkage also occurred in non-diabetic conditions as set up in Objective 1. (Objective 1) We first employed an in vitro approach to induce oxidative stress in the embryo and then examine the effect on RA concentrations. To this end, embryos from normal mice at GD8 were cultured in vitro in serum added with varying concentrations of an oxidative stress inducing agent antimycin A, which inhibits complex III electron transport and thus increases mitochondrial production of free radicals. One day after culture, embryos were collected for measurement of RA concentrations using the RA reporter cell line. After confirming that in vitro induction of oxidative stress in non-diabetic conditions could lead to a reduction in embryonic RA concentrations, we then employed an in vivo approach to induce oxidative stress by intraperitoneal injection of varying dosages of antimycin A to pregnant mice at GD8. Embryos were collected at GD9 for measurement of 8-isoprostane to confirm the induction of oxidative stress in the embryo. Embryos were then subjected to analysis of RA homeostasis in terms of RA synthesis and RA concentrations using the in vitro assay of Raldh activity and the RA reporter cell line. Apoptosis is associated with oxidative stress-induced malformations. Thus, the expression levels of pro-apoptotic genes including Bax was determined by real-time qRT-PCR. The frequencies of resorptions and malformations were recorded. To further investigate if there is a causal link between oxidative stress-induced impairment in embryonic development and RA deficiency, 8 hours following antimycin A treatment, pregnant mice were orally fed an exogenous sub-teratogenic dose (1.25 mg/kg) of RA to raise embryonic RA concentrations so as to determine whether correction of RA deficiency could rescue embryos from malformations. (Objective 2) We have previously identified a paradoxical teratogenic mechanism for RA in which excess RA induces malformations via causing a prolonged suppression of RA synthesis, leading to RA deficiency (PNAS 2012, 109:13668-73). However, the underlying mechanism of how excess RA suppresses RA synthesis remains unclear. We find that following overexposure to RA, there is a significant elevation in oxidative stress. To investigate our hypothesis that such an increase in oxidative stress suppresses RA synthesis and leads to RA deficiency, we tested whether alleviating oxidative stress could restore RA homeostasis and reduce the susceptibility of the mouse embryo to specific malformations induced by overexposure to RA. To this end, starting 2 days before administering a teratogenic dose (100 mg/kg) of RA at GD9, pregnant mice were fed a rodent chow supplemented with Vitamin E and supplementation continued up to GD12. Fetuses were examined for malformations at near-term (GD18). We have previously shown that excess RA induced a spectrum of renal malformations with different degree of severity. Thus, we specifically investigated whether alleviation of oxidative stress could restore RA homeostasis in the embryonic kidney to rescue embryos from RA-induced renal malformations. To examine this, kidney rudiments were collected from embryos at GD12 and then subjected to analysis of RA synthesis and RA concentrations, and the expression levels of some target genes of RA signalling that are crucial for kidney development. Kidneys in near-term fetuses were examined for malformations.

14113314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113314.value: Results are shown in Figures 1-7 in PART C Section 8 No 2. (Objective 3) Maternal supplementation with VitE to alleviate oxidative stress (Fig. 1A) without affecting blood glucose levels (Fig. 1B) could significantly restore RA synthesis (Fig. 1C) and RA concentrations (Fig. 1D) in embryos of diabetic mice and normalize the expressions of pro-apoptotic and developmentally important genes (Fig. 1E). Fetuses of VitE-fed diabetic mice became less susceptible to various types of malformations (Fig. 1G) when challenged with bisdiamine that further lowered embryonic RA concentrations (Fig. 1F). Maternal supplementation of RA to correct RA deficiency (Fig. 2A) without alleviating oxidative stress (Fig. 2B) and blood glucose levels (Fig. 2C) could similarly normalize gene expressions (Fig. 2D) in embryos of diabetic mice and reduced their susceptibility to malformations (Fig. 2E). Notably, we found that alleviation of oxidative stress in diabetic mice (Fig. 3A) could correct RA deficiency in adult tissue such as the uterus (Fig. 3B), which implicates that the causal relationship between oxidative stress and RA deficiency is not limited to embryonic tissues. (Objective 1) Mouse embryos exposed in vitro to the oxidative stress inducer antimycin A developed neural tube defects (Fig. 4A and B), with a concomitant dose-dependent reduction in RA concentrations (Fig. 4C). Results of in vivo induction of oxidative stress with antimycin A (Fig. 5A) further demonstrated a suppression of RA synthesis (Fig. 5B) and lowering of embryonic RA concentrations (Fig. 5C). Resorptions were increased (Fig. 5D) and neural tube defects were induced (Fig. 5E). However, maternal replenishment of RA could significantly prevent oxidative stress-induced resorptions and rescued embryos from developing neural tube defects, and suppressed the upregulation of pro-apoptotic gene (Fig. 5F). Together, these findings support that the link between oxidative stress and RA deficiency also occurs under non-diabetic conditions. (Objective 2) Results showed that pre-treatment of pregnant mice with antioxidant VitE could significantly ameliorate/abolish the teratogenic effects of RA in inducing various types of malformations (Fig. 6). Specifically, pre-treatment with VitE could prevent suppression of RA synthesis (Fig. 7A) and RA deficiency (Fig. 7B) in kidneys of RA-overexposed embryos, and normalized the expression of genes crucial for kidney development (Fig. 7C), leading to prevention of renal malformations (Fig. 7D). These findings support our hypothesis that the paradoxical teratogenic effect of RA in causing RA deficiency is mediated via increases in oxidative stress that suppresses RA synthesis. *A manuscript is under preparation for publication.

14113314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113314.value: Findings of this project have unravelled a mechanistic link between oxidative stress and dysregulation of RA homeostasis in the embryo. This link not only sheds light on an unrecognized mechanism for RA teratogenesis and diabetic embryopathy, but has much wider implications. It is because RA is a key transcriptional regulator, with hundreds of genes important for cell proliferation and differentiation identified to be RA targets. On the other hand, increased oxidative stress, other than being involved in abnormal embryogenesis, plays a pivotal role in the development and progression of diseases such as diabetes mellitus, obesity, endometriosis, alcoholic liver diseases, cancer and neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer’s. Interestingly, disturbance in RA or vitamin A levels is also found to be associated with these diseases. However, whether any mechanistic link exists between oxidative stress and changes in RA homeostasis in these diseases remains largely unexplored. Thus, further study should be conducted to decipher if there is a causal relationship between oxidative stress and RA homeostasis under different pathological conditions, which may bring insights into the pathogenic mechanisms that underlie a wide variety of diseases, thus paving the way for the design of therapeutic strategies for treatment of these diseases.

14113314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113314.value: Oxidative stress is associated with the generation of reactive oxygen species that can serve as signaling factors. However, increased oxidative stress is well-documented to play pathological roles in development of birth defects. On the other hand, retinoic acid (RA), a bioactive vitamin A metabolite, is a master signaling molecule that regulates the transcription of hundreds of genes involved in cell proliferation and differentiation. A tight regulation of RA concentrations is critical for normal development of multiple organ systems during embryogenesis. This project aims to investigate whether there is any causal link between these two important pathways. Indeed, our findings show that oxidative stress suppresses RA synthesis and leads to RA deficiency in mouse embryos, which increases their propensity to a wide variety of malformations. Notably, alleviation of oxidative stress with antioxidants can restore RA synthesis and correct embryonic RA deficiency. Similarly, direct replenishment of RA can abolish the detrimental effect of oxidative stress. The unravel of this previously unrecognized linkage of oxidative stress with dysregulation of RA homeostasis has significant implications in understanding not only their role in abnormal embryo development, but also the pathogenesis and progression of other oxidative stress-associated diseases, bringing new insights to developing therapeutic strategies.

14113414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113414.value: The proposed project aims to investigate the effect of green tea catechin supplements on mammographic breast density and endogenous estrogen concentrations among overweight/obese postmenopausal Chinese women in Hong Kong. Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed female malignancy in Hong Kong. Among postmenopausal women, mammographic density, obesity, estrogen are well-established risk factors of breast cancer. Increased mammographic density is strongly associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. In addition, obese postmenopausal women have high estrogen levels and an increased risk of breast cancer. Researchers are trying to identify safe and effective preventive agents, and there is accumulating data that green tea catechins have anti-carcinogenic properties. In vitro and animal studies suggest that green tea catechins are cytotoxic to breast cancer cells. Although epidemiological studies on green tea and breast cancer have found inconsistent results across different geographical regions, green tea catechins have shown their potential in lowering mammographic density and endogenous estrogen concentrations in cross-sectional studies. These inverse associations are compatible with the biological evidence of antiestrogenic, antiproliferative and antiangiogenic activities of green tea catechins. Therefore, the potential biological mechanisms that green tea catechins can reduce breast cancer risk may be through decreasing mammographic density and estrogen concentrations. Very few clinical trials, however, have examined the effect of green tea catechin supplements on these two breast cancer intermediate markers. We propose to conduct a randomized controlled trial to address directly this important issue among overweight/obese postmenopausal Chinese women in Hong Kong. Local women aged 50-69 years and with body mass index 23.0 kg/m2 or above will be randomly assigned to an intervention group with daily supplementation of 1,000 mg green tea catechins, or a placebo group. Each group will have 142 participants and the intervention period will be one year. Baseline and follow-up blood samples will be collected and mammograms will be performed. The intervention effect will be estimated by calculating the difference of changes in mammographic density, serum estrone and estradiol concentrations from baseline to follow-up between the intervention and placebo groups using intention-to-treat analysis. Given the importance of mammographic density and estrogen in breast cancer development, the findings of this project will provide new insights regarding the role of green tea catechins in breast cancer etiology. The protective effect of green tea catechins against breast cancer through decreasing mammographic density and/or hormone, if well-established among Chinese women, would have important implications for breast cancer prevention. 此項課題旨在研究在絕經后體重過重/肥胖婦女中補充綠茶酚是否會降低其乳腺密度及雌激素水平。 乳癌是香港婦女中發病率最高的一種癌癥。在絕經后婦女中，肥胖、高乳腺密度以及高雌激素水平都是乳癌的重要危險因素。絕經后的肥胖婦女有著較高的雌激素水平，同時也是乳癌的高危人群。近年來，研究者們致力於發現安全有效的預防乳癌的方法，而越來越多的證據顯示綠茶酚具有抗癌的功效。生物實驗包括體外以及動物實驗發現綠茶酚對乳癌細胞具有毒性。儘管在不同地區開展的有關綠茶與乳癌關係的流行病學的研究結果迄今為止並不完全一致，但一些橫斷面研究表明綠茶酚能夠降低乳腺密度及內源性雌激素水平。這與綠茶酚的抗雌激素、抗細胞增生以及抗血管新生的生物學證據是一致的。因此，綠茶酚降低乳癌風險的作用機制可能通過降低乳腺密度及雌激素水平。然而，到目前為止，幾乎沒有臨床試驗專門研究在人群中補充綠茶酚是否會降低乳腺密度及雌激素水平。 因此，我們擬開展一項隨機對照雙盲臨床試驗來研究這一重要課題。研究對象為年齡介于50-69歲的絕經后體重過重/肥胖(身體質量指數在23.0kg/m2或以上)的華裔婦女。此研究將採用隨機分組的方法，將研究對象隨機分為兩組：一組為干預組，另一組為對照組。干預組將每天服用1,000毫克的綠茶酚補充劑。每組人數均為142人，兩組服用及隨訪時間均為一年。所有研究對象都需接受兩次乳房X光造影檢查及採集血樣：在服用補充劑或安慰劑之前有一次基線檢查，在服用補充劑或安慰劑一年之後則有一次終末隨訪檢查，以此觀察綠茶酚補充劑是否會降低乳腺密度及雌激素水平。補充劑的效果將通過計算和比較干預組和對照組平均乳腺密度及雌激素水平的變化而得出。 鑒於乳腺密度和雌激素水平是乳癌的兩個最重要的危險因素，此項研究的結果對目前關於綠茶酚在腫瘤病因學以及腫瘤預防中的作用的討論將會提供新的證據。如果綠茶酚通過降低乳腺密度以及降低雌激素從而降低乳癌風險的保護作用能夠確立，這將為乳癌的預防提供一個安全可行的方法。

14113414.label: Realisation of objectives
14113414.value: To achieve these objectives, we have successfully enrolled and randomized 284 postmenopausal Chinese women. Participants in both groups took six tablets per day. Each green tea catechin tablet contained 167 mg (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), yielding a daily dose of approximately 1,000 mg EGCG for the supplement group. Recently, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS) concluded that intake of green tea extracts at doses equal or above 800 mg EGCG/day for 4 months or longer taken as a food supplement may induce liver injury. Because subjects’ safety is our paramount concern, based on the Panel conclusion, we have suggested the subjects to reduce the dosage to 668 mg EGCG per day (4 tablets, 167 mg EGCG /tablet) and to take the supplements for 3 months. Primary objective Due to several issues that will be explained later, the trial started much later than originally planned and will be stopped earlier. We will still make commitment to provide follow-up mammograms for those subjects who would like to come back. Data will be analyzed for those subjects who had both baseline and follow-up mammograms. The project will provide preliminary results of the effect of 668 mg EGCG supplements per day for three months on mammographic density among postmenopausal Chinese women. Secondary objectives At baseline, lifetime tea consumption was measured. Information sought included the type(s) of tea usually consumed, preparation method, the ages at which they started and stopped drinking green tea regularly, the total number of years they had drunk green tea, frequency of cups consumed, frequency of new batches of tea brewed, and the amount of dried tea leaves consumed per month or per year. Anthropometric measurements were taken following standard procedures. Mammographic density was assessed from unprocessed images and from the craniocaudal views (viewing from above, down) of both breasts. Density measures were assessed by using Volpara, an automated software that has good reliability and high correlation with other validated measures of breast density. The average mammographic measures of both breasts were used, with percent density as the primary outcome. Multivariable generalized linear regression models were used to assess the association between lifetime usual intake of green tea and mammographic density, adjusting for other covariates. Similar analyses were conducted to examine the associations between baseline anthropometric measures, including BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-hip ratio, and breast density. Attempts to overcome problems Conducting an RCT at such a scale (total 284 participants, 142 in each group) is very challenging. We encountered several major difficulties during the project implementation. 1) Limited funding and lack of manpower The awarded grant was about 41% of the proposed budget of $1,843,276 to $759,472. Originally, we asked for one research postgraduate student and one research assistant (RA). With substantially reduced funding, we could not support a PhD student or a full-time RA for three years. The School policy does not allow a PhD student to work on a funded RGC project as thesis research. The PI had to find a large amount of resources from other sources, including her own salary as personal donation, to hire a full-time RA and several part-time RAs and student helpers. 2) Difficulty in finding a pharmaceutical company willing to manufacture the green tea catechin supplements in required dosage and the matching placebos, and the much higher costs of supplement and placebo products than originally budgeted. It took much longer (33 months: 24 months to find the pharmaceutical company, 3 months to obtain the clinical trial certificate exemption, and 6 months to order raw materials and manufacture the products) than originally planned (6 months) to get all the preparations done. We stated in the mid-term progress report that it took 18 months to find a pharmaceutical company. After the report submission, the Garden State Nutritionals (GSN), which initially agreed to make the supplements and placebos, notified us that they were not able to produce the products for us. We had to find another company, and finally found the Hong Kong Institute of Biotechnology Ltd. The costs of supplements and placebos ($233,000) were much higher than originally proposed ($38,406). 3) PI appointment status change and the subsequent inability to apply for project extension. The PI’s Assistant Professor appointment was terminated on 31 January 2018 and was appointed as a Research Fellow with effect from 1 February 2018 for only one year. Due to her appointment status change, she was no longer eligible to be a PI of a RGC project. No other faculty in the School or no other Co-Is were willing or eligible to take up the PI responsibilities to extend and complete the project. The PI continued to carry out the project with no formal project extension and funding, including paying all the project expenses out of her own pocket. To speed up the project progress, we found a private clinic, the iRad Medical Diagnostic Centre, for mammogram screening. The costs in iRad (HK$880/mammogram) were much higher than in PWH (HK$500/mammogram, but only 8 mammograms can be done per week). 4) Availability of new evidence of the adverse effect of green tea catechins on the liver In the original proposal, we proposed 1,000 mg of green tea catechins for the supplement group, considering the evidence at that time (November 2013) of NO significant effect of 400 mg and 800 mg green tea catechin supplements per day on hormone levels in the previous RCT, and the dosage should not exceed 1,200 mg, the maximum tolerable dose. On 14 March 2018, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS) considered that green tea extracts at doses at or above 800 mg EGCG/day for 4 months or longer were associated with elevations of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in a small percentage of the population. The Panel concluded that that doses equal or above 800 mg EGCG/day may induce a statistically significant increase of serum transaminases, indicative of liver injury. Because subjects’ safety is our paramount concern, we have suggested the subjects to reduce the dosage to 668 mg EGCG per day (4 tablets, 167 mg EGCG /tablet) and to take the supplements for 3 months. Considering this most updated evidence and other important issues, including that the PI’s appointment as a Research Fellow will end on 31 January 2019 and no funding to continue the project, particularly to continuously monitor serum transaminases of the study subjects (no such funding even in the original proposal), we decided to stop the trial earlier. We will still make commitment to provide follow-up mammograms for those who would like to come back. We are now applying for the ethics approval for the trial amendments. Prof. Jean Kim, an Associate Professor of the School of and a well-trained epidemiologist with a doctoral degree in Epidemiology from Harvard School of Public Health, will oversee the project after Dr. Su Xuefen would have left CUHK after February 2019. Despite these, the whole team has worked extremely hard on the project. We successfully enrolled 284 postmenopausal women and completed the baseline data collection in 6 months, indicating that the project was well accepted by the community and subjects. Many participants sincerely expressed their appreciation of our work.

14113414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113414.value: The mean age of participating women was 54.7 (standard deviation (SD) = 6.45) years old. Women had a mean height of 157 cm (SD = 0.26), BMI of 27.2 kg/m2 (SD = 1.78), waist circumference of 89.8 cm (SD = 6.06), and waist-to-hip ratio of 0.88 (SD = 0.02). Twenty-two (7.7%) women had at least one first-degree family member who had been diagnosed with breast cancer. Among the total 284 subjects, 86 (30%) had less than one cup of green tea per week, whereas 102 (36%) had one to two cups per week, and 96 (34%) had three or more cups per week. Women who drank three or more cups of green tea per week tended to be younger, taller, have an earlier onset of first menstruation and fewer births, to be less likely to use exogenous menopausal hormone replacement therapy, less likely to drink coffee, but to consume more fruits, vegetables, and isoflavones. Among all subjects, mean breast density was 19.2% (SD = 7.85%). Higher green tea intake levels were associated with lower breast density. Mean percent density was higher in women who had less than one cup of green tea per week (20.6%, 95% confidence interval (CI): 19.7-21.4) than those who had one to two cups per week (19.1%, 95% CI: 17.0-21.2) and those having three or more cups per week (18.0%, 95% CI: 16.6-19.4) (P for trend = 0.045). Among women who were never users of hormone therapy, the inverse association between green tea drinking and percent density remained, but became non-significant (less than one cup of green tea per week: 20.4%, 95% CI: 19.6-21.1; one to two cups per week: 18.9%, 95% CI: 18.3-21.2; and three or more cups per week: 18.4%, 95% CI (18.0-20.2); P for trend = 0.10). BMI (P for trend = 0.054) and waist circumstance (P for trend = 0.06) was marginally associated with mammographic density. A significant positive association was observed between waist-to-hip ratio and percent mammographic density (P for trend = 0.042). Mean percent density was lower in women who had waist-to-hip ratio less than 0.80 (19.0%, 95% CI: 18.6-19.4) than those who had waist-to-hip ratio 0.81-0.90 (19.1%, 95% CI 18.8-20.2), those who had waist-to-hip ratio 0.91-0.99 (19.3%, 95% CI 18.9-21.2), and those having waist-to-hip ratio greater than or equal to 1.0 (19.5%, 95% CI: 19.7-21.4) (P for trend = 0.042).

14113414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113414.value: Recently, green tea extracts at doses equal or above 800 mg EGCG/day for 4 months or longer has been found to induce liver injury. In our meta-analysis, we found that higher intake of green tea may potentially reduce breast cancer risk. The harmful effect of green tea extracts on the liver may be because catechins in green tea extracts may be more concentrated or differ in composition and pattern of consumption, than catechins from traditional infusions. We will continue reviewing the effect of green tea catechins, both as extracts and in traditional infusions, and the dose-response relationship, on various diseases. We also propose to examine green tea effects on inflammatory markers, endothelial dysfunction, and bone mineral density. It might be better to use green tea infusions in future studies and safer to take the extract below 800 mg EGCG/day for less than 4 months. Green tea may be a marker of an overall healthy dietary pattern. It will be interesting to look at green tea as part of a healthy life style, for example, the interactive effect between nuts, whole grain, and green tea, and green tea as part of a healthy dietary pattern.

14113414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113414.value: This research project aimed to study the effect of green tea supplements on breast density. Postmenopausal Chinese women were recruited and randomly allocated into two groups. Originally, one group took 1,000 mg green tea extracts per day for one year, and the other group took placebos for the same duration. As the most updated evidence suggests that green tea extracts at doses at or above 800 mg EGCG/day for 4 months or longer are potentially harmful to the liver, subjects have been advised to reduce the dosage of the supplements and to take 4 tablets per day for 3 months. With each tablet containing 167 mg mg (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), this yields a total of 668 mg EGCG per day for the supplement group. The baseline data suggest that higher green tea intake levels were associated with lower breast density, thus may reduce breast cancer risk. Higher waist-to-hip ratio was associated with higher breast density, thus may increase breast cancer risk. To our knowledge, this is the first study to report a positive association between waist-to-hip ratio and breast density. Postmenopausal women may drink more green tea and reduce central obesity to reduce their risk of breast cancer.

14113514.label: Realisation of objectives
14113514.value: In the original proposal we proposed to identify the functional lincRNAs in Muscle Stem Cells (MuSCs) through Pax7 mediated gene regulatory networks. Four aims were proposed. We are pleased to report that all aims have now been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. Aim 1: To create a complete catalog of lincRNAs in MuSCs using RNA sequencing In this Aim, we proposed to create a complete catalog of lincRNAs in MuSCs using RNA-sequencing. All the experiments have been successfully completed with satisfying results. Briefly, we first established protocols to obtain a large pure population of SCs for RNA-seq experiments followed by lincRNA identification through bioinformatics analysis. After obtained RNA-seq data, we started the ab initio discovery of lincRNA. As a result, we have found 62,391 and 46,774 expressed transcripts in quiescent satellite cells (QSCs) and activated satellite cells (ASCs), respectively. Among them, ~90% in both QSCs and ASCs has been annotated as known gene (coding and noncoding) transcripts using RefSeq Gene annotation as a reference. After filtering these known transcripts, we obtained 20.1% (12,540) un-annotated novel transcripts in QSCs, while 23.5% (10,977) un-annotated novel transcripts in ASCs. To eliminate the assembly noise and identify true lincRNAs, we used our newly developed software sebnif (Self Estimation Based Novel lincRNA Filter) to remove: i) short transcripts (size < 200 nt); ii) lowly expressed transcripts, and iii) novel transcripts with high protein coding potential evaluated by our newly developed program iSeeRNA. After further filtering out lowly expressed transcripts, we identified 5,464, and 2,548 expressed lincRNAs in QSCs fresh isolated from Pax7-GFP+ mice and ASCs culture in DM after isolated from Pax7-GFP+ mice, respectively. We further studied the gene expression patterns of those lincRNAs and found that most lincRNAs are lowly expressed in MuSCs comparing to protein-coding genes, which is in line with the previous observation in other cell and tissue types. The findings are included in our publication, Yuan et. al. 2018 Bioinformatics. To extend this work, we also created a database, SKmDB to host all next generation sequencing (NGS) sequencing information from skeletal muscle. SKmDB not only includes all NGS datasets available in the human and mouse skeletal muscle tissues and cells, but also provide preliminary data analyses including gene/isoform expression levels, gene co-expression subnetworks, as well as assembly of putative lincRNAs, typical and super enhancers and transcription factor hotspots. Users can efficiently search, browse and visualize the information with the well-designed user interface and server side. SKmDB thus will offer wet lab biologists useful information to study gene regulatory mechanisms in the field of skeletal muscle development and regeneration. Aim 2: To dissect the interactions among the key components in the Pax7 mediated regulatory circuitry In this Aim, we proposed to dissect the interactions among the key components in the Pax7 mediated regulatory circuitry. To this end, we have analyzed Pax7 ChIP-seq data and identified a subset of Pax7 bound lincRNAs, named Pax7 Associated Muscle lincRNAs or Pams, among which we focused on Pam-1. Knockdown of Pax7 in MuSCs decreased its expression while overexpressing Pax7 increased its expression, suggesting it’s a regulatory target of Pax7. Consistently, Pam-1 expression is relatively high in Pax7 Hi vs Pax7 Lo populations if MusCs were sorted out according to various levels of Pax7 expression. All the above results have been included in a manuscript under preparation “ Pam-1 promotes muscle stem cell proliferation through orchestrating super enhancer-promoter interaction”. AIM 3: To develop a computational pipeline for predicting lincRNA functions in MuSCs. For this aim, we have developed a novel computational framework, lncFunNet (lncRNA Functional inference through integrated Network) that integrates ChIP-seq, CLIP-seq and RNA-seq data to predict, prioritize and annotate lncRNA functions. In mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), using lncFunNet we not only recovered most of the functional lncRNAs known to maintain mESC pluripotency but also predicted a plethora of novel functional lncRNAs. Similarly, in mouse myoblast C2C12 cells, applying lncFunNet led to prediction of reservoirs of functional lncRNAs in both proliferating myoblasts (MBs) and differentiating myotubes (MTs). Further analyses demonstrated that these lncRNAs are frequently bound by key transcription factors, interact with miRNAs and constitute key nodes in biological network motifs. Further experimentations validated their dynamic expression profiles and functionality during myoblast differentiation. This work was published on Nucleic Acids Research 2017 and has been well received when presented in various meetings. Moreover, the work was extended to generate a lncFunTK toolkit (Zhout et al. Bioinformatics 2018) that can run either as standard application or webserver for this purpose. The input data of lncFunTK are gene expression profiles of distinct stages/cell types/tissues, genome-wide transcription factor and miRNA binding profiles from RNA-seq, ChIP-seq and AGO2-CLIP-seq, respectively. LncFunTK analysis also requires other supporting datasets, such as reference genome and gene annotation data, which have been provided by the lncFunTK package by default. lncFunTK calculates Functional Information Score (FIS) to quantitatively measure the functional importance of a given lncRNA within a gene regulatory network constructed through integrating various types of sequencing data. Briefly, FIS for each lncRNA is calculated by summarizing interaction strength of its neighboring genes, thus represents the interaction degree of each lncRNA under the gene regulatory network context. As a result, lncFunTK provides three major outputs for the query lncRNAs: (i) a list of query lncRNAs with associated FISs; (ii) the most significant GO terms associated with the lncRNA for its functional annotation; (iii) a visualized gene regulatory network including top 5 predicted functional lncRNAs and their key neighboring genes (e.g. TF and miRNA genes), which serve as a starting point for further experimental validation. We also generate an HTML file including all aforementioned outputs for user to navigate the lncFunTK results. Altogether, lncFunTK not only predicts functional lncRNAs, but also gives insights into how an lncRNA may function in a certain biological system, which is useful for researchers studying lncRNA functional mechanism. This work was published on Bioinformatics 2018. AIM 4: To experimentally validate functional lincRNAs in MuSCs In this aim, we proposed to experimentally validate functional lincRNAs in MuSCs. Among all the expressed lincRNAs in MuSCs, we have functionally tested a few of them including Linc-YY1 and Malat1. The findings have been published on Nature Communications (Zhou et. al. 2015) and Cell Discovery (Chen X. 2017). In addition, we have also tested the function of Pam-1. Specifically, we found that Pam-2 promotes MuSC proliferation as knockdown Pam-1 decreased Pax7+MyoD+ proliferating myoblasts. To tease out the mechanism, we found Pam-1 is located in a super enhancer region, representing a seRNA; Results from 4C-seq and ChIRP-PCR assays showed that it is involved in the looping of the super enhancer with with Tim2, Focad and Vim gene promoters through binding with these target loci. Furthermore, by RNA pull down/Mass Spec assay, we found it binds with Ddx5 gene; knockdown of Ddx5 also decrease MuSC proliferation. Altogether our findings suggest that Pam-1 is a seRNA that functions to promote super enhancer/target loci interactions through binding with Ddx5. These results are included in the manuscript “Pam-1 promotes muscle stem cell proliferation through orchestrating super enhancer-promoter interaction” ready to be submitted now.

14113514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113514.value: Three papers directly from the proposed study have been published. In “LncFunNet: an integrated computational framework for identification of functional long noncoding RNAs in mouse skeletal muscle cells” and “lncFunTK: a toolkit for functional annotation of long noncoding RNAs”. First, we developed a novel computational framework, lncFunNet (lncRNA Functional inference through integrated Network) that integrates ChIP-seq, CLIP-seq and RNA-seq data to predict, prioritize and annotate lncRNA functions. In mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), using lncFunNet we not only recovered most of the functional lncRNAs known to maintain mESC pluripotency but also predicted a plethora of novel functional lncRNAs. Similarly, in mouse myoblast C2C12 cells, applying lncFunNet led to prediction of reservoirs of functional lncRNAs in both proliferating myoblasts (MBs) and differentiating myotubes (MTs). Further analyses demonstrated that these lncRNAs are frequently bound by key transcription factors, interact with miRNAs and constitute key nodes in biological network motifs. Further experimentation validated their dynamic expression profiles and functionality during myoblast differentiation. Collectively, our studies demonstrate the use of lncFunNet and its implementation "lncFunTK" to annotate and identify functional lncRNAs in a given biological system. In “SKmDB: an integrated database of next generation sequencing information in skeletal muscle”, we created a database, SKmDB to host all next generation sequencing (NGS) sequencing information from skeletal muscle. SKmDB not only includes all NGS datasets available in the human and mouse skeletal muscle tissues and cells, but also provide preliminary data analyses including gene/isoform expression levels, gene co-expression sub-networks, as well as assembly of putative lincRNAs, typical and super enhancers and transcription factor hotspots. Users can efficiently search, browse and visualize the information with the well-designed user interface and server side. SKmDB thus will offer wet lab biologists useful information to study gene regulatory mechanisms in the field of skeletal muscle development and regeneration especially for lincRNA functional studies. In total 8 publications have been generated with this funding acknowledged (PartC8); One more is under preparation to be submitted soon. Our findings were highly received when presented in international and local conferences/seminars (PartC9). One Postdoc Fellow, Dr. Karl K. So was trained under the support of this grant. Two PhD students, Drs. Jiajian Zhou and Laura X. Peng, were also trained under the grant (PartC10). Through this work, we have also developed active collaboration with Prof. Zhenguo Wu and Prof. Jiguang Wang at HKUST; Prof. Huatng Wang, Department of Orthopeadics and Traumatology, CUHK. (PartC11).

14113514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113514.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of lncRNAs particularly lincRNAs, but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and sarcopenia. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of lncRNAs in the muscle cells in the context of normal muscle development, acute and chronic injury induced muscle regeneration and muscle aging. We will also continue to examine the interplay between lncRNAs and transcription factors or RNA binding proteins in myogenesis.

14113514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113514.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Long intergenic ncRNAs, LincRNAs, are the largest family of lncRNAs. The functionality and underlying mechanisms of lincRNA in skeletal muscle stem cells are largely unknown. Here in this project we defined the repertoire of lincRNAs and studied their regulation and function in muscle stem cells. In the long run, we hope this will serve as a starting point for the development of new therapeutic approaches for treating muscle related human diseases.

14113714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113714.value: 背景 糖皮質激素誘導的骨質疏鬆症（GIOP）是繼發性骨質疏鬆和相關骨折的最常見原因。目前骨質疏鬆症診斷的金標準是雙能X線骨密度儀（DXA）測量的面積骨密度（aBMD）。然而，aBMD結果對患者未來骨折風險的預測能力較低。高分辨率的外週高分辨率定量計算機斷層掃描（HR-pQCT）可同時進行骨強度，體積骨密度（vBMD）和骨微觀結構的評估。在長期應用糖皮質激素（GC）的系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）患者中，骨皮質vBMD能夠區別出有無骨折的患者。然而，HR-pQCT評估的骨皮質和骨小梁結構以及骨強度參數是否可以被應用於鑑別長期服用GC的患者有無脊椎骨折，及是否可以較DXA提高骨折預測率，目前仍然不確定。 最近的研究發現，磁共振（MR）波譜測定的骨髓脂肪含量與骨折相關，且獨立於aBMD。然而在GIOP患者中，骨髓脂肪含量的改變是否與骨折相關目前尚不知曉。 研究概述 我們推測，由HR-pQCT及MR評估的骨強度，微結構和骨髓脂肪含量比由DXA評估的aBMD在鑑別GIOP患者有無脊椎骨折方面更為敏感。 這是一個橫斷面研究。我們將從7個中心招募1500名長期服用GC的風濕性疾病患者，尋找X光片診斷的脊柱骨折。150例骨折患者及300例無骨折患者將接受DXA評估aBMD，及HR-pQCT評估手腕和脛骨的vBMD，微結構和骨強度。其中150例（50例骨折100例無骨折）患者將接受磁共振波譜檢查評估脊椎骨髓脂肪含量。 本研究的主要目的是明確HR-pQCT評估的外週骨骼結構對於區分GIOP患者脊椎骨折是否較aBMD更為敏感。 本研究次要目標包括：1）明確HR-pQCT評估的骨強度參數是否能夠獨立於aBMD區分GIOP患者有無脊椎骨折；2）明確磁共振波譜評估的腰椎骨髓脂肪含量是否能夠區分GIOP患者有無脊椎骨折。 重要性及價值 與DXA相比，HR-pQCT可能更適合用於GIOP患者骨折風險的評估。本研究的數據將增進骨髓脂肪積聚在GIOP的發病機制上潛在作用的了解。

14113714.label: Realisation of objectives
14113714.value: All objectives were fully achieved and are described below: For objective 1: The captioned study was started on 01-10-2014. Due to difficulty in recruitment, we have applied for extension which was approved. The revised date of completion of recruitment was 31/3/2017. For this cross-sectional case-control study, we recruited and screened 1,300 ambulatory subjects on long-term glucocorticoid therapy aged 18 years and above from the rheumatology clinics of the Prince of Wales Hospital (PWH) and six other regional hospitals in Hong Kong as planned. Following screening of the initial study cohort of 1,300 patients, 170 were found to have vertebral fracture. Of these 170 patients with fracture, thirty-two patients met the exclusion criteria and 28 patients refused to undergo either DXA ± HR-pQCT examination. The final study cohort therefore consisted of two groups: 1) the fracture group comprising the 110 patients with a radiographically apparent vertebral fracture; 2) the non-fracture group comprising 110 patients on long-term glucocorticoid without a vertebral fracture who were age- (±5 years), sex- and disease- matched with the fracture group. Each group underwent subsequent assessment with DXA and HR-pQCT at the PWH. All 220 patients had bone geometry, vBMD and bone microarchitecture at the distal radius and distal tibia of the non-dominant hand and leg measured by HR-pQCT (XtremeCT, Scanco Medical AG, Switzerland); and DXA as planned in objective 1. For objective 2: μFEA were performed on 3D images of the distal radius and tibia using the FE-solver included in the built-in Image Processing Language software. A special peeling algorithm, specifying a minimum cortical thickness of 6 voxels, was used to identify cortical and trabecular bone tissue. μFEA was performed by converting the binary image data to a mesh of isotropic brick elements. For all elements, a Poisson’s ratio of 0.3 and a Young’s modulus of 10 GPa was specified. A uniaxial compression test with a 1,000 N load was performed. Stiffness (kN/mm) was used to estimate apparent bone strength. An estimate of failure load was calculated based on the assumption that bone failure occurs if > 2% of the elements are strained beyond 0.7%. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of total vBMD and structural parameters were compared with AUC of FN aBMD after adjustment for age. For objective 3: 50 patients (25 with and 25 without fracture) were recruited and completed the magnetic resonance (MR) spectroscopy assessment as planned.

14113714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113714.value: Please refer to the submitted manuscript attached to Part C No 8 for the tables and figures. 1. Areal bone mineral density (aBMD) by DXA 46/110 (42%) patients with fracture were classified as osteoporosis according to DXA criteria (Table 1). 2. Volumetric BMD (vBMD), bone microarchitecture and estimated bone strength by HR-pQCT Most densitometric, microsctructural parameters and estimated bone strength were decreased in the fracture group compared to the non-fracture group at both the distal radius and distal tibia (Table S1). At the distal radius, fracture risk significantly increased from 53 to 114% by one SD difference in vBMD, microstructure and strength parameters (Table S2). Similar trends were observed at the tibia, except that the fracture risk was further increased from 31 to 137% by one SD difference in vBMD, microstructure and strength parameters. The highest odds ratio (OR) were observed at the tibia with total vBMD, cortical thickness (Ct Th) (Figure 1) and trabecular separation (Tb Sp) for microstructural parameters, and with failure load for strength parameters (OR 2.08 to 2.37, p≤0.001 for all) (Table 2). Total vBMD and Ct Th remained significantly associated with fracture after adjustment for femoral neck (FN) aBMD, radius aBMD or fracture risk assessment tool (FRAX) FRAX-BMD (Tables 2, and S1). 3. Subgroup analysis Significantly lower vBMD and deterioration of microarchitecture and strength parameters were observed in anti-resorptives treatment naïve patients with fracture at both the radius and the tibia similar to changes seen in the total cohort (Tables 3, S3 and S4). In patients without osteoporosis, radius total vBMD and Ct Th; tibia total vBMD, Ct Th, trabecular number (Tb N), trabecular separation (Tb Sp), stiffness and failure load were associated with fracture. Similarly, in patients below the FRAX intervention threshold, tibia total vBMD, Ct Th, Tb N and Tb Sp were also associated with fracture (Table S5, Fig. 2A). We also tested the magnitude of the associations between bone parameters in patients without fracture compared to those with either one vertebral fracture or multiple vertebral fractures (Fig. 2B). Odds were higher in patients with multiple fractures compared with those with only one fracture for tibia Ct thickness. 4. The single HR-pQCT parameter with the highest performances for fracture discrimination was total vBMD for vertebral fracture (Table 4). 5. MR spectroscopy failed to demonstrate any different of lumbar vertebral bone marrow fat content between patients with (37.7% ±12.5%) and without fracture (37.7% ±11.1%).

14113714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113714.value: Our findings demonstrate a structural basis, distinct from aBMD, which may account for skeletal fragility in GIOP patients. Changes in total vBMD and Ct Th persisted after adjustment for aBMD and FRAX indicating how HR-pQCT provides useful discriminatory information over and above that provided by DXA examination and the widely used clinical risk assessment score. Total vBMD was able to discriminate vertebral fracture in a significant subgroup of patients that would not have qualified as high risk of fracture using standard parameters such as not being osteoporotic on aBMD criteria or having a FRAX score of <10%. In other words, HR-pQCT parameters may help to identify high-risk patients who otherwise would not have been recommended for osteoporotic treatment. Whole bone estimated failure load had a high OR and area under reciever operating curve (AUC) approaching 0.7, suggesting that it might have high predictive value in discriminating GIOP vertebral fracture patients. Recent prospective studies have shown that bone microstructure and estimated strength can predict fracture risk independently of aBMD in postmenopausal women, and improve fracture prediction beyond central DXA and FRAX. Future longitudinal studies would help to confirm whether these parameters could reliably predict incident vertebral fractures in GIOP patients.

14113714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113714.value: Measurement of areal bone mineral density (aBMD) by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) was able to predict fracture risk. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) yields additional information about volumetric BMD (vBMD), microarchitecture, and strength that may increase understanding of fracture susceptibility. The project aimed to ascertain whether vBMD, microarchitecture and estimated bone strength derived from HR-pQCT can discriminate vertebral fractures in glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) patients independent of aBMD. For this cross-sectional case-control study, we recruited 110 patients on long-term glucocorticoids with vertebral fracture determined radiographically, and 110 patients without fracture. They were ambulatory subjects aged 18 years and above from the rheumatology clinics of the Prince of Wales Hospital (PWH) and six other regional hospitals in Hong Kong. We assessed their 1) vBMD /microarchitecture/ bone strength; and 2) aBMD; and 3) FRAX fracture probability. The results showed that GIOP patients with vertebral fracture have a lower vBMD and cortical thinning of both the distal radius and especially the distal tibia compared to GIOP patients without vertebral fracture. These changes, which are independent of aBMD and FRAX, may help to identify GIOP patients who are at high risk of vertebral fracture though currently would have been considered to be of low fracture risk.

14114414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114414.value: Gastric cancer is the second most common fatal malignancy worldwide. The mortality rate remains unchanged over the past 30 years despite the advances in medical treatment and understanding of gastric tumorigenesis. There is a compelling need to explore biomarkers for early cancer detection, prediction of prognosis and effective therapeutic approach. By comprehensive genome and transcriptome profiling, we found frequent upregulation of Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) in gastric cancer cell lines. YAP1 has been identified as a transcription cofactor and a downstream effector of the Hippo signaling pathway that plays a role in cell differentiation, cell transformation and regulation of organ size. The functional role of YAP1 in gastric tumorigenesis is still unclear and in-depth investigation is lacking. Our preliminary data indicated that YAP1 protein expression was upregulated in gastric cancer. Nuclear accumulation of YAP1 was associated with poor disease specific survival. Functional studies by siRNA knockdown and ectopic expression demonstrated that YAP1 associated with a more aggressive phenotype and accelerated cell growth both in vitro and in vivo. The preliminary findings suggested that YAP1 is an oncoprotein in gastric cancer. We have further demonstrated the constitutive activation of RAF/MEK/ERK pathway in YAP1-expressing cells. As a consequence, YAP1 can enhance serum/EGF induced c-Fos expression in gastric cancer cells. In search for the mechanisms leading to YAP1 upregulation, we have demonstrated for the first time that deregulated Hippo pathway contributed to the stabilization and nuclear accumulation of YAP1 protein in gastric cancer. In addition, microRNA15a/16 that have direct binding sites on YAP1 3’UTR also play roles in the translational regulation of YAP1. We have further identified potential downstream effector protein of YAP1 by ChIP-chip assay. Being an adaptor protein with multiple protein-protein interaction domains, YAP1 has been placed in the crossroad of multiple signaling pathways. It might exert oncogenic role via multiple cellular pathways that promotes gastric tumorigenesis. In this proposal, we aim to comprehensively investigate the YAP1-mediated gastric tumorigenesis through 1) delineating the regulation of YAP1 by Hippo signaling pathway and its implication in gastric tumorigenesis; 2) investigating the regulation of YAP1 by microRNAs in gastric cancer; 3) identifying the downstream targets and cellular pathways that YAP1 regulates in gastric cancer. The research finding not only will enhance our understanding on gastric cancer tumorigenesis but also may lead to the development of potential tumor markers and therapeutic targets for this common malignancy. 胃癌是全世界導致死亡率第二位的惡性腫瘤，在大部分國家中五年生存率低於百分之三十。YAP1是一種轉錄輔助因子，我們的早期研究證實YAP1在胃癌中表達上調並且具有癌基因功能。我們的前期實驗發現YAP1在胃癌中高表達，同時YAP1的核積聚為較差預後的標誌。多因素回歸分析證實YAP1在早期胃癌病人可以作為一個獨立的預後指標。基因表達譜分析揭示YAP1可改變MAPK信號通路，抑癌基因MST1過表達可以磷酸化YAP1並增加 YAP1在細胞漿中的積聚，達到抑制 YAP1 癌基因的功能。我們的實驗數據首次証實YAP1可通活激活快速反應基因通路發揮癌基因功能，並揭示該基因的表達具有一定的臨床意義，並可作為治療胃癌的靶基因。YAP1在胃癌中發生過程中的功能仍有待研究。除Hippo通路調控YAP1表達之外，我們發現miRNA可調控YAP1的表達。有研究証實miRNA在癌症發生過程中有癌基因或是抑癌基因的功能，並可能與診斷和預后相關從而具有臨床意義。通過targetscan查找, 我們在YAP1 mRNA的3’非翻譯區（3’UTR）發現兩個結合位點，可通過完全或部分互補的方式結合而引起YAP1 mRNA的降解和蛋白翻譯的抑制，從而調控YAP1蛋白的表達。文獻報道miR-15b/16在卵巢癌及非小細胞性肺癌中可靶向下調癌基因Bmi-1及cyclin D1並影響細胞增殖周期，但其在胃癌中臨床意義及生物學功能方面未進行深入探討。另外利用ChIP-chip我們進一步發現了YAP1下游的相關效應基因。 YAP1是一種轉錄輔助因子，含有多個蛋白質相互作用結合位點，參與多個信號通路，通過影響多個細胞信號通路以促進胃癌發生，本課題擬在前期研究基礎上進一步深化研究YAP1 在胃癌發生過程中的功能。

14114414.label: Realisation of objectives
14114414.value: During this period, we are making progress in elucidating YAP1 oncogenic properties and in-depth characterization of the downstream pathways of YAP1 in gastric cancer (GC). Our hypothesis that upregulation of YAP1 leads to dysregulation of multiple cellular pathways that promotes gastric tumorigenesis through positively regulating downstream genes with oncogenic function has been proved. Moreover, mechanisms responsible for YAP1 protein upregulation have been detailedly explored, such as dysregulated Hippo signaling pathway, together with its post-transcriptional regulation by microRNAs (miRNAs). The finding has led to the identification of useful tumor markers for GC and specific intervention strategies based on the recognized regulatory pathways, which will be illustrated in the following sections: In the first part, we delineated the dysregulated Hippo signaling pathway in gastric cancer (Kang W et al, World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2016; Kang W et al, Journal of Thoracic Disease, 2017). Hippo is the most important regulator of YAP1, where YAP1 localizes in the central position, conveying the effective signals to the downstream and controlling the cellular proliferative mechanism (Zhao B et al, Genes & Development, 2007). However, ineffective Hippo cascade contributes to over-proliferation of cells, which dramatically enlarges the size of tissues or organs, resulting in tumorigenesis (Zhao B et al, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2011). We have reported previously that the disrupted upstream of Hippo pathway, MST1/2 and the functional cleaved-MST1/2 showed decreased level in tumor compared with normal adjacent non-tumorous tissue (Kang W et al, Clinical Cancer Research, 2011). To get a full image of Hippo pathway in gastric carcinogenesis, we examined the expression of MST1/2 and LATS1/2 together with their inhibitory effect on YAP1 through phosphorylation in gastric carcinogenesis. Recently, aiming at the same pathway, we also summarized the oncogenic function of TEAD family in different types of tumors (Zhou Y et al, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2016). In most of the cases, TEAD family is a group of transcriptional factors that helps YAP1 exerts carcinogenetic role when Hippo is invalid. Theoretically, the DNA-binding ability of TEADs is a supplement for YAP1. Given that YAP1 lacks the DNA binding domain, after its nuclear translocation, it needs TEADs to promote the expression of the downstream targets. Therefore, we further performed a deep investigation on TEAD family, another key component of Hippo and revealed its regulation by several novel tumor-suppressive microRNAs, named miR-377-3p, miR-1343-3p, and miR-4269 (Zhou Y et al, Oncogene, 2017). This study confirmed the necessity of YAP1-TEADs complex for growth promoting the activity of YAP1, which brought up an ideal for therapeutic strategy. Verteporfin (VP, trade name Visudyne by Novartis) has been introduced to inhibit YAP1–TEAD interactions (Liu-Chittenden Y et al, Genes & Development, 2012), thus we combined VP with multiple chemotherapy drugs to treat GC cells. Consequently, the oncogenic character of GC cells was significantly weakened in combination treatment (Kang W, et al, Cell Death and Disease, 2017). In the second part, we investigated the regulatory mechanisms of YAP1 expression. Apart from genetic and epigenetic regulation, post-transcriptional modulation is another significant factor, such as miRNAs. They are a class of small non-coding RNAs which have been identified as new regulators of gene expression through binding to the 3’ untranslated regions (UTRs) of the target mRNA. This results in mRNA degradation or mRNA translational inhibition. Emerging evidence shows that miRNAs are abnormally expressed in various cancers, and the deregulated miRNA expressions are associated with tumor initiation, promotion and progression. In our studies, we provided the first evidence that YAP1 is negatively regulated by tumor-suppressive miRNA miR-15a and miR-16-1 (Kang W et al, Molecular Cancer, 2015). In addition, we found YAP1 is also negatively regulated by aberrantly expressed miR-375 in gastric cancer (Kang W et al, Cell Death and Disease, 2017). In the third part, we have focused on the identification of functional downstream targets of YAP1 in gastric cancer. By ChIP-Chip combined with the available database, we confirmed that CTGF is a key downstream target of YAP1 in gastric cancer. The upregulation of CTGF correlates with poor survival, which is also supported by TCGA database. In addition, CTGF is also a target of miR-375, thus miR-375 is a master controller of Hippo-YAP1-CTGF signaling in gastric cancer (Kang W et al, Cell Death and Disease, 2017). Besides the three main aims of the project, we also comprehensively investigated the miRNA deregulation network in gastric carcinogenesis, such as the downregulation of miR-508-3p (Huang T et al, Molecular Cancer, 2016). In addition to Hippo pathway, other signaling cascades involved in gastric tumorigenesis such as Slit-Robo pathway were also summarized and investigated (Huang T et al, BMC Cancer, 2015; Huang T et al, Oncogene, 2017). All the findings will not only enrich our understanding about the Hippo-YAP1-CTGF signaling pathway and miRNA deregulation contributing to tumorigenesis by targeting Hippo effectors, but also provide clinical translational potential in gastric cancer.

14114414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14114414.value: Our research focus mainly lies in Hippo pathway in gastric carcinogenesis. Increasing evidence has underscored the importance of this cascade in gastrointestinal tissue homeostasis, whereas its deregulation induces tumorigenesis. YAP1 and its close paralog TAZ, transcriptional co-activator with a PDZ-binding motif, function as key effectors negatively controlled by the Hippo pathway. In various cancers, Hippo pathway crosstalks with pro- or anti-tumorigenic pathways such as GPCR, Wnt/β-catenin, Notch and TGF-β signaling and is deregulated by multiple factors including cell density/junction and microRNAs. Under these circumstances, we have firstly summarized the recent research progresses on the deregulation of Hippo pathway in the gastrointestinal tract (Kang W et al, World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2016; Kang W et al, Journal of Thoracic Disease, 2017). As YAP1 expression is significantly associated with poor prognosis of gastric and other gastrointestinal cancers, detailed delineation of Hippo regulation in tumorigenesis remains elusive. Thus, we investigated the possible regulatory mechanisms regarding YAP1 expression, especially from the post-transcriptional level (Kang W et al, Molecular Cancer, 2015). Moreover, the core members of Hippo, YAP1 and TAZ, exert oncogenic activities by transcriptional regulation via physical interaction with TEAD transcription factors. TEAD proteins are required for the participation of coactivators to transmit the signal of pathways for the downstream signaling processes. They also play an important role in tumor initiation and facilitate cancer progression via activating a series of progression-inducing genes, such as CTGF, Cyr61, Myc and Gli2. We, therefore, summarize the functional role of TEAD proteins in tumorigenesis and discuss the key role of TEAD transcription factors in the linking of signal cascade transductions (Zhou Y et al, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2016). After that, further investigation was continued, including the function of TEADs and their regulatory mechanism behind (Zhou Y et al, Oncogene, 2017). Aiming at the whole YAP1-TEADs-CTGF axis, we also identified a master controller that simultaneously targeted and downregulated these three genes, miR-375 (Kang W et al, Cell Death and Disease, 2017). Apart from Hippo pathway, we have comprehensively proved the vital functions of NF-κB and Slit-Robo pathways and their regulation by miRNAs in gastric carcinogenesis (Huang T et al, Molecular Cancer, 2016; Huang T et al, BMC Cancer, 2015; Huang T et al, Oncogene, 2017).

14114414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14114414.value: We have delineated the roles of the key components of Hippo pathway in GC, as well as their regulation by miRNAs. Our findings not only enhance our understanding of the Hippo pathway and deregulated miRNA network in GC development, but also lead to the identification of several useful biomarkers for predicting GC prognosis. And it is quite urgent for us to develop some anti-cancer strategies based on our findings. Therefore, achieving the clinical translational potentials may be our targets in the following research steps. Drugs (Verteporfin) and miRNA mimics (miR-375) will be applied to treat GC in xenograft models, respectively or with combinational usage. Related clinical trials by targeting YAP1/TAZ/TEADs would be the further step. Meanwhile, we are planning to keep revealing other functional roles of Hippo, such as its immunity relevance. Instead of forming into a malignancy by a singular cancer cell itself, it is known that tumorigenesis is always along with an aberrant immune microenvironment, and there will be a vicious circle between them. Increasing knowledge and a more comprehensive picture regarding Hippo’s role in carcinogenesis will elevate our academic research to a higher level.

14114414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14114414.value: Gastric cancer (GC) is the second most common fatal malignancy worldwide. It accounts for 3% to 10% of all cancer-related deaths and is particularly prevalent in China including Hong Kong. The mortality rate remains relatively unchanged over the past 30 years with overall 5-years survival rate is only 10-20%. Numerous academic reports have indicated that abnormal cellular signal transduction leads to carcinogenesis, and Hippo pathway is one of the dysfunctional signaling pathways in gastric tumorigenesis. The research focus of our group mainly lies in Hippo-related molecular mechanism during gastric tumorigenesis, especially the central effector of this pathway, YAP1. In our studies, we have demonstrated that both YAP1 and its essential binding partners, TEADs, function as oncogenes and serve as potential biomarkers for GC diagnosis and prognostic prediction. Their interaction drives gastric initiation and progression, which reveals that interrupting the integrity of YAP1-TEAD complex may serve as an anti-cancer strategy, allowing us to delay or even stop cancer growth. Moreover, our results regarding regulation of YAP1 and TEADs by miRNAs not only enrich the miRNA network in GC, but also give us a hint that miRNAs or their mimics could be employed as medication strategy.
