14115414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115414.value: The uncoupling of bone formation and resorption lies at the root of metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis. Insufficiency in nutrient and oxygen availability, oxidative stress, and autophagy failure are fundamental factors for the decline of bone mass and strength with aging. Accumulating evidences indicate that the above factors affect normal autophagic and lysosomal activities which are the major forces in clearance of aggregated or damaged proteins. Genetic and functional data indicate that enzymes or factors involved in autophagic and/or lysosomal protein degradation function as essential mediators of bone cell function in skeletal physiology and pathology. Lysosomal enzyme cathepsin D (CD), the principal lysosomal aspartate protease, functions in the normal activity of autophagosome and lysosome. It has been shown that CD exists in bone tissues during development and injury. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms of CD mediated autophagosome and lysosome function in bone cells remain unclear. Our recent data shows that mice with CD gene homozygous deletion have severe bone loss accompanied with neurodegenerative disorders. The bone loss phenotype in the mutant mice is characterized by decreased osteoblast numbers, impaired osteoblastic function and increased osteoclastogenesis. Inactivation of CD in osteoblasts alters autophagic gene profiles and affects autophagosome formation. Based on the above findings and our preliminary data, we hypothesize that CD functions as an important mediator of autophagosome for the regulation of coupling of bone formation and resorption. The research plan includes three specific aims. In Aim 1, we will use tissue specific mutagenesis mouse models to determine the role of CD in bone metabolism. Aim 2 is to define the molecular mechanisms that involves in autophagosome formation mediated by CD in osteoblasts and osteoclasts. And in Aim 3, we will explore the potential involvement of CD in postmenopausal osteoporosis using the ovariectomy mouse model. We expect that the proposed project will facilitate the discovery of novel therapeutic target for the patients with metabolic bone diseases.

14115414.label: Realisation of objectives
14115414.value: For Objective 1: Immunohistochemistry staining showed that CD (here use CtsD) was localized in osteoblasts, osteoclasts and macrophages in the skeletal tissues (Fig.1 in the enclosed manuscript). We generated homozygous CtsD knockout mice through cross breeding of the heterozygous strains. The wild type control, heterozygous and mutant littermates were used for the experiments. To determine the effects of CtsD inactivation on bone formation in vivo, X-ray, microCT, histology, histochemistry and bone histomorphometry analysis were performed to examine the skeletal phenotypes during bone growth. Mice with inactivation of CtsD showed growth retardation with decreased body size and body weight. The mutant mice will die at day 26 because of phenotypes in the central nervous system or immune system. The bone mass of the CtsD mutant mice was significantly decreased as indicated by decreased bone volume, bone volume/tissue volume, trabecular thickness and number. Bone histomorphometry and imaging analysis showed that inactivation of CtsD caused decreases osteoblast number, osteoblast surface, and osteoid surface, indicating the impairment of osteoblast numbers and functions (Fig.2 and Fig.3). Inactivation of CtsD decreases mineralization and osteoblast differentiation as indicated by von Kossa staining and in situ hybridization for mature osteoblastic marker osteocalcin (Fig.4). To more accurately examine the effect of CtsD on bone acquisition in mice in vivo, we created genetic mouse with conditional deletion of CtsD in osteoblasts using the Cre-Loxp strategy. Micro-CT analysis of tibia showed a decrease in bone mass of the mutant mice compared with control littermates at 3-week and 12-week of age (Fig.8). To further investigate the effect of CtsD on bone formation in vivo, we created another mouse strain with overexpression of CtsD in osteoblasts. Micro-CT analysis of distal femur showed a decreased in bone mass of the OB-CtsD mutant mice compared with control littermates at 4-week and 8-week of age (Fig. 9). To determine the role of CtsD in osteoclasts, we generated mouse lacking CtsD in osteoclasts. A decrease in bone mass was observed in the mutant mice compared with control littermates at 3-week and 12-week of age (Fig.10) For Objective 2: Primary osteoblasts were isolated from calvaria and cultured under defined osteogenic conditions. CtsD knockdown was performed using siRNA approach, with mock vectors as controls. Osteoblasts with CtsD knockdown had reduced differentiation potential indicated by reduction in the expression of osteogenic marker genes Runx2, ALP and Col1 mRNA and decreased ALP activity (Fig.5). To further define the underling mechanisms, supper array gene profiling for autophagy related genes was performed in MC3T3E1 osteoblastic cells with siRNA mediated knockdown of CtsD. The altered autophagy gene profiles were observed in osteoblasts with CtsD inactivation (Fig.6). Confocal immunofluorescence and Western blot showed that inactivation of CtsD downregulated LC3B levels in osteoblasts, this was accompanied by decreased P62, p-Akt and p-GSK3beta levels and increased ubiquitin level in osteoblasts, indicating an alteration in the formation of autophagosome (Fig.7). To unravel the molecular mechanisms on how CtsD knockdown affects autophagy signaling in osteoclast precursor cell line RAW264.7 cells, PCR array analysis was performed to compare the mRNA expression of 83 genes, including autophagy machinery components and their associated co-regulators, interactors and responsive genes before and after siRNA mediated CtsD knockdown. There is an apparent upregulation of Tgm2 (transglutaminase 2, 1.7-fold), Arkt1 (thymoma viral proto-oncogene 1, 1.6-fold) and Wipi1 (WD repeat domain phosphoinositide interacting 1, 1.5-fold) following CtsD knockdown. On the contrary, Cxcr4 (chemokine CXC motif receptor 4, 3.2-fold), Igf1 (insulin like growth factor 1, 2.5-fold) and Esr1 (estrogen receptor 1, 2.1-fold) was downregulated in response to CtsD suppression (Fig.13). The results confirmed that CtsD altered the expression profiles of autophagy signaling pathway in osteoclast precursor cells. We mainly focused on the gene profiles but not proteomics because of some technical issue that remained to be addressed during performing the proteomics analysis. CtsD knockdown in these cells decreases LC3BII level and upregulates P62 level (Fig.14). The results suggest distinct mode of actions of CtsD mediates the autophagy pathways in osteoblasts and osteoclasts respectively. For Objective 3: The wild type female mice were subjected to ovariectomy (OVX) induced osteoporosis model to mimic the postmenopausal states. Note that there was a significant decrease of bone mass in the OVX group compared with the control group. CtsD mRNA level was reduced in the OVX group compared with the controls. This was accompanied by decreased osteoblast markers osterix, OPN, OCN and OPG. We examined the effect of selected small molecule candidates on regulation of CtsD gene promoter activity. The proximal promoter region of CtsD was subcloned into pGL3 vector to form a CtsD luciferase reporter construct (pCtsD-Luc). MC3T3E1 were transfected with pCtsD-Luc before treated with different doses of tetramethylpyrazine (TMP), baicalein and -estradiol for 24h. TMP significantly enhances the transactivation of CtsD promoter, whereas baicalein and -estradiol increased the CtsD promoter activity at higher doses. Based on this, TMP was selected for further testing how it regulates the expression of CtsD. To further determine the effect of TMP in bone formation in vivo, selected dose of TMP were intraperitoneally injected into the OVX mice. Compared with none-TMP treatment OVX group, TMP treatment remarkably reduced the extent of microstructure destruction in trabecular bone. There was a significant increase in BV/TV and Tb.N and decrease in Tb.Sp in TMP treated OVX group. The serum OCN level in the OVX mice was dramatically while procollagen I level was increased, but these phenotypes were attenuated in the mice treated with TMP (Fig.15). Results from real-time PCR indicated that TMP injection for 2 months could restore OVX-induced downregulation of osteogenic marker genes expression (Fig 16). TMP promoted bone formation in the OVX induced osteoporosis mouse model. This phenomenon was accompanied by increased CtsD and P62 expression in the bone tissue of the OVX groups (Fig 17). The results indicate that TMP enhances bone formation in the mouse OVX-induced osteoporosis model in association with activation of CtsD mediated autophagy pathway. Based on these data, a manuscript was enclosed in the report.

14115414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115414.value: Cathepsin D (CtsD), the principal lysosomal aspartate protease and a main endopeptidase, functions in the normal activity of autophagysome and lysosome. It is shown that CtsD exists in the bone tissue during development and injury. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms of CtsD mediated autophagosome or lysosome function in the skeleton remain unclear. Here, we show that inactivation of CtsD globally causes severe bone loss in the CtsD global knockout mice compared with control littermates. The phenotype is characterized by decreased osteoblast numbers, impaired osteoblastic function, increased osteoclast numbers and enhanced osteoclastic bone resorption. To more accurately determine the role of CtsD on bone acquisition, we generated mouse strains with conditional deletion of CtsD in osteoblasts or osteoclasts using the Cre-Loxp strategy. Mice lacking CtsD in osteoblasts showed a decrease in bone mass compared with control littermates at 3-week and 12-week of age. A decrease in bone mass was also observed in mice lacking CtsD in osteoclasts compared with control littermates at 3-week and 12-week of age. Insterestingly, mouse with overexpression of CtsD in osteoblasts showed a decrease in bone mass compared with control littermates at 4-week and 8-week of age. At molecular level, inactivation of CtsD in osteoblasts downregulated LC3B expression, this was accompanied by decreased P62, p-Akt and p-GSK3beta levels and increased ubiquitin level in osteoblasts. Inactivation of CtsD in osteoclast precursor cell line RAW264.7 cells showed decreased LC3BII and upregulated P62 levels. PCR array analysis revealed distinct pattern of expression profiles associated with autophagy in osteoblasts and osteoclasts. This indicates that the alteration of autophagosome pathway was differentially regulated in the two cell types. Small molecule screening indicated that TMP may serves as an activator for CtsD. TMP increased bone mass in the OVX mouse model. The results suggest that CtsD mediated autophagy pathway plays distinct actions in regulating bone metabolism, targeting CtsD may serve as a potential therapeutic approach for metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis. Based on this project, 2 invited speeches, 1 international conference and 2 regional conferences oral or poster presentations were given by the PI and team members. Collaboration work associated with this project was published in Molecules 2016, 21: 1192. A PhD student was trained when performing the project. And another manuscript was prepared for publication. The detailed information on the meetings, abstracts, publication and manuscript are enclosed in Part C of the report.

14115414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115414.value: Our data suggest that CtsD functions as an important mediator to regulate bone metabolism through distinct mode of actions on autophagy as well as osteoblast and osteoclast functions. The study provides novel insights into the understanding of the regulation of CtsD and autophagy pathway in osteoblastic bone formation and osteoclastic bone resorption. Small molecule CtsD activator was shown to exert beneficial effect on promoting bone formation in OVX induced osteoporosis mouse model. This may facilitate discovery of novel therapies for patients with metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis. We propose to continue determine the pharmacological efficacy and mechanisms of the candidate molecule in the future work and aim to an output with knowledge transfer to benefit patients with metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis.

14116014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116014.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Defects in lncRNAs could lead to the development of many human diseases while the underlying mechanisms are largely unknown. Thus, lncRNAs are considered as the new frontier of biomedical research. Malat1 (metastasis associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript) is an lncRNA initially discovered to be associated with lung cancer. Here in this study we will look into its role in skeletal muscle stem cells and muscle regeneration. Our preliminary study showed that Malat1 inhibits muscle regeneration by blocking the early differentiation of muscle stem cells (satellite cells). Further elucidation at the molecular level revealed that Malat1 inhibits MyoD transcriptional activities through recruiting Suv39h1, a histone H3 lysine 9 (H3-K9) methyltransferase to the MyoD bound loci. Lastly, we found Malat1 is targeted by miR-181 through Ago2-mediated machinery in the myoblast nucleus. Therefore, we hypothesize that miR-181 targeted Malat1 modulates satellite cell functions and muscle regeneration through regulating MyoD transcriptional activity. Three specific aims were designed to test our hypothesis. 1) To determine the anti-myogenic function of Malat1 in muscle stem cells and muscle regeneration. 2) To elucidate the molecular mechanism of how Malat1 inhibits MyoD trans-activation through recruiting Suv39h. 3) To study the regulation of Malat1 by miR-181/Ago2 in the nucleus. Our findings will provide a comprehensive understanding of Malat1 function in injury induced muscle regeneration, which will serve as the starting point for developing novel therapeutic targets toward age-related, metabolic and genetic disruptions of muscle function. 哺乳动物基因组中只有大约3%的碱基是用于编码蛋白质基因，而剩余的很大一部分基因组曾被认为是无用的“垃圾”DNA。但是近年来对基因组的高通量分析发现这些“垃圾”区域能够转录生成许多不同种类的非编码RNA（ncRNAs）。其中长度大于200个碱基的长链非编码RNA（lncRNA）正成为一类重要的基因表达调控因子。lncRNA的缺失会造成许多疾病的发生，但是其潜在的分子机理却并不明确。因此，关于lncRNA的研究成为生物医学研究新的前沿领域。Malat1（metastasis associated lung adenocarcinoma transcript）是一个首先在非小细胞肺癌中发现的lncRNA。在本研究中我们探讨了Malat1在骨骼肌干细胞和肌肉再生过程中的功能。我们的初步研究结果显示Malat1能通过阻碍肌肉干细胞（卫星细胞）的早期分化而抑制肌肉再生。分子水平的研究结果显示Malat1能招募组蛋白H3上9位赖氨酸三甲基化酶Suv39h1至MyoD在基因组上的结合位点并抑制MyoD的转录激活活性。因此，我们猜测Malat1是通过调节MyoD的转录激活活性来调控卫星细胞的功能和肌肉再生过程。在该项研究中我们旨在明确以下两个问题1）确定Malat1在肌肉干细胞和肌肉再生过程中的分化抑制功能。2）阐述Malat1通过招募Suv39h1来抑制MyoD的转录激活活性的分子机理。我们的研究将帮助详细了解Malat1在创伤引起的肌肉再生中的功能。而这些研究结果将会为研发针对年龄、代谢以及遗传因素引起的肌肉功能失调的新的治疗靶点提供有用的信息。

14116014.label: Realisation of objectives
14116014.value: Aim 1: To determine the anti-myogenic function of Malat1 in muscle cells and regeneration. We assessed expression of Malat1 in various myogenesis settings. First, during differentiation of both C2C12 and sorted satellite cells, significant decreased expression of Malat1 was detected in early differentiating myoblasts. To further examine its expression dynamics in vivo, we employed the cardiotoxin (CTX) induced muscle injury-regeneration model and the expression of Malat1 was found to be rapidly induced and peaked at day 1 and dramatically decreased at day 3 when myoblasts started to differentiate. The above results suggested that Malat1 is associated with active myogenesis and differentiation. To elucidate the function of Malat1 during myogenesis and differentiation, first we used siRNA/shRNA to knock down Malat1 in C2C12 cells and observed significantly enhanced C2C12 differentiation as assessed by the examination of several myogenic markers (Myogenin, MyHC, α-Actin and Troponin) at both protein and RNA levels during a differentiation course of 5 days. Conversely, increase of Malat1 level by directly transfecting in vitro transcribed Malat1 transcripts suppressed the C2C12 differentiation. To further decipher the function of Malat1 in vivo, we imported Malat1 knock-out mice from our collaborator. When analyzing the CTX-induced muscle regeneration process, a subtle but notable acceleration was observed in the KO mice compared to WT littermates by H&E staining of the muscle sections at day 7 post injury. In the following immunostaining of the above sections, the increased number of cells positively stained for Myogenin and eMyHC also indicated enhanced muscle regeneration in Malat1 KO mice compared with WT mice. To further validate our findings, we also examined the effect of Malat1 depletion in the dystrophic muscle. As expected, enhanced muscle regeneration was observed in the mdx/Malat1-KO mice compared with littermate mdx/Malat1-WT mice. Aim 2: To elucidate molecular mechanism of how Malat1 inhibits myogenic differentiation. To gain insights into molecular mechanisms of how Malat1 regulates the myogenic differentiation, we conducted a RNA-seq analysis in C2C12 cells transfected with siMalat1 or siNC oligos. We found that many of the up-regulated genes were muscle genes known to be regulated by the muscle master transcription factor, MyoD, leading us to suspect that Malat1 function may be associated with MyoD regulation. Indeed, by exploring MyoD ChIP-Seq data from C2C12 cells, we found that almost 30% of these up-regulated genes contained MyoD binding at their promoters. To investigate how Malat1 inhibits the trans-activation ability of MyoD, we thought of the possibility that Malat1 might interact with Suv39h1 and recruit it to MyoD. To test this notion, we need firstly exclude the possibility that Malat1 modulates Suv39h1 activity through regulating its expression. Indeed, the levels of Suv39h1 and its partners in the repressive complex, HP1β, and HDAC1, were not affected by shMalat1 treatment in C2C12 myoblasts. Next using cross-linked RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) assay, antibodies against Suv39h1 protein retrieved a significant amount of endogenous Malat1 transcripts from C2C12 myoblasts. To strengthen this finding, we then further performed RNA pull-down assay from native non-crosslinked cell lysates using biotinylated in vitro transcribed full length Malat1 transcripts. Consistently, Malat1 transcripts pulled down a substantial amount of endogenous Suv39h1 protein; however, no HP1β, HDAC1, MyoD or YY1 protein was retrieved, suggesting a direct physical interaction between Suv39h1 and Malat1. To further confirm the direct binding between Malat1 and Suv39h1, we performed in vitro RNA-protein EMSA (electrophoretic mobility shift assay). A gradual shift of Malat1 FL RNAs was observed as the concentration of GST-Suv39h1 increases; 1600 nM yielded the most evident shift; GST protein alone or a GST-MyoD protein did not cause the shift. The above results confirmed the physical association between Malat1 FL and Suv39h1. Next to answer the question whether Malat1 is tethered to the MyoD binding DNA loci, Chromatin Isolation by RNA Purification (ChIRP) assay with both odd and even tiling oligos against Malat1 was performed. We were able to specifically retrieve substantial amount of endogenous Malat1 transcripts from the promoter regions of MyoD/Suv39h1 target genes including Myogenin, Tnni2, MyHC, and Ccnd3. Next, we performed ChIP-PCR assays to show that knock-down of Malat1 significantly impaired the binding of endogenous Suv39h1 protein to the MyoD binding loci. Suv39h1 is a methyltransferase which induces trimethylation of histone 3 lysine 9 (H3K9me3) at target sites. Expectedly, H3K9me3 levels at all the above target loci were significantly reduced upon Malat1 knock-down. Altogether the above results supported that Malat1 played a critical role in regulating MyoD trans-activation by recruiting Suv39h1 to the target loci. Aim 3: To study the regulation of Malat1 by miR-181/Ago2 in the nucleus. The interesting down-regulation of Malat1 at the very early stage of myogenic differentiation suggested to us its expression must be tightly regulated. Exploration of the Ago2 CLiP-seq in mouse ESCs revealed a potential association of Ago2 protein with Malat1 transcript, suggesting it could be bound and regulated by miRNA/Ago2 silencing machinery. We thus looked for miRNAs that could potentially target Malat1 upon differentiation; this led to the discovery of a sequence complementarity between Malat1 and 82 miRNAs including miR-181a which happens to be a well-known regulator of skeletal myogenesis. Indeed, by cloning the identified Malat1 binding region into a luciferase reporter, we found that precursor oligos of miR-181a (pre-181a) but not a negative control (pre-NC) or an irrelevant miR-193a, down-regulated the reporter activity. In line with the finding, over-expression of miR-181a led to a significant down-regulation of the endogenous Malat1 in differentiating C2C12 cells while depletion of miR-181a increased the expression of Malat1. To further validate whether this miR-181a /Malat1 regulation could occur in the nucleus. We firstly detected a substantial amount of miR-181a in the nuclear portion. Consistently, we also detected a high amount of Ago2 protein in C2C12 nuclei, indicating the miRNA/Ago2 machinery could possibly function in the nucleus of myoblast cells. To further demonstrate the involvement of Ago2 in this regulation, we showed that biotinylated full length Malat1 transcripts could pull down an evident amount of Ago2 protein from nuclear lysates of early differentiating C2C12 myoblasts; and antibodies against Ago2 also retrieved a significant level of endogenous Malat1 transcripts from nuclear lysates. To further explore how miR-181/Ago2 down-regulates Malat1 transcripts, we first tested whether they could suppress Malat1 transcription as increasing lines of evidence showed the non-canonical functions of nuclear miRNA/Ago in recruiting epigenetic silencing complex which triggered transcriptional silencing. However, by nuclear run-on assay, we did not detect a decrease of nascent Malat1 transcription by miR-181 overexpression, suggesting the regulation may not be at the transcriptional level; instead, miR-181/Ago2 may cause Malat1 degradation through a nuclear RNA induced silencing complex (nRISC) machinery. To test this notion, we found that besides Ago2, multiple components of RISC including Dicer, Trbp which were required for the recruitment of Ago2 to Dicer, and Tnrc6a/GW182 which navigated Ago2 to translocate into the nucleus were all detected in the nuclear portion of C2C12 cells. By RIP and RNA-pull down assays an association of these proteins with Malat1 transcripts was also detected in the C2C12 nuclear lysates. Lastly, to confirm the functionality of the miR-181/Malat1 regulation, we further demonstrated that knock-down of Malat1 could revert the anti-myogenic effect of anti-miR-181a treatment on myogenesis. Altogether the above data suggested that Malat1 was reduced by miR-181a/Ago2 degradation through nRISC dependent machinery in the nucleus of myoblast.

14116014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116014.value: A paper including all the findings “Malat1 interacts with Suv39h1 to regulate MyoD transcriptional activity and is down-regulated by miR-181 binding during myogenic differentiation and skeletal muscle regeneration” is published on Cell Discovery in 2017 (PartC8) and has been cited 14 times since publication. In this paper we characterized the function of Malat1 in skeletal muscle cells and muscle regeneration. Utilizing both in vitro and in vivo assays, we demonstrate that Malat1 has a role in regulating gene expression during myogenic differentiation of myoblast cells. Specifically, we found that knockdown of Malat1 accelerates the myogenic differentiation in cultured cells. Consistently, Malat1 knockout mice display enhanced muscle regeneration after injury and deletion of Malat1 in dystrophic mdx mice also improves the muscle regeneration. Mechanistically, in the proliferating myoblasts, Malat1 recruits Suv39h1 to MyoD-binding loci, causing trimethylation of histone 3 lysine 9 (H3K9me3), which suppresses the target gene expression. Upon differentiation, the pro-myogenic miR-181a is increased and targets the nuclear Malat1 transcripts for degradation through Ago2-dependent nuclear RNA-induced silencing complex machinery; the Malat1 decrease subsequently leads to the destabilization of Suv39h1/HP1β/HDAC1-repressive complex and displacement by a Set7-containing activating complex, which allows MyoD trans-activation to occur. Together, our findings identify a regulatory axis of miR-181a-Malat1-MyoD/Suv39h1 in myogenesis and uncover a previously unknown molecular mechanism of Malat1 action in gene regulation. In addition, a total of 8 publications have been generated with this funding acknowledged (PartC8). Our findings were highly received when presented in international and local conferences/seminars (PartC9). One Postdoc Fellow, Dr. Xiaona Chen was trained under the support of this grant. Two PhD students, Drs. Yuying Li and Jiajian Zhou, were also trained under the grant. All of them obtained the PhD in 2018 (PartC10). Through this work, we have also developed active collaboration with Prof. Shinichi Nakagawa from RIKEN, Japan; Prof. Kannanganattu V. Prasanth from University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign; Prof. Miguel Esteban, Guangzhou Institute of Biomedicine and Health, China; Prof. Zhenguo Wu, HKUST; Prof. Hao Sun, Department of Chemical Pathology, CUHK. (PartC11).

14116014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116014.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of lncRNAs particularly divergently transcribed lincRNAs, but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and sarcopenia. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of lncRNAs in the muscle cells in the context of normal muscle development, acute and chronic injury induced muscle regeneration and muscle aging. We will also continue to examine the interplay between lncRNAs and transcription factors or RNA binding proteins in myogenesis.

14116014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116014.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. The functionality and underlying mechanisms of lncRNA are largely unknown. Thus, lncRNAs are considered as the new frontier of biomedical research. Here in this project we elucidated the function role of a lncRNA, Malat1, in skeletal muscle cell and muscle regeneration process. In the long run, we hope this will serve as a starting point for the development of new therapeutic approaches for treating muscle related human diseases.

14116214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116214.value: Insomnia is one of the most prevalent health problems in general population. In a series of community-based studies on the school-aged children and adolescents in Hong Kong, we found that 4.0% of them had frequent and chronic insomnia disorder. In line with the other studies conducted in western countries, our studies revealed a robust familial aggregation and genetic predisposition of insomnia in Hong Kong Chinese families. Meanwhile, several longitudinal studies (including our prospective 5-year follow-up study) reported that insomnia runs a relatively persistent course not only in adults, but also in children and adolescents. In addition, insomnia is linked to a variety of adverse health outcomes and behavioral problems in children and adolescents, such as poor mental health, frequent temper outburst, diminished academic performance, increased future risk of mental illness, drug abuse, and adverse physical outcome. Therefore, there is an imperative need of developing an effective insomnia prevention program, especially during early and critical developmental stage at childhood and adolescence. Although preventive interventions have moved into the forefront of the healthcare research agenda over the past decades, empirical data on the efficacy of preventive strategies for insomnia disorder, especially in children and adolescents, is conspicuously lacking. As based on one of the widely accepted tripartite models of the etiologies and developmental course of insomnia, there are several modifiable risk factors, especially sleep-related behavioral and cognitive factors, which may predispose and perpetuate the vicious psychopathological cycle leading to chronic insomnia. Thus, we propose to develop an innovative prevention program targeting several potentially modifiable risk factors among high-risk subjects who are genetically predisposed to insomnia and have subthreshold clinical symptoms of insomnia. Our preventive program will feature an integrated cognitive-behavioral therapy-insomnia (CBT-I) to address sleep hygiene, distorted sleep cognitions, maladaptive coping behaviors and stress management. The efficacy of this preventive intervention will be examined in a randomized controlled trial on a group of high-risk adolescents through a prospective 18-month follow-up. To our knowledge, this study will be the first of its kind to answer a pivotal clinical question by examining a research hypothesis on whether insomnia can be prevented. The therapeutic approach and outcomes of this proposed study will have important implications in the context of preventive medicine on an individual level and long-term health care planning from a public health perspective.

14116214.label: Realisation of objectives
14116214.value: The current study aimed to conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of brief cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia in preventing the onset of insomnia in at-risk adolescents. Adolescents (aged 12-18 years) who had a family history of insomnia and sub-threshold insomnia symptoms. All subjects were invited to attend follow up assessment at post intervention, 6 month, 12 month and 18 month after the intervention. The project was completed as planned and the objective was fully achieved. We have recruited a total of 242 eligible adolescents who were randomly assigned to either intervention group (N=121) or non-active control group (N=121). In the intervention group, adolescents received 4-weekly programme covering basic sleep knowledge, sleep hygiene practice, sleep restriction strategies, stimulus control and constructive worry. A total of 21 groups have been conducted with an average of 6 subjects per group. Eighty-two percent of them attended all four treatment sessions, 15 of them (12%) attended three out of four sessions, while the remaining (N = 7, 6%) attended less than three sessions. Two hundred and eighteen adolescents (90·1%) attended post-intervention assessment, 219 (90·5%) attended 6-month follow up, 205 (85%) attended 12-month follow up and 196(81%) attended 18 month follow up. The rates of missing data were similar between the two groups at all time points. . As current study is using a high-risk approach, apart from assessing adolescent’s insomnia symptoms, their parental sleep problems were also one of the criteria in the study protocol. In order to achieve adequate sample size, subjects in this study were recruited through various means including schools, previous education cohort and community subjects. All secondary schools in Hong Kong were invited to participate in the current study. For schools who willing to join the study, they will help to deliver the screening questionnaire to both students and parents. We have finally sent out screening questionnaires (N=11031) to 20 local secondary schools and collected 7714 student and 3693 parental questionnaires. Among these students 624 fulfilled initial inclusion criteria (presence of insomnia symptoms and family history of insomnia). As for community and previous study cohort subjects, we contacted students with positive family history of insomnia and assessed their insomnia symptoms via brief telephone screening interview. Finally, we have invited 335 students to attended face to face clinical interview to ascertain their eligibility and 269 adolescents have completed the screening and baseline questionnaire. However, 27 of them declined not to continue the study prior to the randomisation. Thus, a total of 242 adolescents were finally enrolled and randomized.

14116214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116214.value: The cumulative proportions of youths with the onset of overall insomnia disorder (acute and chronic insomnia) over the 18-month period for intervention and control groups were 8.3% (n=10) vs 24% (n=29); χ2 = 11.0, p = 0·001). The cumulative percentage of acute and chronic insomnia were [6.6 (n=8) vs. 16.5% (n=20) (χ2 = 5.82, p < 0·05)] and, [3.3% (n=4) vs· 9.1% (n=11) (χ2 = 3·48, p = 0.062)], respectively. There were significantly lower incidence rate of overall insomnia over the 18-month period in the intervention group (Breslow generalized Wilcoxon χ2 = 11.2, df = 1, p = 0·001). There were also significant lower incidence rate in acute insomnia (Breslow generalized Wilcoxon χ2 = 6.0, df = 1, p = 0·015) and marginal significant in incidence of chronic insomnia (Breslow generalized Wilcoxon χ2 = 3.35, df = 1, p = 0·067). Hazard ratios (HR) were computed to compare time to incidence rate of insomnia between two groups. The risk was significantly lower for the overall incidence of insomnia (either acute or chronic) (HR= 0.33, 95% C.I.: 0·16 – 0·68, p = 0·003), acute insomnia (HR = 0·39, 95% C.I.: 0.17 – 0.89, p = 0·03) and was also lower at a nearly significant level for chronic insomnia (HR = 0·37, 95% C.I.: 0·12-1·16, p = 0·087) in the intervention group relative to the control group. There was significant interaction effect on severity of insomnia symptoms (F=2.54, p = 0.041). The insomnia symptoms was significantly reduced in the adolescents in the intervention group compared to those in the control group at post-intervention (t[224] = 2.3; p = 0.02), 6-month (t[214] = 2.32; p = 0.02) and 12-month (t[218] = 2.9; p = 0.05), but not at 18month follow up (p = 0.13). In addition, there were also significant interaction effect observed in vulnerability to stress related sleep disturbance as measured by Ford Insomnia Response Stress Test (FIRST) (F= 2.7, p = 0.032) and daytime sleepiness as measured by Pediatric Daytime Sleepiness Scale (PDSS) (F = 2.6, p = 0.039). Intervention group had lower FIRST score at post intervention, 12month and 18 month follow up (all p < 0.05) compared to control group and they also had lower PDSS score at post intervention and 18 month follow up.

14116214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116214.value: To our knowledge, this study was the first study in the world literature that provided novel evidence to support the efficacy of a brief CBT-I in preventing the future onset of insomnia and improving the associated vulnerability factors and functional outcomes. The findings suggested this programme has the potential to reduce the long term health care burden, future medical and mental complications associated with insomnia in young people. Thus, this current study also provided the empirical basis for delivering such a programme as a promising preventive strategy at community level. However, one of the major limitations of the current study is the use of non-active control group. Although non-active control is often used as the first-step to test the effectiveness of the new intervention, it remained possible that other non-specific factors such as contact time or peer support might also partially contribute to the positive outcomes. Thus, incorporation of active control group such as sleep hygiene education in future study could further confirm the efficacy of this brief prevention programme. Nonetheless, the long-term positive outcome of the current study suggested that it is worth to deliver the prevention programme to prevent the onset of insomnia at a community level.

14116214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116214.value: Adolescence is a vulnerable period predisposing to the emergence of insomnia. Particularly, there was a 3-fold increased risk among those with a family history of insomnia. This study aimed to assess whether a brief CBT-I could prevent the future development of insomnia in at-risk adolescents. Our study demonstrated that insomnia can be prevented by using a brief group-based CBT-I. The programme has high programme completion and follow up rate, which revealed that it is a feasible and effective approach to reduce the incidence of insomnia in at-risk adolescents. The main findings of the current study indicated that adolescents who received the prevention programme were at a lower risk of developing insomnia throughout 18 month period compared to the control group. In addition, they also had lower level of insomnia symptoms, lower vulnerability towards the stressful events and lower daytime sleepiness compared to their peers in the control group. Therefore, it is suggested that the delivery of the current prevention programme might have the potential to reduce the long term health care burden, future medical and mental complications associated with insomnia in young people and provided the empirical basis for delivering such a programme as a promising preventive strategy at community level.

14117314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117314.value: Biosynthesis of active urease involves post-translational carbamylation of an active-site lysine residue and insertion of two nickel ions to its active site. In Helicobactor pylori, four urease accessory proteins, UreE, UreF, UreG and UreH, assist this maturation process. UreG, a SIMIBI GTPase that binds nickel, plays a central role in urease maturation, as it is currently believed that GTP hydrolysis drives the delivery of nickel to apo-urease. We have previously shown that binding of GTP and nickel induces the formation of UreG dimer. Upon stimulation by bicarbonate, the nickel/GTP-bound UreG dimer can then activate apo-urease in the presence of UreF/UreH via a GTP-hydrolysis dependent process. Current biochemical evidence suggests that UreG serves a molecular switch that change conformations in responses to binding of nickel and/or different guanine nucleotides. The main theme of this proposal is to study how transition among different conformational sub-states of UreG provides a mechanism for the protein to facilitate urease maturation – for example, to bind or release its nickel and to switch protein-interacting partners. This proposal aims to address three important aspects on how UreG carries its functions: First, we will address the structural mechanism of how nickel delivery is controlled by GTP hydrolysis by solving the structures of apo-, GDP-bound, and nickel/GTP-bound forms of UreG. Comparison of these structures will reveal the conformational changes that are responsible for binding/release of nickel ions. Second, we will address the mechanism of how bicarbonate activates the GTPase activity of UreG. Third, we will address the questions if UreG uses the same interacting surface in binding both UreE and UreF/UreH, and if different conformational sub-states of UreG provide a mechanism for UreG to switch protein-interacting partners between UreE and UreF/UreH. In cells, the fidelity of metal delivery to metalloenzymes is often ensured by specific protein-protein interactions. The proposed structure-function study on UreG will serve as a paradigm to study how other metallochaperones (such as HypB and CooC1, accessory proteins for hydrogenase and carbon monoxide dehydrogenase) couples NTP hydrolysis to metal delivery. Moreover, as UreG is essential to the maturation of urease and to colonization of H. pylori in acidic stomach, mechanistic insights obtained in this study will lay the foundation for the future design of drugs that specifically inhibit the activity of UreG. 活性尿素酶的生物合成涉及活性位點賴氨酸的氨甲醯化與兩個鎳離子的插入。在幽門螺旋桿菌中，能幫助尿素酶成熟過程的四個尿素酶輔助蛋白質分別是UreE、UreF、UreG和UreH。隸屬於SIMIBI家族的GTPase UreG能夠結合鎳離子並且在尿素酶的成熟過程中發揮核心作用，因為GTP水解驅使鎳離子運送到尿素酶的活化前體。我們之前的研究表明，GTP和鎳離子的結合能誘導UreG二聚體的形成。在碳酸氫鹽的刺激下，結合了鎳離子/GTP的UreG二聚體能在UreF/UreH存在的前提下，通過GTP水解來活化尿素酶前體。 目前的生化實驗證據表明，在結合鎳離子和/或不同的鳥嘌呤核苷酸時，UreG能對此做出構象變化並由此成為一個分子開關。本提案的主題是研究UreG在不同構象子狀態中如何轉換以提供一個蛋白質促進尿素酶活化的機制——例如，結合或者釋放鎳離子和切換蛋白質相互作用的夥伴。本項提案的目的在於解決UreG如何行使其功能的三個重要問題： 首先，我們將通過測定活化前體、結合GDP和結合鎳離子/GTP狀態的UreG的結構以研究鎳離子的運送是如何由GTP水解控制的機制。對於這些結構的比較將揭示蛋白質構象的變化對於結合/釋放鎳離子的作用。其次，我們將研究碳酸氫鹽如何啟動UreG的GTPase活性的機制。再次，我們將研究UreG 是否使用相同的蛋白質互作表面來結合UreE和UreF/UreH，以及UreG不同的構象子狀態是否能提供一種機制使得UreG能在蛋白質互作中與UreE和UreF/UreH之間進行轉換。 在細胞中，金屬運送到金屬酶的保真度通常由特定的蛋白質相互作用來確保。我們關於研究UreG結構和功能的研究將作為範例來研究其他金屬伴侶蛋白（例如HYPB和CooC1，輔助蛋白的氫化酶和一氧化碳脫氫酶）如何結合NTP水解來運送金屬離子。此外，UreG對於尿素酶的成熟過程及其對於幽門螺旋桿菌在酸性胃中的繁殖起著至關重要的作用，本研究提供的機理方面的見解將為能特異性抑制UreG活性的藥物設計奠定基礎。

14117314.label: Realisation of objectives
14117314.value: The main theme of this project is to elucidate how conformational changes in UreG couple GTP hydrolysis to urease maturation. We have previously showed that UreG binds nickel ions and forms dimer in the presence of GTP. We have determined the crystal structure of UreG from Klebsiella pneumoniae (KpUreG) in complex with nickel ions and GMPPNP, a nonhydrolyzable analog of GTP. Full length KpUreG was crystallized but crystals were of poor diffraction quality. In our hand, truncation of the 4 residues at the N-terminus and one residue at the C-terminus of KpUreG improved the diffraction quality of UreG to 1.8 Å resolution. KpUreG(delta-N4,deltaC1) was crystallized in 100 mM Hepes pH 7.5, 1.8 M ammonium sulfate, 3% dioxane at 16°C using the hanging-drop-vapor-diffusion method. Diffraction data were collected using an in-house Rigaku FRE+ diffractometer and the phase was solved by molecular replacement using the crystal structure of Helicobacter pylori UreG (HpUreG) in the UreG2F2H2 complex. The structure was refined using the programs PHENIX and COOT. To understand the conformational changes in UreG upon GTP binding/hydrolysis, the structure of Ni/GMPPNP-bound KpUreG was compared to that of GDP-bound HpUreG in the UreG2F2H2 complex (Fig. 1 & 2, Yuen et al. 2017). In general, most residues in the two structures were superimposable but large conformation changes were observed in the G2 region (residue 37-52) and in residues near the CPH nickel-binding motif (residues 62-68). The comparison between the two homologous proteins is warrant because (1) KpUreG shares high sequence homology (64% of their residues are identical) with HpUreG; (2) Ni/GMPPNP-bound KpUreG is structurally homologous to GDP-bound HpUreG; (3) residues that are important for the observed conformational changes are conserved in both KpUreG and HpUreG. Our structural comparison explains why GTP binding/hydrolysis promote nickel binding/release. We showed that GTP-dependent conformational changes are induced by charge-charge repulsion between Asp37 and the gamma-phosphate group of GTP. The conformational changes in the G2 region bring Glu42 to form an inter-subunit salt bridge with Arg130, promoting dimerization of UreG that brings the nickel-binding motif of each promoter together. In the GDP-bound HpUreG, residues Cys66 and His68 were pointing away from each other, which are not able to bind nickel ions. In the Ni/GMPPNP-bound KpUreG, Cys66 and His68 of each protomer move in an opposite direction towards the metal binding site to form a square-planar coordination geometry for nickel ions binding. The structural insights obtained were further tested by mutagenesis and biochemical studies in HpUreG (Fig. 3, Yuen et al. 2017). We created a double mutant D37A/E42A of HpUreG, and showed that the mutations abolished the dimerization of UreG, GTPase activity and the ability to activate urease in vitro. Our results suggest that the Asp37 and Glu42 are essential for the GTP-induced conformational changes, which are in turn important for GTPase activity and urease activation. We further showed that GTP binding/hydrolysis allosterically regulate the protein-binding partners of UreG (Fig 4, Yuen et al. 2017). Our structural analyses suggest that UreG exists in two distinct conformational states: the GDP-bound state and the GTP-bound state. We mixed purified samples of H. pylori UreG2F2H2 complex and UreE2 dimer. Upon addition of GTP-gamma-S, HpUreG dissociated from the UreG2F2H2 complex and formed the UreE2G2 complex. On the other hand, the UreG2F2H2 complex largely remained intact when GDP was added. These results suggest that UreG prefers to bind UreF/UreH in the GDP-bound state but prefers to form the UreE2G2 complex in the GTP-bound state. Moreover, the ability of HpUreG to swap protein-binding partners was abolished by the D37A/E42A mutations, further substantiating the conclusion that the conformational changes upon GTP hydrolysis/binding determine the protein-binding partners of UreG. To establish that the swapping of protein-binding partners is essential to urease activation, we have used an in vitro urease activation assay in which purified samples of urease accessory proteins are added to the apourease (Fig. 5, Yuen et al. 2017). We showed that addition of nickel-charged UreE2 dimer and UreG2F2H2 complex can activate urease. The activation is likely mediated by the formation of UreE2G2 complex, as addition of nickel-charged UreE2G2 and UreF2H2 complexes can also activate urease in vitro. Moreover, we have designed a new experiment to demonstrate the direct protein-protein interaction among urease accessory proteins is essential to the transfer of nickel for urease maturation (Fig. S10, Yuen et al. 2017). We set up the protein components of the urease activation assay in either side of a dialysis membrane in a two-chamber dialyzer. The dialysis membrane allows diffusion of nickel ions but prevents direct protein-protein interactions. When the nickel-charged UreE2 dimer was separated from UreG2F2H2 and apourease, urease was not activated. Urease was activated only when all the protein components were located in the same chamber of the dialyzer, suggesting protein-protein interactions are essential. Our results also suggest that bicarbonate activates GTPase activity of UreG by serving as one of the substrates of UreG. GTPase activity of HpUreG were measured in 0 – 200 mM bicarbonate, 0 – 4 mM GTP, 0.2 M KCl, 1 mM TCEP, 20 mM Hepes pH 7.5 at 37°C. The bicarbonate-dependent GTPase activity of HpUreG followed the Michaelis-Menten kinetics, with Km values of 13 ± 4 mM for bicarbonate and 0.29 ± 0.04 mM for GTP. That bicarbonate is a substrate of UreG is further supported by the observation that acetate, a structural analog of bicarbonate, inhibits GTPase activity of HpUreG. Through structure determination, mutagenesis and biochemical studies, we have addressed all objectives of this project. Our research findings have been published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, USA: Yuen MH, Fong YH, Nim YS, Lau PH, Wong KB (2017) Structural insights into how GTP-dependent conformational changes in a metallochaperone UreG facilitate urease maturation. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA, in press http://www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.1712658114.

14117314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117314.value: 1. GTP binding/hydrolysis induces large conformational changes in UreG. We have determined the crystal structure of KpUreG dimer in complex with nickel ions and GMPPNP (a GTP analog) and compared the structure with the GDP-bound HpUreG. We showed that GTP-binding to UreG induces large conformational changes in the G2 region and the CPH nickel-binding motif. 2. Our work reveals how GTP binding/hydrolysis induce nickel binding/release. Upon GTP binding, Cys66 and His68 of the nickel-binding motif from both protomers of UreG form a square-planar coordination that binds a nickel ion at the dimeric interface. Since square-planar coordination is favoured for Ni(II), which have a d8 electron configuration but not for other ions such as Zn(II), it explains the specificity of UreG towards binding Ni(II) in the presence of GTP. GTP hydrolysis reverts the conformation of UreG to the GDP-bound state, disrupting the square-planar coordination and promoting the release of nickel ions. 3. The conformational states of UreG determine the protein-binding partners of UreG. We showed that UreG prefers to bind UreF2H2 in the GDP-bound state, but switches from the UreG2F2H2 complex to form the UreE2G2 complex in the presence of GTP. GTP induces conformational changes in the G2 region so that an invariant residue Tyr39 of UreG is protruding into the UreF2H2 binding interface, justifying why GTP-binding promotes the dissociation of UreG from the UreG2F2H2 complex. Binding of GTP introduces charge-charge repulsion between the Asp37 and the gamma-phosphate group of GTP, which induce large conformational changes in the G2 region that bring Glu42 to form an inter-subunit salt bridge with Arg130. Structural insights are supported by mutagenesis studies. We showed that the double mutation of D37A/E42A abolished GTP-dependent dimerization of UreG and prevented the dissociation of UreG from the UreG2F2H2 complex. 4. Nickel is transferred from the nickel-delivery pathway through protein-protein interactions. By using an in vitro urease assay, we demonstrated that the nickel charged UreE2, UreE2G2 or UreG2 can provide the sole nickel source for urease activation. We showed that nickel ions are transferred along the nickel delivery pathway of “UreE2 → UreE2G2 → UreG2 → apourease” through protein-protein interactions, without releasing the free nickel ions to the solution. Taken together, we propose a mechanism of how UreG couples GTP-dependent conformational changes to facilitate urease activation (Fig. 6, Yuen et al. 2017). Our work has been published in Yuen et al. 2017, PNAS (http://www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.1712658114)

14117314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117314.value: Supported by this GRF grant, we have delineated how UreG couples conformational changes due to GTP hydrolysis/binding to facilitate nickel delivery for urease maturation. Since the survival of H. pylori in acidic stomach relies on the biosynthesis of active urease, the nickel delivery pathway for urease activation could be a novel drug target against H. pylori infection. Moreover, it is currently not known how the nickel-charged UreG interacts with the apourease and UreF2H2 in the activation complex, and what triggers the GTP hydrolysis during urease maturation. Presumably, premature GTP hydrolysis outside the activation complex would result in losing the nickel ions to the solution. Future structural studies on UreG/UreF/UreH in complex with urease may help to fill in the knowledge gap here.

14117314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117314.value: Urease, a nickel-containing enzyme, is a virulence factor for Helicobacter pylori, which infects half of the human population and causes peptic ulcers and stomach cancers worldwide. Urease hydrolyses stomach urea into the neutralizing ammonia, and allows the pathogen to thrive in acidic stomach. Our work provides a paradigm on how the bacterial cells solve the problem of delivering nickel, a toxic metal, to the active site of urease. We showed how GTP hydrolysis/binding induce conformational changes in UreG, which allow the protein to control the binding/release of nickel ions and to swap its protein-binding partners along the nickel delivery pathway. As a result, the nickel ions are passing from one protein to another, without releasing the free toxic metal ions to the cells. As the survival of H. pylori in acidic stomach requires the production of active urease, our work may shed new insights into the development of drugs against the H. pylori infection.

14117414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117414.value: Background Intracranial arterial stenosis (ICAS) accounts for around 50% of ischemic stroke and transient ischemic attack (TIA) in China. Those with symptomatic ICAS face a high risk of stroke recurrence, for whom the percentage of luminal stenosis is usually regarded as the basis for risk stratification and clinical decision making. However, the anatomic severity of ICAS isn’t always proportionate to its hemodynamic significance, which may also affect recurrent risk of stroke patients with ICAS. The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) technique, when applied to ICAS by reconstructing source images of intracranial computed tomographic angiography (CTA), is capable of depicting hemodynamic features of blood flow in the case of ICAS, which may yield good predictors for stroke recurrence and hence facilitate risk stratification of stroke patients with symptomatic ICAS. Objective We aim to evaluate the predictive values of hemodynamic features of ICAS, assessed via CFD models reconstructed from intracranial CTA images, in predicting stroke recurrence and other outcome events in ischemic stroke or TIA patients with symptomatic ICAS. Method This is a retrospective-prospective cohort study. A total of 300 in-patients at Prince of Wales Hospital, with ischemic stroke or TIA due to an ≥50% ICAS identified on intracranial CTA, will be enrolled. Eligible patients admitted before or after the start date of the proposed study, will be retrospectively or prospectively enrolled, respectively. Clinical records will be collected. Percentage of luminal stenosis of the index ICAS will be evaluated on CTA images. CTA source images will be processed using CFD technique for evaluation of hemodynamics of the index ICAS. All patients will be regularly followed up for the primary outcome of recurrent ischemic stroke in the territory of the evaluated artery and other outcome events, with a mean follow-up of around 2 years. We will evaluate the predictive values of hemodynamic features of ICAS, alone and combining with anatomic severity of the lesion, in predicting risk of recurrent events in patients enrolled. Significance (1) CTA images, together with CFD models based on CTA, will provide anatomic and hemodynamic significance of an ICAS without using any invasive technique, which will help establish an all-in-one noninvasive method for comprehensive evaluation of ICAS. (2) Patients with symptomatic ICAS are at high risk of recurrence. Results of the proposed study will facilitate risk stratification and thus guide clinical decision making for the study population.

14117514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117514.value: Central auditory processing forms the basis of higher-level communicative abilities (e.g., spoken language). Disorders of the central auditory processing system are associated with disorders of literacy (e.g., dyslexia), learning (Chermak et al., 1999; Hugdahl et al., 1998; King et al., 2003), and music (Peretz, 2008). Surprisingly, despite the rapid expansion of knowledge in human molecular genetics, efforts in identifying genetic candidates of central auditory processing in humans have been lagging behind. This stands in contrast with efforts in identifying candidate genes that contribute to peripheral and non-brain related communication functions such as auditory hair cells (Zheng et al., 2000) and craniofacial anomalies (Jabs et al., 1991) that have started at least a decade ago. A class of brain-growth related, microcephaly primary hereditary (MCPH) genes represents an exceptional opportunity for identifying genes that affect brain and higher-level communicative functions. Recent findings from multiple laboratories across the globe using different methodological approaches have confirmed the associations between selective SNPs of MCPH genes and brain anatomy (Rimol et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2008) and central auditory (pitch) perception (Wong et al., 2012). Furthermore, some of these SNPs show sex-dependent effects (Rimol et al. & Wang et al.). Thus, we hypothesize that MCPH genes play an important role in central nervous system functions that ultimately affect central auditory processes, potentially more so in males. Though these studies provide important leads to establishing MCPH genes’ central auditory roles, they are isolated in that no single study was conducted to connect all relevant SNPs with brain and central auditory functions. Furthermore, it is unclear whether the narrow behavioral phenotype explored (pitch perception) was one of the many auditory phenotypes with which these genes are associated. The focus of the proposed research is to comprehensively investigate the role of MCPH genes in central auditory functions and their neural underpinnings in subjects of Han Chinese decent, including examination of potential sex-dependent effects. If successful, it will not only provide a list of gene candidates for examining functions and disorders of the central nervous system that affect central auditory processing, but also lay a foundation for exploration of other genes that are related to communicative behaviors through bioinformatics and proteomics. Furthermore, because all Chinese languages use pitch to signal word meaning, MCPH genes might be particularly important biomarkers for language deficits in Chinese speakers, especially those who speak a Chinese language with more complex tonal system (e.g., Cantonese). 中樞聽覺處理是高階溝通能力（例如：口語）的基礎。而中樞聽覺處理系統的障礙，亦與閱讀（如：失讀症）﹑學習 (Chermak et al., 1999; Hugdahl et al., 1998; King et al., 2003)，和音樂 (Peretz, 2008) 方面的障礙緊密相關。令人意外的是，雖然人類分子遺傳學的研究發展迅速，有關知識愈來愈豐富，但有關負責人類中樞聽覺處理的基因的研究仍然相對落後。然而，自至少十年前開始，學界已有不少研究著手找尋哪些基因會影響與外周神經系統有關，及與大腦無關的溝通功能（例如：聽覺毛細胞 (Zheng et al., 2000) ﹑顱面異常 (Jabs et al., 1991)）。目前學界已發現一些與大腦發展有關，且導致先天性小頭症(MCPH)的基因；這正正為識別影響大腦及高階溝通功能的基因提供了大好機會。近年來，全球不同的實驗室使用不同的研究方法證實了以下三者之間有密切關係：先天性小頭症基因的選擇性單核苷酸多態性(SNP)﹑大腦結構 (Rimol et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2008)﹑和中樞聽覺（音高）感知。其中一些SNP更帶有性別差異 (Rimol et al. & Wang et al.)。因此，我們假設先天性小頭症基因在中樞神經系統功能上扮演著重要角色，最終影響中樞聽覺處理，並多數在男性身上發生。以往的研究雖然帶領我們認識先天性小頭症基因在中樞聽覺系統起著的作用，卻沒有一個研究把所有相關的SNP與大腦和中樞聽覺功能連結起來。再者，目前學界仍不清楚知道已探究的狹窄行為表型（音高感知）是否眾多跟這些基因有關的聽覺表型的其中之一。是次研究的重點為詳細地探究先天性小頭症基因在中樞聽覺功能中扮演的角色，並其在漢族人身上的神經機制，包括研究潛在的性別差異。如果成功，是次研究不旦能提供一張基因的列單，以探討中樞神經系統的功能和障礙及其對中樞聽覺處理的影響，更能為學界提供一個的基礎，透過生物資訊學和蛋白質體學去發掘其他與溝通行為有關的基因。此外，由於所有中國語言均以音高表示字義，先天性小頭症基因可能是中文母語人士──尤其那些音調系統複雜的（如：廣東話）──出現語言障礙的重要生物標記。

14117514.label: Realisation of objectives
14117514.value: To achieve the two (revised) project objectives, we tested 426 native speakers of Cantonese (all Han Chinese, age range 18-27 years) on a number of auditory tasks, covering lexical tone processing, musical pitch perception, rhythm perception, and auditory working memory. A non-verbal IQ score was also obtained from the participants (all scored at least 85, mean = 108). All participants passed a hearing screening test. A saliva sample was collected using an Oragene kit. Two groups of SNPs were examined. The hypothesized microcephaly SNPs have been hypothesized to be related to brain, pitch and/or lexical tone functions (Rimol et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2008; Passemard et al., 2016; Dediu & Ladd, 2007; Wong et al. 2012) (see Table 1 of Wong et al., submitted). The control SNPs are hypothesized to be related to general language functions, especially those with grammar, because of their relationship with the neurotransmitter dopamine and potentially the cortico-striatal pathway (Wong et al., 2012b; Wong et al., 2013), or have been shown repeatedly to be related to language impairment, motor speech disorder, and/or specifically the phenotype of non-word repetition (Vernes et al., 2008; Newbury et al., 2009) (see Table S1 of Wong et al., submitted). These control SNPs are not hypothesized to be associated directly with lexical tone or non-language related auditory behaviors such as those being examined. Associations between auditory behaviors and the genetic variants were investigated via general linear models and machine-learning techniques (support vector machine) to provide convergence of results. To address the first project objective, we used multiple linear regression and forward stepwise regression to identify SNPs that showed significant associations after correction for multiple comparisons and after factors such as IQ, gender, age and years of musical training were controlled. We looked specifically for association between the hypothesized SNPs and lexical tone processing. A priori, we did not expect the hypothesized SNPs to be associated with behaviors that are auditory but not lexical tone specific. As an additional control procedure, we examined the associations between the control SNPs and auditory behaviors, and again did not expect a significant association a priori. As will be discussed below, we were able to find a lexical-tone specific association. Machine learning was then performed to provide converging evidence for the GLM results. Specifically, a nested k-fold leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) procedure with support vector machine (SVM) classifier was used (Pedregosa et al 2011). To address the second objective, we examined significant associations that were identified in the GLMs and specifically looked for interactions with gender.

14117514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117514.value: Objective 1. In both multiple linear regression and forward stepwise regression, a significant model fit was found for lexical tone. In the multiple linear regression model, significant associations were found for age, years of musical training, and ASPM (rs41310927). In the stepwise regression analysis, years of musical training with IQ contributed to the first two models that explained up to 15.6% of variance in lexical tone perception. The final significant model had rs41310927 explaining another 1.6% of variance. No other microcephaly (hypothesized) SNPs contributed to lexical tone processing or any auditory behaviors. rs41310927 did not show significant association with any other auditory behaviors. The control SNPs did not show significant association with any auditory behaviors. After the contribution of musical experience and IQ, rs41310927 explained about 1.6% of variance in lexical tone processing. As expected, the effect size was small and within the limits of how much variance one SNP can explain as far as human cognitive abilities are concerned. [Okbay et al. (2016) found that the 74 SNPs that they examined together explained only 4% of variance in educational attainment (an average of .05% variance explained).] The aforementioned GLM analysis all suggested significant association between rs41310927 and lexical tone perception, along with IQ and years of musical training. In order to obtain converging evidence from multiple types of analytics, machine learning (support vector machine) was used. Predictability is estimated by the correlation coefficients (cc) between the predicted and the observed lexical tone performance. With only SNP rs41310927 as the predictor, the distribution of predicted cc (mean = .0881) was also significantly different (p = .019) from the null distribution, although as expected, the predicted cc with one SNP was much lower than when the other two variables were used as predictors (mean cc = .3754). Objective 2. There was no significant interaction between rs41310927 and gender. The association between lexical tone and rs41310927 did not seem to be male-dependent. This speaks to the potential broad applicability of our results if rs41310927 is eventually proved to be useful for clinical diagnosis of communication disorders. This research has resulted in several manuscripts and conference presentations concerning enhanced and disordered pitch processing. The manuscript that reported the main findings has been submitted to Nature Human Behaviour for consideration for publication. Two PhD students participated in this research (though they also worked on other projects).

14117514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117514.value: The odds ratios for an rs41310927 C allele carrier performing below the mean or one standard deviation below the mean on the lexical tone perception task are 2.13 (95% CI:1.38 – 3.29) and 1.90 (95% CI:1.11 – 3.26), respectively. In tone language speakers, poor tone perception is associated with a number of communication disorders, including Developmental Language Disorder (Wong et al., 2009) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (Xiaoyue Wang et al., 2017). Future research could investigate whether ASPM is a candidate gene for communication disorders and whether it is a genetic marker specific to individuals who speak a tone language (but not individuals who speak a non-tone language). Individuals with communication disorders should be genotyped for rs41310927. As discussed in Wong et al. (submitted), we believe our research that identified an association between a genetic variant and a linguistic feature provided strong evidence for the genetic-biasing hypothesis of language evolution. That hypothesis postulates the co-evolution of gene and language so that populations with an increased allele frequency of a gene favoring a linguistic feature would retain that feature in their language. Future research should further pursue direct experimentation between genes and other linguistic features to provide additional evidence for that hypothesis.

14117514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117514.value: All Chinese languages, including Cantonese, use pitch, called “lexical tones,” to contrast word meaning (e.g., /si/ spoken in high-level and low-level tones mean ‘teacher’ and ‘yes,’ respectively). Not surprisingly, poor lexical tone perception is associated with different communication disorders including Developmental Language Disorder and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Our research has identified a candidate gene, ASPM (rs41310927), for lexical tone processing. We found that adult native speakers of Cantonese who were carriers of the C copy of rs41310927 were at greater risk for tone processing difficulties. Only adults with no reported history of language and cognitive problems were tested in this project. Future research should examine individuals with a confirmed diagnosis of communication disorders in order to understand whether rs41310927 is associated with an actual increased risk for communication disorders. Findings from this research have implications for more than one discipline. In addition to its potential to improve early detection of communication disorders, this research also provided strong evidence for a hypothesis of language evolution called the genetic-biasing hypothesis. It is possible that populations of people who tend to have the C copy of rs41310927 would avoid having lexical tone in their language and instead adopt other linguistic features.

14118314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118314.value: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality, morbidity and rising healthcare cost worldwide (1). At least one in three strokes is directly attributable to atrial fibrillation (AF, common cardiac arrhythmia which predisposes clot formation in the heart that can dislodge to the brain causing stroke) (2-4). AF-related strokes are highly preventable by oral anticoagulation therapy (OAC, e.g. warfarin) reducing the risk of stroke by 60-70% (5). In ‘real-world’ practice, AF is diagnosed at time of stroke in 20-45% of cases (6) and detection can be difficult because AF may be present without symptoms and intermittent in nature. Furthermore, utilization of adequate OAC for stroke prevention is suboptimal in Hong Kong (7). Many AF patients are not prescribed OAC for reasons including, patient refusal due to poor awareness and understanding of their risk of stroke, fear of bleeding on OAC and physician reluctance to prescribe OAC (8). The challenge is to identify AF prior to occurrence of stroke. The latest European guidelines recommend opportunistic screening for people >65 years by pulse palpation followed by 12-lead ECG (9). However, 12-lead ECG requires a trained technician, time-consuming, requires the patient to lie on an examination couch and is not readily available in most outpatient clinics in Hong Kong. A practical screening test is needed. Our group has validated and optimized the diagnostic accuracy of a micro-miniaturized hand-held ECG device (AliveCor™) for AF-detection (10). A 30-second single-lead ECG recording is automatically recorded, uploaded to a secure server for interpretation and a printable and electronic report is available for download within 1 minute. Our study aims to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability and incremental cost of an outpatient based AF-screening program using the AliveCor device. We plan to screen >25,000 patients >65 years of age attending 6 medical outpatient clinics at a university affiliated hospital over 24 months. Based on our study, we anticipate ~500 (1.4%) newly diagnosed patients with AF in this age group (11). These newly diagnosed AF patients will be randomized to routine care versus individualized stroke prevention strategy which consists of patient education, stroke and bleeding risk assessment, evidence-based OAC recommendation (9), patient audit and follow-up to improve OAC utilization for stroke prevention. Long-term impact of population AF screening on health economic and service provision will be evaluated using Markov chain-decision modeling. We envisage this study will provide timely evidence to inform policy decisions concerning population-based AF-screening for AF for stroke prevention. 中風可導致死亡，甚至引發其他疾病，並增加全球醫療成本。現時每三個中風案例，便有一個是由心房顫動引發中風。心房顫動 (Atrial Fibrillation, AF) 簡稱房顫，是一種常見的心律失常，它導致心房中的血液滯留，形成血栓。脫落的血栓容易引起腦血管栓塞，造成中風。服食口服抗凝血藥 (如華化林) 能有效減低60-70%房顫引發的中風風險。可是，在現實的生活中由房顫引發中風的病人往往沒有明顯或持續性的病徵，因為大多數患有房顫的長者是無症狀，亦可能是間歇性的，從而令診斷增加困難。可惜的是，有20-45％的患者在中風期間才被診斷出來。在香港使用口服抗凝血藥預防或治療房顫引發的中風尚未普及。很多房顫患者因不同原因拒絕進行藥物治療，如患者對房顫引發中風的意識低、害怕食用抗凝藥物後引致更多的出血風險和醫生不願意處方抗凝藥物等。 究竟我們可以怎樣做才能有效預防房顫引致的中風﹖這正是我們現在所面對的挑戰。根據歐洲指引建議，為65歲人士進行脈搏檢查和12導聯的心電圖檢查能預防房顫引致的中風。然而，進行12導聯心電圖檢查需要一位受過專業訓練的技術員操作並耗費時間。再加上病人要躺在檢查床上進行，現時香港很多門診均沒有相關的設施配合。因此，一個實用的檢查方案是刻不容緩。 我們的團隊計劃試驗使用一個嶄新的微型掌上心電圖儀器 (AliveCorTM) 來診斷房顫。這嶄新的科技能有效地把30秒單導聯心電自動記錄下來，傳送到一個有保安系統的伺服器並進行分析，結果可於1分鐘內供下載 (列印報告及電子報告均可)。 我們的研究主要評估在門診使用AliveCorTM儀器進行篩選房顫患者的可行性，及其經濟效益。我們計劃為25,000多名病人進行篩選，年齡介乎65歲並曾經到訪6次大學附屬醫院門診的病人進行為期24個月的研究。我們估計大概有500人(約1.4%)在這年齡組別中被診斷出房顫。 這些新確診的房顫患者將隨機分配到常規護理或個人貼身護理(當中包括健康教育、中風及出血風險評估、建議合適藥物治療並調校藥物劑量以配合病人的實際需要。我們會使用馬爾可夫鏈模型(Markov Chain- decision Modeling)，評估這項研究對患者的健康及經濟成效的影響。期望這個研究計劃能有效地篩選出房顫患者並為他們及早診斷房顫及預防中風。

14118314.label: Realisation of objectives
14118314.value: This is the largest outpatient clinic based atrial fibrillation (AF) screening program in Hong Kong. All 5 study objectives were achieved. In total, we successfully screened 17,745 patients using the AliveCor hand-held ECG device at 6 specialty medical out-patient clinics (SOPCs), including 2 cardiology and 4 general medicine SOPCs, in the Prince of Wales Hospital between December 2014 and December 2017. For Objective 1, we reached the target screening sample size of 24,360 over 36 months (initial sample size estimation was 25,000). All ECGs were over-read by a cardiologist. We demonstrated AF screening using the AliveCor hand-held ECG device with 30-second automated reporting in general practice settings was feasible and well accepted by patients and staff. We assessed the impact of AF screening (Objective 2) by identifying the prevalence of AF (n=1,951; 16.3%) and the rate of newly identified AF (n=328; 2.7%) in patients aged ≥65 years (n=11,971) (Objective 2a) and the utilization rate (61.4%) of oral anticoagulants (OAC) for stroke prevention in screen-detected AF patients (Objective 2b). We performed a cost-effectiveness analysis to evaluate the increment cost effective ratio (ICER) per stroke avoided for screened vs a non-screened population of men and women aged ≥65 years with no known history of AF (Objective 2c). We evaluated the psychological and health status of 57 newly identified AF patients using Spielberger 6-item anxiety questionnaire and EQ-5D respectively (Objective 2d) at baseline and 12-month follow-up. For Objectives 3 & 4, 142 screen-positive patients were enrolled in Stage 2 of our study to assess the effectiveness of an individualized stroke prevention strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to individualized stroke prevention or routine care (71 patients each arm). All patients were guideline-eligible for consideration of OAC, with a CHA2DS2VASc score ≥2. Of those, 133 patients completed 1-year follow-up (9 declined, lost to follow-up or died) of which 54 (40.6%) newly diagnosed AF and 79 (59.4%) with known AF were not taking OAC. We surveyed patients’ knowledge of AF and understanding of OAC use at baseline and 12-month follow-up; and clinical outcomes including death, stroke and major bleeding at 12 months using the Hospital Authority’s computerized Clinical Management System (CMS) and medical chart review. The 71 patients randomized to individualized stroke prevention received personalized stroke risk assessment based on CHA2DS2VASc score and education talk by a cardiologist regarding their risk of stroke and benefit of OAC in stroke prevention. We found no significant differences in utilization of OAC for stroke prevention (Objective 3a), 12-month clinical outcomes (Objective 3b) and patient awareness of AF and understanding of stroke risk & stroke prevention therapy (Objective 3c) between patients in the individualized stroke prevention and routine care groups. Moreover, we compared the psychological and health status between groups. Cost-effectiveness analysis of the ICER per QALY gained and stroke avoided for patients who underwent individualized stroke prevention strategy vs routine care (Objective 4) was performed. Lastly, we evaluated the long-term health economic and service provision implications of large scale AF screening (Objective 2c & 5). The AF screening in an out-patient clinic was considered a dominant strategy and cost-saving from a health care provider perspective with negative ICER of HKD939,189 per stroke prevented (Objective 2c). The results have shown significantly lower hospitalization and stroke-related costs in the screened compared to non-screened population (HKD10,368,735 vs. HKD47,936,275). Thus, a Markov chain-decision model was not necessary in this situation (Objective 5) but may be used in the future if there are new strategies for AF screening and stroke prevention.
