14118314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14118314.value: 17,745 patients (mean 76.6±7.8 years) underwent 24,360 AF screening using a hand-held ECG device at 6 SOPCs in Prince of Wales Hospital over 36 months. 4,766 (26.9%) patients underwent repeat screening. We demonstrated that AF screening in an out-patient clinic setting was feasible and well accepted by patients (Part C9:1). We identified AF in 16.3% (n=1,951) of patients aged ≥65 years of which 16.8% (n=328) were newly diagnosed and 83.2% (n=1,623) were known AF. We found that repeated screening at 6 to 12 months interval was associated with ~1% incremental yield in detecting new AF (Part C9:2). Therefore, repeated AF screening may be a more effective strategy compared to single-time point screening. Almost all patients with newly diagnosed AF (97.7%) were at high risk of stroke (CHA2DS2VASc score≥2) that warrant oral anticoagulation therapy (OAC). However, at 12-month follow-up only 11.7% of patients with newly diagnosed AF compared to 70.5% of patients with known AF were treated with OAC. Prescription of OAC>1 month from first diagnosis of AF was associated with significantly higher incidence of stroke in patients with increasing CHA2DS2VASc scores. Our findings stress the importance of prompt OAC initiation after diagnosis for effective stroke prevention (Part C9:3). In Phase 2, 142 screen-positive patients were randomized 1:1 to individualized stroke prevention or routine care. This was a high stroke risk group with mean CHA2DS2VASc score of 4.0±1.7. At 12-month follow-up, utilization rate of OAC was higher in the stroke prevention group (42.4%) compared to routine care (29.9%) but was not statistical significant (p=0.14). There were no significant differences in 12-month clinical outcomes between the 2 groups (death 4.8% vs 5.6% and ischemic stroke 0% vs 5.6%, all p=NS). Rates of death (12.8% vs 31.8%; p=0.04) but not stroke was lower in the prevention group at 3-year follow-up (n=83). There were no significant differences in patient awareness of AF and OAC use between the 2 groups. Individualized stroke prevention intervention was not considered cost-effective with ICER per QALY gained of HKD16,670,513 and per stroke avoided of HKD325,075. Overall, hospitalization and stroke-related costs were significantly higher in the non-screened compared to screened population (HKD47,936,275 vs. HKD10,368,735). We conclude that AF screening in an out-patient clinic was considered a dominant strategy and cost-saving from a health care provider perspective with negative ICER of HKD939,189 per stroke prevented. Markov model may be used in the future if there are new strategies for AF screening and stroke prevention.

14118314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118314.value: We continued to complete 3-year patient follow-up. Future directions and potential benefits of a large outcomes database are multiple. We have conducted sub-studies to evaluate a novel method of AF detection by analyzing pulsatile photoplethysmographic (PPG) signals acquired from facial and fingertip using a smartphone camera (Part C9:7, C8:1 & 2). Our results of the validation studies have demonstrated that facial PPG acquired without physical contact is a potential screening tool for large scale AF detection (Part C8:3). Furthermore, the diagnostic performance of the AliveCor ECG device screening can be improved by a combined strategy: primary screening with hand-held ECG and secondary screening with facial PPG (Part C9:5). Recently, we evaluated the feasibility of high-throughput AF detection by analyzing facial PPG signals from multiple patients concurrently using a single digital camera and a pre-trained deep convolutional neural network (Part C9:6 & C8:4). We anticipate our results will improve outcomes of AF patients with regard to acceptance of screening and subsequent OAC treatment. We plan to expand our study on self-management and home monitoring of AF using off-the-shelf devices such as smartwatches and wristbands (Part C9:4).

14118314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118314.value: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is common and a major cause of stroke in the elderly. Our study was the largest AF screening with clinical and economic outcomes in Hong Kong. In total, 17,745 patients (average age 76.6±7.8 years) were screened average 1.4 times (range 1-10) using a hand-held ECG device in 6 out-patient clinics at Prince of Wales Hospital. Newly-diagnosed AF was found in 2.7% of patients. Almost all of these patients were at high-risk of stroke that warrant oral anticoagulation (OAC) therapy for stroke prevention. Repeated screening was performed on screen-negative patients and we found an incremental yield of 1% each time at repeated screening. 142 screen-positive high-stroke risk patients without appropriate OAC treatment were randomized to individualized stroke prevention or routine care. Patients who received individualized stroke prevention intervention were more likely to take OAC and had lower risk of death at 3-year. This study demonstrated that large-scale repeated AF screening in an out-patient setting is feasible, cost-saving and can facilitate improvements in clinical outcomes for AF patients in Hong Kong. We anticipate the local elderly population may benefit from AF screening and education to guide their stroke prevention options to maximize return on health expenditure in the long-term.

14118414.label: Realisation of objectives
14118414.value: This project was successfully completed with the proposed objectives fulfilled. Objective 1 aimed to investigate the role of ER stress in endothelial dysfunction in an in vitro I-R model, with focusing on NO- and EDHF-pathway. This objective was fulfilled with the finding of ER-stress mediated downregulation of eNOS expression and activity, evidenced by lowered eNOS protein level and decreased phosphorylation of eNOS at Ser1177. ER stress also mediates the impairment of IKCa/SKCa channel dependent EDHF-type response. Inhibition of ER stress restored KCa channel activity, concomitant with an improved EDHF-type response. These results were obtained from experiments performed at multiple levels including tissue studies (freshly isolated coronary arteries) in myograph, cellular studies (primary cultured coronary endothelial cells) using electrophysiological techniques, and molecular studies with western blotting. The second objective of this project was fulfilled through both functional studies and molecular studies of coronary endothelium. We demonstrated that under H-R condition, activation of the ER stress sensor molecule PERK and its downstream molecule eIF2α leads to the inhibition of Akt and eNOS activity, resulting in the loss of NO function in coronary arteries. Objective 3 and 4 studied TRPC3-mediated Ca2+ influx in H-R-induced endothelial dysfunction and the role of ER stress in regulating TRPC3-Ca2+signaling. These objectives were fulfilled by a series of cellular and molecular studies in primary cultured coronary endothelial cells and TRPC3 gene-manipulated cells. By employing patch-clamp technique,immunofluorescence,and co-immunoprecipitation methods, we demonstrated the interaction between IP3R1 and TRPC3 in coronary endothelial cells and the impact of ER stress under H-R condition. Inhibition of Ca2+ influx via TRPC3 channels significantly contributes to the compromised endothelial function caused by H-R. In summary, this project was successfully completed with research findings published in peer reviewed journals and reported in both local and international conferences.

14118414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14118414.value: 1. Endothelial dilator function of coronary arteries is impaired by ER stress. Both NO-mediated and IKCa/SKCa-dependent EDHF-mediated vasorelaxant responses are significantly attenuated. ER stress mediates H-R-induced impairment. 2. Activation of PERK and its downstream molecule eIF2α mediates ER stress-induced eNOS inhibition and NO loss through Akt-dependent mechanism. 3. ER stress plays a role in H-R-induced inhibition of TRPC3 channels. TRPC3 inhibition and the resultant reduction of Ca2+ influx suppress KCa channel activity and significantly contribute to the compromised endothelial function caused by H-R. The results derived from this study were published in a number of peer-reviewed journals. In addition, the research findings from this project have been reported at recognized local research conferences as well as well-known international conferences including Experimental Biology and American Heart Association scientific session with abstracts printed in FASEB Journal and Circulation, etc.

14118414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118414.value: Based on our previous studies, this project took a step forward in understanding the molecular basis of coronary endothelial dysfunction caused by I-R injury. The finding of ER stress-TRPC3-KCa signal conduction may eventually help identify new target sites for treating I-R injury. Further investigation on how I-R activates ER stress sensors in vascular cells and whether interactions among different sensor molecules may affect eNOS-NO and TRPC3-KCa signaling to regulate endothelial function in response to I-R would be directions for future studies, with the aim to further enrich our knowledge of vascular pathology related to ischemic injury.

14118414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118414.value: Although ER stress has been implicated in various cardiovascular disorders including ischemic heart disease, mechanistic understanding of the linkage between ER stress and endothelial dysfunction remains quite limited. With unraveling the role played by ER stress sensor molecules in regulating not only eNOS-NO signaling but also KCa-dependent EDHF pathway in coronary endothelium, we further demonstrated that inhibition of TRPC3-Ca2+ signal conduction by I-R is responsible for the suppressed endothelial KCa channel activity and the channel associated EDHF function. These new findings advance our understanding of the significance of ER stress in I-R injury and may eventually help identify new target sites for protecting coronary function in ischemic heart disease.

14118914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118914.value: The goal of this project is to understand how autophagy affects the early secretory pathway. The autophagic pathway and the secretory pathway are two important membrane trafficking processes, the defects of which will result in a wide range of human diseases including cancer, developmental defects, lipid absorption disorder and neurodegeneration. Autophagy is a lysosomal degradation process that can be induced by stresses such as amino acid starvation. Its activation is regulated by the kinase ULK1. The secretory pathway transport membrane and secreted proteins to plasma membrane and other membrane compartments. The process starts at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and then, the cargo proteins are exported towards the Golgi apparatus from specialized regions of the ER called ER exit sites by COPII vesicles, the formation of which requires a set of coat proteins including Sar1, Sec23, Sec24, Sec13, and Sec31. Nutrient starvation is a strong inducer for autophagy. As the cells are starved, it will be advantageous for them to slow down cellular secretion to conserve proteins, lipids and energy for survival. Therefore, coordination between autophagy and cellular secretion must exist. We have recently discovered that autophagy could induce drastic changes in the morphology of the ER exit sites and the trafficking of cargo proteins. We have further identified that the effect is, at least in part, mediated by the phosphorylation of Sec23 by the kinase ULK1. Based on this and other initial findings shown in the proposal, we will investigate how autophagy affects the biogenesis and vesicular traffic at the ER exit sites, using our research expertise in the phospho-regulation of COPII coat proteins and vesicular transport and our well-established research platforms in protein interaction studies. Upon completion of this project, we will unravel the mechanism how autophagy regulates cellular secretion, and provide a new perspective on the inter-dependence between these membrane trafficking processes that could be useful in finding the etiology of the related diseases.

14118914.label: Realisation of objectives
14118914.value: In the following, the descriptions of the results of the first three objectives are reiterations of the interim report. Those objectives have been completed with satisfaction. Reviewers can refer to the interim report for details. The status of objective 4 is new. 1. To identify the ULK1 phosphorylation sites on Sec23 and generate phospho-mimicking and phosphor-deficient mutant Sec23. In this aim, we needed to obtain purified Sec23 in preparative scale, and subjected the protein for ULK1 phosphorylation in vitro. Phosphorylation sites on Sec23 would be identified by mass spectrometry analysis. Then the candidate phosphorylation sites would be confirmed by mutagenesis studies. We overexpressed and purified Sec23A, ULK1 and ULK1(KD) separately in tens of microgram quantity in HEK293T cells and subjected Sec23A to phosphorylation by ULK1. We put in ULK1 (KD) in a parallel reaction as negative control. At the end of the kinase reaction, we ran an SDS-PAGE and isolated Sec23A from the gel and the gel-purified protein was subjected to mass spectrometry identification of phosphorylated peptide sequence. The samples were sent to BGI proteomic analysis. Four candidate phosphorylation sites were identified and listed in Table 1. The candidate ULK1 phosphorylation sites are Serine 207, Serine 312, threonine 405, and Serine 607. We constructed phosphorylation deficient mutants by changing these residues to alanine individually and tested if ULK1 could still phosphorylate the mutant Sec23A. In this experiment, ULK1 was co-expressed with the Myc-Sec23A mutants. Sec23 proteins were immunoprecipitated with anti-Myc antibody and the extent of Sec23A phosphorylation was detected by phospho-Ser/Thr antibody. The Sec23A mutant proteins are expressed to a level similar to the wildtype protein, suggesting the mutation did not invoke drastic degradation. The extent of phospho-Sec23A, however, varied significantly. S207A, T312A and T405A mutations all reduced the level of phospho-Ser/Thr of the protein, indicating they were bona fide ULK1 phosphorylation sites. It should be noted that the reduced phosphorylation on T312A mutant was less consistent than the other two mutations, so we were hesitant whether S312 was indeed a real phosphorylation site for ULK1. S670 remained similar to wildtype Sec23A, suggesting the phosphorylation status of this residue was not likely subjected to ULK1 regulation in vivo. 2. To determine the change in biochemical properties of Sec23 when it becomes phosphorylated by ULK1 In this aim, we investigated the change of biochemical properties of ULK1 phosphorylation by two methods. We determined if the ULK1 phosphorylation mutants conferred a change in the ERES by microscopy study. Second, we determined if the ULK1 phosphorylation mutants caused changes to the interaction between Sec23 and other COPII coat components. We expressed the phosphorylation deficient mutants and phospho-mimicking mutants (i.e. Ser/Thr to Asp) in cells to determine if any of these mutants recapitulate the change in ERES morphology caused by autophagy. T405A caused the mutant Sec23A protein slight more cytosolic even though the transfected cells were induced with autophagy by amino acid starvation. However, T405D presented highly punctate fluorescence signals similar to the ERES under active autophagy, and further increase in the fluorescence puncta was observed when To a lesser extent, the S207 mutations also behaved similarly to T405, i.e., phospho-deficient mutation causes lack of change in ERES upon autophagy activation and phospho-mimicking mutation causes increase in fluorescence intensity at ERES. Again, mutations to S312 are not consistent to autophagy-induced changes we have observed previously and, therefore, we did not follow up on this mutation. In summary, S207 and T405 are two residues that are phosphorylated by ULK1 and caused changes to the ERES morphology upon autophagy activation. We tested how these mutations may affect the biochemical property of Sec23A. Since ULK1 phosphorylation caused reduced interaction between Sec23A and Sec31A, we tested if mutating the residues S207 and T405 may recapitulate this change. The S207A mutation reduced the interaction with Sec31A but S207D mutation essentially abrogated the interaction. T405D only showed a slight decrease in Sec31A binding compared to wildtype Sec23A protein. Unexpectedly, T405A mutation abrogated the interaction. Since both sites are potentially phosphorylated by ULK1 during active autophagy, we constructed double mutations at these residues and determine if their binding to Sec31A was affected. All combination of double mutants showed significant reduction in Sec31A binding. However, the S207A, T405A mutant suffered from very extensive protein degradation, making the interpretation of its ability to bind to Sec31A unreliable. The protein expression level of S207D, T405D mutant was also reduced compared to wildtype protein, but its ability to bind to Sec31A was the weakest among the double mutants. We also determined if the binding of the Sec23A mutants toward Sar1 was affected in a similarly designed co-IP experiment. The Sec23A mutants were largely similar to the wildtype protein in binding to Sar1, with T405A as exception. Increased Sar1 binding was observed in this mutant. 3. To determine how phospho-Sec23 affects COPII vesicle budding in vitro. In this experiment, cytosol overexpressed with in the Sec23 mutants will be added to an in vitro COPII budding reaction based on the method developed by Kim and colleagues (JBC 280, 7758-68 (2005) and JCB 179, 951-63 (2007)). The amount of protein on the budded COPII vesicles was determined and compared among the Sec23 mutants. As shown in Figure 7, Sec23 S207D mutant seemed to have the strongest effect and inhibited COPII vesicle budding more than the other mutants tested. For reason we could not understand, S207D inhibited the amount of Sar1b on the budded vesicle more than other COPII coat subunits, such as Sec31A. We knew the quality of the Sar1b antibody was not very good and we were inclined to believe Sec31A signal was more indicative of the efficiency of COPII vesicle budding in this experiment. In this case, the amount of reduction caused by S207D mutant was approximately 30 % compared with wildtype Sec23. Therefore, this in vitro experiment did not accurately recapitulate the potential in vivo effect of the Sec23 mutants. Objective 4. To determine how phospho-Sec23 affects COPII vesicle formation and ER exit sites biogenesis in vivo. In this objective, we proposed to investigate the in vivo effect of Sec23 phosphorylation on COPII vesicle formation by fluorescence recovery after photo-bleaching (FRAP). Since we have identified S207 and T405 residues being important for ULK1 phospho-regulation, we overexpressed these mutants (and various combinations of the double mutants) and determine the fluorescence recovery of co-transfected GFP-Sec31, a subunit of outer layer of COPII vesicle coat. We found that the phospho-mimicking mutants of S207 (S207D) and T405 (T405D) could drastically reduce the fluorescence recovery of GFP-Sec31 after bleaching. Of note, the reduced fluorescence recovery was most obvious in the plateau phase of the recovery curve, i.e. the immobile fraction of the signal significantly increased. This result suggests that phosphorylation of S207 and T405 by ULK1 increases the association of Sec31 at the ER exit sites and this pool of Sec31 is not actively budding off COPII vesicle, and therefore, reduces transport of cargo proteins. In contrast to the phospho-mimicking mutants, the phospho-deficient mutants, S207A and T405A, only caused small reduction in the fluorescence recovery of GFP-Sec31 and such reduced recovery was due to slower half-time recovery in both cases. Of note, S207D and T405D double mutant did not cause further reduction of the GFP-Sec31 fluorescence recovery.

14118914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14118914.value: We initially discovered a protein interaction between the autophagy-activating kinase ULK1 and Sec23A and this interaction is subjected to regulation by the degree of autophagy in cells. With the funding support of RGC, we are able to elucidate ULK1 phosphorylates Sec23A at serine 207 and threonine 405. This biochemical event results in slow down of cargo transport at the ER-exit sites. This effect is supposed to be important for the cells to coordinate autophagy and general cellular secretion. During amino acid deprivation, the cells would like to conserve nutrients as much as possible, and therefore, it is advantageous to reduce secretion of proteins.

14118914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118914.value: COPII vesicle coat consists of Sec23/Sec24 dimer, and Sec13/Sec31 tetramer. In addition, Sec16 is also localized to the ER exit sites and essential to COPII vesicle formation. Sec16 has been shown to be phosphorylated by ULK1. In this project, we only concentrate on Sec23 as a substrate for ULK1. How ULK1 regulate COPII vesicle via both of its substrates, Sec23 and Sec16, has not been investigated. This aspect is a potential point for further development.

14118914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118914.value: This project studies two very important cellular processes, autophagy and exocytosis. When cells are under nutrient deprivation, they activate autophagy so that unfolded proteins and obsolete organelles are degraded; amino acids and lipids from the degradation process are recycled to ensure survival of the cells. Intuitively, secretion of proteins to the outside of the cells will have to stop in order to conserve amino acids under starved condition. The mechanism how autophagy reduces exocytosis is, at least in part, mediated by the phosphorylation of Sec23A by autophagy activating kinase ULK1. This project has identified Sec23A as a substrate of ULK1. ULK1 phosphorylates Sec23A at amino acids serine 207 and threonine 405 and cause accumulation of COPII vesicle coat proteins at the ER exit sites and block cargo proteins from exporting from ER. Overall, we have unraveled a mechanism of how autophagy regulates cellular secretion, and provided a new perspective on the inter-dependence between these processes.

14119214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119214.value: A remarkable and essential ability of human and other higher animals is the acquisition of novel motor skills that is essential for survival and daily lives. The loss of motor ability as well as the capability to learn new motor skills is highly disabling in some diseases, for example, Parkinson’s disease and ischemic brain disorders. The understanding of the neurobiological basis of how we acquire and retain new motor skills is not only a fundamental question in neuroscience but also has clinical implication and usefulness. Multiple brain areas, such as the well-studied cerebellum and basal ganglia, are likely involved in these processes. In addition to the role of movement control, there is recent emerging evidence that the primary motor cortex contribute directly to the formation of long-term memory of motor skills. However, many critical questions still remain regarding the nature and mechanism of motor engram formation in the motor cortex, and also the recall and retention of the memory trace. To gain insight into these processes, in a motor skill-learning model of rodent, our team will apply advanced techniques to probe directly the neural network in the primary motor cortex that encodes motor memory. Specifically, during the training of the animals, we will record and analyse the dynamics of activities from ensemble of neurons in different layers of the motor cortex. We will correlate our findings with the emergence and maintenance of training-induced synaptic plasticity in vivo. Finally, we will elucidate the mechanism of memory retention by examining the effect of dopamine, a neuromodulator that has been consistently implicated in the learning process. Our results will advance the understanding of how novel motor skills are learned and consolidated, and will also provide the cellular correlates of the impaired cortical plasticity and motor learning deficits observed in a number of common neurological disorders. 人類和其他高等動物擁有的一個重要並顯著的能力在於能夠學習新的運動技能以適應生存和生活需要。許多神經系統疾病將導致運動能力以及學習能力的喪失，當中包括帕金森氏病和缺血性腦中風。研究大腦如何通過學習獲得和保留新的運動技能不僅是神經科學領域的一個基本問題，也有十分重要的臨床意義和實用性。多個大腦區域，例如已被廣泛研究的小腦和基底神經節都可能參與了這個過程。此外，最新研究證據表明，初級運動皮層除了對運動的控制功能，還直接參與了運動技能長期記憶的形成。由於許多關鍵問題仍然未知，當中包括初級運動皮質如何編碼運動印跡的形成、回憶和保留。為了深入研究這些過程，我們的團隊將通過研究齧齒類動物的運動技能學習模式，運用先進的實驗技術直接探測編碼運動記憶的初級運動皮質的神經網路。具體來說，在動物的訓練過程中，我們將記錄、分析多個皮質亞層的神經元集群活動的動態變化，隨後研究神經元活動與經訓練誘導的突觸可塑性之間的相關性。最後，我們將闡明多巴胺如何影響訓練誘導的突觸可塑性，原因在於多巴胺作為一種重要的神經調節遞質，在多項學習行為範式中起了強化作用。本項研究結果將推進認識運動技能學習和鞏固過程的機制，同時也為一些在常見的神經系統疾病中觀察到的皮層可塑性受損和運動學習障礙等症狀提供相關的細胞學基礎。

14119214.label: Realisation of objectives
14119214.value: We have achieved the proposed 3 objectives fully, namely to apply in vivo recording to capture the electrophysiological characteristics of the primary motor cortex output neurons that encode motor memory, to elucidate the profiles of synaptic plasticity that underlie the motor learning process as well as determined the role of dopamine innervation originating from the midbrain. Major technical challenges, including the application of long-term in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the behaving animals, the tracking of training-induced long-term synaptic plasticity and the application of a variety of statistical and machine-learning techniques to analyse the data, have been met successfully by the team. The major results of the present proposal were published as a 19-page full paper in the high impact journal Nature Communications.

14119214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119214.value: The major findings are as follows: 1. Over days of training, a substantial proportion of layer 5b (L5b) neurons progressively changed from being non-informative about forelimb velocity and trajectory to possessing rich mutual information about motor behavioural outputs. 2. The decreased variance of these neurons during motor task execution with motor training suggests that they become engaged in circuitry encoding the forelimb reaching task only after learning. This increase in proportion of L5b neurons. 3. We have also identified the fine temporal scale of the refinement of motor coding, demonstrating a progressive shortening of the temporal lag on an order of tens of milliseconds with respect to peak mutual information. Therefore, apart from becoming more movement-encoding, task-recruited L5b neurons also become more time-locked to motor execution with a shorter time lag. 4. These changes were accompanied by an increase in the collective predictive power of motor output by recruited L5b neurons, as forelimb movement velocity and trajectory could be decoded from the population activity of these neurons accurately, signifying an improved encoding of motor movement. 5. Motor learning-induced changes were not only reflected in the reduced firing variance and increased information content of single neurons during motor task execution, but also in the joint neuronal firing statistics, as a task-specific, stable correlation structure emerged and persisted among recruited L5b neurons during training. 6.We also revealed that evoked field potential in L5b were potentiated in vivo during the process of motor training. Involvement of synaptic plasticity is further accentuated by the fact that in the absence of dopamine, long-term potentiation could not be maintained across days, suggesting resolving of newly potentiated synapses. Behaviourally, this manifests as repeated de-learning and re-learning of the motor task across days. Overall, we conclude that the emergence of a larger pool of task specific, movement encoding L5b neurons that exhibit more correlated, less variable firing, with shorter and less variable time lead preceding motor execution, as well as more reproducible population activity, may be the neural substrate underlying enhanced precision of forelimb movement, as they may help to generate more temporally synchronous or amplified output signal from M1 to downstream circuitry for more precise motor control and execution. This ability is critically dependent on the innervation from the midbrain ventral tegmental area.

14119214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119214.value: To address the mechanism of motor learning, in this study, we attempted to provide direct evidence for the involvement of synaptic reorganization in L5b neurons. We revealed that evoked field potential in L5b were potentiated in vivo during the process of motor training. The similarity between training-induced long-term potentiation and the performance of the animal in the motor task strongly implicates that the potentiation of synaptic inputs to L5b neurons contribute to the emergence of the motor memory, possibly among task-recruited neurons whose firing became phase-locked to evoked field potential. However, a very important question remains to be investigated is how the plasticity of the synaptic inputs from different sources, including cortical and subcortical that code different information, ultimately shapes the firing characteristics of L5b neurons. Solving this question will further advance out understanding of the general mechanism of emergent behaviour encoded by the cortex. Further grant proposal will be applied to address this fundamental neuroscience question.

14119214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119214.value: Motor skills are essential for all aspects of our daily life. It is well known that learning a new motor skill requires repeated practice. But how practising shapes our brain in controlling our motor system is a fundamental question in biomedical science that is still mysterious. This study employed sophisticated neurophysiological techniques to record activities from neurons in the motor cortex of experimental rats when they were trained to learn a novel motor skill, namely, a forelimb reach-for-food task. Statistical and machine-learning techniques were used to track and visualise the activities of the neurons, and revealed the process of emergent reproducible activities as a result of repeated practice. This study also revealed that the formation of motor memory is highly disrupted in the absence of dopamine in the motor cortex, a condition that could be present in Parkinson’s disease, explaining deficient motor learning in the disease.

14119814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119814.value: We have observed a clear correlation between chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation changes. Fruit-specific gene expression pattern is also associated with fruit-specific DHS and DMR. Intriguingly, we found that some DHSs and DMRs appeared in gene promoters during early stages of fruit development ahead of their gene expression. For example, the ripe fruit specific gene RIN contains promoter DHS and DMR in fruits as early as 17 day-post-anthesis, but not in the leaf tissue. However, the expression of RIN gene could only be detected after 38 day-post-anthesis. This suggests that chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation changes have already took place during the leaf to fruit transition. While open chromatin and de-methylation enables gene expression, transcription factors are still required to bind to these DHS to recruit mediator and PolII for transcription. We also analyzed the transcription factor binding motifs identified in those DHSs and attempt to establish the association between transcription factor gene expression and their potentially binding DHS, as well as their target gene expression.

14119814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119814.value: Based on the result of this GRF project, we are examining DNA methylation dynamics in additional plant species and profiled their chromatin accessibility.

14119814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119814.value: Tomato is a unique model system to study the epigenome reprograming during plant growth and development. No global demethylation event targeting non-transposon regions has been reported in other plant species so far. In this GRF project, we have examined the developmental dynamics of chromatin accessibility in the tomato genome using DNase-Seq in order to establish a link between the large number of DMRs and sudden change of transcriptional activity during tomato fruit development. We have now completed experiments as proposed. We have also carried out additional BS-Seq experiments to obtain higher genome coverage for differentially methylated region (DMR) identification, and we have done the association study (between DHS, DMR and gene expression) and found that chromatin accessibility change is associated with DNA methylation dynamics during fruit ripening. This is highly conserved in all 11 fruit species we examined.

14200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200114.value: We consider the problem of approximating multi-dimensional signals (typically, images, volumes or videos) on a basis of a uniformly shifted kernel function. It is known from approximation theory (Strang-Fix) that the ability of these shifted functions to reconstruct multi-dimensional polynomials up to degree L-1 ensures that the approximation error decreases as the L-th power of the sampling step used --- L-th approximation order property. In this research project, we propose to characterize the full class of multi-dimensional kernels with the smallest support that have a given approximation order. Within this class, we plan to identify the kernels that have the smallest approximation error. Finally, we also plan to derive computationally efficient interpolation and approximation algorithms which can be used in biomedical imaging applications, and more generally in visualization applications. 我們研究的問題是如何利用均勻移動核函數基來近似多維信號（例如圖像, 體積,視頻等）。由近似理論（Strang-Fix）可知，這些移動函數能夠可以重建最高L-1級的多維多項式, 這從而保證了近似誤差隨采樣間隔的L次冪遞減，即L階近似特性。 在本研究項目中，我們提出找到在給定近似階數下全部有最小支撐集的多維核函數。在這些函數中，進而找到給出最小估計誤差的核函數。最終，我們計劃得到能夠應用於生物醫學圖像且可推廣到可視化應用的高計算效率的插值及近似算法。

14200114.label: Realisation of objectives
14200114.value: All the objectives have been addressed and achieved: * 1. Characterization of the multidimensional approximation kernels that have minimal support for a given approximation order: we have been able to show that these functions are 2D piecewise polynomials and how they are related to spline functions. * 2. Find the minimal support kernels that yield the smallest appproximation error: we have been able to calculate several flavors of the two-dimensional kernels that are characterized by a maximal order and a minimal support. We have been able to demonstrate the gain in using these kernels, albeit non-separability comes at a higher computational cost. * 3. Develop efficient approximation algorithms that use minimal support kernels: in order to mitigate for the decrease in computational efficiency caused by non-separability, we have developed new algorithms that approximate the kernels as a small sum of separable kernels. We have been able to demonstrate that this approach allows efficient implementation of the approximation using 2D MOMS, making them competitive with classical separable kernels, while having significantly higher approximation quality. * 4. Validate an optical flow algorithms and various resampling schemes in medical imaging applications (CT and MRI): we have applied our new approximation schemes to a host of applications like PET-MRI registration, EEG topography interpolation, 3D PSF estimation, estimation of star locations in radioastronomy (2D Fourier interpolation). The main contributors to this project are: * Dr. Chris Gilliam, post-doc in my group between 2013 and 2017 * Dr. Ma Lan (PhD 2017 from CUHK) * Dr. Li Jizhou (PhD 2018 from CUHK) * Dr. Zafer Dogan (PhD 2015 from EPFL) * Dr. Pan Hanjie (PhD 2018 from EPFL) * Thomas Küstner (PhD student at the university of Stuttgart/Tübingen) I was supervisor of the two PhD students from CUHK and co-supervisor of the other two students from EPFL (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne). A new PhD student at CUHK, Xinxin Zhang, is working on a continuation of this project.

14200114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200114.value: The two-dimensional MOMS and the fast algorithmics used are involved in our main paper on image registration (journal paper #2), for which image approximation is a central issue. In particular, we were able to show how, using the optimal approximation techniques that we have developed in this project, the accuracy of the registration is significantly increased, while the computation cost has been kept as small as possible. We have recently shown that by performing a high-quality multidimensional approximation of the displacement field (in addition to the approximation involved in image warping), the registration algorithm that we have developed has become extremely robust to large displacements, significant noise corruption and intensity variations (conference paper #4) We have extended our approach to 3D volumes, an essential step in order to deal with real-life biomedical images (MRI, CT, PET, fluorescence microscopy). In that case, the approximation speed becomes really essential and we have successfully demonstrated highly accurate and fast registration of 3D MRI images (conference paper #2). A very nice follow-up of this research is a wide collaboration work with Thomas Küstner (PhD student at the university of Stuttgart/Tübingen), radiologists from the university of Tübingen, and researchers from the National Institute of Health and Medical Research (INSERM) in France, on the effect of the accurate registration of MRI 3D images of the heart/lungs, to correct for motion in PET images (journal paper #5, unfortunately no funding agencies are credited). Another, very different, successful demonstration of the accuracy of our approximation algorithms is a real application to radioastronomy (journal paper #4) where two-dimensional Fourier interpolation is used, together with sparse algorithms developed earlier (journal paper #1, conference paper #1), to extract the accurate positions of stars from large scale interferometric radio-frequency measurements. We also applied our approach to fluorescence microscopy and showed how, by combining Bessel functions and 2D OMOMS, it is possible to calculate very efficiently and accurately, the point-spread function of a wide-field microscope (journal paper #3). We have also shown how, when the parameters of the PSF are unknown, to estimate them from a distorted image by minimizing a criterion whose multidimensional shape is optimally approximated using the tools developed in this project (conference paper #3). Finally, we have also explored the problem of electrode 2D topography reconstruction from electro-encephalographic measurements, as a an optimal approximation problem for the purpose of source separation (conference paper #5).

14200114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200114.value: We are currently developing the image registration part in a direction that allows multimodal alignment (CT and MRI for instance), encouraged by our findings that approximating the displacement field on a 2D MOMS basis and more recently, approximating the local intensity relations between multimodal images using such a basis, leads to a very robust and accurate algorithm, while not sacrificing the computation speed. We have recently purchased a hyperspectral camera to generate our own set of multimodal images. In addition, we are developing a collaboration with Prince of Wales Hospital to facilitate the acquisition of image sequences under a specific MRI modality (T1rho), by estimating very accurately the motion (caused by breathing) between each repetition time, thereby ensuring much longer acquisition times than what is currently achievable when patients are required not to breathe.

14200114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200114.value: Being able to “see” between pixels is an essential ingredient in most applications of image processing, and in particular in medical imaging (e.g., Magnetic Resonance Imaging, nuclear imaging), biological imaging (microscopy), radioastronomy. The quality of the inter-pixel prediction is also critical to estimate the motion in image sequences accurately. This project investigates how to optimize this process, which is known as “image approximation”. We provide precise results regarding the best image approximation methods, and demonstrate their superior performance in various practical imaging applications.

14200414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200414.value: In most ball games, officiating errors are frequent. When such errors have a direct impact on the outcome of a game, they bring unfairness to players and frustration to viewers. Major causes of these errors are the high speed of balls and occlusion of the balls by players. Therefore, instant review systems have become increasingly indispensable in many sports. They have been accepted by governing bodies in tennis, cricket, football and volley ball as a mean of adjudication. Badminton is very popular especially in Asia. There are over 120 tournaments listed in the tournament calendar of Badminton World Federation (BWF) in 2013. Badminton is a fast game. The official record of the fastest shuttlecock speed is 332 km/hour. Officiating errors are frequent in badminton games. The BWF planned to use an instant review system as a mean of adjudication in Djarum Indonesia Open in June 2013. However, BWF withdrew the plan at the last minute and decided to undertake more tests. Whilst camera-based technology is very successful and widely used in tennis tournaments for instant review, it faces a number of new challenges in badminton games. Firstly, occlusion of the shuttlecock by players is much more frequent in a badminton game than in a tennis game because the size of a badminton court is about a quarter of that of a tennis court. Secondly, a shuttlecock is not a spherical object. Its pose changes in the flight and so does its appearance. Estimation of the impact area that a shuttlecock makes with the court during the bounce phase is difficult. These problems can be alleviated by using many cameras of very high frame rates and high resolutions, which however are expensive. Moreover, this also means higher computation requirements which make real-time implementation difficult. At present, there are no academic work published on badminton officiation. We propose to develop algorithms to overcome the difficulties and an architecture to integrate the algorithms together to form a real-time and robust officiating system for badminton games. The proposed system uses 16 video cameras which cost about US$70K in total and our goal is to achieve an accuracy to within 3 mm which is better than the Hawk-eye system for tennis, which is accurate to within 5 mm. We believe the project will advance our understanding of the problems in badminton officiation. The results will help improve the accuracy and make computer officiation more affordable. 很多球類比賽經常有頻密的裁決錯誤。錯誤通常是由於球速太高，或者球員阻擋了裁判視線。當錯誤裁決影響了勝負，觀眾會感到沮喪，對球員也不公平。因此，電腦即時裁決系統已經成為許多運動比賽不可或缺的一部份。即時裁決系統亦獲得網球、板球、足球和排球的理事機構在正式比賽中採用。 羽毛球運動非常受歡迎，尤其是在亞洲。羽毛球世界聯合會2013年的比賽日曆列出了超過120場正式比賽。羽毛球是一個高速的運動，羽毛球最快的飛行時速官方記錄是332公里。因此，羽毛球比賽經常有裁決錯誤。羽毛球世界聯合會計畫在2013年6月印尼公開賽時使用電腦即時裁決系統，但在最後一刻撤回計畫，決定先做更多測試。雖然基於攝像機的電腦即時裁決技術在網球比賽中非常成功，獲廣泛使用。它在羽毛球比賽中要解決多個新挑戰。首先，裁判視線受球員阻擋的情況更加頻繁，因為羽毛球場大約只是網球場四分之一大。其次，羽毛球不是一個圓球，所以羽毛球飛行中的外觀會隨觀看角度的變化而變化。羽毛球落地的位置亦很難準確估測。使用多部高幀率和高解析度的攝像機能緩解這些問題，但亦會大幅增加裁決系統的成本。此外，這也意味著電腦裁決系統需要更高的計算要求，令即時電腦裁決更難實現。 現時有關羽毛球裁決的學術研究欠缺。我們在本研究計劃建議開發多個演算法克服上述的挑戰，並開發一個系統結構，將這些演算法連結組合成一個即時和穩健的羽毛球比賽裁決系統。擬議的系統使用16部成本約七萬美元的視頻攝像機。我們的目標精確度是3毫米。目前網球鷹眼系統的精確度是5毫米。在羽毛球比賽中使用電腦裁決要面對很多問題，本研究計劃將提高大家對這些問題的理解。研究結果將有助提高羽毛球比賽裁決的精確度，使電腦裁決更經濟更普及。

14200414.label: Realisation of objectives
14200414.value: We have achieved all four objectives stated in section 5.2. In the original plan, we propose to estimate 2D tracks captured by different cameras of a flying shuttlecock (objective 2), which are then used to estimate the 3D trajectory (objectives 3 and 4). We tested the layered data association method originally designed for tracking a tennis ball on the badminton games video clips. The layered data association method cannot maintain good performance when there are occlusion and significant blurring. Our investigation shows that it is more effective to combine objectives 2, 3 and 4 together using a 3D shuttlecock trajectory model as a prior to estimate 2D track of a shuttlecock. The 3D trajectory does not need to be very precise. However, a fast and effective algorithm is needed to estimate the 3D trajectory so that the estimated 3D trajectory information can be obtained for estimation of the 2D tracks. A 3D trajectory is determined by four parameters which are initial speed and three flight angles. We quantized these parameters and created a trajectory table which relates 3D shuttlecock trajectories to 2D tracks. Four consecutive frames from each camera are used to generate shuttlecock candidates using layered data association. The trajectory table is then used to help estimate the most likely candidate in each frame. This approach allows our tracker to estimate the 3D trajectory of a shuttlecock as well as its 2D track captured by each camera at about 50 frames per second on an i7 machine. Hence the tracker can track a shuttlecock in real-time. We first extracted the boundary lines of a badminton court in each frame, which are used to obtain parameters needed for the conversion between 3D to 2D data. The additional 2D trajectory information derived from the 3D shuttlecock trajectory model is used together with the layered data association method to track a shuttlecock. A test dataset which contains video clips of badminton games taken from different angles was created. We have manually labelled the true shuttlecock location in each frame of the video sequences in the test database. We have carried out experiments to compare our tracker with existing trackers. Experimental results show that our tracker have the highest average successful rate which is 94.3%. When there are occlusion, hitting by rackets and significant blurring, all other existing trackers fail with successful rates below 5%. Our tacker can maintain reasonable successful rates at 92.6%, 70.4% and 89.7% for occlusion, hitting by rackets and significant blurring respectively. The 3D trajectory obtained using our tracker is not very precise. Hence, we consider we have only achieved 80% of objective 4. More explanation of the trajectory estimation is given in section 6.1. Experimental results, test video sequences and the program can be found at https://visiondk.com/zshuang/ .

14200414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200414.value: 6.1 Major findings and research outcome (maximum 400 words; please make reference to Part C where necessary) Our investigation shows that it is more effective to combine estimation of 2D shuttlecock track and its 3D trajectory together. A fast and effective algorithm is needed to estimate the 3D trajectory so that the estimated 3D trajectory information can be obtained for estimation of the 2D tracks. A 3D trajectory is determined by four parameters which are the initial speed and three flight angles of a shuttlecock. We quantized these parameters and created a trajectory table which relates 3D shuttlecock trajectories to their 2D tracks. Four consecutive frames from each camera are used to generate shuttlecock candidates using layered data association. The trajectory table is then used to help estimate the most likely candidate in each frame. However, the 3D trajectory thus obtained is not very precise. That is the reason we consider we have only achieved 80% of objective 4. In actual implementation we can increase the accuracy of the 3D trajectory by using finer quantization of the 4 parameters but that will increase the table size and so the computation time of the 3D trajectory and 2D track. In addition to the coarse quantization of the 4 parameters, the low accuracy is also due to the fact that each tracker camera needs to cover the whole badminton court. The work was reported in the following two papers. Huang, Z., Cham, W.K., 'A Novel Algorithm For Shuttlecock Tracking,' Proceedings of Asia-Pacific Signal and Information Processing Association (APSIPA) Annual Summit and Conference 2015, Hong Kong, Dec 16-19, 2015, pp.346-349. Huang, Z., Cham, W.K., 'Realtime Shuttlecock Tracking Using Scene Context' submitted to The Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation (Reference number JVCI-17-592).

14200414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200414.value: The shuttlecock tracker can track a shuttlecock in real-time with satisfying successful rate. The accuracy of the 3D trajectory obtained by the tracker is not high. However, we believe this shuttlecock tracker is sufficient to be used in a badminton officiating system. In a badminton officiating system, there are high-speed bounce-phase video cameras which are to capture the moment when a shuttlecock hits the ground. The officiating decision will be determined mainly by information provided by these bounce-phase video cameras. The coarse 3D trajectory estimated by our tracker provides initial conditions (speed and angle) for the computation of an accurate 3D trajectory estimated based on video data from the high-speed bounce-phase video cameras. The coarse 3D trajectory is also useful in providing augmented reality which enhances viewer’s understanding and experience of a badminton game.

14200614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200614.value: Network coding (NC) has recently become a new and popular research area in both communication theory and wireless communications. It offers potential improvement in system throughput and robustness. It features linear combinations of more than one input data streams to share the same communication link, and thus reduces the required system resources. To realize network coding in practical wireless communication networks, physical-layer network coding (PNC) has been introduced to enhance the throughput in wireless full-duplex relay channels by simply adding up the power of the two electromagnetic radio waves at the relay node. However, there have been few efforts in exploring applications of PNC in optical systems, due to the relatively more complicated optical signal processing required and more stringent requirement in optical signal synchronization, in order to realize the linear combinations of the multiple high-speed optical signal streams. Although optical transmission offers high capacity communication, it is still very desirable to have effective means to further enhance the system throughput, especially if the optical networks have only limited number of optical links. With the recent advances in high-speed electronic digital signal processing, instead of using all-optical techniques to perform high-speed signal logic operation to realize all-optical NC, we can simply perform optical power addition of the optical signals at the optical node, whilst the complicated signal processing of PNC signal decoding can be performed in electronic domain at the receiver side. Only single optical receiver is needed to detect and separate the two independent optical data streams. The stringent signal synchronization of the optical signal streams can be further alleviated by proper design of the signal formats and the decoding algorithms at the receiver. Hence, the feasibility and practicality of applying PNC in optical systems can be greatly enhanced. With the advantages offered by PNC, the system efficiency of optical systems can be further enhanced. In this project, we will investigate the signal processing techniques to perform PNC on two high-speed optical signal streams, and the related enabling techniques, including the signal format design to facilitate optical channel estimation, different advanced signal modulation formats, impacts from optical impairments, direct and coherent detection schemes, etc. After these basic functionalities of PNC have been characterized in optical systems, we will further investigate its performance in practical optical systems in which the number of available optical links is usually limited and thus can take good advantage of PNC to enhance the system throughput. 網絡編碼（NC）是一個在通信理論和無線通信領域中頗嶄新的研究課題，它提供了系統吞吐量的改進。它設有多個輸入數據流的線性組合，以共享相同的通信鏈路，從而降低了所需的系統資源。在無線通信網絡中，物理層網絡編碼（PNC）亦已大大提高無線全雙工中繼信道的吞吐量。然而，在高速光通信領域中，光學信號的處理相對較複雜和更嚴格，但為了進一步提高了系統的吞吐量，仍是值得探索PNC在光通信領域中的應用。隨著近年的進步，光信號只需的在光節點執行光功率相加，然而較複雜PNC信號解碼步驟可以在單個光接收器檢測後用高速電子數字信號處理器進行，這樣就可實現檢測和分離兩個獨立的光學數據流，而且光信號流的嚴格信號同步可以通過信號格式和解碼算法的優化設計以進一步減輕。因此，PNC在高速光通信系統中的可行性和實用性便可大大提高。在這個項目中，我們將研究多種對於高速光信號流的信號處理技術，包括信號格式的設計，光學信道估計，和相關的性能優化技術，以實現PNC在高速光通信領域的應用，及進一步提高光網絡在有限信道的情況下的吞吐量和性能。

14200614.label: Realisation of objectives
14200614.value: In this project, we have explored the applications of physical layer network coding (PNC) technique in optical fiber transmission so as to improve the system throughput in high-speed optical links. Two input optical signals are simply optically combined at the intermediate network node so as to share the same output fiber link, and let the destined nodes do the signal separation and recovery process, via electronic digital processing algorithms. First, we have investigated the performance of PNC techniques for two optical signals in optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) format in an optical multicast topology while coherent detection is adopted at the receiver end. A simple pilot subcarrier-aided approach has been employed to realize channel estimation and compensate both common phase errors, and carrier frequency offset, via digital signal processing algorithms. System performance of individual recovered optical signals have been experimentally characterized to confirm the feasibility of application of PNC in high-speed coherent optical system. In addition, we have also investigated the case of optically-combining two optical Nyquist polarization-multiplexed QPSK signals with complete spectral overlap, under variable bandwidth situations. By proper signal power control, the individual signals could be separated and properly recovered by digital processing techniques. The stronger optical signal was decoded first from the spectrally overlapped composite signal. The relatively weaker optical signal could then be recovered subtracting the recovered strong signal from the spectrally overlapped composite signal. The performance have been experimentally characterized. The impacts of the time offset and the relative polarization state to the system have also been carefully characterized. The above works have addressed the project objectives 1 and 2. To address project objective 3, we have investigated the application of PNC in some practical optical systems. For example, we have considered to apply PNC to simultaneously support wired and wireless virtual private network (VPN) in a radio-on-fiber (RoF) type OFDM passive optical network (PON). This enhanced much flexible configuration of full-duplex VPN in hybrid fiber-wireless systems and also brought a considerable throughput improvement. The performance of PNC in both wired VPN and wireless VPN have been experimentally characterized to confirm the feasibility. Moreover, we have investigated the application of PNC techniques in a visible light communication (VLC) link and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is adopted in which multiple wireless users transmit their optical signals to a common receiver, simultaneously. This resulted in an overlapped (non-orthogonal) optical signal at the receiver where the two individual signals were decoded and separated using multi-user detection techniques. Such scenario was very similar to PNC. In view of the stringent relative power ratio requirement among all the input signals in NOMA, we have proposed a novel yet simple phase pre-distortion technique which could greatly relax such stringent input power ratio requirement, thus could greatly enhance the practicality of the NOMA or PNC in VLC links. We have performed both numerical simulation study and experimental characterization to prove the concept. The experimental results have shown great performance improvement. We have further applied a multi-carrier precoding technique, based on orthogonal circulant matrix transform to equalize the signal-to-noise ratios of all the subcarriers in the OFDM signals under NOMA. The results have shown satisfactory performance improvement. Furthermore, we have proposed and investigated the phase pre-distorted joint-detection of VLC signals under NOMA. Experimental results have showed that the proposed detection method outperforms the conventional successive interference cancellation method and it works well under the cases of low, medium, and high power ratios. Finally, we have applied the PNC technique in a passive optical interconnect architecture for datacenter networks and significant improvement in packet delay especially under high traffic load was achieved.

14200614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200614.value: In this project, we have explored the applications of physical layer network coding (PNC) technique in optical fiber transmission so as to improve the system throughput in high-speed optical links. First, we have investigated the performance of PNC techniques for two optical signals in optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) format in an optical multicast topology. The system performance of individual recovered optical signals have been experimentally characterized and published in a journal paper [C8-1]. The results confirmed the feasibility of PNC scheme in optical systems. Second, we have investigated the case of optically-combining two optical Nyquist polarization-multiplexed QPSK signals with complete spectral overlap under variable bandwidth situations [C9-2 & C9-4]. By proper signal power control, the stronger optical signal was decoded first from the spectrally overlapped composite signal while the relatively weaker optical signal could then be recovered by subtracting the recovered strong signal from the spectrally overlapped composite signal. We have also investigated the application of PNC in a number of practical optical systems. One of them was to apply PNC to support wired and wireless virtual private network (VPN) in a radio-on-fiber (RoF) type OFDM passive optical network (PON) [C9-1] to gain considerable throughput improvement. Another one was a visible light communication (VLC) link and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) was adopted to let multiple wireless users transmit their optical signals to a common receiver, simultaneously. The received overlapped signal was decoded to separate the individual ones using multi-user detection techniques. We have proposed a phase pre-distortion technique [C9-5, C8-2] to relax the stringent input power ratio requirement, thus enhanced the practicality of the NOMA in VLC links. Further proposals of digital signal processing based on a multi-carrier precoding technique with an orthogonal circulant matrix transform [C9-3] to equalize the signal-to-noise ratios of all the subcarriers of OFDM signals under NOMA, as well as a joint-detection scheme [C8-3] which outperformed the conventional successive interference cancellation method, were investigated and shown good feasibility and performance enhancement. Finally, we have applied the PNC technique in a passive optical interconnect architecture for datacenter networks [C8-4] and significant improvement in packet delay especially under high traffic load was achieved.

14200614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200614.value: The main challenge of applying PNC technique to optical system is the complexity of the digital signal processing required to decode and retrieve the individual signals from an overlapped composite one. The synchronization issue among the input signals and their input signal qualities definitely affect the performance of the signal decoding. Therefore, further pilot signals may be inserted to the signals so as to facilitate the signal quality compensation as well as the effectiveness of the decoding processing with reduced possible power penalty. In additional, the signal decoding scheme is mostly for separating two combined signals. If the system has to support more than two users in this application, the complexity of the digital decoding processing would increase drastically. Therefore, feasible transmission multiple access schemes may be further explored so as to support pairwise signal processing while more users can be supported in the system. More investigations have yet to be performed to enhance the scalability of the PNC technique in optical systems.

14200614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200614.value: Physical-layer network coding (PNC) has been introduced in wireless communication area so as to enhance the system throughput in wireless full-duplex relay channels by simply adding up the power of the two electromagnetic radio waves at the relay node. This project aims to explore applications of PNC in optical systems, in which high system capacity can be achieved. In this project, we have investigate the signal processing techniques to perform PNC on two high-speed optical signal streams, and the related enabling techniques, including the signal format design to facilitate optical channel estimation, multi-user signal detection techniques, the issue of signal synchronization, different advanced signal modulation formats, impacts from optical impairments, direct and coherent detection schemes, etc. The investigations were carried out through numerical simulations and experiments with system characterizations. In addition, we have investigated the applications of PNC techniques in some practical optical systems, including radio-over fiber systems, visible light communication systems and data center interconnection networks.

14200714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200714.value: Problems concerning a network often involves a link model that describes how nodes are interconnected. The classic network coding problem, for instance, models the communication channels as edges in a graph and so graph-theoretic results such as the max-flow min-cut theorem can be applied to characterize the maximum throughput. We are interested in more complicated interconnections that may not be adequately captured by graphs, such as the correlation in a distributed random source and the broadcast and interference of signals over a wireless network. There were preliminary results that extend the max-flow min-cut theorem to those cases. In particular, we have formulated a general link model using matroids and linking systems, and discovered meaningful notions of paths and flows that generalizes Menger's theorem and the Ford-Fulkerson algorithm. Under the matroidal framework, we also extended the notion of partition connectivity from tree packing to mutual information for multiple random variables, which is applicable to undirected network coding, secret key agreement and data exchange problems. We propose to investigate other related graph-theoretic results and see whether they can be extended using the new framework. One concrete idea is to consider fractional flows using polylinking systems and extend the more efficient push-relabel algorithms for computing the maximum flow. 一個網絡的問題往往涉及到一個描述節點如何相互關聯的模型。例如在經典的網絡編碼問題裡，通信的信道會以圖的邊來表示，一些圖論的結果如最大流最小割定理可應用於計算最大的組播速率。我們感興趣的是一些無法通過圖來表示的複雜互連，如在分佈式隨機源上的相關性和在無線網絡上的信號廣播和干擾。初步的結果發現，對於這種複雜的互連情況，最大流最小割定理仍能被擴展。我們制定了一套採用擬陣來描述的網絡鏈路模型，並發現推廣路徑和流的方法，用以擴展Menger's定理和Ford-Fulkerson演算法。利用這個擬陣的理论，我們還把樹包裝的連通概念擴展到多個隨機變量的互信息，應用於無向網絡編碼，秘密密鑰協議和數據交換的問題。我們計劃研究和推廣其他相關的圖論結果，例如用polylinking system來推廣分數流和計算最大流的push-relabel演算法。

14200714.label: Realisation of objectives
14200714.value: Overall, both objectives have been achieved to a significant extent, resulting in 7 journal publications and 14 conference publications. The first objective of the project is to obtain fundamental results relating matroid theory and information flows. To achieve this objective, we studied various abstract mathematical structures in submodular function optimization techniques and attempted to give meaningful information-theoretic interpretations of those abstract structures. This approach has been very fruitful, leading to various new concepts and applications. We were able to relate the measure of multivariate mutual information to Dilworth Truncation, principle sequence of partitions (PSP), and the principle sequence (PS). These results have been published in renowned journals, including the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, and the Proceedings of IEEE. We have also conveyed our results in conferences or through emails to the researchers who first studied multiterminal secrecy capacity (Prof. P. Narayan), PSP (Prof. H. Narayanan), and PS (Prof. S. Fujishige). The feedbacks are very positive. The second objective of the project is to construct efficient algorithms for computing the maximum flow and decomposing the flow into disjoint paths. To achieve this objective, we have studied and implemented both the submodular function minimization and max-flow min-cut algorithms for the computation of the multivariate mutual information. Due to the complexity of the algorithms, we have extended the project duration for half a year to complete the implementation. Preliminary versions of the software have been released and are now available as public GitHub repositories. The algorithms have been presented in conferences such as the well-recognized IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory. I have also presented the results during research visits to renowned universities, including Massachusetts Institute of Technology, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, National University of Singapore, and Nanyang Technological University.

14200714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200714.value: Inspired by the capacity for multiterminal secret key agreement, we proposed a multivariate information measure, called multivariate mutual information (MMI)[J2], that generalizes Shannon's mutual information from two random variables to multiple random variables. Using the submodular function optimization techniques, we proved that the MMI provides an alternative characterization of the secrecy capacity in the important no-helper case. This established a concrete operational meaning of the MMI as the secrecy capacity, much like the way Shannon's mutual information was shown to characterize the channel capacity. We further clarified its connections to some combinatorial structures, namely the Dilworth Truncation, principal sequence of partitions, and the principal sequences. This connections not only enrich these combinatorial structures with information-theoretic interpretations but also substantiate that the MMI can be computed in strongly polynomial time, unlike many other multivariate information measures. We also derived various fundamental properties of the MMI, including the well-known data processing inequality. With these properties, we can solve other information theory problems, such as successive omniscience[J1], data exchange[J4], and secret key agreement[J3,J5]. While the MMI can be used to solve other related problems in information theory, it is also useful in machine learning. We formulated an information-theoretic paradigm based on the MMI for data clustering, referred to as the info-clustering[J7]. Our info-clustering not only subsumes some existing solutions as special cases[C5], but it also inspires new computationally meaningful solutions. We have implemented algorithms containing the submodular function minimization to obtain the info-clustering solution[C8]. We realized that, for these algorithms to be useful, they should be specialized to solve practical problems. One of the promising reductions is to consider the graphical models. Under this model, we found that the computation can be improved by using a parametric max-flow min-cut algorithm[C11]. The algorithm has been implemented and is ready to apply to applications like large-scale social networks.

14200714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200714.value: While we have derived some important properties of the MMI, it is worthwhile to explore further. Discovering new properties may help us resolve other open problems in information theory. This can be done via studying some related combinatorial structures like principal partitions and submodular function optimization. It is also worthwhile to investigate our info-clustering framework when there is estimation error or dynamic change in the graphical models. This can be done by studying the robustness and adaptiveness of the max-flow min-cut algorithm.

14200714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200714.value: We proposed a multivariate mutual information measure and characterized its operational meaning and fundamental properties. This measure turns out to be useful not only in solving related information theory problems but also in formulating an info-clustering paradigm for data clustering in machine learning. One of the promising applications is to find clusters in large-scale social networks using the max-flow min-cut algorithm.

14200814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200814.value: Causal discovery has become a research area that is gaining more attention recently. It is a particular type of knowledge discovery method that uncovers the hidden causal relation among variables. With the availability of massive data in different disciplines, there is a need to extend the current causal discovery methodologies to cope with large data sets. The massive of data does not only refer to the increase in the number of sample records but also the number of attributes in the databases. This project intends to address the problem of causal discovery with lots of variables and is motivated by some characteristics of causal diagrams. Existing causal discovery algorithms are mostly efficient when the number of variables is reasonable. With the increase in the number of variables in the causal diagram, the connectivity of the nodes usually remains small unless the variables are defined in such a way that their natures are all related. Specifically, some variables are intrinsically different from others, while some are not. Because of this, it is possible for us to design some strategies to divide or combine variables when we perform causal discovery with large number of variables. Some variables may be combined to form groups of variable such that we only need to unveil the causal relationship among variable groups. Some variables may form causal sub-graphs if they are less likely to be related to variables in other sub-groups. So that it is more efficient to apply causal discovery algorithms to each sub-graph before we merge them back to form the whole causal structure involving all variables. This project intends to develop a framework for causal discovery through data groupings. Data partition or combination strategies would be investigated and tested. These strategies will consider the issue of latent confounding variables such that the presence of hidden common causes to some subsets of variables would be detected and identified. Latent confounders are common in many real data sets but unfortunately many current causal discovery methods assume that there is no latent confounder in the domain. The combination of some variables would modify the original form into high dimensional super variables for causal discovery. Therefore, this causal discovery framework would also include the study of efficient algorithms that can deal with high dimensional data.

14200814.label: Realisation of objectives
14200814.value: This project intends to study causal discovery methodologies with large datasets. We have studied and identified a few research issues for this topic. Solutions have been proposed and published. There are some typical assumptions we have made in causal discovery may not be held in some real datasets due to the fact that the data may be collected over a period of time or from a number of channels. For the former case when data is collected over a period of time, the distribution of the cause may change alone with time and hence the typical assumption that both the distribution of the cause is fixed is violated. For the latter case when the data are collected from a number of channels, the basic principle behind the cause mechanism is the same. However, there may have some slight variations in terms of the exact parameters involved in the causal mechanism. Thus, the causal mechanisms may not be homogeneous as in the case of small datasets, even though the causal direction are consistent for all observations. Given that there have some small variations in the distribution of the cause and causal mechanisms, traditional causal discovery methodologies may fail. Thus, for objective 1, instead of applying simple divide and conquer approach, the framework we propose in this project is focusing on the change in the distribution of the cause and the causal mechanism. This approach enables us to handle observations that are either collected from multiple sources or through a long period of time that leads to the non-stationary property of the observed data. For objective 2, following the results from objective 1, we have made a number of proposed methods for addressing the issues. First, we proposed a causal mixture model based on additive noise model. This mixture model combines a number of causal mechanisms driving the observed data. The idea is that the causal system composes of a set of causal models of the same causal direction. Each causal model has its own set of parameters and the difficulty arises when we do not know both the parameters and the identity of the model that each observation falls into. We proposed the Gaussian process partially observable model and incorporate Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion for estimating the model parameters. Second, we proposed a non-stationary causal model inference method called ENCI (embedding-based non-stationary causal model inference). We assume that the entire data set consists of a number of data groups and we make use of the variation of marginal and conditional densities in each group. The variation is related to the mean of marginal densities and conditional densities of all groups and thus we decompose the densities into two parts; the base and the variation. Kernel embedding is adopted to transform them into a linear model and then causal direction is inferred by exploiting the causal asymmetry of the obtained linear model. For objective 3 related to high dimensional data, direct estimation of the data distributions become very difficult and we have to use different approaches which do not require any density estimation. We have proposed two approaches; one is the method using the freeness condition and the other one is based on spectral measures. The first approach follows the line of using Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space embeddings. Instead of calculating the complexity metric as in other methods, we use the independence between the covariance matrices of the cause and the mechanism. The freeness condition, which is the covariance matrices of the RKHS embedding of the distribution of the cause is free independent with the covariance matrix of the RKHS embeddings of the distribution of the effect given the cause. Typically, we assume that there is no confounder between the cause and effect variables. Most existing causal methods would fail to work if there is any confounder as the confounder violates some required assumptions. The second method we proposed is able to detect if there is a confounder between the observations and also to identify the causal mechanism between them. We compare the first moment of the regression vector induced spectral measure with the first moment of a uniform reference measure. The confounder is inferred by the causal-confounding asymmetry that the two moments coincide in causal cases while differ in confounder cases. We have also provided theoretical analysis to show that the confounder identifiable. For objective 4, real datasets have been applied to test our proposed methods of the mixture additive noise model, ENCI, the freeness condition-based inference method and the spectral-based method using real benchmark datasets. Hong Kong Stock Market data has been used to form a causal graph. A small sample of the results have been published. We consider that objective 4 have been achieved although there are rooms for improvements. It would be more desirable to seek for proprietary datasets from some companies. As our primary aim is to investigate and demonstrate the viability of our approaches and to publish our research findings, we use a conservative approach to achieve our objectives. A difficulty we encountered in this project is the recruitment of postgraduate students. Offers were made but the students declined the offer in the last minute. Luckily, I could deploy graduate students supported by the general fund to do research work for this project.
