14200814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200814.value: We have published three journal papers and one conference paper in this project. The conference paper with the title of "Causal Inference and Mechanism Clustering of a mixture of additive noise models. It describes the mixture of additive noise model which has addressed the objectives 1 and 2 in this project. It is published in NIPS which is a highly reputable conference with low acceptance rate. It describes the framework, algorithm, results and analysis of the causal model we proposed. Our proposed method addresses the issue for combining observations from multiple sources such that the mechanisms behind each source may have some variations. Three journal papers are published in reputable journals. The first journal paper is under the title of "A Kernel Embedding–Based Approach for Nonstationary Causal Model Inference" is published in Neural Computation. This paper introduces a non-stationary causal model and develop algorithms for inferring the complete causal relations of the model which is related to objective 2. The approach we proposed aims at combining data sources such that the data distribution of each source varies. This work is a direct outcome of this project but we have omitted the acknowledgement due to careless mistake. The second journal paper is under the title of "Causal Inference on Multidimensional Data Using Free Probability Theory" and is published in IEEE transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems. The third paper is under the title of "Confounder Detection in High-Dimensional Linear Models Using First Moments of Spectral Measures" is published in Neural Computation. Both the second and third journal papers are related to objective 3. We consider the handling of high dimensional data. A novel condition based on the freeness condition is proposed in the third paper. The fourth on further addresses the issue of detecting confounders. Absence of any confounder is a typical assumption researchers often made in causal discovery. This assumption could easily be violated in large datasets. Examples using real datasets are included in the above publication and they include stock data in finance and sociological data from general surveys. We have acknowledged the support of RGC in these papers. The project code is not included and this project is the only one that the PI is supported by RGC at the time of publication.

14200814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200814.value: We have successfully proposed a couple of novel causal inference approaches. These methods address the emerging issues in causal discovery, especially that we have relaxed some assumptions researchers typically made in small datasets. We have been focusing on the issues of mixture mechanisms and non-stationary data which are highly relevant to real and large datasets in causal discovery. Although we have applied and tested our methods using real data sets, they are mainly for the purpose of testing the algorithms and demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed methods. We would like to further investigate more potential use of our methods on other real datasets. Our datasets are mostly public available datasets. Further collaboration with companies or institutions who hold some interesting datasets would help us to demonstrate the effectiveness of the outcomes of this project. This would also great potential benefits to them as we could provide technological skills to analyze the causal relationship of their data.

14200814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200814.value: The project has investigated and proposed some novel, effective and efficient algorithms for causal discovery in large datasets. Given the observed data, we aim at finding the causal relationship among the variables. Differ from other existing approaches, we do not assume the data are homogeneous which is a typical assumption made in other causal discovery approaches for handling small datasets. We consider that it is possible to have some variations in the data distribution and as well as the causal mechanism behind them. Our investigation also includes the cases when the observations are high dimensional. Currently, there are very few current research works in causal analysis attempting to address the issue of confounders. We consider the case that there may exist some confounders among the high dimensional variables and we provide methods to detect the existence of the confounders.

14200914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200914.value: We request support for the research on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based coherent burst-mode receivers (BMRs) for high-speed and smart optical packet networks (OPNs). The remarkable growth of Internet traffic has translated into a demand for high-capacity and flexible optical systems and networks. Recent technological innovations in spectrally-efficient modulation and multiplexing schemes and digital coherent detection have enabled point-to-point links to approach information limit at low cost and with low power consumption. Simultaneously, flexible optical networking is widely advocated today by major vendors and operators to optimize the use of network resources. Wavelength-tunable OPNs, where data are carried in packets or bursts and the wavelengths of transmitters/receivers are tunable to select the desired wavelength channel with sub-wavelength granularity, are promising to realize overall resource optimization. Coherent BMR is one of the key elements in OPNs. BMRs based on advanced single-carrier formats, such as quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK), have been widely investigated in the literature. However, the investigation of multi-carrier format based coherent BMRs has not been well established. In this project, we will investigate OFDM-based BMRs, by using the expertise gained through our previous works on direct-detection BMRs, digital impairment (including carrier frequency offset) compensation for single-carrier formats, and our preliminary studies on fast channel estimation, synchronization, and carrier frequency offset estimation for continuous-mode OFDM. We will systematically investigate the design of OFDM-based coherent BMRs, from the development of algorithms for compensating one or more impairments at the receivers to combining these algorithms efficiently for OPN applications, by taking into account the transient characteristics of tunable lasers. The former focuses on fast convergence, short overhead, and high performance, while the latter examines the validity of individual algorithms in the presence of other impairments (in particular, the transient characteristics during wavelength tuning) and aims to identify the optimal way to rapidly compensate all relevant impairments in BMRs, in-sequence or jointly, with minimized complexity to realize overall subsystem optimization. This proposal aligns with the current R&D strategic direction for next-generation high-capacity and flexible optical networks, which exploit the recent availability of high-speed microelectronics, and simultaneously addresses the problems of capacity crunch, network flexibility, and overall resource optimization. The work also strategically enhances the research collaborations internally and with an overseas research institute, Tyndall National Institute Ireland, for the development of smart and evolvable optical networks. 互聯網流量的飛速增長，已轉化為對高容量和靈活的光通信系統和網絡的需求。近年來，在高頻譜效率的調製和複用方案及數字相干檢測方面的技術創新，使得點對點鏈路在低成本和低能耗的條件下臨近信息容量的極限。同時，現今大多數廠商和運營商廣泛採用靈活的光網絡以優化網絡資源的使用。在波長可調的光包交換網絡中，數據以封包或突發的形式傳送，收發機可以在子波長粒度調節以選擇合適的信道波長，從而實現了整體資源的優化。相干突發模式光接收機是光包交換網絡的關鍵要素之一。基於單載波的先進調製格式，例如正交相移鍵控（QPSK）的突發模式光接收機已經被廣泛地研究。然而對基於多載波調製格式的相干突發模式光接收機的研究尚未完善。 在本項目中，基於我們之前在直接檢測突發模式光接收機和單載波調製格式損傷（包括載波頻偏）數字補償的研究成果，以及對線路交換模式正交頻分複用（OFDM）的快速信道估計、同步和載波頻偏估計的前期研究，我們將研究基於正交頻分複用的突發模式光接收機。我們將系統研究基於正交頻分複用相干突發模式光接收機的設計，從開發接收機的算法以補償一種或多種損傷，到有效結合這些算法以應用在光包交換網絡中，這些算法將考慮到可調激光器的瞬態特性。前者著重於快速收斂、短的數據包開銷和高性能，而後者則著重於研究在有其他損傷（特別是在波長調節時激光器的瞬態特性）的情況下每個單獨算法的有效性，以及找出快速補償突發模式光接收機中所有相關損傷的最佳方式。這些補償算法依次序進行或者協同進行，從而達到以最低的複雜度去實現子系統的整體優化。 此研究案與目前的下一代高容量、靈活的光網絡的戰略研發方向一致。它利用最新的高速微電子器件，同時解決容量危機、網絡靈活性和整體資源優化的問題。這個項目還將戰略性地增強香港中文大學內部的研究合作，以及與海外研究機構-愛爾蘭Tyndall國家研究院，在智能和可進化的光網絡發展方面的研究合作。

14200914.label: Realisation of objectives
14200914.value: To achieve the objectives of this project, we have developed several system-level digital signal processing (DSP) techniques to optimize the performance of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). Efficient combination of these developed DSP schemes and the optimization of OFDM-based optical networks has also been investigated. The summary of the research works carried out during this project is presented as follows. • Optical physical-layer network coding (OPNC), in particular, our recent work on coherent common channel OPNC, is presented in [J1]. The proposed OPNC technique offers the possibility for the burst mode receiver at receiving nodes to handle data streams coming from multiple transmitters simultaneously. The key contribution of our prior work is that it provides a novel solution for OFDM-based coherent burst mode transmissions to fully utilize the network resources, thus improving network capacity. • We have proposed an adaptive indoor multiple inputs and multiple output (MIMO) OFDM system using a receiver module with angular diversity [J2]. The key idea is to utilize the singular value decomposition (SVD) based adaptive loading algorithm so as to adaptively allocate data bits and power according to the variable channel conditions. Feasibility and robustness of the proposed scheme are investigated in an indoor visible light communication (VLC) with decentralized terminals, where the received packets from transmitters at different locations are of different amplitudes and phases. The scenario is related to the case of burst-mode transmission, where each receiving node receives packets from different transmitting nodes that are of different distances, thus the received packets have different phase and amplitude. The proposed adaptive scheme provides a basic framework to facilitate the development of the adaptive threshold estimation and fast convergence in OFDM-based burst mode receivers (BMRs). • For the first time, we present the experimental characterizations of the impact of user mobility on the transmission performance of the OFDM based mobile VLC (mobi-VLC) system. The results are published in a top-tier journal, Optics Letters [J3]. The mobi-VLC is related to the burst-mode transmission, where each receiving node dynamically receives packets from different transmitting nodes that are of different distances, resulting in time-varying phases and amplitudes of the received packets. Our experimental results show that the system performance degrades with the increase in user mobility speed and in moving distance. Furthermore, we propose the use of the channel-independent OCT precoding to combat the mobility-induced performance degradation. The effectiveness of the OCT precoding is evaluated by the comparisons with the conventional OFDM scheme and the discrete multitone (DMT) with adaptive bit and power loading. Results show that the OCT precoding offers significant packet loss reduction and outperforms the adaptive-loaded DMT in the mobi-VLC system, resulting from the channel-independent property and enhanced inter-symbol interference (ISI) tolerance. The demonstrated OCT precoding based mobi-VLC system exhibits advantages of reduced bit error rate (BER), enhanced ISI tolerance, and reduced implementation complexity. • The first investigation of IM/DD OFDM using the set-partitioned QAM (SP-QAM) format is presented in [J4, C6]. We have also derived the SP-64QAM, which can be more power efficient than SP-128QAM and 8QAM. Experimental results show that SP-128QAM OFDM and the proposed SP-64QAM OFDM exhibit greatly improved performance compared to conventional 16QAM- or 8QAM-OFDM in the IM/DD system. Furthermore, we also show that power-efficient SP formats with fine spectral efficiency granularity can be very promising to combine with adaptive loading to approach the capacity limit of OFDM systems. The constellation design and symbol error rate (SER) of SP-QAM formats are investigated in [J4]. Based on the SER analysis, we derive the adaptive bit and power loading algorithm and have experimentally investigated its performance. It is shown that the data rate can be boosted from 36 Gbit/s to 42 Gbit/s in the presence of severe dispersion-induced spectral nulls after 40-km single-mode fiber. Furthermore, the adaptive algorithm also greatly enhances the tolerance to fiber nonlinearity, and thus allows for more power budget. • The dynamics of distributed feedback (DFB) laser and discrete mode laser (DML) for optical injection locking (OIL) is experimentally investigated in [J5, C5]. The dynamic stabilization time, in terms of instantaneous frequency by the Wigner-Ville (WV) distribution and time-resolved phase error variance, are investigated. We show that the injection power has a minor impact on the locking time, and 10~20 ns locking time can be achieved with bursty injection. The relationship between injection ratio and unlocking time is also studied, and results show that a larger injection power will result in a longer unlocking time, varying from around 10 ns to tens of ns. The investigations provide a framework for the injection locking based coherent detection in the BMRs. • A novel offset quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) scheme is proposed to improve the dispersion tolerance to that of one subcarrier without cyclic prefix [C1]. Compared to conventional OFDM, this technology can greatly relax the length of cyclic prefix (CP) for dispersion compensation and achieve ~20% increase in net data rate for the same transmission reach. On the other hand, it reduces the memory length of pulse-shaping filters and results in lower complexity than Nyquist frequency-division multiplexing (FDM). Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can support a 224-Gbit/s polarization-division multiplexing (PDM) offset-QPSK OFDM signal over a dispersion of ~160,000 ps/nm without any CP. The proposed scheme exhibits advantages of enhanced spectral efficiency and larger dispersion tolerance. • In [C2], a channel independent orthogonal circulant matrix transform (OCT) based precoding scheme for the OFDM-based systems is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. To implement the proposed OCT precoding scheme, only one linear transformation is required at transmitter and receiver, respectively. We show that compared to the conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT) precoding, the proposed OCT precoding exhibits enhanced tolerance of inter-symbol interference (ISI) with the same CP length. The performance is experimentally verified and results indicate that OCT precoding has comparable BER with the optimal bit and power loading, while providing significantly reduced implementation complexity. Further performance enhancement can be achieved by the bit-loaded multi-band OCT precoding, i.e., load different order of QAM formats to different OCT precoded sub-bands, the corresponding results are reported in [C4]. Although demonstrated in the intensity modulation and direct detection (IM/DD) VLC system, the proposed scheme does not have specific requirements on the OFDM schemes. Besides, we can also apply the OCT scheme to jointly preprocess the transmitting nodes, which may help improve the throughput of OFDM-based burst-mode networks without incurring high complexity. • To facilitate fast performance monitoring, proactive monitoring in software-defined networks is proposed and different monitoring strategies are discussed [C3]. We show that with the assistance of proactive monitoring, the monitoring time can be significantly reduced by around 70%-77%.

14200914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200914.value: Within this project, various techniques, covering DSP, networking and performance monitoring, has been developed to address the objectives. The major findings are listed as follows: (1) the OPNC, and particularly coherent common channel OPNC to double the capacity of optical networks [J1]; (2) a SVD-based adaptive loading scheme for MIMO-OFDM based optical IM/DD systems [J2]; (3) the first experimental investigation of mobi-VLC [J3]; (4) the SP-QAM based OFDM scheme and the adaptively-loaded SP-QAM-OFDM scheme [J4, C6]; (5) the investigations of the dynamic properties of optical injection locked laser for coherent detection [J5, C5]; (6) a novel offset-QAM OFDM scheme to improve the dispersion tolerance and to enhance the spectral efficiency [C1]; (7) a single-band OCT precoding scheme and a bit-loaded multi-band OCT precoding scheme for achieving CSI-free linear equalization so as to mitigate the fading issue in optical systems [C2, C4]; (8) the proactive monitoring scheme to realize fast OPM [C3]. Totally 5 journal publications have been generated, including the top-tier journals such as Optics Letters, Optics Express, etc. We have also published 6 conference papers in flagship international conferences, including The Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC) and Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics (CLEO). Our collaboration with the overseas researchers, including Dr. Jian Zhao at Tyndall National Institute and University College Cork, Ireland, has also been strengthened through this project.

14200914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200914.value: This project mainly focuses on the investigations of the multi-carrier OFDM based coherent BMRs, further development of the research may include the following two aspects, (1) The performance comparison with the single-carrier modulation formats, such as carrierless amplitude and phase (CAP) modulation. The single-carrier modulation formats, though exhibiting less efficient flexibility, provides reduced implementation complexity and enhanced nonlinearity tolerance. Therefore, it is worthy of further extensive investigations. (2) Real-time implementation and investigation using the field-programmable gate array (FPGA). It is also desirable to verify the feasibility and robustness of the developed schemes of this project in the FPGA-based real-time transmissions. It may help further optimize the performance of these schemes regarding the further reducing their implementation complexity while maintaining the transmission performance.

14200914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200914.value: This project simultaneously addresses the problems of capacity crunch, network flexibility, and overall performance optimization by investigating OFDM-based coherent BMRs. The study includes understanding of fundamental limits, development of novel DSP techniques, and investigation of performance versus complexity tradeoff. The topic of this project has been attracting the interests from both academia and multi-national companies such as Alcatel-Lucent and Huawei. The output of this project enhances the understanding of performance versus cost/complexity tradeoff for BMRs using multicarrier modulation formats like OFDM, and thus provides valuable guidelines to identify optimal solutions. The generated outputs of this projects have been published in top tier journals and flagship conferences. This project also helps reinforce the international collaborative relationship with the Tyndall National Institute and University College Cork, Ireland.

14201014.value: 通過區域負載平衡來優化數據中心的總電力成本

14201014.label: Project Objectives
14201014.value: We will investigate GLB's impact on local electricity demand variation and consequently the electricity prices. In particular, we plan to apply statistical modeling and regression analysis on the empirical data, to characterize the relationship between GLB load percentages (i.e., the percentage of the data center workload that can be geographic load-balanced) and electricity price increment. We will evaluate how well common GLB approaches perform, taking into account GLB's impact on electricity prices. From the results we will check whether new approaches are needed. We will investigate architecture-shifting solutions to properly realize the full economic potential of GLB. In particular, motivated by the recent practice of large CSPs moving into electricity markets, we will explore a broker-assisted approach that allows CSPs to directly purchase electricity from markets through brokers. By doing GLB and electricity procurement jointly, CSPs can eliminate the trading inefficiency between utilities and CSPs, and GLB no longer causes economic loss to utilities. Meanwhile, CSPs can still exploit GLB across multiple geo-locations to reduce electricity cost. We will identify key challenges in this approach and utilize optimization theory to design sound solutions to address the challenges. We also plan to work with industrial partners to validate our findings using real-world traces.

14201014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201014.value: 該項目旨在研究如何利用區域負載平衡（ GLB ）來減少一群在地理上錯落分佈的數據中心的總電力成本。GLB的核心思想是把工作動態地交由位於電價比較便宜的地區的數據中心來處理。現有的GLB研究都基於一個重要的假設，即電價不受GLB的影響。我們的初步研究發現這個假設在實際中並不廣泛成立。從而，我們計劃在沒有這個假設的前提下來研究GLB方案。我們的研究計劃包括 (i) 評估地區電價如何受GLB影響，(ii) 在考慮對地區電價影響的前提下，設計新的GLB方案降低數據中心總電費。

14201014.label: Realisation of objectives
14201014.value: We have achieved all the revised objectives. The results are reported in the published journal/conference papers on top/reputable venues. The relationship between the impact of GLB load balancing and electricity price increment is roughly linear, according to regression analysis. Roughly, about 10% prediction error caused by GLB load balancing will incur about 10% price increment. We have evaluated how well common GLB approaches perform, taking into account GLB's impact on electricity prices. The results show that the performance is worse than expected. In particular, datacenter owners who operate multiple geo-distributed datacenters using existing solutions may only obtain minor economic saving by doing load balancing, since the solutions didn't consider the potential impact of GLB on the electricity price. In some case study, the datacenter owner pays higher electricity cost by doing GLB as compared to not doing GLB. This observation suggests that new approach and solutions are needed to fully release the economic benefit of GLB. We then went forward to propose a GLB solution that avoids the drawback observed in the existing solutions. In particular we encourage datacenter owners to go directly into the electricity market to purchase electricity. We formulate the problem, which turns out to be a non-convex problem. We then design a solution to solve the problem optimally, by properly exploiting the problem structure. We prove the optimality of our algorithm. Along the way, we also solve a variant of a classical news-vendor problem optimally. We use simulations based on real-world traces to demonstrate the performance of our algorithm. The results show that our solution does not suffer from the negative economic impact of doing GLB (like existing solutions). Our solution achieves up to 22% cost saving as compared to alternative baselines.

14201014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201014.value: Most existing studies on GLB assume that the use of GLB has no impact on electricity prices, even though GLB increases local electricity demand variation. In practice, however, electricity retail prices are determined by how supply and demand are dynamically balanced by local electricity utilities. Firstly, in order to understand GLS’s economic potential and impact, we carry out a comprehensive study on how GLB interacts with electricity supply chains. (Achieving objective 1.) In particular, we show that a separate GLB solution, which relies on utility companies for electricity procurement (EP), will make the electricity supply chains less efficient. Then, utility companies have to increase electricity retail prices to ensure a certain profit margin. (Achieving objective 1 and 2.) Consequently, CSP doing GLB may end up getting minor cost reduction or even paying higher electricity cost than not doing GLB, as shown in our case study based on real-world traces. (Achieving objective 2.) Secondly, motivated by the recent practice of large CSPs moving into electricity markets, we allow CSPs to join the deregulated market directly and propose a joint GLB and EP solution. By considering the real-world market mechanisms and exploring the full design space of strategic bidding, we formulate a stochastic optimization problem to minimize the total cost expectation. (Achieving objective 3.) Under the ideal setting where exact values of market prices and workloads are given, this problem reduces to a simple linear programming and is easy to solve. However, under the realistic setting where only distributional information of these variables is available when making decisions, the problem unfolds into a non-convex infinite-dimensional one and is challenging. One of our main contributions is to develop a nestedloop algorithm that is proven to solve the challenging problem optimally. Our study also highlights the intriguing role of uncertainty in demands and prices, measured by their variances. While uncertainty in electricity demands deteriorates the cost-saving performance of joint GLB and EP, counter-intuitively, uncertainty in market prices can be exploited to achieve a cost reduction even larger than the setting without price uncertainty. (Achieving objective 3.) Finally, our trace-driven evaluations corroborate our theoretical results, demonstrate fast convergence of our algorithm, and show that it can reduce the cost for the CSP by up to 20% as compared to baseline alternatives. (Achieving objective 3.) An INFOCOM-2017 paper that contains results from this project missed the funding acknowledgment. The funding ack was added into its journal version accepted into IEEE/ACM Trans on Networking in 2018.

14201014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201014.value: Our works, in particular the broker-assisted approach, have several limitations. First, we assume that all the day-ahead market’s MCPs and real-time market prices are mutually independent, which may not hold in practice. Second, we assume that the CSP has negligible market power, which may not hold for local markets even though globally datacenters today only consume less than 2% of the total electricity. Finally, we do not model possible strategic behaviors of other market participants. Addressing these limitations is an interesting research direction.

14201014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201014.value: This project studies the use of geographic load-balancing (GLB) to reduce electricity cost of data centers. The key idea of such “cost-aware” GLB is to route workload to data centers at locations with cheaper electricity. First, our case-study suggests that GLB can cause a 10% demand variation for a utility, and consequently a 7% increase in the electricity price. Therefore, to evaluate GLB's potential in reducing electricity cost, it is critical to understand how GLB can alter electricity demand patterns, and the impact of this uncertainty on the electricity prices. Such understanding is currently missing. We carry out a comprehensive study on using GLB to reduce electricity cost to fill in the gap. A particular result is a broker-assisted solution to eliminate the GLB-induced trading inefficiency between CSPs and local utilities, while still enjoying the economic benefit of GLB. Our advocated holistic approach is likely to set a new standard for future studies in this field. We believe that our approach and results are critical for understanding and unleashing GLB's economic potential in practice.

14201114.value: 隨機動態規劃的計算方法及其在金融工程中的應用

14201114.label: Project Objectives
14201114.value: Develop a computational approach to solve stochastic dynamic programming problems based on the idea of supersolution iteration. Use regression-based Monte Carlo methods to study related computational issues arising from the implementation of the above approach, targeting especially to overcome the curse of dimensionality encountered in large-scaled control problems. 14201114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201114.value: Many applications in financial engineering require people to make decisions over time. In between are examples including asset pricing, investment optimization, and trading execution of large portfolios. These applications involve making decisions, then observing new information coming in from the market, after which investors make more decisions, and so on. Stochastic dynamic programming lays out an elegant principle to help solve such sequential decision problems. However, two difficulties, the curse of dimensionality and model misspecification, limit significantly its usefulness. The former refers to a fact that the problems quickly becomes computationally intractable as their dimensionality increases, while the latter one points to the danger of using inaccurate models in decision making. People usually rely on easy-to-compute heuristic rules in practice to solve large-scaled complex control problems. Several research challenges thus arise naturally in this regard. Is there any systematic way to assess such heuristic rules? If we know that a given rule is not good, how should we improve it? How should we make our decisions robust so that they perform comparably well for a class of unspecified models near the approximating model, given the possibility that the model obtained from data admits some statistical error? The proposed project aims to develop an innovative supersolution-based approach to solve SDP problems iteratively. Our approach will provide confidence interval estimates for the true optimal value of an SDP problem. The tightness of such intervals will characterize analytically the quality of the currently used control policies. Meanwhile, our approach ensures that the obtained control policies will converge to the true optimal one. This enables a way of policy improvement via iterations. Our approach will also integrate techniques from deterministic optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, and statistics to achieve computational efficiency, targeting to overcome the aforementioned curse of dimensionality the traditional numerical SDP methods encounter. Finally, it can be generalized to compute robust control policies to incorporate the impact of model misspecification into our decision-making procedure. Results from the proposed study will contribute practical tools to support financial decision-making efficiently and scientifically. 金融工程的諸多應用要求決策人進行動態決策， 其中例子包括資產定價， 投資優化，和訂單執行。這些應用的模式往往是做出決策，然後從市場中觀察新的信息，繼而做出新的決策。 隨機動態規劃奠定了解決這類問題的理論基礎。但是，兩個困難， “維度災難”和模型的不確定性，顯著妨礙了其作用的發揮。 前者是指隨機動態規劃方法的計算複雜度隨著問題維度的增加變得不可控制，而後者是指在決策中使用不精確模型帶來的危險。有鑒於此，人們常用一些易於計算的經驗方法來處理大規模的複雜控制問題。 於是幾個研究課題自然產生。 有無一個系統性的方法可用於這些經驗方法的效果評估？ 如果我們知道它們不理想，應當如何改進？給定我們從數據擬合出來的近似模型存在統計誤差，如何使決策變得穩健，讓它在我們所使用的近似模型周圍的一組模型下都表現理想？ 該研究項目的目標是發展出一個新穎的基於超解的迭代算法來解決隨機動態規劃問題。此方法將提供真實解的置信區間估計，使得我們能夠從區間的鬆緊程度來定量判斷所用策略的優劣。同時此方法可以保證得到的控制策略將最終收斂於最優解，使得我們能夠有一個通過迭代改善現有策略的機制。我們的方法整合確定性優化，Monte Carlo模擬，和統計等技術來達到克服維度災難及提升計算效率的目標。最後，我們還計劃將此方法擴展至穩健控制領域，充分考慮到模型錯誤所導致的影響。從此研究產生出的計算工具將會為科學有效的金融決策提供支持。

14201114.label: Realisation of objectives
14201114.value: 1. The principal investigator developed a supersolution based computational approach to solving stochastic dynamic programs. The resulted confidence interval estimates enable us not only to assess the quality of heuristic policies, but also to improve its performance if we find that they are not satisfactory. 2. Stemming from objective 1, the principal investigator established a regression-based Monte Carlo method to study large-scaled control problems. In it, the new method deploys the technique of pathwise optimization to achieve efficient and accurate outcomes. Meanwhile it introduces state sampler to address the exploration and exploitation tradeoff. In addition, the principal investigator analyzed the algorithm complexity and managed to prove the convergence rate of the algorithm. 3. The principal investigate successfully formulated the corresponding duality for SDP problems with model uncertainty. In particular, he and his coauthors studied one important class of stochastic models, stochastic differential equations (SDE). SDE finds many applications in economics and finance to model random uncertainties. The research of the principal investigator presented a novel approach to expanding probability densities of SDEs, which lays out the foundation for further statistical inferences. 4. The principal investigator also investigated various applications of this new method, including portfolio investment, American option pricing, optimal trading execution, and inventory management. The new approach demonstrates a great potential in solving some problems that are well known to be intractable in the literature. In particular, related to the theme of this project, he and his coauthors developed a closed-form approximation to the option price under one class of stochastic volatility model. The explicit expression yielded from the method is appealing from the practical perspective because it can lead to fast calibration, pricing, and hedging.

14201114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201114.value: The project leads to three publications so far. One is in the Journal of Econometrics (Paper 1 in Part C), one of the major research outlets in the field of econometrics. In this paper the principal investigator and his coauthors developed a new delta expansion approach to deriving analytical approximation to the transition densities of multivariate diffusions using the Itô-Taylor expansion of the conditional expectation of the Dirac delta function. The new approach yields an explicit recursive formulas for the expansion coefficients and is universally applicable for a wide spectrum of models. This research lays out important theoretical foundation for statistical inference about diffusion models. The other two (Paper 2 and 3 in Part C) are on option pricing under a class of stochastic volatility models, the stochastic alpha–beta–rho (SABR) model. This model is widely used in quantitative modelling in the fixed income and foreign exchange markets as a benchmark. The two papers appeared in Journal of Economic and Dynamic Control and Journal of Quantitative Finance, respectively, developing closed-form approximations to the prices of vanilla under this model. The resulted explicit expression from the method is appealing from the practical perspective because it can lead to fast calibration, pricing, and hedging. In addition, some of the research outcomes are summarized in one paper (Paper 4 in Part C) that is under review with the journal of Management Sciences. In it, the principal investigator systematically develop a duality/supersolution based recursive approach to obtaining and improving confidence interval estimates for the true value of stochastic dynamic programming problem with finite time horizon.

14201114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201114.value: The principal investigator will continue the investigation stemmed out from this research project on the computational approach for stochastic dynamic programming (SDP). A particular near-term objective is to extend the study to reinforcement learning, an active subfield of machine learning that is closely related to SDP.

14201114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201114.value: Stochastic dynamic programming (SDP) provides a powerful framework for modelling and solving decision-making problems under a random environment where uncertainty is resolved and actions are taken sequentially over time. However, its application is largely limited by the significant computational complexity. Hence, people often have to settle for a suboptimal decision that strikes a reasonable balance between convenient implementation and adequate performance. Such practice naturally gives rise to the following two research questions: 1. How can we assess the quality of a given control policy? 2. If we know the performance of a policy is not satisfactory, do we have a systematic way to improve it? This funded project develops a systematic computational approach to address the above important issues. It demonstrates a great potential in solving some problems that are widely known to be intractable in the literature. The new method can find wide applications in finance and economics.

14201214.label: Project Objectives
14201214.value: Understand the physics (crack initiation, propagation and fracture) of soft tissue cutting through finite element modeling and experimental characterization/validation. 14201214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201214.value: This proposal seeks to understand the physics and mechanics of cutting fresh soft tissues, e.g. brain, via finite element modeling and experimental validation for (1) developing an ultra-precision vibrating blade microtome (an instrument for sectioning soft tissues) and (2) establishing quantitative relationships between the cutting quality and cutting parameters. The final goal of this work is to combine the microtome with a parallel super-resolution microscope in order to map the synaptic connections of an entire mouse brain, i.e. connectome, which approximately contains 75 million neurons and 100 billion synapses. With the advent of many super-resolution imaging techniques developed in recent years, the bottleneck of obtaining the connectome via light microscopy lies in the precise tissue sectioning and the mapping/stitching of synaptic connections across different tissue sections, which call for 20-50µm tissue sections with distortion-free surfaces and 200nm RMS flatness. However, state-of-the-art vibrating blade microtomes can only generate 100µm fresh tissue sections with 1µm RMS and significant tissue damage and distortion. In fact, to date no one really understands the physics of cutting soft tissue with an oscillating blade; thus all operating parameters are from empirical data. We will develop a finite element model and devise optical experiments to validate/improve the modeling results. A custom-developed high-speed (600fps) fluorescence optical extensometer will be used to record the tissue deformation; insights obtained from the experiments will be used to guide the design of the vibrating blade microtome. The heart of the new microtome is a compliant mechanism that generates highly repeatable oscillatory blade motion, minimizing the out-of-plane parasitic motion to be within 200nm and thus ensuring a satisfactorily flat section. This can be achieved by directing the actuator load to a merged center of mass and stiffness of the mechanism which consequently eliminates the source of error motions. Upon completion of the microtome development, we will integrate it with a parallel super-resolution microscope developed by our team. Control electronics and software will be developed to realize a fully automated serial sectioning and image acquisition/reconstruction procedure for obtaining a connectome. The result of this work may improve the fundamental understanding of cutting viscoelastic materials, resulting in a new vibrating blade microtome with superior performance that enables the mapping of 3-D resolved connectome. The new vibrating blade microtome will also have impact in various biological and clinical applications. For example, to generate ultra-flat and thin tissue sections for pathological/histological studies without freezing the tissue. 本研究將通過有限元模擬和實驗驗證的方法解釋活組織切片過程中的力學現象，用以（1）開發（用於軟組織切片的）超精密振動切片機，及（2）建立切片質量和儀器操作參數的定量關係。在此基礎上，本項目將超薄切片機與平行超分辨率顯微鏡結合，最終實現對整個鼠腦內部突觸連接體（例如含有約75萬個神經元和1千億個突觸的神經連接體）的測繪。 近年來，隨著超分辨率成像技術的出現和快速發展，精確地進行組織切片並拼接不同切面的神經突觸已成為了目前以光學顯微鏡觀察三維神經連接的瓶頸。利用光學顯微鏡觀察神經連接要求組織的切片厚度為20-50微米，截面無任何扭曲變形，並具有200納米的表面粗糙度。而目前的振動刀片切片機僅能製備切割厚度100微米，表面粗糙度為1微米的活生物組織切片，組織的切面也有明顯破壞與變形。不僅如此，目前對軟組織切片這一過程的力學現象少有解釋，控制軟組織切片質量的操作參數往往由過往經驗猜測獲得。 我們將建立軟組織切片過程的有限元模型，並設計可通過光學顯微鏡實時觀測的實驗來驗證該模型。我們將自行開發高速(600幀/秒)熒光形變測量計用以觀察組織的形變，實驗觀察結果將用於振動切片機的優化及設計。此新型超薄切片機的核心是一個往復振蕩的，具有高度可重複性的柔性機構。通過將製動器載荷加載在該柔性機構的質量和剛度中心（兩者重合）消除誤差運動的來源，從而將面外連帶運動降低到200納米以內，保證了理想的平面切片。切片機開發完成以後將與平行超分辨率顯微鏡組合。我們還將開發電子控制設備及軟件，從而實現獲取神經連接體的全自動化連續切片和圖像採集、重建過程。 此項工作的結果將增加對切割黏彈性材料的力學機理的理解，同時開發出全新高性能的、能夠實現對三維解析神經連接體進行測繪的振動切片機。新的振動切片機也可用於各種生物及臨床應用。例如，不通過冷凍組織而獲取超平、超薄的組織切片以進行病理、組織學的研究。

14201214.label: Realisation of objectives
14201214.value: We have achieved all the proposed objectives of this project, i.e., (1) we have developed new models/theories and experimental methods to section soft tissues with high precision; (2) the model provides deterministic links between the sectioning quality and the microtome operation parameters (vibration frequency, vibration amplitude, and sample feed rate.); (3) new microtomes based on flexures have been developed, achieving high operation speed, i.e., 500 Hz, which lead to better sectioning results (200 nm RMS surface flatness), verified both by experiments and our model; and (4) working with teams at MIT to integrate the microtome with a super-resolution microscope for constructing brain connectomes of mice. While all goals have been satisfactorily addressed, it is worthwhile to note that more imaging experiments under goal 4 is still ongoing as the generation of a brain connectome is a long process. (The 3-D super-resolution microscope/microtome setup is located at MIT, led by Prof. Peter So.) Comparing with the traditional electron microscope approach which will take 20+ years to complete a brain connectome, our new fluorescent system will reduce that to 1-2 years; and we expect the result to be highly impactful and may be published in the next 1-2 years. Notably, we have published the recent application of our microtome in Nature Biotechnology, where the microtome help to realize 3-D imaging of any optically cleared organ/tissues. (In collaboration with Prof. KC Chung, MIT; Journal Output [2])

14201214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201214.value: The most important finding, leading to the development of new high performance microtome, is that soft tissue can be sectioned with much better quality at a speed higher than 200 Hz (while all conventional microtomes operate at a speed below 100 Hz) due to the viscoelastic effect that the material is stiffened by the high oscillating speed of the microtome. The results is precisely predicted by the model and verified by experiments on agarose and different tissue samples. (Journal Output [1]) The new microtome fulfills the requirements of generating connectomes based on super-resolution fluorescent microscope; as such, the completed 3-D imaging system is currently under operation at MIT to create the first 3-D brain map of mouse with 50 nm resolution, capable of visualizing neuronal synaptic connections for the first time. In addition, top brain teams around the globe are seeking to collaborate with our team to learn the new microtome design, including teams from Taiwan (NTHU), mainland China (HUST), MIT and Harvard University. We expect the new microtome to be broadly adopted for the emerging new applications, e.g., expansion microscopy or optical clearning (Journal Output [2]). Beyond microtome and 3-D imaging system, the grant also support other related research activities and projects, including the development of an alignment-free liquid-capsule pressure sensor for cardiovascular monitoring (Journal Output [3]), the development of a confocal system for studying the photoactivation of extracellular-signal-regulated kinase signaling (Journal Output [4]), the development of a novel compact spectrometer with custom-printed gratings (Journal Output [5]), the development of a hybrid imprinting process to fabricate a multilayer compound eye for multispectral imaging (Journal Output [6]), the development of a compact high-resolution endomicroscopy based on fiber bundles (Journal Output [7]), and the development of a ultra-sensitive fiber-optic DNA sensor (Journal Output [8]).

14201214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201214.value: The microtome’s operation speed may be further increased to improve the cutting results; one limiting issue is that when the cutting speed increases, the resonant modes of the microtome may be also excited, generating unwanted dynamics to compromise the cutting results. We are currently investigating active vibration suppression methods to reduce the vibration of the system in the undesired axes. If successful, the microtome may be operated at 500 – 600 Hz.

14201214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201214.value: This work helps understand the physics and mechanics of cutting fresh soft tissues, e.g. brain, via finite element modeling and experimental validation. New ultra-precision vibrating blade microtomes (an instrument for sectioning soft tissues) have been developed to achieve the goal. New analytical models have been developed, establishing quantitative relationships between the cutting quality and cutting parameters. The new microtome is designed based on flexure principles and is currently integrated with a super-resolution microscope at MIT to map the synaptic connections of an entire mouse brain, i.e. connectome, which approximately contains 75 million neurons and 100 billion synapses. The work is still ongoing and expected to be finished in 1-2 years with high impact as it may help scientist to understand how brain functions down to the molecular level. In addition, new imaging and sensing methods, including compact spectrometers, confocal imaging systems, pressure sensors for cardiovascular monitoring, fiber-optic DNA sensors etc., have been developed via the support of the grant.

14201314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201314.value: The SARS epidemic in 2003 was traced back to an outbreak in a hospital in Hong Kong. In 2013, a Frenchman died of a SARS-like virus. He got infected while he was sharing a common hospital room with an infective. To ensure public health, we need a further understanding of human interaction dynamics in a hospital environment and a deeper investigation of nosocomial infections for effective and efficient control strategies. This research leverages our recent work in the active RFID traceability technologies. Our system is developed with the capability to determine the indoor location of an active tag. This system was installed inside two wards (11A & 11C) of Prince of Wales Hospital for a 4-month formal pilot study with patient and medical staff participation to improve patient care. Based on the user feedbacks collected, we find that time and space play an important role in shaping human behaviors, inferring human interactions, and influencing epidemic spread of infectious diseases in a healthcare institute. Our research aims at enhancing the capability of tracking the movement of people and tracing the infection of a hospital-acquired disease for each individual in order to monitor and control the epidemic spread of nosocomial infections. To achieve this goal, we plan to conduct the following research activities: 1. network models of dynamic human behaviors for an enhanced spatial-temporal analysis to determine human interaction patterns and contacts in a relatively close community, 2. epidemic models to track and trace nosocomial infections based on the time-varying contact networks to increase our understanding of transmission mechanisms in hospital, 3. traceability analysis of tracking the mobility and infection for each individual to identify risk behaviors by linking both the network and epidemic models, 4. effective and efficient control strategies against epidemic spread under different scenarios to take advantage of the network structure and disease dynamics. This research is unique. First, since our focus is on the movement of people, our methods are very different from those used to track products in a supply chain. Further, we plan to conduct the traceability analysis of the dynamic interactions and infections of people at individual level for network epidemiology study in hospital. This differs from either the popular modeling of a static network or the traditional epidemiology study for a large region. Finally, many spatial-temporal analyses and epidemiology models are developed for outdoor applications while this work deals with indoor activities. 非典疫情於二零零三年在香港一家醫院爆發，蔓延社區而造成數百名市民死亡。 十年後，一名法國人因與一位攜帶非典類似病毒的病人共用同一病房而感染病毒死亡。這些案例清楚地顯示院內感染是個重要問題。為保障公眾健康，我們需要進一步明白醫院環境內活動的動態分析和深入了解室内疾病傳播的控制策略。 這項研究充分利用我們近期在有源射頻識別追溯技術的工作，新開發的系統能夠確定有源標籤的室內位置。該系統在威爾斯親王醫院的兩間病房已作過四個月的測試，并為是項研究提供的有用的數據。 我們的研究目的在於加強跟踪人們在醫院範圍內活動的情況和追蹤室内疾病傳染的過程。通過這些分析，我們能制定戰略來監測和控制院內感染疫情的蔓延。

14201314.label: Realisation of objectives
14201314.value: 1. hospital risk management system (HRMS): The HRMS targets to mitigate several aspects of hospital risks that centered on the patients. The objective is to empower the hospital staff to deliver better care and safety to the patients. By attaching RFID active tags on some selected (generally profiled as high-risk) patients, via the use of RFID wristband, and together with the use of RFID readers, Real Time Location System (RTLS) and such, the HRMS will be able to track the location and movement of the tagged patients in real time. Furthermore, the sensor devices that are integrated into patient’s RFID wristband will be able to monitor and report the patient’s conditions (body temperature, pulse rate and body motion) to the HRMS in regular intervals. Combined, we thus have a convenient solution that monitors the locations and conditions of the tracked patients, in a 24x7 and effortless manner. Beyond tracking the patients alone, better patient safety and care can further be achieved by ensuring the quality and timeliness of services that are provided to the patients. Also better patient safety and care can further be achieved by ensuring the quality and timeliness of services that are provided to the patients. Hence, we extend our scope by: - tracking the location of ward equipment (via a RFID Tag): the HRMS can ensure the ward staff that (a sufficient quantity of) critical equipment are always at arm’s length inside the ward area and will be readily available for providing medical care to the patients when needed. - tracking the movement (in/out of the ward) of caregiver from the Central Pharmacy (via a RFID badge), ward staff will be able to ensure timely delivery of drugs from the Central Pharmacy; and thus the timely drug dispensing to the patients in turn, - tracking the movement (in/out of the ward) of caregiver from the Central Laboratory (via a RFID badge), ward staff will be able to ensure timely delivery of patients’ specimen to the Central Laboratory for various testing and investigation, - monitoring the ward condition (temperature and humidity) (via sensors in ward), ward staff will be able to ensure a suitable ward condition is properly maintained in a relatively effortless manner, It is therefore required to attach additional RFID active tags to selected ward equipment (RFID tag), and caregivers (RFID badge) of the Central Pharmacy and Central Laboratory; and to install sensor devices inside the different areas or zones in the ward (sensor devices will be integrated with RFID readers). However, the benefit of tracking the location and condition of patients, caregivers, equipment and ward can be easily overshadowed if the ward staffs are required to deal with the vast amount of tracked data of all the tracked subjects, on a daily basis. A management dashboard, called the Ward Management Console, will therefore be provided to consolidate all the tracked data and present them to the ward staff in a user-friendly and convenient way. Although the Ward Management Console is designed to be user-friendly, we understand that ward staff are in general occupied by routine and ad-hoc tasks that they cannot spend too much time on the Console to monitor the location and condition of the tagged subjects on regular basis; therefore we supplement the Console by introducing a robotic Alert Engine, which helps to monitor the tracked subjects on behalf of the ward staff. Ward staff can simply define Alert Rules and instruct the Alert Engine to watch for the alerting location, movement and condition of the tracked subjects (e.g. Patient A has not stayed in the ward for the last 3 hours). Ward staff can even define how the ward staff will be notified if a particular alert condition holds true (in that case an alarm will be fired). The benefit of the use of Alert Engine and Alert Rule is that when a particular alert condition is found on a particular tracked subject, the ward staff will immediately be notified; and from the “actionable” information displayed on the Ward Management Console, the ward staff can respond and take appropriate action with no unnecessary delay. By adopting an event/alertdriven style of work, it is our purpose to ensure the HRMS will fit seamlessly into the care workflow practiced by the ward staff day by day. On the other hand, we will also like to extend the scope of tracking to include ward staff as well. By doing so, we will be able to collect more traceability information, providing a more thorough picture and history of human interactivities inside ward area, which is vital but currently unavailable data set to prove any medical hypothesis of how an infectious disease being spread in a hospital. A proven hypothesis will then become a resource to devise prevention and response plan for future outbreak. Ward staff will be tagged by a RFID badge, similar to the staff from Central Pharmacy and Central Laboratory. 2. ward management console (WMC): The Ward Management Console is targeted for use by ward staff exclusively. For the term “ward staff”, we are referring to the nursing professionals: ward manager, nursing specialist, nursing officer, register and enrolled nurse. The project will launch a Ward Management Console for use in general ward environment. The Console will be running 24x7 on nurse station desktop with no downtime on user side. It is also expected that the machine running the Console will be properly positioned on the desktop, so that it can be readily accessed and operated by caregivers whilst it will be out of the reach of other patients in the ward. 3. system performance requirement: The performance and accuracy of the HRMS will largely depend on the underlying RFID software, hardware and infrastructure; which will be fine-tuned before and during the pilot run in ward environment. 4. security requirement: HRMS will capture patient’s personal data from the 2D barcode on patient’s wristband when the patient is first tagged. The personal data captured include patient’s English name, date of birth, gender and the UPI number (HN#) as assigned by the hospital during the admission process; but no HKID information. The personal data is captured by the Wand Management Console at nurse station and stored into the database directly. No personal data will be transmitted in the wireless RFID network (between RFID Tags and Readers). 5. collection of user statistics: The HRMS system is required to record some statistical data for regular project review (monthly) and post-project evaluation. 6. traceability analysis: The spatial and temporal data collected by the RFID positioning system provide a voluminous, detailed set of records all tagged objects at a particular location at a specific time. To make sense of the underlying data, a set of analytic tools and processes will be developed for analysts and managerial staff to gain insights from the data. 7. contact analysis: The massive volume of tracking data provides the ground for discovering contact occurrence data between any pair of tagged objects during the pilot run. After converting the spatial-temporal data into contact occurrence data, the contact visualization tool set will be used to: (i) Visual the contact information as a whole, (ii) Investigate the contact history of a particular tagged object, (iii) Discover sub-group of most-frequently interacting people.

14201314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201314.value: This preject leverages on the PI’s previous work in developing a hospital risk management system (HRMS) with indoor application of the RFID technology. This technology tracks the location and movement of human and medical equipment and monitors real-time ward events. We have conducted a four-month pilot study of our system in a public hospital in Hong Kong. Based on the data collected, we plan to conduct further investigation for developing network-based control strategies for minimizing nosocomial inflections. Major findings and outcome are listed as follows: 1. An implementable RFID traceability system 2. An mechanism to implement the system in a realistic setting 3. A database of RFID traceability data collected from Prince of Wales Hospital 4. A traceability analytics approach 5. A contact analytics approach 5. A mathematical model for analyzing the spreading of nosocomial inflections 6. An evaluation of different control strategies

14201314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201314.value: The RFID traceabiliilty system and models can be used to analyze and control nosocomial inflections. In this project, significant effect has been spent on the development of the system, its implementation, data collection, and mathematical models. Our work in control strategies leads us to work further in this direction. We may explore effective and efficient control strategies of target immunization against nosocomial inflections. Our study is different from the existing work that generally focuses on city-level outbreaks. We believe that our work is relevant because human contact which leads to disease transmission has unique characteristics in a relatively closed and highly structured healthcare setting. We propose to conduct this work in three steps. First, we will construct time-varying human contact networks to characterize the dynamic and complex interaction between patients and healthcare workers in a healthcare institution. Second, we will formulate a concise optimization model for the outbreak minimization problem and investigate its relation to the influence maximization problem which is extensively studied in social influence analysis. Third, we will utilize optimization approaches to solve the outbreak minimization problem and derive effective and efficient control strategies against nosocomial inflections.

14201314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201314.value: SARS outbreak in 2003 makes researchers around the world conduct research work to improving the analysis and control of contagious diseases. The origin of SARS in Hong Kong was traced back to a patient admitted in a hospital. It is necessary for us to carry out more work in understanding nosocomial inflection analysis and control. In this work, we attempt to develop models and systems to achieve this goal. Based on many years of research in this direction, we have perfected our RFID traceability system and implementation mechanism. Further, we have developed a mathematical model to help us analyzing and controlling nosocomial inflections.

14201614.label: Realisation of objectives
14201614.value: Objective 1: (A) Novel Design of Dual-band Rat-race Coupler with Reconfigurable Power Dividing Ratio In this work, a novel design of reconfigurable rat-race coupler with dual-band operation has been developed. With proper circuit design, the proposed device is capable of offering the same power division ratio at two widely separated frequency bands. Moreover, the coupling ratio can be reconfigured to enable re-distribution of output power (transmission mode and rat-race mode). Besides, the proposed device also features wide operating bandwidth (~ 15%), low insertion loss (< 1 dB), high port isolation, compact size, and single control voltage with minimal number of RF switches. One journal publication was produced out of this work (IEEE Microwave and Wireless Components Letters, 2018). (B) Novel Design of Variable Signal Splitter with Extended Control Range (Voltage dividing ratio and phase difference) In this work, two novel signal control devices with enhanced characteristics (voltage dividing ratio + phase difference) have been developed. Under the control of an external voltage (tuning reactance), the input signal is split into two output components with variable voltage ratio and 0º/180º phase difference. It is also proven that that input port is always matched (i.e. independent of the tuning reactance). Compared to conventional approaches, the proposed circuit is simple and compact in structure, requires only single control voltage and minimal number of tuning diodes, and consumes almost zero bias current. Out of this research, two international conference papers (APMC, Nov. 2017) were generated. Objective 2: Realization of Polarization Agile Antenna In this work, two different types of polarization agile antennas are demonstrated including 1) linear-polarization with steerable angle of orientation; and 2) reconfigurable linear/circular polarization states. The proposed configuration basically consists of a variable signal splitter and a dual-fed dual-polarized antenna. The dual-fed antenna is used to create two linearly-polarized waves with orthogonal direction. Meanwhile, the variable splitter divides the input signal into two output components with unequal magnitude and phase difference of 0°/180°. The voltage ratio is determined by the junction capacitance of the tuning diodes (under the control of an external voltage). Therefore, by vector addition, the combined radiation field in free space will produce a linear-polarized (VLP/HLP) and/or circular-polarized (LHCP/RHCP) wave. In compared to prior works, the proposed topology offers several advantages including compact size, zero DC power consumption, easy to fabricate and single control voltage with minimal number of tuning diodes. Out of this work, one journal paper (IEEE Antenna and Wireless Propagation Letters, May 2017) and two conference publications (Asia-Pacific Microwave Conference, Nov. 2017) were produced.

14201614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201614.value: Several novel microwave signal control devices have been developed and applied to the realization of various types of polarization agile antennas. Below is a brief summary of the major findings: 1. Dual-band rat-race coupler with reconfigurable power dividing ratio has been proposed for the first time (published in IEEE MWCL 2018). This new device is compact in size, wideband and simple to control. It can offer rat-race or transmission mode operation at two widely separated frequency bands by using a simple electronic switching mechanism. One of its application is the development of dual-band antenna with reconfigurable polarization states. 2. Several variable microwave power splitters have been newly developed. These devices can offer extended control of output signals (both magnitude and polarity). The first design (published in June 2017, AWPL) is based upon the combination of two tunable rat-race couplers, while the other two devices are relying on a simplified lumped-distributed circuit structure (presented in Nov. 2017, APMC). For demonstration, they have also been applied to the realization of advanced antenna with reconfigurable polarization states (also reported in AWPL 2017 and APMC 2017). Research output (summary): 2 IEEE journal papers (published in AWPL 2017 and MWCL 2018) 2 IEEE international conference papers (presented in APMC 2017). One research student was trained (graduated in 2017). Student paper competition (Champion), IEEE (HK) AP/MTT PG conference 2017.

14201614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201614.value: Polarization diversity has received much attention from industry in recent years, due to its ability to enhance channel capacity and combat multi-path fading. The proposed polarization agile antennas are low cost, simple in structure and compact in size. Further investigation of its application to current and future wireless communication systems are of great interest. Besides, the proposed signal control devices can easily be extended to the realization of antenna array with reconfigurable polarization states and minimal construction complexity (by sharing a common control circuitry between radiating elements). Last but not the least, the proposed reconfigurable rat-race coupler may also be applied to the development of adaptive antenna technology for multi-band communication systems.

14201614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201614.value: In recent years, with increasingly demand for high data-rate wireless applications (e.g. 4G, Wi-Fi), advanced antenna technology has drawn much attention from the telecommunication community. By altering the operating frequency, polarization state or radiation pattern of antenna, the RF transmitter/receiver can be made to adapt to the ever-changing environment caused by different wave propagation phenomena (e.g. multipath effect), and hence to increase channel capacity as well as transmission quality. This research project investigates the design and development of low cost, low profile and high performance (e.g. efficiency) polarization reconfigurable antennas which is crucial to the success of future communication systems (5G, IOT).

14201714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201714.value: 在過去十年中，移動電話的大量持有和數字多媒體的廣泛應用產生了對於高速大容量無線通信前所未有的需求。這場無線通信的革命得益於先進的數字信號處理技術的問世，以及在微電子和蜂窩網絡方面持續不斷的技術突破。其中，促進無線網絡提供極高數據傳輸速率的一項關鍵技術是對多輸入多輸出(MIMO) 連接的採用。對於MIMO技術的廣泛研究旨在提高其信道容量，帶寬，增益和分集。其研究成果被列入多種無線標準，包括IEEE 802.11n (Wi-Fi), IEEE 802.16 (WiMax), 4G和3GPP LTE。 MIMO系統一般允許在通信鏈路發送端和接收端同時使用多於一個天線。這種拓撲結構不僅可以實現更高的頻譜效率，也能更好的權衡分集和速率。儘管MIMO的優點很多，它卻存在一些固有的缺點。首先，不可避免的干擾會大大降低MIMO的潛在增益，尤其是在應用於多用戶共享頻譜時個體用戶需要處理在同一小區內不期望的干擾。其次，如何為MIMO干擾信道設計最佳方式來權衡分集、速率和復雜性也是個重要的問題。雖然近年來提出的各種干擾對齊策略提高了MIMO系統的整體性能，還有很多挑戰有待解決。在這個項目中，我們建議採取更深入，更綜合的信號處理方法來研究MIMO干擾信道的相關問題。我們的目標是設計出一套專門針對分佈式無線MIMO信道的干擾可控的信號傳輸技術。這項技術旨在實現最大傳輸速率或最大容量因子，即自由度。我們還將設計針對MIMO干擾信道和MIMO X信道的有效空時調製和編碼，從而提高系統的可靠性。新的空時碼將能夠得到干擾信道的最大分集增益。我們還將詳細分析所提出編碼的速率、分集和解碼複雜度之間的平衡。我們預期，所提出的新穎的信號處理技術可以用於不同信道條件下的MIMO傳輸，來顯著提高未來無線通信系統的數據速率。該項目的成果將在商業和軍事中都具有潛在的應用前景，諸如蜂窩通信，無線區域網絡，家庭網絡，設備網絡和傳感器網絡。

14201714.label: Realisation of objectives
14201714.value: It is essential to be able to approximate capacity characterization of wireless communications, where the Degree of Freedom (DoF) provides accurate capacity estimation and offers fundamental insights into how interference management can be achieved. DoF represents the number of interference-free dimensions in distributed wireless networks. However, when aligning an arbitrarily large number of interferers within a MIMO system, the link itself might not necessarily be free from interference. In this project, we aim to design effective interference resilient signal transmission techniques that are tailored for distributed wireless MIMO channels with an objective to maximizing the achievable transmission rate or DoF. We consider the abstract model where there are K pairs of transmitter-receiver concurrently sending data while each pair causes interference to all other pairs, referred to as K-user interference channels and specifically for a two-user X channels where each transmitter sends data to both receivers and each receiver gets desired signals from both transmitters but also receives multi-user interference. In this study, all the transmitters and receivers are equipped with multiple antennas. 1. Interference Alignment for MIMO X channels We studied the MIMO X network where each node is installed with an arbitrary number of antennas and a systematic interference alignment and cancellation scheme has been devised that can approach the DoF upper bound as far as possible. By carefully grouping the information messages and designing the corresponding pre-coding vectors, we managed to make the scheme flexible for arbitrary number of transmitter/receiver antennas. Specifically, we divided the MIMO X channels into three categories according to the number of antennas to be used in each node. The first case represents the scenario when the number of antennas at both receivers is larger than that of the two transmitters. The second case is just the opposite in which both transmitters have more antennas than both receivers. The third category refers to cases that do not fall under the previous two categories, namely one of the two receivers has more antennas than one transmitter and not as many antennas as the other transmitter. For the first case, the channel matrix between any pair of transmitter and receiver is “tall”, so the interference cannot be cancelled by any precoding vectors. To maximize the signal space, we utilized the interference alignment to “squeeze” all the interference at receiver. For the second case, the channel matrix is a “fat” one, so we developed pre-coding vectors that are orthogonal to the channel matrix to cancel the interference. For the third case, we treated the interference from the two transmitters in different way. For the interference coming from the transmitter having more antennas than the receiver, we cancelled the interference as many as possible and then align them. Whilst for the interference from the other transmitter that has fewer antennas than the receiver, we aligned them in a subspace with the least number of dimensions. 2. Interference Alignment for 3-user MIMO Interference Channels Here, we designed an effective interference alignment technique for 3-user MIMO interference channels. To maximize the sum DoF, we considered a general case that all three transmitters could send different number of signals. Assume that a total of D signals can be sent from all the transmitters, which should be maximized. Then, we have three strategies to distribute the signals among the three transmitters. In strategy 1, each transmitter sends the same number of signals, denoted by X, In strategy 2, one transmitter sends one more signal than other two transmitters while in strategy 3, one transmitter sends one less signal than other two transmitters. Hence, existing works can be viewed as strategy 1 only and clearly it may not achieve the maximum sum of DoF. In order to maximize the value of X, equivalently the sum of DoF, we proposed interference alignment and cancellation to null the interference so as to leave maximum signal space. For Strategies 1, 2, and 3, we determined the optimal value of X, respectively, and then choose the best strategy. During the course of this study, we also spent effort in devising a cost-efficient optimization of base station densities for multi-tier heterogeneous cellular networks. A multitier heterogeneous network providing universal coverage may also include distributed antennas and relays stations, therefore, coupled together with the deployment of successful MIMO configuration will help to meet the exponential of mobile data traffic. 3. Blind Interference Alignment with Reconfigurable Antenna and Space-Time Codes for MIMO Wireless Networks In wireless interference network, interference alignment requires perfect channel state information at the transmitters so that interference can be aligned by choosing proper beam-forming vectors. However, it is very difficult to obtain the perfect CSI at transmitters in the distributed network. To address this problem, we explored blind interference alignment (BIA) schemes that do not need the CSI at transmitters, by utilizing reconfigurable antennas at each receiver. We considered using one reconfigurable antenna at each receiver instead of multiple conventional antennas. We further proposed a systematic design of BIA schemes that can be applied to K-user interference channels. The transmitted signals of each user was chosen so that the interference was received at least once in a “clean” state, meaning that all transmitters excluding the one generating the interference should keep silent in some time slots. Then, with the known interference, each receiver can cancel it from the received signals at other time slots and blind interference alignment can be achieved at receiver by selecting different patterns of reconfigurable antenna, equivalently choosing different channel modes. For MIMO wireless networks using conventional multiple antennas, we derived a set of design criteria for space-time codes that can achieve full diversity without CSI at the transmitters. Unfortunately there is no way that the receiver of the target user could have access to the system parameters of other users generating the undesired interference. In this work, we enhanced the design algorithm with an objective to getting a systematic space-time coding structure for each user with multiple antennas that can achieve full diversity after interference cancellation. The advantage of this method is that no channel state information at the transmitter side is known a priori and inter-user interference is canceled by using group ZF receiver rather than interference alignment. Full diversity space-time code design without CSIT for MIMO interference channel and MIMO X channel has been studied. We also dedicated our effort to improve the transmission rate of the space-time codes for both the MIMO interference channels as well as the MIMO X channels.

14201714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201714.value: We studied the how DoF gain can be obtained in a MIMO X channel and proposed an interference alignment scheme with synergistic CSIT for its deployment. The achievable DoF is shown to be greater than the optimal DoF obtained with outdated CSIT, and that achievable DoF equals to the optimal value with outdated CSIT together with transmitter cooperation [C2]. We explored the architecture optimization of multitier open-access downlink heterogeneous cellular networks. By using stochastic geometry, the problems of optimizing the densities of BSs in different tiers are shown to be linear-fractional programming that can be transformed into linear programming by employing Chamers-Cooper transformation. The linear-fractional programming can then be solved efficiently. Our results indicate that enlarging the densities of BSs may not always improve network throughput and the optimal densities of each tier exist to satisfying users' demands. Numerical results demonstrate the significant throughput gain from the optimal deployment of multitier heterogeneous cellular networks [J1]. We also considered an asynchronous two-way relay network in which a few distributed relays assist in the communication between two single-antenna terminals through analog network coding. The asynchronous transmission between relays and terminals causes symbol misalignments and results in diversity lass in space-time codes. We proposed a family of zero-padded time reversal STC for the path delay difference. For two-relay scenarios, three code designs based on Alamouti code, quasi-orthogonal space-time block code and multi-group decodable STC are provided for each relay with one, two or four antennas, respectively. Simulations confirm the full diversity gain of all designs. The bit-error-rate performance in asynchronous situations is almost similar to that in synchronous cases [J2] We derived the DoF for a three-user MIMO broadcast channel with delayed CSIT for most antenna configurations except for the case of 2N

14201714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201714.value: Current interference alignment techniques take advantage of channel variations by exploiting beamforming at transmitters, which means the channel state information (CSI) is required at transmitters. However, in practice the CSI is usually estimated at receivers and then fed back to the transmitters, which means the CSI at transmitters may be imperfect. In particular, for high speed vehicular communications the wireless channel varies fast and the channel estimation is hard to be perfect. Hence, it is interesting and necessary to investigate the effect of imperfect CSI estimation on the performance of interference alignment. On the other hand, it should be aware that the feedback of CSI is usually expressed with a sequence of binary bits, which means the received CSI is quantized instead of perfect one. Such quantized feedback of CSI can certainly bring inaccuracy to the interference alignment and cancellation, and hence lead to interference leakage. Perhaps in future work, one should investigate the impact of quantized feedback on interference alignment for various communication networks. Further, it is also necessary to design low-overhead CSI feedback strategies by leveraging spatial and temporal correlations of multiple antenna channels to improve CSI quantization in limited feedback.

14201714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201714.value: One of the key driving technologies that facilitate wireless networks to be able to deliver extremely high data rates is the adoption of MIMO connectivity. MIMO, however, suffers from several inherent drawbacks. First, inevitable interference will greatly degrade MIMO’s potential gain, especially in multiuser applications. Second, it is not trivial how diversity, rate and complexity can be comprised in the best possible manner for MIMO interference channels. In this project, we have designed a suite of interference resilient signal transmission techniques that are tailored for distributed wireless MIMO channels with an objective to maximizing the achievable transmission rate and the degree of freedom. Specifically, DoF of a three-user MIMO broadcast channel with delayed CSIT for most antenna configurations has been studied in great detail. We also devise effective space-time modulation and coding schemes for MIMO interference channels and MIMO X channels to improve the reliability of the system. The new space-time codes are able to reap the maximum diversity benefit of the interference channels. In addition, The outcomes of the project will have potential applications for both commercial and military communication systems such as cellular communications, wireless LAN, home networks, device networks, and sensor networks.
