14201814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201814.value: Video content distribution has become a major application of the Internet. Large video service providers such as YouTube and Netflix have hundreds of millions of users, consuming a good fraction of Internet bandwidth. Improving the efficiency and user experience of such large-scale systems can create significant impact, and is an active area of research. For our research in this area, we are collaborating with a large-scale Internet video service provider in China - Tencent Video. They are operating a CDN-based VoD streaming system similar to YouTube or Netflix. The video content includes movies, TV episodes, Short videos (MVs, Sports, News) and user generated content. The customer base is large, with 45 million active users on a daily basis. Each user access of a video generates a separate view report. By analyzing the view reports, it is possible to improve service efficiency, service functionality and user quality of experience (QoE). We have started working on a couple of fronts: (a) How to allocate resources (mainly server bandwidth) to different user requests given the fact that users tend to quit a video before the end? (b) How to compute a reliable indicator of video popularity dynamically? We applied for GRF to work on (a) last year. Though it was not funded, we have made some progress. In particular, we have completed a study of the users' video browsing behavior. We have also formulated the problem of "smart progressive downloading" that tries to use available bandwidth for judicious pre-fetching, taking into account of which users are more likely to make use of the pre-fetched content. Preliminary analysis and simulation has already demonstrated that the idea works. We propose to continue this study, to derive our results analytically; and to incorporate our strategy to work with multi-version video distribution systems. Question (b) is a new direction. Currently, a common practice is to use view count to indicate video popularity. We propose to enhance it by (1) removing fake views; and (2) incorporating viewing duration. We also propose to take a systematic look at video popularity distribution, and how it changes over time. These results can help video recommendation, system accounting, as well as improving resource allocation strategies. Since there is a significant overlap with last year's GRF application, we submit this proposal as a re-submission. 视频内容分发已经成为互联网的一个主要的应用。诸如Youtube、Netflix 之类的大型视频服务提供商，拥有数以亿计的用户，占据了大部分的网络带宽。因此，提高此类大型视频服务系统的工作效率和用户体验可以产生巨大的影响，是一个热门研究领域。 我们和中国的一家大型网络视频服务提供商——腾讯视频合作，展开了在这个领域的研究。腾讯视频和YouTube以及Netflix一样，使用基于内容分发网络（ CDN）技术的流媒体点播系统。视频内容包括电影、电视节目、视频短片（MV 、体育、新闻等）和用户自行上传的内容等。腾讯视频的用户群很大，每天有四千五百万左右的活跃用户。腾讯视频会针对每个用户的每个视频观看行为产成独立的报告。我们可以通过分析用户行为报告来提高系统的服务效率、服务功能和用户体验。我们已经开始了如下几个方面的研究：（ 1）如何针对不同的用户请求分配资源（主要是服务器带宽）；（2）如何对视频的热度提供一个动态可靠的计算指标。

14201814.label: Realisation of objectives
14201814.value: In this project, our first overall goal is to refine our idea of "Smart Progressive Downloading" (SPD) through modeling/analysis, and trying to incorporate it into a practical video streaming protocol such as DASH. We have mostly completed this objective and published a journal paper with complete analysis of the model and algorithms for SPD. I gave it 90% because it is still possible to derive a more complete model and solution, but the usefulness may only be academic. SPD is the best streaming approach for a content provider if it wishes to use up all its procured maximum (server) bandwidth. DASH is the de facto standard in practice. When we tried to incorporate our idea into DASH (object 2), we find that there is a significant difference in the objective of DASH, namely it does not necessarily try to use up all the bandwidth procured. Hence it is not realistic to make SPD part of DASH. So we cannot claim we completed this objective. The fault, I think, is that we did not formulate a realistic objective originally. We have a good/solid solution with regards to fake views, and our publications on this topic are accumulating citations. This goal is completed satisfactorily. The method of using view duration for indicating popularity is well put forth in our paper, so that objective is also mostly finished (I would put 100% if content providers actually take our suggestion and start using it). Lastly, we have done a lot of work on video popularity dynamics analysis, modeling and prediction. The work on this topic is the major part of a PhD thesis (Jiqiang Wu). We have published a couple of IEEE journal papers on this, and the work on prediction is still being submitted to a journal.

14201814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201814.value: Multimedia content distribution is a practical and demanding problem for the Internet. Our work from this project has made important contributions in this area. Interesting problems continue to come up, and we have started working on a couple of them: a) Smart streaming of panoramic videos: in this case, we need to design algorithms to stream videos to satisfy users current attention (which is only part of the entire video). This problem is very challenging, as it requires modeling user's attention, and understanding good coding techniques for satisfying user's attention yet saving as much bandwidth as possible at the same time. b) Economic analysis of multiple content providers competing for eyeballs. For this work, we got an interesting data set that show the video content provider market is an oligopoly. Our economic model allows us to explain why that is so (rather than a monopoly).

14201814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201814.value: Our research formulated the problem, and derived the best strategy (smart progressive downloading) to use up a content provider's procured bandwidth to satisfy video streaming needs. This is an important contribution for many video streaming scenarios. Our work also proposed effective ways to detect view counts (for videos) generated artificially (e.g. by robots). This is useful for enhancing a content provider's service. Lastly, we have analyzed how video popularity change over time, for different videos, and proposed methods to predict future popularity based on past history and other features. This is a very hot research topic, and the insights are useful even beyond predicting video popularity.

14201914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201914.value: In this information age, we deal with a vast amount of data every day, for personal or business use. Cloud technologies appear promising in streamlining information processing --- Users do not need to store all their data and install all related software in their local machine, or take care of issues like backup and versioning. A crucial feature of cloud computing is security. Traditional encryption provides confidentiality, but disallows useful operations like indexing. Searchable encryption (SE) aims to provide confidentiality and searchability simultaneously. The data owner can delegate a token for a specific query, which allows the server to perform the query over encrypted data. Motivated by the wide applicability, a flurry of new SE schemes appeared. However, many of them follow an ad-hoc design of translating particular queries to its encrypted version, and might not have undergone rigorous analysis according to the cryptographers' standard. Also, designing SE schemes which achieve multiple features simultaneously is a non-trivial task, due to the difficulty in striking a balance in security, functionality, and efficiency. This project aims to push the frontier of this vibrant field. Firstly, we propose a design framework of SE, which shed light on what are the essential designs for each feature. In particular, it provides a foundation for our goal of proposing the following new symmetric-key SE (SSE) schemes with interesting properties. We aim to propose an SSE for similarity search. The novelty here is that unforeseen query can be supported, as long a similarity measure is defined. Then we address how to achieve (almost)-optimal efficiency (O(r/p + log(r))) for performing parallel search over dynamic data while the state-of-the-art is O(r/p log(n)), where p, r, n are the numbers of processors, query results, and records in the whole database respectively. Finally, SSE received more attention than public-key SE due to its high efficiency. We will investigate the possibility of a general framework of extending SSE to the public-key setting, such that everyone can create ciphertext for a recipient to decrypt or generate search token. Two closely related primitives of SE are order-preserving encryption and deterministic encryption. Our final foci include investigating the security of SE schemes based on these primitives, and propose chosen-ciphertext-secure public-key deterministic encryption schemes under a broader class of assumptions. Completion of this project will result in new SE schemes for practical scenarios and unlock the potential of cloud computing, and make a broad impact on cryptography, network, systems, and database communities. 在這個信息時代，無論是為個人或商業使用，我們每天都在處理大量數據。雲端運算技術有很大潛力簡化信息處理 - 用戶無需存儲所有數據，並無需在於本地機器安裝及維護所有相關的軟件（如備份和版本控制）。安全性在雲計算是重要的一環。傳統加密方法只能提供機密性，但不允許如搜索等有用操作。 可搜尋加密（SE）旨在同時提供機密性和可搜索性。數據擁有者可以為特定的查詢建造一個令牌，從而允許並委託服務器對已加密數據進行查詢。 在其廣泛應用的推動下，新的SE方案不斷湧現。然而，不少方案都是按照特定查詢即席設計其加密版本，並沒有根據合乎密碼學家標準之嚴格分析。另外，面對在安全性，功能性和效率中取得平衡的難度， 設計能同時實現多種功能的 SE方案並不簡單。 此項目旨在突破SE這個領域。首先，我們提出一個通用框架，用以闡明每個功能的設計理念。特別是，它為以下新的對稱密鑰SE（SSE）的方案奠定了基礎： 一）提出支持相似搜索的SSE，其創新之處在於只要有相似性的定義，SSE便能支持未知的查詢。 二）如何實現近乎最優效率的並行搜索動態SSE，目前最先進的SSE的並行搜索效率並非最高。 三）SSE的效率比公鑰SE高，故SSE受到較多的關注。我們將調查如何延伸SSE到公鑰SE，使得每個人都可以加密，而且收件人依然可以解密或產生搜索令牌。 保序加密和確定性加密是和SE密切相關的工具。我們另一個焦點包括調查基於這些工具的SE方案的安全性，並提出更好的方案。 此項目將產生能應用於實際情景的新SE方案，開發雲端運算的潛力，並在密碼學，網絡，系統和數據庫等領域產生廣泛的影響。

14201914.label: Realisation of objectives
14201914.value: In addition to our works in ICDCS15, ProvSec 15, and ITCS16 reported in our mid-term report. We have many more results which realized the objectives of this project. In short, the main results include ICDCS15, ITCS16, SecureComm16 (2 papers), ACNS17, Infocom18, and TDSC18. We also have many related results as we went further in multiple directions. 1) Our survey formed the basis of the whole project. Part of the survey has been presented in my various invited talks and my two postgraduate courses (see "Other impact"). We have also written a book chapter per invitation. However, due to some issue with the editor, we decided to withdraw it and find another place to publish it. 2) We did have some related results but there is no accepted paper directly addressing the main objective so far. Yet, this is because the more we delve into it, the more interesting problems we found, which has led us to two other funded GRF proposals. Our initial write-up as reported in the mid-term review is nearly completely re-written. Back then, we formulated a "game-based" security definition (which is a usual definition for public-key searchable encryption) and proposed a provably secure scheme based on practical cryptographic primitives. We then got an important comment from a reviewer asking whether a "simulation-based" security definition is achievable (which is usual for a symmetric-key scheme). Achieving it turns out to be highly non-trivial. To start with, it required a dedicated effort to formulate the new definition. We achieved two results, one is "weakly" secure (similar to the game-based definition) but is more practical, one is "fully" secure but requires primitives which do not exist in the literature yet! This is currently under submission. We also found alternative ways to achieve the same general objective. Eventually, our study here has led us to our funded GRF17/18 proposal. We thus consider this as a success since we did achieve what we intended, and we are opening two new research avenues with many unsolved research problems! Besides, we did achieve some specific results under the general context of this objective. In COCOON16, we proposed a combiner for security against chosen-ciphertext attack (CCA), the de-facto security of encryption, in both symmetric-key and public-key settings. Namely, we show how to combine two encryption schemes, where we cannot be assured that which one is really CCA-secure, to a new scheme that is CCA-secure. In SACMAT16, we proposed a framework of multi-authority attribute-based encryption (ABE) with outsourcing and revocation. In other words, we understood what it takes for some advanced features of ABE. The knowledge forms a valuable baseline for anonymous ABE which implies public-key searchable encryption. In Usenix Security17, we proposed a password hardening service which allows an authentication server, with the help of a crypto server, to authenticate its users who may use weak passwords, without storing any information that can be exploited by an offline dictionary attack. We are not simply trusting the crypto server, so we built the secure two-party computation protocol between them. We then thought about extending this concept to a new notion which enables a user who only has a weak password to not only get authenticated but also derive a cryptographic key. Similar to our objective which extends symmetric-key to public-key, we extend weak-password to symmetric-key. This idea contributes to our funded GRF18/19 proposal. In TIFS18, we study an application of searchable encryption in biometric identification, i.e., given a biometric reading, an untrusted server can search over the encrypted database to find a match. We proposed schemes in both symmetric-key and public-key setting, under different threat models. Again, this forms the baseline of what can be achieved for a specific application. 3) Our TDSC18 work proposed two schemes for similarity search over encrypted high-dimensional data. One is based on symmetric-key primitive (pseudorandom functions) and another uses public-key homomorphic encryption. Both use locality sensitive hashing to avoid preparing indices for every possible query. In Infocom18, we realized sub-linear encrypted image searches, by employing an untrusted crypto server similar to our Usenix Security17 work. We also worked on other data types. In SecureComm16 (Zhang--Wang--Chow) and AsiaCCS16, we realized encrypted and authenticated multi-pattern matching respectively. In PETS17, we realized threshold private set intersection, which allows a party to search the membership of her query data in another dataset but only learn the result when there is a sufficient number of matches. In ESORICS17, we realized privacy-preserving decision trees evaluation via linear functions, i.e., relying on only additive (instead of fully) homomorphic encryption. The last two papers are not exactly searchable encryption but the querier can still search without knowing the counterparty's database. 4) In SecureComm16 (Lai--Chow), we proposed a parallel and dynamic structured encryption scheme which supports matrix and graph data in particular. In ACNS17, we proposed forward-secure searchable encryption on labeled bipartite graphs. We also proposed a generalized definition of forward security and a generic construction to equip a non-forward-secure scheme forward security. 5) In AsiaCCS17, we proposed the first updatable block-level message-locked encryption in the literature. This allows the server to efficiently search existing encrypted blocks for deduplication while allowing efficient (sub-linear) block-level update. As explained in the mid-term report, instead of studying non-rigorous schemes directly which rely on the property-preserving property of underlying encryption, we moved our focus to a more general question of processing encrypted data and study how existing works fail to provide privacy. In particular, in IWSEC16, we proposed privacy-preserving wi-fi fingerprinting indoor localization. This allows a client to query a database server to learn its location based on its wi-fi fingerprint. The server would not now the client's query and the client would not learn extra information about the database. Existing solutions did not follow a cryptographic approach or are more heavyweight than our solution. In WiSec17, we proposed a system which supports encrypted geosocial query, i.e., answering the questions of where is this user, who is nearby, and how close is this user from another user. Our system also works on multi-dimensional data. In PAC17, we proposed a secure strategyproof ascending-price spectrum auction scheme which allows a set of network nodes to perform bidding using encrypted bids. This work also points out that an existing scheme fails to provide privacy as claimed. In TrustCom16, we studied a more general functionality of performing ridge regression over encrypted data, which a specific machine learning technique for analyzing multiple regression data. In TDSC (to appear), we revisited the study of anonymous communication which handles forwarding of encrypted traffic. Before our work, anonymity definitions are usually not well-defined or too complicated. In between are ad-hoc definitions for specific protocols which sometimes only provide weakened anonymity guarantees. We gave a hierarchy of anonymity definitions. We also proposed a modular construction from any key-private public-key encryption scheme, and a new primitive -- oblivious forwarding protocols (with two constructions). With all these results, we thus consider all our objectives are achieved successfully. * Regarding "research experience for undergraduate students," I have been supervising many undergraduates for research-type final-year projects (requires no support) or summer projects (supported by the Faculty). I did recruit a part-time student helper for a research project on searchable encryption, just I eventually supported him via another means. That said, I appreciate the budget for this purpose, and I will continue to foster undergraduate research. (1200 words. The HTML tags are for better formatting online.)

14201914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201914.value: *ITCS16: We show how to perform many cryptographic tasks with privacy and authenticity including searchable encryption in the parallel random-access machine model. *ProvSec15: We show that programmability of the random oracle model is necessary for the signature scheme implied by the first public-key searchable encryption due to Boneh et al. *SACMAT16: We show a framework of upgrading a selected class of attribute-based encryption to support multi-authority, outsourcing, and revocation. *COCOON16: We show how to achieve chosen-ciphertext security when given two encryption schemes which only one of them is really secure, without requiring to know which one is it. *AsiaCCS16, SecureComm16: (Zhang--Wang--Chow) We show how to ensure authenticity and privacy for multi-pattern matching over encrypted query and database. *ICDCS15, SecureComm16 (Lai--Chow), ACNS17: We build forward secure, dynamic and parallel searchable encryption schemes for a bipartite graph which covers the basic keyword-file data structure in particular. *Usenix Security17: We show an existing password hardening scheme is vulnerable to offline attacks, propose a stronger security definition, and propose a password hardening scheme which is secure and even more efficient. *TDSC18, Infocom18: We show how to support similarity search over encrypted images in different settings. *IWSEC16, WiSec17: We show how to process encrypted location data for wifi localization and location-based services over social networks. *AsiaCCS17: We show how to how to deduplicate encrypted data at block-level while supporting update efficiently. *PoPETS17: We show how to do threshold private set intersection. *TrustCom16, ESORICS17: We show how to perform privacy-preserving ridge regression and decision tree evaluations. *PAC17: We show how an existing scheme fails to provide privacy and how to do privacy-preserving strategyproof ascending-price spectrum auction. *TIFS18: We show how to do privacy-preserving biometric authentication. *TDSC (to appear): We revisit anonymous communication. Specifically, we propose a rigorous security definition and a generic construction which achieves it. We also propose two instantiations and evaluate them empirically.

14201914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201914.value: It turns out that Objective 2 is a very rich research topic which is bigger than we have expected. It has led to a funded GRF project "Sublinear Multi-Writer Searchable Encryption --- Bridging Symmetric-Key to Public-Key Paradigm" in the year of 2017/18. The objectives of this project centered around searchable encryption, which belongs to the bigger topic of processing encrypted data. This project carried out solid research work which has led to two funded GRF projects in the year of 2018/19 on "Password-Hardening Services" and 2019/20 on "Deep Learning with Privacy."

14201914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201914.value: We deal with a vast amount of data every day. Cloud technologies appear promising in streamlining information processing --- Users do not need to store all their data and install all related software in their local machine, or take care of issues like backup and versioning. A crucial feature of cloud computing is security. Traditional encryption provides confidentiality, but disallows useful operations like indexing. Searchable encryption provides confidentiality and searchability simultaneously --- The data owner can use his/her secret to authorize the server to perform a specific query over encrypted data. Early research focuses on keyword search. Supporting feature-rich data such as images and dynamic updates of the encrypted database and seem natural yet non-trivial since the underlying data structure is also encrypted. Supporting parallel processing requires special data structure too which can be more difficult to maintain across updates. Moreover, insertion of a record may be linked to a previously authorized search (i.e. no "forward security"), which leaks partial information about the insertion. We proposed dynamic and parallel searchable encryption schemes for structured data with forward security. We also studied processing encrypted data in general, e.g., deduplication over encrypted data, private matchmaking, biometric authentication, location-based services, machine learning as a service, etc.

14202514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202514.value: The aim of this project is to develop a virtual environment for the training of percutaneous nephroscopic skills, and to build a virtual operative anatomy model facilitating surgeons in learning surgical anatomy in the renal region. With the development of techniques for percutaneous access and equipment to fragmentize calculi, nephroscopic surgery has been more commonly used by urologists as the procedure of choice for lithotripsy, kidney stone extraction, the removal of large renal calculi and the management of intra-renal strictures, infundibular stenosis, renal cysts and renal pyelocalyceal tumors. Although it is more invasive than retrograde ureteroscopy, In difficult renal anatomies and patient conditions, percutaneous nephroscopy has been demonstrated high efficiency and low morbidity. However, compared to open kidney surgery, urologists must have firm knowledge of surgical-anatomic landmarks of calyces and the collecting system in mind so as to access target, such as calculi, tumors or occluded collecting system aptly. The learning curve on real patient cases is considerably steep for novice clinicians to acquire the ability on localizing adequate incision placement and directing least traumatic anatomical pathways to target through percutaneous nephroscopic techniques. Training on animals or human cadaver is not able to reproduce phenomena likely to occur in real life and there is a call for virtual reality based trainer which could simulate more life-like with pathological conditions. This research will be using virtual reality with reference to stereoscopic endoscopic images as well as ultra-high resolution visible human renal datasets for the learner to interactively navigate and incise in the virtual environment. Surgical sites in percutaneous nephroscopy can be complicated as renal calyces orientated quite differently from patient to patient, major variations include the varying size/direction of calyces; relative positioning of big artery or vein; as well as shifting of kidney itself towards ribs or colon. 3-D images with preoperative information on the kidney cortex, medullary pyramid, renal capsule/pelvis, calyces and vasculature, will be provided while a comprehensive anatomical database with pathological variations is to be incorporated. To summarize, this is a joint project between a pioneer VR development team and a leading urology surgery team in Hong Kong. We aim to construct a training system with simulated percutaneous nephroscopy on different conditions of renal cavity for practicing incision/stone fragmentation skills on virtual patients. We expect the proposed system to strengthen existing urology education and will translate into improved urology surgical skill in the operating theatre in the end. 摘要 這項目的是開發用於經皮腎鏡技術培訓的虛擬環境，並建立一個虛擬手術解剖模型促進外科醫生學習在腎區的三維解剖結構。 隨著經皮進入技術和瓦解結石設備的發展，經皮腎鏡手術已成為泌尿科醫生作為首選的取腎結石、去除腎囊腫或腫瘤及管理腎內狹窄的程序。雖然它比衝擊波碎石和逆行輸尿管鏡手術更具侵入性的，經皮腎鏡手術被應用於複雜病時既高效且併發率低。基於這些優點，經皮腎鏡術被廣泛地應用到管理連接部梗阻的輸尿管、腎盞／腎漏斗部狹窄、以及尿路上皮癌等。然而相對於開腹腎臟手術，泌尿科醫師必須深入掌握腎盞和腎集合系統的外科解剖知識，以便到達目標：如結石、腫瘤或腎集合系統的阻塞位置等。對新醫生來說，判斷切口位置和如何減少小創傷，對經皮腎鏡技術能力的要求十分高，學習曲線是相當陡峭的。但目前的此手術培訓主要仍基於人類屍體或豬，局限於正常或動物解剖模擬，有必要開發更符現實生活病理狀態的訓練系統。 本研究將使用虛擬現實（VR）並參考超高分辨率的虛擬人腹腔的數據集，讓學習者能互動地在虛擬空間中定位和解剖。因在不同病人中，可作腎鏡進入腎盞的取向可以完全不同，其他主要病理變化包括腎盞的不同尺寸/方向、大的動脈或靜脈的相對位置、以及對肋骨或結腸腎臟本身的轉移等；手術部位比較複雜。新研發系統將提供術前信息，顯示包括腎皮質、腎髓金字塔、腎小囊/骨盆、腎盞和血管系統等的三維圖像，並併入全面的病理變化解剖數據。 總的來說，這是一個由創新的虛擬環境開發團隊和領先的腎鏡手術團隊在香港的深入合作的項目，我們的目標是建立一個虛擬腎鏡培訓體系，模擬出能實行切開/石碎片技能上虛擬病人。我們預計建議的制度，能加強現有泌尿外科教育，最終將提升泌尿外科手術總體水平。

14202814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202814.value: 本课题将￼就建立下一代由蜂窝网和Wi-Fi高度集成的宽带移动通信网络提供新的政策建议、经济机制和技术算法。随着智能手机和平板电脑的广泛使用，用户对移动数据的需求一直在迅速增长。思科最近预测全球移动数据流量将在2012年至2017年之间增长13倍。这将与全球蜂窝网络容量的相对缓慢增长形成鲜明对比。从另一方面来讲，Wi-Fi技术以其无牌照特性和在全球的广泛使用成为蜂窝技术的极佳伴侣。Wi-Fi网络可以帮助负载过大的蜂窝网络分流，降低移动运营商的成本，提高用户的满意度。为了实现蜂窝和Wi-Fi技术的高度集成，我们需要采取前瞻性的无线频谱政策，设计有效的经济机制，和提供创新性的技术解决方案。这将导致移动系统生态系统的模式转变，并会影响到频谱监管机构，蜂窝和Wi-Fi无线运营商以及手机用户关于技术和经济的多种决定。在本课题中，我们计划解决以下几个关键问题：（1）应该如何在蜂窝和Wi-Fi无线技术之间分配频谱资源？ （2）如何提供经济激励措施和以最大限度地提高和共享Wi-Fi数据分流带来的效益？ （3）如何优化数据分流算法，降低网络成本，改善网络服务质量？ （4）用户应如何在异质无线网络中协作？我们的研究团队在无线资源分配，网络优化和控制，网络博弈和经济学方面有多年的研究经验。本课题的研究成果会帮助我们了解规划未来移动宽带网络的机会和挑战，并对如何显著提高网络性能和用户满意度有更深的认识。本课题带来的新的政策，经济，技术方面的建议和解决方案将加速下一代由蜂窝网和Wi-Fi高度集成的宽带移动通信网络的建设。

14202814.label: Realisation of objectives
14202814.value: We are pleased to report that the project team has achieved all project objectives, through collaborations with many top researchers around the world. This project is theoretical in nature. We have answered several key questions related to the integration and interactions between cellular and Wi-Fi networks in future networks. These questions include: (1) How should a spectrum regulator allocate spectrum between cellular and Wi-Fi technologies? (2) How to provide economic incentives to maximize and fairly share the data offloading benefits in the network? (3) How to optimize data offloading algorithms that best trade off network cost reductions and users’ Quality of Service improvements? (4) How should users take advantage of integrated and heterogeneous mobile networks in a collaborative fashion? Here is a quick summary of our key results: We have studied how users should switch between licensed and unlicensed spectrum bands and effectively offload the traffic to reduce the stress on the cellular networks. We have investigated how the regulator should allocate spectrum resources among licensed and unlicensed spectrum. We have proposed low complexity close-to-optimal scheduling algorithms for discrete power control in cellular networks. We have suggested optimal dynamic pricing and admission control mechanisms to support heterogeneous secondary users. We examined how a community wireless network operator should offer contracts to owners of private Wi-Fi access points. We analyzed user-provided wireless networks and propose effective incentive mechanisms for communication and energy resources sharing. We analyzed how cellular users should trade mobile data with each other to improve their satisfaction levels. We proposed a reverse auction mechanism for cellular networks and Wi-Fi networks to fairly share the unlicensed bands. We considered the interactions among Wi-Fi operators, advertisers, and mobile users, and propose a differential pricing scheme to maximize the Wi-Fi operator's profit. We proposed resource allocation and incentive mechanisms for mobile crowd sensing. We have extensively used methodologies including auction theory, pricing theory, noncooperative game theory, bargaining theory, mechanism design, nonlinear optimization, and graph theory in our research. Results related to this projects have appeared in 1 monograph, 19 top IEEE/ACM journals and magazines, and 22 leading international conference papers. This project has helped train 6 Ph.D. students and has led to one Best Paper Award Finalist and one Best Student Paper Award. The detailed summary is given in Part C.

14202814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202814.value: We study how users should switch between licensed and unlicensed spectrum bands and effectively offload the traffic to reduce the stress on the cellular networks. We characterize the impact of incomplete network information, users' QoS requirements, service providers' economics incentives, group bargaining of Wi-Fi providers with cellular providers, secrecy and energy considerations. This is related to journal publications 2, 4, 9, 12, 13, 17, and 18 and conference publication 7. We study how the regulator should allocate spectrum resources among licensed and unlicensed spectrum. We propose contract and information market models to support the super-WiFi services over TV white space networks. This is related to journal publications 6, 7, 8, and 10, the monograph, conference publications 5, 6, 11 and 15. We propose low complexity close-to-optimal scheduling algorithms for discrete power control in cellular networks. This is related to journal publication 1 and conference paper 6. We propose optimal dynamic pricing and admission control mechanisms to support heterogeneous secondary users, and we characterize how an MVNO should invest spectrum resources under uncertainty. This is related to journal publications 3 and 11. We examine how a community wireless network operator should offer contracts to owners of private Wi-Fi access points, under both complete and incomplete network information. This is related to journal publication 16 and conference publications 1 and 10. We analyze user-provided wireless networks and propose effective incentive mechanisms for communication and energy resources sharing. We study the network optimization and auction mechanism design for crowdsourced mobile video streaming. This is related to journal publications 13 and 18 and conference publications 4, 5, 12, 14, 16, 17 and 19. We analyze how cellular users should trade mobile data with each other to improve their satisfaction. This is related to journal publication 15 and conference publication 13. We propose a reverse auction mechanism for cellular networks and Wi-Fi networks to fairly share the unlicensed bands. This is related to journal publication 20 and conference publication 2. We consider the interactions among Wi-Fi operators, advertisers, and mobile users, and propose a differential pricing scheme to maximize the Wi-Fi operator's profit. This is related to journal publication 21 and conference publication 3. We propose resource allocation and incentive mechanisms for mobile crowd sensing, considering the impact of diversity and social relationship. This is related to conference publications 8, 9, 15 and 18.

14202814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202814.value: This research project has been successfully concluded and related research outputs have been published. In the future, it is possible to further develop incentive mechanisms for distributed cellular and Wi-Fi network integrations considering more advanced learning models, relying on the measurement data regarding users' wireless data consumption patterns.

14202814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202814.value: With the proliferation of smartphones and tablets, the demand for mobile data has been growing very rapidly. This is pushing the mobile cellular network to its limit. The Wi-Fi technology is uniquely positioned to complement the cellular technology, due to its unlicensed nature and the worldwide adoption at home and work. In particular, Wi-Fi networks can help to offload the traffic from over-stressed cellular networks, and reduce cellular operators’ costs and increase users’ service satisfaction. To achieve a seamless integration of cellular and Wi-Fi technologies, however, requires us to have forward-looking policy reforms, effective economic mechanism designs, and innovative technology solutions. We have focused on the following key questions in this project: (1) How should a spectrum regulator allocate spectrum between cellular and Wi-Fi technologies? (2) How to provide economic incentives to maximize and fairly share the data offloading benefits in the network? (3) How to optimize data offloading algorithms that best trade off network cost reductions and users’ Quality of Service improvements? (4) How should users take advantage of integrated and heterogeneous mobile networks in a collaborative fashion? The outputs of the research provide a deeper understanding of opportunities and challenges of designing future mobile broadband networks.

14202914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202914.value: Fundamental to all cooperative control problems of multi-agent systems is the consensus problem. In the formulation of the consensus problem, the communication graph is assumed to be known and is required to satisfy certain connectivity assumption. However, in real applications such as formation, rendezvous, flocking, and so on, the communication graph for multi-agent systems is defined dynamically and the connectivity of the communication graph is not assumed but must be maintained by the control law. Thus, it would be more interesting to consider the problem of designing a distributed control law for multi-agent systems that is able to preserve the connectivity of the communication graph while achieving the leader following. Such a problem is called the leader following with connectivity preservation. So far the research on the connectivity preservation problem is mainly limited to multiple single integrator or multiple double integrator systems. The main objective of this project is to develop a framework for handling the leader following with connectivity preservation problem for general nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems. The basic assumption of this framework is that the leader following problem of each pair of follower and leader is solvable by a conventional control law. The collection of these individual control laws is called a purely decentralized control law. To overcome the communication constraints, we further conceive a so-called distributed observer for the leader system which will provide the estimated leader signal to every follower while satisfying the communication constraints. Based on the distributed observer and the purely decentralized control law, we will then synthesize a distributed control law according to the certainty equivalent principle. A preliminary version of this framework has been successfully tested for the leader following problem for general linear multi-agent systems, and some classes of nonlinear systems such as Euler-Lagrange systems and rigid body systems, and has also been applied to solve the leader following with connectivity preservation problem for multiple single and double integrator systems. In this project, we will further incorporate adaptive control techniques and the artificial potential function method into this framework so that it can handle the leader following with connectivity preservation problem for uncertain nonlinear systems such as Euler-Lagrange systems and rigid body systems. The success of this project will not only enhance our capability to handle various cooperative control problems for nonlinear multi-agent systems, but also advance control techniques for multi-input, multi-output nonlinear uncertain systems. 趋同问题是若干多智能体系统的合作控制问题的基础. 在现有的趋同问题的描述中, 通常假定系统的通讯图满足一定的连通性. 但是在诸如编队,蜂拥,群聚等实际应用中, 系统的通讯图是动态定义的, 其连通性必须由分布式控制器保持, 而不能依靠假定。因此，欲使趋同问题的描述更实际，必须要求分布式控制器在应对编队,蜂拥,群聚等问题时能保持系统的通讯图的连通性。我们将此问题称为趋同兼连通性保持问题。截至目前为此，连通性保持问题的研究主要限于单积分型或二重积分型的多智能体系统。本项目的主要目的是构建一个对付不确定性非线性多智能体的趋同兼连通性保持问题的框架 。该框架由三个步骤构成. 首先，在 假定多智能体中的每个跟随者都能获取领导者的信息的前提下， 设计一个纯分散式控制器来解决多智能体系统的每个跟随者与领导者的跟踪问题。其次， 为领导者设计一个分布式观测器。该观测器可为每个跟随者 提供领导者的信息的估计。最后，利用确定性等价原理将纯分散式控制器与分布式观测器合成为一个分布式控制器。该框架的初级版已成功用于解决单积分型或二重积分型的多智能体系统的趋同兼连通性保持问题。本项目将进一步将初级版升级使其可应用于诸如欧拉型群体系统或航天器型群体系统的趋同兼连通性保持问题。该项目的成功实施不仅将提高我们控制实际非线性多智能体系统的能力,而且能推进对付带有不确定性参数的多输入多输出非线性系统的控制技术.

14202914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202914.value: Two expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. This project has only addressed the cooperative control of continuous-time multi-agent systems. The extension of this project to discrete-time systems is on-going. 2. In tis project, we assume that the state of the leader is available by the distributed observer. Such an observer is more precisely called state-based observer. In case only the output of the leader is available, one has to further consider the output based distributed observer. This generalization is also under way.

14202914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202914.value: The cooperative control of multi-agent systems has been one of the central control problems since the 2000, and it includes but is not limited to such problems as consensus/synchronization, formation, rendezvous, and flocking. What makes the cooperative control of multi-agent systems challenging is that the control law has to be distributed in order to satisfy communication constraints and has to maintain the connection of the communication networks. In this project, we have developed a distributed observer based design framework to handle the so-called leader following with connectivity preservation problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems which includes the rendezvous problem as a special case and can be modified to include the flocking problem by further imposing collision avoidance requirement. Moreover, we have further incorporated adaptive control techniques and the potential function method into this framework so that it can handle the leader following with connectivity preservation problem for uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems such as Euler-Lagrange systems and rigid body systems. The framework has also been applied to some multiple robot coordination problem and attitude synchronization problem of multiple spacecraft systems. The outcome of this project has significantly enhanced our capability to handle various cooperative control problems for practical nonlinear multi-agent systems.

14203314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203314.value: In many real-world applications, data with multiple aspects can be described by tensors (i.e., multidimensional arrays). For example, user customer ratings by a tensor with three modes (user, item, and time). In addition, data are often associated with some contextual information, for example the location information for users and side information for items in user customer rating systems. Tensor analysis has been known as an important approach to model the multiple aspects of data. However, in these systems, data are also characterized by their sparsity, heterogeneity, volume, veracity, etc. Many traditional methods suffer from either high resource dependance or insufficient modeling of contextual information. In this proposal, we plan to examine data characteristics that are emerging in various systems, investigate new tensor analysis models dealing with complex context information, and develop new optimization algorithms with reduced requirements on computational resources. More specifically, we plan to tackle the following important issues: (1) to develop novel tensor analysis models to extract the knowledge embedded in data; and (2) to provide scalable solutions for big data settings in applications such as recommendation in location-based social networks, mobile web recommendation, mobile advertisement in tourism, etc. ===== 在許多實際應用中，具有多個方面內容的數據可以由張量（即多維數組）描述。例如，用戶的客戶評級可以表示成三模的張量，即用戶、項、時間。此外，數據往往與某些上下文信息相關聯，例如用戶的客戶評級系統，該信息表示包括用戶的地理位置信息和項的邊信息。 張量分析已被公認為對多方面數據建模的重要方法。然而，在這些系統中，數據的特徵還表現在他們的稀疏性、異質性、巨量、準確性等，目前傳統的方法要么不能處理數據的大量依賴性，或者不能充分對上下文信息建模。 在本提議，我們計劃研究正在各種系統出現的數據特點，調研可處理複雜上下文信息的新的張量分析模型，並開發新的優化算法減少計算資源的需求。具體而言，我們計劃解決以下幾個重要問題：（1）開發新穎張量分析模型提取嵌入在數據中的知識;（2）提供可伸縮的用於大數據環境下應用的解決方案。相應的應用包括基於位置的社交網絡的推薦，移動網絡的推薦，旅遊線路的移動廣告等。

14203314.label: Realisation of objectives
14203314.value: The objectives of the proposed project on the modeling and application of tensor analysis have been fully completed based on the research plan. The proposed new models and conducted applications are recorded in multiple published papers. Objective 1: Novel Models for Tensor Analysis During the project, we have developed multiple novel algorithms and models for different types of data, from continuous to ranking data as well as the temporal, geometry, and social information. 1) On temporal information In the AAAI2016 paper [1], the proposed STELLAR model is built upon a ranking-based pairwise tensor factorization framework with a fine-grained modeling of user-POI, POI-time, and POI-POI interactions for successive POI recommendation. Successive point-of-interest (POI) recommendation in location-based social networks (LBSNs) becomes a significant task since it helps users to navigate a number of candidate POIs and provides the best POI recommendations based on users’ most recent check-in knowledge. However, all existing methods for successive POI recommendation only focus on modeling the correlation between POIs based on users’ check-in sequences, but ignore an important fact that successive POI recommendation is a time-subtle recommendation task. To capture the impact of time on successive POI recommendation, in this paper, we propose a spatial-temporal latent ranking (STELLAR) method to explicitly model the interactions among users, POI, and time. In the first ICONIP2016 paper [2], we extended the STELLAR model proposed in AAAI2016 and proposed an Aggregated Temporal Tensor Factorization (ATTF) model for POI recommendation to capture the three temporal features together, as well as at different time scales. Specifically, we employ temporal tensor factorization to model the check-in activity, subsuming the three temporal features together. Furthermore, we exploit a linear combination operator to aggregate temporal latent features’ contributions at different time scales. Experiments show that the ATTF model achieves better performance than previous models. 2) On geometry information In the ICONIP2017 paper [3], we propose a Geo-Pairwise Ranking Matrix Factorization (Geo-PRMF) model for POI recommendation, which incorporates co-geographical influence into a personalized pairwise preference ranking matrix factorization model. In our Geo-PRMF, the co-geographical influence which assumes that users follow similar visiting patterns in close areas is proposed to filter geographically noisy POIs. In the WWW2017 paper [4], we propose a Geo-Temporal sequential embedding rank (Geo-Teaser) model for POI recommendation. We first take the challenge that check-in sequences on different days naturally exhibit the various temporal characteristics, for example, ``work’’ on the weekday and ``entertainment’’ on weekend. To address this challenge, we first propose a temporal POI embedding model to learn POI representations under some particular temporal state and thus it can capture the contextual check-in information in sequences and the various temporal characteristics on different days as well. We also propose a new way to incorporate the geographical influence into the pairwise preference ranking method by discriminating the unvisited POIs according to geographical information. Then, we develop a geographically hierarchical pairwise preference ranking model. 3) On social information In the SIGIR2017 paper [5], we first propose an EmbeddingWARP model to mine business opportunities from location-based social networks (LBSNs), which guides the investors to decide to open what kind of business at which place. At first, we define the properties of a business district and propose a greedy algorithm to partition a city into different districts. The interacting relations between a district and a business category are modeled through a collaborative filtering technique. Next, we propose an embedding model to learn latent representations of categories, which captures the functional correlations among business categories. Furthermore, we propose a ranking model based on the pairwise loss to recommend categories for a specific district. In the IJCAI2016 paper [6], we propose a Homophily-based Non-negative Matrix Factorization (HNMF) for overlapping community detection. A standard framework to deal with overlapping community detection is Matrix Factorization (MF). Most of the previous works only view links as consequences of communities (community-to-link) but fail to explore how nodes’ community memberships can be represented by their linked neighbors (link-to-community). To solve this problem, we propose HNMF to model both-sided relationships between links and communities. From the link-to-community perspective, we propose a new community representation learning with network embedding by assuming that linked nodes have similar community representations. Objective 2: Scalable Implementations for Tensor Analysis Models To solve the challenge of the large volume and the dynamism of multi-aspect data in the tensor analysis problem, we focus on the online learning mechanism instead of utilizing map-reduce techniques as stated in the proposal. Online machine learning is a method where data is available in a sequential order and the predictor is updated at each step. So online learning methods will not learn on the entire training data, thus making the whole system scalable. In the second ICONIP2016 paper [7], we proposed an ActivePMF on TaskRec (Probabilistic Matrix Factorization with Active Learning on Task Recommendation Framework), a generic online updating method for learning a factor analysis model for crowdsourcing systems. Our proposed algorithm runs a batch update to further improve the performance. Complexity analysis and experimental results shows that our model is efficient and is scalable to large datasets. In the IEEE2018 paper [8], we propose a kernelized online imbalanced learning algorithm, which produces a nonlinear classifier for the data by maximizing the AUC score while minimizing a functional regularizer. We address four major challenges that arise from our approach. First, to control the number of support vectors without sacrificing the model performance, we introduce two buffers with fixed budgets to capture the global information on the decision boundary by storing the corresponding learned support vectors. Second, to restrict the fluctuation of the learned decision function and achieve smooth updating, we confine the influence on a new support vector to its k-nearest opposite support vectors. Third, to avoid information loss, we propose an effective compensation scheme after the replacement is conducted when either buffer is full. With such a compensation scheme, the performance of the learned model is comparable to the one learned with infinite budgets. Fourth, to determine good kernels for data similarity representation, we exploit the multiple kernel learning framework to automatically learn a set of kernels. Objective 3: Big Data Applications for Tensor Analysis Models In this project, we successfully apply our proposed tensor analysis models into plenty of big data applications and achieve the state-of-the-art results in many of them. For example, we proposed four novel and effective models for the point-of-interest (POI) recommendation task in location-based social networks (LBSNs) [1, 2, 3, 4], which significantly outperform previous models and explicitly promote the development of this area. We also designed a new model which first consider the link-to-community relationship for the overlapping community detection task [6]. Besides applying to existing applications, we also explored new big data application. For instance, in [5], we first proposed the business opportunity mining task from location-based social networks and designed a novel framework to solve this task effectively. 14203314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203314.value: The tensor object is a general data structure to model the complex interactions of objects in real-world rich context systems. Tensors can generalize the research problems via multiway analysis models, and then develop efficient and effective algorithms, and evaluate them in real applications. To capture the observed temporal features, we proposed the Aggregated Temporal Tensor Factorization (ATTF) model for POI recommendation. Experiments on two real-life datasets show that the ATTF model achieves better performance than models capturing temporal influence at a single scale. Besides, our proposed ATTF model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. To both capture the geometry and temporal data characteristics, we proposed a Geo-Temporal sequential embedding rank (Geo-Teaser) model for POI recommendation. The model captures the contextual check-in information in sequences and the various temporal characteristics on different days as well. Experimental results show that the Geo-Teaser model outperforms state-of-the-art models. Compared with the best baseline competitor, the Geo-Teaser model improves at least 20% on two real-life datasets for precision and recall metrics. To capture the social information, we propose a Weighted Approximate-Rank Pairwise (WARP) loss based model for recommender systems. Experimental results show that our proposed method successfully addresses the business mining problem for guiding the business owners to open new commercial shops in certain categories in a particular area. These models and papers are highly cited by other researchers and have been attracted interests from different research communities. The resulting algorithms and performance have expanded the current tensor analysis models for various data analytics applications.

14203314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203314.value: One important direction of tensor analysis is the scalability issue with the large volume and the dynamism of multi-aspect data. The resulting algorithms will expand the current multiway analysis models from moderate scale data to large scale data with petabytes or exabytes to fit the current Internet-scale massive data requirements. In the project, we utilize online learning algorithms to settle the scalability issue. However, we can also ask for the expected algorithm toolkits, which can be helpful for various data analytics applications. Advanced distributed learning frameworks can be investigated to split the data and merge the results using map-reduce techniques and other graph-based categorized learning frameworks. Another important topic is to develop useful approximation algorithms for tensor analysis models. Tensor analysis models often involve with substantial computational complexity to find the optima. One potential solution is to provide advanced optimization algorithms, such as stochastic gradient descent and online learning algorithms. Besides, we can follow the theoretical analysis of the convergence rate and theoretical analysis of regret bounds.

14203314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203314.value: Many real-world systems are associated with data from various sources or multiple aspects. The rich information and complex relationships between various objects are valuable in studying user behaviors for social workers, advertising, and marketing, etc. Therefore, research and industry communities tend to explore the complex interactions under rich contextual environments. Our project has modeled the complex interactions of objects in real-world rich context systems and has generalized the research problems via multiway analysis models by developing efficient and effective algorithms and models as well as evaluating them in many real applications.

rows: We propose to develop a new unified text mining framework that can conduct social-aware trend discovery on news content together with the related social media content.

14203414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203414.value: News articles reporting various events are produced daily by many news agencies or sources. Furthermore, with the emerging trend of user participation, a large amount of social media content such as reader comments and blogs discussing news events exist. Due to the massive, unstructured, and dynamic nature of news and related social media content, it is impossible for human to read and digest even just a small proportion. We propose to develop a new unified text mining framework that can conduct social-aware trend discovery on news content together with the related social media content. Trends are collectively organized as an array of latent information structure, namely, latent event topic hierarchy, facets, and storylines. For example, the set of news documents from different news sources reporting the same event about Egypt protest occurred in the middle of August 2013 would form a storyline. Moreover, this storyline is associated with a specific event topic "political protest in a country or region". In general, this specific topic is a sub-topic under a more general topic and these topics become a part of the latent event topic hierarchy. Such latent event topic hierarchy and storylines are automatically discovered and constructed via analyzing the news text content. Furthermore, latent facets, which model another dimension different from event topics, are jointly discovered from sentences in news documents and sentences in the corresponding social media content. An example of a facet is "political causes of an event". Facets are further organized as sentence-level facets and word-level facets, and they are discovered based on joint modeling and mining of the words and sentences in the news content and the corresponding social media content. Discovering facets also facilitates precise matching selected sentences of social media messages with sentences of news documents facilitating the detection of social attitude for different facets of news content. The capability of conducting social-aware trend discovery via the latent information structure mentioned above can support the development of intelligent content analysis applications. We intend to develop a system for social-aware structured browsing of news and social media content. Another application is to develop a social-aware news event summarization system. To tackle the technical challenges for achieving our goal, we intend to investigate generative graphical topic models and some variants. Our proposed framework provides a principled formalism for joint modeling of news and social media text content at both word and sentence levels. 在信息爆炸的互聯網時代，新聞機構和新聞源每天產生了關於各種事件的大量新聞報導。此外，隨著用戶在互聯網上的不斷活躍，和新聞相關的大量社交媒體內容被產生，比如，讀者對新聞的評論和博客中的讀者針對新聞的討論等。由於新聞和與新聞相關的社交媒體具有海量，無結構和動態等特點，這些信息很難被人們全部瀏覽和理解。 針對這個問題，我們提出了一種創新和統一的文本挖掘框架。這個框架將新聞內容和相關社交媒體內容聯合起來，對面向社交的新聞趨勢進行發現和預測。在這個框架中，新聞趨勢被組織成了一系列的隱藏結構信息，也就是，隱藏層次事件主題，要素和故事情節。比如，來自不同新聞源的新聞報導了同一個事件——發生在2013年8月份中旬的埃及抗議活動。這些新聞將組成一個故事情節。此外，這個故事情節和特定事件主題“在一個國家或地區的政治抗議”存在聯繫。通常來說，特定的事件主題是一個一般主題的子主題。這些主題構成了一個具有層次結構的隱藏事件主題模型。通過分析新聞文本的內容，這些隱藏層次事件主題和故事情節將被自動地挖掘和構建。更進一步來講，和事件主題不同，要素從另一個維度對新聞內容和相應的社交媒體內容進行建模。通過使用新聞文本的句子和相應社交媒體內容的句子，我們可以對要素進行聯合的挖掘和發現。在上述例子中，一個要素可以是“一個事件發生的政治原因”。要素可以被進一步組織成句子要素和詞要素。通過對新聞內容和相應社交媒體內容中的詞和句子進行聯合建模和挖掘，我們可以挖掘出句子要素和詞要素。要素的挖掘使匹配社交媒體信息中的句子和新聞文檔中的句子變得更加容易。通過句子匹配，我們可以進一步對社交媒體中針對新聞內容的不同要素的觀點進行挖掘和決策。 通過上述提出的隱藏結構信息，進行面向社交的新聞趨勢的發現和預測能夠幫助其他智能文本分析應用的開發。比如，我們可以開發出面向社交的新聞內容和社交媒體的結構瀏覽系統。對面向社交的新聞趨勢的發現和挖掘還能夠幫助我們開發出面向社交媒體的新聞事件摘要係統。為了達到我們的目標，我們試圖調查生成圖主題模型和該模型的其他變種。我們提出的框架對新聞和社交媒體在詞和句子層面進行聯合建模提供了一個理論上的形式化方法。

14203414.label: Realisation of objectives
14203414.value: The first objective has been fully achieved by developing a framework that is able to conduct social-aware trend discovery on news content together with the related social media content. In our framework, we discover trends represented as a suite of latent information structure in the form of latent facets and storylines. The set of news documents from different news sources reporting the same event are considered as a storyline. The content of this storyline is highly related to a specific event topic. Our framework is also able to discover latent facets capturing another dimension different from event topics. One characteristic of our framework is the ability to discover latent facets based on joint modeling and coordinated mining of the words and sentences found in the text content of news and the related social media. Both sentence-level facets and word-level facets are detected in our model. To tackle the technical challenges, our model is designed based on generative graphical topic models. Our proposed graphical model incorporates a joint modeling and mining of news and social media text content at both word and sentence levels enabling the detection of various kinds of latent information structure conducted in a coordinated manner. The second objective has been fully achieved. Our text mining framework is employed to develop intelligent content analysis applications. We have developed an application system which allows social-aware structured browsing of news and social media content. Another application is related to text summarization. Specifically, based on the above framework, we further develop several models for social-aware news event summarization. To achieve this goal, our models for generating text summaries consider the reader interests found in the related social media messages as well as salience information found the news documents.

14203414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203414.value: This research has produced some results and generated some papers. The proposed framework is capable of capturing the intricate fine-grained associations among news content, events, facets, and reader comments. It also allows social-aware structured browsing of news and social media content. The research findings have been reported in several papers, namely a paper accepted in IEEE Transactions of Knowledge and Data Engineering (No. 2 in Section 8), and two published conference papers (No. 2 and 3 in Section 9). We have developed a technique for handling the interactions among the reader comments in social networks and latent topics based on co-clustering for modeling the user community. The research finding has been published in a paper appeared in ACM Transactions on Information Systems (No. 1 in Section 8). A technique for analyzing news reader comments across English and Chinese culture has been developed based on a probabilistic graphical model and the research finding has been published in Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) (No. 1 in Section 9). For the second objective, we have successfully adopted and derived some models for social-aware news event summarization. A cascaded attention based unsupervised model has been developed for estimating the salience information from the news documents. This model can be employed to tackle compressive multi-document summarization. This research finding has been published in a natural language processing (NLP) conference (No. 5 in Section 9). Another related model based on a deep recurrent generative neural decoder and variational inference has been developed for tackling abstractive news summarization. This research finding has been published in the same conference as above (No. 6 in Section 9). We also develop a new model for learning domain-specific and sentiment-aware embeddings that simultaneously captures the information of sentiment semantics and domain sensitivity of words. This research finding has been published in the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) (No. 7 in Section 9).

14203414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203414.value: One future direction is to analyze the news content and social media content under the setting of a mix of multiple languages, for example, a mix of English and Chinese texts. This issue is related to code-switching problem in language processing. One challenge is to develop a suitable model that can handle code-switched texts. Another challenge is to acquire suitable data sets that contain a large amount of code-switched words and sentences.

14203414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203414.value: A large amount of news articles are generated every day. Besides, a massive amount of user generated comments related to news articles or events are written by ordinary users. The voluminous and unorganized nature of news and related social media content impose great difficulty for effective understanding and analysis. We propose to develop a new unified text mining framework that can conduct social-aware trend discovery on news content together with the related social media content. Latent event topics and facets are automatically discovered. Also, our proposed framework provides a principled formalism for joint modeling of news and social media text content at both word and sentence levels. Such capability of conducting social-aware trend discovery via the latent information structure can support the development of intelligent content analysis applications. Based on the new framework mentioned above, we also develop several new models for social-aware news and text summarization models.

14203714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203714.value: With the growth in smartphone adoption and world-wide deployment of high-speed mobile data networks such as 3G/4G, mobile video streaming is not only feasible but also commonplace nowadays. According to a recent study, global mobile data traffic will increase 13-fold between 2012 and 2017, with video traffic accounting for over 66 percent of all mobile data traffic by the end of the forecasted period. Despite rapid advances in mobile networks, streaming high-quality video to mobile users remains a challenge. While modern mobile networks can offer very high peak bandwidth, their nature of wireless transmission unavoidably exhibits bandwidth fluctuations, which are far more significant than their wired counterparts. Moreover, with the recent widespread adoption of streaming video over HTTP/TCP, the throughput of a video session is further modulated by TCP’s built-in flow and congestion control algorithms. In fact one cannot expect reliable and consistent performance when streaming video over mobile networks – the encounter of playback rebuffering is the norm rather than the exception. One problem is the lack of network or transport-level QoS control in mobile networks. Most, if not all, of the industry have largely given-up on the hope of offering predictable performance in mobile video streaming, leading to the switch of focus to adaptive video streaming. However, our investigations show that while adaptive video streaming can improve streaming performance, its performance is still highly unpredictable. In this project we argue that predicting the streaming performance over mobile networks is not only possible, but also feasible in today’s mobile networks. The key insight is that the streaming community has been using the wrong metric – throughput statistics, to directly inform the choice of video bitrate. By contrast, we propose a novel framework called post-streaming rate analysis to extract the correlation between traffic flow statistics and video bitrate selection, and quantify their impact to streaming performance. Our pilot study shows that the proposed framework can (a) quantify the tradeoffs between video bitrate selection and streaming performance; and (b) enable online video bitrate selection with predictable streaming performance – to the best of the PI’s knowledge it is the first video bitrate selection algorithm possessing such property. Achieving predictable performance has always been one of the holy-grails in mobile video streaming. With the rapid migration from physical media to online media streaming, we expect results from this research project to have a far-reaching impact to the global mobile/media industry. 隨著智能手機的普及和高速移動數據網絡（如3G/4G）在全球範圍內的廣泛部署，移動視頻傳輸不僅是可行的，也是司空見慣的。最近的一項研究表明，全球移動數據流量在2012年至2017年間將增長13倍，其中2017年視頻流量在移動數據總 流量中佔比將超過66％。但是儘管移動網絡在快速發展，傳輸高品質的視頻給移動用戶仍然是一個挑戰。現代移動網絡雖然能夠提供極高的峰值帶寬，但是無線傳 輸上不可避免地存在帶寬的波動，並且這種帶寬波動比有線網絡中帶寬波動更為顯 著。此外，隨著近年來HTTP/ TCP架構被廣泛應用與視頻傳輸，傳輸視頻的帶寬進 一步由TCP協議內置的流量控制和擁塞控制算法調節。事實上當人們通過移動網絡 看視頻時，他們大多沒有期望得到可靠穩定的傳輸性能—遇到視頻播放卡頓是一種常態，而不是例外。 上述問題是源於移動網絡普遍缺乏對網絡層或傳輸層服務質量的控制。現今業界在很大程度上已經放棄了為移動視頻傳輸提供可預測的性能，因此現在的視頻傳輸研究重點轉向自適應視頻傳輸。然而，我們的研究發現，雖然自適應視頻流可以提高視頻傳輸性能，但是它的傳輸性能依然非常難以預測。在這個項目中，我們認為在今天的移動網絡中，預測視頻傳輸性能不僅是可能的，而且是可行的。問題的關鍵是業界一直在使用錯誤的指標– 網絡吞吐量去指導視頻比特率的選擇。應對這一挑戰，我們提出了一個全新的視頻傳后分析框架。這是一個用於提取網絡吞吐量和視頻比特率選擇之間的相關性，量化兩者對視頻傳輸性能影響的新框架。我們的初步研究顯示，該框架能夠 （一）量化視頻比特率選擇和視頻傳輸性能之間的關係;及 （二）進行實時視頻比特率選擇并提供可預測的傳輸性能—據我們所知，這是第一個可以提供上述兩種性質的視頻比特率選擇算法。實現可預測的視頻傳輸性能是視頻傳輸研究的重要目標之一。隨著網絡媒體的快速發展，這研究項目的成果能對全球移動/媒體行業產生深遠的影響。

14203714.label: Realisation of objectives
14203714.value: (i) Development of the Post Streaming Rate Analysis (PSRA) framework In this project we successfully developed the PSRA framework for constant-bitrate streaming as well as adaptive video streaming. The framework was designed based on the observation that real-world mobile networks do exhibit both short-term and long-term bandwidth characteristics which can be exploited to provide predictable and consistent streaming performance. The key results were summarized and reported in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing as a regular paper in 2017 (output #9.1). We first conducted a systematic investigation of existing prediction algorithms and analyzed their characteristics when applied to the prediction of TCP throughput in mobile networks. The empirical results verified that TCP throughput over mobile networks is far more predictable than one might expect. In addition, we applied recent results in differential entropy to obtain an estimated lower bound on throughput prediction error. To our knowledge this is the first known result on lower-bounding the error in predicting throughput in mobile networks. The results were published in research output #9.3. The PSRA framework exploits mobile networks’ throughput characteristics by analyzing past throughput trace data captured as a by-product of actual streaming sessions. Specifically, PSRA executes the streaming algorithm over these past throughput trace data to determine the maximum video bitrate that could have been delivered and relate that to other system parameters via a statistical model. In this project we successfully applied PSRA to four streaming applications and reported the results in outputs #9.1, #9.2, #9.4, and #9.6. Moreover, we extended PSRA into an even more general framework called Post Streaming Quality Analysis (PSQA) that employs the same data-driven principle to automatically optimize any arbitrary streaming algorithms according to a given performance metric. This generalized PSQA framework has an even wider applicability as the performance metric can be user-defined and thus can be tailored to the target applications/services. We first reported the PSQA framework in INFOCOM 2016 (output #9.5) and then later reported two of its applications, one in reducing data wastage (output #9.7) and another in adaptive live video streaming (output #9.8). (ii) Application of PSRA to Video Encoding Portfolio Composition We investigated two issues in video encoding portfolio composition (henceforth called VEPC) as applied to mobile video streaming. First, we investigated the impact of the VEPC on the performance of existing streaming algorithms and show that different bitrate compositions could impact streaming performance significantly and unpredictably. This refutes the common notion that the only key requirement for a VEPC is sufficient number of bitrate choices that covers the full spectrum of the network conditions. Instead, the specific bitrate choices for a VEPC could impact streaming performance in a substantial but unpredictable way. In contrast, by applying the PSRA framework to rate adaptation we show that the performance variations due to VEPC can be greatly reduced. In fact PSRA-optimized adaptive video streaming can maintain the given streaming performance target irrespective of the VEPC chosen. The results have been reported in IEEE TMC (output #8.1). Second, for a service provider offering premium streaming service (e.g., paid movies and shows) it is essential to guarantee the video quality to not lower than some reasonable level (e.g., 480p). The current state-of-art in mobile video streaming is to employ rate-adaptation to react to and compensate for the wide bandwidth fluctuations in mobile networks. However, if the bandwidth drops sufficiently low the rate adaptation algorithm will be forced to select a very low bitrate version of the video (e.g., 144p) to sustain continuous playback, thus violating the need to maintain good video quality in premium services. Note that it is not sufficient to merely configure the VEPC such that all bitrate choices are above the desired minimum quality as this handicaps the rate adaptation algorithm’s ability to compensate for low-bandwidth situations and will result in playback rebuffering. We developed a new approach based on the PSRA framework to tackle this challenge. The key idea is to exploit prefetch buffering to solve the challenge of guaranteeing both video quality and streaming performance - by choosing a sufficiently large prefetch buffer one can stream a video at a higher bitrate than is otherwise possible. The challenge is to select the correct prefetch buffer size given the minimum video quality requirement, streaming performance target, and network/system conditions. This is where PSRA comes in – by incorporating the prefetch buffer into the PSRA framework we can generate an extended statistical model that captures the relation between streaming performance, minimum video quality, and prefetch buffer size. Results from extensive trace-driven simulations confirmed that this quality-priority PSRA framework can achieve both guaranteed video quality and streaming performance with reasonable perfetch sizes. The results were reported in research output #9.2. (iii) Application of PSRA to Bitrate Selection in Constant Bitrate Video Streaming We investigated the application of PSRA to online bitrate selection for constant-bitrate video streaming. Specifically, we apply PSRA to analyze past throughput trace data to determine the maximum video bitrate (or video quality level in case of VBR encoding) that could have been delivered and generate a statistical model to relate the bitrate choice with streaming performance in terms of playback rebuffering probability. The model is then used to select the video bitrate for future streaming sessions. With expanded throughput trace dataset the results verified that PSRA can effectively achieve the rebuffering probability target set by service provider over a wide range of network and system conditions. The results were reported in research output #9.1 for CBR video streaming and output #9.4 for VBR video streaming respectively. (iv) Application of PSRA to Rate Adaptation for Adaptive Video Streaming. We investigated the application of PSRA to adaptive video streaming over mobile networks – TDRA-PSRA. Based on our previous work in applying PSRA to constant bitrate video streaming, we show that it is possible to not only predict the average streaming performance, but also control it explicitly, e.g., via a target rebuffering probability. Our simulation results obtained from real-world mobile network trace data revealed three remarkable properties of TDRA-PSRA: (a) the actual average streaming performance is very close to the target set forth by the service provider; (b) it enables the service provider to control the tradeoff between streaming performance and video quality; (c) it offers a mean to directly control the frequency of bit-rate switches - a key factor to subjective video quality. The results were reported in research output #8.1. In addition, we extended our investigation to the streaming of variable-bit-rate (VBR) encoded videos. Unlike constant-bitrate (CBR) encoded video the actual bitrate demand of a given video can vary significantly over its playback time depending on the actual video content encoded. This poses another dimension of challenges as the streaming algorithm not only have to deal with varying network bandwidth, but also time-varying bandwidth demands as well. Surprisingly, we can extend the PSRA framework even to this problem and the results show that it is possible to provide predictable and consistent streaming performance for streaming variable bitrate video over bandwidth-varying mobile networks. The results were reported in outputs #9.4 and #9.6.

14203714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203714.value: This project opens up a novel data-driven approach to the optimization of streaming algorithms. In existing approaches streaming algorithms were often designed with operating parameters hand-tuned based on some specific network setups. Our results demonstrated that it is difficult, if not impossible, for a single set of parameters to work consistently across different network environments and this explains the wildly different performance of the same streaming algorithm when executed in different network settings. The proposed Post-Streaming Analysis frameworks (PSRA and PSQA) addressed this challenge by incorporating the specific network the system operates in into the optimization process, and offer a way for the system to automatically and continuously fine-tune its operating parameters. This last point is hinged on mobile network’s bandwidth predictability over a timescale of one day which was validated in an extensive empirical study reported in output #9.3. This enables, for the first time in the literature, streaming algorithms that can provide statistically predictable performance over a wide range of mobile networks. We first applied the PSRA framework to non-adaptive streaming (output #9.1) and then later to adaptive CBR streaming (output #8.1, #9.1) as well as adaptive VBR streaming (outputs #9.2, #9.4, #9.6). Armed with the success of the PSRA framework we further generalized it into the PSQA framework where the optimization goal is replaced by a general objective function. This significantly expands the scope of the framework as there is no restriction to the form of the objective function. By designing specific objective function one can then apply PSQA to automatically optimize the streaming system continuously. We first presented the PSQA framework in output #8.5 and then applied it to two applications, one in reducing data wastage (output #9.7) and another in delay-sensitive live video streaming (output #9.8).

14203714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203714.value: This project demonstrated that different network settings require different operating parameters for optimal performance in mobile streaming. The proposed Post-Streaming Analysis frameworks offered practical and efficient solutions to this problem. On the other hand, the extensive results in our investigations revealed an even deeper dimension to the problem – one not only needs different operating parameters for different network settings, but also potentially completely different algorithms for the broad diversity of networks in practice. In other words, there is only so much one can optimize by tuning an algorithm’s parameters – in some cases, one needs different algorithms altogether to exploit the underlying network’s characteristics for optimal performance. This is a new uncharted area as all existing streaming systems, practical and in the literature, are built upon a specific adaptive streaming algorithm. We envision the next generation of streaming system will comprise not one, but an ensemble of multiple streaming algorithms designed to complement each other and to be dynamically selected and applied according to the properties of the underlying network. The PI has conducted a pilot study of this new paradigm which showed great potentials and submitted a new GRF Proposal for funding the research of this new paradigm to adaptive streaming.

14203714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203714.value: Fueled by the growth of 3G/4G mobile networks, mobile video streaming has become one of the main applications in the mobile Internet. Due to mobile networks’ inherent bandwidth fluctuations, the industry as well as researchers have developed many adaptive streaming algorithms to compensate for such fluctuations to improve streaming performance. Given the wide range of network settings it is not surprising that existing algorithms can and do perform differently across different network and system conditions. This project breaks away from the conventional one-size-fits-all approach to designing adaptive streaming systems by developing new Post-Streaming Analysis (PSA) frameworks where past throughput trace data - captured as a by-product of streaming, are analyzed to construct a statistical model to automatically optimize the adaptation algorithm for future streaming sessions according to the underlying network and system configurations. Compared to existing approaches, PSA-optimized streaming algorithms can achieve predictable, consistent, and controllable streaming performance across a wide range of network and system configurations. Results from extensive trace-driven simulations as well as experiments verified PSA’s performance under real-world mobile network and system configurations. It is practical and readily deployable in today’s as well as future mobile streaming systems.
