14204014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204014.value: A large population of people have problems using their voices. They encountered different types of voice problems, including pitch changes, roughness, breathiness, strain, and many others. Currently perceptual evaluation is a standard procedure for voice assessment by speech therapists. Despite good efforts on developing validated perceptual evaluation scales, there is always a strong desire for alternative assessment methods that are objective and repeatable. It is believed that the degree of voice abnormalities could be quantified by analyzing the acoustical signal of voice. This project aims at developing effective methods of acoustical analysis and classification for objective and quantitative assessment of voice disorders. Our investigation is based on a speech database that contains normal and pathological voices from one hundred and twenty Cantonese speakers. We propose to apply the approach of transform-domain periodic-aperiodic decomposition to extract acoustic features that represent waveform irregularities caused by abnormal vocal folds vibration. A voice signal is separated into a periodic component and an aperiodic one. The aperiodic component is used to derive a set of feature parameters that capture waveform irregularities. We adopt a pattern-classification perspective on quantifying the severity level of voice disorders and propose an exemplar-based modeling approach to tackle the problem. An observed voice sample is represented as a sparse linear combination of the exemplars from a large dictionary. By estimating the sparse weights, the exemplars that best represent the incoming voice can be identified, and the severity level of voice disorder can be computed from these exemplars accordingly. The acoustic assessment scores can be used to cross-validate the results of human perceptual evaluation, and hence improve the objectivity and reliability of clinical diagnosis of voice disorders. They can also be used to evaluate clinical treatment outcome and monitor treatment progress. This is an inter-disciplinary work that involves the areas of signal processing, speech science and voice rehabilitation. The investigators have done a lot of work in these areas and been closely collaborating in the past few years. We seek for a funding of HK$1.204 million to support the project for three years. 嗓音問題十分普遍。患者所呈現的問題包括基音異常，聲音嘶啞，聲帶疲勞等等。目前言語治療師以聽覺主觀評估作為標準的檢驗手段，也建立了相關的評估量表。與此同時，行業內對於更加客觀準確並且可重複的嗓音評估方法有著極其殷切的需求。我們認為，嗓音異常的種類和程度直接反映在對應的聲學信號的特徵上。本項目的目標是研究和開發用於嗓音異常定量評估的聲學信號分析方法。項目的開展建基於一個早前由中文大學言語治療部開發的病態嗓音資料庫。該資料庫包含一百多個具代表性的患者的錄音，並由專業言語治療師詳細標注。在信號分析方面，我們將在變換域提取和分離嗓音信號中週期性和非週期性的部分，並從非週期性部分中提取波形的不規則特徵，以模式分類的角度進行嗓音異常的定量評估，並計畫把稀疏性估計技術應用在病態嗓音的分類問題上。基於聲學信號的評測結果將會與主觀評分進行對比，由此進一步改善客觀評估方法的性能。本項目的研究成果將有助於提高嗓音臨床康復治療的效率和準確性。項目團隊成員包括語音信號處理和嗓音治療方面的專業研究人員，項目為期三年，獲批經費50萬港幣。

14204014.label: Realisation of objectives
14204014.value: Realisation of Objective 1 This project objective has been fully achieved. Conventional acoustic features generally refer to perturbation and spectral features, e.g., jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio, that are applicable mostly to stationary speech sounds. Standard signal processing tool kits like OpenSMILE have been developed to facilitate efficient computation of these features. We investigated the effectiveness of a compact and minimalistic voice parameter set, named eGeMAPS. The feature set contains 88 elements, which are the statistical functionals of 25 low-level signal descriptors. These feature parameters are computed for each speech utterance, whether it is sustained vowel or continuous speech. Experimental results showed that the use of conventional features led to similar percentage accuracy on utterance-level prediction of disorder severity with sustained vowels and continuous speech. The relevant work were presented in one journal paper (J1) and two conference papers (C1, C5). Realisation of Objective 2 This project objective has been fully achieved. Toward designing more effective voice features, especially for continuous speech, we started with an investigation on explicitly characterizing waveform irregularities that are caused by voice disorders. Due to the wide variety of voice problems, periodic-aperiodic signal decomposition could not be reliably carried out as we initially expected. Therefore we made a major shift of research methodology and adopted a data-driven approach to extracting features from disordered voice. It was noted that conventional voice features failed to characterize local and phoneme-specific markers. To address the problem, we propose to apply automatic speech recognition (ASR) to decode continuous speech into a phone sequence and derive phone-dependent acoustic features from the ASR posteriors. State-of-the-art deep neural network (DNN) architecture was applied to acoustic modeling of ASR. The ASR posterior features were found to be highly effective in discriminating impaired voices from normal. With only three well-designed posterior features, we were able to achieve similar prediction accuracy to the 88 eGeMAPS features. For continuous speech utterances, the ASR posterior features could be jointly used with the eGeMAPS features to complement each other. In addition, we investigated the use of Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence measure to quantify phone-level distortion between unimpaired voice and impaired one. The relevant research work were presented in three conference papers (C2, C3, C4) and one journal paper (J1). Realisation of Objective 3 This project objective has been fully achieved. In the proposed system, preliminary prediction of severity level of voice disorder is carried out first for each input utterance. Feature extraction and voice classification are carried out in two independent streams, which involve the ASR posterior features and the conventional voice features respectively. The two streams of features are expected to capture different aspects of voice disorder and be complementary to each other. Separate multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained by the ASR features and conventional voice features to give predictions of disorder severity for the input utterance. By combining the utterance-level prediction scores from the MLPs, the system outputs an overall severity level of voice disorder, i.e., mild, moderate, or severe, for the subject under assessment. The complete system gave a subject-level classification accuracy of 81%. Subjects with severe voice disorders could be perfectly separated from those with mild disorders and normal voice. The classification accuracy for mild subjects is 95%. The relevant work were presented mainly in two conference papers (C3, C5) and one journal paper (J1). In addition to realising the above objectives, our research was extended to other types of speech disorder, namely post-stroke aphasia and child speech sound disorder. Aphasia is an acquired neurogenic speech-language disorder resulting from physical damage to specific brain regions. People with aphasia (PWA) suffer from various types of speech and language deficits, which are manifested in phonation, articulation, fluency, lexical richness and semantics. We proposed a range of acoustic, posterior and linguistic features to measure the severity degree of aphasia in Cantonese-speaking individuals. These features include supra-segmental duration, continuous bags-of-words and KL divergence. With respect to subjective assessment scores, the automatically predicted scores could achieve a correlation of 0.89. The relevant work led to 2 conference papers (C6, C7).

14204014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204014.value: Automating acoustical assessment of voice disorder has long been a goal of inter-disciplinary research actively pursued by the engineering and clinical research communities. Our research addressed the challenges in using flexible natural speech to replace highly controlled sounds in voice assessment. We have shown that ASR posteriors obtained from DNN based speech models carry important information about disorder-related voice changes. With a low-dimension posterior based feature vector, the accuracy of predicting severity of voice disorder is comparable to that with conventional features with a much higher dimension [C2][C3]. By combining the contributions from the ASR voice features and conventional voice features, a subject-level prediction accuracy of over 80% on three severity classes has been achieved [J1][C5]. Subjects with mild disorder and those with severe disorder could be perfectly distinguished by the proposed method. Our research suggested that an effective and reliable voice assessment system could be implemented by jointly evaluating sustained vowels and continuous speech [C5].

14204014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204014.value: In the present work, speech utterances from all training and test speakers have the same content, though they are natural speech. It would be more desirable from clinical perspectives to allow the use of speech with arbitrary content. The proposed design of feature extraction process can be extended to facilitate such general applications. On the other hand, the effectiveness of ASR voice features depends mainly on whether the input speech contains phonemes that are able to reflect the difference between disorder and normal voices. In principle, the proposed method can be straightforwardly extended to other languages. Recently the project team is closely collaborating with a major hospital in Guangzhou in collecting disordered voice data from patients who speak Putonghua and/or other Chinese dialects.

14204014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204014.value: Acoustical analysis of speech signals is an effective non-invasive method of assessing voice problems. It provides objective evidences to assist clinical diagnosis and to evaluate the outcomes of treatment and rehabilitation. This research addressed the problems of extracting robust features from naturally spoken utterances and using these features to quantify the degree of voice disorder. We adopted a data-driven approach which bases on the latest deep learning techniques. Based on the results of this research, we will be able to develop computer software tools that automatically analyse a voice signal and generate objective assessment scores. These scores can be used to cross-validate the results of human perceptual evaluation, and hence improve the objectivity and reliability of clinical diagnosis of voice disorders. The proposed research is expected to make significantly contributions to the area of speech and language rehabilitation.

14204514.label: Project Objectives
14204514.value: To identify the optimal terminal wealth for dynamic mean-LPM problem formulation with a general stochastic opportunity set by solving a static optimization problem using the martingale approach. Two crucial subtasks are i) to derive conditions under which the existence and uniqueness of the Lagrangian multiplies can be guaranteed, which is a key step in applying the martingale approach, and in establishing a theoretical foundation for developing efficient numerical solution schemes; and ii) to prove that the probability of reaching the upper bound of the terminal wealth is decreasing with respect to the magnitude of the upper level. To derive analytical optimal portfolio policies for dynamic mean-LPM portfolio selection with general parameter setting when the market parameters are deterministic. One important issue for real implementation is to represent the portfolio policy in terms of the current wealth (instead of using the function form in terms of the market state density generated directly from solving the backward stochastic differential equation). We will explore other analytically solvable cases in this research as well. To derive analytical optimal portfolio policies for dynamic mean-CVaR portfolio selection by i) embedding the problem into a family of parameterized problems in terms of the VaR level, ii) investigating the relationship between the parameterized problem and the mean-LPM portfolio selection problem, and iii) developing a two-phase solution framework. One important subtask is to design a local search algorithm for finding the optimal VaR level which may not be unique, as the quantile of the optimal terminal wealth may not be unique. To formulate and study the mean-variance-CVaR portfolio optimization problem and to derive an analytical portfolio policy. Furthermore, to design a general framework of multiobjective analysis to strike a balance among the expected return and multiple risk measures. To carry out numerical tests and simulation study to evaluate performances of various models against real market data, to verify and understand the features of the newly proposed models in this research, to compare different characteristics of different models under different market conditions and to reveal the benefits gained from adopting these proposed models in this research.

14204514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204514.value: One of the most critical issues in achieving good portfolio performance is to balance two conflicting goals, maximization of expected investment return and minimization of investment risk, which in turn depends on which risk measure an investor takes to guide his/her investment decisions. Instead of concentrating solely on controlling “symmetric” risks measured by central moments of the investment return, more and more portfolio formulations in recent years have shifted their focus to manage “asymmetric” downside risks of investment return falling below a certain threshold, as a result of recognizing that most investors care primarily about the avoidance of worst-case scenarios, in addition to their strong desire in achieving good returns in nominal situations. Among the existing downside risk measures, the lower-partial moments (LPM) and the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) are probably most promising. In this project we take the challenge to investigate dynamic mean-LPM and dynamic mean-CVaR portfolio optimization problems in continuous-time, while the current literature has only witnessed the emergence of their static versions. While the portfolio policy generated from any static model is of a buy-and-hold nature, a state-dependent policy derived from a dynamic model is more suitable for problems with a long investment horizon, as the dynamic policy adjusts itself adaptively in response to volatile market situations. Our contributions in this project will be two-fold in both building up tractable formulations and deriving corresponding analytical solutions. By imposing a limit funding level on the terminal wealth, we conquer the ill-posedness exhibited in a class of mean-downside risk portfolio models and offer a flexibility to tame the aggressiveness of the portfolio policies. For a general market setting with a stochastic opportunity set, we will establish a theoretical foundation for developing efficient numerical solution schemes by applying the martingale approach. Furthermore, for situations with a deterministic opportunity set, we will derive analytical forms of the optimal portfolio policies for both dynamic mean-LPM and dynamic mean-CVaR formulations. Minimizing risk measures in terms of the central moments or in terms of the expected tail with a very small percentage of distribution mass may conflict with each other in nature. Our ultimate goal in this project is to develop a dynamic mean-variance-CVaR portfolio model to control a more complete spectrum of the overall risk. The derived analytical portfolio policy will enable us to strike a balance among the expected return and multiple essential risk measures. 投资组合中最关键的问题之一是怎样平衡回报与风险，而选择合适的风险度量指标是该问题的基础和前提。传统的风险度量常常是基于对称中心矩构建的。 然而出于风险控制的目的，投资者往往更关心投资组合在极端市场情况下的损失值以及损失超过某一预先设定值时的概率，近年来有越来越多的学者提出采用下行风险度量指标来控制该风险。最著名的下行风险度量包括下偏矩（LPM）与条件风险值CVaR。现时人们已经开始将下行风险度量与静态投资组合结合起来指导实践， 遗憾的是现今的文献还未见到其在动态投资组合中的尝试，然而在变化莫测的市场中，动态投资决策对于长期投资问题是至关重要的。 本课题将在基于下行风险度量的投资组合建模与求解两方面做出贡献。通过在最终财富上加上一个合理的上限，我们不仅保证了问题的可解性，而且可以利用这一上限来调节投资策略的冒进度。对一般随机市场环境，通过应用鞅方法，我们在理论上可以得出有效数值算法；对确定性市场，我们能推导出动态均值-LPM与动态均值-CVaR问题的解析解。 不同的风险度量指标从不同的角度反映了风险的特征，因而极小化中心矩风险或尾部风险可能相互抵触。本课题的一个终极目标是对风险进行多角度综合管理，以期达到投资组合中回报与风险的全面平衡。

14204514.label: Realisation of objectives
14204514.value: In this project we extend the state-of-the-art to investigate dynamic mean-down-side risk portfolio selection, including dynamic mean-LPM, dynamic mean-CVaR, and dynamic mean-VaR portfolio optimization problems in continuous-time. Our contributions in this project are two-fold in both building up tractable formulations and deriving corresponding analytical solutions. By imposing a limit funding level on the terminal wealth, we conquer the ill-posedness exhibited in a class of mean-downside risk portfolio models and offer a flexibility to tame the aggressiveness of the portfolio policies. For a general market setting with a stochastic opportunity set, we have established a theoretical foundation for developing efficient numerical solution schemes by applying the martingale approach. Furthermore, for situations with a deterministic opportunity set, we have derived analytical forms of the optimal portfolio policies for all three dynamic mean-LPM, dynamic mean-CVaR and dynamic mean-VaR formulations.

14204514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204514.value: We have investigated dynamic mean-downside risk portfolio optimization problems in continuous-time, where the downside risk measures can be either the lower-partial moments (LPM) or the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). Our contributions are twofold, both building up tractable formulations and deriving corresponding analytical solutions. By imposing a limit funding level on the terminal wealth, we conquer the ill-posedness exhibited in a class of mean-downside risk portfolio models. For a general market setting, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the Lagrangian multiplies, which is a key step in applying the martingale approach, and establish a theoretical foundation for developing ecient numerical solution approaches. Moreover, for situations where the opportunity set of the market setting is deterministic, we derive analytical portfolio policies for both dynamic mean-LPM and mean-CVaR formulations. We investigate the dynamic mean–VaR portfolio selection formulation in continuous time. By imposing a limit funding level on the terminal wealth, we conquer the ill-posedness exhibited in the original dynamic mean–VaR portfolio formulation. To overcome the difficulties arising from the VaR constraint and no bankruptcy constraint, we have combined the martingale approach with the quantile optimization technique in our solution framework to derive the optimal portfolio policy. In particular, we have characterized the condition for the existence of the Lagrange multiplier. When the opportunity set of the market setting is deterministic, the portfolio policy becomes analytical. Furthermore, the limit funding level not only enables us to solve the dynamic mean–VaR portfolio selection problem, but also offers a flexibility to tame the aggressiveness of the portfolio policy. We investigate a portfolio optimization methodology using nonparametric value at risk (VaR). In particular, we adopt kernel VaR and quadratic VaR as risk measures. As the resulting models are nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problems, albeit with some special structures, we propose some specially devised block coordinate descent (BCD) methods for finding approximate or local optimal solutions. Computational results show that the BCD methods are efficient for finding local solutions with good quality and they compare favorably with the branch-and-bound-based global optimal solution procedures. From the simulation test and empirical analysis that we carry out, we are able to conclude that the mean-VaR models using kernel VaR and quadratic VaR are more robust compared to those using historical VaR or parametric VaR under the normal distribution assumption, especially when the information of the return distribution is limited.

14204514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204514.value: We will investigate a discrete-time mean-risk portfolio selection problem, where risk is measured by the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). By embedding this time-inconsistent problem into a family of expected utility maximization problems with a piecewise linear utility function, we may solve the problem analytically. In contrast to the case of a complete, continuous-time market, the mean-CVaR efficient frontier in this generally incomplete, discrete-time setting should be a straight line in the mean-CVaR plane and there is in particular a constant trade-off between risk and return. We will further solve an inverse investment problem, where we investigate how mean-CVaR preferences need to adapt such that the pre-commited optimal strategy remains optimal at any point in time. Our result may be able to show that, although conceptually distinct, a pre-commited mean-CVaR investor behaves like a naive mean-CVaR investor with a time-increasing confidence level for the CVaR, who revises her investment decision at every point in time.

14204514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204514.value: Shifting from controlling solely “symmetric” risks measured by central moments of the investment return, a trend has become evident in recent years to focus more on establishing portfolio formulations to manage “asymmetric” downside risks of investment returns falling below a certain threshold, as driven by the fact that most investors care primarily about the avoidance of worst-case scenarios, in addition to their constant desire in achieving good returns in nominal situations. Our contributions in this project are two-fold in both building up tractable formulations and deriving corresponding analytical solutions. By imposing a limit funding level on the terminal wealth, we conquer the ill-posedness documented in the literature for a class of mean-downside risk portfolio models. For dynamic mean-LPM, dynamic mean-VaR and dynamic mean-CVaR formulations, we establish a theoretical foundation for developing efficient numerical solution approaches by applying the martingale approach, and derive analytical investment policies under some additional market conditions, such as deterministic opportunity set. Our research produces implementable tools and methods for investors to put into practice, more specifically, to enhance investors’ capability in achieving better portfolio performance and to increase their skill levels of robust risk management.

14204614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14204614.value: 基於機電轉換的生物動能收集裝置

14204614.label: Project Objectives
14204614.value: Making good exploitation of the human kinetic energy, which is sustainable yet receiving little attention in the past: Systematic analyses for human motions that related to energy harvesting were not performed. Various human motion patterns will be investigated. It would provide guidance towards better exploitation of the kinetic energy from human motions and other biological activities. Understanding physical insights of human motions on harvesting energy as well as the impact of energy harvesting on human efforts: Attentions should be paid on the backward effect of energy harvesting from human motions. For the human powered energy harvesting system, not only the energy that is taken away from human body, but also possible changes in force, stroke, etc., are of concern. This kind of research requires investigation on both ergonomic studies and energy harvesting systems. Study on energy harvesting efficiencies within the human motion environment: Excitation of the biomechanical energy harvesters is different from that of conventional energy harvesting systems, which are mainly work under high-frequency harmonic excitation. Human motions are usually low frequency movements, while resonant frequencies of most resonant harvesters are much higher than those of human motions, in particular, for micro-scale structures. Techniques for broadening the harvester’s bandwidth will be investigated. Implementation of energy harvesting systems: Valuable technologies have been proposed in the area of kinetic energy harvesting during the past decade. Yet, there are still important issues to be further investigated before practical implementation of energy harvesting systems. In this project, effort will be put to further investigate on the improvement and implementation of these energy harvesting systems. Establishing foundation for the development of future self-powered personal mobile devices and autonomous distributed sensing systems: By comparatively studying the potential harvestable energy associated with different human motions, this project will provide guidelines for rational exploitation of the kinetic energy from human motions and other biological activities. Issues such as preferential transduction mechanisms, harvesting interface circuits, etc., are also important for the exploitation and utilization of the kinetic energy.

14204614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204614.value: During activities, human body generates significant amount of biomechanical energy, which is one of the promising energy forms in our living environment. With the rapid developments on low power wireless electronics and micro-electromechanical systems, future personal mobile devices and distributed sensing systems might become sustainable by scavenging energy from human motions and other biological activities. These eco-friendly devices will provide us convenient and comfortable livings, while enabling lower maintenance cost. The feasibilities of some human motion energy harvesters have been shown in the previous literature. However, design, modeling and analysis of the biologically exciting energy harvesting devices and systems are still at their early stage. Energy harvesters should be designed and optimized with the considerations of human comfort and biomechanics. So far, there is no deep analysis on the backward effect induced by energy harvesting on human efforts. In addition, optimal design strategies of self-adaptive energy harvesting systems are not explored. This project aims at providing in-depth studies on the physical principles and insights of the electromechanical energy conversions towards optimization for the kinetic energy harvesting systems under various human motions, as well as overall evaluation about the impact of energy harvesting on human efforts. Moreover, the optimal design strategies of self-adaptive energy harvesting systems will also be provided. It will establish foundation for the development of future self-powered personal mobile devices and autonomous distributed sensing systems. The scientific knowledge created through this project will facilitate the continuing research efforts on energy harvesting, ergonomics, and the full realization of self-powered mobile devices. 在日常生活中，人體會產生大量的生物動能，是一種非常有前景的綠色能源。隨著低功耗無綫電子和微機電系統的迅速發展，通過從人體運動和其它生物活動中收集能量，未來的個人移動裝置和分佈式感應系統有望實現能源獨立。這些環保的裝置一方面可以為我們提供便利及舒適的生活，另一方面可以降低維護成本。之前的文獻已經探索了一些人體動能收集裝置的可行性，但是，生物激勵的能量收集裝置及系統的設計、建模和分析依然處於初期階段。迄今，尚無能量收集效應對人體舒適性和運動姿態影響的深入分析，以及考慮了人體舒適性及生物力學的能量收集裝置的優化設計方法。另外，尚無對自適應能量收集系統的優化策略之探討。本項目將對各種人體運動激勵下的機電能量轉換的物理機理進行深入研究，從而得到動能收集系統的優化。同時，將對能量收集技術對人體運動的影響進行系統探討，建立自適應能量收集系統的優化設計策略。本項目將建立未來自供能個人移動裝置和獨立分佈式感應系統的發展基礎。另外，項目所創造的科學知識將促進關於能量收集和人體工程學的進一步研究，以及自供能移動裝置的完全實現。

14204614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204614.value: A piezoelectric energy harvester has been designed for rotational motion applications such as turnstiles in MRT stations. The piezoelectric energy harvester was mounted on a rotating system. As the harvester rotates, the piezoelectric elements in the energy harvester were repeatedly deformed to generate electrical power. A novel design of the harvesting structure was proposed and analyzed theoretically (see J1). Experiments were conducted to validate the concept and analysis. We also investigated theoretical investigation on a coupling system consisting of bistable oscillator with an elastic magnifier (EM) to improve the output performances in vibration energy harvesting (see J3). Lumped-parameter nonlinear equations of the coupling system were derived to describe the broadband large-amplitude periodic displacement responses of the coupling system. The effects of the system mass ratio and stiffness ration on the output performances were studied. It showed that increasing the mass ratio and stiffness ratio can improve the system output performances. The distinct advantage in the coupling system lies in the existence of large-orbit periodic vibration over low level range (see J6). We proposed a novel knee-mounted biomechanical energy harvester with enhanced efﬁciency and safety (J4). The designed transmission system can convert the bi-directional knee rotation input into uni-directional rotation for the generator. Without the constraint of induced impact on the human body, this device can harvest biomechanical energy from both the knee ﬂexion and extension to improve the efﬁciency over previous single-direction energy harvesters. A prototype was fabricated and tested to evaluate the energy harvesting performance and effect on the human gait. The experimental results showed that the energy harvesting efﬁciency was improved, and the prototype can harvest an average power of 3.6W at 1.5ms−1 walking speed, which is sufﬁcient to power most portable electronic devices. In addition, a smart energy harvester was investigated to target the negative work of ankle joint during normal walking and convert biomechanical energy into electricity (J7). One-way clutch was employed to ﬁlter the plantarﬂexion of ankle joint and mechanical switch array was used to disconnect the electrical load at swing phase, so that the harvester can accurately capture the negative of ankle joint. A light weight prototype was fabricated. The experiments also demonstrated that the proposed harvester can reduce metabolic expenditure of 0.8W with consequent COH of −2.29. The result of reduction in metabolic expenditure was also supported by measuring the EMG signals of related muscles.

14204614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204614.value: Future research will focus on the quantitative evaluation of the user’s effort. To perform this, the connections between the human body and biomechanical energy harvester will have to be improved. In addition, another prototype will be developed which will have a symmetrical mounting. The testing methods will be a combination of local torque monitoring, global gait analysis, and VO2 (oxygen consumption) testing. A sensor–controller detection method will also be used to enable a controllable energy harvesting scheme and reduce the user’s effort. Light wearable energy harvesters for smart watches and smart wristbands will also be developed.

14204614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204614.value: During activities, human body generates significant amount of biomechanical energy, which is one of the promising energy forms in our living environment. With the rapid developments on low power wireless electronics and micro-electromechanical systems, future personal mobile devices and distributed sensing systems might become sustainable by scavenging energy from human motions and other biological activities. These eco-friendly devices would provide us convenient and comfortable livings, while enabling lower maintenance cost. Energy harvesters were designed and optimized with the considerations of human comfort and biomechanics. Analysis has been performed on the backward effect induced by energy harvesting on human efforts. This project provided in-depth studies on the physical principles and insights of the electromechanical energy conversions towards optimization for the kinetic energy harvesting systems under various human motions, as well as overall evaluation about the impact of energy harvesting on human efforts. Moreover, the optimal design strategies of self-adaptive energy harvesting systems have also been considered. It established foundation for the development of future self-powered personal mobile devices and autonomous distributed sensing systems. The scientific knowledge created through this project would facilitate the continuing research efforts on energy harvesting, ergonomics, and the full realization of self-powered mobile devices.

14204714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204714.value: 物理層網絡編碼在多址接入系統中的應用 摘要 研究目的： 本項目旨在為物理層網絡編碼（PNC）研究開闢一個新領域：PNC 在非中繼網絡中 的應用。具體來講，本提案提出了在多址接入網絡（multiple access setting）中應用PNC 的新方法。 研究背景： 物理層網絡編碼技術（PNC），最早由本次項目負責人（PI）的研究團隊在2006 年 的國際移動通信與網絡峰會（Mobicom）上提出[1]。通過利用物理層上的網絡編碼 特性，PNC 可以將無線中繼網絡的吞吐量提高100％ [1]。截至今日，PNC 逐漸發展成網絡編碼（Network Coding）研究領域中非常重要的一個分支，並且受到了廣 泛關注。例如，[1]是被引用次數最多的2006 年Mobicom 會議論文（超過1000 谷歌引用）。有幾個國際期刊的特刊，其中包括一個IEEE JSAC 特刊和兩個 EURASIP 專題，以及眾多的研討會和國際會議分會也一直致力於研究和探討 PNC。之前關於PNC 的研究主要集中於其在中繼網絡中的應用。這並不奇怪，因為網絡編 碼的基礎正是基於中間節點（即，中繼節點）將來自多個源節點的信息混合併將混合後的信息進行轉發。但是，我們近期的實驗發現了PNC 研究的一個新領域。具體來說，我們發現PNC 在非中繼網絡中依然可以發揮作用。在此之前，PNC 在非中繼 網絡中的應用從未被探索過。該項目旨在填補這一研究空白。 項目概述： 為了提高吞吐量，PNC 允許無線網絡中多個源節點同時發送信息。 PNC 接收器則基於重疊信號計算出一個網絡編碼數據包（例如，將源數據包進行按位異或運算。在中繼系統中，PNC 接收器是一個中繼節點，它只負責轉發網絡編碼數據包至其他節點。而在非中繼或者多址系統中，PNC 接收器則是最終的目的地：其最終目標並不是得到網絡編碼數據包，而是從各個源節點同時發送的每個源信息。一個有趣的問題是，PNC 解碼器所得到的網絡編碼數據包在非中繼系統中是否仍然有用？在本提案中，我們提出一個新的系統結構，稱為網絡編碼多址接入（NCMA，其中PNC 解碼器與傳統的多用戶解碼器（MUD）相結合，來提高無線多用戶接入網絡的吞吐量。我們基於軟件無線電平台快速開發的NCMA 原型機表明，從PNC 解碼器得到的網絡編碼數據包是有用的並且可以被充分利用，從而提高系統的吞吐量。受到初期研究成果的鼓勵，本提案提出一個為期三年的全面研究計劃。為了確保理 論的合理性，現實的針對性以及實際的影響力，該項研究的結構由三個相互關聯的部分所組成：（1）我們將基於NCMA 開發出不同種類的原型機來進行實驗; （2）我們將開展基礎理論研究以解釋我們觀察到的實驗現象，並根據理論研究的結果拓展新的NCMA 系統設計;（3）我們將與德國航空航天中心（DLR）合作來共同探討NCMA 在實際衛星網絡中的應用。 研究意義： 本提案旨在探討一個從未被研究過的，但是具有顯著科學意義的研究課題。可以說與無線中繼網絡相比，無線非中繼網絡則更為普遍並且廣泛存在於很多實際系統中。如果成功，本項目不僅將擴大PNC 的應用範圍，同時也將開闢很多新的並且有趣的無線網絡研究方向。

14204714.label: Realisation of objectives
14204714.value: All three objectives of this project have been met, with some research outcomes extending beyond the original three objectives. Objectives 1 and 2: With respect to objective 1, we completed an NCMA prototype on our software-defined radio (SDR) platform. Unlike many communications system prototypes on SDR developed at other research organizations which perform offline signal processing, our NCMA prototype operates in real time and can actually run real applications. For example, we successfully demonstrate simultaneous transmissions of two image files from two nodes to an AP [5] (see also demo in https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DgMeck1B9O8&feature=youtu.be). We have also successfully completed NCMA prototypes with higher-order modulation with MIMO capability. Results were published in [6, 7, 14]. Overall, our results indicate that MIMO-NCMA has good performance in the medium-to-high SNR regime. In this project, we have also successfully refined the PNC decoder (one of the decoders used in the NCMA system), to find the best trade-off between complexity and error-rate performance. Our results and outcomes on this front are published in [13] On the theoretical front of high-order modulated PNC decoders, we also discovered many new hereto unknown results. In particular, we find that high-order modulated PNC decoders can be very sensitive to tiny perturbations on channel characteristics. This theoretical investigation is quite subtle and the results have been published as a 20-page double-column paper in [2]. Another piece of theoretical work [3] investigated the impact of symbol misalignment estimation in PNC systems so that systems that are more robust can be designed. Guided by our theoretical understanding and taking on the challenge of overcoming the above sensitivity issue, we have successfully implemented a state-of-the-art lattice-coded PNC prototype in [9]. Objective 3: A PhD student of the PI’s group, Shakeel Salamat, visited DLR (German Aerospace Center) in the summer of 2015 in our collaborative effort with DLR. DLR had also sent three researchers to visit us in Hong Kong in our research collaboration. During these visits, the discussions were focused on the design of PNC channel decoders as well as their implementation over the SDR platform. Our collaboration results in several joint publications ([15] is one such publication). DLR is particularly interested in short-packet communications that have high reliability and low latency requirements. Our collaborative efforts focused on that front. Shakeel studied the impact of inaccurate phase estimation in PNC systems where messages are transmitted in short blocks. Short messages are of interest in a number of emerging applications such as machine-to-machine communication systems, Internet-of-things, messaging and signaling in cellular communications. In satellite communication, phase noise is one of the major factors that affects the overall performance of communication system. Due to phase noise, the channel (phase) estimates at the receiver side may not be perfect. On top of that, if short blocks are used to transmit, then long preamble or pilot sequences for channel state information are also not efficient. Short preamble sequence may also result in imperfect phase estimation at the relay. Thus, a new design is called for in the case of short-message NCMA/PNC. We have been able to quantify of the relative phase offset and derived the upper bound of packet error rate for the BPSK modulated PNC system with short messages. In addition, we have designed of LDPC based XOR-CD PNC decoder to achieve the packet error rate bound. These results were incorporated into our designs of NCMA systems for satellite communications. Leveraging the insights from the research in this project, we have also explored a few new frontiers beyond the objectives 1, 2, and 3. For example, while this project focuses on the uplink of an NCMA system, in [4], we began our research on the downlink aspect. The investigation in [4] yielded preliminary results that form the basis of a new ongoing research project. In [8], we explored distributed-base station system that may could form the basis of the investigation of a distributed-base station NCMA system in the future (see Section 6.2 for possible further developments for NCMA). 14204714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204714.value: Cited references are with respect to the publications listed at the end of Section 5.3. Altogether, 9 journal publications and 6 conference publications are associated with this projects. A number of students have also been trained under this project. Specific research outcomes and deliverables have been articulated in Section 5.3. Here, we focus on the big picture and additional salient findings arising from this project. A number of PHY-layers decoders are used in NCMA systems (e.g., MUD decoder, PNC decoder, and single-user decoder). Among them, PNC decoder is the most challenging to design, due to its sensitivity to imperfections in real communications (e.g., asynchronies between transmitters and receivers, channel-estimation error, power imbalance, etc.). The research in this project is unique in that it combines theoretical results and experimental prototyping to produce an overall robust and practical NCMS system. We found that the decoders for high-order modulated NCMA systems would need to be designed carefully to reduce complexity to make them amenable to real-time operation in real prototypes. In addition, high-order modulated NCMA systems are susceptible to imperfections in real environments (e.g., asynchronies between the oscillators of transmitters and receivers, imperfect channel-parameter estimations, etc.). The use of MIMO technique can improve the throughput and robustness of NCMA systems significantly. In a comprehensive design of an NCMA system, we have been able to achieve success for modulations up to 16-QAM (this is equivalent to a 256-QAM single-user system, considering the superimposed constellation of the two users in the NCMA system, and is quite challenging to realize on the software-defined radio platform). A high point of this research is the demonstration of PNC decoding in a system that makes use of lattice codes (which require very high-order modulations). Two major challenges are: (1) for good performance, channels of simultaneously transmitting nodes must be aligned; (2) for practicality, the complexity of lattice encoding at the transmitters and lattice decoding at the receiver must be reduced. We successfully addressed these challenges and implemented a first lattice-coded prototype on an SDR platform in [9]. In our implementation, the nodes use low-cost temperature-compensated oscillators only. The low overhead and accurate channel alignment were achieved by (1) a channel precoding system implemented over FPGA to realize fast feedback of channel-state information; (2) a highly-accurate carrier frequency offset estimation method; and (3) a partial-feedback channel estimation method that significantly reduces the amount of feedback information required.

14204714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204714.value: A potential direction for further research is the application of NCMA in IIoT (Industrial Internet of Things). This project has been focusing on boosting the throughput of a wireless network. For many IIoT applications – e.g., robotic control, automatic guided vehicles (AGV) – low latency and high reliability are of paramount importance. Whether NCMA can be extended to fulfill the low latency and high reliability requirements will be of interest. For robustness, we could consider the use of noncoherent detection at the PHY layer. Having a reliable link at the PHY layer under a favorable environment is not good enough in many IIoT settings. For example, the communication path between the transmitter and the receiver could be blocked by moving objects in a factory setting once in a while. To improve reliability, we need diversity. Instead of a single-node base station, we could install a distributed multi-node base station on the ceiling of a factory. If the path between a node of a base station and an AGV is blocked, the other nodes of a base station and the AGV may still be clear. An NCMA system based on multiple BSs will come into play in that regard.

14204714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204714.value: This project successfully demonstrated the application of physical-layer network coding (PNC) in multiple-access wireless networks. PNC was originally proposed by the PI’s research group in 2006. It was shown that PNC could boost throughput in wireless relay networks by 100%. Research on PNC attracted a wide following subsequently. Prior to this project, studies of PNC primarily focused on its use in relay networks. This project was the first exploration of the use of PNC in multiple-access networks without relays (a more common use case in practical networks such as Wi-Fi and cellular networks) To that end, this project has not only successfully produced many useful theoretical results to guide the design of such networks, but have also demonstrated the viability of the design in real prototypes on the software-defined radio platform. Two high points of this research are (1) the demonstration of the support of real TCP/IP applications over one of our network prototypes; (2) the demonstration of the first lattice-coded PNC system. Overall, this project has not only expanded the scope of PNC applications, but has also opened up many future research directions in wireless networking -- e.g., potential application of PNC in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).

14204814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14204814.value: 不利用全局定位的飛行機器人視覺反饋飛行控制

14204814.label: Project Objectives
14204814.value: Design a position-based visual servoing controller based on the nonlinear dynamics of a quadrotor robot for controlling its flying in an indoor unstructured environment without using any global positioning system; Design an adaptive algorithm for estimating on-line linear velocity and position of the aerial robot by fusing inertial measurements with image coordinates and optical flows of natural feature points of the environment; Use the Lyapunov theory to prove the asymptotic stability of the developed controller for hovering and trajectory tracking of the robot and analyze its robustness to model errors, measurement errors and disturbances; Verify the performance of the developed controller by experiments on a quadrotor robot at our laboratory.
rows: Design a position-based visual servoing controller based on the nonlinear dynamics of a quadrotor robot for controlling its flying in an indoor unstructured environment without using any global positioning system;

Design an adaptive algorithm for estimating on-line linear velocity and position of the aerial robot by fusing inertial measurements with image coordinates and optical flows of natural feature points of the environment;

Use the Lyapunov theory to prove the asymptotic stability of the developed controller for hovering and trajectory tracking of the robot and analyze its robustness to model errors, measurement errors and disturbances;
Verify the performance of the developed controller by experiments on a quadrotor robot at our laboratory.

14204814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204814.value: Autonomous flying control of an aerial robot must rely on feedback of position of the robot, which is mainly obtained by global positioning systems. The satellite-based GPS systems provide a simple solution to position measurement of outdoor aerial robots, but are not suitable for indoor environments. Positioning approaches such as visual tracking systems and landmark-based systems apply to structured environments only. Automatic flying control without global positioning systems is one of the most crucial problems for aerial robots, in particular those flying in indoor unstructured environments or outdoor environments where the GPS signals cannot be reliably detected. In this project, we will develop a new vision-based controller for a quadrotor robot to fly in an indoor environment automatically without using any global positioning system. The novelty of the controller to be developed can be summarized as follows: First, this controller employs an adaptive algorithm to estimate the linear velocity and position of the aerial robot on-line by fusing measurements from inertial sensors, such as IMU, with visual information of the environment captured by a vision system. Second, images of natural feature points, instead of artificial landmarks, in the environment and the optical flow are used in the velocity and position estimation. Third, unlike SLAM(Simultaneous Localization And Mapping)-based methods which involve tedious, unreliable and complicated map management and feature matching, this adaptive algorithm has a simple structure suitable for real-time implementation. Finally, this controller will be designed on the basis of the nonlinear dynamics of the quadrotor robot and its asymptotic stability will be proved by the Lyapunov theory. In addition to controller design and stability analysis, we will also investigate the robustness of the controller to be developed to modeling errors, measurement errors and disturbances. Experiments will be carried out on a quadrotor robot at our laboratory to validate the developed controller. The research outputs will contribute to the advancement of robotics and technology development in Hong Kong as well as the rest of the world. 飛行機器人的自動飛行控制必須使用位置反饋，而位置信息一般通過GPS等全局定位系統獲取。GPS雖然是室外飛行機器人定位的簡單解決方案，但不能適用於室內環境﹔視覺跟蹤、路標定位等系統隻適應於結構環境。不使用全局定位系統的自動飛行控制是飛行機器人的關鍵技術之一，特別是對於室內非結構環境或GPS信號不穩定的室外環境的飛行機器人極為重要。本項目中，我們將研究一個新的視覺反饋控制方法，以供四旋翼機器人不需要全局定位系統的自主飛行。這一新方法的特點在於以下幾點：首先，該方法融合IMU與視覺信息利用一個自適應算法在線估計機器人的線速度和位置。其次，機器人的線速度和位置估計使用環境中的自然特征而不是人為路標。第三，與同時構圖與定位法（SLAM）等不同，該方法不需要管理復雜的地圖和特征比對，結構簡單非常適合實時實現。最后，控制器的設計將充分考慮機器人的非線性動力學，而且控制器的穩定性可以利用Laypunov理論証明。除了控制器的設計與分析外，我們還將研究控制器對模型誤差、測量誤差、干擾等的魯棒性，並在實驗室的四旋翼飛行機器人平台進行實驗驗証。本項目的研究成果將對香港以至世界機器人技術的發展作出貢獻。

14204814.label: Realisation of objectives
14204814.value: The objectives of this project have been fully achieved as detailed in the following: (1) We developed a new imaged-based controller for a quadrotor robot to track moving target in an indoor environment using feedback from on-board cameras. Using the image feedback makes it possible to control the motion of an aerial robot without using a global positioning system. The dynamics of the robot has been taken into account in the controller design so as to ensure superior dynamic responses. The controller is then extend to flying and manipulation control of an aerial vehicle carrying a robot manipulator. In addition to localization, the challenges in controlling a flying manipulator include the complicated dynamics of the system and singularities of the robot manipulator. A hybrid visual servoing controller was developed to control flying and grasping of the manipulator mounted on a quadrotor while avoding the singular configurations. We further developed the controller to formation control of a group of quadrotors. The novelty of the new formation controller lies in that the linear velocities of the aerial robots are not employed in the control algorithm. Not using linear velocity can significantly improve the robustness of the controller because measurements of linear velocities are subject to various noises. The performance of the controllers was verified by experiments. The results have been published at Springer lecture notes and presented at major international conferences (sponsored by IEEE) in robotics and automation. Therefore, the first objective stated in the proposal has been achieved. (2) We developed a new framework for vision-based localization of robots using a class of consensus dynamics for formation control of networked agent systems. It was firstly proven that the vision-based localization problem of a robot in a GPS-denied environment can be transferred to a consensus problem of multi-robot systems, and then an adaptive algorithm has been developed for calculating position and velocity of the robot using image coordinates of the feature points in the environment. Compared to existing vision-based algorithms, which use both the image coordinates and optical flow, the proposed algorithm is simpler to implement and more computationally efficient because optical flow is not used. In addition, we have developed a geometric model for fusing IMU information with visual tracking process of nature feature points to estimate the trajectory of a robot including aerial robots in a 3-D space. The model employs tracking of a certain number of natural feature points in the environment, and fuses them with sensor data from IMU to perform iterative adaptive estimation of both the robot trajectory and the positions of the selected feature points. The good performance of the developed algorithms has been validated using experiments of aerial vehicles and autonomous ground vehicles as well. The work has been published at IEEE Trans. on Cybernetics or presented at an international conference sponsored by IEEE. Those represent that the second objective has been fully achieved. (3) We have developed an approach for on-line calibration of the vision system and the other sensors, such as the inertial measurement system, of a robotic system, which is critical for fusing information measured by the different sensing systems. The calibration accuracy significantly affects the performance/accuracy of the localization and mapping of robots. Calibration of the two sensing systems is a tedious and complicated process. Unlike the traditional approaches which estimate a huge number of states including the unknown positions of the robot, the unknown structure captured by the vision system, and the unknown parameters between the IMU and the vision system, the developed on-line approach only estimates the interested parameters of the IMU-vision system based on a novel concept called constrained Gaussian filter with virtual measurement. As a result, the dimension of the states under estimation is significantly reduced and the efficiency is greatly improved, and hence is suitable for real-time implementation. The reduction in dimension can also help improve the accuracy of the calibration for the uncertainties in the state estimation using the Kalman filter can be reduced. The performance of the algorithm has been verified by experiments. Parts of the results have been published on IEEE Trans. on robotics. This part of work also contributes to the achievement of the second objective. (4) We have analyzed the stability of the developed visual servoing controllers for a single UAV, a UAV carrying a robot manipulator, and a group of UAVs using Lyapunov theory based on the full nonlinear dynamics of the system. It has been theoretically proved that the controllers yield stable motion control or trajectory tracking of the aerial robots provided that the natural feature points or the targets can be traced by the vision system for a long time. The robustness of the controllers was also investigated. The stability and robustness have been verified by simulations and experiments. The convergence of the location algorithm has also been proved using control theory. The theoretical work means that the third objective has been achieved. (5) We have developed an experimental platform for experimental verification of the controllers. The experimental system consists of quadrotors, on-board vision system, and optical track system for tracking position and orientation of the quadrotors. The position and orientation measured by the optical track system are considered the ground truth for evaluating the performance of the controllers. An embedded system is developed to process the image processing and to carry out the necessary calculation of the controllers in order to achieve the real-time efficiency. The developed control algorithms were implemented on the quadrotors and experiments were conducted to verify the performance. Therefore, the forth objective has been achieved.

14204814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204814.value: (1) We developed a new imaged-based controller for a quadrotor to track moving target in an indoor environment using visual feedback. Using the image feedback makes it possible to control an aerial robot without a global positioning system. The controller is then extended to flying and manipulation control of an aerial vehicle carrying a manipulator. The complicated dynamics and singularities of the robot manipulator are taken into account in designing a hybrid visual servoing controller. The controller has been further developed to formation control of a group of quadrotors without using the linear velocities. The results led to a paper (paper 2) published in the Springer lecture notes and two papers presented at IEEE international conferences (conference papers 2 and 3). (2) We developed a new framework for vision-based localization of a robot in a GPS-denied environment. Based on a novel formulation using formation control of networked agent systems, an adaptive algorithm has been developed for localizing the robot by fusing image coordinates of the feature points with IMU inputs. Compared to existing algorithms that use both the image coordinates and optical flow, the proposed algorithm is simpler to implement and more computationally efficient for the optical flow is not employed. The work led to publication of a paper on IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics (paper 1). By introducing geometric constraints to this algorithm, a real-time visual SLAM method is developed for mobile robots. The results led to another paper published on IEEE Transections on Cybernetics (paper 4). (3) We have developed an approach for on-line calibration of the vision system and the other sensors, such as inertial sensors, odometry, etc., of a robotic system. Calibration of two sensors is tedious and complicated. Unlike traditional approaches that estimate a huge number of states including the unknown positions of the robot, the unknown structure of the environment, and the unknown parameters between the two sensing systems, the developed on-line approach estimates only the interested parameters using a new concept called constrained Gaussian filter with virtual measurement. As a result, the dimension of the states to be estimated is significantly reduced and the efficiency is greatly improved. The results have been published on IEEE Transaction on robotics (paper 3). (4) The stability and robustness of the controllers were verified by the experiments. (5) Under the support of this project, we have trained one Ph.D. student and one M.Phil. student.

14204814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204814.value: The project can be further developed in the following aspects: (1) Improving the robustness of the controllers to uncertainties and disturbances. In the controller design, the noises and disturbances were not explicitly considered. (2) Analyzing the stability of the performance of the controllers more rigorously. The developed analysis assumes that the natural feature points are always in the field of view of the vision system. However, this condition can be hardly satisfied. The discontinuity due to changes of the feature points in the field of view of the vision system must be considered in both controller design and stability analysis. (3) Extension of the localization and control algorithms to flying in outdoor environments. More experiments should be carried out to investigate the performance of the methods in the natural environments.

14204814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204814.value: In this project, we investigated localization and control of unmanned aerial vehicles using visual feedback in a GPS-denied environment. A novel adaptive algorithm has been developed to estimate position and orientation of a robot in a 3D space using the information from its on-board vision system based on the framework of consensus control of multi-agent systems. The algorithm has the advantages of being simple to implement on aerial robots and computationally efficient for real-time performance. On the basis of the new localization algorithm, we designed new vision-based controllers for a single quadrotor, a quadrotor carrying out a robot manipulator, and a group of quadrotors, respectively. In addition, a new on-line algorithm is proposed to calibrate the vision system and the other sensors of a robot using a newly developed constrained Gaussian filter with virtual measurements. The stability of the proposed controllers and the convergence of the localization algorithm have been proved using Lyapunov theory. The performance of the controllers and the algorithms was verified by experiments. The research results led to several publications in top journals and presentations at international conferences in robotics and automation. With the support, we also trained a M. Phil. student and a Ph.D. student. In conclusion, the project has been successfully completed.

14205114.value: 關於雲計算的網絡經濟學理論：理論與實現

14205114.label: Project Objectives
14205114.value: How profitable are PaaS/IaaS providers as compared to SaaS providers and who has more market power? rows: How profitable are PaaS/IaaS providers as compared to SaaS providers and who has more market power?
Does the current economics market allows competition among cloud players which will result in efficient resource allocation and good user perceived performance?
How does the degree of resource sharing in cloud may impact the conditions to (1) and (2)?

14205114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205114.value: 在過去的幾年裡，有一個被稱為“雲計算”的新計算服務日益增長。雲計算所聲稱的優點是在節約成本，彈性，可擴展性和資源的复用。事實上，大公司如谷歌，微軟，亞馬遜和中國的公司，如華為和騰訊都在積極進入這個雲計算市場，把自己定位為一個主要的雲計算服務提供商。 這一研究項目的目的是探討從“網絡經濟”的觀點看雲計算模式。我們力求提供雲計算的數學理論模型，並尋求了解雲計算些的互作用可能影響縮放和新的服務交付網絡的性能。 在我們研究的第一部分，我們建議研究價格競爭和資源的擁擠在雲計算市場的互動模式。本研究的第二部分，我們建議研究重點介紹如何當市場位於經濟平衡態的雲計算平台上分配資源（如CPU，內存，甚至網絡帶寬）。本研究的目的是開發雲計算平台的數學理論和定價/資源分配算法，使所有用戶都能受益。

14205114.label: Realisation of objectives
14205114.value: In the project, we have completed the three objectives. In particular, we have published number of important papers concerning cloud computing systems, especially on the price differentiation and we proposed to use the Kelly mechanism to provide price differentiation so that different cloud computing players can maximize their utilities. We also show that depending on the role and service provides, PaaS/IaaS providers can have more market power over SaaS because PaaS providers can also play a role of SaaS providers but not vice versa. In our research work, we have shown the current economics market allows competition and this is a healthy side to lower the price for cloud computing users. We also show that the degree of resource usage and sharing by cloud service providers can significant affect their profitability and market power.

14205114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205114.value: We have use economic theory to show the benefit of clouding computing. As we have predicted in our model, cloud computing is indeed gaining an exponential momentum in real life. One main research result is in formulating the competition between different cloud players (e.g., cloud users, cloud resource providers,...etc) and how pricing can affect the resource allocation and resource utilization. This model will be the basis for other researchers to determine the proper pricing under specific cloud usage scenario. This result is mainly presented in our ACM TOMPECS journal. Our research results have also shown the PaaS/IaaS can be more powerful than SaaS providers because they can also play a role of a SaaS provider but not vice versa. This is the reason why many cloud computing companies (e.g., Amazon, Microsoft) are building their dat centers, not only to deliver cloud services for their own products, but also services for other smaller companies. In relation to this project, we have also shown that users can also play a significant role to affect the clouding computing service (e..g, Amazon) by provide product rating. We have also developed various machine learning models to answer important questions like how many ratings do we need to accurately represent the intrinsic quality of cloud service, as well as machine learning algorithms to discover the online reputation systems for many E-commerce systems which operate on cloud systems.

14205114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205114.value: Since we only received HK$500,000 (or US$64000) for 3 years, we just wish that we could have received more funding to continue to do more experimental work. Some interesting experimental works which can be considered as further experiments include: - Provide software and probing techniques to estimate the truthfulness of cloud resource allocation - Provide software platform to debase product rating for E-commerce systems which operate on cloud systems.

14205114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205114.value: The significant of this research is in arguing the viability of cloud computing and their usage. As we have predicted, cloud became very popular and it is gaining more momentum. We have also provide a fundamental theory to determine the appropriate pricing and differentiation for cloud, and in particular, when there are more than one cloud providers in the market, how will this price competition affect the resource allocation. In short, we have illustrate the economics merits of clouds, and how resources should be allocated. We have also shown some important applications in cloud computing, e.g., E-commerce systems, and how the user rating and online reputation systems may affect the eco-system of E-commerce under the cloud setting.

14205214.label: Project Objectives
14205214.value: Framework design for building reliable service-oriented systems This objective is to design a framework for building a reliable service-oriented system, which should be composed of distributed service components provided by different organizations. The framework will consider the system itself, the remote service components, as well as the Internet connections, and will enhance service reliability at both server side and user side. Moreover, instead of the traditional model-oriented techniques, we will investigate service reliability from the data-oriented aspect of services computing Data-oriented collaborative service reliability prediction This objective is to investigate service reliability prediction in terms of data-oriented and collaborative techniques, which should make use of historical service usage experience of different users. Accurate service reliability prediction will be achieved from three main perspectives. Firstly, we will incorporate location information of both servers and users into the traditional collaborative filtering techniques to enable more accurate reliability predictions. Secondly, we will consider time-aware reliability prediction models for the adaptation to the data dynamics over time. Finally, we will study incremental learning techniques to predict service reliability more efficiently. Data-oriented fault tolerance for service-oriented systems Fault tolerance strategy is indispensable when building reliable service-oriented systems. In this objective, we aim at investigating data-oriented fault tolerance strategies for reliable service-oriented systems from three aspects. Firstly, instead of considering fault tolerance strategy at design time, we will provide flexible fault tolerance strategies, which can automatically adapt to the dynamic environment at runtime. Secondly, we focus on personalized fault tolerance strategy selection for service-oriented systems, whose goal is to dynamically select the optimal fault tolerance strategy based on both global and local information. Finally, we will present identification techniques for fault-tolerant service-oriented systems to help system developers find and focus on core service components in their service-oriented systems. We will collect service reliability and failure information through Planet-Lab, arrange the information into an easily-processing data format, and publish the data for research purpose.

14205214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205214.value: At the age of Web 2.0, the rising prevalence of services computing has been witnessed by its acceptance in an increasing number of banks, governments, and commercial companies, which design and develop their software systems employing service-oriented architecture (SOA) to offer timely services to their customers. Among the many factors that affect the quality of a service-oriented system, reliability is an important metric to evaluate the usefulness and quality of the system. A highly reliable system not only generates revenues for the company by saving the cost of repairing or rebooting, but also offers pleasant user experience to the company’s customers, which contributes to keeping old customers as well as attracting new ones. However, due to their large customer bases, service-oriented systems (e.g., Amazon Web Services, Google Apps, etc.) are more vulnerable to service crash caused by various reliability issues, compared to traditional software systems. For some service-oriented systems, only a few minutes’ downtime may result in big financial losses. Hence, to avoid such a huge loss, establishing a systematic way to predict and enhance reliability of service-oriented systems becomes a necessary and urgent research target. Service-oriented systems, which are composed of distributed service components, are usually very complex, large-scale, and highly dynamic. The service components are developed and maintained by third-parties, often without any source codes, and invoked by unpredictable Internet connections. Therefore, no single reliability prediction model can accurately predict the reliability of service-oriented systems. Likewise, no single fault-tolerance strategy can be employed to effectively tolerate faults in the highly dynamic services computing environment. To address this critical challenge, this project focuses on data-oriented reliability prediction and fault tolerance in services computing. Compared with traditional software reliability engineering techniques, three paradigm shifts are made in this project: (1) from model focused to data focused; (2) from system oriented to user oriented; and (3) from development-environment centric to operational-environment centric. Specifically, we will first design a framework for building reliable service-oriented systems. Secondly, we will employ service location and time information as well as incremental learning techniques to predict service reliability more efficiently and effectively. Thirdly, we will investigate comprehensive data-oriented fault tolerance techniques at the user-side for the achievement of high service reliability from user’s perspective. Finally, we will publish reusable research datasets and release an open-source service reliability toolkit to promote the development of highly reliable service-oriented systems.

14205214.label: Realisation of objectives
14205214.value: All the objectives in this project have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. We designed general frameworks for improving the reliability of various service-oriented systems, such as mobile systems and cloud service systems, which are in support of most applications and services nowadays. In addition, we proposed several approaches and employed a set of advanced techniques to predict collaborative service reliability, which is built on top of the massive amount of system-generated reliability data. Moreover, we investigated the data-oriented fault tolerance from various perspectives, app review, android performance, add cost, etc. To achieve the project objectives, a number of machine learning and data mining techniques are employed and designed, including online learning, spatial-temporal latent ranking, feature selection, etc.

14205214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205214.value: In total, there are 3 journal papers and 17 conference papers are published, covering the project’s objectives in various aspects. These publications all acknowledge the support of this grant. We describe the resulting outcomes as follows. (We use [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], and [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], etc.) The first objective is to design frameworks for building reliable service-oriented systems that consist of distributed service components. We first designed a framework to collect the QoS information from service users while preserving the privacy [C3]. Meanwhile, an N-version obfuscation framework is proposed to address potential security issues for accesses from mobile platforms [C5, J3]. The second objective focuses on data-oriented collaborative service reliability prediction. Due to a large amount of data involved, we study several machine learning methods, including online non-negative dictionary learning for data analysis[C8], training efficient feature map for shift-invariant kernels[C2], overlapping community detection[C9, J1], etc. These techniques can help capture the characteristics of system-generated reliability data and make predictions accordingly. Especially, we employ regularized matrix factorization with asymmetric correlation for service reliability prediction[C6]. To obtain better service prediction, we study the regression tasks with a fast relative-error approximation algorithm[C11]. In the third objective, we study the data-oriented fault tolerance for service-oriented systems. With mobile systems as the main object, our study is conducted from three aspects, i.e., app issues, ad costs, and system performance. Towards this end, an automated tool is proposed to prioritize potential app issues through the user review mining [C1]. Furthermore, we investigate the service issues across various main-stream platforms [C12]. To assist mobile app developers, a data-driven method is proposed to measure the ad costs [C16]. Moreover, we design an effective mobile app profiling method to detect the performance problem automatically [C10]. In addition, we propose a general framework for fault tolerance using system logs in distributed service systems. We investigate and propose automated log parsing approaches [C7, J2] as well as anomaly detection methods [C13] for large-scale data in a systematic manner. Moreover, we study several machine learning techniques that could help enhance the data-oriented fault tolerance, including spatial-temporal ranking [C4, C15], location-based social networks [C17], contextual bandits [C14], etc. The fourth objective focuses on realization and toolkit publication. We implement the above-mentioned techniques and conducted comprehensive experiments. We also initiate a public repository on Github, i.e., LogPAI (https://github.com/logpai), to share the source code and data to promote related research.

14205214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205214.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives of our project, where a comprehensive framework for reliability prediction and fault tolerance in services computing is established and evaluated. For future research, we can design and implement a toolkit that contains data-driven reliability prediction methods. Besides, we can collect more platform-generated data, e.g., logs, QoS information, in a systematic and comprehensive way. We have initiated collection efforts for logs data as a benchmark, namely, LogPAI (https://github.com/logpai) repository, where the associated analysis tools are also provided. This initiative would allow our proposed and well-evaluated techniques to be reproducible and employable by researchers and practitioners. Further efforts can be devoted for other service related data, such as service execution traces and user feedback. The fourth objective focuses on realization and toolkit publication. We implement the above-mentioned techniques and conducted comprehensive experiments. We also initiate a public repository on Github, i.e., LogPAI (https://github.com/logpai), to share the source code and data to promote related research.

14205214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205214.value: We investigated the reliability prediction and fault tolerance in services computing via modeling and exploiting platform-generated big data, including framework design for building reliable systems, service reliability prediction, and fault tolerance. Various data mining and machine learning techniques are proposed and employed, such as anomaly detection, collaborative filtering, feature selection, matrix factorization, regression, online learning, and so on. Design and implementation for the proposed techniques were provided, and empirical experimentation was extensively conducted. The research outcome can bring new insights and practical application for systematic reliability engineering of modern service-oriented systems.

14205314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205314.value: The past few years have witnessed an emergence of sparse and low-rank matrix optimization models and their applications in data sciences, signal processing, machine learning etc. A natural extension of matrix to higher-dimensional space is tensor. Traditional matrix-based data analysis is inherently two-dimensional, which limits its ability in extracting information from a multi-dimensional perspective. Tensor-based multi-dimensional data analysis has shown that tensor models can take full advantage of the multi-dimensional structures of the data, and generate more useful information. In the era of big data analytics, we are facing huge-scale dense data in the form of tensor from different areas such as computer vision, diffusion MRI, spectral hypergraph theory and higher-order Markov chains. How to extract useful information from these tensor data becomes a very challenging task. Stimulated by the need of big data analytics, and motivated by the success of compressed sensing and low-rank matrix optimization, it is important and timely to study methods for analyzing massive tensor data. A common observation for huge-scale data analysis is that the data exhibits a low-dimensional property. This leads to the study of low-rank tensor optimization problems. A common way to handle tensor optimization problems is to unfold the tensor into a matrix. However, the usual way to unfold the tensor lacks rigorous analysis on the connection between the resulting matrix and the original tensor. As a result, finding ways to deal with tensor data and solving low-rank tensor optimization problems are in demand. In real applications arising from data sciences, signal processing, computer vision, medical imaging etc., challenges also lie in arbitrary gross outliers, missing data, and huge-scale and dense data. It is thus important to investigate efficient optimization algorithms to deal with these problems. The primal goals of our research under this project are: (i) to develop new matricization schemes for tensor and to analyze the corresponding relation between its CP rank and the rank of its matrix counterpart; (ii) to apply the matricization scheme to low-rank tensor recovery problems and their variants, and to develop efficient first-order optimization algorithms for solving these problems; (iii) to develop efficient algorithms for solving sparse PCA for tensor; (iv) to apply these models and algorithms to solve tensor optimization problems arising from real applications such as statistics, signal processing, machine learning and bioinformatics; (v) to develop a suit of codes with a uniform interface for solving these low-rank tensor optimization problems. 稀疏和低秩矩陣優化最近幾年有著蓬勃發展並且被廣泛應用于數據科學，信號處理，機器學習等領域。張量是矩陣的一個自然的高維推廣。傳統的基於矩陣的數據分析是二維的，這對於從高維來對信息進行提取是一種限制。基於張量的數據分析可以有效的利用數據的高維特性來產生更加有效的信息。在大數據時代，我們需要處理大規模的稠密的張量數據。這些數據來源於計算機視覺，核磁共振，超圖理論以及高維馬爾科夫鏈等領域。如果從這些張量數據裡面提取有用的信息是一個非常具有挑戰性的任務。 由於大數據時代的推動，並與基於壓縮感知和低秩矩陣優化的成功，研究大規模的張量數據是重要並且及時的。大規模高維數據的一個常見特性是這些數據一般在本質上是具有低維性質的。這促使我們研究低秩張量的優化問題。處理張量優化問題的一個常用辦法是把張量展開成為一個矩陣。但是，傳統的把張量展成矩陣的辦法對於張量和展開后的矩陣的秩之間的關係缺乏嚴格的理論分析。所以，找到一個有效的處理張量數據並且求解低秩張量優化問題的方法就變得非常關鍵。在很多實際應用中，比如數據科學，信號處理，計算機視覺，醫學圖像等，數據中存在噪聲或者缺失信息，並且數據是非常大規模並且稠密的，這些都給研究帶來很多挑戰。所以，深入研究相關的有效的優化算法是非常有必要的。 我們在這項研究中的主要目標有：(1) 研究一種新的將張量展成矩陣的方法，並且研究得到的矩陣和原始的張量的秩之間的關係；(2) 將這種新的矩陣化的方法應用于求解低秩張量的恢復問題，並且提出有效的一階優化算法來解決這些問題；(3) 研究求解張量的稀疏主元分析的優化算法；(4) 將這些模型和算法應用到統計學，信號處理，機器學習，生物信息學等領域；(5) 發展一套求解低秩張量優化的軟件包。
