14205314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205314.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project include: 1. We designed new methods based on gauge dual for solving robust PCA and SDP problems. In particular, it sheds lights on new algorithms for solving robust tensor PCA problems. 2. Studied stochastic quasi-Newton method for solving large-scale nonconvex machine learning problems. This class of methods is very suitable for solving tensor optimization problems. 3. Designed an efficient algorithm for solving an classification problem arising in bioinformatics. 4. Designed an efficient first-order algorithm for solving quatile regression problem arising in statistics. 5. Proposed a new approach for tuning the learning-rate in stochastic gradient descent algorithm for solving machine learning problems. This new algorithm is well suited for solving large-scale machine learning problems based on tensor data. 6. Designed a proximal average approximation algorithm for solving composite optimization problems in machine learning problems. 7. Characterized the Lojasiewicz exponent of orthogonality-constrained homogeneous quadratic optimization problems and established the linear convergence of a large class of retraction-based line-search methods and a stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for solving such problems.

14205314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205314.value: Potential for further development include: 1. Research results in this project indicate that designing new step size and incorporating second-order information is very important to speed up stochastic algorithms for solving nonconvex machine learning problems. How to make these algorithms more robust and scalable deserves more investigation. 2. Robust tensor PCA problem is important for bioinformatics and machine learning applications. How to extend the results obtained in this project for robust matrix PCA problem to its tensor counterpart is a very promising research direction. 3. Currently, the Lojasiewicz exponents of many optimization problems that arise in practice (especially the non-smooth ones) are not known. An important direction is to characterize such exponents, as they will lead to a deeper understanding of the convergence behavior of a host of iterative methods.

14205314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205314.value: Low-rank tensor recovery and tensor PCA problems appear frequently and have important applications in machine learning and computer vision. In this project, we designed various algorithms for solving this class of problems, and provided theoretical foundations for them. These algorithms are shown to be suitable for solving problems in bioinformatics, signal processing, machine learning, statistics, and so on.

14205414.label: Project Objectives
14205414.value: develop blind and semiblind hyperspectral unmixing formulations that can accommodate unknown model order and can resist undesirable effects caused by outliers. develop pragmatic optimization methods for the formulations, and custom-devise efficiently implementable algorithms for practical purposes. conduct extensive experiments, including those for real hyperspectral data, to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms and to identify their advantages. study theoretical aspects that can shed light into fundamental limits and performance tradeoffs of the methods developed.

14205414.label: Realisation of objectives
14205414.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. For Objective 1, we successfully developed a robust semiblind hyperspectral unmixing formulation by using the smooth power-p data fitting error function and by incorporating a dictionary adjusted scheme. Following this direction, we also considered the volume minimization-based blind hyperspectral unmixing approach, which is powerful in its theoretical recovery guarantees but is known to be sensitive to outliers in its original form. We were successful with establishing a robustified volume minimization-based solution. Furthermore, we proposed a new hyperspectral unmixing formulation by a probabilistic approach. The new formulation overcomes some design difficulties in our previous works, specifically, the need to tune certain system parameters which have no clear guidelines. For Objective 2, our investigation led to a practical optimization approach for the formulations described in Objective 1. The approach was established via a judicious combination of recent advances in first-order optimization, such as majorization minimization, inexact alternating minimization, and accelerated proximal gradient. It is not only equipped with the theoretical guarantee of convergence to a stationary solution, but also it was found to be efficient in our experiments and simulations which we conducted rather extensively. For Objective 3, we demonstrated that our proposed algorithmic solutions yield promising performance. In one of our real hyperspectral imaging experiments we found that our algorithm can identify outliers caused by abnormality in the image. The abnormality found appears to match with what domain study indicates. As yet another exciting discovery, we successfully expanded the applicability of our blind unmixing solution to topic modeling in machine learning. For Objective 4, we developed a novel theoretical analysis framework for the self-dictionary sparse regression problem. We established a new branch of blind unmixing theory by studying the maximum volume inscribed ellipsoid. The aforementioned work provides new insight into the theory underpinning blind hyperspectral unmixing, and its contribution is very original and novel from a theoretical viewpoint.

14205414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205414.value: This research has led to significant advancement in the hyperspectral unmixing (HU) techniques and has gone the extra mile on some of the objectives. On the practical side, our main contributions lie in two directions. One is semiblind HU leveraged on availability of a spectral dictionary. The inherent drawback with the dictionary-aided semiblind HU approach is that the spectral sample of a material in the dictionary is never exactly the same as that in the actual environment, and this leads to model mismatch. In our paper in IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing in 2016, we proposed a remedial solution by considering a dictionary-adjusted formulation to correct the mismatch effects. In that work we also advocated the use of non-convex sparse promoting regularization to improve performance. Another is blind HU via volume minimization (VolMin). The PI’s previous work has shown that VolMin has attractive blind recovery guarantees (theoretically). However, VolMin is also known to be sensitive to outliers. In our paper in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing in 2016, we developed a robustified VolMin formulation. Remarkably, in our real experiment we demonstrated that the new robust VolMin solution is not only much more robust than before, it also identifies abnormality in the image. Through the developments in the two aforementioned research outcomes, we established a flexible and efficient optimization framework, which is not limited to HU but can also be applied to related problems in machine learning and big data. In our ICASSP 2018 paper, we modified this optimization framework to serve another application, namely, hyperspectral super-resolution, a problem closely related to HU. The work shows order-of-magnitude improvement in runtime. We also leveraged on our research advances in HU by studying a completely different HU framework. The work, published in ICASSP 2017, has much potential. It brings statistical inference concepts to HU and can overcome limitations with the existing robust formulations. The difficulty is that the new approach involves stochastic optimization and is much harder to solve. The optimization framework we built previously helped us much in tackling this new direction. We also made several important theoretical contributions. The signature one is the paper published in SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences in 2018, where we established a new theory, maximum volume inscribed ellipsoid, for HU. In our work in IEEE Signal Processing Letters in 2016, we analyzed robustness of the self-dictionary HU convex formulation under unknown model order.

14205414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205414.value: The PI is much grateful for receiving this GRF. Through this project, he has sharpened his and his team’s skills and built synergy on structured matrix factorization and related optimization techniques. The structured matrix factorization techniques built not only received some attention in remote sensing, as indicated by citations, some very recent developments in machine learning and big data---such as topic discovery, document classification, community detection and crowdsourcing---suggest that similar matrix factorization techniques are much sought after. A very promising further development is to pursue applications in machine learning and big data. In fact, in his latest research the PI is actively looking into such possibilities. The optimization techniques built for the project also have great potential for further development. Presently, non-convex optimization---with emphasis on problem structure exploitation---has attracted attention in machine learning, data science, signal processing, etc. The synergy built from this project has been very helpful with the PI’s other research developments in this topic.

14205414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205414.value: Hyperspectral imaging is a powerful imaging technology that can allow one to identify materials our naked eyes could not distinguish, and it has found a wide spectrum of applications, e.g., agriculture, land-cover mapping and environment monitoring in remote sensing; planetary exploration in astrophysics; pigment identification in art conservation; food inspection; medical imaging; to name a few. While hyperspectral imaging attracts most interest from remote sensing, in recent years we have also seen growing and increasingly widespread interest from other different fields. In this project we investigated hyperspectral unmixing (HU), an important topic that aims at identifying the materials and their compositions from the image without or with little supervision. We developed practical HU solutions that yield robustness against adverse effects arising from real applications, namely, outliers in the image and model order uncertainties. We also developed new theory for better fundamental understanding of HU. Our methods draw insight from recent advances in mathematical optimization, particularly, those we see in machine learning and big data; more precisely we custom-designed our optimization schemes with a balance between theory and practice. Our research is expected to have long-term impact on the scientific side, providing new algorithmic tools to practitioners.

14205514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205514.value: 目的 此項目的目的是製造首個用於高效太赫茲生物醫學成像的可變折射率液晶體聚焦鏡。 項目背景 傳統太赫茲光譜的成像通常是緩慢的，特別是光柵掃描。這些系統依賴兩個電動線性平台來移動樣品（或太赫茲發射器和檢測器），限制了掃描速度。此外，該線性平台往往受反沖影響，導致測量精度下降。即使移動發射器和檢測器進行掃描，樣品在整個測量中也需要保持靜止，使光柵掃描過於費時，令這些系統不適合用於生物醫學的體內成像。一種克服這些問題的方法是使用自適應透鏡將太赫茲光束轉向，使樣品與發射器和檢測器可以保持靜止。我們提出的解決方案是設計和製造液晶體自適應透鏡引導太赫茲光束同時保持樣品靜止。這免除了使用繁瑣的電動線性平台，並提高了數據採集的效率。 項目簡介 自適應液晶體透鏡在可見光頻率是相當成熟的技術。然而，將液晶體透鏡縮放到用於太赫茲頻率面臨一些顯著挑戰。在可見光的頻率，這些採用玻璃窗結構和電極的透鏡由氧化銦錫（ITO）製成，但這在太赫茲頻率具高吸收性。因此，全世界只有少數組別曾嘗試製造液晶透鏡。在這個項目中，我們將會設計和製造創新的液晶透鏡，相比現有的科技有著顯注的優勢。我們將使用一種低損耗性的窗口材料（Topas）並優化金屬電極的設計，以達致聚焦點的三維轉向同時將太赫茲頻率範圍的信號損失減到最低。此項目將為太赫茲靜態樣本成像帶來基礎性突破。 項目的重要性 我們團隊的跨學科專業知識（太赫茲成像，太赫茲光譜學，光學裝置製造，液晶體裝置製造和醫療成像），將有利於我們製造首個可變折射率的液晶體聚焦鏡。這些鏡頭也將能容易和實惠地適應目前在全球許多組別使用中的光譜系統。我們所提出的聚鏡，將大大推動包括生物醫學成像在內的太赫茲光譜和成像的多種應用。

14205514.label: Realisation of objectives
14205514.value: Note on administrative arrangements: This project was originally awarded to Prof Macpherson as PI and the PI was changed to Prof Tsang only during the final months of the project when Prof Macpherson took no pay leave from CUHK. Hence most of the objectives (and publications) were produced by Prof Macpherson (with only one conference publication co-authored with Prof Tsang). The "we" below refers mostly to work carried out by Prof Macpherson and her students. Objectives 1&2. We have designed, simulated and fabricated a LC adaptive lens for use at THz frequencies. The proposed LC lens has two LC cells (one with horizontal and the other with a vertical grating electrode) and a 45。linear polarizer in the middle. For each cell, the electrode design incorporates a 60/30-um period/width grating (100-nm Au with 20-nm Cr on bottom) on 1-mm-thick fused silica. Five periodic gratings make up a unit electrode (300µm) where the voltage is the same. The active area for the device consists of 36 unit electrodes (1.08cm). A 200-µm-thick RDP-94990 LC material is chosen as the LC layer due to its relatively high transmission and large birefringence (△n≈0.2 at the broadband THz range). A 500-µm-thick silicon wafer is used as bottom substrate. The LC is initially aligned horizontally by use of a PI layer. The 45。linear polarizer, with 20/10-µm period/width grid wires, is fabricated on the silicon of the first LC cell. To test the effectiveness of this design, we have measured the LC orientation change and the corresponding phase shifting results at desired positions with a standard transmission THz time-domain spectroscopy system. Here, we present two phase shifting examples. One is a linear and the other is a quadratic distribution of phase change. The one-dimension results and the corresponding applied voltages for one LC cell were presented in a conference paper (Kaidi Li et al, “ Electrically Tunable Terahertz Liquid Crystal Spatial Phase Shifter”, Nagoya, Sept 2018, THz conference. The results demonstrated that we have successfully controlled the orientation of the LC molecules and thus the birefringence at desired different positions across the lens.) Objective 3. We have designed and fabricated a micro-controller to control the voltages applied onto different electrodes. Multiple rheostats (each with a resistance range from 10Ω to 2MΩ) are soldered on a circuit board in parallel connection. Each rheostat has three output lines: two of them are connected to the voltage source and another one is connected to one of the electrodes. The output voltage can be adjusted continuously by changing the resistance of the rheostat. By properly choosing the voltage source, the voltage controller can output different voltages in a large range from 0V up to the maximum of the voltage source, which provides good capacity to adjust the LC molecule orientations. Objective 4. We have integrated the designed LC lens into our THz imaging system (transmission mode). The continuous THz source pumped by CO2 laser at 2.53THz is used as THz generator, and the Golay cell (Microtech SN: 220712-D) mounted in a two-dimensional translation stage is used as the detector in the imaging system. The LC lens is fixed in the parallel beam path between the THz source and detector. For the first LC lens design (200-µm-thick RDP-94990 LC material), the focus length is about 27.5 cm. The THz beam profile measurement results demonstrated the effectiveness of the LC lens design. By integrating two LC lenses into the system, it can be applied to perform imaging of physically static samples at the focus point. Objectives 5&6. For the first LC lens design (200-µm-thick RDP-94990 LC material), the beam steering capacity is relatively small. We simulated the LC beam steering results for different LC layer thickness, and the simulation results demonstrated that larger beam steering can be achieved with thicker LC layer. But the switching speed is low for thick LC layer. To overcome this issue, we proposed a novel electrode structure, able to switch to and from both in- and out-plane orientations (Tip-Top) to largely increase the switching speed. Furthermore, since the ultimate goal is to use the adaptive lens to aid THz imaging of biomedical samples, it is important to minimize the data acquisition time whilst maintaining accurate extraction of the sample properties. To this end, we have also developed several adaptive sampling techniques to significantly increase the sampling rate and keep the accuracy. We have fabricated another LC adaptive lens with thick LC layer (500-µm-thick RDP-94990 LC material) and the new Tip-Top electrode design was used to improve the switching speed. We have measured the refractive index distribution after applying different voltages and the results demonstrated that we can control the orientation of the LC molecules effectively at desired different positions across the lens. We have not yet integrated the new LC lens into a THz imaging system nor optimize the software to image medical samples, but given the project was only partially funded, this part of the project objectives was not carried out.

14205514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205514.value: In this project we have designed and fabricated a LC adaptive lens and also developed a micro-controller to control the voltages applied on different electrodes. Two-dimensional LC orientation and THz phase shift control was achieved using the proposed design. The LC lens was also integrated into our THz imaging system and the beam profile measurement results demonstrated the focusing ability of the LC lens and can be used for imaging of physically static samples. To aid THz imaging of biomedical samples in vivo, we have proposed a novel electrode structure to improve the switching speed and also developed several adaptive sampling techniques to significantly increase the sampling rate and keep the accuracy. The imaging of the biomedical samples in vivo is ongoing. We have finished the fundamental work for the system of this project and have achieved very promising results which will have great impact in the terahertz community as well as the LC community. This project so far has an output of 12 journal papers and 9 international conference proceedings. These publications relate to different aspects of the project, such as the two dimensional LC phase shifter (conference proceedings 1), new electrode design to help increasing the switch speed (journal paper 1); developing techniques and algorithms for faster and accurate data acquisition (journal papers 6,7, 10 and 11); and investigation of biomedical applications (journal papers 2, 3 & 9).

14205514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205514.value: There is potential to further develop the research to the applications of in-vivo measurements. By adopting a thicker LC layer and combing with the novel electrode design (improving switching speed), the new LC lens can be integrated into a THz reflection imaging system. The imaging software can also be optimized by using the adaptive sampling techniques. Corresponding data processing methods will also be developed. Another area for future work is the combination of the LC device with THz compressed sensing imaging techniques. The proposed LC device can achieve two-dimensional amplitude and phase modulation, which is very suitable for compressed sensing sampling demands. The device is basically ready for this application.

14205514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205514.value: The project developed novel electrically tunable optics for THz signals. The liquid crystal based THz lens can have electically tunable focal lengths and may also be used in beam steering applications. The novel THz optics have potential applications in medical imaging and solid-state beam steering of THz signals for security scanning applications.

14205814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205814.value: This project aims to develop deep learning architectures for expressive text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis that incorporates effective prosodic control. Recent technological advancements have raised the intelligibility of synthetic speech to approach human speech, but there remains an apparent gap in naturalness. A main contributing factor towards perceived naturalness is prosody, which refers to intonation, rhythm and stress in speech. Prosody can express abundant information beyond words and grammar in a spoken message, including emphasis, intent and emotions. Research in linguistics has established a hierarchical structure of speech prosody, whose layers from top down are: intonational phrase, prosodic phrase, prosodic word, syllable and phoneme. Prosodic units in different layers are associated with different boundaries. This hierarchical prosodic structure is manifested through its acoustic correlates, including the fundamental frequency contour, segmental duration allocations, intensity distributions and boundary pauses. The manifestations involve intricate relationships between prosodic contexts and acoustic features, which presents a major challenge in modeling prosody for synthesis This problem is further aggravated by the additional challenge of data sparsity, since it is difficult to ensure that a training dataset achieves sufficient coverage of the vast combinatorial prosodic-acoustic space. Consequently, existing speech synthesis techniques are limited in prosodic control. Rule-based techniques encounter difficulty in specifying rules to cover the complex prosodic-acoustic mappings. Concatenative techniques degrade in quality when needed acoustic units in certain prosodic contexts are absent from the stored database. Modifications via signal processing also lower output quality. Statistical parametric synthesis, primarily based on hidden Markov models, adopts strong independence assumptions which may abandon information useful for synthesis. The approach builds decision trees by data partitioning, which is vulnerable to sparse data. To address these challenges, we propose to develop a deep learning (DL) speech synthesis framework. DL applies layered, non-linear transformations for supervised or unsupervised learning in pattern analysis and classifications. The layered organization should lend itself well for learning the hierarchical prosodic structure. DL also uses a single network to model all training data, which facilitates data sharing and avoids data partitioning. The network can learn characteristics and correlations among prosodic contexts and acoustic features, while generalizing over others. Unsupervised learning can learn from unlabeled datasets to increase coverage of the prosodic-acoustic space. We believe that the DL framework will offer better prosodic control and raise naturalness in synthetic speech. This will benefit diverse applications, such as multimedia systems, spoken dialog systems and assistive systems for the visually impaired.

14205814.label: Realisation of objectives
14205814.value: Objective 1: Define the hierarchical prosodic structure of speech for the deep learning model We define the prosodic structure of Mandarin, containing 21 tonal symbolic identities (i.e. tonal syllable finals) and 18 numerical features (e.g. position of the syllable in current word, number of words in the previous phrase), for speech synthesis using Weighted Multi-distribution Deep Belief Network. We were invited by Google and Microsoft to co-author a joint paper that reviews different techniques (ours and theirs) in the use of deep learning for speech synthesis. We also investigate the learning of cross-lingual information from language-specific prosodic structure features. We first try the idea of transferring spectral information across languages in the conventional hidden Markov model (HMM) framework, and find that we can directly build one-to-one mapping between tied-states of two languages based on Kullback-Leibler divergence. The tied states are the leaf nodes of decision trees clustered on prosodic contexts. Based on the mapping, we can replace the tied-states in one language with those in another language for the target speaker to transfer speaker-dependent spectral information across languages. This reveals that the representation of context-dependent spectral information, tied-states, in different languages can be treated as speaker-dependent universal elementary units. Following this thinking line, we conjecture that in deep learning models, there are also shared representations helpful for modelling cross-lingual information. In our experiments we found that the shared hidden layers across different languages enhance speech synthesis performance of both the auxiliary and target languages, which verifies our hypothesis. This finding is also beneficial for building speech synthesis system of low resource languages. Objective 2: Explore possible deep learning architectures for prosodic control in E-TTS We first compare three different architectures already used in TTS tasks including Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), Deep Belief Network (DBN) and Deep Neural Network (DNN). We then decide to use the latter two models, as well as the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for further investigation in E-TTS and related speech generation tasks because: (i) they use the centralized network scheme and are able to avoid the data partitioning issue in conventional TTS systems; and (ii) the frequency domain correlations between speech spectral coefficients can also be modelled by the network hidden layer weights, which potentially improve the quality of the synthesized speed. We extend the DBN model to the Weighted Multi-distribution DBN (wMD-DBN) for context-dependent statistical parametric speech synthesis. The proposed model uses an extra weighting vector on the acoustic output layer of DBN to reduce the dimensional imbalance between spectrum and pitch parameters in the model training procedure. Experimental results show that wMD-DBN could generate smooth pitch contours which contributed to the naturalness of the synthesized speech. We also began to explore ways to adapt a given speaker’s voice to sound like a target speaker’s voice, which is referred to as the voice conversion task. We propose to use deep learning models, DNNs and DBLSTM RNNs, to model the acoustic-to-acoustic regression for a voice conversion task. We build an HMM-based system as a baseline system. Experiments show that the deep learning models can properly model the speech contexts, while RNNs have the advantage on modelling accuracy and can produce smoother articulatory trajectory. DBLSTM RNN are demonstrated to have good performance on converted speech generation with more challenged conditions that (a) non parallel training data; and (b) arbitrary source speaker (i.e., many-to-one conversion vs. conventional one-to-one conversion). The deep learning models outperform the baseline HMM-based model. Based on the above voice conversion technique, we build a personalized cross-lingual TTS system with only limited data of target speaker in a non-target language. A general TTS engine first synthesizes speech in the target language (in a non-target voice). Then, the acoustic-to-acoustic regression from the non-target speaker target-language speech to the target-speaker target-language speech is modelled by a DBLSMT model. We introduce the phonetic posteriorgram (PPG), represent the articulation speech sounds in a speaker-normalized and language-independent space, to achieve the voice conversion across languages. Experimental results show that our method can achieve comparable performance to the benchmark HMM-based system in both speech quality and speaker similarity. In addition to the advantage of the voice conversion technique mentioned above, our proposed method also offers the advantages that (a) it does not need cross-lingual training data; and (b) it can achieve arbitrary target language synthesis (by using TTS engines in different languages). We also propose to learn cross-lingual information via multilingual DBLSTM that shares hidden layers across different languages. With this architecture, the cross-lingual information can be learned and benefit the training of a TTS synthesizer for low-resource or resource-limited languages. The input to the DBLSTM is a single uniform representation of feature vectors of different languages combined together. The multilingual DBLSTM has input layer and hidden layers that are shared across different languages, while the output layer is not shared. Different languages have their own output layers and related weight matrices from hidden layers. The quality of the synthetic speech generated by the multilingual DBLSTM outperforms the quality of the synthetic speech by monolingual DBLSTM, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed method. Objective 3: Perform objective and subjective evaluations of the outputs from deep learning synthesizers We have chosen both objective and subjective metrics to evaluate the quality of synthesized speech. In objective evaluations, speech spectral distortion is found to have strong correlation with the speech quality and can be used to tune the deep learning model structure parameters. In subjective evaluations, preference tests and Mean Opinion Scoring (MOS) tests are used to evaluate the naturalness of the generated speech.

14205814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205814.value: Our major findings include the following: (1) Hierarchical prosodic structure information is essential for synthesizing speech with natural prosody [Ling, Meng, et al. 2015]. (2) Jointly training of multi-streams of acoustic features requires balanced weights to address the different convergent rates of difference streams with deep learning techniques. Experimental results also show that spectral features converge faster than pitch features [Ling, Meng, et al. 2015]. (3) DBLSTM is superior to DNN in capturing temporal information of input features, and generating smooth spectral trajectory [Sun, Meng, et al. 2015]. (4) Dynamic features reduce the mel-cepstrum distortion of the DNN approach, but they do not have obvious effect on the DBLSTM method [Sun, Meng, et al. 2015]. (5) Shared hidden layers of a multilingual DBLSTM can be trained with speech data from both low-resource (or resource-limited) languages and resource-rich languages (i.e. languages with sufficient training data), and the layers can enhance the output speech performance [Yu, Meng, et al. 2016]. Our research outcomes include the following: (1) We developed a new methodology of transforming the voice of a monolingual speaker to speak a new language, by extending the conventional technique of HMM-based text-to-speech synthesis [Wang, Meng, et al. 2015]. (2) We have developed a new, deep learning technique for speech synthesis that can replace the conventional technique based on HMMs and we have investigated the convergence rate of pitch as a key prosodic feature in comparison with other acoustic features [Ling, Meng, et al. 2015]. (3) In order to transform the speech of a source speaker to sound like the speech (i.e. the “voice color”) of another target speaker, we have developed a Deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (D-BLSTM) based Recurrent Neural Networks to achieve such automatic transformation, which we refer to as “voice conversion” [Sun, Meng, et al. 2015]. (4) Should the targeted output involve a low-resource language with limited training data, we have developed a new BLSTM deep learning approach that can leverage the availability of training data in other languages to assist the task [Yu, Meng et al. 2016]. (5) Voice conversion tasks typically requires parallel training data, which is expensive to acquire. We have relaxed this requirement by demonstrating that the use of a speaker-normalized representation known as “phonetic posteriorgrams” (PPG) will be able to achieve voice conversion without parallel data [Sun, Li, Meng, et al. 2016]. (6) We further explored and extended the use of PPGs for voice-conversion from many speakers to the same speaker, and cross-lingual as well (i.e. no parallel training data), by using the DBLSM (Deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) approach [Sung, Wang, Meng et al. 2016].

14205814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205814.value: In the future, we hope to investigate the use of end-to-end (E2E) architectures for effective prosodic control to synthesize expressive speech. Presently, prosodic control in E2E architectures is weak due to the nature of the autoregressive model. Further work needs to be done to synthesize prosody that captures emotion and style.

14205814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205814.value: This project has developed one of the first deep learning approaches for text-to-speech synthesis, to replace the conventional approach based on Hidden Markov Models. Deep learning synthesis can model the complex, non-linear relationships between parameters and can generate improved quality synthetic speech outputs. It can also capture prosodic properties in synthesis. We further attempt to transform, based on a deep learning approach, a source speaker’s speech with his/her speaking styles, into synthetic speech that sounds as if it were spoken by another target speaker. As deep learning typically requires much data, the output may be affected if the target language is lower-resource without much data. We have developed a method that can mitigate this constraint by borrowing data from other languages with sufficient data. We further improved our deep learning based text-to-speech synthesis problem, in terms of relaxing the need for parallel data from two speakers, and even enabling the cross-lingual speech synthesis for many-to-one speakers.

14205914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205914.value: With cloud computing, the capability of a robotic system is no longer limited by the onboard computational power, memory size, and sensor functionality. Robots with various capabilities can share and combine computational resources, sensory information, perception knowledge, and autonomous skills via a cloud platform. Current research efforts are concentrated primarily on exploiting the shared computing power and storage by ubiquitous network connectivity. In this proposed research, we are developing a cloud robotic system capable of accomplishing complex tasks in real-time based on optimized perception and control strategies using robots and sensors with their resources and capabilities combined and optimized under the cloud structure. Therefore, our focus is on optimizing the combined resources and capabilities of the multi-robot system that is united under the cloud structure to make decisions for various types of robots in the system to optimize their performance of cooperation to accomplish complex tasks that cannot be completed by any single element of the system. To achieve optimized perception of the multi-robot system, especially when the robots are different in resources and capabilities, multisensory information fusion and integration (MFI) stand out as the key technology. Different from traditional MFI, the challenges introduced by cloud robotics include difficult synchronization of data among distributed robots connected to the cloud and inefficient resource retrieval. To conquer these difficulties, we will start from building a general platform for the cloud robotic system, followed by proposing optimized protocols for real-time data transmission under cloud structure, then developing perception and control algorithms based on the MFI information and resource optimization. 14205914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205914.value: With cloud computing, the capability of a robotic system is no longer limited by the onboard computational power, memory size, and sensor functionality. Robots with various capabilities can share and combine computational resources, sensory information, perception knowledge, and autonomous skills via a cloud platform. Current research efforts are concentrated primarily on exploiting the shared computing power and storage by ubiquitous network connectivity. In this proposed research, we developed a cloud robotic system capable of accomplishing complex tasks in real-time based on optimized perception and control strategies using robots and sensors with their resources and capabilities combined and optimized under the cloud structure. Therefore, our focus is on optimizing the combined resources and capabilities of the multi-robot system that is united under the cloud structure to make decisions for various types of robots in the system to optimize their performance of cooperation to accomplish complex tasks that cannot be completed by any single element of the system.

14206114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206114.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research on developing deep models for human pose estimation from images. The proposed technologies have many important applications such as action recognition, character animation, content based video and image retrieval, sports coverage and education. As a concrete example, we apply them to recognize the social interactions and construct social networks using images collected from websites and personal photo albums. Human pose estimation is the task of determining, from an image, the positions of human body parts such as head, shoulder, elbow and wrist. It is a fundamental computer vision problem with great challenges: (1) to robustly describe human body appearance that has variation in clothing, lighting, background clutter, articulation, and occlusion, (2) to model the high-order human articulation patterns, (3) to estimate the poses of multiple interacting persons when they overlap in images, where the expected visual cues of occluded body parts are corrupted. With carefully designed multi-layer architectures, our proposed deep models jointly learn feature representation, high-order body articulation patterns, and non-linear relationship among three different information sources -- visual cue, body articulation and appearance mixture. The joint learning of these components creates synergy through close interaction in the training process, and can generate performance far greater than learning individual components separately or sequentially. We further capture the unique visual patterns generated among multiple interacting persons and handle inter-person occlusions. Such visual patterns are used for multi-person pose joint estimation with a new deep model. The rich multi-person pose information is applied for recognizing human interactions and social relationships in the applications of building social networks from image collections. To the best of our knowledge, this project will be the first to use deep models for single- and multi-person pose estimation. We will also contribute a very large-scale dataset, which is 25 times larger than existing pose estimation datasets and has rich annotations including poses, actions, social interactions, and social roles. It will facilitate the training of robust large-scale deep models and is also valuable to many other applications. This project will significantly advance the state-of-the-art on human pose estimation and social interaction recognition. It will also enable many inspiring applications that use the proposed technologies in movie production, sports, dance design, intelligent web, video surveillance, and clinical analysis. 該項目的目標是研究新的深度模型從圖像對人體姿勢。所提出的技術有許多重要應用如動作識別，角色動畫化，基於內容的視頻和圖像檢索，體育報導和教育。作為一個具體的例子中，我們應用它從網絡圖像和個人相冊中識別社交行為和建立社交網絡從網絡。 人體姿態估計是從圖像中確定位置的任務，人體部位，如頭，肩，肘，腕關節。這是一個基本的計算機視覺問題有很大的挑戰： （ 1 ）需要對人體外觀在服裝，光照，背景，運動和遮擋具有魯棒性，（2）需要對複雜的人體關節運動模式進行建模，（3）需要估計多個正在交互並在圖像中重疊人的姿態，其中預期的視覺信息由於遮擋而丟失。 有了精心設計的多層架構，我們提出的深度模型聯合學習特徵表示，高階體關節運動模式，以及非線性的三種不同的信息源（視覺信息，身體關節運動信息以及人體外觀類型）的關係。這些成分的聯合學習產生的協同作用，通過在學習過程中的密切互動，並能產生遠比分別或依次學習各個組分學習更好的學習效果。我們進一步捕獲多個相互作用的人員中產生獨特的視覺模式以處理人與人在圖像中的相互遮擋。使用新的深度模型，這樣的視覺模式可用於多人聯合姿態估計。 豐富的多人姿態信息將被應用於從圖像集建立社交網絡和社會關係。 以我們所知，這個項目將是第一個使用深模型同時對多人進行姿態估計。我們也將建立一個非常大的規模數據集。該數據集比現有的姿態估計數據集大25倍，並具有豐富的標註，包括姿態，動作，社會交往和社會角色。這將有利於訓練大型深度模型並且對許多其他應用也是有價值。 該項目將顯著推進人體姿態估計與社會互動的識別。它還將推進許多鼓舞人心的科技應用，包括電影製作，體育，舞蹈設計，智能網，視頻監控和臨床分析。

14206114.label: Realisation of objectives
14206114.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed and implemented deep learning models that jointly learn visual features, part appearance mixtures and their non-linear relationship for pose estimation. In a classical neural network, there is no message passing between neurons in the same layer. To tackle the challenging pose estimation problem, we proposed a CRF-CNN framework which can simultaneously model structural information (visual features, part appearance, etc.) in both output and hidden feature layers in a probabilistic way. A message passing scheme is proposed, so that in various layers each body joint receives messages from all the others in an efficient way. Such message passing can be implemented with convolution between features maps in the same layer, and it is also integrated with feedforward propagation in neural networks. The overall framework is trained in an end-to-end manner to achieve optimal accuracy. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on several benchmarks. (2) We have developed a deep model that captures the visual interaction patterns of persons for multi-person pose joint estimation and social interaction recognition. A multi-task deep recurrent neural network is designed to model complex correlations multi-person pose estimation. Our idea is to replicate the network and refine the predictions through multiple steps. The coarse prediction from the first network is used as the input of the hidden layer of the second network, which also takes the original data as input in the bottom layer. This process can be repeated through multiple steps. As the number of the steps increases, more complex multi-person relationship could be modeled. (3) Based on proposed multi-person recognition and immediacy results, we have proposed to tackle the task of estimating people's social relations from their images. Such an algorithm can help design a system to understand persons' social networks in a quantitative way. (4) We have created a large-scale data with 10,000 images, in which all the immediacy cues and the human poses are annotated. Data are collected from four major sources: Getty Images website, photos of celebrities, movies and drama series. The annotations of each image include human poses, human interactions, relative distance, leanin direction, human body orientation, and relative orientation. The proposed dataset was more challenging and more suitable than existing datasets for practical use. It contains persons of different ages (from infancy to adulthood), various poses (lying, sitting, standing, etc.), and different viewpoints (frontal view, side view and back view).

14206114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206114.value: As research outcomes, 2 journal paper and 21 conference papers were published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision. 21papers were published in the top computer vision and machine learning conferences (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and NIPS). Pose estimation is a fundamental task in computer vision. In Part C.9.4, we proposed to build a multi-source deep model in order to extract non-linear representation from these different aspects of information sources. With the deep model, the global, high-order human body articulation patterns in these information sources are extracted for pose estimation. The task for estimating body locations and the task for human detection are jointly learned using a unified deep model. In Part C.9.8, we proposed a novel end-to-end framework for human pose estimation that combines deep nerual networks with deformable mixture of parts. We explicitly incorporate domain prior knowledge into the framework, which greatly regularizes the learning process and enables the flexibility of our framework for loopy models or tree-structured models. In Part C.9.6, we proposed a structured feature learning framework to reason the correlations among body joints at the feature level in human pose estimation. The relationships between feature maps of joints are captured with the introduced geometrical transform kernels, which can be easily implemented with a convolution layer. Features and their relationships are jointly learned in an end-to-end learning system. In Part C.9.17, we proposed to incorporate convolutional neural networks with a multi-context attention mechanism into an end-to-end framework for human pose estimation. Accurate pose estimation would also benefit the research of person analysis and re-identification. In Part C.9.15, to close the gap between the person detection and person re-identification, we proposed a joint deep learning framework for person search. We jointly handle both person detection and re-identification in a single convolutional neural network. In Part C.9.19, to analyze different attributes of pedestrians, which is a key component for security-centric computer vision systems, we proposed a new attention based deep neural network, named as HydraPlus-Net (HPnet), that multi-directionally feeds the multi-level attention maps to different feature layers. Such a network is able to capture multiple attentions from low-level to semantic-level and explores the multi-scale selectiveness of attentive features to enrich the final feature representations for a pedestrian image. Our proposed research also benefits the study of other related topics, including object detection (Part C.9.2, C.9.6, C.9.13), crowd analysis (Part C.8.1, C.8.2, C.9.10, C.9.11) , and image classification (Part C.9.14, C.9.5)

14206114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206114.value: In our study, we developed novel algorithms for accurately estimating human poses from 2D images. This project significantly advances the accuracy of human pose estimation and social relation recognition. In terms of methology, we developed novel algorithms that combine traditional graphical models with deep neural networks, which can benefit related research problems that are modeled by graphical models. The algorithms for 2D pose estimation can also be extended to handle 3D human pose estimation in the future. In terms of applications, the proposed research has wide applications in action recognition, human aniamtion, content based video and image retrieval, sports education, etc. It will also enable many prosmising applications based on human estimation in movie production, sports, dance design, intelligent web, video surveillance, and clinical analysis.

14206114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206114.value: The objective of this project is to develop deep learning models for estimating human poses from 2D images, which is the task of recovering the positions of human body joints from the information in 2D images. It is a fundamental computer vision problem with great challenges. In this project, we proposed different deep learning models to robustly model human body appearance which has great variations in clothing, lighting, background clutter, articulation, and occlusion for accurate pose estimation. The high-order articulation relations between human body joints and between multiple persons are modeled by the proposed deep learning models. We contribute a large-scale dataset with rich annotations including poses, actions, social interactions, and social roles. The proposed algorithms achieved and advanced the state-of-the-art performance of human pose estimation.

14206614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206614.value: Recently, there has been a surge of interest in fiber optical parametric amplifiers (FOPA) for applications in low-noise amplification, phase-sensitive amplification, multiwavelength amplification, optical conjugation, optical comb generation, optical regeneration, optical sampling, optical pulse generation, switching and demultiplexing. FOPAs offer many advantages including low noise figure, high gain, wide gain bandwidth, uniform gain profile, flexible gain region, and ultrafast response for optical signal processing. With Raman gain, the parametric amplification can be further enhanced to produce stronger signal, higher wavelength conversion efficiency, and wider wavelength coverage to the S and L communication bands. Most of the Raman-assisted FOPAs reported to date operate in the linear amplification regime. In this proposal, we investigate the mechanism leading to the onset of saturation in a Raman-assisted FOPA and address its influence in both the linear and the saturated operation regimes. By deferring the onset of saturation in a Raman-assisted FOPA, we anticipate superior performance in multi-wavelength amplification for both phase-insensitive and phase-sensitive operations. In the saturation regime, the stronger output signal can enhance the overall signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the system. The operation is beneficial for applications in optical amplitude and phase noise suppression and regeneration. With Raman-assisted processing, depletion of the parametric pump is substantially suppressed through compensation of the pump power by stimulated Raman gain. For a conventional and a Raman-assisted FOPAs offering identical unsaturated gains in the linear regime, the profiles of the parametric pump power and the signal gain will be very different along the fiber. Such a difference results in suppression of cross-gain modulation crosstalk as well as high-order four-wave mixing products in a Raman-assisted FOPA. Consequently, multi-wavelength amplification can be realized with improved system performance. The role of the Raman pump for multi-wavelength amplification of varying number of channels with mixed modulation formats, bit-rates, and power levels will be analyzed under both phase-insensitive and phase-sensitive operations. On the other hand, in the saturation regime, the different parametric pump power profiles will result in much stronger output signal from the Raman-assisted FOPA. The pronounced output gives rise to improved system SNR by eliminating the need for further signal amplification. We will investigate improvement in phase-preserving amplitude generation that relies on clamping of the output power in phase-insensitive operation. Furthermore, Raman-assisted phase-sensitive amplification will be demonstrated in the saturation regime to unveil the advantages in enhancing the output SNR of amplitude and phase-regenerated data signals. 近期光纖參量放大器在低噪聲光放大，相位敏感光放大，多波長光放大，光學共軛，光梳產生，光再生，光採樣，光脈衝產生、開關及解複用等應用領域中吸引了廣泛的研究興趣。光纖參量放大器擁有諸多優點，包括低的噪聲係數，高的增益，大的增益帶寬，均衡的增益譜，靈活的增益區間，以及適用於光學信號處理的快速響 應。通過拉曼增益的輔助，光纖參量放大可以進一步被增強，從而產生更強的輸出信號，更高的波長轉換效率，以及能覆蓋S和L通信波段的更大的增益帶寬。目前，關於拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器的研究多數停留於線性放大區間。在這項提案中，我們將研究在拉曼輔助光纖放大器中增益飽和發生 的機制。我們的研究也將涉及這一機制如何影響在線性區和飽和區工作的拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器。通過推遲增益飽和的發生，我們預計拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器會 在相位不敏感和相位敏感的多波長光放大中有更優異的表現。工作於飽和區時，拉曼輔助光纖放大器產生的更強的輸出信號會帶來系統整體信噪比的提升，有利於光 幅度和相位噪聲的抑制及再生等應用。 通過受激拉曼增益的補償，拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器中參量放大泵浦光的耗盡會被大大抑制。當傳統的和拉曼輔助的兩個光纖參量放大器提供同樣的線性信號增益時， 參量放大泵浦光和信號光沿著光纖的分佈有著很大的區別。這一區別會抑制拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器中交叉相位調製引起的串擾以及高階四波混頻的產生。因此，拉 曼輔助光纖參量放大器在多波長放大中將會有更好的表現。我們將研究在不同的信道數量，混合的調製格式、比特率、以及光功率下，拉曼泵浦光在多波長相位不敏 感和相位敏感光放大中起到的作用。另一方面，區別于傳統光纖參量放大器的参量放大泵 浦光分佈使得拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器在飽和區間工作時有更強的輸出信號。由於後續的信號放大不再必要，系統的信噪比將會提升。我們將研究工作於相位不敏感 狀態下拉曼輔助光纖參量放大器對於輸出信號光強的鉗制，以更好的應用於相位保持的信號幅度再生。我們亦將研究工作于飽和區的拉曼輔助相位敏感光放大器，以揭示其對於強度和相位再生信號的信噪比的增強。

14206614.label: Realisation of objectives
14206614.value: 1. To demonstrate multi-wavelength amplification in a Raman-assisted FOPA and to investigate the performance under one or more of the following conditions: varying number of channels, mixed modulation formats, mixed bit rates, and mixed power levels. Raman amplification has been applied to improve the performance of polarization-insensitive optical parametric processing using a two-pump configuration [J3]. The study is important as the optical signals in fiber communication networks are composed of different polarizations. We apply our scheme for four-wave mixing wavelength conversion. In our demonstration, we have achieved wavelength conversion without power loss (i.e., ~0 dB conversion efficiency) and negligible polarization dependency using a highly nonlinear fiber without pump dithering [C11]. With the Raman pump, the conversion efficiency has been increased by ~29 dB. Also, we continue to study the mitigation of nonlinear distortion in optical phase conjugation (OPC) of an optical OFDM multi-carrier communication system [J4]. The nonlinear distortion originates from four-wave mixing and cross-phase modulation among the multiple carriers, similar to the case of a multi-wavelength communication system. We characterized and compared the linearity in Raman-assisted and conventional OPC systems. The result shows a power deviation reduction of ∼14 dB through Raman amplification. We extended the work to Raman-enhanced OPC in WDM transmission systems. The optimum launched power is increased by 2 dB and the maximum Q factor is increased by 0.4 dB compared to direct transmission [J10]. Furthermore, we have investigated the use of backward Raman amplification in reducing the nonlinear distortion and crosstalk in multichannel optical parametric sampling [J9, C6, C10], wavelength multicast [J7, C7], serial-to-parallel data conversion containing multiple channels at mixed power levels through time lens processing [J5, J9, C8], dynamic range improvement in FOPA [J11], and optical frequency comb for multichannel source generation [J6]. 2. To develop a model to investigate the saturation regime of a Raman-assisted FOPA for improved performance in optical regeneration of fiber communication signals. The regeneration of fiber communication signals relies on both amplitude noise and phase noise reduction. In phase-sensitive amplification, phase regeneration and amplitude regeneration can be achieved. We have successfully developed a model for Raman-assisted FOPA for phase-sensitive amplification [J2]. The result has been verified by experiment. By solving the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) using split-step Fourier method (SSFM), we have obtained the power profiles of the interplaying waves along the fiber. The maximum gain, minimum gain, and the gain extinction ratio (GER) are evaluated for the cases of conventional phase-sensitive amplification and Raman-assisted phase-sensitive amplification. Optical add-drop filter with superior system performance has also been demonstrated using Raman-assisted phase-sensitive fiber amplifier [J8, C12]. Also, we continue the work in suppressing nonlinear distortion in optical phase conjugation using a Raman pump [J4]. A more detailed theoretical model is used to elaborate the mechanism of nonlinear distortion suppression via Raman amplification. The nonlinear distortion suppression is investigated under different subcarrier numbers and optical bandwidth to satisfy network scenarios that vary from current 10GHz Ethernet to superchannels with optical bandwidth beyond 100GHz. Multiwavelength operation in a transmission system has been demonstrated and modelled [J10]. In addition, we analyze Raman-assisted four-wave mixing in a two-pump configuration by numerically solving a set of coupled wave equations, allowing us to predict the conversion efficiency and its enhancement due to Raman amplification [J3]. Raman-assisted time lens based on optical parametric processing has been demonstrated and theoretically modelled [J5]. Finally, by deferring the gain saturation in a Raman-assisted FOPA, dynamic range improvement has been successfully demonstrated and theoretically analyzed. We experimentally show that the 1 dB compression point at the gain peak of a FOPA can be improved by 4.2 dB when it is assisted with a backward Raman pump to deliver an unsaturated gain of about 25 dB. An efficient 5-wave numerical model is derived to describe gain saturation in a Raman-assisted FOPA [J11, C9]. 3. To perform amplitude regeneration in a saturated Raman-assisted FOPA and to investigate the tradeoff between amplitude and phase regeneration using phase-sensitive amplification in the amplifier. Backward Raman amplification has been used to increase the phase-insensitive parametric gain, which in turn improves the phase sensitive operation. As a result of increased phase-insensitive parametric gain from the Raman-amplified parametric pump, the GER of the Raman-enhanced PS-FOPA is increased by 9.2 dB compared to the conventional PS-FOPA. Combined with the direct Raman gain, the maximum phase-sensitive gain is increased by 18.7 dB. This process has been modelled using the coupled wave equations. The dependence of the maximum and minimum phase-sensitive gains, the GER, the net Raman gain, and the optical signal-to-noise enhancement has been evaluated and experimentally measured as a function of the input Raman pump power [J2]. Also, a phase-locked loop has been designed and tested to stabilize the phase-sensitive operation for signal regeneration. Our investigation of phase-sensitive processing has been extended to the implementation of a reconfigurable add-drop filter, which is a key element in a wavelength routed network. Our results show that for data filtering, both PSA and RA-PSA (Raman-assisted phase-sensitive amplifier) schemes have almost the same performance. The OSNR penalty is less than 0.15 dB and 0.3 dB for QPSK and 16-QAM formats, respectively. For wavelength reuse, the RA-PSA scheme performs better than the PSA scheme. OSNR penalty for the QPSK format is 0.37 dB in the RA-PSA scheme, compared to 1.2 dB in the PSA scheme. For the 16-QAM format, the improvement is more significant. The RA-PSA scheme has a 1.1 dB OSNR penalty but the PSA scheme cannot even approach the HD-FEC limit. The improvement of system performance inherits from the enhanced gain extinction ratio in RA-PSA, which reduces the intra-band crosstalk [J8, C12]. The influences of the Raman pump in the linear and saturated characteristics of FOPAs are also investigated. In particular, the spectral asymmetry in saturated Raman-assisted parametric amplification is studied experimentally and numerically using a five-wave model. We identify that the interplay between dispersive waves and high-order four-wave mixing processes breaks the gain symmetry [J11, C9].

14206614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206614.value: Following the research plan stated in our proposal, we have investigated the use of Raman gain in optical parametric amplifier for effective multi-wavelength amplification and optical signal regeneration. The two functionalities are realized in the linear and saturated regions of the amplifier, respectively. In multi-wavelength amplification and signal regeneration, the key challenge is to suppress the undesirable crosstalks among the channels, which arise from both parametric pump depletion and undesirable nonlinear mixing products among the channels and the pump. Through detailed theoretical analysis involving the nonlinear Schrödinger equation that describes wave propagation in fiber along with the coupled wave equations, we have modelled the power evolution of the pump, signal, and idler waves along the fiber [J1, C2]. As a result, we are able to explain and to optimize the role of the Raman gain in controlling the parametric amplification and signal regeneration. Capabilities that have been demonstrated include extension of the dynamic range of linear operation [J11, C9], mitigation of undesirable distortion products in optical phase conjugators [J4, J10, C1] and optical parametric samplers [J9, C6, C10]. Apart from phase-insensitive optical parametric amplification and processing, phase-sensitive operation has attracted much interest in providing a powerful means for many low-noise applications. We have investigated both theoretically and experimentally the use of Raman-assisted phase-sensitive optical parametric amplifier [J2, C3] for high-performance wavelength add-drop filter [J8, C12]. This functionality offers an added advantage for phase-sensitive amplification based transmission links. Finally, we extend our studies to other features and applications of Raman-enhanced optical parametric amplification and processing. The work includes highly efficient polarization-insensitive wavelength conversion [J3, C11], time lens optical processing [J5, C8], optical frequency comb generation [J6], high-performance wavelength multicast [J7, C7]. More details can be found from the previous section on Realisation of Objectives.

14206614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206614.value: While Raman amplifiers have been commonly used in practical fiber transmission systems to provide wide-band distributed gain to optical signals, their use in fiber optical parametric amplifiers is still not well explored. The key issue is that FOPAs are more vulnerable to channel crosstalk compared to commercial erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs), which has been addressed and minimized with the use of Raman gain in this project. However, the Raman gain itself will introduce additional noise due to relative intensity noise of the Raman pump and amplified spontaneous Raman scattering. The noise figure is similar or slightly smaller than that of a commercial EDFA, and is sometimes dominated by noise from the transmitter laser and the optical receiver. However, under certain applications such as low-noise phase-sensitive amplification and processing, the additional noise can limit practical use of the amplifier. Therefore, a more rigorous study of the excess noise introduced by Raman assisted FOPA is important. Another future direction is to perform in-depth study on how the Raman gain can reinforce multi-wavelength optical processing. A GRF proposal entitled “Distortion-Compensated Optical Phase Conjugators for Multi-Wavelength Communication Systems” was submitted by the PI and was granted by RGC in 2016.

14206614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206614.value: The wide deployment of erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) has given rise to fiber transmission of optical signals over thousands of kilometers. However, these fiber amplifiers suffer from limitations such as confined optical bandwidth within the C+L bands, accumulated amplified spontaneous emission noise that also interacts with fiber nonlinearities to generate nonlinear phase noise, and incapability to regenerate optical signals. These issues can potentially be solved by replacing some of the EDFAs by phase-insensitive or phase-sensitive fiber optical parametric amplifiers (FOPAs). Unfortunately, FOPAs also introduce additional challenges in multi-wavelength amplification and in optical regeneration owing to the relatively large channel crosstalk in the amplifiers. In this project, we have theoretically modelled and experimentally demonstrated the use of Raman gain to compensate for the channel crosstalk through modifying the power evolution of the interacting waves along the fiber. Consequently, the system performances have been greatly improved in multi-wavelength amplification and in optical processing for a wide range of applications that are needed in future optical networks.

14206814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206814.value: 為了應付大數據分析中的計算問題，一階優化算法已成為優化領域中一個重要的研究課題。其中，針對矩陣范數正則化問題的一階算法的研究在近年已有很多的成果，而這類算法亦已被應用到不同的計算問題上。 可是，我們對這類算法的收斂速度還沒有很深入的了解。本項目的目標是要提出新的理論方法去分析一階算法的收斂速度，並用這套理論去解釋一階算法在現實計算中的效率。

14206814.label: Realisation of objectives
14206814.value: To achieve Objective 1, we developed an approach based on variational analysis to study Lipschitzian error bounds for structured convex optimization problems. Using this approach, we not only streamlined the proofs of existing error bound results but also gave a condition under which a Lipschitzian error bound holds for nuclear norm-regularized risk minimization problems. This resolves a fundamental open question in the field. Furthermore, we furnished an example showing that the error bound does not hold if the said condition is violated. Such an example is the first of its kind and has been used in subsequent works by other authors to study regularity properties of nonlinear semidefinite programming problems. We also moved beyond the convex setting and established an error bound for the non-convex phase synchronization problem. The problem has many applications in signal processing, and our newly developed error bound allows us to establish, for the first time, the linear convergence of the so-called generalized power method for the problem. To achieve Objective 2, we first focused on a class of inexact gradient methods. We showed that the rate at which the inexactness converges to zero will determine the convergence rate of the method. We applied our results to establish, for the first time, the linear convergence of two highly popular algorithms in machine learning under an error bound assumption - the stochastic variance-reduced gradient method and the incremental aggregated gradient method. Next, we considered a class of inexact second-order methods called sequential quadratic approximation methods and showed that if an error bound condition holds and the subproblems are solved to a certain prescribed accuracy, they will converge superlinearly. Such result significantly improves those in the literature by allowing the underlying optimization problem to have non-unique / degenerate optimal solutions.

14206814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206814.value: The major findings of the project have already been summarized in Section 5.3 above. They have led to the publication of four journal articles - two in Mathematical Programming, one in SIAM Journal on Optimization, one in Optimization Methods and Software - and one article at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML). Both Mathematical Programming and SIAM Journal on Optimization are top-ranked journals in the field of optimization, while ICML is one of the top conferences in the field of machine learning.

14206814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206814.value: Our results in this project open two directions for further study. First, while error bounds for convex optimization problems are relatively well studied, there have not been many error bound results for non-convex optimization problems. To fill this gap, one approach is to focus on structured problems that arise in applications, such as the phase synchronization problem mentioned in Section 5.3. Second, although there is a rather systematic approach to error bound-based convergence analysis of first-order methods, the same cannot be said for second-order methods. It would be interesting to identify a large class of second-order methods for which strong convergence rate results can be developed under the error bound assumption.

14206814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206814.value: Modern machine learning and data analytics applications often call for the solution of large-scale optimization problems. This has motivated the development of lightweight solutions methods to tackle these problems. A key measure of the efficiency of such methods is the convergence rate. In this project, we showed that many different solution methods possess strong convergence rate guarantees when applied to a class of machine learning and data analytics applications. This is achieved by identifying regularity properties of those applications. The outcomes of this research significantly advance our understanding of those machine learning and data analytics applications that are amenable to efficient computation.

14207214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207214.value: 獨立采樣技術：擊敗大檢索之利器

14207214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207214.value: A "reporting" query, in general, retrieves all the elements satisfying a condition. Nowadays, many applications need to deal with "big data", namely, datasets at a scale of tera bytes. On such datasets, a query easily turns into (what we call) a “big query”---one whose result contains a huge number of elements. Even the simple task of enumerating all those elements can prove to be problematic. For example, assuming that a hard disk can write 4k bytes in one millisecond, it takes an hour to write a query result of 4 billion integers. No user wants to wait that long just for the result to come out (we are talking about very simple queries with no joins involved), not to mention that a result of 4 billion elements is rather small on a tera-byte dataset. Indeed, the rapid increase of data scale causes a major shift in the way normal users would explore databases. They can no longer issue queries "as they wish" because now almost every query necessitates painfully long waiting time. The project will build a system for querying big data on a simple philosophy: whenever the result size is excessively large, return just a sample set (unless, of course, the user insists on the opposite). While query sampling is a decades-old concept, in this project we rejuvenate it with a new feature: independence. That is, the sample set returned by each query must be independent from the samples returned by all previous queries. This new feature ensures strong fairness: the elements satisfying a query predicate always have the same chance of being reported, irrespective of the samples for the previous queries. It even allows one to issue the same query multiple times to fetch different sets of samples. Realizing the feature calls for novel techniques that turn independent query sampling into a first-class citizen with indigenous algorithm support in a database system. This project plans to develop a suite of such techniques with attractive performance both in theory and practice. 一般而言，數據庫檢索以報告所有滿足檢索條件的元素爲目的。如今，在許多應用中，我們都需要處理“大數據”，即那些規模在萬億字節這個等級的數據集。在這樣的場合，檢索很容易變成我們稱之為的“大檢索”---即那些其結果蘊含著巨大的元素個數的檢索。對大檢索來說，傳統的以枚舉所有結果元素的做法並不可行。舉例來說，假定硬盤可以在一毫秒內寫入4K字節，它需要一個小時來寫四十億個結果元素，假定每個元素用4個字節表示。很少用戶願意花如此之久的時間來等待結果的輸出。然而，在一個萬億字節的數據集之上，一個四十億元素的結果只是一個相當小的結果，就算是對很簡單的查詢而言。 事實上，數據規模的迅速增加將導致普通用戶使用數據庫的方法上的一些重大的轉變。他們不再能“隨心所欲地”來進行檢索，因為幾乎每個檢索都將需要漫長的等待時間。本研究項目計劃開發一個基于以下理念的系統：對于結果過大的檢索，只返回一個樣本集（除非用戶堅持需要完整的結果）。注意，樣本採樣是一個幾十年的老觀念；但在本項目中，我們將賦予其一個新的特色：獨立性。具體來說，每個檢索返回的樣本必須獨立於先前所有的檢索所返回的​​樣本。這項新特色可確保高程度的公平性：無論過去我們處理過怎樣的檢索，對于下一個檢索來說，每個滿足條件的元素總是以相同的概率被返回。此特色甚至允許用戶多次發出相同的檢索以獲取不同的​​樣本。本項目研究的中心是去設計一套新技術來在數據庫系統實現這樣的獨立檢索採樣。

14207314.label: Project Objectives
14207314.value: To demonstrate experimentally a mid-infrared silicon Raman laser and develop silicon based photonic integrated circuits for efficient generation and extraction of anti-Stokes photons.
