rows: To demonstrate experimentally a mid-infrared silicon Raman laser and develop silicon based photonic integrated circuits for efficient generation and extraction of anti-Stokes photons.

To study mid-infrared silicon coherent anti-stokes Raman scattering (CARS) and other schemes for stimulated anti-Stokes generation and carry out experimental measurements of their thermal characteristics in order to assess whether laser enhanced cooling of a silicon chip is feasible.

14207314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207314.value: In 2010 laser induced cooling of solid state materials reached cryogenic temperatures, below that attainable with multistage thermoelectric coolers. The established approach for optical cooling of solid state materials use pump lasers which are tuned to the absorption resonances in specially selected materials where anti-Stokes fluorescence can occur. In the process of anti-Stokes fluorescence, energy from lattice vibrations (phonons) in the material is added to the energy of electrons excited by the input pump photons, and the output photons (anti-Stokes fluorescence) may thus have more energy (shorter wavelengths) than the input pump photons when the excited electrons relax back to their ground state. Thus the anti-Stokes florescence is accompanied by a reduction in the population of phonons in the material. Heat is removed by the anti-Stokes photons. There will be a net cooling if heating from competing processes (photon absorption, or other heat generation mechanisms in the material) is less than the total power removed by the difference in power between the output anti-Stokes stimulated emission power and absorbed input pump laser power. There are two major problems in this approach for laser induced cooling of solid state materials. First the cooling efficiency is low, being limited to ~2 percent because of the small difference in energy between the anti-Stokes photon and pump photon. Secondly the laser induced cooling occurs only in a few select materials, such as ytterbium doped crystals, which have the necessary anti-Stokes fluorescence levels. In this proposal we shall study the feasibility of a radically different approach, applicable to a wider range of Raman active materials, for laser induced cooling of solid state materials. By making use of Raman resonances in materials, larger differences in energy between the anti-Stokes and pump photons are possible, thus offering the potential for higher cooling efficiency than fluorescence based schemes. We shall investigate experimentally the thermal behavior of photonic structures which are designed to enhance the output of anti-Stokes Raman scattered photons. Silicon based nanophotonic structures will be engineered for enhanced generation and extraction of the stimulated anti-Stokes photons. The proposed investigation will include experimental work in the mid-infrared spectral region to avoid the heating from two photon absorption. Mid-infrared waveguide resonators will be fabricated and experimental measurements of net cooling or heating of the waveguides will be carried out to assess the feasibility of using the Raman interaction for laser induced cooling of silicon. 在本项目中，我们将研究拉曼材料的热学特性， 尝试应用于固态材料的激光制冷。相比于荧光制冷机制， 通过采用拉曼谐振，制冷效率将有可能得到极大地增强。 我们将在实验上研究光子器件的热学特性， 以用于增强反斯托克斯的散射光子。 设计硅基纳米光子结构以用来增强所产生的， 以及所提取出的受激反斯托克斯光子。 研究项目还将包括中红外光谱范围， 以避免双光子吸收所产生的热量。制作中红外波导谐振腔， 并在实验上测量冷却或加热特性， 评估使用拉曼作用进行硅激光制冷的可行性。

14207314.label: Realisation of objectives
14207314.value: The project proposal and original objectives greatly underestimated the difficulty in attaining sufficient optical gain in stimulated Raman scattering at the mid infrared wavelengths and it was not possible to complete the original scientific objectives of obtaining anti-Stokes Raman lasing. We did make our best research efforts in the project and published three journal papers and several conference papers. Our work towards the first objective initially faced the challenge of making low loss waveguides in the mid infrared wavelengths. Extremely low optical losses are required because the Raman gain coefficient scales inversely with the pump wavelength and it would not be possible to make a laser if the linear losses exceeded the available optical gain. We showed that optical scattering losses and optical absorption losses in the oxide cladding could be reduced by making suspended waveguide structures. Our work on subwavelength engineering of the suspended waveguide structures were successful in demonstrating suspended microring resonators with record high Q for the mid infrared [J1, Zhou et al. J. of Applied Physics 2017], but the Q attained were still over two orders of magnitude less than the Q (several million) that was required for the successful demonstration of Raman lasing in the near infrared [C9, Zhang et al IEEE Photonics Conference 2019]. One of the major limitations in the waveguide fabrication at CUHK using the electron beam lithography system is the stitching errors which tended to dominate the scattering losses whenever we tried to make millimeter lengths waveguides. The commercial tunable mid infrared laser we purchased in this project was used in characterizing mid-infrared waveguides which was not limited to the measurement of losses and waveguide grating couplers, but also included the study of plasmonic structures to increase the intensity of light in the plasmonic slot. For example we demonstrated mid-infrared plasmonic slot waveguide coupled to silicon waveguides (C4, Zhu, CLEO 2018). We also successfully designed and tested the novel design of dual-band waveguide grating couplers for coupling the widely separated Raman pump and Stokes wavelength with a single grating coupler [J2, Zhou, Optics Letters, 2018]. Although our cavity Q in the mid-infrared was not sufficiently high for Raman lasing, we nonetheless achieved state of the art performance and were invited to write an invited paper on this work [J3, Zhou et al, IEEE Journal of Selected Topics In Quantum Electronics, 2019]. Because of the difficulties in making ultralow loss long waveguides at the mid-infrared, we switched to a different strategy in 2017 and decided to start the investigation of Raman lasing at shorter wavelengths where there is a more mature process for the etching of long 220nm thick silicon waveguides with negligible optical absorption in the oxide, and where the Raman gain coefficient is larger. In 2017 we designed a silicon photonic integrated circuit tape-out making use of the IMEC foundry service for the fabrication completed the tapeout of a chip with pin diodes beside the silicon waveguides. The diodes were needed to remove the free carriers generated by two photon absorption in the near infrared. The foundry took over a year to fabricate and ship the chips to us, and we did not receive the devices until the final month of the already extended project. Nonetheless we were able to test the devices and using the 2.8mm long multimode ring cavity in the chip, we obtained a loaded cavity Q of about two million, and we were able to successfully demonstrate Raman lasing at a Stokes wavelength of 1440nm with a continuous wave 1340nm wavelength pump laser. The high Q enabled us to achieve a record low threshold for the Raman laser, requiring only 0.6mW threshold pump power. These results were presented at IEEE Photonics conference as a post deadline paper. We reported the record low Raman threshold power attained in the ring cavity in the 2019 IEEE Photonics Conference post deadline paper [C7, Zhang et al, 2019]. We were able to observe the spontaneous anti-Stokes emission from the laser, but there was insufficient gain for anti-Stokes lasing in this resonator. In summary we addressed the first objective by the development of an ultralow threshold silicon Raman laser and we making measurements of the very low level of antistokes output. We also developed a novel dual band grating coupler which could simultaneously couple the pump and anti-Stokes or Stokes outputs. However there was insufficient gain at the anti-stokes output to achieve an anti-stokes silicon laser, ( we note that has not be demonstrated yet by any group in the world). For the second objective, because we were unable to obtain any mid-infrared anti-Stokes gain (see the above mentioned problems of low Raman gain coefficient and high linear losses in the mid infrared waveguides that we fabricated) we focussed our efforts in reducing losses and developing the components for mid-infrared silicon photonics. Our research efforts in reducing losses of silicon waveguides at the mid-infrared led to advances in the subwavelength engineered waveguide platform, including the development of dual wavelength band grating couplers capable of coupling the widely separated pump and stokes wavelength. We also experimentally demonstrated some of the highest Q mid-IR racetrack resonators yet reported, albeit at a still modest value of only 40600 [J3, Zhou et al IEEE J. of Sel. Top in Quant, Electron. 2019] at about 2300nm wavelength because of losses from moisture/surface absorption, and losses from stitching errors in long waveguides. The mid-IR is much more challenging because of the less mature device fabrication using dry etching of devices patterned by electron beam lithography, (rather than the use of deep UV photolithography which can make longer waveguides without stitching errors). Because we were unable to achieve any significant anti-Stokes output we did not proceed with the thermal characterization as no cooling or heating mitigation would be present due to the anti-Stokes output being several orders of magnitude less than the Stokes output. Hence we estimate we only completed about 50% of the second objective.

14207314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207314.value: In this project we developed a new platform for mid-infrared silicon photonics using the subwavelength engineered suspended silicon waveguides [J1, Zhou et al Journal of Applied Physics 2018]. We attained record high cavity Q for the mid-infrared resonators and demonstrated dual band waveguide grating couplers which couples simultaneously couple the Raman pump and the Stokes emission output from a silicon waveguide [ J2, Zhou et al, Optics Letters 2018]. We also demonstrated a record low pump power integrated Raman laser with only 0.6mW pump power required in a 2.8mm long ring silicon waveguide cavity [C7, Zhang et al, IEEE Photonics Conference 2019]. We observed an increase in spontaneous anti-Stokes emission when the silicon Raman laser was pumped above threshold, but the anti-stokes Raman gain was insufficient for anti-Stokes lasing. The same resonator was used for demonstrating cascaded four wave mixing for generating a frequency comb [C8]. We advanced the state of the art in mid-infrared silicon photonics. The invited talks and invited journal paper [J3, Zhou et al IEEE J. of selected topics in Quantum Electronics, 2019] show our impact in the mid-infrared integrated photonics research community. The conference papers in this project (C1-C6) acknowledged the funding support ( except C1 which forgot acknowledgment in abstract but the RGC funding was acknowledged in the presentation). Although we were unable to achieve mid-infrared anti-Stokes silicon laser, the project did successfully train a PhD student, Wen Zhou, in the design and characterization of mid-infrared silicon photonic devices. The advances in silicon photonics in the mid infrared may enable future development of integrated silicon photonic gas sensors based on the high Q mid infrared resonator structures developed in this project. The GRF project also provided research experience to an undergraduate student who was tasked with writing labview instrumentation drivers needed for the project. The undergraduate student worked with another undergraduate student (who was hired under another GRF project because the instrumentation software was needed by both projects). They were able to complete the task assigned and demonstrate the labview drivers for interfacing the optical power meters with the tunable lasers and optical delay lines. However because of time commitments to their final year courses, the students did not continue with other tasks in the second semester and there is a small balance remaining in the earmarked budget for undergraduate research (unfortunately the rules did not allow this funding to be used to hire another student).

14207314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207314.value: Although we did not succeed in completing the project objectives because of the practical difficulties encountered in making ultralow loss waveguide resonators at the mid-infrared, we still think that the original objectives may be theoretically attainable provides there is a sufficiently robust process for making low loss mid infrared silicon waveguides. The possibility of solid state laser cooling by the process of anti-Stokes stimulated emission in an anti-Stokes integrated silicon Raman laser remains an open area for further research and development. The success of the IMEC chip delivered at the end of the project points to a possible way forward to continue further investigations towards this project. We plan to use wide multimode waveguide designs which are less sensitive to stitching errors and which can potentially reduce scattering loss and enable the ultrahigh Q cavities need for Raman lasing in the mid- infrared wavelengths. Although we underestimated the timescale needed for the project to develop the new mid-infrared silicon photonics platform, we are still optimistic that the ultimate goal of solid state cooling using Raman cooling in silicon waveguides may be attainable and we plan to continue work in this direction.

14207314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207314.value: The project developed new silicon photonic integrated structures, including dual band waveguide grating couplers and mid infrared suspended silicon waveguide resonators, which may find further applications in environmental monitoring, The project also demonstrated a silicon Raman laser which had the lowest pump threshold power yet reported for a ring cavity. With only 0.6mW pump power we observed Raman lasing in a 2.8mm long silicon waveguide ring cavity. These results may lead to further advances in integrated silicon Raman lasers towards the ultimate goal, yet to be achieved, of attaining solid state laser cooling by having efficient anti-stokes Raman lasing on a silicon photonic circuit.

14207414.label: Project Objectives
14207414.value: Compact representation of BSP solid in graphics memory: A solid model in BSP-based hierarchical representation consumes much more memory than B-rep of the same model. In order to process models with large size, a compact representation of BSP solid will be investigated by reorganizing the geometric and hierarchical information. Moreover, to remove the redundancy caused by the operations of construction or manipulation, a highly-parallel algorithm will also be investigated to collapse the redundant sub-trees. GPU-based hierarchy construction for converting B-rep models into BSP solids: Because all models to be manipulated in the proposed solid modeler must be converted into BSP-based hierarchical representation, an efficient algorithm to do this conversion will be investigated. The major difficulty to overcome includes how to handle the dynamic memory and how to balance variant workloads on different cores of GPU. Streaming technique on merging BSP trees for robust Boolean operations: Robust Boolean operations can be realized by merging trees of BSP solids. The membership classification of regions defined by tree-nodes will be evaluated by linear programming (LP), where spatial coherence will be used to speed up the computation. Advanced streaming technique will be investigated for distributing fine-grained tasks in a uniform manner onto all the GPU cores. Boundary evaluation for BSP solids: Applications in CAD often need to display the surface of a model being processed. A highly-parallel algorithm will be developed to sample the boundary of a BSP solid into surfels for the purpose of rendering. To serve the demand of B-rep in downstream applications (e.g., tool-path planning), a parallel algorithm for converting BSP solids into two-manifold mesh surfaces will be developed.

14207414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207414.value: The purpose of this research is to provide an accurate solid modeler for freeform polyhedral objects on a many-core GPU, which will significantly improve the efficiency of geometric modeling in a variety of design and manufacturing applications (e.g., NC machining simulation, moldability analysis, additive manufacturing, etc.). Recent development in these areas trends to process objects with more and more complex shapes, which are hard to be handled by the existing commercial solid modelers (e.g., ACIS and Parasolid). As solid modeling operations can be performed repeatedly for many times in a CAD/CAM process, existing solid modelers are being more and more challenged in their efficiency and robustness of computation. The majority of existing solid modelers use the boundary representation (B-rep) to present 3D objects. Solid modeling operations for objects in B-rep are based on intersection calculation, membership classification and direct manipulation of B-rep. Although the resultant shape of operations can be accurately represented, the operations are lack of efficiency and prone to robustness problems caused by finite-precision arithmetic. Volumetric representation is robust in modeling complex objects. However, it is more expensive in the cost of memory-usage and computational time. To solve the problem of both efficiency and robustness, prior research tries to use the uniformly sampled volume data to represent and model complex objects on the high-performance streaming architecture of graphics processing units (GPUs). However, as the computation and the shape representation are both taken in the image space, resultant objects are not conformal to the exact boundary of input models – i.e., spatial aliasing exists, which affects the correctness and the accuracy of downstream geometric operations. To meet these challenges, in the proposed project we will investigate efficient and robust techniques for accurately modeling freeform polyhedral objects by employing the hierarchical representation of binary space partition (BSP) and the computing ability of many-core GPUs on graphics hardware. The BSP representation of a polyhedral solid is conformal to its boundary surface, and the plane-based representation of BSP hierarchy can provide a lightweight solution for the robustness issues. As a result, the solid modeling operations can be performed accurately and robustly on GPUs. The research will provide a solution for hierarchical GPU-based solid modeling. Problems to be studied include compact representation of BSP hierarchy, hierarchy construction from B-rep, hierarchy manipulation and B-rep reconstruction. Moreover, methods for using the hierarchical GPU-based solid modeling in the applications of design and manufacturing will also be investigated. 本研究的目的是設計一個針對自由多面體的精確建模工具。這個工具是基于多核GPU進行運算的，這樣可以顯著提高幾何建模效率，尤其是應用在各種設計和制造方面（如數控加工仿真，注塑成型分析，增材制造等）。這些領域需要造型的形狀越來越複雜，對于那些特別複雜的模型，市面上的實體建模工具（例如，ACIS與Parasolid）很難進行處理。此外，實體建模的基本操作（例如布爾操作）在實際操作中被大量應用，而這些基本操作在市場上的建模工具中都是相當耗時的。因此，不管從效率還是運算的魯棒性上，現有的建模工具都已經無法滿足我們的要求了。 大多數現有的實體建模工具都是利用邊界表示法（B-rep）在計算機中表達3D模型的。基于B-rep的運算操作都是基于交點計算、分類算法和直接操作。雖然得到的形狀可以精確地被計算機表達，但是這些操作極其缺乏效率，而且因爲使用近似運算的原因，非常容易造成魯棒性上的問題。另外，與B-rep不同的體表示法雖然在複雜實體建模上非常魯棒，但是它在運算中會消耗更多的內存和計算時間。爲了解決效率和魯棒性的問題，以前的研究運用均勻采樣的體信息來對複雜的模型建模。這些建模方法也能運用高性能的圖形處理單元（GPU）進行加速。然而，由于模型表達與計算都是在圖像空間中進行的，所得到的模型與輸入模型的確切邊界是不共形的，也就是說，會有空間誤差的出現，這樣會影響模型表達的正確性進而影響下遊應用的准確性。 爲了解決現有建模軟件的問題，本項目將研究高效並且魯棒的自由多面實體造型技術。該技術基于層次架構的二分空間分割（BSP）表達模型，並且運用多核圖形處理單元進行並行高速計算。與之前在圖象空間表達的研究不同，我們研究的技術不會有空間誤差效應出現。我們項目將會對基于層次架構的GPU建模技術進行全面深入的研究，包括層次架構的構造，架構的操作和B-rep的重建。此外，我們還會對該技術在設計和制造的一些應用進行深入研究。

14207414.label: Realisation of objectives
14207414.value: 1) Compact representation of BSP solid in graphics memory: To achieve this objective, we have developed a compact BSP representation in this project. By this new representation, the BSP hierarchy is converted into two one-dimensional arrays. One array – called stream of clipping planes (SCP) is used to store all the oriented clipping planes. As a result, the plane of a facet split into multiple fragments has only one entry stored in SCP. Another array – called stream of BSP nodes (SBN) is used to store the hierarchy of a BSP solid, where the solid/empty leaf nodes appear only once and the parent-to-children pointers on the tree are converted into indices. Moreover, in order to further collapse the topology of a binary tree, a tree-collapse algorithm via the depth-first search (DFS) has been developed to remove the redundancy. 2) GPU-based hierarchy construction for converting B-rep models into BSP solids: We have implemented the method with five steps for constructing the BSP hierarchy of a freeform solid model H. The balance of workload is very important to this implementation. A dynamic workload balance algorithm has been developed to improve the efficiency of computation. 3) Streaming technique on merging BSP trees for robust Boolean operations: In this objective of our project, Boolean operations between two models are realized by merging trees of BSP solids. The membership classification of regions defined by tree-nodes is evaluated by linear programming (LP), where spatial coherence will be used to speed up the computation. We have successfully implemented this function on GPU based on advanced streaming technique. 4) B-rep evaluation for BSP solids: There are two sub-tasks of this research objective. For rendering surfaces of models under processing, a highly-parallel algorithm has been developed to sample the boundary of a BSP solid into surfels. To serve the demand of B-rep in downstream applications (e.g., tool-path planning), a parallel algorithm for converting BSP solids into two-manifold mesh surfaces is also developed.

14207414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207414.value: This project has investigated techniques in hierarchical GPU-based solid modeling for 3D freeform objects. In our framework, freeform solids are represented and manipulated accurately by using the hierarchical representation of binary space partition (BSP), which is conformal to the boundary of freeform objects. The robustness issues caused by finite precision arithmetic are solved in a lightweight manner on the plane-based representation of BSP hierarchy. The high-performance of MIMD parallelism on GPUs are exploited to conduct the computation. These problems are genuinely interesting and also challenging. The results of our research have been published in top journals and conferences. As by-products, the parallel algorithms developed in this research have also benefited some other related research work - especially the 3D / 4D printing research focus on models with complicated shape and structure.

14207414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207414.value: The current framework only considered the solids with single material. The future research will be conducted to extend this framework to the highly efficient modeling framework for heterogeneous materials and anisotropic materials. At the same time, we will continue the research that already started for using this framework in additive manufacturing (both 3D and 4D printing technology).

14207614.label: Project Objectives
14207614.value: In view of ubiquitous nonlinearity in the AUV dynamics, the first objective of the proposed research is to develop effective methods for AUV nonlinear control based on neural computation. By means of model linearization, objective convexification, and global search, the mission will be accomplished in due course. In the presence of uncertainties in model parameters and external disturbances, our second objective is to develop robust motion control methods based on neural computation. By developing or applying highly efficient real-time modeling and learning algorithms, the model fidelity will be improved. By using or reformulating optimization criteria, the robustness of AUV control systems will be optimized. Its success will raise AUV control performance to a new height. In face of the challenging nonholonomicity in many AUVs, our third objective is to develop intelligent motion control and planning methods based on neural computation for underactuated dynamic systems by means of receding horizon motion planning and model transformation. Its breakthrough will open new doors for widespread AUV applications. In addition to the motion control of individual AUVs, our fourth objective is to develop coordination, synchronization, and formation control methods for a fleet of AUVs based on neural computation while taking the characteristics of ocean environments into account. In pursuit of practical applicability for undersea operations, our fifth objective is to apply the developed methodology for motion control of newly emerged power-efficient underwater gliders with buoyancy-based propulsion mechanisms.

14207614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207614.value: Autonomous underwater vehicles are vitally important tools with widespread applications for ocean exploration, environmental monitoring, underwater rescue, wreckage recovery, etc. The developments of autonomous underwater vehicles have brought enormous economic and scientific benefits for mankind. It emerged as an interdisciplinary area as a synergistic integration of mechanics, electronics, control theory, and other related fields of science and engineering. Despite the rapid recent developments, the research faces many obstacles. Specifically, the control performance is often compromised due to several intrinsic properties of the subjects such as nonlinearity, uncertainty, and nonholonomicity. High-performance motion planning and control methods with the-state-of-the-art integrated technologies are highly demanded for more deployment and applications of various autonomous underwater vehicles. Originating from engineering process control, an advanced model-based optimal control technique, called model predictive control, has been explored in recent years for applications in areas such as robotics, aerospace and automotive engineering. Because of its desirable characteristics, model predictive control is widely considered as an attractive motion control technique in both academia and industries. However, several challenging issues on steering autonomous underwater vehicles remain unaddressed, such as the model fidelity, real-time optimization efficiency, disturbance attenuation, and robustness against model mismatch and parameter perturbation. In parallel to the research of autonomous underwater vehicles and model predictive control in the past few decades, neural network research has made significant progress, aiming at building brain-like models for modeling complex systems and computing optimal solutions. It is envisioned that the advances in neural network research will play a more important role in the motion control of autonomous underwater vehicles. In this proposed research, we will develop high-performance motion control methodologies for various autonomous underwater vehicles. Our primary objective is targeted to model nonlinearity, uncertainty, and nonholonomicity. The research will consist of two coherent parts. In the first part, we will develop robust model predictive control and other approaches based on neural computation for steering autonomous underwater vehicles. Various specific features and issues of autonomous underwater vehicles such as nonlinear dynamics, persistent uncertainties, and underactuation will be thoroughly analyzed. The second part will focus on the applications of the intelligent control methodology to specific motion control tasks. In particular, we will make in-depth investigation on the control of underwater gliders which are more practically useful for many oceanographic missions. It is expected that the outcomes of the proposed project will significantly advance the frontiers of motion control of autonomous underwater vehicles in both theories and applications. 水下自主航行器 作为一种重要的工具，在海洋勘探，环境监测，水下救援，残骸回收等方面有着广泛的应用。水下自主航行器的研究涉及众多学科领域：如机械，电子，控制理论 以及其他科学与工程学科，它的发展 给人类带来了巨大的经济效益和科学研究价值。然而目前，水下自主航行器的研究仍然面临着很多阻碍。由于其本身的非线性，不确定性和非完整性，控制的性能往往受到了较大的影响。所以对于水下自主航行器来说，迫切需要高性能的运动规划和最先进的控制方法。 模型预测控制是一种近年来发展起来的重要方法，它来自于过程控制，是一种基于模型的优化控制方法。目前这种方法在机器人、航天，自动化等领域都得到了广泛运用，是一种在学术界和工业界都充满前景的控制技术。 然而对于水下自主航行器，还有一些具有挑战性的难题没有得到解决，如模型的保真度，实时优化的效率，干扰的抑制能力，对模型失配和参数摄动的鲁棒性。 在水下自主航行器和模型预测控制发展的同时，神经网络的研究在过去几十年也得到了长足的发展。神经网络是以人脑为模型的智能计算方法，有能力为复杂系统做优化和计算。我们可以想象，神经网络的先进性和智能性势必将为水下航行器的运动控制起到日益重要的作用。在即将进行的研究中，我们计划开发出针对多种水下自主航行器的高性能运动控制方法。我们的主要目标是有针对性地模拟非线性，不确定性和非完整性。这项研究主要分为两个相关的部分。第一部分，我们将开发基于神经计算的鲁棒模型预测控制方法和其在水下自主航行器上的应用，深入分析水下自主航行器的具体特性和问题，如非线性动力学，持续的不确定性和欠驱动问题。第二部分将集中讨论智能控制方法在执行具体运动控制目标上的应用效果。我们将特别及深入地调研水下滑翔机的控制，使其应用到更多的海洋任务中。预期的成果将在理论和应用两方面显著推进水下自主航行器的运动控制效果，达到国际前沿水平。

14207614.label: Realisation of objectives
14207614.value: The majority of the objectives have been accomplished. Several advanced control and optimization methods were developed for the motion control of marine vessels in general and autonomous underwater vehicles in particular. To deal with the nonlinearity in AUV dynamics, we developed several effective neurodynamics-based nonlinear model predictive control methods for constrained AUV path following by means of linear parameter-varying system modeling, global optimization, fuzzy approximation, etc. To deal with the uncertainty in AUV modeling and control, we developed several effective neurodynamics-based nonlinear model predictive control methods by refining the controlled output variables within an invariant time tube with three coupled neurodynamic models operating in three different timescales. To deal with the under-actuation in many AUVs, we developed neurodynamics-based real-time path planning methods for trajectory generation based on receding horizons. To deal with multi-vehicle systems, we developed neurodynamics-based distributed optimization, task assignment, and containment maneuvering methods for the coordination, synchronization, and formation control of fleets of marine vehicles. To deal with applicability of intelligent control of various autonomous marine vehicles, we developed motion control and path planning methods based on neurodynamic optimization that are also applicable for motion control of highly underactuated underwater gliders. Because of the shortage of available mathematical and physical models of underwater gliders, the simulation results were not sufficiently performed and demonstrated. As a result, this objective was not completely achieved.

rows: In view of ubiquitous nonlinearity in the AUV dynamics, the first objective of the proposed research is to develop effective methods for AUV nonlinear control based on neural computation. By means of model linearization, objective convexification, and global search, the mission will be accomplished in due course.

In the presence of uncertainties in model parameters and external disturbances, our second objective is to develop robust motion control methods based on neural computation. By developing or applying highly efficient real-time modeling and learning algorithms, the model fidelity will be improved. By using or reformulating optimization criteria, the robustness of AUV control systems will be optimized. Its success will raise AUV control performance to a new height.

In face of the challenging nonholonomicity in many AUVs, our third objective is to develop intelligent motion control and planning methods based on neural computation for underactuated dynamic systems by means of receding horizon motion planning and model transformation. Its breakthrough will open new doors for widespread AUV applications.

In addition to the motion control of individual AUVs, our fourth objective is to develop coordination, synchronization, and formation control methods for a fleet of AUVs based on neural computation while taking the characteristics of ocean environments into account.

In pursuit of practical applicability for undersea operations, our fifth objective is to apply the developed methodology for motion control of newly emerged power-efficient underwater gliders with buoyancy-based propulsion mechanisms.

14207614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207614.value: Numerous results have been obtained in the project in terms of theory, methodology, and applications. In terms of theory and methodology, the results are summarized as follows: 1. Collaborative neurodynamic and multi-agent approaches were developed for constrained distributed optimization (TAC, Yang, Liu, Wang, 2017) and minimax optimization (TNNLS, Le and Wang, 2017; TAC, Yang, Wang, Liu, 2019). 2. Neurodynamic behaviors of recurrent neural networks, such as multistability and synchronization were analyzed theoretically (NN, Liu, Zeng, and Wang 2016; TSMCS, Liu, Zeng, and Wang 2017; TNNLS, Guo, Liu, and Wang, 2019; TSMCS, Guo, Liu, and Wang, 2019). These results can be used as guidelines for designing neural networks for marine vehicle control applications. 3. Collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches to constrained global optimization with nonconvex objective functions (Yan, Fan, and Wang, 2017). By utilizing a team of neurodynamic optimization models initialized by using a particle swarm optimization algorithm, we would be able to solve constrained global optimization problems effectively and efficiently. 4. Furthermore, collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches were also developed for multi-objective optimization. By employing a team of neurodynamic optimization models, both Pareto-optimality and high diversity along Pareto fronts can be achieved (TNNLS, Yang, Liu, Wang, 2018; TNNLS, Leung and Wang, 2018). 5. In addition, neurodynamics-based approaches were developed for intelligent information processing such as sparse signal processing (Liu and Wang, 2016), nonnegative matrix factorization (Fan and Wang, 2017, Che and Wang, 2018), robust regression (TNNLS, Xia and Wang, 2018), and data clustering and image segmentation (Fan and Wang, 2018). In terms of marine vehicle control applications based on the aforementioned theory and methodology, the results are summarized as follows: 1. A neural dynamic surface control approaches were developed (TNNLS, Peng, Wang, and Wang; 2017) and applied for cooperative dynamic positioning of multiple marine offshore vehicles based on modular control synthesis method (TMECH, Peng, Wang, Wang2016). 2. A neurodynamics-based nonlinear and robust model predictive control approach was developed by (TIE, Yan, Le, Wang, 2016). 3. Distributed control approaches were developed for the containment maneuvering of multiple autonomous surface vehicles observer-based output feedback and spatial-temporal decoupling (Peng, Wang and Wang, 2017) and based on neurodynamic and fuzzy approximation (Peng, Wang, and Wang, 2018). 4. Neurodynamics-based intelligent control approaches were developed for the constrained and path-following of autonomous underwater vehicles based on an output feedback of extended state observers(TSMCS, Peng and Wang, 2018), based on command optimization and disturbance estimation (TIE, Peng, Wang, and Wang, 2019), and subject to velocity and input constraints (TIE, Peng, Wang, Han, 2019).

14207614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207614.value: Many avenues are open for further investigations. There are substantial potentials for the further development of neurodynamics-based intelligent control of marine vehicles. For example, our present results on task assignments of multi-vehicle systems are based on linear assignment formulation only. More general task assignments can be formulated based on the quadratic assignment problem and could be solved by means of neurodynamics-based combinatorial optimization. Furthermore, neurodynamics-based distributed model predive control could be developed for distributed control of AUV fleets. In addition, specific AUV dynamics, especially underwater gliders, should be further explore with customized control methods for best performance. In view of the aforementioned potentials, our further investigations will aim at collaborative neurodynamic approaches to general task assignments and distributed control of multi-AUV systems with various specific AUV dynamics.

14207614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207614.value: As a brain-like computationally intelligent paradigm, neurodynamic optimization has been shown to be capable of solving many optimization problems arising in numerous applications such as the motion planning and control of autonomous underwater vehicles. This RGC funded project were successfully completed and resulted in many publications that showcase the state of the art of neurodynamic optimization and neurodynamics-based methodologies for path planning and motion control of marine vehicles under various physical constraints. The research findings include the results on the analysis, modelling and design of neurodynamic optimization systems. The research findings also include several specific intelligent control methods based on neurodynamic optimization for constrained trajectory-generation and path-following motion control of autonomous marine vehicles. In addition, the research findings also include a few related applications for neurodynamics-based intelligent information processing.

14207814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207814.value: Our goal is to develop deep learning frameworks for joint person re-identification and person attribute recognition over distributed camera networks with visual features. Person re-identification is to visually match pedestrian images observed by different camera views, at different locations and time in order to recognize the identities of query images from a large gallery of candidates. It has important applications of tracking persons through non-overlapping camera views and searching for persons of interest from large visual databases. If a query image is unavailable, users expect to search for the target from an image database with lingual description of its attributes. Attribute recognition from images becomes important. Both research topicsare drawing great interests from the academic field and industry because of their wide applications in public security. They are academically challenging because pedestrian images undergo complex photometric and geometric variations due to the variations of poses, viewpoints, lighting conditions and camera settings. As far as we know, this will be the first work of using deep learning for person re-identification and attribute recognition. Deep learning has become a major breakthrough in artificial intelligence and achieved amazing success on solving grand challenges in many fields including computer vision. Considering the nature of our tasks and deep learning principles, novel neural network architectures are proposed. Different from existing approaches that design and learn the modules of feature extraction, photometric/geometric transforms and similarity metrics sequentially, we unify them under one deep architecture for joint optimization. While existing methods train each attribute classifier separately, we propose a multi-task learning deep model which jointly trains all the attribute classifiers and the visual similarity metric between pedestrian images. Since the deep architecture allows sharing low-level and middle-level representations among different yet related learning tasks, the generalization capability can be significantly improved through multi-task learning. We further extend the proposed deep models for domain adaptation. The learned attribute classifiers and similarity metric can adapt to a new scene given a small number of training samples collected from the target scene. A benchmark dataset with 10,000 pedestrians captured by 30 cameras will be built. It is far larger than any existing datasets and has much more complete annotations for comprehensive evaluation. The outcome of this project will not only have substantial impact on person re-identification and attribute recognition, but can also be generalized to other vision problems such as face recognition, general object re-identification and retrieval in big visual data. 本項目的目的在於提出基於深度學習的框架，在分佈式攝像頭網絡中基於視覺特徵對行人的身份再標識，以及對行人的各種屬性進行識別。 行人再標識是將在不同時間和地點由不同攝像頭觀察到的行人圖像進行視覺匹配，從而根據查詢圖像從數據庫中眾多候選圖像中進行身份的識別。它有許多重要的應用，例如跨攝像頭的行人跟踪，以及從大規模數據庫中尋找感興趣的行人等等。在查詢圖像不可獲得的情況下，用戶期望通過對行人屬性的語言描述從數據庫中搜索目標。因此基於圖像的屬性識別變得重要。這兩個研究課題在公眾安全方面有很多重要的應用，因此受到學術界和工業界的廣泛關注。由於姿態、角度、光線條件和攝像頭設置的變化，行人的圖像會經歷複雜的光學和幾何變化，因此這兩個研究課題極具挑戰性。 據我們所知，這將是第一個基於深度學習的行人再標識和屬性識別的研究工作。深度學習是人工智能的重大突破，已經在包括計算機視覺在內的許多領域取得了巨大成功。基於我們任務的性質和深度學習的原理，我們將提出新的神經網絡結構。現有方法對特徵提取、光學和幾何變換、相似度度量等主要模塊進行分別設計和學習。與之不同，我們將他們統一在深度學習的框架下進行聯合優化。現有方法對每個屬性分類器進行分別訓練。與之不同，我們提出了一個多任務深度學習的模型對所有屬性分類器和行人圖像間視覺像似度度量進行聯合訓練。我們將提出的深度模型進一步擴展，用於領域適應。給定從目標場景獲得的少量訓練樣本，學習得到的屬性分類器和相似度度量可以自適應到一個新的場景。我們還將建立一個包括從三十個攝像頭獲取的10,000個行人的基準數據庫。它將在規模上遠遠超過任何現有數據庫，並且具有更加完整的標註，用於全面的實驗評估。 該項目的成果不但會對行人再標識和屬性識別產生重要影響，還可以推廣到其它的計算機視覺問題，例如人臉識別，一般物體的再標識和大規模視覺數據的檢索等等。

14207814.label: Realisation of objectives
14207814.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have proposed a deep neural network for person re-identification. Observing that there are person misalignment caused by drastic viewpoint change and pose variations between person images, which hinders the deep neural networks to learn effective person features. To handle such misalignments, we apply adjacency constrained patch matching to build dense correspondence between person image pairs. In addition, saliency matching is proposed based on patch matching results. Matching patches with inconsistent saliency brings penalty, and images of the same identity are recognized by minimizing the saliency matching cost. The proposed deep neural networks then conduct person re-identification based on the result of saliency matching correspondences. The pooled saliency region pairs are trained to predict whether they are from the same person. (2) Training deep learning models with large-scale supervisions has shown to result in strong feature representations for different task. In order to improve the feature representations for person re-identification. We created a large-scale attribute database 1 that contains rich attribute annotations (over 300 attributes) for ~180k samples and 494 classes based on the ImageNet dataset. The proposed database contains rich annotations including rotation, viewpoint, object part location, part occlusion, part existence, 10 common attributes, and 314 class specific attributes. We show that attributes are useful in discriminating intra-class variation and improving feature learning. Different ways of using attributes are investigated through extensive experiments. We found that it is more effective to learn feature representations by predicting attribute mixture types than predicting attributes directly. The factor guided hierarchical clustering that constructs semantically meaningful attribute mixture types. With this clustering approach, the importance of attributes in representing variation can be ranked. With such rich annotations and proposed training techniques, person feature learning can be significantly boosted to improve the final person re-identification performance. (3) In order to extend the deep learning models to handle person images from multiple datasets, we propose a novel domain guided dropout operation to tackle domain gaps between different domains. We train training samples from multiple datasets jointly by predicting their identity IDs. The domain guided dropout is an effective method of muting nonrelated neurons for each domain. Different from the standard dropout technique, which treats all neurons equally, our method assigns each neuron a specific dropout rate for each domain according to its effectiveness on that domain. After the baseline model is trained jointly with datasets of all the domains, we replace the standard dropout with the deterministic domain guided dropout and resume the training for several epochs. We observe that the proposed dropout scheme consistently improves the performance on all the domains after several epochs, especially on the smaller-scale ones. This step produces better generic feature representations that are effective on all the domains simultaneously. (4) We have also created a large-scale dataset for training deep learning models to estimate immediacy between multiple persons. The large-scale dataset consists of 10,000 images containing multiple persons collected from Getty website, photos of celebrities, movies and drama series. We have annotated multiple person attributes of each collected images. The attribute annotations include (1) Pose: we annotate the pose of each person. (2) Interaction: we defined 7 kinds of frequently appearing interactions and annotated the interaction for each pair of persons. (3) Relative distance: the physical distance separating one person from another. (4) Leaning direction: we annotate the leaning direction of each person as leaning forward to the other person, leaning backward or stand straight. (5) Orientation: whether a person is facing the camera (front view), facing left, facing right or facing back. (6) Relative orientation: relative body orientation of paired persons. Our dataset is more challenging and more suitable for practical use in the following aspects: the age of characters varies from infancy to adulthood; the postures of human are diverse, including lying, sitting and standing; all kinds of viewpoints are included (front view, side view and back view). The proposed dataset provides rich annotations to train a deep learning model for learning discriminative person representations.

14207814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207814.value: As research outcomes, 2 journal papers and 28 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision and machine learning. 28 papers were published on top conferences on computer vision and machine learning (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and NIPS). In this project, we have proposed novel approaches on person re-identification (Part C.8 No.1 and Part C.9 No.5) with deep neural networks. Saliency matching and domain guided dropout were proposed to improve the robustness and performance of person re-identification on images from different cameras. To integrate spatial-temporal information to further improve the re-identification performance, in (Part C.9 No. 24), we design a deep neural network to generate spatial-temporal-path proposals to tackle the vehicle re-identification problem. Such spatial-temporal path proposals encode all possible trajectories of and can therefore incorporate spatial-temporal constraints into solving the re-identification problem. To better tackle person re-identification problems, person pose estimation was studied by our different proposed approaches (Part C.9 No. 3, 4, 18, 20, 22, 28). The human pose estimation problem is tackled by either structured learning neural networks or better contextual encoding models. The final pose estimation performance outperforms state-of-the-art approaches and has been shown to lead to better person re-identification performance when integrated into the framework. We have also studied to use attribute recognition as auxiliary tasks to improve general visual, face, and person features in (Part C.8 No. 2, Part C.9 No. 7, 8, 9, 13, 16). Language data have also been investigated jointly with person image features to further improve the person features (Part C.9 No.17, 23). To crop person images from general scenes, object and pedestrian detection and tracking is an important prior step. We proposed various deep learning based detection and tracking approaches (Part C.9 No. 1, 2, 6, 10-14, 25, 26), which show to have state-of-the-art performance on detection and tracking from images and videos. The joint person detection and search method (Part C.9 No. 15) can jointly integrate and learn person detection and re-identification networks together to improve the robustness of both tasks in an end-to-end manner. In addition, relations between multiple persons and objects were also investigated to learn discriminative visual features in (Part C.9 No. 19, 21). All the methods in the published papers demonstrate our achieved strong foundations and outcomes during the implementation of this project.

14207814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207814.value: In our study, we found that jointly training the deep neural networks with person re-identification and attribute recognition results in improved general visual and person features and can significantly boost the re-identification performance. We will further purse this research direction to investigate how to better integrate multiple and related vision tasks in joint training or end-to-end training manner to improve the visual features. We also found that natural language data can serve as strong supervisions for visual understanding and retrieval. We will continue to work on this direction.

14207814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207814.value: In this project, we propose a joint deep learning framework that integrates both person re-identification and attribute recognition to learn more robust and discriminative visual features for person recognition. The final results show improved person re-identification accuracy on multiple public datasets. To tackle the challenging problem of domain gaps between images collected from different camera networks. A novel approach, domain guided dropout, was proposed to enable the joint learning of visual features from multiple person datasets. After successful training, different neurons will be activated for different datasets to implicitly mitigate the domain gap problem. Large-scale datasets that include more than 290,000 annotated images on person immediacy prediction and general object attributes were created to facilitate the future research on related vision tasks.

14208314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208314.value: Formation control of automated mobile agents, such as unmanned vehicles or robots, is a cross-disciplinary research area that has many applications. For example, in Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC), one of the basic objectives is to design control algorithms for vehicles to automatically maintain a formation. In topographic surveys or reconnaissance missions, a fleet of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV’s) may require automated control algorithms to keep a desired formation during operation. A team of robots may need to reach a specific formation in a complicated environment in order to accomplish a rescue mission. All these applications are related to formation control. Formation control has the dual goal of defining relative positions of automated agents to form patterns and planning the trajectory for formation according to given objectives. Traditionally, the desired formation pattern is uniquely defined and known to all individual agents. However, in many applications, one encounters scenarios in which the formation pattern depends on exogenous factors. Moreover, initially only individual agents may know about these factors. As an example, consider a platoon of cars on a multi-lane highway. In between exits, the platoon may target for a formation in which the spacing between cars is tightly packed. Near an exit, some cars may choose to leave the platoon and exit the highway, in order to change lane, the spacing between certain cars may needed to be adjusted to ensure smooth lane transition. For human drivers, these intentions are usually conveyed via turn signal lights. However, experienced drivers also learn to detect these choices by observing neighboring car trajectories. For formation control, these two methods can be used to provide critical input information to automatic control algorithms. In this project, we focus on a more complicated type of formation control that allows the formation target be dependent on the choices of individual agents. This type of models is closer to real-life applications but also leads to high modeling complexity. Novel techniques on cooperative distributed control will be applied in order to derive solutions. Knowledge and techniques developed in the proposed project can be utilized in many important applications, including automatic control of car platoons, piloting of unmanned vehicles, and coordinating teams of robots. 自主移動智能體（如無人汽車和自主機器人）的編隊控制問題是一個具有廣泛應用場景的跨學科研究領域 。例如，協同自適應巡航控制（CACC）問題的一個基本目標就是，為無人汽車設計控制算法來自動保持車隊的隊形；在地形測量或偵查任務中，無人駕駛飛機（UAV）需要運用自動控制算法來保持一個期望的操作隊形； 為了完成搜救任務，機器人隊伍需要在複雜的環境下達到一個特定的隊形。這些應用場景都與編隊控制息息相關。 編隊控制有雙重目標：確定自主智能體在編隊中的相對位置來組成隊形，和根據給定目標為編隊規劃路徑。傳統意義上，編隊的期望隊形是唯一確定的，也是為每一個智能體所知的。但是，許多應用中會經常遇到編隊的期望隊形需要依賴外界因素的情況，而且，這些因素往往只被單個智能體所掌握。例如，多車道高速公路上的一排車輛，在兩個出口之間行駛的時候，車輛之間的間隔會比較緊湊。在接近出口的時候，有些汽車可能選擇離開車隊以駛離高速公里。為了轉換車道，一些車輛之間的間隔就需要作出調整來保證車道轉換的平穩性。人類駕駛員一般會通過轉彎信號燈來傳達轉線的意圖。但是有經驗的司機也會通過觀察附近車輛的運動軌跡從而察覺到這些意圖。 對於編隊控制問題來說，這兩種方法都可以為自動控制算法提供關鍵的信息輸入。 在本項目中，我們關注一種更複雜的編隊控制問題，其中，編隊的目標取決於單個智能體的選擇。這種模型更貼近現實生活，但也導致了高度的建模複雜性。為了解決問題，我們將會應用新的分布式合作控制技術。 本項目中所獲取的知識和研發的新技術可以應用於眾多領域，包括車隊的自動控制，無人車輛的自動駕駛和機器人隊伍的協同等。

14208314.label: Realisation of objectives
14208314.value: The project consists of three research tasks with the goal of finding new methods for formation control design. Hence, the tasks are closely related. The first task focuses mostly on feedback law design for formation control, the second task emphasizes on trajectory optimization and collision avoidance issues and the third task provides numerical and simulation study for the problems investigated in the previous tasks. The proposed tasks were all completed, resulting in two journal publications and four conference papers. A technical report was prepared and has subsequently been submitted for publication. The first application scenario involves systems in which agents are allowed to communicate their state information with each other. Distributed feedback control laws are designed for three types of linear agent models, namely, identical models (CCC 2016), non-identical models (IEEE CDC 2016, International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control 2017) and heterogeneous models (IEEE CDC2015). Our general conclusion is that if agents in the same cluster are connected and being cohesive enough, the agents can achieve different sub-formations via properly designed cluster synchronization algorithms. For identical linear models, we propose new distributed static control laws in which each agent uses relative state information with respect to its neighboring agents; for non-identical models, we propose dynamic control laws which can synchronise systems described by the same models; for heterogeneous models, we design observer-type distributed control laws based on output regulation theory. We have also investigated two types of coupling schemes among agents - one scheme assumes cooperative couplings among all agents and the other allows competitive inter-cluster couplings. For each scheme, both algebraic conditions and graph topological conditions on the coupling network have been established. It is found that the real part of some eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian matrix should be larger than the unstable dynamics of the agent models. In terms of graph topologies, we show that agents in the same cluster should be contained in a directed spanning tree. (Task 1) We have also carried out numerical studies for a variety of realistic agent models, including harmonic oscillators with identical/non-identical frequencies, Nomoto ship steering models, and third-order integrators with distinct parameters. These models illustrate the effectiveness of the designed controllers and the rationality of the proposed coupling structures. (Task 3) For a class of linear dynamic systems jointly controlled by multiple agents, we find that the set of target states (formation), determined by all agents’ individual choices, can be realized without explicit information exchange among agents if and only if the targets satisfy a compatibility condition. To reach compatible targets, optimal linear controllers are designed by minimizing the average control cost of all agents. For incompatible targets, nonlinear controllers are designed by minimizing a composite cost function that incorporates both averaged control cost of all agents and the averaged target-reaching errors of all possible targets. The nonlinear controller consists of two phases where agents use control actions to indicate their choices in the first phase, while in the second phase they cooperatively steer the system state to reach the selected target. The average cost of such nonlinear control laws is proven to be strictly larger than the average cost of strategies where agents’ choices are fully disclosed to each other via explicit inter-agent communications before taking control actions. A preprint of this work was mentioned in the proposal. After the project started, subsequent work was carried out to refine and modify the paper. The final version of the paper was published in the journal SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 2015. (Task 1 and Task 2) In the process of reaching a formation or formation switching, inter-agent collision avoidance is ensured by a high-level trajectory planning and optimization algorithm. Each agent predicts potential collisions in a finite time horizon with all its neighbors, and then chooses the least detour velocity to avoid collision. Low-level trajectory tracking control algorithm is designed for a fleet of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) so as to track the generated waypoints by the high-level trajectory planning algorithm. These algorithms are implemented in field experiments for outdoor formation flight of four UAVs, each equipped with a GPS receiver to obtain its own real-time position information. The control algorithms and experiment results are reported in the Chinese Control Conference 2016. (Task 2 & Task 3) We have also considered a formation control problem motivated by bilinear controllers. We have studied a string of interconnected second-order systems that can describe kinematics of mobile agents. The proposed feedback control policy of each agent uses absolute velocity information and relative position information between neighboring agents. An oscillation matrix in mechanical systems is formulated to characterize the closed-loop dynamics of the formation. By controlling the entries of the oscillation matrix, the team can reach the target formation, which can be identified with the eigenvector of the oscillation matrix associated with its zero eigenvalue, provided that the target formation satisfies some feasibility constraints. For agents with dynamics described by double integrators, we show that the two agents located at the endpoints of the string structure should know their own position. On the other hand, for models where the agent’s acceleration depends on its position, the control laws do not use absolute real-time position as input. In addition, collision avoidance among agents can be achieved by letting the velocity feedback gain be large enough. A simulation example shows the effectiveness of this observation. The above results are summarized in a technical report, which has been submitted for publication. (Task 1 & Task 3)

14208314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208314.value: "Distributed Control of Linear Systems Allowing Choices", (SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, 53(2), pp. 670–689, 2015), studies a set of choice-based systems that are governed by linear dynamics. We show how choice-based targets can be realized by nonlinear controllers without explicit communication and how control actions can serve as signaling tools. The generated trajectories minimize a composite cost function that incorporates both control costs and target-reaching errors. "Output cluster synchronization of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems,” (IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 2015), considers the cluster synchronization problem for coupled agents with heterogeneous linear dynamic models. Distributed controllers are designed using output regulation theory. A necessary and sufficient algebraic condition that relates parameters from the interaction graph and the internal models is derived. "Cluster synchronization of coupled linear systems under directed nonnegative graphs,” (Chinese Control Conference, 2016), studies cluster synchronization of identical multi-agent systems connected via directed nonnegative links. A distributed control law is designed for each agent, and cluster synchronization is shown to be achievable if the graph topology admits directed cluster spanning trees with respect to the clustering structure. "Cluster synchronization of coupled systems with non-identical linear dynamics", (International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control, 27(9), pp. 1462-1479, 2017), investigates how to reach cluster synchronization for non-identical agents whose inter-cluster connections contain both negative and positive links. A distributed dynamic coupling strategy is proposed for each agent, and lower bounds on the global and local weighting factors are derived under the condition that the interaction subgraph associated with each cluster admits a directed spanning tree. Simulations for two applications, cluster heading alignment of non-identical ships and cluster phase synchronization of non-identical harmonic oscillators, illustrate essential parts of the derived theoretical results. "Autonomous formation flight of UAVs: Control algorithms and field experiments", (2016 Chinese Control Conference), presents results in autonomous formation flight simulations and outdoor experiments for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Efficient optimal collision-avoidance trajectory planning algorithm and low-level control schemes are designed. Formation control for a string of interconnected second-order systems via target feedback, manuscript submitted 2018. In this manuscript, we studied formation control of second-order linear systems connected in a string. Nonlinear feedback control laws are proposed for the agents, and target formations that are eigenvectors of an oscillation matrix is shown to be achievable for two classes of system models. Simulation examples illustrate the control designs and show how to avoid inter-agent collisions by adjusting a control gain.

14208314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208314.value: The work on formation control of interconnected systems has a relatively restrictive configuration topology, that is, we assume the configuration is prescribed by a Laplacian matrix that assumes an oscillation matrix structure. It is interesting to extend the approach there to more general graph topology; for example, systems with Laplacian matrices that have a banded structure. More detailed analysis for the conditions to guarantee collision-free trajectories can also be investigated. For the generalised cluster synchronization approach, an interesting and challenging extension is to consider systems with dynamically changing link weights. Moreover, current algorithms still require some type of global information to guarantee convergence. How to remove such global information in order to develop fully distributed algorithms could be a key research issue.

14208314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208314.value: In this project, we investigated the problem of formation control of automated mobile agents. Examples of such mobile agents include unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles as well as all types of mobile robotic systems. These systems occur commonly in many industrial and commercial applications. Specific research tasks we studied include: 1) trajectory planning and control design for reaching a given formation for a group of coupled agents; 2) control design for systems that allow agents reaching final target states that depend on their individual choices; 3) development of distributed formation control algorithms by means of methodologies developed for achieving generalised cluster synchronization; and 4) new design method for formation control with trajectories that are collision-free. The newly discovered algorithms may be used in applications such as search and rescue missions, intelligent transportation, and multi-robot system control.

14209214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209214.value: Multiple patterning is a technology of separating a complex layout into more than one mask in order to print the layout successfully. As the process technology of semiconductor scales down to the nanometer era, the gap between the illuminating wavelength and the process node becomes bigger. Double patterning lithography (DPL) has helped to fill the gap for the 22nm technology by effectively doubling the pattern density achievable with an extra mask. To shrink further down the process node to below 22nm, DPL will be pushed to its limit and triple patterning lithography (TPL) is now one strong option being studied to make possible the advancement. According to the ITRS Roadmap [1], industry has already explored triple patterning or even higher order patterning with test-chip patterns. With additional masks to accommodate features, TPL can eliminate the conflicts unresolvable by the DPL technology and reduce the number of stitches used, leading to less overlay error and higher yield. Most previous works on TPL focus on layout decomposition. After a layout is generated, it is decomposed into three masks such that the features on the same mask will not be placed closer than a critical distance from each other. However, a layout designed without considering multiple patterning can be hard to decompose or even contain indecomposable features (native conflicts). While redesigning an indecomposable layout will incur high ECO cost, generating a TPL-friendly layout can benefit the decomposition process. It is observed that most problematic patterns originate from the contact layer and the M1 layer. TPL-aware cell design and TPL-friendly placement and routing must work together to avoid indecomposable patterns in the final layout. In this project, we propose to work on this TPL-aware placement and routing problem which is not well studied yet. Continued semiconductor scaling will bring a rapid increase in the number of multiple patterned levels. The need for efficient DPL/TPL enabled design tools with robust design methodologies is becoming pivotal. The success of this project will definitely contribute to the VLSI CAD community and to the design of high performance microprocessors. 多重掩模是一项将复杂版图分解到多块掩模版上，以成功制作版图的技术。随着半导体加工工艺进入纳米量级的时代，曝光光源的波长越来越难满足工艺节点的需要。双重掩模光刻通过使用两块掩模版成功地使线条密度翻倍，促成了22nm工艺的实现。如果工艺节点进一步前进，达到22nm以下，双重掩模光刻技术将达到极限，而正在为所大家研究的三重掩模光刻技术如今有望成为实现下一个工艺节点的方案。根据ITRS路线图 [1]，工业界已经使用测试芯片探索了三重甚至更多重光刻技术。通过多使用一块掩模版来放置线条，三重掩模光刻能够解决双重掩模光刻技术下不能解决的冲突，并且减少使用的缝合点的数目，从而得到更小的重合误差和更大的产出。 以前的关于三重掩模光刻的研究多数集中于版图的分解问题。当一块版图形成后，它会被分解到三块掩模版上，使得同一块掩模版上的两个线条的距离必须大于关键尺寸。然而，设计时没有考虑多重掩模光刻的版图可能会很难分解，甚至含有一些无法分解的线条（原生冲突）。因为对一块无法分解的版图进行重新设计会产生高昂的工程变更命令代价，所以设计三重掩模光刻友好的版图会对版图的分解带来很大的好处。根据观察，大多数问题线条来源于接触层和M1层。考虑三重掩模光刻的单元设计和三重淹没友好的布局与布线必须一起进行，来防止不可分解的线条在最终版图中出现。在这个项目中，我们提出在考虑三重掩模光刻的布局与布线问题上进行研究，因为目前大家对这个问题的研究还不是很透彻。 半导体尺寸持续的减小将导致所使用的掩模版的数目急剧增加。对高效和鲁棒性强的双重掩模光刻/三重掩模光刻设计工具的需求至关重要。这个项目的成功将一定会对超大规模集成电路的计算机辅助设计领域和高性能微处理器领域做出重大贡献。

14209214.label: Realisation of objectives
14209214.value: In this period of the project, much efforts have been spent on studying and developing methodologies to perform layout decomposition and triple patterning lithography (TPL) aware placement and routing. The results are encouraging as can be seen from the list of related publications in the top conferences and journal of the field. The PI together with the students in her group worked on the problems by transforming them to graph problems, analytical problems or mathematical problems and use different kinds of optimization and problem solving techniques to provide practical and effective solutions to the problems. Softwares were developed to tackle the problems. Triple patterning lithography (TPL) is regarded as a promising technique to handle the manufacturing challenges in the sub-10nm technology. It is necessary to consider TPL in early design stages to make the layout more TPL friendly and reduce the manufacturing cost. In parts of the project, a flow to co-optimize cell layout decomposition and detailed placement was developed. The cell decomposition step will enumerate all decomposition solutions with the minimum number of stitches. Results show that our methodology can outperform the existing works in all aspects including the stitch number, half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL), and running time. Our placer is further extended to consider the displacement of cells as a constraint and as an objective, which can help to preserve the quality of the input placement. Effectiveness of the extensions is verified by the experiments. Besides triple patterning, block copolymer directed self-assembly (DSA) is also a promising technique to print contacts and vias for the sub-10 nm technology. In DSA with multiple patterning, multiple masks are used to print the DSA templates which will then be used to guide the self-assembly of the block copolymer. In parts of this project, we developed approaches to solve the simultaneous template optimization and mask assignment problem for DSA with multiple patterning. Results show that our approache outperform the state-of-the-art work in reducing the manufacturing cost. Besides DSA, 1-D gridded design is also promising in enabling the scaling to sub-10 nm technology. Line-end cuts are needed to fabricate 1-D layouts, where two techniques are available to resolve conflicts: (1) cut redistribution and (2) cut mask assignment. As parts of the project, we study the two techniques and incorporated them to enable the manufacturing of cut patterns in 1-D gridded designs. Both double patterning and triple patterning were considered. An integer linear programming (ILP) approach is first used to solve simultaneously the cut redistribution and mask assignment problem optimally. An efficient graph-theoretic approach is then developed based on a novel integrated graph model and a longest-path-based refinement algorithm. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our graph theoretic approach which is of order of magnitude faster than the ILP-based method while it can obtain very comparable results.

14209214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209214.value: It is found that considering lithography issues during the physical design process is feasible and is very important to improve the yield of manufacturing of VLSI designs [TCAD2016, DATE2015-1]. This helps by not creating more and difficult problems for the lithography process. We need a flow to co-optimize the objective of successful lithography in detailed placement. An effective and fast algorithm to co-optimize template cost and mask assignment for DSA with double patterning and triple patterning is developed [TCAD2018-1, DATE2015-2]. To solve this problem, graph algorithms are applicable to achieve good timing and quality. To co-optimize cut redistribution and mask assignment for 1-D gridded design, graph-theoretic approaches for both 2-masks and 3-masks cases are shown to be effective [TCAD2018-2, ICCAD2016].

14209214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209214.value: To the best of our knowledge, all the existing TPL aware placers assume no conflict between cells in different rows. However, with the scaling of the minimum feature size, it is possible to have coloring conflicts cross standard cell rows. This is possible in advanced nodes. In the near future, we should also consider TPL conflicts across rows. Besides, as identification of all possible native conflicts is still an open problem, it is also interesting to solve this problem as future work.

14209214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209214.value: Placement and routing are important steps in the physical design cycle of Very Large Scaled Integrated (VLSI) circuit design. As technology scales down to 10nm or beyond, many problems need to be resolved in the lithography process, which is an essential step to produce chips on a wafer from a set of masks. In order to overcome the problems in the lithography process, many different techniques have been used. Examples are multiple patterning, Directed Self-Assembly block copolymer and 1D-gridded design. No matter what techniques are used, the placement and routing processes in the physical design cycle need to be aware of and be co-optimized with the right metric of the objective, which is to produce the chips successfully. Therefore, in this project, we study and research on how to incorporate these lithography issues in placement and routing, and in particular, we are targeted at multiple patterning, DSA and 1D-gridded designs.

14209314.value: 圖查詢：關鍵字，模式，子圖

14209314.label: Project Objectives
14209314.value: The primitive objective of this project is to integrate different types of graph query in a framework on top of which graph queries can be combined together to answer complex graph queries. We focus on keywords, patterns, and subgraphs that are widely used in graph query processing, and study graph queries by considering keywords, patterns, and subgraphs as input/output. We investigate new algorithms to reduce processing cost, and investigate new approximate algorithms to reduce the high time complexity. The second objective is to investigate new optimization techniques to process complex graph queries that are specified by combining the different types of graph queries together. We focus on scalability issues using database techniques such as graph traversal, graph storage, and graph indexing.

14209314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209314.value: 在實際應用中，圖已被廣泛地用于維護實體間的複雜關係。現存許多大圖數據，如在線書目網絡(DBLP, PubMed)，在線社交網絡(Facebook, Flickr, LinkedIn, MySpace)，維基佰科甚至整個萬維網。這些大圖的規模正在迅速地增長。例如，以結點表示用戶、邊表示朋友關係的Facebook已包含了超過1,150,000,000個結點，結點平均的度爲190。(http://newsroom.fb.com/Key-Facts) 許多研究使用關鍵字、圖模式和子圖處理大圖上的圖查詢問題。每個研究專注于一種特定類型的圖查詢問題，而並未能很好地研究如何將這些查詢技術結合到一個整體架構中以便將一個圖查詢的結果應用到隨後其他的圖查詢。例如，圖關鍵字查詢返回子圖的集合，其中每個子圖包含了用戶給定的關鍵字。但是如何將這些産生的子圖用于進一步的圖查詢中仍然是個尚未解抉的問題。此外，由于圖數據的規模龐大，當只有部分圖數據存儲在內存中時，許多現存的內存圖算法在執行時會産生大量的隨機I/O訪問，這使得減少I/O開銷成爲具有挑戰性的問題。 在本項目中，我們專注于利用圖查詢來實現圖的探索。我們旨在在多種不同類型的圖查詢操作上建立一個統一的圖查詢處理架構，使這些查詢操作可以鏈接起來處理更加複雜的圖查詢。我們的研究集中在三種廣泛用于圖查詢處理的部分：關鍵字、圖模式和子圖。我們研究9種分別以關鍵字、圖模式、子圖作爲輸入和輸出的圖查詢問題，重新審視現有的算法所面臨的挑戰、爲不能完全駐留內存的圖數據設計減少I/O開銷的新算法，並爲降低NP難解問題的時間複雜度設計新的近似算法。我們關注使用數據庫技術解抉可擴展性問題如圖遍曆、圖存儲和圖索引。 本項目的學術意義是雙重的。除了在學術會議和期刊上發表本項目的研究成果，我們將會在圖查詢處理系統的原型上實現本項目中的方法和技術，以顯示我們方法的優勢。
