14209314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209314.value: We summarize the main results below. First, we study keywords search. (a) We study a generic top-down processing strategy to answer a given keyword query independent from the semantics in the existing works (TKDE). (b) Given a rooted tree, we study top-k matches in a directed graph based on the twig-pattern matching semantics (VLDB’15). (c) We study top-k shortest path join and OMMPR query, where the former is to compute top-k shortest paths between two sets of nodes identified by user-given keywords, and the latter is to find optimal multi-meeting point route to support ride-sharing (TKDE). (d) We study how to cluster multi-valued attributed graphs into densely connected components with homogeneous attribute values, with a focus on subspace clustering (Information Sciences). Second, we study NLP processing over knowledge graphs for answering questions (Q&A). The challenge is how to bridge the gap between unstructured natural language questions and graph-structure data. We propose new approaches to generate templates automatically (SIGMOD’15). Third, we study continuous pattern detection over evolving graphs (VLDB Journal). Fourth, we study query processing over uncertain graphs and random walk based sampling. For uncertain graphs, we study expected query evaluation and threshold query evaluation (TKDE). For random walk based graph sampling, we propose two algorithms, namely, rejection-controlled metropolis-Hastings and generalized maximum-degree random walk, to address the drawbacks of three widely-used random walk based graph sampling algorithms (ICDE’15). Fifth, we study influence maximization in social networks under a structural diversity model (Information Sciences), top-r k-influential communities (VLDB’15), and personalized influential topic search (TKDE). Sixth, we explore hierarchies in online social networks which are modeled as directed graphs, and show that we can find a representative hierarchy for a directed graph (TKDE). Seventh, we study many efficient graph algorithms (e.g., triangle listing, supergraph search, the Steiner component with the maximum connectivity, Group Steiner Tree, and a general solution based on graph ordering) and report our finding in IEEE Bigdata’16, ICDE’16, VLDB’15, and SIGMOD’16. In addition, we study I/O efficient graph algorithms (e.g, DFS, core decomposition, core maintenance) and report our findings in SIGMOD’15 and ICDE’16. Eighth, we have developed systems. We propose and implement a hybrid pulling/pushing mechanism for I/O-efficient distributed and iterative graph computing (SIGMOD’16), and investigate fine-grained parallelism to speedup graph analytics computing (SIGMOD’16).

14209314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209314.value: Graph processing has been studied. There are still many remaining issues such as how to make it easy for users to query and how to further enhance the efficiency. We will continue to work on these issues.

14209314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209314.value: The project is to explore different types of graph queries. We focus on keywords, patterns, and subgraphs that are widely used in graph query processing. We investigate new ways to query and new algorithms to achieve high efficiency, and we develop systems with new mechanisms to process graph queries. For instance, we show that we can find a representative hierarchical structure from an online social network modelled as a directed graph. This makes possible to identify the global core structure hidden in a social network. We also find dense subgraphs by further considering how influential such dense subgraphs are, which is different from the previous works that study one of the two issues, density and influence. In addition, we develop graph processing systems to support graph algorithms in general. As an example, we propose a new approach to significantly reduce CPU cash misses when dealing with graph algorithms in general. Our findings are reported in major international journals and top international conferences. Several packages are provided for people to use.

14209414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14209414.value: 俱有可擴展性的無線雲端蜂窩網：協作信號處理和資源分配

14209414.label: Project Objectives
14209414.value: To develop scalable PHY-layer collaborative signal processing schemes – We will systematically investigate the cooperative signal processing mechanisms that can fully exploit the benefit of large-scale collaboration of BSs/RRHs. We are interested in developing schemes that are not only spectral efficient, but also scalable in the sense that the computational complexity does not grow significantly with the network size. To develop user-centric virtual cell formation mechanisms -- We argue that the traditional concept of cells becomes blurred in C-RAN due to the full cooperation of baseband signal processing. In this project, we advocate an alternative concept called virtual cell, which consists of a number of RRHs associated with one or multiple mobile users. We will investigate efficient mechanisms that form virtual cells dynamically on the fly depending on active user demand, traffic location distribution, and etc.. To construct scalable MAC-layer resource allocation and frequency reuse schemes – The centralized C-RAN architecture allows extremely flexible and aggressive channel allocation and frequency reuse among the large number of RRHs. We will explore such opportunity to develop low-complexity solutions for resource allocation, channel assignment, and frequency reuse in C-RAN. To design power-efficient dynamic service provisioning mechanisms – Wireless traffic load is highly dynamic in time and space. C-RAN offers the flexibility of consolidating workloads across the network during off-peak hours, and turning off idle computational power to save power and energy. We will investigate online dynamic service provisioning mechanisms, which optimize the decision of turning on/off servers without knowing the future workload.

We will explore such opportunity to develop low-complexity solutions for resource allocation, channel assignment, and frequency reuse in C-RAN.

To design power-efficient dynamic service provisioning mechanisms – Wireless traffic load is highly dynamic in time and space. C-RAN offers the flexibility of consolidating workloads across the network during off-peak hours, and turning off idle computational power to save power and energy. We will investigate online dynamic service provisioning mechanisms, which optimize the decision of turning on/off servers without knowing the future workload.

14209414.label: Realisation of objectives
14209414.value: The project objectives have all been fulfilled satisfactorily. In particular, we have comprehensively studied low-complexity and scalable algorithms for the PHY-layer signal processing and MAC layer resource allocation problems in large-scale CRANs. The project objectives have all been fulfilled satisfactorily. As to the first project objective, we have established a unified theoretical framework for dynamic clustering by exploiting the near-sparsity of large C-RAN channel matrices. Based on this framework, we have proposed a dynamic nested clustering algorithm that greatly improves the system scalability in terms of baseband-processing and channel-estimation complexity. To further reduce the complexity, we have formulated the signal detection in C-RAN as an inference problem over a bipartite random geometric graph. Then, we have proposed a randomized Gaussian message passing algorithm that has linear complexity with the size of the CRAN system. As to the second project objective, we have investigated user-centric joint cooperation, where virtual cells are formed by cooperating base stations around the users. We derived the optimal size of the virtual cells. Based on stochastic geometry models of the base station and user locations, we resolve the correlation of the transmit powers introduced by joint precoding, and derive an integral expression of the average user throughput. As to the third project objective, we have proposed a pricing-based resource allocation strategy in virtualized CRANs, where one Mobile Network Operator (MNO) owns the physical resource and multiple Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs) serve their users with resources leased from the MNO. We formulated as a bi-level optimization problem, where the upper level corresponds to revenue maximization of the MNO and the lower level corresponds to the utility-surplus maximization of the MVNOs. To solve the problem efficiently, we propose to solve the MVNO problem with a low-complexity algorithm, which scales well with the network size. Based on the analysis of the revenue of the MNO, we find that different utility function families result in distinct revenue trends with respect to the price, and correspondingly propose efficient algorithms to find the optimal price that maximizes the revenue. Besides, we also proposed a deep reinforcement-learning based base station activation strategy that activates the optimal subset of base stations to significantly lower the energy consumption without compromising the quality of service. As to the fourth project objective, we have studied efficient allocation of computing resources to minimize the hardware and energy costs of CRANs. we have shown that the computing resource consumption increases non-linearly with the user density. In particular, the required computing resource drastically increases when densely populated hotspots are present in the system.

14209414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209414.value: The research outcomes are summarized in 11 journal papers and 12 conference papers, as detailed in Part C. Below is a brief summary of the major findings. Scalable PHY-layer collaborative signal has been studied in journal papers 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.6, 8.7, and conference papers 9.2, 9.4, 9.5, 9.6, 9.10, 9.12. In particular, we established a unified theoretical framework for dynamic clustering by exploiting the near-sparsity of large C-RAN channel matrices. Based on this, we proposed several algorithms to improve the scalability of PHY-layer signal processing in large-scale CRANs, including a dynamic nested clustering algorithm and a randomized message passing algorithm. We further developed a locally orthogonal training sequence allocation scheme, which makes sure the overhead for training is scalable. We studied the optimal planning of user-centric virtual cell in 8.8, 9.1, and 9.3. We derived the performance of user-centric joint transmission in an ultra-dense networks with a number of virtual cells. Based on this, we derived the optimal radius of user-centric virtual cells. We also studied the inter-cell interference cancellation scheme that mitigates the interference between virtual cells. Scalable MAC-layer resource allocation was investigated in 8.10, 9.8, 9.9 and 9.11. We investigated a two-stage spectrum leasing framework, where an MVNO acquires spectrum resources through both advance reservation and on-demand request. The MVNO jointly optimizes the amount of spectrum resources to lease in the two stages by taking into account traffic intensity, random user locations, wireless channel statistics, quality-of-service requirements, and the price differences. The computing resource planning and allocation are investigated 8.5 and 8.9. In particular, how much computing capability is needed at the BBU center, given certain number of base stations and user density. We showed that the computing resource consumption increases non-linearly with the user density. In particular, the required computing resource drastically increases when densely populated hotspots are present in the system.

14209414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209414.value: In future work, we plan to focus on the planning and optimization of CRAN architecture, including the frontal/backhaul connectivity and capacity, the BBU computing server planning, edge service placement, and edge intelligence enabled by CRAN architecture. In particular, CRAN architecture is particularly well suited for edge computing and edge intelligence applications, due to the close proximity of the dense base stations and users. We have conducted preliminary investigation on mobile edge computing, where mobile users or IoT devices can offload the computing tasks to edge servers, which are likely to be located at the BBU pool or aggregation points. Then, computing resource, fronthaul bandwidth resource, and wireless spectrum resource need to be carefully managed. This will be the key focus of our future work.

14209414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209414.value: With centralized processing, cooperative radio, cloud, and clean infrastructure, CRAN is a promising solution to address the unprecedented challenges today’s wireless cellular system is facing. There lacked a fundamental understanding of how the enormous centralized baseband-processing power can be leveraged with affordable computation and communication complexities. In this project, we have systematically investigated the efficiency and scalability of collaborative baseband signal processing, dynamic virtual cell formation, cooperative radio resource management and frequency reuse, and dynamic computing resource sharing and idling. The project addressed the issues by proposing a suite of algorithms based on optimization, stochastic geometry, probabilistic inference, and graph theory. The work has led to 11 journal publications and 12 conference publications at top-tier venues.

14209514.label: Realisation of objectives
14209514.value: The recent emergence of versatile micro/nanorobots provides new strategies of healthcare and disease treatment, especially for targeted delivery of therapeutic agents to otherwise inaccessible regions. However, for successful translation of laboratory microrobotic tools into clinical outcomes, critical challenges still remain, such as controllable cargo loading/release on site, robust spatiotemporal navigation in real time and reliable biocompatibility/biodegradation inside the body. In this GRF project, the PI aims to develop a novel type of helical swimming microrobots using spirulina as a biotemplate, and after the functionalization, the helical microrobots can not only be remotely driven by a low-strength rotating magnetic field, but are capable of performing localized on-demanding drug delivery tasks for biomedical applications. In the first half period of this project, we mainly focused on the development of a green and facile method for batch fabrication of magnetic helical microrobots using helical-shaped spirulina (S. platensis) as the biological template. As a result, We have successfully prepared porous hollow microswimmers possessing an outer shell aggregated by mesoporous spindle-like magnetite nanoparticles and a helical-shaped inner cavity. The fabrication is straightforward and cost-effective due to mass-production process of biotemplated synthesis. The fabricated microswimmers are superparamagnetic and exhibit low cytotoxicity. For the first time in the literature of helical microswimmers, a porous hollow architecture is successfully constructed with an ultrahigh specific surface area for surface functionalization and enabling diffusion-based cargo loading/release. Furthermore, experimental and analytical results indicate better swimming performance of the microswimmers than the existing non-hollow helical micromachines of comparable sizes and dimensions. In the second half of this project period, the PI further focuses on the investigation of the helical swimming microrobots for targeted delivery with controlled loading and release capability by using the biohybrid design. PI's group has discovered that biohybrid helical microrobots are promsing to act as a microrobotic platform that could be further developed for in vivo imaging–guided therapy and reported a proof of concept for the engineering of multifunctional microrobotic devices. The PI's group has also investigated the loading, transport and release of molecular cargos using cell-based magnetic microswimmers engineered from multicellular Spirulina. The loading is attained by harnessing the dehydration and rehydration of Spirulina cells, inside which model macromolecules are encapsulated as a discrete phase, and for small molecules, as a continuous phase. Driven by low-strength magnetic fields, the molecule-laden swimmer manages to perform navigation in an intestinal tract mimicry, imitating the process of guest-molecule transport in the gastrointestinal tract. The loaded molecules can be released from the swimmer through host degradation and/or concentration gradient-driven diffusion, with the speed of release tailored by the magnetite-coating thickness. Furthermore, evaluation tests in a stem-cell system infer that the bioactivity of the guest molecules remains intact after the loading-release procedure. In the end, we have demonstrated a feasible approach for gastrointestinal delivery of molecular agents using cell-based microswimmers. Overall, we have achieved all the six objectives without deviation from the original plan. Some key results have been published in the top journals in the robotics field, including Science Robotics, Nature Communications, IJRR, T-Ro, and also disseminated in the IEEE RAS flagship conferences such as ICRA and IROS. More details are shown in the research output in the following parts of this final report.

The major finding and research outcomes have been published in many top-tier journals, including Science Robotics (AAAS), Nature Communications, Science Advances, International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR), IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-Ro), IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics (T-MECH), IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), Advanced Functional Materials, and so on. Some research results were also presented (or will be presented) in IEEE international conferences, such as IEEE ICRA2019, IEEE/ASEM AIM2019, IEEE/RSJ IROS2018 and IEEE ROBIO2017. In addition, PI and co-workers have filed two US non-provisional patents, in which one is related to biosensing using biohybrid microrobots, and the other one is related to the development of an electromagnetic coils system for precise control of magnetic microrobots. Three key research outcomes are listed below. - We reported biohybrid magnetic robots endowed with multifunctional capabilities by integrating desired structural and functional attributes from a biological matrix and an engineered coating. Helical microswimmers were fabricated from Spirulina microalgae via a facile dip-coating process in magnetite (Fe3O4) suspensions, superparamagnetic, and equipped with robust navigation capability in various biofluids. The innate properties of the microalgae allowed in vivo fluorescence imaging and remote diagnostic sensing without the need for any surface modification. Furthermore, in vivo magnetic resonance imaging tracked a swarm of microswimmers inside rodent stomachs, a deep organ where fluorescence-based imaging ceased to work because of its penetration limitation. Meanwhile, the microswimmers were able to degrade and exhibited selective cytotoxicity to cancer cell lines, subject to the thickness of the Fe3O4 coating, which could be tailored via the dip-coating process. The biohybrid microrobots reported herein represent a microrobotic platform that could be further developed for in vivo imaging–guided therapy and a proof of concept for the engineering of multifunctional microrobotic and nanorobotic devices. The main results were published in the top robotics journal "Science Robotics" in 2017, and it was also highlighted in the Science News (https://www.sciencemag.org/news/2017/11/robot-made-algae-can-swim-through-your-body-thanks-magnets), the RGC YouTube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l2NQfgW8tSQ&t=8s), and many international and local media. The paper is also indexed in ISI Web of Science as a "ISI highly cited paper". - We reported cell-based helical microswimmers fabricated from multicellular Spirulina with engineered magnetite coatings for loading and release of biomacromolecules or small molecules which are encapsulated into the Spirulina cells. We have demonstrated a feasible approach for gastrointestinal delivery of molecular agents using cell-based microswimmers. More details are shown in our paper published in Applied Materials Today. - Within the framework of this project, we have also developed the Methods and Systems for Controlling Electromagnetic Field Generators. The details are shown in our filed US non-provisional patent.

14209514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209514.value: To ultimately realize clinic applications, such as image-guided therapy, using these biohybrid microrobots, several essential aspects remain to be explored in our future work: (i) the loading/release capability of extra diagnostic/therapeutic cargo, (ii) in vivo residence subject to the adverse effect of potential host responses, (iii) the navigation of a swarm to lesion location, and (iv) the in vivo diagnostic/therapeutic effect on lesions, for example, malignant tumors. One specific aspect worth immediate attention is the intriguing Spirulina induced apoptosis to cancer cells, whose specificity is of profound importance for nanomedicine and may open the door to a series of innovative therapies for cancer treatment. To reveal the full mechanism behind this phenomenon and therefore enable medical applications, a great endeavor remains to be made in collaboration with biologists and oncologists.

14209514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209514.value: Recent breakthroughs in medical micro/nanorobots have further established the prominent role of this technology in the future of minimally invasive medicine. Plenty of versatile micro/nanorobotic devices have inspired diverse proofs of concept for clinical applications, relying on different strategies of diagnostic/therapeutic intervention such as biopsy, ablation, hyperthermia, detoxification, remote sensing, cell transport, drug delivery, and so on. Notwithstanding, critical challenges still remain to successfully translate these clinical aspirations of medical micro/nanorobots into realistic therapies on account of their safety issues and operating complexity inside the body. In the present GRF project, we focus on potential applications of targeted delivery using biohybrid helical micro/nanorobots and further exploit their capability for on-demand targeted drug delivery both in vitro and in vivo for clinic applications, such as minimally invasive imaging-guided therapy.

14209814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209814.value: Stochastic control theory has been developed for over 50 years, and is now widely considered to be well established with a very few if any major open problems left. However, recent study on some applied problems has introduced non-standard features that may lead to new types of stochastic control problems. For instance, many experimental evidences suggest that people often exaggerate small probabilities of both very good and very bad events. This exaggeration of small probabilities can be modeled through the so-called probability distortion. Motivated by this, we propose in this project a brand new type of stochastic control problem in which the system dynamics is nonlinear and the objective functional involves probability distortion. The new problem introduced in this project brings in significant, and indeed fundamental, difficulties that render the failure of Pontryagin's maximum principle and Bellman's dynamic programming, the two most powerful approaches in solving classical stochastic control problems. The aim of this project is to develop some general theory to solve this new stochastic control problem. We propose two possible approaches in achieving this goal. One is to carry out calculus of variations via either Kolmogorov's forward partial differential equations or backward stochastic differential equations, and the other is to develop a dual approach and a change of decision variables that will eventually lead to solutions of the original problem. 14300214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300214.value: Mild, catalytic hydrogenation of aliphatic carbon-carbon bonds with water as the hydrogenating agent will be attempted at low temperatures below 200 degree C to provide more energy rich fuels. The catalysis couples the water splitting and carbon-carbon bond cleavages to give hydrogen enriched organic products and energy richer compounds. This can also provide a new method for organic synthesis. Hopefully, wastes and fossil based raw materials can be converted into fuels and industrially important intermediates in economically more attractive manners. 在溫和條件並溫度低於200℃時,以水為氫化劑的催化氫化 脂族碳 - 碳鍵的化學反應，可以提供更豐富的能源燃料。結合催化水分解和碳 - 碳鍵斷裂能給予豐富含氫的有機食品和能源化合物。這也可以提供用於新的有機合成方法。 希望能轉化廢物和化石原料為燃料, 和工業上的重要中間體, 成為在經濟上更具吸引力的化學方法。

14300214.label: Realisation of objectives
14300214.value: The rhodium porphyrin catalysed hydrogenation of 1,2-diarylcyclopropanes with water as the hydrogen source has been achieved in good yields at 200 degree C. The mechanistic pathways of this catalytic process initially goes through a rhodium porphyrin radical 1,2-addition across the more substituted double bond to yield a dirhodium porphyrin propyl intermediate which further undergoes hydrogenation with water in a hydrolytic process or a bimetallic reductive elimination with rhodium porphyrin hydride to produce the alkane products. The rhodium porphyrin hydride is generated from the reaction of rhodium porphyrin dimer with water. The hydrolysis of dirhodium porphyrin propyl intermediate gives rhodium porphyrin hydroxide which is transformed thermally to give rhodium porphyrin dimer. Other three membered rings of epoxides and aziridines react with rhodium porphyrin alkyls or hydride only in stoichiometric manners to give the C-O bond opening products isolated products or C-N opening complex mixtures.

14300214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300214.value: The rhodium porphyrin catalysed hydrogenation of 1,2-diarylcyclopropanes with water as the hydrogen source has been achieved in good yields at 200 degree C. The mechanistic pathways of this catalytic process initially goes through a rhodium porphyrin radical 1,2-addition across the more substituted double bond to yield a dirhodium porphyrin propyl intermediate which further undergoes hydrogenation with water in a hydrolytic process or a bimetallic reductive elimination with rhodium porphyrin hydride to produce the alkane products. The rhodium porphyrin hydride is generated from the reaction of rhodium porphyrin dimer with water. The hydrolysis of dirhodium porphyrin propyl intermediate gives rhodium porphyrin hydroxide which is transformed thermally to give rhodium porphyrin dimer. The serendipitous discovery of an attempted rhodium porphyrin catalyzed hydrogenation of a 1,1-dibromocyclopropane gives the thermal rearrangement intermediate-allylic bromide before yielding the final ring opening mono-debromovinyl bromide. Thus a novel rhodium porphyrin catalysed dehydrobromination of allylic and benzylic bromides with water has been developed.

14300214.value: The rhodium porphyrin catalytic hydrogenation of ring strained compounds such as cyclobutanes and more functionalized cyclopropane with water can be investigated as a greener hydrogenation synthetic method.

14300314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300314.value: This project aims at devising a new construction of integrable systems and applying it to the study of mirror symmetry and geometric quantization for flag varieties. The theory of integrable systems is intimately related to and has applications to a wide range of other subjects such as complex geometry, symplectic topology, representation theory, Schubert calculus, etc. On the other hand, mirror symmetry is a much younger subject which began with its discovery by string-theorists in the late 80's. Nevertheless, it has been exerting a profound influence on the development of subjects like algebraic geometry, symplectic topology, differential geometry, etc for the last 20 years. An important class of integrable systems is given by the Gelfand-Cetlin systems which were constructed by Guillemin and Sternberg using representation theory. These integrable systems, or Lagrangian torus fibrations, on complete flag varieties of type A were recently applied to construct mirrors for such varieties along the lines of the famous SYZ proposal, leading to a nice picture explaining mirror symmetry in this case. Unfortunately, the same construction does not yield the correct mirrors for partial flag varieties such as Grassmannians. The main objective of this project is to construct a new class of integrable systems which can be applied to study mirror symmetry for flag varieties of all type. We plan to apply the SYZ construction to these integrable systems to construct the correct mirrors. This would shed new light even on known cases. For example, for complete flag varieties of type A, our mirrors would contain the old mirrors as open dense subsets and the new mirrors would additionally satisfy certain topological constraints derived from physical principles. By doing so, we would get a much better and more unified understanding of mirror symmetry for flag varieties. We also plan to apply these new integrable systems to study geometric quantization for flag varieties. Our systems would enjoy some pleasant properties which are absent for the Gelfand-Cetlin systems (or other similar systems constructed using Okounkov bodies). Indeed, the lack of these properties in the Gelfand-Cetlin systems have resulted in some issues when they are applied to the study of geometric quantization. We therefore expect that our new construction would lead to new insights in this subject. We also speculate further possible applications to Schubert calculus, toric degenerations, and representation theory as the construction of the desired integrable systems should be closely related to all these subjects. 本項目旨在發展出一套新的可積系統的構建和把它應用到鏡對稱 和幾何量子化的研究。 可積系統理論與複幾何、辛拓撲、表示論、舒伯特演算等科目是 密切相關的，且已被範圍應用到這些學科上。在另一方面，鏡對 稱始於上世紀80年代弦理論學家的驚人發現，它是一個非常年輕 的學科，然而，在過去的20年，鏡對稱已經對代數幾何、辛拓撲 、微分幾何等學科的發展產生深遠的影響。 一類重要的可積系統是由Guillemin和Sternberg用表示論構建的 Gelfand- Cetlin系統。這些可積系統，或拉格朗日圓環纖維束 ， 最近被應用到構造類型A的旗簇的鏡流形，這種構建是沿著著名 的SYZ提案的線路所建立的，從而得出一個很好的圖像說明在此 情況下的鏡對稱現象。 不幸的是，同樣的構建被應用到其他旗簇如Grassmann流形時不 會得出正確的鏡流形。本項目的主要目的就是建立一類新的可積 系統並應用它去研究鏡對稱，我們期望通過應用SYZ提案於這些 可積系統上能建造出所有旗簇的正確的鏡流形。 這將為已知的情況帶來新的啟示。例如，對於類型A的旗簇，我 們的鏡流形將包含舊的鏡流形作為開放稠密子集，而且新的鏡流 形將另外滿足由物理原理所衍生出的某些拓撲約束。通過這樣做 ，我們會得到一個更好的，更統一的對旗簇鏡對稱的認識。 我們還計劃將這些新的可積系統應用到旗簇的幾何量子化的研究 。我們的可積系統擁有一些很好的性質，這些性質都是以前的 Gelfand-Cetlin系統（或其它相似的採用Okounkov體所構建的可 積系統）所缺乏的。事實上，正由於Gelfand-Cetlin系統缺乏某些 特性，導致了他們被應用到幾何量化的研究時出現了一些問題。 因此，我們希望藉著我們的新可積系統可以為這些問題帶來新的 見解。

14300314.label: Realisation of objectives
14300314.value: The first objective of this project was to construct a new class of integrable systems on flag varieties. The PI and collaborators succeeded in constructing new families of integrable systems on at least two classes of flag varieties: the quadrics and a family of two-step flag varieties. Recall that for the purpose of SYZ mirror symmetry, the Gelfand-Cetlin fibration is not desirable because the preimage of the boundary of the image polytope (called the Gelfand-Cetlin polytope) is not an algebraic subvariety in the flag manifold. To construct the SYZ mirror, we need a more compatible class of integrable systems. Our starting point was Auroux's pioneering work in which he constructed non-toric Lagrangian fibrations on toric manifolds (e.g. the projective plane) by deforming the affine structure on the base of the toric moment map. We followed his approach to deform the Gelfand-Cetlin system in a similar way so that facets of the Gelfand-Cetlin polytope are being deformed and pushed into the interior of the base forming walls and singularities. Another key notion is Tyurin’s pseudotoric structure, which is a natural generalization of Auroux’s construction. While pseudotoric structures trivially exist in cohomogeneity one examples (as in Auroux’s examples), their constructions in general cases are highly nontrivial. In Tyurin’s original paper, he constructed pseudotoric structures for any smooth quadric hypersurface in a projective space. In joint work with his collaborators, the PI succeeded in constructing such structures on another class of examples, namely, the family of two-step flag varieties. We also discovered that the integrable systems are compatible with the SYZ proposal in the following sense: there exist suitable choices of an anticanonical divisor and a meromorphic volume form with respect to which the fibration is special Lagrangian. Furthermore, we expect that the fibration, which is currently defined outside a codimension 2 subvariety, to be extendable to the whole space, and then the preimage of the boundary of the image convex body would be precisely the anticanonical divisor chosen beforehand. The second objective of this project was to apply the new class of integrable systems to obtain a better understanding of mirror symmetry for flag varieties. To do so, the PI and collaborators examine Rietsch’s Lie-theoretic construction of Landau-Ginzburg mirrors for flag varieties, which are known to give the correct mirrors for various classes of examples, especially in the type A case. More precisely, Givental originally constructed a Landau-Ginzburg mirror for a type A full flag manifold whose ambient space is an algebraic torus and the superpotential is a certain Laurent polynomial. Generalizing his construction to other type A partial flag manifolds also give Landau-Ginzburg mirrors, but in general the superpotential does not have enough critical points. More recently, Rietsch gave a uniform Lie-theoretic construction of Landau-Ginzburg mirrors for flag varieties of any type. Furthermore, in various classes of examples including Grassmannians, her mirrors were shown to give the correct number of critical points. Another feature of Rietsch’s mirror is that the superpotential in general has fewer terms than Givental’s mirror superpotential. In joint work with his collaborators, the PI succeeded in explaining the number of terms in Rietsch’s mirror for the two classes of flag varieties mentioned above. More precisely, by connecting our special Lagrangian torus fibrations with the Gelfand-Cetlin fibrations along smooth families of integrable systems, we see that facets of the Gelfand-Cetlin polytope are being pushed into the interior of the base to become walls. Geometrically, this corresponds to deforming (or partially smoothing of) the anticanonical divisor. Accordingly, terms in the superpotential of Givental’s mirror are being merged together, which, conjecturally, correspond to holomorphic disks being glued together. This process gives rise to terms in the superpotential of Rietsch’s mirror superpotential and explain why the number of terms is less than that in Giventals’ mirror superpotential. The PI has also tried to explore the relation between construction of such integrable systems (and the corresponding SYZ mirror construction) with the GIT quotient construction of the space concerned. As a testing ground, the PI investigated the relation for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds as a GIT quotient of a vector space. By using instanton corrections coming from Woodward's quasimap Floer theory instead of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's Lagrangian Floer theory, we show that the resulting SYZ mirror (which we call the quasimap SYZ mirror) coincides with the one written down via physical means as expected. The next step would be investigating the case for flag manifolds, which can also be regarded as GIT quotients of vector spaces. The third objective of this project was to apply the new class of integrable systems to study geometric quantization for flag varieties. The PI and collaborators have gained some new insights on this problem using the new integrable systems we constructed. We expect to develop and use the preliminary ideas we obtained to get some concrete new results in the near future. Again, viewing the flag varieties as GIT quotients could be useful and even crucial in this study.

14300314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300314.value: By generalizing Auroux’s idea in constructing non-toric Lagrangian fibrations on toric manifolds and also exploiting Tyurin’s notion of pseudotoric structures, we constructed new families of integrable systems on a class of two-step flag varieties of type A. Along the way, we clarify a general relation between pseudotoric structures and special Lagrangian torus fibrations, the latter of which are important in the study of SYZ mirror symmetry. We applied the newly constructed integrable systems to understand mirror symmetry for quadric hypersurfaces and the family of two-step flag varieties of type A. In particular, we describe how one can obtain the superpotential of Rietsch’s originally Lie-theoretic Landau-Ginzburg mirrors from the superpotential of Givental’s mirror in the type A case by connecting the Gelfand-Cetlin system with our newly constructed integrable system along a smooth family. As we go from the former to the latter, facets of the Gelfand-Cetlin polytope are being pushed into the interior of the base of the fibration forming walls; geometrically this corresponds to deforming, or partially smoothing of, the anticanonical divisor. At the same time, holomorphic disks, which correspond to terms in the superpotential, are being merged together, so terms in Givental’s superpotential are being combined together to produce the terms in Rietsch’s superpotential. This nicely explain why in general Rietsch’s superpotential has fewer terms than Givental’s superpotential. Recently, our proposal has been realized by the works of Hong, Kim and Lau for the Grassmannian of 2-planes in 4-space, providing more evidence for our proposal. In order to investigate how the fact that a variety is a GIT quotient can be exploited in the construction of integrable systems and SYZ mirrors, we study the construction of the quasimap SYZ mirror for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are GIT quotients of vector spaces. Here we use the instanton corrections coming from Woodward's quasimap Floer theory instead of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's Lagrangian Floer theory, and we show that the quasimap SYZ mirror of a toric Calabi-Yau manifold coincides with the one predicted using physical methods. The next step would be investigating the case for flag manifolds, which can also be regarded as GIT quotients of vector spaces. Using the newly constructed integrable systems, we have also obtained some new but preliminary ideas on how to gain a deeper understanding of the geometric quantization for flag varieties. These are expected to lead to concrete new results in the near future.

14300314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300314.value: An immediate follow-up question is whether there exist pseudotoric structures on other flag varieties or even other Fano manifolds. It is desirable to have better criteria to guarantee the existence of such structures. One can then proceed to find a suitable anticanonical divisor and a compatible meromorphic volume form and ask whether the induced Lagrangian fibration is special with respect to them. We expect that this is always the case, but a general proof is lacking. On the other hand, the GIT perspective needs further investigation and a lot of questions can be asked. A natural question is to make use of an integrable system on a space equipped with a group action, which is usually easier to find (e.g. in the case of vector spaces), and then try to construct an integrable system on the GIT quotient. These are in turn closely related to the so-called gauged linear sigma models (GLSM), which are currently studied by several groups of people. These models can help to understand mirror symmetry for GIT quotients. In particular, it is plausible that the original physical proof of Hori-Vafa for mirror symmetry for toric manifolds and their hypersurfaces/complete intersections can be made rigorous.

14300314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300314.value: Mirror Symmetry was discovered by String theorists in the early 1990s. It predicts that there is a highly nontrivial and mysterious equivalence between the Symplectic Geometry of a space and the Complex Geometry of a completely different space. This led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been striving to understand the geometry of Mirror Symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that Mirror Symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of Mirror Symmetry. Our construction of new integrable systems on flag varieties is an important step towards a complete understanding of Mirror Symmetry for such spaces, especially from the SYZ perspective. Our results shed new light on the difference between various constructions of mirrors for such spaces. In particular, we now have a better geometric picture to see why the old construction is inadequate.

14300414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300414.value: Methane hydrates and methane gas in underground deposits are the largest reserve of hydrocarbon fuel remaining on earth. The gaseous nature of methane under ambient conditions makes it difficult transport and store, leading to interest in the development of methods to convert it to methanol, a liquid fuel used in Indy racecars. A major challenge, however, is being able to mediate this conversion in a controlled fashion that avoids its overoxidation. Recently, Prof. Sunney Chan has identified two tricopper model systems that are able to achieve this. We helped to develop one of these systems, a peptide-bound tricopper complex that promotes the oxidation of methane to methanol when encapsulated in a mesoporous carbon framework. Intriguingly, the sequence of the peptide used for this study was derived from particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO), the major protein that catalyzes this conversion of methane to methanol in nature. In this proposal, we seek to build on this discovery by exploring ways to better characterize the structure and properties of this tricopper peptide complex, to enhance its stability, and to encapsulate it in a water-soluble framework suitable for both catalytic and structural studies. 甲烷水合物和氣體甲烷是地下蘊藏量最大的碳氢燃料。在常規條件下，氣體甲烷不便於運輸和儲存。目前主要的發展趨勢是將其轉化為液體燃料，甲醇。然而，如何建立一個有效，同時避免過度氧化的平台是一項重大的挑戰。近年，陳長謙教授的團隊確定了兩個"三銅"模型系統，可以實現這個目標。針對其中一個模型系統，我們將合作研究一個肽-銅複合體。在介孔碳的框架結構中，固定的複合體可以促進氣體甲烷轉化為甲醇。有趣的是，用於該研究的肽序列源於顆粒型甲烷單加氧酶(pMMO)，是自然界中催化甲烷轉化為甲醇的主要蛋白。在這個研究項目中，我們將進一步剖釋該肽-銅複合體的結構和特性，提高其穩定性，並增強整體結構的水溶性，以利於催化和結構研究。

14300414.label: Realisation of objectives
14300414.value: This project was focused on the use of two different crystallization domains to aid in the structure determination of a peptide, pmoA(38-49), thought to provide the major ligands to a tricopper cluster in the membrane-bound particulate methane monoxygenase (pMMO). Support for the viability of this pMMO peptide to form the desired complex was the precipitation of the isolated peptide when bound to copper, its EPR and mass spectra, and the ability of the pMMO peptide copper complex to catalyze one cycle of methane oxidation when formed within mesoporous carbon. The first crystallization domain employed was a mutant SAM-TEL crystallization domain developed by the laboratory of James Bowie (UCLA). Here individual SAM-TEL monomers combine form a helical repeat in a process that is pH driven. Based on the structures of proteins containing this domain, we felt we could fuse the pMMO peptide to the SAM-TEL C-terminus and thereby position the pmoA(38-49) peptide in an isolated location amenable to its structural determination. One problem we encountered, before the grant started, was the intercalation of two different SAM-TEL helical repeats whose formation would prevent the pMMO peptide from adopting a folded conformation. Following the plan of the proposal, we prepared mutants that designed prevent this intercalation, and were gratified that this effort was successful. Unfortunately, while crystals of the resulting SAM-TEL-pMMO peptide mutant could be obtained and characterized, when copper was added, the rod-shaped crystals expanded one end like a fan. We tried multiple solutions, but ultimately could not overcome this problem. We also tried to put the pmoA(38-49) peptide sequence between two SAM-TEL domains with the intent of anchoring the pMMO peptide more tightly. Unfortunately, we were unable to get crystals of this TEL-pMMO peptide-TEL construct. The second crystallization module that was explored was the Cry3Aa protein from Bacillus thuringiensis. This protein is novel because it naturally forms crystals in bacteria. One approached focused on fusing the pMMO peptide to the C-terminus of the protein. Here though crystals could be obtained, the pMMO peptide in the presence and absence of copper could not be observed. To better anchor the protein we decided to insert the pmoA(38-49) into an internal loop of Cry3Aa between residues 111-123. The helical region of pmoA was designed to be replace residues in an existing helix in Cry3Aa and then allow the residual residues to adopt its preferred conformation. The clone for this construct was produced, the protein overexpressed, the protein purified, and then crystallized. The good news was that we could see the helix and the loop residues of the pmoA(38-49) region. However, soaking with Cu(II)acetate or Cu(II)chloride showed no copper binding to the pmoA(38-49) peptide residues, though no binding was also observed to an endogenous copper binding site in Cry3Aa that we had previously identified. By altering the soaking conditions, we were able to identify conditions where we could observe copper binding to the endogenous copper site in Cry3Aa, but unfortunately, even under these conditions no binding of copper to the pmoA(38-49) sequence was observed. Thus for both crystallization-module-pMMO peptide constructs targeted in Specific Aim 1 and 2, we were able to produce crystals with the pmoA peptide poised to bind copper (hence the 80% achieved), but for both we were unable to get the copper complex - either because of crystal shearing (SAM-TEL-pMMO peptide) or due to lack of binding (Cry3Aa-pMMO peptide). Given these difficulties, as a side project, we decided to explore whether the Cry3Aa protein could be used to anchor other metal binding proteins. For this study we chose SmtA, a bacterial metallothionein known to bind copper, but also toxic heavy metals such as cadmium and chromium. This project was more successful. We were able to show that we could fuse up to six copies of metallothionin to Cry3Aa and demonstrate the use of this construct to remove Cd and Cr from aqueous solutions containing 0.1 ppm heavy metal. This latter work has been published.

14300414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300414.value: Unfortunately, we were unsuccessful obtaining structure of the pmoA(38-49) peptide bound to copper. We were particularly surprised by the lack of any copper binding in this latest Cry3Aa-pmoA(38-49) construct - given the binding to the binding of copper in the endogenous copper binding site within the Cry3Aa protein, and the fact that both pmoA(38-49) peptide and SAM-TEL-pmoA(38-49) show a clear copper dependent precipitation at 3 equivalents copper consistent with formation of a copper peptide complex. Our current view is that the poor binding might be dependent factors associated with the ligand environment and thermodynamics of cluster formation. Copper binding to both pmoA(38-49) peptide and SAM-TEL-pmoA(38-49) could be driven by a thermodynamic driving force linked to its precipitation. It maybe that the copper complex is not inherently stable in the absence of this driving force, particularly outside of the hydrophobic membrane environment of the bilayer. This would be consistent with the facile loss of the trinuclear copper cluster during purification. Notably, the endogeous site in Cry3Aa that does bind copper is also fairly buried, and here too copper binding might be enhanced its environment - because it doesn't need to compete with water binding. Despite this setback, we were able to demonstrate an novel application of using a crystallization module to a metal binding peptide domain to produce a functional material. Here the fusion of Cry3Aa to multiple copies of the bacterial metallothionin SmtA was shown to produce immobilized crystals that could be used to remove heavy metals from aqueous solutions even at 0.1 ppm. This construct could eventually find application in the bioremediation of heavy atoms from contaminated waters.

14300414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300414.value: In terms of the determination of the SAM-TEL-pMMO and Cry3Aa-pMMO fusions, we believe that pre-crystallization of the domain with copper is unlikely to be successful. We are now working on trying to take advantage the insolubility of the pMMO peptide in the presence of copper, by trying to crystallize their complex by slow mixing in capillary solutions. In terms of the Cry3Aa-metallothionin construct, we are planning on exploring its use both as an environmental tool to quicky precipitate heavy atoms from aqueous streams and waters as well as a recyclable heavy atom binding filter to remove heavy atoms from drinking water.

14300414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300414.value: This research was focused on using two different protein crystallization modules to aid in the structural characterization of a targeted copper binding protein. Unfortunately, neither method was successful in allowing us to determine the structure of the copper binding protein. We were, however, able to use of one these protein modules to immobilize a different metal binding domain that binds heavy atoms that are toxic to the environment. The resulting technology is significant because it could potentially be used to remove soluble heavy atoms from environmental streams and drinking water.

14300514.label: Project Objectives
14300514.value: To conduct theoretical investigations on the use of various high dimensional variable selection method on change-points estimation in time series. In particular: * The consistency, convergence rate and the asymptotic distribution of the number and location of the change-points will be examined. * Extensions to change-point related time series models such as estimation in thresholds models will be investigated. To build practical and computationally efficient algorithms for the estimation procedure. By means of simulation experiments, to thoroughly examine the applications of the proposed estimation procedure on various models with a wide variety of stochastic structures. To illustrate the application of the proposed estimation procedure to real data sets.

14300514.label: Realisation of objectives
14300514.value: The main research objectives of this proposal have been realized. New statistical techniques for chang-points estimations and their related propoerties have been established. These methodologies include GOGA technqiues for linear and non-linear time series as well as high-dimensional time series. Consistency and asymptotic results related to oracle properties have been obtained. The findings of this project cover a wide scope of statistical inference for change-points problems encountered in linear and non-linear time series. Together they cover objectives 1-3 to a large extent. In the course of these findings, new numerical procedures have to be developed and some of these methods have been reported in the relevant publications, which addresses objective 4.

14300514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300514.value: The major finding of this proposal is to employ group orthogonal greedy algorithm (GOGA) techniques to conduct statistical inference for chang-points problems for both linear and non-linear time series models. In particular, by making use of the GOGA, consistency and oracle properties of the estimates are established. Further, by means of a high-dimensional regression framework, new techniques about inference of chang-point for time series were established. Numerical methods have also been developed in the course of this project to handle the convergence properties and the nested GOGA techniques. The collected research outcomes not only offer an novel method to analyze change-point of high-dimensional time series, but also provide a new method to estimate thresholds in non-linear time series. Important research findings from this project were reported in major international conferences and published in premiere refereed journals, as stipulated in Part C: Tables 8 and 9.

14300514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300514.value: As GOGA techniques are high-dimensional in nature, the results obtained in this proposal can be used in many other contexts. In particular, by introducing the idea nested GOGA, results from this project offer a novel way to analyze hihg-dimensional time series with change-points, which is of huge potential interest in financial risk management. The techniques developed in this project can be applied both to linear and non-linear time series. Further, by combining with a high-dimensional regression framework, this project offers new insight into the inference not only for the change-points themsleves, but also for the thresholds in non-linear time series. In summary, with the established theoretical properties of the change-points estimates, the pursuit of high-dimensional time series will be greatly enhanced. Finally, in areas such as financial risk management and network engineering, where change-points in high-dimensional situations are rules rather than exceptions, results of this project offer a viable means to handle structural changes that often occur in finance and economics.

14300514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300514.value: All of the major objectives have been realized in this project. By virtue of the GOGA techniques, advances in model estimation and calibration of change-points can now be efficiently conducted. This will bring significant impacts in modeling important features not only for a single time series, but also for several series jointly such as in the case of portfolio management and network traffic, where the joint effects of different assets have to be taken into account. In particular, the four objectives achieved in this proposal offer a platform and new direction that will lead to important advances in the pursuit of modeling multivariate financial data. Finally, by publishing relevant papers in statistics as indicated in objective five, important research developments can be disseminated to practitioners timely and effectively.

14300614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300614.value: Image segmentation refers to the identification of the boundaries of objects of interest in a given image. It is an important task in image processing with numerous practical applications, e.g., police may want to isolate a car from a crime scene photo, or a medical doctor may want to see the outline of blood vessels in a patient’s MRI image. The task is difficult as image contents vary across applications and are usually degraded by different kinds of noise and blur. Our proposal is to design efficient methods that are based on minimization to segment images under different forms of degradation and in different applications. The Mumford-Shah model is a fundamental tool in segmentation. It finds the segmented regions and their boundaries by minimizing a functional consisting of three terms: (i) a data fidelity term, (ii) the length of the boundaries, and (iii) a regularization term that guarantees the solution is smooth inside each segmented region. The model can produce very good segmentation. However, since the minimization problem is non-convex, there are no fast algorithms to solve it. Over the years, researchers have tried to find good ways to either simplify the functional or approximate the solution. The popular Chan-Vese model looks for two constant regions. In spite of this vast simplification, the functional is still non-convex and difficult to solve. Recently, we developed an effective two-stage segmentation method to tackle the problem. In the first stage, we seek a smooth solution of a convex approximation of the Mumford-Shah model. In the second stage, a thresholding technique is used to find the segmented solution. Our method produces results that are better than many competing methods and can easily handle blurred images corrupted by Poisson or multiplicative Gamma noise where most existing methods cannot. The goal of the project is to extend our methodology to design new efficient algorithms that can segment more general images such as vector-valued (e.g., color) images and images with missing information. We will analyze the functional in order to automatically tune the parameters according to the degradation model. We will explore the relationship between image segmentation and image restoration so as to derive new algorithms. We will provide convergence theory for these new algorithms and will compare them with the state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. For medical and biological segmentation results, we will turn to specialists to validate our algorithms. 圖像分割是識別給定圖像中的我們所關心的物體的邊界。它是圖像處理中的一項很重要的任務，有著非常廣泛的實際應用。例如：有助於員警從犯罪現場的圖像中提取出車輛資訊，或者醫生從病人的MRI圖像中識別出血管的輪廓。由於在不同的應用中，所涉及圖像的內容特性變化很大，再加上不同種類的噪聲和模糊對圖象的影響，這些都使得圖像分割具有天然的困難性。本計劃書是基於極小化理論，對於圖像在不同的破壞形式下和多樣的應用領域中，設計出有效的圖像分割方法。 Mumford-Shah 模型是一種基本的圖像分割手法。它是通過極小化一個目標函數來達到分割不同的區域和提取這些區域的邊界的目的。這個目標函數由以下三項組成：1）數據擬合項，2）區域邊界的總長度項，3）使得分割結果在每個區域的光滑性的懲罰項。Mumford-Shah 模型一般能給出很好的分割結果。但是，由於它本身極小化問題的非凸性，到目前為止還沒有有效的快速的求解方法。多年來，眾多研究學者已經在簡化其目標函數和尋找其近似解方面做了諸多的有效嘗試。比較流行的Chan-Vese 模型是尋找兩個常量區域，儘管此模型的目標函數已經足夠簡化，但是這個目標函數本身仍然是非凸的，求解難的問題依舊存在。 最近，我們提出了一種有效的兩階段分割方法來解決上述的問題。階段一，從Mumford-Shah模型的一個凸逼近中尋找一個光滑解。階段二，用一種閥值技術來獲得最終的分割結果。通過多方位的比較，我們的方法的結果優於眾多其它非常有競爭力的方法。特別的，對於現有的眾多方法在模糊圖像或者有Poisson和Gamma噪聲破壞的情形下失效的問題，我們的方法依然能給出很好的分割結果。 本計劃書所提的項目的目的是對我們現有的所提方法進行擴展，從而設計出新的、更具有一般性的有效方法。例如對於向量圖像（例如彩色圖像）和丟失某些部分資訊的圖像的分割問題。我們將對所提出的模型中的目標函數的參數進行分析，根據模型的特性，以便設計出自動的選取其最優參數的方法。我們還將探究圖像分割方法和圖像恢復方法之間的關係，借此推導出新的方法。對於新推導出的方法，我們將給出其收斂性和它們在速度，精度和魯棒性方面與其它最新方法的比較。對於醫學和生物學的分割結果，我們還將借助于這些方面的專家來對我們的方法做進一步驗證。

14300614.value: 1) In Paper 3, we have extended our methodologies to vector-valued images (such as color images in different color spaces). We also have extended it to images with information loss. In Paper 5, we have applied nonconvex model to improve our two-stage segmentation method. 2) Since the first part of our 2-stage method is a restoration method, and since non-convex restoration models have been proven to be better than convex restoration models in recovering straight edges, in Paper 5, we considered a segmentation model that in the first stage, the optimization model combines a convex data-fitting term with a non-convex regularization term. In Paper 1, we explored restoration models for manifold-valued images (e.g. denoising color images in the chromaticity and brightness space and also processing images with SO(3)-valued entries in the analysis of polycrystalline materials by means of Electron Backscattered Diffraction (EBSD)). In Paper 2, we consider reconstruction of parallel MRI images (which is a technique to accelerate the MRI imaging). These restoration and reconstruction models can be used as the Stage 1 models for our 2-stage segmentation method. 3) The parameter choices and the comparison with the state-of-the-art algorithms are done in all papers. In particular, in Paper 5, the problem is non-convex in general. But by choosing the regularization parameters appropriately, we can prove that the combined model is convex and hence can be solved fast by standard convex solvers. 4) Comparison between our algorithms with state-of-the-art algorithms are done in all papers. The 2-stage segmentation method is extended to classification method for hyperspectral imaging, which is the main theme of the M.Phil. student Kelvin Kan's thesis. The work is being submitted for publication. Extension to classification of point cloud data-set is the main theme of another M.Phil student. His work is submitted for publication also.

14300614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300614.value: In Paper 1, we have developed the half-quadratic minimization method for the restoration of images having values in a complete, connected Riemannian manifold. We prove the convergence of the method for Hadamard spaces. In Paper 2, we have developed an adaptive directional Haar Framelets to reconstruct the images obtained from parallel MRI machines. The small numbers of filters from these tightframe systems reduce much the artefacts as compared to state-of-the-methods, such as TV reconstruction or ESPIRiT system. In Paper 3, we have extended our 2-stage method to color images. We found that for color images, applying the 2-stage method to the RGC channels respectively cannot give good results. This is due to the strong correlation of the channels. In order to overcome this, we have lifted the results in each channel to another color space (the Lab space) where the cross-channel correlations are significantly weakened. There we applied our 2-stage method to the RGC and Lab channels simultaneously and obtained very good results when compared to other state-of-the-art methods. In Paper 3, we also considered segementing images with information loss (e.g. 60% of the pixels are not given) and the results are nice too. In Paper 4, we have extended the FEAST method, a contour-integral eigensolver, for finding eigenvalues for Hermitian matrices to non-Hermitian matrices. Since the first part of our 2-stage method is a restoration method, and since non-convex restoration models have been proven to be better than convex restoration models in recovering straight edges, in Paper 5, we have considered using non-convex model in the Stage 1 of our 2-stage method. The difficulty here is that the non-convex regularizers may make the resulting optimization problems extremely difficult to solve. Here we notice that the data-fitting term is quadratic (and convex). We proved that when the regularization parameter of the data-fitting term is properly tuned, the combined optimization model is still convex although it has a non-convex term. Hence the optimization can be done extremely fast using standard method for convex problems. The resulting segmentation results are significantly improved over other state-of-the-art convex and nonconvex models.

14300614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300614.value: In Paper 1, we explored restoration models for manifold-valued images (e.g. denoising color images in the chromaticity and brightness space and also processing images with SO(3)-valued entries in the analysis of polycrystalline materials by means of Electron Backscattered Diffraction (EBSD)). In Paper 2, we consider reconstruction of parallel MRI images (which is a technique to accelerate the MRI imaging). The models we developed in these two papers are good for these very special images. In the future, we will consider combining these restoration models into the first stage of our 2-stage model to get good segmentation results for these special images. The idea developed here can be extended to classification problems. Examples are classification of hyperspectral images and classification of point cloud data sets. One of the MPhil students supported by this funding did his thesis based on this. His work is being submitted for publication. Anther MPhil. student is applying it for classification of point cloud data set. Both of the work has been submitted for possible publication.

14300614.value: Image segmentation refers to the identification of the boundaries of objects of interest in a given image. It is an important task in image processing with numerous practical applications, e.g., police may want to isolate a car from a crime scene photo, or a medical doctor may want to see the outline of blood vessels in a patient’s MRI image. The task is difficult as image contents vary across applications and are usually degraded by different kinds of noise and blur. Our objective is to design efficient methods that are based on minimization to segment images under different forms of degradation and in different applications. In this project, we have developed new segmentation method based on an effective two-stage segmentation method we invented earlier. 14300814.label: Project Objectives
14300814.value: To evaluate and revamp existing multiple testing procedures in NI trials. There are several existing testing procedures and we will examine and compare them to generate the best paradigm for NI tests. To provide appropriate testing methods for a wide spectrum of data collected in NI studies. Existing multiple testing techniques only apply to very restricted settings and we seek to propose procedures that will be able to handle different types of data including (i) heterogeneous treatment variances (ii) non-normal responses, (iii) categorical data, and (iv) a mixture of continuous and categorical endpoints. To derive distribution theories regarding the testing statistics. The distributions of all test statistics have to been clearly derived. In some cases, asymptotic theorems will be developed. To offer a comprehensive simulation study to assess the merits of different competing testing procedures. Besides asymptotic theorems, simulation studies will be used to evaluate different procedures, especially when the sample size is small. These simulation studies will include the investigation of familywise error rate and test power. To disseminate our findings to researchers and practitioners using NI studies, and to provide clear guidance to practitioners in choosing an appropriate method among different testing procedures

14300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300814.value: The objective of a non-inferiority (NI) clinical trial is to assert the efficacy of an experimental (new) treatment compared to an active control by proving that the experimental treatment maintains a considerable fraction of the treatment effect of the control. Both the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency have issued strict guidelines regarding NI trials to offer technical guidance for the pharmaceutical industry and the clinical research community. Non-inferiority studies are gaining popularity recently amid the rapid increase in scientific endeavor to explore potential substitutes of standard treatments. However, there is a shortage of appropriate statistical procedures that could be employed to analyze the findings of NI trials. A valid NI trial is required to demonstrate assay sensitivity, which provides the differentiable ability to distinguish an effective treatment from an ineffective one. This requirement implies that in an NI study, the active control has to preserve the expected effect with a magnitude comparable to those reported in previous placebo-controlled studies. An NI trial with the inclusion of experimental treatments, active control and placebo is called a three-arm NI trial. Testing procedures for three-arm NI trials are available, but most only provide methodologies to deal with a single experimental treatment. However, clinical studies often involve multiple treatments, including cases in which there are different doses of a new drug or different combinations of several new drugs. Recently, Kwong et al. (2012, Statistics in Medicine, 31, 2833-2843) laid the groundwork for statistical procedures for three-arm NI trials with multiple experimental treatments. The Kwong et al. (2012) testing procedure applies to less intricate settings. It is suitable only for treatment responses that are normally distributed with homogeneous variance. Hence, more sophisticated statistical methods are required. In this project, we will seek to propose testing techniques for NI trials with more complex data structures, including heterogeneous variances, non-normal responses and categorical data. The determination of the required sample size before the onset of an NI trial will also be explored. The findings should be tremendously valuable not only to practitioners in the field of NI clinical studies, but also to patients who await treatment substitutes that might be more affordable or have fewer side-effects. 非劣效性臨床試驗的目的是通過比較實驗（新）療法與有效療法，證明實驗療法能保持有效療法中相當大一部分的功效。美國食品和藥物管理局以及歐洲藥品管理局都發佈了嚴格的非劣效性試驗準則，為製藥工業和臨床研究機構提供技術指導。非劣效性試驗的研究近來得到了廣泛的關注。大量的科學工作致力於探索潛在的可代替標準療法的治療手段。然而，我們缺乏分析非劣效性試驗結果的統計方法。 一個有效的非劣效性試驗需要有一定的檢測靈敏度，從而區分出有效和無效的療法。這說明非劣效性試驗中的有效療法需要保持著與先前安慰劑對照試驗報告中相若的預期效果。包含了實驗療法、有效療法和安慰劑的非劣效性試驗稱為三臂非劣效性試驗。已有的三臂非劣效性試驗方法中，大部分隻適用於單個實驗療法的情形。然而，臨床試驗通常涉及到多個實驗療法，例如一種新藥可有不同劑量，又或幾種新藥可有不同組合。最近，Kwong等（2012, Statistics in Medicine, 31, 2833-2843）為涉及多個實驗療法的三臂劣效性試驗提出了統計分析方法。 Kwong等（2012）提出的檢驗方法不適用於複雜的設定。它只適用於治療反應為均方差正態分佈的情形。所以，更複雜的統計方法是必需的。在這個課題中，我們將提出檢驗方法，以用於帶有複雜資料結構的非劣效性試驗，包括異方差、非正態的治療反應以及分類資料。我們也會探討非劣效性試驗所需的樣本量。研究結果不僅會對非劣效性臨床研究領域的從業人員非常有價值，同時對於期待更實惠或者較少副作用替代療法的患者亦是非常有價值。

14300814.label: Realisation of objectives
14300814.value: Previous research studies on NI testing procedures with multiple treatments are focused on less complicated clinical trial settings. In practice, practitioners often confront with more complex clinical environments with more demanding medical objectives. This research project enables the comparisons of treatment efficacies in an NI trial with both multiple experimental treatments and multiple reference treatments. Further, our research results can be applied to handle simultaneous targets of establishing NI and possible superiority of experimental treatments. Even though the described models in this study concentrate on normal responses, the methodological development allows easy extension of our methods to other types of responses amid the asymptotic distributions of statistics for non-normal responses are usually normal. Besides theoretical investigation regarding the test statistics, extensive simulation studies are conducted to explore the performance of our proposed methods. The simulation results are very encouraging, indicating that our proposed methods are able to control familywise type I error with superb test power. Finally, besides publications in a high-ranking journal, the findings of our research are presented in international conferences.

14300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300814.value: Noninferiority (NI) clinical trials are becoming more popular, especially in cancer and cardiovascular research. There has been a shortage of appropriate statistical tools to compare treatment efficacies in NI trials. This project investigates general testing paradigms that include multiple reference treatments and multiple experimental treatments, hence encompassing a very broad clinical trial spectrum. As indicated in the United States Food and Drug Administration Guidance, it is deemed useful to explore whether an experimental treatment is superior to the reference treatment after the confirmation of NI. Our research team has derived appropriate statistical tools to allow clinical data analysts to proceed to examine whether an experimental treatment is in fact better the standard treatment. Several stagewise-stepwise procedures are given. The evaluation of the necessary critical values are also discussed. All the suggested procedures in our project are derived with the desirable feature that they control the familywise type I error rate strongly at a pre-determined level. That is, the probability of making any type I error is not exceeding a pre-specified level under any configurations of the parameters. In addition, the test power of different testing procedures are compared in order to understand their relative merits. Clinical examples are provided to illustrate the use of our methods to ensure that practitioners in clinical studies are able to select the most appropriate procedure for the understanding of their related findings.

14300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300814.value: A very controversial issue in three-arm NI trials is the adoption of the placebo in the trial. It would be an important and worthwhile future research task to explore the feasibility to modify our research work such that data resulted from a clinical study without the placebo can be analyzed accordingly. It will definitely involves the ideas and concepts of meta-analysis where assay sensitivity could be inferred from past placebo-controlled trials. Another interesting future research direction is to extend our work to survival outcomes. Since survival outcomes shares a significant portion of clinical trial activities nowadays, NI studies involving survival outcomes will definitely be useful for practitioners in this area.

14300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300814.value: The growing popularity of NI trials in the past decade represents the drug development industry's increasing need to search for appropriate substitutes for standard treatments. Unlike superiority studies, an NI trial is designed to declare that an experimental treatment can be considered a potential substitute for the reference treatment when the former is not inferior to the latter by a clinically significant margin. The loss of efficacy must be justified by compelling reasons, such as an easing of side effects, a reduction of the cost of treatment, or a less complicated treatment regimen. The research findings in this project provide appropriate and powerful statistical tools to tackle data analysis of a wider spectrum of NI clinical settings, allowing the inclusion of multiple experimental treatments and multiple standard treatments. Further, our proposed procedures permit the testing of superiority after the confirmation of NI, leading to a more comprehensive understanding of the important characteristics regarding the efficacy of the tested treatments. Consequently, it empowers researchers in clinical studies in their search for more effective treatments of various types of diseases.
