14300914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300914.value: The study of networks, systems that consist of a number of elementary components, known as nodes, interacting with one another, has become increasingly important in many disciplines including physics and systems biology. The collective behavior of a network arises from the interactions of the nodes. When two nodes interact, they are said to be connected or linked to one another. For a biological network, knowing the information of such connectivity of the network is a significant first step for understanding the functionality of the network. Thus extracting or inferring connectivity of a network has been an active and important research problem in systems biology. All existing methods have their limitations and the problem is far from being solved. Recently, we have developed a method that can extract the connectivity of bidirectional networks with uniform coupling using measurements of the dynamics of the nodes as the only input data. Our method gives very good accuracy for a variety of networks with different dynamics. In realistic situations, coupling strength can be different for different nodes and the connections can be directional as in networks of neurons, making the extraction of connectivity even more challenging. In this project, we propose to tackle these challenges. We will use our present approach to develop a method that is applicable to weighted bidirectional networks in which the coupling strength can be different for different connections and to extract information about the relative coupling strength of the connections. Up until now, most methods focus on bidirectional networks with uniform coupling and the problem to predict the weights of the connections is well known to be very difficult. Hence our successful development of such a method would be a major advance in the field. Second, we will carry out a systematic numerical investigation to explore directional networks in which the nodes can be connected in one direction only. Directional networks are extremely difficult to deal with so any understanding that we can gain would be highly fruitful. Third, we will investigate the accuracy of extraction methods using statistical correlation. This is particularly important for establishing the correct functional brain networks as many present studies are based on methods using statistical correlation. Finally, we will apply our methods to analyze experimental measurements of retina and cortical neuronal networks of rats, and expect to further improve our methods and to understand better these networks. 關於網絡的研究對物理學以至生物學等許多學科都日益重要。一個網絡是由許多互相作用的基本部分組成，這些基本部分稱為網絡的節點，而基本部分之間的相互作用則為節點的連結。一個網絡的整體行為由個別節點的相互作用所導致，所以知道網絡的連結性將是我們理解網絡，特別是生物學中的網絡的功能重要的第一步。因此，如何從量度的數據獲取網絡的連結性是一個活躍及重要的硏究課題。最近我們開展了一個方法，只需要節點的動態訊息便可找出網絡的連結性。現時方法適用於節點的相互作用是雙向性並有一致的強度。在現實的網絡中，節點之間相互作用的強度往往各不相同並且是單向性，要獲取這些更複雜網絡的連結性將是一個更大的挑戰。這個研究計劃的目標是建基於我們現有的基礎，開展一些方法可以應用於雙向性但相互作用強度不一的網絡，並且探討怎樣獲取單向性網絡的連結性。最後我們將應用建立了的方法去分析老鼠視網膜及大腦神經細胞網絡的實驗數據，希望可以加深我們對這些神經細胞網絡的理解。

14300914.label: Realisation of objectives
14300914.value: We have developed a method that can reconstruct both the links and the weights of the links for weighted bidirectional networks. The method is based on a mathematical result derived for a model class of bidirectional networks whose dynamics approach a fixed point in the noise-free limit. We have tested our method using numerical simulations and found good accuracy even for networks with more general dynamics that go beyond the model class. Thus we have achieved objective 1. We have exceeded objective 2. The problem of reconstruction of directional or directed networks is known to be highly challenging. By extending our earlier approach for bidirectional networks to directed networks, we have derived a mathematical result relating the adjacency matrix of a network to quantities calculable from measured time series of the nodes for directed networks that are subjected to a white noise and whose dynamics approach a fixed point in the noise-free limit. Based on this mathematical result, we have successfully developed a method for reconstructing general directed and weighted networks. When the coupling function has additional properties, we are further able to reconstruct the weights of the links, incoming links, or outgoing links. We have tested our method using numerical simulations and found good accuracy in general. In realistic problems, the networks of interest are often subjected to noise that has a finite correlation time and cannot be approximated by a white noise. The mathematical calculations for correlated noise are non-trivial and much more complicated than those for white noise. After great efforts, we have successfully generalized our method to reconstruct directed networks subjected to either white noise or colored noise with a finite correlation time. Regarding objective 3, our original method is based on a mathematical relation for weighted bidirectional networks whose graphs have only one connected part and makes use of the pseudo-inverse of a dynamical covariance matrix. By extending the mathematical derivation to networks whose graphs have more than one connected part, we have found that the adjacency matrix of the model class of bidirectional networks is related to the inverse of the covariance matrix. This new and more general mathematical relation allows us to gain analytic understanding of the shortcomings of methods using statistical correlation (either Pearson correlation or partial correlation coefficient) in general and not only for functional brain networks. We have clearly demonstrated such shortcomings using numerical simulations. Thus we have achieved objective 3 successfully. The successful development of a reconstruction method for general directed networks has exceeded our original objective 2 and takes up more time than was originally planned. Yet it also allows us to reconstruct realistic networks from experimental measurements and to expand our original research plan for objective 4 to a detailed study of the properties of the network structure of the cultured cortical neuronal network reconstructed using our method from multi-electrode array measurements and to a systematic study of the relation between dynamics and network structure. We first solved the problem of obtaining complex values by applying low-pass filter to the experimental measurements. By assuming that the coupling function has certain property, we have further inferred the weights of the links. Based on the outgoing coupling strength, we can classify the nodes into excitatory, inhibitory or nodes with no outgoing links. The ratio between the number of excitatory and inhibitory nodes is in general agreement with known values for rats. With this reconstructed network, we study the relation of spike rates of individual nodes and network features. Several interesting results have already been found: (1) spike rate is highly related to the average coupling strength of the incoming excitatory links, and (2) nodes with high spike rate are mostly excitatory nodes. Result (1) allows us to predict which nodes would have high spike rate. Indeed this prediction method has high accuracy with both sensitivity and specificity close to 80%. With the reconstructed network, many new exciting questions can be addressed. For example, it has been found that the cultured neuronal network has interesting synchronized bursts or network bursts in which many nodes spike together. It is believed that such network bursts play an important role in the functions of neuronal network and an important question would be to understand the underlying mechanism for such network bursts. Using our reconstructed network, we can attempt to address this exciting and important question. Thus this new systematic study warrants a project of its own, and we have successfully secured funding for a new RGC GRF project (14304017), which is a continuation of the present project. Further work will be done and reported for this new project.

14300914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300914.value: We have established a systematic approach for developing methods for reconstructing networks from dynamics of nodes. In this approach, we derive mathematical results that relate the weighted adjacency matrix of a network to quantities that can be calculated using measured time series of the nodes using a model class of networks that are subjected to noise and whose dynamics approach a fixed point in the noise-free limit. Then we perform clustering analysis of the quantities that relate to the off-diagonal elements of the weighted adjacency matrix (which separate into two groups according to whether there is a link from node j to node i or not) and thus reconstruct the links. Finally, we test our method using numerical simulations. Using this approach, we have successfully developed a method for reconstructing the links and their weights for weighted bidirectional networks (publications 1 and 3) and for reconstructing the links and their directions for weighted directed networks subjected to white noise (publication 2) or correlated noise of finite correlation time (publication 3). When the coupling function has additional properties, our methods can further reconstruct the weights of the links, incoming links, or outgoing links (publications 2 and 3). Moreover, we have gained analytic understanding of the shortcomings of methods using statistical correlation (Pearson correlation or partial correlation coefficient) and have clearly demonstrated such shortcomings using numerical simulations (publication 3). Applying our method for directed networks subjected to white noise, we have successfully reconstructed in-vitro cultured neuronal networks from experimental multi-electrode array measurements of cortical neurons from rats. By assuming that the coupling function has certain property, we can also infer the synaptic weights of the links. Based on the outgoing coupling strength, we can classify the nodes into excitatory, inhibitory or nodes with no outgoing links. The ratio between the number of excitatory and inhibitory nodes is in general agreement with known values for rats. With this reconstructed network, we have carried out a systematic study of the relation of spike rates of individual nodes and network features. Several interesting results have been found: (1) spike rate is highly related to the average coupling strength of the incoming excitatory links, and (2) nodes with high spike rate are mostly excitatory nodes. Result (1) allows us to predict accurately which nodes would have high spike rate with both sensitivity and specificity close to 80%.

14300914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300914.value: The reconstruction method for general directed networks developed in this project enables us to reconstruct realistic networks from dynamics of the nodes. Dynamics of the nodes can be readily measured for in-vitro cultured neuronal networks using multi-electrode array allowing us to apply our method to reconstruct neuronal networks from experimental data. With the reconstructed networks, many new exciting questions can be addressed. For example, synchronized bursts or network bursts in which many nodes spike together have been observed and believed to play an important role in the functions of neuronal network. An important question would be to understand the underlying mechanism for such network bursts. This new study thus warrants a project of its own. In real-world problems, it is common that some nodes are unknown or measurements from some nodes are unavailable. These nodes are known as hidden nodes. It is thus important to understand the effects of hidden nodes on the reconstruction results. To follow up on these further developments, we have proposed a new RGC GRF project as a continuation of the present one and have successfully secured funding for the new project. Further work and results will be done and reported for the new project.

14300914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300914.value: Many systems of interest in physics and biology consist of a number of interacting components, and can be represented by networks with the components being the nodes and the interactions being the links between the nodes of the network. Knowing the network structure such as the links, their directions and relative coupling strength can provide us useful insights of the functionality and overall behavior of these systems. A vast amount of data has been taken for various biological networks and a grand challenge is to reconstruct the network structure from these measurements. Our project addressed this challenge and we have successfully developed methods that can reconstruct the network structure using only measurements of the dynamics of the nodes based on a solid mathematical framework. We have applied our method to reconstruct in-vitro neuronal networks of rats in culture from experimental data. Not only can we reconstruct the links but also infer the relative synaptic weights of the links. We have found several interesting results such as high spike rate nodes are mostly excitatory nodes and that we can predict accurately whether a node has high spike rate or not based on its average strength of the incoming excitatory links.

14301014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301014.value: 擴散現象於大自然和人類社會中皆甚為普遍。數學上，此等現象由微分方程描述。 這些拋物型方程都具有共通的正則化效果。簡單而言，粗糙的初始態，如某些化學成分在液體中的濃度，一下子其濃度便變得光滑了。但初始值是很差時，方程就不必可解。因此從數學上確定那些初始值是有解的是重要的課題。 拋物型方程種類繁多，由其結構如擴散係數而確定。 數學工作者致力確定某類方程可解的最廣泛的初始值。一九四四年美國數學家Widder確定了熱方程的初始跡及可解性。近代對其它滲透方程亦有進展。本計劃沿此方向，研究某幾類非缐性拋物方程的同樣問題。

14301014.label: Realisation of objectives
14301014.value: We will present our findings in the following orders: (1) The initial-boundary value problem for the porous medium equation, (2) The initial-boundary value problem for the heat equation, (3) the generalised curve shortening problem with general initial data, and (4) some issues on the thin film equations. (1) The most important outcome of this project is the study for the general initial-boundary problem for the porous medium equation in the slow diffusion (see [3] for the mathematical formulation). In 1980's people studied this problem assuming the boundary data to be zero. It was shown that for any (non-negative) weak solution of the problem, the initial trace exists, consisting of a bottom trace and a corner trace (both are Radon measures). There is only one exception, namely a solution called the friendly giant which becomes unbounded when time approaches zero. Conversely, given a pair of Radon measures on the interior and the boundary of the domain, there exists a unique weak solution of the equation vanishing along the lateral boundary of which initial trace is the given Radon measures. More than thirty years have elapsed, results were not known when the weak solution does not vanish along the lateral boundary. In the beginning of this project, we proposed to study the problem for non-zero lateral boundary data but had no confidence that the problem can be solved completely. Fortunately, we found a smart way to show that any such weak solution must admit a Radon measure as its lateral trace. Moreover, when the weak solution satisfies a "finite mass" condition, it admits an initial trace consisting of a bottom and corner traces as the zero-lateral-boundary case. Conversely, we prove that for any given triple Radon measures on the bottom, at the corner and along the lateral boundary, there is a weak solution whose trace triple is the given one with "finite mass". A related technical question is: When the lateral boundary data is given by a continuous function, is the weak solution continuous up to the lateral boundary? Such so-called regularity problem occupies an important role in the modern study of nonlinear diffusion equations. In [4] we given a positive answer to this question. Our result is a significant one in the area of porous medium equations. We believe it will be cited in any serious treatise/book on the subject. There are still a few, open questions. First, is the weak solution for the initial-boundary value problem unique? It is known to be true when the lateral boundary data vanishes, and, as shown in [4], remains valid when the lateral boundary data is continuous. However, the uniqueness issue for the most general case is open. At this moment we have no idea how to proceed. Second, what will happen if the weak solution does not satisfy the "finite mass" condition? When the lateral boundary data is continuous, it is shown in [4] that it must be the unique friendly giant, that is, a solution blows up at zero everywhere. But the general case remains open. We conjecture that it must be the friendly giant and also it is unique. Third, the same initial-value problem in the fast diffusion case. It is known that this case is very different from the slow diffusion case. The fast diffusion case of the porous medium equation is less studied than the slow diffusion case. The Cauchy problem (that is, the underlying domain is the entire space, so there is no corner or lateral boundary) was solved long ago. We tried to modify our argument in the slow diffusion to cover the fast diffusion case but in vain. A serious thought concludes that this is a very difficult problem. (2) The American mathematician D V Widder was a pioneer of the study of the initial trace problem for (non-negative) solution of the heat equation. In 1930's he solved the Cauchy problem as well as the initial-boundary problem for the one dimensional heat equation (see his treatise "Heat Equation"). In fact, a representation formula for the solution was obtained. Can one extend his results to the higher dimensional heat equation? The Cauchy problem was done long ago, but the initial-boundary problem has been open for almost eighty years. In [5] we solve the problem by extending Widder's result to higher dimension. The treatment is parallel to the porous medium case where the only difference is that in the case of the heat equation, the "finite mass" condition always holds so there is no friendly giant. We raise two questions concerning our result. First, there are other representation formulas for the solution of the heat equation (see [5] for details). Is there a way to combine these two approaches? Next, with a representation formula at hand, one may adapt the potential theoretic method to study the non-tangential limits and obtain Fatou-type result for the solution. This could be a fruitful direction. (3) We completed a manuscript [6] related to the initial trace problem for the generalized curve shortening problem. Although it can be shown an initial trace (as a Radon measure) exists for the solution of the Cauchy problem for such equations, a complete characterization of these measures are not available. Therefore, we studied the Cauchy problem with general integrable data, a situation not studied before. Some results have been obtained. Even in such situation situations, the proofs are rather technical. We feel the treatment on the fast diffusion case of the porous medium equation will be useful in this context, but did not look into this matter. (4) The initial trace problem for the fourth order thin film equations. With full time and energy devoted to (1) and (2), we did not pay much attention to this problem, which is considered to be relatively less interesting. Nevertheless, in the process of reading literature, we did obtain some interesting results, see [1] and [2]. Objective 1 is estimated to be 80% completed. In the beginning we hoped to solve the problem for initial data which are Radon measures satisfying certain concentration condition. However, at the end we could only solve it for a large class of integrable data. The general case is not hopeless, but needs more time to work out. Objective 2 is achieved more than expected (and may be rated 200%). The initial-boundary value problem for the porous medium equation is essentially solved completely. Objective 3. We did not pay much attention to this objective. The breakthrough in Objective 2 drew our energy on it. Furthermore, as thin film equations no longer stays as a popular topic, the study has come to a halt.

14301014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301014.value: 1. In [3], we show that every nonnegative weak solution of the porous medium equation takes a Radon measure as its lateral boundary data. When the solution satisfies a "finite mass" condition, it has an initial trace consisting of a bottom and corner traces, which are Radon measures, too. Conversely, given Radon measures on the bottom, corner and lateral boundary, there is a nonnegative weak solution of the porous medium equation satisfying the "finite mass" condition with the prescribed Radon measures as its trace triple. When the lateral boundary data is given by a continuous function, much more precise results are obtained in [4]. For instance, the weak solution is unique and a characterization of the "finite mass" condition is found. 2. In the manuscript [5], the triple trace issue for the initial-boundary value problem for the heat equation is completed solved and a representation formula is available. This generalizes a classical result of Widder in 1930's to higher dimensions. 3. In the manuscript [6], the initial trace issue for the Cauchy problem of the generalized curve shortening problem is studied. We show the solution exists globally when the initial data belong to some class of integrable functions. 4. In the papers [1] and [2], some interesting results concerning the stability of the solutions for the one and two dimensional thin film equations are present.

14301014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301014.value: 1. After spending several years in initial and lateral boundary traces, on one hand, there are many interesting, open problem worthwhile to pursue. Some of them are discussed in 5.3. In particular, the uniqueness of the solution with prescribed trace triple could be solved by some generalized maximum principle for measures as data. It seems difficult, but not hopeless to investigate this problem further in the future. 2. On the other hand, it is interesting to extend our study to cover other partial differential equations. The most immediate ones are porous medium equations in the fast diffusion case. The problem is difficult, but one may first study it by assuming the lateral boundary data vanishes. The technique in the Cauchy problem should be useful. Other equations are interesting too. For instance, one may consider convex solutions of the Monge-Ampere equations, whose boundary data should also be measures but may not be Radon. Can we solve the Dirichlet problem with boundary data a regular Borel measure? 3. The initial trace problem for the curve shortening is not so easy. One approach may try to borrow tricks from the porous medium equation in the fast diffusion case.

14301014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301014.value: The wave equation, the heat equation and the Laplace equation are the prototype of partial differential equations. In particular, the heat equation is used widely to model diffusion, a phenomenon common in nature. The importance of the porous medium equation lies on the fact that it is a nonlinear version of the heat equation. In the project, the porous medium equation and its variants are studied. We focus on the situation where a diffusion obeying the porous medium equation is present in a region. Can one determine the diffusion (that is, the solution of the equation) completely by measuring the diffusion at time zero as well as its values along the boundary of the region in all subsequent time ? In the language of mathematics, we would like to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the porous medium equation and its variants. We have succeeded in treating this problem in some most important cases.

14301114.value: 非預先組織低聚分子的自排

14301114.label: Project Objectives
14301114.value: To prepare a homologous series of oligo(amide-triazole)s of different chain length and number of interacting group, and to correlate these parameters to their self-sorting and organogelation efficiencies by physical methods. To prepare a second series of oligo(amide-traizole) compounds with an elongated spacer unit, and to observe whether the fidelity of the self-sorting can be affected by the spacer length. To study the self-sorting between the normal and elongated series of oligomers, and to understand whether self-sorting can occur with two oligomers having the same number of interacting unit but different spacer length.

14301114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301114.value: Understanding how molecules interact in a complex molecular mixture is an emerging field of practical and theoretical interests. This kind of research can lead us to a better understanding of how specific biological processes can occur so selectively and uniquely in a complex mixture of biomolecules in our body. Molecular self-sorting is one of the interesting phenomena in chemical science, in which a particular molecule is able to recognize and interact with itself or another specific partner, but discriminate the rest in the presence of other potentially interfering molecules. In daily life this process is reminiscent to how people interact in a social group and subsequently how connections are set up and subgroups are formed. In order to dissect the many factors that can contribute to this phenomenon, this proposal seeks to prepare a group of oligo(amide-triazole) molecules having different number of interacting motifs, and to correlate the fidelity of their self-sorting properties to the gradual change of molecular structure and parameters. This kind of research will improve our understanding of the intricate interactions among these molecules, and can help us to design functional molecules with practical relevance. 了解個別分子在複雜的分子混合物是如何相互作用，是實踐和理論研究的一個新興領域。這方面的研究令我們更好地理解生物分子之間的相互作用為何能夠在複雜的環境下可以產生如此高的選擇性和獨特性。分子自排是有趣的化學現象，在這種特定的作用下，分子能夠識別並與其自身或另一特定分子相互作用，但同時能夠排斥或鑑別其他潛在干擾分子。為了研究可以促進這種現象的許多因素，本建議旨在以製備一組寡（酰胺三唑）分子，從而建立這些分子自排序的屬性和分子結構的關係。

14301114.label: Realisation of objectives
14301114.value: Oligo(amide-triazole) gelators with different number and density of amide units 1. Synthesis of target oligo(amide-triazole)s A series of structurally flexible, non-preorganized p-xylylene-linked oligo(amide-triazole)s [1 OAT-CO2H-2n, 2 OAT-H-2n, and 3 OAT-COPrg-(2n+1)] (see Appendix Figure 1 for structures) bearing carboxylic acid, hydride and N-propargyl amide end groups was prepared by copper(I)-catalyzed click chemistry using two iterative synthesis protocols. In addition to the (n+1) approach, the (n+2) approach was also used to grow the oligomers. The latter approach significantly shortened the time required to prepare the higher oligomers. In addition, a racemic 4-butyldecyl (i.e. R) was chosen as the side chain unit that shortened the synthesis route and enhanced the solubility of the products. In a similar manner, an elongated series of oligo(amide-triazole)s (OATe) (4, 5 and 6) with an extended spacer unit (−CH2CH2C6H4CH2CH2−) was similarly prepared. All the synthesized compounds were purified and fully characterized by spectroscopic methods. 2. Organogelation studies The gelation properties of the OAT and OATe compounds were examined and the key findings are summarized below: (i) A comparison of the gel-to-sol transition temperature (Tg) is not a good indicator to assess the relative gel strength because significant differences in the entropy (∆S) of gel-to-sol transition were found in the oligomers. Hence, the enthalpy (∆H) of gel-to-sol transition is a much more accurate parameter to represent the gel strength. Using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) technique, it was found that for oligomers within the same series and with the same end group, both the ∆H and ∆S increased monotonically with increasing number of amide units. However, a plateauing effect could be observed once the number of amide units became very large. This observation demonstrated the presence of a synergistic binding effect and a higher degree of molecular order with increasing number of amide functionalities. (ii) OAT oligomers with more than 5 CONH units are good gelators, while OATe oligomers require more than 6 CONH units in order to gel. The OAT gels were always stronger than the OATe gels having the same number of CONH groups, indicating that a higher amide density can lead to a gel with higher stability. (iii) A change of the oligomer end group significantly affected the ∆H and ∆S of the gel assembly. Oligomers with the N-propargylamide end group were found to have larger ∆H (i.e. the gels were more stable) and ∆S (i.e. the gels were packed more orderly) than those bearing carboxylic acid or hydride end groups. (iv) It was found that oligomers with N-propargyl amide end group were found to be kinetically trapped in the melted state. On the other hand, the corresponding saturated N-propyl amide analog still possessed translational freedom in the melted state. It was very intriguing to find out such a tiny change of functionality could affect the structure and stability of gel assembly. 3. Self-sorting studies For those organogelating oligomers, it was found that binary (1:1) and ternary (1:1:1) mixtures of them were also good multicomponent organogelators. Hence, mixed xerogels were prepared from two/three different oligomers and their self-sorting properties were examined by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The results were summarized below: (i) For the 1:1 mixed xerogels, narcissistic self-sorting behavior was not apparent with a difference of one CONH unit. (ii) For the 1:1 mixed xerogels prepared from oligomers bearing a difference of more than two CONH units, narcissistic self-sorting was found. The degree of self-sorting could be correlated to the difference in the number of CONH units by constructing the phase diagrams of the binary systems. Generally, a higher self-sorting tendency was noted when the difference in the number of CONH units became larger. (iii) Self-sorting could also be observed between xerogels of the OAT series and the elongated OATe series bearing the same number of CONH units, indicating that a difference in the amide density (i.e. spacer length) could also produce self-sorting. (iv) Self-sorting could also be identified in mixed wet gels by DSC experiments. (v) Self-sorting could also be found in ternary system containing three homologous oligomers having difference number of CONH units. After completing the work on oligo(amide-triazole)s, it was decided to investigate whether gels of two photoisomers could also exhibit self-sorting. As a result, additional work was carried out on the design, synthesis and self-sorting study of di-(dithienylethene) organogelators. This work was not in the original objectives of this proposal, but can be considered as an extension or further development of our initial research scopes. Photoresponsive di-(dithienylethene) organogelators 1. Synthesis A series of di-(dithienylethene) compounds 7a‒7e bearing different side chains and end groups was prepared (see Appendix Figure 2 for structures). The dithienylethene unit served as a photoresponsive moiety which could undergo reversible photo-induced (UV) cyclization to isomerize between the ring-open (o) and ring-closed (c) forms. 2. Photoresponsive organogelation studies (i) Among the five compounds synthesized, only compound 7e showed good gelating properties in aromatic solvents. The minimum gelation concentration (MGC) of the doubly ring-open form 7e-oo was <10 mg/mL. (ii) Upon photo-irradiation with UV light (313 nm), partial dissolution of the 1.5% 1,2-dichlorobenzene gel sample of 7e-oo was noted, indicating the singly (7e-oc) and doubly ring-closed isomers (7e-cc) were inferior gelators. The doubly ring-closed form 7e-cc was isolated and its MGC values were determined to be >25 mg/mL. 3. Self-sorting studies The 1:1 mixed xerogel of 7e-oo and 7e-cc was subjected to DSC examination. It was found that narcissistic self-sorting between the photoisomers could happen in the mixed gel state. The resulting also indicated that flexible, structurally closely related ring-open and ring-closed isomers also exhibited narcissistic self-sorting. In summary, objectives 1, 2 and 3 are fully addressed and fully achieved in this research work. Objective 1 was completed by studying the OAT series of compounds, while objective 2 was achieved by studying the OATe series of compounds. Finally, objective 3 was accomplished by studying both the OAT and OATe series of compounds together. For the di-(dithienylethene) series of compounds, it was shown that narcissistic self-sorting could also be found in structurally closely related photo-isomers.

14301114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301114.value: 1. We demonstrated here for structurally flexible, non-preorganized molecules such as oligo(amide-triazole)s and di-(dithienylethene)s, a slight change of their structure could seriously affect their self-assembly structure and self-sorting behavior. Contrary to our presumption, narcissistic self-sorting does not just only prevail in mixtures making up of structurally very different chemical entities, but appears to be fairly general even in mixtures of structurally closely related analogs. 2. It was found that upon mixing of the oligo(amide-triazole)s, narcissistic self-sorting could be observed in both the wet gel and xerogel states if (i) the difference in the amide units is greater than one or (ii) the amide unit densities (i.e. different spacer lengths) are different. 3. In the oligo(amide-triazole) series, it was noted that oligomers with N-propargyl amide end group were found to be kinetically trapped in the melted state. On the other hand, the corresponding saturated N-propyl amide analog did not show the same effect. It was very intriguing to find out such a tiny change of functionality could affect the structure and stability of the self-assembly. 4. It was reasoned that the use gel-to-sol transition temperature (Tg), a commonly used parameter to assess the gel strength of a series of structurally related organogelators, could be misleading. This is because using the Tg values to compare the relative stability (i.e. ΔH) of two gels is only valid when the entropy of changes (ΔS) of the two systems are equal. We demonstrated in this research work that the ΔS of structurally related compounds can be very different. Hence, it was resolved that the relative stability of two gels should be evaluated by comparing their ΔH values. 5. The result of the oligo(amide-triazole) research work was published in Chem. Sci., one of the top journals in chemistry and also presented as a poster in the 12th International Symposium on Macrocyclic and Supramolecular Chemistry 2017, and as an invited lecture in the 9th International Symposium on High-Tech Polymer Materials 2016. The result of the di(dithienylethene) work was published in Org. Biomol. Chem. 6. The work constituted part of the PhD thesis of Ms Kun Zheng, who graduated with a PhD degree in Sep 2018 and is now working as a scientist in the industrial company BYD in Shenzhen.

14301114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301114.value: In this project we showed that narcissistic self-sorting appeared to be a general phenomenon in the molecular world. Many material applications involve mixing of several molecular entities in order to achieve the desired functions. It is therefore extremely important to ensure that these molecules do not segregate into separate regions over a long period of time, which could result in a deterioration of their performance. From this research work it was revealed that tiny changes of molecular structures can deter the self-assembling process. Hence it is of practical interest to investigate what structural factors and molecular mechanisms that can deter or prevent the narcissistic self-sorting process.

14301114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301114.value: Many material applications rely on how the various molecular components interact with each other in a mixture. In this project, it was found that molecules, no matter how structurally similar they are, tend to segregate themselves in a mixture. This phenomenon is named self-sorting and it can have negative impacts on materials performance. At the same time, it was also found that the extent of segregation could also be controlled by tiny structural changes on the molecules. Thus the research outcome of this work can help us how to design materials with durable performance.

14301214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301214.value: Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) is the remnant radiation of the hot early universe. In the past decade, CMB anisotropies have been measured with high precision, by a host of satellite missions as well as ground-based observatories, making it possible to extract information about the evolution and energy content of the universe to unprecedented details. For example, results by the WMAP and Planck results point to a set of cosmological parameters that are consistent with other cosmological observations at percent-level precision. It has been claimed that spatial and temporal variations of the fine structure constant were observed in quasar absorption spectroscopy data, which, if true, may call for fundamental revision of the standard models of particle physics and cosmology. We propose to make use of the high quality CMB data to constrain (or detect) spatial variations of the fine structure constant, over cosmological scale. Furthermore, in the standard CMB analysis, the cosmic reionization is assumed to occur instantaneously and isotropically. We propose to search for directional dependence of the reionization history and optical depth. If such anisotropies in reionization exist, CMB data may need to be re-analysed, and the standard cosmological parameters may need to be revised. 宇宙微波背景輻射是從早期宇宙遺留的熱輻射。在過去十年，宇宙微波背景輻射的各向異性已被一系列的觀測計劃準確量度，大大加深人們對宇宙演化及能量成份的理解。例如WMAP 及PLANCK的觀測結果，指向準確度達至百分之一程度的宇宙參數。我們計劃利用這些高質素的宇宙微波背景輻射數據，來約束或測量精细结構常數在宇宙尺度的空間變化。我們亦會找尋宇宙再電離的歷史及光學厚度的各向異性，以判斷標準微波背景輻射數據分析- 以及從而獲得的宇宙參數 -是否可靠。

14301214.label: Realisation of objectives
14301214.value: Objective 1: Search for/constrain spatial variation of the fine structure constant from high precision cosmic microwave background data Both the WMAP 9-year and PLANCK 2015 cosmic microwave background (CMB) data have been analysed as a function of different fractions of the sky map, to search for or constrain spatial variations of the fine structure constant α, both with or without varying other cosmological parameters at the same time. For the WMAP 9-year data, we find that α has significant directional variations, by up to +0.5% and -0.7% in the two extreme directions, with uncertainties of 0.3%, when other cosmological parameters are fixed. However, when α is varied together with all other cosmological parameters, its directional variations are within the uncertainties and therefore constrained to 0.3% level. We applied an extra hemispherical mask, to block off half of the sky centering on 12 different directions and analyzed the PLANCK 2015 data, varying the standard cosmological parameters, with or without varying α together. There is a significant deviation of α between the directions of the 1st and 11th pixels, corresponding to the directions in galactic coordinates of (b = 41.81°, l = 45.00°) and (b = 41.81°, l = 225.00°), with the best-fit values of α differing from the standard value αo by -0.17% and +0.11% respectively. The two posterior distributions of β = α/αo -1 for these two directions differ by 3σ, representing a serious tension. Furthermore, several other cosmological parameters show 2-3 σ variations as well, including the Hubble parameter Ho, spectral index ns and the cosmological baryon Ωbh^2 and dark matter densities Ωch^2. In particular, Ho in unit of km/s/Mpc have means of 63.5 and 71.2 and standard deviations of 2.1 and 2.4 in the directions of pixels 1 and 11 respectively, a 2.4 σ difference. The best-fit values of ns are 1.009 (±0.018) and 0.943 (±0.015) in these two directions, a 2.9 σ difference. Ωbh^2 and Ωch^2 all show spatial variations by more than 2 σ. The directional variations of β, ns, Ho, Ωbh^2 and Ωch^2 (relative to the full-sky results) all follow a dipole form Acosθ +B, where θ is the angle to the best-fit dipole axis. The confidence levels of dipole magnitudes of β and ns are 99.9% and 99.8% respectively. The best-fit dipole axes for β, ns, Ωch^2, Ho, and reionization optical depth τ_re all align within 1-σ uncertainties, pointing to the direction of V= (b = −33.2 ± 15.5°, l = 211.6 ± 19.2°). The dipole axes for Ωbh^2 and ln(10^10As) are also aligned with each other, but they are perpendicular to V. Our results may suggest either new physics, or previously unknown systematic errors in the standard CMB analysis. As an example of the latter, we study implications of a non-zero neutrino degeneracy ξ (assumed to be zero in standard CMB analysis) on cosmological parameters. We found correlations between ξ and H0, as well as between ξ and the tensor-to-scalar parameter r. We therefore conclude that possible neutrino degeneracy should not be ignored in CMB data analyses. Objective 2: Search for/constrain spatial variation of the reionization history from high precision cosmic microwave background data In standard CMB analyses, the reionization history is parameterized by the reionization optical depth τ_re. We find that the WMAP CMB temperature angular power spectrum depend strongly on τ_re. The anisotropies of τ_re are reduced significantly when an extra galactic cut is applied, which suggests that they are related to local structures (foreground). In the PLANCK 2015 data, we find maximum 1.4 σ difference in the best-fit values of τ_re in the different directions, much less deviations than those in α and Ho. If α is fixed to the standard value, the spatial variation of τ_re is reduced to 1.2 σ only. We therefore conclude that there is no significant directional dependence in the reionization history shown by the PLANCK 2015 data. Both objectives 1 and 2 have been realized fully.

14301214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301214.value: 1. We find that the directional variations of the WMAP CMB temperature power depend strongly on the reionization optical depth τ_re. The anisotropies of τ_re are reduced significantly when an extra galactic cut is applied, which suggests that they are related to local structures. This result was submitted to APJ, but the referee wanted us to analyze the Planck data instead. 2. We find significant directional dependence of β, ns, Ho, Ωbh^2 and Ωch^2 in the Planck 2015 data, at 2-3 σ level. The directional variations of β, ns, Ho, Ωbh^2 and Ωch^2 all follow a dipole form Acosθ +B, where θ is the angle to the best-fit dipole axis. The confidence levels of dipole magnitudes of β and ns are 99.9% and 99.8% respectively. The best-fit dipole axes for β, ns, Ωch^2, Ho, and τ_re all align within 1-σ, pointing to the direction of V= (b = −33.2 ± 15.5°, l = 211.6 ± 19.2°). The dipole axes for Ωbh^2 and ln(10^10As) are also aligned with each other, but they are perpendicular to V. A paper has been submitted to PRL [4]. 3. Our results suggest unknown systematics in standard CMB fittings. We thus studied the implications of a non-zero neutrino degeneracy ξ on cosmological parameters extracted from CMB data. We discovered correlations between ξ and Ho, and ξ and ns in CMB fittings. The current CMB+BAO data are not sensitive enough to determine the value of ξ. Therefore, ξ can be considered to be a non-negligible systematic uncertainty in the cosmological parameters extracted from CMB. A paper has been submitted to PRD [2]. 4. Since Ho depends on the dark energy, we investigated the impacts of dark energy on constraining the total neutrino mass. We considered the wCDM and HDE models, both having an additional free parameter compared with ΛCDM. We analyzed the Planck 2015 CMB temperature and polarization data, combined with BAO distance scales, type Ia supernovae, H0, and Planck lensing. Compared to the ΛCDM model, the upper limit on the sum of neutrino masses becomes much looser in the wCDM model but tighter in the HDE model. This result has been published in PRD [3]. 5. We study whether the preferred axis in 2 above could be due to a net rotation of our local halo. We find a universal angular momentum profile for cold dark matter halos. A paper has been published in APJ [5].

14301214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301214.value: 1. Our finding that the Hubble parameter has a surprisingly strong directional dependence 63.5 and 71.2 (km/s/Mpc) may lead to a resolution of the tension between the CMB and local measurements of Ho. It may be a result of directional dependence of cosmological parameters, especially dark matter or dark energy density. The unexpected dipole form of the directional dependences of β, ns, Ho, Ωbh^2 and Ωch^2 should be checked further with other cosmological observations. This is an interesting result that should be followed up. It represents possible new physics, or suggests the existence of previously unknown systematic uncertainties in the standard CMB analysis. 2. We have only made use of CMB temperature data so far. The high quality Planck CMB polarization data should also be analyzed for possible directional dependence. 3. Our result that a non-zero neutrino asymmetry (assumed zero in standard CMB analysis) have significant implications on H0 and inflationary parameters should be followed up, particularly since CMB is considered to be an important observational tool to study/constrain inflationary cosmological models. Whether neutrino asymmetry can lead to the directional dependence of cosmological parameters and fine structure constant should also be investigated.

14301214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301214.value: In the standard model of cosmology, the thermal radiations produced in the hot and dense early universe decoupled during the recombination epoch, when neutral atoms formed at around 400,000 years since the Big Bang. These photons free-streamed to us, their wavelengths red-shifted by about a thousand times due to the expansion of the universe, to form the cosmic microwave background (CMB), which carry information about the state of the early universe, and it is possible to put tight constraints on deviations from standard physics models over cosmological scale using high precision CMB data. We made use of the high quality CMB data by both the WMAP and PLANCK missions to search for directional variations of the fine structure constant α and cosmological parameters. Surprisingly, we find significant directional dependence in α, Hubble parameter, and several other cosmological parameters. They all follow a dipole form of distribution with a seemingly preferred direction. These suggest either new physics, or unknown systematic errors in the analysis of the CMB data. As one possible example of the latter, we study implications of degeneracy of cosmological neutrinos on cosmological parameters extracted from CMB data, and conclude that it may indeed lead to significant systematic errors.

14301314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301314.value: The aim of the proposed research is to develop an efficient and accurate reconstruction algorithm for the recovery of a metric tensor and irregular obstacles in a bounded domain by using incomplete boundary data. Given an initial point on the boundary, a family of geodesics, parametrized by the shooting directions pointing inside the domain, can be defined by using the metric tensor. The inverse problem considered in this project is the reconstruction of a metric tensor by the scattering relation, which consists of the lengths of the geodesics, the entering and the leaving boundary points and directions. The main challenge in the design of numerical methods is multifold. In most practical cases, the metric tensor is highly heterogeneous. Moreover, the domain of interest may contain unknown obstacles which may possibly be concave. Furthermore, the boundary data is usually incomplete, meaning that data are only observed on a subset of the boundary. Traditional computational methods can only solve the above inverse problem for slowly varying and continuous metric tensors with complete data as well as the situation when the domain does not contain any obstacle. These methods are unable to handle the above-mentioned cases and there is very limited research addressing the above issues. In this project, we will develop a novel adaptive phase space method for the simultaneous reconstruction of metric tensors in a domain equipped with highly heterogeneous coefficients and irregular unknown obstacles by incomplete boundary data. Moreover, plenty of numerical simulations will be conducted to validate the accuracy and efficiency the proposed numerical reconstruction algorithm. The proposed research will provide a numerical scheme that can accurately and efficiently recover a metric tensor and irregular obstacles in a bounded domain using only incomplete boundary data. By using an innovative characterization of geodesics, the measurement data can be classified as broken and non-broken, which correspond respectively to geodesics with and without reflections by the obstacles. The non-broken geodesics are first used to reconstruct the convex hulls of obstacles and the broken geodesics are then used to recover the concave parts of the obstacles. In addition, based on a recent advance in boundary rigidity problem, we develop a local reconstruction algorithm for the metric tensor. The method allows the reconstruction of the metric tensor in a layer-by-layer fashion, giving a huge saving in computational times and costs. Consequently, the proposed scheme gives a breakthrough in travel time tomography. 本次的研究在於設計一個高效精確的重建法， 從而在邊界條件不完整的情況下對存在不規則障礙物的有界區域的度量張量進行重建。 根據邊界上的起點， 我們可以通過度量張量生成一簇指向測量區域內部的測地線。該項目的目的在於通過測地線的散射關係來重建有界區域的度量張量。 其中散射關係指的是測地線的長度， 測地線進入和離開有界區域的位置以及方向。項目的主要難點在於如何設計一個廣泛適用的數值方法。 因為在多數情況下， 有界區域的度量張量是各項異性的， 同時估算區域可能包含未知障礙物或邊界條件可能是不完善的。 然而傳統的算法只能處理度量張量平滑變化同時邊界條件完整的情況。 面對前面提出的難點，傳統算法顯然是不適用的。然而， 對于如何解決這個難點的研究目前仍然十分少見。 本項目中， 我們將設計一種相空間上自適的新穎算法， 用來對存有未知障礙物且邊界條件不完善的各向異性區域的度量張量進行重建。同時， 我們將進行大量的數值試驗來驗證新算法的準確性和高效性。 本次的研究將首先提出對存有未知障礙物且邊界條件不完整的各向異性區域的度量張量重建的數值算法。 通過運用對測地線的創新性分類， 測量數據可以被分為折斷性和非折斷性兩類， 分別對測地線應存在反射和不存在反射兩種情況。 其中非折斷性測地線將用來重建未知障礙物的凸包， 而折斷性測地線將用來重建未知障礙物的凹陷部分。 更重要的是， 根據關於邊界剛性問題的研究的最新進展， 我們設計了局部度量張量重建算法。 這個算法可以讓我們實現度量張量逐層重建， 這將會極大地減少時間和花費。總的來說， 本項目提出的算法將會是走時成像技術領域的一個突破性成果。

14301314.label: Realisation of objectives
14301314.value: The objectives of the proposal are fully achieved. The proposed method combines several advances in mathematics and numerical analysis, and achieves the proposed objectives. One key feature of the method is a layer-by-layer idea. This idea allows one to incorporate boundary data adaptively, and only uses those that are available. This idea also makes the computations very efficient. The method can also handles obstacle naturally by incorporating some suitable jump conditions. This is due to the ray based nature of the proposed numerical method. Finally the computation of the unknown metric is achieved by combing several steps, namely a convergent Neumann series for the inversion of geodesic transforms for each local region, a layer stripping approach as well as an optimization approach for the linearized Stefanov-Uhlmann identity. All these, together with an appropriately chosen regularization allow the success of the method.

14301314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301314.value: A brand new numerical procedure is developed for the determination of the required unknowns. The new method is based on two major steps. In the first step, a numerical procedure is developed to find an unknown function using its integral along geodesics. The method is based on the use of a convergent Neumann series and a layer-by-layer reconstruction technique. In fact, the layer-by-layer technique allows one to find the solution locally in each small region in each layer. The resulting algorithm is very efficient and accurate. In the second major step, a nonlinear problem is solved to obtain the required unknown metric. This is based on a linearization of the nonlinear model, and then use the idea in the first step together with an iterative process. The resulting scheme is efficient and accurate. Some tests using benchmark test cases are performed, and these results show the excellent performance of the proposed techniques.

14301314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301314.value: There are certainly some potential for further research. One possibility is to test the proposed method using real data. Another possibility is to apply some upscaling techniques in order to further speed up the computations. In fact, some of these ideas have been explored. One more possibility is to apply the technique to another related model of wave type.

14301314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301314.value: In seismic exploration, one needs to determine the inner structure of the earth by using seismic signal obtained from the surface of the earth. Another example is ultra-sound imaging in which data are obtained on the surface of body. These signals are typically in the form of travel time information, and one needs to use the travel time data is reconstruction earth structure. The problem is a complicated one as the computation is very intensive, and some type of fast techniques are needed. In this project, a new solver is developed. The solver is based on some recent advances in mathematical analysis, and allows one to solve the problem efficiently and accurately. We anticipate that the method gives a great potential in the development in practical tools in various kinds of applications in which boundary data is involved.

14302014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302014.value: 人為的二氧化碳排放是全球表面平均溫度從二十世紀中開始上升的主要原因。全球森林被視為陸地的碳匯，能抵銷部分因燃燒化石燃料所造成的碳排放。但是未來氣候變化有可能把森林轉為一個淨碳源，導致氣候及碳循環的正反饋，繼而加速暖化。土壤呼吸由自養及異養呼吸所組成，每年其總二氧化碳排放量比燃燒化石燃料的貢獻高出十倍，故可對全球碳循環構成重大影響。過往大部分研究以手動氣箱不頻繁的測量土壤呼吸，因此未能取得高時間解析度的數據以分析於不同時間尺度的主要環境控制因子。迄今為止，有關亞洲亞熱界次生林土壤呼吸動態的研究仍較缺乏。 本研究旨在：﹝甲﹞量化香港一亞熱界次生林土壤呼吸的強度及自養呼吸對總呼吸量的貢獻；﹝乙﹞研究次生林土壤呼吸在日夜、季節及年際的時間變化及其環境控制因子；及﹝丙﹞調查實驗性增溫對次生林土壤呼吸的影響。本研究將進行挖壕及增溫實驗，並設立一套自動氣箱系統每小時持續監測土壤呼吸。此外，本研究會同時於田野測量一些輔助環境參數以研究它們與土壤呼吸隨時間變化的關係。 本研究所得的結果將有助揭示土壤於亞熱界次生林碳循環中所扮演的角色。透過使用自動氣箱系統，土壤呼吸於不同時間尺度的變化能被量化，以準確計算出全年土壤呼吸總量。另外，本研究建立的土壤呼吸及其環境控制的關係，能改善土壤呼吸於森林及全球碳循環模型的參數設定。田野操控實驗的結果能幫助了解氣候變化如何影響土壤呼吸的速率及敏感性，進而改變氣候及碳循環反饋的強度。

14302014.label: Realisation of objectives
14302014.value: This project involved the establishment of an automatic chamber system with a warming set-up for investigating the impacts of experimental warming on soil respiration in a subtropical secondary forest. Initially we encountered difficulties in securing a suitable field site that was easily accessible by research personnel and supported by a reliable supply of AC power. After an extended search, we identified a suitable location for our field research and subsequently installed all the infrastructure for the continuous monitoring of soil respiration. Since then, we were able to measure the rate of soil respiration quasi-continuously from 20 different plots in a subtropical secondary forest, and subsequently used the high-frequency data to investigate the variations of soil respiration over multiple temporal scales ranging from diel, seasonal, to inter-annual scales. Through the use of root trenching experiments and the continuous year-round flux measurements, we were able to quantify the annual CO2 emissions from the secondary forest, and assessed the relative contribution of autotrophic respiration to total soil respiration. By measuring various environmental variables simultaneously with soil respiration with a high temporal resolution, we were able to identify the key governing factors of the temporal variations in soil respiration. The warming experiment conducted in the field allowed us to assess the influence of increasing temperature on the rate and variability of soil respiration in the subtropical secondary forest.

14302014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302014.value: We found that the soils in our subtropical secondary forest was a net source of CO2, with an annual respiration rate of around 1760 g C m-2 year-1. Autotrophic respiration from roots was found to contribute to 21-51% of the total soil respiration (Comeau et al., 2018). Soil respiration in the forest showed a strong diurnal pattern, with a maximum rate in the late afternoon and a minimum rate in the early morning. The daily range of soil respiration was around 0.43 μmol m-2 s-1, and the diurnal variations of soil respiration closely resembled that of soil temperature. Moreover, soil respiration demonstrated significant seasonal variations, with a maximum CO2 emission observed in the summer in July and very low rates during the wintertime between December and February. Soil temperature again had an exponential relationship with soil respiration over the annual scale, while soil moisture had a rather weak relationship with soil respiration. On the other hand, the inter-annual variability of soil respiration was relatively small, and was related to volumetric soil water content. Experimental warming increased the rate of soil respiration by about 25%, indicating a positive climate-carbon cycle feedback that could contribute to further warming in future.

14302014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302014.value: Our research has generated a valuable data set of soil respiration in subtropical secondary forest ecosystems. We will share our data set with the regional and international flux network, and explore opportunities to carry out data synthesis work over a broader spatial scale to examine the response of soil respiration to changing environments. We hope to continue with the field experiments and flux measurements as far as practicable, such that the response of forest soil respiration to warming over the long term could be tested. Based on the observational data of soil respiration collected, this study calls for more detailed investigations into the mechanisms of changing respiratory activities through microbiological analyses and other advanced techniques.

14302014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302014.value: This study examines the magnitude and temporal variability of soil respiration in a subtropical secondary forest, and its response to experimental warming. Our results showed that forest soils emitted a considerable amount of CO2 into the atmosphere, with the majority of respiratory activities coming from microorganisms rather than plant roots. Soil respiration varied considerably over time at diurnal and seasonal scales, and thus high-frequency measurement is needed to produce reliable estimates. Soil temperature was a key governing factor of soil respiration, and experimental warming was shown to increase soil respiration by microorganisms significantly. This enhanced CO2 release by soils in response to warming can produce a vicious cycle and a positive feedback that further accelerates climate warming in future.

14302114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302114.value: 微衛星DNA中不穩定的髮夾結構DNA序列能否形成啞鈴結構 - DNA重複序列突變的一種新型潛在途徑？

14302114.label: Project Objectives
14302114.value: To determine if variations of the repeat lengths will lead to dumbbell structures formed by TTTA and AAAT repeats. The onset of several diseases has been found to associate with tandem repeat expansions. For example, when the repeat length of TTTA in CYP19A1 gene located in chromosome 15 of the human genome is above 10, there will be a higher risk of breast cancer in female. It will be interesting to see if there will be difference in the solution structural behaviors of TTTA and AAAT repeats at different repeat lengths. Although TTTA and AAAT cannot form stable loops, a longer repeat of TTTA and AAAT may allow the formation of the higher order dumbbell structure through the improved stability in the stem region by allowing more TA or AT base pairs and a better 3’-5’ coaxial stacking. At present, it remains unclear if a longer repeat can facilitate a less stable hairpin-forming sequence to fold into a more stable dumbbell structure. The minimum repeat length to form a stable dumbbell may reflect the threshold of repeat length that may lead to expansion or contraction mutations. To determine if different types of loop closing base pairs and stem lengths will lead to formation of dumbbell structures with TTTA or AAAT loops. In addition to tetranucleotide microsatellites, TTTA and AAAT can be mixed with other types of bases in 5 to 9mer microsatellites to form dumbbell structures with different loop closing base pairs and stem lengths. These variations allow tuning of the stability of the resulting dumbbell structures. In general, TTTA or AAAT embedded in 5 to 9mer microsatellites containing more C or G will result in dumbbell structures which are more stable than those formed from microsatellites containing more A or T. However, the same situation will also apply to the hairpin structure formed by these repeats. At present, it remains unclear whether a more or less stable closing base pair and stem will favor the formation of the higher order dumbbell structure. A systematic investigation of the closing base pair and stem length effects will improve our understanding of the relationship between dumbbell formation and sequence context. To determine how different types of 3’ and 5’ coaxial stackings affect the formation of dumbbell structures with TTTA or AAAT loops. The 3’-5’ stack appears to be a critical source of stabilizing interactions that enhance the formation of the higher order dumbbell structures. Pending on which residue becomes the starting 5’-terminal residue, the same dumbbell structures with different types of 3’-5’ stacks can be formed from different types of microsatellites. It will be interesting to know how these other types of microsatellites affect the formation of dumbbell structure through introducing a different 3’-5’ stack to the dumbbell structure. For TTTA or AAAT embedded in the longest 9mer microsatellites, there are a total of six groups of 3’-5’stacks. A complete study of these different stacks helps to understand their roles in governing the relative stabilities and thus the formation of dumbbell structures.

14302114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302114.value: This project aims to determine if less stable DNA hairpin-forming sequences in microsatellites can fold into a more stable and higher order dumbbell structure. Specifically, we will determine the sequence requirements for the formation of dumbbells with TTTA or AAAT loops. It is now well known that mutations do not arise randomly in the genome sequences and spontaneous mutagenesis depends on the context of the DNA sequences. Tandem repeats (TRs) is one type of such hypermutational sequences. The presence of TRs with 9 repeating unit bases or fewer, also known as microsatellites, can affect gene products and gene regulation when they are localized in coding and non-coding regions, respectively. The microsatellite instability due to DNA expansion or contraction has been proposed to be related to the formation of non-B form secondary structures such as hairpin. The exceptionally stable hairpin-forming sequences are abundant in the human genome but they are rare in microsatellites, suggesting the culprit of microsatellite instability may be due to a novel secondary structure rather than hairpin. Recent findings show that the formation of a dumbbell structures stabilizes the slipped hairpin structure of CCTG repeats and thereby increases the formation propensity of unusual structure. Tandem repeat analysis also reveals that TTTA and ATTT are the two most abundant tetranucleotide microsatellites in the human genome. Yet it remains elusive if these microsatellites can fold into a dumbbell structure. In this project, we propose to perform nuclear magnetic resonance structural investigations on the solution structural behaviors of TTTA and AAAT repeats in microsatellites through (i) the variations of repeat length, (ii) different types of loop closing base pairs and stem lengths, and (iii) different types of 3’-5’ coaxial stacking so as to determine if these less stable hairpin-forming sequences in microsatellites can fold into a dumbbell structure. The higher order dumbbell structure may appear to be a novel DNA secondary structure that leads to DNA expansion or contraction during DNA replication, providing an alternative mechanistic pathway for TR variations. The long term impact will improve our understandings of the origin of the diseases that are related to dumbbell-forming sequences in microsatellites and provide us a structural target for designing therapeutics to inhibit DNA expansion or contraction, thereby controlling the chance of genetic mutations and/or the effect on gene regulation and transcription. 該課題旨在研究微衛星DNA中不穩定的髮夾結構DNA序列能否形成更穩定的高級啞鈴結構。我們將具體研究形成具有TTTA或AAAT環的啞鈴結構DNA的序列要求。 眾所周知，基因組序列的突變並不是隨機發生的，自發的基因突變通常與DNA序列上下文有關。 DNA重複序列是一種具有高突變率的序列。 重複單元小於或等於9的序列被稱為微衛星DNA。 當微衛星DNA位於編碼區或非編碼區時，它們可能會分別影響基因產物或參與基因調控。 研究指出，非B型二級結構DNA （例如髮夾結構）的形成與DNA重複序列的增加或減少變異有關，從而導致微衛星DNA的不穩定性。 然而，那些形成高穩定髮夾結構的序列在微衛星DNA中的存在頻率很低，說明微衛星DNA的不穩定性可能由另一種新型的DNA二級結構導致，而並非髮夾結構DNA。 近期研究表明CCTG DNA重複序列可形成啞鈴結構, 令CCTG重複序列的滑移髮夾結構更加穩定， 從而增強了DNA異常結構的形成趨勢。 對人類基因組的DNA重複序列的分析發現，TTTA和AAAT是四核苷酸微衛星中頻率最高的兩種序列。 然而，這些微衛星DNA序列能否形成高級的啞鈴結構尚不清楚，有待進一步研究證明。 在該課題中，我們計劃利用核磁共振結構分析來研究含有TTTA或AAAT序列的微衛星DNA在溶液中的結構和行為。 我們將通過三個方面來研究不穩定的髮夾結構DNA序列能否形成啞鈴狀結構：（1）改變重複序列的長度；（2）採用不同類型的閉環堿基對和莖長度；（3）採用不同類型的3’- 5’末端同軸堆疊堿基對。 高級的啞鈴結構可能會成為一種新型的DNA二級結構，導致DNA複製過程中重複序列的增加或減少，為重複序列的變異提供另一種潛在機制。 該研究課題長遠的影響體現在：一方面提高人們對同啞鈴結構DNA有關疾病的病源認識，另一方面為研究者提供一個結構目標，有利於他們設計治療方案來抑制DNA序列的增加或減少變異， 從而控制基因突變，基因轉錄和基因調控等過程。

14302114.label: Realisation of objectives
14302114.value: In this project, all three objectives have been achieved successfully. For the first objective, high resolution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic investigations have been conducted to study TTTA and AAAT repeats. The results show that a novel minidumbbell (MDB) structure is formed in TTTA but not AAAT repeats (see Section 8, item 1). The MDB comprises two type II tetraloops, in which the first and fourth residues form a loop closing base pair, the second residue folds into the minor groove interacting with another minor groove residue of the other loop, and the third residue stacks on the loop closing base pair. In addition, variations of the repeat lengths have also been studied by NMR. The MDB structure was observed also in longer TTTA repeats and a competing MDB mechanism has been proposed to explain how repeat expansion mutation occurs during DNA replication (see Section 8, items 1 and 4). For the second objective, different types of loop closing base pairs and stem lengths have also been studied by high resolution NMR spectroscopy. Our results reveal that in addition to TTTA repeats which can form a MDB with TA loop closing base pairs, CCTG repeats can also fold into a MDB with CG Watson-Crick base pairs (see Section 8, item 2). Solution structures of these TTTA and CCTG MDBs have been determined by NMR and restrained molecular dynamics (rMD) calculations. These structures show all fundamental stabilizing interactions required for the formation of MDBs. Among these, the stabilizing forces between the minor groove residues from each of the loops are indispensable (see Section 8, item 3 and Section 10, item 1). Such loop-loop interactions between the minor groove residues have not been observed in longer stem length dumbbell structures. For the third objective, through studying the high resolution MDB structures determined by NMR and rMD, the 3’ and 5’ coaxial stacking was found to be very important in maintaining these highly compact structures formed by only eight residues (see Section 8, item 3) . We have demonstrated that both 3’-A stacking on 5’-T and 3’-G stacking on 5’-C can bring about the formation of MDBs. In addition, upon lowering the pH, a 5’-C can be protonated to become a 5’-C+. We have found by NMR and ultra-violet absorption spectroscopy that an unusually stable MDB can be formed with a stack between 3’-G and 5’-C+ (see Section 8, item 5). Based on a systematic study of all possible types of non-repeating type II loop sequences with T-A or C-G loop closing base pairs, other combinations of coaxial stacking have also been studied using native gel electrophoresis and one-dimensional 31P NMR spectroscopy (see Section 10, item 2). The results reveal these different types of stacking bring out the formation of MDBs with different thermodynamic stabilities and provide a better understanding of the sequence criteria for the formation of MDBs.

14302114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302114.value: TTTA repeats show the capabilities to fold into a novel type of DNA secondary structures, called minidumbbell (MDB) (see Section 8, item 1). The MDB comprises two type II tetraloops, in which the first and fourth residues form a loop closing base pair, the second residue folds into the minor groove interacting with another minor groove residue of the other loop, and the third residue stacks on the loop closing base pair. This novel structure has been proposed to be a structural intermediate that leads to TTTA repeat expansions during DNA replication, affecting the biofilm production in Staphylococcus aureus. In addition, two CCTG repeats have also been found to form this novel MDB structure (see Section 8, item 2), providing a possible mechanistic pathway for CCTG repeat expansion of myotonic dystrophy type 2 (DM2) disease in human. To better understand how short chain DNA strands containing only eight residues can fold into these highly compact MDB structures, solution structures of the MDBs formed by TTTA and CCTG repeats were determined, respectively (see Section 8, item 3), revealing all fundamental stabilizing interactions embedded in these structures. Based on this type of tiny structure, a novel repeat expansion pathway based on competing MDBs was proposed, providing new views on how strand slippage and escape repair can occur during DNA replication (see Section 8, item 4). Upon lowering the pH, an unusually stable MDB can be formed by two repeats of CCTG with cytosine protonation of the first two residues (see Section 8, item 5). This extraordinarily stable MDB shows the potential to be used as a simple and efficient pH-controlled molecular switch.

14302114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302114.value: The novel MDB structure provides a new structural and recognition target for further development of drugs. Potentially, these drugs will help to regulate repeat expansions that affect biofilm formation in Staphylococcus aureus and DM2 in human. In addition, the extraordinarily stable MDB formed by CCTG repeats in acidic conditions shows the potential for further development of pH-controlled molecular switches. Further efforts can be put on studying DNA-drug interaction studies and applying the MDB as a structural motif in DNA nanotechnology.

14302114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302114.value: The outcomes of this project reveal new views that short DNA sequences are not necessarily unstructured but can fold into a stable structure. The new type of DNA secondary structure, the minidumbbell (MDB), can serve as a structural intermediate that can lead to DNA expansion mutations during DNA replication. The new proposed mechanistic pathway provides a new target for developing therapeutics that can control the drug resistance behavior of Staphylococcus aureus and the onset of myotonic dystrophy type 2 disease.

14302214.label: Project Objectives
14302214.value: We will investigate the hyperbolicity of augmented trees that represent self-similar sets. We intend to classify such graphs through their graph structure. The classification and the hyperbolic boundaries will be used to study the Lipschitz equivalence of the self-similar sets. We call a Markov chain on an augmented tree admissible if the Martin boundary of the chain can be identified with the underlying self-similar set. We will study the admissible Markov chains, and the induced harmonic functions and harmonic measures on the self-similar sets. These will relate to the well-known problem on the existence of Laplacian on self-similar sets; non-local Dirichlet forms will also arise in such consideration and will be investigated. Recently there is a lot of interest in the geometry of graphs and their applications, and curvature is one of the major notions under investigation. We will adopt such consideration on the augmented trees, and explore the limit behavior on the hyperbolic boundaries. We will compare this discrete approximation with a known theory of fractal curvature measure, which is a continuous version by $epsilon$-neighborhood approximation in the Euclidian space.

14302214.label: Realisation of objectives
14302214.value: In the 80's, Gromov extracted a fundamental structure of thin triangle in hyperbolic geometry and defined the notion of hyperbolic graph on countable sets. By introducing certain metric on the graph, its completion gives a hyperbolic boundary. This setup has been used extensively to study the geometry of discrete groups and their limit behavior at the boundary. One of the main achievements in this project is to build a hyperbolic structure on self-similar sets. A self-similar set has a symbolic representation of its cells and forms a tree. We prove that by adding new edges to the tree of neighboring cells, we obtain an augmented tree which is hyperbolic, and the self-similar set is H"older equivalent to the hyperbolic boundary. The importance of this result is that if we run a reversible transient random walk on a hyperbolic graph, then the limits of the sample paths, called Martin boundary, is homeomorphic to the hyperbolic boundary, and hence also homeomorphic to the self-similar sets under consideration. It is well-known that in the study of Markov chains, there is a discrete potential theory to investigate the harmonic structure, Laplacian and energy of the system. We can therefore transfer this theory onto self-similar sets. In this regard, our contribution is to investigate a special class of random walk on the augmented tree that have return ratio $lambda$; the corresponding energy on the graph will induce a non-local regular Dirichlet form on the self-similar set. Through the hyperbolic structure, we obtain an explicit expression of the kernel of the Dirichlet form, which is corresponding to a fractional Laplacian.
