14302214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302214.value: (Note: the reference in the following are in Part 7, Peer-reviewed journal publications) 1. For any contractive iterated function system (IFS, including the Moran systems), we showed that there is a (Gromov) hyperbolic graph (X,E) (augmented tree) on the symbolic space, which yields a H"older equivalence of the hyperbolic boundary and the invariant set K of the IFS [1]. This completes some previous studies by eliminating the superfluous conditions, and admits more classes of sets (e.g., the Moran sets). We used this to study the Lipschitz equivalence of self-similar sets. We also showed that the bounded degree property of the graphs can be used to characterize certain separation properties of the IFS (open set condition, weak separation condition); the bounded degree property is particularly important when we consider random walks on such graphs. 2. On the augmented tree $(X,E)$ in the last paragraph, we introduced certain reversible random walks with return ratio $0 < lambda < 1$ [2]. We showed that the Martin boundary M can be identified with the hyperbolic boundary and K. With this setup and a device of Silverstein, we were able to obtain precise estimates of the Martin kernel and the Naim kernel in terms of the Gromov product. The Naim kernel turns out to be a jump kernel $Theta(x,y) approx |x-y|^{-(alpha+beta)}$ where $alpha$ is the Hausdorff dimension of K and $beta$ depends on $lambda$. For suitable $beta$, the kernel defines a non-local Dirichlet form on K. This provides a natural way to consider the fractional Laplacian $(-Delta)^{beta/2}$ on self-similar sets. It also extends a consideration of Kigami, where he investigated random walks on a trees with Cantor type sets as boundaries. 3. In another direction, we considered a homogeneous IFS that satisfies the open set condition (OSC), and study the subclass $F_K$ of the IFS that generated the same self-similar sets K [3]. This phenomenon occurs very often in the fractal formation. We call the IFSs in $F_K$ isotopic, and give the isotopic class $F_K$ a multiplication operation defined by composition. By using a new technique on the OSC, we proved that $F_K$ is finitely generated if either (i) K is totally disconnected, or (ii) the convex hull Co(K) is a polytope, and there exists a line L passing through a vertex of Co(K) such that $L cap K$ is a totally disconnected infinite set. These conditions are easy to check and are satisfied by many standard self-similar sets. 4. The "hot spot" conjecture concerns an observation that a heat current on a domain will spread out, and the hot spot will drift to the boundary. This phenomena is closely related to the behavior of the eigenfunction of the second eigenvalue of the heat equation. Although the hot spots conjecture was proved to be false on some classical domains, the problem still generates a lot of interests on identifying the domains that the conjecture holds. The question can also be asked on fractal sets that admit Laplacians. It is known that the conjecture holds on the Sierpinski gasket and its variants. In [4], we show surprisingly that the hot spots conjecture fails on the hexagasket, a typical nested fractal set. The technique we use is the spectral decimation method of eigenvalues of Laplacian on fractals.

14302214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302214.value: In this research, we concentrate on the self-similar sets, which does not include the classical domains. Recently, we discover that on a compact space of homogenous type K, there is a refining net of partitions of $K$, which gives a hyperbolic augmented tree, and our consideration of the boundary theories can be applied to those sets. The class of space of homogenous type is very broad, it covers the classical domains, Reimannian manifolds, and the fractal sets called d-sets, it has been studied in harmonic analysis for a long time. This consideration will unify the contempory and classical treatment, and will greatly enrich the scope of our study. The non-local Dirichlet forms arisen in our study has the class of Besov spaces as its domain. The parameter $beta$ in the expression of the Dirichlet form is interesting; it depends on the return ratio of the random walk, and the domain can be trivial when $beta$ is large. The critical $beta$ is the largest value that the Besov space is non-trivial, it carries a lot of important information of the underlying set, but is still poorly understood. We will take special attention of this in the future study.

14302214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302214.value: The boundary theories study objects and behaviors of some processes approach to or at infinity. A self-similar set is the boundary of an iterated function system, a hyperbolic boundary is the boundary of a hyperbolic graph, and a Martin boundary is the boundary of a random walk; each one has its own characteristic structure. In this study, we are able to link these three important boundaries together and obtain a natural approach to investigate the energy forms (Dirichlet forms) on the self-similar sets, which extends some well-known results of Dirichlet forms on Euclidean domains.

14302714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302714.value: Geometry of special holonomy is the study of spaces with rich algebraic structures. Calabi-Yau manifolds and G_2 manifolds are examples of such. These spaces play very important roles in mathematics. They also arise naturally as internal spaces in string theory, M-theory and F-theory in physics. The principal investigator plans to continue his studies on the geometry of spaces of geometric cycles on these manifolds. This includes symmetry properties, natural flat bundle structures, DT4 invariants, relative theory and so on. 和樂群的幾何是研究有豐富代數結構的空間。卡拉比丘流形和G2流形是其中的例子。這些空間在數學中扮演非常重要的角色。它們也是弦理論,M理論和F理論中自然出現的內部空間。 主研究員計劃繼續他在這些空間的幾何探討,包括對稱性,平坦叢結構,DT4 不變量和有關的理論。

14302714.label: Realisation of objectives
14302714.value: The PI has obtained important results on the geometry of special cycles in manifolds with special holonomy, including Calabi-Yau fourfolds, G2 manifolds and hyperkahler manifolds. In joint work with Yalong Cao, we studied the moduli spaces of these calibrated cycles and used them to construct Donaldson-Thomas invariants. We also related them to other geometric structures via mirror symmetry. For other type of special geometry, like hyperkahler geometry or G2 geometry, we also have deepened our understanding. This includes a mathematical construction of Rozansky-Witten theory on hyperkahler manifolds, also Plucker type formulas for Mukai flops of hyperkahler manifolds.

14303014.label: Project Objectives
14303014.value: Characterization of critical non-Hermitian quantum systems. We will systematically study the eigen modes and evolutions of non-Hermitian quantum systems and identify the critical points in the parameter space where catastrophic phenomena (such as mode bifurcation and instability) occur. The critical scaling behaviors of the mode frequencies, amplitudes, and phase/amplitude fluctuations will be thoroughly investigated. Ultrasensitive metrology schemes based on critical non-Hermitian quantum systems. We will investigate the dependence of the eigen modes of non-Hermitian systems as functions of external parameters near the critical points. The susceptibility to external parameters will be studied for quantum metrology. Design and simulation of realistic physical systems for proof-of-principles applications, such as ultrasensitive displacement metrology and magnetometry.

14303014.value: 超靈敏測量在基礎研究和技術應用方面都有重要意義。提高測量靈敏度的最前沿研究已經遇到量子極限。應用量子壓縮態和糾纏態可以將標準量子極限提高到海森堡極限。量子態在環境噪音下卻十分脆弱。動力學去耦則可以抑制環境噪音並同時增強探測目標之微弱信號或其特徵噪聲。基於受動力學去耦保護量子相干性的超靈敏磁探測已有理論設計並在實驗上得到演示。然而，除了退相干之外，量子探針還受能量耗散的影響，這構成量子探測的瓶頸。 本項目致力於發展一套新的超靈敏量子探測路線。其主要思想來自一個新發現的量子現象，即宇稱-時間（PT）對稱。某些非厄米哈密頓量，如果具有PT對稱， 可以具有實本徵值。更一般言之，一個具有耗散的量子系統可以被泵浦到一個穩定的本徵模式。非厄米系統的一個重要特性是在模式分支和失穩處的臨界點。該臨界行為對外界微擾極為敏感。因此非厄米系統的臨界響應可以用於超靈敏探測。 在本項目我們將研究以臨界非厄米系統進行超靈敏探測。我們將研究被泵浦的耗散系統的量子臨界行為並據此發展超靈敏探測方案。我們將設計並數值模擬實際物理系統，例如耦合腔、光機系統、以及自旋系綜等。 本項目將有助於實現原子尺度磁探測、亞原子分辨的成像、重力波探測等前沿研究，也可為耗散系統量子臨界行為的研究帶來新的思路。長遠而言，項目的研究可提供一個量子相干探測的新領域。

14303014.label: Realisation of objectives
14303014.value: We studied the coupling of a spin ensemble in diamond and a microwave cavity. The theory is formulated in the quantum Langevian equations. The eigenmodes of the systems are calculated. We ran systematic numerical simulations of the coupled systems with realistic parameters of diamond spins and the microwave cavity (including spin dephasing, spectral diffusion, random distribution of strains, temperature fluctuation, magnetic field inhomogeneity, etc). We discovered that the system would undergo a non-equilibrium phase transition to reach the masing state if proper pumping and cavity design are fulfilled. We considered the sensitivity of the microwave photon output from the maser as a function of various parameters, such as tempeature and magnetic field. We show that the actively pumped spin-cavity system provides an interesting sensing scheme. These research largely address Objective 1, 2, and 3. We formulate the quantum Fisher information theory for parameter estimation near the exceptional points of non-Hermitian systems and applied the theory to the parameter estimation of coupled cavity systems. The quantum Fisher information theory is rigorous and independent of any specific sensing schemes. The theory can be widely applied to all different kinds of non-Hermitian systems. We discovered that the state coalescence at the exceptional points (which results in vanishing state distinguishability) counteracts the divergence of the energy level susceptibility to a perturbative parameter and hence the sensitivity being a smooth function (without singularity as claimed by some recent proposals). This work largely address Objective 1 & 2. We studied the eigenmodes of a coupled system of atoms and photons. A non-equlibrium topological phase transitions (in analogue to the Haldane phases in a two-dimensional hexagonal lattice with interlaced magnetic field). Furthermore, in collaboration with Liang Jiang's group in Yale University, we proposed a scheme of homonomic quantum gates for continuous variable qubits - photons in coherent states based on engineering pump and dissipation of microwave photons in superconducting resonators. These systems provide new platforms for studying non-Hermitian physics and its metrology applications. These works partly addresses Objective 1.

14303014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303014.value: (1) We established a rigorous theory on the sensitivity of parameter estimation near the exceptional point of non-Hermitian coupled cavity systems, using the framework of quantum Fisher information. The quantum Fisher information formalism gives the lower bound of the sensitivity regardless of the specific measuring scheme. While two recent experiments claimed that the energy level susceptibility divergence at the exceptional points could lead to unlimited sensitivity of parameter estimation, out theory shows that the divergence would actually be cancelled by the vanishing state distinguishability at the exceptional point. We show that the sensitivity is a smooth function of the perturbative parameter near the exceptional point. The work is under review (preprint attached). (2) We studied an ensemble of electron spins of nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond and a high-quality microwave cavity. We found that this system, under pump and dissipation, can form macroscopic quantum coherence of spins and photons - a superradiance maser. The maser coherence is extremely sensitive to external magnetic field and cavity geometric configuration, which provides a scheme of ultrasensitive, active quantum metrology. The work is published in Nature Communications 6, 8251 (2015) and recently a group in UK has experimentally verified our proposal. (3) We studied the coupling of a spatially extended ensemble of atoms coupled to three frequency-modulated lasers. We show that this systems is equivalent to a long sought after model - the Haldane model. The single particle states and the topological phase transitions of this systems are studied. Such a system is useful for quantum simulation of condensed matter physics and for quantum metrology. The work is published in Optica 2, 712-715 (2015) as a cover story. (4) In collaboration with Liang Jiang's group in Yale University, we proposed a scheme of homonomic quantum gates for continuous variable qubits - photons in coherent states. The scheme is based on engineering pump and dissipation of microwave photons in superconducting resonators. The work is published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 140502 (2016). (5) In collaboration with the experimental group led by Patrice Bertet, we demonstrated a scheme of single photon storage in an ensemble of electron spins in diamond. The systems is suitable for studying non-Hermitian dynamics of spin wave excitations and microwave photons. The work is published as Phys. Rev. A 92, 020301(R) (2015)

14303014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303014.value: Our proposal on diamond maser has stimulated many experimental works. Theoretical studies on diamond maser, especially on the collective spin coherence will be of great interest for further studies. The quantum Fisher information formalism of parameter estimation in non-Hermitian systems can be further extended to study the cases of exceptional points in parity-symmetric systems, which corresponds to non-equilibrium phase transitions (such as lasing or masing).

14303014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303014.value: Ultrasensitive metrology is important to a wide range of basic research and applications. The state-of-the-art research on improving the sensitivity has encountered the fundamental quantum limits. Especially, dissipation of quantum probes is a bottleneck of quantum metrology. This project developed a new strategy of ultrasensitive quantum metrology, with schemes to make use of, or at least to accommodate, the dissipation instead of avoiding it. With dissipation, a quantum system’s trajectory is governed by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, which may have critical points associated with mode bifurcation and instability. The critical behaviors are extremely sensitive to external perturbation. Thus we studied critical non-Hermitian systems for ultrasensitive metrology. We designed and numerically simulated realistic physical systems such as coupled cavities, atom-photon systems, spin-cavity systems. We developed rigorous quantum Fisher information formalism. We also made a discovery of room-temperature masing in a coupled spin-cavity system with pump and dissipation – a non-equilibrium phase transition. The masing is studied for applications in metrology of temperature and magnetic fields. The outputs from this project may offer some new playgrounds of quantum coherence technology.

14303114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303114.value: 氧气的还原反应（ORR）通常指的是在电极上发生的半反应，将氧气还原成水。它是电化学之中的一个至关重要的反应，其缓慢的速率是当前限制燃料电池功率输出的主因。它又是水分子裂解的逆反应，二者之间紧密相关。了解这一反应的机制，在基础与应用研究上，特别是在清洁再生能源的发展上，有着重大的意义。ORR发生在溶液与金属界面区域，同时也受电极电势的影响，在原子微观层面上探索这一反应有相当的挑战性。在实验上，界面区域的谱学信号微弱，难以测量。在计算模拟上，有多重因素需要考虑。现有的研究之中，这些因素还未能得到系统的探索，相应的反应机理也未形成共识。 在本项目中，我们计划模拟在酸性条件下，金属铂与钯晶体表面的ORR。利用现有的高性能计算条件，我们对机理的研究将更加全面并接近真实的反应条件，在模型中不但考虑金属平板与电极电势，还考虑电解质（比如H+，及SO42-/HSO4-，ClO4-, Cl-, 或CN-）及其与水分子之间的作用。在溶液的环境之中，以多元动力学的方法探索自由能表面。以此来模拟分析在常温溶化条件下，分子的动力学作用及其对ORR的影响，取得对ORR机理更为深入的了解。

14303114.label: Realisation of objectives
14303114.value: We encountered two problems at the start of this project. The first was that the computational resources required were considerably higher than the standard HPC budget of HK$100,000. It was enough to study the solvation of electrolytes near Pt(111), but the dynamic simulations were slow. So in August of 2016, we decided to spend a big chunk of the budget to the purchase of an HPC cluster with 576 cores. After its installment, we have been able to do fairly extensive simulations on the ORR reaction, as originally planned. The second problem was that shortly after our reaction simulations started, Professor Bill Goddard's group at Caltech published the first meta-dynamic study on the oxygen reduction reactions on Pt(100). (Phys.Chem.Chem.Phys. 2017, v.19, p.2666). We tried to reproduce their results, but run into problems, as the barrier would vary considerably with the choice of collective variables and the parameters for the bias potentials employed to sample the free energy surfaces. We therefore tried instead to use thermodynamic integration to calculate the free energy, while kept trying meta-dynamics to sample the reaction channels. Eventually, we are able to identify the problems. Furthermore, by trying both thermodynamic integration and meta-dynamics sampling, interesting new features are revealed about the mechanisms of ORR on Pt(111). Thermodynamic integration By thermodynamic integration, we examined the reduction of an O2* adsorbed on Pt(111) solvated by dozens of water molecules in three acid models. In the first model, it was just a H, which became H+ automatically by losing an electron to the Pt(111) slab. This was the modeled employed in Goddard’s paper and in most of the other previous studies as well. In the second model, a HBr molecule was present, which was automatically dissociated in the interfacial region, with Br- adsorbed on Pt(111) and H+ solvated by water molecules. In the third model, a HClO4 molecule was present, which dissociated into solvated H+ and ClO4- in the interfacial region. The free energy barrier was then calculated for the O2* dissociation, OOH* formation and OH* neutralization. The O2 dissociation produced adsorbed O atoms (O*), which were reactive. Goddard and coworkers identified a hydrolysis channel before, O* + H2O* ---> OH* + OH*, (reaction 1) which was also seen in our simulation. But, with the H+ in the nearby solution, the neutralization channel O* + H(+) + e ---> OH* (reaction 2) was actually more facile than previously thought. These two channels, together with the O2* dissociation, produced three OH* adsorbed on Pt(111). The OOH* formation was found to coupled quite strongly with the O2* dissociation channel. In other words, O2* dissociation and O-H formation were often coupled, indicating that OOH* formation played a less significant role than previously thought. OH* neutralization to form H2O* was quite facile, although its free energy was close to zero, depending on the surface coverage. Energetically, it was not as favorable as previously thought. These results also demonstrate that the presence of an anion, either adsorbed on Pt(111) as in the case of Br-* or in the solution as in the case of ClO4-, makes a significant difference in the calculated barriers. Such anions should be explicitly included in the simulation of ORR in the interfacial region near a metal surface. Meta-dynamics After many trials, we were able to get to the bottom of the difference between Goddard’s and our own meta-dynamics results. The first reason was that O* produced by the O2* dissociation was quite reactive, and its product (OH*) much more stable than O*. Once OH* was formed, it’s impossible for the configuration to go back to the reactant well. As the reaction path was only sampled once, the value of the barrier was very sensitive to the parameters for the bias potential and the error in the barrier was large. The way out of it was to put an artificial big bias at O—O distance around 3 Å so that the dynamics would bounce back to the reactant well, and several rounds of back-and-forth between reactant and product wells would reduce the error in the dissociation barrier. Even with this method, one would still have to be very careful, because there were several types of adsorption sites for O*, top, bridge, and fcc. After a while, one of the O atom could get stuck in a fcc site which was less reactive. This fact didn’t show up in thermodynamic integration, because O—O distance was constrained. But it was an important factor in the less constrained meta-dynamics simulations. In fact, the meta-dynamics also showed that O2* could be tilted up, with only one end adsorbed on Pt, and the other end accepting a H+ to form OOH*. These adsorption structures could change the dissociation barrier for O2* significantly. Finding out these complicating factors for meta-dynamics also helped us understand several interesting aspects of the ORR mechanism: 1. O* does play a significant role. After O2 dissociation, either one or both the O* have a definite probability to fall into a fcc site. By focusing on O*, we were able to calculate both the hydrolysis and neutralization barriers (reaction 1 and reaction 2), which were higher than the O2 dissociation barrier. 2. We were also able to estimate the free energy change for the hydrolysis of O* for the first time, which did not contribute to the electro-chemical potential because it’s not a redox reaction. It could be responsible for part of the over-potential. 3. It’s also obvious that when O2* was tilted up, the O-O bond was strengthened. It led to the formation of OOH*, but not to the breaking of O-O bond, contrary to the prevalent opinion that OOH* was an important ORR channel. H+ attack on an O could facilitate O2 dissociation only when both O atoms were chemisorbed on Pt and the O—O distance was increasing. Acid dissociation on Pt surface Another interesting observation in our AIMD simulations was that a water molecule adsorbed on Pt(111) could easily go through acid dissociation. It was observed in previous first principle calculations for a monolayer of water on Pt(111), and attributed to structural stress. Actually, it’s due to the stabilization effects for OH-, when it’s adsorbed on Pt. We found the dissociation free energy barrier for H2O* into H+ and OH* to be only 0.14 eV. This also meant that neutralization of OH* was not very exergonic, although the barrier was low. We further explored the solvation of two other acids, H2SO4 and H3PO4 in the interfacial region, in addition to the commonly used HBr and HClO4. (The originally suggested CN- was removed from our consideration. It’s very toxic and not very often used in experiments.) The lowering of barrier was also found to be true for H2SO4 and H3PO4 adsorbed on Pt(111). For H2SO4, both protons would be lost to the interfacial solution, while in bulk solution the pKa for HSO4- was only 2.0. H3PO4 could also easily dissociate the first two protons, although there was a small barrier for the third proton.

14303114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303114.value: Major findings: (a). For the modeling of ORR in acidic media, the explicit inclusion of an anion, either adsorbed on the metal surface or solvated in the interfacial area could make a significance in the calculated barrier. It should be considered in future simulations. (b). When a H+ is present in the solvation layer, the neutralization of an adsorbed O* is facile. Together with the hydrolysis of an O* by an neighboring H2O* and O2* dissociation, it would produce 3 OH*, although only the neutralization of O* would contribute to the electric potential. (c). The attack of an O in O2* and the dissociation of O2 are often coupled with one another, leading to the breaking of O—O bond and the formation of OH*+O*, rather than the formation of OOH*. While the OOH* formation itself leads to the strengthening of O—O bond, and is not an important channel in the mechanism of ORR. This is contrary to the prevalent opinion about the importance of OOH* formation. (d). The dissociation of O2* often leads to the formation of O*, especially when O* is trapped in the relatively stable FCC site. It can subsequently react with a solvated H+ by neutralization or with a H2O* by hydrolysis. With free energy barriers larger than that for O2* dissociation, these processes are kinetically important. The quite exergonic hydrolysis of O* does not contribute to the electric potential, and is likely part of the reasons for the over-potential. Blocking such fcc sites for O* would help improve the efficiency of fuel cells. (e). When H2O, H2SO4, or H3PO4 is adsorbed on Pt(111), the free energy barrier for acid dissociation is greatly reduced. It means the enhanced presence of H+, and also the blocking of some of the adsorption sites for O2. One paper, based on the thermodynamic integration results, has been published. The results were also presented in a recent conference. Two other papers will be sent out for review soon. One M.Phil. and one Ph.D. student have been trained.

14303114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303114.value: Despite its complexity, thermodynamic integration and meta-dynamics simulation with explicit water molecules, acid, metal slab and O2 present the most realistic model for such ORR in the interfacial region and reveal many interesting features. It should be pushed further for other systems, other metal surfaces, alloys, etc. We are working on these models.

14303114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303114.value: Oxygen reduction reaction takes place at the cathode of a fuel cell, which is a promising clean energy technique. Its mechanism is complicated. By ab initio molecular dynamic simulations, we have explored the underlying solvation interaction and reaction dynamics. The elementary reaction steps and the reactive intermediates are identified, and the free energy changes and barriers have been obtained. The solvation effects are examined. These results should be helpful for experimentalists to design more efficient fuel cells.

14303214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303214.value: Fluorescent probes based on the Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) mechanism have been extensively studied for detection of protease activity, nucleic acid hybridization, and real-time polymerase chain reactions. These FRET-based probes generally contain a fluorophore and a non-fluorescent quencher which are in close proximity so that the quencher can effectively quench the fluorescence of the fluorophore via FRET. Upon interaction with a target protease or nucleic acid, these two components are separated thereby restoring the fluorescence. To achieve effective quenching and subsequent activation, it is desirable that the quencher exhibits a broad absorption that overlaps with the emission of the fluorophore to facilitate the FRET process and an effective non-radiative relaxation pathway to reduce the background signal. To date, only a few classes of “dark” quenchers have been developed and most of them can only pair with blue and green fluorophores (< 500 nm) which limits their use in bioimaging. For in vivo imaging, the fluorophores should absorb and emit in the near-infrared region (650-900 nm) to minimize auto-fluorescence and enhance light penetration through tissue. To our knowledge, dark quenchers that can work in this region are very rare. Even though a few of these quenchers are commercially available, they are very expensive, less versatile in term of the conjugation methods, and unstable in a reducing environment. Therefore, there has been an impetus to develop more efficient dark quenchers with tunable spectral features and various reactive groups for conjugation. The aim of this project is to develop a series of boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) based quenchers for FRET-based bioimaging. BODIPYs are highly versatile functional dyes which have tunable absorption and photophysical properties, good solubility and stability in many solvent systems, and diverse chemical reactivity. In this project, we will design and synthesize a series of conjugatable ferrocenyl BODIPY derivatives with different absorption features, in which the ferrocene moiety acts as an electron donor to effectively quench the fluorescence of the BODIPYs. Emphasis will be placed on the pi-extended analogues which absorb in the near-infrared region. To evaluate the usefulness of these dark quenchers, we will conjugate these compounds with the complementary fluorescent dyes via an enzyme-cleavable linker and study their fluorescence quenching efficiency and subsequent activation by the enzymes both in aqueous solutions and in vitro. Finally, the efficacy of these probes for in vivo imaging on mouse xenografts will be examined.

14303214.label: Realisation of objectives
14303214.value: The first objective of this project is to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of ferrocenyl boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) derivatives which have different absorption features and functional groups for conjugation, and can be used as dark quenchers for the construction of Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) based fluorescent probes, focusing on those which absorb in the near-infrared region. As the first endeavor toward this objective, we prepared a ferrocenylethenyl and styryl conjugated BODIPY substituted with a triethylene glycol chain (Dalton Trans. 2016, 45, 17798). With this extended pi- system, this compound exhibited the longest-wavelength absorption at 659 nm in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), which would match well with fluorescent probes, such as distyryl BODIPYs, that emit at ca. 650 nm. This compound also contained an alkynyl group at the meso position to facilitate coupling with fluorescent probes through copper-promoted alkyne-azide cycloaddition reaction. A similar ferrocenylethenyl-styryl BODIPY with two triethylene glycol chains was also prepared (Eur. J. Med. Chem. submitted). By introducing two iodo groups to the 2- and 6-positions of the BODIPY core, the longest-wavelength absorption shifted to 675 nm in DMF, which allowed this quencher to be used complementary with phthalocyanine-based probes. This compound contained a carboxy group at the meso position that enabled coupling through amide formation. The additional triethylene glycol chain could enhance the hydrophilicity of the compound. To shift the absorption further to the near-infrared region, we also synthesized a ferrocene-containing distyryl BODIPY (ChemPhotoChem 2019, 3, in press; 10.1002/cptc.201900115). Apart from the 2,6-diiodo BODIPY unit, an N,N-dimethylamino moiety was also introduced to one of the styryl branches of BODIPY, which could induce a significant intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) effect. As a result, this compound showed the strongest absorption at 701 nm and several broad absorption bands at 513, 396, and 353 nm. The wide range of absorptions in 300-800 nm suggested that this compound could serve as a broad-spectrum energy acceptor for a range of fluorophores, particularly those that emit in the near-infrared region. This compound was also substituted with an alkynyl group at the meso position for further conjugation. Finally, two additional ferrocenyl BODIPY derivatives were also synthesized, including a bis(ferrocenylethenyl) BODIPY, which should exhibit a superior quenching efficiency, and a ferrocenylethenyl-styryl BODIPY substituted with two 4-(N,N-dimethylamino)phenylethynyl groups at the 2- and 6-positions, which absorbed at ca. 740 nm. Unfortunately, these dyes possessed limited solubility and were relatively unstable which precluded further conjugation (unpublished results). Nevertheless, three versatile and efficient ferrocenyl BODIPY-based dark quenchers were prepared and characterized. Hence, the first objective was essentially accomplished. After preparing these compounds, their electronic absorption and fluorescence spectroscopic properties were examined in DMF and in aqueous media. These studies could shed light on the spectral matching of these dark quenchers with the complementary fluorescent probes. By comparing the fluorescence spectra of the probes before and after conjugation with the dark quenchers, the fluorescence quenching efficiency of the quenchers was also determined. For phthalocyanine-based probes, apart from fluorescence emission, they could also generate singlet oxygen. Hence, we also examined the singlet oxygen generation efficiency of these probes and the corresponding conjugates by a steady-state method using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as the singlet oxygen scavenger, and determined the quenching efficiency of the dark quenchers in this respect. By monitoring the absorption spectra of the three dark quenchers in aqueous media over a period of time, we found that they were relatively stable which is a desirable feature for biomedical applications. Hence, the second objective was also fully addressed. With these dark quenchers in hand, we conjugated these compounds with the complementary dyes, including distyryl BODIPYs and phthalocyanines, via a glutathione-responsive disulfide linker or a cathepsin B-cleavable Gly-Phe-Leu-Gly-Lys peptide substrate. For comparison, the corresponding non-cleavable analogues with a hydrocarbon or Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Lys linker were also prepared. All these conjugates were purified with various chromatographic methods and characterized with various spectroscopic techniques. They were deactivated in the native form owing to the efficient FRET from the excited dye to the ferrocenyl BODIPY unit, followed by photoinduced electron transfer (PET) or ICT arising from the ferrocene group. Upon interactions with glutathione or cathepsin B in aqueous media, the fluorescence emission of the cleavable probes was significantly increased owing to the detachment of the ferrocenyl BODIPY unit. For the phthalocyanine-based probes, their singlet oxygen generation could also be restored upon addition of these stimuli. Apart from these studies, we also investigated the activation of these conjugates at the cellular level. It was found that the intracellular fluorescence and/or photocytotoxicity of these activatable probes was significantly higher than that of the non-cleavable counterparts, indicating that the ferrocenyl BODIPY-based dark quenchers could effectively quench the photoactivities of the dyes, and therefore could be used in FRET-based activatable fluorescent probes and photosensitizers. The completion of these studies showed that the third objective was also accomplished. To address the last objective, we further extended the study to tumor-bearing nude mice. For the two phthalocyanine-based activatable probes with a disulfide or Gly-Phe-Leu-Gly-Lys linker, we monitored the activation in fluorescence emission inside a HT29 human colorectal carcinoma in the nude mice using an infrared imaging system. It was found that the intratumoral fluorescence intensity was gradually increased over a period of 24 h, while that for the non-cleavable conjugates the intensity could hardly be observed. The results suggested that the linker was cleaved by the intracellular thiols or cathepsin B inside the tumor, and the separation of the dark quencher from the phthalocyanine unit restored its fluorescence emission.

14303214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303214.value: In this project, we prepared three novel ferrocenyl BODIPY derivatives and used these compounds as dark quenchers to construct three FRET-based activatable fluorescent probes and photosensitizers. In the first system, a ferrocenylethenyl-styryl BODIPY dark quencher was conjugated to a distyryl BODIPY fluorophore through a glutathione-cleavable disulfide linker using copper-promoted alkyne-azide cycloaddition reaction (Dalton Trans. 2016, 45, 17798). This conjugate also contained a biotin moiety as a potential tumor-directing ligand. The molecular probe was deactivated in the native form through FRET followed by ICT due to the conjugated ferrocenyl unit. Upon interaction with glutathione in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and inside cancer cells, the fluorescence emission was significantly increased due to detachment of the quencher from the fluorophore. As shown by flow cytometry, this probe also exhibited preferential uptake by the biotin-receptor-expressing A549 human lung adenocarcinoma epithelial cells over the Chinese hamster ovary CHO-K1 cells used as the negative control. Apart from using distyryl BODIPYs as fluorescent probes, we also employed zinc(II) phthalocyanines which can strike a balance in fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen production, enabling the resulting conjugates having potential applications in bioimaging and photodynamic therapy. To match the fluorescence emission position of these dyes at ca. 700 nm, the ferrocenyl BODIPY-based dark quenchers were modified by introducing two iodo groups to the 2- and 6-positions of the BODIPY core and an N,N-dimethylamino moiety to one of the styryl branches of BODIPY. The longest-wavelength absorption of the corresponding derivatives was shifted to 675 and 701 nm, respectively. The two components were then conjugated through a glutathione-responsive disulfide linker (ChemPhotoChem 2019, 3, in press; 10.1002/cptc.201900115) or a cathepsin B-cleavable Gly-Phe-Leu-Gly-Lys peptide substrate (Eur. J. Med. Chem. submitted) using click chemistry or amide formation. The photoactivities of the phthalocyanine unit were largely quenched through FRET followed by PET or ICT. Upon exposure to glutathione or cathespin B in PBS and inside HT29 and HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells, the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation efficiency of the photosensitizer were significantly enhanced due to cleavage of the linker and separation of the two components. The activation process was confirmed by comparing the results with those of using the non-cleavable analogues and the cathespin B inhibitor CA074-Me (for the cathepsin B-responsive probe) as negative controls. Finally, the activation in fluorescence emission was also demonstrated in tumor-bearing nude mice for both these conjugates.

14303214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303214.value: The overall results of this study show that ferrocenyl BODIPYs could act as efficient dark quenchers of which the absorption positions can be tuned readily through chemical modification. To enable the quenchers to be used with fluorescent probes that emit at >700 nm, the pi-skeleton needs to be further extended. Moreover, to facilitate the conjugation and the application of the resulting conjugates in aqueous media, the hydrophilicity of the quenchers should also be improved further. It is worth to re-investigate the synthesis of bis(alkynyl) BODIPYs with more and longer oligoethylene glycol chains. It is believed that alkynyl moieties are more effective than iodo group in inducing bathochromic shift. With other structural features that promote red-shift of the absorption bands, these compounds should absorb at ca. 750 nm. The hydrophilic oligoethylene glycol chains can enhance the water solubility of the conjugates and promote their cellular uptake. With a series of these dark quenchers that can match with a range of functional dyes, more advanced FRET-based fluorescent probes and photosensitizers can also be constructed. For example, by using peptide substrates that are specific to certain disease-associated proteases as the linkers, the resulting conjugates could have theranostic applications against this disease.

14303214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303214.value: Fluorescent probes based on the fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) mechanism have been extensively studied for various biomedical applications. They generally contain a fluorophore and a non-fluorescent quencher in close proximity so that the quencher can effectively quench the fluorescence of the fluorophore via FRET. Upon cleavage of the linker in a specific manner, the fluorescence can be restored for detection. To date, only a few near-infrared-absorbing dark quenchers are commercially available and most of them are expensive and less versatile in term of the conjugation methods. In this project, we have designed and prepared a series of conjugatable ferrocenyl BODIPY dark quenchers with different absorption features, and employed these compounds to construct several FRET-based glutathione- or cathespin B-activated fluorescent probes and photosensitizers. The activation in terms of fluorescence emission and/or singlet oxygen generation has been validated in aqueous media and inside cancer cells. The activation in fluorescence emission has also been demonstrated in tumor-bearing nude mice. The results suggest that these ferrocenyl BODIPY derivatives are efficient and tailorable dark quenchers. On the basis that both glutathione and cathespin B are often elevated in cancer cells, these FRET-based molecular probes are potential theranostic agents for cancer imaging and therapy.

14303314.label: Project Objectives
14303314.value: To achieve high PCE with a thick (>200nm)-film ternary organic polymer solar cell. Device optimization will be performed by iteratively testing of different active layer materials, three components’ mass ratio, solvent and additive, pre- and post-treatments. To elucidate the fundamental relationship between the active layer morphology and charge transport process as well as device performance.

14303314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303314.value: This project aims to utilize and develop powerful synchrotron-based techniques in order to elucidate the morphology and structure of optically thick (>200 nm) active layers for ternary organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices. It will be of crucial importance for the understanding of fundamental mechanisms of exciton dissociation, recombination and charge transport inside active layer and in turn result in substantial improvement in device performance. OPV devices hold great promise for inexpensive, flexible and portable solar energy harvesting. A great amount of research efforts have been devoted to this area leading to a rapid improvement in power conversion efficiency (PCE) exceeding 10% within the recent five years. However, most of the high efficiency OPV devices were achieved with very thin active layers (<110 nm). Only 60%-80% of incident photons were absorbed. The increasing charge recombination and relatively low charge mobility limit further increase of the active layer thickness. As a result, one can foresee significant improvement of PV performance if thicker active layer can be employed without hampering exciton dissociation and charge collection. Therefore, in this project we aim to fabricate high efficiency OPV devices with thick active layers. We propose to fulfill this goal with a ternary organic polymer system by combining fullerene derivative with one host polymer, such as poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT), which can maintain high charge carrier mobility with thick films and one sensitizer polymer which has shown high PCE. Our preliminary experiments have confirmed the feasibility of such a system. Interestingly, the three components in the active layer exhibited new format of molecular packing and orientation compared with their binary counterparts. It suggests that a detailed exploration of new morphology and electronic process in this system is very demanding. To study the three-phase morphology, synchrotron-based grazing incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) will be employed to probe the molecule level structural behavior such as molecular ordering, lattice spacing and orientation of polymers. We propose to develop and exploit a new technique - grazing incidence transmission small-angle X-ray scattering (GTSAXS) in order to study the nanoscale phase separation in the active layer. In all cases, these results will be correlated with the characterization results on charge transport process and device performance. We expect that the proposed work will motivate new routes to high efficiency OPV devices that are viable for mass production. Beyond these OPV motivations, this work will also contribute to the development of new implementations at next-generation synchrotron beamlines.

14303314.label: Realisation of objectives
14303314.value: On the road of realizing high efficiency thick-film ternary organic polymer solar cell (objective 1), we first fabricated a ternary device base on two donors and one acceptor: P3HT:PTB7:PC71BM. The ternary system has shown higher PCE (~5%) with a thick actively layer (~200nm) than both binary counterpart could (RSCAdv, 2015, 5, 88500). Then, we performed a comparative study on six different ternary systems to understand the rule to achieve morphology compatibility. Among these six ternary systems, two high-performance ternary systems (PTB7: PPor-2:PC71BM and DPP-DTDT:PPor-2:PC71BM) have been identified which outperformed both binary counterparts with PCEs of 8.2% and 6.0% achieved with a donor1:donor2 mass ratio of 1:1 (Chem. Mater. 2016, 28, 6186−6195). Following our proposed selection rule for the two donors capable of comparable loadings, we further reported a ternary system composed of two morphologically compatible polymers (PTB7-Th and PPor-2) with distinct chemical structures that can achieve a high PCE of 9.0% with a mass ratio of 1:1. Besides the expected improvement in short circuit current due to the broadening of the absorption spectrum, the fill factor of the ternary device was improved significantly. It was attributed to the balanced electron and hole mobility and reduced recombination benefiting from the high morphology compatibility of the system (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2017, 5, 11739–11745). Most recently, we investigated a one-donor/two-acceptors ternary system: PBDB-T:ITIC:ITIC-Th and obtained a best PCE of 9.76% at a ITIC-Th:ITIC mass ratio of 1:1 with a significant increase of in-plane electron mobility, in accordance with the morphology observations (described in objective 3) (Adv. Mater, 2018, 1802888). To enable the characterization of active layer morphology (objective 2), we successfully obtained frequent synchrotron beam time for proposed X-ray scattering measurements at 14B1, 16B1, 19U2 of SSRF in Shanghai and 23A1 of TLS in Taiwan. We employed a combination of grazing incidence wide angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) and grazing incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS) to study the molecular packing and phase separation information of the active layer simultaneously. Particularly, GIWAXS technique can clearly detect the crystalline structure and orientation of each components in the ternary blend film. However, the new technique GTSAXS which could provide both in-plane and out-of-plane structural information was not able to be carried out due to the limited brightness of the bending-magnet beamlines available in Shanghai (16B1) and Taiwan (23A1) during the funding period. Therefore, we employed GISAXS as an alternative to obtain the nanoscale phase separation information. By fitting the GISAXS profiles with proper models, we could extract in-plane length scales of each phase and obtained deeper understanding on the morphology-device correlation (see objective 3). Recently, we have successfully acquired promising GTSAXS data of organic bulk heterojunction layers at an undulator beamline 19U2, SSRF. Therefore, in future projects, we will be able to use this technique to further investigate the out-of-plane morphology of organic bulk heterojunction active layers. On the aspect of morphology understanding of thick-film ternary organic polymer solar cells (objective 3), we have obtained many insightful results, which helped explain the outstanding device performance and provided guidelines for organic photovoltaic material design and synthesis. To achieve a high-power-conversion-efficiency thick-film device, we proposed a brand new route - combining one high-crystallinity polymer with one high-power-conversion efficiency polymer. The high-crystallinity polymer will ensure the efficient charge transport throughout the thick film while the high-performance polymer is in responsible of light absorption and exciton generation. This idea has been successfully demonstrated in the ternary system of P3HT:PTB7:PC71BM since P3HT has relatively high crystallinity but low PCE, while PTB7 has high PCE but cannot sustain its efficiency with thick film. (RSCAdv, 2015, 5, 88500). Then we found that many polymer combinations cannot work with comparable loadings in ternary cells. How to find compatible materials that allow comparable loadings of each component remains a challenge. Consequently, we studied the donor polymer compatibilities in ternary systems from a morphological point of view. Four typical donor polymers with totally different chemical structures and absorption ranges were mutually combined to form six distinct ternary systems with fullerene derivative acceptors. Ternary morphologies were characterized by both GIWAXS and GISAXS measurements and correlated with device performance. Two high-performance ternary systems were identified. We found that polymers that have strong lamellar interactions and relatively similar phase separation behaviors with the fullerene derivative are more likely to be compatible in ternary systems. This result provided guidance for polymer selection for future ternary organic solar cell research while relaxing the limitation of chemical structure similarity and greatly extends the donor candidate pool (Chem. Mater. 2016, 28, 6186−6195). During the progressing of this project, we established good collaborations with several teams in mainland China and obtained interesting results. For instance, one work, in collaboration with Hongzheng Chen’s group in Zhejiang University, studied ternary PTB7:PDTP-DFBT:PCBM system. Here, PDTP-DFBT was added as a sensitizer. A high PCE of 9.06% was achieved with interfacial modification with C3-SAM. Morphology results indicated an increase of crystallinity and favorable face-on oriented domains in this ternary system. (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2016, 4, 1702). A newly synthesized non-fullerene electron acceptor SF(DPPB)4 was reported. The solar cell device of P3HT: SF(DPPB)4 showed remarkable thermal stability and high open-circuit voltage, which is a good candidate for ternary cells (Energy Environ. Sci. 2016, 9, 604). Furthermore, we worked with Xiaowei Zhan’s group in Beijing University to explore the influence of a new solvent additive BPO on the morphology and device performance of solar cell devices. We found that this additive could act as a “molecular lock” that could form strong hydrogen bonds resulting in the sustaining of pi-pi ordering and high PCE after a high-temperature heating for a long time (Adv. Mater. 2016, 28, 5822–5829). We also investigated the morphology of many non-fullerene systems, which opened the ternary material candidate pools from two donors/ one acceptors to two acceptors/one donors (Sci China Chem, 2017, 60, 2, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2017, 139, 1336−1343, Adv. Mater. 2017, 29, 1605216, Adv. Mater. 2017, 29, 1701308, Sol. RRL 2017, 1, 1700148). With these accumulations on the morphology understanding of non-fullerene systems, we recently uncovered a hidden structure order along the backbone of two fused-ring electron acceptors ITIC and ITIC-Th. The backbone ordering could be greatly enhanced in the ternary film by the mutual mixing of ITIC and ITIC-Th with PDBD-T, consistent with the observed improved in-plane electron mobility and better ternary device performance. (Adv. Mater, 1802888, 2018).

14303314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303314.value: Through this project, we published 14 publications in peer-reviewed journals and presented our results 8 times in local and international conferences (see part C). Overall, our results provided guidelines and insights for pre-screening and synthesizing materials for ternary solar cell fabrications from morphology point of view. Major finding 1: We revealed the importance of morphology compatibility, proposed general morphological rules for ternary cells, relaxed the confinement of chemical structure similarity. Major finding 2: We proposed new directions for achieving high-performance thick film ternary cells. Major finding 3: We extensively investigated the morphology of many donor and non-fullerene acceptor systems, extending the potential material pools for ternary systems. Major finding 4: We revealed a hidden structure ordering of a ternary systems consisting of two non-fullerene acceptors, opening a new direction for fabricating high-performance ternary cells with favorable morphology.

14303314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303314.value: Ternary organic solar cells are emerging as a promising strategy to enhance device power conversion efficiency by broadening the range of light absorption via the incorporation of additional light-absorbing components. On the other hand, thick film organic solar cells could reduce the device performance fluctuation and improve product stability in mass production. This project utilizes state-of-art scattering techniques to systematically investigate the morphology and structure of thick film ternary organic solar cells. It reveals hidden structure ordering as well as fundamental mechanisms to morphology compatibility in thick film ternary devices. It motivates new routes to high performance organic solar cells that are viable for mass production.

14303414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303414.value: 利用T-Map 建構標記特徵曲面的度量形狀空間

14303414.label: Project Objectives
14303414.value: Design a metric space model for landmark-labeled geometric objects using Teichmuller distance. This includes (i) formulating metric space for general landmark-labeled surfaces with arbitrary topologies; (ii) developing algorithms to accurately and efficiently compute landmark matching T-Maps between surfaces of arbitrarily topologies to approximate the Teichmuller distance; (iii) finding the optimized correspondence between feature landmarks and (iv) extending the metric shape space model on triangular meshes to point clouds. Design algorithms to compute Teichmuller morphing, which incorporate the Teichmuller geodesic together with the mean curvature interpolation to obtain a smooth and meaningful interpolation between two landmark-labeled shapes. Applications of the algorithms to practical medical morphometry problems. This includes (i) landmark-labeled brain cortical surface morphometry for analyzing William Syndrome and Alzheimer’s diseases and (ii) statistical shape analysis of the landmark-labeled brainstem surfaces for analyzing Scoliosis disease.

14303414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303414.value: 隨著圖像獲取技術的進展，現實世界中的幾何物體現在可被精準高效地捕捉。這使得大量的三維幾何數據可被收集用來進行大規模統計形狀分析的科學研究。為了有效地進行這種分析，建立三維幾何物體的度量形狀空間並使這種度量可用來衡量形狀之間的距離是極其重要的。通常有一些重要的特徵與幾何物體相關聯，稱之為地標。結合這些地標的度量形狀空間有望得到更好的統計形態分析結果。在這個項目中我們感興趣的是，對於標記了重要特徵的曲面，我們稱之為地標標記曲面，建立一個度量形狀空間，使其數學結構可用來理解形狀。 本研究主要可以劃分成兩部分。在研究的第一部分，我們的目標是利用Teichmuller理論來發展地標標記曲面上的度量形狀空間。首先我們將研究利用Teichmuller空間來表示地標標記曲面空間。Teichmuller空間具有所謂Teichmuller度量，其可從曲面之間地標匹配的Teichmuller映射獲得。其次，高效準確地計算任意拓撲曲面之間地標匹配的Teichmuller映射對於計算高精度的Teichmuller度量是非常必要的。基於這個動機，我們將研究更好的算法來增強計算曲面網格之間Teichmuller映射的精度和效率。第三，我們將考慮結合Teichmuller測地線和平均曲率插值以獲得兩個地表標記曲面之間有意義的光滑形變的可能性。這將有助於理解一個形狀連續變形到另一個形狀的過程。第四，地標之間的匹配在定義度量形狀空間時扮著重要角色。為了這個目標，我們將研究如何尋找最優的地標匹配使得曲面之間地標匹配的Teichmuller映射具有最小的保角失真。一個最優的地標匹配將有望給出更好的度量形狀空間模型。最後，幾何形狀有時也用點雲來表示。我們也將考慮將本研究提出的定義在三角網格上的具有Teichmuller距離形狀空間模型擴展到有特徵標記的點雲上。 接著在研究的第二部分，我們感興趣的是應用提出的算法到實際的醫學形態學問題。更具體地，我們將應用形狀空間模型來研究大腦皮質表面，並以腦溝作為地標。我們將利用提出的Teichmuller度量來進行正常樣本和患病樣本（威廉症候群或阿茨海默氏症）之間的統計形狀分析。提出的算法也將用於研究腦幹曲面以分析脊柱側彎等病症。

14303414.label: Realisation of objectives
14303414.value: In this project, we have proposed several objectives. The ultimate goal is to develop mathematical algorithms for the shape analysis of landmark-labeled surfaces via Teichmuller extremal maps and Teichmuller metric. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: Our first objective is to design a metric shape space model for landmark-labeled geometric objects using Teichmuller distance. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. There are several tasks involved in this objective. Below, we describe in detail what we have achieved for each tasks. Firstly, the PI has successfully formulated the metric space for general landmark-labeled surfaces with arbitrary topology. The main goal is to design a shape metric to measure geometric differences between different landmark-labeled surfaces. The basic idea is to obtain the Teichmuller distance from the landmark-matching Teichmuller map between landmark-endowed surfaces. The logarithm of the dilation of the Teichmuller map gives rise to a well-defined metric on the shape space. Surfaces are represented discretely by triangulation meshes or point clouds. A landmark-labeled surface can be considered as a Riemann surface of finite type. Given two landmark-labeled surfaces with the same number of landmarks, a geometric shape distance, called the Teichmuller distance, can be defined. The challenge of computing this metric is that a complicated optimization problem over all landmark-matching surface mappings have to be solved. In this project, the PI has proposed to approximate the Teichmuller distance via the computation of Teichmuller mapping. This method has shown to be effective to obtain the shape metric. Of course, a major challenge is to compute the Teichmuller map accurately. To achieve high accuracy, a special numerical treatment has been designed to handle the discrete surfaces for the numerical computation of the Teichmuller map. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method to compute the Teichmuller map and Teichmuller distance accurately. The Teichmuller distance has also been shown useful for the shape analysis of landmark-labeled surfaces for various applications, such as facial recognition, teeth morphometry and medical shape analysis. Furthermore, many discrete surfaces nowadays are represented by point clouds, instead of triangulation meshes. It is therefore important to develop numerical algorithm to extend the metric shape space model on triangular meshes to point clouds. The PI has successfully developed an effective algorithm to achieve this goal. More specifically, a numerical algorithm, called TEMPO, has been developed to compute the Teichmuller extremal map between two landmark-labeled point clouds. The algorithm combines an efficient point cloud parameterization method and the quasiconformal iteration. Numerical results on extensive point cloud data has shown the developed method is effective and accurate for computing the Teichmuller extremal map as well as the Teichmuller distance between point clouds. Another important task is to delineate and prescribe their correspondences between important landmark features on various surfaces. Accurate and meaningful delineation of landmark features is crucial for effective shape analysis of landmark-labeled surfaces. For this goal, the PI has successfully developed a method to delineate and obtain their correspondences between landmark feature curves on discrete surfaces, based on Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions. Results show that the method can obtain landmark features efficiently and accurately. Objective 2: The second objective is to develop algorithms for analyzing the transition between two landmark-labeled surfaces. Analyzing the transition between geometric shapes is particularly important in medical imaging and computer visions to understand shape deformation. In this project, we have studied to analyze shape transition through Teichmuller metric. One of the main challenges to study geometric transition is to define a meaningful path between geometric shapes. The transition path can then be analyzed, such as analyzing the length, for the purpose of shape morphometry. In this project, we have analyzed the feasibility of using Teichmuller geodesic as the transition path between landmark-labeled surfaces. The computation of Teichmuller geodesic is a crucial step. It can be shown that the Teichmuller geodesic is the straight line in the space of Beltrami coefficients. In this project, the Teichmuller geodesic is approximated by a linear interpolation between two Beltrami coefficients of Teichmuller types. With the developed algorithm for the computation of Teichmuller extremal map, the associated Teichmuller embeddings can be reconstructed from the Beltrami coefficients of Teichmuller types. We have analyzed the effectiveness of using Teichmuller geodesic and curvature matching for the purpose of shape morphometry. Experimental results on premolar surfaces show that our proposed model is effective for teeth morphometry with high accuracy. It is therefore believed this developed method is promising for describing shape transition and shape analysis. Objective 3: Our third objective is to apply the developed algorithms to practical medical morphometry applications. We have analyzed the effectiveness of using our developed shape analysis algorithms for different shape analysis problem. More specifically, the developed algorithm has been applied to analyze brain structures for disease analysis with high accuracy. The developed algorithms have also been applied to landmark-labeled premolar surfaces for the morphometry of molar structures. Results are also encouraging. These demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed shape model for analyzing landmark-labeled surfaces. Our developed numerical methods for computing the Teichmuller distance have also applied to convoluted brain cortical surfaces. The numerical accuracy is high even on brain surfaces with complicated geometry. It demonstrates our developed methods are very stable and robust.

14303414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303414.value: In this project, we have developed various mathematical models for shape analysis of landmark-labeled surfaces, which have resulted in 2 published papers and 2 submitted papers (under revision) in different applied mathematics journals. Details are as follows. (1) Development of the metric shape space model for landmark-labeled surfaces: To perform shape analysis of landmark-endowed surfaces, we have developed a metric shape space model using Teichmuller distance [1]. The Teichmuller distance can be approximated from the landmark-matching Teichmuller map between the landmark-endowed surfaces. The logarithm of the dilation of the Teichmuller map gives rise to a well-defined metric on the shape space. (2) Efficient and accurate algorithm for computing Teichmuller extremal maps of landmark-labeled point cloud surfaces: Many discrete surfaces are represented by point clouds. In order to apply the metric shape space model to point cloud surfaces, we have developed a numerical algorithm, called TEMPO, to compute Teichmuller extremal map and Teichmuller distance between landmark-labeled surfaces [1]. The method is accurate and efficient even on complicated convoluted brain surfaces. The developed algorithm can be used to compute Teichmuller distance and Teichmuller geodesic to analyse the geometric changes and transition between landmark-labeled surfaces. (3) Theoretical study of quasiconformality on point clouds: In order to apply the metric shape model on landmark-labeled point cloud surfaces, a precise definition and thorough analysis of quasiconformality on point clouds are necessary. In [2], we have theoretically define and analyse quasiconformality on point clouds. These theories are essential to develop the discrete definition of Teichmuller map on point cloud surfaces and numerical algorithm to compute the Teichmuller distance between point cloud surfaces [1,2]. (4) Delineating and finding correspondences of landmark features: Accurate and meaningful delineation of landmark features is crucial for effective shape analysis of landmark-labeled surfaces. In [3], we have successfully developed a method to delineate and obtain their correspondences between landmark feature curves on discrete surfaces, based on Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions. (5) Applications of the developed models: we have analyzed the effectiveness of developed models for different medical shape analysis problem [1,3,4]. Our developed algorithms have been applied to analyze brain structures with high accuracy. The developed algorithms have also been applied to landmark-labeled premolar surfaces for the morphometry of molar structures. The numerical accuracy is high even on brain surfaces with complicated geometry. It demonstrates our developed numerical methods are very stable and robust.

14303414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303414.value: There are several areas for further development of the research. Details are described as follows. (1) Computation of Teichmuller distance for noisy discrete surfaces: Currently, our numerical algorithms for the computation of Teichmuller extremal map and Teichmuller distance work only on discrete surfaces of reasonable quality. The algorithm may fail when the input surfaces are very noisy. We will explore the possibility to extend the algorithms to handle this situation. (2) Extension of the metric shape space model to landmark-labeled inconsistent shapes: Currently, we assume the two shapes to be analysed are consistent. That is, we assume there exists a bijective map between two surfaces. In many practical situtations, the two shapes are inconsistent in the sense that the two shapes may not bijectively correspond to each other’s (for instance, due to occulsions). We are interested in extending our metric shape space model to analyse landmark-labeled inconsistent shapes. (3) Extension of the metric shape space to region-labeled discrete surfaces: Our metric shape space model can analyze surfaces, which are labeled by landmark points or curves. In some situations, we may label feature regions on a surface. We are interested extending our model to build a metric shape space model for region-labeled discrete surfaces.

14303414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303414.value: In this project, the main goal is to develop an effective metric shape space model for landmark-labeled surfaces. We have explored three research directions: 1. Design a metric shape space of landmark-labeled surfaces using Teichmuller distance; 2. Develop efficient and accurate algorithms for computing Teichmuller distance between landmark-labeled discrete surfaces, which can be represented by point clouds and 3. Applications of the algorithms to practical problems. We have successfully developed and implemented mathematical models for the above three goals. For the metric shape space model, we have developed an effective geometric distance between landmark-labeled surfaces using the Teichmuller distance. The Teichmuller distance can be approximated by computing the Teichmuller extremal map. The developed metric is effective for measuring geometric difference and analyzing transition between landmark-labeled surfaces. We have also developed efficient numerical algorithm, called TEMPO, to compute the Teichmuller distance on discrete surfaces, which can be represented by point clouds. Furthermore, we have developed effective method to delineate landmark features on discrete surfaces, which is essential for our developed metric shape space model. With the developed algorithms, we have developed tools for practical medical morphometry applications . These tools are useful in medical imaging for the purpose of disease analysis.

14303614.label: Realisation of objectives
14303614.value: We have successfully realized almost all the objectives as detailed below. 1. We synthesized and characterized a series of racemic functionalized hexabenzoperylenes (HBPs). 2. We synthesized a few functionalized HBPs containing chiral auxiliaries. 3. We studied molecular packing and self-assemblies of functionalized HBPs, and obtained a few single crystal structures. We discovered that the two-dimensional π-stacking of HBP with brickwork arrangement can accommodate a variety of functional groups without sacrificing π-π interactions in the solid state. 4. We fabricated and characterized field effect transistors of functionalized HBPs, and investigated relationship between molecular/supramolecular structures and device performance. By combining a transistor channel of functionalized HBPs and a microfluidic channel, we fabricated electronic sensors for highly sensitive and selective detection of chemical and biological species. 5. We obtained the single crystal structure of triazolo[4,5-b]pyridine-functionalized HBP, which presents a p-n heterojunction at molecular level, and investigated the photo-induced current in the thin film transistors.

14303614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303614.value: We synthesized a series of functionalized hexabenzoperylenes (HBPs), and, on the basis of these molecules, developed a new group of organic semiconductors, which present an unusual type of two-dimensional π-stacking with brickwork arrangement of twisted π-faces. We fabricated organic field effect transistors (OFETs) and OFET-based sensors for chemical and biological species in aqueous solution, and studied the structure-property relationship for functionalized HBPs in these devices. A major finding from this project is that the self-assembly of functionalized HBPs presents an unusual type of two-dimensional π-stacking for organic semiconductors. As a consequence of this unprecedented molecular assembly, through a dip-coating process, alkylatd HBPs easily formed micrometer-sized one-molecule-thick nanosheets, on which field-effect transistors were successfully fabricated. These results were published in Advanced Materials, 2015, 27, 3418–3423. A reviewer of this work for Advanced Materials commented that "it is generally considered that nonplanarity hinders molecule packing, which reduces charge carrier mobility. This work challenges this assumption because the nonplanar molecules have an extraordinarily close packing distance, which facilitates charge migration. This work expands knowledge of organic semiconductors". Another major finding from this project is that the two-dimensional π-stacking of functionalized HBPs in the crystals is able to accommodate a variety of functional groups without sacrificing π-π interactions. This molecular packing motif provides a general sensing platform for the detection of a variety of chemical and biological species by allowing functionalization of organic semiconductors without impairing charge transport. Integration of a microchannel on a thin-film transistor of functionalized HBPs enabled highly sensitive and selective detection of fluoride ions and streptavidin (a protein) in water when HBPs were equipped with a Si–O bond cleavable by fluoride and a biotin moiety to bind streptavidin, respectively (Chem, 2018, 4, 1416–1426). This project led to four research articles (three primary research articles and one review). Three of them have already been published in top journals of chemistry and material science, and one of them was submitted for review very recently. The results of this project were also presented during invited lectures at five international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project. These outcomes are detailed in Part C.

14303614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303614.value: Based on the success of functionalized HBPs in chemical and biological sensors, we envision that by grafting different reactive or binding sites to HBPs, the thin film transistors of HBPs will be able to detect specific chemical and biological species for food quality control, environmental monitoring and medical diagnosis. For example, we proposed a new type of OFET-based bioelectronic noses by attachment of human olfactory receptors to the surface of HBP films through native chemical ligation. And this proposal recently received support from the Croucher Senior Research Fellowship 2019-2020

14303614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303614.value: With the financial support from this General Research Fund, we developed a new group of organic semiconductors on the basis of functionalized hexabenzoperylenes (HBPs), fabricated organic electronic devices, and studied structure-property relationship for organic semiconductor materials. In particular, we discovered an unusual type of two-dimensional π-stacking with brickwork arrangement of twisted π-faces of functionalized HBPs, and demonstrated that this π-stacking can accommodate a variety of functional groups without sacrificing π-π interactions in the solid state. Functionalized HBPs enabled a new supramolecular platform for OFET-based chemical and biological sensors, which can circumvent the need for bulky and expensive equipment by combining the sensory electrical output with easy device fabrication. This project led to four research articles. Three of them have already been published in top journals of chemistry and material science, and one of them was submitted for review very recently. The results of this project were also presented at five international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project.

14303714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303714.value: Hypercontractive inequalities have played a significant role in a number of areas in real analysis and probability theory. They has also played an important role in discrete Fourier analysis starting from the works of Kahn-Kalai-Linial ('88) and Talagrand ('94) and these works have had a non-trivial impact on several problems in theoretical computer science. The connection between hypercontractive inequalities and information theory dates back to Ahlswede-Gacs ('76) and in this work we propose to extend this connection further. The PI has done extensive research over the past few years on multi-terminal information theory problems; in particular trying to determine capacity regions for certain settings, problems that have been open for decades. He has been successful in solving some non-trivial instances and has developed some new strategies for establishing capacity regions (via so called factorization inequalities). Factorization inequalities yield a direct way to "single-letterize" a capacity region expression and for instance, preliminary investigations have yielded that tensorization of hypercontractivity is identical to one particular factorization inequality. The ideas used for single-letterization in information theory and those used for establishing tensorization have developed independently. As a result there is a strong chance that an in-depth study of the relationship between hypercontractivity and information theory can yield to new results in both probability theory and information theory. The preliminary research indicates that hypercontractivity parameters may be expressible using information theoretic parameters. These could potentially be used to provide non-trivial explicit bounds to various hypercontractivity parameters. In the short term the project proposes to investigate the non-trivial extension of the results obtained during preliminary research and in the longer term it aims to explore the connection between hypercontractivity and information theory in much greater depth. The longer term objective should ultimately result in (hopefully) the resolutions of problems that have been open for decades. 超收縮不等式在實分析與概率論的多個領域有著顯著地位 [Gro75, DGS92, Jan97]。從[KKL88, Tal94]開始，超收縮不等式也在離散傅立葉分析有著重要地位，在理論計算機科學領域的一些問題有著不可忽略的影響。超收縮不等式與信息理論的聯繫可以追溯到[AG76]。在這項研究提案中我們將擴展這樣的聯繫。 項目負責人在過去幾年裡已經在多終端信息理論領域做了廣泛深入的研究，特別是在探求特定設置下的信息容量區域方面的一些數十年未解決的問題。負責人已經成功解決一些非顯然的實例問題[Nai10, GGNY11a, GN12]，並且提出新的關於探究信息容量區域的研究策略（通過所謂的因子分解不等式的方法）。 因子分解不等式開闢了“單字母化”信息容量區域表達式的直接方法，例如，初步研究已經得出，超收縮的張量性質等價於某一種因子分解不等式。 信息理論中單字母化的發展獨立於超收縮的張量性的發展。因此，深入研究超收縮和信息理論的聯繫在很大機率上會產生新的概率論和信息論的成果。 初步研究表明，超收縮的參數可以用信息論的參數表達。這些信息論的參數可以潛在性地用來確定具體而有意義的超收縮參數邊界。 短期上，項目繼續拓展初步研究的結果。長期上，項目旨在更深入的探索超收縮與信息理論的聯繫.

14303714.label: Realisation of objectives
14303714.value: Hypercontractive inequalities in information Theory The main emphasis of this grant proposal was to investigate the interesting connections between hypercontractive inequalities and information theory. The project started off with a discovery of error by the PI in a strong data-processing inequality claimed by Erkip and Cover, and its fix led to rediscovery and investigation of connections between information theory and hypercontractivity. The PI has the managed to establish the alternate characterizations of hypercontractivity and reverse hypercontractivity using information measures. The PI had established four equivalent characterizations of hypercontractive parameters for pairs of random variables, which was originally presented in a workshop in Zurich in 2014. There were three characterizations that were in terms of information measures and a year later the PI became aware that one of three characterizations could be deduced from a characterization of a generalized Brascamp-Lieb inequality derived by Carlen and Cordero-Erasquin in 2007. The PI, along with Sudeep Kamath - then a post-doctoral researcher at Princeton - who had visited the PI in Hong Kong, managed to established the strong data processing constant (equivalently a limiting hypercontractivity parameter) for sums of i.i.d. random variables. This short result then sparked a flurry of activity within the community. Tom Courtade, of U.C. Berkeley, used this connection establish a very simple proof of the the monotonicity of entopy and Oliver Johnson has built on this work for more finer estimates. Building on the discussions during the visit, Sudeep Kamath, proved an equivalent characterization of reverse hypercontractive parameters for a regime of parameters that were an immediate consequence of the PIs work in the forward direction. The PI along with Salman Beigi, who visited the PI for a longer duration, managed to establish the equivalent characterization of reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequalities that included the reverse hypercontractive inequalities as a special case. The PI also used reverse hypercontractive inequalities to make extensions and progress on a Boolean function conjecture. The new information theoretic characterizations of hypercontractive parameters were used to obtain hypercontractive and reverse hypercontractive parameters for the Binary Erasure channel. These works, done with a doctoral student of the PI, led also to an alternate proof of the Bonami-Beckner inequality which can be viewed a determining the hypercontractivity parameters of the BSC channel. Recently the PI and collaborators have identified new sub-additive functionals that unify an entire class of functional inequalities. The PI plans to put together a monograph describing these interesting connections and implications, a topic which has already got traction in the information theory community thanks to the work of the PI as well as other researchers who did follow on work. Thus the grant was very helpful and the PI is very happy with the ability to pursue these deep and interesting connections as well as inspire other researchers to pursue the same.
