14303714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303714.value: The major research findings of this proposal could be summarized as follows: Traditionally hypercontractivity parameters have been expressed using the language of Markov semi-groups and/or functional inequalities; however as a result of these investigations we have shown that there are equivalent characterizations using information theoretic functionals. [see work of PI with Salman Beigi] Among the various equivalent characterizations discovered one of them had been known earlier, however the proof techniques are substantially different. Additionally, determining the optimal set of hypercontractivity parameters was done only for very special distributions and the results of Gross, Bonami-Beckner, and Borell were important in this aspect. As a result of our characterizations, we could frame obtain the set for larger class of distributions as well as obtain alternate proofs of previous results [see work of PI with his doctoral student Yannan Wang]. Follow-on work by some of the PIs collaborators have shown that computation of the optimal rate region of a Gray-Wyner source coding problem is equivalent to determining hypercontractivity parameters for the given source pair. In summary the research findings and follow on work has kick-started an intense interplay between problems in information theory and functional inequalities.

14303714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303714.value: The PI wishes to put together these scattered results into a monograph at some point soon, as he has already got requests for doing so. The recent results unifying the Brascamp Lieb inequality and the entropy power inequality also merit follow up work. Original motivation of the PI to look into these problems came from his interest in some network information theoretic probelms. One such problem, determining the capacity region of the Gaussian Z-interference channel, which remain open seems to be intricately intertwined to reverse entropy power inequalities and other functional analysis inequalities that are of concurrent interest even in the math community. There is indication that the connections between sub-additivity, factorization/tensorization have a lot of life in it and we are quite at the beginning of understanding the full equivalence and implications picture.

14303714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303714.value: This project aimed to explore the connections between hypercontractive inequalities, originally studied by functional analysts, computer scientists and physicists, and single-letterization phenomenon in information theory. The research was able to unearth fundamental connections between the two areas and this has been picked up by other researchers as well and is fast blossoming into a rich area with new results. This interplay has indeed led to several new results and has provided impetus for starting much more systematic and deep investigations into these areas. This is one of the most serendipitous research endeavors that has happened recently in the research in network information theory to make progress on long standing open problems in the area. This has already yielded results: some by the PI, some by other authors such as Courtade, Jingbo Liu, Ozgur in the information theory community and others by Johnson, Madiman, etc from the math community.

14303814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303814.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a clinical modality for treatment of certain localized and superficial cancers. It requires a photosensitive drug, light of specific wavelength, and molecular oxygen to induce a series of photochemical reactions, leading to the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly singlet oxygen as the major cytotoxic agent. These ROS destroy tumors by multi-factorial mechanisms, including killing malignant cells by apoptosis and/or necrosis, shutting down the tumor vasculature, and stimulating the host immune system. With a view to improving the therapeutic outcome, various strategies have been explored to enhance the ROS generation efficiency and tumor selectivity of the photosensitizers. To address the latter aspect, conjugation to tumor-specific vehicles and encapsulation in colloidal nanocarriers are two common approaches. Recently, “smart” photosensitizing systems that can be activated by tumor-associated stimuli have received considerable attention. In these systems, the photosensitizers are either self-quenched due to aggregation or deactivated by the neighboring quenchers. Upon interaction with the acidic and reducing environment of tumors, cancer-related proteases, or mRNAs that have high tumor specificity, the photosensitizers are disaggregated or detached from the quenchers, resulting in restoration of their fluorescence and photosensitizing properties. This approach can therefore overcome the drawback of non-specific photodamage in PDT. To further improve the therapeutic efficacy of these systems and extend their theranostic applications, we propose herein a research project to introduce additional functional units to these activatable photosensitizers. Based on our previous finding that zinc(II) phthalocyanine substituted with a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate group serves as a highly efficient glutathione-activated photosensitizer, we will conjugate this photosensitizer-quencher system with a tumor-targeting carrier (e.g. folate) and an anticancer drug (e.g. doxorubicin). The latter will be connected via a singlet-oxygen-cleavable linker. It is envisaged that the conjugates can be taken up selectively by tumor cells via receptor-mediated endocytosis and then activated by the enhanced level of intracellular glutathione therein to trigger the fluorescence emission and formation of singlet oxygen. This ROS will then cleave the linker releasing the anticancer drug in a controllable manner. These multi-component molecular conjugates are therefore promising tumor-targeting activatable theranostic agents for cancer imaging and dual photodynamic and chemo-therapy. It is believed that the multi-level control in these compounds will greatly enhance their overall therapeutic efficacy. The proposed works include molecular design, synthesis, study of their cleavage kinetics, and evaluation of their in vitro and in vivo response.

14303814.label: Realisation of objectives
14303814.value: The first objective of this project involves the design, synthesis, and characterization of a series of multifunctional zinc(II) phthalocyanines which contain a tumor-targeting ligand, a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate (DNBS) substituent as a glutathione (GSH)-responsive group, and an antitumor drug linked via a singlet-oxygen-cleavable linker, as well as some non-tumor-targeting and non-cleavable counterparts for comparison. Being a strongly electron-withdrawing group, DNBS can effectively quench the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation of the phthalocyanines through photoinduced electron transfer (PET), and can be removed upon cleavage with GSH, which is often elevated in tumor cells and can therefore be regarded as a tumor biomarker, thereby restoring the photoactivities of the phthalocyanines. The use of a singlet-oxygen-cleavable linker can enable the antitumor drug to be released in a controllable manner through the photosensitizing process triggered by the phthalocyanines. With a large hydrophobic pi system, phthalocyanines tend to aggregate, particularly in polar media, which usually lowers the solubility of these macrocycles and hinders the preparation and purification processes. Our initial attempts to prepare multifunctional zinc(II) phthalocyanines were not very successful. For example, folate-conjugated phthalocyanines were found to have poor solubility even in polar aprotic solvents, such as N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). The DNBS substituent would further reduce the solubility of the phthalocyanine core. To circumvent this problem, a cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (cRGDfK) moiety was introduced to a zinc(II) phthalocyanine core substituted with three DNBS moieties through a triethylene glycol chain (Eur. J. Med. Chem. 2019, 174, 56-65). This moiety could not only enhance the solubility of the phthalocyanine core, but also serve as a targeting group for the alpha-v-beta-3 integrin, which is a transmembrane glycoprotein upregulated on the surface of proliferating endothelial cells, such as those in tumor neovasculature. To prepare this conjugate, the DNBS and cRGDfK moieties were introduced sequentially. Hence, the non-DNBS- and non-RGD-containing precursors were also available for comparison. As a side project, we also synthesized a zinc(II) phthalocyanine conjugated with the heptapeptide QRHKPRE, which exhibited high and selective affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpressed in a range of cancer cells (RSC Adv. in press). In addition, we also prepared another di-beta-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanine with a DNBS substituent and a branching unit connecting to a tumor-directing biotin group and the anticancer drug combretastain A-4 through a singlet-oxygen-cleavable aminoacrylate linker (J. Med. Chem. to be submitted). This biotinylated GSH-activated phthalocyanine-based photosensitizer could generate singlet oxygen upon the actions of GSH and light to trigger the release of combretastain A-4 for dual chemo and photodynamic therapy. For comparison, a non-singlet-oxygen-cleavable analogue was also prepared similarly. To extend the study further, we also designed and synthesized a multi-stimuli-responsive phthalocyanine that can perform sequential logic operations as a molecular keypad lock with four inputs (J. Am. Chem. Soc. to be submitted). The compound contains several inter-related functional units. The first part involves a zinc(II) phthalocyanine core substituted with three DNBS moieties. This phthalocyanine unit is also connected to a bis(ferrocenylethenyl) boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) moiety through an acid-cleavable ketal linker. With an extended pi system, this BODIPY absorbs at ca. 720 nm that can overlap well with the fluorescence band of the phthalocyanine to enable an efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) process. The presence of two electron-donating ferreocenyl units can effectively quench the indirectly excited BODIPY through intramolecular charge transfer (ICT). Hence, this ferrocenyl BODIPY moiety can provide another quenching pathway for the phthalocyanine unit that can be relaxed upon addition of acid. On the basis that tumor cells generally have a lower extracellular pH than normal cells, a slightly acidic environment can be regarded as another tumor-associated stimulus. Furthermore, the phthalocyanine is further connected to a pyrene acted as an energy donor through a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive thioketal linker. Hence, this FRET process from the excited pyrene to the phthalocyanine will be disrupted if singlet oxygen is generated from the phthalocyanine unit. This specially designed molecule was found to be responsive toward several stimuli, including GSH, acid, and the two excitation sources for the phthalocyanine (at > 610 nm) and pyrene (at 345 nm). Based on the fact that GSH would become ineffective in the cleavage of DNBS in acidic environment, the response was sequence dependent and the signals generated could be manipulated to construct a molecular keypad lock with four inputs. All the new compounds were purified with various chromatographic technique and characterized with various spectroscopic methods. Hence, the first objective was deemed to be fully achieved. In addition, the electronic absorption and fluorescence properties of these compounds were studied in detail both in DMF and in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) with 0.1% Tween 80. The singlet oxygen generation efficiency of these compounds was also evaluated in these two media. Their photostability in aqueous media was briefly examined using electronic absorption spectroscopy. The response of these compounds in terms of fluorescence emission, singlet oxygen generation, and the drug release toward the different stimuli, including GSH, acid, and light was also monitored closely with various spectroscopic methods and/or high-performance liquid chromatography. Therefore, the second objective was also accomplished. For the third objective regarding the in vitro properties of these compounds, cell-line studies were carried out using the cyclic RGD-conjugated, QRHKPRE-substituted, and biotinylated zinc(II) phthalocyanines. For the RGD conjugate, we examined its cellular uptake against a range of cancer cell lines with different levels of integrin expression, including the integrin-overexpressed A549 human lung carcinoma and MDA-MB-231 human breast adenocarcinoma cells, as well as the low integrin-expressed MCF-7 human breast adenocarcinoma cells and HEK-293 human embryonic kidney normal cells, using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry. To demonstrate the activation in fluorescence emission by GSH inside the cells, GSH-OEt and the thiol depletion agent N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) were used for post-incubation, and the results under different conditions were compared. In addition, the photocytotoxicity of this conjugate, either with or without post-treatment with GSH-OEt, against two integrin-positive and integrin-negative cell lines was also examined. For the QRHKPRE-conjugated analogue, its receptor-mediated endocytosis, subcellular localization, photocytotoxicity, cell-death mechanism, and in vivo biodistribution were studied using HT29 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells and HT29 tumor-bearing nude mice. For the biotin-conjugated derivative, similar in vitro studies were performed using the biotin-receptor-overexpressed HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells and the low biotin-receptor-expressed HCT-116 human colorectal carcinoma cells. Competition assay with biotin was also carried out to reveal whether the uptake was mainly through a biotin-receptor-mediated process. Finally, the dual therapeutic effect of this conjugate was also studied against these two cell lines. By analyzing the results with those of the non-cleavable analogue, free combretastain A-4, and under different conditions, including light irradiation and post-treatment with GSH-OEt, the cytotoxicities due to the chemo and photodynamic therapy components could be determined, which allowed the calculation of the combination index to reveal the synergistic therapeutic effect. All these studies showed that the third objective was also achieved.

14303814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303814.value: A zinc(II) phthalocyanine substituted with an EGFR-targeted heptapeptide QRHKPRE (RSC Adv. in press) and another analogue with three DNBS groups and a cyclic RGD moiety (Eur. J. Med. Chem. 2019, 174, 56-65) were prepared and characterized. With three electron-withdrawing DNBS groups, the latter was fully quenched in fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation in DMF and PBS due to the strong PET effect. In the presence of GSH, the DNBS moieties were cleaved and these photoactivities were restored. As shown by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, the intracellular fluorescence intensity of the conjugate was significantly higher in the integrin-positive A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells than in the integrin-negative MCF-7 and HEK-293 cells. The photocytotoxicity was also found to be higher toward MDA-MB-231 than toward MCF-7 cells. Another multifunctional zinc(II) phthalocyanine substituted with a DNBS group, a biotin moiety, and the anticancer drug combretastatin A-4 through a singlet-oxygen-cleavable aminoacrylate linker was also prepared (J. Med. Chem. to be submitted). Its photoactivities were also significantly quenched by the DNBS substituent. Confocal microscopic studies showed that this prodrug was preferentially taken up by biotin-receptor-positive HepG2 cells, and then activated by the intracellular GSH, leading to recovery of the fluorescence and photosensitizing properties. Cell viability assays also demonstrated that upon red-light irradiation, the singlet oxygen generated by the phthalocyanine not only induced a significant photocytotoxicity, but also triggered the release of combretastatin A-4, resulting in enhanced anticancer efficacy. The combination index calculated further quantitatively indicated that the prodrug exhibited synergistic chemo and photodynamic therapeutic effects at certain drug doses. Finally, we also prepared a novel conjugate of tris(DNBS)-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanine, bis(ferrocenyl) BODIPY, and pyrene connected with an acid-sensitive ketal bridge and a singlet-oxygen-cleavable thioketal linker, respectively (J. Am. Chem. Soc. to be submitted). The fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen production of this conjugate were found to be responsive toward several stimuli, including the tumor-associated GSH and slightly acidic environment, as well as two different light sources at > 610 nm and 345 nm. More interestingly, the response was sequence dependent. Based on the effects of these four stimuli on the fluorescence intensity of the pyrene unit in PBS, it was demonstrated that the compound could perform sequential logic operations as a four-input molecular keypad lock. As a round-up of this project, the current research status of stimuli responsive phthalocyanines used as fluorescent probes and photosensitizers has been reviewed (Coord. Chem. Rev. 2019, 379, 30-46).

14303814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303814.value: This research project involves the design and synthesis of multifunctional phthalocyanines for theranostic applications. In order to exhibit multifunctions in a singlet molecule, various functional components need to be introduced to the phthalocyanine core. However, the synthesis of these compound could be very tedious and the solubility of the resulting conjugates would also be a problem. In fact, these were the difficulties we encountered during the early stage of this research, and we needed to put extra effort to successfully synthesize these compounds eventually. To circumvent the synthetic challenge, bioorthogonal chemistry could be used to assemble these components at the cellular or even animal level. This approach has been widely used for on-site delivery of various bioimaging and therapeutic agents, but the use of highly efficient bioligation methods for construction of multifunctional theranostic agents remains little studied. As an extended study of this project, we could first incubate the cancer cells with a tagged targeting group (e.g. azide-modified cyclic RGD), and then introduce an activatable photosensitizer with the complementary unit (e.g. alkyne-appended DNBS-substituted phthalocyanine). It is expected that the two components could be coupled on the cell surface, and various functional units could also be introduced similarly.

14303814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303814.value: Photodynamic therapy has emerged as a treatment modality for certain localized and superficial cancers. It requires a photosensitive drug, light of specific wavelength, and oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS). To enhance the therapeutic efficacy, smart photosensitizing systems that can be activated by tumor-associated stimuli have been developed. With a view to further improving the efficacy, we introduced additional functional units to these activatable photosensitizers. By using 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate-substitited zinc(II) phthalocyanines as glutathione-activated photosensitizers, we conjugated these compounds with a tumor-targeting ligand (e.g. cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartic acid peptide sequence and biotin) and/or an anticancer drug (e.g. combretastatin A-4) linked through a ROS-cleavable linker. It was found that the conjugates could be taken up selectively by tumor cells via receptor-mediated endocytosis and then activated by the enhanced level of intracellular glutathione to trigger the fluorescence emission and formation of singlet oxygen. This ROS then cleaved the linker releasing the anticancer drug in a controllable manner, resulting in synergistic therapeutic effects. Therefore, these multicomponent molecular conjugates can serve as tumor-targeting activatable theranostic agents for cancer imaging and dual chemo and photodynamic therapy.

14303914.label: Project Objectives
14303914.value: Develop a biomorphic route to fabricate high quality multi-semiconductor components carbon-based catalyst with mesoporous structures to perform photocatalysis in eliminating toxic organic compounds in water. Characterize the morphology, surface area, and pore size of the product. Establish relationships between these results with the photocatalytic activity. These information will be used as benchmark to modify the processing parameters (composition, concentration, and temperature) in seeking an optimal fabrication condition for high quality products. Evaluate the performance and reusability of the products in degrading the triarylmethane dyes (phenol, methyl violet and malachite) under the ultra violet and visible light range. Study the electrostatic interactions between the functional groups on the surface of the AFC fibers and the hydrolysis ions in the precursor solution during sample preparation. Investigate how the functional groups would affect the nucleation and growth of the metal oxides on the surface of the ACF fibers. Use appropriate semiconductor components to produce p-n heterojuctions for the catalyst in an attempt to inhibit or delay the rate of annihilation of electron-hole pairs and to extend the response range of light adsorption. Use different combinations of semiconductors to adjust the selectivity of the active components in adsorbing specific types of organic compounds. Establish models for the relationships between processing, microstructure, degrading performance and the rate of the catalytic reaction.

14303914.label: Realisation of objectives
14303914.value: Most of the objectives in the project have been tackled and largely achieved. Work related to Objective (1): Several multi-components carbon-based catalysts with mesoporous structures were produced. The catalysts were fabricated via a biomorphic approach by using kapok fibers as bio-templates. The fabrication involved carbonization, activation (by ZnCl or CO2), impregnation of the active ingredients, hydrolysis and/or annealing. The products include: 3-D hierarchical structure of gamma-AlO(OH)/Mg-Al-LDH/C (article 1/part C); porous MoS2/CoAl-LDH/hollow carbon fibers (article 6/part C); porous TiO2-MnTiO3/hollow carbon fibers (article 7/part C). Another product using eggshell membrane as substrate to fabricate porous MgFe2O4 compounds was also reported (article 8/part C). All the products possess the abilities of dye adsorption, and/or antibiotics elimination. Most of them can also perform photo-catalysis for disintegration of pollutants under solar irradiation. Work related to Objective (2): Most of the sample products were characterized by XRD, SEM, TEM, and BET. Their phases, crystalline structures, microstructures, compositions, and morphologies were identified. Taking the porous TiO2-MnTiO3/hollow carbon fibers (article 7/part C) as an example, the sample was found to be hollow-tube-like with an average diameter of 10 micron. We estimated that nearly 90% volume of the sample was empty. As for the active ingredients, nanometer-size TiO2-MnTiO3 crystallites were found uniformly distributed on the surface of the HACF. From the BET results, we found that the sample had a narrow pore-size distribution of 2 to 4 nm, thus, they had the mixed micro/meso-pore structure. By adjusting the Ti : Mn ratio and the Mn/Ti : HAFC ratio, and/or by various heat-treatments at temperatures ranged between 600 and 900oC, the size and shape of the crystallites appeared different leading to different performance in dye elimination in water treatments. Work related to Objective (3): In the samples, most of the active ingredients were with oxide-base semiconductors. They could stand relatively high temperature with their phases unchanged. The products were found to be re-usable after receiving high temperature treatment to eliminate the adsorbed dyes and the pollutants. An good example is shown in the re-usability of Fe3O4@MgAl-LDH (in article 4/part C) Work related to Objective (4): It was proven that the electrostatic interactions between the functional groups on the surface of the HACF and the hydrolysis ions in the precursor solution would play a dominant role in the sample preparation (articles 6 and 7/part C). Another example could be seen in using the eggshell membrane to adsorb metal ions to enable the nucleation and anchoring of the MgFe2O4 through electrostatics (article 8/part C). In general, the possible functional groups on the substrate surface would be carboxyl, carbonyl, phenol, and chrome. Work related to Objective (5): In related work, attempts had been made to synthesize porous photoelectrical structures of graphic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) by using thermal condensation process. An appropriate amount of residual oxygen in C3N4 sheet would lead to enhancement of light adsorption and inhibition of charge recombination. When the secondary phase MoS2 was added, it served as electron trapper to extend the lifetime of separated e-h pairs, while the accumulated holes on the surface of C3N4 could oxidize the dye. Inspired by this result, we had synthesized the TiO3-based heterojunction system (article 7/part C) and MoS2/CoAl-LDH/HCF (article 6/part C). The photocatalytic performance under visible light was found to be satisfactory. Work related to Objective (6): The pseudo 1st order and 2nd order models had been used to interpret the dye adsorption behaviors of various products. High values of R2 in the fitting curves were obtained, indicating that the process was sorption rather than the intra-particle diffusion between the dye molecules and the adsorbent samples

14303914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303914.value: The major findings and outcomes are as follows. 1. We have developed a facile fabrication route for this type of photocatalysts via a biomorphic approach. 2. We have produced several high quality photocatalysts that could effectively adsorb or/and degrade organic dyes and compounds in water. 3. Most of the adsorption behaviors of the products followed the pseudo-second-order model.

14303914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303914.value: The work in this project inspire us to launch the making of improved materials for electrodes in energy storage devices. The biomorphic approach to fabricate porous multi-compoenets photo-catalysts have been utilized to the synthesis of electrodes for lithium ion battery and supercapacitors. The idea is basically the same as in catalysis, it aims to provide more surface area for interactions between the electrode and the elctrolyte.

14303914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303914.value: This work is in-line with the global trend of using green approach to re-generate clean water by removing unwanted pollutants by using biomasses-based adsorbents or/and photocatalysts. Most of the products that studied in this project are re-usable and highly effective. They have a good potential to be utilized in commercial water treatment.

14304014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304014.value: In replacing the known case that (p,q) = (1,2) we introduce notion of p-order tilt-stable (sharp) minimizers (of a proper lower semi-continuous function f on some Banach space X) and that of q-order stable minimizers, and show, via the consideration of Holder metric regularity/sub-regularity of subdifferentials of f, that these are equivalent properties exactly when p and q are "matched" in the sense that q = (1+p)/p. Results are further extended when f is perturbed with respect to certain parameters. We propose a new projection-based method for solving convex feasibility problems; with the help of some linear regularity, we establish linear convergence results for this new method under some new control strategy introduced by us.

14304114.label: Project Objectives
14304114.value: • Characterization of trail degradation and identification of controlling factors Field assessment, consisting of more than 50 sampling points, will be conducted to characterize the type, extent and severity of trail degradation and erosion in Hong Kong. The assessment not only can lay a foundation for the subsequent works of this study, but also enable us to identify those factors controlling the occurrence of trail degradation. Country park managers will be trained to apply the assessment protocol for future and wider applications. • Investigation of factors, processes and mechanisms controlling trail erosion Soil loss of 8 unbounded plots will be monitored for two hydrological years. Parallel to the runoff plot monitoring is the rainfall simulation experiment (no. of runs = 32). The combination of monitoring and experiment not only will enable us to understand the process of trail degradation as a response to rainfall and human activities, but also will provide quantitative data for the selection of “best” erosion model for predicting trail erosion in Hong Kong. • Construction of a Virtual Geographic Environment (VGE) for trail management By integrating geographic data, erosion prediction model and virtual reality into a VGE, this research is able to: (a) identify the “hot spots” of degradation and erosion along the whole trail visually; (b) evaluate and predict the impacts caused by trail degradation and erosion using model simulation; (c) compare the cost and effectiveness of various design and management alternatives by means of virtual geographic experiments; and (d) optimize best management practices that minimize project costs and sediment loss.

14304114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304114.value: Trails are the essential infrastructure in parks and protected areas, serving important functions of protecting natural resource and landscape while providing recreation and tourism opportunities. In recent decades, the demand for nature-based tourism and recreational use of country parks in Hong Kong has increased dramatically. To support visitor use, a network of trail, consisting of 4 long trails (total length = 298 km) and 63 short trails, has been established in the territory. However, many of these trails have degraded over time probably because of recreational overuse and a lack of appropriate maintenance. Degraded trails not only are visual eyesores, but also create difficult and unsafe travel conditions. Furthermore, soil erosion associated with trail degradation may cause negative impacts on the local biodiversity. Eventually, trail degradation and erosion will translate to depletion of both renewable and non-renewable resources and deprivation of ecological integrity of an area. Although adverse aspects of trail degradation and erosion have been mentioned recurrently in Hong Kong, the performance of present trail management is far from satisfactory probably because of lacking information, knowledge and effective management means. With this in mind, this study will examine the threefold issue of degradation, erosion and management of a popular hiking trail in Hong Kong. To be specific, this study will involve: • Characterization of trail degradation and identification of controlling factors • Investigation of factors, processes and mechanisms controlling trail erosion • Construction of a Virtual Geographic Environment for trail management This research represents the first multi-disciplinary attempt to examine trail degradation and trail erosion in a unified platform. It is expected that this research will encourage the integration and advancement of knowledge in of two disciplines, namely recreation ecology and soil erosion. This research not only will develop the best fit model for trail erosion in Hong Kong, but also will contribute to the scientific understanding of trail degradation that inform trail management in protected areas within the region such as south China. Furthermore, this research will establish a paradigm for trail management in Hong Kong. Such findings and results of this research are expected to be attractive to both local and international readers. 步道是公園和保護區的重要基礎設施，其功能除了保護自然資源和景觀，同時亦提供娛樂和旅遊機會。近幾十年來，在香港郊野公園內，以自然為基礎的旅遊和康樂活動急劇增加。為了滿足使用客的需求，有關當局建設了一個由4條遠足步道（總長度= 298公里）和63長度較短的步道組成之步道網絡。然而，隨著時間的推移，這些步道有很多地方已經退化，其原因可能是過度使用和缺乏適當的維護。退化的步道，不僅是視覺的缺陷，還會對使用者構成不便甚至危險。此外，步道退化引至土壤侵蝕亦可能對當地生物多樣性構成負面影響。最後，步道退化和侵蝕將轉化為可再生能源和不可再生資源的枯竭和生態完整性的缺失。雖然香港已有人指出步道退化和侵蝕的不良影響，但由於缺乏資料，知識和有效的管理手段，目前步道管理仍差強人意。有見及此，本研究將探討香港一條熱門的遠足徑的退化，土壤侵蝕和管理三方面的問題。具體而言，本研究將涉及： •識別步道退化的特徵和控制因素 •查找土壤侵蝕上土壤侵蝕的成因，過程和機制 •為步道管理建造一個虛擬地理環境 這項研究可能是世界上第一個將步道退化和侵蝕研究整合的多學科的嘗試。預計這項研究將有助整合和提升休閒生態學和土壤侵蝕之知識。這項研究不僅為香港步道侵蝕建造的最佳擬合模型，也有助加深我們對步道退化的科學理解，並應用於其他地區（例如：南中國）的保護區之步道管理。此外，本研究將在香港建立一個管理步道的範例。這樣的研究結果和發現預計對本地和國際讀者都具有吸引力。

14304114.label: Realisation of objectives
14304114.value: • Characterization of trail degradation and identification of controlling factors 4 trails (total length is approximately 10.28 km) in Hong Kong were selected to characterize the patterns of trail degradation in Hong Kong. These trails were different in terms of visitor volume, usage, geology and vegetation, etc. Sites were systematically sampled along the trail at an interval of 50 m. There were 204 sampling sites in total. At these sites, both degradation indicators and site condition variables were measured. Field surveys were conducted at these trails in the period of October 2015 - Jan 2018, aiming at capture the annual change of the trail condition. The sampling scheme covered both dry and season seasons, aiming at finding out the seasonal variations. By comparing the physical characteristics of the sampling sites and those of control ones, the differences were assumed as the change of the trail due to degradation and erosion. • Investigation of factors, processes and mechanisms controlling trail erosion Soil loss of 7 bounded plots at 4 studied trails were monitored for two hydrological years (March 2016 to February 2018). Parallel to the runoff plot monitoring was the rainfall simulation experiment (no. of runs = 36) conducted at various sites of the studied trails. The combination of monitoring and experiment not only enabled us to understand the process of trail degradation as a response to rainfall and human activities, but also provided quantitative data for the selection of “best” erosion model for predicting trail erosion in Hong Kong. • Construction of a Virtual Geographic Environment for trail management By integrating geographic data, erosion prediction model and virtual reality into a VGE, this research is able to: (a) identify the “hot spots” of degradation and erosion along the whole trail visually; (b) evaluate and predict the impacts caused by trail degradation and erosion using model simulation; (c) compare the cost and effectiveness of various management alternatives; and (d) optimize best management practices that minimize project costs and sediment loss.

14304114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304114.value: Referring to the first objective, 4 trails (total length is approximately 10.28 km) in Hong Kong were selected to understand the patterns of trail degradation in Hong Kong and identify controlling factors of trail degradation. Measurement included the site condition (trail and terrain slope, trail slope alignment angle, aspect, position, etc.), degradation indicators (trail morphology (width, incision and form), trail surface composition (type and area of different types of coverage), presence and extent of degradation features (e.g., multiple trails) and soil compaction. By comparing the physical characteristics of the sampling sites and those of control ones, the differences are assumed as post-impact changes due to degradation and erosion. Based on the data gathered from the field survey, visitor volume and activities were identified as two key factors determining the type and rate of trail degradation. Referring to the second objective, 7 bounded plots were set up at 4 studied trails and they were monitored for two hydrological years (March 2016 to February 2018). The monitoring period was from March 2016 to February 2018, covering two full hydrological years. Furthermore, 36 sessions of rainfall simulation were conducted. Based on the data gathered from the field survey, runoff plots and rainfall simulation, we performed various statistical analyses and modelling methods to investigation of the processes of degradation and soil erosion. It was found that the trampling of visitors results in the removal of surface materials and soil compaction. There was a moderated association between degradation and soil erosion and the amount of removed materials could not be fully explained by the erosion model constructed. Referring to the third objective, a VGE had been constructed for the improvement of trail management. The VGE to be developed consists of three layers, namely data layer, functional layer and service layer. The function layers were constructed based on the data and results of the above mentioned exercises. When the service layer was constructed, we consulted the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) which is the responsible organization for the management of trails in Hong Kong. Based on the VGA, a few hot spots at the studied trails were identified. Furthermore, we recommended carrying capacities of various trails to AFCD for their considerations. The results of this study are well accepted by AFCD and the general public. The research team had organized one training workshop for AFCD officials and one public forum for the general public.

14304114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304114.value: This study provides three recommendations for the trail management in Hong Kong. First, it is important to regulate the visitor volume and activities taken place in country parks. Although legally trails are common assets that there is almost no restriction for the individual users, the AFCD should carefully divert the visitor flow through carefully design of the trail network. Second, scientific data are important to minimize the user’s impacts and successful management. However, current the present management is passive and based on experience that the focus is to make efforts to fix the damages but not to prevent trail from excessive impacts. Nevertheless, the VGE established by this study may be an effective tools for trail management. Third, it is no specific standards (e.g., widths, gradients and material used) for trail design. As a result, certain trails or segments may be vulnerable and not able to absorb impacts generated by the users. Experience on sustainable trail design and building can be borrowed from foreign countries.

14304114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304114.value: This proposed study has significance in both theoretical and practical terms. These are: • Every year, the Hong Kong SAR Government invests significant amounts of money in implementation and maintenance of trail. This project will provide an objective review of the problems of trail degradation and soil erosion based on scientific data while taking into account public perceptions that may facilitate a better investment and utilization of the money. • This project will identify the key controlling factors for successful trail management, which could be adopted in future design specifications and assessment protocol that eventually should greatly contribute to a better trail management in Hong Kong. • This project will fill the knowledge gap pertaining to the trail management in Hong Kong.

14304314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304314.value: 最近表面等離子體激元（SP）介導的發光排放受到廣泛關注由於其在固態照明，傳感，電信，醫療診斷，材料特性鑑定的應用。原則上，當光發射器接近金屬等離子系統，它們可以與表面等離子體激元法（SPPs）強烈地相互作用，導致自發發射速率變形，定向和偏振的發射，並且激光發射。然而，我們對於SP排放的認識仍處於初級階段。雖然它是通過已知的兩個連續的增強，即激發和發射，攜手在生產最後結果。但每個增強包含幾個交織的子步驟，使得理解困難。特別是，每個子步驟都有其自身的特點。因此，有秩序地研究和進行定量分析是必不可少的。在這個項目中，我們試圖解決這些問題。首先，我們已經開發了基於速率方程模型和耦合模理論去耦SP的調解排放，使我們可以單獨研究每個子步驟。其次，我們描述每個子步驟其各自的速率常數和局部密度的態器（LDOS）。換句話說，我們專注於更基本的或固有的參數。我們預期這些參數可以彌合外部參數和SP發射之間的不明間隙，並揭示了更多關於該過程的基本機制。為了實現這些，我們將研究兩種電漿系統類型。然後，我們將通過幾個多功能光學顯微鏡和一個陰極發光系統，測量相關的速率常數和LDOS。我們試圖建立這些參數及其發光增強關係之間的聯繫。最後，數值模擬將提供理論支持。最後，我們預計該項目將理解表面等離子介導的排放，以及其他相關的現象，如表面增強拉曼散射和熱輻射。

14304314.label: Realisation of objectives
14304314.value: We have realized all the objectives as listed. We have carried out in-depth studies on surface plasmon mediated emission both theoretically and experimentally. For the objectives 1 & 3, we combine rate equation model and temporal coupled mode theory to formulate the energy transfer processes of light emitters when they are coupled to surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) supported on periodic metallic structures. Under weak coupling, the entire surface plasmon mediated emission can be divided into two sub-processes and they are spontaneous emission and excitation enhancements. Each enhancement is dictated by how energy is being transferred between light emitters and SPPs. For spontaneous emission enhancement, energy is transferred from the emitters to SPPs and the other way round for excitation enhancement. The analytical models are simple but powerful. In fact, they are expressed in terms of the physical quantities of SPPs and thus gain us deeper understanding and better control of the processes. For example, for the spontaneous emission enhancement, we find, for a particular SPP propagation direction, the energy transfer rate from emitters to SPPs depends on the interplay between the Ohmic absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs. Weaker radiation damping and stronger absorption lead to faster transfer from the emitters to SPPs, yielding stronger emission. On the other hand, for the excitation enhancement, the transfer rate from SPPs to emitters is expressed as the ratio between the square of the total decay rate and the radiative decay rate. Such ratio further collapses into the field intensity enhancement rendered by SPPs. Therefore, larger field enhancement induces stronger excitation. As a result, by tailoring the absorption and radiation damping of SPPs, we manage to optimize the fluorescence enhancement. The results have been confirmed with finite-difference time-domain simulations with good agreement. More importantly, as the models are expressed in measurable quantities, both transfer rates can be determined experimentally. For the objective 2, we have developed experimental skills for measuring the energy transfer rates. The methods are completely frequency domain based without involving time-resolved techniques such as fluorescence lifetime spectroscopy. By combining the abovementioned models with angle- and polarization-resolved reflectivity and photoluminescence spectroscopy, we determine the quantities required for the models one by one. For example, we measure the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs by using angle-resolved reflectivity spectroscopy and then the energy transfer rates by the Fourier-space photoluminescence spectroscopy. For the photoluminescence measurements, either a goniometer or a wide-field microscope is used depending on the sample area. Our approach is intriguing due to its simplicity, which requires routine optics and several mechanical stages, and thus is highly affordable to most of the research laboratories. For the objective 4 & 5, as the excitation and emission energy transfer rates of the emitters are strongly dependently on the decay rates of SPPs, how one can tailor the geometry of the periodic arrays is of importance. We have developed basic understanding of the effects of the lattice and basis of the system on the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs. For example, the spectral positions of the resonances are defined by the momentum matching equation deduced from the empty lattice approximation. On the other hand, when the size of the basis is smaller than wavelength, the radiation damping basically is governed by Mie scattering from a single basis. Interactions between bases are considered negligible. Based on such knowledge, we are now in the position of rationally design plasmonic systems with desired emission enhancement and profile.

14304314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304314.value: By combing rate equation and temporal coupled mode theory, we have formulated the energy transfers rates between light emitters and surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) for the excitation and emission enhancement processes in surface plasmon mediated emission under weak coupling (part C, No. 1,3-5). The models take into consideration of the physical quantities of SPPs and thus provide physical understanding of the excitation and emission processes. The analytical models are found to agree well with the results from the finite-different time-domain simulations (part C, No. 3-5). Based on the models, we have measured the energy transfer rates in the excitation and emission enhancements (part C, No. 3-5) and conclude the transfer rate from SPPs to emitters in the excitation process depends solely on the field enhancement while the rate from emitters to SPPs at a particular propagation direction in the emission enhancement relies on not only the field enhancement but also the spectral density of states. The coupling between two resonators, for example a light emitter and a SPP mode, has also been studied in a strong coupling regime (part C, No. 7). In particular, as the coupling occurs in an open and dissipative environment, the interaction constant between two resonators are complex. By using couple mode theory, we have developed a new scheme to extract such constant both theoretically and experimentally. Finally, we begin to explore the chiral surface plasmon mediated emission by studying the polarization conversion arising from the periodic structures (part C, No. 2). We have measured the rotation angle and ellipticity of the reflections at different incident and sample azimuthal angles under different polarizations. Our results indicate the reflections arise from the interference between the nonresonant background and the SPP radiation damping. More importantly, we find the polarization is defined by the propagation direction and the interplay between the radiative decay and absorption rates of SPPs.

14304314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304314.value: We have carried out in-depth studies on the surface plasmon mediated emission enhancement from periodic metallic arrays. However, the bases so far are limited to circular nanoholes. In fact, the bases can be extended to cover different shapes such as ellipse, rectangle, cross, L-shape, gammadion, etc, where more interesting physics will involve. For example, for the L- and gammadion shapes in which the mirror symmetry is broken, the energy transfer rates between the light emitters and SPPs could be different when under circular polarized excitations. In addition, our approach has only been applied to the optically pumped systems but not the electrically pumped counterparts although they share the same physics. Therefore, the next step should move towards the current injected light emitting diodes coupled with suitable plasmonic systems.

14304314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304314.value: When light emitters are placed in close proximity to a plasmonic system, energy can be transferred between the emitters and surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). The strong plasmonic fields can strongly enhance the excitation of the emitters. At the same time, the emission rate is also increased because of the large density-of-states created by SPPs. These two processes work hand in hand in producing the surface plasmon mediated fluorescence (SPMF). As SPMF has stimulated numerous applications in solid-state lighting, sensing, and bio detection, it is currently under intensive investigation. In particular, the knowledge of the energy transfer rates from the SPPs to the emitters and vice versa is of great importance. However, the excitation and emission processes are usually entangled together, making the differentiation difficult. In this project, we have studied the processes quantitatively by combining the rate equation model and temporal coupled mode theory. Remarkably, we find the excitation and coupling rates can be expressed in terms of measurable quantities, which can be accessed by performing angle- and polarization- resolved reflectivity and photoluminescence spectroscopy.

14305014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305014.value: Latent variables that should be examined using multiple observed variables are common in substantive research. The assessment of the interrelationships among latent variables is often necessary to build a model that reflects reality. Structural equation modeling is well recognized as the most important statistical tool for such assessment. In recent years, structural equation models (SEMs) have been extensively applied to behavioral, medical, and social sciences. Basic SEMs have been generalized in many directions to cope with complex situations in reality. Important extensions include semiparametric SEM for estimating the true distributions of latent variables and residual errors as well as relaxing their normality assumption, SEM with a nonparametric structural equation (termed as nonparametric SEM below) for capturing the true relationships among latent variables using unspecified smoothing functions, and transformation SEM for handling highly non-normal data. Classical methods in SEMs are incapable of handling such advanced SEMs. Thus, the Bayesian approach has become a dominant tool used for recent SEM development. In addition to its power and efficiency in managing complex models and/or data structures, the Bayesian approach offers other advantages, such as the capability to utilize useful prior information and the production of reliable results for small samples. The local influence (LI) analysis, which is a popular statistical method used for identifying influential observations and for assessing the stability of estimation outputs with respect to model inputs, has been widely applied in many statistical models. However, most LI results were obtained in connection with the maximum likelihood (ML) approach. Results of Bayesian LI analysis are relatively limited. This project mainly aims to develop Bayesian LI methods for advanced SEMs with complex data, including but not limited to the abovementioned nonparametric, semiparametric, and transformation SEMs. In addition to identifying influential observations, as in ML-based methods, the Bayesian LI analysis also identifies the important influential aspects related to the Bayesian approach, such as those related to sampling and prior distributions. This study also develops efficient and user-friendly computer programs to produce the results. These programs will be made freely available for practitioners. Finally, the developed methodologies are applied to real problems in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

14305014.label: Realisation of objectives
14305014.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. We have developed Bayesian LI methods to simultaneously detect outliers/influential observations, examine model assumptions, and perform sensitivity analysis for advanced SEMs with complex data. As specified, we applied different perturbation schemes to conduct LI analyses for various advanced SEMs, including (a) mixture SEMs, (b) longitudinal SEMs, (c) nonparametric SEMs, and (d) transformation SEMs. The objective in Item 1 of Section 5.2 (related to development of Bayesian LI methods for advanced SEMs) is fully achieved. 2. We have developed efficient and user-friendly computer programs to produce statistical results. The satisfactory performance of the proposed methodologies has been well demonstrated by simulation studies in the publications listed in Section 8. The computer codes, many of which were written in freely available software such as WinBUGS, R, and Rcpp, have been published or provided in freely available websites for general use (see the corresponding papers in Section 8). The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 (related to computer programs) are fully achieved. 3. We have applied the developed methodologies to analyze many real datasets that are relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The real-life applications include but are not limited to the followings: (1) A study of osteoporosis prevention and control for old Chinese men in Hong Kong. (2) A study on diabetic kidney disease conducted by the Institute of Diabetes at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. (3) A study on survival of patients after acute myocardial infarction. (4) A study on the Interuniversity Consortium for Political and Social Research. (5) A study on the determinants of the capital structure of Chinese-listed companies. (6) A study of the National Longitudinal Surveys of Youth in the US. (7) A childhood cancer survivor study. (8) A medical cost study of chronic heart failure patients. Important findings and insights have been obtained through these real applications. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to applications) are fully achieved.

14305014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305014.value: Structural equation models (SEMs) are the most important models to assess the interrelationships among latent and observed variables. Recently, a variety of advanced SEMs have been developed to manage complex data structures in various disciplines. The local influence analysis is a popular statistical method for identifying influential observations and assessing the stability of estimation outputs with respect to model inputs. Traditional local influence analyses have mainly focused on the maximum likelihood approach. Results of Bayesian local influence analysis are relatively limited. This project has developed Bayesian local influence methods for advanced SEMs, including but not limited to mixture, longitudinal, nonparametric, and transformation SEMs. The novel methods developed in this project contribute significantly to the field of SEMs and statistical diagnosis. The methodologies have been applied to many real studies. Important findings and new insights were obtained. The major results are represented by 15 publications in prestigious international journals, such as Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, Statistica Sinica, Sociological Methods and Research, Multivariate Behavioral Research, Statistics in Medicine, Statistical Methods and Medical Research, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, and Computational Statistics and Data Analysis. Important extensions of the proposed methods (beyond the project objectives) have also been considered.

14305114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305114.value: 在這個計畫中主研究員計畫研究具有非負或非正二次雙截曲率 Kaler流形的結構。尤其是，他想要瞭解具有非負二次雙截曲率 緊緻Kahler流形與 b_2=1的 Kahler C-空間之間的關係。他還想 在沒有假設曲率是有界情況下研究非緊完備Kahler流形上 Ricci 流和在單值化問題中可能的應用. 主研究員還想在完備非緊流形上研究實閉 (p,p) 形式的 Poincare-Lelong方程. 主研究員想研究和准局域質量和正質量定理相關的幾何問題. 首先主研究員想要研究Brown-York准局域質量是否Wang-Yau 准局域質量的局部或全局最低值和hoop-conjecture的關係. 主研究員還想研究帶邊緊緻流形數量曲率剛性現象, 這是與 Min Oo 的猜想有關. 主研究員還想研究Bartnik數據的延展問題.

14305114.label: Realisation of objectives
14305114.value: Objectives of the project are: 1. Uniformization of Kähler manifolds and related PDE problems: (i) To understand compact Kähler manifolds in terms of quadratic bisectional curvature; (ii) To study Kähler-Ricci flow under more relaxed curvature conditions and heat equation for the Hodge Laplace to understand structure of complete noncompact Kähler manifolds. 2. Quasi-local mass and related geometric problems: (i) To study the relation between Wang-Yau quasilocal mass and the Brown-York mass related extension problem for compact surface with positive curvature; (ii) To study scalar curvature rigidity problem for compact manifolds with boundary. For the first objective, with the collaboration with Chau and Li the PI obtained the following: (a) We proved a long time existence result for Kähler-Ricci flow for U(n) invariant Kähler metrics on C^n which initial metric with nonnegative bisectional curvature. More general, long time existence result for U(n) initial metric which is uniformly equivalent to a U(n) invariant metric with nonnegative bisectional curvature that is not a so-called cigar. (b) Some comparison of existence times for Kähler-Ricci flows with different initial metrics g_0, h_0. Assuming g_0, h_0 both have bounded curvature, then the maximal existence times T(h_0) of solution of Kähler-Ricci flow with initial data h_0 can be estimated in terms of the corresponding existence time T(g_0) plus the C^0 distance of h_0 from g_0. Curvature estimates have also been obtained. Using this, we gave some application on the existence time estimates for initial data which may not have bounded curvature. Motivated by some existence results on Ricci flow with curvature bounded by c/t, the PI and one of his students Huang studied the Ricci flow with this kind of curvature bound in the Kähler category. Unlike some previous results, here we do not assume the initial metric to have bounded curvature (a) The first question is about whether the Ricci flow will preserve the Kähler condition. We proved that if the curvature g(t) of the solution Ricci flow is bounded by c/t and if the initial metric is Kähler, then g(t) is also Kähler. As an application, we proved that a complete Kähler manifold with nonnegative complex sectional curvature and with maximum volume growth is biholomorphic to C^n. (b) Another question is whether the Kähler-Ricci flow will preserve the nonnegativity of bisectional curvature. We proved that if the curvature of the flow is bounded by a/t where a is a small constant depending only on the dimension of the manifold, then the Kähler-Ricci flow will preserve the nonnegativity of bisectional curvature. In particular, if the initial metric g_0 is C^0 close to a metric with bounded curvature and if it is Kähler with nonnegative bisectional curvature, then we can deform the initial metric through Kähler-Ricci flow which also has nonnegative bisectional curvature. In particular, if g_0 also has maximum volume growth, then the manifold is biholomorphic to C^n. For the second objective, the PI has obtained the following with his collaborators. (a) It is known that one can compute the ADM mass of an asymptotically flat (AF) manifold as the limit of the integral of the Einstein tensor applied to the radial conformal Killing vector field and the unit outward normal to coordinate spheres. Similar formulae holds for asymptotically hyperbolic space (AH) for the total mass integrals, which can be considered as a vector in Minkowski space. Using this, Miao, Xie and the PI proved that the ADM mass of an AF manifold is the limit of some quasi-local mass integrals of the coordinate spheres which involve the mean curvature and the principal curvatures of the coordinate spheres. Similar results are also obtained by AH manifolds. In this case, quasi-local mass quantities are used. (b) Motivated by these result, Miao and the PI consider some functional on space of metrics on compact manifolds with smooth boundary in terms of the Einstein tensor and other geometric quantities. We characterize critical points of such functional. In some case, we can conclude the critical is Einstein. We also consider critical points of metrics of functional involving second mean curvatures of the boundary. Some relation between the critical points and static metrics are given. (c) With Shi the PI obtained results for singular metrics on compact and noncompact manifolds in terms of scalar curvature. For the compact case, we study properties of singular metrics which are related to the Yamabe invariant of the manifold. In the noncompact case, we study positive mass theorem for singular metrics, which have also been studied by many people. (d) With Wang, the PI obtained some conformal positive mass theorems, which are motivated by the study of uniqueness of black holes. With Liu, the PI computed explicitly the Brown-York mass of the coordinate spheres of the Kerr metric in Boyer-Linquist coordinates. The results have been generalized by other people. I think the objectives have been achieved.

14305114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305114.value: (a) In [7], (item 8), Chau, Li and the proved that if the initial metric g_0 is U(n) invariant on C^n and has nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature, then the Kähler-Ricci flow has long time solution g(t) with bounded curvature for t>0. After rescaling g(t) will converge to the standard metric on C^n. In [1](item 8), Chau, Li and the PI proved that the maximal existence time T(g_0) is a continuous function with respect to the C^0 norm in the set of Kähler metrics with bounded curvature on a fixed complex manifolds. By obtaining some curvature exismates, results are extended to Kähler-Ricci flow with initial metrics which may have unbounded curvature. (b) In [2] (item 8), Huang and PI proved that if the initial metric g_0 is Kähler and if g(t) is a solution to the Ricci flow so that the curvature of g(t) is bounded by C/t for some C>0 for t>0, then g(t) is also Kähler. Huang and the PI also proved that nonnegativity of bisectional curvature will be preserved under Kähler-Ricci flow provided the curvature of g(t) is bounded by a/t where a is small enough depending on the dimension of the manifold. Applications to the study on a uniformization conjecture by Yau are given. (c) In [3](item 8) Miao, Xie and the PI obtained results relating some quasi-local mass quantities of the coordinate spheres of AF or AH manifolds and the total mass, generalizing some known results in dimension three. In [4] (item 8), Miao and the PI introduced some functionals on space of metrics on compact manifolds with smooth boundary in terms of the Einstein tensor and other geometric quantities. Under certain conditions, the critical points are Einstein metrics or static metrics. (d) In [8] (item 8) Shi and the PI proved that on a compact manifold, a singular metric is Lipschitz for example with small singular set, and realizes the nonpositive Yamabe invariant, then it must be Einstein. In the noncompact case, we proved a positive mass theorem for singular metrics, which have also been studied by many people. (e ) In [6] (item 8) Wang and the PI obtained conformal positive mass theorems. The results are motivated by the study of uniqueness of black holes. In [5] (item 8) Liu and PI are able to compute the Brown-York quasilocal mass for the coordinate spheres of the Kerr metric in Boyer-Linquist coordinates.

14305114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305114.value: We want to remove the assumption on the smallness that the curvature is bounded by a/t with a small on the preservation of nonnegativity of bisectional curvature for solution to the Kähler-Ricci flow. Existence of Kähler-Ricci without assuming the initial metric has bounded curvature is also interesting and useful. Previous, existence results have been obtained under addition assumption that the metric is U(n) invariant. There is some progress by the PI. For singular metric realizing the nonpositive Yamabe invariant, there are two open questions. In the result of Shi and the PI we assume the metric is in some Sobolev space. One would like to see if one can relax the condition. In fact, in dimension three there are some results by assuming the metrics are in L^infty. Another more subtle question is for the case with positive Yamabe invariant. This is not well-understood even for smooth metrics. In case of quasilocal mass, we usually need to embed a surface to some reference spacetime. There is some qusilocal mass type quantity introduced recently in terms of the intrinsic geometry. One would like to understand more on this kind of quantiy.

14305114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305114.value: The shape of an object may evolve because of some external force. For example, a small stone in the sea may evolve to be more and more round. If the shape of the stone is higher irregular, namely if the curvature of the surface is extremely large, what can we expect. In this project, we consider the evolution equation similar to this situation. This is also related to the so-called complex structure of the geometric object. From daily experience, one cannot distinguish between gravitation and acceleration (or deceleration) if we only confine to small region. We want to measure the total energy of a bounded region—quasi-local energy. We want to measure the total energy of an isolated system. In this project, some relations between them have been found. Some properties of the total energy and quasilocal energy have been found.

14305214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305214.value: 稀薄原子氣體的玻色愛因斯坦凝聚體（BEC）是一種在溫度接近絕對零度時通過玻色愛因斯坦凝聚相變產生的宏觀量子物質，自從1995年首次實現，BEC一直以來都是量子現象的絕佳載體。自旋是粒子的內禀角動量，它使粒子產生磁矩，而材料的磁性就源於材料中粒子磁矩的相對取向，大約80年之前，海森堡就已經指出自旋之間的相互作用可以決定它們的相對取向，但直到今天，關於磁性問題的很多細節都還沒有被完全理解。 得益於光緒囚禁技術的發展，BEC中原子的自旋自由度可以被釋放出來形成具有內部自旋自由度的旋量BEC，這一發現使得我們可以把量子氣體和磁性這兩個物理學中及具吸引力的方向結合起來，利用這樣一個獨特的平台，我們可以研究同時具有外部和內部相干性的量子物質。之前，對於同種原子的旋量BEC已經進行了深入的研究，並已經取得了很多的成就，包括基態的性質，內态直接的相干混合及非平衡態動力學，自旋織構，自旋壓縮和糾纏等。 在本工作中，基於我們最近的一些研究進展，包括銣和鈉原子的雙BEC，以及剛剛觀測到的這兩種原子之間的異核相干自旋交換，我們計劃將旋量量子氣體的研究擴展到兩種不同原子。在這一系統中，異核的自旋交換以及它與同核自旋交換的互相影響會帶來比同核旋量量子氣體更加豐富的物理內容。在已有的初步結果的基礎上，我們計劃在此一新奇旋量系統上開展一系列的研究，包括對純異核自旋動力學的詳細研究，同核和異核自旋動力學直接的相互影響，以及這一系統的基態性質等。為了更加高效和可信的進行數據收集，我們也將進行一些系統的升級。 這一工作中的發現將進一步拓展超冷量子氣體的研究領域，促進我們對旋量量子氣體的知識，並提供對於量子磁性問題的認知。

14305214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305214.value: The main purpose of this project is to investigate a novel quantum gas system: a Bose-Bose mixture with spinor degree of freedom. Such a spinor mixture had never been explored before by any other groups. Based on some preliminary heteronuclear spin dynamics observed before the funding starts, we carried out a systematic study with this novel system. Following our research plan, we first finished all major technical upgrades, including the more stable Na laser cooling system, more precise low magnetic field, a 946 nm “magic wavelength” optical trap, and internal state manipulation. These upgrades made the system’s stability and repeatability much better than before. This has enabled us to carry out a clear investigation of the heteronuclear spin dynamics. For the laser cooling of Na, we developed a 4-pass AOM system to generate the repumping light. This result was published in Review of Science Instruments in 2017. With the improved system, we were able to finish a detailed studied on the non-equilibrium heteronuclear spin-exchange dynamics which we first observed in the preliminary investigation. The spin-exchange processes are much richer in heteronuclear spinor system than in the familiar single species spinor systems. There are 6 possible spin exchange channels and we studied one of them in detail the dependence on an external magnetic field and found a resonant-like feature. This was later understood as the competition between the total Zeeman energy difference and the spin-dependent interaction. The resonance happens at the point when the two energy scales match with each other. In addition, we also found a unique way of controlling the spinor dynamics with differential vector light shift. These results were published in Physical Review Letters in 2015. We also investigated the long-term evolution starting from a mean-field ground state and found spin dynamics driven by quantum fluctuation. Currently, there is still some difficulty in the theoretical modeling. We also tried to use Na as magnetic impurity to probe its homonuclear dynamics at near zero B field under the influence of the Rb. Somehow, we couldn’t not observe signatures of the heteronuclear spin exchange. A possible explanation is the homonuclear spin dynamics always dominates the heteronuclear one. These topics will be studied further soon. We also studied controlling the heteronculear spin dynamics with microwave and light and observed nice results. We are writing a paper on this experiment now.

14305214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305214.value: Spin dynamics control with vector light shift is a unique capability of heteronuclear spinor systems. Since light field can be controlled to near arbitrary geometry, it may be used to realize a magnetic spin lattice by using a standing wave. At the node and anti-node of the lattice, the vector light shifts are different and thus the spin dynamics will also have different rate. This may lead to interesting excitation and topological effects. Another possibility is to combine the heteronuclear spin exchange with spin-orbit coupling (SOC). It is hard to realize SOC for Na, but relatively easy for Rb. If we apply Raman beams to generate SOC for Rb, the spin exchange interaction could lead to SOC in Na. This is a novel way of exploring synthetic gauge field in ultracold systems.

14305214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305214.value: Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of dilute atomic bosons is a macroscopic quantum matter which forms following the Bose-Einstein condensation phase transition at near absolute zero temperatures. Spin is the intrinsic angular momentum of particles and is the origin of the magnetic moments of them. Magnetism of materials is just a manifestation of the properties of thee spins and the spin exchange interaction between them. The spinor BEC, which is a BEC with the spin degree of freedom, unifies quantum gases and magnetism together for exploring physics related to quantum matters with both external and internal coherences. In the current work, have, for the first time, extended spinor gases to two species. We observed the coherent spin oscillation between Na and Rb atoms and developed various ways to control them. Specifically, we used the differential Zeeman shifts caused by a magnetic field or a circular polarized light to tune the oscillation amplitude and frequency of the spin dynamics. Our investigations opened a new research direction for ultracold atomic physics. The heteronuclear spin exchange may find application in entanglement generation between different atoms which should have application in quantum information and quantum metrology.
