14305314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305314.value: The aims of this proposal are to (i) investigate the plasmonic switching of gold nanocrystals (NCs) induced by coated polyaniline (PANI) and (ii) utilize the gold/PANI nanostructures to build smart windows/mirrors with greatly improved performances. Smart windows/mirrors, whose transmittance/reflectance can be adjusted by applying external stimuli can greatly improve the comfortability of automobile vehicles and considerably reduce the energy consumptions of air conditioning in buildings. A commonly adopted technique to drive smart windows/mirrors is to use chromic materials, for which electrochromic, gasochromic, photochromic, and thermochromic ones have been tested. Among them, electrochromic materials, including transition metal oxides and conjugated polymers, are most popular. Commercialization has been realized with electrochromic metal oxides. However, they are limited by low coloration efficiencies, slow response speeds, and high redox switching potentials. Conjugated polymers can overcome the limitations associated with metal oxides and further provide higher degrees of color tailorability. Polymers are also of higher processability and suitable for flexible substrates. However, they suffer from degradation, which affects their long-term cyclability and color contrast. Deterioration under high applied electrochemical potentials is one major cause for polymer degradation. Here we propose to integrate a frequently used electrochromic polymer, PANI, with plasmonic gold NCs to achieve high color contrasts under relatively low electrochemical potentials. PANI exhibits distinct dielectric function changes when switched chemically or electrochemically. Gold NCs possess strong absorption and scattering capabilities at plasmon wavelengths. The plasmonic properties of gold NCs are extremely sensitive to their dielectric environment. A minuscule change in the dielectric function of the surrounding environment can cause a large change in the plasmon of adjacent gold NCs. The introduction of gold NCs is thus expected to largely improve the color contrasts of the hybrid system and at the same time avoid the electrochemical deterioration. We will prepare (gold NC core)/(PANI shell) nanostructures and study their plasmonic switching behaviors. For practical applications, we will prepare dense arrays of the nanostructures and nanostructure-based composite films, fabricate smart-window/mirror devices, and examine their electrochemical color-switching behaviors. Buildings and other man-made structures consume ~30% to 40% of the primary energy on the world, where air conditioning costs a large fraction. The success of this proposal is expected to incubate the production of smart windows/mirrors with greatly improved performances, which can remarkably reduce energy consumption, improve living quality, and ease the pressure of environmental pollution in densely populated areas, such as Hong Kong and cities in mainland China.

14305314.label: Realisation of objectives
14305314.value: This project has four objectives: (1) prepare (gold nanocrystal core)/(PANI shell) nanostructures and study the plasmonic switching behaviors on the single-particle level; (2) study the plasmonic switching behaviors of the substrate-coupled core/shell nanostructures on the single-particle level; (3) prepare dense arrays of the core/shell nanostructures and examine their electrochemical color-switching behaviors; (4) prepare nanostructure/PEDOT:PSS composite films and investigate their electrochemical color-switching behaviors. I would like to describe the realization of these objectives one by one below. We developed a robust method for uniformly coating polyaniline (PANI) on differently shaped and sized colloidal Au nanocrystals (nanospheres, nanorods and nanobipyramids). The coating of PANI is realized through surfactant-assisted chemical oxidative polymerization. The resultant polymer coating is in the emeraldine form of PANI. The thickness of the PANI coating can be adjusted by changing the monomer concentration and/or repeating the coating process multiple times. The average thickness of the PANI coating can be varied from 1.7 nm to a few hundred nanometers. We studied the plasmon switching behaviors of the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals at the single-particle level. The plasmon switching was realized by changing either the pH or applying an electrochemical potential. PANI exhibits large changes in its dielectric function when it is proton-doped or dedoped, or when it is oxidized or reduced electrochemically. As a result, the PANI coating enables an unprecedented switching performance on the localized plasmon resonance of colloidal Au nanocrystals, with the modulation depth in the scattering intensity and the plasmonic spectral shift reaching up to 10 dB and 100 nm, respectively (Advanced Materials, 2017, 29, 1604862). The plasmon switching is highly reversible, with a remarkable stability over 200 cycles. The plasmonic switching time is less than 10 ms. Moreover, the plasmon energy can be precisely controlled within the shift range by applying an electrochemical potential. Our (Au nanocrystal core)/(PANI shell) nanostructures provide a facile, low-cost, yet robust approach to the design and fabrication of high-performance plasmonic switches. They will also ﬁnd intriguing applications in a wide range of areas, such as smart windows, information displays, anti-counterfeiting inks, and pH-responsive photothermal systems for cancer therapy. With these results, the first objective is completely achieved. We deposited the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals on cover glass substrates, indium tin oxide (ITO)-coated glass slides and thin Au films that were fabricated by electron-beam evaporation. On the glass and ITO substrates, which have small refractive indexes, the plasmon switching behaviors of the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals were found to be mainly determined by the core@shell nanostructures themselves. The effect of the substrates is small. When the core@shell nanostructures were deposited on the AU films, the plasmon coupling between the Au nanocrystal and the Au film occurred. However, we found that the plasmon coupling behavior exhibited large fluctuations even for the same core@shell nanostructure sample. The fluctuation was caused by the rough surface of the AU films. In addition, our Au films were found to be unstable when liquid solutions were applied on them. We also purchased commercial Au films and encountered the same problem. We then changed the Au films with chemically-synthesized Au nanplates, which have atomically smooth surfaces (Nanoscale, 2016, 8, 17645 and Advanced Functional Materials, 2018, 28, 1705516). The PANI-coated Au nanospheres were deposited on Au nanoplates to form Au nanosphere-nanoplate heterodimers. Active plasmonic Fano resonance switching was enabled by varying the refractive index of the PANI layer that ﬁlled in the gap between the Au nanosphere and the Au nanoplate through proton-doping and dedoping. A reversible spectral shift of 20 nm was observed on the individual heterodimers during switching. The maximal spectral shift decreased as the interparticle gap distance was enlarged, showing a strong dependence of the spectral shift on the local electric ﬁeld intensity enhancement in the gap region. Our results provide insights into the development of plasmonic structures supporting actively switchable Fano resonances, which can lead to new technological applications, such as switchable cloaking and display, dynamic coding of optical signals, color sorting and ﬁltering. The Au heterodimers with PANI in the gap can also be applied for the sensing of local environmental parameters such as pH values and heavy metal ions. These results fulfill the second objective of this project. We deposited the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals on ITO substrates by drop-casting. The real-time observation of the spectral changes of the ensemble core@shell nanostructures under the electrochemical switching was realized by use of a custom-designed electrochemical cell. The ensemble PANI-coated Au nanocrystals exhibit good electrochemical plasmonic switching performances. Reversible plasmonic shifts of 20, 50, and 150 nm are obtained for the ensemble PANI-coated Au nanospheres, nanorods, and nanobipyramids deposited on the transparent conductive substrates (Advanced Materials, 2017, 29, 1604862). Moreover, with a much smaller amount of materials, our core@shell nanostructure monolayers show peak extinction values and maximal modulation depths that are comparable to those of micrometer-scale thick PANI ﬁlms. Our results open a route to the design and development of reversibly switchable, plasmon-based color pixels, displays, and smart windows using high-quality colloidal metal nanocrystals. In addition, the real-time control of the plasmon resonance of PANI-coated Au nanocrystals also offers a great possibility for developing highly compact photonic and optoelectronic devices. These results fulfill the third objective of this project. In our original proposal, we proposed to disperse the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals into PEDOT:PSS to form composite films for active plasmon switching. In PEDOT:PSS, PEDOT is a conjugated, conductive polymer with positive charges along the backbone. PSS, which is negatively charged, is added to form a macromolecular salt. PEDOT is therefore a major component in terms of the electrical conductance. At that time, we could not coat PEDOT on colloidal Au nanocrystals. So we proposed the dispersion of the PANI-coated Au nanocrystals in PEDOT:PSS to realize active plasmon switching. During the progress of the project, we discovered an approach for coating different conjugated polymers on pre-synthesized colloidal Au nanocrystals. The approach is based on electrochemical polymerization. It is general and suitable for PANI, polypyrrole, PEDOT, and polyindole. It also works for colloidal nanocrystals made of Pt and Pd. Because these conjugated polymers all show electrochemical potential-dependent dielectric functions, plasmonic metal nanocrystals coated with these polymers also exhibit active switching behaviors. We have finished this sub-project, which is now at the stage of the manuscript preparation. With these results, the fourth objective is completely achieved. We also carried out several experiments that are closely relevant to the project. For example, we synthesized Au nanoplates and high-aspect-ration Ag nanorods and studied their plasmonic properties. Because of our knowledge and experience on active plasmon switching, we were invited to contribute one review article on Chemical Reviews (2018, 118, 3054) and one progress report on Advanced Materials (2018, 30, 1704338). Our review article is comprehensive. It summarizes the principles, structures and applications of active plasmonics. Our progress report highlights the most promising recent examples of utilizing advanced plasmonic materials for the realization of dynamic color display. It also discusses the performances, advantages, and disadvantages of different technologies. Emphasis is placed on both the potential and possible limitations of various hybrid materials for dynamic plasmonic color display.

14305314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305314.value: There are four major findings out of this project. (i) A robust chemical approach is developed for the coating of polyaniline onto variously shaped and sized Au nanocrystals. The approach is based on surfactant-assisted oxidative polymerization. The thickness of the polymer coating can be controlled. The polyaniline-coated Au nanocrystals exhibit excellent plasmon switching performances (large scattering intensity modulation depths, reversible large plasmon shifts, high stability, short switching time) that can be controlled either chemical or electrochemically. (ii) The polyaniline-coated Au nanocrystals are deposited on transparent conductive substrates through drop-casting to give thin films. Such thin films can be macroscopic in area. The ensemble core@shell nanostructures exhibit remarkable plasmon switching performances that are controllable electrochemically. In particular, the plasmon energy can be precisely controlled within the shift range by applying an appropriate electrochemical potential. (iii) Au nanocrystal heterodimers are ingeniously formed with the gap filled with polyaniline. The thickness of the polyaniline layer can be controlled. The active switching of plasmonic Fano resonance is realized. This result is important because plasmonic Fano resonance allows for attractive applications such as electromagnetically induced transparency, light trapping, and refractometric sensing with high ﬁgures of merit, and the active switching of plasmonic Fano resonance holds great promise in modulating optical signals, dynamically harvesting light energy, and constructing switchable plasmonic sensors. (iv) A general approach is developed for coating different conjugated polymers on pre-synthesized colloidal noble metal nanocrystals through electrochemical polymerization. The approach is applicable for polyaniline, polypyrrole, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) and polyindole. It is also expected to be applicable for other polymers. Our results open a route to the design and development of reversibly switchable, plasmon-based color pixels, displays, and smart windows using high-quality colloidal plasmonic metal nanocrystals. In addition, the real-time control of the plasmon resonance of the polymer-coated plasmonic metal nanocrystals also offers a great possibility for developing highly compact photonic and optoelectronic devices. Ten papers are published out of this project. There are two on each of Advanced Materials, Advanced Optical Materials and Nanoscale. There is one on each of ACS Nano, Advanced Functional Materials, Advanced Healthcare Materials and Chemical Reviews. Two PhD students are trained on this project. One is in materials science and engineering, and the other is in physics. Both of them have successfully defended for their PhD degrees in August 2018.

14305314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305314.value: There are two future directions based on this project. (i) Design and fabricate optical devices using high-quality plasmonic metal nanocrystals that are coated with conjugated polymers. Through the control of the dielectric functions of the conjugated polymers, the phase, intensity, polarization and wavelength of light waves can be controlled reversibly at the position of each core@shell nanostructure. As a result, the optical devices made of the core@shell nanostructures will be able to control the light intensity, light propagation direction, realize dynamically reconfigurable color control and even lead to the invention of lenses with dynamically adjustable focus lengths. (ii) We have realized the active plasmon switching by coating polyaniline on pre-synthesized gold nanocrystals at both the single-particle and ensemble levels. The switching performances are evaluated by recording scattering or extinction spectra. The spectral changes ultimately determine the color changes. However, a great deal of effort will be required to realize practically meaningful color changes. First, a sufficient amount of the core@shell nanostructures is required to assemble together to give bright colors. Second, the plasmon wavelengths of the core@shell nanostructures have to be adjusted to satisfy the requirements of different applications, such as switchable color displays and smart windows.

14305314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305314.value: Colors are almost existent everywhere around us. Our eyes are always sensitive to any vivid color changes. Colors not only can make our lives cheerful and beautiful, but also carry and convey extremely rich information. To produce rich colors and vivid color changes has been a research goal for centuries. Nanocrystals made of noble metals, such as gold and silver, have many electrons that are move nearly freely. Under light with proper wavelengths (that is, proper colors), the free electrons in metal nanocrystals can oscillate collectively and interact strongly with the light. Metal nanocrystals therefore exhibit rich colors. Their colors are very sensitively dependent on the surrounding environment. If the surrounding environment is changed, the color of a metal nanocrystal will also change. If we coat a switchable material on a metal nanocrystal, the color of the metal nanocrystal can also be switched. In this project, we have found that conductive polymers can function as such materials. We have developed approaches to uniformly coat conductive polymers on pre-synthesized metal nanocrystals and realize the reversible color switching. Our discovery will be useful for the design and development of reversibly switchable color displays, smart windows and compact photonic and optoelectronic devices.

14305714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305714.value: Rocks in the upper crust of the Earth are embedded with pore space made up of numerous cavities with dimensions ranging over ten orders of magnitude. They include minute pores on the submicron scale and elongated fractures and faults that may extend over hundreds of km. In most instances, these features in the pore space are interconnected, thus constituting a percolative structure for fluid flow. A fundamental understanding of the transport properties of rock is of importance in many natural resources and environmental applications, such as the migration and extraction of conventional and unconventional hydrocarbon resources, contaminant transport, sequestration of carbon dioxide in geological repository, nuclear waste disposal and reservoir-induced seismicity. It is well known that the transport properties are intimately related to the pore space, but given its geometric complexity, quantitative characterization of the pertinent geometric attributes poses significant challenge, thus hindering a deeper rock physics understanding of the interplay between pore geometry and transport properties. This proposal builds upon scientific advances on two fronts. For porous sandstones, the pore geometry is such that it can now be imaged in 3D comprehensively using X-ray microcomputed tomography. Furthermore, advances in computation have opened up the possibility of directly calculating the transport properties from the 3D images. A focus of many such digital rock physics studies has been to develop codes for simulating permeability in a specific rock, and there is a paucity of systematic investigation that integrates experimental and digital rock physics research on sandstones over a spectrum of porosity and anisotropy. Accordingly we propose to measure the electrical and hydraulic transport properties of four sandstones in the laboratory, characterize their pore geometry using microCT, and formulate a multi-scale hybrid scheme (with lattice Boltzmann and finite element simulations) to calculate the permeability and formation factor. The interconnected porosity and flow paths for electrical and hydraulic transport will be characterized. The overall objective of the proposed project is to develop a unified computational scheme for digital rock physics that can predict accurately the macroscopic transport properties and anisotropy, but more importantly, it should, in conjunction with the laboratory measurements, elucidate the fundamental physics behind the interplay of pore geometry and transport properties in an important reservoir rock.

14305714.label: Realisation of objectives
14305714.value: 1. MicroCT data of high quality have been acquired for two types of Benheim sandstone, Bleurswiller sandstone and Boise sandstone. 2. Hydraulic permeability of the sandstones has been determined in a gas permeameter. Electrical conductivity and formation factor of samples saturated with fluid of a range of salinity have been characterized. In particular, the anisotropy of these transport properties have been characterized, and this is probably one of the first set of such systematic measurements. 3. Segmentation and pore geometry have been conducted on the microCT images. 4. The numerical code has been set up and tested on the acquired CT data. 5. Comprehensive lattice Boltzmann and finite element simulations of the transport properties. 6. Systematic synthesis of the unique data set from rock physics experiments, CT imaging and digital rock physics modeling to arrive at insights into how pore space geometry controls hydraulic and electrical transport in a porous reservoir rock.

14305714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305714.value: We were able to develop a comprehensive voxel-based computation scheme to simulate the transport properties of porous rocks. The hybrid computation scheme is based on a hierarchical multi-scale approach for pore-scale simulation of hydraulic permeability and formation factor consistently using the lattice Boltzmann method, which is then linked with finite element simulation in a homogenized scheme to compute and upscale the transport properties to specimen scale. The power of this innovative approach has been demonstrated on microCT data of Fontainebleau sandstone. The simulated permeability and formation factor have magnitude and anisotropy that are in good agreement with experimental rock physics data. Together with results on connected porosity and specific surface area, they provide useful insights into how pore geometry controls the evolution of the transport properties. This pioneer effort in digital rock physics was presented by Sun & Wong (2018). In parallel the computational scheme has been implemented on three other sandstones, and the new simulations and syntheses of all the results highlight the influence of clay content and bedding anisotropy on transport properties of porous sandstones. A comprehensive manuscript is still in preparation for future submission. Our digital rock physics research highlights the gap in our understanding of the connection between pore geometry complexity, damage development and poroelastic properties (including Skempton's coefficient, Biot's coefficient, compressibility and permeability), especially in the presence of preexisting and stress-induced anisotropy. A theoretical analysis that elucidates this important issue in anostropic poroelasticity was presented by Wong (2017). A challenge in digital rock physics has been the direct in situ 3D imaging of the whole rock sample as it is triaxially compressed. In collaboration with colleagues in Oslo and Strasbourg, we conducted one of the first such investigations at synchrotron facility in Grenoble. The μCT data in 4D provide an integrated perspective of the spatiotemporal evolution of damage and strain localization on scales ranging from grain to continuum. It represents the first unambiguous observation of bifurcation and compaction localization in a porous carbonate rock. The results have been presented by Huang et al. (2019).

14305714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305714.value: Our collaborative research on 4D synchrotron imaging of porous rock opens up a number of future avenues for fundamental investigation of the multi-scale processes associated with mechanical deformation, fluid transport and failure, and we would like to pursue them proactively in the future.

14305714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305714.value: Rocks in the upper crust of the Earth are embedded with pore space made up of numerous cavities with dimensions ranging over ten orders of magnitude. In most instances, these features in the pore space are interconnected, thus constituting a percolative structure for fluid flow. A fundamental understanding of the transport properties of rock is of importance in many natural resources and environmental applications. This project builds upon scientific advances on two fronts: 3D imaging of pore space using X-ray microcomputed tomography, and advances in computation. There have been a paucity of systematic investigations that integrate experimental and digital rock physics research over a spectrum of porosity and anisotropy. In this project a unified computational scheme for digital rock physics was successfully implemented for four porous sandstones. It can predict accurately the macroscopic transport properties and anisotropy, but more importantly, in conjunction with the laboratory measurements, it elucidate the fundamental physics behind the interplay of pore geometry and transport properties in an important reservoir rock. A pioneer effort to conduct 4D imaging of deformation and failure in a synchrotron facility was also pursued.

14306014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306014.value: Thin film solar cells made of polycrystalline materials are highly attractive because of the perceived advantages of cheap cost, easy preparation and ease of scale-up over single crystal-based cells. A successful material for thin film solar cells, CuIn1-xGaxSe2 (CIGS), has demonstrated high cell efficiencies with over ~20% and proved as the choice of absorber for high efficiency thin film polycrystalline solar cells. However, the elements, In and Ga in CIGS are rare and costly, and consequently, they face earth abundance problem for future global scale power applications. Recently, a quaternary compound, Cu2ZnSnS4(CZTS), with In and Ga substituted by cheap and abundant Zn, Sn has been studied as an alternative photovoltaic material. CZTS has similar electrical properties as CIGS and is an excellent cheap substitute for CIGS material. Unfortunately, at present, the conversion efficiency of CZTS solar cell remains low compared with CIGS solar cells. Grain boundaries (GB) together with many other defects were responsible for the low solar cell efficiency of CZTS. In the case of CIGS solar cells, high efficiency has been achieved due to its special energy band alignment at GB which was introduced by the local charge distribution and composition non-uniformity. How is the energy band aligned at GB in CZTS thin film and how does it affect the CZTS photovoltaic performance are key questions for understanding the low efficiency of the CZTS solar cell. Unveiling such information can also provide a direction for optimization of the fabrication method to further improve the efficiency of CZTS. This requires a comprehensive nano-scale electrical characterization of the CZTS at GB. In this project, the scanning probe microscopy (SPM) techniques, which have been extensively used and proved for its power in the CIGS research, will be applied to study the microscopic electrical properties both on the grain and GB of the CZTS solar cells. With different operation modes of the SPM, such as STS, SKPM and CP-AFM, various electrical properties of the thin film at GBs will be investigated and the alignment of the conduction band, valance band and fermi level of CZTS at GBs will be analyzed. Furthermore, the band alignment and local and overall photovoltaic performance will be correlated. Through our experiments, we expect to bring new understanding for the low effeciency of the present CZTS solar cell and to provide guidance for the performance optimization of the future CZTS solar cells. 基于多晶材料的薄膜太阳能电池由于其相对于单晶太阳能电池 所拥有的低成本、易于生产、易于增大电池面积等优势而获得了 广泛的关注。对于薄膜太阳能电池，铜铟镓硒(CIGS)作为一种成 功的材料，已经展示了超过20％的高转换效率，为高效薄膜太阳 能电池吸收层的首选材料之一。然而，CIGS中的铟，镓元素十分 稀有，价格高昂，因而他们也将面对未来全球尺度电力应用中出 现的元素地球丰度问题。 近来， 在CIGS的基础上，由廉价、矿源丰富的锌、锡替代铟、 镓演化而来的四元复合物，铜锌锡硫(CZTS)作为CIGS光电材料 的替代物得到了人们的关注与研究。CZTS与CIGS具有相似的电 学性质，是CIGS材料理想的廉价替代物。然而，到目前为止， CZTS太阳能电池的光电转化效率相对于CIGS仍然处于一个较低 的水平。晶界面以及其他各种缺陷导致了CZTS太阳能电池的低 效率。在CIGS太阳能电池中，电池的高效率归功于由局域电荷 分布以及化学组份分布的不均一性实现的晶界面特殊的能带结 构。了解CZTS薄膜的能带结构，以及其如何影响CZTS的光电性 能是理解目前CZTS低效率的关键。同时对这些信息的了解也可 以提供电池制备工艺优化的新方向，从而进一步提高CZTS太阳 能电池转化效率。而这要求对CZTS晶界面进行全面的纳米尺度 电学性质表征。 本项目将利用在CIGS研究中被广泛采用并证实可行的扫描探针 技术(SPM)研究CZTS太阳能电池晶粒与晶界面的微观电学性质。 利用SPM不同功能的工作模式，例如STS,SKPM以及CP-AFM, 通 过对薄膜晶界面各种电学性质的研究，分析CZTS在晶界面的导 带，价带,费米面位置等能带结构，以及其与太阳能电池局域和 总体光电性能的关联。我们预期我们的研究能够为CZTS太阳能 电池低效率物理机理带来新的理解，并为未来太阳能电池优化指 引方向。

14306014.label: Realisation of objectives
14306014.value: Polycrystalline semiconductors are important energy materials and the grain boundaries (GBs) play crucial role in their electrical transport property. While in general grain boundary is detrimental, for Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS), it was found that the grain boundary is benign to the electrical transport and a record solar cell energy conversion efficiency of 22.9%, the best among all thin film solar cells, has been achieved with a polycrystalline film. In contrast, for Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS), Cu2ZnSnSe4 (CZTSe), and Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 (CZTSSe), their grain boundaries do not appear to be benign to the electrical transport and much lower energy conversion efficiency has been reported. For objective 1 “To investigate the microscopic electrical properties of Cu2ZnSnS4 thin film at the grain boundaries and grains including surface potential difference, energy band gap, local photocurrent and local Schottky contact barriers”, we performed our study by design and prepare well controlled CIGS, CZTS, CZTSe, and CZTSSe samples with decent conversion efficiency. By careful treatment of the samples to remove artifacts, we used a combination of techniques, namely atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM), to probe at nanoscales the composition, structure, and electrical properties of the individual grain boundary in direct comparison to those of the individual grain interior (GI). We discovered that the grain boundary of CIGS in fact consists of a boundary layer of finite thickness in addition to the grain boundary surface/interface. This boundary layer has a definitive composition, structure, and electronic band, independent of the overall Cu content in the CIGS films. Based on the experimental observations, we analyze the energy band alignment at the GBs (Objective 2). The band alignment between grain boundary and grain interior was discovered to be of type II with downward offset for both conduction and valence bands at grain boundary, well correlating to the local copper deficiency and structure. Our findings expressively support the type inversion and large hole barrier in this grain boundary layer, and establish a comprehensive mechanism for the suppression of carrier recombination therein. For CZTS, CZTSe and CZTSSe films, we have for the first time independently determined the band edge positions for both the conduction band and the valence band using scanning tunneling spectroscopy. While the composition of GB was nearly the same as that of GI for both CZTS and CZTSe films, opposite band bending behaviors near GBs were discovered for them. For CZTS, both the conduction band and valence band were found to bend towards the forbidden gap near GBs, resulting in enhanced carrier recombination and relatively poor device performance. For CZTSe, in contrast, both the conduction band and valence band were found to bend away from the forbidden gap near GBs, which could be responsible for the relative better device performance due to the potentially impeded carrier recombination. In the case of CZTSSe thin film, by actively substituting Se with S near GBs, both conduction band and valence band at GBs were demonstrated to bend away from the forbidden gap, leading in principle to a lower carrier recombination at GBs and improved device performance. Our findings could provide a direction for manipulating the band bending between GB and GI to improve the performance of CZTSSe family solar cells. From the correlation between the band alignment at grain boundary and the global photovoltaic performance, the mechanism of the lower conversion efficiency of CZTS compared to the ~20% CIGS solar cells was identified as the large carrier recombination rate at the grain boundary interface due to the lack of core/shell structure found for CIGS (Objective 3). The above results were published in two papers in one of the best journal in energy field, Nano Energy. In addition, there are six invited talks, including one in American Vacuum Society (AVS) annual meeting, presented on these materials. We regard that all the objectives are well achieved. While quite a number of researchers have participated in this work, a Ph. D student was successfully trained.

14306014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306014.value: Polycrystalline Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS) thin film is a well-known light absorber material for photovoltaic solar cells. However, the mechanism of the benignity of its grain boundary (GB) remains in dispute. By using a combination of experimental techniques, we have systematically investigated the compositions, structures, and properties of the grain interior (GI) and GB of the polycrystalline CIGS films at nanometer scale. A definitive Cu deficient layer with thickness depending on the overall Cu content of the films was observed near the non Σ3 GBs with distinctly different characteristics from GIs. The band alignment between GB and GI was discovered to be of type II with downward offset for both conduction and valence bands at GB, well correlating to the local copper deficiency and structure. Our findings expressively support the type inversion and large hole barrier in this GB layer, and establish a comprehensive mechanism for the benignity of the CIGS grain boundaries towards carrier recombination. The above results were published in paper 1 and publicized in various conferences through invited talks. Similarly, the family of polycrystalline Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 (CZTSSe) light absorber thin films have been studied using various experimental techniques to systematically investigate the compositions and electronic structures of their GI and GB at nanometer scales. We have for the first time independently determined the band edge positions for both the conduction band and the valence band using scanning tunneling spectroscopy. While the composition of GB was nearly the same as that of GI for both CZTS and CZTSe films, opposite band bending behaviors near GBs were discovered for them. For CZTS, both the conduction band and valence band were found to bend towards the forbidden gap near GBs, resulting in enhanced carrier recombination and relatively poor device performance. For CZTSe, in contrast, both the conduction band and valence band were found to bend away from the forbidden gap near GBs, which could be responsible for the relative better device performance due to the potentially impeded carrier recombination. In the case of CZTSSe thin film, by actively substituting Se with S near GBs, both conduction band and valence band at GBs were demonstrated to bend away from the forbidden gap, leading in principle to a lower carrier recombination at GBs and improved device performance. These findings were published in paper 2 and presented in a number of invited talks.

14306014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306014.value: With the findings of higher recombination rate at the grain boundaries for CZTS in comparison to CIGS, a natural route is to modify the grain boundary of CZTS and aim to make it like CIGS, namely with a high barrier for the carriers at the grain boundary to expel them from the highly concentrated defect region. We intend to use both defect passivation and composition modification to achieve this goal. Alkali metal elements and hydrogen atoms can be used for defect passivation and cation permutation can be used to open up the bandgap at the grain boundaries.

14306114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306114.value: Selective and sustainable transformation of small molecules such as N2, CO, CO2, N2O and NO into high-value chemical feedstocks are of fundamental importance both in basic research and industrial application. Among these molecules, the activation of dinitrogen is a longstanding challenge in chemical research since it is extremely stable and generally resists coordination unless certain reaction conditions are met. Strong reducing agents are often required to facilitate the formation of early transition metal-dinitrogen complexes. However, significant progress has been recently made in this area. Tantalum polyhydride can directly activate dinitrogen in the absence of any external reducing agents. Subsequent transformation into organonitrogen species is unfortunately coupled with ancillary ligand rearrangements, making these transformations problematic. In this regard, ligand design has become a crucial theme. An ideal ligand should be able to promote the desired reactions and on the other hand, be inert to the reagents used. On the basis of our preliminary results on tantalacarboranes (Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 9039), we plan in this proposal to develop a new family of heteroatom appended dicarbollyl ligands and to prepare the corresponding half-sandwich tantalacarborane complexes as well as to study their reaction chemistry. It is anticipated that donor functionalities appended to the dicarbollyl ligands can not only fulfill the electronic and steric requirements of the metal but also tune the reactivity patterns of the resultant metal complexes in the activation and transformation of small molecules. The results derived from this research would provide valuable information on the structure-property relationships and enhance our fundamental understanding of reaction mechanisms, which might lead to a catalytic transformation of small molecules. 在基礎研究和工業應用中，將N2、CO、CO2、N2O、NO等小分子有選擇性、可持續的轉化爲具有高附加值的化工原料具有非常重要的作用。其中，N2分子由于其很强的化學惰性和只有在特定反應條件下才具有的弱配位性，使得N2活化一直是化學科學研究領域最具挑戰性的課題之一。前過渡金屬-N2絡合物往往需要在强還原劑的條件下才能合成，然而最近研究發現金屬鉭的多氫化物可以在沒有還原劑存在的條件下直接活化N2，但隨後將其轉化爲有機含氮化合物的反應却沒有成功，配體的重排使這種轉化反應更具有不確定性。因此，配體設計在這類反應中尤爲重要，一個理想的配體應該既能促進所需反應又不會與所使用的試劑反應。基于對金屬鉭碳硼烷的初步研究 (Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 9039)，我們希望發展一系列含雜原子的碳硼烷配體，製備其相應的半三明治型鉭碳硼烷化合物，幷研究其化學反應活性。希望碳硼烷上的雜原子配體不僅能滿足金屬的電子和立體需求，還能調節金屬配合物在小分子活化和轉化反應中的反應活性。這些研究結果將對結構與反應性能的相互關係提供有效信息，加深對反應機理的理解，幷爲小分子的催化轉化反應提供理論依據。

14306114.label: Realisation of objectives
14306114.value: It is of great interests to develop transition metal-mediated activation of small molecules such as CO and N2 for the selective and sustainable transformation into high-value chemical feedstocks. Although substantial advances toward this goal have been made in the past decades, the number of well-defined organometallic complexes that can efficiently activate these small molecules under mild conditions remains small. Early transition metal polyhydrides can activate dinitrogen in the absence of any external reducing agents. Subsequent transformation into organonitrogen species is unfortunately coupled with ancillary ligand rearrangements, making these transformations problematic. In this regard, ligand design has become a crucial theme. An ideal ligand should be able to promote the desired reactions and on the other hand, be inert to the reagents used. On the basis of our preliminary results on tantalacarboranes, we proposed to develop a new family of functional group appended dicarbollyl ligands and to prepare the corresponding half-sandwich early transition metal metallacarborane complexes as well as to study their reaction chemistry. We used transition metal-mediated or catalyzed cage C-C or cage B-C coupling methods to synthesize a class of new functionalized carboranes. These carborane derivatives can be converted into the corresponding dicarbollide ligands via selective deboronation reaction. With these new ligands in hand, we subsequently prepared a series of metallacarboranes of tantalum, zirconium and yttrium alkyls. The newly prepared complexes were fully characterized by various spectroscopic data and single-crystal X-ray analyses. Reactivity studies showed that tantalacarborane alkyl such as [η1:η5-(Me2NCH2CH2)C2B9H10]TaMe3 mediated a facile rupture of the C-N multiple bond in aryl isonitriles and multiple insertion of alkyl isonitriles to give N-heterocycles via cascade C-C/C-N couplings. This work offered a very effective method for the construction of six-membered N-heterocycles. Further studied of tantalacarborane trimethyl complexes with isonitriles indicated that these reactions were very diverse. The major observations were as follows: (1) reaction with 1 equiv of adamantyl isonitrile gave tantalum imido complexes, (2) reaction with alkyl isonitrile, followed by aryl ones afforded tantalum imido amido complexes, (3) reaction with aryl isonitrile, followed by alkyl ones generated imido tantalaaziridines, (4) reaction with 1 equiv of alkyl isonitrile bearing α-hydrogen yielded double methyl migratory insertion products tantalaaziridines, and (5) reaction with 4 equiv of alkyl isonitriles bearing α-hydrogen produced two fused six-membered N-heterocyclic complexes. Reactivity studies of (η5- C5Me5)[η1:η5-{Me2NCH2CH2}C2B9H10]Zr(Me) showed that it underwent either protonation or insertion reaction with terminal alkynes dependent upon the nature of substituents on sp-C. Its reaction with alkyl nitriles gave the mono-insertion products, whereas aryl nitrile yielded zirconacarborane amide. This work confirmed that the incorporation of an amido sidearm to the dicarbollyl ligand enhanced the thermal stability of the resultant zirconacarborane alkyls, on the other hand, reduced the reactivity of the complexes because of the relatively strong coordination of the appended N atom to the electrophilic Zr center. On the other hand, the Zr–C σ bond in mixed-sandwich zirconacarborane alkyl complex [η1:σ:η5-{MeN(CH2)CH2CH2}C2B9H10]Zr[η5-C5H3(TMS)2] reacted with ketone, heterocumulenes, nitriles and CO to give various mono-insertion products. The reaction with isonitriles proceeded in a double-insertion pathway, whereas the Zr-C bond was protonated by methanol to afford a Zr-methoxy species. We then extended our research to include yttracarborane alkyls. The Y-C σ bond in [η1:η5-O(CH2)2C2B9H9]Y(σ:η1-CH2C6H4-o-NMe2)(THF)2 was reactive toward unsaturated organic molecules to give either mono- or di-insertion products dependent on the nature of substrates. Carbodiimides and ketones afforded mono-insertion complexes, whereas isocynides and isocynates yielded di-insertion products. Having obtained the aforementioned results, we studied the reaction of tantalacarboranes with dinitrogen. Under blue light irradiation, a tantalacarborane dinitrogen complex {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2) was isolated and structurally characterized. Single-crystal X-ray analyses indicate that the N-N distance of 1.335(6) Å falls in between N-N single and N=N double bond distances, suggesting a significant activation of N2 in such a tantalacarborane dinitrogen complex. In fact, its protonation with HCl gave N2H4 in 77% yield (Scheme 1). Scheme 1. Tantalacarborane Methyl Mediated Activation of N2 and Its Transformation [η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe3 + N2 --> {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2) (X-ray structure) {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2) + HCl --> N2H4 (77%) + NH3 (<3%) On the other hand, reaction of [η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe3 with a mixture of H2/N2 = 1/9 in the presence of DMPE generated another tantalacarborane hydride dinitrogen complex {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaH}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2). 1H NMR spectrum confirmed the presence of metal hydride. However, the H positions in the complex cannot be located by single-crystal X-ray analyses. Upon heating, this tantalacarborane hydride dinitrogen complex was successfully converted to a trinuclear tantalum imido/nitrido cluster {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]Ta}3(u-NH)3(u-N)2 in which the N-N multiple bonds have been completely cleaved (Scheme 2). This is a significant advance in this field. Unfortunately, this cluster was almost insoluble in THF once crystallized out, leading to very poor NMR characterization. As a result, the number of H atoms on N cannot be confirmed by either NMR techniques or single-crystal X-ray analyses. This work has not been published yet. We have modified the ligands by adding longer carbon chains to enhance the solubility of the corresponding metal clusters. We hope that the complete work can be published in the near future. Scheme 2. Tantalacarborane Hydride Mediated Activation of N2 and Its Transformation [η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaMe3 + H2 + N2 --> {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaH}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2) (X-ray structure) {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]TaH}2(u-N2)(u-Me2PCH2CH2PMe2) --> {[η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)C2B9H10]Ta}3(u-NH)3(u-N)2 (X-ray structure) In summary, a series of new carborane ligands were prepared and fully characterized. Their transition metal complexes of tantalum, zirconium and yttrium were subsequently synthesized and structurally characterized. These new complexes reacted with a wide range of unsaturated molecules including ketones, isonitriles, nitriles, isocyanates, carbodiimides, thiocyanates, CO and N2 to give a large class of insertion and migration products. It is noteworthy that dinitrogen activation and transformation have been successfully achieved.

14306114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306114.value: (1) A series of new carborane ligands were prepared and fully characterized (Pubs. #2, #6, #8, #9, #10, #13, #15,#18, and #19). For examples, -1a: Nickel catalyzed Ccage-Csp2 bond forming reaction via cross-coupling reaction of o-carboranyl with aryls has been developed for efficient and high yield synthesis of 1-aryl-o-carboranes and 1,2-diaryl-o-carboranes. This is a general method for cage C-arylation of o-carboranes and also represents the first transition metal catalyzed cage C,C’-diarylation of o-carboranes, which offers a facile and direct route for the incorporation of o-carborane unit into conjugated π systems. -1b: A regioselective and efficient Pd-catalyzed dialkenylation of cage B(4,5)−H of o-carboranes via direct B−H activation has been achieved with the help of a traceless directing group -COOH. This provides a new methodology for transition metal catalyzed Heck-type reaction of carborane with alkenes, which can be used for the preparation of cage boron dialkenylated carboranes for various purposes. -1c: A controlled and efficient Pd(II)-catalyzed diarylation of cage B(4,5)−H bonds in o-carboranes via direct B−H activation has been achieved, leading to the preparation of a series of novel B(4,5) diarylated-o-carborane derivatives for possible applications in organometallics. (2) A series of transition metal complexes bearing dicarbollyl or carboranyl ligands were synthesized via salt metathesis or acid-base reactions. Their structures were confirmed by various spectroscopic data and single-crystal X-ray analyses (Pubs. #3-5, #7 and #14). For examples, treatment of (Me2NHCH2CH2)C2B9H11 with excess NaH in refluxing THF, followed by reaction with TaMe3Cl2 in toluene at room temperature afforded [η1:η5-(Me2NCH2CH2)C2B9H10]TaMe3 in 90% yield. Reaction of Me3TaCl2 with 1 equiv of [Me2C(C5H4)(C2B10H10)]Li2(OEt2)2 in toluene at room temperature afforded [η5:σ-Me2C(C5H4)(C2B10H10)]TaMe3 in 58% yield. (3) The reaction chemistry of Ta-C/H bonds was investigated. The results showed that (a) reaction with 1 equiv of adamantyl isonitrile gave tantalum imido complexes, (b) reaction with alkyl isonitrile, followed by aryl ones afforded tantalum imido amido complexes, (c) reaction with aryl isonitrile, followed by alkyl ones generated imido tantalaaziridines, (d) reaction with 1 equiv of alkyl isonitrile bearing α-hydrogen yielded double methyl migratory insertion products tantalaaziridines, and (e) reaction with 4 equiv of alkyl isonitriles bearing α-hydrogen produced two fused six-membered N-heterocyclic complexes. Their reaction mechanisms were proposed (Pubs #11, #12, #16 and #17). (4) Two tantalum dinitrogen complexes were prepared and structurally characterized. Single-crystal X-ray analyses indicate that the N2 molecule is significantly activated after binding to the Ta center. These tantalum dinitrogen complexes can be protonated by HCl to give N2H4 in 77% yield, or be converted to imido/nitrido via complete cleavage of N≡N triple bond (unpublished results, Pub #20). In summary, this original work has resulted in 19 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including Angew Chem Int Ed (x 3), Chem Sci (x 1), Chem Commun (x 3), Inorg. Chem (x 1), Org. Chem. Front (x 1), Inorg. Chem. Front (x 1), Organometallics (x 5), Dalton Trans (x 1), and J. Organomet. Chem (x 3). PI was invited to give one plenary, two keynote and one invited lectures at international conferences. One PhD and one MPhil students were trained. The PhD student, Dr. Cen Tang, was awarded the best postgraduate student research output award (2016/2017) by The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

14306114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306114.value: We have made a significant advance in N2 activation and transformation. Unfortunately, the final products metal imido/nitrido clusters were almost insoluble in THF once crystallized out, leading to very poor NMR characterization. As a result, the number of H atoms on N in these clusters cannot be confirmed by either NMR techniques or single-crystal X-ray analyses. In the future, we will modify the ligands by adding longer carbon chains to enhance the solubility of the corresponding metal clusters, in the hope to solve the characterization issues.

14306114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306114.value: It is of great interests to develop transition metal-mediated activation of small molecules such as N2 and CO for the selective and sustainable transformation into high-value chemical feedstocks. Although substantial advances toward this goal have been made in the past decades, the number of well-defined organometallic complexes that can efficiently activate these small molecules under mild conditions remains small. Early transition metal polyhydrides can activate dinitrogen in the absence of any external reducing agents. Subsequent transformation into organonitrogen species is unfortunately coupled with ancillary ligand rearrangements, making these transformations problematic. In this regard, ligand design has become a crucial theme. An ideal ligand should be able to promote the desired reactions and on the other hand, be inert to the reagents used. On the basis of our extensive experience in carborane research, we took the challenge to develop a new family of functional group appended dicarbollyl ligands and to prepare the corresponding half-sandwich early transition metal complexes as well as to study their reaction chemistry. The results of this work show that these new metal complexes can activate a series of unsaturated molecules including dinitrogen and convert them into useful organic molecules, which might lead to a catalytic transformation of dinitrogen into organonitrogen species.

14306414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306414.value: 本项目将致力于研究规范O(3)西格玛模型的稳定性和动态理论。我们将研究这一模型中存在的一些特殊解并且考虑这些解的线性稳定性和动态稳定性。另外对于筑波解我们将考虑它的轨道稳定性。通过对特殊解的研究，我们希望构造在这些解附近的小扰动整体解。从而进一步了解规范西格玛模型的实际物理意义。

14306414.label: Realisation of objectives
14306414.value: In this project I have addressed all the three problems listed in the revised objectives in Section 5.2. Four main publications are now available online. They are 1. "Global m-equivariant solutions of Nematic Liquid Crystal Flows in Dimension Two", Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis, Vol. 226, Issue 2, 2017; 2. "Twisted Solutions to a Simplified Ericksen–Leslie Equation", Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis, Vol. 232, Issue 1, 2018; 3. "Freedericksz Transition in Nematic Liquid Crystal Flows in Dimension Two", SIAM J. Math. Anal., 50(5), 2018; 4. "Disclinations in limiting Landau-de Gennes theory", submitted and available at arXiv:1905.01638. All these works are related to existence, linear stability and nonlinear stability/instability of harmonic maps in associated models. O(3) sigma model and more generally sigma model with values in spheres play key roles in the study of physics and geometry. In the first three papers, I have considered the famous Ericksen-Leslie system. It is a hydro-dynamical system for nematic liquid crystal flow and shares some similar properties with the gauged O(3) harmonic map heat flow, Ginzburg-Landau equation and Yang-Mills-Higgs equation. One can see that gauged O(3) harmonic maps is a coupled system between Yang-Mills fields and harmonic maps, while Ericksen-Leslie model is a coupled system between Navier-Stokes equation and harmonic map heat flow. Our achievements in Ericksen-Leslie system are as follows. In fact we have focused on some stability/instability phenomena in Ericksen-Leslie system. In the first three articles, three problems have been addressed. They are orbital stability of harmonic maps, concentration instability and Fréedericksz transition. For the orbital stability, we found in the first article that when circulation Reynolds number is nontrivial, the orientation variable of liquid crystal material will not approach to any m-equivariant harmonic maps while time goes to infinity. The orientation variable will circulate around the z-axis with angular variable diverging according to a logarithm law. Though the solutions will not approach to a fixed harmonic maps while time goes to infinity, but the solution found keeps close to the family of harmonic maps generated by rotation and scaling group actions. In the second paper, we studied the concentration instability associated with twisted solution of the Ericksen-Leslie system in 3D. We found that the twisted solution exists globally in time and will blow up exponentially fast as time goes to infinity if the twist rate is non-zero. The optimal blow-up rate is also found which depends on the ratio of the twist rate and topological degree of the orientation variable. For the Fréedericksz transition, we focused on the effects from external magnetic field. We successfully showed the existence of a critical threshold for external magnetic field. Below the threshold, there is only one constant equilibrium state and no transition will happen. But above the threshold, constant solution is no longer stable. It will transit to another equilibrium state with lower energy. Moreover we show that when the external magnetic field is blow or beyond the critical threshold, solutions will converge to the associated equilibrium solutions exponentially. At the critical threshold, solution will converge to the constant equilibrium state according to an algebraic decay rate. This result rigorously verifies the second order phase transition observed in the liquid crystal theory. Large efforts have been devoted to studying problems in the fourth paper. Though the paper is available online in 2019, but its completion date and initial submission date are earlier than the deadline of the current project. This work has been submitted to a very competitive journal. In fact in the fourth paper, I have considered the linear instability of the famous hedgehog solution for the O(3) sigma model when value of variables is embedded into the standard 4-sphere. This problem has its background from theory of liquid crystal. In the theory of liquid crystal, Landau-de Gennes model is a unified model for the uniaxial and biaxial liquid crystal materials. In 1988, N. Schopohl and T. J. Sluckin considered the hedgehog solution to the Landau-de Gennes model. Later on in 1989, Penzenstadler and Trebin found that in the low temperature regime, the hedgehog solution is not stable. There exists a second solution which admits the so-called biaxial torus structure. It was until 2000 that the third core structure was found numerically by Gartland and Mkaddem. The structure is referred as split-core solution. After the work of Gartland and Mkaddem, mathematicians have being tried to prove rigorously the existence of these three fundamental structures in the Landau-de Gennes model. In the fourth paper and its forthcoming one, we solve this open problem in the low temperature regime. In fact we show that in the low temperature limit, the hedgehog solution is linearly unstable. By a novel bifurcation method relying on a S2-valued Signorini type problem, we find two solutions bifurcated from the hedgehog solution. One has half degree biaxial torus structure, while another solution has split-core structure with strength 1. More precisely for the biaxial torus solution, solution must be uniaxial on a ring disclination. On the torus near the ring disclination (except the points on the ring disclination), solution must be biaxial. As for the split-core solution, it must be uniaxial on the z-axis except singularities of the split-core solution. On the singularities, solution is isotropic. Moreover on the dumbbell close to the split-core segment (off the z-axis), solution is biaxial. Our results rigorously verify the numerical results of Gartland-Mkaddem and An-Wang-Zhang. More than their works, we also find that the energies of the biaxial solution and split-core solution are identical. This energy is strictly less than the energy of the hedgehog solution. Due to the work of Schoen-Uhlenbeck, the biaxial and split-core solutions found are still not energy minimizers. There exists a fourth solution which is singularity free. Our results may also be used to explain symmetry breaking in Yang-Mills-Higgs model. So far the project is of great success. The impact is far-reaching. Not only does it lead to solutions of many important problems in liquid crystal theory. It also opens several new streams for our future study. For example in the low temperature limit, Landau-de Gennes model is reduced to a S4-valued sigma model whose variables take values in 4-sphere. In our forthcoming work, we will address the original Landau-de Gennes model in low temperature regime (without taking low temperature limit). We will also verify the associated biaxial torus and split-core structures in the associated model. In this problem, we will generalize many techniques used in the thin obstacle problem for scalar variable to the vectorial case. Due to the close relationship between Ginzburg-Landau theory, PI also plans to address the dynamical problems for disclinations. Particularly PI is interested in the dynamics of disclinations when Landau-de Gennes model is coupled with Navier-Stokes equation. Such model is referred as Beris-Edward model in physics. Recently some well-posedness result and partial regularity result have been studied by several groups. It is now the moment to consider more challenging problems on the dynamics of disclinations in the associated hydrodynamical model, i.e. Beris-Edward system.

14306414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306414.value: The project is of great success. The impact is far-reaching. As one can see, the solved problems are all closely related to problems in both mathematics and physics. We have already studied several instability issues in the theory of nematic liquid crystals. These instability issue are even new in physical world. For example we rigorously prove the logarithm divergence on the angular variable in Ericksen-Leslie system when circulation Reynolds number is non-trivial. This result reveals the relationship between orientation variable and fluid. We also show that the liquid crystal material will blow up according to an explicit exponential function. Moreover our results also justify the so-called Fréedericksz Transition, which provides a quantitative study on the Fréedericksz Transition. For the disclination in Landau-de Gennes model, our research successfully solves a long-time open problem on the existence of hedgehog, biaxial torus and split-core solutions in Landau-de Gennes model. Basically for multiple solution problem, one can use standard min-max argument. But this argument can not provide us explicit structures of solutions near disclinations. Based on this consideration, we introduce a novel method to find multiple solutions in Landau-de Gennes model. I believe this method will have more applications in other physical models.

14306714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306714.value: The pursuit of quantum Hall states is a long-term effort in ultra cold atom physics. The highly controllable atomic samples provide physicists promising opportunities to explore both bosonic and fermionic quantum Hall states. Whereas recent experimental progresses have shown exciting evidences for approaching the quantum region in ultra cold atoms, there exist two crucial questions. The first one is how to detect the atomic quantum Hall states. As it is difficult to apply conventional diagnoses of electronic quantum Hall states based on measuring transport properties to atoms confined in nonuniform traps, it is highly desirable to introduce new probing schemes tailored for atomic quantum Hall states. The second question is what new physics atomic samples may bring to quantum Hall states. It is unclear at this stage whether the short-range interaction among atoms could lead to new properties of quantum Hall states that are absent in electronic systems with Coulomb interaction. In this project, we aim to provide answers to the above two questions by studying Contact of atomic quantum Hall states, a fundamental property of ultra cold atoms characterizing the probability of having two atoms simultaneously within a short distance. Whereas this important quantity has been extensively studied in systems without angular momentum, its importance in the strongly correlated quantum Hall states that carry very large angular momentum has not been explored. Making use of the intrinsic entanglement between the relative motion of any pair of atoms with the rest of the system, we will unveil the connection between Contact and the total angular momentum of atomic quantum Hall states. We will invent schemes to probe quantum Hall states using standard measurements in current experiments on photoassociation, momentum distribution and energy, which are directly related to Contact. We will also establish universal relations among physical quantities of atomic quantum Hall states. These relations originate from an intrinsic property of atomic systems, where the range of interaction is much smaller than interparticle distance, and reveal unique features of atomic quantum Hall states that are absent in their electronic counterparts. This project will provide physicists novel algorithms closely related to current experimental efforts to probe atomic quantum Halls states. It will also introduce a new theoretical approach to characterize quantum Hall states. The outcome will offer insights into connecting many-body physics of atomic quantum Hall states and short-range correlations, which are generally believed to be disconnected from each other. 超冷原子物理一直致力於實現量子霍爾態。高度可控的原子樣品給物理學家提供了很好的機會去探索玻色子和費米子的量子霍爾態。儘管最近的實驗進展已經為接近量子霍爾态提供了激動人心的證據，目前的研究還存在兩個關鍵的挑戰。第一個是如何在實驗上探測原子系統中的量子霍爾態。因為難以直接把電子系統中常規的探測輸运性质的方法直接用到被束縛在非均勻的勢阱里的原子系统中，我们需要引入專門針對原子系统中的量子霍爾態的新的探測方案。第二個問題是原子系统中的量子霍爾態会给我们提供什么新的物理。目前還不清楚原子之間的短程相互作用是否会導致不存在於電子系統里的新的物理现象。 在這個項目中，我們的目標是通過研究原子系统中的量子霍爾態的“接触”來解答上述兩個問題。“接触”是超冷原子的一个 基本屬性，它刻画在短距离里同時具有兩個原子的概率。這個重要的物理量在無角動量的系统中已被廣泛研究。但在具有極大角動量的量子霍爾態这一强关联系统中还没有被系统研究。 利用量子霍爾態中任何一对原子的相对运动和其他原子的关联，本课题将揭示“接触”和量子霍爾態的总角动量之间的联系。 我們將提出使用光締合，動量分佈和能量， 这些跟“接触”直接相关的物理量来测量量子霍爾態。我們還將建立原子系统中的量子霍爾態的各个物理量的之间的普遍關係。這些關係起源于原子系统的一个內在屬性：原子之间相互作用的範圍比原子的平均距離小得多。这个特征将产生许多不存在於電子系统中的特性。 該項目將为实验物理學家提供探测原子系统中的量子霍爾態的新办法。它也將提供新的理论角度來描述和理解量子霍爾態。其結果將有助於揭示原子系统中的量子霍爾態的多体物理和短程关联之间的联系。

14306714.label: Realisation of objectives
14306714.value: We followed closely our plan. The majority of the revised objectives were addressed. We first considered a generic short-range interaction and included diagonal contacts of all partial waves. We derived exact universal relations and used two-body solutions to verify them. We then applied these relations to atomic quantum Hall states and discovered an intrinsic correlation between diagonal contacts and an entanglement spectrum of quantum Hall states. We wrote a paper to summarize these results in 2016, which was published in Physical Review Letters. We later considered off-diagonal contacts, which capture the coherence between different partial waves in two-body scatterings. These off-diagonal contacts and the diagonal ones form the so-called contact matrix, which fully characterizes the asymptotic form of the many-body wavefunction at short distance. We found that the contact matrix could be used as a new tool to probe many strongly correlated systems in addition to quantum Hall states. We wrote a paper on contact matrix in 2017, which was published in Physical Review A. We further considered the effects of transverse trapping potentials, which are crucial in quasi-one and quasi-two dimensions. We identified a crossover from the intermediate to the short length scale, and discovered a universal relation between three-dimensional contacts and their counterparts in one and two dimensions. These results can be directly applied to quantum Hall states and other strongly correlated states in low dimensions. We wrote a paper on contacts in quasi-one and quasi-two dimensional traps in 2017, which is currently under review.

14306714.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306714.value: Contact is a central quantity that was discovered in ultracold atom systems with s-wave interaction. We discovered that such concept actually exists for generic short-range interactions including any partial wave scatterings. We derived universal relations for an arbitrary scattering. Moreover, we pointed out that, putting contacts of all partial wave scatterings together defines contact spectrum, which allows physics to trace quantum Hall states from short-range correlations. We further generalize contact spectrum to contact matrix. We point out that, to fully capture the short-range correlations in a dilute many-body system, off-diagonal contacts should be introduced to characterized the coherence of the pairwise wavefunction at short distance in a many-body system. Such off-diagonal contacts have powerful applications in macroscopic phenomena and strongly correlated systems. For instance, they allow physicists to probe directly the phase coherence in superfluids with multiple order parameters. Regarding quantum Hall states and many other important phases at low dimensions, it is crucial to explore how contacts control thermodynamic properties of such systems. We discovered that, in quasi-1D and quasi-2D traps, 1D and 2D contacts should be defined using momentum distributions in the intermediate momentum regime. We have pointed out that these low-dimensional contacts have exact relations with 3D contacts that control the system in the large momentum regime.

14306714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306714.value: We may explore the dimension crossover of contacts when the confinement continuously changes the dimension of a many-body system. The resultant quantum Hall states and other strongly correlated system may also be studied.

14306714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306714.value: In ultracold atoms, the range of interaction is much smaller than the average inter-particle spacing. In this project, we discovered this length separation leads to universal relations for generic short-range interactions including arbitrary scatterings. To fully capture the short-range correlations of a dilute many-body system, we establish the concept of contact spectrum and contact matrix, which have powerful applications in quantum Hall states and other strongly correlated systems by bridging few- and many-body physics. We have further discovered how contacts control universal relations in quasi-low-dimensional traps.

14306814.label: Project Objectives
14306814.value: We shall propose a mixed variational formulation for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Helmholtz-type equation in a non-spherical geometry for the polytropic index n<1, study its well-posedness, propose efficient and adaptive finite element methods for solving the variational system. We shall propose a mixed variational formulation for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Helmholtz-type equation in a non-spherical geometry for the polytropic index n>1, study its well-posedness, propose efficient and adaptive finite element methods for solving the variational system. We shall study several linearizations for the inhomogeneous Helmholtz-type equation in a non-spherical geometry for both the polytropic index n<1 and n>1, study the well-posedness of the linearized systems and the convergence of the linearized solutions. Then we shall propose efficient and adaptive finite element methods for solving the linearized systems and efficient iterative solvers for solving the resulting finite element systems. We shall study important mathematical properties such as numerical accuracy, stability and convergence of the proposed numerical methods. We shall carry out a large number of simulations to test the proposed numerical methods. Then we will test our numerical methods for the concerned nonlinear Helmholtz-type model system on parallel supercomputers.

14306814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306814.value: 在本研究項目中，我們將提出一些有效高精度的數值方法, 求解帶有特殊約束的非線性Helmholtz方程，並分析這些方法的收斂性和穩定性。雖然本質上這是一個計算和應用數學的研究項目，但它所產生的結果可能會直接應用到正在進行的 Juno and Cassini 兩項重要科學研究。木星和土星兩顆行星的一些非常引人注目和令人著迷的特性，即它們的穩定性，快速性，交替性，及它們的雲級緯向風特性等等， 一直是科學家們研究的一個重大項目。這些緯向風的變化和性質，可能會提供一些發生在木星和土星內部的重要物理和化學過程的信息。盡管帶狀緯向風已被觀察到數百年，能准確地測量它們也有幾十年，但他們到底是如何產生和如何一直維持的， 在過去的半個世紀中仍極具爭議。現有至少兩種關於緯向風的起源的主要觀點。一種觀點認為是由行星內部熱量的變化而產生的熱流的直接貢獻。另一種觀點是，交替緯向風僅限於非常穩定的行星大氣層中位於頂部的非常薄的一層范圍內， 同地球大氣層中的流體動力學類似。 為了更深入地了解並幫楚解決這個科學難題，美國航空航天局於2011年8月成功發射了 Juno 宇宙飛船，現正在往木星的航途上，並將於2016年到達木星。通過環繞木星，從南極到北極，再從北極到南極， Juno 飛船的主要科學目標之一是以前所未有的高精度測量木星的引力場。然而，這些引 力場的測量數據的准確解釋， 要求設計極端高精度的數值方法求解同木星自我引力場，內壓 和高度旋轉效應聯合產生的平衡態下的引力場模型，即帶有特殊約束的非線性Helmholtz方程。 這將是數學和數值方法上的一個極具挑戰性的研究項目。 有限元方法，可自動被免由幾何極點產生的數值奇點，並可處理任意的幾何形狀的物理區域，特別適合於上面涉及的木星引力場模型與非球形的幾何形狀。我們將提出一些全新思想和技術，設計非球面幾何區域上的非線性 Helmholtz 方程的高精度有限元方法，來滿足高精度重力場測量數據的准確解釋。這些有限元方法不僅有效，穩定，並將有一些重要的數學性質。Juno 宇宙飛船將於2016年到達木星， 我們這一研究項目正是開始的恰當時機，這項研究的結果將會為 Juno 宇宙飛船的使命做出最直接重要的貢獻。

14306814.label: Realisation of objectives
14306814.value: We have made tremendous efforts for the objectives proposed in this project, and are very pleased to claim that we have achieved much more outcomes than we planned in the original proposal, in all aspects of numerical methods and simulations as well as mathematical theories. For the well-posedness, mathematical properties and stability of the physical solutions stated in the Objectives, we carried out several analytical and numerical investigations [1,2,3,4, 6, 10-11]. Physically, Jovian zonal winds have been accurately measured and extensively studied for a number of decades, but their generation and penetration depth remain highly controversial. One most important objective of the Juno spacecraft is to probe the extent of penetration of the zonal winds into the interior of Jupiter by measuring their effects on its gravitational field with very high precision. The zonal external potential of Jovian gravitational field can be modeled by the nonlinear Helmholtz equation in our project. Based on the polytropic model of Jupiter, we made an effort in the work [1, 3] to compute the odd gravitational components of the Legendre expansion of the zonal external potential. In order to impose the equatorially anti-symmetric condition at the equatorial plane, we constructed a three-dimensional finite element mesh by making a tetrahedralization of the Northern hemisphere of Jupiter, and then solved the governing equations accurately. Several new physical observations were derived in [1,3], and our results are substantially different from those of the previous study in spherical geometry based on the thermal wind equation and have improved the current understanding of the Jovian gravitational field. In the works [2, 4], we used the thermal wind equation (TWE) to study the external gravitational component generated by zonal winds in gaseous planets. We derived that the TWE must be extended to include a gravitational perturbation to generate a new generalized equation as the thermal-gravitational wind equation (TGWE). The generalized equation represents a kernel integral equation with Green’s function being an integrand and is more technical to compute than TWE. Furthermore, we proposed a spectral finite element method for solving the TGWE in a spherical geometry, then applied the scheme to a gaseous Jupiter-like object with idealized zonal winds. We showed the solutions to the TGWE are essentially different from those solutions to the TWE, and the TGWE should be used to estimate the gravitational components of zonal winds in gaseous planets. In [5], the unique existence, stability and finite element approximation of a more general nonlinear Helmholtz system than the one stated in the project, with very general boundary conditions, were carefully studied, especially for the very challenging high frequency case in both two and three dimensions. Piecewise linear finite elements were suggested for solving the nonlinear Helmholtz equation, and the stability of both true and finite element solutions were established in terms of high wavenumber. More importantly, stability and optimal error estimates of finite element solutions were derived. In the work [11] we carried out a detailed sensitivity, resolution and stability study of both the phased and phaseless numerical reconstructions using the scattering coefficients for the Helmholtz model. We compared the stability and the degree of ill-posedness of the phased and phaseless reconstructions in terms of their corresponding newly defined condition numbers. Our new reconstruction method in [11] is based on the evaluation of Fourier coefficients and applies to the reconstructions of all star-like geometries. As the scattering coefficients do not require star-like shapes, our new reconstruction method can be extended to more general multiply-connected domains and non-star like geometries as planned in Objectives 1-3. In [6] we provided a systematic mathematical and numerical framework to analyze the effects of pulsed electric fields on heterogeneous physical media, which can be modeled by a more general time-dependent Helmholtz equation than the one we proposed in the project. Under very weak conditions on the given data, we established the unique existence and stability of this governing time-dependent electric interface model and the regularity of its solutions. In addition, we proposed a fully discrete finite element method for the numerical approximation of the solutions to this interface model equation, and established optimal error estimates of the finite element solution in both L2-norm and energy-norm. As we know, time-dependent interface problems are frequently encountered in many applied sciences. The typical mathematical model is the parabolic- or wave-type interface equations with discontinuous coefficients, which may arise when the physical processes involve two or more materials or media with different properties, such as the bulk modulus in acoustic propagation or the conductivity in heat diffusion. So our new mathematical and numerical framework in the work [6] can motivate many new research directions, and find more potential applications in the areas like electromagnetism, biomedicine, food sciences, and biotechnology. Linearized Helmholtz models may arise from Maxwell system and its numerical solutions are quite challenging. We constructed an adaptive edge element method in [12] to approximate an optimal control problem corresponding to a magnetostatic saddle-point Maxwell’s system that may yield various Helmholtz equations. We derived an a posteriori error estimator of the residue type for the lowest-order edge element approximation of the problem and proved it to be both reliable and efficient. With this new estimator and a general marking strategy, we proposed an adaptive edge element method and demonstrated that it generates a sequence of discrete solutions converging strongly to the exact solution satisfying the resulting optimality systems. In our recent work [7], we had a systematic finite element study of a three-dimensional MHD system, which is a much more generalized model than the Helmholtz-type. Several important regularities and a priori estimates for the velocity, pressure and magnetic field were derived, and optimal error estimates of the discrete finite element velocity and magnetic field were established in energy-norm. This is the first time to be able to establish optimal second order convergence of finite element methods for a MHD system. Furthermore, we had conducted deep investigations of fast and robust preconditioning-type and adaptive finite element methods for the Helmholtz related inverse problems in our recent works [8, 9, 13, 14]. In numerical solutions of many application problems, one may need to ensure the solutions to be non-negative due to the nature of the physical quantity involved, such as the solutions to our nonlinear Helmholtz equation for modeling the gravitational field of Jupiter or Saturn in this project. We performed a mathematical analysis in the work [14] on a special non-negative matrix tri-factorization (NMF) and applied this NMF to several application problems. We proposed a sparse low-rank approximation of positive data and images in terms of tensor products of positive vectors, and investigated its effectiveness in terms of the number of tensor products to be used in the approximation. In addition, a semi-smooth Newton method based on primal-dual active sets for the non-negative factorization was proposed and formulated. We emphasize that, as planned in Objective 5, we have carried out in [1-5, 8-14] a large number of numerical simulations to test all the proposed numerical methods in this project for various Helmholtz-type or related model systems. And these numerical experiments have well confirmed the effectiveness, accuracy and stability of these methods as predicted by our theoretical analyses in [1-15].
