14306814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306814.value: We have achieved much more outcomes than we expected in the original proposal. The major findings and research outcome are summarized below. We successfully computed in [1,3] the odd gravitational components of the zonal external potential, and constructed a stable finite element method to solve the nonlinear Helmholtz equation. New physical observations were obtained [1,3], and our results improved a lot the current understanding of the Jovian gravitational field. We used in [2, 4] the thermal wind equation (TWE) to study the external gravitational field, and find that the TWE must include a gravitational perturbation in order to generate a thermal-gravitational wind equation (TGWE). We proposed a spectral method for the TGWE in a spherical geometry, then applied the scheme to a gaseous Jupiter-like object. In [5], the unique existence, stability and finite element approximation of a general nonlinear Helmholtz system were established. Linear finite elements were proposed, and stability and optimal error estimates of finite element solutions were derived. We carried out in [11] a detailed sensitivity and stability study of the phaseless numerical reconstructions using scattering coefficients for the Helmholtz model. Our new reconstruction method applies to general multiply-connected domains. In [6] we provided a systematic mathematical and numerical framework to analyze the effects of pulsed electric fields on heterogeneous physical media. We established the unique existence and stability of this electric interface Helmholtz model, and proposed a finite element method and established its optimal error estimates. We constructed an adaptive edge element method in [12] to approximate an optimal control problem corresponding to a saddle-point Maxwell’s system, and derived a posteriori error estimator and proved it to be both reliable and efficient. With this new estimator, we proposed an adaptive edge element method and demonstrated that it generates a sequence of discrete solutions converging strongly to the exact solution to the optimality system. We had a systematic finite element study of a MHD system [7]. Regularities, a priori estimates and optimal second order finite element accuracy were derived for the velocity, pressure and magnetic field. We proposed and analyzed fast and robust preconditioning-type and adaptive finite element methods for the Helmholtz related inverse problems [8,9,13,14]. We performed a deep analysis in [14] on a non-negative matrix tri-factorization and applied it to several application problems. We proposed an efficient sparse low-rank approximation of positive data and images in terms of tensor products of positive vectors.

14306814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306814.value: Several new important physical observations were derived in [1,3]. It will be important to mathematically justify these observations using the nonlinear Helmholtz model. New analytical tools and higher order time marching schemes are needed to develop for the justifications. Numerical solutions to the TGWE are observed essentially different from those solutions to the TWE, and to provide more stable numerical predictions for the estimate of the gravitational components of zonal winds. It will be very interesting to mathematically justify these observations from the nonlinear Helmholtz model or its improved model. But new and more advanced mathematical tools and more accurate finite element methods are needed to develop for the justifications. In [5], the unique existence, stability and linear finite element approximation of a general nonlinear Helmholtz system, with general boundary conditions, were studied in terms of high wavenumber, and stability and optimal error estimates of finite element solutions were derived. The solutions are known to be highly oscillating for high wavenumbers, so higher order finite elements should have less numerical pollution errors. It will be interesting and important to extend the results in [5] to the case with higher order finite elements. These topics are very good PhD research projects.

14306814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306814.value: This three-year RGC project made a systematic and deep mathematical and numerical investigation into challenging nonlinear Helmholtz and Helmholtz-type mathematical problems. These model problems have wide applications in many areas, and are particularly motivated by the exploration into the geodynamo or astrophysical simulations and predictions. Many efficient numerical methods were proposed and analysed for solving nonlinear Helmholtz-type equations. The project is applied in nature but the theories and methods produced may have direct applications to many applications, e.g., the numerical predicted zonal winds may provide valuable information about key physical processes taking place in the deep interiors of Jupiter and Saturn. Accurate numerical methods were constructed that preserve the positivity of the physical solution to the nonlinear Helmholtz model and meets the requirement for interpretation of high-precision gravity measurements by spacecraft. In comparison to existing numerical methods for the concerned model system, the proposed methods are much more convenient and less expensive for many planets and astrophysical bodies which are rotating rapidly. The finite element methods and preconditioning iterative solvers developed may be applied for numerical modeling of shape, gravity and structure of rapidly rotating gaseous planets in our solar systems. This proposed research is scientifically important and numerically challenging.

14400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14400014.value: The principal aim of the research is to assess the effectiveness of institutional mechanisms for the advancement of women in Hong Kong, namely the Equal Opportunities Commission (EOC), a statutory body created in 1996 under the Sex Discrimination Ordinance and the Women’s Commission (WoC), an advisory body formed subsequently in 2001, with responsibility for advising the government on its obligations under CEDAW and in relation to gender equality more broadly. Prior to the enactment of the Hong Kong Bill of Rights Ordinance (BORO) no institutional mechanisms existed to advance the status of women. The enactment of BORO in 1991 helped to contextualize the local application of international human rights norms, particularly during the Female Inheritance Movement of 1994. In 1995, the Beijing Platform for Action (BPFA 1995) signaled the importance of institutional mechanisms, as a means to advance the status of women. Strategic objective H of the BPFA specified that institutional mechanisms should act as a catalyst to drive gender into legislation, public policy and programmes. While there has been widespread adoption of national machineries by Member States, the form and effectiveness of institutional mechanisms has varied. In October 1996, CEDAW was extended to Hong Kong by the British Colonial Government, which strengthened the impetus to create institutional mechanisms to advance the status of women. The EOC plays a central role in implementing anti-discrimination legislation, while the WoC has supported the development of policy initiatives including gender mainstreaming. To date, there has been little evaluation of the effectiveness of the EOC and the WoC. Where research exists, it has tended to focus on the functions of both institutions with analysis of EOC statistics on complaint investigation and conciliation and legal assistance as a way to evaluate the EOC’s role. There has been no evident attempt to develop appropriate benchmarks and indicators to analyse and measure the effectiveness of these institutions. Both the EOC and WoC have now been in existence for more than a decade. This research adopts a socio-legal approach using empirical research methods to capture multiple stakeholders’ perspectives on the role of the EOC and WoC in driving gender into legislation, policy and programmes. A central aim of this research project is to map, track and evaluate specific strategies to advance the status of women. The project aims to support the development of benchmarks and indicators to measure the EOC and WoC’s performance over time.

14400114.label: Realisation of objectives
14400114.value: The data collection and fieldwork was very successful; since many informants remembered me or knew of me from 30 years ago, and since I knew the history and local politics, it was easy to begin fieldwork. Indeed, I conducted my first interview with a farmer in his field spreading pesticides on the second day of fieldwork. The only part of the project I was not able to complete was the questionnaire to be distributed through the Environmental Protection Bureau, as the bureau head had been forced to resign. I conducted a second, 40 person random-sample village survey instead. All four objectives listed in the proposal were met: Objective #1: My research was able to confirm that illegal pesticides are easily available in rural Taiwan. While it is not possible to say how many pounds of illegal pesticides are used or what percentage of farmers use them (this information is nearly impossible to get since illegal pesticide use is heavily punished by Taiwan authorities), I am able to describe the conditions under which farmers are most likely to resort to banned and unauthorized pesticides, or to higher concentrations of pesticide than are permitted by the government. I describe the causes of this, including the perspectives of farmers that make illegal pesticide use seem moral (SEA paper, and Chapter 2). For example, many farmers note that government standards require ever weaker concentrations of pesticides, and thus believe that the government is overreacting to what conventional farmers see as environmentalists’ idealistic campaigns and consumers’ irrational worries. Objective #2: My research has identified a range of environmental approaches, from “natural agriculture (自然農法)” to “organic (有機)” to “poison free (無毒)” to “customary agriculture (慣習農法).” In my EASA paper (which is part of Chapter 2 “How Farmers Decide to Use Pesticide”), I contrasted the moral viewpoints of a top administrator of the Kaohsiung region’s extension station (which includes all of Pingtung) and a well-known ecological activist and promoter of organic farming. I am able to show how these perceptions are related not only to the risks and uncertainties surrounding agrochemicals, but also relate to ideas of the nature of development and ideals for the future of society. Objective #3: Chinese and Taiwanese have been portrayed as having “low trust” by social scientists (see for example Francis Fukuyama’s book Trust). My research shows that it is inappropriate to generalize about “trust” in the abstract, because Taiwanese in fact build trust in culturally specific ways. I have found that while consumers tend not to trust organic certifications because there are many rumors of farmers selling non-organic products as organic, consumers do trust certain large store brands and also trust neighbors, friends, and farmers with whom they have personal relationships. Taiwan has a system of direct delivery to the home (宅配) that allows urban consumers to order organic products from farmers they trust. Nevertheless, the uncertainty about the risks from pesticides means that most consumers are unsure about how seriously to treat the danger of long-term exposure to pesticide residues. Some consumers occasionally will buy organic produce if the price difference is not too great, but will emphasize their doubts about organic produce and about the dangers from pesticides when the price differential is high. My research also shows that while many villagers claim to get most of their food from friends and relatives (and thus not be exposed to pesticides), this turns out to be an exaggeration; most families do buy vegetables to obtain a variety of foods. In my questionnaire, I asked families whether they grew their own pesticide-free vegetables, because it is widely said that farmers do so, but I found that only about 20 percent of farmers have such a private pesticide-free plot. Objective #4: Information about pesticides is widely disseminated in Taiwan; licensed dealers, Agricultural Extension publications and personnel, Farmer’s Association pesticide retailers and extension agents, and wholesale produce buyers all tell farmers how to use pesticides and about possible dangers. Still, as scholars of science and society have found elsewhere, understandings of science are shaped by politics, culture, and economic interests. State regulations are very important for controlling the risks from pesticides, but cannot be enforced unless there is popular support and farmers’ economic interests are also protected. Two cases have ended up being most revealing. One is a “green” campaign to protect birds of prey, specifically the kites that are now rare in Taiwan and ironically more numerous in highly urbanized Hong Kong, simply because there the birds are not affected by pesticides. Bird protection activists in Pingtung accused farmers of deliberately poisoning sparrows by laying out red beans and rice soaked in carbofuran insecticide that is particularly toxic to birds. The Hakka TV Channel held a round table discussion in Wandan while I lived there, and several of my informants spoke out at this event, criticizing the activists for spreading false information. They noted that red beans are too large for sparrows to eat. An activist apologized, but insisted birds must be better protected. Off camera, one key informant complained bitterly that urban activists expect farmers to tolerate a 20 percent loss of their crop to birds, but urban workers would never tolerate a 20 percent cut in their salary. A second example concerns the herbicide Paraquat (巴拉刈). Paraquat is considered an environmentally benign chemical in that it breaks down quickly when in contact with soil (and thus does not persist in water) and is inert seven days after use. While the EU has begun to ban it because agricultural workers who have been exposed to it over a long time may have a higher risk of developing Parkinson’s Disease, the risk to consumers appears to be low. Paraquat is extremely toxic if drunk, however, so it has a very bad reputation in Taiwan. Just 20 cc will dissolve the esophagus, leading to a painful lingering death. This has led to a sort of panic among consumers, and the government is moving to ban its use in Taiwan. In this case, scientific information is overridden by cultural fears. There is still great uncertainty about the long-term dangers of pesticides. The EU and Japan increasingly restrict certain pesticides that scientists in Taiwan told me were very safe. Thus, the science itself can be unclear or disputed, which leads consumers to worry about the risks. Ideas about development, about the ideal or good society, and nostalgia for a countryside full of fish, frogs and birds, influence actors’ ideas towards pesticides.

14400114.label: Major findings and research outcome
14400114.value: The findings of this research have been reported in six conference papers, and a book in progress that is provisionally entitled “Pesticides and Risk: Sustainability and Food Safety in Taiwan.” The first full draft of the book will be complete by the end of November 2017. The book examines how farmers, scientists, and consumers evaluate the risks of pesticides, to their health and to the environment. It shows that much of the debate is not about science but about values, i.e. what the ideal society should look like. Scientists claim that when used according to instructions, pesticides are safe. Nevertheless, there are uncertainties, and new risks, like the neonicotinoids’ effects on bees, are sometimes discovered years after a new pesticide is introduced. This research describes how farmers and consumers decide what pesticides to use and what food to eat, given the risks and uncertainties. Many rural consumers eat fruits and vegetables produced by friends and neighbors, therefore relying on personal connections and trust to find safe food. But many also exaggerate how often they eat such trusted food, in order to reduce the risk in their mind, though not in their stomach. Deaths due to pesticide use and residues in food are not common in Taiwan according to official statistics and epidemiological data, but farmers and consumers are frightened by the risks posed by pesticides. But it is difficult to know what those risks actually are. Some consumers try to reduce any inadvertent exposure to pesticides by eating home-grown crops, but fewer than 20 percent of families grow their own foods. Even fewer buy organic produce from stores, both because it is more expensive and because they do not trust it to be truly pesticide-free. Conventional farmers feel they have no choice but to use pesticides, but case studies from organic farmers interviewed in this research show the alternatives, the challenges, and reveal different ideals of development. Some of the most prosperous Wandan farmers make their livelihood growing organic fruits and vegetables. Taiwan’s small scale and labor intensive agriculture seems suited for organic methods, but the small size of fields makes organic farms susceptible to pesticide drift from neighboring plots.

14400114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14400114.value: Taiwan is about to introduce a new regulatory system that will seek to further control pesticide use. Farmers will need to report how much land they have planted in what crops, and will only be able to buy pesticides approved for those crops. A national computerized database will track each farmer’s pesticide purchases. This will prevent farmers from buying pesticides that are not approved for their particular crop, and thus presumably prevent unauthorized pesticide use. It will be interesting to see if this works, or if a black market in pesticides is instead the result. In addition, the conflict between “customary” (pesticide-using) farmers and organic or pesticide-free farmers bears watching. Because Taiwan’s farms are small, farmers need to try to produce high value produce. Organic products sell for higher prices. On the other hand, organic farms often yield lower harvests, and insect pests can severely damage many crops. As consumers seek both cheap and healthy products, it remains to be seen whether the balance of farming will swing more towards organic methods or more towards pesticide use.

14400114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14400114.value: This research examines how farmers, scientists, and consumers understand the risks of pesticides to their health and to the environment, and how they cope with the risk and uncertainty. It shows that much of the debate between proponents of organic vs customary farming (using pesticides) is not about science but about values. Organic farmers wish to preserve a traditional countryside and emphasize the known (pest resistance) and unknown long term effects of pesticides. Scientists argue that we need pesticides to feed the world, and that they are safe when used correctly. Both sides have scientific support, but given the uncertainties in the data, they come to different conclusions. Many rural consumers say they eat fruits and vegetables produced by friends and neighbors. But many also exaggerate how often they eat such trusted food, in order to reduce the risk in their mind. Taiwan’s small scale and labor intensive agriculture seems suited for organic methods, but the small size of fields makes organic farms susceptible to drift of pesticides from neighboring plots. Conventional farmers feel they have no choice but to use pesticides, but case studies from organic farmers show the alternatives, and different ideals of development.

14400414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14400414.value: Wealth inequality (WI), and its negative social consequences (e.g., poor population health and social instability), have grown in prominence on social agendas across the world, and Hong Kong is no exception. Despite a relatively high Gini coefficient of .537, very little is known about the psychological mechanism of Hong Kong citizens' acceptance of WI (AWI) and their likelihood to participate in collective action against it (termed "collective action intention"; CAI). Moreover, as the Hong Kong population is aging, research attention should also be directed to potential differences between younger and older generations in such matters. Drawing upon social and lifespan psychological literature, we design a territory-wide survey to examine antecedents and consequences of AWI among Hong Kong citizens. Specifically, we will examine the inter-relations among income, perceived upward mobility, perceived social support, age, AWI, and CAI. Based on Social Identity Theory, we hypothesize individuals' incomes will be positively related to AWI, and this relation will be qualified by perceived upward mobility. Among low-income individuals, those who perceive little chance of improving their financial conditions are expected to manifest lower levels of AWI than those who perceive more upward mobility. Conversely, high-income individuals are expected to be more accepting of WI regardless of perceived mobility. Taking into consideration Socioemotional Selectivity Theory, we further hypothesize this interaction between income and perceived mobility on AWI will only emerge among younger individuals. Because of their limited future time perspective (and thus less emphasis on self-interest and achievement), older individuals' AWI will be less affected by income and perceived mobility. Regarding consequences of AWI, we expect individuals' AWI will interact with perceived social support to affect their CAI. Among individuals with low AWI, those who perceive more support from significant others with respect to their participation in collective action against WI will be more likely to engage in such action than those with little support. Conversely, individuals with high AWI are expected to report lower levels of CAI regardless of perceived support. We further hypothesize this interaction between AWI and perceived support on CAI will only emerge among older individuals, because of their emphasis on social connectedness and conflict avoidance with significant others. Conceptually speaking, this proposal integrates concepts from lifespan psychology to advance our understanding of WI and social unrest. Practically speaking, our findings will provide implications for designing public policies and intervention for reducing tensions among different social classes and age groups. 財富不均（Wealth Inequality, WI）及其造成的負面社會影響（如貧困群體的健康問題和社會不穩定性）已成為香港，乃至全球社會普遍關注的問題。除相對較高的堅尼系數（Gini coefficient of .537）外，學術界關於香港人對財富不均接納性（Acceptance of WI, AWI）及其參與反對財富不均集體行為可能性（簡稱之“集體行為意向”，Collective Action Intention; CAI）之心理機制探討甚少。與此同時，香港正步入老年化社會階段，年輕和年長群體在以上問題中存在的潛在差異也是值得研究的問題。基於社會心理學和發展心理學文獻資料，我們設計了一項全港性的調查以探討AWI的前因及後果。再者，我們還將檢驗受訪者的收入、感知到的上升流動性（perceived upward mobility）、感知到的社群支持（perceived social support）、年齡、AWI和CAI等因素之間的關係。 基於社會認同理論（Social Identity Theory），我們假設個人收入水平與AWI之間存在正相關，該關係並將受到感知到的上升流動性影響。在低收入群體中，感知到自身經濟地位有較小上升機會或空間的個體將表現出較低水平的AWI。相反，無論感知到的上升流動性如何，高收入群體將對WI表現出較高的接納性。此外，基於社交情緒選擇理論（Socioemotional Selectivity Theory），我們進一步假設收入水平和感知到的流動性對AWI的交互作用僅僅出現在年輕群體中。由於老年人對未來時間的認知較為短暫（因而較少關注自身利益和成就），他們的AWI水平將較少受到收入水平和感知到的流動性影響。 關於AWI的後果，我們預期個體的AWI與感知到的社會支持對CAI存在交互影響作用。在低AWI群體中，那些感知到重要他人對其參與反財富不均的社會集體行為持贊同態度的個體更有可能參與此類集群行為。相反，無論感知到的社群支持水平如何，高AWI個體將報告較低水平的CAI。我們進一步假設AWI和感知到的社群支持對CAI的交互作用僅僅出現于老年群體中，因為他們更加重視與重要他人的社會聯繫及衝突迴避。 理論而言，這研究融合了發展心理學的相關概念以加深我們對財富不均和社會不穩定性的理解。從實踐角度而言，我們的研究成果可以為公共政策規劃以及緩解不同社會階級和年齡群體之間的矛盾提供建議。

14400414.label: Realisation of objectives
14400414.value: To recap, we aim to advance understanding of acceptance of wealth inequality (AWI) among Hong Kong citizens by testing a conceptual framework which specifies links among individual income (as antecedent of AWI), AWI, and collective action intention (CAI) against it, and the moderating roles of perceived upward mobility and future time perspective (FTP), an age-related variable that has yet been examined in WI research. Focusing on responses of those with regular income (N=866) collected from the territory-wide survey, we conducted various data analyses, including a series of moderated mediation analyses, to address each of our major objectives. Objective 1: “This territory-wide study on AWI of Hong Kong people will examine whether and how the impact of income and perceived upward mobility on AWI differ across age groups.” Our Reply: As specified in our proposal, Objective 1 is the major purpose of the study which basically concerns two propositions. One is the positive association between income and AWI, i.e., whether those with higher income will also be more accepting of WI. The second proposition is the interaction effect among income, perceived upward mobility, and age on AWI. That is, whether the link between income and AWI will be moderated by mobility and age. For instance, the income—AWI link may be more profound for those with higher mobility because they are the ones who also see possibilities of moving up the social ladder further, thus more accepting of WI, even if their current income is not high. Adding in the age effect, one may argue that this interaction may only emerge among those with extended FTP (usually younger), as they are more concerned about self-interest and achievement. In contrast, people with limited FTP (usually older) are characterized as having weaker instrumental needs. Among them, income may thus be less unrelated to AWI, regardless of mobility levels. Before we elaborate the findings, we should note that all our major analyses for interpretation used future time perspective (FTP), a psychological construct consistently found to capture the age effects, instead of biological age, because the argument for the age effects mainly focuses on how much future time one perceives to have in life. To examine these two propositions, we ran two sets of analyses, one set of bivariate correlations among the variables concerned, and another set of moderated mediation testing the 3-way interaction effect. First, as expected, personal income was positively related to AWI. Second, moderated mediation analysis revealed a significant three-way interaction effect among income, mobility, and FTP on AWI. Simple slope analysis showed that income was positively related to AWI only when mobility and FTP were relatively high. Interestingly, there was no interaction effect among income, mobility, and age on AWI. On the other hand, age was negatively associated with FTP as expected. These findings provide strong support to the two proportions, and thus Objective 1. First, income was positively related to AWI. Whereas this finding may seem rather intuitive, we know of no systematic research on this relation. Moreover, the correlation was not large at all (r = .16), and this positive association became non-significant in the multivariate analyses (i.e., with other variables in the model), indicating the importance of considering other explanatory variables in understanding WI. Turning to the three-way interaction effect on AWI, our analyses reveal that higher income was associated with higher AWI only when mobility and FTP are both high. In other words, the effect of income on AWI is far more complicated than one may think. Our findings point out that at least two additional factors, namely, mobility and FTP, play significant roles in understanding AWI. That is, income is positively associated with AWI only when those individuals are more concerned with instrumental needs and achievement (longer FTP) and also see the possibilities of moving up in the social ladder (higher in mobility). Objective 2: “It will investigate age differences in the effects of AWI and perceived social support on CAI.” Our Reply: As mentioned above, we used FTP, a psychological construct capturing age, for all our major analyses reported because FTP provides better explanatory power. To examine Objective 2, we examined whether FTP would interact with AWI and social support (i.e., whether their significant others support them for collective action) in predicting CAI, as specified in our proposal. Moderated mediation analysis revealed that older age was related to more limited FTP, as expected. Also, the significant and negative linkage between AWI and CAI was qualified by social support and FTP; the three-way interaction was indeed significant. Simple slope analysis was then conducted to examine the pattern of this interaction effect. Specifically, it was found that the negative AWI—CAI link only held for those with extended FTP and high support. This negative association did not emerge for those with low support. On the other hand, among people with limited FTP, there was no association between AWI and CAI when they perceived high support. But the negative AWI–CAI association was significant when they perceived low support. These findings were generally consistent with Socioemotional Selectivity Theory. People with limited FTP should be more concerned about social relationships and more sensitive to social support. Hence, when perceiving high support for collective action, they will have high CAI anyway, regardless of AWI. In contrast, when perceiving low support, they tend to engage in collective action only when having low AWI (i.e., the negative AWI–CAI linkage). These findings from the significant three-way interaction largely support the scope of Objective 2. However, we should note that part of the results were unexpected. Specifically, the negative AWI—CAI link only held for those with extended FTP (i.e., usually younger) and high support, but not for those with low support. Conceptually, we would expect that social support should matter less for individuals with extended FTP and so this finding is quite the opposite. A closer examination of the data suggests that this may be a suppression effect and should be interpreted with caution. Objective 3: “It will also explore if future time perspective (FTP) can help explain the proposed age effects on AWI and CAI.” Our Reply: Objective 3 is more of an extension of the first two objectives, focusing on the general explanatory power of FTP of the age effects across analyses. As stated above, all our analyses reported mostly focus on FTP and found that it did confirm the age effects in various aspects. For instance, FTP was negatively associated with age at the bivariate level, as expected. More importantly, we tried some analyses with either FTP or age as the predictor variable and found that FTP derived significant findings as proposed, but not age. For instance, the three-way interaction effect among income, mobility, and FTP on AWI was significant as hypothesized (mentioned above when addressing Objective 1). However, this interaction effect was non-significant if age was used. To conclude, our analyses all support the utility of using FTP to explain the age effects on AWI and CAI. In sum, our findings bear significant conceptual and practical implications, and have largely addressed the scopes of the three objectives. With almost 25% of our sample reported a strong CAI, we believe that the issue of WI is certainly pressing and more research, like ours, should be conducted to further advance our understanding of it.

14400414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14400414.value: The current study aims to advance understanding of acceptance of wealth inequality (AWI) among Hong Kong citizens by testing a conceptual framework which specifies links among individual income (as antecedent), AWI, and collective action intention (CAI) against it, and the moderating roles of perceived upward mobility and future time perspective (FTP) in these relations. Zero-order correlations support the intuitions of how income, AWI, and CAI are inter-correlated. More specifically, however, multivariate analyses reveal that income is unrelated to AWI when other factors are considered at the same time, whereas perceived upward mobility is positively associated with AWI. Importantly, there emerges a three-way interaction among income, mobility, and FTP on AWI, and higher AWI predicts lower CAI. Taken together, these findings reveal that higher income may lead to lower CAI (thus easing social tension and unrest such as protests due to WI) via higher AWI only when mobility and FTP are both high. Note that our interaction effect is still significant after we have controlled for past collective action which is a strong predictor of AWI (attitudes) and CAI (behavioral intention). Our observed conditional indirect effect of income—AWI—CAI also seems robust and striking. The importance of perceived upward mobility in understanding AWI (and hence CAI), as revealed in the three-way interaction effect, points out the alarming consequence of the perception of being stuck in the social hierarchy (i.e., low in mobility). This finding precisely echoes what is happening in Hong Kong, when even individuals with decent income mostly cannot afford to buy a residential property. To the extent that they do not see any promising future to move up the social hierarchy, they feel extremely frustrated and negative toward the government. In addition to structural changes in the labor market and employment conditions, interventions targeting WI should focus on psychological factors such as perceived upward mobility and future time perspective. We presented our findings in three international conferences. We also managed to produce two separate papers thus far. The first paper, reporting the key findings on the overall test of our proposed model, was under review in European Journal of Social Psychology. The second paper focuses on AWI and CAI among housewives in Hong Kong, an important segment of our population that has largely been ignored in political psychological research. This paper is ready to be submitted to Psychology of Women Quarterly. We are confident that both papers will be published eventually.

14400414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14400414.value: Whereas the findings mostly confirmed our major hypotheses, future research should be conducted to explore various unanswered questions. First, this study was conducted in a city with one of the highest Gini coefficients in the world. One may argue that our findings will only be gathered in places with high levels of wealth inequality. It thus would be interesting to see how the current results, especially the moderating roles of perceived upward mobility, will be generalized in countries with lower levels of wealth inequality. For instance, one plausible inference is that the impact of perceived upward mobility should be smaller for countries/cities with lower inequality because people generally may sense more opportunities in such places. A multiple-city comparison of our conceptual model can clarify such issues. Moreover, the obvious merit of our phone-survey for a large-scale territory-wide study is the representativeness of our findings. However, a phone-survey typically precludes some more complicated research design, such as a longitudinal study on participants’ collective action intentions reported at one time and their actual collective action some time later. Future studies should adopt a longitudinal approach to examine such issues.

14400414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14400414.value: Wealth inequality (WI) has pervasive social and political consequences. In Hong Kong, the latest Gini coefficient is .539, one of the highest in the world. We thus aimed to advance understanding on the concept of acceptance of WI (AWI) and its social psychological correlates. Through a territory-wide phone-survey, we successfully collect data from a representative sample of 1,402 Hong Kong citizens. Our analyses, focusing on those with income (N=866), confirm that those with higher income were more accepting of WI, and those with higher AWI were also less likely to engage in collective action against WI (CAI). Most importantly, however, higher income may lead to lower CAI (thus easing social tension and unrest such as protests due to WI) only when perceived upward mobility and future time perspective are both high. Taken together, these findings suggest that the income—AWI—CAI links are not as intuitive as one may think because the associations also depend on whether individuals perceive a chance for climbing up the social hierarchy, with ample amount of future time/life left. In addition to structural changes in the labor market/employment conditions, interventions targeting WI should focus on psychological factors such as perceived upward mobility and future time perspective.

14400614.value: 本計畫的執行目標，希望深化吾人對明代文學史、思想史、考據學及上古神話學接受史等相關課題之研究與認知。茲將計畫研究目的條列於下： 確定研究範圍後，便開始相關資料的蒐集工作。由於資料以明人的《楚辭》專著為核心，須往北京、上海、杭州、臺北、京都蒐集希見之明代楚辭著述，方能通盤了解明代楚辭學研究概況，為報告之撰寫做好充分準備。 根據史傳、方志及集部等資料，編製〈明代後期楚辭學年表〉、〈明代後期楚辭學著述知見錄〉、〈明代後期楚辭學著述者小傳〉、〈明代後期楚辭學著述者籍貫分佈圖〉。 通過對楚辭學著述的解讀，探討在政爭激烈的明代後期，人們如何藉《楚辭》來表達自己的理想，如明志、紓憤、教育子弟等。 通過對楚辭著述者之生平、著作及相關資料的考辨，了解明代地緣文化的面貌。如楚辭著述者的籍貫以長江流域諸省佔絕大多數，然各省作者的文化背景又互有差異。 作為尚情重趣之潮流的追隨者，明代後期楚辭著述者如何詮釋屈原人格、《楚辭》文辭？這些著述者如何擺脫傳統儒家思想的準則，理解屈騷「有失中庸」、「華而少實」的特徵，是本計畫探研的重點之一。 在博雅好奇的風氣下，明代後期楚辭著述者如何展開名物考據，如何解讀神話材料、建構楚辭神話體系，是本計畫的另一重點。

14400614.label: Major findings and research outcome
14400614.value: 本計畫以明代後期（ca.1500-1644）楚辭學著述為核心，探討《楚辭》在世俗化語境下的接受情況。明代正德以降，楚辭學著述大量湧現。截至明清之際，據統計有近八十種。因為屈騷的獨特性，學術風氣在儒學主導的傳統社會中一旦有變，新的學術特色很快就體現於楚辭接受情況。明代後期楚辭接受有幾個面貌︰一、政治面貌的呈現︰明代後期，政爭甚為激烈。由於屈騷對忠奸之辨的強調，影響到學者透過註騷來表達政見，乃至官場失意的哀憤。二、地緣文化的反映︰明代楚辭著述者的籍貫絕大多數在長江沿岸，如四川、湖廣、江西、南直隸及浙江諸省份，這與當地的文化傳統、地理環境、經濟發展、出版事業關係甚大。三、博學尚趣的潮流︰博雅風氣在明代前期已流行於吳中，而心學的流行引發個性解放的思維，以致楚辭著述和評點者對屈原個性及作品的審視不再以儒家思想為唯一準則。這幾種面貌，皆可印證經典之世俗化，與道學權威在明代後期的衰落關係甚大，亦構成本研究之主體。

14400614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14400614.value: 本計畫日後之延伸研究可分為幾個方面︰ 一、明代楚辭專題研究︰包括明人對對楚辭各篇的詮釋、楚辭神話的解讀、楚辭小學的探研、楚辭刊刻的考察等等。 二、明代文選學研究︰《文選》收錄楚辭，楚辭在《文選》的語境下如何被接受，值得探討。 三、清代及近代楚辭學、文選學研究︰清人及近代楚辭學、文選學專著達數百種之多，目前我們對於近來駱鴻凱、周貞亮之相關著作已初步開展，期待有以為繼。

14400614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14400614.value: 《楚辭》是中國詩歌源頭之一，而明代後期（ca.1500-1644）是楚辭研究興盛期，情況可歸納如下︰一、明代後期，政爭激烈。註解《楚辭》成為學者表達政見、紓洩哀憤的途徑。二、明代楚辭著述者的籍貫絕大多數在長江沿岸，這與當地文化、地理、經濟等關係甚大。三、博雅尚趣的風氣在明代後期大為流行，影響到楚辭著述和評點的準則。明代後期《楚辭》之研究情況，可見當時經典世俗化之一斑。

14400814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14400814.value: 認知與情感發展對青少年冒險行為的影響

14400814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14400814.value: The purpose of the proposed study is to examine the influence of cognitive and affective maturity on risk taking behavior in Chinese adolescents. The traditional, cognitive, developmental view rooted in Piaget’s theory sees adolescent risk-taking mainly as a cognitive or decision-making issue that relies on a set of prerequisite, cognitive developmental stages. These include inductive reasoning and the understanding of probability, which develop in late childhood around the age of 12 years, and executive functioning including working memory, which matures in mid-adolescence around 16 years of age but as early as 14 years. From this cognitive perspective, youths after mid-adolescence should make risk-taking decisions as competently as adults. A more recent approach to adolescent risk-taking also considers emotion regulation and related affect development, including response inhibition, impulse control, and future orientation abilities that continue to mature until early adulthood. In this view adolescents, whose general cognitive skills have almost fully developed, may perform poorly in affective decision making due to the immaturity of their emotion regulation skills. We will conduct a series of tests and experiments to examine specific cognitive, executive functioning, emotion regulation, and risk taking behavior on 150 Chinese adolescents aged 14 to 21 years (divided into three age groups, 14-15, 16-17 and 18-21 years) and 50 young adults aged 24 to 28 years serving as the control group. Data analyses will consider maturity and the relative contribution of the cognitive and affective factors affecting risk taking. Clarification of the real reasons behind adolescent risk taking, which underlies various criminal acts and delinquency including drug abuse, will help to inform the criminal justice system and youth intervention programs. 研究旨在考察認知與情感發展對青少年冒險行為的影響。傳統的認知發展理論觀點認為，青少年的冒險行為受認知功能發展的影響。這些認知功能包括在童年後期即12歲左右獲得的歸納推理和理解概率的能力，以及在16歲左右（可以早到14歲）發展完善的執行功能，例如工作記憶能力。因此，青春期後的青少年與成人具有同樣的冒險決策過程。 後來的研究和理論強調青少年冒險行為還可能受到情緒調節以及相關的情感發展的影響，包括反應抑制、衝動控制能力等，這些情緒調節能力直到成人初期才會發展成熟。儘管青少年具有完善的認知功能，但由於他們的情感發展尚未成熟，他們的決策可能會因為情緒控制能力欠佳而不如成人。 在這樣的理論和研究背景下， 我們將通過一系列的測試和實驗考察中國青少年的認知、執行功能、情緒調節與冒險行為的關係。我們會選取150名年齡介於14-21歲的青少年作為研究物件，並將其分為三組（分別是14-15歲，16-17歲，18-21歲）進行研究，並會選取50名24-28歲的成人進行對照研究。我們將分析認知、情感發展對冒險行為的影響。

14401214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14401214.value: 本次研究的目的是了解被告在法庭審訊開始前認罪的決定的原因及影響，一個被稱為“碎損的審訊”的現象。 被告認罪是香港及其他普通法系地區案件完結最首要的方式。 選擇認罪可以賦予被告一個展示其悔意的機會並會得到相應的判刑寬減。對政府來講，被告認罪可以節省法庭本來用作開庭審訊的資源，可以使檢控官專注於其他案件，還可以是案件證人免於出庭作證，從而節省公共開支。但是, 當被告臨開庭審訊前選擇認罪，因此而引致的公共開支可能更高，其原因在於當被告在事前已經選擇開庭審訊進行抗辯，但其後又在開庭前改變其不認罪的初衷。這種現象被稱為“碎損的審訊”，因為這種現象為法庭審訊的進行帶來了阻礙。法庭在人員上的花費包括 --- 法官，檢控官，辯護律師 （特別是當律師是由政府所資助的），甚至包括法庭文書人員，庭警，法庭證人都要出席的開銷統統都白费了。在其他普通法系的地區，其中包括英國及澳洲，已經採納了相應的政策降低被告在開庭審訊前臨時改變由抗辯到認罪的機會及做法，香港正考慮引入該等政策。這個問題最有趣的地方是，假設被告因悔意而預備認罪，其何不在第一次有機會認罪的時候選擇認罪呢？ 是次研究將集合不同的研討方法。 第一，將出席香港裁判法院旁聽其審訊以追踪的刑事案件的審訊過程，其中的觀察所得可以用來量化並檢驗影響被告認罪的一系列與法律相關及不相關的變量因素。這些變量因素包括犯罪類型，被控告的次數，針對被告人的證據，代表律師，保釋情況，犯罪記錄和人口統計特徵的類型。這兩種二元和多元分析將用來評估哪些因素的影響“破損的審判”。第二，部分被告將會接受訪問。此舉有助解釋為什麼某些因素比其他因素更突出。最後，部分法律執業者（辯護律師，檢察官和法官）也將接受採訪，以了解及研究“破損的審判”對法院系統的影響。 這項研究將有助於確定哪些變量因素最有可能影響到被告認罪或不認罪的決定，並從被告及法律執業者的層面上了解及解釋為何被告在開庭前改變初衷選擇認罪。根據這些研究結果，這項研究將提供政策建議，以平衡香港的司法系統的高效運行，同時確保無辜的被告受到保護。

14401214.label: Realisation of objectives
14401214.value: Overall, all the objectives set out in the proposal have been successfully achieved. Data collection of this study comprised of two stages. Courtroom observations were conducted in a Magistrates’ Court in Hong Kong to collect relevant legal and extra-legal variables to determine which variables would influence defendants, who had initially entered a not guilty plea, into pleading guilty at the start of trial. These variables included: the type of offense, the type of legal representation, the circumstances of the case, the background of the defendant, and changes since the initial plea arraignment (when defendants are able to plead guilty at the first opportunity). Information on a total of 427 cases were collected in the study period. Interviews were then conducted with a sample of 58 defendants and 16 legal practitioners, including barristers, solicitors, prosecutors and magistrates, to achieve a deeper understanding of why defendants might enter late guilty pleas, especially to ascertain whether they are ‘playing the system’ or that there are pressures that lead them to make this decision. The advantage of this mixed methods design allowed for the use of qualitative data to help explain the quantitative results as well as provide stronger empirical evidence through the convergence of both methods. The findings of the study were then used to provide recommendations that will enhance the operations of the criminal justice system of Hong Kong.

14401214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14401214.value: This project resulted in a number of papers presented at international conferences and publications in esteemed international peer-reviewed journals. It was found that defendants who were represented by publicly-funded lawyers or who were held in prolonged pre-trial detention were more disposed into entering late guilty pleas. It was also found that contrary to arguments made elsewhere, the findings do not support the notion that defendants enter late guilty pleas solely because they are trying to gain some form of tactical advantage i.e. playing the system. The mainstay of the research findings is published in an article in the Asian Journal of Comparative Law (Cambridge University Press). To delve deeper into the experiences of defendants, two groups were examined: emerging adults and defendants who were held in pre-trial detention. For the first group, it was discovered that emerging young adult defendants had a lack of understanding of the justice system, faced stress in being caught up in the justice process, and were susceptible to influence by others in making legal decisions including plea decisions. The findings can be found in an article published in the International Journal of Offender Therapy and Comparative Criminology (Sage). For defendants in pre-trial detention, it was revealed that pre-trial detention was already punitive which help to explain why defendants who are remanded in custody are more likely to plead guilty. An article on this has been accepted for publication in the Howard Journal of Crime and Justice (Wiley). Interviews with legal practitioners demonstrated that there are informal mechanisms that are used to manage the adverse effects that late guilty pleas may bring. The findings offer insights regarding strategies and reforms on other aspects of the criminal procedure in responding to late guilty pleas. An article on this is published in Common Law World Review (Sage).

14401214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14401214.value: There is great potential for further research in this area. During the study period, the sentencing guidelines have changed in Hong Kong with respect to the sentence discount for guilty pleas. Previously, a one-third sentence discount was generally given to all defendants who pleaded guilty regardless of when the plea was entered. Nowadays, the court must consider the stage of when the plea was entered in handing out sentence reductions. My co-investigators and I have submitted a new GRF proposal, which has been accepted, to investigate the the impact of the timing of guilty pleas on court sentencing under Hong Kong’s new sentencing framework for guilty pleas.

14401214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14401214.value: This project investigated the phenomenon of ‘cracked trials’, namely why defendants enter late guilty pleas when they had initially indicated that they were ready to test the state’s case at trial. Cracked trials are regarded as having an adverse effect of the justice system because they are said to waste judicial resources and time. Through both collecting data from courtroom observations and interviews with defendants and legal practitioners, it was discovered that there were other factors that have a strong effect on defendants’ decisions to enter late guilty pleas. It was previously asserted by some that defendants enter late guilty pleas because of tactical advantage; in other words, they do so to play the system. The findings of this project do not lend credibility to this line of thought. Instead it was found that other reasons such as the adverse conditions of being held in pre-trial detention and the overall pressures of being caught up in the criminal justice process is more likely to lead defendants into cracking their trials. Moreover, there are ways where the adverse disruptions of late guilty pleas can be minimized.

14401814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14401814.value: Using 7- and 9-year-olds, this study examines the relations among two types of mind understanding (representational (r) and interpretive (i) theory of mind (ToM)) and the understanding, identification, and moral evaluation of lies differing in liar intention (lying for the benefit of oneself vs. the lie recipient) and lie content (lying about a fact or an opinion) over a span of one year. First, I hypothesize that rToM, the recognition that the mind records reality and represents it objectively, is particularly akin to understanding how lies about facts work, because such lies instill supposedly factual but wrong information into another mind. Second, I hypothesize that iToM, the recognition that the mind interprets reality and represents it subjectively (especially when reality is ambiguous), is particularly akin to understanding how lies about opinions work, because such lies express a hypocritical opinion about reality that appears as reasonable as the genuine opinion. Third, for lie identification and evaluation, I hypothesize that children pay more attention to liar intention than lie content, and this interacts with ToM. Specifically, they are less likely to call a piece of false communication a lie and would evaluate it less negatively if it is for the lie recipient’s than the liar’s benefit, and this effect is more pronounced in high- than low-ToM children. This is because both rToM and iToM are indicators of the child’s overall sensitivity to others’ mind states and thus they should predict the child’s consideration of liar intention when moral decisions are to be made. Fourth, I am interested in tracking developmental changes in the mentioned relationships and thus propose to study two age groups over one year to acquire data covering four age points for developmental analysis (i.e., 7, 8, 9 and 10 years). I hypothesize that the mentioned effects are more pronounced with older than younger children because their richer social experience orients them more toward others’ mind states when social information is processed. The significance of this study lies in its exploration of how the cognitive understanding versus moral-evaluative aspect of children's lie perception may differentially interact with the nature of the lie and the perceiver’s mentalizing abilities. This has not been studied before. The longitudinal design provides an opportunity to examine the directions of influence of the hypothesized relationships and how they develop over time, controlling for extraneous variables such as nonverbal intelligence, general language ability, and executive functioning. 是次研究以七歲及九歲兒童為被試，以一年間隔作縱向研究，目的為探究他們的兩種心理狀態理解能力 (心理表徵理論，及解釋性心智理論)，與對不同謊言的意圖 (為自己利益說謊 或 為聽者利益說謊) 之理解、識別，及道德評價，以及謊言內容（有關事實或意見）的關係。首先，我假設心理表徵理論，(即心靈記錄現實，並客觀地於心靈重現現實)，是用於理解對事實說謊的謊言，因這類謊言是為了把錯誤的事實灌輸給他人。第二，我假設解釋性心智理論 (即心靈解釋現實，並主觀地於心靈重現現實，特別是當現實是含糊），是用於理解對意見說謊的謊言，因這類謊言表達了一個對現實虛假、但合理的意見。第三，對於謊言的識別和評價，我推測兒童會更注重說謊者的意圖，多於謊言的內容，且這種傾向與心智理論能力有相互影響。具體而言，他們會較少判斷一段錯誤訊息為謊言，而且當這是為了接收者的利益多於說謊者的利益時，他們會較少給予負面評價；而這種結果向在心智理論能力較強的兒童身上較顯著。心理表徵理論及解釋性心智理論，皆是兒童了解他人心理狀態的能力之指標，因此它們應該能預測兒童在作出道德評價時，也會考慮說謊者的意圖。第四，對於上述的關聯性在成長階段中的發展，我很感興趣。因此提議以一年間隔，研究兩個年齡組別 (即7，8，9和10歲)。我假設，相對於年幼的兒童，上述的效果在年齡較大的兒童身上會更為顯著。因為他們較豐富的社交體驗，會使他們在處理社交信息時，更為注意別人的心理狀態。是次研究的意義在於了解兒童對於謊言的認知能力與道德評價，如何與謊言的性質和兒童的心智理解能力產生相互影響。這個領域還未曾被探究，而這次的縱向研究提供了機會去了解 (在控制變量，如非言語智力，一般的語言能力，以及執行功能後)上述假設之關係，以及它們如何隨著時間發展。

14401814.label: Realisation of objectives
14401814.value: Objective 1: This research uses a longitudinal design involving two time points for testing which are 1 year apart. First and second testing were both completed. Liar motivation and lie content were successfully separated by recording and analysing children's differential responses to four types of lies: (1) selfish lies about deeds, (2) selfish lies about opinions, (3) prosocial lies about deeds, (4) prosocial lies about opinions. By contrasting children's responses to types (1) and (2) with responses to (3) and (4), we are able to examine the pure effect of liar motivation (selfish vs. prosocial). By contrasting their responses to types (1) and (3) against responses to (2) and (4), we are able to examine the pure effect of lie content (about deeds vs. about opinions). Objective 1 is 100% accomplished because liar motivation and lie content are separated and examined independently in relation to the children's lie understanding and evaluation. Objective 2: rToM and iToM were successfully measured at first and second testing. We are able to correlate them differentially to factual lies vs. opinion lies: rToM correlates more strongly with factual than opinion lies, whereas iToM correlates with opinion lies only. Hence objective 2 is 100% accomplished. Objective 3: Lie identification and evaluation data were successfully recorded and correlated with liar motivation. rToM and iToM are used as covariates to examine how much they mediate the relationship between liar motivation and lie identification/evaluation. It turns out that rToM and iToM are significant mediators: The effect of liar motivation is more pronounced in children with higher rToM and iToM scores. Objective 3 is thus 100% accomplished. Objective 4: The longitudinal results show that Time 1 rToM predicts Time 2 understanding and evaluation for both selfish and prosocial lies, yet Time 1 iToM predicts Time 2 prosocial lie evaluation only. These patterns emerge even after general and verbal intelligence, and the "auto-regressors" (i.e., Time 1 lie understanding/evaluation) are controlled. Hence, iToM turns out to be a relatively weak predictor of lie perception compared to rToM. Since iToM has not been receiving much research attention in the literature, future work may need to further examine its ontology, refine the concept, and investigate how it is related to different aspects of lie perception. Also, Time 1 rToM predicts Time 2 factual lies more than opinion lies; Time 1 iToM on the other hand predicts Time 2 opinion lies only. This replicates the corresponding cross-sectional result mentioned under Objective 2. Objective 4 is 100% accomplished. Earlier rToM appears to be a precondition for lie perception at a later time point. Earlier iToM is a precondition only for later evaluation of prosocial and opinion lies. On the other hand, earlier lie perception does NOT seem to predict later ToM. Objective 5: The data from both age groups indicate that overall speaking the relationship between ToM and lie perception is stronger at age 7 and 8 than 9. It is assumed that as the child develops she starts to consider other factors (that are not captured in this research) in her judgement and therefore at an older age the effects of ToM may be overshadowed by these factors. Objective 5 is 100% accomplished. The relationship between mind and lie perception weakens with age in the age range from 7 to 9 years. Objective 6: The present research paradigm turns out to be an effective way to study mind perception in relation to everyday socio-cognitive behaviour such as lying. The child's perception of the mind as a recording (rToM) and interpretive agent (iToM) can be accurately captured by the present experimental tasks; for everyday socio-cognitive behaviour we could set up structured scenarios similar to the current lie understanding tasks, manipulating some important underlying dimensions (e.g., liar motivation, lie content) so that the concept itself could be further refined. The overall paradigm can be applied to studying more complex deceptive behaviour in different social contexts. Objective 6 is 100% accomplished.

14401814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14401814.value: This research successfully establishes a longitudinal link between mind perception, i.e., theory of mind (ToM), and lie perception in 7- to 9-year-olds. The direction of influence basically is from mind to lie perception, not the other way round. For lie perception, liar motivation (selfish vs. prosocial) and lie content (lying about deeds vs. opinions) significantly affect the child's judgement in moral terms. The specific findings are: 1. In both age groups at both time points, liar motivation affects lie evaluation. A prosocial motive is associated with higher evaluations than a selfish motive, independent of lie content. Lie content does not have a direct main effect on evaluation, but it interacts with motivation: A prosocial motive raises evaluation more for factual than opinion lies. In other words, in children at these ages, being honest with what one has actually done (behaviour) is perceived as more important than being honest with one's own feelings or opinions (thoughts). 2. The motivation main effect and motivation x content interaction effect on evaluation appear to be constant across the ages. This is different from the relationship between ToM and lie evaluation, which diminishes with age. 3. Time 1 rToM predicts Time 2 understanding and evaluation of both selfish and prosocial lies, including lies about deeds and, to a lesser extent, lies about opinions. The correlations are positive: Better Time 1 rToM performance is associated with better lie understanding and more positive lie evaluation at Time 2. General intelligence, verbal ability, and executive functioning are controlled in this analysis. 4. Time 1 iToM predicts the evaluation of Time 2 prosocial, opinion lies only, with general intelligence, verbal ability, and executive functioning controlled. This effect is also positive. 5. The effect of liar motivation on evaluation is mediated by rToM and iToM at both time points: The liar motivation effect is particularly pronounced for children relatively high on rToM and iToM. 6. Overall speaking, the relationships between ToM and lie understanding/evaluation are more prominent at the younger than older ages.

14401814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14401814.value: Overall, rToM is a better predictor of lie understanding and evaluation than iToM. The logical next step is to ask why: Why is rToM more important than iToM when it comes to children's lie perception? Perhaps children in this age range define lies solely in terms of whether the content of a statement matches reality. Therefore, recognising the recording function of the mind (i.e., rToM) is important in understanding lies because rToM is also concerned with whether someone's mind content matches reality. If this is correct, rToM should NOT be associated with lies that MATCH reality: Suppose the liar mistakenly thought that X is Y and told a lie that X is not Y, yet in reality X is not Y. By adult standard this is still a lie, but would children at 7 or 8 think this is a lie? Would their rToM be useful in helping them understand this type of lies? Another question that can be raised in future research is whether iToM is predictive of other lie types such as lying for modesty's and politeness's sake (e.g., denying one's achievement), because iToM is concerned with the mind's flexible use of information from reality for specific purposes.

14401814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14401814.value: This research examines how children's folk knowledge about the mind may be related to their understanding and moral evaluation of lies. I focus on two aspects of folk mind knowledge: 1. knowing that the mind can remember things; 2. knowing that it can interpret things. If the child knows that the mind can faithfully remember information, she may also understand that a lie works by misinforming the mind. If the child knows that different minds can interpret the same information differently, she may also appreciate the working of "white lies" in which the liar hides her genuine feelings about reality and choose to communicate an untruthful opinion (i.e., an alternative interpretation of the same reality that is also believable). Hence, this research contributes to advancing our understanding of child psychology by rooting children's understanding and perception of different types of lies in their broader knowledge about how the human mind works. I trace such developments for one year so as to figure out the temporal relationships among these abilities. This research is significant because it integrates lie perception development into the broader context of mind reading, informing us on whether mind reading constitutes a precondition for lie interpretation in children.

14401914.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14401914.value: 近代中國的音樂與德性建設：在上海興起的中國音樂現代性, 1918-1937

14401914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14401914.value: This project examines how early-twentieth-century Chinese engaged modernity musically during colonial encounter with the West. As Chinese re-evaluated China’s existing musical establishments and began to accept Western musical practices, a new musical culture emerged, envisioning music as best cultivating necessary virtues for cultural strengthening of the modern nation. Musical reformers were music advocates who promoted such new visions, engaging complex negotiations between the modern West and China’s past, in ways the concept of “Western impact” cannot adequately address. This project seeks to understand how Chinese conducted the negotiations in their discourse, how transnational and contingent socio-political factors converged to make possible their founding of new musical institutions, and how Chinese realized their reform values and expressed personal feelings in their new music making. Specifically, this project examines how music advocates asserted scientific, aesthetic, and moral values to define music as virtues, and how their new music-making practices--including composition, performance, and transmission-- realized those modern values. Music advocates’ approaches were diverse, split between emphasizing Western adoptions and keeping pre-existing Chinese foundations. Comparing and contrasting both approaches, the project presents an analytical framework that examines Chinese adoption of the musical West on the one hand, and shows mediated continuity from native culture on the other. Examining both approaches as co-building music and virtues in Chinese modernity, the project will enhance understanding of the complex musical condition of agency and changes in Chinese modernity. The project contextualizes interwar-period music advocacies as developed from the late-Qing education reform culture, and focuses on new musical formations emerging in Shanghai (1918-1937), where colonialism brought circulation of cosmopolitan resources and propelled nation-building aspirations. Reconstructing the city’s soundscape through musical-cultural mapping and network analysis, using rare sound recordings and films, this project locates modern Chinese musical thinking, practices, and feeling in a complex web of local and transnational relations emerging from colonialism. Methodology of the project crosses disciplines. Drawing from recent studies in musicology (on the German field of music, Gramit 2002), cultural anthropology (on the construction of “classical music” in colonial India, Weidman 2006), urban musicology (Baker 2008), and ethnomusicology (Castro 2011, Solis 2012), and built from previous studies on modernity of Republican Shanghai (Lee 1999, Yeh 2000), this project integrates discourse and historical analyses with musicological and ethnographic approaches. Outcomes will enhance understanding of the Chinese musical negotiation of national identity and modernity, and will generate new intellectual dialogues on music and culture internationally. 此項目探討中國在二十世紀初與殖民西方接觸後，如何在音樂的領域實踐現代性。當音樂人重新評價中國過去的音樂建立，且開始接受西方的音樂操作，一種新的音樂文化形成興起。音樂被視為從文化上強化國家的最有效途徑，培育在此轉化過程中所需的種種德性。音樂改革者就是推廣此新願景的音樂提倡者，在近代西方與中國的過去之間進行交涉。當中複雜的的過程與意義，並非以所謂「西方碰撞」的視點能充份說明。此項目尋索音樂人如何在其話語裡進行這些交涉、跨國族和隨發性的社會政治因素如何匯合，產生使新音樂機構成立的可能，以及中國人如何在其新的音樂製作中如何實現改革的價值和表達個人的情感。 具體研究內容包括審視音樂提倡者如何以科學 、審美、和道德的價值確立音樂為德性的主張，其新的音樂製作實踐—作曲、演奏、和傳輸—如何展現那些現代的德性價值。音樂提倡者路徑不一，以強調引進西方古典音樂為發展基礎的一派，與以中國音樂固有傳統為基礎的一派形成分歧。次項目提出比較兩種路徑的分析的框架， 審視音樂人採用西方音樂的同時，也闡述本土文化在調解下的連續性。兩種路徑 共同地建設中國現代性中的音樂與德性，此視點將增進我們對中國音樂領域裡 「代理」和轉變的認識，放在現代性的審視中呈現複雜的音樂條件 。 項目把兩戰時期的音樂提倡放在源自晚清教育改革文化的歷史脈絡， 所探討種種新的音樂形成，焦點放在上海 （1918-1937）。在那裡，殖民主義流通了大都會規模的資源，並引動建設國族的抱負。通過製作音樂文化的地圖、網絡分析、運用珍稀的錄音和電影資料，此項目重構上海的城市音景，把現代中國的音樂思考、實踐、與情感置於殖民勢力下興起的本土和跨國族的複雜網絡中。 項目方法跨越學科邊界，把話語和歷史分析與音樂學和民族誌的研究方法整合採用。參考近年研究成果， 涵蓋的領域包括音樂學（有關德國的音樂場域，Gramit 2002)，文化人類學（有關對殖民印度的「古典音樂」建構，Weidman 2006)，都市音樂學（Baker 2008），和民族音樂學（Castro 2011, Solis 2012)，以及對共和時期上海的現代性研究（Lee 1999, Yeh 2000)。 項目研究成果將增進對中國人就國族身份和現代性進行音樂交涉的理解，也將就音樂與文化之間的關係，在國際學術界產生新的對話。

14402114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14402114.value: 重繪民初中國的跨文化現代性版圖：中國左翼知識份子對柏格森生命哲學的接受

14402114.label: Project Objectives
14402114.value: To investigate Chinese Leftist intellectuals’ reception of Bergsonism; To criticize the dominant binary oppositions of right/left, irrationalism/scientism and tradition/modernity by this case study; To remap the transcultural currents across Europe and Asia in the early twentieth century; To theorize as to the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese modernity; To illustrate the relevance of Chinese Leftist legacy to today’s debate of New Left thought and Bergsonism in the West.
rows: To investigate Chinese Leftist intellectuals’ reception of Bergsonism;
To criticize the dominant binary oppositions of right/left, irrationalism/scientism and tradition/modernity by this case study;
To remap the transcultural currents across Europe and Asia in the early twentieth century;
To theorize as to the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese modernity;
To illustrate the relevance of Chinese Leftist legacy to today’s debate of New Left thought and Bergsonism in the West.

14402114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14402114.value: Henri Bergson had great influence among intellectuals in early Republican China. Studying the Chinese reception of his Philosophy of Life has become popular since the mid-1980s, although most studies are mainly focused on the relationship between Begrson’s philosophy and Neo-Confucianism. This research aims to alter this dominant interpretation by placing the Chinese leftist intellectuals’ reception of Bergson in the foreground. Bergson was an influential French philosopher from the 1890s to the 1930s. By the First World War, all his major works were translated into most European languages. He was the Nobel Laureate in Literature in 1927. However, his influence dissipated quickly after the Second World War. Bergson was equally famous among intellectuals in early twentieth century China. John Dewey delivered a series of six lectures, titled “Three Contemporary Philosophers,” in Beijing, March 1920. Dewey’s Lectures started the “Bergson Fever” in Republican China. Bergson’s influence in Republican China lasted for about 30 years. Major Western Marxist theoreticians usually categorize Bergson and vitalist philosophers as irrationalists and conservative thinkers. They criticize his Philosophy of Life as being a variant of bourgeoisie philosophy from the imperialist age. Therefore, it is problematic and even politically incorrect to associate Bergson with Leftist thought in Western academic circles. This study will seek to correct this ideological bias, since Bergson’s philosophy was the common intellectual resource shared by some of the most prominent Chinese Leftist intellectuals in early Republican China. This research will investigate nine well-known Chinese Leftist intellectuals, including Marxists, Left-wing literary writers and anarchists. Their reception of Bergson provides an important aspect to examine and analyze the transcultural currents across Europe and Asia in early twentieth century. This research will delineate how Bergson’s texts, ideas and philosophical rhetoric circulated and traveled from the West to China. It will also probe into the process of such transcultural circulation, which transformed the original meanings of Bergson’s texts and ideas and incorporated them into the discourse of the Chinese Leftist intellectuals. The major contribution of this research to the literature can be seen by its proposed analysis of this subject in three ways. Firstly, it challenges and deconstructs the binary oppositions of right/left, irrationalism/scientism and tradition/modernity. Secondly, it re-examines the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese modernity by adding a crucial dimension of comparative intellectual thought. Thirdly, it illustrates the relevance of the Chinese Leftist legacy to today’s debate of New Left thought and Bergsonism in the West. 柏格森在民初的知識份子圈子裡有相當大的影響力。1980年代中期以來，有關生命哲學在中國的接受研究漸趨蓬勃，但絕大多數相關研究卻傾向集中探討柏格森哲學與新儒家之間的關係。本研究嘗試重申中國左翼知識份子對柏格森思想的接受之重要性，並借此修改上述主導學界的詮釋偏向。 1890年代至1930年代期間，柏格森曾是頗具影響力的哲學家。一戰前夕，他所有重要的作品都已在大多數的歐洲國家被翻譯出版。他並於1927年獲得諾貝爾文學奬。然而，他的影響力於二戰後卻瞬即消散。柏格森在二十世紀初的中國知識份子圈子裡同樣享負盛名。1920年3月，杜威在北京發表了共六場題為「現代的三個哲學家」的系列演講。杜威的演講開啟了民國時期中國的「柏格森熱」。此後，柏格森在民國時期中國的影響力維持了三十多年。 主要的西方馬克思主義理論家，通常都會將柏格森和生機論哲學家歸入非理性主義者和保守思想家的行列。他們批評，柏格森的生命哲學是帝國主義時期資產階級哲學的變體。因此，在西方學術界裡，將柏格森與左翼思想連繫起來的想法，往往是成疑的，甚或被視為政治不正確。本研究嘗試糾正這一意識形態偏見，因為我們發現，柏格森哲學是民初部份最著名的中國左翼知識份子共享的知識資源。本計劃主要研究九位著名中國左翼知識份子，其中包括馬克思主義者、左翼文學作家和無政府主義者。他們對柏格森思想的接受，為我們提供了一個重要的研究面向，讓我們得以借此考察和分析二十世紀初橫跨歐亞的種種跨文化潮流和脈絡。 本研究嘗試描述，柏格森的文本、觀念和哲學修辭是如何從西方流通和旅行到中國的。我們並會探究下述的跨文化流通過程，即柏格森的文本和觀念之原初意義是如何被轉化和吸納進中國左翼知識份子的論述裡的。就著本研究所提出的這一主題分析，本計劃對於相關研究領域的主要貢獻包括以下三個方面：一、本研究挑戰和解拆了左／右、非理性主義／科學主義以及傳統／現代等種種二元對立的思考模式；二、本研究透過引入比較知識份子思想這一重要的研究維度，重新考察中國現代性的跨文化和混雜性質；三、本研究嘗試闡述中國左翼傳統遺產如何對應和關聯於當今西方新左翼思想和柏格森主義的爭論。

14402114.label: Realisation of objectives
14402114.value: All five objectives have been achieved and summarized as follow. 1. A basic understanding of the Chinese leftist intellectuals’ reception of Bergsonism was achieved. Firstly, in order to understand better the historical background of Chinese intellectuals’ reception of the philosophy of life, archival and documentary research conducted from 2015 to 2017. The PI and the research assistants (RAs) collected the primary materials from the databases and book collections in the libraries in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Mainland China and Japan. We have already collected 396 books and 824 articles. Secondly, in order to investigate Chinese leftist intellectuals’ reception of Bergsonism, the PI identified nine major Chinese leftist intellectuals who are obviously related to Bergson and the philosophy of life. The PI and RAs collected, sorted out and listed 1056 works by these intellectuals which are related to the philosophy of life. The above materials are useful for the building of a basic dataset for the reception of Bergson and the philosophy of life in China. The PI further analyzed these materials and attended sixteen international conferences, held in Netherlands, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Mainland China and Hong Kong, to present his research findings and analyses. 2. The PI finished a peer-reviewed book chapter related to this research project. It is titled “From Creative Evolution to Dialectical Materialism: On Qu Qiu-bai and Antonio Gramsci’s Reception of Henri Bergson’s Philosophy of Life.” It will be published (with the confirmation letter) in a peer-reviewed publication of the Institute of Chinese Literature and Philosophy, Academia Sinica. This paper mainly investigates Qu Qiubai (瞿秋白)’s reception of Bergsonism. Qu’s appropriations of Bergonism, the Yogacara School and anarchism exemplary in his early writings. The PI try to delineate how the three major traditions of thoughts compositely engaged Qu in his approach of Bolshevik political practices and dialectic materialism. On the basis of this, the paper further examines the trajectory how Qu observed in his endorsement of dialectic materialism over Bergson’s theory of creative evolution. The paper also finds that such a pendulum movement from philosophy of life towards dialectic materialism largely concurred the thoughts and discourses of Italian Marxist Antonio Gramsci, a contemporary of Qu. Furthermore, this paper points out that Qu radically rewrote and transformed the theoretical formation of both Western thought and traditional Chinese thought. Therefore, the major contribution of this research to the field is that it challenges and deconstructs the binary oppositions of right/left, irrationalism/scientism and tradition/modernity. 3. The PI and the RAs remapped the transcultural currents across Europe and Asia, and tracing the process of textual transaction in which “Bergson Fever” in East Asia was cultivated in the early twentieth century. We found out a bibliography of Japanese intellectuals’ reception of Henri Bergson’s philosophy of life. The bibliography listed out 104 books and 532 articles. We found that Bergson’s philosophy of life and the discourse of vitalism was equally popular in Japan in the early twentieth century, but most of the scholars in the research area of “Bergson in China” did not mention this important phenomenon. The PI further analyzed this “Bergson Fever” in East Asia and proposed a new idea, “East Asian Vitalism,” (東亞生命主義) in his conference presentation in Seoul on 24th November, 2018. 4. The PI finished a peer-reviewed single-authored monograph related to this research project. The subtitle of the book is “Qu Qiubai and Transcultural Modernity.” The PI found that Qu’s complicated thought provides an important case for re-examining the transcultural and hybrid nature of Chinese modernity. The book is accepted by the Chinese University Press (with the publishing agreement). The Press “is highly confident on the academic quality and contribution” of the book. Both of the two reviewers recommend the book published by the Press. The reviewers recognize that “it is the first book dealing with Qu Qiubai from the perspective of political philosophy and Buddhism.” The advantage of the book “lies in the author’s effort of connecting different philosophical sources with Qu Qiubai’s multi-layered thoughts.” The book therefore presents “a complicated Qu Qiubai” with reference to the theories of Bergsonism, Western Marxism and Buddhism. The reviewers praise that the book “is written in a clear and readable style.” They also note that the book covers all the main topics in the research field of Qu Qiubai’s thought. It “can bring inspiration to the experts” in this field and “suitable to be the reference book” for these experts. 5. The Co-I organized a conference on “Visual Representations, World Literature and Left-wing Cosmopolitanism in Modern China and East Asia” on 22nd and 23rd May, 2015. It involved 21 scholars from France, the United State, Taiwan, Mainland China and Hong Kong. The Co-I delivered a keynote speech in the conference, titled “World Literature and Left-wing Cosmopolitanism: Some New Considerations and Suggestions.” In the speech, the Co-I discussed modern Chinese left-wing intellectuals and writers’ translation and reception of the discourse of “Cosmopolitanism”. David Harvey, a leading figure in New Left thought and contemporary globalization, reconsidered the significance of “Cosmopolitanism” for developing an emancipatory form of global governance in his book, Cosmopolitanism and the Geographies of Freedom (2009). However, Harvey just relied on the sources from cultural geography and Western social theories. The Co-I offered the sources from the field of modern Chinese literature and East Asian modernity, and enriched the discussion on “Cosmopolitanism” in his keynote speech. The conference benefited the PI’s research project. The PI presented his paper titled, “Suicide and Vital Impulse: On Qu Qiu-bai and Zhu Qianzhi (朱謙之)’s Early Thought and their Relationship with Philosophy of Life.” The PI found that suicide was an important social phenomenon in late Qing and early Republican China. A great deal of Chinese leftist intellectuals in early Republican China were involved in the debate on suicide, and most of them tried to analyze and discuss this social issue from the perspective of the philosophy of life. One of the panelists of this conference, WU Pei-chen, is an expert in Taiwanese Literature and Japanese Literature. She told the PI that suicide was also a hot topic and important social issue in Japan in the early twentieth century. With Wu’s help, the PI found that Li Dazhao (李大釗) also discussed the famous suicide case of FUJIMURA Misao (藤村操) in his articles. In other words, suicide trend is a common social issue in both China and Japan in early twentieth century. Actually, the Chinese leftist intellectuals’ debate on suicide in early twentieth century is still relevant today. Franco ‘Bifo’ Berardi’s book, titled “Heroes: Mass Murder and Suicide,” was published by Verso in 2015. Bifo, a contemporary Italian leftist theorist, analyzed the relationship between capitalism and mental health in this book. The PI’s research offers the sources from the field of modern Chinese literature and East Asian modernity, and can enrich Bifo’s discussion on the relationship between capitalism and mental health.
