14405914.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14405914.value: 媒體,民意,和作為傳播事件的政治醜聞

14405914.label: Project Objectives
14405914.value: To develop a conceptually and empirically informed account of political scandals as communicative events by identifying the major stages involved and the main mechanisms and processes that drive the evolution of the scandal events. To examine the role of the conventional mass media in the publicization, construction, and negotiation of political scandals. To examine the impact of political scandals on public opinion toward the politicians involved in the scandals, politicians in general, and the political system.
rows: To develop a conceptually and empirically informed account of political scandals as communicative events by identifying the major stages involved and the main mechanisms and processes that drive the evolution of the scandal events.
To examine the role of the conventional mass media in the publicization, construction, and negotiation of political scandals.
To examine the impact of political scandals on public opinion toward the politicians involved in the scandals, politicians in general, and the political system.

14405914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14405914.value: Political scandals are prominent features in many contemporary liberal democratic societies and have received significant amount of scholarly attention around the world. In Hong Kong, the past few years have also witnessed the publicization of numerous scandals involving politicians and government leaders. Some of the scandals have derailed the careers of the politicians concerned. However, little research has been done in Hong Kong regarding the dynamics and impact of scandals. Against this background, this project will examine the dynamics of political scandals and their impact on public opinion. As numerous scholars have pointed out, the word “scandal” has a double meaning in everyday usage. It can refer to the behavioral transgression that is publicly denounced, or to the communication activities and contents – news coverage, public discourses, citizens’ expressions through the Internet, etc. – surrounding the publicization of the wrongdoing. This project will focus primarily on the latter meaning of scandal. It treats political scandals as communicative events in which politicians, media professionals, and ordinary citizens offer interpretations, explanations, and evaluations regarding issues surrounding the publicized misconduct. These communication processes occur via both conventional mass media and new media platforms such as social networking sites. These communication processes are essential to the construction of a scandal in the first place. They would shape the evolution and ultimate resolution of a scandal event, as well as the effects of scandals on public opinion. More specifically, the project asks: 1. How do the news media construct a wrongdoing as “scandalous”? How are the nature and implications of a wrongdoing negotiated and contested in the media? 2. How do citizens respond to political scandals through new media? How do the conventional news media and new media platforms interact with each other to shape the dynamics of scandals? 3. How do scandals, as communicative events, evolve? And how do scandals arrive at their closure? 4. How do scandals influence public opinion toward politicians and the political system itself? How do the communication processes shape the effects of scandals? This project has high levels of social significance given the prominence of scandals in local politics in recent years. This project should also contribute to the general theoretical understanding of political scandals by adopting and developing the communicative event perspective. The findings regarding specific questions, such as the effects of scandals on public opinion or the way citizens communicate about scandals online, will also inform similar research in other countries. 很多當代民主社會中，政治醜聞在是一個頗為常見的現象，對政治過程產生著重要影響，亦引起了眾多學者的關注。在香港，過去幾年亦出現了多宗跟政府官員或政治人物有關的醜聞，其中一些更對個別政治人物的政治生涯產生了極大的影響。不過，到目前為止，有關香港政治醜聞的研究並不多見。 在此背景下，本研究計劃將對探討政治醜聞的動態發展和它們對民意的影響。正如不少學者指出，醜聞一詞可以有兩重意思：它可意指被批評的越矩行為，也可意指在越矩行為被公開時所出現的一連串傳播行為和內容，包括新聞報導、公眾輿論、市民在網上的討論等等。本研究計劃主要集中在醜聞的第二重意義之上，亦即是說，本研究計劃視醜聞為傳播事件，其中涉及的是醜聞主角、其他政治人物、媒體工作者，以至普通市民對被公開的越矩行為作出詮釋、解釋、討論，和評價。這些傳播過程同時存在於主流大眾媒體以及新媒體平台之上。這些傳播過程首先使一項越矩行為被建構成為醜聞。它們亦主宰著醜聞事件的發展和演變，從而左右醜聞事件對民意的影響。 更具體地說，本研究計劃提出以下問題： 1. 新聞媒體如何把越矩行為建構成醜聞？一項越矩行為的特質和後果如何在媒體中被商議和爭論？ 2. 一般市民如何在新媒體上回應醜聞事件？傳統媒體和新媒體的互動如何形塑醜聞事件的動態發展？ 3. 作為傳播事件，醜聞如何演變？醜聞事件如何達至其結局？ 4. 醜聞事件如何影響市民對政治人物以至政治制度的觀感？傳播過程如何影響醜聞事件的效應？ 由於近年香港出現多次重大的政治醜聞，此研究計劃對香港有重要的社會意義。同時，通過闡釋傳播事件這概念框架，此計劃可以幫助我們在理論層面上加深對政治醜聞的理解。有關個別研究問題的結果，例如醜聞對民意的影響或市民如何在新媒體上討論醜聞或傳播跟醜聞有關的資訊，也可以為其他國家的相關研究提供參考和對照點。

14405914.label: Realisation of objectives
14405914.value: The PI has conducted a number of case studies which helped addressed the first two objectives. Specifically, a study of the discourses surrounding “black materials” in Hong Kong, a study of the Chinese case of the trial of Bo Xilai, and a study of the scandal events during the 2012 Chief Executive elections helped the PI to examine political scandals as communicative events. Each of the case studies involved the PI and a full-time research assistant reading a systematically retrieved corpus of media texts iteratively in order to reconstruct the scandal processes. The case studies pointed toward both commonalities among the cases and differences due to contextual variations. They thus contribute to an informed understanding of the main mechanisms and processes that drive the evolution of the scandal events. The PI has also conducted a population survey to examine how scandals influenced public opinion. The survey findings provided the PI an overview of the extent to which individual Hong Kong citizens would remember various political scandals involving politicians and government officials. The data also allow the PI to examine the relationship between memories of political scandals, media use, and social and political attitudes and evaluations. This part of the project has helped address objective 3. Notably, the PI has also taken the opportunity and the resource offered by the project to conduct some in-depth interviews with journalists working on investigative reporting. The interviews gave the PI further insights into the production of investigative journalism, which is the source of many political scandals.

14405914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14405914.value: As noted above, several case studies were conducted to examine the dynamics of scandals as communicative events. The study on the transformation of the discourse of "black materials," for instance, highlighted changes in the ways scandals are imagined and constructed in the public arena in Hong Kong after handover, and how the changing imagination was tied to the transformation of mainland-Hong Kong relationship. The study on the scandals surrounding the 2012 Chief Executive election contributed to the study of how minor transgressions can evolve into full-blown scandals having significant impact on the protagonists' political career. The study of the trial of Bo Xilai in China, meanwhile, illustrated the different logics of the scandal event in an authoritarian system, or more precisely, in the context of responsive authoritarianism in China. Besides the case study, the survey illustrated how scandals may influence public opinion. It is found that people process political scandals differently based on their preexisting attitudes. More interestingly, the study found evidence for the spillover effects of political scandals, that is, a political scandal surrounding a certain politician can influence the reputation of other politicians associated with the implicated political. The extent of spillover effects, however, is found to be dependent on people's understanding of the connections and relationships between political figures, as well as the extent of their political cynicism and social media communication. These findings are reported in a journal article.

14405914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14405914.value: The work involved in the project has allowed the PI to develop new studies in various directions. For example, drawing upon the experience of analyzing the Bo Xilai trial in China, the PI currently works with a PhD student on analyzing live broadcasting of court trials in China. More generally, the project generates many findings and insights that await further development. For just one example, the "spillover effects" of political scandals reported in a journal article can be further examined in future studies. While the current journal article reports how a scandal may damage the reputation of politicians associated with the protagonist, it would be interesting to examine if it is possible for a scandal to benefit the reputation of politicians who are seen as "the contrast" of the implicated politician. In any case, the PI will continue his work in the area through some occasionally small-scale studies, and the PI may consider conducting another systematic project on the topic of political scandals in the future if there are significant developments either in the theoretical or the empirical realm.

14405914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14405914.value: This project examines the processes and impact of political scandals. It follows a communicative event perspective, that is, it treats scandals as the communicative events surrounding the publicization of a moral and/or political transgression committed by a political figure. Part of the project thus aims at developing analyses of the main mechanisms and processes that drive the evolution of scandal events. Particular attention is paid to the role of conventional mass media in publicizing, constructing and negotiating political scandals. In addition, the project also examines the impact of political scandals on public opinion. It examines how people process information about political scandals, thereby highlighting the reasons why scandals may not always influence public opinion toward politicians. At the same time, it also examines the mechanisms through which and the conditions under which political scandals may influence people’s opinions toward political objects other than the protagonists involved in the scandal itself.

14406214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14406214.value: This project focuses on the practice of Cantonese music by Hong Kong migrants to Great Britain after WW2 to examine the role of music in shaping our understanding of diaspora and home. I explore the history, structure, and practices of individuals and groups involved in Cantonese music in Britain to understand the role of music in shaping their experiences as a migrant community. What function does Cantonese music play in the Chinese diaspora in Britain? How do these musical activities relate to broader political and social policies concerning ethnic relations in Britain? Prior to the 1980s, Chinese music groups functioned primarily as social spaces to distinguish themselves from the dominant British population. With changes in policies on multiculturalism in post-1980s Britain, these groups began to orientate towards integrating with the multi-ethnic communities in Britain to redefine notions of self, ethnicity, home, and diaspora. The organisational structures and processes of Cantonese music groups in Britain reveal their understanding of what being Chinese means, and how musical styles and aesthetics enable them to position themselves within a multicultural context. Through field and archival research in Britain, and analysis of musical repertoire and events, I propose to examine the intersection of music, social space, and Chinese identities in the diasporic experiences of Hong Kong migrant communities in Britain. I suggest that Cantonese music is a popular and effective means of social integration for them because it is linked to changing understanding of multiculturalism, and of Chinesness in Britain since the latter part of the 20th century. This project is an original study on Chinese performing arts in Great Britain, and more broadly, in Europe. It will offer innovative insights into Cantonese music outside its conventional provenance in the Pearl River Delta. It will also provide new perspectives from the arts and humanities on the impact of migration and diaspora on identity formations, and in the process, emphasise the importance of expressive cultures in our understanding of social communities. 本計劃聚焦於二次戰後赴英國香港移民的廣東音樂活動，主要檢視音樂以何種角色形塑了有關離散與家鄉的認知。研究中將以英國當地廣東音樂的個人與團體實踐，及其歷史和社團組織作為切入點，探討音樂以何種角色為這些人塑造了一種移民群體的經驗。 對英國的離散華人而言，廣東音樂具有什麼功能？這些音樂活動，跟英國涉及族群關係的政治和社會政策有何關聯？1980年代以前，中國音樂團體作為一種社會空間，已經對華人以及主導英國社會的英裔人口做了區分。到了後1980年代，英國多元文化主義政策的變遷更帶動這些團體進一步與英國多元族裔的群體相互整合，以便重新定義自我（self）、族群特性（ethnicity）、家鄉（home），以及離散（diaspora）等概念。英國廣東音樂團體的組織結構和組織過程，一方面彰顯出他們對「何謂中國」的理解，一方面也反映出音樂風格與美學如何幫助他們在一個多元文化的環境底下定位自我。 本計劃透過英國實地的田野與檔案研究、音樂曲目和活動的分析，來檢視音樂、社會空間，以及中國認同在英國香港移民離散經驗中的交會；並且指出，廣東音樂由於聯繫著20世紀下半葉以來多元文化主義以及中國性的認識在英國的改變，儼然成為了一種普遍而有效的社會整合方式。 本計劃是對於中國表演藝術在英國，或者更廣來說，在歐洲之狀況的一項創新研究。這項研究將對廣東音樂在珠江三角洲這個起源地之外的實踐情形提出新的觀察，同時也會以新觀點來解讀藝術、人文對於移民和離散群體認同建構的衝擊，尤其強調表達文化對於我們了解社會群體的重要性。

14406514.label: Realisation of objectives
14406514.value: Full realizations of objectives 1 and 3: To formulate a rigorous framework for reliability assessment and error analysis of VGI, and To construct a general model of the credibility of VGI and its visualization. A general framework for reliability assessment and error analysis of VGI has been constructed. The framework provides an approach to the calculation of both positional accuracy and semantic trust, and an information fusion system based on fuzzy inference in order to derive the integrated data quality proxy measure——Credibility. Besides the framework, specific methods in assessing positional accuracy and semantic trust have been examined. Appropriate techniques have been formulated for the calculation and visualization of the membership functions and the construction of the fuzzy rule base for assessment. The framework has been applied and assessed VGI, particularly the OpenStreetMap (OSM), data quality in practical problems with supportive empirical results (see Wei J.R. et at., 2019). Full realizations of objective 2: To design an appropriate sampling scheme for quality evaluation of VGI With respect to the VGI sampling scheme, we have theoretically explored unequal probability sampling to investigate the quality in the whole region. We find that it is necessary to design a suitable spatial sampling scheme for VGI quality evaluation. The collection process of VGI data provides plenty of prior information such as contributor number for the design of a spatial sampling scheme. In order to utilize this prior information to reduce the estimation variance of the sampling design, a new spatially balanced sampling method, called the spatially correlated Poisson sampling with anisotropy (SCPSA), is proposed. In the proposed method, prior information is used as anisotropy measure of VGI quality distribution rather than just using it to construct unequal probabilities, because most of the information is not proper for the construction of unequal probabilities in traditional sampling design because (there has been no proof of a linear relationship between them and the quality in VGI). Numerical simulations and practical applications in OSM have shown the effectiveness of the new sampling design. (See Zhang et al., 2019) Full realizations of objectives 4 and 5: To improve current quality measures and to construct new quality measures for VGI, and To develop novel methods for the analysis and propagation of errors in VGI. Positional accuracy is a fundamental basis for the VGI quality assurance. A buffer-zone method can be used for its assessment, but the buffer radius in the conventional technique is subjectively specified; as result, different selections of the buffer radius lead to different positional accuracies. To solve this problem, a statistically defined buffer zone for the positional accuracy assessment in VGI is proposed in this study. To facilitate practical applications, we have also developed an iterative method to obtain a theoretically defined buffer zone. In addition to the positional accuracy assessment, we have derived a measure of positional quality, which comprises the assessment of positional accuracy and the level of confidence in such assessment determined with respect to a statistically defined buffer zone. Both numerical simulations and real-life applications confirm the high significance of the proposed statistical approach to the buffer-zone-based assessment of positional uncertainty in VGI (see Zhang et al., 2019). Full realizations of objective 6: To apply the proposed approach to solve selected real-life problems and to evaluate its applicability and effectiveness in solving practical problems As aforementioned, the proposed approach and all VGI quality assessment methods have been supported by real-life applications in OSM (see Zhang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Wei et al., 2019)

To improve current quality measures and to construct new quality measures for VGI
To develop novel methods for the analysis and propagation of errors in VGI.
To apply the proposed approach to solve selected real-life problems to evaluate its applicability and effectiveness in solving practical problems.

14406514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14406514.value: A general framework for reliability assessment and error analysis of VGI has been constructed. The framework provides an approach to the calculation of both positional accuracy and semantic trust, and an fuzzy-inference-based information fusion system to determine Credibility. Specific methods in assessing positional accuracy and semantic trust have also been examined. Novel techniques have been formulated for the calculation and visualization of the membership functions and the construction of the fuzzy rule base for assessment. The framework has been applied and assessed the OpenStreetMap (OSM) data quality with supportive empirical results (see Wei J.R. et at., 2019). With respect to the VGI sampling scheme, we have theoretically explored unequal probability sampling and find that it is necessary to design a suitable spatial sampling scheme for VGI quality evaluation. The collection process of VGI data provides plenty of prior information for the design of a spatial sampling scheme. In order to utilize this prior information to reduce the estimation variance of the sampling design, a new spatially balanced sampling method, called the spatially correlated Poisson sampling with anisotropy (SCPSA), is proposed. In the proposed method, prior information is used as anisotropy measure of VGI quality distribution rather than just using it to construct unequal probabilities, because most of the information is not proper for the construction of unequal probabilities in traditional sampling design. Numerical simulations and practical applications in OSM have shown the effectiveness of the new sampling design. (See Zhang et al., 2019) We have constructed a new quality measures and novel methods for the analysis and propagation of errors in VGI. Positional accuracy is a fundamental basis for the VGI quality assurance. A buffer-zone method can be used for its assessment, but the buffer radius in the conventional technique is subjectively specified. To solve this problem, a statistically defined buffer zone for the positional accuracy assessment is proposed. To facilitate practical applications, we have also developed an iterative method to obtain a theoretically defined buffer zone. In addition, we have derived a measure of positional quality, which comprises the assessment of positional accuracy and the level of confidence. Both numerical simulations and real-life applications confirm the high significance of the proposed statistical approach (see Zhang et al., 2019). As aforementioned, the proposed approach and all VGI quality assessment methods have been supported by real-life applications in OSM (see Zhang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Wei et al., 2019)

14406514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14406514.value: With respect to VGI, the present framework can be extended to error analysis and propagation of polygons of various shapes. A special distance measure could be developed as a basis for such a task. In terms of credibility of data quality of VGI coming from various sources and scales, other data fusion methods can be explored to perform evidence combination. To take advantage of the power of AI, we could attempt to employ deep learning algorithms to assess VGI data quality. It might also be useful to explore other VGI credibility measures to make quality assessment more comprehensive. The issue of the currency of the reference map on which VGI data quality is assessed deserves further investigation. The proposed general framework for reliability assessment and error analysis of VGI may be extended to the assessments of data quality and reliability problems in other geographical problems.

14406514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14406514.value: In recent years, there has been a burgeoning growth of interest in volunteered geographic information (VGI), a version of crowdsourcing in which the general public create and contribute georeferenced information about our living environment to internet sites where information of various kinds is synthesized into databases for public or private consumption and decision making. VGI created by amateur citizens has provided an interesting alternative or complement to traditional information collected or generated via authoritative or professional sources. In the course of development of VGI, problems have started to crop up and remained unsolved. Among other things, quality of this type of crowd-sourced data is a major concern because they come from known or unknown participants with varying technical know hows. Credibility of the information is a big problem, and VGI quality assurance has become a major issue in theory and practice. Potential errors contained and propagated in VGI cast a certain level of doubt on its reliability. Quality assurance is thus of paramount importance. Therefore, reliability of and errors in VGI have to be formally addressed and rigorously analyzed. To reliably harness the power of VGI, the present research develops novel ways to assess and analyze the reliability of VGI, and to examine errors and their propagation in this crowdsourcing environment.

14407314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14407314.value: Aim The aim of this project is to investigate the nature, feasibility, and desirability of trust as an institutional form to mobilize voluntarism in the provision of heritage conservation in Hong Kong. Background In recent years, there have been increasing demands in Hong Kong for the conservation of local heritage. However, according to neoclassical political economy, heritage conservation, as an "inter-generational public good", would not be easily obtainable through the market or the state. International experience shows that heritage trust, as a voluntary institution, is a possible "third way". Brief Description This project intends to study: * the nature of heritage conservation as an "inter-generational public good"; * the problems of providing heritage conservation by the market and the state in general, and the situation in Hong Kong in particular; * the experience of voluntary heritage trusts in the United Kingdom and Malaysia; * the overall size and network of the major players of Hong Kong’s heritage sector, and the applicability of the United Kingdom and Malaysia's experience to Hong Kong; * and the theoretical implication of the provision of a public good (heritage conservation) through the voluntary sector (the establishment of relevant trust). Significance Despite the increase in public demands to conserve Hong Kong's heritage, there is very little understanding of how best to do so. This project will therefore examine the nature of the trust model, and the feasibility and desirability of it as a possible long-term approach to heritage conservation in Hong Kong, thereby producing insights that will be of great practical value to policymakers. The study will also make an important contribution to the longstanding theoretical debate on whether the provision of certain public goods, such as heritage conservation, is better left to the voluntary sector than to markets or states. 目的 此項目旨在研究，以「信託」作為一種制度形式，動員香港文物保育自願主義的性質、可行性、及可取性。 背境 近年，要求保育本地文物之聲，在香港越益高漲。但是，按新古典政治經濟學來說，文物保育屬於一種「跨世代公共財」，因此不易透過市場或政府可獲得。而國際經驗則說明，文物信託作為一種自願制度形式，可能是可行的第三途徑。 簡述 此項目將探討: * 文物保育之「跨世代公共財」性質 * 透過市場或政府進行文物保育之一般 (及特別在香港) 的困難 * 英國及馬來西亞在文物保育信託方面的經驗 * 有關由自願界別 (成立有關文物信託) 提供公共財 (文物保育) 的理論意涵 意義 儘管香港公眾對保育文物的訴求日有增加，但何為最佳之法，卻知之甚少。因此，本項目將探討信託模式的性質，及其可能成為文物保育長遠之策的可行性及可取性，從而給政策制定者提供極具實用價值的識見。本項目還會給關於自願界別是否比市場或政府能更好地提供公共財這理論爭辯，作重要貢獻。

14407314.label: Realisation of objectives
14407314.value: 1. To define heritage conservation in the theoretical context of provision of public goods through the market, the state, and the voluntary sector. Our research has confirmed that it would be analytically useful to define heritage conservation in the theoretical context of provision of public goods through the market, the state, and the voluntary sector. We argue that since the benefits of heritage (enhancement of identity, self-esteem, and cohesion of community) are non-excludable, non-rival, and are available to both present and future generations, heritage conservation can be conceptualized as an inter-generational public good. According to neoclassical political economy, public goods, particularly inter-generational ones, would rarely be provided by the market. A common solution to this market failure problem is to empower the state to set incentives or use coercive measures to ensure the provision of socially desirable but economically non-viable public goods. This rationale has also been used to argue for the provision of cultural heritage goods by governments. However, such state-led approach to heritage conservation tends to be constrained by the state’s political interest and bureaucrats’ personal interest. Given that neither the market nor the state can be relied upon, there has been a growing attention to the voluntary sector, which is expected to step in to provide public goods when such action generates moral satisfaction to its members for the achievement of altruistic goals. This would be inconceivable to neoclassical political economists, who tend to assume that human beings are selfish by nature. However, according to more recent studies, such as those by Richard Thaler (Nobel laureate in economics 2017) and other behavorial economists, altruistic, voluntary contribution of public goods is both theoretically possible and empirically observable. In short, by defining heritage conservation as a public good, our research has provided a comprehensive perspective which includes consideration of the role of the market, the state, and the voluntary sector. 2. To examine problems in providing heritage conservation through the market and the state in general, and the situation in Hong Kong in particular. As mentioned above, our research defines heritage conservation as an inter-generational public good. This neo-classical political economy perspective has allowed us to identify major problems in providing heritage conservation through the market, namely under supply of heritage conservation due to the high cost on the one hand and the tendency of free-riding on the other. Neither could the state be expected to be an efficient provider, due to problems of government failure. These problems are found to be particularly true in the case of Hong Kong, due to extremely high land cost, and lack of relevant tradition, public consensus, and expertise. 3. To study the experience of heritage conservation through the voluntary sector, specifically the establishment of relevant trusts, in the United Kingdom and Malaysia The United Kingdom provides successful experience of heritage conservation through the voluntary sector. Founded in 1895, the British National Trusts own a large number of properties (including castles, country houses, and historic sites) and land "held in trust", making them the largest single private landowner in the country. They also own large resources in terms of donation, membership subscription, and volunteer services. Due to insufficient funding, our research has not been able to conduct original research on the British National Trusts. But through secondary sources, we found that there are political (fading of the aristocracy), economic (rapid industrialization and urbanization), social (rise of working and middle class), as well as cultural (the general public’s love of nature and heritage) explanations for the success of the British National Trusts. In Malaysia, the Penang Heritage Trust provides another case of success of heritage conservation through the voluntary sector. Founded in 1986, it made major contribution to the inscription of Penang together with Melaka to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008. Our research discussed how the marginalized trajectory of Penang is related to the development of its civil realm, cohesive property and local identity. We examined the engagement pattern of the Penang Heritage Trust, which has mounted resistance against the state’s failure in heritage provision. This bottom-up approach has hereinto preserved Penang’s cultural heritage and associated identity, and reveals the nature and capacity of Penang’s voluntary sector. 4. To contribute to the theoretical discussion of the provision of a public good (heritage conservation) through the voluntary sector (establishment of relevant trusts). During our research, we found that more research on trust is required before we can make major theoretical contribution to the provision of heritage conservation through the voluntary sector. See Section 6.2 below.

14407314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14407314.value: As stated in the title of this project, our original purpose is to investigate "Trust as an Institutional Form for Mobilizing Voluntarism in Heritage Conservation in Hong Kong". During the research, we realized that to what extent trust as an institutional form could be used to mobilize voluntarism would depend on the degree of individuals' trust on the institutions concerned. Therefore, time-series and cross-national data about the level of trust in Hong Kong would be required. The most authoritative data in this regard are provided by the World Values Survey (WVS), which has included Hong Kong in its 5th (2005-2009) and 6th (2010-2014) waves of survey. Realizing that these time-series data would be interrupted if Hong Kong is not included in the next survey, we recommended ourselves to WVS Association to conduct the 7th wave survey in Hong Kong during 2017-19, and we succeeded. Subsequently we obtained necessary funding from RGC and the Hong Kong SAR Government Central Policy Unit. Due to WVS’ time constraint, we have prioritized this over other projects, and the survey is now being conducted. We consider this as an important valuable by-product of the GRF project now being reported.

14407314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14407314.value: The project aims to explore feasible approaches to heritage conservation in Hong Kong. On the one hand, the market often lacks incentives to conserve heritages because the benefits of heritage are non-exclusive and economically non-viable. Neither is the government a promising provider because of political interests and bureaucrats’ personal interests. Private and public provision of heritage in Hong Kong is particularly ineffective due to high land cost, lack of relevant tradition, public consensus and expertise. On the other hand, heritage provision through the voluntary sector is theoretically possible and empirically observable. The United Kingdom and Malaysia provide successful experiences of heritage conservation through the establishment of relevant trusts. To what extent trust as an institutional form could be used to mobilize voluntarism would depend on the degree of individuals’ trust on the institutions concerned. Therefore, time-series and cross-national data about the level of trust are required to understand the feasibility of heritage provision through establishing trusts. We are therefore conducting the 7th wave of the World Values Survey, one of the most reputable global survey to measure trust, in Hong Kong.

14408014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408014.value: The aim of this study is to investigate architectural and urban design practices as a facet of America’s colonial strategy, and to explore the role and impact of Filipino architects within the American colonial civil service. The signing of the Treaty of Paris in 1898 instigated America’s administration of the Philippines. In the following years policies were enacted to liberate the country from its allegedly uncivilized state of being. As part the ‘advancement’ process monumental City Beautiful-inspired urban plans were executed, Classically-formed civic centres were implemented, and public buildings constructed. Composed by both American and Filipino designers these projects came to shape local society’s grasp of the ‘modern Philippine city’, a concept that ultimately reached its peak with the planning of Quezon City after World War Two. Accordingly, a thorough investigation is now proposed to explain architectural and city design practices as a component of America’s colonial policy, and to explore the role and contribution of Filipino architects within America’s colonial civil service. The inquiry considers how the emergence of the first cohorts of Filipino architects promoted America’s reform of local society. It systematically examines the schooling of Filipino architects alongside the ‘Filipinization’ of colonial bureaucracy and the transfer of the Bureau of Public Works (BPW) into Filipino hands. Using well-established research methods to tie together colonial politics, the assimilation of Filipinos into the bureaucratic system, and the shaping of the built environment to the ‘uplifting’ of Philippine society, the project will study the evolution of the Philippines and the individuals who were configuring its built environments from a fresh and novel viewpoint. The results of the study will provide noteworthy insights into the governmental, artistic, and environmental dynamics that existed during America’s colonization of the Philippines. The study’s methodology is also of significance as it uses a novel historical paradigm that enables the association between societal reform, bureaucratic expansion, and the form and meaning of cities to be probed. The study thus will improve our comprehension of the forces shaping Philippine society between the late-1890s and Japan’s invasion of the Philippines in 1941, e.g. political matters such as the Philippine Autonomy Act (1916) and the Tydings-McDuffy Act (1934), decrees providing the framework for Philippine independence. Topics such as the education and employment of architects in other colonial societies, for instance, may also be reappraised by the methods employed in this study. 本研究的目的是探討美國如何以建築及城市設計為殖民地的統治手段，並探討菲律賓建築師在其中所扮演的角色及貢獻。 菲律賓於1898年簽署巴黎條約成為美國的殖民地，藉著美國在當地實施的殖民地政策令菲律賓得到解放。隨後美國在當地建構各種典型的美式文娛中心及公共空間，這種美式建築設計及城市發展模式被視為「進步」的象徵。這些項目由美國建築師及菲律賓建築師共同合作，塑造「現代菲律賓都市」的概念。這個概念在第二次世界大戰後建構奎松市 (Quezon City) 的城市設計上充份表現出來。本研究將探討美國如何利用建築及城市設計為殖民地統治的手段，並探討菲律賓建築師在其中所扮演的角色及貢獻。 首批參與計劃的菲律賓建築師如何促進當地美式城市發展的改革？本研究有系統地審視菲律賓建築師如何從「菲律賓式」的殖民官僚體制及公務局 (Bureau of Public Works)主權回歸的事件中學習，以完善的研究方法結合殖民地統治政策、官僚體制中融入菲律賓人及利用建築環境塑造菲律賓社會「上流」等因素來研究從國家及個人層面上菲律賓建築環境的演變。 本研究的結論將對菲律賓在美國殖民統治期間政府的官僚體制、藝術及環境因素的影響力提出見解。研究方法為本項目的重點，因為它從歷史角度反映了社會改革、官僚體制的擴張及城市發展的形式及當中意義之間 的關連。本研究加深讀者理解1890年代後期至1941年日本侵略菲律賓期間不同政治事件對菲律賓社會的影響，如菲律賓自治法案 (1916)、Tydings-McDuffy法案 (1934)及有關菲律賓獨立的法案等。研究各殖民地社會的建築師之教育及就業狀況亦可以使用本研究採用的方法作重新評估。 關鍵字：菲律賓、美帝國主義、建築師、殖民地公共服務、國家發展

14408014.label: Realisation of objectives
14408014.value: The investigation was formed with four objectives. These were: to evaluate the nature of colonial architectural education given America’s desire to socially engineer Philippine society by means of tutelage; to assess the conditions that shaped the recruitment of Filipino architects into the colonial civil service; to identify the individuals shaping the Philippine built environment during the American colonial era, in so doing exploring their influence upon the nation’s course of design (i.e. architectural and planning practices, building and planning codes, the creation of design schools, etc.); and, to clarify the association between the ‘filipinization’ of the BPW and the negotiation of power between the colonizers and native population. Working diligently, particularly when the RA was employed (for 9 months), much research activity took place and consequently original research findings were produced. More to the point the investigation’s objectives were satisfactorily fulfilled during the course of the investigation. Undertaking during 2015-17 visits to archives in the US and the Philippines, and taking the opportunity during those visits to explore contextual topics associated with the colonial governance of the Philippines, the PI was able to collect an array of documents – written and visual – which has been put into published works. As an example, from visiting the National Library of the Philippines and using connections with scholars in the country the PI was given access to uncatalogued documents from the American colonial era, and during such ‘scouting’ for data he was able to find a city plan hitherto undocumented in historiography. It, for Tayabas, redraws the known timeline of when (and where) Filipino architects considered the act of city planning as part of national development. Yet, because the study sought to clarify what the evolution of the urban environment meant in the milieu of the colonial bureaucracy’s Filipinization/power shifts between Filipinos and Americans the work, thus, was able to clarify how colonial architecture and urban design projects became imbibed with a native character. As such the PI’s findings was able to refute the works of many historians, especially those in the Philippines, which simply label public works projects between 1898 and 1941 as being ‘American colonial’. Clearly, for reasons explained by the PI (in his forthcoming monograph with Routledge), Filipino architects perceived their work in the colonial civil service as helping build cities of a Filipino not American character. In completing the four research objectives, and indicating what education Filipino architects had in the US, what work they did in the Philippines after joining the colonial civil service, etc., the work has evaluated in the context of Americans initiating decolonization what the relationship between the regime type, political process, and public architecture/urban design was. The study in exploring the relationship between power and architecture, and in utilizing a range of theories, the PI was able to show how architecture and city planning became manipulated by Filipinos’ nationalist interests. The redefining (by the PI) of the confluence between colonial power and architecture/urban space in the Philippines affected how Filipinos characterized their own national identity in tangible form during an age prior to national independence being awarded. As such, via a handful of Filipino architects in the Bureau of Public Works, the Filipino nation-state was articulated. Such explanation of its form has resonance for those interested not just in urban design but the evolution of colonial politics in Southeast Asia. To accomplish the project objective a RA (from the Philippines) was employed. Based at the PI’s university the RA was able to take on a host of research tasks, read documents from the perspective of the Filipino, and arrange meetings with scholars in the Philippines as well help give access to materials usually closed from the general public. By helping speed up the research process, and also the depth of analysis, a number of challenges which previously slowed down the investigation were overcome. As an outcome the second half of the project, i.e. from mid-2016 to late-2017, took on a different character to the study undertaken from early-2015 to mid-2016. Given the new impetus from mid-2016 the PI was able to author a number of papers alongside the drafting of chapters for a book. One means by which the RA was able to offer fundamental assistance to the PI was via her capacity to recognize the evolution of Philippine society through the grand colonial narrative of Spanish and American influence, and to appreciate culturally how buildings and spaces reflected cultural identity notwithstanding issues of aesthetics applicable to building design at different times in the past. With this capacity to ‘read’ both Filipinos and their architecture, the RA was able to deeply clarify how power negotiations between the colonizing and colonized communities affected how towns and cities were built in the Philippines. Given that pre mid-2016 the PI has identified who the Filipino architects were, where they were educated, etc., he was post mid-2016 able to see how the architects and their work fitted into the framework of power negotiation given that in 1916 a landmark Act was passed. The Jones Act, in Filipinizing the colonial civil service, offered a turning point for those in the Division of Architecture to put into built form their cultural and political viewpoints as ‘modern Filipinos’. Finally, the PI is extremely grateful to the RGC for their trust in, first, funding the project and, secondly, by giving funds, permitting the PI opportunity to venture on a course of investigation that has from 2015 provided very fruitful. The fact that the project has been accomplished has from 2017 been articulated in published works by the PI, and reviews by Routledge (as part of the PI’s process to ensure the project is published as a monograph). In the reviewers showing that the project will give an important contribution to urban/colonial history, and that the draft book sent to Routledge in mid-2018 was “outstanding” and lacking in “factual errors or academic mistakes” thus it is envisaged in late-2019/early-2020 a substantial monograph shall be put into the public domain. Without the RGC financial backing, and the PI being given liberty to employ a RA, the PI was able to take forward the project’s objectives and so methodological and theoretical issues that have produced original findings about urban development in the Philippines after 1916.

14408014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408014.value: The project offered innovation in the field of Philippine Studies/American Empire Studies given that it considered native professionals rather than Americans within the frame of urban design and the colonial civil service, and it used new empirical sources (hitherto unknown to scholars). In terms of findings, the investigation was able to disclose – and why – Filipino architects ‘nativized’ the Philippine colonial cityscape following the 1916 watershed of the Jones Act. Significantly too, the PI was able to recognize and explain that the history of Filipino input into urban environmental design began not in the early-1930s, as historiography currently indicates, but rather in 1919 (with the plan of Tayabas), and following the passing of Act No. 3482 in 1928 the act of city planning became a staple of local governance in the run-up to the formation of the Philippine Commonwealth in 1935. As such the research has been able, via publications, to revise the nature/timeline of Filipino urban design activities. Given this actuality the work, to summarize, first, draws clear conclusions about the reach and implications of native bureaucratic actions within the context of the US imperial exercise in the Philippines and, second, leads to a better understanding of the political tensions caused by the Americans’ assimilation policy (as expressed in the lives and actions of professional Filipino architects). The systematic building up of knowledge by the PI has resulted in a number of publications, e.g. papers published in the journals Planning Perspectives and Journal of Planning History, and also the composing of a substantial monograph (now under contract with Routledge). With a draft of the monograph already being composed, and reviewed externally by Routledge during the summer of 2018, it is consequently the intention of the PI to have a full (ready to publish) book by April 2019. This book, complimenting the PI’s recently published book on city planning in the Philippines during 1898-1916, will it is hoped reshape studies of American colonial influence in Southeast Asia, and the impacts it had on both the form and meaning of urban environments.

14408014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408014.value: The PI has in late-2018 submitted a new application to the GRF. It focuses upon the Bureau of Public Works during the Commonwealth Era (1935-46) and in seeking to build upon prior GRF-funded projects intends to explore environmental dynamics in urban and rural locales at the time of American decolonization in the Philippines. The new project, to be brief, not only ventures to understand what public works were undertaken but, of note, what they meant to the construction of the (soon-to-be) sovereign state. Extending into geographical territories within the Philippine Archipelago hitherto ignored by historians, the work will supply new critical ways to consider the late-colonial environment. By using the Bureau of Public Works as a case study the investigation will expose how American decolonization granted nationalist-minded Filipinos new opportunities to direct the Philippines’ future state of being. Therefore, the completed GRF project was a platform from which new research can be built. The 2018 proposed research investigation, via its original analytical scaffold, builds upon the concepts and methods previously utilized by the PI. This is so that the new project can grant a rich and colourful means to understand the final phase of American colonization in the Philippines.

14408014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408014.value: The inquiry considered how the emergence of the first cohort of US-educated Filipino architects promoted America’s reform of Philippine society. It systematically examined the ‘Filipinization’ of the colonial bureaucracy after 1916 and the transfer of the Bureau of Public Works’ Division of Architecture into Filipino hands. Responsible for the design and construction of public edifices, the laying out of roads and public spaces and, when required, the composing of urban districts and city plans, the study provided chance to appreciate Filipino influence upon the governmental process. In doing this not only was the evolving form of the Philippine colonial environment explained, but also its meaning to those who designed new buildings and spaces. Of note too, the research unveiled new connections between the Filipino architects trained overseas and their subsequent endeavours in the Division of Architecture. Many ‘fact’s currently presented within historiography thus were disproved: these include the alleged influence of American landscape designers such as Frederick Law Olmstead. In truth other individuals, e.g. the influential French Beaux Arts architect/teacher Paul Cret, were shown to have actually affected the philosophy and so work of Filipino architects during an age when, significantly, American decolonization was initiated.

14408214.label: Project Objectives
14408214.value: Based on the knowledge of current and future design practice, we will develop a set of parametric urban models that are realistic in the context of high-density city design. This set of urban models will be used for the parametric tests. We will first sensitivity-test the PALM model and calibrate it for the study at hand. Using the calibrated model we will conduct the parametric tests of the urban models under different atmospheric boundary conditions, both at CUHK (for neutral boundary conditions) and at the Centre of the Northern German Supercomputing Alliance (HLRN) (for stable and unstable thermal conditions). We will compare the test results and note the similarities or differentials of urban ventilation performances under different atmospheric boundary conditions. We will select suitable sites that experience differences in urban air ventilation under different atmospheric conditions in order to conduct field measurement so as to ascertain the reliability of the simulated results. Based on the study results, we will draw up a set of Air Ventilation design guidelines that better reflect the realistic conditions. The guidelines will be formatted for designers, planners and policy-makers.

14408214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408214.value: Providing good urban air ventilation is very important for quality and healthy living in a high-density city in the tropical regions. Rapid urbanisation in developing countries in the tropical regions means that a better understanding of how to design and plan a city with wind is needed. Since 2006, based on our previous researches, a more scientific Air Ventilation Assessment (AVA) system to evaluate a development’s project’s urban air ventilation performance has been adopted by the Hong Kong Government for the city’s design and planning practice. However, one of the limits of current scientific understanding is that neutral atmospheric conditions are typically assumed when conducting experimental or simulation studies. Under weak background wind, as is typical for tropical and sub-tropical regions, local and mesoscale thermal effects start to dominate the mixing processes with a significant impact on the direction and speed of urban air ventilation. Studies for complex building structures under stratified atmospheric conditions do not exist. The 2006 AVA system therefore has limitations. This study aims to fill this knowledge gap by conducting highly resolved large-eddy simulations (LES) for buoyancy dominating weak background wind atmospheric conditions. The project will use the PArallelised LES Model (PALM) developed at the Leibniz University of Hannover for simulating turbulent atmospheric flows. The model has been previously verified as being suitable for the task at hand. The code is highly optimised for massively parallel computers, and it can currently use up to 4,096 to the power 3 grid points, which makes it suitable for fine-scale investigation (1–2 m grid) within a very large computational domain (10–20 km) under different atmospheric conditions. The proposed turbulence simulations will be the first-ever to be carried out for complex urban terrain under such realistic conditions. This study aims to provide a better scientific understanding of urban air ventilation patterns under “realistic” atmospheric conditions. Different urban layouts and morphologies will be tested to establish a parametric understanding between urban forms and urban air ventilation performance. The study will inform the current Air Ventilation Assessment (AVA) system in Hong Kong. The city’s urban air ventilation will be more correctly predicted, thereby yielding better data for the design and planning of critical cases in the city’s metro areas. This information on how to design with greater environmental sensitivity will be useful for architects and planners not only in Hong Kong, but also in other high-density cities in the tropical regions. 在高密度的熱帶城市提供良好的城市通風對高質素和健康生活非常重要。熱帶地區的發展中國家及其城市需要更好的理解如何利用風來做設計和規劃。 自2006年起，香港政府在城市設計和規劃中採用了基于我們之前的研究提出的科學的空氣流通評估（AVA）方法，以評估發展項目的空氣流通性能。 然而，目前研究的局限之一是進行試驗和模擬的時候通常假定大氣條件是中性。在亞熱帶和熱帶地區，在弱風條件下，小尺度和中尺度城市环境中的熱效應主宰了城市風的方向和速度，中性大氣條件通常是不存在的。所以2006年的空氣流通評估（AVA）方法仍存在一定的局限性。 本研究旨在通過大渦模擬（LES）在精細尺度下研究熱浮力控制的弱風環境，以填補這方面的空白。本研究將使用由漢諾威萊布尼茲大學（Leibniz University of Hannover）研發的並行大渦模型（PArallelised LES Model ）來模擬大氣湍流。該模型已經被驗證為適合用於當前的研究。該模型已被優化至適用於大規模並行計算機，其可運算的網格點高達4096的三次方，因而可用來在不同大氣下較大的計算區域內（10-20公里）進行精細尺度研究（1-2米網格） 。本研究所提出的湍流模擬將是有史以來第一次在這樣複雜的城市條件下所進行的研究。 本研究旨在提供在真實大氣條件下對城市通風更準確的科學認識。研究不同的城市形態以建立城市型態參數和城市通風效能的關係。是次研究將優化香港現有的空氣流通評估（AVA）方法，能更準確地預測城市的通風，從而改進城市中有通風問題區域的設計和規劃。研究結果不僅對香港的建築師和設計師有用，更可以應用於其他熱帶地區的高密度城市。

14408214.label: Realisation of objectives
14408214.value: Realisation of Objective 1: Based on the statistics of realistic urban morphologies in high-density urban Hong Kong and prospective future design practices, a set of parametric urban scenarios are developed for large-eddy simulation (LES) tests. In the first step, total 48 parametric scenarios are defined. Building dimensions and street layouts are calculated from practical geometric parameters for urban planning. To give finite solutions, the site area (A) is assumed to be 1km2, the floor height (h) is assumed to be 3m, and the floor area is approximately assumed to be 2000m2 or 4000m2, depending on the value of the plot ratio (P). Given the prescribed and assumed parameters, other geometric parameters including building height (H), building number (N), frontal building size (L), and perpendicular building size (D) can be theoretically computed. From all combinations of variables, a total of 27 scenarios with homogeneous (HM) building heights can be obtained, but the ratio of horizontal building size should not be too large. Therefore, a total of 24 scenarios for homogeneous building heights are chosen. For inhomogeneous (IM) scenarios, building heights are generated by a normally distributed random series, which is given a mean of the corresponding homogeneous building height (H) and a standard deviation of H/4. In the second step, some modifications were made to the previous set of parametric scenarios. For example, a floor area including street areas around the building is assumed as 100 m by 100 m. More comprehensive situations are considered, including more ground coverage ratio (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, and 60%), and one more wind direction (45°) was considered beyond perpendicular winds. Realisation of Objective 2: The PALM model is calibrated at both CUHK and the Northern German Supercomputing Alliance (HLRN), for both neutral and unstable thermal conditions. For simulations under neutral conditions at CUHK, we utilized two methods for calibrating and validating the PALM codes: the CFD guidelines proposed by a working group from the Architectural Institute of Japan (AIJ), and the wind tunnel test results in high-density urban areas of Hong Kong in previous AVA studies. Both methods provide substantial confidence to using PALM in this study. For simulations under unstable conditions at HLRN, suitable PALM setups for simulating convective boundary layers have been calibrated. A large model domain is required to catch all relevant turbulent structures, which are considerably larger than neutral stratification, while the grid size must be kept small to sufficiently resolve the street-canyon flows. Special attention must also be given to the choice of lateral boundary conditions such that they do not alter the ventilation results. Noncyclic lateral boundary condition is applied to simulations of non-neutral atmospheric conditions for the first time. Technical challenges were encountered but were solved to realize the projective objectives. For example, the conventional turbulence recycling method produces an artificial circulation at the inflow boundary, as heat fluxes are accumulated, and a temperature gradient is generated. To fix this problem, we proposed a modification to the turbulence recycling method. Total signal of potential temperature at the recycling plate are given back to the inflow boundary, and the artificial circulation is therefore prevented. Moreover, a radiation boundary condition was set as the standard outflow condition in non-cyclic boundary simulations in PALM. This become a problem in the unstable case under weak background wind which cannot ensure positive outflows. Once negative velocities occurred at the outflow, they were artificially strengthened by the radiation condition, which led to strong inward-directed artificial winds at the outflow boundary. In this project, a new technique was introduced to handle the outflow and prevent the strong artificial winds. Realisation of Objective 3: Based on substantial LES experiments of parametric scenarios conducted in this project, some recommendations are highlighted under neutral atmospheric conditions: Inhomogeneous building heights tend to decrease the variance of site-averaged velocity ratios compared to homogeneous scenarios; Horizontal ventilation is moderated by the vertical momentum generated by inhomogeneous building heights; Rectangular building arrays may allow better ventilation than square building arrays; Given a moderate ground coverage ratio in square building arrays, 45° wind input allows better ventilation than 0° wind input; In cases of square arrays, higher ground coverage ratios result in lower site-averaged velocity ratios; But in the case of rectangular arrays, this negative relationship may be reversed. More importantly, this project focus on comparing the similarities or differentials of urban ventilation performances under different atmospheric boundary conditions. In a standard AVA, only neutral stratification is considered, although diabatic and particularly unstable conditions are observed more frequently in nature. The results obtained in this project indicate significant changes in ventilation under diabatic stratifications. A new definition for calculating ventilation was introduced, and used to compare the influence of buildings on ventilation under conditions of neutral and unstable stratification. In general, overall ventilation under unstable conditions is found to be better than that under neutral conditions. Enhanced convective motion due to surface heating in unstable conditions is deemed the main cause. In the vicinity of exposed buildings, however, ventilation was weaker for unstable stratification than for neutral stratification. Moreover, stronger wind direction variance under unstable conditions results in weaker correlation between VRs and frontal area indices than under neutral conditions. This implies that street orientation is less important in street-level ventilation under unstable conditions than in neutral conditions, due to the importance of surface heating effects in unstable conditions. Realisation of Objective 4: With statistics of daytime observations during summer in Hong Kong using traditional meteorological data and sounding data, we demonstrate that neutral atmospheric boundary conditions occur with a very low probability, which implies that current practices are indeed far away from reality. We selected a suitable site (Tsim Sha Tsui East) that experience differences in urban air ventilation under different atmospheric conditions to ascertain the reliability of the simulated results. Field measurements and wind tunnel tests are taken from previous AVA studies. It is found that wind tunnel tests under the neutral assumption underestimate the overall ventilation as measured by pedestrian-level velocity ratio compared to field measurements, which were conducted during an unstably stratified atmospheric boundary. Velocity ratios in the unstable LES case are in line with field measurements, while those in the neutral case are close to the wind tunnel tests. In the test of Tsim Sha Tsui East, the r-square of linear regression between wind tunnel and field measurement is only 0.35. While, the r-square of linear regression between LES neutral experiment and wind tunnel, and the r-square of linear regression between LES unstable experiment and field measurement, are both 0.67. Realisation of Objective 5: The above findings are contributed to air ventilation design guidelines that better reflect the realistic conditions. As overall ventilation under unstable conditions is found to be better than that under neutral conditions, hence current AVA practices under the neutral assumption are conservative if the actual situation includes an unstably stratified boundary layer. However, the situation reversed in the vicinity of exposed buildings. The influence on ventilation by building parameters, such as the plan area index, was altered when unstable stratification was considered. Consequently, differences in stratification (including stable stratification, which may decreases urban ventilation significantly) were shown to have remarkable effects on ventilation estimates, which should be taken into consideration in future AVA practices.

14408214.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408214.value: The negative effects urban heat islands in high-density Hong Kong are increasing and better ventilation are required to improve the city’s living condition (Part C Journal Publication No. 7 & Conference Paper No. 1). In this project, novel methods for exacting building geometries from satellite images proposed (Part C Journal Publication No. 6), and parametric scenarios are developed based on the realistic context of urban forms in Hong Kong (Part C Journal Publications No. 1 & 8). Large-eddy simulations (LES) are implemented over both realistic urban forms and parametric scenarios (Part C Journal Publications No. 1-5, 8, & Conference Papers No. 1-4). Under the more common-used neutral assumption, one novel key finding and recommendation for urban planning deduced from the study is that turbulence level can be a factor in “balancing” ventilation: inhomogeneous building heights generate more turbulence in street canyons and have a negative (positive) effect on velocity ratios of low-density (very high-density) morphological scenarios. The application of this point is that homogeneous building heights are recommended when low density is present, and inhomogeneous building heights may be better in cases of high density (Part C Journal Publication No. 1 & Conference Paper No. 3). With statistics of daytime observations during summer in Hong Kong, the study demonstrates that neutral atmospheric boundary conditions occur with a very low probability, which implies that current practices are indeed far away from reality. Then the study is devoted to addressing this knowledge gap by cross-comparisons of field measurements, wind tunnel tests, and LES under neutral and unstable conditions. It is found that LES-computed velocity ratios under unstable conditions are in line with field measurements, while results of simulations under neutral conditions are close to those of wind tunnel tests (Part C Journal Publication No. 5). Enhanced vertical mixing due to surface heating produces improved ventilation performance in the unstable case. The neutral assumption tends to underestimate pedestrian-level velocity ratios compared to a diabatic condition; hence it is deemed conservative when it is adopted in AVA practices. Moreover, stronger wind direction variance under unstable conditions results in weaker correlation between velocity ratios and frontal area indices than neutral conditions, which implies that street orientations become less important in ventilation under unstable conditions (Part C Journal Publications No. 2 &5, Conference Paper No. 4). These findings are contributed to AVA guidelines.

14408214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408214.value: There are two potential further developments from this research: First, further study should be devoted to see how building porosity can improve urban ventilation under unstable atmospheric conditions. As noted from this research, street orientation or frontal area density will become less important under unstable conditions due to stronger pedestrian-level velocity and variance of wind direction compare to neutral cases, building porosity, especially porosity on and near the ground surface, which was not considered in the current parametric study, should be investigated in the future. Second, urban ventilation under stable stratification during nighttime should be studied in the future. Pedestrian-level ventilation under stable stratification can be the worst situation among various atmospheric conditions as hinted from this research. At the meantime, the effects of urban heat islands during nighttime are increasingly important as pointed out by one publication of this project. Proposed course of action based on the findings of this project is that, more comprehensive thermal stratifications should be accounted in future AVA, for instance, a range of wind profiles representing various atmospheric conditions, rather than only neutral condition, should be tested in AVA practices.

14408214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408214.value: Air ventilation assessment (AVA) system for improving wind environment has been promoted in Hong Kong based on a series of studies after the city was hit by the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) in 2003. The world’s first weak-wind urban AVA system has been applied in the city’s design and planning practices for more than a decade. However, the current AVA is known to have limitations in that it cannot correctly predict urban air ventilation performance in some areas of Hong Kong where convective motion is prominent due to inhomogeneous surface heating in weak wind conditions. One possible cause is that the current AVA methodology adopts the neutral assumption for the atmospheric boundary condition without considering thermal effects in predictions of air flows. This project demonstrates the knowledge gap between current practices and the reality by comparing wind tunnel tests, field measurements, and numerical simulations under neutral and unstable conditions in Hong Kong. Possible adaptations for future AVA practices are proposed based on the comparative results. The findings are of practical useful in improving the city’s planning and designs for better wind comfort under more realistic environmental conditions.

14408314.value: 增長機器？可持續社區？中國城市的價值與財富

14408314.label: Project Objectives
14408314.value: This project aims to employ critical urban theories and sustainability concepts and tools to explicate the embedded values of planning and spatial outcomes in contemporary urban developments in three Chinese cities in order to characterize and seek avenues for improving their futures. Specific objectives are: To compare and contrast the values that drive the planning and development processes in the ancient city of Xi’an, the post-open door city of Shenzhen and the post-colonial city of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. To employ a set of ‘exchange’ and ‘use’ values derived from critical theoretical discourses and sustainability and place-auditing practices to benchmark the principal values of planning and development, and spatial outcomes found in the three cities through: - identifying key stakeholders in the planning and development processes and examining their understanding and value positions regarding growth and sustainability. - auditing and evaluating related development and planning strategies, policies and legislations with the values set. - auditing selected communities in the three cities to ascertain whether they are spaces for growth or spaces for nurturing sustainable communities. - examining a case of controversial (re)development and identifying the value positions of different stakeholders and the consequent spatial outcome. To synthesise and analyse the research findings and examine the relationships between values and spatial outcomes (‘urban fortunes’) in the three cities and what actions each might take to achieve a more sustainable future.

Specific objectives are:

To compare and contrast the values that drive the planning and development processes in the ancient city of Xi’an, the post-open door city of Shenzhen and the post-colonial city of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

To synthesise and analyse the research findings and examine the relationships between values and spatial outcomes (‘urban fortunes’) in the three cities and what actions each might take to achieve a more sustainable future.

14408314.label: Realisation of objectives
14408314.value: The three objectives set for the research have been achieved and they are elaborated as follows. 1. To compare and contrast the values that drive the planning and development processes in the ancient city of Xi’an, the post-open door city of Shenzhen and the postcolonial city of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR). The comparative study provides the PI with a better understanding of the operation of the three cities under the ‘One Country, Two Systems’ arrangement. It is obvious in the cases of Xi’an and Shenzhen that policies initiated by the Central Government have significant impacts on development and planning processes of the two systems, a dimension not emphasised in the original proposal. Although Xi’an and Shenzhen are in very different stages of development, its growth-at-all costs approaches adopted after China’s open door policy have been moderated in recent years by the Central Government’s call for ecological modernization and various social policies that have endeavoured to minimise the gap between the rich and the poor, as well as the urbanites and rural dwellers. Central Government’s role in the planning and development of Hong Kong SAR has been less visible. Instead, critical urban theories have been instrumental to unpack the political economy of the city, showing how skewed economic and political power relationships have produced an urban landscape that exhibits socio-spatial injustice, prompting counteractions by the civil society. 2. To employ a set of ‘exchange’ and ‘use’ values derived from critical theoretical discourses and sustainability and place-auditing practices to benchmark the principal values of planning and development, and spatial outcomes found in the three cities. Invoking the concepts of ‘exchange’ and ‘use’ values in the research has proved to be invaluable. It is because through various interviews and disseminating research results in talks and seminars, participants have been enlightened by the differentiation of these two concepts. Introducing a discourse on ‘use values’ helps people appreciate better the various dimensions of development and inspire them to reflect on the core values in planning and developing a place. We have used the concepts to understand the underlying values and spatial outcomes of controversial development cases in the three cities. In all three cities, local champions prove to be important in sensitising people to the importance of use values in the development process. Places without local advocates are usually bull-dozed, with their accumulated use values over time destroyed. In the Chinese cases, the values adopted by the local government have proved to be instrumental in balancing exchange and use values. For instance, in the name of rebuilding its glorious Tang Dynasty culture, Xi’an has had a period of intensified removal of old urban villages surrounding heritage sties, leading to displacement of villages from their homes of many centuries. Similarly, wholesale redevelopment of urban villages in Shenzhen has displaced many migrant workers, depriving their right to a lower cost living closer to the centre of the city. However, recently, both city governments have moderated the rate of removal and have tried to pursue a strategy that is less destructive, as both governments realise the negative impacts of forceful removal on socio-political instability and the proper functioning of the urban economy that has to rely on people with varied skills. In the case of Hong Kong, community-driven inter-agency cooperation has been important to save places with high use values. Interestingly, the situation may not be as confrontational as cities elsewhere and hence the cases bear significant theoretical and practical implications. 3. To synthesise and analyse the research findings and examine the relationships between values and spatial outcomes (‘urban fortunes’) in the three cities and what actions each might take to achieve a more sustainable future. The research proves the importance of values in guiding urban development and its spatial outcomes. Development that focuses on exchange values alone will produce an urban landscape that tends to wipe out existing histories and communities, replacing them with gated communities and luxuries housing. The various cases highlight a few important points to better balance exchange and use values in order to achieve a more sustainable future: • Policies at the national level are instrumental in checking the impacts of rapid urban development on local communities with rich history and heritage. This observation and conclusion echo United Nation’s New Urban Agenda. • Local governments that respect research findings and are willing to conduct grounded research work tend to have a better appreciation of the socio-economic functions of local communities with high use values. Hence, unlike the conclusions of most critical urban development literature, local governments do not automatically become part of the growth coalition. In the context of China, local governments are also checked by the Central Government (and the Party) who always adopts a more balanced and comprehensive understanding of development. The recent relocation of urban and rural planning units under the Ministry of Natural Resources is a case in point. • In the course of economic and urban development, redevelopment may sometimes be inevitable. Cases in Hong Kong have pointed to at least three valuable lessons: communities with close ties and a long history showing high use value should be conserved in redevelopment projects; the concerned community members can either be accommodated or proactively adopting heritage buildings which can then act as a new nucleus for building future sustainable communities; and the balancing of exchange and use values require good will and collaboration among different parties and such an endeavour is invaluable for nourishing even more use values in place, essential for place and community sustainability.
