14408314.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408314.value: The research attempts to explore the values adopted by different stakeholders in the planning and development of Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Xi’an. In the case of Chinese cities in the mainland, it is found that evolving Central Government policies have played a significant role in guiding local urban developments. Realising the limitations of an exchange value biased development strategy pursued since the Open Door Policy, the Central Government has in recent years paid much more attention to use value related issues. Papers 1, 3, 11 and 17 have tried to examine such a transition and its implications on the local contexts. The latter is further examined and it is found that the Shenzhen Government is more sensitive to sustainability issues when compared to the Xi’an Government (papers 3, 4, 15, 16 and 17). Unless local government and their planners are sensitive to the importance of use values, local histories and heritage, a ‘slash and burn’ approach would be adopted in the course of development, ruining sometimes century old communities (papers 3, 4, 17). Different from mainland China, the role of Central Government is less visible in Hong Kong’s urban development process. Papers 5, 7, 9 and 10 attempt to invoke critical urban development theories and the latest sustainability discourses to examine Hong Kong’s urban development and it is found that the exchange value focused development of the city has led to sustainability road-blocks. However, the civil society has played an active role in counteracting the power of the state and the private sector to protect the use values of their communities. Interestingly, while the degree of confrontation between the communities and the government cum development interests varies, the research shows that bonding, bridging and linking social capitals within and beyond a community have been instrumental in balancing exchange and use values in the development and planning process (papers 6, 8, 12 and 13). The research has been productive in terms of linking two rather discrete fields of studies, critical urban theories and sustainability discourses, to understand and provide suggestions for China’s future development. Critical urban theories prove to be instrumental in laying bare power politics involved in urban development and sustainability discourses. And sustainable development that promotes a more humane and ecological urbanism based on use values is fundamental to steering urban development at various levels. Papers 2, 9, 14 and 17 have tried to elaborate on these conclusions.

14408314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408314.value: China’s spatial revolution carries significant theoretical and practical implications and should be followed closely especially when most of the world’s future cities to accommodate the growing urban population have yet to be built. China’s urban experiments whether in Xi’an or Shenzhen have revealed the importance of Central and local government policies and their embedded values in pursuing urban development. As all the case studies in the research project underline the importance of balancing exchange and use values, further studies on examining the detailed mechanisms that foster the connections and integration between central and local government policies as well as local governments’ interactions, negotiations and collaborations with local stakeholders to pursue sustainable developments that address or redress power relationships will be extremely useful. Examination of the context and reasons behind the innovation of concrete mechanisms in balancing exchange and use values and their implications on the power relationships among different stakeholders in more cities can confirm if China is experimenting with a qualitatively different approach towards a more sustainable future.

14408314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408314.value: The cityscape is a manifestation of a city’s power relationships and the values embedded in the planning and development processes. Places with high use values usually have vibrant economic activities, rich history, hard and soft heritage and cohesive communities. Places with monotonous luxurious housing may have very high exchange values but may not be the best sites to build sustainable communities. Who should decide on the balance of exchange and use values in a place? For cities in mainland China, it is found that the central and local governments play a significant role in determining the purposes and processes of planning and development. While Chinese cities seemed to have pursued a growth-at-all-costs approach after the Open Door Policy, the Central Government has since the early 2010s, tried to steer the country towards a more sustainable pathway that redresses imbalanced power relationships. Case studies in Shenzhen and Xi’an testify such a change. The situation in Hong Kong is different. Instead of the government, it is the city’s civil society that has played an active role in preserving use values of their beloved places, leading to innovative cross-sector and multi-actor approaches to counteract displacement and to facilitate continuous sustainable community building.

14408414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408414.value: This research project investigates the popularization and localization of Hong Kong cuisine in postwar Japan, in particular the Heisei era (1989-present), from historical and ethnographic perspectives. It will be a pioneering study that sheds new light on Japanese studies, Hong Kong studies, Japan-Hong Kong relations and Asian foodways. The history of Hong Kong cuisine in Japan can be traced to the Meiji period (1868-1912) when some Chinese restaurants in Yokohama Chinatown and Kobe Chinatown recruited chefs from Hong Kong. However, in the prewar period, Hong Kong cuisine was introduced to Japan only as a part of Cantonese cuisine (kanton ryōri). Following the rise of tourist flows between Japan and Hong Kong and the boom of Hong Kong movies in Japan in the 1970s and 1980s, Hong Kong cuisine (honkon ryōri), represented by dim sum, wonton noodle, conge, fried rice, roasted meat and steamed fish, finally became an independent culinary genre. The popularity of Hong Kong cuisine can be seen from the increasing number of Hong Kong cuisine restaurants, grocery stores and food products in major cities of Japan during the last few decades. Most are located outside Chinatown and run by the Japanese. Hong Kong cuisine has drawn media attention, frequently featured on Japanese television and websites and covered in the print media. Globalization and localization are two sides of the same coin. Hong Kong cuisine has been localized considerably in Heisei Japan. For example, dim sum can now be served on a circular conveyor belt like kaiten sushi (sushi-go-around). Wonton soup noodle uses very small wonton and the soup tastes like Japanese ramen. More interestingly, the Japanese have created some Hong Kong dishes (such as Hong Kong fried rice, Hong Kong taxi rice and Hong Kong fried noodle with XO sauce) out of their own imagination. This kind of culinary hybridization and exchange will be theoretically and empirically examined. Based on data collection, fieldwork, theoretical analysis, this research project will break new grounds in these aspects: First, it is a pioneering research on the history and impact of Hong Kong cuisine in Japan. Second, it provides a strong case study to demonstrate the interplay of globalization and localization in transnational cultural flows. Third, the data and analysis generated from this research not only have academic significance, but also provide important references for food business. 本研究從歷史及民族誌的角度探討戰後日本，特別是平成時代(1989至今），香港料理的普及在地化，它對日本研究、港日關係及亞洲飲食文化研究均具開拓性。 香港料理在日本的歷史可追溯自明治時代(1868-1912) 。當時一些橫濱及神戶唐人街的中國餐廳從香港招聘厨師。不過香港菜在戰前日本只隸屬廣東料理。自上世紀七、八十年代，港日旅客交流日趨頻密，以點心、雲吞麵、粥、炒飯、燒味及清蒸海鲜為代表的香港菜開始獨立起來。數十年間日本各大城市的香港茶館、雜貨店及食品不斷增加，它们大多設在唐人街之外及由日人經營。香港菜受日本傳媒關注，不時在電視、報章雜誌及網站被介紹。 全球化及在地化是銅版的兩面。香港茶在平成日本經在地化洗禮。例如港式點心像旋轉壽司般放在輸送帶上。雲吞麵的雲吞變小及湯底似日式拉麵。日人憑想像創造出、香港炒飯、的士炒飯、香港XO醬炒麵等茶式。這種食的混種化與交流值得從理論及實踐上探討。 透過資料搜集、實地調查及理論分析，此研究在以下三方面有所突破：第一，這是香港料理在日本的歷史與影響的開拓性研究。第二，這對跨文化交流中全球化及在地化在的關係提供個案研究。第三，此研究產生的數據及分析不但具學術價值，而且可供飲食業參考。

14408414.label: Realisation of objectives
14408414.value: The four academic objectives have been fully achieved during the two-year project period. (1) Outline the history of Hong Kong cuisine in postwar Japan from the 1970s to the present: This project is mainly a historical study. We (PI and RA) have collected many primary and secondary sources about Hong Kong cuisine in postwar Japan from archives, libraries, museums and databases of Japanese newspapers. All data are classified into folders and have been used for publications and public lectures. I have also interviewed some Hong Kong chefs and restaurant owners in Japan and all these interviews are recorded and transcribed. We now have a relatively clear picture of the development of Hong Kong cuisine in postwar Japan, in particular the new trends during the last three decades. (2) Acquire data about Hong Kong restaurants and food products in Heisei Japan: We have gathered data of hundreds of Hong Kong restaurants in Japan and classified them into different categories. This project has focused more on dimsum restaurants and Hong Kong-style cafes (cha chaan teng) in Tokyo, Kobe and Yokohama. Hong Kong yamcha and fast-food are highlighted because they are the two most representative and popular forms of food culture in Japan. The PI have visited many dimsum restaurants and Hong Kong-style cafes in these three Japanese cities. As for food products, we have gathered many data and then classified them into different categories. It is interesting to know that some Japanese companies also manufacture Hong Kong food ingredients and products as well as the Japanese have created many Hong Kong food items that cannot be found in Hong Kong. (3) Provide an analysis of localization and hybridization of Hong Kong cuisine in Japan: This is also an ethnographic and anthropological study. All empirical data are analyzed in the lens of localization and hybridization of Hong Kong cuisine in contemporary Japan. The project and the publications generated from it show good balance of theory and empirical data. The project has demonstrated that Hong Kong cuisine has been remade and reimagined by the Japanese. It explains why and how the Japanese consume localized Hong Kong food. In terms of Hong Kong-Japan culinary exchange, the history of Hong Kong cuisine in Japan reflects local adaptation and cultural appropriation. (4) Understand the attitudes of the Japanese towards Hong Kong cuisine: We conducted a survey on 450 Japanese, asking them about their attitudes towards Hong Kong cuisine through 14 questions. All the data have been made into charts for analysis and used for publications. We also interviewed a number of Japanese in Japan and Hong Kong to understand their images of Hong Kong cuisine. Our major finding is that the Japanese have different images and imagination of Hong Kong cuisine. For instance, they tend to associate beauty and health as the two key elements in Hong Kong cuisine.

14408414.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408414.value: Major findings: (1) Hong Kong cuisine, as an independent food genre, did not appear in Japan until the 1980s. Its popularity reached the peak in the 1990s and began to decline in the 2000s. (2) Hong Kong cuisine has been in the process of localization from the very beginning and now it has been highly localized in terms of the taste, serving, ingredients used, chefs, images, way of serving, eating custom and the design of the restaurant. (3) The Japanese have very different images of Hong Kong cuisine. They tend to associate it with beauty, wealth and fung-shui. (4) The Japanese have created many new Hong Kong food items that cannot be found in Hong Kong. (5) For safety reasons, the Japanese whenever possible use Japanese ingredients to replace Chinese ingredients to make Hong Kong cuisine. 14408414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408414.value: (1) Each coin has two sides. It would be better if a research on the localization of Japanese cuisine in Hong Kong can be done. By doing these, the whole picture of Hong Kong-Japan culinary exchange will be clear. I have published academic papers and made presentations on this topic. (2) The Cantonese community in Japanese Chinatown is a topic of great potential and significance. Thanks to this GRF, I came to know some Cantonese leaders in Yokohama and Kobe Chinatowns and the running of the Cantonese clan associations. 14408414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408414.value: This is a pioneering project on the popularization and localization of Hong Kong food culture in contemporary Japan from historical and ethnographic perspectives. It has traced the origins of Hong Kong cuisine in Japan in the last hundred years, highlighting the rise and fall of Hong Kong cuisine since the 1980s to the present. The project combines theories of globalization, localization, and hybridization with empirical study from data collection, survey and on-site observation. The main objective of the project is to trace the historical development of Hong Kong cuisine and to analyze its cultural significance in the lens of localization. It shows that Hong Kong cuisine has been highly localized in Japan and the Japanese have created their own imaginations of Hong Kong cuisine. The same food item may have different meanings to Hongkongers and Japanese. The publications and data generated from this project are not only academically significant, they also provide important references for the Hong Kong people who want to run a food business in Japan.

14408514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408514.value: "Current Literature" （當代文藝）was founded by Xu Su（徐速，1924－1981）and published monthly in Hong Kong (12/1965-4/1979, 9/1982-8/1983, 2/1999-12/2000) . It is arguably the most popular Hong Kong middle-brow literary journal of the 1970s, yet its success has been largely ignored by the academia. Driven by Xu Su’s passion to promote literature among general readers, this unassuming and politically neutral journal has succeeded, mainly in the 1970s, not only in nurturing aspiring writers locally and abroad, but also in creating a vibrant Sinophone literary community outside China. A closer look at the major contributors to this journal in the 1970s reveals three geographical locations: the colonial cities of Hong Kong and Macao, the tropical region comprising Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and the Philippines, and the politically unstable Indochina countries such as Vietnam, Laos, Thailand and Burma. Other contributors, lesser in number by comparison, came from Taiwan, Europe and North America. This project has two major objectives. Firstly, this research will regard "Current Literature" as an important site of cultural production, delineate its vision and characteristics, compare it to its rivals of this period such as "Haiyang Wenyi"（海洋文藝）, and evaluate the impact it has made upon the emerging Sinophone literatures of Hong Kong and South-East Asia. Secondly, this research will assess the literary achievements of individual writers and explicate the main features of various literary communities formed by these writers. In short, upon completion of this project, we will arrive at a better understanding of (1) the historical role played by Hong Kong and "Current Literature" in the formation of Sinophone literatures of various regions outside China; (2) the works and styles of notable writers who have made significant contributions to the success of the journal; (3) lesser-known Sinophone writings of Indochina countries; (4) Sinophone literature as a whole. 《當代文藝》是南來作家徐速於一九六五年在香港創辦的文學雜誌，歷經三個階段（12/1965-1979，9/1982-81983，2/1999-12／2000）。三個階段之中，以第一階段的行銷時間最長，銷路最廣，也最具文學影響力。目前學術界對這份曾經暢銷六、七〇年代的重要刊物尚未有深入的研究。 《當代文藝》於政治與文藝兩方面保持中立的態度，使它不僅成為培養香港與外地作家的重要園地，還促成了海外華語語系文學的發展。以第一階段為例，主要作者來自三大地區：港澳兩地、東南亞地區、以及台灣、北美與歐洲等地，包括了當年大部份的海外華人生活區域，其影響力可見一斑。 本研究計劃有兩大目的。一、《當代文藝》為當年重要的文化生產場域，本計劃將釐清其創辦宗旨、文藝取向與刊物特點，進而分析其對香港以及東南亞華語文學創作所產生的積極作用。二、分析海外不同地區的文學特色，亦評估個別作者的文學成就。 本計劃完成以後，將會增進學術界對以下四個方面的認識：一、香港以及《當代文藝》作為當年海外文化生產中心的歷史角色；二、《當代文藝》的重要作者、他們的作品與風格；三、東南亞華語文學創作；四、華語語系文學。

14408814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408814.value: The educational challenge of the 21st century facing many countries is to achieve higher levels of learning for all students and increase global competitiveness in a knowledge society. School reforms across different education systems have targeted student learning outcomes and teaching is considered as the most powerful influence on student’s achievement. International evidence suggests that the success of educational reforms depends on teachers’ individual and collective capacity and links to the school-wide capacity for promoting students’ learning. Since 1990s, the concept of professional learning communities (PLCs) has gained increasing attention from education systems. Research evidence consistently highlights the importance of interdependent learning and collaboration as the cornerstone of school improvement and effective professional development. However, much of the existing literature on PLCs has focused on Anglo-American settings. The absence of empirical research on PLCs is particularly acute in Asian settings and justifies the need to explore the diversity and complexity of PLCs in different cultural contexts and broaden our understanding of critical issues facing educators, including those in Asia. Today’s centre of high performance in school education is East Asia. According to the OECD’s 2009 PISA assessments, four of the world’s five highest-performing systems were Shanghai, Hong Kong, Korea and Singapore. Evidence indicates that high performance in these education systems comes from effective education strategies that focus on well-designed and well-implemented programs that continuously improve learning and teaching. We propose to conduct a comparative and empirical study of the practices of PLCs across Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei. The study aims to understand the practices of PLCs from a socio-cultural and comparative perspective by addressing similarities and diversities across a number of theoretical and practical issues. This three-stage research is expected to reveal complex relationships within contexts, processes of PLCs, and educational outcomes within the three education systems. Stage I is a comparative socio-cultural study of education reforms in the three Chinese societies and exploration of their relationships to educational transformation and school improvement. Stage II involves comparative and quantitative assessments of the processes of PLCs across the systems and teachers’ perceptions of organizational outcomes. Stage III involves qualitative case studies on the processes of PLCs in the schools. The findings of the study will make a significant contribution to enhanced understanding of the PLCs across three Chinese societies and shed lights on school improvement and educational transformation in other cultural contexts. 對很多國家而言，廿一世紀教育的挑戰是在全球化及知識型社會中提升競爭力。各國的教育體系都將教育改革聚焦在促進教師的教學效能，從而提升學生的學習水平。很多大型的國際教育研究都顯示，一個教育體系的成敗是取決於教師個人的素養、教師團隊的集體力量、以及學校促進學生學習的策略上。 從上世紀九十年代開始，很多學者都關注到「專業學習社群」的重要性，對其概念、形成和影響等進行研究。很多的成果都顯示，教師團隊中的互相學習及協作，都對教師的專業發展及學校改進都有積極作用。現存有關「專業學習社群」的文獻，大都是緣自英國、美國、以及一些西方的國家，來自其他文化或地域的甚少，尤其來自亞洲國家或地區的教育研究更是付之闕如。這也說明在其他文化背景下來研究「專業學習社群」的迫切性，和探究「專業學習社群」在其他教育體系中的概念、形態及功能等的需要性。這新建議的研究方向，將有助大家瞭解「專業學習社群」在不同文化背景下的異同。 今天，在國際教育比試中發現，大部份的高效能的教育體系都在亞洲。聯合國經濟合作暨發展組織在二零零九年公佈的學生能力國際評估計劃之結果題示，首五名學生成績優異的國家或地區當中，有四個國家或地區都在亞洲，當中包括上海、香港、韓國及星加波。有研究顯示，他們都很成功，是因為這些教育體系都擁有一些不斷有效提升教與學效能的策略和措施。 我們就以上的議論，建議進行一項比較及實徵的教育研究，以瞭解香港、上海與臺北的教育體育，為甚麼他們能在國際的教育比試中成功，以及「專業學習社群」在這三個教育體系中的作用。主要目的是探究「專業學習社群」在三地的異同、「專業學習社群」在三地的教育改革中擔當的角色及作用，和「專業學習社群」與這三個教育體系在國際教育比試中的成功有何關係。 這研究旨在探索教育改革、「專業學習社群」和教育產出的關係，並分為三個階段進行。首階段是瞭解三個教育體系中教育改革的背景、策略和措施，以及教育改革和學校改進的關係。第二階段是一項量化的比較研究，旨在探究「專業學習社群」在三地之異同，當中包括型態、過程及影響。第三階段是一些質化的個案研究，從三地之教育體系中，尋找一些成功實踐「專業學習社群」的學校，引證前階段所發現的成果，及進一步發掘新的發現。 總體上，這研究將幫助我們進一步瞭解「專業學習社群」在華人社會教育體系上的作用，這將有助啟示學校改進和教育變革理論的發展。

14408814.label: Realisation of objectives
14408814.value: The research has addressed different research questions in different stages. In Stage I, a comparative socio-cultural study of education reforms in Shanghai and Hong Kong was conducted, which aimed to explore of their relations to educational transformation and school improvement. The contextual analyses have mapped the educational reform and school improvement in each of the two Chinese societies, Hong Kong and Shanghai. With document analysis and in-depth interviews conducted in each setting, we have captured qualitative insights from system administrators, principals, and teachers in both cities. The interviews involved participants respectively from Hong Kong and Shanghai, including four policy makers/administrators from the Bureau of Education, and six school principals and 10 department heads. The interviews were digitally-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The transcripts were coded, based on emergent themes and categories for identifying significant themes grounded in both contexts. Similarities and diversities across the two education systems were mapped to address research questions. Relevant documents including government and school policies regarding professional learning were collected. All these have provided background information for our understanding of school reforms in specific contexts. In Stage II, comparative and quantitative assessments of the processes of PLCs between schools in Hong Kong and those in Shanghai as well as teachers’ perceptions of organizational outcomes were carried out. As informed by the exploratory enquiry at Stage I and extensive literature review, an item pool was created to form the subscales involved in the instrument, namely, the Educational Transformation and School Improvement Questionnaire (ETSIQ). It has been developed for the purposes of this stage of research quantitative data collection at Stage II, which allowed for empirical comparison of organizational features between Shanghai and Hong Kong. The ETSIQ assessed teachers’ perceptions of PLCs practices, processes of school improvement and transformation, as well as school outcomes. In the first dimension, teachers were asked to rate (i) their perceptions of the effectiveness of education reform within their respective systems, and (ii) feelings about the extent to which the bureau-school relationship in practices. These scales could offer basic information for our understanding of the differences between the two education systems in terms of context, background, history and governance paradigm. As to the second dimension of the ETSIQ, teachers were asked to rate their perceptions of (i) the practice of leadership for change by the principals, (ii) organizational climate in general, (iii) the extent of clarity and sharing of school goals, (iv) the practice of continuous professional development, (v) the practice of teacher collaborative learning, as well as (vi) the capacity of collective enquiry among teachers. The assessments of these six scales have allowed us to understand the PLC processes and insights of the relationship among them, at both the organizational and teacher levels. The third dimension of the ETSIQ concerns about school outcomes, in which teachers were asked to rate their feelings about school life, including, (i) teacher efficacy, (ii) teacher empowerment, (iii) teacher commitment and (iv) job satisfaction. These scales have provided the possibility of examining the effects of the PLCs processes on school outcomes and as evidence of construct validity of the questionnaire, ETSIQ. A sample of 25 schools from Shanghai, with 30 teachers from each of the school, was involved in the survey conducted from November to December in 2015. Similarly, with the same instrument, the ETSIQ, a sample of 25 schools participated in the survey in Hong Kong from May to July in 2016. In total, around 750 teachers from 25 Shanghai schools and 720 teachers from 25 Hong Kong schools have returned their responses in this study. The two samples of schools were randomly selected with different stratum characteristics of school and teacher demography. So, quantitative data were collected to answer the related research questions empirically. In Stage III, qualitative case studies on the processes of PLCs in schools in Shanghai and Hong Kong were attempted. The case studies have provided a basic understanding of the complexity and dynamic of the PLCs processes and how they had impacts on school improvement and transformation. The qualitative data collected in this stage will be used to support or refute the findings from Stage I and to compare the findings from the empirical analyses of quantitative data in Stage II. In these multiple case studies, a total six schools both from Shanghai and Hong Kong, three from each cities, with sapient characteristics of ETSIQ and high organizational outcomes were identified. A group of seven respondents from each school with different demographic characteristics and experience were interviewed, including the principal, three senior teachers and three junior teachers. In the interviews, the key features of PLCs across the two education systems were revisited and revised based on both qualitative and quantitative data analyses and findings derived from three different stages of the research. The findings have helped refine the theoretical framework for the study of PLCs in the Chinese societies and shed light on school improvement and educational transformation in other cultural contexts.

14408814.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408814.value: Based on the development the theoretical framework, and the adopted three stages of designed research methodology, major findings of the GRF project are as below for the time being. We have explored the characteristics and concepts of professional learning community in the context of Shanghai and Hong Kong, as well as examined how the PLC practices and leadership processes might have related to school transformation and improvement in both cities. The major findings include: • Exploring the characteristics of professional learning communities in Shanghai and Hong Kong with mixed methodologies; • Examining the relationship among educational reform, the PLC practices and the processes of school transformation and improvement; • Investigating into how transformational leadership might have effects on teachers’ work attitudes in Chinese educational contexts; • Exploring conceptual features of school capacity for teacher learning in the two cities; • Connecting principal leadership to teachers' professional development from the perspectives of principals; • Exploring the relationship of educational reforms and professional learning community practices in both top performing education systems in the PISA studies; • How both Shanghai and Hong Kong education systems have strived for excellence and equity via reforms and by enhancing teachers’ professional learning; • How could be the system-wide educational reform agenda supporting leadership for teacher learning; • Providing evidence of how principal leadership leads to effective teacher professional learning; • Providing empirical support for the relationship between teacher capacity of professional learning • and teacher self-efficacy from structural equation modelling; and • Comparing the development of professional learning communities in schools in Shanghai and Hong Kong. Though the schedule of the GRF project has ended according to the time frame designed in the plan, statistical analyses in a comparative perspective from the quantitative data obtained from both Shanghai and Hong Kong will be further carried and at least a few more publications will be released in the near future. It is planned that an academic book or a special issue for an academic journal will be worked out after more findings and outcomes are obtained from further data analyses in comparing educational reform, PLC practices and organizational outcomes between the two cities.

14408814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408814.value: Basically, the GRF project has addressed some of the research questions in the plan, though more writing and publications are pending. This project has also allowed the availability of both qualitative and quantitative be ready for inquiry. Further analyses of the quantitative data with advanced statistics will allow new discoveries from the original hypotheses. Further reflecting on the available data and re-integrating with the quantitative and qualitative findings may generate new research problems and new research questions. A meta-analysis of the findings of this study together with the existing related studies and literature would also allow further conceptualization of the theory of ‘professional learning community’ in the field and re-define its roles in educational transformation and school improvement. It is to further suggest that a global conceptualization of the professional learning community process, in which a transition from country perspectives to international commonalities, should be proposed in future research.

14408814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408814.value: School reforms across different education systems have targeted student learning outcomes and teaching is considered as the most powerful influence on student’s achievement. International evidence suggests that the success of educational reforms depends on teachers’ individual and collective capacity and links to the school-wide capacity for promoting students’ learning. Research evidence consistently highlights the importance of the practice of professional learning community (PLC) within schools, in which teachers’ interdependent learning and collaboration as the cornerstone of school improvement and effective professional development. The purpose of this study is to explore the diversity and complexity of PLCs in different cultural contexts. This study aims to supplement the existing literature on PLCs and broaden our understanding of critical issues facing educators. A comparative, empirical study of the practices of PLCs between Hong Kong and Shanghai was conducted, by addressing similarities and diversities across a number of theoretical and practical issues. The three-stage research has revealed the complex relationships among contexts, processes of PLCs, and educational outcomes in both Shanghai and Hong Kong. The study has contributed to enhance our understanding of the PLCs in the two Chinese societies and shed lights on school improvement and educational transformation in other cultural contexts.

14408914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14408914.value: Different speakers produce their speech sounds differently. For example, the word "bit" spoken by one speaker may be acoustically more similar to another speaker's production of "bet", rather than "bit". Consequently, speech sounds are often difficult to acoustically categorize reliably. Despite such variability, most people are able to perceptually categorize speech sounds rather accurately. This evokes the question why human speech perception seems so effortless. An important way that the brain tackles variation is through reliance on context. Contextual information provides useful cues to listeners, for example about the timbre of a particular speaker's voice. Listeners use such information to "recalibrate", or normalize, the perception of speech sounds. The influence of context on speech perception has been termed extrinsic normalization. An important and unresolved question is at which level of speech processing extrinsic normalization takes place. A number of researchers have found qualitatively similar normalization effects with speech and nonspeech contexts, arguing that both effects originate from general auditory processing levels. However, other researchers have disputed this general auditory origin, arguing that effects of nonspeech contexts may indeed originate from general auditory stages, but that effects of speech contexts mostly originate from more specific, non-auditory, levels of processing. The timing of contextual influences therefore would provide critical evidence for this debate. Electroencephalography (EEG), which has fine temporal resolution, is well suited to examine the early (general auditory) vs. late (speech specific) levels of processing. However, relatively few studies have used EEG to investigate this question. In this project, we propose to examine the neural mechanism of extrinsic normalization. First, we establish the cognitive and neural locus of extrinsic normalization with the first four experiments. Second, in the last two experiments, we compare the established locus of extrinsic normalization to other perceptual mechanisms that are known to reduce perceptual overlap between speech sounds. Findings of this project can contribute to the debate regarding the cognitive locus of extrinsic normalization. Moreover, it will provide detailed insights of how different normalization processes operate together to achieve perceptual constancy under widely varying listening conditions. Unveiling these combined processes will advance the understanding of our remarkable ability to understand speech sounds so accurately. 不同人所發的語音在物理聲學層面上有很大的差異。例如，從語音的聲學特征來看，一位說話者說的“bit”可能會更接近另一位說話者的“bet”，而不是“bit”。因此，僅通過聲學特征很難對語音進行準確的歸類。然而，作為聽話者，大多數人卻可以對語音進行準確的感知，且毫不費力。這就引出一個問題：為何語音感知看似如此輕易？ 大腦處理這一問題的一個重要手段是依靠語境。聽話人可以從語境中提取有用的線索，如說話人的音色等，幫助“校正”感知，或對語音進行感知上的歸一化。語境對語音感知的這種影響被稱作外在歸一化（或語境歸一化）。 但是，目前亟待解決的問題是外在歸一化究竟發生在言語加工的哪一個層面。由於許多研究者發現語音和非語音語境都可以引發性質上類似的歸一化效果（雖然效果大小不同），進而認為兩者所引發的歸一化都是源於較低級的聽覺加工層面。但也有不少學者質疑這一觀點，認為由非語音語境所引發的歸一化現象源於聽覺加工層面，而由語音語境所引發的歸一化則更多地源於更特定的語音加工層面。 測量語境歸一化發生的時間可以為解決這一爭議提供關鍵性證據。腦電圖技術具有較好的的時間分辨率，因此適於研究這一問題：究竟感知歸一化是發生在較早的聽覺加工層面還是較晚的語音加工層面。然而，鮮有利用腦電圖技術來系統地研究這一問題。 在本項目中，我們主要研究外在歸一化的神經機制。首先，我們通過四組實驗確定外在歸一化的神經加工層面。隨後，通過最後兩項實驗，我們將把外在歸一化同已知的的感知歸一化機制進行對比。 本項目的研究成果可以為有關外在歸一化的加工層面的爭辯做出貢獻，並深化我們對不同的歸一化機制如何在各種聽覺條件下互相協作以實現聽話人感知恆常性這一問題的理解。通過揭示這些互相協作的加工過程，我們會對人類非同尋常的準確的言語感知能力有更全面更細緻的了解。

14408914.label: Realisation of objectives
14408914.value: It is a fundamental question in speech perception research how linguistic content is retrieved from speech signals in the face of within- and between-talker variance. To achieve rapid and accurate speech perception, it has been well demonstrated that phonetic cues in the context play an important role in talker normalization. According to the context tuning mechanism, listeners tune to a particular talker’s phonetic space based on contextual phonetic cues, which can provide important frames of reference for normalizing talker variation in spoken word recognition. In this project, six experiments outlined in the proposal have been conducted over a period of 36 months. Except for Experiment 2, which is a cross-linguistic behavioral study, EEG data have been collected using a NeuroScan 128-channel system in all other five experiments. Details about the construction of the speech materials can be found in http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/xhp0000504.supp. Please note that for most experiments, in particular, all EEG experiments, the vowels /u/ and /o/ were not preceded by the consonant /f/ for precisely time-locking the recording of the EEG signals to the onset of the vowels. Moreover, there were also some tuning about Experiment 2. Dutch listeners were replaced with a group of native English listeners. While the target continuum stuck to /u-o/ continuum, two contexts were involved. One context was the concatenation of the vowels /e/ and /i/, the other was the concatenation of the vowels /œ/ and /y/. Vowels /e/ and /i/ are common in both Cantonese and English, but vowels /œ/ and /y/ occur only in Cantonese.

14408914.label: Major findings and research outcome
14408914.value: 1. The lexical tone was only influenced by F0 in immediately preceding and following contexts. However, vowel quality was only influenced by the F1 in preceding contexts, but this extended to contexts from preceding trials. Contextual influences on tone and vowel quality are qualitatively different, which has important implications for understanding the mechanism of context effects in speech perception. 2. By conducting the lexical tone normalization task and the vowel normalization task in a comparable set-up (i.e., the same subjects, the similar experimental paradigm and the same data analysis strategies), we found that the lexical tone normalization occurred in the P3 time window (250-500ms) but the vowel normalization occurred in the N2 time window (200-400ms). The different ERP components as well as different time windows suggest that the perceptual normalization of lexical tones and that of vowels may be implemented relatively independently. 3. In our previous study of talker normalization of lexical tones, we found that the context effect was a product of multiple levels of processing, with the primary contribution from phonological cues. We adopted a cross-linguistic design and found that phonological knowledge was a significant component for vowel normalization. Phonological cues likely enable listeners to effectively calibrate the acoustic-to-phonological mapping of speech sounds for each talker, facilitating the categorization accordingly.

14408914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14408914.value: We have completed a GRF project (RGC Ref No.448413) on tone normalization, and this GRF project on vowel normalization. We are surely interested in further extending this line of research to consonant normalization. Given pitch is a prominent feature for both lexical tones as well as music notes. In particular, we have found that pitch information embedded in non-speech signals provides negligible contributions to the normalization of lexical tones. However, whether pitch information in music is helpful for tone normalization is still an open question. We have already been awarded another GRF project (RGC Ref No. 15607518) which systematically investigates the contribution of music pitch in tone normalization.

14408914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14408914.value: It is a fundamental question in speech perception research how linguistic content is retrieved from speech signals in the face of within- and between-talker variance. The process of recognizing intended words despite the acoustic variations induced by talker variability is called talker normalization. Context plays an important role in such a process. Listeners tune to a particular talker’s phonetic space based on contextual phonetic cues, which can provide important frames of reference for normalizing talker variation in spoken word recognition. Contextual influences on tone and vowel quality are qualitatively different: lexical tone is only influenced by F0 in immediately preceding and following contexts, while vowel quality is only influenced by the F1 in preceding contexts, but this extends to even earlier contexts. In this project, behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) experiments have been conducted to systematically examine the psychological and neural bases of context dependent talker normalization in vowel and tone perception. Findings of this project have important implications for understanding the mechanism of context effects in speech perception, leading to a deeper understanding of perceptual constancy in general.

14409014.label: Project Objectives
14409014.value: This project identifies and studies a hitherto unexplored aspect of the late sixteenth century Korean War (1592-1598): the impact of strategic pragmatism and clique politics on Ming China’s policy towards Korea and Japan. This project sheds new lights on the studies of both the Korean War (1592-1598) and the Ming political history. It argues that strategic pragmatism and clique politics were the two most important factors shaping Ming China’s decision and actions during the War. It therefore transcends the conventional cultural explanation of Ming China’s foreign policy. With these findings, this project aims at producing at least two well-documented papers for peer-reviewed academic journals, and one book of collected papers on the Korean War.

14409014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14409014.value: This research project studies Ming China’s decision making process during the Korean War (1592-1598). It argues that strategic pragmatism and clique politics were the two most important factors shaping Ming China’s decisions to go to war, to negotiate, and then to go to war again, with Japan. While it is true that the Ming emperor and his ministers discussed the Korean crisis with such vocabulary of tributary system like “celestial dynasty”, “vassal states” and “tribute”, this project cautions against a too conventional cultural explanation of Ming China’s stance and actions during the War. As news of Japanese invasion of Korea reached Beijing in late 1592, a consensus of rescuing Korea and defeating the Japanese was quickly established. Strategic pragmatism was clearly at work: the Ming government was determined to prevent the Korean Peninsula from becoming a gangboard of hostile force threatening China’s northeastern coast. However, by early 1593, as the Ming counterattack was checked by Japan’s ambush in Byeokjegwan, a bizarre peace talk began and was to last for four years. At this point, clique politics made its presence felt. The Ming court was split into “hawkish” and “dovish” camps. Shi Xing石星, Minister of War and leader of the doves, with the tacit agreement from his superior, Zhao Zhigao趙志臯the Grand Secretary, advocated for a peace deal that would have granted Japanese overlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi the title of “King of Japan” in return for Japan’s retreat from Korea. Unsurprisingly, doves invited hawks, and Zhao Zhigao and Shi Xing were confronted by his hawkish colleagues like Wang Dewan王德完, He Qiaoyuan何喬遠 and, later on, more drastically, by Xing Jie邢玠. A war of memorials, impeachment, ferocious accusations and indignant defense broke out in the Ming court. It was in this sense that Beijing became the other theatre of the Korean War. This project unveils the complex process through which the Ming government formulated its Korean policy during these critical seven years. It explicates how a hidden network weaved Shi Xing, Zhao Zhigao and other “dovish” officials together, only to throw them against their “hawkish” colleagues. It also argues that emperor Wanli’s ambiguous attitude and inaction during the Korean War were a deliberate and conscious choice of governance style, and this style can be better understood by taking into consideration the political climate of Ming China in late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. 本研究計劃旨在理解明朝政府在萬曆朝鮮戰爭(1592-1598)期間的決策過程。從決定出兵援朝抗日，到決定以「封貢」方案議和，到決定再度用兵抗日，這個複雜的決策過程，牽涉哪些主要官員？反映什麼派系之爭？作為最高領導人的明神宗，又在這個複雜的決策過程中扮演什麼角色？本研究計劃一一予以解答。本研究計劃也認為，明朝政府在萬曆朝鮮戰爭期間的決策過程，是萬曆時期明朝政府運作、黨派政治的縮影。

14409014.label: Realisation of objectives
14409014.value: This research project unveils a hitherto seldom studied aspect of the 16th-century Korea War: the Ming court politics. The objectives of the project are “two well-documented papers for peer-reviewed academic journals”. I have more than fully achieved these objectives. I have published one paper in peer-refereed academic journals, organized two special issues for peer-refereed academic journals, delivered seven conference papers, trained one MPhil. student, in addition to contributing to CUHK’s initiative of Knowledge Transfer. I unveil the complex historical process in which Ming court politics intertwined with the dynamics of the War. The “doves” network, including Shen Weijing, Shi Xing and Zhao Zhigao, were undermined and ultimately destroyed by the “hawks” headed by Shen Weijing within the institutional context of the Ming Grand Secretariat. It is in this sense that the Ming court politics can be understood as “the other theatre” of the War. I also cover other important and interesting aspects of the War, such as the Ming fiscal operation, the Ming government’s strategic realism, the Ming-Korea trade during the War, etc.. I am poised to further advance my findings and by writing an English monograph fit for academic press by 2019.

14409014.label: Major findings and research outcome
14409014.value: This research project studies Ming government’s policy in the Korean War (1592-1598) in terms of Ming court politics. Ming court politics was an important context within which the Ming government decided to go to war, to negotiate, and then to go to war again, with Japan. In my 2017 article published in Mingdai Yanjiu, I document and analyze the personnel change of the Grand Secretariat, the most important decision-making body of the Ming state apparatus, and show how Shen Yiguan came to dominate the Secretariat by the latter half of the War. I then juxtapose the the personnel change of the Grand Secretariat with Ming government’s policy towards the Korea theatre. I unveils the complex process through which the Ming government formulated its Korean policy during these critical seven years. It explicates how a hidden network weaved Shi Xing, Zhao Zhigao and other dovish officials together, only to throw them against their hawkish colleagues. It also argues that emperor Wanli’s ambiguous attitude and inaction during the Korean War were a deliberate and conscious choice of governance style, and this style can be better understood by taking into consideration the political climate of Ming China in late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. At the end, a constellation of incidents and institutional constraints led to the rise of the “hawks” at the expense of the “doves” in Beijing, hence the Ming government’s decision to go to war with Japan again. In my other articles and conference papers, I cover several important aspects of the War. For instance, in my 2014 journal paper, I study the Ming military personnel records and show that this otherwise impressive database had extremely little records about the Ming military officers who participated in the war. I point out that this is the result of the transformation of the Ming military organization. In my paper for the AAS-in-Kyoto Conference in June 2016, I explore the Ming fiscal operation for the War. In my paper for the AAS-in-Seoul Conference in June 2017, I argue that strategic realism led the Ming government to consider breaking up Korea into several Ming protectorates. I have also contributed to CUHK’s recent initiative on Knowledge Transfer. Using historical archives of the War, I have trained one MPhil student and offered an undergraduate course. I also attended a TV talk show introducing to the audience some of the intriguing issues of the War.

14409014.value: The P.I. have published two papers in peer-refereed academic journals, organized two special issues for peer-refereed academic journals, and delivered seven conference papers. The P.I. is ready to combine his findings and advance his research by writing an English monograph fit for academic press. The P.I. expects to finish the manuscript and solicit a book contract from an academic press in 2019.

14409014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14409014.value: In this research project, I point out that the 16th-century Korea War had created a theatre in the Ming court, outside of Korea. The Ming ministers were divided not only by their different views of the War, but the War inevitably sharpened the hostility that already existed. Shen Weijing, Shi Xing and Zhao Zhigao formed a “dove” party, only to be attacked and finally annihilated by their hawkish rivals under Shen Yiguan. The significance and value of this project is that it demonstrates the historical process through which an international wars interacted with Ming internal politics in the 16th-century.

14409514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14409514.value: Increasing physical activity (PA) in children has become a public health priority. Despite the known health benefits of PA, evidence indicates that children with physical disabilities are much less physically active than both able-bodied peers and children with other disability types. Childhood is a critical period to intervene for both prevention and remediation, and there is a pressing need for an improved understanding of the potential correlates of PA. Home and schools are the most important settings where children accrue health promoting PA, and the accurate identification and assessment of environmental and psychosocial correlates of PA that are conducive to fostering children’s PA throughout the day is critical in developing suitable PA promotion strategies. The proposed study uses a multi-method design and applies the International Classification of Functioning, Disability (ICF) model to examine the independent associations and interactions of individual (e.g., perceived competence, body functions due to the presence of a disability), social (e.g., social support from significant others), and environmental (home and school settings) variables with PA in children with physical disabilities. A representative sample of Hong Kong children with physical disabilities studying in special schools (N=252, 27.1% of total population) will participate. Specifically, we will assess children’s PA and associated environmental variables in both home and school settings during one normal school day per week for four consecutive weeks. The children will wear an accelerometer to assess their overall PA during those days and we will use a validated tool (BEACHES) to obtain observational data at home [1-hour visit yielding 180 observation intervals daily per child x 4 days] and at school (30-min before school, 30-min recess, 30-min lunch break, 60-min after school yielding 450 observation intervals daily at school per child x 4 days]. In addition to PA and associated environmental correlates, we will assess psychosocial variables using a well-established measure and a personal interview. By using both quantitative (observation and cross-sectional) and qualitative (interview) design, we will extend the literature by identifying the relative contribution and interactive effects of environmental and psychosocial facilitators and barriers to children’s leisure time PA at both home and school. Grounded on the relevant knowledge and experiences of well-established local and international researchers, the information gained will be useful to educators and policy makers for establishing health promotion priorities and for the development and implementation of effective interventions to combat sedentary-related problems for this under-researched yet disadvantaged population.

14409514.label: Realisation of objectives
14409514.value: Evidence indicates that children with physical disabilities are much less physically active than both their counterparts with typical development and those with other types of disabilities. According to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model, individual’s activity and participation with disabilities are influenced by environmental and personal factors. By using this ICF model as a theoretical framework and a multi-method design, this project was the first to examine the relative contribution and interactive effects of environmental and psychosocial factors on leisure-time physical activity (PA) in both home and school settings in a group of children with physical disabilities. A total of 149 children with physical disabilities were successfully recruited from three local special schools for children with physical disabilities. Children’s PA levels were assessed using both direct observation tool (BEACHES) and an objective measure (i.e., ActiGraph GT3X) during school time and at home on a normal school day. Specifically, in order to achieve Objective 1, children’s PA in various settings (i.e., during recess and lunch, and before and after school) at school and PA between the time (lasted for 60 minutes) they arrived at home and before dinner were assessed. To achieve Objectives 2 and 3, environmental characteristics and events in both home and school settings were assessed using BEACHES. The indicators included location (school, home, indoors, outdoors), people present (presence of parents, teachers, siblings, and peers), behavior motivated (prompts for PA and sedentary behavior), motivator (persons who motivate the child to be active or sedentary), media viewing (whether or not the child engages in media-related activity such as TV), and eating behavior (whether or not the child ingests food). Using the adapted sport participation questionnaire, personal, psychological, and social reasons for PA participation and non-participation were assessed. Additionally, barriers and facilitators relating to built and natural environment, equipment barriers, and availability of resources were further explored in face-to-face interviews. Additionally, sociodemographic data (e.g., gender, age, severity of disability) were obtained from the schools and parents/guardians. All the three objectives have been achieved by the research methods mentioned above. Overall, we found that children with physical disabilities spent most of their time being sedentary and very little time in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). As predicted, PA levels of children with physical disabilities were influenced by environmental, psychological, and sociodemographic factors.

14409514.label: Major findings and research outcome
14409514.value: This project was the first attempt to document unstructured PA in naturalistic settings and to examine the environmental and psychosocial correlates of PA by applying the ICF model in children with physical disabilities. The findings of this project advanced our understanding of PA and its influencing factors in children with physical disabilities and will aid the development of future home- and school-based interventions that promote PA and health for this group of children. In general, children with physical disabilities were not physically active across unstructured setting at school and in home. Overall, they spent approximately 90% of their time being sedentary, and spent very little time (<10%) in MVPA. We found that MVPA was associated with environmental variables and such relationships were moderated by different settings. Specifically, at recess, prompts to be active from others and presence of other child motivator were significant and positive predictors of MVPA; during after-school period, viewing media was a significant and negative predictor of MVPA; and at home, presence of father and father as the motivator were significant and positive predictors of MVPA. Meanwhile, low level of self-perceived physical competence was an important psychological barrier to PA participation of this group of children. As predicted, the PA levels of children with physical disabilities were also moderated by demographic factors. Specifically, level of mobility was significantly correlated to MVPA with children who walked without assistance engaging in more MVPA during recess, lunch, and after-school periods than those who needed assistance. Gender was also found to be significantly related to MVPA during after-school period, in which boys having higher MVPA than girls.

14409514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14409514.value: Despite the well-known health benefits by regular PA participation, children with physical disabilities in Hong Kong were inactive not only during school time but also at home. Based on the key findings of this project, it is worth considering some possible research gaps in the field. First, environmental factors play an important role in promoting children’s MVPA in both school and home settings. For example, prompts to be active from others such as peers and father were found to increase children’s MVPA at recess and home, respectively. Further research is therefore warranted to develop effective PA interventions with the presence of significant others in these settings. Second, when promoting PA participation in children with physical disabilities, there is a need to consider psychological factors such as self-perceived physical competence. Third, future research and PA interventions should also consider key demographic factors, such as gender and level of mobility, that influence PA participation.

14409514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14409514.value: Despite the known health benefits of physical activity (PA), evidence indicates that children with physical disabilities are insufficiently active for health purposes. There is a growing need for a better understanding of potentially modifiable variables that are associated PA in this population. This project was the first to examine PA of this group of children and relevant environmental and psychological factors. A total of 149 children with physical disabilities from local special schools participated in this project. Their PA levels during school time and at home were assessed using both direct observations and an objective measure. Psychological barriers and facilitators of children’s PA participation were assessed using self-report questionnaire and a face-to-face interview. Overall, children with physical disabilities were not physically active in terms of both amount and intensity. Furthermore, girls and those who walked with assistance had less PA than their counterparts. Additionally, various environmental (social supports from peers and father) and psychological (self-perceived physical competence) factors played an important role in increasing children’s PA participation. We believe the findings are of significance to develop effective home- or school-based strategies/interventions in PA promotion and therefore to enhance efforts in improving children’s health and wellbeing.

14409814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14409814.value: 民主決策的阻礙性行動：直接行動的商討理論

14409814.label: Project Objectives
14409814.value: The first objective is to refine the category of direct action by constructing a typology of activist tactics and strategies. The political theory literature employs categories such as conscientious objection, civil disobedience, and militant resistance to guide normative evaluations of political protest (Rawls 1999). These categories have been useful framing devices for many political campaigns, but the sheer diversity of contemporary activist tactics—including occupations (Parkinson 2012: 146-72), legislative disruption (Spary 2010), culture jamming (Klein 2000), ecotage (Welchman 2001), consumer boycotts (McFarland 2011), and cyber-activism (Wray 1999)—strains their applicability to contemporary realities. This project explores alternative ways in which these tactics can be categorised, focusing particularly on their use as a means of either communicating political opposition (Brownlee 2012) or levying costs on political opponents (Stears and Humphrey 2006). This project thus clarifies, develops and utilises the concept of direct action, such that a comprehensive analysis of the impacts that different kinds of activist tactics have on deliberative systems can be carried out. The second objective of this research is to contribute to ongoing research into the concept of a deliberative system. Although there has been a significant amount of research on deliberative democracy, much of this work focuses on deliberation in micro-cosmic and highly regulated forums (Steiner 2012). This research is valuable, but commentators have expressed the concern that an exclusive focus on such forums is limiting for a normative theory that aspires to re-think the practice of self-government through the cultivation of society-wide spaces of democratic deliberation (Chambers 2009; Habermas 2006; Parkinson 2006). The ‘systemic turn’ aims to show that the democratic goals of self-government and political equality can be achieved through inclusive and informed macro-level deliberation, rather than through deliberative forums that are easily manipulated or marginalised in the policy-making process (Mansbridge et al 2012: 1-4). The aim of this project is to contribute to this emerging agenda, through studying the strengths and weaknesses of direct action as a means of instigating or contributing to society-wide deliberation. The third objective is to forge a constructive relationship between the theoretical literature on deliberative democracy and the empirical literature on the study of contentious politics and social movements. The systemic turn in deliberative democracy envisages an expanded role for direct action, but there has not been sufficient empirically-informed theoretical reflection on the desirability and feasibility of this development (Mansbridge et al 2012: 17-19). A reason for this is that deliberative theory has not engaged with the relevant empirical literature, which offers extensive analysis of the internal organization of direct action movements, their capacity to impact public debates, and the response of state actors to direct action. A core aim of this project is thus to elaborate a normative account of the nature and role of direct action in democratic politics, through synthesising the theoretical literature on deliberative democracy and the empirical literature on contentious politics and social movements.
rows: The first objective is to refine the category of direct action by constructing a typology of activist tactics and strategies. The political theory literature employs categories such as conscientious objection, civil disobedience, and militant resistance to guide normative evaluations of political protest (Rawls 1999). These categories have been useful framing devices for many political campaigns, but the sheer diversity of contemporary activist tactics—including occupations (Parkinson 2012: 146-72), legislative disruption (Spary 2010), culture jamming (Klein 2000), ecotage (Welchman 2001), consumer boycotts (McFarland 2011), and cyber-activism (Wray 1999)—strains their applicability to contemporary realities. This project explores alternative ways in which these tactics can be categorised, focusing particularly on their use as a means of either communicating political opposition (Brownlee 2012) or levying costs on political opponents (Stears and Humphrey 2006). This project thus clarifies, develops and utilises the concept of direct action, such that a comprehensive analysis of the impacts that different kinds of activist tactics have on deliberative systems can be carried out.

The second objective of this research is to contribute to ongoing research into the concept of a deliberative system. Although there has been a significant amount of research on deliberative democracy, much of this work focuses on deliberation in micro-cosmic and highly regulated forums (Steiner 2012). This research is valuable, but commentators have expressed the concern that an exclusive focus on such forums is limiting for a normative theory that aspires to re-think the practice of self-government through the cultivation of society-wide spaces of democratic deliberation (Chambers 2009; Habermas 2006; Parkinson 2006). The ‘systemic turn’ aims to show that the democratic goals of self-government and political equality can be achieved through inclusive and informed macro-level deliberation, rather than through deliberative forums that are easily manipulated or marginalised in the policy-making process (Mansbridge et al 2012: 1-4). The aim of this project is to contribute to this emerging agenda, through studying the strengths and weaknesses of direct action as a means of instigating or contributing to society-wide deliberation.

The third objective is to forge a constructive relationship between the theoretical literature on deliberative democracy and the empirical literature on the study of contentious politics and social movements. The systemic turn in deliberative democracy envisages an expanded role for direct action, but there has not been sufficient empirically-informed theoretical reflection on the desirability and feasibility of this development (Mansbridge et al 2012: 17-19). A reason for this is that deliberative theory has not engaged with the relevant empirical literature, which offers extensive analysis of the internal organization of direct action movements, their capacity to impact public debates, and the response of state actors to direct action. A core aim of this project is thus to elaborate a normative account of the nature and role of direct action in democratic politics, through synthesising the theoretical literature on deliberative democracy and the empirical literature on contentious politics and social movements.

14409814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14409814.value: Direct action involves achieving political goals through disruptive acts of protest. The last decade has witnessed a proliferation of this kind of disruptive activism across democratic societies. The tactics range from the familiar, such as occupations of public space as a protest against unregulated financial markets, to the innovative, such as occupations of cyber space as a means of disrupting corporate or government institutions. The relationship between direct action and democratic politics remains a matter of considerable dispute within both democratic practice and democratic theory. There is ongoing debate about the nature of this kind of activism, its moral status, and its broader role in the ebb and flow of political life. This project aims to cast light on these debates through drawing on the deliberative turn in democratic theorizing. This move might strike some as unusual, because the type of political behaviour associated with the deliberative paradigm seems to be a long way removed from the confrontational and disruptive nature of direct action. The most recent developments within deliberative theorising, however, cast doubt on this assumption. The concept of a ‘deliberative system’ has been introduced to fix ideas about the important role that non-conventional modes of political behaviour can play in a deliberative democracy. There is, in fact, recognition that direct action can make important contributions to deliberative systems, but theorists have called for further research into the positive and negative impacts that direct action can have. The aim of this project is to answer this call for further research through exploring the relationship between the systemic turn in deliberative democracy and direct action. The project thus addresses a number of questions that, according to scholars, have yet to be resolved in the literature, including: What is direct action? In what ways can direct action enhance deliberative systems? When does direct action become counter-productive as a means of addressing deficiencies in deliberative systems? Should the tactics and/or objectives of activists count as decisive in evaluations of their actions? What ethical considerations are relevant to the response of state actors to direct action? The overarching aim of the project is thus to draw on some of the most recent developments in democratic theory to construct a framework that can orientate evaluations of direct action. 直接行動就是要透過顛覆性的行為，來達至某種政治目標。在過去的十年，我們看到民主社會中阻礙性行動如雨後春筍般出現。這些行動的策略形形式式，當中包括：佔領公共空間來抗議去規管化的金融市場，或者更具創意的，會以佔領網絡空間來窒礙企業和政府的運作。在當下民主實踐以及民主理論的討論上，直接行動跟民主政治的關係仍然是極具爭議的題目。有關阻礙性行動的性質、道德理據，以至它在政治生活的功用，在學術界依然未有定案。 這項研究計劃的目標，則是嘗試從商討民主的角度去理解阻礙性行動。不少人可能會認為，商討民主與阻礙性行動是風馬牛不相及。因為他們都假定了與商討理論相關的政治行為，跟具有對抗性和顛覆性的直接行動存在一定的距離。然而，當今的商討民主理論正是質疑這種假設。迄今，學界正開始利用商討的概念來分析與傳統模式有別的政治行為，理解這些行為對協商民主的影響。事實上，直接行動對我們理解商討民主有著重要的意義，而不少學者已在研究協商民主對直接行動的正面及負面效果。 本研究的目的，正是進一步探究商討民主及直接行動的關係。因而，本研究會回答以下一些學界尚未圓滿梳解的問題：什麼是直接行動？直接行動如何促進商討民主？在什麼情況下，直接行動會對商討民主產生負面影響？究竟行動者的策略對評估他們的行動是否具決定性？ 國家的決策者在應對直接行動時，又有什麼道德考慮？本研究的總體目標，正是透過最新穎的民主理論來建構了一個框架，用以評價直接行動。

14409814.label: Realisation of objectives
14409814.value: The project objectives, as listed above in part 5.1, have been fully achieved. This success was facilitated primarily by the twelve-month period of relief teaching during the first year of the project, which enabled the PI to engage in reflection, reading and writing, dissemination of findings at international conferences, and visits to international research centers. The foundation established during this period enabled the PI to continue research activities alongside the resumption of teaching and administrative duties in the second and final year of the project. The first objective was to refine the category of direct action by constructing a typology of activist tactics and strategies. This objective has been achieved through elaborating a core distinction between deliberative and non-deliberative disruption. This distinction has been drawn through reference to a conception of deliberative action, defined as a mode of conduct that is epistemic-reflective, respectful of others, and dialogic in intent. The concept of deliberative disruption thus refers to communicative forms of protest that are carried out to engage an audience in a manner that is reflective, respectful and dialogic. The concept of non-deliberative disruption refers to non-communicative forms of protest that are not carried out to engage an audience, but to achieve goals through methods such as the imposition of costs or manipulative rhetoric. This distinction can be employed as a means of mapping established and emergent modes of disruptive protest, according to the extent to which such acts embody or fail to embody the features of deliberative action. The research carried out during this project therefore included efforts to frame certain forms of protest as deliberative disruptions, other instances as non-deliberative disruptions, and further instances as partially-deliberative disruptions (i.e. ‘mixed’ cases). The latter category has facilitated the analysis of innovative forms of protest that often appear to embody both deliberative and non-deliberative elements, such as instances of ‘online’ or ‘digital’ disruption (e.g. distributed denial of server actions). The deliberative framework can also be sensitive to an important issue which is often overlooked in the normative literature on disruptive protest, which is that contrasting attitudes can be adopted by protesters toward the various agents that are impacted by their action. So, for instance, a protest might be framed as an attempt to engage in a rational and respectful dialogue with a certain addressee and/or public, while simultaneously imposing non-discursive pressure upon other addressees and/or publics that are not regarded as legitimate discursive interlocutors. This can have significant implications for the normative evaluation of protest, insofar as it corrects a notable tendency in the literature to focus primarily or solely upon those dimensions of activist conduct that are hardest to reconcile with deliberative democratic norms. This leads into the realization of the second objective, which was to contribute to ongoing research into the concept of a deliberative system. This objective was pursued through critical analysis of the emergent literature on deliberative systems, which led to a minor modification of the research plan. The PI had originally envisaged operationalizing the concept of a deliberative system as it is broadly defined in the literature, through using it to study the relationship between disruptive protest and deliberative democracy. This objective was modified due to conceptual ambiguities and normative shortcomings that the PI discovered upon closer analysis of the literature, which has also been a theme of other critical commentaries on the systemic turn during the period of the project (see, e.g., David Owen and Graham Smith, ‘Survey Article: Deliberation, Democracy, and the Systemic Turn’, The Journal of Political Philosophy, 23:2 (2015), pp. 213-234). A problem that became particularly apparent during the project was that the boundaries of a deliberative system are often drawn with insufficient clarity, such that it is difficult to determine what is internal and external to the system. The PI therefore suggested a refinement to the framework, which draws upon the aforementioned idea of deliberative action to sharpen the conceptual edges of the system. The reformulated conception of a deliberative system, along with the typology of activist tactics described above, has been utilized to show that certain forms of disruptive protest (e.g. deliberative disruptions) should be seen as constitutive features of a deliberative system, while other forms of protest (e.g. non-deliberative disruptions) are best treated as external elements that can have positive or negative impacts upon systemic functionality. This not only has the analytical advantage of fixing ideas about the boundaries of a deliberative system, but also opens up a hitherto neglected means of gauging the normative value of disruptive protest. It does this through foregrounding the intrinsic value that certain forms of protest can embody as instances of deliberative action, as well the more familiar theme of the instrumental value that such actions can yield for deliberative systems. The research has also touched on other issues relevant to the ongoing elaboration of the deliberative systems paradigm, particularly the issue of transnational and global deliberation. This is reflected in work that has explored the transnational dimensions of certain instances of disruptive protest, as well as general reflections on the potential that the ‘systemic turn’ holds for ongoing analysis of deliberation at global and transnational levels. The third objective of the project was to forge a constructive relationship between the theoretical literature on deliberative democracy and the empirical literature on the study of contentious politics and social movements. This has been a crucial goal that has informed almost all the research that has been carried out, both enabling the current project objectives to be met and opening up avenues for a further project (see below 6.2). The empirical literature on contentious politics and social movements has provided crucial resources for addressing the previous two objectives. First, the typology of deliberative, partially-deliberative, and non-deliberative disruptions has been informed and illustrated by real world cases as described in the empirical literature. Second—and perhaps even more importantly—the empirical studies have enabled the PI to better explore the strengths and weaknesses of direct action as a means of stimulating society-wide deliberation. Of particular value have been a number of studies that draw connections between the manner and conduct of protest and the nature and extent of the media coverage that it receives. This has allowed the PI to compare and contrast the respective merits of deliberative and non-deliberative disruption as a means of realizing the functionality of a deliberative system. The empirical literature has also been vital in considering the relationship between protesters and state actors. Of particular note is the extensive empirical literature on protest policing, which has documented a pervasive trend away from negotiated approached to the use of preventative and militarized force by police across a number of territorial jurisdictions. The theoretical literature on deliberative democracy, along with the literature on civil disobedience, often neglects the important issue of policing, in favor of focusing upon legislative or judicial arenas relevant to the reception of protest movements. This project has corrected this oversight, by drawing on the empirical literature on contentious politics and social movements to show how more tolerant policing strategies can play a crucial role in increasing the prospects for protest movements to make a positive impact upon the democratic deliberation of relevant publics.
