15101914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15101914.value: Tuberculosis is caused by an infectious bacterium, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which has a single, highly active, chromosomally encoded class A beta-lactamase, BlaC. Inactivation of BlaC resensitizes the organism to existing beta-lactam antibiotics, especially meropenem. As clavulanate is the only FDA-approved effective BlaC beta-lactamase inhibitor, extensive efforts should be directed to the development of new inhibitors against BlaC. High-throughput screening accelerates the discovery of potential drug candidates from chemical libraries. However, it is susceptible to false-positive hits. Many compounds have a high propensity to form aggregates under aqueous conditions, which inhibit beta-lactamase activity through a non-specific mechanism. It is highly desirable to develop a reliable high-throughput screening tool that can identify active-site-binding drug candidates. Using the “active-site-labeling” approach, we successfully developed a novel fluorescent molecular drug target (P99_V211Cf) from the class C Enterobacter cloacae P99 AmpC beta-lactamase for in vitro drug screening. The P99 enzyme is labeled with a fluorophore in the close proximity to its active site so as to enable it to fluorescently respond to the drug binding event at the active site. The fluorescent P99 beta-lactamase catalytic activity is maintained so that it can act as a “natural” molecular drug target. Using a similar approach in the present project, we will develop a new fluorescent molecular drug target from BlaC for in vitro drug screening. By rational design, Thr216 of the engineered cysteine-free BlaC enzyme will be replaced by a unique cysteine, which will be labeled with an environment-sensitive fluorophore, fluorescein (f) or badan (b), to generate BlaC_T216Cf or BlaC_T216Cb. Residue located at the position 216 in class A beta-lactamases is found to be ideal for labelling with fluorophore. It is not essential for function and can serve as a “generic” site for fluorophore labeling in the development of fluorescent drug targets with other clinically relevant class A beta-lactamases. In this project, we will solve the crystal structure of fluorescent BlaC and elucidate its mechanism of fluorescence enhancement. We will label BlaC_T216C with different fluorophores and test their properties. We will engineer BlaC (a class A extended-spectrum beta-lactamase) as a new fluorescent screening tool for inhibitors and compare its properties to the class C P99_V211Cf. This innovative “active-site-labelling” strategy will open a possibility for developing tailor-made BlaC-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against this M. tuberculosis beta-lactamase that mediates beta-lactam antibiotic resistance. 結核病是一種傳染性細菌(結核桿菌)引起的 ，其中有一個單一的，高活性，染色體編碼的類A的β-內酰胺酶(BlaC)。BlaC的滅活再次使到結核桿菌對現有的β-內酰胺類抗生素有敏感性，尤其是美羅培南抗生素。由於克拉維酸是唯一FDA批准的有效的BlaCβ-內酰胺酶抑製劑，廣泛的努力方向應針對 BlaC新抑製劑的開發。 高通量篩選加速潛力的候選藥物化學庫的發現。然而，很容易出現假陽性的命中。許多化合物具有高的傾向，以形成含水條件下的聚集體，聚集體通過非特異性機制抑制β-內酰胺酶的活性。人們非常希望開發一種可靠的高通量篩選的工具去識別活性位點結合的候選藥物。使用“主動活性位點標籤”的做法，我們成功地從C類陰溝腸桿菌P99 AmpC β-內酰胺酶開發出一種新的熒光分子藥物靶標（P99_V211Cf）的體外藥物篩選。在P99酶中的標記在靠近其活性位點的熒光團，以使其能夠在活性部位反應的藥物結合事件中發熒光。熒光P99β-內酰胺酶的催化活性得到保持，以便它可以作為一個“自然”分子藥物靶點。 使用類似的方法在本項目中，我們將從BlaC開發出一個新的熒光分子藥物靶標進行體外藥物篩選。通過合理設計，工程化的無半胱氨酸的BlaC酶的Thr216將被一個獨特的半胱氨酸更換，這將被貼上一個環境敏感的熒光團”熒光素（f）或巴丹（b）”，以產生BlaC_T216Cf或BlaC_T216Cb。位於類A的β-內酰胺酶的216位置的氨基酸殘基被發現是非常適合與熒光標記。它不是功能必需並且可以作為一個“通用”的熒光團標記位置，適用於其他臨床上相關的類A的β-內酰胺酶作 為熒光分子藥物靶標的開發。在這個項目中，我們會解決熒光BlaC的晶體結構，並闡明熒光增強的機制。我們將用不同的熒光標籤BlaC_T216C，並測試其性能。我們將設計BlaC（A類廣譜的β-內酰胺酶）作為一種新的抑製劑熒光篩選工具並且與C類P99_V211Cf比較其性能。這種創新的“主動活性位點標籤”的戰略將打開量身定制的BlaC型的抑製劑熒光篩查工具開發的可能性，去抵抗這種結核桿菌的β-內酰胺酶介導的β-內酰胺類抗生素耐藥的問題。

15101914.label: Realisation of objectives
15101914.value: [Objective 1] Thr-216 in BlaC was replaced by Cys by site-directed mutagenesis to generate T216C. Various fluorophores (e.g. fluorescein and badan) were labelled on the mutated residue and the prospective fluorescent sensor enzyme was screened. The badan-labeled BlaC (T216Cb) did not give significant signal change upon binding with substrate or inhibitor, and was not used for further studies. The functionality of the most promising fluorescein-labelled enzyme T216Cf against antibiotics and inhibitors was investigated with fluorescence spectrometry. An immediate surge in fluorescence intensity of T216Cf upon penicillins addition and positive signals induced by carbapenems and inhibitors were observed. However, response to cephalosporins was insignificant. The relationship between enzyme-inhibitor complex formation and fluorescence intensity change was also revealed by the combination of electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) and fluorescence spectrometry. The kinetic parameters were measured and calculated to examine the impact of mutagenesis and labelling. Furthermore, a second mutation to Trp was introduced at Ile-105 in an attempt to enhance the biosensor sensitivity. Surprisingly, T216Cf/I105W showed a major improvement in sensitivity, as much as from +35% to +83% upon inhibitor addition. Moreover, the purity and quality of T216C and T216Cf prepared were confirmed by ESI-MS. Adding ampicillin and penicillin G to T216Cf induced an immediate increase of 18% and 15% in the fluorescence intensity. Reducing the background fluorescence intensity can be a mean to increase the sensitivity of T216Cf. Fluorescein fluorescence is effectively quenched by tryptophan located in close proximity to the probe. A model was built based on the BlaC crystal structure to locate the neighbouring residues of the flurophore which were then mutated to tryptophan. The change in fluorescence intensity of T216Cf/I105W was compared with T216Cf when two penicillins (ampicillin and penicillin G) and two carbapenems (meropenem and imipenem) were added. With all four antibiotics, T216Cf/I105W gave a significantly higher signal change than T216Cf. Kinetic data by others showed that I105W has little impact on the turnover rate kcat. For meropenem, the similar slopes in T216Cf and T216Cf/T237W spectra denote a similar inhibitor binding rate. The maximum fluorescence intensity changes for T216Cf/I105W is generally higher than T216Cf. The quenching by tryptophan is largely affected by the relative position of the fluorescein attached on the protein and the tryptophan side chain. Time-dependent fluorescence spectra of T216Cf/I105W against different concentrations of clavulanate were measured. The mutation of I105W on T216Cf biosensor has clearly benefited from the increase in sensitivity. [Objective 2] To monitor the development of the fluorescence signal over time, time-dependent fluorescence spectra of T216Cf against various substrates (ampicillin, penicillin G, meropenem, and cephalothin) and inhibitors (clavulanate, tazobactam, sulbactam) were recorded. We found that penicillins caused an instant rise of nearly 20% in the fluorescence intensity, but the signal quickly declined to baseline as the substrates were hydrolysed and less bound to the labelled enzyme. Interestingly, a strong but slow positive signal was given by the binding of meropenem (a carbapenem), which is a very poor substrate to BlaC beta-lactamase. Due to this low capability in meropenem hydrolysis, the substrate durably binds to the enzyme and results in a steady signal. Similar profiles were seen in the time-dependent emission spectra of T216Cf against inhibitors. The fluorescence signal increased steadily and reached a plateau within an hour. Clavulanate induced the largest rise of 35% and maximum was reached after 16 min. Addition of sulbactam caused the an 18% increase in fluorescence intensity after 8 min. For tazobactam, the maximum intensity of 28% increase was attained after 60 min. Importantly, fluorescence intensity increased once the clavulanate was added. At any inhibitor concentration, no decline in the intensity was seen, suggesting that the enzyme is incapable to hydrolyse clavulanate. Furthermore, mass spectrometry results suggested that clavulanate covalently bound to T216Cf and the amount of T216Cf-clavulanate complex accumulated over time. We found that the time-dependent fluorescence spectrum exhibited a highly similar change in fluorescence intensity. The strong correlation between the two measurements suggested that the fluorescence signal is indeed prompted by the binding to the biosensor. For inhibitor screening tests and to track the fast fluorescence changes as well as study the effect of multiple injections, an automatic injector equipped on a 96-well microplate reader was used to obtain time-dependent fluorescence spectra. We found that each of the three inhibitors (sulbactam, tazobactam, and clavulanate) caused a significant increase in fluorescence intensity. Therefore, the innovative “active-site labelling” strategy has opened a possibility for developing tailor-made BlaC-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against M. tuberculosis beta-lactamase that mediates beta-lactam antibiotic resistance. [Objective 3] Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to understand the mechanism behind the fuorescence signals, which is transferable to similar beta-lactamase-based biosensor. The change in residues in proximity to the fluorescein, solvent exposure, and interaction with quenchers such as tryptophan all contribute to the fluorescence signals. The promising results suggested that the new T216Cf has great potential to be refined as a powerful biosensor for drug screening. We found that the BlaC beta-lactamase-based fluorescent biosensors T216Cf and T216Cf/I105W have shown their capability as "turn-on" biosensors for inhibitor screening. Importantly, MD simulation provides insight into the conceivable hypothesis by calculating the trajectories of protein and solvent in a given system for us to further understand the experimental results. The structures of T216Cf/I105W, with and without clavulanate as inhibitor, were also modelled based on the equilibrium average coordinates from the MD simulations of the T216Cf structures. The stability and change in local environment of the fluorescein probe in the 30 ns simulations were analysed using tools of GROMACS 5.0 and VMD. We found that while the fluorescein for two of the proposed models, CRF-m and CSF-m, equilibrate at the same position unaffected by clavulanate binding, the equilibrium position of the fluorophore in CRF-t enzyme-inhibitor complex model is distinct from that of the inhibitor-free protein. Furthermore, the charged residues in the vicinity of the fluorescein were analyzed. We found that with clavulanate bound, the fluorescein is surrounded by substantially more charged residues, and in a closer shell, than that without inhibitor bound. Importantly, fluorescein absorption at 494 nm corresponds to the dianion, whose accumulation is promoted by the surrounding charged residues. Thus the absorption and hence fluorescence intensity increases. More importantly, crystal structure of the biosensor would be the ultimate verification to the MD simulations. The crystallisation condition for the purified T216Cf at high concentration was screened with the aid of screening kits. Crystallisation of T216Cf was performed by sitting-drop vapour diffusion method with three screening kits, Crystal Screen, Crystal Screen 2, and Index, providing total of 192 conditions. In the 192 initial screen conditions tested, T216Cf formed crystals under the condition of Crystal Screen #25 (0.1 M imidazole pH 6.5, 1.0 M Sodium acetate trihydrate) in both subwells with protein to buffer ratio of 1:1 and 1:2 (v/v). Birefringence of the crystals was observed under polarised light, the crystals also appeared fluorescent under UV light, confirming the presence of T216Cf in crystal. However, the crystals formed were too small for data analysis. The condition, therefore, has to be optimised by altering the concentration of the buffer and the pH in future studies.

15101914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15101914.value: Using a fluorescein-labeled AmpC beta-lactamase as an example, we first demonstrated that rapid characterization of beta-lactamase inhibitors can be achieved by real-time fluorescence monitoring of interactions between a beta-lactamase and its inhibitors (see Part C, Biotechnol. J. 2016, 11, 257-265). Then we make use of this powerful “active-site-labeling” approach as well as structure-based rational design to develop a new fluorescent molecular drug target from the clinically important Mycobacterium tuberculosis BlaC beta-lactamase for in vitro drug screening. The BlaC enzyme is labeled with a fluorophore in the close proximity to its active site so as to enable it to fluorescently respond to the drug binding event at the active site. The fluorescent BlaC beta-lactamase catalytic activity is maintained so that it can act as a “natural” molecular drug target. The fluoroscein-labelled BlaC beta-lactamase mutant T216Cf has clearly shown its advantages as a sensitive and selective biosensor in beta-lactamase inhibitor screening. The T216C mutant (with a second C285S mutation) was successfully produced and purified. High sensitivity and applicability of fluorescein-5-maleimide (f) was regarded as the most suitable label of the four different fluorophores tested. Similar to the native enzyme, the active site of T216Cf could be recovered after hydrolysis of the antibiotic substrate. Juxtaposing the formation of enzyme-inhibitor complex and the change in fluorescence intensity confirmed the relationship between inhibitor binding and fluorescence signal (see Part C, manuscript). Fluorescence spectra recorded with microplate reader exhibited the ability of T216Cf to be used in large-scale automated drug screening. However, the fluorescence intensity change for T216Cf has not exceeded 35%. To enhance the sensitivity of this biosensor, a second mutation near the active site was introduced to further improve its performance. The sensitivity of the biosensor (T216Cf) was further improved by the mutation of Ile-105 to tryptophan (to generate T216Cf/I105W). The design was based on the hypothesis that side chain indole of tryptophan, spatially close to the fluorescein, forms  interactions with the heterocyclic ring of fluorescein, and quenches the fluorescence when no substrate or inhibitor binds to the active site. When the inhibitor (e.g. clavulanate) binds to the enzyme, the local environment is changed and the quenching effect is reduced significantly (see Part C, conference abstract). Taken together, combination of beta-lactam antibiotics and beta-lactamase inhibitors has been proven effective against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. T216Cf has exhibited great potential to be refined as a quick biosensor with high specificity and sensitivity for inhibitor screening.

15101914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101914.value: Fluorescence changes of T216Cf/I105W doubled that of T216Cf under the same conditions. Time-dependent fluorescence spectra of T216Cf/I105W against different concentrations of various inhibitors will be measured to further examine the impact of the mutation on Ile-105. The mutation of I105W on T216Cf has clearly benefited from the enhanced sensitivity. However, the efficiency will need to be improved. Mutation of residue in vicinity of Ile-105 to Trp will be considered as possible optimisation of this beta-lactamase-based biosensor. Moreover, we are preparing a manuscript with the title “Rational design of a biosensor with enhanced sensitivity for beta-lactamase inhibitors by reducing the background fluorescence at the enzyme active site, Zoe Chan, Yu-Wai Chen, Man-Wah Tsang, Shik-Chi Edman Tsang, Kwok-Yin Wong*, Yun-Chung Leung*”. It will be submitted to the journal “Bioconjugate Chemistry” and published in 2019. More importantly, crystal structure of the biosensor would be the ultimate verification to the MD simulations. The crystallisation conditions for the purified T216Cf and T216Cf/I105W at high concentration will be optimized and good crystals obtained will be used for solving the structures. On the other hand, high-throughput screening using T216Cf/I105W or T216Cf will be performed to accelerate the discovery of potential drug candidates from chemical libraries.

15101914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101914.value: Tuberculosis is one of the top ten causes of death. Despite being preventable and curable owing to the discovery of antibiotics, the bacteria have become more resistant or extensively resistant to the existing drugs. New treatment against tuberculosis is urgently needed. While new drugs often take decades from research to being commercially available, revisiting the possibilities of approved drugs in treating tuberculosis may provide a much quicker path. BlaC, a beta-lactamase responsible for the beta-lactam antibiotic resistance, was successfully engineered to be a sensitive and efficient biosensor for screening potential inhibitors to use in combination with currently available beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g. meropenem). Thr-216, a residue close to the active site, was replaced by Cys and named as T216C BlaC. Subsequently, a fluorescent sensor enzyme T216Cf was prepared by attaching a fluorophore (f) on the mutated residue (Cys-216). Fluorescence measurements were conducted on the labelled protein T216Cf and compared with data obtained from mass spectrometry. Enhancement in the signal was also successfully achieved by quenching the background fluorescence through mutating Ile-105, a residue near to the fluorescein, to Trp (I105W/T216Cf). The promising results suggested that the new T216Cf has enormous potential to be refined as a powerful biosensor for drug discovery.

15102314.label: Project Objectives
15102314.value: The main objective of the proposed study is to evaluate several hypotheses regarding the control of trunk muscles and recovery of postural stability accompanying internal postural perturbations in people with and without CLBP. It is hypothesized that accompanying internal postural perturbation (self-generated by voluntary arm movement), individuals with CLBP will demonstrate 1) a delayed activation of the deep trunk muscles; 2) co-contraction of the superficial trunk muscles; and 3) altered muscle control pattern associated with balance deficits accompanying postural perturbation.

15102314.label: Realisation of objectives
15102314.value: The objectives were achieved via studying of the trunk muscle activation pattern and postural control using EMG and force platform respectively, during rapid bilateral voluntary arm flexion in respond to an auditory trigger in standing position. There were a total of 40 participants in the study. Preliminary findings were presented in the International Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine 2017 conference at Bueno Aires Argentina. A manuscript was submitted to the journal "Spine" for review. All list objectives were completely achieved, in addition to a new objective. The results suggested that accompanying trivial and predictable postural perturbation, people with chronic low back pain people have altered muscle control, which is associated impaired ability to recover postural stability. The followings are the result listed according to each objective of the study: Objective 1: Individuals with CLBP will demonstrate a delayed activation of the deep trunk muscles When compared with their age- and gender-matched pain-free controls, LBP participants have delayed activation or less frequent anticipatory activation of the deep core (Transervsus Abdominis) muscles; Proportional of trials with anticipatory activation: 18% in LBP vs 82.7% in Control, P < 0.0001, Activation timing: 83.2 (66.6) ms in LBP vs 24.9 (36.5) ms in control, P = 0.026. Objective 2: Individuals with CLBP will demonstrate co-contraction of the superficial trunk muscles When compared with their age- and gender-matched pain-free controls, LBP participants a) have earlier onset of trunk flexor (Rectus Abdominis): Proportional of trials with anticipatory activation: 100% in LBP vs 0% in Control, P < 0.0001, Activation timing: (-63.7) (30.6) ms in LBP vs 134.2 (8.2) ms in Control, P = 0.0001; b) has earlier onset of trunk flexor-extensor co-contraction [-34.9 (20.3) ms in LBP vs 91.7 (42.1) in Control, P = 0.0001], and longer duration of co-contraction [1467 (508.1) ms in LBP vs 572.5 (705) ms in Control, P = 0.0012]; Objective 3: Individuals with CLBP will demonstrate altered muscle control pattern associated with balance deficits accompanying postural perturbation When compared with their age- and gender-matched pain-free controls, LBP participants a) were more frequently activate one of the trunk extensors (Superficial Lumbar Multifidus) later, Proportional of trials with delayed activation: 22.0% in LBP vs 0% in Control, P < 0.0001; b) took a longer time to regain postural stability (911.2 (265.3) ms in LBP vs 757.1 (172.1) ms in Control, P = 0.03) and required a greater number of postural adjustments (9.5 (2.7) in LBP vs 5.9 (1.7) in Control, P = 0.0001) during recovery; Besides, there was a significant moderately positive correlation between trunk muscle co-contraction time and postural recovery time (r = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.33 – 0.84, P = 0.0006) with data combined from both groups. The result suggested that a longer duration of trunk flexor-extensor co-contraction is associated with a longer postural recovery time. In addition, there was a strong negative correlation between trunk muscle co-contraction onset timing and postural recovery time (r = -0.76, 95% CI = (-0.89) – (-0.51), P <0.0001) with data combined from both groups. Therefore the earliest onset of trunk flexor-extensor co-contraction is associated with a longer postural recovery time. Additional finding: When compared with their age- and gender-matched pain-free controls, LBP participants have delayed reaction time for activation of the Anterior Deltoid muscle (LBP - 282.0 (75.2) ms vs Control - 213.4 (60.3) ms, P = 0.028) and shoulder flexion movement (LBP - 297.4 (74.5) ms vs Control - 223.5 (54.0) ms, P = 0.004). This is an additional finding from the study hypothesis. There is no under-achievements of the project and therefore did not require any attempt to overcome any problems.

15102314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102314.value: The result of this research further proved the balance impairment in people with chronic low back pain, which is a functional impairment largely neglected in the evaluation and treatment in people with this condition. Further research should be developed to investigate if the balance impairment could be improved with specific muscle control training or balance training.

15102314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102314.value: Standing balance is a fundamental function of daily lives. Balance impairment and altered control of the trunk muscles in people with chronic low back pain has been reported in previous studies and yet the association between these two factors is still unclear. Our present study revealed that people with LBP adopted a trunk stiffening strategy which is also associated with poor recovery of balance even after a trivial and predictable balance perturbation. The result provide insight into the development of specific treatment protocol to improve balance dysfunction in people with chronic low back pain.

15102514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15102514.value: It has been demonstrated in various populations that the integrity of bone tissue is highly correlated with muscle mass/strength. In fact, according to the muscle-bone unit theory, muscle and bone can be considered as a functional unit. The concept of muscle-bone unit is highly relevant to people after stroke, as muscle weakness/ atrophy and bone loss are some of the key physical impairments, which may in turn lead to serious health consequences such as fall-related fractures. However, the influence of different muscle contraction characteristics (e.g., contraction type, speed) on the muscle-bone relationship is not clear. Moreover, spasticity is also a common impairment in muscle function after stroke but its effect on bone properties is very much understudied. Understanding these muscle-bone relationships is important before effective therapeutic interventions/physical activity guidelines can be formulated to enhance the health of the muscle-bone unit after stroke. Part 1 of the study will address this key issue by investigating the influence of different muscle contraction types and speeds on the strength of the muscle-bone link, as well as the impact of spasticity on the bone properties in chronic stroke patients. The intimate relationship between muscle function and bone tissue also suggests the potential of modifying bone turnover by improving muscle function in stroke patients. Whole-body vibration (WBV), a technique that provides mechanical loading to the bone tissue as well as augmenting muscle activation, is hypothesized to achieve this. Animal research has shown that higher vibration frequencies are associated with higher rate of bone formation. It is also known from human studies that the level of muscle activation is enhanced as the stimulation frequency is increased during WBV application. However, it is unknown whether higher frequencies will lead to better bone and muscle outcomes after longer-term WBV exposure. Part 2 of the study will address this key issue by comparing different vibration frequencies in their effects in modifying muscle and bone outcomes in people with chronic stroke. Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability in Hong Kong and other regions of the world. This project will be the first worldwide to systematically examine the muscle-bone relationship and how it is impacted by different vibration frequencies among chronic stroke patients. It will advance the scientific evidence base related to the muscle-bone unit post-stroke, and has potential clinical value to benefit the stroke population by informing stroke rehabilitation practice in an evidence-based manner. 研究顯示，肌肉力量都與骨組織的完整性高度相關。事實上，根據肌肉-骨骼單元理論，肌肉和骨骼被認為是一個功能單元。肌肉-骨骼單元理念與中風人士關係密切。因為肌無力、肌萎縮及骨質疏鬆是中風後常見的肢體障礙，而他們轉而又會給健康帶來不利影響，例如跌倒導致的骨折。然而，不同肌肉的收縮特點（例如：收縮類型，速度）對肌肉-骨骼之間關係的影響並不明確。而且，痙攣作為中風後常見的肌肉功能損害症狀，針對它對於中風後骨骼的影響的研究卻很少。了解這些肌肉-骨骼相關性在有效的治療干預很重要，中風後活動指南便可以照此來加強肌肉-骨骼單元。研究的第一部分將會研究不同肌肉收縮類型和速度對肌肉-骨骼連接處的影響，以及中風後痙攣對骨骼性能的影響。 肌肉功能和骨組織之間的密切關係也預示著通過提高肌肉功能來加強骨骼的可能性。全身震動療法作為一種能在給骨組織提供機械負重的同時還能增加肌肉活性的技術。動物實驗顯示振動頻率與骨生成率呈正相關。也有研究顯示，在全身振動治療技術中也顯示隨著振動頻率的增加，人的肌肉活化水平也增加。但是在長期的全身振動治療下，更高的振動頻率是否會使骨骼與肌肉更強仍是未知的。研究的第二部分將通過對中風人士進行不同振動頻率的干預所帶來的不同肌肉和骨骼參數進行比較，從而對這個重要問題進行闡述。 中風是香港乃至全世界導致殘疾的主導原因。通過系統地研究肌肉-骨骼相關性及在中風人士中使用不同振動頻率如何影響此相關性，這個研究項目將是世界首創。它不僅將會推進卒中后肌肉-骨骼單元理念的循證科學發展，而且給中風後的康復實踐提供詢證訓練方式，存在潛在的臨床價值。

15102514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15102514.value: Objective 1 and 2: We found that all pQCT-derived bone parameters demonstrated significant side-to-side differences between the paretic and non-paretic side (p<0.05). We found that knee isometric extension strength was significantly associated with bone strength index measured at the distal tibial epiphysis and tibial diaphysis. Leg muscle spasticity on the other hand, was not significantly related to bone strength indices measured at the tibia. A separate analysis involving female chronic stroke survivors showed that the cortical bone area (p=0.001), cortical bone mineral content (p=0.003), bone strength index (p=0.001) of the tibial diaphysis showed significant percentage side-to-side difference, whereas the cortical bone mineral density (p=0.063) and total bone area (p=0.866) demonstrated no significant percent side-to-side difference. Knee extension and flexion strength values on the hemi-paretic side were also significantly lower than the non-paretic side, regardless of the contraction speeds and types. The side-to-side difference in concentric knee extension strength at 60°/s (R2=0.507, F=7.886, P=0.001) and isometric knee extension strength (R2=0.422, F=5.591, P=0.005) remained independently associated with tibial BSI, after controlling for age, height, time since onset of stroke, and post-menopausal duration. Objective 3: Participants with chronic stroke performed three different exercises on the whole-body vibration (WBV) platform with different vibration conditions (frequency: 20 Hz, 30 Hz, 40 Hz; amplitude: 0.8 mm, 1.5 mm), or without vibration. Muscle activity in bilateral vastus medialis (VM), medial hamstrings (MH), tibialis anterior (TA), and medial gastrocnemius (MG) was measured by surface electromyography. Acceleration at the platform and bilateral hips and knees was measured by tri‐axial accelerometers. Significantly greater muscle activity was observed in the bilateral MG (p< 0.001), TA (p < 0.001), and MH (p < 0.001), but not VM, compared with the same exercises without WBV. WBV with higher amplitude or higher frequency led to greater augmentation of muscle activation (p < 0.05). Body posture significantly affected leg muscle activation (p< 0.001). WBV‐induced muscle activation was largely similar between paretic and non‐paretic sides, except the TA. Greater WBV induced leg muscle activation was associated with lower WBV transmissibility measured at the more proximal joints (p < 0.05). In summary, higher WBV frequency or amplitude induces substantially higher levels of leg muscle activation, which in turn leads to lower transmissibility to the upper body. Considering these factors, a squatting position with WBV at 30‐40 Hz with a high amplitude (eg, 1.5 mm) is an appropriate choice if the treatment goal is to enhance leg muscle activation. An 8 week WBV intervention protocol using the two different WBV frequencies resulted in no significant between-group difference in the serum level of carboxy-terminal collagen crosslinks (CTx; a bone resorption marker) in individuals with stroke.

15102514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102514.value: The findings in this study should form the basis of further study in the area of bone and muscle health in stroke survivors. First, the tibial distal epiphysis still suffered significant bone loss among those who had sustained a stroke 12– 24 months ago, resulting in reduced bone strength index. Such changes were significantly associated with knee extension muscle strength measured at the initial assessment. Also, the results showed that isometric and concentric strength at moderate contraction speed are particularly correlated with bone health. Further research should explore the development of intervention protocols to modify these factors in the endeavor to prevent bone loss in this patient population. Second, only people with chronic stroke with mild to moderate motor impairment were included in the research. Stroke survivors with other levels of motor impairment should be included in future studies.

15102514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102514.value: The research project aimed to identify the key muscle function that impacts bone health the most among individuals with chronic stroke. The results showed that knee muscle strength, but not muscle spasticity, was the most important factor in influencing lower limb bone density after stroke. Therefore, the results clearly show the strong muscle-bone link in stroke patients. An important clinical implication is that enhancement of leg muscle strength through strength training, which is not a customary practice in stroke rehabilitation, may be a key strategy to improve bone health in stroke survivors. In addition, it was found that whole-body vibration with higher frequencies is more effective in increasing leg muscle activation on both the affected and unaffected sides post-stroke. Thus, whole-body vibration with higher frequencies (>30Hz) may have potential in improving muscle performance and bone health after stroke.

15103614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103614.value: With the increase in aging population, postmenopausal osteoporosis becomes one of the major public health problems that poses significant medical and socioeconomic burden to the society. It is a metabolic bone disease characterized by low bone mass and deterioration of microarchitecture that resulting in an increase in bone fragility. Recent study showed that hormone replacement therapy (HRT) significantly reduced the risk of bone fractures in postmenopausal women but increased the risk to develop breast, endometrial and ovarian cancers and sides effects were reported with the use of the selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) amongst postmenopausal women. Recent reports indicated that phytoestrogens (plant-derived compounds that have estrogenic properties) can attenuate bone loss associated with estrogen deficiency in both animal and human studies. However, as the in vivo effects of phytoestrogens are similar to estrogens and their actions are mediated through estrogen receptors (ERalpha and ERbeta), there are increasing concerns for the safety of using phytoestrogens. Our laboratory and others demonstrated that Herba Epimedii (HEP, a commonly prescribed Chinese medicine for bone diseases) and icariin (the major bioactive ingredient in HEP) could protect against estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss in ovariectomized animals without inducing uterotrophic growth. Our follow-up in vitro studies demonstrated that icariin could stimulate osteoblastic functions in rat osteoblast-like UMR 106 cells in an estrogen receptor (ER) dependent manner. However, icariin appears to be a unique phytoestrogen that induce ERalpha phosphorylation at serine 118 but did not stimulate ER mediated estrogen response element (ERE)-dependent luciferase activities in bone cells. Recent study indicated that icaritin, a metabolite of icariin, has more potent effects than icariin in bone cells. We hypothesize that icariin and icaritin could exert tissue-selective estrogenic responses in vivo and their osteoprotective actions are at least in part mediated by the activation of rapid estrogen signaling pathways in bone cells. In this revised proposal, we have designed studies to systematically characterize the in vivo selective estrogenic effects of icariin using ovariectomized rats and immature mice model; to characterize the in vitro selective estrogenic effects of icariin and icaritin; as well as to determine the mechanism by which icariin and icaritin activate estrogenic signaling in osteoblastic cells. It is hope that this study will increase our understanding of the mechanism of actions by which icariin exert selective estrogen-like effects in bone cells and provide the mechanistic basis for developing new generation of SERM for prevention and treatment of osteoporosis.

15103614.label: Realisation of objectives
15103614.value: 1. For Objective 1, 100% of the proposed work has been completed. In this objective, the in vivo tissue selectivity of icariin were evaluated using immature CD-1 mice as well as ovariectomized (OVX) Sprague Dawley (SD) rat model. We have demonstrated that icariin did not exert estrogenic effects in mammary gland, ovary and uterus in CD-1 mice based on the evaluation of the endothelium histomorphology as well as the expression of proliferation marker, proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA). Moreover, icariin did not alter estrogen-dependent mRNA expression (progesterone receptor, PR and complement component 3, C3) in uterus of CD-1 mice. As for the long term estrogenic effect of icariin, six-month old OVX SD rats were treated with diet containing 0, 50, 500 and 3000ppm icariin for 3 months. The effects on bone metabolism were evaluated based on serum bone formation markers, urine bone resorption marker, biomechanical properties of the diaphysis of tibia and femur by three-point bending test as well as bone mineral density and micro-structure of trabecular bone at distal femoral end and proximal tibial head by micro-CT. Our results showed that icariin protected against bone loss at all three bone sites measured without inducing estrogenic effects in the uterus (uterus weight, PR, estrogen receptor ER and C3 mRNA expression) in OVX rats. Icariin induced alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and osteocalcin mRNA and inhibited IL-6 mRNA expression in tibial head of OVX rats in a dose-dependent manner. In addition to the proposed bone and reproductive tissues, we also evaluated the estrogenic effects of icariin in striatum by studying the expression of dopamine metabolism-related enzyme (tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and transporter (dopamine transporter, DAT). 2. For objective 2, 100% of the proposed work has been completed. The estrogenic activities of icariin and icaritin were evaluated in four different estrogen-sensitive cells, including osteoblasts (MC3T3-E1), human breast cancer (MCF-7) cells, human endometrial (Ishikawa) cells as well as human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells. The effects of icariin and icaritin on osteoblast cell viability, differentiation and mineralization, cell apoptosis as well as mRNA expression of several estrogen-regulated bone forming genes (OCN, OPG, and ALP) were measured. For the effects in human breast cancer cells, their effects on cell proliferation and the mRNA expressions of pS2, insulin-like growth factor I receptor (IGF-IR), ER in the presence or absence of ER inhibitor, ICI 182,780 were studied. Their effects in Ishikawa cells on ALP activities and the mRNA expression of ALP, PR and C3 were studied. Their effects on cell proliferation and ER mRNA expression in SH-SY5Y cells were also measured. We were unable to detect TH and DAT expression in SH-SY5Y cells. To overcome this problem, we have transfected estrogen response element (ERE)-reporter construct into all four cell lines so that their estrogenic responses to treatment with icariin and icaritin could be characterized. Our results indicate that icariin and icaritin exerted direct estrogenic activities in all four cell lines. 3) For objective 3, 100% of the proposed work has been completed. The mechanisms by which icariin and icaritin activate ERs were systematically characterized. The ability of icariin and icaritin to bind to ERs, induce ERE-dependent reporter transcription as well as the dependency on ERalpha and ERbeta were assessed. The ability of icariin and icaritin to induce rapid ER signaling were assessed by determining the time-dependent as well as dose-dependent phosphorylation of ERalpha at Ser 118 as well as at Ser 167 as well as the phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and Akt in osteoblastic cells. The involvement of G-protein coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) as well as IGF-IR in mediating the rapid signaling induced by icariin and icaritin were also evaluated.

15103614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103614.value: Major findings: 1. Our study demonstrated that icariin exerts tissue-selective estrogenic effects in vivo using both ovariectomized (OVX) rats as well as immature CD-1 mice model. The optimal dose for estrogen-like bone protective effects in OVX rats was at 500 ppm (vs 50 and 3000ppm). Icariin did not exert uterotrophic effects in both OVX rats and immature CD-1 mice and icariin did not stimulate the maturation of ovary and breast in CD-1 mice. 2. Both icariin and icaritin exerted direct estrogenic actions in estrogen receptor (ER) positive cell lines (MCF-7 breast cancer cell, MC3T3-E1 osteoblastic cells, Ishikawa endometrial cells and SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells). However, icariin is not a ligand while icaritin is only a weak ligand of ERalpha and ERbeta. Both of them could not induce ERE-dependent transcription in these cell lines. Our results suggest that non-classical ER signaling pathways are involved in mediating their actions in estrogen target tissues. 3. The estrogenic actions of icariin and icaritin in osteoblast were selectively mediated by ERalpha, but not ERbeta. Moreover, icariin and icaritin rapidly activated phosphorylation of ER alpha via MAPK- and PI3K-dependent pathway. Icariin was also shown to activate IGF-IR signaling pathways and the activation of ERalpha phosphoryation by icariin required the kinase activity of IGF-IR. Taken together, our results suggest that the cross-talk between IGF-IR and ER signaling pathways mediates the actions of icariin in osteoblastic cells. 4. Blocking GPER could further enhance the stimulatory effect of icariin and icaritin on cell proliferation and ALP activity as well as the signaling pathways induced in MC3T3-E1 cells. Our results suggest that GPER might be a negative regulator in the bone protective effect of icariin and icaritin. We have presented our research in five international conferences as shown in Part C Section 9. The project also trained one Ph.D student, Dr. Liping Zhou.

15103614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103614.value: Our studies demonstrated that icariin exerts tissue-selective estrogenic activities in vivo with beneficial effects in bone tissues and minimal side effects in reproductive tissues (breast, ovary and uterus). The estrogenic actions exerted by icariin and icaritin are different from those of estrogen as they are mediated by rapid ER alpha signaling rather than by classical ER signaling pathways in ER-positive cells. However, it is unclear if icariin and icaritin will alter the responsiveness of estrogen sensitive tissues to estrogen. Thus, it will be important to study the coordinate regulation of different ERs (including ERalpha and GPER) in response to treatment with icariin and icaritin in bone cells. It is also unclear if ERalpha is indispensable for the effects of icariin and icaritin on osteogenesis and if other non-ERalpha dependent pathways are involved in mediating their actions in bone. Based on these findings, Ms Ka Ying Wong (Ph.D candidate) in my laboratory is working on her dissertation project to study how different ERs are being regulated and activated in bone cells by icariin. We have also submitted a continuation GRF proposal (2019-2020) entitled “Study of the membrane-initiated estrogen receptor (ER)-dependent and -independent bone protective actions of icariin”.

15103614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103614.value: Icariin is a major bioactive ingredient in Herba Epimedii, a Chinese herb commonly prescribed for management of bone health in China. Previous study showed that icariin behaved as phytoestrogen and protected against estrogen-deficiency induced bone loss without inducing undesirable effects in uterus. The research of the funded project confirmed that icariin exerted tissue-selective estrogenic effects in bone and did not exert estrogenic effects in reproductive tissues including breast, ovary and uterus. Our study further showed that the mechanism involved in activation of estrogen receptors by icariin as well as its metabolite, icaritin were different from that of estrogen and involved the selective activation of rapid non-genomic signaling pathways. Our research provides new insights for developing new generation of tissue- and pathway-selective drugs for management of postmenopausal osteoporosis. This information will also be useful for medical professional to assess the risk and benefits of using icariin as therapeutic agents of osteoporosis. Last but not least, this work will increase our understanding of the mechanism involved in mediating the actions of bone protective Chinese herbs and increase the international acceptance of the use of Chinese medicine for management of bone diseases.

15104014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104014.value: Clear ocular vision is essential for all our daily activities. Myopia is said to be present if the images of distant objects are focused not on the retina, but in front of it. Myopia is much commoner in Oriental populations (including Chinese in Hong Kong) than in Western populations. The main concern is the many devastating ocular complications (e.g. glaucoma and cataracts) arising from high-grade myopia. Recent work from our group and another research group has identified the vasoactive intestinal peptide receptor 2 (VIPR2) gene to be a novel susceptibility gene for high myopia. The association signal is robust and reliable because of the big total sample size of the two studies. The sequence variants found to be associated in these two studies are unlikely to be the genuine causal variants driving the underlying association with high myopia. The proposed study aims to conduct an in-depth study of the associated region to identify the common causal variants in 3 phases. The first phase conducts genotyping for a large number of sequence variants within the associated region reported previously. Associated sequence variants will be annotated for regulatory features to help prioritize the sequence variants for follow-up in a second phase. The second phase will genotype the associated sequence variants (from Phase 1) with a much large sample size for replication. The third phase will use in vitro experimental methods to evaluate the functional effects of replicated and associated sequence variants on the VIPR2 gene. The study design has over 80% power to pinpoint the causal variants with functional effects. Identification and characterisation of causal variants in myopia susceptibility genes will help in elucidating the mechanistic pathways involved in the development of myopia, and shedding light on better methods of preventing/treating myopia. 清晰的視覺是我們所有日常活動不可缺少的。如果遠處物體的圖像被聚焦在視網膜前面，而不是在視網膜上，這就是近視。近視在東方人群（包括香港的中國人）比西方人群比較常見。主要關注的是由高度近視引起的許多破壞力極強的眼部併發症（如青光眼和白內障）。 從我們的研究團隊和另一個研究小組最近的工作已經確定血管活性腸肽受體2（VIPR2）基因是一個新的高度近視易感基因。因為這兩項研究的大總樣本量，因此該關聯信號是穩健和可靠的。在這兩項研究發現的序列變異不太可能是引致高度近視的真正致病變序列。 我們提出的研究旨在進行于關聯區域的深入研究，這研究分三個階段進行，以鑒定常見致病的序列變異。第一階段會在相關聯的區域内進行大量基因型驗證檢測，鑒定有關聯後，我們會對序列變異調控方面的功能加以注解，以便按優先次序為序列變異進行後續的第二階段研究。第二階段將會用更大量的樣本為已在第一階段鑒定有關聯的序列變異進行基因型驗證檢測，以達致複製的目的。第三階段將採用體外實驗方法來評估已獲複製的關聯序列變異功能方面的作用。此項研究設計可以精確找出有功能影響的致病序列變異，其統計功率超过80%。 近視易感基因的鑑定與特性鑒定將有助於闡明參與近視發展的機制途徑和預防/治療近視的較好方法。

15104014.label: Realisation of objectives
15104014.value: Our initial plan was to genotype using iPlex assay (on MassARRAY platform) about one-third of our samples in Phase 1 of the study, and then the remaining samples in Phase 2 (also by iPlex assay). With greatly reduced funding approved (cut down to HK505,445 from the proposed budget of HK1,800,300), we revised the objectives to genotype fewer SNPs. If we were to genotype these “fewer” SNPs (single nucleotide polymorphisms ) with iPlex assays, the cost for the planned Phase 1 study would take up the majority of the approved funding. We therefore revised our plan to genotype ~200 SNPs with the custom Infinium iSelect HD BeadChips, which happened to be used for another on-going project (now already completed). The cost structure of iSelect BeadChips turned out to be both a plus and a minus for the current study. The cost for additional SNPs (~200 for the current study) added to the original much larger numbers of SNPs was very attractive and could be afforded by the approved budget. However, the cost structure of the iSelect BeadChips also demanded a certain minimum number of DNA samples to be genotyped. Finally, the majority of our samples were genotyped in Phase 1 (as has been explained in one progress report). In Phase 2, we genotyped about one-third of our samples (see explanation above) with the proposed method. We indeed genotyped a smaller number of SNPs (21 SNPs as guided by the results of Phase 1 and the linkage disequilibrium structure of the zoomed-in region) by iPlex assays as planned. Not unexpectedly, two iPlex assays were finally used to genotype 11 SNPs (9 SNPs by one iPlex assay and 2 by another iPlex assay). However, one SNP genotyped by this method turned out to give a high failure rate. Six of these 21 SNPs were genotyped by another in-house method (unlabelled probe melting analysis, which was in routine use in our laboratory). We encountered a lot of technical difficulties for the remaining 5 SNPs. This is most likely due to the fact the zoomed-in region in Phase 2 contains many highly repetitive DNA regions that make the primer design very difficult, if not impossible, and produce many non-specific product upon PCR amplification. We filled in this gap with imputing the genotypes of these few SNPs with reference to the “1000 Genomes” reference panel (Chinese). With hindsight, the use of iSelect BeadChips rather than the planned MassARRAY platform in Phase 1 study might in fact be advantageous to the study from another perspective. Illumina’s iSelect BeadChips use 50-mer oligos to capture the target sequences for genotyping and the use of such long oligos ensures high specificity even in the regions with many repetitive sequences. Otherwise, we might not be able to zoom in this interesting region in the Phase 2 study. Finally, all our samples were successfully genotyped with only a small number of genotypes imputed in the Phase 2 study. Annotation of associated SNPs was performed with current databases in public domains. Technically, this part was not demanding. However, public databases such as ENCODE have sparse data of gene expression and epigenetic information in cell lines of ocular origin.

15104014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104014.value: Based on our previous results, we selected 202 SNPs in strong linkage disequilibrium (LD) (r2>0.4). Of these, 24 SNPs had a score of 3a or lower as annotated by the RegulomeDB database; the lower the score, the better the prediction). Finally, different numbers of SNPs were removed at different stages from assay design to the final genotyping experiments. In total, 150 SNPs were successfully genotyped by iSelect BeadChips and 2 more important SNPs already removed during the manufacturing stage were genotyped separately by an in-house assay. Single-marker and haplotype analyses were performed (using Plink) and LD plots visualized by Haploview. These SNPs spread from intron 1 of the VIPR2 gene and extend ~50 kb downstream of the gene. Most SNPs that are within the gene (~60) are strong LD with each other and form three LD blocks defined by solid spine of LD (in Haploview), and the remaining SNPs are with much weaker LD among themselves and with other SNPs located within the gene. Single-marker association analysis did not produce significant results after multiple-testing correction. However, sliding-window haplotype analysis consistently generated significant results with haplotype windows of different sizes up to 14 SNPs even after multiple-testing adjustment. These significant haplotype windows cluster around two LD blocks that are located in intron 5 of the gene and extend some distance into flanking regions. Therefore, we followed up the SNPs in these two LD blocks in Phase 2. Since the Phase 2 study involved a smaller sample size when compared with the Phase 1 study (see Section 5.2), single-marker analysis did not reveal any significant results. However, sliding-window haplotype analysis gave positive findings that were just significant after multiple-testing correction. On the other hand, combined analysis of Phase-1 and Phase-2 genotype data gave very significant association signals even with single markers and, of course, haplotype windows. Conditional association analysis indicated that two SNPs (rs2730265 and rs2540357) seemed to be more important than the other SNPs. In summary, our results indicate that the causal variants driving the association signals should be located within these two LD blocks centering around intron 5 of the VIPR2 gene and spreading into adjacent introns. Annotation of the region bound by these two SNPs indicates the presence of a CTCT-binding site, histone modification signals, etc. found in cell lines of non-ocular origins. Therefore, the relevance and significance of such annotations remain uncertain. (Annotation of associated SNPs is the original proposed objective 3.)

15104014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104014.value: We have zoomed in a putative candidate region that may harbor the causal variant(s) driving the association signals. However, the candidate region contains many SNPs in very strong LD with each other. This means association analysis (including conditional analysis) may not be helpful in pinpointing the causal variants. Experimental functional studies are required to address this question and in-depth studies of the involved regulatory SNPs can be investigated using appropriate novel genomic technologies such CRISPR-Cas9, chromosome conformation capture and massively parallel reporter assay – just to give a few examples. One hurdle is the availability of appropriate ocular cell lines. Now the most commonly used cell line for this purpose is a retinal pigment epithelial cell line.

15104014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104014.value: Our research group first identified several years ago that the VIPR2 gene was associated with the development of high myopia. We followed up this initial finding to attempt to locate the common sequence variants that drove the association signals. The current adopted a cost-efficient two-stage approach to achieve this aim. In Phase 1, we genotyped a large proportion of the selected genetic markers called single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in a large portion of our samples. We followed up the initial signals in Phase 2 by genotyping a much smaller number of SNPs in the remaining samples. Overall, we zoomed in a region within the VIPR2 gene that seemed to contain the causal sequences driving the genetic association between VIPR2 and myopia development. This zoomed-in region centres on intron 5 of the VIPR2 gene and spreads into adjacent regions. We suggest identifying the causal variants and examining their functional effects by novel genomic technologies in future studies.

15104114.label: Realisation of objectives
15104114.value: The sole objective of this study was realised by a series of experiments conducted according to the following three stages. Stage 1. Preparation of cells and testing agents Upon obtaining the MB49 cell line from a collaborator, the cells were propagated and characterized in our laboratory. A new batch of Ganoderma lucidum was used for ethanol extraction, whereas the final product GLe was tested for quality assurance based on the FRAP total antioxidant reducing capacity assay and an array of experiments with the human uroepithelial cells (HUC) model. BCG was purchased through the clinical partner. Then GLe and BCG were tested on the newly established MB49 cell line for determining the cytotoxic and growth inhibitory effects in-vitro. By using the LDH cytotoxicity assay, GLe was shown to be a potent cytotoxic agent with 85-88% effectiveness at 80 ug/ml or above while BCG at clinical dosage recommended by the manufacturer was only effective to demonstrate 20-30% cytotoxicity on MB49 cells. Consistently, GLe at range of 0-100 ug/ml exhibited a clear dose-dependent growth inhibition according to the trypan blue exclusion assay. However, no apoptotic activity was observed in the GLe-treated MB49 cells, which was in contrast with the G2/M cell cycle arrest appeared in the pre-cancerous HUC cells. Furthermore, gene expression assays indicated that both GLe and BCG were immunoilogical active in inducing the expression of genes of IL-6, IL-12b and IFN- but suppressing the gene of CXCL15. Whilst consistent with its cytotoxic profile, the effects of GLe on cytokine gene expressions were clearly does-dependent. In-vitro results suggested concentrations of 0-80 ug/ml for GLe and 0-2 clinical dose for BCG to be evaluated in-vivo using the MB49/C57 mice model. Stage 2. Setup and optimization of the MB49/C57 bladder cancer mice model Due to a licensing problem of the original proposed imaging equipment, the luciferase (Luc)-based live imaging was not performed in this study. Whilst live transabdominal micro-ultrasound imaging technique was used to guide through the whole experiment from ensuring the successful inoculation of MB49 cells into the mice bladder and monitoring the tumor growth to determining the tumor volume. Our laboratory setting recorded a 100% successful rate for the MB49/C57 model establishment with the earliest full-blown tumors detected on day 5 following the electrocautery inoculation of MB49 cells. Upon successful setup of the mice model, assay protocols for all outcome measures were optimized. Stage 3. Main study A total of 60 MB49-impanted mice and 8 wild-type C57 mice were used to address the study objective. The control mice received neither GLe nor BCG treatment, where the positive control mice were MB49 implanted while the wild-type mice were used as the negative control. Results indicated that the tumor growth inhibitory effects of GLe were more significant than BCG in terms of tumor volumes and time for tumor occurrence. When compared with the positive control, MB49 tumors treated with BCG were shown to be growing in smaller sizes but BCG did not affect the tumor incidence at various time points. On the other hand, GLe was not only shown to have the smallest tumor volumes at all time points (for example on day 15, 3.83 mm3 compared with for 13.71 mm3 BCG and 17.56 mm3 for positive control), it also delayed the tumor occurrence by 7 days with tumors first detected in this group om day 12. Tumor existence was double confirmed at the end point by histological analysis. The signs of inflammation were detected by gross anatomical investigation of all dissected tumor-bearing bladders. Urine specimens were collected from all mice at various time points for measuring the levels of cytokines. The urinary cytokine profile of the GLe-treated mice was shown to be consistent with the gene expression profile measured in the MB49 cells treated with GLe in-vitro. GLe was demonstrated to increase the infiltration of T-cytotoxic cells (CD3+;CD8+) according to the immunohistochemical analysis, which could be an response to the cytokine stimulation. Regarding the toxicity tolerance, none of the GLe-treated mice died before the end-point of the experiment, whereas no sign of major adverse effects including reduction of body weight, changes of physiological activities monitored by the ultrasound platform, and grading of hematuria. In conclusion, in-vivo effects of GLe demonstrated in orthotopic MB49/C57 bladder cancer mice model suggested intravesical GLe could be an effective and safe remedy to replace the conventional BCG therapy in inhibiting the recurrence and growth of bladder tumor. Results also supported the notion of immuniological mechanism underlying the GLe chemoprevention with induction of cytokine secretion in urine as well as T cytotoxic cells infiltration into the bladder wall, which requires further elucidation.

15104114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104114.value: The major novel findings of this study have partially published in two publications listed in Part C. In vitro, ethanol extract of Ganoderma lucidum (GLe) was shown to be active in inducing several cytokines in MB49 cells, particularly the induction of IFN--γ gene expression was 2.7 times of that induced by the conventional BCG treatment (Yuen et al., 2017). In this relation, at the tested dosage range, GLe was demonstrated to kill 24.7-88.1% MB49 cells as compared with the 7.6-19.6% of clinical dosage of BCG (Yuen et al., 2017). By using the syngeneic orthotopic MB49/C57 bladder cancer mice model, intravesical GLe was shown at the first time to be more superior than BCG in vivo to delay the tumor formation and inhibit the growth of MB49 tumor, as confirmed by ultrasound imaging and histological analysis (Yuen et al., 2018). However, no significant side effects were discovered in the GLe-treated group (Yuen et al., 2018). Additionally, further analysis of the tissue sections using the immunohistochemistry technique has also discovered the infiltration of T-cytotoxic cells into the bladder wall upon the intravesical GLe treatment. These findings were consistently with the secretion pattern of cytokines in urine specimens that shed the light on the mechanistic investigations of intravesical GLe therapy for bladder cancer. An additional journal publication is expected following the publication of Yuen et al., 2018 in the Journal of Ethnopharmacology.

15104114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104114.value: Intravesical therapy with the ethanol extract of Ganoderma lucidum (GLe) has demonstrated to be effective and safe in inhibiting the growth of MB49 tumor in mice. Before this knowledge can be translated into clinical for applying to patients for trials, the following stages of further development are needed: 1) Ingredient characterization and fingerprint profiling of the GLe, and 2) Understanding the mechanistic pathways of the GLe-mediated tumor inhibitory activities. Secondly, Ganoderma lucidum is regarded as a superior herbal tonic in Chinese Medicine and used as precious health supplement by the general population. Cancer patients are commonly used G. lucidum and its products orally for boosting the immune system. With the positive findings of the current study, owing to the inconvenience of intravesical therapy that requires the direct instillations of drugs into the bladder for 1-2 hours in each treatment, it is worthy to also explore the effects of oral treatment with G. lucidum by using the same syngeneic orthotopic model. Urine specimens can be collected from bladder cancer patients who are consuming G. lucidum, and then comparing their cytokine profiles with those mice treated orally.

15104114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104114.value: Ganoderma lucidum, known as Lingzhi in Chinese is a medicinal mushroom commonly used by the general population as health supplement for various health benefits, including immune boosting in cancer patients. This study used a bladder cancer mice model to expand the scope to investigate the possibility of intravescial therapy with an ethanol extract of Lingzhi (called GLe), hence without going through the digestive system and metabolism. Results indicated that GLe possessed potent cytotoxic effects, delayed tumor formation and reduced tumor size in the mice. Further examination of the tissue sections was also indicated infiltration of T-cytotoxic cells in the bladder wall, which was consistent with the secretion profile of the urinary cytokines upon intravesical GLe thaerpy. This project has addressed the problem of high recurrence and progression of transitional cell carcinoma (TCC), which provided critical scientific evidence for the basis of Lingzhi’s anti-tumor activities in bladder cancer, for the first time, demonstrated the effectiveness and safety of using Lingzhi intravesically on TCC chemoprevention on animals. This establishes the fundamental mechanism of TCC prophylaxis with GLe, in order to pave the way to the next level – human trials and in-depth mechanistic investigations.

15104314.value: Identify alternative reactions within the active site of Class A β-lactamase by mutating catalytically critical residues We plan to conduct extensive mutagenesis of several catalytically critical residues to perturb the local environment of the catalytic Ser70 residue and trigger it to undergo alternative inactivating reactions. The mutants will be screened for loss of activity by nitrocefin assay. Mass spectrometry will be used to search for unexpected mass changes that result form alternative reactions. Our preliminary studies have indeed identified a few such mutants that show loss of β-lactamase activity and unexpected mass changes. Any peptide regions showing unexpected mass change will be subjected to peptide fragmentation and tandem-MS to identify exactly the amino acid residues responsible for the mass change. 15104314.label: Realisation of objectives
15104314.value: The project has progressed very well through the 36-month period and is now completed with all objectives realized to 100%. We would like to report our activities and results obtained according to the four proposed objectives. Objective 1. Identify alternative reactions within the active site of Class A β-lactamase by mutating catalytically critical residues Using the Class A β-lactamase PenP as model enzyme, we have generated a series of mutant constructs targeting five key residues within the active site including Lys73, Glu166, Ser130, Lys234 and Arg244. Alternative enzymatic activity in these mutant enzymes has been assessed by Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) method as well as UV spectroscopy. Our results reveal that any mutational substitution at Lys73 would lead to complete loss of enzymatic activity in PenP, confirming that this residue is indispensable for β-lactamase catalysis. In contrast, mutations at Ser130, Lys234 and Arg244 lead to kinetic profiles nearly identical to that for wild-type, suggesting that no alternative activities are induced by these mutations. Interestingly, mutations at Glu166 lead to changes in enzymatic activity that may suggest alternative reaction schemes. For example, ESI-MS and UV data shows that mutants Glu166His and Glu166Tyr retain measurable, albeit significantly slowed, hydrolytic activity toward β-lactam antibiotics. Additionally, mutations like Glu166Arg and Glu166Lys lead to unexpected mass change of -18 and +154 in reference to the apo enzyme (E), suggesting possible novel alternative reactions that irreversibly modify the PenP enzyme. Objective 2. Investigate the mechanism of alternative reactions in mutant β-lactamases by mass spectrometry (MS) fingerprinting We have carried out MS fingerprinting experiments to study the PenP mutants, both in apo state and in substrate-bound intermediate states. These studies allow us to identify alternative reactions because the relevant modifications to the PenP enzyme can be tracked at single-residue level. For Lys73 mutants, MS fingerprinting has confirmed that all mutant enzymes remain unmodified in presence of β-lactam substrates like penicillin and cephaloridine. This is consistent with our kinetics measurement that there is no detectable catalytic activity in these mutants. For Ser130, Lys234 and Arg244 mutants, we didn’t characterize them by MS fingerprinting because they are deemed as similar to wild-type based on their ultrafast kinetics. Thus they are unlikely to undergo alternative reactions. For Glu166His and Glu166Tyr mutants, MS fingerprinting shows only one modification, i.e. the formation of enzyme-substrate (ES*) acyl adduct at the site of the catalytic Ser70 residue. This ES* modification is gradually reversed at the deacylation stage, with the hydrolyzed substrate released as product (P) and the apo enzyme (E) regenerated. This result suggests that the catalytic mechanism in these two mutants is largely the same as that seen in wild-type. The slower kinetics may be due to some rate-limiting factors related to the mutations but not alternative reactions. For Glu166Lys and Glu166Arg mutants, we obtained some intriguing data. MS fingerprinting has identified the catalytic Ser70 residue as solely responsible for the mass change of -18. Considering the chemical structure of Ser70, the most plausible model for such modification is the loss of –OH side chain and the resulting conversion to dehydroalanine (Dha). No residues were identified to account for the mass change of +154. It is possible that this modification may be temporary and thus can be lost during the experimental procedure of peptide fragmentation. Nonetheless, the possible Ser70-to-Dha conversion to account for the mass change of -18 is completely novel and suggests that alternative reactions can occur within the active site of Class A β-lactamases. Objective 3. Determine crystal structures of mutants undergoing the alternative reactions to delineate the reaction schemes We have determined the high-resolution structures of several PenP mutants, both in apo form and in substrate-bound intermediate states using x-ray crystallography. Computational simulations using Molecular Dynamics (MD) or the Molecular Mechanism/Quantum Mechanics (QM/MM) approach were also carried out to delineate the functional roles of mutant residues in the catalytic process. For Glu166His mutant, we determined four structures including the apo structure; the post-acylation structure after the crystal was soaked in cephaloridine-containing solution; the deacylation-1min structure when the soaked crystal was transferred to cephaloridine-free solution and equilibrated for 1 minute; and the deacylation-6min structure when the equilibration time was 6 minutes. Our structures reveal that the mutated His166 flips out of the activate site in the post-acylation structure and flips back in to serve as substitute general base in the deacylation-1min and -6min structures. MD simulations confirm that such flipping motions are triggered by proton shuttling events that occur in the catalytic process. For Glu166Tyr mutant, we also determined similar structures to represent the apo state, the post-acylation reaction intermediate and the deacylation-3s state after 3 seconds of equilibration time. The mutated Tyr166 does not undergo flipping motions as seen in Glu166His structures. In contrast, in the deacylation-3s structure, Tyr166 is seen to coordinate a centrally located water molecule and position it on the right trajectory with perfect geometry to carry out nucleophilic attack on the ES* acyl adduct. Our QM/MM analysis confirms that this attack occurs in sync with proton shuttling between Lys73 and Tyr166 to initiate the deacylation reaction. For Glu166Lys and Glu166Arg, we have determined their apo structures at high resolution of 2.0 Å. The electron density maps clearly show that the –OH group of Ser70 is absent, confirming that Ser70 is indeed converted to Dha. In some data sets we even observed a covalent bond between Dha70 and Lys73, suggesting that the unsaturated =C side chain group of Dha70 can react with the –NH3 + group of Lys73 and form lysinoalanine-like moiety. Furthermore, Glu166Arg and Glu166Lys mutations lead to significant conformational change within the Ω-loop region with the mutated Arg166 or Lys166 residues flipped completely out of the active site. Objective 4. Explore the feasibility of inducing Ser70 to Dha conversion in Class A β-lactamase using small molecule compounds Our literature search on small molecules that can modify catalytic serine residues led us to the large family of serine protease inhibitors. In fact, one such compound, phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF), has been used in our buffer for PenP purification. Comparing the MS profile of Glu166Arg and Glu166Lys mutants purified either in the presence or absence of PMSF confirms that indeed PMSF is responsible for Ser70-to-Dha conversion. Our docking studies suggests that PMSF can only modify the catalytic Ser70 in Glu166Arg and Glu166Lys mutants because these two mutations cause conformational change in the Ω-loop and effectively enlarge the active site to allow access by PMSF. Following this thread of thinking, we tried a series of sulfonyl fluoride compounds with smaller side chain groups than PMSF to fit into the narrowly shaped active site of Class A β-lactamases. A few of them can covalently modify Ser70 and leads to permanent loss of enzymatic activity. These compounds can serve as lead candidates for design of novel inhibitors for Class A β-lactamases.

15104314.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104314.value: Our enzyme kinetics studies of the Glu166His mutant reveal that His166 can serve as a substitute general base for the deacylation reaction to retain enzymatic activity at significantly reduced level. Crystallographic snapshots of the Glu166His mutant hydrolyzing the cephaloridine substrate reveals that His166 undergoes “flipping” motions to move in and out of the active site. Such motions likely contribute to its reduced kinetic rate as compared to wild-type. These findings were reported in a publication in J. Biol. Chem. in 2017 (Part C, item 8[1]). We have also conducted structural studies to investigate why carbapenems can resist hydrolysis by serine-based Class A or C β-lactamases. Our data show that the unique stereochemical features of carbapenems such as its hydroxyethyl side chain in trans conformation interacts with general base Glu166 and interferes with the deacylation reaction. Based on these findings, we have designed a modified penicillin compound (MPC-1) with carbapenem-like hydroxyethyl group “grafted” onto the β-lactam core. This compound shows specific inhibitory effect against Class C β-lactamase that is ~2-5 times more potent than the clinically used Class C β-lactamase inhibitor drugs. This work has been published in Antimicrob Agents Chemother. in 2017 (Part C, item 8[2]). A Chinese patent has been filed too (Part C, item 11[1]). Our lab have also published a paper in PNAS during the period of this project (Part C, item 8[3]). While this paper reports our work on the autophagy protein Beclin1 and thus not directly related to β-lactamases, it is still included here because it is an integral part of the research program within our lab and involve the same lab personnel. For example, Dr. Yunjiao He, the joint first author for items 8[1] and 8[2] in Research Output, is also the joint first author of item 8[3]. In addition to the published work above, we also have two manuscripts to be submitted soon (Part C, item 8[4] and 8[5]). One manuscript is related to our structural and QM/MM study of the catalytic process in the Glu166Tyr mutant. The other is related to the Ser70-to-Dha conversion observed in Glu166Arg and Glu166Lys mutants. Both manuscripts also involve rationally designed candidate compounds that can act as novel inhibitors for Class A β-lactamases by either mimicking the Glu166Tyr mutation or inducing the Ser70-to-Dha conversion. We are in the process of filing patent application for these lead compounds and will submit the manuscripts as soon as the patent applications are confirmed by the government entities.

15104314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104314.value: A novel finding from our study involves the conversion of catalytic Ser70 residue to Dha by serine protease inhibitors like PMSF in Class A β-lactamases. Our structural and computational studies reveal that these compounds can modify Ser70 using their reactive sulfonyl chloride head group if their side chain groups are small enough to fit into the narrow active site of Class A β-lactamases. For future studies, we aim to build PMSF derivatives that retain the sulfonyl chloride head group but have rationally designed side chain groups to facilitate efficient binding to the active site of Class A β-lactamases. These compounds can potentially serve as novel inhibitors by covalently and irreversibly modifying the catalytic Ser70 residue. Another novel finding of this project is our rationally designed inhibitor molecule termed Modified Penicillin Compound 1 (MPC-1). By “grafting” carbapenem-specific stereochemical features onto the penicillin core, we have converted this antibiotic substrate into a selective inhibitor of Class C β-lactamases with potency ~2-5 times higher than the clinically used drugs like sulbactam. For further studies we will carry out structure-activity optimization of the MPC-1 lead compound to enhance its specificity and potency.

15104314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104314.value: Antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria is an emerging global healthcare problem that leads to more adverse effect in patients and higher risk of bacterial infection being spread. A major mechanism of antibiotic resistance is the production of β-lactamases, a large group of bacterial enzymes that can readily hydrolyze and inactivate nearly all the clinically used β-lactam antibiotics. There is urgent need to identify novel antibiotics and inhibitors of β-lactamases. We have conducted biochemical and structural studies of Class A β-lactamases to delineate its catalytic mechanism and identify novel alternative reactions that can be targeted for inhibitor design. Our results show that residue Glu166 plays multiple roles in the catalytic process of β-lactam hydrolysis ranging from acting as general base for the deacylation reaction to being exploited by carbapenem compounds to avoid hydrolysis. Furthermore, mutational perturbation of Glu166 can even expose the catalytic Ser70 residue to blockage by serine protease inhibitors. Based on our mechanistic findings, we have designed a few lead compounds that can inhibit Class A and C β-lactamases with higher potency than clinically used β-lactamase inhibitors. These results offer the possibility of targeting the key catalytic residue Glu166 for design and discovery of novel β-lactamase inhibitors.
