15200614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200614.value: The research has adopted the model used in Australia to develop a robust tool to calculate embodied carbon of building materials. The tools can be used for future research on this topic. Based on costs and material quantities data of 26 construction projects (including heritage conservation and new-build projects) in Hong Kong, we extracted and filtered the data to apply to the model with embodied carbon data of the major building components. The set of data is difficult to get and the process of critical reviewing and selecting the valid data and findings provide very good reference similar process of research on embodied carbon of construction materials. We have developed a framework to explain the relationship between embodied carbon and construction cost of the major building components in heritage conversations. The Hong Kong findings suggest that mean embodied carbon for refurbished buildings is 33-39% lower than new-build projects, and the cost for refurbished buildings is 22-50% lower than new-build projects (per square metre of floor area). Embodied carbon ranges from 645-1,059 kgCO2e/m2 for new-build and 294-655 kgCO2e/m2 for refurbished projects in Hong Kong. Overall, a very strong linear relationship between embodied energy and construction cost was found and can be used to predict the former, given the latter. The relationship line and results could help balanced decision-makings concerning heritage buildings redevelopment in the context of environmental and economic sustainability.

15200614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200614.value: The research process and findings of this study could be used to build importance weightings in considering whether to conserve heritage building or not. The study provides good foundation for further in-depth investigation into the costs/embodied carbon relationship for different types of conservation: partial rebuilt, refurbishment, adaptive re-use and decoration etc. The same research approach could be repeated for different cities of different mature status in terms of economic growth and governance in the construction industry.

15200614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200614.value: This research has contributed to quantify the merits of reusing heritage buildings over new construction from an environmental perspective with due consideration of construction cost to support decision-making for sustainable heritage conservation. Overall, the study shows that a very strong linear relationship between embodied energy and construction cost was found and can be used to predict the former, given the latter. The relationship line and results could help balanced decision-makings concerning heritage buildings redevelopment in the context of environmental and economic sustainability. The identified ratio in terms of carbon emission over cost can be monetarized when there is a mature carbon trading mechanism. Although conservation decisions also depend on socio-cultural aspects, findings of this research will contribute one key dimension for conservation decision-makings by providing comparison of embodied carbon intensity over costs for new-build and heritage conservation buildings. Such comparison could also be presented for different trades and for different material groupings and elements.

15201214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201214.value: The linear analysis and effective length can hardly be applied to design of steel and metal structures consisted of curved members such as arches which have an initial shape with considerable out-of-straightness deflection whereas the effective length method assumes no out-of-straightness deflection until buckling. A new nonlinear beam-column element capable of considering the shear deformation is to be developed in this project under the concept of consistent deformation. For the traditional displacement interpolation function, the beam-column element produces membrane locking under large deformation and shear locking when the element becomes slender. To eliminate the membrane and shear locking, force equilibrium equations are employed to derive the displacement function. Numerical examples show that membrane locking in the traditional nonlinear beam-column element may cause a considerable error. Comparison of the present formulae based on the Timoshenko beam theory with that based on the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory indicates that the new formulations are only slightly more complicated, with several parameters needed to modify the expressions of Euler-Bernoulli beam element to consider shear deformation. Thus, the new present formulae are suitable for computer analysis and readily for incorporation into the space frames analysis with general treatments of 3D co-rotational rotations adopted by many researchers. The proposed beam-column element will be used with 2D co-rotational approach for plane frame analysis allowing for large translations and rotations. Classical plane problems of nonlinear analysis using the proposed beam-column element , 2D and 3D co-rotational approach will be studied. Previous research findings and development on nonlinear analysis of structures consisted of straight members by the proposer has, to a certain extent, generated an impact to the practice of structural engineers. The second-order and advanced analysis has been placed in the latest design steel code 2011 published by the Hong Kong SAR government (see web http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/SUOS2011.pdf ), in which the applicant is the first principal consultant. The work by the investigator was given the Grand Award by the UK-Hong Kong joint structural engineering division of the The Hong Kong Institution of Engineers this year (2013) for its application to design of a large span space structure in Singapore without any assumption of effective length. This project will enhance the design capacity of second order analysis to structures consisted of highly curved members, which are common in many architectural structures and their design cannot be conducted rationally by the effective length method. 在保證變形協調的原則下，本項目提出了一個新的可以考慮剪切 變形的非綫性梁柱單元。傳統梁柱單元所采用的位移插值函數會 産生自鎖問題，爲了消除自鎖，本項目所提出的單元利用力的平 衡微分方程來推導能够保證單元變形協調的位移函數。計算實例 表明非綫性梁柱單元若采用傳統的位移差值函數會産生相當大的 計算誤差。此外，本項目所提出的非綫性梁柱單元是基于考慮剪 切變形的鐵木辛柯梁理論下的公式，相比于其在忽略剪切變形的 歐拉梁理論下的公式幷不會複雜很多，只需添加多幾個參數就可 以考慮剪切變形的影響。因此，本項目所提出的單元可以很方便 地編寫成電腦程序，幷結合已有的成熟的三維拖動坐標方法進行 空間框架分析。爲了方便說明，文中只推導了該非綫性單元在二 維情况下的公式幷采用二維的拖動坐標方法進行了平面框架的大 位移和大轉動分析。通過幾個經典的算例可以證明本項目所提出 的可以考慮剪切變形的非綫性梁柱單元有非常高的精度和效率。 申請人以前的研究發現及在非綫性分析上的發展對結構工程的實 踐産生了一定程度的影響。二階和高等分析方法已經寫入最新的 2011版香港鋼結構規範中，其中申請人是首席顧問，詳見 http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/SUOS2011.pdf。 申請人的研究成果在應用于新加坡的一個大跨空間結構設計時， 不需要采用任何有效長度假設，有效地解决了傳統方法所遭遇的 困難，從而獲得了本年度香港工程師學會中的英國-香港聯合結構 分部的結構大獎。本項目將會進一步加强二階分析方法對曲型結 構的設計能力。

15201214.label: Realisation of objectives
15201214.value: Traditional linear axial displacement and cubic transverse displacement interpolations produce membrane locking in the large deflection beam-column element. Individual linear transverse displacement and rotation interpolations produces shear locking in the slender beam element. When it comes to the design of curved members, reliable result becomes difficult to obtain. In this project, a beam-column element with second-order effect and shear deformation has been developed and it eliminated locking phenomenon with the consistent displacement interpolations. The proposed beam-column element combined with co-rotational approach allows large deflection analysis of frame with curved member with high accuracy and efficiency. The objectives of formulating a curved members with initial imperfections are completed and the theory is published. The theory is also incorporated into a software for practical uses. The efficiency and accuracy of the new theory and element are evaluated in a number of examples. The use of the new method is more economical with the new formulation free from shear locking. Application of the method and new element is done to some constructed projects. The work will be of much benefit to engineers for design of steel structures with curved elements, which is common in construction industry to date.

15201414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201414.value: 大部分享有盛譽的製造公司都有一個緊密結合和合作的供應網絡。開放式電子物流標準(OELS)是實現供應鏈整合的重要網絡技術。在OELS中， 數據的傳輸和處理是由開放數據和處理標準管理的。它們定義了數據的格式、結構和貿易伙伴之間的數據流語義。實施OELS 能促使供應鏈的電子整合和信息分享。此外，OELS的重要性是被製造業和政府認可的。中國和臺灣政府甚至把OELS的實施藍圖視為長期經濟計劃的一部分。縱使OELS十分重要，OELS的緩慢發展及其低採用率仍然令人值得關注。儘管政府和龍頭企業如美國英特爾公司和諾基亞作了重大的投資。OELS的潛在失效成為了政府和供應鏈參與者的一個重大的絆腳石。 研究員也開始關注現時的模型並不適用於解釋和瞭解OELS之採用。由於社會建設的多樣化和緊密結合的網絡作用，使OELS的發展和實施變得複雜。「軸輻路網」設置也影響OELS的採用，例如一個大客戶與其供應商的遠景結合會影響OELS的結構和功能。最近一些有關OELS的研究指出，遠景結合的出現需要在應用研究模型和方法學驗證。此外， OELS用戶群的性質（稱為用戶配置）需要進一步研究其影響OELS傳播的結構和行為。用戶配置將研究重點從單一公司的採用轉為多個相互依賴的公司。他們有不同的技術能力和整體戰略性及結構上的安排。雖然用戶配置的分析在學術上與科學和經濟有關，但是其應用在OELS的研究中依然稀少。此研究的目的是結合多個理論觀點和運用改進方法的配置分析，藉以試驗OELS傳播的決策和過程。項目會產生一個新算法和決策支援系統。新算法結合結構性公式建模和神經網絡，而決策支援系統則能幫助他們對OELS的採用做決策。

15201414.label: Realisation of objectives
15201414.value: Objective 1 (100% achieved) The key objective of this study is the development of a robust model to understand the adoption of OELS in manufacturing industries. Drawing on various theoretical frameworks including the structural embeddedness theory, the relational view of the firm, and organizational ambidexterity theory, a unified research model was developed to examine the influences of two categories of network configurations characteristics: exchange structure and tie architecture, which were conceptualized as the push forces of OELS diffusion. This study thus aims to enhance the inter-organizational systems literature by investigating how network configurations characteristics, specifically, exchange structure and tie architecture, affect the actual OELS adoption. The diffusion model also incorporated two relational mechanisms – bridging and bonding –as the full forces of OELS diffusion. This study theoretically develops two relational mechanisms pertinent to the context of OELS assimilation and provides the proxies to measure these two mechanisms. By surfacing the complementary effects between bonding mechanism and the two bridging mechanisms on OELS adoption, this study safeguards against the conventional belief that bonding and bridging are substitutes, and demonstrates how these two mechanisms are mutually reinforced to facilitate the adoption intention and the actual assimilation of OELS. Different network configurations, i.e., supplier versus buyer and potential adopter versus current adopter are also compared to enhance the understanding of how to promote OELS adoption based on firms’ positions in their supply chains. By comparing different value preferences of potential adopters and existing adopters, this research shows that different diffusion models should be developed to study pre-adoption and post-adoption stages. Although OELS is a key technology that generates value to manufacturers to achieve supply chain performance, there are still knowledge gaps with respect to how OELS can help in generating value. The findings empirically confirm that OELS enable companies to enjoy durable competitive advantages to pursue higher-order performance by developing bonding and bridging capabilities to continually restructure supply chain processes and respond to external changes. Objective 2 (100% achieved) A two-staged analytical method combining regression analysis with neural network analysis was developed to analyse the proposed research models. Applying regression solely might be subject to the risk of oversimplifying the complex relationships between different factors. Although explanatory analytics can inform the strength of a causal relationship, the results cannot represent the model’s accuracy in predicting new data. For practitioners, the ability to predict accurately is more emphasized compared to the understanding of the causal relationships between variables. Predictive analytics can provide insights for the predictive performance of the model. To this end, predictive analytics can be employed to assess the distance between theory and practice. In addition, compared with explanatory analyses, predictive analyses do not require the assumption of a particular type of distribution function for the underlying data sample to execute the input and output mapping. Therefore, to balance the goals of explaining and predicting, the two-staged analytical model conducted predictive analysis with the significant variables yielded from explanatory analysis to alleviate the overfitting problem in predictive algorithms such as neural networks. This combination can lead to a better understanding of the antecedents to OELS adoption while identifying appropriate predictors for adoption. In the two staged analytical framework, explanatory analyses, i.e., regression and SEM, were applied first to test to interpret the casual relationships among the proposed factors. Predictive analysis, i.e., neural networks and Bayesian MCMC, were conducted subsequently to assess the predictability of the models or even modify the models if the minimum level of predictive power cannot be obtained. Neural network analysis can incorporate the complex non-linear relationships involved in the process of OELS adoption, which can offset the drawbacks of linear models which oversimplify the complexities in the decision process. Compared with regression analysis, neural networks do not require the assumption of a particular type of distribution function for the underlying data sample to execute the input and output mapping. Therefore, to balance the goals of explaining and predicting, neural network analysis is conducted with the significant variables from regression analysis. In this way, the overfitting problem in neural network analysis could be alleviated. Objective 3 (100% achieved) To empirically test the research model with the developed analytical models, this project collected two rounds of data with questionnaire instruments developed based on a comprehensive literature review. This study collected data from manufacturing companies operating in Mainland China using a self-report survey instrument which was carefully developed following existing guidelines and exemplars. China is considered as an ideal environment to study OELS and supply chain management because of the growing efforts devoted by Chinese companies in deploying OELS to integrate partners within their global supply chains. The first sampling frame was the member companies of the Shenzhen Anti-Counterfeiting Association (SACA), and the second sampling frame was the list of manufacturing firms belonging to the industry categories within Chinese Industrial Classification (CIC) codes 1311–4290. To collect data from both the potential adopters and adopters of OELS, this study prepared two versions of survey. A professional marketing company was hired to collect data. The employees of the company first contacted the potential respondents through phone to solicit their cooperation and to identify whether the companies the respondents were working for were potential adopters or current adopters of OELS. The two sets of data enabled the test of the research models to investigate the factors affecting both the adoption intention and the actual adoption of OELS while comparing the differences between the suppliers and buyers and between the potential adopters and current adopters of OELS. The survey instrument employed in this study was designed based on a comprehensive review of the literature on inter-organizational information systems, inter-organizational relationship management and supply chain process management. Whenever possible, existing measurements in the literature were adapted from past studies to safeguard the content validity of the constructs and their fit in the research context, and to ensure that the overlap among the constructs was minimal. The surveys were conducted through computer-aided phone interviews by the employees of the professional research company. Based on standard practice, senior executives such as chief executive officer, chief technology officer, and senior operation managers, were identified to be the key informants because they have adequate knowledge about their companies’ overall operational and IT capabilities. Using the developed two-staged analytical model, the results can inform both the strength of a causal relationship from explanatory analysis while also present the model’s accuracy in predicting new data which is of vital importance for practitioners. The empirical results showed the differences between the potential adopters and the current adopters regarding the antecedents to OELS. The findings also confirm the positive impacts of OELS adoption on both operational and financial performance.

15201414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201414.value: Major findings: (1) A two-staged analytical model was developed to combine explanatory analysis with predictive analytics [Part C(8): item 6]. Empirical data was collected from the member companies of SACA in mainland China using a survey instrument. The results extended the understanding of the adoption of OELS by investigating the influence of the structural patterns of interdependence, contextual characteristics of supplier portfolio and information sharing [Part C(8): item 6]. The importance of investigating network structures and the significance of structural embeddedness theory as a promising paradigm to study inter-organizational information systems (IOS) were revealed. [Part C(8): item 6 and Part C(9) item 2] (2) Based on the factors derived from structural embeddedness perspective, the influences of network-level properties, specifically, exchange structure and tie structure, on OELS adoption were investigated. It was found that the network configurations could have significant impacts on firms’ strategic behaviours regarding OELS adoption [Part C(8): items 4-5 and Part C(9) items 1-4]. In addition, through revealing the different impacts that these factors have on OELS intention in the buyer and the supplier models, the importance of differentiating the roles of buyer and supplier when investigating OELS adoption was identified [Part C(8): item 4, Part C(9) item 5]. The results demonstrate important differences between the perspectives of buyer and seller regarding the determinants of OELS adoption [Part C(8): item 4, Part C(9) item 5]. (3) By showing that OELS can act as effective boundary-spanning mechanisms enabling both bonding and bridging ties, leading to supply chain ambidexterity, the findings contributed to both the ambidexterity literature and the IOS literature by explaining how OELS technologies can help companies overcome resource constraints to achieve ambidexterity in supply chain network. In addition, it was found that OELS adoption is positively associated with both operational and financial performance, which extended the understandings about the influence of OELS. Moreover, the results suggested that ambidexterity has positive influence on both operational performance and financial performance, which provided performance implications of supply chain process ambidexterity [Part C(8): item 3]. Other findings: (1) An exact heuristic algorithm has been developed to solve Bi-objective optimization problems. [Part C(8): item 1] (2) An improved approach under group decision-making environment has been developed in decision making for the selection of cloud vendor. [Part C(8): item 2] Successful PhD training: One PhD student had been trained up and she was graduated on 28 February 2019.

15201414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201414.value: Despite the contributions of this study for both the theory and practice, it is believed that the study could be even more rigorous if the following suggestions can be achieved: (1) Future studies can consider the dynamism of time when evaluating the antecedents and outcomes of OELS. The current study used cross-sectional data collected at a single point in time, which might be subject to the risk that the influence of the investigated factors on OELS and the organizational outcomes are only temporal, which could not show the influence of the research findings over time. It is important for future research to conduct longitudinal studies to ensure that organizations can sustain supply chain competitive advantage through OELS adoption. (2) Future research should collect data from more contexts. The current study collected from China where there is a collectivist cultural environment and therefore the respondents may have a tendency to agree regardless of the content of the questions. Thus there might be a slight chance of acquiescence bias in our data. Therefore, although the research was conducted rigorously to ensure internal validity, the generalizability of the results may also be constrained by the research context. To address this limitation, future studies could collect data from more countries to verify the research model to overcome the bias in data and enhance the generalizability of the findings. (3) Further research can incorporate other network configurations, such as network density, firm centrality, and structural equivalence when investigating OELS diffusion. Current study only evaluated several network properties such as dependence, relationship duration and tie strength. However, there might be more characteristics pertaining to supply chain network that may affect the adoption of OELS. Future studies can explore this direction by identifying more relevant factors in analysis.

15201414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201414.value: The recent advance of the internet and web technologies has introduced more powerful IOS technologies such as OELS for supply chain integration. OELS facilitate the information flows between business partners, enhance inter-organizational communication and coordination, and improve firms’ ability to achieve a collaborative supply chain network. The inadequate adoption and assimilation of OELS, however, present a major obstacle to successful supply chain management, which makes it imperative to understand the factors affecting the adoption of OELS. In an effort to understand the theoretical antecedents to and the impacts of OELS adoption, a unified research model is developed and tested using empirical data collected from Chinese manufacturing companies. This research investigates the influence of the network properties and relational mechanisms on OELS adoption and the resultant organizational outcomes, which shows the differences between the potential and current adopters and between buyers and suppliers regarding the antecedents to OELS. The research also advances the analytical methods by combining explanatory analyses and predictive analyses together. This study enhances the understanding of OELS adoption by showing the factors promoting/prohibiting OELS diffusion, which has yielded valuable implications for academics, practitioners, and policymakers to guide the strategies to promote more companies to adopt OELS.

15201614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15201614.value: 應用於屏幕图像编码之高效運動補償預測

15201614.label: Project Objectives
15201614.value: So far, the intra-frame coding techniques in screen content have widely been investigated in the literature and JCTVC. Besides, the conventional motion-compensated prediction in inter-frame coding is not appropriate for screen content such as text/graphics due to its distinct spatial and temporal characteristics. One of the main requirements for motion-compensated prediction in SCC is the preservation of important edge and structural information. Therefore, one of the objectives in this proposal is focusing on designing low-complexity motion estimation algorithms on domain other than pixel domain for this purpose. Motion-compensated prediction in existing video coding standards all simply assume translational motion model. For most motions from camera-captured nature video, this model is well suited. However, motion in screen content is always due to user's activities such as document editing/reading with scrolling, web browsing with zooming and scrolling, etc. In this proposal, we will evaluate the impact of these new motion types on motion-compensated prediction in SCC, and explore the characteristics of such screen motions that enter into the motion estimation algorithm. New motion estimation strategies will then be designed. Instead of the translational model, we will try to incorporate the specific motion activities in screen content into the motion estimation process, which is a novel idea in SCC. These schemes provide high coding efficiency, operate with reasonable complexity, and tailor make for SCC. The motion characteristics motivate us to adopt adaptive search range for motion estimation. We are going to take user's interaction and gestures into consideration to determine a restricted search range in motion estimation, resulting in expediting the motion estimation process in SCC. In respond the challenge of the new motion types on screen content further, efforts will be made toward both theoretical and practical aspects of incorporating the screen motion activities into multiple reference frame (MRF) buffers in the standard video codec. We will then contrive a way to utilize the concept of MRF in order to simultaneously encode mixed motion activities efficiently. This arrangement is much better to handle real screen motions in SCC. By doing so, trade-off among coding efficiency, complexity and memory usage will be optimized.

15201614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201614.value: 移動設備和大屏幕之間的屏幕共享需要高效率，低複雜度的屏幕內容編碼, 這是減少設備之間傳輸龐大數據量的一項關鍵技術。它不僅用於家庭娛樂, 也應用於雲瑞移動計算的屏幕虛擬化。基於這些普及與應用, 在視頻編碼（JCTVC）聯合協作小組現已建立了相關的專案小組開發屏幕內容編碼的標準。市場預計屏幕內容傳輸之應用將繼續在未來幾年不斷增長。電腦屏幕上的內容具有不同於自然图像的空間和時間的特性。例如，屏幕內容的視頻通常集中於有限數量的顏色, 強烈的邊緣, 和非平移運動。雖然各種幀內編碼技術已被提出及用於屏幕畫面編碼，但是幀間編碼技術和方案仍然非常初步。本項目將基於移動設備的手勢介面而為運動補償預測進行深入而細微之探討, 從而提出一些高效和嶄新的幀間編碼技術作為解決這些挑戰性問題。

15201614.label: Realisation of objectives
15201614.value: All four objectives mentioned in 5.1 have been achieved by consideration of the unique characteristics of screen content video. Computer screen content sharing is playing an essential role in cloud-mobile computing, remote desktop, video conference with document sharing, wireless or WiFi screen mirroring, etc. Efficient coding of these data is crucial for the success of these applications. However, there are some very special characteristics for the compression of video-like screen content which is a combination of camera-captured continuous-tone content (photograph, movie, and natural video sequences), and the computer-generated discontinuous-tone content (text, graphics, and icon). In contrast to the continuous-tone content, discontinuous-tone content often has sharp edges that are not encoded well by the conventional transformed-based image/video coding coders. Consequently, SCC has attracted attention from both academia and industry, and the Joint Collaborative Team on Video Coding (JCTVC) working on high efficiency video coding (HEVC) has formed an ad hoc group to develop SCC technology and standardization. This research work successfully investigated this emerging SCC with high coding efficiency and low computational complexity by examining the use of efficient intra-frame prediction and inter-frame prediction with motion estimation and compensation techniques in new domains and considering the user's gestures and behavior, and the current architecture of video codecs. To evaluate the proposed idea, we first implemented the new prediction framework in screen content coding (SCC). Our work investigated a possible solution of performing SCC prediction in domain other than pixel domain, which is specially designed for screen contents for intra/inter-frame coding. After the investigation, edge, and Base Colors/Index Map (BCIM) domains are possible solutions. BCIM provides the structural information of the text/graphics block. It means that pixels represented by the same base color forms a partition, which indicates the structural information in the block. Therefore, one possible way to obtain the true block/motion vectors in text/graphics blocks is to convert block pixels into BCIM domain for intra/inter-frame prediction. Significant gains can be achieved by performing the prediction in these domains. As expected, the BCIM domain approach in SCC results in increase of computational complexity. Consequently, a two-bit depth representation has designed for efficient implementation. (Objective 1) In addition, motion-compensated prediction adopted in the current video coding standards always assumes the use of the translational motion model, which is best fitted for motions induced by camera-captured nature video. In contrast, motion in screen contents always come from user's activities such as document editing/reading with scrolling, web browsing with zooming and scrolling, etc. In our work, we evaluated the impact of these new motion types on motion-compensated prediction in SCC, and explored the characteristics of such screen motions that enter into the proposed SCC prediction scheme. By doing so, some new motion estimation strategies such as a single reference frame multiple motion models (SRefMMotion) scheme was proposed and tested. This scheme offers high coding efficiency, operate with reasonable complexity, and tailor make for SCC. (Objective 2) We also investigated whether it is possible to use the characteristics of screen motions in SCC to reduce the complexity of SCC by adopting adaptive search range for intra/inter-frame prediction. Users' interaction and gesture were proposed to determine a restricted search range in motion estimation. For our investigation, it is found that the motion due to document reading or webpage browsing only induces vertical translational motion. In this situation, only the vertical search window is enough for BCIM-ME or edge-based ME. A smart scheme was designed to take the characteristics of various motions due to user's interaction and gesture into consideration for adaptive search range motion estimation. We are the first to consider user's interaction and gesture in speeding up estimation and prediction in video coding. Significant gains can be achieved with significant complexity reduction. (Objective 3) To further adopt the new motion types on screen content, investigations were made toward both theoretical and practical aspects of incorporating the screen motion activities into multiple reference frame buffers in the standard video codec. We then built a way to utilize the concept of multiple reference frame buffers in order to simultaneously encode mixed motion activities efficiently. This arrangement is much better to handle real screen motions that can be incorporated into the reference software screen content model version 8.3 (SCM8.3). Finally, our scheme can provide the trade-off among coding efficiency, complexity and memory usage can be optimized. (Objective 4)

15201614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201614.value: With rapid developments of cloud-mobile computing in the past few years, screen content coding(SCC) is a crucial technology to solve the cloud computing bottleneck to transfer huge amount of data between the cloud and the users. The major component in screen content(SC) is discontinuous tone such as text, graphics, and icon, which exhibits different characteristics compared with the continuous-tone content. SC always contains very sharp edges and thin lines. Consequently, the popular image/video compression standards, which are designed for smooth edges and thick lines, are not well suited for SC. The research aim of this project is to develop a SCC scheme so that the high-quality reconstruction of SCs can be achieved. A number of novel SCC coding techniques using different domain(edge/BCIM-domain) optimization(Part C Journal[2]), rate-distortion cost, and online learning were proposed successfully(Part C Journal[1, 3 and 4], and Part C Conference[2, 3]). Even though this approach would guarantee the highest rate-distortion gain, it is computationally impossible for practical systems. Consequently, some efficient algorithms based on the user's interactions have also been derived by restricting the search window of intra/inter-frame prediction (Part C Conference [1,2]). The restriction mainly takes the user’s gestures into consideration, which includes zoom, rotation, and unidirectional motion. These types of motions are unique to SCs, that can speed up our SCC scheme by about 50%. However, the new motion types on SC induce higher order motion models with additional parameters that complicate the incorporation of the proposed techniques into the reference software SC Model Version 8.3(SCM8.3). In respond, we extend the set of reference frames for prediction with a reference frame that contains the zooming effect due to the user’s gesture. Therefore, a single reference frame multiple motion models(SRefMMotion) scheme has been designed to facilitate the use of multiple models in a single reference frame(Part C Conference [4]). The proposed scheme makes a new arrangement of SRefMMotion that supports different model parameters. It enables different blocks in the same frame can use different models even when they are predicted from the same reference. As a result, the proposed approaches give a significant improvement in quality of the reconstructed frames with reasonable complexity. We also found that all these proposed techniques become feasible to incorporate in the current SCC standard. As a result, three journal papers and four conference papers have been published in this project. In addition, one journal paper is also under review.

15201614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201614.value: SCC is a major technology that enables display mirroring and sharing. Current applications include WiFi display, wireless HDMI (e.g. Apple TV and Chromcast), and etc, which allows a user wirelessly stream the content on a mobile device to a big screen such as HDTV. Recent development in ultra-HD screen with high quality graphics and multimedia contents have further stimulated R&D, standardization initiatives and industry efforts in this area. Besides, virtualization of the screen in the coming cloud-mobile computing environment requires high efficient and low complexity SCC to solve the bandwidth problem for transmission of screen content between the cloud and users. In order to support this, JCTVC specified the new emerging SCC and finished SCC coding standard. Our project coincides with this goal by designing a SCC scheme, and it can make the SCC system more practical. This project will have a remarkable impact on the advancement of future SCC technology. The project also forms the basis for the 3D SCC and game video coding – the next revolution of VR video, which also requires techniques for video coding optimization developed in this project.

15201614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201614.value: Screen sharing and mirroring between a mobile device and a big screen needs high efficient and low complexity screen content coding (SCC), which is a key technology to reduce enormous amount of data transferred between devices. Different from camera-captured natural video, a computer screen content has discriminative spatial and temporal features. For instance, screen content video usually concentrates on a limited number of colors with shape edges and thin lines, and non-translational motions. Due to this fact, a completely new SCC scheme has been developed that incorporates the specific motion behavior to screen contents into our proposed new-domain motion estimation, and takes users' gestures into consideration. Nowadays multi-touch gestures often induce more than one motion activities in the screen such as translation, zoom in and out, rotation, fading, etc. For this investigation, we designed the SCC scheme such that those mixed motions in screen sequences can be handled by multiple reference frame architecture with the help of users' gestures. Through this research, we implemented a new SCC scheme which lays down solid foundation for many commercial products that require screen sharing/mirroring.

15202214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15202214.value: 基於地面甚高頻與電場觀測對閃電下行先導及相關空間電場特性的研究

15202214.label: Project Objectives
15202214.value: Most of cloud-to-ground lightning is initiated by a DNL that starts inside the cloud and propagates toward ground. As the leader extends, the charge deposited on its channel produces electric field changes that can be sensed on ground at close distance. In addition, leader spatial progression can be observed by using high-speed camera or VHF interferometry systems in 3D. Based on electrostatic theory, equations describing the relationship of the leader charges and currents with the leader progression images and leader-produced electric field changes will be established. It is proved that a leader channel is comprised of a conductive core surrounded by a corona sheath with charges. The charge deposited in the corona sheath is related to the potential difference between the leader core and that of the ambient one. The gradient of the ambient potential gives the electric field in space. Furthermore, the divergence of the space electric field is related to the space charge. With this in mind, equations describing the relationship of the leader charge distribution and the space electric field and the space charge will be established. Based on equations developed in above, a specific algorithm for field observations and for retrieving the leader charge evolution and the associated space electric field profile from the observed data will be developed. The field observation includes the measurement of leader-caused electric field changes and the capture of leader-channel progression images. Meanwhile, practicability and feasibility of the proposed algorithm will be examined and fine-tuned by using existing data. According to the proposed algorithm, plans for observations of electric fields with slow antennas and leader images with high-speed camera or VHF interferometry system for DNLs will be made and implemented. One advantage of the VHF interferometer is that it can see a leader process that may be optically invisible. In collaboration with the Lightning Protection Centre of Shenzhen Metrology Bureau, our university has established a lightning field observation station in suburban area of Shenzhen, a city next to Hong Kong. The field observations will be mainly carried out there in summers. With the data observed in field experiment and the proposed algorithm, the evolution of leader charge and current for DNLs will be estimated. Furthermore, the profile of the space electric field and space charge along the route of the leader channel will be estimated. Based on the results in above, possible relationships of the leader behaviors (including the leader speed, leader charge, leader current and channel bending) with the space electric field and space charge profiles will be analyzed. Also possible interpretations of the leader initiation and progression in connection to the space electric field and space charge profiles will be attempted and discussed.

15202214.value: 雲-地閃電對人類的生命和財產有很大的危害。大多數雲-地閃電開始於雷雲內負電荷區域並向地面下行，即始於下行負先導。先導之後是快速的大電流過程，即回擊過程；而打擊點則是由下行負先導所決定。因此，研究下行負先導對理解閃電的物理機制和做好閃電的防護顯尤為重要。 一般而言，下行負先導的起始和發展是由雷雲内外的空間電荷所形成的空間電場所決定。因此，了解先導的空間行進及其相關空間電場的分佈是理解先導過程物理機制的關鍵。然而，現有的大多數關於先導的信息都是基於高速光學或地面甚高頻源映射等觀測所得的先導的空間發展图像，有關先導電荷和電流的演變的信息幾乎沒有。此外，特定先導過程及其有關的空間電場和空間電荷之相關性研究依然幾乎没有。 本研究旨在探索出一種基於地面高頻閃電源及閃電電場的觀測來研究下行負先導的電荷演變及相關空間電場和電荷分佈的合適方法。下行負先導的3D圖像可以由高速攝像或者高頻閃電干涉儀觀測所得。甚高頻干涉儀可以觀測到全方位雲內外閃電先導的行進過程。一方面，先導引起的地面電場變化理論上是源於先導行進過程中滯留在先導通道中的電荷；另一方面，滯留在先導通道的電荷則是由先導過程中的空間電場分佈決定的。這也意味著知道先導的行進過程以及先導引起的地面電場變化就可以了解先導電荷的演變以及其過程相關的空間電場的分佈，因此也就知道了先導電流演變和空間電荷分佈。本研究的成功將增進我們對先導行進，先導電荷演變，空間電場分佈以及空間電荷之關係的了解。這毫無疑問為我們更好的解釋先導的行為提供了非常大的幫助。

15202214.label: Realisation of objectives
15202214.value: The main purpose of this project is to develop an approach for the studying of the leader charge evolution and the associated space electric field profile based on very-high-frequency (VHF) lightning source and very-low-frequency (VLF) electric field change measurements of lightning leaders on ground. There are 6 core tasks: (1) to establish a model describing the relationship of the leader charges/currents with the leader progression images and leader-produced electric field changes; (2) To identify the relationship between the leader charges/currents and the space electric fields and the space charges; (3) to develop a practical algorithm for retrieving the leader charge evolution and the associated space electric field profile from the observed VHF and electric filed change data; (4) to carry out field observations of lightning leaders with leader imaging and electric field measuring systems; (5) to apply the proposed models to observed lightning leader data to validate the model and discuss the results; and (6) to understand the relationship between the leader progression properties and the leader channel electric properties. To achieve these tasks, starting from January of 2015 to the end of June, 2018, we have been carried our continuously field observation of natural and artificial lightning leaders and numerous lightning data have been obtained and analyzed with the proposed models. (a) Firstly, we had successfully obtained the relevant data of a rocket-triggered lightning discharge, which included a preliminary downward leader (PDL), followed by an M-component and two leader-return stroke processes. Based on measurements of VHF radiation sources and VLF electric field changes, the spatial evolution of the PDL, the M-component and the two leader-return stroke processes has been studied. While a classically-triggered negative discharge usually starts with an upward positive leader (UPL) initiated from the tip of the ascending triggering-wire, the present discharge started with a preliminary downward negative leader (PDL) that was most likely a leader process along the channel trace possibly built by the undetected UPL. The M-component was found to be a process that newly developed in-cloud leaders/streamers added to the pre-existing grounded channel built by the PDL. Leaders preceding the two return strokes started inside the cloud and propagated downward to the triggering-wire trace, but with a different channel to that of the PDL. Part of the work was published on Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics (DOI: 10.1016/j.jastp.2017.07.008). Meanwhile, a half analytic electromagnetic wave model for explaining the behavior of lightning VLF/LF pulses propagating in the earth-ionosphere waveguide has been developed. Part of the work was presented at 33rd Int. Conf. on Lightning Protection held on 25-30 Sept. 2016, Estoril, Portugal (DOI: 10.1109/ICLP.2016.7791487). By these efforts, we have achieved 50% of Tasks (1) & (2), 30% of Tasks (3) & (4). (b) Secondarily, based on the lightning data obtained in (a) and the ideal in the proposal, a specific approach for retrieving the leader charge evolution and the leader-associated ambient electric fields under complicated earth boundary condition have been successfully developed. With this approach and based on simultaneously observed electrical fields and high-speed images of lightning discharges, the evolution of the channel charge density of a natural positive downward leader struck at a high-rise building was estimated. It was found that the observed electrical field with complicated earth boundary was much larger than that with flat ground, which means that the complicated earth boundary has a great influence on the electrical field observation during lightning discharges. The charge density estimated for the leader varied along the leader channel in a range of 0.2 ~ 5.4 mC/m. Part of the work was presented at 10th Asia-pacific Int. Conf. on Lightning held on 16-19 May 2017, Krabi, Thailand. By these efforts, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (1) & (2), 50% of Tasks (3) & (4), 30% of Tasks (5) &(6). (c) Thirdly, we have succeeded in observations of lightning strikes to the Shenzhen Meteorological Gradient Tower (SZMGT) for the first time. The 356-m-high SZMGT was built in 2016. While its main purpose is to monitor the vertical gradients of meteorological parameters near ground, the tower was also specially equipped to observe the electric and optical signals, particularly the electric current of lightning strokes to it during thunderstorms. Details of the lightning observation systems on the tower and preliminary results were presented at 34th International Conference on Lightning Protection held on 02-07 Sept. 2018, Rzeszow, Poland (DOI: 10.1109/ICLP.2018.8503458). By this effort, we have achieved 70% of Tasks (3) & (4), 50% of Task (5) & (6). (d) Fourthly, the approach developed in (b) have been applied to the upward positive connecting leaders (UPCL) initiated from SZMGT to analyze the leader channel extension and expansion properties. It was found that the UPCL behaved in step-wise when it extended upward, with a mean step length of 2.6 m, a mean inter-step interval of 27 μs, and a mean average speed of 1.06 ×10^5 m/s. The luminous channel radius of the UPCL as a function of time had a stable increasing trend at its upward-going stage, but showed a periodical shrinking and expansion property after its connection to the cloud. More importantly, the luminous channel radius had an obvious increasing trend with the increase of height, which was about 2.5 m (minimum) ~ 4.5 m (maximum) when around the tower tip and about 3.6 m (minimum) ~ 6.6 m (maximum) when at 24 m high above the tower tip. Such a channel radius property is well in consistent with the modeling results of the leader corona sheath radius in literature. Part of the work was presented at 34th Int. Conf. on Lightning Protection held on 02-07 Sept. 2018, Rzeszow, Poland (DOI: 10.1109/ICLP.2018.8503302). By this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task (3) & (4), and 70% of Tasks (5) & (6). (e) Lastly, the approach developed in (b) have been applied to the downward negative leaders obtained in rocket-triggered lightning discharges in a) above. With the method, the line charge density and the current of two downward negative leaders in a rocket-triggered lightning discharge have been successfully retrieved from the measurements of broadband interferometer images and electric field changes at close distance on ground. Only the descending channel portion between about 900 to 400 m high of the two leaders were analyzed, where the channel was in free air rather than the trace of triggering wire. The line charge density for both leaders showed a general increasing trend with a big impulsive change around 500 m high, as the leaders moved downward, which was in good agreement with the prediction of existing downward leader models. The range of the line charge density was similar for the two leaders (-0.02 ~ -0.33 mC/m). The estimated leader currents for two leaders (-20 ~ -315 A and -77 ~ -541 A, respectively) were also in good agreement with independent estimations in the literature. The results were published on IEEE Trans. on EMC. (DOI: 10.1109/TEMC.2018.2864199). By this effort, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (5) & (6) and hence the purpose of the whole project.

It is proved that a leader channel is comprised of a conductive core surrounded by a corona sheath with charges. The charge deposited in the corona sheath is related to the potential difference between the leader core and that of the ambient one. The gradient of the ambient potential gives the electric field in space. Furthermore, the divergence of the space electric field is related to the space charge. With this in mind, equations describing the relationship of the leader charge distribution and the space electric field and the space charge will be established.

Based on equations developed in above, a specific algorithm for field observations and for retrieving the leader charge evolution and the associated space electric field profile from the observed data will be developed. The field observation includes the measurement of leader-caused electric field changes and the capture of leader-channel progression images. Meanwhile, practicability and feasibility of the proposed algorithm will be examined and fine-tuned by using existing data.

According to the proposed algorithm, plans for observations of electric fields with slow antennas and leader images with high-speed camera or VHF interferometer system for DNLs will be made and implemented. One advantage of the VHF interferometer is that it can see a leader process that may be optically invisible. In collaboration with the Lightning Protection Centre of Shenzhen Meteorology Bureau, our university has established a lightning field observation station in suburban area of Shenzhen, a city next to Hong Kong. The field observations will be mainly carried out there in summers.

With the data observed in field experiment and the proposed algorithm, the evolution of leader charge and current for DNLs will be estimated. Furthermore, the profile of the space electric field and space charge along the route of the leader channel will be estimated.

Based on the results in above, possible relationships of the leader behaviors (including the leader speed, leader charge, leader current and channel bending) with the space electric field and space charge profiles will be analyzed. Also possible interpretations of the leader initiation and progression in connection to the space electric field and space charge profiles will be attempted and discussed.

15202214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202214.value: (a) Firstly, we have successfully obtained and analyzed a set of VHF/VLF data of a rocket-triggered lightning discharge. The discharge included a preliminary downward leader (PDL), followed by an M-component and two leader-return-stroke processes. The M-component was found to be a process that newly developed streamers in cloud added to the pre-existing grounded channel built by the PDL. The two leader-return-stroke processes took a channel path that was different from that of the PDL (Ref.: Journal paper No.1 in Part C). Meanwhile, a half analytic electromagnetic wave model for explaining the behavior of lightning VLF/LF pulses propagating in the earth-ionosphere waveguide has been developed (Ref: Conf. paper No.1 in Part C) (b) Secondly, a specific approach for retrieving the leader charge evolution and the leader-associated ambient electric fields under complicated earth boundary condition have been successfully developed. With this approach, for the first time, the evolution of the channel charges of a natural positive downward leader struck at a high-rise building was estimated based on simultaneously observations of VFL/LF electrical fields and high-speed images of the leader (Ref: Conf. paper No.2 in Part C). Also with this approach, the evolution of the leader charges and currents of two downward negative leaders in a rocket-triggered lightning discharge were successfully retrieved based on the VHF sources and VFL/LF electric fields measurements of the leaders, for the first time (Ref.: Journal paper No.2 in Part C). The both results are in good agreement with independent estimations in literature. (c) Thirdly, we have successfully carried out observations of lightning strikes to the 356-m-high Shenzhen Meteorological Gradient Tower (SZMGT). The tower was specially equipped to observe lightning strokes to it. The measurements included the lightning current, electric field changes and high-speed camera images (Ref.: Conf. paper No.3 in Part C). Meanwhile, a method for studying the channel extension and expansion properties from high-speed optical images of lightning discharges has been developed. Its application to upward positive leaders initiated from SZMGT revealed that the leader channel radius as a function of time had a stable increasing trend at its up-going stage, but showed a periodical shrinking and expansion property as it connected to the cloud. The leader channel radius (ranging from 2.5~6.6 m) had an obvious increasing trend with the increase of height, which was well consistent with theoretical predictions in literature (Ref.: Conf. paper No. 4 in Part C).

15202214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202214.value: By this project, we have developed a method that can retrieve the electric charges, currents and the ambient electric fields associated with a leader process in a lightning discharge from the measurements of VHF radiation sources, high-speed camera images and VLF/LF electric fields on ground. This method can be further developed into an indirect remote sensing technique for detecting the charge density and current of a lightning leader at close distances on ground. Furthermore, with the charge and current profile of a lightning leader being detected, the background electric field associated with the initiation of the leader can be retrieved and investigated, which will be very helpful for understanding the mechanism of the leader initiation and hence for the development of an effective lightning warning and protection system.

15202214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202214.value: Lightning is very deleterious to the life and property of human beings. A cloud-to-ground lightning discharge is usually initiated by a negatively- or positively-charged leader process starting inside the cloud and going downward or starting from the tip of a grounded objects and going upward, followed by a large transient current process - the return stroke process. It is the leader process that determines where the lightning strikes on the earth. Theoretically, the leader initiation and development are governed by the ambient electric field due to the space charges inside and outside the thundercloud. However, we are lacking of techniques to directly measure these leader-associated parameters. In this research, we have successfully developed an approach that can obtain the evolution of the charge of a leader process and the profile of the ambient electric field associated with the initiation and propagation of the leader based on measurements such as VHF sources or high-speed camera images and electric field changes of the leader. The approach was successfully applied to analyze both positively- and negatively-charged leaders properties. The results have enriched our knowledge on the leader initiation and progression and are very useful for both lightning physics and protection.

15202314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202314.value: GNSS實時定位技術（RTK）已經在測量與高精度導航領域得到了廣泛的應用。但是，目前的RTK技術存在以下問題：1）定位結果不可靠，大約有1%的定位結果爲錯誤結果； 2）GNSS定位覆蓋率在某些情况（如城市環境）受到限制；3）參考站的間距通常在30-100 km，以保證消除GNSS誤差的影響。 本研究擬采用集成多種衛星導航系統（美國GPS,中國北斗系統，俄國GLONASS系統，以及歐洲GALILIEO系統）以及多頻信號以解决上述問題。GNSS RTK定位可靠性于覆蓋性問題將通過優化多系統多頻數據處理。通過高精度數字氣象模型以及多頻數據，本項目試圖建立新的RTK算法以保證在200-300km內可靠求解模糊度。本研究將可將目前的RTK網絡間距離增大，以提供廣域RTK服務。

15202314.label: Realisation of objectives
15202314.value: 1) To develop new methods for mitigating ionospheric and tropospheric effects over long-range GNSS RTK network through multiple constellations, multiple frequency siganls, and the latest NWP model GNSS propagation errors are the main reason which requires long observation time to obtain precise positioning results. In this study, we analyzed the latest NWP models and evaluated the accuracy of the models for GNSS correction. Although the NWP models are much better than the traditional tropospheric correction models used in GNSS positioning, the accuracy cannot guarantee the accuracy required for GNSS, particularly in raining seasons. In this study, we developed a novel algorithm to using the NWP model as a constraint to reduce the convergence time. Also, algorithms are developed to integrate ambiguity resolution and ionospheric correction into one iteration loop for three frequency GNSS data processing. As a results, we can achieve GNSS positioning with very long baselines (i.e. over 700 km) with the accuracy much better than the PPP can achieve. 2) To develop new methods for fast and reliable ambiguity resolution based on multiple GNSS systems and multiple frequency bands to increase the reliability and coverage of RTK service The ambiguity resolution is a key indicator for GNSS positioning quality. We developed a new strict method to evaluate the similarity of ambiguity, which will be more reliable than any of the existing methods. 3) To carry out field experiments to demonstrate the advantages of multiple GNSS multiple frequency RTK service We have established a GNSS multi-constellation network in HK and developed RTK platform. We also tested our new methods developed in this projects to different lengths of baselines, from 10-700 km to verify our methods.

15202314.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202314.value: The aim of this research is to develop algorithms to improve GNSS RTK services based on multiple GNSS systems and multiple frequency signals. There are three main tasks in this research: 1) to develop new methods for mitigating ionospheric and tropospheric effects over long-range GNSS network; 2) to develop new methods for fast and reliable ambiguity resolution based on multiple GNSS systems and multiple frequency bands to increase the reliability and coverage of RTK service; 3) to carry out field experiments to demonstrate the advantages of multiple GNSS multiple frequency RTK service. To achieve the first objective, we have evaluated the long-term NWP performance on tropospheric delay estimation on GNSS positioning accuracy. The correlation of tropospheric delays in different distances are analyzed and proposed algorithms to mitigating tropospheric delay over large GNSS network. New algorithms to mitigate ionosphere with three frequency GNSS data are implemented in RTK processing software. To achieve the second objective, we have developed a new criterion for ambiguity resolution validation, which is much robust than the existing methods, particularly over long baselines. To achieve the third objectives, we have tested baselines from a few kilometers, 70-80 kilometers, and up to 500 km. Experiments demonstrated that we can fix ambiguity for over 500 kilometers with a few min. Ten papers are published in the project and one patent is granted on GNSS data processing method developed in the project.

15202314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202314.value: 1. In recent years, PPP and network PPP techniques are developing in GNSS data processing. In these approaches, we need to further investigate different systematic biases which were cancelled out in the differential process. 2. For GNSS data processing, pseudorange is affecting RTK performance. How to improve pseudoraneg positioning accuracy or develop methods to reduce the effect of pseudorange on RTK positioning; 3. Beidou system is recently upgraded to the third generation. European Galileo system will be operation in 2020. How these new developments will affect GNSS performance, particularly in urban region need to be studied; 4. The reliability and integrity of RTK solution need to be further studied, as carrier phase will be potentially used by autonomous vehicle and other safety related applications.

15202314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202314.value: The Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) positioning technology has been widely used in surveying and precision navigation, which greatly improves surveying efficiency and extends the applications of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) for precision guidance. Up to now, large numbers of GNSS RTK networks have been established worldwide to support GNSS RTK operation. Currently, the distances between the reference stations in Hong Kong and China RTK networks are normally within 50 km. A large number of reference stations are required to cover the whole China. For example, more than 4000 GPS reference stations have been established in China (mainly in the east part of China) to support RTK operation in China. On the other hand, in the west part of China, there are only a few RTK networks to cover very limited regions. The research output of this project can extend the station distance to more than 200 km, which will potentially significantly reduce the number of stations required for global coverage. Most of the existing RTK network is based on GPS signals, which only have two frequency bands. It has been demonstrated that with multiple signal bands (3-4), the RTK positioning performance can be significantly improved. Chinese Beidou system has been operational since December 2012. Beidou is the first operational GNSS system to cover Asia-Pacific region with three frequency bands. This project will be one of the first RTK networks to integrate all existing multiple GNSS systems (GPS/Beidou/GLONASS) and multiple frequency signals (three frequency bands of Beidou) to demonstrate the advantages of such integration in the world. We have demonstrated the advantages of three frequency GNSS signals on ionosphere mitigation, and reliability on ambiguity resolution.

15202614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202614.value: Acoustic field inside an enclosure strongly depends on its boundary shape. Numerous applications point to the need for more efficient acoustic modeling tools which allow flexible manipulation of the enclosure boundary towards a better acoustic design. The task is scientifically challenging in that the ideal method should be able to: 1) cope with enclosures of complex shapes; 2) accommodate a sufficiently wide frequency range and 3) offer the flexibility for boundary shape modification and optimization. Whilst existing numerical methods can very well handle the first requirement for a given geometry, most of them have inherent difficulty in meeting the other two. This project attempts to provide a solution to this problem by proposing a Wavelet-decomposed Galerkin Formulation (WDGF) along with an iterative procedure for acoustic boundary design for achieving a desired acoustic target in a general interior acoustic problem. This proposal is inspired by our preliminary study, which showed the remarkable ability of the D-wavelets in approximating the sound distribution over a long acoustic boundary. That work, however, was limited to a simple rectangular configuration at rather low frequencies. The proposed WDGF further takes advantage of the extraordinary fitting ability and the multi-scale nature of the wavelets, which are used as a global basis for sound pressure decomposition under Galerkin framework. The proposed method is expected to allow flexible and unified handling of the cavity boundaries, in which grid points are needed only for defining the shape of the boundary, i.e. the proposed approach is basically mesh-free and able to handle large boundary variations, conducive to boundary shape design and optimization. Meanwhile, several techniques are proposed to improve, select and compress the wavelet basis, including the use of Plane-Wave-Enriched Legendre Wavelets, multi-scale analyses and Boundary Contribution Analyses. Using these measures, along with the enriched physical character of the wavelets, the efficiency and the frequency outreach of the method are expected to be increased. As an application, the proposed boundary design methodology is used to the interior design of a silencer to maximize its noise transmission loss. The successful completion of the project is expected to contribute to solving a fundamental acoustic design problem of significant importance. 封闭空间内的声场极大的依赖于其空间的边界形状。众多的应用型研究都可以归结为通过对封闭声腔的形状改变/优化达到控制声场的目的，因此研究基于封闭声腔边界形状调整的高效声学建模工具是关键。其算法的难点在于1）可以处理复杂的声腔形状；2）支持相当宽的频率范围；3）对于声腔边界的形状修改和优化提供高效率的支持。传统的数值方法，可以很好的处理上述难点1，对于另外两点，尚缺乏有效的手段。本研究课题致力于在一般的内声场问题中，开发一种基于小波分解的伽辽金算法（Wavelet-decomposed Galerkin Formulation，WDGF）,用于声场的建模和优化，以期解决上述三个难点。当前研究基于我们预研课题，即通过对矩形声腔内低频率声场分布模型的研究，发现Daubechies小波在全局逼近方面有惊人的表现。故当前研究项目(WDGF)将利用小波出色的函数逼近特性和多尺度特性，在伽辽金方法框架下，对于未知声场进行全局分解。作为一种无网格的方法，新方法将考虑对声腔边界进行非常灵活而又统一处理，只需要一些点描述声腔的几何形状，而无需其他节点信息，这样将非常有利于边界的形状设计及优化。同时，以下技术被用于改进现有的方法，包括利用平面波增强Legendre小波的物理特性，利用多尺度分析快速分析声学边界贡献率，这些技术将提高现有方法的频率分析范围和计算效率。该研究结果将被应用到消声器的边界设计，通过改变边界形状来提高消声器的声传递损失。该研究的成功实施将对声学设计具有显著的意义。

15202614.label: Realisation of objectives
15202614.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out in this reporting period and related research outcomes, in relation to the research objectives are summarized as follows: 1). A general methodology for acoustic boundary design and optimization has been established. As the core solver of the acoustic field prediction, a global wavelet-based Galerkin expansion of the Kirchhoff-Helmholtz equation was also proposed. The efficacy of the proposed modelling framework was investigated and demonstrated. This part of work directly targets the first three objectives of the project (Objectives 1, 2 & 3). A general procedure, comprising a Wavelet-Garlerkin formulation and a so-called vertex-driven shape optimization was proposed to deal with the general problem of internal sound field prediction and the optimization of the boundary shape. Owing to the compactly supported orthogonal property of the wavelet and its extraordinary fitting capability, Daubechies wavelet scaling function was proposed as a global basis function to expand the unknown sound pressure under the general Galerkin framework. A method named vertex-driven shape optimization was established and demonstrated. Using acoustically rigid rectangular cavity as a benchmark problem, the proposed WGM was shown to be able to achieve high accuracy without any boundary meshing. The accuracy of the WGM strongly depends on the resolution level m and the number of Gauss integration points, and in principle also on the wavelet support length L, but to a much less extent. As long as the support length L is larger than the expansion domain, the accuracy keeps almost the same. The accuracy increases when the value of the resolution level m increases to a certain value, beyond which ill-conditioned problem may takes place. This ill-condition problem can be eased by increasing the number of Gauss integration points based on the adaptive refining strategy proposed in the project. Based on the strong ability of wavelet scale functions in approximating unknown functions in a relative large interval, the proposed WGM allows global expansion and therefore allows flexible handling of the cavity boundaries in a unified way without meshing the geometry model like FEM/BEM usually does. This empowers the new approach with its superiority in acoustic mutation and shape optimization problems over other conventional simulation methods. Potentials of the approach are demonstrated using a polygonal cavity with internal partial partition by following a vertex-driven shape optimization procedure proposed in this paper. 2). The importance and the feasibility of shape optimization problems were investigated through three typical application problems: a). Optimization of acoustic mufflers through adjusting their internal layout. Possibility of optimizing the noise reduction performance of silencers through adjusting internal layout and chamber shape was explored. The broadband sound attenuation characteristics of expansion chamber silencers can be altered by their internal configuration. A systematic approach based on the sub-structuring modeling principle was established to investigate the effects of several typical silencer configurations and provide guidelines for possible system optimization. Through numerical examples, the effects of various internal arrangements, including the side-branch partitions, multi-chamber partitions, non-symmetric inlet/outlet, and their combined effects were investigated. Numerical predictions showed good agreements with both finite element method (FEM) and experiments. b). Creation of the acoustic quiet zone through shape-optimization of an internal partition using Wavelet-Galerkin formulation. c). Realization of acoustic black hole effect through tailoring structural thickness using Wavelet-decomposed vibration model. Experiments were also carried out to verify the conclusions reached. This also fulfill then objective 4. Using the Wavelet-Garlerkin formulation developed above, an example was investigated to show its efficiency in the shape optimization problem. The studied case involved a 2-D rectangular cavity with rigid walls. The accuracy of the prediction in terms of the sound pressure level along the developed cavity wall, when compared to other methods, was shown to be excellent. Without any meshing (one interval over the whole length of the wall), WGM achieved remarkable accuracy, even at the location close to the excitation source where polynomial basis fails. As an optimization example, the sound pressure level within a pre-defined rectangular area is to be minimized at one given frequency by changing the shape of an internal partition. c). Applications of the wavelet-based modelling approach was extended to other vibration problems. In addition, realization of acoustic black hole effect through tailoring structural thickness using Wavelet-decomposed vibration model was explored. Acoustics Black Hole (ABH) effect occurs in a structure with diminishing thickness which gradually reduces the phase velocity of flexural waves. A semi-analytical model was proposed to analyze a Euler-Bernoulli beam with embedded ABH feature and its full coupling with the damping layers coated over its surface. By decomposing the transverse displacement field of the beam over the basis of a set of wavelets, the extremalization of the Hamiltonian via Lagrange’s equation yields a set of linear equations, which can be solved for structural responses. Highly consistent with the FEM and experimental results, numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-based model is particularly suitable to characterize the ABH-induced drastic wavelength fluctuation phenomenon. The ABH feature as well as the effect of the wedge truncation and that of the damping layers on the vibration response of the beam was analyzed. Due to its modular and energy-based feature, the proposed framework offers a general platform allowing embodiment of other control or energy harvesting elements into the model to guide ABH structural design for various applications. As a further application of the model, possibilities of optimizing structural profile to enhance the ABH effects were also explored. During the execution of the project, numerous experiments were carried out as reported above, targeting either at validating models or ascertaining the obtained physical phenomena, on both silencer design and ABH realization. This fulfills the objective #4.

15202614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202614.value: Research outcome, in relation to Section 5.3 are summarized as follows: 1). General methodology for acoustic boundary design and optimization: Using acoustically rigid rectangular cavity as a benchmark problem, the proposed WGM was shown to be able to achieve high accuracy without any boundary meshing. This part of the work forms the theoretical basis for the entire project. The result was summarized in a comprehensive paper published in the International Journal of Applied Mechanics. 2). Demonstration of the feasibility with typical application problems: a). Through numerical examples, the effects of various internal arrangements, including the side-branch partitions, multi-chamber partitions, non-symmetric inlet/outlet, and their combined effects were investigated. Numerical predictions showed good agreements with both finite element method (FEM) and experiments. Investigations suggested some critical issues and possible solutions for better silencer design. This part of the work, directly targeting the objective #4, was summarized in two publications in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. Meanwhile, based on the same principle, the noise reduction of ducted ventilation systems was also investigated, with results published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America. b). Creation of the acoustic quiet zone through shape-optimization of an internal partition using Wavelet-Galerkin formulation. It is shown that the acoustic field distribution inside the enclosure, especially within the predefined area, can be significantly altered through appropriate changes in its geometry or internal geometrical setting. This can be interpreted as a result of the alteration to the mode-shapes of the enclosure. This part of result, directly targeting the objectives #3 & 4, was also included in the paper published in the International Journal of Applied Mechanics. c). The feasibility study of applying wavelets for the modeling of high frequency vibration problems showed that the wavelet-based method outperforms existing simulation methods in its efficiency and high frequency outreach. Outcome of this part of the research was published in the International Journal of Applied Mechanics. Studies on Acoustics Black Hole (ABH) show highly consistent results with the FEM and experimental results, numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-based model is particularly suitable to characterize the ABH-induced drastic wavelength fluctuation phenomenon. Studies on various possibilities of optimizing structural profile to enhance the ABH effects provide guidance to practical design. These two parts of work, which directly target the objectives #3 & 4, are summarized in two papers published in Journal of Sound and Vibration.

15202614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202614.value: The proposed general analysis and optimization strategy using Wavelet-based approach has started finding their wide applications in various fields, ranging from the noble aerospace industry to everyday domestic product design and manufacturing. The former was initiated through the establishment of a joint Lab with the China Academy for Space Technology, with focus on exploring better acoustic design for space structure interior sound field. The latter is evidenced by a recently agreed collaboration with Midea, the main domestic manufacturer in China, who shows great interest in exploring the potential application of the ABH-based technology. Future effort consists in finding more applications cases. Meanwhile, a good packaging of the simulation tool will also facilitate its use.
