15202814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202814.value: Ultra-precision freeform surfaces possessing non-rotationally symmetric geometry with sub-micrometer form accuracy and nanometric surface finish are playing an increasingly important role in various fields such as aerospace, biomedical engineering, illumination, green energy, etc. The complex geometry of these surfaces has to be precise in order that performance improvement is achieved. However, ensuring that their manufacture follows the intended geometry requires an accurate knowledge of the position of the workpiece relative to the machining tool. The geometric complexity of ultra-precision freeform surfaces entails considerable challenges in precisely localizing the workpiece for different processes including the machining and measurement processes. Although the rapid development of ultra-precision machining technologies and coordinate measuring instrumentations has witnessed fruitful achievements in the past few decades, currently an efficient method for localization of freeform workpieces on machine tools and measuring instruments with sub-micrometer repeatability and low uncertainty is still lacking. As a result, this project aims to achieve better accuracy and efficiency in the manufacturing of ultra-precision freeform surfaces. A Fiducial-Aided Calibration and Positioning (FACP) method and system are proposed. The FACP method makes use of fiducials to purposely design high precision fiducial fixtures to form a FA-CAD of the freeform workpiece which will not only calibrate the geometric error of the volume of the machine tool where machining is undertaken but also establish an intrinsic reference datum of the workpiece for precise location on the machine tool and the measuring instrument so as to link the machining and the measurement process for form characterization and compensation of the form errors of the workpiece. Hence, the proposed FACP method is able to transfer the accuracy of the precision measuring instrument in a thermally controlled environment to the machine tools on the shop floor, and the accuracy of ultra-precision freeform surfaces can be improved accordingly. A FACP system will be established to implement the FACP method as a generic method for all types of freeform surfaces which can be easily implemented on ultra-precision machine tools possessing on-machine probing capability. The project if successful will not only provide an important means for significantly improving the efficiency and accuracy of the traditional manufacturing process of ultra-precision freeform surfaces but also enhance the capability of the measuring instrument in the form characterization of these surfaces. The possible outcome of the proposed study will contribute significantly to a novel precision metrology method and system for precision manufacture of ultra-precision freeform surfaces.

15202814.label: Realisation of objectives
15202814.value: Ultra-precision freeform surfaces are well-recognized as having the potential to revolutionize the design of advanced optical systems in many fields, such as aerospace, biomedical engineering, optics, and green energy. It is well-known that the use of ultra-precision freeform surfaces considerably improves the performance of optical and other systems. The complex geometry of these surfaces has to be precise in order that performance improvement is achieved. However, ensuring that the manufacture follows the intended geometry requires accurate knowledge of the position of the workpiece relative to the machining tool at all times. Although the ultra-precision multi-axis machining technologies and coordinate measuring instrumentations have been rapidly developed in the past few decades, there is still no efficient localization method for freeform workpiece on a machine tool with sub-micrometer form repeatability and low uncertainty. This not only leads to a significant gap between the machining and measurement of ultra-precision freeform surfaces but also creates considerable uncertainty regarding the quality assessment of these surfaces, which hinders the further improvement of the accuracy in the manufacturing of ultra-precision freeform surfaces. Using the surface itself as a means for establishing an accurate reference, i.e. an intrinsic reference, is difficult if not impossible because of the lack of detail on the freeform surface: the geometry is necessarily of low spatial bandwidth. As a result, this project aims to provide an external reference linked rigidly to freeform workpieces throughout the manufacture and measurement, and hence a Fiducial-Aided Calibration and Positioning (FACP) system has been developed to improve the accuracy and efficiency in the manufacture of ultra-precision freeform surfaces. The FACP method makes use of fiducials to purposely design high-precision fiducial fixtures to form a FA-CAD of the freeform workpiece which not only calibrates the geometric volume error of the machine tool where machining is undertaken but also establishes an intrinsic reference datum of the workpiece for precise location on the machine tool in different machining processes as well as linking the measuring instrument for form characterization and compensation of the form errors of the workpiece. Hence, a FACP system has been established which is able to transfer the accuracy of the measuring instruments such as the high-precision coordinate measuring machine in a thermally controlled environment to the machine tools to improve the machining accuracy of ultra-precision freeform surfaces. To achieve the objectives of the project, research work has been done to study the design of the fiducial fixture by using standard geometries such as a ball artefact as basic elements which serve as inherent features of ultra-precision freeform surfaces in the manufacturing and measurement processes. A series of fiducial fixtures have been designed and fabricated taking into consideration the repeatability of the localization of the fiducials, the kinematics of the machine, the geometry and shape of the workpiece, the accuracy requirement, etc. Tool collision checks have been conducted for the given tool path so as to avoid collisions between the tool and the fiducials based on computer simulations (Objective 1). Further study has been conducted to study different types of fiducials and designs of fiducial fixtures and their effect and accuracy in locating freeform surfaces on machine tools and measuring instruments. The pyramid artifacts are also designed for the fiducial fixture to facilitate non-contact on-machine measurement of fiducials by using an autostereoscopic-based metrology method (Objective 1 and Objective 2). In the present study, a fiducial-aided positioning (FAP) method has been developed which attempts to precisely locate the freeform surfaces in order to improve the accuracy and efficiency in the characterization of machined freeform surfaces (Objective 2). The FAP method makes use of fiducials to establish intrinsic surface features which are used to determine the coordinate transformation between the coordinate frame of the designed surface and the measuring instruments. A series of simulation experiments and practical experiments has been conducted to demonstrate that the proposed FAP method has the ability to improve the preference in the positioning process to align the machined freeform surface with the designed one in different coordinate systems with lower uncertainty compared with the traditional method. For Objective 3 and Objective 4, a novel fiducial-aided calibration and positioning (FACP) method named fiducial aided on-machine positioning method (FAOPM) has been developed which combines the on-machine measurement and off-machine measurement technologies to precisely position optical freeform surfaces during the precision manufacturing cycle including rough machining, fine machining, measurement, and error compensation. The FAOPM makes use of fiducials to purposely design high-precision fiducial fixtures to form a Fiducial-aided Computer Aided Design (FA-CAD) of freeform workpieces which not only calibrates the geometric error of the machine tool where machining is undertaken but also establishes an intrinsic reference datum of the workpiece for precise location on the machine tool and the measuring instrument so as to link the machining and the measurement process for form characterization and compensation of the form errors of a workpiece. A prototype FAOPM system has been established and a series of simulation and measuring experiments have been conducted to realize the capability of the FAOPM (Objective 5). The results indicate that the positions of the workpiece during the precision manufacturing and measurement cycle were precisely achieved and the form accuracy of the optical freeform surfaces was remarkably improved based on the FAOPM. Based on the foundation of the FAOPM (Objective 4 and objective 5) for measuring various types of freeform surfaces, the project team has conducted research work to extend the applications of the FACP method for measuring multiscale complex surfaces. A series of advanced data fusion methods has been developed such as Gaussian Process Data Modelling and Maximum Likelihood Data Fusion Method and a weighted least square-based data fusion method. Hence, a fiducial-aided data fusion method (FADFM) has been developed for the measurement of multiscale complex surfaces. This method improves the quality of the datasets in both two main steps of the data fusion process: one is enhancing the robustness of the surface registration and the other is reducing the uncertainty and computational time in the fusion process. A series of experiments and the results show that the data fusion method is effective in supporting multi-scale measurement of freeform surfaces. Further work will be done to explore the potential application of the FACP method for volumetric error estimation of the multi-axis ultra-precision machine tools.

15202814.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202814.value: In this project, a series of fiducial fixtures has been designed and built by using standard geometries such as a ball artefact as basic elements which serve as inherent features of ultra-precision freeform surfaces in the manufacturing and measurement processes (Conference Paper 1 and Journal Paper 2). The pyramid artifacts are also designed for the fiducial fixture for facilitating non-contact on-machine measurement of fiducials by using an autostereoscopic-based metrology method (Journal Paper 1). Hence, a fiducial-aided positioning (FAP) method has been developed which attempts to precisely locate the freeform workpiece on multi-axis machine tools (Conference Paper 3 and Journal Paper 3). Experimental results demonstrate the technical feasibility of the FAP method to improve the accuracy and efficiency in the manufacturing of freeform surfaces on multi-axis machine tools. To demonstrate the capability of the fiducial-aided calibration and positioning (FACP) method on ultra-precision machine tools, a fiducial-aided on-machine positioning method (FAOPM) (Journal Paper 4) has been developed which combines the on-machine measurement and off-machine measurement technologies to precisely position optical freeform surfaces during the precision manufacturing cycle including rough machining, fine machining, measurement, and error compensation. The results indicate that the positions of the workpiece during the precision manufacturing and measurement cycle were precisely positioned and the form accuracy of the optical freeform surfaces was remarkably improved to sub-micrometer level based on the FAOPM. Moreover, advanced data fusion methods named Gaussian Process Data Modelling and Maximum Likelihood Data Fusion Method (Journal Paper 7) and a weighted least square-based data fusion method (Journal Paper 6) have been developed which provide solid foundations for further extending the development of the FACP method to measure multi-scale complex freeform surfaces. Hence, a fiducial-aided data fusion method (Conference Pape 2 and Journal Paper 5) has been developed for the measurement of multiscale complex surfaces. Further work is being done to explore the potential application of the FACP method for volumetric error estimation of the multi-axis ultra-precision machine tools (Journal Paper 8). Up to present, one PhD student has been trained and he has submitted a thesis and is awaiting an oral examination. Seven refereed journal papers have been published and one refereed journal paper is under preparation to disseminate the research results of the project. The results of the project have also been presented in three refereed International conferences.

15202814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202814.value: Some suggestions for potential future work are given below: (i) As on-machine measurement systems are usually mounted on the moving axes, the errors of the axes are considered embedded in the measuring data. In the fiducial-aided calibration and positioning system, all errors caused by systems and environment are integrated into volume geometric errors and compensated for by modifying the tool path. With increasing geometric complexity in the advanced optical industry, the form errors may not be completely eliminated based on volume errors. To address this problem, a generalized fiducial-aided calibration model will be needed, which should be able to separate each error of the machine tool so as to fulfill the demands. (ii) Although the designed system can fulfill the experimental demands in a thermally controlled laboratory, the extended applications of the proposed fiducial-aided calibration and positioning method could be hindered when the manufacturing process is carried out in an industrial field with high dynamics and an uncontrolled environment. Hence, it is vital to develop a 3D measuring system with fast measurement speed and relatively high measurement accuracy. For example, a white light interferometer, fringe deflectometer, or 3D camera will be mounted on the machine to measure the freeform surfaces and the fiducials.

15202814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202814.value: Ultra-precision freeform surfaces (UPFS) are well-recognized as having the potential to revolutionize the design of advanced optical systems in many fields, such as aerospace, biomedical engineering, etc. However, ensuring that the manufacture follows the intended geometry requires accurate knowledge of the position of the workpiece relative to the machining tool at all times. This project provides an external reference linked rigidly to a freeform workpiece throughout the manufacture and measurement. Research work has been done to design the fiducial fixture. Hence, a fiducial-aided on-machine positioning method (FAOPM) has been developed which combines the on-machine measurement and off-machine measurement technologies to precisely position optical freeform surfaces during the precision manufacturing cycle including rough and fine machining, measurement, and error compensation. The experimental results conducted on an ultra-precision machine indicate that the positions of the workpiece during the precision manufacturing and measurement cycle were precisely located and the form accuracy of the UPFS was remarkably improved. In this project, one PhD student has been trained, seven refereed journal papers have been published and three refereed international conference papers have been presented to disseminate the research results. The project contributes significantly to a novel method and system for the manufacture of UPFS.

15203114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203114.value: Modification of functional movement patterns has been practiced in many clinical settings with gait retraining being one of the most common functional motor modification strategies. Gait retraining has been successfully applied to patients with neurological conditions. In the recent decade, emerging evidence supports the application of gait retraining for patients with orthopedic conditions, such as knee osteoarthritis, patellofemoral pain, and tibial stress fracture. Previous studies have demonstrated that a 2-week retraining program using different types of real time biofeedback is temporarily able to control implicit biomechanical risk factors, such as excessive peak positive acceleration (PPA) of the tibia. There is a growing evidence of the sensory processing network to retrieve task-relevant information is modality independent. This phenomenon has been testified in many upper limb functional tasks but not in any locomotive task e.g. gait. Specifically, the extents of motor learning using different feedback modalities and the cross-modal flexibility of the human brain during locomotive task remain unclear. Recent studies have demonstrated that electroencephalography can be used to record the intra-stride electrocortical dynamics during human locomotion. It has been shown that activities in the sensorimotor, posterior parietal, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex exhibited significant gait-event specific changes in spectral power. Such power increases indicate specific cortical involvement at different gait events during constant speed locomotion. Examination of the intra-stride electrocortical activity before and after gait retraining using different biofeedback modalities may provide a novel insight for better understanding of motor learning. In addition, the attentional cost of different sensory modalities during locomotive task was not evaluated. Participants may resume the original motor pattern when attention is diverted from their motor performance by a competing cognitive demand. Comparison of retraining under a dual cognitive task condition may provide information for the attentional cost of different feedback modalities. Therefore, the aim of this study is to evaluate how sensory modality affects both cerebral activity and motor performance in young adults before and after a course of 2-week gait retraining, with and without an additional non-motor task. The findings of this study will facilitate the optimization and enhancement of the existing rehabilitation protocols. In addition, such information will provide critical insight into the neural mechanisms of gait disorders and corresponding rehabilitation for a wider spectrum of patients. These findings will also provide additional information regarding the significance of neural control during whole body interactions within natural environments. 步態訓練是臨床最常見的運動功能修正策略之一。步態訓練已成功應用於神經系統疾病患者，如中風及大腦麻痺病人。在最近的十年中，新的證據支持步態訓練運用於不同的骨科疾病，如膝關節炎，髕股關節疼痛，脛骨應力性骨折。有研究發現，為期兩週的步態回饋訓練能有效控制脛骨的正加速度最大值（ PPA ）。過量的脛骨PPA可引致脛骨應力性骨折。然而，步態訓練之基礎理論，特別是學習行走訓練時的回饋模式對人體力學表現與大腦學習程度仍不清楚。首先，之前發表之實驗並沒有在分散注意的情況下測試參與者。注意力轉移時，參與者有可能會恢復原本的運動模式。更重要的是，在培訓期間的大腦學習過程沒有被評估。了解步態訓練的學習機制將有利於優化和提升現有的康復療程。因此，本研究的目的是評估不同回饋模式的步態訓練如何影響人體力學表現及大腦活動。

15203114.label: Realisation of objectives
15203114.value: In general, we have accomplished the set objectives in this proposal as we originally planned. However, we have further improved the research quality in the present study with additional efforts as the follows. We received very constructive comments at the 9th Annual Meeting of Japanese Orthopaedic Society of Knee, Arthroscopy and Sports Medicine and therefore we performed additional experiments to further strengthen the answers to our research questions. Specifically, we repeated the experiment and added another accelerometer to measure tibial shock, while we kept the shoe sensor as originally proposed. Other than the planned study, we found additional interesting findings that gait retraining using shoe sensors, which are most common site for commercial products, may provide false impact loading reduction. Such findings alarm the industrial sector that the current mode of wearable sensors for gait modification may not be optimized. Additionally, I have discussed the EEG data with two renowned professors in this area (Dr. Rosa Chan from City University of Hong Kong and Prof. Mark Jensen from the University of Washington) and both of them pointed out the limitations of the method employed to analyze the EEG. In brief, scholars critique the potential bias of independent component analysis based clustering of brain signals and it has not been a well-accepted method in recent literature. Both Dr. Chan and Prof. Jensen suggest a newer and more robust method to reanalyze the data. We have just finished the data analyze with the new algorithm and we are comparing the findings by each method. Before we submit the findings to a neuroscience journal, we will seek expert advice from Prof. Barbara Shinn-Cunningham from Department of Biomedical Engineering of Boston University, who is one of the reviewers for our previous paper submitted to NeuroImage.

15203114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203114.value: This study examined the effects of walking and running retraining using visual and auditory feedback on impact loading control and its neural circuitry in 64 adults (32 regular runners included). They underwent a course of real time biofeedback training to soften the footfalls and we measured the performance with and without distracting the subjects. Our findings suggest both visual and auditory feedback are effective method for current gait retraining protocol. However, when the subjects are cognitively loaded, subjects who completed visual feedback gait retraining present with reliance on augmented feedback after training. On the other hand, subjects underwent auditory feedback gait retraining do not require augmented feedback at the end of the program. Walking retraining with visual cues was coupled with posterior alpha event-related synchronization (ERS) and desynchronization (ERD) at different gait events. The posterior alpha ERS happened before the onset of visual feedback, indicating a memory clearance process that helped the subjects to reserve more neural resources for the upcoming visual instruction, so as to facilitate the motor learning. The posterior alpha ERD happened after each visual feedback, suggesting an active role of posterior regions in integrating visual inputs from the visual cortex, and accordingly updating the motor plan. Gamma ERS would be generated when auditory cortex (AC) was being stimulated, which is coherent with our findings. The lower-gamma ERS in our study was observed around 300 ms after the onset of audio feedback, falling into the 200-400 ms latency range of gamma ERS in AC as reported in other studies. It indicated the active engagement of auditory cortex in receiving auditory feedbacks during the gait training. It was observed that after visual feedback gait training, when exposed to visual feedback again during the second assessment; visual cortex did not exhibit a significant alpha ERD in the pre-training assessment. Similarly, when these subjects were provided with a “novel” feedback type, i.e. audio feedback, the reaction in lower-gamma band at auditory cortex was not prominent (p=0.166), though an increase in its average power could be observed from the ERSP curves. Interestingly, after auditory feedback gait training, when exposed to the audio feedback again, or to a “novel” visual feedback during the second assessment, the significant time-frequency features in alpha and lower-gamma band were remained. Significant ERD (p=0.041) in alpha band was observed at visual cortex, and significant ERS (p=0.042) in lower-gamma band was observed during at auditory cortex.

15203114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203114.value: This study allows better understanding on the neural mechanism for gait control, which can be applied in future rehabilitation protocol (e.g. transcranial magnetic stimulation) to treat gait disorders, control system for stable robotics locomotion, and brain-machine interface. Clinically, the findings can also be applied in running injury prevention and treatment for patients with knee osteoarthritis.

15203114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203114.value: The present study investigated the effects of gait retraining programs using two different sensory feedbacks to soften both walking and running footfalls. In brief, gait retraining is effective to lower impact loading for both walking and running. However, trained subjects who completed visual gait retraining may still require biofeedback after training for further impact reduction. On the other hand, auditory gait retraining appears to be more effective as trained subjects do not exhibit such reliance after training. Such findings can be explained by the difference in the visual and auditory circuits for gait modification.

15203414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203414.value: Clean refrigerant propane (blend R290) is widely used in new air-conditioning systems following the phasing out of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) in many countries. Although this clean refrigerant has zero Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), low Global Warming Potential (GWP) and good thermodynamic and heat transfer properties, it is flammable and poses fire and explosion hazards. Air-conditioning units are commonly put inside small commercial flats with floor area less than 200 square metre and in restaurants, offices and retail shops. An explosion will occur when propane refrigerants leak from the air-conditioning unit, mix with room air in a ratio higher than the lower flammability limit (LFL) and there exists an ignition source. Fires resulting from explosions of leaked clean refrigerant in air-conditioning units have been reported all over the world, with three involving R290 propane in Hong Kong since 2013. This sounds an alarm on fire safety when using hydrocarbon based clean refrigerants in new environmentally friendly air-conditioning systems. Understanding of the explosion potential of flammable clean refrigerant propane leaking from air-conditioning units in small commercial flats of floor area less than 200 square metre is limited. A scientific study is proposed in this project to model the leakage of propane refrigerants, and to estimate the leakage rates in typical arrangements of air-conditioning units in small flats, the mixing of leaked propane with air and its spread in regions near to the leakage source, the explosion and flame spread, and the possible explosion control by discharging an appropriate suppressing agent. Leakage of propane refrigerant data from air-conditioning units will be surveyed to estimate the leakage rate. Four common ventilation modes with air inlets and outlets at high and low levels due to building constraints in small flats will be considered. The mixing processes of leaked propane with air will be studied by numerical models. Propane concentration distribution will be predicted and then used for studying explosions. A model chamber will be built to experimentally study the mixing process and hence explosions at a remote site in China. Measured temperature and pressure results will be compared with numerical predictions. Further, an explosion tube already developed by the Principal Investigator (PI) will be used to study the possible suppression of propane explosion by four typical suppressing agents. These are nitrogen, carbon dioxide, fine water mist and chemical powder.

15203414.label: Realisation of objectives
15203414.value: Chlorofluorocarbons were not allowed in air-conditioning and refrigeration (ACR) systems before the Montreal Protocol. Consequently, clean refrigerants were used for meeting the requirements of zero ozone depletion and low global warming potential. However, many clean refrigerants such as hydrocarbon refrigerants consisting propane are flammable. Explosion of leaked flammable refrigerants had already led to explosion. This is particularly dangerous when refrigerators are put inside cupboards in small flats. To alert the owners, consumers, technicians and craftsmen on the fire and explosion hazards arising from using clean refrigerants in ACR systems, this project was started with the two proposed objectives completed. For objective 1 to study the fire and explosion hazards due to leaking of clean refrigerant propane from air-conditioning units installed in commercial flats of floor area less than 200 m2; experimentally and numerically: Numerical experiments with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) were carried out in the selected flat to study the mixing of leaked clean refrigerants from ACR systems with air by predicting the air flow induced by four different ventilation modes. The CFD package FLUENT was used to predict velocity, temperature and pressure patterns under the four ventilation modes. Explosions in the small commercial flat due to the leaking of clean refrigerant propane were investigated using flame growth models. The transient over-pressure during the explosion were estimated with some predicted results on flame fronts justified by experiments. A rectangular chamber model was set up to simulate the explosion of flammable clean refrigerants leaked from a refrigerator put in a cupboard under well-covered or partially-covered conditions, representing the cupboard door being opened or closed. A mathematical model was developed based on conservation of mass and energy. Changes in burning flame surface and pressure under these two covered conditions were predicted. In the case where the chamber was not well-covered, the unburned gas and combustion gas were discharged from the pressure relief port at subsonic speed. Experiments on explosion of leaked propane were carried out to justify the model developed. After studying the dispersion of leaking flammable clean refrigerants, explosion upon ignition was simulated with the transient gas explosion pressure predicted. CFD modelling of explosion was carried out in the flat using the software Flame Acceleration Simulator (FLACS). Further, another case on gas explosion in a garage was also simulated. The minimum mass of clean refrigerants involved in the explosion was estimated to be 3 kg to give adequate high pressure rise of over 21 kPa. A possible explosion scenario in that garage is due to leakage of flammable clean refrigerants. A model box chamber made of steel to give a size 1 m by 0.6 m by 1 m was constructed to study real explosion scenarios with leaked propane in summer 2016. Fixed amount of propane refrigerant was injected from the lower level to study the dispersion and explosion under the four ventilation modes. For objective 2 to recommend appropriate chemical suppressing agents for propane refrigerant explosion based on the above: Explosion of propane was studied by an explosion tube of maximum 25 m long at Harbin, Heilongjiang, China. Experiments were conducted in a single zone first. The explosion tube was then divided into two zones by a thin polyvinyl chloride film sheet with different mixing ratios of propane and air adjusted. Explosion phenomena and flame propagation in the tube were studied analytically using experimental results and theoretical derivation. Experimental data was compiled to justify the explosion models. Flame propagation characteristics were fitted with an exponential function on time in studying explosion analytically. A flame velocity model for explosion in an open tube was proposed and verified by the experimental data. This model was also used to calculate the flame velocity of experiments reported in the literature. It is demonstrated that the developed flame velocity model is appropriate for premixed gas deflagration up to equivalence ratio of 1 at the initial stage of flame propagation. Further explosion control experiments were then carried out to study the deflagration phenomenon to get general patterns; the differences in deflagration under different mixing ratios of propane and air; and comparison on the effectiveness of different explosion suppressants. Four fire suppressants including nitrogen, carbon dioxide, fine water mist and chemical powder were studied. Chemical powders are identified to be appropriate in suppressing clean refrigerant fires for refrigerators put in cupboards. That is because they are independent on the flame conditions and so having better suppression performance than other agents. The chemical fire extinguishing mechanisms were reviewed and summarized. Condensed phase compounds including powders of certain alkali metal compounds with gas loaded appear to achieve quicker fire suppression in small cupboards. New gas-solid composite particles composed of zeolite particles of diameter up to 2 μm and absorbed 2-bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene are also appropriate for extinguishing fires. Further, mixed-phase systems with two fire suppression agents of powders and gases are identified. Examples are halocarbon gelled dry chemicals, including monoammonium phosphate powder, thixotropically gelled with halon 1211 and 1301, sodium bicarbonate powder gelled with pentafluoropropane and hexafluoropropane. The cost of installing two sets of fire suppression systems is high in large space. However, it is very appropriate in cupboards with refrigerators. The results of the above tasks had been published in 6 journal papers and 6 conference papers on better understanding of explosions of flammable clean refrigerants leaking from ACR systems. Recommendations from this completed project were integrated with the associated literature, design guides and existing fire codes on clean refrigerants for the Hong Kong Fire Services Department to consider. The results will be applicable to the urban public in general, in Hong Kong at least; and in particular, to government and regulatory bodies dealing with building safety; and existing building owners, through better fire safety management. The potential explosion hazards of leaked flammable clean refrigerants from refrigerators stored in small cupboards were reported to the Chief Executive at the Hong Kong Institution of Engineers (HKIE) Annual Dinner on 16 March 2018, while the PI received the HKIE Gold Medal 2018. Leakage of flammable clean refrigerants would give mixing ratio with air above the lower limit easily. Any spark would give explosion. Presence of solid barriers would hinder pressure development, and deflagration to denotation (DDT) would occur. Even the explosion of a small amount of flammable clean refrigerant can be disastrous.

15203414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203414.value: It is not known how much ﬂammable clean refrigerants are in use. Use of clean refrigerants and their potential fire hazards in Hong Kong are reviewed. Low-cost flammable refrigerants including propane are surveyed to be commonly used, and becomes the essential constituent of alternative refrigerants. As propane is flammable, many alternative refrigerants which are claimed to be safe have not been approved by the authority. In small apartments in the Asia-Oceania area, many ACR units are installed in boxes or cupboards for space-saving or aesthetic reasons. Leakage of ﬂammable clean refrigerants from ACR units in those small boxes can give explosion as reported in Section 5.3. Firefighters have to get special training on ﬁres started from leaked ﬂammable refrigerants. In addition, ﬁre ofﬁcers are having difﬁculties in establishing and implementing regulations and controls for the use of ﬂammable refrigerants due to the size of the market. This is a big problem requiring time to solve. However, the immediate need is to work on appropriate ﬁre safety management for handling ﬂammable clean refrigerants. Official publications of the local authorities in Hong Kong had been searched for the cause of fire involving ventilation and air-conditioning control system or window units. However, there is no information on such type of fire which is resulted from the leakage of refrigerants. Normally, the incident commander of the fire department concluded that the cause of fire was suspected to be attributable to short circuit of electric wiring of the ventilation and air-conditioning control system or window units. Potential fire hazards of flammable clean refrigerants are surveyed to be often neglected by owners or property management staff of the buildings and maintenance contractors. There is a need to bring such concern to the attention of the stakeholders concerned. Local fire codes, including the control of use of clean refrigerants in ventilation and air-conditioning control systems, window units and packaging systems in Hong Kong are recommended to be upgraded. All these explosion hazards of flammable clean refrigerants were discussed with senior government officers including Mr. Frank Chan, Secretary for Transport and Housing, and Mr. Elvis Au, Deputy Director of Environmental Protection, Department of Environmental Protection of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government. A total of 6 journal papers and 6 conference presentations were published. Two PhD students, with partial support from this project, were graduated as listed in Section 11.

15203414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203414.value: Environmentally friendly ACR systems using flammable clean refrigerants might have explosions since 2013. More explosions are expected, as those systems are starting to deteriorate. In dense urban areas, most of the citizens live in small apartments in tall buildings. High quantities of combustibles are stored in small flats, whether they are used as residential buildings, restaurants, offices or retail shops. There is an urgent need to solve problems involving the explosion of leaked flammable refrigerants from ACR systems. This study should be extended on protecting buildings with new fire retardants; strength of dry wall; integrity of structure and building; effects of shocks on adjacent buildings; and community safety. Clean refrigerants should satisfy ordinance under the firefighting capacity and safety criteria. However, safety regulations, codes of practice and design guides on handling flammable clean refrigerants in many places have not yet been set up based on research studies. The government is recommended to take appropriate actions to protect the citizens against clean refrigerant explosions. A contingency plan should be worked out scientifically to have better control and tighter system maintenance inspection on the use of clean refrigerants through systematic research.

15203414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203414.value: Many clean refrigerants in air-conditioning and refrigeration (ACR) systems are flammable and pose fire and explosion hazards. Fires and explosions resulted from flammable clean refrigerants leaked from ACR units have been reported all over the world. This sounds an alarm on fire safety when using hydrocarbon based clean refrigerants in new environmentally friendly ACR systems. An explosion will occur when flammable clean refrigerants leak from the ACR unit, mix with air in a ratio higher than the lower flammability limit and there exists an ignition source. This project worked on combustion of leaked propane refrigerant; flame front formation; and shock formation, propagation and strength with different ventilation provisions in small flats. Completed works included modelling the leakage of propane refrigerants, estimating the leakage rates in typical arrangements of ACR units in small flats, the mixing of leaked propane with air and its spread in regions near to the leakage source, the explosion and flame spread, and the possible explosion control by discharging an appropriate suppressing agent including chemical powder. An explosion tube was used to study the possible suppression of propane explosion. Results are very useful for life safety inside spaces with ACR systems using flammable clean refrigerants.

15203914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203914.value: Representation learning, which concerns with learning representations to extract and organize discriminative information from the available data, is a recently developed and rapidly growing field in machine learning and computational intelligence. It is tightly coupled with deep learning methods which hierarchically organize multiple nonlinear transformations with the goal of yielding more abstract and ultimately more useful representations. Transfer learning, also advocated recently, deals with the scenarios that the test and training sets have similar but pretty distinct distributions. Its main challenges are “what to transfer, how to transfer, and when to transfer”. The purpose of this research is to study how these two new learning paradigms should be put together. In fact, deep representation learning is supposed to be well suited for transfer learning, due to its objective of abstract representation of the source data variations and its advantage of using layered network architecture to model out-of-distribution training examples. Thus, the challenges are (i) how to carry out transfer learning between deep layered networks and (ii) how to enhance or enrich deep learning of hierarchical representation by leveraging the knowledge from the other domains. In this project, we propose to develop methods for more effective transfer learning and/or deep representation learning, and to exploit new approaches to and benefits of combining these two learning paradigms. The problem of learning and transferring representations with data from multiple domains will be studied in the context of multi-task learning, domain adaptation learning and co-clustering. While we will formulate and devise deep representation transfer learning algorithms for these three application scenarios, attempts will be made to advance the development of these two learning paradigms. These include: (i) adding a cognitive aspect to the learning process by addressing the question of at what abstraction level (realized by deep representation learning networks) transfer learning should be carried out; and (ii) studying the theoretical problem of distance between domains/distributions. The success of this research will lead to the impact of (i) opening a new problem in transfer learning, i.e., why to transfer; and (ii) strengthening the foundation and effectiveness of both deep representation learning and transfer learning. 表示學習涉及到從可用的數據中抽取和組織鑑別信息來進行學習表示, 它是新近發展而來及快速發展的機器學習和計算智能領域。表示學習是和深度學習方法緊密相伴的。它們以層次的方式來組織多個非線性變換來產生較抽象的並最終更有用的表示。在過去的十多年來, 遷移學習也得到了鼓勵來處理測試和訓練域有相似但又不同分佈的場景。其面臨的挑戰主要是「遷移什麼, 如何遷移以及何時遷移」。本研究的目的是探討如何把這兩種新學習模式結合起來。實際上, 由於深度表示學習可以被用來抽象表達變化的源域數據並利用層次網絡結構來建模服從分佈的訓練數據，因此其被認為非常適合於遷移學習。目前面臨的挑戰是：(一) 如何執行深度的層次網絡間的遷移學習； (二) 如何利用其它域的知識來增強或豐富層次表示的深度學習。 在本項目中，我們旨在提出新的及更為有效的遷移學習及深度表示學習模式，並受益於上述兩種學習模式的結合。針對目前三種典型的遷移學習方法，即歸納式遷移、直推式遷移及無監督遷移學習，我們將主要在多任務學習、領域適應學習及協同聚類三種應用場景下探討多域數據的學習和遷移表示問題。當具體設計相關場景的深度表示遷移學習方法時, 我們將做出努力對上述兩種學習模式進行改進並產生影響。具體包括： (一) 增加應該在何種抽象層次（通過深度學習網絡來實現）來執行遷移學習方面的認知知識； (二) 研究新的領域間或領域間分佈距離的理論問題。該研究的成功所帶來的貢獻有：(一) 打開了遷移學習的一個新問題 ── 為什麼遷移？ (二) 同時增強了深度表示學習和遷移學習的基礎和有效性。

15203914.label: Realisation of objectives
15203914.value: Our first objective is to design effective deep representation learning methods that can properly share a subset of feature representations obtained from data of multiple tasks. Particularly, we aim at exploiting the hierarchical representations in deep layered network so that the question “At what abstraction level (realised by deep representation learning networks) should transfer learning be carried out?” can be addressed. Through the study of this project, it has been found that parameters in deep neural networks eventually transit from general to task-specific as the layer goes higher/deeper. The hierarchical representations have been fully exploited in developing a set of state-of-the-art deep transfer learning models (see the publications in Part C), making this objective almost fully achieved. The hierarchical representation in the popular convolutional neural network (CNN) has been studied and a layer driven transfer model has been proposed with attractive performance improvement. The research work for this objective has been carried out for quite a number of deep and traditional machine learning models. In addition to the CNN model, we also studied another popular deep learning model, i.e., the autoencoder. The layer-by-layer denoising effect of an autoencoder variant has been studied in details and some theoretical works have also been achieved. The theoretical findings have been demonstrated beneficial to develop simple and yet effective deep transfer learning models. Research for other models has been carried out and it includes the less popular graphical models like the topic model as well as the tensor model. Their deep versions have been developed and their abilities of deep representation learning have been examined. Completely based on graphical model representation, the proposed framework can seamlessly merge inference and learning, and has clear interpretability of conditional independence. Our second objective is to study and devise appropriate measure for the distance between domains in the context of domain adaptation. Based on the new distance measure, we aim at developing deep representation transfer learning methods for domain adaptation and carrying out a theoretical analysis of the learning problem involved. We consider that this objective has been fully achieved. The transferability of each particular layer in a deep neural network can be quantified and the parameters from lower-layers are applicable to both source and target tasks, while the transferability declines in higher/deeper layers. A multi-layer joint kernelized mean (MJKM) distance measure between the target data and the source data for more effective transfer of knowledge from the source domain to the target domain has been developed. In view of the difference in transferability between layers in deep network, a model incorporated with MJKM has been proposed and state-of-the-art adaptation performance has been obtained. In the work for the deep linear model, efforts have been paid to leverage the representations in multiple layers of the network models. While a theoretical study has been conducted, showing that the second moments of the source domain distribution and target domain distribution should be similar, encouraging domain adaptation performance has been obtained by the newly devised model. Our third objective is to develop deep representation transfer clustering algorithms by making good use of the feature representation learned or being learned. Different deep representation learning network models will be investigated. We also aim at studying the interpretation of feature representation obtained by the new transfer clustering algorithms. We were not able to fully complete this objective. Transfer learning without label information, i.e. the transfer clustering context, has long been considered difficult. While the performance improvement achieved by combining deep feature representation and transfer clustering has been insignificant in our study. It points out that label information is indispensable in knowledge transfer. Hence, we plan to explore a semi-supervised transfer clustering instead in the near future.

15203914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203914.value: In this project, we propose to develop methods for more effective transfer learning and/or deep representation learning, and to exploit new approaches and benefits to combine these two learning paradigms. It has been found that parameters in deep neural networks eventually transit from general to task-specific as the layer goes higher/deeper (see the reported IJCAI’17 paper and SIGIR’18 paper in Part C). The transferability of each particular layer in a deep neural network can be quantified and the parameters from lower-layers are applicable to both source and target tasks, while the transferability declines in higher/deeper layers. Therefore, the network pre-trained on source dataset is not likely to be discriminative enough when it is applied to the target dataset directly. Inspired by such characteristic of deep neural networks, we have proposed to utilize deep features extracted from the deep networks and to compute the multi-layer joint kernelized mean distance between the target data and the source data for more effective transfer of knowledge from the source domain to the target domain (see the SIGIR’18 paper). In addition, we have also found that in order to achieve good adaptation performance, the second moments of the source domain distribution and target domain distribution should be similar. Based on our new analysis, a novel extremely easy feature learning algorithm for domain adaptation has been proposed (see the IJCAI’17 paper). Furthermore, it has been found that the key of effective deep domain adaptation is to reduce effects of the discrepancy between the training data and test data. A deep learning method called Stacked Robust Adaptively Regularized Auto-regressions (SRARAs) (see the 2019 IEEE TKDE journal paper) has been proposed to learn useful representations for domain adaptation problems. Each layer of SRARAs contains two steps: a linear transformation step and a non-linear squashing transformation step. The first step can effectively reduce the discrepancy between the training data and test data and contributes to highly effective adaptation performance. While the three aforementioned papers have worked on the convolutional neural network (CNN), the deep linear model, and the autoencoder model respectively, we also studied the problem with respect to the traditional spectral clustering model (see the Pattern Recognition journal paper in Part C), the graphical model (see the ICPR’18 paper in Part C) and the topical graph models (see the CIKM’16 paper and the 2017 Neural Network journal paper).

15203914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203914.value: Deep domain adaptation or deep transfer learning has become a hot topic in recent years of machine learning research. Our findings pinpointed that the (deep) layered based representations learned by the model should have the between-domain distribution discrepancy reduced appropriately. By following this direction, the current and future deep learning models can be made more effective by devising the corresponding deep transfer learning variants. The research of this project is still on-going and our current works are based on the emerging Generative Adversarial Network model. We expect to achieve yet another milestone of state-of-the-art adaptation performance.

15203914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203914.value: Humans are good at learning based on some previous related experience, e.g., learning French based on the knowledge/experience of English. Hence, studying the deep layered representations of artificial neural networks in such kind of transfer learning setting can be influential to develop highly effective machine learning models for different data-driven artificial intelligence applications. This project studied how to learn and transfer the representations in some selected machine learning models, including the popular convolutional neural network and the autoencoder model. We found that the key is to reduce the distribution discrepancy between the domains involved, e.g., the difference between French and English. Various approaches to exploit this idea have been explored and state-of-the-art performance has been achieved by the proposed models. The project confirms the potential of deep transfer learning models and based upon which human-like performance can be expected in various tasks.

15204414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204414.value: Transmission line theory has been well developed. It is usually applied to analyze the propagation of surges as well as ac waves in multi-conductor systems. This theory is fundamental to an understanding of propagation phenomena over a line system. In practice, there exist line structures in which conductors run vertically above the ground, which can be found in electrical transmission lines, radio base stations and microstrip transmission lines as well as lightning protection systems for high-rise buildings. In such open structures there is no path for returning current. The transitional transmission line theory, therefore, is not applicable as the transverse electromagnetic (TEM) mode of propagation is not supported. This project aims at developing a traveling wave theory for the analysis of surge behavior in vertical structures, which may be caused by lightning or switching. Surges at any position along the line and at any time will be analytically determined using surge impedances, attenuation factors and propagation velocity. Both impedances and attention factors will be uniquely defined for forward and backward surges, as well as for incident, reflected and transmitted surges. Coefficients of surge reflection and transmission at line discontinuities will be provided. This project will extend the existing transmission line theory to vertical structures with non-TEM mode of propagation. The output of the research will provide a simple, efficient and intuitive time-domain solution for surges analysis of vertical structures. Surge behavior along vertical lines can be determined simply with the general knowledge of surge propagation and multiple reflections. The structures of concern contain multiple lossy conductors. They are erected on a lossy ground and terminated with a grounding network. The output could be further extended and developed for transient analysis in a high-speed digital network, and for modeling the lightning channel during a lightning return stroke. 電磁波在傳統傳輸綫上的傳播現已有一套很完善的理論。這套理論常應用于分析雷電引起的過電壓，以及交流電壓在多導體系統中的傳播。這套理論有助于對多平行綫的電磁傳播現象的深刻理解。在現實生活中，存在著大量非平行綫結構，比如垂直于在地面的直綫結構。這種綫結構常出現在電力綫路、無綫電基站和微帶 輸電綫路，以及高層建築物的雷電保護系統。這種開放的結構是沒有電流返回路徑的。因此，傳統傳輸綫理論是不適用于分析不支持橫向電磁波（TEM）傳播模式的結構。 本項目旨于導出一套用于分析垂直綫結構的行波理論，這些電磁行波可以由閃電或開關操作導致的。在垂直綫結構中，浪涌阻抗、 衰减因子和傳播速度可能隨時間和位置而變。這些隨時間和位置而變的阻抗和衰减因子將被唯一確定，電磁波在不連續處的折反射和透射係數也將被推導出來。 通過分析垂直綫結構電磁波的傳播，本項目將進一步拓展現有的傳輸綫理論。本研究將會提供一個簡單、直觀、 高效地時間域解决方案。通過簡單的浪涌傳播和折反射分析，沿垂直綫各處的浪涌可以簡單地確定下來。所關注的垂直綫結構可包含多個有損的導體，可以是竪立在有損地面上，可以與接地網絡聯結。本項目的成果可以進一步用于高速數字網絡中的瞬態分析，以及雷電閃絡通道的建模研究。

15204414.label: Realisation of objectives
15204414.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved generally. (a) Electromagnetic phenomena in a multi-conductor system are of interest in the study of electromagnetic compatibility for circuit-printed boards, communication systems, electric power systems, and even lightning protection systems in buildings. Such phenomena are analyzed using the transmission line theory if the wires are relatively long and run in parallel. Surge propagation on vertical structures is particularly important in predicting lightning overvoltage on electrical power systems as well as providing reference information for surge protection design. However, the traditional theory is not applicable to the vertical structures, as the vertical line does not support a TEM-mode wave propagation. Significant errors were observed when the traditional one is used. Note that traveling wave theory is very useful analyzing lightning transients on a transmission line. In this project, attempts have been made to develop an extended traveling wave theory for a vertical structure. This structure consists of a single conductor without any returning current path, subject to a lightning strike. This conductor can be either a free-space conductor or a grounded conductor as long as the reflected surge from the ground has not arrived. Initially, we tried the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method for studying the wave propagation, and found it was difficult to get generalized models for studying the transients on the vertical conductor. Then we introduced transient characteristic impedance of a line, similar to the transmission line, for analyzing the transient propagation. After a couple of months, we made a great advance in this area, that is, we developed a simple approach to calculate the transient impedance. It was derived using both vector potential and scalar potential on the vertical conductor. Later we further developed an analytical formula for calculating this impedance. Unlike traditional constant characteristic impedance, the transient impedance of a vertical conductor varies with position and time, and is determined by conductor radius primarily. With this transient impedance, we can describe wave propagation graphically and effectively. Because of this time/position variant impedance, the wave of current propagates with attenuation even if the conductor is lossless, while the propagation of electric potential is lossless. It is found that the transient impedance is affected by the waveform of the source. So this causes some trouble in analyzing lightning transients on the structure. To overcome this problem, we tried several waveforms (e.g., impulse function, step function, ramp function, etc.) to test the effectiveness of the theory. Later we found the ramp waveform is the most effective one. We can get the response of the lightning strike with an arbitrary waveform by using the transient impedance under a ramp current source. Later we found that there is a similarity between the configuration of a single conductor struck by lightning and that of a line dipole antenna. Then we named it extended traveling theory for a dipole antenna. (b) A practical dipole antenna may have a structure with varying wire radius or with resistive loading for broadband characteristics. Such an antenna has been widely used as a receiving antenna measuring pulse electric fields in lightning observation. A practical vertical tower has variant cross-sectional dimensions as well, e.g., a multi-stage tower in a transmission line system. All these lead to a discontinuity either in the dipole or the vertical structure. Similar to the traditional transmission line theory, transmission and reflection of a wave were introduced at the discontinuity of a line. They are determined by the characteristic impedance of the line and the equivalent impedance of connected loads. With the reflection coefficient, we are able to describe the further propagation of waves on the wire after the reflection. The conclusions were obtained initially by observation and numerical computation. However, we took more than half year to prove the theory we developed theoretically. Three different boundary conditions that the traveling wave may encounter were settled in this project. These include: lightning surge propagation (1) on a grounded vertical conductor, (2) over conductors with different radius, (3) over a lumped electric element. The expressions of the surges have been derived under the source current with a ramp waveform. Corresponding reflection coefficients were derived to describe the propagation of reflected and transmitted waves. A traveling wave model is proposed for the incident, reflected and transmitted waves. Then, with a proposed convolution technique, the surge response under an arbitrary wave-form current/voltage source is obtained. The proposed formulas have been validated with the FDTD and PEEC methods, and good agreements have been observed (c) In practical situations, the vertical structure is subject to a lightning strike. To apply the proposed traveling wave theory for analyzing lightning transients on the structure, we have to include the lightning channel in our model. The engineering model of the lightning return stroke is the one widely used in lightning protection design. In this model, the return stroke channel is considered as a straight vertical antenna. The return stroke current propagates along the channel. These models are very efficient at predicting distant lighting-induced electromagnetic fields. For the lossy ground, Green’s functions have been derived for electric current/charge dipoles with Maxwell’s equations, and simplified formulas have been provided. For the vertical conductors. The effect of lossy wire has been addressed as well by varying the resistance value of the wire in the calculation. It is found that the wire resistance could be neglected as the resistance is much less than the transient impedance of the wire. It is found again that the lossy ground can be simply replaced with the perfect ground in the analysis. In order to simulate a more actual tower configuration, we then extend the proposed traveling wave model from a single line to multiple parallel lines. Compared with the quasi-static definition of transient impedance, the full-wave definition is proposed. The time domain reflection coefficient and the propagation behavior of current are extended to multiple conductors. The proposed model is further extended to consider the multi-layer tower having legs with different radius and different spacing distance in each layer. With the proposed model, the phenomenon of lightning current surge behavior along vertical structure can be finally established mathematically. The proposed theory was validated numerically by the FDTD method, and the error was generally less than 1%.

15204414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204414.value: To shield the insights on surge propagations on a vertical conductor, we developed a traveling wave theory [J1]. In this approach, the vertical line without returning current path is characterized by transient impedance. This transient impedance varies with time and position. A simplified formula of transient impedance was derived with the assumption of ramp current excitation [J6]. By using the attenuation coefficient of current, a simple iterative method was then presented for the evaluation of surge propagation without these constraints [J1]. The iterative method was validated numerically using the PEEC method. It was found that the transient current attenuates during its propagation even on a lossless line while the transient voltage does not attenuate. Transient impedance varies with conductor radius, and is significantly affected by the waveform of the excitation. In order to address the response of a vertical structure under a lightning strick with an arbitrary waveform, an algorithm has been developed in [C3] for the conversion between different waveforms. A convolution technique has been also developed later to address the transient response under either a current source or voltage source [J6,C3]. This makes the application of the proposed theory in the antenna possible. We have addressed three different kinds of discontinuities; namely (1) ground connection, (2) change of wire radius, (3) connection of a lumped circuit element. The expressions of the surges have been addressed in [J3] for (1), in [J6,C1] for (2-3). Corresponding reflection coefficients were derived to describe the propagation of reflected and transmitted waves. A traveling wave model is proposed for the incident, reflected and transmitted waves. The proposed formulas have been validated with the FDTD and PEEC methods, and good agreements have been observed. To apply the traveling wave theory for practical cases. We developed the extended traveling wave theory for multiple parallel lines [J7]. The proposed model is further extended to consider the multi-layer tower having legs with different radius and different spacing distance in each layer, which is commonly used in the transmission line system. The effect of lightning surges propagating along a vertical structure was also addressed. The coupling effect observed in adjacent electrical circuits was addressed in [J2,C2]. Simplified formulas were for circuit modeling and transient analysis. The ground potential arising from a direct lightning strike to a tall vertical structure and others was addressed as well in [J4,C4]. It is found that the wire resistance could be neglected as the resistance is much less than the transient impedance of the wire [J3,C1]. It is found again that the lossy ground can be simply replaced with the perfect ground in the analysis [J1]. Note: J* and C* represent journal and conference papers, respectively.

15204414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204414.value: The lightning return stroke is commonly represented as a hard current source in lightning transient analysis. In this project, the propagation of a wave on the grounded tower has been well addressed under either a current source or a voltage source. It is found that the surge current in the tower is significantly different if the discontinuity at the striking point or the lightning attachment is taken into account. This issue will be further investigated and addressed in a coming project. In modeling the lightning return stroke, the physical process of a lightning flash will be taken into consideration.

15204414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204414.value: Transmission line theory has been well developed, and is fundamental to an understanding of propagation phenomena over a line. In practice, there exist line structures in which conductors run vertically above the ground or conductors without a returning path, such as dipole antennas, towers in electric power/telecommunication systems, lightning protection systems, in which the traditional theory is not applicable as the transverse electromagnetic mode of propagation is not supported. This project has developed a traveling wave theory for the analysis of surge behavior in such a structure. As this is similar to a dipole, we name it the traveling wave theory for a dipole structure. Analytical formulas of transient impedance and reflection coefficient at a discontinuity have been provided. Surges at any position along the line and at any time can be analytically determined using such parameters. This project has extended the transmission line theory to a multi-dipole structure or tower. The output of the research has provided a simple, efficient and intuitive time-domain solution for surges analysis in the dipole structures. Surge behavior along vertical lines can be determined simply with the general knowledge of surge propagation and multiple reflections.

15204614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204614.value: Healing of skin wounds plays an important role in human health. Widely used bulk gel dressings limit the breathability of new born tissues on wounds and restrict the wound healing speed. Dressings comprised of hydrogel fibers are highly desired to promote wound healing. Current hydrogel fibers fall into two groups: super absorbent staple fibers and conventional hydrogel filaments as scaffolds for cells and tissues. All these hydrogel fibers contain only a single polymer network and demonstrate poor mechanical properties, thus do not suit the dressing application that requires elasticity and integrity under frequent stretch and compression even in wet state. When they are reinforced with other strong filaments in weaving fabrics or nonwovens, the resultant blend bandages lost the transparency and elasticity of hydrogels, showed lower water absorption than the pure gel fibers. The hydrogel fibers still often break and leave residues in wounds, requiring frequent rinse and replacement. We propose here a new technique to manufacture hydrogel fibers with two polymer networks that give high toughness and elasticity, and to weave the fibers into skin adaptive bandages for the wound dressing application. Double network (DN) hydrogel fibers will be manufactured from double polymer components by creative integration of electron beam radiation into a gel spinning process. This integration enables the fast and continuous fabrication of DN structures in polymer fibers for the first time, which realizes distinguished toughness and elasticity of gel fibers in wet state. In addition, a stretch after the DN structure formation produces wet shrinkable gel fibers of high strength. These novel hydrogel fibers can be easily woven into uniaxially shrinkable bandages that provide satisfying breathability and tension for wound healing. Such bandages retain transparency, elasticity and integrity in wet state as wound dressings. They are skin adaptive wrap layers, because they uniaxially shrink upon wetting and present a mild tension over body surfaces. This novel fiber manufacturing technique is general for a variety of polymers (both natural and synthetic polymers) and applicable to various textile structures. It can promote the advancement of wide areas such as biomedical and sanitary textiles, soft optical sensors and biocompatible tough actuators. This research will offer a multiscale toolbox for the control of material properties. It will enable us to extract important information about gel toughening, fiber strengthening and wound healing mechanisms, to explore fundamental principles of soft matter enhancing, textile material processing and wound caring technologies. 皮膚傷口的癒合對人類健康至關重要。目前使用的塊狀凝膠敷料限制新生組織的呼吸作用和傷口愈合速度。由水凝膠纖維組成的透氣繃帶可以提高傷口的愈合速度。目前的水凝膠纖維有兩類：超吸水的短纖和用作細胞及組織支架的普通凝膠長纖。所有這些凝膠纖維只含單一聚合物網路，顯示較差的力學性能，因而不適合在濕態仍承受反復拉伸和擠壓的整體彈性敷料的應用。當凝膠被高強度纖維以機織布或無紡布的形式增強時，得到的複合凝膠繃帶會失去透明性和彈性，吸水率也明顯減低。這些複合凝膠纖維還會破碎並留下殘餘物在傷口上，需要頻繁更換和清理。我們計畫發展高韌性和彈性的雙網路結構水凝膠纖維製造技術，並把這些纖維織成單軸收縮的皮膚適應性的繃帶用於傷口敷料。這一技術可以帶動醫療衛生紡織品、軟光學感測器、生物相容的韌性驅動器等廣泛領域發展。這一研究可以獲得關於凝膠增韌、纖維增強和傷口癒合機理的重要資訊，從而拓展有關軟物質強化、纖維材料加工和傷口處理技術的基本規律。

15204614.label: Realisation of objectives
15204614.value: (1) To design and fabricate model hydrogels with controlled double network (DN) structures based on a basic understanding of the molecular mechanisms of ionic crosslink and radiation chemistry, clarify the contribution of covalent linkage between double networks to the toughness of hydrogel. Double network (DN) hydrogels have been synthesized from polyacrylamide (PAAm) and i-carrageenan (IC) in petri dishes. Their mechanical properties have been adjusted with changing material ratio and cross-linker concentration, in which the optimal gel composition was concluded. Based on the thermal reversibility of IC ionic network, we have quantitatively estimated the contribution of DN structure to the toughness of hydrogels by comparing the tensile behavior of DN and single network hydrogels. By stretching the gels in proceeding cycles, the contribution of sacrificial bonds to the gel toughness was analyzed, and the thermal healing performance of the stretched gels was also assessed carefully. The DN gels were also manufactured into fibers by synthesis within tube templates, which were converted into tough dry fibers by drying under tension. This dry fiber shrank to original wet shape upon wetting and showed promising shape memory property. This part of work was published in J. Mater. Chem. B 2014, 2, 7631-8. Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (2) To fabricate DN hydrogel fibers by a continuous gel spinning process integrated with electron beam radiation, investigate the magnitude of DN contribution to the toughness of 1-dimentional anisotropic materials. In order to obtain suitable microfluidic spinning devices, flexible gel fibers composed of agar and polyacrylamide networks were prepared in tube molds and used as the templates of channels. Such gel material can withstand the temperature required for thermal curing of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Channels with different cross sections and representative 3D structures were smoothly fabricated, based on the versatile manipulation of gel templates and thermal replica molding of PDMS. This part of work was published in Polymers, 2019, 11, 64. Hydrogel fibers have also been fabricated by wet spinning from commercial PAAm and carrageenan materials. The fibers were irradiated by electron beam (1.0 MeV) at wet states with different doses. The mechanical properties of resultant gel fibers were measured at wet and dry states. The stability of dry gel fibers in airs of changing humidity was also assessed, to reveal its usability in practical weather and skin conditions. This part was summarized into a manuscript too (Moisture responsive gel fibers from wet spinning and electron beam crosslinking). Hydrophilic and thermoplastic polyurethane (HTPU) consisting of crystalline polyethylene glycol (PEG) segment and hydrophobic segment was studied. This HTPU absorbed high amount of water and formed a stable hydrogel. Its tensile properties were carefully studied at different levels of swelling, which demonstrated a transition from plastic to elastomer when the water content reached 35 wt%. The shape memory performance of HTPU was assessed with heat and water stimuli. This dry fiber is stable against humid air (up to 92% RH), and easy to reserve in various environments. This work was published in J Mater Sci 2017, 52, 4421-34. Furthermore, the HTPU was combined with PAAm network by in situ polymerization. By adjusting their mass ratio and PAAm cross-link density, this DN hydrogel was obviously improved in tensile property, which also exhibited good recoverability without any hysteresis. Strong dry gel fibers with a modulus of 2.17 GPa and strength of 60 MPa were prepared from this DN hydrogel, which were also stable against humid air. This part was published in J Mater Sci, 2019, 54, online. Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (3) To strengthen the above DN gel fibers by a post stretch and addition of nano fillers based on the principles of polymer orientation and reinforcement, investigate the strengthening effects and wet shrinkage properties of resultant fibers. To obtain stronger gel fibers, chitosan has been added into spinning dopes. The dissolved chitosan changed into nanofibers when the spinning dope entered alkaline coagulation baths, which greatly increased the resultant fiber strength. Optimal spinning conditions have been deduced by adjusting the amount of chitosan in dopes. This part was prepared into a manuscript (Chemoresponsive Nanocomposite Hydrogels to Mimic the Sea Cucumber Dermis). Polyacrylamide/iota-carrageenan double-network hydrogels were further strengthened by incorporating bacterial cellulose microclusters. By extension-drying and post-annealing, strong dry strands were fabricated with tensile strength over 100 MPa. Their water-stimulated shape recovery behavior supports smart dressing application. This part has been prepared into a manuscript (Wet and dry properties of double network gels strengthened with bacterial cellulose micro clusters). Double networks were also synthesized in silk fiber swollen by LiBr solution through in situ polymerization of acrylamide or sodium acrylate. These modified silks exhibited superior water absorption and greatly improved mechanical properties in both dry and wet states. They showed low cytotoxicity towards skin keratinocytes, are suitable for wound dressing fabrication. This study was published in International Journal of Biological Macromolecules 2017, 95, 826-32. The silk fibroin (SF) was also combined with hydrogels in a core-sheath fiber by coaxial wet spinning. Double-layered hollow structure was observed in these fibers. They demonstrated higher absorbency and porous structure in side wall, suitable for water management and drug release control. This work was published in ACS Biomater. Sci. Eng. 2019, 56, 3119-30. Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (4) To construct uniaxially shrinkable bandages out of the above DN gel fibers by weaving, investigate the contributions of different gel fibers to the skin adaptive properties of bandages. The above radiation crosslinked hydrogel fibers were converted into dry gel fibers: stretch-1 and stretch-2, according to our proposed approach. Woven fabrics were fabricated on a manually operated weaving instrument. This dry fabric was cut into narrow bandages, sterilized under UV lamp and applied to the open wound of rat skin, where saline solution was dropped. Commercial hydrogel pads were also applied to similar rat wounds for comparison. The fiber swelling, pour closing and warp direction shrinkage of woven bandages were observed under. Compared to the hydrogel pads, this woven bandage presented not only suitable transparency, but also dynamic adaption upon wetting and improved breathability and comfort allowing faster healing process. This part was involved in a manuscript (Skin adaptive antibacterial wound dressings composed of water responsive gel fibers). Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (5) To functionalize the above skin adaptive bandages with durable antibacterial reagents, investigate the relationship between dressing structures and wound healing mechanisms by assessing different bandages on rat cutaneous wounds. The antibacterial modification of poly(ethyleneglycol) methyl ether (mPEG)-poly(caprolactone) (PCL)-mPEG was achieved with bis(2-hydroxyethyl) methylammonium chloride (DMA). At an appropriate substitution degree, the DMA unit rendered the copolymer highly antibacterial, and did not alter its thermosensitivity, non-cytotoxicity, and drug release control. Thus obtained hydrogels presented satisfying immunity to microorganisms, which was published in Colloids and Surfaces B: Biointerfaces 2016, 143, 342-51. The above antibacterial copolymer was also incorporated into the gel fiber networks of woven bandages, and allowed the quick healing of rat cutaneous wounds without any infections, which was obviously superior to the commercial hydrogel pads. This part was involved in the manuscript (Skin adaptive antibacterial wound dressings composed of water responsive gel fibers). Thus, this objective was fully achieved.
