15204614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204614.value: The contribution of second network to the hydrogel toughness has been quantitatively identified. In addition to common materials for hydrogel synthesis (like polyacrylamide and polysaccharides), hydrophilic polyurethane was identified as a promising hydrogel material, which is easier to process and more reliable in application. Based on our systematic study on double network hydrogels, we were invited to contribute a review paper to the special issue: J Polym Sci, B: Polym Phys 2018, 56, 1325–35. A pater was awarded the Chen Weiji Prize by the China Textile Engineering Society, 2014. Robust shape memory gel fibers and smart wound dressings have been fabricated. Chitosan and bacterial cellulose microcluster were successfully incorporated into hydrogel fibers as reinforcement. Additionally, silk fibroin was combined with hydrogels in two new approaches: polymerization in swollen silk, and coaxial wet spinning. Thus obtained gel fibers presented outstanding mechanical and water management properties. A Chinese patent was authorized based on our invention on the Preparation of novel hydrogel fibers of high toughness (ZL201310589034.4, granted: 04-Jan-2017). Based on our well recognized expertise on functional fibers, we were invited to contribute a chapter to the handbook: Engineering of High-Performance Textiles, Edited by Menghe Miao and John Xin. Woodhead / Elsevier UK, 2018, Page 32 out of 544. Totally, this project has produced 8 published papers, 4 manuscripts in submission, 1 patent, 1 book chapter, 8 conference papers, 1 prize, and two PhD theses (refer to Section C).

15204614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204614.value: Besides the proposed shape memory gel fibers and smart wound dressing, versatile core-sheath fibers were also fabricated from silk fibroin and hydrogels. More functions will be explored for this type of core-sheath fibers by adding different functional reagents inside.

15204614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204614.value: The research project is a study looking at a new approach to promote cutaneous wound healing with smart gel woven bandages. It involves the synthesis of double network hydrogels, fabrication of dry gel filaments, and characterization of their particular tensile properties as well as water stimulated shape recovery. A comprehensive analysis is undertaken to see the capabilities and relationships of different polymers, additives, and processing techniques in relation to such properties concerned. Traditional hydrogel wound dressings may impart moisture protection to cutaneous wounds at the expense of breathability. Significant reduction in breathability may overtake their moisture advantages, which in turn lower the wound healing rate. Different from the traditional hydrogel pads, the new smart dressing developed here is water responsive, where the woven bandage will close up its pores only when water is provided. The breathable characteristic is of particularly importance for the dressing that allows the skin cells to proliferate fast in abundant oxygen. The “smart” gel woven dressing can be applied to promote cutaneous wound healing but not limited to this case. The successful outcomes represent a product innovation and definitely trigger the development of a new generation biomedical textiles.

15205014.label: Project Objectives
15205014.value: To develop a dynamic vector-hysteresis macroscopic model based on micromagnetics for core loss computation in electromagnetic devices. The proposed effective modeling method will not only have the versatility and precision of micromagnetics, but also allow fast implementation to obtain macro magnetization characteristics, such as magnetization curves and core losses. To implement a seamless coupling between the finite element computation of the electromagnetic field and the hysteresis model. The designers will have a transparent, unified approach to precisely determine the magnetic field distribution in magnetic cores and compute the core losses of the electromagnetic devices in a user-friendly manner. An integrated and standardized approach will form a solid foundation for commercial applications.

15205014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205014.value: 用於電磁場，電路以及機械運動耦合分析的數值方法業已成為分析乃至設計電磁裝置之有力工具。然而當前並無普適而精確的方法以計及磁芯的鐵耗，此一缺失寔已影響上述方法的有效性。然則磁芯乃多數電磁裝置不可或缺之部件，即或鐵耗的些許缩减必當導致電能消耗的巨額节省。此外，鐵耗所致之熱能耗散不僅造成器材的熱損傷，亦對材料性能有負面影響。為解決前述問題，鐵耗的精確分析及其重要。 在常規運行條件下，通常採用實驗數據，經驗公式與插值模型來估計鐵耗。然而，由於功率電子技術的流行，藉複雜之磁場波形與高階諧波，於鐵耗仿真引發出前所未有之挑戰，此蓋因舊有之方式不足以精確預測鐵耗。鐵耗的精確計算有賴于任意外場下磁芯動態磁滯的模擬。而堪能表述不同場合下磁芯行為的模型，當具有物理機制。借由磁化過程不同的物理洞見，已有眾多研究得以提出，從而能以极少的參數描述觀測結果。由于此等研究為一多學科課題，涵蓋凝聚態物理，材料工程以及電磁學，多數已有的模型均混有似是而非之假設以及過度簡化之推導。為克服此類困難，基於微磁學的第一原理模型已於介觀尺度獲精確構建。微磁學理論以系統自由能的變分極小來表述磁化強度的動力學特性。部分磁滯即由此变分的多重局部極小所決定。然而，因自旋間交換能以及靜磁場能具有不同作用範圍，微磁學之直接應用被限於納米至微米尺度。故需一溝通介觀至宏觀尺度之方法，此即構成本申請項目之主要課題。 於本課題中，擬提出一基於微磁學之鐵耗模型，當用於分析電磁裝置時需完備而可行。鐵耗之各成分，諸如靜態磁滯損耗，渦流損耗，以及異常或附加損耗，將自然納入模型中。此方案關鍵之優點在於既保有電磁學之精確，又避免昂貴之計算負擔。為達成此目的，有限元方法將用於大尺度下微磁學之漸進表述。這一漸進表述能對原有之空間多尺度問題實施成功降階，其中大量冗餘信息得以濾除。故此方法必能快速而有效。一俟獲此變分問題之解，磁化強度的演化即可獲知。就電機工程常用工作頻段而言，磁化強度的瞬態大可忽略，然后可考慮一似穩態近似，構成慢動力學以進一步簡化計算。繼而取一宏觀釘扎統計模型耦合於有限元表述以計及微磁學不易解釋之部分磁滯。一高效參數辨識方法亦將提出。最終計算結果將與实验數據相比較，而鐵耗模型將嵌入有限元模型從而廣泛用於電磁裝置之設計優化。

15205014.label: Realisation of objectives
15205014.value: The project objectives have been achieved. The dynamic vector-hysteresis macroscopic modeling has been developed. In the case of electrical engineering, the fast dynamics, such as aftereffect and accommodation, is trifling. Hence, the rate-independent vector hysteresis is of the first importance. Moreover, although it is believed that the interaction between the diffusive magnetic field in the conducting medium and the rate-independent vector hysteresis could fully describe the core losses, the computational burden is unaffordable. To develop an engineering model, the eddy current loss is evaluated via Maxwell’s equations and the excess loss is evaluated by means of the statistical loss theory, respectively. To develop a rate-independent vector-hysteresis model based on micromagnetics in the large-scale (macroscopic) ferromagnetic body, we spent much time on understanding the fundamental physics in ferromagnetic materials. Our experience proves that, condensed matter physics, even micromagnetics, cannot be solely used to solve the real-world problem. A phenomenological approach is a necessary ingredient to improve the accuracy. As far as the origin of the hysteresis concerned, the exchange energy and the energy loss due to pinning effect must be taken into account. The former is estimated in the mean-field limit, which is still physically justified, but the latter must be carefully treated using fitting and interpolating. Combing these effects into an energy framework, we can always get a satisfying hysteresis modeling in general operating regimes. Specifically, the ideal magnetization curve is first constructed in terms of equilibrium statistical mechanics. At next step, the energy loss due to pinning effects is included by means of energy conservation. The modeling of pinning effect is flexible. A lumped pinning field leads to an improved Jiles-Atherton model, whereas a distributed dry-friction field a generalized play-type model. As for the excess loss in the loss separation framework, it is proved that the original form could provide precisely prediction, but it is usually oversimplified because of complicated parameter identification. After the implementation of a sophisticated parameter identification procedure, this difficulty is circumvented. To determine the magnetic field distribution in electromagnetic devices, a 3-D finite-element formulation based on an edge element and a novel Coulomb gauge is developed. Simultaneously, to implement a seamless coupling between the finite element computation of the electromagnetic field and the hysteresis model, a stable and efficient iteration algorithm for solving highly nonlinear magnetic field problems is proposed. The classical Newton-Raphson method usually fails to converge in this problem. To guarantee the convergence, the successive quadratic programming of the squared residual using Brent’s method and the two-scale time-stepping scheme, are employed. The developed core loss estimation method is applied to design electromagnetic devices such as electric motors, electric generators and magnetic gears.

15205014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205014.value: Classical loss separation has been carefully examined and extended. The findings are summarized as: (1) The framework of loss separation still works well in general scenarios, i.e., core losses due to vector applied field and high frequencies. (2) The eddy current loss should take the skin-effect and the nonlinear magnetic characteristic of the medium into account; (3) the access loss derived from statistical loss theory should not be simplified in the classical form. As aforementioned, the rate-independent vector hysteresis modeling is of the central interest. Based on the simplification of micromagnetics and certain postulations of pinning fields, the macroscopic averaged magnetization can be derived. It is found that: (1) Given the mean-field approach, the canonical distribution can naturally give rise to the anhysteretic part of the vector Jiles-Atherton model and the vector play model; on the other hand, (2) in the zero-temperature limit, adding the variable dry-friction pinning field to simulate the potential wells in the system, a vector play type modeling is obtained, which is equivalent to the classic Preisach model in the case of scalar hysteresis; De facto, the play model and Jiles-Atherton models are only special case of the general model. And, since different pinning field mechanisms are used, it seems that, the play model is more suitable for the modeling of the hard magnetic material, and Jiles-Atherton model is a satisfying candidate for soft magnetic materials. Somehow, Jiles-Atherton model can be regarded as a perturbation of the play model; no doubt the Jiles-Atherton model is oversimplified, but it is prevailing due to its efficient implementation. (3) The resulting models, not only obey the properties of rotational hysteresis loss, but are fast and efficient modeling. In the real-world applications of pertaining hysteresis, another challenging is the coupling between the hysteresis modeling and the finite element method. The conventional fixed-point solver sacrifices too much computational overhead to keep convergence. The better solution is to make an adaptive compromise between the convergence and efficiency. To achieve this goal, we found that the famous Newton-Raphson iteration still works, if it is combined with multi-scale time-stepping scheme. Firstly, the successive quadratic function approximation of the squared residual using Brent’s method (a type of trust-region methodology) is used to relax the Newton-Raphson iteration. Secondly, two time-stepping scales are used in finite element method and the hysteresis modeling, respectively. A PhD student, LIN Qifang (Registration Date :29 Sept 2016. Normal Study End : 04 Dec 2020) was trained by the support of this project during the period : 3 Oct 2017 – 30 Jun 2018. Her work is to apply the coreloss computation method to design of electric machines.

15205014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205014.value: As is well known, hysteresis actually belongs to non-equilibrium phenomenon. In this project, it is approximately treated by means of equilibrium statistical mechanics. If we use Planck-Fork equation to describe the dynamics of the magnetization process, it can be formulated as a level-crossing problem. The multiscale analysis of the governing equation might give a promising microscopic physical interpretation of the loss separation. Another possible development is to conduct the bifurcation analysis of the Landau-Lifschitz equation. The resulting reduced form derived by means of central manifold theorem preserves the critical point of the system. This is a good starting point to investigate the Barkhaussen effects. Detailed analysis of Barkhaussen effect is very useful since it is believed that the superposition of Barkhaussen jump gives a representation of dynamic magnetic hysteresis. It also has useful applications , such as indestructive testing.

15205014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205014.value: A novel vector hysteresis modeling is deduced based on the micromagnetics and statistical mechanics directly. This model can be degenerated into classical hysteresis modeling under certain postulations, i.e., phenomenological modeling of pinning field due to dislocations, grain boundaries, and stresses, etc. In addition, the proposed model gives a guideline to improve the classical models. While the ferromagnetic body is subjected to arbitrary applied field in general case, the proposed model still works fairly well. On the basis of the vector hysteresis modeling, a more detailed core loss estimation using loss separation is proposed. This gives an accurate core loss separation in various situations. A detailed computation requires the coupling of the Maxwell’s equations and the hysteresis modeling. Up to now, this detailed computation easily fails to converge and computationally complicated. The proposed solver overcomes this problem: the famous classical solve is conserved and relaxed to guarantee convergence, namely, a fast and efficient algorithm to solve electromagnetic problem including hysteresis phenomenon is established.

15205214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205214.value: Since 1980s, the rapid economic development in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) in South China has led to a tremendous increase of energy consumption, resulting in regional air pollution. Hong Kong and the PRD are heavily impacted by photochemical ozone (O3) and secondary organic aerosols pollution, which imposes adverse effects on human health and the environment. With subtropical climate and coastal features, Hong Kong is often under the influence of both continental and maritime air masses. Moreover, complex topography and land-use, mesoscale circulations like sea-land breezes, mountain-valley breezes and urban heat island circulations could play significant roles in transporting, redistributing and mixing urban plumes. Although many air pollution studies have been carried out in South China, all of these studies were undertaken at inland locations on the continent, which may not truly reflect the interaction between continental anthropogenic emissions and the marine boundary layer. Our knowledge on some key scientific issues in this coastal region, such as photochemistry of air pollutants downwind of the emission sources, long-range transport of air pollution from inland China to the South China Sea and the coastal PRD region, and the association between mesoscale recirculation and air pollutants over coastal region is still unclear. Therefore, there is an urgent need to characterize the interaction between continental anthropogenic emissions and marine environment over the South China Sea and subtropical continental regions. The proposed research will be carried out in two stages; first, intensive field campaign scheduled in the fall of 2014 will be conducted to measure atmospheric air pollutants and meteorological conditions around the estuary of the Pearl River. The field experiment will be conducted at 2 sampling locations near the estuary (Tung Chung, Hong Kong; Neilingding Island, Guangdong) to measure the atmospheric chemical composition and abundance. This will be followed by a comprehensive analysis of the chemical database using a combination of statistical analysis of field observations, mesoscale meteorological simulations, diagnostic and prognostic box models, i.e. an observation-based box model, an emission-based model, and chemical transport models. The proposed study will significantly improve our understanding of photochemical formation and transport mechanisms for subtropical coastal regions with complex coupling of meteorology and chemistry, and will advance our knowledge of the atmospheric chemistry in the marine boundary and have wide implications for other subtropical coastal regions. The scientific findings will have direct policy implications for reducing O3 pollution and visibility degradation in subtropical South China. 20世紀80年代以來，隨著中國南部珠江三角洲（珠三角）經濟快速發展，能源消耗急劇增加，從而導致區域空氣污染。多年來，香港和珠三角飽受光化學臭氧和二次有機氣溶膠的污染。而這些污染物對人體健康和環境均造成不良影響。因其亞熱帶氣候和沿海功能，香港常年受到陸地和海洋氣團的影響。而且，複雜的地形和土地利用，中尺度環流如海陸風和山谷風，以及城市熱島環流都會影響污染氣團的遷移，擴散和混合。儘管在華南地區進行了大量的相關研究，所有這些工作都是在大陸內陸地區完成，因而可能不能真實反映出陸地人為排放和海洋邊界層之間的相互作用。我們對這一地區一些關鍵的科學問題尚不了解，比如排放源下風向處空氣污染物的光化學機制，污染物從中國內陸到南中國海及珠三角沿海的長距離輸送，以及中尺度環流和沿海地區空氣污染物的相互關係。因此，迫切需要研究陸地人為源排放與南中國海及其沿海地區的海洋環境之間相互作用。 本研究項目將分兩步進行：首先於2015年秋季在珠江口及香港陸地同步進行密集空氣污染物和氣象數據的採集。然後利用數據統計方法，光化學箱式模型和化學遷移模型等手段對採樣數據進行全面的分析。本項目將顯著提高我們對在復雜氣象和化學耦合條件下的亞熱帶沿海地區的光化學形成和傳輸機制的了解，並會增進我們對海洋邊界大氣化學的認知。同時，有助於對其他亞熱帶沿海地區的了解和研究。本項目的科學發現將對降低華南臭氧污染和能見度惡化有著直接的政策影響。

15205214.label: Realisation of objectives
15205214.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The achievements are shown as follows. • The photochemical O3 pollution was investigated at a suburban site (Tung Chung, TC) on the east bank of Pearl River Estuary (PRE) in Hong Kong and a rural site on the west bank (Qi’ao island, QAI) in Zhuhai, Guangdong province through the analysis of spatial-temporal variations of O3 and its precursors, diurnal profiles and descriptive statistics. • The impacts of different O3 precursors and individual VOC species on O3 episode days and non-episode days were investigated by using the photochemical box model incorporating the Master Chemical Mechanism (PBM-MCM). The spatial distribution of chemical production rate for O3 over PRD was simulated by WRF-CMAQ. • The characteristics of mesoscale circulations over PRE were determined, and their impact on air pollutants over PRE and its coast (including western Hong Kong) was explored by WRF-CMAQ. • The formation mechanism of photochemical O3 was investigated comprehensively using the PBM-MCM model and compared with the field measurement data accordingly. The simulation results of O3 and NO2 were validated by the statistics at eight suburban sites in PRD. In addition, the simulated meteorological parameters were also well reproduced compared to seven observation sites in South China.

15205214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205214.value: • Three and sixteen O3 episode days were captured at TC and QAI, respectively, which were mostly associated with tropical cyclones (typhoons) and continental anticyclones. • O3 concentrations are usually higher at downwind locations. Hence, TC suffered severer O3 pollution with northwesterly winds, while QAI experienced higher O3 concentrations with prevailing northeasterly winds. • The frequent downdrafts were found over PRE due to thermal discrepancies between land and water areas. The horizontal divergent wind fields were formed following the downdrafts, which resulted in the local breezes in PRE region. • O3 and O3 precursors were accumulated due to the combination of local breezes and synoptic winds over PRE. This provided the intensive production of O3 in presence of favorable meteorological conditions and less NO titration. The chemical production rates over PRE were even higher than those in the surrounding land areas. • The combination of sea breezes and background winds further accumulated air pollutants in the coast of PRD. Besides, the sea breezes returned the aged air masses from South China Sea to the coast, which resulted in increase of O3 with a level of 11.71±2.58 ppbv at TC and 15.48±3.26 ppbv at QAI at night time. • Among the sampling period, VOC samples were collected on 17 selective days including 8 O3 episode days and 9 non-episode days. The O3 episodes days were solely captured at QAI when northeasterly winds prevailed. Besides, the TVOCs at QAI (23.45±0.82 ppbv) were much higher than that at TC (12.73±1.00 ppbv). • In comparison, the O3 production rate at QAI (1.14±0.03 x 108 molecules cm-3 s-1) were much larger than TC (7.67±0.19 x 107 molecules cm-3 s-1) during the 8 O3 episode days, implying more effective production of O3 at QAI. In addition, QAI had larger mixing ratios of oxidative radicals, i.e., OH and HO2, and higher recycling rates of the radicals than those at TC. • The production of O3 was VOC-limited (relative incremental reactivity of NOx was negative) at TC during the sampling period, but it was either VOC-limited or transition (even NOx-limited) under different cases at QAI. • Formaldehyde, tetramethylbenzenes and xylenes were the top 3 VOCs with the highest potentials of modulating local O3 production at QAI on episodes, while those at TC were formaldehyde, xylenes and acetaldehyde, irrespective of episode or non-episode days.

15205214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205214.value: More sampling measurements on O3 episode days with northwesterly winds are proposed to investigate the transport of air pollution from inland cities of Pearl River Delta (PRD) to Hong Kong. The developed PBM-MCM photochemical box model can be further improved by applying “spin-up” time to get the radical intermediate steady and thus eliminate the slight underestimation of the simulated O3 without “spin-up” operation. For each daily simulation, the interval between each input of the measured data injected into the model can be shortened from 1 hour to 200 seconds, so that it would be more accurate to simulate the in-situ photochemical reactions. Moreover, the higher resolution of terrain and land cover data over PRD can be applied in WRF to further improve the simulation in the future.

15205214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205214.value: As one of the key areas in South China, Pearl River Estuary (PRE) is experiencing severe photochemical air pollution. This project characterised O3 and its precursors on the two banks of PRE. O3 concentrations are usually higher at downwind locations. Hence, TC suffered severer O3 pollution with northwesterly winds, while QAI experienced higher O3 concentrations with prevailing northeasterly winds. Moreover, higher O3 days occurrence was observed at the west bank (QAI) than that at the east bank (TC) due to more frequent northeasterly winds. The chemical transport model revealed that the interception of background winds generated by the horizontal air flow after the downdrafts resulted in a convergence zone over PRE, leading to accumulation of great amount of O3 and its precursors transported from upwind locations. Consequently, the air pollutants trapped over PRE provided sufficient O3 precursors for photochemical reactions. The extensive photochemical reactions would result in more locally-produced O3 with less NO titration because of almost zero emissions of NO over PRE. This study deepened our understandings on the formation and accumulation of O3 over PRE, which can be deemed as an O3 “pool” in South China according to the analysis. To control the O3 pollution in PRE, we should conduct measures not only in Hong Kong but also in mainland China where O3 is still increasing in most of the territories.

15205514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205514.value: Auxetic fabrics are fabrics having a negative Poisson’s ratio. Opposite to conventional fabrics, auxetic fabrics laterally expand when stretched. This unusual behavior makes them very attractive in garment use with reduced garment pressure on the skin and better shape fit with the human body. The most important point to the realization of the auxetic fabrics is the proper design of their structures and manufacturing processes. A survey of the literature has shown that auxetic fabrics so far developed are only based on knitted structures. Therefore, there is a need to conduct a study on auxetic fabrics based on woven structures to get a basic understanding of auxetic behavior, physical and mechanical properties as well as manufacturing process of such a kind of auxetic fabric structures. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of the structure and mechanical behaviors of auxetic woven fabrics which are formed by modification of their yarn crimping directions and degree. Based on previous studies done by the PI, a special manufacturing process will be developed to fabricate this kind of non-conventional fabrics. Various auxetic woven fabric samples will be produced using different kinds of thermoplastic fibers and structural parameters. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be conducted to investigate their auxetic behavior, physical and mechanical properties. A wearing performance study of the auxetic woven fabrics will also be carried out based on the measurement of fabric pressures and shape fit of fauxetic fabrics on a spherical surface. 拉脹織物具有負的泊松比。與普通織物不同，拉脹織物在受拉伸時會發生側向膨脹。這種特性使得拉脹織物特別適合服用以降低服裝對皮膚的壓力並更好地貼合人體。為了成功織造拉脹織物，最為重要的是合理設計織物結構和織造過程。文獻表明目前拉脹織物的開發只局限於針織結構。因此，有必要開展基於機織結構的拉脹織物研究，從而對這類織物的拉脹行為，物理力學行為和織造過程有壹個基本的了解。 具體地講，本項目將通過改變紗線屈曲方向和程度來制成拉脹機織物，並研究其結構與力學行為的基礎問題。基於研究負責人的前期研究，本項目將開發壹種特殊的織造過程用於生產這類特別的織物。使用不同類型的熱塑性纖維和織物結構參數來織造多種具有拉脹特性的機織物樣品。並通過理論與實驗研究來分析這些織物的拉脹行為，物理與力學性能。本項目也將通過將這類織物置於球面上來測量織物的壓力和適形性來評價這類織物的服用性能。

15205514.label: Realisation of objectives
15205514.value: Objective 1: This objective has been totally achieved. A new class of auxetic woven structure was successfully developed based on a novel concept in which elastic and non-elastic yarns were used to produce auxetic behavior based on both foldable and reentrant honeycomb geometries due to different shrinkage effects. This concept is different from the initially proposed concept in which auxetic behavior of the woven fabric structure is only obtained via an extra heat-setting process to change the crimping directions of weft and warp yarns. Compared to the initially proposed concept, the new concept is easier realized with weaving process and the extra heat-setting process is no longer needed. Meanwhile, the relationships between the auxetic effect and the geometrical architecture of the woven structure were studied and established. Objective 2: This objective has totally been achieved. Various weaving processes were specially developed to fabricate auxetic woven fabrics by using both elastic and non-elastic yarns based on the auxetic woven structures developed in Objective 1. A difficulty was encountered during the beam preparation when the elastic yarns were used as warp yarns. This problem was solved with the use of a sizing process of elastic yarns. Based on the weaving processes developed, a series of uni- and bi-stretch auxetic woven fabrics with negative Poisson’s ratio behavior in both weft and warp directions were successfully produced on a Dobby weaving machine with two separate beams to better control yarn tension during weaving process. To protect the new technology developed, an invention patent entitled “Auxetic woven fabrics and relevant fabrication method” has been granted in China. Objective 3: This objective has totally been achieved. All auxetic woven fabrics produced were tested using an Instron 5566 tester. For the uni-stretch woven fabrics, the tensile tests were mainly conducted in the extensible direction while for the bi-stretch woven fabrics, tensile tests were conducted in both weft and warp directions. During all the tests, a camera with high resolution was employed to record the deformation process of samples. Based on the videos recoded by the camera, the data in size changes of fabric samples were extracted for the calculation of Poisson’s ratio values and fabric deformations at different tensile strains were analyzed to understand the deformation mechanisms of fabrics. Meanwhile, other physical properties of the produced fabrics such as air permeability and elastic recovery were also tested. Objective 4: This objective has totally been achieved. A geometrical model for the woven fabric structure with the reentrant geometry was established based on the testing results and observations of microstructures of auxetic woven fabrics under different tensile strains. Two semi-empirical equations were successfully developed to theoretically calculate Poisson’s ratio values of auxteic fabrics when stretched in weft and warp directions. Meanwhile, a finite element model was established for the zig-zag foldable geometry to simulate the influences of different micro-parameters on the auxetic behavior. All these models can be used to guide the design and fabrication of the new auxetic woven fabrics with predefined auxetic properties.

15205514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205514.value: 1. New auxetic woven structures and manufacturing processes developed to produce uni- and bi-stretch auxetic woven fabrics by using non-auxetic elastic and non-elastic yarns and combination of loose and tight weaves. It is found that different auxetic structures including foldable geometries and reentrant hexagons can be achieved into woven fabrics by creating different shrinkage effects. The study has provided a new approach to produce auxetic woven fabrics with a simple way and low costs by using conventional weaving machinery (Please refer to the patent and publications 1-3 as attached in Part C). 2. The auxetic behavior of the auxetic yarn woven fabrics is strain-dependent. All the experimental studies have confirmed that the auxetic behavior of the auxetic woven fabrics decreases with increase of the tensile strain. It is also found that all the woven fabrics have different auxetic behaiors in weft and warp directions and the fabrics developed based on foldable geometries and reentrant hexagons have better auxetic behavior when stretched in warp direction than stretched in weft direction (Please refer to publications 2 and 3 attached in Part C). 3. The geometrical model and semi-empirical equations developed to theoretically calculate the Poisson’s ratio values of the auxetic woven fabric based on reentrant hexagonal geometry for given tensile strain and initial structural parameters in both weft and warp directions. It is found that the auxetic behavior of the fabric structure is greatly affected by the horizontal and diagonal rib lengths and the angle formed between them. While both the horizontal and diagonal rib have different variation trends when stretched in the warp and weft directions, an increase in the angle formed between them will lead to an increase of the auxetic effect of the fabric. (Please refer to publication 4 attached in Part C). 4. Finite element model developed to simulate the deformation behavior of the foldable geometry used for developing auxetic woven fabrics. (Please refer to publication 5 attached in Part C). 5. Five refereed journal papers, one invention patent, one chapter book and four oral presentations at international conferences.

Finite element method will continuously be used for further simulating the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of auxetic woven fabrics under different loading conditions.

15205514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205514.value: This research project is concerned with a systematic study of auxetic woven fabrics which expand when stretched. The auxetic woven fabrics are first designed and fabricated based on different auxetic geometries by using elastic and non-elastic yarns and special weaving processes. Then, the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the woven fabrics produced under tensile loading conditions are experimentally and theoretically studied. Geometrical and finite element models are finally developed to predict the deformation behavior of this special type of fabrics. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characteristics, formation principle, manufacturing method and deformation behavior of auxetic woven fabrics. Thanks to their unusual properties different from conventional woven fabrics, the auxetic woven fabrics developed will enable new applications in functional clothing such as tight wear, sportswear and maternity wear with better shape fitting and comfort. The study will promote the new development of textile products using the latest concept and technologies to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and fashion industry.

15205714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205714.value: Photonic crystals with periodic structures are able to trap and confine photons and are hence expected to have a wide range of important applications. Research on photonic crystals with quasi-periodic structures is greatly hampered by the difficulties encountered in the fabrication of structures with a complex spatial variation. Here we propose to fabricate the quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane using electrochemical anodization on Ti substrates. The quasi-periodic structural variation of the membrane will be accurately controlled by current pulses, which determine the amount of Ti metal substrate to be oxidized. To demonstrate the possible applications of the electrochemically anodized quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal, we will use it as a full-spectrum reflector in dye-sensitized solar cells to enhance the solar light harvesting. Both experimental and theoretical work will be conducted to study the mechanism of light harvesting enhancement and to find ways to optimize the quasi-periodic structure for light harvesting purpose. Considering the multifunctional nature of TiO2 and the flexibility of the hole-through nanotube membrane, it is reasonable to believe that the fabricated quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane will find its vast applications not only in optics, but also in much wider and more attractive areas where the optical properties of quasi-periodic photonic crystals and the multi-functionalities of TiO2 are uniquely and wisely integrated. 具有周期性結構的光子晶體由于其獨特的光子俘獲本領所帶來 的“陷光”效應，從而有著廣泛的應用前景。而具有准周期結構 的光子晶體的研究則由于其制備工藝的複雜，受到了很大的阻 礙。在此我們提出了用電化學陽極氧化的方法在钛片上制備具 有准周期結構的二氧化钛納米管光子晶體薄膜，其准周期結構 可以通過電流脈衝精確控制钛的氧化來實現。爲了演示其應用 前景，我們將把它應用于染料敏化太陽能電池，以實現全光譜 太陽能捕獲，其光捕獲的機理將通過一系列的理論和實驗加以 研究，從而尋找進一步優化其結構的方法。由于二氧化钛本身 所具有的多功能性以及貫通納米管薄膜所具有的柔性，我們堅 信該准周期光子晶體薄膜不僅在光學，還在其他更吸引人的領 域有著更廣闊的應用前景。

15205714.label: Realisation of objectives
15205714.value: All the objectives are 100% achieved. 1. To fabricate quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane by electrochemical anodization: Electrochemical anodization was used to fabricate the quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal. In order to achieve the desired optical properties, the spatial variation of the quasi-periodic structure was precisely controlled. A time-diminishing current pulse anodization method was used. During the anodization, the low current pulse duration was fixed while the high current pulse duration follows a relation, tn=t1-(n-1)d, where d is the common difference of the arithmetic sequence, and t1 is the time duration for the first high current pulse. The TiO2 nanotube arrays fabricated in this way showed an arithmetic sequence in the variation of the structure along the axial direction of the nanotubes. Various other types of anodization parameters, such as, the electrolyte composition, the anodization temperature, and voltage/current pulse, were optimized in order to obtain a clear-cut structure with well-defined structural parameters. 2. To study the optical properties of the quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane and relate its properties to the structure: The optical properties of the fabricated quasi-periodic photonic crystal are crucial to the success of the solar light capture. The reflectance and transmittance of the TiO2 nanotube membrane with different structural parameters were studied and compared by the UV-Vis spectroscopy measurement. To simulate the actual working condition of a solar cell, the reflectance and transmittance of the TiO2 nanotube membrane immersed in electrolyte were also measured. The measured data were compared with the theoretically calculated spectra to build the structure-property relationship. 3. To apply the fabricated quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane to dye-sensitized solar cells to achieve full-spectrum light harvesting: The electrochemically anodized quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane was self-detached from the Ti substrate using a well-established method developed in our lab. The nanotube membrane thus obtained was open at both ends which facilitates the easy infiltration of electrolyte. It was then glued to the FTO transparent electrode by annealing, with the doctor-bladed TiO2 nanoparticle absorbing layer acting as the glue. The glued photoanode was then soaked in a solvent containing the N719 dye molecules at 60 degree C for 24 h. Rinsing in pure ethanol was followed to remove non-chemisorbed dye. The photoanode and the Pt-coated counter electrode were assembled into a sandwich type cell with a spacer put in between to avoid short-circuit. The cell was finally sealed with UV epoxy for various kinds of solar cell characterizations. 4. To calculate the optical band structure, reflectance and transmittance of quasi-periodic photonic crystal and to predict the power conversion efficiency enhancement of the solar cell by using theoretical simulation: Finite-element full wave simulation was used to study the optical properties of the synthesized quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane. The TiO2 nanotubes was arranged in a hexagonal lattice with the tube diameter, tube wall thickness, tube length and axial geometry all determined from SEM images. The reflectance and transmittance of the nanotube membrane was studied and the distribution of the optical field in the quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane was calculated in order to explore the mechanism of light harvesting enhancement. From the calculated reflectance spectrum we can easily conclude that the width and position of the reflectance peak depend on the number of unit cells and the initial period. To evaluate the performance of a DSSC coupled by a quasi-periodic photonic crystal, we calculated the photocurrent enhancement ΔJsc/Jsc based on the parameters including LHE(λ) and LHEref(λ) (which are the wavelength dependent absorptances of a DSSC coupled with a quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane and a reference DSSC, respectively), and the incident photon flux F(λ) (which is determined from the standard AM1.5 solar spectral irradiance). The power conversion efficiency of the solar cell can be expressed as η=FF×Jsc×Voc/Pi, where FF is the fill factor, Jsc is the short-circuit current, Voc is the open-circuit voltage and Pi is the incident light intensity. The photocurrent enhancement ΔJsc/Jsc is a good approximation of the power conversion efficiency enhancement Δη/η, since the fill factor FF, and the open-circuit voltage Voc, are insensitive to variation of the structural parameters of the quasi-periodic photonic crystal.

15205714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205714.value: • Various types of nanostructured electrodes based on anodic TiO2 nanotubes are fabricated and used as the anode for the dye-sensitized solar cells. To enhance the light harvesting, a multi-layered TiO2 nanotube/nanoparticle hybrid structure is constructed (RSC Adv. 4, 45180, 2014). A hierarchical TiO2 nanowire–nanoparticle/nanotube architecture is found to further enhance the power conversion efficiency (J.Mater.Chem.A 3, 20366, 2015). The angular dependence of a dye-sensitized solar cell is found to be reduced by coupling the photoanode to a TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal, a very attractive feature for practical applications (Nanoscale 6, 13060, 2014). By coupling an aperiodic photonic crystal to the photoanode of a dye-sensitized solar cell, we achieve nearly full-visible-spectrum light harvesting, as evidenced by both experimental and simulated results (Sci.Rep. 4, 6642, 2014). • To improve the cell performance under low irradiance condition, a photoanode was designed by attaching a TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal (NTPC) onto the thin TiO2 nanoparticle (NP) layer for applications in thin and semi-transparent DSSCs. The incorporation of a 2.3-miron-thick TiO2 NTPC yield PCE enhancements up to 99.1% and 130%, under 1 and 0.5 Sun conditions, respectively (J.Power Sources 293, 170, 2015). We also developed a low temperature transfer of well-aligned TiO2 nanotube membrane onto a plastic substrate for efficient flexible photovoltaic device applications. The well-designed TiO2 nanotube membrane was treated with hot water to obtain a hybrid structure of nanotubes and nanoparticles. The plastic DSSCs based on the TiO2 nanotube membranes yield an exciting efficiency of 6.25% and at the same time maintain 90% of its initial efficiency after hundreds of bending cycles (J.Power Sources 343, 47, 2017). • We further explored the full-spectrum light harvesting by making use of rationally-designed Au@Ag core-shell plasmonic nanocuboids. A high photon-to-electron conversion efficiency (IPCE) over the entire visible range, with a remarkable IPCE enhancement of 20–60% in the range of 550–750 nm was achieved in perovskite solar cells, leading to a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.31% (Nano Energy 41, 654, 2017). Finally, we summarized the recent advances in photonic crystals for enhanced light harvesting in sensitized solar cells in a review article (J.Mater.Chem.C 3, 10665, 2015).

15205714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205714.value: The TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal itself can find more applications in photocatalytic reaction, smart windows, desalination of sea water, and even in lasing.

15205714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205714.value: Photonic crystals with periodic structures are able to trap and confine photons and are hence expected to have a wide range of important applications. Research on photonic crystals with quasi-periodic structures is greatly hampered by the difficulties encountered in the fabrication of structures with a complex spatial variation. In this project, we developed a simple electrochemical anodization technique to fabricate the quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane on Ti substrates. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the application of the quasi-periodic TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal as a full-spectrum reflector in dye-sensitized solar cells to enhance the solar light harvesting. Both experimental and theoretical work have been conducted to study the mechanism of light harvesting enhancement and to find ways to optimize the quasi-periodic structure for further enhancement in light harvesting. Considering the multifunctional nature of TiO2 and the flexibility of the hole-through nanotube membrane, it is reasonable to believe that the fabricated quasi-periodic photonic crystal membrane will find its vast applications not only in optics, but also in much wider and more attractive areas where the optical properties of quasi-periodic photonic crystals and the multi-functionalities of TiO2 are uniquely and wisely integrated.

15205914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205914.value: 在經濟全球化之下，資金及人力資源更易流動，從而促進經濟發展。不過，它同時令地方資本市場及房地產市場更容易受外來因素衝擊，以致市場經常波動，甚至形成泡沫。可是，傳統金融學的資產定價理論模型並未能充分解釋這些市場波動。這暗示非理性市場行為事實上存在。學界因此亦開始着手研究這些市場行為。其中一個較重要的概念被稱為市場情緒（或投資者情緒）。由於房地產也被視為其中一種投資產品，它跟其他股票市場投資一樣，受非理性市場行為影響。這個於股票市場研究中較為常見的概念因此亦適用於研究房地產市場。研究這個未被深入探討的課題對購房決定和房屋政策有所啟示。本研究旨於建立一系列香港房地產市場情緒指數以評估該市場中人士的行為。這除了令我們對房地產資產如何定價有進一步了解，並為有意置業人士提供一個指標以作參考。由於房屋是生活中不可或缺的一部分，此研究不但在學術作出貢獻，並且對社會有一定價值。

15205914.label: Realisation of objectives
15205914.value: The three research objectives are fully achieved in this project, and we have the findings and implications which can be summarized as follows: (Objective 1) As a result of globalization in recent years, the interrelation between international property markets has grown stronger and stronger. Financial crises occur more frequently than before and market irrationalities become more often. Market irrationalities are highly likely to challenge classical theories such as the efficient market hypothesis (EMH) by driving markets away from the fundamental level. This project has found a number of irrational market behaviors in the property market, including sentiment, contagion, spillover effect. These irrational market behaviors make the real estate market (or securitized real estate market) harder to predict, and many traditional investment rules may fail. The main implication is that investors should be more careful and take those market irrationalities into account. (see Paper nos: 1, 2(a)-(g), 3) (Objective 2) With the increasingly frequent market irrationalities caused by globalization in recent years, the property markets have become harder to predict. The EMH is under heavy criticism by a number of professionals. If EMH is not true, then the traditional “buy-and-hold” strategy believed by many investors for long may not work. Therefore, some investors look for alternative indicators which can reliably reflect the market conditions and act as a guide for investment. This project has provided important indicators that reflect property market conditions more accurately and directly than others. One of those is sentiment, the definition of which is the propensity to speculate (Baker and Wurgler, 2006). There are also the coskewness and cokurtosis statistics which measure the degree of contagion between markets. Investors can make use of these indicators to improve their trading strategies in order to earn more profit. Policy makers can also implement appropriate measures according to the indicators to stabilize the real estate market. (see Paper nos: 1, 2(b),(c),(e),(g), 3) (Objective 3) One type of market irrationalities is sentiment, which drives the relative demand for speculative investments, and hence triggers cross-sectional effects even if arbitrage forces are the same across markets. However, previous studies on market sentiment mainly investigate equity markets and rarely work on real estate market. The global financial crisis in 2008 is caused by the burst of the U.S.’s property market, so it is suspected that sentiment exists in the real estate market. Furthermore, developers are faced with challenging decisions such as the optimal timing and density of their projects in order to ride the boom-bust cycles in the real estate market. The increasingly important role of market sentiment further complicates this situation. Therefore, it is important to study sentiment in the property market. This project has found that market sentiment affects housing price as well as rent. Moreover, market sentiment quantified by sentiment index is an efficient predictor of price level, return rate of price and trading volume. In addition, sentiment can affect the expected waiting time to invest, the optimal density and project value of a real estate project, too. This implies that developers should be aware of market sentiment in their project development. (see Paper nos: 1, 2(b),(c), 3) We have successfully achieved the three objectives in full and obtained the above core findings and implications, with the following core publications: 1. The PhD thesis titled "A non-systematic factor awakens: the role of sentiment in the housing market" (objectives 1, 2 and 3). 2. The following 7 core journal publications: (a) Can we predict the property cycle? A study of securitized property market (objective 1). (b) Market sentiment in private housing market (objectives 1, 2 and 3). (c) Fundamentals and Market Sentiment in Housing Market (objectives 1, 2 and 3). (d) Spatial spillover effect of urban landscape views on property price (objective 1). (e) Does Liquidity Effect Housing market performance? An Empirical Study with Spatial Panel Approach (objectives 1 and 2). (f) Capturing the abrupt changes in Asian residential property markets (objective 1). (g) Is there really any Contagion among Major Equity and Securitized Real Estate Markets? Analysis from a New Perspective (objectives 1 and 2). 3. The international conference paper titled "The role of sentiment in optimal development of residential projects" (objectives 1, 2 and 3). The full list of the publications can be found in Part C. In addition, under this project, we have successfully trained a PhD student Wang Zi-you who passed on the PhD requirements in early 2017.

15205914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205914.value: The major findings of the project are listed as follows: 1. Sentiment is a prominent indicator (or efficient predictor) of price and liquidity (trading volume). 2. Investors in housing market are more likely to be sentiment-influenced. In trading process, a delaying effect on the expected waiting time (duration) from buy to sell is found. 3. Sentiment affects housing price and its lagged term has an important bearing on rent. 4. In a real estate project, the expected waiting time to invest exhibits a U-shape pattern against sentiment; and the turning point of the U-shape pattern is more likely to appear earlier in projects with longer development periods. Meanwhile, as market sentiment intensifies, the optimal density and project value declines, ceteris paribus. 5. Strong spatial spillover effects of liquidity shocks are found in the Hong Kong housing market. 6. The cointegrating relationships influence the securitized real estate markets in the long term and become stronger during bullish markets. 7. Detected change points are found in Asian residential property markets, reflecting some significant political issues and economic collapses. A “diffusion relationship” happens from one location to another. 8. the case-resampling bootstrap method diminishes the overall effect of contagion. However, when the case-resampling bootstrap method is applied on the cokurtosis test, additional channels of contagion are detected. Furthermore, the overall effect of contagion is greater on the general equity markets than on the securitized real estate markets.

15205914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205914.value: As the irrational market behaviours make the real estate market (or securitized real estate market) harder to predict, and cause failure of many traditional investment rules to fail (including the “buy-and-hold” strategy believed by many investors for long), one potential for further development of the research is to investigate alternative trading rules under market irrationalities. One may take market sentiment into account and study how the trading strategies vary according to the sentiment level.

15205914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205914.value: The project proffers a better understanding of irrational market behaviours in the property market, provides investors and users with an indicator which reflects property market conditions more accurately and directly than others, and investigates the relationship between market sentiment and property market returns. It has significant implications to investors, policy makers and developers. Investors should take market irrationalities into account in their investment, and make use of various indicators to improve their trading strategies in order to earn more profit. Policy makers can implement appropriate measures according to the indicators to stabilize the real estate market. Developers should be aware of market sentiment and take appropriate measures to reduce risk in their project development.

15206414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206414.value: 基于光热效应的新型高灵敏度光纤气体传感器

15206414.label: Project Objectives
15206414.value: To investigate theoretically the PT effect in gas-filled HC-PBFs. This includes modelling the changes of gas temperature, density and pressure following light absorption; studying the effects of these changes on the effective-refractive-index and accumulated phase of the fundamental mode; studying the linear and non-linear dependence of phase modulation on the fibre length, the power level and modulation parameters of the pump; and analyzing various noises and performance-limiting factors. To investigate experimentally the detection of trace-gas based on PTI with HC-PBF. This includes proof-of-principle demonstration, testing the effect of varying the power and modulation parameters of the pump on the output signal, characterisation of various noise factors associated with the use of HC-PCF and various interferometer configurations, and optimisation of system parameters to achieve best detection sensitivity. To carry out preliminary investigation on distributed gas sensor along a HC-PBF.

15206414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206414.value: This project is to study photothermal (PT) effect in gas-filled hollow-core photonic bandgap fibres (HC-PBFs) and to exploit the use of PT interferometry (PTI) for high sensitivity and distributed optical fibre gas sensors. A HC-PBF allows the confinement of an optical mode and gas-phase materials simultaneously in its hollow-core, and this provides an excellent platform for strong light-gas interaction inside the fibre-core over a long distance. By propagating a modulated pump (excitation) laser beam in the gas-filled HC-PBF and tuning its wavelength to an absorption line of a trace gas within the hollow-core, the effective-refractive-index and hence accumulated phase of the fundamental mode will be modulated. This phase modulation is proportional to the trace gas concentration and can be detected interferometrically by propagating a probe laser beam along the same HC-PBF. The phase modulation scales up with the propagation distance and the pump power, and hence the use of a longer fibre and a higher-power pump will allow extremely sensitive optical fibre gas sensors. We will perform numerical modelling of the effective-refractive-index change of the fundamental mode following the absorption of the pump beam; study theoretically and experimentally the effect of varying the power and modulation parameters of the pump as well as the length of HC-PBF on the performance of PTI-based gas sensors; and evaluate the minimum detectable absorbance (or gas concentration) limited by various noise factors. We will also study the use of PTI for distributed measurement of gas concentration along the entire length of a HC-PBF cable. The spatial distribution of phase modulation following the absorption of the pump beam may be detected by using a coherent phase-OTDR (optical time-domain reflectometry) operating at the probe wavelength. The effect of varying system parameters on the minimum detectable absorbance, spatial resolution, and maximum measurable distance will be investigated. 本專案將研究填充了氣體的空芯光子帶隙光纖的光熱效應，並且探究其在高靈敏度和分散式光纖氣體感測器的應用。空芯光子帶隙光纖使得光學模式和氣態物質同時限制在其中心空芯孔中，提供了一個非常好的平臺來研究長距離光與物質相互作用。通過輸入一束泵浦光進入空芯光子帶隙光纖，並且調節其波長到氣體吸收線，另外一束探索光的有效折射率和相位將會被調製。該相位調製的大小正比於痕量氣體的濃度並且能被干涉解調。相位調製的大小還正比於傳輸距離和泵浦光功率，因此使用較長的光纖和較高的泵浦功率將會實現高靈敏度的光纖氣體感測器。我們將完成由於吸收泵浦光引起的有效折射率的變化的數值模擬；理論和實驗研究不同的泵浦光功率和調製參數以及空芯光子帶隙光纖長度對氣體感測器性能的影響；評估受限於各種雜訊因素的最小可探測氣體濃度。我們還將研究利用該方法實現沿著同一根空芯光子帶隙光纖的分散式氣體濃度測量。

15206414.label: Realisation of objectives
15206414.value: Objective 1: PT phase modulation in gas-filled HC-PBFs were investigated theoretically and numerically. Analytical formulation that relates the phase modulation to the key system parameters such as absorption coefficient and gas concentration, pump power level and fiber length are established. Numerical modeling on the dynamics of temperature distribution in the hollow-core resulting from pump absorption was conducted by using the heat-transfer equation, and the results were further used to compute the phase modulation of the probe beam. For the HC-1550-02 fiber with a hollow-core diameter of ~10 micrometer operating at the P(9) absorption of acetylene, the phase modulation was found to increase with pulsed duration (for pulse pump modulation) up to about 1.2 microsecond and decrease with modulation frequency (for sinusoidal pump modulation) down to about 800 kHz, determined by the heat conduction time from the core center to the silica boundary. At steady state, the normalized phase modulation coefficient was computed to be about 1.7 micro-radian (peak to peak) per ppm acetylene, per mW pump power, per meter length of HC-PBF. The various noise and error factors associated with different interferometric detection circuits, i.e., Mach-Zehnder, Sagnac and in-fiber modal interferometers were examined and compared. The shot noise limited performance of these configurations are more or less the same for similar systems parameters but the Sagnac configuration achieves quadrature operation passively and avoids the use of active stabilization of the interferometer, which is required for the Mach-Zehnder interferometer configuration. The operation point of the Sagnac configuration is independent of the length of the sensing HC-PBF and can therefore be used as a universal demodulation system for different lengths of sensing HC-PBFs. Demodulation based on modal interferometer provides a single fiber solution for interferometric gas detection, but the probe wavelength still needs to be servo-controlled to the quadrature point of the modal interference fringes. The modal interferometer detects the phase difference between two different propagation modes and hence the PT modulation signal is smaller than that of the Mach-Zehnder and Sagnac configurations. Objective 2: Experimental investigation of trace-gas detection based on PTI in the HC-1550-02 fiber was conducted. The experiments used a DFB or ECDL as the pump source and an ECDL or a SLD source as the probe. The wavelengths of both the pump and the probe are around 1550 nm. Both sinusoidal and pulse modulations of the pump were studied. For pulse pump modulation, intensity modulation with a AOM was used for PT phase modulation and a Sagnac inteterferometer with a 3x3 directional coupler was used for phase detection. Boxcar averaging was used to improve signal to noise ratio. The phase modulation dynamics was examined with different pulse duration and amplitudes, and the experimental results agreed well with the results of numerical modelling. For sinusoidal pump modulation, the pump was modulated in either wavelength or intensity to produce PT phase modulation and Mach-Zehnder, Sagnac and modal ineterferometers were tested for the detection of PT phase modulation. The second or first harmonic was detected by use of a lock-in amplifier to improve signal to noise ratio. The effects of varying of the pump power level and modulation parameters of the pump on the output signal were studied and the pros and cons of different interferometric detection configurations were compared. The best short-term detection limit (i.e., 2 ppb acetylene) was achieved with the Mach-Zehnder configuration while the best long term stability was achieved with the Sagnac configuration (i.e., 0.87 dB over 6 hours). To improve the response time of the HC-PCF gas sensors, we studied the use of a femtosecond laser micro-machining system for large-scale drilling of micro-channels along the HC-PBF. By optimizing fabrication parameters, we were able to fabricate 200 to 300 high quality micro-channels along a single HC-1550-02 fiber with an average loss of <0.01 dB per channel. This forms the foundation of fast PT gas sensors with HC-PBFs. Objective 3: The theories of distributed and quasi-distributed gas detection based on PT phase modulation along a HC-PBF was developed, which are based on respectively the backscattering of the inner surface of the hollow-core fiber and the reflections at the HC-PBF and conventional SMF interface. A two-pulse coherent phase OTDR system was developed (in collaboration with Tsinghua University) and used for the detection of the distributed or quasi-distributed phase modulation. The effects of pump power level, duration and repetition rate on the detectable concentration level, spatial resolution and maximum measurement distance were analyzed. A quasi-distributed sensing experiment with two 28-meter-long HC-PBF sensing sections connected by single-mode transmission fibers demonstrated a limit of detection (LOD) of 10 ppb acetylene with a pump power level of 55 mW. A distributed sensing experiment over a 200-meter-long sensing cable made of serially connected HC-PBFs demonstrated a LOD of 5 ppm with 62.5 mW peak pump power. The spatial resolution of the current distributed detection system is limited to 30 m, but it is possible to reduce down to 1 meter by using shorter pulse duration and optimized system design.

15206414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206414.value: Gas detection based on PT phase modulation in gas-filled HC-PBFs can achieved extremely high detection sensitivity. The sensitivity enhanced is attributed to the tightly confined and highly overlapping pump and probe fields as well the longer interaction as compared with the conventional free-space optical gas cells. This enables PT gas sensors with performance (i.e., detection limit and dynamic range) three orders better than the traditional direct absorption intensity based sensors [2015 Nature Communications, 2016 Scientific Reports, 2017 Journal of Lightwave Technology]. Heat-transfer dynamics of gases in the hollow-core showed that the thermal conduction from the core center to the core-cladding boundary is responsible for the response time of the PT phase modulation sensors. Hence it is possible to further improve the detection limit by optimizing the fiber dimensions and the pump modulation frequency/pulse width [2016 Scientific Reports, APOS2016]. The use of Sagnac interferometers for PT phase detection can achieve stable operation over a long term of many hours, and can be used as a universal demodulation system for PT sensors with different lengths of HC-PBFs [2017 Journal of Lightwave Technology, CLEO2016]. Drilling of micro-channels along a HC-PBF induces very little loss (<0.01 dB per channel). The response time of the HC-PBF gas sensors can be improved significantly by drilling a large number of micro-channels along the sensing HC-PBF [2017 Journal of Lightwave Technology]. It is possible to develop a distributed gas detection system based on PT phase modulation along a hollow-core optical fiber. A preliminary distributed sensing experiment over a 200-meter-long sensing cable demonstrated a lower detection limit of 5 ppm with a spatial resolution of 30 m. 1 meter spatial resolution is possible by optimizing the pulse modulation parameters [2017 OPTICS EXPRESS].

15206414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206414.value: PT gas sensor with hollow-core fiber is an ultra-sensitive technique and we are conducting further investigations, aiming for practical applications.

15206414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206414.value: This project is to study photothermal (PT) effect in gas-filled hollow-core photonic bandgap fibres (HC-PBFs) and to exploit the use of PT interferometry (PTI) for high sensitivity and distributed optical fiber gas sensing. We conducted numerical modelling of the effective-refractive-index change of the fundamental mode following the absorption of the pump beam and examined theoretically and experimentally the effect of varying the power and modulation parameters of the pump as well as the length of HC-PBF on the performance of PTI-based gas sensors. Experiments shown that the HC-PBF-based PTI is an ultra-sensitive technique for absorptive gas detection and we have demonstrated ppb level gas detection with dynamic range of over 5 orders of magnitude and response time of well below 1 min. We also studied the use of PTI for distributed measurement of gas concentration along the entire length of a HC-PBF, and achieved ppm level detection of acetylene with a spatial resolution of 30 m over a length of 200 m.

15206514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206514.value: 非線性現象廣泛存在於各類科學和工程問題之中。非線性可能會給系統帶來分析和設計上的麻煩和困難，但也可能在系統的性能提高上提供有利的幫助。因此非線性問題的分析和設計是當前學術界一個關注熱點。本研究旨在開發一套系統的解決工程應用中出現的一類非線性問題的分析和設計方法。這是一套創新性的非線性頻域分析方法，可以直接將非線性系統的頻域輸出譜函數求解出來，並進行系統參數的優化分析和設計。為此，本課題要解決一系列的基本理論和方法上的困難。比如，如何準確的求解出非線性的頻域輸出譜函數，如何知道給定系統是否滿足Volterra級數展開，以及如何針對實際工程問題進行分析和設計等。

15206514.label: Realisation of objectives
15206514.value: All tasks specified in the project objectives are successfully completed with productive and benchmark results achieved. Those are reported as follows: Objective 1: Development of easy-to-compute parametric convergence criteria for Volterra series expansion of nonlinear systems in terms of model parameters, input magnitude and frequency. The convergence bound for Volterra series expansion of nonlinear systems is investigated with a novel parametric approach in this study. To this aim, two fundamental concepts —parametric bound of convergence (PBoC) and parametric convergence margin (PCM) are proposed, which are related to the conditions, under which a given NARX model can be approximated by a convergent Volterra series, in terms of system characteristic parameters including model parameters (of interest), input magnitude, and frequency. The estimation of the PBoC and PCM is given in the frequency domain, which is expressed in terms of these characteristic parameters, and does not require iterative calculations. The results provide a fundamental basis for nonlinear analysis and design using Volterra series based methods, and also present a significant insight into understanding nonlinear influence (super/sub harmonics and modulation) with respect to model parameters and input magnitude. Based on the results above, MIMO systems are studied by using a vehicle suspension system. Parametric convergence bounds for Volterra series expansion of nonlinear systems described by a SIMO nonlinear auto-regressive with exogenous inputs model are studied in the frequency domain, referred to as parametric bound of convergence (PBoC). With the resulting PBoC of characteristic parameters, nonlinear systems with a nonlinear multiobjective performance (MOP) function can then be analyzed in the frequency domain using a nonlinear characteristic output spectrum method based on the Volterra series expansion. The results demonstrate a systematic and novel method for nonlinear analysis and design. These results were published in the following papers: (1) On Convergence of Volterra Series Expansion of a Class of Nonlinear Systems, Asian Journal of Control, Mar 2017 (2) Estimation of parametric convergence bounds for Volterra series expansion of nonlinear systems, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 45 (2014) 28–48; (3) An SIMO Nonlinear System Approach to Analysis and Design of Vehicle Suspensions, IEEE/ASME TRANSACTIONS ON MECHATRONICS, DECEMBER 2015 (4) Estimation of Parametric Convergence Bounds for Volterra Series Expansion of Nonlinear Systems, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, 2014 (5) Parameterized Convergence Bounds for Volterra Series Expansion of NARX Models, IEEE Transaction on Signal Processing, 2013 Objective 2: Determination of the nonlinear characteristic output spectrum (nCOS), which is an analytical function of any characteristic parameters of interest. A systematic method for nonlinear analysis, design, and estimation in the frequency domain is proposed in this study using a new concept-nonlinear characteristic output spectrum (nCOS). The nCOS function is an analytical and explicit expression for the relationship between nonlinear output spectrum and system characteristic parameters of interest (including frequency, nonlinear parameters, and excitation magnitude), and can provide a significant insight into nonlinear analysis and design in the frequency domain. Given some simulation or experimental output data of a nonlinear system, the nCOS function of the system can be accurately determined up to any high nonlinear orders with less simulation trials and computation cost compared with a pure simulation-based study or traditional theoretical computations. Moreover, the method can also be used to accurately determine the linear and nonlinear components in the nonlinear output frequency response (or an output spectrum) of a nonlinear system. These results are definitely of significance to nonlinear analysis and design, nonlinear signal processing, system identification, fault detection, etc., in practice. The nCOS function can be any system output function or multiobjective performance function to be optimized. It is shown for the first time that the nCOS function can be expressed into an explicit and analytical polynomial function of any model parameters which define underlying linear dynamics of the system. This novel nCOS function can obviously facilitate parameter analysis and design of nonlinear vibration control systems and provide a useful tool for a simple linear control design, while simultaneously considering inherent nonlinear dynamics of a system. A case study in vehicle suspension control demonstrates these new results. Nonlinearity always brings difficulties to the analysis and design of practical systems. We show that, the nonlinear output spectrum can be expressed as a polynomial function with respect to linear model parameters, based on the recently developed concepts of parametric characteristic analysis and nonlinear Characteristic Output Spectrum (nCOS) function. The coefficients of the new nCOS function are independent of the linear parameters of interest, and can be directly determined with proposed procedures. It is shown that the new results reveal a straightforward insight into the parametric optimization of the amplifier for suppression of intermodulation distortion. These results were published in the following papers: (6) Nonlinear Characteristic Output Spectrum for Nonlinear Analysis and Design, IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, 2014 (7) Frequency-Domain Analysis and Design of Linear Feedback of Nonlinear Systems and Applications in Vehicle Suspensions, IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, 2016 (8) A Novel Characteristic Parameter Approach for Analysis and Design of Linear Components in Nonlinear Systems, IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2016 We also published a monograph which summarize most results of the above. (9) Xingjian Jing, ZQ Lang, Frequency Domain Analysis and Design of Nonlinear Systems based on Volterra Series Expansion: A Parametric Characteristic Approach, Springer, 2015 Objective 3: The nCOS function based application in crack detection or vibration control Nonlinearity detection and characterization for crack-/damage-related fault evaluation/detection is a hot engineering topic. We investigate a novel and systematic nonlinear decomposition and regulation method for nonlinearity characterization. It is shown that, using the proposed output decomposition and regulation, the even-order nonlinearity and crack-incurred nonlinearity (not a simple even-order nonlinearity although at its initial stage) can all be effectively evaluated by the magnitude of the second-order harmonic response, and the latter is a linear function of the crack severity and can be accurately estimated with the proposed method. The theory and methods of this study would provide a useful and alternative frequency-domain approach for nonlinear signal processing in crack/damage evaluation, nonlinearity detection and characterization, and can benefit a broad spectrum of engineering practice. These results were published in the following papers: (10) A nonlinear decomposition and regulation method for nonlinearity characterization, Nonlinear Dynamics, February 2016 (11) A second-order output spectrum approach for fault detection of bolt loosening in a satellite-like structure with a sensor chain, Nonlinear Dynamics, July 2017 (12) A Sensor Network based Virtual Beam-like Structure Method for Fault Diagnosis and Monitoring of Complex Structures with Improved Bacterial Optimization, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, Feb 2017 (13) Fault diagnosis of sensor networked structures with multiple faults using a virtual beam based approach, Journal of Sound and Vibration, July 2017 (14) Vibration signal based fault diagnosis in complex structures: A beam-like-structure approach, Structure Health Monitoring, 2018 We also develop some other results by using the nCOS method and nonlinear analysis methods in vibration control, energy harvesting and sensor design. The results are published in the other more than 10 papers, such as (15) A nonlinear vibration isolator achieving high-static-low-dynamic stiffness and tunable anti-resonance frequency band, to appear in Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, 2016 (16) Analysis and design of a nonlinear stiffness and damping system with a scissor-like structure, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, 2016 (17) Vibration energy harvesting with a nonlinear structure, Nonlinear Dynamics, 2016 (18) Vibration isolation by exploring bio-inspired structural nonlinearity. Bioinspiration & biomimetics, 2015

15206514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206514.value: (1) General and specific parametric convergence bounds (PCB) guiding the convergence of Volterra series expansion to a nonlinear system: Parametric Convergence Bounds & Parametric Convergence Margins These are systematically developed in recent years with results published in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017. These results can clearly say at what parametric range and what frequency range a given nonlinear system has a convergent Volterra series expansion. On the other hand, the results indicate also the appearance of complicated non-Volterra nonlinear dynamics such as chaos or bifurcation with a specific and explicit parameter range. These results solve the long lasting fundamental issue related to the application of Volterra series based methods. (2) A benchmark parametric characteristic approach-nCOS (initially OFRF) For nonlinear analysis and design in the frequency domain, we systematically proposed and developed this frequency domain method, which presents an explicit analytical structure and expression of the output spectrum of nonlinear systems with respect to model parameters of interest (both linear and/or nonlinear components), frequency variable, and excitation amplitude (which are referred to as characteristic parameters). The nonlinear output spectrum can be obtained subject to any input signal without restricted to any specific excitation or nonlinear forms, compared with all other existing frequency domain methods in the literature. (3) Nonlinear frequency-domain features: SOOS more robust and more reliable We theoretically revealed and experimentally validated that the second order output spectrum is the most reliable nonlinear features for several benchmark structural faults such as cracks and bolt loosening, and thus developed a systematic SOOS based method for health monitoring and fault diagnosis in complex structures.

15206514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206514.value: We will develop the above theory and methods more efficient and convenient in practical implementation and establish more benchmark practical methods based on the existing technical lines with real applications. The discovery in this project also leads to a new study on bio-inspired structures and their nonlinear benefits in engineering applications, which have been focused in a following GRF project and several other high-impact industrial applications and awards. The application of the theory and methods in structural health monitoring is very powerful and effective compared to many other existing methods, which will also be further investigated.

15206514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206514.value: This project presents a series of pioneer studies on the potential influence of nonlinear dynamics in engineering systems and develops systematic and fundamental methods about how to employ nonlinear benefits in engineering practices. It is demonstrated that nonlinearity can play a critical and helpful role in system dynamic response and employment of these benefits can bring significant advantages in system output performance. This project therefore lays down very benchmark ways with a special frequency domain insight to engineering nonlinearities and their practical utilization.

15206814.label: Project Objectives
15206814.value: Iris segmentation under relaxed imaging constraints: This project will develop highly accurate and generalized algorithms to accurately segment human irises from facial images acquired at greater standoff distances (3-8 meters) and in a less constrained imaging environments. Degradation of image quality significantly reduces contrast between pupillary and limbic boundaries. Therefore a variational framework to accurately recover iris image boundaries, along with the specialized post-processing strategies to mitigate multiple sources of noise, will be developed. The segmentation strategy for visible wavelength illumination images will be seamlessly adapted for the near infrared illumination images such that no modifications are required to segment iris images under variable spectral bands. Matching at-a-distance iris images: With the availability of accurately segmented iris images, we will study how to recover and accurately match discriminant iris features under illumination, scale and viewpoint changes. Our objective is to (i) introduce feature-level formulation to simultaneously recover and match multiple iris features (embedded in multiple spectral bands, representations, etc.), (ii) develop iris texture descriptors which are invariant to frequently observed photometric and geometric transforms, (iii) jointly incorporate local and global iris features while nonlinearly rewarding (also penalizing) iris bits based on their spatial-coherence, and (iv) simultaneously recover and encode key periocular features, using a set of representative textons, to further improve iris matching performance to an acceptable level.
