15206814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206814.value: 目前人們對安全方面的需求日益增大，其中自動身份識別是最關鍵的和具有挑戰性的任務之一。迄今為止，還沒有研究工作可以實現一個自動並暗中進行可靠的人類身份識別的系統。許多以此為目標的研究項目使用虹膜作為主要的識別途徑，在變化的光線環境下，從一定距離外對移動的對象提取數據。 虹膜紋理被認為是人類的一個具有高度獨特性的特徵，因此虹膜識別成為生物識別研究中最熱門的領域之一。然而，目前部署的自動虹膜識別系統需要使用近紅外光照近距離獲取高質量的虹膜圖像。這些成像上的限制使得自動虹膜識別技術難以被應用到監視、取證、搜尋失踪兒童或吸毒檢測等方面。 本項目的主要目標有以下三個：（1）發展新的理論模型和算法，使虹膜識別技術更先進，令其可以應用于現實場景下取得的圖像，例如高度自由的攝像環境、更遠的成像距離、失去焦點、角度上的旋轉、被眼睫毛、光反射、頭髮或眼鏡遮擋等等情況。（2）利用眼睛附近區域，亦即眼週上的具有獨特性的特徵，以顯著提高在自由成像環境下虹膜識別的準確性。（3）開發一種創新性的策略，綜合利用不同光譜下的虹膜數據來進行匹配。目前為止，使用可見光而非近紅外對虹膜數據進行採集并匹配，亦可獲得令人滿意的匹配精度。然而可惜的是，目前大部份可以使用的虹膜實驗數據均是採集于近紅外線，極少数採集于可見光。鑒於此種情況，本項目將會深度探索并實現可以準確匹配這種跨光譜圖像的更高層次的複合模型。在目前針對虹膜識別的研究成果基礎上，本項目將會引進創新性的虹膜特徵——這些特徵不會隨著角度的旋轉、成像範圍以及透視成像的效果而變化。本項目亦會建立對虹膜多次測量的特徵匹配算法，引進非線性及針對局部特徵的匹配策略，以消除在不同距離下成像而造成的分辨率不同的影響。我們的初步研究結果非常令人振奮，可確認該項目的可行性及巨大的潛在價值。使用本項目開發的技術，虹膜分割和識別技術將會更加先進，可極大擴展生物特徵识别技術在非受限環境下的應用。

15206814.label: Realisation of objectives
15206814.value: This project was revised and approved with two key objectives. Two Co-Investigators were not involved in the project as the revised/approved project was shortened with about half of the requested funding amount. The first objective of this project was ‘iris segmentation under relaxed imaging constraints’. We deeply pursued our research to confront challenges with this objective and attempted to address the problems in different phases. We firstly introduced a variational framework to accurately recover iris image boundaries, along with the specialized post-processing operators, from the noisy iris images acquired under visible and near-infrared illuminations. This research yielded highly promising results, especially for the lass constrained images, and the developed method was also published in a top-tiered computer vision conference [ICCV15]. Success of deep learning capabilities for a range of computer vision problems motivated us to further investigate such capabilities to address performance limitations for the segmentation of challenging iris images under relaxed constraints. Our research was far-beyond mere application of any deep learning capabilities or algorithm as this can only offer limited performance improvements. Our research pursued a fully convolutional neural network based strategy to achieve most accurate iris segmentation results on several public databases. These results were presented and were published in another top-tiered compute vision conference [ICCV17]. Our investigation into the nature of segmented iris texture details from the images acquired under visible and near infrared illumination resulted into a new class of practical iris recognition systems and research. This was a paradigm shift with the traditional iris recognition systems which only acquire images from one spectrum or unable to exploit rich iris texture information from multiple spectrums, largely due to the challenges in establishing pixel-to-pixel correspondences in the acquired images. For the first time, our research introduced such capabilities and demonstrated simultaneous recovery of iris texture details with pixel-to-pixel correspondences from visible and near-infrared spectrums. Therefore, our research introduced significantly accurate iris recognition capabilities, by simultaneously recovering and matching such complimentary information, without causing any additional inconvenience to the unknown user during the user authentication process. The details of this research, along with the algorithms and results, were also published in a top-tiered journal [TIP17]. The second objective of our project was ‘matching at-a-distance iris images’. This was in fact the key research objective and required us to carefully consider the fundamental reasons for the degradation of matching accuracy for the iris images acquired under relaxed imaging constraints. Spatial relationships of rich randomly varying iris texture presents valuable information that should be preserved even during the matching stage. Therefore, we introduced fully convolutional neural network based approach to recover binary iris features that preserved spatial correspondences in the original iris texture images. A key research challenge in this work was confronted by introducing a new loss function, along with a fully convolutional network to preserve the valuable spatial relationships among the iris features, which ensured that the network adequately considers the involuntary shifts and rotations during the iris imaging. This new iris recognition framework was evaluated on multiple public databases to establish outperforming results and online deployment capabilities. These findings were published in top conference [ICCV17]. This framework was further improved by incorporating iris detection capabilities and these capabilities, along with extensive experimental results, appear in recent journal publication [PR19]. In order to accurately consolidate the iris texture details from multiple scales for the at-a-distance iris images, our research also introduced deep neural network based iris recognition capabilities that uses dilated kernels to capture such information from multiple scales. This research achieved highly promising results across multiple iris databases and the details of these findings appear in another top journal publication [TIFS19]. Iris images acquired for the user authentication inherently include periocular information and these can be employed directly employed to establish the identity of individuals. Periocular information is especially significant for the iris images that are acquired under relaxed imaging constraints. Our research therefore deeply pursued on the recovery of such information and introduced a novel framework to incorporate automatically determined semantics information, i.e. gender, left or right, etc., to advance periocular image matching capabilities available today. We trained several branches of convolutional neural network from the semantics information corresponding to the training data and therefore such trained network was capable of recovering more comprehensive ocular images features. This research output appears in a top journal publication [TIFS17] and illustrates outperforming results on several public databases. Eyebrow and eye regions acquired during the iris imaging illustrate critical information for periocular precognition. Therefore feature learning phase must attract additional attention. Therefore, inspired by the human perception that inherently incorporates attention to important distinguishing regions, we introduced attention based approach to more accurately recover discriminating periocular images and introduced a new loss function to provide much needed marginal effects for the positive and negative samples during the training. The details of this framework appears in another top journal publication [TIFS18] and offers most accurate results, both for the open-set and closed-set, user authentication and recognition problems using periocular images. Success of surveillance capabilities for missing children’s or wandering elderly, requires us to develop accurate cross-spectral iris recognition capabilities. Therefore, our research during this project also confronted open challenges with such research problem. Our research using convolutional neural networks indicated that the feature vectors recovered from such networks are generally sparse. Therefore we pursued a supervised discrete hashing scheme to significantly reduce the iris template size and improve the matching speed using Hamming distance for the convolutional neural network based features. Such high speed matching is especially critical for accurately matching iris images acquired under visible illumination from the surveillance, with those under near-infrared illumination. The details of this investigation, along with outperforming cross-spectral iris matching results on public databases, appear in another journal publication [PR18].

Therefore a variational framework to accurately recover iris image boundaries, along with the specialized post-processing strategies to mitigate multiple sources of noise, will be developed. rows: Iris segmentation under relaxed imaging constraints: This project will develop highly accurate and generalized algorithms to accurately segment human irises from facial images acquired at greater standoff distances (3-8 meters) and in a less constrained imaging environments. Degradation of image quality significantly reduces contrast between pupillary and limbic boundaries. Therefore a variational framework to accurately recover iris image boundaries, along with the specialized post-processing strategies to mitigate multiple sources of noise, will be developed. The segmentation strategy for visible wavelength illumination images will be seamlessly adapted for the near infrared illumination images such that no modifications are required to segment iris images under variable spectral bands.

Matching at-a-distance iris images: With the availability of accurately segmented iris images, we will study how to recover and accurately match discriminant iris features under illumination, scale and viewpoint changes. Our objective is to (i) introduce feature-level formulation to simultaneously recover and match multiple iris features (embedded in multiple spectral bands, representations, etc.), (ii) develop iris texture descriptors which are invariant to frequently observed photometric and geometric transforms, (iii) jointly incorporate local and global iris features while nonlinearly rewarding (also penalizing) iris bits based on their spatial-coherence, and (iv) simultaneously recover and encode key periocular features, using a set of representative textons, to further improve iris matching performance to an acceptable level.

15206814.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206814.value: (a) Our research introduced a total-variation based formulation to in which the slowly varying image structure such as eyelid, limbic boundaries, etc. and the surrounding texture or noises were differently penalized. Our research incorporated l1 norm, which is more effective in preserving the geometrical properties and computationally efficient, to automatically segment iris images acquired under relaxed imaging constraints. The details of this research, method and experimental results, appear in a top conference [ICCV15] and offer computationally simpler alternative for challenging iris segmentation problems. (b) Our research also introduced a series of robust post-processing operations to accurately localize limbic boundaries in noisy iris images. Our research introduces an adaptive and self-corrective methodology in these post-processing operations to independently exploit local features as much as possible and help in reducing the global errors. These post-processing operations effectively use the intermediate results and adopt dynamic threshold mechanisms. Such strategies [ICCV15] have significantly helped to improve the overall iris segmentation accuracy for iris images acquired under relaxed imaging constraints. (c) Most significant information in the iris images is preserved in the spatial arrangement of (widely believed) random gray levels that should be preserved while matching the corresponding features. Therefore, for the first time, our research considered fully convolutional network to recover the iris features that can preserve spatial correspondences in the original iris texture images [ICCV17]. It is necessary to consider spatial shifts and translations in the iris features. Therefore we introduced [ICCV17] a new loss function, i.e., Soft Shifted Triplet Loss, during the network training to enable most accurate matching from the iris feature templates. (d) Iris images under relaxed imaging constraints illustrate significantly larger scale changes. One effective approach to recover iris features at different scales is to incorporate dilated kernels in the network. Such an approach TIFS19] can offer significant performance improvement and a promising alternative to match iris images acquired under relaxed imaging constraints. (e) Simultaneous acquisition of iris texture details with pixel-to-pixel correspondences, under visible and near-infrared illumination, can provide rich and complimentary information, and especially useful for iris recognition under relaxed imaging constraints. Such an approach was carefully pursued in this project with highly promising results that appear in a journal [TIP17] publication. (f) This project introduced a new framework [PR19] to accurately match such cross-spectral iris images and benefited from a trained network that can recover cross-spectral pixel relationships in encoding the features. Incorporating supervised discrete hashing and recovering binary features can significantly speed-up cross-spectral iris image matching. (g) Inherently embedded semantics information in the periocular images can be automatically utilized [TIFS17] to accurately match periocular images. (h) The eyebrow and eye regions in the periocular images represent highly discriminating information and therefore enhanced attention [TIFS18] to the periocular features can significantly improve periocular image matching capabilities available today.

15206814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206814.value: This project has introduced significant advances in the development of accurate iris recognition techniques for the real-world applications. Despite significant efforts and results in accurately matching periocular details from the iris images, with semantics information and automated attention to discriminating regions, our research could not pursue a unified strategy to introduce feature-level formulation for the iris and periocular information. Such strategy requires careful recovery of low-level and high-level information, along with disparate source of respective noise, and will be pursued in further extension of this work. Advanced iris and periocular recognition capabilities introduced from this project can be simultaneously incorporated to realize extremely accurate and secured biometrics system using facial features. Such capabilities can be introduced by dynamically integrating facial features, i.e., iris, periocular and face, and is part of further work to avail full potential from the advancements in at-a-distance iris recognition capabilities. One of the most challenging aspect of less-constrained iris recognition is to match off-angle images, i.e. cross-view iris matching, and such images are also inherently acquired in a range of devices like augmented or virtual reality applications. Development of cross-view iris recognition capabilities is one of the most challenging research problem that needs to be pursued in further research.

15206814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206814.value: Automated human recognition in real environments is one of the most critical and challenging tasks to meet growing demand for the stringent security. This research project has confronted research challenges in developing reliable recognition mechanism using iris images that are generally acquired under less constrained imaging scenarios or non-ideal conditions. Advanced capabilities to accurately detect and segment region of the interest from the eye images, generally acquired from the commercial iris sensors, were developed and the success of these methods can be ascertained from the outperforming segmentation accuracies illustrated on several public iris image databases in the high-quality publications resulting from this project. Segmented iris images require advanced capabilities to recover features that are invariant to common geometric or photometric transformations observed in less-constrained iris images. This project confronted such research challenges and introduced fundamental algorithms to automatically recover and match these features to enable highly accurate iris recognition capabilities. In the event when the iris texture is severely degraded due to high-level of relaxation during the imaging, periocular information can be focused to establish identity of the individuals. This research project deep research on information revealed from such images and introduced novel methods to match such images with very high level of accuracy.

15206914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206914.value: This project aims to develop new rare earth-doped bismuth sodium titanate-based photoluminescent relaxor ceramics for multifunctional photonic applications. The work will focus on developing ceramics with both enhanced and tunable photoluminescence intensity and color. Bismuth sodium titanate-based relaxor ferroelectrics with efficient and reversible electric-field-induced relaxor-to-ferroelectric phase transition will be used as the host materials for the photoluminescent ceramics. It is anticipated that, attributed to the large structural change arisen from the phase transition, the local field around the rare earth ions will be altered and hence the photoluminescence intensity can be enhanced and tuned effectively by an electric field. As the resulting effects on various electronic transitions are different, the overall color of emissions can also be adjusted. More importantly, the changes are reversible and can be induced by a relatively low electric field, making the newly developed ceramics promising for practical applications. In combination with the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties, they would usher in widespread applications, such as optical amplifiers, optical waveguides, display lighting, and biomedicine. They are also environmental friendly as they are lead-free and do not contain any toxic elements. The fabrication process is also simple and involves sintering at relatively low temperatures, and thus they can help to save energy and hence save the environment. In this project, we also hope to elucidate the relationships between the relaxor-to-ferroelectric phase transition and photoluminescence properties, including the physical process of electronic transitions, of the ceramics. 本項目旨在開發具有可調光致發光特性的無鉛陶瓷。這工作主要研究稀土摻雜鈦酸鉍鈉基弛豫陶瓷的光致發光性能及其可調控性。鈦酸鉍鈉基弛豫陶瓷具有高效和可逆的弛豫鐵電相變。相變過程中出現的結構變化可改變稀土離子周圍的局部電場，從而影響電子的躍遷和由此產生的光致發光強度和顏色。由於鈦酸鉍鈉基弛豫陶瓷的弛豫鐵電相變是可逆的和可通過低電場誘導，它的發光強度和顏色從而能通過外加電場有效地控制。新開發的陶瓷不含鉛或其他有毒元素，燒結溫度也比其他陶瓷低。因此可節省能源和減小對環境的污染。新開發的陶瓷有望能廣泛應用於不同範籌，如光放大器，光學波導，顯示照明和生物醫藥等。

15206914.label: Realisation of objectives
15206914.value: Rare earth-doped lead-free ferroelectric ceramics with tunable photoluminescence (PL) properties have been successfully developed. The characteristics of ferroelectric ceramics have been utilized for realizing the real-time modulation of PL responses. The effects of rare earth dopants on the ferroelectric hosts as well as the the relationship between the relaxor-to-ferroelectric phase transition have been investigated systematically. The optimum conditions of the ceramics, including the type and amount of the rare earth dopants and the host materials have also been determined. Pr-doped Ba0.85Ca0.15Ti0.90Zr0.10O3 (Pr-BCTZ) lead-free ferroelectric ceramics have first been fabricated for investigating the effects of ferroelectric characteristics such as polarization switching and phase transition on the PL responses. BCTZ will undergo a phase transition at room temperature under a low electric field of 2 kV/mm, which is much lower than that for Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-BaTiO3-K0.5Na0.5NbO3 (8 kV/mm). Our results have shown that a real-time modulation of down-conversion PL emissions of the ceramic can be realized via the application of an external electric field. The remarkable polarization reversal and phase evolution of the ceramic deriving from a tri-critical point near MPB enable reliable responses to the applied electric field. As evidenced by in-situ X-ray diffraction analysis, the applied electric field induces not only typical polarization switching and minor crystal deformation, but also tetragonal-to-rhombohedral phase transformation of the host. Unlike the former two responses, the field-induced phase transformation is irreversible, but engenders greater effect on photoluminescence emissions as a result of an increase in structural symmetry. After the phase transition is completed in a few cycles of electric field, the photoluminescence emissions become governed mainly by the reversible polarization switching. Owing to the minor and opposite effect arisen from the field-induced crystal deformation, the observed photoluminescence intensity however deviates slightly from the modulating electric field. The effects of phase transition on the PL modulation in Er-doped BaZr0.15Ti0.85O3 (BZT) ceramics have also been investigated for substantiating the mechanism of the electric field-induced PL modulation. BZT is a relaxor-like ferroelectrics exhibiting a rhombohedral-cubic phase transition at ~65C. As evidenced by the in-situ X-ray analysis, an electric field of 2 kV/mm can induce the rhombohedral-cubic phase change at room temperature. As a result of the enhancement in structural symmetry, both the down-conversion and up-conversion PL emissions become weakened significantly (> 70%). Similar reductions in PL intensity have also been observed in the ceramic undergone the transition initiated by thermal heating. However, as the phase transition is not reversible, the modulation of PL emissions cannot be restored upon the removal of the electric field. Another ferroelectric host 0.94Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-0.06BaTiO3 (BNT-6BT) has then been used for enhancing the extent and degree of reversibility of the electric field-driven PL modulation. BNT-6BT is an nonergodic relaxor exhibiting a butterfly-shaped strain hysteresis and good piezoelectric properties at room temperature. At temperatures above the ferroelectric-relaxor transition temperature (TF‑R ∼75C), it features a large and reversible strain owing to the thermally induced ergodicity. Our results have revealed that 1 mol% Eu can lower the TF-R of BNT-6BT via the introduction of composition and charge disorders that disrupts the original long-range ferroelectric macrodomains into randomly dynamic and weakly correlated polar nanoregions (PNRs). As a result, the ceramic becomes an ergodic relaxor at room temperature, giving a constricted polarization hysteresis loop and sprout-shaped strain hysteresis loop with a negligible remanent strain at zero electric field. Owing to the high degree of ergodicity, the ceramic exhibits a reversible transformation from the ergodic relaxor state to a metastable ferroelectric state under a high electric field. Because of the presence the presence of random PNRs with different symmetries of R3C and P4bm which are weakly correlated and free to rotate, the system quickly restores to the state with the lower free energy after the removal of external electric field, and thus giving a large and reversible strain (~ 0.45% at 7 kV/mm). The ceramic also exhibits strong down-conversion photoluminescence emissions that can also be modulated by an external electric field. Unlike the Pr-doped BCTZ ceramics, the real-time PL modulation in Eu-doped BNT-6BT ceramics is reversible and of high degree (~ 40%), and is not be attributed to the electric field-induced phase transition. As evidenced by in-situ X-ray diffraction analysis, the external electric field does not induce any significant phase transition but a reversible change in dimensions of the ceramic lattices, which is in agreement with the observed large electric field-induced strain. Based on the results, it is suggested that the real-time electric field-modulation of PL is attributed to the reversible changes in structural symmetry (giant strain arisen from PNRs’ interaction) and then the local crystal field in the ergodic relaxor. Tb/Eu-codoped BNT-6BT relaxor ferroelectrics have also been successfully fabricated for further investigating the mechanism of PL modulation and the feasibility of modulating the emission color by external electric fields. Among the systems, the BNT-6BT ceramics co-doped with 0.5 mol% Tb and 0.4 mol% Eu exhibits the highest degree of ergodicity, as evidenced by a high-temperature dielectric relaxation and ferroelectric characteristics such as polarization and strain hysteresis loops. The reversibility of the electric field-induced structural symmetry changes is substantiated by the in situ Raman results. The energy transfer process between Tb3+ and Eu3+ has been investigated for elucidating the mechanisms of PL modulations. Our results demonstrate that more dynamic and weakly correlated PNRs are formed after the introduction of Tb3+ and Eu3+. As a result, the ceramics become more ergodic, exhibiting not only a reversible transition between the randomly oriented PNRs and unstable ordered ferroelectric domains under an electric field, but also a transformation between P4bm and R3c PNRs. The resulting reduction in structural symmetry modifies the local field around the luminescent centers and then enhances their photoluminescence emissions. However, the enhancement in the red emissions of Eu3+ is cancelled out because of the impeded energy transfer from Tb3+ to Eu3+ caused by the boosted radiative emissions at 544 nm of Tb3+. Accordingly, the overall emission color can be modulated reversibly from orange to green by an electric field of 7 kV/mm.

15206914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206914.value: Rare earth-doped lead-free ferroelectric ceramics with tunable photoluminescence (PL) properties have been successfully developed, and the mechanisms of modulating the PL emissions have been elucidated together with the evidences of the in-situ structural measurements. The characteristics of ferroelectric oxides, such as polarization switching, phase transition and relaxor ergodicity, have been utilized for realizing the real-time and reversible modulation of PL emissions. As a result of the changes in structural symmetry and then crystal field around the luminescent center induced by external electric fields, the PL emissions intensity and color of the rare earth-doped ferroelectric ceramics can be effectively and reversibly modulated. For the normal ferroelectric ceramics having a phase transition temperature near room temperature such as BCTZ and BZT, a low electric field can induce the transition and then a change in structural symmetry; e.g., an increase in structural symmetry in BCTZ arising from the tetragonal-rhombohedral transition and that in BZT arising from the rhombohedral-cubic transition. The increase in structural symmetry leads to a decrease in the local crystal field around the luminescent centers such as Pr in BCTZ and Er in BZT, and then a significant reduction in PL emission intensity in accordance with the Judd-Ofelt theory. However, as the phase transition is relatively stable upon the removal of the electric field, the modulation of PL emission is not reversible. On the other hand, the PL emission of the Pr-BCTZ can be modulated reversibly by electric fields via the switching of its polarization. As compared to the phase transition, the resulting structural change and then the extent of the PL modulation are smaller. Besides the phase transition and polarization switching, we have also demonstrated that the PL emission can be considerably and reversibly modulated by piezoelectric or electric field-induced strain. Via the doping with 1 mol% Eu, the degree of ergodicity of BNT-6BT ceramic increases significantly and the ceramic becomes ergodic at room temperature. It contains more polar nanoregions that are randomly oriented and weakly correlated. Owing to the presence of different symmetries of R3C and P4bm, the polar nanoregions can be aligned effectively by an applied field and restore almost completely to the random orientation upon the removal of the field, and thus providing a large and reversible strain. Together with the resulting lattice distortion, the local crystal field around Eu3+ and then the PL emission are modulated considerably (~40%) in a reversible and in-situ manner.

15206914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206914.value: The Eu-doped BNT-6BT relaxor ferroelectrics that exhibit large and reversible PL modulation under electric fields at room temperature should find potential applications in optoelectronic industries. The ferroelectrics in thin film form should be of great interest for investigation not only for research but also application purposes. Based on the inter-relationships between structural distortion, macroscopic strain and photoluminescence established in this work, multifunctional materials with better tunable photoluminescence responses can be developed.

15206914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206914.value: We have realized real-time field-induced photoluminescence modulation in bulk lead-free ferroelectric ceramics doped with rare earth elements. As compared with thin film samples, bulk ceramics have advantages of simple fabrication, low cost, and high emission intensity. Our results reveal that an applied electric field induces not only typical polarization switching and minor crystal deformation, but also phase transformation of certain normal ferroelectric ceramics. The electric field-induced phase transformation is irreversible and engenders dominant effect on the modulation of photoluminescence emissions as a result of an increase in structural symmetry. We have have also found that the doping of Eu can transform a typical bismuth sodium titanate-based ferroelectric relaxor to become ergodic at room temperature. It contains more polar nanoregions that facilitates the production of large and reversible strain and structural changes. By virtue of this, both the extent and degree of reversibility of photoluminescence modulation are enhanced considerably, and room-temperature in situ tunable photoluminescence response is then achieved under electric field. Moreover, the inter-relationships between structural distortion, macroscopic strain and photoluminescence has been established, which is essential not only for understanding the underlying mechanism but also for developing multifunctional materials with tunable photoluminescence responses.

15207414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207414.value: To alleviate the recurrent traffic congestion problem in Hong Kong, recent attention has been given to develop Traffic Control and Surveillance Systems (TCSS). The potential benefits to be gained from development of TCSS for improvement of network degradability are also substantial under conditions with non-recurrent congestions due to bad weather and/or incidents. Reliability and control issues have become very important and critical in making the TCSS more efficient in congested networks with uncertainties over the year. This project proposes a reliability-based two-tier dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) model for modeling the interaction between local-area and network-wide traffic control and surveillance systems under recurrent and non-recurrent congestion conditions. The traffic model proposed in this project would make full use of the available data from multiple sensor systems (traffic data) and the historical data (weather and incident data). The first-order (mean) and second-order (variance and covariance) statistical properties of the traffic data are investigated to facilitate the traffic flow estimation in the whole network with stochastic variations on road traffic over time. This project proposes to develop a reliability-based two-tier DTA model for estimating the local-area and network-wide traffic flows so as to assess the impacts of TCSS on road network with uncertainties over the whole year. The first stage of the project will develop a reliability-based two-tier DTA model to estimate the traffic flow variations at local-area and network-level with taking account the mean, variance and covariance of input data over the year. The second stage of the project will calibrate and validate the developed model under degradable road network conditions caused by adverse weather and incidents, in which the stochastic fundamental diagrams between traffic flows, densities and speeds will be calibrated for local-area and network-wide road networks in the study area with the use of the traffic data and historical data over the whole year. With taking account the stochastic traffic variation under different conditions over the year, the third and fourth stages of the project will make use of the developed model for reliability-based optimization of the traffic control strategies (such as lane control on highways and traffic signal control on urban roads) and optimization of the traffic surveillance systems (e.g. number and location of traffic sensors) respectively. Finally, all the analyses and developments will be demonstrated with case studies in Hong Kong. 為了有效解決香港日益嚴重的交通擁堵問題，必須要藉助於交通控制與交通監測系統（Traffic Control and Surveillance Systems, TCSS）。 TCSS可以有效提升交通網絡的可靠性，不論是在常態擁堵還是在惡劣天氣與/或交通事故誘發的非常態擁堵情況下，TCSS都會產生極大的效益。對於經常遭受不確定性因素影響的擁擠交通路網，可靠性成為十分重要並且非常關鍵的衡量TCSS應用效果的指標。本項目將提出一個基於可靠性的兩階動態交通分配模型，該模型網絡加載採用宏觀與微觀相結合的方法，從而體現局部路網與全局路網之間的相互作用，在此基礎上研究基於可靠性的交通控制與交通監測模型。本項目將充分利用現有的多源交通數據、氣象數據和事故數據，利用均值、方差和協方差等數據的統計特徵，開展交通網絡可靠性分析，狀態估計，以及模型驗證工作。 項目研究重點是提出基於可靠性的兩階動態交通分配模型，預測局部路網和全局路網的狀態，從而評估TCSS對於不確定性道路網絡的影響。項目第一階段工作是發展基於可靠性的兩階動態交通分配模型，估計局部路網和全局路網交通狀態，利用全年數據的均值、方差和協方差評估網絡狀態波動情況。項目第二階段工作是標定上述模型的參數並對模型的應用效果進行驗證，主要考慮惡劣天氣與交通事故誘發的網絡能力降低這一狀況；根據全年曆史數據，對局部路網和全局路網的隨機基本圖進行標定。項目第三和第四階段工作是應用所提出的基於可靠性的兩階動態交通分配模型開展交通控制策略優化（包括快速路車道控制和城市道路信號控制）和交通監測系統優化（包括檢測器佈局）研究，同時考慮全年中交通網絡狀態隨機波動的影響，以提升可靠性為主要目標。最終選擇香港的實際路網進行實例研究，展現所提出模型的應用價值。

15207414.label: Realisation of objectives
15207414.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, an analytical reliability-based dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) model was proposed for prediction of traffic flow and travel time distribution on links (see publication nos. (1) and (12)). In the proposed model, the stochastic link performance function is used to depict the link travel time variation so as to capture the stochastic effects induced by non-recurrent congestion. The proposed DTA model can predict the mean and the standard deviation of route travel time. Hence, the route travel time according to the given reliability level, i.e., percentile value of route travel time, can be obtained. Another bi-level programming model was proposed for dynamic journey time estimation (DJTE) (see publication no. (2)). In the proposed model, the objective of the upper-level problem is a weighed least squared function to minimize the difference of mean and standard deviation between the observed and estimated path travel times. In the lower-level problem, the reliability-based DTA model is employed to account for travelers’ path choice behaviors under supply uncertainty. Numerical examples were used to illustrate the application of the proposed DJTE model. Based on the proposed DJTE model, a database of estimated traffic conditions can be established for journey time prediction (see publication no. (13)). The journey time prediction is formulated as a multi-level k-NN model. Similar records in terms of link flows, mean and standard deviation of path journey times in the database are selected for predicting the path journey times. In connection to the project objective 2, the effects of rainfall intensity on the heteroscedastic traffic speed dispersion were studied (see publication no. (4)) based on the traffic and rainfall intensity data in Hong Kong. The coefficient of variation of speed (CVS) was employed to measure the vehicular traffic speed dispersion. A generalized function of CVS with the effects of rainfall intensity was proposed, calibrated, and validated with different sets of empirical data. The generalized function of CVS can be used for assessing and modeling the level-of-service performance of urban roads under adverse weather conditions. The network reliability affected by traffic incident was also studied (see publication nos. (1) and (12)). When incident happens, significant traffic delay was induced; consequently, network reliability was decreased. If the traffic incident duration becomes longer, the impact will be more serious. Numerical example was conducted to demonstrate the impact of incident duration on the network reliability. In relation to the project objective 3, various traffic control strategies such as speed limit control (see publication no. (1)), lane-changing control (see publication no. (5)), location tax credit scheme (see publication no. (6)), road pricing (see publication no. (7)) and traffic signal control (see publication no. (16)) have been investigated. The impacts of a traffic incident on the on-time arrival probability with and without dynamic speed limit control have been examined (see publication no. (1)). The numerical results show that, under certain circumstances, the speed limit control can reduce the total network delay during the time intervals with a traffic incident. A novel mesoscopic multilane model was proposed to enable simultaneous simulation of mandatory and discretionary lane-changing behaviors to realistically capture multilane traffic dynamics (see publication no. (5)). The proposed model can be used to assess the dynamic mesoscopic multilane traffic state and predict the impact of traffic incident or lane control strategy. Another urban system equilibrium model was proposed for design of a tradable location tax credit scheme to balance traffic congestion and environmental externalities (see publication no. (6)). An analytical model for maximizing the social welfare was also proposed to determine the optimal toll level and location simultaneously with consideration of travel time uncertainty (see publication no. (7)). In addition, to investigate the stochastic features in urban traffic dynamics, a stochastic link flow model was proposed for signalized traffic networks with demand uncertainties due to recurrent and non-recurrent conditions (see publication no. (16)). The effects of connected automated vehicles on the design of the freeway traffic control schemes have also been studied (see publication nos. (11) and (14)). A multiclass multilane cell transmission model was developed to simulate traffic flow dynamics mixed with connected automated vehicles and regular human-piloted vehicles by capturing the interaction between these two vehicle classes. The effects of variations in headway and safety gap distributions with respect to different vehicle-class proportions and the impact of speed limit control on the fundamental diagram are explicitly considered. Furthermore, the effects of the time-varying nature of travel demand on the behavior of macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) network traffic dynamics were investigated for design of high-level control strategies such as perimeter control and traffic rationing (see publication nos. (9) and (10)). With respect to the project objective 4, an automatic traffic incident detection algorithm was proposed for traffic surveillance purposes on the basis of the traffic data obtained from fixed traffic sensors in Hong Kong (see publication no. (3)). In the proposed algorithm, continuous detection thresholds are adopted. These continuous detection thresholds are generated by the calibrated generalized detection threshold functions in which both pre-incident traffic and rain conditions are modeled explicitly. The results of case study show that consideration of rain effect for determination of the detection threshold could improve the overall traffic incident detection performance. The effects of the number and the location of traffic sensors for network-wide travel time estimation was also studied (see publication no. (8)). The numerical example indicates that the number and the location of the sensors have a significant impact on the accuracy and quality of the travel time estimates. An optimization model was also developed for determination of the optimal number and location of traffic sensors for traffic surveillance systems under different recurrent and non-recurrent conditions (see publication no. (15)).

15207414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207414.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, reliability-based two-tier dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) models were proposed for estimation and prediction of traffic flow and/or travel time distribution on links (see publication nos. (1), (2), (12) and (13)). Link travel time variations were considered to capture the stochastic effects induced by non-recurrent congestion. Numerical examples were used to illustrate the application of the proposed traffic models. In respect to the project objective 2, a generalized function of the coefficient of variation of speed (CVS) was calibrated and validated using different sets of empirical data in Hong Kong with consideration of the effects of rainfall intensity. The generalized function of CVS can be used for assessing and modeling the level-of-service performance of urban roads under adverse weather conditions (see publication no. (4)). The impact of traffic incident on network reliability was also studied (see publication nos. (1) and (12)). Numerical results show that, in the case of 2-lanes blocked traffic incident, the network reliability drops from 86% to 75% when the incident duration increases from 10 min to 30 min. With regard to the project objective 3, various traffic control strategies were investigated with consideration of travel time and/or demand uncertainty due to recurrent and non-recurrent traffic conditions. These traffic control strategies include speed limit control (see publication nos. (1), (11) and (14)), lane-changing control (see publication no. (5)), location tax credit scheme (see publication no. (6)), road pricing (see publication no. (7)), traffic signal control (see publication no. (16)), perimeter control and traffic rationing scheme (see publication nos. (9) and (10)). A macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) framework was also developed for analyzing the network traffic dynamics for design of the robust control strategies. In connection to the project objective 4, an optimization model was developed for determination of the optimal number and location of traffic sensors for traffic surveillance systems under different recurrent and non-recurrent conditions (see publication no. (15)). The effects of the number and the location of traffic sensors for network-wide travel time estimation was also studied (see publication no. (8)). In addition, on the basis of the traffic data obtained from fixed traffic sensors in Hong Kong, an automatic traffic incident detection algorithm was proposed for traffic surveillance purposes (see publication no. (3)).

15207414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207414.value: In this project, various traffic models were proposed for assessing the impacts of traffic control and surveillance on road network degradability under adverse weather and incident conditions. However, the traffic control strategies have been studied separately under different traffic conditions. Thus, further study is recommended to develop an optimal control framework that integrates several traffic control schemes for improving the efficiency of the road networks. Empirical experiments under controlled environments can also be conducted in future study to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework. Regarding the development of traffic surveillance systems, the numerical results show that the number and location of traffic sensors have a significant impact on the accuracy and quality of traffic estimates. Thus, the sensor location problem merits further study. The proposed model can be extended to optimize the multiple traffic sensors for estimation of OD traffic demand and link/path travel times in road network with uncertainty separately and simultaneously. The estimated results can then be used for assessing the network performance for traffic management and control in road network with uncertainties.

15207414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207414.value: Development of Traffic Control and Surveillance Systems (TCSS) is essential for alleviation of traffic congestion and improvement of network degradability, particularly under conditions with non-recurrent congestions due to bad weather and/or incidents. This research project thus aims to develop a reliability-based dynamic traffic assignment model to estimate the traffic flows, travel times and their variations over time so as to assess the impacts of TCSS on road network with uncertainties. Various traffic models have been proposed for estimation of the traffic parameters such as flow and travel time. Optimal traffic control strategies and traffic surveillance systems have been studied to improve the network reliability under various recurrent and non-recurrent conditions. The output of this project can help the government and the road authorities to better assess the road network performance under uncertainty conditions. This can be helpful for improving the efficiency and reliability of the road networks particularly in Asian cities with heavy rainfall and frequent traffic incidents.

15207914.label: Project Objectives
15207914.value: Towards a blind and universal DSP platform for arbitrary modulation formats: Future transceivers are expected to simultaneously support multiple modulation formats and it is highly desirable to have a blind and universal DSP platform that is applicable to any modulation format. While some DSP blocks such as CD compensation are format-independent, others such as frequency offset compensation(FOE) are somewhat format dependent. We will formulate a blind and universal FOE algorithm based on optimizing a cost function derived from the product of received signals and their delayed conjugate. In addition, we will study a blind and universal cycle-slip detection and correction algorithm based on examining the evolution of twice estimated phase noise. The FOE accuracy and the reduction in cycle-slip probability will be characterized for each modulation format. The theoretical and simulation results will be verified experimentally. Fast and robust parameter estimation and lightpath initializations: For future EON with heterogeneous traffic patterns and dynamic lightpath provisioning requirements, it is imperative to quickly estimate the channel parameters and signal characteristics for fast link initialization. We will study a fast, blind and universal DSP algorithm that use a minimal number of symbols to obtain rough estimates of timing phase, polarization rotation, frequency offset and carrier phase so that data detection and decision-directed DSP can immediately follow. In addition, for future scenarios in which the modulation format of the incoming signals is not known in advance, we will derive a phase-noise-insensitive modulation format identification technique based on the statistical distributions of the received signal powers. The theoretical and simulation results will be verified experimentally.

15207914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207914.value: Digital coherent communications define the current generation of long-haul optical transceivers operating at 100Gb/s and above. They enable high spectral efficiency transmissions with electronic digital signal processing(DSP) units to compensate various transmission impairments and laser imperfections. Moving forward, due to emerging data center, cloud computing/storage applications and the increasing dominance of tablets and smart phones, the nature of future Internet traffic is envisioned to be much more dynamic, unpredictable and diverse in bit rate and reach demands. Major telecommunication service providers are desperately searching for new solutions to accommodate such unprecedented traffic patterns and ensure high quality of service. Technologies enabling variable rate/bandwidth transmissions, dynamic lightpath provisioning or other forms of flexibility that can adapt to network conditions and traffic demands are generally described under the framework of Software Defined Networking(SDN) or Elastic Optical Networks(EON). Such flexibilities, if properly leveraged, provide a whole new dimension in operating networks much more efficiently. EON has been investigated and long desired by the networking community for years, but the indisputable upcoming trend of heterogeneous traffic and the appropriateness of digital coherent communications hardware for flexible transmissions have now fueled EON as the most important research area in optical communications and networking. EON is a multi-disciplinary area and research advances can range from device physics that enable variable-bandwidth filtering to control plane protocols for intelligent routing and wavelength assignment to maximize network efficiency. The relevant physical layer aspects include signaling and DSP technologies supporting transmissions of arbitrary bit rates/bandwidth/spectral efficiency/network paths. Preliminary advances on this front are reported in the past year or two but a fully flexible transceiver to truly unleash the potentials of EON is very far away from reality at the moment. The objectives of the proposed research are to address key physical layer issues in realizing flexible transceivers for EON. In particular, we will 1)develop blind and universal receiver DSP algorithms for arbitrary modulation formats;2) investigate and demonstrate high-speed rate-adaptive transmissions using time-domain hybrid QAM;3) derive fast and robust channel estimation and signal characterization techniques for dynamic lightpath initializations. The successful completion of the proposed research will provide and connect the vital components for a fully flexible digital coherent transceiver. The crucial and unique insights developed will allow system designers to build intelligence and adaptability in the physical layer, which in turn contribute to the overarching goal of EON in supporting the upcoming era of ultra-high-speed, heterogeneous and dynamic optical communications. 現今工作在100Gb/s及以上速率的長距離光收發模組主要採用數字化相干光通信技術，實現了高頻譜效率的光信號傳輸，同時能在電域中通過數字信號處理技術對傳輸過程中信號的損傷、激光器的非理想性進行補償。在不遠的將來，隨著更多大數據中心的建立、雲計算/雲存儲的應用以及各種智能可攜式裝置的使用，可以預見用戶對網絡資源的需求將會變得更加動態和不可預見性。同時網絡資源的分配會根據用戶對速率和接入距離的不同需求而變得更加靈活多樣。如今各大電信運營商都在為滿足這種空前的多樣化用戶需求尋找新的網絡解決方案以保證高的服務品質。通常我們把那些採用了速率/帶寬可調的傳輸技術、動態光路調配技術以及其它可根據網絡鏈路條件和帶寬需求而靈活配置硬體的網絡歸為軟體定義網絡（Software Defined Networking--SDN）或者彈性光網絡(Elastic Optical Networks--EON)。這些技術將能使網絡的運營和使用更加有效率。在網絡研究領域，與彈性網絡相關的研究已經開展多時，但是隨著近年來對互聯網流量需求的迅猛增長以及數字相干光通信這種適合靈活組網傳輸技術的發展，現在彈性光網絡成為了光通信與組網中研究熱點。彈性光網絡技術涉及到多個學科最先進的領域，研究範圍從最底層的物理器件比如帶寬可調的光濾波器一直到實現網絡效率最大化的智慧路由與波長分配控制平面協議。其中相關的物理層技術包括了基於數字信號處理的能實現任意比特速率/帶寬/頻譜效率/網絡路由路徑信號傳輸的技術。雖然在過去的一兩年裡彈性光網絡的研究取得了一些初步進展，但是能真正發揮彈性光網絡優勢的完全可靈活配置的光收發器仍然離我們很遠。 本課題將以可靈活配置光收發器中物理層中的若干關鍵技術為研究目標。具體來說包括1）設計與碼型無關的任何碼型通用的接收端數字信號處理算法；2）研究並實驗展示使用時域混合QAM調製碼型的速率自適應高速信號傳輸；3）為動態光路由的初始化設計快速可靠的通道估計和信號特徵估計算法。 本課題的圓滿完成能夠為完全可靈活配置數字相干收發器提供關鍵的組成部分。該課題研究所取得的重要和獨到的經驗和成果將會為系統設計師構建具有智能與適應性的網路物理層提供指導，並為實現以能支持未來超高速、異構和動態的光通信的彈性光網絡做出了貢獻。

15207914.label: Realisation of objectives
15207914.value: The objectives of the proposed research has been largely achieved. We have developed numerous modulation format identification schemes beyond the use of statistical distributions of the received signal powers as stated in the original proposal. We have also developed quick polarization tracking algorithms based on radius-directed linear kalman filter for fast link initialization. Monitoring of important physical state parameters such as OSNR and modulation format and bit rates are also derived for universal transceivers are also developed as part of the project. We have also developed the cycle slip detection and correction technique as stated in the project objectives and we researched and submitted the work 3 months after the announcement of the results published the work "Non-data-aided and universal cycle slip detection and correction for coherent communication systems" by Y. Gao et el at Optics Express vol. 22, no. 25 at Dec 2014 . Finally, we had some preliminary investigations for universal FOE algorithm but we realized that the the performance improvements compared to other techniques is not significant and also FOE has been considered a solved issue. We have therefore put more focus on the objective of modulation format identification.

15207914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207914.value: To enable flexible transceivers at the physical layer, one will need to determine the modulation format, monitor the state of the link such as OSNR and preferably use the same set of DSP for different modulation formats at the receiver. We have derived low-cost methods to monitor the OSNR of the link using low-bandwidth coherent receivers and RF power measurements. The proposed method is also insensitive to cascaded filtering effects in variable link length conditions. We also developed polarization state tracking methodologies using Kalman fitering For modulation format identification techniques, we showed that it can be achieved using signal power distributions and asynchronous delay-tap sampling. We have also studied and laid down some ground work for a universal DSP for arbitrary modulation formats including cycle slip detection and correction As a recognition of our work in the field, we are also invited to write a review paper in Journal of Lightwave Technology on Optical Performance Monitoring in 2016.

15207914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207914.value: Flexible transceivers can also be extended to variable bandwidth signals and probabilistic shaped signals and this will be attempted in the future through potential new seed funding

15207914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207914.value: Internet traffic is becoming more dynamic with the popularity of short-lived high speed videos, cloud computing and Internet of Things application. As traditional optical networks are built to handle steady traffic with constant bit rate, this project studied and developed key digital signal processing strategies to handle variable-speed internet traffic in real time and opens up new dimension to cater for emerging internet traffic patterns and enable more efficient optical network operation

15208014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208014.value: 人們常常使用照片作為事件發生的證據。 識別數字圖像的來源可以增加人們對照片作為證據的信賴，這在執法案例中十分重要，因為尋找非法圖像的來源可以幫助確定那些非法圖像是否來自特定的相機或由其他地方下載。 目前源相機識別的最先進技術是利用一種名為圖像不均一響應(PRNU)的傳感器噪聲進行相關性計算。但是提取的傳感器噪聲容易受到去噪產生的偽影和場景內容的影響。如果測試照片過暗，過度曝光或有複雜的紋路，識別的準確率會非常低。而且基於相關性的識別方法不適用於經過幾何變形的圖像，因為噪聲圖形將會跟隨幾何變形而改變。這些是當前源相機識別技術所面臨的挑戰。 在源相機識別中，對於解決場景內容以及幾何變形問題的需求將越來越多。 這個項目的目的是研發有效的源相機識別技術。 我們先研究不同去噪算法對噪聲中偽影的影響。然後我們將試驗基於特征的源相機識別方法。 我們提議提取兩種不同的特征。 他們是圖像特征和噪聲殘留特征。 圖像特征是用來量化場景內容的複雜度。噪聲殘留特征包含了設備的獨有特征。通過這兩種特征的組合， 只有不受場景內容影響的可靠特征才會被用來識別圖像的來源。我們提議研究採用擁有平移，旋轉以及縮放不變性特征從而解決幾何變形問題。 這樣我們所提出的源相機識別方法對於處理場景內容和幾何變形問題是有創新性的。而且，因為本方法只需從圖像中提取一部分的特征，所以跟基於相關性計算的方法相比，它的計算複雜度將會降低。這使得我們提議的方案切實可行。 鑒於現今社交媒體的普及和大量的數字圖像的出現，我們所提議的源相機識別將可以增加人們對數字照片信任。 開發源相機識軟件工具對於推進數字圖像取證領域的發展是很有價值的。

15208014.label: Realisation of objectives
15208014.value: The objective of this project is to develop effective and efficient techniques for source camera identification. State-of-the-art techniques for source camera identification extract a type of sensor noise called Photo-response Non-uniformity (PRNU) and perform correlation-based identification. The extracted PRNU is, however, sensitive towards the denoising artifacts and scene content. The identification accuracy will be very low if the testing photo is too dark, overly exposed or has complicated textures. We have studied the effect of artifacts from a number of denoising filters on the source identification accuracy. It is found that different denoising artifacts introduce different types of artifacts to the PRNU signal. In order to reliably extract the PRNU signal, a novel wavelet-based denoising approach has been developed. The denoising operation is applied adaptively according to the region characteristics so as to remove the scene content and denoising artifacts found in the PRNU signal. In order to test the effectiveness of the proposed denoising method, extensive experimental works have been carried out. Our experimental results shown that the proposed method can improve the camera identification rate and the false acceptance rate. The improvement is significant for highly compressed photos. Details regarding the proposed denoising method have been reported in a conference paper published in 2015 International Conference on Noise and Fluctuations (ICNF). Besides, existing source camera identification methods always consider the noise magnitude as features to characterize the severity of the scene content problem. While the noise magnitude can act as a feature for characterizing scene content problem, it can also be considered as a feature for strong PRNU signal incurred in the particular camera sensor. Motivated by this observation, instead of using the noise magnitude as the feature, local variance is used as a feature to characterize the scene content artifact. The local variance is estimated from a set of pixels with similar textures. Hence it is a more reliable feature than the noise magnitude of a single pixel. We have performed experiments to verify the effectiveness of using the local variance on characterizing scene content artifacts. Results show that the local variance relates linearly with the severity of the scene content problem. This implies that the local variance can potentially be used for reliable identification. With the use of local-variance as features, a local variance based method is developed for source camera identification. The sensitivity of the method towards the scene content problem is reduced by using the local-variance as features. We have conducted both source camera identification and source camera classification experiments on 19 cameras. The cameras covered a wide range of brands and models. Besides, multiple devices from the same brand/model were also included. Experimental results show that our proposed local variance feature give reliable detection statistics. This in turn makes our proposed method outperforms other existing state-of-the-art algorithms in both source camera identification and source camera classification problems. Besides, the improvement is more significant when the image size becomes smaller. Details regarding the method and results were summarized in a paper published in Digital Investigation in 2017. The geometric distortion is a serious problem as the noise residue will become distorted by operations such as translation, scaling and rotation. The translation problem can be solved by using a sliding window based correlation calculation. However, scaling and rotation are more difficult. Our studies found that the PRNU is very sensitive to the geometric distortion. A transformation model to relate key points is often used to compensate for the geometric distortion in image registration problem. Using significant PRNU location, a least square framework has been developed to estimate model parameters. Due to the noise like characteristics of the PRNU and the noise residue, the estimation of the model parameters depends strongly on the scene content. In order to reduce the scene content problem, features are extracted from the binarized PRNU signal. It is found that the estimation from the binarized PRNU signal is more robust than that from the original PRNU signal. In summary, all the objectives have been achieved. Artifacts from different denoising algorithms and their effect on the accuracy of the source camera identification have been studied. Using the noise magnitude as features, a wavelet-based denoising approach has been developed for source camera identification. Besides, the local variance has been employed as more reliable features for characterizing the scene content and denoising artifacts than the noise magnitude. Simulations in both source camera identification and source camera classification problems have been carried out. To solve the geometric distortion problem, binarized PRNU signal has been used for the least square estimation of the model parameters. Simulations have confirmed that features from the binarized PRNU signal are more robust than those from the original PRNU signal. Details of the algorithms and their simulation results have been reported in the following two papers: • Chao Shi, Ngai-Fong law, Frank H.F. 15208014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208014.value: The objective of this project is to develop effective and efficient techniques for source camera identification. Existing source camera identification methods are strongly affected by the scene content and denoising artifacts. We have performed a thorough study of the artifacts from different denoising algorithms and their effect on the accuracy of the source camera identification. To reduce these artifacts, a wavelet-based method based on the noise magnitude has been developed. Experimental results have shown that the wavelet-based method can effectively suppress the denoising and scene content artifacts. The improvement is significant for highly compressed photos. As people often share photos in social media, the proposed method allows the source camera to be identified accurately even though photos in social media are highly compressed. Instead of using noise magnitude at a single pixel to characterize denoising and scene content artifacts, local variance from a group of neighboring pixels can be analyzed. We have shown both theoretically and experimentally that the local variance is more reliable than the noise magnitude in characterizing denoising and scene content artifacts. Using the local variance as features, an algorithm has been developed to solve both source camera identification and source camera classification problems. Our experimental results show that local variance based method outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms. Improvement is significant when the image size is small. Thus reliable camera source can be achieved even for thumbnail images. To solve the geometric distortion problem, a least square framework for obtaining invariant features has been studied in which the binarized PRNU signal is used for the least square estimation of the model parameters. Simulations have confirmed that features from the binarized PRNU signal are more robust than those from the original PRNU signal. Details of the proposed algorithms and simulation results have been reported in the following two papers: • Chao Shi, Ngai-Fong law, Frank H.F. Leung and Wan-Chi Siu, “A Local Variance Based Approach to Alleviate the Scene Content Interference for Source Camera Identification”, Digital Investigation, Vol. 22, 74-87, Sept 2017. • Kwun-fung Lau, N.F. Law and W.C. Siu, “Use of Sensor Noise for Source Identification”, 23rd International Conf on Noise and Fluctuations, Xian, June 2-5, 2015, China Besides, we are finalizing a software package for PRNU-based source camera identification. After performing the final test, the package will be used for demonstration in both undergraduate teaching and research.

15208014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208014.value: Existing PRNU-based source camera identification focuses on images only. Due to the popularity of videos nowadays, it would be good to extend the source identification to videos. Despite that, PRNU-based source camera identification from videos has certain limitations. First, video content usually does not change much from one frame to another frame. Thus, artifacts in the noise residues may accumulate if consecutive frames are used to construct the PRNU signal. This in turn will affect the accuracy of the source identification. Second, conditions for capturing the videos may change. For example, image focus may be changed during the course of video capture. Third, video signals often have higher compression than images. The video signal may be transmitted through network or uploaded to the cloud for storage. Blocking artifacts may appear in which the noise residues will be affected. One future direction is to extend the PRNU-based method for verifying the source of the received video clips.

15208014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208014.value: People often use photos as proof of the occurrence of certain events. Identifying the source of a digital photo is an important step to gain people’s trust on the use of digital photos to provide such a proof. State-of-the-art techniques for source camera identification extract a type of sensor noise called PRNU and perform correlation-based identification. The PRNU is, however, sensitive towards the denoising and scene content artifacts. The correlation-based identification method cannot deal with geometric distortion. These are the challenges faced by existing techniques. In this project, we have developed effective techniques four source camera identification. Two novel algorithms have been developed for source camera identification. The first algorithm uses wavelets and the noise magnitude to compensate for the denoising and scene content artifacts while the second algorithm uses local variance as features in developing a robust source camera identification method. To solve for the geometric distortion method, features are extracted from the binarized noise pattern which are then used for identifying the model parameters for compensating the geometric distortion. Extensive experimental works have been carried out to study the robustness of these methods. Using our proposed methods, robust source camera identification can be achieved.

15208314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208314.value: Oxygenated volatile organic compounds (OVOCs), composed of alcohols, aldehydes and ketones, account for a significant fraction of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). It can be produced directly from biogenic and anthropogenic sources, or formed secondarily from the oxidation of VOCs in the atmosphere. OVOCs play an important role in the production of ozone and secondary pollutants in the troposphere, and have a comparable effect on the atmospheric oxidizing capacity to that of non-methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs). Compared with studies on NMHCs, the investigation of OVOCs is much less common which is because the precise quantification of these species is more difficult than NMHCs. Hong Kong, as a part of the fast-developing Pearl River Delta (PRD) region, is experiencing an increasing ozone trend and regional photochemical smog problem, which significantly reduces visibility and adversely affects human health. Although previous studies demonstrated a substantial contribution of OVOCs to ozone formation in Hong Kong and the PRD region, these studies mainly focused on aldehydes and ketones, while studies on other key components such as alcohols are rare. Moreover, the sources and characteristics of OVOCs, essential to evaluate their impact on atmospheric ozone formation, are currently not well established in Hong Kong. Airborne OVOCs are typically collected onto solid sorbent cartridge and then extracted by solvents for further analysis. Several drawbacks have been identified for this method such as the long sampling intervals and various interferences. The long sampling interval may lead to the underestimation of OVOCs concentrations due to the decay of OVOC species. Therefore, reliable and high temporal-resolution methods for OVOCs analysis are extremely required in Hong Kong and the PRD region. We propose a three-year systematic study to better understand the sources, atmospheric transformation, transportation, and fate of OVOCs in Hong Kong. Proton-transfer-reaction mass-spectrometry (PTR-MS), with high sensitivity (10-100 pptv) and rapid response time (1-10 seconds), will be firstly used in Hong Kong to investigate OVOCs emissions from various sources. The sources and distributions of OVOCs will be examined through an intensive sampling campaign, and the impact of OVOCs on ozone formation will be evaluated through computer modeling. The real-time study of OVOCs can generate sufficient data to fulfill the sample size requirement for source apportionment, and give further insight into the characteristics of OVOCs in Hong Kong, which are very useful in formulating effective VOC control strategies to control ozone pollution in Hong Kong and the PRD region. 由醇、醛、酮類化合物組成的含氧可揮發性有機物(OVOCs)是可揮發性有機物(VOCs)的重要組成部分。含氧可揮發性有機物可直接來源於人為排放和生物質排放，也可來源於大氣中可揮發性有機物經氧化反應的二次生成。含氧可揮發性有機物在對流層中對於臭氧以及二次污染物的形成有重要的作用，而且在大氣層中比非甲烷碳氫化合物擁有更強的氧化能力。相比於非甲烷碳氫化合物，關於含氧可揮發性有機物的研究則相對較少，因為這些物質的精確定量化更為困難。香港，作為快速發展的珠江三角洲地區的一部分，正在經歷臭氧持續增長和地區性的光化學煙霧問題，這嚴重降低了能見度並對人體健康造成負面影響。儘管先前的一些研究證實含氧可揮發性有機物對香港及珠江三角洲地區的臭氧形成有大量貢獻，但是這些研究主要集中於醛類和酮類物質，但對於其他種類如醇類方面的研究還比較匱乏。另外，在香港，對於含氧可揮發性有機物的來源、特徵和評估其對大氣中的臭氧生成發麵的研究還不夠完善。 大氣含氧可揮發性有機物通常被採集於固體吸附桶中，然後被溶劑萃取以進行之後的分析。這種方法已被證實有諸如較長的採樣時間和易受多種干擾等一些缺點。較長的採樣時間會導致因含氧可揮發性有機物的降解而低估其濃度。因此，香港及珠江三角洲地區概念股需要可靠且擁有高時間解析度的分析方法。我們提出了一個為期三年的系統的關於香港含氧可揮發性有機物的來源、大氣轉化與轉移的研究計畫。質子轉移反應質譜儀(PTR-MS)擁有高敏感度(10-100 pptv)和快速回應時間(1-10 s)，它將首次被應用於研究香港地區含氧可揮發性有機物的多種排放源。我們會通過密集採樣活動來調查研究含氧可揮發性有機物的來源和分佈，並通過電腦模型來評估其對於臭氧生成的影響。含氧可揮發性有機物的即時線上觀測研究可以為進行來源解析提供足夠多資料和樣本容量，也可以更好地研究其在香港的主要特徵，這有利於提供更為有效的控制策略來更好地控制香港及珠江三角洲地區的臭氧污染。

15208314.label: Realisation of objectives
15208314.value: The proton transfer reaction–mass spectrometry (PTR-MS) technique was firstly introduced to on-line measure OVOCs and VOCs in urban area of Hong Kong. Because the Proton Affinity of formaldehyde (170.4 kcal mol-1) is just slightly higher than that of water (165.2 kcal mol-1), the backward reaction of protonated formaldehyde with H2O can lead to an underestimation of HCHO by PTR-MS. Hence, it is a worldwide issue to be tackled for measuring HCHO by PTR-MS. In this project, the integrated effect of ambient relative humidity (RH) and temperature (T) on formaldehyde measurements by PTR-MS was explored in this study. A Poly 2-D regression was found to be the best nonlinear surface simulation (r = 0.97) of the experimental reaction rate coefficient ratio, ambient RH, and T for formaldehyde measurement. Inter-comparisons were performed between PTR-MS and other traditional VOC and OVOC measurement techniques, namely, (1) offline 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (DNPH) cartridge sampling followed by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis; (2) online gas chromatography (GC) with flame ionization detection (FID); and (3) offline canister sampling followed by GC with mass spectrometer detection (MSD), FID, and electron capture detection (ECD). In general, good agreements were found between PTR-MS and other analytical techniques for OVOC species (i.e. formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, and acetone etc.) and aromatic hydrocarbons with correlation coefficients no less than 0.75. In order to determine the emission profiles of OVOCs from major primary sources in Hong Kong, a roadside study and a tunnel study were conducted to obtain the emission profiles of OVOCs and VOCs from vehicular emissions through both on-line and off-line measuring techniques. The emission factors of OVOCs and VOCs from diesel and non-diesel vehicles were also obtained through this project. And it was found that the emissions of OVOCs, especially for formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, and acetone, were much higher than the other regular VOC species (e.g. benzene, toluene, butane, propane). The distribution of OVOCs and their source contributions from primary emissions and secondary productions in Hong Kong was investigated and determined through the roadside study at Mong Kok Air Quality Monitoring Station. It was found that about 60% of OVOCs were emitted from multiple primary sources, such as diesel/gasoline/LPG vehicular emissions, and solvent usage, and secondary productions contributed 40% of ambient OVOCs in Hong Kong. LPG vehicular emissions was found to be the largest contributor both before and after LPG catalytic convertor replacement programme, however, its contribution decreased from 44.7% to 37.8%. The ozone formation potential of VOCs and OVOCs from LPG vehicular emissions also decreased from 58.6 ppbv O3 ppbv-1 to 25.8 ppbv O3 ppbv-1. All of these changes indicate that the fulfillment of the LPG catalytic convertor replacement programme was effective on reducing LPG vehicular emissions and improve the air quality of Hong Kong. Moreover, diesel vehicular emissions should be paid more attention on the next step to keep improving the air quality of Hong Kong.

15208414.value: 開發新型的獨立新風系統（DOAS）以改善能源效率和環境健康

15208414.label: Project Objectives
15208414.value: Formulate the optimal system configuration and the associated operating parameters for an extra low temperature direct expansion air-conditioning system coupled with an HP heat exchanger (ETHP-DOAS) for achieving dehumidification and cooling requirements under various outdoor and cooling load conditions; Estimate the potential for energy saving, health and environmental benefits of applying the technology in commercial buildings in Hong Kong; Establish performance characteristics of ETHP-DOAS systems; and Provide useful information on the curbing of energy use and improving environmental health quality for air-conditioning in commercial buildings in hot and humid climates.

Estimate the potential for energy saving, health and environmental benefits of applying the technology in commercial buildings in Hong Kong;
Establish performance characteristics of ETHP-DOAS systems; and
