15208414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208414.value: Recent research advocates the use of dedicated outdoor air systems (DOAS) to avoid moisture-related and cross contamination problems for better environmental health. Previous studies focused on the use of active-desiccant technology coupled with chilled ceilings, for which many disadvantages have been reported. The PI has recently completed successful research into the feasible use of DOAS coupled with terminal units, but the environmental health objective could only be realized under some restricted conditions. A novel DOAS for better energy efficiency and environmental health objectives is proposed in this study. The proposed system consists of an extra-low temperature (ET) DOAS coupled with heat pipe (HP) technology. In this system, a multi-stage direct-expansion (DX) air-conditioner will be used to generate ET outdoor air (OA) to be delivered to the conditioned space to mix with return air, and successively enter a HP for heat exchange with exhaust air to become reheated supply air for space cooling. The proposed system (ETHP-DOAS) therefore enables the omission of a cooling device at the conditioned space and the recovery of exhaust air energy for reheating purposes. As such, cooling does not need to be performed at the conditioned space and recirculated-air does not need to be returned to the central air-handler thereby avoiding moisture-related problem and cross contamination for environmental health. Energy savings can be derived from reheating, pumping and fan energy reductions. For generating ETOA, a multi-stage air-conditioner is proposed because of higher equipment efficiency associated with working under higher evaporating temperature (1-stage) and smaller temperature lifts (between evaporator and condenser). The DX air-conditioner is proposed owing to its advantages over water-based installations. Whether or not ETHP-DOAS can achieve better energy efficiency and environmental health objectives depends upon whether ETHP-DOAS can be designed to treat OA to the desired conditions and the heat recovery performance achieved by the HP. In the proposed study, simulation studies will be conducted to identify the optimal configuration and operating parameters, as well as prediction of the potential benefits over conventional systems. Mathematical models for predicting the performance of ETHP-DOAS will be formulated. For validation of the mathematical models, an experimental unit comprising a self-assembled multi-stage DX air-conditioner, a HP, variable speed fans and the associated devices will be assembled and installed in an environmental chamber for laboratory tests. The aim is to provide useful information on how to improve energy and environmental health quality for air-conditioning in hot and humid climates.

15208414.label: Realisation of objectives
15208414.value: A novel dedicated outdoor air system (DOAS) for better energy efficiency and environmental health objectives is proposed in this study. Its performance characteristics, system configuration, and energy and environmental benefits when used in office buildings in Hong Kong were investigated through simulation and pilot studies. The proposed DOAS consists of a multi-stage variable speed direct expansion (DX) air-conditioner as the central system to generate extra-low temperature (XT) outdoor air (OA) to handle the entire space cooling load and a mixing chamber as the terminal system to mix XT OA and return air (RA) to become supply air (SA). For the successful application of the proposed system (XT-DOAS), the major concern is how the multi-stage DX air-conditioner must be designed to achieve the desired air conditions and better energy efficiency under highly variable indoor and outdoor operating conditions. As a preliminary enquiry, performance evaluation of XT-DOAS as compared to a conventional system was performed by simulation studies based on actual equipment performance models and realistic building and system characteristics. The results showed that XT-DOAS as compared to conventional system, is superior for achieving the desired relative humidities; can better achieve the desired thermal comfort conditions; and depends on the type of terminal system (variable air volume (VAV) and constant air volume (CAV)) can save 15.6 % to 22.6% annual energy use for air-conditioning; reduce the annual cumulative number of non-comfortable hours by 31% to 69.4%; and reduce the system exergy loss rate by 13.6% to 18.6%. To further enhance the performance of XT-DOAS, the optimum number of cooling stages and treated OA temperature need to be determined. As the thermodynamic states of moist air entering and leaving individual cooling stages will affect the performance of XT-DOAS, the optimization process requires the development and validation of a coil performance model that takes into account the extra-high and extra-low entering air temperature at the first and the last cooling stages. Factory test data and field measurement data were collected for the model development. Based on the developed model, energy and exergy analyses confirmed that the optimum configuration for XT-DOAS is two cooling stage with a treated OA temperature of 7 °C. Given a better performance of VAV control, the terminal system of XT-DOAS was assumed provided with VAV control. The drawback is the risk of overcooling due to the minimum air flow fraction requirement of VAV system. To maintain space air temperature and to avoid overcooling, conventional VAV (Con_VAV) systems are provided with reheating coil because of the uncertainties in the possible variations in indoor and outdoor conditions thus the fluctuations of cooling demand. To confirm the effective use of the optimized XT-DOAS (without reheat provision) operating under a highly variable indoor and outdoor conditions, a probabilistic approach based on Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 iterations was adopted to investigate the overcooling risk of XT-DOAS as compared to Con_VAV. The results showed that the potential annual overcooling hours using XT-DOAS were 29 hours, which is equivalent to 0.31% long-term percentage of dissatisfied (LPD). These results, as compared to 426 overcooling hours and 1.69% LPD achieved by the typical Con_VAV system, confirmed the excellent performance of XT-DOAS. From the above, the investigation of XT-DOAS can be summarized into four major aspects: the effective use for achieving the desired air conditions and better energy efficiency; the development of a realistic coil performance model; the determination of the optimum configuration; and the assessment of overcooling risk. To conclude, the optimal system configuration and the associated operating parameters for XT-DOAS was formulated; the potential for energy saving, health and environmental benefits of applying the technology in commercial buildings in Hong Kong was estimated, the performance characteristics of XT-DOAS systems was established; and useful information on the curbing of energy use and improving environmental health quality provides useful information on the curbing of energy use and improving environmental health quality for air-conditioning in commercial buildings in hot and humid climates was generated.

15208414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208414.value: Performance evaluation of the proposed XT-DOAS, as compared to conventional system, for achieving better energy efficiency and environmental health objectives, was conducted. A realistic DX coil performance model that covers an exceptionally large entering air temperature range (from 6 °C DB to 35 °C DB), which is absent in the current literature, was successfully developed based on site measurement and manufacturers' factory test data. The configuration of XT-DOAS was optimized for the number of cooling stages and the treated OA temperature. Probabilistic assessment of the overcooling risk of the optimized XT-DOAS and the conventional system with VAV control, both without reheating provisions, was conducted to confirm the better performance of XT-DOAS.

15208414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208414.value: XT-DOAS is a novel concept. There are limitations with the current study. Further works include: 1) Evaluate its feasible application in countries/regions with significantly different climatic and living conditions from that of Hong Kong. 2) Investigate of the influence of SA conditions on the indoor air distribution and thus thermal comfort. 3) Experimental works can be done to identify the optimum air mixing speed at the mixing box whereby condensation can be avoided to achieve environmental health objective. 4) Experimental verifications of performance of the XT-DOAS.

15208414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208414.value: This project aims to evaluate the effective use of a novel dedicated outdoor air system for better energy efficiency and environmental health objectives. In the study, energy simulations, site measurements, manufacturers’ factory test data and Monte Carlo simulations were adopted to identify the performance characteristics, system configuration, and energy and environmental benefits of XT-DOAS when used in office buildings in Hong Kong. The results confirmed the effective use of XT-DOAS for achieving the desired air conditions and better energy efficiency. A realistic coil performance model covering a wide range of entering and leaving air conditions, which is useful for energy simulations and analyses, was developed. The optimum system configuration of XT-DOAS was established. A probabilistic approach, which takes into account the uncertainty in indoor and outdoor conditions, for overcooling risk assessment was developed. The work is original and adds very useful knowledge about the performance of XT-DOAS operating under a range of indoor and outdoor conditions.

15209314.label: Project Objectives
15209314.value: To develop algorithms for capturing 3D data and optimizing the processing of captured 3D data for forming real-time as-built models of a monitored building. This should include: 1) quantifying the trade-offs between the 3D data quality and the time needed for data collection; 2) optimizing the Level of Accuracy (LOA) and Level of Detail (LOD) of the point clouds for capturing the geometric details required for various cases of construction progress monitoring; 3) develop a list of typical geometric changes for indicating construction progresses of the concerned structural elements; 4) achieving adaptive 3D imaging by developing and integrating 3D imaging sensor model, geometric complexity-quality model and sensor space planning algorithm. To identify what construction information should be included in the BIM models and 4D models of the construction project; for the purpose of progress monitoring. To develop a technical method which can compare the discrpencies between the project data acquired from laser scanning and 3D imaging technologies and those contained in the BIM models. This comparison method will become a managerial tool to assist the project managers to manage project progress.

15209314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209314.value: Construction progress monitoring is crucial to the success of a project. This process site management team to clearly understand and compare the expect progress and actual progress of a project. Discrepancies between as-built and as-designed progress are used by project managers in adjusting job site arrangements. Early detection of such discrepancies provides opportunities for early remedial actions to minimize potential negative impacts to the project. However, current construction progress monitoring methods rely heavily on the capacities of site manageemnt team in collecting progress data and comparing these with planned progress data. The process is complex in the following two aspects, as summarized by Golparvar-Fard et al. (2009): 1) progress data collection is time-consuming; and 2) progress report and 2D drawings can’t intuitively reflect the spatial aspect of the construction progress (Koo and Fischer, 2000) and thus the comparison between actual and planned progress data is inaccurate (Golparvar-Fard et al. 2006). In order to improve the current construction monitoring practice, This study aims to develop a new methodlogy to monitor the construction progress of structural elements by integrating Building Information modeling (BIM) with laser scanning and imaging technologies (conceptual framework is shown in figure 1). It is expected that the methodlogy to be developed will provide a new approach to monitoring construction progress, and this methodology will assist project managers to improve the efficiency of their project management practice 施工進度的監控是非常重要的， 它决定一個項目的成敗。這個過 程中管理團隊必须清楚地了解和比較期待和實際 的進展情況。通 过比較期待和實際進展的差異，項目經理調整作業現場安排。及 早發現的這種 差異提供了及早採取補救行動的可能，以盡量減少 对項目潛在的負面影響。然而，目前的施工進度監控 方法很大程 度上依賴於管理團隊手工收集進度數據與計劃進度的能力。該過 程非常耗时，而且不准确。本研究将开发一套新的方法自动收集 项目的進度數據， 从而提高项目管理的效率。

15209314.label: Realisation of objectives
15209314.value: All three objectives listed above are fully achieved. Specifically, during this project, we developed a computer algorithm to convert scanned points clouds to 3D models; we then developed a method to compare 3D models developed from points clouds with BIM models to evaluate project progress. Based on the results of this comparison, project progress discrepancies are identified. All these three objectives are reported in journal papers. In addition, a computer software (BIMGLE) is developed based on results from this project and another project funded by Innovation and Technology Funds. Details of this software can be viewed at: https://www.cvplab.org/index.php/2018/07/10/smart-construction-platform-based-on-cloud-bim-and-image-processing-bimgle/.

15209414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209414.value: The social media world has experienced tremendous growth in recent years. On social media platforms, people all around the world are connected together. They actively interact with each other and collectively create a massive amount of online text streams. Such text streams, if explored well, contain a great wealth of information and offer significant opportunities for timely emergency response and appropriate actions. As an essential technique to deal with the problem of information explosion, text summarization aims to automatically extract the most important information from source documents to produce a condensed version. Although research on text summarization already has more than half a century of history, when confronted with online social media text, traditional summarization approaches are no longer adequate. Unlike carefully authored news articles or scientific papers, social media text is characterized by the short, noisy, large scale, and dynamic natures. The traditional summarization approaches that are dominated by content analysis inevitably suffer from its sparse and noisy text representation. Moreover, these approaches normally focus on static document collections and thus are insufficient to handle the continuously growing and dynamically changing text streams. New methods and new approaches are highly demanded to meet these new challenges. In this project, we propose a novel summarization framework to address the problems raised by the less-informative and dynamic social media content. Our objective is to develop adaptive models and scalable algorithms based up this framework to explore three key intrinsic dimensions of social media text stream, i.e., the temporal, social and content dimensions. We integrate together the content analysis and time-series modeling techniques to automatically determine “what and when is worth to summarize” by tracking and modeling the dynamic changes in the stream over time. With emphasis on the roles of social influence and social interactions, which are critical to information dissemination on social media networks, we aim to alleviate the sparse and noisy text presentation problem in summary content selection and make further efforts to generate more informative summaries that not only depict topic evolvement but also explain how key people push forward the development of topic. The deliverables of the project include innovative solutions to dynamic and social content modeling and summarization and benchmark datasets to support research development and performance evaluation. They will contribute to promoting the research in social media summarization and add value to the practical applications like marketing management and emergency response. 作为流行的社会媒体，微博在信息传播中扮演着重要角色。由于微博数据量庞大，为帮助用户快速全面地掌握有效信息，面向微博数据流的话题传播摘要研究具有广阔的应用前景和深远的研究价值。该项目立足于微博数据流的独特性，研究话题在微博网络中的发展演变规律，并概括总结话题传播过程中的重要信息及其相互关联。我们致力于分析微博数据流的多维度信息，包括流量和内容随时间的变化、用户的参与行为以及用户／信息之间的交互行为等，以应对微博内容和流量变化快且内容稀疏口语化表达多所带来的挑战。我们聚焦话题的复杂传播演变过程，旨在跟踪和识别话题的分解、演变和合并规律。我们关注用户的社会行为，借助于用户的信息交流模式解析重要话题信息间的因果关系。我们提出崭新的微博数据流挖掘系统框架，并在此基础之上开发相应的模型和技术，设计高效的增量式算法以满足实时处理的系统需求。针对某些关键技术的前期研究结果表明，该项目的实施切实可行，该项目的成果将有助于推进社会媒体摘要的进程，并为市场管理和应急管理等领域带来应用价值。

15209414.label: Realisation of objectives
15209414.value: The project “Making Sense of Social Media Streams through Text Summarization” was proposed in October 2013, funded in June 2014, commenced in January 2015, and competed in June 2018. The main research objectives of this project, as mentioned in the previous proposal are to (1) model the influence of social connections and social communications on information dissemination in social media, (2) explore topic summarization models with particular reference to the unique characteristics of social media, and (3) develop effective approaches and algorithms to capture topic dynamic changes in social media text streams and support valuable and timely social media information digest. With the efforts of several PhD students, research associates and research assistants, basically these targets were smoothly and successfully completed. Our researches were developed along the following main directions. Social Influence and Information Diffusion Modeling Although previous work has studied interpersonal influence as probability of activating others during information diffusion, they ignored an important fact that information diffusion is the result of influence and dynamic interactions among users create influence. We proposed a novel temporal influence model (TIM) to explore how influence emerges during communications by dynamically tracking users’ opinion behaviors over time. The learned influence model was validated in opinion prediction. Like other existing influence models, TIM suffered from the following two problems. First, it simply formulated opinions as derived sentiment categories but ignore the content conveyed in the opinions. Second, it only made use of the most recently received information without taking into consideration the long-term historical communication. To keep track of user opinion behaviors and infer user opinion influence from the historical exchanged textual information, we developed a content-based influence model (CIM) with two alternative learning strategies. One is sentiment category based. The other is sentiment word based. This work was further extended to a content-based sequential opinion influence model (CSIM). We also noticed that people on social media often have two identities, i.e., personal identities and social identities with which people behave to fit the expectations of the others in the same group. We further explored users’ dual identities to build a more comprehensive opinion influence model (DI2) for a better understanding of opinion dynamics. Following the current trend, CIM, CSIM and DI2 were all developed based on neural network frameworks and deep learning techniques. Information diffusion is closely related to social influence. Previously, we have successfully developed social representation learning approaches to model the information diffusion process and address the information diffusion prediction issue. We have attempted several solutions to integrate the network structural information, like using it as constraint/regulation on information diffusion, or jointly learning user representation for both information diffusion and social link prediction tasks. In this project, we focused more on neural network-based diffusion models. We proposed a diffusion attention network to effectively explore the implicit user-to-user diffusion dependency among information cascade users. The user-to-cascade importance and the time-decay effect were also captured and utilized by the model. To better explore both the sequential nature of an information diffusion process and the structural characteristics of user social connection, we further developed a novel sequential neural network with structure attention. Overall, we have well explored the temporal, social, content information and integrated them for social influence and information diffusion modeling. From Extractive to Generative Neural Summarization Developed so far, multi-document summarization has reached its bottleneck due to the lack of sufficient training data and diverse categories of documents. To address this issue, we leveraged the plentiful text classification data to improve the performance of summarization. More important, our approach was able to catch the variations of summary styles with respect to different text categories. For query-focused summarization, we proposed to apply the attention mechanism to simulate the attentive reading of human behavior when a query is given and jointly tackled query relevance ranking and sentence saliency ranking. Borrowed from machine translation researches, sequence-to-sequence models made themselves a viable solution to generation-based summarization. Encouraged by the success of these models, our research focus gradually moved from extractive to generative approaches. Considering copying and rewriting (e.g., using paraphrases) are two writing styles when humans summarize, we proposed a novel sequence-to-sequence model to fuse a copy decoder and a rewrite decoder to mimic human summarization behaviors. While the copy decoder picks up the most important words from the source text, the rewrite decoder restricts the generation output within a small yet highly relevant vocabulary according to the source text. Having noticed that the development of neural summarization research has been significantly hampered by the costly acquisition of reference summaries, we proposed an effective way to automatically collect large scales of news-related multi-document summaries with reference to social media’s reactions. The dataset has been released for public access. Real-Time Summarization and Dynamic Topic Modeling on Social Media Text Stream In relation to text stream summarization, to help further understand how information was propagated over the social media, we have conducted a preliminary study that tried to summarize the topics on social media. Two approaches, i.e., stream-based (temporal clustering) and semantic-based (semantic clustering) approaches, were developed to detect the important subtopics within a trending topic. Then a short sub-summary is generated for each subtopic. In addition, we proposed three new measures to evaluate the position-aware coverage, sequential novelty and sequence correlation of system-generated summaries. We participated in 2016 real-time temporal summarization track in Text Retrieval Conference (TREC) (a well-known worldwide research competition in information/web retrieval). The track encouraged participating teams to explore techniques for constructing real-time update summaries from social media streams (on Twitter) in response to users’ information needs. It provided us an excellent opportunity and the platform to develop our research that met the target of this project. The experience obtained in this exercise helped us to gain a more comprehensive understanding of users’ information seeking and dissemination behaviors and to make use of the social media characteristic to develop unique social summarization models and the corresponding algorithms. Finally, we got the first place in the competition and developed a neural network-based reinforcement learning approach for real-time pushing on text stream as the research output. Tracking the evolution of an event and predicting its subsequent trends play an important role in social media. In a recent work, we proposed an evolutionary context-aware neural sequential model to track the evolutionary trends of the streaming text and investigated their focused context-aware topics. In overall, the main goals of this project have been completely achieved, and the research results have been published in or accepted to 4 recognized journals and 14 conferences (with RGC funding acknowledgments), including the top conferences in information retrieval (SIGIR, CIKM and WWW), computational linguistics (ACL and COLING) and artificial intelligence (AAAI).

15209414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209414.value: The main research outcomes are summarized as follows. Social Influence and Information Diffusion Modeling For social influence modeling, TIM presented in IEEE IS was a dynamic model which modeled user behaviors as a Markov chain and coupled chains together to temporally correlate opinion influence among multiple users. CIM published in COLING’2016 was a content-based model, which explored how opinion words affect influence modeling and opinion prediction. TIM and CIM were extended into a content-based sequential opinion influence model which was accepted to IEEE TAC. Modeling user influence with dual identities, published in CIKM’2017, was the work integrating both influence role detection and influence modeling. On information diffusion, we were concerned with both the stable network structure (structural information) and the dynamic diffusion cascade (sequential information). We focused on social representation learning and applied learned representation to predict potential diffusion in the future. The sequential models with structural attention and the attention networks that capture implicit user-to-user diffusion dependency among information cascade users are explored. The results were published in CIKM’2018 and WWW’2018. From Extractive to Generative Neural Summarization For text summarization, we focused on the development of neural network models, moving gradually from extractive to generative approaches. We leveraged text classification datasets to learn better document representations for summarization and explored the variations of summary styles with respect to different text categories. We proposed to apply the attention mechanism to simulate the human’s attentive reading behavior when a query is given and jointly tackled query relevance ranking and sentence saliency ranking. We developed a novel sequence-to-sequence model to fuse a copy decoder and a rewrite decoder to mimic human summarization behaviors. We also devised an effective way to automatically collect large scales of news-related multi-document summaries with reference to social media’s reactions. The research achievements were published in proceedings of AAAI’2016, COLING’2016 and AAAI’2017. Real-Time Summarization and Dynamic Topic Modeling on Social Media Text Stream On real-time text summarization, the neural network-based reinforcement learning approach for real-time pushing on text stream was presented in SIGIR’2017. The work of tracking evolutionary trends of the streaming text with context-aware neural sequential models was published in IS. We also participated in 2016 Real-Time Temporal Summarization track in Text Retrieval Conference (a well-known worldwide research competition). The performance of our submitted system was ranked in the first place. The report was included in proceedings of TREC’2016.

15209414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209414.value: On the occasion of the boom of deep learning and neural network technologies, we had a very good chance to explore and investigate neural models for social text summarization, dynamic text stream tracking, textual information diffusion and impact of social influence in this project. The experience gained from his project allowed us to well understand the potentials of neural technologies and at the same time the limitations of them. Currently, state-of-the-art sequence-to-sequence (aka encoder-decoder) models only worked well in the sentence-level. They failed to, or at least are deficient in, handling long documents that contain the diverse information. Based on research findings derived from this project, we proposed another project to further explore multi-sentence document-to-summary generation mechanisms. Meanwhile, social network can be naturally formulated as a social graph. Graph modeling is more capable of capturing global context information than sequence modeling like sequence-to-sequence. It is also our plan to develop graph-based neural summarization models, e.g., to incorporate external linguistic knowledge or to fuse the events/facts extracted from source documents.

15209514.label: Realisation of objectives
15209514.value: Urban PM samples (PM2.5 from selected sites of Hong Kong and Guangzhou have been collected monthly since April 2014. In addition, air PM samples were also obtained in four cities in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region (Shanghai, Nanjing, Hangzhou and Ningbo) for a comparative study. Continued sampling was conducted in the YRD and PRD for three years since 2016. Basic chemical properties of the PM samples have been measured, including carbonaceous compounds (e.g., OC, EC), water-soluble inorganic ions (e.g., anions Cl-, NO3-, SO42-; and cations NH4+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+) , trace metals (e.g., As, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Mn, Ni, Pb, Sb, Sn, V and Zn) and major elements (e.g., Al, Ca, Fe, and Mg). Furthermore, Pb isotopic composition analysis (ratios of 204Pb/207Pb, 206Pb/207Pb, and 208Pb/207Pb) have been determined in selective samples for PM-source identification in the study area. Bioaccessibility for different pollutants has been investigated using simulated lung fluid. Relationships between the bioaccessibility and each potential contribution factor have been analyzed by correlation analysis (CA). Microbiological studies and toxicity tests have been conducted in selected samples.

15209514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209514.value: We performed integrated mixture−toxicity experiments and modeling to quantify the contribution of metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), two default culprit component groups of PM2.5 toxicity, to in vitro oxidative stress caused by wintertime PM2.5 from Beijing and Guangzhou, two megacities in China. PM2.5 from Beijing exhibited greater toxic potencies at equal mass concentrations. The targeted chemical analysis revealed higher burden of metals and PAHs per unit mass of PM2.5 in Beijing. These chemicals together explained 38 and 24% on average of PM2.5-induced reactive oxygen species in Beijing and Guangzhou, respectively, while >60% of the eﬀects remained to be resolved in terms of contributing chemicals. PAHs contributed approximately twice the share of the PM2.5 mixture eﬀects as metals. Fe, Cu, and Mn were the dominant metals, constituting >80% of the metal-shared proportion of the PM2.5 eﬀects. Dibenzo[a,l]pyrene alone explained >65% of the PAH-shared proportion of the PM2.5 toxicity eﬀects. The signiﬁcant contribution from coal combustion and vehicular emissions in Beijing suggested the major source disparities of toxicologically active PAHs between the two cities. Our study provided novel quantitative insights into the role of varying toxic component proﬁles in shaping the diﬀerential toxic potencies of city-speciﬁc PM2.5 pollution. The spatiotemporally diﬀerentiated bacterial communities and ARG abundances, and the compositions, mobility, and potential hosts of ARGs in the atmosphere have strong implications for human inhalational exposure over spatiotemporal scales. By comparing other contributing pathways for the intake of ARGs (e.g., drinking water and food ingestion) in China and the U.S.A., we identiﬁed the region-speciﬁc importance of inhalation in China as well as country-speciﬁc exposure scenarios. Our study thus highlights the signiﬁcance of inhalation as an integral part of the aggregate exposure pathways of environmentally disseminated ARGs, which, in turn, may help in the formulation of adaptive strategies to mitigate the exposure risks in China and beyond.

15209514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209514.value: The focus of air-pollution studies should shift to measuring health effects, not just emissions and atmospheric chemistry. This must involve specialists from fields as diverse as molecular biology, toxicology, health sciences and economics. Researchers should rank sources of PM2.5 by how harmful they are, and examine the toxicity of samples of real air.

15209514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209514.value: Levels of PM2.5 alone give only a rough guide to the toxicity of air pollutants in a particular place. Reducing PM2.5 by the same amount in different places will not deliver the same health benefits everywhere. To protect millions more lives, scientists need to help governments and municipalities to determine the most hazardous constituents of air pollution and mitigate them first. Researchers and policymakers need to rethink methods for assessing health risks and regulatory measures for reducing those risks. The focus of air-pollution studies should shift to measuring health effects, not just emissions and atmospheric chemistry. This must involve specialists from fields as diverse as molecular biology, toxicology, health sciences and economics. Researchers should rank sources of PM2.5 by how harmful they are, and examine the toxicity of samples of real air.

15209614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209614.value: 隨機切換控制問題在各個領域(如科學、工程、金融管理和經濟學)已引起廣泛興趣和實際重視。最近,人們大幅增加了這一系列的隨機控制問題的研究,以及其金融應用。例如,在金融市場中,一個人可能在他/她的投資期間會遇到牛熊兩個市場情況。但是,在一些切換控制框架,它所固有的系統動態或代價泛函,或者兩者兼而有之,都可能涉及到兩個狀態和它的期望值。在本研究項目中,我們計畫研究這類切換控制問題,其中動態系統和代價泛函涉及隨機係數。這在很大程度上不同於標準文獻中的切換控制理論,為克服這類數學困難, 本項目將發展新的方法。此外,我們還將根據理論成果提出一類具有挑戰性而實際上又很重要的投資組合決策模式。這一模型同時闡述了如何正確投資機制應有的設計,以便在有限的時間之內管理好風險資產。

15209614.label: Realisation of objectives
15209614.value: In this project, we investigate dynamic optimization problems featuring both stochastic control and regime-switching system over a finite time horizon. We develop new methodologies, which are significantly different from those in the standard regime-switching control theory in the existing literature. In our models, the inclusion of expected values introduces major technical difficulties, which include, among others, time inconsistency leading to failure of dynamic programming approach. To cope with the mathematical difficulty caused by the expectation term, we adopt the so-called mean-field formulations to study our problems. We apply our theoretical results to some challenging, yet practically relevant and important, risk-sensitive problems in wealth management to obtain the properties of the optimal strategies and analyse two regimes with bull and bear markets to achieve a certain level over a finite time investment horizon (paper 1, 2 and 7 in Part C). Also, we extend this fundamental idea to the general case to develop optimal stopping problems within the regime-switching framework (paper 5 in Part C). In Paper 5, we propose a real-life model with regime-switching (seasonal changes) and finite maturity. During this project period, we further study open-loop and closed-loop solvabilities of stochastic linear quadratic (LQ) control problems (paper 3 in Part C). In particular, our work corrects an incorrect result found in the recent important paper entitled “Indefinite stochastic linear quadratic control and generalized differential Riccati equation, SIAM J. Control Optim., 40 (2002), pp. 1296- 1311”. The results derived from our work are expected to help readers to have a clear picture on stochastic LQ control. Except these, based on the modes of Markov chain, we introduce the corresponding decomposition technique of augmented state and control to successfully construct the optimal control of the original mean-field LQ optimal control with Markov jumps (paper 4 in Part C). Recently, we develop the idea of paper 3 to show new results for open-loop and closed-loop solvabilities of regime-switching stochastic (LQ) control problems (paper 6 in Part C). Our study adds to the understanding of risk-taking behaviors and investment decision mechanisms of investors in at least three aspects below. First, it is one of the early studies addressing investors' decision-making process theoretically using an American-style optimal stopping mechanism under the regime-switching system. Therefore, this model sheds light on the cutting-edge development of the financial industry and its corresponding literature. Second, it contributes to the mathematical finance/financial engineering literature by formulating mean-variance portfolio problem with cash flows in wealth management under the regime-switching system. Third, findings of this project provide important and timely implication practitioners and policy makers by helping them understand their risk-taking behaviors when they encounter two regimes with bull and bear markets over their investment time horizon. In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our study has important yet practical relevance. With the alarm bells the on-going financial crisis rings, risk hedging has drawn much more attention than ever. Among various approaches of hedging and managing risk, American-style options and mean-variance portfolios under the regime-switching system are preferable by institutional investors. Further developing the methods presented by prior research, our approach determines the region in which managers should exit their investee companies based on dynamic regime-switching models in financial investment. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions.

15209614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209614.value: The mean-field type of optimal regime-switching stochastic control models deals with problems in which either the system dynamics or the objective functional, or both, involve the states as well as the expected values of the states. The current work of this project employs the mean-field formulation to cope with seemingly non-tractable nonseparability within some regime-switching control frameworks. In particular, we revisit three challenging, yet practically important, portfolio selection models over a finite-time investment horizon, reformulate them as regime-switching linear quadratic (LQ) control problems of a mean-field type, and derive their optimal strategies with analytical solution qualities. Except these, we further derive the equilibrium strategy and equilibrium value function in a closed-form using backward induction approach within a game theoretic framework during this project period. In addition, one of our findings corrects an incorrect result found in the recent important paper entitled “Indefinite stochastic linear quadratic control and generalized differential Riccati equation, SIAM J. Control Optim., 40 (2002), pp. 1296-1311” and presents two counterexamples (paper 3 in Part C). We published some papers and completed some working papers. Although I did not project expenses for graduate student training in the original GRF proposal submitted to RGC in October 2013, our university appointed Mr. Sun Jingrui as a Research Assistant to work with me on this GRF-sponsored project in the period of 1 April – 30 September, 2015. On or before 30 June 2015, he was a PhD student of University of Science and Technology of China. We together completed the journal article entitled “Open-loop and closed-loop solvabilities for stochastic linear quadratic optimal control problems” (paper 3 in Part C, published on SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization). Then he introduced this work into his dissertation. On or after 1 July 2015, he obtained PhD degree and continued his research works with me on this GRF-sponsored project. Based on some of results derived from this project, I gave the following invited talks in the conferences. The talk entitled “Time Consistent Behavioral Portfolio Policy for Dynamic Mean-Variance Formulation” is based on results of paper 1 and 2 (in Part C) and “Selling Financial Assets at the Right Time” is based on results of paper 5 (in Part C). In particular, the 5th NUS Workshop on Risk and Regulation invited specialists from various countries, including those from Australia, France, Germany, UK, US, etc. It provides a forum for researchers and practitioners to present and discuss on risk management and regulation so that I can communicate with peers about our research works (see Part C). In addition, except this project period, I presented an invited talk in the international conference on Advanced Methods in Mathematical Finance in Angers, France from 28 August 2018 to 31 August 2018. This conference also invited specialists from various universities, including those from Princeton University, Oxford University, University of Cambridge, ETH Zurich, etc (Part C does not include this conference because it happened after this project is completed). Therefore, I would like to express my sincere thanks for the RGC’s support on my research works.

15209614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209614.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for regime-switching stochastic control problems, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for standard and non-standard time-inconsistent problems within the regime-switching framework (paper 7 in Part C). We will further study these potential research in the future works. [1] Optimal control techniques proposed in this project can be further employed to study more general portfolio selection models, while one encounter two regimes with bull and bear markets over his/her investment time horizon. [2] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze time-inconsistent models within the regime-switching framework. [3] Our methods developed in this project can be applied to airline industry and manager's compensation with underlying assets following stochastic volatility and interest rates within the regime-switching framework.

15209614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209614.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as optimal policy and equilibrium strategy in portfolio selection (paper 1, 2 and 7 in Part C), fund management, incentive compensation and agency theory (paper 5 in Part C) within the regime-switching framework. Specific to the literature on portfolio theory and investment, we expect the results to help shed light on the investment strategies on the basis of financial underlying assets for two regimes with bull and bear markets over the investment time horizon (paper 1, 2, 5 and 7 in Part C). In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve the optimal control studied and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic control under the regime-switching system (paper 3, 4, 5 and 6 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings corrects an incorrect result found in the recent important paper entitled “Indefinite stochastic linear quadratic control and generalized differential Riccati equation, SIAM J. Control Optim., 40 (2002), pp. 1296-1311” and presents two counterexamples (paper 3 in Part C). Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance.

rows: To propose and develop an electrolytic-capacitor-free power supply system for high-power LED lighting applications utilizing multistring arrays.

15210714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210714.value: The rapid advances in light-emitting-diode (LED) devices and systems over the last two decades have significantly transformed the landscape of lighting technology. This is evident from the inclusion of LED lighting in the agendas of national or international energy or environmental policies, new business developments by global lighting companies, publication of industry standards, and rapidly increasing number of research papers and technical conferences on LED lighting. LED lighting must be available at reasonably low cost and be able to bring about long-term energy saving for its wide adoption in the consumer market. Therefore, low-cost and energy-efficient LED drivers that comply with industry standards must be developed to meet these requirements. Currently, the presence of electrolytic capacitors in LED drivers poses a strong limitation to the reliability and operational lifetime of LED drivers. In comparison to inductors, electrolytic capacitors have a higher energy density and are typically used as energy buffer in ac-to-dc power conversion. However, they have a relatively short lifetime of between 5000 and 10000 hours compared to LEDs (> 50000 hours) and this can be further reduced if they operate in high-temperature environments such as those encountered in high-power lighting applications or closed lighting fixtures. An electrolytic-capacitor-free power supply system for high-power LED lighting applications is proposed in this project. The proposed system consists of two power conversion stages. The first stage is a power-factor pre-regulator that uses film capacitor only. With the addition of a new and flexible ripple estimation circuit, the pre-regulator can maintain a near-unity power factor without sacrificing its dynamic response. The second stage is a LCC-resonant converter that uses capacitors for achieving near-lossless current balancing in multistring LED array. Unlike conventional resonant converters, output voltage regulation is achieved by varying the effective value of the resonant capacitor instead of varying the operating frequency. This ensures that the impedance of the current-balancing capacitors, and hence, the LED current in the array, is kept constant. With no electrolytic capacitor, and with the use of near-lossless capacitive current balancing, the completed system should exhibit long lifetime and high efficiency. 過去二十年發光二極管（簡稱LED）在材料及系統設計方面的迅速發展已完全改變照明技術的面貌。我們可以從多方面看見LED照明在不同領域的發展，包括國內及國際能源政策加入LED的相關項目、照明企業開拓并大力發展LED業務、LED產品的標準化，及快速增長的科研成果和學術報告及文獻。 為了促進LED廣泛地被市場採納，LED必須擁有低成本和節約用電的雙特性。因此，為了配合這個理念，高效能及符合工業標準的LED驅動器自然成為不可或缺的一部分。可惜目前市面上出現的LED驅動器由於一般採用了電解電容，這導致它們的可靠性和壽命大大降低。無可否認，電解電容擁有高儲能密度的優勢，也因此被廣泛用於功率變換器上。然而它們的使用壽命一般在5000小時與10000小時之間，遠遠低於LED本身的壽命（大於50000小時），因而LED及它們所需的驅動器普遍存在壽命長度不匹配的嚴重問題。更甚的是，當電解電容長期在高溫環境下工作，它們的壽命甚至可以比預計的5000-10000小時縮短許多。 本研究項目中主要針對大功率LED照明系統提出一種不含電解電容的驅動器。所提出的驅動器包含兩級功率變換，第一級為實現功率因素校正，第二級為實現對LED陣列的電流平衡和控制。在不使用電解電容的前提下，第一級的輸出電壓將含有大量的二次諧波。若沒有適當的措施，二次諧波的存在將嚴重影響功率因素，令其無法符合國際標準的要求。因此，本項目將提出一個全新的諧波發生器，有效地將電路中存在的二次諧波抵消和消除它對功率因素的影響。在第二級所採用的諧振型直流變換器中，與其採用傳統的變頻控制，我們提出使用開關電容技術以達到同樣的穩壓控制。在新的控制方案中，開關頻率保持恆定，因此保證LED電流平衡的有效性不會隨開關頻率的改變而變化。最後，當兩級電路被整合成一完整的驅動系統，其壽命和能源效益將比現有的產品有著顯著的提升。

15210714.label: Realisation of objectives
15210714.value: The project aims to develop an electrolytic-capacitor-free high-power LED lighting system utilizing multistring arrays. For high-power lighting systems, a typical two-stage architecture was adopted where the first stage is responsible for input current shaping or power factor correction (PFC), and the second stage is responsible for load voltage (or load current) regulation. With the removal of electrolytic capacitor from the PFC stage's output, excessive voltage ripple inevitably appears on the dc bus voltage which can substantially degrade the power factor of the input current. Unlike conventional approach that limits the effect of voltage ripple by adopting a very small bandwidth for the PFC stage, which results in poor dynamic response of the PFC stage and leads to more stringent design requirements for the second stage (e.g. excessive voltage stress due to large voltage overshoot), a method based on ripple estimation-cancellation was proposed to cancel the effect of voltage ripple by replicating the ripple and subtracting it from the sampled voltage ripple. By doing so, the PFC stage's bandwidth can be substantially increased, thus improving its dynamic response, without sacrificing its input current shaping performance. In our work, ripple estimation is implemented using an amplitude tuner and a phase shifter circuit, both of which are analog circuits that can be easily integrated with existing commercial PFC controller ICs. Considering the additional cost of implementing the ripple estimation circuit, further works were done in this project to simplify its implementation, and after an in-depth study, we had formulated a systematic way of deriving a family of three ripple estimation circuits that differ in level of circuit complexity and accuracy of ripple estimation. We had constructed the prototypes of all three circuits and compared their performances in detail. We find that for practical applications the ripple estimation circuit that uses only one amplitude tuner and an all-pass filter is preferred as it gives a good ripple estimation performance while keeping the level of circuit complexity low, which favors its integration into existing commercial PFC controller ICs. In the second phase of the project, we focused on addressing the issue of current balancing in a high-power multi-color multi-string LED lighting system. To achieve a passive, and hence lossless, current balancing, the LEDs in each string are arranged such that they behave as ac load and a capacitor in connected in series with each LED string for current balancing. All LED strings are connected to a common ac voltage bus generated by a high-frequency resonant inverter which supplies power to all LED strings. In the above conventional system configuration, frequency modulation is typically used to regulate the magnitude of the ac bus voltage under load variations, for example, when some of LEDs are dimmed. It is known that frequency variation will alter the capacitive impedances of the current-balancing capacitors and will subsequently alter the current flowing through all LED strings, including those which are not meant to be dimmed. A fully switched-capacitor-controlled LCC resonant converter is designed to address this challenge. With the replacement of all fixed capacitors in the resonant tank of the LCC converter with switch-controlled capacitors (SCCs), the regulation of the common ac bus voltage, current balancing, and individual current control of the LED strings can be readily achieved with a single LED driver by varying the effective capacitances of the SCCs under constant switching frequency. In this way, the circuit complexity can be greatly reduced while both the power regulation and dimming performances of the LED lighting system can be significantly improved. An experimental prototype of driving LED growth light for indoor farming applications is designed and constructed which successfully verified the proposed solution.

15210714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210714.value: The proposed solution can be adopted for the development of high-power LED grow light systems for large-scale indoor farms. For such an application, the LEDs and driver circuitry will typically operate in multi-kW power range for long hours. They are also typically enclosed in a compact casing with limited air ventilation. In the future, instead of focusing on the functionality of the driver circuitry (PFC, dimming, current balancing, etc), a system-level investigation of the LED lighting system under specific, especially harsh, operating conditions should be made. Other non-electrical issues such as thermal management, total cost, reliability, manufacturability, etc should also be considered.

15210714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210714.value: An electrolytic-capacitor-free power supply system for high-power LED lighting applications is investigated in this project. The proposed system consists of two power conversion stages. The first stage is a power-factor pre-regulator that uses film capacitor only. With the addition of a new and flexible ripple estimation circuit, the pre-regulator can maintain a near-unity power factor without sacrificing its dynamic response. The second stage is an LCC resonant converter that uses capacitors for achieving lossless current balancing in a multi-string LED array. Unlike conventional resonant converters, output voltage regulation is achieved by varying the effective value of the resonant capacitor instead of varying the operating frequency. This ensures that the impedance of the current-balancing capacitors, and hence, the LED current in the array, is kept constant. With no electrolytic capacitor, and with the use of lossless capacitive current balancing, the developed LED lighting system should exhibit long lifetime and high efficiency.

15210914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210914.value: In this project, the use of coherent detection technique for improving the performance of a free space optical communication system will be studied. Free space optical communication system or optical wireless communication is a promising alternative to traditional radio frequency based wireless communication systems. It is free from expensive spectrum licensing, provides large amount of bandwidth with ease and speediness of system installation. In addition, it potentially offers large amount of bandwidth in underwater environment which is not possible for normal RF based communication systems. It is expected to complement RF based wireless communication technology to enable ubiquitous broadband connectivity. Coherent detection technique is believed to enable significant system performance improvement. However, a number of key system design issues need to be addressed before they can be employed in practical system implementation. In the proposed project, we plan to address these issues by evaluating the effect of detector size on the system performance and algorithm parameter selection. Through the use of 2D detector array, the effect of performance limitation caused by fading and wavefront distortion associated with atmospheric turbulence will be reduced. By employing new modulation techniques, further system performance improvement is expected. System implementation on a realtime platform and propagation channel simulator will enable the effectiveness of the proposed schemes to be evaluated in a practical system environment thus enables significant technology advancement in this interesting research area. 本项目将开展利用相干检测技术提高空间光通信系统性能的研究。 同传统无线通信技术相比，空间光通信或无线光通信在很多情况下可成为一个更好的选择。 此技术不需要昂贵的无线频谱执照，系统设立简单并可提供很宽的频谱。同时它也可以用于射频技术无法实现的水下通信。从很大程度上，无线光通信技术可同射频无线技术很好地互补以实现未来的宽带通信系统。相干通信技术可大大地系统的性能。可是要将其用于实际系统中，很多关键技术还需得到很好地解决。本项目将研究探测器大小对系统性能及算法参数选择的影响。通过利用二維探测器阵列，以减小由于大气湍流引起的衰减及波前失真。通过利用新调制技术以进一步改善系统性能。通过实时实验系统及信道模拟器，此技术在实际系统中的可行性可以得到很好的评估。

15210914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210914.value: In the project, we have studied a number of key issues related to free space optical communication systems. We have proposed and evaluated a number of schemes for realizing carrier phase estimation which is one the key functions in an coherent detection systems. We have also investigated a number of modulation schemes and equalization schemes that help to significantly improve the performance of free space optical communication systems such as visible light based free space optical communication systems. In particular, we have proposed and experimentally evaluated the system performance based on spectrally efficient frequency division multiplexing modulation(SEFDM). We have established a quasi-multiple input multiple output(MIMO) model for the system and have proposed the use of MMSE-sorted QR decomposition(MMSE-SQRD) based MIMO decoder that have helped to eliminate ICI in the SEFDM based system. We have also investigated a number of modulation schemes. We have demonstrated that the proposed schemes can not only be used in free space optical communication systems but can also be used in optical communication systems for data centres. Two conference papers and two journal papers have been published and all the objectives have been successfully realized.

15210914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210914.value: We will further investigate the schemes developed in the project and explore their potential application sin other related areas.

15210914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210914.value: Free space optical communication system uses light propagating in free space for information delivery. It offers the advantages of flexible system set up and potential large system bandwidth. However, the performance of such systems is often limited by system component bandwidth and various transmission channel impairments. In the project, we have explore a number of modulation, detection and equalization schemes that help to improve system performance. We have also evaluated the potential application of the proposed schemes in other optical communication systems such as optical communication systems for data centers. The techniques developed here shall certainly help to further develop the research area.

15211114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211114.value: 今天的萬維網已經從簡單的搜索引擎的平臺改變成基於社會媒體的多方位的信息交換、分享、甚至於情感支持的平臺。因此情感分析的研究得到很大的重視。現階段基於文本的情感分析的研究大多數集中在文本中所表達的帶有情感的詞彙，並將所表達的情感作爲一個分類問題來解決。實際上，人們對同一篇文字所激發的情感因角色不同而不同。如果文字中沒有明顯情感詞彙時，要預測人們因文字所激發的情感則更具挑戰。 本項目旨在通過使用多種信息建立讀者的情感模型和預測方法。 首先，我們認爲在情感分析的模型中應該區分不同的角色，將作者、評價者和讀者區分對待，因此在分類時可以進行不同角色的情感分析。在建立情感詞庫時，我們認爲不同詞彙表達情感的強度不同，而且情感詞常常會表達多重情感。因此在整理情感詞彙時應該引入強度和情感維度。第二，文字對事件的描述也會引起情感的變化，即使文字中沒有使用情感的描述。因此，我們認爲要把對事件的描述引入情感分析的模型中。第三，情感本身是相當個人化的。一個可以讓一個人悲傷的故事，可以讓另一個人快樂，中間的曲直變化和每個人的價值系統、偏好、以及他們和表述中的人物的關係等相關。基於這一觀察，我們認爲應該建立讀者的個人偏好描述系統包括對人物、組織、社會/政治問題的情感偏向。我們計劃基於考慮多重信息，建立情感分析的預測模型。本項目主要以中文文本作爲分析的基礎，但所建立的模型應該是一個通用的模型。 本項目的成果會跟深入的建立情感分析的分析模型並擴大分析的範圍。使我們能夠通過計算機技術進一步了解語言文字對讀者情感的影響，勢必將情感分析的影響和其相關技術的應用擴大到社會學和政治學的領域，希望通過我們的工作預測網絡和社會媒體上人們情感的變化以及是否可以導致人們對社會和政治環境相關的行動。

15211114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211114.value: Firstly, multi-dimensional emotion models, such as the EPA model, have very strong theoretic basis in cognitive science. Yet they are not widely applied or used in NLP because annotation of lexical items is too expensive. We argue that word embedding learnt through a large text corpus should contain affect information. Therefore, we developed a bootstrapping method using a very small EPA lexicon to obtain the EPA of almost all lexical items regardless of their role as emotion words in the traditional sense (Refer to Journal #1 ). Secondly, emotion is a very subjective issue and learning profiles of individuals will help to address the personal bias issue. In this project, we make use of social media links and friends networks to obtain extended context to learn the information on subjectivity/profile. By making use of the learnt profiles, we demonstrate the ability to make sentiment/emotion predictions better than the state-of-the-art algorithms on benchmarking data(Refer to Journal #3 & Conf. #1). Thirdly, to address the data sparseness issue due to the “silent majority” phenomenon in social media, we use a deep learning approach to predict the profiles of missing data using social network links and text similarity using extended context to obtain sufficient information for better prediction(Refer to Conf. #4). Fourthly, we developed a method to identify named entities for classical Chinese and helped to construct a Chinese emotion corpus as a language resource to make prediction of persons much easier(Conf. #2 &3). Lastly, we proposed a dual memory network method to make better predictions by incorporating user bias in product review with performance outperform the state-of-the-art method s(refer to Conf. #6). We also participated in fake new detection work making use of the affective resources and methods developed by this team (Refer to Conf. #7). During the study of deep learning models, we also found that most of the attention methods used in current NLP models are based on local context which is mostly statistically based although attention mechanism come from cognition theory. So, we explored the use of cognition grounded data to build attention models using reading time. To address the issue of data sparseness issue, we developed a method to predict reading time of words and the method demonstrated, again, better than state-of-the art performance (Refer conf. #5). This discovery and method is now being submitted to a journal. One fully supported PhD and one partly supported PhD.

15211114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211114.value: In this project, we are able to capture reader/writer profiles using appropriate embedding representations. The effectiveness our profile representations is proven to be effective in both sentiment classification as well as emotion classification. Even though deep learning based representation works, the representation is not semantically explainable. So one direction of our work is to further inject semantically meaning into deep learning models. We are able to develop effective methods to acquire multidimensional representation of affects for lexical terms. However, the acquired information contains only affects in the respective dimensions. Embedding representation of words, on the other hand, contains all kinds of contextual information including semantic information as well as affective information even though there is no way of pin pointing them because embedding is a low dimensional representation. So our future direction should consider incorporating affective information in the multi-dimensional representation into deep learning models. Adding explicit knowledge into deep learning model is not straight forward. One possible way is to add sentiment score or affective information in a weighted manner similar to that of adding attention layer into deep learning models.

15211114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211114.value: Emotion is a cognition process which is very individualized. In other words, different people may have very different reactions to the same event. Past works in emotion analysis are more focused on collective text information for emotion classification. Personal bias is not taking into consideration in emotion analysis. This work takes into consider of profiles of individuals to make sentiment predictions with impressive improvement especially in social media text. In one work, we constructed an intersubjectivity network which links review writers, terms they used, as well as the polarities of the terms. A deep learning model was also proposed to learn reader/writer embeddings for sentiment analysis. Evaluations on three commonly used benchmark data show our proposed approach has achieved the state-of-the-art performance. In product review related tasks, Current tasks handle user profile and product information in a unified model which may not be able to learn salient features of users and products effectively. We proposed a dual user and product memory network model to learn user profiles and product reviews using separate memory networks. Then, the two representations are used jointly for sentiment prediction. Comparison to state-of-the-art model also shows the effectiveness of our solution.

15211614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211614.value: Noise control is of importance in improving the indoor environmental quality. It is common to encounter noise problems such as transmission noise due to a noisy fan in a ventilation ductwork system. Generally, there are two types of noise control methods used: active noise control and passive noise control. Engineers are very concerned about whether they can attenuate the noise, especially the low-frequency and broad-band noise in the ventilation ductwork system. However, it is known that a traditional passive noise control method (dissipative or reactive mufflers) has a very limited effect on reducing the low-frequency broad-band noise since a typical dissipative muffler such as duct lining with fibrous material can hardly absorb any noise at low frequencies. A reactive muffler such as a Helmholtz resonator can be used to control the noise at its resonance peak and can be set to a low frequency, but its working range is very narrow. Although active noise control (ANC) systems have the potential advantage of controlling low-frequency noise, there are problems related to its reliability and its high cost. Recent studies on the duct-borne noise control method conducted by the PI and Co-I suggest that the Helmholtz resonators array mounted periodically in a duct will provide more effective noise control in ducts by broadening the bandwidth they attenuate and increasing the magnitude of sound attenuation. The principle objectives of this research are: 1) to study theoretically, numerically and experimentally the effects of different Helmholtz resonators with different periodic mounting distance on the attenuation of duct-borne noise, and to develop a method to optimize the periodic duct-resonator structure, and 2) to study the performance of the periodic duct-resonator structure with “defects” (or called quasi-periodic duct-resonator structure). The long-term significance of this research is that it will lead to: 1) an alternative passive noise method that engineers can use to control the low-frequency board-band noise in ventilation systems; 2) an innovative adaptive-passive method to achieve a wide noise attenuation band and to track some narrow noise peaks within it by adaptively tuning some of the resonators according to the incoming noise.

15211614.label: Realisation of objectives
15211614.value: This project aims at investigating low-frequency broadband noise control in ventilation ductwork systems based on Helmholtz resonator arrays. A theoretical study of the dispersion characteristics of sound wave propagation in a periodic ducted Helmholtz resonators system has been presented. Owing to the coupling of Bragg reflection and Helmholtz resonator’s resonances, a periodic system can provide much broader noise attenuation band at the designed resonance frequencies of the Helmholtz resonator. However, the broader the noise attenuation band the lower the peak attenuation amplitude. The noise attenuation capacity of a Helmholtz resonator has been verified. Although different average transmission loss curves with different bandwidths and peak amplitudes can be obtained with different periodic distances, the area under the average transmission loss curve and the sound power storage are always the same and average transmission loss curves always fall into the boundaries of a noise control zone. A noise control zone compromising the attenuation bandwidth or peak amplitude is first proposed to illustrate the limitation of noise control for ducted Helmholtz resonator system and can be used to analyze the feasibility of desired broad attenuation bandwidth and peak amplitude in noise control optimization. Some modified ducted Helmholtz resonators system based on the periodic ducted Helmholtz resonators system is proposed and investigated. The transmission loss achieved by a periodic ducted Helmholtz resonators system is depended on the structure and the number of Helmholtz resonators. However, the number of Helmholtz resonators is restricted by the available space in longitudinal direction of the duct. Moreover, such system will occupy a large space and may have some spare space in the transverse direction of the duct. By adding Helmholtz resonators on the available space in the transverse direction, some modified ducted Helmholtz resonator system is therefore proposed. Several identical Helmholtz resonators mounted on the same cross-section of a duct has broader noise attenuation band and higher peak amplitude without effects on the Helmholtz resonator’s resonance frequency. It means the modified ducted Helmholtz resonator can also take full advantage of periodicity to obtain a broader noise attenuation band. Besides, added Helmholtz resonators can improve the noise attenuation performance of the whole system. The more Helmholtz resonators added, the better noise attenuation performance of the system. It is flexible to install added Helmholtz resonators on the unoccupied space of the transverse direction of the duct. The proposed modified ducted Helmholtz resonator system fully utilizes the available space to improve noise attenuation performance. Aiming at broader noise attenuation bands for hybrid noise control at low frequencies, a duct with an array of dual Helmholtz resonators distributed periodically is investigated. Owing to the coupling of Bragg reflection and dual Helmholtz resonator’s resonances, a periodic dual array can provide much broader noise attenuation bands at the designed resonance frequencies of the dual Helmholtz resonator. A Helmholtz resonator with different types of neck has been investigated. An extended neck or a spiral neck takes the place of the traditional straight neck of the Helmholtz resonator. The acoustic performance of the Helmholtz resonator with these two types of necks is analyzed theoretically and numerically. The length correction factor is introduced through a modified one-dimensional approach to account for the non-planar effects that result from the neck being extended into the cavity. The spiral neck is transformed to an equivalent straight neck, and the acoustic performance is then derived by a one-dimensional approach. The theoretical prediction results fit well with the Finite Element Method simulation results. Without changing the cavity volume of the Helmholtz resonator, the resonance frequency shows a significant drop when the extended neck length or the spiral neck length is increased. An identical change in the extension neck length or the spiral neck length will produce the same decrease in resonance frequency. For a certain designed resonance frequency of Helmholtz resonator, the utilization of the extended neck or the spiral neck can reduce the cavity volume. Then, the noise attenuation capacity of a Helmholtz resonator is proposed and the theoretical formula of it has been derived theoretically. The noise attenuation capacity is defined as the integral of transmission loss in the frequency domain. The transmission loss index is mainly used to evaluate the acoustic transmission performance in the frequency domain. However, it cannot provide a quantitative characteristic of the noise attenuation band. The proposed noise attenuation capacity index can be considered as one of the key parameters to evaluate the Helmholtz resonator’s noise attenuation performance quantitatively and distinctly. The effects of the neck length, cross-sectional area of the neck, cavity volume and cross-sectional area of the duct on the noise attenuation capacity are analyzed theoretically and numerically. The results show that the noise attenuation capacity is only related to the geometries of the neck and the cross-sectional area of the duct. The cavity volume has no effects on it. Similar to the significance of the Helmholtz resonator’s resonance frequency, the proposed theoretical formula of the noise attenuation capacity provides a distinct parameter to evaluate the Helmholtz resonator’s noise attenuation band quantitatively and illuminates the limitations in Helmholtz resonator’s noise control applications. It is an important supplement to the theoretical studies and engineering applications of Helmholtz resonators. These theoretical models that can be used to investigate the periodic duct-resonator structure with different resonators and with different periodic distance. An efficient optimization method so as to guide the muffler design composed of periodic Helmholtz resonators whilst minimizing the transmitted sound in the duct, and the theoretical model that can be used to describe the “defects” in the periodic duct-resonator structure and to explore the potential application in adaptive-pass noise control using the quasi-periodic structure have been established. The theoretical analysis of the ventilation ductwork systems has been validated by Finite Element Method using the commercial software (COMSOL Multiphysics). Measurements so as to validate the proposed theoretical model and the numerical simulation have been conducted.

15211614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211614.value: A Helmholtz resonator with different types of neck has been investigated. An extended neck or a spiral neck takes the place of the traditional straight neck of the Helmholtz resonator. The length correction factor is introduced through a modified one-dimensional approach to account for the non-planar effects that result from the neck being extended into the cavity. Without changing the cavity volume of the Helmholtz resonator, the resonance frequency shows a significant drop when the extended neck length or the spiral neck length is increased. The noise attenuation capacity of a Helmholtz resonator is proposed and the theoretical formula of it has been derived theoretically. The noise attenuation capacity is defined as the integral of transmission loss in the frequency domain. The proposed noise attenuation capacity index can be considered as one of the key parameters to evaluate the Helmholtz resonator’s noise attenuation performance quantitatively and distinctly. It is an important supplement to the theoretical studies and engineering applications of Helmholtz resonators. The acoustic performance of three kinds of Helmholtz resonator arrays are investigated theoretically and numerically. The dual Helmholtz resonator consisting of two Helmholtz resonator s connected in series is considered as a serial Helmholtz resonator array. Two Helmholtz resonator s mounted on the same cross-section of the duct constitute a parallel Helmholtz resonator array. The lined Helmholtz resonator array is composed of two Helmholtz resonator s installed on the longitudinal direction of the duct. Different installation methods have significant effects on transmission loss performance. The noise attenuation capacity has been adopted to evaluate the noise attenuation performances of these arrays, and shows its potential in the noise control optimization and Helmholtz resonator design. A theoretical study of the dispersion characteristics of sound wave propagation in a periodic ducted Helmholtz resonators system has been presented. Owing to the coupling of Bragg reflection and Helmholtz resonator’s resonances, a periodic system can provide much broader noise attenuation band at the designed resonance frequencies of the Helmholtz resonator. However, the broader the noise attenuation band the lower the peak attenuation amplitude. A noise control zone compromising the attenuation bandwidth or peak amplitude is first proposed to illustrate the limitation of noise control for ducted Helmholtz resonator system and can be used to analyze the feasibility of desired broad attenuation bandwidth and peak amplitude in noise control optimization.

15211614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211614.value: 1. The transmission loss performance of a Helmholtz resonator with a spiral neck or an extended neck is analyzed without the effect of the flows. However, the flow effects have significant impact on the transmission loss performance. A theoretical model considering the flow effects should be developed in the future work. 2. The theoretical formula of the Helmholtz resonator’s noise attenuation capacity can be investigated and compared with that under different flow conditions, i.e. laminar flow, turbulent flow and different Mach numbers. Moreover, the concept of the noise attenuation capacity can be extended to other silencer. It can also be adopted to other research areas related to Helmholtz resonator, like notch filter and metamaterials, with further investigations. 3. Flow is inevitable in ventilation ductwork system and the Helmholtz resonator array mounted on the duct can produce additional noise. The effects of localized turbulence due to Helmholtz resonator arrays should be taken into account. The complicated acoustic and turbulent interaction of different Helmholtz resonator arrays, i.e. the periodic ducted Helmholtz resonator array, the periodic dual Helmholtz resonator array and the modified Helmholtz resonator array, is the main content of future work.

15211614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211614.value: A ventilation ductwork system is an essential system in buildings that provides conditioned or fresh air to indoor environments so as to ensure good indoor air quality. However, it is common to encounter noise problems such as transmission noise due to a noisy fan in a ventilation ductwork system. The accompanied duct noise from the ventilation system could propagate into the occupied zones through the waveguide and could deteriorate human being’s working or living environment quality. Given that people speed more and more time indoor and noise level is one of the key factors in the indoor environmental quality assessment, alleviating such duct-borne noise is thus of great importance to obtain satisfaction with acoustics and overall environmental satisfaction. This project aims at investigating low-frequency broadband noise control in ventilation ductwork systems based on Helmholtz resonator arrays. A good design for a Helmholtz resonator is important for noise attenuation in ventilation ductwork systems. Some modified Helmholtz resonators have been proposed. Based on the theoretical analysis of the dispersion characteristics of sound wave propagation in a ducted Helmholtz resonator system, the improvements on the noise attenuation performance of some ducted Helmholtz resonator systems have been achieved.
