15211714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211714.value: Social engineering attacks, identity theft, and frauds in Hong Kong and mainland China are on the rise, mainly because people in this region are increasingly eager to use their mobile phones to access remote services. Financial institutions such as banks and insurance companies also encourage customers to use remote services as a means to reduce operation cost. In Hong Kong, online shopping and payment systems are prevalent. Certainly, remote services bring great benefit and convenience to customers. However, these services have also become a hotbed for criminals to carry out fraudulent activities. Traditional authentication methods that use passwords are no longer sufficient to safeguard the security of remote services. Voice biometrics has the potential to become an important component of the authentication process. In particular, speaker verification technology can be used to verify the identity of a caller during a live call and stop the financial transaction when potential fraud is detected. Voice biometrics is also particularly useful for call centers to reduce the risk of leaking customers' information caused by social engineering fraudulence. This project aims to develop machine learning algorithms for text-independent speaker verification. In particular, mixture of probabilistic linear discriminant analysis (PLDA) will be applied to overcome the utterance-length variability. Unlike the conventional PLDA for i-vector based speaker verification where information of utterance length is disregarded, our proposed mixture of PLDA can explicitly model utterances of variable length. This capability is important and significant for verifying speakers during a live call because in such situations it is impractical to control the length of the conversation. To further improve the performance of state-of-the-art speaker verification systems, empirical kernel maps and support vector machines will be applied to explicitly incorporate the information of background speakers in the verification process. The proposed method is novel in that instead of simply computing a likelihood ratio as in the conventional PLDA, the method constructs a discriminative model from the likelihood-ratio scores, which has the advantage of maximizing the discrimination between client speakers and impostors. The proposed methods will be evaluated on the latest dataset provided by the NIST. The proposed work will provide insight into fundamental machine learning models. It will also address the session and utterance-length variability in speaker verification systems. 15211714.label: Realisation of objectives
15211714.value: For Objective 1, we have conducted extensive experiments to investigate the relationship between the discriminative power of i-vector/PLDA systems and the duration and SNR of utterances. In particular, we have progressively reduced the utterance length and varied the SNR and tested speaker verification systems using the truncated utterances and noise contaminated utterances. The investigations and experimental results motivated us to developed SNR- and duration-invariant PLDA models and mixture of PLDA models to address the issues. As for the scoring stage of speaker verification, we have developed an empirical kernel-map PLDA that outperforms conventional PLDA but at the expense of higher computation cost. For Objective 2, we have built a speaker verification system based on the software we developed for Objective 1. The system allows users to register and to verify his/her voice.

15211714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211714.value: We have developed three variants of PLDA models for robust speaker verification: (1) SNR- and duration-invariant PLDA, (2) SNR- and duration-dependent mixture of PLDA, and (3) empirical kernel-map PLDA. We have also investigated the relationship between the discriminative power of i-vector/PLDA systems and the length of utterances. Our major findings include the following: (1) Utterance-length variability mainly affects the scale of the posterior covariance matrices of i-vectors. This finding allows us to develop fast scoring algorithms for PLDA models with uncertainty propagation. (2) By substituting the session-dependent loading matrices by the ones trained from development data, the computation cost of uncertainty propagation can be reduced to the one comparable with the conventional PLDA. (3) PLDA mixture models can improve the performance of speaker verification systems when the test utterances have a wide range of SNR and duration. (4) Duration and noise variability in utterances can be directly modeled by PLDA with SNR and duration subspace. (5) The mixture posteriors in the PLDA mixture models can be found by deep neural networks using i-vectors as input. (6) By incorporating the empirical kernel map into PLDA scoring, we have significantly reduced verification error rate but at the expense of computation time. This project has resulted in four journal papers and four conference papers. A demo system based on i-vectors and PLDA models has been constructed. Users can speak any languages to register themselves in the system. Once registered, they can perform authentication by providing five seconds of speech. A video of the demo can be found in https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nvqs4BeG6mM.

15211714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211714.value: The mixture of PLDA, SNR-invariant PLDA, and duration-invariant PLDA can be extended to speech distorted by reverberation effects. Also, it is of interest to replace these PLDA models by more advanced nonlinear generative models such as variational autoencoders. While this project focus on the robustness of PLDA models to noise and duration variability, it is of interest to investigate how these models can be applied to domain adaptation.

15212714.label: Realisation of objectives
15212714.value: The project aims to develop high performance rechargeable batteries based on solid oxide fuel cell technology with the in-situ hydrogen storage/generation via a redox cycling unit (RCU) consisting of a metal/metal oxide pair. Both experimental studies and modeling studies have been conducted by the project team. The project objectives have been 100% achieved through the efforts of the PI and the Co-I - Prof. Kevin Huang from University of South Carolina, USA. Detailed information is provided below. 1. To fabricate novel rechargeable batteries with SDC/ESB bilayer electrolyte and a nano-structured SSC cathode; The ZrO2-supported Fe-oxide with Mo addition will be used in the RCU; The battery will be finished by locating the RCU near the fuel electrode of the SOFC. The Solid-Oxide Metal-Air Redox Battery (SOMARB) has been developed as a type of high-temperature reversible battery. The ZrO2-based material (yttria stabilized zirconia: YSZ) was used as the support. Ni/YSZ composite was used as fuel electrode and Lanthanum strontium manganite (LSM)/YSZ composite was used as the air electrode. Fe-oxide was used in the redox couple unit (RCU) for conversion between H2O and H2. The battery achieved good performance at temperature between 600-700oC. In addition, bilayer electrolyte has been studied to achieve good cell batteries. It is found that bilayer electrolyte can prevent electronic leakage thus help enhance the stability and performance of the cell. Nanostructured electrodes were fabricated by infiltration method. It is found that the nanostructured electrodes can significantly improve the cell performance as the electrochemical reaction sites can be enlarged significantly. 2. To characterize the novel rechargeable battery. The microstructure of the battery will be characterized using a scanning electron microscope (SEM). The polarization and EIS curves of the battery will be measured using an electrochemical workstation. The oxidation/reduction kinetics of the redox materials will be measured at different temperatures. The rechargeable battery electrochemical performance has been characterized by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and electrical conductivity relaxation (ECR) method. The electrode microstructure is characterized by SEM and TEM. The material properties are characterized by X-ray diffraction. Testing of the RCU is done at different temperatures. 3. To develop a theoretical electrolyte model to simulate the transport of ions and electrons across the SDC/ESB bilayer electrolyte in charging/discharging. A theoretical model is developed to study the transport of electrons and ions in the bilayer electrolyte. The distribution of the electrons and ions in the bilayer electrolyte is obtained. Based on parametric simulation, the bilayer electrolyte is optimized. 4. To develop a multi-physics model to simulate the coupled transport and reaction phenomena in the battery at the cell level. A multi-physics model is developed to simulate the performance of the rechargeable batteries developed in the project. The model is solved with commercial software COMSOL. Parametric simulations are conducted to understand the effects of operating/structural parameters on the performance of the batteries. Based on extensive parametric simulations, the configuration of the batteries can be optimized, such as the distance between the battery and the RCU. 5. To evaluate battery durability. The long-term performance of the battery is evaluated by operating the battery for more than 10 cycles. The batteries deliver stable output in the charge-discharge cycles without significant performance degradation.

15212714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212714.value: A rechargeable batteries based on solid oxide electrolyte and a redox cycling unit (RCU) is developed for energy storage with an operating temperature of about 600oC. The rechargeable batteries are fabricated, characterized, tested and modeled. It is found that the battery performance is dependent significantly on the operating condition, such as temperature and current density as well as the microstructure of the electrode and the RCU. The porosity of the RCU should be higher than 0.5 to avoid significant diffusion resistance. The current density of the solid oxide cell is found to significantly affect the H2 distribution in the cell. By developing nanostructured electrodes, the cell performance is found to increase significantly due to the greatly enhanced the electrochemical reaction sites. It is also found that the reduction of the metal oxide to metal for H2 production is a limiting factor for electricity generation (discharge mode). The bilayer electrolyte configuration is a good strategy to improve the stability of the electrolyte and minimize the electron leakage. To further improve the durability of the batteries, the operating conditions of the solid oxide cell need to be further decreased. Some new perovskite materials are developed for use as potential cathode and anode materials for the solid oxide cells. The rechargeable batteries could reach a high round trip efficiency of about 80%. For practical applications, the operating temperature of the batteries should be decreased. The research results are published as 19 papers in excellent SCI journals. The feasibility of the technology is demonstrated and the technology could be promising if the operating temperature can be reduced.

15212714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212714.value: To further improve the long-term durability of the proposed batteries, the working temperature of the solid oxide cells should be further decreased (down to 400oC). Extensive research efforts are needed to develop suitable electrolytes for operation at reduced temperature. High performance of the electrodes are also needed. Some layered perovskite materials can be developed for achieving good electrochemicatalytic performance at reduced temperature.

15212714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212714.value: Electrical energy storage (EES) is the key to enabling future smart grid and integrating intermittent renewable resources into power grids. Grid-scale EES requires high rate capacity, high round-trip efficiency, and good durability. The project aims to develop rechargeable batteries based on solid oxide cells (SOC) and a redox cycling unit (RCU). The SOC is used for power generation (discharge) or hydrogen production (charge) and the RCU is used for hydrogen generation (discharge) or hydrogen storage (charge). With bilayer electrolyte and nanostructured electrodes, the batteries could be operated with good efficiency, high rate capacity and high efficiency. The project explores innovative rechargeable batteries for large scale electrical energy storage. The research findings provide insights in the operating mechanisms of the proposed rechargeable batteries, especially the interaction between the SOC and the RCU. The project contribute to sustainable energy conversion and storage, which is important for a sustainable society.

15212914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212914.value: Maintaining thermal comfort in our buildings and the provision of hot water altogether consumes about 50% of global energy supplies, which currently are primarily fossil fuels. On the other hand, for these two uses, low grade ambient thermal and cooling sources which are renewable and sustainable, should suffice. Solar energy can be used for both hot water production and building heating, and diurnal natural cooling can be used for cooling buildings. This project aims at advancing one of the key technologies, the thermal energy storage(TES) technology, which enables the typical disparity between the availability of renewable sources and the timing of the demand for them to be resolved. Use of the latent heat of Phase-change-materials (PCM) is the focus of the proposed study. Integration of the high-conductivity solid cellular structure to enhance the conduction heat transfer of the solid phase while allowing the convection heat transfer of the liquid phase will be the major targeted characteristics of the technology. A pore structure geometry modelling method will be implemented to model the effects of pore structure on the transient conduction and convection heat transfer processes involving phase changes. The performance of different designs will be evaluated using the two indices proposed by the PI in his previous research, i.e., the volumetric storage capacity and the charging and discharging rates for a given temperature range and over a specified charging and discharging period. The outcome of the project will provide scientific guidance towards the development of new materials and engineering designs that address sustainability. The actual high resolution geometry of open cell metal foams will be obtained using computed X-ray tomography, and the data will be fed into a CFD code as the geometry input. This pore goemtry modelling method used for fluid flow and heat transfer is perceived to possess advantages over the current one and two temperature macro-scale model in properly modelling the convection heat transfer. More significantly, this method is more helpful in developing the optimal metal-foam morphology. The modelling results will be firstly validated with experimental results, and the model then used to examine a wide range of design possibilities under realistic application conditions. 在全球範圍內，用於提供良好的建築物熱環境和供應熱水所耗費的能源佔據了全部能源消耗的50%，這其中的主要能源來自於石油。另一方面，環境冷熱源作為可再生及可持續的低品位能源，可以很好地滿足上述兩方面的能源需求。具體來講，太陽能可以被用於熱水供應和建築供暖，而白天的自然冷源可以用於建築供冷。本研究課題的目的是發展儲能技術這項關鍵技術，以有效地解決存在於可再生能源供應與能耗需求時間上不匹配這個典型問題。本研究的重點在於如何提高相變材料中潛熱的利用效能。其主要技術特點在於通過將高導熱性的固態多孔結構整合到相變材料中去，以提高固相時相變材料的導熱效能並在液相時允許對流換熱。我們將採用一個多孔結構的幾何建模方法建立模型用以評估多孔結構對於包含相變的瞬時導熱和對流換熱過程的作用。我們將使用本項目首席研究員在之前的研究中提出的兩個指標來評估不同設計的性能。具體的說,該兩項指標為在給定工作溫度範圍及充能、放能時間段內，單位體積的蓄能能力以及所能達到的充能、放能速率。本項目的成果將會為新材料研發及工程設計領域提供可靠的科學技術指引，已達到可持續發展的目的。 首先，能反映該連通型泡沫金屬實際形態的高分辨率幾何結構將會通過使用X光計算機斷層掃描技術取得，之後這些數據將會作為幾何輸入被導入CFD計算流體力學模型中。這種用於模擬流體流動及換熱特性的多孔幾何模型相較於現有的單溫度及雙溫度宏觀模型在模擬對流換熱方面有著顯著的優勢。最為突出的是，這種方法對於開發最優的泡沫金屬形態有著極為顯著的幫助。該模擬結果將會首先與實驗結果進行對比校驗，之後將會被用於檢驗不同的設計方案在實際運行工況下的效能。

15212914.label: Realisation of objectives
15212914.value: The original objectives consist of two essential works: a) The first two objectives are to study heat transfer enhancement using open-cell metal foam with PCM impregnated inside; b) the second two are to examine the resultant maximum storage capacities using such a PCM. The overall research are conducted via combined use of modeling and experimental methods. Significant results are obtained as follows. a) Via dimensional analysis, it was found that the convection effects within liquid PCM, depending the temperature difference and geometry conditions of a thermal storage application, are just two times of pure conduction in terms of the equivalent conductivity. Therefore, a simplified pure conduction method is adopted to approximate the transient heat transfer within the PCM media, and equivalent conductivity is used to simulate the effects of different pore sizes of the metal form. The method helps to decouple the foam structure optimization from its application to a TES(thermal energy storage) device optimization. This study was published in the International Journal Heat and Mass Transfer (Fang et al 2018). b). Then efforts were made to define key performance indicators of an optimized TES device. In the first attempt, charging rate and discharging rate were proposed and experimentally compared with stratified water storage tank (Zhang and Niu 2016), and it was found that a PCM based tube and shell TES device would have substantially low charging and discharging rate when heat transfer were not enhanced.Then study focused on the optimized design of the tube-and-shell TES device. Firstly, the conjugate numerical heat transfer analysis method was validated against the theoretical value in the case of pipe flow and convection heat transfer, and then against experimental PCM melting process in a literature. Afterwards, the modeling analysis is used to examine the effects of design parameters on the key performance indicator of a TES device. Then the storage capacity at the same discharging rate was used the key performance indicator, what was compared with that a stratified water storage(SWS) tank. In such a way, the optimum design was found to exist, and it was found that for building cooling applications, a capacity of 4.4 times of that of stratified water storage tank can be achieved. (Fang et al 2018) c). To further examine the effects of other design parameters such as the length of the fluid flow path and the flow conditions in terms of laminar vs turbulent, an quasi-analytical approach was developed in comparison with the numerical approach, and it was found that turbulence can be employed to increase the charging and discharging rate. These studies clearly pointed out the directions and key technology know-how to realize practically competitive designs of PCM based tube and shell TES design. (Fang et al 2019) d). Finally an experimental test rig was constructed in collaboration with Shanghai University of using the PCM achieved two-fold effective storage capacity of a SWS system. This would be a first experimental study of a practical design that had achieved a practical performance (Fang et al 2019b, under review). This conclusion would look very encouraging for manufacturers who wish to develop TES alternative to water storage, and advantageous in terms of storage capacities.

These studies clearly pointed out the directions and key technology know-how to realize practically competitive designs of PCM based tube and shell TES design. (Fang et al 2019) d). Finally an experimental test rig was constructed in collaboration with Shanghai University of Science and Technology using the PCM achieved two-fold effective storage capacity of a SWS system. 15212914.value: Currently the PCM identified and tested, although made from low end by-products paraffin of petroleum, remains expensive, as it will compete with water in the market. In addition, preventing potential leaking in the storage device must be assured. The research team is working with colleagues working on chemical technology to tackle these two potentials batteries.

15212914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212914.value: In many applications, such as hot water supply, solar water heater, and cooling storage using chilled water, these exists the problem of the bulkiness of the device. i.e., the energy storage density is too low, which severely limits the potentials of energy saving using natural heating and cooling sources. It's very much like the case that our smart phone performance is being hindered by the frequent charging needs of the batteries. This research is about increasing the storage capacity of the thermal energy very much similar to increasing the capacity of a electrical battery used for a mobile device. The technology involved the use of phase-change materials(PCM) or artificial ice with a freezing temperature other than zero. The research is, on one hand, about improving the heat transfer properties of a PCM, and on the other hand, about the proper packing of the PCM in a container so that the final energy storage capacity can be substantially increased. What has been found in this project is that a capacity of more than 4 times of that a water storage can be potentially achieved by theoretical analysis, and that 2 times capacity has been demonstrated in a practical design.

15213014.label: Realisation of objectives
15213014.value: i. Design and application of a compact and efficient brushless variable speed constant frequency electric machine. Based on flux modulation method, this machine is designed with magnetic field and electric field integration. The operation principle and the relationship within the internal physical quantities have been comprehensively explained based on magnetic flux modulation effect, and the gear ratios regulation elaborated. The harmonic components and spectra of magnetic fields have been investigated. One potential structure with the radial flux structure and two consequent pole rotors have been designed. Another has a radial flux structure with one flux modulation rotor and surface mounted PM rotor has also studied and compared. Both designs can realize good power flow regulation and constant voltage and frequency electricity generation under variable wind speeds. With magnetic flux modulation effects, this design can efficiently capture the wind energy and continuously change the power flow to realize the wind energy split and mixing at different working modes. This design can be used as to generate power at constant frequency to infinite busbars without power electronic devices. With this design, under fluctuating wind speed, although the inner rotor speed changes as wind speed changes, the outer rotor can be controlled to produce constant frequency output via the inner stator windings supply. The innovative wind power generator system has a two-fold merit: it increases the utilization rate of wind and henc significantly improving the energy conversion efficiency of the electric generator. It also has a high reliability and eliminates maintenance problems related to slip ring assembly and brushes that are inevitable in conventional doubly fed electric machines. ii. Modeling and optimization of compound-structure electric machine. • The proposed modeling and optimization design techniques are powerful tools to analyze complicated operations of the electric system with multi rotating parts as well as its control system. By using surface response methodology (SRM), the relationship between the design parameters, such as PM height, slot and york dimensions and modulation pole height and width. The associated performance of the proposed machine, such as torque, efficiency has been re-established. • Based on the surface response model, improved optimization methods including genetic algorithm (GA) have been used to calculate the objective function. iii. Commission and test the prototype and control system to operate at different working modes stably and efficiently. The whole wind system, including the electric machine with two sets of stator windings and rotors, the power converters, position sensor and electronic controller, is used to verify the efficiency of proposed system. • The related work to verify the MPPT control and power flow regulation strategy of the whole system has been carried out. • The machine and its system performance including the efficiency of the machine and the efficiency of the whole system, the temperature rise of machine with different loadings have been evaluated. • The test under various operating conditions have been used to quantitatively analyze the effective improvements of the machine. The improvement of wind power generation technology will improve the wind energy harvesting efficiency to reduce global warming and environmental hazards.

15213014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213014.value: The electrical continuously variable transmission system is a very promising concept for variable-speed constant-frequency wind power generation due to its ability of seamless speed adjustment. In this paper, a novel wind energy conversion system based on electrical continuously variable transmission is proposed. This system combines the merits of two popular wind generation concepts: It enjoys high torque density like the permanent-magnet synchronous generator system and, also, it needs only a partial-scale converter like a doubly fed induction generator system. With a special doubly fed dual rotor structure, the system realizes both speed variation and power generation within one single machine, which makes it very compact. Besides introducing its structure and working principle, the design and performance analysis of the machine are presented. A prototype is made and tested for validation. A new brushless contra-rotating power split transmission (CR-PST) system for the direct-drive wind power generation is developed. The core element of this system is a doubly fed dual-rotor flux-modulation permanent magnet machine, which has two contra-rotating rotors connected with two wind blades to absorb the wind energy, and two sets of stator windings to realize torque split between the two shafts. This proposed CR-PST system has compact structure and bidirectional flux-modulation design, as well as increased wind power conversion efficiency. Compared with the conventional wind turbine system, which can only work with single maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control strategy, the proposed CR-PST system can collect increased wind energy with dual MPPT method for the given wind speed. Time-stepping finite-element method is used to analyze the steady and dynamic performance of the proposed system and the control strategy is verified by experiments and simulation results.

15213014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213014.value: The future study could focus on how to control the inner rotor position with a small servo motor and with the bi-directional flux modulation effect, the resultant induced voltages in two sets of stator windings can be adjusted accordingly. Consequently, in a wide wind speed range the various-speed constant-amplitude-voltage operation is realized. With the advent of high-temperature superconducting (HTS) materials, increasing attention is given to HTS machines, which have good application potentials in large wind turbine systems. In future, HTS material based brushless variable speed constant frequency wind generation system can be designed with much more compact than conventional machines, by virtue of the large excitation current and high efficiency of the former, because the losses in the superconducting wires are virtually zero.

15213014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213014.value: This project aims to design a gearless, brushless, variable speed constant frequency power split wind generator to enhance the wind energy harvesting efficiency. The innovative wind power generator system has two-fold merits: it has high reliability without those maintenance problems due to gearboxes, slip ring assembly and brushes which are inevitable in conventional doubly fed generators. This design has great potential in variable speed constant frequency wind energy system in that it has, i) Compact and integrated structure without large-capacity converters. With this dual stator and rotor coupled structure, the volume is reduced greatly compared to the mechanical CVT based design. The outer stator is directly connected to the power grid using small-capacity AC/AC converter. ii) Enhanced control flexibility. This machine ingeniously integrates the magnetic flux modulating effects to achieve continuously changeable speed regulation to keep the outer rotor speed constant over a wide range of wind speed. Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and power flow regulation can be realized through controlling the inner stator winding currents. iii) Improved efficiency and reliability. The innovative system increases the effective wind speed range and enhances the efficiency for energy extraction.

15213214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213214.value: In Hong Kong, about 800 tonnes of sewage sludge solids are produced everyday. This amount will dramatically increase and reach about 1,500 tonnes solids/day in 2014 due to the extension and upgrading of some existing sewage treatment facilities and the completion of the Harbour Area Treatment Scheme (HATS) Stage 2A. To correctly manage the anticipated increases in sewage sludge production, the EPD of Hong Kong is currently constructing the world’s largest sewage sludge incinerator which is designed to combust a maximum of 2,000 tonnes of sludge a day. The combustion of sewage sludge produces incinerated sewage sludge ash (ISSA). Unfortunately this is currently a problem because ISSA requires disposal. The current plan is to dispose of the ISSA to landfill. However, Hong Kong is rapidly running out of landfill capacity for the disposal of the city’s municipal solid waste. Consequently, it is of acute importance to investigate different ways of diverting and using this ISSA from landfill via the identification and investigation of adequate re-use and resource recovery pathways. The aim is to develop technology to allow the ISSA to be a valuable resource by extracting phosphate and producing a supplementary cementitious material from the residual fraction Although a few previous preliminary studies have been done in this area, all of these studies and processes are based on recovering phosphate from a Ca-phosphate mineral. It is highly likely that the phosphate in HK ISSA, due to the high proportion of primary sludge generated by the CEPT (Chemically Enhanced Primary Treatment) will be in the form of Fe-phosphate. Another factor that may affect the form of phosphate minerals present in HK ISSA is the extensive use of seawater for toilet flushing. These will require the modification of existing recovery processes or the development of entirely new ones. The research aims to demonstrate that it is possible to re-use the unique characteristics of ISSA produced in Hong Kong as a source of phosphate for the production of either fertilizers or high purity phosphoric acid. This research project has the potential to significantly improve the economics of sewage sludge incineration as a waste management technology and to improve public perception of sewage sludge incineration from an environmental point of view. 在香港,每天大約有800噸的污水淤泥產生. 由於污水處理設施的擴張和升級改造工程,以及海港淨化第2A階段的完成,這個數量在2014年的時候可能會迅速增加至每天1500噸.為了正確處理預期增加的污水淤泥,香港環保署目前正在建造一個世界上最大的淤泥焚化爐,設計每天最大焚燒量達2,000噸. 儘管如此,焚燒淤泥產生的淤泥灰仍然需要處理.目前的計畫是將淤泥灰丟棄到填埋區.然而,香港現有的填埋區所剩空間不多,可能很快就會被城市固體垃圾用盡.因此,探索和研究合適的方法將淤泥灰迴圈再用和資源回收,減少填埋,是非常重要的工作. 這個專案的目的在於開發新技術,從淤泥灰中提取用途廣泛的磷元素,然後將剩下的灰用於替代水泥,從而將淤泥灰轉化為有用的資源.前人對這一方面有一定的研究,但是這些研究都是基於從含鋁的磷酸鹽中提取磷.然而,香港的淤泥灰中磷的存在方式很大可能與此不同,原因是從化學輔助一級處理污水後得到的初沉淤泥中的磷可能大量是以含鐵的磷酸鹽形式存在.另外,香港廣泛使用海水沖廁,這也有可能會影響香港的淤泥灰中磷元素的存在形式.這就需要改進現有的提磷方法甚至需要開發適用於香港淤泥灰的新方法. 這項研究旨在驗證迴圈再用具有含磷特殊性質的香港淤泥灰來提取磷,然後用於生產肥料或者高純度的磷酸是可行的.這項研究具有很大的潛力提高焚化污水淤泥作為廢料管理技術的經濟效益以及提高公眾從環保角度看待焚化處理污水淤泥.

15213214.label: Realisation of objectives
15213214.value: Firstly, this project systematically assessed the physicochemical, morphological and mineralogical characteristics of ISSA from Hong Kong, and the leachability and risk of heavy metals. The results showed that a low hydraulic and pozzolanic potential was associated with the ISSA due to the presence of low contents of SiO2, Al2O3 and CaO and high contents of P, S and Cl. Although high concentrations of Zn and Cu followed by Ni, Pb and As, Se were detected, a low leaching rate of these metals rendered them classifiable as non-hazardous. The leached metals concentrations from ISSA were mainly pH dependent, and metals solubilization occurred mainly at low pH. Different leaching tests should be adopted based on the simulated different environmental conditions and exposure scenarios for assessing the leachability as contrasting results could be obtained due to the differences in complexing abilities and final pH of the leaching solutions. Then, this project investigated P recovery and leaching of metals from ISSA using inorganic acids (sulphuric acid and nitric acid), organic acids (oxalic acid and citric acid), and chelating agents (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and ethylene diamine tetramethylene phosphonate (EDTMP)). Chemical extraction of P from ISSA is adversely influenced by co-dissolution of metals. The results show that both organic and inorganic acids extract P-containing phases but organic acids leach more trace elements, particularly Cu, Zn, Pb and As. Sulphuric acid was the most efficient for P recovery and achieved 94% of total extraction under the optimal conditions, which were 2-h reaction with 0.2 mol/L H2SO4 at a liquid-to-solid ratio of 20:1. EDTA extracted only 20% of the available P, but the leachates were contaminated with high levels of trace elements under optimum conditions (3-h reaction with EDTA at 0.02 mol/L, pH 2, and liquid-to-solid ratio of 20:1). Therefore, EDTA was considered an appropriate pre-treatment agent for reducing the total metal/metalloid content in ISSA, which produced negligible changes in the structure of ISSA and reduced contamination during subsequent P extraction using sulphuric acid. As such, a two-step extraction method which can produce highly purified P-extract where ISSA is treated first with EDTA and then with sulphuric acid was developed. The recovery conditions of this two-step extraction method were optimized (pre-extraction by 0.02 mol/L of EDTA at a liquid to solid ratio (L/kg) of 20:1 during 120 min, then extraction by 0.2 mol/L sulphuric and at a liquid to solid ratio of 20:1 during 120 min). Compared with direct extraction by sulphuric acid (namely, single-step leaching), the two-step extraction method dissolved 2.34 mmol/kg ISSA less of P, but with 5.16 mmol/kg ISSA less of metal(loid) contamination. Furthermore, the potential for co-precipitation of P and the metal(loid) contaminates in the extracts was examined from pH 2 to 12 (adjusted by addition of NaOH and Ca(OH)2). By applying Ca(OH)2 and at the optimal pH of 4, the two-step extraction method could significantly increase Ca-P in the precipitate and notably decreased the metal(loid) contaminants by 50% compared to the single-step method. In addition, a novel procedure for P recovery as struvite from ISSA was proposed and investigated in this project. The procedure is divided into three steps: transform P in the ISSA to amorphous iron phosphate (Fe-P) and aluminum phosphate (Al-P) by acid washing followed by alkali precipitation, re-dissolve Fe-P and Al-P via acid washing and adsorption of Fe and Al ions by a cation exchange resin (CER), and struvite crystallization. Results showed that about 80.4% P in the ISSA was successfully transformed to Fe-P and Al-P accompanied by achieving the removal of most undesirable metals. Subsequently, Fe and Al ions in the leachate of completely re-dissolution of Fe-P and Al-P in 2N HCl were absorbed by CER to obtain a purified P solution. Over 99.0% of P in the purified P solution was recovered as struvite with a high purity (76.0%) and low heavy metal contents (＜50 mg/ kg) at a 1:1:1M ratio of Mg: N: P and pH of 9.5. Overall, 79.7% P in the ISSA could be recovered as struvite with negligible environmental risk. Moreover, to simplify the P recycling process and maximize the P recovery, this project innovatively used Mg/Ca-modified biochars to take up P from the acid-extract from ISSA at low pH (<2). Peanut shell and sugarcane bagasse were used to synthesize Mg/Ca-modified biochars at pyrolysis temperatures of 450 oC, 700 oC and 850 oC. Preliminary results indicated Mg-modified sugarcane bagasse biochar pyrolysed at 700 oC produced optimal P-absorption. This biochar was positively charged and had a high specific surface area (1440 m2/g), consistent with a layered porous structure. The optimal biochar showed rapid adsorption of P which could be described by the pseudo-second-order model. Successful adsorption of P from the acid-extract by the optimal biochar was mainly due to chemical precipitation and its adsorption capacity is ~130 mg P/g biochar. The post-sorption biochar complied with relevant acceptance criteria and had potential to be used as a P-fertilizer. After the extraction, the residual ISSA from each study was assessed in particular detail, focusing on the leachability of remaining Zn and Cu, major element composition, crystalline phases and overall degree of crystallinity and particle size distribution. The residual ISSA was also evaluated as a pozzolanic material using a Strength Activity Index (SAI) test with mortars containing Portland cement with a 20% substitution by ISSA. All results were compared to tests with untreated ISSA. Overall, the use of 3 of the 6 extractants could be ruled out due to poor P recovery potential and/or a serious compromise of the potential reuse of residual ISSA in Portland cement-based materials. The results highlight the added value of considering the potential reuse of residual ISSA when trying to optimize P recovery from ISSA by wet methods. At last, bench-scale Pot experiments under various conditions were conducted to evaluate the agronomic effectiveness of three produced different RPFs (struvite (SP), calcium phosphate compounds (CaP), P-loaded biochar (BP)) recovered from ISSA as sources of P on cultivation of choy sum (Brassica campestris L. ssp. Chinensis var. utillis Tsen et Lee) and ryegrass. Choy sum was grown through hydroponics using standard Hoagland solution with P substituted by RPFs or commercial monopotassium phosphate (MP) at 31mg P/L. Ryegrass, meanwhile, was cultivated by soil culture using RPFs or commercial compound fertilizer (CoF). The plant growth was characterized based on shoot length, biomass yield, P concentration and heavy metal accumulation in plants. The results showed that RPF greatly facilitated plant growth and demonstrated superior/comparable effects to that of MP/CoF. In general, choy sum fertilized with SP showed the best effect due to the Mg involved and high P bioavailability of SP, while ryegrass fertilized with BP performed the best of all groups because of additional nutrient elements in BP. Additionally, accumulation of heavy metal in plants under all conditions did not exceed the limits stipulated in the regulations. These denote that recovering P from ISSA is an attractive technology to produce P-fertilizers, which can help alleviate both the scarcity of phosphate resources and the burden of ash management.

15213214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213214.value: As summarized in Part C, 10 SCI journal papers (of which 5 are considered Top 10% by CiteScore) and 1 book chapter have been produced by this project. In order to safeguard the environment security and resilience for sustainable development, there is an imminent need to develop effective strategies to recycling ISSA from T·Park in Hong Kong. In this project, the comprehensive physical and chemical characteristics of Hong Kong ISSA were obtained. The leachability and the associated environmental risk of metal(loid)s from the ISSA were highlighted in an attempt to improve the public perception of sewage sludge incineration from an environmental perspective. Afterwards, an innovative two-step extraction method was developed to obtain a P-extract with high purity. During the extraction process, effect of several extractants on the release of P and associated metals from ISSA was comprehensively investigated. Then, a series of P fertilizer products, including Ca-P, P-loaded biochar and struvite, were formed by laboratory scale processes. Agronomic analysis of the regenerated P products from ISSA under various cultivation conditions on different crops was conducted by trial-scale results. In addition, the characteristics and re-use values of P-free ISSA as cementitious materials were evaluated. These findings will provide valuable information for establishing pilot-scale/full-scale investigations and unprecedented local technical guideline for design and operation of sustainable ISSA treatment system in the future.

15213214.value: For beneficial reuse of ISSA from the world’s largest sewage sludge incineration facility (T·Park) in Hong Kong, transforming what is currently regarded as a problematic waste into an innovative business opportunity. This project evaluated the feasibility of wet-extraction (e.g., H2SO4 leaching) for recovering P from ISSA in high-purity extracts and transforming into P fertilizers (e.g., struvite). The performances and mechanisms of P recycling and transformation processes were systematically investigated in this project, which provided a solid and scientific foundation for future pilot-scale/field-scale projects for sustainable management of ISSA. The agronomic analysis-relevant findings of our project will be expected to deliver indispensable information for facilitating the future application of the produced P fertilizers.

15213414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213414.value: Navigation is about route planning or guiding for cars or persons. The foremost important key to the success of a navigation system is to compute an accurate and reliable path before considering effective audio-visual means of guiding users to traverse that path. Such navigation solutions are often multi-criteria that vary both spatially and temporally. Traditional path finding models have largely been based on pre-defining weights of planar graph arcs and nodes for one or a combination of criteria. These weights are often more objective and static parameters such as distance, time and toll cost. Yet, our empirical studies show that even when the same parameter(s) are used, path computation and solution can vary for different navigation systems; and that all these may differ from the path adopted by experienced drivers or pedestrians. What are the problems? One thought is mobility, which involves a lot of behavioral issues, may not be adequately incorporated. However, factors like safety and familiarity are not easy to be quantified and pre-computed. These spatio-temporal variants are also perceived differently from individuals to individuals. This study therefore proposes a reverse engineering approach for navigation solutions – instead of deriving a path from all pre-determined variables, existing travel behavior is the prime determinant. Flow (both traffic and pedestrian flow) data from different sources (e.g. sensors, images, mobile positioning) are used to classify the paths at different times into essential, optional and undesirable paths. Algorithms are to be developed to stitch the preferred paths to the origin and destination. The resulting path may not be contradictory to that from previous models, but rather to evaluate, reinforce or complement these past methods by a heuristic: preferred environment implied by empirical flow data. On the other hand, the relative weights and importance of other unknown behavioral variables associated with these popular paths will be uncovered. This is enabled through multiple criteria decision making (MCDM) methods and spatial correlation techniques for environmental variables such as visibility of landmarks or traffic signs, path geometry and surrounding land use. It is hoped that the findings can contribute to improving existing commercial navigation systems, in which path findings for both car drivers and pedestrians have widely been adopted in many big cities in recent decades. Suggestions from these systems would become more credible and closer to human preference. 導航能為駕駛者及行人規劃及指導路線。一個成功的導航系統，最重要的是爲使用者提供準確及可靠的路綫，然後才提供一個有效的表達方式去指導使用者到達目的地。導航系統的解决方案隨著空間和時間而變化。傳統的路綫找尋模型依靠預先對地圖中各曲綫及節點定立的參數(比重)去計算路線。而這些參數(比重)基於一個或數個較為客觀及靜態的準則去量度，例如距離，時間和路費成本。然而，我們的經驗研究表明，即使使用相同的參數(比重)，不同的導航系統也會計算出不同的路綫，而且這些路綫也可能和有經驗的駕駛者及行人使用的路綫不相同。究竟是什麼問題？其中一個原因可能是由于流動涉及到行爲的問題不能被充分整合。然而，像安全性和熟悉性的因素不容易被量化及預先計算。而且這些時間及空間的變數也是因人而異的。因此，本研究提出以逆向工程作爲導航系統的解决方案──而不是利用一些預先制定的參數去計算路綫，現有的交通行爲是主要的决定因素。流量（包括車輛及行人）的數據有不同的來源（例如：傳感器，圖像，移動定位）；基於這些數據，道路會在不同時間被分為不同的級別：必需，可選擇及不建議。本研究會撰寫計算由出發點至目的地路綫的算法。算法中會包括多準則決策（MCDM）及利用環境變量的空間相關技術，例如地標，交通標誌或道路（幾何）的可見度以及附近的土地利用。通過新算法計算出的路綫不一定和使用傳統算法所計算出的路綫有衝突，但通過新算法的啓發：透過實證流量決定首撰的路線，傳統的算法可以被評估，加強或補充。另一方面，和這些流行路綫相關，而未被發現的變數之間的比重及重要性也可以被發現。爲駕駛者及行人提供的導航系統已在最近十年在許多大城市中被廣泛采用，希望透過是次研究，現有的商業導航系統能被改善。使這些系統計算出的路綫，變得更加可靠，更加貼近人們的偏好。

15213414.label: Realisation of objectives
15213414.value: Despite the popularity of using various commercial online path finding systems for driving and walking, such as Google, Baidu, there have always been a doubt that these solutions may not be the best as these are presumed to be derived from simple parameters such as distance and toll fee. The project rationale is to derive a more realistic path finding system taking into account of the people’s perception/behavior. It is assumed that popular paths which are reflected in higher flow volume are better choices. Hong Kong with its very dense network of driving and walking paths offers a good study case that offers numerous path alternatives. As the project scope covers both driving and walking paths, to achieve objective 1, data collection and analyses are treated and explained separately. Regarding the research on driving paths, several origin-destination pairs distributed in various directions throughout HK Island and covering long and short routes were tested. For each pair of O-D, path finding solutions from the followings are compared and analysed: a) Four path finding engines in the market namely Google, HKeRouting, Baidu and Gaode b) Site observations from taxi drivers, recording the major and minor paths they have taken; and c) In-house development of the heuristic flow- and behavior-based path finding model (objective 1). The comparison extracted all common and different street segments (one segment is defined from junction to junction) among all the above-mentioned six routes. In particular, the heuristic model was analysed to what extent it matched with those routes chosen by the taxi drivers. The generation of a complete driving network with appropriate attributes was key to the derivation of driving routes. Apart from distance and time that were already available in base map from Survey and Mapping Office of the Lands Department and traffic information from the Transport Department, the new model requires flow volume in space and time. Real time vehicular flow volume were collected from various sources: AADT of Transport Department, data from GoGo Van, headway information of public transport from HKeTransport (Pun-Cheng, 2018), and at last supplemented by site observations of manual counting and video-recording. Correlation between real time traffic and number of lanes was also conducted, so that streets with no traffic flow data might be inferred from the number of lanes. Integration of all these data has produced flow map patterns or path trajectories of varying time-spans. On the other hand, paths are computed and classified in accordance with traditional centrality measures of degree, betweenness, closeness, clustering coefficient and page rank. Like number of lanes, these are correlated with three types of traffic flow data as mentioned previously. Essentially multiple linear regression model and random forest were applied. All these then form a dynamic database for path computation. The algorithm starts with a defined origin (starting node, ns) and destination (ending node, ne). Traditional approach was to trace all interconnected arcs and nodes and find one with least cost or energy. Exhaustive search of all possible combinations may sometimes involve backward search which lowers computational efficiency. Unlike previous studies of using a rectangle or symmetrical meshes, the search region was confined by a filtering parabola in the direction from the origin, O towards the destination, D. The size of the parabola as defined by the distance a which varies with different path finding applications. a, better to be empirically derived, is an acceptable walking distance or backward direction driving distance. This can confine searching space to a reasonable extent and eliminate unnecessary connections that lead to winding and illogical paths. When searching a path from a chosen origin to destination, instead of starting to search a connected path sequentially and iteratively from ns or ne, the basis is to look for paths of higher flow (that shows more preferred and popular paths despite the risk of traffic delays) in the direction towards ne. Based on the identification of primary essential paths (pe), secondary optional paths (po) and undesirable paths (pu) according to their real time car traffic flow, the heuristic path finding algorithm has been developed in accordance with the explanation in the proposal. The main principle is to give priority to the most popular set of paths instead of shortest or fastest ones. For walking network, the commercial Central Business District and the residential Yuen Long District were taken as the case studies. All walking paths including streets, elevated walkways, subways and paths inside malls and MTR were digitized and quantified with various environmental variables of road width, brightness, greenness and flow volume. The first three were mostly obtainable or derived from base maps with features like parks, lamp posts; whereas pedestrian flow volume was measured on site in daytime and at night. Each district was assigned a fixed origin and destination and about 50 subjects were asked to indicate their routine route on the map. Besides, they were also interviewed on the preference of different walking environments. Paths (junction to junction) were recorded 0-50, with higher number being more popular. Routes from Google were then compared with the actual walking routes of the subjects. When quantifying no matter driving or walking paths, apart from flow volume, other environmental variables such as openness, greenness, brightness were also collected. Each of these has been correlated with the paths chosen by the taxi drivers and the walking subjects, thus achieving objective 2, “to identify, quantify and assign weights to significant behavioral variables in path finding based on the real time flow volume and path popularity”. There are some problems for fulfilling the original design. First, securing traffic flow data of 7x24 hours to cover the whole area was challenging. Interpolated or estimated data such as inferring from number of lanes, adopting an interpolated model were some of the solutions. Processing CCTV image data for deriving the count of vehicles under varying environmental conditions pose another solution for major roads and highways. Second, behavioural data were confined to taxi drivers and interviewed pedestrian subjects. The scope could be extended if online positioning devices were agreed to be installed, and more companies’ data like taxi companies and Google could be obtained with reasonable cost.

15213414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213414.value: The followings are the major findings and research outcome for driving: a) Deriving a more accurate approach to traffic flow estimation could provide a better methodology for navigation software engineering when real-time traffic flow may not be every-where and every time available, we have researched into the relationships between traffic flow and topological and geometrical properties of the road network. It is found that a combination of topological and geometrical measures results in higher correlation (R) than a mere single measure. The multiple regression approach is more superior to estimating traffic flow based on mere road network properties such as length (Pun, Zhao & Liu, 2019). Besides, correlation between traffic flow and number of lanes have found to be high (Pun-Cheng & Zhao, 2018). b) Image processing using a three-frame differencing approach has proved to be accurate to detect and count vehicles captured by CCTV images, even under bad weather conditions in Hong Kong (Yang & Pun-Cheng, 2018). c) Actual driving behavior (for experienced taxi drivers) has proved to be different from the paths provided by commercial navigation engines, especially in the choice of minor roads closer to the origins and destinations. It is as well noted that these engines themselves do not provide the same solutions. The followings are the major findings related to walking (Pun-Cheng & So, 2019): a) It is interesting to find that people do not really select walking routes according to their perceived and preferred variables for comfort. There is no dominant selection for ground-level paths of high degree of greenness, wide roads and low pedestrian flow. A marked difference can be seen at night time. Paths of high pedestrian flow and high brightness are two obvious preferred environmental variables for the sake of safety. b) Currently, navigation engines focus mainly on distance and time. To improve recommended routes, other factors like pedestrian flow, brightness and greenness should also be incorporated into the computation. In particular within a street block, more people prefer walking through a park or sitting out area instead of just by a main road. c) The routes picked by the subjects are significantly different from that recommended by Google, which is of about 5 minutes’ walking time. This implies pedestrian’s behavior and preference of different walking environments should be incorporated in future navigation engines.

15213414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213414.value: Data sourcing and big data analysis are two areas worthy of further investigation. In terms of transport research in which navigation is sub-area, sourcing of dynamic information like traffic flow, pedestrian flow, drivers and pedestrian behaviours always pose a big challenge especially if fine details in space (up to per street segment) and time (up to per minute) are required. This project has suggested and implemented some methods only. Future research may focus on real time data collection via electronic devices, transmission, summarization, analysis and propagation. These are also related to positioning accuracy of at least metre level, big data analytics of extracting reliable information into meaningful summary, computational efficiency in terms of several minutes and privacy encryption. On the other hand, transport activities might be correlated with other disciplines such as pollution, demography and land use. Likewise, it is also interesting to know if vehicular traffic and pedestrian traffic patterns have any effect on each other, so as to throw more lights on transport planning.

15213414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213414.value: Navigation systems for both vehicles and pedestrians have become increasingly popular in the past decade with a lot of online searching engines. Conventional path finding algorithms starting from late 1950s have largely been based on planar graphs interconnected arcs and nodes, starting from the origin or destination and traversing those with least cost pre-defined weights normally of easily quantifiable variables such as distance, time and fare. The more subjective behavioral issues are not accounted for very well into these traditional models. There is little empirical research on whether the algorithms in these commercialized navigation systems match the actual path finding choice of experienced drivers or pedestrians. This project has adopted a reverse engineering approach closer to human behavior, in which behavioral variables such as visibility, familiarity and security will also be considered and quantified to more accurately compute an optimal (which needs not be the shortest or fastest) path with time variant. The significance of this research is two-fold: academically it is a new path finding approach incorporating new behavioral variables; commercially such algorithms can be implemented in future navigation systems. The suggested paths of ‘drive to’ or ‘walk to’ will become more reliable and marketable.

15213814.label: Project Objectives
15213814.value: VM-aware PCM-based memory optimization techniques in mobile virtualization environment. By cooperating VMM and PCM, our objective is to jointly optimize the time/energy of VMs by developing energy-aware PCM page tuning techniques that can adapt to various memory demands. PCM-based VM management techniques that target on optimizing performance-critical VM activities (e.g. checkpoint/restore). PCM-assisted VM-image storage optimization techniques. 15213814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213814.value: 通過在移動設備中同時運行多個虛擬機，移動虛擬化技術可以有效降低系統開發成本，並利用代碼重用縮短產品開發時間及虛擬機相互隔離的特性增強系統隱私和安全性。然而，移動虛擬化技術也給內、外存等底層設備的設計帶來了新的挑戰。首先，每個虛擬機及其承載的應用程序的內存需求存在很大差異，而且諸如檢查點信息保存等虛擬機關鍵功能需要大量訪存和IO操作。傳統的DRAM存儲器由於容量大小固定不能滿足以上要求，當缺頁頻率增大后更將導致系統性能下降。其次，諸如eMMC、SD存儲卡和SSDs（固態硬盤）這類基於NAND閃存的存儲器已被廣泛地運用於移動設備中，但是它們的特性在移動虛擬化環境中還沒有被充分考慮，這將有可能導致NAND閃存壽命縮短和系統性能下降。最后，移動設備資源有限，特別是有限的能量和存儲容量等因素需要在移動虛擬化技術的開發過程中加以考慮。 我們首次提出在移動虛擬化中使用相變存儲器等新型非易失存儲技術解決來解決上述問題。具體來說，我們將從以下幾方面探索基於相變存儲器的移動虛擬化技術：（1）虛擬機感知的存儲技術。在綜合考慮性能和能耗優化的同時,使系統能滿足各虛擬機對存儲容量的不同需求﹔（2）虛擬機管理技術。主要優化以性能為考量的虛擬機功能（如檢查點/恢復）。目標是通過優化檢查點/恢復時間，實現系統性能、能耗和相變存儲器存儲容量三者間的平衡，以較低的能耗實現重復數據刪除並減少相變存儲器的空間佔用﹔（3）虛擬機鏡像的存儲優化技術。通過將冷/熱數據（例如文件系統的元數據和常規數據）分別存入虛擬機鏡像文件中和緩存入相變存儲器中，來提高系統的性能和NAND閃存的壽命，以達到減少IO阻塞的目標。 本項目所研究的移動虛擬化和新型存儲技術的協同設計，將為移動虛擬化研究創造新的發展機遇。項目在實現移動虛擬化的過程中，可以在新型的存儲技術和系統結構設計之間找到理想的折衷方案，這將為現實生活中的許多移動應用創造更好的發展機會。

15213814.label: Realisation of objectives
15213814.value: The project has been going very well, and all objectives have been 100% achieved. With the support of this fund, one MPhil student was recruited; the student converted to the PhD program and successfully passed his defense in May 2019. In total, 6 journal papers and 8 conferences have been published. Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 1, we have investigated VM (Virtual Machine)-aware PCM (Phase Change Memory)-based memory optimization techniques in mobile virtualization environment. We have developed several techniques to jointly optimize the time/energy of VMs by developing energy-aware PCM page tuning techniques that can adapt to various memory demands by cooperating VMM (Virtual Machine Monitor) and PCM. Our detailed activities are as follows: (1) We investigate how to utilize NVM (Non-Volatile Memory) such as PCM to optimize I/O and energy performance in smart phones. In particular, we propose a NVM-aware random access (NVMRA) scheme that can exploit the I/O behaviors of applications to improve the random write performance for each application. Based on different I/O behaviors, such as random write-dominant I/O behavior, NVMRA adopts different storing decisions so as to jointly optimize I/O performance and energy. We also study how to utilize NVM to transparently optimize I/O and energy performance by adding a software layer that works on the bottom of the software I/O stack and makes use of application I/O features to transparently manage NVM. The above results have been published in [J1]. (2) We have developed VM-aware PCM-based memory optimization. In particular, we propose a technique called Balloonfish that can efficiently and effectively utilize NVM for joint energy/performance optimization in virtualized smart phones. Balloonfish can convert the memory cell state between multilevel and single-level and dynamically allocate memory space among multiple virtual machines so as to achieve a balance between performance and memory space. Our evaluation based on the Samsung Exynos 5250 system-on-chip with various real Android applications shows that our technique achieves joint energy/performance improvement compared with the previous work. These results have been published in the journal article [J2]. (3) We studied page optimization techniques for hybrid main memory architecture. Specifically, the storage subsystem in mobile devices such as smartphones has always been a prohibitive factor that slows down the pace of reaching even higher performance while maintaining good user experience. Despite today’s smartphones are equipped with larger-than-ever main memories, they consume more energy and still run out of memory. But the slow NAND flash based storage vetoes the possibility of swapping—an important technique to extend main memory—and leaves a system that constantly terminates user applications under memory pressure. We proposed NVM-Swap by revisiting swapping for smartphones with fast, byte-addressable, non-volatile memory technologies. Instead of using flash, we build the swap area with NVM, to allow high performance without sacrificing user experience. NVM-Swap supports Lazy Swap-in, which can reduce memory copy operations by giving the swapped out pages a second chance to stay in byte-addressable NVM backed swap area. To avoid fast worn-out of certain NVM, we also propose Heap-Wear, a wear leveling algorithm that distributes writes in NVM more evenly. Evaluation results based on the Google Nexus 5 smartphone show that our solution can effectively enhance smartphone performance and achieve better wear-leveling of NVM. The above results have been published in the journal article [J6]. (4) In [C3], we aim to optimize redundant writes in NVM-based virtual machine with garbage collector, in which a large amount of extra NVM writes are generated. We propose three techniques: Living Objects Remapping (LORE), Dead Object Stamping (DOS), and Smart Wiping with Maximum Likelihood Estimation (SMILE) to reduce the unnecessary writes when garbage collector handles objects. The experimental results show that the proposed techniques not only significantly reduce the writes during each garbage collection cycle but also greatly improve the performance of virtual machine. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 2, we have investigated PCM-based VM management techniques that target on optimizing performance-critical VM activities (e.g. checkpoint/restore). Our objective is to balance the trade-offs among the time, energy and PCM space by optimizing the checkpoint/restore duration while reducing PCM usage with deduplicatoin under energy constraints of mobile devices. To achieve Objective 2, we have conducted various studies in optimizing checkpoint/restore. Specifically, we propose a technique called FLIC that is a fast and lightweight checkpointing machinery for virtualized mobile devices by taking advantages of recent byte-addressable, non-volatile memory. Instead of saving the VM’s entire memory to storage, we store its working set pages in NVRAM, avoiding accessing slow flash memory (compared to server-grade SSDs). To further reduce the write activities to flash memory, we propose an energy-efficient data deduplication to eliminate redundant data in VM snapshot and save storage space. Experimental results based on an Exynos 5250 SoC show that our approach can effectively improve the performance of checkpointing in mobile virutalization and save energy [C1, J5]. Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 3, we have investigated PCM-assisted VM-image storage optimization techniques. By separating hot/cold data of a running VM (e.g. file system metadata and regular file data) and caching hot data in PCM, our objective is to reduce IO traffic to improve the system performance and lifetime of NAND flash in mobile devices. As NAND flash is widely used as storage media in mobile devices, our research activities for Objective 3 are divided into two parts: In Part I, we studied underlying NAND flash management schemes so as to fully understand how to exploit NAND flash characteristics in optimize VM-image-aware optimization; In Part II, we then investigate how to utilize PCM to optimize VM-image storage by considering underlying NAND flash. Our detailed activities in the two parts are shown as follows: (1) We have conducted several studies for understanding and optimizing underlying NAND flash. In particular, FTL (Flash Translation Layer), a software module, has been utilized to manage NAND flash, and it mainly contains three components: address translator, wear leveling and garbage collection. Thus, we have investigated various FTLs by considering average/worst-case performance, reliability, endurance. The results from these studies have been published in [J3, C2, C4, C6, C7, C8]. (2) We studied how to separate regular data and metadata of a guest file system in a virtual machine image file and how to utilize NVM to optimize I/O performance by storing frequently-updated data in NVM. The proposed scheme is evaluated on a real hardware embedded platform. The experimental results show that the proposed techniques can improve write performance to 45.21% in mobile devices with virtualization. The above results have been published in [J4, C5].

15213814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213814.value: Mobile virtualization, in which multiple virtual machines run on a on a single device, can benefit higher resource utilization, and better security. Though hardware extensions (e.g., the ARM virtualization extension) can significantly improve the performance of mobile virtualization, running multiple VMs at the same time still inevitably requires more resources, especially for memory and storage. New byte-addressable, non-volatile memories such as phase change memory, spintransfer torque RAM (STT-RAM) and memristor, provide opportunities to optimize memory and storage in virtualized mobile systems. In this project, we have proposed several NVM-based optimization techniques that have shown promising results. There are several directions for future work. First, how to employ the proposed schemes with non-volatile processors would be an interesting direction to explore. Second, some other emerging non-volatile memories, such as domain-wall memory, present different features compared with PCM and STT-RAM. How to utilize these new emerging non-volatile memories to optimize the storage performance and the energy consumption would be interesting. Third, it can be a new research direction to optimize memory and storage performances by exploiting the interactions between our client-side mobile virtualization techniques and cloud-side optimization techniques.

15213814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213814.value: By allowing a mobile device to host multiple virtual machines, mobile virtualization can help reduce development cost and shorten the time to market with code reuse, and enhance privacy and security with VM isolation. However, mobile virtualization posts new challenges to the design of the underlying memory and storage systems. In this project, we for the first time propose to use emerging non-volatile memory technology, more specifically, phase change memory, to optimize mobile virtualization design. We have proposed various VM-aware memory techniques to achieve (1) joint time performance and energy optimization that can adapt to various memory demands; (2) VM optimization management techniques that target at optimizing performance-critical VM functions; (3) VM-image storage optimization techniques by separating hot/cold data. The experimental results show that the proposed techniques can significantly improve the system performance compared with state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed research, which synergistically integrates emerging memory techniques with mobile VM execution and management, can open the door for a new class of research in mobile virtualization. It can help enable mobile virtualization systems to leverage emerging device technologies and architecture design and hence benefit numerous real-life mobile applications.

15214014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214014.value: In developed countries, corrosion of metals has been costing about 3% of gross national product every year, much more than the costs arisen from all natural disasters combined. Well-designed experimental tests can evaluate key parameters that affect and control the corrosion process, while theoretical work can improve our understanding of the phenomena, which is important for the development of design tools for corrosion prediction and protection. There are two main areas of theoretical research. Thermodynamics of corrosion answers the question "whether or not a corrosion process is possible", while Kinetics of corrosion answers the question "how fast a corrosion process can proceed under a given environmental condition". The goal of this proposal is to develop a theoretical framework based on phase field method (PFM) for predicting corrosion kinetics, especially for localized corrosion such as pitting, crevice and stress corrosion cracking. There are different levels of theoretical modeling of corrosion kinetics in terms of length scale. Atomistic approaches make it possible to understand corrosion mechanisms at atomic level. However, these methods cannot reach the length and time scales at which corrosion takes place. On the other hand, macroscale approaches at centimeter and meter scales normally provide average behavior of a system, but are difficult to capture key features of localized corrosion at mesoscale – the most important class of corrosion that can result in sudden failure of a structure. PFM is one of the mesoscale methods that experienced fast advances over the last two decades and it has been used to predict microstructure evolution in many material processes. However, due to the complexity, PFM has not yet been applied to corrosion process of any real systems. In fact, to the best knowledge of the authors, there are no mesoscale theories that can predict topological evolution of corrosion interfaces during localized corrosion. This project will aim to develop a theoretical framework using PFM that can predict the corrosion processes occurred at the double layer (nanometer scale) up to micrometers of corrosion films on metal surface and into the metal bulk. This research team has more than 10 years of PFM modeling experience and will join hands with experimentalists in this project. Combining with the modeling methods in macro and atomistic scales, our project will deliver important tools for the development of new corrosion resistant materials as well as for the prediction of life time of materials in corrosive environment.

15214014.label: Realisation of objectives
15214014.value: For the objective #1, A new electrochemical potential was proposed within the phase field framework, in order to solve the diffusion (Cahn-Hilliard) and phase field (Alan-Cahn) equations. The Poisson's relation was used to govern the charge distribution and electrical potential distribution. An electrical double layer across the metal-electrolyte interface was successfully realized in nano-scale. The problem for this early work was that it only dealt with very small (a few nanometers) scale in order to capture the properties of double layer near metal surface. Therefore, the model is not feasible for simulating micro-scale corrosion problems, which happens in micro-meter or even millimeter scales. A micro-to-macroscale quantitative phase-field model was later developed for the investigation of crevice corrosion of iron in salt water. Six types of ionic species and some associated chemical reactions have been considered. In addition to the transient distributions of ion concentrations and electric potential in the electrolyte, some physical and chemical properties related to corrosion, such as overpotential, pH value and corrosion rate, under different metal potentials are studied. Benchmarking of the phase-field model against a sharp interface model is conducted. The corrosion rates predicted by the model are in the same order of magnitudes with experimental results. For the objective #2, We continued to develop more comprehensive models for studying localized corrosion in pure metal and alloys. The types of localized corrosion we studied are (1) pitting corrosion and (2) stress corrosion cracking. For pitting corrosion, we developed a thermodynamically consistent phase field model for the quantitative prediction of the pitting corrosion kinetics in metallic materials. Both the ion transport in the electrolyte and the electrochemical reactions at the electrolyte/metal interface are explicitly taken into consideration. A calibration study is performed to couple the kinetic interface parameter with the corrosion current density to obtain a direct relationship between overpotential and the kinetic interface parameter. The phase field model is validated against the experimental results, and several examples are presented for applications of the phase-field model to understanding the pitting corrosion behavior in stressed material, ceramic particles-reinforced steel, and the effect of crystallographic orientation. For stress corrosion cracking, a phase field (PF) model was proposed to investigate corrosion in a stressed metal. The Allen–Cahn equation, associated with the Nernst–Planck, Poisson’s, and mechanical equilibrium equations, was established to govern phase transformation, ion diffusion, electric potential distribution, and mechanical deformation, respectively. The electrochemical reaction rate was expressed as a function of the electrochemical potentials of reactants and products based on a detailed balance of reactions, which conforms to a generalized Butler–Volmer relationship. The numerical results reveal that the stress concentration at the tip of a corrosion pit promote a higher corrosion rate, which leads to a sharpened tip and the accelerated failure of a metallic structure. To consider a more complicated scenario, a metal matrix composite (MMC) reinforced with inert fibers/particles was investigated. If a fixed displacement boundary condition is applied, the corrosion resistance of the MMC would benefit from the decrease in reinforcement stiffness; whereas when the MMC is under a constant load, a stiffer reinforcement would result in an increase in corrosion resistance. This research project has resulted in 4 journal publications, 4 international conference presentations, and trained one postdoc and one PhD student.

15214014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214014.value: A quantitative phase-field model for corrosion, especially for localized corrosion in the form of crevice corrosion, pitting corrosion and stress corrosion cracking was developed. This model considered ion and electron transports, chemical reactions in anode and cathode, overpotential, pH, mechanical load/stresses, crystalline orientation, grain boundaries, and effect of composites. To the best our knowledge, this model is the most comprehensive model published so far in the literature.

15214014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214014.value: Our model can be extended to study corrosion with passive film formation, porous metal formation during electrochemical dealloying, and anisotropic nano/micro metal oxide structure evolution.

15214414.label: Project Objectives
15214414.value: To develop a coated CNT-graphene hybrid sensor network comprising quasi-dispersed sensing elements, for in-situ acquisition of ultrasonic elastic disturbance (UED); To model and understand nonlinearities of UED incurred by fatigue damage; To establish quantitative correlations between nonlinearities of UED and parameters of fatigue damage, whereby small-scale fatigue damage can be evaluated quantitatively; To develop a probability-based diagnostic imaging algorithm, for presenting monitoring results quantitatively, intuitively, and promptly; and To experimentally validate the proposed sensor network coating concept and fatigue damage characterization methodology.

To model and understand nonlinearities of UED incurred by fatigue damage;

15214414.label: Realisation of objectives
15214414.value: In this project, five objectives have been proposed, and all of them have been fully accomplished by end of this project. This research project was proposed based on the recognition that current structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques are confronted by two inherent bottlenecks: (i) the dilemma in striking a compromise between “sensing cost” and “sensing effectiveness”, because a limited number of distributed sensors acquire information fairly locally, and may fail to delineate the overall structural integrity; and (ii) the inefficiency in detecting fatigue damage, because fatigue damage, usually imperceptibly small, may not produce noticeable changes in global or local measurement. In this GRF project, an in-situ active sensing approach has been developed by exploring the nonlinearity of ultrasonic elastic disturbance (UED), perceived by a novel coated sensor network made of carbon-graphene nanoplatelet hybrids. The innovative sensor network can be sprayed and deposited onto structures for acquisition of nonlinearity of UED. The dynamic particulate motion induced by traversing UED modulates the infrastructure of carbon nanotube (CNT) in the hybrids, and consequently changes the piezoresistivity measured by the coated sensor network. In order to achieve all these objectives, fundamental investigations were first carried out. This included that a sprayable in-situ CNT-based active sensor network coating was developed to provide a novel, quick and convenient means to create a sensor network with quasi-dispersed sensing elements; fatigue-driven nonlinearity in UED was modelled and interpreted; quantitative correlations between UED nonlinearity and fatigue damage parameters were established; and identification results were presented in a quantitative, prompt, and visualized manner, facilitating user-friendly in-situ SHM. All the fundamental studies were well validated experimentally. In conclusion, all the proposed research objectives have been successfully and fully accomplished. The direct outcome of this research is a novel coated sensor network which can be used for cost-effective, quantitative, in-situ SHM.
