15214414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214414.value: Upon completion of this GRF project, a novel coated sensor network which can be used for cost-effective, quantitative, in-situ SHM, has been fully developed. In particular, the proposed approach possesses the capacity of evaluating fatigue damage at a quantitative level (including the co-presence of multiple fatigue cracks, and their individual locations and severity). Benefiting from in-depth fundamental interrogation and intensive experiment, this proposed research has reached some very important conclusions and achieved significant findings and outcomes which can benefit relevant students in future. By reaping the dual merits of carbon nanotube (CNT)-based sensing and nonlinear UED-based damage characterization, this proposed research have contributed the following key innovations: (1) a coated in-situ active sensor network with quasi-dispersed sensing elements for acquisition of UED which can flexibly accommodate various structures: metals or composites, flat or curved; (2) characterization of small-scale fatigue damage, by taking advantage of the high sensitivity of nonlinear properties of UED, via rigorous modeling and in-depth understanding of the nonlinearity of UED incurred by fatigue damage; (3) scrutiny of fatigued zones in a quantitative manner, in contrast to traditional approaches that can detect fatigue damage at a qualitative level (existence only); and (4) visualization of results in intuitive images, to highlight the probability of fatigue damage occurrence and facilitate user-friendly in-situ SHM. Scientific research-wise, new mechanisms have been explored, by which SHM methods can be developed to identify fatigue damage with desired accuracy, sensitivity and cost-effectiveness, outperforming existing techniques; real-world application-wise, innovative sensing methods have been delivered to accommodate demanding requirements from practical deployment of SHM. Not only will the outcomes arising from the project yield in-depth insight into the mechanism of using nonlinear elastic disturbance to characterize small-scale damage, but it will also contribute an innovative SHM solution with in-situ sensing capacity. A number of high level publications have been arising from this research project, including 23 papers in top-tier SCI journals, along with another 13 papers in the international conference proceedings (see Part C). Two US patents, directly related to this RGC-funded project, have been granted (see Part C). Outputs from this project has also been awarded the Gold Medal of the 46th International Exhibition of Inventions of Geneva, 11-15, April, 2018, Geneva, Swiss.

15214414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214414.value: Although all the proposed objectives have been well achieved, the team has also identified some potential directions along which deeper and broader research could be expanded. The recent advances and technological breakthroughs in additive manufacturing have ushered a new avenue to improve the developed sensing network coating approach. In this completed project, spraying-based deposition approach was developed. In future, more advanced additive manufacturing approaches, including inkjet-printing or 3-D printing techniques can also be used. By doing these, some demerits associated with the use of spraying-based deposition can be overcome, such as the difficulty in precisely controlling the thickness of sprayed sensors. On the other hand, the nonlinearity captured extracted from captured AU wave signals was observed extremely weak, and it was prone to measurement noise and uncertainties. This has entailed more effective signal processing methods to efficiently extract desired nonlinearities of AU wave signals. Last but not the least, the developed approach/system has also attracted great interest from industrial partners, including Airbus (Beijing) Research Institute. It is recently that the team demonstrated the developed approach to Airbus, who expressed their great interest in investing this new technique. The team will continue the promotion of the research achievements arising from this GRF project.

15214414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214414.value: Sensing, the infrastructure of any health monitoring technique, plays an essential role in acquiring information, on the basis of which structural integrity can be evaluated. In practice, a limited number of sensors are spatially distributed, forming a sensor network. During the network configuration, a paramount target is to compromise “sensing cost” with “sensing effectiveness” – to acquire the most information with the fewest sensors. However, owing to its distributed nature, a distributed sensor network may “overlook” some information, leading to inaccurate or even erroneous results. This completed GRF project has is dedicated to fundamental research and development of an in-situ sensing approach for characterizing fatigue damage. An innovative active sensor network using carbon-graphene nanoplatelet hybrids has been developed, which can be sprayed and coated onto a structure in the modality of a thin film, to create a coated sensor network comprising quasi-dispersed sensing elements. This coated network can be employed to in-situ perceive nonlinear ultrasonic waves which have proven sensitivity to small damage (e.g., fatigue crack). Not only will the success of the project yield in-depth insight into the mechanism of using nonlinear elastic disturbance to characterize small-scale damage, but it will also contribute an innovative SHM solution with in-situ sensing capacity.

15215214.label: Project Objectives
15215214.value: To conduct theoretical investigation of triboelectrical generation mechanisms in FTENG with respect to interacting surfaces of the fabrics, to numerically analyze the deformation, strain/stress fields then derive the sliding distance and energy overcoming friction, based on the verified model, to study the effects of elastic moduli, cross-sectional shape and size of the fibers and yarns, ends and picks of the fabrics. To study the surface profile, texture and friction, washability and ball-punching behavior of FEC experimentally, together with a theoretical investigation of the FEC by extending Leef' knitted fabric geometrical model and finite element analysis, the interacting surfaces being the FEC and washing machine wall or punching ball. Using the verified model, to study the effects of elastic moduli, cross-sectional shape and size of fibers and yarns, fabric cover factors and overfeed ratio of the non-conductive yarns. To develop a new measurement scheme for fabric surface and friction by combining soft tactile sensor of optical fiber grating/silicone (compression and friction force) and laser triangulation method (surface profile). To compare the measurement results from the newly developed fabric tribological tester and the KESF tester as well as the subjective assessment results, and the effectiveness of the two objective measurement techniques. To design, fabricate and characterize stretchable, deformable and soft tri-axial tactile sensors and arrays for pressure and shear stress mapping on a three-dimensional surface, to carry out experimental investigations on the materials, structural parameters of sensor unit cells, fabrication methods and tools development. To improve the designs of FTENG and FEC according to the verified theoretical analysis in Objective 1 and 2, to fabricate enhanced versions and to achieve a higher energy conversion efficiency and energy density for FTENG, and better washablity and durability in ball-punching tests for FEC.

15215214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215214.value: 与传统的基于硅或者薄膜的电子器件相比，纺织电子器件具有柔软，易弯曲，可拉伸，可在三维方向上变形，体积轻， 耐用等特点。因此，它们可以用于触觉传感衣，健康监测系统和机器人皮肤等产品。摩擦学，一个源于希腊的词汇，是研究滑动面间相互作用的学科。纺织电子器件与周围环境和人体有很多相互接触的表面，同时组成纤维集合体也有很多内表面，这些是决定装置的功能性、耐用性和可靠性的关键。 此研究主要致力于以下方面的科学知识和技术进步创新：首先，研究关于两种所选取织物结构器件的摩擦学响应的新理论模型和数值仿真方法, 有关表面轮廓，拓扑结构，织物不同级别的纹理结构，织物结构器件是纤维和纱线等级的织物摩擦发电机（FTENG）以及织物连接器 (FEC)。这些理论模型将由相应的织物结构的实验来验证。如果验证成功，它们将为可穿戴的智能设备的织物结构选择和设计提供实用的指导。其次, 我们将设计出新型的柔性的、可变形的和高灵敏度的触觉传感器以及基于此的传感器阵列, 可以同时测量三维对象(例如手指, 脚踝, 脖子等)的压力和剪切应力. 这些传感器将会具有与人体皮肤相似的弹性模量。第三， 纺织品摩擦仪将采用光纤光栅/硅胶复合传感技术，以及激光三角测量技术。纺织品摩擦仪将应用不同纺织品表面粗糙度和摩擦力的测量。现有的纺织品表面评价系统（KESF）是用金属探头和织物进行表面接触的。我们仪器将和KESF系统进行比较。如果成功的话，这将是第一个真正模拟人的手指的用于织物触觉评价的测量技术。最后，基于这个项目的理论模型和数值仿真的结果，新型的设定表面摩擦性能的织物将会被设计和制作出来。它们的表面粗糙度和摩擦力将用新研制的摩擦测量仪器来表征。我们将首次给出两种基于织物的电子设备(FTENG 和 FEC)的产生电能与织物摩擦性能之间的关系。

15215214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215214.value: Theoretical investigation has resulted in full understanding of the triboelectrical generation mechanism in contact-mode FTENG with respect to interacting surfaces of the fabrics, to numerically analyze the deformation, strain/stress fields then derive the contact times and energy overcoming friction. (Yang B et al, AEM, 2016) The surface profile, texture and friction, compression of various fabrics made from 21 types of fibers have been studied experimentally, together with the theoretical investigation. The effects have been examined for elastic moduli, cross-sectional shape and size of the fibers and yarns, ends and picks of the fabrics. (Liu RS et al, Nano Energy, 2018, Tao XM, Accounts of Chemical Research, 2019) A new measurement scheme has been successfully set up for fabric surface and friction by combining soft tactile sensor of optical fiber grating/silicone (compression and friction force) and laser triangulation method (surface profile). The measurement results from the newly developed fabric tribological tester are comparable to the KESF tester as well as the subjective assessment results. (Liu RS et al, Nano Energy, 2018) We designed, fabricated and characterized stretchable, deformable and soft tactile sensors and arrays for pressure and shear stress mapping by using triboelectricity principle. The transient behavior of the charge generation did not warant its application as sensors as the measured values as depedent on the measurement history. But they can be good switches. (Yang B et al, Advanced Energy Materials, 2016) The improved designs of FTENG and FEC according to the verified theoretical analysis have yield much enhanced energy conversion efficiency and energy density for FTENG. 15215214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215214.value: This study has contributed significantly to the creation of scientific knowledge and technological advancement in the following aspects: First, new theoretical treatments and numeric simulations have been conducted on tribological responses of fabric devices and verified by corresponding experiments of the selected textile structures. Secondly, novel soft, deformable and highly sensitive tactile sensors and sensing arrays will be designed, fabricated and tested for simultaneous pressure and shear-stress mapping on three-dimensional subjects such as hand fingers, foot, ankle and neck of human body. Thirdly, a fabric tribological meter has been developed by using optical fiber Bragg grating/elastomer composite sensing technique and laser triangulation method. The fabric tribological meter was used to measure the surface roughness and friction of various textile fabrics. Finally, new textile structures with deterministic surfaces have been designed and fabricated and the relationships between functions of the textile-based electronic devices and tribological properties were revealed for the first time.

15215314.label: Realisation of objectives
15215314.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed Objectives 1 and 2. Realization of Objective 1: (1) A series of concentric axial compression tests was completed on DTCCs. An analysis-oriented theoretical model was developed for these DTCCs under axial compression. The predictions of the theoretical model are in close agreement with the test results. A journal publication arose from this work (Teng et al. 2018). (2) A design-oriented stress-strain model was developed for concrete under the combined confinement of transverse steel reinforcement and FRP. This model provides a good basis for developing a design-oriented stress-strain model for the core concrete in DTCCs. A journal paper reporting this work was published (Lin et al. 2016). (3) A novel testing method for determining the hoop elastic modulus of filament-wound FRP tubes was developed. This offers a much simpler method than the existing method to achieve the same objective. (4) A series of cyclic axial compression tests were completed on DTCCs. Different cyclic loading schemes (i.e., full cyclic loading and partial unloading/reloading) were examined. The test results were compared with existing cyclic stress-strain models. (5) Ten DTCC specimens under eccentric compression were tested. The main parameters included the initial load eccentricity and the slenderness ratio. Realization of Objective 2: (1) A three-dimensional FE approach was developed to examine the stress-strain behaviour of confined concrete in DTCCs under concentric axial compression. (2) Based on the experimental results of DTCCs under eccentric compression, an eccentricity-dependent stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in DTCCs was proposed by modifying an existing model. (3) A column analysis model with the incorporation of the developed eccentricity-dependent stress-strain model, together with some reasonable simplifications on the modelling of high-strength steel tube, was used to simulate the test DTCCs under eccentric compression. A joint-supervision Ph.D. graduate, Dr. Z.H. Wang, was trained in this project. She was a PhD student of Zhejiang University and worked at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University from September 2014 to September 2015 and December 2016 to March 2017 under the joint supervision of the PI. She obtained her Ph.D. degree from Zhejiang University in December 2017. The title of her Ph.D. thesis is: Experimental Study and Analytical Modeling of Double-Tube Concrete Column with an FRP External Tube and a High-strength Steel Internal Tube (DTCC). 15215314.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215314.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: Concentric compression tests: (1) The experimental results show that in DTCCs the concrete is well confined by both the FRP tube and the high-strength steel tube, and the buckling of the high-strength steel tube is suppressed so that its high material strength is effectively utilized, leading to excellent column performance. (2) Due to the high yield stress of high-strength steel, the hoop stress developed to confine the core concrete is much higher than can be derived from a normal-strength steel tube, giving the use of high-strength steel in DTCCs an additional advantage. Cyclic compression tests: (3) The test results indicate that DTCCs possess an excellent load-carrying capacity, as well as ductility. The failure of hybrid DTCCs under cyclic compression is characterised by the rupture of the external FRP tube. (4) The cyclic compression tests indicated that the envelope stress-strain curve is very similar to the monotonic stress-strain curve Eccentric compression tests: (5) With the increase of eccentricity and (or) slenderness, the axial load-strain curve of DTCCs exhibits a more distinct strain-softening stage after the peak load. (6) The concrete in a DTCC under eccentric compression is less effectively confined by the FRP tube compared to that under concentric compression. Findings Related to Objective 2: (1) The three-dimensional FE approach can provide close predictions for the test results of DTCCs under concentric axial compression. (2) The ultimate axial strain at the extreme compression fiber of a DTCC under eccentric compression is much larger than the ultimate axial strain of the corresponding DTCC under concentric compression. (3) Jiang and Teng’s (2012) model with the incorporation of the proposed eccentricity-dependent stress-strain model can predict well the load-displacement curves of the test DTCCs under eccentric compression.

15215314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215314.value: Objective 3 in the original application (i.e., to develop a theoretical model for DTCCs subjected to seismic loading) was removed as a result of funding reduction. This objective is of great value and importance and deserves further research.

15215314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215314.value: This project was aimed at understanding and modelling the behaviour of a new form of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP)-concrete-steel hybrid columns proposed by the PI. These columns consist of a concrete-filled FRP tube that is internally reinforced with a high-strength steel tube (referred to as hybrid double-tube concrete columns or DTCCs). The three components in a DTCC (i.e., the external FRP tube, the concrete infill, and the internal high-strength steel tube) are combined in an optimal manner to deliver excellent short- and long-term performance. A systematic experimental study including both axial compression tests and eccentric compression tests as well as advanced theoretical analysis was carried out in this project. The test results confirm that in a DTCC with a high-strength steel tube, the local buckling of the high-strength steel tube is effectively prevented, and the concrete is very well confined, leading to a very ductile column response. DTCCs thus provide an effective column form for the efficient use of high strength steel. The research has also led to the development of an eccentricity-dependent stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in DTCCs which can be used in the design of such columns under static loading.

15216114.label: Project Objectives
15216114.value: While, flow variability and ecology of perennials are somewhat well studied, the ephemeral tributaries and their influence have received less attention, though the total ephemeral length often approaches that of the perennial sections. The goal of this study is to determine the role of stream flow generation in ephemeral streams on regulating water quality and flood safety in the river network.

The goal of this study is to determine the role of stream flow generation in ephemeral streams on regulating water quality and flood safety in the river network.

15216114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216114.value: In Hong Kong, high annual rainfall, contrasting wet and dry seasonal precipitation patterns and hilly geography are the major factors that lead to the formation of ephemeral (non-perennial) streams. They are a unique feature of Hong Kong’s river networks and commonly found in the headwaters. Because ephemeral streams in Hong Kong mostly occur in the origin of a river network, their stream flow generation has a significant influence on the water quality and flood formation in the entire downstream perennial part of the river. However, little research effort has been put on assessing the significance of flow generation in the ephemeral streams. The main objective of this study aims to quantify the past and present nexus of stream flow generation in ephemeral streams and its implication on the water quality and flood risk integrity of Hong Kong’s permanent perennial streams. This work is a continuation of the Principal Investigator’s (PI) effort in characterizing the attributes of streams and rivers to facilitate ecological rehabilitation of the flood control channels in Hong Kong. Three catchments with different levels of urbanisation and stream regulation have been carefully selected for field surveys and data analysis. A fourth catchment with a well grown secondary forest has also been selected to use as a reference. The primary field data observed in two annual cycles will be utilised to assess the present flow conditions in quantity and quality of the ephemeral and perennial streams. Using multivariate analysis, flow data of the ephemeral and perennial streams will be correlated with a number of water quality parameters used as passive tracers that directly trace the contributions of distinct water sources. Twenty-five years of historical data collected by the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department (EPD) from the perennial streams will be used to identify the sources of flow generation based on the passive tracer concentrations. This information will provide vital information of unrecorded historical ephemeral flow patterns. Similar data acquisitions and analyses will be conducted for the water quality parameters such as total nitrogen, total phosphorous and chlorophyll-a. Finally, short term and long term historical patterns of water quality will be analysed to assess the impact of ephemeral flow generation on water quality. The major finding of this study will be useful for decision makers to design a healthy ephemeral stream network that would provide a significant contribution to regulating the downstream water quality and flood risk. 年降雨量高，旱雨季降雨量差異大以及丘陵地形是導致香港季節性河流產生的主要因素。它們是香港河流網的獨特特性，一般存在於河流的源頭。由於季節性河流大多存在於河流的發源處，他們流量的產生對整個下游河流的水質和洪水的形成有著非常重要的影響。然而，對評價季節性河流流量產生重要性的研究工作還很少。本文的主要目的旨在量化季節性河流過去和現在流量產生的關係以及對香港常年河流(永久流)的水質和洪水風險完整性的影響。這項工作延續了首席研究員PI在描述河流屬性以及香港生態恢復防洪通道方面做出的努力。精心挑選了城市化和河道整治水平不同的三個流域進行實地調查和數據分析。第四個流域選在一個生長很好的次生林中，用來作為參考。兩個年度週期收集的主要數據會被用來對當前季節性河流和常年河流進行定性和定量分析。使用多變量分析方法,與季節性河流和常年河流數據有關的一系列水質參數作為被動追踪劑,直接跟踪不同水源的貢獻。由香港環境保護署(環保署)收集25年的常年河流的歷史數據將被用來通過追踪劑的濃度識別流量的來源。此信息將對沒有歷史記錄的季節性河流提供重要信息，將水質參數如總氮、總磷和葉綠素a進行類似的數據收集和分析。最後,通過分析短期和長期的水質模式來評估暫生流生成對水質的影響。本研究的主要發現將有助於決策者設計健康的季節性河流網絡，並對調節下游水質和洪水的風險控製作出重要貢獻。

15216114.label: Realisation of objectives
15216114.value: Field observations, sampling frequency and overview of the status quo of ephemeral streams After several reconnaissance visits covering almost all ephemeral paths in the catchments contributing to Ho Chung river, Tseng Lan Shue stream, Tai Po Kau stream and Yuen Long Nullah, data (e.g. bankfull dimensions) were analyzed to select ephemerals/ephemeral reaches for detailed sampling. In addition to Hong Kong ephemerals as proposed, several ephemeral streams in Sri Lanka were selected for detailed sampling after similar reconnaissance surveys. Reasons to sample Sri Lankan streams were due to their pristine and unregulated nature, as well as the comparable perennials. Some sites needed more than a year or more to be certain whether they were ephemeral streams. Detailed sampling in Hong Kong and Sri Lanka were carried out in 2015 to 2018. A few more sampling sessions were carried out in early 2019 to strengthen/validate certain results. Unlike the Sri Lankan ephemerals, Hong Kong ephemerals did not continuously flow for a week even during the wet season. In the dry season, ephemerals were basically without a continuous surface flow. Therefore, water quality sampling was conducted only in the wet season in Hong Kong. Flood control potential of ephemerals: observation of abstraction losses in perennial and ephemeral streams The bankfull discharges of ephemerals went as high as 18 m3/s (3 m2/s/m per unit width). The discharge per unit width at maximum was two folds in perennial streams, relative to ephemerals. Ephemerals showed 10% increase in bankfull discharge for every 200 m stream length, and it was only about 5% increase for perennials. Considering the fact that all streams were in the same mountainous region and had similar slopes, it was conspicuous that the equal or more prominent role ephemerals play in flood control. Infiltration (one of the main abstraction losses) and channel roughness (a factor that govern the discharge) were studied for two ephemeral flow conditions. They included, ephemerals with a surface flow (wet season) and with disconnected pools (close to completely dry state; dry season). The highest infiltration of all cases was observed at the active channel (stream bed) of ephemerals in the dry season. Negative and positive correlations were observed in flood plain areas of both stream types in the wet season with infiltration for live biomass and organic content of the soil, respectively. In addition for a few cases moisture content showed a positive effect on infiltration. Ephemeral channels in general were two to three times rougher than perennials, and the differences were statistically significant for both seasons. As per correlation analyses it was obvious that the impact of biomass (standing crop and/or litter) and herb diversity on increased and decreased stream roughness, respectively. Impact of vegetation parameters on roughness were more prominent in perennials, whereas mean particle size had an equal strong prominence on increasing friction for both streams (only exception was perennials in the dry season). Impact of ephemeral sediment on water quality Sediments of ephemeral and perennial streams together with their respective waters were placed in mesocosms under laboratory conditions, and water quality observations were taken for a 30 day period at frequent intervals. Mesocosm dedicated to ephemeral streams showed relatively high rates of reduction in nitrate nitrogen, and ammoniacal nitrogen than mesocosm dedicated for perennial streams; however, the differences were not statistically significant (at P<0.05). The soluble reactive phosphorus variations were more or less the same. Therefore, it seemed the denitrification potential of ephemeral streams was relatively high, perhaps elucidating special (different and/or uncommon) microbial communities. Vegetation survey of ephemeral sites and allometric relationships for vegetation age & calculation of bankfull discharges Each year sampling was conducted during a period when ephemeral streams had low surface flows. Sampling was realized contiguously using belt transects. The standing crop biomass (hereafter biomass) of herbaceous vegetation in ephemeral channels were comparatively lower than perennials so does the herb diversity. Herb diversity showed a peak from 1.5 to 4.5 m from the centerline/thalweg of ephemeral and perennial streams. Out of 24 herbs only three were common for both. A peak herb biomass zone was observed in perennials in the same region where diversity peaked. In ephemerals, herb biomass increased laterally up to ~1.5 m, and thereafter it was constant. Seedling experiment results were in line with the diversity observations made in the field for both stream types. This suggested seed dispersion is the main reason for the herb vegetation in both stream types. Diameter at knee (DKH) height was observed and with the aid of growth factors the tree age was determined. The ephemerals had trees with DKH 2 to 25 cm (i.e., age from one year to 30 years), and about 75% of these trees were less than five years old. It should be noted about 90% of the trees with ages less than five years were in fact only about two years old. Beyond the bank full level most of the trees were mature with a few young (ages less than five years) trees. Also, it was evident unlike in Hong Kong sites, that trees corresponding to 10-15 years were exceptional in Sri Lankan ephemeral sites. These were well reflected in the catchment hydrology represented by the maximum annual rainfall against the return period. Here, we have considered the flow generation was proportional to the rainfall of the catchment. This is a valid assumption considering the mountainous nature of the study areas, as the lag time between rainfall and peak discharge is shorter. Sri Lankan ephemerals seemed to receive a rainfall which is about one third of the average total annual rainfall within a single month for every 30 years. Also for every two to five years those were subjected to a monthly rainfall which is about one fifth to one fourth of the total annual rainfall. This meant the magnitude of the seasonal (every year) high flow events and flow events with a five year return period were quite similar. Unlike in Sri Lanka, the increased rainfall to an increased return period was proportionally high and was more uniform (see the rapid increment in Sri Lanka from a return period of seven years to 15 years). Temporal variation of stream flow generation and implications on water quality We have used redundancy analyses (RDA) and Men-Kendall test to understand temporal variation of stream flow generation and water quality for the past 30 year period using the database maintained by the Environmental Protection Department. Modelling of raw data included from upstream and downstream sampling locations. It should be noted that well defined ephemeral streams were only observed in upstream rural areas, forest and/or grassland land use. Ephemeral streams through built urbanized downstream areas were rather unfound, and perhaps had been regulated into concreted storm drains. Firstly, the correlations of different variables made with time were observed separately for season and location (i.e. as upstream and downstream). In this regard for nine rivers RDA plots, and Man-Kendall tests were conducted to workout the correlations. Secondly, strength of correlations were checked against rural upstream stations with <40% of built areas, and downstream stations with >70% of built areas.

15216114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216114.value: # The fact that ephemeral streams are unique not only due to hydrologic permanence, but also because of its herb composition. Only 12% of the herbs were common to both ephemerals and perennials. In the riparian like zone, herb diversity in ephemerals is similar to those of perennials. However, perennials biomass production was significantly higher than the ephemerals. Seedling experiment results were in line with the diversity observations made in the field for both stream types. These prove ephemeral streams have its own ecosystem which are important in biodiversity and ecological conservation programs. # The tree ages of ephemeral streams aided hindcasting of past hydrological events that are representative of stream flow rate. Also, the results showed the role of ephemerals in climate change studies. The oldest trees of ephemerals were found to be about 25-30 years old and matched well with the flow events that had a return period of 30 years. Hong Kong’s catchment hydrology showed at least a few contrasting differences to Sri Lankan study catchment. Once in 30 years a monthly rainfall which is almost half of the total annual rainfall happens in Hong Kong (this is one fifth to one fourth in Sri Lanka). This was why in Hong Kong trees could be found for all age groups (up to 25-30 years) and in Sri Lanka trees around 10 -15 years were rather unfound. # The ephemeral stream’s water has less nutrients than perennials, but without statistical significance. During normal flow condition water quality may be practically good even for potable use. However, prolonged dry seasons (which is attributed to climate change) seem to be problematic as the disconnected pools would produce waters that is very high in nutrient content (nitrogen and carbon), which is similar to domestic wastewaters (such waters are referred as blackwaters). Even though, this scenario was not evident in most of the ephemerals, it was the case in a few. # In Hong Kong catchments with built areas less than 40% (and with several ephemerals) showed an improving trend for many water quality parameters; however, their downstream counterparts with built areas more than 70% (and without ephemeral paths) showed a deterioration of some parameters. This also proves the importance of ephemeral paths on water quality. # Nitrate, phosphate and discharge seemed to be independent to the seasons, but rather related to spatial locations. For many cases discharges at downstream stations increased. Independency from season was more obvious in the downstream monitoring stations. This suggests that the hydrological factors related to stream discharge are affected by the increase of impervious cover as such abstraction losses only play a minor role in governing the discharge. This was not the case in the upstream catchments with high ephemeral density. # The increase in bank-full discharge per unit length was high in ephemerals. This would be vital for flood safety at bank-full or similar extreme flow events. The relatively high flood control potential of ephemeral streams was further validated by high infiltration values in ephemerals beds.

15216114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216114.value: 1. Ephemeral streams and the adjacent trees may capture certain history of the catchment hydrology. In many areas, including Hong Kong ephemeral streams together with perennial streams are simply regulated to collect flood water. This is not a sustainable management of a vital water resource especially in the context of climate change. Ephemeral streams are also known to produce black water flows in recent decades. Such blackwater contained ephemeral streams were rather unheard of a few decades back, and we contribute this to climate variability. It is essential to study the occurrence of blackwater events and their impact on downstream perennial waters/ecosystems. 2. The polarization of rainfall events with climate change has resulted in wet seasons getting wetter while dry seasons being drier, with total annual rainfall remains more or less the same. It is clear that the dry season’s groundwater recharge is low. Increased wet season rainfall does not mean infiltration will increase, as once the soil is saturated and reach steady state, infiltration remains constant. Therefore, the net effect is more rainfall producing more runoff. It is necessary to find our ways to effectively manage ephemeral streams to increase the infiltration (ground water recharge) or to engineer them to make infiltration (i.e. groundwater recharge) similar to values before climate change impacts.

15216114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216114.value: Ephemeral streams (ES) are an obvious stream type in Hong Kong (HK) due to contrasting wet and dry seasons, but have not being subject to detailed scientific investigations. The lack of knowledge in ES results in ES being disappeared or heavily regulated. Currently ES are only abundant in rural upstream catchments. This study observed and validated the eco-hydrologic significance of ES in HK and Sri Lanka. ES have unique herbaceous plant communities proving importance in biodiversity/conservation programs. The tree ages of ES matched well with the catchment hydrology, and matched well with past flow events. The result elucidated the role and potential use of ES in climate change related studies. ES showed proportionately high potential in flood control too. Furthermore, water quality of ES were excellent and at certain cases confirmed potable conditions. However, though not very common, it seemed prolonged dry seasons, probably as a result of climate change is increasing the chances of nutrient rich water build up in ES pools. Those nutrients would be eventually carried to perennial streams causing severe nuisances. Therefore, climate variability, ES and water resources management will be recommended as a potential and important future study topic.

15216314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216314.value: Abstract The current development trend of optical fiber sensor system is large scale and multi-functional which helps improving the system simplicity and efficiency as well as reducing its cost. Hence, a compact and sensitive optical fiber device that is capable of performing multiple sensing functions is critical. In recent years, fiber in-line open air-cavity interferometers fabricated by femtosecond laser appear as compact, versatile and highly sensitive sensor devices with small temperature cross-sensitivity, yet they inherently possess poor robustness. An efficient way to overcome this difficulty is to utilize an inner air-cavity or internal micro-structure which makes the device “open” to the external environment. Recently, we demonstrated a fiber internal mirror structure consisting of a hollow sphere inside the optical fiber, which can respond to the external environment. The main objective of the project is to develop a miniature and robust optical fiber in-line interferometer based on fiber internal mirror fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining and fusion splicing technique. The key issues to be addressed include inscription of micro-structures at the fiber end facet, fusion splicing of the fiber tip with micro-structure together with another cleaved fiber tip to form a hollow sphere acting as fiber internal mirror, construction of a fiber in-line interferometer based on dual fiber internal mirrors, evaluation of the fabricated fiber in-line interferometer based on fiber internal mirror, test of the device response to temperature, strain, bending, external refractive index and high temperature sustainability and comparison of the results obtained with that of other miniature optical fiber sensors, exploitation of the full potential of the device developed. The main outcome of the project would be a new class of fiber in-line interferometer device based on fiber internal mirror, which exhibits ultra compact size, good flexibility, high sensitivity and versatile sensing capability. The project is expected to have impacts on basic fiber element for photonics, which can be used to perform many photonics applications. 當前微型光纖傳感器系統的一個重要發展方向是大規模及多功能，這有助於實現系統的簡單有效及經濟性。本專案就此提出了原創性的方案:將飛秒鐳射微加工、光纖熔接以及熔融拉錐技術相結合，製作出基於內置微腔的光纖內反射鏡以構成單光纖干涉型感測器。當沿光纖纖芯傳輸的光束到達微腔邊緣時被分為兩路，一路仍經由纖芯傳輸，一路則被微腔外壁反射，再經由光纖包層與空氣介面反射，在另一微腔的反射端重新疊加形成單光纖Mach-Zehnder干涉儀。該系統能用來進行應力，溫度，折射率及彎曲測量，具良好的高溫穩定性，並能進行三參數同時測量。 本專案將理論分析確認基於內反射鏡單光纖干涉儀的傳感特徵，設計、製造多功能光纖傳感器，構建簡單高效的光纖傳感系統。專案的開展將有利於推動光纖傳感器件的集成化，有效促進多點,多參數光纖傳感網的發展。

15216414.label: Project Objectives
15216414.value: For Challenge-1, we propose a two-level composition architecture generic/simple enough for a wide range of wireless mission-critical CPSs. CPS physical domain-specific knowledge often allows us to abstract the physical domain states and behaviors into computing domain discrete meta-states and corresponding real-time semantics. Consequently, we can model the composition of CPSs via temporal interaction patterns between discrete meta-states. For Challenge-2, we propose a framework of detailed technologies that exploit cross computing and physical domain features to realize the 2-level composition architecture and support mission-critical dependability. At the upper (interaction) level, paradigm changes necessitate the design of a comprehensive set of temporal interaction patterns based on the notion of leasing [tan13]. At the lower (micro-CPSs, aka uCPSs) level, by exploiting physical domain invariant-set theory and convergence time bound, we propose a scheme to encapsulate physical domain states and behaviors into computing domain meta-states and corresponding real-time semantics. Validation: In order to tangibly validate the effectiveness of our proposed composition framework, we will build a CPS test-bed to demonstrate the proposed concepts and approaches. This test-bed shall also serve the basis for our future CPS research.

15216414.label: Realisation of objectives
15216414.value: For the revised objective 1, we have conducted studies on various wireless mission-critical cyber-physical systems, which include those for quadcopters, fixed-wing airplanes, smart vehicles, submarines, and robots. We find that a two-level composition architecture is generic/simple enough for a wide range of wireless mission-critical CPSs. This architecture (see [TCPS19][Thesis15]) include a physical subsystem, where fine-grain continuous control is carried out to a physical plant, and a cyber subsystem, where coarse grain complex decisions are made to guide the fine grain control of the physical subsystem. The physical subsystem feeds the cyber subsystem with sensory data of the physical plant, together with other possible meta-information. The cyber subsystem feeds the physical subsystem with reference points or reference trajectories, to manoeuvre the fine grain control. In addition, bounding filters at the reference input of the physical subsystem can further constrain the trajectories of the physical plant to a bounded state space, which can be further abstracted as a computing domain discrete state (i.e., a "meta-state"). Also, to connect the physical and cyber subsystems, we need a wireless communication networks layer. For mission critical CPSs, such layer also needs to support real-time (more specifically, soft real-time) quality of service. Such (soft) real-time wireless networks are also called wireless field buses. Besides the many existing wireless field bus proposals, we proposed an inter-cell channel time-slot scheduling scheme for multichannel multi radio cellular field buses [RTSS15]. This scheme can help building future 5G cellular technology based wireless field buses, as 5G features large scale smart antenna arrays capable of multichannel multi radio communications. For the revised objective 2, we have developed various technologies for the above mentioned two level composition architecture. In [TCPS19][Thesis15], a Lyapunov stability theory based bound is found for the trajectories of physical subsystem with linear controllers. Using this bound, we can abstract the continuous behaviours of the physical subsystem plant into discrete meta-states (e.g. "safe", "unsafe"). In [TCAD16][JIRS16], fast converging convoy formation control strategies are proposed for non-holonomic smart vehicles, so that similar meta-state concepts can be enforced via fast convoy formations (with convergence time bounds). Similarly, in [TECS17], fast converging convoy formation control strategies are proposed for non-linear quadcopters tracing air pollutants. With these bounds and strategies to abstract the continuous trajectories of the physical subsystem plants to discrete meta-states (and corresponding convergence time bounds) , we can carry out high level interactions between plants, and use timed automata (or even more general: hybrid automata) to describe such interactions. Furthermore, frequently used interaction patterns can be formalised with timed automata or hybrid automata, to standardise the interactions. In [Thesis15], we proposed a hybrid automata based interaction pattern, which can guarantee certain mutual exclusion safety rules for wireless CPSs. The guarantee works even when the wireless communication links fail arbitrarily. For the revised objective 3, we have developed several CPS test-beds to demonstrate and validate our proposed concepts and approaches. In [MSN15], a quadcopter platform is developed which enforces the two-level control-CPS concepts, where physical quadcopters are implemented. In [JIRS16] and [TCAD16], non-holonomic smart vehicle simulation environments were built. In [TECS17], quadcopter convoy simulation environments were built. In [TCPS19], computer vision aided inverted pendulum emulation test-bed and physical experiment test-bed are both built. In [ICSE19], [Thesis17], and [Thesis18], ArduPilot emulation test-beds, as well as a more sophisticated computer vision aided inverted pendulum emulation test-beds are built/used. As for real-time scheduling aspects, in [TMSCS16], a NAND flash memory storage system test bed is built, to experiment with real-time scheduling theories. 15216414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216414.value: After studying various wireless mission critical cyber physical systems, which include those for quadcopters, fixed-wing airplanes, smart vehicles, submarines, and robots. We find that a two-level composition architecture is generic/simple enough for a wide range of wireless mission-critical CPSs. This architecture is depicted in our works [TCPS19][Thesis15], where the lower level is a physical subsystem that carries out fine-grain continuous control of the physical plant, and the higher level is a cyber subsystem that discretely senses the physical subsystem, makes complex decisions, and sends these decisions as reference commands (in the form of reference points or reference trajectories) to the physical subsystem. The reference commands may be bounded by a filter at the entrance to the physical subsystem to limit the scale of fluctuations. In the physical subsystem, convergence theories and technologies can be exploited to bound the trajectory of the physical plant. Once the physical plant's trajectory enters such bound, we can regard the physical plant enters a virtual discrete state, i.e. the so-called meta-state (such as "safe", "unsafe"). Correspondingly, in the cyber subsystem, we can coordinate several physical plants as if they have discrete meta-states and dwelling durations in these meta-states (e.g. staying in the "safe" meta-state for 10 seconds, staying in the "unsafe" meta-state for 20 seconds). In our works [TCPS19][Thesis15][JIRS16][TCAD16][TECS17], various meta-state forming theories and technologies are proposed for linear control systems, non-holonomic smart vehicles, non-linear control quadcopters etc. In our work [Thesis15], the cyber subsystem meta-state based coordinations are modelled by timed/hybrid automata, and temporal coordination patterns are defined, so that even when wireless communication links fail arbitrarily, certain safety rules are still guaranteed. This project also results in various test beds for our CPS research: including those for quadcopters, fixed-wing airplanes, smart vehicles, submarines, and robots [ICSE19][Thesis18][Thesis17][MSN15], and for real-time scheduling [TMSCS16]. Also, to connect the physical subsystem with the cyber subsystem, (soft) real-time wireless communication networks (e.g. wireless field buses) are studied. In [RTSS15], we propose an inter cell channel time-slot scheduling scheme for multichannel multi radio cellular field buses, which matches the features of future 5G technologies. References: See the "References" list of Part B-5.3, which labels the items in Part C.

15216414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216414.value: During the process of this project, we encounter great demands for testing and debugging cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, how to test and/or debug CPSs with complex cyber subsystems are still open problems. This is mainly because the cyber subsystems for nowadays CPSs are so complex (each can include millions of lines of source code) that traditional formal modelling and analysis methods are no longer feasible. We have to test and/or debug them as black boxes. In [TCPS19], by exploiting Lyapunov stability theories, we made a pilot study on how to reduce the testing effort of control-CPSs. In [ICSE19], by exploiting the autoregressive system identification technologies, we explored the possibility of judging the correctness of a control-CPS's cyber execution by merely looking at its continuous domain trajectory. In [DATE19], we explored the possibility of predicting the correctness of a control-CPS's safety with online testing. References: See the "References" list of Part B-5.3, which labels the items in Part C.

15216414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216414.value: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are the inevitable results of computing infiltrating all kinds of physical world practices. Typical CPSs include robotics, smart vehicles, avionics etc. Many of such CPSs are wireless and mission-critical. In this project, we explore the proper architecture to compose wireless mission-critical CPSs. By studying various wireless mission-critical CPSs, we point out that a two-level architecture consisting of a physical subsystem and a cyber subsystem is a generic and simple enough composition architecture meeting our needs. We propose various technologies to regulate the continuous world behaviours of the physical subsystem, so that these behaviours can be abstracted as high-level discrete states (e.g. "safe", "unsafe") with temporal features (e.g. "staying in 'safe' for at least 10 seconds before switching to 'unsafe'"). With these high-level discrete states and temporal features, we propose design patterns to compose different physical subsystems at the cyber subsystem level, so that certain safety rules are guaranteed even in face of unreliable wireless communication links. The above outcomes of this project can help standardise and simplify the design, implementation, and verifications of composing wireless mission-critical CPSs, significantly reduce their development cost, boost their safety, hence benefit both the industry and the society.

15216814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216814.value: The interest in researches that broaden the roles and capabilities of magnetic fluids has increased rapidly over the last decade in the mechanical and biotechnological engineering communities. This is due to the emerging roles of these functional fluids in mechanical and biomedical applications, such as better thermal management for electronic products due to thermo-magnetic convection, greater reachability of the medication to the target spot with guidance from an external magnetic field…etc. Among all the foreseen technological barriers in the practical biomedical applications, flow instabilities at the interface between the magnetic fluids and the miscible biofluid induced by an external magnetic field are key problems needed to be well understood. The project is a continuation of our earlier pilot study aiming to conduct systematic experimental studies on the labyrinthine instabilities of miscible magnetic fluids in a Hele-Shaw cell (Wen et al., 2007a,b). Remarkable flow visualization of interfacial morphologies shows two distinct features of instabilities: (i) the miscible labyrinthine fingers caused by the magnetic dipolar forces; (ii) the secondary waves dominated by the third-dimensional effects. This interesting secondary wave phenomenon has not been observed in the literature before and the underlying mechanism is partially explained. Therefore, this project addresses two specific objectives—(1) investigate thoroughly the instabilities of the interface between a magnetic droplet and a miscible fluid induced by a perpendicular external magnetic field and (2) to expand our experiments on a stationary Hele-Shaw cell to a rotating one. The roles of viscosity ratio, density ratio, gap width, and the magnetic field strength in the flow instabilities will be clarified; meanwhile, the importance and interconnection of centrifugal force, Coriolis force and magnetic force on the flow instabilities in the rotating Hele-Shaw cell will be explored. A precision control mechanism of the interface divider, a rotating Hele-Shaw cell and a high definition flow imaging system will be built to characterize the flow instabilities at the miscible interface. The visualization data will be analyzed in detail to gain insight into the flow physics and its consequences to the growth rate and the wavelength selection of flow instabilities. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from this project will help to validate the theoretical and simulation results and to develop the biotechnological and biomedical applications of the functional magnetic fluids in Hong Kong. 在過去的十年中，機械和生物工程界積極地發展磁流體的功能及應用。這主要是因為這些功能性流體在機械和生物工程领域中所表现出的顯著作用，例如：熱磁對流對電子產品的熱能管理提升，以及利用外磁場有效引導磁流體藥物到達目標病變器官位置.等等。然而，在實際生物醫學應用時，所有可预見的技術障礙中，外部磁場所誘發的磁流體與可互溶的生物流體接觸面的流體失穩現象，是一決定性關鍵問題。本項目將延續我們先前進行的一系列海倫流動模型中的可互溶磁流體的失穩現象的系统性實驗研究，從先前的研究中所觀察得到的可互溶流體接觸面形態清楚地顯示了兩種失穩因素：(1)磁偶極導致的可互溶迷宮式指狀失穩界面圖形及(2)由第三维效應决定的二次波。這個二次波現象到目前還没有完整的原理解释，也没有在其他文獻中被觀察到過。因此，本項目將致力於兩個明確的目標：(1)詳盡研究由垂直的外部磁場所導致的磁性液滴與可混合流體的接觸面的不穩定性，(2)將我們的實驗從静止的海倫流動模型拓展到可旋轉的模型。與此同時，探索在旋轉的海倫流動模型中，地心引力，科氏力與磁力對於流體不穩定性的重要性和相關性。實驗中將建立精確的接觸面分離控制機構，旋轉的海倫流動模型以及高清晰度的流體成像系统，以用來分析流體混合接觸面的不穩定性。對测量到的可视化數據做分析，進一步加深對流體物理现象以及其對流體不穩定性的成長率和波長選擇的影響的認識。我們期望從本項目中獲得的结論能够有助於驗證理論和模擬的结果，從而開展功能性磁流體在香港的生物技術和生物醫學中的應用。

15216814.label: Realisation of objectives
15216814.value: In this project, flow instabilities of miscible magnetic fluids surrounded by miscible fluids have been throughly studied with extensive experiments. More than 200 experiments were conducted in a stationary Hele-Shaw cell and a rotational Hele-Shaw cell with different magnetic field strengths, gap spans, rotational speeds, and magnetic fluid samples. To achieve all the proposed objectives, the investigation was carried out by four steps: 1. A stationary Hele-Shaw cell experimental setup was developed. Two parallel plates are used for the Hele-Shaw cell configuration with a narrow gap formed by h-mm-thick spacers. The Hele-Shaw cell then confines a magnetic drop with an initial radius in the central region, which is surrounded by a miscible non-magnetic fluid (diesel). A pair of Helmholtz coils is designed to generate a magnetic field stabilised at 27C by immersion in a water box. The morphologic features of the magnetic drop are monitored and captured by a Nikon D7000 camera for fingering instability analysis. 2. The unsteady morphologic evolutions of the magnetic drop were studied under different magnetic fields (by varying the maximum pre-set magnetic field strengths, H, and sweep rates, SR = dHt/dt, where Ht is the instant magnetic field strength), gap spans, h, and magnetic fluid samples. The flow instability mechanism was explored. Two different instability waves were observed. We found that the flow instability can be well evaluated by a modified Péclect number and divided into two different flow regimes, i.e. the Stokes regime and the Hele-Shaw regime. 3. A rotation system was developed and connected to the Hele-Shaw cell by a belt, so that the rotational motion of the Hele-Shaw cell can be accurately controlled by adjusting the voltage of a DC motor. The uniform perpendicular magnetic field strength, H, was again induced by a pair of Helmholtz coils . The coils are immersed in a water box to keep the temperature constant at 27 C and to stabilize the uniformity of the magnetic field. Experiments were conducted with different magnetic field strengths, gap depths, and rotation speeds. Detailed interface morphologic features were analyzed. Two major phases in the growth of instabilities were defined: a magnetization phase and a rotation phase, which are dominated by the magnetic and the rotation effect, respectively. The significance of the rotation effect was confirmed by the linear regression between the rotation growth rate and the rotational Peclect number. 4. The magnetic fluid technology was further tried in the biomedical application. A novel window-MARAS protocol (Magnetic-Assisted Rapid Aptamer Selection) for detecting the target concentration in blind serum samples was developed. The feasibility of the technology was demonstrated. Through this project, a Hele-Shaw experimental system was developed, which can provide both the stationary and the rotational interface evolutions under the magnetic field. The experimental investigation clearly showed the interface instability evolutions of the magnetic drops under the magnetic field and the rotational frame and the consequences to the aerodynamic performance. The underlying mechanism of the flow instability was studied. In summary, all the proposed objectives of this research project have been well achieved.

15216814.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216814.value: 1. A comprehensive experimental study is presented to analyze the instabilities of a magnetic fluid drop surrounded by miscible fluid confined in a Hele-Shaw cell. The experimental conditions include different magnetic fields, gap spans and magnetic fluid samples, and are further coupled into a modified Péclect number Pe' to evaluate the instabilities. Two distinct instabilities are induced by the external magnetic fields with different sweep rates: (i) a labyrinthine fingering instability, where small fingerings emerge around the initial circular interface in the early period, and (ii) secondary waves in the later period. The initial growth rate of the interfacial length of the magnetic drop is found to increase linearly with Pe'. In addition, secondary waves can only be triggered when the three-dimensional magnetic microconvection is strong enough to make Pe' exceed a critical value, i.e. Pe' > 19 000. In this flow regime of high Pe', the length scale of the secondary wave instability is found to be 7 ± 1, corresponding to the Stokes regime; meanwhile, in the flow regime of low Pe', the flow corresponds to the Hele-Shaw regime introduced by Fernandez et al. (2002). 2. The instabilities and growth of magnetic fluids with miscible diesel confined within a rotating Hele-Shaw cell were also experimentally analyzed. Variations in the prominence of labyrinthine instabilities were observed under a range of experimental conditions, with different magnetic field strengths, gap depths, and rotation speeds. These instabilities are characterized by two modified Peclect numbers, namely, Pem (the ratio of the characteristic magnetic advection rate and the diffusion rate) and Pec (the ratio of characteristic rotation advection and the diffusion rate). The magnetic effect is characterized by dipolar repulsion, triggering a distinctive fingering pattern differing from the progressive diffusion pattern that occurs without magnetic fields or rotation. Under the same rotation speed, the magnetoviscous effect will hinder the growth rate of the magnetic drops at the later stage. However, both the rotation effect and the gap depth greatly enhance the growth rate. In contrast, the countering pressure gradient produces an opposite force that constrains the trend toward expansion. Main fingering structures that evolve from the secondary waves are verified as having a wavelength to gap depth h relation of (7 ± 1) h. 3. Four journal papers and one conference presentation were published, referred to this project. A MSc student (later on being the RA) has graduated by the support of this project.

15216814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216814.value: The above major findings are further extended to the potential bio-medical application. Smart aptamers, with a predetermined affinity and capable of specifically binding to C-reactive protein (CRP), have been successfully selected using the window-MARAS protocol (Magnetic-Assisted Rapid Aptamer Selection). The assessment of specificity of aptamers with and without primer in detecting the target concentration in blind serum samples reveals that a multiple negative selection step alone is enough to achieve a satisfactory result. Without going through the primer-free procedure, using libraries with primers can preserve the rapidity and simplicity of MARAS. The result of the aptamer-based ELISA measurement demonstrates that the use of magnetic particles in detection is unnecessary and that the aptamer can be used to replace monoclonal antibody as a detecting probe in immunoassays. Two aptamer-based measurement approaches, including aptamer-based q-PCR and aptamer-based ELISA, have also been developed to unveil the great potential of the aptamer in possible clinical applications. More magnetic fluid applications in the biomedical industry will be explored in the future.

15216814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216814.value: In this project, the instabilities of a magnetic fluid drop surrounded by miscible fluid confined in a Hele-Shaw cell was experimentally investigated and applied to the novel window-MARAS protocol (Magnetic-Assisted Rapid Aptamer Selection) for detecting the target concentration in blind serum samples, which has a great potential of the aptamer in possible clinical applications. Factors such as magnetic field strengths, gap spans, rotational speeds, and magnetic fluid samples were examined to understand their corresponding impacts on the interfacial instability. These factors were further grouped into three dimensionless parameters (modified Péclect numbers) and used to delineate different flow regimes. Through this project, our knowledge of flow physics about the magnetic fluid instability under the magnetic fields of different strengths and rotational speeds was understood. This investigation also made it possible to apply the magnetic fluids in the biomedical engineering.

15217014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217014.value: There are more service firms than manufacturers in the Fortune 500 list of companies and increasing numbers of products today are designed with the inclusion of service components. The service sector plays a predominant role in the economic development of countries. This trend is of particular relevance to Hong Kong as its service sector accounts for more than 90% of GDP and was worth US$46.9 billion in total trade volume in 2012. However, service operations of service sectors ranging from automotive repair to logistics services can be environmentally damaging [1, 2]. Service operations require a wide spectrum of material and resource inputs, while producing pollutants and disposals in the delivery process, posing massive threats and damage to the environment. Under growing public pressure for environmental protection, the service sector is encountering new challenges as well as opportunities to become environmentally sustainable. One viable way for sustainable operations management in the service sector is to adopt green service practices (GSPs), which are defined as pursuing environmentally responsible practices in service provision and delivery. GSPs promote the use of eco-friendly materials, conservation of resources, and resource efficiency in service operations [3]. Yet, the literature and practices on sustainable operations management are confined to treating the environmental damage caused by physical product development and consumption (e.g., product stewardship). Not much is known about the fundamental organizational capacities that are critical to facilitate GSP implementation and development to make both environmental and economic gains, given that service operations are largely characterized by changing market and customer expectations. This study explores the organizational capacity of service operations by examining the organizational dynamic capabilities (ODC) in terms of building, integrating, and re-configuring internal as well as external competence/resources that facilitate GSP implementation. To address this timely research topic, we propose to develop and empirically validate a theoretical model grounded in dynamic capability theory to investigate the ODC that facilitate GSP implementation. Specifically, this research investigates the underlying dimensions of ODC and their interactions, business activities that constitute GSPs, and the environmental and economic performance implications of GSPs. This research will benefit the service industry by providing managerial insights into the organizational capabilities that are conducive to GSP implementation to attain desirable performance outcomes. The findings will also be valuable for policy makers to formulate policies and create incentives to strengthen service companies’ environmental and economic performance while sustaining Hong Kong’s role as a leading service economy. 如今，在世界五百強企業中，服務行業的數量已超過製造業。越來越多的產品在設計中包含了服務概念，也使得服務行業在經濟發展中起到了主導地位。這一趨勢在香港尤為顯著。2012年，香港的服務業交易額已達469億美元，佔據了GDP總額的90%以上。然而，服務行業中的服務操作無論汽車維修或是物流服務都需要大量的材料和資源投入，並同時製造出污染及廢棄物，這將對環境產生惡劣的影響。在公眾日益增強的環保意識與壓力下，綠色服務將為整個行業迎來新的挑戰與機遇。綠色服務實踐（GSPs）是一項能使服務行業執行可持續營運的切實途徑。綠色服務實踐可定義為於服務的供給與傳遞過程中執行環保措施，致力於在服務過程中推動使用環保材料，進行資源節流以及提高資源利用率。然而，現階段關於可持續營運管理的文獻及實踐僅僅局限於將環境的破壞歸結於產品的發展與消耗過程（例如：產品責任）。很少有人將此與基礎組織能力相關聯。實際上，在考慮到服務營運將隨市場與客戶的需求而變化的基礎上，這一能力將推動綠色服務實踐的執行與發展，並在環境與經濟方面得以獲益。本研究通過驗證組織動態能力於構建，整合及重新配置內部與外部資源的基礎上，探索組織服務營運能力作用於綠色服務實踐的推進。為解決這一研究問題，本文提出開發和實證驗證以動態能力理論為基礎的理論模型，用以研究組織動態理論於實施綠色服務實踐的作用。更具體的來說，這一研究探索了組織動態理論潛在的維度和他們的相互作用及商業活動，並用以構成綠色服務實踐及達到其在環保與經濟上的效應。這一研究通過提供對組織能力的管理見解，有助於綠色服務實踐的執行和達到其理想的效果而有益於整個服務行業。研究結果更是有助於政策制定者制定相關政策法規及誘因體制，以提高服務企業的環境和經濟表現，維持香港服務經濟的領先地位。

We found that empirically validated theory-based model manifests in a 7-dimension model of capability, including supplier relationship management process capability, service performance management process capability, information and technology management process capability, order process management process capability, customer relationship management process capability, demand management process capability, and capacity and resource management process capability. 15217214.label: Project Objectives
15217214.value: Different copulas have different probability properties, rendering some copulas more suitable for certain fading scenarios -- depending on whether the different antennas are differently/identically polarized, aligned linearly or span a 2D or 3D grid, are spaced uniformly. This investigation aims to comprehensively investigate many copulas, to thoroughly deduce each copula’s such properties, to determine which copula best fits which fading scenarios. This investigation is to rigorously derive CLOSED-form expressions for various performance metrics, like “outage probability”, the “amount of fade”, etc. for arbitrarily cross-CORRELATED fading across MULTIPLE receive-antennas, even as each antenna’s fading may follow its ARBITRARILY UNIQUE probability distribution. These to-be-derived expressions are to be simple enough to yield intuitive insights on the system performance. The above performance expressions are to be derived for various kinds of combining-reception schemes, possibly including “selection combining” (SC), “generalized selection combining” (GSC), “equal-gain combining” (EGC), and “maximum-ratio combining” (MRC). It would be worthwhile to investigate all these combining schemes, because they each have different advantages / disadvantages, e.g. SC requires the least hardware, EGC is simplest in algorithm, MRC’s output has the optimum SNR.

15217214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217214.value: The ‘survival-Gumbel’ copula model is the "best" copula model for cross-correlated multi-branch fading modeling, leading to the simplest closed-form expressions for an MIMO system's outage probability. This expression is given in the IET journal paper. Other copula models, while mathematically less simple in the expression for outage probability and for other performance metrics, may better fit fading statistics empirically measured, due to these other copulas' greater flexibility in their fading probability density distributions' tail characteristics. Part of this analysis has been covered in the conference paper. Careful mathematical analysis of various aspects of this complicated issue has already been done, but is in the process of being preapred as manuscripts for submission to journals.

15217214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217214.value: For the current 4G wireless communications and its subsequent generations, transceivers deploy multiple antennas. One key question: How is the system performance determined by the fading statistics over the receive-antennas (i.e. branches)? Answers to this question, if qualitatively insightful, can guide the initial stages of system design toward an appropriate architecture. Specifically, how may “diversity reception” schemes (e.g., “selection combining” reception, “maximum-ratio combining” reception) perform (in terms of metrics like “outage probability” (Pout), “amount of fading”, etc.), based on particular channel conditions (e.g., given a certain “amount” of Weibull / Rician / lognormal fading)? The existing literature has answers to these important questions, but in terms of very complicated mathematical expressions, from which intuitive insights are difficult to extract. This research has advanced a mathematical paradigm (until now unrecognized in the wireless fading literature) to formulate the statistics of multi-branch correlated fading, leading towards categorically simpler expressions in closed forms, for various performance metrics of diversity reception. This entirely new approach is based on the probability concept of “copula”, which specifies flexibly the statistical cross-dependence across random scalars (describing the antennas’ fading), to go with any random scalars’ any given marginal univariate distributions.

15218114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218114.value: Today's building automation systems (BASs) provide us with a tremendous amount of real-time building operational data. Buildings are becoming not only energy-intensive, but also information-intensive. The effective utilization of the massive BAS data sets can help to optimize and diagnose the performance of buildings so as to improve their performance. Data mining (DM) is an emerging powerful technology with great potential for discovering knowledge hidden in big sets of data. However, advanced DM techniques are rarely adopted in BASs. One obstacle is that it is extremely challenging for building automation professionals to keep up with the constantly emerging sophisticated DM techniques. A second obstacle is that DM itself cannot tell the value or the significance of the knowledge discovered, and domain knowledge in the building field is therefore still needed to interpret that knowledge. The poor quality of BAS data, which usually contains a substantial number of outliers and missing values, is another big challenge for data analysis. Joint research efforts on building automation and big data analysis are essential for making a breakthrough in the application of advanced DM techniques in BASs. The main goal of this research is to develop a holistic DM-based solution for discovering and applying knowledge hidden in the massive BAS data. The goal is to be achieved by fulfilling the following five tasks. Firstly, the state-of-the-art DM techniques will be explored by conducting case studies on the BAS data of a high-rising building. Secondly, reliable data preparation algorithms will be developed to improve the quality of BAS data and transform them to suitable formats required by the typical DM techniques. Thirdly, novel general domain knowledge representation methods will be developed for translating the knowledge discovered by DM (e.g., correlations, clusters, association rules, patterns decision trees, and models) to meaningful and actionable knowledge (such as daily power consumption and occupancy patterns). Fourthly, novel cross-levels (i.e., the building, system, and component levels) and cross-services (e.g., air conditioning, lighting and lift services) building performance optimization and diagnosis strategies will be developed based on the knowledge obtained and then validated on two buildings. Lastly, application software and generalization procedures will be developed to implement the solution for typical BASs. This interdisciplinary research will bring innovative ideas and enabling technology for the development of more powerful building automation systems. The research outcomes will be also valuable to the development of optimization and diagnosis strategies for improving building operational performance.

15218114.label: Realisation of objectives
15218114.value: All five objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1: To explore the state-of-the-art DM techniques using case studies on the BAS data of a high-rising building. The strengths and restrictions of a variety of DM techniques taking account of the characteristics of BAS data and the building operational needs will be identified Critical and comprehensive exploration of the state-of-the-art data mining (DM) and machine learning (ML) techniques were conducted on the big building operational data retrieved from Building Automation Systems of International Commerce Center (ICC) which is the tallest building in Hong Kong, the CIC Zero Carbon Building (ZCB) and education buildings in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The DM and DL techniques explored include the algorithms for association rule mining (e.g., A-priori, FP-growth, QuantMiner, Probability projection algorithm, motif discovery and TRuleGrowth), clustering analysis (e.g., k-means, PAM, hierarchical clustering, density-based clustering and decision tree), frequent subgraph mining (CloseGraph algorithm) and ML-based predictive modeling (e.g., support vector machine, random forest, multi-layer perceptron, boosting tree, k-nearest Neighbors and deep learning). The typical problems with big BAS data as well as typical data structure were analyzed. The typical problems identified include high dimensionality, multivariate time series, multiple scales, different types (numerical vs. categorical), large volume and poor quality due to sensor faults and unreliable data transmission. DM-based data pre-processing methods aiming at each problems were developed to improve the data quality, reduce dimension, extract main features, transform data format suitable for different DM algorithms. BAS data are usually saved in two-dimensional data table with x-axis representing different variables at the same time instant and y-axis representing samples at different time instants. BAS can be analyzed as cross-sectional data (along x-axis), multivariate time series (along y-axis) and multi-relational data (multiple tables) using different DM techniques. The strengths and restrictions of a variety of advanced DM techniques taking into account of the characteristics of BAS data and the building operations were understood and published in a number of journal papers, which provide valuable experiences and suggestions on selecting suitable DM algorithms for typical tasks in building operation management. Objective 2: To develop reliable algorithms to improve the quality of BAS data and transforming the BAS data to the suitable formats required by typical DM techniques The accuracy and reliability of the data mining results are largely determined by the data quality. The problems with BAS data quality were identified upon achieving Objective 1. Aiming at each problem, a diversity of methods for data cleaning, data transformation and data reduction were developed to improve the data quality and the methods were tested using big real building operational data. Data cleaning handles missing values and removes outliers in big data. Missing values can be filled in using the global constant, moving average, imputation or inference-based models. Outliers can be identified using unsupervised clustering, supervised classification and semi-supervised recognition. Data transformation includes scaling of data sets and transformation of data attribute or type. Commonly used scaling methods include the max–min normalization, Z-score normalization and decimal point normalization. The Symbolic Aggregate approXimate (SAX)-based data transformation method was developed to transform numerical time series into series of symbols, which are the required format of temporal associate mining using motif discovery and TRuleGrowth algorithm. Various advance data mining algorithms were used and tested and recommendation for different tasks and applications are provided in the publications. Objective 3: To develop general domain knowledge representation methods for interpreting the knowledge discovered by mining BAS data sets The data-driven knowledge obtained from data mining and machine learning is valuable supplementary to domain knowledge in developing building operation management strategies. However, it is not easy for building professionals to understand the data-driven knowledge. The data-driven knowledge obtained from analyzing big building operational data using data mining and machine learning includes association rules, clusters, classifications, predictive models and etc. This project addressed this challenges in two ways. Firstly, domain knowledge based post-mining methods was developed for interpreting data-driven knowledge, particularly for association rules, clusters and classifications. Secondly, interpretable machine learning based methods were developed to enhance the interpretability of data-driven knowledge, particularly for various black-box models. The methods were tested using the big building operational data. Objective 4: To develop and validate cross-levels and cross-services building performance optimization and diagnosis strategies based on the knowledge obtained Different from conventional data analysis methods, which focused only on individual services system, such as air conditioning (AC) system, operational data from different services including AC, lighting, and lift and different levels of components, subsystems and systems were analyzed simultaneously and in a purely data-driven approach involving very little physical/domain knowledge. The data-driven knowledge, including association rules, clusters, classifications, predictive models, and etc., were obtained and used for fault detection as well as rule-based and model-based optimization. For example, the association rules between power consumptions of non-essential lighting and chiller plant were obtained and used for anomaly detection. The frequent patterns of power consumption of vertical transportation system (i.e., the lifts), non-essential lighting and chiller plants during the morning start-up period were identified and used for chiller sequence control. Objective 5: To develop, validate and enhance the application software and generalization procedures needed to generalize the application of advanced DM techniques To generalize the applications of advanced DM techniques to typical modern BASs, a generic DM-based framework for knowledge discovery in massive BAS data and applications of the knowledge for building energy management were developed. The framework consists of five phases, i.e., data pre-processing, data partitioning, knowledge discovery, post-mining and applications. The framework and the DM techniques associated with each phases were deliberately designed considering the characteristics of BAS data and the type of knowledge to be discovered. Case studies for demonstrating the implementation the framework in various applications (e.g., predictive modeling, fault diagnosis) in the three buildings were presented in the publications produced from this project. The open-source software R and Python were used in this project.
