15218114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218114.value: The major contributions of this project include the knowledge and experiences gained in analyzing big building operation data as well as the generic DM-based big data analysis framework and associated data analysis methods developed for analyzing big building data. The research outcomes are beneficial to the building industry to improve the building operation performance. The specific research outcomes are briefly summarized below. A preliminary generic framework for knowledge discovery in massive BAS data using DM techniques was developed [Automation in Construction, Vol. 50, 2015]. The framework was further developed and enriched for discovering different type of knowledge and for different applications [Energy and Buildings, Vol. 109, 2015; Building Services Engineering Research and Technology, Vol. 39, 2018; Applied Energy, Vol. 251, 2019] The potential of one of the most promising techniques in advanced data analytics, i.e., deep learning, in predicting 24-h ahead building cooling load profiles was investigated [Applied Energy, Vol. 195, 2017]. The results showed that deep learning can enhance the performance of building cooling load prediction, especially when used in an unsupervised manner for constructing high-level features as model inputs. The findings are enlightening and could bring more flexible and effective solutions for building energy predictions. A critical review on the current utilization of unsupervised data analytics in mining massive building operational data was presented [Energy and Building, Vol. 159, 2018]. The commonly used unsupervised analytics are summarized and compared according to their knowledge representations and applications. The challenges and opportunities are elaborated, which provides valuable guidance to research and applications in the multi-disciplinary field of building automation and data science. To enhance the practical value of advanced machine learning techniques in the building field, a comprehensive methodology to explain and evaluate data-driven building energy performance models was developed based on interpretable machine learning. It is valuable to building professionals in understanding the inference mechanism learnt, e.g., why a certain prediction is made and what are the supporting and conflicting evidences towards the prediction. A novel metric, i.e., trust, is proposed as an alternative approach other than conventional accuracy metrics to evaluate model performance [Applied Energy, Vol. 235; 2019].

15218114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218114.value: This project extensively and systematically investigated advanced data mining and machine learning algorithms for knowledge discovery from big building data. The knowledge and experiences gained in this project are valuable for the development of smart buildings and smart cities in the IoT era when the data related to built environment (including buildings, transportation vehicles, data centers, etc.) dramatically increase. The research on big building data conducted in this project can be further developed in two directions. Firstly, the big data analysis methods and framework developed in this project can be improved in terms of computation efficiency, accuracy, convenience for deployment in clouds and practical applications in building management. The ultimate goal is to develop automated big data analysis and application tools for smart buildings. Secondly, the methods developed in this project can be adopted and further developed for other built environment like transportation vehicles (buses, cold chains and metros) in the context of smart cities to improve energy efficiency and built environment quality. The sources of big data are critically important for big data research applications. The PI plans to closely work with industrial partners like building owners, equipment manufacturers and transportation operators to realize knowledge transfer.

15218114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218114.value: Today's buildings are becoming not only energy-intensive, but also information-intensive. Building automation systems in modern buildings provide us with a huge amount of real-time building operational data. The main goal of this project is to develop a holistic solution for effective utilization of big building data to improve building operation performance. The solution consists of a generic framework of big data analysis procedures and methods based on advanced data mining and machine learning algorithms. Comprehensive case studies on real big building operational data are conducted, which accumulate valuable knowledge and experiences in handling big building data. This project conducts interdisciplinary research of building engineering and big data analytics, which brings innovative ideas and enabling technology for the development of more powerful big data analysis methods and tools for smart buildings. This project also reveals the great potentials of data-driven knowledge and investigates methods to merge data-driven and domain knowledge in building operation management. The research outcomes are beneficial to the building industry in the development of optimization and diagnosis strategies for improving building operational performance.

15218414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218414.value: 近年來世界各地建立了很多結構新穎的大跨度懸索鋼橋。當這些橋梁建在强風地區時，强風會引起它們相當大的振動。大幅度抖振響應的頻繁出現會對鋼構件以及它們的連接件造成疲勞破壞。于此同時,大跨度橋梁還承受汽車和（或）火車荷載，這些動力荷載也會影響橋梁的疲勞壽命。因此,對多種疲勞荷載作用下的橋梁進行疲勞損傷診斷對于橋梁的維護和安全是十分必要的.但是,由于大跨度橋梁結構系統的複雜性，疲勞荷載的隨機性以及疲勞損傷機理的複雜性，這是一個沒有介决的具有挑戰性的課題。 近些年,人們發展了長期健康監測系統,用于測量大跨度橋梁的動力荷載以及結構響應，幷且追踪運行故障的徵兆以及潜在的破壞,同時評估橋梁結構的功能性和安全性。雖然有些領域鼓勵將結構健康監測技術和疲勞損傷診斷兩者結合起來，以便實現可靠、穩定的疲勞損傷診斷結果。然而在土木工程領域裏,結構健康監測和大跨度橋梁的疲勞損傷診斷是分開。 這個研究項目的主要目的是在申請人過去15年工作的基礎上，發展一個針對在交通荷載和風荷載共同作用下的大跨度橋梁的基于健康監測的疲勞損傷診斷方法。 研究項目主要涉及五項工作：（1）將多尺度有限元建模、模型更新方法同應力分析結合起來估計大跨度橋梁在交通和風荷載共同作用下的整體和局部反應；（2）基于健康監測系統連續不斷的實地監測數據分析以前的荷載歷程,發展未來荷載模型和預測未來的荷載；（3）確定多種傳感器的最優布置方案使得橋梁整體和局部反應重構結果達到最優；（4）基于連續損傷力學和監測數據提出一個橋梁的疲勞損傷診斷模型：（5）通過實例驗證提出的基于結構健康監測的疲勞損傷診斷方法的有效性。 預計本項目提出的方法將會是對大跨度橋進行梁疲勞損傷診斷最爲全面、可靠的方法之一。參加本項目的研究人員通過此項目的實踐也將成爲高水平的研究者。

15218414.label: Realisation of objectives
15218414.value: Objective 1: To integrate multi-scale modelling and model updating with stress analysis for predicting both global and local structural responses of a long-span cable-support bridge under vehicle traffic loading. A multi-scale modeling method has been proposed for dynamic stress analysis of long-span cable-supported bridges under vehicle traffic loading by using shell/plate elements to simulate the critical structural components (local models) and using beam/truss elements to simulate the rest part of the bridge (global model). With the appropriate coupling of the global and local models, the multi-scale finite element (FE) model can capture simultaneously not only the global behavior in terms of displacement and acceleration but also the local behavior in terms of stress and strain. A multi-scale FE model has been established for the Stonecutters cable-stayed bridge in Hong Kong. In consideration of uncertainties involved, the multi-scale FE model shall be updated to best represent the real bridge. A novel multi-scale model updating method has been developed. The many-objective optimization problem with four or more conflicting objective functions is first formulated because both global model and local models shall be updated simultaneously. The meta-model-assisted multi-objective optimization evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) is then developed by combination of R2 indicator-based MOEA, Kriging meta-model and evolution control strategy, for the multi-scale model of the bridge is large in size and complex in system. The developed method has been applied to the Stonecutters Bridge. The modal frequencies, displacement and stress influence lines measured by the structural health monitoring (SHM) system installed in the bridge were used to define the multiple objective functions. The updated results showed that the proposed method is feasible and can improve the accuracy of the multi-scale model. For fatigue damage prognosis, it is desirable if the multi-scale fatigue damage phenomenon can be simulated from microscopic short crack nucleation and growth at a material level to macroscopic structural component degradation at an element level. The multi-scale modelling method described above, which includes the mega-scale modelling and the macro-scale modeling, has been extended to include the micro-scale modelling. In the micro-scale modelling, micro-scale elements are used to model material microstructures. Image-based microstructural modelling method is used to generate micro-scale elements. The micro-scale elements are very tiny and cover only a small part of the critical shell element. As a result, a particular meshing scheme is used for generating the transition elements, which are used to connect the micro-scale elements to the macro-scale elements. Objective 2: To develop loading models so that the previous loading histories can be analyzed and the future loading can be forecast. Fatigue damage prognosis of bridges under vehicle loading needs the knowledge on the past and future vehicle loading. In this regard, a novel procedure for simulating vehicle load has been developed based on the data recorded by weigh-in-motion (WIM) system and the agent-based traffic flow microsimulation. The past traffic volume recorded by the WIM system is first used to forecast the future traffic volume in terms of the annual average hourly traffic (AAHT) volume and using the seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) method so that the both seasonality and growth trend effects on fatigue damage accumulation can be considered. The WIM data are then analyzed and used to determine the probability models of major vehicle parameters such as vehicle type, speed, axle weight, and axle spacing. The motions of individual vehicles on the bridge are finally simulated by using the agent-based traffic flow microsimulation, including both free flow and congested flow conditions, considering the drivers’ behavior of vehicle following and lane changing, and employing the Monte Carlo simulation. The Tsing Ma suspension bridge in Hong Kong has been taken as a case study to demonstrate the traffic load simulation. The developed vehicle loading model was also applied to the multi-scale model of the Stonecutters Bridge for dynamic stress analysis. The obtained results showed that the proposed framework is effective and accurate for dynamic stress analysis. Objective 3: To determine the optimal placement of multi-type sensors for the best global and local response reconstruction of the bridge. The need to perform dynamic response reconstruction always arises as the measurement of structural response is often limited to a few locations for a large civil structure. Besides, it is usually very difficult, if not impossible, to measure external excitation under the operation condition of a structure. An algorithm for optimal placement of multi-type sensors, including strain gauges, displacement transducers and accelerometers, has been proposed for the best reconstruction of responses of key structural components and the best estimation of external excitations under the framework of Kalman filter. The structural responses of key locations without sensors can be reconstructed with the estimated generalized state and excitation. The number and spatial location of the multi-type sensors are determined by adding the optimal sensor which gains the maximal reduction of the average estimation error of reconstructed responses to a desired target level. For the given mode number in response reconstruction and the given locations of external excitations, the optimal multi-sensor placement achieved by the proposed method is independent of the form and time history of external excitation. The experimental validation of the multi-type sensor placement and response reconstruction method has also been performed using a test bed for the Tsing Ma suspension bridge. The experimental results showed that the reconstructed responses using the measured responses from the limited multi-type sensors agree well with the actual bridge responses. Objective 4: To propose an FDP model for the bridge in terms of the continuum damage mechanics and measurement data from the SHM system. Two physics-based multi-scale fatigue damage models have been developed to link the continuous fatigue damage evolution in macro-scale to short/long cracks evolution process in micro-scale for both high and low cycle fatigue problem of metallic material. The effectiveness of the developed model has been verified through the comparison of the numerical results with the experimental results. It showed that the model can describe both the continuous average damage evolution for easier engineering application and the internal collective behavior of short/long cracks for better understanding of high and low cycle fatigue failure mechanisms. Auto-adaptive multi-block cycle-jump algorithm has been developed for progressive fatigue damage simulation of long-span bridges. The progressive fatigue damage from local component damage evolution to entire structural failure is simulated with non-standard varying block cycle length which is automatically obtained during computation to speed up fatigue evolution simulation without user intervention. The progressive fatigue damage of the Stonecutters Bridge under cyclic loading has been simulated. The results showed that the algorithm and the multi-scale FE model can improve the computational efficiency of fatigue damage simulation without losing accuracy. The multi-scale fatigue damage prognosis algorithm has been finally developed to predict the trans-scale fatigue damage accumulation of long-span cable-supported bridges under vehicle traffic loading based on the multi-scale FE model, the future vehicle loading on the bridge, the physics-based multi-scale fatigue damage models, and the auto-adaptive multi-block cycle-jump algorithm. The proposed algorithm has been applied to the Stonecutters Bridge for the time period from 2010 to 2020. The results showed that the macro-scale fatigue damage accumulation and micro-scale short crack evolution of the critical components of the bridge can be simultaneously predicted and visualized.

15218414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218414.value: Many long-span cable-supported bridges have been built around the world. Most of these bridges carry immense traffic loadings and suffer from traffic-induced fatigue damage. The fatigue damage prognosis (FDP) of the bridges under vehicle loadings is therefore necessary and imperative for bridge maintenance and safety. This study therefore developed a structural health monitoring (SHM)-based FDP framework with five major tasks: (1) integrate multi-scale finite element modelling and model updating with stress analysis for predicting both the global and local structural responses of long-span bridges under vehicle loadings; (2) develop future vehicle loading models based on incessant field measurement data from the SHM system so that the previous loading histories can be analyzed and future loadings can be forecast; (3) determine the optimal placement of multi-type sensors for the best global and local response reconstruction of the bridge; (4) propose an FDP model for the bridge based on micro and macro fatigue damage models; and (5) examine the feasibility of the proposed SHM-based FDP method through a case study. The project has been successfully completed. The findings and experiences obtained from this study can shed light on the fatigue damage estimation of long-span cable-supported bridges.

15218614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218614.value: In this research, we will study various "min-sum" rectangle packing problems that aim to minimize the total packing cost, where the packing cost of each rectangle depends on its placement position. These problems are different from those classical cases, where the main aim is to optimize min-max objectives, such as minimization of the highest position of the rectangles. Min-sum rectangle packing problems have wide applications in berth allocations at container ports, where, because of today’s intense competition, port operators are struggling to enhance efficiency through better utilization of berthing spaces. Most berth allocation problems can be transformed into min-sum rectangle packing problems, since the berth occupation of each vessel can be represented by a rectangle in a time-space diagram that also incorporates the packing cost for the vessel's stay and handling. Existing studies on such problems are limited. In the rectangle packing literature, no known works study min-sum objectives. In the berth allocation literature, existing algorithms follow restricted approaches, and their performance falls far behind algorithms for rectangle packing problems having min-max objectives. Existing lower bounds on the optimal berth allocation costs can hardly be used for algorithm design and evaluation, due to either having significant deviations from the optimum, or to needing a disproportionate amount of computation time. We therefore plan to study new solution approaches and optimization techniques for min-sum rectangle packing problems with berth allocation applications. In particular, we aim to derive lower bounds that only show small deviations from the optimum and that can be easily computed, and to design exact algorithms that can efficiently generate optimal packings for small and median sized instances, as well as to develop fast heuristics that can produce near-optimal packings for large sized instances. The best algorithms will be translated into a computer tool that will be validated by our industrial partners in Hong Kong port, so as to identify how existing berth allocation practices can be improved on. The outcome of the project is promising, as our new idea has already been proved feasible in a preliminary study, from which much improved lower bounds and algorithms have been obtained for a basic berth allocation problem. The success of the project will significantly enrich the literature on min-sum rectangle packing problems and berth allocation problems. It will also contribute to new optimization methods and techniques, and will open up fresh directions leading to further related interesting topics and useful results. 本項目旨在研究面向船舶泊位分配的各種二維裝箱求和最小化問題。由於競爭日益激烈，提高運營效率成為全球港口管理的重點。船舶的泊位分配是港口運營的一個關鍵環節，對提升港口的整體效益至關重要。泊位分配問題可以轉換成一個二維時空坐標系中的長方形裝箱問題。其中，坐標系的橫軸表示泊位，縱軸表示時間，每一個長方形表示一艘船舶，長方形的長和寬分別對應船舶的長度和其貨物裝卸的時間。我們要決定每一個長方形的坐標，以決定其對應船舶泊位的起始位置和貨物裝卸的起始時間。長方形的裝箱費用由其坐標所決定，通常表示船舶在港口的加權等待時間。我們的目標是最小化長方形裝箱的總費用，也就是最小化船舶總的加權等待時間，以便最大化港口的整體吞吐量。 由此可見，面向泊位分配的二維裝箱問題屬於求和最小化問題。其與經典的二維裝箱問題不同。後者屬於最小最大化問題，通常旨在最小化長方形在坐標系中的最高位置，或是最小化裝下所有長方形所需箱子的最大個數。 二維裝箱求和最小化問題的現有研究十分有限。其中，在裝箱問題的文獻中，我們尚未發現對此類問題的研究。而在泊位分配問題的文獻中，對此類問題的現有求解方法有諸多局限性，其求解效率較經典裝箱的最小最大化問題相差甚遠。此外，現有泊位分配問題最優解的下界，通常需要很長的計算時間或較最優解差距甚大，因此很難在問題求解中有效應用。 在本項目中，我們將研究各種面向泊位分配的二維裝箱求和最小化問題，設計新的求解方法，包括能夠快速計算的有效下界，能夠有效求解中小規模問題的精確解算法，以及能夠有效求解大規模問題的近似算法。我們還計劃將部分研究成果轉化成泊位分配決策系統，供港口決策者使用，以提高包括香港在內的各地港口的運營效率。 通過先期研究，我們已經發現了一些二維裝箱求和最小化問題的重要性質，並運用這些性質設計了幾種新的問題求解方法和最優解下限的計算方法。我們相信本項目的研究成果將推進二維裝箱問題以及船舶泊位分配問題的研究，拓展最優化的理論和技術，並由此開創新的研究課題和研究方向。

15218614.label: Realisation of objectives
15218614.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved, as explained below: 1. In this project, we have studied several variants of the min-sum rectangle packing problems arising from applications in container terminal management, including a continuous berth space allocation and a multi-period yard space allocation problem. (i) For the berth allocation problem with the objective of minimizing the total weighted turnaround time of incoming vessels, we have developed a new lower bound on the optimal objective value. The problem is computationally challenging, as it is known to be strong NP-hard. The development of the new lower bound is achieved by relaxing the problem into a novel optimization model on vectors of functions, which we can efficiently solve by a constructive algorithm in quadratic time, even when the sizes, arrival times, and handling times of the vessels take continuous values. We have proved that the new lower bound can be significantly better than a widely known linear programming relaxation lower bound. It can be used as a good approximation of the optimal solution in the development of solution methods, as well as in the evaluation of solution qualities. (ii) For the multi-period yard space allocation problem with the objective of minimizing the total container movement costs from vessels to the yard, we have developed a sophisticated mixed integer programming model, from which a strong linear programming relaxation can be derived by a set-partition reformulation. It can also be used as a good approximation of the optimal solution for the yard space allocation problem in the development of solution methods, as well as in the evaluation of solution qualities. With these, we have achieved Objective 1. 2. For the min-sum rectangle packing problem formulated for continuous berth allocation, based on the newly derived lower bound, we have developed a new exact algorithm based on the branch-and-bound approach. The algorithm incorporates a new heuristic method of computing an upper bound of the optimal solution, as well as several new dominance rules to reduce search space. Computational results show that the new method outperforms other methods used in the literature, and can solve to optimality all the test data of up to 24 vessels in just one hour. This exact algorithm has also been successfully extended to other variants of the problem, such as the one that takes into account decisions on quay crane assignment. With these, we have achieved Objective 2. 3. For the min-sum rectangle packing problem formulated for continuous berth allocation, the heuristic that we developed adopts a best-fit strategy and follows a one-loop approach, which guarantees optimality for some special cases of the problem. It can produce near-optimal solutions to large instances of the problem with 40 vessels or more in very short running time. For the min-sum rectangle packing problem formulated for the multi-period yard space allocation problem, we have developed several heuristic methods based on a local branching strategy, as well as a particle swarm optimization framework. The proposed heuristic method can produce near optimal solutions for large sized instances of up to 40 vessels and 300 yard sub-blocks. With these, we have achieved Objective 3. 4. For both the min-sum rectangle packing problems for continuous berth allocations and multi-period yard space allocations, we have conducted extensive numerical experiments to evaluate both the quality and performance of our newly proposed lower bounds and solution algorithms. (i) For the continuous berth allocation problem and its variants, we have used more than 300 test instances, including both those available in the literature and those newly generated. The test instances and their computational results have been made available to the research community. Our computational results have shown that, for small test instances with up to 24 vessels, compared to CPLEX our newly proposed algorithm has not only solved more and larger instances, but has often done so in more than 94% less computing time. Moreover, for instances of 40 vessels or more, the best solutions found by the newly proposed algorithm within an hour time limit outperform those produced by other metaheuristic methods from the literature, the improvement being more than 16% on average, as well as achieving a gap of about 10%, on average, from the best-known lower bounds. (ii) For the multi-period yard space allocation problem, we have used and tested our newly proposed algorithms over randomly generated instances with different combinations of vessel numbers and sub-block numbers. The computational results have shown that our newly proposed algorithm can produce near-optimal solutions of no more than 2.3% from the optimal solutions within an acceptable running time. It significantly outperforms commercial optimization solvers, such as CPLEX, as well as other simple heuristic methods. With these, we have achieved Objective 4. 5. In this project, we have implemented a suite of optimization algorithms for min-sum rectangle packing problems, particularly for several variants of continuous berth allocation problems. By incorporating these implementations, we have developed an optimization engine using simple graphic tools that can be used to optimize and analyze berth allocations for supporting decisions of port management. With these, we have achieved Objective 5.

15218614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218614.value: The project has had a fruitful research outcome, including one publication entitled “New Lower Bound and Exact Method for the Continuous Berth Allocation Problem”, published in Operations Research, and one entitled “Multi-Period Yard Template Planning in Container Terminals”, published in Transportation Research Part B (see part C). The major findings from this project are summarized as follows: 1. Many space allocation problems, such as berth allocation problems and yard space allocation problems, can be formulated as a min-sum rectangle packing problem, aiming to minimize the sum of packing costs, such as weighted turnaround costs for vessels in berth allocation, and transportation costs for vessels in yard space allocation. This is unlike the classic rectangle packing problems that often aim to optimize a min-max objective, e.g., to minimize the highest position occupied by given rectangles. Therefore, many solution methods and techniques known to be effective for the classic min-max rectangle packing problems are not applicable or effective when directly applied to min-sum rectangle packing problems. Moreover, very limited studies on modeling and optimization methods for the min-sum rectangle packing problems are available in the literature. Results obtained from this project have filled the gap, and provide a solid base for future studies. 2. The approach proposed in this project, that of developing new lower bounds for the continuous berth allocation problem, is applicable to other rectangle packing problems. The approach starts with a reformulation of the rectangle packing problem, for which a vector of functions is introduced to represent the space allocated. The reformulation is then relaxed by eliminating all the variables and constraints except for the newly introduced functions, and is then strengthened by including valid constraints on the functions. This has opened a new direction for the study on rectangle packing problems and their various applications. 3. From our studies, we have demonstrated an effective approach to tackling difficult space allocation problems, such as berth allocation and yard space allocation. It first formulates the problems into min-max rectangle packing problems, and then utilizes good lower and upper bounds derived for the min-max rectangle packing problems to develop solution algorithms. This can be applied to other more complicated variants of space allocation problems, such as those berth allocation problems with different objectives, side constraints, and input uncertainties.

15218614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218614.value: The project has opened several future research directions: First, there is still room for improvement of the lower bounds derived for the min-max rectangle packing problems of berth allocation and yard space allocation. We will follow this direction in future to strengthen the lower bounds by including more valid constraints into the relaxations. Second, this project mainly focuses on new solution methods for the continuous berth allocation problem and the multi-period yard space allocation problem. The new methods can also be useful in solving some more complicated variants of these problems, such as those integrating the berth allocation and yard space allocation with quay crane assignment. To achieve this, we will need to extend our newly derived lower bounds and solution algorithms. Third, the min-max rectangle packing problems studied in this project are different from the classic rectangle packing problems, which mainly aim to optimize min-max objectives. Therefore, by changing the objective function, the new relaxation models proposed in this project can also be modified to derive new lower bounds for the classic min-sum rectangle packing problems. In the future, we will investigate further how to compute these lower bounds, and how good these lower bounds actually are.

15218614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218614.value: This project studies various “min-sum” rectangle packing problems that aim to minimize the total packing cost, where the packing cost of each rectangle depends on its placement position. These problems are different from the classical cases, which mainly aim to optimize min-max objectives, such as to minimize the highest position of rectangles. Min-sum rectangle packing problems have wide applications for port management. For example, in berth allocation the starting berth location and berthing time of each vessel need to be determined, so as to minimize the total staying cost of all the vessels. It can be transformed into a min-sum rectangle packing problem, where the berth occupation of each vessel is represented by a rectangle in a time-space diagram, with the height, width, and packing cost of the rectangle indicating the vessel’s length, handling time, and staying cost, respectively. In this project, we have developed new solution methods for min-sum rectangle packing problems, including novel reformulations, effective lower bounds, and efficient algorithms. They have significant academic value, for outperforming the best existing methods and opening up promising future research directions. The new solution methods can also be utilized to enhance best practices of berth and yard space allocations at port.

15219014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219014.value: Application of ground-coupled heat pumps (GCHP) is becoming a popular option for governmental and commercial buildings in mainland China due to increasing pressures of air pollution control, carbon emission reduction and energy conservation of buildings from the central and municipal governments in recent years. More and more large-scale GCHP systems have been completed. Currently vertical borehole ground heat exchangers (GHEs) are mainly used to discharge heat to ground and extract heat from ground, respectively, in summer and winter for GCHP systems, but the high initial cost and substantial land areas are needed to drill and distribute boreholes around buildings. In order to save cost and reduce land area usage, the pile foundation of buildings has been used to act as GHEs recently. U-tubes or spiral tubes can be installed into building foundation piles to form pile foundation GHEs so that the cost and land area for developing traditional boreholes can be significantly saved. Due to existence of groundwater surrounding the pile foundation GHEs, the heat and moisture transfer around the pile GHEs can be greatly enhanced. This project is to investigate the impact of groundwater advection in different soils including saturated and unsaturated moisture porous soils on the heat and mass transfer of the pile foundation GHEs so that a detailed validated simulation model can be developed. A three-dimensional heat and moisture transfer model of pile foundation GHEs surrounded with groundwater advection will be developed in this project. The heat and mass transfer model will be established on the basis of the theory in porous media and the theory of soil water dynamics. The simulation model will be validated by experiments indetails. An on-site experiment will be carried out on an existing pile foundation GCHP system to validate the analytical and numerical simulation results of the model, and to obtain practical engineering experience. A lab test rig will also be established so that the groundwater advection effects can be investigated and the simulation can be validated in details. An engineering design guideline and software package of the novel system will then be developed. This project has great significance in terms of improving the performance of pile foundation GHEs and promoting further development of the GCHP applications for energy saving and CO2 emission reduction. It can also benefit potential GCHP users in the Pearl River Delta region for hybrid hot water production and space cooling in buildings. 由於降低碳排放、减少霧霾以及節能壓力的增加，地源熱泵系統越來越受到重視。傳統的U型管地源熱泵系統初投資大，土地使用面積大。近年來采用的將螺旋管裝入樁基的地源熱泵系統，相比較傳統的幷行U型管換熱系統，具有單管換熱面積大，換熱效率高；螺旋管內流體流型優，不會産生流體堵塞現象，幷且能避免供水管和回水管之間的熱短路效應等優點，是高效的土壤源熱泵換熱系統，能顯著降低熱泵系統的初投資和土地使用面積。本項目將研究在地下水滲流和非滲流條件下，樁基螺旋管熱泵系統的傳熱傳質性能幷采用現場實測進行驗證。 項目首先建立土壤介質內樁基螺旋管地源熱泵系統的傳熱傳濕模型，並充分考慮地下水平流效應對傳熱傳質的影響。基於簡化多孔介質模型和土壤-水耦合動力理論建立土壤內傳熱傳質模型，求解控制方程獲得理論解和數值解。然後，採用現場實測對獲得的數值解進行驗證。最後，根據上述理論分析、數值求解和實驗驗證結果，發展建立適用於中國大陸和香港地區的樁基地埋管土壤源熱泵系統的工程設計指導。

15219014.label: Realisation of objectives
15219014.value: The objectives can be divided into two parts: firstly, the model development and validation, which includes the first, second and third objectives; secondly, the model application and heat transfer analysis, which includes the fourth and fifth objectives. As described in objectives 1 to 3, the three-dimensional heat and moisture transfer model of energy piles with spiral coils surrounded by underground medium with groundwater advection is developed and the model is validated by the sandbox experiment. The initial cost of the whole ground source heat pump system (GSHP) can be avoided if the energy piles are employed because the length of boreholes can be reduced, therefore the expense on drilling boreholes is decreased. The simulations based on the theoretical models show that groundwater seepage has a significant effect on the heat transfer effectiveness of the energy piles, which demonstrates that the greater the transfusion the more effective the heat transfer, thereby more heat load can be charged with the energy piles and the initial investment can be further reduced. The exploration on spiral models with groundwater transfusion can provide sufficient theoretical evidence for corresponding engineering projects, which can boost the continuous development of the GSHP technology and sublime the significance of pile foundation energy piles in terms of not only academic research but also engineering field. Groundwater seepage exists commonly surrounding energy piles in many projects, especially in coastal area or those with rich groundwater source. The underground is seemed as a homogeneous porous medium, in which its heat transfer process consists of conduction by solid matrix and liquid in its pores and convection of the moving groundwater. It is assumed that the velocity of groundwater transfusion is uniform in the whole domain. The advection problems of groundwater can be transferred to the moving source problem, which can be solved by the Green function theory. The Green function can describe the temperature response of an arbitrary point in an infinite homogeneous medium to an instantaneous point heat source with unit heat intensity. The temperature fluctuation caused by a heat source with complex shape can be regarded as the superposition of the thermal responses which a number of instantaneous point heat sources caused, and superposition is the integral from the perspective of mathematics. For the energy piles, the buried spiral tubes are simplified as a series of continuous coils, and the dimension of tubes can be neglected with a little loss of accuracy for facilitating the research. During the derivation of analytical model, firstly, the spiral coil is seemed to be infinite and the temperature response is deduced by Green’s function; after that, the finite spiral coil can be calculated by considering the ground surface as the symmetry plane. It considers the complex geometry of spiral coil and can overcome the shortcomings of existing models such as cylindrical models and ring-coil models. The heat exchange group model is validated by the sandbox experiment. The experiment rig is composed of a sandbox, five heat exchangers, a water bath providing constant temperatures, thermocouples, a glass rotameter, and a data logger. The sandbox is sized 1 m × 1 m × 1 m, with the heat exchangers buried inside. The total flow rate is measured by a glass rotameter with a testing uncertainty of ± 0.1 LPM. Four T-type thermocouples are placed next to the central pipe at the middle depth to test the sand temperature variations. The testing range of the thermocouples is −10 to 40 °C and the testing uncertainty is ± 0.5 °C. The sand thermophysical properties are tested by the cutting-ring method, drying method, and the transient hot-wire method. For a certain soil point, the temperature variations obtained by analytical method and experiment have the same trend and the absolute errors are less than 0.25 °C. Consequently, the analytical model for the GHX group is well validated by the experiment. As described in the Objectives 4 to 5, different configurations of energy piles for finding the optimum GSHP A/C design parameters are analyzed and a software package is developed to produce an engineering design guideline for the industry. The GSHP system model is established and a typical residential building is taken as an example. The building has 21 floors, with an area of 295 m2 on each floor. There are no inner zones in the building, and the heating load is dominant. A group of 25 spiral-coil energy piles is designed according to the pre-simulation. When the pile layout is arranged from a matrix shape to a stripe shape or line shape, the outlet fluid temperature decreases by from 11.8°C to 10.5 °C or 9.0 °C in 10 years. The slim layout (a stripe shape or line shape) can alleviate the cold accumulation in soil. This is because the piles in a slim layout have larger boundary areas per soil volume, which strengthens the heat exchange with the soil outside the energy pile group. When the pile layout is arranged from a matrix shape to the stripe shape and line shape, 1) the average heating COP is enhanced from 2.59 to 2.82 and 3.07 in the 10th year, 2) the annual heating deficiency is reduced from 83.7MWh to 56.1 MWh and 29.7 MWh in the 10th year while the total accumulated value are respectively 515.7MWh, 283.8 MWh and 132.1 MWh in the ten-year period, and 3) the accumulated power consumption for heating decreases from 1312.4MWh to 1297.9 MWh and 1272.0 MWh, respectively. Therefore, a slim pile layout can exchange more heat with soil, enhance the heating capacity and lower the power consumption. If the building foundation and land occupation are available, the slim layout is optimum layout design. A software package of the ground source heat pump system using spiral coil energy piles with seepage for performance simulation named Energy pile-Star is developed. In terms of the software, the whole GSHP system model is established, which is composed of the proposed spiral coil energy pile part, building load part, water pump part and heat pump part. The heat pump model should be fitted from the sample catalog of manufacturer. The water pump model adopts a commonly used method with a typical pump efficiency. First, the heating and cooling load of the building should be input in the software. Then, the parameters of the heat pump, water pumps, and energy piles are iteratively calculated to help the system efficiency and economy to satisfy the design demand. After that, the soil temperatures distribution, the outlet ﬂuid temperature, the heating COP of heat pump, the system COP and heating deficiency can be obtained and analyzed. It can be used for the performance prediction during system operation and the parameters optimization during design process. The easy operation method and accurate operation results enable this software widely applied in the industry. In addition, several journal and conference papers were published during the research and cited many times by the peer researchers. All the objectives were completed very well. This project effectively will help promote accurate engineering design and effective application of the ground source heat pump technology using spiral coil energy piles with groundwater flow.

15219014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219014.value: The new three-dimensional heat transfer model of spiral coil pile foundation ground heat exchangers (GHEs) with seepage has been developed. This analytical model takes the practical geometry of spiral coil and the groundwater flow into account and the accuracy is improved compared to the previous analytical models such as the solid cylindrical heat source model and the ring heat source model. This proposed three-dimensional spiral coil energy pile model can fast calculate the temperature at any point in the soil around the pile foundation GHEs. This model has been cited many times and evaluated highly by other researchers. Using this model, the influential factors during engineering design of geothermal heat exchangers can be analyzed. These important parameters consist of the centre to centre distance of the U-tube, thermal conductivity of the backfill material, distance of adjacent boreholes, types of circulating liquid or underground medium, arrangement of boreholes and the minimum temperature of the circulating liquid which enters the heat pump. This research helps to reduce the initial cost and improve the economic performance of the system. Based on the single energy pile model, the pile group model considering the thermal interaction among different piles has also been developed. The sandbox experiment in the lab is established to validate the model. The result simulated by the model is validated well against the experiment. Then the soil heat transfer and the system performance under different configurations of pile groups is analyzed to guide the design of practical projects. Results show that a slim pile group layout is eﬀective to keep high system efficiency, contributing to higher heating or cooling capacities and lower energy consumptions. The software of ground source heat pump system using spiral coil energy piles with seepage for performance simulation named as Energy Pile-Star has been developed as well. It is used for the performance prediction during system operation and the parameters optimization during design process. The easy operation method and accurate operation results will help researchers and engineers design the systems. Now, this software package is under the process of registration for a legal copyright. In addition, several SCI papers were published during the research. This project effectively promotes the reasonable design and application of ground source heat pump using spiral coil energy piles under the condition with groundwater flow.

15219014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219014.value: Since pile foundation GHEs can save the drilling cost and has a larger heat transfer rate compared to borehole GHEs, the ground source heat pump using spiral coil energy pile has a potential engineering application in the future. The proposed heat transfer model of pile foundation GHEs provides a theoretical basis for future research on the GHE design and system performance simulation. Based on that, the developed software package effectively improves the design accuracy of pile foundation GHE which makes the ground source heat pump projects economical and efficient. This is the first software package on the spiral coil energy pile GHEs with seepage which makes the future design process simpler and more accurate than before. In addition, future research on the system performance can be investigated, such as the applicability of the system in different kinds of buildings under different climate zones, the optimization of system operation strategy, and the influence of different factors on the system performance. This research project makes a key primary contribution to the development of ground source heat pump with spiral coil energy piles and provides possibility for future research on the system improvement.

15219014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219014.value: China is experiencing a rapid urbanization and the building energy accounts for more than 30% of the total energy consumption in the whole country. To reduce the energy consumption, the ground source heat pump (GSHP) as an efficient air conditioning system has a potential increase in application. Building pile foundations as the ground heat exchangers of GSHP can save land occupation and initial cost in the high dense city. This research proposed an accurate heat transfer model of spiral coil energy pile by considering the practical geometry of spiral coil and the groundwater flow. It can calculate the three-dimensional temperature distribution around the pile foundation GHEs. The sandbox experiment in the lab was established to validate the model. Based on this, the software named Energy Pile-Star was developed to effectively improve the design accuracy of pile foundation GHE which makes the ground source heat pump projects economic and efficient. Furthermore, the system performance under different configurations of pile groups was analyzed to guide the design of practical projects. This research provides a theoretical basis for the GHE design and GSHP system performance simulation.

15219314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219314.value: Adhesion, a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature, plays an essential role in many biological processes whose consequences could be either beneficial or unfavorable. Among various adhesion-mediated processes, biofouling, which is defined as the unfavorable attachment and accumulation of marine sessile organisms (e.g., barnacles, mussels, and tubeworms) on engineering materials, stands out for the heavy economic loss it caused. Current strategies for combating biofouling are mainly based on the applications of chemicals which tend to have lasting and disastrous impact on the ecological environment. Developing green strategies for biofouling control is in urgent demand and necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the physical and mechanical factors that determine the adhesion behavior between fouling organisms and substrata. On the other hand, from a biomimetic point of view, the robust adhesion achieved by fouling organisms also implies ingenious strategies for strong adhesion underwater, which would be of great value to the design of waterproof cement. In this project, we propose a comprehensive study on the mechanics of adhesion between tubeworm Hydroides elegans, a typical fouling organism, and solid substrata. The emphasis of our study will be placed on the mechanical factors that determine the adhesion strength of tubeworm on substrata, including the mechanical properties of tubeworm cement and substrata, the multiscale surface topography, surface crystallographic orientation and grain boundary density of substrata. The purpose of this study is to identify factors governing the adhesion between tubeworm and substrata, and subsequently come up with theories to quantify their corresponding effects. The established theoretical models would allow us to tailor the adhesion strength by substratum optimization. The prospective results of this project would not only make possible the advent of new green antifouling materials but also provide guideline to the design of biomimetic waterproof cement. 粘附是一種自然界中司空見慣的現象，但它在許多生物過程中起著至關重要的作用。從人類的角度來講，由粘附導致的生物過程有些是有利的，有些則是有害的。其中“生物淤積”是一種典型的有害現象。它主要是由於海洋生物（如：藤壺，貽貝，管形蟲等）不斷地附著在工程材料（如：船體，管道）表面而引起。給工程界帶來了巨大的經濟損失。目前去除生物淤積的方法主要是利用化學藥劑，這會給海洋環境帶來長時間的影響。開發環保的抗生物淤積的方法，需要我們對粘附生物的粘附機理，特別是那些決定粘附強度的物理和力學的因素有足夠深入的了解。另一方面，從仿生材料的角度來講，這些海洋生物所展現的在水環境中優異的附著能力，也給防水粘結劑的開發帶來了啓發。在本項目中，我們計劃對管形蟲的粘附從力學的角度進行綜合的研究。我們研究的重點將放在影響其粘附強度的物理和力學因素，包括管形蟲粘結劑和固體基底的力學性能、基底的表面形貌和晶體取向、晶界密度等等。本研究的目的是尋找出起決定性作用的因素并通過調控這些因素來控制管形蟲和基底之間的粘附強度。本項目的結果不僅有助於開發新的抗生物淤積材料，而且還對仿生防水粘結劑的研製提供方向性指導。

15219314.label: Realisation of objectives
15219314.value: Objectives 1: To theoretically model the adhesion behavior between tubeworm and diverse solid substrata. The attachment of tubeworm Hydroides elegans onto the submerged solid surfaces begins with the engagement of larvae on the substrata, followed by a metamorphic biomineralization process after settlement. Only after tubeworm larvae settle down on a substrata can metamorphosis happen. In this project, we assumed that the success rate of settlement of a larva on a substrata is intimately dependent on the adhesion force between it and the substrata. In order to depict the adhesion between a tubeworm larva and a solid substratum, a contact mechanics-based model was established, by which the dependence of adhesion force on the mechanical properties and the surface morphology of the substrata is studied. For tubeworm larvae, we assume that the success rate of attachment on substrata depends on the pull-off force between them. As the tubeworm larvae resemble cylinders in shape, an adhesive contact problem between a 2D (plane-strain) cylinder and a flat or wavy substratum was studied with attention focused on the dependence of the pull-off force, which refers to the force required to separate them, on the characteristic size of tubeworm and substratum. Even though fouling attachment involves complex chemical and biological processes, this simplified mechanics model allows us to capture the mechanical essences in fouling attachment. It was found that the pull-off force between the tubeworm larva and a flat substratum is related to the elastic moduli of the substratum, the size of the tubeworm larva, and the adhesion energy in between. Soft substrata and small adhesion energy are found favorable for lower pull-off force. On the other hand, for a substrata with wavy surface profile simplified as a trigonometric function with two characteristic length scales (wavelength and amplitude), three stable attachment configurations may occur, depending on the relative sizes between the tubeworm larvae and the wavy profile. Our analysis showed that the minimum pull-off force or best antifouling performance can be achieved by controlling the wavelength and the amplitude of the wavy morphology. Upon the completion of the above work, Objective 1 of this project is achieved by 100%. Objectives 2: To gain a fundamental understanding of the effects of substratum feature (e.g. elasticity, surface topography and texture) on the adhesion with tubeworm. The theoretical model indicates that low stiffness of the substrata and optimized surface morphology are crucial for antifouling performance. To investigate the effect of substrata elastic moduli on antifouling performance, flat PDMS specimen with various elastic moduli were prepared for antifouling performance test against the tubeworm larvae. By comparing the numbers of settled tubeworms on these specimens after 24 h and 48 h immersion, we found that the number of settled tubeworms increased with the increase of the elastic moduli of the specimens. It’s consistent with the theoretical prediction. As natural antifouling surfaces, the leaves of mangrove tree Sonneratia apetala attracted our attention. Possible mechanisms for its excellent antifouling competence such as low surface wettability, antifoulant of oleanolic acid and post-settlement detachment have been excluded in literature. So the ridge-like microscopic surface morphology of the leaves was proposed as the dominant mechanism. To verify this hypothesis, PDMS replicas of S. apetala leaves were prepared by mould casting methods. Settlement test with tubeworm larvae on these polymeric replicas confirms that the ridge-like surface topography can effectively prevent biofouling. It was concluded that the settlement of tubeworms on a textured surface is sensitive to the characteristic length scale of the texture. For S. apetala leaves and their PDMS replicas, the inter-ridge spacing is around 5 μm which is around 10% of the radius of a tubeworm larva (~50 μm). In the light of the theoretical results obtained, such optimized surface morphology should give rise to a lower adhesion force and therefore better antifouling performance. To further verify the finding obtained from the theoretical model, a synthetic surface with ridge-like topography was prepared by water bath method with graphite paper in an aqueous solution containing Nickel and Cobalt nitrates. The characteristic length scales of the morphology are in the optimal range, which implies great antifouling potential according to the theoretical model. Settlement test with tubeworm larvae was also carried out for these synthetic ridge-like surfaces. The numbers of the settled tubeworms after 24 h and 48 h immersion were comparable to those of the PDMS replica of the S. apetala leaves, confirming the feasibility of the optimized ridge-like surface topography in controlling biofouling. Upon the completion of the above work, Objective 2 of this project is achieved 100%.

15219314.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219314.value: The effect of substrata on biofouling has long been recognized and studied. However, a lot of studies based on empirical descriptions of the attachment of biofouling organisms on substrata lacks a physical basis, much less the quantitative estimation and prediction competence. To shed light on the elastic moduli and size dependence of the antifouling performance of the substrata, a quantitative model with a physical basis, rigorous formulation and prediction competence was established in our study. Based on contact mechanics, a theoretical model was built to quantify the dependence of tubeworm settlement on substrata. In this model, the success rate of attachment on substrata is assumed dependent on the maximum adhesion force that can be achieved between them. Considering the cylindrical shape of tubeworm larvae, an adhesive contact problem between a 2D (plane-strain) cylinder and a substrate was studied in the theoretical framework of contact mechanics. It was found that soft substrata and surface with appropriate morphology can be adopted to reduce the adhesion force and therefore prevent biofouling. To validate the theoretical findings, settlement tests of tubeworms were carried out on flat PDMS specimens with different levels of stiffnesses. The results confirmed the feasibility of using soft substrata to control biofouling. To further validate the theoretical finding regarding the effects of surface topography on adhesion, polymeric replicas of mangrove leaves and the synthetic surfaces with ridge-like topography were prepared and applied for settlement test. It was confirm that the ridge-like surface morphology with appropriate characteristic length scales can effectively prevent biofouling. These results not only explained why mangrove leaves possess superb antifouling competence but also provided guideline for the design of structure surfaces as an environmentally friendly approach for tackling biofouling.

15219314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219314.value: Based on the results of this project, further development of the research can be made in the following three aspects: 1. Our present study mainly focused on the effects of surface topography and mechanical properties on the attachment of tubeworms. For a given substratum, the settlement of the fouling organisms also depends on the other factors such as the chemical composition of the substratum and flow rate. The quantitative effects of these factors on the antifouling performance are still unclear and deserve in-depth investigation. 2. In our current study, tubeworms H. elegans larvae were adopted to characterize the antifouling performance of materials with optimized surface morphology. The applicability of the optimal surface morphology to the other fouling species such as barnacles and mollusks remains unclear and deserves further study. 3. Our work provided a strategy for prohibiting the attachment of the typical fouler, tubeworm. This strategy was mainly inspired by the ridge-like surface morphology of mangrove leaves. Different surface morphologies with comparable antifouling capacity may also exist in the other flora and fauna and deserve further investigations.

15219314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219314.value: To explore environmentally friendly approaches for tackling biofouling problem in marine industry, in this project we investigated the adhesion behavior between tubeworms and solid substrata. A contact mechanics-based theoretical model was established to study the adhesion force between a tubeworm and a substratum, which was found dependent on the stiffness and surface morphology of the substratum. For a substratum with ridge-like wavy morphology, parametric study was carried out and found the optimal design with minimal adhesion force. Therefore, substrata with lower stiffness and optimized surface morphology would result in lower adhesion force and therefore yield less probability of being adhered by the tubeworm larvae. According to this theoretical finding, biomimetic substrata with ridge-like topography were fabricated by moulding methods. The follow-up attachment tests confirmed the feasibility of using structured surface topography to control biofouling. These results also accounted for the superior antifouling property owned by the mangrove leaves in nature. In summary, this project not only shed light on the effect of substrata on the adhesion with tubeworms but also provided guidance for the design of engineering materials and structures with enhanced antifouling performance.

15220014.value: Prof Nordholm, Sven Prof Ye, Yinyu

15220014.label: Project Objectives
15220014.value: Study the source localization problem and the optimization of the microphone array structure. By exploring the convex relaxation techniques (SDP and SOCP), characterization of the optimality conditions when microphone locations are unknowns will be developed. Also, we will derive the geometry for the exact localizable regions for general configurations and comparing different convex relaxations. Furthermore, we will explore the sizes of localizable regions and to investigate the maximization of these regions for different optimization formulations by changing the configurations. Study the speech enhancement problem and investigate various beamforming performance indicators. Based on different indicators, design problems with array configurations and microphone locations being unknown variables will be formulated. To avoid the effect of filter length, the optimal frequency response function itself will be sought directly instead, which act as the performance limit for the design problem. By exploiting those performance indicators with analytic expression for the optimal response function, the characterization of the optimality conditions for the location variables will be developed and studied. The sensitivity of the performance with respect to various design conditions can also be investigated. Develop novel and efficient algorithms for the microphone location design problem. Because of the nonconvexity, an inner-outer loop structure can be employed. We will make use of hybrid algorithms to avoid local minima and to minimize the complexity of the inner subproblems. The conditioning of the subproblems will be enhanced by regularization in order to improve convergence and accuracy. Finally, based on the results developed in 1 and 2, we extend the study to reveberant environments. Using the image-source method (ISM), the impulse response function can be extracted and similar design problems are formulated. By using more general transfer functions, we will explore the simultaneous updates for the filter coefficients and the microphone locations. This could speed up the convergence of the algorithms significantly.

15220014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220014.value: In this project, we consider the design of acoustic beamforming systems for both localization of speaker sources and enhancement of speech quality. There are many applications with such systems, such as speech communication, sound source localization, noise detection, and voice control devices deployed in intelligent home or for factory automation. Microphone array is now a standard feature in many products like notebook computers. Indeed, speech is the most natural mean of communication to provide a natural mean of controlling devices, which has the potential to change our living lifestyle. For the beamforming system to work satisfactorily, the localization accuracy of speaker must be acceptable and robust. Moreover, noise should be suppressed as much as possible so that the enhanced speech should have little distortion. There is a pressing need to conduct research in this area to ensure localization accuracy and sound quality. For both localization and speech enhancement problem, apart from beamforming filter coefficients, the microphone locations also play a very important role in the design. This problem has often been ignored, partly due to the ease of implementing regular microphone arrays such as linear, circular or rectangular. With the help of wireless communication devices, it is possible to scatter the array around and create many different irregular array configurations for transmission of acoustic signals. Furthermore, the speech quality and the localization accuracy can be improved significantly if microphone locations are also optimized. In view of this, we propose to study the optimization of microphone locations together with the filter coefficients using performance indicators including the localization accuracy and the speech quality. We will develop novel beamforming methods and hence beamformer designs, which can perform better comparing with the state-of-art methods and designs. In addition, for localization problems, we will carry out theoretical analysis on the localizable regions for different configurations and derive the geometries of such regions using semi-definite programming. In speech enhancement, we will study the optimality conditions for the optimization of the location variables and hope to shed insights into the overall design problem. We believe this research will benefit academia as well as practitioners. 在這個計劃中，我們考慮聲波束形成系統的設計和增強的語音品質。現在有很多此類系統的應用，包括語音通信、 聲源定位、 雜訊檢測和語音控制設備部署在智慧家居或工廠自動化等。麥克風陣列現在是在很多產品，如筆記本電腦的標準功能。事實上，語音是溝通的最自然，提供自然意思是溝通的說的控制設備，這有可能會改變我們生活的生活方式。波束形成系統令人滿意地工作，為講者定位的精度必須是可接受和魯棒性。此外，應將抑制雜訊盡可能多地這樣增強的語音應該有失真度小。那裡是迫切需要在這一領域，確保定位精度和聲音品質進行研究。 用於定位和語音增強問題，除了波束形成的濾波器係數，麥克風位置也在設計中發揮非常重要的作用。這個問題經常被忽視，部分原因是輕鬆的實現定期麥克風陣列如直線、 圓或矩形。無線通訊設備的説明，它是可能分散各地的陣列和很多不同的不規則陣列為創建配置的聲信號的傳輸。此外，語音品質和定位精度可顯著提高如果麥克風的位置也進行了優化。為此，我們建議對麥克風位置與使用性能指標包括的定位精度和語音品質的濾波器係數優化進行研究。我們將開發新型波束形成方法，它可以執行更好地比較先進的方法和設計。此外，對於聲源定位的問題，我們將會進行理論分析和使用半定規劃。在語音增強中我們將研究的位置變數優化的最優性條件，希望對整體設計問題能有新的見解。我們相信這項研究將有利於學術界以及從業人員。

15220014.label: Realisation of objectives
15220014.value: In this project, our main objectives are to investigate different beamforming signal enhancement algorithms and the influence of the array configurations on the performance of the beamformers. We also want to study more advanced optimization techniques for solving the design problems with different performance indicators, and study the performance of beamformers in reverberant environments. Following the objectives of the proposal, we have published 15 journal papers and 9 conference presentations to achieve all the objectives. To summarize, the research team has investigated and proposed several novel optimization algorithms for beamforming signal enhancement and speaker localization. Influence and optimization of array configurations have been explored. In the design process, one way is to formulate the problem as an optimization problem to approach a given target response function. In the formulation, a signal propagation model can be used so that the beamformer response can be calculated. Under this framework, we have studied various approaches in formulating the beamformer design problem with configuration as design variables and solved via nonlinear optimization techniques. In particular, we have studied the linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamformer. Different from the literature, we have formulated the design problem in reverberant environments, in which reflections of sound waves by walls, ceiling and floor are accounted by simulating the acoustic field via a fast image source method (ISM), which provides a tool to synthesize room impulse responses (RIRs) in an efficient manner, and the resulting impulse responses can be used to describe the acoustic environment. In solving the beamformer filters, the frequency response function is optimized directly, which represents the performance limit when the filter length is infinite. Using the performance limit, the effect of filter length is lifted so that we can further optimize on the array configuration by considering the microphone locations as design variables. In solving this nonlinear optimization problem, we propose a hybrid descent method to combine the genetic algorithm with a local search technique. We found that when the reverberation time T60 increases, the array span increases significantly and microphones move close to the wall. Another method is to explore the placement of microphones on a grid and solved via the Taguchi method to determine microphone configuration. The Taguchi method is a robust and systematic optimization approach for designing reliable and high-quality models. The method conducts systematic trials based on an orthogonal array which represents a subset of representative configurations. Numerical results demonstrate that the method is capable to develop better microphone configurations. In addition to the array structure, another important aspect is the size of the array. We find the number of microphone sensors can often be reduced to obtain a prescribed performance. This motivates the development of sparse optimization on the configuration with the number of sensors being a design variable. Sparse designs have been achieved in both filter lengths and the size of the configuration. In the iterative process, we have also developed an algorithm to design the filter coefficients and the configuration simultaneously to achieve faster convergence. For certain applications restricted to linear arrays, it is possible to reduce the configuration design by varying the aperture only. We have developed a robust design to achieve noise reduction and dereverberation in the target speech. In optimizing the performance of beamformers, the formulated problem becomes a semi-infinite optimization problem. An efficient algorithm is the exchange algorithm for which the iterative matrix is restricted to be the set of active points. When L1 norm is employed, the objective function becomes semi-convex. It is advantageous to have a strictly convex function for fast convergence of the algorithm. In view of this, we have proposed a perturbed exchange algorithm and applied to design beamformers. We have shown that the solution can be obtained in a finite of iterations, giving an approximate solution to the original problem. We have proven that the approximate solution of the perturbed problem converges to the true solution as the perturbation diminishes. In addition to the complexity of the algorithm, it is advantageous to have filters with many zeroes. When the Lasso penalty is deployed, an iterative method based on generalized gradient descents for non-smooth optimization problem is developed. Moreover, we have investigated the use of the penalty decomposition method, in which the L0 norm is imposed as a constraint in the design process. 15220014.value: In the formulation of optimization problem for beamformers, we have studied various approaches in formulating the beamformer design problem with configuration as design variables to approach the target response function via nonlinear optimization techniques [9.1,9.4,8.6]. We have formulated the design problem in reverberant environments and propose a hybrid descent method to combine the genetic algorithm with a local search technique to obtain better designs. We have also studied the Taguchi method to determine microphone configuration [8.3] in a discrete and systematic manner based on an orthogonal array. In the size of configuration, we have studied sparse designs in both filter lengths and the size of the configuration [9.7, 8.8]. We find the number of microphone sensors can often be reduced in order to obtain a prescribed performance requirement. In the iterative process, we have also developed an algorithm to design the filter coefficients and the configuration simultaneously [9.9, 8.15] in order to achieve faster convergence. For linear array, we have developed a robust design to optimize on the aperture and to achieve noise reduction and dereverberation. In developing novel optimization algorithms, we have proposed a perturbed exchange algorithm and applied to design beamformers [9.5, 8.4]. To achieve sparseness in the filters, we apply the Lasso penalty and an iterative method based on generalized gradient descents for non-smooth optimization problem is developed in [8.11, 8.12]. 15220014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220014.value: In this project, we consider the design of acoustic beamforming systems for both localization of speaker sources and enhancement of speech quality. There are many applications with such systems, such as speech communication, sound source localization, noise detection, and voice control devices deployed in intelligent home or for factory automation. Microphone array is now a standard feature in many products like notebook computers. Indeed, speech is the most natural mean of communication to provide a natural mean of controlling devices, which has the potential to change our living lifestyle. For the beamforming system to work satisfactorily, the localization accuracy of speaker must be acceptable and robust. Moreover, noise should be suppressed as much as possible so that the enhanced speech should have little distortion. Here, we study the optimization of microphone locations together with the filter coefficients using performance indicators including the localization accuracy and the speech quality. We develop novel beamforming methods and hence beamformer designs. In addition, for localization problems, we carry out theoretical analysis on the localizable regions for different configurations and derive the geometries of such regions using semi-definite programming.

15220114.value: 大量高維數據的高效檢索技術

15220114.label: Project Objectives
15220114.value: Effective partitioning techniques for high-dimensional data and indexes. In a distributed architecture, a similarity query may invoke accesses to the data and indexes stored on multiple machines. In order to maximize the query throughput, a desirable partitioning method should satisfy two requirements: (i) minimize the network I/O cost for processing a query, and (ii) balance the load among machines. We will exploit the characteristics and distribution of high-dimensional data points to design effective partitioning techniques for these two requirements. Efficient caching techniques for high-dimensional data and indexes. Caching techniques are essential in reducing expensive disk accesses at machines. Existing caching techniques for web search engines have not considered the characteristics of high-dimensional data and their indexes. To utilize the cache space, we will investigate compact memory representations for high-dimensional data and indexes. Also, we will develop efficient cache replacement policies for high-dimensional data and indexes. Finally, we will study how to allocate RAM among different types of caches in order to reduce the total query processing time. Disk access time reduction techniques for high-dimensional data. We will investigate techniques for reducing the total disk I/O time of queries, in order to improve the query throughput of the system. We will carefully exploit fast sequential disk page accesses to schedule the accesses to high-dimensional data on disks. Also, we will study shared query processing techniques to further reduce disk I/O time.

15220114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220114.value: Similarity search has a broad range of applications such as near-duplicate detection systems (TinEye), public video surveillance systems, photo sharing sites (Flickr), and sensor data analysis. In these applications, data objects are represented as high-dimensional points, and users wish to find data objects similar to a specified query object. These applications are facing two key challenges nowadays: (i) managing a massive amount of data objects, and (ii) processing queries at a rapid rate. The massive data amount is due to widespread usage of devices (e.g., cameras, sensors), whereas the rapid query rate is caused by the vast number of users or monitoring targets. These challenges hinder the above applications from reporting accurate query results to a large number of users in reasonable response time. Although there has been extensive academic research on efficient similarity search, existing methods fail to tackle the challenges (i) and (ii). These methods assume that a single machine can accommodate all data and indexes, which no longer hold for the above applications. A promising approach is to adopt a distributed architecture with multiple commodity machines for storing data, indexes, and processing queries. This approach scales well with the data size and the query throughput, by deploying more machines. In this project, we study how to improve the query throughput of this system from the data engineering perspective, at a fixed number of machines. This project aims at developing techniques to optimize the query throughput of similarity search on massive high-dimensional data in a distributed architecture. Our track records in multi-dimensional data processing and distributed databases are essential to the success of this project. The performance bottlenecks are caused by the network transfer cost and the disk access cost. To achieve high query throughput, we will investigate three fundamental directions towards alleviating the above bottlenecks: (i) partitioning, (ii) caching, and (iii) reducing disk access time for high-dimensional data. We will carefully exploit the characteristics and distribution of high-dimensional data in designing optimization techniques. Also, we will build (iv) a prototype similarity search system for massive high-dimensional data with our proposed techniques, and release it as open-source software. We envision that this project will advance the query processing techniques for massive high-dimensional data, and improve the query throughput significantly for a broad range of applications, e.g., near-duplicate detection systems, public video surveillance systems, photo sharing sites, and sensor data analysis. 相似性搜索具有廣泛應用範圍，例如接近重複檢測系統，公共視頻監控系統，照片分享網站，和傳感器數據分析。在這些應用中，並且用戶希望找到相似於查詢對象的數據對象，而數據對象表示為高維的點。這些應用面臨兩個主要挑戰：（一）大量的數據對象，及（二）查詢到達速率非常快。這些挑戰阻礙處理大量用戶的查詢，不能為他們迅速報告準確的查詢結果。 雖然現有相似性搜索的學術研究，它們只用一台機器，不再適用於大數據。一個更具擴展性的方法是採用分佈式結構，使用多個機器存儲數據，索引和處理查詢。在這項目中，我們從數據工程角度研究如何提高相似性搜索的查詢吞吐量。 本項目旨在開發技術以增強相似性搜索的查詢吞吐量。我們在多維數據處理和分佈式數據庫的研究往績有利於本項目的成功。分佈式系統的性能瓶頸是由網絡傳輸和磁盤訪問造成。為了增強查詢吞吐量，我們將研究三個根本方向以減輕上述瓶頸：（一）分割數據，（二）緩存數據，及（三）減少訪問磁盤。我們將利用高維數據的分佈和特點以設計優化技術。我們預想，這項目將推動大規模高維數據的查詢處理技術，以及在以上應用中顯著提高查詢的吞吐量。

15220114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220114.value: Various applications (e.g., near-duplicate detection systems, public video surveillance systems, photo sharing sites, and sensor data analysis) require the similarity search functionality. For example, photographers use a near-duplicate detection system to detect photo piracy on websites, police search for suspects from public surveillance videos, and data analysts search for similar patterns from historical sensor data. In these applications, users need to obtain accurate results in reasonable response time (e.g., within seconds). The outcome of this research project will advance the techniques for boosting the query throughput for similarity search on massive high-dimensional data. Also, our techniques will benefit the providers of similarity search applications, e.g., near-duplicate detection systems (TinEye), public video surveillance systems, photo sharing sites (Flickr), and sensor data analysis. By using our techniques, the providers of these applications may deploy fewer machines and reduce their operational cost. In addition, we will release our prototype similarity search system to the public, as an open-source alternative to commercial/proprietary searching technologies (e.g., Google Images).
