15220214.label: Realisation of objectives
15220214.value: The principal investigator has been working closely with the Co-PIs and their students on the related research topics as specified in the research proposal since the commencement of the project in January, 2015. Based on the valuable comments and advice provided by the reviewers in the assessment reports, the project objectives were revised with the focus on the following two major tasks which were approved by the panel for further investigation and development: • Develop a flexible data management scheme by a unique personal medical record e-book structure to handle high-dimension medical data for analysis; • Propose a general mechanism for robust medical evaluation with quantitative measurement by hierarchical vessel analysis and abnormalities grading through dynamic feature selection, fusion, classification and ensemble learning, which is guided by the data in the personal medical record e-book. Previously we have conducted substantial work on computer-aided diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy and mobile cloud computing framework with demonstrated research outputs, which laid the basis for further development of this new project in a new but different context on the aspects of scope, methodology, implementation and deliveries. To tackle the challenging issues concerned in this project, we adopted a hybrid approach by proposing a new data structure of personal medical record e-book and developing robust algorithms in a hierarchical manner to bridge the gap between data management, medical applications and cloud computing. More specifically, we have studied the above issues with the demonstrated outputs as follows: 1) Development of A Personal Medical Record e-Book We introduce a personal medical record e-book structure to integrate multiple medical features and family/social historic medical background information for medical monitoring. Unlike the conventional database systems for medical records, our new data structure offers a general framework to facilitate the management of large collections of high-dimensional medical records with in a unified structure for feature extraction, representation, indexing and classification. The description of an individual's entire medical history is represented in an e-book structure where each page of the e-book provides the details of the medical state on a particular medical encounter and a collection of the record pages shows the detailed information about an individual’s medical records over the entire time period. More specifically, different medical features together with some historic and family background information are represented in column-wise of each book page and the specific data at different scale levels are represented in row-wise of each page. Multiple medical features constitute different dimension data and grouped in different summarized tables at different levels. Under the proposed medical record e-book structure, a series of combinatory database views is created in order to allow user access tools to treat the fact table partitions as a single, large table for fast information retrieval. In addition, key reference data is structured into a set of sub-tables. The proposed new framework for the integration of multiple medical features for medical analysis resulted in the research output [2] while the new methods for medical image enhancement and feature extraction is further evidenced by outputs [1], [3] and [5]. The feasibility of the proposed general framework for multiple medical feature extraction and representation is also demonstrated by the award wining prototype of smart retinal imaging. For more details of research outputs, please refer to Part C of the report. 2) Development of A Hierarchical Approach to Robust and Quantitative Medical Assessment We propose a general mechanism for robust medical evaluation with quantitative measurement in a hierarchical manner which includes a series of tasks such as robust feature clustering and dynamic feature selection, fusion, classification and ensemble learning. More specifically, we have the following research outputs to demonstrate our accomplishment of the specified tasks of this project: • Robust feature clustering for dynamic feature selection The selection of the most representative features subset from the original features set with a relatively high dimension is another important issue in computer-aided detection. The traditional feature selection schemes such as principal components analysis, independent components analysis, singular value decomposition requires a sufficient number of samples per subject to select the salient feature sequence. However, it is not practical to accumulate a large number of samples in medical applications. Feature clustering is crucial for the success of classification. We developed a new robust feature clustering approach to facilitate dynamic feature selection, which resulted in the research output [7]. The novelty of our solution of robust dual clustering with adaptive manifold regularization is characterized as follows:  We propose a novel multiple features learning method by integrating the merits of both feature selection and feature extraction, which could discern the importance of original feature set and alleviate the drawback of feature extraction that the transformed result is difficult to interpret.  The advantage of manifold learning is incorporated into our framework to capture the relation among multiple features. Co-local geometric preserving is proposed to preserve the geometric properties of multiples features. Meanwhile, a co-graph regularization is proposed to exploit both the consistent information of different features and the complementary information among multiple features.  To avoid the problem of simultaneously optimize the selection matrix and transformation matrix, the l2,1-norm is exerted to co-regularize the different projection matrices to obtain row sparse. By projecting the spectral-spatial feature into a common feature space, the redundant features and noises have been discarded, and only the significant original features have been transformed. • Design of effective algorithms for classification via ensemble learning Traditional approaches often adopt single classifier to lesion detection. Single classifier is more sensitive to the values of parameters and the change of training data, which leads to single classifier less stable and robust. In order to solve these limitations, we propose a new ensemble learning framework to identify medical images which belong to different types of lesion. Our proposed algorithms include “Incremental semi-supervised clustering ensemble for high dimensional data clustering”(research output [3]), “Correlated logistic model with elastic net regularization for multi-label image classification” (research output [4]) and ``Adaptive ensembling of semi-supervised clustering solutions” (research output [5]). A comparison study of different classifiers is further reported in research output [6]. We also developed a prototype system to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed algorithms with extensive functionality testing and performance evaluation. The demo illustrates new algorithms and functions for diabetic retinopathy detection by multi-feature retinal analysis. The prototype system won the First runner-up for Innovation Award of Excellence (Hong Kong) on the 2nd Hong Kong Innovation Day competition (25 November, 2015). This award winning prototype was also selected to represent Hong Kong for the Global Healthcare Innovation Competition which was held in Calgary, Canada during 25-26 August, 2016, Please refer to the project website http://smart-healthcare.comp.polyu.edu.hk/Eye.html

The award winning demo illustrates new algorithms and functions for diabetic retinopathy detection by multi-feature retinal analysis.

15220214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220214.value: One of the direction of future work is to design multi-objective optimization evolutionary algorithm for classifier optimization. Since the accuracy and diversity of multiple classifiers are very important metrics for the performance of the ensemble learning approach, we need to identify an optimal set of classifiers from a given large population of candidate classifiers based on these metrics. To meet the requirements, we propose to adopt Multi-objective Optimization Evolutionary Algorithm (MOEA) to search for the optimal set of classifiers. Specifically, we search for a small set of classifiers in a population based on a multi-objective cost function F(x), with the accuracy and diversity of the multiple classifiers as sub-objectives, instead of a single objective function. One important issue in multi-objective optimization is how to identify the optimal solutions, and an effective approach is based on the Pareto optimality concept. The set of Pareto optimal solutions are those with the property that each of these solutions cannot improve any of the objective functions without the worsening of some other objective functions. Our main objective is to search for a set of Pareto-optimal solutions, which characterize those classifier ensembles which are equally effective with respect to both the accuracy and diversity measures.

15220214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220214.value: Computer-aided personalized medical monitoring is in high demand by different group of users ranging from medical service providers to doctors and patients. Such an intelligent system is regarded as powerful and effective because it adopts AI technologies to handle large and diverse collection of medical data for healthcare related applications. However, it remains a challenging task to develop a smart system which can meet various requirements from different user groups by offering customized medical services without the limitation of time, location, environment, and cost. This project aims to develop solutions by leveraging mobile cloud computing paradigm to support computer-aided personalized medical monitoring. Unlike the conventional approaches, we propose the concept of personal medical record e-book and develop the relevant mechanisms and algorithms to bridge the gap between data management, medical applications and cloud based mobile computing. The feasibility of our approach is further demonstrated by developing a prototype system for diabetic care on our mobile cloud computing platform. The findings will not only enhance the health service to the public and improve the quality of life and life expectancy, but also make substantial contributions to multidisciplinary research in multimedia, pattern recognition, cloud computing with excellent potentials for economic growth.

15220514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220514.value: Women are constantly frustrated in finding bras that fit correctly and shape comfortably. As breasts are viscoelastic in nature, how they respond to the strain caused by wearing a bra is considered unpredictable. A revolutionary method to measure the biomechanical interactions between the body and a bra would bring substantial benefits to academia, industry and the general public. Finite Element Modelling (FEM) is widely used in the engineering disciplines, but its application to garment design is still in its infancy because the contact mechanics between a bra and breast soft tissues are highly nonlinear and the 3D force transmission is very complex. This project proposes to develop a scientific algorithm to simulate these 3D forces and the resulting deformation of the breasts with the aim of designing a bra that will give the optimum support and desired shaping for a given subject. 48 subjects representing the 16 most prevalent size groups in China, will participate in the bra fit and body scanning experiments. Meshes of FE body sub-models (including bone, muscle, breast, nipple, and skin) will be constructed, based on a combination of a digital anatomically-correct Chinese female model and individual subject’s high-resolution 3D body scan image. The material coefficients will be initially assigned based on in vivo measurements (breast damping ratio, skin thickness and stiffness). They will then be validated by comparing the predicted values with the experimental data. The mechanical properties (tensile, bending, shear, compression, friction) of the bra components (cup, wire, gore, band and strap) will be tested and inputted into the FE bra sub-model. To simulate the realistic bra wearing conditions, different types of elastic contacts between different elements will be innovatively applied. Algorithms will be combined to simulate the results of the 3D deformation, stresses and strains. This research addresses women’s fundamental needs for a comfortable daily-wear wired bra. Through the validated FE model, the bra shaping effects and stress values can be predicted. This new method will not only facilitate future bra design optimization, but also lead to further research into 3D Computer-Aided-Design of other soft goods. The scientific understanding of the biomechanical body-garment interaction will enable the future design of all kinds of wearable products. This will ensure the sustainable growth of the Hong Kong Design industry. Non-RGC funding will also be sought to develop a Graphical User Interface for the FE models to enable the design of functional garments and other products. 婦女在尋找適合舒適正確的胸罩和形狀不斷受挫。由於乳房粘彈性質，他們如何造成的穿著胸罩的應變是被認為不可預測的。一種革命性的方法來測量身體與胸罩之間的力學相互作用，會為學術界、工業界和廣大公眾帶來極大的好處。有限元建模FEM已經廣泛在工程領域使用，但其應用到服裝設計仍處於嬰兒期, 因為胸罩和乳房的軟組織之間的接觸力學,是高度非線性和3D的力傳遞是非常複雜的。此項目擬制定科學的算法來模擬這些3D的力量和由此產生的乳房變形來設計最佳承托的胸罩，給個別女人塑造她想要造型。48中國女人分屬於16种最常見的尺寸將參加人體掃描實驗。基於三維人體掃描圖像和數字解剖模, FEM模型包括骨骼，肌肉，乳房，乳頭，和皮膚的構造。該材料係數（乳房阻尼比，皮膚的厚度和硬度）將被初始分配，然後將通過比較預測與實驗數據值，進行驗證。力學性能如拉伸、彎曲、胸罩組件（胸杯、鋼圈、鷄心、橡根和肩帶）的剪切、擠壓、摩擦都會進行測試，並輸入到FE胸罩子模型。為了模擬真實的文胸穿着的條件下，不同類型的不同元件之間的彈性接觸會創新性地應用。算法將被合併，以模擬3D變形、應力和應變的結果。本研究針對婦女基本需求的一個舒適的日常佩戴的鋼圈胸罩。通過驗證有限元模型，胸罩的整形效果和應力值可被預測。這種新方法不僅方便日後文胸的設計優化，也帶來進一步的3D研究和其他軟商品的計算機輔助設計。對人體與服裝互動的生物力學的科學認識將有助設計各類的未來產品，這將確保香港設計的可持續增長，並有机会尋求非研資局撥款，來制定一個有限元模型的圖形用戶界面來設計功能性服裝等產品。

15220514.label: Realisation of objectives
15220514.value: Women often wear ill-fitting bras which cause pain, discomfort and sagging due to the over-simplified bra-sizing system used in the manufacture of commercial bras. In addition, a long development process is required for conventional bra design from creating the prototype to manufacturing the final product, which include the key steps of material selection, pattern making and grading. Thus, in order to reduce the time of the product development cycle and assist bra designers in determining individual bra fit that provides an optimal supportive shape and comfortable pressure, numerical simulation is a potential new tool. Bra designers can gain a better understanding of the interaction process between the breasts and bras with different design features by using numerical simulation. In this study, the non-linear material coefficients of the soft tissues of the breasts was firstly determined. An optimal approach based on static and dynamic FE models with the corresponding deformations during different movements was used. The Mooney-Rivlin material parameters of the breasts in-vivo were iteratively modified through an optimization process until the predicted deformation of breasts matches the experimental results. Based on the proposed method for determining the optimal material coefficients of the breast tissues, a subject-specific biomechanical model was constructed with high accuracy for simulating the interaction between bra and breast tissues. To predict the shaping effects and contact pressure induced by a bra, the bra wearing process was simulated by using an FE contact model in a user defined coordinate system. Three primary steps are involved: 1) obtaining a stress-free sub-model of both the breasts and bra; 2) applying the gravity load and closing the bra strap and underband at the center of the back of the body; and 3) adjusting the bra position by using “virtual hands”. The contact force of the bra and the gravity of the breasts can achieve equilibrium after carrying out these three steps. The contour maps generated by using FE software are used to visually evaluate the amount of breast deformation and contact pressure and quantitatively analyze the results. The simulated results in terms of the breast shape and pressure distribution were validated with a fit trial based on an underwire bra. Results indicated that the FE model can predict the deformation of the breast shape with reasonable accuracy. On the basis of the FE contact model, the impacts of different bra features including the material properties of the bra cup fabric, bra style (underwired vs. wireless bra) and different gore sizes on breast shaping effects and contact pressure were further investigated. It is found from the simulation results that, amongst the three types of cup materials studied, a rigid material has a better performance in shaping the breasts but induces a higher contact pressure at the bottom of the breasts. Although soft flexible material could reduce the contact pressure at the bottom of the breasts, its poor support creates a pressure hotspot at an intersecting point between the shoulder and the neck. The wireless bra induces less pressure on the breasts, however, the underwired bra has better shaping effects in terms of lifting, gathering and supporting of the breasts. The effectiveness of the wireless bra on breast deformation is only three-fifths of that of the underwired bra and this relationship could be used to predict the deformation of breasts with different materials of underwires in the early stages of bra design. The simulation results of different bra gore size show that this design feature can change the breast shape to a certain extent and also cause fitting problems if the gore size is not appropriate. It is observed that a reduction in the length of the upper part of the gore contributes to the gathering effect of the breasts, thus resulting in a deep cleavage. The length of the bottom part of the gore can readily change the lifting effects and the position of the bra underwire, thus leading to poor fit of the bra against the breast roots and wear discomfort. It is believed that the wear system based on a biomechanical model can predict bra fit on the real human body, and produce the ultimate shape and amount of pressure, which provide the fundamentals of fit evaluation for bra designers. The FE contact model proposed in this study can help to provide a better understanding of the interaction process between breasts and a bra by predicting the amount of deformation and contact pressure with reasonable accuracy. Bra manufacturers will benefit from this numerical simulation method so that they can determine more suitable fabrics and pattern for bras in the early stages of the bra design process.

15220514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220514.value: A model of the breasts with realistic material coefficients has been constructed. The nonlinear hyper-elastic material parameters of the breast tissues are predicted through FE simulation of the large deformation experienced by unsupported breasts by using a dynamic analysis. By iteratively changing the input parameters with reasonable accuracy and validating the process with the experimental results of the breast deformation during forward leaning, an optimal solution of determining the material coefficients of the breasts has been obtained. With the optimal prediction of hyper-elastic parameters of breast tissues, the biomechanical FE model of the body can be applied to simulate breast deformation when interacting with a bra more accurately based on a real life situation. A novel bra try-on system based on numerical simulation has been designed to predict the effects of different bras on shaping the breasts and the amount of contact pressure induced. The contact models for the breasts and bra are realized by releasing the tension of the initial prototype and donning the bra onto the body to simulate the stress distribution and shaping effects during the wearing process. The simulation results are validated with experimental data from a fit trial in terms of the pressure distribution and shaping effects. The results show that the simulation results are in very good agreement with the experimental results. The influence of different bra design parameters (viz., cup fabric, gore length and insertion of underwires) on the shaping effects of the breasts and the corresponding amount of contact pressure are compared by using the developed try-on model for bras. With the validated FE contact model, the impact of the elastic modulus values of the bra cup material on the breast shape and the associated pressure are simulated by applying different virtual materials with different elastic modulus values. The results indicate that the Young’s modulus of the bra cup material is a key parameter in bra design that can be used to manipulate the breast shaping effects. The validated FE model not only enhances current knowledge on biomechanical body parts-garment interactions, but also provides useful information for the comparison of bra design features and the selection of suitable materials for bras. Bra designers and customers can therefore benefit because the model can be used to advance bra design and the development process. The output of the study could also extend to the design and development of other soft and wearable apparel.

15220514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220514.value: Future studies are recommended to build the FE models based on more subjects to observe the robustness of the simulation method. The biomechanical model of the breasts needs to be modified based on several aspects: i) the geometric configurations of the breasts should incorporate different components such as the adipose and glandular tissues and ligaments. Different parts of the breasts need to be assigned with different material properties; ii) to predict the material coefficients of the breasts, a more advanced optimization algorithm should be used to individually modify the 5 different hyper-elastic material coefficients; and iii) the rigid torso model can be modified by adding subcutaneous tissues and skin which would allow more realistic simulations of the pressure distribution on the body. Other mechanical properties of the bra cup fabric (such as the compression modulus of the foam used for the bra cup, thickness, friction, etc.) or other design factors (such as shape of the cup and underwire, orientation of the bra straps, etc.) can be tested as variables that impact the interaction between the breasts and bra.

15220514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220514.value: Women experience ill-fitting bras which cause pain, discomfort and sagging for a long time. In addition, traditional bra design experiences a long process of development from prototype to a real product, in which including key steps of material selection, pattern making and grading. In order to shorten the product development cycle and assist the bra designer to improve bra fit with optimized supportive shape and comfortable pressure, computer simulation method has been adopted. The interaction mechanism between the breasts and bras with different design features was systematically investigated, including determination of the realistic material coefficients of breast tissues thus to be used to build accurate biomechanical FE model; development of a subject-specific FE model to simulate the wearing process of a bra; parametric design for different bra features to evaluate the shaping effects of breasts and pressure distribution on body. The FE contact model visualises the interaction mechanism of breast and bra by predicting the deformation and contact pressure with a reasonable accuracy. Bra manufacturers can be benefitted from this numerical simulation method to choose more suitable fabric and proper pattern making for bra at the early stage of bra development.

15221114.label: Project Objectives
15221114.value: Design and analysis of micrometer-scale lens array for high-resolution focusing: We will study how to generate a localized light filed for ultrahigh-resolution laser nanofabrication. Particularly, we will pay attention on the resolution enhancement approaches compatible with SLM based rapid laser nanomanufacturing technologies. We will investigate diffractive binary-optic microlenses for elimination of light noise, and superlenses for focusing of light beyond the diffraction limit. We will exploit its potential to access the feature size of submicron regime; Develop micro-optics and superlens for laser beam reshaping and localization: One of the distinct features of the proposed nanofabrication technology is that it uses an MEMS device to simultaneously manipulate around one million beamlets for processing optical images. In order to achieve an ultrahigh resolution exposure, it is crucial to use micro-optics for laser beam reshaping and superlens for light localization. We will fabricate those micrometer scale lens components through lithography, reactive ion etching and thermal reflow methods. The fabricated micro-optics and superlens will be integrated into our maskless exposure setup and compared with the theoretical predictions for system optimization; Develop a rapid 3D biofabrication technology for microengineering of biomaterials: In order to achieve 3D fabrication capability, techniques similar to conventional rapid prototyping (RP) technology will be developed in this project. The objective model will be sliced into a number of layers and then be loaded to the optical engine for a layer-by-layer processing. In order to facilitate bioprocessing, biocompatible fabrication recipe for tissue engineering will be developed. We will pay particular attention on hydrogels for the fabrication of scaffolds because of its close resemblance to native tissues. The fabricated 3D biochips will be biocompatible and noncytotoxic, and are thus feasible for cell culture and proliferation; Mimicking 3D microenvironments for the regulation of stem cell behaviors: The technology developed in this project will be used for the fabrication of 3D scaffolds and biochips with micro-scale features. With the collaboration with researchers of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, we are going to mimic 3D microenvironments for the regulation of human mesenchymal stem cell behaviors. The effects of 3D and/or tiny geometric and mechanical cues of extracellular microenvironments in vitro on the stem cell proliferation will be investigated. The dependence of the best initial cell-seeding density and culture time on the geometric and mechanical cues of scaffolds will be also studied.

15221114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221114.value: Advanced manufacturing is one of the crucial technologies for the economic well-beings. Although there are a plenty of well-established platforms, it is an ever-growing demand to develop new technologies for manufacturing new devices and products. Recently, “additive manufacturing” technologies attracted great attentions in both research and industry. For instance, the Obama administration announced a $1 billion investment on the innovation of additive manufacturing technologies, including creating the National Additive Manufacturing Innovation Institute, in March 2012. As often referred as “3D printing”, this technology can produce complex 3D constructs or components directly from a computer file. Moreover, it can process a variety of materials and thus is very promising in a wide range of industries. On the other hand, one of remarkable progresses in biomedical researches is the emergence of tissue engineering. It is an interdisciplinary field that applies the principles of both the life sciences and engineering to develop biological substitutes that can restore, maintain, and improve tissue functions. Micro-engineered biochips have been demonstrated to control or guide the cell growing in a biomimic extracellular microenvironment or scaffolds to form tissues and even organs that can be safely implanted in the body. Those technologies rely on a feasible biofabrication technology to fabricate 3D constructs with micro-/nano-scale features. This project aims to develop a new additive nano-manufacturing approach by using laser technologies for rapid fabrication of complex 3D biochips for tissue engineering. In particular, we will: 1) design and analysis of micrometer-scale lens array for high-resolution focusing, 2) develop micro-optics and superlens for laser beam reshaping and localization, 3) develop a rapid 3D biofabrication technology for microengineering of biomaterials, and 4) mimicking 3D microenvironments for the regulation of stem cell behaviors. The project will be an important step towards the “3D nano-bio-printing” for tissue engineering. The successful implementation of the proposed research will bring significant improvement in the biomaterial processing technology for e.g. cell and developmental biology, transplantation science, and biomedical engineering. It can foster the development of some emerging biomedical approaches, e.g. cells (or organs) on chips, in biology and medicine researches. Eventually such a technology will pave an avenue to “print” biological tissues or multi-tissue scaffolds to develop artificial organs for patients that require life-saving organ transplantation. 先进制造技术是社会经济发展攸关的基础科技之一。尽管目前已经发展了很多成熟的技术平台，人们依然不断要求开发用于制造新器件和新产品的新制造技术。近日，增材制造技术引起了研究和业界的高度关注。比如，2012年3月奥巴马政府宣布价值10亿美元投入，用于创建国家增材制造创新研究所和相关技术研究。这项技术也常被称为“3D打印”技术，可以直接将电脑数据文件用于制造复杂的三维结构或组件。此外，它还可以用于加工处理多种材料，因此在众多产业都具有广阔的应用前景。 另一方面，在生物医学领域中最近的组织工程研究进展备受注目。它是一个同时运用应用生命科学和工程学技术，研究和发展用于恢复、保持和改进生命组织功能的跨学科领域。通过先进微制造技术制备的生物芯片，可以用于控制或引导细胞在仿生细胞外微环境或支架中生长，形成可安全植入人体的组织和器官。这些科学研究依赖于一些可靠的、可用于制造微纳特征尺度的生物制造技术。 本项目旨在通过发展新型激光增材制造技术，研制用于组织工程研究的3D生物芯片及其快速微纳制造方法。我们将主要研究：1) 研究和设计基于微米尺度透镜阵列的高分辨率光学聚焦和成像技术；2）研究和发展用于激光光束整形和会聚的微光学器件技术；3）研究和发展用于生物材料微结构制备的快速3D生物制造技术；4）研究和制备用于调节干细胞行为的3D微细胞环境。 本项目将会是实现组织工程“3D纳米生物打印”技术的重要一步。项目的成功实施将会给生物材料加工技术带来显著的进步，可用于细胞和发育生物学、移植学和生物医学工程等。可以促进一些新兴生物医学技术和方法的发展，如细胞（或器官）生物芯片技术。我们相信，这项技术的发展最终将为需要器官移植的病人们“打印”人造器官生物组织或多组织支架铺平道路。

15221114.label: Realisation of objectives
15221114.value: This project proposed to develop laser additive nano-fabrication technology for 3D micropatterning of biomaterials and fabrication of biochips for tissue engineering. In the past several years, some remarkable results in line with the project’s objectives have been achieved: 1. Top-lensed microlens array has been designed and fabricated for laser beam reshaping and focusing We have numerically and experimentally investigated various kinds of micrometer-scale microlens for light beam shaping and focusing. In particular, we have designed a top-lensed microlens and systematically investigated its light focusing characteristics. With the ray-tracing method, numerical simulations have revealed that such a lens-on-lens structure can not only focus the light beam as usual but also efficiently elongate the depth of focus to 475 μm. Such a special microlens is very promising to relieve the tolerance of working distance in microlens-based lithography technoloiges. The designed microlenses have been fabricated by using our own-established digital UV lithography system. SU-8 resin was used to make the microlens array because of its high transmissivity (in the visible spectral range) and excellent mechanical property. Experimental results verified that such a special microlens can effectively engineer the focal structure to elongate the depth of focus or even produce two separate focal points. The results have been presented in an international conference CLEO Pacific Rim 2018, see the conference paper No.1. 2. A rapid 3D micropatterning technology has been developed for microengineering of biomaterials The core mission of the project is to develop a 3D nano-fabrication technology for processing of biomaterials so as to facilitate the research of tissue engineering. In the project, we have developed a spatial-light-modulator based rapid additive nano-fabrication technology, called optical 3D μ-printing technology, for processing biomaterials, particularly various kind of hydrogels. We have demonstrated that poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) hydrogel, which is a pH-responsive hydrogel widely used in tissue engineering, can be rapidly micropatterned into various kind 2D/3D microstructures within 10 to 20 s. The lateral and depth resolutions of the technology for patterning PAA are about 4.8 μm and 200 nm, respectively. It is believed that such a micropatterning technology can trigger innovations in microengineering of PAA ionic hydrogels for a myriad of bio applications. The results have been published in the top journal Advanced Materials (IF: 19.8), see the journal paper No.1. The work was highlighted by Materials Views China. Moreover, the technology has been demonstrated to process other kinds of polymer materials, such as gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) (see the journal paper No. 2), poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) (see the journal paper No. 3), poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) (see the journal paper No. 4), and SU-8 epoxy (see the journal paper No. 2 & 5) and revealed its great promise for many different bio-/micro-engineering applications. 3. 3D cellular-scale microscaffolds have been demonstrated to mimic extracellular microenvironments for regulation of stem cell behaviors With the own-developed 3D μ-printing technology, we have collaborated with the Co-I, Dr. Liming Bian of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, to design and fabricate 3D microscaffolds and biochip for tissue engineering. We demonstrated that the optical resolution of the optical 3D μ-printing technology is 600 nm and can rapidly fabricate 3D microscaffold arrays with size matching the single-cell size on a single chip. We showed that the increase of the cubical size of the microscaffolds led to enhanced spreading of the seeded human mesenchymal stem cells and activation of mechanosensing signaling. Moreover, we demonstrated that the surfaces of suspended beams can be spatially selectively modified with a bioactive coating (gelatin methacrylate) for tailorable cell adhesion and spreading on the 3D microscaffolds. The results have been published in the international journal Scientific Reports, see the journal paper No.2. 4. 3D surface-engineered biochips have been directly printed for investigation of cell migration We have also collaborated with the Co-I to design and fabricate microfluidic biochips and microengineer the bottom surface of their microchannels for tissue engineering. Considering that poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) is a polymer material widely used for biochips, we managed to directly pattern a positive-tone PDMS to fabricate large-area microfluidic chips and use a negative-tone PDMS to fabricate high-resolution on-chip 3D microstructures. In our experiments, a large-area microfluidic chip of 5.5 × 2.8 cm2 with complex three-dimensional (3D) staggered herringbone mixers (SHMs) was fabricated from the positive-tone PDMS. Thereafter, the microchannels were further 3D engineered to customize extracellular microenvironments for cell study. In particular, corrugated microstructures with different slopes were printed on bottom surfaces to investigate the migration behaviors of human mesenchymal cell (hMSCs). It was demonstrated that the cells migrated at the fastest speed on flat surface. With the increment of the heights of the microgrooves, the migration speeds of cells became lower gradually. The results have been published in Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering, see the journal paper No. 3. In summary, we have successfully developed an additive nano-fabrication technology to process various kinds of polymer materials for tissue engineering. All of the above results are closely in line with the project objectives. Result-1 is the outcome associated with the objective-1 & 2; result-2 and result-3 are the outcomes associated with the objective-3; result-3 and result-4 are the outcomes associated with the objective-4. For the research objective No.2 , we have managed to put more research effects on novel micro-optics rather than superlens for light beam reshaping and localization. It is because we have reduced our research ambition of the project on nanolithography and adjusted the objective feature size of the technology from sub-100 nm to submicron regime (see the revised research objective No. 1) in line with the reduction of funding support. During the project execution period, we achieved the new objective and reached 600 nm (see the journal paper No.2) through the use of UV lightsource (at the wavelength of 365 nm) and improved projection optics. Moreover, we observed that the working distance of superlenses are too short to practically process biomaterials. Hence, we dedicated to develop a special micro-optics, i.e. top-lensed microlens, to enhance the tolerance of working distance for microlens-based nanolithography systems. To reflect the minor change on the research route, we have put the percentage achieved of the objective No. 2 to 90%.

15221114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221114.value: In recent years, additive manufacturing technologies have attracted great attention because of its great promise in processing materials for a wide range of applications. With the support of the GRF, we have dedicated to develop an additive nanofabrication technology for 3D printing of polymer materials for tissue engineering. In the project, we have successfully developed an optical 3D µ-printing technology and demonstrated rapid 3D micropatterning of various kind of biomaterials, such as poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) and gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogels. Experimental results revealed that the developed technology can not only rapidly fabricate micrometer-scale 2D/3D hydrogel microstructures but also allow in situ patterning of hydrogels on a very small area of target for modification and functionalization or of microstructures. Collaborating with the Co-I, Dr. Liming Bian of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, we have carried out systematical research on the development of biochips and design of on-chip microstructures for tissue engineering. We demonstrated that 3D microscaffold arrays with size matching the single-cell size can be quickly printed on a single chip. The surfaces of their suspended beams can be spatially selectively modified by using GelMA to achieve tailorable adhesion and spreading of human mesenchymal stem cells on the 3D microscaffolds. Moreover, poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) biochips with complex 3D staggered herringbone mixers have been fabricated to study the migration behavior of human mesenchymal cell (hMSCs). 3D corrugated microstructures with different slopes have been fabricated on the bottom of microchannels to investigate hMSCs’ migration behaviors. These research outcomes associated with the project have been published in renowned international journals, such as Advanced Materials and Scientific Reports (see the attached journal paper No. 1 & 2). The work about the 3D micropatterning of PAA hydrogels was highlighted by Materials Views China.

15221114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221114.value: The PI and Co-I plan to continue the collaboration on the development of biofabrication technologies to process biomaterials for tissue engineering. We will exploit the application of the developed 3D μ-printing technology in emergent biomedical researches, such as organs on a chip and transplantation science. Moreover, the PI will try to secure new grant to enable the development of new generation nanolithography to overcome the diffraction limit in pursuit of sub-100 nm regime. The ultimate goal of the research team is to develop a 3D nano-bio-printing technology to print biological tissues for development of artificial organs for regeneration medicine.

15221214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15221214.value: 针对异质多媒体数据匹配的大尺度距离度量学习

15221214.label: Project Objectives
15221214.value: Supervised cross modal metric learning – The distance metric learning problem for heterogeneous data can be considered as a learning task with pairwise constraints. Different from single modal metric learning, sample pairs are generated across modals. Then metric learning is modeled as a sample pair classification problem, which can be easily solved by standard SVM solvers. An iterating SVM will be proposed to ensure that the learned distance metric is semi-positive definite. Cache technique in large scale SVM will be introduced, which makes it possible to deal with large scale pairwise constraints. Therefore, the proposed model could effectively use the label information and have good scalability. Semi-supervised cross modal metric learning – Despite the availability of large amounts of training samples, the data labeling is quite time-consuming and expensive. The lack of labeled training samples may make the trained distance metric inaccurate and easily overfitting. To make good use of the unlabeled and linked data, a set of unlabeled sample pairs will be generated. Then graph Laplacian regularization can be used to train a more accurate distance metric with good generalization ability. Different from the graph regularization in each modality, the model with cross modal graph regularization can be effectively solved by Laplacian SVM or other semi-supervised solvers. Multiple kernel cross modal metric learning – The data in the same modality may have different representations. In this case, we need a multiple feature distance metric for cross modal matching. All the previous work only focuses on multiple feature learning in the same modality. We proposed a multiple feature kernel for heterogeneous data and then model this problem as a generalized multiple kernel learning (MKL) model, which can be solved by the current MKL solvers.

15221214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221214.value: 异质多媒体数据广泛存在于许多应用中，如照片-素描人脸识别，静止图像-视频序列人脸匹配，异质模式图像合成和跨媒体检索等。无处不在的数码影像设备、移动终端和社交网络的应用，如新闻媒体网站、微博、手机、社交网络等，会持续产生大量的异质和异构数据，使得异质多媒体数据的匹配在跨模态和跨媒体信息检索中的地位愈加重要。测度学习是异质数据匹配的流行方法之一，它通过学习一个半正定矩阵来衡量异质数据的（不）相似性。然而，针对异质数据匹配，目前的测度学习方法仍然存在一些尚未解决、极具挑战性的问题和局限性。首先，当前测度学习方法在处理多样化和复杂的数据类型时具有局限性，如文本、图形、图像、音频、视频、二维和三维数据等；其次，当前方法的可扩展性差，难以应用于大规模异质多媒体数据匹配应用；第三，大部分数据的标签是不可得到的，如果将目前的测度学习方法推广到半监督和弱监督情形；第四，同一模态的数据可能有不同的表示，所以对跨模态数据匹配需要学习一个多特征相似性测度。因此，我们希望针对跨模态和跨媒体数据匹配，从可扩展性、半监督和弱监督学习、跨模态多特征学习等方面，开展测度学习研究。 在本项目中，为了进行异质多媒体数据匹配，我们将采用基于大规模样本对的核分类模型来进行跨模态距离度量学习。通过将跨模态度量学习问题表示为一个包含训练样本对约束的样本对分类问题，我们将提出基于支持向量机（SVM）的迭代训练算法来有效求解这个问题。该度量学习模型具有以下优点。首先，通过定义并引入跨模态样本对核函数和数据相关的核函数，如高斯核和直方图核，我们可以处理复杂类型的数据。第二，通过引入缓存技术，我们的模型将可以处理百万级数量的样本对约束。基于我们提出的迭代支持向量机训练算法，我们可以从海量数据中使用大规模度量学习得到所需要的跨模态距离度量。第三，通过引入图拉普拉斯正则化项，我们的度量学习模型还可以对大量的无标记或联合数据加以利用，而且该半监督模型可以使用拉普拉斯支持向量机求解。第四，考虑到每个模态中的数据可能有不同的表示，我们将研究多重核度量学习模型来将数据的不同表示进行有效结合。 我们提出的测度学习方法可以显著提高异质多媒体数据的匹配效果，并且在大规模跨媒体检索中有广泛应用。我们已经取得一些振奋人心的初步结果，验证了本项目的可行性和巨大潜力。本项目的研究成果将为跨模态数据匹配提供新的视角和方向，有望在多媒体内容分析和测度学习领域中产生很大影响力。

15221214.label: Realisation of objectives
15221214.value: 1. Supervised cross modal metric learning Distance metric learning aims to learn from the given training data a valid distance metric, with which the similarity between data samples can be more effectively evaluated for classification .We investigated the problem of supervised cross modal metric learning under the scenario of person re-identification, and developed a novel cross-image representation method. Usually, person re-identification is modeled as learning a metric to either match single-image representation (SIR) or classify cross-image representation (CIR). We connected these two categories of methods, and propose a joint metric learning framework to unify SIR and CIR using convolutional neural network (CNN). Specifically, our deep architecture contains one shared sub-network together with two sub-networks that extract the SIRs of given images and the CIRs of given image pairs, respectively. The SIR sub-network is required to be computed once for each image (in both the probe and gallery sets), and the depth of the CIR sub-network is required to be minimal to reduce computational burden. Therefore, the two types of representation can be jointly optimized for pursuing better matching accuracy with moderate computational cost. Furthermore, the representations learned with pairwise comparison and triplet comparison objectives can be combined to improve matching performance. We also developed an efficient metric learning method for large scale problems. We formulate metric learning as a kernel classification problem with the positive semi-definite constraint, and solve it by iterated training of support vector machines (SVMs). The new formulation is easy to implement and efficient in training with the off-the-shelf SVM solvers. Two novel metric learning models, namely positive-semidefinite constrained metric learning (PCML) and nonnegative-coefficient constrained metric learning (NCML), are developed. Both PCML and NCML can guarantee the global optimality of their solutions. Experiments on general classification, face verification, and person re-identification showed that our methods can achieve comparable classification accuracy and are efficient in training. 2. Semi-supervised cross modal metric learning We studied cross modal metric learning with the application of facial attribute transfer, and developed a deep convolutional network based model for identity-aware transfer (DIAT) of facial attributes. Given the source input image and the reference attribute, DIAT aims to generate a facial image that owns the reference attribute as well as keeps the same or similar identity to the input image. In general, our model consists of a mask network and an attribute transform network which work in synergy to generate photo-realistic facial image with the reference attribute. Considering that the reference attribute may be only related to some parts of the image, the mask network is introduced to avoid the incorrect editing on attribute irrelevant region. Then the estimated mask is adopted to combine the input and transformed image for producing the transfer result. For joint training of transform network and mask network, we incorporate the adversarial attribute loss and identity aware adaptive perceptual loss. Furthermore, a denoising network is presented to serve for perceptual regularization to suppress the artifacts in transfer result, while an attribute ratio regularization is introduced to constrain the size of attribute relevant region. DIAT can provide a unified solution for several representative facial attribute transfer tasks, e.g., expression transfer, accessory removal, age progression and gender transfer, and can be extended for other face enhancement tasks such as face hallucination. 3. Multiple kernel cross modal metric learning Distance and similarity measures usually are complementary to pattern classification. We proposed a novel method to learn a combined distance and similarity measure (CDSM) and extended CDSM for learning nonlinear measures via the kernel trick. With pairwise constraints, several approaches have been proposed to combine distance and similarity measures. However, it remains less investigated to use triplets of samples for joint learning of distance and similarity measures. Moreover, the kernel extension of triplet-based model is also nontrivial and computationally expensive. By incorporating with the max-margin model, we suggest a triplet-based CDSM learning model with a unified regularizer of the Frobenius norm. A support vector machine (SVM)-based algorithm is then adopted to solve the optimization problem. Two effective strategies are adopted to speed up training and testing of kernelized CDSM. Experiments demonstrated that CDSM and kernelized CDSM outperform several state-of-the-art metric learning methods.

Semi-supervised cross modal metric learning – Despite the availability of large amounts of training samples, the data labeling is quite time-consuming and expensive. The lack of labeled training samples may make the trained distance metric inaccurate and easily overfitting. To make good use of the unlabeled and linked data, a set of unlabeled sample pairs will be generated. Then graph Laplacian regularization can be used to train a more accurate distance metric with good generalization ability. Different from the graph regularization in each modality, the model with cross modal graph regularization can be effectively solved by Laplacian SVM or other semi-supervised solvers.

Multiple kernel cross modal metric learning – The data in the same modality may have different representations. In this case, we need a multiple feature distance metric for cross modal matching. All the previous work only focuses on multiple feature learning in the same modality. We proposed a multiple feature kernel for heterogeneous data and then model this problem as a generalized multiple kernel learning (MKL) model, which can be solved by the current MKL solvers.

15221214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221214.value: 1. We proposed two distance metric learning models, namely PCML and NCML, which can guarantee the positive semidefinite property of the learned matrix M, and can be solved efficiently by the existing SVM solvers. Compared with the state-of-the-art metric learning methods, the proposed methods can not only achieve favorable classification accuracy, but also much more efficient for large scale problems. [J1] 2. We proposed a joint single image representation (SIR) and cross image representation (CIR) metric learning approach for person re-identification. A pairwise comparison formulation and a triplet comparison formulation for joint SIR and CIR learning was developed by using a deep neural network. [C1] 3. We presented a max-margin model for combined distance and similarity metric (CDSM) learning. By analyzing the CDSM from pairwise kernel perspective, we extended CDSM to its kernelized version for learning nonlinear metrics, and suggested two effective strategies to reduce the computational burden. [J2] 4. A deep identity-aware transfer (i.e., DIAT) model is presented for facial attribute transfer. The whole transfer model consists of two subnetworks, i.e., mask network and attribute transform network, which work collaboratively to produce the transfer result. DIAT can also be extended to face hallucination and performs favorably in recovering facial details. [J3] 5. A CNN-based system was developed for content weighted image compression. With the importance map, we suggest a non-entropy based loss for rate control. Spatially variant bit allocation is also allowed to emphasize the salient regions. Using the straight-through estimator, our model can be trained in an end-to-end manner. Experiments clearly show the superiority of our model in retaining structures and removing artifacts, leading to remarkable visual quality. [C2] 6. We proposed a principled algorithm within the maximum a posterior framework to tackle image restoration with a partially known or inaccurate blur kernels. Specifically, the residual caused by a partially known or inaccurate degradation model is spatially dependent and highly complex in distribution. With a training set of degraded and ground-truth image pairs, we parameterize and learn the fidelity term for a degradation model in a task-driven manner. Furthermore, the regularization term can also be learned along with the fidelity term, thereby forming a simultaneous fidelity and regularization learning model. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model for image deconvolution with inaccurate blur kernel and rain streak removal. [J4]

15221214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221214.value: This project mainly focuses on metric learning for pairwise matching of cross-modal data. The learned distance metric can provide means for predicting the pairwise similarity of two samples, which is just a special type of pairwise symmetric relationship. Besides pairwise similarity, there are still many other pairwise relationship types, such as relative order relationship, pairwise interaction, etc. Therefore, in future research, one feasible and encouraging topic is to generalize the metric learning models developed in this project to pairwise relative order relationship prediction, and to apply them to some tasks such as relative attribute order, perspective transform among image pairs, etc. Different from pairwise similarity, the relative order relationship is anti-symmetric. Thus, one should generalize the metric learning models by re-designing the model objective, modifying and introducing new constraints, and developing proper learning algorithms. When predicting multiple relative order relationships, we should also investigate the principled solution for their modeling and joint learning issue. Moreover, it is also deserved to apply these model to real world applications such as relative attribute prediction, camera pose estimation, etc.

15221214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221214.value: In this project, we studied the cross-modal metric learning methods, which aim to match two instances from different modalities, e.g., face image vs. sketch, pedestrian image vs. surveillance video, etc. To this end, we first studied supervised cross-modal metric learning, in which each training instance is annotated with a class label. Specifically, we developed two models to learn the Mahalanobis distance and deep similarity metrics, respectively. Second, we studied the cross-modal metric learning in the case of semi-supervised learning, in which only a few number of training instances are labeled. We also reduced the difference in face modalities by transferring the attributes of face images, e.g., age, expression, etc. Furthermore, we combined the distance and similarity measures, and extend it for learning the nonlinear metric with the kernel trick. The experiments on general classification, face verification, person re-identification and facial style transfer demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed methods. All these studies have important application value in many cross modality matching and transferring areas such as cross-modality retrieval, image style transfer, etc.

15221414.label: Realisation of objectives
15221414.value: The project involves three objectives, i.e., (1) Development of MTInSAR algorithms to parameterize and mitigate the atmospheric artifacts; (2) Improvement of accuracies and reliabilities of deformation measurements derived by MTInSAR; (3) Retrieval of spatial-temporal variations of water vapours at fine scales from MTInSAR measurements. The realisation of these objectives is summarized as follows. To achieve the first objective, we firstly analysed the relationship between the phase measurements and the components of atmospheric delay (i.e., the stratified part and turbulent part). We found that although phase contribution of stratified component can be parametrized according to topographic heights, a simple linear model commonly adopted in current algorithms is deficient to describe the contribution. Moreover, the estimation of linear parameters could be distorted by other phase components (e.g., deformation and DEM error). In this project, we successfully developed a Multi-Temporal InSAR (MTInSAR) model that jointly parameterized the stratified atmospheric delay (SAD) and signals of our interests (i.e., the deformation) where the linear relationship between SAD and target height is guaranteed by dividing the processing area into patches with limited height gradient. The synthetic and real data tests indicate the proposed algorithm has outstanding performance over the state-of-the-arts and has been integrated into our InSAR software platform of our group for routine data processing. The algorithm has been published in [1] and presented in [2]. It was then applied for retrieval of ground deformation associated with Tatun Volcano Group in Taiwan where the atmospheric delay is serious. The result was presented in [3]. The realisation of the first objective is complete. The second objective (i.e., the quality enhancement of InSAR derived deformation) is a post procedure of the joint model where the stratified atmospheric delay has been mitigated. It mainly focuses on the separation of DEM residuals and turbulent component of atmospheric delay, which is one of major contributions of InSAR measurements. DEM residuals are due to the inaccurate external DEM product used in InSAR processing chain, which commonly exist and need to be mitigated. Conventional MTInSAR algorithms usually take DEM residual as a parameter and estimate it by solution space searching. However, there is a lack of knowledge on to what extent the DEM can be mitigated. Flowing the standard MTInSAR framework, we conducted theoretical analysis on the factors that can affect the DEM residual estimation and conclude that interferogram network, baseline status, deformation model bias and phase noise can distort the estimation. The analysis indicates that the current MTInSAR algorithms are far from being optimized and also sheds light on the directions of future algorithm development. The result was published in [4]. Based on the accuracy analysis, we explored one strategy to reduce the effects of DEM residuals on retrieval of deformation. Such a strategy is based on the fact that DEM contributed phases are proportional to the lengths of perpendicular baselines. In interferograms with extremely short baselines, deformation becomes the only signal to be parameterized and therefore the model reliability can be improved. However, the number of such interferograms generated from original SAR images is limited. Considering that the interferograms are the linear combination of SAR images, interferograms with ultrashort baselines can be constructed by integer combination of original ones. Based on these pseudo interferograms, we developed a concise MTInSAR model for deformation retrieval without the need of DEM residual estimation, which was submitted and is under second round of review [5]. To mitigate the effect of turbulent component of atmospheric delay, its feature of spatial correlation is used, leading to a pixel-wise processing algorithm that was published in [6]. With these algorithms, a set of applications were conducted, which covered the topics related to landslide monitoring [7-10] and infrastructure monitoring [11]. The second objective has been realized. Retrieval of water vapor distribution from MTInSAR measurements is the third objective of this project. Actually, it is a transformation from the atmospheric delay based on the available models. After the atmospheric delay has been isolated from phase measurements, we conduct the transformation using the state-of-the-arts where no innovative algorithm was developed. The retrieved water vapor map has higher spatial resolution than that from meteorological stations while the temporal resolution is low, which limited the applications of the products. Overall, the realisation of this objective is also complete. Overall, the project has been well conducted and the work is closely related to the project objectives. 15221414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221414.value: Major findings In this project, a suite of MTInSAR processing algorithms have been developed aiming to parameterize and mitigate two components of atmospheric delay which is a challenging topic in InSAR community. Most of them were published in top remote sensing journals. Compared with the state-of-the-arts, these algorithms have superior performance on atmospheric delay correction. They are expected to advance the research in this aspect. With these algorithms, accurate retrieval of deformations associated with landslides and infrastructure was conducted, which helped to investigate the mechanism behind the deformation. Research outcomes A total of 10 papers directly related to this project were published and 1 manuscript is under review.

15221414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221414.value: Since the processing algorithms developed in this project have superior performance on mitigating atmospheric delay in InSAR measurements, they have promising potential to be used for deformation monitoring in tropical and sub-tropical zones. Naturally, one future development of this research could be the study of urban resilience to geohazards in Greater Bay Area by satellite radar. It’s widely accepted that high density cities are vulnerable to geohazards (e.g., mudslides, sinkhole, and landslides). Close monitoring of the health status of urban infrastructures is vital for enhancing urban resilience. Space radar technology with advanced data processing algorithms makes large-scale monitoring of deformation possible. It is no doubt that such a future development has a practical meaning.

15221414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221414.value: Large-scale ground deformation can be retrieved from satellite radar images, which has long been used to study the mechanism of geohazards (e.g., landslides and earthquakes) and the health status of infrastructures (e.g., high-rise buildings and cross-sea bridges). However, when the radar waves penetrate the atmospheric layers, the signal will be delayed and thereby errors are involved in the mapped ground deformation. To improve the quality of the measured deformation, atmospheric delay needs to be mitigated, which is a challenging topic in radar community. In this project, by discomposing the atmospheric delay into stratified and turbulent components, we developed a suite of innovative processing algorithms for each component based on their distinct features over other signals. These algorithms were integrated into a processing platform and the performance was verified by synthetic test and case studies related to landside and infrastructure deformation mapping. The research outputs of this project are expected to advance the research on atmospheric delay. Considering Hong Kong located in sub-tropical zones suffers the effect of complicated atmospheric status, the developed algorithms can also enhance the local application of radar data for e.g., monitoring of deformation associated with reclamation areas.

15221614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221614.value: Foot and ankle problems have become a major burden on public healthcare systems and can have a significant impact on people’s lives. In many cases, conservative nonsurgical treatments fail in alleviating the symptoms, leaving invasive surgical treatment as the only viable option. Surgical treatments often need, especially for patients with end-stage arthritis, including osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis or post-traumatic arthritis. Ankle joint fusion (arthrodesis) and total ankle joint replacement (arthroplasty) are two of the most common surgical treatments for restoring normal functionality. Ankle arthrodesis is effective in relieving pain for end-stage arthritis, chronic instability and degenerative deformity of ankle structures, but the joint fusion limits the relative motion and increases the joint stiffness. Total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) replaces the damaged ankle with prosthetic components. Unlike knee and hip joints, total ankle replacement does not have a high success rate, primarily due to the limited understanding of the complicated ankle joint structures and biomechanics. The foot/ankle comprises of 28 identifiable bones and soft tissues, and is an intricate and synergetic system. Individual segments interact interdependently with the remaining parts and, in turn, are heavily influenced by alterations in adjacent components. Surgical intervention may result in functional alterations to the surrounding structures. It is thus necessary to consider the biomechanical effects not only around the surgical regions, but also over the entire foot and ankle. Surgeons may often question the consequences of treatment when so little is known about the biomechanical impact. However, it is not easy to predict how surgery on one site will influence adjacent segments, particularly in the long-term. Our team has worked on comprehensive computational foot/ankle modeling for over 15 years, and established an analytical platform. With modification and improvement, the platform will be able to incorporate surgical operations into the model and become an effective tool for outcome prediction. In this proposed project, experimental studies will be carried out to obtain kinematic and kinetic information during walking. Computational models established on the experimental data can further provide biomechanical information on load transfer inside the foot/ankle structures. A comparison of joint and tissue loading before and after surgical treatment can be used to understand the biomechanical consequence of the treatment. The overall objective is to better understand foot and ankle biomechanics, which can provide information for the evaluation of surgical treatments and design of better ankle prostheses. 足踝问题已成为重大的公共卫生负担之一，影响着人的生活质素。许多情况下非手术的保守治疗可以减轻症状。但对于严重病症，比如晚期关节炎，包括骨关节炎，类风湿性关节炎或创伤后关节炎，通常需要手术治疗。 踝关节融合术和踝关节置换术是两种主要手术治疗方法，藉以减轻症状及恢复正常功能。踝关节融合术可有效治疗晚期关节炎，关节不稳定和退行性畸形，但是该手术限制了踝关节的运动，造成关节僵硬。踝关节置换术（TAA）是另外一种外科手术，用假体取代受损关节。由于复杂的踝关节结构和有限的生物力学知识，踝关节置换的成功率远远低于膝关节和髋关节。 足踝涉及28个骨骼和众多软组织，是一个复杂的协同系统。部件之间相互作用相互依赖，任何部分的改变都可能影响相邻组织，乃至整个足踝的生物力学行为。因此，手术的生物力学研究不能仅限于手术区域，而是整个脚踝。 术后效果可以作为制定手术方案的重要依据。然而，由于测量技术和方法的限制，术后效果很难通过现有方法预测。计算生物力学在预测生物力学行为领域凸显优势。我们的团队在足踝的计算模型有多年研究基础，已建立了一个研究平台。随着修改和完善，该平台将用于术后效果预测，并成为这个项目的有效工具。 此研究项目将通过步态实验获取运动学和动力学信息，并建立足踝计算模型，获取足踝结构内部负载传递的生物力学信息，并对比手术前后的足踝生物力学信息。本研究的结果可以深入了解足踝关节生物力学，为手术治疗和踝关节假体设计提供依据。

15221614.label: Realisation of objectives
15221614.value: Objective 1: To investigate walking kinematics and kinetics of the foot and ankle through in vivo experiments and cadaveric studies after different ankle surgical treatments. The data obtained from these experiments will help in understanding how surgical treatment, such as ankle fusion and total ankle replacement, changes the foot and ankle biomechanical behavior and, at the same time, provide input values and validation data for the computational model; This objective is fully achieved to date. Gait analysis for 4 subjects with normally functioned musculoskeletal system have been conducted using video record, Vicon motion capturing system and force platforms. As this project is focused on the foot and ankle, the gait analysis experiments were designed to collect data of the lower limbs. The 3D motion capture system records human motion through capturing trajectories of reflective markers attached on human body. The musculoskeletal system of the lower limbs of the subjects were defined into seven rigid-body segments using reflective 16 markers, including the pelvis, the left and right thigh, the left and right lower leg, and the left and right foot. To measure plantar pressure during balanced standing and walking, Fscan sensors were trimmed to fit the foot sizes and attached to the plantar feet using double-side adhesive tape. Two force platforms on the walking way were used to record ground reaction forces. Before conduction of the walking trials, each subject was asked to stand statically with foot separated in shoulder-width in one force platform for five seconds for the calibration of the motion capture system and to record plantar pressure for balanced standing condition. During the walking experiments, all subjects were asked to walk in their natural speed, with each foot stepping on individual force platforms. Each subject walked for 3 trials. In this experiment, the tempo-spatial parameters of the biomechanics of the lower limb, including joint motion, joint force and moment, joint and segment velocity, acceleration, plantar pressure and ground reaction forces were obtained. These data were further used to validate the finite element model of the foot and ankle, and served as boundary and loading conditions for gait simulation. Cadaveric experiment has been conducted to measure the joint contact pressure in specific loading conditions of the foot and ankle for validation of the finite element model. A right foot and ankle from a fresh cadaver of a male was used. Extrinsic groups of muscles were individually isolated from the soft tissues. To apply loading to the muscles, equivalent weights were hang on the separated ends of the muscles. An incision on the dorsi-foot over the talonavicular joint were made, and a contact pressure sensor was inserted into the joint. Under the specific muscle loadings, contact pressure at the talonavicular joint was recorded. The measured contact pressure was then compared to the calculated contact pressure at this joint through finite element analysis for validation of the finite element model of the foot and ankle. Objective 2: To understand the internal biomechanical behavior of the foot/ankle structures after surgical treatment through comprehensive finite element analyses. Incorporating previously developed foot/ankle models, a full-featured foot and ankle model which can simulate surgical treatment will be developed to understand how the treatment influences the function of the foot and ankle and may possibly lead to other joint problems; This objective is fully achieved to date. Finite element model of the intact foot and ankle had been developed in previous work. Based on this, a finite element model of foot with total ankle arthroplasty and a finite element model of foot with ankle arthrodesis were established to simulate two reconstructive ankle surgeries. The STAR ankle replacement implant was adopted in this simulation, a three-component implant consisting of a tibia plate, mobile bearing, and a talar component. These components were scanned to digital data using 3D scanning device, and reconstructed into geometries. To replace the ankle joint in the finite element model of the intact foot, the geometries of the three components were imported into the foot model, and moved to the ankle joint position through translation and rotation functions. Boolean operation of subtraction were conducted between the model of the foot and ankle and the implant to cut and remove the tibia and talar bones of the ankle joint. Then the implant of the tibia plate was tied to the cutting interface of the tibia bone, and the talar component was tied to the cutting interface of the talar bone to simulate the fixation of the implants to the bones. The mobile bearing interacted with the other two components in frictionless contact. Ligaments around the ankle joint were maintained. To simulate ankle arthrodesis surgery, the contact surface of the ankle joint in the finite element model of the intact foot were tied to totally constrain relative motion at the articular surface. The finite element model was validated through comparison of plantar pressure and joint contact pressure between experimental measurement and computational prediction. Reasonable agreements were shown in the comparisons. Gait simulation were conducted among the finite element models of the intact foot, the total ankle arthroplasty foot and the ankle arthrodesis foot. Biomechanical parameters of the inner foot, including joint contact pressure, bone stress distribution, force transmission, were analysed and compared among three models to demonstrate the effects of the two ankle surgeries on the entire foot. Results showed that total ankle arthroplasty resulted in more apparent deviations in the latter half of the stance phase than the first half stage, while ankle arthrodesis more obviously changed the foot biomechanics at the first half of the stance phase. Objective 3: To provide biomechanical information for designing an ankle prosthesis with a superior biomechanical performance. The new design will be expected to be more representative of a normal ankle in both functionality and strength. This objective is fully achieved to date. In addition to the biomechanics of the inner foot, performance of the prosthetic ankle during gait has also been investigated. Results in this project showed that asymmetric stress distribution was induced in the bearing component that the lateral side sustained much higher stress than the medial side, especially at the latter half of the stance phase. The design of the prosthetic ankle could theoretically achieve full range of motion in the sagittal and transverse planes, however, results in this study showed limited range of motion in the sagittal plane. Existing designs do not allow joint motion in the frontal plane. But the motion of a natural ankle joint is a complex tri-axial movement. Improvement of the design could possibly achieve through change the geometries of implants to be a more closer representation of the anatomical characteristics of a natural ankle.

15221614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221614.value: The project investigated the consequences of two surgical approaches for treatment of ankle problems. Total ankle arthroplasty did not visually change plantar pressure distribution. It did not increase the peak plantar pressure nor change the location of the center of pressure. Ankle arthrodesis resulted in apparent increase of the peak plantar pressure and anteriorly forwarded the center of pressure. Total ankle arthroplasty resulted in substantial increase of contact pressure at the talonavicular, medial cuneonavicular, and the first to the forth tarsometatarsal joints in the latter half of the stance phase. Ankle arthrodesis apparently increased contact pressure at the talonavicular, three cuneonavicular, and the first to third tarsometatarsal joints. Neither of them resulted in increase of contact pressure at the subtalar joint. Both surgeries increased bone stress in the metatarsals. Existing design of three-component ankle prosthesis could not reserve full range of motion, even in the sagittal plane. The mobile bearing sustained asymmetric stress during gait. The results were published in outputs (1) and (4)

15221614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221614.value: Improvement of the biomechanical performance could be possibly improved by optimization of the contour of the implants. Further research could be conducted on the optimization of the ankle prosthetic design. Biomechanical analysis is necessary for a new design and finite element analysis is a feasible and effective tool in prediction of biomechanics. It rapidly responds to any modification of contours and materials. Course of action of the optimization of ankle prosthesis design could be as followed: Modify the contour of the geometrical model of the ankle implants to be a closer representation of the anatomical characteristics of a natural ankle joint. Assembly the modified geometries of the ankle implants into finite element model of the foot and ankle. Simulate walking with the boundary and loading conditions the same in this project. Depending on the simulation results, modify the geometrics and materials, and do parametric study to make the biomechanical parameters maximumly fit that of an intact foot. Print a prototype using 3D printing technique and discuss with surgeons to get a protocol for fixation in the implants. Test the fixation protocols and the implants in cadaveric experiments.

15221614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221614.value: Finite element analysis is a feasible tool to investigate biomechanical performance of the inner foot. finite element models should be developed as closer as possible to represent the foot and ankle anatomy in terms of the geometries, tissue properties and boundary and loading conditions. It must be validated before used for analysis. Neither total ankle arthroplasty nor ankle arthrodesis were superior to the other. Both surgeries resulted in deviations of biomechanical parameters from that of an intact foot. Contact pressure at the subtalar joint was not affected by neither of two ankle surgeries. Deterioration of the joint after surgery in the clinical reports might be a progressive procedure of the pre-existing degeneration. Existing design of the ankle prosthesis could not reserve full range of motion of the ankle joint, even in the sagittal plane. It resulted in asymmetric loading in the mobile bearing component.
