15221714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15221714.value: 壓力升高下的雙元液滴碰撞動力學

15221714.label: Project Objectives
15221714.value: The overriding objectives of the proposed program are (a) to establish an experimental apparatus for studying droplet collision under the high pressures up to 50atm. (b) to systematically quantify the influence of the gas pressure, the size ratio and the impact parameter on the collision outcomes in terms of bouncing, coalescence and separation. (c) to develop and validate the numerical simulation based on the Front Tracking method for deep understanding of the experimental results. (d) to identify the implications of these fundamental information on droplet collision in actual engines. (e) to actively acquire droplet collision images that are needed by the development of high-fidelity numerical simulation capability for dispersed liquid-gas two-phase flow. The specific research objectives for the proposed experiments are (a) to establish an experimental apparatus, in which binary droplet collision can be studied either under the gas pressures up to 50atm or with the large Weber numbers up to O(10^5). (b) to systematically investigate the head-on collision of water and hydrocarbon (such as decane, dodecane, tetradecane and hexadecane) droplets in order to quantitatively identify the regime diagram of collision outcomes under elevated pressures. (c) to measure the velocities of the bouncing droplets and to determine their dependence on the Weber number and the gas pressure. (d) to examine the dependence of the regime diagram of collision outcomes on the size disparity with the varying size ratio of the larger droplet to the smaller one from 1.0 to 6.0. (e) examine the dependence of the regime diagram of collision outcomes on the impact parameter, which can be "continuously" adjusted between 0 and 1. The specific research objectives for the proposed numerical simulations are (a) to validate an in-house computer code based on the Front Tracking method against the experimental results obtained in the proposed experiment for the head-on collision of water and hydrocarbon droplets under the pressures of 40 to 50 atm. The van der Waals force shall be implemented in the code as the physically realistic mechanism for interface merging. The rarefied gas effects can be neglected under such high pressures. (b) to simulate the head-on collision of equal-size droplets for the pressures under which the rarefied gas effects cannot be neglected. A correlation between the artificially augmented van der Waals force and the pressure shall be established by adjusting the simulation results to reproduce experimentally observed coalescence events. (c) to use the validated in-house computer code to study the influence of the size ratio on the droplet collision outcomes, with emphasis on quantitatively predicting the boundaries between collision regimes. (d) to extend the applicability of the in-house computer code from its current axis-symmetric version to a three-dimensional version in order to study the off-center collision. Sufficient nimbleness should be given to this challenging objective.

15221714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221714.value: 近年來人們對能源短缺、環境汙染及氣候變化等問題的關註促使 開發更加清潔高效的燃燒能量轉換裝置。大部分的這種裝置都包 含氣液兩相流動，如液體燃料的霧化過程。其能量的轉換效率及 汙染物的排放與霧化過程密切相關。簡單說來，燃料的霧化過程 中伴隨有復雜的液滴碰撞現象。液滴碰撞改變了最終的燃料液滴 尺寸分布和液滴數目，從而影響到燃燒器的霧化效果和燃燒特性 。此外，氣體環境中的液滴碰撞現象廣泛存在於眾多工程技術及 自然現象中，如雨滴的形成、噴墨打印及塗層處理等。 早期的研究主要關註於液滴在大氣中的碰撞現象，之後擴展到液 體碳氫燃料液滴在各種壓力條件下（0.6~12atm）的空氣及其它氣 體環境中的碰撞，同時還擴展到不同尺寸、不同組分之間的液滴 碰撞現象。盡管人們在這個領域中已經取得了豐碩的成果，但燃 燒發動機氣缸內真實的高壓環境壓力（高達50atm）中的液滴碰 撞現象還沒有被研究。因此，進一步擴展前人在高壓條件下液滴 碰撞的實驗和數值研究成果成為本研究項目的重點。 為了充分研究高達50atm壓力條件下的液滴碰撞現象，本項目規 劃了詳細的研究計劃，重點從定量的角度對液滴碰撞過程中的彈 開、融合、分離現象進行解釋和區分。為了順利開展高壓條件下 的液滴碰撞實驗，我們將構建一套新型的高壓液滴產生系統。利 用這一新型實驗平臺對氣體環境壓力、液滴尺寸及其它液滴碰撞 參數的影響進行系統的研究。所獲得的實驗結果可以用於驗證現 有的液滴數值計算模型（如Front Tracking模型），從而使人們可 以利用數值方法加強對這一現象的理解和認識。此外，獲得的高 壓環境下液滴碰撞的基本規律可以對實際燃燒室中霧化過程的研 究提供指導。

15221714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221714.value: 1. Modeling bouncing droplets under standard and elevated pressures The kinetic energy recovery factor for bouncing droplets under atmosphere air has been numerically studied. A linear fitting formula was found to satisfactorily correlate the kinetic energy recovery factor with various collision parameters. The relevant work has been published on [Zhenyu Zhang and Peng Zhang, Phys. Fluids 29, 103306 (2017)]. The modelling of kinetic energy recovery factor has been extended to the droplet collision under elevated pressures. A practically useful model was proposed for the Lagrangian simulations of the free and impinging sprays under high ambient pressures. Again, the model produces qualitatively satisfactory predictions on the sprays. The relevant work has been published on [Zhenyu Zhang and Peng Zhang, Atomization Sprays, 28(8) (2018) 673–694]. A practically useful formula describing the nonmonotonic kinetic energy recovery with varying impact parameters was proposed and analyzed, which enhances the fundamental understanding and improves the modeling for off-center droplet collision. The relevant work has been published on [Chengming He, Xi Xia, and Peng Zhang, Phys. Fluids 31, 052004 (2019)]. 2. Demonstrating the significance of droplet bouncing in modeling impinging sprays under elevated pressures An improved droplet collision model by considering the ambient pressure effects has been proposed and applied in the simulation of impinging sprays under an elevated pressure up to 30 atm. The results show that the model can produce quantitatively satisfactory predictions to the shape, the penetration length, and the Sauter mean diameter (SMD) of the impinging sprays. The applicability of the model can be extended to higher pressures. The relevant work has been published on [Zhenyu Zhang, Yicheng Chi, Longji Shang, Peng Zhang, Zhenfeng Zhao, Int. J. Heat Mass Transf. 102 (2016) 657–668]. Based on the proposed pressure-dependent modelling for binary droplet collision, the comparison between cross-impingement spray and opposed-impingement spray in high-pressure chamber shows that the uncertainty of the kinetic energy recovery factor, which affects the post-collision characteristics of bouncing droplets, was found to cause insignificant difference in model predictions. The presence of strong swirling flow in the opposed-impingement deflects sprays and therefore shows slightly better combustion performance by producing more spatially uniform droplet distribution. However, the spray of cross-impingement enhances droplet collisions hence promotes atomization in the absence of swirling flow. The relevant work has been published on [Zhenyu Zhang and Peng Zhang, Appl. Therm. Eng. 144 (2018) 137–146].

15221714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221714.value: A single overarching goal of engine combustion is to develop a validated, accurate, all-round and predictive modelling capability so that to optimize the design and operation of advance engines. The binary droplet collision modelling is one of the indispensable components of the numerical simulation of combustion engines with liquid fuels. However, the binary droplet collision is an extremely complex phenomenon and influenced by many factors such as Weber number, size ratio, Ohnesorge number, impact parameter, ambient gas pressure. In this project, the fundamental understanding about the influences of gas pressure, size ratio, Weber number and Ohnesorge number on either head-on or off-center collisions between binary droplets have been obtained, and practically useful models for accounting for the understanding have been proposed and applied. Future development of the research is to further improve the applicability and accuracy of the proposed models under more complex and realistic situations in engines.

15221714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221714.value: Recent concerns over energy sustainability, pollution control and climate change have urged the need to develop cleaner and more efficient combustion energy conversion devices. These devices involve two-phase flow of fuel spray, in which the energy conversion efficiency and exhaust emissions greatly relies on the characteristics of the sprays, especially of the accompanying droplet collision that substantially influences the droplet number and size and the subsequent development of the spray and combustion characteristics. The earlier studies were mainly focused on droplet collision in the atmospheric air or slightly reduced and elevated pressures. Droplet collision under the prevalent pressures in an engine combustor, say, up to 30-50atm, has never been studied. Consequently, the extension of the previous experimental and numerical studies on droplet collision to higher pressures is the major focus of the proposed research program. A comprehensive research project has been successfully conducted to study various collision parameters on the droplet collision under high pressures. The obtained experimental results have been used to quantitatively validate the numerical simulations. Furthermore, the implications of the obtained fundamental information on droplet collision have been identified by studying the dense sprays in actual combustion engines.

15222014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222014.value: Scoliosis is a prevalent disease among the adolescent (adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, AIS), which was reported to be about 3% of population in Hong Kong (2 to 4% in the US). Severe scoliosis causes a number of diseases, including early degeneration of backbone, cardiopulmonary compromise, and even early mortality. Scoliosis is assessed and monitored traditionally by standing X-ray radiography, and it can be detected at its early stage before it becomes worse, especially for the fast growing youngsters. As X-ray radiography comes with ionizing radiation, an excessive risk of cancer was reported. To overcome radiation issues, ultrasound is an emerging diagnosis modality to assess scoliosis, giving its great advantages of no radiation, possibly real-time measurement, low cost and non-invasiveness. The principle investigator (PI), Zheng and his co-workers have recently developed a new three-dimensional (3D) free-hand ultrasound system for the assessment of scoliosis. It has been successfully demonstrated that the 3D ultrasound system is a reliable method for obtaining the 3D profile of spine deformity. It allows subjects to be scanned under different postures including standing or prone. However, this ultrasound method cannot be used for scanning subjects when they wear conventional spinal braces (though the team has demonstrated 3D ultrasound can be used with a specially designed brace with subject back exposed), and only X-ray imaging can be used. It is very important to understand how the spinal deformity is corrected during the fitting of brace, but it is not feasible to use X-ray for such kind of real-time monitoring. In addition, the current 3D ultrasound system needs to be used with a supporting frame to hold the subject steadily, as the movement of subject may cause distortion of the images and subsequently affect the measurement accuracy. Furthermore, the operator has to manually scan the ultrasound probe over the whole back region. To address the above problems, a new ultrasound system with flexible ultrasound arrays (FUSA) is proposed for the assessment of scoliosis without any manual or mechanical scanning needed. More importantly, it can be used when a brace is worn by the subject. It is uses electronic scanning of the arrange transducers to obtain images at different locations. The transducer arrays, position sensors, corresponding hardware, software, and beam-forming and image reconstruction algorithms will be developed. Different spatial sensors will be explored to find an optimized one for the proposed application. The new system will be validated with spine phantoms and scoliosis subjects.

15222014.label: Realisation of objectives
15222014.value: To achieve the objective 1, the team has explored different methods to make ultrasound transducer flexible. First, we have used flexible PCB to attach individual single element ultrasound transducers (5MHz) to make 1D and 2D flexible transducer arrays (Conf paper No.1), and we studied the optimized density required using experiments and computer simulation. Before using flexible PCB, we also tried embedding transducers into silicone gel to make it flexible, but found it would challenging to make a large array due to the difficulty for the electronic connections and also to make all the transducers align along the same orientation. A similar flexible concept has been used for a force sensor “Shi XM, Cheng CH, Zheng YP, Wai PKA. An EGaln-based flexible piezoresistive shear and normal force sensor with hysteresis analysis in normal force direction. Journal of Micromechanics and microengineering. 26(10), Article number 105020, 2016”. This force sensor can be potentially used for sensing the shape of the flexible transducer. In addition to flexible force sensor, we have also explored the use of motion sensor, including using an array of micro accelerometer and magnetic sensors, and the feasibility was demonstrated (Conf paper No. 1). We found that it is a challenge to increase the element density by using individual single element transducers in laboratory setting. Therefore, we further explore the possibility of using flexible 1D array transducer (5MHz) with much higher element density (128 elements in 10 cm length) (Conf paper No. 2). With the collaboration with a company in Guangzhou, China, we fabricated such a transducer. We conducted computer simulation and experiments for scanning spine phantom with different scoliotic angles, and the transducer was configured in linear, concave, convex and S shape (Journal paper No. 4, Conf paper No. 4), where a new technique of spatial sensing was adopted by using optical scanning of the transducer contour. To further increase the flexibility and density of the transducer, we explored a novel idea of using laser to generate ultrasound, i.e. photoacoustic effect, and propose an innovative optical beam forming technique for ultrasound. With the support from the university, we have successfully filed a patent for this technique (Other impact No. 1). Since it uses nanoparticles activated by laser to generate ultrasound, the transducer can be very flexible and large density. For the objective 2, we developed a new algorithm for rapid formation of 3D ultrasound imaging (Journal paper No. 3), which can be used for the flexible ultrasound transducer beam forming as well, where real-time imaging is the key advantage, such imaging speed is very essential. In addition, new algorithms have also been developed for using the spatial information to conduct 3D measurement, cohesively with a system using EM spatial sensing technique (Conf paper No. 3, Journal paper No. 1 and 2), and the algorithms can be ultimately used for the flexible transducer array (Journal paper No. 4). For the objective 3, the newly developed system has been used with two spine phantoms, with one silicone gel embedded with a deformed spine, while the other with spinal phantoms emerged in a water tank (and different scoliotic curves can be achieved) (Conf paper No. 1 and Journal paper No. 4). Repeatable scanning was conducted using these phantoms. In addition, the feasibility of scanning subjects with scoliosis was conducted and feasibility was demonstrated. Due to the reduced budget, we were not able to conduct a large scale subject tests, and future studies are being planned.

15222014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222014.value: With the feasibility of the proposed flexible ultrasound transducers demonstrated in this study, we are now working with a company, which focuses on 3D ultrasound imaging for spinal deformity, to apply an ITF project to develop this novel technique into a product. In addition, more research and development is required to tackle various challenges faced by handling a transducer sheet with thousands of elements. Furthermore, we are planning for more studies on how to benefit from such a new type of transducers, which can achieve real-time dynamic scanning of any musculoskeletal body parts.

15222014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222014.value: Ultrasound imaging has many clinical applications due to its radiation-free and easy-to-use features. Conventional ultrasound transducers normally have fixed shape, thus it has difficult to fit with curved body surface, particularly when scanning over a larger area, such as our spine. In this project, we successfully developed a novel flexible ultrasound transducer and its corresponding imaging method and system. With this flexible transducer, the ultrasound probe can fit into different contour of our body shape to conduct a better scanning. In addition, a 2D flexible ultrasound transducer can also provide real-time dynamic imaging of a large part of our subject, such as during the bending of our spine, which cannot be achieved in conventional imaging method. The achievements of this project have potential to lead to products in the near future.

15222214.value: 由於在結構、經濟和美學上的優勢，越來越多的大跨度斜拉索橋在世界範圍內得以建設，它們的安全性與功能性對整個社會都至關重要。在斜拉索橋中，斜拉索作為關鍵的承重構件，具有阻尼低、柔度高的特點，因此常常會遭受劇烈的振動。尤其是在風、風雨共同作用或參數振動的激勵下，人們常常會觀察到斜拉索的驚人的大幅度振動。這些劇烈振動會在索以及端部錨固處導致過大的應力和過早的疲勞破壞，從而危害整座橋樑的使用性與安全性。 在斜拉索上安裝各種被動、主動或者半主動的阻尼器，已經成為一種眾所周知的減振策略。這其中，被動式液態粘滯阻尼器在斜拉索中得到了廣泛的應用，但是當安裝在索的支座附近時，被動阻尼所提供的阻尼性能往往非常有限。而另一方面，半主動和主動式的方法在實驗和理論上都被證明了是更加有效的振動控制方法，但是它們的應用受制於一些長期未能解決的實際問題，在土木工程領域的接受度目前還很有限。但仔細觀察半主動和主動的阻尼器所產生的滯回特性會發現非常明顯的負剛度特性，因此這一發現激勵人們去尋找一種具有負剛度特性的純被動式的阻尼器。但遺憾的是，迄今為止，還沒有任何基於被動式負剛度阻尼器在斜拉索振動控制中的相關研究的報導。而其中的主要困難在於目前大多數被動式負剛度阻尼器的原理過於複雜或者體積過於龐大，很難直接應用到橋樑的斜拉索上。 本項目的申請人，發明了一種全新的被動式磁性負剛度阻尼器。這個新型負剛度阻尼器的原理在本項目的申請書中做了詳盡的闡述，相關概念是首次被提出。它把負剛度和電渦流阻尼有效的結合在簡單緊湊的構造設計中，製造和安裝都非常簡便。本項目將對基於負剛度阻尼器的斜拉索振動控制進行全面的研究。預計這種負剛度阻尼器可以達到與主動、半主動阻尼器非常接近的控制性能。申請人已經進行了初步實驗並成功驗證了所提出的磁式負剛度概念。而在斜拉索振動控制的應用中，從機理、模擬、設計方法到實驗驗證等諸多實際問題，目前仍沒有解決。本項目的主要目的，就是通過系列的理論與實驗研究，來填補這方面的知識空白。研究的內容涵蓋了阻尼器的測試與模擬、針對斜拉索振動控制的阻尼器的優化設計、阻尼器控制效果與實用性的實驗評估等等。

15222214.label: Realisation of objectives
15222214.value: This project investigated a novel negative-stiffness damper (NSD) for vibration suppressions of stay cables. The proposed six objectives have been fully achieved during the 3.5-year project period. The significant achievements of this completed project include: 1. Two different configurations of NSDs, both composed of permanent magnets and conductive pipes, were designed, fabricated, and experimentally tested. [Objective 1] 2. The numerical model of NSD was developed, including the modeling of magnetic force and eddy-current damping forces. [Objective 2] 3. The effects of critical design parameters of NSDs were evaluated based on the experimental testing and numerical model. Subsequently, the optimal design of NSDs was formulated with respect to the damping density and stiffness density. [Objective 1 and Objective 7] 4. The dynamic behavior of a taut cable with an NSD was investigated analytically and numerically. The benefits of an NSD in stay cable vibration suppression were theoretically explained. [Objective 3] 5. The optimal combination of the damping and negative stiffness coefficients of the NSD was derived to maximize the damping performance of the NSD in stay cable vibration suppression. [Objective 3] 6. A series of laboratory experiments were conducted on a scaled stay cable with the NSD of different designs parameters. [Objective 4] 7. The superior performance of NSDs was successfully illustrated through the systematic numerical and experimental studies. [Objective 5] 8. The control performance of the passive NSD was compared with the existing active control techniques. The pros and cons of the developed NSDs were evaluated through the performance comparison. [Objective 6] 9. The proposed NSD was applied to a field test of a full-scale stay cable to further evaluate its practical control performance. [Objective 6]

15222214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222214.value: The major findings and outcome of this project include: (1) Two innovative designs of NSD have been proposed, fabricated, and tested. The testing results demonstrated that they can successfully offer the expected negative stiffness behavior. Compared with the conventional NSD, the magnetic NSDs efficiently integrate the negative stiffness and eddy-current damping in a simple and compact configuration, which make them suitable for various applications in structural vibration suppression or isolation. [Research Output: Journal Paper 2, Patent 1] (2) The modeling of the proposed magnetic NSDs was successfully conducted using the Coulombian model. The modeling results agree with the testing results very well, thus validating the effectiveness of the developed model. Subsequently, the optimal design of NSDs with respect to the damping and stiffness densities was formulated to improve the efficiency of the NSDs and facilitate the future adoption by engineers. [Research Output: Journal Paper 4] (3) The dynamic behavior of a stay cable with an NSD close to one end was investigated analytically and numerically. The results clearly indicate that NSD can achieve a significantly higher damping level than traditional viscous dampers. The vibration of stay cables can be better suppressed by NSD. [Research Output: Journal Paper 3] (4) The optimal combination of negative stiffness and damping coefficients was obtained through the numerical solution. The deficiency of asymptotic solution in predicting the performance of NSD has been pointed out. The benefit of the NSD was theoretically explained. In addition, the potential stability problem of NSD installed on a stay cable has been discussed, and the stability boundary has been derived and its physical meaning was explained. [Research Output: Journal Paper 3] (5) A series of dynamic experiments on a scaled stay cable with an NSD was conducted in the laboratory to evaluate the vibration suppression performance of NSD. Experimental results indicate that the passive NSD performed much more effectively than conventional viscous dampers in mitigating the vibration of the stay cable. As the negative stiffness strength increased, the cable responses under various dynamic loadings became smaller, thus indicating that high damping had been added to the stay cable. A damping ratio higher than 10% was obtained in the cable vibration tests. Numerical simulation results taking account of the flexural rigidity and boundary conditions agreed well with the experimental results [Research Output: Journal Paper 5] (6) A systematic comparison between passive NSDs and active control in cable vibration mitigation was conducted, in which two active control methods, namely, linear quadratic regulator (LQR) and output feedback control, were considered. The comparison indicates that a passive NSD can offer a stay cable with a high damping level comparable to that of LQR control. The NSD is regarded as more practical and reliable because it offers protection by completely passive means without the need for the feedback and actuation that are required in active control. [Research Output: Journal Paper 6] (7) The impact of nonlinearity in NSD on the vibration control performance for stay cables was investigated. A linearization method based on energy equivalent principle was proposed, and subsequently, the impact of two types of nonlinear stiffness, namely, displacement hardening and softening stiffness, was evaluated. The Hilbert transform analysis results validate the accuracy of the linearization method. [Research Output: Journal Paper 7] (8) Some other interesting applications were also explored, including an inerter damper for cable vibration mitigation, where the inerter damper shows very similar behavior to an NSD, and the integration of vibration control and energy harvesting functions in stay cable tests. [Research Output: Journal Papers 1 and 8]

15222214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222214.value: Further improvement of this research will be conducted in the following aspects: 1. The application of NSDs to full-scale stay cables will be explored. 2. The improved NSD design will be developed to further enhance the efficiency.

15222214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222214.value: An increasing number of long-span cable-stayed bridges are constructed worldwide because of their structural, economic, and aesthetic merits. However, stay cables are often susceptible to excessive vibration because of their flexibility and low levels of inherent damping. These problematic oscillations may lead to undue stress and fatigue failure in the cables or their anchors, and are detrimental to the long-term serviceability and safety of an entire bridge. This project investigated a novel solution for mitigating stay cable vibrations by utilizing the newly invented negative stiffness dampers (NSDs). The systematic research program, including the modeling and testing of NSDs, numerical and experimental studies of stay cables installed with NSDs, has been completed in this project. The research outcome indicated that the passive NSD can achieve a significantly better control performance than traditional viscous fluid dampers. Therefore, NSDs will be a promising device for vibration suppression of stay cables in a large number of cable-stayed bridges.

15300114.label: Project Objectives
15300114.value: We will investigate the behavior of the solution set of the PVIP in a general framework. We will study the solvability, sensitivity, consistency and continuity of the solution set and the smoothing regularization approximations of the PVIP. Moreover, we will provide conditions for convergence of the solution sets of the approximated problems when the smoothing regularization parameters go to zero. We will use new results obtained in part 1 to develop efficient smoothing regularization methods for solving optimization problems with variational inequality constraints. We will establish comprehensive convergence theorems of the algorithms. We will use new results obtained in part 1 to develop smoothing regularization methods for differential variational inequality problems. We will investigate the convergence of various time-stepping methods for solving this problem with smoothing regularization approximation. The convergence is dependent on the behavior of the solution set of the PVIP in a dynamical system. We will apply the new theoretical results and algorithms to estimate the characteristics of a popular demand model in economics, and various transportation problems in large urban networks with researchers in economics and engineering.

15300114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300114.value: The variational inequality problem (VIP) has been used widely in science, engineering and economics as a powerful framework for the modeling of equilibrium problems. The parametric VIP(PVIP) is concerned with the study of the behavior of the solution set of the VIP when some parameters in the problem are subject to change. The parameters often represent uncertainties, data errors and dynamic scenarios in practical applications. Moreover, the PVIP is involved in many mathematical models as constraints, including optimization problems with variational inequality constraints and differential variational inequality problems. Hence, it is imperative for us to understand the behavior of the solution set of the PVIP. However, little is known about the stability, sensitivity, consistency, continuity and semicontinuity of the solution set of the PVIP where both the given function and set depend on the parameters. The solution set of the PVIP can be discontinuous with respect to the parameters when the function is strongly monotone, because the geometry of the given set varies with the parameter. This distinguishes the problem studied in this project from the PVIP where only the given function depends on the parameters. The aim of this project is to obtain new and significant results on the solution sets of the PVIP where both the given function and set depend on the parameters. These results will be used to develop efficient algorithms for solving mathematical problems that involve the PVIP as constraints. Our approach is to consider the solution sets of the PVIP as a multi-valued mapping defined on certain classes of parameters, and to use several measures of distance between two sets to characterize the behavior of the solution sets. We will use regularization method to define a single-valued solution function, and investigate the behavior of the trajectories defined by the solution function. Moreover, we will reformulate the regularized PVIP as parametric nonsmooth equations or nonsmooth optimization problems, and develop smoothing methods to solve such nonsmooth problems. We will give new convergence theorems of smoothing regularization methods for optimization problems with variational inequality constraints and differential variational inequality problems. We will apply the new theoretical results and algorithms to optimization problems involving set-valued stochastic equilibrium constraints for estimating the characteristics of a popular demand model in economics, and differential variational inequality problems for various transportation problems in large urban networks. The outcome of this project will be significant to optimization theory, algorithms and applications. 作爲均衡問題建模的強大工具，變分不等式問題在科學，工程學和經濟學等領域中被廣泛應用。參數變分不等式（PVIP）研究當變分不等式中一些參數改變時，變分不等式解集的變化情況。在實際應用中，參數通常被表達爲不確定因素，數據誤差和動態實現等。進一步，PVIP在很多數學模型中被當作約束，比如帶變分不等式約束的優化問題、微分變分不等式問題等。因此，研究並理解PVIP中解集的的性質是非常必要的。然而，當變分不等式中所給出的函數和集合都與參數相關時，我們對PVIP解集的穩定性，敏感性，一致性，連續性和半連續性知之甚少。由于所給集合隨參數改變而改變，即便在所給函數是強單調的情況下，PVIP的解集關于參數也可能是不連續的。這使得目前在這個課題上，只有僅當PVIP中所給函數與參數相關的情況得到了研究。本項目的目標是在PVIP中所給函數和集合都與參數相關時，得到新的有意義的結果。這些結果將被用于發展解帶有PVIP約束的數學規劃問題的有效算法。我們將PVIP的解集看做定義在特定參數集合上的多值映射，並采用兩個集合之間的多種距離來描述PVIP解集的變化。我們將采用正則化方法，用單值函數逼近該多值函數，並且研究該單值函數軌迹的變化。進一步，我們將正則化後的PVIP寫爲帶參數的非光滑等式系統或者非光滑優化問題，並且開發相應的光滑化方法去解這樣的非光滑問題。針對帶有變分不等式約束的優化問題和微分變分不等式問題的光滑正則化方法，我們將給出新的收斂性理論。我們將新的理論結果和算法應用到帶集值隨機均衡約束的優化問題和微分變分不等式問題上。這兩個問題將分別應用到估計經濟學上需求模型的性質問題和大規模城市網絡上的一系列交通問題上。本項目的結論將在優化理論、算法和應用上産生重大影響。

15300214.value: 因為其優異的性質和在能源，器件和材料等方面的廣泛應用，石墨烯的研究目前正逐漸成為一個越來越熱門的研究領域。目前製備大面積，高質量石墨烯的最好的方方是氣相沉積法。這一方法到目前為止已經有大量的實驗研究並引起了很多的理論關注。然而由於這一生長石墨烯方法的複雜性，我們對於其生長機制的了解卻非常少，一直與目前大多數的實驗設計是基於經驗判斷的。實驗上發現，石墨烯在生長過程中可能呈現各種各樣的形狀，包括，三角形，四邊形，六邊形，圓形以及分枝狀結構的分形形狀等。為了深入了解石墨烯的生長機制，我們這裡提出研究石墨烯在生長過程中的動力學行為。這一研究將結合第一性原理計算，分子動力學模擬動力學蒙特卡洛模擬的各種多尺度方法進行。在這一研究中，第一性原理方法將被用來計算石墨烯在金屬表面生長的各種關鍵參數；分子動力學模擬將被用來模擬石墨烯的成核過程和尺寸較小石墨烯籌的生長過程；動力學蒙特卡洛模擬將被用來模擬大尺度石墨烯生長的動力學過程，包括形狀演化等。這一研究的成功將會使我們對石墨烯生長的機制有深入的了解並我實驗上進一步合成均勻的，大面積，高質量石墨烯提供理論指導。同時，這一研究的成功也將為我們對二維晶體的外延生長的研究提供理論工具。

15300414.label: Project Objectives
15300414.value: To grow various types of electron-pinned defect-dipole-induced colossal permittivity (CP) thin films. To characterize structural, dielectric and electrical properties of the grown CP thin films. To establish a comprehensive understanding on the thin-film synthesis process, resultant structural properties and their relations with CP behaviors. To design and fabricate CP thin-film capacitors exhibiting stable CP>10,000 and low tanδ. The performances of the thin-film capacitors will be superior to the current state-of-art results from existing thin-film dielectrics.

15300414.label: Realisation of objectives
15300414.value: 1. In order to achieve the project objective 1, first we have designed a variety of electron-pinned defect-dipole-induced colossal permittivity (CP) ceramic targets. Then we employed pulsed laser deposition (PLD) technique to grow CP thin films. As a typical example, the ceramics were prepared using a conventional solid state reaction method. A proportionate amount of starting materials of ZnO, Nb2O5, and TiO2 with analytical grade purity was weighted according to the stoichiometry of (Zn1/3Nb2/3)0.05Ti0.95O2. The ceramics were fabricated by ball milling, calcinations, pressing, and sintering. Thin films were deposited by PLD on Pt/Si substrates with an operation wavelength of KrF (λ = 248 nm). Thin film deposition was made at substrate temperature below 300 ˚C in a dynamic oxygen atmosphere (2 Pa) with a laser energy density of about 2 J cm-2. Film thickness was about 700 nm estimated from the laser pulses and the deposition rate, which could be further confirmed by the cross sectional analysis of scan electron microscopy (SEM). Amorphous films were crystallized by RTA (Hefei Kejing OTF-1200X-4-RTP) treatment at 600 1C for 1 min with a heating rate of 30 ˚C s-1 under a N2 atmosphere. Furthermore, we grow CP co-doped TiO2/polymer composite films for the first time. The novel CP ceramic/polymer composite films were prepared by combining solution casting and hot-pressing (HP) processes. The poly(vinylidene fluoride trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) 55/45 mol% copolymer was utilized as matrix. The sintered ceramic powders were dispersed in an aqueous solution of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2, 35% w/v, Acros Organics) with stirring and heating at 100 ˚C for 3 h. The suspensions were subsequently centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 5 min. The collected powders were washed with distilled water and ethanol. Finally, surface hydroxylated ceramic powders (2.5% (Er + Nb)–OH) were obtained by drying overnight at 70 ˚C in an oven. P(VDF-TrFE) 55/45 mol% copolymer powders purchased from Piezotech were utilized as the matrix. To begin with, P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer powders were dissolved in a dimethylformamide (DMF) to obtain a solution with 10 wt% concentration. Different weight ratios of 2.5% (Er + Nb)–OH were ultrasonically dispersed in DMF and then introduced into P(VDF-TrFE) solution with constantly stirring at 50 ˚C for 8 h and sonicated for about 30 min to form stable suspensions. As-deposited composite film was subsequently dried on a hotplate at 70 ˚C. The film was annealed at 120 ˚C overnight in an oven and then allowed to cool to room temperature. To improve the uniformity, the solution-cast film was then hot-pressed at 200 ˚C for 10 min. Gold layers were deposited on the films by sputtering to serve as electrode layers for electrical measurements. The above results have been published in international journals, including J. Mater. Chem. C and RSC Adv.. 2. To achieve the objective 2, an X-ray diffractometer (XRD) (Rigaku, SmartLab) was employed to analyze the crystalline structure. The Bruker Vertex-70 Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrophotometer, field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) were used for material morphology and crystal structure characterization. The vibrational properties of samples were characterized by Raman spectroscopy (HORIBA, HR800) excited by 488 nm laser with a spot size of about 1 mm. The valence states of elements in the samples were analyzed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) on the system of a Thermo SCIENTIFIC ESCALAB 250Xi (Escalab 250Xi; Thermo Scientific, Leicestershire, UK). A monochromatic aluminum Kα radiation source with energy of 1486.8 eV was used in the system. The dielectric behaviors of the capacitors were measured using an Impedance Analyzer (Agilent E4980A) from 100 to 2 MHz as a function of frequency. A high voltage power supply (model P0621, TREK, Inc.) was used for the breakdown strength measurement. All samples were kept inside a 400 mL beaker filled with silicon oil to limit moisture influence on testing results and sparking while applying high voltage. The temperature dependence of the dielectric properties was measured by equiping with a temperature-controlled probe stage. 3. To achieve the objective 3, we investigated the mechanism of the observed CP performance, and a series of compositional, structural and dielectric analyses of the samples were conducted. The general relationship between larger ionic radii of the acceptor ion and the presence or the absence of a defect dipole effect are studied. We investigated the difference in ionic radius that can affect the formation of defect dipole clusters as well as the overall CP dielectric properties. The presence of structural secondary phases at the grain boundary was also observed, which is relevant to the observed CP behaviors. Synthesis optimization, structural analysis, characterization of the dielectric properties and energy storage density are systematically investigated in the CP materials. The relevant results are published in the journal of Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys and others. In order to investigate the underlying mechanism regarding electron-pinned defect-dipoles, the dielectric properties of amorphous and anatase Zn,Nb co-doped TiO2 CP thin films were further investigated. For the samples deposited at 150 ˚C and room temperature, the comparisons in the aspects of structure, dielectric permittivity and loss as a function of frequency are performed. For the CP composite films, the surface morphology of HP and without HP synthesis of composite film is measured, revealing that HP method could decrease the defects such as voids in the composite films. The effects of surface hydroxylation of ceramic filers and film layers on the electric breakdown strength and dielectric properties of the samples are investigated. The related works are published in J. Mater. Chem. C and RSC Adv.. 4. To achieve the objective 4, we constructed parallel-plate capacitors to measure dielectric and electrical properties. The ceramics were pasted with silver on both sides. For fabricating CP thin-film capacitors, a top Au electrode with a radius of 100 micrometer was covered on the CP thin films with a shadow mask and deposited by thermal evaporation. In addition, we also designed and fabricated insulator/semiconductor/insulator multilayer capacitors. Ag electrodes were prepared on both sides of the TiO2 by magnetron sputtering in Ar atmosphere (40 sccm) for 5 min. The sputtering power is 40 W and the pressure of Ar atmosphere was 1 Pa during the sputtering process. Dielectric studies show that the maximum dielectric permittivity (~ 30,000) of our prepared samples is about 100 times higher than that (~ 300) of conventional TiO2. The minimum dielectric loss is 0.03 (at 10000–100000 Hz). Furthermore, CP is almost independent of the frequency (100–1000000 Hz) and the temperature (20–350 K). The performances are superior to the current state-of-art results from existing thin-film dielectrics.

15300414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300414.value: 1. We are the first team to grow electron-pinned defect-dipole-induced CP thin films by PLD technique. Novel CP properties are studied in CP films with different phase structures. Compared with the amorphous thin films, the annealed anatase ones exhibited a simultaneous increase in both dielectric permittivity and loss. These findings suggest that co-doping with various phase structures can yield CP effects. CP properties are mainly attributed to the effect of the electron-pinned defect-dipoles in co-doped TiO2 rather than grain boundary effect. Frequency and bias dependent dielectric behaviors are also observed in thin-films affected by the electrode-film interface and mobile ions. (see: Part C: Journal 1,3, 8, Conference 1,2) 2. We achieved CP co-doped TiO2/polymer composite films for the first time. We found that CP ceramic/polymer composite films can be achieved by combining solution casting and HP processes. We found that high-performance of dielectric capacitors simultaneously possessing large dielectric constant, negligible dielectric loss and acceptable breakdown electric field can be successfully achieved in the flexible composite films. (see: Part C: Journal 4,9 Conference: 4,5). 3. Through employing a range of dopants into TiO2, we found that the radius, valence, and electronic shell structure of doping ions should play important roles in CP effects. The two types of defect clusters can be correlated/overlapped together. Thus, the high CP and low dielectric loss could be acquired under the mechanism of large defect-dipole clusters with the highly localized electrons. (see: Part C: Journal 5,6,7, Conference: 3,4). 4. In addition to the CP properties, we first found that the up/downconversion photoluminescence from the CP materials. Dielectric measurements indicate that the fabricated materials simultaneously present CP properties with relatively low dielectric loss. (see: Part C: Journal 2, 3,10, Conference: 3) 5. Regarding the research output, we have published 9 SCI journal papers with acknowledgements of this project. The PI collaborated with the Co-I and we have co-authored two papers published in international journals. One postgraduate student Mei-Yan Tse has been under training during this period. The postgraduate student was awarded degree and she has published 3 journal papers as the first author and others as co-author. She presented her results in international conference. The PI has given keynote/invited talks in several international conferences. Our research wins TechConnect “Global Innovation Awards” 2018 in US. One provisional US patent was filed.

15300414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300414.value: Our work may pave the way for developing highly stable and superior dielectrics through a simple and scalable route to meet requirements of further miniaturization in microelectronic and energy-storage devices. The interfacial effect of the thin-films needs to be further studied in detail for fabricating practical devices with further enhanced performances. Due to the existence of the link between defect/local states and mixed cation valences in complex oxides, this study could be extended to more oxide-based material systems in the future. We presented that the solution casting offers opportunity for high reliability and low cost manufacturing, while HP method reduces voids and other structural defects. Multi-layered capacitors based on our process can be further developed, which are superior to conventional electrochemical construction in many aspects including high power density and improved safety. Enhancing energy storage density is a major issue in developing fully solid-state capacitor system. Our work demonstrates the coexistence of both interesting luminescence and attractive dielectric characteristics, showing the potential for multifunctional applications. Along the research direction, further development includes designing and fabricating proof-of concept devices fully utilizing dielectric and optical characteristics of CP thin films and heterostructures through stacking these CP materials.

15300414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300414.value: Design and fabrication of colossal permittivity (CP) thin films achieved in this project are of significant importance, both scientifically and technologically. Our results would be a step towards further fundamental understanding and applications of the CP materials. In this research project, various routes to synthesize electron-pinned defect-dipole induced CP thin films and multilayer structures are proposed and realized. We have made efforts to carry out a series of compositional, structural and dielectric analyses of the CP samples. A variety of CP thin-film capacitors are designed and fabricated, which are useful for further development in practical applications. We have addressed some fundamental issues in dielectric materials science by considering the existence of the link between defect/local states and mixed cation valences in complex oxides. New insights into CP mechanism are provided, leading to an improved understanding of the CP material. Our works are helpful for not only investigating the new class of colossal permittivity materials, but also developing dielectric thin film device application. The results achieved in this project may pave the way for developing highly stable and superior dielectrics through a simple and scalable route to meet requirements of further miniaturization in microelectronic and energy-storage devices.

15300514.label: Project Objectives
15300514.value: To introduce and formulate the stochastic control problems for backward and forward-backward large-population systems (BLP and FBLP). In particular, in their linear-quadratic (LQ) cases. To develop the forward-backward large-population (FBLP) control theory in a systematical way. To develop the backward large-population (BLP) control theory in a systematical way. To apply the theoretical results of BLP and FBLP, based on (2) and (3), to some practical problems.

15300514.label: Realisation of objectives
15300514.value: In this project, we have some progressive research activities and realize all objective as stated in proposal. More details are listed as follows. 1. To introduce and formulate the stochastic control problems for backward and forward-backward large-population systems (BLP and FBLP). In particular, in their linear-quadratic (LQ) cases. For objective 1 above, we first introduce the backward and forward-backward mean-field game (MFG) with some financial and economics backgrounds, more particularly, the multi-agent portfolio selection with relative performance for backward MFG, and Habit formation for production planning in competitive market economy. As to objective 1, we also formulate the backward large population (BLP) system, and forward-backward large-population (FBLP) system, in the linear-quadratic case. We also carefully exam in such LQ case, which part is needed to have coupling, and which part not. We both consider the theoretical investigation and practical application concerns. 2. To develop the forward-backward large-population (FBLP) control theory in a systematical way. For objective 2 above, we study the FBLP with more systematic manner. We study the auxiliary control of FBSDE system with maximum principle, and derive the related Hamiltonian system. Then, we apply the consistency condition to derive one asymmetric Hamiltonian system for MFG scheme of our FBLP. We also verify the related near Nash equilibrium with some FBSDE estimate. Such estimate are very different to that of standard forward system. 3. To develop the backward large-population (BLP) control theory in a systematical way. Based on results on objective 2, we continue to study the BLP control. Note that in BLP system, there has only backward state, without the forward state involved, thus its LP procedure is also very different to FBLP above. We proceed the control and consistency condition with backward SDE estimate. More important, we apply some new method to treat the second solution component (it is also called adjust solution component). To this end, some new estimate for BLP system is deviced and applied. Some modified BSDE estimates are also proposed to this end. 4. To apply the theoretical results of BLP and FBLP, based on (2) and (3), to some practical problems. For objective 4, we apply the results from objective 1-3 to some real financial and economics applications. We study the relative performance with BLP formulation, and apply it to some pension fund investment problems. Such problems arise from insurance problem, and we investigate also its comparison with other portfolio strategies. We also connect it to some forward linear quadratic with some future target. This implies some interesting connections with quadratic hedging problems.

15300514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300514.value: (1) The BLP and FBLP control are solved to substantial extent, the related MFG solutions are derived and related near Nash equilibrium are also verified. (2) The connection between forward LP control and FBLP are discussed, and some new connection between these two problems are revealed. We also get some connection between backward LP and forward LP with som terminal constraint. (3) The related Nash equilibriums and their comparisons are also carefully examined. We also have some effective simulation to such comparisons, and highlight some real insights. (4) We also device some new criteria to solvability of related asymmetric fully-coupled FBSDE system. Some novel but useful FBSDE prior estimates are also derived. Such estimates should have its own rights in other stochastic control fields.

15300514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300514.value: Our project carried out implies some future research directions and potential as follows: (1) It is important to have more technical treatment to the fully-coupled FBSDE system arise, in particular, we can apply some new well-posedness condition to check its solvability. For example, the reduction method or second type bridge method, or some transform method between different FBSDE systems. (2) It is an interesting potential to study the BLP and FBLP in more complex manner such as leader-follower BLP or FBLP problems. Such problems have interesting and appealing economic explanations. (3) It is also a good potential to study the BLP and FBLP with cooperation or social optimal pattern, and compare its results for competitive Nash equilibrium in current project.

15300514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300514.value: We study the stochastic control for large population (LP) system with focus on backward and forward-backward systems. Unlike the classical forward LP system with forward state given initial condition only, the backward or forward-backward system are given the ``terminal" (or, final) condition instead (or, together with) the forward state. The backward and forward-backward LP system (for short, BLP, FBLP) arise naturally from various important and interesting real applications. Thus, its LP control has also important values in academic and practical aspects. However, because the specified ``terminal" condition, the structure and related control method for BLP and FBLP is very different to that of forward system, and many technical difficulties arise, in particular, when dealing with the fully-coupled FBSDE system. We overcome such difficulties to some substantial extent and the derived results have important application potential as well.

15300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300814.value: 催化交叉偶聯過程中已成為最直接和廣泛使用的化學修飾組裝結構，在物質和藥物有吸引力的化合物。事實上，這些方法已經徹底改變了化學家的方式來執行複雜的有機合成。在中心處的這些合成技術，催化劑的開發，允許選擇性的鍵的裂解/ - 工程用相對不反應，但豐富的原料的性質部件將是非常有吸引力的。因此，催化劑的探索和發展，特別是對現代催化研究創新有機合成。 惰性拆建（Ar-O）在芳醚鍵的有效裂解一直是長期存在的挑戰和未解決的合成問題。然而，苯甲醚是通用的芳烴源的性質，這將是對交叉耦合及相關芳基化過程中非常有吸引力。為了滿足對綠色化學合成，我們的目標是合理設計的可調配體/催化劑，將激活惰性C-O鍵，實現區域專一性鍵形成。當然，催化劑應使高效（要求低催化劑載量）和高效（可以迎合特定鍵形成反應）。基礎知識，從催化劑的開發，而這些配體的各種應用的過程中獲得，將是為追求高學術上的興趣和潛在的工業應用價值。 芳香施工方法的新發展將推動當前的耦合過程，並提出了催化研究。這個項目的目的是：（1）合理設計和使用簡便的交叉組合的方式探索出一條新的類高度可調的催化劑/配體; （2）探索新的和通用的耦合夥伴在這種類型的反應; （3）研究這些新工藝的基本機制; （4）來實現這種催化劑體系的木質素C（Ar）的 - O鍵斷裂的可能性。 該項目預計將探索交叉偶聯反應的新領域。所提出的研究是基於我們以前的成功，在配體/催化劑的設計，合成，以及我們在芳香建設的研究豐富經驗。

15300814.label: Realisation of objectives
15300814.value: This is the completion report of project 153008/14P. This project had gone through the period of 1-Jan-2015 to 31-Dec-2017. The PI moved from The Hong Kong Polytechnic University to The Chinese University of Hong Kong on 1-March-2017, and started to setting up the new laboratory in Department of Chemistry. With regard to the realisation of objectives, we have accomplished the goal of the proposed works. We designed the new class of highly tunable ligands using simple synthetic approaches. The corresponding outcomes were published in SCI peer-reviewed journals (Organic Letters, 2015, 17, 4612; Organic Syntheses, 2015, 92, 195; Organometallics, 2016, 35, 1553; Organic Chemistry Frontiers, 2016, 273). Having the newly developed catalyst systems, we explored the new/versatile cross coupling partners. We were able to show the highly selective mono-alpha-arylation of heteroarylketones using versatile ketones and aryl mesylates as the coupling partners. Moreover, we also achieved the regioselective phosphorylation using simple and readily available reagents. These workdone were published in peer -reviewed journals (Organic Letters, 2015, 17, 5906; Organic Letters, 2016, 18, 1872). On the area of fundamental mechanistic study, we attempted to use Hiyama cross-coupling as the prototypical example. We found that in this reaction, the water (or the acid) additive was highly essential in facilitating the intended cross-coupling. With the aid of water, a more general palladium-catalyzed Hiyama cross-coupling was realized. It should be noted that the first examples of tri-ortho-substituted biaryls were accessed from this strategy. This workdone was published in Chemistry A European Journal, 2016, 22, 6471. Moreover, this finding was highlighted by the back-cover art of this journal (Chemistry A European Journal, 2016, 22, 6695). In addition to this investigation, we also try to use more naturally available alkyl ether as the typical natural examples. We interesting found that the cyclic ethers were able to cross-couple with indole using atom economical dehydrogenative C(sp3)-H/C(sp2)-H coupling. This ground work was published in Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry, 2016, 14, 2608. Overall, we have accomplished the goal of the proposed investigations. The findings were recognized by the SCI peer-reviewed journals, as attached.

15300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300814.value: The major findings of the proposed investigations were the development of new class of phosphine ligands which allowed the previously problematic reactions to be realized successfully. In addition, the new/versatile cross-coupling partners were probed, as the new opportunity to established more effective synthetic methods. The major research outcome have been published in SCI peer-reviewed journals, and as the detail below We rationally designed and synthesized new phosphine ligands for highly mono-selective alpha arylation of acetone, a highly useful 3-carbon feedstock. We the tunable electronic property, we were able to switch the rate-limiting-step from reductive elimination to oxidative addition. The substrate scope was fully extended to electron-deficient arenes without deleterious effects. This major finding was published in (Organic Letters, 2015, 17, 4612). In addition, the more general and reliable synthesis (in large scale) of the ligands was published in (Organic Syntheses, 2015, 92, 195). With the solid groudwork of these phosphine ligands, we further developed a new series of P,N mixed donor ligands using facile and modular synthetic approach. The corresponding P,N-palladium complex (after the oxidative addition of 4-chlorotoluene) was grown, and characterized using single crystal X-ray analysis. This research outcome was published in (Organometallics, 2016, 35, 1553). In deriving this P,N-type ligand, the corresponding analog showed exceedingly high reactivity in promoting difficult tetra-ortho-substituted biaryl syntheses. This workdone was published in (Organic Chemistry Frontiers, 2016, 3, 273). To explore versatile/new cross coupling partners/reagents, we attempted to tackle the difficult C-P bond formation, as the resulting products would render the palladium complex coordinative saturated. With the use of indolylphosphine ligand, the first examples of cross-coupling of aryl mesylates with H-PR2 partners were realized. This finding was published in (Organic Letters, 2015, 17, 5906). Moreover, we explored the possibility in using the heteroarylketones as the versatile reagents for selective arylation, under palladium catalysis. This work was published in (Organic Letters, 2016, 18, 1872). Regarding the new commonly available cross-coupling partner, we found that the use of cyclic ethers were able to cross-coupling with indole core using dehydrogenative strategy. This research outcome was published in (Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry 2016, 14, 2608). During the course of mechanistic study, we interesting found that the use of water (or acid) additive facilitated the Hiyama cross-coupling reaction. With this new catalyst system, the first tri-ortho-substituted biaryl synthesis using aryl siloxanes was realized. This major finding was published in (Chemistry A European Journal, 2016, 6471). Particularly noteworthy is that this work was also highlighted by the journal editor as the "HOT PAPER", and displayed as the back-cover art (Chemistry A European Journal, 2016, 6695).

15300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300814.value: The aforementioned finding showed potential in further design and developing new phosphine ligands, which are able to tackle the specific window of difficult or unexplored cross-coupling reaction (or the corresponding coupling partners). In this regard, this finding serves as essential ground work in upgrading new synthetic strategy.

15300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300814.value: New way of assembling organic molecule is highly significant in central science for pharmaceutical, agricultural and material applications. With the design of new simple catalyst, the new architecture of organic molecules become viable. The new catalyst systems certainly allow the facile access to those useful organic frameworks, in a straightforward and atom-economical manner.

15301014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301014.value: Polymer films are widely used in electronic packaging, lubrication, and adhesives for micro-fabrications. As technology advances, ever thinner films are employed. It was first found nearly two decades ago that the glass transition temperature, Tg, of polymer films with thickness in the nanometer range can be different from that of the bulk. Those results imply that a polymer can turn from a glassy solid into a liquid upon confinement in a nanometer thin film geometry. A better understanding of the thin film confinement effects is not only of academic interest, but also technological importance. We propose to conduct computer simulations to study the detailed dynamical properties of polymer nanofilms at the molecular level. Much attention will be given to the confinement effects as revealed in their viscosity measured from driven flow under the influence of an applied uniform external force. Molecular motions at equilibrium or supercooled conditions will also be studied. A liquid-like surface layer with an enhanced flow mobility have been found to exist on the free surface of short-chain unentangled polymer films. We aim at a better understanding of its origin and the associated transport mechanism. In recent simulations, we observed a surface mobile layer exhibiting a velocity profile that decays exponentially from the free surface, in contrast to the usual parabolic profile for uniform films of simple liquids. We will study the temperature dependence of this profile and relate it the to local dynamical time scale of the microscopic motions in the film. The flow of thin films of long-chain entangled polymer will also be studied with an emphasis on the film substrate interaction. Moreover, we will examine a wider range of detailed structures and local rigidity of the polymer chains with the possibility of added impurities in order to identify the structural and thermodynamic factors which have the stronger impacts on the confinement effects.

15301014.label: Realisation of objectives
15301014.value: Thermally activated flow dynamics of polystyrene nanometer thin films supported by silicon have been studied for a wide range of film thickness and molecular weights (Mw). At low Mw, the effective viscosity of the films is smaller than the bulk and decreases with decreasing film thickness. This is due to enhancement of the total shear flow by the augmented mobility at the free surface. As Mw increases, with thickness becoming smaller than the polymer radius of gyration, the effective viscosity switches from being substrate-independent to substrate-dependent. Based on observations from extensive molecular dynamics studies, we propose that interfacial slippage then dominates and leads to plug flow. The friction coefficient is found to decrease for very thin films, demonstrating a surface-promoted confinement effect. In addition, we have measured the effective viscosity of polystyrene films with a small added amount of dioctyl phthalate (DOP). Our result shows that at small Mw, the addition of DOP causes the effective viscosity to decrease. But for higher Mw, the effective viscosity is relatively unchanged. A model assuming the effective viscosity to be dominated by enhanced surface mobility for the lower Mw films but surface-promoted interfacial slippage for the higher Mw films is able to account for the observations. The dynamics of many glassy systems are known to exhibit string-like hopping motions each consisting of a line of particles displacing one another. By using molecular dynamics simulations of glassy polymers, we show that these motions become highly repetitive back-and-forth motions as temperature decreases and do not necessarily contribute to net displacements. Particle hops which constitute string-like motions are reversed with a high probability, reaching 73 percent and beyond at low temperature. Structural relaxation rate is then dictated not by a simple particle hopping rate but instead by the rate at which particles break away from hopping repetitions. These repetitions slow down the dynamics in glass and contribute significantly to kinetic arrest. They are also proposed to be the main contributor of the non-Arrhenius behavior of glass. We observe that disruption of string repetitions and hence also structural relaxations are brought about by pair-interactions between strings. We have studied hopping repetitions in both bulk and film geometries. At a free film surface, string repetitions are found to be significantly reduced and this explains the restoration of Arrhenius behaviors observed previously in experiments. We have proposed an interacting lattice gas model of structural glass characterized by particle distinguishability and site-particle-dependent random nearest-neighboring particle interactions. This incorporates disorder quenched in the configuration space rather than in the physical space. The model exhibits non-trivial energetics while still admitting exact equilibrium states directly constructible at arbitrary temperature and density. The dynamics is defined by activated hopping following standard kinetic Monte Carlo approach without explicit facilitation rule. Kinetic simulations show emergent dynamic facilitation behaviors in the glassy phase in which motions of individual voids are significant only when accelerated by other voids nearby. This provides a microscopic justification for the dynamic facilitation picture of structural glass. In addition, the fragility characterizing the deviation from Arrhenius behavior is highly tunable and is found to depend on the distribution of the quenched noise in the particle interactions. We have derived a microscopic theory of glassy dynamics based on the transport of voids by micro-string motions, each of which involves particles arranged in a line hopping simultaneously displacing one another. Disorder is modeled by a random energy landscape transient in the physical space but quenched in the configuration space of distinguishable particles. We study the evolution of local regions with m coupled voids. At low temperature, energetically accessible local particle configurations can be organized into a random tree with nodes and edges denoting configurations and micro-string propagations respectively. A micro-string propagation initiated by a void is shown to facilitate similar motions by other voids via perturbing the random energy landscape. Dynamics is dominated by coupled voids of an optimal group size, which increases as temperature decreases. We obtain explicit expressions of the particle diffusion coefficient and a particle return probability, which describe glassy behaviors at low temperature and small void density. Comparison with our lattice model of glass shows very good quantitative agreements using only two adjustable parameters related to typical energy fluctuations and the interaction range of the micro-strings.

15301014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301014.value: Using polystyrene as a prototypical example, unentangled polymer thin films are shown to exhibit thermally activated flow dynamics dictated by a reduced polymer viscosity confirming previous observations. In contrast, entangled polymer films at high molecular weights show dynamics dominated by interfacial slippage which results at plug flow. The friction coefficient is found to decrease for very thin films, demonstrating a related surface-promoted confinement effect (see publication 1). This transition of the flow limiting mechanism is further confirmed by adding impurities to the polymer which alter only the polymer viscosity by not the interfacial friction (see publication 2). We have shown in polymer dynamic simulations that microscopic particle motions in glassy systems become highly repetitive back-and-forth hopping motions as temperature decreases and do not necessarily contribute to net displacements. Particle hops are reversed with a high probability, reaching 73 percent and beyond at low temperature. This causes the dynamic slowdown characterizing glasses (see publication 4). Geometries of polymer chains under confinement effects in film or tube geometry are also studied (see publication 3). To illustrate and to further study the hopping repetition dynamics in generic glassy systems, we have proposed an interacting lattice gas model of structural glass characterized by particle distinguishability and site-particle-dependent random nearest-neighboring particle interactions. This incorporates disorder quenched in the configuration space rather than in the physical space. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of the model demonstrate typical glassy behaviors, hopping repetition at low temperature, and a dynamical facilitation picture of glassy dynamics (see publication 5). We have further derived a microscopic theory of glassy dynamics based on the transport of voids by micro-string motions. Disorder is modeled by a random energy landscape transient in the physical space but quenched in the configuration space of distinguishable particles. We obtain explicit expressions of the particle diffusion coefficient and related quantities which agree with our lattice model simulations for a wide range of temperature and density using only two tunable parameters (see publication 6).

15301014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301014.value: The highly repetitive property of the particle hopping motions is of high relevance in understanding glassy dynamics. This will be further investigated both using molecular dynamics simulations in a new GRF project and using glassy colloidal experiments in a new project proposal. The type of disordered quenched in the configuration space but not in the physical space as implemented in our lattice model of glass are now further studied analytically using the replica method in collaboration with other experts in the field and this may lead to further research projects.

15301014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301014.value: Thin polymer films on solid substrates flow spontaneously due to thermal activations. For long-chain polymers in the glassy state, we observe dynamics limited mainly by frictional interactions with the substrates. The frictional force is weaker for thinner films demonstrating a new thin-film confinement effect. These understandings are of direct relevance to technological applications of glassy polymer nanofilms. Materials in the glassy state are known to exhibit very slow dynamics at low temperature characterized by intermittent microscopic particle hopping motions. We observe highly repetitive back-and-forth particle hopping motions which we suggest as the main factor of the dynamic slowdown. The repetitive nature of the motions is due to trapping of particles in a rugged potential energy landscape with random energies depending of the local configurations of the particles. This is further quantitatively explained using a lattice model of glass and an analytic theory. Our findings contribute to the understanding of the nature of the glassy state of materials.

15301214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301214.value: Quantum dots (QDs), discovered in the 1980s, are semiconductors that contain a size- and shape-dependent band gap. These have been promising structures for applications that range from light emitting diodes, solar cells and lasers to medical imaging devices. The sub-10 nm chemically-derived carbon-based QDs with two-dimensional graphitic planes are called graphene quantum dots (GQDs). GQDs have attracted extensive scientific and technological interest in recent years because of their superior properties such as tunable luminescence, high chemical and optical stability. Most notable is their potential as replacements for toxic metal-based QDs currently in use. The Principle Investigator’s (PI) team has discovered recently that glucose-derived GQDs prepared by a facile microwave-assisted hydrothermal method exhibited broadband emission covering deep ultraviolet, visible to near infrared (from 300 nm to over 900 nm) spectral range. This unique and exciting feature of the GQDs has pointed us to conduct a systematic study on GQDs aiming to unveil its broadband emission mechanism. The study could enable us to develop all-carbon broadband photodetectors with low cost, nontoxicity, high-tunability and high performance. The strong light absorption, excellent solution processibility of GQDs, and the possibility of fine-tuning the electronic structure motivate the integration of GQDs into organic photovoltaics. We will also explore the potential applications of the GQDs in high efficiency photovoltaic devices.

15301214.label: Realisation of objectives
15301214.value: We fabricated nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (N-GQDs) which possess broadband absorption and emission ranging from 300 to >1000 nm (objective 1). The broadband emission is attributed to the layered structure of the N-GQDs that contains a large conjugated system and provides extensive delocalized π electrons (objective 2). The N-GQDs exhibited photoresponse from 365 to 980 nm with responsivity as high as 325 V/W at 405 nm (objective 3). By employing GQDs in PEDOT:PSS, we have achieved an efficiency of 13.22% in Si/PEDOT:PSS hybrid solar cells (Objective 4). The efficiency enhancement is based on concurrent improvement in optical and electrical properties by the photon downconversion process and the improved conductivity of PEDOT:PSS via appropriate incorporation of GQDs. Furthermore, by utilizing GQDs in n-type Si heterojunction solar cells, we have achieved a high efficiency of 16.55% in n-type Si heterojunction solar cells. GQDs were also used to enhance the performance of Pt-free dye-sensitized solar cells.

15301214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301214.value: The broadband emission from the N-GQDs covering 300 to >1000 nm was demonstrated. The broadband optical properties of the N-GQDs are attributed to the layered structure of the N-GQDs which create a large conjugated system containing extensive delocalized π electrons. The deep ultraviolet emission comes from the localized π electron in double bonds. The visible emission is caused by the partial conjugated π electrons in the N-GQDs. As for near-infrared (NIR) emission, the conjugated π electrons in the layered structure of the N-GQDs facilitate the NIR absorption. Furthermore, the N-GQDs exhibited photoresponse from 365 to 980 nm with responsivity as high as 325 V/W at 405 nm. The unique broadband emission and photoresponse of the layered N-GQDs may lead to applications in a wide range of optoelectronic devices including photodetectors, solar cells, and light-emitting devices. The percent doping of nitrogen played a larger role in shifting emission to the red and in enhancing photostability. The properties of the NIR emitting species of nitrogen-doped particles were highly dependent on the percent of dopant. Single particle studies along with steady state fluorescence studies of multiple sizes of undoped and N-doped GQDs suggest either that single particles are not capable of multiple emission bands or that the multiple emissive species observed in bulk samples come from the same particle, but only one emission band is sufficiently bright enough to be observed at the single particle level. We have successfully fabricated Si/PEDOT:PSS hybrid solar cells with an efficiency up to 13.22% by concurrent improvement in optical and electrical properties via the downconversion effect and enhanced conductivity of PEDOT:PSS due to introduction of GQDs. The low-cost, photon-managing, and high-performance device design based on low-temperature solution processes holds the promise for more cost-effective Si-based optical devices. We have synthesized a metal-free composite ink that contains GQDs and PEDOT:PSS that can be used on paper to serve as the counter electrode in a flexible dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC). This paper-based GQD/PEDOT:PSS electrode is low-cost, light-weight, flexible, environmentally friendly, and easy to cut and process for device fabrication.

15301214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301214.value: GQDs have significant potential to enhance the performance of a wide range of solar cells. In general, the conversion efficiency of the solar cells can be enhanced about 10-15% by incorporation of GQDs in the solar cell structures. In the course of the study, we found that the synthesis method of the GQDs using glucose as sole precursor could be extended to prepare large-scale carbon spheres which in turn can be acted as reducing agent for MnO2 ink. The MnO2 ink could be a versatile candidate for large-scale production of flexible and printable electronic devices for energy storage and conversion.

15301214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301214.value: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) have been widely studied in recent years due to its unique structure related properties, such as optical, electrical and optoelectrical properties. Furthermore, GQDs are environmentally friendly due to its non-toxic and biologically inert properties, which have attracted worldwide interests from academic and industry. We have developed a facile technique to prepare GQDs with broadband absorption and emission characteristics. The applications of GQDs in optoelectronic detectors, solar cells and light emitting diodes are encouraging.
