15301414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301414.value: In recent years, lanthanide-doped upconversion nanocrystals (NCs), which emit light at shorter wavelengths than the excitation wavelength, have emerged as excellent alternatives to organic fluorophores and quantum dots for fluorescence bioimaging. Although they have brought about new benefits to bioimaging such as high signal-to-noise ratio and large imaging penetration depth, the quantum efficiency of upconversion NCs is generally much lower than that of conventional counterparts and has become a critical and challenging issue to be tackled. The broad objective of the proposed research is to devise hybrid upconversion nanomaterials, based on hetero-integration of double- or triple-resonant plasmonic gold nanorods and nanobipyramids with lanthanide-doped CaF2 NCs in an arrangement analogous to planet-satellite core-shell configuration. By simultaneously matching the double or triple plasmon resonances of gold nanoparticles with both excitation and desired emission wavelengths of upconversion NCs, we expect to significantly increase the quantum efficiency of such hybrid nanostructures and selectively enhance the luminescence at particular wavelengths; by precisely tuning the separation distance between gold cores and NCs shells, we expect to largely augment plasmonic enhancement effects to be dominant over luminescence quenching. To achieve this aim, we will first study how the upconversion luminescence is affected by gold nanostructures through full-wave numerical calculations, and identify critical geometry parameters such as nanoparticle dimensions and the distance between Au and CaF2. In parallel, our collaborator Prof. Stefan Maier at Imperial College London will employ the sophisticated transformation optics approach to design crescent-shape Au nanoparticles with multiple plasmon resonances, with an expectation of enhancing the upconversion emission in the whole visible spectrum. Advanced synthesis protocols will then be developed to flexibly control the nanostructure geometry in order to realize the desired properties predicted by our theoretical design. Subsequently, comprehensive characterizations combining dark-field scattering spectroscopy and in-situ, steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy will be performed at the single-particle level, aiming at providing a complete scenario for understanding the enhancement mechanisms and further optimizing the structure geometry. At the end of this project, the fabricated hybrids will be used by the research group led by Prof. Xueyuan Chen at Chinese Academy of Sciences for various biological imaging experiments to test the plasmon-enhanced luminescence effect. The obtained results will not only pave the way for enhancing the upconversion efficiency, but also deepen our understanding of nanoscale light-matter interactions, which will also largely facilitate the development of more efficient optoelectronics devices. 最近，鑭族元素摻雜的發光波長短於激發波長的上轉換納米晶體 逐漸成為可以替代熒光生物成像中使用的有機熒光團和量子點的 熒光標記物。盡管他們在生物成像方面具有諸多新的優勢，比如 信噪比高和成像穿透深度大等，這些上轉換納米晶體的量子效率 通常遠遠低於傳統的熒光標記物，成為亟待解決的緊迫且具挑戰 性的問題。本建議研究的整體目標是設計雜化的上轉換納米材料 ，基本原理是把具有雙共振（三共振）的表面等離激元金納米棒 （納米雙錐體）和鑭族元素摻雜的氟化鈣納米晶體以類似於行星 -衛星式的核-殼構型排列方式進行異質集成。通過同時匹配金納 米顆粒的雙重或者三重等離激元共振峰和上轉換納米晶體的激發 與發光波長，我們期望可以顯著提高這種雜化納米結構的量子效 率並且有選擇性地提高特定波長的發光強度；通過精確調控金顆 粒核與納米晶體殼層的分隔距離，我們期望可以使得等離激元增 強效應遠大於熒光淬滅。為此，我們首先使用全波數值模擬方法 來研究金納米結構如何影響上轉換發光，同時確定比如納米顆粒 尺寸以及金與氟化鈣間距等關鍵幾何參數。與此同時，我們的合 作者帝國理工學院的Stefan Maier教授將會利用成熟的變換光學方法來設計具有多重等離激元共振的月牙形金納米顆粒來增強整個可見光波段的上轉換發光效率。基於以上理論結果，我們將會發展先進的合成方法來靈活地控制納米結構構型從而實現理論設計所預測的性質。結合暗場散射和原位，穩態及時間分辨的熒光光譜法將被用來在單顆粒級別上表征合成的雜化納米結構，目標是提供一個完整的圖景來理解增強機理和進一步優化結構構型。最後，我們的合作者中國科學研究院的Xueyuan Chen教授將會把本研究中合成的雜化納米結構用於各種生物成像，從而檢測等離激元共振增強的發光效應。本研究中所取得的結果將不但為增強上轉換效率鋪平道路，同時也會深化我們對納米尺度上光與物質相互作用的理解，這也會在很大程度上促進高效光電子器件的發展。

15301414.label: Realisation of objectives
15301414.value: We have achieved much more than the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities and beyond, with details discussed in the following with respect to the approved revised project objectives. (1) We have successfully carried out theoretical design and numerical calculation of the electromagnetic interaction between an upconversion emitter of three energy levels and a gold nano-rod (GNR), and clearly shown that the nonlinear upconversion luminescence enhancement effect arising from the localized plasmonic near-field-induced absorption may be balanced by the negative effect of electronic transition from an intermediate state to the ground state of the upconversion emitter. We have investigated the dependence of fluorescence enhancement factor on the emitter-GNR separation, and we have found a maximum enhancement factor of 120 folds and 160 folds at upconversion emission wavelengths of 650 and 540 nm, respectively. Such maximum enhancement factors are achieved at the emitter-GNR separation ranging from 5 to 15 nm, depending on the initial quantum efficiency of the upconversion emitter. The modified upconversion luminescence property by adjusting the aspect ratio of the GNR and the relative position of the emitter indicates the dominate role of excitation process in the total upconversion luminescence enhancement. These findings are of great importance for rationally designing composite nanostructures of metal nanoparticles and upconversion nanocrystals with maximized plasmonic enhancement for bioimaging and sensing applications. These results have been published in Scientific Reports 5, 15235 (2015). Objective 1 achieved. (2) In experiment, we have synthesized GNR@SiO2@CaF2:Yb3+,Er3+ hybrid core-shell-satellite nanostructures with precise control over the thickness of SiO2 shell. We have evaluated the shell thickness-dependent plasmonic enhancement of the upconversion emission intensity in ensemble and studied plasmonic modulation of emission polarization at the single particle level. On the one hand, the hybrid plasmonic upconversion nanostructures with optimal shell thickness exhibit an improved bioimaging performance compared to bare UCNCs. On the other hand, we have observed an extraordinary polarized nature of the light at both upconversion emission bands, which stems from the relationship between excitation polarization and GNR orientation. Here, the polarization-resolved single-particle shattering and upconversion luminescence experiments were carried out on an upgraded integrated multifunctional dark-field microscope system. We used electrodynamic simulations combined with Förster resonance energy transfer theory to fully explain the observed effect. Our results provide an extensive insight into the way how the coherent interaction between emission dipoles of UCNCs and plasmonic dipoles of GNRs determines the polarization states of upconversion emissions in various situations, and thus open the way to accurate control of the UC emission polarization for a wide range of bioimaging and biosensing applications. As a trial experiment beyond the revised objectives of this project, we have also carried out multiphoton imaging of HeLa cells incubated with CaF2:Yb3+,Er3+ UCNCs and GNR@SiO2@CaF2:Yb3+,Er3+ hybrid nanostructures on a commercial confocal laser scanning microscope. The samples were excited by a 980 nm wavelength laser, and two visible upconversion emission channels were detected at green (500–600 nm) and red (600–700 nm) spectral regions. An overlay of the green-channel, red-channel, and bright-field images demonstrates that the hybrid nanostructures had crossed the cell membrane and accumulated in the cytoplasmic region. Under the same laser power, the upconversion luminescence intensity in the HeLa cells incubated with the bare UCNCs was lower than that in the cells incubated with the hybrid nanostructures. Our results demonstrated that the GNR@SiO2@CaF2:Yb3+,Er3+ hybrid nanostructures can be used as a promising fluorescent probe in bioimaging applications. These results have been published in Light: Science & Applications 6, e16217 (2017). Objectives 2 and 3 achieved. (3) Inspired by the experimental results summarized in part (2), we have further realized a hybrid plasmonic upconversion nanostructure consisting of a GNR@SiO2 coupled with NaGdF4:Yb3+,Nd3+@NaGdF4:Yb3+,Er3+@NaGdF4 core–shell–shell UCNCs, which exhibits strongly enhanced UC fluorescence with an intensity enhancement factor up to 20 folds and flexibly tunable upconversion emission colours. In experiment, our results clearly show that controlling the SiO2 spacer thickness enables readily manipulating the intensity ratio of the Er3+ red, green, and blue emissions, thereby achieving the emission colour tuning from pale yellow to green upon excitation at 808 nm. In theory, electrodynamic simulations reveal that the tuneable upconversion colours come from the interplay of plasmon-mediated simultaneous excitation and emission enhancements in the Er3+ green emission yet only excitation enhancement in the blue and red emissions. These results not only provide an upfront experimental design for constructing hybrid plasmonic UC nanostructures with high efficiency and colour tunability, but also deepen our understanding of the interaction mechanism between Er3+ emissions and plasmon resonances in such complex hybrid nanostructures. These results have been published in Advanced Functional Materials 6, e16217 (2017). Objective 4 achieved. (4) Beyond the approved revised project objectives, we have also carried out studies related to upconversion luminescence from rare earth metal ions and other fluorescent nanomaterials. For example, in collaboration with Prof. Mingying Peng of South China University of Technology, we investigated the band-gap modulation and color-tuning properties of single Bi3+-doped yttrium-scandium-niobium vanadates using the upgraded integrated multifunctional dark-field microscope system mentioned in part (2), with results published in Chemistry of Materials 28, 6292-2703 (2016); we have also observed recoverable and unrecoverable Bi3+-related photoemissions induced by thermal expansion and contraction of LuVO4:Bi3+ and ScVO4:Bi3+ compounds, with results published in Chemistry of Materials 28, 7807-7815 (2016).

15301414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301414.value: Major findings and research outcome of this GRF research project are summarized in the following 4 aspects. (1) We have found that the plasmonic near-field enhancement of a gold nanorod (GNR) can significantly increase the absorption of a nearby upconversion emitter, but this could be balanced by the negative effect of electronic transitions between intermediate states and the ground state of the emitter. By optimizing the emitter-GNR dependence of the overall luminescence enhancement factor in the range from 5 to 15 nm, we have found a maximum enhancement factor of 120 and 160 folds at upconversion emission wavelengths of 650 and 540 nm, respectively (refer to item 1 in Part C). (2) We have successfully designed and synthesized GNR@SiO2@CaF2:Yb3+,Er3+ hybrid core-shell-satellite nanostructures with precise control over the thickness of SiO2 shell. On the one hand, we have observed a SiO2 shell thickness-dependent plasmonic enhancement of the upconversion emission intensity in ensemble, and we have also demonstrated that the hybrid plasmonic upconversion nanostructures with an optimal shell thickness exhibit an improved bioimaging performance compared to bare upconversion nanoparticles. On the other hand, we have observed, at the single-particle level, an extraordinary polarized nature of the upconversion luminescence signals at both emission bands, which stems from the relationship between excitation polarization and GNR orientation. In theory, we have used electrodynamic simulations combined with Förster resonance energy transfer theory to fully explain the observed effect (refer to item 3 in Part C). (3) We have further designed and realized a hybrid plasmonic upconversion nanostructure consisting of a GNR@SiO2 coupled with NaGdF4:Yb3+,Nd3+@NaGdF4:Yb3+,Er3+@NaGdF4 core–shell–shell UCNCs, and found that such hybrid structures exhibit a strongly enhanced upconversion luminescence with an intensity enhancement factor up to 20 folds. Interestingly, we have also observed that the overall emission colour can be flexibly tuned by varying the SiO2 shell thickness which in turn manipulates the intensity ratio of the Er3+ red, green, and blue emissions, thereby achieving the emission color tuning from pale yellow to green upon excitation at 808 nm. In theory, electrodynamic simulations reveal that the tunable upconversion colors come from the interplay of plasmon-mediated simultaneous excitation and emission enhancements in the Er3+ green emission yet only excitation enhancement in the blue and red emissions (refer to item 4 in Part C). (4) Recently, in collaboration with Professor Siu Fung Yu at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, we have systematically studied the plasmonic influence in the upconversion emission characteristics of NaYF4 hexagonal micro-rods deposited on a silver-coated substrate and observed an enhanced upconversion spontaneous emission and whispery gallery mode lasing (refer to item 8 in Part C).

15301414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301414.value: After completing this GRF research project, we have now extended plasmon-enhanced upconversion luminescence effect to plasmonic local heating-enhanced upconversion luminescence mediated by the efficient multiple-phonon absorption at elevated local temperatures. This new study is an exciting collaboration with Professor Dayong Jin of the University of Technology Sydney and the Southern University of Science and Technology, China, who is an international leader in the area of upconversion nanocrystals and their applications in super-resolution bioimaging. I hope to develop, based on our preliminary results, a new GRF or CRF proposal by largely extending the scope of current investigation to, for instance, advanced plasmonic upconversion-based near-infrared cellular imaging and sensing.

15301414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301414.value: Fluorescence imaging has been widely considered as one of the most promising techniques in bioimaging because of its high spatial resolution, great sensitivity and low cost. In recent years, lanthanide-doped upconversion nanocrystals (UCNCs) have emerged as excellent alternatives to organic fluorophores and quantum dots for fluorescence bioimaging. Compared to conventional down-conversion counterparts, UCNCs exhibit many unique advantages, such as non-photo-bleaching, weak photo-damage to biological tissues, high fluorescence signal to noise ratio and large imaging penetration depth, among many others. However, the UCNC quantum yields in general are on the order of 1% or even smaller, which is due largely to the intrinsic nature of anti-Stokes emissions and the low absorption cross-section of activator ions. Through carrying out this GRF project, we have demonstrated the feasibility of using plasmonic enhancement effects to increase the quantum yields of UCNCs in general. Specifically, we have theoretically designed and experimentally synthesized several hybrid metal-dielectric-UCNC core-shell-satellite nanostructures with precise control over the dielectric shell thickness. Our ensemble and single-particle spectroscopy results have revealed significant upconversion luminescence intensity enhancement of such hybrid structures compared to bare UCNCs, consistent with our theory and electromagnetic simulation results. Indeed, the hybrid plasmonic upconversion nanostructures with an optimal shell thickness exhibit an improved multi-channel imaging performance compared to bare counterparts.

15301514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301514.value: There has been continuous interest in the studies of dilute magnetic oxide (DMO) semiconductors, which exhibit room-temperature magnetism. In terms of physics, the mechanism for the ferromagnetic response is yet to be fully established. In applications, the (multi-)functionality of the host oxides generally involved in DMO, and the ease of fabrication of such materials, make them attractive candidates for the next-generation spintronic, photonic and electronic devices. Further exploration on the performances of such materials should provide prospects for new device schemes. Various studies indicated the possibility of electrically modulated magnetism in ferromagnets like transition metal ferromagnets and III-V dilute magnetic semiconductors. There are obvious advantages for such a solid-state manipulation scheme, with particular potential for memory applications. Given the versatility of oxide semiconductors, incorporating the active control of magnetism in such materials is of particular interest. Here we propose to examine the non-volatile control of magnetic response in DMO materials by electric field. In particular, the ferromagnetic response of DMO such as Mn-doped ZnO under the influence of remanent polarization from a ferroelectric copolymer will be investigated. Ferroelectric copolymer offer several advantages, including low-processing temperature which prevents interdiffusion across the DMO surface. Besides, the mechanical flexibility of copolymer thin films eliminates the issue of strain-induced magnetic modulation due to the piezoelectric response from ferroelectric material. Finally, the non-volatile nature of remanent polarization allows the retention of modulated magnetic states in DMO for applications. Dilute magnetic oxide of Mn-doped ZnO will be prepared in this work by pulsed laser deposition. By preparing metal-insulator-semiconductor type structure using ferroelectric copolymer of poly(vinylidenefluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) as the polarization retention layer, non-volatile modulation of magnetic responses (such as Curie temperature, hall response, anisotropy) in the DMO layer will be explored. Magnetic and Hall measurements will be employed to establish the presence of the effect. Successful implementation of the project will provide a convenient and robust means of modulating magnetic behavior of DMO, based on the well-studied field effect mechanism. The non-volatile manipulation of magnetic response is desirable for long-retention, high-speed and low-power applications. Fundamentally, the scheme can be used for revealing the correlations between magnetism and charge carrier in DMO, without altering the microstructure of the magnetic materials. 室溫下具有磁性的稀磁氧化物半導體一直被受科學界關注。在物理層面上，它們的磁性機理還沒有被確切地解釋；在實際應用中，摻雜磁性氧化物的多樣性和易制性使其有望成為下一代自旋電子學和光電學的基礎材料。因此，對稀磁氧化物的深層研究有著其實際意義。 最近的文獻指出，傳統鐵磁材料如過渡金屬和(III，V)族磁性半導體可利用電場來調控其磁學特性。這種全固態的調控方式在數據存儲的應用領域上具有極大的優勢，特別是鑑於半導體氧化物的多樣性，這種動態調控磁性材料的方法具有其深入研究的價值。 因此，我們提出一項運用電場對稀磁氧化物薄膜的磁性作出非易失性調控之研究。我們會研究利用鐵電共聚合物中的剩餘極化，對摻錳的氧化鋅的鐵磁性作出調控。由於鐵電共聚合物具有低製備溫度之優勢，這將有效防止與稀磁氧化物在接合面的相互擴散影響。此外，柔性的共聚合物薄膜可以有效的避免鐵電材料的壓電效應,從而減低因壓力引申的磁性改變。最後，鐵電共聚合物的非易失性剩餘極化將有效保留稀磁氧化物調製後的磁性狀態，從而成為可實際應用的存儲器件。 是項研究會利用脈衝激光沉積技術生長摻錳的氧化鋅稀磁氧化物薄膜。我們將以鐵電聚偏氟乙烯-六氟丙烯共聚物(P(VDF-TrFE)) 作為剩餘極化保留層，以製作金屬/絕緣層/半導體結構。透過這種結構，我們會研究共聚合物及其非易失性對稀磁氧化物薄膜磁性（包括居里溫度，霍爾效應及各向異性等效應）的影響。 在應用層面上，這項研究利用已經成熟的場效應技術， 提供一種極其方便的稀磁氧化物薄膜磁性調製方法。這種非易失性的磁性調控技術將為長時間、高速及低能耗存儲的應用作出頁獻。從基礎研究的角度看，這個項目避免了改變材料的微結構，將材料的磁學和稀磁氧化物中的載流子屬性直接聯繫起來，具有非常大的研究價值。

15301714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301714.value: This proposal concerns theoretical and numerical analysis of nonlinear diffusion equations with time-delay, which may be originally considered as a model on population of Australian blowflies, however the model can also be used for modeling other species like insects in the woods and etc. The existence and stability of the migration wave profiles and asymptotic behavior will be discussed. Our focus will be mainly on the equations and system describing the local nonlinear diffusion equations with delay. The non-local and non-classical diffusion models (more realistic mathematical models) may also be part of the project. Our main goals are to study how the global solutions in time will, under the perturbed initial data around the wave profile (small or large), converge to the wave profiles (monotone or non-monotone). The results clearly will depend on the key parameter called the the principle birth and death ratio. This study will derive estimates (various structures) of solutions (continuous and discrete) of nonlinear diffusion equations with delay. These efforts will enable theoretical analysis to become practically useful to understand complicated system with various physical background or the results of this study will provide us with more insights in how and why the mathematical modeling partial differential equations should be modified and, in return, will provide with better understanding of biology itself. 这个建议涉及非线性时滞扩散方程，是原本被视为对澳大利亚苍蝇的人口模型的理论和数值分析，但模型也可以用于模拟其他种类的昆虫​​一样在树林里等的存在和迁移浪潮型材和渐近行为的稳定性进行讨论。我们的重点将主要集中在方程和系统描述与延迟局部非线性扩散方程，及非本地和非经典扩散模型（更真实的数学模型）也将是该项目的一部分。全球解决方案的时候，在周围的波浪曲线的扰动初始数据（大或小）会如何，收敛于波型（单调或非单调）是我们的主要目标，这显然将取决于关键参数调用的出生和死亡的比例。 本研究将得出解的估计（各种结构）（连续和离散） 非线性扩散方程的延迟。这些努力将使理论分析成为实用的理解复杂的方程和系统与物理背景和研究的结果将为我们提供更多的见解 如何以及为什么数学建模偏微分方程方程式应修改和纠正，并在返回时，这将提供更好地理解生物本身。

15301714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301714.value: Before this project started we already begun studying the stability of the wave propagation for Blowflies equations, which was published in [Exponential stability of nonmonotone traveling waves for Nicholson's blowflies equation, CK Lin, CT Lin, Y Lin, M Mei, SIAM journal on mathematical analysis, 46 (2), 1053-1084]. For this local PDES, we derive first time the various exponontial stability for nonmonotone traveling waves under several critical the ratios of birth and death rates associated with delay parameters and critical traveling wave speed. Based on the above analysis we consider Asymptotic Behavior of Solutions For Nonlocal Diffusive Nicholson's Blowflies Equation with Dirichlet Boundary Condition. First of all, we investigate the existence, uniqueness of the positive steady solution for the nonlocal Nicholson's Equation, which may be trivial or non-trivial steady solutions based on the ratio size of birth rate and death rate. In different cases, we prove that the global stability of zero solution / nontrivial steady solution by using the technical energy method, where the global stability of the positive steady solution is established with the monotone method when the equation is monotone, and when the equation is non-monotone, the approach is based on the spatial decomposition technique. In addition we also investiaged asymptotic behavior of solutions to Euler equations with time-dependent damping in critical case, which maybe treated as a quasi-state case for nonlocal systems. This study derives estimates (various structures) of solutions to nonlinear diffusion equations with delay. These efforts will enable theoretical analysis to become practically useful to understand complicated equations and system with physical background or the results of this study will provide us with more insights in how and why the mathematical modeling partial differential equations should be modified and corrected and, in return, which will provide with better understanding of biology itself. Also during this period we considered other related numerical solution techenqiues for the state steady systems ( or elliptic systems) and Maxwell types systems. This leads to my new research directions for matematerial modeling and computations, which can be seen from the outputs.

15301714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301714.value: The mathematical theory of nonlinear partial differential equations describing various physical processes plays an important role in applied mathematics and mathematical physics. But only a few types of partial differential equations have been solved successfully in explicit representation formulas. Different qualitative methods (continuous and discrete or numerical) are employed to solve differential equations. Asymptotic method is one of the most powerful tools of qualitative analysis of differential equations, which allow us to obtain an explicit approximate representation for solutions with respect to a large time. Also some simple asymptotic profiles and decay estimates may be derived through nonlinear analysis based on various of techniques. Asymptotic formulas enable us to know such basic properties of solutions as how solutions grow or decay in different regions, where solutions are monotonous or oscillate. This project may lead to a systematic research on the challenging topics to study the influence of the nonlinear delay term in the asymptotic behavior of solutions (continuous and discrete), even It is quite difficult to obtain some information via numerical experiments.

15301714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301714.value: This results of this study will provide with further development of the theory of asymptotic methods for nonlinear diffusion equations with delay (in particular with non-monotone wave profiles), which is relatively new topic and deserve significant consideration. A description of the large time asymptotic behavior of solutions of nonlinear diffusion equations requires principally new approaches and the reorientation of points of view in the asymptotic methods. The study will not only open some mathematically challenging problems, but also can be used to explain how the species under consideration migrate, which in turn will results in some urban area environment control and management policies, for example.

15302014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302014.value: Loess sequences in arid and semi-arid regions have been used to indicate past climatic change because their depositional processes vary with climate. Thus extensive deposits of loess interbedded with palaeosols in north China have been equated with alternating Pleistocene arid and humid periods in east Asia. Much less is known about palaeoclimate in tropical regions due to a lack of accessible proxy data. Preliminary unfunded work by the PI of this proposal reports extensive and thick deposits of late Pleistocene loess in humid tropical south China between 18 and 23 ºN, and requires investigation, as few laboratory analyses could be conducted. Hypotheses regarding the source and overall extent of the south China loess, as well as its stratification, detailed chronology, pedological and mineralogical properties remain unconfirmed. It is proposed to conduct a detailed spatial and chronological analysis of the south China loess at three different scales of enquiry: remote sensing to determine the spatial extent, fieldwork to investigate and obtain samples from exposed cuttings in a north-south transect, and laboratory analysis including two high resolution sections for Optically Stimulated Luminescence (OSL) dating. In addition, the research will investigate whether soil can form from existing loess during humid phases, or whether a continued dust input forms the parent material for palaeosols, as the south China loess appears to have lost its dust source, the exposed east Asian shelf, during Pleistocene humid phases. This is important as loess-palaeosol boundaries are commonly used as proxy climate markers, and post-depositional pedogenesis in loess may suggest deposition during a humid, rather than arid period. The combination of high resolution OSL dating, grain size analysis and MS measurements in this project, will give a comprehensive and detailed record of dust deposition in south China over the late Pleistocene period, suitable for comparison with other types of climatic proxy data for humid tropical east Asia. 在乾旱和半乾旱地區黃土序列已被用來表示過去的氣候變化，因為它們的沉積過程是隨著氣候而改變的。因此，對於中國南方的黃土建議從調查的三個不同的尺度進行詳細的空間和時間順序分析：第一是用遙感的手段來確定空間範圍，第二是用外業來調查和從暴露岩屑的南北向的橫斷面來獲取樣本，第三是實驗室分析包括兩個高解析部分的釋光測年。此外，由於中國南方的黃土在更新世的潮濕階段似乎失去了塵源和暴露的東亞沙洲，因此這個研究將要調查在潮濕階段土壤是否可以從現有的黃土中形成，或者是由不斷的灰塵投入形成了古土壤的母質。

15302014.label: Realisation of objectives
15302014.value: The first objective to ascertain the spatial land chronological extent of Quaternary loess in south China has been achieved 90%, The results of locating of the samples collected in the field were inconclusive, but appears to be confined to the area south of Nanning, which appear to be late Quaternary, as well as parts of the Pearl River area in northern Guangdong, which correspond to the last Glacial Maximum (LGM). The second objective has only 90% been achieved as we estimate the Nanning loess to be younger than the Old Red Sands of the south China coast, and to have accumulated during a more recent period, though the degree of aridity at this time is uncertain. The third objective is only 80% achieved, as we were unable to return to the field to conduct fieldwork as planned, in more than one major part of the study area. This was because in the summer of 2016, the PI was involved in teaching over most of summer semester, and therefore both teams could not find a suitable date. Following this the Co-I (SHL) went on sabbatical leave in 2017, and the original PI (JN) retired. The new PI (CW) is a specialist in remote sensing and land surveying, and was the most suitable person in the original PI’s department to become new PI. The fourth objective was dependent on the third objective being met, and so was only 60% achieved at the end of the project. Nevertheless, the researchers feel that since only 50% of the budget applied for was granted, the objectives have been responsibly addressed, and a reasonable research output in terms of publications has been achieved.

15302014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302014.value: Two field visits were conducted to Nanning, Guangxi Province in December 2015 and March 2016, with the Co-I Dr Shenghua Li and his research students as well as with other earth science colleagues and research students from universities in Guangdong. A vehicle traverse from north to south was conducted to visit sites where sections were exposed, and samples were taken. One field visit to Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City and Dalat) was also conducted, and samples collected. Samples from all field trips were analysed for particle size analysis, dates, and other physical properties at the laboratories of the Co-I Dr Shenghua Li at the University of Hong Kong. The particle size distributions of all sample data collected correspond to the known sizes for loess. However, the dating of the Nanning samples was inconclusive, as the dates, which were found to be 77,000 to 105,000 years old, did not correspond to any recognized marked arid phases in the last glacial cycle. For Vietnam samples while the physical properties of the samples correspond to those of loess, the results are ambiguous due to the character of the local basalt geology being an alternative explanation. Therefore we continued literature searches to try and explain the findings and link them with known deposits elsewhere in southern China and neighbouring countries. As Objective 1 is to establish the spatial extent of Quaternary loess, we extended the study to countries adjoining the east Asian shelf, including northern Thailand. The northern Thailand study is now complete, with a paper published in Aeolian Research. This part of the study established that the northern Thailand loess is derived from local sources during the last glacial maximum, and may not be part of a regional process involving the east Asian shelf. Therefore it may be unrelated to the south China deposits, except in terms of the timing of its formation.

15302014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302014.value: It was expected that objectives 1 and 2 – establishing the spatial extent of the deposits as well as their relationship to the Old Red Sands of Guangdong, would be addressed by the results of dating the samples but this was not the case as the dates were inconclusive. Using remote sensing for this would not be meaningful unless we can establish their identity in the field. We were unable to return to the field in the summer of 2016, as planned, as the PI was involved in teaching over most of summer semester, and therefore both teams could not find a common suitable date. Future investigations should focus on establishment of the source areas for other aeolian deposits in southern China, as well as other areas adjacent to the east Asian Shelf, such as the Isthmus of Kra in southern Thailand.

15302014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302014.value: This research has investigated Quaternary Aeolian sediments in southern China, and compared them chronologically and spatially to other similar deposits in tropical and sub-topical Asia bordering the east Asian shelf. The objective was to use the deposits as proxy indicators of climatic conditions when the deposits were formed. Remote sensing and field surveys were undertaken in southern China to extend the known area of loess-like-material outside the known region, including Vietnam and Thailand. The north Thailand deposit was investigated and confirmed to be Quaternary loess of local origin, and comparable to deposits in east central Guangdong, southern China. Results for Vietnam were inconclusive and ambiguous, as the basalt bedrock could have been the source of loess-like sediments, which appeared to be present only above basalt, whereas loess is usually unconformable with the underlying bedrock.

15302114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302114.value: In this project, we aim to make an extensive study on four important classes of structured tensors, namely positive semi-definite symmetric tensors, Hankel tensors, Toeplitz tensors (including circulant tensors) and M-tensors, for both theory and algorithms. These four classes of structred tensors naturally arise from applications. We will study their generating functions, eigenvalues, Hadarmard products or Z-Hadamard products, positive semi-definiteness for even order Hankel tensors and Toeplitz tensors, determinants of principal subtensors, etc. We will construct algorithms for computing their eigenvalues. We will also study odd order positive semi-definite symmetric tensors and some associated matrices and tensors. The success of this research project will not only greatly advance the theory of tensors (hypermatrices), but also make strong impact in the related application areas. 在本项目中， 我们将对四类结构张量：半正定对称张量，汉克尔张量，托泼利兹张量（包括循环张量）和M张量， 的理论和算法进行广泛的研究。 这四类结构张量都从应用中自然产生。 我们将研究它们的生成函数，特征值， 哈达玛乘积或Z哈达玛乘积，偶数阶汉克尔张量和托泼利兹张量的半正定性， 主子张量的行列式等。 我们将构造算法来计算它们的特征值。 我们也将研究奇数阶半正定对称张量和一些有关的矩陳和张量。 本研究项目的成功将不仅对张量（超矩陳）理论产生巨大推动， 并将在有关应用领域产生重要影响。

15302214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302214.value: 數值求解外延增長方程的誤差分析

15302214.label: Project Objectives
15302214.value: We will begin by considering numerical analysis on a molecular beam epitaxial (MBE) equation in 1-dimensional space and then extend the analysis to 2D case. Spectrum analysis will be carried out to establish an estimate for the smallest eigenvalue of a linearized MBE operator under different regularity assumptions on initial datum functions at different stages. Based on aforementioned spectrum analysis, we will attempt to get a better estimate on the error constant, which usually grows exponentially as the small diffusion parameter goes to zero. A priori error estimate will be studied when the thin film epitaxial growth approaches to different states, e.g., transition states, metastable states and steady state. This will help to understand large time behaviors of the thin film growth, which is a challenging problem in the study of MBE models. A posteriori error estimates and adaptive computations will be further investigated.

15302214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302214.value: Numerical methods have been extensively studied for investigating thin film epitaxial growths. A class of typical governing equations are of Ehrlich-Schwoebel type, which involves a small positive diffusion parameter, a fourth-order diffusion term and a strong nonlinear second-order term. These difficulties require a careful study of numerical methods for complex solution dynamics. Meanwhile, a large time simulation is required to reach the steady state of numerical solutions. It has been a great challenge in error analysis for numerical solutions of thin film epitaxy equations at a large time because the error constant increases to infinity exponentially as the small diffusion parameter goes to zero. This project focuses on both a priori and a posteriori error estimates for semi-discrete and fully discrete numerical schemes of aforementioned thin film epitaxy equations at different developmental stages. Under proper assumptions on initial data and suitable constraints on the space mesh size and the time step size at different states, rigorous error estimates will be given to limit the growth of the error constant for very small diffusion parameters. The goal of this project is to establish optimal order and quasi-optimal order error bounds for some highly efficient numerical methods for the thin film epitaxial growth simulations. 數值方法在研究薄膜外延增長中已經得到了廣泛的應用。一類典型的外延增長方程具有Ehrlich-Schowoebel型的能量。它含有一個小的正擴散系數，四階擴散項和強非線性的二階項。這些困難使得方程的解存在復雜的動態發展，設計數值方法時需要十分精細。同時，數值求解達到平衡狀態是一個相當長的過程。針對數值解在大時間處的誤差分析是一個巨大的困難。因為當小擴散參數趨近於零時，誤差常數將指數階的增長到無窮。 本項目主要研究以上提到的薄膜外延增長方程的半離散和全離散數值格式在解的不同發展階段的誤差估計。在針對初值適當的假設及對在不同狀態下空間網格和時間步長的一定限制下，我們將進行嚴格的誤差分析，從而剔除誤差常數中指數階增長的小擴散系數的倒數。本項目的目標是針對薄膜外延增長數值模擬構造高效的數值 方法，並且得到數值解誤差估計的最優階和擬最優階的誤差界。

15302214.label: Realisation of objectives
15302214.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. Under the support of this GRF grant, we have proved an improved error analysis for a finite difference scheme for solving the epitaxial thin film model with slope selection. The unique solvability and unconditional energy stability are assured by the convex nature of the splitting scheme. It is observed that a standard error estimate, based on the discrete Gronwall inequality, leads to a onvergence constant growing exponentially as the small diffusion parameter goes to zero, To improve this error estimate, we employed a spectrum estimate for the linearized operator associated with the 1-D slope selection gradient flow. With the help of the aforementioned linearized spectrum estimate, we are able to derive a convergence analysis for the finite difference scheme, in which the convergence constant depends on 1/ε only in a polynomial order, rather than exponential. We also studied several semi-implicit schemes for the MBE equation. The stability and error analysis have been investigated.

15302214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302214.value: In this project, we have investigated several energy stable numerical schemes for the epitaxy growth equations. The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1. In a series of recent papers [Li, Qiao, Tang, SINUM, 2016; Li, Qiao, JSC, 2017; Li, Qiao, CMS, 2017], we made an important contribution in the stability analysis of the stabilized semi-implicit schemes for Allen-Cahn, Cahn-Hilliard equations and epitaxy growth equations. These schemes are widely used in practice but previous analysis indicated that the second-order versions of these schemes can only be conditionally energy stable. By using advanced PDE and numerical analysis techniques, we showed that under reasonable assumptions, the first and second-order versions with a Fourier spectral method in space are indeed unconditionally energy stable. This is a surprising and break through result. 2. In [Li, Qiao, Zhang, SINUM, 2017; Qiao, Wang, Wise, Zhang, IJNAM, 2017], error estimates for epitaxy growth equations are given. To improve the error estimate, we employed a spectrum estimate for the linearized operator associated with the 1-D slope selection (SS) gradient flow. With the help of the aforementioned linearized spectrum estimate, we are able to derive a convergence analysis for the finite difference scheme, in which the convergence constant depends on 1/ε only in a polynomial order, rather than exponential. 3. In [Peng, Qiao, Sun, JCM, 2017], we have used our developed efficient numerical methods for epitaxy growth equations in simulating a diffuse interface model with the Peng-Robinson equation of state for two-phase fluid systems. This model plays an important role in reservoir engineering as well as in environmental protection, such as subsurface CO2 sequestration. The numerical results matched the experimental results quite well.

15302214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302214.value: The further development of this research is to solve other gradient flows problem by using the developed methods. The stability and error analysis will be studied for the 2D thin film epitaxial growth equation with slope selection with the a prior estimate obtained in this research. A better stabilization strategy will be studied so that the stabilization constant could be as small as needed in practice.

15302214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302214.value: Energy stable numerical schemes have been successfully implemented in solving nonlinear diffusion equations modeling epitaxial growth of thin films. The numerical results have verified mathematical justifications and experiments observations of the thin film growth rates. For complex thin-film systems, the evolution process of thin-film epitaxial growth has been resolved accurately and efficiently at large times. Improved error estimates have been obtained with the help of the linearized spectrum estimate.

15302614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302614.value: 大氣反應性氮氧化物包括一氧化氮、二氧化氮及其眾多的化學反應產物和中間體，在大氣化學、地球生物化學循環和氣候變化中均扮演重要角色，也與光化學煙霧、灰霾、酸沉降和水體富營養化等區域性環境問題密切相關。五氧化二氮是大氣氮氧化物的關鍵中間體之一。國際最新研究表明，對於五氧化二氮在大氣顆粒物表面的水解反應的認識還存在嚴重不足，而這些過程可能對當前世界主要城市（包括香港）所普遍面臨的大氣光化學煙霧具有重要影響。 近期研究已表明：在光化學活躍季節，香港近地面大氣中含有較高濃度的五氧化二氮。然而，對於香港邊界層頂大氣五氧化二氮的含量及化學過程卻仍屬未知。鑒於五氧化二氮化學行為在不同高度大氣的差異性，我們計劃在大帽山頂開展觀測和模擬研究。此項研究旨在全面認識香港大氣邊界層內五氧化二氮的化學過程及其對大氣氧化性和光化學煙霧的影響，預期可以填補關於高污染亞熱帶海岸地區獨特大氣環境中五氧化二氮化學轉化的知識空白，也可提高當前空氣質量模式的模擬性能。

15302614.label: Realisation of objectives
15302614.value: We carried out detailed analysis of data obtained from the 2013 autumn field study at a high elevations site, Tai Mo Shan (22.410°N, 114.125°E; 957 m a.s.l.) in Hong Kong. In the campaign, dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) and nitryl chloride (ClNO2) were measured together with NOx, NOy, O3, HONO, VOCs, aerosol ionic compositions, particle size distribution and numbers and meteorological data like wind, temperature, relative humidity, as well as photolysis frequency of NO2. We employed statistical methods, steady-state approach and combination of high resolution meteorological and measurement-constrained chemical models. We found the highest concentrations reported to date in the literature for ClNO2 (4.7 ppbv) and N2O5 (7.7 ppbv) in the early morning of a night in a well processed air mass originated from the major industrial/urban areas of the Pearl River Delta. We employed an iterative box model to investigate five N2O5/ClNO2-laden nights. We estimated the N2O5 uptake coefficient and ClNO2 yield and calculated the relative importance of N2O5 heterogeneous reactions to NOx loss and the accumulated ClNO2 production over the entire night. The average uptake coefficient was estimated to 0.004 ± 0.003, and the average yield was 0.42 ± 0.26. As the air masses aged, the accumulated ClNO2 was found to reach up to 6.0 ppbv, indicating significant production of ClNO2 in the polluted air from the Pearl River Delta. The model calculation shows that ClNO2 formation (N2O5 + Cl−), N2O5 hydrolysis (N2O5 + H2O), and NO3 reactions with volatile organic compounds (NO3 + VOCs) consumed 23%, 27%, and 47% of the produced NO3, respectively, as the average for five nights. A significant portion of the NOx in the air masses (70% ± 10%) was removed during the night via NO3 reactions with VOCs (~ 40%) and N2O5 heterogeneous loss (~ 60%). The ClNO2 and N2O5 data were constrained into a box model (MCM v3.2) incorporated with updated Cl mechanisms to evaluate the contribution of N2O5 and ClNO2 to oxidative capacity of the atmosphere. The model results show increase of HOx (OH+HO2) by up to 107% and can ultimately increase the total production of ozone in the following day by up to 41%. We also extended the data analysis into a roadside environment and in the inner Pearl River delta to assess the impact of reactive nitrogen on the oxidative capacity in different environmental conditions.

15302614.value: (1) ClNO2 and N2O5 plumes were frequently observed at Mt Tai Mao Shan and an inner PRD site in early periods of night, indicating active nocturnal N2O5 heterogeneous processes in the residual boundary-layer atmosphere of southern China (paper 1, 2, 5). (2) The determined γN2O5 would be useful for improving the modelling performance in this region (paper 2, 4, 5). 15302614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302614.value: Reactive oxidized nitrogen compounds, which include NOx (NO + NO2) and their reaction intermediates/products, play important roles in atmospheric chemistry, biogeochemical cycle, and climate. They contribute to modern environmental pollution such as photochemical smog, haze, acid deposition, and eutrophication. Dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) is one of the reactive intermediates of NOx, yet significant knowledge gaps exist regarding the loss of N2O5 on particle surfaces and subsequent production of highly reactive chlorine radical (Cl). These processes have the potential to significantly influence the formation of ozone, a photochemical air pollutant in world’s major cities, including Hong Kong. To better understand the chemistry of N2O5 in the boundary-layer atmosphere and to quantify its contribution to the regional-scale ozone formation, we analyzed comprehensive field study of NO3, N2O5, ClNO2, and other key species a mountain-top site (Tai Mo Shao) with advanced models. The research improved understanding of hydrolysis of N2O5 and production of Cl in South China and their impacts on the atmospheric oxidative capacity and formation of ground-level ozone. This study has filled the knowledge gap on heterogeneous chemistry of N2O5, the findings are well received by the scientific community. The research has laid foundation for further development of this important research area.

15303114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303114.value: Transition metal catalysis has significantly streamlined organic synthesis through selective activation, functionalization, and transformation of organic molecules. In particular, advancement on coinage metal catalysis has led to the discovery of novel organic transformation reactions conducted under mild reaction conditions. Using multi-component coupling reactions, structurally diverse synthetic intermediates can be assembled in a modular approach and transformed to complex molecular structures in high efficiency and selectivity by coinage metal catalysis. In this proposal, we plan to employ silver catalysis to explore the novel synthetic utilities of easily accessible propargylamines for selective organic transformation reactions and bioconjugation of peptides and proteins in aqueous medium. Propargylamines can be synthesized by a gold-catalyzed three-component coupling reaction of aldehydes, amines and alkynes in a combinatorial manner. We plan to develop silver-catalyzed cascade cyclization of alkynyl alcohol-linked propargylamines to afford isochromans. In addition, we propose to use silver catalysis to convert structurally diverse propargylamines into enones and alpha-acyloxy-beta-amino carbonyl compounds via propargylamine N-oxides as the key intermediates. Through mechanistic studies, the reaction pathways in these novel organic transformation reactions will be revealed. Bioconjugation has emerged as an important interdisciplinary research area between Chemistry and Biology aiming to study complex biological systems. In particular, site-specific modification of biomolecules provides an indispensible tool for the development of biopharmaceuticals. On the basis of our track record in catalysis and bioconjugation research, we propose to develop dual labeling of peptides and proteins by silver-mediated cysteine modification with propargylamines. The success of this project would have significant impact on the research areas of Organic Chemistry, Protein Science, and Chemical Biology. 過渡金屬催化作用通過對有機分子進行選擇性活化、官能團化和化學轉化，能有效簡化和優化有機合成的過程。其中，利用貨幣金屬作為催化劑已被成功應用於溫和條件下新型有機合成反應的開發。利用貨幣金屬的催化作用，通過多組分偶聯反應，結構不同的合成中間體可以被高效、高選擇性地組裝或轉化到復雜的分子結構中。 在這個研究計劃中，我們打算採用銀的催化作用，以新方法實現對炔丙胺的選擇性轉化，並將其應用於多肽和蛋白質在水溶液中的生物偶聯。炔丙胺可以通過金催化的醛、胺和炔烴三組分偶聯反應得到。我們計劃發展一種通過銀催化的炔醇衍生化的炔丙胺的串聯環化反應合成異色滿的方法。此外，我們計劃利用銀的催化作用，通過形成炔丙胺氮氧化物作為關鍵中間體，將炔丙胺選擇性轉化為烯酮或α-酰氧基-β-氨基羰基化合物。這些新型的有機轉化反應的反應途徑將會通過機理研究予以揭示。 生物偶聯已經成為一個結合了化學與生命科學，旨在研究複雜生物系統的一個重要的交叉學科研究領域。生物分子的特定位點選擇性修飾已成為生物醫藥發展的過程中不可或缺的工具之一。基於我們在催化合成和生物偶聯方面取得的研究成果，我們計劃利用炔丙胺，在銀催化下對半胱氨酸上的巰基進行修飾，應用於多肽和蛋白質的雙標記。這個項目的成功將會對有機化學，蛋白質科學和化學生物學的發展帶來重大的影響。

15303114.label: Realisation of objectives
15303114.value: (1) We have developed a series of silver-mediated transformations of propargylamines to provide diverse patterns of products, including enones, α-thioketones, and isochromans. A variety of enone derivatives were obtained by silver-catalyzed transformation of propargylamines with 3-chloroperoxybenzoic acid (m-CPBA) in aprotic solvent. We have developed a novel silver-catalyzed transformation of propargylamines to provide enones and acyloxy ketones via propargylic amine N-oxide in one pot process under mild reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies indicated that in situ generated isoxazolinium ion is the key intermediate which could convert to enone in an aprotic solvent and to ketone and enone in a protic solvent. This reaction scope has been explored by using propargylamines with different combinations of aldehydes, amines and alkynes. To further demonstrate the substrate scope for the reaction, we designed and synthesized a series of sterically hindered propargylamines with adjacent quaternary carbon center (R ≠ H), which could be obtained through gold catalyzed three-component coupling reaction by using ketones couple with amines and alkynes. In contrast, when the reactions were carried out in protic solvent with N-Boc-L-cysteine methyl ester (Boc = tert-butoxycarbonyl) as nucleophile, α-thioketones were obtained. Moreover, the first silver-mediated cascade cyclization of alkynyl alcohol-linked propargylamines giving isochroman scaffolds was developed. The yields of isochroman derivatives were improved by increasing the length of the alkyl chain of propargyl alcohols. Notably, the eight-membered ring product, which is difficult to access otherwise due to their unfavorable transannular interactions and entropic factors, was obtained in synthetically useful yield. Both R1 and R2 could be hydrogen or electron-donating groups or electron-withdrawing groups, to give the desired eight-membered ring products in moderate yields. In this connection, we have successfully achieved the objectives of 1. To develop silver-catalyzed cascade cyclization of alkynyl alcohol-linked propargylamines 2. To develop silver-catalyzed transformation of propargylamines into enones and alpha acyloxy-beta-amino carbonyl compounds 3. To conduct mechanistic studies on the silver-catalyzed propargylamine transformation reactions (2) On the basis of our work on the development of organic transformation reactions for alkynyl-linked propargylamines, we have discovered a new strategy for amine activation to give reactive amine anion by in situ generated iminium cation-amine anion pair through decomposition of sterically hindered aminals. Utilizing this strategy, a highly regio- and chemoselective cyclocarboamination of ortho-formyl phenylacetylenes with secondary amines has been realized under metal-free mild reaction conditions. The cyclocarboamination with notably tunable product profiles depends on the separation and purification procedure, a diverse range of 1, 3-diamino-1H-indenes (essentially reactive enamines) and 3-amino-1-indanones were obtained, respectively. Moreover, using iodine as an electrophile to couple with various ortho-formyl phenylacetylenes and secondary amines, a series of 3-amino-2-iodo-1-indanones were efficiently achieved with four bonds (C=O, C-C, C-N and C-I) formation in an one-pot three-component reaction. These results demonstrated an unprecedented methodology for the construction of highly functionalized 1H-indene and 1-indanone compounds. (3) We have developed a new isoxazolinium-mediated cysteine modification of peptides and proteins. Versatile isoxazolinium reagents could be modularly prepared via gold and silver catalysis. Using a stoichiometric amount of isoxazolinium reagents generated in situ from a catalytic amount of silver salts, cysteine-containing peptides could be efficiently modified to afford products in nearly complete conversions. The modification was highly chemoselective towards free cysteine residue and the resulting phenylacyl thioether linkage was stable towards excess thiol-containing reagents and reducing reagents. For protein bioconjugation, free cysteine containing proteins HSA and BSA, as well as a site-directed mutated therapeutic protein (BCArg) could be efficiently and selectively labelled using small amounts of the isoxazolinium reagents. Labelling peptides and proteins with functional moieties such as fluorescent tags have also been performed and analyzed by LC-MS and SDS-PAGE analyses. Besides, it has been found that the phenylacyl thioether linkage bearing an alkyne moiety could be rapidly cleaved under irradiation of UV-A light, giving the formation of a thioaldehyde moiety, which could be converted back to cysteine by reduction. In this connection, we have achieved the objective of 4. To develop dual labeling of peptides and proteins by silver-mediated cysteine modification with propargylamines

15303114.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303114.value: (1) Silver-mediated transformation has emerged as an important approach for organic synthesis, owing to its high selectivity, compatibility, mild reaction conditions and cost-effectiveness compared to other expensive transition metals. Our work disclosed a novel silver-catalyzed transformation of propargylamines to provide enones and acyloxy ketones via propargylic amine N-oxide in one pot process under mild reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies indicated that in situ generated isoxazolinium ion is the key intermediate which could convert to enone in an aprotic solvent and to ketone and enone in a protic solvent. (2) Cascade cyclization has been a long-standing interest for synthetic chemists as molecular complexity can be built up from simple starting materials via tandem reaction sequences in a one-pot reaction. We hypothesized that the allene moieties generated from propargylamines would be amenable for further synthetic elaboration via cycloisomerization with alkynes. We developed a new cycloisomerization reaction of alkynyl alcohol-linked propargylamines. (3) Amines are abundant in biologically active natural products, medicines and functional materials. Selective synthesis of amines from readily available precursors is a significant research direction in chemical research. Our work is an unprecedented metal-free cyclocarboamination of orthoformyl phenylacetylenes with secondary amines involving a transient iminium cation/amine anion pair which generated in situ via reversible equilibrium of aminal to give 3-amino-1H-indenes and 3-amino-1-indanones. (4) Selective biomolecule modification is an important chemical biology tool for manipulating the properties of biomolecules and investigating their functions in complex biological systems. Notably, we have developed a new cysteine modification using isoxazoliniums generated in situ via silver catalysis. The modification could proceed efficiently with high chemoselectivity towards cysteine residue on peptides and proteins. In most cases, only a stoichiometric amount of isoxazolinium reagents with a catalytic amount of silver salts were needed to give high to excellent conversions. Besides, easily accessible isoxazolinium reagents with versatile functional groups were compatible with this modification. Fluorescent tags could be efficiently labelled on the cysteine-containing peptides and proteins by directly employing fluorescent tag-derived isoxazolinium reagents or by sequential modification using the azide-alkyne click reaction. The resulting phenylacyl thioether linkage was stable towards various thiol-containing reagents and reductants. Investigation of the effect of the modification on a therapeutic protein (BCArg) revealed that the incorporated tag gave little influence on the enzymatic activity and anticancer property of the protein, which suggested that the isoxazolinium reagents could be potentially employed as promising reagents for labeling bioactive proteins in the future.

15303114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303114.value: (1) We have developed efficient silver-catalyzed transformation reactions of propargylamines to provide enones and acyloxy ketones via propargylic amine N-oxides as well as cascade cyclization of alkynyl alcohol-linked propargylamines affording isochroman scaffolds. In this project, we have set up efficient methodologies allowing the easy access of diverse classes of propargylamines, enones, acyloxy ketones and isochromans. Effort will be directed towards the application of these useful synthetic building blocks in organic synthesis. (2) We have developed a new approach for a highly regio- and chemoselective cyclocarboamination of ortho-formyl phenylacetylenes with secondary amines under metal-free mild reaction conditions. We will further expand the scope of this reaction including more diverse starting materials. We also plan to investigate the reactivity of the resulting highly functionalized 1H-indene and 1-indanone compounds for further organic transformation reactions. (3) We have developed a new cysteine modification using isoxazoliniums generated in situ via silver catalysis. Effort will be directed towards strategic incorporation of biophysical probes/affinity tags to bioactive peptides and proteins and investigations of the applications on chemical proteomics.

15303114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303114.value: Catalysis is an important technology for our modern society aiming to provide a diversity of chemicals for the production of commodity including agrochemicals, functional materials, and pharmaceuticals. Notably, catalysis is an important area in green chemistry supporting the desirable development of our sustainable society. Through catalysis, renewable resources can be efficiently converted into diverse useful materials and commercial products using a minimum amount of energy under environmentally friendly conditions without generation of toxic chemical wastes. In this project, we have developed silver catalysis for efficient organic transformation reactions that facilitate the construction of complex molecular compounds under mild reaction conditions. In addition, we have expanded the scope of silver catalysis into chemical biology research by selective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins. These newly developed synthetic methodologies would have great applications on fine chemical and pharmaceutical industries. In addition, the new and selective bioconjugation methods would have a significant impact on the fields of Chemical Biology, Biomedical Research, and Biopharmaceuticals Development.

15303514.value: Manelalides以及其衍生物的合成以及生物活性检测

15303514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303514.value: Natural products have provided considerable value to the pharmaceutical industry over the past half century. In particular, the therapeutic area of oncology has benefited from numerous drug classes derived from natural product sources. Drug discovery from marine natural products has enjoyed a renaissance in the past few years. Several marine-derived agents are now approved, most as ‘‘first-in-class’’ drugs, with five of seven appearing in the past few years. Nature provides us with many complex natural products that have interesting medicinal properties. Unfortunately, the amounts of these compounds that is isolated is usually quite low, making their development into useful medicinal agents very difficult. The total chemical synthesis of these compounds is therefore important and has been a key tool in drug discovery and development. The synthesis allows verification of the primary structure proposed on the basis of studies of the marine natural product, and can be employed to study and address some of shortcomings of natural products through manipulation of pharmacological properties, structure activity relationship studies, and the preparation of drug candidates for mechanistic studies. Our present studies focus on newly isolated anticancer marine natural products called mandelalides. Biological studies of these marine natural product indicated that they possesses potent cytotoxicity activity to human NCI-H460 lung cancer cells and mouse Neuro-2A neuroblastoma cells in the nanomolar range. Mandelalides are variously glycosylated, unusual polyketide macrolides isolated from a new species of Lissoclinum ascidian collected from South Africa, Algoa Bay near Port Elizabeth and the surrounding Nelson Mandela Metropole. The important biological properties of mandelalides and their natural scarcity, coupled with its intriguing molecular architecture, render it an attractive synthetic target for further development. To the best of our knowledge, a complete total synthesis of mandelalides has not yet been reported. The long-term goal of this research is to develop highly effective anticancer agents from mandelalides, and to carry out the molecular design, chemical synthesis and biological testing of simpler biological mimics of these molecules. We are directing our efforts to prepare mandelalides by organic synthesis, employing strategies and methods that can be modified for the preparation of analogues. We are also going to carry out analogue synthesis that aims at determining the minimal molecular architecture of mandelalides necessary for its biological activity. The investigation towards the total synthesis of mandelalides and their analogues should have impacts on both the synthetic and medicinal communities. 天然产物在药物产业体现出重要价值已经超过半个世纪，特别是肿瘤治疗领域，大量抗癌药物都是基于天然产物发展而来。近年来，海洋天然产物相关药物研发产业迎来了复兴。目前已有多种基于海洋天然产物的新药获审批通过，大部分为首选药物， 其中五分之七属于近年研制的新药。大自然为我们提供了大量复杂的天然产物，它们均具有有趣的医药特性。令人遗憾的是，这些化合物极低的分离产率导致对它们在医药方向的实用化开发非常艰难。因此，这些化合物的全合成是后续药物发现发展过程中的关键。通过对其药理学特性的处理、构效关系的研究及备选药物的制备，化学合成研究能帮助我们证實这些海洋天然产物的结构，同时也为研究和克服天然产物在成药方面的缺陷提供巨大帮助。 我们目前的研究重点是一系例最新分离的称为mandelalides的抗癌症海洋天然产物。这些海洋天然产物的生物活性检测显示它们具有很强的细胞毒性，对人肺癌细胞NCI-H460及小鼠成神经细胞瘤细胞Neuro-2A上可达纳摩尔级别。Mandelalides是一种多样化糖基化的、非常见的大环内酯化合物，可由生长在南非伊丽莎白港附近的阿尔哥亚湾及纳尔逊曼德拉市周边地区的一种新种类热带海鞘（Lissoclinum ascidian）中分离得到。Mandelalides在生物性质上的重要性、在自然界的罕见性及独特的的分子结构，让它成为后续研究中一个引人注目的研究对象。在我们所知范围之内，暂未有mandelalides完整全合成的相关报道。 长远来看，本项目意在以mandelalides为基础开发一系列高效抗癌药物，并对其简化后的生物学模似物的分子设计、化学合成及生物活性进行研究检测。我们将采用利于类似物制备的合成策略及方法，通过有机合成手段制备mandelalides。我们亦将对其衍生物进行制备和研究，以探寻mandelalides能产生生物活性的最简略分子结构。研究mandelalides及其衍生物的全合成应会在合成及药物研究领域产生相当影响。

15303614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303614.value: 鑭摻雜納米晶體微腔器的五光子上轉換激光

15303614.label: Project Objectives
15303614.value: To design and realize high-luminescent low-loss Tm3+ doped NCs. The NCs should support five-photon up-conversion emission (1I6 -> 3F4 transition, ~347 nm emission peak) under near-infrared excitation. Hence, the NCs can be used to verify ‘direct pumping’ which can compensate depopulation of intermediate energy levels. To design and fabricate Fabry Perot microcavity, which will favor the re-absorption of radiative relaxation emission and the population of the intermediate energy levels, embedded with the lanthanide-doped NCs. To demonstrate unambiguously five-photon up-conversion UV lasing from the Tm3+ doped NCs under near-infrared excitation.

15303614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303614.value: Up-conversion, which performs sequential absorption of two or more photons through upward transition from the ladder-like energy levels of the lanthanide ions, emits light with wavelength shorter than that of the absorbed light. Recently, multi-photon up-conversion emission in the range of ultraviolet (UV) has been observed from lanthanide-doped nanocrystals (NCs). However, the presence of relaxation process, which is an intrinsic property of lanthanide-ions, depopulates the population of the intermediate energy levels. As a result, up-conversion efficiency decreases with the increase of intermediate energy levels. This is because up-conversion transition can only be activated after the population of the previous lower energy levels. Hence, it is difficult to improve the multi-photon UV up-conversion efficiency of lanthanide-doped NCs unless there are no intermediate energy levels. Here, we propose to ‘directly pump’ the intermediate energy levels of the activator ions so that the depopulation of carriers arisen from the relaxation process can be compensated. This can be done by using a special design Fabry Perot microcavity to populate the intermediate energy levels through the re-absorption of strongly confined radiative relaxation emission. Hence, the populating process of the intermediate energy levels can now be controlled by the use of Fabry Perot microcavities and it is independent of the choice and concentration of activator ions. The ultimate goal of this proposal is to demonstrate five-photon UV up-conversion lasing, which requires a large quantity of population inversion and a sufficient density of states at the highest energy level of the activator ions, from the Fabry Perot microcavity. Therefore, this could verify unambiguously that the multi-photon up-conversion efficiency of lanthanide-doped NCs can be significantly enhanced by ‘direct pumping’ of the intermediate energy levels. 上轉換發光是指在鑭系元素離子的階梯狀能級通過能級躍遷連續吸收兩個或者多個光子而發出波長比吸收光的波長更短的發光類型。最近發光在紫外光區的多光子上轉換發光已經在鑭系元素摻雜的納米晶中發現。儘管如此，鑭系元素離子所固有的弛豫特性降低了中間能級的粒子數。這導致上轉換的效率隨著中間能級數量的增多而降低。這是由於上轉換躍遷只有在之前一個較低能級的粒子數充足的情況下才會被激活。因此，除非中間能級不存在，否則很難提高鑭系元素離子摻雜的納米晶的紫外光多光子上轉換發光效率。 在此，我們提出通過“直接泵浦”激活離子的中間能級以補償由於弛豫導致的載流子數減少。這可以通過設計一個特別的法布里-珀羅微腔重吸收強烈限域的輻射弛豫發光以填充中間能級來實現。故而，中間能級的粒子填充可以由法布里-珀羅微腔來控製，而不受激活離子的種類和濃度的限制。這樣做的最終目標是為了獲得從法布里-珀羅微腔產生的需要，大量的粒子數反轉以及激活離子最高能級充裕的態密度的五光子紫外光上轉換激光。因此，這樣可以非常確定的證實鑭系元素摻雜的納米晶的多光子上轉換發光效率可以通過“直接泵浦”中間能級而獲得顯著地提升。

15303614.label: Realisation of objectives
15303614.value: We have completed the objectives of this project. We have designed and fabricated core-shell-shell nanoparticles which can provide effective 5-photon upconversion UV emission via the use of Tm3+ dopant under 980 nm excitation at room temperature. We use a spatial confinement of energy migration that can prevent energy loss to the crystal lattice and increases the local density of excitation energy. Through the use of Tm3+ ion as an energy accumulator, the excitation energy can be maximally amassed to generate intense ultraviolet emissions on near-infrared excitation in an effective way. Furthermore, we have demonstrated unambiguously 5-photon lasing emission at 310 nm wavelength can be obtained at room temperature under 980 nm laser excitation. This is verified by the observation of the change in laser mode spacing with the diameter of the microcavities. Please be noted that 310 nm lasing is more difficult that achieving 347 nm lasing as was proposed due to the higher photon energy. On the other hand, we demonstrated experimentally and proved theoretically that the use of laser cavity to populate intermediate energy levels of rare earth ions. It is observed that the upconversion efficiency of Tm3+-doped nanoparticles can be improved by an order of magnitude provided that a laser cavity is established to support lasing emission. This improvement can be explained as the clamping of population at a required threshold value, which allows the suppression of undesired radiative recombination of the intermediate states. This also verify our proposed idea of our GRF project. In fact, the above mentioned tasks have already covered the objectives of our project and we can considered our project had been completed. Nevertheless, we found that our knowledge of rare earth doping design and the newly developed laser theories for rare earth materials can extend our knowledge to other applications using upconversion materials. For example, we realize upconversion white-light lasing from Tm3+ and Er3+ -doped β-NaYF4 hexagonal microrods under near-infrared excitation at room temperature for the first time. This can be done by the mixture of the three basic colors of white - we use 40% Yb3+ and 2% Tm3+ as the co-doping concentration to maximize blue emission intensity at 450 nm. We further introduce Er3+ into the microrods to excite red and green emission intensity with peaks at 654 and 540 nm, respectively. We further design a hexagonal microrods laser cavity with suitable diameter to support whispering gallery modes at red, green and blue wavelength with a linewidth of less than 0.4 nm. Hence, simultaneously excite RGB lasing within the same microcavity and demonstrate white light lasing at room temperature fore the first time. Furthermore, Co-investigator has suggested to use plasmonic effect to improve the lasing characteristics of the white light lasers in order to suit for the practical applications. He led to the fabrication of a nanometer thick silver coated on a SiO2 substrate. Hence, by placing the microrod on an Ag-coated substrate, it is shown that the microrod demonstrate the enhancement of upconversion spontaneous emission through the presence of surface plasmonic resonant by 10 times. In addition, the lasing threshold of the microrod can be reduced by 50% This is because of the formation of low-loss whispering gallery modes, which arise from the coupling between the whispering gallery modes of the bare microrod and the surface plasmonic resonant modes propagating on the surface of the Ag layer. This indicate that plasmonic effect can introduce to the laser cavity to further improve the lasing characteristics of upconversion lasers. Hence, we have confident that our proposed can realize upconversion lasers with performance as good as the commercial available lasing devices. Due to the unique properties of upconversion nanoparticles (i.e. near infrared excitation and visible emission), it is also useful for the application as a probe of heavy metal ions in water. Co-investigator had borrowed of our high performance upconversion nanoparticles to probing of Cu2+ ion. The nanoparticles has core-shell structure and incorporated with CFC to sense heavy metal. It is demonstrated that there is a significant improvement in sensitivity and selectivity due to specific accumulation of analyte ions on the probe. Down to 82 bbp of Cu2+ can be detected using the proposed probes. This work has suggested that upconversion nanoparticles is an alternative method to realize sensor for on-site monitoring of contaminated drinking water with high sensitivity and selectivity even for other heavy metal in water. In conclusion, we have completed all the objectives of this project, furthermore, we find that upconversion nanoparticles has many practical applications such as white-light lighting and heavy metal sensors that may be important to our everyday life.

15303614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303614.value: 1) Design and fabrication of Tm3+ doped core-shell-shell nanoparticles, and realize 5-photon upconversion deep UV lasers (310 nm) under 980 nm excitation at room temperature - see reference 1 paper published in Nature Comm. 2) We demonstrate the use of laser cavity can enhance the upconversion efficiency by an order of magnitude - see reference 2 paper published in ACS Nano. 3) We make us of Tm3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ doping in hexagonal microcavities to achieve white light lasers under 980 nm excitation at room temperature for the first time - see reference 3 paper published in ACS Photon. 4) We further improve the lasing efficiency of the hexagonal microcavities by using plasmonic effect - see reference 4 paper published in Inorganic Chem. 5) We attempt to use the upconversion nanoparticles as a sensor - see reference 5 paper published in Nanoscale Advances.

15303614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303614.value: Our proposed methods to fabricate upconversion nanoparticles lasers is a technical breakthrough because we can achieve deep ultraviolet lasing under 980 nm excitation at room temperature with upconversion efficiency much higher than that reported in the literature so that they have potential to be computerized. Currently, we are working on even short lasing wavelength in the UVC regime - below 250 nm. If we can fabricate a low-loss host material at UVC regime that can be formed the laser microcavities and can sustain high intensity near IR excitation, we should be able to obtain ~220 nm lasing using Tm3+ and Gd3+ ions as the activators.

15303614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303614.value: Deep UV lasers have enormous practical applications - to sterilize bacteria and viruses, decontaminate drinking water and in fluorescence sensors to detect chemicals. Currently, the available deep UV lasers, which are bulky in size and expensive to operate, required upconversion excitation from bulk optical crystals. The available AlGaN based semiconductor lasers still have difficult to reach UVC regime due to the difficult to growth highly doped AlN layers. Here, we developed an alternative method to realize deep UV lasing emission via upconversion through the use of rare earth doped upconversion nanoparticles. With the proper design of the nanoparticles and microcavities, we show that high-efficiency deep UV lasing can be obtained at room temperature under near-IR excitation and the optical properties of the nanoparticles are compatible with the semiconductor materials. In this case, we should be able to integrate the nanoparticles with the commercially available 980 nm semiconductor lasers to form a compact deep UV lasers at low cost.

15303714.label: Project Objectives
15303714.value: To establish the ligand set that promotes d8-d8 metal-metal interaction in dinuclear cyclometallated arylpalladium complexes: We will prepare well-defined dinuclear arylpalladium(II) complexes bearing bridging strong sigma donor ligands. The redox properties of the Pd(II) complexes will be examined by cyclic voltammetry, and the redox couples can be resolved by pulse differential voltammetry. Controlled potential electrolysis would afford the oxidized Pd complexes, which can be studied by spectroelectrochemistry. The d8-d8 metal interaction can be characterized by low-lying metal-metal to ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) and can be assessed by low temperature photoluminescence studies. To establish the role of Pd(III)-Pd(III) in the catalytic carboradical coupling reactions: By oxidation of the Pd(II) precursors with acylsilanes as acyl donors, we plan to prepare the acylpalladium(III, III) complexes bearing bridging strong sigma donor ligands. Kinetic study of the reductive elimination of the Pd(III, III) complexes will be performed along with computational study; the key factors associated with the product turnover will be delineated. To design ligands that enable regioselective and enantioselective C-H functionalizations: Based on the physical studies of the arylpalladium complexes, we will design robust catalysts for the oxidative C-H coupling reactions. In particular, attention will be directed to substrates with oxygen directing groups and unactivated alkanes, which are challenging substrates for C-H acylations.

15303714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303714.value: Catalytic site-selective C-H bond functionalization is receiving current attention for developing atom-economical synthesis. Recently, we achieved Pd(OAc)2-catalyzed oxidative arene acylations with aldehydes as acyl donors and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) as oxidant; aryl ketones were formed in excellent yields and ortho-selectivity [Org. Lett. 2010, 12, 3926; Adv. Syn. Catal. 2011, 353, 2999]. Compared to the Friedel Crafts acylation, the Pd-catalyzed reaction constitutes a powerful route to 1,2-difunctionalized aryl ketones. A principal step of the acylations is the coupling of arylpalladium(II) complexes with acyl radicals.
