15403614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15403614.value: Background: Amongst people with mental disorders, the prevalence of smoking has been reported to be the highest among people with schizophrenia, ranging from 54%-90%. It is more than two to three times (20%-30%) of the general population. The co-occurrence of schizophrenia and smoking will lead to a higher chance of smoking-related diseases such as cardiovascular disease, lung diseases and reduced life expectancy. Currently, there is a large gap in knowledge regarding smoking cessation in people with schizophrenia; there has been few studies examining non-pharmacological interventions in smoking cessation on people with schizophrenia. Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) for mental health disorders has found that it has in general positive outcomes for the clients; improvements were consistently found in a number of studies. ACT is more encouraging compared to traditional methods of smoking cessation, where the individual is seen to be at fault for the habit. To date, no randomized trial has been conducted to compare the effects of ACT in smoking cessation among people with schizophrenia. Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) in enhancing smoking cessation among people with schizophrenia living in the community. Design: This is a randomised controlled trial. Individual, face to face, assessor-blinded with assessments will be conducted before intervention, after intervention, and at the 6th and 12th month after the initial session of ACT intervention. Participants and setting: 140 individuals aged 18 years or older, currently smoking but not undergoing any smoking cessation or similar programme, who were diagnosed with schizophrenia and were referred to 4 community-based mental health rehabilitation settings by medical doctors will be included in this trial. Interventions: Social chats on encouraging medication adherence for 5-10 mins per session, 10 sessions, will be given to subjects allocated to control group (CG), on weekly basis. Subjects of Intervention Group (IG): will additionally be provided 30-45 mins, individual, face to face ACT by trained ACT interventionists per each session. Main outcome measures and data analysis: The primary outcome will be the self-reported not smoking for at least 7 days preceding to the assessment at the 6th and 12th month after the pre-intervention assessment. A comparative analysis of the proportion of smokers who quit smoking in either intervention or control groups at the 6 and 12-month follow-up will be performed according to intention-to-treat principles. Subjects who do not adhere to the study programme (‘lost-to-follow-up’) will be presumed smoking. 背景：精神病者中，以患有精神分裂的有最多人吸煙，由54%至90%不等。這是一般人口的兩至三倍(20-30%)。精神分裂與吸煙的雙生現象會引致更大機會患上與吸煙相關的疾病，例如心臟血管疾病、肝病及壽命的縮短。現時，有關精神分裂病人的戒煙研究有很大的學術空白；也沒有多少研究是關於以非藥物方式介入精神分裂患者的戒煙。針對精神病患的接納與承諾治療 (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy - ACT) 發現，該治療對受助者有整體正面後果；若干研究一致發現有改善。傳統的戒煙方法視患者為有過失，要負上責任，相對而言，ACT更有鼓勵性。至今，從沒有人做過隨機試驗，以比較ACT對精神分裂患者戒煙的果效。 目的：評估接納與承諾治療(ACT)對促進住在社區內的精神分裂患者戒煙的果效 設計：這是隨機受控試驗 (randomised controlled trial)。個人、面對面、由單盲評估人於介入前、介入後、以及ACT首節介入後、六個月和十二個月進行評估 參與者與設施：此研究包括156個18歲或以上人士，現時吸煙，沒有接受任何戒煙或類似計劃，被診斷為精神分裂及被醫生轉介到4間社區為本的精神康復設施。 介入：被分配到對照組(CG)的實驗對象接受一次簡短的鼓勵戒煙之教育講解，以及獲發一本自助戒煙的小冊子。介入組(IG)：除接受一次簡短戒煙之教育講解，會額外提供10節，每星期一次，由受過訓練的治療師的ACT面談。每節為時20至30分鐘。 主要結果量度及數據分析：介入前評估、之後的六個月及十二個月再次評估，若自我報告之前七天沒有吸煙，是為主要研究結果。根據治療動機原則，會進行比較分析六個月及十二個月介入組或對照組的吸煙者戒煙的比例。沒有堅持研究(無法跟進)的研究對象會被認定為吸煙。

15403614.label: Realisation of objectives
15403614.value: All the proposed objectives were completed but only 92.9% proposed sample size was achieved. We faced several challenges that ultimately led to the failure to recruit a sufficient number of samples within the study period. The challenges are 1. Participants living in different institutions, except for government-run residential homes, generally, we could approach only a few potential eligible participants in private homes. 2. We have taken a lot of time to obtain the institutions’ approval for approach potential participants. 3. Motivation to quit, 4. nicotine was found to have a soothing effect on the schizophrenic symptoms for some patients, and this is exactly when things get really complicated. We conducted a prospective individually randomized controlled, double-blinded parallel trial which was registered on the clinical trial website (https://clinicaltrials.gov: NCT03253445). Randomization was carried out according to a code generated by the computer with a block size of six and a 1:1 allocation. All participants gave their written informed consent to participate in the study, and the study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The study population consisted of current smokers who had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and were living in one of the 51 community-based residential mental health rehabilitation settings in Hong Kong. Included criteria is schizophrenic patients aged 18 or over, had smoked at least one cigarette daily in the past 30 days, and were able to communicate in Cantonese. Those patients with disorientation, developmental disabilities, and/or an organic mental disorder are not eligible. Schizophrenic smokers who had received a diagnosis of alcohol or drug dependence in the year preceding recruitment, whose medication regime had been revised in the last 3 months, or who were participating in a smoking cessation programme at the time of the recruitment were also excluded . Potential subjects were referred by staff of the residential settings to meetthe research assistant of the project in the residential rehabilitation centre in privacy for screening. Eligible patients were invited to take part in the trial. Recruitment was conducted over a period of about 1.5 years between May 2015 and December 2016 in halfway houses, long stay care homes, Integrated community centres for mental wellness (ICCMW), sheltered workshops, and residential settings run by different non-governmental organizations and private sector groups. Participants in both groups received the usual care, consisting of a 5-minute brief educational talk encouraging smoking cessation plus a self-help written leaflet on smoking cessation. In addition to the usual care, all participants in the ACT Intervention Group were offered 10 weekly face-to-face individual sessions of ACT by a trained therapist. Each session lasted about 30 minutes. Most components of the ACT intervention in this study were drawn from an ACT manual developed by the ACT founder and his team (Hayes & et al, 2006) while specific metaphors for smoking cessation were extracted from relevant studies (Bricker, Mann, Marek, Liu & Peterson, 2010). Based on a previous study (Mak & Loke, 2015); some metaphors and exercises were modified to fit the Chinese target group. The intervention was an integration of psycho-education and the six core ACT processes (acceptance, present, values, committed action, self as context, and defusion). The aim was to help the participants to (1) increase their acceptance of thoughts and feelings related to cigarette cravings and withdrawal symptoms; (2) clarify their life values and enhance engagement with those values; (3) build up behavior repertoire in line with their committed life values and which the participants can use choose and even in the presence of cravings and/or withdrawal symptoms. For the control group, we provided a brief educational talk of about 5 minutes encouraging the participants to quit smoking, as well as a self-help quitting leaflet on smoking cessation. Ten sessions of face-to-face educational support were provided on a weekly basis, based on the leaflet material available to the public. Each session lasted for about 5-10 minutes. We compared the baseline characteristics of the patients in the intervention and control groups using an χ2 test for ordinal variables and a t-test for continuous variables. For the primary and secondary outcomes, we used an χ2 test to assess the effect of the intervention and calculated the absolute difference in percentages with a 95% confidence interval (CI) for the primary and secondary outcomes. For process measures, generalized estimating equation (GEE) models, with attendance rate in the 10-session treatment as a covariate, were used to assess treatment processes from baseline to the follow-up assessments. GEE models accounted for the dependence between repeated measures within individuals and can take into account missing data (Faul, Erdfelder, Lang, Buchner, 2007). The interactions with each time variable of the treatment groups were assessed to examine whether the groups differed significantly with regard to changes in outcomes. All patients were included in the analysis based on the intention-to-treat principle whenever applicable. Analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM, Armonk, NY, USA). References: • Bricker JB, Mann SL, Marek PM, Liu J, Peterson AV. Telephone-delivered acceptance and commitment therapy for adult smoking cessation: A feasibility study. Nicotine Tob Res 2010;12:454-8. • Faul F, Erdfelder E, Lang AG, Buchner A. G* Power 3: A flexible statistical power analysis program for the social, behavioral, and biomedical sciences. Behav Res Methods. 2007;39:175-91. • Flaxman PE, Blackledge JT, Bond FW. Acceptance and commitment therapy: Distinctive features. Routledge; 2010. • Hayes SC, Luoma JB, Bond FW, Masuda A, Lillis J. Acceptance and commitment therapy: Model, processes and outcomes. Behav Res Ther 2006;44:1-25. • Mak YW, Loke AY. The acceptance and commitment therapy for smoking cessation in the primary health care setting: a study protocol. BMC public health 2015;15:105.

15403614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15403614.value: Results of an χ2 test to assess the effect of the intervention and calculated the absolute difference in percentages with a 95% confidence interval (CI) for the primary and secondary outcomes on the 130 participants enrolled and randomized, with 65 participants in each of the ACT and control groups, we observed a trend of difference in self-reported 7-day point prevalence at the 6-month (primary outcome) and 12-month follow-ups. The 12.3% and 10.8% rates of abstinence in the intervention group were greater than the 7.7% and 7.7% rates for the control group, although no statistically significant differences between the groups were observed. A similar trend of difference in the biochemically validated quit rates was also found in the 6-month and 12-month follow-ups. The 9.2% and 9.2% rates of biochemically validated abstinence in intervention group were greater than the 4.6% and 6.2% rates for the control group, while the self-reported smoking reduction and quit attempt rates were slightly lower in the ACT group than in the education group at both the 6- and 12-month follow-ups. The mean level of exhaled carbon monoxide (CO) in the intervention group was 13.3 ppm at the 6-month follow-up, falling to 10.1 ppm at the 12-month follow-up, which was significantly lower than the levels seen in the control group (18 ppm). Results of GEE results on smoking-specific experiential avoidance (psychological inflexibility), participants in the ACT reported a gradual decrease in their AIS scores from baseline to the 12-month follow-up, while participants in the education group showed a trend of increase. Significant group differences were observed at 6 months (p=0.02) and 12 months (p=0.04), with an estimated effect size of 0.29 at 6 months and 0.27 at 12 months. For ACT-specific experiential avoidance, participants in the ACT group showed a gradual increase in psychological flexibility over the study period, whereas participants in the social support group remained relatively stable. A significant group difference in AAQII scores was observed at 12 months (p=0.03), with an estimated effect size of 0.27.

15403614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15403614.value: The present study found that ACT led to a reduction in avoidance and inflexibility and level of exhaled carbon monoxide test, but not to an increase in the success rates for smoking cessation. Nevertheless, one significant achievement in the use of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy was the enhanced psychological flexibility of the participants assigned to the ACT group. This process of identifying avoidance behaviour and developing a more flexible approach to addressing it is central to this intervention and is regarded as an important process indicator supporting the use of ACT for making behavioural changes. The findings support further research on using ACT in patients from wider socio-demographic and clinical characteristics among Asian/Chinese populations and/or different clinical settings. A larger-scale research may allow investigation of the relationships between perceived outcomes, psychological flexibility (mediator), and smoking cessation outcomes of ACT using both quantitative and qualitative approaches. It is also important to have further research on the cost-effectiveness of ACT in patients with different types of mental disorders and physical health problems. Two studies of ACT were established and sent to apply Health Medical Research Fund to further investigate the clinical efficacy of this intervention approach for wider patient populations.

15403614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15403614.value: Various approaches have been put forward and tried out to help the patients with schizophrenia to quit smoking, with very limited success. These patients tend to use cigarettes as a remedy to the symptoms, if not cure. Another problem with the conventional quitting program is the tendency to put the blame on smokers for failure, implicitly or even without proclaiming it. The study is an attempt to help the schizophrenic smokers, an under-represented segment of population, to have successful cessation using ACT. We found that ACT led to a reduction in avoidance and inflexibility and decrease in exhaled carbon monoxide, but not to an increase in the success rates for smoking cessation. Nevertheless, one significant achievement in the use of ACT was the enhanced psychological flexibility of the participants assigned to the ACT group. This process of identifying avoidance behaviour and developing a more flexible approach to addressing it is central to this intervention and is regarded as an important process indicator supporting the use of ACT for making behavioural changes. It is a virgin land waiting to be explored and by far, the results appear pointing in the right direction but deserved more attention and future input.

15404414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15404414.value: On the basis of the findings of an earlier project on the representation of war in Asian films in which the PI collaborated with two international scholars, this project proposes to study specifically the memory of World War II in Hong Kong in the two decades after the 1945 Japanese surrender. For the most part, scholarship in this area has so far favored the use of official records and memoirs and oral histories of participants in and survivors of the War, treating them more or less as “authentic” accounts of the horror of those years. These efforts can thus be described as “historical,” insofar that they set out to reconstruct and document what transpired during the war years. And while there exist isolated studies with an approach more akin to that of cultural studies, such as the depiction of the War in Asian cinema, nothing systematic has been attempted to arrive at an understanding the diverse attitudes towards the War, using films and other products of popular culture in Hong Kong as the primary materials. This project seeks to address this gap in the current scholarship by taking a broad survey of a range of popular culture genres, such as children’s comics, dime novels, films (both local and imported), works of fiction thinly disguised as reportage, newspaper cartoons and radio plays, with an aim to analyze the intricate process through which a momentous historical event, such as World War II, is remembered. Rather than recovering a “true picture” of the War, the project will study the way that the War is re-imagined and re-created in the popular consciousness, where accuracy of representation may only be of secondary concern. The results of this project will take the form of a series of academic articles to be published in internationally recognized journals in relevant disciplines. They will also be disseminated through direct communications with experts in the field and discussions with colleagues at academic conferences. They will contribute to current scholarship in these areas: 1) Hong Kong history, 2) War and memory, and 3) Studies of diasporic imagination. 有關第二次世界大戰的回憶的研究，多從歷史研究角度出發，較多偏重官方的記錄文獻，參戰者或生還者的回憶錄或傳記，以及他們的口述歷史等。間中亦有從文化研究切入，如戰爭在電影中的呈現等，在這命題的作出極具意義的嘗試。 然而，目前的研究還缺乏對二次大戰香港戰後的通俗文化所產生的回響作出一個系統的考察。本研究計劃發掘其他通俗文化的類型，像廉紙文學(pulp literature) 、漫畫及連環圖、廣播劇、電影、報告文學等，目的不在於還原戰爭的真相，而是透過這些通俗文化產物去了解大眾意識如何銓釋及重構這件歷史大事。 預計本計劃的成果將涉及下列三方面的研究:香港史、戰爭與回憶、流散研究(diaspora studies)。

15404414.label: Realisation of objectives
15404414.value: The objectives of the project have by and large been fully achieved. Objective 2 and Objective 3 have been realized in full., For Objective 2, the PI reached out to historians, literary scholars and film studies scholars. In particular, he held an international conference in May 2015: Men of War: Masculinity and War in the 20th Century at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, with participation of scholars from the Netherlands, Japan, the US, Israel, Mainland China, and Hong Kong. A long-term relationship is now in place between the PI and the Institute of the Study of War, Holocaust and Genocide in the Netherlands, where the PI gave a presentation of his work in November 2016. The contact with the Institute has resulted in a research project for the PI at the Netherlands Institute of Advanced Study in the Humanities and Social Sciences in 2018. For Objective 3, the PI has made preliminary but substantive investigations in other genres of recollection of war not included in Objective 1, most notably ghost stories and oral histories. Ethnographic studies of the ghost stories in Hong Kong remains scant, with only scattered articles here and there and a special volume of “Recognizing Ghosts” in the Winter 2014 issue of Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese. While modern society has produced urban anxieties that find reflections in ghost stories with different themes, the brutalities and sufferings of Hong Kong during World War II are still remembered in ghost stories that are associated with different sites and place names in Hong Kong, testament to the tenacity of war memories. These stories are purportedly traceable to specific incidents during the occupation years in Hong Kong. While the specifics have yet to be verified, for the purpose of the project, that perhaps is beside the point. The PI has also looked into the results of oral history projects that have come into existence in the last two decades in connection with the way WWII is remembered. Many of these oral history projects were inspired by and undertaken in the spirit of arriving at a closure on the chapter of colonial rule in Hong Kong history. WWII being an important event in Hong Kong past, it is only natural that in their recollections, many interviewees touch upon the years of the Occupation as well as the years leading to and following it. My explorations have taken me to these sources: “Voices of Hong Kong” of Oral History Archives, The Hong Kong Heritage Project, Promotion Project of the Historical Archives of Anti-Japanese War in Hong Kong, Hong Kong Oral History Archives, the oral history materials in Daily Life of Hong Kong during the Japanese Occupation by Lau Chiu-pang and Chow Ka-kin, and several others whose primary focus is not on WWII such as the Community Involvement Broadcast Community Oral History of Radio and Television Hong Kong, and Chinese Women and Hong Kong Christianity: An Oral History. These forays have allowed the PI to take note of the diversity of representations of everyday life in Japanese-occupied Hong Kong, combining to give a very different picture from the textbook version that emphasizes on the sufferings of the occupied and the arrogance of the occupiers, and the antagonism between the two. While there is little disagreement over the bleakness of life during the Japanese occupation, many interviewees took the time to strive for a degree of normalcy and hope in their daily life. Taken together, the rich resources of oral histories are something that promises fruitful explorations. The two projected articles stated in Objective 1 are in progress at this point. The first article examines a sub-genre of dime novels popular in the 1950s and 1960s – the spy thriller by Qiu Zhang. Not much is known about Qiu, who, as extant materials indicate, came from a military background and spent most of the Hong Kong occupied years in Shaoguan in northern Guangdong. He is the creator of a number of spy novels focusing on Agent No. 5, a Chinese spy from Chongqing, and his interactions with the British intelligence and military in Hong Kong before the Japanese occupation. A parallel plot is also developed on his involvement with his assistants as well as two Japanese female agents, all having gone through espionage training with Agent No. 5 at an unspecified time before the onset of Japanese aggression against China. Such is the background allows Qiu Zhang to weave his fantastic tales of adventures, but at the same time to give voice to the popular understanding of the reason behind the “fall of Hong Kong.” My article examines Qiu’s rendition of the intricate ethnic and racial relationship in the unfolding of the war: between the British colonizers, the indigenous Hong Kongers, Chinese from the mainland, Chinese of Hong Kong’s upper social stratum (高等華人), the South Asians who served in the British Army, the Canadians who were dispatched to Hong Kong in its defense, and the ruthless, vindictive and at times laughable Japanese aggressors. The second article looks at another neglected memory of Hong Kong, that of the non-antagonistic relationship between the occupiers and the occupied in the war period. Making use of what I have read of the oral histories mentioned above, I look at the recollections of those who had the occasions to interact with Japanese in their daily life: as co-workers, students and teachers, service-providers and clients, subordinates and supervisors and so on. It appears that language (knowledge of Japanese) plays as important a role as the depth of personal contact with Japanese in shaping the way they remember their war-time experience. These two articles are at different stages of preparation, with the first article closer to completion than the second. The PI has had a difficult time to conceptualize the articles in the beginning, and hence the delay in fully realizing Objective 1 of the project, but now anticipates finishing the articles by the end of the year, when he will submit them for publication.

15404414.label: Major findings and research outcome
15404414.value: The major research findings consist of the following: 1. In the context of renewed interest in the study of the history of the Japanese occupation days in Hong Kong in recent years, this study looks at the way WWII is remembered in Hong Kong popular culture, which takes a variety of forms, depending on the genre one chooses to look at. As is the nature of popular culture, there exists a high degree of cross-fertilization among genres, where a story might emerge first in one genre and migrate into another, the most notable example is the permeability between dime novels, radio drama, and film. In other words, a basic plot is retold many times, subjecting the recurrent themes to be treated in different ways. 2. However, close examination on some of the genres reveals the fact that generic characteristics come to bear on the shaping of the memories. The PI’s investigation into Qiu Zhang’s novels about the espionage activities before the fall of Hong Kong shows that Qiu consciously models his works on spy thrillers popular internationally at the time. Against a background of growing anxiety over the advent of the war, for example, Qiu creates the intrepid Agent No. 5, handsome and selfless, who is caught in an emotional web with two Japanese female agents and his own assistants. Such a set-up enables Qiu to bring the personal and international considerations into the crafting of the memory of the World War II. 3. The project serves to underscore the complexity of the remembrance of the War which is often simplistically recollected as a period of unrelieved doom and gloom. Without downplaying the brutality of the War, the suffering that it inflicts, and the bleakness of life under military assault and occupation, the materials that the PI examines add details to the “master memory” and modify it. Some personal recollections capture the heroism of everyday life as people strived to maintain a degree of normalcy in the chaos of the day. The relationship between the occupiers and the occupied is not necessarily marked with antagonism, allowing a different conception of “them” and “us.”

15404414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15404414.value: Box 5.3 Realization of Objectives above has pointed to a number of areas that promises fruitful inquiries: 1.other genres of popular culture that the PI has not had the chance to deal with, such as ghost stories, radio drama, pulp literature and so on, are all repositories of popular feelings of the war; 2. oral histories remain one of the most underused trove of information. The PI's second article has barely scratched the surface. What remains will contribute to a nuanced understanding of the memory of war upon examination; 3. war memories in Hong Kong is a topic that lends itself to comparison with other places. In the course of his research, for example, the PI is alerted to many references that point to the comparability between Hong Kong and Singapore. The PI has been awarded a fellowship to study point#3 by the Netherlands Institute of Advanced Study in the Humanities and Social Sciences from September 2018 to January 2019, during which he will also make use of oral histories.

15404414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15404414.value: This project sets out to study the way World War II is remembered in popular culture in Hong Kong. The potential scope of enquiry is wide, including a wide range of popular culture genres, but the PI has taken a detailed look at 1) the spy thriller of Qiu Zhang, who in his fantastic tales of espionage intrigues, paints a picture of intricate racial and ethnic relationship that in a significant way accounts for the failure of Hong Kong defense in 1941, leading to the "fall of Hong Kong"; and 2) the non-antagonistic interactions between the Japanese occupiers and the indigenous Hong Kongers during the occupation years from the information given in oral histories in Hong Kong. 15405014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15405014.value: This research proposal aims to apply and further develop a digital annotation scheme to analyze an expanded corpus of comics from 1970s to 2000s in terms of both multimodal complexity and narratival development. The combination of text and image has stimulated a number of studies in both Humanities and Digital Humanities, aiming at elucidating the relationship between pictures and words as elements used in the creation of meanings. Comicbooks, because of their complex multimodal narrative, have motivated an expanding range of studies examining the semiotic labor of elements on the page. Such studies predominantly present interpretative analyses of isolated elements without a solid empirical basis that sufficiently supports the explanation of the visual-verbal relationship in co-creating meanings in comicbooks. To address this methodological insufficiency it is essential to develop a systematic framework of annotation and description that enables critical reading and identification of meaning-making patterns involving multiple semiotic resources (Walsh, 2012). Our annotation scheme was designed in close cooperation between the Bremen-Hong Kong research team. It connects with existent academic accounts of comics by locating meaning-making features, covering for the first time page layout as a primary building block in the meaning-making process in comicbooks. This allows our research to go beyond feature-identification and elucidate how different semiotic elements construe the narrative in tandem. The corpus, that includes comics and graphic novels for cross-analysis and validation, provides additional data that will facilitate refinement of our established digital annotation system and the collation of textual examples of various visual complexities. Further, the project will provide annotated illustrative corpora of complex text-image combinations to the research community. Our corpus-based, empirical annotation of comics as multimodal documents is expected to yield four outcomes: (1) to enable a re-conceptualization of research methodology in analyzing comics texts; (2) to provide access to the understanding of diachronic changes in narrative construction in comics; (3) systematically demonstrate the pictorial turn (Mitchell, 1995) in comics, where the meaning-making focus has shifted from the verbal language to the visual in comics texts; (4) to make considerable contribution to the development of theory and research in the field of visual arts and communication, and Digital Humanities as a whole.

15405014.label: Realisation of objectives
15405014.value: As the basis for our studies, we first created an archive of comicbooks that could provide data for subsequent diachronic empirical investigations. The archive was built primarily focusing on U.S. superhero comics as this tradition is broadly recognized as one of the most long-lived. Regularity in publication is important for a diachronic study because it brings to the corpus a greater variety of artists using the semiotic systems under investigation. Superhero comics have been published continuously over the decades and are not particularly connected to single authors, as for example Tintin is attached to Hergé or Astro Boy to Osamu Tezuka. The archive was initially based more specifically on a collection of reprints of Superman and Batman stories curated by decades, published by DC Comics. These two characters show the greatest continuity and regularity in publications and could provide samples for the corpus consistently across decades. Each year represented in our corpus consequently contains stories concerning these two characters, although more characters and stories within the same broad genre were added as necessary to meet our targeted number of corpus samples. Altogether 1260 pages were selected for annotation, spread across seven full decades, starting in 1940 and moving on to the 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s and ending in 2009. The 2010s were not included, although data is available in our archive, because this is still an on-going period and also because it appears to be undergoing considerable changes due, on the one hand, to advances in technology affecting the process of production, circulation and consumption of comics and, on the other, to increasingly strong intertextual ties with other cultural industry media -- most significantly cinema -- that may be influencing design decisions and so affect comics' communicative potential. As such, the 2010s is still a story to be told when we consider a diachronic approach to the study of comics organized around decades. The corpus was organized by selecting three pages from each story available so as to cover a variety of stories and, consequently, of artists, the assumed principal users of the communicative system under investigation. Following these criteria, we collected 18 pages per year that led to a total of 180 pages per decade. From within each story selected, we included the first three odd pages after the title page. Title pages were excluded as they are designed in terms of layout with different purposes in mind, setting out story title, credits, and so on, which all affect page layout. For similar reasons, spreads -- that is, double pages to be read as single large pages -- were also excluded from the corpus. These pages would need to be examined in their own right. When any of the initial three pages selected was a page spread, we instead took the next single odd page available. Finally, as mentioned above, since we could not fill all years with the same number of pages relying on Superman and Batman publications alone, we included other publications from the same genre in the corpus selection. The final corpus was then composed of contributions from 420 stories, representing 100 writers and 124 pencilers. Generally speaking, in the process of comics production, writers are responsible for the script while pencilers are in charge of drawings, deciding page layout, number of panels and shape -- how much information a writer provides to a penciler varies and even if a sketchy version of each page is provided, the penciler can still modify as deemed necessary depending on narrative flow. Our aim with this corpus design was to guarantee a broad range of artists who, working within well-established titles, would bring in their personal style and exploration of the semiotic capabilities of the medium while still being constrained by established institutions and editorial guidelines. As a thriving industry, the publication of superhero comics has been historically characterized by a high-volume, production-line structure with constrained spaces for experimentation. This area can therefore be expected to exhibit a more homogeneous organization and so be more supportive of the search for empirically motivated patterning. Concomitantly with building the corpus, the system network was refined and considerably extended to include, in the taxonomy, specific features that will allow capturing in more detail semiotic changes across decades. The process included extensive work with the research team, coordinated by the PI at PolyU and Prof. John Bateman, Co-I, at the University of Bremen. The system network was applied to the corpus annotation using the free access UAM Corpus Tool for Text and Image Annotation, developed by Mick O’Donnel , which guarantees the accessibility and application by other research teams in the future. The process of annotation was carried out with the assistant of two student helpers who received extensive training for the use of the software and categories of analysis. For that, a manual and a glossary were developed and students attended training sessions conducted by the PI and the Research Assistant/Associate. At a second stage, the student helpers annotated a sample of 20 pages, each, and we ran inter-ater reliability – it was necessary to repeat the sample annotation for three rounds, each time identifying annotation problems (such as high discrepancy) and discussed with student helpers until we reached acceptable agreement scores, which allowed us to move to corpus annotation per se. Since the corpus designed was distributed across years, with each year containing 18 pages, its segmentation and annotation was performed by assigning each member of the research group specific years across decade. The two student helpers received a higher workload while both the Research Associate and the PI were each assigned a smaller number of years from each decade, to ensure we were aware of possible difficulties and challenges with the research process. Following annotation, the UAM Image Tool was also used to export the annotation results as a csv-file for statistical analysis. The resulting file defined a table with 107 rows, one for each annotation feature defined in the classification network, and 1262 columns consisting of one column for each page annotated and two additional columns identifying the choice points in the classification network and corresponding values of either zero (not selected) or one (selected) for each annotation feature defined. This table served as the basis for the various analyses reported in the research outcome; all results discussed, as well as the corresponding graphs and tables, were produced on the basis of this data using R (R Core Team 2016) (R3.3.3, 2017) within RStudio (Version 1.1.442, 2018). A sub-corpus of 378 pages was selected by isolating the first three years of each decade (years 0, 1 and 2) in order to perform content analysis in order to address the pictorial turn in comics, more specifically, whether the number of words has been reduced in comics. The methodology followed that of previous studies (Veloso and Bateman, 2014; Veloso, 2018) and consisted of the isolation of language that consisted of 55 columns and 2079 rows, that included page code, number of panels per page, number of caption, content transcription, speech bubble content and semiotic properties that point to relevance for future research. Results show a decrease in the reduction of words in captions but a stable occurrence of words in speech bubbles.

15405014.label: Major findings and research outcome
15405014.value: The study demonstrates (see Veloso et al.; Bateman et al., both under revision) through empirical results that comics are not more complex today compared with the past, but complexity is of varying degrees across decades, with properties varying on different degrees across decades. The research demonstrates that it is possible to study comics from a quantitative perspective to elucidate aspects hitherto only asserted in broad terms. The research demonstrates that it is possible to make page design accessible to empirical study, as a more refined set of classification categories allows us to track changing visual styles in comics; the research provides a model for research with multimodally complex texts, from corpus size, annotation to analysis. Results were reported in a number of international conferences in the areas of linguistics, multimodality and comics studies, from which researchers benefitted largely with feedback. Valuable insights have been reported in research articles already published, with two under revision, and other two papers currently under preparation for submission.

15405014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15405014.value: A more abstract level of description may provide contact with issues of narrative and intended meanings and how layout contribute to story-telling, an area still to be explored. The system of annotation allows for the study, based on empirical evidence, of issues of style, still here a term used vaguely – the taxonomy developed for this study may provide with evidence of what style constitutes for specific artists, for instance. The taxonomy can still be developed into new levels of delicacy for specific features and, applied to larger corpus – now that the methodology has been established and demonstrated to work through the publication of peer reviewed articles – to apply knowledge of structure on content, that is, how different features may contribute to narrative.

15405014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15405014.value: The combination of text and image has stimulated a number of studies in both Humanities and Digital Humanities, aiming at elucidating the relationship between pictorial and verbal elements used in the creation of meanings. Comicbooks, because of their complex multimodal narrative, have motivated an expanding range of studies examining the semiotic labor of elements on the page. Therefore, this research applies and further develops a digital annotation scheme to analyze an expanded corpus - a data set organized according to very specific criteria – of 1260 pages of super-hero comics published between 1940 and 2009. Annotated corpora then support the identification of patterns involving multiple semiotic resources more effectively than is currently possible. Our annotation scheme was designed in close cooperation between researchers at PolyU and the University of Bremen, Germany. The study demonstrates through empirical results that comics are not more complex today than they were in the past – complexity varies in different degrees across decades, that is, some properties emerge while other fade out, while others do seem to be steadily used across decades but with slight changes that seem to give them a perceptually different look but still based on basic organizing principles.

15405514.label: Project Objectives
15405514.value: To investigate the relationship between valence-reducing phenomena and the overt marking of speaker affectedness in Chinese, and potentially in other languages as well; To trace the development of versatile transfer verb constructions—in particular ‘give’ and ‘take’ constructions—and identify their structural type (e.g. causative, passive or unaccusative) and their pragmatic function(s) (e.g. event enabling, agent defocusing, adversity marking and/or speaker affectedness marking) as these constructions extend from 3- and 2-place predicates to 1-place predicates; To examine diachronic evidence to determine whether there is a robust stepwise (3 > 2 > 1) valence-reduction progression in the history of the Chinese language, using large-scale historical databases; To provide a pragmatic analysis of the subjective—and potentially also intersubjective and interpersonal—characteristics of the valence-reduced ‘give’/'take’ constructions in Chinese (e.g. Mandarin, Hui’an, Chaozhou, Cantonese) conversations, and to subsequently compare subtle differences in pragmatic interpretation (if any) in the use of ‘give’ constructions in different varieties of Chinese; To compare valence-reducing phenomena in Chinese with those of other languages, in particular the versatile ‘give’/'take’ constructions of neighboring and contact languages (e.g. Manchu-Tungusic, Indo-Aryan, Austronesian), and enhance our knowledge of the typology of valence-reduced constructions; To contribute to theoretical research that investigates the interfaces between semantics (meaning), syntax (structure) and discourse (pragmatics); To contribute to classroom pedagogy by providing second language learners with a principled explanation for differences in meaning that are triggered by differences in valence and their ensuing consequences in the emergence of new grammatical and pragmatic functions (e.g. differences in pragmatic meaning between factual utterances such as hua si le ‘The flower withered and died’ and speaker-affected utterances such as hua gei (ta) si le ‘Unfortunately, the flower withered and died’).

To compare valence-reducing phenomena in Chinese with those of other languages, in particular the versatile ‘give’/'take’ constructions of neighboring and contact languages (e.g. Manchu-Tungusic, Indo-Aryan, Austronesian), and enhance our knowledge of the typology of valence-reduced constructions;
To contribute to theoretical research that investigates the interfaces between semantics (meaning), syntax (structure) and discourse (pragmatics);

To contribute to classroom pedagogy by providing second language learners with a principled explanation for differences in meaning that are triggered by differences in valence and their ensuing consequences in the emergence of new grammatical and pragmatic functions (e.g. differences in pragmatic meaning between factual utterances such as hua si le ‘The flower withered and died’ and speaker-affected utterances such as hua gei (ta) si le ‘Unfortunately, the flower withered and died’).

15405514.label: Realisation of objectives
15405514.value: We have fully achieved objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 (100%), and we have achieved 80% of objective 5. Thus far, we have published 3 journal articles (in Linguistics, Diachronica and Faits de Langues), and we have submitted 2 journal articles and 1 handbook chapter for review (to Lingua, Language and Linguistics, The Routledge Handbook of Chinese Discourse Analysis. We have been most productive in analyzing the relationship between valence reduction and speaker affectedness marking for two Asian languages--namely, Chinese and Korean. Work on Indo-Aryan languages (e.g. Hindi and Odia) and on Austronesian languages (e.g. Malay/Indonesian) are still in progress, and we hope to see some publications in the next two years. We were not able to continue with our analysis of the Manchu language as originally planned, because our consultant had left for University College London. In its place, however, we have begun to examine the pragmatic functions of the voice system of Mongolian, with the help of our research collaborators Gegentana and Benjamin Brosig. In the course of exploring potential speaker-affectedness constructions in Mongolian, we found a fascinating paradigm of postnominal possessive markers with affective functions. Preliminary findings for this new study were reported at the Workshop on Diachrony of Nominalization and Nominalizers during the 7th International Conference on the Syntax of the World's Languages (SWL-7) in Mexico City in 2016. We now have a paper submitted to Journal of Pragmatics (Brosig, Gegentana & Yap, under review). Although this paper acknowledges partial funding from this project, we will report it as a direct output from Brosig's postdoctoral project (1-YWOU). Specific achievements for each objective: Objective 1: We completed 1 paper (Chen & Yap, 2018) showing how causative GIVE constructions in some Chinese varieties (e.g. Mandarin and Southern Min) develop into middle constructions that express the speaker's affectedness (e.g. hua gei si le). This paper sheds light on the relationship between valence-reduced constructions and speaker stance. In addition, we completed 1 paper (Yap & Ahn, under review) showing how Korean -i causatives develop into -i passives and -i middles, initially with frequent adversative readings. We also completed 2 papers (Ahn & Yap, 2017; Ahn & Yap, under review) showing how Korean -eci middles develop into -eci passives. Crucially, the development of Korean -i involves valence reduction, while the development of Korean -eci involves valence increment. These Korean studies show that speaker-affectedness constructions can emerge through both valence-reducing and valence-incrementing phenomena. Objective 2: Rich diachronic insights were obtained mostly for Korean (Ahn & Yap, 2017; Yap & Ahn, under review). The Korean studies provided evidence of both valence-reducing (causative-to-passive and causative-to-middle) and valence-incrementing (middle-to-passive) phenomena within the Korean voice system, indicating that valence changes in either direction could contribute to the emergence of speaker stance, although contextual and socio-interactional analysis are still needed to determine the type of speaker stance that emerges. Our diachronic insights for Chinese build on previous works by others (e.g. Chappell, Peyraube & Wu (2011) on Southern Min kang7). By adding a usage frequency analysis, we now have a fuller description of approximately when and how transfer verbs become recruited for pragmatic uses. Speaker affectedness readings emerged relatively late in Modern Chinese, crucially after the transfer verbs have grammaticalized into highly versatile case markers for a wide range of semantic roles. In the case of Southern Min transfer verb ka 'provide, share', the case marking functions include comitative, patient/theme, benefactive/malefactive, and speaker-affectedness marking--the latter in [NP ka gua VP] constructions that include complaints, pleas and threats/warnings. In the case of Mandarin and Southern Min GIVE constructions, the GIVE-derived case markers are able to signal the presence of elidable affected arguments (or what C.-T. Huang (2013) refers to as 'phantom affectees'), including not only the affected patients but also the affected speaker and third person referents. Objective 3: Our diachronic analyses reveal the following chronological sequence in the directionality of valence-change phenomena involving Chinese GIVE and Korean -i constructions: 3-place predicates (e.g. causatives) > 2-place predicates (e.g. passives) and 1-place predicates (e.g. middles, including speaker-affected constructions), but there is no evidence of direct syntactic derivation. On the contrary, our analysis reveals that semantic generalization often induces syntactic reanalysis. Diachronic evidence from Korean also points to the viability of a middle-to-passive extension. There is thus far no evidence of a passive-to-middle development, which is consistent with a robust tendency across languages (see Haspelmath 1988; Heine & Kuteva 2002, 2007). Objective 4: Comparisons were made between different varieties of Chinese. Mandarin and Southern Min varieties were found to have highly grammaticalized ‘give’ constructions which could yield speaker-affected middle constructions. Previous studies indicate that extensions from causative to passive uses are common across Chinese varieties. Our study, which focuses on extensions from causative to middle uses, reveals great variation within the Sinitic language family, with severe restrictions found in dialects such as Hong Kong Cantonese and Shanghai Wu. In terms of pragmatic differences, our cross-dialectal analysis of middle GIVE constructions in Chinese reveals that mainland Mandarin speakers tend to focus more on a causative interpretation (often accompanied by a hint of blame assignment), while Southern Min speakers tend to focus more on a resultative state interpretation (often accompanied by expressions of perplexity at some adverse outcome rather than on blame assignment). These differences are subtle and deserve further investigation using larger population and corpus samples, and across more Chinese varieties. Objective 5: In terms of etymology, our analysis indicates that many language make extensive use of verbal sources as voice markers. A case in point is the pan-Chinese use of GIVE constructions. However, although many languages recruit voice markers from verbal sources (e.g. Thai thuuk 'hit', Malay kena 'touch', Korean -eci < ci 'fall'), nominal sources have also been identified. For example, evidence from Korean suggests that its voice marker -i appears to be derived from its proximal demonstrative i 'this'). Different etymological histories help to account for the variations seen in the patterns of valence changes (e.g. causative-to-passive; causative-to-middle; middle-to-passive), but worth noting is the absence (thus far) of counterdirectionality in valence change. Our next step is to further investigate the voice systems of Indo-Aryan and Austronesian languages in terms of the relationship between valence change and subtle differences in speaker stance, an area that is still under-researched. We are indicating an 80% achievement rate for Objective 5, mainly because we are still in the process of preparing publications for the Indo-Aryan and Austronesian languages. Objective 6: We have now provided diachronic evidence from Chinese and Korean to show how semantic extensions accompanied by syntactic facilitations and constraints often give rise to pragmatic uses whereby the speaker can express their subjective and intersubjective stance in discourse. In this respect, our findings contribute to research studies on the interface between semantics, syntax and pragmatics. Our ongoing crosslinguistic investigations into the voice systems of Mongolic, Indo-Aryan and Austronesian languages will also better position us to compare valence-change phenomena between verb-final (e.g. Korean), verb-initial (e.g. Malay/Indonesian) and verb-medial (e.g. Chinese) languages. Objective 7: We have been able to use the insights from our findings pertaining to valence-change phenomena for pedagogical purposes, more specifically, to explain the pragmatic differences between different voice constructinos, both in grammar instruction courses and in extended writing assignments for discourse analysis courses.

15405514.label: Major findings and research outcome
15405514.value: Our study has shed light on how valence change phenomeana--particularly causative-to-passive and causative-to-middle developments--give rise to constructions with speaker-affectedness readings. We now have an in-depth understanding of the relationship between causative, passive and middle constructions within the voice system of Chinese (with a special focus on Mandarin and Southern Min varieties). In addition, we have identified pragmatic differences in speaker stance associated with regional and dialectal variations. From a crosslinguistic perspective, we have identified similar valence-reducing changes in Korean, but at the same time we have also found that valence-incrementing changes (e.g. middle-to-passive extensions) are possible as well. No converse directionality (e.g. middle-to-causative, passive-to-causative, passive-to-middle) were attested. This may have typological implications for the directionality of valence change within the voice systems of languages.

15405514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15405514.value: (1) Revising papers currently under review based on editorial and reviewer comments--currently we have 3 papers under review (Ahn & Yap; Yap & Ahn; Yap & Chor); (2) Preparing a paper for journal submission related to the versatile transfer verb kang in Southern Min (Yap, Xu & Wong, forthcoming); (3) Analysing the voice system of Indo-Aryan languages (e.g. Hindi/Urdu) to compare how changes in valence within this language family gives rise to variations in speaker stance (paving the way for future research grants); (4) Analyzing how voice as well as nominalization phenomena in Austronesian languages (e.g. Malay/Indonesian) contribute to variations in speaker stance (again paving the way for future research grants).

15405514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15405514.value: Different constructions offer different perspectives. For example, we can say 'His leadership gives us hope' or '(Careful!) This old rope can give anytime.' The former construction has 3 core participants: the giver (he and his leadership style), the recipient (us), and the theme (hope). The latter construction expresses only 1 core participant: the theme (this old rope). Crucially, this single-participant 'give' construction conveys more than just information about the rope being in a dismal condition; it also provides information about the speaker’s subjective affect, evaluation, and attitude—in this case, the speaker's anxiety in light of imminent danger. This study investigates how changes in the valence (i.e. number of core participants) of versatile transfer verbs contribute to the development of voice and pragmatic markers that convey subjective speaker stances. We include diachronic corpus analyses using online historical databases to identify pathways for the emergence of speaker-affected constructions. Crosslinguistically, we also examine the conditions (phonological, morphosyntactic, discourse-pragmatic, etc.) that facilitate valence changes in other Asian languages (including Korean, Indo-Aryan and Austronesian). Our findings contribute to theoretical studies on the interface between semantics (valence and argument structure), grammar (structural type) and pragmatics (speaker stance), as well as more in-depth explanations for grammar instruction.

15500214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500214.value: Tour guides are the first contact point for customers in tours. They maintain close and continuous contact with customers throughout the journey. Due to this extensive contact with customers, tour guide performance should have a significant effect on customer satisfaction. The notion that role stress, job performance and job satisfaction are correlated is well documented in the literature. Yet, how employees’ job performance and job satisfaction relate to customer satisfaction is unclear. This study examines the effects of role ambiguity and role conflict on the job performance and job satisfaction of tour guides and their subsequent effect on customer satisfaction. 導遊在旅行團中扮演十分重要的角色， 他們是前線員工，和團員有緊密及連續的接觸。 故此，導遊的工作表現對團員（即顧客）的滿意度有很大影響。很多研究指出，員工所面對的角色壓力，與其工作表現和工作滿意度是互助影響的。可是，文獻並沒有清晰指出員工的工作表現及滿意度如何影響顧客滿意度。有鑑於此，本研究希望探討旅行團導遊的 角色壓力 (角色模糊, 角色衝突) 及工作成果 (工作表現,工作滿意度) 對團員滿意度的影響。

15500514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500514.value: Amidst continuing globalization, firms from developed nations have been increasingly relying on suppliers from emerging economies to achieve cost efficiency and consequently global competitiveness. This reliance has led to the flourishing of various small- to medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in China’s Pearl River Delta region (PRD). These enterprises serve mainly as manufacturers and exporters of parts or finished products for overseas and particularly Western developed markets. In addition to private firms founded by native mainland Chinese entrepreneurs, many of these SMEs are foreign-invested ventures which moved their production to the PRD to enjoy lower operating costs. However, with the rising environmental awareness in developed markets, these internationalizing SMEs now have to satisfy increasingly stringent environmental requirements in order to secure their foreign business orders and license to operate. This suggests the importance of their operating in a more environmentally-oriented manner. Despite the increasing importance of environmental orientation to the performance of these SMEs, there exists virtually no research on what drives the development of their environmental orientation and how this orientation affects their organizational outcomes. This research paucity is particularly unsatisfactory when considering the rapidly growing economic significance of these firms as well as their production of nearly half of all pollutants in China. Against this backdrop, this study will propose and empirically test a model that delineates the major antecedents and consequences of environmental orientation for manufacturing SMEs operating in the PRD. Within the aforementioned context, this study will build on the existing environmental and strategic management literature to specifically examine the major determinants of environmental orientation, and if this orientation can really help firms nurture organizationally competitive capabilities that are conducive to their pro-environmental strategic practices, and consequently enhance corporate performance. It will also examine if indigenous and foreign-invested SMEs exhibit any differences in terms of the relationship among environmental orientation, and its antecedents and consequences. This examination advances understanding of boundary condition associated with effective transformation of environmental orientation into favorable organizational outcomes. Overall, this study will provide useful academic and practical insights into the complex and contingent process underlying the development of environmental orientation and its impacts on organizational outcomes. These insights will further research endeavors in the area of environmental management and strategy. They can also offer valuable inputs for SME executives and the relevant policy makers to formulate appropriate strategies to better manage the business─environment relationship in the global and Chinese marketplaces.

15500714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500714.value: 我們建議提供國際行業內資訊傳輸的證據。具體來講，我們調查市場在具有不同的投資者保護程度的國家環境下對業界同行財務公報的過度反應和反應不足的程度。許多研究已經證明行業內資訊傳輸的存在。但是直到最近，托马斯 和張 （2008 年）才發現過度反應與反應不足的同时存在。托马斯 和張 呼籲進一步的相关研究。 我們專注于提供國際上的證據，並使用适度的自信假说（MCH） 預測過度反應和有限注意假說 （LAH) 預測反應不足。MCH預測因為在評估信息時存在的偏見投資者對不精確的價值相關信息反應過度，但是對精確的信息反應不足。LAH 预测投資者由於有限的關注對價值相關的信息反应不足。業界同行早期的收益公告是對其業內同行的即将公布的收益相关但不精確的信號。因此，MCH 預測過度反應。然而，MCH 的预测只有當市場關注才有效。在对投資者保護程度高的國家，收入信號應更值相關和市場應更多注意對盈利資訊。这導致我們根据 MCH 預測過度反應應該更强烈在对投資者保護更高的國家。另一方面，在對於投資者保護較弱國家，收入信號不太价值相關和市場因此關注較少。這導致我們 根据LAH 預測反應不足會變得更強在对投資者保護不足的國家。 值得提出的一點是，MCH 也預言市场对精確的信號反应不足。不過，我們相信早期的業界同行收入本身就是一種不精確的信號。因此，我們認為關於我們研究的業界同行收入信息傳輸MCH關於反應過度的預測比起關於反應不足的預測更相關。如果我們能發現相對於對投資者保護差的國家在對投資者保護高的國家裡反應不足更明顯，我們可以認為MCH的相關機制在起作用。要進一步瞭解這些假設的作用，我們會進行幾個分析。 这些分析依赖信號精确度和对公司市場關注的变化。關於信號精確度，我們分析在業界同行的經濟層面的聯繫。關於市場關注度，我們分析當市場關注度不足時的市場反應。我們的研究將提供重要的國際證據，並有助於這兩個關鍵的行為金融理論的理解。

15500714.label: Realisation of objectives
15500714.value: We successfully achieved the three project objectives. With respect to the first objective, we use data from 35 countries (other than USA) provided by DataStream and document international evidence of the existence of overreaction/underreaction to intra-industry information transfer. Interestingly, we find only evidence of overreaction and no evidence of underreaction. With respect the second objective, we find that overreaction only exists in countries with a rich information environment that is arguably positively related to investor protection. With respect to the third objective, our findings are consistent with the predictions of the moderated confidence hypothesis and the information bias hypothesis. Specifically, the moderated confidence hypothesis predicts overreaction to imprecise information while the information of a firm’s peer is imprecise for the firm itself; the information bias hypothesis predicts that overreaction is stronger in a rich information environment, which is exactly what we find.

15500714.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500714.value: We investigate over-/under-reaction to intra-industry information transfer in international settings and whether over-/under-reaction varies with the information environment. We find that only overreaction to early earnings announcements made by industry peers exists in international setting. Interestingly, we find that high investor protection and more information disclosures are associated with more overreaction, suggesting that investors are more likely to digest imprecise information with bias when information asymmetry is lower. Among countries with low investor protection and less information disclosure, investors do not react to intra-industry information. We also find that individualism and uncertainty avoidance enhance overreaction by changing the disclosure behavior of firms and affecting investors’ behavior. We manage to have a complete manuscript based on the findings of this research project. Now the manuscript is under review at a prestigious academic journal. Moreover, we already presented early versions of the manuscript twice: one at Drexel University and the other at 2017 American Accounting Association Annual Meeting.

15500714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500714.value: Our initial results about the effect of country-level culture on over-/under-reaction to intra-industry information transfer seem intriguing. We plan to have further review and understanding of country culture-related research and investigate further how and why country-level culture shapes intra-industry transfer. Moreover, it is of interest to examine the dynamics of inter-industry information transfer, which we plan to explore using both US and non-US data.

15500714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500714.value: Our research is an early attempt to investigate how the information environment affects the efficiency of intra-industry information transfer in an international context. We find more overreaction in countries with a rich information environment. In other words, our finding suggests that ironically, a rich information environment is likely to associate with more information bias. We attribute our finding to the possibility that investors do not pay attention to intra-industry information when the information environment is poor. We also find that informal institutions shape managers’ disclosure behavior and affect how investors process information, which in turn affects the efficiency of intra-industry information transfer. Specifically, we find that in societies with high individualism and lower uncertainty avoidance, investors are more likely to overreact to peers’ earnings information. Overall, our findings demonstrate that country culture and information environments affect the efficiency of intra-industry information transfer.

15501214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15501214.value: LinkedIn的力量-因參與LinkedIn, 資訊管理專業人士會不會考慮自己的職業發展？

15501214.label: Project Objectives
15501214.value: What is the mechanism by which professionals are motivated to participate in LinkedIn? To what extent does participation in LinkedIn influence the different dimensions of their professional commitment and how does this in turn affect their ILPA? How much does LinkedIn influence IT professionals in Hong Kong?
rows: What is the mechanism by which professionals are motivated to participate in LinkedIn?
To what extent does participation in LinkedIn influence the different dimensions of their professional commitment and how does this in turn affect their ILPA?
How much does LinkedIn influence IT professionals in Hong Kong?

15501214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501214.value: This proposal explores a common phenomenon of turnover intention – intention to leave an organization for professional advancement (ILPA). Nowadays, LinkedIn provides a good platform for professionals to get connected, to share their experience in career development and to seek jobs. Based on self-determination theory, we would like to investigate how participating in LinkedIn influences ILPA. In our theoretical framework, we first argue that professionals would receive autonomy, competence and relatedness supports for career development from participating in LinkedIn. Second, these three essential supports for career development would drive the autonomous and controlled motivations for participating in LinkedIn. Third, we hypothesize that the autonomous motivations for participating in LinkedIn have a positive influence on both affective professional commitment and normative professional commitment. Moreover, the controlled motivations for participating in LinkedIn have positive influence on continuous professional commitment. Fourth, the influence of autonomous and controlled motivations on the three dimensions of professional commitment will be mediated by actual use of LinkedIn. Fifth, these three dimensions of professional commitment have a positive influence on ILPA. Control factors such as organizational commitment, professional tenure, organizational tenure and biographic profile will be surveyed. This study will contribute to the literature on two untapped areas – 1) to what extent social media influence professional commitment and ILPA, and 2) how SDT can explain why people are so involved with LinkedIn. Hence, this study will shed light on turnover intention and SDT from a new perspective. Moreover, the extent to which participating in LinkedIn influences ILPA will be examined in the context of IT professionals in Hong Kong. Last, the findings of this study will draw the attention of companies in setting their policies for retaining IT professionals. The target population of this study will be those Hong Kong IT professionals, who are active participants in LinkedIn. Using an online survey, participants will be invited by emails posted to their LinkedIn discussion groups such as the “Hong Kong IT Professionals Association.” Reminders will be sent, and we expect a response rate of around 20%. To control for common method bias, we will collect the data in three waves. The first wave will involve constructs related to the supports and motivations for participating in LinkedIn as a career development tool. The second wave is to collect use data such as number of existing connections, and the third wave will be on constructs related to commitments and ILPA.

15501214.label: Realisation of objectives
15501214.value: After a comprehensive review on the literature of self-determination theory and presentation of our initial proposal in the 19th World Multi-Conference on Systemics, Cybernetics and Informatics in July 2015, we revised our theoretical framework of participating LinkedIn for professional advancement. We sent our questionnaire via the inbox messaging services from LinkedIn to our target population during the period from 1st June 2015 to 31st August 2015. Selected respondents received inbox messages with a link to an online questionnaire. A total of 260 questionnaires were returned out of 5810 messages with around 4.5 percent response rate. Our original plan was to survey only the IT professionals in Hong Kong. However, due to the low response rate, we included participants of 30 discussion groups in LinkedIn. Those discussion groups are related to supply chain management, banking industry, IT services, and tourism industry. The respondents are from different professions in different locations. Hence, our findings reflect the general picture of the motivations behind participating LinkedIn instead of the IT professionals in Hong Kong. In this regard, the objective 3 is achieved in some sense. Data analyses were conducted. The results of this study suggest that professionals who use LinkedIn intend to leave their organizations for professional advancement, whether immediately or in the future. Many companies and recruiters use LinkedIn to identify potential employees and the site plays an important role for professionals, as this demonstrates their desire for intention to leave an organization for professional advancement. Our findings confirm that professionals obtain support for the three basic needs through LinkedIn use and are motivated both intrinsically and extrinsically to continue their use to achieve intentional to leave an organization for professional advancement (ILPA). A professional seeking advancement, whether to remain in the same organization or to move to a different organization, is likely to believe that using LinkedIn will help him/her to achieve this goal. Hence, objective 1 is vastly achieved. Our findings also indicated that if a professional feels obligated to stay with his/her profession (Normative Professional Commitment), his/her tendency to stay with his/her organization is relatively high. To a certain extent, when a professional has a strong sense of belonging to his/her organization (Affective Organizational Commitment), is older (age), has a relatively high position within the organization (position), or must sacrifice too much to leave his/her organization (Continuance Organizational Commitment), his/her desire to leave is low. Furthermore, when a professional receives strong support from his/her organization (Organizational Support and Development), he/she is highly likely to remain and stay loyal to the organization. In this regard, objective 2 is vastly achieved. Moreover, our findings showed that there are some strong relationships between perceived autonomy support and external regulation, perceived relatedness support and intrinsic motivation. These findings aroused our interest on the possible reasons behind. We have reviewed some literature of using time perspective in decision making. On one hand, autonomy support offers choice and options that induce people to think for the future. On the other hand, people with future orientation have higher tendency to achieve reward based on external regulation. This kind of argument may help to explain the strong relationship between perceived autonomy support and external regulation. Due to the interesting findings, we need to spend more time in searching on the literature in order to reframe our theoretical model and related hypotheses. We have written a manuscript and submitted to the Journal of Management Information Systems for potential publication.

15501214.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501214.value: The findings of the current study are as follows. First, in line with self-determination theory, results demonstrate the support of perceived autonomy, competence, and relatedness is fulfilled through LinkedIn use and that professionals are intrinsically and extrinsically motivated to continue their LinkedIn use to eventually achieve intentional to leave an organization for professional advancement (ILPA). This is consistent with many previous studies on motivation through the self-determination approach. Our study confirms that the LinkedIn website enables and supports professionals to search for jobs, gain new insights and information, and build networks, whether their use is intrinsically or extrinsically motivated. Second, our study sheds new light on the evolution of job search processes that have progressed in parallel with technology, and encourage overall turnover. Professionals are increasingly dependent on social media for professional development and career advancement, prompting increased mobility. The easy access to Internet at anytime and anywhere no doubt has changed the way professionals are motivated and how they interact with others for their career development and advancement. The nature of LinkedIn not only serves as a platform for professionals who specifically look for job change, but also enables professionals to achieve different personal goals that could eventually lead to ILPA. As a whole, we suggest professionals using LinkedIn have mixed agendas, some have an immediate need for a new job while others may not, but just seeing what is available on the job market or utilizing the platform to build up networks, might change that view. Furthermore, we conducted a post-hoc analysis to demonstrate that each of the three basic psychological needs and motivations according to the SDT model could be time relevant and that such time relevancy plays an important role impacting on one’s behaviors and leading outcomes. Many researchers to date have only concentrated on the connections between time perspective and motivational regulations while excluding the three basic psychological needs. How time perspectives relate to, and influence, the support of the three needs together with the corresponding motivations has not been explored to the same extent and remains unclear. Our findings from the post-hoc analysis help explain a professional’s behavior and motivation to participate in LinkedIn applying the time perspective concept. In this regard, we have written a manuscript entitled "The power of LinkedIn: How LinkedIn enables professionals to leave their organizations for professional advancement" submitted to the Journal of Management Information Systems for potential publication.

15501214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501214.value: This research used a relatively small sample considering that there are hundreds of millions of LinkedIn members. Therefore, a large-scale study should be conducted to confirm the results of this research. Second, there are many other professional network sites besides LinkedIn. in China, for example, several professional networks have been established and are attracting a growing number of subscribers. Future research should consider including these websites to be more representative. in addition, it would be interesting to further explore and compare ILPA between professionals in similar context that use network sites and those who do not. Third, the investigated constructs are not supposed to remain unchanged over time, and the research method may not fully capture the dynamics of professionals' career development and network building. Finally, the problem of common method bias may exist, although it is not a significant concern as confirmed in our analysis. To address the above issues, future research should consider using multi-methods and longitudinal research designs. This would allow better understanding of professionals' motivation and thereby underlying "how/why" of the relationships if ILPA triggers LinkedIn usage or vice versa if LinkedIn usage inspires professionals' ILPA.

15501214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501214.value: With the growth of Web 2.0/3.0, social network sites have been created for various purposes for a wide spectrum of users. Creating a digital footprint has become imperative, especially for professionals seeking career development and professional advancement. This study explores how LinkedIn enables professionals’ intention to leave an organization for professional advancement (ILPA). Our framework leverages self-determination theory (SDT) to demonstrate why professionals use this online social networking service. To validate our theoretical framework, 379 randomly selected active LinkedIn users completed an online questionnaire. The relationship between motivations to use LinkedIn and ILPA are examined and the results support all our hypotheses. Our post-hoc analysis indicates a strong relationship between needing support and motivation for participating in LinkedIn. We attempt to explain the findings by using the time perspective concept. This study is also of practical value to companies seeking to set policies to retain professionals. Implications for theory and practice are discussed.
