15508614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508614.value: This project aims to provide direct evidence on the properties of non-GAAP accounting earnings that are used in executive compensation contracts. A large literature in accounting (e.g. Holthausen and Watts, 2001; Kothari, Ramanna, and Skinner, 2010) argues that: (1) accounting performance measures such as earnings mandated by the prevailing accounting standards (hereafter GAAP-earnings) play an important role in management compensation contracts; and (2) contracting demand for accounting numbers is an important force that shapes accounting rules and financial reporting practices. Lambert (2010) suggests that evidence on whether and how earnings used in actual compensation contracts (hereafter Compensation-earnings) differ from GAAP-earnings is important in understanding the role of contracting in shaping accounting standards. However, due to data availability, there has not been any direct empirical evidence on the comparison between Compensation-earnings and GAAP-earnings. The requirement by the 2006 Securities and Exchange Commission (hereafter SEC) rule 33-8732A for expanded disclosure on information related to executive compensation allows us to directly observe Compensation-earnings. By exploiting this unique opportunity, this project will be the first to provide direct answers to the following questions: (1) how do Compensation-earnings differ from GAAP-earnings; (2) to what extent do efficiency contracting theories or agency problems explain the differences between Compensation-earnings and GAAP-earnings; (3) to what extent do Compensation-earnings accentuate, preserve, or eliminate the properties of GAAP-earnings such as conditional conservatism. The evidence from this project will improve our understanding of the performance measurement in firms’ performance evaluation and compensation system that serves to organize and coordinate firm-wide efforts and decisions (Murphy and Jensen, 2011; Murphy, 2012; Indjejikian, Matějka, Merchant, and Van der Stede, 2013). Furthermore, evidence from this project helps to inform the heated debate in accounting on the main purpose (contracting vs. valuation) that the accounting system serves (e.g. Kothari, Ramanna, and Skinner, 2010; Lambert, 2010). This study also has public policy (financial reporting standard setting) implications with regard to the desirability of certain possible features of accounting standards (e.g. conservatism and fair value accounting) and with regard to the desirability of the possible convergence of U.S. GAAP with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

15508614.label: Realisation of objectives
15508614.value: Objective #1: To provide direct large-sample evidence on how firms modify GAAP earnings in compensation contracts. We have manually collected a large sample of the earnings (Compensation Earnings) that are used in determining bonus payouts. Comparing Compensation Earnings to the GAAP Earnings of the same firm/year, we find that firms make economically significant adjustments to GAAP Earnings in arriving at Compensation Earnings. While GAAP Earnings exhibit conservatism, we fail to detect conservatism (either by statistical significance or by magnitude of coefficient) in Compensation Earnings using the same sample and the same research design. The absence of conservatism in Compensation Earnings is also documented in various subsamples partitioned on market-to-book ratio, leverage, firm size, and corporate governance. Further analyses indicate that the adjustment from GAAP Earnings to Compensation Earnings involves substantially the removal of less persistent components of GAAP Earnings, resulting in Compensation Earnings that are more persistent than GAAP Earnings. However, Compensation Earnings are not a result of mechanically removing transitory items from GAAP Earnings. Objective #2: To provide evidence on the role of efficient contracting theories in explaining Compensation-GAAP earnings differences. In a related literature, Bushman, Engel, and Smith (2006) and Banker, Huang, and Natarajan (2009) find a positive association between the stewardship and valuation roles of accounting. Bushman et al. propose theoretically a source of this positive association: because managerial actions have multiperiod effects that are not fully captured in the current earnings number, valuation earnings coefficient is included in the incentive coefficient to motivate the manager to internalize the discounted all-in value impact of current period action. Our results suggest that a plausible mechanism for valuation earnings coefficient to be included in compensation incentive coefficient is for the performance measurement of bonus contracts to focus on the relatively persistent (recurring) components of earnings. Thus, our analyses indicate that Compensation Earnings are consistent with efficient contracting. Objective #3: To provide evidence on the role of agency problems in explaining Compensation-GAAP earnings differences. Our results show that the removal of conservatism from Compensation Earnings is exhibited both in firms with good corporate governance and in firms with bad corporate governance. The results suggest that the removal of conservatism from Compensation Earnings is not an indication for agency problems, (i.e., unlikely to be a result of managers’ rent seeking behavior).

15508614.label: Major findings and research outcome
15508614.value: Motivated by competing theories on the properties of earnings required for compensation performance measurement, we provide direct evidence on the properties of actual accounting earnings that are used in determining compensation payouts (Compensation Earnings). Using a large sample of manually collected Compensation Earnings for U.S. firms, we show that firms make economically significant adjustments to GAAP Earnings in arriving at Compensation Earnings. While GAAP Earnings exhibit conservatism, we fail to detect conservatism (either by statistical significance or by magnitude of coefficient) in Compensation Earnings using the same sample and the same research design. The absence of conservatism in Compensation Earnings is also documented in various subsamples partitioned on market-to-book ratio, leverage, firm size, and corporate governance. Further analyses indicate that the adjustment from GAAP Earnings to Compensation Earnings involves the removal of less persistent components of GAAP Earnings, resulting in Compensation Earnings that are more persistent than GAAP Earnings. We add to the literature of executive compensation contracting by providing direct evidence on the trade-off of two potentially valuable features of accounting performance measures (conservatism and persistence). We believe that this study will be of interest to researchers, regulators, and accounting standard setters.

15508614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15508614.value: From the presentation of our paper at various research seminars of leading institutions and international conferences, we have obtained a lot of constructive comments. We are conducting additional analyses based on these comments. We are also in the process of revising the research manuscript for submission for publication at top accounting research journals. In addition, our manually collected data on Compensation Earnings opens up plenty of research opportunities to provide insights into how performance is measured for compensation purposes in the framework of efficient contracting and agency problems. We are in the process of developing follow-up research to take advantage of this unique data set.

Further analyses indicate that the adjustment from GAAP Earnings to Compensation Earnings involves the removal of less persistent components of GAAP Earnings. We add to the literature of executive compensation contracting by providing direct evidence on the trade-off of two potentially valuable features of accounting performance measures (conservatism and persistence). 15508914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508914.value: The illiquidity measure (thereafter ILLIQ) proposed in Amihud (JFM, 2002) has been widely used in finance literature as a proxy of illiquidity. The ILLIQ measure is defined as the average ratio of absolute return and dollar trading volume and is intended to capture the price impact of trading. One advantage of the ILLIQ is that unlike most existing measures of illiquidity which require detailed microstructure data, the ILLIQ measure only requires information on daily return and trading volume. As such, researchers can easily construct ILLIQ for a large sample of stocks over a long sample period. However, ILLIQ may be a biased proxy for illiquidity. Security returns are not only affected by trading activities but also by large information shocks. Therefore, high absolute returns associated with low dollar trading volume on a given day may not be necessarily the effect of illiquidity. In addition, the literature has shown that investors tend to misreact to large information shocks, e.g., Barberis, Shleifer, and Vishny (1998), Daniel, Hirshleifer, and Subrahmanyam (1998), and Hong and Stein (1999). Such misreaction to large information shocks may potentially bias the risk premium associated with ILLIQ measure. In this study, we use large discontinuous changes, known as jumps, in stock prices as proxy for large information shocks and show that investors underreact to large information shocks. That is, stocks with higher (lower) cumulative jump returns are associated with higher (lower) future returns. Jumps in stock prices are identified following the procedure proposed in Jiang and Oomen (2008). With documented evidence of investor misreaction to large information shocks, we further examine the effect of information shocks on Amihud illiquidity measure. We divide the entire stock sample into subsamples with and without jumps in stock prices. Our preliminary results indicate that the difference in illiquidity premium between with and without explicitly controlling for information shocks is positive and statistically significant. This implies that the use of ILLIQ as a proxy of illiquidity overestimates illiquidity premium and therefore could overestimate price impact of trading. Our study not only sheds new lights on the relationship between information and liquidity and on investors’ behaviors in the stock market, but also provides a more reliable measure of illiquidity premium associated with ILLIQ. The results of this study have important implications from both theoretical and practical perspectives as information shocks and liquidity are a great concern when investors design and implement their portfolio strategies. 15508914.label: Major findings and research outcome
15508914.value: Using jumps in stock prices as a proxy for large information shocks, we provide evidence consistent with short-term underreaction in the US equity market. Strategies long (short) stocks with positive (negative) lagged jump returns earn significantly positive returns over the next one- to three-month horizons. The results based on intraday jumps, especially overnight jumps, provide further evidence consistent with underreaction. The underreaction is robust to controlling for other firm characteristics, extends stock return momentum over intermediate to short horizons, and captures market underreaction to information shocks beyond earnings surprises. We further show that limited investor attention contributes to short-term underreaction.

15508914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15508914.value: One of potential developments is to examine whether there is seasonality in information arrival and, if it does, whether investors recognize such seasonality and respond accordingly. We have undertaken a preliminary investigation on this potential.

15508914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15508914.value: This research examines how investors react to unexpected information in the US stock market. Based on monthly returns, the research finds that investors underestimate the impact of unexpected information on stock prices and the information is gradually incorporated into stock prices over a period up to three months. An investment strategy buying (selling) stocks with unexpected good (bad) news earn significantly positive (negative) returns over the next one- to three-month horizons.

16100014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100014.value: Because of the anatomical and dynamic barriers, drug delivery to the posterior segment of the eye remains a challenge. As sustained release depots that can be placed in proximity to retina by direct injection to the vitreous (jelly-like substance in the back of the eye), polymeric nanoparticles are useful carriers proven to reduce the injection frequency. However, to realize the therapeutic benefits of existing and emerging ocular drugs of a wide variety, nanoparticles must be able to localize and deliver the cargoes to specific types of cells in retina. Given that the retina consists of multiple cell types arranged in distinctive layers, and that there is a net vitreous outflow moving the particles from inner to outer retina, we hypothesize that cell targeting can be achieved by balancing the physical movement of nanoparticles and their interaction with cells. The rates of these two processes will be modulated by altering the size, charge, and surface modification of nanoparticles. To further refine the level of cell targeting, we propose to modify the nanoparticle surface with ligands and peptides that recognize retinal ganglion cells and retinal pigmented epithelial cells. These two retinal cells are implicated in blinding eye diseases and are therefore important cellular targets for treatment. We plan to synthesize polymers conjugated with varying ligands, and prepare nanoparticles of a range of size and charge. We will obtain the extent and rate of uptake of these nanoparticles by different retinal cells in culture. We will profile the vitreal and retinal distribution of nanoparticles in the animal eye after intravitreal injection. All these measurements will allow us to correlate the localization of nanoparticles with their physiochemical properties. Nanoparticles will be optimized to achieve in vivo homing to retinal ganglion cells and retinal pigmented epithelium. This project leverages our prior experience in designing and synthesizing polymeric nanosystems for drug delivery and our expertise in ocular drug delivery. We expect the outcome of this project will have significant impact on translational research in visual science and ocular drug development.

16100014.label: Realisation of objectives
16100014.value: Research activities and major findings related to Objective 1 Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with different zeta potentials were prepared with ethanol injection method and applied for exploring the effect of surface charge on retinal distribution. C57/BL6 mice were used and LissRhodamine labelled nanoparticles were injected through intravitreal injection. The robust drug delivery system has not only allowed us to form nanoparticles around the same size (~70nm) with surface charge ranged from -30 mV to +45 mV but could serve as potential drug carriers for RNAi-based therapeutics in future application. The lipid nanoparticles varying in surface charge were injected to the vitreous of mice. The nanoparticle in various ocular tissues were visualized and quantified by fluorescence measurement and tissue imaging via confocal microscope. We found that only intravitreally injected nanoparticles with positive charge could be retained in the eye effectively. Nanoparticles with negative, neutral and slight positive charge were cleared from the eye within 6 hours. More LNPs of +45 mV however remained in the vitreous than LNPs of +35mV, resulting in slightly more LNPs of +35mV in the retina at both 6h and 24 h post injection. LNPs of +35mV could penetration the retina with more accumulation in the retinal ganglion cell, inner plexiform, and inner nuclear layers at 6 hours while majority got cleared after 24hours. In summary, we correlated the surface charge of the intravitreal lipid nanoparticles with their clearance from the vitreous, retinal penetration and accumulation. This will provide the basis for further improvement of the nanoparticle design to target retinal tissues. Research activities and major findings related to Objective 2 Short oligopeptide (IKRG) derived from BDNF has been proven to interact with TrkB receptors that are abundantly expressed in neurons. We modified pegylated lipid with IKRG peptide via click chemistry of thiol-maleimide reaction. By including IKRG-pegylated lipid in the formulation, we could obtain IKRG-modified lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). With Cy5 labeled siRNA as model RNAi-therapeutics, the effectiveness of IKRG-LNPs for improving siRNA delivery into the cells was examined in PC12 culture, which is a neuroblastoma cell line known to overexpress TrkB receptor on the cell surface similar to most neurons. With 10-20% of the ligands grafted on the surface, flow cytometry data indicated that the cellular uptake of the nanoparticles increased by 2-3 folds after 4 hours of incubation. In addition, IKRG modified polymeric nanoparticles made of PEG-b-PCL were prepared and evaluated. These particles were also found to be internalized selectively into PC12 but not for Hela cells. While PC12 cells express TrkB receptors abundantly, Hela cells do not. This study has been extended to other types of neurons and the ligand effect of IKRG was found to enhance the delivery to dorsal root ganglion cells (DRGs). With PTEN inhibitor encapsulated, this drug delivery system showed prolonged and enhanced neural regenerative effect and attenuated toxicity. The positive outcome can be attributed to the increased and targeted cellular uptake and sustainable release by the peptide-modified nanoparticles. In summary, we have explored the capability of the targeting effects of the IKRG peptide in neuronal cells and proved its promising potential with desirable enhancement of cellular internalization and targeting effect to neurons. Research activities and major findings related to Objective 3 Cy5-siRNA loaded nanoparticles with and without 10% IKRG ligand grafted on the surface were injected into the vitreous of C57 mice. After 72 hours, retinal flatmount was prepared and visualized by confocal microscope. Compared to LNPs without peptide ligand modification (plain LNPs), LNPs with 10% IKRG showed significantly more retention of both particles and siRNA in the retinal tissues, suggesting cellular internalization by the retinal ganglion cells. Therefore, we determined not only BDNF mimetic peptide could enhance cellular uptake efficiency of LNPs but the in vivo cellular targeting effect to the retinal ganglion cell layer. The desirable targeted delivery of cy5-siRNA in the retinal flatmount confirmed that the combination of different optimal parameters promote the delivery efficiency of the encapsulated cargo and can change the distribution and location of the nanoparticles favourably after intravitreally injected. Deviation from planned objectives and reasons for under-achievements We have systematically investigated how surface charge of intravitreal lipid nanoparticles affected their intraocular distribution. We also explored the potential of BDNF-mimetic peptide IKRG as specific ligand for targeting the retinal ganglion cells. When combined optimal surface charge with the conjugated ligand, the targeted delivery of siRNA demonstrated the superiority of the designed lipid nano-sized delivery systems. We have not, however, pursued the targeting of retinal pigmented epithelium as originally planned. The main reason is that the lipid nanoparticles did not have sufficient stability to maintain the carrier integrity when transporting through the retinal tissue. The lipid nanoparticles will have been disintegrated before reaching the retinal pigmented epithelium, and the modification of particle surface with targeting ligands will not be useful. Efforts are now underway to adjust the particle stability, for example, by adding covalent crosslinks between the lipids. We have also demonstrated that the nanoparticles decorated with BDNF-mimetic peptides can deliver therapeutics to the neurons in dorsal root ganglion (DRG). Thus these nanoparticles can also find applications in treating neural degeneration other than those in the eye. We encapsulated the FAM-siRNA into the LNPs (siLNPs) as model RNAi therapeutics to validate the finds for charge impact. The charge lipids inserted into the LNPs were modified to maintain the surface charge of +33mV. After 6/24 hour post injection, C57 mice were sacrificed and the eyes are nucleated. Cryosection were performed and the retinas were visualized by confocal microscope. When same amount of naked siRNA was injected, within 6 hours, naked siRNA was cleared without any signal in penetrating the retina. After 6 h, the intravitreally injected LNPs carrying siRNA could penetrate and distribute into the inner-retina, including the ganglion cell and inner plexiform layers. However, in the outer layers of the retina including RPE layer, only certain amount of fluorescence of Rhodamine were detected but without the FAM fluorescence. After 24 h, majority of the siLNPs were cleared. The remaining FAM-siRNA and PE-Rhod labeled LNPs were separated and distributed at different locations in the eye. The green FAM-siRNA obviously stayed in the surface layer which was around the ganglion cell layer in the retina, while the red PE-Rhod labeled LNPs showed some distribution in the deeper layer of the retina including outer nuclear and photoreceptor layers of the retina. These data suggest that LNPs could only protect and facilitate the transport of the siRNA into several inner layers of the retina, e.g. retinal ganglion cell layer. With the instability and gradual disassembly of siLNPs, targeting the most outer layer, RPE layer, remained challenging. Based on our current results, the unmet goal of targeting RPE layer via intravitreally injected lipid nanoparticles remain challenging. One proposed direction is to improve the stability of the particles. By covalent crosslinking of the lipid nanoparticles to different extent, various stability could be achieved. It is also possible to introduce responsive bonds cleavable by the exposure of external or physiological stimuli (e.g. light, oxidative potential, and enzyme) By developing desirable LNPs with optimal stability as well as specific RPE targeting ligand (e.g folate), integrity of intravitreal particles could be maintained after interacting with multiple retinal cell layers while specific uptake of LNPs into the RPE could be achieved.

16100014.value: Retina is known as the drug target for various posterior ocular conditions such as glaucoma and age-related macular degeneration. Targeted delivery of therapeutics into specific sites of the retina is essential for improving the delivery efficiency and drug efficacy. 16100214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100214.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disease that affects an increasing number of people due to aging population. The disease is characterized clinically by the movement impairment and pathologically by a selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra of the brainstem. Recent research in PD has involved the characterization of genes that are linked to familial PD (FPD). For instance, the identification of mutations of α-synuclein (α-syn) that can cause FPD has supported a major role for protein aggregation in the development of PD. α-syn is the major component of Lewy bodies (LBs) and the formation of α-syn oligomers or aggregates has consistently been found to be neurotoxic in different models of PD. Several factors have been found to affect α-syn aggregation or oligomerization. Nitration, abnormal truncation and phosphorylation of α-syn have been shown to affect its aggregation and deposition in the LBs. Among these post-translational modifications, extensive focus has been put on how phosphorylation can affect the aggregation and toxicity of α-syn. Five amino acid residues have been suggested as being phosphorylated in α-syn (S87, Y125, S129, Y133 and Y136), and three major classes of kinase are involved: casein kinases (CKs), polo-like kinases (PLKs) and G protein-coupled receptor kinases (GRKs). Studies have found that CKs and PLKs can target multiple residues for phosphorylation in α-syn, whereas GRKs target mainly the S129 residue. In our recent studies, we have found that nitric oxide can contribute to PD through S-nitrosylation by compromising neuroprotective pathways in neurons. We have preliminary data showing the modification of GRK 2, 5 and 6 by nitric oxide (NO) through S-nitrosylation that affects their kinase activities in the phosphorylation of α-syn. This initial finding suggests that NO can contribute to PD by affecting the aggregation of α-syn through modulating the kinase activity of GRKs. In this resubmission, we have revised our proposal to address all the suggestions from the reviewers and have also provided new preliminary data supporting our hypothesis. We propose to characterize fully how NO, through the S-nitrosylation of GRKs, can regulate the phosphorylation and aggregation of α-syn both in vitro and in vivo. We will also explore if other kinases such as CKs and PLKs can also be S-nitrosylated and whether or not this affects their kinase activity towards α-syn. 帕金森氏病是一種常見的神經退化性疾病,由於人口老齡化,此疾病影響的病人越來越多。這種疾病的主要臨床特徵是運動障礙和多巴胺能神經元在腦幹的黑質選擇性退化。最近的帕金森氏病研究已參與鏈接到家族性帕金森氏病的基因的特徵。例如,α突觸核蛋白,其突變可導致家族性帕金森氏病的鑑定已經支持對蛋白聚集在帕金森氏病發病的重要作用。α突觸核蛋白是路易體的主要成分,此外α突觸核蛋白的寡聚體或聚集體的形成,一直被認為是神經毒素在不同帕金森氏病模型的主要組成部分。硝化，異常截斷和磷酸化α突觸核蛋白已被證明影響在路易體的聚集和沉積。在這些轉譯後修飾，廣泛的重點已放在如何磷酸化會影響α突觸核蛋白的聚集和毒性。α突觸核蛋白的五個氨基酸(S87,Y125,S129,Y133和Y136) 已被證明被三大類的蛋白激酶(酪蛋白激酶(CKS),polo樣激酶(PLKs)和G蛋白偶合受體激酶(GRKs))磷酸化, 研究發現，酪蛋白激酶和polo樣激酶可以針對多個殘基磷酸化α-突觸核蛋白，而G蛋白偶合受體激酶目標主要是S129殘基。在我們最近的研究中,我們已經發現,一氧化氮可以通過S-亞硝基化降低神經細胞的神經保護途徑並引起帕金森氏病的發病。我們的初步數據顯示G蛋白偶合受體激酶2，5和6通過一氧化氮S-亞硝基化能影響其激酶活性對α突觸核蛋白的磷酸化的修飾。這個初始的發現表明，一氧化氮可通過調節G蛋白偶合受體激酶的激酶活性影響α-突觸核蛋白的聚集因此影響帕金森氏病的發病。在這個重新提交，我們修改我們的提議，以解決從審評的所有建議，並也提供了新的初步數據支持我們的假設。我們提出了以表徵完全如何一氧化氮，通過S-亞硝基化G蛋白偶合受體激酶能調節α-突觸核蛋白的磷酸化和聚集。我們也將探討是否有其他激酶，如酪蛋白激酶和polo樣激酶也可以S-亞硝基化和會否影響對α-突觸核蛋白的磷酸化。

16100214.label: Realisation of objectives
16100214.value: 1. We have characterized how nitric oxide (NO) through S-nitrosylation can modulate the kinase activity of GRK2, 5 and 6 towards the phosphorylation of α-synuclein (α-syn) at ser129. With the use of biotin switch assay, we confirmed that GRK2, 5 and 6 can be S-nitrosylated both in vitro and in vivo. We further found that S-nitrosylation of GRK2 inhibited its kinase activity in the phosphorylation of α-syn at which agreed with previous studies. However, unlike GRK2, we found that S-nitrosylation of GRK 5 and 6 increased their kinase activity toward the phosphorylation of α-syn. We were also able to produce recombinant proteins of GRK 6 and set up in vitro kinase activity assay to show that through S-nitrosylation, GSNO can increase the GRK6 activity in a dose-dependent manner. We had further identified the S-nitrosyaltion site of GRK6 at cys 474. We explored the possible effect of S-nitrosylation of other kinases such as CK2 and PLK2 toward the phosphorylation of α-syn, we found that both CK2 and PLK2 can also be S-nitrosylated by NO. Similar to GRK 5& 6, we found that CK2 S-nitrosylation at cys147 could enhance its kinase activity to the phosphorylation of α syn at ser129. For PLK2, we planned to study the effect of its S-nitrosylation in the future study. 2. Since we had robustly found that GRK 5 & 6 can be S-nitrosylated by nitric oxide and this modification can increase its kinase activity towards the phosphorylation of α-syn at ser129. We set up cellular assay to determine if coexpression of GRK 6 and α-syn in the presence of NO donor NOC18 would enhance α-syn aggregation. We focused on GRK6 as GRK 5 & 6 are highly homologous and they both have the same effect on α-syn. We found that indeed in the presence of NOC18, GRK 6 enhanced the propensity of α-syn to aggregate, however the effect was limited. In addition, we didn’t observe significant changes in cell viability associated with GRK6 and α-syn coexpresssion with the treatment of NOC18. It is possible that the cellular model is not a good approach to determine the potential long-term effect of GRK6 S-nitrosylation in the pathogenesis of PD. We therefore focused on how S-nitrosylation of GRK6 could contribute to the pathogenesis of PD in the A53T a-syn transgenic model. 3. In this objective, we focused on using the A53T a-syn transgenic mice to determine how GRKs S-nitrosylation is related to PD pathogenesis. We were particularly interested in how aging and overexpression of A53T a-syn in transgenic mice would affect GRKs S-nitrosyaltion. In addition, we wanted to determine the role of S-nitrosylation in the pathogenesis of PD in this mouse model. We mainly focused on GRK6 and CK2 alpha as we found that both GRK6 and CK2 could increase the phosphorylation of α-syn at ser129. From our aging study, we found that both GRK6 and CK2 S-nitrosylation was increased in an age dependent manner, these results suggested that nitrosative stress was increased in the mouse brain during aging and contributed to the process of neurodegeneration. To prove this concept further, we treated 9 month old A53T transgenic mice and littermate control with L-NNA, a nitric oxide synthase (NOS) inhibitor, for a month. We got two important findings in this experiment. The first one was that in A53T transgenic mice without L-NNA treatment, they were having significantly higher levels of S-nitrosylated GRK6 and CK2, suggesting that overexpression of pathogenic A53T α-syn could increase nitrosative stress in the mouse brain. In the treatment of L-NNA, the levels of GRK6 and CK2 were significantly reduced, suggesting that NOS inhibition could reverse the A53T a-syn induced increased in the S-nitrosylation of GRK6 and CK2. To further tested the important role of NOS, we crossed neuronal NOS (nNOS) knockout mice with the A53T α-syn transgenic mice to obtain mice that expressed A53T a-syn transgene but lacking one copy of nNOS in the mouse brain. We found that both a-syn and phosphor-α-syn at ser129 were decreased in an age-dependent manner in the double mutant mice (A53T a-syn transgene and nNOS knockout). Taken together, these results suggested that modulation of NOS activity could be a new therapeutic approach for PD treatment. From the mouse study, we also use S-nitrosylation of GAPDH as control and found that similar results could be observed as in GRK6 and CK2. Increased GAPDH S-nitrosylation has been well characterized in PD models and PD patients, which support our findings are relevant to the pathogenesis in PD. We therefore didn’t further look into the GRKs S-nitrosylation in PD patients as we would like to preserve the precious samples for out following study. In addition, aging and α-syn overexpression samples would be very difficult to obtain in the human brain samples as in our A53T transgenic setting, therefore we adjusted our focus on the well-characterized animal PD model instead.

16100214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100214.value: From our proposal, we proposed to study the role of S-nitrosylation of G protein-coupled receptor kinases (GRK5 & 6) in Parkinson’s disease (PD). We hypothesized that increased in nitrosative stress could modify GRK 5 & 6 and increase phosphorylation of α-syn at S129 which could contribute to the neurodegeneration in PD. In addition, we also explored the possible S-nitrosylation of casein kinase 2 (CK2) and polo-like kinases (PLKs) which also could contribute to the α-syn phosphorylation at S129. In this project, we found that GRK5&6, CK2 alpha and PLK2 could all be S-nitrosylated. S-nitrosylation of GRK5&6 and CK2 enhanced their kinase activity toward α-syn phosphorylation at S129. Alpha-syn phosphorylation at S129 is known to contribute to PD but the exact role is not fully understood. We had explored if increased phosphorylation of α-syn S129 by increased kinase activity vby GRK5&6 and CK2 S-nitrosylation could directly contribute the α-syn aggregation and causing cell death in neurons. We found that the role of S129 α-syn phosphorylation on effect of its protein aggregation was inconsistent in the cellular model and not associated with cell viability. However, from the extensive A53T transgenic animal PD model study, we found that there were significant linkages among the factors involving the pathogenesis of PD, which is aging, expression of mutant A53T α-syn and nitrosative stress. In particular, we found that aging could lead to increase in nitrosative stress in the S-nitrosylation of different proteins such as GRKs and CK2 and this observation could link to changes in the level of S129 phospho-α-syn. On the other hand, we have also observed overexpression of A53T α-syn could also enhance the nitrosative stress in the transgeneic mice. These results provide a mechanism of how increasing loading of mutant α-syn and aging can contribute to PD by increasing nitrosative stress in the brain. In fact, this study suggests a novel mechanism of how aging and mutant α-syn could contribute to PD through increased in nitrosative stress in the brain

16100214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100214.value: Aging and increased expression of a-syn are known to be two major contributing factors to pathogenesis of Parkinson’s disease (PD). From our study, we found that these two contributing factors can increased nitrosative stress in the brain. Increased nitrosative in turn will contribute to PD by increasing neuronal cell death as shown in different studies. Our study clearly indicates that modulation of nitrosative stress could be a new therapeutic approach to PD. In addition, we have preliminary data showing that PLK2 can be S-nitrosylated. We plan to further study how S-nitrosylation of PLK2 might affect its kinase activity toward phosphorylation of α-syn and contribute to PD.

16100214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100214.value: This study clearly suggests that the role of imbalance of nitric oxide (NO) metabolism, a gaseous signaling molecule in the brain, can contribute to the disease development of a second most common neurodegenerative disease, Parkinson’s disease (PD). From this study, increased loading of NO was found in aging and mouse model of PD, which served as an indicator of how changes of NO metabolism could contribute the disease development. Further study and potentially modification of this NO pathway could lead to the development of new therapeutic strategies for this neurodegenerative disorder.

16100814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100814.value: Our brain function depends on efficient communication between neurons through synaptic transmission. Neurons display complex dendritic arborization to receive and process synaptic inputs. On the dendrites of excitatory neurons, there are protrusions called dendritic spines, where excitatory synapses are located. The stabilization and morphology of dendritic spines are influenced by synaptic activity. This extrinsic modulation of spine morphogenesis represents a crucial mechanism by which experience modulates synaptic strength and is central to brain development and adult brain function such as memory formation. Although dendritic spine plasticity has been extensively studied in the past decade, the information is still limited and the identification of new signaling mechanisms will be warranted. Spine remodeling requires the synthesis of new proteins. Interestingly, mRNAs are not restricted in the cell body of neuron. A subset of mRNA transcripts is also localized in dendrites, where their local protein synthesis upon synaptic stimulation might lead to structural changes of the synapse. Many of these mRNAs encode proteins whose functions have not been characterized. By comparing with our previous proteomic study, we found that some of these proteins are putative substrates of the serine/threonine kinase Cdk5, a key signaling protein that regulates spine morphogenesis and synaptic function. We hypothesize that these putative Cdk5 substrates represent locally synthesized proteins near synapses that regulate activity-dependent spine morphogenesis. To test this hypothesis, a putative GTPase-binding protein TBC1D24 was selected for further study. While the function of TBC1D24 is virtually unknown, three missense mutations of TBC1D24 have been associated with epilepsy and intellectual disability. We have found that TBC1D24 is a novel synaptic protein whose mRNA is localized in dendrites and its protein expression depends on neuronal activity. In the proposed study, we will investigate the synaptic function of TBC1D24 in neuron by knocking down its expression using RNAi and examine the effect on spine morphogenesis. The dendritic targeting of TBC1D24 mRNA, the regulation of its protein synthesis by synaptic activity, and the phosphorylation by Cdk5 will be determined. By generating TBC1D24 mutants and performing rescue experiments, we will address whether the disease-associated mutations of TBC1D24 impair dendritic spine morphogenesis. Given that aberrant neuronal protein synthesis and altered spine morphogenesis have been implicated in various neurodevelopmental diseases, and TBC1D24 mutations are associated with intellectual disability, the proposed study should identify a new regulatory protein at the synapse and increase our understanding of the molecular basis of brain disorders.

16100814.label: Realisation of objectives
16100814.value: Objective 1 To examine dendritic localization of the Tbc1d24 mRNA, rat primary hippocampal neurons were subjected to high resolution fluorescence in situ hybridization with sense or antisense probes against Tbc1d24, followed by immunofluorescence staining by anti-MAP2 antibody to label the neuronal dendrites. Images were acquired by confocal imaging. In situ hybridization revealed that Tbc1d24 mRNA existed as puncta that were present not only in the soma but also in distal dendrites (more than 100 m away from soma). We further determined the subcellular localization of TBC1D24 protein in neuron. Triple immunofluorescence staining with antibodies against TBC1D24, the presynaptic scaffold protein Bassoon, and GFP was performed in cultured hippocampal neurons co-transfected with tdTomato and GFP-tagged intrabody against the postsynaptic scaffold protein PSD-95. Images were acquired using super-resolution structured illumination microscopy in order to better distinguish the pre- and postsynaptic sites. TBC1D24 was present at the periphery of the Bassoon puncta and overlapped with PSD-95. The presence of TBC1D24 in the postsynaptic density was confirmed by fractionation of adult mouse brain and Western blot analysis. To ask whether TBC1D24 expression is regulated by neuronal activity, mature hippocampal neurons (14 days in vitro) were treated with the GABAA receptor antagonist bicuculline or the voltage-gated sodium channel blocker tetrodotoxin (TTX) for different durations. No significant difference in TBC1D24 expression was observed after either treatment. This was in contrast to the other dendritically localized RNAs that we examined (prmt8 and strn4), in which their protein expression was reduced by TTX treatment. Together these findings demonstrate that TBC1D24 protein is enriched at the postsynaptic sites. While the Tbc1d24 mRNA is detected in distal dendrites and hence may undergo local dendritic translation, neuronal activity is not the major stimulus to regulate the expression. Objective 2 To determine the function of TBC1D24 in dendritic spine morphogenesis, we introduced either the shRNA that targeted TBC1D24 or control shRNA into dissociated hippocampal neurons together with GFP construct, which outlined the dendrites and dendritic spines of the transfected neurons. Knockdown efficiency of the shRNA was validated by both immunostaining and Western blot analysis. Compared to neurons transfected with control shRNA, knockdown of TBC1D24 significantly reduced the number of dendritic spines. The spine loss was rescued by co-expression of the RNAi-resistant TBC1D24, thereby ruling out off-target effect. To ask whether the spine loss induced by the TBC1D244-shRNA represents reduced number of synapses, neurons were co-transfected with tdTomato and the GFP-tagged PSD-95 intrabody together with the shRNAs. Introduction of TBC1D24-shRNA significantly reduced the number of dendritic spines that contained PSD-95, and the phenotype was rescued by co-expression of RNAi-resistant TBC1D24. Knockdown of TBC1D24 also significantly reduced the number of PSD-95 puncta that were juxtaposed to the presynaptic excitatory marker vGLUT1 on the GFP-positive neuron. We performed whole-cell patch electrophysiological recording to directly examine excitatory synaptic transmission of neurons transfected with control or TBC1D24-shRNA. The frequency but not the amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic current was reduced in the GFP-positive neuron after knockdown of TBC1D24, which is consistent with a cell-autonomous decrease in synapse number on the postsynaptic neuron. We further determine whether TBC1D24 is crucial for synaptogenesis in human neurons. CRIPSR-mediated genome editing was performed in the human induced pluripotent cell (hiPSC) line IMR90, which resulted in error-prone non-homologous repair after the Cas9-mediated double-strand breaks on the TBC1D24 gene and the presence of premature stop codon. After clonal selection, knockout of the TBC1D24 gene was confirmed by Western blot showing the complete absence of TBC1D24 protein. Two independent clones of the TBC1D24 knockout iPSCs and the control iPSCs were differentiated into cortical neurons. Neural differentiation was monitored through immunostaining to show the expression of neural precursor markers Nestin and Sox2 in the neural rosettes and the expression of cortical markers TBR1 and BRN2. We found that absence of TBC1D24 caused significant reduction in the number of synaptophysin puncta that formed on the dendrites of the hiPSC-derived neurons, indicating the essential role of TBC1D24 in synapse development in human neurons. We also addressed the mechanism by which TBC1D24 maintains excitatory synapses. We hypothesize that TBC1D24 might mediate its synaptic function through inhibition of the small GTPase ARF6. Expression of the constitutively-active (Q67L) ARF6 but not the wild-type or dominant-negative (T27N) ARF6 significantly reduced the number of vGLUT1/PSD-95 puncta of hippocampal neurons, therefore mimics the effect of TBC1D24 knockdown in inducing loss of excitatory synapses. We also treated hippocampal neurons transfected with control- or TBC1D24-shRNA with the ARF6 inhibitor SecinH3. Pharmacological inhibition of ARF6 reversed the spine loss induced by TBC1D24-shRNA, while the inhibitor had no effect on the control neurons. SecinH3 treatment also partially rescued the loss of excitatory synapses induced by the TBC1D24-shRNA. These findings indicate that TBC1D24 maintains excitatory synapses via suppression of ARF6 activity. Objective 3 We examined four intellectual disability-associated missense mutations of the tbc1d24 gene, which resulted in the amino acid substitutions R40L, E153K, R242C and F251L. By expressing the four mutants in HEK-293T cells and primary hippocampal neurons, we found that only the F251L substitution drastically reduced TBC1D24 protein expression. To confirm the effect of F251L substitution on TBC1D24 expression and to investigate the consequences on brain function, we generated F251L knock-in mice harboring this missense mutation. Western blot analysis was performed to confirm the large reduction of TBC1D24 protein expression in the cerebral cortices and hippocampi of the knock-in mice. However, the level of tbc1d24 mRNA was similar to that of wild-type control, indicating that the mutation affects TBC1D24 expression at the post-transcriptional level. To test whether the mutation impairs protein stability, 293T cells expressing the wild-type or F251L mutant TBC1D24 were treated with the protein synthesis inhibitor cycloheximide to monitor turnover of the proteins. Increased protein turnover was observed for the F251L mutant as compared to wild-type TBC1D24. We cultured dissociated hippocampal neurons from embryos to investigate how the TBC1D24-F251L knock-in mutation affects dendritic spine morphogenesis. The homozygous knock-in neuron showed no significant difference in dendritic spine number compared to the wild-type control. However, dendritic spine heads were significantly larger in the mutant neurons. We then characterize the synaptic phenotype and animal behaviors of the TBC1D24 F251L knock-in mice. The homozygous and heterozygous mutant mice exhibit increased susceptibility to seizure induced by pentylentetrazole. Most homozygous mice died prematurely around postnatal day 21, while the heterozygous mice survived into adulthood. No apparent difference in brain size and anatomy across genotypes was observed. We examined excitatory synapses of the heterozygous knock-in mice in vivo by immunohistochemistry. There was significantly greater number but smaller puncta of the postsynaptic protein Homer1 in the stratum radiatum of CA1 hippocampus of the knock-in mice. Through stereotaxic injection of viruses that expressed YFP into the hippocampi, we found that the CA1 neurons of the F251L knock-in mice possessed fewer dendritic spines than the wild-type littermates. We also performed various behavioral tasks on the wild-type and heterozygous F251L mutant mice. The heterozygous mutant mice exhibited reduced fear memory after contextual fear conditioning, while no significant difference in the open field test and elevated plus maze was observed across genotypes. Therefore, depletion of TBC1D24 at early developmental stage due to the F251L mutation is associated with increased seizure susceptibility and impaired memory formation, and the behavioral abnormalities are associated with excitatory postsynaptic defects.

16100814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100814.value: Genetic variations that alter synapse development underlie many inherited neurodevelopemental disorders. The TBC1D24 gene, which encodes a signaling protein involved in the regulation of GTPases, contains more than 50 mutations identified to be associated with epilepsy, deafness, onychodystrophy, osteodystrophy, mental retardation, and seizures (DOORS) syndrome and intellectual disability. These human genetic studies clearly indicate the importance of this protein, but the precise function of TBC1D24 in the brain is not completely understood. Previous studies have demonstrated an important role of TBC1D24 in the control of neurotransmitter release from presynaptic neuron. In this project, we demonstrate that the Tbc1d24 mRNA is localized in dendrites, suggesting a potential role in the postsynaptic neuron. Super-resolution imaging and biochemical fractionation reveal that the TBC1D24 protein is present at postsynaptic sites. Using RNA-interference to deplete TBC1D24 both in vitro and in vivo, we found that TBC1D24 promotes the maintenance of dendritic spines and excitatory synapses of hippocampal neurons. Mechanistically, TBC1D24 regulates synapse maintenance through suppression of the small GTPase ARF6. Despite recent emerging studies on TBC1D24, there is still a lack of animal behavioural study on transgenic mice with tbcld24 gene mutations. We demonstrate that knockdown of TBC1D24 in the adult hippocampus in vivo alters animal behaviours, such as increased anxiety and hyperactivity, as well as impaired contextual fear conditioning. Moreover, we show that the disease-related missense mutation which leads to substitution of one amino acid (F251L) can destabilize and greatly reduce TBC1D24 expression. We generate F251L knock-in mice, which display aberrant excitatory synapses in the hippocampus, impaired contextual fear memory and increased susceptibility to seizure. These findings unravel a previously uncharacterized function of TBC1D24 in determining the proper number of synapses on the postsynaptic neuron. The study also represents the first report of how TBC1D24 depletion in vivo affects animal behaviours and memory formation in rodent, indicating that its deficiency leads to phenotypes that are relevant to the human disorder. This work has been submitted to PLOS Genetics and is currently under review. In relation to the current project in which we identify novel signaling proteins for spine morphogenesis based on mRNAs present in the hippocampal neuropil, we have also examined the functions of two other dendritically localized mRNAs that encode the scaffold protein STRN4 and the enzyme protein arginine methyltransferase 8 (PRMT8). The study on STRN4 has been published in Journal of Biological Chemistry, and the study on PRMT8 is submitted and reviewed by Cell Reports.

16100814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100814.value: By injecting shRNA targeting TBC1D24 in adult mouse hippocampus, we show that adult-onset depletion of TBC1D24 results in synaptic and cognitive deficits, indicating that TBC1D24 is crucial not only during early development but also in the mature brain. Although many patients carrying TBC1D24 gene mutations show early-onset epilepsy and developmental delay, our study raises the interesting possibility that adult therapeutic intervention may also have beneficial effect. Since pharmacological inhibition of ARF6 by secinH3 reverses the synaptic loss in TBC1D24- deficient cultured neurons, ARF6 inhibition may be a potential therapeutic strategy. The F251L knock-in mice generated in our study will be useful for future study of the disease pathophysiology and identification of drug targets. In the present study we focus on the effect of TBC1D24 depletion on excitatory synapses. Mass spectrometry has recently unraveled the inhibitory synaptic proteome, and interestingly TBC1D24 also represents one of the proteins associated with the inhibitory postsynaptic density. It is crucial to delineate how TBC1D24 regulates the development and function of inhibitory synapses using the F251L knock-in mice that we generate, which may provide new insights on the mechanism underlying excitatory-inhibitory imbalance and hence epilepsy in patients with TBC1D24 gene mutations.

16100814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100814.value: Neurons in the brain process and store information via the specialized structures called synapses. Despite its small size, each synapse contains a highly complicated signaling network consisting of enormous number of proteins. It is believed that dysfunction of these proteins will affect synaptic transmission and causes cognitive deficits that underlie neurodevelopmental disorders such as intellectual disability (ID). Recently many novel ID-associated gene mutations have been identified. It is crucial to delineate how the gene products function normally in the brain, which may lead to better understanding of the pathophysiology of ID. Human genetic studies have linked numerous gene mutations on tbc1d24 to epilepsy and intellectual disability. However, the function of this gene is not well-defined. Here we found that TBC1D24 protein is located at synapses of neurons in the hippocampus, a brain region that is critical to learning and memory. By depleting TBC1D24 expression through RNA interference or generation of mutant mice harboring an ID-associated tbc1d24 missense mutation that destabilizes the protein, we demonstrate that TBC1D24 deficiency impairs the maintenance of excitatory synapses in the brain as well as memory formation. This study unravels synaptic defect as the potential mechanism underlying cognitive deficits in individuals carrying tbc1d24 gene mutations.

16101114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101114.value: Plant hormone ethylene plays important roles in regulating developmental processes and signaling networks involved in plant responses to a wide range of biotic and abiotic stresses. Significant progress has been made in identifying the key components and understanding the roles of ethylene in plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses. Similar to a stress hormone, reactive oxygen species (ROS) are constantly produced in the plant cell. Environmental stresses significantly alter the ROS homeostasis and result in an excessive amount of ROS, leading to cellular oxidative damage and the induction of cell death. Plants have developed a molecular and cellular mechanism using ROS as signaling molecules to regulate both normal and stress-tolerant physiological processes. Post-translational modification (PTM) such as reversible protein phosphorylation and protein degradation plays a central role in cell signaling, regulation of gene expression, controlling the growth and development and the plant's adaptation to environmental changes. With the advent of powerful and robust quantitative PTM proteomics, we are now able to profile PTM proteins on a large scale and to determine the PTM sites associated with an environmental stresses and ethylene. In this proposed project, PTM proteomics will be applied onto the study of PTM-mediated cell signaling in stress and ethylene responses of a model plant Arabidopsis, focusing especially on the modification enzymes and proteins that target both EIN2 N- and C-terminal regions. To that end, we hereby propose to 1) profile the PTM sites and redox status of EIN2 under ethylene and stress induction using quantitative PTM proteomics approach, 2) profile ethylene and stress-induced phosphoproteomic changes resulting from the gene expression of both 35S-EIN2-NEND and 35S-EIN2-CEND; 3) identify kinase, phosphatase, endoprotease and other EIN2-targeting proteins using MS-based interactomics approach, and 4) determine the biochemical and cellular functions of these newly identified phosphoproteins and EIN2-modifying enzymes by performing molecular biological, cellular, physiological and reverse genetic analysis during ethylene- and stress-elicited signaling. This research is expected to provide information on the molecular mechanisms underlying crosstalk between ethylene and stress signaling in the regulation of plant stress responses. This work is expected to establish an intricate cell-signaling network involving numerous stress and ethylene signaling components. 16101414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101414.value: To achieve functional recovery after spinal cord injury, injured axons must regenerate past the injury and reform functional connections. Even limited regeneration could improve function, enhance quality of life, and decrease the burden of disability for people who have suffered spinal cord injuries. Recently we discovered molecular pathways that can be targeted to induce robust axon regeneration in the adult CNS. We will test whether deleting Pten and Socs3 in cortical neurons combined with decreasing extrinsic inhibition enables long-distance axon regeneration after a complete crush lesion at the thoracic level. Our proposed experiments might lead to the development of new repair strategies of promoting axon regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury. 為了促進脊髓損傷後功能恢復，受傷的軸突必須重新張過損傷區，并產生功能的連接。即使是有限的再生也可能改善功能，提高生活質量，和減少脊髓損傷造成的負擔。最近我們發現可以有針對性地誘導成年小鼠中樞神經系統軸突再生的的分子途徑。我們將測試在皮層神經元敲除PTEN和SOCS3并結合減少外在的抑制因素是否可以進一步使軸突再生。我們所提出的實驗可能產生促進脊髓損傷後軸突再生和功能恢復的新方法。

16101414.label: Realisation of objectives
16101414.value: Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes permanent functional deficits due to the failure of axon regeneration in the adult central nervous system (CNS). The lack of regeneration has largely been attributed to the diminished growth capacity of the neurons and the inhibitory environment. Many efforts have been attempted to promote the axon regeneration in the spinal cord, mostly either before or immediately after injury. Then, the question is, with well-established gliosis and inhibitory extra-cellular matrix at the lesion site in the chronic SCI, whether CNS neurons can still regenerate. As one of the longest projecting axons, corticospinal tract (CST) involves voluntary fine motor control and plays an important functional role in humans. The loss of the regrowth potential of axons in the corticospinal motor neurons (CSMN) is accompanied by corresponding down-regulation of mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) activity in neurons after injury. Deleting Pten in CSMN of young mice before the injury can prevent the down-regulation, and thus promote robust axonal regrowth after injury, although the majority of the axons are still prevented from crossing the lesion, suggesting the inhibitory nature of the lesion site. Pten deletion has also been shown to rescue axon growth defects in degenerating motor neurons. However, whether injured adult CSMN can re-activate the growth program and regenerate their axons remains elusive. Thus, in this study, we tested whether chronically-injured corticospinal tract can still regenerate after pten deletion. In order to induce much more robust regeneration, it will also be necessary to combine with other intrinsic mechanisms to regulate regrowth in adult. Deleting both Pten and suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 (Socs3) in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) promotes long-distance axonal regeneration. Thus, we also assessed this using corticospinal tract in this study. Importantly, whether the axons with enhanced growth capacity are still prevented from growth by the lesion site through those known inhibitors such as CSPG or myelin inhibitors was not demonstrated. Thus it will be very interesting to test whether the combination of removing inhibitory molecules and promoting intrinsic growth capacity can further enhance the axonal regeneration. Pten deletion initiated 12 months after T8 crush promotes CST regeneration Through Cre-expressing, self-complementary AAV serotype 2/1, a large number of corticospinal motor neurons (CSMNs) can be targeted in adult mice, and biotin dextran amine (BDA) tracing can be effectively used to assess the axon sprouting or regeneration. We tested the effect of this strategy in a chronically injury paradigm. A T8 crush was carried out, and 12 months later we injected AAV-Cre or AAV-GFP into one side of the hemisphere. CST was then traced 4 months later by BDA. In the controls rarely could a few axons be seen approaching the injury site. In Pten-deleted mice, we did not see the obvious extension of the main CST bundle. However, a few axons grew into and even beyond the lesion, up to 1.5 mm. Seven months after the AAV-Cre injection, the main CST bundle extended up to the boundary of the lesion, and evident axons regrew into the injury site and even across the lesion for up to 3 mm. The result was published in Journal of Neuroscience in July 2015. Pten deletion promotes corticospinal tract regrowth similarly as Pten;Socs3 double deletion We further examined CST sprouting effect after deletion of Pten, Socs3 or both genes. We used AAV-Cre to mediate the conditional knockout. We injected AAV-Cre into one side of the motor cortex in 4 groups of the adult mice, WT, Pten floxed, Socs3 floxed, Pten/Socs3 double floxed mice. Mice receiving virus injection did not show any developmental abnormities. After 6 weeks, we applied a unilateral pyramidotomy, where CST axons from one side of the sensorimotor cortex were transected at the level of the medulla above the pyramidal decussation. To detect collateral sprouting from the uninjured CST, we injected the tracer biotin dextran amine (BDA) into the motor cortex at 8 weeks after injury. Compared with the control group in which there was limited sprouting across the midline, both Pten and Pten/Socs3 deletion resulted in extensive trans-midline sprouting. Pten and Pten/Socs3 deletion revealed more robust sprouting, while Socs3 deletion only resulted in modest numbers of axons across the midline. However, co-delete Socs3 with Pten did not show synergistic effects. Quantification of the sprouting axons suggested that the numbers of sprouting axons at different levels did not increase. Effects of decreasing both extrinsic and intrinsic inhibitions on axon regeneration To examine whether inhibiting CSPGs can further promote axon regeneration after Pten deletion. We used a simpler optic nerve injury model to demonstrate whether this approach is feasible. Similarly as the pyramidotomy experiment, we used AAV-Cre to mediate the conditional knockout. For the optic nerve crush experiment, we used 5-6 weeks old WT or Pten floxed mice. Either AAV2-Cre or AAV2-GFP virus was injected into the vitreous bodies of with a Hamilton microsyringe. Three weeks after the virus injection, the optic nerve was gently exposed intraorbitally and crushed with jeweler’s forceps around 1 mm behind the optic disk. In order to degrade CSPGs in vivo, 1ul ChondroitinaseABC in gel-foam was attached to the crush site immediately after injury. Penicillinase was used as control. After ChABC digestion, we found evident axon regeneration. When we combined ChABC with Pten deletion, we found the additional treatment by ChABC promoted more axons to regenerate beyond the lesion site. The result demonstrated the effect of removing extrinsic inhibition could further enhance axon regeneration induced by the intrinsic mechanism. Consistent with our finding in the optic nerve, a similar enhancing effect of ChABC was also reported in the CST sprouting model by others. It would be redundant to further test ChABC on CST sprouting or regeneration. To test the hypothesis that combining an elevation of neuron-intrinsic growth ability and a reduction of extrinsic growth inhibition may further improve injury-induced axonal growth, we collaborated with Prof. Binhai Zheng’s group at UCSD and examined the CST regeneration by co-deleting Pten and Nogo. Caudal to the injury site, there were minimal numbers of axons in control or Nogo-deleted mice. In contrast, both Pten and Pten/Nogo-deleted mice exhibited significantly higher numbers of axons beyond the injury site. These data provide proof-of- principle evidence that manipulating both neuron-intrinsic and -extrinsic factors can further improve axon regeneration.

16101414.value: 1. Pten deletion promotes regeneration of corticospinal tract axons after chronic spinal cord injury, even at one year after lesion. 16101414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101414.value: It is surprising that combining Pten/Socs3 did not achieve significant more CST growth from our own study. Also, the effect of combining ChABC (from others) or Nogo KO (from our collaboration study) with Pten deletion only modestly enhances CST sprouting or regeneration. It suggested that in order to promote more and faster CST regeneration, other combination strategy may be needed. Along this line, we have been actively trying to identify novel mechanisms for axon regeneration. We demonstrated that axon regenerative capacity could be boosted with the right stimulants on neuronal activity through either an optogenetic or a chemogenetic approach. The result was published in PNAS in February 2016. We found that overexpression of melanopsin in retinas of mice could enhance neuronal firing of RGCs and promote axonal regeneration after optic nerve crush. Our work identifies a mechanistic link between axon regeneration and neuronal activity in vivo and provides an intrinsic factor that can be further exploited to promote neural repair after injury. When combining enhancing neuronal activity with Pten deletion, we found that this strategy further promotes CST axon sprouting than single treatment. Thus, we have turned our focus onto this combination strategy instead. Studies are currently under investigation.

16101414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101414.value: To achieve functional recovery after spinal cord injury, injured axons must regenerate past the injury and reform functional connections. Even limited regeneration could improve function, enhance quality of life, and decrease the burden of disability for people who have suffered spinal cord injuries. Recently we discovered molecular pathways that can be targeted to induce robust axon regeneration in the adult CNS. In this study, we focused on the corticospinal tract that is mainly involved with the voluntary fine motor control. We have found that chronically-injured corticospinal tract can be induced to regenerate across the lesion site after knocking out Pten, a gene that intrinsically inhibits axon regeneration. Surprisingly, deleting both Pten and Socs3, another intrinsic inhibitor, does not further enhance the corticospinal tract sprouting after pyramidotomy. Combining with decreasing certain extrinsic inhibition can further enhance axon regeneration or sprouting. Our findings may lead to the development of new repair strategies for promoting axon sprouting and regeneration after spinal cord injury.

16101614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101614.value: Mutations in the Seipin/BSCL2 gene cause congenital generalized lipodystrophy in human. An almost complete lack of adipose tissues gives rise to a plethora of metabolic disorders such as insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia and hepatic steatosis, owing in part to ectopic fat deposition in non-adipose tissues. To understand the pathology associated with Seipin dysfunction and to develop therapeutic strategies, it is critical to elucidate the role of Seipin in lipid homeostasis at cellular and organismal levels. Our long-term goal is to understand how storage and mobilization of fat are regulated at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-lipid droplets (LD) interface. The objective of this proposal is to decipher how proper targeting of Seipin to the proximity of LDs is linked to its role in regulating LD size. We have previously shown that physical and functional coupling of LDs to the ER is facilitated by a macro-molecular complex and requires an intact tubular ER network. Seipin has been reported to localize at ER-LD junctions in yeast. By visualizing a functional C. elegans Seipin::GFP fusion protein, we discovered novel tubular structures that partially or completely encase a subset of LDs. This led us to formulate a central hypothesis that these Seipin positive cages are derived from the tubular ER network and control LD size by promoting fat storage or restricting fat mobilization. The aims of the proposed experiments are to (1) define the molecular determinants of Seipin localization in vivo; (2) define the functional relationship between LDs and Seipin positive cages; (3) identify the subcellular origin and components of Seipin positive cages. This proposal explores how protein-protein and protein-lipid interactions contribute to Seipin targeting to a hitherto uncharacterized cytoplasmic compartment. We expect our research to refine our understanding on LD interaction with other sub-cellular compartments, and how functional heterogeneity of LDs can be enforced as a result. Our work should provide insights on cellular lipid homeostasis and how it is perturbed in lipodystrophy and related diseases. 人體中，BSCL2基因（編碼Seipin蛋白）中的某些突變能夠導致一種先天性的全身脂肪代謝障礙。脂肪組織的幾近完全缺失將引起大量的代謝紊亂症狀，如胰島素抗性、高甘油三酯血症及肝臟脂肪變性等，這些症狀的產生在一定程度上是由非脂肪組織中脂肪的異常積累所引起。出於理解與Seipin蛋白功能失調相關的病理學機制、以及開發臨床治療方法的需要，在細胞與生物體水平上闡明脂質內穩態中Seipin所扮演的角色顯得尤為關鍵。我們的長期目標在於探明內質網﹣脂滴交界面上脂肪調動與貯存的調節機制。而本篇研究計劃的目標在於破譯Seipin的定位及調節脂滴大小的機制，同時探討Seipin定位與調節現象間的承接關係。我們之前有報導過，脂滴與內質網間實體性或功能性的偶聯是由一大分子複合物所促使的，並且這種偶聯需要一個完整的內質網管狀網絡。在酵母中，已有研究發現Seipin定位於內質網與脂滴的接合點。將秀麗隱桿線蟲中Seipin與綠色螢光蛋白融合，通過觀察該融合蛋白，我們發現一些新穎的管狀結構，這些管狀結構或完全或不完全地圍繞在部份脂滴上。以上的發現引導著我們提出一重要假設：這些包含Seipin的籠狀結構起源於內質網管狀網絡，且這種結構能夠通過促進脂肪貯存或限制脂肪調動來調節脂滴的大小。本研究方案的目的在于：（1）明確Seipin在細胞中靶向定位的分子決定因素；（2）明確脂滴與Seipin所在籠狀結構間的功能關係；（3）鑑定Seipin所在籠狀結構的組分及其在亞細胞水平上的起源。Seipin靶向定位於迄今為止未被發現的一特殊胞質區室，基於此，該研究方案會繼續觀察相關的蛋白與蛋白之間、蛋白與脂質之間的相互作用，進而探討這些作用對Seipin定位所作的貢獻。我們期望這一研究能夠拓展我們對脂滴與其他亞細胞區室結構互作關係的認識，同時改善我們對脂滴功能異質性成因的理解。我們的工作將為細胞中脂質內穩態、如何對抗脂肪代謝障礙及關聯疾病提供深入見解。

16101614.label: Realisation of objectives
16101614.value: (1.1) Identification of key residues for proper targeting of Seipin We have constructed multiple C. elegans strains that express tagRFP/GFP fusion of C. elegans SEIP-1 mutants from single-copy transgenes. Proper targeting of C. elegans SEIP-1 was not affected when the C-terminal RKRK residues were all mutated to alanines. Moreover, purified C. elegans SEIP-1 C-terminus (231-274 a.a.) failed to bind liposomes reconstituted from brain lipid extracts, which were enriched with anionic phosphoinositides. Therefore, we have yet to obtain convincing evidence that supports a role of C-terminal basic residues for SEIP-1 targeting. To identify additional determinants for SEIP-1 targeting, we next focused on SEIP-1 residues that are orthologous to those mutated in human seipin in lipodystrophy patients. These residues are A185 and Y160 in the conserved loop region of SEIP-1. Similar to A185P, Y160C mutant SEIP-1 (analogous to Y187C found in seipin of a lipodystrophy patient) was also partially retained in the general ER and in punctate structures in the proximity of LDs. Such altered localization may in part be due to the instability of these SEIP-1 mutants, as confirmed by Western blotting. In addition, we used CRISPR to engineer mutations in the endogenous seip-1 locus so that SEIP-1(A185P) was expressed. The average LD size was reduced in worms that expressed SEIP-1(A185P), and shared the aberrant LD morphology phenotype of seip-1(-) worms. In summary, we identified A185 and Y160 as conserved residues that are critical for proper targeting SEIP-1. We have generated transgenic worms that expressed GFP fusion of human seipin at single-copy level. We noted that human seipin also localized to peri-LD cages. Furthermore, the heterologous expression of human seipin in C. elegans seip-1(-) mutant restored the median LD diameter to wild type level. Our results indicate that the localization and function of seipin family members are conserved. (1.2) Identification of lipid species that dictate Seipin targeting to peri-LD cages Seipin::GFP fusion protein was primarily retained in the general ER in fat-3 mutant animals. FAT-3 acts in the de novo PUFAs synthesis pathway in C. elegans by introducing extra double bonds to C18:2n6 and C18:3n3 at their delta-6 position. To pinpoint the dependence of proper Seipin targeting on specific FAs species, we surveyed all desaturases in this pathway using either genetic null alleles or RNAi-mediated knockdown. Our genetic analysis led us to conclude that the proper targeting of SEIP-1::GFP to peri-LD cages relies specifically on C18:3n6 and/or C20:3n6. We then supplemented these FAs to the E. coli diet of fat-3 mutants. Supplementation of either FA could restore proper SEIP-1::GFP targeting. We also noted the effect of C18:3n6 supplementation was more potent than C20:3n6. We developed a GC-MS assay to measure the absolute quantity of FAs in C. elegans. Using this assay, we compared the FAs profile between wild-type and fat-3 mutant animals. We noted that, in addition to PUFAs, the absolute abundance of two cyclopropane FA (CFAs) species (C17:0Δ and C19:0Δ) was also reduced in fat-3 mutants. Since CFAs in C. elegans are exclusively derived from their E. coli diet, we sought to manipulate the dietary CFA level in order to assess the functional importance of CFAs in SEIP-1::GFP targeting. In E. coli, CFAs are synthesized by a sole CFA synthase from monounsaturated fatty acids. To this end, we obtained the E. coli CFA synthase deletion mutant and its parental strain BW25113 from the Keio collection. In contrast to wild-type C. elegans fed wild-type BW25113, proper targeting of SEIP-1::GFP to peri-LD cages was also perturbed in wild-type C. elegans fed Δcfa BW25113 strain. Furthermore, targeting of SEIP-1::GFP to peri-LD cages was completely blocked in fat-3 mutant C. elegans fed the Δcfa E. coli. In summary, we identified CFAs and specific PUFAs that dictate seipin targeting to peri-LD cages. (2.1) Elaboration of Seipin positive cages during LD expansion To capture the dynamics of peri-LD cages biogenesis and maturation, we stably co-expressed C. elegans Seipin::Venus and mRuby::LiveDrop in heterologous, mammalian COS7 cells. LiveDrop contains a membrane hairpin domain of Drosophila GPAT4 (160–216 a.a.) and was reported as a marker of all nascent LDs. Prior to oleic acid (OA) supplementation, we noted that SEIP-1 was present in the ER tubules and bright puncta. Upon OA loading, we observed stepwise maturation of SEIP-1 positive structures from the puncta adjacent to nascent LDs to spherical cages enclosing the expanding LDs. We concluded that peri-LD cages defined by C. elegans SEIP-1 are elaborated from ER tubules during LD expansion. (2.2) Modification of SEIP-1 positive cages during fat mobilization We have investigated if SEIP-1 positive peri-LD cages form a physical barrier for the recruitment of the triglyceride lipase ATGL-1 to block lipolysis. To this end, we knocked in the GFP coding sequence into the atgl-1 locus of C. elegans by CRISPR. The ATGL-1::GFP fusion protein was found on the surface of LDs in the presence or absence of peri-LD cages. Furthermore, the reduction in LD size during fasting appeared to be independent of peri-LD cages. We therefore conclude that peri-LD cages do not promote LD expansion by inhibiting lipolysis. (3.1) Determination of the relationship between Seipin cages and the tubular ER The integrity of the tubular ER network is maintained by the evolutionarily conserved protein Atlastin. We have previously shown that loss of Atlastin function, reduced LD size. We postulated that the disruption of the ER network would alter the structure or function of peri-LD cages. Consistent with this model, over-expression of SEIP-1 failed to promote LD expansion in Atlastin deficient animals although the targeting of SEIP-1 to peri-LD cages was unperturbed. We conclude that Atlastin acts upstream of SEIP-1 to promote LD expansion. To resolve peri-LD cages at the ultrastructural level, we generated additional COS7 cell lines that stably expressed a C. elegans SEIP-1::APEX2 fusion protein at low levels. The APEX2 peroxidase reacts with diaminobenzidine (DAB) to generate local deposits that can be stained with uranyl acetate and osmium tetroxide. Accordingly, we found that C. elegans SEIP-1::APEX2-mediated deposits was specifically enriched on ER tubules in the proximity of LDs in oleic acid loaded cells. Our results suggest that peri-LD cages are conserved ER subdomains that support LD expansion. (3.2) Identification of proteins that physically or functionally interact with Seipin We did not detect overt co-localization of SEIP-1 with USE1 and calnexin in C. elegans, although these two proteins have previously been reported to physically interact with human seipin. We next turned our attention to Pex30 because it has been reported that Fld1/seipin and Pex30 define an ER subdomain for LD and peroxisome biogenesis in yeast. To this end, we ectopically co-expressed yeast Pex30 and C. elegans Seipin in COS7 cells. Upon oleic acid loading, Pex30 was enriched in peri-LD cages with Seipin. Notably, the enrichment of Pex30 was also restricted to a subset of LDs. We concluded that C. elegans Seipin and yeast Pex30 marked the same ER subdomain for LD expansion.
