16103714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103714.value: Recently, genome-wide search has identified more than 370,000 conventional G-quadruplex (G4) forming sequences in the human genome. However, my group also found that non-conventional G-qudruplex sequences can also fold into G-quadruplexes indicating a much large pool of G-quadruplex sequences in human genome. G4 motifs are evolutionarily conserved in telomeres, mitotic and meiotic double-strand break sites, and transcriptional start sites near promoters, suggesting multiple roles for G4 structures in DNA replication, transcription and translation. In addition, studies have shown that failure to resolve G-quadraplex structures makes these G4 sequences hotspots for genomic instability. Currently, it is known that many human diseases, such as cancer, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), are involved in G4 DNA and RNA. With the support of this grant together with other supports, we have made tremendous progresses in the structure-functional study of G-quadruplex of DNA and RNA in human DNA replication initiation and related diseases as shown in many publications attached to this report. The referees for these papers all gave very positive responses. In order to conduct the mechanistic study of G-quadruplex mediated human DNA replication origin recognition, we have to determine the structures of different types of G-quadruplex DNA and RNA and identify the proteins that bind to these G-quadruplexes. Firstly, we have determined noval G-quadruplex structure of human telomeric DNA by NMR spectroscopy (Liu, C et al (2018) Chem. Sci. (IF 9.1)) and a chair type telomeric DNA structure by x-ray (Geng, YY et al (2019) Nucleic Acids Res. (IF 11.5)). These two papers have made noticeable contributions towards our understanding of the biology of human telomeric DNA and anti-cancer drug design. Meanwhile, we used the similar techniques studied G-quadruplex structures of the human G4C2 DNA repeats which is believed to be the major genetic cause of human ALS/FTD as described in the two papers by Zhou B. et al ((2015) and (2018) Sci. Rep.). A novel crystal structure of d(G4C2)2 will be submitted soon. Finally, we have identified those protein components Orc1 and Cdc6 in the pre-replication complex and EBNA1 DNA binding protein from EBV can bind to human G-quadruplexes. We have determined structures of G-quadruplex/Cdc6 complexes. Other complexes will be determined soon. These results are in preparation for publications. In conclusion, we discovered several novel structural folds of G-quadruplexes and G-quadruplex/Cdc6 complexes. These mechanistic studies will provide insight on the molecular mechanism for origin selection in human and human viruses.

16103714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103714.value: This RGC supported research has enabled us to determine novel G-quadruplex structures formed by human telomeric DNA sequences and G4C2 DNA repeats, which were published on high impact journals. The new G-quadruplex structures of human telomeric DNA are the targets for anti-cancer drug design. We are among the first two groups in the world determined G-qadruplex structures of G4C2 repeat DNAs which are the potential drug targets for the potential treatment of incurable ALS/FTD. Currently we are collaborating with the chemists to design anti-cancer and anti-ALS/FTD compounds based on our high resolution G-quadruplex structures. We are the front-runner in these two fields of studies. Based on the structure of Cdc6/G-quadruplex, we have carried out many different mutations of Cdc6 that can selectively bind to G-quadruplex DNA and G-quadruplex RNA. These specific G-quadruplex binding peptides can be further design as fluorescent probes. These new probes could solve the currently unsolved problems in tracking G-quadruplex formation in vivo during cell cycle and in different disease states. The impact of the above work will be tremendous in the G-quadruplex research.

16103714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103714.value: All life forms on earth require DNA replications for them to survive and evolve. DNA replication involves replication initiation, elongation and termination. For yeast, it is known that particular DNA sequences determine where the DNA starts to be replicated (replication initiation). However, story is much more complicated for human. Because there are about 10,000 replication origins for replication initiation, we still do not know what determine the initiation of human DNA replication. In this proposed research, we studied a possible factor, namely G-quadruplex forming DNA sequences, for determining the human DNA replication initiation. Our research has identified that proteins that involve in determining the replication initiation could bind to the human G-qadruplexes indicating that these G-quadruplexes could form the origins of human DNA replication. This work contribute to our understanding of fundamental biology of DNA replication. Meanwhile, we have determined new G-quadruplex structures of human telomeric DNA. New compounds will be designed based on these structures for potential treatment of cancer. In addition, we have determined new structures of G4C2 DNA repeats which are thought to be the main cause of incurable human FTD/ALS. We are developing compounds targeting on these structures of G4C2 DNA repeats for possible anti-FTD/ALS treatment.

16200014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200014.value: 鄰近問題（proximity problem）的近似算法的改進

16200014.label: Project Objectives
16200014.value: Design and analyze efficient approximation algorithms for proximity problems such as diameter, bichromatic closest pair, external nearest neighbors, and Euclidean minimum spanning trees.
rows: Design and analyze efficient approximation algorithms for proximity problems such as diameter, bichromatic closest pair, external nearest neighbors, and Euclidean minimum spanning trees.

16200014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200014.value: Proximity problems are among the most fundamental problems in Computational Geometry, with numerous applications in areas such as information retrieval, pattern recognition, and machine learning. Examples of problems that have been extensively studied include closest pair, diameter, bichromatic closest pair, external nearest neighbors, and Euclidean minimum spanning trees. As proximity problems are often hard to solve exactly, it is natural to consider these problems in the context of approximation. While approximation algorithms for these problems are known that are optimal in terms of the dependency of their running times on the input size, it seems that the dependency of their running times on the desired approximation accuracy can be significantly improved. In applications where high accuracy is important, the approximation-dependencies can dominate the running time. We propose to design approximation algorithms whose running times are efficient both in terms of the input size and the desired approximation accuracy. 鄰近問題（proximity problem）是計算幾何中最基礎的一類問題。其在諸如資訊檢索、模式識別以及機器學習等領域中有極為廣泛的應用。包括最近點對問題(closest pair)、直徑問題(diameter)、雙色最近點對問題(bichromatic closest pair)、外部最近鄰問題(external nearest neighbors) 以及歐幾里德最小生成樹問題(Euclidean minimum spanning trees)在內的這一系列鄰近問題已經得到了深入和細緻的研究。由於鄰近問題之複雜，精確地求解往往十分困難，因此我們通常考慮使用近似算法求取它的近似解。如果僅僅考慮輸入規模 對算法運行時間的影響，這些問題目前已經存在最優的近似算法了，但是如果我們同時也考慮近似精度對算法運行時間的影響，那麼這些算法的運行時間仍然有極大的改進空間。在應用算法時，如果我們對近似精度的要求很高，算法的運行時間則主要由近似精度決定。我們計畫設計能夠在大規模輸入和高精度要求下快速地解決鄰近問題的近似算法。

16200014.label: Realisation of objectives
16200014.value: The goal of our project was to develop efficient approximation algorithms for proximity problems. This objective has been fully realized. Throughout our work, we assume that the input points reside in real d-dimensional space and the dimension d is fixed. We treat both the number of points n and the approximation parameter eps as asymptotic quantities. In light of its deep connections to approximate nearest-neighbor searching and many other fundamental proximity problems, the polytope membership problem turns out to be central to our work. In this problem, we are given a convex polytope K in d dimensions, and the objective is to preprocess K into a data structure so that, given any query point q, it is possible to determine efficiently whether q is in K. We consider this problem in an approximate setting. Given an approximation parameter eps, the query can be answered either way if the distance from q to K's boundary is at most eps times K's diameter. In J1, we presented the most efficient data structure known until then for the approximate polytope membership problem. This data structure is based on a simple quadtree-based decomposition of space. The quadtree hierarchically subdivides space into hypercube cells, stopping when a cell is either entirely inside or outside of K, or (if it intersects K's boundary) it is locally approximable by at most t halfspaces, where t denotes the desired query time. Queries are answered by descending the quadtree to determine the leaf cell containing the query point, and (if not inside or outside) testing whether the query point lies within the approximating halfspaces. While the data structure is simple, the analysis of its space requirements is quite involved and is based on a deeper understanding of the local structure of the convex body's boundary. In J2, we improve the state of the art for many fundamental proximity problems including approximate polytope membership. Until this work, virtually all algorithms proposed for finding approximate solutions to proximity problems were based on subdividing space using axis-aligned fat cells, generally hypercubes arranged in grids or quadtrees. The question of whether more adaptive subdivisions (whose cells may be elongated and oriented in any direction) could yield faster approximation algorithms remained open. In this paper, we present a novel technique to decompose geometric problems non-uniformly in different directions. The key element of our approach is a hierarchy of Macbeath regions which yields major improvements to a plethora of fundamental problems in geometric approximation. Among the static problems, we obtain major improvements to the computation of eps-kernels, approximate diameter, approximate bichromatic closest pair, and approximate Euclidean minimum spanning trees. Among the data structure problems, we obtain major improvements to approximate polytope membership and approximate nearest neighbor searching. In C1, we develop a very efficient approximation algorithm for the Euclidean minimum spanning tree (EMST) problem. After almost 25 years of study, all known near-linear time algorithms for the eps-approximate EMST problem have exponential eps dependencies that grow linearly with dimension. In this paper, we show that these dimensional exponential eps dependencies can be eliminated altogether. Our algorithm is based on quadtrees and is simple and deterministic. In C2, we consider the approximate EMST problem in the context of range searching, which is a fundamental tool in computational geometry. Typically, range searching involves either counting or reporting the points lying within a given query region, but it is often desirable to compute statistics that better describe the structure of the point set lying within the region, not just the count. Often, such properties are based on graph structures that are implicitly defined by the point sets. One of the most fundamental example of such a graph is the EMST. Given a set P of n points in d dimensions, our objective is to preprocess P so that given an admissible query region Q, it is possible to efficiently approximate the weight of the EMST of the subset of P that lies within Q. We allow two natural sources of approximation error, first by treating the query region Q as a fuzzy object (so that points near the region's boundary may be included or excluded at the algorithm's discretion) and second by approximating the MST weight itself. In C2, we formalize these concepts precisely and present an efficient data structure for answering such queries. Our approach uses simple data structures based on quadtrees, and it can be applied whenever the query range is a fat compact set of constant combinatorial complexity. Approximation problems involving a single convex body have received a great deal of attention in the computational geometry community. In contrast, works involving multiple convex bodies are generally limited to very low dimensions or do not consider approximation. In C3, we consider approximations to two natural problems involving multiple convex bodies: detecting whether two polytopes intersect and computing their Minkowski sum. These problems arise naturally in a number of applications. Examples include geometric packing and covering, wire and component layout in VLSI, map overlay in geographic information systems, motion planning, and collision detection. In the approximate polytope intersection problem, we are given a collection of two or more convex polytopes in d dimensions, which we are allowed to preprocess individually. Given any two preprocessed polytopes A and B, the query determines whether A and B intersect approximately. More generally, we can answer queries for the images of A and B under affine transformations. We present efficient data structures for approximate intersection and show how it can also be used to approximate the Minkowski sum of any two polytopes. Finally, we present a surprising impact of these results on approximating the width of a set of points. Our algorithms and data structures in this paper are based on a data structure defined by a hierarchy of Macbeath regions, which we developed in J2. While approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) searching in Euclidean spaces is fairly well understood, much less is known in the non-Euclidean case. In C4, we present an efficient approach to approximate nearest-neighbor searching involving non-Euclidean distances, including convex scaling distance functions and Bregman divergences. The main idea of our paper is as follows. In the Euclidean case, the best data structure reduces ANN to approximate polytope membership using the well-known lifting transformation, as described in J1. However, this transformation applies only for the Euclidean distance. In C4, we discovered a novel way of circumventing this limitation. The key observation is that the convex approximation techniques developed in J2 do not only apply to convex polytopes, but can be adapted to work on any convex body, even one with curved boundaries. This provides an additional degree of flexibility. Rather than applying a transformation to linearize the various distance functions, we can go a bit overboard and "convexify" them. Under mild assumptions on the growth rates of the distance functions, our approach allows us to answer queries in space and time that nearly match the best known result for the Euclidean metric.

16200014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200014.value: We have presented significantly faster approximation algorithms for many fundamental proximity problems in our work. Here we present the rough running times of some of our key algorithms to give some flavor of our results. Our improvements arise as a result of novel techniques such as Macbeath regions [J2] and convexification [C4]. In J2, we reduce the dependency of the running time or storage on the approximation parameter eps for several problems. Among the static problems, we obtain major improvements to the computation of eps-kernels, approximate diameter, and approximate bichromatic closest pair. We reduce the respective running times for the first two problems from O(n + 1/eps^d) to O(n + 1/eps^{d/2}), and for the third problem from O(n/eps^{d/3}) to O(n/eps^{d/4}). Among the data structure problems, we obtain major improvements to approximate polytope membership and approximate nearest-neighbor searching. We reduce the respective storage for these problems for logarithmic query time from O(1/eps^d) to O(1/eps^{d/2}) and from O(n/eps^d) to O(n/eps^{d/2}). In C1, we present an approximation algorithm for the Euclidean minimum spanning tree (EMST) that runs in time O(n log n + n / eps^2). Previous algorithms have running times that grow as O(n / eps^{O(d)}). Thus, our algorithm is the first one for this problem that eliminates the exponential eps dependence on dimension. In C2, we consider this problem in the context of range searching and show that we can answer approximate queries in logarithmic time with a data structure of linear space. In C3, we show how to preprocess polytopes into data structures of size O(1/eps^{d/2}) such that we can answer in polylogarithmic time whether two polytopes intersect approximately. Using this result, we show how to approximate the Minkowski sum of two given polytopes in time O(n + 1/eps^{d/2}). We also reduce the running time for computing the approximate width of a set of points from O(n + 1/eps^d) to O(n + 1/eps^{d/2}). In C4, we present algorithms for approximate nearest-neighbor searching under a variety of non-Euclidean distances. In particular, we consider convex scaling distance functions and Bregman divergences. Under mild assumptions on the growth rates of these functions, we present data structures that answer queries in logarithmic time using O(n/eps^{d/2}) space, nearly matching the best known results for the Euclidean metric.

16200014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200014.value: In our work, we have reduced the eps-dependencies in the running time of algorithms for many fundamental proximity problems. The key question now is whether the resulting eps-dependencies are optimal or if they can be reduced further. The most important problems to consider from this perspective are the diameter and width problems. Another interesting line of work is to extend our data structures for detecting the intersection of convex bodies to return the approximate separation distance if the bodies do not intersect or the approximate penetration distance if they do. We would also like to tackle more general queries involving multiple convex bodies such as approximate membership with respect to the Minkowski sum of a constant number of bodies.

16200014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200014.value: In this project, we considered many fundamental proximity problems involving distances between points, which have numerous applications in fields such as machine learning, data mining, and motion planning. We have developed data structures and algorithms for solving these problems approximately that are much more efficient than previous approaches.

16200114.value: 摳圖為基礎的三維模型和相關數據轉換和合成

16200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200114.value: With the advent of 3D technology in recent years, there are a growing number of 3D applications and projects such as 3D movies, free-viewpoint TV, 3D gaming, etc. There is also growing availability of 3D-ready devices including TVs, displays, set-top boxes, DVD and Blu-Ray players, gaming consoles, mobile devices such as smartphones and gaming devices. As of today, the generation, synthesis, representation and processing of 3D content are often less than satisfactory. Thus there is a need for intensive research on such topics. One problem is the limitation of the traditional representation of a multiview 3D signal with each view composing of 2 components: texture plus depth. This 2-component/view representation is problematic as it fails to reflect that some pixels (e.g. at object bourndary) should be partly foreground and partly background. Such failure often leads to low quality syntheized view. Motivated by the fact that image matting is a tool that can decompose an image into foreground, background with a corresponding alpha matte, we propose in this project to apply image matting tools to 3D multiview representation so that each view can be decomposed into 5 components: foreground texture, foreground depth, background texture, background depth and an alpha matte. This ground-breaking 5-component/view representation should bring signficant benefit to view synthesis. It can also potentially enable us to perform much more sophisticated and powerful 3D operation with higher accuracy. We propose to investigate several important problems related to this novel 5-component/view representation, namely, the generation of the 5-component/view representation, the use of the alpha matte to refine the often erroneous depth map, the view synthesis using the 5-component/view representation and the coding of the 5-component/view 3D data. With these tools developed, we hope that this ground-breaking representation and associated tools can inspire new 3D applications. 隨著3D技術在近幾年的出現，也有越來越多的3D應用程序和 3D電影項目：如，自由視點電視，3D遊戲等。也有設備，包 括3D就緒電視，顯示器，機頂盒，DVD和藍光播放器，遊戲 機，移動設備的日益普及：如智能手機和遊戲設備。截至今 日，3D內容的生成，合成，表徵和加工往往不盡如人意。因 此，有必要對3D此類話題的深入研究。其中一個問題是信號 的2個部分組成每個視圖組成的傳統的3D多視點表示的局限 性：質地加上深度。這種表示法是有問題的，因為每個像素 只被允許採取只有一個深度值，從而有效地排除的像素的可 能性是部分部分的前景和背景。然而，眾所周知的是存在一 種技術叫做圖像摳圖廣泛應用於電影製作和圖像/視頻編輯分 解圖像到前台，後台及相應的α磨砂處理，擁有多少像素是一 部分一部分的前景和背景。由於沒有認識到像素的存在可以 部分部分前景和背景，傳統的雙組分/視圖表達變成一種阻礙 有效的3D處理。 在這個項目中，我們建議採用圖像摳圖工具，3D多視角的代表 性，使每個視圖可以分解為五個部分：前台質感，深度的前景， 背景紋理，深度的背景和阿爾法磨砂。這種突破性的五個組件/ 視圖表示能夠正確反映多的像素可以部分部分的前景和背景。 可能它可以使我們以更高的精度進行更為複雜和強大的3D運 算。我們提出了調查與此相關的新穎的五組分/視圖表示重要 的幾個問題，即，在五組分/視圖表示的生成，使用了阿爾法 遮片來使用縮小的深度圖經常錯誤時，視圖合成五組分/視圖 表示和五組分/視圖三維數據的編碼。有了這些工具開發的， 我們希望這個突破性的代表及相關的3D工具，可以激發新的 應用程序。

16200214.value: 智能無線設備的普及，以及隨之而來的新型無線應用的推廣，帶來了無線數據指數級的增長。於此同時，爲了滿足網絡容量需求，越來越多無線接入點被架設，這就帶來了關於無線網絡能耗以及其對於全球暖化影響的憂慮。所以更高的網絡能效已經被認為是下一代無線網絡的主要性能指標之一。全世界的無線網絡運營商都面臨著網絡擴容的成本效益問題，因為資本支出和運營支出都在飛速增長，然而利潤的增長卻趨於緩慢。所以，爲了能以經濟有效的方式增加網絡容量和能效，我們需要新的設計理念需要。 云型無線接入網（Cloud-RAN）是最近提出的一種革命性的未來無線網絡架構。在傳統的蜂窩網中，網絡的運算和處理性能被分散“凍結”在各個基站，而在Cloud-RAN中，這些資源被集中放置在一個資源池中，這樣就能夠有效的應付網絡的動態需求，同時可以提供例如自動化和彈性化這些新特性。在Cloud-RAN中，所有的基帶信號處理都集中到一個單一地點。傳統的性能強大的基站被低功耗低成本的遠端無線接入點（RRH）替代。這樣一種網絡結構能夠極大的降低資本支出和運營支出。它可以靈活的處理動態的網絡流量，還可以利用集中式的信號處理和資源分配極大的提高頻譜效率和能效。但這種新架構也帶來了新的挑戰。特別地，考慮了實際系統限制之後的Cloud-RAN的性能還沒有得到全面的分析。實際的網絡運行需要有效的協作波束成形技術和用戶調度算法，這些都需要先獲取通信信道信息。在這個項目里，我們的主要目標是解決Cloud-RAN中的關鍵性技術難題，從而滿足未來無線網絡對於網絡容量和網絡能效的要求。我們提出的研究任務包括開發能改進Cloud-RAN網絡能效的新方法；分析Cloud-RAN的性能增益；設計有效的獲取信道信息的方法；爲了應付實際系統中信道信息的不確定性，開發有效的隨機協作波束形成算法；開發有效的壓縮方法來應對傳輸鏈路上的有限容量。

16200214.label: Realisation of objectives
16200214.value: This project investigated a new architecture for radio access networks (RANs), i.e., the Cloud-RAN, which is expected to play a key role in the upcoming 5G networks. The Cloud-RAN provides a revolutionary way to densify radio access networks. In particular, all the baseband signal processing will be shifted to a central location, called the baseband unit (BBU) pool, and conventional powerful base stations can then be replaced by low-power and low-cost remote radio heads (RRHs). In this way, it enjoys significant cost advantages, and can reduce both the capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operational expenditure (OPEX) for mobile operators. With a large number of RRHs, the spatial reuse efficiency of the radio spectrum can be significantly improve, which subsequently boosts the network capacity. Furthermore, the architecture of Cloud-RANs enables centralized coordination and signal processing for efficient interference management and flexible network adaptation. Therefore, it is promising to resolve the main challenges for next-generation wireless networks, including higher energy efficiency and spectral efficiency, higher cost efficiency, scalable connectivity, and low latency. Nevertheless, this new RAN architecture also brings new design challenges. The research objectives of this project covered key research problems in Cloud-RANs, including developing efficient transmission schemes to improve the network performance, especially the network energy efficiency (Research Objective 1), proposing efficient channel state information (CSI) acquisition methods in Cloud-RANs (Objective 2), and developing computationally efficient large-scale coordinated beamforming algorithms for Cloud-RANs (Objective 3). Our investigation closely followed the stated research objectives. Moreover, considering the latest development in the field, we also investigated cache management for low-latency centralized processing in the BBU pool in Cloud-RANs, as well as resource allocation in mobile edge computing, a technique powered by the computing resources in Cloud-RANs. Following is the detailed description of the realization of the objectives. • First, we focused on designing green Cloud-RANs by reducing the network power consumption, i.e., to address Research Objective 1. We have developed a series of algorithms that can efficiently and adaptively switch off some RRHs, as well as the corresponding fronthaul links, for power saving. In this way, the network power consumption will be significant reduced, while the quality of service (QoS) of the active users are satisfactorily met. The main innovation in our methods is to induce a group sparsity pattern in the transmit beamformer, which helps to determine the set of active RRHs. We developed different ways for group sparsity inducing, invoking methods such as sparse optimization and random matrix theory. The proposed algorithms can also be applied to other design problems in Cloud-RANs, such as user admission, and fronthaul data assignment in cache-enabled wireless networks. • To address Research Objective 2, i.e., effective CSI acquisition, we investigated the possibility of only obtaining CSI of part of the interference links, while accounting for the estimation error in the available partial CSI. In this way, the radio resources spent on CSI acquisition, i.e., the training overhead, can be significantly reduced. To overcome the limited and uncertain CSI, we developed two different approaches to improve the network performance, including a stochastic coordinated beamforming algorithm and a robust coordinated beamforming algorithm. The results were promising, which showed that partial CSI, assisted by the proposed beamforming algorithms, only introduces marginal performance loss, while significantly reducing the CSI acquisition overhead. • The group sparse beamforming algorithms developed for Research Objective 1 focused on inducing the sparsity pattern, but their computation efficiency cannot meet the requirement of dense Cloud-RANs, which bring high-dimensional optimization problems. Thus we developed scalable large-scale convex optimization algorithms to improve the computation efficiency of coordinated beamforming in Cloud-RANs. We proposed a unified two-stage algorithmic framework that can handle general second-order cone programming problems, for which the coordinated beamforming problem is a special case. It includes a new problem transformation stage based on the matrix stuffing technique, and a solving stage that relies on computationally efficient first-order optimization algorithms. Armed with this new framework, we were able to simulate the performance of a Cloud-RAN with up to 150 RRHs and 150 users, while the conventional method struggles at 50. • To improve the efficiency of centralized processing at the BBU pool, which is itself a distributed computing environment, we investigated cache management for in-memory processing with distributed computing servers. In-memory data processing speeds up computation as the processed data is pre-stored (or cached) in the main memory, which is much faster to access than the disk. A few key problems for cache management were investigated. We developed a new dependency-aware cache management policy, which outperforms conventional ones, such as the popular least recently used (LRU) policy. We also developed a new mechanism for cache sharing among different computing tasks, with isolation guarantee and high efficiency. Furthermore, we also investigated load balancing at different servers, and proposed a new method by selectively partitioning data, which saves cache space compared with repetition based method, and avoids encoding/decoding complexity compared with erasure coding based methods. • Considering the recent development in wireless communications and networking, we also investigated an important technique enabled by the architecture of Cloud-RANs, namely Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). MEC deploys computing servers at the edge of the network, which can leverage the computing resources in the BBU pool in Cloud-RANs. In this way, mobile users can offload their computation-intensive applications to the proximate edge servers, and obtain the results with ultra-low latency, which is critical for emerging mobile applications such as autonomous driving, tactile Internet, and Internet of Things. We performed pioneer studies on this topic and investigated key design problems, including dynamic computation offloading, and joint radio and computation resource allocation. These studies have attracted lots of attention, and inspired many follow-up works. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project (Research Objectives 1 to 3), we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area (Research Objective 4). Specifically, as a result of this project, two PhD students (Yuanming Shi and Yuyi Mao) and one MPhil student (Xinyi Zhang) have been trained and graduated. In addition, with fruitful research outcomes, we were able to publish 11 journal papers, as well as 9 conference papers in IEEE flagship conferences. In particular, one journal paper [journal paper #3] received The 2016 IEEE Signal Processing Society Young Author Best Paper Award.

16200214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200214.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are summarized as follows. As for references, [C1] and [J1] represent conference paper #1 and journal paper #1 in Part C, respectively. • Effective Group Sparse Beamforming Algorithms for Green Cloud-RANs: In [J2, J3], we developed efficient large-scale optimization algorithms to meet the real-time execution requirement in wireless communications. In [J5], we considered the user admission problem in Cloud-RANs, which was solved in the same sparsity based framework as group sparse beamforming. The technique was further extended to cache-enabled wireless networks in [J8]. In [J10, C1], random matrix theory was applied to enhance the sparsity inducing capability, and reduce the complexity in selecting the active remote radio heads (RRHs) in Cloud-RANs for network power minimization. A general framework for sparse and low-rank optimization for dense networks was presented in [J11]. • Group Sparse Beamforming with Partial and Uncertain CSI: One main limiting factor in Cloud-RANs is the enormous channel state information (CSI) that is needed for the centralized signal processing. In practice, due to the limited radio resources that can be used for channel estimation, we will not be able to obtain CSI of all the links. To account for the practical constraints in CSI, we developed group sparse beamforming for partial and uncertain CSI in [J4] and [J1], respectively. The results were promising, which showed that partial and uncertain CSI will only bring marginal performance loss. • Cache Management for Cloud Processing: Effective centralized signal processing in the baseband unit (BBU) pool is essential for interference management and resource allocation in Cloud-RANs. In [C6 – C9], we investigated cache management for in-memory data processing in the distributed computing environment in the BBU pool, which helps to achieve low-latency processing that is essential for wireless communications. • Mobile Edge Computing in Cloud-RANs: One of the recent trends in wireless communications is to equip computing resources at the radio access points to support low-latency mobile applications, called as mobile edge computing (MEC). In Cloud-RANs, the BBU pool typically has abundant computing power, which can be used to support MEC. In [J6, J7, J9, C2, C3, C4, C5], we investigated key research problems in MEC, including computation offloading and resource allocation. Our results demonstrated that it is critical to take dynamics in channel states and task arrivals into consideration, and the importance of the joint allocation of computation and radio resource among multiple mobile users was also shown.

16200214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200214.value: This project has produced promising results on the centralized radio access network architecture, namely Cloud-RANs. The Cloud-RAN architecture will play a key role in the upcoming 5G network. It can significantly improve the spectral efficiency and energy efficiency, and also enable other communication technologies, such as wireless edge caching and mobile edge computing. This is a fascinating area, and there are many interesting directions to explore. One important further development will be to test the algorithms proposed in this project in real systems. Computation efficiency of these algorithms will need to be further improved, for which machine learning based methods are promising. Furthermore, the acquisition of high-dimensional channel state information requires further efforts, especially to consider it jointly with the beamforming algorithm design. The investigation on mobile edge computing in this project demonstrated the potential of such computing platforms for emerging wireless applications, such as connected vehicle, UAVs, and Internet of Things. This young research topic will require more investigation. On one hand, new transmission and coding schemes will be needed to ensure low-latency computation task offloading. On the other hand, coordination among multiple edge servers will be needed to improve the computation efficiency while serving many mobile users.

16200214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200214.value: The mobile data traffic keeps increasing at an exponential rate, which calls for a substantial boost in the wireless network capacity. Network densification, i.e., to deploy more radio access points, is an effective way to increase the network capacity without additional spectrum, as it significantly increases the spatial reuse efficiency of the same spectrum. However, the performance of dense wireless networks is limited by co-channel interference, and thus effective interference management plays a vital role. The Cloud Radio Access Network (Cloud-RAN) is a cost-effective network architecture with the capability of centralized signal processing, which can effectively manage interference. Thus, it has been regarded as a key technology for the upcoming 5G network. This project investigated key research problems in Cloud-RANs. In particular, effective coordinated beamforming algorithms have been developed, which help to improve both the spectral efficiency and energy efficiency of Cloud-RANs. Cache management for centralized processing at the Cloud center has also been investigated. Furthermore, a new technique enabled by Cloud-RANs, namely mobile edge computing, was also studied. Overall, this project has developed a few key techniques for designing and optimizing Cloud-RANs, and the developed methodologies will also be valuable for other types of wireless networks.

16200514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200514.value: Despite the fact that many advanced control schemes have been developed, how to effectively control a nonlinear system with satisfactory performance with respect to uncertainties and disturbance is still an open problem. All the existing control schemes originate from the feedback control of the linear system. Hence, stability analysis of the closed-loop system must be carried out based on theoretical analysis. However, the pre-designed controller needs to be fine-tuned in a real application because reality is different from theory. There is no guarantee that good performance can be obtained in practice. In addition, the tuning process is tedious and time consuming. In this research, a new method of control design is proposed to deal with a class of nonlinear mechanical systems with uncertainties. Unlike the current control theory, the proposed feedback control is designed to realize controllability. In other words, the stability of the closed-loop system is not the concern in the proposed research. This is because the closed-loop system will be able to reach its desired states within a finite time from any initial conditions of the states. Consider that most of the physical process and operation to be carried out by a feedback system only can last for a finite time, the controllability more precise defines the requirement of the task. It is shown that to achieve controllability one needs to solve a set of algebraic equations to meet the constraints given by the initial and final states. The problem of control design becomes the solution of the possible function of the states which must be satisfying the initial and final boundary conditions within the given time. The design process consists of two parts, the kinematic part and dynamics part. The resultant control input is a nonlinear function of the current state and final state. However, there is no feedback-gain that needs to be tuned in the proposed controller. The control input is calculated on-line. The preliminary analysis is carried out on a LTI system. The numerical simulations confirm the advantages of the proposed control scheme over the conventional schemes in the control tasks such as tracking, stabilization and disturbance attenuation. However, further investigations need to be conducted in order to deal with nonlinear mechanical systems with uncertainties and time-delay. Should the further theoretical analysis and experimental verification on multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems confirm the idea proposed in this research, it will have a profound impact on controller design and implementation. 如今已有很多先进的控制理论、方法，但在非线性系统的控制方面，尤其是在系统参数未知及噪声干扰的条件下，如何实现系统的最优控制仍然是一道难题。现有非线性控制理论大多是建立在线性系统理论的基础上，因此，仍然需要分析闭环系统的稳定性。然而，由于实际情况与理论假设不尽相同，预先设计的控制器需要在线调节后才能执行实际的控制任务。在这样的情况下，控制器的性能并不能可靠保证。 本研究针对系统参数未知的非线性机械系统提出了一种新的控制器设计方法。与传统理论的区别是，本研究的控制器设计是从系统的可控性、可达性出发，突出闭环系统可以在有限时间内，从初始状态达到终止状态的特点。这种思想符合实际物理过程都需在有限时间内完成的客观要求，从而使得从可控性、可达性出发设计的控制器更精确的定义了控制任务，进而还可将非线性系统的微分方程求解转化成代数方程的求解。控制器设计变成在有限时间内寻找可以从初始状态到达终止状态的可行方案。设计过程包含两部分：运动学和动力学。本文在线性非时变系统上对上述的新控制器进行了初步研究，数值仿真结果证明新控制器优于传统控制器。但是，对于非线性、参数未知系统需要更进一步的分析。此方案若能在多输入多输出系统中进行更进一步的理论分析和实践验证，那将对控制器设计和实施产生深远影响

16200514.label: Realisation of objectives
16200514.value: The objectives listed in the original application keep the same. However, the terminology reachability instead of controllability is used to design controller. Both of these two terminologies describes the desired state can be achieved from any other initial state within a finite time period by a permissible control input. The difference lies in that controllability needs a coordinate transformation to transform the desired state to zero state for further analysis. Considering the conciseness, reachability is selected as design principle since coordinate transformation is not necessary. For the objective one, a unified theoretical framework to realize reachability in a class of nonlinear systems governed by Lagrange equation has been established. Within this new framework, the kinematic design and the dynamic design are carried out separately in order to obtain the value of controller to achieve reachability. A new algorithm is developed to estimate the unknowns in the system, and an on-line updated mechanism is created to compensate the uncertainties on-line. A group of critical problems in the field of controller design can be solved in this new framework, which includes the coupling dynamics, matched or mismatched disturbances, parameters unknown, internal dynamics, and non-minimum phase. The developed framework can provide excellent performance in terms of high accuracy and low energy-consumption. Furthermore, the control scheme is automatically calculated without any manually tuning of gains. For the objective two, the major challenge is how to maintain the control accuracy when the system exists the time-delay effects. The study has two layers: one is to reduce the time-delay introduced by human being, e.g. the direct time derivative to estimate the higher-order derivatives of the state; the other one tries to strictly comply the time consumption in physical system to avoid the improper energy input, e.g. the energy coupling in elastic connection. For the first layer, a new observer is proposed to give the instantaneous estimation based on integral with the kinematic constraints among the states. The convergence of the proposed observer has been given. The realization of the second layer is synthesizing the highest-order derivatives in two sides of an elastic connection to make the input energy fully utilized to complete the task. For the objective three, a screw-driven and belt-driven platform are built up to reflect the aforementioned problems. In order to reduce the random noise with low frequency distribution, a linear regression filter is proposed. The efficiency of the proposed controller, proposed observer, and the proposed filter are verified in two typical control tasks: regulation and tracking. The experiments prove that the proposed control strategy can be realized in real-time control, and the proposed control strategy outperforms the conventional controller based on stability and finite-time stability in terms of accuracy, energy-consumption, and degree of automation level. The proposed strategy can be automatically adaptive to different tasks with various uncertainties. And there are not any gains needed to be tuned manually.

16200514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200514.value: Reachability is more suitable than stability to describe a physical task since it defines a task that can be completed within a finite time period. It is because of this finite time condition. A new type of kinematic constraints, call triple constraints, is discovered. Further, the highest-order derivatives is the kernel to guarantee the triple constraints in kinematic domain. Then a proper external input is described as the one who can generate the value of the highest-order derivative in the dynamic domain. As a result, the differential equation is naturally transformed to be a zero-order algebraic equation due to the triple constraints, and this algebraic equation reflects a linear relation between the external input and the highest-order derivatives. Then the developed controller contains kinematic and dynamic step. This breakthrough indicates that the controller for a finite time task can be calculated by solving an algebraic equation with certain accuracy, which is different from designing a stable structure as conventional controller does. In order to accurately solving the algebraic equation in the presence of uncertainties, two estimators are developed to estimate the unknown parameters and uncertainties, and the estimation errors are compensated by an updating mechanism. Details can refer to Journal paper No. 2. To realize the developed controller in the output control, a new observer is established to reconstruct the value of instantaneous full states from the partial measured states. The drifting issues in normal integration is obviously inhibited in the proposed integration observer. In the meantime, the proposed integration observer has the ability to inhibit measurement noise. Details can refer to Journal paper No. 1. The developed controller can also be extended to solve a group of control problems, e.g. matched or mismatched disturbances, systems with flexible components, the coupling dynamics, and internal dynamics. Details can refer to Journal paper No. 3 and 4. In all, this new framework achieves a better performance in terms of higher accuracy, lower energy-consumption, and higher degree of automation compared with the conventional controllers.

16200514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200514.value: The proposed course of action has three layers. The first layer is applying the developed controller based on reachability to other nonlinear systems governed by Lagrange equation, like electronic system, magnetic systems, and so on, for achieving accurate performance with low energy-consumption and high degree of automation level. The second layer is the promotion of the proposed controller to real industrial applications to achieve accurate performance with low energy-consumption and high degree of automation level. The third layer is the further theoretical exploring on reachability based controller design. Several bold guess can be drawn after the completion of the project: if a nonlinear system can be rewritten as a quasi-linear form in between the external input and the highest-order time derivatives, this nonlinear system is controllable and the developed reachability based controller can be applied on it; the solution space provided by the proposed controller is different and more widely than conventional controller design, then there will be a great chance that the developed controller can cover more types of physical system than that can be controlled by conventional controllers. Rigorous proof and verification for these propositions can be found in the near future.

16200514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200514.value: A physical system is generally governed by a nonlinear differential equation. However, a control task asks for finding a suitable input to drive the system to reach a desired state with a finite time, which is different from system analysis. Therefore, mathematic tools in the realm of differential equation may not be tailored for this task. This research provides a unified theoretical framework to design controller based on reachability instead of the conventional controller designed on stability. This new framework contains a two-step on-line updated strategy to calculate control value, two new observers to estimate the full states from the partial measured state, and a linear regression filter to inhibit the propagation of the low frequency noise. Adopting this new framework in real applications, a better performance can be achieved in terms of higher accuracy, lower energy-consumption, and higher degree of automation compared with the conventional controllers. The breakthrough lies in that the assumptions drawn by conventional controllers are released, e.g. the structure and boundary of uncertainty are not necessary to be known, the tedious and less instructional gains-tuning is overcame. Therefore, the proposed theoretical framework fills the gap between the conventional control theory and the industrial applications.

16200614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200614.value: Asian options, whose payoffs depend on the average of the underlying asset prices over a pre-specified time period, are among the most important path-dependent options in the financial markets. Due to the "average" structure, Asian options and Asian-type derivatives have wide applications in equity, interest rate, currency, energy, and commodity, and are traded actively in the equity derivatives markets, the commodity markets, and the foreign exchange markets. The associated pricing problem has attracted much attention from both practitioners and researchers throughout the world, including Hong Kong - the fifth largest foreign exchange market in the world. However, analytical pricing of Asian options, in particular discrete Asian options, is very challenging primarily because the distributions of average prices may have no analytical solutions. Indeed, only a few published studies are focused on analytical pricing or analytical approximations, and most of them deal with only continuous Asian options under very special models, e.g., the Black-Scholes model and jump diffusion models with exponential-type jumps. In this project, we propose a unified analytical approximation approach to pricing both continuous and discrete Asian options under general one- or two-dimensional time-homogeneous Markov process models, which nest most popular option pricing models, including various exponential Levy models, the CEV model, regime switching models, and stochastic volatility models. Specifically, this unified approach combines functional equation, transform inversion, and Markov approximation. (1) We will express the double Laplace transform (resp. Z-Laplace transform) of the continuous (resp. discrete) Asian option price with respect to maturity (resp. number of monitoring dates) and transformed strike in terms of the double Laplace transform (resp. Z-Laplace transform) of the continuous (resp. discrete) average price. (2) We propose investigating two functional equations related to continuous and discrete Asian options, respectively, and plan to show that their bounded solutions, if exist, must be unique and are exactly equal to the double Laplace transform of the continuous average price and the Z-Laplace transform of the discrete average price, respectively. In the special case, i.e., for continuous time Markov chains (CTMCs), we expect to solve these two functional equations explicitly, thus obtaining analytical pricing formulas in terms of double transform inversion under CTMCs. (3) We shall develop accurate and efficient pricing algorithms for both continuous and discrete Asian options under a general Markov process by first constructing a CTMC sufficiently close to the underlying model and then inverting the closed-form double transforms of Asian option prices under the approximate CTMC. 亚式期权是金融市场上最流行的依赖路径期权之一，它的收益依赖于相关资产价格在一段预先确定的时间内的平均值。这种"平均"收益结构使得亚式期权以及亚式衍生品广泛应用于股票，利率，货币，能源，和商品市场。它们在股票，能源及外汇市场上交易活跃。相关的定价问题已经吸引了全世界范围内的从业者和研究人员的关注，也包括世界第五大外汇市场 -- 香港。 然而，亚式期权的解析定价，尤其是离散亚式期权的解析定价非常困难，这主要是因为相关资产的平均价格的概率分布一般没有解析解。其实在已经发表的研究中只有很少一部分是关于解析定价或解析逼近的，而且其中大部分只考虑一些非常特殊模型下的连续亚式期权的定价，比如布莱克-斯科尔斯模型和带指数跳跃的跳跃扩散模型。 在这个研究项目里，我们对于一般的一维和二维时齐马氏过程下连续与离散亚式期权的定价提出了一个统一的解析逼近方法。这类模型包含很多很流行的期权定价模型，比如各种莱维模型，CEV模型，状态转换模型和随机波动模型。 具体来说，这种统一方法把泛函方程，逆变换和马氏过程逼近结合在一起。(1) 我们将用连续(分别地，离散)平均价格关于到期日(分别地，观测日期的数量)和变换后的执行价格的二重拉普拉斯变换(分别地，Z-拉普拉斯变换)来表示相应的连续(分别地，离散)亚式期权价格的二重拉普拉斯变换(分别地，Z-拉普拉斯变换)。(2) 我们准备研究和连续与离散亚式期权分别相关的两个泛函方程。我们计划证明他们的有界解，如果存在的话，一定是唯一的，并且分别等于连续平均价格的二重拉普拉斯变换和离散平均价格的Z-拉普拉斯变换。在连续时间马氏链这种特殊情形下，我们希望能把这两个泛函方程清晰地解出来，从而得到连续时间马氏链下连续与离散亚式期权的包含二重逆变换的解析定价公式。(3) 我们准备对于一般马氏过程下连续与离散亚式期权设计准确快速的定价算法。首先对于目标模型构造一个足够接近的连续时间马氏链。然后对这个逼近的连续时间马氏链下连续与离散亚式期权价格的准确形式的二重变换做逆变换来求出相应的亚式期权价格。

16200614.label: Realisation of objectives
16200614.value: In this project, we have achieved the project objectives by developing a unified analytical approximation approach to pricing both continuous and discrete Asian options under Markov process models. More specifically, for each of the two types of Asian options, i.e., continuous Asian options and discrete Asian options, we have derived the double transform of the Asian option price in terms of the unique bounded solution to a related functional equation by showing that the double transform of the integral or the sum of the underlying asset prices is the unique bounded solution to the corresponding functional equation, and have also obtained the analytical solution to the functional equation in the special case of continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). Based on these results, we have succeeded in deriving analytical approximations to both continuous and discrete Asian option prices by first constructing a CTMC that well approximates the target Markov process model and then obtaining double transform based analytical solutions to both continuous and discrete Asian option prices under the approximate CTMC. Then a pricing method based on CTMC approximation and double transform inversion has been developed to implement the analytical approximation pricing formulas. Numerical results indicate that our pricing method is accurate and efficient under many popular Markov process models. Moreover, we have further improved this analytical approximation pricing method by deriving single transform based analytical solutions to both continuous and discrete Asian option prices under CTMCs. To make the pricing method more accurate and efficient, we have also obtained computable error bounds for both the discretization errors and the truncation errors involved in the inversion of these single Laplace transforms under CTMCs by analyzing these two types of errors quantitatively and establishing a comparison inequality between European and Asian option prices, and these computable error bounds are useful for providing benchmark prices thanks to the error control. Some extensions about pricing of Asian options with floating strikes and computations of Asian options sensitivities have also been studied.

16200614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200614.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are detailed as follows. We have derived analytical approximations in terms of double transforms to both continuous and discrete Asian option prices under Markov process models. This is made possible mainly because we have shown that the double transforms of the integral and the sum of the underlying asset prices are the unique bounded solutions to two related functional equations and have also obtained the analytical solutions to these two functional equations in the special case of continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). An accurate and efficient pricing method has been developed to implement the analytical approximation pricing formulas. Moreover, we have further improved this analytical approximation pricing method by simplifying the double transform based analytical pricing formulas for both continuous and discrete Asian options under CTMCs to single transform based analytical pricing formulas. In addition, we have also derived computable error bounds for both the discretization errors and the truncation errors involved in the inversion of these single Laplace transforms under CTMCs, and the resulting pricing method with computable error bounds is useful for providing benchmark prices due to the error control.

16200614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200614.value: In this project, we have concentrated on analytical approximations to continuous and discrete Asian option prices under Markov process models. Potential future research problems might include the study of analytical approximations to continuous and discrete Asian option prices under Markov process models with default risk. This problem is more difficult due to the incorporation of default risk into the complicated model structure. A potential approach might be still to apply the CTMC approximation and transform inversion method by investigating the transforms of the integral and the sum of the more complicated defaultable asset prices.

16200614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200614.value: Option pricing is not only theoretically important but also practically significant in finance. Asian options are among the most popular path-dependent options actively traded in various financial markets. However, analytical pricing or analytical approximation of either continuous or discrete Asian options under general Markov process models is very challenging. In this project, we have developed a unified analytical approximation approach to pricing both continuous and discrete Asian options under general Markov process models. Numerical results indicate that our pricing methods are accurate and efficient. Theoretically, to the best of our knowledge, we provide one of the first approaches to deriving analytical approximations to both continuous and discrete Asian option prices under Markov process models. In practice, Asian options can help overcome some risk management difficulties encountered by firms, dealers and buyers in the financial markets due to their payoff structures. Our research provides accurate and efficient methods for pricing both continuous and discrete Asian options under Markov process models and hence is of importance for their applications in various financial markets.

16200714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200714.value: The 21st century will be the age of Asian skyscrapers. The past two decades have witnessed a major shift in tall buildings from west to east, particularly in Asia Pacific regions that include Hong Kong and mainland China. Advances to ever-taller high-rise buildings are often accompanied by more irregular geometric shapes, which increase the building’s vulnerability under wind excitations. Structurally irregular buildings with unsymmetric distribution of mass and stiffness may accentuate torsional effects, which can lead to increased stresses and amplify swaying motions at the perimeter of the building. The wind-induced torsional response of buildings is considered to be one of the more difficult issues from a structural design point of view, not only because of its complicated nature but also because the current codes of practice do not provide adequate guidance. For modern tall buildings of complex irregular shapes, the wind-induced torsional response is important for the design in terms of both serviceability and survivability. Although today’s wind tunnel testing provides the best practice for determining aerodynamic wind loading on complex buildings, this experimental approach offers no analytical methods for structural engineers to best minimize dynamic torsional loads and response of buildings. While torsion in buildings of complex shapes may not be entirely eliminated since engineers can hardly change the building shape which is dictated by the architect, the effects of torsion can be more effectively minimized by altering the dynamic properties of the building via computational structural optimization techniques. The ultimate objective of this project is to create an innovative analytical optimization methodology to assess combined lateral and torsional design wind load cases and to minimize the torsional wind load effects on high-rise buildings with complex structural forms. Research will be uniquely addressed to improve current aerodynamic wind tunnel load analysis routines and reduce dynamic torsional loads by computational structural topology optimization, thus helping to enhance design quality and cost efficiency of the new generation of tall buildings. Upon successful completion of the project, the immediate outcome of this research will be a computer system that is directly applicable to accurate analysis and updating of combined wind-induced loads while achieving integrated design optimization for minimization of torsional wind effects on modern high-rise buildings.

16200714.label: Realisation of objectives
16200714.value: The realization of the research objectives has been achieved in the following hierarchical sub-tasks of investigations. 1. Development of an Optimization Framework for Determining Design Envelope as a Representation of Combined Critical Wind Load Cases Accurate assessment of the design wind load combinations for structural design tall buildings on the basis of wind tunnel tests is an extremely important and complicated issue. Recent investigations indicate that the traditional experimental determination of wind load combinations for tall buildings, especially those with irregular shapes, relies partly on subjective judgments and lacks a systematic and reliable method of evaluating critical load cases. A novel computer based optimization approach has been investigated to determine the peak resultant load cases of wind excited tall buildings with three dimensional correlated wind loads measured in wind tunnel tests. A multivariate normal distribution is assumed for random wind-induced structural load components in each incident wind direction. The equivalence surface of probability can then be interpreted as an ellipsoid, corresponding to a certain statistical threshold, and the peak factor is utilized to determine the size of the ellipsoid. An optimization-based framework is developed in the search for a convex hull that serves as a design envelope. The individual combined load cases can be expressed in terms of the coordinates of the vertices of the optimized polyhedron. The Pareto front is also integrated in this new method to enable the prediction of the appropriate number of load cases. 2. Development of an analytical method for evaluating lateral-torsional coupling and topology optimization algorithm for minimizing peak torque of tall irregular buildings subject to wind loads Once the aerodynamic wind load spectra are experimentally derived from wind tunnel tests and the critical design load envelope can be systematically and accurately established using the optimization-based framework developed, the next important research task in this project is to investigate an effective method to evaluate the coupled lateral-torsional response and to minimize the torsional wind load effects on high-rise buildings with complex structural forms. An attempt has been made to develop an innovative computer-based topology optimization methodology that is capable of optimizing the layout of structural elements in order to maximize torsional stiffness while minimizing floor eccentricities, as well as lateral-torsional coupling by separating the translational and torsional frequencies. Hybrid genetic algorithms (HGAs) resulting from the incorporation of local search methods into genetic algorithms have been investigated. The possibility of combining a GA and a local search Optimality Criteria (OC) method has been explored to determine an effective form of hybridization for the structural topology design of tall irregular building structures. The GA framework first starts with a randomly generated initial population and then produces new offspring designs with random changes in both the topology and the element sizing by crossover and mutation. Unlike the genetic evolution operator, the OC operator is a deterministic, gradient-based algorithm which improves the element sizing design with predefined topology subject to the specified structural design performance constraints. The OC technique is an efficient local search method which can resize the elements rapidly through the use of a recursive algorithm and yield a result which satisfies the necessary optimality conditions. The balance between global exploration of the topology by the GA and local element optimisation by the OC is crucial to achieving a better quality design whilst avoiding premature convergence. Using the innovative structural topology optimization, not only can the optimal deposition of structural element stiffness be sought to improve the torsional stiffness of a building, but also the equivalent static wind-induced torques (incorporating both the aerodynamic buffeting loads and the resonance dynamic loads) can be subsequently reduced by the increase in the torsional frequencies of the building. In order to realize the benefit of wind-induced load reduction, it is necessary to instantaneously update the wind-induced structural loads during the optimal design synthesis process. Once the aerodynamic wind load spectra are experimentally derived from wind tunnel tests, they can be explicitly expressed in the form of an algebraic function of the modal frequency using regression analysis. Such algebraic functions can then be used to directly update the prediction of wind-induced structural loads on the building for any instantaneous change in the dynamic properties of the building during the torsional stiffness optimization process. With the aid of piece-wise regression analysis, the power spectral density function of modal torsional wind forces for a tall building can be inversely related to the modal frequency of the building and is explicitly expressed as an algebraic function in terms of the modal frequency. 3. Practical Design Verification Much effort has been made to verify the practical applications of the developed computer-based topology optimization technique to stiffen the torsional resistance of buildings as well as the systematic framework for obtaining wind tunnel derived load combinations for real-life complex high-rise buildings. A series of wind tunnel tests for reinforced concrete residential buildings with T-shape, L-shape and irregular plan forms have been conducted to obtain aerodynamic wind loads acting on the surfaces of buildings. Some initial success of the evolutionary hybrid OC-GA method has been demonstrated in its applications to the structural topology optimization and wind-load determination system of tall irregular residential buildings. Results have been analyzed for comparison with those derived from the current practice and significant improvements have been achieved.

16200714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200714.value: Modern tall buildings are wind sensitive structures. The accurate determination of wind loads on tall buildings is essential to efficient and safe design. One major outcome of this research is a novel optimization-based technique for determining wind tunnel derived load cases for structural design of wind sensitive tall buildings. Results on a 30-story residential building have shown that this technique provides a powerful tool for the assessment of extreme wind load effects. Not only is the technique capable of the systematic determination of critical wind load combinations without any subjective judgment, it also provides more accurate prediction of wind load cases while maintaining the conservativeness derived from statistical analysis. Another major outcome of this research is the evolutionary hybrid genetic algorithm that is capable of simultaneously searching optimal structural topology and element sizes of wind sensitive modern tall buildings with irregular planforms. The hybrid method involves exploring topologies using a GA, then refining the element sizes using a local search OC algorithm. Several practical building examples showed that the hybrid OC–GA method can generate superior designs to pure GA while exhibiting rapid and smooth convergence. The hybrid OC–GA method promises to become a useful tool for optimizing both structural form and element size in large-scale practical building structures. Three MPhil students (Gang AN, Danqi HE and Xuemeng ZHU) and one post-doc fellow (Dr. Honglei BAI) have been appointed to work on this project. This research project has resulted in three MPhil theses, three conference papers and five top journal publications.

16200714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200714.value: Research conducted to date on structural topology optimization has been mainly focused on structural cost and performance strategies of tall buildings. In view of the increasing concern on global warming, the current trend towards sustainable development has led to new challenges for the design of high-rise buildings. It is important to continue the research by addressing multidisciplinary design optimization of tall green buildings taking into due consideration of resource and energy consumption with minimum environmental impacts. To support multidisciplinary performance-oriented modelling for sustainable building design, one must both model geometric interdependences in a parametric way and include non-geometric physical, environmental, and economic design reasoning. For sustainable design, one must also provide a holistic model because of the relevant criteria crossing disciplinary boarders. Multidisciplinary optimization requires a mathematical or algorithmic formal definition of the interdisciplinary interdependencies. Multidisciplinary interdependencies in the design object caused by the demand for energy efficiency and sustainability and the variety of possible solution configurations within these dependencies turn building design into a complex task.

16200714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200714.value: Advances to ever-taller high-rise buildings are often accompanied by more irregular geometric shapes, which increase the building’s vulnerability under wind excitations. Structurally irregular buildings with unsymmetric distribution of mass and stiffness may accentuate torsional effects, which can lead to increased stresses and amplify swaying motions at the perimeter of the building. The ultimate objective of this project is to create an innovative analytical optimization methodology to assess combined lateral and torsional design wind load cases and to minimize the torsional wind load effects on high-rise buildings with complex structural forms. Research has been uniquely addressed to improve current aerodynamic wind tunnel load analysis routines and reduce dynamic torsional loads by computational structural topology optimization, thus helping to enhance design quality and cost efficiency of the new generation of tall buildings. The immediate outcome of this research is a computer system that is directly applicable to accurate analysis and updating of combined wind-induced loads while achieving integrated design optimization for minimization of torsional wind effects on modern high-rise buildings.
