16201114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201114.value: Adsorption cooling systems can be an energy efficient strategy for smart green building operation since they need neither CFCs nor HCFCs and can be integrated with waste heat from industrial processes, boilers in hospitals and hotels, commercial kitchens, or solar panels, etc., thus greatly reducing the dependence on fossil fuels. Unfortunately, adsorption cooling systems have not been widely commercialized due to their large size and low cooling efficiency (i.e. low coefficient of performance (COP) and low specific cooling power (SCP)). A lot of previous research activities have been on the development of new adsorbents to enhance the performance. Indeed, smart design of the evaporator and careful choice of working fluid can be another research direction to substantially enhance the efficiency. In this study, a capillary-assisted evaporator using nanofluid as an adsorbate is proposed. Nanofluids created by suspending nanoparticles in base fluids (i.e. water) have remarkably higher thermal conductivity than existing heat transfer fluids. Some preliminary results in our previous work show that the heat transfer coefficient of the evaporator after using capillary-action technology can increase by about 60%, and it is also found that nanofluids can contribute to about 10% improvement in both the COP and SCP. It is believed that using a proper nanofluid as the adsorbate in a capillary-assisted evaporator can substantially improve the cooling performance of an adsorption cooling system. However, a number of academic challenges need to be addressed. This project will first investigate and characterize the thermal-physical properties of different nanofluids so that suitable adsorbates could be developed. Next, a mathematical model describing the thermofluid behavior of nanofluids in micro-grooves will be developed. This novel model will focus on the concentration distributions of nanoparticles in the nanofluids and their thermofluid characteristics (i.e. deposition due to adhesion, convection due to evaporation, settling due to gravity), and it will also be verified by a series of experiments. Based on the model, an enhanced capillary-assisted evaporator with the new physics of nanofluid flowing in the micro-grooves will be designed, built and tested experimentally. Finally, the developed evaporator will be integrated into an adsorption cooling system to analyze the system cooling performance. This research will reveal the impact of nanoparticle concentration in a micro-channel flow and the related heat transfer characteristics. The findings will not only enhance the thermal-physical knowledge of nanofluids in microfluidic science, but also steer new development of adsorption cooling system applications. 眾所周知，建築物能源消費的主要來源是製冷系統。而吸附式製冷系統是一個很好的替代品，它可以用來取代傳統的壓縮式製冷系統。這是因為吸附式製冷系統不需要壓縮機，而且還可以利用太陽能和廢能，能有效利用能源，降低能耗。除此之外，吸附式製冷系統採用的是一般十分普遍的吸附質(製冷劑)，例如：水和甲醇等天然物質，其特徵是不會造成臭氧層破壞和帶來溫室效應。所以，吸附式製冷系統被譽為下一代既環保又具有節能潛力的製冷系統。然而，傳統的壓縮式製冷系統仍然在大多數應用中佔主導地位，這是因為吸附式製冷系統具有較低的性能係數和製冷功率，導致一個龐大的製冷系統。所以，吸附式製冷系統很難被廣泛的運用。提高吸附質的導熱係數或汽化潛熱和同時改善蒸發器的設計毫無疑問地是可以大大改進吸附式製冷系統的冷卻性能和能源效率。至今，許多研究專注於開發新的吸附劑，其中新開發的吸附劑具有更大的吸附能力和吸附速率。但是，並不是很多的研究是關於吸附質和蒸發器的設計。在這項研究中，一種新型的蒸發器被建議出來。其包括運用納米液體作為吸附質和同時利用毛細管輔助增加其吸附質的蒸發表面積。納米液體是懸浮著一定份量納米顆粒的液體。因為納米液體的導熱係數比普通水高，所以納米液體一度被視為下一代的傳熱液體。也意味著納米液體有很好的潛質成為新一代的吸附質運用在吸附式製冷系統中。根據一些初步的研究結果顯示，在毛細管的輔助下，蒸發器的傳熱係數增加了約百分之六十。除此之外，初步研究還發現了單單靠納米流體作為吸附質可以將吸附式製冷系統的性能係數和製冷功率同時提升約百分之十左右。所以，有理由相信用納米流體作為吸附質運用於毛細管輔助的蒸發器是可以大大提高吸附式製冷系統的冷卻性能。但是，還有一些研究上的難題需要解決。該研究項目將首先研究和鑑定不同的納米流體的熱物理性能，從而可以研發出適合運用於吸附式製冷系統中的吸附質。接下來，一種可以用來模擬納米流體在微槽的數學模型將會被研發。這種新穎的數學模型將重點研發集中在納米流體中的納米顆粒和其熱流體特性的濃度分佈（例如：由於納米流體粘合性的沉積問題，由蒸發過程引起的對流問題和由納米顆粒重力影響的沉降問題）。這種新穎的數學模型將會通過一系列的實驗來驗證。基於該數學模型，納米流體作為吸附質運用於毛細管輔助的蒸發器將被設計，製造和測試。最後，經測試後的蒸發器會被安裝到吸附式製冷系統中，接著就會分析整套系統的冷卻性能。本研究將揭示納米顆粒的濃度在微通道流動和相關的熱傳遞特性。研究結果不僅會提高納米流體的熱物理知識，還可以進一步發展吸附式製冷系統，從而可以被廣泛應用。

16201114.label: Realisation of objectives
16201114.value: All project objectives have been achieved. The thermal-physical properties of nanofluids have been investigated and characterized extensively. By adding Al2O3 and TiO2 nanoparticles to water, the enthalpy of evaporation decreased with an increase of nanoparticle concentration and the larger the nanoparticle size, the smaller the enthalpy of evaporation. Experimental results show that most of the nanofluids have lower saturated vapor pressure and evaporation rate than those of water, particularly with an increase of nanoparticle concentration, but a few nanofluids with lower volume concentrations show slightly larger values than those of water. Therefore, the evaporation rate of nanofluids as well as their saturated vapor pressure, can be increased or decreased, depending on their volume concentration and the type of nanofluid. A semi-analytical model for estimating the evaporation rate of water and nanofluids as a function of temperature, humidity and air velocity was developed. After comparing the modeling results with the experiment, the agreement between them is generally good. As the presence of nanofluid can affect the overall system response, a simulation model consisting of pressure variations and detailed compressible flow with flow resistance was developed, which other similar studies had not taken into consideration, thus a detailed simulation of operating sequences can be conducted. Based on the simulation results of a double-bed adsorption cooling system, the coefficient of performance (COP) of the adsorption cooling system was increased by 20% compared to the basic cycle by conducting heat recovery for 30 seconds. The specific cooling power (SCP) was also increased by 15% increase. The major advantage through conducting the mass recovery is in the SCP, whereby it was increased by 40%. Additionally, performing only the pre-heating and pre-cooling process can also bring some benefits to the system. Therefore, for adsorption cooling systems that cannot carry out the mass recovery and/or heat recovery cycles, performing pre-heating and pre-cooling process only is recommended. This not only can reduce the cost, but also simplify the control program of the systems. Moreover, mass recovery followed by pre-heating and pre-cooling cycle is highly preferred when the SCP is the optimization target, since the SCP was hugely increased by 41%. The effect of an externally micro-grooved surface on evaporation of aqueous nanofluids was studied and its potential application was discussed. In order to prepare a stable nanofluid, the duration time required for ultrasonication, which is a common technique in the preparation process of nanofluid, was firstly investigated. Next, experiments were conducted to investigate the effect of the micro-grooved surface on the evaporation rate of the nanofluids under different environmental conditions. Results show that the advantage of the enhanced thermal properties of nanofluids can only be manifested by the presence of micro-grooves. The use of a heat exchanger with nanofluids together with micro-grooves shows a better heat transfer performance than a heat exchanger without micro-grooves using water as the coolant. The enhancement is dependent on the vapor pressure and the largest improvement can be up to 44.6%. When a nanofluid is applied in the capillary-assisted evaporator, it is unavoidable that the nanoparticles will remain on the surface of the evaporator and form residue. Thus, both particle size and concentration on the residue pattern was investigated. A comprehensive study was made of the residue patterns of Al2O3 and TiO2 aqueous nanofluid droplets on different substrates (i.e. glass, stainless steel and Teflon). It was found that a ring-shaped pattern was formed at low concentrations and small particle sizes, while a uniform pattern was formed at high concentrations and large particle sizes for Al2O3 nanofluids. In addition, only ring-shaped residue patterns were observed for all concentrations of TiO2 nanofluids. In the case of different substrates, on a material with a high contact angle with water, it was difficult to form a ring-shaped pattern. The widths of the ring-shaped pattern were analyzed as well. The results showed that the width of the ring-shaped pattern was larger for small particles. The materials of substrate and nanoparticle also influenced the width. The nanofluids were also tested as an adsorbate in an adsorption cooling system, and the results show that using 0.01% TiO2 nanofluid as the adsorbate enhances the cooling performance by about 9%. In order to test the actual performance of the adsorption cooling system under different climate condition, a solar-powered double-bed adsorption cooling system has been built and tested in the Guangzhou climate. The effect of the pre-heating process on the cooling performance of the adsorption cooling system powered by solar energy has been experimentally investigated. A SCP of 52.2 W/kg and a COP of 0.20 were achieved under a 2-h pre-heating process. The average SCP and COP were improved by 26.1% and 33.3%, respectively, as compared to the case without conducting the pre-heating process. In addition, the influence of dead volume on the SCP and COP of the adsorption cooling system has also been investigated. Using various numbers of heat exchangers in the adsorber achieved different values of adsorber dead volume. The results show that a higher SCP value is obtained with a smaller dead volume. Finally, the cooling performance of the adsorption cooling system was also studied under various operating conditions and a maximum SCP and COP are 180.4 W/kg and 0.29, respectively. The system was later improved by using vehicle radiators as an adsorbent bed and 6 single-glazed flat plate solar collectors with the total area of 12 m2 were utilized to collect solar energy. A minimum area of solar collectors of 6 m2 was recommended for a 1–2 kW scale adsorption cooling system. A SCP of 208.2 W/kg of the adsorption cooling system and an energy efficiency ratio of 4.5 driven by solar energy were achieved with a maximum solar intensity of 880 W/m2.

16201114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201114.value: Aqueous nanofluids with 13 nm, 20 nm, and 80 nm Al2O3 nanoparticles and 21 nm sized TiO2 nanoparticles at the various concentrations were studied. A semi-analytical model for estimating the evaporation rate of water and nanofluids as a function of temperature, humidity and air velocity was developed. Furthermore, a numerical model consisting of pressure variations and detailed compressible flow with flow resistance was developed so that a double-bed adsorption cooling system can be simulated (Tso and Chao 2015, Tso et al. 2015, Chan et al. 2015). Simulation was conducted to investigate the effect of heat recovery, mass recovery, pre-heating and pre-cooling processes and their combinations on the system performance of a double-bed adsorption cooling system. The agreement between the experimental data and simulation result are good and these models can be used for future studies on investigating different operating scenarios for an adsorption cooling system with nanofluids as working fluids. Then the combined effect of nanofluid and micro-grooves were studied. Experiments were conducted to investigate the effect of the micro-grooved surface on the evaporation rate of the nanofluids under different environmental conditions. The use of a heat exchanger with nanofluids together with micro-grooves shows a better heat transfer performance than a heat exchanger without micro-grooves using water as the coolant. The largest improvement of 44.6% was found at 1.68 kPa vapor pressure when using 0.5 vol% Al2O3 nanofluid as the coolant (Fu et al. 2017). Al2O3 nanofluids (13 nm sized nanoparticles) and TiO2 nanofluids (21 nm sized nanoparticles) were utilized as the adsorbate for the cooling performance test in the adsorption cooling system. The results show that by using 0.01% TiO2 nanofluids as the adsorbate, both specific cooling power (SCP) and coefficient of performance (COP) were enhanced by about 9%. In order to test the actual performance of the adsorption cooling system under actual climate condition, field experiments have been conducted. A solar-powered double-bed adsorption cooling system has been built and tested in the Guangzhou climate (Zhu et al. 2017). Moreover, the cooling performance of the adsorption cooling system was also studied under various operating conditions and a maximum SCP of 180.4 W/kg and COP of 0.29 can be achieved. With a maximum solar intensity of 880 W/m2, the SCP of the adsorption cooling system can even go up to 208.2 W/kg with an energy efficiency ratio of 4.5 achieved (Chan et al. 2018, Zhu et al. 2018).

16201114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201114.value: Although the performance of adsorption cooling systems can be enhanced by the capillary-assisted and nanofluid based evaporator in the project, during the study, it was also found that nanoparticles from the nanofluid may deposit on the surface of the evaporator especially inside the micro-grooves. The residue patterns were found to be highly related to the nanofluid properties and substrate surface properties (Lee et al. 2017). Since the patterns may have further effect on the heat transfer and evaporative process, based on this useful fundamental knowledge obtained, further research efforts can be put on investigating the effect of surface treatment on the evaporator on heat transfer enhancement e.g. superhydrophilic surface. How the surface treatment affects the formation of residue and hence affects the heat transfer? Moreover, several studies show that hybrid nanofluids, in which two types or more of nanoparticles are dispersed in a base-fluid, exhibit better thermo-physical properties than single-particle nanofluids. Therefore, by using the models and experimental tools developed in this project, it is feasible and worth studying whether an adsorption cooling system’s performance could be further improved by adopting hybrid nanofluid, or not.

16201114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201114.value: Adsorption cooling systems can be an energy efficient strategy for smart green building operation because they don’t need environmental-unfriendly refrigerants, e.g. CFCs and HCFCs, and they can make good use of waste heat from industrial processes. However, this technology has not been widely commercialized due to their large size and low cooling efficiency. In this study, a smart design of the evaporator of the cooling system and careful choice of working fluid are proposed to substantially enhance the efficiency. Firstly, micro-grooves are cut on the heating surface of the evaporator. The cooling effect is enhanced because the working fluid is absorbed to the micro-grooves due to capillary action. Second, nanofluids (suspending some nanoparticles in water) are used as the working fluid. Nanofluids have already been recognized as effective heat transfer fluids. Mathematical models has been developed and a prototype of the capillary-assisted and nanofluid based evaporator was built and tested in different scenarios. The performance of the cooling systems are significantly improved, leading to a possible dramatic reduction in size. Therefore, the finding in this project will help engineers and researchers further design and improve the technologies, and provide an energy saving alternative to the market.

16202514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202514.value: There is a broad and strong westward oceanic current trapped against the northern continental slope in the South China Sea (SCS). It flows across the entire northern slope from the Luzon Strait with hundreds of kilometers in width and thousands of meters in depth. This prominent current is termed as northern SCS slope current or NSC. It shapes the nature of the entire SCS circulation as well as the associated heat and freshwater transports that affect regional climate variability. As the NSC flows over the sloping bottom topography, it forms strong cross-slope currents and enhances water exchanges between the continental shelf and continental slope as well as between the continental slope and the deep ocean. As a result, the NSC transports upslope the cold, salty and nutrient rich deep waters towards the continental shelf (e.g. Hong Kong waters) or downslope the warm and fresh shelf/coastal waters into the deep ocean off the southern China, which play significant roles in the maintenances of oceanic circulation and biological productivity in the SCS. Slope current is a widespread phenomenon and has been extensively studied in many parts of the world’s oceans, although its complete dynamical rationalization remains un-established. The physical process of the NSC has not been investigated, despite its important roles in the regional marine environment and regional climate variability. It involves with dynamic forcing arising from Southeast Asia monsoon wind forcing, topographic wave over the sloping bottom and inflow/outflow through straits around the SCS. It is hypothesized that: (H1) The NSC is controlled by the variation of continental slope in the direction of the current direction, the inflow/outflow hydrodynamics in the straits as well as wind-forced SCS currents; (H2) The interaction and feedback between the NSC and its bottom frictional layer greatly are the key dynamics controlling the development and substance of the NSC and the associated cross-slope-shelf-deep ocean transports; (H3) The intensities of NSC and its cross-slope-shelf-deep ocean transports are determined by the cross-/along-isobath pressure gradients originated from the flow responses to variable sloping bottom topography and stratified water column. We will combine existing field measurements with novel process-oriented and realistic numerical simulations to isolate individual dynamic components of the extremely complex NSC and to provide a holistic understanding of dynamics for the NSC as well as for the slope currents in the other parts of the world’s ocean. The study topic is regionally relevant and globally significant.

16202514.label: Realisation of objectives
16202514.value: During this project, we have conducted a series of studies on slope currents that form the three-dimensional basin-wide circulation in the South China Sea. These studies address the project objectives. The details are: 1. We investigated South China Sea (SCS) circulation forced by winds and inflow/outflow over the continental slope around the basin edge. This study provides a new insight on the vertical structure of the SCS circulation. We, for the first time, find a three-layer alternating spinning circulation in the SCS. This new understanding of the three-dimensional circulation in the SCS is crucial for determining the transports of water masses, energy, and biogeochemical substances in the regional and adjacent larger oceans. We reveal the existence of a unique three-layer cyclonic-anticyclonic-cyclonic (CAC) circulation in the upper (<750 m), middle (750-1500 m), and deep (>1500 m) layers in the SCS with differing seasonality. An inflow-outflow-inflow structure in Luzon Strait induces largely the CAC circulation, which leads to vortex stretching in the SCS basin because of a lateral planetary vorticity flux in each of the respective layers. The formation of Joint Effects of Baroclinicity and Relief (JEBAR) is an intrinsic dynamic response to the CAC circulation. The JEBAR arises from the CAC flow-topography interaction in the SCS. The result has been published in the top journal in physical oceanography: Journal of Physical Oceanography. 2. We conducted numerical modeling of intrinsically and extrinsically forced seasonal circulation in the entire China Seas (including SCS). In this study, we developed a new three-dimensional, high-resolution ocean circulation model for the entire China Seas (CS) region. The model considered the unique regional linked physics associated with the western boundary current, monsoonal wind and tidal forcings, and topography in both the SCS and their adjacent oceans. From this well validated model, we derived new insights into the three-dimensional seasonal circulation of the SCS in response to the intrinsic forcing of monsoonal winds and extrinsic forcing of flow exchange with adjacent oceans through the straits and over the slope around the periphery of the SCS. Besides the East Asian monsoon forcing, we found that these extrinsic forcing interacted coherently with each other and with the interior circulation to jointly shape the SCS circulation. Specifically, we revealed rotating layered circulation along the slope in the SCS. The slope circulation in the South China Sea had a vertical cyclonic-anticyclonic-cyclonic pattern in the upper-middle-lower layers, which we related to the inflow-outflow-inflow transport in those layers in the Luzon Strait. The findings have been published in top oceanography journal: Journal of Geophysical Research (Oceans). 3. In order to resolve the ocean circulation that is driven by low-frequency currents (e.g. wind-driven current) as well as high-frequency current (e.g. tidally driven current) in the limited area numerical model such as in the modeling of ocean circulation in the South China Sea, we need to develop a new open boundary condition that can accommodate these dominant forcing with different frequency. In limited-area ocean models, open boundary conditions (OBCs) often create dynamic inconsistencies and perform poorly in resolving tidal or subtidal flow when both forces exist. Orlanski-type radiation OBCs are reasonably efficient at treating the subtidally forced flow, and Flather-type OBCs are commonly adapted for the tidally forced flow. However, neither of them performs well when tidal and subtidal forces simultaneously drive the flows. We have developed a novel OBC that integrates the active OBC in Gan and Allen (2005) and a Flather-type OBC. This new OBC accommodates the concurrent Tidal and Subtidal (TST) forcing, and the respective tidal or subtidal forcing, at the open boundary of a limited-area model. This new TST-OBC treats the tidal component with a Flather-type OBC, and it separates subtidal barotropic and baroclinic components into local (forced) and global (unforced) components. Then an unforced Orlanski-type OBC can be applied to the global part. We applied the TST-OBC to all model variables to reduce dynamic inconsistence. Using the Regional Ocean Modeling System, we applied the TST-OBC to the shallow East China Sea shelf where strong tidal and subtidal forces over complex topography govern the circulation. Our numerical experiments and analyses suggest that the TST-OBC was robust for both concurrent tidal-subtidal forcing and solely tidal or subtidal forcing at the open boundary. It reduced spurious energy reflection, and, overall, it performed better than an Orlanski-type or Flather-type OBC in reproducing realistic tidal and sub-tidal shelf circulation. The findings have been published in top oceanography journal: Journal of Geophysical Research (Oceans). 4. We investigated the fundamental dynamics in the three-dimensional slope current. Both observational and reanalysis sea surface temperature data reveal that upwelling occurs frequently off the northeastern coast of Hainan Island (downstream of the change in topography off Tongluo Cape), which cannot be attributed to the along-shelf wind alone. To identify dynamics of the upwelling, we conduct a numerical experiment using an idealized topography that is simplified from the actual topography off the eastern and northeastern coasts of Hainan Island. The result indicates that the upwelling downstream of the change in topography is associated with onshore cross-isobath transport. Analysis of the vertically integrated momentum balance shows that the upwelling linked onshore transport is primarily intensified by the along-isobath barotropic pressure gradient force (PGT), but is weakened by the along-isobath baroclinic pressure gradient force (PGC). The along-isobath PGT is linked to the advection of relative vorticity, the bottom stress curl and the gradient of momentum flux in vorticity equation. On the other hand, the PGC-related process is diagnosed by potential vorticity (PV) balance. Similar to the negative PV term from wind stress, the negative PV terms of the joint effect of baroclinicity and relief and the baroclinic bottom pressure torque weaken the upwelling-linked onshore transport downstream of the change in topography. The onshore transport is enhanced by the positive PV from bottom stress. In addition, the cross-isobath forces play an important role in upwelling intensification in the shallow nearshore region. The findings have been published in top oceanography journal: Journal of Geophysical Research (Oceans).

16202514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202514.value: 1: We have developed a new three-dimensional, high-resolution ocean circulation model for the South China Seas (SCS). Unlike previous studies, the model considered the unique regional linked physics associated with the western boundary current, monsoonal wind and tidal forcings, and topography in both the SCS and their adjacent oceans. The new model captures the three-layer circulation in the SCS, which most of the current global failed to do it. 2. We also developed a new numerical open boundary condition (OBC) that is able to accommodate the concurrent Tidal and Subtidal (TST) forcing, and the respective tidal or subtidal forcing, at the open boundary of a limited-area model. The TST-OBC fills the gap for existing OBC which performs poorly when tidal and subtidal forces simultaneously drive the flows. TST-OBC allows us to resolve slope current that forms the SCS three-layer circulation. 3. Through new approach of dynamics analysis utilizing Layer Integrated Vorticity Equation (LIVE), we have identified that characteristic of the slope current and its associated basin-wide circulation in the SCS, and provided new physics of the slope current in response to inflow-outflow through straits around the SCS basin. 4. We further conducted the geophysical fluid dynamics study for the along-isobath and cross-isobath transport over the sloping topography. We found that cross-isobath transport is intensified by the along-isobath barotropic pressure gradient force (PGT), but is weakened by the along-isobath baroclinic pressure gradient. force (PGC). We then links PGT and PGC to bottom stress curl and JEBAR effect.

16202514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202514.value: The basin-wide circulation in the South China Sea (SCS) is formed by the slope current flowing over the continental slope surrounding the SCS. Besides driven by the monsoonal winds in the region, the slope current is driven by the inflow-outflow through straits around the periphery of the SCS. The response of the slope current, and the underlying physics to the inflow-outflow were unknown. Thus, the three-dimensional SCS basin-wide circulation was largely unclear. This study developed an advanced numerical ocean model to resolve the slope current and identify the circulation in the SCS. The significance and value of the research include: (1) advance numerical ocean modeling by developing novel TST-OBC; (2) develop a new SCS model capable of resolving the basin-wide ocean circulation in the SCS that other global ocean models can't not resolve; (3) identify a alternating spinning three-layer circulation in the SCS and associated new physics.

16203214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16203214.value: 基于计算机仿真实验的鲁棒最优选择

16203214.label: Project Objectives
16203214.value: We will build a general robust selection-of-the-best (RSB) framework accounting for model ambiguity. Since our framework considers ambiguities in both input distribution family and pertinent parameters, we will define a suitable and reasonable ambiguity set in our framework. Suppose two indifference-zone (IZ) parameters exist among scenarios for each decision and the worst-case performances across decisions. We will then design two-layer R&S procedures under the IZ formulation, either two-stage or fully sequential, to select the best decision. These procedures will identify the worst-case distribution in the first stage and the best decision in the second. Suppose there are k decisions and m scenarios for each decision in the problem of interest. Intuitively, the RBS problem can be viewed as selecting the best one from k×m ”systems”, where a ``system'' refers to a decision and scenario pair. In this case, a relatively small error tolerance will be allocated to each pairwise comparison between the best and the others. However, we will show that this rule of error allocations is quite conservative and study a more efficient rule. Suppose that it is difficult to specify the IZ parameter among scenarios for each decision. In the absence of this IZ parameter, the original procedure seems to fail because in the first stage one cannot guarantee the worst scenario will be selected for each decision, which as a consequence prevents the selection of the best decision in the second stage. Hence, we will adapt our procedure to solve RSB in this situation.

16203214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203214.value: 在管理实践中，决策者常常需要在有限个方案中选出一个最优方案。这里的最优通常是通过比较方案的平均表现而获得的。这类问题在运筹学中被称为最优选择问题。文献中解决此类问题的方法通常假设这些方案可以通过计算机模型进行仿真，因此可以通过观测随机仿真的结果对比不同方案的平均表现。在计算机仿真模型中，输入变量的随机分布往往具有不确定性。但现有的最优选择算法都忽视了此类的不确定性，因此可能对最优选择的结果产生不好的影响。在本研究中，我们建议通过鲁棒方法来选出最优方案。我们将设计两阶段算法和连续算法，研究这些算法的统计性质，并与现有最优选择算法进行比较。

16204214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204214.value: Reinforced concrete (RC) frame structures infilled with masonry walls are considered as one of the most common structural forms for low- to medium-rise construction in the world. In design practice the infills are presumed to make no contribution to the stiffness and lateral strength of the structure in relation to withstanding horizontal loading. The conventional tight-fit infill walls can significantly increase the in-plane stiffness of frames, thus improving the wind or earthquake load-carrying capacity. However, under strong seismic excitation the severe interaction between infill walls and the frame may cause brittle shear failure in the columns and lead to catastrophic failure of the structure with an undesirable soft-storey mechanism. It has extensively been reported that severe damage to masonry-infilled frames has been observed in every single disastrous earthquake, including many newly-built ones, particularly in the 1999 Izmit earthquake in Turkey, the 2010 Maule earthquake in Chile, and the 2008 Sichuan earthquake and 2013 Lushan earthquake in China. Inherent problems relating to seismic analysis and design methods for tight-fit unreinforced infilled frame structures clearly have not yet been solved. Some guidelines for evaluating tight-fit infilled frames have been provided in different countries, but they are well recognised as far from satisfactory in terms of completeness and reliability. The primary objective of the proposed research is to develop an inspiring and innovative system, by a combined experimental and computational study, for designing masonry-infilled RC frames, where the infill panels are isolated from the bounding frame by incorporating flexible connections at the column-to-infill interfaces. A series of seismic shake-table tests of scaled specimens will be conducted to investigate the efficiency of the proposed flexible connection system. The experimental studies are expected to lead to the production of practical guidelines for seismic design of masonry-infilled frame buildings. Moreover, computational simulations will be carried out, where a new nonlinear finite element modelling is to be proposed for solving the problems. Hong Kong is recently classified as a region of moderate seismicity with a seismic intensity of VII and a peak ground acceleration of 0.15g. In view of the large number of masonry-infilled frame buildings in Hong Kong, the proposed research is expected to provide crucial guidance for seismic assessment and the design of safer and better-performing frame structures. The test results and design guidelines/recommendations from the proposed research are also expected to benefit infrastructure development in other countries that are threatened by earthquakes.

16204214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204214.value: Masonry-infilled reinforced concrete frame structures are recognised as one of the most common structural forms for medium- and high-rise buildings in the world. Although this structural form has been widely adopted for buildings for many years, it has been extensively reported that in every single disastrous earthquake during the past decades relatively poor seismic performance and severe damage of a considerable amount of infilled frame buildings. The primary objective of the proposed research is to investigate thoroughly the seismic behaviour and performance of masonry-infilled reinforced concrete frame structures through shaking table tests, thus developing effective and practical methods for mitigating the seismic damage of masonry-infilled frame buildings. In view of the large number of infilled frame buildings in Hong Kong and in the world, the proposed research is expected to provide crucial guidance for designing safer and well-performing frame structures with infills under earthquake actions. Results and design recommendations of the proposed research are expected to benefit the infrastructural development in the countries and regions that are threatened by earthquake disasters.

16204714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204714.value: 經過三十年的深入研究和開發，氮化鎵（GaN）基半導體器件已經逐步走向了量產化。其中最值得關注的是LED產業，在過去的十年裡蓬勃發展，引領了固態照明的革命。基於氮化鎵材料在LED照明領域的巨大成功，將氮化鎵晶體管應用於高功率開關及高頻領域也成為了研究熱點。在功率電子器件中，研究人員集中注意力來挖掘氮化鎵晶體管在硅基功率器件尚未實現的領域的應用潛力。氮化鎵的寬帶隙，高擊穿場強和電子飽和速率等獨特的材料性質賦予了氮化鎵晶體管相對於其他材料體系的天然優勢，正如其最高的Johnson品質因數（綜合了高壓及高頻工作因數）所體現的。此外，氮化鎵晶體管的大電流和高性能也與對於高功率LED照明的不斷增加的需求相契合。 基於相同的氮化鎵材料體系，LED及驅動晶體管的單芯片集成可以有效提高器件性能并降低生產成本。然而LED和晶體管對材料的要求差異巨大。經過二十年的深入研究和發展，LED已經成熟發展為一個蓬勃發展的產業，而氮化鎵晶體管在幾個跨國功率電子公司的推動下也進入了大規模生產的節奏。然而所有這些都是針對特定的應用領域的分立器件。儘管氮化鎵基LED及晶體管的單芯片整合有著先天優勢，將兩者集成在一起的嘗試還很少見。這是由高溫過程及複雜工藝帶來的相關問題。 基於我們在LED及晶體管材料與器件方面多年的專業知識及經驗，我們提出通過選區外延生長的方式對LED及晶體管的單芯片集成進行深入研究。我們將探索包括疊放式，分佈式在內的多種器件結構

16204714.label: Realisation of objectives
16204714.value: 1. Design and fabricate monolithically integrated HEMT-LED by selective area growth of HEMT on LED We have designed and fabricated monolithically integrated HEMT-LED by selective area growth (SAG) of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on InGaN/GaN LEDs. The fabrication process started from deposition of a 500 nm SiO2 as a regrowth mask on the LED epi structure by plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), followed by photolithography and wet etching by buffered oxide etchant (BOE) to expose the regrowth area. The AlGaN/GaN HEMTs were grown in the regrowth window in an Aixtron metal organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) system. By utilizing the SAG technique, the challenges of plasma damage and etch stop control that are commonly encountered in the selective epi removal (SER) method can be effectively circumvented. With control voltages VDD and gate modulation voltages applied to the HEMT-LED, the HEMT-LED emitted modulated blue light under modulated gate-bias. In most of the applications, LEDs operate in the forward mode at voltages larger than the VF. Resistors are typically used in the driving circuits of LEDs to control the operating current and the light output. Power dissipated by the resistors is wasted and generates heat in the circuits. The use of a HEMT with low Ron to convert the current control mode to gate voltage control mode will be more efficient. The HEMT (Wg/Lg=100μm/1μm) shows good controllability over the emission brightness of the LED via the injected current, demonstrating viability of the integrated device for a wide range of applications such as smart lighting, micro-displays, and VLCs. The results have been published in Applied Physics Letters, IEEE Electron Device Letters, and Journal of Crystal Growth. 2. Design and fabricate a side-by-side HEMT-LED integration without metal interconnection In the first stage, we demonstrated a monolithically integrated HEMT-LED by SAG of HEMT on LED epi structure. Despite the increased off-state breakdown voltage of HEMT on LED by carbon doping, the theoretical breakdown voltage is still limited by the relatively thin regrowth buffer and the parasitic leakage channel at regrowth interface. To further increase the breakdown characteristic, a side-by-side HEMT-LED integration scheme appeared to be a feasible option. Besides this, in our first experiment, there was difficulty in running reliable metal interconnects across the greatly enhanced epi growth at the interface region between the SAG epi and the SiO2 mask. The outputs of the HEMTs were therefore connected to the cathodes of the LEDs by wire-bonding. Furthermore, the metal wire interconnection may introduce extra parasitic components and degrade the performance of the integrated devices, especially for high frequency operation applications. As a result, a side-by-side metal-interconnection-free scheme was proposed by combining SER and SAG techniques. With a seamless contact between the GaN channel of the HEMTs and the n-type layer of the LEDs, the interconnection related parasitics can be effectively eliminated. For the laterally connected LEDs with HEMTs in this work, the IOFF of the HEMTs remains at a low level (around 3 orders lower) and only reaches 6.3 µA/mm at VDS of 200V, indicating a high buffer resistivity was retained after the high-temperature selective area growth process. To reduce the power dissipation and heat generation from the driving transistor and improve current spreading from the driving HEMTs to the LEDs, a HEMT with a larger Wg/Lg (475 µm/2 µm) was used in the integrated HEMT-LED devices. The forward current of the HEMT-LED devices can be well controlled by the gate bias of the driving transistor. In addition, the LOP of the integrated LEDs exhibits the same response as the driving current of the integrated HEMTs, demonstrating good controllability of the LEDs by the gate voltage via the injected current. Besides the gate modulation capability, light emission of the integrated LED can also be suitably controlled by the VDD of the HEMT-LED device. The detailed results have been published in Applied Physics Letters. 3. Develop a common buffer platform for the side-by-side HEMT-LED integration scheme and demonstrate a high performance integrated HEMT-LED In the second stage, we demonstrated a side-by-side integration scheme for HEMT-LED integration by combining SER and SAG procedures. This method is highlighted by an intimate and seamless contact between the GaN channel of the HEMT and the n-type layer of the LED. Direct contact of the HEMT channel and the n-GaN electrode of the LED allows for conversion of a current-controlled LED to a voltage-controlled device by the gate and drain biases. A voltage controlled LED is simpler to work with during the IC design for the driver circuit. The device is composed of a HEMT with a Wg/Lg ratio of 475 μm/2 μm and an LED with a light-emitting area of 450 μm×460 μm. The HEMT/LED footprint ratio used in this work is ~ 0.27, which was based on a layout design considering the direct current (DC) driving capability of the HEMT and the operation current density of the LED. LOP of the integrated HEMT-LED can be fully modulated by VGS and VDD through the injection current from the driving transistor. No light emission was observed while the HEMT is pinched off with a VGS below -4 V. With increasing VGS, a nearly linear modulation of the LOP can be observed before saturation. Note that the saturation of the LOP appears at a more negative VGS when the HEMT-LED is biased at a smaller VDD. Besides the gate modulation, the brightness of the HEMT-LED can also be tuned by VDD. Furthermore, the LOP of the integrated HEMT-LED can reach ~ 7 mW at an injection current of ~80 mA (VDD = 8 V and VGS = 1 V), which is a dramatic improvement compared to the previously reported 2 mW at 80 mA injection current in the last year. The improvement can be attributed to improved crystalline quality with the optimal GaN/AlN buffer structure. Further enhanced brightness of the integrated LED can be achieved by a number of technologies such as epitaxial structure design, surface roughening, advanced packaging and et al. Since the 2DEG channel of the HEMT and the n-type GaN of the LED were internally connected during selective area growth, we define the virtual D (drain) terminal to be at the HEMT/LED edge. The G-to-S distance (LGS) is 3.5 μm and G-to-D distance (LGD) is 15 μm. The breakdown voltage is defined as the measured voltage when the off-state current density reaches 1 mA/mm. At forward VDD bias, a breakdown voltage exceeding 530 V can be achieved for the integrated HEMT-LED, while at reverse bias conditions, the breakdown voltage of the HEMT-LED is around 270 V. The high breakdown performance of the integrated HEMT-LED is mainly attributed to the high resistivity GaN/AlN buffer underneath. At reverse bias, the dominant off-state leakage current flows from the source terminal to the gate terminal. As a result, the smaller LGS of 3.5 μm results in a reduced breakdown voltage. The breakdown performance at reverse bias conditions can be further improved with an optimized layout design. The results have been published in Journal of Electronic Materials and IEEE Photonics Technology Letters.

16204714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204714.value: After we demonstrated the capability of a novel three-terminal voltage-controlled light emitter, we explored other possibilities. We then report for the first time on-chip integration of III-nitride voltage-controlled light emitters with visible and ultraviolet (UV) photodiodes (PDs). InGaN/GaN and AlGaN/GaN heterostructures were grown in specific regions by selective-area epitaxy, allowing monolithic integration of versatile devices including visible light emitting diodes (LEDs), visible-light PDs, AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), and UV-light Schottky barrier (SB) PDs. A serial connection between the LED and HEMT through the epitaxial layers enables a threeterminal voltage-controlled light emitter (HEMT-LED), efficiently converting voltage-controlled signals into visiblelight signals that can be coupled into an adjacent visiblelight PD generating electrical signals. While the integrated blue HEMT-LED and PD transmits signals carried by visible light, the visible-blind SB-PD on a chip receives external UV light control signals with negligible interference from the on-chip visible-light source. This integration scheme can be extended to open an avenue for developing a variety of applications, such as smart lighting, on-chip optical interconnect, optical wireless communication, and opto-isolators.

16204714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204714.value: Conventional LED is a two-terminal electronic device that emits light proportional to the amount of current injected into the device. When used as an individual discrete device, it is simple and can be driven by a simple battery. However, living in the world of integrated circuits and reducing form factors of all the gadgets, integrating LEDs with ICs is necessary to extend their applications and reduce energy consumption. The technologies we explored and developed in the project pave the way towards this goal. We converted conventional LEDs being controlled by electrical current to one that can be turned on/off with one voltage and the light intensity with the level of another voltage drive. This property is very desirable to all integrated circuit design topology.

16204814.label: Project Objectives
16204814.value: Objective A: To formulate the Cache Induced Opportunistic MIMO Cooperation as a Stochastic Optimization Problem In this project, we shall formally cast the design as a stochastic optimization problem to optimize directly the end-to-end video streaming performance metric (e.g. playback interruption probability) rather than conventional heuristic metrics (e.g. physical layer capacity or throughput). The optimization variables involved are the (a) cache update policy and (b) MIMO precoding policy. Note that conventional caching algorithms in fixed line peer-to-peer (P2P) systems or content distribution network (CDN) cannot be applied to this problem because they have a different role and target (load balancing). However, in our case, the cache update algorithm is to create MIMO cooperation opportunity while the MIMO precoding policy is to harvest the benefit when such an opportunity occurs. Furthermore, unlike conventional P2P or CDN systems, the cache and MIMO precoding designs are tightly coupled together. Objective C: To evaluate performance in LTE+ Systems We shall apply the multi-timescale cache and mimo precoding solution and insights obtained in (A) and (B) to design practical solutions for LTE+ systems. For example, we will study the tradeoff between video streaming performance and system parameters (such as the SNR, the cache size and the number of antennas). We shall also characterize the potential benefits and robustness of the cache-induced opportunistic MIMO cooperation solutions with LTE+ system.

16204814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204814.value: 為了消除無線蜂窩系統中眾所周知的“干擾瓶頸”，人們為未來5G無線通信系統提出了一些包括“協同多入多出（MIMO）”的先進物理層技術。但是傳統的協同MIMO方案需要配備高速回程傳輸線路以便在基站之間交換負載數據。這對於MIMO協同的實際實現帶來了巨大的挑戰。 實際上，在pico小區密集的城鎮地區，高速回程傳輸線路可能非常昂貴。我們能否在不採用昂貴的高速回程傳輸線路的情況下依然獲得協同MIMO的好處？在本項目中，我們將為多媒體流應用提出一個新的稱為“基於緩存的機會MIMO協同”方案。這種方案只需要採用便宜的低速回程傳輸線路就可以完全釋放出協同MIMO方案的潛在增益。通過緩存一部分被基站發送的多媒體文件，鄰近的基站可以在不通過回程傳輸線路交換負載數據的情況下採用MIMO協同傳輸。但是，這種方法需要攻克幾個關鍵技術難點。首先，系統性能依賴於MIMO協同的概率（即用戶所訪問的數據同時存在於多個鄰近基站的概率）。此概率由基站的緩存數據結構和緩存算法所決定。其次，基站端緩存算法（用於創造MIMO協同機會）的設計和MIMO預編碼算法緊密耦合在一起。在對等網絡（P2P）或內容分發網絡（CDN）中採用的傳統緩存設計是針對有線互聯網設計的。這些緩存技術主要被設計來解決網絡中的負載平衡問題（這與創造物理層MIMO協同機會完全不同），其中緩存算法和物理層算法是完全獨立的，因而不能應用於本項目所提出的基於緩存的機會MIMO協同方案中。最後，未來5G無線通信系統中主要的容量需求來自於高質量視頻流應用。視頻流應用需要優化的主要性能指標是回放中斷和回放溢出概率。由於需要對回放緩存複雜的隊列和無線接入網絡中的信道進行動態建模，其相應的優化問題非常困難。通過利用其中所涉及的隨機過程內在的分層時間尺度結構，我們提出了新的隨機分解技術並為緩存更新和MIMO 協同推導具有魯棒性的多時間尺度解決方案。綜上，在未來5G無線通信系統中的高質量視頻流應用中，如何在不採用昂貴的高速回程傳輸線路時實現MIMO協同的好處是一個具有重大應用價值的科研問題。本項目的研究成果將為解決該問題奠定重要的理論和實踐基礎。

16204814.label: Realisation of objectives
16204814.value: In this project, we have established a mathematical formulation and theoretical understanding of physical layer caching in wireless networks. In particular, we have proposed an effective scheme that can exploit the cache in the base stations of wireless network to strive for opportunities for MIMO cooperation, resulting in significant gain in the capacity of the radio interface without strong backhaul connections. This observation opens up a lot of opportunities especially in dense small cell networks where the bottleneck is the expensive backhaul connecting to every small cells. Using the technology, we can achieve similar capacity gain without these expensive backhaul in the network. We have obtained theoretical analytical results. As a result of the efforts, we have published 9 IEEE transactions papers and 5 IEEE top conference papers.

16204814.label: Summary of objectives addressed
16204814.value: Objectives Addressed Percentage achieved 1.Objective A: To formulate the Cache Induced Opportunistic MIMO Cooperation as a Stochastic Optimization Problem In this project, we shall formally cast the design as a stochastic optimization problem to optimize directly the end-to-end video streaming performance metric (e.g. playback interruption probability) rather than conventional heuristic metrics (e.g. physical layer capacity or throughput). The optimization variables involved are the (a) cache update policy and (b) MIMO precoding policy. Note that conventional caching algorithms in fixed line peer-to-peer (P2P) systems or content distribution network (CDN) cannot be applied to this problem because they have a different role and target (load balancing). However, in our case, the cache update algorithm is to create MIMO cooperation opportunity while the MIMO precoding policy is to harvest the benefit when such an opportunity occurs. Furthermore, unlike conventional P2P or CDN systems, the cache and MIMO precoding designs are tightly coupled together.Yes100% 2.Objective C: To evaluate performance in LTE+ Systems We shall apply the multi-timescale cache and mimo precoding solution and insights obtained in (A) and (B) to design practical solutions for LTE+ systems. For example, we will study the tradeoff between video streaming performance and system parameters (such as the SNR, the cache size and the number of antennas). We shall also characterize the potential benefits and robustness of the cache-induced opportunistic MIMO cooperation solutions with LTE+ system.Yes100%

The optimization variables involved are the (a) cache update policy and (b) MIMO precoding policy. Note that conventional caching algorithms in fixed line peer-to-peer (P2P) systems or content distribution network (CDN) cannot be applied to this problem because they have a different role and target (load balancing). However, in our case, the cache update algorithm is to create MIMO cooperation opportunity while the MIMO precoding policy is to harvest the benefit when such an opportunity occurs. Objective C: To evaluate performance in LTE+ Systems We shall apply the multi-timescale cache and mimo precoding solution and insights obtained in (A) and (B) to design practical solutions for LTE+ systems. For example, we will study the tradeoff between video streaming performance and system parameters (such as the SNR, the cache size and the number of antennas). We shall also characterize the potential benefits and robustness of the cache-induced opportunistic MIMO cooperation solutions with LTE+ system.

16204814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204814.value: The major findings in the project include (1) Cache can have profound benefits in wireless network compared with fixed line networks. In fixed line networks, the role of cache is to reduce the number of hops from the source to the client devices and load balancing. However, in wireless networks, the role of cache is to induce a more favourable communication topology by providing dynamic side information to the base stations. (2) Through edge caching in the wireless networks, a lot of unfavourable topology (such as relay channel, interference channel) can be transformed into favourable toplogies, achieving huge gain in the network capacity. (3) We have developed a mathematical framework to understand the fundamental limits of caching in some wireless networks. (4) We have also come up with various practical designs on how to cache information and how to utilise the cached side information and illustrated that practical gains can be obtained in real systems. As a result, we have produced 9 IEEE transaction papers and 5 IEEE conference papers.

16204814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204814.value: This is a new topic of research and there are still a lot of unexplored areas. For example, what is the fundamental limits for cached wireless networks in more general settings? How to accommodate mobility in the network? How to accommodate dynamically changing popularity of content? All these require further investigations.

16204814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204814.value: In this project, we have studied a new way of improving the capacity of future wireless networks for content distribution. It is known that there are huge capacity demand for future networks but most of the increased demands come from high quality content access. Content has a subtle feature that can be exploit. Specifically, contents are catchable and we showed that by appropriately caching some contents in the edge of the wireless network (base stations), the cached contents can provide valuable side information, which can substantially enhance the capacity of future wireless networks. The impacts and the potential of the technology is far reaching because through the proposed caching schemes, we can effectively translate storage capacity into wireless network transmission capacity.

16205114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205114.value: 漩渦進水口和排水隧道的水流-空氣相互作用

16205114.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16205114.value: Prof GHIDAOUI, Mohamed S. Prof Lam, Kit Ming

16205114.label: Project Objectives
16205114.value: To understand the dynamical behaviours of air pockets in a drainage tunnel through experiments; To understand the physical mechanisms of the interaction between rising air pockets and the vortex intake inflow in the vertical drop shaft; To obtain original velocity and pressure data on hydraulic surges in the drop shaft – tunnel system for validation of numerical models.
rows: To understand the dynamical behaviours of air pockets in a drainage tunnel through experiments;
To understand the physical mechanisms of the interaction between rising air pockets and the vortex intake inflow in the vertical drop shaft;
To obtain original velocity and pressure data on hydraulic surges in the drop shaft – tunnel system for validation of numerical models.

16205114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205114.value: Vortex intakes are used in water supply or drainage systems to convey water stably from upland high-level catchment to a tunnel at a lower elevation. The vortex intake transforms an open channel flow into a vortex flow that swirls down a vertical drop shaft (heights of the order of 100 m) with good energy dissipation. Under normal conditions, there is a continuous air core in the middle of the drop shaft that allows the air to escape freely. During heavy rainstorms, however, the tunnel can be pressurized, and large amounts of air can enter into the tunnel-drop shaft system. The interaction of air pockets and water in the drop shaft can lead to unstable hydraulic surges and oscillations that significantly impair the drainage performance. With aging urban infrastructure and more intense rainfall due to climate change, the understanding of air-water interaction in vortex intakes is increasingly important in Hong Kong and other major cities. Despite many past studies, the mechanism of air-water interaction is not well-understood, and the theoretical development is also hampered by the lack of data on physical models of adequate size. It is proposed to carry out a comprehensive experimental study of the fluid mechanics of air-water interactions in vortex intake and drainage tunnel systems. A series of experiments will be conducted on physical models of prototype systems at different model scales. The propagation of air pockets, pressure transmission and vertical surging process will be observed for different intake and tunnel flow configurations. Detailed velocity and pressure measurements will be made at key locations in a twin drop shaft and tunnel both for the water and air phase. The experiments will be supplemented and interpreted by numerical modelling of the air-water interaction in the tunnel-drop shaft system. This basic research is engendered by field observations including a devastating flash flood. The findings will provide valuable insights into the physical mechanisms of air-water interaction in intake shafts, and benefit the design and operation of water supply and drainage systems. The original data will provide benchmark data set for validation of numerical models. 漩渦進水口是供排水系統的一個主要水工設施，用於把上游集水區截取的水流，平穩地輸送到位於較低高程的供排水隧洞。明渠流經過漩渦進水口後，在豎井（落差可逾100米）中形成穩定的螺旋流，可得良好的消能效果。在正常的運行情況下，螺旋流中間存在連續的空腔，空氣在此中可自由流動。但在暴雨時，排水隧道內可形成有壓流，大量的空氣可能進入隧道-豎井系統中。水流和空氣的相互作用，可導致水湧和大幅振蕩，嚴重損害系統的排水能力。應對城市基礎設施的老化和氣候變化帶來的挑戰，了解隧道-豎井系統的水流-空氣動力學，對香港及其它大城市，顯得日益重要。以往的相關研究，缺乏大型模型實驗數據，未能掌握水流-空氣相互作用的機理。 這個計劃，將開展有關漩渦進水口和排水隧道內的水-空氣相互作用的流體力學全面研究。用不同比尺的水力模型進行一系列的實驗。在不同的進水口和隧道流量狀態下，觀察氣泡的運動，壓力的傳播和豎井中的垂直湧動過程。在雙豎井和隧道的關鍵位置，對水和氣兩相進行詳細的速度和壓力測量。另外，也將開展相關的數值模擬計算。 此項基礎研究，建基於實地觀察 (包括災害性的的暴發洪水)。研究結果將闡明排水隧道內的水和空氣相互作用的物理機制。有利於供水排水系統的設計和運行。亦可為三維計算力學模型的驗證，提供可靠的基準數據。

16205114.label: Realisation of objectives
16205114.value: 1. To understand the dynamical behaviours of air pockets in a drainage tunnel through experiments (Achieved 100%) The dynamics of an air pocket in a surcharged horizontal drainage tunnel and its subsequent release from a dropshaft have been studied with physical experiment and numerical simulation. A comprehensive series of experiments has been performed on a physical model of a simplified drainage system, which consists of a vertical riser and a horizontal pipe connected to a constant head tank. The horizontal pipe is equipped with ball valves to form air pockets with different sizes. By opening the valve, an air pocket propagates into the horizontal pipe – riser system initially filled with water. First, the propagation of an air pocket in the horizontal pipe without a vertical riser is studied. The experiments show that the air pocket propagation is similar to a gravity current; the slope and constant speed of the air front are in agreement with gravity current theory. The initial water length, air volume and boundary condition at the end gate do not appear to affect the initial air pocket propagation velocity. Second, the air pocket propagation in a pressurized horizontal pipe with or without air release is studied with 14 experiments. The downstream end of pipe is either closed or fitted with an orifice. The pressure variation and the air pocket motion are measured. It is found that the maximum pressure mostly occurred at the moment when the water front hit the downstream end. The existence of air in the pipe has an important effect on the magnitude of the peak pressure. When the orifice size is very small, the air is entrapped in the pipe and can hardly escape from the orifice. The air pocket acts as an “air cushion” to prevent strong pressure surge during water front filling process. When the size of orifice increases, the peak pressure head increases as air escapes faster from the orifice and thus is not able to provide resistance to the advancing water front. Further increasing the orifice size results in decreased momentum change in impact and reduced peak pressure. The air pressure variations can be well predicted by a one-dimensional rigid-column model until the water front hit the pipe end. Third, the dynamics of an air pocket in a surcharged horizontal drainage tunnel (diameter D) and its subsequent release from a vertical dropshaft (diameter D_r) have been studied with over 50 experiments. Two series of experiments have been performed, one with an independent upstream head and one without. The trajectories of the air pockets in horizontal pipe and vertical riser, and pressure variation in the horizontal pipe are measured. Experiments are performed with different riser diameters, upstream pressures and air pocket volumes. The dynamics of air pocket during the occurrence of a geyser is elucidated for the first time through high-speed camera imaging. It is concluded that an external independent pressure head is essential for the formation of geyser - for small riser diameter and large air volume (D_r/D < 0.62). Air pocket pressure is significantly higher than the hydrostatic pressure induced by water column above, resulting in rapid acceleration of air and water, and jetting out of air-water mixture from the riser top (Cong et al. 2017). An unsteady three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is developed to simulate the pressure transients and air-water interactions during geyser events using the Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) technique. Model predictions of air-water interfaces in the vertical shaft are in good agreement with laboratory measurements; the mechanism for the formation of geysers is elucidated. CFD simulations have also been carried out for an idealized prototype drainage system and the mechanism of prototype geyser is unraveled. It is shown that the geyser behavior can be characterized by extremely large vertical air velocities that result in dispersed air-water mixtures often observed in the field (Chan et al. 2017). 2. To understand the physical mechanisms of the interaction between rising air pockets and the vortex intake inflow in the vertical drop shaft (Achieved 80%) To address Objective 2, an experimental study is carried out to investigate the air-water interaction in a plunging drop shaft conveying water to an underground tunnel. Plunging intakes are chosen as they are compact and can entrain significant amounts of air. The physical model consists of a plunging intake, a drop shaft, a horizontal pipe (tunnel), an inflow tank and an outflow tank with a sealed air chamber. Experiments were carried out under various inflows to the plunging dropshaft. The depth-discharge relation of the approach channel flow is measured. The total entrained air flow rate in the dropshaft is measured using a sealed air chamber fitted with a 0.019 m diameter air vent and Pitot tube in the outflow tank. The length of air slug, and the pressure in various positions of the tunnel and dropshaft are also measured. Experimental observation shows that there exist three air-water flow regimes in the shaft. Under low flow condition (< 0.7 L/s), there is no net transport of entrained air into the tunnel as air bubbles rise back to the surface in the dropshaft. At flow greater than 0.7L/s and less than 2.5 L/s, air is stably entrained and transported to the tunnel. The entrained air flow rate is approximately linearly proportional to the discharge. Under higher water discharge (Qw > 2.5 L/s), instability and oscillating flow phenomenon of air from the shaft occurs at a period of around 8 seconds, resulting from the air pocket pressurization and the release of air pocket in the vertical shaft. The tunnel-dropshaft system model is also used to study the interaction between a rising air pocket and the inflow in a vertical drop shaft. Initially there is a constant inflow from the plunging drop shaft and air entrainment can be observed at the dropshaft. An air pocket is then introduced at the upstream by opening a gate valve; the air pocket travels downstream as a gravity current and rise up at the dropshaft. An ejection of air-water mixture is observed at the dropshaft and causes back flow in the approach channel of the dropshaft. The dynamics of air pocket in a vertical shaft with downward flow is measured using high speed camera. 3. To obtain original velocity and pressure data on hydraulic surges in the drop shaft – tunnel system for validation of numerical models. (Achieved 100%) The experiments cover a combination of parameters, including the riser diameter, pressure head and air pocket volume. For the first time, the movement of the air-water interface in the tunnel and in the vertical riser has been measured using high speed camera (100 fps) along with pressure variations at key points. The data is invaluable to understand the mechanism of geyser formation and used for the validation of three-dimensional CFD models (Chan et al. 2017).

16205114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205114.value: This research has provided invaluable original experimental data for understanding the dynamical behaviours of air pockets in a drainage tunnel and mechanism of geyser. Without an external pressure head, the air pocket migration in a water-filled vertical riser is found to be similar to a slug flow. The rising velocity of the air pocket relative to the free surface is nearly constant and close to the speed of a Taylor bubble; no geyser is observed. When an external pressure head is applied to the horizontal pipe, two types of flow are observed. For large riser diameter and small air volume, the rise of the air pocket in the vertical riser resembles a Taylor bubble, with an air pressure equal to the hydrostatic pressure of the water column above. The air breaks within the riser and no geyser is observed. For small riser diameter and large air volume, the horizontal air pocket shoots past the riser junction and only partially enters the shaft. The air pocket pressure is found to be significantly higher than the hydrostatic value, resulting in rapid acceleration of air and water, and jetting out of air-water mixture from the riser top. A theoretical model with experimental support shows that geysers are more likely to occur for small risers (riser to tunnel diameter ratio ≤ 0.62) and large air volumes. An unsteady three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is developed to simulate the pressure transients and air-water interactions by the release of trapped air from horizontal tunnel into a vertical riser. Model predictions of air-water interface in the vertical shaft are in good agreement with laboratory measurements. It is found that during a geyser event, compression of the air pocket in the riser can lead to rapid acceleration of the overlying water column and its expulsion from the rise. Comprehensive numerical modeling on the effect of vertical shaft diameter, upstream pressure head and the air pocket volume shows that geyser formation is mainly controlled by the riser to tunnel diameter ratio. 3D CFD simulations have also been carried out for an idealized prototype drainage system. It is shown that the geyser behavior can be characterized by extremely large vertical air velocities that result in dispersed air-water mixtures often observed in the field. The research outcome has been published as two papers (Cong et al. 2017; Chan et al. 2017) in top international peer-reviewed journals and one paper (Chan et al. 2017) in conference proceedings of hydraulic engineering research. One post-graduate research student is trained and graduated under the project.

16205114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205114.value: The findings of this study has laid the foundation for further research on the air-water interaction in tunnel-dropshaft system and the formation of geysers. Several potential research questions to be addressed are: 1) The effect of a series of air pockets or continuous air injection on the mechanism of geyser. It is observed in the field that geysers are formed intermittently, suggesting the role of continuous air input to the system. The present experimental set-up can be modified for continuous injection of air from a compressed air source. 2) In the present experiments, there is no net flow in the tunnel. The dynamics of air pocket in a tunnel with a net flow will be studied in the future. In particular, it would be profitable to study the interaction between the inflow from a scroll vortex dropshaft and a rising air pocket in a larger scale model. 3) To estimate the size of air pocket, it is important to characterize the entrainment of air from the drop shaft of vortex and plunging intakes to the tunnel under various flow conditions. Detailed air entrainment rate and air concentration measurements are required for comparison with numerical models. 4) Although a 3D CFD approach is used successfully to elucidate the mechanism of geyser, the use of a 3D model requires extensive computational effort and is not well-suited for evaluating prototype scenarios. A one-dimensional model with numerical shock-capturing scheme can be developed to model the air-water interaction in a surcharged drainage tunnel for prototype scenario assessment. This serves as a useful supplement to the 3D calculations and to assist problem formulation and interpretation of the laboratory experiments.

16205114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205114.value: Geysers are explosive eruptions of air-water mixture from manholes in drainage systems. When the design capacity of storm water drainage systems is exceeded during heavy rainfall, rapid inflows can lead to air-water interactions that give rise to geysers, causing damages and threatening human lives. Experiments have been performed on a simplified drainage system consisting of a vertical riser and a horizontal tunnel. An air pocket is introduced into the system filled with water. The motion of air pocket in the horizontal tunnel and the vertical riser is recorded using high speed camera and the pressure variations are measured. It is found that with independent pressure on the tunnel, a geyser can be formed for small riser to tunnel diameter ratio and large air volume. The air pocket pressure is significantly higher than the hydrostatic pressure of the overlying water column, resulting in rapid acceleration of air and water, and jetting out of air-water mixture from the riser top. Numerical simulations show that the geyser is characterized by large vertical air velocities that result in dispersed air-water mixtures often observed in the field. The mechanism of geyser formation is elucidated by experiments and theory for the first time. The findings will benefit the design of drainage systems.

16205314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205314.value: This project proposes to fabricate and characterize low-cost Nano Spike Electroporation (EP) devices for DNA transfer in microfluidic systems at ultralow voltage. Electroporation (EP) is one of the important techniques for the introduction of molecules, genes and drugs to cells in medicine and biotechnology. In comparison with mechanical methods (particle bombardment, micro needles, etc.), viral vector-mediated methods and chemical methods (calcium phosphate, etc.), EP can have higher DNA transfer efficiency for many different cell types. Recently, EP has been applied to electroporation therapy for treatment of head and neck cancer and to gene therapy. However, the delivery efficiency of DNA molecules is still a series issue. Although conventional EP systems have good EP efficiency, applying high voltage in these systems usually causes high mortality of cells. To date, many micro EP chips demonstrate high efficiency and cell viability. However, these micro chips still suffer from low reliability issues due to undesirable electrolysis. Therefore, we propose to fabricate low-cost Nano Spike EP devices consisting of a microfluidic channel and a pair of electrodes with an array of nano spikes using nanoimprint lithography, electrochemical anodization and MEMS technology. These devices can realize ultra-low voltage EP under pulsed RF electric field, much lower than micro EP chips with high cell viability without electrolysis. Moreover, the digital function generator and fluorescence detection system will enable high-speed optimization of electroporation protocols. Different types of molecules, such as plasmid DNA molecules and reporter genes, will be delivered into different cells on the Nano Spike EP devices under different pulsed electroporation protocols to achieve ultralow applied voltage. A basic condition for the success of such fabrication technology is an application with a very large demand. Electroporation has a wide range of applications in drug delivery and gene therapy in Hong Kong SAR and China. 本研究計畫研制一新型低成本低電壓納米釘電穿孔細胞芯片，主要用於高性能微流控系統。在生命科學及醫學領域中，電穿孔（Electroporation）是一種基因轉殖和藥物導入細胞的重要技術之一。與機械方法（基因槍轟擊技術，微針等），病毒載體方法和化學方法（磷酸鈣等）比較，對許多不同類型的細胞而言，微電穿孔芯片技術已能達到相當高的電穿孔效率。然而，許多微電穿孔芯片因為微電極附近產生的電化學及電解反應，仍有低可靠性的問題。因此，本研究計畫提出研製一低成本的納米釘電穿孔芯片:包括一微流控管道，一對納米釘結構的電極。納米釘結構電極擬使用納米加工技術，電化學陽極氧化和MEMS技術來製作。因納米釘附近局部電場放大作用，納米釘電穿孔細胞芯片可以實現超低電壓電穿孔。比微電穿孔細胞芯片，可達到較高的電穿孔效率及高細胞存活率，並且大幅減少電化學及電解反應。預期本研究計畫所研制的納米釘電穿孔細胞芯片技術將可有效的運用在藥物輸送和基因治療研究。

16205314.label: Realisation of objectives
16205314.value: All three objectives have been successfully achieved. 1. We successfully used low-cost commercial Al foils to fabricate an array of 3D nano-spike electroporation (EP) chips using nano-imprint technology and in-house-developed electrochemical anodization and etching (see the published papers for detailed info). 2. We developed the digital fluorescence microscopy setup using Olympus IX70 epi-fluorescence microscope and QImaging CCD camera. It has been used for the testing of the membrane permeability and cell viability study under different RF pulsed electric field on nano-spike EP devices (see the published papers for detailed info). 3. To improve the EP efficiency and cell viability, we applied feedback system control (FSC) scheme with 11 combinations and achieve the ultra-low-voltage EP for HeLa cells with high EP efficiency of (90%+-5%) and applied voltage of 1 volts pulse durations of 6ms and pulse number of 10. This FSC method can save more than 80% of R&D time (5.5 hours) in comparison with the conventional methods (32 hours). With the ultra-low-voltage nano-spike EP chip, we also developed smartphone-based portable electroporator system, “Electroporation Lab on Smartphone,” for nano EP chips (see the published papers for detailed info).

16205314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205314.value: We successfully used low-cost commercial Al foils to fabricate an array of 3D nano-spike electroporation (EP) chips using nano-imprint technology and in-house-developed electrochemical anodization and etching. To improve the EP efficiency and cell viability, we applied feedback system control (FSC) scheme with 11 combinations and achieve the ultra-low-voltage EP for HeLa cells with high EP efficiency of (90%+-5%) and applied voltage of 1 volts pulse durations of 6ms and pulse number of 10. This FSC method can save more than 80% of R&D time (5.5 hours) in comparison with the conventional methods (32 hours). With the ultra-low-voltage nano-spike EP chip, we also developed smartphone-based portable electroporator system, “Electroporation Lab on Smartphone,” for nano EP chips. An android application on a smartphone with a Bluetooth module and a library with different electroporation protocols, such as amplitude, duration, duty cycle and number of pulses is developed to control an Arduino MCU electric pulse generator. In addition, we applied 3D nano-spike chip to new biotechnologies. A low-cost label-free nano-spike Bio-Impedance Sensor (nBIS) has been developed for detection and phenotyping of cancer/non-cancer cells (HeLa, MCF7 and HEK293) with the limit of detection (LOD) of 10 cells/mL. The normalized charge transfer resistance, Rct, (20-30% difference among different cells) was shown to be a promising electric biomarker for cancer cell detection and phenotyping. A nano-spike electric protein extraction (NS-EPEx) chip for highly energy-efficient protein extraction from mammalian cells. For the same protein yield, NS-EPEx chip can be operated at applied voltages of 4V and save energy by 2~3 orders of magnitude (0.12kJ/kg) as compared to the other methods (10~1,000 kJ/kg). We also developed nano-spike electric cell lysing (NSP-ECL) chips with excellent cell lysis efficiencies ηl ysis (ca 100%) at low applied voltages (2 V), 2∼3 orders of magnitude lower than that of conventional systems. The energy consumption of NSP-ECL chips was 0.5-2 mJ/mL, 3∼9 orders of magnitude lower as compared with the other methods (5J/mL-540kJ/mL).
