16205414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205414.value: Pseudo-ductile cementitious composites (PDCC) are fiber reinforced cement-based materials which exhibit strain hardening behavior up to a high tensile strain, accompanied by the formation of multiple fine cracks with small openings. Various experimental studies have indicated that the application of PDCC in structural elements can significantly improve the mechanical performance. By limiting the opening of cracks, durability can also be enhanced. Despite the effectiveness of the material, its widespread use is limited by the high cost, which is governed by the fiber. In current practice, PDCC is designed to exhibit pseudo-ductility under direct tension, and the required fiber volume fraction is around 2%. In most practical applications, concrete members are under bending or combined bending and axial force. It is well known that material exhibiting tension softening behavior under uniform tension may show hardening behavior under bending. There is hence an opportunity to reduce the amount of fibers in cementitious composites, while still maintaining strain hardening behavior in structural components. A comprehensive theory for predicting the ductility of members made with softening fiber composites is not yet available. In this proposal, theoretical and experimental investigations will be conducted to establish and verify a scientific approach for determining the crack spacing and mechanical behavior of members under bending, combined bending/compression or drying shrinkage. The research tasks include (i) systematic testing on beams of different sizes made with various fiber contents in order to study the change of crack spacing and member ductility under pure bending, (ii) measuring the fiber/matrix interfacial parameters and bridging stress vs crack opening relations for cementitious composites with various fiber contents, (iii) based on the results of (ii), perform numerical analysis with a combined continuum/micromechanics approach to compute the crack spacing and deformation behavior of beams tested in (i), (iv) comparing the numerical and experimental results for verification/refinement of the theoretical approach, (v) using the approach in (iii) to simulate the behavior of fiber reinforced composite members under combined bending and compression, or subjected to restrained drying shrinkage , and (vi) experimental testing of members simulated in (v) to verify the predictions. By establishing an approach for predicting load vs deformation and shrinkage behavior under practical conditions, structural components with high performance/cost can be designed using softening fiber reinforced cementitious composites with relatively low fiber content. The results will facilitate the wider use of fiber reinforced cementitious composites to build safer and more durable structures. 虚延性水泥基复合材料（PDCC）是一种具备应变硬化行为和高拉伸应变的水泥基材料，其多次开裂性能有效控制裂缝的开张。各种实验研究已经表明，PDCC的应用可以显著改善结构的机械性能。通过限制裂缝的开张，耐久性也得以提高。尽管该材料具备良好性能，它的广泛使用却受制于纤维的高成本。在当前的材料设计中，PDCC需在直接拉伸下呈现虚延展性，所需的纤维体积含量是2％左右。在大多数实际应用中，混凝土构件承受弯曲作用或合并的弯曲和轴向拉力。在这些情况下，在直接拉伸下出现软化的材料也能显示弯曲硬化的行为，因而有机会减少在水泥基材料中的纤维量，同时让结构部件仍然保持应变硬化行为。要达到以上目的，需建立能预测软化复合材料结构延展性的全面理论。在本提案中，理论和实验研究将同时进行，以建立和验证一个能确定构件在不同受力情况下裂缝间距和机械行为的科学方法。本研究的任务包括（一）研究不同尺寸和不同纤维含量的梁，在纯弯曲实验中裂纹间距和构件延展性的变化（二）测定纤维/水泥基体的界面参数和含不同纤维量的复合材料中桥连力与裂缝宽度的关系，（三）根据（二）的结果，采用结合了连续与细观力学的方法计算在（一）中测试的梁的裂缝间距和变形行为，（四）比较数值模拟和实验结果，对理论方法进行验证/细化，（五）用（三）中的计算方法，模拟纤维增强复合构件在弯曲和压缩共同作用下或干燥收缩受到约束时的行为，和（六）通过实验检测在（五）中模拟的构件来验证预测。通过建立能在实际情况下预测变形和收缩行为的方法，可以利用含较低纤维量的软化水泥基复合材料设计具有高性价比的结构部件。研究结果将有助于更广泛地使用纤维增强水泥基复合材料打造更安全，更耐用的结构。

16205414.label: Realisation of objectives
16205414.value: All four objectives have been fully achieved. The first objective is on the measurement of load versus displacement relation and monitoring of cracking in steel fiber reinforced concrete beams with different fiber volume fractions. Three sets of specimens of 150x100x1000mm in size, were made with 1%, 1.5% and 2.0% of steel fiber respectively. Then, with the steel fiber volume fraction fixed at 1.5%, two additional sets of specimens, 100x100x700mm in size and 200x100x1500mm in size, were prepared to study the size effect. These specimens were cured for 28 days before testing. The monitoring of crack development during the test is a major aspect of the study. In these tests, the crack number and spacing were observed by eye from photographs taken during the tests. Moreover, acoustic emission sensors were placed on the specimen surface so the location of any newly formed crack (which releases energy and therefore acts as an acoustic source) could be determined from the difference in signal arrival times at the sensors. To perform such measurements accurately, we have developed (i) a new algorithm for detecting the arrival time of the AE signal, and (ii) a novel nonlinear framework for determining the source of the AE event. With these new approaches, the formation and propagation of cracks can be more accurately captured, especially when cracking occurs inside the specimen first and then propagate to the surface. For the second objective, the tension-softening relations of the three kinds of fiber reinforced concrete (with different fiber contents) have been obtained through an inverse analysis method. Beams with a notch at the bottom were tested in three-point testing, with the loading point right above the notch. During the test, the applied load and crack mouth opening displacement (CMOD) at the bottom of the notch were continuously monitored. From the load versus CMOD plot, the tensile strength was first identified from the end point of the initial linear part. The softening curve was then taken to be a multilinear relation, with the slope and extent of each subsequent branch obtained from the fitting of the post-cracking nonlinear load versus CMOD behavior. For the purpose of predicting the cracking process, it is not necessary to obtain the full tension-softening curve up to a crack opening of several centimeters when all the fibers would be pulled out from the matrix. In our case, the softening behavior up to 5 mm crack opening was obtained. The original objective also includes the determination of fiber/matrix interface properties for the modeling approach described in the proposal. However, as shown in the paragraph below, we have developed alternative approaches for crack spacing determination which only requires the tension-softening curve for composite exhibiting softening behavior or the complete tensile stress versus strain behavior for composite exhibiting hardening behavior. The determination of interfacial properties is hence no longer necessary. For the third objective, to determine the crack spacing in fiber reinforced cementitious composites, two separate approaches have been developed for composites with different behavior. For tension-softening composites, the crack spacing during the evolution of multiple cracking in a beam member is predicted with a minimum energy based approach. For a given moment applied over a region of the beam, the energy per unit length of the member as a function of crack spacing is calculated by the finite element method. The pattern corresponding to minimum energy is taken to be the one most likely to occur. In the analysis, the fracture behavior of the quasi-brittle material is simulated by a bilinear or linear tension-softening law. With appropriate normalization, the key parameters controlling crack spacing can be found and their effects on the multiple cracking process have been systematically studied. For strain hardening composites, an effective truss and interface model has been developed for finite element analysis. In this model, the bridging stress from all the fibers is represented by an equivalent truss element that is connected to a continuum matrix element through an interface element carrying pure shear. The functional form for the stress versus strain relation of the truss element follows the stress versus displacement expression derived from micromechanics. Its maximum stress is determined from the ultimate strength of the composite, while strain is obtained by dividing displacement with a fictitious length derived from the ultimate strain. For the matrix element, its strength is equal to the first cracking strength of the composite, while the post-peak bridging behavior includes that from the matrix (obtained from the fracture energy assuming linear softening) and that from the direct transfer of fiber stress at the crack surface, assuming the presence of a pulley at the exit point of each inclined fiber, as in the widely adopted snubbing friction model. The ‘pulley’ component is of the same form as the truss stress. The interface element is first assumed to be transferring constant friction, with its value derived from the average crack spacing measured at ultimate load. Based on this constant value, interfacial softening/hardening is incorporated to obtain better fitting of the measured crack opening versus strain relation. For the steel fiber reinforced concrete beams tested in this project, the measured crack spacing has been compared to that predicted from the minimum energy approach. In the analysis, the measured tensile-softening curve was fitted with a trilinear function. For the same material composition, there is a relatively large variation in the test results on both crack spacing and softening behavior. The crack spacing analysis was therefore performed for several softening curves within the variation of test data. The range of determined crack spacing was found to be overlapping significantly with the experimental values. In addition, the theoretical approach has been employed to predict the crack spacing for fiber reinforced beams in the literature, and good agreement can be obtained. The truss and interface model was verified with data from a study in the literature, which reported (i) the direct stress versus strain relation and crack spacing at ultimate load for a strain hardening fiber reinforced cement-based composite, and (ii) the crack spacing at failure of a beam made of the same material. With the material parameters of the truss and interface model obtained from the tensile test data, the predicted crack spacing under flexural loading was found to be in agreement with test results For the fourth objective, steel fiber reinforced concrete members with the same composition as those tested before were prepared and wet cured for 7 days. The specimens were then transferred to a room kept at 27 oC and 50% humidity. Half of the specimens were sealed on the side surfaces and the bottom surface was glued to the top of a steel member, so shrinkage was restrained. Crack development was monitored over time. The other specimens were sealed on all sides except the upper surface and free shrinkage over its depth was measured with strain gauges. Knowing the free shrinkage and the geometric dimensions, finite element analysis was performed to find the energy corresponding to various crack spacing along the member. The crack spacing for minimum energy was compared to measured results. Reasonable agreement was achieved, with the trend of test results correctly predicted, though the value of predicted crack spacing was consistently below the measured value.

16205414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205414.value: The accuracy of acoustic emission technique in locating cracks relies on the proper determination of wave arrival time. Conventional arrival detection techniques only work well for waves with high signal to noise ratio (SNR). A new detection method based on the power characteristics of the AE wave has been developed. The method was verified both experimentally, by comparing the detection accuracy with visual inspection on a test record (which is considered the most accurate but highly tedious), and theoretically, by assessing its detection accuracy when noise of different levels is superposed on a simulated wave. The method is found to be more accurate than existing approaches in the literature, particular when the SNR is low. The development of the method and the results can be found in paper 1 of the journal list. Knowing the wave arrival time, an algorithm is required to find the wave source. While existing algorithms are based on the assumption of homogeneous material properties, cracking in fiber reinforced materials results in heterogeneity and local variations in wave velocity. A new iterative algorithm which can account for error in the wave velocity has been developed. Using simulated wave sources and arrival times at various sensors (with error artificially introduced), the new algorithm was found to detect the wave source with higher accuracy than existing approaches. The crack path obtained for a tested beam member was also in good agreement with visual observation. Details are found in paper 2 of the journal list. An approach based on energy minimization has been developed to predict the crack spacing in a beam made with tension-softening material such as steel fiber reinforced concrete, when flexural loading is applied. Through a parametric study, the key factors affecting crack spacing are identified. The predicted crack spacing has been compared to test results and good agreement is achieved. The derivation of the approach and its verification are reported in paper 3 of the journal list. For fiber reinforced composites exhibiting hardening behavior, an effective truss and interface model has been developed to describe the crack bridging behavior and fiber/matrix stress transfer respectively. After obtaining the relevant parameters from the direct tensile stress versus strain curve and the crack spacing at ultimate strain, the model can be applied to predict crack spacing under general loading conditions. The model derivation, verification and application are reported in the fourth journal paper and the second conference paper.

16205414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205414.value: Among the various experimental and theoretical studies described above, the effective truss and interface element model has great potential for further development. This model, which can consider the transfer of stress from the fiber back to the matrix to induce further cracking, can be conveniently used in conventional finite element codes for determination of crack spacing and width in members under different loading conditions. In the present study, problems with relatively simple geometries have been studied so a finite element mesh with constant size can be used. Also, cracking only occurs along one direction in the studied problems. In the future, it is of interest to study situations with (i) highly non-uniform stress fields (such as that under a concentrated load) where different element sizes need to be employed, and (ii) cracking occurring in different directions (such as a rectangular plate under biaxial bending). Moreover, to extend the application of the modelling approach beyond monotonic quasi-static loading, cyclic and creep loading should be addressed. Under such conditions, ways to describe the constitutive behavior of the truss and interface elements, and approaches to extract the material parameters from relevant test results, need to be further studies.

16205414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205414.value: Concrete structures make up an enormous portion of the civil infrastructure around the world. To make infrastructure development more sustainable, it is important to enhance the durability of concrete structures, so the frequency of repair or reconstruction can be reduced. Concrete durability is significantly affected by cracking, as water and other chemicals can easily penetrate through the cracks to induce concrete degradation and corrosion of the steel reinforcements. Experimental research has shown that small cracks of opening below 0.05 mm have relatively little effect on water/chemical penetration and such small crack openings can be achieved by the incorporation of fiber reinforcements. Under a certain deformation (e.g., that corresponding to the service condition of the member), the crack opening is inversely proportional to the spacing of cracks. Under direct tension, theories are available for predicting the crack spacing. However, in most real-world situations, structural members are subject to bending effects. In this study, new theoretical approaches are developed for the derivation of crack spacing under more general loading conditions (e.g., beam under bending, concrete member under shrinkage restraint). With these models, the cracking condition under practical situations can be predicted for the durability design of concrete structures under various environmental conditions.

16205614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205614.value: 近年来，手机、平板电脑以及可穿戴设备在人们的生活中越来越普及，为机器人技术或机器人自动化解决方案在3C制造业中的应用带来了巨大的机会。目前， 3C制造业的范围和规模已经超越了传统机器人应用最多的行业：汽车行业。全球的３Ｃ制造业主要集中在中国，在中国的东海岸地区就拥有２０００万多的３Ｃ从业人员。相比之下，中国的汽车行业只有500万从业人员，生产全球２５％以上的汽车。在３Ｃ产业，目前机器人普及率为１１台机器人每一万劳动力，与汽车行业的普及率相比是非常低的，其中中国为１４５，日本和美国为１４５０。为了应对劳动力成本上升和劳动力短缺的矛盾，３Ｃ行业已经加大力度寻找并推广Ｃ制造的机器人解决方案。例如，具有业界领导地位的富士康公司，2012年启动了相关工程，旨在到2014年时为其工厂引入一百万台机器人。 3C制造的典型动作包括组装、测试及包装。与汽车行业的自动化相比，利用机器人将这些动作进行自动化面临着巨大的挑战：（1）在狭窄的空间中要对细小零件以及柔性零件进行操作；（2）精度要求从100微米提高到10至30微米；（3）系统搭建时间由一年缩短至2~4周；（4）投资回报期由三年缩短至一年以内。为了应对这些问题，我们要在设计及搭建3C机器人自动化工作站时进行全盘考虑，使系统其具备以下特点：（1）工作站由多个相互协作的机器人模块组成，各个模块实现类似人体的手臂、手腕、手指等等的不同功能；（2）每个模块仅具有所需最少的自由度，模块的运动类型互补、精度等级匹配，使工作站得以快速搭建、成本低廉、易于维护；（3）工作站内有相关辅助模块，如视觉/力传感器、工件供料机、夹具等，帮助自动化制造的过程。 3C装配与测试任务的精度要求很高，因此在设计机器人工作站时，如何给各个模块分配其相应的重复精度成为了一个重要的问题。这些模块往往具有不同的机械结构，且由不同的厂商提供。为了准确高效的评估各个模块及整个工作站的精度，在项目中我们将建立：（1）一个准确的机器人重复精度模型。这个模型需要适用于不同拓扑结构及运动类型的机器人，并且能够抓住影响精度的主要因素。（2）一个与模型相适应的精度评价指标，来表征3C组装、测试任务所需要的精度要求。（3）一个高效的估计算法，使我们能够在设计阶段初步评价模块化的机器人工作站的重复精度。

16205614.label: Realisation of objectives
16205614.value: Objective 1 A four-layers robot work cell model is developed to describe the topologies of all components in it, which is integrate into an offline programming system. By using the 3D virtual modeling technology, the work cell can be visualized at an early concept design stage. The four layers of the work cell is factory line, stations, mechanisms and basic units. All the components have their position and orientation information and their other properties. A factory line can include several stations and each station is relatively independent and connect by conveyors or other mechanisms to make sure the work pieces transferring from on to another. A station consists several mechanisms, each of them can complete a specific task. Basic units include fixtures, joints, links and tools. The four-layers robot work cell model gives the universal work cell description which simplify the design, analysis and verification steps. Objective 2 The calibration of a robot can be classified into 3 levels depending on the types of error modeled. In level-1 calibration, only joint errors are modeled; and level-2 calibration is also known as the kinematic calibration; and level-3 calibration is called a non-kinematic calibration, which models errors other than geometric defaults such as stiffness and temperature. In our work Level 1 and 2 is considered and develop the calibration algorithm using POE Theory with the Adjoint Error Model. The errors of kinematic parameter can be calibrated by measuring the complete pose or partial pose of the robot end-effector in a set of robot configurations. In practice, the choice of the measurement system becomes one of the most critical issues, since the choice of different measurement systems determines the efficiency and cost(both time and money) of a robot calibration process. A Wire Draw Encoder is developed based Measurement System which is low cost and portable measurement for Robot Calibration. As an interdisciplinary engineering challenge, the development of the Wire Draw Encoder based Measurement System involves many techniques such as electronic design, embedded system programming, precise mechanical design, real time communication protocol, error analysis, etc. Objective 3 Tool path accuracy is a key component to promote the overall performance of work cell. The tool path consists of discrete data points for most of the applications. An algorithm is designed by using the least squares global approximation and B-spline curve to fit the given tool path and giving assigned tolerances to limit the errors. Several algorithms are developed to evaluate the modular robot work cells. We developed a work piece localization algorithm applied in manufacturing process, this algorithm can reduce the time wasting in manual work piece localization process. We developed a work cell calibration algorithm which can be widely used in industry work cell. We test this evaluation algorithm for modular robot work cells that can accurately estimate the repeatability at an early concept design stage. We developed a compatible formulation for repeatability evaluation criteria that can faithfully represent the precision requirement of the intended 3C assembly/testing task. We developed an accurate repeatability model for robot modules and work cells with distinct topologies and motion types, which captures the main factors affecting their precision. We developed a work piece localization algorithm and use it in manufacturing process, this algorithm reduce time to a large extend and improve the efficiency. We developed a flexible grasping and fixturing algorithm for different kinds of work piece. In this work cell, we apply this grasping and fixturing algorithm in this automatic grasping and fixturing process. We developed a work piece pose estimation algorithm in our work cell which can be used for the pose estimation for the metal work pieces.

16205714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205714.value: 固體表面對流體的影響會使得納米通道中的流體流動同大尺度系統有很大的不同。在納米流體系統中,過小的尺度使得流體進入納米通道變得困難。實驗表明,將水壓人0.6-2 納米的碳納米管中需要50到300 兆帕的壓強。如此高的浸入壓不僅對納米流體系統本身是個威脅,對納米流體系統的實際應用也是個挑戰。 近期我們在納米通道流動的分子動力學模擬中發現溫度對納米通道的浸入壓有很奇特的影響。存在一個臨界溫度,當系統的溫度高於這個臨界溫度時,浸入壓會快速減小。這個臨界溫度與流固耦合力相關。然而,關於這個臨界溫度的具體的資訊還尚不清楚。為降低浸入壓從而促進納米流體系統的實際應用,大量的理論和實驗工作對溫度如何影響浸入壓是必要的。 在這個專案中,我們將用分子動力學模擬和實驗的方法研究溫度對納米通道浸入壓的影響,並尋找這個臨界溫度與其他參數的關係,如通道尺寸和通道表面的親疏水度。獲得的結果對納米流體系統的設計和應用將有重要意義。

16205714.label: Realisation of objectives
16205714.value: For objectives 1 and 2, we have performed extensive molecular dynamics simulations to compute the pressure needed to drive fluids (including water) into nanochannels of various surface properties and the critical temperatures. A paper about the infiltration pressure for nanochannels has been published in a prestigious journal. For objective 3, we have fabricated quite a few nanofluidic systems and measured the infiltration pressure under different surface conditions. Based on the experiments, we found an interesting phenomenon, which led to the design of moving-part free fluidic diodes. These fluidic diodes are the first diodes that can work under low Reynolds numbers for simple fluids. Therefore, all the objectives are achieved.

16205714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205714.value: The infiltration pressure of water for nanochannels have been studied through molecular dynamics simulations. It is found that the entrance energy barrier significantly raises the infiltration pressure, which makes the classic Young-Laplace equation invalid for nanochannels. As the channel surface is tuned from superhydrophobic to hydrophobic, the infiltration pressure is greatly reduced mainly due to the decrease of the capillary pressure (Young-Laplace equation) caused by the contact angle change, while the contribution of the entrance energy barrier to the infiltration pressure, which is termed entrance barrier pressure, increases from 25% to 60%. In addition to MD simulations, nanochannels are also fabricated and the infiltration pressures for different surface wettabilities (or contact angles) are obtained.

16205714.value: Based on the findings in this project, nanoscale fluidic diodes without moving parts can be fabricated for various applications, such as flow control in small scale chips and nanofluidic transistors. We are fabricating more devices to achieve further functions.

16205714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205714.value: The pressure needed to drive water into a nanochannel depends on the size and surface properties of the channel. This allows us to develop a fluidic diode without using moving part. In this project, we first studies the infiltration pressure for various nanochannels and then developed a nanofluidic device that can produce unidirectional water flows. Such a device could be easily integrated into lab-on-a-chip technologies for flow control.

16206014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206014.value: Heterogeneous multi-robot systems for hospital services (HeMRS) is about facilitating cooperation and situation awareness for both patients and medical personnels with multiple mobile robotic systems. Mobile robots are entering our daily lives. They have been providing services, such as guidance, courier, tele-presence, surveillance and autonomous transportation. However, not much progress has been reported about heterogeneous multi-robot systems working in large-scale dynamic environments, such as hospitals. We believe that amongst the main reasons is that a hybrid cognitive architecture (HCA) is lacking. Such an HCA ought to jointly consider the requirements from the target human users (patients, nurses and doctors) and robotic abilities. HeMRS operationalizes natural cooperation as balancing operational and cooperation demands in a hybrid cognitive architecture, which minimizes human cognitive and attentive task load and optimizes joint work flow in medical services. In HeMRS, heterogeneous robots serve patients and medical personnel in an intelligent and integrated manner. HeMRS designs the related HCA by closely coupling user models to how mobile robotics interacts with the environment. Hybrid robotic mapping, navigation and planning combine, provide efficient help to the operation of hospital service, and act as a modern healthcare system along with the complete medication process. HeMRS not only considers single robot function, or single type of data, but also a heterogeneous multi-robot system. The HCA bases planning and execution on a cognitive control model. User attention, characteristics of agent behaviors, and skill acquisition guide autonomous action execution in a cooperative context, by which all the human users and robots have efficient and sufficient interconnect and content awareness through dedicated modules. Besides, a data center is also deployed to assist the operation of the HCA. The cooperative pattern ensures behavior changes coherently system-wide. Overall, HeMRS focuses on cooperation in hospital environment and aids the medical activities. Medical personnel and multiple robots jointly serve patients in an adaptive active/passive manner. Several important modules are to be presented with a real-time integrated system, such as reliable courier service, call-response-based allocation of multiple robots, autonomous navigation, tele-presence of doctors and surveillance of environment. The results will play an important role in hospitals of Hong Kong in the near future. 用於醫院服務的多異構機器人系統（HeMRS）旨在利用多機器人系統增強醫患間的聯繫與情形理解。當今移動機器人正在逐漸進入人們的日常生活。他們可提供多種多樣的服務形式，如導航指引，運送服務，遠程會議與監控等等。然而，關於在大範圍動態環境中的實用多機器人系統鮮有報道，如醫院等動態環境。這是由多方面原因造成的，其中我們認爲最重要的就是高效的混雜的認知框架(HCA)尚未合理的建立。合理的HCA應該綜合考量用戶（如醫生、護士）的需求及機器人的相關配置和能力。HeMRS系統從HCA的角度提供自然的人機交互機制以平衡操作和合作的需要，從而人員可以以最少的認知和操作的負擔，與機器人合作，優化醫療服務質量。換言之，機器人將以更加智能的方式向醫患雙方提供高效而集成化的服務。 HeRMS將統一考慮用戶模型與移動機器人與環境的互動模型，定義進階的HCA。混雜的機器人建圖、導航與規劃系統，提供低成本並高效的機器人導航能力；作爲現代醫學服務系統的組成部分，服務於整個醫治過程。HeMRS不僅僅考慮單一機器人或單一種類數據類型的操作，而且將發揮不同種類異構機器人的特性。任務的規劃與執行將基於HCA模型，因此用戶的關注點，機器人的特性等將在統一的框架下進行整合。利用HCA提供的信息，工作人員可以更好的了解服務機器人的當前狀態，而多機器人系統也會通過HCA進行合理的系統級的自我規劃。一切數據的執行、發布和記錄將通過數據中心統一管理。這一合作模式保證了系統級別的行爲統一。 總之，HeMRS着眼於服務醫療環境中各個醫學行爲的合作與協作。各類醫護人員與多機器人系統有機的結合，相互補充。相關的重要模塊和科學問題將加以解決並通過實時的實驗示範進行驗證，如可靠的自主運送服務，機器人應召，多機器人分配，醫生的遠程再現等。 我們相信HeMRS系統將代表香港醫學服務的未來。

16206014.label: Realisation of objectives
16206014.value: We have finished all the previously defined research objectives. For each objective, the realization is described as follows: 1 Design of a hybrid cognitive architecture (HCA) for both human-robot interaction and cooperation, especially for multi-robot systems. The HCA will provide the ground for sharing common understandings of the environment among robots and human users. We proposed to use a hierarchical structure to realize the cognition of environment, with emphasis to human-robot interaction and cooperation. We have successfully combined convolutional neural network (CNN) with fully connected network, to realize human-like perception of the environment. The HCA is trained with input of depth images, and output from manual guidance in the training phase. Afterwards, the robot can move autonomously in the environment with the learned model. As for the experiments, we have tested the model in typical indoor office environments. The general result of decision making, comparing to human-decisions. The robot-decision is much alike to human-decision under the same situations. It can be further observed over the time series. We have also studies the data analysis of the high-dimensional feature map of the HCA. In order to demonstrate how the trained network functions as a artificial brain, we try to visualize the feature maps generated from the last layer of CNN. The second-last layer represents the feature maps, which are further categorized by the last fully connected layer. The outcome leads to the selection of control commands. However, it is not easy to visualize these feature maps. To solve this problem, we adopt a latent variable Gaussian Process model (GPLVM), more specifically, with Spike and Slab Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models (SSGPLVM). We project into a lower dimensional space for visualization of the learned model. 2 Design and implementation of a low-cost robotic navigation system for large-scale dynamic indoor environments. As mentioned in the proposal, this objective is the core of the project. It is conducted with massive work packages and new development. We have launched three sub-projects to come up with a hybrid solution to low-cost navigation, including: - TSLAM (Team SLAM): a multirobot SLAM system without knowing initial states. The overall schematics of TSLAM is shown in figure . It depicts the overall structure of a multi-robot navigation system with capabilities like co-localization and co-exploration of an unknown environment. Considering the low feature quality in camera images captured in real environment, we proposed a novel keypoint filtering algorithm to select the most suitable features for navigation. The selected keypoints are further processed for feature triangulation and co-localization. - 3D-TSLAM: a 3D point-cloud version of TSLAM. 3D-TSLAM is another pure visual solution to low-cost multi-robot mapping. It adopted the original LSD-SLAM and revised it to a multi-robot version. The 3D point-clouds are generated by stereo matching across consequence image frames. - VLC-based low-cost navigation: a visible-light-communication (VLC)-based localization and navigation system, which has an endpoint-cost within one US dollar. We propose to use visible lights as beacons for low-cost indoor localization. A number of modulated LED lights are adopted for localization besides illumination purpose. The proposed solution consists of two components: light signal decomposition and Bayesian localization. Specifically, a correlation-based method is used to decompose asynchronously mixed light signals to extract “fingerprints”. In the signal decomposition, no synchronization working conditions are required, which contributes to further cut down the overall cost of the system. Then a Gaussian Process (GP) is used to model the “fingerprints” distributions. Following the GP, a Bayesian localization framework is applied to increase the localization precision. We demonstrate our localization system by real-time experiments performed on a tablet PC in an indoor environment, achieving sub-meter accuracy which outperforms other existing low-cost indoor localization approaches such as RSSI-based approaches. - Navigation in dynamic environment: We solved the problem that dynamic objects in the environment may affect the map quality. A CRF-based method which fused ICP and clustering algorithms successfully registered and removed dynamic objects in the environment. 3 Design and implementation of an advanced tele-presence system, to enable remote communication among medical personal and patients. Regarding this objective, the core is a network server which enables remote access and video transmission. We have achieved this goal by a Nginx Server with HLS RTMP protocol. For the video client, we used a hardware terminal based on Hi3818C and OV9712. We novelly revised the firmware of the module, and enabled the communication of the terminal with the RTMP server based on Nginx. Online access capability and a front-end have also been established. It finally reached to 720P resolution 30fps transmission rate. We also tried to apply the tele-presence structure into a remote SLAM system, where the real-time video stream and inertial measurements were taken as input to a centralized SLAM server. It enables the development of low-cost visual navigation modules. 4 Design and development of an integrated prototype system to facilitate medical services in typical hospital environments. We have selected BIBA robot as the main platform to work on. It will be further extended with several other TurtleBot robots to form a team of service robots for HeMRS. We collaborate with local company B-free to further apply the developed navigation system to intelligent wheelchair. We used the integrated system to participate Cybathlon competition for disabled people. We finally won full score in the competition, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed framework. With the complete know-how and the real systems of multi-robot localization and mapping and low-cost navigation systems, we are still looking forward to a multi-robot service system applied to hospital services as an application demonstration or for further commercialization.

16206014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206014.value: There are several aspects to further develop in the research route: - Multi-robot collaborative task allocation. It can base on the existing findings of this project and be further extended with higher-level perception, i.e. from the navigation level to task level. Besides, resource allocation could also be considered with task allocation, since the server resource and network bandwidth are both limited. - Recognition of abnormal human behaviors or phenomenons. It is a practical need from hospital scenario, since various patients may encounter different needs or even in danger. The abnormal behaviors should be detected by the service robots and instant alerts to doctors could be triggered.

16206014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206014.value: The project completed the necessary know-how and prototype systems for a multi-agent service robot system, including navigation and low-cost localization system. The project is defined in the context of hospital service and could be easily extended to any location-based multi-purpose services. The localization system led to a major reward in AI in China. Besides, we developed a hybrid cognitive model, trying to understand human's intention using a deep-learning structure. The conducted results may lead to boost in not only robotics, but also analytic research or psychology.

16206114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206114.value: In light of energy crises and environmental concerns, electric vehicles (EVs) have been proposed as a possible solution to mitigate these problems. At present, however, EVs have not been widely adopted. In China, for example, EVs only constitute less than 0.01% of total new car sales. Other than pricing, limited driving range and a scarcity of charging facilities are critical issues inhibiting their widespread adoption. Some have alluded to the EV market as a chicken-and-egg phenomenon: without sufficient charging stations consumers would not switch to EVs, and without sufficient EVs private operators would not deploy sufficient charging stations. Perhaps the government has a role to play to break this standoff via implementing certain subsidy policies to jumpstart the market, with the subsidies to be justified by commensurate benefits to the environment. This proposal will study three stakeholders involved in the development of a sustainable EV market: drivers, charging infrastructure providers, and the government. By gaining a good understanding of the pertinent factors at work and their interactions, this project aims to identify showstoppers, and better yet, develop any needed subsidy policies over time to facilitate successful mass adoption of EVs. We propose first to develop vehicle and route choice models for EVs while accounting for their lifecycle, usage, and detour costs. Secondly, we will investigate the optimal deployment of charging stations over time. This will capture the interactions between drivers’ vehicle and route choices and the deployment of charging stations. More charging stations will encourage greater and faster EV adoption at the expense of a higher initial charging infrastructure cost. We will investigate whether and under what conditions win-win deployment schemes would exist, in which consumers will massively adopt EVs and charging infrastructure providers will enjoy reasonable profitability. Thirdly, we will analyze the need for and possible impact of subsidy policies to jumpstart the EV market, with the subsidizes to be phased out over time as the market gradually matures, in what we call an evolutionary deployment subsidy policy. This project will open up theoretically interesting, yet practically important issues in integrating EV adoption, optimal deployment of charging stations over time, and government subsidy policy to facilitate the emergence of a sustainable EV market and charging infrastructure. Throughout this study, we will use Hong Kong as a context to demonstrate this modeling framework.

16206114.label: Realisation of objectives
16206114.value: All three objectives have been achieved. 1. This project developed vehicle and route choice models via surveys to study the impacts of different purchase and operating costs on the propensity of drivers switching to EV. We subsequently calibrated these choice models using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE). 2. Based on the EV adoption and route choice models developed, we linked up with infrastructure network design models to study how best to deploy charging stations to promote EV adoption and its financial implications. 3. Based on the infrastructure network design models developed, we studied the need of subsidy to promote EV adoption and how such a scheme can be justified based on its impact on EV promotion. Such an understanding is important to answer the question: should government subsidize EV first or should government subsidize charging stations first?

The study lays a solid foundation, with tools and techniques developed, to analyze the development, which is very important to address the energy crises and environmental concerns.

16206214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206214.value: In recent years, several organic pollutants originating from anthropogenic chemicals, including pharmaceuticals, personal care products, pesticides and metabolites, have been found to persist in the environment, and have been observed to be capable of long-range transport, to bioaccumulate in human and animal tissues, to biomagnify in food chains, and to have potential significant impacts on human health and the environment. These pollutants are classified as “persistent organic pollutants (POPs)”, and are a subject of great concern within the scientific community due to their frequent detection in treated sewage, surface and groundwater and even drinking water. Many conventional technologies have been used for the removal of these compounds, including adsorption, biotechnology, chemical oxidation, etc. However, they usually suffer from one disadvantage or another such as incomplete removal, high consumption of chemical reagent, high treatment cost, and time-consuming. The TiO2-based photocatalytic process has shown great potential as a low-cost, environmentally friendly and sustainable treatment technology to remove POPs in sewage to overcome the shortcomings of the conventional technologies. At present, the main technical barriers that impede its commercialization remain the inefficient exploitation of visible light, low adsorption capacity for hydrophobic contaminants and post-recovery of the TiO2 particles after water treatment. Here we propose to design and synthesize a novel photocatalytic magnetic adsorbent particle that integrates the characteristics of (1) excellent visible-light photocatalytic activity, (2) high adsorption capacity, (3) high stability, and (4) magnetic separability based on TiO2 photocatalyst. Different approaches, including non-metal doping and surface modification, will be integrated to enhance the POP photodegradation performance of the photocatalytic magnetic adsorbent particle. Various instruments (e.g., SEM, TEM, BET, XRD and VSM) will be applied to characterize the physicochemical properties of the synthesized particle. The photocatalytic performance of the synthesized particle for POP degradation and the products after photodegradation will be investigated; and the mechanisms for the POP removal will be probed. In addition, the proposed project will develop a sewage treatment prototype for POP removal and particle recovery through photocatalytic degradation and magnetic separation. Experiments will be carried out to evaluate the prototype’s POP removal performance, particle recovery efficiency and the sustainability of the process. The results of this study will significantly improve our understanding of the process of photocatalytic degradation of POPs by TiO2-based particles and provide a valuable knowledge base for the application of photocatalytic, regenerable and magnetic particles for POP removal and particle recovery. 近年来，在环境中发现了几种有机污染物的持久存在，它们主要来源于人为的化学制品，包括药物，个人护理用品，农药和代谢物。这些有机污染物可进行长距离迁移，在人类和动物组织中生物累积并在食物链中产生生物放大作用，从而对人类健康和环境产生显著影响。这些污染物被归类为“持久性有机污染物（POPs）”，由于它们时常被检测出存在于处理过的污水，地表和地下水甚至是饮用水中，成为科学界十分关注的议题。用于去除这些化合物的传统技术包括吸附、生物技术和化学氧化等。但是它们通常具有以下缺点，例如去除不彻底，化学试剂消耗大，治理成本高，治理时间长等。与传统技术相比，TiO2基光催化过程作为一种低成本，环境友好的可持续治理技术在污水中的POPs去除中显现出巨大的潜能。但是当前阻碍此技术商业化的主要技术难题包括可见光的不充分利用，疏水性污染物的低吸附能力，以及水处理后TiO2颗粒的再复原。此课题的目标是设计合成一种新型的TiO2基光催化磁性吸附材料，它具有（1）优异的可见光光催化活性；（2）强吸附能力；（3）高稳定性；以及（4）可磁性分离特性。此外，非金属掺杂和表面修饰技术将用于提高此材料的POPs光催化降解性能。多种仪器包括SEM，TEM，BET，XRD和VSM将用于表征此合成材料的物理化学性质。我们将对此材料降解持久性有机污染物的光催化性能、光降解后的产物、以及POP去除机理进行深入研究。同时，我们将建立一个基于光催化降解和磁选技术的原型用于去除POP以及颗粒复原并将评估此原型的POP去除能力、颗粒的回收效率、以及处理过程的可持续性。研究结果将显著提高我们对TiO2基材料光催化降解持久性有机污染物过程的理解，并将为这种具有光催化、可再生的磁性材料用于降解POP以及颗粒复原提供宝贵的理论基础。

16206214.value: A visible-light-driven magnetically recoverable N-doped TiO2nanophotocatalyst was developed through fine-tuning the pertinent factors (calcination temperature, Fe3O4 loading, and nitrogen doping) involved during synthesis, to enhance the degradation of ibuprofen (IBU, which is classified as POP or PPCP). The average size of the fine-tuned magnetic nano-photocatalyst was 19 nm, while the specific surface area was 47 m2/g. Two types of visible light sources, i.e., LEDs and CFLs of similar irradiance, were employed for degradation of IBU. It was found that CFLs, with irradiance ∼320 W cm−2and peak emissive wavelength 543 nm, served as the better visible light source resulting in a photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 94%. Under visible light emitted by CFLs, degradation of 94% of IBU and 93% of BZP-3 within 5 h, while 71%degradation of CBZ in 9 h, was achieved. Moreover, the synthesized nano-photocatalyst exhibited superparamagnetic behavior, which enabled its successful magnetic separation of 95% efficiency from the solution. The recovered nano-photocatalyst can be recycled and reused to lower water treatment cost, and be more sustainable and environmentally friendly.

16206414.label: Project Objectives
16206414.value: Develop hybrid parallelization techniques for individual components in depth and in comparison. Specifically, object extraction, image subtraction, and object cross match tasks all have different computational characteristics: object extraction is memory access intensive and control complex, in that it extracts hundreds of thousands of raw objects from an image and iteratively performs local refinement on these raw objects; image subtraction is mostly computation intensive, since it solves matrix equations the pair of images under comparison; finally the cross match of objects is both computation and memory access intensive, where all objects in the two input tables are compared against each other. Therefore, we will propose suitable parallelization techniques for individual tasks based on their characteristics on the many-core CPU, on the GPU, or both, and compare these techniques to gain insight into their performance impact. Design and implement a holistic, parallel astronomical data processing system with many-core CPU and GPU parallelization. Recently, there has been some work on GPU-accelerated algorithms for small computation programs, e.g., graph component labeling. However, little work has been done on accelerating the entire workflow of online astronomic processing. Furthermore, as the three components in the processing pipeline are inter-related, we propose to streamline these tasks and integrate them tightly for a greater performance on heterogeneous processors. Study hardware and system support characteristics for astronomical data processing applications. The current many-core CPUs with co-processors as well as the GPUs are going through rapid development. As a representative Big Data science application workload, the processing pipeline of astronomical data is a great opportunity for us to study the support from the underlying CPU and GPU hardware as well as the runtime system, and the insights gained will be useful to future designs of many-core heterogeneous processors.

16206414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206414.value: Several new astronomy projects, including the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope (LSST) in the US, and the Ground-based Wide-Angle Cameras (GWAC) in China, are building either a single, large telescope or an array of smaller cameras to continuously observe a considerable portion of the sky. Once in operation, these instruments will produce observation images every few seconds. Furthermore, complex processing is required to catalog raw images online, and transient objects, such as stars that change positions or brightness, should be detected from the data instantly to enable timely follow-up observation. Consequently, accelerating the online processing of these data is crucial to meet the demands of these projects and to facilitate astronomic discoveries. There have been initial studies on utilizing commodity computer processors such as multicore CPUs (Central Processing Units) and GPUs (Graphics Processing Units) to parallelize computation on astronomical data. However, the pipeline processing of camera data during normal observations is complex, involving image processing, astrometry computation, and database operations. As a result, parallelizing this pipeline remains a challenging open problem, especially in a heterogeneous environment with both multicore CPUs and GPUs. Moreover, recent developments in heterogeneous processors, such as the Intel Phi co-processors for the CPU, and the dynamic scheduling capabilities in NVIDIA Kepler GPUs to involve multiple CPU cores, pose interesting opportunities to parallel computing. We propose Star Flow, an open-source software package that utilizes state-of-the-art many-core CPUs with their co-processors as well as GPUs to parallelize the processing pipeline of astronomical observation data. In Star Flow, we will tackle three major components in the processing pipeline: (1) source extraction, (2) image subtraction, and (3) cross match. In source extraction, the tabular attributes of hundreds of thousands of stars and galaxies are extracted from each observation image. Image subtraction and cross match are two alternatives of finding transient objects with the difference being whether the input are observation images or tabular data. To our best knowledge, Star Flow will be the first parallel software system utilizing both many-core CPUs and GPUs for the online processing of astronomic observation data. We expect to produce innovative algorithms for parallelizing complex computation tasks on heterogeneous processors. Our software will be put in public domain as well as be used by our collaborator, the National Astronomical Observatories of China (NAOC). Methodologies and insights gained from this project will be valuable to other Big Data applications, especially those in data-intensive sciences.

16206414.label: Realisation of objectives
16206414.value: We have realized the project to the full extent. Specifically, we have developed hybrid parallelization techniques for individual components (source extraction, image subtraction, and cross match) in depth and in comparison (Objective 1); designed and implemented a holistic parallel astronomical data processing system with both CPU and GPU parallelization (Objective 2); studied hardware and system support characteristics for astronomical data processing applications (Objective 3). We have published our papers in international conferences; our software artifacts have been used by our astronomer collaborators; a PhD student has graduated with her thesis work on the project.

16206414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206414.value: We find that (1) Image subtraction is highly data-parallel and computation intensive and therefore accelerating it on both the CPU and the GPU achieves the best performance; (2) object extraction goes through a sequence of data analysis steps each of which depends on the results from the previous step. Consequently, the most effective method is to transfer the input image to the GPU and parallelize all steps on the GPU; (3) cross-match is data-parallel and data-intensive. We utilize both the CPUs and the GPUs on a computer cluster to accelerate cross-match of large astronomic catalogs. Additionally, we find that on modern CPU-GPU clusters, utilizing the MPI programming interface with the InfiniBand network connection runs much faster than adopting state-of-the-art distributed computing platforms for cross-matching astronomic catalogs. Our findings were published in proceedings of international conferences in 2015 and 2016. The 2015 paper is on cross-matching big catalogs with an indexing method. The 2016 paper is on a multi-assignment single join method for cross-matching on CPU-GPU clusters. The PhD graduate Ms Xiaoying Jia's thesis was on accelerating cross-match of astronomic catalogs.

16206414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206414.value: Our cross-match algorithms work on two catalogs, which is the common case in astronomical data analysis. With the increase of astronomical databases, astronomers may want to examine more than two catalogs at once. One direction for further development is to extend our binary cross-match algorithms to handle multiple catalogs. Our method for such multi-way cross-match could be that we first design the access method of each individual catalog, then determine the matching order among the catalogs, and finally execute the match in order.

16206414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206414.value: Astronomical data are growing exponentially due to the new development of big astronomy observatory projects. However, the data processing speed lags behind the data generation. Furthermore, after cataloging the astronomic observation images into attribute tables, cross-matching these catalogs is also time-consuming. Therefore, we proposed to utilize modern computers consisting of both CPUs and GPUs to speed up astronomic data processing and cross-matching of astronomic catalogs. Our resulting software artifacts facilitate astronomers to make timely scientific discovery. Our methodologies are also useful to other researchers who work on accelerating data-intensive applications.

16206614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206614.value: Frequency synthesizers and oscillators are among the most critical components in any wireless or wired communication system, whose function is to generate local oscillator (LO) signals with sufficiently good purity over a required frequency tuning range. The signal purity is typically referred to and quantified as either phase noise, which is by definition the ratio between the power at the signal frequency and the noise power at a frequency offset away, or equivalently jitter, which is the deviation in time from the zero-crossing points. In wireless communications, if the phase noise is not good enough, the noise generated by mixing of the LO signal and RF unwanted signals (typically referred to as interferences or blockers) at the same frequency offset would fall in the same frequency band and significantly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the output. There exists a fundamental trade-off between the phase noise and other performance factors, including oscillation frequency, frequency tuning range, and power consumption. In particular, it can be shown that the phase noise can be improved by 6dB if the power is doubled. If the phase noise can be effectively cancelled, a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) or a synthesizer with bad phase noise but low power can be employed and combined with the phase noise cancellation to obtain overall system performance in terms of good phase noise and low power simultaneously. The objective of this proposed project is to develop an effective phase-noise cancellation technique for CMOS VCOs and synthesizers. The phase noise will be detected and fed back or fed forward for cancellation, which would effectively reduce and improve the overall phase noise. Based on the investigation and the system specifications, suitable system architecture will first be proposed for phase noise cancellation, from which building specifications will be derived and verified by behavioral simulations at the system level. After the block specifications are determined and verified, the critical building blocks, including the VCO core and the phase-noise detection and compensation circuitry, will be designed and fabricated. Finally, all the building blocks will be integrated and demonstrated with the proposed phase-noise cancellation technique for improved performance in the overall phase noise and power consumption.

16206614.label: Realisation of objectives
16206614.value: All the project objectives have been successfully achieved. More specifically, several novel system architecture for phase-noise cancellation were proposed, based on which several innovative circuit design techniques were developed, designed, fabricated, and measured. Finally, all required building blocks with proposed design techniques were integrated, and the proposed system architectures were experimentally demonstrated with state-of-the-art performance, which have not only contributed to advancement of the filed but also resulted in several publications in the flagship journals and conferences in the research area as further described and detailed in Section 6.

16206614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206614.value: • There exists a severe trade-off between the loop bandwidth and noise suppression in existing PLL architectures. A novel solution was proposed to eliminate the trade-off to achieve good noise suppression without affecting the bandwidth and thus other performance by cascading the PLL with a sub-sampling delay-locked loop (DLL). With the proposed techniques, a PLL was successfully designed, simulated, fabricated, measured, and demonstrated with 24dB noise suppression and state-of-the-art performance in terms of phase noise, jitter, and settling time. The work was published in the IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference in February 2016, which is the flagship conference in the area of radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFIC) design. • In parallel, another phase-noise cancellation technique utilizing a novel phase-averaging filtering technique capable of wide-band spur-and-phase-noise suppression was also proposed, designed, and demonstrated. A long delay line with feedback to a phase interpolator was employed to implement a deep notch to help filter both the phase noise and the spur. A PLL prototype achieved phase noise suppression of 20dB and integrated jitter reduction from 3.57ps to 1.48ps. The work was published in the IEEE Symposium on VLSI Circuits. • Finally, another novel solution for suppression of the spurious tones at the output of RF PLLs due to the component mismatches was proposed. An automatic calibration loop is embedded to measure the intrinsic mismatch errors and to feed forward for cancellation. Employing the proposed calibration technique, a PPL prototype demonstrating state-of-the-art performance was also presented in the IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference in February 2016.

16206714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206714.value: 連續密度隱馬爾可夫模型 (CDHMM) 在過去超過二十年一直是自動語音識別 (ASR) 的主導技術 。 HMM狀態通常使用高斯混合模型 (GMM) ，但使用人工神經網絡 (ANN) 的建議也已經提出了很久。在ANN-HMM混合框架下，一個神經網絡被用於估計HMM狀態的後驗概率，而在識別的時候，後驗概率會轉換為概率。ANN-HMM混合模型的框架在以前沒有成為主流的原因如下：（1）它的計算量很大; （2）它的非參數性使得它諸如在講者適應任務上難以修改其模型參數; （3）最重要的是，它的表現通常比不上GMM-HMM。但聲學建模技術已經在近幾年開始利用深度學習方法成功用深神經網絡 (DNN) 改變這個情況。DNN是一個簡單而有許多隱藏圖層的多層感知器 。雖然這個概念並不新鮮，但時它的受歡迎程度因著深信念網絡 (DBN) 快速前訓練算法的提出，令DNN可以很容易地建成而飆升。從那時起， 在語音識別，自然語言處理，以及計算機視覺的許多問題上，DNN已被證明優於很多其它最先進的方法。其結果是， 儘管DNN有很高的計算需求，通常必須使用圖形處理器 (GPU)，DNN以經被廣泛接受。 在這個研究項目中，首席研究員 (PI) 想把深度學習的概念延伸到多任務學習 (MTL) 上，使用MTL-DNNs來解決ASR的問題。多任務學習 (MTL) 是機器學習方法之一，旨在通過共同學習多個相關任務來共同提高學習任務的泛化性能。過去已經證明，如果多個相關的任務共享一些內部表示，然後通過一起學習，它們能彼此將知識傳授給對方 。從MTL學習得知的共用內部表示對處理未來 的數據會更好。當前的聲學模型學習方法試圖單從聲學特性學習音素模型 。但人類不是孤立地學口語，我們會利用其他與聲音相關的線索，例如字形，詞彙等等一起學習 。通過識別相關任務， PI認為可以利用MTL把音素模型學習得更好。MTL可以很容易通過人工神經網絡 (ANN) 來實現，而新的深度學習方法應該會帶來更好的結果。 這個研究項希望對找尋有助於語言發音學習的相關任務方面揭示新的可能 。其結果將進一步被利用來改進現有的語音識別技術。

16206714.label: Realisation of objectives
16206714.value: We had performed a thorough investigation into each of the proposed objectives. For objective #1, we had compared multi-condition training and multitask learning (MTL) for creating acoustic models for automatic speech recognition (ASR) of noisy speech using the smaller Aurora2 noisy digits corpus as well as the larger Aurora4 noisy WSJ corpus. If the two methods are compared without any additional pre-processing, multi-condition training was found to outperform multitask learning. During our investigation, other methods were also proposed to deal with noise robustness ASR. For example, noisy speech may be enhanced by denoising autoencoder and the denoised speech is used for acoustic modelling as usual to get better ASR performance. Qian et al. also proposed a multi-task joint learning of deep neural networks (DNNs) for robust ASR by integrating feature denoising and acoustic modelling in a joint training framework, and obtained very good result on Aurora4. We feel that these approaches are better in dealing with ASR of noisy speech. As a result, we did not pursue further in this objective. For objectives #2 and #3, we did a thorough literature review on the relatedness issue in MTL, and conclude that it is still not clear how to define “task relatedness” in a formal way for MTL training. On the other hand, we notice that most works only turn on one target in one task at a time. We are the first to propose that it should be better to turn on multiple targets from multiple tasks for an input during MTL training so that the relationships among the different tasks can be better modelled, and they also serve as the regularizers of each other during MTL training. We demonstrated the effectiveness of this approach in various tasks. For example, (a) ASR of low-resource languages with the use of universal phonemes; (b) acoustic modelling of distinct triphones by training the monophones simultaneously; (c) score calibration for noise-robust speaker verification by MTL of auxiliary information such as SNRs and speaker identities. For objective #4, we investigated different neural network (NN) architectures for acoustic modelling for ASR. They include stacked multi-layer perceptrons as in normal DNN, convolutional NN (CNN), recurrent NN (RNN) and its different variations such as long short-time memory (LSTM) and simple recurrent unit (SRU). We then proposed the new multiple-history RNN (MHRNN) to mitigate RNN training problem due to vanishing gradients and showed that MHLSTM performed better in TIMIT phoneme recognition and was more resilient to noisy alignments. We also investigated the use of maxout nonlinearity and data augmentation with CNNs and LSTMs in improving the performance of lipreading in the low-resource Ouluvs2 task. We also tested these architectures on two different tasks: speech recognition and speaker verification, and found that MTL works well even for simple DNNs. For objective #5, we evaluated MTL on TIMIT phoneme recognition, Wall Street Journal speech recognition, Switchboard conversational speech recognition and multilingual speech recognition. We found that MTL worked well for both small data (~1 hour of training speeches) as well as “big” data (~300 hour of training speeches).

16206714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206714.value: [ Below, CP=conference paper and JP=journal paper, when we refer our publications from Part C. ] Although there were attempt to formally define task relatedness, they usually made restrictive assumptions and might not apply in real-world problems. Instead, we established an important heuristic guideline for MTL: one should find a secondary task related to the primary task that can exploit extra information from its training data. For instance, in speech recognition, we had proposed learning the graphemes of the same language as the secondary task in phoneme modelling [CF2, JP1]. The grapheme learning task exploits extra information in the acoustic training data to learn implicit phone-to-grapheme mappings of the language. Then, if several low-resource languages are to be learned together, we proposed in [JP1] to derive a universal phone set (UPS) among the languages and use the UPS learning as an additional secondary task in the learning of the multi-lingual phonetic models. In [CP1], we showed that it is possible to train all ~64,000 distinct triphones in Switchboard by using a stacked DNN with the learning of monophones as the secondary task. In [JP2], we investigated MTL on a different task, namely score calibration for noise-robust speaker verification. There we proposed using the learning of SNR and speaker identity as the secondary tasks. We then investigated different neural network (NN) architectures for acoustic modelling for ASR. In [CP7], we proposed the new multiple-history RNN (MHRNN) to improve RNN training problem due to vanishing gradients and showed that MHLSTM performed better in TIMIT phoneme recognition and is more resilient to noisy alignments. In [CP8], we also investigated the use of maxout nonlinearity and data augmentation with CNNs and LSTMs in improving the performance of lipreading in the low-resource Ouluvs2 task. We believe that all these NNs may be combined with MTL to further improve their performance. We also showed in [CP4] that DNNs could be adapted effectively for creating acoustic models for the hearing-impaired. Similarly, in [CP6], we showed that document vectors could be derived by adapting an LSTM language model. Furthermore, we demonstrated how computation of DNNs could be greatly reduced in [CP5] by clustering the weight vectors in the output softmax layer. Again, we believe that these techniques can be combined with MTL training to further improve the performance of many speech-related tasks.

16206714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206714.value: In this project, we establish an important heuristic guideline for multitask learning (MTL): one should find a secondary task related to the primary task that can exploit extra information from its training data. We have demonstrated the effectiveness of MTL in various problems, namely, distinct triphone modelling, multilingual acoustic modelling, and score calibration for noise-robust speaker verification. We believe that MTL can be applied to many other problems. One kind of problems of particular interest may be those that involve several modalities. For example, audio-visual automatic speech recognition (AVASR) and sign-language recognition (SLR). The audio and visual modalities in AVASR were usually learned separately in the past and then they were fused together in AVASR. SLR involves movements of various parts of the body as well as facial expressions, which should be related. MTL can be effective in training models to solve these problems.

16206714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206714.value: Learning a single task well may not be easy. However, it turns out that it can be more effective to learn several “related” tasks together and each task can be learned better than if they are learned alone in a framework called multitask learning (MTL). In this project, we establish an important heuristic guideline for MTL: one should find a secondary task related to the primary task that can exploit extra information from its training data. For instance, in speech recognition, we may learn the graphemes of the same language as the secondary task in phoneme modelling. The grapheme learning task exploits extra information in the acoustic training data to learn implicit phone-to-grapheme mappings of the language. For learning low-resource languages, one may learn several low-resource languages together by first deriving a universal phone set (UPS) among the languages and use the UPS learning as an additional secondary task. One may also learn a large number of distinct triphones by learning the monophones as the secondary task. We also demonstrated that besides speech recognition, MTL can be applied to score calibration for noise-robust speaker verification.

16206814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206814.value: The latest developments of information technology and data analytics have enabled supply chains to operate with unprecedented flexibility. As a result, supply chain networks are now often operated with dynamic, instead of static, configurations. We propose to study the optimal supply chain design decisions under the possibility of such dynamic configurations. The setting of interest is one in which environmental factors such as demand are random, such that dynamic configurations deliver benefits by allowing inventory sharing under informational pooling. We consider the planning problem of locating distribution centers (DCs) to serve retailers at which demand is random. The DCs, subject to realized demand information and availability of stock, can dynamically share inventory and serve retailers in different network configurations. The key trade-off is the one between physical and informational pooling of inventory – the former of which requires centralization of stock at larger DCs while the latter does not. The key influence of this trade-off on network configurations is that, the former strategy encourages the location of larger, centralized DCs and the latter favors the opposite. When both strategies are used in a complementary manner, the overall effects on optimal location strategies are unclear. We propose to analytically and empirically study the optimal supply chain design strategies that balance this trade-off under different market conditions. 信息技術和數據分析的最新技術使供應鏈具有前所未有的靈活性。因此，現代供應鏈網絡必須以動態方法管理。本項目將研究這種動態配置下的最佳供應鏈設計。在動態配置下，以信息技術達至庫存共享可提高供應鏈應付難預測的需求變化。我們將研究零售商的配送中心規劃問題。受需求變化和庫存情況影響，動態庫存共享將對網絡配置有不同的影響。規劃的關鍵的權衡是庫存的共享方式 - 集中庫存適合配送網絡大型而集中的配送中心，而信息庫存共享則相反。在同時使用兩種策略下，最佳的網絡配置尚須研究。 我們將建立模型及使用數據進行 解析和實證研究，優化供應鏈設計的戰略，平衡不同市場條件下的這種權衡。

16206914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206914.value: Adaptive linear filtering is one of the most fundamental operations in all of statistical signal processing. Optimal solutions designed under various criteria have been known for decades, and these are employed ubiquitously in practice. The emergence of exciting new signal processing applications, however, is posing unprecedented novel challenges. These challenges arise since nearly all optimal linear filtering strategies require knowledge of a certain inverse covariance matrix, which in practice is estimated from training samples often using the traditional sample covariance estimator. This estimator performs very well in classical applications, for which the number of samples is typically orders of magnitude larger than the number of variables (or the filter size); however, for many emerging applications, the filter size may be very high and the number of available training samples may be quite constrained, in which case the classical estimation and filtering methods fail remarkably. Prominent examples include (i) multi-antenna communication receivers with large antenna arrays, which are currently revolutionizing the wireless industry, and (ii) high-frequency portfolio optimization, a topic drawing considerable attention in finance. Addressing this critical problem calls for a new paradigm in covariance estimation and linear filter design. To this end, a very promising solution has been proposed recently, based on the theory of large random matrices, yielding robust methods that can effectively mitigate finite sampling effects in high-dimensional filtering applications. Such methods, which work by applying carefully optimized linear or non-linear “shrinkage functions” to the eigenvalues of the traditional covariance estimators, have been shown to substantially outperform classical solutions and currently represent the state-of-the-art in high-dimensional covariance estimation and linear filter design. This approach, however, is very new, with existing solutions designed based on certain stationarity and independence assumptions which are often violated in practice, ultimately leading to jeopardized performance. Here we outline a plan for designing a novel class of covariance estimators and robust adaptive linear filters, relaxing critical assumptions that are present in the existing early contributions. We will leverage our strong backgrounds in the fields of random matrix theory and signal processing to design a linear-shrinkage and non-linear-shrinkage estimation and design framework that will be used subsequently to present novel linear filtering implementations for large multi-antenna multi-user communication receivers, as well as to design robust high-frequency portfolio optimization strategies. 自适应线性滤波是在所有统计信号处理中最重要的操作之一。多种在不同衡量标准下设计出的最优解决方案在几十年前就已提出，并在实际中被广泛应用。但是一些令人振奋的新兴数字信号处理应用给我们带来了前所未有的挑战。这是因为几乎所有最优线性滤波方案需要知道某个协方差矩阵的逆，而这个在实际中是从训练样本中估计出来的，并且通常使用的是传统的样本估计协方差。在传统的应用中，即样本的数量大于变量的个数（或者滤波器的规模）好几个数量级，这个估计方法有较高的准确度。但是，在很多新兴的应用中，滤波器的规模可能会非常大，并且训练样本的个数非常有限。在这种情况下，传统的估计和滤波方法的效果显著降低。典型的例子包括（i）带有大规模天线阵列的多天线通信接收机。这个目前正在给无线通信产业带来新一轮革命；（ii）高频投资组合优化。这是个在金融界引起广泛关注的课题。 解决这个重要的问题需要一个新的方法来进行协方差矩阵的估计和线性滤波的设计。到目前为止，建立在大型随机矩阵理论之上，一个非常有潜力的解决方案最近被提出。它能提供鲁棒的方法来有效的减小在高维滤波应用中有限样本的影响。这些方法的机制是将细致优化的线性或非线性“收缩函数”应用在传统估计的协方差矩阵的特征值上。 它们展现的效果显著的优于传统的方法，并且是目前在高维协方差估计和线性滤波器设计领域最前沿的方法。但是，这个方法非常的新，现有的设计方案都是建立在特定稳态和独立的假设下。这些假设通常违背了现实情况，最终会影响这个方法的效果。 这里我们大致描述一个设计一类新颖的协方差估计和鲁棒自适应线性滤波器的计划。它将放宽在现有早期成果中严格的假设。我们将利用我们在随机矩阵理论和信号处理方面坚实的背景来设计一个线性收缩和非线性收缩的估计方法。同时我们将设计一个框架，它将应用于提出一个新型线性滤波器给大规模多天线多用户通信的接收端，也可应用于设计鲁棒的高频投资组合优化策略。 、

16206914.label: Realisation of objectives
16206914.value: All key objectives have been successfully met. The project has produced numerous key contributions, and has led to 4 journal and 2 conference publications, all in leading IEEE journals or conference proceedings. Objective 1: "Design a novel high-dimensional linear filtering framework which is robust to non-stationarity effects" This first objective was addressed through a number of important contributions. A foundation was laid in our first journal contribution, Journal Paper 1, where we developed a framework to characterize the performance of a new class of robust linear filtering strategies based on applying a linear shrinkage adaptation to Tyler’s classical high dimensional robust covariance estimator. We established analytical machinery for describing the performance of such filtering structures under large-dimensional asymptotics using methods from the field of random matrices. Moreover, an optimal data-driven shrinkage approach was developed, which is directly applicable to beamforming in array processing applications, as well as portfolio design. This is a substantial contribution and laid the foundation for a broader theoretical development to embrace a wide class of data imperfections. This direction was further pursued in our subsequent journal paper contributions, Journal Papers 2 and 4 (also, Conference Paper [1]), where we presented an extended framework to embrace critical factors such as outliers and model mismatch. Specifically, our framework produced robust covariance estimation strategies (required for covariance-based linear filtering) under high-dimensional asymptotics. They accounted, for the first time, for the effect of spurious outlier samples, both with and without regularization. This led to novel insights into classical covariance estimation and linear filtering strategies that have been employed for over half a century. Finally, in Journal Paper 3, we developed a theoretical framework for embracing low-rank models, that are important in the context of robust adaptive filtering in array processing. Objective 2: "Investigate new linear filter implementations for multi-antenna wireless communication receivers" This objective was completely addressed, with core results presented in Journal Paper 3. Specifically, we exploited the analytical framework discussed in relation to Objective 1 to propose a new, optimized class of MVDR-beamforming solutions. These solutions were shown to significantly outperform existing state-of-the-art linear-filter receivers, in terms of output power, interference suppression, and beampattern. Remarkably, our solutions outperformed standard “diagonal loading” receiver structures, even when such structures were provided an “oracle” (but unobservable) loading parameter. Our proposed filtering methods provide a significant advance to the communications and array processing communities, which are interested in high-dimensional multi-antenna filtering strategies. Objective 3: "Investigate new linear filter implementations for high-frequency minimum-variance portfolio optimization" This objective was also completely addressed, with the core results reported in Journal Paper 1 and Conference Paper 2. Specifically, the linear filtering design framework proposed in Journal Paper 1 was successfully applied to yield novel portfolio designs based on a minimum risk principle. Such solutions were shown to perform exceptionally well compared with competing strategies on both simulated and real-world data sets, while operating with only very low computational complexity. One of the major attributes of the proposed solutions was the demonstrated robustness to non-stationarity effects, heavy-tail behavior and outliers in the data, which resulted in exceptional performance. Our proposed portfolio solutions were shown to outperform existing benchmark portfolio designs on simulated data, as well as on real stock-return data from the Hong Kong Hang Seng Index. We also presented solutions to deal with temporal correlations in a data driven way. Objective 4: "Derive new random-matrix theoretic properties and results to facilitate the design framework" This final objective was also extensively addressed. All of our main contributions involved the development of new results in high-dimensional random matrix theory. This involved two main branches. The first main branch involved the analysis of robust covariance estimation methods, which are defined as the solutions to stochastic matrix-valued fixed-point equations. Novel random matrix results were proposed in Journal Papers 1, 2, and 4, and Conference Paper 1. As an example, the technical developments in Journal Paper 1 required characterizing the asymptotic stochastic properties of certain quadratic forms involving robust shrinkage covariance estimators, for which prior results were not available in the literature. Advanced analytical methods were proposed to address such problems, and these are outlined in detail in the appendix of the journal contribution. A similar comment applies for Journal Papers 2 and 4, where novel random matrix results were presented for certain quadratic forms involving robust covariance estimation schemes (and their regularized versions) with outlier data samples, which previously had not been studied. Once again, the appendices in these papers provide the technical details of random matrix contributions. The second main branch involved developing random matrix theories to described linear filtering strategies for low-rank models (referred to as “spiked” models). This required a very different set of analytical tools, and the results were presented in Journal Paper 3 and Conference Paper 2.
