16206914.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206914.value: Below is a brief summary of some of the major contributions in this project: [Journal Paper 1 and Conference Paper 2]: These contributions proposed new financial portfolio design strategies, considering a minimum risk criterion. The significance of these contributions is that they gave optimized solutions for large portfolio scenarios, for which the number of available market returns is typically of similar order to the number of assets. This was achieved by developing and exploiting advanced technical results from the field of random matrix theory. Our solutions not only accounted for high-dimensionality of the portfolios, but also for outlier and heavy-tailed effects (a common feature of financial data sets), as well as inherent low-rank covariance structure in the data. Our methods showed improved performance when compared with competing portfolio designs, both on simulated time-series and real financial data sets. The proposed methods will be of interest to financial practitioners interested in automated portfolio solutions. [Journal Papers 2 and 4, and Conference Paper 1]: These contributions presented fundamental theory and algorithms for robust covariance estimation under high dimensions. Despite the fact that robust covariance estimators have been known for decades, their performance under high-dimensions was unclear, particularly when the data is corrupted by outliers (i.e., precisely the case when they are most needed!). We presented the first analysis framework for describing the properties of a wide class of robust covariance estimators, accounting for outliers, and under various modeling assumptions. These results will be of interest to theoreticians and practitioners working with high-dimensional complex data sets, who require robust covariance estimation solutions. [Journal Paper 3]: This contribution proposed new MVDR-linear filtering strategies to be used in multi-antenna communication receivers or other array processing applications. For such applications, a distinguishing factor was that the signal model exhibited a low rank covariance structure in the received signals (assuming high-dimensional antenna arrays). This was exploited by again leveraging tools from high dimensional random matrix theory, and making connections to so-called “spiked” random matrix models. Our proposed filtering solutions were simple to implement and, remarkably, were shown to outperform the benchmark “diagonal loading” beamformer, even when it is fed the (unobservable) best loading parameter. Our proposed solutions will be of interest to communications and signal processing engineers.

16206914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206914.value: There are various avenues for further development. Here we briefly indicate a few of such directions. It would be interesting to conduct a second-order analysis of our proposed MVDR beamformers (i.e., deriving central limit theorems), which would provide insights into the fluctuations of the output SINR of the filters. In addition, our work has assumed that the Direction of Arrival (DoA) of the desired signal component is known. In numerous applications this is reasonable; however, in others it may need to be estimated, and estimation errors would lead to a performance degradation. An important challenge will be to quantify the effect of such errors on beamformer performance, and to extend our results to produce DoA-robust methods. While our main objective was to develop robust linear filtering strategies, with a focus on portfolio and multiple-antenna receiver design, the theory and covariance estimation tools developed in this project could be applied more broadly to study problems in machine learning and big data. An example, which we have been thinking carefully about, is the application of these tools to provide new robust classification solutions for Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA).

16206914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206914.value: The project has provided new mathematical theory and tools for performing linear filtering of complex high-dimensional data in a way that is robust to statistical errors and outliers. We have applied these methods to develop solutions for two filtering applications: (i) to design automated financial portfolios that seek to allocate resources to assets in a way as to minimize financial risk, and (ii) to design multi-antenna receiver structures that combine received signals to suppress interference. The excellent performance of our proposed solutions was demonstrated by benchmarking against competing strategies, through computer simulations and on real-world data. The methods and tools developed in this work may be useful more broadly for addressing problems in “big data” machine learning, which often involve extracting and interpreting information from complex, high-dimensional data sets.

16207014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207014.value: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) has been widely used as one of the key techniques in managing the power consumption of microprocessor. The basic idea of DVFS is to lower the supply voltage and clock frequency of the microprocessor when it is idling or having low computing activities in order to save power. During high computing activities, supply voltage and clock frequency of the microprocessor increase to boost up the computing power. DVFS technique needs a switching converter with a fast reference-tracking, which means the converter output voltage needs to change quickly with respect to the sudden change in its reference voltage. In order to further enhance the overall performance of the new generation of microprocessor for handheld portable devices, the increase and decrease of the power supply voltage for the future DVFS technique will be more frequent, more rapid and with a finer voltage steps. This poses a very stringent requirement for reference-tracking in switching converter design. In particular, one of the most important criteria in reference-tracking is not to allow any overshoot or undershoot of the output voltage during the fast reference-tracking operation. The overshoots or undershoots will degrade the reliability and performance of the microprocessor. This project involves the design of on-chip switching DC-DC converter for DFVS applications. Switching converter will be used as the DC-DC converter for the microprocessor as it will provide high efficiency (close to 95%) with various voltage and current ranges compared with other DC-DC converters such as linear regulator and charge pump circuit. Some existing switching converters have fast reference-tracking capability but with large overshoots and undershoots during the reference-tracking. In this project, switching converter with an accurate turn-on and turn-off sequence for DVFS applications will be developed to eliminate the overshoots and undershoots. 作為微處理器管理功率消耗的一種關鍵技術，動態電壓頻率調整（DVFS）技術被廣泛應用。DVFS的基本思路是在微處理器空閒或處理小規模運算時降低其電源電壓和時鐘頻率來節省功耗。在處理大規模運算時，將提高處理器的電源電壓和時鐘頻率來增大運算能力。DVFS技術需要一個具備快速跟隨參考電壓能力的開關式穩壓電源。這個穩壓電源需要在參考電壓突然跳變時迅速改變其輸出電壓。為了進一步提升新一代便攜式設備中微處理器的能力，未來的DVFS技術將會更頻繁，更快速，更精細地控制電源電壓。這給開關式穩壓電源的電壓跟隨技術提出了更加嚴格的要求。關鍵的是，在快速跟隨參考電壓的過程中，輸出電壓不能產生任何過衝或下衝，因為這些過衝或下衝會降低微處理器的性能和可靠性。這是此項技術最重要的標準之一。 該項目包含適用於DVFS應用的片上開關式穩壓電源。微處理器的DC-DC電源將採用開關式穩壓電源。因為與線性穩壓源和電荷泵穩壓源相比，開關式穩壓源在不同電壓和電流的的範圍都可以提供高效率（接近95%）。一些現有的開關式穩壓源具有快速跟隨的能力，但在跟隨時有大的過衝或下衝。這個項目將開發適用於DVFS應用的開關式穩壓源，使其具有精確的導通和關斷時序，從而消除過衝和下衝。

16207014.label: Realisation of objectives
16207014.value: This project is related to the development of a very fast-transient DC-DC converter for dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) applications. In order to allow the microprocessor to operate at fine-grained DVFS to save more energy, two issues need to be addressed. One is to make sure the converter can accurately turn on and turn off the power switches such that the output voltage reaches its final value without any overshoot or undershoot. Another issue is how to design a fast-response DC-DC converter such that it can quickly respond to changes in any system parameters during operation. These corresponds to the first two objectives of this project. For the first objective, a single on/off reference tracking mechanism has been developed which can much better control the turn-on/off of the power switches across a wide output voltage range. For objective 2, several methods have been investigated and implemented. In particular, a 3-level buck converter has been developed to operate at up to 50 MHz to provide a very fast response for DVFS application. Some of the ideas in objectives 1 and 2 are integrated to the switching converter design and two switching converters with fast reference-tracking response have been developed, implemented and characterized to complete objective 3 of this project.

16207014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207014.value: Several novel ideas and novel techniques have been developed in this project. Some of them are integrated in the final design of the fast-transient DC-DC converter for DVFS applications. First is the single on/off reference tracking using turning point prediction method. We found that the slope of the rate of change of output voltage is the highest at the time the converter turns-on/off the power switches. Therefore, the conventional method to estimate the turn-on/off time of the converter is not easily controlled. Small error in estimating the turn-on/off time will give large overshoot and undershoot at the output. We have developed a new turning point output voltage (TPOV) prediction method to predict the turn-on/off of the power switches by monitoring the output voltage instead. By doing so, the overshoot and undershoot voltages are greatly reduced. This idea is published in [conference paper 3] and the complete design was discussed in the [journal paper 4] which is under review. Since the transient response time highly depends on the switching frequency and the value of the inductor used in the design, we have developed a new figure-of merit (FOM) to determine how effective the turning prediction method is. This FOM is also discussed in [journal paper 4]. Delay-line-based voltage-to-duty-cycle control [journal paper 1] and 3-level buck converter topology [journal paper 2 and conference papers 1 & 2] have been studied to enhance the response time of the converter controller design. We found that 3-level converter can provide a much faster response time due to its 3-level topology. However, the voltage across the flying capacitor (V_c-fly) of the 3-level converter needs to be precisely controlled to prevent the malfunction of the converter. In this project, we have developed a real-time calibration method to control V_c-fly such that the 3-level converter can be completely implemented on-chip for fast DVFS applications [journal paper 3].

16207014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207014.value: In this project, turning point prediction method and 3-level converter with real-time calibration have been developed and they have achieved fast-transient response for DVFS applications with minimal overshoot and undershoot voltages. The converters can operate near to the ideal transient response time. Turning point prediction method is particularly good for determining the turn-on/off of the converter while 3-level converter is particularly good for high voltage applications due to its 3-level topology. We believe that some of our developed techniques can be applied to the design of the new generation of multi-core microprocessors with much higher power requirements.

16207014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207014.value: This project is related to the development of a very fast-transient DC-DC converter such that the output voltage of the converter can go up and down quickly to respond to the dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) requirements of the microprocessor. In this project we have developed several chips that can provide a fast-transient response. In addition, there are no significant overshoots and undershoots with a wide range of output voltages and currents. Outcomes of this project can lead to a much finer-grained DVFS operation to further reduce the power consumption of future microprocessors.

16207114.value: The growing popularity of wireless sensor networks has led to the ever-increasing volume of non-binary sensor data, which is the most natural representation of physical measurement, like distance, temperature, etc. In the existing bit-oriented layering approach to communication system design, the transformation from non-binary source to binary source (i.e., the source coding layer) and that from the binary source to modulation and coding (i.e., the channel coding layer) are implemented as two independent layers so as to facilitate divide-and-conquer. The modulation and coding scheme assumes that the input data are always streams of independent bits. Data are compressed and bit-interleaved to destroy their non-binary source nature, if any. Conventional wisdom says that bit-oriented layering is necessary because it significantly simplifies system design by avoiding the complicated joint source-channel coding issue. This project proposes a symbol-oriented layering approach to improve bandwidth/power efficiency of future wireless sensor networks by exploiting, rather than destroying, the non-binary nature of data. Our goal is to investigate how such advantages can be realized at an affordable complexity-performance tradeoff. 無線傳感器網絡的日益普及，導致不斷增加的非二進制傳感器的數據，這是物理測量的最自然的表示，像距離，溫度等。在現有的比特分層方法來設計通信系統，從非二進制源改造為二進制源（即源編碼層）和從該二進制源調製和編碼（即信道編碼層）被實現為兩個獨立層，以簡化設計。現有的調製和編碼方案假定輸入數據始終是獨立的比特流, 並以數據壓縮和比特交錯摧毀他們的非二進制源的性質。傳統觀念認為，比特分層是必要的，因為它避免複雜的聯合信源信道編碼的問題，簡化了系統的設計。本項目提出了一種符號分層的新方法通過利用而非常破壞數據的非二進制性質，以提高未來的無線傳感器網絡的帶寬/功率的效率。本項目的目標是調查如何能設計出符號分層的複雜性和性能的最佳能折衷方案从實現它的優勢。

16207114.label: Realisation of objectives
16207114.value: Under the modeling assumption of having a non-binary discrete memoryless source (e.g. resulting from an equiprobable scalar quantizer) and a discrete memoryless channel (e.g. resulting from an AWGN channel with a hard-decision demodulator), the stimulated annealing algorithm has been applied to find excellent index assignment (IA) mappings with near-optimal mean-square distortion for both M-PSK and M-PAM alphabets. In addition, we found that the natural M-ary code (NMC) construction can (recursively) reduce the M-symbol IA problem to a single-symbol version. The latter is equivalent to a certain traveling salesman problem with well-known graph-theoretic solutions. Though the NMC construction is proved to be suboptimal (unlike its optimal binary counterpart, the natural binary code), it is only marginally worse than the best mappings found by our extensive computer searches. Hence, Objective 1 has been realized with the above findings. To realize both Objectives 2 and 3, we addressed the key challenge of developing an accurate model of the visual MIMO channel, which is critical to the practical display-camera communication system and barcoding applications. With sufficiently accurate synchronization, we showed that the linear, nonlinear and spatial distortions inherent in the channel can be systematically estimated (with low training overhead) and compensated so that the visual MIMO channel can be converted into a (possibly signal-dependent) AWGN channel, which can be further converted into a discrete memoryless channel with a hard-decision demodulator. Some differential precoder, non-binary (up to 8-level) modulation and channel codes (e.g. Reed-Solomon code and low-density parity-check codes) as well as the corresponding efficient (near-optimal) decoding and detection algorithms have been developed to optimize the error probability performance of such a system. The aforementioned system optimization is made possible, thanks to the relatively tractability of our developed channel model. To meet Objective 4, the superior performance of some representative system combining the aforementioned results associated with Objectives 1 to 3 has been demonstrated in comparison with the baseline binary system.

16207114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207114.value: The proposed IA mapping is superior to that of the binary baseline only when the modulation alphabet M is larger than 2. The performance gain is achieved assuming that the knowledge of M is available to the receiver. A straightforward implementation of the proposed method thus requires the value of M to be made available in the packet header. Though the extra packet overhead is small, this requirement prevents the proposed method from being used in the existing communication systems since a packet format change would involve changing the communication standard. It is possible to develop a detector that jointly detects the value of M and the transmitted modulation signal. However, a straightforward implementation of such a detector may require a prohibitively high complexity. It is therefore of practical importance to develop a reduced-complexity version of it so that in case of transmitting non-binary data, the existing standardized systems can also benefit from the proposed method with minor additional complexity. Note that the proposed IA mapping can be easily implemented by table lookup.

16207114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207114.value: There is a recent dramatic growth in Internet of Things (IoT)-related applications in various areas such as healthcare, smart city, etc. Non-binary data resulting from analog-to-digital converters or quantizers may dominate the data traffic of such communication networks. The conventional bit-oriented layering approach adopts a source-channel separation approach that is straightforward to implement but is far from optimal. This project investigated a practical joint source-channel coding approach, called the non-binary index assignment, to enhance system performance/bandwidth/power efficiency by exploiting (instead of destroying) the non-binary nature of source data. We constructed a near-optimal non-binary index assignment mapping called the natural M-ary code, which generalizes both the optimal binary index assignment mapping (the natural binary code) in case of binary symmetric channels and the known single-symbol index assignment mappings in case of M-ary discrete memoryless channels. The proposed method can be implemented by table lookup. With further development of reduced-complexity detectors, it is possible to apply the proposed method to existing systems. A practical system demo on visual MIMO communications has been developed to confirm the benefits of the proposed method.

16207314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207314.value: The internet-of-things (IoT) promises the connection of machines, sensors and other objects to the internet so that they can become part of our information network. Wireless sensor networks, RFID and health monitoring can all loosely be considered examples of possible parts of an IoT. The IoT is predicted to bring a revolution in the way we monitor our health, environment and infrastructure and allow enhancements in efficiency, performance and services. There are many challenges in enabling this revolution and in this proposal we consider the issue of the power source for the devices or things in IoT. In many instances the devices will be portable and wireless and need battery power which has finite life and therefore needs to be replenished periodically. As the IoT expands and the need for much longer operation of the IoT devices increases, the number of batteries that need to be replaced will become prohibitive. Replacement may even be impossible in some inaccessible areas. To overcome this challenge, we are therefore proposing to harvest ambient RF energy using multiple antennas. The work is novel in that it can provide a continuous power source for sensors and devices for IoT by making use of ambient RF energy radiated from Wifi, cellular and other wireless access points and basestations. While the power collected will be low, combining ambient energy harvesting with the latest low power technologies and electronics can allow the development of standalone wireless devices that do not need batteries. One of the key elements in the proposed approach is using multiple antennas to collect the ambient energy. By combining the individual antenna elements after rectification and at dc, high gain, wide beam width rectifying antennas can be formed which will be able to collect ambient RF energy from a broad range of directions, increasing the collection capability of the harvesting. 物联网使机器、传感器以及其它的物件连接到因特网中，这样它们便成为我们信息网络的一部分。无线传感器网络、无线射频识别以及健康监测都可以被简单地认为是可能成为物联网一部分。可以预见，物联网将在我们监测健康、环境与基础设施的方式上带来一场革命，提高了效率、性能与服务。为了实现物联网，我们需要克服很多的挑战。在本次提案中，我们考虑物联网设备电源的问题。在很多例子中，设备都是无线与可移动的，并且它们的电池寿命有限，需要周期性地补充。随着物联网的拓展，物联网设备需要工作更长时间，从而使得需要更换的电池数量也急剧增加。在某些难以接近的区域，更换电池可能显得不切实际。为了克服这个挑战，我们便提出使用多天线来收集周围的射频能量。这个工作的创新之处在于通过利用从Wifi、手机以及其他无线接入点和基站辐射出来的射频能量，它为物联网中的传感器与设备提供了一个连续的电源。尽管收集到的功率很低，但是周围能量收集技术与低功耗电子技术的结合将促进不需要电池的独立无线设备的发展。在提出的方案中，一个关键点就是利用多天线收集周围的能量。每个天线接收的信号经过整流后变成直流信号并且叠加起来，这样便可以得到一个高增益，宽波束的整流天线。这样的整流天线可以收集宽角度范围内的周围射频能量，从而增加能量收集的容量

16207314.label: Realisation of objectives
16207314.value: All three objectives have been fully met. For the first objective (objective 1) we have looked into matching techniques [8.1] and developed a straightforward method based on a ladder matching network [8.1] that performs close to the optimal conjugate match without significant circuit complexity. On the otherhand we have also leveraged our work on multiport antennas for wireless communications and have found that the best approach is to develop compact multiport antennas with sufficiently low mutual to not require any matching network at all. This has been enhanced by also developing some novel pixel antenna optimization techniques [8.2,9.4]. For the second objective (objective 2) we have developed a wide variety of multiport antennas for ambient energy harvesting [8.3,8.4,9.1,9.2,9.3]. These have included pixel and patch designs [8.3,8.4]. For the final objective (objective 3) we have put all our ideas into a design in which the number of ports utilized is dependent on frequency [8.5]. At 900 MHz we use 4 ports while at 1800 MHz we use 12 ports [8.5]. A prototype has been developed and ambient RF measurements acquired around campus [8.5]. These show that even in ambient RF conditions we can harvest over 10uW making the system suitable for IoT applications. We have also written a review of our results [9.5] for an upcoming conference.

16207314.value: Major findings of this work include: 1) The use of multiple antennas significantly enhances ambient RF energy harvesting capability [8.3,8.4,8.5,9.1,9.2,9.3,9.5] 2) The number of multiple antenna ports utilized should be matched to the frequency and area available. 16207314.value: Due to the positive outcomes of this research, which has shown that enhancements to energy harvesting capability can be achieved with multiple antennas, further research is to be continued. 16207314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207314.value: This research project has demonstrated that it is possible to power IoT devices by harvesting RF energy from the everyday RF emissions of WiFi and cellular systems. While the harvested power is low the implication is that the IoT devices can be powered without batteries and therefore have working lifetimes of many years. This could be important in the development of IoT systems which are currently limited by the need for the IoT devices to have regular battery replacement of charging.

16207414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207414.value: To increase land use for development and to sustain economic growth, multi-propped deep basements for underground car parks, shopping malls, or subway stations are often constructed adjacent to existing buildings in cities such as Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Chicago, Sydney and London. Any excavation for deep underground stations and basements walls will inevitably cause stress change and ground movements around the excavation, affecting adjacent buildings. Tilting, and even collapse, of buildings have been reported. It is clear that the interaction between an excavation and an adjacent piled foundation is still not fully understood. In order to investigate and understand the interactions between a multi-propped excavation and a pile foundation and the deformation mechanisms in clay and sand, three-dimensional centrifuge model tests will be carried out using the state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge at HKUST together with three-dimensional numerical analyses. Multi-propped deep excavation will be simulated in-flight to study how excavation-induced stress changes and ground movements affect pile groups and piled-raft foundations that support adjacent buildings. Several key governing factors affecting the interactions and deformation mechanisms, such as the ratio of the depth of the retaining wall to the excavation depth, the distance between the retaining wall and pile group/piled-raft foundation, and the relative wall to soil stiffness will be simulated and investigated. It is anticipated that the outcomes of this proposed research will provide new insights into, and understanding of, excavation-piled foundation interactions and deformation mechanisms and improve current design guidelines, which will have major beneficial impacts on safety, the environment and the economy worldwide.

16207414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207414.value: Based on the innovative in-flight excavation and propping system developed, novel centrifuge model tests were carried out. In addition, advanced three-dimensional back-analyses and parametric study were conducted. The following conclusions may be drawn: a). A downward load transfer mechanism during excavation can be identified. Shaft resistance in the upper part of an adjacent pile decreases due to excavation-induced downward soil movement and a decrease in normal stress acting on the pile. To maintain vertical equilibrium, the pile has to settle to mobilize higher shaft resistance in its lower part, together with pile toe resistance. This has significant implication on the design of piles. Serviceability issues should be considered in design, due to induced pile settlement and an effective reduction in factor of safety. b). The constraint conditions at the pile head do not seem to have significant influence on the settlement of pile due to excavation. The maximum pile head settlement is about 0.6% of the pile diameter at the end of the 8 m excavation. Excavation induced pile group settlement increases with the depth of excavation. c). On the contrary, excavation-induced bending moment in the upper part of the pile is significantly influenced by the restraint imposed on the pile head. Stronger restraint induces larger bending moment. However, the effect of the pile head conditions on the induced bending moment in the lower part (below 1.75 times the excavation depth) of the pile is limited. d). Induced bending moment purely due to excavation can exceed the pile bending capacity. This suggests that structural integrity of piles should be carefully checked and protected in the design and construction of deep excavations adjacent to existing pile foundations, especially for piles in pile-raft foundations. e). For a given geometry and excavation depth, excavation induced pile group settlement decreases with an increase in sand density. This is because denser sand has a higher soil stiffness resulting in smaller soil movements, which decreases the pile group settlement. In contrast to the pile group settlement, pile group tilting does not follow any clear trend with the excavation depth. Thanks to the support of this project and other international collaborations, a total of four journal and four conference papers have been published. Details are given in Part C. Moreover, one research students, one M.Phil and one Ph.D, have been trained.

16207414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207414.value: Even though significant advances have been made in understanding the three-dimensional stress transfer and deformation mechanisms of a nearby piled foundation due to multi-propped deep excavation, full-scale trials and centrifuge model tests of large pile groups such as 9x9 or more pile groups and piled rafts should be carried out to investigate and understand pile-soil interaction to improve current designs, particularly in clays.

16207414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207414.value: A state-of-the-art three-dimensional model package was developed for simulating a multi-propped deep excavation adjacent to an existing axially-loaded pile group in-flight in a geotechnical centrifuge. The three-dimensional stress transfer and deformation mechanisms of a nearby piled foundation due to multi-propped deep excavation in sand were understood. The potential loss of pile capacity due to excavation was identified. New guidelines for safe distances of a new excavation from existing foundations in sand were established. Moreover, the effects of strain- and path-dependent soil stiffness on soil-structure interaction from an engineer's perspective were revealed. The findings from this project have clear and significant impacts on the safe and sustainable design of piled foundations, basements and tunnels in any major congested cities worldwide.

16207714.label: Project Objectives
16207714.value: Objective 1: Quantify the effects induced by human behavior on wireless signals Humans and their movement affect wireless propagation paths. In a typical indoor environment, there is one main path (LOS) and several paths reflected from surroundings such as the ceiling, floor and walls. If someone is present in the room, other paths will be scattered by the human body. As channel state information (CSI) can reflect fine-grained physical layer information, we will investigate the changes in CSI values associated with different human activities. We will also investigate human activities in different environments. Objective 2: Device-free passive motion detection WLAN-enabled device-free passive (Dfp) motion detection relies on received signal strength (RSS) to provide acceptable accuracy in the area of interest. However, RSS measurement is susceptible itself due to multipath effects in indoor environments. In addition, narrowband interference from substantial active communication devices working on the open ISM band can make the RSS measurement unreliable. In this task, we will design a DfP Fine-grained Indoor Motion Detection system to overcome these limitations. It will be based on the insight that CSI maintains temporal stability in static environments even in the presence of 2.4GHz narrowband interference, but it exhibits burst patterns when motion takes place. It will use a novel feature extracted from CSI will be used to leverage its temporal stability and frequency diversity. Objective 3: Device-free passive indoor location fingerprinting Many emerging applications such as intruder detection and border protection drive the fast- increasing development of DfP localization techniques. In this task we will design a CSI-based DfP indoor localization system. This is motivated by the observations that CSI is capable of capturing the environmental variance due to the frequency diversity of its wide band channel. An entity’s position can be uniquely identified by monitoring the shift of CSI features. Therefore, a “passive” radio map will be constructed as a prerequisite which includes fingerprints for entities located in some crucial reference positions, as well as clear environment. Objective 4: Device-free fall detection Fall are a major health threat and an obstacle to independent living for the elderly. Automatic fall detection is highly needed. Current proposed fall detection systems either need hardware installation or disrupt people’s daily life. These limitations make it hard to deploy fall detection systems widely in residential settings. In this work we proposed to analyze the influence of human activity on wireless signal. And propose a novel and truly unobtrusive detection method based on advanced wireless technologies. We will implement WiFall on laptops equipped with commercial 802.11n network interface cards (NICs).

16207714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207714.value: 近年來，無線網絡設備和技術的快速發展帶動了定位技術，移動探測和物體追蹤等研究。無線技術在識別環境變化方面具有非常好的前景。然而，關於無線信號和人體活動之間關系的研究非常少。我們研究發現當一個人體活動發生，例如，跌倒的時候，信號的傳輸路徑將會發生變化從而能夠被探測到。為了設計和實現利用無線網絡來進行監測人體行為，我們需要解決以下問題：首先，我們需要找到一個無線信號的表達方式。這種表達方式要對人體動作變化敏感但是對環境變化具有魯棒性。再者，現有的簡單無線信號傳播模型不能直接應用於復雜的人類行為活動。最后，目前的方法很難找出人體活動和無線信號特性之間的關系。因此在現實社會中利用無線網絡實現人體行為檢測並不簡單，而是由許多的挑戰和實際問題。為了實現以上的目的，我們計劃在這個研究中完成三個主要任務。我們將首先研究在無線網絡環境下人體活動的系統特性，並設計一個不需要佩戴設備的移動探測機制。我們也將利用細致的無線信道狀態信息來實現室內定位的功能。最后，我們計劃在實驗平台上實現無佩戴設備的跌倒監測系統。

16207714.label: Realisation of objectives
16207714.value: For the effect induced by human behavior using wireless networks, in this project, we have investigated the human activities in different environments. By analyzing the latest works, we summarize the general framework of existing Wi-Fi radar systems, and figure out that the design of these systems mainly follows a data-driven approach or a model-based approach. For each kind of Wi-Fi radar, we give a detailed analysis to the fundamental principles and state-of-the-art applications. (Objective 1) A novel device-free indoor motion detection system that uses existing WLAN infrastructure is implemented. For the first time, we propose to leverage the characteristics of fine-grained CSI from PHY layer for distinguishing static/dynamic environments in the indoor area of interest. We first exploit such feature using CSI Feature Extraction module and then utilize the DBSCAN algorithm in Burst Detection module to monitor the motion behavior. After that, we apply one scheme to reduce the false alarm rate. We have implemented FIMD with commercial IEEE 802.11n NICs and compared it against traditional RSS-based RASID system. (Objective 2) For indoor localization, we present a CSI-based passive device-free indoor fingerprinting system in WLAN. It is the first proposal to leverage temporal stability and frequency diversity characteristics of CSI for developing a “passive” fingerprint for device-free localization. In contrast to the traditional fingerprint approach, we integrate an Anomaly Detection block to facilitate the device-free nature. We apply the kernel density based approach to calculate the CSI correlation and thus detect abnormal entities. We implement it with commercial IEEE 802.11n NICs and evaluated its performance in two different indoor scenarios. (Objective 3) In this work, we first look for the correlations between different radio signal variations and activities by analyzing radio propagation model. Based on our observation, we propose WiFall, a truly unobtrusive fall detection system. WiFall employs physical layer Channel State Information (CSI) as the indicator of activities. It can detect fall of the human without hardware modification, extra environmental setup, or any wearable device. We implement WiFall on desktops equipped with commodity 802.11n NIC, and evaluate the performance in three typical indoor scenarios with several layouts of transmitter-receiver (Tx-Rx) links. In our area of interest, WiFall can achieve fall detection for a single person with high accuracy. (Objective 4)

16207714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207714.value: We conduct a comprehensive survey to analyze the general framework of existing Wi-Fi radar systems, and figure out that the design of these systems mainly follows a data-driven approach or a model-based approach. For each kind of Wi-Fi radar, we give a detailed analysis to the fundamental principles and state-of-the-art applications. This work was published in IEEE Communication Magazine 2018. (J6) We also implemented a novel device-free indoor motion detection system that uses existing WLAN infrastructure. We then further use wifi signal to detect more fine grained activities. We present WiHear, which enables Wi-Fi signals to “hear” our talks without deploying any devices. To achieve this, WiHear needs to detect and analyze fine-grained radio reflections from mouth movements. WiHear solves this micromovement detection problem by introducing Mouth Motion Profile that leverages partial multipath effects and wavelet packet transformation. Since Wi-Fi signals do not require line-of-sight, WiHear can “hear” people talks within the radio range. Further, WiHear can simultaneously “hear” multiple people’s talks leveraging MIMO technology. This work was published in IEEE TMC 2016 and also selected as the featured article of that issue. (J2, J3, J4) For indoor localization, we present a CSI-based passive device-free indoor fingerprinting system in WLAN. It is the first proposal to leverage temporal stability and frequency diversity characteristics of CSI for developing a fingerprint for device-free localization. (J5) We designed and implemented WiFall system, which aims to detect the fall of the elderly, and can also identify some other activities. WiFall takes advantage of the physical layer Channel State Information in widely deployed off-the-shelf WiFi infrastructure. To demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness, we implement the WiFall servers on laptops with commodity 802.11n NICs and conduct comprehensive experiment in three different scenarios with various Tx-Rx layouts. 16207714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207714.value: Wi-Fi, which enables convenient wireless access to Internet services, has become integral to our modern lives. With widely-deployed Wi-Fi infrastructure, modern people can enjoy a variety of online services such as web browsing, online shopping, social interaction, and e-commerce almost at any time and any place. Traditionally, the most significant functionality of Wi-Fi is to enable high-throughput data communication between terminal devices and the Internet. However, beyond that, we observe that a novel type of system based on commodity Wi-Fi is increasingly attracting intense academic interest. Without hardware modification and redeployment, we are exploiting channel state information output by commodity Wi-Fi and transforming existing Wi-Fi systems into radar-like ones that can recognize human behavior along with data communication. This fancy functionality is tremendously expanding the boundaries of Wi-Fi to a new realm and triggering revolutionary applications in the context of the Internet of Things.

16207814.label: Project Objectives
16207814.value: Objective 1: To enable robust estimation for heavy-tailed distributions with outliers Task 1.1: Robust estimation in the presence of outliers: To design mean and covariance matrix estimators robust to outliers based on a well-defined maximum likelihood framework of normalized samples that will give superior performance to existing methods without the need for parameter tuning. Task 1.2: Robust estimation for heavy-tailed distributions: To extend the previous framework from normalized Gaussian data to normalized heavy-tailed distributions. Objective 2: To develop an algorithmic framework for robust estimation Task 2.1: Fixed-point iterative methods: To explore iterative methods derived from the fixed-point equations corresponding to the maximum likelihood robust optimization framework developed in the previous objective. Task 2.2: Successive convex approximation approach: To cosider majorization-minimization and successive convex approximation methods as a more powerful framework to derive provable convergent algorithms. Objective 3: To facilitate regularized robust estimation for high dimensional data Task 3.1: Regularization via shrinkage: To embrace the high-dimensional setting by incorporating shrinkage in the robust estimation of mean and covariance matrix. Task 3.2: Regularization via sparsity: To regularize the previous robust estimators to model sparsity assumptions, which will help in coping with small data samples (or high dimensionality).

16207814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207814.value: Parameter estimation is a ubiquitous problem faced in a variety of applications rooted in the fields of signal processing, wireless communication, system identification, control, finance, etc. In all these areas, given the observed data samples, the problem is to estimate the unknown parameters of a model. An underlying assumption in this process lies in the modeling of the probability distribution of the observations or measurements. Usually, a Gaussian assumption is made since it is justifiable in many applications and leads to nice mathematical derivations, e.g., the popular sample covariance matrix estimator. However, in many other applications, this model is not good enough and one has to give up the nice mathematical Gaussian framework and choose another distribution with so-called heavy tails. For example, in financial systems, one needs to model the returns and, in particular, the idiosyncratic component that has been demonstrated to have heavy tails; in such a case, using a Gaussian distribution would lead to sub-optimal prediction strategies and a catastrophic underestimation of the risk, which may lead to a heavy financial loss (as was the case in the recent financial crisis). Apart from the problem of making a reasonable model assumption, the second problem that affects real-world applications is data contamination. Due to the complicated setup for the data collection process, even a simple error may lead to serious anomalies in the measured data; faulty data storage or transmission has a similar effect. Such anomalous data are called outliers. Ignoring these outliers and using the data naively to fit the model would lead to model parameters that are far from reality; thus, fitting methods robust to outliers are necessary. A third problem in many real-world applications is the scarcity of data samples in comparison with the dimensionality of the model, which is due to the high cost involved in the data collection procedure. This proposal aims at developing efficient and effective techniques to deal with the three aforementioned problems: i) estimation methods for non-Gaussian distributions with heavy tails, ii) fitting techniques robust to data anomalies or outliers, and iii) algorithms that can work with scarce data or, equivalently, in high dimensions. 参数估计问题广泛出现于信号处理，无线通信，系统辨识，控制理论，金融工程等应用领域。在这些领域中，许多问题通常可以抽象成为基于观测数据对模型参数参数进行统计估计。在估计过程中，我们通常需要对数据建立概率分布模型，而在经典理论与多数实际应用中，数据服从高斯分布的假设被广泛采用。做高斯假设的原因之一是在某些特定应用场景中，该分布能大致刻画实际数据的分布情况。而更重要的是，在数学建模过程中，采用高斯假设往往可以得到简洁漂亮的数学表达式。例如，在高斯分布假设下，样本协方差矩阵即为协方差矩阵的极大似然估计。但是，在一些大偏差值以较高频率出现的应用中，高斯分布假设并不符合数据经验分布。为了更准确刻画数据统计特性，我们必须舍弃高斯分布在数学分析上带来的便利，而使用所谓的厚尾分布来模拟这些数据。例如，在金融系统中，时间序列特征成分的经验分布常常表现出厚尾特性，而在这种情况下如果仍然使用高斯分布来对其建模，则此模型将与实际情况产生严重偏差，进而导致模型做出次最优决策，或者因对风险估计不足而导致投资严重损失（这是近年金融危机产生的原因之一）。 在实际应用问题中，我们不仅仅需要对数据合理建模，同时也需要谨慎处理异常数据。由于数据的采集过程通常十分复杂，在此过程中一个简单的错误将可能导致测得数据严重异常；相似现象也常出现于数据的储存与传输中。我们将因此产生的错误观测值称为异常值。如果在模型训练过程中对异常值不做处理，学习得到的模型参数将因为异常值影响而与参数真实值产生极大偏差。因此，提高模型对异常值的鲁棒性变得尤为重要。除了厚尾分布与异常值外，高维度小样本（例如由于高实验成本导致测量数据量过小）是现实中统计分析面对的第三大问题。 本项目旨在设计数学模型与相应高效算法以解决以下三点问题。（1）对厚尾非高斯分布数据建模并估计模型参数；（2）探寻对异常值鲁棒的模型拟合方法；（3）设计能处理高维度小样本数据的数学模型与相应高效快速算法。

16207814.label: Realisation of objectives
16207814.value: The main goal of this project was the development of robust estimation methods for heavy-tailed distributions with outliers, both the theoretical characterization of the solution and the practical numerical algorithms. All the objectives have been more than satisfactorily completed and the output consists of one book, eight IEEE top journal papers (including a long overview paper on the mathematical framework majorization-minimization based algorithms), and six conference papers. Objective 1 was focused on estimation of covariance matrices under heavy tail and outliers. Many of the publications from this project (including the book) deal directly with this issue by developing an optimization framework and then deriving practical iterative numerical methods based on the majorization-minimization technique. This objective has been fully accomplished and, in fact, Objective 3 below is a continuation of this objective. Objective 2 was on developing a more general algorithmic framework based on majorization-minimization (MM) (with the covariance matrix estimation being just one particular example). The main publication for this objective is the overview paper where MM is fully developed in its many variations and extensions and many applications are given in different areas. In just one year since its publication it has already accumulated 60 citations. Objective 3 dealt with the additional difficulty of the small sample regime (or, equivalently, high-dimensional setting) which can be addressed via regularization methods that result in shrinkage estimators. This objective is closely connected to Objective 1 (which is a simpler version without regularization). Most of the publications of this project fall within this objective (including the book). In addition to the academic publishing output, we are currently working on developing a software package that implements the obtained techniques in the R language. To be more specific, in August we will make publicly available an R package that will contain all the developed algorithms (will be available at https://github.com/dppalomar).

16207814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207814.value: The major findings of this project were the development of theory and practical algorithms for the estimation of the mean and the covariance matrix of multivariate random observations that follow a heavy-tailed distribution (the Gaussian case being trivial in comparison). In addition, the important practical issue in many applications of having a small sample in comparison with the dimensionality of the observations is specifically addressed. We have achieved this via a regularization term in the log-likelihood of the estimation process. The resulting solutions and algorithms are actually easy to implement in practice. Apart from the particular problem of estimating the mean and covariance, we have also further developed the MM method and applied it to many other problems in different areas, publishing a long review paper. In fact, the obtained algorithms are so practical that we are in the process of developing a software package under the programming language R commonly used in statistics and finance. In particular, in August we will make publicly available an R package for the practical estimation of mean and covariance matrix for heavy-tailed distributions that will also work in the small sample regime (will be available in the GitHub page https://github.com/dppalomar).

16207814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207814.value: During this project we obtained many results, more than expected. Nevertheless, this only opened the door for many other future problems. One very interesting area is estimation of parameters when there are missing data. Another promising topic is that of imputation of the missing data so that other algorithms that require full data can still be used after the imputation. We are currently working on that with really good results.

16207814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207814.value: In science and engineering, we model many observations as random quantities, hence the importance of statistics in our modern world. In many cases, such random quantities follow the so-called normal or Gaussian distribution (introduced by Gauss in the 19th century). Such distribution has been long studied and it allows for nice analysis and mathematical manipulation. It is very convenient and easy to manage. However, in many other cases the Gaussian distribution is not a realistic model of the world in the sense that the random quantities can have more extreme values than the Gaussian would predict. We say that such distributions have heavy tails (because if one plots the distribution, the tails look fatter than those of the Gaussian). The shocking reality is that all the methods previously derived under the assumption of the Gaussian distribution perform really bad when we have heavy tails. This project has considered this particular issue by developing estimation methods that work well under heavy tails. In particular, the mathematical theory has been developed and then practical methods have been derived. They really work well in practice and we have developed open source software that can be used by anybody in the world.

16207914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207914.value: Graph partitioning is a popular topic in academia and in commercial applications, particularly social networks, where users are grouped into communities for advertising and analysis purposes. Existing approaches mainly partition the graph so that either the connectivity, or the similarity, of the users inside the groups is maximized. However, the plethora of available information and the requirements of new applications render partitioning more demanding. For instance, in some cases, we need to partition a huge social graph into a predefined set of clusters, where users in the same cluster are socially connected and they have similar characteristics. In this proposal, we model several novel and challenging problems in social networks as instances of Uniform Metric Labeling (UML) and Minimum Multiway-Cut (MMC). Since existing techniques for both problems incur prohibitive cost for the huge graphs, typical in current social networks, we propose approximate solutions based on game theory and novel data structures. The project involves interesting research problems in diverse areas, including graph algorithms, game theory and big data management. Moreover, given the proliferation of social networks, we expect it to have significant impact in terms of potential applications. 图形分割是学术界、工业领域的热点课题，尤其是在社交网络，需要将用户划分为多个群组，方便广告宣传和分析。当前方法主要以群组内用户的连通性或相似性最大化为准则对图形进行分割。然而，可用信息量的增大及新应用要求的增高，使图形分割的难度增加。例如，在部分情况下，我们需要将一个大规模社交图分割为预定义的聚类，使得同一聚类内的用户既具有社交相关性又具有类似特征。在本文中，我们将社交网络几个新出现的高难度问题看成是均匀度量标记(UML)和最小多路分割(MMC)问题。对大型的图，如当前社交网络，上述两个问题的现有方法所需成本太大。于是，我们提出基于博弈理论和新型数据结构的近似求解方法。该方法涉及图形算法、博弈理论和大数据管理等多个领域非常有趣的研究问题。此外，鉴于社交网络不断扩散，我们希望本文的方法能有较大的应用潜力。

16207914.label: Realisation of objectives
16207914.value: Real-time Multi-criteria Graph Partitioning (RMGP) groups the users of a social network based on their connectivity and their similarity to a set of input classes. As an example, assume that a geo-social network wishes to promote upcoming events to users based on proximity and social connectivity. We refer to this task as Geo-Social Event Organization (GSEO). Each event corresponds to a class, and the cost of assigning a user to a class is his/her current distance, or travel time, to the respective event. RMGP assigns each user to an event that minimizes (i) the distance/travel time between the user and the event, and (ii) the social connectivity between users assigned to different events. Consequently, a user is assigned to an event that is nearby and, at the same time, it is recommended to several of his friends. As another example consider Topic-Aware Graph Partitioning (TAGP), where an on-line discussion forum wishes to place an advertisement for each user, in a manner that maximizes the "word of mouth" effect. In the corresponding RMGP task, each potential advertisement constitutes a class. The assignment cost of a user is based on some (dis-)similarity measure (e.g., tf-idf) between his current discussions and the advertisement topic. The social connectivity between users is based on the number of common discussions in which they have participated. Thus, users are likely to be assigned advertisements that match their own interests, and those of their frequent discussion co-participants. In general, RMGP refers to the partition of a graph according to connectivity (i.e., social cost), and one or more additional criteria (i.e., assignment cost). Specifically, in addition to social cost, we have the travel cost in GSEO and the text similarity in TAGP. A combination of multiple criteria can also be supported. For example, if each user has a profile, the assignment cost could take into account both the distance of each user and his preference to an event (e.g., based on textual similarity between the profile and the event description). In some cases, there may be constraints on the class capacities, e.g., in TAGP the number of users that will receive an advertisement depends on the budget of the corresponding advertiser. We consider constrained and unconstrained RMGP as an on-line process because input parameters change frequently. For example, in GSEO, locations of users may be updated through check-ins, while new events may appear frequently. Therefore, RMGP recommendations should be efficiently generated in order to accommodate the fast-pace changes. Moreover, for some tasks only a subset of the network, determined at query time, may participate in RMGP. For instance, if a geosocial network wishes to advertise events at a certain area, only the users who recently checked-in that area, and the corresponding induced sub-graph, are relevant. Our first approach to effectively solve RMGP in real world social networks views the problem as a game, where each user corresponds to a player: his goal is to find the class that minimizes his assignment and social costs. As we show, the game reaches an equilibrium, i.e., a local minimum where no user has incentive to deviate. Modeling and solving RMGP as a game has several advantages. First, the game mimics the behavior of individual real-world users who aim at optimizing their own objectives, independently of those of the others. Consequently, it yields recommendations (i.e., solutions) that are likely to be followed by the users. On the other hand, optimization methods that minimize the global cost, without considering the individual objectives, could lead to recommendations that are not followed by numerous users, rendering the solution meaningless. Moreover, the resulting algorithms are fast, allowing the real-time execution of queries, and facilitate distributed processing. Our second approach applies a local search framework: starting from an initial solution, it gradually drops the overall cost, even if the cost of some individual users may increase after a step. As it involves more deviations compared to the game theoretic framework (where users choose classes only based on their own benefit), it is more expensive in terms of running time, but it yields solutions of better quality. Moreover, we show how the game theoretic and local search approaches can be unified into a common agent based framework. This permits the application of shared optimization techniques and data structures for both approaches. Optimizations developed during the project to enhance efficiency include: (i) the generation of good initial assignments for the game theoretic and local search approaches, (ii) the fast elimination of individual assignments that can never be performed, (iii) the parallel execution for assignments that do not affect each other, and (iv) prevention of unnecessary computations through proper book-keeping. These optimizations are supported by various indexing schemes. Our extensive experiments, with real and synthetic datasets, demonstrate that our agent based framework achieves superior solutions than the current state-of-the-art, while substantially dropping the execution time.

16207914.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207914.value: In the first conference publication, we introduce RMGP (Real-time Multi-criteria Graph Partitioning), and model the problem as a game. An important issue in RMGP, and all tasks that partition a graph according to connectivity and additional criteria, is how to set the relative importance of the social aspect in the total cost. For instance, in GSEO the distance-based assignment cost can be in the order of thousands (of meters), whereas the edge weights may be in the range [0, 1]. To solve this issue, we propose effective normalization techniques for adjusting the importance of the assignment and social costs. In addition, we introduce the several optimizations, which significantly increase the speed of the game-theoretic approach. The second conference publication applies RMGP in the context of constrained GSEO, i.e., the events may have constraints on the number of users that they can accommodate. The Nash Equilibrium concept is inadequate due to the capacity constraints. Specifically, a user v has an incentive to perform a unilateral deviation from his assigned event e1 to another one e2, if e2 yields a smaller cost for v. Due to the existence of capacity constraints, a unilateral deviation is legal, if it does not violate the minimum capacity of e1, or the maximum capacity of e2. Now consider two users v and u, assigned to e1 and e2, respectively, and that e1 is at its minimum capacity, so that e1 cannot loose a user. Also, assume that both v and u would benefit by swapping events. Although individual unilateral deviations would be illegal, it is possible for v and u to exchange events by a bilateral deviation. In order to cover such cases, we introduce the concept of pairwise stability, which increases the quality of the solutions achieved by the game theoretic approach. Our journal paper introduces a local search approach that can be applied to RMGP, with and without capacity constraints. We show how the game theoretic and local search approaches can be unified into a common agent based framework. Moreover, we propose various optimizations that improve the quality of the solution, while reducing the execution time. Additionally, we build data structures for faster real-time performance. Our extensive experiments, with real and synthetic datasets, demonstrate that our framework achieves superior solutions than the current state-of-the-art, while substantially dropping the execution time. Additionally, the proposed techniques generate the assignments of maximum cardinality subject to the capacity constraints.

16207914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207914.value: We plan to investigate additional search heuristics to improve the efficiency or solution quality. For instance, a hill climbing variant would perform, at each round, the unilateral or bilateral deviation that incurs the largest cost drop. We could also explore trilateral or deviations of higher degree, which could improve the solution quality at the expense of running time. Alternatively, we could apply a form of simulated annealing that allows deviations to solutions of worse quality in order to escape local minima. Finally, in our scenario, we assume that each node is assigned to a single class. An interesting extension would allow multiple assignments, e.g., a user could attend different nearby events. A possible way to formulate this problem is by associating each user with the number of events that he is willing to attend. An alternative is to define a distance budget per user v, so that v can only be assigned to some event e, only if the distance between v and e is within the budget of v. When such an assignment occurs, the distance is deducted from the budget. In either case, this version of problem would necessitate novel techniques.

16207914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207914.value: Real-time Multi-criteria Graph Partitioning (RMGP) refers to the partition of a graph according to connectivity, and one or more additional criteria. RMGP is becoming increasingly important with the proliferation of social networks and related services. In this project, we designed an effective and efficient agent-based framework that unifies the game-theoretic and the local search perspectives, and developed concrete implementations that integrate various optimizations to enhance performance. We investigated the behavior of our algorithms through an extensive experimental evaluation with real datasets. The proposed methods outperform the state-of-the-art competitors in effectiveness, solution quality and efficiency.

16208114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208114.value: Optical interconnects offer the key merit of energy-efficient, high-speed optical communications compared with the conventional metal interconnects. Silicon (Si) photonic waveguides, due to their low propagation loss at the technologically relevant 1300 / 1550nm wavelengths and compatibility with the standard complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process technologies, are promising building blocks for optical interconnects. Over the past decade, many functional and electrically reconfigurable Si photonic devices with integrated electronic structures have been demonstrated. Specifically, Si micrometer-sized ring (microring) resonators integrated with pn or p-i-n diodes have been shown by many research groups including ours to be a versatile structure as wavelength-selective filters, delays, switches, routers, modulators and defect-state-absorption (DSA) photodetectors. In this project, we seek to experimentally investigate a Si microring DSA photodetector that is energy-efficient, high-speed, wavelength-selective and compact in size for 1300 / 1550 nm. Although research groups including ours have demonstrated Si DSA photodetectors in 1550 nm, the photodetectors are either limited in responsivity (which limits their applications to power monitors) or impose a relatively large device size of millimeters (which is undesirable for dense on-chip integration or energy efficiency). To date, Si DSA photodetectors in 1300 nm have not been demonstrated. Here, we seek to significantly enhance the Si microring DSA photodetector performance in 1300 / 1550 nm by optimizing the DSA through implanting various types of ions and annealing, optimizing the diode designs, and critically coupling to a few-micrometer-sized moderate-quality-factor microring resonator. Our initial analysis based on the literature and our on-going work suggests that it will be feasible for such a DSA photodetector to attain a responsivity at cavity resonances at or above 0.5 A/W for 1300 / 1550 nm, at or beyond 60Gb/s data rate, upon a 1-3V-range voltage that is compatible with CMOS. The micrometer-sized resonator also enables a low femto-Farad (fF)-range capacitance that is favorable for energy-efficient high-speed photodetection. We envision that a successful demonstration of the proposal will enable a technologically competitive, cost-effective, all-silicon on-chip photodetector technology that constitutes a viable alternative to the current commercially available heterogeneous integrated germanium (Ge)-on-Si on-chip photodetectors. One significant merit of the proposed technology is that it only requires relatively robust CMOS technology (ion implantation and annealing), without using Ge epitaxial process. The 1550nm Si-photodetectors will find critical applications as a wavelength-selective photodetector for on-chip optical interconnects. The 1300nm Si-photodetectors will find promising applications as a wavelength-selective photodetector for optical interconnects in datacenters. 光互連，相對於傳統的金屬連接，有著低能耗，高速度的重要優勢。矽基光學波導，因其在技術相關的1300nm/1550nm 波長範圍傳輸損耗低，並且和互補式金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）技術兼容，因而是光互連中重要的組成部件。在過去的十年裏，很多功能性的和電可重構的矽基光學器件及集成電子結構被證明。特別是矽基微米量級的環形腔和pn或p-i-n二極管的集成結構已經被很多研究小組，包括我們組證明為具有多種用途的結構，比如用於波長選擇濾波器，延時器，光開關，路由器，調制器，以及基於缺陷態吸收（DSA）的光電探測器。 在這個項目裏，我們力求通過實驗研究證明一個矽基環形腔結構的，基於缺陷態吸收的高能效，高速，具有波長選擇性，結構緊湊的，用於1300/1550nm波長的光電探測器。盡管已經有研究小組，包括我們，都已經實現證明了用於1550nm波長的基於缺陷態吸收的矽基光電探測器。 但是已經被證明的光電探測器或只有有限的光響應 （其應用因而只局限於功率監測計），或需要毫米級別的相對大的器件面積（不利於高密度片上集成並且能耗不理想）。根據我們的調研，目前用於1300nm的基於缺陷態吸收的矽基光電探測器還沒有被證明。 這裏，我們希望能夠通過離子註入不同類型的離子，調整退火過程，優化二極管設計，以及控制波導臨界耦合到幾個微米大小並且品質因子合適的微環腔，以極大的增強基於DSA的矽基環形腔結構的光電探測器在1300/1550nm的性能。根據文獻和我們正在進行的工作，我們初步分析， 在1300/1550nm波長，這種基於DSA的光電探測器在反向偏壓為1V到3V的CMOS兼容範圍內，其響應微環腔諧振波長達到0.5A/W，傳輸速率大於等於60Gb/s，是可行性的。於此同時，微米大小的環形腔能夠將二極管電容降低到幾個飛法（fF），這對於高能效高速的光電探測是很有利的。 我們預想，如果成功證明本提案，我們將提供一個技術性兼容，成本低，全矽基的片上光電探測器技術，其將會成為現行商用中的異構鍺矽（Ge-on-Si）集成的光電探測器的一個可行的替代技術。所提方案技術的一個顯著優勢是其只需要相對健全的CMOS技術（離子註入和退火），不需要Ge外延生長技術。用於1550nm的矽基光電探測器，作為一個波長選擇的光電探測器會在片上光互連中有著重要作用。而用於1300nm的矽基光電探測器，作為一個波長選擇的光電探測器，會在數據中心的光互連網絡中有良好的應用前景。

16208214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208214.value: The rapid development of the service industry calls for new models and solution schemes for effective operations management. This project considers situations where sequencing and scheduling decisions are needed in service operations. Existing scheduling models mainly originate from manufacturing and may not be suitable for some service applications, due to a number of differences between the two industries. This proposed project will focus on one import difference: how to evaluate a schedule. In service operations, customers are directly involved in the service process. As such, the quality of a schedule is heavily affected by the subjective perceptions of the customers. The customers’ perceived feelings should therefore be considered as a criterion in evaluating a schedule. Motivated by our daily life experience and previous research results in the literature, we have identified two typical perceived feelings, fairness and satisfaction, and will study service-oriented scheduling problems to which these two perceived feelings are relevant. Perceived fairness emphasizes the relative order of getting served among a group of customers. When the service provider needs to treat the customers sequentially, a given sequence may exist, such as first-come-first-served, which is acceptable as fair to all customers. However, the service provider may need to alter this fair sequence, at a cost of reduced fairness, due to operational constraints and efficiency considerations. Hence we face the scheduling problem of balancing the customers’ perceived fairness against the service provider’s operational concerns. Perceived satisfaction has been studied for situations where a service is composed of multiple sequential events and different sequences of delivering the events may lead to different satisfaction perceptions. For example, where in the sequence is the optimal position to put the most (least) pleasant event? Behavioral scientists have recognized the event sequencing effect on the service quality. Some people also suggest that knowing this may help improve the service quality by taking actions at the operational level; however, no scholarly work has been published so far. We will study event scheduling to achieve the greatest perceived satisfaction while considering operational efficiency and constraints. In summary, we will address the above two issues in service-oriented scheduling problems. The work includes establishing measurement schemes for the perceived feelings, setting up appropriate models, and developing solution schemes. We also hope that this work can initiate a new area in scheduling research, as well as make an impact on the service industry. 快速发展的服务业需要有效的运营管理模型。本项目研究服务业中的若干调度排序问题。传统的调度模型主要基于制造业的实践，由于多种因素的制约，经常不能直接用于服务业。本项目着重考虑其中一个重要因素：对调度指标的评价。 在服务业中，顾客直接参与整个服务过程，所以顾客对服务质量有强烈的主观感受。这种感受应该被用来评价一个调度方案的性能。基于从日常生活中的直接体验和文献研究，我们选择了两个典型的主观感受：相对公平性和满意度，来研究它们对调度问题的影响。 相对公平性强调对顾客服务的相对次序。在很多排队服务的场合，多有一个被广泛接受的公平服务次序，例如先到先服务。但是，这个既定的次序对于服务提供者来讲，可能运营效率很低，所以我们有必要修改既定的次序，从而达到公平服务和运营效率的平衡。 关于顾客满意度的评价，我们考虑的服务是一个包括多个事件的打包服务。行为科学研究表明，这些事件发生的次序影响顾客对整个服务的满意度。然而在运营管理研究中，人们还没有探索如何利用这个发现来安排事件的调度次序，从而在满足运营条件的约束下，提供用户最满意的服务。 总之，本项目将研究在服务业调度决策中面临的以上两个问题。研究内容包括对相对公平性和满意度的定量描述，调度模型的建立，以及问题求解的方法。我们希望本项目可以开辟一个新的调度研究领域，并对服务业产生正面影响。

16208214.label: Realisation of objectives
16208214.value: We have achieved all three objectives of this project. Objective 1. [To study scheduling problems in service operations when the perceived fairness has to be considered. This includes to propose the measures of relative fairness, to build decision models balancing achieved fairness and operational efficiency, and to design algorithms to solve the problems.] We start this line of work from the rescheduling problem of berth allocation, the main results being presented at an international conference (Section 9, No.1). We then propose a general model, referred to as scheduling with soft precedence constraints (SPC), and write a paper for possible publication. Similar to the conventional precedence constraint, SPC specifies some partial order over the jobs; however, an SPC can be violated, but with a certain penalty or cost. The scheduling problem is to balance the tradeoff between the SPC violation penalty and other criteria relative to job completion times. We demonstrate the SPC model by the case where SPC is defined by a bipartite network.We discuss the complexity of the problems for different scenarios and develop approximation algorithms. The paper (Section 8, No.2) is now under the third round of review with European Journal of Operational Research. Objective 2. [To study scheduling problems in service operations when the perceived satisfaction has to be considered. This includes to propose the measures for perceived satisfaction to build decision models balancing the satisfaction against operational efficiency, and to design algorithms to solve the problems.] We study the optimal sequencing and selection of activities a service package comprises to maximize user utility. Empirical literature shows an ideal schedule often entails an interior peak; that is, the most engaging activity (aka peak activity) is scheduled neither at the beginning nor the end of the package. Theoretic literature, on the other hand, points to a U-shaped schedule such that the peak activity should be scheduled either at the beginning or the end. Our paper bridges the gap in the literature by showing heterogeneity in memory decay, a well-documented psychological phenomenon, provides theoretic support for empirical findings of interior peaks. It also generates practical implications for choosing and sequencing activities in designing service packages. We characterize structural properties of the optimal service schedule, building on which we develop a novel dynamic-programming algorithm that optimally solves the service-design problem in pseudo-polynomial time. We find, surprisingly, the heterogeneity in memory-decay processes is sufficient to explain the phenomenon of interior peaks, which has been observed in practice but remains to be explained by the extant behavioral models. An interior peak is optimal when the memory-decay rate of the peak activity is neither too high nor too low. Furthermore, we show that when an interior peak is optimal, the service provider can schedule a low point immediately before the peak activity, creating an unexpectedly pleasant service experience. We also analyze the problem of activity selection, and show it can be optimal to choose a portfolio of activities with either the highest or lowest utility values, but not those with medium utility values. This line of work is mostly conducted by a PhD student who has been recognized in two Best Student Paper Competitions (Section 11). The paper (Section 8, item 3) is now under review with Manufacturing and Service Operations Management, where an earlier version of the paper was rejected but encouraged for resubmission by the same journal. Objective 3. [To propose one or several of the following extensions: to identify and study other types of perceived feelings in service-oriented scheduling model, to further consider uncertainty and game-theoretic behavior in the proposed models, and to conduct some initial empirical studies to validate the results.] We have studied the first two extensions proposed above. Extension 1, we notice that jobs owners often have preference of certain time periods, which can be modeled by time-varying machine cost. Under such context, we study a scheduling problem which aims to minimize the summation of total weighted completion time and the total machine time slot cost. Focusing on the case of non-increasing time slot cost with non-preemptive jobs, we show that the problem can be solved in polynomial-time when the time slot cost decreases with certain patterns, including linearly decreasing, decreasing concave, and decreasing convex cases. Different methodologies are used for three cases. For the linearly decreasing case, we can classify all the jobs into three categories and schedule the job sets one by one. For the decreasing concave case, we calculate each job’s worst starting time and try to make them far away from their worst starting times. For the decreasing concave case, we calculate each job’s best starting time and let them start close to their best starting time. The above work has been published in Journal of Scheduling (Section 8, No.1). Extension 2: We notice that people’s perceived feeling to a product can be affected by personal experiencing. A recent business practice for retailers is to encourage showrooming – consumers browsing product in the offline channel but switching to the online channel for purchases, with an aim to leverage both the low cost from the online channel and the real experience from the offline channel. We address such a dual-channel system, i.e., concurrently running a mix of online and offline channels by a joint decision on pricing for the two channels as well as their associated return policy. Using an appropriate model we show that a well-designed dual-channel system can indeed increase the profitability of a retailer. We also identify several barriers for retailers to engage with consumers directly such as consumer valuation uncertainty and cost efficiency of handling returns, and show that it may be beneficial for retailers to engage with consumers indirectly via consumer showrooming. One paper of these results has been accepted in Journal of the Operational Research Society (Section 8, No.4).

16208214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208214.value: First, we consider the phenomenon that customers often regard relative fairness as an important factor in their perceived feeling. To handle this factor, we propose a concept, referred to as scheduling with soft precedence constraints (SPC), to measure the importance of maintaining relative fairness. SPC specifies some partial order over the jobs, which can be violated with a certain penalty or cost. The scheduling problem is to balance the tradeoff between the SPC violation penalty and other criteria relative to job completion times. To demonstrate this concept, we study a special case where SPC is defined by a bipartite network. We discuss the complexity of the problems for different scenarios and develop approximation algorithms. The paper (Section 8, No.2) is now under the third round of review. Second, we consider the design of a service package that includes multiple events, where customers’ satisfaction levels are affected by the order of the events being offered. One particular issue is when to offer the peak event (the most liked event). In practice we often observe an interior peak; that is, the peak event is scheduled neither at the beginning nor the end of the package. Theoretic literature, on the other hand, points to a U-shaped schedule such that the peak activity should be scheduled either at the beginning or the end. Our paper bridges the gap in the literature by showing heterogeneity in memory decay, a well-documented psychological phenomenon, provides theoretic support for empirical findings of interior peaks. It also generates practical implications for choosing and sequencing activities in designing service packages. This work is recognized in two Best Student Paper Competitions (Section 9, items 2 and 3, and Section 11). The paper (Section 8, item 3) is now under review with Manufacturing and Service Operations Management. Third, we have explored other OR/OM problems related to perceived feelings. In one case, jobs owners often have preference of certain time periods, which can be modeled by time-varying machine cost. We study a scheduling problem with machine time slot cost. The work is published in Journal of Scheduling (Section 8, No.1). In another case, Extension 2: We notice that people’s perceived feeling to a product can be affected by personal experiencing, a reason motivating for retailers is to encourage showrooming. We address such a dual-channel system with respect to profitability and applicability. One paper of these results has been accepted in Journal of the Operational Research Society (Section 8, No.4).

16208214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208214.value: We still have 2 working papers under review by journals, and we need to revise and further get them published. In addition, we find our work has attracted lots of interest, as partially evidenced by the two-time recognition in Best Student Papers competition. This encourages us to continue working along this direction. Currently we are exploring work design, how to schedule break times so that workers can contain their fatigue and maintain their performance at a high level.

16208214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208214.value: Scheduling is to arrange a set of events over time so that some performance can be optimized. Traditionally the scheduling performance is measured by the completion time of each event. While such performance measure is reasonable in many situations, it overlooks another factor, the impact on people’s feeling psychologically. One example is the relative fairness. Considering a busy restaurant, most customers can reasonably tolerate a long waiting time and still enjoy their meal as long as they feel they have been treated fairly, e.g., with the courses served among all the tables on a first-come-first-served (FCFS) basis; but the restaurant may also consider not following the FCFS order strictly due to a number of reasons related to its operational efficiency. Another example is the customers’ perceived satisfaction after experiencing a series of events with difference utilities, which is affected by the order of the events to be held. In this project we have studied scheduling problems involving these two psychological feelings, which will enable decision makers to generate scheduling decisions more friendly to customers, especially in the service industry.
