16208414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208414.value: In MIMO feedback control, the signal transmission between the plant and controller is almost always done using SISO connections, i.e., each signal, whether it is one of the inputs or one of the outputs, has its own dedicated transmission connection and the number of transmission connections is equal to the number of signals to be transmitted. Even in networked control, where the signals are transmitted through communication channels, almost all research works assume that the measurement signals and control signals have their own dedicated communication channels. Whenever a signal needs to be transmitted, it has always been assumed that there is a channel, whether ideal or with limited capacity, available for the transmission. However, that is not always the case in practice. In some situations such as remote control and distributed control, there is only one or a few buses for the transmission of many or all signals. In some other situations, such as control via wireless communication, there may be many channels, each with a small transmission capability, so as to collectively provide sufficient amount of information for a small number of signals in the control of a remote plant. In both situations, the number of channels available very often are not equal to the number of signals to be transmitted and, unavoidably, MIMO communication technology has to be used. In this proposed project, we will take an unprecedented step to develop a theory of MIMO control using MIMO communication. Our preliminary research has shown that when MIMO control meets MIMO communication, better performance, lower cost, and greater flexibility can be achieved. This project will be the first step in the matching making of MIMO control and MIMO communication. We expect that it will open the door to a large space of research opportunities and activities. 在多输入多输出反馈控制中，受控对象和控制器之间的信号 传输基本上是通过单输入单输出的连接来进行，即每个输入 或者输出信号都有一个专用的传输连接并且传输连接的数量 和待传输信号的数量是相等的。即使是在信号通过通信信道 传输的网络化控制中，几乎所有现有的研究工作都假设测量 信号和控制信号都有其专用的通信信道，每个信号都通过一个 或理想或具有有限容量的通信信道来传输。然而，在实际应用中 并不总是如此。在诸如远程控制和分布式控制这些情形下， 只有一条或少数几条总线可用来传输信号。在其他一些情形下， 诸如通过无线通信来控制，可能会存在很多小容量的通信通道， 它们联合起来可以提供足够的信息容量来传输少量的控制信号 从而控制远程的受控对象。在以上两类情形中，可用信道的数量 常常不等于待传输信号的数量，而且不可避免地将要运用多输入 多输出通信技术。在该拟议项目中，我们将跨出前所未有的一步 来发展在多输入多输出控制中运用多输入多输出通信的理论。 我们的初步研究表明当多输入多输出控制邂逅多输入多输出通信 时可以取得更好的性能，更低的成本以及更多的灵活性。 该项目将是多输入多输出控制携手多输入多输出通信的第一步。 我们期望该项目将打开一扇门通往更广阔的研究机会和研究 工作。

16208414.label: Realisation of objectives
16208414.value: The study towards Objective 1 is a great success. We think we have achieved 120 percent of this objective, i.e., we have achieved more than what we envisioned when the proposal was written. Two full length papers have been published in the top journals in the subject area. The obtained results establishes the connection between networked control and majorization theory. The study towards Objective 2 is also successful by realizing that the state estimation problem is dual to state feedback stabilization problem if the so call "innovation" is to be transmitted through the communication channel. Under this system architecture, the results for state estimation problem are dual to the state feedback stabilization problem. In the case when the measurement is to be transmitted through the communication channel, the duality no longer holds and the problem becomes much harder. The state estimation problem is this case is left unsolved. This is why we consider 90 percent of this objective is achieved. This unsolved problem is still in our mind and we hope that a breakthrough will be found in near future. The study towards objective 3 is also successful. The output feedback stabilization problem can be decomposed or separated into the state feedback stabilization problem and state estimation problem. In the case when the "innovation" is transmitted through the communication channel, the stabilization problem and the estimation problem are dual to each other. The duality and separation then give a very nice solution to the output feedback stabilization problem. In the case when the duality does not hold, i.e., when the measurement is to be transmitted through the communication channel, the problem is still open, because the corresponding estimation problem is unsolved. This is why we say we achieved 90 percent of this objective. We are continuing our research towards objectives 2 and 3. As soon as a breakthrough is obtained for the estimation problem, the output feedback stabilization problem can then be solved by using the separation principle.

16208414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208414.value: When a MIMO system is under state feedback control and when the control signals are transmitted using a MIMO transducer, the closed-loop system can be stabilized if and only if a condition is satisfied. This condition is in terms of the cyclic topological entropies of the system and the capacities of the subchannels in the transducer, expressed using majorization partial order. This result holds when the subchannels have features like Guassian additive noise and fading. This indeed gives the fundamental limitation of a information constrained MIMO channel in feedback stabilization.

16208414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208414.value: This project opens the door to further future research. The results we have obtained in this project are mostly for continuous-time systems. We did some investigation for discrete-time systems with the expectation that the results should be analogous. However it turns out that the matter in the discrete-time case is very different and is much harder. We are continuing the research in this direct now. Another direction for further study is to consider other channel features such as quantization and delay. We plan to propose a future RGC project for such a study.

16208514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208514.value: Customer loyalty is critically important for a company to gain a competitive advantage and achieve sustainable profits. Earning the loyalty of merely 5% of customers can improve profits by almost 100% for traditional retailers. The rapid development of Web technologies reinforces the importance of loyalty because of today’s significantly lower switching barriers. Prior studies have shown that 70% of users rely on multiple search engines and nearly 50% of new customers of an e-commerce site subsequently switch to other sites. Therefore, effectively tracking customer loyalty and understanding how and why loyalty changes and customers leave have become indispensable for online service providers facing fierce market competition In this project, we plan to develop a new interactive visualization system which will enable analysts to track the dynamics of customer loyalty over time. Our system will provide a visual summary of customers’ switching behavior and enable analysts to define and assign customers to categories such as “hard-core loyals” and “switchers”. The analysts can then visually track how individual customers change categories over time. We will also study the competitions among different service providers on social media and their effects on customer loyalty. We propose to conduct case studies and interview domain experts to validate the usefulness of our technique for understanding customer loyalty and switching behavior. The completion of this project will result in novel visualization techniques for customer loyalty data, an open-source system for customer loyalty analysis, and new insights into customer behavior. 客戶忠誠度對一個公司獲得競爭優勢和實現可持續的利潤有非常重要的意義。根據研究，對傳統零售商，贏得僅僅5%的客戶的忠誠度就可以 提高利潤近100％。網絡技術的迅速發展讓轉換產品或服務的障礙顯著降低，忠誠度變得更加重要。現有的研究表明，70％的用戶依賴於多個搜索引擎，而且近50％的電子商務網站的客戶會隨後轉到其他網站。因此，在線服務商在面對激烈市場競爭時，必然需要有效跟蹤客戶的忠誠度，並了解忠誠度的變化情況以及客戶離開的原因。 在這個項目中，我們計劃開發一種新的交互式可視化系統，能讓分析師動態跟蹤客戶忠誠度的變化情況。我們的系統會 提供客戶轉換行為的可視化概覽，使分析人員能夠定義並將客戶分成不同的類別，如“鐵桿忠誠者”和“切換用戶”。 然後分析人員可以直觀地跟蹤個體客戶如何隨著時間變化改變其類別。 我們也將研究不同的服務供應商在社會媒體上的競爭以及這些競爭對顧客忠誠度的影響。我們將進行案例研究和采訪 領域專家來驗證我們的技術在幫助理解客戶的忠誠度和轉換行為方面的有用性。 該項目的建成，將產生能分析客戶忠誠度數據的新的可視化技術，和一個客戶忠誠度分析的開源系統，以及對客戶行為的新的見解。

16208514.label: Realisation of objectives
16208514.value: All the objectives of the project have been achieved. O1: Derive a set of design principles to address the most important questions raised by experts in loyalty analysis. We have worked closely with three domain experts (two applied scientists and a software development engineer), from the search department of a corporation for eight months. We have identified 5 design principles to address the most important questions raised by experts in loyalty analysis: 1) User Flow Revelation; 2) Intuitive Storytelling Metaphor; 3) Multi-Scale Visual Representation; 4) Interactive Pattern Unfolding; 5) Comparative Analysis. O2: Design a set of novel visualization techniques to interactively reveal the evolving patterns of customer loyalty and defection. We have designed a set of novel visualization techniques to interactively reveal the evolving patterns of customer loyalty and defection. These visualization techniques include a flow view which is based on a flow metaphor for visualizing the dynamics of user loyalty, and density map and world cloud to facilitate the in-depth analysis of user loyalty. O3: Apply the techniques to real data and conduct case studies and user studies to evaluate the techniques We have applied the techniques to a real dataset which consists of top 100,000 active customers in the US market during the first week of July 2012 from the massive search logs, as suggested by the domain experts and some interesting findings related to customer behavior have been obtained. We have also conducted in-depth interviews with five experts to evaluate the usability of the system, including four program managers and a software development engineer (SDE) from the search department of a company. Case studies and the interview with domain experts demonstrated the usefulness of the flow view for showing the overall loyalty trend along the time. Besides investigating the customer behaviors based on the search log data, we have also investigated the customer loyalty problems in different application domains and from different perspectives: 1. The learning behaviors of the students based on the MOOC (Massive Open Online Courses) data. When students take a course and watch videos, they also show some loyalty behaviors (i.e., whether they stick to the course or video). We have developed a system VisMOOC which help instructors analyze the clickstream data from MOOCs. It can show how engaging a MOOC video is and how many students skip part of the videos. The system VisMOOC has won two awards: HKICT'15 best innovation silver award and APICTA'15 merit award in E-leaning. In addition, we have developed PeakVizor, which can analyze the correlation between the loyalty of students to a video segment and learning behaviors of students. Furthermore, we have developed DropoutSeer, a visualization system to predict whether a student will drop out a MOOC course (i.e., loyal to a course) or not and also provide the relationship between the online learning activity and dropout behavior of learners. 2. The loyalty of a BitCoin Exchange to its partners in the BitCoin Market. We have developed BitExTract, a visual analytics system which can extract intelligence of Bitcoin exchanges. Bitcoin exchanges provide the dominant trading platform where most ordinary customers exchange fiat currency for Bitcoins and vice versa. A huge number of Bitcoins have been transferred between exchanges, thus building up a sophisticated network of transactions. Our system enable analysts to investigate the relationships among Bitcoin exchanges and shed lights on the different trading mechanisms, especially how stable (i.e., "loyal") of one Bitcoin exchange to its trading partners. 3. Customer reviews of restaurants in Yelp. With the rapid development of e-commerce, there is an increasing number of online review websites, such as Yelp, to help customers make better purchase decisions. We have developed E-Comp, a visualization system which allows users to easily compare local businesses at different levels of details based on the rating score and text comments by other customers. It can shed lights on why customers choose to visit a restaurant multiple times or decide not to visit a restaurant anymore. O4. Release an open-source version of our system so that people can freely test it and apply it to other similar business data. Multiple of our system has been open-sourced and people can freely test and use it. For example, our VisMOOC system is available at https://github.com/HKUST-VISLab/vismooc-front-end. The E-Comp system is available at https://github.com/jiayouwyhit/E-Comp-EuroVis18. The code of LoyalTracker cannot be released to the public due to the IP right of Microsoft as it contains property code from Microsoft.

16208514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208514.value: 1. We have developed LoyalTracker, a visual analytics system to track user loyalty and switching behavior towards multiple search engines from the vast amount of user log data. We derived a set of design principles to address the most important questions raised by the domain experts of loyalty analysis and proposed several novel visualizations. The paper has been published in our top venue IEEE VAST conference and won Honorable Mention for Best Paper Award. [J1] 2. We have developed VisMOOC, a visual analytical system to help instructors and educational analysts understand online learning behaviors related to course videos using clickstream data from Coursera. It can analyze which parts of the video have been viewed by students for multiple times and which parts of the video are often skipped by students. [C1] 3. We have developed PeakVizor, a visual analytic system to help course instructors and education experts to analyze peaks in video clickstreams in MOOCs from different aspects. It can show the correlation between loyalty and learning behaviors. We found that learners with high grades generally tend to be highly loyal, that is, they click on the peaks more often and interact with the key content in the videos actively. [J3] 4. We have developed E-Comp, a visual analytics system based on online reviews like Yelp, to help customers compare local businesses at different levels of details. Both the numerical rating and review text have been considered. It can shed lights on why customers choose some restaurants and give them high scores and why they feel some restaurants no longer attractive and decide not to visit anymore. [J4] 5. We have developed BitExTract, a visual analysis system to help users explore, analyze, and compare the evolution of different Bitcoin exchanges. It can shed lights on the evolution and trends in the Bitcoin market, and gain hints for how loyal a Bitcoin exchange is to its partners. [J5] 6. We have studied other problems related to customer loyalty and developed visual analytics system to analyze the co-occurrence problem in urban computing [J2], the skyline problem in high dimensional data analysis [J6], and the bi-directional movement behaviors of people [C2].

16208514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208514.value: Customer loyalty is a very broad topic. In this project, we focus on the customer loyalty to a search engine, a MOOC course, a restaurant, or a Bitcoin exchange. More research is needed to generalize our techniques to other application domains.

16208514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208514.value: In this project we analyzed the customer loyalty problem in different domains (e.g., search engines, MOOC courses, restaurants, and Bitcoin exchanges) and developed multiple visual analytics systems to help domain experts analyze a large amount of data related to customer behaviors, especially their loyalty to a business or a partner. Some novel visualization techniques have been developed and new findings have been obtained.

16208614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208614.value: The big Internet companies like Google, Apple, and Microsoft are driving the gigantic demand of 3D reconstruction of very large-scale urban environment. They are proposing competing 3D platforms for 3D Maps applications, not only from aerial views but also from street views on the ground level! A variational approach to 3D surface reconstruction from multiple views is the state of the art vision methodology from input overlapping images to the texture-mapped models of multiple levels of details. However, in order to produce visual high-quality results, the approach usually assumes a well-structured multiple views, that is, the non-redundancy of views, the accurate camera geometries, and the uniform distribution of the camera configuration . These assumptions can be hold in a small scale laboratory setting, unfortunately, not for the largely available collections of images from the Internet, the unstructured multiple views. The unstructured Internet views are captured by different users, at different space time, and with different image resolutions. In this project, we propose a graph-based methodology to solve the challenges from the unstructured collections of views for a large-scale city three-dimensional reconstruction. We start with a large-scale quasi-dense structure from motion for obtaining registered and sufficiently dense point clouds. Then we carry out a preliminary over-sampling of the reconstructed point clouds into small portions of connected subsets of point clouds. After that, from the set of image pairs and the set of point portions, we build up a bipartite graph from these two disjoint sets, then we introduce a bigraph sparsification method to compute a small subset of image pairs from those computed in multi-view stereo. This drastically reduces both the time and memory complexity of a costly discrete variational stereo optimization algorithm. 16208814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208814.value: Morphing is a special visual effect that provides a smooth, natural transition between a pair of images or videos. It often involves a combination of warping the image domain and blending the pixel colors. Morphing has been extensively studied in the fields of computer graphics and image processing with easily over one thousand research papers on the topic and a number of applications, particularly in film and entertainment. The main challenge in achieving good image morphs is to create a map that aligns corresponding image elements. We believe that there is an opportunity to make significant contributions in this area by helping automate this often tedious task. We propose an algorithm that creates a map by optimizing the compatibility of corresponding warped image neighborhoods using an adaptation of structural similarity. The optimization is regularized by a thin-plate spline, and may be guided by a few user-drawn points. We parameterize the map over a halfway domain and show that this representation offers many benefits. The map is able to treat the image pair symmetrically, model simple occlusions continuously, span partially overlapping images, and define extrapolated correspondences. We also propose methods to improve the morphs by optimizing quadratic motion paths and by seamlessly extending content across the image boundaries. We parallelize the algorithm on a GPU to achieve a responsive interface. Our current algorithm for morphing image pairs attains good results with little effort, showing that this is a promising direction. We will further refine these ideas and extend them to morphing video pairs (animations). In addition to developing the basic morphing algorithm for both images and videos, we plan to investigate a number of extensions and applications, such as portrait morphing and generation of optimized slide show sequences. 高精度，最優化的圖像和視頻變形技術 圖像或視頻的變形是指把壹副圖像或壹段視頻以壹種自然流暢的方式變換到另壹幅圖像或壹段視頻的特效技術。它通常包含了幾何變形和顏色插值兩個方面的內容。該課題在計算機圖形學和圖像處理領域已被深入研究，有多達上千篇論文和眾多應用，尤其是在電影和娛樂產業的有著廣泛的應用。 獲得好的圖像變形特效的關鍵在於創建兩幅圖像間精確的對應關系。傳統上這個過程依賴於手工完成，而我們相信有機會可以使這個繁瑣的手動指定過程自動化，從而大大改進變形技術。我們提出了壹個算法可以通過最優化兩個相互匹配的扭曲的鄰域的結構相似性來自動獲得兩幅圖像間的對應關系。這個優化過程同時受薄膜樣條函數的約束，以及允許用戶指定少量的點作為指導。我們將這個對應函數定義在壹個中間域上，因為中間域展示出了以下優點：對兩副輸入圖像對稱處理；可以解決簡單的遮擋問題；具有外推性。除此之外，我們還提出了更多的方法優化圖像變形技術，包括采用二次曲線作為變形路徑，無縫擴展圖像邊界，采用GPU並行加速算法實現可交互的用戶界面。 目前我們的算法已經可以利用非常少的用戶輸入獲得兩幅圖像間高質量的變形動畫。這顯示出了該研究方向的前景。我們將繼續優化算法，並擴展該算法到兩個視頻間的變形。 除了研究圖像和視頻變形技術的基礎算法，我們還將探索壹系列潛在的擴展和應用，比如肖像畫的變形，圖像展示最優化順序的獲取等。

16208814.label: Realisation of objectives
16208814.value: We have achieved the four objectives set forth in this proposal. [Objectives 2 and 3 were duplicated due to a typo on the proposal.] More specifically: 1) We presented a variety of contributions to the wellstudied problem of generating high-quality morphs between two images. The novel halfway parameterization for establishing correspondences provides a way to handle simple occlusions without compromising the optimization process. Our similarity metric allows neighborhoods with the same structure to be matched, even those with distinct color distributions and geometric distortions. An interactive user interface, allows artists to quickly specify desired point-correspondences to achieve the desired morphs. We also introduced a framework for multiscale combination of shape and color attributes from a pair of images related by a correspondence map. We have shown that this space of combinations spans a rich variety of hybrid images. 2,3) We presented a new approach to create smooth transitions between videos of different objects. The main new issues that we had to address to handle videos were related to video synchronization and temporal coherence of the mapping. We show how our interface and algorithms allow a user to efficiently morph between challenging input videos. 4) To achieve the above objective for both image and video sequences, we designed a fast coarse-to-fine optimization algorithm that runs entirely on the GPU. We also introduced a fast, per-pixel iterative search algorithm for inverting the mapping does not require mesh rasterization. 5) We explored extensions in the mentioned application domains and decided to pursue the following two: a) A framework for multiscale combination of shape and color attributes from a pair of images. This approach allowed an artist significantly more control to manipulate the transitions and was particularly well suited for protrait morphs. b) We used the halfway parameterization approach in estabilishing correspondence for image quality accessment. We were able to determine the similarity of retargeted images using this approach.

16208814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208814.value: The main outcome of this work was the development of novel correspondence and morphing techniques that improved on the state-of-the-art on image and video morphing. Their results showed that the halfway domain parameterization successfully maps correspondences among images and videos in many scenarios where there is no significant disocclusion. It proved to be an effective method for other applications as well, including our editing system to provide further control for non-affine combination of images based on color and geometry, and image quality assessment. Please refer to 5.3 for details on specific contributions. Additionally, we explored related image correspondence methods based on deep learning for the application of colorization. The advantage of these new approaches over the traditional halfway parameterization is added robustness in matching, particularly in case of occlusions. The drawback is that it does not allow for a continuous mapping, which is is not suitable to some applications. Note that, as shown in the proposal's implementation results, the research for some of the contributions started in parallel with the proposal and were published prior to the official start date, which was delayed further by six months. Since they are key in achieving some of the listed objectives, I still listed them here for your consideration.

16208814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208814.value: We are currently exploring ways to handle more complex occlusions using the halfway domain framework. If successful, this approach will be more powerful. We are also exploring hybrid correspondence methods that use both the halfway domain as well as deep learning based methods for correspondence in other applications where a continuous mapping is not required. This would make these techniques even more widely applicable.

16208814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208814.value: Morphing between images/videos is a long-studied problem, addressed in numerous publications since the 1980s. The most challenging step is to establish a good correspondence map between the input images/videos, as this is crucial to prevent ghosting artifacts during the transition. In this work we made significant advances to the state-of-the-art in image and video morphing by proposing fast semi-automatic frameworks that allow users to easily generate morphs between images, videos, and control the transition between the inputs in a more natural way. The research has been publicized at top graphics venues and the implementation has been available online.

16208914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208914.value: Degrading/removing endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) and pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) and controlling disinfection by-products (DBPs) are two emerging issues in supplying safe drinking water. For recalcitrant EDCs/PPCPs, their oxidative degradation is often achieved by the UV/peroxide process producing hydroxyl radicals. However, the radical production is not efficient and requires excessive peroxide dosing, resulting a high level of unreacted peroxide in the treated water that has to be removed. In drinking water treatment, chlorine is often used to quench the unreacted peroxide and provide disinfection residuals to protect the drinking water from bacteria regrowth or being re-contaminated in water distribution systems. This UV/peroxide treatment followed by chlorine dosing not only requires large peroxide and chlorine dosages but may also lead to increases in the formation of DBPs. The UV/chlorine process uses UV light to split aqueous chlorine to hydroxyl radicals and chlorine atoms, both of which are very strong oxidants. The UV/chlorine process was recently found more efficient, compared to the UV/peroxide process, in producing the reactive radical species at acidic to neutral pH and the remaining chlorine can be used directly for providing the residual protection. It is now being considered as an emerging technology capable of degrading a large number of trace organic pollutants. However, much less is known about the effectiveness of the UV/chlorine process in degrading recalcitrant EDCs/PPCPs, compared with our knowledge about the UV/peroxide process. Little is known about the pathways and byproducts of the degradation by the UV/chlorine process, which is expected to be complicated due to the co-presence of the two very reactive radical species. Little is known about whether the UV/chlorine oxidation will change the properties of NOM, which is also ubiquitously present in drinking water. The consequential formation of DBPs and the possible alteration of genotoxicity of the water after the subsequent chlorine contact for distribution system protection are also unclear. This proposed study will fill the above knowledge gaps to improve our fundamental understanding on the UV/chlorine process in degrading EDCs/PPCPs and in the formation of byproducts during the UV/chlorine treatment and after the subsequent chlorine contact. The knowledge acquired will generalize recommendations to the selection between the UV/chlorine and UV/peroxide processes under different drinking water treatment conditions to take advantage of the produced chlorine atoms to effectively degrade EDCs/PPCPs, while the formation of DBPs can be minimized. 內分泌干擾物（EDCs）及藥物與個人護理品（PPCPs）的降解/去除和消毒副產物（DBPs）的控制是安全飲用水供給中的兩個新興問題。UV/過氧化氫過程由於能產生羥基自由基，通常能夠達到對頑固型EDCs或PPCPs的氧化降解。然而，該過程中自由基的產生效率不高，因此需要投加過量的過氧化氫，導致已處理的水中仍殘留高濃度未反應的過氧化氫需被去除。在飲用水處理中，氯常被用作未反應的過氧化氫的終止劑並提供給水系統的消毒餘氯以防止飲用水中的細菌再生或飲用水的再污染。這種在UV/過氧化氫過程後續投加氯的處理技術不僅需要投加大量的過氧化氫和氯，而且可能增大消毒副產物的生成量。 UV/氯過程運用紫外光將水中的氯組分分裂為羥基自由基和氯原子這兩種極強的氧化劑。近來的研究表明，與UV/過氧化氫過程相比，UV/氯過程在酸性至中性pH條件下具有更高的活性自由基組分生成效率，且剩餘的氯能夠直接用來提供後續的餘氯保護。UV/氯過程已被認為是一種能夠降解大量的微量有機污染物的新興技術。然而，與對UV/過氧化氫過程的瞭解程度相比，我們對UV/氯過程降解頑固型EDCs和PPCPs的有效性瞭解尚淺。由於羥基自由基和氯自由基的聯合作用，UV/氯過程降解污染物的路徑和副產物的生成可能更為複雜，而目前我們對其知之甚少。天然有機物（NOM）是飲用水中無處不在的物質，UV/氯的氧化過程對其特性的改變尚未被探究。為了保護給水管網系統而投加氯所帶來的消毒副產物的間接產生以及水的基因毒性改變同樣不為人知。 本研究計畫將填補以上知識空缺，提升我們對UV/氯過程降解EDCs和PPCPs的基本瞭解，提升我們對UV/氯處理過程和後續氯投加過程中副產物產生的基本認識。本研究所得到的結果將為不同飲用水處理條件下UV/氯過程和UV/過氧化氫過程之間的選擇提供一個推廣性的建議，充分利用UV/氯過程中產生的氯自由基，在更有效的去除EDCs和PPCPs的同時減少消毒副產物產生。

16208914.label: Realisation of objectives
16208914.value: The project started on the date as scheduled. Objective 1 was completed. Tests were conducted with 34 pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) to examine their degradation under different conditions and a kinetic model was built to calculate the contributions from different mechanisms in synthetic water. The degradation and the contributions of HO• and reactive chlorine species (RCS) were compounds’ structure specific. A good linear relationship was found between the RCS reactivity and negative values of the Hammett constant for aromatic PPCPs, indicating that electron-donating groups promote the attack of benzene derivatives by RCS. Tests were also conducted to investigate the PPCP removal from the UV/chlorine process, compared with that of the UV/hydrogen peroxide process at environmentally-relevant concentrations in three authentic sand-filtered natural waters. Ten target PPCPs were included. Both hydroxyl radicals and RCS were found to contribute to the observed PPCP degradation. The removal efficiencies of chlorine- and UV-resistant PPCPs such as carbamazepine and caffeine in the UV/chlorine process were 2–3 times greater than in the UV/hydrogen peroxide process in waters lack of ammonia. In ammonia-rich waters, the UV/chlorine process was still 5–7% more effective than the UV/hydrogen peroxide process. The results formulated two journal papers. The effects of various conditions on the degradation of ibuprofen, DEET, metronidazole, nalidixic acid and caffeine, by the UV/chlorine process were quantified. The degradation rate of ibuprofen, nalidixic acid and caffeine increased monotonically with increasing chlorine dosage from 0 to 100 μM and the degradation rate of DEET was less affected by the chlorine concentrations. The degradation was faster at mild acid and neutral pH than that at basic pH. Temperature and chloride concentration did not significantly affect the degradation. The degradation was decreased by the presence of natural organic matter (NOM) and bicarbonate. Both HO• and Cl• contributed to the degradation, and the contribution of Cl• increased with increasing pH from 6 to 9. It was interestingly found that the co-presence of bromide enhanced the degradation. Additional tests were conducted to reveal the effect of bromide with 9 selected PPCPs. The observed loss rate constants of 7 PPCPs at 10 μM bromide were 1.6−23 times of those observed in the absence of bromide (except for iopromide and ibuprofen). Bromide plays multiple roles in PPCP degradation. It reacts rapidly with free chlorine to produce a trace amount of free bromine to degrade some PPCPs. Bromide also reduces the level of HO• and change the RCS to bromine-containing species, which resulted in decreases in ibuprofen degradation and enhancement in carbamazepine and caffeine degradation, respectively. The results formulated three journal papers. Objective 2 was completed. The pathways, intermediates and products of selected PPCPs, including ibuprofen, trimethoprim and carbamazepine degradation by the UV/chlorine process under representative conditions were identified. For ibuprofen, the degradation was initiated by HO•-induced hydroxylation and Cl•-induced chlorine substitution, and sustained through decarboxylation, demethylation, chlorination and ring cleavage reactions to form more stable products. Significant amounts of chlorinated intermediates/byproducts were formed, which was due to the formation of hydroxylated intermediates that were more reactive toward electrophilic attack by chlorine species. Four unknown chlorinated products were identified. The known disinfection by-products (DBPs) comprised 17.4% of the TOCl. The pathways of IBP degradation were proposed. The results formulated one journal paper. For trimethoprim, the RCS reacted with trimethoprim to form chlorinated products at m/z of 325. The hydroxylation and demethylation of m/z 325 generated m/z 327 and m/z 341, through the further oxidation. Meanwhile, reactions of m/z 325 with HO• and RCS or free chlorine generated dichlorinated and hydroxylated products (i.e., m/z 377). All the chlorinated products could be further depleted to produce products with less degree of halogenation Hydroxylation mainly took place in the 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzyl moiety while hydrogen abstraction occurred in the methylene group by the radical attack. The results formulated one journal paper. For carbamazepine, 24 transformation products were identified. The products indicate that the 10,11-double bond and aromatic ring in CBZ are the sites most susceptible to attack by radicals. Subsequent reaction produces hydroxylated and chlorinated aromatic ring products. Four specific products were quantified and their evolution was related with the chlorine dose, pH, and NOM concentration. CBZ-10,11-epoxide, the main quantified transformation product, was observed with a peak transformation yield of 3–32% depending on the conditions. The more toxic acridine was formed with peak transformation yields of 0.4–1%. All four quantified products together amounted to a peak transformation yield of 34.5%. The results formulated one journal paper. Objective 3 was completed. Tests were conducted to understand the significance of halogenated DBP formation from EDCs/PPCPs after the UV/chlorine treatment followed by subsequent chlorination, compared to that after the UV/peroxide treatment followed by chlorine quenching and provision of chlorine residuals using selected target PPCPs including IBP and DEET. For the UV/chlorine process, most of the DBPs were formed during the UV/chlorine co-exposure period and the subsequent chlorination further increased their formation. Trichloromethane, 1,1,1-trichloro-2- propanone and dichloroacetic acid were the major known DBPs. In comparison to the UV/peroxide process accompanied with post-chlorination, the formation of DBPs and TOCl in the UV/chlorine process together with post-chlorination was 5%–63% higher, likely due to the generation of more DBP precursors from the attack of RCS, in addition to hydroxyl radicals. The results formulated one conference presentation and one journal paper. Objective 4 was completed. Tests were conducted to compare the influences of UV/chlorine and UV/peroxide advanced oxidation of NOM at the equivalent degradation of two model micropollutants on the formation of DBPs and toxicity during post-chlorination. At 90% degradation of carbamazepine, the UV/chlorine process resulted in comparable yields of dichloroacetic acid, trichloroacetic acid, chloroform, chloral hydrate, dichloroacetonitrile, trichloropropanone and TOCl during the post-chlorination, compared to the UV/peroxide process. The cytotoxicity with the UV/chlorine process was 32% lower than with the UV/peroxide process, however, the genotoxicity was similar. At the 90% degradation of atrazine, the UV/chlorine process increased the chloroacetic acid yields by 35−81% but did not increase the yields of other four known DBPs and TOCl, compared to the UV/peroxide process. The cytotoxicity and genotoxicity with the UV/chlorine process were 22‒27% lower than those with the UV/peroxide process, likely due to the selective destruction of the precursors of cytotoxic and genotoxic DBPs by RCS. The TOCl yields were positively correlated to the decreases in the specific UV absorbance at 254 nm and humic-like fluorescence. The TOCl yields also exhibited a linear relationship with the genotoxicity. Although the UV/chlorine process increases the formation of some DBPs under certain circumstances, compared to the UV/peroxide process, it does not enhance the genotoxicity and even decreases the cytotoxicity. In addition, the presence of bromide shifted the chlorinated DBPs into the brominated ones. On the other hand, the presence of ammonia exerts two opposite effects: In the chloramination regime, DBP formation decreased with increasing ammonia concentration; while in the breakpoint chlorination regime, increasing ammonia concentration increased DBP formation after the UV/chlorine process. The results formulated one manuscript submitted and 3 conference presentations.

16208914.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208914.value: The major findings obtained formulated 8 highly-cited (289 times, average citations per item of 36.13) journal papers (#1–8) and 9 presentations (#1–9) in nine international conferences. We are also working on another 2 journal papers, one (Journal publication #9) submitted and one under preparation. This project trained 3 postgraduate students at HKUST: 2 obtained their MPhil degrees in 2015 and 2016 and the other one obtained his PhD degree in 2018. This study also involved close collaboration between HKUST and Sun Yat-Sen University. Major findings are: The degradation of PPCPs was attributed to hydroxyl radicals and/or reactive chlorine species (RCS) and was compounds’ structure specific (Journal papers #1–3, 6–8 and Conference presentations #3–6). PPCPs with electron-donating groups promote the attack by RCS (Journal paper #6). The degradation was faster at mild acid and neutral pH than that at basic pH and the contribution of RCS increased with increasing pH. The removal of chlorine- and UV-resistant PPCPs in the UV/chlorine process were greater than in the UV/peroxide process (Journal paper #2). The degradation was affected by the presence of natural organic matter, bicarbonate and ammonia (Conference presentation #8). Bromide plays multiple roles in the degradation (Journal paper #8). It reacts with free chlorine to produce free bromine to degrade some PPCPs. Bromide also transforms HO• and RCS to bromine-containing species, which resulted in decreases in ibuprofen degradation and enhancement in carbamazepine and caffeine degradation. The degradation of ibuprofen, trimethoprim and carbamazepine was initiated by HO•-induced hydroxylation and Cl•-induced chlorine substitution, and sustained through decarboxylation, demethylation, chlorination and ring cleavage to form stable products (Journal papers #1, 3, 5 and Conference presentations #4, 5). More chlorinated intermediates/DBPs were formed after the PPCP degradation by the UV/chlorine process, compared to the UV peroxide process, due to the formation of more hydroxylated intermediates that were more reactive toward chlorine attack (Journal paper #4 and Conference presentation #7). The byproduct formation also depended on chlorine doses, pH, and NOM and ammonia concentrations (Journal papers #1 and 6). The UV/chlorine process, compared to the UV/peroxide process, gave comparable or slightly higher yields of some DBPs and TOCl from NOM during post-chlorination (Journal paper #9 and Conference presentations #1, 2). Nonetheless, the UV/chlorine process did not enhance the genotoxicity and even decreased the cytotoxicity.

16208914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208914.value: In this project and using fluorescence spectroscopy, we observed some changes in NOM by the UV/chlorine and UV/peroxide processes and their correlations with the DBP formation. However, the information provided by fluorescence spectroscopy is very limited. To have a better understanding of the formation of DBPs and their precursors, the transformation of NOM should be evaluated by more advanced methods. This formulated another funded GRF proposal entitled “Investigation of changes of DOM’s characteristics and chlor(am)ination by-product formation potential due to micropollutant abatement by UV/peroxide using Q-TOF-MS(/MS) methods”. UV-LED is an emerging UV light source that provides versatile wavelengths of UV lights to drive the UV/chlorine processes. However, this wavelength dependency is unknown and deserves investigation. Another RGC/GRF proposal entitled “Degradation of emerging micropollutants in water supply by optimal UV-LED photolysis of chlorine and chloramine” was submited and funded in 2017. This study focused on the formation of regulated DBPs from Suwannee River NOM only. However, orgnaic matter from different sources such as reclaimed water may provide different DBP precursors and produced other emerging DBPs more toxic to human, which deserve further investigation. Some preliminary tests were conducted and used to seek for additional funding.

16208914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208914.value: Controlling micropollutants such as endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) and pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) and reducing the formation of disinfection by-products (DBPs) are two emerging issues in supplying safe drinking water. In this research, we proposed an UV/chlorine process, which uses UV light to split aqueous chlorine to hydroxyl radicals and chlorine-containing radicals, to be a better solution, compared to the commonly-used UV/peroxide process, to achieve the control of both micropollutants and DBPs. In this project, we have extensively investigated the effectiveness of the UV/chlorine process in degrading recalcitrant EDCs/PPCPs. We understood deeply the pathways and byproducts of the degradation by the UV/chlorine process. We disclosed how the radicals produced in the UV/chlorine process interact with natural organic matter and other impurities in drinking water and the consequential formation of DBPs and the possible alteration of toxicity of the treated water. This project not only largely advanced our fundamental knowledge about the chemistry of the UV/chlorine process in degrading EDCs/PPCPs and in the formation of byproducts but also generalized recommendations to the selection between the UV/chlorine and UV/peroxide processes under different drinking water treatment conditions very useful in real-world practices.

16209014.label: Project Objectives

16209014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209014.value: We propose to develop algorithms that enable a robotic system to learn visuomotor transformations describing how the image projections of the local surface at the end effector of a robot arm change with the arm's pose. We propose to base these algorithms around reinforcement learning to maximize visual consistency. This work will extend prior work in learning visuomotor transformations by expanding from point to surface-based transformations. It will also remove the requirement to mark the end effector with explicit visual markers. A key advantage of this approach is that the algorithms developed will be self-calibrating. Visuomotor transformations are learned as the arm moves through the environment. This will also enable the system to adapt to changes in configuration. The framework presented here may also lead to new insights into the principles guiding the development of neurons discovered in the ventral premotor cortex of macaque monkeys, whose visual receptive fields are anchored to the arm and hand. 隨著機械手的運動，機械手末端平面的圖像投影亦會隨之運動，我們提出開發一種可以使得機器人系統學習如何表示上述視覺運動轉換關係的算法。我們所提出的算法將基於強化學習來最大化圖像投影的視覺一致性。相較於傳統的基於機械手末端點的轉換表示方法，我們的工作嘗試將其拓展為基於末端平面的轉換表示，從而去除了對於機械手末端使用視覺標記物進行顯式標記的要求。我們所採取的的方法的一個顯著優勢在於它是一個自校正系統。隨著機器人系統在環境中進行運動，我們提出的算法可以領機器人系統逐漸學習到視覺運動轉換的關係。這可以使得機器人系統對其安裝或配置改變進行自適應。我們提出的這一學習算法同樣也可能為研究短尾猴腹側運動前皮層內接受野錨定于手臂的神經元的發展過程帶來一些新的見解。

16209014.label: Realisation of objectives
16209014.value: Both objectives were achieved. Our first objective was the development of a mathematical algorithm for learning the visuomotor transformations required for visually guided reaching by autonomous robots. We developed an algorithm that enables a robot to learn the visuomotor transformation from its joint angle space to visual space. The learned transformation can accurately predict location and shape of robot end effector’s image projection. using the concept of local visual consistency. There were several key innovations of this work, in comparison to previous work. First, the algorithm approximates the end effector by a planar region, rather than a point, in 3-D space. This enables us to extract and represent more visual information about the end effector than just position, such as orientation and size. It also relaxes the requirement that the end effector location be marked unambiguously by a known marker that is visible globally across all frames. Second, the algorithm uses spatially and temporally local, rather than global, measures of image consistency. This means that we do not require a predefined static marker be attached to the robot arm to enable the localization of the end effector in the image. This local consistency measure also enables our algorithm to adapt to changes in the end effector’s appearance. This work was reported in the IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems in 2016. We extended this work further We propose a biologically inspired model that enables a humanoid robot to learn how to track its end effector by integrating visual and proprioceptive cues as it interacts with the environment. A key novel feature of this model is the incorporation of sensorimotor prediction, where the robot predicts the sensory consequences of its current body motion as measured by proprioceptive feedback. The robot develops the ability to perform smoothly track the hand as it performs reaching movements, both in the presence and absence of visual input, and to track exteroceptive visual motions. Our framework makes a number of advances over past work. First, our model does not require a fiducial marker to indicate the robot hand explicitly. Second, it does not require the forward kinematics of the robot arm to be known. Third, it does not depend upon pre-defined visual feature descriptors. These are learned during interaction with the environment. This work was reported at both the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks in 2018, as well as in the Frontiers in Neurobotics in 2018. Our second objective was to characterize this algorithm using a robot with a monocular vision system and a robot arm. These experiments were performed using a seven degrees of freedom robot built from SCHUNK PowerCube modules. The PowerCube modules come fitted with integrated control, regulating and power electronics, enabling them to be controlled easily by high level commands. The computer running the learning algorithm sends motor commands and receives feedback about the joint angles via a controller area network (CAN). A camera with 640 by 480 pixel resolution is mounted at a fixed location above robot arm. The focal length of the camera is 524 pixels. One pixel corresponds approximately to 0.196 degrees of visual angle. We also tested the algorithm using a humanoid robot, the iCub running in a simulation environment. The iCub arm had seven degrees of freedom as well. However, we did not actively control all of them. In the experiments with the Schunk arm, we controlled three degrees of freedom. With the iCub, we controlled four. Both scenarios are more general than the two degrees of freedom specified in the objective. Our robotic experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can learn location and shape of the image region corresponding to the end effector, and how it deforms as the arm moves randomly in front of the camera. Our experiments with the iCub demonstrated that the incorporation of prediction leads to better performance than without prediction. In addition, the predictions of our model match well qualitatively with the results of human psychophysical findings. In addition to the characterization with the robot arms, we also applied the algorithm to model eye movements as human users performed selection by reaching towards different hyperlinks while browsing the web. This enabled us to perform inference about the user intent. We incorporated it into a gaze-based web browser, as reported in the International Journal of Human Computer Interaction. The results of our robotic experiments were reported in both the IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems in 2016 and in Frontiers in Neurobotics in 2018.

16209014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209014.value: The work in this project resulted in several major findings. First, we developed an algorithm that enables a robot to learn a forward kinematic model describing the visuomotor transformation between robot arm joint angles and an ellipse bounding the image region corresponding to a robot arm end effector. The algorithm also enables the bounding ellipse to adapt to structural changes of the end effector. Our algorithm is based upon maximizing a measure of consistency based upon the distance between matching SIFT key points within the ellipses bounding image regions corresponding to the end effector in adjacent frames. Because this measure of image consistency is local in space and time, we do not require a predefined static marker be attached to the robot arm to enable the localization of the end effector in the image. Our experiment using the natural texture of the robot arm has demonstrated that no special preparation, e.g. specific markers, need be applied to a commercially available robot arm. It also demonstrates that the algorithm is robust to violations of the planar assumption, still attaining a high level of performance. Our algorithm was inspired by the adaptive behavior observed in bimodal (tactile–visual) neurons in the macaque ventral premotor cortex. Similar to experimental findings that the visual receptive fields of these neurons extend to cover a tool after use , our algorithm can adapt to the addition of a tool to the end effector. This increases its flexibility. Second, we proposed a model based on the Active Efficient Coding (AEC) framework that enables a robot to learn to track its end effector using a combination of visual and proprioceptive cues. Rather than simply concatenating the two sets of features, the proposed model predicts visual consequences of actions, which removes information correlated with proprioception from vision. The model enables a robot to learn to track an object for three cases: using both visual and proprioceptive cues corresponding to the typical case of end effector tracking, using only visual cues corresponding to tracking of an external independently moving object, and using pure proprioception corresponding to tracking of the end effector in darkness. We compared predictions of our model with findings from human psychophysical experiments studying the contribution of proprioception to human oculomotor control. Our model exhibits similar qualitative characteristics. For example, our results suggest that incorporating proprioception reduces phase delay. This characteristic of the human oculomotor system has been found repeatedly.

16209014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209014.value: Moving forward, it will be interesting to investigate how to extend the algorithm so that the region bounding the end effector can be more complex than an ellipse. For example, there may be situations where the ellipse is not a good estimate of the bounding region due to the shape of the end effector. In our current implementation, The ellipse converges to cover an area that strikes a balance between covering the entire end effector and excluding points not corresponding to the end effector. A more complex bounding region could better exclude points not corresponding to the end effector. Another future direction would be to further relax the planar assumption to enable more realistic representations of the end effector. Eventually, we would like to see whether the forward kinematic model learned here can be used to learn an inverse model to guide reaching behavior.

16209014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209014.value: This project has resulted in the development of algorithms that enable a robotic system to learn visuomotor transformations describing how the image projections of the local surface at the end effector of a robot arm change with the arm's pose. These algorithms are based around around reinforcement learning to maximize visual consistency. The work extends prior work in learning visuomotor transformations by expanding from point to surface-based transformations. It also removes the requirement to mark the end effector with explicit visual markers. A key advantage of this approach is that the algorithms developed are self-calibrating. Visuomotor transformations are learned as the arm moves through the environment. This enables the system to adapt to changes in configuration. We also studied the role of sensory prediction and multi-sensory fusion in this task. Our results suggest that both of these result in significant improvements in performance. We have validated these algorithms in both real and simulated environments. The proposed models have properties that are qualitatively similar to the characteristics of human eye-hand coordination. We hypothesize that this approach will enable robots with more robust operation, mimicking that of biological systems.

16209114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209114.value: Being an important example of distributed sensing and information collection and fusion, a wireless sensor network (WSN) typically consists of a number of sensor nodes working collaboratively to collect physical information, such as temperature, humidity, movement, chemical composition, from a physical region. Both research and applications of WSNs have been increasing tremendously in the last few years. Growing applications are found in, for example, unmanned aerial vehicles, mobile sensor networks, remote surgery, environment monitoring, smart grid and industrial automation. Despite the benefits wireless sensors offers, there are still many shortcomings WSNs have, e.g., wireless channels are subject to channel fading and interference, which may lead to data drops. Such defective channels may deteriorate estimation performance or even make the system unstable. The underpinning theory reveals that there is a tradeoff between transmission bit rate, bandwidth and transmission power. If higher transmission powers are used, then dropouts are less frequent. Most wireless sensors, however, use on-board batteries, which are difficult to replace or even impossible in some inaccessible territories. Since in many applications, wireless sensors are expected to work for several years without the replacement of batteries, energy conservation is of considerable importance, thus power control becomes critical. There are two important problems in the study of WSNs, namely, the estimation problem and the communication problem, which have traditionally been studied separately. An integrated approach which takes specific communication constraints into account in the estimation process will, in general, not only give better performance, but also provides us a direct insight into sensor's transmission power control policy given some specific communication constraints. As both the theoretic research and applications of WSNs grow rapidly, innovative and integrated analysis and design are urgently needed for the sensor power control in WSNs. This project, aiming at filling this gap, is composed of the following three main thrusts: 1) Build integrated and practical model for the communication channel, the relationship between transmission power, packet arrival probability and the estimation performance; 2) Investigate both periodic and state-dependent transmission power schedules; 3) Apply MDP method to sequentially optimize transmission power usage. In the past few years, the project team members have been working actively in the area of remote state estimation, sensor scheduling, sensitivity analysis and MDP, which have led to many published works in leading journals. These preliminary works and experiences enable us to carry out the project successfully. 無線感測器網絡是分佈式感知和信息收集與融合的一個重要例子。它通常由一定數量的感測器組成。這些感測器相互協作以在一定的物理區域收集物理信息（例如溫度，濕度，移動，化學組成）。過去的幾年間，對於無線感測器網絡的研究及其應用都取得了長足的進展。例如在無人機，移動感測器網絡，遠程手術，環境監測，智能電網，以及工業自動化等領域中，都可以找到越來越多的應用。 儘管無線感測器可以提供很多好處，它依然存在許多缺點。例如，無線通道受制於通道增益和干擾，會產生丟包，這些受影響的通道可能會損害估計效果，甚至導致系統的不穩定。現有的理論論證了我們需要在傳輸比特率，頻寬，以及傳輸功率間進行取捨。通常如果使用較高的傳輸功率，丟包現象將會減少。由於對於無線感測器來說，其使用的電池很難置換，甚至在一些區域不可能進行置換；而在一些應用中，通常希望無線感測器工作很多年而不進行電池的置換，因此對於能量的節省很重要。所以，功率的控制在無線感測器網絡中處於至關重要的地位。 在研究無線感測器網路的時候，有兩個主要的問題，即估計問題和通訊問題。這兩個問題在之前是被分開研究的。現在我們在估計問題中考慮了特定的通訊限制，這一綜合研究的方法不僅將提供更好的估計表現，也將使我們對在特定通訊限制下的感測器的傳輸功率控制策略有一個直觀的瞭解。 由於對無線感測器網絡的理論研究和應用方面的飛速發展，對於其中的感測器功率控制亟需創新型的綜合分析和設計着眼於填補這個空缺，當前的這個項目便是由以下三個目標推動：1）建立一個綜合和實用的通訊通道模型，並構建傳輸功率和估計效果的關聯模型。2）構建一個馬爾科夫決策過程的框架以解決最優功率控制規劃的問題；3）利用博弈論的方法研究多個感測器情境下的最優能量控制。 在過去的幾年間，我們的項目團隊已經在遠程估計，感測器規劃，敏感性分析以及馬爾科夫決策過程等領域做了很多工作，並在一些頂級期刊中發表了論文。這些前期工作的成果和經驗將使我們在實施當前項目時更加順利。

16209114.label: Realisation of objectives
16209114.value: We have made excellent progress with this funding. Following the original objectives of the project, we have successfully integrated state estimation and communication via transmission power scheduling. For a number of different application scenarios (e.g., remote estimation with smart sensors/normal sensors), we have constructed novel types of power scheduling protocols, derived the corresponding minimum mean-squared error estimate at theremote estimator, analyzed the communication power vs remote estimation quality tradeoffs, etc. In addition to the original objectives, we have successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as stochastic sensor activation, quickest change detection, etc. The results are fruitful which are summarized and published in 8 leading international journals and 4 leading international conferences. Two PhD students and one MPhil student are also trained during the project period.

16209414.label: Realisation of objectives
16209414.value: In this project, we focused on the roles of grain size (GS), grain boundary (GB) and A-M interface (INT) in the PT behavior of polycrystalline NiTi. Their contributions to the energetics and kinetics of PT are investigated from both theoretical and experimental point of views mainly through the following two Tasks. Task I. Fabrication and characterization of material’s structure and behavior: (1) NiTi nano polycrystalline samples with well controlled GS and semi-amorphous samples by severe plastic deformation (SPD) though cold rolling and proper heat treatment were fabricated. The key issues of the fabrication procedures were identified and clarified. (2) The micro- and nano-structures of the fabricated samples were characterized by advanced in-situ X-ray diffraction to gain information on the crystallographic changes of PT process such as the evolution of diffraction patterns. The grain size dependent diffraction profiles and the features of the lattice deformation inside a nano-grain were identified and interpreted and the critical effects of GS on the single domain formation were examined and verified by the experiment. (3) The macroscopic thermal and mechanical responses of the fabricated samples were obtained by performing monotonic and cyclic tests on the standard dog-bone tensile specimen. The important effects of GS on the macroscopic responses were quantified and examined. GS effects on the internal heat sources (hysteresis heat and latent heat), the temperature dependence of the stress, the cyclic stability were examined in the study. The objective of identifying the emergence of novel properties and behaviors of the polycrystal due to GS reduction were realized. The experimental results were summarized and analyzed and clear physical picture and understanding of the PT process inside a nanoscale grain were acquired, based on which a systematic comparison and verification with the modeling results in Task II can be realized. Task II. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulation of nano- and macro-scale phase transition responses were performed on the following three aspects. (1) Continuum, mechanism-based multiscaled methodology were adopted throughout this task. The phase transition in polycrystal is treated as a multiscale process from the grain (as the basic “cell” of the polycrystal) to the macroscopic level. In this task, theoretical analysis were perform in close parallel with the computation. Dimensional analysis weree employed to investigate the key quantitative features of the computational results. (2) at the grain level (“Core-shell” structure), we will study the increased contributions from both the constraint of the elastic non-transformable GB (the “shell”) and the A-M interface to the response of the transformable crystallite (the “Core”) as the GS is reduced. In the analysis and simulation, the GB is modeled as non-transformable linear elastic material, the crystallite is modelled as nonlinear elastic media with Landau-Ginzburg type nonlocal and non-convex strain energy density and the A-M interface is modeled as a transient zone of nanometer thickness separating high and low strain regions (phases). The mechanical responses such as stress-strain curve, strain distribution and the energy dissipation of the grain (cell) were quantified at this fundamental level. As the first step towards the understanding of the observed GS effects, direct relationship among the different length scales were established. Because of the gradual dominance of interfacial energy terms with the GS reduction, the traditional equations of state for PT of bulk crystallite must be revised significantly by incorporating the important effects of these nano-scale interfaces. Scaling laws were established among the governing parameters of the responses. In-depth understanding of the observed phenomena were achieved. Through comparison between experiment and analysis and further improvement of the experiment and the modelling, the roles of the nano interfaces in the observed size dependent phenomena were identified and verified. The established scaling relationship will in turn serve as a guideline to further improve the experimental work of the project. Physical insight into the size-dependent phenomenon and identification of the governing physical parameters have been achieved.

16209414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209414.value: In the aspects of experimental study of the project, in situ X-ray diffraction during loading and unloading is performed for samples of different grain sizes so as to investigate the effects of grain size (GS) on the stress-induced nanoscale phase transition mechanism in polycrystalline superelastic NiTi. It is shown that when the grain size is above 68 nm, the evolution of the diffraction profiles during loading and unloading exhibits well-defined distinct diffraction peaks with significant changes in their diffracted intensities corresponding to the nucleation and growth mechanism of B19' martensite (high strain) phase. However, when grain size falls below 68 nm, the evolution of diffraction peaks gradually degenerates from the multiple peaks mode to a continuous and reversible single peak shift mode. Such drastic changes in characteristics of diffraction peaks indicate a gradual change in the mechanism from traditional nucleation and growth mode in coarse-grained polycrystals to a continuous lattice deformation inside the nano-sized grains. The results provide lattice level scenarios for the understanding of grain size effects on the change of phase transition mode from a first-order to a continuous one which brings significant changes in the macroscopic thermomechanical behavior and properties of the polycrystalline superelastic NiTi. The findings are published in Acta Mater in 2015. In the aspects of theoretical of the project, the roles of grain size, and grain boundary thickness on the stress- induced phase transition behaviors of nanocrystalline shape memory alloys are analyzed by using a Core-shell type “crystallite-amorphous composite” model. A non-dimensionalized length scale is identified as the governing parameter which is indicative of the energy competition between the crystallite and the grain boundary. Closed form analytical solutions of a reduced effective 1D model with embedded microstructure length scales are obtained. It is shown that, with grain size reduction, the energy of the elastic non-transformable grain boundary will indeed gradually become dominant in the phase transition process, and eventually bring fundamental changes of the deformation behaviors: breakdown of two-phase coexistence and vanishing of superelastic hysteresis. The predictions are supported by the published experimental data of nanocrystalline NiTi SMAs. The theoretical results on the effects of micro-scale interfaces are published in Int. J. Solids and Structure in 2015 and the theoretical results on the effects of nano-scale interfaces are published in J. Mech. Physics of Solids in 2018.

16209414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209414.value: With the fast development of nanotechnology and the race for better material performance, extreme grain refinement of polycrystals and nano-scale phase transition have become active research topics in recent years. This project, through both experimental and theoretical studies, shows that when the GS falls below 60 nm, not only is the thermally-induced martensitic PT completely suppressed, but also the superelastic stress hysteresis, typically large in coarse-grained NiTi, also decreases rapidly. It is revealed that such significant effects of GS reduction on the macroscopic responses originate from the large area-to-volume ratios of the nano-scale interfaces (grain boundary and phase interface, both are of nanometer thickness), in particular, the interfacial energy terms will gradually become dominant over the bulk counterparts in the energetics of the phase transition, eventually bring fundamental changes in the phase transition properties of the material.

16209514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209514.value: Art is a creative journey, rather than a deliverable end product. The creation process is valuable as it captures the development of the drawing by the artist. Even though the sketching process may be distinctive among artists, it generally progresses in a similar fashion, from coarse to fine, global to local, near to far, inconspicuous to salient parts. In this project, we aim to develop a system that is able to simulate a sketching process that is largely indistinguishable from how an artist would draw. Each snapshot of the drawing and the dynamic drawing order will resemble a work by a human. There exist graphics techniques which take an image or a 3D model as input and produce compelling images resembling artworks created by humans. However, very few researchers have studied the sketching process itself. A closely related recent work considers only line drawings and orders the lines to produce an animated construction of the drawing. In contrast, our objective is to identify various kinds of strokes artists use in the drawing process and produce an animation that starts from a blank canvas to the final drawing. Such a system will be useful for teaching students how to draw and for reconstructing the drawing process of historical art masterpieces. To evaluate our system, we will conduct a user study, where the drawing animations synthesized by our system and from the artists will be played side by side and participants will vote on which animation is visually plausible. Finally, the proposed framework can be extended to simulate the the process of creating artwork with other stroke-based media. 比起一個靜態的最終產品，藝術更是一種創造性的旅程。藝術創作的過程有其獨特的價值，它能捕捉到藝術家對於創作對象的理解和表達。儘管每位藝術家的繪畫過程各有特色，他們也遵循著共同的規律。 比如由輪廓到細節，由整體到局部，從近到遠。在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發一個系統，該系統能夠自動模擬人類的（鉛筆素描）寫生過程。過程中的每一筆，與人類繪畫過程幾無二緻。 現有的圖形學研究，利用圖像或三維模型作為輸入，並產生 類似人類創造的畵作。 然而，這些研究主要集中在最終的靜態圖像，而不是動態的“ 寫生過程”本身。不同于之前的研究，我們的目標是找出寫生時爲了表達不同形狀時常用的筆觸，筆法，以及繪畫順序。基於此，我們的系統可以生成從無到有的寫生動畫。這樣的系統將可以用於教授學生入門級的寫生技巧，也可以用來重建 歷史名作的動態繪製過程。為了評估我們的系統地有效性，我們將進行 用戶研究：將系統生成的寫生過程進行一個簡單的圖霛測試。用戶將會觀看到描繪同一物體的兩個寫生視頻,一個來自系統生成，一個來自藝術家，並判斷哪一個是人類所畫。 最後，我們所提出的系統框架可以被擴展至除了鉛筆素描之外的其他繪畫技法，以模擬油畫、國畫、水粉等其它種類繪畫的生成過程 。

16209514.label: Realisation of objectives
16209514.value: The creation process of a drawing provides a vivid visual progression, allowing the audience to better comprehend the drawing. The main goal of this project is to simulate the process of how people sketch via observing a 3D object. Cognitive science reveals that what geometric elements artists draw and their drawing order reflect how artists schematize and conceptualize objects. In the early stages of drawing, the cognition process requires conceptual skills, but requires perceptual skills in the later stages. With conceptual skills, artists analyze the drawing subject and abstract it into meaningful simpler elements that make up the whole object. As drawing progresses, the artists then treat the drawing subject as a whole and focus on adding perceptual features that were not expressed in the conceptual stage. We proposed a multi-phase process to draw organic shapes, comprising posture phase, primitive phase, contour phase, and finally detail phase. In determining what to draw in the early phases, we obtain contextual features that serve as auxilliary lines, which then guide the drawing of local features derived from local geometric properties (such as normal and curvature) in the later phases. We fulfilled the first objective by developing structure-aware shape analysis methods to extract the intended drawing trajectories, in particular, auxiliary trajectories that depict proportions of parts, fitted primitives, and partial symmetry. To fulfil the second objective of ordering and filtering the trajectories, we viewed the sketching process as an information delivery process and introduced the concept of sketching entropy which measures the shape information gain. A complete sequence of a drawing is determined by requiring every next drawn stroke to maximize the information gain. To synthesize dynamic humanized strokes, which is the third objective, we adopted a feedback control system to simulate the action of a human moving a pen along an intended trajectory, producing visually plausible results, as confirmed by our user study. Putting together the above three components, we developed a complete system that takes a 3D model with semantic segmentation as input and generates a plausible dynamic sketch. This fulfilled the fourth objective. The above-mentioned methods were developed to extract trajectories for sketching organic objects. We fulfilled the last objective by investigating sketching of man-made structures, mainly urban structures reconstructed from multi-view stereo technique. Urban structures are highly regular and composed of repetitive components, requiring different shape analysis and segmentation methods for extracting more accurate trajectories. Finally, we developed an interactive system to transform a 2D sketch into a 3D one with the help of existing 3D models in a shape collection. These contributions are elaborated in Section 6.1. In view of these results, we consider that the objectives of the project have been fulfilled.

16209514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209514.value: We developed an approach to simulate how people draw and what they draw. Given a 3D model, our approach extracts drawing trajectories in four sketching phases by shape analysis methods and determines the order of the trajectories based on sketching entropy which provides a unified way to model stroke selection and ordering, both within and across phases. Finally, we synthesize humanized dynamic strokes from the trajectories using a feedback control system. Our system is able to generate visually plausible simulation of the sketching process as confirmed by our user study. One reviewer commented, “I found this work fascinating (could a computer draw like a human?), especially for the contribution on sketching entropy.” Another reviewer commented, “This paper significantly advances the state of the art in animating the creation of sketches.” This work was published in the proceedings of the conference Expressive 2014 [Liu et al. 2014]. Other than drawing organic objects, we have applied our framework to sketch urban environments reconstructed with multi-view stereo technique [Liu, PhD thesis]. To address the high geometrical and topological noise levels in the 3D reconstructed surfaces, we proposed a segmentation algorithm to first partition the reconstructed surfaces into structural segments, such as roofs, facades, and columns. We extensively demonstrated the efficiency and robustness of the proposed method on real reconstruction models, yielding significantly better performance than classical mesh segmentation methods [Liu et al. ICCV 2015]. We have also studied the problem of arranging graphics elements into appealing layouts. Such tasks are traditionally accomplished through the users issuing numerous alignment and distribution commands. Our group-aware arrangement commands significantly reduce the amount of user interactions required. This work was published in the proceedings of the ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI) 2015 [Xu et al. 2015]. In addition, we have proposed model-guided 3D sketching and developed a tool that facilitates rapid concept redesign of 3D models via 3D sketching. We adopted an incremental plane-by-plane sketching workflow and proposed a novel solution for inferring a 3D planar canvas by analyzing structural relations between the 3D model and a group of 2D strokes constrained on the canvas. This work has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics [Xu et al. 2018]. Finally, we developed an interactive system to lift a 2D sketch into a 3D sketch. The key idea is to perform structure and shape matching to retrieve a candidate 3D model that provides plane information, followed by back projection and optimization of the sketch strokes. This work was presented as a technical brief at SIGGRAPH Asia conference 2016 [Li et al. 2016]. `

16209514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209514.value: Our sketching simulation technique can be extended to simulate the creation process of other stroke-based media. Each medium has its own characteristics that the simulation should capture. In addition to sketching trajectories that characterize a specific medium, the drawing order also plays an important role in rendering of strokes in different media, such as water colors and ink painting. For example, in Chinese ink painting, there are various rendering effects caused by different wetness and intensity levels. We have defined the sketching entropy with respect to only the perceptual salience. It would be interesting to incorporate other types of information, such as color, motion or pattern, to define the entropy. For example, Gestalt relations can be regarded as the pattern information, and drawing strokes that obey Gestalt rules together causes the pattern information to increase. The concept of sketching entropy can also be applied to other applications such as clutter removal for line drawing simplification.

16209514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209514.value: The creation process of a drawing, which captures the visual progression of the drawing by an artist, is valuable, because it shows how the artist expresses emotions and artistic apprehension, allowing the audience to better comprehend the drawing. To our best knowledge, we were the first to tackle the problem of emulating the process of drawing by observation. Our work has received very positive comments in peer reviews. By producing the final drawing through simulating the entire drawing process, our work also indirectly enables new stroke-based rendering effects.

16209714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209714.value: Nowadays, complex sculptured surface parts, such as aero-engine blades and high precision lenses, are exclusively machined on a five-axis machine, owing to the unique advantages of a larger range of tool accessibility, faster material-removal rate, and better surface finishing quality. When planning a five-axis machining operation, with the surface finishing quality upheld, one important objective is to reduce the total machining time. This is particularly desirable for large parts like those in the aircraft and automotive industries which often take days or even weeks to machine. There are currently two kinds of approaches to this objective – optimal tool path generation and optimal feed rate assignment. In the former, tool paths are computed with the goal of minimizing the total length traveled by the cutter. In the latter, which is performed by the machine’s controller, for a given tool path, the maximum feed rate is sought to minimize the machining time, but with all the physical loading constraints (e.g., the limit on an axis’ acceleration) of the machine tool satisfied. These two are usually independent of each other: a tool path is computed in the part coordinate system without considering the machine itself and how feed rate is assigned, whereas the controller calculates the best varying feed rate for a given tool path, but reactively, is not able to provide useful information to the early stage when the tool path is computed. It is not uncommon that a tool path with the least total travel distance by the cutter may pose an unexpected huge kinematic and dynamic loading on the machine’s axes, forcing the controller to assign very low feed rate to the tool path, and thus actually prolonging the real machining time. This project will develop a new five-axis tool path machining system with a new tool path generation algorithm that will incorporate the specific machine’s loading constraints and the corresponding optimal feedrate planning method. A new mathematical model called machine-dependent potential field will be introduced to generate a tool path that strives to minimize the total cutter travel length while at the same time adapts to the speeds and accelerations of the machine’s axes versus the part surface, allowing possibly larger feed rates to be assigned later by the controller. This new system is expected to perform much better than the existing systems in real situations in reducing the total machining time, along with other potential benefits.
