16209814.label: Project Objectives
16209814.value: Objective 1: An Economic Analysis Framework for Lifetime-Constrained BES under Dynamic Pricing We will build a framework that characterizes the economic value of BES under dynamic electricity pricing with explicit lifetime constraint, which is shown to fall into the purview of stochastic shortest path (SSP) problems. Based on this framework, we will characterize (i) how the intrinsic coupling between lifetime and operational policy influences the total economic value of BES, and (ii) how this coupling influences the structure of the optimal policy. In order to solve the dimensionality problem of our proposed SSP, we will exploit the monotonic structure of the state space with respect to the underlying monotonic structure of the remaining throughput of BES. Based on this structure, we aim at proposing an efficient and amenable algorithm to achieve the optimal operation of BES. Objective 2: Adaptive and Online Algorithm for Energy Trading with Lifetime-Constrained BES Based on the economic analysis framework, considering the limited price knowledge in the energy-trading market, we further optimize the operational policy of BES in an online fashion, which is proved to be a stochastic shortest path problem with forbidden paths. Unfortunately, this has been widely considered as a difficult problem and generally claimed to be NP-complete. To tackle this difficulty, in addition to exploiting the aforementioned monotonic property of the state space, we will further (i) optimize the sequential subpaths by implementation-friendly algorithms based on model predictive control (MPC), and (ii) optimize the global path with sequentially updated price knowledge based on Bayesian learning. Objective 3: Tradeoff between Conservativeness and Aggressiveness for BES Operation A paradigm is that each residential user (with local demand) is equipped with BES device to minimize its monetary cost as well as guarantee its BES lifetime, and this could be achieved by appropriately charging/discharging the battery in response to both the exogenous dynamic electricity price and the local dynamic demand. In particular, we aim to solve (i) how to minimize the total monetary cost for each user without lifetime guarantee (a SSP problem in essence), and (ii) how to minimize the total monetary cost as well as guarantee the lifetime requirement (a constrained SSP problem in essence). We will link the SSP and the constrained SSP to their corresponding underlying absorbing Markov chain (AMC) and propose computationally tractable algorithms. Furthermore, we will also investigate online algorithms based on the underlying open-loop and closed-loop control systems for the SSP and constrained SSP, respectively. Objective 4: Equilibrium Price Distributions of Dynamic Energy-trading Market with Networked BES Based on the above investigation of single BES, we will further consider an entire power system which consists of an exogenous Dynamic Market (DM) and an internal Energy-trading Market (EM). Within the EM, we will consider a large number of BES operators and one energy-trading platform controlled by a Community Control Center (CCC). We will develop a pricing algorithm for CCC to automatically and adaptively react to the aggregate decisions made by the numerous BES operators, thus balancing the total system demand as well as maximizing the reward for CCC. We will analyze the equilibrium trading price distributions based on mean field equilibrium. Considering the high computational complexity induced by the heterogeneous SSP problems, we aim to develop a robust and efficient pricing algorithm for CCC, such that it can adaptively learn the behaviors of BES operators and set the trading prices in an online fashion.

16209814.label: Realisation of objectives
16209814.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 1: i) We have established a stochastic shortest path (SSP)-based planning framework for distributed battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in smart grid. Our proposed planning framework can quantify the economic value of a lifetime-constrained BESS within its expected lifetime. To achieve this target, we defined the lifetime of the BESS as the serving duration within which the BESS’s capacity stays above a certain threshold of its initial capacity, and defined the economic value of the BESS as the total peak-shaving value within its entire lifetime. We showed that, when the electricity price dynamics are Markovian, the average lifetime can be analytically characterized as the average number of steps before being absorbed in the embedded absorbing Markov chain, and thus facilitates an efficient computation of BESS’s expected lifetime. ii) We characterized the monotonic property of the state space of the proposed model. Based on this property, we proposed a layering-and-grouping method to partition the large state space into multiple nonoverlapping smaller ones, and further proposed an efficient parallel value iteration algorithm. The algorithm runs value iteration within each group of states in parallel, and thus significantly improves the computational efficiency. We validated our model and algorithm on a practical BESS via real price data sets from two different electricity markets. Comparison of the computational efficiency between the standard Gauss–Seidel value iteration and our parallel algorithm was also illustrated through extensive simulation. Meanwhile, the numerical results also show promising insights for both planning and operational management of distributed BESSs in practice. In summary, Objective 1 of this project has been completed. (100%) (2) Realization of Objective 2: We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 2: i) We proposed a model predictive control-based online energy management solution for microgrids with BESSs. The proposed online algorithm can handle the forecasting errors of the renewable energy generation when performing peer-to-peer energy trading among different microgrids. ii) We proposed an online mechanism that can truthfully elicit the charging flexibility from battery electric vehicles in smart grid. Specifically, key to the designed mechanism is a pricing-based online algorithm that can incentive agents (i.e., owners of battery electric vehicles) to truthfully report their charging flexibility to the system operator with a guaranteed economic performance. We have theoretically derived the upper bound for the competitive ratio of our proposed online algorithm, which indicates that the deviation of our online algorithm from the offline optimal results is bounded even in the worst case. Moreover, numerical simulation has demonstrated that the economic performance of our designed online mechanism is close to the offline optimal results. In summary, Objective 2 of this project has been finished. (100%) (3) Realization of Objective 3: We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 3: i) We investigated the optimal operation of a distributed BESS for energy arbitrage under dynamic pricing, and the Pareto optimal arbitrage policy that balances the economic value and lifetime tradeoff of the BESS has been obtained. To achieve a balanced performance between economic value and lifetime, we proposed a constrained stochastic shortest path (CSSP)-based sequential decision making model. The proposed model allows the operators to exactly quantify the degree of how aggressive or conservative the charging/discharging behaviors should be. Therefore, the operators are capable of adjusting their arbitrage policies to achieve a predetermined balance in their BESSs’ value and lifetime performances. ii) We exploited the hidden structure of the proposed CSSP problem and proved the existence of optimal deterministic and stationary policies. We obtained the globally-optimal value-lifetime performance pairs and their corresponding optimal policies in different scenarios, and further provided the conditions for these pairs and policies to be Pareto optimal. By exploiting the hidden structure of the CSSP framework, we proposed an efficient parallel iterative algorithm, with guaranteed convergence, to compute the Pareto boundary of the feasible value-lifetime region. Based on this parallel algorithm, we performed extensive simulation to validate our model via practical data of battery parameters and electricity prices. In summary, Objective 3 of this project has been completed. (100%) (4) Realization of Objective 4: We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 4: i) We investigated a hybrid energy trading market that is comprised of an external utility company and a local trading market managed by a local trading center (LTC). We first quantified the respective benefits of the energy consumers and the sellers from the local trading and then investigated how they can optimize their benefits by controlling their energy scheduling in response to the LTC’s pricing. Two different types of the LTC were considered: 1) the nonprofit-oriented LTC, which solely aims at benefiting the energy consumers and the sellers; and 2) the profit-oriented LTC, which aims at maximizing its own profit while guaranteeing the required benefit for each consumer and seller. For each type of the LTC, the optimal trading problem was formulated and the associated algorithm was further proposed to efficiently find the LTC’s optimal price, as well as the optimal energy scheduling for each consumer and seller. Numerical results were provided to validate the benefits of the hybrid energy trading market and the performance of the proposed algorithms. ii) Another important application of BESSs is to provide a flexible and efficient energy management solution for networked microgrids (MGs) via cooperation. Specifically, the cooperation of multiple networked MGs can alleviate the mismatch problem between distributed generation and demand, and reduce the overall cost of the power system. Based on Objective 4 in this project, we studied the energy management problem of multiple MGs that are interconnected by both the direct current energy exchange network and the alternating current traditional distribution networks. In our proposed model, each MG is equipped with renewable energy generators as well as distributed BESSs. The objective of our problem is to minimize the overall energy cost in a distribution network consisting of multiple MGs, with the practical operating constraints (e.g., power balance and the battery’s operational constraints) explicitly incorporated. Considering the privacy and scalability, we proposed a distributed algorithm with convergence assurance based on the alternating direction method of multipliers. Simulations were made for different MG exchange topologies on three radial distribution network testbeds. Numerical results have demonstrated that certain topologies are more favorable than others, and the cooperation strategy for the energy exchange is significantly affected by the MGs’ locations in the distribution network. In summary, Objective 4 of this project has been completed. (100%)

16209814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209814.value: Major findings and research outcome in this project are summarized as follows: 1. A stochastic shortest path (SSP)-based framework for quantifying the economic value of a lifetime-constrained distributed battery energy storage system (BESS) in smart grid has been established. BESS investors can leverage the proposed model and algorithm for assessing the expected economic return of their system planning decisions. Meanwhile, a constrained SSP-based framework for modeling the operation of a lifetime-constrained distributed BESS has been proposed. The proposed framework can find the Pareto-optimal operational policy for achieving an optimal tradeoff between the lifetime and economic performances of a distributed BESS. The research outcome of this part has been published in journal papers [1] [2] listed in Part C. 2. We designed a hybrid energy trading market that is comprised of an external utility company and a local trading market managed by a local trading center. In the designed energy trading market, a group of energy-users, who are equipped with the capabilities of distributed energy generation, can trade energy in a cooperative manner with the goal to minimize their total energy-provisioning cost while meeting each individual energy-user’s local energy demand. The research outcome of this part has been published by journal paper [3] listed in Part C. 3. We proposed a novel queueing model for battery swapping and charging stations (BSCSs), and theoretically analyzed its asymptotic performance. Based on the proposed performance analysis model for a single BSCS, we further investigated the optimal charging scheduling strategy for managing multiple BSCSs. Meanwhile, we also proposed an online mechanism for eliciting charging flexibility from battery electric vehicles. The online mechanism can enable system operators to obtain multi-dimensional charging flexibility from battery electric vehicles, leading to a good candidate of demand-side management program in smart grid. The research outcome of this part has been published by journal papers [4][5][6] listed in Part C. 4. We studied the energy management problem of multiple networked microgrids equipped with BESSs. To handle the non-convex power flow constraints, we exploited the recent results of the exact optimal power flow relaxation method which can equivalently transform the original non-convex problem into a second-order cone programming problem and efficiently determine the optimal solution successfully. We also proposed a distributed algorithm with convergence assurance based on the alternating direction method of multipliers. The research outcome of this part has been published by journal paper [7] listed in Part C.

16209814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209814.value: This project mainly focused on the planning and operation of a single and micro-scale distributed battery energy storage system (BESS), the problem of how to integrate grid-scale BESSs in smart grid has not been investigated. In practical systems, when the capacity of a BESS is in grid-scale or the number of distributed BESSs is in large-scale, especially when peer-to-peer energy trading is enabled among different BESSs, the operation of current power grid will need a substantial transformation. Apart from the problem of being in large-scale, another problem that needs further development is the situation when BESSs are owned by different self-interested agents. In practice, it is not easy to incentivize all the storage operators to behave in a certain way such that we can achieve a desired system-wide objective. Therefore, we need to design a market mechanism, with appropriate incentive and pricing schemes, such that all the self-interested agents can act individually for their own benefits, but ultimately lead to a desired system-wide objective, e.g., to minimize the total electricity generation cost or carbon emission, etc.

16209814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209814.value: This project primarily concerns ubiquitous battery energy storage systems (BESSs) (e.g., lithium-ion batteries and lead-acid batteries) that are extensively being deployed in power systems all over the world. For example, in cities such as San Francisco and New York where power is costly, large commercial buildings are installed with batteries in their basements, for the purpose of buying and storing electricity at night when rates are low, and tapping into the batteries during peak afternoons when prices are high. Towards this end, this project has proposed multiple models and algorithms that can be used for assessing and optimizing the economic value of BESSs. Meanwhile, this project has investigated the optimal operation of BESSs that can balance the tradeoff between lifetime performance and economic performance. Moreover, the hybrid energy trading market and the energy management framework designed in this project can provide rich insight into the design and operation of power grid with integration of BESSs in practice.

16210714.label: Realisation of objectives
16210714.value: With respect to computer musicology, this project has advanced the state of the art in computer musicology by developing continuous valued models in both probabilistic (symbolic) STG and neural (distributed) TRAAM forms, that are unified, task-independent, and corpus-trained. Both new families of models are capable of simultaneously integrating multiple aspects of music structure, such as microtonal melodies in blues, rhythms in flamenco, and lyric improvisation in hip hop. With respect to the cognitive science of music, this project has advanced our understanding by building computational models that explain how relations between different aspects of music can be learned via either symbolic or distributed representations. The models make similar predictions, preferences, and expectations as humans, even for continuous valued languages in music, such as microtonal melodies. With respect to computer music applications, this project has demonstrated how new stochastic transduction grammar approaches in both probabilistic and neural implementations can be exploited for new applications for computer music including quality ranking, similarity detection, automatic improvisation and accompaniment. With respect to formal language theory, this project has explored new symbolic and neural types of STGs. It has shown how their contrasting properties are computationally effective in different ways when it comes to representing and learning the relations between musical sublanguages. The project has shown efficiency tradeoffs in algorithms for applying and inducing such STGs; category induction in particular was a strong driver to explore the neural approaches of TRAAM. Work from the project earned the Best Presentation Award from the International Computer Music Association, at the 41st International Computer Music Conference (ICMC 2015).

16210714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210714.value: In the first half of the project, we worked toward continuous valued music transduction grammars for two very different modeling approaches. The two competing approaches employ neural versus symbolic stochastic transduction grammar (STG) architectures, both of which can handle continuous values for the first time. We iteratively developed, prototyped, and implemented scaled up versions of a new neural architecture for continuous valued music transduction grammars introduced a powerful class of bilingual recursive neural networks. TRAAM (transduction recursive auto-associative memory) is the first of our new models in this class. It represents the first bilingual generalization of Pollack's (1990) classic RAAM models, which are the foundation of monolingual autoencoders. These models offer an attack on computational complexity by using implicit vector space representations of categories, instead of combinatorially exploding the space of possible nonterminals. They also allow discriminative objective criteria that recursively propagate error signals. We discussed how these models can for example be applied to automatic learning of hip hop improvisation (IJCAI 2015, ICMC 2015, ISMIR 2015) and flamenco accompaniment (SMPC 2015). In the second half of the project, based on our experiences with the strengths and weaknesses of the neural version, we began formulating a new symbolic architecture for continuous valued music transduction grammars as a contrastive approach to the neural architecture. We had begun formulating these in the first half of the project (in parallel with developing the continuous valued transduction grammars based on bilingual recursive neural networks, discussed above), as the first compositionally structured stochastic transduction grammars capable of generating parallel music streams of continuous values. In this symbolic rather than neural version of the approach to continuous valued transduction grammars, we employed gaussian mixture models for STG preterminals. We developed an efficient EM training approach for the class of continuous stochastic ITGs (inversion transduction grammars). We applied these models to learning how much to `bend' notes in genres like blues, that rely heavily upon microtones that cannot be adequately modeled without continuous values (ICCC 2016, ISMIR 2016). In parallel, we also continued to articulate how these symbolic and neural approaches contrast, and to explain how they address foundational issues of musical creativity (MUME 2016) with respect to objective 1 (computer musicology) and objective 2 (cognitive science of music).

16210714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210714.value: The two complementary approaches to continuous STGs — symbolic and neural — with different strengths and weaknesses provide different tradeoffs between computational efficiency, generalization, and descriptive precision. The neural approaches, a form of deep learning, attack the exponential complexity of concept formation, whereas the symbolic approaches attack the lack of precision in neural representations. We now plan to work on hybrid models that combine the strengths, and expect this to open up many music applications.

16210714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210714.value: Whereas most previous probabilistic grammar models of music typically described a single language for an individual problem—perhaps for key finding, meter finding, melody identification, pitch or rhythm expectation, transcription, music information retrieval, or the like—we have instead shifted the focus to explicitly modeling the structural relations between different separate languages. Formally, a transduction is a relation between two languages—aptly described using stochastic transduction grammars (STGs). Our attack on the challenges of fully unsupervised induction of music STGs consists of three synergistic prongs, each of which amplifies the contribution of the others: (a) continuous values, (b) computational complexity, and (c) objective criteria: We have exploited information-theoretic concepts of minimum description length to develop, test and refine more musically discriminating functions for measuring the generalization quality of competing probabilistic musical relations being considered as hypotheses, to accurately drive Bayesian induction of STGs. We have succeeded in showing that inducing relationships between multiple musical languages by harnessing these three complementary strategies in tandem can, in fact (and perhaps counterintuitively), render fully unsupervised learning of multiple musical structures more tractable than if attempted only for individual musical languages in isolation.

16210814.label: Project Objectives
16210814.value: To develop analytical models and processing technology for the fabrication of advanced porous Polyurethane foam (PUF) incorporated with phase change materials (PCM) to achieve the following two important goals: 1)To control the indoor temperature of an electric vehicle in order to save temperature regulating energy; 2)To reduce the total weight of the electric vehicle by replacing accessories with low density nano-cellular foam in order to reduce the load on electric battery. To investigate the effect of microstructure and thermal properties of PU and PCM on overall thermal behavior of PUF/PCM composites and put forward a PUF/PCM optimization scheme. To verify the analytical model by fabricating and characterizing the PUF/PCM composites with different micro structures and material distributions. To evaluate the travel range improvement of electric vehicles with this new functional material under different weather conditions.

16210814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210814.value: Increased concerns over the environmental impact of gasoline cars, higher gasoline prices, and improvements in battery technology, have led to renewed interest in electric cars, which are more environmentally friendly and cheaper to run. Electric vehicles have a fatal disadvantage that the travel range is limited by battery capacity, which restricts further popularization. In this proposed research, our objective is to maximize electric energy efficiency for vehicle propulsion by reducing or even cutting off non-propulsion power consumption such as air conditioning in order to prolong the travel range. To achieve this goal without decreasing the comfort, a porous foam composite incorporated with phase change materials will be developed. Thermal energy will be stored or released to regulate the indoor temperature in a comfortable range while the electric vehicles are running with little energy supply from the battery. The proposed research is of great significance for PCM composite design and theoretical understanding. PCM technology has been widely researched in energy related fields. However scientific work in this field has just started. Since PCM study is vague and mostly superficial, much effort is needed to draw a comprehensive picture. Even though the mechanism of pure phase change has been studied for decades, a comprehensive model for PCM composite is still premature. So it is of great significance to conduct most fundamental research based on micro structure and theoretical level. The methodology of this research relies on theoretical understanding in the relationship between the micro structure and macro behavior and its thermal dynamic meaning, which it is substantial for further PCM system design. Only with comprehensive modeling can a reliable PCM composite be achieved. The outcomes of the proposed research will develop a novel model for advanced foam/PCM model composites, which will bridge the gap our understanding of the materials thermal property, micro structure and macro thermal performance. Our innovations will dramatically decrease the energy cost on the temperature regulation in electric vehicles. It will play an important role in electric vehicle development which will be of great help reducing greenhouse gas emission and decrease the dependency upon non-renewable fossil fuel. 化石燃料汽车对环境危害的担忧在日益加深，同时，较高的汽油价格和改进的电池技术促使环境友好、性价比高的电动车重新进入视野。然而，因为电池容量有限导致行程较短的致命缺点，限制了电动汽车进一步的推广。在本研究中，我们希望通过限制非动力的能源消耗，如空调，以最大限度地提高用于车辆行驶的电池运用率。为了实现这一目标，并保持原有舒适性，我们提出开发复合多孔泡沫相变材料的研究方案。在汽车行驶过程中，热能将通过相变材料的相转变过程储存或释放来调节室内的温度，使车内温度稳定在一个舒适的范围内，从而使很少电量以维持空调运行。 该研究对相变复合材料设计和理论理解具有重要意义。虽然相变材料技术已经在能源相关领域被广泛研究，但由于这些研究并不深入，进一步致力于全面理解相变材料很有必要。所以这一领域的科研工作事实上才刚刚开始。具体来说，虽然相转变的机理已经研究了很长时间，但是相变复合材料的模型仍然是不成熟的，所以进行对微观结构与理论模型的进一步研究是必要和有意义的。本研究将着眼于发掘微观结构与宏观表现的关系以及其背后的热动力学意义，因为这可以实质性指导相变材料系统设计。只有在准确的物理模型上才能得到可靠的相变复合材料。 该研究目的在于为先进的泡沫/相变复合材料建立新的数学模型，这将为复合材料的热性能，微观结构和宏观热性能之间建立可靠的联系。在此基础上，我们的创新设计将大大降低电动汽车的温控能源消耗。由于减少温室气体排放和对不可再生的化石燃料的依赖，这将在电动汽车发展中起到重要作用。

16211014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211014.value: Fluid flows in complex geometries are very common in engineering problems, and the major difficulties arise in how to represent the body, the moving walls, and the interaction between body and fluid. Treating the coupling of the structural deformations and the fluid flow poses a number of challenging problems for numerical simulations, where the elastic boundary changes the flow of the fluid and the fluid moves the elastic boundary simultaneously. In computational fluid dynamics, the immersed boundary method is an approach to simulate fluid-structure interactions. In the past decades, the immersed boundary method with rectangular mesh for the fluid and Lagrangian mesh for the moving body has been well defined and validated in the incompressible flow simulations. But, there is limited research in its extension to the compressible flows. In the past years, the gas-kinetic scheme with moving body-fitted mesh for the compressible Navier-Stokes simulation has been well-developed and tested as well. The purpose of this proposal is to combine the advantages of both the immersed boundary method (IBM) and the gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) to design new IBM-GKS methods for compressible flow simulations, and to apply them to the problems related to the fluid-structure interactions. 复杂几何区域的流动问题普遍存在于工程应用中。 弹性的固体边界会同时改变流体和固体边界的运动， 形成所谓的流固耦合问题。如何表示边界、处理移动边界、 考虑结构变形和流体的相互作用等等，都对数值模拟 提出了巨大挑战。在计算流体力学中，浸润边界方法 （Immersed Boundary Method, IBM）是模拟流体和结构相互作用 的一种方法。在过去的几十年里， 浸润边界方法运用矩形网格和运动边界的拉格朗日网格 成功地处理了这类问题，并在不可压流动中得到了验证。 但是，将该方法扩展到可压流动的研究相对较少。 另一方面，气体动理学格式（Gas Kinetic Scheme, GKS） 能够有效的处理可压缩流动问题。 在过去的几年里，气体动理学格式运用贴体的移动边界 网格技术处理了一部分包含刚体运动的可压缩 Navier-Stokes流动的流固耦合问题， 并取得了很好的计算结果。然而，贴体网格依然有其局限性， 很难处理更复杂的弹性边界运动。 该项目通过结合浸润边界方法和气体动理学格式的优点， 期望发展出新的IBM-GKS方法来处理复杂几何区域 的可压缩流固耦合问题。

16211014.label: Realisation of objectives
16211014.value: With the support of the current research grant, we have constructed gas-kinetic schemes for the flow simulations. Firstly, an immersed boundary gas-kinetic scheme (IB-GKS) is proposed for the viscous compressible flows around stationary and moving objects. In the immersed boundary method (IBM), a regular Eulerian mesh is used for the fluid together with a set of Lagrangian points to represent an immersed boundary. The key point in IBM is to evaluate the force on the boundary points, and re-distribute the force to the fluid in the Eulerian mesh points around the boundary. Similar to the implicit velocity correction-based method, the force on the boundary can be obtained by solving a linear system which couples the momentum changes between the boundary points and neighboring fluid points. As a result, the non-slip boundary condition can accurately satisfied on the boundary. After evaluating the external forcing term to the fluid element close to the boundary, the gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) with the external force is used to evolve the flow motion. The IB-GKS is applied for the simulation of both stationary and moving objects, including single-body and multi-body cases. There is no special mesh treatment needed in the computation and the same Cartesian mesh is adopted in all cases. Numerical experiments validate the current approach. The scheme works very well for inviscid flow at the low speed limit, but seems have accuracy problem for the high speed flow computation if the boundary layer cannot be well resolved by the mesh resolution. In order to over this difficulty in the immersed boundary method, we further developed the gas-kinetic scheme in the Cartesian coordinates. One of the very successful extension is the following method. A Cartesian grid method combined with a simplified gas kinetic scheme is presented for subsonic and supersonic viscous flow simulation on complex geometries. Under the Cartesian mesh, the boundaries are represented by a set of direction-oriented boundary points, and the computational grid points are classified into four different categories, the fluid point, the solid point, the drop point, and the interpolation point. A constrained weighted least square method is employed to evaluate the physical quantities at the interpolation points. Different boundary conditions, including isothermal boundary, adiabatic boundary, and Euler slip boundary, are presented by different interpolation strategies. We adopt a simplified gas kinetic scheme as the flux solver for both subsonic and supersonic flow computations. The methodology of constructing a simplified kinetic flux function can be extended to other flow systems. A few numerical examples are used to validate the Cartesian grid method and the simplified flux solver. The reconstruction scheme for recovering the boundary conditions of compressible viscous and heat conducting flow with a Cartesian mesh can provide a smooth distribution of physical quantities at solid boundary, and present an accurate solution for the flow study with complex geometry. Better solutions have been obtained through the interpolation-based methods for the satisfaction of boundary condition rather than the forcing term approximation at boundary in the immersed boundary method. One of the main publications for the new approach is in the paper [S.Z. Chen, K. Xu, and Z.H. Li, Journal of Computational Physics 326 (2016) 862–877]. During this period, in order to increase the robustness and accuracy of the scheme and apply the scheme to a wide application regimes, we have also worked on the development of the unified gas-kinetic scheme, compact higher-order methods, and multi-physics flow solvers. The higher-order scheme, such as the two-stage fourth-order method in space and time, has been successfully constructed. The construction of compact scheme is also very successful in both structured and unstructured mesh. A series of higher-order methods have been obtained. In order to extend the scheme to solve more complicated flow problems, the unified gas-kinetic schemes for rarefied flow, photon transport and plasma physics, have been developed and applied to a wide range of flow problems. One of the engineering applications for the Cartesian grid method is to the prediction of falling trajectory of Tian-gong I in the low orbit.

16211014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211014.value: In this project, we developed a Cartesian grid method for complex immersed boundary problems, and use a simplified gas kinetic scheme for subsonic and supersonic flow simulation. A constrained weighted least square method is employed to update the physical quantities at the interpolation points. Different boundary conditions, including isothermal, adiabatic, and Euler slip conditions, are presented by different interpolation strategies. The new method is capable of simulating inviscid and viscous, compressible and near incompressible flow problems. The numerical results demonstrate that the new method converges to the correct physical solutions for both subsonic and supersonic flows as the mesh refines. The current scheme is robust under various flow condition from low Mach number to high Mach number flows, from inviscid to viscous ones. The interpolation procedure proposed in this study provides a smooth distribution of physical quantities at solid boundary and can tackle with arbitrary geometry. The current methodology can be further extended to the other flow systems, such as to the numerical schemes for both continuum and rarefied flow computations.

16211014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211014.value: The development of gas-kinetic scheme for the continuum flow simulation in Cartesian grid is very successful through the research in this project. However, for the hypersonic flow in the near space flight, the real gas dynamics is a multiscale flow problem. For example, around a hypersonic flying vehicle, the flow physics at different regions may correspond to different regimes, where the local Knudsen number can be changed significantly in several orders of magnitude, such as from the highly compressible flow at the leading edge and highly rarefied one at the trailing edge. With a variation of flow physics, a multiscale method has to be developed. At the same time, due to the complicated geometry of the flight vehicle, a Cartesian method is a good choice. In the future, we are going to combine the Cartesian grid technique developed in this project with the multiscale modeling in the unified gas-kinetic scheme and develop numerical scheme with a wide applicable flow regime.

16211014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211014.value: Fluid flows in complex geometries are very common in engineering problems, and the major difficulties arise in how to represent the body, the moving walls, and the interaction between body and fluid. Treating the coupling of the structural deformations and the fluid flow poses a number of challenging. In computational fluid dynamics, in order to represent complicated geometry, a Cartesian grid is much easier to be generated and used in the computations. However, with the use of the Cartesian mesh, the treatment of the boundary condition for the cut-cell becomes complicated. In the past decades, many techniques have been developed, such as the immersed boundary method and the interpolation method. In the past, the gas-kinetic scheme with moving body-fitted mesh for the compressible viscous flow simulation has been constructed. Through this project, we have extended the scheme to the Cartesian grid and developed the corresponding scheme successfully for the hypersonic flow computation with complicated geometry.

A particular goal of interest is to find a set of effective link toll patterns to reduce the link flows to below a desirable target level such as road environmental capacity constraints. To extend the trial-and-error procedure by considering both the short-run and long-run demand changes: the changes in demand provoked by short run changes in price along the same demand curve, and the long run demand shift due to changes in the background variables such as inflation and real income growth over the implementation period.

16211114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211114.value: Road pricing is widely recognized as an efficient means of dealing with traffic congestion and vehicular emissions. It has been the subject of a substantial number of theoretical and empirical studies in recent years. Many congestion pricing schemes have been implemented in a number of cities worldwide, such as Singapore and London. Congestion pricing schemes are often posted and examined in the form of either first-best (marginal-cost) pricing or second-best pricing. The former is concerned with a perfect pricing environment for achieving social optimum and the latter deals with pricing schemes under realistic social, economic or physical constraints for achieving a desirable target. Exact calculation of either first-best or second-best toll charges requires knowledge of demand functions, which is generally not readily available in practice. In this case congestion pricing can still go ahead on a trial-and-error basis without using the demand functions: the tolls are imposed first and then updated according to the observed network flows. Congestion pricing schemes are generally derived and evaluated on the basis of static traffic equilibrium. The incontestable fact is that traffic flow on a certain road or route changes from day to day. More realistically, even if a new equilibrium is reachable, network flows tend to temporarily evolve towards to a new stable state in response to adjustment of road pricing schemes. Thus, there is a great need for the development of efficient road-use pricing methods in networks taking into account day-to-day flow dynamics. The project will revisit the trial-and-error implementation procedure of road pricing with day-to-day network flow dynamics and evolution. The first part of the project will focus on designing a trial-and-error method of marginal-cost pricing leading the network flows to the system-optimum with unknown demand functions; appropriate time periods between two adjacent trials are sought under day-to-day flow dynamics. The second part will develop the trial-and-error method of second-best pricing to achieve alternative desirable goals such as finding a set of effective link toll patterns to reduce the link flows to below a desirable target level. The third part will extend the procedure by considering both short-run and long-run demand changes throughout the implementation period. This project reconsiders the pricing design problem in a politically and socially acceptable manner under more realistic conditions of traffic flow evolution. It will bring the existing large body of research on equilibrium-based pricing further towards the real-life practicality of how it might be implemented. 道路收费被广泛认为是一种解决交通拥堵和车辆排放的有效手段。关于这一课题已经有大量的理论和实证研究。拥堵收费已在世界各地实施，如新加坡，伦敦和斯德哥尔摩。 交通拥堵收费常采用最优（边际成本）定价或次优定价的形式。前者的目的是在理想环境下实现社会最优；后者考虑如何在现实的社会、经济或物理约束下达到预期目标。确定最优或次优收费方案需要准确的需求函数信息，而这一信息在实践中往往难以准确获得。在这种情况下，交通拥堵收费可以通过试错法实现，而不依赖于需求函数信息：定价方案根据实际的均衡交通流逐步调整。 对于交通拥堵收费方案的推导和评估通常基于静态交通平衡模型。然而一个无可争辩的事实是，现实网络中的路段或路径流量常常是逐日变化的。当收费方案改变时，网络流量更有可能逐渐地，而不是瞬间迅速地，演化到一个新的平衡状态。因此，考虑基于逐日流量演化的拥堵收费模型是有现实意义的。 该项目将研究，在网络流逐日演化的情况下，如何通过试错法实施拥堵收费以达到期望目标。第一部分将专注于在未知需求函数的情况下利用试错法实现系统最优; 在逐日流量演化的假设下，确定收费方案的调整时间间隔。第二部分将讨论实现次优定价的试错法，比如寻找一套有效的收费模式来将路段流量限制在某个目标流量值之下。第三部分将扩展前两部分的内容，同时考虑整个拥堵收费实施期间的短期和长期需求变化。 该项目基于更现实的假设，以易于决策者和出行者接受的形式，讨论道路拥堵收费问题。这一项目将有助于进一步推动现有的大量基于静态平衡模型的道路收费研究的应用和实施。

16211114.label: Realisation of objectives
16211114.value: Throughout the three years of the research period, we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the Network Congestion Pricing with Day-to-day Flow Dynamics in the original proposal were addressed. Roadway congestion is a source of enormous economic costs. A fundamental question in both theoretical analysis and actual implementation of congestion pricing is how to estimate or update the optimal charge level of congestion tolls in a simple yet practical manner. To this end, the so-called trial-and-error method proved to be efficient and promising. It uncovers the unknown demand curves based on the change in observed link flows resulting from a given pricing trial, and thereby obviates the requirement for an analytical demand function. A key assumption in sequential trial-and-error implementation of congestion pricing based on observed flows, is the existence and immediate appearance of user equilibrium for any given toll charges and thus the pricing schemes can be derived and evaluated for certain objectives. The reality is that traffic flow on a certain road or route changes from day to day. Once a pricing scheme is imposed or altered, travelers take time to learn and adjust their trip-making decisions in a new pricing environment before reaching a new equilibrium, even they can be quickly informed of altered toll charges, as advanced information technology is nowadays available. Therefore, it is essential to take into account the process of day-to-day network flow adjustment towards equilibrium in the trial-and-error implementation of road pricing, which employs the demand revelation mechanism that requires a series of price changes to derive the demand functions properly. In this project, we incorporated the day-to-day flow evolution and dynamics into the trial-and-error procedure for the implementation of congestion pricing in a general network. The proposed study substantially enhance the trial-and-error procedure that allows for the traffic planner to estimate or update easily the socially optimal congestion tolls by using readily available traffic count data. Neither the demand functions nor the mechanism of the flow evolution are explicitly required in identifying a set of optimal link tolls for achieving a predetermined target flow pattern or the unknown system optimum one. The trial-and-error methods to be developed can thus assist in the design, implementation and evaluation of various urban road pricing schemes.

16211114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211114.value: Major findings and research outcome 1. Developed a dynamic model for a link-based day-to-day network traffic dynamics and equilibria, which can characterize the processes of achieving equilibria from a non-equilibrium state in traffic networks. Several desirable properties of the dynamical system model were established, including the equivalence between its stationary state and user equilibrium, the invariance of its evolutionary trajectories, and the uniqueness and stability of its stationary points. It was also found that those physical laws that govern the physical world may also apply for human’s aggregate social behavior. That is: the network flow dynamics was shown to be analogous to a damped oscillatory physical system. Moreover, the dynamic model was further extended to address rational behavior adjustment process with boundedly rational user equilibrium. Publications: Xiao, F., Yang, H. and Ye, H., 2016. 16211114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211114.value: Congestion pricing schemes are often posted and examined in the form of either first-best pricing or second-best pricing. The former is concerned with a perfect pricing environment for achieving social optimum and the latter deals with pricing schemes under realistic social, economic or physical constraints for achieving a desirable target. Exact calculation of either first-best or second-best toll charges requires knowledge of demand functions, which is generally not readily available in practice. Congestion pricing schemes are generally derived and evaluated on the basis of static traffic equilibrium. The incontestable fact is that traffic flow on a certain road or route changes from day to day. More realistically, even if a new equilibrium is reachable, network flows tend to temporarily evolve towards to a new stable state in response to adjustment of road pricing schemes. This project investigated the pricing design problem under more realistic conditions of traffic flow evolution. A few trial-and-error implementation methods were developed and demonstrated; various interesting findings and insights were obtained and summarized in a number of papers published in leading transportation journals.

16211214.label: Project Objectives
16211214.value: Identify Relevant Domains from A Massive Number of Domains: In the first stage, we will design a series of effective similarity measures to identify similar domains to a given target domain. When there is a new domain, we use the proposed similarity measures to select the most relevant domains from a huge number of existing domains, say millions. The proposed measures should guarantee that the training data from the selected domains can improve the recommendation quality in the new domain without bringing negative transfer. Unification of Heterogeneous Knowledge: In the second stage, our objective is to unify and integrate heterogeneous, noise and inconsistent preference data from all selected domains for knowledge transfer. Lifelong Online Knowledge Transfer: In the third stage, we will solve this lifelong learning problem for coming domains by using the knowledge obtained in the previous two steps. We will design a unified model to make the collaborative filtering models compatible with different forms of knowledge from existing domains. Unlike transfer learning methods, we will use the obtained knowledge in new domains to improve the recommendation performance in existing domains, which is known as reversely knowledge transfer. Since it is unrealistic to store all received data, we will propose an efficient online learning method to update the older models without accessing the previous data. This is very important for lifelong collaborative filtering since the volume of data received over lifetime may be very huge. Evaluation: We will develop a scalable prototype system for lifelong collaborative filtering based on scalable online learning algorithms, and evaluate the developed framework and system on real-world collaborative filtering tasks. We will disseminate the research results in the form of high-quality publications, and make the demo and algorithm available in an open source manner.

16211214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211214.value: 协同过滤是推荐系统的一个重要的智能预测方法。 在很多应用中，协同过滤方法已经取得了很大的成就， 例如， 网上图书推荐， 朋友推荐等。在某一个特定的领域， 用户的兴趣随着时间而飘移， 例如在电子书籍，电影，社交和电子商务等领域里。 对于新兴领域， 协同过滤技术所面对的严重问题是数据的稀疏问题。 即： 在某一个新的领域，我们的数据通常不足以让模型对用户的真实喜好有好的了解，从而对在新领域的个性化推荐问题十分困难。 迁移学习是解决数据稀疏问题的一个好方法。然而，在迁移学习领域， 仍有一些突出的挑战是未解。首先，现有的迁移学习方法假定推荐器系统分为源领域和目标领域，而两者都已知。 然而， 在推荐系统里， 一个系统可以在不同时候处理各种不同的问题， 而且在很长一段时间内操作。 这可以被称为系统的一生， 其中， 不断地有新的问题出现， 而过去的任何阶段都可以看作是一个源领域。 其次，现有迁移学习方法假设所有的数据都处于相同的分布。但是， 由于我们关心的系统在很长一段时间内操作，许多新的类型的数据的可以不断出现。 因此，这个迁移学习的问题是一个开放形的问题。 即： 如何找到一个新的解决方案来统一这些异构数据源， 从而进行有效的知识迁移。最后，迁移学习只能从旧域借用知识，以帮助建立预测模型在目标域提高预测精度。 而在我们的终生学习问题中， 新的领域也可以帮助旧的领域提高精度。 我们在这一项目中， 将研发一个崭新的基于终生学习的推荐系统， 使得系统能够在接到一个新的领域数据时， 用这一数据去改进整个系统生命周期中的所有领域。 我们管这一方法叫做终生协同过滤 （LCF）。 具体来说， 我们将解决： 1） 有效的相似度领域衡量机制， 2） 在线推荐算法。 好的相似度可以使我们在众多推荐领域中找到相关的领域集合， 来进行知识的迁移， 同时防止知识的抵消。 这个项目包括数据的采集， 整理， 和利用这些数据来验证我们的算法。 同时， 我们最有效的算法将应用与实际的问题中去。

16211214.label: Realisation of objectives
16211214.value: We have realised all the objectives of the project. In particular, we have identified a number of similarity measures to discern the distance between source domains and target domains. We have done this for a wide spectrum of domains, including online recommendation domains using reinforcement learning and bandit algorithms, hierarchical attention learning algorithms for sentiment analyses problems, as well as distant domain measures for continual learning in the life-time of an agent. In addition, we have designed measures to map different domain representations to a unified space, in which we can measure their similarities and differences. In the unified space, lifelong recommendation systems can be improved based on a variety of problem representations. In recommendation problems, we have designed a unified transfer learning algorithm for active learning that allows new data to be carefully labeled, for exploration and exploitation tradeoff using bandit algorithms, and for learning the sentiment of social comments based on transfer learning. Finally, we have designed several prototype systems to test the ideas. The bandit algorithm has been applied to WeChat news recommendation domain with millions of users using it, and the lifelong learning algorithm was published at ICML 2018, a highly regarded venue for publication in machine learning. Objective 1: We have designed algorithms that can identify domains from a large number of other domains. In this first stage, we have designed a series of effective similarity measures on domain distances to a given target domain. When there is a new domain, we use the proposed similarity measures to select the most relevant domains from a large number of existing domains. The number of such domains can be in the order of millions, thus. very large. The distance measures guarantee that the training data from the selected domains can improve the recommendation system's quality in the new domain without bringing negative transfer. We have tested different similarity measures that have both generality and effectiveness. We have designed an experiment that links the social media space and the physical space. Our method allows more effective extraction of features by comparing different domains. Objective 2: We have designed a framework to unify and integrate heterogeneous, noisy and inconsistent preference data from all selected domains for knowledge transfer. In particular, we have designed a method to unify heterogenous domain knowledge to allow for more effective feature engineering for cross-domain collaborative filtering. This has been tested successfully on different domains. Objective 3: We have solved this lifelong learning problem for coming domains by using the knowledge obtained in the previous two steps. We have designed a unified model to make the collaborative filtering models compatible with different forms of knowledge from existing domains. Unlike transfer learning methods, we used the obtained knowledge in new domains to improve the recommendation performance in existing domains, which is known as reverse knowledge transfer. Since it is unrealistic to store all received data, we have designed an efficient online learning method to update the older models without accessing the previous data. Objective 4: We have developed a scalable prototype system for lifelong collaborative filtering based on scalable online learning algorithms, and evaluated the developed system on WeChat news recommendation domains, which are real-world collaborative filtering tasks. We have disseminated the research results in the form of high-quality publications such as IJCAI and AAAI, and made the demo and algorithm available in an open source manner.

16211214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211214.value: We have developed a spectrum of effective algorithms and mathematical tools for judging the differences and similarities between problem domains. The frameworks and algorithms allow different domains to be mapped to a common space and heterogeneous data to be compared. Our active learning, reinforcement learning, and hierarchical attention algorithms allow different types of recommendation problems to be learned in a lifelong manner. Our results were published in top journals and conferences such as AAAI and IJCAI. In addition, prototype systems were built to illustrate the utility of the inventions, and a prototype system has been successfully tested on the WeChat news recommendation data.

16211214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211214.value: We will continue to develop lifelong learning algorithms via AUTOML frameworks, to allow systems to transfer knowledge in their lifetimes. These algorithms will benefit machine learning both in practice and in theory.

16211214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211214.value: Machine learning has been developed for individual algorithms. However, every time a new domain arrives, machine learning has to start from the beginning. In this project, we allow machines to continuously learn in lifetime. This allows the agents to be more intelligent. Our project makes machine learning closer to human learning behaviour, in that the automated agent can acquire knowledge while based on previous experiences, thus making learning much faster. The algorithm can benefit in making AI systems more adaptable, such as automatous cars, mobile recommendation systems, dialog systems, computer vision, and so on.

16211614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16211614.value: Epsilon近似摘要之通訊複雜性研究

16211614.label: Project Objectives
16211614.value: Design communication-efficient algorithms for computing epsilon-approximations over massive distributed data. We will consider various range spaces, in particular axis-parallel rectangles and halfspaces. We will consider both the flat communication model, as well as more complicated network topologies such as a tree or a general graph. While communication is the primary measure of cost, we will also try to make the algorithms efficient in terms of space and time. Study the communication complexity of computing epsilon-approximations for various range spaces. We will establish a general connection between the communication complexity and the discrepancy of the range space under investigation. We will study both the deterministic and randomized communication complexity.

16211614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211614.value: Sampling is a fundamental and highly effective approach to dealing with big data sets. It significantly reduces the size of the data, thereby making "big data" small, with the hope that certain properties of the data are still preserved in the sample. As information loss is inevitable in the sampling process, the majority of research on sampling theory focuses on the relationship between the sample size and its quality, which is usually some measure of error with respect to the property to be preserved. In this project, we are interested in geometric data, i.e., a set of points in a d-dimensional Euclidean space, and the property under investigation is data density, which means that the density of the sample should reflect the density of the underlying data: in denser regions of the data, more points should be sampled, while less points should be sampled in sparser regions of the data. Ideally, we want the sample density to be exactly proportional to the data density everywhere in the Euclidean space. However, since the sample consists of only a small subset of the data points, errors will have to be introduced. This is more precisely captured by the notion of epsilon-approximations, a concept well studied in the computational geometry literature. Informally speaking, an epsilon-approximation is a sample of the underlying data set that preserves the data density up to a given error of epsilon. However, all existing algorithms for constructing epsilon-approximations work only on a centralized data set. With the rapidly growing data size nowadays, it is common practice to collect, store, and manage data in a distributed fashion, such as using a computer cluster, a sensor network, or even the Internet. Thus, it is important to design algorithms to construct epsilon-approximations over distributed data, and study their complexities, which is the focus of this project. This project falls into the area of theoretical computer science. 採樣技術為攻克大數據問題的一個有效方法，可使得大數據變小，而同時保持其重要特性。由於在採樣過程中信息丟失不可避免，所以採樣理論的研究重點在于發現採樣大小和質量之間的內在關係，而質量的定義則和具體的採樣特性相關。本項目將注重于幾何數據，而我們所想要的採樣特性是空間密度，即在原始數據密集的地區，採樣點相對較多，而在原始數據稀疏的地方，采樣點也較少。在理想情況下，采樣密度應當嚴格和原始數據的空間密度成正比。然而，由于采樣大小有限，誤差不可完全避免，而誤差大小則恰好由計算幾何領域中Epslion近似摘要這一理念所刻畫。Epsilon近似摘要可以有效的保持數據密度，因此在很多應用中都很重要。Epsilon近似摘要在傳統的集中環境下已有很好的研究，而在大量的分佈式數據中則當前尚無有效計算方法。本研究將從通訊複雜度的角度出發，研究在分佈式環境下Epsilon近似摘要的有效計算方法。

16211614.label: Realisation of objectives
16211614.value: We have successfully achieved both objectives of this project. Objective 1: To achieve Objective 1, our idea is to exploit the discrepancy function of a given range space. We have designed a randomized algorithm in the simultaneous message passing model to compute an eps-approximation for any range space with known discrepancy. The algorithm works for any range space, with its communication cost depending on its discrepancy function. In addition, for the most common range spaces, such as axis-parallel rectangles and halfspaces, we have derived the precise communication costs of our algorithm. Objective 2: This objective is more theoretical. To establish the communication complexity of computing epsilon-approximations for various range spaces, we have proved almost tight lower bounds for many interesting range spaces. The lower bounds hold in the blackboard model and actually hold for computing any data structure that allows one to estimate the range count within ε accuracy, which may not be a subset of points of the data set as required by the strict definition of an eps-approximation. We provide both deterministic and randomized lower bounds, which are related to different notions of discrepancy of the underlying range space. In particular, we relate deterministic lower bounds to the partial l1-discrepancy, and line the randomized lower bounds to the (partial) l2-discrepancy and the (partial) generalized l-infinity-discrepancy.

16211714.value: 面向單細胞基因組圖譜分析的集成玻璃微/納毛細管平臺

16211714.label: Project Objectives
16211714.value: To demonstrate extraction of intact chromosomal DNA from a few cells using integrated glass micro/nanocapillaries. To demonstrate genome-wide mapping of single chromosomal DNA stretched through integrated glass nanocapillaries.

To demonstrate genome-wide mapping of single chromosomal DNA stretched through integrated glass nanocapillaries.

16211714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211714.value: Cancer can be considered as a genetic meltdown within individual cells. Understanding and curing cancer would require information on the extent and progression of such meltdown across a tumor tissue over time. Thus, rare cells obtained from small tumor biopsies are to be directly analyzed without the requirement of culturing them. This calls for a powerful technology capable of single-cell genome analysis. Recent optical mapping strategies, by stretching out single DNA molecules and linearly arraying genome information content in space, aim at an integrated view of the genome, essentially a scaffold for its assembly and large-scale organization without delving into single-base-pair resolution. Yet, conventional mapping of DNA does not suit single-cell genome analysis as it relies on enzymatic-based labeling schemes with substantial preprocessing of DNA prior to the analysis. A recent optical mapping approach avoids enzymatic-based labeling and takes advantage of sequence-dependent thermal denaturation of ds-DNA (denaturation mapping). Performing such mapping in aqueous solutions on fluorescently labeled DNA stretched in nanochannels offers advantages over those using surface-bound manipulation of DNA (e.g. combing DNA), including straightforward integration with sample-preparation and sample-extraction microfluidics, continuous throughput, and more homogenous stretching. Nanochannels rely on confinement-induced passive stretching of DNA into an equilibrium conformation without the requirement of complex hydrodynamic flow patterns. Hence, the technique is inherently parallel and suitable for high-throughput DNA linearization. Indeed, the last decade has seen pioneering studies in nanochannel-based genome mapping via restriction enzyme digests, nick labeling, or simply sequence-specific chemical and thermal denaturation. Each of these studies has made notable contributions towards the capability of single-cell genome-wide mapping. Nevertheless, nearly all have excluded sample-preparation microfluidics. An integrated approach that extracts single-cell DNA close to the nanochannel entrance is particularly crucial for direct single-cell genome analysis where the fragmentation of molecules often due to pipetting and transport must be avoided. Here, based on an innovative process technology, we propose an integrated platform towards a single-cell genome-wide mapping. The novelty, apart from the integration of sample-preparation and genome-wide mapping modules, arises from a unique and convenient process for integrating cylindrical glass micro/nanocapillaries using standard equipment tools in semiconductor fabrication industry. Specifically, we propose an integrated unique design that employs cylindrical glass micro/nanocapillaries for (1) extracting intact chromosomal DNA from a few cells; (2) mapping stretched single chromosomal DNA; we further propose (3) an all-inclusive approach for extracting, stretching, and mapping chromosomal DNA from a few or even a single cell. 癌症被認為是一種個別細胞中的“基因災難性突變”，研究和治療需要借助腫瘤組織獲取有關這種基因突變隨時間變化的範圍和過程的資訊。因此，從小的腫瘤活體切片獲取的罕見細胞需要不經培養就直接分析。這就急需一種能夠進行單細胞基因分析的有力技術。近來出現的光學圖譜分析技術，通過拉伸單個DNA分子並在空間中線性排列出基因資訊，能夠獲得基因組的綜合視圖，從而無需達到單個堿基對的解析度就能獲得基因組的整體構成。然而傳統的DNA圖譜分析依賴酶的標記，需要在分析前進行複雜的預處理，所以並不適用於單細胞分析。最近報導了一種光學圖譜分析方法（基因變性圖譜分析法）避免了基於複雜的酶的標記並利用雙鏈DNA的基於序列的熱變性特點。對在充滿水溶液的納米流道拉伸的螢光標記DNA進行圖譜分析比其他使用表面固定操控DNA技術（如DNA的分子梳技術）更有優勢，其中包括易於與樣品預處理和提取的微流技術集成，連續的處理能力以及均勻的拉伸。 在納米流道中，DNA由空間約束被動拉伸為平衡結構而無需複雜的流場。因此，此項技術在本質上相容且適用于高處理能力的DNA線性化。實際上，過去的十年中已經出現一些基於納米流道的基因組圖譜分析的先驅性研究，包括限制性內切酶技術、切口標記技術或簡單的特定序列化學和熱變性技術。每項研究都對單細胞全組基因圖譜分析做出了顯著貢獻。然而幾乎所有技術都不包括樣品預處理的微流技術。這樣，開發一種能在納米流道入口從單細胞提取DNA的方法尤為重要，尤其是對於解決直接的單細胞基因組分析中由於移液和轉移而經常發生的分子斷裂。 這裡，基於一種創新性的製造工藝，我們提出了一個面向單細胞全組基因圖譜分析的集成平臺。其新穎之處，不僅在於集成了樣品預處理和全組基因組圖譜分析模組，更體現在一種獨特而方便的工藝方法，能夠使用半導體製造工藝中的標準設備來集成柱形玻璃微/納毛細管。特別地，我們提出了一種獨特的集成設計，可使玻璃微/納毛細管用於（1）從少量細胞中提取完整的染色體DNA；（2）圖譜分析拉伸的單鏈染色體DNA；我們還提出了（3）一種包括了從很少的甚至是單個的細胞中提取，拉伸，圖譜分析染色體DNA的方法。

16211714.label: Realisation of objectives
16211714.value: It was a fabrication-intensive project and we had to improvise alternative approaches along the way to achieve major portions of objectives. Objective 1 has been achieved by introducing a new structure, namely silicon point constrictions. This structure has replaced integrated glass micro/nanocapillaries that were originally proposed but then abandoned due to issues with driving individual cells through them for single-cell lysis. Unlike the capillaries with a diameter only a fraction of a mammalian cell size, point constrictions can be fabricated sufficiently large featuring a knife-like sharp edge to remove the cytosol while leaving the nucleus as well as chromosomal DNA therein intact. Instead of targeting a few cells, many cells have been lysed serially one at a time in a flow-through (pressure-driven) design wherein microfluidic channels are arranged in parallel, each featuring a cascade of point constrictions. Specifically, we varied the constriction size and the number of constrictions and, investigated the effect on the reagent-free cell lysis and the isolation of intact nuclei. Further isolation of the chromosomal DNA from intact nuclei using point constrictions alone turned out to be problematic. To address the issue in a timely manner, we had to resort to the combination of mechanical and chemical lysis. We used point constrictions of a suitable size to trap intact nuclei and lyse them on chip by introducing chemical reagent. Objective 2 has also encountered an issue with the proposed glass nanocapillaries. We discovered that imaging and mapping DNA molecules stretched in the nanocapillaries is challenging due to lack of optical clarity. Various measures taken to enhance clarity (e.g. high magnification lenses) did not help much as the issue was identified to be inherent to the device itself. Resolving the issue required a major undertaking in device fabrication with an increased level of complexity and cost. Instead, we used point constrictions and applied hydrodynamic flow to stretch the chromosomal DNA upon release from nuclei (trapped and lysed in Objective 1). This platform has allowed us to image and map the stretched DNA. We are in the process of concluding our experiments and the results will be summarized in a peer-reviewed publication. As for the nanocapillaries initially fabricated for the DNA mapping, we characterized them for ion concentration polarization and molecular enrichment. Apart from the nuclei isolation and DNA mapping, we have demonstrated the utility of point constrictions for cell mechanoporation based on rapid membrane deformations for intracellular delivery of external agents. Additionally, we have utilized the fabrication method and demonstrated innovative devices featuring unique 3D microelectrodes for electrokinetic separation of blood plasma as well as dielectrophoretic railing and sorting of cells.

16211714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211714.value: A major outcome of this project is the successful development of single-cell point constrictions and their method of fabrication for various cell-based applications primarily for reagent-free rapid cell lysis and intact nuclei isolation (Huang et al., under review). Large constrictions have also been demonstrated for cell mechanoporation based on rapid membrane deformations and the intracellular delivery of exogenous agents (Xing et al., Anal. Chem., 2018). The fabrication method has been utilized for the formation of unique 3D microelectrodes to demonstrate innovative devices for electrokinetic separation of blood plasma (Xing et al., Anal. Chem., 2016) and dielectrophoretic railing and isolation of cells (Xing et al., Lab Chip 2018). Overall, the project led to a number of peer-reviewed publications in journals (4 published, 1 under review, and 1 under preparation) and international conferences (7 published). The project also contributed to the training of postgraduate students (PhD: 2 graduated; 3 ongoing and MPhil: 2 graduated).

16211714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211714.value: Further extraction of chromosomal DNA from intact nuclei through mechanical means turns out to be a major challenge. The task could be better addressed by a combination of physical forces (mechanical, electrical, or thermal). Additionally, on-chip lytic agents can be electrically generated through electrolysis. Point constrictions are made of doped silicon and conducive to electrical activation to create such additional effects.

16211714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211714.value: Miniaturized analytical devices have been successfully developed and demonstrated for various applications including reagent-free cell lysis for intact nuclei isolation; cell mechanoporation for intracellular delivery of exogenous agents; blood plasma extraction and dielectrophoretic railing and sorting of cells for downstream analyses. These technologies are likely to enable advances in life sciences and contribute to future product development in clinical and healthcare applications.

16212014.label: Project Objectives
16212014.value: To develop an open-loop source-degenerated resistive amplifier with low gain distortion, common-mode feedback, and power supply ripple rejection. To develop the on-chip current biasing scheme to compensate for the process variation; To develop an on-chip digital calibration scheme and circuits to achieve the high MDAC gain accuracy; To develop an embedded temperature sensor and a compensation scheme to compensate for the open-loop MDAC’s temperature dependence; To develop a low-power multi-bit GS/s SAR ADC; To fabricate and test the 12-bit 2GS/s pipeline-SAR hybrid ADC.

16212014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212014.value: 近年來,半導體產業界進入了納米時代。這些小器件所具有的小電容和高跨導為電路工作在GHz頻率下提供了可能。對於數位電路和低精度模數轉換電路,這已成為現實。雖然業界具有對於高精度(>12比特)的高速模數轉換電路的極大需求,這些電路的設計要求目前還是遠遠超過了這些器件的極限。 流水線模數轉換器是在GS/s速度下高精度量化的唯一結構。目前流水線模數轉換器的技術瓶頸在於回饋式的數模放大器(MDAC)。在回饋式的MDAC裡,環路中的跨導放大器需要極高的次級點來穩定環路。對於GS/s的量化速度要求下,相應的次級點頻率遠遠超出了現有工藝的極限。通過增加電源電壓,回饋式MDAC也可以實現GS/s的量化速度,但是卻要消耗很大的功率,功率效益會在0.5pJ/step以上。即使是一個典型的0.5pJ/step流水線模數轉換器,2GS/s速度下12比特精度下也需要消耗4瓦的功耗! 在這個專案中,我們會另闢蹊徑來研究一種開環的MDAC。開環MDAC不需要高的次級點,所以對於器件的頻寬要求大大的降低。但是,開環MDAC面臨一系列的技術挑戰,包括信號擺動引起的非線性,工藝差異,電源波動,溫度差異,和共摸影響。在這個專案中,我們將研發一系列新的電路技術來可靠的解決這些挑戰。我們同時會研發一個GS/s多位量化逐次逼近技術來第一次在GS/s的速率下實現流水線和逐次逼近混合結構。我們前期研究表明,通過開環MDAC和流水線/逐次逼近混合結構,高精度模數轉化電路在GS/s取樣速率下可以實現5倍功耗的降低。 雖然有了納米器件,電路設計員還沒有找到很好的設計方法來將其巨大的潛力實現在類比電路上。該專案將會跳離基於回饋放大器的傳統電路。該專案中的開環電路技術為通向納米器件潛力開啟了一扇門。該專案的成功將是在追求高速高精度模數轉換電路道路上的一個突破。該項吸引了工業界極大的興趣和支援,聯合電子會向該專案捐助他們40納米CMOS電路技術的流片機會。

16212014.label: Realisation of objectives
16212014.value: At the end of this project, the project team has achieved all the project objectives. However, the ADC speeds in objective 4 and 5 are lower than the planned speed. The pipelined-SAR ADC speed is 300MS/s, while the SAR ADC speed is 700MS/s. This is due to the limitation of the fabrication process, which is 65nm CMOS process. Indeed, the designed chip from this project achieved the fastest speed for single-channel pipelined-SAR ADC.

16212014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212014.value: In this project, we have studied the speed limitation of the pipelined-SAR ADC by building a quantitative circuit model. We found that the first SAR ADC is the bottleneck for this pipelined-SAR architecture. This is the first time this is found in the high-speed ADC community. Based on this finding, we have developed new architecture and circuits to speed up the first SAR ADC. We developed a loop-unrolled SAR ADC with split capacitor, which can speed up the SAR ADC by 60%. One problem we found for loop-unrolled SAR ADC is that the offset of the comparators changes significantly during the bit cycles, which will reduce the linearity of the SAR ADC. We have developed a new background calibration architecture to compensate this offset variation. In the end, we have developed a 6-bit SAR ADC with 700MS/s sampling speed. This is the fastest 6-bit SAR ADC achieved in 65nm process. We have also developed an open-loop MDAC with resistive load to reduce the power consumption of the pipelined-SAR ADC. We have developed a new methodology to design the optimal 2-stage open-loop MDACs. To eliminate negative effects due to PVT (process voltage temperature) variation, we have developed a new calibration technique for the MDAC. In the end, we have successfully designed a 12bit 300MS/s pipelined SAR ADC chip in a 65nm CMOS process. Measurements show that the chip can achieve 63.55dB SNDR with the power consumption of 12.5mW. The figure-of-merit is 34fJ/conversion. This reaches the state-of-the-art in the ADC design community. We have also measured multiple chips with supply voltage variations. The measurements show our design is quite robust against PVT spread. Therefore, all the design objectives in this project are met successfully.

16212014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212014.value: The new design of high-speed pipelined-SAR from this project is leading to possible solutions for future applications. 5G communication is for commercial application next year in China. Many other countries will follow soon. In the research community, 6G communication is actively being pursued. In these applications, high-speed low-power ADC is critical for mobile phones. In 5G receiver, the ADC requires to sample at 2.4GS/s with 12-14 bit resolution. The pipelined-SAR design in this work has already provided an efficient foundation for a time-interleaved design with 8 channels to achieve the 2.4GS/s sampling rate. Currently, ZTE and Huawei are in the discussion with the project team to apply the ADC design expertise from this project to develop a 2GS/s 12bit ADC. We are planning to apply and carry new projects on this topic soon.

16212014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212014.value: In this project, we have studied and found the cause of the speed limitation of pipelined-SAR ADCs. We have made new designs on architecture and circuits for SAR ADCs to achieve the fastest speed so far. I have also developed open-loop MDAC and the new calibration technique to remove the PVT variation occurring in open-loop MDACs. As a result, we have designed a high-speed pipelined-SAR ADC with good robustness. The design is tested with fabricated chips. The measured results from the chip show the new design from this project achieved the fastest single-channel pipelined SAR ADC with state-of-the-art low power consumption. This is a solid step to push up the ADC speed in the ADC community. The new design from this project can be readily applied to achieve ADC with much higher speed at GS/s. The outcome of this project has good commercialization prospect. It has attracted major telecom companies to develop collaborated research with the project team.

16212114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16212114.value: 用於100-Gbit以太網系統時鐘數據恢復電路的低壓CMOS四通道重定時晶片系統

16212114.label: Project Objectives
16212114.value: To design, implement and test a novel low-power quad-channel quarter-rate retimer SoC consisting of a shared global frequency-locked loop (FLL) that feeds the recovered clock to four identical phase-locked loops (PLL). The half-rate clock is divided by an injection-locked frequency divider to obtain four phases locally within each of the four PLLs. Since the power hungry voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and frequency divider are shared by four paths, power consumption can be greatly reduced. The phase alignment and adjustment will be realized by a phase interpolator (PI) locally instead of tuning the VCO frequency as in conventional architecture. This topology can greatly reduce power and improve the phase alignment accuracy between the four channels and correct any error due to routing mismatch. To support reconfigurable data output formats, a quarter-rate phase detector (PD) incorporating a 1-3 tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE) will be designed to achieve phase detection, equalization and 1:4 de-multiplexing. A multi-mode 2:1/4:1 multiplexer will also be implemented.

Since the power hungry voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and frequency divider are shared by four paths, power consumption can be greatly reduced.
