To support reconfigurable data output formats, a quarter-rate phase detector (PD) incorporating a 1-3 tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE) will be designed to achieve phase detection, equalization and 1:4 de-multiplexing. A multi-mode 2:1/4:1 multiplexer will also be implemented.

16212114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212114.value: The global internet protocol (IP) traffic has quadrupled from 2007 to 2012 and has reached 0.53 zettabytes per year (1 ZB = 1 billion terabytes) in 2012, according to Cisco, a leading network equipment manufacturer. It is projected that by the end of 2015, the annual global IP traffic will exceed 1 ZB fueled by two key rapidly growing trends – wireless networked devices and video traffic. To keep pace with this tremendous demand, the data communication speed between network equipment in the cloud computing infrastructure, such as data centers, needs be upgraded urgently. Today’s servers and storage equipment in data centers communicate with each other using the first generation 100 Gigabit Ethernet (100GbE) standard, which uses 10 parallel channels/links each carrying 10-Gb/s data. For link distance less than 10 m, copper-based cables are widely used. However, for longer range connections, as the product of the bandwidth and the data rate exceeds 100 Gb/s-m, optical fibers are needed because the copper cables present too much attenuation to the signal. To improve the link speed and density, the second-generation 100-Gb/s Ethernet (100GbE) will be upgraded to 25-Gb/s x 4 channels as proposed by the IEEE P802.3ba Ethernet Task Force. Therefore, all the copper cables in data centers longer than ~4 meters will need to be replaced by optical fibers. This will create very large demand for 100GbE optical transceiver modules which perform the conversion of the signal between optical and electrical domains. In a 100GbE receiver module, four retiming circuits (i.e. quad retimer) are employed to recover the clock signals and synchronize them to the four 25-Gb/s data streams for precision sampling. Categorized by the timing relationship between the clock and data, there are mainly three operation modes: full rate, half rate and quarter rate. In full-rate operation, the rising edges of the clock are aligned with each transition edge of data and thus the clock is running at 25GHz. In half-rate operation, both the rising and falling edges are utilized to reduce the clock frequency by half. To further reduce the clock frequency and power consumption, quarter-rate mode operates with 4-phase clocks. The design tradeoff is the power consumption versus the number of output data streams. Currently, state-of-the-art quad retimer ICs can only operate in one particular mode. This project aims to research and develop a low-power CMOS reconfigurable quad-channel retimer IC that can support all three modes. 據國際領先網絡設備製造商思科公司報告： 2012年全球互聯網協議(IP)流量達到了0.53ZB(1ZB=10^9 TB) ，為2007年的四倍多。 得益於無線網絡終端和在線視頻應用的快速發展，據預測 2015年全球IP流量將超過1ZB 。 為了滿足這一巨大需求，雲計算數據中心內網絡設施間的通信速率迫切需要進行升級。 而現今數據中心內的服務器和儲存設施間依然使用第一代100千兆以太網(100GbE ）標准進行通信。 第一代100GbE採用並行10通道，每通道傳輸速率為10千兆每秒(Gb/s) 。在距離小於10米的鏈路中，銅基電纜被廣泛採用。 但對於帶寬和數據速率乘積超過100千兆每秒 • 米(Gb/s • m)的長距離鏈路，銅基電纜由於衰減過大不能繼續使用，而光纖作為傳輸介質成了必然的選擇。 為了提高連接速度和密度，第二代100GbE將被升級為由IEEE P802.3ba 以太網工作組提出的並行4通道、每通道速率25Gb/s的架構。 因此,數據中心所有長於4米的銅纜將被光纖取代，這將引發對 100GbE 光電轉換收發模塊的巨大需求。 在 100GbE 系統 接收模 塊 中，四通道重定時器電路 被用來恢復 時鐘 信號並精確採 樣 四通道 速率為 25 Gb/s 的數據流。 依據時鐘 和數據之 間 的 時 序關係 進 行分 類 ， 時 脈 產 生 電 路主要有三種 工作 模式 ： 全速率，半速率和四分之一速率。 在全速率 工作模式下 ，每個通道時鐘頻 率 為 25GHz ，時鐘的上升 沿 對 準數據信號的 變 化沿。 在半速率工作模式下， 利用 時鐘 的上升沿和下降沿 分別對 數據 進 行採 樣以此來減半時鐘頻率 。 四分之一速率模式利用四相 位時鐘來進 一步 降低時鐘頻 率和功耗。 工作模式間的選擇在於 功耗與 輸 出 數據通道數的權衡 。 目前，最先 進 的四通道 時 脈 產 生芯片 僅 可以在一個特定的模式下 工作 。 該項 目旨在研 發 一種基於 CMOS 工藝 的低功耗三種模式可 重構 的四通道 重定時器電路 芯片。

16212114.label: Realisation of objectives
16212114.value: The two design objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. We have designed, implemented and tested a novel low-power quad-channel quarter-rate retimer SoC consisting of a shared global frequency-locked loop (FLL) that feeds the recovered clock to four identical phase-locked loops (PLL). Secondly, to support reconfigurable data output formats, a quarter-rate phase detector (PD) incorporating a 1-3 tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE) has been designed and implemented to achieve phase detection, equalization and 1:4 de-multiplexing.

16212114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212114.value: The quarter-rate retimer receiver architecture has been experimentally verified and the results are published in the journal paper "A 26-Gb/s 0.31-pJ/bit Receiver with Linear Sampling Phase Detector for Data and Edge Equalization," IEEE SSC Letters, Feb 2018. The application of this system architecture is further exploited to implement a novel optical-to-millimeter-wave system-on-a-chip (SoC) by integrating the quarter-rate optical receiver architecture with a wideband millimeter-wave power amplifier (see "A Full Ka-Band Power Ampliﬁer with 32.9% PAE and 15.3dBm Power in 65-nm CMOS," IEEE TCAS-I, April, 2018). The combined SoC is the second-generation optical-to-millimeter-wave SoC for 5G hybrid ﬁber-wireless networks where broadband millimeter-wave links are utilized to supplement the backhaul optical links. High integration level, large data bandwidth and lower power consumption are shown to be feasible using the quarter-rate architecture. The first-generation fiber-wireless SoC design was reported in 2015 under this project and published in "A 60-GHz 4-Gb/s Fully Integrated NRZ-to-QPSK Fiber-Wireless Modulator," IEEE TCAS-I, March 2017. The quarter-rate retimer receiver developed in this project is based on a novel linear phase detector with embedded data and clock edge equalization. This development was carried out in conjunction with another project “Integrated Baseband-over-Fiber Optical Receiver with 60GHz QPSK Transmitters for Hybrid 5G Network,” supported by GRF Project No. 16201815, in order to demonstrate the application of the quarter-rate architecture at a higher scale of integration.

16212114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212114.value: Based on our current success, to further raise the performance and expand the application of the current SoC, the quarter-rate system can be improved to support both the legacy binary non-return-to-zero (NRZ) signaling and the emerging 4-level pulse-amplitude-modulation (PAM4) scheme. To meet this requirement, the receiver linearity must be enhanced and the PAM4 decoder design must be investigated. To support the up and coming 5G applications with hybrid fiber-wireless broadband links, linearization circuit techniques for millimeter-wave power amplifier and transmitter design need to be further researched.

16212114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212114.value: In this project, the proposed quarter-rate retiming architecture is experimentally demonstrated to be the optimal architecture for energy-efficient high-speed serial link receiver design at above 20Gbit/s. This technology will potentially benefit 5G network deployment and data-center applications. This project has successfully trained a PhD student and a post-doc fellow. Dr. Haikun Jia, the Post-doc Fellow, led the overall system design and worked closely with the PhD student, Yipeng Wang on the receiver design. Dr. Yipeng Wang has graduated in September 2016 and now works for Xilinx Singapore.

16212214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212214.value: Dress-up simulation is one of the core technologies supporting on-line shopping of garment products. Currently there is no real-time system that caters for changing and selection different dress codes or dress combinations for on-line portal. The proposal details a solution to meet the demand. The solution scheme relies on a number of new computer-aided design, modeling, simulation and rendering techniques and algorithms. Human and garment models are represented by semantic parametric features. The semantic parametric features are used to encapsulate design data to facilitate the subsequent design. The garment dress-up model is constructed using a duplicated skin and multi-layer shell map technique. The multi-layer representation provides a structure to support the choice of different dress codes or dress combinations. The duplicated skin technique allows the speedy direct transfer of the dresses parametrically across different human models. The parametric modeling of the garment and the human model is made possible by the set of semantic features representing the human model and the garments. The dress-up model is transformed into a meshless surfel-grid model which is a point-based model with defined surface normal. The meshless surfel-grid model with augmented radial basis function is a weak formulation that speeds up the wrinkle tensor computation when compares against the commonly used mesh model. This will enable a fast evaluation of cloth wrinkles in the dress-up simulation. The layered depth images (LDI) coupled surfel-grid model offers additional advantage of fast rendering using OpenGL depth buffering pixel data capitalizing on graphics processing unit (GPU) based parallel processing. The adoption of the LDI surfel-grid representation is in line with the use of the voxel-based coherence collision detection algorithm developed previously by the Principal Investigator. This algorithm is further enhanced by the degeneracy classification currently being developed at HKUST. The new meshless LDI surfel-grid representation-based solution scheme enables an efficient dress-up model construction using a multi-layer shell map and fast rendering using a LDI surfel-grid representation. 裝扮仿真是支持網上購買服裝產品的一個的核心技術。目前沒有服裝網購平台可以提供實時更換和選擇不同服裝或服裝組合。這提案提供一個滿足需求詳細的解決方案。該解決方案依賴一些新的計算機輔助設計，建模，仿真和图形展像技術和算法。人体和服裝模型是建基於語義參數特徵。該參數化語義特徵内含設計數據以支援後續設計。服裝裝扮模型是使用重複外層結構和多層殼圖的技術。多層殼圖提供結構以支持不同的服裝組合的選擇。該重複外層結構技術使參數化裝扮快速直接傳送到不同的人體模型。語義特徵表示人體模型和服裝支持人體和衣服的參數化建模。裝扮模型轉化為以點和徑向基函數為基礎的無網格面元網格模型，比常用的網格模型皺紋計算方法較快，加速裝扮模擬。支持面元網格模型的分層深度圖像技术（LDI），利用 OpenGL的深度緩衝的像素數據和圖形處理單元（GPU）的並行處理，提供快速額外的好處。採用了LDI面元網格是配合由項目負責人早前開發的體素碰撞檢測算法。本算法在香港科技大學進一步增強腐朽特徵處理。新的無網格 LDI面元網代表的解決方案方案提供有效率的參數化多層殼圖結構的快速裝扮图形展像。

16212314.value: 实用的并行错误的重现

16212314.label: Project Objectives
16212314.value: Formulate a new symbolic causal model for multi-threaded C/C++ programs. As the theoretical foundation, we first plan to formulate a novel symbolic causal model that underpins the correctness and the efficiency of our bug reproduction algorithms. A causal model is the key to the static reasoning of the global execution order any bug reproduction technique would search for, in order to trigger the bug. As all existing causal models are based on real values collected at runtime, we plan to define and to prove similar causal guarantees if the inter-dependencies of the read and write operations become symbolic. Both the PI and Co-I have a rich experience already in achieving this objective. The PI has the in-depth experience in applying existing causal models to detect bugs. The Co-I's expertise in relaxed memory models is well suited in addressing the instruction reordering issues prevalent on modern commodity multiprocessors in the framework. Design highly parallelized constraint-solving algorithms. Our approach can potentially generate a large number of first order formulae to encode the program execution. As the execution prolongs, the scalability of the constraint solver can quickly become a limiting factor for achieving our research objective. Our idea is a clever reduction from a search problem to a verification problem by bounding the number of preemptions. The reduced verification is friendly to parallel processing as they can be carried out independently. We plan to explore both GPU and cluster-based parallelization models to make our technique scale to long production executions. Extend Klee to perform multithreaded symbolic execution We plan to perform two non-trivial modifications to the Klee symbolic execution engine. We first change the state-space exploration strategy as, in our research, Klee only needs to explore a known program path instead of splitting the state-space upon each branch. The second modification is to properly handle the program state sharing at the thread forking point. Our idea is to use a ``copy-on-evaluate'' strategy to implement the sharing of symbolic variables. Quantify the runtime characteristics of our technique We will carefully evaluate the impact of our technique from various aspects. We will use real large concurrent systems as subjects of our evaluation. We will design experiments to first capture the monitoring overhead of the proposed technique. The monitoring overhead includes both the program slowdown and the storage cost for the generated logs. To evaluate the bug reproducibility, we will use seeded faults to conduct the controlled experiments as well as real bugs to assess the practical capability. We also plan to implement a few related approaches for benchmarking.

16212314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212314.value: The AMD Opteron 6300 Series Processors already contain as many as 16 cores. This multi-core trend of today's CPU architecture mandates software engineers to divide computation into many independent subtasks to accommodate the ever increasing computation needs. This type of so-called concurrent programs, often running for days, weeks, or even months, are becoming highly complex, processing large volumes of data and carrying out many computation tasks simultaneously at a random pace. Failures in this type of systems are well known to be extremely difficult to reproduce, making them hard to understand and to remedy. For instance, it took professional software engineers many months to figure out what went wrong in the software failure that caused 2003 Northeast electricity blackout in USA and Canada. For software errors triggered by a seemingly random process, engineers face tremendous difficulties in recreating and comprehending them. To improve the effectiveness of bug reproduction, the conventional wisdom calls for a hybrid approach by using a watchdog to monitor the dynamic behavior of the program, in order to simplify the post-mortem analysis. Techniques that follow this design are well known to be heavyweight because the watchdog needs to capture the high degree of randomness that is pervasive in concurrent software. The corresponding runtime slow down incurred by the watchdog is so significant that it is even formidable to use in the development phase, whereas most of the catastrophic software failures happen in the field. This proposed research has the potential of changing this unsatisfactory landscape and making the reproduction of concurrency bugs practical to testing or even to production environments. We have prototyped a method, fundamentally and completely different from all existing solutions, that no longer tracks any inter-task dependencies randomly generated at the runtime of the program. Instead, the watchdog only logs the internal logic flow of each independent task, a mature technique perfected through many years of research to incur very low execution overhead. We formulate random dependencies, in the post-mortem analysis phase, as hypotheses verifiable using automatic theorem provers. By shifting the analysis cost from execution time to post-execution time, our technique is essentially only as low as a typical performance profiler already widely used in production. In the proposal, we present a detailed case study to illustrate the key conceptual steps of the technique. We also outline the key theoretical and engineering challenges and how they will be addressed. 并行错误重现是很昂贵的。我们提出一个新的羽量级的方法让并行错误可以在实际情况当中被应用。这个方法是基于对本地执行路径的追踪和符号执行方法的结合。程序的开销可以被降低到基本的监控操作。

16212314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212314.value: The proposed research showed that concurrency bugs could be reproduced cheaply, recognising the cost of global synchronisation as well as the benefit of thread-local monitoring. This, of course, would also rely on a precise knowledge of the program behaviour prior to runtime, which has led to the discovery of better static analysis algorithms. The proposed research concluded successfully by producing both top-grade research papers and research tools that pave the foundation for further research. Specifically, the work of reproducing Heisenburg bugs was well recognised by the PLDI community and won a distinguished paper award. Meanwhile, the research team were inspired by many observations during the course and went on solving relevant problems, which had led to further publications in OOPSLA.

16212314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212314.value: The project has concluded and there is no plan of further development.

16212314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212314.value: In today’s software design, software engineers spin off as many independent tasks as they reasonably can for leveraging the many processing cores available on the single commodity CPU chip. Failures in this type of systems are well known to be extremely difficult to reproduce, making them hard to understand and to remedy. One attractive idea to compact this difficulty is what can be referred to as the “time machine” for software execution, a family of techniques under the umbrella term of “record and replay” (RR). Unfortunately, the overall runtime overhead of RR techniques is still so significant that it is even difficult to use them in the testing environment. This proposed research has the potential of changing this unsatisfactory landscape. We have prototype a method that is fundamentally and completely different from all existing solutions. Rather than tracking any inter-task dependencies or record any intermediate results, the proposed technique exerts a very minimal interference to the recorded program by only watching the outcome of the decision points in the program. Monitoring decision outcomes has a very deep foundation in research and there are many effective solutions of how to do it cheaply.

16212514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212514.value: During the Wenchuan earthquake, over 20,000 lives were lost due to earthquake- induced landslides. In the past five years after the earthquake, landslide activities in the Wenchuan earthquake zone led to over 1,600 additional fatalities. Indeed human safety in a landslide-prone area is a serious concern, and decision makers often give top priority to the risks to human lives in engineering planning and design. Yet the human risks due to landslides are sometimes considered “intangible” due to extremely limited casualty data in previous studies and hence receive less attention as opposed to structural vulnerability. Landslide hazards often occur in chain events. One initiation event triggers one or several hazards. Human vulnerability to one hazard can also be affected by the occurrence of other hazards. Conventional risk assessment often does not consider the interactions among multiple hazards and the impact of the presence of one hazard on the vulnerabilities to other hazards. Such assessment grossly underestimated the risks in particular places, such as the Wenchuan earthquake zone in China, and resulted in repetitive engineering reconstructions and large numbers of human casualties. The primary objectives of this proposed research project are to develop a large database of landslide-induced casualties and to propose a methodology to assess the human risks posed by landslides considering possible cascading effects, as well as interactions among the vulnerabilities to the hazards. The first step in this project is to compile a comprehensive database of landslide-induced human casualties, particularly the landslide cases in the Wenchuan earthquake zone that involved a large number of casualties. Based on the information in the database and judgement, mathematical models for simulating the human fleeing process from an idealised landslide and evaluating the casualty rates, considering the interactions among the vulnerabilities to multiple hazards, will be developed. Subsequently, a methodology to assess risks to humans posed by multiple landslide hazards considering interactions among the hazards and possible cascading effects will be proposed. A detailed case study in the Wenchuan earthquake zone, which involves slides, debris flows and landslide dams, will finally be conducted to illustrate the multi-hazard human risk analysis methodology. The proposed project will provide a large landslide casualty database and extend the existing landslide risk assessment methodologies to complex situations involving interactions among multiple hazards and among the vulnerabilities to these hazards. Effective landslide management and prevention strategies will also be suggested based on scientific analyses and historical landslide casualty data. 在2008年的汶川地震中，超過2000人因地震誘發的滑坡喪生，震後五年內汶川震區的滑坡災害又導致1600多人死亡，人民的生命安全受到滑坡的嚴重威脅。在工程決策中工程師通常將人的安全放在首位。但是，由於現有的傷亡資料十分有限，滑坡威脅難於定量評估。 滑坡災害通常與災害鏈的方式發生。一個初發事件可引發一個或者數個災害，遇險人員就會同時處於數個災害的威脅之下。傳統的風險評估方法通常不考慮多個災害事件之間的層疊作用及抵禦災害能力不斷下降的影響。因此，這類方法可能嚴重低估特定地區的滑坡風險。 該項研究專案的主要目的，是建立一個滑坡災害人員傷亡記錄的大型資料庫，提出一個考慮災害之間的層疊影響的滑坡風險評估方法，並用之於評估滑坡災害對生命威脅的風險。本項研究的第一步是建立一個完整的滑坡災害人員傷亡資料庫，尤其要建立人員傷亡嚴重的汶川地震區滑坡事件的資料庫。然後結合資料庫資訊和分析判斷，建立數學模型，類比滑坡發生時人類的逃生過程，計算傷亡概率。在充分研究災害之間的相互作用和層疊效應之後，提出一個新的滑坡生命風險評估方法。進行汶川地震區滑坡災害的實例研究，以此展現所提出的多重災害下生命風險評估方法的應用。最後，根據科學分析和歷史傷亡資料，提出有效的滑坡風險管理策略。

16212514.label: Realisation of objectives
16212514.value: Task 1: Compilation of a comprehensive database of landslide casualties The scarcity of landslide fatality data has limited the ability to consider many important factors vital to human vulnerability and to validate existing models. During the period of Sept. 2014 and Jan. 2017, we compiled two large databases: a database of landslides that involved severe fatalities, and a database of all sorts of fatalities caused by the Wenchuan earthquake. 1. Landslide fatality database The majority of the entries are the recent landslides in the Wenchuan earthquake zone in China, and in the earthquake-prone regions around the world (e.g. Japan, Taiwan, Nepal, Pakistan, Chile, USA, and New Zealand). We also organised landslide database into two datasets: a Chinese landslide dataset and a global landslide dataset. The information includes landslide location, date, type, size, activity, causal factors, and consequences of failure. So far the database has the following entries: (1) 37 major landslides involving the death of 7483 people in the Wenchuan earthquake zone; (2) 15 rock slides involving the death of 728 people; (3) 314 fatal landslides involving the death of 15572 people around the world. Each entry includes the following information: (1) Factors related to the landslide intensity: Geological and topographic features, type of landslide, lithology, volume, run-out distance, run-out velocity, area of deposition, etc.; (2) Factors related to human susceptibility: Distribution of population at risk prior to the landslide, age, gender, education, physical capability, experience of landslides, etc.; (3) Factors related to preparedness and evacuation: Risk prevention plan, training, warning time, availability and resilience of shelters, landslide time, evacuation effort etc.; (4) Number of casualties by each type of hazard, severity of injuries. This task was undertaken by Dr ZHANG Shuai and three MSc students (Mr HONG Fan, Ms CHEN Zhu and Ms DENG Meilan). 2. Wenchuan earthquake general fatality database This research comprehensively recorded, analysed and presented the fatalities caused by the Wenchuan earthquake at the town/township level, including affected areas in Sichuan Province, Gansu Province and Shanxi Province. The primary purpose is to reconstruct the distribution of the fatalities (over 69,000) in the entire earthquake area and to provide data for seismic vulnerability analysis considering local geological/topographic, and social-economic conditions. We have had a comprehensive collection of the annals and government statistics at the town/county level. This task formed the major content of Mr HE Shuanglin’s MPhil thesis. This project provided us an opportunity to continuously monitor the landslide activities in the Wenchuan earthquake zone between 2014 and 2017, making HKUST one of the very few institutions who continuously monitored the evolution of landslide hazards in the Wenchuan earthquake zone in the 10-year period after the earthquake. Accordingly more than 10 top journal papers have been published to document our observations. Task 2: Quantifying human vulnerability to landslides based on casualty data Two levels of vulnerability analyses have been performed: site-specific level and global level. At site specific level, we investigated the risk to people at a specific site or distributed along a highway. A physically-based multi-hazard risk assessment platform for regional rainfall-induced slope failures and debris flows has been established to evaluate the likelihood of landslides and debris flows under a storm event, the runout of the landslide or debris flow materials over the digital terrain, and the risk to the population at risk inside the study area. A theoretical vulnerability model has been developed for multi-hazard scenarios. Several papers have been published on this topic. At the global level, an empirical method is being established by relating fatality ratio to major factors affecting life safety, such as Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale, population density, per capita GDP and topography. Specifically, Beichuan County, Dujiangyan City and Lushan were selected as representative site-specific study sites for deriving an empirical formula to describe the relationship between fatality rate and the four aforementioned key parameters. Both multiple regression analysis and calibrated VIS model are applied and their goodness-of-fit is compared. In addition, for the multiple regression analysis, different combinations of the site-specific data sets are examined and compared in the derivation of both linear form and log form of empirical formulas. We have conducted a detailed case study, the August 2010 Zhouqu debris flow case, in order to establish vulnerability models for estimating the human vulnerability and building vulnerability to landslides based on casualty and building damage data. The August 2010 Zhouqu debris flow led to the loss of over 1700 lives and the damage to over 300 houses. First, the distributions of the buildings and the population in Zhouqu before the debris flow were established. Second, the distributions of the fatalities and building damage caused by the Zhouqu debris flow were determined. Then large-scale numerical analyses were performed to reproduce the Zhouqu debris flow and calculate the hazard intensity (flow depth and flow velocity). The movement and deposition process of the debris flow were simulated using a two-dimensional finite model FLO-2D, coupled with the geographic information system. The study area included Sanyanyu Gully and Luojiayu Gully of Zhouqu County. The deposition, velocity, impact force, and influence zone of the debris flow were simulated. Finally, empirical vulnerability relations between fatality rate and debris flow intensity and between building damage degree and debris flow intensity were established. Additionally, a fatal landslide occurred on 20 Dec. 2015 in Shenzhen, which killed 77 people and buried 33 buildings. The research team responded to this disaster immediately, assisting in the disaster relief and took this event as a new case study. We visited the sites twice, promptly measuring the landslide characteristics and surveying the damaged buildings. We have established a numerical model to simulate the movements of the landslide and the impact forces on the buildings. Task 3: Suggestions for effective management and prevention strategies We have established a Bayesian network linking the fatality rate with a large number of influence factors based on the theory proposed by Peng and Zhang (2012). The prior probabilities and posterior probabilities were calculated based on a dataset of 396 cases of landslides and the debris flow intensity obtained from the numerical analysis. By comparing the sensitivity of prior probabilities and conditional probabilities of different nodes (factors), several key factors that influence landslide fatality have been identified, such as time of the day, evacuation and building structure type. Managing these key factors is essential to effectively reduce landslide fatality. The Bayesian network establishes quantitative relations between fatality rate and a number of social-economic factors that are essential to landslide risk management, such as role of local administration, political aspects and hazard preparedness training. These factors are reflected in the probability distributions of the time required to respond to an idealised landslide, make evacuation decisions, and evacuate the population at risk to safer places. For instance, the response time, delay time and movement time are influenced by preparedness and evacuation training. To decrease the casualties, it is necessary to establish a good contingency plan, especially for landslide hazards that occur in night time, enhance the evacuation organization and the capacity of buildings.

16212514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212514.value: In this project, we compiled a comprehensive database of over 15,000 landslide fatalities involving cases from around the world. We also reconstructed the distribution of the fatalities (over 69,000) caused by the Wenchuan earthquake. The two datasets are of retention value and will serve as basis for many follow-up studies. Based on the two datasets, we have established empirical models for estimating the fatality rate and degree of building damage when exposed to landslides. A physically-based multi-hazard risk assessment platform for regional rainfall-induced slope failures and debris flows has been established to evaluate the likelihood of landslides and debris flows under a storm event, the runout of the landslide or debris flow materials over the digital terrain, and the risk to the population at risk inside the study area. Two detailed case studies were also performed to illustrate our proposed methodologies: The Zhouqu case that involved a death toll of 1700 people and the Province Road 303 case which is the largest aid project supported by the HKSAR government. We have also established a Bayesian network to link the fatality rate with a large number of social-economic factors such as time of landslide, organised evacuation and public preparedness. The key factors affecting the fatality rate have been identified, which provides us guides to effective landslide risk management. The methodologies developed in this project were applied to (1) guide the risk-based decision in the selection of the new highway alignment for Province Road 303 near the Epicentre of the Wenchuan earthquake; (2) support a landslide warning system for the highway; and (3) investigate the fatal landslide occurring in Shenzhen on 20 Dec. 2015, which killed 77 people and buried 33 buildings. This research project has been very fruitful. Twelve international journal papers and five international conference papers have been published. The outcome was presented in five keynote/invited lectures in international conferences. Two PhD student, 1 MPhil student, and three MSc students were trained in this project. Among them, Dr Chen, Hongxin received the HKIE Ringo Yu Prize for Best PhD Thesis in Geotechnical Studies 2015, and Dr Danka won Kézdi Prize in May 2015 from Hungarian Society of ISSMGE. The PI, Dr Zhang, received GEOSNet Award over ASCE Georisk 2017 in June 2017 in Denver, Colorado and Wilson Tang Best Paper Award in June 2016 on the 6th Asian Pacific Symposium on Structural Reliability and Its Applications, Shanghai.

16212514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212514.value: Human safety in landslide-prone areas is a serious concern, and decision makers often give top priority to the risks to human lives in engineering planning and design. The primary objectives of this proposed research project were to develop a large database of landslide-induced casualties and to propose a methodology to assess the human vulnerability to landslides based on field data. In this project, we (1) compiled a comprehensive database of over 15,000 landslide fatalities involving cases from around the world; (2) reconstructed the distribution of the fatalities (over 69,000) caused by the Wenchuan earthquake; (3) established empirical models for estimating fatality rate and degree of building damage when exposed to landslides; (4) conducted two detailed case studies (the Zhouqu case that involved a death toll of 1700 people and the Province Road 303 case which is the largest aid project supported by the HKSAR government). The methodologies developed in this project were applied to guide the selection of the new highway alignment for Province Road 303 near the Epicentre of the Wenchuan earthquake, and to investigate the fatal landslide that occurred in Shenzhen on 20 Dec. 2015, which killed 77 people and buried 33 buildings.

16212714.label: Project Objectives
16212714.value: To adopt a digital filter to prevent control transmissions from leaking out to adjacent data channels. In order to mitigate the interference from the data channel, we will employ an OFDM nulling technique that leverages the orthogonality property of OFDM to null the interference from data channels by "taking samples" from the nulling points of the data channel, where the sum of power leakage of the data signal equals to zero. In order to increase reliability, we will adopt a high transmission power and strong coding scheme to enhance the control messages. To design the overall Pilotfish system for guard-band control support. For each 802.11n channel, Pilotfish places several narrow control bands, which cling to the both sides of the data channel. These control bands will collectively provide a general communication channel for exchanging control messages with a data rate of 250Kbps. To implement Pilotfish using the Sora software radio platform [5] for feasibility validation. To conduct comprehensive performance evaluation to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design. To build two example applications: control channel RTS/CTS (CCRC) and concurrent feedback, to demonstrate that Pilotfish can be positioned as a general explicit control channel to enable a wide range of applications. CCRC will use Pilotfish to perform contention and exchange RTS/CTS in the control channel, and therefore, removes the MAC access overhead. Concurrent feedback will exploit Pilotfish to send immediate feedback to the sender, therefore, enables fine-grained adaptation.

16212714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212714.value: The data transmission rate at the physical layer(PHY) in wireless networks can be up to 600Mbps in IEEE802.11n. Future standards, such as IEEE802.11ac, are expected to provide even higher data rates (>1Gbps). However, the efficiency of the Wi-Fi protocol can drop dramatically with the increase of data transmission rate[1]. It was reported that only 60Mbps actual throughput can be achieved with 300Mbps data rate[2]. Wi-Fi network heavily relies on implicit control mechanisms of carrier-sensing and random backoff. Recent research has shown that implicit control is quite inefficient when the PHY speed is high. On the other hand, explicit control channels provide advanced features to improve spectrum efficiency with clear overhead. An explicit control channel can be setup in a separate spectrum-band or inside the data channel. The former solution is simple but requires additional spectrum. The latter with introduce interference into the data channel. In this project, we propose a novel approach to augment Wi-Fi with an explicit and decoupled control channel, without introducing any overhead. Our design is based on the observation that between every two adjacent Wi-Fi channels there is a guard-band reserved. If we can leverage these guard-bands to carry control messages, we can introduce control channel into Wi-Fi networks for FREE. In wireless communication, a guard-band is reserved to prevent signal power leakage from causing a significant interference on the adjacent channel. Therefore, to create a control channel inside the guard-band we need to make sure the transmissions on the guard-band will not cause additional interference to nearby data channels. Moreover, the nearby data transmissions should not cause severe interference in the guard-band control message exchange. In this project, we will build a guard-band control channel by (1) applying a filter to suppress the control channel’s out-of-band emission, (2) leveraging the orthogonality property of OFDM to null the interference from data channel, and (3) providing a reliable PHY with high transmission power and strong channel coding. To demonstrate the feasibility, we will implement Pilotfish system and evaluate the design using Sora software radio platform. Moreover, we will propose two applications, control channel RTS/CTS and concurrent feedback, based on the Pilotfish system. Wi-Fi networks have been widely deployed and evolved aggressively. The current control mechanism has significantly hindered the development of next-generation WiFi networks. Efficient solutions resulting from this research will provide a new direction for efficient control mechanism design, which has tremendous technological and social significance. 在无线网络(IEEE 802.11n)中物理层(PHY)数据传输速率可以达到600Mbps。未来的标准，如IEEE802.11ac，预计将提供更高的数据速率（>1Gbps）。但是Wi-Fi协议的效率 随着数据传输速率的增加而急剧下降。据报道，在300Mbps数据速率的网络中只能实现60Mbps的实际吞吐量。 Wi-Fi网络在很大程度上依赖于频谱感知、随机退避这一隐式的控制机制。最近的研究表明，当PHY速率高时，隐式的控制是相当低效的 。另一方面，显式的控制信道能提高频谱效率却带来了明显的开销。一个显式的 控制信道可以被设置在一个单独的频谱或数据信道内。 前者的解决方案是简单的，但是需要额外的频谱。后者将带来对数据信道的干扰。 在这个项目中，我们提出了一种新的方法来提供显式和解耦的控制通道以提升无线网络性能且不会引入任何额外开销。我们基于观察发现，每两个相邻的Wi-Fi信道之间有一个防护频带，如果我们可以利用这些保护频带进行控制消息的传递，我们将能为Wi-Fi网络免费地引入控制通道。 在无线通信中，防护频带的设计是为了防止从相邻信道泄漏的信号造成的显著干扰。因此，为了在防护频带内创建一个控制通道，我们需要确保在该防护频带上进行的传输不会造成对附近的数据信道的附加干扰。此外，附近信道上的数据传输也不应该对防护频带上的控制消息交换造成严重干扰。 在这个项目中，我们将通过下面方法建立防护频带上的控制信道：（1）应用过滤器以抑制控制信道的带外泄露；（2）利用OFDM的正交性，消除从数据信道产生的干扰；（3）通过高传输功率和鲁棒的信道编码提供可靠的物理层。为了验证可行性，我们将在软件无线电平台上实现Pilotfish系统并进行验证。此外，我们将基于Pilotfish系统，提出两个应用程序，控制信道 RTS / CTS和并发反馈。 Wi-Fi网络已经被广泛部署，并积极发展。当前的控制机制明显阻碍了下一代无线网络的发展。从本研究得到的有效解决方案将为设计有效的控制机制提供一个新的方向，它具有巨大的技术和社会意义。

16212714.label: Realisation of objectives
16212714.value: Through this project, we have successfully achieved all the objectives proposed and obtained the results from the following aspects. 1. Design scheme to utilize the guard-band frequencies for communications (for ojectives 1-6) In this project, we utilized guard-bands to create new communication channels that can provide meaningful capacity but do not add burden to the incumbents (i.e., existing systems which occupy the communication spectrum). However, designing a system to realize independent communication is non-trivial because we need to address two important concerns: First, since guard-band is very close to incumbent’s frequency, the guard-band system should suppress its out-of-band emission extremely well, otherwise it could destructively affect incumbents. Second, OFDM based incumbents generate strong out-of-band emission which severely pollutes the guard-bands. Our solutions for these challenges are two-fold. First, we choose Filter Bank Multi-Carrier (FBMC) as our physical layer (PHY) structure, which has been proved much more efficient in suppressing out-of-band emission than both single carrier PHY (e.g. DSSS) and OFDM. Second, we develop the Nulled Decoding technique which nulls incumbents’ OFDM signal while decoding the guard-band transmission, thereby significantly improving the SINR in guard-bands and making decoding possible. We have built a prototype of our design using the Sora software radio system and the experimental results validated the design. 2. Exploring Smart Pilot for Wireless Rate Adaptation (for objectives 3-5) Rate adaptation is an essential component in today’s wireless standards. However, how to estimate the optimal data rate in a fluctuated channel remains of great concern. When experiencing rapid time varying and frequency selective fading channel, the existing proposed metrics can be inaccurate. The reason roots from the fact that there are not enough cost-efficient pilots, which are pre-known symbols inserted in a packet for channel estimation. In this project, we observe that by digging into both PHY layer decoder and upper layer protocol headers, more reliable data bits with high confidence level can be exploited. These data bits, termed smart pilot, can be used to calibrate the channel estimation measurements cost-efficiently. Based on the calibrated estimation, we further propose a novel greedy rate selection algorithm to track the optimal data rate, which successfully avoids the impact of deep fading subcarriers in both legacy 802.11a/g and 802.11n MIMO systems. 3. Less Transmissions, More Throughput: Bringing Carpool to Public WLANs (for objectives 1-3) The performance of Wi-Fi hotspots in crowded environments is extremely poor. The fundamental causes of this problem are high media access control (MAC) overhead and traffic asymmetry. Instead of considering the traffic asymmetry and the MAC overhead separately, we believe these two issues are correlated and should be considered together. We have the observation that if AP can send data for multiple STAs concurrently in a single transmission, the number of contentions will be reduced, and each downlink transmission can convey more traffic. In this project, we develop Carpool, a practical design that enables frame aggregation for multiple receivers at PHY in the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) based WLANs. Carpool employs a lightweight frame structure to aggregate frames for multiple STAs, and a real-time channel estimation (RTE) scheme that continuously calibrates the channel estimation in the decoding process. In particular, a Bloom filter based aggregation header is introduced in the new frame format to indicate the receiver of each sub-frame. The aggregation header is placed right after the preamble so that irrelevant STAs within the transmission range can drop the frame without decoding it. To cope with channel variance and guarantee reliable transmission of Carpool frame, we consider correctly decoded data as known “pilots” and use such data pilots in different positions to capture the channel variance in the transmission. To empower real-time channel estimation in existing OFDM PHY, we create a phase offset side channel to check whether an OFDM symbol is correctly decoded, and use the correctly decoded symbols to capture the channel variance during the transmission. Different from existing dirty coding side channels, the phase offset side channel carries a few free bits per symbol by exploiting the inherent redundancy and phase tracking ability of the OFDM-based PHY, while having no impact on data decoding in IEEE 802.11 standards. 4. Bringing Low Power to Wi-Fi Communications (for objectives 1-4) The high sampling rate in Wi-Fi is set to support bandwidth-hungry applications. It becomes energy inefficient in the post-PC era in which the emerging low-end smart devices increase the disparity in workloads. Recent advances scale down the receiver’s sampling rates by leveraging the redundancy in the physical layer, which, however, requires packet modifications or very high signal-to-noise ratio. To overcome these limitations, we propose Sampleless Wi-Fi, a standard compatible solution that allows energy-constrained devices to scale down their sampling rates regardless of channel conditions. Inspired by rateless codes, Sampleless Wi-Fi recovers under-sampled packets by accumulating redundancy in packet retransmissions. To harvest the diversity gain as rateless codes without modifying legacy packets, Sampleless Wi-Fi creates new constellation diversity by exploiting the time shift effect at receivers. We implement Sampleless Wi-Fi on the GNURadio/USRP platform.

Design free control channel utilizing the guard-band frequencies We utilized guard-bands to create new communication channels that can provide meaningful capacity but do not add burden to the incumbents. We propose independent communication in guard-band whitespace, which creates new communication channels without requiring spectrum resource. We develop the Pilotfish system which employs advanced PHY techniques to address the uncommon challenges in guard-band whitespace. We implement Pilotfish using software radio and verify the Pilotfish design through experiments. Specifically, 1) we prove that Pilotfish transmissions do not interfere with incumbent transmissions. 2) We show Nulled Decoding is able to greatly improve SINR in guard-band and therefore enable the decoding in guard-band whitespace. 2. Core technologies to improve wireless spectrum efficiency 2.1) Rate adaptation is an essential component in today’s wireless standards. When experiencing rapid time varying and frequency selective fading channel, the existing solutions cannot estimate channel accurately enough due to limited cost-efficient pilots. We observe that by digging into both PHY layer decoder and upper layer protocol headers, more reliable data bits with high confidence level can be exploited. We leverage those smart pilots to calibrate the channel estimation measurements and further propose a novel greedy rate selection algorithm to track the optimal data rate. Our experiments on GNU radio testbed show that SmartPilot improve the channel estimation accuracy by 87%. 2.2) The performance of Wi-Fi hotspots in crowded environments is extremely poor. We have the observation that if AP can send data for multiple STAs concurrently in a single transmission, the number of contentions will be reduced. We develop Carpool, a practical design that enables frame aggregation for multiple receivers at PHY in the OFDM-based WLANs. We design a lightweight aggregation mechanism and a real-time channel estimation algorithm to facilitate scalable and reliable transmissions in large audience environments. We implement Carpool on the GNURadio/USRP testbed to demonstrate its feasibility and merits. 3. Improve spectrum efficiency when Wi-Fi needs to support diversified devices The high sampling rate in Wi-Fi causes energy inefficient when facing low-end smart devices. We propose Sampleless Wi-Fi, a standard compatible solution that allows energy-constrained devices to scale down their sampling rates regardless of channel conditions. Sampleless Wi-Fi recovers under-sampled packets by accumulating redundancy in packet retransmissions. We implement Sampleless Wi-Fi on the GNURadio/USRP platform. Evaluation results validate Sampleless Wi-Fi in reliably receiving and decoding legacy packets at sub-Nyquist rates across a wide range of channel conditions.

16212714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212714.value: The directions explored in this project are interesting and not fully investigated ones. Specifically, how to fully explore the potential free channel communication opportunity not only in WiFi networks, but also other wireless networks, how to further improve spectrum efficiency by exploring more joint PHY and MAC related information, etc. are the areas that still need more effort and still have open questions to be investigated.

16212714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212714.value: Spectrum resource for wireless communication has become scarce. Existing communication bands are being overwhelmed with the rapid growth of broadband access needs, which therefore has driven governments to seek for innovative use of spectrum and turn more spectrum from other purposes to wireless communications. In this project, we are working from various aspects to improve the wireless system spectrum efficiency. We developed the Pilotfish system which realizes independent communication and turns guard-band whitespace into new communication channels. To estimate the varying channel condition accurately, we dig into both PHY layer decoder and upper layer protocol headers, and exploit the more reliable data bits with high confidence level as smart pilots to calibrate the channel estimation measurements and further propose a novel greedy rate selection algorithm to track the optimal data rate. We also develop a practical system that enables frame aggregation for multiple receivers at PHY in the OFDM-based WLANs. With such a design, we can allow AP send data for multiple STAs concurrently in a single transmission, which can reduce the number of contentions. In this project, we also explore the technology to improve spectrum efficiency when Wi-Fi needs to support diversified devices.

16212814.label: Project Objectives
16212814.value: We shall fabricate highly effective cathodes based on hierarchical spinel nanostructures with controllable oxygen vacancy concentrations to enhance their electric and ionic conductivity. The fabricated cathode materials will be comprehensively examined by various material characterization equipment and facilities with more attention on porosity, surface stress, deformation, electric conductivity, electrochemical properties, and catalytic activity. We shall construct Li-air batteries with the fabricated cathode materials and test the performance of the constructed batteries. Space charge effects of oxygen vacancies and stress-catalysis coupling behaviors in the non-stoichiometric spinel nanostructures promise a comprehensive study of cathode porosity/size/morphology and Li2O2 interaction effect on cycling-history dependent ORR and OER kinetics in aprotic Li-air batteries.

16212814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212814.value: Due to high specific capacity and being environmentally friendly, rechargeable Li-air batteries, especially with nonaqueous (i.e., proton-free) electrolytes, are receiving increasing interest and worldwide research effort. The energy-converting performance of Li-air batteries is largely determined by electrochemical absorption and release of cathodic active oxygen. The cathodes of aprotic Li-air batteries are designed as highly porous structures with large surface-area-to-volume ratio to enhance the catalysis range and redox reversibility of Li2O2, in terms of cyclic oxygen reduction reactions (ORRs) and oxygen evolution reactions (OERs). As a result, the surfaces/interfaces and cathode deformation are crucial for oxygen/charge transport, electrocatalysis, ORR/OER kinetics, as well as the (rate) capacity and rechargeability of the batteries. Although great progress, particularly in experiments, has been achieved in the research area of Li-air batteries, the role of surface stress/strain and deformation of the cathode in the capacity-limiting mechanism and electrochemical performance of aprotic Li-air batteries has not yet been systematically investigated and thus has become a bottleneck for further development of rechargeable high-capacity Li-air batteries. Based on our rich research experience in thermodynamics/kinetics, atomistic simulations, phase field simulations and electrode materials for Li-based batteries, we propose to comprehensibly investigate the role of surface/interface stress and deformation of the cathodes in aprotic Li-air batteries based on a spinel oxide cathode material system, with emphasis on the ORR/OER kinetics and overpotentials, by conducting experiments, atomistic calculations and phase field simulations, and theoretical studies. We shall fabricate hierarchical tetragonal/cubic spinel CoMn3O4 nanostructures, with sufficiently large surfaces to enlarge the electrochemical reaction area and controllable oxygen vacancies to enhance the catalytic activity, as cathodes, to fabricate a novel type of Li-air battery. We shall conduct first-principle calculations, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and phase field simulations to systematically study at multiple scales the role of surface stress, pre-strain and structural defects in the electrochemical properties of defective spinel cathodes. We shall theoretically study the role of surface/interface stress and deformation of nanostructured spinel oxide cathodes on the ORR and OER kinetics by integrating thermodynamic and kinetic models with the developed surface eigenstress and eigendisplacement models. The experimental investigations, numerical calculations and theoretical studies will interact to and verify each other and thus generate great synergetic effects. Successful completion of the proposed experiments, multiscale simulations and theoretical studies will improve understanding of the capacity-limiting mechanism of rechargeable nonaqueous Li-air batteries, which will have a significant impact on both academic research and engineering practice. 由于其非常高的储能密度和良好的环境兼容性，锂空气电池，尤其是采用非水电解液的锂空电池，正在吸引全世界范围内日益增加的科研力度。锂空电池的能量转化效率很大程度上取决于其正极材料对于电化学活性材料（氧气）的吸附与释放，因而现阶段非水电解液锂空电池的正极材料多采用比表面积大的多孔结构，以便最大程度地提高其对过氧化锂电化学反应的催化性能和可逆性。所以，电池正极材料的变形和界面应力对O2-, O22-和电荷的传输，正极的电化学催化性能及锂空电池的充放电与循环性能都至关重要。尽管锂空电池的研究，尤其是实验方面的工作，已经取得很多突破性进展，但是正极材料的表面/界面应力及其变形对非水电解液锂空电池的储能机理和其电化学性能的影响仍缺乏系统的研究。这也成为锂空电池领域进一步发展的瓶颈问题。 基于我们研究组在锂电池的制备，热力学与动力学，电池材料的第一性原理计算和相场理论模拟的丰富经验，我们提议系统深入研究正极材料的表面/界面应力及其变形对非水电解液锂空电池的储能机理和其电化学性能的影响。我们将采用尖晶石结构氧化物为锂空电池正极材料体系。通过材料制备与表征，第一性原理计算和相场理论模拟，我们将重点研究锂空电池的电化学还原与氧化机理和引发充电/放电过电位的根本原因。为了保证电化学反应界面和电化学催化活性，我们将制备全新的锂空电池正极材料 – 富含氧空位的、多尺度多孔纳米结构的尖晶石氧化物。通过第一性原理计算，分子动力学和相场理论模拟， 我们将在多尺度下系统地研究表面应力，材料预变形和结构缺陷对于尖晶石氧化物正极的电化学活性的影响。通过结合本征应力应变模型和热力学与动力学机理，我们将理论研究纳米尖晶石氧化物正极的界面应力和表面形变对于氧气电化学还原与氧化机理的影响。我们的实验研究，多尺度模拟和理论研究将加深对于非水电解液锂空电池的储能机理的认识，因而对锂空电池的学术研究和工业应用都将有重要影响。

16212814.label: Realisation of objectives
16212814.value: We initially concentrated on studying Objective 1 according to the Revised objective. We were able to reinforce enough manpower from the University internal support in the form of international postgraduate studentship at a later stage of the project, thus allowing us to study Objectives 2 and 3. The Revision to exclude the two Objectives was approved because of the lack of enough funding. Now, all three objectives in this project have been fully achieved according to the original research plans. Significant progress has been made, many original and interesting results have been obtained and a number of high quality papers have been published in prestigious journals. The major outcomes from the project are described in the following. (1) Fabrication of non-stoichiometric spinel CoxMn3-xO4 and investigation on oxygen vacancy effects. (Objective 1) A low temperature approach is applied to fabricate a non-stoichiometric spinel CoxMn3-xO4 (CMO) using strong reducing agent. Controllable oxygen vacancies are developed across the intra/inter-crystalline sites and surfaces of the ultrafine CMOs by thermal treatment at 400 C in Ar (CMO-4). Systematic studies are made of the effect of heating temperature on the generation of oxygen vacancies and the performance of LOBs. Oxygen vacancies were confirmed by various characterization tools. Post electrochemical analysis are applied to monitor the formation/decomposition of Li2O2 and parasitic reaction products (RCOOLi and Li2CO3) during ORR/OER. The results from ex situ analysis reveal enhanced ability of CMO-4 in decomposition of Li2O2 than the pristine CMO due to the lower charge transfer resistance of CMO-4. (2) Fabrication of inverse spinel NiFeOx nanofiber oxygen catalysts and the effect of cathode-Li2-xO2 interaction on electrochemical performance of aprotic Li-air batteries. (Objective 1) The influence of Li2O2 morphology and its nucleation mechanism on LOB performance are probed by experiments and the first-principle calculations. One-dimensional porous spinel NiFeOx nanofibers (NFs) prepared via electrospinning followed by calcination are applied as catalyst in oxygen electrode. The electrochemical performance is significantly improved in terms of the specific capacity, cycle numbers and overpotentials due to the formation of film-liked Li2O2 assisted by NiFeOx NFs. Heterogeneous nucleation and growth model of Li2O2/Li2-xO2 justify the morphological transformation from nanoparticles to layers. The large surface area and vacancy rich NiFeOx NFs facilitate mass/ion transport and oxygen catalytic activities. (3) In-situ encapsulated Co-Ni in graphitic carbon nanofibers (CNFs) and the encapsulation effects on electrochemical performance of aprotic Li-air batteries. (Objective 1) The agglomeration of catalysts particles during interaction with reaction products may result in the breakage/deformation of oxygen electrode. A binder-free hierarchically porous CNFs with in-situ encapsulated Co-Ni catalysts (Co-Ni/CNF) are synthesized via electrospinning. The uniformly distributed Co-Ni nanoparticles prevent the catalyst agglomeration after cycles. The inherently interconnected, graphitic network facilitate ion and electron transport in oxygen electrode. The Co-Ni/CNF electrode delivers high specific capacity of 8635 mAh g-1 at 200 mA g-1, and sustains 60 cycles at upper limit capacity of 1000 mAh g-1. (4) Mesoporous MnCo2S4 nanosheets (NSs) surrounding macrospores and the effect of porosity on mass transport and discharge storage during ORR/OER in LOBs. (Objective 1) Mesoporous MnCo2S4 (MCS) NSs are grown on carbon paper (MCS/CP) via electrodeposition and vulcanization. The structure, morphology and electrochemical performance of MCS/CP as the oxygen electrode in LOBs are studied and compared with those of MnCo2O4 NSs on CP (MCO/CP). The LOB cell made of mesoporous MCS NSs catalyst shows exceptionally high initial capacity of 10760 mAh g-1 and sustains 96 cycles at 500 mAh g-1, much higher than the mesopores-free MnCo2O4 (MCO) counterpart. This arise from the efficient bifunctional catalytic activities with ameliorated ORR and OER kinetics of the MCS catalyst. (5) Porous RuO2 nanosheet/CNT hybrid electrode combined with DMSO-based electrolyte for Li-O2 and Li ion O2 batteries. (Objective 2) Holey 2D RuO2 NSs fabricated by graphene template are assembled with CNT interlayers to enhance mass/electron transport through a conductive and porous structure. The 2D-1D RuO2/CNT hybrid oxygen electrode presents an exceptional LOB performance. The first principle calculations are combined with microscopic images to reveal the growth mechanism of Li2O2. The RuO2/CNT electrode is paired with Si/C anode and LiO2-soluble dimethyl sulfoxide-based electrolyte to operate lithium ion oxygen battery (LIOB). The LIOB delivers ultrahigh gravimetric energy and power density of 1897 Wh Kg-1 and 1396 W Kg-1, respectively. (6) 2D and metallic MoS2 NSs electrocatalyst developed for multifunctional purposes: ORR, OER and LOBs. (Objective 2) Transition metal oxides have very limited conductivities necessitating incorporation of a conductive medium. Development of highly conductive, low cost and catalytically active materials is one of the major challenges in the field of electrochemistry. 2D metallic MoS2 (1T-MoS2) NSs are synthesized as highly active electrocatalyst for LOB. 2D 1T-MoS2 NSs prepared from in situ-redox intercalation and exfoliation technique are interleaved with CNTs to make a 1T-MoS2/CNT electrode. The 1T-MoS2/CNT sustains over 100 cycles at 500 mAh g-1 owing to the catalytically active surface of 1T-MoS2 accessible by Li+ ions and O2. Density functional theory calculations and rotational ring disk results reveal catalytically active basal planes in 1T-MoS2, while only edges of the semiconducting form of 2H-MoS2 are active. (7) Synthesis of holey graphene monolith and the effect of porosity on electrochemical performance of aprotic Li-air batteries. (Objective 3) Highly porous graphene monoliths (HPGMs) were synthesized using a hard template method combined with hydrothermal self-assembly and evaporation-induced drying technique. A high density, 1.58 g cm−3, a large surface area, 689 m2 g-1, and a large pore volume, 0.59 cm3 g-1, allow the HPGM electrode to deliver a remarkable volumetric density of 485 mAh cm−3 and corresponding volumetric energy density of 1109 Wh L-1 for 157 cycles. Efficient pore size distribution in the holey structure HPGM provides sufficient Li+ ion and oxygen diffusion channels, while defective edges in individual graphene NSs enhanced the catalytic activities. Assembly of a lithium ion oxygen battery using Li2O2 cathode and lithiated aluminum anode with nafion membrane for reduced O2 crossover LIOB is fabricated from a lithiated aluminum (Al) anode, a Li2O2-preloaded carbon cathode and Nafion membrane. The LIOB presents an excellent energy density and cyclic stability. In view of abundance and availability of the cathode and anode materials, the assembly strategy developed here can offer a promising route to large-scale fabrication of LIOBs for real-world applications.

16212814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212814.value: Objective 1: The large surface area, oxygen-deficient CoMn2O4-x presents enhanced performance in LOB than CoMn2O4. While CoMn2O4 reveals an excellent ORR catalytic activity, the oxygen vacancies mitigate O2¬ and Li+ mobility, facile O-O dissociation, Li2O2 nucleation and growth while acting as active sites to bind O2 upon OER (J01). Vacancy rich NiFeOx catalyst reduced Li2O2 crystallite size, generated Li vacancies in Li2O2 (Li2-xO2) and enlarged the electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Therefore, fast charge transport and lower oxidation barrier gave rise to enhanced LOB performance (J02). Hierarchically CNFs with in-situ encapsulated Co-Ni catalysts show reversible formation/removal of Li2O2. The Co-Ni nanoparticles catalytically decompose the Li2O2 layer formed on CNF surface (J03). Micron-size voids surrounded by mesoporous 2D MnCo2S4 (MCS) NSs accommodate Li2O2 and mitigate the strain from deposition of reaction products. The low binding energy of LiO2 on MCS prevents the formation of Li2O2 films, lowering the OER overpotential (J04). Objective 2: First-principle calculations revealed facile O2 reduction and enhanced solvation of intermediate phases at CNT/electrolyte interfaces assisted by deficient NiFeOx NF catalyst, thus promoting Li2O2 film formation. Li2O2 films did not necessarily correlate with lower capacity compared to Li2O2 particles (J02). Micron-size voids surrounded by mesoporous 2D MCS NSs accommodated Li2O2 and mitigated the strain from deposition of reaction products. The DFT calculations reveal a lower adsorption energy for LiO2 on MCS than MCO, which is responsible for the lower OER overpotential and the higher catalytic ability of MCS/CP. (J04). 2D trigonal phase MoS2 (1T-MoS2) nanosheets are fabricated as the highly active electrocatalyst for LOBs. The density functional theory calculations identify the catalytically active basal planes in 1T-MoS2 during ORR and the initial ORR path during LOB cycles, agreeing with the results from rotational ring disk electrode. (J08). Objective 3: Study of the Li2O2 growth mechanism in the holey 2D RuO2 NSs and CNT hybrid present a strong interaction between Li2O2 and RuO2. The state hybridization transforms the inherently insulating Li2O2 and reduces overpotentials (J05). Bimodal pores of diameter ranging 1-6 and 40 nm created in porous graphene facilitate ion transport, oxygen diffusion and provide sufficient space to accommodate Li2O2. The high-density porous graphene lead to exceptional volumetric/energy density and stable ORR/OER (J06). LIOB fabricated with Li2O2-preloaded cathode and pre-lithiated Al anode survives over 100 cycles at 1000 mAhg-1 and delivers an energy density of 1178 Wh.kg−1. The decomposition/reproduction of preloaded Li2O2 alleviate the volume change of cathode during cyclic. (J07).

16212814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212814.value: In addition to LOBs and LIOBs studied in this project, the use of developed electrocatalysts can be extended to other energy storage devices, such as lithium ion batteries, sodium ion batteries, sodium oxygen batteries and lithium sulfur batteries. The catalytically active metal oxides and sulfides with large surface areas can be hybridized with nanocarbon materials like CNTs or graphene to use as anodes in high performance SIBs. In addition, 2D metal dichalcogenide (such as MoS2, Sb2S3) are considered promising candidates as anodes for SIBs. In summary, metal sulfides with good mechanical durability, excellent electrical conductivities and tunable surface areas and porosities have great potential for accelerated development of other emerging energy storage systems alternative to the first-generation LIBs.

16212814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212814.value: Environmental crisis due to CO2 emission and the shortage of fossil fuel require rapid utilization of clean energy resources. Development of high energy density storage systems are necessary to store the intermittent renewable energies and to transfer them through the grids to final users either in households and electronics or in transportation system. Because the state-of-the-art LIBs are reaching their limit of applicable capacities, developing high energy density systems such as LOBs, LSBs and other metal batteries is increasingly more important. Although LOBs has a potential to deliver an exceptionally high energy density, its shortcomings such as low cyclic life needs to be addressed. In this project, we successfully synthesized many effective ORR/OER bifunctional electrocatalysts. The influences of vacancies in catalysts and discharge products, i.e. Li2O2, morphologies and porosities on electrochemical properties were specifically studied. Significant improvements in electrochemical performance have been achieved for rechargeable LOBs, through rational design and synthesis of both oxygen electrode and the cell assembly. The fundamental understanding are achieved using systematic experimental approach combined with theoretical analysis. In light of these new findings, further research can be extended to develop commercially viable full cell Li-air batteries in the future.

16213014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213014.value: Disinfection of drinking water has been one of the most important achievements in public health in the past century. Chlorine is the most widely used disinfectant in drinking water disinfection. Chlorine successfully eliminates pathogens, but it may react with natural organic matter and bromide in source water to generate unintended halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs). About 600 halogenated DBPs have been identified in drinking waters. Trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs) are the two most dominant groups of halogenated DBPs in chlorine-disinfected waters. Human consumption of chlorinated drinking water containing halogenated DBPs is somewhat connected to increased spontaneous abortions, stillbirth, birth defects, bladder cancer, and colorectal cancer. A few halogenated DBPs have been regulated in the Disinfectants/DBPs Rule by the U.S. EPA, which sets the maximum levels for the sum of four THMs and five HAAs at 80 and 60 microgram/liter, respectively. Strategies for controlling halogenated DBPs in chlorinated drinking waters generally include source control, precursor removal, and alternative disinfectants. Even with these strategies, many halogenated DBPs including THMs and HAAs are still present at significant levels in drinking water. Most recently, the PI’s group has found that many aromatic halogenated DBPs are formed during chlorination, and they act as intermediate DBPs to decompose and form commonly known DBPs including THMs and HAAs. In this project the PI proposes to remove intermediate aromatic halogenated DBPs during chlorination by granular activated carbon (a relatively cheap adsorbent) adsorption, which is a new approach to controlling regulated THMs and HAAs in drinking water. 在過去的一個世紀里，飲用水消毒是公共衛生領域最重要的成就之一。在飲用水消毒工藝中，氯是最為常用的消毒劑。氯消毒雖然能抑制水中大部分病原體，但投加的氯同時也能與水中的天然有機物和溴離子反應生成鹵代消毒副產物。在氯消毒的飲用水中，三鹵甲烷和鹵乙酸是最常見的鹵代消毒副產物。迄今飲用水中已鑒定的鹵代消毒副產物大約有600種。流行病學研究表明人類飲用氯消毒的飲用水與增加的自然流產、死胎、新生兒先天缺陷、膀胱癌和腸癌等有某種程度的相關性。在美國國家環保局制定的消毒劑/消毒副產物法規中，一些鹵代消毒副產物已被列入規範，例如四種三鹵甲烷的總量不得超過80微克/升；五種鹵代乙酸的總量不得超過60微克/升。 控制鹵代消毒副產物的措施主要包括控制水源水質、去除消毒副產物前體物和使用替代消毒劑。即使採用這些措施，包括三鹵甲烷、鹵乙酸在內的許多鹵代消毒副產物在飲用水中仍然大量存在。最近本課題組在氯消毒的飲用水中發現了很多鹵代芳香類有機物。這些物質被視為中間體消毒副產物，它們可進一步分解轉化為常見的三鹵甲烷、鹵乙酸類消毒副產物。因此，本項目旨在將顆粒活性炭（一種相對便宜的吸附劑）應用於在氯消毒過程中，吸附並去除這些中間體鹵代芳香類消毒副產物從而達到控制三鹵甲烷和鹵乙酸的目的。這為控制飲用水中三鹵甲烷和鹵乙酸提供了一種新途徑。

16213014.label: Realisation of objectives
16213014.value: (1) A new granular activated carbon (GAC) treatment approach has been developed to effectively control the formation of the regulated disinfection byproducts (DBPs), trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs), in chlorinated drinking water by targeting the intermediate aromatic halogenated DBPs. As intermediate aromatic halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs) have been reported to form and decompose during chlorination, and they reached their maximum levels mainly at chlorine contact times around 0.5 to 3 h, their removal by GAC adsorption should be conducted after the chlorine disinfection process in the drinking water treatment train. To simulate the new approach (i.e., GAC adsorption “after chlorination”, Cl2→GAC), a 0.5 h-chlorinated simulated source water sample was delivered to a lab-scale micro-column GAC filtration system. The DBP levels in the samples before and after the GAC adsorption were characterized by a sensitive precursor ion scan (PIS) method using ultra performance liquid chromatography/electrospray ionization-triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UPLC/ESI-tqMS). By setting PIS of 79/81 and 35/37 in the ESI negative mode, various brominated and chlorinated DBPs (including intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs) were detected. By comparing the intensity of each DBP in the PIS spectra of the chlorinated samples before and after GAC adsorption, we found that GAC adsorption could effectively remove various intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs. Besides, the levels of overall halogenated DBPs in the samples before and after GAC adsorption were quantified by total organic halogen (TOX) analysis, and a significant TOX removal was observed. Accordingly, the DBP control with the new approach was demonstrated to be feasible in the lab-scale test. (2) As GAC adsorption has been traditionally used to remove natural organic matter (NOM), the precursor of halogenated DBPs, in drinking water treatment plants. To verify whether GAC adsorption can be applied for removing halogenated DBPs “after chlorination” (i.e., the new approach) instead of removing NOM “prior to chlorination” (i.e., the traditional approach), we evaluated the control of DBPs with the new and traditional approaches using two types of lab-scale column tests. First, a commercially available lab-scale micro-column system (as mentioned in (1)) was used to simulate the GAC adsorption in both approaches. For the new approach, a simulated source water sample was dosed with chlorine, and after a 0.5 h-contact time, the disinfected water sample was subjected to the GAC micro-column adsorption (i.e., Cl2→GAC). For the traditional approach, the simulated source water sample was treated by the GAC micro-column adsorption and the effluent samples were chlorinated for 0.5 h (i.e., GAC→Cl2). A control sample was prepared by chlorinating the simulated source water sample with no GAC adsorption (i.e., Cl2 only). To evaluate the DBP formation in the sample with each approach, the sample was pretreated and subjected to UPLC/ESI-tqMS and TOX analyses. Second, a rapid small-scale column test (RSSCT) system was established to predict the treatment of halogenated DBPs with a pilot-scale GAC filter. The simulated source water was treated by the traditional and new approaches using the RSSCTs. Effluent samples with both approaches were collected and analyzed for the DBP concentrations (including the levels of intermediate aromatic DBPs, THMs, HAAs, and TOX). Additionally, via an in vivo bioassay with the embryos of a high-salinity-tolerance marine polychaete, we studied the comparative developmental toxicity of the DBP mixtures in the effluent samples with both approaches. The results indicated that GAC adsorption “after chlorination” (i.e., for intermediate DBP removal) was more effective in removing halogenated DBPs than GAC adsorption “prior to chlorination” (i.e., for NOM removal). (3) The factors that affect the control of halogenated DBPs with the new approach were further studied to optimize the DBP removal. The same source waters were also treated with the traditional approach and with chlorination only for comparison. The effects of the initial bromide level (i.e., the bromide level in source water, ranging from 0 to 2 mg/L) and the chlorine contact time (ranging from 0.5 to 3.0 h) on the DBP control with the new approach were systematically investigated using the lab-scale GAC micro-column test. The DBP removal with each approach for each factor was indicated by the TOX removal. Substantially higher TOX removals were found in various treatment scenarios with the new approach than those with the traditional approach, which verified the effectiveness of DBP control with the new approach. Moreover, an optimized DBP control scenario with the new approach for a specific source water was recommended.

16213014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213014.value: (1) Various intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs were detected in the chlorinated water samples and their levels were significantly decreased after the GAC adsorption using a lab-scale micro-column test, which corroborated the effectiveness of the new approach for controlling halogenated DBPs. (2) The practical application of the new approach was further validated using RSSCTs, which can well-predict the performance of a pilot-scale and even full-scale GAC filter in water treatment plants. By analyzing the RSSCT effluent samples with both approaches, significant higher removals of various halogenated aromatic DBPs were observed in the effluents with the new approach than those with the traditional approach; the removals of THMs, HAAs, and TOX with the new approach always exceeded those with the traditional approach; and the effluents with the new approach were considerably less developmentally toxic than those with the traditional approach. Besides, 1-d subsequent chlorination was also conducted for the effluent samples with both approaches to investigate the DBP formation in the distribution system. The DBP levels (including THMs, HAAs, and TOX) and overall toxicity in the simulated tap waters with the new approach were considerably lower than those with the traditional approach. The findings indicated that the new approach was substantially more effective in controlling halogenated DBPs than the traditional approach in drinking water chlorination. (3) The effects of the initial bromide level and contact time on the DBP control with the new approach were investigated. With increasing the initial bromide level from 0 to 2 mg/L, the TOX removal with the new approach increased from 52% to 74%, while the removal with the traditional approach increased from 18% to 37%. Besides, as the chlorine contact time increased from 0.5 to 3.0 h, the TOX removal with the new approach increased from 61% to 75%, while the removal with the traditional approach increased from 21% to 36%. Increasing the bromide level and chlorine contact time enhanced the halogenated DBP removal with both new and traditional approaches, but the removal with the new approach was always two times higher or more than that with the traditional approach, which justified the superiority of the new approach. The results have been published in top environmental journals including Environmental Science & Technology, Science Bulletin, and Separation and Purification Technology. The results have also been presented in prestigious international conferences.

16213014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213014.value: (1) For different source waters and chlorine contact times, the effective removal of intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs by GAC adsorption (i.e., the new approach) was a promising DBP control strategy. Since the effectiveness of GAC adsorption might be affected by the physical-chemical characteristics of GAC particles and the operational conditions of the GAC filter, the PI would propose to further investigate and optimize the DBP removal with the new approach by varying the GAC structure and operational condition. (2) The new approach significantly removed halogenated DBPs including intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs. Since there are numerous unidentified intermediate halogenated DBPs and they might be potentially toxic, the PI would propose to further investigate other intermediate DBPs that might be responsible for the enhanced TOX removal and the significant toxicity reduction with the new approach. (3) To further validate the performance of the new approach for the effective DBP control in drinking water treatment, the PI would also propose to scale-up and establish a pilot-scale treatment system with the new approach in a typical drinking water treatment plant. If possible, this new approach may be extended for further application for the DBP control in wastewater or reclaimed water treatment.

16213014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213014.value: Chlorine is widely used in drinking water disinfection. It may react with natural organic matter (NOM) and bromide in source water to produce undesired halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs), which are associated with adverse health effects. Some DBPs have been regulated in the U.S. and other countries. One strategy for controlling halogenated DBPs is to remove NOM (DBP precursor). Granular activated carbon (GAC) adsorption has been commonly used for NOM removal, but it may not be very effective due to size exclusion effects. Recently, the PI has found that many halogenated aromatic DBPs are formed during chlorination, and they act as intermediate DBPs to decompose and form aliphatic DBPs. In this project, the PI developed a new approach (i.e., chlorine disinfection – GAC adsorption) to effectively control halogenated DBPs by removing intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs via GAC adsorption. Compared with the traditional approach (i.e., GAC adsorption – chlorine disinfection), the new approach was demonstrated to be substantially more effective in removing halogenated DBPs and reducing the toxicity of the disinfected water than the traditional approach. For different source waters and chlorine contact times, the DBP removal with the new approach was always two times higher or more than that with the traditional approach.
