16213414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213414.value: 本項目旨在探究鋰空氣電池多孔電極中質量、離子及電子的協同傳輸機理。由於鋰空氣電池的理論容量是鋰離子電池的十倍以上，已成為最具前景的電動汽車電源。但目前，鋰空氣電池的實際容量只有理論容量的30％。為此，我們的研究將集中在如何提高電池的實際容量，甚至達到其理論值。提高電池的實際容量不僅需要改善材料的電化學特性，而且還需要協同提升氧氣、鋰離子及電子在多孔電極中的傳輸速率。我們的初步研究表明：對於給定材料的多孔電極，隨著放電容量的增加，沉積在電極孔隙中的顆粒狀或薄膜狀固體產物將會造成三相介面的破壞，最終導致電池放電結束。這是鋰空氣電池實際容量未能達到理論值的重要原因。為了實現電池實際容量的最大化，我們需要在三相介面不被破壞的情況下，協同提升氧氣、鋰離子及電子的傳輸極限。解決這一問題的關鍵在於對鋰空氣電池多孔電極中質量、離子及和電子的協同傳輸機理的認識。然而，鋰空氣電池的充放電過程會伴隨著電極孔隙中固體產物的分解和沉積，與燃料電池中氣相、液相或氣液兩相的傳輸現象相比，鋰空氣電池多孔電極中的傳輸現象更複雜。另外，鋰空氣電池中引入了氧氣、鋰離子、電子及固體產物，與只引入鋰離子及電子的鋰離子電池相比，鋰空氣電池多孔電極中的傳輸現象也更複雜。以上這些複雜的傳輸現象都會給本專案的研究帶來一定的挑戰。 本項目將通過以下幾個方面來探究鋰空氣電池多孔電極中質量、離子及電子的協同傳輸機理：i）通過先進的實驗手段測得固體產物的電導率並擬合出固體產物電導率與其特徵尺寸的關係式；ii）製備有序的多孔電極，以保證三相介面不被沉積的固體產物破壞；iii）建立電極孔隙中質量、離子及電子傳輸的微觀模型，並獲得孔結構的優化設計參數；iv）建立多孔電極中質量、離子及電子傳輸的宏觀模型，並獲得多孔電極的優化設計參數。 本專案的成果將革命性地提高鋰空氣電池的實際容量並大力推動鋰空氣電池及其電動汽車的發展。

16213414.label: Realisation of objectives
16213414.value: During the undertaking of this project, we have achieved much more than what was listed in the objectives. We have developed a unique gradient electrode combining carbon black powders with the high surface area and carbon nanotubes with high permeability for air cathode. This electrode design optimizes the fraction of carbon nanotube and carbon black in the cathode to reach the best cycling performance. Moreover, by optimizing the fabrication method, we fabricated a new cathode with the screen-printing method, which formed large pores for oxygen transport, unlike the high transport resistance with the slurry-casting method. Combining experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculation, we found the deposition morphology of discharge products was highly related with the oxygen pressure and discharge capacity under the same current density. With the increase of the oxygen pressure, the morphology transformed from the partial toroid-shaped morphology to the disc-shaped morphology with split layers. Moreover, from the computational simulation, we found there was a large amount of Li2O residuals under the high pressure, which led to the formation of disc-shaped particles. Due to the large surface area, the charging overpotential with the disc-shaped morphology was much lower compared with the alternatives under low pressure. Based on the morphology characterization, one-dimensional mathematical continuum model was developed by treating the discharge product as a discontinuous deposit layer. With this model, we combined the electrochemical reactions and mass transport in the non-aqueous lithium-air batteries and depicted the deposition process during the discharge. Compared with the previous solid deposit-layer model, our porous deposit-layer model was better coincidental with the experimental results. In addition, to achieve the operation under ambient atmosphere, efficient catalysts (RuO2/NiO) were developed for catalyzing the side reaction products during the cycling, which enabled long cycling performance under ambient environment. In addition to the non-aqueous lithium-air batteries, we also developed high-performance solid lithium-air batteries with the assembly of the porous cathode and dense separator. With this unique structure, we achieved a much larger triple-phase boundary for electrochemical reactions and active materials transportation comparing with the traditional solid-state lithium-air batteries. Meanwhile, we combined this assembly with selective silicon oil and achieved the long cycling with ambient air. Based on the understandings of the foregoing tasks, we optimized the non-aqueous and solid lithium-air batteries with better mass transport and highly effective catalysts. Additionally, we gained a better understanding of the whole system through continuum modeling and density functional theory simulation from bottom to upper.

16213414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213414.value: With the support of the present RGC grant, we have made significant contributions to the development of non-aqueous lithium-air batteries and solid-state lithium-air batteries. The results obtained in this project have been presented in 20 top-rated journal papers, as listed in Sections 8. The major findings are summarized as follows: We have optimized the fraction of carbon nanotube and carbon black in the gradient cathode to ensure the mass transport and electrochemical reactions. We have developed a new screen-printing method to fabricate cathode, which decreased the transport resistance of oxygen. We have investigated the deposition morphology under different oxygen pressures and capacities, and we found the formed disk-like particles were easy to be decomposed with small overpotential. With the experimental investigation of the deposition morphology, we have developed a mathematical model to describe the effect of porous deposit-layer on the discharge process. We have developed an advanced structure for solid-state lithium-air batteries with much larger triple-phase boundaries for oxygen transport and low ionic resistance, which were able to cycle under the ambient environment. We have developed an efficient nano-structured catalyst for non-aqueous lithium-air batteries for stable cycling with the ambient atmosphere.

16213414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213414.value: The present project has primarily focused on the development of efficient cathode for mass transport and electrochemical reactions in the lithium-air batteries, with which the oxygen transport in the lithium-air batteries was experimentally and numerically studied. The outcome of this project have deepened our fundamental understanding of the oxygen transport and electrochemical reactions in the non-aqueous lithium-air batteries and solid-state lithium-air batteries and provided the needed information for the design of the effective cathode for practical applications.

16213414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213414.value: With the increasing applications of electric vehicles, high energy density and lightweight rechargeable batteries are greatly in need. Current battery technologies, like lithium-ion batteries, are limited by their low energy densities. However, lithium-air batteries with lightest lithium metal as an anode and the unlimited air as a cathode are promising for future application. In this project, we have optimized the cathode structure for oxygen transportation in the non-aqueous lithium-air batteries from experiments and simulations. Moreover, combining ex-situ characterizations and computational simulations, we gained a better understanding of the discharge process. Based on those characterizations, we developed several cathode structures loaded with efficient catalysts, which were able to enhance the decomposition of the side products during charging process under the ambient atmosphere. Those catalysts made it possible to operate with air. In addition to the non-aqueous lithium-air batteries, we also optimized the ion transport and oxygen transfer in the solid lithium-air batteries. We developed a solid assembly electrolyte with the integration of cathode and separator, which decreased the lithium ion transport length and achieved the stable cycling under ambient environment. The lithium-air batteries with the developed cathode and separator in this project have shown promising applications in the electric vehicles.

16300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300014.value: Diminishing energy resources and the cumulative impact of their consumption on the environment are key concerns of our society. Fundamental scientific breakthroughs that underscore advances in the efficiency and selectivity of catalytic reactions will play an important role in realizing real-world solutions in these areas. It has been shown that Au nanoparticles dispersed on Fe2O3 (hematite) can be the most effective catalyst for CO oxidation at low temperature. This has important applications in purification of hydrogen-rich reformer gas in fuel cells and catalyzing the water-gas shift reaction for producing hydrogen. Investigations using surface-sensitive techniques under ultrahigh-vacuum conditions can provide important insight about the fundamental physics and chemistry of stepped single-crystal surfaces and model industrial catalysts, which usually consist of small facetted particles exhibiting a high density of atomic step defect sites. Recent advances have been made that bridge the critical pressure gap between these fundamental studies and realistic processes that occur close to atmospheric pressure. This work revealed evidence of dynamic catalytic particle shape changes under realistic reaction conditions that must be taken into account in our understanding of catalytic processes. In the proposed research, we will study Au nanoparticle shape dynamics on Fe2O3. We will take a meticulous surface science approach to preparation of pure epitaxial Fe2O3 films on a Pt(111) surface. As an alternative to the method for preparing Fe2O3 by stepwise oxidation of Fe films at very high molecular oxygen pressure, we will attempt to grow Fe2O3 continuously by Fe/O codeposition using atomic oxygen at low pressure. Film growth, crystal/defect structure and morphology will be studied using real-time low energy electron microscopy imaging and spatially-resolving micro-low energy electron diffraction capabilities. Growth of thin oxide films on metal substrates avoids impurities that can influence surface catalytic phenomena, and mitigates charging effects that could arise using powerful electron-based techniques. Development of a new low-pressure approach to film growth would open the door to wider in-situ surface science studies by other techniques. We will grow self-organized Au nanoparticles on Fe2O3 and search for evidence of dynamic nanoparticle shape changes under gas exposure in the high vacuum range using diffraction spot-profile-analysis and facet-diffraction analysis techniques. Extension of this work to the study of nanoparticle shapes following CO oxidation reaction near atmospheric pressure in a high-pressure reaction chamber will help to bridge the pressure gap in our understanding of dynamic shape effects and their role in catalysis by Au. .

16300014.label: Realisation of objectives
16300014.value: We carried out extensive experimental investigations and developed several significant new experimental methods in order to achieve project objectives. Different approaches were taken to prepare iron oxide films with different oxidation states on the Pt(111) surface for use as model systems in studies of Au nanoparticle catalysis and other applications. This work focused on the use of atomic oxygen to oxidize iron as an alternative to molecular oxygen that is commonly used as oxidizing species. An atomic oxygen flux was generated in our work by thermal dissociation of O2 molecules in a thermal cracker, which we implemented in these investigations of iron oxide for the first time. The anticipated advantage of atomic oxidation was that it would be able to facilitate the preparation of oxides with high oxidation state, particularly hematite (Fe2O3), at considerably lower pressure than required for oxidation by molecular oxygen. A comparative study of iron oxide monolayer and thicker film growth was made using molecular and atomic oxygen as oxidizing species. Differences between oxides formed using atomic and molecular oxygen for otherwise identical growth procedures identified the impact of atomic oxidation definitively. We experimented with concurrent Fe deposition/oxidation and post-deposition oxidation procedures and determined that the latter was more effective at forming oxide films. Therefore, our detailed subsequent work focused exclusively on the latter. The growth, morphology, geometric and defect structure of iron oxides on Pt(111) were characterized with high spatial resolution using complementary low energy electron microscopy (LEEM) and selected-area micro-low energy electron diffraction (micro-LEED). The development of the scanning micro-LEED method provided access to detailed structural information that was critical to our understanding of the experimental results. In scanning micro-LEED measurements, the position of a very small illuminating beam (250nm) was scanned across the surface in a two-dimensional array using beam deflectors. Structural information was determined quantitatively by evaluating peak positions in each of these highly spatially-resolved patterns. The peak positions were determined precisely using spot profile analysis peak-fitting methods. A challenge to the implementation of scanning micro-LEED is that it entails the analysis of a large number of micro-LEED peaks, on the order of 20,000. We addressed this challenge by developing the Source Extraction and Photometry (SEP)–Spot Profile Analysis (SPA) tool. The implementation of the SEP-SPA package in a Python-based multi-core, multi-threading programming architecture is able to automate diffraction peak identification and perform analysis with high throughput. Investigations of Au nanoparticles on hematite were carried out using thin hematite films with bi-phase surface termination that was grown on Pt(111) using atomic oxidation by methods developed in this project. Au nanoparticle growth was performed by depositing Au onto hematite at room temperature. The hematite bi-phase termination was chosen because it has a periodically modulated surface structure with ~40Å repeat distance in a triangular superlattice arrangement. This super-structural feature of the bi-phase surface serves as a template for the growth of Au nanoparticles with the same periodic arrangement and presumably also with identical nanocrystalline orientations. The assembly of such an ensemble of identical oriented nanoparticles was expected to align weak diffraction features from individual particles. This would be advantageous for detecting evidence of Au nanocrystalline structure and surface facet morphologies in diffraction measurements that average signal from many nanoparticles in our investigations. Despite using this optimized approach, we could not detect any diffraction signal that could be linked to nanoparticle shapes. This shortcoming was attributed to possible smearing of diffraction signal due to variations of nanoparticle shapes in an imperfect ensemble. In order to overcome this problem, we attempted to diminish signal smearing by modifying our approach in two ways, (1) reducing the electron beam probe size to the smallest possible, 250 nm, in order to average over fewer nanoparticles, (2) attempting to improve nanoparticle ordering and uniformity by annealing the sample to different temperatures. We also varied diffraction conditions by changing the incident electron energy and by adjusting the incidence angle in order to search for the elusive signal. However, these none of approaches revealed any signal that could be linked to nanoparticle shape. We now speculate that diffraction peaks produced by nanoparticle facets are intrinsically broadened due to the small facet sizes, in particular, in inverse proportion to the real-space facet dimensions. Possible approaches to discriminate this weak signal are given in section 6.2. We also participated in the development of a high pressure cell (HPC) during this project, with the aim of bridging the pressure gap between ultra-high vacuum (UHV) surface science experiments and catalysis under realistic reaction conditions close to atmospheric pressure. The attachment of the HPC to the SPELEEM instrument at the Elettra synchrotron radiation facility in Trieste, Italy facilitated UHV spectroscopic imaging experiments following near-ambient catalytic studies in the HPC. This work was done in collaboration with Prof. Ernst Bauer (EB) and Dr. Anastassia Pavlovska (AP) of Arizona State University and Dr. Andrea Locatelli (AL) at Elettra. Scientific visits by the PI Prof. Michael Altman (MA), HKUST post-doctoral associate Dr. Qiang Wu (QW), Prof. Bauer and Dr. Pavlovska were made to Elettra that were dedicated to the development and implementation the HPC in proposed experiments. The accumulated period of visits that were fully or partially funded by the project was 164 person/days [2015: QW (28 days), EB(28 days), AP (28 days); 2016: MA(11 days), EB (15 days), AP (15 days); 2017: MA (7 days), EB (16 days), AP (16 days)]. MA, EB, AP and AL also spent considerable time performing ancillary work on the HPC development outside the visit periods. The HPC adapted the “temporal analysis of products” (TAP) method used in the study of particle catalysts at near-ambient pressure to the study of model single crystal surfaces. We addressed several challenges to achieve this milestone, including (1) identification of non-reactive capillary material and optimizing introduction of gases via the capillary exclusively to the sample surface, (2) reliability of pulse valve and controller used to produce a temporal structure of gas exposure, (3) problems with differential pumping of the mass spectrometer used to measure reaction products, (4) problems with sample temperature measurement due to double thermocouple junction, (5) water contamination due to insufficient baking of the HPC chamber and unbakeable valves, (6) introduction of controlled gas mixtures with well-defined compositions and pressure. In light of difficulties to observe diffraction signal from Au nanoparticles described above, our work using the HPC focused on understanding the origins of low temperature catalysis by Au nanoparticles on hematite at low temperature that motivated this proposal initially. However, it was difficult in the end to prove that the observed reactions were not taking place at the sample heating filament, hot sample holder parts, or at regions of the Pt sample substrate that were not covered with hematite. Although a paper was prepared that described our results, submission of the paper for publication was withheld because of these uncertainties. This exposed the current limitations of the UHV-compatible TAP approach that was developed in this work.

16300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300014.value: In this project, we demonstrated that iron oxide thin film growth on Pt(111) using atomic oxygen can produce oxides with different oxidation states and in a variety of previously unknown structural polymorphs [C8:2,3; C9:2-7,9]. The FeO monolayer formed using atomic oxygen is laterally expanded and rotated compared to the monolayer produced by molecular oxidation and it exhibits significantly higher crystalline quality. These structural differences are attributed to mild interfacial alloying during molecular oxidation that is suppressed during atomic oxidation. Atomic oxidation also drives the formation of a new oxygen-enriched layer with higher order coincidence (HOC) lattice structure. Notably, this new oxide can oxidize CO at elevated temperature, which makes it a potentially interesting catalyst. The formation of hematite (Fe2O3) was also achieved using an alternative approach at low pressure. This high oxidation state was produced by thermally inducing a transformation of magnetite (Fe3O4) following its supersaturation with oxygen under exposure to atomic oxygen. These results guide improved interface formation, which serves as a foundation for growing thick iron oxide films. Our work also expands our knowledge of ultrathin reactive iron oxide films and it opens the door to the growth of oxide structural polymorphs and oxide films with high oxidation state at low pressure using atomic oxygen. In the course of this work, we developed and implemented the powerful scanning micro-LEED methodology for determining several aspects of surface structure with high precision and high spatial resolution. This work produced a sophisticated software tool for data analysis with high throughput that can be shared and will advance capabilities of other researchers around the world [C8:1; C9:8]. Notwithstanding the uncertainty about the role of extrinsic factors in our observations described in section 5.3, TAP studies allowed a critical assessment of some of the most important principles that have been believed to facilitate effective CO oxidation at low temperature on hematite-based catalysts [C8:4; C9:1,10]. The presence of Au nanoparticles alone does not reduce the reaction temperature on the hematite surface to room temperature but only shifts the onset temperature to lower values and increases the reaction rate at high temperatures. Ionic Au is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition for reaction to occur at room temperature. Reduction and a small admixture of H2O is needed for reaction at room temperature. These results support the model that ionic Au + vacancies + same H2O facilitate low temperature CO oxidation.

16300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300014.value: Further experimental and theoretical investigations of the new iron oxides identified in this project can be carried out to determine their geometric structural arrangements in detail and to explore their physical properties, chemical properties and functionalities. We intend to use other powerful techniques, such as scanning tunneling microscopy, to learn more about atomic structural arrangements. It would also be interesting to investigate the catalytic activity of the HOC-structured oxide discovered in this work for CO oxidation at ambient pressures. Continued exploration using methods similar to those used in the project may also identify other oxide structural polymorphs and could lead to control over the surface termination of the hematite formed using atomic oxygen. It may be possible to discriminate broad facet diffraction peak signal produced by Au nanoparticles by eliminating noise arising from secondary electrons using an imaging electron energy analyzer to cut off secondary electron background. Implementation of a direct electron detector would also eliminate detector noise. The TAP method could be taken further advantage of for studying catalysis by well-defined single crystal surfaces in the future, provided methods can be developed to exclude reactions at regions in the experimental setup other than the model surface under deliberate investigation.

16300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300014.value: A new approach to grow iron oxide thin films using atomic rather than molecular oxygen was developed in this project. This approach can produce oxides with different oxidation states and in a variety of previously unknown structural polymorphs. Among these, a new oxygen-enriched layer that can oxidize CO at elevated temperature was found that may be a potentially interesting catalytic material. Our results guide improved interface formation, which serves as a foundation for growing thick iron oxide films. They also open the door to the growth of oxide films with high oxidation state at low pressure for use as model substrates for Au nanoparticle catalysis and other applications. We developed a new method for determining surface structure with high precision and high spatial resolution. This work produced a sophisticated software tool for data analysis with high throughput that can advance capabilities of other researchers around the world. We also adapted the “temporal analysis of products” method to the study of catalytic reactions on model single crystal surfaces at near-ambient pressure. This development facilitates the coupling of catalytic studies at realistic ambient reaction conditions with idealized fundamental studies in ultra-high vacuum using powerful surface science tools.

16300214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300214.value: To understand the impacts of atmospheric aerosol particles on the environment, much recent research has focused on the secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. Current models over-simplify SOA formation by assuming that (1) gas-to-particle conversion is instantaneous since particles are assumed to be in a liquid phase; (2) the conversion is purely physical partitioning without involving any chemical reaction once the organic vapors are in the particle phase. However, there is growing evidence that atmospheric particles are complex mixtures of inorganics and organics in different phase states, and that chemical reactions in the particle phase can be a significant contributor to SOA formation. In this study, we propose to investigate the effects of particulate organics at different phase states (liquid, solid, and semi-solid) mixed with ammonium sulfate on the reactive uptake of gas phase amines by ammonium sulfate particles. Amines, as an important class of atmospheric organic nitrogen species, were found to efficiently replace ammonium ions which are commonly found in atmospheric particles, and lead to the incorporation of amine vapors into particle phase. Previous studies have often used pure ammonium salts to study this reaction. The difference in phase states (hence viscosity and diffusivity) may affect the reaction kinetics of amine-ammonia exchange reactions. The objective of the current study is to understand whether, and to what extent, organics will suppress (e.g., for solid and semi-solid organics) or enhance (e.g., for liquid organics) amine-ammonium exchange reactions. An electrodynamic balance (EDB) coupled with Raman spectroscopic and light-scattering measurements will be employed to measure mass and compositional changes of the particles. Glycerol, sucrose, and oleic acid (without and with ozone exposure) are chosen as the organics to mix with ammonium sulfate. They represent a wide range of phase state, viscosity, and hydrophilicity of organics. Methylamine and dimethylamine, commonly observed in atmosphere, are chosen as the organic vapors to react with ammonium sulfate. Uptake kinetics (or coefficients) in these systems will be investigated under different relative humidity (RH) conditions. The results of the current study will be helpful in understanding how the phase, viscosity (thus diffusivity), and hydrophobic interactions between organic vapors and particulate organics affect the reactive uptake of amines into ammonium sulfate particles. Model representation of SOA formation will be improved with more information of the effects of phase states on multi-phase processes. 为理解大气颗粒物对环境的影响，很多最近的研究均聚焦于二次有机气溶胶（SOA）的形成过程。现在的大气模型将二次有机气溶胶的形成过于简化，因其假设：（1）大气颗粒物是液相的，故气相到颗粒相的转化是瞬时完成的；（2）气相到颗粒相的转化纯粹是物理过程，有机蒸气可以存在于颗粒相中，完全不含任何化学反应过程。然而，越来越多的证据显示，大气颗粒物是由不同相态的无机物和有机物共同混合组成的，而且颗粒相中的化学反应能够显著促进二次有机气溶胶的形成过程。在本课题中，我们试图研究颗粒相中与硫酸铵混合的不同相态的有机物（液相，固相和半固相）对于颗粒物吸收有机胺的影响。胺类，作为大气中很重要的一种含氮的有机物，能够显著取代广泛存在与大气颗粒物中的铵根离子，并导致胺类的蒸气进入颗粒相。之前的研究仅是利用铵盐来考察类似的化学反应。不同相态的有机物具有不同的黏性和挥发性，将会影响这种有机胺和无机氨交换的化学反应动力学特征。 本课题的目标是考察有机物是否会抑制（例如固态、半固态的有机物）或促进（例如液态的有机物）有机胺-无机氨的交换反应，以及这种抑制或促进的程度。我们将利用电动天平 (electrodynamic balance)和与其耦合的拉曼光谱技术、光散射技术来测量颗粒物质量和化学组成的变化。我们选取甘油、蔗糖、油酸和经过臭氧处理的油酸来与硫酸铵进行混合。一甲基胺、二甲基胺在大气中能够广泛观测到，我们选取这两种有机胺，作为与硫酸铵-有机物颗粒反应的气态物质。颗粒相中的这几种有机物代表了很广泛的相态、黏性和亲水性的物质特征。我们还会在不同相对湿度（RH）下来考察颗粒物对有机胺的吸收动力学（或吸收因子）。本研究的结果将会对于理解颗粒相物质的相态、黏性（扩散性）和亲水性如何影响硫酸铵-有机物颗粒对于胺类吸收，很有帮助。拥有更多关于物质相态对于多相过程影响的信息，大气模型对于二次有机气溶胶形成过程的描述也会得以改进。

16300214.label: Realisation of objectives
16300214.value: (1) Uptake of amines by ammonium sulfate-glycerol mixed particles Glycerol was found to evaporate from the particle phase, ultimately only ammonium sulfate was left. It significantly changed the physical properties of particles. The experiments with glycerol were designed to study the effect of particle viscosity on amine uptake, which can be addressed in the experiments with sucrose. (2) Uptake of amines by ammonium sulfate-sucrose mixed particles Bulk solutions containing ammonium sulfate and sucrose were prepared gravimetrically and then used to generate ammonium-sucrose mixed particles. Evaporation of sucrose was negligible, therefore, the sucrose molar fraction in the dried particles was precisely controlled. Experiments were conducted at various RH conditions to control the initial phase state of ammonium sulfate. Crystallization of sucrose was not observed. The uptake profiles for MA and DMA were similar and DMA was used in the experiments due to its higher abundance in ambient. Particle mass change due to DMA uptake and the additional water uptake (due to stronger hygroscopicity of dimethylaminium sulfate than ammonium sulfate) was quantified by the balancing DC voltage. Changes in particle composition and phase state were indicated from the Raman spectra and Mie scattering patterns. The percentage of ammonium (NH4+) displaced by DMA was calculated for each experiment. The DMA uptake coefficient was estimated for each experiment. The role of sucrose (surrogate for viscous hydrophilic organics) in the equilibrium particle composition and the kinetics DMA uptake was investigated comprehensively. (3) Uptake of amines by ammonium sulfate-oleic acid mixed particles Oleic acid (OA) is immiscible with an aqueous phase, therefore, OA was coated onto an ammonium sulfate particle. OA vapor from a heated OA reservoir was directed into the EDB and subsequently condensed onto the particle surface. Aged OA coating was achieved by feeding ozone into the EDB, and the aging extent can be varied by controlling the ozone concentration and exposure time. The RH was varied to control the initial phase state of ammonium sulfate. The percentage of ammonium (NH4+) displaced by DMA was calculated for each experiment . The DMA uptake coefficient was estimated for each experiment. The role of fresh/aged oleic acid (surrogate for hydrophobic organics) in the equilibrium particle composition and the kinetics DMA uptake was investigated comprehensively.

16300214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300214.value: At first, the hygroscopicity of selected short-chain alkyl aminium sulfate salts over a wide range of RH (< 3 – 90%) was investigated. All the studied aminium sulfate salts exhibit stronger hygroscopicity than their ammonium counterparts. The measured water-to-solute molar ratio as a function of RH served as the basis for deriving the particle-phase composition during amine uptake. For details, please see Chu et al. (2015). For DMA uptake by ammonium sulfate-sucrose mixed particles, effective DMA uptake was observed for most cases, except for the water-limiting scenario at <5% RH and the formation of an ultraviscous sucrose coating at 10% RH and below. DMA uptake coefficients (γ) were estimated using the particle mass measurements during DMA uptake. Addition of sucrose can increase γ by absorbing water or inhibiting AS crystallization and decrease γ by elevating the particle viscosity and forming a coating layer. DMA uptake can be facilitated for crystalline AS or retarded for aqueous AS with hydrophilic viscous organics (e.g., secondary organic material formed via the oxidation of biogenic volatile organic compounds) present in aerosol particles. See Chu and Chan (2017a) for details. For DMA uptake by ammonium sulfate-oleic acid mixed particles, over 74% of the original NH4+ ions were displaced by DMA, except those conditioned at <5% RH where water is limited. Regarding the uptake kinetics, we speculate that the fresh or aged OA coating retarded DMA uptake by preventing the particle surface from effectively accommodating DMA gas molecules. Judging from the estimated DMA uptake coefficients, as the weight percentage of coating increased, the retardation effect first intensified and then leveling off, likely when the ammonium sulfate particle surface was completely covered by fresh or aged OA. We propose that the accommodation of DMA on the particle coating is the rate-limiting step of DMA uptake. Intensive aging of the OA coating increased the viscosity of the coating. It had little effect on the equilibrium particle-phase compositions but showed down the diffusion of DMA in the coating, which further retarded DMA uptake. For details, please refer to Chu and Chan (2017b). The exchange reaction between DMA and NH3 was also found during the co-absorption of NH3 and DMA by sulfuric acid particles. At 10% RH, NH3 displaced particle-phase dimethylaminium ion (DMAH+) due to the crystallization of ammonium sulfate. At 50% RH, DMA displaced particle-phase NH4+ because DMA possesses stronger alkalinity than NH3. See Sauerwein and Chan (2017) for details. References Chu, Y., Sauerwein, M., and Chan, C. K. (2015). 16300214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300214.value: The experimental data for amine uptake by ammonium sulfate-organic mixed particles can be simulated using a multi-layer kinetics model, in order to obtain detailed kinetic parameters which are difficult to be measured in the experiments. The research group propose to initiate a collaboration with Dr. Manabu Shiraiwa at UC Irvine. Dr. Shiraiwa has established a multi-layer kinetics model, which gives empirically fitted values of multi-phase reaction kinetic parameters.

16300214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300214.value: Short-chain alkyl amines are important alkaline gases besides ammonia in the atmosphere. Although the abundance of amine gases is low, concentrations of amines in aerosol particles are much higher. Based on laboratory experiments, this project has addressed the following scientific questions: (1) what is the difference in water contents between amine- and ammonia-sulfuric acid mixtures, (2) to what extent amine can be absorbed by ammonium-containing particles, and (3) how the amine gas uptake rate can be influenced by organics of different physical properties in the particles. Findings from this work will help to explain the enrichment of amines relative to ammonia in ambient aerosol particles under various environmental conditions.

16300314.label: Realisation of objectives
16300314.value: The project investigated ToF-SIMS fragmentation of polymers employing both experimental and density functional theory calculation to better understand the process. It was found that the molecular structures of the ion fragment are related to their stability. The atomic arrangement and neighboring atoms in a polymer chain also influence the abundance of the fragments. This work shows that DFT model can predict the fragmentation to a good degree of accuracy. This work prepared several polymers including P2VP, P4VP and 5FPS to test the extent the model can predict the fragmentation under ToF-SIMS analysis. These polymers possess unique structures enabling us to relate the structures of the secondary ion to the polymer structure.

16300314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300314.value: Density functional theory calculations were used to analyze the time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) positive and negative ion spectra of poly(2-vinylpyridine) (P2VP) and poly(4-vinylpyridine) (P4VP) [Wong 2017]. Most of the ions from these structural isomers shared the same accurate mass, but had different relative abundance. This is attributed to the disparity in the molecular structures affecting the ion stability. The molecular structures of these ions were assigned and their stability was evaluated based on calculations using the Kohn-Sham density functional theory with Becke’s three-parameter Lee-Yang-Parr exchange-correlation functional and a correlation-consistent, polarized, valence, double-zeta basis set for cations and the same basis set with a triple-zeta for anions. The computational results agreed with the experimental observations that the nitrogen-containing cations were more favorably formed in P2VP than in P4VP due to higher ion stability. Nevertheless, our assumption was invalid in the formation of positive ions such as C6H7N+˙ (m/z = 93) and C8H10N+ (m/z = 120). Their formation did not necessarily depend on the ion stability. Instead, the transition state chemistry and the matrix effect both played a role. In the negative ion spectra, we found that nitrogen-containing anions such as C5H4N- (m/z = 78), C6H6N- (m/z = 92), C7H6N- (m/z = 104), C8H6N- (m/z = 116), C9H10N- (m/z = 132), C13H11N2- (m/z = 195) and C14H13N2- (m/z = 209) ions were more favorably formed in P4VP, which is in line with our computational results without exception. We speculate that whether anions would form from P2VP and P4VP is more dependent on the stability of the ions. In addition, we also studied the ToF-SIMS fragmentation mechanisms of polystyrenes—phenyl-fluorinated polystyrene (5FPS), phenyl-deuterated polystyrene (5DPS), and hydrogenated polystyrene (PS) using density functional theory calculations [Ng 2018]. From the positive ion spectra of 5FPS, we identified some characteristic molecular ion structures with isomeric geometries such as benzylic, benzocyclobutene, benzocyclopentene, cyclopentane and tropylium systems. The positive fluorinated ions from 5FPS tended to rearrange and produce fewer fluorine-containing molecular ions. Consequently, the fluorine-containing polycyclic aromatic ions had much lower intensities than their hydrocarbon counterparts.

16300314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300314.value: We analyzed ToF-SIMS positive and negative ion spectra of five polymers with well-defined structures (P2VP, P4VP, PS, 5FPS and 5DPS) and have shown that the stability of ions in ToF-SIMS spectra can be determined by density functional calculations. Although we can successfully analyzed the ToF-SIMS spectra and proposed fragmentation mechanisms of polymers in the ToF-SIMS process, yet the number of polymers that have been analyzed by our approach is small. It would be extremely useful if a dozen of polymers with well-defined can be analyzed with our approach, confirming the validity of our method.

16300314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300314.value: ToF-SIMS is one of the most powerful surface analysis techniques, especially for polymers. The limitation of this technique is that the ion formation mechanisms in a ToF-SIMS process are still not fully established. The reconstruction of the fragmentation pathways by detailed analyses of the structures of the fragment ions is the first step in the interpretation of ToF-SIMS spectra. The fragmentation process of a polymer is undoubtedly related to its polymer chain structure. Based on analysis results of several polymers with well-defined structures, we successfully established some relationships between the structures of the secondary ions and the polymer chain structures. In addition, we have shown that the stability of various ions can be determined by density functional theory calculations and proposed the fragmentation processes of polymers in the ToF-SIMS process. Our works have advanced our understanding of fragmentation processes of polymers in the ToF-SIMS process, allowing easier and correct interpretation of ToF-SIMS spectra of polymers.

16300414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300414.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to investigate Casimir forces between micromechanical elements of non-conventional shapes. Casimir forces refer to the interactions between neutral conductors that arise when the presence of boundaries leads to changes in the quantum zero point energy. Micromechanical devices have become indispensible tools in science and technology, from motion detectors to barcode scanners. Advances in microfabrication have produced ultra sensitive transducers, enabling novel interactions like the Casimir force to be explored with unprecedented sensitivity. At the same time, the critical dimensions and separations between state-of-the-art micromechanical components have already been reduced to submicron ranges. With continual miniaturization, a better understanding of the fundamental interactions between surfaces will be crucial for the successful fabrication and operation of micromechanical devices. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the strong dependence of the Casimir force on the shape of the interacting objects. A number of novel configurations will be measured, including non-monotonic Casimir forces in a modified glide symmetric geometry, lateral Casimir forces between surfaces with non-sinusoidal corrugations and a bridge that can yield the difference in the Casimir force between two sets of surfaces with different properties. Successful implementation of the proposed project will not only verify the validity of various theoretical algorithms, answer open questions and stimulate new theoretical research, but could also bring about new ways of controlling the Casimir interaction based on engineering the shape of the interacting elements. The proposed project is made feasible by a recent technological innovation made in the PI’s group where the force sensing element and the actuator that controls the separation are integrated on the same silicon chip. Since both the shape and the initial locations of the interacting elements are defined by lithography, no external, manual alignment is required. Such capability allows the measurement of the Casimir force between a wide range of novel nanostructured surfaces. The PI has extensive experience with micromechanical devices and Casimir force measurements. In addition to implementing the new on-chip platform describe above, he also pioneered the use of micromechanical torsional balances in the study of Casimir forces and recently demonstrated the geometry dependence of the Casimir force on a strongly deformed silicon surface. 16300614.label: Project Objectives
16300614.value: Lattice Polyhedron Algebra: The Cartesian product of lattice polytopes is not closed as operation in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces. Our first objective is to define an algebra for the lattice polytopes inside the infinite-dimensional space of infinite tuples having only finite number of nonzero entries. Decomposition of Lattice Polytopes into Lattice base Simplices: It is known that not every lattice polytope can be dissected into a collection of finitely many lattice simplices. Our second objective is to resolve that every lattice polytope can be written as a collection lattice simplices minus a collection of finitely many lattice base simplices. Canonical Integral Base and Rational Vector Bases: It is well known that the coefficients of Ehrhart polynomials are valutions (= finitely additive measure) with rational numbers, and these valuations form a basis for the lattice polytope algebra. This basis is not closed under the Cartesian product. Our third objective is to find a basis which is closed under the Cartesian product, and such a basis can be the powers of the half-closed and half-open unit interval. Application to Polytopes Associated with Graphs: Our objective is to apply the combinatorial meanings for the coefficients of Ehrhart polynomials to further understand the polynomials associated with graphs and the intrinsic properties of graphs themselves. Extension to Bounded Polyhedra: Our objective is to find combinatorial meanings for the elementary mixed volumes (quermassintegrals) modulo certain infinitesimal objects. In Nature/446/26 April 2007 material scientist David Kinderlehrer found applications of elementary mixed volumes in grain growth, indicating that sometimes pure math may have unexpected applications in natural sciences.

16300614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300614.value: Counting the number of objects and measuring the size of geometric shapes are basic procedures to understand physical bodies by quantity. Since numbers can be added and multiplied, the sum and product rules must be followed and give rise to measures on certain classes of concerned geometric objects. For instance, number of individuals, length of a line, area of a surface, and volume of a solid, are measures. Notice that a closed interval has two endpoints and an open interval does not. So the half-closed-and-half-open unit interval seems to be a natural (neutral) standard for measuring the pure length of lines; its square as the standard for measuring the pure area of surfaces, and its cubic power as the standard for measuring the pure volume of solids. So after scaling, nice solid geometric bodies may have pure volumes, pure areas, pure lengths, and pure counts compared with the standards of volume, area, length, and count. (For example, the length of a rectangular solid, being the sum of three side lengths, is already used to measure the size of luggage in airlines.) In Nature/446/26 April 2007 material scientist has found applications of these pure measures in grain growth. Given any convex body K and its enlarged body K(r), obtained by replacing each point x of K with a ball of radius r centered at x, the volume of K(r) is a polynomial function of r, whose degree is the dimension of K. It is known that the coefficients of this polynomial are measures on the class of convex bodies, invariant under rigid motions of the Euclidean space, and can be uniquely extended into invariant measures on the class of polyconvex sets. The first purpose of this project is to find the combinatorial meanings of these rigid motion invariant measures and to identify them as the pure count, pure length, pure area, the pure volume, etc. Given a lattice polytope P and its dilation nP (enlarged n times). The number of lattice points of nP is a polynomial function of n. The coefficients of this polynomial are related to many parts of mathematics such as convex geometry, toric geometry, polyhedral combinatorics, commutative algebra, topology and geometry. The second purpose of this project is to find the combinatorial meanings of these unimodular invariant measures and identify them as the pure count, the pure lattice length, the pure lattice area, the pure lattice volume, etc.

16300614.label: Realisation of objectives
16300614.value: The objective 1 is achieved by defining an algebra generated by lattice polytopes in all dimensions. We first identify the polytopes in all dimensions in the infinite-dimensional vector space of infinite sequences having zero tails. The embedding is simple, just adding infinite zero coordinates to a vector with finite coordinates. Then the algebra generated by polyhedrons is meaningful. To reduce the size of the polyhedron algebra we make no difference for translates and dissections of polytopes. By doing so we obtain an algebra for polytopes and polyhedron sets in multi-dimensions. Restricted to lattice polytopes and polyhedrons, we obtain the lattice polytope algebra. The objective 2 is achieved by decompose lattice polytopes into lattice-base simplices. Notice that it is not true that each lattice polytope can be dissected into lattice-base simplices. In fact there are indeed examples of lattice polytopes that cannot be dissected into lattice-base simplices. However, in the lattice polytope algebra, each polytope can be decomposed into a linear combination of lattice-base simplices by special constructions. We obtain that the lattice polytope algebra is also generated by lattice-base simplices. In fact it is confirmed that the classes of lattice-base simplices form a basis for the lattice polytope algebra. The objective 3 is to find the combinatorial/geometric meanings for the coefficients of Ehrhart polynomials. We apply the lattice polytope algebra and obtain another lattice-basis of Cartesian product of half-closed and half-open unit intervals. It turns out that the lattice polytope algebra is a one-variable algebra generated by the half-closed and half-open unit interval. This is a big achievement, since the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial is joust the coefficients of the half-closed and half-open unit interval in the lattice polytope algebra. This obtained by finding the connection matrices between the two bases: one consists of the class of lattice-bases in all dimensions, and the other consists of the classes of all Cartesian products of the half-closed and half-open unit interval. The object 4 is achieved by having obtained various applications to graph polynomials and signed graphs. The Tutte polynomial in graph theory is a two-variable polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients. For a long time it is an interesting and important problem in graph theory to find the meanings for each value of the Tutte polynomial at integers. With the geometric idea from the lattice polytope algebra, we luckily found the combinatorial/geometric meanings for all values of the Tutte polynomial at positive integers for both variables. It is still unknown for the values of the Tutte polynomial for one variable at positive integers and the other variable at negative integers. The objective 5 is to find applications in mixed volumes of classical geometric measures theory. This is partially achieved by comparing the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial and the Steiner formula on the volume of the convex bodies and Weyl tube formula for embedded manifold in a Euclidean space. The work is still under development, involving the deep and intrinsic parts of geometry and topology.

Our third objective is to find a basis which is closed under the Cartesian product, and such a basis can be the powers of the half-closed and half-open unit interval.

Application to Polytopes Associated with Graphs: Our objective is to apply the combinatorial meanings for the coefficients of Ehrhart polynomials to further understand the polynomials associated with graphs and the intrinsic properties of graphs themselves.

Extension to Bounded Polyhedra: Our objective is to find combinatorial meanings for the elementary mixed volumes (quermassintegrals) modulo certain infinitesimal objects. In Nature/446/26 April 2007 material scientist David Kinderlehrer found applications of elementary mixed volumes in grain growth, indicating that sometimes pure math may have unexpected applications in natural sciences.

16300614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300614.value: We introduced the lattice polytope algebra generated by lattice polytopes in all dimensions subject to identification of translates and dissections, whose algebra is generated by Cartesian product of sets. The SL(Z) (special linear group over integers) invariants of the lattice polytope algebra are classified into Ehrhart polynomials. The first big result is the construction of a canonical bases generated by the Cartesian products of the half-closed and half-open interval. This leads to the discovery of the combinatorial/geometric meanings for the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomials. The result will be written up and planned to be submitted to the very top math journal. The second significant result is the combinatorial/geometric meaning for the coefficients of the Tutte polynomial at positive integers for its two variables. We introduce complementary polynomial and dual complementary polynomial, which turns out to the Tutte polynomial. The duality gives rise to the combinatorial/geometric interpretation for the Tutte polynomial. This result is a nontrivial application of Ehrhart theory and lattice polytope algebra to graph theory. The result is published in the third paper in Part C. The third result is the unified treatment for the combinatorial interpretations of chromatic polynomial, flow polynomial, and other graph polynomials at special values. This is also based on the Ehrhart theory and lattice polytope algebra. New results were discovered at the same time. For instance, the number of cut (Eulerian) equivalence classes of a graph is the value of its chromatic (flow) polynomial at zero. Weighted Tutte like polynomials are introduced and various formulas are obtained. See the second paper in Part C. For signed graph application, we classified the minimal structures at integer level for integral flows (joint with other two authors) and integral tensions. However, at half-integer level, the integral flows are decomposed into elementary circuits and integral tensions are decomposed into elementary co-circuits. The results show that the integer level phenomenon is quite different from phenomenon of half-integer level, much like phase transition. The work on integral tensions is presented in the fourth paper in Part C and the work on integral flows in the first paper in Part C. For real dilations of rational polytopes (whose vertex coordinates are rational numbers), we obtain Ehrhart quasi-polynomials, which obeys the similar reciprocity law on its variable. The work is presented in the conference paper in Part C.

16300614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300614.value: The applications for the chromatic polynomial, flow polynomial, and Tutte polynomial of signed-graphs are not yet studied. The situation is quite different from the graph case, since the matroid of a signed graph is not necessarily regular, while the matroid of a graph is always regular. The torsion of a signed graph is a power of 2, so it a dyadic matroid. The application of rational polytope algebra will give rise to many interesting and significant results for signed graphs on polynomials. The research on signed graphs along the direction can be further developed. Finding the combinatorial/geometric meanings for mixed volume is challengeable and is a difficult classical problem. Little progress was made and not much developed since it is founded by Minkowski. Actually, the problem is not well known to younger mathematicians. However, the field is much worth to be explored, since it is fundamental and related to the deep parts of mathematics such as intersection theory of algebraic geometry. The investigation along this direction is worth to be further developed.

16300614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300614.value: Length, area and volume are elementary geometric quantities invariant under rigid motions. If we are restricted to lattice geometric objects, say, counting the number of the lattice points of a dilated lattice polytope by n times is a polynomial function of n, known as Ehrhart polynomial, which is invariant under the unimodular group. The coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial are much like the length, area and volume, etc., but their meanings are mysterious except the top coefficient and the constant. The project found a geometric/combinatorial interpretation for the coefficients of Ehrhart polynomial. The Ehrhart polynomial has application to chromatic, flow, and Tutte polynomial of graphs. Such graph polynomials are important invariants of graphs and are decomposed into Ehrhart polynomials with respect to acyclic orientations, totally cyclic orientations, and their combinations. The special values of such polynomials are found geometric/combinatorial meanings by the Ehrhart theory. The theory of lattice polytope algebra and its application to graph theory are significant in the sense that both are fundamental to understand the invariants of lattice polytopes and polyhedra and values of the above graph polynomials. The results discovered are simple, natural, and beautiful.

16300714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300714.value: 关于限价单成交的生存分析

16300714.label: Project Objectives
16300714.value: Find survival models that best fit the limit order execution times and account for the features of the limit order book data. Apply the survival models to analyze limit order book data collected from major stock exchanges in China and around the world.
rows: Find survival models that best fit the limit order execution times and account for the features of the limit order book data.
Apply the survival models to analyze limit order book data collected from major stock exchanges in China and around the world.

16300714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300714.value: Thirty years back, intermediation played vital roles in the stock and futures markets around the world, including the NYSE specialists, the Tokyo Saitori and the Nasdaq and London dealers. As of 2013, however, nearly all major equity or derivatives markets, including Hong Kong, Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges as the major emerging markets, are largely electronic limit order markets. Despite worldwide proliferation of limit order markets, many important issues remain unclear. As questioned by Parlour and Seppi, ``Is the society better off because of the global adoption of limit order markets?" In a limit order market, a trader can submit a limit order, which can only transact at a limit price or lower (higher) if it's a buy (sell). In contrast, a market order transacts at the best available price. A limit order enjoys price protection but suffers the possibility of expiry/non-execution, delayed execution or being "picked off". Thus, time to execution of limit orders is its key element and has become a criterion to measure the liquidity and efficiency of markets. Viewing execution as an event, survival analysis is the most natural tool. Survival analysis is a major branch of statistical science that aims at studying time to events, understanding and explaining the event occurrence and their relationships with existing factors. In particular, analysis of censored data is a central subject of survival analysis. A limit order may also be canceled and revised, which is thus viewed as censored. The event-causing mechanism in limit order markets are complicated by heterogeneous arrivals of orders, right censoring due to cancelation/revision which could be dependent or informative, interval censoring in hypothetical limit orders, time-dependent covariates, etc. Broader statistical models and finer statistical methodologies are therefore much desired. The generalized accelerated failure time model is probably the most general statistical models for the analysis of time-to-event data. It includes the popular Cox model and linear models as special cases. We intend to employ the counting process approach to analyze order arrivals and try to fit the accelerated failure time models and/or transformation models. In view of the importance of limit order markets, we believe the output of this research will contribute to understanding of the advantages and disadvantages of limit order markets, finding optimal submission strategies and assisting the price discovery process. Eventually it will help pave the way towards optimal market designs and winning edges in market competitions. 三十年前，中介在世界各地的在股票和期货市场，包括纽约证交所，东京saitori和纳斯达克和伦敦经销商，起到了至关重要的作用。然而, 截至 2013，几乎所有主要的股票和衍生品市场，包括香港，上海和深圳证券交易所作为主要的新兴市场，都是电子限价订单市场。尽管限价指令市场全球推广，许多重要问题尚不清楚。正如Parlour 和Seppi的质疑，` `因为全球采用限价指令市场，社会是变得更好还是更坏？” 限价单市场中，买（卖）方交易者可以提交订单但以限价或低于（高于）限价成交。相反，市价单则在最好的价格成交。限价单享受价格保护但有过期，不能执行，延迟执或“被选择”的缺陷。因此， 成交时间是限价单执行的关键因素，也成为衡量市场流动性和效率的标准。 把限价单成交看作一个事件，生存分析是分析它的最自然的工具。生存分析， 作为统计科学的 一个重要分支，旨在通过对事件时间的分析来学习，理解和解释事件的发生以及存在的关系。 分析删失数据尤其是生存分析的一个重要课题。限价单也可能被取消和修改，因此被视为删失数据是合适的。限价单市场复杂的部分原因是下单时间的异构化和删失的存在。由于取消/修改本身包含相关信息，区间删失，随时间变化的协变量等等因素，因此更需要广泛而有效的统计模型和统计方法。 广义加速失效时间模型是时间事件的数据分析的最一般的统计模型。它包括流行的Cox模型和线性模型。我们打算使用计数过程的方法来分析订单到达并试图应用加速失效时间模型和/或转换模型。基于限价订单市场的重要性，我们相信这一研究的成果将有助于了解限价订单市场的优点和缺点，寻找最优提交策略，协助价格发现过程。最终它将为实现最佳的市场设计和市场竞争优势铺平道路。

16300714.label: Realisation of objectives
16300714.value: For analysis of limit order book data, despite the rich literature on linear transformation models, the application is still limited to some extent due to a fixed error distribution since in reality we usually don't know the baseline distribution for a given survival dataset. We propose a new linear transformation model with baseline distribution belonging to a certain distribution family. We also provide an efficient algorithm to solve for the MLE of our model and apply it to a real time-to-execution dataset. We introduced the new generalized gamma linear transformation model and clarify the model identifiability problem. We calculate the likelihood function and propose an algorithm to get the maximum likelihood estimates of the linear transformation model. We conducted simulation studies to evaluate the finite sample performance of the linear transformation model. We apply our model to the real data set.

16300714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300714.value: We found that the existing transformations are not appropriate for analyzing limit order book data. We discovered the generalized gamma linear transformation model, which is more flexible than the standard linear transformation model, is particularly fit for analysis of limit order book data.

16300714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300714.value: There is a possibility that the generalized gamma linear transformation model can be further extended to more general models. However, there exists a danger of overfitting, to which we must pay special attention when the model becomes too large. It is also possible that the model can be applied to cryptocurrency trading data.

16300714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300714.value: In the financial market, market participants are involved in different kinds of market events, either in need of hedging against the risk in other financial instruments, or seeking price differences between similar products that should not exist theoretically. Other types of market participants may make decisions of buying or selling a specific asset in hope of capturing price changes in the future. Besides, there are market makers whose task is to quote bid and ask prices in a specific instrument and provide liquidity to the market. All types of market participants care about how to better model the market dynamics and correspond to those that get executed after submission. Various models in survival analysis all need assumptions on the given distribution of the baseline failure time. However, in reality, we usually do not know this distribution for a given survival dataset. The generalized gamma linear transformation model that we found aims at solving the given-distribution issue. Taking advantage of a generalized gamma distribution, the new model incorporates several models as special cases and may serve as a more appropriate and general model in survival analysis. It may also help market participant design better trading strategies.

16300814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300814.value: 達怖方程的對稱性及其特徵解的研究

16300814.label: Project Objectives
16300814.value: To develop infinite expansions of elliptic functions as general solutions to Darboux class equations. To investigate hidden symmetries in eigen-solutions to the Darboux equations. It is believed that the symmetries involve certain affine Weyl groups. To investigate criteria on the Darboux class equations that would lead to meromorphic solutions via Nevanlinna theory.
rows: To develop infinite expansions of elliptic functions as general solutions to Darboux class equations.
To investigate hidden symmetries in eigen-solutions to the Darboux equations. It is believed that the symmetries involve certain affine Weyl groups.
To investigate criteria on the Darboux class equations that would lead to meromorphic solutions via Nevanlinna theory.

16300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300814.value: The project propose to extend a classical method and complex analytic method involving the expansion of infinite special functions to find general solutions and eigen-solutions to a class of periodic differential equations named after Darboux (1882). The Darboux class equations and its algebraic forms play an important role in the understanding of numerous applications, as well as in pure mathematics (such as integrable systems). The equations have a long and distinguished history, and yet our understanding to them is still inadequate. 達布方程可以畫分為特殊函數方程類別，並已有超過一個世紀的歷史，但它在相當長的時間給人們遣忘，因此對於這方程的了解還是在起歩階段，但它反覆在眾多數學物理問題、方程穩定性理論、代數幾何、正交各項式、可積系統等領域出現。本項目旨在用復變函數的方法研究發展達佈方程的解的基本理論及其解的形式。

16300814.label: Realisation of objectives
16300814.value: Overview: I believe that I have realized two out of the three objectives as stated in the original project proposal. . The third objective is partially achieved. Although I feel our progress has been slow, we have eventually overcome a bottleneck after a long struggle. We are writing four papers (under revision), one paper has been published, and one PhD student graduated. General comments against the objectives: That are (1): To develop infinite expansions of elliptic functions as general solutions to Darboux class equations, and (2): To investigate hidden symmetries in eigen-solutions to the Darboux equations. It is believed that the symmetries involve certain affine Weyl groups. Since objectives (1) and (2) are potentially of wider interest from amongst the researchers in both research areas of integrable systems and special functions than objective (3) which is about function theoretic, and in particular Nevanlinna theory interpretation, I spent most in my time and effort in tackling objectives (1) and (2) (I find them most intriguing), to the point of almost ignoring the objective (3). I and my collaborators had previously worked out some examples of infinite special function expansions to Heun equation and biconfluent Heun equations, so objective (1) is not hard to achieve as reported in the mid-term progress report. What remains are the investigation of those solutions that the infinite sum terminate. They resemble the eigen-solutions of classical special function examples (e.g., Legendre or Hermite polynomials). These special solutions from the classical examples typically form eigen-spaces each of dimension one. The ones we encountered for the Heun class equations have dimensions increase with respect to monodromy/Stoke’s data. Moreover, we have observed that the parameter spaces that lead to the termination of these infinite special function solutions resemble those of the corresponding Painleve equations obtained via isomonodromy deformation of the Heun equations/connections (Fuchs (1907), Ganier (1912) and Jimbo-Miwa (1981)). It is the fundamental works of K. Okamoto (e.g., 1986, 1987) that the Hamiltonians of these parameter spaces form affine Weyl groups. So the natural questions are if the corresponding parameter spaces for the Heun equations can also be identified with Lie group structures. Thus, I consider the objective (2) is the most important part of this project. However, we can now conclude that the algebraic structures of these parameter spaces are not of any Weyl groups or Lie algebras. Although we still do not have a deeper description of them, they are more complicated and to our surprise, these parameter spaces are strongly correlated with the monodromy/Stoke’s data of these Heun equations when being regarded as ``connections” defined on the Riemann sphere with four points or less deleted. These connections are already recorded in the Appendix C of Jimbo-Miwa’s Physical 2D (1981), 407-448 (*). Previous researchers either concentrated on the symmetries of Hamiltonians associated with the Painleve’ equations (e.g., Okamoto) or the Lax Pairs formulations of these connections in the calculations of boundary value problems applying isomonodromy deformations method (e.g., Ablowitz, Clarkson, Flaschka, Its, Kapaev, Newell, etc). Our findings show that these symmetry groups from the parameter spaces of the Painleve’ IV and VI equations have their origins derived from the corresponding connections (via isomonodromy deformation) from the Jimbo-Miwa paper . In particular these connections “degenerate” in certain senses, i.e., that either certain monodromy around a log-pole becomes trivial, or the Stoke’s data reduced. It is under these considerations that the parameter spaces of the Heun equation and biconfluent Heun connections are ``exactly’’ the same as the corresponding spaces for the P6 and P4 respectively. Our findings show that these parameter spaces are intrinsic properties of the connections independent of isomonodromy deformation. Moreover, the corresponding Heun or biconfluent Heun differential equations can admit special solutions (after choosing accessory parameters), however, only on a ``large subset’’ of the corresponding parameter spaces. Detailed description: we use the biconfluent Heun equation (BHE) or connection (BHC) to illustrate our findings. Our earlier findings show that the parameter space of BHE (after taking the symmetry group of the differential equation into consideration) admitting special solutions has a three hyperplanes missing (see the first figure of the file ``missing_planes’’ in section 11 Part C of this report) against the full picture of P4 (the second figure of the file ``missing_planes’’. These special solutions are given in the joint paper with Law and Yu. It took me more than two years with numerous failed attempts to finally identify all the “missing hyper-planes’’ by considering the corresponding connection (1st order system) and applying differential Galois theory. Let us adopt the notation in (*): (a), the BHC can be transformed to a parabolic type connection (a 1st order system where the singular point at the origin is removed) by a gauge transformation only if 2 times theta_0 is an integer; (b) if the differential Galois group of the BHC becomes (solvable) triangulisable algebraic group only if theta_0 + theta_infty or theta_0 - theta_infty is an integer. These two conditions allow us to ``fill up’’ all the hyper-planes exactly as those of the P4. Here the part (b) corresponds to degeneration of Stoke’s lines at infinity from four to two. Moreover, one can give a new description of the special solutions of the P4 with parameters lying in the corresponding affine Weyl group to lie in the differential field generated by a Picard-Viessot extension of a parabolic operator (including the rational solutions). At the same time, a solution of the BHE terminates from an infinite sum of parabolic functions as a result of the corresponding parameter space also lie in the same differential field generated by the same Picard-Viessot extension of the parabolic operator (including (Heun) polynomial solutions). The isolated points that lie in the interior of Weyl chambers (for P4) are excluded from the above consideration. The corresponding rational solutions of P4 are not in any differential field generated by a Picard-Viessot extension of a parabolic operator. On the other hand, we have identified no obvious lie algebra structures in the BHC/BHE settings. The gauge transformations although serves as action “jumping over’’ from one hyperplane to another, they are singular so that one cannot ‘’jump back’’ to the original position. So it appears that something lies deeper is still not being understood. The situation for the Heun or the Darboux equations against the P6 has parts that are similar and parts that are very different from that of BHE/BHC-P4 setting, except that no Stoke’s data would appear in this case. Further results: A different part mentioned above is achieved in a joint paper by Ching and Tsang and the author. There we have successfully developed a sheave theoretic language of the Heun connection in order to handle the monodromy and growth at singular points of the solutions that lie in invariant subspaces when the accessory parameter is appropriately chosen. The full set of parameter space for the degeneration of Heun connection matches that for the P6. Much time and effort have been used in this effort that is not anticipated.

16300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300814.value: Major findings: we have identified that, when appropriately described, the degenerations of the connections for the Heun and biconfluent equations recorded in Jimbo-Miwa’s Physical 2D (1981), 407-448 are as interesting as the Hamiltonians and Painleve equations approaches that most of the current researches are written about. Moreover, we have derived new infinite/terminated solutions for the corresponding scaler differential equations with four punctures on the Riemann sphere also have similar degeneration interpretations. Major findings in terms of papers: (1) Local infinite expansions of elliptic functions for the Darboux equations and identification parameter space of the Darboux equation as a connection with that of P6 (joint with Ching and Tsang). (2) Half-plane infinite expansions of parabolic functions for the biconfluent Heun equations. The parameter spaces that lead to the termination of these infinite sums as well as degeneration (in terms of differential Galois theory and Picard-Viessot extension) of the biconfluent Heun connection matches that of the P4. But no Lie algebraic structures is found (joint with Law and Yu). (3) Sheave theoretic approach has been used to handle handle the monodromy and growth at singular points of the solutions that lie in invariant subspaces when the accessory parameter is appropriately chosen. The full set of parameter space for the degeneration of Heun connection matches that for the P6. (4) Global (entire) solutions to the Whittaker-Hill equation are obtained as infinite expansions in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions have been obtained. We show that entire solutions with finite exponent of convergence in the sense of Nevanlinna theory corresponds to finite-gap solutions. (5) A full symmetry group of the Darboux equation has been worked out against that of the Heun equation in a joint paper with Ching and Tsang. The paper is published in the Kumamoto Journal of Mathematics in 2018. This paper is a by-product of this project and overlaps with the earlier project no. 601111.

16300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300814.value: (1) Probing into deeper rationale that leads to the parameter spaces of the Heun connections. This direction is guaranteed to be hard. (2) Parameter space identifications for the other confluent Heun connections/equations and Painleve equations (3) A proper sheave theoretic approach that can handle confluent Heun connections where irregular singularities appear. Our sheave theoretic approach is good only to the Heun connection since there is no irregular singularity. Wild fundamental groups may be needed. (4) Orthogonality of the solutions that lie in the invariant subspaces of the Heun equations. E.g. new finite 2F1 sum has been identified. Partial orthogonality has been worked out. But we still do not understand the what is behind the full picture since we are dealing with rank two systems. This development which is likely to be related to Serre duality is extremely interesting. (5) Infinite expansions already achieved can be put in the setting of I-adic settings. Some partial results have been already obtained. We are preparing a new GRF in this direction.

16300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300814.value: A common viewpoint about special functions is that they are not old, not interesting and probably not relevant in today’s scientific advancement. The findings in this project show that the above statement is a misconception. Not only the prime models in the so-called non-linear science have close connection to linear differential equations with good singularity structures which are themselves centuries old, very little is being understood about the deeper properties of these objects despite the fact they appear in numerous physical models ranging from cosmology to rotating harmonic oscillators. This project has identified previously unnoticed algebraic structures which have nice geometric but not understood structures.
