16301014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301014.value: Terrestrial and marine microorganisms are well known as a valuable source of biologically active compounds which could be developed into effective medicine for treatment of diseases and for fighting against bacterial infection. In April 2013, it was reported that the myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum So ce1485 collected from a soil sample produces a novel structural type of macrolactone ring-containing compounds, i.e. the maltepolides A–F. These macrolides are the 20-membered macrolactones and possess a conjugate diene ketone moiety and, except for maltepolide E, a 2,3,5-trisubstituted tetrahydrofuran subunit within the macrolactone core. Alternative, maltepolide E has a hydroxy vinyl epoxide subunit which was suggested to reorganize to the 2,3,5-trisubstituted tetrahydrofuran subunit upon exposing to slightly acidic or basic pHs. Preliminary biological investigation revealed that the maltepolides deliver cytostatic activity on the L929 mouse fibroblast cell line and cause unique morphological changes in certain dividing cells. It was proposed that the maltepolides might interfere with spindle assembly associated with cell growth and multiplication. This profile renders maltepolides promising candidates for the development of cytostatic drugs for chemotherapy of cancer and treatment of infection and skin diseases. Two possible processes were proposed for the generation of the maltepolides by the producing myxobacterium according to the results of biosynthesis studies. It was disclosed that maltepolides A–F might be derived from an advanced macrolactone precursor. The latter serves as a common intermediate to maltepolides A–F through a vinylogous Payne rearrangement as the key step. As a continuation of the PI’s previous studies on successful diverted total synthesis using advanced common intermediates, it is proposed in the current study that a biomimetic synthesis strategy will be established for accessing maltepolides and analogues. The key steps will mimic the proposed transformation of the proposed advanced macrolactone precursor into maltepolide congeners and analogues under the laboratory setting. This proposed study allows us to explore the key chemical transformation relevant to the biosynthesis of these naturally occurring macrolactone-containing compounds (or macrolides) and develop a flexible and efficient chemical synthesis route. The synthetic analogues made available in this project are useful for examining the structure–activity relationship and understanding the mechanism of action of the maltepolides. 陸地和海洋微生物是衆所週知的生物活性化合物的重要來源，可用于開發有效的醫藥品用于疾病的治療和抵抗細菌感染。2013年4月，有報道從一種土壤樣本中得到的粘細菌Sorangium cellulosum So ce1485産生一種新型結搆類型的大環內酯化合物，稱為maltepolides A–F。這些大環內酯具有20圓環，並在環骨架內含有共軛二烯酮單元、以及2,3,5-三取代四氫呋喃亞結搆單元（除maltepolide E以外）。另外，maltepolide E有一個羥基烯環氧亞結搆單元，后者被認為只要在稍微偏酸、鹼性的pH中就能重排成2,3,5-三取代四氫呋喃亞結搆單元。初步生物學研究表明maltepolides具有抑製L929老鼠纖維組織母細胞株生長的活性及在某些分裂細胞中引起特有的形態學上的改變，據此提出了maltepolides可能幹擾與細胞生長和繁殖有關的紡錘體的組裝， 從而使得maltepolides有望成為開發抑製細胞生長的候選藥物用于癌症的化療，以及傳染病和皮膚疾病的治療。根據生物合成研究的結果，該粘細菌産生maltepolides有兩種可能的過程。研究表明maltepolides A–F可能出自同一個高級的大環內酯前體，后者作為共同中間體通過烯基Payne重排反應這一關鍵步驟轉化為maltepolides A–F。本項目負責人利用高級共同中間體進行天然産物的多樣性全合成研究已有成功的案例，本研究計劃擬利用一種仿生合成的策略來製備maltepolides及其類似物，其關鍵步驟是要在實驗室條件下模擬將設想的高級大環內酯前體轉化為maltepolide同系物和類似物，通過探索一種與大環內酯生物合成密切相關的重要的化學轉化過程，從而開發高可塑性、高效率的化學合成路綫。本研究得到的合成類似物 將可用于建立有價值的構效關繫以及幫助理解maltepolides的作用機理。

16301014.label: Realisation of objectives
16301014.value: After disclosure of the structures of maltepolide A–E by Prusov and co-workers (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2013, 52, 5402–5405), a total synthesis of the proposed structure of maltepolide C was reported by Ghosh and co-workers (Org. Lett. 2016, 18, 4092–4095); however, the NMR data of their synthesized compound did not match with the naturally occurring maltepolide C. Two other synthetic papers were reported; Mohapatra and co-workers synthesized the C8–C24 fragment of maltepolide C (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 2015, 5266–5274), and the team of Rao and Srihari synthesized the C13–C24 fragments of maltepolide A, C, and D (Org. Biomol. Chem. 2016, 14, 9629–9638). Up to the end of December 2018, there is no synthesis of maltepolide E reported in the literature. The structure of maltepolide E is unique among maltepolides and it was proposed as the common precursor of maltepolide A–D and F. In the pH ranges of <6.5 and >7.5, the alkenyl epoxy moiety of maltepolide E underwent an intramolecular epoxide ring-opening cyclization reaction to form two tetrahydrofuran-containing macrocyclic cores which were found in maltepolide A–D and F. In Prusov and co-workers’ total synthesis, they used an intramolecular Heck reaction to construct the C6–C9 diene moiety of maltepolide C; however, the palladium catalyst used for catalyzing the Heck reaction is known to react with an alkenyl epoxy moiety. Therefore, the intramolecular Heck reaction is highly riskier for total synthesis of maltepolide E. In our original proposal, we envisioned a diene–ene ring-closing metathesis (RCM) strategy for construction of the macrocyclic cores of maltepolide E and its hypothetic biosynthesis precursor. The vinylogous Payne rearrangement was proposed in the biosynthesis of maltepolide E. Although we were interested in simulating this transformation using chemically synthesized compounds, our first priority focused on development of new chemistry needed for construction of the highly functionalized macrocyclic cores. We have realized the diene–ene RCM synthetic strategy in the synthesis of the truncated maltepolide E that is lacking the C20–C24 alkenyl epoxide side chain. Moreover, we have achieved formation of the truncated maltepolide A and B from the truncated maltepolide E in a manner as proposed for the biosynthesis of maltepolide A and B from maltepolide C [See section 8, journal publication #1; section 9, conference paper #1, and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. More specifically, Objective 1 has been achieved by establishment of the flexible retrosynthetic bond disconnections at the lactone C(=O)–O bond, the C8/C9 double bond, and C19/C20 single bond, resulting in the C1–C8 acid fragment, the C9–C19 aldehyde fragment, and the C20–C24 side chain [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. This synthetic strategy allowed us quickly to verify feasibility of the key diene–ene RCM reaction in the formation of the structurally simplified maltepolide E core by using two (C1–C8 and C9–C19) fragments among the three as mentioned above. Synthesis of the C1–C8 acid fragment has been accomplished by employing the Masamune anti-selective aldol reaction, the Wittig olefination, and the Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling catalyzed by our Pd(OAc)2–Aphos-Y catalyst system as the key steps [See section 8, journal publication #1]. The C9–C19 fragment has been prepared by using the Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons olefination of the keto phosphonate with the epoxy aldehyde as the key step after failure of the attempted Au(I)-catalyzed Meyer–Schuster rearrangement of a propargyl alcohol [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Objective 2 has been achieved by performing the diene–ene RCM reaction of two seco substrates prepared from the C1–C8 acid and the C9–C19 alcohol in the presence of Grubbs second generation Ru(II) catalyst. The desired 20-membered lactone cores were formed in good chemical yields and in almost a single (E)-geometric isomer for the newly formed C8/C9 double bond. Two different protecting groups (PMB and TBS ethers) for the C5-hydroxy group were examined and no visible difference in the RCM reaction was noted. However, the C5-OTBS ether allowed selective deprotection in the presence of the C17-OPMB ether and facilitated installation of the C5–C9 (6E,8E)-dienyl keto subunit within the 20-membered lactone core [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Objective 3 has been achieved for the formation of maltepolide analogues starting from the above synthesized C19-truncated maltepolide E core instead of the immediate maltepolide E precursor as initially proposed for study on the vinylogous Payne rearrangement within the macrolactone skeleton. This adjustment was largely due to lack of manpower to conduct the experimental work of substantial work load to develop the requisite synthetic route. Nevertheless, the proposed biosynthesis of maltepolide A and B from maltepolide E has been reproduced using our synthesized C19-truncated maltepolide E; upon releasing the C17-OH group, an intramolecular epoxide ring-opening cyclization reaction took place to form the C19-truncated maltepolide A and B, that contain the signature tetrahydrofuran ring within the macrocyclic cores [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Objective 4 has been achieved for synthesis of analogous compounds possessing the macrolactone core [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. At the time of submitting this completion report, bioassay of several synthetic samples has not been carried out and it will be arranged with a collaborator if the quality of the sample purity remains suitable for bioassay.

16301014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301014.value: The most significant finding of this project is the establishment of the diene–ene RCM strategy for the construction of the macrolactone core of maltepolide E. It is believed that the C20–C24 side chain would not deteriorate the outcome of the diene–ene RCM reaction. This ring closure approach should be superior to the intramolecular Heck reaction reported by Ghosh and co-workers (Org. Lett. 2016, 18, 4092–4095) in the total synthesis of maltepolide C. According to the known transformations of maltepolide E into maltepolide A–D and F, the diene–ene RCM strategy should provide a general access to the core structures of all known maltepolides [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Another major finding is the realization of an intramolecular epoxide ring-opening cyclization reaction using the C19-truncated maltepolide E; the finding confirms the obtained reactivity of the alkenyl epoxide unit is a general phenomenon and could be used for synthesis of functionalized tetrahydrofuran (THF) compounds [See section 8, journal publication #1 and section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Other findings are related to applications of the specific reactions and transformations in synthesis of complex molecules. The Au(I)-catalyzed Meyer–Schuster rearrangement of propargyl alcohols to conjugate enones is attractive for installation of the reactive functionality; however, it has been confirmed less applicable to the substrates possessing an epoxy moiety due to formation of unexpected compounds [See section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Also, a retro-aldol reaction has been observed by cleavage of the C4–C5 single bond within the 20-membered macrolactone skeleton to form the seco compound under very mild acidic conditions (TBAF–AcOH, v/v 5:1, room temperature) [See section 10, Man Ki SIT’s PhD thesis]. Overall, a different ring closure via a diene–ene RCM reaction has been established and the synthesized C19-truncated maltepolide E has been demonstrated to undergo an intramolecular epoxide ring-opening cyclization reaction to furnish the THF-containing cores of maltepolide A and B. The research outcome enriches the chemistry of maltepolides and facilitates further study to understand the bioactivity of maltepolides and synthetic analogues.

16301014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301014.value: The established diene–ene RCM strategy should be applicable to the total synthesis of maltepolide E and other maltepolides. After release of our research data in a journal publication (to be submitted for review), it is possible that other research groups might use the same strategy in the synthesis of maltepolides and analogues. Due to lack of manpower, it is not sure how much continuing research we could carry out.

16301014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301014.value: Maltepolides are a novel family of macrolactones isolated from the fermentation broth of the myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum So ce 1485. Maltepolide A–C and E exhibit moderate cytostatic activity on L929 mouse fibroblast cell lines. According to the observation that maltepolide A and E cause unique morphological changes in the diving transformed PtK2 cells, they are proposed to inhibit some kinesin or another factor involved in spindle assembly. This project aims to develop a superior chemical synthesis route to access maltepolide E, from which other maltepolide congeners could be obtained by the known method. A diene–ene ring-closing metathesis reaction, different from intramolecular Heck reaction reported by others, has been established for construction of the unique ring skeleton of maltepolide E. Some analogous compounds of maltepolide E without the C20–C24 side chain have been synthesized and their chemistry has been examined. The outcome of this project has potential application in accessing structural analogues of maltepolides that are valuable molecular tools for understanding the molecular basis of their biological profiles.

16301114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301114.value: Cyclic codes are a subclass of linear codes and are very important, because they possess algebraic structures that can be utilized in a variety of ways and their encoding can be efficiently implemented using simple shift registers. They have real-world applications in broadcast systems such as DVB and ATSC; computer applications such as RAID 6 systems; CDMA communication systems and deep-space communication; consumer electronics such as CDs, DVDs, Blu-ray Discs; and cryptography. Cyclic codes are also a subject of mathematics and are related to a number of mathematical areas such as algebra, algebraic function fields, algebraic geometry, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorial designs, finite geometries, finite fields, and number theory. The objective of this project is to construct cyclic codes over finite fields with both good error-correcting capability and rich algebraic properties. We will use algebraic, combinatorial, geometrical and number-theoretic tools in this project. The outcome of this project is expected to contribute to not only the theory of error correcting codes but also their applications in consumer electronics and communications engineering. 循环码是线性码的一个重要子类。由于它们具有良好的代数结构，人们可以用简单的移位寄存器对它们进行有效的编码。循环码在计算机系统，码分多址通信系统，深空通信系统，家用电器和密码学等领域有广泛的应用。循环码也是数学的一个分支，并且与代数，代数函数域，代数几何，代数数论，结合方案，组合设计，有限几何，有限域和数论相关。 本项目的主要任务是构造有限域上既有丰富的代数结构又有良好纠错能力的循环码。在此项目中，我们将使用代数工具，组合工具，几何工具，和数论工具。本项目的科研成果将对编码理论有贡献，并在电子消费产品和通信工程有应用。

16301114.value: Both objectives have been achieved. Cyclic codes with very good error-correcting capability and rich algebraic structures have been constructed with algebraic, combinatorial and number-theoretic tools. Properties of the codes constructed in this project have been proved and analysed.

16301214.label: Project Objectives
16301214.value: To produce narrow-band biphotons from a hot Rb atomic vapor cell with a coherence time of more than 50 ns (or bandwidth <20 MHz). To generate hyperentangled narrow-band biphotons from a hot Rb vapor cell. 16301214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301214.value: Entangled photon pairs, termed as biphotons, have been a benchmark tool in the field of quantum optics. Recent protocols of long distance quantum communication based on efficient photon-atom quantum interface have stimulated a great demand for single photons with optical bandwidth comparable to or narrower than the atomic linewidth, which is typically about several MHz. In the past years, laser cooled atoms is an efficient nonlinear medium for producing narrow-band biphotons, but the apparatus is too large and complicated for practical applications and engineering. Hot atomic vapor cells, which require nearly free management, could be an alternative solution, but so far the experimental demonstrations have not been very successful. Here, we propose a plan of experimental research to produce narrow-band biphotons from a hot atomic vapor cell using spontaneous four-wave mixing with electrometrically induced transparency. We aim to generate biphotons with a coherence time of longer than 200 ns and a bandwidth of narrower than 2 MHz. Our systematical investigation will provide the community a clear answer to the question whether a hot atomic vapor cell can be as efficient as the cold atoms for producing narrow-band biphtoton with high quality. Our research will lead to practical applications in quantum communication and quantum information processing. 糾纏光子對，又稱雙光子，已經成為量子光學領域的標準研究工具。近來提出的基於高效光子-原子量子接口的遠距離量子通訊協議，對窄帶（帶寬接近或窄於原子線寬，大約兆赫左右）單光子源提出了極大的需求。在過去幾年裡，雖然用冷原子非線性介質來產生窄帶糾纏光子對已經被證實是非常有效的，但其實驗裝置和操作的複雜度不適合於實用和工程推廣。作為一種替代方案，熱原子蒸氣室簡單易行，然而到目前為止實驗證明均不怎麼成功。在這裡，我們提出了一個基於熱原子蒸氣室中電磁誘導透明四波混頻產生窄帶糾纏光子對的方案。我們旨在產生相干時間超過200納秒和帶寬窄於2兆赫的雙光子。我們系統的研究會有助於給出一個明確的答案，也就是熱原子蒸氣室是否也能如冷原子那樣有效地用於產生高質量的窄帶雙光子。我們的研究成果可以應用在量子通訊和量子信息處理領域。

16301214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301214.value: In this project, we aimed to produce narrow-band entangled photon pairs (biphotons) from a hot atomic vapor cell. We have achieved the following major findings and research outcomce: (1) Bright subnatural-linewidth biphotons from a Doppler-broadened hot atomic vapor cell. We produced time-frequency entangled photon pairs with the world narrowest linewidth (1.9 MHz) and the longest coherence time (94 ns) from a hot 87Rb atomic vapor cell – the best result among this kind of experiments in the world by now. We use on-resonance spontaneous four-wave mixing in a hot paraffin-coated 87Rb vapour cell to produce biphotons with controllable bandwidth (1.9–3.2 MHz) and coherence time (47–94 ns). Our backward phase-matching scheme with spatially separated optical pumping is the key to suppress uncorrelated photons from resonance fluorescence. This result was published on Nature Communications 7, 12783 (2016). Later, by optimizing the system atomic energy scheme and making use of the hollow beam optical pumping, we improved the photon pair rate up to 40,000 pairs per second and the spectral brightness as high as 14,000 s^(-1)MHz(-1) [Appl. Phys. Lett. 110, 161101 (2017)]. The result may lead towards miniature narrowband biphoton sources. This narrow-band biphoton source will be useful in quantum information applications. Representative Publications: [1] Nature Communications 7, 12783 (2016). [2] Appl. Phys. Lett. 110, 161101 (2017) (2) Narrow-band biphotons with polarization-frequency-coupled hyperentanglement. Making use of a frequency shifter and linear optics, we demonstrated the generation of narrow-band biphotons with polarization-frequency-coupled entanglement. By decoupling the hyperentanglement, we further produced frequency-bin entanglement with tunable phase. Our results demonstrated a new approach to control and engineer the quantum state of photon pairs. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. A 91, 043820 (2015). [2] J. Opt. 17, 105201 (2015). (3) Quantum-state purity of heralded single photons produced from frequency-anticorrelated biphotons. Our research clarified a misunderstanding of the quantum-state purity of heralded single photons. It has been commonly believed that the frequency entanglement projects the heralded single photon into a mixed state. We found that this statement is not true. We found that the quantum-state purity in the time-frequency domain depends strongly on the response time uncertainty of the trigger-photon detector that heralds the generation of its paired photon. If the trigger response time is much shorter than the two-photon coherence time, the time-frequency quantum-state purity of heralded single photons approaches unity and the heralded single photon is in a nearly pure state. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. A 92, 043836 (2015).

16301214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301214.value: Flying single photons are basic building blocks for connecting a quantum network, where entanglement plays a crucial role. In order to interact with the atomic nodes (in a photon-atom quantum network) efficiently, the photons are required to have a bandwidth narrower than the atomic natural linewidth. Such kind of narrowband biphotons used to be produced from a cold atom system, which is complicated, space consuming, and expensive. In this research project, making use of backward phase-matching scheme with spatially separated optical pumping technique, we successfully produce bright subnatural linewidth (as low as 1.9 MHz) biphotons with a coherence time up to 94 ns, from a hot 87Rb atomic vapor cell. We further show that these narrow-band biphotons can be used to produce heralded single photons with high quantum-state purity. Our research result proved that narrow-band entangled photon pairs can be produced from in a much simpler process with a much lower cost, brining hope to further advancement of practical photonic quantum communication network.

16301514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301514.value: Crystal melting is ubiquitous in nature, but its microscopic mechanisms are poorly understood. A major challenge is that trajectories of single atoms or molecules can hardly be measured during melting by conventional techniques such as X-ray diffraction, calorimetry and electron microscopy. Colloids are excellent model systems because the micrometer-sized particles can be directly observed by optical video microscopy and their thermal motions can be tracked by image processing. Recently, we have studied the melting of monolayers, thin films and three-dimensional (3D) defect-free crystals by using tunable repulsive microgel spheres. Here, we propose to explore (1) the melting of 3D and thin-film crystals near a single defect, (2) melting in confined geometries by using repulsive microgel spheres, and (3) premelting at crystal surfaces by using novel tunable attractive latex spheres. Defects can dramatically change the melting behaviors, but their effects are often entangled and the single-defect effect can hardly be extracted in molecular crystals. We will locally heat a crystalline region with only one defect so that the single-defect effect on melting can be experimentally measured for the first time. Many open questions can be systematically studied: what are the nucleation precursors and whether they are pinned near the defect? How does the nucleation kinetics change for different types of defects? Melting behaviors may qualitatively change when the system size becomes small, but the atomic nanocrystals do not have well-defined boundary conditions and the microscopic melting kinetics cannot be resolved. To this end, we will study the melting of colloidal crystals confined in small cells with various shapes. To better mimic atoms with attractive interactions, we have developed a method to add tunable attractions between latex spheres. This breakthrough makes surface premelting become measurable because only attractive particles can form crystal-vapor interfaces. In this proposal, we will study surface premelting in 2D and thin-film crystals with single-particle resolution for the first time. A preliminary observation shows a surprising solid-solid transition during the premelting, which provides new challenges to the melting theory. These novel experiments will enable us to study some important open questions in melting with single-particle dynamics. The results can offer direct experimental evidence to the current debates for future refinement of the underlying theory. A better understanding on melting is of fundamental importance in condensed matter physics, and of practical interest for material science, nanotechnology, metallurgy and related industries. 結晶熔化是自然界中普遍存在的现象，但其微觀機理知之甚少。一個主要的挑戰是，單個原子或分子的軌跡幾乎不能由X射線衍射， 比热测量和電子顯微鏡这些常規技術測量。相比之下，膠體是極好的模型系統，因為在微米尺寸的膠體顆粒可以通過光學顯微鏡直接觀察到，其熱運動可以通過圖像 處理進行定量追踪。最近，我們已研究了有具有可調排斥力的微米小球组成的單层晶体，多层晶体和三維無缺陷晶體的熔化。這裡，我們提出了通過使用同样的系统 探討（1）三維和薄膜晶體中單个缺陷附近的熔化行为，（2）小尺寸晶体的熔化行为。 缺陷可顯著地改變它的熔化行為，但分子晶體中多种缺陷 互相影响，只能研究某一缺陷密度下的熔化行为，难以观测单个缺陷如何其影响熔化。我們將局部加熱胶体晶体内部有且只有一個缺陷的区域，使得在單缺陷如何熔 化可以首次通过實驗进行微观观測。許多悬而未决的問題可以被系統地研究，比如：形成液体核之前的先驱结构是什么？它們是否都发生在缺陷附近？不同類型的缺 陷是如何影响形成液体核的过程的？當晶体體積很小，熔化行為可以大大改變，但原子组成的納米晶體受基底和周围环境影响往往没有简单的邊界條件，并且微观尺 度上的熔化動力學無法从实验上分辨。為此，我們將利用胶体晶体研究限定在小盒子中的各種形狀的膠體晶體的熔化。 這些新颖的實驗使我們能夠研究一些熔化过程中的單粒子尺度上的重要問題。从而对目前的一些爭論提供直接的實驗澄清，对熔化基本理論的改進提供实验数据指导。這對凝聚態物理有相當的重要性，对材料學，納米技術，冶金及相關领域也有一定价值。

16301514.label: Realisation of objectives
16301514.value: The objectives are basically well achieved. In particular, the deleted Objective 3 about surface melting turned out to be very fruitful. Objective 1. We measured the melting near a grain boundary and the results are published as part of Nature Communications, 6, 6942 (2015). We obtained experiment results about melting near a single dislocation defect. The new student supported by the grant worked in a more exciting direction about surface melting and published a paper in Nature. Objective 2. We measured the melting of crystals in various small cavities and discovered that a small enough crystal can spontaneously fluctuate between crystal and liquid states. This phenomenon has been conjectured in theory and not observed before. We finished a rough draft, but the student postpone his PhD thesis defense for a few years and went to sell insurances. A new student carried over this project and will obtain more statistics because we are aiming for a top journal about this result. We also measured melting in monolayer 2D crystals [Nature, 531, 485 (2016)] and several-layer thin-film samples [Nature Communications, 8, 14978 (2017), Phys. Rev. X 8, 021045 (2018)] which can also be regarded as confined system in Objective 2. In recent years, we published 8 papers about colloidal crystal melting, including high impact journals Nature, Nature Reviews Materials, Physical Review X, Nature Communications, Advanced Functional Materials, etc. This is the only RGC grant about melting in our group.

16301514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301514.value: How a crystal melt from grain boundaried inside 3D bulk crystal has been rarely studied because it is difficult to look inside the bulk. High-angle grain boundary melting was firstly observed by using a colloidal crystal in 2005 and published as a cover article in the prestigious journal Science. Here we made the first observation of low-angle grain boundary melting in similar colloidal crystals and found that its melting behavior is different. Even below the melting temperature, the surfaces of a crystal could form a thin layer of liquid, a phenomenon known as premelting. It is important in glacier motion, skating, etc., but not very well understood. We achieved the first experimental observation of surface premelting at the single-particle level by using a novel colloidal crystal and found rich phenomena. For example, monolayer and bilayer crystals have distinct melting behaviors because 2D is the critical dimension.

16301614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301614.value: Live cell imaging is a crucial technique to gain better understandings of the mystery of life. In the living context, fluorescent probes are ideal tools for the direct visualization of biological events with high spatial and temporal resolution. Whereas the use of fluorescent proteins and nanoparticles have their advantages, the chemical and photophysical properties of small organic dyes could be deliberately and systematically modulated via the modification of their chemical structures to generate an almost unlimited range of potential applications. Organic fluorogens with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics have demonstrated their potential to be ideal candidates for live cell imaging. Opposite to conventional organic dyes, the AIE luminogens are non-luminescent when molecularly dissolved but highly emissive upon aggregation. As small molecules, the AIE luminogens normally enter cells through diffusion, accumulate in the target location, and generate light emission. Inherently, they possess large Stokes shift (> 100 nm) with appreciable brightness and they are resistant to photo-bleaching and blinking, owing to the formation of aggregates inside the cells. In addition, they are structurally simple and synthetically accessible: the excitation/emission wavelengths as well as the functionalities can be fine-tuned via structural modification. Our previous experiments have proven the feasibility of constructing AIE dyes for specific imaging and tracking mitochondria as well as for mapping intracellular pH in a broad range. In this study, we propose to enrich our AIE library in this area, mainly focusing on the development of AIE dyes for ratiometric, lifetime and photoactivatable imaging. Efforts will be directed towards the design and synthesis of new AIE luminogens with improved photostability, biocompatibility, and signal-to-noise ratio for monitoring the change in intracellular environment and organelle morphologies, evaluating cell viability and vitality, and tracing the physiological activities of living cells in a relatively long period of time. Systematic studies will be carried out to interpret the involved biological processes and their relationship to pathological conditions. It is anticipated that this research project will generate a new and versatile fluorescent toolbox to complement the current development of instrumentations in order to advance the understanding of biological events through visualizing cell structures and functions with high resolution and in an extended time window. 活細胞成像是探索生命奧妙的重要工具。而熒光探針以其在時間和空間上的高分辨率，被認為是實現細胞結構和功能可視化的理想工具。而傳統使用的熒光蛋白和熒光納米顆粒各有優缺點。熒光蛋白可以通過遺傳編碼表達到特定蛋白上，但是每個細胞對熒光蛋白的表達量不均勻的，有的細胞甚至不表達熒光蛋白，因此不適用於定量成像及高通量檢測。而熒光納米顆粒雖然具有很好的光穩定性，它們通常以內吞的形式進入細胞，不能理想地靶向細胞內不同的位點。另一方面，有機小分子染料的化學及物理性質可以通過簡單的合成方法對其結構進行修飾來調控，以配合不同的需要。我們早期實驗證明聚集誘導發光AIE分子是理想的細胞成像材料。 AIE分子通過擴散的方式進入細胞，積聚在目標位置並發出很強的熒光信號。由於聚集體的形成，這類分子對光致漂白和閃爍具有抵抗性，因此適用於長時間觀測細胞內環境或結構的變化。在前期研究的基礎上，本項目將集中於可用於細胞內定量成像探針的開發，包括比率型熒光探針、用於熒光壽命成像的探針及具有光活性的熒光染料。通過分子設計，我們將實現具有良好的光穩定性、生物相容性和高信噪比的探針以用於檢測細胞內環境的變化及細胞器形態的變化，評估細胞的生存力和活力，並追踪活細胞的生理活動。

16301614.label: Realisation of objectives
16301614.value: The purpose of this proposed investigation is to synthesize new luminescent materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics and exploration of their biological applications. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. Fluorescent materials and devices have attracted much attention because of their potential applications in biomedical science and bioengineering. Many luminophores have been prepared but all suffer from drawbacks. One of the most severe problems is that their bright emissions in solutions are often weakened or quenched when they are dispersed in aqueous media or aggregated in living cells. Such aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) has limited their biological applications. In this reporting period, we found that some molecules such as tetraphenylethene and siloles show little to no fluorescence in solution but emit efficiently when aggregated. We termed this phenomenon as aggregation-induced emission (AIE) and such effect is exact opposite of ACQ. Through designed experiments and theoretical calculation, we identified the restriction of intramolecular motion (RIM) as the mechanism of the AIE phenomenon. The RIR mechanism of AIE luminogens (AIEgens) makes them promise as fluorescence turn-on sensors with high sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio for biosensory and imaging applications. Thus, in this project, we have synthesized new AIEgens with different molecular structures and emission colors, particularly those with near infrared-red (NIR) emission (>700 nm) because they can be excited using low-energy light irradiation to minimize photodamage to living bodies. Their longer-wavelength emission can circumvent the spectral overlap with biosubstrate autofluorescence and endow them with high penetration depths, which is advantageous for in vivo deep tissue imaging. These AIEgens can enter cells as isolated molecules or aggregates and by the decoration of various substituents, these AIEgens can endow with different functionalities. For example, the introduction of morpholine group to the molecular structure will impart the resulting AIEgens with lysosome-targeting specificity. Boronic acid unit, on the other hand, will enable the resulting molecules to differentiate dead bacteria from the living ones. Melding biological recognition peptides such as cyclic RGD with AIEgens furnishes AIE bioconjugates for specific detection of integrin αvβ3, a protein playing a critical role in regulating tumor growth and metastasis. Through structural modification, we have successfully developed fluorescent bioprobes based on AIEgens for the specific imaging of plasma membrane, mitochondria, lipid droplets and lysosomes in cells and bacteria. We also prepared conjugates of AIEgens and antibodies and successfully applied them for wash-free imaging of specific cancer cells. Because most of NIR-emissive AIEgens possess a donor-acceptor structure, they also show two-photon or three-photon absorption with large absorption cross-section. Thus, they can be excited by low-energy NIR irradiation to avoid photo-damage to living bodies. Coupled with their long emission wavelengths and high emission efficiency, we have successfully performed three-photon luminescence (3PL) in vivo imaging of mouse brains using strong red-emission AIE nanodots. A clear 3PL from the intravenously injected AIE-dots can reveal the vascular architecture in a mouse brain at a maximum depth of 150 µm. Tiny structures of capillary vessels can also be observed a depth of 300 μm in the mouse brain. This is the first report on the utilization of AIEgen-doped nanoparticles for 3PL in vivo bioimaging. In vivo long-term cell tracking can provide valuable information for the study of tumor cell metastasis and treatments in stem cells. Small organic molecules can enter cells but can easily leak out upon washing. However, AIEgens can easily enter cells as nanoparticles and once aggregated, they cannot be easily washed away. Because of this, we can track tumor cells for 12 days, which is much longer than that of the commercial Qtracker® 655. We have also successfully demonstrated that AIE dots can be used for stem cell tracing for up to 42 days in mice, exhibiting superior in vivo tracking capability compared to the most widely used commercial cell trackers, PKH26 and Qtracker® 655. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a reliable clinical tool for curing superficial tumors. Conventional photosensitizers suffer from long incubation and irradiation times, poor photostability, low selectivity and reduced photosensitizing efficiency. We have constructed an AIEgen-based PDT reagent with mitochondrion-targeting ability. This endows the AIE photosensitizer with high brightness and photostability in image-guided therapy. The mitochondrion-targeting feature of the probe also greatly increases its therapeutic efficiency. This combination of therapeutic and imaging properties enables the monitoring of biological processes in real time during PDT. A safe bioprobe should neither inhibit nor promote cell activity. An MTT assay shows that many AIEgens exert no or minor effects on cell viability. The mice injected with buffer saline or AIE dots through the tail vein showed no notable change in the body weight after seven days. Serum analyses reveal few differences in the activities of enzymes and the amount of blood urea nitrogen between the treated and untreated mice. No pathological abnormalities were observed in the histological analysis of the major organs harvested from the treated mice. Overall, these results suggest that AIEgens and AIE dots possess excellent biocompatibility and are suitable for in vitro and in vivo bioimaging.

16301614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301614.value: In this project, we have synthesized new luminogenic materials with aggregation-induced emission characteristics and have explored their technological applications. The fluorescence turn-on character of AIEgens makes them promising materials for biosensory and imaging applications. Their emission color and organelle specificity can be tuned by introduction of appropriate substituents. The AIEgens with donor-acceptor structures show large two-photon or three-photon absorption with large absorption cross-section. This makes them promising materials for multiphoton imaging, especially for ultra-deep in vivo fluorescence imaging of tissues. Conventional ACQ bioprobes are emissive both before and after cellular uptake, and washing is thus required to remove un-entry dye molecules to improve their noise-to-signal ratio. On the other hand, AIEgens are non-emissive when molecularly dissolved but emit intensely when bound to the target of interest. As such, they can be applied in wash-free biological imaging. This allows a very high image contrast between the stained and un-stained cells. As washing is not required prior to obtaining the confocal microscopic images, the operation time and cost are greatly reduced. Traditional fluorophores are normally used at low concentrations to avoid emission quenching. However, at low concentrations, they have low photostability and are unsuitable for monitoring biological processes. On the contrary, AIEgens show high photostability even at low concentrations. Thus, AIEgens are excellent candidates for real-time monitoring of the dynamics of subcellular organelles. Aside from being wash-free and highly photostable, AIEgens possess other favorable characteristics compared to their ACQ counterparts, including large Stokes shifts, high resolution, high concentration tolerance and suitability for nanoparticle fabrication. Long-term tumor tracking could be achieved by fabricating AIE dots, which show the advantages of large absorptivity, long retention times, high specificity and photostability as well as superior biocompatibility. Some AIEgens can differentiate cancer cells from normal cells. They can generate reactive oxygenic species to kill cancer cells, making AIEgens promising as theranostic systems. As you can see in Part C of this report, 20 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high citation indexes and some are written by invitation. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result

16301614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301614.value: The development of new luminescent materials has allowed us to gain unprecedented knowledge, opening a new avenue to scientific achievement and societal development. In this investigation, new luminogenic materials with aggregation-induced emission characteristics are prepared and have found to be promising materials for biological applications with the merits of bright emission, superb photostability, efficient cellular uptake and retention, and excellent biocompatibility. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the synthesis of new materials. We have placed special emphasis on their working mechanism and structure–property relationship because such information guides the future design of new compounds with enhanced and new properties. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the biological applications of our materials.

16301614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301614.value: The development of new luminescent materials is of fundamental importance and has far-reaching practical implications, as reflected by the award of the Nobel Prize in 2008 and 2014 for the discovery of green fluorescent proteins and the development of a super-resolved fluorescent microscope respectively. Many luminophores such as quantum dots, hybrid nanoparticles and conventional organic dyes have been prepared but all suffer from different drawbacks. In this investigation, new luminogenic materials called aggregation-induced emission luminogens are synthesized and are found to show bright emission, superb photostability, long-term retention and excellent biocompatibility. Such properties enable them to find wide biological applications, such as in vitro and in vivo imaging, biological process monitoring and disease therapy.

16302114.label: Realisation of objectives
16302114.value: We studied the elliptic representations in the framework of harmonic analysis on real reductive Lie groups by the techniques in the theory of Dirac cohomology. We proved that the elliptic representations are precisely the representations with nonzero Dirac index provided the concerned group is connected. We also showed that an irreducible unitary elliptic representation with regular infinitesimal character must be an Aq(lambda)-module for the reductive groups of rational points defined over real numbers. The connection of calculation of Dirac cohomology and the endoscopic transfer factors were also studied in the frame work of L-packets, orbital integrals on regular elliptic integrals and psedu-coefficients of discrete series. We also studied the connection of the Dirac cohomology of the elliptic representations and the Fourier transform of the orbital integrals on regular elliptic elements in terms of K characters. We applied the Dirac cohomology for classification of irreducible unitary representations with regular infinitesimal characters for linear reductive groups.

16302114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302114.value: 1) We determined the Dirac cohomology of cohomologically induced modules and classified tempered representations with nonzero Dirac cohomology. 2) We determined Dirac cohomology of the space of square integrable functions on semisimple Lie groups and apply this result for geometric quantization and construction of models of discrete series representations. 3) We showed that the set of irreducible elliptic representations is the same as the of irreducible representations with nonzero Dirac index and computed their K-characters. 4) We made use of Dirac cohomology to describe the endoscopic transfer of the discrete series. 5) We use Dirac cohomology to classify unitary representations with regular infinitesimal characters.

16302114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302114.value: The results obtained will be applied for understanding the unitary dual (classification of irreducible unitary representations) and for character lifting in connection with the Langlands functoriality.

16302114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302114.value: Understanding irreducible unitary representations and applying it to harmonic analysis on reductive groups is a central problem in representation theory. The recent development of Dirac cohomology has made important impact on understanding and geometric construction of irreducible unitary representations. We have been playing a major role in developing the theory of Dirac cohomology and demonstrating that Dirac cohomology is now an important tool in representation theory. It is in close connection with basic properties and classical results for irreducible admissible representations such as characters, endoscopic transfers and functoriality.

16302214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302214.value: RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) is the enzyme that transcribes the information encoded in DNA into messenger RNA in eukaryotic cells. Pol II is equipped with a proofreading mechanism that can detect mis-incorporated nucleotides and enable subsequent cleavage. Some mis-incorporations due to DNA lesions can be recognized by this proofreading mechanism, while others cannot, thus causing transcriptional mutagenesis that can lead to transcription-related diseases such as cancer. Our proposed studies aim to elucidate mechanisms of Pol II proofreading, which is enabled by the backtracking motion of Pol II along RNA and DNA. Furthermore, we want to understand why certain DNA lesions can escape the backtracking process. In order to dissect how the alteration of chemical interactions due to DNA lesions can impact the backtracking process, we will systematically study a series of DNA lesions including the hydrogen-bond-deficient Thymine analogs (F and I), bulky Cytosine analogs (5mC and 5fC), and DNA damage on guanine (8-oxoG and O6-meG). This will allow us to investigate the role of electrostatic interactions and steric effect in backtracking because the selected DNA modifications cover a wide range of different sizes and ability to form hydrogen bonds. The proposed studies will provide foundation for understanding the mechanisms for certain DNA lesions to escape the Pol II’s proofreading mechanism. We propose to use molecular dynamics simulations to study these processes because molecular dynamics simulations can model the dynamics through the atomic level interactions, while current experimental techniques are inadequate to describe the dynamic transition of backtracking in sufficient details. In order to overcome the timescale gap between experiments and simulations, we will apply the algorithms we have developed to construct Markov State Models to extract long timescale dynamics from many short simulations. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate predictions that will be tested by experimental collaborators, and these experiments will further help refine our theoretical models to achieve a detailed understanding of the Pol II’s proofreading mechanism. 16302214.label: Realisation of objectives
16302214.value: All four objectives of the proposal have been well achieved. For objective 1: We have successfully completed this objective to elucidate mechanisms of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) proofreading, which is enabled by the backtracking motion of Pol II and cleavage of mis-incorporated nucleotide. In eukaryotic cells, Pol II can detect and cleave mis-incorporated nucleotides in a proofreading mechanism enabled by the backtracking of the enzyme. The backtracking is thus a critical component to maintain the high fidelity of gene transcription, but its dynamic mechanism at molecular level remains largely a mystery. We successfully revealed dynamics underlying Pol II backtracking at millisecond timescale and in all-atom details. To achieve this, we constructed Markov State Models (MSMs) from many short molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We found that the Pol II backtracking (from pre-translocation to the one-nucleotide-backtracked state) occurs in a stepwise model, where the fraying of the terminal RNA nucleotide is a prerequisite step for backtracking. Our simulations identified an important role for the Bridge Helix by serving as a critical checkpoint for the fraying motion through its highly conserved residue T831. This residue is able to sense the weakened base pairing due to mis-incorporation and further promote the fraying and subsequent backtracking. We also found that the dynamics of backtracking with mis-incorporation is significantly slower than that of normal forward translocation upon incorporating a matched nucleotide. These simulation predictions regarding the role of T831 have been further validated by our site-directed mutagenesis and cleavage assays. These results were published in Nature Communications, 7, 11244, (2016). After backtracking, Pol II can further cleave the mis-incorporated nucleotide to complete its proofreading function. However, the molecular mechanism for RNA cleavage reaction catalysed by RNA Pol II is poorly understood. We combined ab initio quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics simulations (QM/MM) and biochemical cleavage assays to show that Pol II utilises downstream phosphate oxygen to activate the attacking nucleophile in hydrolysis, while the newly formed RNA 3’-end is protonated through active-site water without a defined general acid. Our suggested mechanism, in which the phosphate Rp-oxygen serves as the general base rather than any Pol II residues, suggests that Pol II compartmentalizes its backtracking (with conformational change highly reliant on Pol II residues to recognize NTP mis-incorporation) and cleavage mechanisms (Pol II independent reaction mechanism) in order to coordinate these two functions. Our study therefore provides important new insights into understanding how RNA is cleaved by RNA pol II and structural basis on how it performs proofreading by simultaneous backtracking and intrinsic cleavage (Nature Catalysis, Accepted, (2018)). For objective 2: In this objective, we aim to investigate how hydrogen-bond-deficient analogs of nucleobases could alter Pol II’s ability to detect mis-incorporations, backtrack and cleave the mis-incorporations. To investigate how Pol II backtracking and cleavage respond to hydrogen bond deficient modification, we explored and showed that the deaza modification on the 7’ position of Guanine base does not impact Pol II’s backtracking and cleavage rate. These results on the N7-modification of the base indicates that nucleobase does not directly involved in the cleavage reactions of Pol II. In addition, we show that thiol substitution of Rp-oxygen of the terminal nucleotide substantially slows down the cleavage upon backtracking, further confirming that it is not the nucleobase but the terminal nucleotide phosphate that plays a major role in Pol II’s intrinsic cleavage (Nature Catalysis, Accepted, (2018)). In addition, we have set up MD simulations of thymine modifications F and I by deriving electrostatic force field parameters via fitting to Quantum Mechanics calculations. However, we could not observe any noticeable difference between F and I systems, suggesting that standard force fields with fixed atomic charges are insufficient to describe stronger base stacking effects due to the presence of the iodine atom. Nevertheless, based on our study of the cleavage of the backtracked nucleotide (Nature Catalysis, Accepted, (2018)), we expect that hydrogen-bond-deficient analogs such as the nonpolar analogs of Thymine F may lead to deficiency of base paring and promote the backtracking, but would not have substantial impact on the subsequent cleavage of mis-incorporated nucleotides. To put our studies of backtracking and cleavage in the context of the overall Pol II elongation cycle (including other steps such as translocation and pyrophosphate ion release), We combined the individual steps into a five-state kinetic network model to study the dynamics of overall nucleotide addition cycle (Accounts of Chemical Research, 49 (4), 687–694, (2016) and Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol, 49,54,(2018)). During this process, we have also built a structural model with completed transcription bubble of Pol II to study the NTP loading pathway (PLoS. Comp. Bio., 11(7), e100435, (2015)). For objective 3: In this objective, we aim to investigate how cytosine modifications produced in its demethylation pathway (such as 5fC and 5caC) may impact Pol II’s ability in both backward- (backtracking) and forward-translocation. We have fully addressed this objective by performing large-scale MD simulations (accumulated to tens of microseconds) to compare the difference of dynamics of wildtype Pol II, 5mC, and 5fC systems. Based on MD simulations, we built MSMs to study the mechanism for Pol II translocation with the 5caC base modification. To efficiently build MSMs, we applied the time-lagged independent component analysis to help choose slowest collective variables and further group MD conformations into metastable conformational states. In comparison to the wildtype Pol II, the translocation of 5caC system is significantly slowed down in the post-translocation region due to the presence of several intermediate conformational states. These intermediate conformations are mainly stabilized by the hydrogen bonds formed between carboxylic acid group on 5caC and Q531 on fork loop 3 of Pol II’s Rpb2 subunit. These newly formed interactions may not only slow down the forward translocations, but also with the potential to facilitate the backtracking. Our model provides novel structural dynamic insights in how Pol II is arrested by epigenetic modifications (Konovalov et. al. “Elucidating mechanisms of translocation for methylation derivatives of Cytosine”, manuscript attached). In order to study Pol II’s translocation in the presence of methylation derivatives of Cytosine, we have also developed a general protocol (WIREs Comput Mol Sci., 8:e1343, (2017) and several new algorithms (J. Comput. Chem., 38(3):152-160, (2017), J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017), J. Chem. Phys.,149, 072337, (2018)) for constructing MSMs to investigate functional conformational changes. For objective 4: We have performed MD simulations and biochemical experiments to investigate how the mismatched rA:8OG base pair is stabilized both in the active site of Pol II and in the +1 site. Using the in vitro transcription assay, we confirm that Pol II supports both adenine and cytosine incorporation opposite 8OG and further elucidate its molecular mechanisms using MD simulations. We systematically simulate all possible (syn/anti) conformations of 8OG/dG paired with either matching cytosine or a mismatched adenine ribonucleotide (Eighty 50-ns MD simulations for 16 systems in total). We show that for RNA Pol II to bypass 8OG DNA damage with erroneous incorporation of adenine, 8OG must assume the uncommon syn conformation before entering the active site due to instability of A:8OG (anti) both in the active site and in the +1 site. Our simulations elucidate molecular mechanisms of how 8OG DNA damage induces transcription errors by RNA Polymerase II (J. Biol., Chem., submitted, (2018)).

16302214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302214.value: RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) is responsible for transcribing DNA into mRNA in eukaryotic cells. To maintain high accuracy of transcription, Pol II has a proofreading mechanism that can detect mis-incorporated nucleotides and enable subsequent cleavage. Transcriptional mutagenesis especially those caused by DNA lesions can lead to transcription-related diseases such as cancer. With the support of this grant, we have elucidated molecular mechanisms of Pol II’s proofreading, which is enabled by the backtracking motion of Pol II followed by the cleavage of mis-incorporated nucleotides. Based on the protocol we developed to construct Markov State Models (MSMs) built from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations (WIREs Comput Mol Sci., 8:e1343, (2017), we found that the Pol II backtracking occurs in a stepwise fashion. We further identified a highly conserved Pol II residue T831 that serves as a checkpoint for Pol II to probe the mis-incorporation, promote the fraying of terminal nucleotide, and further lead to backtracking (Nature Communications, 7, 11244, (2016)). After backtracking, Pol II can further cleave the mis-incorporated nucleotide by utilizing downstream phosphate oxygen to activate the attacking nucleophile in hydrolysis. Results from our QM/MM simulations and biochemical cleavage assays confirm that the phosphate Rp-oxygen serves as the general base rather than any Pol II residues. These results provide important new insights into Pol II’s proofreading mechanisms, as they indicate that Pol II compartmentalizes its backtracking (with conformational change highly reliant on Pol II residues to recognize mis-incorporation) and cleavage (Pol II independent reaction mechanism) in order to coordinate these two functions (Nature Catalysis, Accepted, (2018)). Furthermore, we systematically studied a series of DNA lesions including the hydrogen-bond-deficient modifications on nucleobases, bulky Cytosine analogs such as 5fC and 5caC (Konovalov et. al. Manuscript attached), and 8-oxo-G DNA damage (J. Biol., Chem., submitted, (2018)). Our studies provide the foundation for understanding molecular mechanisms Pol II’s proofreading and how certain DNA modifications bypass this proofreading mechanism. Finally, we also place the Pol II’s backtracking and cleavage in context the completed elongation cycle and developed kinetic network model to study the dynamics of overall transcriptional dynamics (Accounts of Chemical Research, 49 (4), 687–694, (2016), and Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol, 49,54, (2018)) Due to the above findings, the PI has been invited to give talks in prestigious international conferences. Two Ph. D and one M. Phil. students partially supported by this grant have successfully obtained their degrees.

16302214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302214.value: DNA damage that can escape the proofreading mechanisms of Pol II may lead to transcriptional mutagenesis and further cause human diseases such as cancer. Supported by this grant, we have successfully elucidated dynamic mechanisms of two critical steps in Pol II’s proofreading scheme: Backtracking upon the mis-incorporation, and the subsequent cleavage of the mis-incorporated nucleotide. We also systematically studied the effects of various DNA modifications on Pol II’s proofreading mechanisms. We anticipate that our results could be easily extended to study other DNA damage causing mutagenesis, and in the long term facilitate rational drug design for transcription-related human diseases. During our studies, we also developed a protocol to construct MSMs from large-scale MD simulations to investigate dynamics of Pol II’s conformational changes. We expect that these computational algorithms hold great potential to be widely applied to study other important functional conformational changes of biological macromolecules.

16302214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302214.value: In eukaryotic cells, RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) transcribes the information encoded in DNA into messenger RNA. To achieve high accuracy of transcription, Pol II is equipped with a proofreading mechanism that can detect errors (mismatched nucleotides) and further correct them (cleavage mis-incorporated nucleotides). We combined computer simulations (MD simulations) and statistical mechanics models (MSMs) to elucidate molecular mechanisms of Pol II’s proofreading mechanism. We found that Pol II can detect mis-incorporations with the help of a highly conserved Threonine residue and further pause the transcription by inducing a backward motion (backtracking). After backtracking, Pol II can cleave the mis-incorporated nucleotide via hydrolysis, where it utilizes downstream phosphate oxygen to activate the attacking nucleophile. We also systematically studied the impact of various DNA lesions on Pol II’s backtracking and proofreading mechanism. Our studies greatly advance the understanding of molecular mechanisms underlying Pol II’s proofreading, and how certain DNA lesions bypass this proofreading mechanism.

16302614.label: Project Objectives
16302614.value: Our first objective is to develop and optimize sample preparation protocols and instrumentation settings for generating tandem mass spectra of intact glycopeptides and deglycosylated peptides. This includes incorporating and perfecting existing methods of glycopeptide digestion, enrichment and separation, to reduce the mixtures into manageable complexity. Moreover, the settings for performing the LC-MS experiment will be optimized systematically to produce tandem mass spectra of glycopeptides with the desirable characteristics for identification with spectral library searching. Our second objective is to build spectral libraries of intact glycopeptides using a glycopeptide fragmentation pattern prediction tool, MassAnalyzer, and to extend our spectral library searching software, SpectraST, for intact glycopeptide identification. An automated computational work-flow with comparable sophistication and throughput to search engines used in proteomics will be developed. This includes optimization of the similarity scoring function, rigorous statistical validation, data visualization, as well as integration of the software into existing data analysis pipelines to provide support of different mass spectrometers and computational platforms. Our third objective is to validate our method, first using standard purified glycoproteins, and then using complex samples. The sensitivity and accuracy of our method for glycopeptide identification can be established using purified glycoproteins with known glycan structures injected at known concentrations.

16302614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302614.value: Proteomics, the systematic and high-throughput identification of all proteins in a biological system, has advanced rapidly recently. Technologically, proteomics is dependent upon the now ubiquitious liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument. Typically, peptides from digested protein samples are separated by chromatography and fragmented in the mass spectrometer, yielding tandem mass (MS/MS) spectra that record the characteristic fragmentation patterns of peptides. This information can then be used to deduce the peptide sequences by computational methods. The capability to detect and quantify thousands of proteins directly in a complex mixture has revolutionized life science research. One of the most important frontiers in proteomics is the elucidation of protein glycosylations, the most prevalent and complex post-translational modification. Due to the wide variety of possible glycan structures and modification sites, the heterogeneity of glycoforms at each modified site, and the relative lack of knowledge in protein glycosylation, this challenge remains intractable by state-of-the-art proteomics methods. Currently, glycoproteins must still be purified by painstaking biochemical methods first and characterized in small numbers, typically employing mass spectrometry. Moreover, MS/MS spectra that capture the fragmentation patterns of glycans and glycopeptides are still often interpreted in a low-throughput manner, with significant manual intervention. The goal of this proposed project is to develop an integrated experimental and computational work-flow to profile intact glycopeptides in complex biological samples. The deliverables of the project include two inter-dependent components. The first is an experimental strategy that preferentially targets glycoproteins for analysis, and decouples the problems of glycan structure determination and site localization to simplify the subsequent data analysis. The second is the requisite computational method to analyze the mass spectrometry data effectively and efficiently without human intervention. Experimentally, we plan to (i) optimize fractionation and enrichment techniques to maximize the sensitivity and simplify the mixture for analysis, and (ii) perform separate and parallel LC-MS analyses of intact glycopeptides and deglycosylated peptides to facilitate the interpretation of the data. Computationally, a novel spectral library-based approach will be developed to (i) use spectrum prediction to build spectral libraries of possible glycopeptides defined through a traditional proteomic analysis of the deglycosylated peptides, (ii) search these libraries for efficient identification of the intact glycopeptides, and (iii) anticipate potential ambiguous identifications and trigger multi-level tandem mass spectrometry selectively to resolve ambiguities. This proposed project, if successful, will deliver the first truly high-throughput profiling method for glycoproteomics that can produce site-specific information of protein glycosylation at the systems level. 蛋白質組學旨在有系統地和高通量地鑑定生物系統中所有的蛋白質，最近有迅速的發展。技術上，蛋白質組學取決於現已普遍的液相色譜 - 質譜（LC-MS）儀器。通常情況下，此技術可從消化的蛋白質樣品所得的肽，通過色譜質譜儀中分離並碎裂，得到串聯質譜（MS / MS），當中記錄了肽的特徵碎片圖案。通過計算方法，這個圖案可以用來推算肽序列。這能直接在複雜生物樣品裡檢測和定量數千個蛋白質的技術，已經徹底改變了生命科學的研究。 蛋白質組學其中一個最重要的前沿是糖蛋白質的鑑定。糖基化是最普遍的和最複雜的蛋白翻譯後修飾，但蛋白質糖基化的知識是相對缺乏的。由於聚醣結構和修飾位點有很繁多的可能性，在每個修改飾位點亦存在異質性，這一挑戰仍然難以最先進的蛋白質組學方法處理。目前，糖蛋白仍必須通過艱苦的生化方法先提純，再採用質譜法逐一分析。此外，聚醣和糖肽的串聯質譜譜圖仍然必須以低通量的人工方法解釋。 此項目的目標是開發一個綜合實驗和計算方法的流程，來直接從複雜生物樣品中鑑定完整的糖肽。該項目的成果包含兩個相互依存的組成部分。其一是實驗策略，針對糖蛋白進行液相色譜 - 質譜分析，把聚醣結構確定和飾位點定位的問題分開處理，從而簡化後續的數據分析。其二計算方法，能有效和高效地分析質譜數據，而無需人工干預。在實驗策略方面，我們計劃在（一）優化分餾和濃縮的技術來逹至最大靈敏度和特异性，以及（二）實踐平行的液相色譜 - 質譜分析，來分別鑑定完整糖肽和去糖的肽，以便數據的解釋。在計算方法方面，我們將發展一個新的基於譜庫技術的方法，其中（一）先以傳統蛋白質組學分析去糖基化肽來介定可能的糖肽，再使用串聯質譜預測方法來建立涵蓋所有可能糖肽的譜庫，（二）搜索此譜庫，有效的識別完整糖肽，及（三）預測可有模糊解釋的情況，選擇性地觸發多級串聯質譜來辨識。 此項目將提供充首個真正的高通量的糖蛋白質分析方法，可以在系統層面逹至糖蛋白質聚醣結構和修飾位點的全分析。

16302614.label: Realisation of objectives
16302614.value: The captioned project has been completed with full realization of the objectives. Objective 1 Our first objective is to develop and optimize sample preparation protocols and instrumentation settings for generating tandem mass spectra of intact glycopeptides and deglycosylated peptides. This includes incorporating and perfecting existing methods of glycopeptide digestion, enrichment and separation, to reduce the mixtures into manageable complexity. Moreover, the settings for performing the LC-MS experiment will be optimized systematically to produce tandem mass spectra of glycopeptides with the desirable characteristics for identification with spectral library searching. This objective has been completed and the outcome has been described in the Interim Progress Report. Namely, we worked out the glycopeptide enrichment and LC-MS analysis protocol by adapting and optimizing existing methods. This was detailed in the paper in Analytica Chimica Acta. Objective 2 Our second objective is to build spectral libraries of intact glycopeptides using a glycopeptide fragmentation pattern prediction tool, MassAnalyzer, and to extend our spectral library searching software, SpectraST, for intact glycopeptide identification. This objective has been largely accomplished and the result published in Analytica Chimica Acta, and the predicted spectral library and software released for the community to use. In brief, given glycoprotein sequences as input, the tool enumerates all possible N-glycopeptide structures (from a database of 500+ known N-glycan structures), and predicts the fragment ion spectra computationally. Indistinguishable spectra (all due to glycan isomerism) were clustered and merged to properly reflect the ambiguity, resulting in 381 distinct clusters. These spectra are compiled into a spectral library by SpectraST, and the search algorithm was fine-tuned to match these spectra effectively. We also developed a method to produce an error estimate for a glycopeptide match by using a known non-glycoprotein to generate “decoys” to fit the negative score distribution, so that the method can be used in the case of mixtures. Since the Interim Progress Report, we have spent some time rewriting the search engine, SpectraST, to make it easier and more systematic to encode glycan structures and to annotate glycan fragments in the predicted spectra, together with some performance enhancements. A script for producing plots to visualize the spectral matches was also included. The code-base has been updated in the repository. (SpectraST belongs to the open-source Trans-Proteomic Pipeline suite, which is available online at https://sourceforge.net/projects/sashimi/.) As mentioned in the Interim Progress Report, significant development in mass spectrometry technology that makes it more straightforward to obtain the peptide sequence of the intact glycopeptide, without a parallel LC-MS run on the deglycosylated peptides as we proposed. (The advent of the Thermo Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer, which can obtain two MS2/3 spectra at different collision energies at once, and to a lesser extent, the improvement in scan speeds of mass analyzers in general, could make it possible to determine both the glycan structure and the peptide sequence in a single run without much loss in sensitivity.) Although we were not able to identify a collaborative partner to acquire data on these newer machines, our effort in integrating our software with existing data analysis pipeline should allow Trans-Proteomic Pipeline users to integrate an “open modification” sequence database search (e.g. by MSFragger) of a higher-collision energy scan with our method to determine the glycan structure. At least one recent publication has validated this approach (Z. An et al, Biomed. Res. Int., 1564136, 2018) with data, although they implemented their own software and did not use our tool. Objective 3 Our third objective (revised at the beginning of the project due to partial funding) is to validate our method. This has been accomplished as part of Objective 2 and such validation was included in the Analytica Chimica Acta publication to prove that the computational method works. Using human transferrin as a standard, we validated the method by confirming the similarity of the predicted and manually verified experimental spectra, as well as the ability of the search engine to detect glycopeptides from a background of noise spectra and non-glycopeptides. Our method was found to outperform GlycoPep Grader, another published tool for glycopeptide identification from MS/MS that does not make use of a library. With our tool, we were able to perform a site-specific N-glycosylation profile of human transferrin, which agreed with the literature. To demonstrate the utility of the tool, we also attempted a site-specific N-glycosylation profiling on human acetylcholinesterase, an important protein in the synapse, for the first time.

16302614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302614.value: The major research outcome of this project was the development of a computational method for direct analysis of intact glycopeptides by LC-MS/MS by a spectral library-based approach. The method has been validated with data, and implemented in a readily usable workflow. Another important outcome of the project was the training of two researchers in glycoproteomics, Dr. Peggy Pei-Jing Pai and Dr. Yingwei Hu. Dr. Pai has learned high-throughput profiling skills to accompany her traditional analytical chemistry training, and made contributions in several other projects. Dr. Hu worked on the computational methodology, which was briefly discussed in his PhD thesis, and stayed on for postdoctoral training to validate the method more thoroughly, complete the publication and improve the software. Moreover, he has since continued on in glycoproteomics research as a postdoctoral scientist in Johns Hopkins University, where he is key developer of GPQuest 2.0, another software for glycopeptide analysis.

16302614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302614.value: In the process of validating our computational method (Objectives 2 and 3), we invented a novel error estimation strategy, which we mentioned in passing in the paper but has since received increased attention by researchers. As no reasonable method exists for generating “decoy” glycopeptide spectra, we proposed a strategy that introduce decoy query spectra (as opposed to library spectra) that cannot possibly be correctly matched to the library. The premise is that all false matches are essentially samples of the score distribution of incorrect matches, regardless of how the false matches were generated. Unlike the traditional target-decoy strategy, which uses the same query data and thus limits the number of decoy matches that it can generate, we can obtain a much larger sample of such false matches from searching other comparable data (not from the experiment in question). Theoretically, this “Big Data” approach of learning about the incorrect score distribution from a huge amount of data should give us more reliable error estimates. This idea is now being pursued in the wider context of proteomics. Although it is an unintended by-product outside the scope of the proposal, it is a promising avenue to greater impact in the proteomics field at large.

16302614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302614.value: Proteomics, the systematic and high-throughput identifcation of all proteins in a biological system, has advanced rapidly in recently years. One of the most important frontier in proteomics is the elucidation of protein glycosylations, the most prevalent and complex post-translational modification on proteins. Due to the wide variety of possible glycan structures and modification sites, the heterogeneity of glycoforms at each modified site, and our relative lack of knowledge in protein glycosylation in general, this challenge remains intractable by state-of-the-art proteomics methods. This research project aimed to develop an integrated experimental and computational work-flow to profile intact glycopeptides in complex biological samples. The approach entails the enumeration of all possible glycopeptides, defined by peptide sequences as well as known glycan structures, the prediction of their fragmentation patterns, and the searching of these predicted spectra by an adapted mass spectral library search engine. This method was the first to employ a spectral library-based approach to achieve site-specific glycopeptide profiling in a high-throughput manner.

16303014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303014.value: Ordinary band insulators cannot conduct electricity due to the presence of a band gap and it takes energy larger than the band gap to excite electrons in the material. Recently, new types of band insulators, called topological insulators, have been discovered. Topological insulators have a band gap in the bulk, similar to ordinary band insulators, such that exciting electrons in the bulk costs finite energy. However, topological insulators support conducting surface states and electric currents can be driven by an arbitrary small electric field. Moreover, these gapless surface states are topologically protected in the sense that they cannot be removed by perturbations, which respect certain symmetries and do not close the bulk energy gap. Recently, it was realized that some superconductors, called topological superconductors, possess bulk single-particle excitation band gap and support gapless excitation modes on their surfaces. The zero energy surface modes of these topological superconductors are called Majorana fermions. A Majorana fermion is an exotic particle, which may have applications in quantum computation. The study of both topological insulators and superconductors is now one of the central topics in condensed matter physics. In the past year, more topological phases, such as quantum anomalous Hall insulators and topological crystalline insulators, have been discovered theoretically and experimentally. At the same time, there are also important developments in topological phases, which are nodal in the bulk but still support protected surface states. These include Weyl semi-metals, 3D Dirac semi-metals and nodal topological superconductors. In recent studies, the PI and collaborators pointed out that certain fully gapped topological superconductors can be used to generate spin-polarized and correlated spin-polarized currents. These are due to new phenomena that the PI and collaborators call Majorana induced selective equal spin Andreev reflections and resonant crossed Andreev reflections. These findings can have an important impact on the applications of topological superconductors in spintronics. In the proposal, we would like to extend the study of possible spintronic applications to new topological phases, including new non-superconducting topological phases and nodal topological phases. We propose to study: 1) Giant spin-polarized currents induced by nodal topological superconductors, 2) Spintronic applications of 2D topological crystalline Chern insulators, 3) Giant spin current carried by the surface states of Weyl semi-metals, 4) Surface state properties and magnetic impurity effects on topological 3D Dirac material surfaces. 常規能帶絕緣體不導電是因為存在能隙，所以激活它裏面的電子需要大於此能隙的能量。最近，人們發現了壹種叫拓撲絕緣體的新型絕緣體。從主體的能隙這方面來講，這種拓撲絕緣體和常規的絕緣體類似，所以激活主體中的電子需要相當的能量。然而，拓撲絕緣體裏存在導電的表面態，所以任意小的電場就可以產生電流。 而且這些沒有能隙的表面態是被拓撲學機制保護的，也就是說它們不會被擾動破壞，只要這種擾動不破壞一定的對稱性，也不導致能隙消失。 最近，人們意識到，一些被稱作拓撲超導體的超導體，在主體具有單粒子激發能隙並且在表面支持無能隙的激發模式。這些超導體的零能量表面模式被稱作馬約拉納費米子。馬約拉納費米子是一種奇異的粒子，它在量子計算中具有廣泛的應用。對拓撲絕緣體和拓撲超導體的研究是凝聚態物理的中心課題之一。 去年，更多的拓撲相，例如量子反常霍爾絕緣體和拓撲晶格絕緣體，都在理論上和實驗上被發現。同時，還有很多重要的拓撲相，它們主體內有結點但仍能支持被保護的表面態。這些包括外爾半金屬，三維狄拉克半金屬和結點拓撲超導體。 在最近的研究里，項目負責人和合作者指出，特定的有能隙的拓撲超導體可以用於產生自旋極化且關聯的電流。這些都源於一些新的現象，它們被項目負責人和合作者稱作馬拉多納導致的選擇性等自旋安德烈夫反射和共振交互安德烈夫反射。這些發現可以對拓撲超導體在自旋電子學中的應用產生重要影響。 在這個方案中，我們將對可能的自旋電子學的應用擴展到新的拓撲相，包括新的非超導的拓撲相和結點拓撲相。我們提議去研究：1）結點拓撲超導體產生的大自旋極化電流，2）拓撲晶格陳絕緣體的自旋電子學應用，3）外爾半金屬中表面態攜帶的大自旋電流，4）三維狄拉克材料的表面態性質以及磁性雜質在其中的效應。
