16303014.value: During this report period, the PI and collaborators have finished more than 10 manuscripts to address the proposed objectives. Objective 1: Giant spin-polarised currents induced by nodal topological superconductors. The manuscripts are: 1. Generating Giant Spin Currents Using Nodal Topological Superconductors Noah F. Q. Yuan, Yao Lu, James J. He, K. T. Law Phys. Rev. B 95, 195102 (2017). In this work, we show that a superconductor with Dresselhaus spin orbit coupling can be turned into a nodal topological superconductor with large number of Majorana modes residing on the edge of the sample. A giant spin current can be injected into a nodal topological superconductor, using a normal paramagnetic lead, through a large number of zero energy Majorana fermions at the superconductor edge. The giant spin current is caused by the selective equal spin Andreev reflections (SESAR) induced by Majorana fermions. In each SESAR event, a pair of electrons with certain spin polarization are injected into the nodal topological superconductor, even though the pairing in the bulk of the nodal superconductor is spin-singlet s-wave. We further explain the origin of the spin current by showing that the pairing correlation at the edge of a nodal topological superconductor is predominantly equal spin-triplet at zero energy. 2.Magnetic Field Driven Nodal Topological Superconductivity in Monolayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Wen-Yu He, Benjamin T. Zhou, James J. He, Ting Zhang, K. T. Law Communications Physics volume 1, 40 (2018). [Note: The GRF grant is acknowledged in the arXiv version (arXiv:1604.02867) but somehow omitted in the published version]. Recently, the PI and experimental collaborators discovered a type of two-dimensional superconductors called Ising superconductors. Ising superconductors possess the so called Ising spin orbit couplings (SOC) which pin electron spins to the out-of-plane directions. The Ising SOC can strongly enhance the in-plane upper critical fields H_c2 of the Ising superconductors. These works are published in: a. Science 350, 1353 (2015). (Two Dimensional Ising Superconductivity in Gated MoS2) b. Nature Physics 12, 139-143 (2016). (Evidence of Ising pairing in superconducting NbSe2 atomic layers) In this manuscript, we proposed that when the applied in-plane magnetic field is smaller than the H_c2 but higher than the Pauli limit, the Ising superconductor becomes a nodal topological superconductor. This nodal topological can be use to induce giant spin currents. 3. Proximity effect and Ising superconductivity in superconductor/transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures Ryohei Wakatsuki, K. T. Law arXiv:1604.04898. The PI and collaborator also proposed a way to realise nodal topological superconductors using transition metal dichalcogenides/s-wave superconductor heterostructures. 16303014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303014.value: In this project, we studied theoretical how to generate spin current using nodal topological materials. This work provides guidance for experimentalists to explore new ways of generating large spin current. We have also studied how to generate nodal topological phases in specific materials such as in NbSe2. This work also provides a foundation for the further study of spin-orbit coupling effects in topological materials. In the near future, the PI will study materials with different lattice structures (as a result have different spin-orbit coupling). We will study how to make use of these different types of spin-orbit coupling to generate topological phases. We hope that our predictions can be tested experimentally in the near future.

16303114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303114.value: The goal of this project is to develop and apply efficient numerical methods for solving elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs) defined on hypersurfaces. PDEs defined on interfaces or surfaces arise in many fields in science and engineering. For example, in image processing or computer graphics, one might try to remove noise or to regularize a surface using variational methods which might result in solving a degenerated elliptic PDE. Or, in the field of material sciences, the growth of crystals is seriously influenced by the concentration of certain chemicals on the interface separating the crystal phase and the liquid phase, and such concentration can be numerically modeled by the solution to an elliptic diffusion PDE. In this project, we propose to develop novel and flexible numerical methods for efficient computing and inverting various elliptic operators defined on manifolds. On the surface, we also propose to develop various efficient operations for surface representation. In the first part of the project, the investigator will develop and analyze new Laplace-Beltrami solvers based on the PI's previous work on the Grid Based Particle Method (GBPM) and a new Cell Based Particle Method (CBPM) for numerical representation of interfaces. In the second part of the project, we generalize and extend several numerical approaches for solving the eikonal equation. We solve this degenerated elliptic nonlinear PDE to obtain the viscosity solution by a fast sweeping method based on the Lax-Friedrichs numerical Hamiltonian. We study the diffusion map on manifold to a noisy GBPM/CBPM data set and use the techniques to regularize big data in high dimensional space. We also propose to study numerically the stability of various algorithms in computing the eigenfunctions of the Schrodinger operator defined on surfaces. Based on these results, we propose to study some related inverse problems related to shape optimization. The outcome from this proposal should provide an alternative to other numerical methods in various applications and is important to many disciplines, including crystal growth modelings, surface regularization in image processing and computer graphics, high frequency asymptotic solution to surface wave propagations in seismic and geophysics, multiphase flows with surfactants, and nanostructures design. 本項目的目標是發展和應用有效的數值方法解決定義在超曲面上的橢圓偏微分方程。定義在界面和曲面上的偏微分方程會出現在科學和工程的很多領域。比如,在圖像處理和計算機圖形學中,我們可能會使用變分法來去除圖像中的噪聲或正則化一個曲面,這可能會導致我們要解一個退化的橢圓偏微分方程。或者,在材料科學領域,晶體的增長會受到分佈在晶相和液相的分離界面上的化學物質濃度的嚴重影響,化學物質的這種濃度分佈可以通過橢圓擴散方程的求解來數值模擬。 在本項目中,我們計劃發展新穎和靈活的數值方法,這些方法可以有效地計算流形上的橢圓算子和對流形上的橢圓算子求逆。對曲面而言,我們也計劃發展一些有效的運算來更好地表示曲面。在項目的第一部分裡,研究者會基於之前在GBPM和最近的CBPM對曲面的數值表示方面的所做的工作,發展和分析新的Laplace-Beltrami求解方法。在項目的第二部分裡,我們推廣和延伸了解Eikonal方程的一些數值方法。我們是基於Lax-Friedrichs數值Hamiltonian,採用fast sweeping方法求解這個退化的非線性橢圓偏微分方程,得到了粘性解。我們研究了有噪聲的GBPM/CBPM數據集對應的流形上的擴散映射 (diffusion map),並且使用這種技術來正則化高維空間中的大數據。對於定義在曲面上的薛定諤算子,我們也計劃研究用以計算它的特徵函數的不同算法的數值穩定性。基於這些結果,我們計劃研究與形狀優化相關的相應反問題。這個計劃得到的結果可以作為應用中的其他數值方法的一種替代性的選擇,並且在許多學科中都會發揮重要作用,包括晶體增長的模擬,圖像處理和計算機圖形學中的曲面正則化,地震學和地球物理學中曲面波傳播的高頻漸進解求解,加入表面活性劑的多相流模擬,納米結構設計等等。

16303114.label: Realisation of objectives
16303114.value: Objective 1. The PI and a PhD student submitted a recent work [wanleuzha18]. We proposed a new and simple discretization, named the Modified Virtual Grid Difference (MVGD), for numerical approximation of the Laplace-Beltrami (LB) operator on manifolds sampled by point clouds. The key observation was that both the manifold and a function defined on it can both be parametrized in a local Cartesian coordinate system and approximated using least squares. Based on the above observation, we first introduced a local virtual grid with a scale adapted to the sampling density centered at each point. Then we proposed a modified finite difference scheme on the virtual grid to discretize the LB operator. The new discretization provides more diagonal dominance to the resulting linear system and improves its conditioning. Objective 2. Published in [wonleu15], we proposed a computational efficient yet simple numerical algorithm to solve the surface eikonal equation on general implicit surfaces. We first approximated the solution to the surface eikonal equation by the Euclidean weighted distance function defined in a tubular neighbourhood of the implicit surface, and then applied the efficient fast sweeping method to numerically compute the corresponding viscosity solution. Unlike some other embedding methods, our approach allows $h = O(Delta x)$. This implies that the total number of grid points in the computational tube is optimal and is given by $O(Delta x^{1-d})$ for a co-dimensional one surface in $mathbb{R}^d$. In [youwonleu17,youleu18,youleu18b], we proposed new Eulerian numerical approaches for constructing forward flow maps in continuous dynamical systems. This would be an important building block for any efficient numerical approach when we perform similar task on surfaces. Objective 3. In a series of studies [wccy16,wccy18], we first established theoretical recovery guarantees of a family of Riemannian optimization algorithms for low rank matrix recovery, which is about recovering an $m imes n$ rank $r$ matrix from $p < mn$ number of linear measurements. The algorithms were first interpreted as the iterative hard thresholding algorithms with subspace projections. Then we proved that if the restricted isometry constant $R_{3r}$ of the sensing operator is less than $C_k/sqrt{r}$ where $C_k$ depends on the condition number of the matrix, the Riemannian gradient descent method and a restarted variant of the Riemannian conjugate gradient method are guaranteed to converge to the measured rank r matrix provided they are initialized by one step hard thresholding. Then in the second work, we studied the Riemannian optimization methods on the embedded manifold of low rank matrices for the problem of matrix completion. Assume $m$ entries of an $n imes n$ rank $r$ matrix are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. We first proved that with high probability the Riemannian gradient descent and conjugate gradient descent algorithms initialized by one step hard thresholding are guaranteed to converge linearly to the measured matrix provided $m ge C_k n^{1.5} r log^{1.5}(n)$. The sampling complexity was further improved to $m ge C_k n r^2 log^2(n)$ via the resampled Riemannian gradient descent initialization. These results are important for big data research in high dimensional space. As a further development to big data research, we proposed in [lylc17] a variational formulation for dimension reduction on Riemannian manifolds. The algorithm is developed based on the level set method together with a recently developed principal flow algorithm. The original principal flow algorithm is a Lagrangian technique which extends the principal component analysis (PCA) to dimension reduction on Riemannian manifolds. We proposed to incorporate the level set method to obtain a fully implicit formulation so that the overall algorithm can naturally handle various topological changes in the curve evolution. Objective 4. In [gloleuqia16], we proposed novel operator-splitting based fast sweeping methods to solve the generalized eikonal equation. We developed various operator-splitting methods relying on the Peaceman-Rachford scheme, the Douglas-Rachford scheme, the $ heta$-scheme, and the regularized $ heta$-scheme. After applying the operator-splitting strategy, each splitting step corresponds to a much-simpler Hamilton-Jacobi equation so that we can apply the Lax-Friedrichs sweeping method to solve these splitted equations efficiently and easily. Related to this, we proposed in [gloleuqia17] a simple efficient operator-splitting method for computing effective Hamiltonians when the Hamiltonian is either convex or nonconvex in the gradient variable. In [klwq17], we proposed a numerically efficient algorithm for simulating the multi-color optical self- focusing phenomena in nematic liquid crystals. The propagation of the nematicon was modeled by the Schr"odinger equation coupled with a nonlinear elliptic partial differential equation governing the angle between the crystal and the direction of propagation. Numerically, the Schr"odinger equation was solved by a fast Huygens sweeping method, while the nonlinear elliptic PDE is handled by the alternating direction explicit (ADE) method. The overall algorithm is shown to be numerically efficient for computing high frequency beam propagations. Objective 5. In [yhlz18], we developed an effective interface tracking method to simulate the incompressible Stokes flow with moving interfaces. The Stokes equations were first rewritten into a system of elliptic equations with singular sources which can be efficiently solved by a simple weak formulation. The key idea was to first split the solution into a singular part and a regular part additively. The singular part captured the interface conditions, while the regular part approximated the equations in the whole domain, which can be solved by the standard finite element formulation. 16303114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303114.value: Supported by this project, we have published 12 articles in total and have trained two PhD students and one MPhil student. Both PhDs are now working as a postdoc researcher. One is now at the HKUST Department of Mathematics, while the other one is working at the Georgia Tech. The MPhil student is pursuing his PhD at the UBC, Canada. We have developed various algorithms and approaches to interface problems. One method is called the Modified Virtual Grid Difference (MVGD). The implementation of this approach is rather straight forward. We are now able to provide a simple approach to construct a well-conditioned differential matrix associated to the Laplace-Beltramni operator. We have also developed some fast sweeping and operator-splitting approaches to solve different Hamilton-Jacobi equations on surfaces based on the level set approach. We also looked into some cases in big data research where the interface is regarded as an low dimension approximation to the high dimensional data. There are large number of possible extensions and applications of the numerical approaches developed due to the support of this funding.

16303114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303114.value: Dynamic interface problem is still an extremely interesting and important field of research. There are plenty of problems we can continue to work on. For example, this proposal concentrates on numerical approaches to solve elliptic or parabolic type equations on surfaces. It is interesting to see how well these methods can be applied to hyperbolic or higher order nonlinear equations. Special attentions might be needed to impose constraints due to the physical properties of the equation. For example, when solving a hyperbolic equation on surfaces, one might need the ENO/WENO philosophy in the local reconstruction. This could be a possible future research direction.

16303114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303114.value: This project develops and applies efficient numerical methods for solving elliptic partial differential equations defined on hypersurfaces. PDEs defined on interfaces or surfaces arise in many fields in science and engineering. For example, in image processing or computer graphics, one might try to remove noise or to regularize a surface using variational methods which might result in solving a degenerated elliptic PDE. Or, in the field of material sciences, the growth of crystals is seriously influenced by the concentration of certain chemicals on the interface separating the crystal phase and the liquid phase, and such concentration can be numerically modeled by the solution to an elliptic diffusion PDE. In this project, we have developed novel and flexible numerical methods for efficient computing and inverting various elliptic operators defined on manifolds. On the surface, we have also developed various efficient operations for surface representation. The outcome can provide an alternative to other numerical methods in various applications and is important to many disciplines, including crystal growth modelings, surface regularization in image processing and computer graphics, high frequency asymptotic solution to surface wave propagations in seismic and geophysics, multiphase flows with surfactants, and nanostructures design.

16303314.label: Project Objectives

16303314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303314.value: The study of cohomology of locally symmetric spaces is a major subject in mathematics with diverse applications. It arises naturally in the theory of automorphic forms and of Shimura varieties, which play fundamental roles in number theory and geometry. I propose to study two concrete conjectures for the cohomology of locally symmetric spaces. The first conjecture asserts that the cuspidal cohomology of any locally symmetric space does not vanish in the middle dimensions, at least when one passes over to a finite cover. A special case of this is Thurston's well-known conjecture about the first Betti number of hyperbolic three manifolds, which remains open even in the arithmetic case. For each simple Lie group G Vogan and Zuckerman computed a positive integer r(G) related to the classification of unitary representations with non-zero cohomology. Our second conjecture asserts that for any arithmetic manifold associated to G, there could be no non-trivial cohomology below the degree r(G). For compact arithmetic manifolds, this conjecture follows from a combination of the Matsushima formula and the representation-theoretic results of Vogan and Zuckerman. Thus our investigation shall concentrate on the non-compact case. 關於局部對稱空間的上同調的研究是是數學中的一個重要問題，有廣泛的應用。它自然地出現在自守型理論中，而後者在數論中俱有基礎性的地位。 本項目計劃研究對稱空間的上同調理論中的二個具體猜想。 第一個猜想斷言任何俱有非零上同調的緩增表示必定是自守表示。 對任何單李群 $G$，Vogan 和 Zuckerman 計算了一個正整數 $r(G)$，它與對所有俱有非零上同調的酉表示的分類問題有關。 我們的第二個猜想是：任何與 $G$ 相關的算術流型的度數低於 $r(G)$ 的上同調群必然是平凡的。

16303314.label: Realisation of objectives
16303314.value: In the original proposal we proposed to study two conjectures concerning cohomology of locally symmetric spaces. The first conjecture is concerned with the study of tempered unitary representations occurring in the space of cusp forms, while the second is concerned with the determination of cohomology in lower degrees. The first conjecture, Conjecture 1, remains unproven, and this is consistent with our original anticipations. Together with Eischen, Harris and Skinner, we studied p-adic L-functions for (tempered) cohomological automorphic forms on unitary groups. Of course the scope of this joint work is vastly beyond Conjecture 1. The ultimate goal of the study of p-adic L-functions on unitary Shimura varieties is to prove a higher-dimensional version of the Main Conjecture of Iwasawa theory. This work completes the construction of p-adic L-functions for unitary groups, and establishes something close to one direction of this conjecture. On the other hand, the second conjecture, Conjecture 2, is now completely proven in my work with Sun. In fact we went much further than the original conjecture by establishing two general results, one local and one global, in addition to the proof of Conjecture 2. As a result, the structures of cohomology in lower degrees for congruence subgroups in the global situation and for induced representations in the local case are essentially understood.

16303314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303314.value: The objective of this project was to study two conjectures, with the specific aim to give a complete proof of Conjecture 2. In joint work with Eischen, Harris and Skinner we studied p-adic L-functions attached to tempered automorphic forms on unitary groups. This pertains to Conjecture 1, but has scope and depth far beyond it. The major finding here is the construction for the first time, of p-adic L-functions attached to unitary group of arbitrary dimensions. These functions directly generalize the p-adic zeta function of Kubota and Leopoldt that has played a central role in algebraic number theory, through its association with Galois cohomology, in the form of Iwasawa's Main Conjecture. Indeed let n be the dimension of the hermitian space defining our unitary group. Then for n=1 our work recover Katz's well-known theory of p-adic L-functions of Hecke characters. For each semi-simple Lie group G, Vogan and Zuckerman computed a non-negative integer r(G) related to the classification of unitary representations with non-zero cohomology. In my join work with Sun, we prove that below the degree r(G), the cohomology of any congruence subgroup of G is isomorphic to the continuous cohomology of the trivial representation of G. This is precisely the content of Conjecture 2 in my original proposal. We also establishes two general results beyond Conjecture 2. The first is local: we define an integer q(G) which turns out to be great than or equal to r(G), and we prove that below degree q(G), the continuous cohomology of any representation induced from a proper parabolic subgroup is trivial. The second is once again concerned with congruence groups: we show that below degree q(G), there is an injective homomorphism from the cohomology of any congruence subgroup of G to the cohomology of the trivial representation of G.

16303314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303314.value: The study of p-adic L-functions for Shimura varieties is a deep and important subject in number theory. A complete understanding of these L-functions requires much input from representation theory, automorphic forms, and arithmetic algebraic geometry. It may require a whole generation of mathematicians in this area to bring this theory to a satisfactory completion in its various aspects. The elucidation of cohomology of arithmetic manifolds (or equivalently of arithmetic subgroups of semi-simple Lie groups) also awaits deeper understanding of the structure of automorphic forms, at least in those aspect that pertains to cohomology. It should be emphasized that cohomological automorphic forms are of particular interest in number theory.

16303314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303314.value: This project lies deeply in the territory of pure mathematics. Its content and methods touches upon representation theory, harmonic analysis, and number theory. Our work with Eischen, Harris and Skinner laid part of the foundation of a theory, the theory of p-adic L-functions for high dimensional varieties, that is still being intensively developed. Our work with Sun resolves some long standing issues in the cohomology of locally symmetric spaces, and at the same time motivates us to do further investigations towards a even deeper and more complete understanding of this important subject.

Liu等人預測，TI可以在二維（2D）有機系骨架結構實現。這項目的目的是製作有機基TI材料。我們將採用在表面配位自組裝製造包含具有很強的自旋軌道耦合效應製作重元素或磁特性的元素的二維金屬有機框架（2D-MOFs材料）。我們將2D-MOFs長在硼氮化物緩衝層上。我們將將使用掃描隧道顯微鏡來分辨這些二維的MOFs的結構。接下來，我們將利用低溫掃描隧道譜研究2D-MOFs材料的電子特性。我們將測量局部態密度，特別是在2D-MOF域的邊緣。我們也將與角分辨光電子能譜（ARPES）的小组工作進行合作以獲得能帶結構。在整個過程中我們將密切配合理論小组，包括結構設計，數據解釋和理論模型作。

16303514.label: Realisation of objectives
16303514.value: Objects 1 and 2 have been successfully achieved. We used porous supramolecular structures as templates to make two-dimensional (2D) superlattices of Bi nanoclusters on a Au(111) surface. First, we applied on-surface self-assembly to prepare 2D porous supramolecular structures containing well-ordered nanopores. Then, we deposited Bi atoms on the surface. The Bi atoms were confined in the supramolecular pores and formed nanoclusters of a critical size that is defined by the pore size. These nanoclusters were arranged as a 2D superlattice dictated by the structure of the supramolecular templates. The nanocluster size and superlattice periodicity can be adjusted by appropriately designing the supramolecular structures. We designed low-dimensional metal–organic structures incorporating heavy metal Pb atoms as coordination centres are formed on a Au(111) surface by means of on-surface metallo-supramolecular assembly. The molecular building blocks are porphyrin derivatives functionalized with pyridyl groups. These building blocks are linked via a unique pyridyl–Pb–pyridyl coordination motif that does not exist in conventional coordination chemistry but emerges on the surface. The Pb atoms are coordinated in structures of distinctive morphologies, including one-dimensional single chains, double-chains and ladders, and two-dimensional porous networks, owing to the specific sites of the pyridyl groups in the molecular building blocks. We report on a discovery of a metal-organic demi-regular structure self-assembled on a Cu(111) surface. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we resolve that single Cu adatoms are linked with 1,3,5-tris[4-(pyridin-4-yl)phenyl]benzen molecules to form a nanometer scale demi-regular lattice exhibiting a (36; 4, 32, 4, 3) tessellation. The lattice is articulated by perfectly-arranged twofold and threefold pyridyl-Cu coordination motifs with a 1:6 ratio and features a local dodecagonal symmetry. We find that this structure is thermodynamically very robust, and emerges solely at a critical in-plane compression. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the nanocompartments provided by this structure can be used as template to fabricate metallic nano-tiles that pave the surface in a p31m wallpaper group. We designed heterometallic nanoclusters with precise stoichiometry of Bi3Cu4 and Bi7Cu12 can be stabilized in the scaffold of two‐dimensional metal–organic networks on a Cu(111) surface through on‐surface metallosupramolecular self‐assembly processes. The atomic structures of the nanoclusters were resolved using scanning tunneling microscopy and density functional theory calculations. The nanoclusters feature highly symmetric planar hexagonal shapes and core–shell charge modulation. The clusters are arranged as triangular lattices with a periodicity that can be tuned by choosing molecules of different size. This work shows that on‐surface metallosupramolecular self‐assembly creates unique possibilities for the design and synthesis of multinuclear heterometallic nanoclusters. We applied supramolecular assembly to control the adsorption configuration of Co-porphyrin molecules on Au(111) and Cu(111) surfaces. By means of cryogenic scanning tunneling microscopy, we reveal that the Kondo effect associated with the Co center is absent or present in different supramolecular systems. We perform first-principles calculations to obtain spin-polarized electronic structures and compute the Kondo temperatures using the Anderson impurity model. The switching behavior is traced to varied molecular adsorption heights in different supramolecular structures. These findings unravel that a competition between intermolecular interactions and molecule–substrate interactions subtly regulates the molecular Kondo effect in supramolecular systems. Object 3 has been partially achieved. We employ a surface-supported coordination assembly protocol to synthesis monolayer of a two-dimensional coordination network (Ni3(HITP)2) on a Au(111) surface. The electronic coupling between the π orbital of the diimine ligand and the d orbital of the metal ion delocalizes the π electrons over the metalladiimine ring, rendering efficient π-conjugation. Density-functional theory calculations and scanning tunneling spectroscopy confirm this feature. Furthermore, the substrate interacts weakly with the monolayer without distorting its band structure. A charge transfer to the substrate up shifts the electronic bands of the monolayer by 51 meV. The topological band gaps are not celarly resolved. The main reason is the metal substrate contribute a high background signal which dominates the signature of the networks. To overcome this problem, we are working on growing the structures on an insulating substrate. We have collaborated with a Spanish research group to use ARPES to resolve the band structure of the 2D metal-orgainc networks. The data are being analyzed and a manuscript is under preparation.

16303514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303514.value: 1. We have demonstrated a new strategy could potentially enable the fabrication of 2D nanocluster arrays on surfaces using supramolecular structures as the template. We proposed an application of the Bi cluster superlattices. Owing to the large spin–orbital coupling effect in Bi, we expect that the Bi cluster superlattice formed on Au(111) may be a promising candidate for realizing the artificial 2D quantum spin-Hall insulator. (Ref. 2) 2. We investigated the self-assembly of Pb with a series of pyridyl-functionalized porphyrin derivatives. A two-fold pyridyl–Pb–pyridyl coordination motif articulates the molecular building blocks into metal–organic structures. The physical and chemical properties of these structures including the oxidation state of the Pb atoms deserve further studies. The structures reported here are in close contact with the Au surface, which might significantly alter their electronic, in particular the non-trivial topological, properties. (Ref. 1) 3. We demonstrated the assembly of a non-Archimedean demi-regular lattice of Cu atoms in an interfacial metal–organic framework. The co-existing and perfectly arranged twofold and threefold Cu–pyridyl coordination modes emerging from critical in-plane compression are the key ingredients for forming this structure. The unique lattice symmetry and high stability are expected to lead to novel physical properties that deserve further study. We concluded that regular, semi-regular and demi-regular lattices can be achieved by Cu–pyridyl coordination on surfaces. (Ref. 5) 4. We have synthesized multinuclear heterometallic nanoclusters of Bi3Cu4 and Bi7Cu12 in two‐dimensional metal‐organic networks via on‐surface supramolecular self‐assembly. The nanoclusters feature precise stoichiometry, highly symmetric structure and core–shell charge modulation. This work demonstrates that on‐surface supramolecular self‐assembly provides a new route for designing and synthesizing complex metal clusters. (Ref. 6) 5. We demonstrated that monolayer of two-dimensional Ni3(HITP)2 can be synthesized on a Au(111) substrate. The Au substrate does not distort its geometric or electronic structure. The strong conjugation of the monolayer renders highly dispersive bands as confirmed by DFT calculation and tunneling spectroscopy measurements. To explore the functionality of this system, future work of transferring the monolayer to an insulating substrate is highly desirable. (Ref. 7)

16303514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303514.value: Most of the surfaces that have been used are metals, which strongly interact with the 2D networks grown on top. The strong molecule-surface interaction effectively screens the electronic properties of the networks. In future, it is highly desirable to grow these structures on insulating surfaces. We expect the weak molecule-substrate interaction may retain the intrinsic electronic band structures of the networks.

16303514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303514.value: 2D metal-organic networks containing heavy metal atoms are predicted to have remarkable electronic properties. Such materials exhibit quantum behaviors that can be widely used in future electronic applications. Thus the successful synthesis of 2D heavy metal networks represents a major leap towards functional 2D materials. This project has been devoted in this direction. The results obtained reveal the fundamental mechanism of growing such structures and provide insights of the electronic properties of these materials.

16303614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303614.value: Carbon dioxide is an abundant, nontoxic, easily available, and renewable carbon resource. There is therefore growing interest in the efficient transformation of carbon dioxide into useful chemicals. Due to its great thermodynamic stability, the transformation of carbon dioxide presents a significant challenge in regard to chemistry. Over the years, progress has been made in exploring the chemical reactions of carbon dioxide despite its great thermodynamic stability. A large number of its reactions with transition metal complexes have been reported. In many of these reported reactions, carbon dioxide can be transformed into other organic products when proper transition metal complexes are employed. However, useful and economic chemical processes for transformation of carbon dioxide into useful chemicals are rather limited. Further development of better and more effective chemical processes would be highly desirable. In this proposed study, density functional theory calculations will be undertaken to explore mechanistic issues relevant to such reactions. We hope that this research work will provide a potential guide for experimental work and help develop new or improved chemical reactions for carbon dioxide. 在自然界中, 二氧化碳是无毒性, 含量丰富,可再生的碳资源。将二氧化碳转化成有用的化工产品是很有趣的科研课题。但是，由于二氧化碳是热力学很稳定的化合物，它的化学转化难度大，具有挑战性。最近这些年，人们对二氧化碳的化学反应有了很多的研究，尤其是过渡金属参与的化学反应。本计划主要是对这些化学反应的反应机理进行理论研究。由此，希望对一些重要的实验现象进行解释，从而对发展有用的二氧化碳催化反应提供理论基础。

16303614.label: Realisation of objectives
16303614.value: Objective 1: Mechanisms for a number of transition-metal mediated or catalyzed reactions involving carbon dioxide have been investigated with the aid of Density Functional Theorey (DFT) calculations. Factors influencing the reactions studied have been identified. Objective 2: Through our DFT studies, we were able to understand how carbon dioxide has been activated and functionalized, from which we explained why some reactions do not occur and predict some possible reactions.

16303614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303614.value: Through our study on carboxylative cyclization of propargylamine using CO2 catalyzed by NHC-gold(I) complexes, we found that the substrate propargylamine assists(catalyzes) the deprotonation and protonation processes, and solvents, which are polar and capable of hydrogen-bonding, promote the catalytic reactions through stabilizing the carbamate ion intermediate species. Our DFT studies (and findings) on copper-catalyzed boracarboxylation of alkene with CO2 and diboron allow us to explain a couple of known three-component reactions and predict a few possible reactions involving three components. We also studies related mechanisms on reactions of carbon monooxide with boroles and on metal-catalyzed cyclization of alpha-pyrroles. Through these studies, we explained relevant regioselectivity and rationalized major/minor products observed.

16303614.value: Over the years, we have witnessed development of various metal-catalyzed reactions involving carbon dioxide. The insights obtained from this project contribute significantly to this expanding development. We will spend our research effort to understand many recently reported relevant reactions and continue to make our contribution to the development of this research area.

16303814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303814.value: 大型强子对撞机时代的超对称研究

16303814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303814.value: Similar to a building, the objects in the Universe are made of ``bricks'' - elementary particles, such as electrons, up and down quarks, photons, etc. Supersymmetry (SUSY) is a symmetry between fermionic and bosonic elementary particles that was proposed to be a fundamental guideline for constructing the ultimate theory of particle physics. SUSY predicts that, for the elementary particles discovered so far, each boson (e.g., photon) has a fermionic superpartner, and each fermion (e.g., electron) has a bosonic superpartner, both of which are yet to be discovered. Amazingly, SUSY provides elegant solutions to some of the most fundamental puzzles in nature. SUSY explains why the electroweak phase transition, which generates masses for the W and Z bosons (the force carriers of the weak interaction) and hence distinguishes them from photons, occurs at an energy scale about 16 orders lower than the unique fundamental scale in the nature - the Planck scale. In addition, SUSY can unify the strong, weak, and electromagnetic interactions at a high energy scale, where these interactions have the same interaction strength and are just different manifestations of the same force. Accelerators are basic tools used in particle physics. They may create new particles such as superparticles via particle collisions. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the world's largest accelerator. It is very successful in exploring the tiny objects in the nature: using only 1% of the data expected to be collected during the LHC program, the Higgs boson, whose existence was predicted about half a century ago, has been discovered. By the end of the funding period, 3-4 times more data are expected to be collected at a higher energy scale of collisions. As one of the top priorities of the LHC program, the search for SUSY (or superparticles) is very challenging, because of the limitation of our understanding on SUSY in both theoretical and collider regards. So far no SUSY signature has been observed. To respond to these mysteries in a time frame that impacts the field, the PI proposes two directions to explore: data-driven studies on SUSY theory and phenomenology, and theory-driven analyses on SUSY collider search. This proposal, if it is approved, will benefit the development of both particle physics and its community in Hong Kong. N/A

16304014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304014.value: The Kepler problem is a mathematical model for a solar system consisting of a single planet or an atom consisting of a singe electron, depending on whether it is considered classically or quantum mechanically. Besides its historically significant importance in fundamental physics, this old problem has a long history full of mathematical surprises since the early 18th century. For example, in the 1960s it was discovered that the Kepler problem has "magnetized cousins", (i.e., analogous mathematical models for the hypothetic hydrogen atoms in which the nucleus carries both electric and magnetic charge). These magnetized cousins share the characteristic beauty and simplicity of the Kepler problem, and were not expected to exist in higher than five dimensions. But we found high dimensional quantum models in 2005 and high dimensional classical models (in odd dimension only) in 2012. Due to some intricacies of these models in higher dimensions, it is not clear how the quantum models are linked to the classical models. The main goal of this project is to find out the missing link between the quantum and classical models. A secondary goal is to understand why magnetized Kepler problems in even dimensions can only exist quantum mechanically. Along the way we should also gain a good understanding of various quantization schemes. The project proposed here is part of a long-term project whose ultimate goal is to find clues or hints to fundamental physics via uncovering the beautiful mathematics hidden behind the Kepler problem. 开普勒问题是最简单的太阳系或氢原子的数学模型。除了它在基础物理里的历史性作用之外，这一古老问题一直有令人惊讶的新发现。譬如，在20世纪60年代末人们发现了磁化开普勒问题，即磁化氢原子（其原子核既带电荷也带磁荷）的数学模型。这些磁化开普勒问题具有开普勒问题的所有数学特征，但专家们不相信在5维以上会存在。在2005年我给出了量子高维磁化开普勒问题的构造，在2012年我发现我给出了经典高奇数维磁化开普勒问题的构造。由于高维磁化开普勒问题的非平凡性，量子高奇数维磁化开普勒问题和经典高奇数维磁化开普勒问题的联系不清楚。 这一研究计划的一个目的是搞清楚这两者之间的关系。还有一个目的是要回答偶数维磁化开普勒问题为什么只在量子的层面上才有。 这一研究计划是一项长期研究计划的一部分，其终极目标是通过对隐藏在开普勒问题背后的数学进行探索以求达到对基础物理的深入发展提供有价值的线索。

16304014.label: Realisation of objectives
16304014.value: In the written account of his talk delivered to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Bi-National Colloquium in 1981, Freeman Dyson wrote: "We ought to give greater attention and greater support to unfashionable research. At any particular moment in the history of science, the most important and fruitful ideas are often lying dormant merely because they are unfashionable." In my view, the research on the Kepler problem --- a mathematical model for the simplest solar system or the simplest atom---is unfashionable yet deserves greater attention and greater support. It is with this big picture in mind that we embarked on a long-term project about ten years ago --- a research journey starting from the mathematical research of the Kepler problem with an eye towards the fundamental physics. This journey is justified because of many findings along the way, and it has a huge potential to provide significant clues to the currently stalled fundamental physics. A good feature of this long-term project/journey is that its various aspects reinforce and inspire each other so that if we become stuck in one direction, we can obtain hints from another direction, and a mistake from overlooking something from one angle can be easily spotted by scrutinizing the problem from another angle. The original project in this proposal is a sub-project in the aforementioned long-term project. However, the first two major findings in this project period belong to two strongly related but different sub-projects. Given the nature of our journey, this is not a surprise. As for things we proposed to do earlier, we reported in the midterm report that they are partially done and will be carried out in the future. Since history is the best teacher, in fundamental science or mathematics I firmly believe that a researcher should be an explorer with a free mind: he only cares about making new exciting observations, never mind the order of his findings. It is with this free-minded spirit that we made three major findings during this project period as recorded in the six published research papers. It is worth to mention that the third major finding --- indirectly related to the original project --- is the resolution of a natural problem in mathematical physics out of a synthesis of three beautiful geometric ideas since the 1970s and has been cited even by people working on philosophy, moreover, this is the third time that I accidentally discovered something in other people's field.

16304014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304014.value: In our early work, we discovered an intimate relationship between the orbits of the magnetized Kepler problems and the Lorentz group. To state the result, we let G = SO(3, 1) x R_+ where R_+ is the multiplicative group of positive real numbers, and X be the set of oriented orbits of all magnetized Kepler problems of the same type: either all ellipses or all parabolas. Then there is a natural transitive action of G on X. In other words, for any two oriented orbits of the magnetized Kepler problems with magnetic charge mu and mu', suppose that they are either both ellipses or both parabolas, then there is a Lorentz transformation plus a dilation which transform one orbit into the other. Note that, the Lie group G is the structure group of Euclidean Jordan algebra consisting of Hermitian matrices of order 2, and the magnetized Kepler problems are naturally associated with this Jordan algebra. One might conjecture that this is a general phenomenon. We confirm this conjecture for all Hermitian-type simple Euclidean Jordan algebras, and the work appeared in research output no. 2, 3, and 4. This result is our first major finding. Our next major finding is the dynamic symmetric analysis for the rank-one generalized Kepler problems associated with all simple Euclidean Jordan algebras of degrees 2 and 4, and the work appeared in research output no. 5 and 6. Our third major finding is an accidental discovery inspired by a talk at a workshop. It extends Tulczyjew’s ingenious approach to the dynamics from particles to electrically charged particles in non-abelian gauge fields. This approach unifies Lagrangian and Hamiltonian descriptions of particle dynamics and is quite appealing to geometry-oriented minds. This geometric approach is very flexible in the sense that it can be easily adapted to different settings, especially to systems with singular Lagrangians or subject to constraints. The work appeared in research output no. 1. Papers 7 and 8 are written versions of my conference talk and lecture respectively.

16304014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304014.value: One can extend the first two major findings further, to all simple Euclidean Jordan algebras and generalized Kepler problems of all rank. As for the third major finding, one can find its applications in geometry and mechanics.

16304014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304014.value: The Kepler problem is a mathematical model for either the simplest solar system or the simplest atom, depending on whether it is viewed at the classical level or the quantum level. Jordan algebra originated from quantum mechanics. Lorentz transformation is the signature of special relativity. Our study in the past showed that these three are interrelated, and that leads to a general mathematical theory. The first two major findings in this project further enrich this general theory and remove some of the mystery as well. If history is a guide, this general theory might provide a clue to the fundamental physics. The third major finding is the resolution of a natural problem in mathematical physics out of a synthesis of three beautiful geometric ideas since the 1970s and has been cited even by people working on philosophy. It enlightens our geometric understanding of mechanics.

16304314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304314.value: Graphene is a single sheet of carbon atoms arranged in a perfect honeycomb lattice. This geometric structure has given rise to many novel physical characteristics. Recently, we have found that by etching 100 nm holes in graphene, arranged in a triangular lattice with a lattice constant of 150 nm, the so-called antidot graphene can display something not observed in pristine graphene — a quasigap in the electronic density of state that is centered at the Fermi level. Such phenomenon is known to be caused by Coulomb interaction between localized electronic states, and our experiment has found surprising consequences that can be attributed to the Coulomb correlation gap, i.e., the quantum mechanical phase effects can be sustained over a record distance of ten microns, a distance that is denoted as the dephasing length. The resulting transport characteristics within the dephasing length are called “mesoscopic phenomena.” Because of this large dephasing length, we have for the first time directly observed the strong localization of electrons in two dimensions through sample size scaling. In this proposal, we aim to follow up on this interesting discovery through both experiments and theory. In particular, we would like to directly measure the Coulomb correlation gap by tunneling spectroscopy, as well as to explore the various potential physical implications of the Coulomb gap, such as the effect of diminished inelastic scattering on the superconducting proximity effect. In theory, we would like to resolve the puzzles on why the strong localization effect was only observed in the vicinity of the charge neutrality point, and why a Coulomb gap can exist in antidot graphene, while the electron-electron interaction effect is generally regarded as weak in pristine graphene. Completion of this project can provide a deeper understanding of nanostructured antidot graphene’s novel characteristics, with guidance towards their controlled manipulations.

16304314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304314.value: The major findings of this project are: (1) Direct observation of an electron-electron correlation gap in antidot graphene. The size of the gap varies from around 10 to 20 meV, as a function of the applied magnetic field. The manifestations of the gap are in the form of nonlinear I-V behavior at low temperatures, and the temperature-activated behavior of the conductance. (2) Derivation of a 4 by 4 matrix Hamiltonian for the antidot graphene, and the explicit demonstration of the existence of Berry curvature through both theoretical calculations from the derived Hamiltonian, as well as experimental measurements. (3) Observed the spatial variation of the carrier density in graphene under a large bias current. This carrier density variation was found to depend on the bias direction; hence it cannot be caused by the heating effect, which should be independent of the bias current direction. A simple self-consistent calculation on longitudinal transport coupled with carrier density variation is shown to explain the experimental results very well. Another outcome is that Dr. Ting Zhang has obtained a 2D metal-insulator transition in systems described by the Weyl Hamiltonian, driven by the Berry phase. This achievement is reported in GRF 16307114 completion report. Dr. Ting Zhang is part of my research group, even though he also has his own projects, as well as collaborations with other faculty members.

16304314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304314.value: Antidot graphene has a bandstructure gap. Within the gap there are clearly puddles of electrons and holes. How to measure the charge carrier density within the gap, as well as locating the bandedge experimentally, has always been a difficult problem because the Hall measurements cannot give accurate results owing to the mixing of the longitudinal and transverse currents. We have designed a device that can automatically perform two measurements by switching the voltage and current electrodes. By averaging the results, the KWANT simulations have already shown good results may be obtained. We will carry this out experimentally very soon. Theoretically, even though we have the 4 by 4 Hamiltonian for the antidot graphene, it still only describes the wavefunctions within the two bands, but not the states within the gap. Hence it is still incomplete. A direct consequence is that we do not know the boundary condition at the edge of the holes if we attempt to use our 4 by 4 continuum Hamiltonian to perform real-space calculations. This problem is under serious consideration at present.

16304314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304314.value: Graphene is a monolayer of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb lattice. By making an ordered array of nano-sized holes on graphene, leading to so-called antidot graphene, we can alter the electronic properties of graphene drastically. When we started on this approach to broaden the characteristics of graphene, not all the implications of the hole array were known. Through this project, we have considerably advanced our understanding of antidot graphene. Most significantly, we have for the first time derived a phenomenological 4 by 4 matrix Hamiltonian for the antidot graphene, and obtained from it some surprising topological quantum mechanical characteristics not previously expected, but they were experimentally verified by us. Another important outcome of this project is the direct observation of an electronic correlation gap in antidot graphene. As we know, electrons carry charges, which means they can interact through their electric field. The importance of such interaction effects can be gauged by the ratio of the electron-electron interaction energy to the kinetic energy of the electrons. In pristine graphene, such interactions can be ignored because this ratio is very small. However, in antidot graphene this ratio is no longer so small, and as a result the electron-electron interaction can open a gap around the Fermi level. We have directly observed this so-called “correlation gap”. Implications of such a gap is still to be explored.

16304414.label: Project Objectives
16304414.value: To compute observable signatures of inflationary models (especially those motivated by UV theories) in anticipation of results from ongoing cosmological experiments. To construct inflationary models from string theory and develop them in response to results from PLANCK and other cosmological missions. To construct models and scenarios of dark matter from string theory, and to study their physical implications and signatures in particle physics and cosmology. To examine de Sitter solutions from string theory to shed light on the dark energy problem, and conceptual issues of gravity in spacetime with positive vacuum energy.

16304414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304414.value: A multi-faceted program in theoretical cosmology is proposed. A confluence of cosmological measurements has given us an increasingly precise picture of our universe, from its earliest moment to its current state. Observational data reveal that all known matter constitutes less than 5% of the total energy-matter content of the universe, and the remaining 95% is made up of dark matter and dark energy. While the observational evidence for dark energy (Nobel Prize 2011) is compelling, its theoretical underpinning remains a great mystery. Likewise, a variety of astrophysical and cosmological experiments are racing to discover the identity of dark matter, which has direct impact on particle physics. Current and near-future observations of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and large-scale structure allow us to probe with high precision the early universe where fundamental physics leaves its fingerprint. These measurements significantly constrain the mechanisms behind the primordial fluctuations responsible for structure formation. There is mounting evidence that the flatness of the universe and its structure derive from an inflationary epoch, with quantum fluctuations seeding density perturbations. Upcoming observations are expected to decide between qualitatively different classes of inflationary dynamics. For example, the tensor to scalar ratio is closely related to the field range of the inflaton, and non-Gaussianity can distinguish between slow-roll versus more general single field inflation, and single-field versus multiple field inflation. The sensitivity of primordial inflation to Planck-suppressed operators also provides an opportunity to connect cosmological observations with the structure of the UV completion of gravity. String theory is a paradigmatic extension of relativistic quantum mechanics which incorporates the physics of gravity and space-time. It provides a concrete framework for addressing puzzles in particle physics beyond the Standard Model that require a UV completion. Theoretical cosmology, on the other hand, addresses questions such as what one might learn about high energy physics from the information accessible in the sky, and what one might learn from high energy physics about the history of the universe. The two synergistic disciplines constitute an integral part of the efforts to address long standing open issues, such as uncovering the true quantum nature of space-time at ultra-short distances and its implications to the physics of early universe and relatedly particle physics. This proposal aims to improve our understanding of (i) dark matter scenarios, (ii) the nature of dark energy, (ii) inflationary cosmology and its predictions through the lens of fundamental physics, in particular string theory.

16304414.label: Realisation of objectives
16304414.value: The proposed objectives have all been successfully realized. During the funding period, we have published 14 journal articles and delivered 40 invited talks at international conferences. The proposed objectives are deeply intertwined. Progress in one triggers advances in another. Some results we obtained have impact on several of the objectives. Here we give an overview of how the proposed project objectives are addressed: Objective 1 (Publications 1, 6, 7, 11, 13): We developed the effective field theory for spacetime symmetry breaking (article 1). An inflationary background breaks time-translational symmetry and possibly other spacetime and internal symmetries. The formalism developed in article 1 can be applied to such general inflationary models. In article 6, we pointed out the possibility that a heavy scalar or pseudoscalar in the TeV scale can play the role of the inflaton, while preserving the minimalist features of Higgs inflation. In article 7, we developed the path integral formalism for multi-field inflation, which facilitates the computation of inflationary perturbations. In article 11, we used holographic techniques to compute inflationary non-Gaussianities for general single-field inflation, including models with a non-trivial sound speed. In this holographic approach, the inflationary dynamics is captured by a relevant deformation of the dual conformal field theory (CFT) in the UV, while the inflationary correlators are computed by conformal perturbation theory. This approach gives a different perspective of inflationary fluctuations and helps build the foundation for the research program of ``Cosmological Collider Physics” (that is actively pursued by researchers worldwide, including researchers in Hong Kong) . In publication 13, we considered the flattening effects due to coupling the inflaton field to the high-energy degrees of freedom. We computed the inflationary observables for a family of string inflation models which generalize chaotic inflation and found that the tensor-to-scalar ratio for this family of models is in the range of r~ 0.04-0.14, which is potentially detectable by ongoing and near-future experiments. Objective 2 (Publications 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14): Axion inflation models are phenomenologically interesting as the level of primordial gravitational waves generated by them is observable. However, realization of these models requires super-Planckian axion decay constants. We have proposed a mechanism to widen the axion window (article 2) and we constructed string theory models implementing this mechanism (article 3). These results have useful implications to dark matter searches, inflation, and axion physics. We also found stringent quantum gravity constraints on the low energy effective action of string theory (articles 4 and 5). Our results further substantiated the weak gravity conjecture, and suggested that certain bottom-up approaches of physics beyond the Standard Model are not realizable in string theory. In articles 9, 12, 14, we found new evidence for the weak gravity conjecture, through several independent lines of arguments, including holography duality, entropy considerations, and IR consistencies (such as unitarity, casuality, and analyticity). A novelty of large field inflation models (i.e., inflation models that give rise to a detectable level of gravitational waves) in string theory is the multi-branched feature of the inflation potential. This feature is exhibited in a wide class of string inflation models known as axion monodromy inflation. Transitions between different branches can occur non-perturbatively (via nucleation of a domain wall) and spoil the slow-roll properties of inflation. To avoid these transitions, we put an upper bound on the inflation field range and hence the amplitude of the tensor mode. Our finding reported in article 10 is that the transition rate between different branches of the inflaton potential can deviate significantly from the standard Coleman formula for vacuum decay that was widely used in the literature. Moreover, coupling the inflaton to the high-energy degrees of freedom generically lowers the tensor-to-scalar ratio. This effect, known as flattening, has been observed in the string theory context through the properties of the Dirac-Born-Infeld and Chern-Simons D-brane action. In article 14, we revisited such flattening effects in type IIB flux compactifications with mobile D7-branes, with the inflaton identified with the D7-brane position. We observe that, with a generic choice of background fluxes, flattening effects are larger than previously observed, allowing to fit these models within current experimental bounds. In particular, we computed the cosmological observables in scenarios compatible with closed-string moduli stabilization, finding tensor-to-scalar ratios as low as r ∼ 0.04. These are models of single field inflation in which the inflaton is much lighter than the other scalars through a mild tuning of the compactification data. Objective 3 (Publications 2, 3): Axion is a theoretically well motivated candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model. If their decay constant is within the right range, they can serve as dark matter and/or the inflaton. The case for axion dark matter has become more compelling in the absence of super-partner signals at the LHC. Although axion-like particles are abundant in string theory, their decay constants are widely believed to fall outside the desired dark matter and inflaton range. We designed a novel scenario motivated by string theory that involves multiple axions (articles 2 and 3) and found that the axion decay can both be enhanced to super-Planckian values for inflation and lowered to the desired dark matter window. Objective 4 (Publications 8): In article 8, we reviewed the dark energy problem and discussed attempts to realize dark energy in string theory. Our results have significant implications on the string theory landscape. This work suggested interesting future research directions that the PI and other researchers in the field can pursue.

16304414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304414.value: We have made significant progress in the proposed projects: 1) We showed that UV complete models of inflation can produce novel observable signals (e.g., non-Gaussianities, tensor modes) that are potentially detectable from ongoing and future experiments. Our findings can help identify targets for future cosmological missions. 2) We constructed inflationary models from string theory, in particular, models with distinct observational signatures. We found that quantum gravity can impose non-trivial constraints on inflationary models. We also found that string theory can expand the scope of cosmological scenarios to include new scenarios and new signatures. 3) Using string theoretical ideas, we constructed new models of dark matter that widen the allowed parameter windows. Our findings motivated new ways to detect these unknown dark matter particles, and finding correlated experimental signatures in particle physics and cosmology that help in pinning down the composition of the dark sector of the universe. 4) We examined the difficulties in constructing de Sitter vacua in string theory. Our attempts may shed light on what accounts for the accelerated expansion of the universe and whether quantum gravity can impose non-trivial constraints on theories of cosmic acceleration. Here, we highlight the impact of two of our findings: 1) the work on widening the axion window via kinetic and Stuckelberg mixings (Publications 2, 3) has broadened the scope of the search for axion dark matter particles and the inflationary B-mode, 2) the body of work on the weak gravity conjecture (Publications 4, 5, 9, 12, 14) has influenced the CMB Stage 4 experimental community in setting their B-node target (see the CMB-S4 Science Book, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.02743.pdf). Thus, the completed project not only elucidated the theoretical foundation of fundamental physics, but also their experimental consequences.

16304414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304414.value: The research outcome of this project has opened up many new directions for future development. The completed works illustrate the power of string theory in motivating and constraining cosmological scenarios and models, but much of its cosmological implications remains to be explored. For example, it was recently pointed out by several research groups (including the PI’s) that the WGC can rule out models of particle physics that extends the Standard Model by restricting the type of neutrinos (Majorana vs Diac) and their masses as well as the masses of other new particles. Finding out whether a given low energy theory can be consistently coupled to quantum gravity has been an important research area that many researchers, including the PI, are actively pursuing. The work on holographic non-Gaussianties also built the foundation for future studies of ``Cosmological Collider Physics”.

16304414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304414.value: The proposed project is a multi-faceted research program in theoretical cosmology – the first such in Hong Kong. A confluence of cosmological measurements has given us an increasingly precise picture of our universe, from its earliest moment to its current state. Observational data reveal that all known matter constitutes less than 5% of the total energy-matter content of the universe, and the remaining 95% is made up of dark matter and dark energy. While the observational evidence for dark energy is compelling, its theoretical underpinning remains a great mystery. Likewise, a variety of astrophysical and cosmological experiments are racing to discover the identity of dark matter, which has direct impact on particle physics. Current and near-future observations of the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure allow us to probe with high precision the early universe where fundamental physics leaves its fingerprint. These measurements significantly constrain the underlying mechanisms for structure formation. This proposal aims to improve our understanding of (i) dark matter scenarios, (ii) the nature of dark energy, (ii) inflationary cosmology and its predictions through the lens of fundamental physics. String theory combines general relativity with quantum mechanics, and is thus a suitable framework for addressing the above cosmic puzzles.

16304714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304714.value: Alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes are all basic hydrocarbons, in which only hydrogen and carbon are present. They constitute the foundation of organic chemistry. More advanced organic compounds can be synthesized by functionalization reactions from simple hydrocarbons, which ultimately come from crude oil. Thus, the ability to functionalize hydrocarbons ultimately influences the ability of human being to a certain degree. Among the three types of hydrocarbons, alkynes are the most reactive and thus easiest to functionalize. Thus, alkynes have been an important starting point for synthesizing more advanced organic molecules, such as functional materials, pharmaceuticals, etc. Over the past few decades, organic chemists have paid tremendous attention to develop new ways to functionalize alkynes. Among them, electron-normal and electron-deficient alkynes have been extensively studied. In contrast, functionalization of electron-rich alkynes has not been well established. In the project, new functionalization reactions for electron-rich alkynes will be studied. The studies of these selective reactions will not only contribute to fundamental understanding of these species, but also have applications in medicines, materials, other aspects of daily life. 烷烴、烯烴和炔都是基本的烴类化合物。它們構成了有機化學的基礎。更高級的有機化合物也可以從簡單的烴的官能团化反應來合成。因此，烴類官能化反应最終会一定程度上影響人類的能力。在三種類型的烴中炔烴是最活潑的，因此也最容易官能化。因此，炔烴是合成更高級有機分子的一個重要的起點，如功能材料，製藥等。在過去的幾十年中，有機化學家付出很大精力，開發新的炔烴的官能团化方法。其中，電性正常和缺電子炔烴已被廣泛研究。然而，富電子炔的官能化还有待进一步研究。该項目将研究新的富電子炔烴的官能化反應。這些選擇性反應不僅增加人类对這些化合物的基本認識，而且带来人们在合成藥品、材料等日常生活方面的應用。

16304714.label: Realisation of objectives
16304714.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a range of new functionalization reactions for electron-rich alkynes. The research work includes three parts: (a) Development of new strategies for the synthesis of medium and large ring lactones and lactams from electron-rich alkynes; (b) Exploration of the cycloaddition of electron-rich internal alkynes with dipolar compounds, such as electron-deficient isocynides; (c) Regio- and stereoselective functionalization of electron-rich alkynes for the synthesis of stereodefined multi-substituted alkenes. The objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. (1) we developed an efficient catalytic ring-expansion approach for medium-ring lactam synthesis. This reaction represents a new reaction between siloxy alkynes and N-acyliminiums (or analogues), both of which are versatile species in organic synthesis. With the proper choice of the superior Brønsted acid catalyst HNTf2 and the exceptional Ts protecting group, this efficient process, which overcomes the propensity to take multiple side pathways, proceeds specifically to form the desired medium lactams. The lactam products are useful precursors to other medium ring nitrogen-containing heterocycles. (2) We have demonstrated the first highly selective hydrosilylation of unsymmetrical internal alkynes by iridium catalysis. With the proper choice of catalyst, a range of internal thioalkynes participated in the efficient intermolecular hydrosilylation with a diverse set of silanes to furnish the corresponding multi-substituted vinylsilanes with excellent α regio- and syn stereoselectivity. (3) We developed the first [3+2] cyclization of siloxy alkynes for the synthesis of aromatic heterocycles. In contrast to the previous cyclization reactions of siloxy alkynes where they serve as two-carbon partners, in this reaction siloxy alkynes contribute a C‒O unit to cyclization. In the presence of TBAF as the activator, the reaction between siloxy alkynes and electron-deficient isocyanides proceed efficiently to form a range of substituted oxazoles under mild metal-free conditions. Mechanistic studies indicated that siloxy alkynes serve as the ketene precursor. Inspired by careful analysis, complementary conditions (such as using hydroxide as catalyst) were also achieved for this transformation. In addition to the above reactions, we have also studied new cycloaddition reactions of electron-rich alkynes with special partners. We also observed new rearrangement reactions in the study of the above reactions. These results serve as a new foundation to the discovery of a range of other novel organic reactions.

16304714.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304714.value: In this project, we have developed the following new catalytic processes leading to synthesis of useful chiral building blocks and synthetically important structural units. (1) We developed an efficient catalytic ring-expansion approach for medium-ring lactam synthesis. (2) We developed an Ir-catalyzed highly regio- and stereoselective hydrosilylation of internal thioalkynes via an Ir(I) hydride mechanism (3) We developed the first metal-free [2+2+2] cycloaddition of ynamides and nitriles for mild and regioselective synthesis of fully substituted pyridines (4) We developed an organocatalytic synthesis of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes from racemic propargylic alcohols via 1,8-conjugate addition to para-quinone methides. (5) In our effort to develop organocatalytic synthesis of chiral diarylmethyl alkynes, we demonstrated a rare example of improving synthetic procedure by understanding the role of additive. (6) We developed the first highly efficient and stereoselective formal acylcyanation of electron-rich alkynes for the synthesis of fully-substituted acrylonitriles. (7) We developed the first [3+2] cyclization of siloxy alkynes for the synthesis of aromatic heterocycles, which provides a new synthesis for oxazoles.

16304714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304714.value: During the research work of this project, we have also discovered some additional results that can lead to new development. For example, in the synthesis of medium lactones and lactams, we found that sugar molecules can be further employed. However, more detailed studies are needed. In the metal-catalyzed addition reactions of alkynes, we also found that interesting rearrangement reactions that deserve more exploration.

16304714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304714.value: In this project, we have discovered a range of new organic processes with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes are new approaches to medium ring structures, aromatic heterocycles, and stereodefined olefins. These new processes are expected to find applications in medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical industry. These findings will not only contribute to addressing this longstanding challenges in organic synthesis, but also benefit many aspects of human life, from public health to environmental protection.
