16305014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305014.value: Development of new methodologies for the syntheses of fused-heterocyclic polymers with multiple functional substituents is of great interest. The unique electronic structures of the fused-heterocyclic repeat units are expected to endow the polymers with distinct materials properties and enable them to find high-tech applications in polymer optoelectronics systems, such as polymer photovoltaic cells, field effect transistors, and light-emitting diodes. However, fused-heterocyclic polymers, especially those with multiple substituents, have been difficult to synthesize. The conventional synthetic approaches to such polymers commonly involve multiple steps, harsh conditions, elaborate controls, and troublesome procedures. My research group has much experience in the area of developing new alkyne polymerization processes for the syntheses of functional polymers. In our previous studies, aromatic hydrocarbons have been used as the main constructs. We now plan to extend our work to heteroatom-containing systems, especially fused-heterocyclics. Organic chemists have recently reported that some transition-metal complexes can efficiently catalyze the annulations of internal alkynes to afford heterocyclics with multiple substituents through C-H activation. In this work, we will explore the utility of these reactions of internal alkynes for the syntheses of heterocyclic polymers. The goal of this proposed research project is to develop simple and efficient polymerization reactions of internal alkynes for the preparation of multi-substituted fused-heterocyclic polymers with various topological structures and functional properties. A2- and A3-type internal alkynes and B2-type dioximes, dibenzamides and dibenzoic acids will be designed and prepared as monomeric species. Linear and hyperbranched heterocyclic polymers with high molecular weights and macroscopic processability will be synthesized, and the regiochemistry involved in the alkyne polymerization reactions will be studied. Various catalytic and additive species will be screened, in an effort to achieve high efficiency and attain high regioselectivity under mild polymerization conditions. The material properties of the fused-heterocyclic polymers will be studied and their applications in photovoltaic cells, light-emitting diodes, fluorescent sensors, light refractive systems, porous frameworks, and biological probes will be explored. It is anticipated that this research project will establish effective synthetic routes to a variety of new polymers with novel structures, unique functionalities, and practical applications. 發展合成功能化的稠雜環類聚合物的新聚合方法意義重大。稠雜環單元獨特的電子結構有望賦予聚合物新穎的功能特性，使之用於高分子光電材料領域中，比如聚合物光伏電池、場效應電晶體和發光二極體。但是製備稠雜環類，尤其是帶有多個取代基的聚合物，往往比較困難。該類聚合物傳統的合成方法通常需要多個反應步驟、苛刻的反應條件、精密的控制和繁瑣的後處理。 我們課題組在發展新型的炔類反應以及製備功能化炔類聚合物方面具有豐富的研究經驗。在前期的研究中，我們通常使用芳烴作為聚合物的主要構築基元。現在我們準備將研究工作延伸到含雜原子，尤其是稠雜環體系中。有機化學家最近報導了一些基於碳－氫鍵活化、過渡金屬催化內炔環化生成帶有多取代基的雜環化合物的反應。在本項目中，我們將探索利用這些內炔的反應來製備新型的稠雜環類聚合物。 本項目的研究目的是發展簡單、高效的內炔聚合反應，製備具有不同拓撲結構和功能的多取代的稠雜環類聚合物。我們將設計和製備双、三官能度的炔類單體，以及双官能度的肟、苯甲醯胺和苯甲酸類單體；合成高分子量、易加工的線形和超支化的稠雜環類聚合物，並研究這些炔類聚合反應的區域選擇性；探究不同的催化劑和添加劑對聚合反應的影響，優選出最佳的聚合反應條件；研究所製備的稠雜環類聚合物的性質，並探索這些材料在聚合物光伏電池、發光二極體、螢光感測器、光折射體系、多孔框架和生物探針等方面的應用。項目的實施有望發展幾種新型高效的聚合反應，製備一系列具有新穎結構和應用價值的功能化聚合物材料。

16305014.label: Realisation of objectives
16305014.value: The objectives of this proposed research project are to (a) design and synthesize new functional alkyne monomers, (b) develop efficient synthetic methodologies for fused heterocyclic polymers with multiple substituents, (c) search for new catalyst systems and optimize polymerization conditions, and (d) investigate the properties of the new polymers and explore their technological applications. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. The development of new polymerization reactions conducted under monomer non-stoichiometric conditions has great academic and industrial significance. Herein, a new route for synthesizing functional polynaphthalenes (PNs) was developed. The polycoupling reactions of benzoic acid and its derivatives with 4,4’-(1,6-hexylenedioxy)bis(diphenylacetylene) proceeded smoothly in o-xylene in the presence of [Cp*IrCl2]2 and Ag2CO3 at 140 °C, generating multisubstituted PNs with high molecular weights (Mw up to 228 700) in high yields (up to 98%). Unlike traditional two-component polymerizations, one of the monomers in this polymerization is mono-functional. This is an advantage as it avoids the synthetic difficulty and limited scope of bi-functional monomers. The effect of monomer stoichiometry on the polymerization was systematically investigated and the stoichiometric balance between a reactive intermediate and internal diyne is thus more critical than the monomer feed ratio. All the obtained PNs show good thermal stability and excellent optical transparency. They possess good film-forming ability and their thin films exhibit high refractive indices (n = 1.7653–1.6354). The polymer carrying a tetraphenylethene motif is weakly emissive in solution but emits intensely when aggregated, demonstrating a phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission. The efficient solid-state emission and good photosensitivity enable it to be utilized as a material for fabricating two-dimensional fluorescent photopatterns by irradiating its thin films under UV light through copper masks. Multi-substituted poly(isoquinoline)s with high molecular weights (up to 18 340) could be achieved in almost quantitative yields by polyannulations of internal diynes and O-acyloxime derivatives catalyzed by [Cp*RhCl2]2 with Cu(OAc)2·H2O as oxidant in a methanol/THF mixture at 105 °C for 12 h. This polymerization is tolerant to stoichiometric imbalance and various functional groups and is environmentally friendly with acetic acid as the only by-product. Most of the polymers are soluble and transparent in the visible light region. Their thin films exhibit high refractive indices in a wide wavelength region. The poly(isoquinoline) carrying tetraphenylethene units is highly emissive in the aggregated state and can generate discernible photopatterns upon UV irradiation. It can also function as a sensitive fluorescent chemosensor for detecting nitro-aromatic explosives such as picric acid in a superamplification manner. A straightforward and waste-free polymerization route to functional isocoumarin-containing polymers was developed by the oxidative polycoupling of 4,4’-(1,2-diphenyl-1,2-ethenylene)dibenzoic acid and 1,6-bis[4-(phenylethynyl)phenoxy]hexane catalyzed by [Cp*RhCl2]2 and Cu(OAc)2·H2O in dimethylformamide under nitrogen or air at 120 °C for 24 h. All the polymers were prepared in high yields with high molecular weights. An isocoumarin framework forms in situ during the polymerization from readily accessible and inexpensive monomers. The resulting polymers possess good thermal stability, optical transparency and film-forming ability. Their thin films exhibit high and tunable refractive indices and are photopatternable. The presence of tetraphenylethene units in the polymer structures has endowed the polymers with strong solid-state emission. In the presence of Pd2(dba)3, bathophenanthroline, silver acetate and Cu(OAc)2·H2O, the polyannulation of diphenol derivatives and unactivated internal alkynes proceeds smoothly, generating high molecular weights (Mw up to 34 000) polymers with benzofuran derivatives in satisfactory yields. All the polymers possess good film-forming ability and high thermal stability. Due to the presence of fused-heterocyclic rings in the polymer main chains, their thin solid films show high refractive indices (RI = 1.900–1.611). The polymers carrying tetraphenylethene units are photosensitive and can be utilized to generate fluorescent patterns by the photolithography process. Multi-substituted poly(naphthopyran)s (PNPs) with high molecular weights can be readily generated in excellent yields by the cascade oxidative polyannulation of benzoylacetonitrile and internal diynes catalyzed by [RhCp*Cl2]2 and Cu(II) acetate. This polymerization route enjoys the remarkable advantages of high reaction rate and efficiency and wide monomer scope. The thin films of PNPs also display pretty high refractive indices in a wide wavelength range. Interestingly, the emissions of the solid powders of PNPs are turned on upon mechanical perturbation and solvent fuming, demonstrating the phenomena of mechanochromism and vapochromism. This stimuli-response behavior is attributed to the strong intermolecular interaction between the fused-heterocyclic naphthopyran units. Such properties allow the polymers to be used as security materials or fluorescent indicators in various fields.

16305014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305014.value: Fused-heterocyclic polymers are a novel class of polymeric materials with potential high-tech optoelectronic applications due to their unique electronic and photonic properties. However, they are difficult to prepare. In this project, we have developed new synthetic methodologies for their synthesis. They are (i) iridium-catalyzed oxidative polycoupling of arylbenzoic acids with diynes to poly(tetraarylnaphthalene)s; (ii) rhodium-catalyzed polyannulation of internal diynes and O-acyloxime to multi-substituted poly(isoquinoline)s; (iii) rhodium-catalyzed oxidative polycoupling of dibenzoic acid and diynes to isocoumarin-containing polymers; (iv) palladium-catalyzed polyannulation of diphenol derivatives and unactivated internal alkynes to benzofuran-containing polymers and (v) rhodium-catalyzed cascade oxidative polyannulation of benzoylacetonitrile and internal diynes to multi-substituted poly(naphthopyran)s. These methods enjoy the advantages of readily available monomers, simple operation, high efficiency, mild condition, environmental friendliness, high atom economy and high tolerance to functional groups and monomer stoichiometric imbalance. The resulting polymers are often synthesized in high yields with high molecular weights. They are soluble and show high thermal stability, good-filming ability and high refractive index. All these properties make them to find high-technological applications. Indeed, several potential applications have been explored such as high refractive materials, fluorescent bioprobes, photopatterning and fluorescent chemosensors The decipherment of the mechanism of monomer stoichiometry imbalance-promoted polymerization is instructive for further development of transition-metal-catalyzed non-stoichimetric polycouplings of mono-functionalized aromatic substrates with internal diynes to benefit the preparation of functional polymers with diverse structures. As you can see in part C of this report, 18 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16305014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305014.value: Development of new methodologies for the syntheses of fused-heterocyclic polymers with multiple functional substituents is of great interest. The unique electronic structures of the fused-heterocyclic repeat units are expected to endow the polymers with distinct materials properties and enable them to find high-tech applications in polymer optoelectronics systems, such as polymer photovoltaic cells, field effect transistors and light-emitting diodes. However, fused-heterocyclic polymers are difficult to synthesize. The conventional synthetic approaches to such polymers commonly involve multiple steps, harsh conditions, elaborate controls, and troublesome procedures. In this investigation, we have developed new polymerization routes for the synthesis of heterocyclic polymers based on alkyne monomers. These methods show many advantages such as simple operation, high efficiency, mild condition and high tolerance to functional groups. The obtained polymers are soluble, thermally stable and film-forming. They exhibit unique materials properties, making them promising candidates for high-technological applications. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the exploration of new systems. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the high-technological applications of our polymers in the fabrication of optoelectronic devices.

16305014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305014.value: Polymers with fused heterocyclic rings show unique electronic and photonic properties and have found practical applications in a variety of high-tech areas such as polymer solar cells, field-effect transistors, and light-emitting diodes. However, their synthesis often requires multiple steps of reactions, expensive organometallic catalysts, harsh polymerization conditions and troublesome product purification. Thus, the development of new, efficient synthetic methodologies for their preparation is of great scientific importance. In this investigation, we have developed simple, efficient polymerization tools for their synthesis. All the polymers are synthesized in high yields with high molecular weights. They are soluble and film-forming. They exhibit unique materials properties. Materials with such attributes are expected to find an array of applications.

16305214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305214.value: Energy landscape is an important concept in science, which has been widely used in many areas of physics, chemistry and biology. Applications of the energy landscape concept can be found in the calculation and measurement of the chemical reaction rate, lifetime of single molecular bonds (such as receptor-ligand bonds in biochemistry) and folding kinetics of proteins. Our general understanding of this type of problem is through the well-known Arrhenius-Kramers equation, which was obtained under an idealized condition for a single energy barrier. For many practical applications, however, one often encounters complex energy landscapes. There are few experimental systems in which one can actually visualize the energy landscape, and thus much of the work done so far is through computer simulations. A physical model system in which one can directly measure the energy landscape and track individual particle trajectories would be extremely valuable in testing different theoretical ideas. Recently, we developed a two-layer colloidal system to study colloidal diffusion over a periodic energy landscape. This work opens up a whole new realm of investigation at the single-particle level for a range of interesting problems associated with the diffusive and forced barrier-crossing dynamics over complex energy landscapes. In this research, we plan to carry out a systematic study of colloidal dynamics over well-controlled energy landscapes. In one set of experiments, we will use a tilted periodic landscape to study the effects of a tangential force on the barrier-crossing dynamics and non-equilibrium steady-state population distribution of the particles. In the second set of experiments, we will study colloidal diffusion over disordered energy landscapes. The main aim of the experiments is to find a relationship between the long-time diffusion and the characteristics of the disordered energy landscape. In the last set of experiments, we will investigate how the motion of the particles over the tilted energy landscape is influenced by the particle concentration and verify whether the hydrodynamic interactions between the particles, which are mediated through the solvent, can enhance the transport of colloidal particles. The proposed experiments are of fundamental interest for our general understanding of diffusive and forced barrier-crossing dynamics in soft matter systems, and they are also relevant to many biological applications involving complex energy landscapes. With the precise control of the energy landscapes, we will be able to provide a quantitative method by which many energy landscapes of practical importance may be characterized by the measurement of particle dynamics. 在許多物理、化學和生物領域中，能量地形是一個非常重要的科學概念。能量地形概念被應用到計算和測量化學反應速率，單分子鍵（如生物化學中受體和配體的結合）的存續時間，以及蛋白質折疊動力學。通過對單個勢壘的理想化近似，可以得到我們熟知的Arrhenius-Kramers方程，它為我們提供了對此類問題的大體理解。但是在實際應用中，我們經常遇到一些複雜的能量地形。很少的系統能讓我們直接地觀測到真實的能量地形，所以目前大部分的研究都是通過電腦模擬進行的。一個可以直接測量到能量地形同時跟蹤到單個粒子運動軌跡的系統對我們驗證不同的理論是十分有價值的。近期，我們發展出了一個兩層膠體粒子系統來研究膠體粒子在週期性能量地形上的擴散運動。這個工作打開了在單粒子層面上研究相關問題的全新領域，使我們可以更好地研究複雜能量地形上的擴散和外力驅動下勢壘跨越的動力學過程。 在本項研究中，我們計畫進行系統的實驗來研究在可控的能量地形上膠體粒子的運動規律。在第一項實驗中，我們將利用一個傾斜的週期性能量地形來研究切向力對勢壘跨越過程的作用，以及非平衡穩態下粒子數目的分佈規律。在第二項實驗中，我們將研究膠體粒子在無序能量地形上的擴散。它的主要目的在於尋找長時間的擴散系數和無序能量地形的特徵量之間的關係。最後一項實驗中，我們將研究在傾斜的能量地形上粒子濃度對粒子運動的影響，並且驗證由溶劑介導的粒子間的流體相互作用是否會增強膠體粒子的輸運。 上述實驗對我們理解軟物質系統中擴散和勢壘跨越過程的本質十分有意義，並且它們也與許多涉及到複雜能量地形的生物問題相關。有了對能量地形的精確控制，我們可以提供一種量化的方法，使得我們可以通過測量粒子的運動來表徵許多有著實際意義的能量地形。

16305214.label: Realisation of objectives
16305214.value: To fulfill the three research objectives, we carried out three experiments to study the diffusion dynamics of colloidal particles and biomolecules in complex energy landscapes. In one experiment, we studied the transport and diffusion of model colloidal particles over a titled periodic energy landscape. The periodic potential was provided by the colloidal spheres in the bottom layer forming a fixed crystalline pattern on a glass substrate. The corrugated surface of the bottom colloidal crystal provided a gravitational potential field for the diffusing particles in the top layer. By tilting the sample at an angle with respect to the vertical (gravity) direction, a tangential component of the gravitational force F was applied to the diffusing particles. This tilted two-layer colloidal system serves as model system for the study of force-assisted barrier-crossing dynamics over a periodic potential. The measured mean drift velocity v(F,E_b) and diffusion coefficient D(F,E_b) of the particles as a function of F and energy barrier height E_b were found to agree well with the exact results of the one-dimensional Langevin dynamics. We also studied the effects of the external force F on the non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) dynamics of the diffusing particles over the tilted periodic potential, in which detailed balance was broken due to the presence of a steady particle flux. The measured NESS probability density function Pss(x,y) of the particles was found to deviate from the equilibrium distribution P(x,y) to a different extent, depending on the driving force F or distance away from equilibrium. The experimental results were compared with the exact solution of the one-dimensional (1D) Smoluchowski equation and the numerical results of the 2D Smoluchowski equation. In the second experiment, we systematically studied the lateral motion of a transmembrane protein in live muscle cell membranes cultured from Xenopus embryos. The protein chosen for the study was acetylcholine receptor (AChR), which is a well- characterized neurotransmitter receptor for the study of neuromuscular junctions. The lateral mobility of AChRs plays an essential role in determining the response of the postsynaptic membrane to neurotransmitter stimuli. The individual AChRs were labelled with bright and photostable fluorescent quantum dots. With the help of an advanced single-molecule tracking algorithm, we were able to obtain a significantly large volume of individual AChR trajectories from more than 360 live cells over a wide range of sampling rates (up to 80 Hz) and long durations (up to 200 s). A central finding of this investigation is that the moving trajectories of the individual AChRs do not follow the Gaussian statistics for normal Brownian diffusion. Instead, we show for the first time that the measured probability density function P(delta x) of the protein displacement delta x has an exponential tail, which is robust and universal for cells under different conditions. In the third experiment, we systematically studied colloidal diffusion over a quenched two-dimensional (2D) disordered potential. In the experiment, a mixture of bidisperse silica spheres was used to form a randomly packed colloidal monolayer on the bottom substrate, which provided a disordered gravitational potential field U(x,y) to the diffusing particles in the top layer. With the techniques of optical microscopy and multiparticle tracking, we measured the population statistics of the diffusing particles in the top layer and constructed the potential U(x,y) via the Boltzmann distribution. Using the simultaneously obtained energetics and dynamics information, we tested the theory and demonstrate the applications of the newly constructed 2D random potential. Via the above three experiments, the three project objectives were fully achieved.

16305214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305214.value: Colloidal transport and diffusion over a tilted periodic potential: dynamics of individual particles. The energy landscape is an important concept in science, which has been widely used in many areas of physics, chemistry and biology. Without an external force, the thermally activated barrier crossing occurs with an exponentially small probability when the energy barrier height E_b is much larger than the thermal energy of the particle. This situation is changed completely when an external force F is applied to the particle, so that the energy barrier is lowered in the direction of force. Based on the experimental results discussed above, we showed analytically and verified experimentally that in the intermediate range of F, v(F,E_b) and D(F, E_b) have a new scaling form. The experiment provided crucial information for our general understanding of the forced-barrier-crossing dynamics beyond the linear response theory and the Arrhenius–Kramers equation. Results from this work were published in Soft Matter and Physical Review E. Dynamic heterogeneity and non-Gaussian statistics for acetylcholine receptors in live cell membrane. In this work, we showed that the lateral motion of the AChRs in live cell membranes does not follow the Gaussian statistics for normal Brownian diffusion. From a careful analysis of a large volume of the protein trajectories obtained over a wide range of sampling rates and long durations, we found that the normalized histogram of the protein displacements shows an exponential tail, which is robust and universal for cells under different conditions. The experiment indicates that the observed non-Gaussian statistics and dynamic heterogeneity are inherently linked to the slow but active remodeling of the underlying cortical actin network. This work was published in Nature Communications. Colloidal diffusion over a quenched two-dimensional random potential. Our work demonstrated that the two-layer colloidal system is a versatile platform for the study of colloidal diffusion over complex potential landscapes. The disordered configurations generated vary from crystal-like structures with different amounts of defects and grain boundaries introduced by the ‘‘dopant’’ particles to various glass-like structures with either well-mixed states or micro-structured domains. This method thus provides a well-controlled and convenient way to vary the potential landscapes with different disorders. With the simultaneous tracking of the diffusing particles and determining the underlying potential landscape at the single-particle resolution, one is able to study quantitatively a range of interesting issues involved in colloidal diffusion over random fields. This work was published in Soft Matter.

16305214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305214.value: The understanding of thermally activated and force-assisted barrier-crossing dynamics for colloidal diffusion over complex potential landscapes achieved through the research discussed above provides a useful foundation for the further study of diffusive transport in disordered media of practical interest, such as transport of molecules through porous media. So far, we have only explored some well-controlled potential landscapes experimentally. It would certainly be very interesting to extend our study to more complex potential landscapes of practical relevance. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research along this direction.

16305214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305214.value: Diffusion in disordered media is a common problem encountered in many practical applications, including biological applications ranging from molecular motors moving along heterogeneous substrates to the transport of proteins within cells and in cell membranes. While considerable theoretical efforts have been made to solve this problem, systematic experimental investigations aimed at testing the theoretical predictions are quite limited. In this research, we developed a two-layer colloidal system to study colloidal diffusion and transport over controlled potential landscapes. Our experiments demonstrated the importance of quantitative characterization and of understanding the barrier-crossing dynamics of the particles over different types of potential landscapes. Such an understanding opens the door to a wide variety of new experiments using a colloidal monolayer or a patterned substrate as a template to study colloidal diffusion over random potentials. In particular, we demonstrated that the newly developed methods and understanding in physics could be successfully applied to biological systems, such as understanding protein diffusion in live cell membranes.

16305314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305314.value: Aromatic compounds are very stable and have low chemical reactivity due to the high resonance energy (c.f. aromaticity, Huckel’s rule). Consequently, dearomatization of aromatic compounds by breaking the aromaticity (~36 kcal/mole) is very challenging. Over the past few decades synthetic chemists have successfully developed a number of strategies for dearomatization, among which phenol oxidative dearomatization (POD) has achieved the greatest success in organic synthesis. The synthetic utilities of POD have been extensively demonstrated in the context of total synthesis of complex natural products by taking advantage of the reactivity of cyclohexadienones derived from POD for a variety of annulations including [4+2], [3+2] and [5+2] cycloadditions as well as 1,2- and 1,4-addition reactions. However, carbon-carbon bond cleavage of phenol derivatives has yet to be explored. As a result, we will develop two new strategies in this proposal for carbon-carbon bond cleavage of phenol derivatives, which will greatly expand the synthetic utilities of POD in organic synthesis. The first idea of our proposal is to develop a convenient method for the stereoselective synthesis of highly substituted cyclopentenone from phenol derivatives through cleavage of phenol’s carbon-carbon bond, which involves a sequence of transformations: POD, Oxa-Michael cyclization, PCC-mediated oxidative ring expansion and Knoevenagel condensation. This new synthetic strategy: ring-contraction of phenol to cyclopentenone, will be further demonstrated in the synthesis of complex natural products or clinical agents. The second idea of our proposal is to develop a novel method for stereoselective synthesis of highly functionalized tetrahydropyran (THP) from phenol derivatives through cleavage of phenol’s carbon-carbon bond, which could be realized by POD, oxa-Michael cyclization, epoxidation and Eschenmoser fragmentation. The synthetic potential of this new strategy could be explored in the total synthesis of bioactive THP-containing natural products. In addition to the development of new synthetic methods by exploitation of POD, the second part of this proposal will be focused on the first total synthesis of potent antiviral spirooliganones A and B by making full use of arene chemistry, including aromatic Claisen rearrangement, hetereo-Diels-Alder cycloaddition of quinone methide and POD. The short (total 15 steps) synthetic route would permit a practical supply of these scarce natural products and allow us to prepare the analogues for detailed biological studies. The synthetic studies proposed here could provide chemical evidence supporting the biosynthetic hypothesis of these two potent antiviral natural products and greatly expand the synthetic utilities of POD in total synthesis of complex natural products. 摘要：芳香族化合物由于有很高的共振能量 （参见芳香性与休克尔规则）而具有非常好的稳定性和较低的化学反应活性。 因此，通过打破芳香族化合物的芳香性 （~ 36 千卡/摩尔） 是非常具有挑战性的。然而，几十年以来，合成化学家已经成功发展了大量的去芳香环化的策略，其中苯酚氧化去芳香环化（POD） 在有机合成中取得了巨大的成功。通过有效的利用POD产物（环氧己烷二烯酮）在各种派生环加成反应包括 [4 + 2]，[3 + 2] 和 [5 + 2]反应，以及 1，2-加成反应和1，4-加成反应，POD反应广泛的应用在复杂天然产物全合成中，它在合成中的有效性已经得到很好的证明。然而，对于酚衍生物的碳-碳键断裂的探索性研究尚刚刚开始。因此，在项基金计划书中，我们提出了两种新的苯酚衍生物碳-碳键断裂的策略来会扩展和体现POD 在有机合成中的新应用。第一种策略是从酚衍生物通过苯酚的碳-碳键断裂与及一系列后续的高立体选择性的反应来发展多取代环戊烯酮的简易合成方法，即： POD，氧杂-迈克尔环化、PCC氧化环扩张和 Knoevenagel 缩合。这个新的合成策略： 苯酚缩环合成环戊烯酮，将应用于合成复杂的天然产物或临床药物。我们提出的第二种苯酚衍生物碳-碳键断裂策略是发展种新合成方法来合成具有高度官能化和立体选择性的四氢吡喃 （THP）， 即：苯酚衍生物的碳-碳键断裂可以从通过POD、 氧杂-Michael 环化、 环氧化反应和它的全碎片实现。这一新战略具有很好应用前景，特别是在含有THP活性天然产物中的全合成。除了通过充分利用 POD 来发展新的合成方法学，我们计划书的第二部分是探索首次全合成具有强抗病毒的spirooliganones A 和 B。充分利用芳烃化学，包括芳香克莱森重排、杂-Diels-Alder 环加成反应和POD反应。如此简短的合成路线（总 15 步骤）将允许我们供应这些稀缺的天然产物以及类似物，以便于做详尽的生物学研究。另外，这些合成研究能提供化学证据支持这些两个强效的抗病毒天然产物的生物合成假说，也能进一步扩大 POD 在复杂的天然产物全合成中的应用。

16305314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305314.value: This project (Phenol Oxidative Dearomatization, POD) led to many exciting findings in synthetic methodology development and total synthesis of natural products, which are summarized below. (1) Spirooliganones: We have achieved the first biomimetic total syntheses of potent antiviral spirooliganones A and B. Our synthesis featured an unprecedented cascade reaction involving aromatic Claisen rearrangement/o-quinone methide formation/hetero-Diels−Alder cycloaddition and phenol oxidative dearomatization (POD)/spirocyclization. In addition, the successful implementation of hetero-Diels−Alder cycloaddition of o-quinone methide provided compelling chemical evidence for the biogenetic hypothesis of spirooliganones A and B (Org. Lett. 2014, 16, 3740). Our key discovery of in situ generation of o-quinone methide from aromatic Claisen rearrangement was further exploited as a general method for the synthesis of biologically important 2H-chromenes (Chem. Commun. 2017, 53, 6021-6024). (2) Cephalosporolides and penisporolides: we have developed a convergent bioinspired strategy for synthesis of the unique tricyclic 2,2-dimethyl-[5,5]-spiroacetal-cis-fused-γ-lactone (Me2SAFL) through the POD approach, which was further elaborated to collective total syntheses of 12 Me2SAFLs, corresponding to the purported structures of cephalosporolide H (CesH), cephalosporolide I (CesI), penisporolide B (PenB), and their possible diastereomers. Comprehensive and meticulous NMR data analysis of the 12 synthetic Me2SAFLs and the natural products allowed us to conclude that the tricyclic SAFL cores of CesH, CesI and PenB should be revised and that the side chains required an unknown constitutional structure revision (J. Org. Chem. 2016, 81, 4325-4339). Most importantly, our synthetic studies provided chemical evidence to support a possible uniform biosynthesis of all SAFL-containing natural products through a ring contraction rearrangement of 10-membered lactones to the characteristic tricyclic SAFLs. In addition, a reliable NMR method has been established for stereochemical assignments of the spiroisomers of Me2SAFLs, which would be very useful in studies of synthetic/natural Me2SAFLcontaining molecules (Org. Chem. Front. 2017, 4, 140-146). 3) Ascospiroketals: We proposed a new biosynthetic pathway for the tricyclic core of ascospiroketals A and B, which guided us to develop a novel synthetic strategy that lead to convergent asymmetric total syntheses of ent-ascospiroketals A and B (Org. Lett. 2016, 18, 1936-1939). Seven additional diastereomers of ent-ascospiroketal B were prepared and allowed us to conclusively substantiate our synthetic ascospiroketal B. Our synthesis was enabled by a ring contraction rearrangement of the 10-membered lactones to the structurally unique tricyclic 5,5-spiroacetal-cis-fused-γ-lactone (SAFL) framework. The synthetic studies not only greatly extended our biomimetic strategy developed for total synthesis of cephalosporolides but also provided solid chemical evidence supporting plausibly similar biosynthesis of ascospiroketals and cephalosporolides.

16305314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305314.value: Potentials for further development of this project include bioactivity and synthetic chemistry. The project produced a library of natural products and natural product-like compounds, which could be evaluated for potential biological activities. However, the current small GRF grant and time constraint does not allow us to further explore the medicinal value of these molecules. While in the near future, we do plan to exploit the treasure of these synthetic molecules if further funding is secured. Secondly, the potentials of synthetic chemistry include (1) to generalize the biomimetic POD strategy to be an efficient synthetic method for the synthesis of decanolides (10-membered lactones) and tricyclic SAFLs; (2) to extend the POD strategy for the synthesis of 9-, 11-, and 12-membered lactones; (3) to investigate the effect of oxygen of the cyclic ether on the PCC-mediated oxidative ring expansion.

16305314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305314.value: Natural products are the main source of new drugs for all types of diseases and the major obstacle of translating a natural product into a new drug is the scarce of the natural product. This research project is to solve the supply problem of some natural products by developing new and efficient chemical synthesis. Most importantly, a general biomimetic synthetic strategy has been developed for the collective biomimetic total synthesis of bioactive natural products including spirooliganones, cephalosporolides, penisporolides, ascospiroketals, and 2H-chromenes. In addition, these chemical syntheses led to a library of rarely-available, structurally complex and unique molecules for biological activity evaluation, which might result in discovery of new lead compounds and establishment of structure-activity relationship.

16305414.label: Project Objectives
16305414.value: To examine other regions of the string landscape to check our proposal that a vanishingly small cosmological constant is quite generic in string theory. To study the phenomenological properties of these string vacua, in particular the supersymmetry breaking and the cosmological moduli issues.

16305414.label: Realisation of objectives
16305414.value: Arguably the biggest puzzle in physics is why the cosmological constant (i.e., the vacuum energy density, or the dark energy) is so very small (one hundred and twenty orders of magnitude smaller than the natural scale set by Newton's constant, which sets the Planck scale). Since string theory has no free parameter and the cosmological constant is in principle calculable in terms of Newton's constant, this puzzle can be addressed. We give explicit models of the string landscape to demonstrate how this can be accomplished, via a probabilistic approach. This has been clearly achieved.

16305414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305414.value: The dark energy is the biggest mystery in fundamental physics: Why it is there? Why is it so big today ? Why is it so very small compared to the scale set by Newton's constant ? Here we provide an exciting explanation in the framework of the string theory landscape. Along this line, 2 publications have resulted : S.-H. H. Tye, ``Why the cosmological constant is so small: A string theory perspective,'' Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 21, 1803 (2017) doi:10.4310/ATMP.2017.v21.n7.a9 [arXiv:1801.09173 [hep-th]]. S.-H. H. Tye and S. S. C.Wong, ``Linking Light Scalar Modes with A Small Positive Cosmological Constant in String Theory,'' JHEP 1706, 094 (2017) doi:10.1007/JHEP06(2017)094 [arXiv:1611.05786 [hep-th]]. We work out explicit models of the string landscape to demonstrate how this can be accomplished, via a probabilistic approach. The particular models are the multi-complex structure model and the racetrack K"ahler uplift model in Type IIB string theory. This has been clearly achieved. We also show that the scalar fields (i.e., moduli and the dilaton) have masses so small that they may play the role of fuzzy dark matter in explaining the role of dark matter in terms of structure formation in the universe.

16305414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305414.value: Further development have been pushed along the following two main directions: (1) With the natural presence of very light scalar modes, including axions, the fuzzy dark matter scenario has been further pushed to incorporate the solitonic properties coming from the wave dark matter study. We find evidence that more than one light field is necessary to accommodate the existing observational data on dwarf galaxies and the Milky Way. (2) We find that fitting the median value of the cosmological constant to the observed value, a scale of about 100 GeV naturally emerges. This is the electroweak scale despite that fact that we do not know where and how the standard model fits into the string landscape. Both of these directions are being further explored.

16305414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305414.value: The dark energy is the biggest mystery in fundamental physics: Why it is there? Why is it so big today ? It contributes 76% of the total energy-matter content of our universe today. Why is it so very small compared to the scale set by Newton's constant ? It is 122 orders of magnitude smaller than the natural scale set by Newton's constant that appears in Einstein's theory of general relativity. We can always tune the cosmological constant in Einstein's theory to such a small value, but quantum effects will destroy such tuning. Some physicists consider this to be the most puzzling problem in physics. Here we provide an exciting explanation in the framework of the string theory landscape. Since string theory has no free parameters, there is nothing to be fine-tuned. On the other hand, there are many possibilities in the string landscape, so we argue and show that such a small dark energy is natural statistically in the landscape.

16305514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305514.value: As a new state of matter, the topological insulator is considered as a very important discovery in condensed matter physics and materials sciences in the last decade. A topological insulator is insulating in the bulk, but metallic at its boundaries owing to the topological origin of the band structure. The metallic edge or surface states are immune to disorder or impurities and robust against the deformation of the system’s geometry. The exotic magneto-electric behavior and the peculiar properties of interfaces between this new material and others make it an attractive platform for exploring new physics such as searching for Majorana fermions and magnetic monopoles and to explore potential applications in spintronics and quantum computation. In this project, we propose to experimentally study the hybrid structure of 3D topological insulators (TI), superconductors (SC), and ferromagnetic materials (FM). The hybrid structures will be formed by mechanical transfer of exfoliated layered superconductor flakes onto exfoliated Bi-compound based 3D topological insulator nanostructures and flakes and by exfoliated Bi-compound based 3D topological insulator nanostructures and flakes direct onto insulating ferromagnetic substrates. We aim to carry out magneto-transport investigation of superconducting proximity effect in TI/SC hybrid devices and to explore the edge states formed at the TI/SC device boundaries due to proximity effect and the interaction of these edge states. We aim to reveal and demonstrate the theoretically predicted new transport phenomena in TI/FM hybrid structures due to the breaking of time reversal symmetry by the exchange interaction with a proximate of FM. We believe that the fulfillment of this project will greatly advance our understanding of the interactions of topological surface states with SC and FM, and the successful outcome of this project will pave the way for future applications of 3D topological insulators. 作為一種全新的物質形態，拓撲絕緣體被認為是過去十年裡凝聚 態物理及材料科學研究領域一項非常重要的發現。雖然拓撲絕緣 體的體內部是絕緣的，但是由於其能帶結構的拓撲性質，它卻具 有金屬性的邊界態，並且由於拓撲保護，無序度或雜質對該邊緣 態或表面態的影響甚微。拓撲絕緣體不僅本身具有新奇的電磁特 性，而且它和其他材料所構成的界面也具有非常奇特的物理性質。 這使得拓撲絕緣體成為人們探索馬約拉納費米子和磁單極子等新 物理的理想平台，在自旋電子學及量子計算領域也具有非常重要 的應用前景。在本科研項目里，我們將深入研究由三維拓撲絕緣 體與超導體或鐵磁材料所構成的混合結構。我們將通過機械剝離 的方法來獲得三維拓撲絕緣體和超導體的薄片，并利用機械轉移 的手段將二者疊放在一起以形成拓撲絕緣體/超導體混合結構。 我們也將利用機械轉移的方法把三維拓撲絕緣體薄片放置在絕緣 鐵磁襯底上來獲得拓撲絕緣體/鐵磁體混合機構。我們致力於通 過磁輸運的方法研究拓撲絕緣體/超導體混合結構的超導臨近效 應，并深入探索由該效應在拓撲絕緣體/超導體界面處產生的邊 緣態及邊緣態間的相互作用。我們也將深入研究拓撲絕緣體/鐵 磁體混合結構的磁臨近效應，力圖揭示理論預期的時間反演對 稱破缺所導致的新奇量子輸運現象。我們相信本科研項目的順 利執行將會極大促進我們對拓撲表面態與超導電性或鐵磁性之 間相互作用的理解，并為未來三維拓撲絕緣體的實際應用鋪平 前進的道路。

16305514.label: Realisation of objectives
16305514.value: We have successfully exfoliated Bi2Se3. We have fabricated devices based on obtained flakes of n and p type Bi2Se3. We have measured magneto transport properties of these devices and observed SdH oscillations. We have successfully fabricated the Bi2Se3/Nb devices by mechanical transfer of exfoliated Bi2Se3 flakes onto Nb substrate and by e-beam lithography. We have measured transport properties across this hetero interface. We have observed three individual superconducting phases being induced in Bi2Se3 due to the superconducting proximity effect. We have also found unusual superconducting phase at the interface. We have studied 2D superconductivity found at the interface of the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. We have investigated the anisotropic magnetic responses using high-resolution cross-sectional STEM imaging to reveal the distributions and positions of the interstitial Fe atoms residing in the FeTe layer and systematic magnetic characterizations to discovery of a strong anisotropic magnetic response. We have used fast pulsed-signal techniques to measure the current induced depairing in the superconducting interface of the heterostructure. We have studied the current-resistance and temperature-resistance curves in the interface superconductor. We have also studied the robustness of the interfacial superconductivity and 2D vortex dynamics in this 2D superconducting system using four as-grown and aged Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure with different Bi2Te3 epilayer thickness (3, 5, 7, 14 nm). We have systematically investigated the magnetotransport properties of Cd3As2 microribbons, in which the carrier density is found to obey an Arrhenius’s law and observed negative magneto resistance in parallel magnetic fields up to 66% at 50 K and visible at room temperatures. In perpendicular magnetic fields, a positive linear magnetoresistance up to 1,670% at 14 T and 2 K is also observed. We have fabricated the Bi2Se3/YIG hybrid devices by mechanical exfoliation of Bi2Se3 direct on insulating YIG substrates. We have tried to carry out transport measurements of these devices but no effect of YIG on Bi2Se3 has been observed. We think it is because of rough surface of YIG substrate which causes very weak coupling between Bi2Se3 and YIG. We have grown Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3 flakes by chemical vapor deposition method on SiO2/Si substrate where the quality of flakes is identified by Raman and EDX. We have studied their magneto transport properties. We have also tried to grow Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3 flakes on FM CFO substrate but with limited success as the flakes were too small and too thick for further studies. We have epitaxial grown Sb2Se3/Bi2Se3 heterostructures by molecular beam epitaxy. We have successfully observed the proximity effect in these heterostructures, where topological surface states can be induced into the ordinary insulator Sb2Se3 by coupling with the strong topological insulator, Bi2Se3.

16305514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305514.value: Shubnikov–de Haas (SdH) oscillation plays an important role in clarifying the existence of topological surface states. We have observed the SdH oscillations in both n and p type Bi2Se3 flake samples. We show that the observed SdH oscillations originate from the topological surface states and we also deduced the cyclotron mass, Dingle temperature, and Fermi velocity of the systems. This work has been presented in EP2DS conference and published in 2D Materials. We have found that the superconductivity remains robust even when the thickness of Bi2Te3 epilayer is down to 3 nm after two years’ air exposure and exhibits the 2D vortex dynamics in this Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. We have discovered a strong anisotropic magnetic response, and demonstrated the interplays among the different magnetic structures of this heterostructure and its interfacial superconductivity. We have measured the current induced depairing providing information on the magnetic penetration depth and superfluid density, which in turn shed light on the nature of the normal state that underlies this interfacial superconductivity. We have observed a transition in the current-resistance and temperature-resistance curves that quantitatively agrees with the Likharev vortex-explosion phenomenon. These results are published in Sci. Rep., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter, Phys. Rev. B, and Physica C: Superconductivity and its applications. We have observed experimental evidence of the chiral anomaly induced negative MR in our Cd3As2 ribbons with low carrier density when E//B and a large positive linear magnetoresistance when EB. Our work shows that the carrier density plays an important role in the observation of the negative and linear MR and their magnitudes. This result is published in Nat. Commun. We have carried out magnetotransport measurements for CVD grown Bi2Se3 nanoplates, which have shown pronounced weak anti-localization effect in the low B-field region, linear MR in the perpendicular high B-field, and a weak negative MR in the in-plane direction. These magnetotransport features are considered to originate from the topological surface states. These results are included in an MPhil thesis. We have studied the electrical transport properties of epitaxial grown Sb2Se3/Bi2Se3 heterostructures by MBE. The weak anti-localization effect observed can be tuned by adjusting the thickness of the Sb2Se3 layer. This phenomenon indicates an introduction of an additional coherent channel in samples with thin Sb2Se3 capping layer. These results are included in a PhD thesis.

16305514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305514.value: What we have achieved so far indicating that topological insulator based hybrid structures especially with 2D ferromagnetic materials are the most important issue to be explored in future. Using 2D magnetic materials allow us to form van der Waals heterostructures, which can achieve good interface to reveal proximity effect and lead to new physical phenomena. Further exploration of TI based van der Waals heterostructures should be future actions to be taken.

16306214.label: Project Objectives
16306214.value: A special algorithm will be designed to speed up the optimization process in image-based scattering light imaging recovery. We expect our new design and algorithm will reduce the image recovery time by at least an order of magnitude compared to standard techniques. Research will be carried out on the feasibility of illumination with quasi-incoherent light. The influence of the degree of coherence when using wavefront shaping will be quantified. A non-invasive scattered light method for imaging a fluorescent object without mechanical scanning will be introduced. The mechanical scanning part of current systems will be replaced with a SLM. The possibility of specially coded modulated spatial light will be investigated for non-invasive detection application. The application of the wavefront shaping technique for optical cloaking and optical illusion will be studied. The quality of the wavefront shaping system will be improved and the ability to cloak and reshape a complex object will be demonstrated.

16306214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306214.value: 如何克服散射介质的干扰而看到目标物体或者形成清晰的成像，多年来一直是一个活跃的研究领域。 非均匀介质中折射率的变化会引起光的散射，而这种散射可能导致成像质量大幅度下降。不幸的是，这些散射在许多成像应用中是不可避免的，例如在天文观测中遇到的大气湍流，透过纤维组织进行生物医疗显微成像等等。因此，能够克服散射介质的影响获得清晰的图像在应用上有很高价值。近年来开发的一些技术，如光学相干断层扫描（OCT），相位共轭法，散射 矩阵测量以及波前整形，已经开始用来解决非均匀介质的散射问题了。其中相位共轭法和散射矩阵技术，涉及的光学比较复杂，通常只应用于强散射介质。OCT方法也是如此。另一方面，波前整形技术相对来说比较简单和直接。 波前整形法使用空间光调制器（SLM）调制的光场的空间分布（主要是相位的空间分布）来补偿经过随机散射介质所产生的波前畸变，从而实现成像质量的提高。有效的波前整形系统通常包含了闭环优化的算法系统，但迭代过程中优化程序可能需要数分钟才能实现最优化。 此外，目前的波前整形技术需要优化目标提供反馈，最常用的做法是插入信标或检测器，这往往在应用中是不方便或不可能实现的。最近的一个重大突破是通过非侵入性的成像实验上透过散射介质对荧光发光物质进行成像。然而，它依然涉及一些机械扫描过程，对系统的速度和稳定性都会有影响。这个问题可以简单的用SLM取代扫描机制解决。最后， 波前整形技术中，相位优化计算的目标的可以是真正的实物对象或任意图像。如果优化目标是已知对象的图像，整个系统就是一个通常的成像装置，使人透过散射介质看到对象。然而如果优化目标被设置成另一个图像，该系统则可以产生其他一些有趣的应用，例如光学错觉或隐形装置。这将开创一个不同而相对简单的途径来实现宏观光学隐形和视觉错觉。 在本文中，我们将提出一个新的基于SLM的闭环优化系统，通过复杂图像计算机程序恢复实现波前整形。其中专门设计的快速优化算法将用于加快优化过程，预期优化速度至少有一个数量级的改进。通过这一系统，我们将研究常规随机散射介质在准非相干光源下的散射性质，以及在无需机械扫描的情况下透过散射介质对荧光光源的非侵入性成像问题。最后， 我们将进一步展示用于光学隐形和虚拟成像的波前整形技术。本研究的成果可用于图像恢复以及透过多重散射非均匀介质后光学成像质量的改善，也将实际应用于多种生物医学过程，诸如生物深层组织下的医学成像，透过随机介质的强光非线性励磁或激光精确瞄准杀死癌细胞等等。

16306214.label: Realisation of objectives
16306214.value: We have successfully realized the four main objectives set out in the original proposal. The first objective was to develop a special algorithm to speed up (at least an order of magnitude increase in speed) the optimization process in image-based scattering light imaging recovery. We used a phase retrieval technique to recover the distorted wavefront after it passes through a scattering medium. In the conventional method, the wavefront of an optimized shaped is usually calculated by optimization techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA). In our case, the GA-based hardware iteration can then be replaced by computer simulation in the phase retrieval technique to determine the wavefront modulation pattern, resulting in high speed wavefront recovery. Furthermore, using a phase conjugation method and a Fresnel phase scheme was further implemented to speed up the system so that the entire imaging loop can finish in just a few seconds, which is two orders of magnitude faster than the conventional hardware iteration technique. Our results show good fidelity of the recovered image. The present results may contribute toward the realization of real-time imaging restoration in a disordered media. With the success of realizing objective one, it is quite easy to implement the fourth objective of optical cloaking and illusion based on wavefront shaping technique using essentially the same setup (i.e., spatial light modulator (SLM) and CCD) as in objective one mentioned above. We use a combination of phase retrieval and GA to search for the phase pattern for a designed target with given object input. Once this phase pattern is found and loaded into the SLM, the same target will be displayed for an arbitrary input object. A proof-of-principle experiment of turning any object into a specific letter “H” is demonstrated. The second objective was to look at the feasibility of using quasi-incoherent light for illumination. Laser was used for the experiments for objective 1 &2 if one can replace the light source of wavefront shaping from laser to incoherent light that might be more practical. While most of scattering imaging techniques make use of Memory Effect (ME), it has been shown that speckle correlation technique is an easier and more effective method for incoherent light scattering imaging. We have done some research along this direction. When a thin scattering medium is introduced into the imaging system, the Point Spread Function (PSF) becomes a speckle pattern determined by the property of the scattering medium. This scattering pattern is shown to be shift-invariant within the ME range. The imaging process can be denoted as a correlation function of the PSF and the object distribution function I=Obj* PSF (Physica A 168, 49-65 (1990)). If we can calibrate a thin scattering medium by detecting its PSF in a certain object plane, any tested object in that object plane can be recovered by capturing its scattering light I and then doing a deconvolution operation, i.e., Obj=Deconv(I, PSF). Our preliminary result showed that a test object (Letter of “G”) can be recovered by simply deconvoluting its scattering light and system’s PSF. As we can see, this PSF technique is simpler and more effective than the originally proposed wavefront shaping one using CCD and LSM. It does not need any expensive LSM, rigorous alignment of the optics or a complicated control algorithm. Objective three was to replace the mechanical scanning system with an electrically controlled SLM for non-invasive imaging of a fluorescent object behind a scattering medium. However, we found the recent result by Bertolotti and co-workers on speckle deconvolution technique to be more interesting and more appropriate for our objective three (Nature Photon. 8, 784-790 (2014)). This speckle deconvolution technique has been developed rapidly in recent years. The difficulty of using an SLM and a fluorescent light is similar to what we mentioned for objective two above, thus we changed our plan a little bit and made use of speckle deconvolution technique to realize the goal of non-invasive imaging behind a scattering medium. We have applied this speckle deconvolution technique for non-invasive imaging of an object behind a scattering medium. When a thin scattering medium is illuminated by an incoherent light (here a green LED is used), light transmission behavior is just like a shift-invariant imaging system within scattering medium’s ME range. According to the equation I=Obj* PSF, suppose we get a known-beforehand reference object ‘Obj’ and its corresponding speckle pattern ‘I’. The PSF of the scattering system can be derived by deconvolution of ‘Obj’ and ‘I’. After we get the system’s PSF, any other unknown test object can be recovered by deconvolution of its speckle and the derived PSF. Our experimental result demonstrated that an unknown test object (letter H) placed beside a reference object (i.e., letter I), then using the system PSF obtained from the reference object alone, the image of the test object H can be recovered. This speckle deconvolution method can realize non-invasive imaging more easily, although it needs a priori knowledge of the test object. However, the knowledge of an object with a certain shape under a scattering medium can be achieved. For example, the object detected by noninvasive method (Nature 491, 232-234, 2012) can serve as a reference. Besides, the organ detected by X-ray technique below the skin can act as a reference. Meanwhile, in many medical applications, the surroundings of a test object also play an important role in diagnosis and treatment. So the development of a control scenario with a reference object is potentially possible and necessary. Overall, we have realized the four objectives in the proposal, although the detailed methodology to reach the objective three was slightly different from that set out in the original proposal. However, this is nature of research, as time goes by (the time between when the proposal was written and when we actually started the experiment was 2-3 years), with new theory and research results, one has to adapt and change the strategy to reach the objectives in a better and more effective way.

16306214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306214.value: Normally, recovery of the scattered wavefront is done by optimized technique using an SLM and CCD hardware. This process is very slow due to limitation of the hardware refreshing rate, particularly that of the liquid crystal modulator. We have developed an improved method for such an optimization process. The core of the proposed method is to firstly detect the disturbed wavefront, and then to calculate the modulation phase pattern by computer simulation using phase retrieval technique. Fast processing speed resulting in high quality images has been achieved with this new approach. Using supposition of conjugated phase of the scattering wavefront and a Fresnel phase scheme, more than two orders of magnitude improvement in processing speed for imaging restoration was shown compared to the SLM-CCD iteration method (see Part C8 ref. 1 &2). Our results show good fidelity of the recovered image. The present results may contribute toward the realization of real-time imaging restoration in a disordered medium. This wavefront shaping technique for imaging through a random medium was extended to cloaking and illusion, here by using a combination of phase retrieval and GA to search for the phase pattern for a designed target with given object input. Once this phase pattern is found and loaded into the SLM, the same target will be displayed for an arbitrary input object (see Part C9 ref. 4). Therefore, an illusion image is produced for whatever the input object. This is a particularly simple way to produce illusion and cloaking. We have developed a simple method to do non-invasive imaging of an object behind a scattering medium using speckle deconvolution and an incoherent light source. Here when the light passes through a thin scattering medium in an imaging system, the Point Spread Function (PSF) becomes a speckle pattern determined by the property of the scattering medium. Thus, by detecting this speckle pattern and perform a deconvolution on the PSF, we can recover the object image in the image plane of the system (see Part C8 ref. 3). This technique for imaging restoration through scattering medium is simpler and more effective than the wavefront shaping one mentioned above. It does not need any expensive LSM, rigorous alignment of the optics or a complicated control algorithm.

16306214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306214.value: We found the latest technique of using speckle correlation and PSF deconvolution for image restoration through a random medium to be most promising for real world application. As mentioned before, it is simpler, cheaper and more effective than the wavefront shaping one. However the knowledge of an object with a certain shape under a scattering medium can be achieved. For example, the object detected by noninvasive method (Nature 491, 232-234 (2012)) can serve as a reference. Besides, the organ detected by X-ray technique below the skin can act as a reference. Meanwhile, in many medical applications, the surroundings of a tested object also play an important role in diagnosis and treatment. Therefore, the development of a control scenario with a reference object is potentially possible and necessary.

16306214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306214.value: The ability to see through fog or an object embedded in a scattering medium (i.e., a tumor under the skin or in tissue) is very important from a technological point of view. We have developed a wavefront shaping technique and a new algorithm to restore an object image at high speed through a scattering medium. The entire imaging loop can finish in just a few seconds, which is two orders of magnitude faster than the conventional hardware iteration technique. Our results show good fidelity of the recovered image. We remove the expensive spatial modulator and laser, and simply use an incoherent light source and a camera to detect the scattered light to further improve this method. Applying the sparkle deconvolution scattered light pattern recorded in the camera, an object image through the scattering medium can be restored with high fidelity. The present results show strong potential toward the practical realization of real-time imaging restoration in a disordered media.

16307014.label: Project Objectives
16307014.value: Unravel the nature of the active sites in the doped VOx/TiO2 catalyst responsible for its high reactivity for selective oxidation of NH3 to N2 and partial oxidation of H2S to S6, and particularly the exact roles of the dopants (i.e., Nb, W, P) and the matrix (i.e., SiO2, mixed SiO2-MOx aerogels) on the activity, selectivity, stability and accessibility of the catalytic sites for the reactions; Determine the primary reaction pathways for the transformation of NH3 and H2S pollutants in air into N2 and S6 over the doped VOx/TiO2 catalyst at room temperature using in situ and operando spectroscopic techniques to observe the molecular mechanism and process of capture, transformation and inactivation of the pollutants; Carry out an optimization of the catalyst for treatment of NH3 and H2S based on the new knowledge gained of the active sites and reaction mechanism; Evaluate the engineering performance of the optimized catalyst under practical use conditions that involve a mixture of pollutants at high space velocity (GHSV), room temperature and humid conditions.

16307014.label: Realisation of objectives
16307014.value: (1) In-situ and operando spectroscopy techniques were employed to investigate the active sites in doped VOx/TiO2 catalysts. The V-O-Ti sites were active for selective oxidations of NH3 and H2S. It was discovered that on polymeric VOx species on TiO2, NH3 selective oxidation to N2 proceeds through formation of hydrazinium ion followed by its decomposition to N2 and H2O. H2S was selectively oxidized to S6 and H2O on V-O-Ti sites and sulfur solids were deposited. Nb and P serve to stabilize VOx dispersion on titania surface and improves catalyst stability. Embedding VOx/TiO2 in mesoporous silica aerogel matrix enhances the catalytic activity of NH3 and H2S selective oxidation by more than an order of magnitude. The Ti-O-Si sites are responsible for enhanced NH3 and H2S adsorption facilitating their conversions. The aerogel also protects the catalyst from moisture. The catalyst is also active for catalytic oxidation of odor causing volatile organic compounds. (2) The primary reaction pathways for NH3 and H2S selective oxidation over doped VOx/TiO2 was revealed by in situ FTIR and operando micro-Raman spectroscopy technique. It was observed that ammonia adsorbs on V-O-Ti sites and reacts to form an adsorbed hydrazinium intermediate that rapidly decomposes to N2 and H2O at room temperature. H2S reaction involves the oxidation of the adsorbed molecules and deposition of solid S6 on the catalyst. (3) The catalyst composition and preparation were optimized to attain high conversion rate at near room temperature without the formation of undesired byproducts such as NOx and SOx. (4) The optimized catalyst performed well for NH3 and H2S selective oxidation at near room temperature and tolerates humid conditions. A field study carried out using gas mixtures containing NH3, H2S and VOCs drawn from a sewer line on-campus demonstrated the catalyst is effective in decreasing these odorous gases in air. Deliverables: 3 journal articles: 1 accepted and 2 submitted 3 patents: provisional patents submitted 2 articles in preparation following patent submission for NH3 selective oxidation by an order of magnitude by creating acidic Ti-O-Si sites

16307014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307014.value: Odorous gases from NH3, H2S and VOCs are not only a nuisance but also have adverse health impacts. Prolonged exposure to these gases can cause a range of symptoms and generally diminishes overall well-being. Catalysts for treating air pollution problems require temperatures above 250C to be efficient and this makes their application difficult. This project has successfully develop an effective catalyst that can treat these odor-causing compounds at room temperature under high humidity. The catalyst could be used for air cleaner and deodorizer, and could be used indoor spaces of residential, commercial and industrial. It competes with existing catalysts for gas cleaning and excellent potential of making an impact in air pollution treatment.

16307114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307114.value: Graphene is a unique two-dimensional (2D) material consisting of a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a beautiful hexagonal honeycomb lattice structure. Owing to the symmetry of the structure, pristine graphene possesses some novel characteristics that include the absence of effective electronic mass in the vicinity of the Fermi level, and the appearance of a geometric phase (180 degrees) in its quantum mechanical wavefunction when the electron traverses a closed loop. Owing to such unusual characteristics, there have been extensive theoretical studies on graphene. In particular, analytical investigations have shown that while electronic transport in disordered graphene can display diffusive characteristics with a conductance that increases upon the application of a weak magnetic field (the so-called weak localization behavior), no exponential sample size-dependent conductance behavior was obtained. The latter is characteristic of strong Anderson localization common to a disordered 2D system. In this context, the recent experimental observation of strong Anderson localization in anti-dot graphene poses a puzzle: How does it occur? Here the term “anti-dot” denotes a 2D nanostructure of holes etched on graphene, leaving a connected array of nano-sized graphene ribbons. It is the purpose of this proposal to carry out analytical analysis of electronic transport in anti-dot graphene, with the aim of resolving the puzzle posed by the experimental evidence. A second goal of this proposal is to investigate, through a combined analytical and numerical approach, the effect of Coulomb interaction between electrons in anti-dot graphene. This is also prompted by the experimental observation in anti-dot graphene that there is a small Coulomb correlation gap, about 2 meV in width, centered at the Fermi level. While there is some plausible reason why the Coulomb interaction between the electrons can be more important in anti-dot graphene, the aim of the present proposal is to examine the question of Coulomb interaction in a more rigorous manner. Completion of this project will not only resolve some puzzles, but may also provide a theoretical basis to understand anti-dot graphene as an electronic material with characteristics that can qualitatively differ from pristine graphene. 石墨烯是一種由單層碳原子組成的具有正六邊形晶格的二維材料。由于這種結構的特殊對稱性，純淨的石墨烯具備衆多特殊的性質，例如無質量的電子色散關系，以及環繞一個回路變化180度的特殊貝裏相位。經過研究人們發現，這些特性顯著地影響石墨烯的電導疏運性質。例如，理論研究發現在無序石墨烯(指由于制造缺陷在石墨烯晶格結構引入缺陷)當中，雖然可以在電疏運性質中檢測到擴散疏運的特征，以及具備負磁阻特性(指外加磁場導致電阻下降)等典型的“弱局域化”行爲，但是並不能得到隨著樣品尺寸增加，電導呈指數下降的強安德森局域化現象。而該現象在普通二維體系中極爲普遍，也同時出現在anti-dot石墨烯(指在純淨的石墨烯結構上打周期性的孔洞)體系當中。因此目前理論無法解釋我們在實驗中觀察到的anti-dot石墨烯安德森局域化現象。本工作的目標之一，就是爲anti-dot石墨烯中的安德森局域化現象，找出合理的理論解釋。本工作的第二個目標，是通過解析的和模擬的方法，研究anti-dot石墨烯中的電子-電子相互作用。實驗中我們觀察到在anti-dot石墨烯中存在一個在費米面附近的，大約2毫電子伏的庫侖關聯能隙。通過本工作，我們有望通過嚴格地研究anti-dot石墨烯中的缺陷散射和電子-電子相互作用，解釋安德森局域化和庫侖關聯能隙的出現原因，從而不止解答這些疑問，同時爲進一步研究anti-dot石墨烯打下理論基礎。

16307114.label: Realisation of objectives
16307114.value: This project focuses on the electrical transport properties of a nano-structured antidote graphene system. Graphene is a two-dimensional system comprising a monolayer of carbon atoms, and anti-dot means a periodic array of nano-structured holes on the graphene layer. Anti-dot graphene has a gap around the Dirac point. The objectives of this project are to understand the electronic transport behavior in such system. My theoretical endeavor on this project has to be viewed as part of a larger group effort that consists both theory and experiments. In earlier experiments in our group, localization behaviors were found around the band edge of anti-dot graphene; at higher doping levels these localization phenomenon disappear. This is in contrast to both the classical localization behavior in two-dimension electron gas (2DEG), as well as to the anti-localization characteristic in graphene. In classical 2DEG, the scaling theory predicted all electronic states should be localized; while in pristine graphene, due to the existence of a Berry phase pi in the wave-function, a weak-anti-localization behavior occurs in the case of long-ranged Coulomb disorders. In this project I would like to theoretically analyze the experimental observations, in the hope of guiding further experiments on this interesting system. There are two objectives in this project. The first one is “To use Green’s function technique to investigate localization in disordered anti-dot graphene. First we will attempt to recover the diffusion pole in the particle-hole correlation function, then maximally crossed diagrams will be added to obtain the Anderson localization behavior. We will calculate the relevant localization properties such as localization length, negative magneto resistance, etc. for comparison with the experiments” This objective is 95% accomplished. I started with a two-dimensional massive-Dirac Hamiltonian, calculated the Green function, the self-energy, the vertex correction due to ladder diagrams, and finally the maximally-crossed diagrams correction to the conductance. In this 2-by-2 Hamiltonian there is a 0-->pi variation in the Berry phase as doping level increases. I have identified a localization region near the band edge where Berry phase is ~0, i.e., similar to the 2DEG, and an anti-localization region at high doping where the Berry phase ~pi. Between these two phases, there is a localization-to-anti-localization transition. I also calculated the localization length in localized region and found at the transition the localization length diverges. A phase diagram for this transition versus doping level and strength of disorder potential was constructed. Details are present in the manuscript already deposited in arXiv. In achieving this first objective, I encountered some difficulties and unexpected scenarios, which were the main reasons for not achieving 100% of the objective. First, the matrix form of Hamiltonian caused the vector form of Green functions. This made analytical treatment of the problem much more complicated than in 2DEG system. Therefore a completely self-consistent theory was found to be not accessible, but only a numerical treatment was possible. Second, we considered so-called long-range Coulomb disorders whose scattering amplitudes exhibit angular variations. This differs significantly from the simplified treatment in all the prior references, in which only short-range disorders were considered. The treatment of angular dependence introduced considerable complexity, and I had to decompose the vertices onto different angular momentum channels in order to overcome this difficulty. Third, an unexpected situation occurred. That is, together with my collaborator, Dr. Pan Jie, we found that for anti-dot graphene the effective Hamiltonian should not be the same as in the previous references. The actual effective Hamiltonian for the anti-dot graphene is a 4-by-4 matrix, quite different from the Hamiltonian that I started out with. Details of this finding were published in our PRX paper (Phys.Rev.X.7,031043), and this whole discovery represented a big detour from the originally planned road map. In basic research, such detours not only often occur, but are also sometimes desirable, since we have found something new in the process. The 2-by-2 matrix Hamiltonian I used previously was only valid for the A/B asymmetric graphene, where A and B denote the two in-equivalent carbon atoms inside a primitive cell, e.g., different potentials acting on the A and B atoms, which can be the case for pristine graphene placed on boron nitrite substrate. However, the newly obtained effective Hamiltonian, also has the similar 0-->pi variation in the Berry phase versus doping level, so we can expect a similar localization-to-antilocalization transition. Thus the effort I spent on the original 2-by-2 matrix Hamiltonian can be very informative. It also facilitates greatly the calculation on the true anti-dot graphene Hamiltonian that will follow. The remaining work on the localization-to-anti-localization transition in the 2D massive-Dirac fermion system is to verify, in real space, the exponential to power-law decay behavior associated with the 2D localization-to-delocalization transition, since in two-dimensions, an extended state can be characterized by a power-law decay behavior. I have accomplished numerical simulations with quantum-transport code KWANT, and now a direct analysis on real-space Green function is on-going. Once accomplished, a direct observation of real-space decay characteristic in Green function will be at hand, and we can get a much more clear and self-consistent picture of the whole problem. The second objective of this project is “To perform analytical and numerical calculations on electron-electron interaction in disordered anti-dot graphene. We will calculate the Coulomb self-energy and its consequent correlation gap in the density of state, the dephasing scattering rate and other related observable variables. Screening of Coulomb interaction and maximally crossed diagrams should be taken into account in the calculations. The goal is to explain the large dephasing length observed in experiment” This objective is now on-going. In pristine graphene the electron-electron interaction is weak, owing to the small ratio between the Coulomb interaction energy and the electron kinetic energy. However, in gapped anti-dot graphene since the Fermi velocity is decreased (the kinetic energy becomes smaller) the relative importance of electron-electron interaction becomes enhanced. Our group, with my collaborator Dr. Pan Jie and our Taiwan collaborators, Prof. JJ Lin and Dr. Sheng-Shiuan Ye of National Chiao Tung University, have carried out experiments that clearly show the existence of a hard correlation gap at temperatures below 100 mK. Simultaneous with the experimental effort, simulations were done. By using Landau-levels as the basis functions, and by calculating the Coulomb interaction between partially occupied Landau-level orbitals in the presence of a magnetic field, a correlation gap has indeed been verified by the Monte Carlo calculations of the wave-functions under the many-body interaction, followed by the evaluation of the excitation energy relative to the Fermi level at zero temperature. The magnetic field dependence and the order of magnitude of the obtained correlation gap are qualitatively compatible with the experimental observations. The main difficulty in resolving the problem is the extremely huge computation resource requirement. Therefore we use Landau level orbitals instead of atomic orbitals to perform simulations, which can greatly reduce the computation demand. Also the employment of Monte-Carlo method instead of conventional self-consistent diagonalization greatly enhances the stability of simulation result. At present, we are at the last stage of being able to quantitatively explain the data. The preparation of a manuscript on this project will soon be underway.

16307114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307114.value: We have theoretically studied anti-dot graphene system, which is a monolayer graphene with a periodic array of holes. Together with my experimental collaborator, Dr. Pan Jie, we have derived an effective Hamiltonian that differs from the earlier predictions in all the prior literature, and analyzed its topological properties, i.e. the non-zero Berry curvature and corresponding non-local conductance. This work, partially supported by this proposal, was published in Phys. Rev. X. We have also analyzed the 2 by 2 massive Dirac Hamiltonian with long-range Coulomb disorders. Due to the 0-->pi variation of Berry phase with respect to doping level away from the charge neutrality point, we have analytically identified an Anderson-localization (AL) to weak anti-localization (WAL) transition. A manuscript is under preparation, and the analytical part of the manuscript has already been submitted to arXiv. In addition, the electron-electron correlation effect in antidot graphene has indeed been found to be very important at low temperatures, both experimentally and theoretically. The preliminary results have indicated the opening of a hard correlation gap, whose magnitude varies as a function of the applied magnetic field.

16307114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307114.value: The somewhat unexpected discovery and derivation of the effective Hamiltonian for the antidot graphene has many implications. Our next step is to analyze the anti-dot graphene system with this new Hamiltonian. The same Green function method can be used to estimate the coherent back-scattering processes in anti-dot graphene system. Within the new Hamiltonian there is a 0-->pi variation in the Berry phase as a function of the Fermi level doping, and we expect a localization to anti-localization transition should occur in anti-dot graphene systems. We intend to further verify this possible localization/anti-localization transition in anti-dot graphene, and compare the theoretical results with the earlier experimental data.

16307114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307114.value: Graphene is a two-dimensional material consisting of a single layer of carbon atoms, and due to its symmetry graphene-based systems can possess novel characteristics like the appearance of a geometric phase pi in its wave-function when electrons traverse a closed loop. This topological Berry phase gives rise to novel anti-localization characteristics in electronic transport, and can be the basis for violating the traditional scaling theory prediction in 2D systems, which states that in all 2D systems the wavefunctions must be exponentially localized. Furthermore, theoretical simulations carried out in conjunction with the experiment on low temperature transport measurement in antidot graphene (carried out by my experimental colleagues) have shown a correlation hard gap, supported by simulations. So the outcome of this project has provided a much deeper understanding of the transport behaviors in a class of gapped graphene systems. This can be not only of academic interest, but may also have potential applications, e.g., by shrinking the dimension of the holes and their lattice constant, thereby increasing the gap size.
