16401014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16401014.value: Our project titled “Impact of Urban-Rural Return Migration on Rural Economic Development in China” has been funded by ESRC-DFID with minor revisions, effective in May 2014. It will examine the changing patterns of return migration, factors that affect returnees’ entrepreneurial activities, the roles of institutions and policies in these processes and the impacts on non-migrants, villages and local townships. A survey of 2,100 rural households including 1,525 R-returnees and 525 R-stayers will be conducted in seven provinces, interviewing them on household information, socio-demographics, and histories of migration, employment and entrepreneurial activities. Owing to the primary goal of the funding agency, poverty relief, the project focuses on the impact of return migration on rural development. Return migration to small urban places (U-return) is often neglected in previous migration studies. This proposed project aims to study return migration from a new perspective of urbanization. Through returnees’ rural-urban linkages, a new approach is adopted to integrate processes of return migration across sectors into a nested choice model. To be cost effective, we will conduct an urban survey of 1,890 households including 945 U-returnees and 945 active U-labor migrants originated in the same source villages, and follow up them a year after. With a complete sample of all subjects (R-stayers, U-labor migrants, R- and U-returnees) plus census micro-datasets, we will document flows and patterns of return migration, investigate labor migrants’ choice of return, returnees’ choice of settlement (among village, township, town, county-seat, and small city) and choice of employment (among farming, labor, self-employment or entrepreneurship) before evaluating the positive and negative impacts of return migration on urbanization. Significance. There are 100 million cross-county labor and returned migrants in China. Married migrants who left dependents behind are especially prone to return, increasingly so to small urban places where the settlement control is removing. Urbanization has been set as the primary engine for the future growth. Lack of skilled labor and entrepreneurship remain as bottlenecks for developing small urban places in interior regions. It is crucial to know what factors are important to U-return and how returnees’ entrepreneurial potential and rural leadership effect can be maximized through their rural-urban linkages, with a strong policy implication for the migrants' settlement in the tens of millions. The PI conducted a national survey of urban-rural return migration in China in 1997 and has published extensively on the topic. The CO-Is are both strong in survey and migration research. 劳动力迁移研究往往忽视其小城镇回流（U型回迁）。我们从 城市化进程的视角及回流者的城乡联系，对跨地区跨行业的 回流行为进行深入研究。我们将调查1,890农村户，包括小城镇 回流户和城市打工者家庭，一年后跟进调查。通过收集完整的 调查样本加上人口普查的微观数据，我们研究回迁的各项选择， 包括回迁定居地的选择（村、乡、镇、县还是小城市) 及 就业的选择（包括农、工、个体经营或是创业），及回流对 城市化进程的正面和负面影响。

16401014.label: Realisation of objectives
16401014.value: Objective 1. Based on a series of census microdata, we found that return migration has been rising since 2000, with the volume across county (province) more than doubled from 5.5 (2.0) to 10.9 (2.5) and further to 14.0 (4.9) million (Ma, 2019). Based on NPS2015, we found that the main flows of interprovincial return migration were from east coastal to inland regions especially those provinces along the Yangzi-river, where odds of returning (by married adults) more than doubled that of other inland regions. We also found strong selectivity of return migration in favor of more educated, females, young adult migrants at early stages of family cycle (Ma, 2021). Objective 2. In terms of settlement, there has been a trend of urbanization in return migration. Among 15.4 million returnees, 36.6%, 23.2% and 30.1% settled in city, town and rural areas, respectively. Specific to married migrants originated from rural areas, the distribution of settlement type for returnees’ household was 1.16% (city), 2.53% (suburb), 4.62% (city-village), 13.55% (town), 11.14% (town-village), and 67.0% (village) while that for labor migrants was 0.22% (city), 0.51% (suburb), 1.92% (city-village), 7.56% (town), 11.68% (town village), and 78.12% (village). The odds in non-village settlements enhanced considerably by 58.4% while the share in having an urban settlement more than doubled in returnees’ household (21.86%) than the splitting migrants’ household (10.20%). U- and R-returnees are selective of single female returnees and double ones, respectively. In terms of occupation, double or single farming remains somewhat important but less so than stayers for R-returnees while double nonfarm employments especially non-industrial ones becomes the most important for U-returnees. Objective 3. Initially, we did pilot surveys in Wuhan and Anhui and interviewed dozens of returnees. However, household survey in China has become increasingly difficult and costly since 2013 because of strict control by the government. Fortunately, we got special permission from the census department in National Bureau of Statistics to use 1% of National Population Survey conducted in 2015 (NPS15) for this project. In addition to on-site data analysis, we have drawn samples from it for in-depth analysis. These samples have many advantages. First, NPS15 is unique in surveying migrants in both the household in the destination and that at the hukou origin, allowing us to distinct and make complete four sets of household samples containing non-migrants only, (U- and R-) returnees, (sole or couple) labor migrants, and family migrants. Second, NPS15 contains rich and detailed information on migration, occupation, residence, and all the important socio-demographics that are much needed for this proposed project. Third, NPS15 is representative and huge in size, with 6.71 million households and 21.31 million individuals surveyed, from which we draw four large samples from NPS15 (U- and R-) containing (i) R- and U-returnees, (ii) stayers only, (iii) migrants in the destination, and (4) migrants recorded at the hukou origin. Fourth, the size is around 40,000 households for each sample, with the sampling probability being 1, 1/20th, 1/12th, 1/7th, correspondingly. By properly weighting, the large and representative samples enable us to do in-depth analysis in full confidence. Fifth, we saved the costs of survey by 208,000$. Objective 4. First, the level of consumption was strongly enhanced in a return migration, reflected by the change in car ownership (11.8% increased to 19.3%) and that in purchasing commercial housing (2.0% increased to 7.9%), both of which serving an urban/rural linkage in transportation and residence. Second, the use of social capital in information exchange and/or direct assistance across rural/urban sectors can be reflected by the strongly enhancing effect of outmigration (rate) on the propensity of return migration. Third, for joint employment of returnees referenced to stayers, the odds (share) reduced substantially on double farming (35.5% reduced to 14.0%) while that on double non-industrial work increases from 16.9% to 26.1%), reflecting greater entrepreneurship and increased rural-urban linkages among returnees’ than stayers’ households. Objective 5. For explaining household migration, we developed a two-level multinomial logit model of embedded choices (MML2). We divide households into SLFR containing stayers (S), (sole/ couple) labor migrants (L), family migrants (F), and return migrants (R). Key ecological variables are joined with NPS15 variables of household socio-demographics, joint employment and settlement for the model estimation. By using MML2 and NPS15, we explain rural Chinese family’s choices of migration, joint employment and settlement simultaneously in the household context. First, we found that the odds of a couple in making labor migration decline with an increase in mean county income while they are strongly enhanced by both the highest risk for farming (in flooding regions along the Yangzi River) and the presence of in-house parents (who are willing to take extra household duties), indicating a retaining effect of income, a strong pushing effect of risks and a strong enhancing effect of parents as a form of home social capital in mitigating the potential risks of disruption in splitting households (D-risks). Second, family migration helps to avoid the potential D-risks but incurred much greater risks in unstable employment and settlement, reflected by much enhanced and reduced odds in single employment and house ownership, respectively. Third, risks of migration in family disruption and unsettlement are substantially reduced in a return migration, reflected by the reduced odds in having in-house parents and less children, respectively, much greater propensity at the earlier family stages when extra duties are required for the family expansion, as well as more than doubled and tripled odds in purchasing and owning a car and/or a commercial house. Fourth, returnees’ entrepreneurship helps to keep momentum in labor migration and mitigate the potentially high risks in double nonfarm employment in less urbanized regions, reflected by returnees’ much reduced odds in double farming and similarly higher odds (share) for returnees and labor migrants than stayers in double nonindustrial work. Fifth, there is a strong enhancing effect of return migration on urbanization, reflected partially by sixty percent of odds enhancement of urban settlement by return migration. In a word, return migration with entrepreneurship improves the overall welfare of the family by trading slightly increased risks in joint employment for substantially reduced household risks of family disruption and unstable settlement. Objective 6. In-depth interviews with returnees and local officials have been done in our pilot survey in both a city district of Wuhan as well as Hexian (和县) and Chaohu (巢湖市) in Anhui Province. A majority of labor migrants have either bought property in the county seat or built their new house in small towns. Many have returned while more are planning to return and start a new business. Returnees are now playing a key role in the development of small urban places. Some local governments provide small funds and other supports for attracting returnees. Objective 7. We have made appointments with key persons in the policy research in the government to do joint work on new policy of return migration. Unfortunately, the covid-19 lasts so long that research trips are difficult to be approved, apart from extended quarantine period (14 + 7 days). We will continue to work on the report with our collaborators in the government as soon as we have the chance to go.

Summarize our main findings and submit a policy report to the central government through our established connections, with respect to the future settlement of tens of million migrants at various urban/rural strata.

16401014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16401014.value: Trend. Intercountry (interprovincial) return migration has been on the rise since 2000, more than doubled from 5.5 (2.0) to 10.9 (2.5) and further to 14.0 (4.9) million (Ma, 2019). The spatial pattern. Return migration mainly flows from the east coastal to the inland regions along the Yangzi-river. Selectivity. Return migration is selective of female young adults at the early family stages (Ma, 2021). Home Social Capital (HSC). In-house adult parents as HSC strongly enhances the odds of labor migration by taking extra household duties. Higher and Lower Education of Spouses. Lower education strongly enhances labor and family migration while higher education reduces odds of family and return migration. Double-edge Income Effects. Rural income has a retaining effect on labor and return migration but a facilitating one on family migration. Natural Risks. High risks of floods (in provinces along the Yangzi River) strongly enhance on all types of migration while risks of draughts (in other regions) does not. Family Settlement. From labor to return migration, odds for an urban settlement, purchasing a car and commercial housing enhanced by 58.4%, 31.3%, and 1.20 times, respectively. Joint Employment (Stayers’ households=reference). • odds of double farming reduced to negligible in LF migration but bounced back to about one fifth in return migration. • odds of farm-nonfarm employment enhanced greatly by two-third in labor migration but dropped sharply to only 1/10th and slightly to 85% in FR migration, respectively. • odds of single worker enhanced by 1.5 times, 54.0% and 43.2% in LFR, respectively. • odds of double nonindustrial workers enhanced by 53.9%, 1.71 times and 32.6% in LFR migration, respectively. Conclusive findings. Through entrepreneurship, return migration improves the overall family welfare by trading slightly enhanced risks in double nonfarm employment for substantially reduced household risks in settlement. It facilitates urbanization by enhancing settlement and creating small businesses in less urbanized areas. Outcome. “Trends of Migration in China in Four-decades of Economic Reform” was published in Population Science, 2019, 3: pp.16-28. The project was delayed by the government control on data. Since we obtained samples from NPS15 in early 2019, we have been tried hard to finish all the data analysis and finish three manuscripts to be submitted this Fall. “Patterns of Household Labor/ Return Migration in China”, to Population Science. “Explaining Labor/ Return Migration in China”, to Demography. “Choices of Nonfarm Employment and Urban Settlement in Labor/ Return Migration in China”, to World Development.

16401014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16401014.value: The advancement of risks trade-off and the development of MML2 model can be extended to study intra-urban and international migration of the high skilled, respectively. We are proposing to study internal and international migration of college graduates in China, which also involves the choice of migration (between labor, family, and return migration) as well as the sub-choices of joint employment and family settlement.

16401014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16401014.value: Return migration is a complicated process. Previous research were not successful by using opposing theories, binary logit model, and impartial samples of migrants. In this project, we make advancements in following aspects. First, in a common framework, we integrate important risk perspectives and advance theories to explain labor, family and return migration in household context: (i) risks avoidance in labor migration (Stark, 1991), (ii) risks taking in family migration (Todaro, 1969) as well as (iii) household absorption of disruptive risks by home social capital (HSC), (iv) entrepreneurship mitigation of risks in nonfarm employment, and (v) risks trade-off between double nonfarm employment and family settlement in a return migration (Ma, 2021). Second, we developed a two-level multinomial logit model (MML2) to explain simultaneously the household choice of a migration as well as sub-choices of joint employment and family settlement. Third, from NPS15, we constructed large samples of households containing stayers, labor migrants, family migrants, and return migrants, from which household variables in HSC, joint employment and settlement are abstracted and joined with key ecological variables in MML2 for estimation. Fourth, new policies can be formulated based on our conclusive findings that return migration through entrepreneurship has its potentials in facilitating urbanization.

16401314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16401314.value: 去天理的人權：加藤弘之及吳經熊憲法理論中的天論、人權與社會達爾文主義

16401314.label: Project Objectives
16401314.value: To construct a new narrative of Katō Hiroyuki’s constitutional law theory from the 1880s in the light of his concepts of ten (Heaven), Social Darwinism and inalienable rights; To construct a new narrative of John Wu’s constitutional law theory by the mid-1930s in the light of his concept of tian (Heaven), Social Darwinism and inalienable rights; To construct a third new narrative comparing the transplant of evolutionary jurisprudence in constitutional law in Meiji Japan and Republican China in the light of the two aforementioned narratives; and explore its implication on the contemporary discourse on the concepts of rights and constitutionalism.
rows: To construct a new narrative of Katō Hiroyuki’s constitutional law theory from the 1880s in the light of his concepts of ten (Heaven), Social Darwinism and inalienable rights;
To construct a new narrative of John Wu’s constitutional law theory by the mid-1930s in the light of his concept of tian (Heaven), Social Darwinism and inalienable rights;

To construct a third new narrative comparing the transplant of evolutionary jurisprudence in constitutional law in Meiji Japan and Republican China in the light of the two aforementioned narratives; and explore its implication on the contemporary discourse on the concepts of rights and constitutionalism.

16401314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16401314.value: The first two objectives of this project are to examine the impact of Social Darwinism on the constitutional law theories in Meiji Japan and Republican China with specific focuses on the concepts of Heaven and inalienable rights as reflected in the constitutional writings of Katō Hiroyuki (1836-1916) and John Ching-hsiung Wu (1899-1986). The third objective is to compare these two eminent legal and political leaders of the respective countries so as to engage in a broader issue on the different paths of transplanting fundamental legal concepts from the West to Japan and China at the early stage of their pursuit in legal modernization. As a projection from the findings the project will also explore the implication and insight of this empirical study on constitutionalism from a more general perspective. There are two figures and three key concepts that constitute the framework of our inquiry. The two figures in question are Katō Hiroyuki and John Wu. The three concepts are the traditional notion of Heaven, the transplanted Western notion of Social Darwinism, and the concept of inalienable rights in constitutional law theory. Katō was an eminent political, legal and intellectual elite in Meiji Japan. So was Wu in Republican China. Katō headed the Law Department of Tokyo Imperial University and later became the president of the same university. He delivered lectures for the Meiji Emperor on constitutional law and served in the House of Peers, the Privy Council, and the Imperial Academy, among other prestigious settings. John Wu was an eminent law professor, dean of the Soochow Law School, and judge of different courts. He was a Legislative Yuan member and a drafter of the 1935 draft constitution under the Nanjing regime. The primary purpose of our inquiry is to construct a new understanding in the form of narratives on their thoughts pertaining to the three key concepts of Heaven, Social Darwinism, and rights; and how these concepts were positioned and functioned in their mental frameworks. Built upon these new narratives of Katō and Wu, the project will further explore a third narrative comparing Katō and Wu in terms of the three key concepts in question and their intersection. The findings of this inquiry will be archival-based and presented in the form of historical narrative. Such an approach can be more effective in capturing and revealing the complex, and often contradictory, mental constructs in our two cases. 本項目的目標有三個：前兩個目標旨在考察社會達爾文主義 對明治及民國憲法理論的影響，焦點放在加藤弘之(1836-1916) 及吳經熊(1899-1986) 憲法理論中的天論與人權。第三個目標是 比較兩者，以期對中日兩國法律現代化初期移植西方法律的不 同取徑，提供實証的討論。基於以上三個目標所達致的成果， 我們或可進一步探討一些更具普遍意義的憲法人權理論問題。 我們研究的框架建立在兩位關鍵人物以及三個基本理念之上。 前者即加藤弘之及吳經熊。後者是傳統的天的觀念、移植的 社會達爾文觀念以及憲法理論中的 “天賦人權” 觀念。 加藤是日本明治時期最重要的政治、法學及思想界領袖，吳 經熊民國時期在政法學三界亦享有崇高地位。加藤曾主管東京 帝國大學法學院，任東大校長，亦曾任貴族院議員、樞密院 顧問等，他的憲法理論對明治憲法發展影響不少。吳經熊為 出色的法學教授、東吳法學院院長，執掌不同的法官崗位，並 曾積極參與民國24年憲法的修訂與研究。 我們最重要的目的是希望通過叙事的方法，重建他們兩人有關 上述三個基本理念的想法，以及在他們言思框架內，兩人如何 為這些想法定位，如何加以操作。我們期望建構的第三個比較 的叙事，是他們的對比論述。使用叙事的歷史論述方式來處理 這些複雜而充滿吊詭的言思圖象，相信是更有效的方法。

16401314.label: Realisation of objectives
16401314.value: 1. To construct a new narrative of Katō Hiroyuki's constitutional law theory This objective has been accomplished with our 2017 and forthcoming (probably in 2019) articles, through which a new understanding of Katō's constitutional theory has emerged. In a nutshell, Katō used a hybrid of transplanted social Darwinistic naturalism and German constitutional practice to support the Meiji Constitution drafted by Itō Hirobumi and a group of other statist leaders in the 1880s. Our original contribution (not found in the voluminous literature on Katō) is that our narrative points to the fact that Katō was caught in the gap between the transplanted naturalism and the traditional mindset of Japanese indigenous naturalism (especially the kind reflected in the Japanese concept of divinity of the Emperor) and claims that such contradiction could be reconciled with help of the concept of 'wakon yōsai.' This concept separates the preservation of the Japanese spirit from the pragmatic adoption of foreign ideas when there is a need for Western learning. For Katō, the ideas of social Darwinism and German imperial constitution were both convenient vehicles to help realize Japan's 'wakon yōsai' version of imperial constitution, under which individual rights would naturally be tied to the Imperial Family and thus perfectly alienable. 2. To construct a new narrative of John Wu's constitutional law theory This objective has been accomplished with our 2016 article, through which a new understanding of John Wu's constitutionalism has emerged. Our original contribution is to have pointed out the unmistakable presence of Darwinian tenets behind the authoritarian and statist notion of rights in Wu's draft Constitution of the Republic of China (RoC) for the Guomindang regime in the mid-1930s. Wu's idea of constitutional rights in the late 1920s and early 1930s can be traced to his tacit agreement to a worldview that rejected the conceptual naturalist idea that there should be necessary substantive moral constraints on the content of law. Largely missing in the existing literature is this long-neglected but significant aspect in understanding how Wu helped shape the theory and practice of constitutionalism (a legal transplant from the West often linked to social Darwinist notions) in China. That is partly because of his subsequent conversion to Catholicism that made him a staunch advocate of Catholic natural law theory from the 1940s. Nonetheless, our research has revealed that up to the mid-1930s, Wu openly advocated the notion of alienable rights of citizens, arguing that the state provided rights to its citizens and thus, the state could take away any rights from them as it deemed necessary. 3. To construct a third new narrative comparing the transplant of evolutionary jurisprudence in constitutional law in Meiji Japan and Republican China and explore its implications on the discourse on rights and constitutionalism. This objective has been accomplished as the abovementioned two new narratives are compared with the aim of furthering our understanding of constitutionalism during the Meiji and the RoC period. Such comparison had never been done before. Our 2017 article discusses a number of similarities and differences in terms of constitutional theories embraced by the two nations. Although social Darwinian tenets were clearly present in the constitutions of both countries, their chief draftsmen-Katō and Wu-took very different approaches to their adoption. For Katō, adopting Darwinistic and scientific naturalism was a timely and expedient move; there was no need to dismiss the traditional values and beliefs, which were clearly incompatible with such naturalistic beliefs as social Darwinism and modern natural science as they were deeply rooted in Shinto, Japan's indigenous religion that supported the divine rights claimed by the Japanese Imperial Family and had the notion of Heaven (ten in Japanese) at its core. For Wu, on the other hand, there was no place in constitutionalism for the traditional Chinese notion of Heaven (tian in Chinese) or any natural law theories of the Western legal heritage for that matter. He held the view that the Confucian notion of Heaven forming the cosmological and ontological foundations for Confucian morality was part of a propaganda campaign orchestrated by the ruling aristocracy in order to dominate and oppress the common people. Wu stood firmly on the ground of social Darwinism that turned into the Three People's Principles associated with Sun Yat-sen. In order to explain Darwinistic naturalism evident in the constitutional theories of Katō and Wu, we have come up with an original concept that we call 'constitutional naturalism.' The concept refers to the mindset behind constitutional thoughts that embraces the following beliefs all at once: (1) The only natural order is the order of the natural world, which can only be approached and comprehended through science; (2) according to the latest scientific knowledge, human society is evolutionary under the Darwinian principles of natural selection and survival of the fittest; (3) law as human institution follows the same path as evolution; (4) laws (including constitutional rights) should reflect the effect of the Darwinian principles; (5) there is, therefore, no natural law, higher moral order, or higher justice surpassing national law or the natural world; (6) transcendental sources have no place in individual rights and thus, individual rights are alienable; (7) the state is the only source of legal rights for individuals; (8) constitutional rights must, therefore, not be established on account of religion or morality; and (9) constitutional rights can, therefore, be subject to change if the power structure including the judiciary and other aspects of the state apparatus changes. These nine tenets are fundamentally Darwinian but contextualized in the domain of constitutional thoughts that include non-Darwinian beliefs. Thus, constitutional naturalism is not parallel to Social Darwinism. The notion is conceived to refer to a strand of constitutionalism built upon expanded ideas of Social Darwinism. In our six English-language conference papers, with the hope of gaining deeper insight into constitutional rights and for comparison's sake, we also considered Western contemporaries of Katō and Wu from the perspective of constitutional naturalism, ranging from Axel Hägerström (1868-1939) and Oliver Wendell Holmes (1841-1935), both proponents of legal realism, to Frede Castberg (1893-1977), a prominent advocate of Norwegian-style natural law theory, to Rudolf Stammler (1856-1938), a renowned German neo-Kantian natural law theorist. Indeed we have gained new insights from this extended comparative examination of the notable twentieth-century jurists of the West and East Asia, which we believe contribute to today's constitutional rights discourse in not only East Asia but also Europe and the United States. In fact, our next project is to apply the idea of constitutional naturalism in studying Justice Holmes who developed a close friendship with Wu despite their 58-year age difference and also provided an authoritative interpretation of the Meiji Constitution in which Katō had a hand.

16401314.label: Major findings and research outcome
16401314.value: We published two book chapters in 2016 and 2017 respectively and another one is to appear in early 2019. Between September 2015 and May 2018, we presented a total of seven papers at international conferences (and another one in October 2018) as well as one paper at an academic workshop (see Part C of this report). Our major accomplishments are: (1) We have constructed an original narrative of Katō's constitutional theory that focuses on the ideological gap between his belief in the constitutionality of the divine status of the Emperor deeply rooted in the native Japanese tradition of the naturalistic religion Shinto and his adherence to the naturalistic social Darwinism as he defended the Imperial Order of the Meiji Emperor drawing on the German constitutional model. Although his involvement in the creation of the Meiji Constitution was indirect, Katō's opinions had a significant impact on the emerging constitutional framework for Meiji Japan as the county strove to become a modern nation-state. (2) We have constructed an original narrative of John Wu's constitutional theory that focuses on his naturalistic social Darwinism as he took the lead, under the Nanjing regime in the mid-1930s, in drafting the Constitution of the Republic of China modeled on the constitutions of Western powers. Wu, educated in China then the U.S., earned an international reputation as a legal scholar by the time he returned to China in 1924, where he held multiple influential positions. His Darwinist leanings are evident in his writings of the 1920s and 1930s and so is their impact in the process of introducing Western constitutional law into China. Our narrative shows how his authoritarian constitutional thoughts are linked to Darwinistic naturalism. (3) We have constructed an original comparative narrative of formative influences of Darwinistic naturalism on the transplant of Western constitutional law in Meiji Japan and the Republic of China. During their active participation in political discourse and the development of a constitution in their respective countries, Katō and Wu both subscribed to social Darwinistic naturalism but adopted it in a very different manner with two divergent outcomes-Japan's wakon yōsai and China's strict adherence to the Guomindang ideology. (4) We have proposed an original concept termed 'constitutional naturalism' to refer to a certain intellectual phenomenon in integrating social Darwinism and Western constitutionalism into a brand of constitutional order that could justify the alienability of individual rights.

16401314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16401314.value: The concept of 'constitutional naturalism' we developed in this research is worth exploring further. Our immediate future plan is to revisit Justice Holmes and make sense of his complex legal thoughts and constitutional doctrines, which remain highly controversial among scholars to this day, from the perspective of constitutional naturalism. Once we have a reasonably good grip on Holmes's constitutional theory, we will construct its narrative in light of constitutional naturalism then another narrative comparing Holmes, Katō and Wu with the aim of refining the notion of constitutional naturalism in global perspective. With the idea of constitutional naturalism in global perspective, we hope to contribute to enriching the current global discourse of constitutional rights. In early 2018 the PI applied for the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme that would facilitate our next project.

16401314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16401314.value: Are individual rights constitutionally protected? In other words, are they inalienable? According to social Darwinism that conjures up such phrases as 'survival of the fittest' and 'natural selection,' all rights are alienable, that is, they can be taken away. Our project has addressed the inherent incompatibility between the inalienability of constitutional rights and social Darwinism that could lead to an understanding that all rights are alienable. We have examined this issue by comparing a Japanese and a Chinese legal scholar-Katō Hiroyuki and John Wu-both of whom exerted formative influences of Darwinistic naturalism on the transplant of Western constitutional law in Meiji Japan and the Republic of China. Katō adopted the ideas of social Darwinism and German imperial constitution to help realize Japan's hybrid version of constitution and defended the authoritarian Meiji Constitution under which individual rights would naturally be tied to the Imperial Family and thus alienable. Wu also employed tenets of social Darwinism to reject natural rights (inalienability) in coming up with an authoritarian constitutional order aligned with the Guomindang ideology, in which case the rights could be taken away by the government. Implications from this historical comparative study are applicable to all ages and countries.

16401414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16401414.value: 中國與印度的地方發展及民族資本

16401414.label: Project Objectives

16401414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16401414.value: This proposed study will analyze the local developmental impact of remittances and ethnic foreign direct investment in India and China. Since 2005, those countries have ranked first and second, respectively, in international remittance receipts; together, they now account for one-third of total remittance flows worldwide. A significant portion of China’s “foreign” direct investment comes from ethnic Chinese investors based in other countries. As with conventional forms of international capital, remittances and diasporic investment tend to be concentrated in particular localities rather than evenly distributed throughout the country. What are the developmental implications of such ethnic capital flows from abroad? In some localities, remittances go primarily towards consumption; in other localities, they are combined with diasporic investment and allocated towards industry and commerce. Sometimes remittances finance further outmigration; in other areas, its developmental effects attract return migration. Explaining such variation requires mid-range analysis of local contextual factors, including political and economic history, geographic endowments, social structure, demographic trends, cultural legacies, and contemporary developments in the local political economy. The research design of this study is thus structured around three pairs of localities in China and India that have all attracted significant volumes of remittances and ethnic FDI: 1) Zhejiang and Gujarat; 2) Zhongguancun and Bangalore; and 3) Fujian and Kerala. The proposed in-depth case studies of these localities will involve: 1) Collection and review of primary source documents, including national and local government reports, policy statements, official economic and demographic statistics, and public records of financial institutions. 2) Review of the locality-specific secondary literature across disciplines, including political science, sociology, economics, anthropology, and geography. 3) Field research in each pair of localities, including interviews with local officials, households, and businesses owners/managers. The intended contribution of this project is both empirical and analytical. Empirically, multiple cross-national paired comparisons of subnational localities in China and India have not been undertaken in previous research. Analytically, the comparative results will enable the PI to theorize more broadly about the contextually contingent impact of ethnic capital on development. 這個研究將會分析匯款和僑胞的外國直接投資對印度和中國地方發展的影響。自2005年以來，這兩個國家分別在國際匯款收據單上位列第一第二名,合計佔據了世界三分之一的匯款流量。其中，中國的“外國”直接投資很大一部分來自於居住在其它國家的華裔投資者。與傳統形式的國際資本一樣，匯款與流散投資都趨向于集中在幾個特定的地方而不是平均地分佈於國家之內。這些來自於國外的民族資本流動有什麼發展性的意義呢？ 在有些地方，匯款主要流向於消費。在另外的地方，匯款會與流散投資結合，並且分配在工業和商業領域。有的時候，匯款投資會導致更多的外移民；在另外的地區，匯款的發展影響會吸引移民回流。解釋這些變化需要對地方背景因素進行理論與事實相結合的分析，包括分析當地的政治及經濟歷史、地理資源、社會結構、人口趨向、文化遺產、和當地政治經濟的當代發展。 這個研究設計圍繞中國與印度的三組都吸引了大量匯款和僑胞的外國直接投資的地方展開：1）浙江和古吉拉突邦；2）中關村和班加羅爾；以及3）廣東和喀拉拉邦。對這些地方更深入的案例分析將會包括： 1）搜集與考察一手資料檔，包括國家及地方政府報告、政策申明、官方的經濟與人口統計資料、以及金融機構的公開記錄。 2）回顧關於各個地方不同領域的二手文獻，包括政治科學、社會學、經濟學、考古學和地理學。 3）對每一個地方比較組進行田野調查，包括對地方官員、戶主、以及企業主或經理的採訪。 這項研究希望在實證和理論兩個層面做出貢獻。。實證研究方面，以往的研究沒有進行過對中國與印度地區性的多重跨國對比組研究。理論分析上，比較得出的結果可以對僑胞的外國直接投資在不同背景及情況下產生的發展性影響建立理論。

16401414.label: Realisation of objectives
16401414.value: Realising the objectives of this project entailed three main components: 1) Field research: Conducting field research in six sub-national localities in China and India, including collection of primary data sources; 2) Literature review: Reviewing the relevant historical and secondary literature on each of the sites; 3) Research outputs: Writing up the findings, presenting them at conferences/seminars to receive feedback, and preparing publications. All of the research objectives were realised. This final report focuses on activities since the mid-term progress report. Field Research I have conducted field research all six localities specified in the original proposal, as well as sites with significant communities of Chinese and Indians from those same localities, including Dubai, Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Singapore. As indicated in the table below, I conducted a total of 417 interviews with migrant households, migrant laborers/professionals, returnee entrepreneurs, returnee venture capitalists, native place and trade associations, government agencies, researchers, and journalists, of which 343 were in the original six fieldwork sites. Summary of Field Interviews, 2015 - 2018 Site # of Interviews Bangalore 42 Beijing 43 Guangdong 45 Guangzhou 24 Kaiping 12 Nansha 3 Taishan 6 Gujarat 53 Ahmedabad 15 Anand 22 Surat 16 Kerala 89 Kochi 43 Malappuram 30 Trivandrum 16 Zhejiang 71 Cangnan (WZ) 14 Hangzhou 8 Ningbo 12 Wenzhou 33 Yiwu 4 Main cases sub-total: 343 Other sites 74 Dubai 38 Hong Kong 15 Shanghai 12 Singapore 9 TOTAL INTERVIEWS 417 In 2017, I traveled to Kerala along the southwestern coast of India. I started out at the Centre for Development Studies (CDS) in Thiruvanathapuram (Trivandrum), hosted by migration specialist Professor Irudaya Rajan. As the leading research center for migration studies in India, CDS conducts regular surveys of migration flows from Kerala to the Gulf. Being based at CDS allowed me to gather valuable data about demographic trends in migration. Since Trivandrum is the state capital, I interviewed local government ministers and bureaucrats, and learn about their perspectives on Kerala’s heavy dependence on Gulf remittances, and the local social and political impacts on return migration. Various researchers and officials provided valuable contacts for fieldwork in northern Kerala and Dubai. In Cochin (Kochi), I interviewed staff at NORKA Roots, which is devoted towards the concerns of non-resident Keralites (NRKs), and returnees ranging from drivers to private entrepreneurs and development aid workers. In 2018, I returned to Bangalore and Kerala, and added Dubai as an additional field site. The interviews in Bangalore revealed new trends since my first visit in 2015. Both outsourcing and information-technology are declining and are being overtaken by returnee entrepreneurs engaged in internet-of-things (IOT), artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning. Huawei’s relocation of its design center to Bangalore is indicative of this trend. Meanwhile, returnees are increasingly engaged in social responsibility and NGO work. During my return visit to Cochin in 2018, I conducted over two dozen interviews with returnees from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (especially Dubai), Qatar, Oman, and Kuwait across a diversity of occupations including artists, carpenters, cooks, drivers, health care professionals, housemaids, engineers, entrepreneurs in the hospitality sector, masons, and scientists. Blue-collar workers generally recounted the grueling working conditions abroad. Professionals missed the more cosmopolitan lifestyle that they had in the Gulf—with the exception of women who lived in Saudi Arabia who were confined to their homes. Interviewees also complained about the dearth of meaningful employment for well-educated Malayalis within Kerala, viewing its remittance economy as a resource curse. During that same trip I conducted fieldwork in the northern Muslim-dominant district of Malappuram in Kerala. The impact of Gulf migration is most visibly apparent in Malappuram as rural roads are lined with gold shops, “Gulf mansions” built by returnees, and banks. Unlike earlier generations of Gulf remittances that primarily went into gold and real estate, more recent ones are also funding educational and religious institutions (mosques and madrasas), and engaged in social services. For example, I visited a non-profit Muslim college (SAFI) that was established in 2005 and funded by Gulf returnees. I also interviewed a social worker who is dedicated to raising money to help release Indians imprisoned in the Middle East, and transport the corpses of Indians from the Middle East. Because so many of my interviewees in Kerala had worked in Dubai, I added it as a related field site so I could meet Malayalis (Keralans) currently working there. Over 85 percent of Indians residing in Dubai are from Kerala, and Malayalis view Dubai as an extension of the State of Kerala. In Dubai I interviewed construction workers, dentists, engineers, nurses, restaurant owners, and white-collar professionals who were all from Kerala. Meanwhile, Dubai hosts a population of approximately 270,000 Chinese and those engaged in commerce are primarily from Wenzhou, Zhejiang. Their businesses are concentrated in Dragon Mart, which has nearly 4,000 stores and is regarded as the largest Chinese market in the Middle East and outside of China. At Dragon Mart, I interviewed traders from Zhejiang as well as Guangdong. Research Outputs In addition to earlier presentations of papers on the Bangalore-Beijing dyad at Oxford University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, during the second half of the project, I delivered 7 presentations at various research workshops, seminars, and conferences: “Moving Markets and Money: Zhejiang and Gujarat’s Transnational Traders,” Social Science Research Council (SSRC)’s InterAsian Connections V: Seoul Workshop on “Genealogies of Financialization: Reframing Sovereignty in Asia (1600-present),” Seoul National University, April 27-30, 2016. “Moving Markets and Money: Zhejiang and Gujarat’s Transnational Traders,” UCLA-CUHK-HKUST Workshop on Migration Studies, Chinese University of Hong Kong, December 6-7, 2016. “Elite Returnees in Beijing and Bangalore: Information Technology and Beyond,” Dissemination Workshop on Transnational Migration in Transition: Transformative Characteristics of Temporary Migration, European Union Project, Centre for Development Studies, Thiruvanathapuram, Kerala, January 23-24, 2017. “Co-Ethnic Capital in Coastal China and India: The Developmental Diasporas of Guangdong and Kerala,” International Consortium of Chinese Studies (ICCS), Centre for Economic Research, Mannheim, Germany, June 20-21, 2017. “Co-Ethnic Capital in Coastal China and India: The Developmental Diasporas of Guangdong and Kerala,” Business History Seminar, Harvard Business School, Cambridge, MA, September 25, 2017. “Co-Ethnic Capital in Coastal China and India: The Developmental Diasporas of Guangdong and Kerala,” Department of Sociology, Hong Kong Baptist University, November 2, 2018. “Elite Returnees in Beijing and Bangalore,” Center for Global Asia Lecture Series, NYU Shanghai, November 26, 2018. One of the unexpected, positive externalities of this project is that universities in India have started soliciting my assistance in developing their China studies programs. The United Board and Harvard-Yenching Institute invited me to deliver lectures on Teaching about China in India Colleges at Christ University in Bangalore on January 7, 2018. Interacting with Indian academics enabled me to develop additional contacts for fieldwork and receive informal feedback on this project. The overarching output of this project is a book manuscript. I have submitted a book proposal to Cornell University Press and received encouraging feedback from the acquisitions editor (Roger Haydon) who published two of my previous books. [A letter of interest from Cornell University Press is attached to this report.] Intermediate publications include the following: “Cosmopolitan Capitalism: Local State-Society Relations in China and India,” Journal of Asian Studies 75, 2 (May 2016): 335-361. “Rescaling State-Society Relations in China and India,” in Prasenjit Duara and Elizabeth Perry, eds., Beyond Regimes: China and India Compared (Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 2018), Ch. 7, 257-293. Note that I have intentionally "saved" original empirical findings for presentation in the book manuscript.

16401414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16401414.value: Major findings are presented according to the comparative research design of three pairs of sub-national cases in China and India. Zhejiang and Gujarat The developmental imprint of migrants from Zhejiang and Gujarat striking similarities. First, with the most dynamic private sectors in India and China, the preponderance of migrants from Zhejiang and Gujarat engage in commerce. Second, the migratory merchants of Wenzhou and Surat possess dense transnational networks supporting reliable channels of informal finance and dominate niche markets around the world. Third, despite historical differences in out-migration, the respective local governments recognize their native place diasporas as resources for domestic development. These shared features distinguish Zhejiang and Gujarat from other localities in China and India. A key difference is that Gujaratis are more likely to identify as Gujaratis while abroad, while migrants from Zhejiang are more likely to identify with their native place. Beijing and Bangalore Zhongguancun in Beijing is home to about half of the Chinese firms currently listed on NASDAQ. Hailed as the “Outsourcing Capital of the World” during the early 2000s, Bangalore now leads in post-IT frontier technologies including artificial intelligence (AI) and the internet-of-things (IOT). ZGC and Bangalore are both beneficiaries of national industrial policy, while their local governments also provided a supportive environment. Their technology sectors rely on blended domestic and diasporic networks of human, social, and financial capital. Leading entrepreneurs and venture capitalists in Beijing and Bangalore may not be native to those cities, but rather, elite returnees attracted by the local infrastructure and eco-system for start-ups. Some have become philanthropists and/or social activists, more so in Bangalore than Beijing. Guangdong and Kerala With long southern coastlines and historically significant ports for maritime trade, Guangdong and Kerala have experienced continued circulation of migrants who have re-invested in their localities. The governments in Guangdong and Kerala are sensitive to these realities, and have adapted a proactive stance towards incorporating their transnational extensions of society. Local state identity is as much shaped by outmigration as native place retains some degree of co-ethnic identity for those who have left. Meanwhile, both have attracted domestic migrants from other parts of the country. Even though their contemporary political reputations lie at opposite ends of the ideological spectrum—neoliberalism in Guangdong versus communism in Kerala—the fact that both have multi-generational as well as more recent diasporic populations has had complex developmental implications, including local inequality and complicated regional politics.

16401414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16401414.value: The PI has already pursued a cognate research direction that focuses on local state agency in China's economic development with a graduate student trained in this project. Next, examining interactions between China and India’s migrants represents a logical next step. This project compared the local diasporic impact of three sets of sub-national cases. However, at multiple junctures of the research process the PI learned that their diasporic populations have intersected historically, as well as in the contemporary era. This was most apparent in sites outside of mainland China and India, including Dubai, Hong Kong, and Singapore. But there are also communities of Chinese in India (e.g., Kolkata, Mumbai), and Indians in China (e.g., Dunhuang, Guangzhou, Yiwu). To analyze the nature of interactions between China and India, the PI has started a collaboration with other China-India scholars, including Prasenjit Duara (Duke), Arunabh Ghosh (Harvard), and Tansen Sen (NYU) on an Oxford Handbook of India-China Connections. The Handbook is organized along connecting sites (e.g., Dunhuang, Guangzhou, Burma, Yiwu, etc.), connecting peoples (e.g., Buddhist monks, traders, diplomats, tourists, intellectuals, politicians), connecting ideas (cowries, silk, manuscripts, relics, tea, opium, mobile phones), connecting ideas (e.g., afterlife, medicine, astronomy, modern science), and so on.

16401414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16401414.value: At a moment when populist xenophobia is gripping domestic politics in large swaths of the world, the empirical findings of this study contribute much-needed nuance to enduring debates about the implications of international migration, return migration, remittances, foreign direct investment, and political identity. While these debates are conducted based on national-level generalizations, the explicitly sub-national lens of this study provides an alternative, multi-scalar approach for appreciating the local impact of international migration on migrant-sending areas. The combination of migratory circulation, remittances, and local state agency in encouraging return migration and investment have made the six localities in this study known to national leaders, social scientists, foreign investors, and other observers. None of the individual localities should be taken to represent China or India as a whole even though there is a tendency to generalize from their experiences to the rest of the country. This project shows that migration can have a mixed developmental impact on particular localities. On the one hand, remittances can increase local welfare, contribute to economic development, and enhance local educational and health care institutions. On the other hand, reliance on diasporic resources may disincentivize local investment, introduce local inequality, and distort local patterns of consumption.

16402114.label: Project Objectives
16402114.value: To obtain acoustic data by recording 12 Miao speakers from the Yuliang Village, Wanshui Town, Kaili District, Guizhou Province. To conduct laboratory work (acoustic measurement and mathematical treatment) on the raw data collected from the field. To conduct phonological analysis of the phonetic data obtained from Objective (2). To engage in follow-up fieldwork in the Kaili District and record more speakers there, followed by laboratory and phonological analyses. To research into ONE more Miao-speaking area in the neighboring provinces of Yunnan, Guangxi, Hunan or Sichuan. To explore the theoretical significance of the present project along these lines: (a) In relation to phonetics and perceptual studies, is it possible to have six level tones in a language? (b) If so, then how to represent the six level tones in phonology, and how to construct a tonal typology accommodating six level tones?

16402114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16402114.value: The present project aims to (1) investigate the acoustic and phonological properties of the tonal systems of the Miao dialects spoken in the Kaili area, Guizhou province, China, to verify a tonal pattern of six level- or even-pitched tones, which has arguably the greatest theoretical significance for tonetics, tonology and tonal typology; and (2) extend the investigation to more Miao varieties to explore the tonal typology of Miao. So far only five or less level tones have been confirmed in a single language, and the current theoretical framework for tone representation, the Five-Point Scale, can only define up to five level tones. The PI recently came across a theoretically significant six-level-tone system in a Miao dialect spoken in the Yuliang Village, Wanshui Town, Kaili District, Guizhou Province 貴州省凱里市灣水鎮魚粱村. To verify this pattern and to find out the tonal typology of Miao, which is famous for its large numbers of level tones, the PI proposed this project. If the six-level-tone system is confirmed, not only is our typological knowledge enriched, but also would the fundamental theory in current phonology need to be rewritten. 本研究項目有兩個主要目標：第一，詳細調研我國貴州省凱里地區苗語方言裏聲調的聲學數據和音韻系統特徵，特別是查證該地有哪個方言真正擁有六個平調。假如真的找到有多於五個平調的方言，這對語言聲調系統的對立格局研究、聲調學、語言類型學都有至關重要的理論價值。第二，對其他地區的苗語方言進行初步調查，並考察苗語各種聲調在類型學上的特點。 直至目前為止，語言學家只能找到最多有五個平調的語言。事實上，語言學家慣用的標調方式，即「五度系統」，最多也只能處理五個平調。但是，本研究項目的負責人最近在貴州省凱里市灣水鎮魚粱村找到了一種似乎具備六個平調的苗語方言，是現行五度系統沒法標示的。 苗語方言以平調數目較多而著稱，本項目的負責學者準備調查苗語聲調的類型特點，並確認是否真正存著具有多於五個平調的語言。如果擁有六個平調的語言真的存在，那麼當今語言學有關人類語言的發音和音韻系統的基本認識必須改寫；如果不存在，音韻學如何處理表面上似乎有六個平調的聲調系統也是十分重要的課題。本研究必定會加深對各種聲調系統類型的認識，而且還可能改變語音學與音韻學的基本框架。

16402114.label: Realisation of objectives
16402114.value: All the objectives, except No. 4, listed above have been perfectly achieved, detailed below. 1. Actually more than 12 Miao speakers were recorded. 2. All the data obtained from the field were carefully examined and laboratory work has been conducted on the data. 3. A thorough phonological analysis was carried out on the data. 4. No follow-up fieldwork was conducted because more than enough data had been obtained from the first round of firld investigation. 5. I have extended my comparative researches to other Miao-speaking areas in Hunan, and to other languages related to Miao, including Yao, Vietnamese, and surrounding Chinese dialects. 6. It is confirmed that, phonetically and perceptually, six level tones can exist in one language. Partially based on the results of this project, a general tone inventory has been proposed and a tonal typology has been established, which is a breakthrough for tone studies.

(b) If so, then how to represent the six level tones in phonology, and how to construct a tonal typology accommodating six level tones?

16402114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16402114.value: Tone has been represented on a five-point scale since the early years of modern tone studies in 1930. In this internationally standardized system the maximal number of level tones in a language is limited to five. This project has confirmed that there is a six level tone system which exists in a Miao language. The direct theoretical and practical significance of the result of the project is that the current paradigm of tone studies should be substantially modified or even overthrown. Partially based on the results of this project, a general tone inventory has been proposed and a tonal typology has been established, which is a breakthrough in the field.

16402114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16402114.value: With the establishment of tonal typology, a new research field is emerging on the horizon. Numerous new research topics will arise: to test the tonotypes in the general tone inventory and to find out more new ones. In fact, the general tone inventory proposed is just like a periodic table of tonal elements, which will serve as a basic theoretical framework for all the fields of tone studies such as tonal typology, tone evolution, descriptive fieldwork, perceptual study of tonal categories, etc.

16402114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16402114.value: Modern tone studies started a century ago, and so far, at least four thousands contour tone systems have been documented. Unfortunately, however, tonal typology had not been established until recently when the studies supported by or related to this project were conducted. A general tone inventory was proposed by the PI which is akin to a periodic table of tonal elements, which will serve as a basic theoretical framework for all the fields of tone studies such as tonal typology, tone evolution studies, descriptive fieldwork, perceptual study of tonal categories, etc.

16500114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16500114.value: 上市公司授予股東投資決策審批權的研究

16500114.label: Project Objectives
16500114.value: To examine the association between ownership characteristics, including state ownership and block shareholders, and the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders. To examine the association between the firm's business environment, such as uncertainty and competition, and the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders. To examine the association of shareholder right to approve investment decisions and the percentage of institutional shareholding after IPO. To examine the impact of the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders on the firm's over- and under-investment behaviors.

To examine the association between the firm's business environment, such as uncertainty and competition, and the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders.
To examine the association of shareholder right to approve investment decisions and the percentage of institutional shareholding after IPO.
To examine the impact of the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders on the firm's over- and under-investment behaviors.

16500114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500114.value: Shareholders of listed companies around the world typically do not have the right to approve or reject investment decisions. Recently, there have been calls for giving shareholders such power. The desirability of this practice is uncertain as researchers are divided on whether shareholders would really be better off with the enhanced control over corporate investment decisions. The reason is that although this right is helpful in curbing the agency problems between managers and shareholders, the latter do not have superior information over the former to improve the decisions. The proposed study intends to take advantage of a unique setting in China’s listed companies: many of them have included provisions in the corporate charters or bylaws to empower shareholders with the right to approve investment decisions. In addition, the threshold of the size of investment that requires shareholder approval varies widely among firms. While some charters require shareholder approval if the investment is higher than 30 percent of total assets, others set the threshold much lower. In comparison to those in other countries, shareholders of China’s listed companies are more empowered with investment decisions. The empowerment provisions, however, raise at least two interesting questions. First, since most Chinese listed companies have a majority shareholder who can dictate the voting outcomes, how can the provisions even be meaningful to other shareholders? In other words, why do firms initiate those provisions? Second, China’s weak legal environment makes it easy for firms to circumvent their own empowerment provisions. Thus, can the provisions reduce the agency problems such as over-investing? The proposed study attempts to answer these two questions. It is expected to show that firms give shareholders more right in approving investment decisions when they are state-owned enterprises (SOEs) or have more ownership of block shareholders who do not have representation on the board. In addition, those firms are in less competitive industries or operate in a less uncertain business environment. When a firm includes the empowerment provisions in their charters, they are likely to attract more institutional investors. Further, the empowerment provision is associated with lower over-investment behavior, especially when the firm has more institutional investors. In summary, the proposed study will provide evidence on the benefits of the empowerment provisions as a corporate governance mechanism in certain circumstances. The results will inform regulators in countries with relatively weak legal environment about the desirability of empowering shareholders with the right to approve major investment decisions.

16500114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500114.value: Objective (1): Firms with majority shareholders who own higher percentage of shares grant more investment decision rights to shareholders. But state ownership doesn't have impact. Objective (2): There is no association between the firm's business environment, such as uncertainty and competition, and the granting of investment decision rights to shareholders. The lack of results could be due to the noise in the measures of business environment. Objective (3): Firms which grant more investment decision rights to shareholders have higher percentage of institutional shareholding after IPO. Objective (4): Firms which grant more investment decision rights have less under-investment. In addition, they have better acquisition quality as measured by market reactions to the announcement of acquisition. Moreover, the cash holdings of this group of firms are valued more than the rest by the market. The above results are obtained using difference-in-difference methodology, taking advantage of the 2006 change in China's Company Law which gives shareholders more decision rights to some firms, and makes no change to others.

16500114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500114.value: Because the results from objective (4) are more free from the endogeneity problems, they have been written up as a draft and presented in a conference and workshops in a few universities. Revision is underway to incorporate more tests to further support the main findings. The paper is expected to be submitted to a good finance journal soon.

16500114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500114.value: This study investigates the effectiveness of enhanced shareholder empowerment in a weak institutional environment. Using China’s regulation to grant shareholders with more decision rights on acquisition as a setting, we find companies whose shareholders gained more control over acquisition decisions from the regulation experience higher market reactions around the initial acquisition announcement date. they are also less likely to engage in overinvestment. In addition, the stock market give higher valuation to the cash holdings of these companies. Moreover, we find that these effects are weak for SOEs. Overall, our results suggest that shareholders’ voting serves a governance role in a weak institutional environment such as that in China. Our results also imply that the government ownership would hamper the governance function of shareholders’ voting.

16500414.label: Project Objectives
16500414.value: Determine whether there are systematic differences in executive pay disparity between the firms included in the ExecuComp database and those not. 16500414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500414.value: Pay disparity among senior executives of public listed firms, especially the pay gap between the CEO and other senior executives, has been increasing over time since 1970s and has received increasing attention from investors, rating agencies, and regulators. There are debates on why the pay disparity varies across firms and increases over time, and on the implication of the pay disparity for firm behavior and performance. The emerging literature on the executive pay disparity has offered several explanations of the executive pay disparity (e.g., Murphy and Zábojník, 2004, 2007; Kale, Reis, and Venkateswaran, 2009; Bebchuk, Cremers, and Peyer, 2011). To our best knowledge, all empirical studies on executive pay disparity have relied on the ExecuComp database. The objective of this project is to compare the executive pay disparity, its economic determinants, and its association with firm behavior and performance between the US firms included in the ExecuComp database and those not. This project is important for several reasons. First, the ExecuComp database only includes the firms that comprise the S&P 1500 index. Although these firms comprise about 88 percent of the market capitalization of publicly traded firms in the US, they only represent about 25 percent of the firms in the Compustat database. Thus, the current studies on the executive pay disparity have missed a substantial portion of firms (Cadman, Klasa, and Matsunaga, 2010). Moreover, the characteristics, governance structure, managerial labor market, and contracting environments are quite distinct between the firms included in the ExecuComp database and those not (Cadman et al., 2010). Therefore examining the executive pay disparity in the firms not included in the ExecuComp database could provide valuable insights into how executive pay disparity is determined and how it affects firm behavior and performance. Finally, given the debates on executive pay disparity, it is important to know how different theories are able to explain the executive pay disparity and its implication in a group of firms with distinct characteristics. 自上世紀70年代開始，上市公司高管的薪酬差異一直在持續上升，特別是CEO与其他高管之間的薪酬差異。投資者，評級機構及監管機構對這一現象的關注也在持續上升。為什麼高管薪酬差異會持續上升，為什麼高管薪酬差異的大小在公司間有區別，高管薪酬差異對公司的行為及業績會有什麽影響？對於這些問題的爭議一直不斷。以往文獻提供了若干解釋（例如Murphy 与 Zábojník, 2004, 2007; Kale, Reis, 与 Venkateswaran, 2009; Bebchuk, Cremers, 与 Peyer, 2011）。但據我們所知，所有關於高管薪酬差異的實證研究都是基於execucomp數據庫。本課題將比較高管薪酬差異以及其成因与經濟後果在被execucomp數據庫包括的公司（execucomp公司）及其他公司（non-execucomp公司）之間的差異。本課題有如下重要性。首先，execucomp數據庫只包括了在標普1500指數內的公司。儘管這些公司的市值占到所有美國上市公司總市值的88%，但是它們只占所有包括進compustat數據庫公司數量的25%。所以，現有的研究忽略了相當大的一部分公司（Cadman, Klasa, 与 Matsunaga, 2010）。另外，execucomp公司与non-execucomp公司在公司特徵，治理結構，管理人員市場，以及訂約環境上有非常大的差異。所以，研究non-execucomp公司的高管薪酬差異對於我們理解高管薪酬差異的成因及經濟後果有重要意義。最后，鑒於目前對於高管薪酬差異的爭議，測試不同的理論是普適程度也非常重要。

16500414.label: Realisation of objectives
16500414.value: The compensation data is collected from Capital IQ People intelligence database. To alleviate the concern that any difference between the Execucomp and non-Execucomp firms is due to data inconsistency, we do not use the compensation data from Execucomp database for Execucomp firms. Accounting data is collected from Compustat and stock return data from CRSP. M&A variables are retrieved from SDC. Since the total compensation from Capital IQ database before 2007 does not include option compensation, the sample is limited after the observations between 2007 and 2014. Several regressions are estimated to achieve the objectives. Objective #1 is achieved by the following regression CPS(i,t) = a0*EXECOMP+control variables (i,t-1) + industry and year fexed effects + e(i,t) CPS is the measure of executive pay disparity and is defined as the fraction of CEO’s total pay to total pay of the top five executives. EXECOMP is a dummy variable that equals one if the firm is covered in Execucomp and zero otherwise. The coefficient of interest is a0. Objective #2 is achieved by estimating the following regression for the execucomp and non-execucomp firms separately. CPS(i,t) = B0*X(i,t-1) + industry and year fexed effects + e(i,t) X is a vector of economic determinants of CPS. Objective #2 is achieved by comparing coefficients B0 between the two subsamples. Objective #3 is achieved by estimating the following regression. Y(i,t+1) = b0*CPS(i,t) + controls + industry and year fixed effects + e(i,t+1) Y includes firm value as measured by Tobin's Q and return on assets. Objective #3 is achieved by comparing coefficient b0 between the two samples of firms. Objective #4 is achieved similarly by estimating the following regression. CAR(i,s,t+1) = b0*CPS(i,t) + controls + industry and year fixed effects + e(i,t+1) where CAR(i,s,t+1) is the market reaction to M&A transactions conducted by firm i in year t+1. Objective #4 is achieved by comparing the coefficient b0 between the two samples.

16500414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500414.value: Pay disparity among executives has been increasing overtime and receiving increasing attention. However, the underlying driving forces are not well understood. Most existing studies on the executive pay disparity are based on firms covered in the ExecuComp database, and thus their conclusions may not be generalizable to other firms that have quite different characteristics and contracting environment. We find that Execucomp firms have higher executive pay disparity than non-Execucomp firms. However, the negative association between executive pay disparity and firm value among Execucomp firms as documented in Bebchuk, Cremers, and Peyer (2001, JFE) does not hold in non-Execucomp firms. The association between executive pay disparity and future accounting performance is even positive for non-Execucomp firms. Overall, our evidence does not support the entrenchment view as an explanation for executive pay disparity among non-Execucomp firms. In contrast, optimal tournament design appears to be an explanation for executive pay disparity among these firms.

16500414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500414.value: Pay disparity among executives has been increasing over time and receiving increasing attention. There are two views towards this phenomenon. One school believes that a high pay disparity is a symptom of managerial power and indicates severe agency problem. Another school believes that a high pay disparity is a result of optimal choice made to attract talent. Most existing studies on the executive pay disparity are based on firms from S&P1500. There is relatively little study on other firms (i.e., firms not included in the S&P1500 index) that have quite different characteristics. My research aims to understand whether pay disparity is driven by different factors and have different value implications in these two types of firms.

16500614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16500614.value: 测量方法与偏好反转: 基于理性的解释

16500614.label: Project Objectives
16500614.value: First, we present a formal theoretical analysis to provide a rational explanation for two types of procedure-dependent preferences. Second, we use lab experiments to test unique predictions of the proposed theory.
rows: First, we present a formal theoretical analysis to provide a rational explanation for two types of procedure-dependent preferences.
Second, we use lab experiments to test unique predictions of the proposed theory.

16500614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500614.value: One fundamental principle of rational choice theory is that of procedure invariance. That is, if two elicitation procedures are strategically equivalent, they should yield the same ordering in stated preferences. However, a great deal of controlled lab experiments show that preferences elicited under different procedures can be systematically varied (e.g., preference reversal). One of the most studied preference reversals is the phenomenon that gambles offering larger payoffs with lower probabilities are favored more in valuations than in choices, relative to gambles offering smaller payoffs with higher probabilities. Another robust finding of systematic preference reversal is that joint evaluation of options, in comparison to separate evaluation, can lead to higher valuation for the option with higher value on a difficult-to-evaluate attribute. In this proposed research we will examine the effect of elicitation procedures on stated preferences. Our major objective is to present a rational, synthesizing theory to account for these preference reversals. Our proposed explanation rests on a two-stage sequential decision process under which a decision maker can endogenously improve her information about preference through costly deliberation. This decision process implies that deliberation can mediate between elicitation procedure and stated preference, i.e., the elicitation procedure may influence the stated preference through affecting the incentive to deliberate over the preference. As a result, even though the underlying preference per se is independent of elicitation procedure, the stated preference may appear to be influenced by how it is elicited. Conditional on information, this theory of contextual deliberation is consistent with the standard expected utility theory. This allows us to stay with the conventional expected utility framework, while endogenously deriving preference reversals and the violation of the independence and the intransitivity axioms. The proposed theory can yield unique predictions that we plan to test experimentally. In particular, we predict that measures of deliberation (e.g., response time) can mediate the relation between elicitation procedure and stated preference. In addition, we expect that the dispersion in stated responses may vary with the elicitation procedure. Moreover, as the cost/need of deliberation becomes sufficiently small or sufficiently large, the role of deliberation in stated preferences would be mitigated and fewer instances of preference reversals would be observed. 测量过程不变性是理性选择理论的基本原则之一。也就是说，如果某两个测量方法在本质上是一致的，那么它们应该会产生一样的偏好表述。然而，很多实验的结果表明，通过不同方法测量的偏好可能会有系统性的不一致(比如偏好反转)。其中一种得到最多关注的偏好反转是指下列现象，相对于提供更少回报但更高概率的赌局而言，那些能提供更多回报但更低概率的赌局可能会得到更高的估值，但是却会被更少人选择。在另外一个稳健的关于系统性偏好反转的发现中，相对于分开评估而言，联合评估能使得那些在某些很难评估的方面上有更高价值的选项获得更高的综合评价。 我们在该研究计划中将会研究测量方法对于偏好的影响。我们的主要研究目的是提出一个基于理性的统一的理论来解释这些偏好反转的现象。我们提出的解释是基于一个两阶段的决策模型，该模型允许决策者可以通过思考(deliberation)来获得更多关于自己偏好的信息。这个决策过程意味着思考可能会是测量方法和偏好表述之间的调节因素，也就是说测量方法可能会通过影响与偏好有关的思考来影响偏好。这样的结果就是，即使内在的偏好本身是独立于测量方法的，体现出来的偏好也可能会看起来好像是受测量方法影响的。如果不考虑信息的因素，那么这个情景考虑的理论和传统的期望效用理论是一致的。这就使得我们可以以传统的期望效用理论为基础，来解释偏好反转现象，并解释违背独立性和传导性公理假设的现象。 从该理论得出的推论，我们计划通过实验来进行实证检验。具体而言，我们预测思考的测量值（比如反馈时间）可能会是测量方法和偏好之间的调节因素。另外，被试间的偏好差别大小可能会随着测量方法的不同而变化。另外，随着思考的成本或者思考的必要性变得非常高或者非常低，思考在偏好表述中的重要性会变弱，偏好反转的现象也会变弱。

16500614.label: Realisation of objectives
16500614.value: First, to present a formal theoretical analysis to provide a rational explanation for two types of procedure-dependent preferences, I develop a theoretical framework of contextual deliberation that endogenizes the dependence of revealed preferences on elicitation procedures. To account for the difference between riskless and risky decision making, the framework is further developed into separate theoretical models to fit the different settings. I demonstrate how the models can explain a variety of seemingly disparate preference reversals. I also derive predictions that can be tested experimentally and permit the identification from other alternative explanations. I have finished all the analysis and reported the results in two papers titled “Contextual Deliberation and Procedure-Dependent Preference Reversals” and “Contextual Deliberation and the Choice-Valuation Preference Reversal.” Second, to test unique predictions of the proposed theory, I conducted laboratory experiment with a novel design. I have completed all the data analysis, and obtained strong support for the main predictions of the theoretical model for the choice-valuation preference reversal. I reported the results in the second paper titled “Contextual Deliberation and the Choice-Valuation Preference Reversal,” which is now submitted for review at a top journal.
