16500614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500614.value: In the paper titled “Contextual Deliberation and Procedure-Dependent Preference Reversals,” I develop a synthesizing theory of contextual deliberation to endogenize the dependence of revealed preferences on elicitation procedures. I show that, when people do not know their preferences perfectly (even for alternatives with well-defined attributes), they can engage in cognitive activities to retrieve or acquire relevant preference information (i.e., deliberation) before responding to a decision task. I find that elicitation procedures can influence ex post preferences through affecting the incentive for deliberation. Consequently, procedure dependence may emerge endogenously. That is, revealed preferences may appear to be procedure dependent, even though the underlying preference/information structure is not. I demonstrate that the theory of contextual deliberation can parsimoniously rationalize seemingly disparate phenomena of procedure-dependent preference reversals (between choice and matching tasks, or between joint and separate valuations), without resorting to any non-standard preference/belief (e.g., the prominence/evaluability hypotheses). In the paper titled “Contextual Deliberation and the Choice-Valuation Preference Reversal,” I extend the theory of contextual deliberation to decision making under risk. I develop the theory by assuming that a decision maker may not immediately recognize her true risk attitude when she faces a decision task (i.e., choice, valuation). Nevertheless, she can decide how much cognitive efforts to invest in retrieving or acquiring preference-relevant information (i.e., deliberation), before responding to the task as an expected-utility maximizer. I spell out the necessary and sufficient conditions under which the choice-valuation preference reversal between P-bets and $-bets arises. I also test predictions of the theory in a novel lab experiment and identify it from other alternative explanations. I show that, when lottery pairing was ex ante unknown, preferences for $-bets were lower in choice than in valuation, and standard reversals were more frequent than nonstandard reversals. However, this behavioral pattern was substantially weakened when pairing information was available. Second, known pairing mitigated the asymmetry of reversals not by significantly changing the lotteries’ mean valuations: neither the P-bets were valued higher nor the $-bets valued lower. Instead, known pairing gave rise to mean-preserving spread in the distribution of stated valuations. In addition, there is some evidence that response time was longer for P-bet than for $-bet choices. These experiment results are remarkably consistent with predictions of contextual deliberation. The paper is currently submitted to a top journal for review.

16500614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500614.value: The theory of contextual deliberation can be extended to accommodate other types of preference construction. For example, previous decisions may endogenously influence preference information, and as a result seemingly irrelevant parameters in previous decisions may influence current decisions. This can then provide a rational explanation for various seemingly abnormal phenomena on dynamic decision making (e.g., the anchoring effect). Similarly, other factors such as mood or decision framing may indirectly influence choice behavior through affecting the cost/effectiveness of deliberation. In addition, the theory of contextual deliberation can be expanded to account for many other paradoxes of risk preferences. Future research can investigate how the theory of contextual deliberation can predict the emergence of preference reversals, i.e., the conditions under which it can be turned on and off. It would also be valuable to construct additional tests to experimentally identify the theory of contextual deliberation from other potential explanations. More sophisticated techniques (e.g., eye tracking and neuroimaging tools) can be employed to measure deliberation and present complemental or supplemental tests for the theoretical predictions. Another fruitful area for future research is to construct structural empirical models to recover the cost of deliberation and improve our understanding and prediction for choice behavior.

16500614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500614.value: Classical economic theories assume that people’s preferences over alternatives can be measured using different methods/procedures (e.g., choice, valuation, matching, joint versus separate evaluation). One basic principle is that different procedures should generate same inference on preferences. If this principle is violated, many economic theories and applications (e.g., consumer research, demand estimation, policy analysis) would be invalidated. Unfortunately, numerous empirical studies document seeming violations of the procedure-independence assumption. For example, preferences can be systematically varied, and even reversed, between choice and matching, between choice and valuation, or across joint and separate evaluations. In this research we provide a new perspective to reconcile the empirically observed preference reversals with the procedure-invariance principle. We show both theoretically and experimentally that various preference reversals may emerge even when people’s preferences are not directly dependent on the measuring procedures. Therefore, this research demonstrates that preference reversals should not necessarily be viewed as contradicting the basic assumption of economic theories. It suggests that the procedure independence assumption should not be abandoned completely, but should be refined to account for the endogenous process of how preferences are constructed. In addition, this new theory can provide a parsimonious framework to account for many other puzzling behavioral anomalies.

16500914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500914.value: When people make their consumption decisions, they often base their decisions on their affective forecasting, that is, their predictions of how the consumption experience will make them feel. For example, when deciding which new car to buy, consumers usually base their decisions on their predictions of how they would feel driving the car. Indeed, past research has shown that consumers’ anticipated feelings such as pleasure, satisfaction, and regret guide a wide range of consumption decisions such as brand choice and dieting decision (e.g., Mellers and McGraw 2001; Shiv and Huber 2000). However, research has shown that very often people’s affective forecasting is not accurate. One major error is that people tend to overestimate the intensity of their emotional reactions to a future event. For instance, people predict that they would be much happier driving a luxury car than driving an economic brand. However, the reported actual experiences of driving these different cars showed no significant difference (Schwarz and Xu 2011). We refer to this as the overprediction bias (also known as the impact bias; Wilson and Gilbert 2003, 2005). Such overprediction bias also occurs for important life events. For example, assistant professors predicted that getting tenure would make their life much happier whereas being denied tenure would lead to great emotional distress. However, in reality, former assistant professors who had achieved tenure were no happier than those who had not (Gilbert et al. 1998). Given that people’s affective forecasting is instrumental to their decision making, it is important to understand how such forecasting error occurs and identify possible ways to correct or reverse the bias. Thus, in this project, drawing on the literatures in affective forecasting and construal level theory, we propose to examine the following questions: (1) What is the mechanism underlying the overprediction bias? And are there ways to correct the overprediction bias? (2) Is it possible that the opposite bias would occur, that is, people may underpredict the difference in their feelings between two consumption experiences? (3) What are the conditions under which each bias would occur? (4) What are the implications of these overprediction biases for consumers and marketers? From a theoretical perspective, this research will contribute to literature on affective forecasting and consumer decision making as well as to construal level theory. From a practical point of view, this research will have important implications for marketers as well as for consumer well-being. 人們經常會按照其情感預測，即估計是次消費體驗將會帶給他們的感覺來作出消費決定。例如：當在選購新車時，消費者通常會按照他們預測的駕駛感覺來作選擇。而事實上，在過去的研究中亦指出消費者預料的感覺，像愉快、滿足及後悔感都能引導廣泛性的消費決定，如作品牌選擇和飲食考慮（如Mellers and McGraw 2001；Shiv and Huber 2000）。 可是，研究亦指出人們的情感預測往往並不準確。其中一個主要的誤差是由於人們慣性地高估了他們在未來事件上情緒反應的強度。譬如，人們預計駕駛名貴車輛定當比駕駛經濟車輛為快樂。但是，根據報告的實際經驗而言，駕駛這兩類車輛的快樂感並沒有指標性的分別（Schwarz and Xu 2011）。我們將此稱為高估偏差（這也被稱為衝擊偏差；Wilson and Gilbert 2003, 2005）。這類的高估偏差亦出現在重要的人生事件上。例如，助理教授們預計獲得常任職位會令到其人生更加快樂，而遭受拒絕則會導致巨大的精神痛苦。可是，事實上，已取得常任職位的前助理教授們並沒有因而比沒有常任職位的更覺快樂（Gilbert et al. 1998）。 鑑於人們的情感預測有助於其決策，了解預測誤差如何發生和找出可能的方法來糾正或逆轉偏差是重要的。因此，在根據情感預測和解釋水平理論的文獻上，我們在這計劃中提議探究以下問題： １． 什麼是高估偏差背後的機制？和有沒有方法去糾正高估偏差？ ２． 相反的偏差，即人們可會低估了他們在兩次消費體驗中感覺的分別會否發生？ ３． 各偏差會在什麼情況下發生？ ４． 這些高估偏差對消費者和營銷者意味著什麼？

16500914.label: Realisation of objectives
16500914.value: All three objectives proposed in the project have been achieved. We focus our investigation of overprediction bias by focusing on one domain closely related to consumer behavior – wait duration judgment. Specifically, we study one form of overprecition bias – people tend to estimate how long a wait duration has been, from a construal level perspective. In a series of laboratory experiments, We show that the overprediction bias about wait duration judgment can be attenuated and even reserved when people think more concretely and they use feelings as the basis of duration judgment (Objectives 1 and 2). We further identify situation factors that moderate the effect: timing of the duration judgment (immediate judgment vs. delayed judgment), whether people trust their feelings (Objective 3). Finally, we extend the scope of investigation by examining the downstream consequences of construal level. Construal level theory (Trope and Liberman 2010) posits that people tend to construe a target at a low level if it is physically closer, is happening in the near future, is related closely to the self, or is real rather than hypothetical. In a series of lab experiments, we found that people tend to rely more on visual processing when construing proximal events while engaging in a greater degree of verbal processing with regard to distal targets; in turn, visual processing is more likely to yield low-level representations, whereas verbal processing facilitates high-level representations (Objective 4). The findings of this project has generated two journal publications in the Journal of Consumer Research, which is a top-tier journal in the field of marketing. I believe that the objectives of this proposal have been satisfactorily achieved.

Specifically, we will investigate the moderating role of evaluation mode, with the prediction that separate evaluation will lead to the overprediction bias and joint evaluation will lead to the underprediction bias.
To examine the downstream consequences of these affective forecasting biases on consumer well-being and marketers.

16500914.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500914.value: People can construe target objects and activities at a high level using general, superordinate features, or they can construe the same targets at a low level using specific, subordinate features of the target. Construal level theory (Trope and Liberman 2010) posits that people tend to construe a target at a low level if it is physically closer, is happening in the near future, is related closely to the self, or is real rather than hypothetical. The influence of psychological distance on construal level has been extensively documented. However, the extant literature takes a black box approach to this effect by viewing it as a direct association between distance and construal level. In the first publication (Yan, Sengupta, and Hong 2016), we seek to unpack this black box and provide more detailed process insights by identifying such an intervening variable: processing mode. We argue that people tend to rely more on visual processing when construing proximal events while engaging in a greater degree of verbal processing with regard to distal targets; in turn, visual processing is more likely to yield low-level representations, whereas verbal processing facilitates high-level representations. In the second publication (Wang, Hong, and Zhou 2018), we apply construal level theory in a very important consumer domain -- waiting. We show that construal levels affect wait duration judgments through two different routes: one based on consumers’ subjective feelings (an affective route) and the other based on mental markers (a cognitive route). We further identify the conditions under which the affective versus the cognitive route operates. Specifically, low-level construal people generate more wait-unrelated thoughts during the wait than high-level construal people. This difference in turn affects duration judgments in opposite directions depending on the judgment strategy that people use. People spontaneously rely on their subjective feelings—how long they feel they have waited. In this case, low- (vs. high-) level construal consumers, who are more distracted by their wait-unrelated thoughts, find the wait to be less boring and hence judge it to be shorter. However, when subjective feelings become less accessible (after a delay) or diagnostic (perceived as less trustworthy), or when mental markers become more accessible, people resort to the number of thoughts they had during the wait to infer the duration—the more thoughts they had, the longer it must have been. In this case, low- (vs. high-) level construal people perceive the wait to be longer.

16500914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500914.value: This research opens up several potential lines of investigation. First, scholars might wish to examine other ramifications of our finding that psychological distance influences processing mode. One interesting possibility lies in the domain of self-control. In particular, one reason that self-control is harder to exert given the physical presence of the tempting object (e.g., a delicious cake; Fedorikhin and Patrick 2010) could be that the reduced spatial distance, by activating visual processing, increases the influence of the visually tempting features of the cake. Interestingly, this line of thought also suggests how self-control can be enhanced, even when the tempting object is physically proximal. Rather than focusing on less vivid health-related benefits (e.g., lower cholesterol), preventive messages should focus on the visualizable benefits of exerting self-control (such as a better physical appearance). These are the benefits that are likely to carry greater weight when the self-control decision is psychologically nigh. Second, while the current research has shown that reduced psychological distance invokes one form of imagery-based processing (visual), future work should consider the possibility that similar effects obtain for other types of imagery based sensory processing (e.g., olfactory and auditory processes).

16500914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500914.value: Consumers can either think of objects and targets at a high, abstract level or a low, concrete level. For instance, “locking a door” may be thought of as “putting a key in the lock” (low-level) or as “securing the house” (high-level). There has been extensive consumer research that examines the impact of construal level on consumer decision making and information processing. In particular, research has established that people tend to think of a target at a concrete level if it feels psychologically close (e.g., physically closer, is happening in the near future, is related closely to the self, or is real rather than hypothetical). We show that people tend to rely more on visual processing when processing psychologically close events, which lead to low concrete representation; in contrast, people tend to engage in verbal processing for psychologically distal targets, which in turn yields high-level abstract representations. We further apply the concept of construal level to consumer waiting and show how this may affect how consumers perceive how long they have waited. Our research not only provides theoretical insights but also offers managerial implications on how marketers should manage consumer wait experience.

16501114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501114.value: The nature of the firm is to develop and institutionalize innovative technologies, superior processes, and optimal organizational forms to acquire and protect core competencies. These core competencies are, by nature and by design, organizational traits. When do managers matter? We hypothesize they should matter when they deliver “infra-core competencies”, competencies that generate consistent superior performance for their employer but are not part of their employer core competencies. To investigate this hypothesis, we consider firm forecasting ability. We argue that, for most firms, forecasting is an infra-core competency provided by individual managers. This proposition has three aspects. The first one is whether good forecasting ability is of economic importance for the firm. That is, does good forecasting ability lead to superior firm welfare? The second aspect is whether this ability is a distinctive trait of the organization or a manager specific skill. Finally, to the extent that forecasting ability is a managerial skill, we examine if it is recognized by employers. Our investigation will shed light on the importance of forecasting ability in a broad range of firms, and contribute to our understanding the role of managerial effects in firm competencies. 企業的本質是發展並機構化創新技術、良好程序、最佳組織形式以取得並保護核心競爭力。這些核心競爭力從本質和設計而言是組織特徵。公司管理者何時起作用呢？我們假設當他們提供準核心競爭力時起作用。準核心競爭力是指管理者為公司提供持續性優良業績的能力，但這種能力並不屬於公司核心競爭力的一部分。為了研究我們的假設，我們考慮公司盈餘預測的能力。我們的論點是，對多數公司而言，預測是一種管理者提供的準核心競爭力。這個提議有三個層面。第一，好的預測能力是否對公司具有經濟重要性，也就是好的預測能力是否為公司帶來福利？第二，這種能力是公司特質或管理者特有技能。最後，如果預測能力在一定程度上屬於管理者特有技能，我們研究它是否被公司認可。我們的研究將為預測能力是否對廣範圍的公司具有重要性提供啟發，並幫助我們理解管理者在公司競爭力中起的作用。

16501114.label: Realisation of objectives
16501114.value: To achieve the first objective, we estimate the effect of forecast quality, measured by management forecast consistency (Hilary, Hsu, and Wang 2015), on firm performance. We measure firm performance from three different perspectives: operating performance (measured by their ROA), productivity (measured using a data envelopment analysis), and valuation (measured by the firm Tobin's Q). To achieve the second objective, we test whether forecast ability is largely a managerial characteristic. Specifically, we test whether past forecasting consistency of a CEO is a strong predictor of future consistency for the same CEO, even after controlling for firm characteristics. In addition, we test whether CEO fixed effects significantly affect forecast consistency in a sample of executives who change employers, using a variance decomposition analysis (e.g., Abowd et al., 1999). To achieve the third objective, we test whether CEOs who issue high-quality earnings forecasts are rewarded for such skill. We consider three aspects of CEO welfare; the probability of finding another CEO appointment in case of departure, the probability of being replaced, and overall CEO compensation. The three objectives have been achieved through our empirical analysis. We document our empirical results in the attached working paper "Forecasting Ability, Firm Welfare and Managerial Skill". We originally wrote the paper for management journals and we submitted the paper to Strategic Management Journal. Unfortunately, the paper was rejected, perhaps because management forecast is largely an accounting topic. We have subsequently revised our paper for accounting journals. It has taken us some time to consider a suitable journal for our paper. On the one hand, management forecast is largely an accounting topic. On the other hand, our empirical methods and results are closely related to the literature on management and organization. We finally decided to submit our paper to Accounting, Organizations and Society, a major international journal concerned with all aspects of the relationship between accounting and human behaviour, organizational structures and processes. The paper is currently under review at this journal.

16501114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501114.value: We find that the ability to make superior forecasts is associated with greater firm performance, and that this ability is supported by managerial skills, and that firms compensate managers who possess such skills. First, firms that forecast their earnings more consistently experience higher profitability, higher productivity and higher valuation. Second, we find that forecast ability is to a large extent a managerial characteristic. Specifically, past forecasting consistency of a CEO is a strong predictor of future consistency for the same CEO, even after controlling for firm characteristics. In addition, we find that CEO fixed effects significantly affect forecast consistency in a sample of executives who change employers. Finally, we find that CEOs who provide better forecasts are more likely to find another CEO position when they depart. This result supports the idea that the labor market attributes the capacity to issue consistent forecasts to managerial skill rather than to the firm’s information environment. Consistent with the view that boards of directors value forecasting skill, we find that CEOs with greater forecast quality have a lower probability of dismissal and earn higher compensation. These results hold when we control for firm performance and financial distress.

16501114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501114.value: One possible further development of this project is to provide cross-sectional analyses to shed light on when managerial forecast ability matters more to a firm. For example, managerial forecast ability may be more valuable for firms with complex operations or for firms that face strong competition.

16501114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501114.value: We contribute to the existing literature by establishing a link between forecast quality and broad managerial skills. In particular, we show that firms managed by CEOs who can form better expectations of future earnings experience higher valuation and profitability. Moreover, we demonstrate that managerial forecasting ability is, to a large extent, a CEO rather than a firm characteristic. Our study also extends the literature that examines the relation between management forecast ability and managers’ career development. Previous studies mainly used accuracy as a signal of managers’ forecast ability. Our study shows that consistency is more important than accuracy in determining managerial turnover and subsequent progress in the labor market. Our results suggest that consistent managers are information suppliers and decision makers with greater information processing ability.

16501514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501514.value: The nature and extent of the demand for high quality accounting practices is of great interest. A vast literature has focused on whether capital providers (e.g., bondholders and shareholders) and information intermediaries consider accounting quality important in various decision making contexts. Although customers and suppliers are often cited as important external users of financial information (e.g., Spiceland, Sepe and Nelson [2012]), researchers have just started exploring the relationship between properties of accounting numbers and contracting with suppliers and customers (Raman and Shahrur [2008], Hui, Klasa and Yeung [2012], Costello [2013]). Given the pivotal role of supplier and customer contracts in determining a firm’s survival and growth, its relationship with accounting perhaps deserves better understanding. In particular, important unanswered questions center on the circumstances under which customers and suppliers are more or less concerned about a firm’s accounting quality in the contracting process. In this study, we propose to examine the relationship between supplier and customer contracting and accounting quality. Specifically, we ask the following main research questions: whether and when accounting quality plays an important role in the process of contracting with suppliers. There are strong reasons to believe that accounting quality is important in such contracting processes. Specifically, contracting parties are particularly concerned with i) contract pricing risk; and ii) contract performance risk. Contract pricing risk reflects the potential that the firm extracts rents with biased historical accounting data. For instance, suppliers may overestimate the costs of products to obtain higher contract prices. Contract performance risk refers to the risk that the chosen supplier is unable to meet the performance targets (i.e., technical requirements and timely delivery, etc.) due primarily to managerial incompetence and weak monitoring environment. We argue that high accounting quality directly minimizes contract pricing risk and indirectly lessens contract performance risk. We thus predict that there is a significant demand for high accounting quality in the contracting process. We plan to acquire contract-level datasets on supplier contracts. We propose to test several hypotheses regarding the role of accounting quality in supplier choice. For example, we plan to examine whether the accounting quality of the chosen suppliers is significantly better when there is greater competition in the contracting process. In addition, we will test whether fixed-price contracts better protect customers from exploitation by suppliers with low accounting quality. Overall, we believe that our evidence contributes to the literature by emphasizing the benefits of accounting quality in product market contracting. 大量文獻研究公司對高品質會計需求的性質和程度。儘管客戶和供應商往往被視為財務信息的重要外部用戶, 研究文獻集中於資金提供者（如債權人和股東）和信息中介是否考慮會計信息質量在決策環境中的重要性, 最近研究人員剛剛開始探索供應商和客戶與會計品質之間的關係。 由於供應商和客戶合同在企業的生存和發展的中的關鍵作用，它们與會計的關係也許值得更深入的了解。特別是，因為合同的重要和風險，客戶和供應商或多或少地關注在承包過程中企業的會計信息質量。在這項研究中，我們提出了審查的供應商和客戶的合同和會計信息質量之間的關係。具體而言，我們提出以下主要研究的問題：是否以及何時會計信息質量在供應商簽訂合同的過程中具有重要的作用。 有充分理由相信，會計質量是承包等過程中起重要的作用。具體而言，各締約方特別關注具有i）合約定價的風險; 及ii）合同履行的風險。合同定價風險反映了潛在的公司的歷史財務數據偏誤。例如，供應商可能高估了產品的成本，以獲得更高的合同價格。合同履行的風險是指主要由於管理的無能和監視失敗的風險, 所選擇的供應商無法滿足合同目標（即，技術要求，交貨及時等）。我們認為，較高的會計信息質量，直接減少了合同定價風險，並間接減輕合同履行的風險。因此，我們預測，客戶和供應商在承包過程中對高品質會計有顯著需求。 我們計劃收集合同級別的供應商合同數據。我們建議測試會計信息質量對供應商選擇作用的幾種假說。例如，我們計劃研究在更激烈的承包競爭過程中, 會計質量是否有對供應商選擇更重要。此外，我們將測試會計信息質量是否在固定價格合約中更好地保障客戶免受供應商剝削。總體而言，我們的證據加深研究文獻對會計信息質量在產品市場的優勢的了解。

16501514.label: Realisation of objectives
16501514.value: The research objectives of the project have been fully achieved. In particular, we use both input- and output-based proxies for low-quality internal accounting information. The input-based proxy is internal control weaknesses, because ineffective internal controls typically result in erroneous and stale internal accounting information (Feng, Li, and McVay 2009; Feng et al. 2015). In particular, ineffective internal control procedures significantly reduce the quality of data input (e.g., duplicated time cards, unauthorized purchases, errors in inventory, etc.), which ultimately reduces the quality of the information output for internal decision making purposes (e.g., erroneous labor costs and material costs). Our output-based proxy is management earnings forecast errors, because inaccurate internal information should also result in larger management forecast errors (Feng et al. 2009; Goodman, Neamtiu, Shroff, and White 2014). Consistent with our main prediction, we find negative associations between a firm’s disclosed internal control weaknesses and the number (and dollar amount) of government contracts awarded to the firm. These negative associations cannot be explained by either firm characteristics correlated with internal control weaknesses or other potential determinants of contract awards (e.g., political connection, financial fraud, or prior awards). Additionally, these results are robust to firm fixed-effects specifications of our regression model (i.e., within-firm variations in the number of contracts and the contract amount are negatively associated with within-firm variations of internal control weaknesses). Next, we test whether buyer scrutiny and information risk premium are contributing factors for the observed negative associations. We find that firms with internal control weaknesses win fewer contracts for which the government requires submission of cost or pricing data in the bidding process. In addition, firms with internal control weaknesses win fewer contracts when the government receives relatively more bids. These results support the buyer scrutiny hypothesis, because these contracts give the government more information to examine the reasonableness of the bids. Also consistent with the information risk premium hypothesis, we find that firms with internal control weaknesses win fewer high-risk contracts, including long-term contracts (that last longer than one year), specialized product contracts (that produce products or services without commercial markets), and fixed-price contracts (that force a firm to bear full risk of cost overrun). In sum, both buyer scrutiny and information risk premium are plausible examinations for why firms with internal control weakness win fewer government contracts. All of our inferences are similar when we use management earnings forecast errors as the alternative proxy for low-quality accounting information. Finally, we provide corroborating evidence that management’s risk attitude indeed plays an important role. As the management becomes more risk-averse, the information risk premium embedded in its bids should be higher, which at the margin reduces the winning probability. We show that the negative associations between government contract awards (high-risk contracts in particular) and internal control weaknesses are more pronounced when managers are more risk-averse, proxied by a low option vega in top management’s equity holdings. Our study contributes to the literature on accounting quality by examining its impact on operating activities. Existing studies focus primarily on the effects of accounting quality on financing and investment activities through lower cost of capital or better external monitoring. Regarding operating activities, Feng et al. (2015) find evidence consistent with internal control weaknesses affecting firms’ inventory management. We provide empirical evidence that accounting information quality is associated with firms’ product market competitiveness in the setting of government contract awards. This study is also related to the literature specifically on government contracts. Prior studies focus on cost padding in government incentive contracts and find mixed results on whether contractors shift costs from commercial segments to government segment (Lichtenberg 1992, Rogerson 1992, Thomas and Tung 1992, Demski and Magee 1992, McGowan and Vendrzyk 2002). The results of our study suggest that the contracting process is an integral element that filters out firms with poor accounting quality.

16501514.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501514.value: In this study, we examine U.S. government contracts awarded to public firms during the period 2003-2012 and test whether the quality of a firm's internal accounting information affects its competitiveness in winning government contracts. Our main proxy for low-quality internal accounting information is the internal control weaknesses disclosed by the management, and our secondary proxy is management earnings forecast errors. Empirically, we find that firms that have disclosed internal control weaknesses or experience larger management forecast errors win fewer government contracts in the following year. Evidence also supports the buyer scrutiny hypothesis and the information risk premium hypothesis as the underlying explanations.

16501514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501514.value: We acknowledge two major limitations of our study. First, firms that compete but fail to win the contract are not disclosed by the government. Although we use all firms that have reported government sales in previous years to approximate the group of firms that participate in the bidding process, this approximation is inherently noisy. One possible future extension is to obtain proprietary data to identify the competitors for a contract (as well as their bids), and conduct a deeper analysis of the impact of accounting quality. Second, although we follow the literature and use internal control weaknesses and management forecast errors as the proxies for the quality of internal accounting information, the underlying construct is unobservable in our context. Future research in this area could utilize more powerful proxies for the quality of internal accounting reports through proprietary sources.

16501514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501514.value: This study examines the potential effects of accounting information quality on firms’ competitiveness in winning government contracts. We construct a dataset of federal government contracts awarded competitively to public firms and test whether firms with low-quality accounting information win fewer contracts. We find that the number and amount of contracts awarded are negatively associated with firms’ internal control weaknesses or management earnings forecast errors, our proxies for low-quality accounting information. Consistent with the buyer scrutiny hypothesis, firms with low-quality accounting information win fewer contracts when the government has more information to evaluate the reasonableness of the bids (i.e., cost or pricing data are requested or when more bids are submitted). Also consistent with the information risk premium hypothesis, firms with low-quality accounting information win fewer high-risk contracts (i.e., long-term contracts, specialized product contracts, and fixed-price contracts).

We will propose how factors such as the partners’ absorptive capacity can moderate the learning process, enhancing the benefits of contextual distance while mitigating its drawbacks. We aim to demonstrate which key factors contribute most to knowledge creation and performance in international alliances.

16501814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501814.value: In an era of globalization, firms build strategic alliances, defined as inter-organizational governance structures that exist between the market and the hierarchy, with overseas partners to achieve certain strategic objectives such as knowledge creation (Fang & Zou, 2010; Kogut & Zander, 1992; Shenkar & Li, 1999). However, the presence of two or more partners makes an alliance’s operation complex, particularly when the partner firms come from countries with different cultures, institutions, and levels of economic development or operate in different industries (Ghemawat, 2001; Nachum & Zaheer, 2005). The findings of prior research suggest that contextual distance—differences between the cultural, institutional, economic and industrial environments in which an alliance’s partners (parent firms) are embedded—decreases the level of inter-partner understanding and communication (Phan & Peridis, 2000; Reus & Lamont, 2009) and their willingness to exchange knowledge (Gupta & Govindarajan, 2000). Thus effective knowledge acquisition, transfer and integration between the partners can be inhibited in an international strategic alliance (ISA) (Nachum & Zaheer, 2005). On the other hand, contextual distance can also promote knowledge creation if conflicts resulting from contextual distance challenge taken-for-granted assumptions and initiate innovation (Phan & Peridis, 2000). Some academic studies have found that distance correlates negatively with knowledge exchange (Gupta & Govindarajan, 2000) and learning (Lane et al., 2001) in ISAs, but others have failed to find any significant relationship between cultural distance and knowledge acquisition (Lyles & Salk, 1996). To reconcile these inconsistencies, this research project proposes to test a double-edged sword view of contextual distance in an attempt to clarify to what extent contextual distance influences knowledge creation and performance in an ISA. Building on the organizational learning perspective, learning between ISA partners will be treated as involving several stages: knowledge identification, exchange, integration/creation, and application (Huber, 1991). We will first propose a conceptual model of how distance arising from national cultures, institutions, economic development and industry backgrounds might impact knowledge exchange and creation and alliance performance. We will then examine how factors such as the partners’ absorptive capacity can moderate the learning process, enhancing the benefits of contextual distance while mitigating its drawbacks. We will design and implement an empirical study in the context of international strategic alliances in China to test the theoretical relationships proposed. The results of this research program will provide greater understanding of the key factors that contribute to knowledge creation and performance in international strategic alliances. 情境距离与知识创造: 国际战略联盟绩效 摘要 本研究提供了关于国际联盟伙伴间的情境距离如何影响他们之间的学习过程以及经营绩效。 我们认为联盟合作方之间的情境差异带来了知识的多元化，但增加了他们之间知识交流的难度，这对于联盟的知识创造和经营绩效产生影响。 文章探讨了研究结果的启示以及对未来研究展望。 关键词：国际联盟，情境距离，学习，中国

16501814.label: Realisation of objectives
16501814.value: We have now completed the project and achieved the project objectives as listed above. 1. In the first phase of the two-phase research project, we focused on building the theoretical framework, developing the constructs, and preparing for a large scale empirical data analysis. We have conducted a comprehensive literature review in building a conceptual model. In particular, we have published a theoretical paper outlining a framework for explaining how contextual distance arising from national cultures, institutions, economic development and industry backgrounds may impact performance outcomes such as post-cross border acquisition or alliance performance. The paper is published in Management and Organization Review (Li, J.T., and G. Wan, 2016. “China’s Cross-border Mergers and Acquisitions: A Contextual Distance Perspective,” Management and Organization Review, 12 (3), 449-456.) 2. In the second phase of the project, we have conducted an empirical study in China to test the theoretical relationships proposed in this study. We are very pleased to report the publications of a top tier, UTD-24 journal article from this project in the Journal of International Business Studies (Xie, Z. and J.T. Li, 2018. “Exporting and Innovating among Emerging Market Firms: The Moderating Role of Institutional Development,” Journal of International Business Studies, 49(2), 222-245.). 3. In addition, we have also published two other internationally refereed journal articles from this project. So there are a total of four journal publications from this project, including one top tier journal article.

16501814.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501814.value: The empirical study in China was designed to test the theoretical relationships proposed in this project on learning, knowledge creation, and innovation. Building on the recombinatory view of innovation and an institutional perspective, this study investigated how the level of institutional development in a firm’s home region and the institutional distance between the home and export markets might influence the effectiveness of learning through exporting. For exporters in emerging economies, more support for R&D and better-developed market intermediaries at home were found to enhance the positive effect of exporting on firms’ innovation, while market openness in the home region tends to dampen it. Exporters exporting more to other emerging economies tend to be more innovative than those exporting more to advanced markets. These findings arise from an empirical study of exporting and innovation among Chinese manufacturers.

16501814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501814.value: There are several areas for future research. For example, investment in R&D alone may not help a firm learn from countries with which there is a large gap in institutional development. Investment in what might be termed ‘‘institutional absorptive capacity’’ may be more important, but what that involves remains unclear. It should be noted that this study’s focus on China should not be taken as circumscribing the applicability of the theoretical framework. The arguments about interaction between national-level and firm-level internationalization should apply to economies in all stages of development.

16501814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501814.value: The findings of this research call managers’ attention to the information advantage emerging market (EM) firms gain by exporting when the market in their home region is not well integrated into the world market. They have a better chance to build up innovation capability before the market at home region is fully opened. Operating in regions with more R&D investment and better-developed market intermediaries helps EM exporters become more innovative by learning through exporting. Further, managers in EMs may be encouraged to pay more attention to destination countries which have a similar level of institutional development. Although the exposure to frontier technology may be limited in such markets, exporting to other EMs is nevertheless an effective way of improving a firm’s innovation performance. Other EMs similar to an EM exporter’s home can serve as an effective and inexpensive source of valuable knowledge, especially applied, experiential knowledge (Pietrobelli & Rabellotti, 2011). Access to this type of knowledge is very important to EM firms seeking to innovate (Amsden, 1989; Corredoira & McDermott, 2014).

16501914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501914.value: The same advisory firms (i.e., fund families) usually manage retail and institutional funds jointly. Institutional funds specialize in managing portfolios for institutional investors such as pensions, endowments, foundations, and insurance firms, whereas retail mutual funds manage assets for individual investors. In the U.S., the assets collectively managed by mutual funds and institutional funds are the largest and the second largest; the assets amount to tens of trillion of dollars, and dwarf the assets of hedge funds by a wide margin, the third largest type of funds by assets. With the availability of a new source of institutional fund data, we examine the performance and incentive issues of retail and institutional funds jointly managed by the same advisory firm. By accounting for both types of funds, we are able to better understand the factors affecting the (dis)economy of scale in fund investment. In addition, we explore how fund families exhibit different incentives in managing both types of funds, given the different fee structures, operating costs, and investor bases; and whether they divert resources and efforts from one type of product to the other. Our analysis will shed new light on the fund industry, and have important welfare implications to fund investors. 同一个投资顾问公司（即基金家族）通常共同管理的零售和机构基金。机构资金专注于管理机构投资者，如养老金，捐赠基金，基金会和保险公司，的资产，而零售共同基金管理的个人投资者的资产。在美国，共同基金管理最多资产，机构资金管理第二多资产。其管理资产达几十万亿美元，比第三多的对冲基金管理的资产要多得多。 用新出来的机构基金数据，我们考察了由同一个投资顾问公司管理的共同基金和机构基金的业绩和激励的问题。通过考虑两种类型的基金，我们能够更好地理解影响基金投资规模经济的因素。此外，我们探讨由于不同的收费结构，运营成本和投资者基础,基金家族如何在管理这两种类型的基金表现出不同的激励机制;以及基金家族是否从一种产品把资源和努力转移到其他产品。我们的分析将帮助更深入的认识基金业，并且对基金投资者具有重要的福利含义。

16502014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502014.value: With the fast development of information technology, large portfolios become more and more relevant. Empirical findings as well as recent theoretical studies reveal that large portfolios behave differently in nature from small portfolios in many important ways. In this proposed project, we focus on the studies of large portfolio risk management and optimization, which are of both great theoretical interest and practical importance. Our results will allow people to (1) make more reliable assessment of portfolio risk, in terms of widely used risk measures including value-at-risk and expected shortfall; and (2) optimize their portfolios to achieve either high return subject to certain risk constraint or low risk subject to certain return constraint. 随着信息科技的快速发展，多维资产投资组合变得越来越相关。理论和经验分析都表明多维资产投资组合和小维数的投资组合在很多方面有本质的不同。在这个项目里，我们关注多维资产投资组合的风险管理和最优化。这两个方面在理论和实践上都很重要。我们的成果会让人们可以（1）得到更可靠的投资组合的风险评估；（2）最优化他们的投资组合来达到某风险范围的最大收益或保证某收益下的最小风险。

16502014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502014.value: For the first time, the high-dimensional Markowitz portfolio optimization problem is solved in the sense that both of its objectives -- maximize the expected return and keep the risk at a pre-set level, are simultaneously achieved. Rigorous proofs as well as comprehensive data analysis were conducted, which all show the superior performance of our proposed methodology. Motivated by the search for minimum variance portfolios, we study high-dimensional covolatility matrices and their inverses and establish consistency properties. The methodology, algorithms and comprehensive empirical studies are documented in papers [1] and [2].

16502014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502014.value: In the finished research, we established fundamental results for relatively ideal situations, such as when returns/idiosyncratic components are independent and identically distributed. These results are important because they build foundations for all variations of portfolio management problems. However, the research results still haven't cover all typical realistic situations. We plan to further investigate more realistic conditions such as existence of heteroscedasticity, market microstructure noise etc.

16502014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502014.value: For the first time, the high-dimensional Markowitz portfolio optimization problem is solved in the sense that both of its objectives -- maximizing the expected return while keeping the risk at a pre-set level, are simultaneously achieved. Motivated by the applications of minimum variance portfolios, we study high-dimensional covolatility matrices and their inverses and establish important consistency properties. We make significant contributions in statistical theory as well as financial applications.

16502114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502114.value: 政治对经济的影响一直是经济金融领域的一个重要课题。 然而，过去的研究多数是集中在宏观层面，使用发达国家数据。我们计划用中国个体公司的数据来阐述这个问题。中国为研究这一问题提供了理想的样本。因为其一，在中国，政治对公司的影响是非常重要的。在象美国之类的发达国家，政策对个体公司的影响是通过公司对于类似利率或者税收的宏观政策做出回应而产生的。而在中国，国有公司的管理者日后可以成为政府官员，而政府官员也可以就任国有公司的高层。这种事业上的交叠，使得国有公司会直接贯彻执行政府命令，使得政治对公司的影响更直接。其二，政治经济学领域研究发现发达国家和发展中国家关于经济发展如何影响官员升迁的作用是不一样的。研究发现在发达国家经济增长对官员连任没有显著效应，但是在发展中国家这一效果是显著的。 同时，研究中国的文献也记录了在中国当地GDP对官员连任的重要性。 因此，政府官员的升迁动机对投资的影响应该在中国更显著。其三，中国在过去的几十年来经历份了高速的发展。理解这种高速发展背后的推动力，本身就是很重要的问题。在这篇论文中，我们计划分析不同省市高官由于不同的升迁投机，如何影响当地公司的投资行为.

16502114.label: Realisation of objectives
16502114.value: This project has generated the following paper that is currently under review at American Economics Review. The paper has been presented at three international conferences: the 2016 China Finance Annual Conference in Dalian, China, the 2016 SFM Conference in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and the 2017 China Financial Research Conference (CFRC) at PBC School of Tsinghua University in Beijing, China. The major findings are as follows: 1. Liu, Laura Xiaolei, Haibing Shu, Shujing Wang, and K.C. John Wei, 2017, “The political cycle of corporate investments: New evidence from Chinese manufacturing firms,” under review at American Economics Review. Summary: Using a comprehensive dataset of industrial firms and government official turnovers at the prefecture level in China, we show that firms significantly increase their investments right before expected turnovers of prefecture governors. More importantly, we find that the increase in investment mainly comes from privately owned firms, especially for politically connected firms and firms affiliated with governments below the prefecture level. The effect is stronger among officials with stronger career incentive and in provinces with weaker institutions. Our results suggest that the career incentive of local government officials and political connections play an important role in generating the political cycle of corporate investment in China. I also complete a paper that is partially related to this project. In this paper, we also examine corporate investment, but focus on whether the initial enforcement of insider trading laws improves capital allocation efficiency. We do find the effect, but it is concentrated in developed markets and manifests shortly after the enforcement year. The paper has already published at Journal of Corporate Finance. The results are summarized as follows: 2. Chen, Zhihong, Yuan Huang, Yuanto Kusdani, and K.C. John Wei, 2017, “The real effect of the initial enforcement of insider trading laws,” Journal of Corporate Finance 45, 687-709 Summary: Based on a difference-in-differences approach, we find strong evidence that the initial enforcement of insider trading laws improves capital allocation efficiency. The effect is concentrated in developed markets and manifests shortly after the enforcement year. Further analysis shows that the improvement is positively associated with the increase in liquidity around the enforcement year and the opaqueness of the information environment before the enforcement year. The improvement is more pronounced for firms operating in more competitive markets, being more financially constrained, and with more severe agency problems. Finally, we find increased accounting performance after the enforcement and the increase is positively associated with the improvement in capital allocation efficiency. Overall, our evidence suggests that the initial enforcement of insider trading laws improves capital allocation efficiency by providing more information to guide managerial decisions and by reducing market frictions arising from information asymmetry and agency problems. I also complete another paper that is also partially related to this project but with a different focus. In this paper, we examine the effect of economic policy uncertainty on the cost of raising equity capital. We use the seasoned equity offerings (SEOs) in the US as our setting and find that economic policy uncertainty raises the discounts of SEOs and SEO activities. The paper has been presented at two international conferences: the 2017 World Finance Conference in Cagliari, Italy, and the 2017 Conference on the Theories and Practices of Securities and Financial Markets (SFM) in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. The paper is currently under revise and we plan to submit the paper to Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis soon. The results are summarized as follows: 3. Chan, Yue-Cheong, Walid Saffar, and K.C. John Wei, “How economic policy uncertainty affects the cost of raising equity capital: Evidence from seasoned equity offerings.” Summary: Economic policy uncertainty (EPU) increases the cost of raising equity capital, especially when the economy is weaker. A one standard deviation increase in the EPU index developed by Baker, Bloom, and Davis (2016) is associated with a 43 basis point increase in SEO discounts during the recent 2000-2014 period. The cross-sectional analysis shows that the EPU effect on SEO discounts is stronger for firms with greater dependence on government spending, less informative stock prices, or a smaller EPU beta. Moreover, EPU also affects the volume and timing of SEO activity. Our results suggest that underwriters and issuers tend to delay the offering process to mitigate the negative effect of EPU on investor interest in offered shares. The outcomes of the project have demonstrated that the projective objectives have been achieved.

16502114.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502114.value: The major objective of this project is to examine whether expected turnovers of government officials in China affect corporate investment in their jurisdictions. We use a comprehensive dataset of industrial firms and government official turnovers at the prefecture level in China to test our hypotheses. We find that firms significantly increase their investments right before expected turnovers of prefecture governors. Cross-sectional analysis shows that the increase in investment mainly comes from privately owned firms, especially for politically connected firms and firms affiliated with governments below the prefecture level. We also find the heterogeneity of officials’ characteristics affects the turnover effect. The effect is stronger among officials with stronger career incentive and in provinces with weaker institutions. Our results suggest that the career incentive of local government officials and political connections play an important role in generating the political cycle of corporate investment in China.

16502114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502114.value: The impacts of political uncertainty on real economy and capital markets have attracted a lot of attention, as evidenced by the surprising outcomes that Briton votes to leave EU (Brexit) and the U.S. citizens vote Donald Trump as the US president in 2016. Since my first paper co-authored with YC Chan that examines and finds that that political news related to the Sino-British confrontation on the future status of Hong Kong increases stock volatility, especially for stocks of local firms. In a GRF supported project (GRF 644213), we use the event of the Bo Xilai political scandal in 2012 in China as an exogenous shock to identify the impact of political uncertainty on asset prices and find that that the Bo scandal caused a significant drop in stock prices, especially for firms that are more politically sensitive. The results are summarized in a paper, which has appeared at the top-three finance journal, Journal of Financial Economics. The effects of expected turnovers of government officials in China on real economy and financial markets are quite an interesting topic. The potential research project is to investigate whether there is any effect on firms’ financing activities around expected turnovers of government officials.

16502114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502114.value: In this project, we use a comprehensive dataset of industrial firms and government official turnovers at the prefecture level in China to investigate how expected turnovers of government officials in China affect corporate investment in their jurisdictions. We find that firms significantly increase their investments right before expected turnovers of prefecture governors. The political cycle effect on corporate investment mainly comes from privately owned firms, especially for politically connected firms and firms affiliated with governments below the prefecture level. We also find the effect is stronger among officials with stronger career incentive and in provinces with weaker institutions. The finding suggests that the career incentive of local government officials and political connections play an important role in generating the political cycle of corporate investment in China.

16502414.label: Project Objectives

16502414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502414.value: With the advent of the Internet and growing popularity of online commerce, manufacturers contemplate adding online branches to sell their products directly to customers, thus bypassing the retailers. This practice is called "encroachment.'' These online channels are often used in conjunction with the more traditional, brick-and-mortar retail stores causing much friction between manufacturers and retailers. For example, in 1999, Levi Strauss & Co. halted web sales due to strong objections from its retailers (Collett 1999). In response, manufacturers try to differentiate their online offers from those available through retailers in order to alleviate the downstream firms' concerns. In this project, we intend to study how encroachment affects the quality of the products offered via different channels. In reality, we observe that the direct outlets of clothing brands often carry products of lower quality compared to those sold at department stores. Apparel brands such as Gap and Coach design lower-quality products specifically for their outlets (Shell 2009). Encroachment might increase the manufacturer's overall market size since it enables the manufacture to offer a broader range of products. However, a head-to-head competition with the retailers may negatively affect the benefits. Matters are further complicated if the firm could offer products of different qualities through different channels. We consider a vertical supply chain with one supplier and one retailer and assume that customers have heterogeneous preferences with respect to quality. We intend to investigate 1) whether it is plausible to offer a range of products with different qualities in the supply chain? 2) conditions under which the manufacturer prefers to offer a more exclusive product through the direct channel or vice versa. 3) conditions under which the manufacturer might forgo the benefits of product differentiation and offer the same quality product through both direct and indirect channels? 4) the effects of offering products with different qualities on the manufacturer and retailer's quantity decisions and profits in comparison to offering a uniform quality in the supply chain.

16502414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502414.value: We study a supply chain with manufacturer encroachment in which product quality is endogenous and customers have heterogeneous preferences for quality. It is known that, when quality is exogenous, encroachment could make the retailer better off. Yet, when quality is endogenous and the manufacturer has enough flexibility in adjusting quality, we find that encroachment always makes the retailer worse off in a large variety of scenarios. We also establish that, while a higher manufacturer’s cost of quality hurts the retailer in absence of encroachment, it could benefit the retailer with encroachment. In addition, we show that a manufacturer offering differentiated products through two channels prefers to sell its high-quality product through the direct channel. Contrary to conventional wisdom, quality differentiation does not always benefit either manufacturer or retailer. Our results may explain why, despite extant theoretical predictions, retailers almost always resent encroachment. These findings also suggest that firms must be cautious when adopting quality differentiation as a strategy to ease channel conflict caused by encroachment. The outcome of this research was a publication in Manufacturing and Service Operations Management (MSOM) which is a leading publication in the Operations Management field.

16502414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502414.value: We achieved the goals of the project. This was a standalone project and as of now the PI does not have an intention to extend the project.

16502414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502414.value: A recent survey shows that nearly half of the 347 manufacturers surveyed sell products from their own website, and 59% of them believe that most brands will sell directly to their customers in the future. Direct selling (also known as encroachment) can increase manufacturers' prots by generating more sales and giving manufacturers a larger share of the margin. If ill managed, however, direct selling can cause substantial damage to supply chain relationships. For example, when Bass Brewers Ltd., the British beer company, launched a home delivery program, its top distributer retaliated by pulling all Bass products off its shelves, forcing Bass Brewers to abandon the direct sales program. Fear of retaliation has become a major barrier for many manufacturers looking to sell directly to their customers. Our study takes on the challenge of finding out whether retailers are justified in their negative reactions to encroachment. We examine how encroachment affects the manufacturer's and the retailer's prots, taking into consideration selling cost asymmetry and quality decisions. We find that under most circumstances, the addition of a direct channel will result in a "win-lose" outcome where the retailer gets the short end of the stick. Moreover, quality differentiation to sell a different product through the direct channel does not solve the problem.

16502514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502514.value: Despite the theoretical basis for the pricing effects of skewness preference, empirically testing the relation between idiosyncratic skewness and returns is not a straightforward exercise. The primary obstacle is that ex ante skewness is difficult to measure. In contrast to variances and covariances, idiosyncratic skewness is not stable over time (Harvey and Siddique (1999), so variables other than lagged skewness are required to measure expected skewness. Boyer, Mitton, and Vorkink (2010) estimated expected idiosyncratic skewness based on historical volatility and other firm variables, and shows that expected skewness is negatively related to cross sectional future stock returns, and helps explain the phenomenon that stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility have low expected returns. Conrad, DIttmar, and Ghysels (2013) have provided the strongest empirical evidence so far. They use options price to estimate ex ante risk neutral moments, and find a negative relation between ex ante skewness and subsequent returns in cross section. A substantial body of literature has address the question of how to extract from observed option prices an estimate of the risk-neutral density of the underlying asset returns (see Jackwerth (1999) for a survey). Other authors, such as Bakshi, Kapadia, and Madan (2003) (BKM) have constructed methods for estimating the higher moments of the risk-neutral returns. In their paper, BKM derive a relation between the moments of the risk-neutral density and the price of securities with quadratic and cubic payoff functions, which can be replicated using a portfolio of out-of-the-money calls and puts with a continuum of strike prices. Thus, the risk neutral moments can be estimated directly from the options prices. Dennis and Mayhew (2009) show that there can be error in the risk neutral moments estimations from two sources - the fact that the interval between adjacent strike prices is not infinitely small and the fact that we do not observe all strike prices from 0 to infinite. They show that the economic effect of error is large. For a strike price interval in the range of $5 the error in skewness can be plus or minus 0.4. We have several objectives in this proposed research. First we will determine what causes the errors in estimating risk neutral skewness with options data. Second we will construct a method that dramatically improves the estimate of risk neutral skewness. Finally we will investigate the relation between correctly estimated risk neutral skewness and subsequent stock returns. 在实际研究中,要探明对称性和股票回报并不容易, 因为未来对称性很难计量,且不稳定. Conrad, DIttmar, and Ghysels (2013) 利用期权价格计算无对称性, 对称性和股票回报是负相关的. Bakshi, Kapadia, and Madan (2003) (BKM) 设计出用期权价格计算无风险对称性的方法. 但Dennis and Mayhew (2009)指出因为没有足够期权, 用期权价格计算无风险对称性有较大的误差. 在所提议的研究计划中,我们有三个目的: 一是期权价格计算无风险对称性的误差原因.二是设计一种让误差减少的方法.三是用没有误差无风险对称性来它和未来股票回报的关系.

16502614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502614.value: The importance of managerial objectives and behavior toward financing and investment decisions has been intensively studied in prior literature. Theoretical and empirical work has suggested that some managers enjoy the quite life or build empires, while others respond to incentives and maximize shareholder value. The effect of managerial behavior on firm policies has been studied in the context of investment policy, payout policy, debt policy, and more recently, cash management. In reality these decisions are interdependent making it difficult to empirically identify how managerial behavior affects the firms’ full set of policies. To address this identification challenge a few studies have analyzed how managers respond to exogenous shocks. In a seminal study, Blanchard, López-de-Silanes, and Shleifer (1994) study what firms do with cash windfalls from legal settlements. This approach is helpful in identifying how managerial behavior affects investments, payout policies, and debt. If managers behave according to the perfect capital markets model, windfalls should be redistributed to investors. If managerial behavior on the other hand is shaped by agency problems, managers will try to ensure their position by keeping the resources inside the firm. Blanchard et al. (1994) identify 11 firms that won or settled lawsuits that did not affect their investment opportunities. They find that firms’ responses are consistent with an agency model of managerial behavior, in which managers keep the resources inside the firm. While these results shed new light on the importance of managerial behavior in relation to investment and financing decisions, the main limitation of the study is the small sample size which makes it impossible to provide inference about the determinants of managerial behavior while controlling for individual firm characteristics. In this project we propose to revisit the identification strategy of Blanchard et al. (1994). Almost two decades have passed since this seminal study. In the meantime the research infrastructure related to news searches and litigation cases has improved considerably. We therefore expect to be able to collect a significantly larger sample of 150-200 firms that won or settled lawsuits that did not change their investment opportunities. A larger sample size is important to be able to identify the determinants of managerial behavior while controlling for individual firm heterogeneity. The larger sample size will allow us to further the approach by Blanchard et al. (1994) and identify the effect of managerial behavior on financing and investment decisions – one of the most pertinent issues in corporate finance. 管理目标和对融资行为和投资决策中的重要性已被广泛研究现有的文献。理论和实证研究已经表明，一些管理人员享有相当的生活或建立帝国，而另一些应对的激励和股东价值最大化。对企业政策管理行为的影响进行了研究，投资政策，派息政策，国债政策的背景下，最近，现金管理。实际上这些决定是相互依赖使得难以凭经验确定管理行为如何影响企业的全套政策。 为了应对这一挑战，确定了几个研究分析了如何管理 应对外来冲击。在一个开创性的研究，查德，洛佩斯•德硅烷和 施莱弗（1994）研究了企业办与法律和解的现金横财。这 方法是在确定的行为如何管理影响投资，支出政策和债务有帮助的。如果管理者根据完善的资本市场模式的行为，意外之财应该被重新分配给投资者。如果在另一方面的管理行为由代理问题形，管理者会尽量保证自己的立场，保持资源的企业内部。布兰查德等人 （1994年）确定11家公司赢得或诉讼解决这并不会影响他们的投资机会。他们发现，企业的反应是与管理行为的代理模式，其中管理人员保证资源的企业内部是一致的。虽然这些结果揭示了相对于投资和融资决策管理行为的重要性，新光源，该研究的主要限制是样本量太小，这使得它不可能提供推断有关管理行为的决定因素，而控制了单个企业的特点。 在这个项目中，我们建议重新审视布兰查德等人的识别策略 （1994年）。因为这一开创性研究近二十年过去了。在此期间，研究基础设施相关的新闻搜索和诉讼案件已大为改善。因此，我们希望能收集150-200企业赢得或解决诉讼并没有改变他们的投资机会显著更大的样本。要能够识别，同时控制了单个企业的异质性管理行为的决定因素较大的样本量是很重要的。在更大的样本量将使我们能够进一步验证布兰查德等人的做法 （1994年），并确定了管理行为的融资和投资决策的影响 - 在企业融资的最重要问题之一。

16502814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502814.value: Existing research suggests that in emerging markets where the role of government is dominant in economic activities, firms often lack the necessary supporting platforms to generate new innovative ideas and thus firm innovation is less likely to occur. Yet, empirical evidence does suggest that even for developing countries where the role of the government in economic activities is predominant, firms can still have innovations with new ideas. In the literature, however, how firms in emerging markets search and obtain new ideas for innovation is not clear. The purpose of this study is to explore the mechanism through which firms in emerging markets search for new ideas under the influence of government innovation policies. Using firms in the Chinese context, we argue that government innovation policies can have a positive impact on firm’s distant search but a negative impact on search intensity for new ideas and knowledge. We further explore how absorptive capacity, firm network ties and regional variations in martketilization in China modify such search processes. Our study not only contributes to the literature of organizational learning by exploring specific mechanisms through which the institutional factors affect learning processes, but also provides important implications to government policy makers and practitioners in terms of resource allocation in the process of a search for new ideas to expand innovation. Case studies, archival longitudinal data analysis, surveys and interviews will be used in the study. 現有文獻指出，在新興市場中，政府在經濟行為中的主導地位導致企業 缺乏產出創意的支持平台，所以企業創新行為較為少見。然而，新興市 場的實證卻表明，即使政府掌控經濟活動，公司依然能夠產生創意。 目前文獻對於新興市場中的公司如何尋求和獲取創意卻很少 涉及。這個項目的目的就是探討新興市場中政府政策影響下的公司如何 尋求創意。我們認為政府政策可以正面影響中國公司的遠距離尋求，但 是卻能負面影響尋求強度。我們進一步探討吸收能力，公司網絡以及地 區市場化差異如何調節這些影響。這個項目不僅通過討論制度具體影響 學習的途徑為組織力量提供貢獻，但是也為政府官員提供了一些新的思 路。這個項目將會使用個案研究，二手資料分析，調查和訪問等方法。

16502914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502914.value: As exemplified by the considerable attention paid to human capital as a critical resource within organizations, the research that focuses on employee contributions as a source for firm survival and success has increased substantially over the past couple of decades. This also coincides with the increased focus on the resource-based view of the firm and the establishment of strategic human resource management (HRM) as a distinct field of study. Empirical research in strategic HRM has made considerable progress in linking bundles of human resource (HR) practices, typically termed as high performance work systems (HPWS), with organizational performance. Despite the progresses that have been made, we do not yet have an accumulated understanding of many of the (disparate sets of) mediators that have been examined in the past and the way in which they play a role in the relationship between a bundle of HR practices and various indicators of organizational outcomes. We address such needs in two different ways by conducting a narrative review of the literature through a multilevel theoretical lens to explicate these mediating processes as well as potential boundary conditions of such processes, and by conducting an empirical review (via meta-analysis techniques) that can summarize statistically what we know about these mediating processes. 正如人力资本作为组织内部关键资源而备受关注，在过去的几十年里，视员工贡献为公司生存和成功的来源的研究明显增多/大量涌现。这也印证了公司资源基础说的愈受关注和战略性人力资源管理这个独特的研究领域的建立。战略性人力资源管理的实证研究已经在对多种人力资源实践（即高绩效工作系统）与组织绩效的关系探索上取得显著进展。但尽管如此，我们对曾被研究过的不同的中介变量以及它们在人力资源实践和多方面的组织成果的关系中所起的作用还没有一个累积性的认识了解。我们通过两种途径弥补了这个空白：通过多层面的理论综述来阐明这些中介机制和潜在的调节情境；通过实证综述（即通过元分析方法）以统计分析的方式来总结这些中介机制。

16503014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503014.value: The microcredit "revolution" of the last few decades has been spurred by the belief that access to microcredit could alleviate poverty. Microcredit would allow poor individuals to set up small businesses, earn high returns and increase consumption and wealth. However, recent research suggests that certain features of traditional microcredit contracts dampen risk-taking and limit impacts on borrowers' incomes and welfare. Our research team has designed an alternative approach to microcredit where local intermediaries are incentivized to recommend borrowers to the microfinance institution (MFI). Unlike traditional microcredit, borrowers are only liable for their own loans, and repayments are due in a single lumpsum at the end of the agricultural cycle, allowing the funds to be invested in high-risk, high-return cash crops. Through a field experiment in 72 Indian villages, we are evaluating this alternative approach (that we call agent-intermediated lending or AIL) relative to the traditional group-based liability (GBL) approach. Our approach has two variants: in trader-agent intermediated lending (TRAIL), local traders, shopkeepers and moneylenders are appointed as agents to the MFI; in village council (gram-panchayat) agent intermediated lending (GRAIL), agents are selected by local government officials. We find not only that the TRAIL scheme generates high repayment rates at lower administrative costs than GBL, but also that it significantly increases borrowers' cultivation of cash crops, agricultural revenues and value-added. This project will collect new data and conduct new theoretical and empirical analysis to answer some open questions. We will conduct new exit surveys of the 3600 sample households and the 48 AIL agents in our study. Crucial information on the motivations and interactions of AIL agents, selection process in AIL villages, group-formation in GBL villages, and the political economy of the villages, political networks of borrowers recommended by GRAIL agents, and service provision will be collected. We will investigate channels by which TRAIL borrowers benefit from the scheme. We will build a dynamic model that allows structural methods to test for the relative importance of different channels. We will also examine how borrowers were selected and influenced by GRAIL agents, and impacts on GRAIL borrowers. We believe that the project will generate important knowledge about the mechanisms behind the relative success of the AIL scheme, which in turn can inform scale-up as well as further innovation in microcredit design. This avenue of research could eventually lead us to realize the "miracle" of microcredit.

16503014.label: Realisation of objectives
16503014.value: Over the project period, we have extensively worked with the data that we collected through the exit survey, in conjunction with data collected previously. These rich data have allowed us to analyse in-depth the treatment effects of the AIL interventions, and examine the mechanisms that brought about these effects. We have developed theoretical models to explain the mechanisms and then tested the predictions of these models in the data. We have presented the results of this research in seminars and conferences at many different universities around the world. We have written 3 research papers. One has been published in a peer-reviewed journal, a second is being prepared for submission very soon. A third already exists as an IEMS working paper and will be submitted for publication within the next semester.
