16503014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503014.value: This project has led to three research papers that broadly examine targeting and microcredit. The first, which is published in the Journal of Development Economics (2017) examines agent-intermediated lending (where a local trader is the agent, or TRAIL) with group-based lending (GBL). It finds that the TRAIL scheme outperforms GBL in raising borrower farm incomes. It argues that a significant part of this differential is because TRAIL agents are incentivised to select more able farmers as borrowers. On the other hand GBL groups cannot screen out unproductive borrowers. This difference in the pattern of selection explains at least 30–40% of the observed difference in income impacts. The second is a paper in preparation that compares the TRAIL scheme with a scheme where the local government appoints the agent (GRAIL). The paper finds that although both TRAIL and GRAIL agents were offered identical contracts, TRAIL outperforms GRAIL in terms of borrower outcomes. Although there is evidence that TRAIL agents selected more able borrowers than the GRAIL scheme, we find that the bulk of the difference in income impacts can be explained by differences in agent engagement. In turn our model explains this in terms of differential incentives: because TRAIL agents are traders they stand to earn profits from the increased farm output of borrowers and therefore time helping them lower cost of production. As political appointees GRAIL agents are more interested in preventing default to ensure the scheme succeeds and helping the lower-ability farmers (either to fulfill their party's pro-poor mission or to ensure future electoral success). If production techniques that lower risk also lower average yield, this can explain why GRAIL borrowers increase output but at a high cost, which prevents them from earning higher farm incomes. A third working paper examines the distributive impacts of the TRAIL, GRAIL and GBL schemes. It finds that the landless borrowers that the TRAIL agents selected had significantly lower baseline farm incomes than the landless who were selected in the GRAIL and GBL schemes. These low-income borrowers saw large relative increases in income through the scheme. In contrast GRAIL and GBL landless and landed borrowers either had no increase in income, or lost money. Thus contrary to expectation, the TRAIL scheme outperformed the other two schemes both in terms of efficiency and equity.

16503014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503014.value: Although we have worked hard to uncover the mechanisms that led to the differential results of the three schemes, our work does not allow us to experimentally verify all the channels that we have identified. There are also other open questions about how the TRAIL scheme could be scaled up: how do TRAIL agents respond to variations in their commission rate, how does the ability to help and monitor borrowers vary by the scale of the scheme, what is the role of competition v. collusion among traders in a village, and what general equilibrium effects might occur if many more farmers in a village can avail of the scheme? We will continue to explore avenues to do further research on these questions.

16503014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503014.value: Our research examines alternatives to the "traditional" group-based model of microcredit, where loans are given to self-formed groups of borrowers who are then jointly liable for each others' loans. Although this model can successfully leverage the information that borrowers have about each other (and that formal lenders do not have), research has shown that these loans cannot help them increase incomes or escape poverty. We show that it is possible to design individual liability loans that also leverage local information through the use of local agents, but do not dampen risk-taking in the way that group loans do. In fact we find that when the agents who select the borrowers have an aligned interest in increasing borrowers' farm incomes, then borrowers successfully produce more output and earn greater profit. These ideas could be applied to other settings where local information is key to successfully targeting program beneficiaries.

16503414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503414.value: 传统的Balassa-Samuelson模型将贸易部门与非贸易部门的相对大小作为外生给定而且假设不随时间变化，据此很多研究认为中美贸易不平衡是由于中国政府人为压低真实汇率的结果。本文主要探讨经济增长过程中内生的结构变迁，即经济体中农业、制造业、服务业构成的动态变化，如何通过影响贸易部门与非贸易部门的相对大小从而影响长期的真实汇率水平及其动态变化。我们为此建立了一个具有两个大国的多部门的动态一般均衡模型，讨论了在平衡贸易与非平衡贸易条件下，内生结构变迁对于总体价格水平与长期真实汇率的影响。我们以此模型对中美两国的经济增长、结构变迁、贸易和相对真实汇率做定量分析，发现人民币相对于美元相对缓慢的升值很大程度上是由以下市场力量造成的：中国在内生的结构变迁过程中贸易部门随着工业化显著扩张，而同时美国却内生性地“去工业化”导致非贸易部门相对扩张。

16503514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503514.value: If a stock is mispriced, profit opportunities attract arbitrageurs to correct the mispricing. However, arbitrage is risky, costly, and limited. The correction of mispricing will take longer when limits to arbitrage are more severe. The limits-to-arbitrage argument suggests that any asset pricing anomaly should be more pronounced for firms with more severe limits to arbitrage (Shleifer and Vishny, 1997). Since there is no consensus on which is the best measure for arbitrage risks, investigators usually consider each individual measure separately from four aspects: noise trader risk, valuation uncertainty, shareholder sophistication, and potential transaction costs (Lam and Wei, 2011). Although all these measures come from economic intuitions, some may also proxy for other risks or aspects. As a result, the conclusions drawn from those measures without statistical power might be misleading. In addition, it would be helpful if someone can construct a composite index that can measure the degree of limits to arbitrage more accurately. The objective of this proposed project is to comprehensively evaluate the power of those commonly used measures in testing the limits-to-arbitrage argument. We will follow the idea from Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan (2013) and others that short selling is riskier, costlier, and more difficult to implement than purchasing. This arbitrage asymmetry suggests that for any appropriate measure of limits to arbitrage, one should observe a significantly negative relation between this measure and future returns for overpriced stocks. In contrast, for underpriced stocks, the relation should be positive and in some cases can become negative. If a measure cannot generate this return predictability pattern, it suggests that the measure is not an appropriate measure for the degree of limits to arbitrage. Well-documented anomalies will be combined to determine the degree of mispricing (Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan; 2013) and we will consider each commonly used measure of limits to arbitrage separately to evaluate its power in testing the limits-to-arbitrage argument. From those measures that pass the arbitrage asymmetry criteria, we will then construct an index using principal component analysis or simple averaging. Both portfolio analysis and regression analysis will be used to determine the power of each proxy to measure the degree of limits to arbitrage. We will also consider each anomaly separately. Our empirical results will help us to understand the power of these measures in testing the limits-to-arbitrage argument. 如果一隻股票定價錯誤，獲利機會吸引套利者來糾正錯誤定價。 然而，套利是有風險的，昂貴的和有限的。當套利限制更為嚴重 時，錯誤定價的修正將需要更長的時間。這些限制對套利的說法 表明，對套利限制更為嚴重的公司, 其任何資產定價異常應該更 明顯（Shleifer和Vishny，1997）。 由於對套利風險最好的衡量沒有達成共識，研究者通常從四個 方面分別考慮：噪音交易者風險，估值的不確定性，股東的複雜 性和潛在的交易成本（Lam 和 Wei，2011年）。儘管所有這些衡 量都從經濟直覺，但有些也可能用來衡量對其他風險。因此， 從這些沒有得出統計結論的衡量都可能會產生誤導。此外，如果 有人可以構造可以更精確地衡量限制套利程度的綜合指數，這將 是有益的，。 本計畫的目的是全面評估這些常用測試限制對套利說的法的限 制套利衡量。我們將遵循Stambaugh, Yu, 和 Yuan (2013)和其他人 的想法，賣空是高風險的，更昂貴，比購買更難以實施的。這種 套利的不對稱表明，對於限制套利的任何適當的衡量，應遵發現 該衡量和過高股票未來收益率之間的關係是顯著負的。相反， 對於過低的股票，該關係應該是正的。如果一項衡量不能產生 這種收益的可預測模式，它表明，這項衡量不是一個用來衡量限 制套利的程度。 所有資產定價異常現象將被合併以確定錯誤定價（Stambaugh, Yu, 和 Yuan，2013）的程度。我們會考慮限制套利的每個常用 的指標分別評估其檢驗套利的說法的功效以套利。從那些通過 套利不對稱條件的衡量中，我們會採用主成分分析或簡單平均 再構造一個指數。投資組合分析和回歸分析將用於確定每個衡 量的功效來測量限制套利的程度。我們也將分別考慮每個資產 定價異常現象。我們的實證結果將有助於我們了解用這些限制 套利衡量檢來驗套利的說法的功效。

16503514.label: Realisation of objectives
16503514.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to comprehensively evaluate which proxies for the degree of limits to arbitrage are the better ones based on the criterion of arbitrage asymmetry proposed by Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan (2015), and (ii) to construct a composite index that combines all of the proxies that are able to generate the return pattern that is consistent with arbitrage asymmetry. We have extensively investigated the relative importance of three theoretical categories of arbitrage costs and of different methods in extracting information contained in all the arbitrage costs into a composite index in explaining the composite mispricing in cross-sectional returns using nine common arbitrage costs measures and ten stock anomalies. We find that arbitrage risk and transaction costs are in general more important than valuation uncertainty. The effect of arbitrage risk on anomaly returns is higher during periods of high investor sentiment or funding illiquidity, while the effect of transaction costs does not depend on these market states. For individual components, binding arbitrage costs shift over time. Transaction costs remain important in recent years, as arbitrage and short selling activities expand and become more sophisticated. More importantly, a measure that simply averages rankings of nine prominent arbitrage costs exhibits the most effective and stable measure of arbitrage costs. We also find that arbitrage costs predict future returns because they affect the long versus short legs of return anomalies differently. We find that overall arbitrage costs explain a significant portion of the average returns associated with stock anomalies in the United States. Arbitrage risk is the predominant arbitrage costs category for both small and large cap stocks. Information uncertainty is important, but only among small cap stocks. Transaction costs do not provide additional explanatory power. There are two significant and useful arbitrage costs principal components in the arbitrage costs space. The results are summarized in a paper, which has been presented in many international academic conferences and a practitioner conference as well as many universities. More significantly, the paper has been well received and it won the Best Research Award at the Conference on the Theories and Practices of Securities and Financial Markets. The paper is currently under review at Review of Financial Studies. A paper partially related to this project examines the profitability effect in an international setting. To distinguish between the behavioral explanation and the q-theory explanation, we use a country-level market development index and the developed-versus-emerging market dichotomy to proxy for arbitrage costs, which is the main focus of this proposal. The paper has been accepted for publication at European Financial Management. The paper is well cited with a Google Scholar citation of 14 as of August 22, 2018. The previous version of the paper was even cited by Fama and French in their 2017 Journal of Financial Economics paper (International tests of a five-factor asset pricing model). The outcomes of the project have demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

The paper was presented at many international conferences and won the Best Research Award at the 2016 SFM conference. 1. Lam, Eric F.Y.C., Chishen Wei, and K.C. John Wei, 2018, “Dissecting arbitrage costs,” under review at Review of Financial Studies. Summary: We examine how various arbitrage costs affect a diverse set of anomaly patterns in average returns. We find that arbitrage risk and transaction costs are in general more important than valuation uncertainty. The effect of arbitrage risk on anomaly returns is higher during periods of high investor sentiment or funding illiquidity, while the effect of transaction costs does not depend on these market states. For individual components, binding arbitrage costs shift over time. Transaction costs remain important in recent years, as arbitrage and short selling activities expand and become more sophisticated. More importantly, a measure that simply averages rankings of nine prominent arbitrage costs exhibits the most effective and stable measure of arbitrage costs. We also find that arbitrage costs predict future returns because they affect the long versus short legs of return anomalies asymmetrically. I also complete a paper related to this project. In this paper, we also examine arbitrage costs, but focus on the country-level measures of arbitrage costs and use it to distinguish between the limits-to-arbitrage/behavioral explanation and the q-theory explanation for the profitability effect in an international setting. The paper has already been accepted for publication at European Financial Management. The results are summarized as follows: 2. Chen, Te-Feng, Lei Sun, K.C. John Wei, and Feixue Xie, 2018, “The profitability effect: Insights from international equity markets,” European Financial Management, Special issue on “Corporate Policies and Asset Prices,” forthcoming. Summary: Using data from 33 international markets over the period 1990-2017, we reveal that the profitability effect exists in many countries other than the U.S., but the size of this effect is sensitive to the measure of profitability and portfolio sorts. The profitability effect is significant in pooled developed and global markets though less so in emerging markets. The evidence lends support to incorporating a profitability factor in regional/global factor models. Cross-region and cross-country analyses show mixed evidence for a positive relation between profitability effects and market developments, though the overall findings lean toward supporting the prediction of the investment model.

16503514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503514.value: The measures of arbitrage costs have been commonly used to distinguish a rational explanation from a behavioral explanation for any cross-sectional returns that cannot be explained by the existing risk models. In the past, many proxies have been proposed and treated equally and independently. However, many of these measures are highly correlated. A comprehensive investigation to extract the information contained in these measures to reduce the dimensionality has an urgent need. In this project, we propose two simple aggregation methods: principal component analysis and averaging ranks. Other more complicated methods might have a potential to increase its power and efficiency. This is in our future research agenda.

16503514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503514.value: Arbitrage costs are very important for arbitrageurs to engage in any arbitrage activities. When arbitrage costs are high, asset mispricing is very difficult to arbitrage away. Many measures have been proposed to proxy for arbitrage costs to distinguish the behavioral explanation from the rational explanation for any existing or new anomaly. However, no comprehensive studies have examined their cross-section differences in terms of ability or power. In this project, we have comprehensively examined these proxies for arbitrage costs to evaluate their ability to distinguish arbitrage asymmetry between overvalued and undervalued stocks. We find that arbitrage risk and transaction costs are in general more important than valuation uncertainty. More importantly, we find a measure that simply averages rankings of nine prominent arbitrage costs exhibits the most effective and stable measure of arbitrage costs.

16503614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503614.value: 目前組織研究有兩個被廣泛接受，但卻是矛盾的觀點。一種觀點是March(1996)行為學效應定律(Law-of-Effect)理論有關適應性學習的研究。另一種觀點是 Staw (1976) 承諾升級 (Escalation of Commitment) 的研究。兩觀點弔詭的是，如果一個人之前的決定的結果不理想，適應學習中的效應定律表明，這個人會減少往後作同一個決定的可能；承諾升級的研究則顯示了相反的結果，即這個人保持甚至增加作同一個決定的可能。雖然這個矛盾在承諾升級和適應性學習的文獻中都有明確指出，但到目前仍沒有解決方案。 是項研究提供了解決這個矛盾的可能途徑。方法是，把自適應學習的受賞或罰的單元，由“決定”層次，提升成到“決定策略”層次。決定策略包括一組決定，而不僅僅是一個單一的決定。換句話說，決定策略是一種系統地組織一批的決定。在此框架下，“策略”，而不是“決定”，是被處罰或加賞的單位。 具體而言，可以把決定組織成一組與效應定律相乎的策略，稱之為效應定律策略。也可以把決定組織成一組與承諾升級相乎的策略，稱之為升級策略。我們發現，效應定律策略的吸引力，在學習過程中一開始就被低估，令效應定律策略被選的機會交少。也因為因為選擇法律效應策略的可能性愈來愈少，低估變得不容易在將來的學習中糾正。其結果是，升級策略被選的機會比法律效應策略被選的機會更高。這個結果，在策略層面上完全合乎效應定律，但在決定層次上卻是完全合乎升級策略。 在建議的研究計劃，我們的目標是建立一套科學的驗證，測試上述思路。我們將依循適應性學習的主要研究方法(March, 1996; Denrell, 2005; Erev & Barron, 2005)，計劃利用計算機模擬研究的核心思想。我們計劃做兩模擬和兩種行為研究。在模擬1中，我們將比較升級戰略和法律效應策略之間的相對被選機會。模擬2將複製模擬1，並加入中性策略的學習。行為研究1和2的研究將收集人類受試的決策行為資料，驗證在模擬1和模擬2，觀察到的一切。

16503614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503614.value: A paradox in organizational research on judgment and decision making is that although the law-of-effect in adaptive learning suggests that people’s tendency to take a decision decreases after the decision receives negative consequences, people often exhibit an opposite action pattern of escalation of commitment. To address this paradox, this paper proposes that the unit of law-of-effect can be extended from a decision level to a strategy level (i.e., a group of planned decisions). A strategy organizes decisions from being consistent with the law-of-effect in one extreme to being consistent with escalation of commitment in another extreme. This paper shows that the favorability of the law-of-effect strategy (versus the escalation strategy) is likely to be underestimated at the beginning of a learning process. This underestimation stabilizes over time because negative consequences decrease the likelihood of choosing the law-of-effect strategy in the future. Accordingly, escalation strategy will be preferred more in the learning process, thereby developing a pattern of behaviors that is contradictory to the law-of-effect at the decision level but consistent with the law-of-effect at the strategy level. This learning pattern was demonstrated in three simulations with different combinations that were specified to capture different aspects of escalation of commitment. This learning perspective offers a novel explanation of escalation, suggesting that escalation may occur without distorted motivation or cognition.

16503614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503614.value: This GRF project serves as a “proof-of-concept” showing that the adaptive learning approach can be compatible with escalation of commitment. However, this work has not yet been a formal approach of escalation of commitment because it does not specify exactly how different major characteristics of escalation of commitment is explicated under adaptive learning. The next stage of this line of research is to formally propose and test adaptive learning as a new approach in understanding escalation of commitment. The adaptive learning approach is a breakthrough in the escalation literature because it offers new insights into a number of issues that the current research and theories of escalation of commitment literature could not address. Building upon the proven basic principle of resolving the learning-escalation paradox from our earlier works, in the next research we will attempt to significantly expand the scope of coverage of the adaptive learning from simply a proof-of-concept to a formal theory of escalation. The major goal is to illustrate and test how adaptive learning can be operating under situations that realistically represent escalation situations.

16503614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503614.value: After a decision maker know that his/her previous decision resulted in a bad outcome, sometimes he/she will stop making the same decision again, but sometimes he/she will escalate his/her commitment to the same decision. These contradictory pattern of behaviors have been a paradox in psychology and management. On the one hand, adaptive learning theory strong suggests that the principle of reward and punishment should be universal, thereby escalation of commitment should not be common. On the other hand, a number of works on escalation bias and sunk costs fallacy have shown the people often increase behavioral tendency after getting negative feedback. This proposed research shows that this paradox can be successfully resolved by making two new conceptualizations. First, people can organize a series of discrete decisions to be under a strategy. Second, learning occurs at strategy level but not decision level. That is, when adaptive learning happens at strategy level, strategy that organize decisions to be consistent with escalation bias will be learned to be more preferable.

16503714.label: Project Objectives
16503714.value: Develop an analytic model of consumers’ observational learning in group buying. A set of information is available to address concerns regarding uncertain product quality and fit, with each consumer's personal taste (e.g. restaurants). Consumers learn by inferring product quality and fit from indirect information, such as price, discount, or quantity sold. This model should also offer the capability to examine a consumer's ability to learn, i.e. by making inferences to different levels of accuracy. Develop an analytic model of vendors’ pricing decisions. Pricing directly affects consumer purchases, and indirectly affects the set of information that later consumers will observe. Lower prices are likely to initially generate higher demand, which is displayed as quantity sold to potential consumers, and becomes part of the basis for their purchase. In this part of the model, vendors should account for both direct and indirect impacts and choose the optimal price to maximize their profits. Extend the model to allow for the option to customize the set of information available and to examine optimal platform design. Vendors with niche products (i.e. high fit variance) can benefit from the non-disclosure of the quantity sold, as consumers may mis-interpret low sales figures as low quality, rather than high fit variance. The group buying platform should be designed according to the vendors’ composition and their characteristics. Empirically identify consumers’ observational learning and evaluate the significance of price, discount, quantity sold, and the interactions between them. Generate insight on the effectiveness of the group buying model, in terms of vendors’ capability to reach new consumers, consumers’ capability to accurately learn from the platform, and consumers’ willingness to re-purchase from vendors.

16503714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503714.value: Group buying is an adventurous exploration of the e-commerce world by entrepreneurs who foresaw the business potential of social networking. The success of Groupon, LivingSocial, and the alike has inspired a growing body of new business ideas, and in the meantime, has made group buying a popular and necessary option for an enormous number of vendors and consumers. Vendors offer products and services at a discounted price through an online group buying platform, and consumers commit to purchase before the actual consumption. The transaction is activated only when a critical mass is reached. Such transactions can create a "win-win" situation, where vendors benefit from increased exposure to consumers (in addition to the revenue generated), and consumers enjoy merchandise at not only a discounted price, but also at a minimized risk for new products and services. Contrary to a mutually beneficial situation, many companies have experienced an adverse effect, i.e., rather than attracting potential future customers, vendors attract more "deal-seekers", who experience the products at the discounted price and never patronize the vendor's business at the regular price. This project poses three research questions: (1) When is it optimal for a vendor to sell through a group buying platform? (2) How does the information available on a group buying platform (such as price, discount level, quantity sold, third-party reviews, etc.), affect a consumer's purchase decision? (3) How does the information as mentioned above affect a consumer's willingness to purchase at the regular price? The preliminary analysis from two benchmark models and a simple learning model suggests that sellers should offer a discount rate that is suitable for the information available through the group buying platform, and then use this price to create a valuable chain of demand. During the project, the theoretic model will be further extended to examine more precise learning processes that consumers are more likely to adopt. In the meantime, a data collection process will be launched to gather daily sales figures from Groupon in over 100 U.S. cities. This data set will be analyzed using a structural equation model to empirically uncover the role of information availability on consumer behavior and the effectiveness of selling through group buying. 团购是一种有效利用社交网络的新兴电子商务模式。在国外，Groupon，LivingSocial等团购网站取得了广泛的成功，并激励了更多样化的商业模型。同时，对众多的商家和消费者来说，团购网站更是成为了一种流行甚至是必须的消费渠道。商家通过团购网站以大幅折扣出售自己的商品，而顾客则形成了在消费之前通过网上购买团购券的习惯。通常团购网站有一个明显的特点，就是购买团购券的顾客必须达到一定的数量。团购的宗旨是让买卖双方都受益。一方面，商家通过这种网络渠道发现了新的客户源，而用户则可以折扣价享受产品及服务。然而现实中，许多商家都经历了负面的团购体验。这些商家虽然吸引了新的客户，然而这些客户却只愿意用折扣价消费。 这个项目从三方面分析并解决以上的困境。（1）什么样的商家最适合团购的营销模式？（2）团购网站上提供的信息对客户的购买决定有何影响？（3）怎样设计团购网站的信息结构以有效的吸引客户？我们用博弈论模型初步分析了客户对信息的学习过程，并且发现商家必须利用网站信息结构去设定折扣率，并进一步通过折扣率吸引对他们有利的顾客。在接下来的项目中，我们将对顾客的学习模型继续细化分析。同时，我们会从团购模式的先驱，Groupon，收集数据，并用数据分析来验证我们的理论结果。

16503714.label: Realisation of objectives
16503714.value: This project has led to two research papers that addressed the above five objectives successfully. In the first research paper, the PI addresses the objectives 1-3 through analyzing the role of information disclosure on the effectiveness of group buying promotions. A game theoretic model is developed to capture the interactions between merchants and consumers through a group buying platform, and our objective is to develop a theoretical framework for the optimal information structure that suits different types of merchants with different market characteristics. This paper answers two research questions. (1) How does the information available on the group buying platform, such as price, discount level, quantity sold, etc., affect consumers' purchase decisions and merchants' pricing decisions? (2) Under what information structure can merchants promote effectively through a group buying platform? The model analyzes both merchants' and consumers' strategies in the scenarios with no information signal, with quantity signal, and with both quantity and discount signals. There are several main findings. First, merchants, particularly merchants with high experience quality, can have more effective discount promotion when signals are available to consumers. When both quantity and discount signals are available, merchants with very high experience quality are better off as it is optimal for them to offer low discounts, i.e., high discount prices, and still attract all valuable consumers to buy their products. In the meantime, those with very low experience quality are worse off in this case as they must offer very high discounts if they want to attract all valuable customers. Second, more information is not necessarily better. In other words, the effect of signals on discount strategies is not straightforward. When there is no additional signal available to merchants, only low-quality merchants with a small existing user base, can attract all their convertible customers through discount promotion. As quantity information becomes available, merchants with very low experience quality benefit as they can now offer a lower discount and still attract customers. By comparing these two cases, we discover that making quantity information available can hurt high-quality merchants, and eventually hurt the platform, as the platform becomes more attractive to very low quality merchants. Note that high-quality merchants are strongly disadvantaged in both no signal and quantity signal cases, whereas they are favored in the case with both quantity and discount signals. We also examine the effect of market composition and consumers' belief formation on merchants' discounting strategies. The second research paper empirically examines the interactions between consumers and merchants through the information on group buying platforms. we compiled a panel data set from a leading daily-deal platform, Groupon.com, that comprises 19,978 deals covering many products and services in a wide range of categories from 172 cities in the United States and Canada. We captured the characteristics for each deal and recorded its sales volume by hour, which leads to a total of 1,835,794 observations. We conducted a series of statistical tests to empirically examine whether offering higher discounts help online daily-deal merchants sell more vouchers. By estimating a panel data model with rich fixed effects to account for product characteristics and time trends and robust standard errors clustered by product subcategories to account for cross-item demand correlations over time, we find a significant negative effect of discount percentage on sales (i.e., number of vouchers sold). Specifically, a one-percent discount decreases sales by 0:0352% [0.0105, 0.0600] per hour. To our knowledge, the prior literature has not documented such an immediate negative effect of discounts on sales. To strengthen identification, we conduct two instrumental variable (IV) estimations. The first exploits exogenous characteristics of competing products in a differentiated product. The second IV estimation uses average hourly wage (AHW) and housing price index (HPI) in each deal's industry and location as instruments. We find that the negative effect of discount percentage on sales is robust to accounting for endogeneity using the IV estimators. Overall, three main findings are generated. First, we present empirical evidence that discount can be detrimental to sales in a new online setting wherein consumers are often not familiar with the merchants offering the discounts and the quality of products or services is difficult to be verified before consumption. Second, we pin down consumers' quality concern as the driving factor of the negative discount impact through both empirical analysis and lab experiment. We are thus among the first to empirically demonstrate quality-signaling effect of price discounts could dominate the cost-saving effect when information asymmetry is pronounced. Third, we present experimental evidence that the negative discount effect may manifest itself only when discount exceeds a threshold. Fourth, we provide evidence that displaying favorable third-party quality cues may backfire in the presence of deep discounts. Lastly, we provide concrete guidance to merchants on how to design a daily deal to attract consumers through price discounts and, also, to daily-deal platform owners on how to improve their business models.

16503714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503714.value: Online daily-deal platforms, such as Groupon and LivingSocial, have become a prominent price promotion tool. As two-sided markets, online daily-deal platforms allow merchants to capitalize on economies of scale in attracting consumers via discounts, and also provide consumers with a chance to explore a wide variety of products and services in their region. In fact, daily-deal platforms have surpassed email and search advertising in advertising spending and arisen as the main marketing channel for many local businesses, and are particularly effective in attracting new customers. Although discounts are appealing to consumers because they help save costs, it may have a more intriguing effect on daily-deal consumers, due to the inherent uncertainty and risk embedded in the setting of online daily deal platforms. Findings from the current research provide concrete guidance to merchants on how to design a daily deal to attract consumers through price discounts and, also, to daily-deal platform owners on how to improve their business models.

16503914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503914.value: In recent years, there is exciting development relating disagreement among investors to asset prices. The basic idea is that when investors disagree and when there are short-sales constraints, the asset price reflects the optimists’ view because the pessimists cannot short and hence sit on the sideline. Therefore, a larger disagreement implies a higher price and hence a lower subsequent return on average. This basic idea is presented in Miller (1977, Journal of Finance), and then subsequently adapted in a number of theory papers. Such theories based on disagreement have found support in the data in a number of recent empirical papers. See Hong and Stein (2007) for a recent review. However, as anyone who has worked on the empirical studies on disagreement will likely point out (the PI included), a main hurdle facing further empirical development of the disagreement literature is the lack of a good disagreement measure. So far, the main disagreement measures are constructed from surveys from professional forecasters or surveys from the general population. It is unclear how well the survey subjects represent the investor population. The survey outcome is also likely affected by respondents’ incentive issues. In addition, the availability of the disagreement measure is limited by how frequent and in which country the survey is conducted. This project has two objectives: (1) construct a disagreement measure from daily institutional trades, which allows a relatively clean control of liquidity; (2) apply the daily disagreement measure to test disagreement theory using stock returns, particularly around news releases. Intuitively, the disagreement measure is based on opposite bets from buyers and sellers, which is consistent with theoretical predictions. However, one needs to control for trades due to liquidity reasons. This project plans to control liquidity-based trades by examining the total net buy of an institution in a given day across all stocks. If total buy > total sell (positive total net buy), this institution is unlikely facing large money outflow and hence hence its sell orders are unlikely due to liquidity reasons. Similarly, if the total net buy is negative, this institution’s buy orders are unlikely a mechanical response to large money inflow. Using sell orders from institutions with positive total net buy and using buy orders from institutions with negative total net sell will likely give a sharper measure of bets from disagreeing investors. The resulting daily disagreement is especially suitable to test disagreement theory around news releases, to be detailed later. 近年来，投资者之间的分歧对资产价格的影响有令人振奋的发展。其基本思想是，投资者有意见分歧，并当股市有卖空约束，资产价格反映乐观观点。因此，较大的意见分歧意味着较高的价格和较低的后续回报。这个基本的想法是呈现在Miller（ 1977年，Journal of Finance）和后续的论文。这个理论已经找到实证论文的支持，见Hong和Stein （ 2007年）的点评。 然而，进一步推进这个研究方向的一个主要障碍是缺乏良好的测度投资者意见分歧的指标。到目前为止，主要的指标是基于专业预测师或普通人群间预测的差别。这样的指标不一定能代表投资者群体的意见分歧。此外，这样的指标只在有限的一些地区有。 本项目有两个目标： （ 1）基于投资者的交易构建一个意见分歧的指标; （2）应用这个意见分歧的指标来测试投资者意见分歧影响股价的理论。

16504014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504014.value: Advance selling is a standard marketing practice where sellers offer customers an opportunity to purchase a product or service before it is available to be consumed. It has been widely applied in many service industries, including airlines, hotels, theatres, cruises, and sports, as well as in numerous retail industries, including wines, toys, books, electronic gadgets, and media products. Prior research shows that sellers and consumers can both enjoy great benefits from advance selling. The existing studies, however, have focused on the advance selling of a single product. In practice many sellers offer multiple related products or services in advance, sometimes in bundles. Expedia.com, orbitz.com, and ctrip.com are among many online travel agents selling vacation packages. Sports clubs, theatres, and museums allow pre-purchase of daily tickets, as well as season and annual passes. Many popular electronic gadgets (e.g., game consoles, tablets, mobile phones) are made available for advance orders before their official release dates, together with their accessories or/and service plans. During advance sales of flight tickets, airlines offer consumers options to prepay for checked luggage, preferred seats, and flexibility to change or cancel their tickets later. Hotels and resorts presell package deals that combine rooms, meals, and various amenity services. Despite the wide applications of multi-product advance selling, sellers may find it difficult to make decisions on when, how, and which products to sell in advance. The difficulty arises from the need to simultaneously manage a line of products over a dynamic selling horizon, as well as consumers’ strategic responses to sellers’ advance selling strategies. Specifically, when sellers offer multiple products in advance, consumers can choose whether, when, and which product(s) to buy. Anticipating consumers’ strategic purchasing behavior, sellers need to carefully plan their pricing and supply strategies over time. Furthermore, a question of particular interest to the sellers is whether to bundle some (or all) products in advance time (i.e., far ahead of consumption) and/or in spot time (i.e., close to consumption). It is also unclear when and how much the sellers benefit from advance selling, with or without product bundling. This project aims to investigate sellers’ optimal advance-selling strategies with multiple inter-correlated products and services. Particularly, we will examine sellers’ joint decisions on pricing, capacity, and product bundling. In addition, we will also explore how the joint decisions affect sellers’ profits, customers’ purchasing behavior, and overall benefit to the society. 现今很多商家在销售产品或者服务的时候采用一种提前销售的策略，也就是容许顾客在产品上市或者享受服务之前提前购买该产品或服务。提前销售战略现已成为很多行业（如旅游、娱乐、和零售等）中的一种常见的营销手段，顾客们可以利用商家提前销售的机会预定各种商品，比如机票，酒店住宿，玩具，书籍，电子产品，酒类，和住宅公寓等等。研究表明商家和顾客都可以从提前销售/购买活动中获利，但是现有研究仅限于单个产品的提前销售分析。 实际生活中很多商家会在提前销售过程中容许顾客同时购买多个产品，有的时候还采取多产品绑定销售。例如很多在线旅游代理网站（Expedia.com, obitz.com, ctrip.com）提前销售旅游套票。健身俱乐部、戏院、和博物馆在容许顾客提前购买单日票的同时，也提供购买季度和年度套票的机会。很多电子产品（比如电子游戏、平板电脑、移动电话）在正式上市之前也容许顾客预订，有的时候还可以同时预订这些电子产品的配件和服务计划。在提前销售机票的时候，航空公司也给旅客提供机会预订很多额外服务，比如托运行李、升级座舱、改签或者取消机票。很多酒店和度假村也会提前销售包括房间、用餐、和各种升级服务的套票。 虽然多产品提前销售应用广泛，很多商家却发现关于多产品销售的时机、方式、策略等决策十分困难。这主要是因为需要动态管理多个产品，而且需要考虑到顾客对于商家提前销售策略的反应。具体来说，如果商家提前销售多个产品，顾客可以自由决定何时购买哪个产品。考虑到这样的顾客行为，商家需要仔细的规划其定价和供给策略，尤其是关于是否在提前销售中绑定产品的决策。此外，商家能从多产品提前销售中获得多大的收益，也是需要研究的重要问题。 本项目的目标在于研究商家在多产品环境下的最优提前销售策略，尤其是定价和产品绑定策略。除此之外，我们也会研究最优提前销售策略如何影响商家利润，消费者行为，和社会总福利。

16504014.label: Realisation of objectives
16504014.value: 1. This objective has been fully achieved. To model multi-product advance selling, we have developed a dynamic framework where a seller who can sell two products to a pool of consumers over two periods, advance and spot. In either period, the seller may offer the products separately or in a bundle. The actual consumption of the products takes place in spot, but the products can be pre-ordered in advance. The consumers are forward-looking and choose whether, when, and which product(s) to buy. Consumers’ purchasing choices are determined by their valuations of the products, which are uncertain in the advance period and revealed to individual buyers in spot. The seller dynamically determines his optimal prices in each period, taking account of consumers’ rational response to his pricing and bundling strategies. To separate and account for the effects of various factors, we have analyzed four different models under the aforementioned framework. The first model, labelled by (i), features two important inter-product relationships: valuation correlation and valuation contingency. The second model, labelled by (ii), focuses on the effects of the service or production cost that the seller incurs for satisfying each consumer’s demand. The first two models assume that the two products are symmetric to each other in terms of valuation distributions, which have allowed us to focus on the fundamental difference between advance selling and bundling, as well as their interactions when adopted simultaneously. Building on the insights from the first two models, we have considered four model extensions. The first two extensions enrich the model (i) by incorporating two types of product asymmetry. The first asymmetric-product model, labelled by (iii), captures the reality that two products may differ in the level of consumers’ valuation uncertainty: in the advance period consumers can be more certain about the valuations for one product than they are about the other product. In the second asymmetric-product model, labelled by (iv), we consider a main product and an auxiliary product, where the latter is valuable only if it is consumed together with the former. In the meanwhile, to explore various bundling strategies, which reflect different levels of the firm’s operational flexibility or market condition (e.g., competition), we have analyzed two extensions of the model (ii) to consider mixed bundling, labeled by (v), where product bundles and individual products are offered at the same time, and dynamic bundling decisions, labeled by (vi), where produce bundling decisions are made sequentially at different time epochs. The main research question for the model (v) is whether, when, and how much the firm can benefit from the flexibility of mixed bundling. For the model (vi), we examine whether the firm is better off by having the flexibility of postponing the decision on spot bundling strategy. Our results from these six models are summarized as follows. We have fully solved the first four models, (i) through (iv), and the last model, (vi), under some conditions. Specifically, we have derived closed-form solutions for the seller’s optimal pricing and bundling strategies, and performed comparative analysis of the solutions with respect to the key factors (the major findings of the comparative analysis are summarized below for objective point 2). In addition, we have examined the seller’s profits to identify the strategic relationship (i.e., complements or substitutes) between advance selling and product bundling. That is, whether a simultaneous adoption of both strategies attenuates or reinforces their respective contribution to the firm. For the model (v), a full characterization is technically challenging and hence we have performed numerical study to examine the effect of mixed bundling. 2. The objective has been fully achieved. The major findings from the comparative studies of the six models are reported as follows: (i) We find that two inter-product relationships, valuation correlation and valuation contingency, critically affect the profit advantages of advance selling and product bundling. In terms of valuation correlation, advance selling is most effective for products with positively-correlated valuations, while the opposite applies to bundling: its value is the highest when product valuations are negatively correlated. Further, valuation contingency (i.e., product complementarity or substitutability) reduces the values of advance selling and bundling, either individually or jointly. Our results show that, in the absence of marginal cost, advance selling and produce bundling are strategic substitutes, i.e., one strategy becomes less valuable when it is adopted in conjunction with the other strategy. The substitutability is strongest when product valuations are substitutable and negatively correlated. The rationale behind our findings is that advance selling and product bundling play similar roles in reducing buyer heterogeneity - bundling acts upon buyer heterogeneity across products, while the benefit of advance selling pivots on buyer heterogeneity over time. (ii) We find that a higher marginal cost reduces the benefits of advance selling and bundling, either individually or jointly. Interesting, for intermediate values of the marginal cost, advance selling and bundling are complementary to each other. In such cases advance selling by itself does not create any value. When it is combined with bundling, however, it can generate positive value to the firm, as it allows the firm to differentiate its bundling strategy over time. (iii) When the two products differ in the consumers’ valuation uncertainty in advance, the values of advance selling and bundling, either individually or jointly, are lower than their counterparts in the symmetric-product setting. (iv) With product asymmetry in consumption priority, the values of advance selling and bundling, either individually or jointly, are higher than their counterparts in the symmetric-product setting. (v) Mixed bundling can continue to benefit the seller when adopted in conjunction with advance selling. (vi) The overall profit from dynamic bundling decisions is lower than that with pre-announced bundling decisions. 3. The objective has been fully achieved. The impact on the firms’ profits has been summarized in objective 2. The aggregate consumer surplus is improved by bundling, either by itself or jointly with advance selling, when marginal cost is sufficiently low. In particular, bundling may hurt consumer surplus by reducing their purchasing flexibility and leading to over-supply or under-supply of the products. In the meanwhile, the effects of bundling on social surplus follow a similar pattern as those on seller’s profit. Specifically, social surplus is improved by static bundling only when the marginal cost is sufficiently small, while it is never improved and sometimes worsened by spot bundling in the two-period setting. From a higher level, to explore the effects of the firm’s advance selling strategy on consumers’ purchasing behavior and welfare, we perform another study, labelled by model (vii), focusing on consumers’ strategic stockpiling behavior during advance selling. Stockpiling (also known as forward buying) means that, when the selling price is low, consumers may buy more than their current consumption need and save the purchased items for future consumption. We characterize the firm’s joint inventory and markdown strategies in the presence of such strategic consumer behavior.

16504014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504014.value: Advance selling is a standard marketing practice where sellers offer customers opportunities to purchase a product or service before it is available for consumption. It has been widely applied in many service and retail industries. Prior research shows that sellers and consumers can all enjoy great benefits from advance selling. The existing studies, however, have focused on a single product, even though multi-product advance selling is ubiquitous in practice. When sellers need to simultaneously manage a line of products over a dynamic selling horizon, they may find it difficult to make decisions on when, how, and which products to sell in advance. This project has aimed to tackle this challenge, and focused on joint optimization of sellers’ pricing and bundling decisions during multi-product advance selling. We have developed a dynamic framework for multi-product advance selling and analyzed six models under the framework. These models capture various important factors that may impact on sellers’ gain from advance selling and product bundling. The analysis on the effects of these factors will provide some guidance for sellers in practice. In addition, the models reveal some interesting interactions between advance selling and product bundling, which is of both academic and practical values.

16504114.value: 分析師有從眾行為嗎？一個基於文本的研究

16504114.label: Project Objectives

16504114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504114.value: Abstract: We propose a novel method to measure an analyst’s innovation (i.e., her private information). Specifically, we use a topic generation model called latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) developed in the field of information retrieval research, to measure the amount of innovative topics contained in her written reports. Using this measure, we solve an important challenge to the herding literature – distinguishing herding behavior (i.e., underweighting private information and overweighting public information) from forecast clustering resulting from reactions to common information. This project will contribute to both the herding literature and analyst literature by providing a more definitive answer to whether analysts herd. Herding behavior broadly refers to a phenomenon in which many people take the same actions, as if they are imitating each other. It has been observed in many different types of activities such as fashion, fads, investment choices, and corporate decisions (see review of Devenow and Welch 1996; Scharfstein and Stein 1990). Academia has devoted a large amount of effort trying to understand herding behavior. There are two views – rational and non-rational views on herding behavior. The rational view believes that herding can be explained by extraneous incentives, and that is the view this proposed study will adopt. However, empirical research on rational herding is often challenged by the difficulty of distinguishing herding from different individuals’ independently reacting similarly to common information. The literature sometimes labels the latter phenomenon “clustering” (Devenow and Welch 1996). One stream of herding literature focuses on whether analysts herd in their forecasts to obtain positive reputational externalities. Theoretical work in this literature refers to it as reputational herding. As reviewed by Graham (1999) and Jegadeesh and Kim (2009), although theoretical studies have come up with various well-crafted models, empirical evidence on analysts’ herding behavior is mixed and limited due to the difficulty of distinguishing herding from the possibility that analysts forecast similarly due to their correlated information. Our central contribution to the herding literature is our innovative measure of analysts’ private information based on the textual information in their reports. With this measure, we can effectively test whether analysts with certain characteristics or under certain circumstances are more likely to underweight their private information. Therefore, our empirical tests can distinguish herding behavior resulting from reputational concerns from forecast clustering, so that we can contribute to the herding literature by providing a more definitive answer as to whether analysts herd. 我們提出了一種新的方法來衡量分析師的創新（即她的私人信息）。具體來說，我們使用的信息檢索研究領域發展的被稱為LDA的話題生成模型，來衡量包含在分析師的書面報告創新性的話題量。通過這個工具，我們解決了一個從眾效應領域的重要的挑戰，區別從眾行為（即過少使用私人信息和過多使用公共信息）和對共同信息的預測集群。本項目將會對分析師是否從眾得到更明確的答案，從而促進從眾研究和分析師研究。 從眾行為泛指一種現象，即很多人採取同樣的行動，就好像他們在模仿對方。它在許多不同類型的活動，如時裝，潮流，投資選擇，以及企業的決策被觀察到（見綜述Devenow and Welch 1996; Scharfstein and Stein 1990）。學術界已經投入了大量的精力試圖了解從眾行為。有兩種觀點 - 對從眾行為理性和非理性的看法。理性的觀點認為，從眾效應可以通過外在誘因來解釋，這是本項目會採用的觀點。然而，理性的從眾效應的實證研究經常會遇到挑戰，比如如何區分從眾行為和不同個體對同樣的信息的獨立但類似的反應。文獻中有時把後一種現象稱為“集群”（Devenow and Welch 1996）。 從眾文獻中的一個流側重於分析師是否從他們從眾的預測中得到正面聲譽。在這個文獻中的理論工作把它叫做聲譽從眾。正如Graham（1999）和Jegadeesh and Kim（2009）回顧，雖然理論研究提出了各種精心設計的模型，分析師的從眾行為的實證證據還沒有定論。因為實證研究在區分分析師的從眾行為和他們對相關的信息的類似反應時有困難。 我們對從眾文獻的核心貢獻在於我們使用了一種創新的方法，即使用分析師報告中文本信息得出分析師的私人信息量。通過這個工具，我們能夠有效地分析具有哪些特性的或在哪些情況下的分析師會更有過少使用自己私人信息的可能性。因此，我們的實證檢驗可以區分聲譽從眾行為和集群行為。這樣，我們就可以通過更明確的回答分析師是否有從眾行為的問題，有助於從眾文獻的進步。

16504214.label: Project Objectives
16504214.value: The work will be conducted on US firms which data are commercially available. In the first stage, I will infer default probabilities from the daily and monthly data of corporate bonds and credit default swaps. In the second stage, I will estimate default probabilities, using the framework of Altman's Z-score and Ohlson's O-score, with a broader set of both macroeconomic and firm-level accounting-related data and probit/logit models. 16504214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504214.value: Default probabilities inferred from financial data are much more highly correlated across different debt issuers than those implied by the standard academic models. It is important to understand what drives these high correlations in order to improve on existing models. This project aims at differentiating between two different hypotheses and finding out which one is correct. One hypothesis is that the default probabilities inferred from credit spreads of corporate bonds and bond credit derivatives reflect the true default probabilities, which are highly correlated themselves. The other hypothesis is that the true default probabilities of different debt issuers are not that highly correlated, but since there is informational asymmetry between debt issuers and debt investors, debt investors have to infer the true default probability of one debt issuer from the observed behavior of other debt issuers, causing their subjective assessments of the default probabilities to be highly correlated across different debt issuers. Depending on which of the two hypotheses is more to the truth, there can be different policy implications. The results of this project will shed light on this important issue.

16504214.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504214.value: In this project, we try to identify variables at the macroeconomic, industry and firm levels that capture covariations of the risk-neutral probabilities. The extant literature models rely more on parameters estimated from historic data during normal times and fail to capture fast changes in crises. We link the correlations in risk-neutral default probabilities to macroeconomic variables, industry factors, as well as firm-specific variables, revealing the time-series patterns of these components, and quantifying the contributions of each of these components. Our methodology differs from what is used in the literature in that we estimate the determinants of the covariations in risk-neutral default probabilities, while the most popular approach in the literature is to rely on common factor structure in the first moment to generate covariation across firms/assets. Our methodology is natural given our interest is in covariations in risk-neutral probabilities. Our results show that, while macroeconomic factors and industry factors both play important roles in generating covariations in risk-neutral default probabilities, the most important source of the variables is related to the physical default probabilities. This is not only because that physical default probabilities are part of risk-neutral probabilities, but also because the differences between the risk-neutral and physical default probabilities, i.e., the risk premiums, are also related to the physical probabilities. A key finding in our paper is that variables that contribute to default probabilities also contribute to default probability covariations. Firm-specific variables such as profitability, leverage, and past stock returns all contribute to the default probability at the firm level. The results in this paper provides constructively ingredients for building the next-generation of credit models for the purpose of pricing credit derivatives written on portfolios of assets subject to defaults. At the industry level, we reconfirm and strengthen the result that the covariation of risk-neutral default probabilities is inversely related to the competitiveness of the industry. We obtain the result using both the industry Herfindahl-Hirschman Index and the Lerner Index. The latter has been shown in the literature as a better (inverse) measure of the competitiveness of the industry.

16504214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504214.value: The project can be extended to a deeper level to find out the contribution of supply chain relatioship to the correlations of risk-neutral default probabilities, if the data on supply chain relationship can be obtained.

16504214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504214.value: In this project we analyze the determinants of high correlations among CDS-implied risk-neutral default probabilities. We document at the firm level that correlations of risk-neutral default probabilities are driven by correlations of actual default probabilities, macroeconomic systematic factors, as well as industry factors, of which only the industry factors have been analyzed in the literature in event-study forms. We find that correlations of actual default probabilities and macroeconomic systematic factors play greater roles and we reconfirm and strengthen the earlier finding that the industry effects are inversely related to the competitiveness of the industry.

16504314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504314.value: Conservatism is a prominent and pervasive feature of accounting practice. A significant branch of accounting research has been devoted to empirically measuring accounting conservatism and understanding its causes and consequences. Since Basu (1997), a widely accepted measure of (conditional) conservatism is an asymmetric earnings-return relation for good versus bad news (proxied by positive and negative stock returns, respectively), interpreted as asymmetric timeliness. However, while the argument advanced for adopting this measure is intuitively appealing, the extant literature has paid little attention to real economic forces (e.g., a firm’s economic decisions), as opposed to accounting practice, that may also cause similar asymmetric behavior. As has been shown in the valuation literature, economic decisions governing business operations constitute a primary force driving the relation between equity value and accounting variables, and so the existing research that infer accounting properties from the observed earnings-return relation is incomplete, and potentially invalid, without controlling for the effect of economic forces. It is important that we consider economic as well as accounting factors in examining the relation between earnings and return in order to interpret the behavior of this relation and infer conservatism. In this proposal, we employ existing valuation models as a starting point to develop a more general relation between earnings and return that incorporate both types of factors. Based on our theoretical model, we conduct empirical analysis aimed to disentangle the effects of real economic forces and those of accounting conservatism in causing the asymmetry property. The study contributes to the literature on accounting conservatism by providing a more comprehensive view of what is really driving the asymmetric timeliness property. 稳健性是会计实施中的一个重要特征。 会计研究的一个任务是确定如何用实证方法衡量稳健性，并了解其成因及后果。从Basu (1997) 开始，一个被广泛接受的衡量（条件）稳健性的方法是观察盈利-回报关系在好、坏消息情况下的不对称性，称之谓非对称及时性。可是，这个方法尽管在直觉上有一定道理，迄今为止的研究都忽视了实体经营活动（而不是会计实践）对盈利-回报关系的影响。另一方面，在定价研究的文献中，实体经济决策被认为是确定价值与会计变量关系的主要因素。这就意味着，如果不考虑经济因素，而单单从盈利-回报关系来判断会计特性是不完整的，甚至可能是无效的。本研究项目中，我们从现有的定价模型出发，建立一个更全面的盈利-回报关系，它同时包含了经济与会计因素。在这个理论模型的前提下，我们展开实证分析，把造成非对称特性的会计因素与经济因素分离开来。这样，我们对造成非对称特性的基本原因会有一个更加全面的理解。

16504414.label: Project Objectives
16504414.value: Develop models of competition in expert services with possible overselling for separate and combined queues, for two and more than two experts Develop methods to mitigate or eliminate expert overselling, including compensation structure, queue configuration, and performance-based allocation of clients

Develop methods to mitigate or eliminate expert overselling, including compensation structure, queue configuration, and performance-based allocation of clients

16504414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504414.value: There are many instances when people need advice and services from experts. The expert possesses expertise that may be difficult or unrealistic for clients to acquire. Due to this knowledge gap, experts could oversell unnecessary services. Requiring experts to adhere to some ethical codes, which is often seen in practice, may not fully eliminate the possibility of overselling either. The present research proposal aims to complement existing related literature by considering competition of expert services in a queuing setting. Although the setting can be generally applied to many kinds of expert services, our primary motivating examples will be from the healthcare sector, where patients choose competing healthcare providers. We want to address the following three questions: i. What is the optimal overselling strategy for experts under competition? When an expert provides unnecessary services to the client, the expert can gain more profit from that particular client, but the service time needed would be longer, which reduces the time spent on other clients. We will characterize, under different conditions, how the experts would choose the level of overselling. Will the experts behave similarly, or will they differentiate? We also want to find conditions under which the experts will choose to be completely truthful. This is an important question from the society’s point of view, since overselling provides no economic value to clients. ii. What proportion of the potential client base could be served, and how is it divided amongst the competing experts? Different experts work at different rates, and can choose their own level of overselling. When overselling occurs, naturally there will be fewer clients willing to queue up since the expected waiting time will be longer. We will examine the proportion of client base that could have been served but are not, i.e., those who decide to drop out because of overselling. We will also look into how the client base will be divided amongst competing experts. iii. How can a social planner induce the experts to provide truthful services? A social planner cares about social welfare maximization and intends to induce the experts not to oversell. We mentioned the code of ethics that helps to mitigate overselling, but in an extreme scenario when experts ignore the ethical code, is it still possible to attain complete honesty of service? Methods may include designing a compensation structure or designing a system that allocates clients based on performance (e.g., average waiting time).

16504414.value: We have achieved all project objectives that we proposed to investigate. 16504414.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504414.value: Our research complements the existing literature on credence goods by considering expert services in a queuing setting, where customers may choose to obtain service from competing service providers, and where waiting time is a concern. We investigate the conditions under which experts would overprovide services. For a monopoly expert, we find that with ample demand, there will be overprovision in equilibrium when revenue becomes more of a concern than throughput. An expert who faces limited demand will set at least as much overprovision when compared to one who faces ample demand. When an expert overprovides, customers would expect to pay more, and expect to wait longer, due to longer individual services. Therefore, with more overprovision, fewer customers will arrive and receive service. Due to the existence of overprovision, counterintuitive situations may occur. For example, an increase in customer's service value could discourage arrivals. We propose an overprovision-mitigating mechanism, which allows a social planner to adjust reimbursements to experts, while keeping customer's payments the same and the expert's annual total reimbursement unchanged. We find that although competition will never cause more overprovision, it does not always discourage overprovision. For competition from experts who specialize in a simple treatment, the original expert may be driven to specialize in a different treatment, or may simply reduce his overprovision level to attract customers. For competition between identical experts, overprovision could be discouraged with limited demand but not ample demand. The greater the potential demand, and when the fee structure is more-than-proportional to a greater extent, the less likely competition will make an impact. We compute equilibria for numerical examples, and find that there may be unique or multiple equilibria. The amount of customers that an expert can gain from others- the throughput effect- increases with competition. Therefore, with more experts in competition, the more likely competition will make an impact. In summary, we have contributed to the existing literature of credence goods/expert services in two ways. First, we have investigated how customers' concern of waiting time can act as a deterrent for experts to overprovide services. Second, we considered competition between service providers in a queuing setting. Third, we proposed a method (the alternative reimbursement system) which mitigates overprovision by only making small adjustments under the current Medicare/Medicaid fee for service system in the United States.

16504414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504414.value: We only model two levels of customer problems. While this model allows the investigation of whether or not and how often the expert will overprovide, it could be interesting to consider more than two or even a continuous level of problems, where the question of how much overprovision could be answered. Our model suggests that overprovision depends on the level of demand and proportionality of fees, and it is likely that how much would depend on the level of demand and proportionality between different levels. Service times are assumed to be fixed, since procedures are usually standardized without much variations. It may be interesting to consider random service times, which adds extra ambiguity to whether the expert is overproviding or simply needs more time to complete the job on hand. In the model of competition between experts, identical experts are considered. It may be interesting to allow expert heterogeneity, for example more skillful experts who can provide speedier services.

We study competition of expert services in a queuing setting. Although the setting can be generally applied to many kinds of expert services, our primary motivating examples are from the healthcare sector, where patients choose competing healthcare providers. We proposed a method (the alternative reimbursement system) which mitigates overprovision by only making small adjustments under the current Medicare/Medicaid fee for service system. 16504614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504614.value: Although online retailing has grown substantially over the past decade, it still accounts for a small portion of total global retailing. To further penetrate markets dominated by brick and mortar stores, online retailers start taking advantage of mobile technology to provide mobile price comparisons and mobile payment. Consumers can use smart phones or tablets to scan product barcodes, QR codes or even label images at brick and mortar stores and then compare prices for the same products as well as read product reviews and ratings. If consumers decide to purchase online, they can make online payment with a few clicks on their smart phones or tablets. Such shopping behavior is called “mobile showrooming” and it has posed a serious threat to offline retailers. Academic research related to mobile showrooming is still in a nascent stage. This proposed study will seek to answer two research questions. How does mobile price comparison apps affect consumer purchasing behavior, defined as whether to purchase online or offline? And what is the new market equilibrium when offline retailers and online retailers compete in this new technology-enabled environment? To answer the first question, this research will develop a model that incorporates technological, economic and individual behavioral factors to explain consumer purchasing behavior. The technological factors will include price comparison on the fly, access to product information on the fly, and integration with mobile payment. The economic factors will include price dispersion and product category. The behavioral factors will include time pressure and sensitivity to price. To answer the second question, we will identify tactics offline retailers can use to alleviate the threat from mobile price comparison apps. And we will examine their effectiveness across various product categories and price dispersions. We will also seek to understand whether there is a complementary or a substitution effect of different tactics if we are able to collect the data. This work will contribute to IS (Information System) research by identifying the technological characteristics that play an important role in affecting consumer purchasing behavior. In addition, it will contribute to research on e-commerce by integrating technological, economic and behavioral factors to understand consumer purchasing behavior. This work will also contribute to research in retailing by identifying tactics which might be used by offline retailers to alleviate the threat from mobile showrooming. 尽管网上零售额在过去十年里高速增长, 它仅占全球零售额的很小部分。为了进一步抢占市场份额﹐网络零售商开始利用移动技术来实现比价和移动支付。消费者可以通过智能手机或平板电脑在实体店扫描商品条码﹐QR码﹐甚至直接扫描商品本身以比较相同商品在网上別的商家的售價以及查阅其它用户对此商品的评论和评分。如果消费者决定向网上別的商家购 买，仅需点击几下智能手机或平板电脑就能完成网上支付。这样的消费行为称作“移动展厅现象”，而这种消费行为已经对线下零售商构成了严重的威胁。有关“移动展厅现象”的学术研究仍处于初級阶段。本研究将探讨以下两个课题。通过移动技术来实现的比价软件会如何影响消费行为，即如何影响消费者在网上购买还是在实体店购买的決定？当网络零售商利用新的科技和线下零售商进行竞争的时候，什么是新的市场均衡？ 要回答第一个研究课题，本研究会建立一个包含科技，经济和个人行为三種因素的 理論模型来解释消费者购买行为。科技因素包含在实体店购物时的价格对比，了解商品信息，和移动支付。经济因素包含价格多元化和产品分类。行为因素包含對商品需求的紧迫性和消费者对价格的敏感性。要回答第二个研究课题，我们将会寻求线下零售商可以使用的策略﹐以减轻来自比價软件的威胁。同时我们会检验这些策略在不同产品和价位上的表现。如果可以收集到数据，我们还会了解不同策略之间的互补性和替代性。 本研究对信息系统学科的贡献在于找出对消费者购买行为有重要影响的系统特征。此外，它对电子商务的学術贡献在于结合科技，经济和行为三種因素来解释消费者购买行为。通过寻求线下零售商可以使用的策略以减轻来自比價软件的威胁，这项研究还对零售业学科也有所贡献。

16504614.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504614.value: We explore how people balance their needs to belong and to be different from their friends by studying their choices of a virtual-house wall color on a leading Chinese social networking site. While learning about the most popular color among a user’s friends generally increases the likelihood for the user to adopt that color, conformity first decreases and then increases with the adoption rate of that choice, which ranges from 50% to 100%. In addition, users who are minority, newer, or of lower social-economic status are more likely to conform upon learning about the popular choice. While a large literature on social influences has documented conformity under normative influences, few studies have examined the impact of the popularity of a choice on conformity. Our large-scale field experiment on a leading Chinese social networking site suggests that conformity to a popular neutral choice among a user’s friends may first decrease and then increase with the adoption rate of that choice. Our research suggests that it is not necessarily true that a more popular choice will always be better received, at least in the context of online social networks. Instead, an intermediate adoption rate such as 55% may lead to even more conversion than an adoption rate such as 80%. Our findings suggest that users carefully trade off their needs to belong to their social circles and at the same time to maintain their individuality. In addition, users of weaker status have a stronger propensity to conform, indicating that such users may have a strong need to earn a sense of belonging in their online social networks.

16504614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504614.value: In the future, the research can be carried out to compare people from different cultural backgrounds and see if they may react to comformity pressure differently.

16504614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504614.value: In recent years, normative advertising campaigns have seen increasing popularity in the field of marketing, and they often prominently show the adoption rate of the desired behavior with the hope that people will conform to the desired behavior. For example, Dartmouth advertises that 74% of Dartmouth drinkers have fewer than four drinks on the average Friday night and Sensodyne advertises that 9 out of 10 dentists recommend their toothpaste. Our findings suggest that designers of such campaigns need to be mindful of the strength of the norm and the characteristics of the target audience. In general, our findings helps the general public to understand how the average person trades off the need to belong and the need to be an individual in his social network and what factors may affect this tradeoff.

16504914.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16504914.value: 考虑补货时间的可替换产品存货管理问题

16504914.label: Project Objectives
16504914.value: To study the structural properties of the optimal objective function and optimal replenishment and substitution policies for the inventory system with two substitutable products, assuming that the replenishment lead times are positive and the replenishment capacities are constrained; To develop efficient heuristics for determining sub-optimal policies for the system.
rows: To study the structural properties of the optimal objective function and optimal replenishment and substitution policies for the inventory system with two substitutable products, assuming that the replenishment lead times are positive and the replenishment capacities are constrained;
To develop efficient heuristics for determining sub-optimal policies for the system.

16504914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504914.value: Ever increasing competition in the global market requires firms to offer better services to customers at lower prices. This trend presents new challenges to supply chain management. Substitution is a useful option for managing end-product inventories: when demand for a certain type of product exceeds supply, another type of products (often one of a higher grade in terms of quality or functionality), can be used as a substitute to supply the demand. In the literature, much research has been done on optimal control of inventory systems with substitutable products. Most of the research focuses on single-period problems, while a limited number of publications address multiple-period problems. To the best of our knowledge, they all assume zero replenishment lead times. For non-substitutable products, there is technically no difference between a system with constant lead time and a system with zero time. But for substitutable products, it is much more challenging analytically and much more difficult computationally for the systems with positive lead times, since the substitution decision and replenishment decision will interplay, and the substitution decision needs to take into account the information on all outstanding orders (thus making the state space multi-dimensional). In this project, we study the management problem in both finite and infinite horizon for an inventory system with two substitutable products, assuming that for both products, replenishments are constrained by supply capacities, and the replenishment lead times are positive. We aim to characterize the structures of the optimal replenishment and substitution policy, and to develop efficient approaches for determining optimal / sub-optimal policies based on said structures.

16504914.label: Realisation of objectives
16504914.value: We have fully realized the objectives of the project. First, we studied an inventory system with flexible substitution: the firm may decide what prices or discount levels to be offered to customers while customers may decide whether to accept the offers. This way, substitution is the result of interactions between the firm and the customer. We derived the optimal policy for inventory replenishment and for pricing of substitution, and obtained useful managerial insights. The results are published in a paper in "Production and Operations Management". Second, we studied an inventory system of two products with possible downward substitution, assuming that the replenishment lead time are positive and the replenishment capacities are constrained. We derived various structural properties of the optimal replenishment and substitution policy. The results are reported in the paper currently under review with "Operations Research" (in the final stage, with minor revision).
