16504914.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504914.value: We study a two-product inventory model that allows substitution. Both products can be used to supply demand over a selling season of N periods, with a one-time replenishment opportunity at the beginning of the season. A substitution could be offered even when the demanded product is available. The substitution rule is flexible in the sense that the seller can choose whether or not to offer substitution and at what price or discount level, and the customer may or may not accept the offer, with the acceptance probability being a decreasing function of the substitution price. The decisions are the replenishment quantities at the beginning of the season, and the dynamic substitution-pricing policy in each period of the season. Using a stochastic dynamic programming approach, we present a complete solution to the problem. Furthermore we show that the objective function is concave and submodular in the inventory levels --- structural properties that facilitate the solution procedure and help identify threshold policies for the optimal substitution/pricing decisions. Finally, with a state transformation we also show that the objective function is L-natural-concave, which allows us to derive similar structural properties of the optimal policy for multiple-season problems. We also study a periodic-review inventory system of two products with positive replenishment lead times, assuming that downward substitution is allowed and that replenishment is capped. We aim to characterize the structures of the optimal policies for product replenishment and substitution that minimizes the expected total discounted cost over a finite horizon. With a Markovian decision programming formulation and an appropriate relaxation of constraints on the substitution quantity, we show that the objective function is L-natural-convex. We then explore various structural properties of the optimal policy through sensitivity analysis. In particular, we prove that the optimal replenishment quantities and the substitution quantity are all monotone in on-hand inventories and each outstanding order, which leads to an optimal policy with a switching surface structure.

16504914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504914.value: In our project we focus on inventory systems with two products. Related results may help to develop effective heuristic for general m product problems, which could be our future research work.

16504914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504914.value: Ever increasing competition in the global market requires firms to offer better services to customers at lower prices. This trend presents new challenges to the firm's supply chain management. Substitution is a useful option of recourse for managing end-product inventories: when demand for a certain type of product exceeds supply, another type of products (often one of a higher grade in terms of quality or functionality), can be used as a substitute to supply the demand. In this project, we study the optimal control problem of a periodic review inventory system with substitutable products. We focus on the impacts of replenishment lead times and pricing of substitution. Our results provide useful insight and efficient strategies to help firms manage inventory replenishment and allocation of substitutable products, which is of practical importance in supply chain management, and also contribute to the literature on supply chains management by solving a theoretically challenging problem.

16505014.label: Project Objectives

Design the experiment, including different treatments, to test our basic hypothesis indicated above.

16505014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505014.value: Nominal rigidity is widely observed. Yet, it is hard to explain if one insists that (i) people be rational, (ii) nominal shocks be public information, and (iii) the physical costs to adjust prices be negligible. With these three assumptions, the flexible-price equilibrium, one in which prices fully respond to the nominal shocks, ought to exist in any plausible model. Although sticky-price equilibria, those in which prices sluggishly or do not fully respond to the nominal shocks, may coexist, it is not obvious why people may select some sticky-price equilibrium over the flexible-price equilibrium. We take an experimental approach to study nominal rigidity. In particular, we are interested in seeking whether some behavioral tendency would make some sticky-price equilibrium more likely to emerge than the flexible-price equilibrium. Our basic hypothesis is as follows. In an environment with multiple equilibria, it is a nontrivial task for people to coordinate to play a certain equilibrium. Since coordination failure in general is costly, people may form some behavioral tendency to avoid it; we purport that people may use what they did in the past for coordination. Given such a tendency, they may tend to stick to the previous price following a nominal shock because the previous price serves as the present coordination device. The project will test this hypothesis through experiments. This project will contribute to better understanding of nominal rigidity. Such understanding, in turn, may help to evaluate monetary policy which is typically built on the assumption that prices are rigid. 名义价格剛性是被普遍觀察到的。然而，名义价格這是很難解釋的，如果我们堅持認為（一）人是理性的， （二）货币衝擊是公共信息，及（iii ）調整價格的物理成本可以忽略不計。在這三個假設之下，弹性價格均衡，也就是價格充分反应货币衝擊的均衡，應该总是在任何合理的模型里存在的。雖然粘性價格均衡，也就是價格緩慢或不完全的反应货币冲击的均衡，可以和弹性價格均衡共同存在于模型中，但是需要解释的是為什麼社会會選擇粘性價格均衡而不是弹性價格均衡。 我們採取的實驗方法來研究名义价格剛性。我們感興趣的是探索人是否有一种行為傾向使得他更倾向选择粘性價格均衡而不是弹性價格均衡。我們的基本假設如下。在多重均衡的環境中，人们進行協調以达到一个特定的均衡是一個有意義的任務，因為一般來說協調失敗对人们来说是有成本的。人們因此可能會形成一些行為傾向，以避免它協調失敗。我們认为，人們很可能有使用他們在過去的行为来进行協調的倾向。给定這種行为倾向，在面临货币衝擊是他們可能傾向於堅持以前的價格，因為以前的價格是作為當前協調的工具。該个研究項目將通過實驗驗證這一假設。 該項目將有助於更好地了解名义价格剛剛性。这种理解可能有助於評估通常建立在假設價格是剛性的貨幣政策。

16505014.label: Realisation of objectives
16505014.value: For objective 1, we found that the basic model in our proposal was sufficient for our purpose and we didn't change that. To compare the experiment data with the model's predication, we developed a program that is capable of computing all symmetric equilibria in parameterized versions. For objective 2, we started with some small-scale tests. After those tests, we determined the parameters in the main treatments. In the way to run the main treatments, we also developed some robustness treatments that may provide supportive evidences for our explanations to findings from the main treatments. Objective 3 was carried over gradually in the three-year duration. After completing some treatments, we spent time to analyze the data to decide whether we should proceed to the subsequent treatments as planned or we should fine-tune some parameters. For objective 4, we analyzed the experimental data before and after the project was complete. The data set is large. We manage to sort out some interesting patterns of behaviors; see the main findings in section 6.1. In summary, we have realized all objects listed in the proposal.

16505014.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505014.value: Neutrality of money has been a well-established proposition in economics at least since Hume. In a lab environment, we find that on nominal rigidity presents right after money is injected in the way that satisfies the sufficient conditions for the neutrality proposition. But nominal rigidity quickly vanishes and, in fact, not only the aggregate price but the distribution of prices move according to the neutrality proposition. Neutrality, however, may not hold on a disaggregated level. When the market is frictional, there is a payoff-relevant pricing bias before a nominal shock: a substantial number of sellers systematically set their prices above or below the average. Also, there is a payoff-relevant pricing bias after the shock: within a group of sellers who share the same pre-shock pricing pattern, a substantial number of sellers systematically change their prices more or less than the increase in the number of tokens. So, in particular, neutrality obtained at the aggregation level is not because of random errors offsetting each other but because of systematic errors offsetting each other. Why is the market friction critical for nonneutrality on the disaggregated level? In the presence of the friction, sellers in the lab post different prices and are aware of the tradeoff between a higher price and a higher expected transaction cost, as sellers in the model in a mixed-strategy equilibrium. But subjects do not seem to have a cognitive capacity to play a mixed-strategy equilibrium. A seller in the lab appears to choose a price from those perceived optimal by her before a shock and a change in the price from those perceived optimal after. There seems no strong reason for her to choose the change proportional to the change in the number of tokens. While our lab environment is special, it captures a feature of the real trading process, that is, a higher price may be offset by a higher trading cost. In a real environment with this feature, a person may perceive some prices as optimal (even though it is likely that none of these prices is actually optimal) and, therefore, a change in the nominal shock goes beyond nominal because she may see more than one change in the price optimal.

16505014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505014.value: One potential development is to add some noise in the money injection: some people would receive more and some less. The noise needs not to be large but it may have profound influences for real people. We intend to apply for a grant from RGC in the future to carry out the research in this line.

16505014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505014.value: A central bank’s action may have far more complicate implications than what may have been thought. Even when the money-printing machine doubles everyone’s pocket, the influence may go beyond doubling prices. For, some people may raise prices less and other more provided that there are perceived tradeoffs between higher prices and higher trading costs. For the public’s interest, the central bank should therefore to carefully choose its actions.

17100014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100014.value: Reef building corals host a diversity of endosymbiotic dinoflagellates of the Genus Symbiodinium. These symbionts are vital to the health and productivity of coral reefs worldwide, as they confer key biogeochemical functions to the coral holobiont via photoautotrophy. In addition to fixed carbon subsidies, Symbiodinium translocate fixed nitrogen in the form of free amino acids to their hosts. The latter may be the mechanism by which corals achieve high rates of productivity and have come to dominate oligotrophic marine “deserts” over deep time. To date, the physiological underpinnings and ecological significance of nitrogen metabolism across the diversity of Symbiodinium are poorly understood. Much like terrestrial plant communities, coral-hosted Symbiodinium may compete for limited nitrogen resources inside the host “habitat”. Thus, competition between symbiont genotypes may lead to succession within the host, therefore explaining the observation that most corals host a single Symbiodinium clade. I predict that this process is governed by variables involved in plant metabolism, namely nitrogen availability, light, and temperature. Here, I propose to test the resource-ratio hypothesis (sensu Tilman) in the Symbiodinium system. By coupling continuous culture techniques (bioreactor) with classic ecological designs (competition & common garden experiments) and advanced quantitative techniques (flow cytometry, qPCR, stable isotope tracers) I will quantify the environmental conditions under which 1) specific Symbiodinium genotypes dominate conspecifics and 2) stable co-existence is maintained. These data can be used to parameterize ecological models to describe the patterns of Symbiodinium distributions in nature, and will inform our understanding of how coral-algal associations may vary in an era of rapid global change. 蟲黃藻，又稱共生藻，是一種存於造礁珊瑚組織的內胚層的單細胞腰鞭毛藻。共生藻在珊瑚蟲細胞內進行光合作用，為宿主珊瑚提供成長所需要的營養和能源。除了加速有機碳循環，共生藻亦會進行固氮作用，提供氮之化合物 – 胺基酸給宿主珊瑚。這種作用機制令造礁珊瑚能在貧營養性的水域中生存，亦是促成珊瑚礁生態系統的高生產力的主要原因。可是，共生藻系群間的氮素代謝之潛力與功能尚不明確。有如植物群落的發展變化過程，共生藻生長由生境中最稀少的必需資源所決定，在珊瑚宿主有限的氮供應下，共生藻系群之間可能因競爭共同的資源而發生排除及演替，導致大部分石珊瑚只具有單一系群的共生藻。這個競爭過程受植物代謝作用的限制，取決於氮供應、光線、溫度等關鍵因素。在此，我們套用資源比例假說(Tilman 1985)，結合連續培養技術、傳統生態設計 (競爭、同質園實驗) 以及高級計量方法 (流式細胞術、定量即時聚合酶鏈鎖反應、穩定同位素)，以量化環境因素，闡明共生藻在宿主珊瑚內的群落結構: 1) 單一共生藻系支配; 2) 共生藻系群穩定共存。本項目通過以上的實驗和數據分析，從而參數生態模型來研判共生藻的自然界中的分布，了解共生藻對造礁石珊瑚和珊瑚礁在全球氣候變遷下的影響和適應機制。

17100214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100214.value: The discovery of experimentally derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) has fostered prospects of patient-specific cell replacement therapies, novel toxicology and drug screening assays, and informative cell models for understanding disease pathogenesis. The latter is particularly valuable to the study of human syndromes caused by gene defects where animal models are lacking or inadequately mimic the human condition. One such vascular variant is Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS), a heritable disease of connective tissues involving collagen types COL5A, COL3A, tenascin-X, and to a lesser extent COL1A, lysyl hydroxlase and ADAM metallopeptidase. Among the six major types, the vascular form of EDS (vEDS) is the most severe. It results principally from mutations in the collagen III, alpha 1 (COL3A1) gene and is thought to cause aberrant collagen fibrillogenesis. These mutations contribute to catastrophic ruptures of large arteries, strokes, pregnancy-related mortalities, and pre-mature death among young adults. The presentation of this disease is heterogeneous, even among patients with the same gene mutation, and it remains unclear why some individuals exhibit severe phenotypes while others do not. In mouse models, COL3A1 deficiency mostly produces a weak disease variant without vascular ruptures, while a spontaneous COL3A1 mutation that leads to vascular defects lacks important disease features found in humans. Currently, there are no adequate therapeutic treatments. To determine how COL3A1 mutations lead to vEDS, we propose to examine and exploit a human cell model of this disease using iPSC lines derived from fibroblasts obtained from two probands. We will correct the Col3A1 gene mutations with TALENs to ensure against phenotypic iPSC variability and determine the principal source of COL3A1 secretion from iPSC-derived vascular progeny. We will examine basic growth characteristics and functional properties of these cells as well as determine the effects of doxycycline on collagen and matrix metalloproteinase synthesis (RNA and protein), stability or activity. By establishing high quality, experimentally confirmed iPSC vascular progeny, this study should lead directly to the development of reliable human tissue models of vEDS suitable for examining the effects of COL3A1 mutations on vasculogenesis and vascular integrity as well as establish a reliable system to test for possible therapeutic (pharmacological or regenerative) interventions.

17100214.label: Realisation of objectives
17100214.value: The goals of this program were completed with only minor modifications from the originally planned experiments. For Aim 1, we have successfully created a series of hiPSC lines from fibroblast obtained from normal and vEDS patients. These lines have been fully characterized and have been made available to the public (particularly for lines i057, i095 and i097). More specifically, several clones for G252V (i095), 2553 mutation (i097) and normal (i057) have been characterized based on the absence of Sendai virus, the presence of pluripotency gene transcripts (Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, Rex1, and others) and surface proteins (SSEA4, Tra-160). We were able to differentiate these cells into cells from all three germ layer lineages (endoderm, ectoderm and mesoderm). The COL3A1 mutations in the hiPSC were also sequenced and confirmed. The derivation of these lines initially took longer than expected due to the need to passage the lines up to 28 times to get rid of the residual Sendai virus; however, when we switched to an updated version of Sendai virus, the i097 clones were obtained between passages 10 and 15. Subsequent clonal analyses (PCR, Western, immunostaining, in vitro differentiation and genomic integrity - karyotyping) showed that these lines were all viable and passed quality control. All hiPSC clones from normal or diseased fibroblasts readily produced teratomas that developed cells from all three germ layers. Based on these analyses, a few sub-clones were excluded from subsequent analyses due to the prevalence of endoderm and mesodermal formation over that of ectoderm. This deviation from the expected values led to their exclusion; however, since we had selected >10 clones for each line, we readily found very high quality hiPSCs lines that contained distinct mutations in the COL3A1 gene. For aim 2, and as described in our interim report, we switched from the TALEN mediated gene correction technologies to Crispr/Cas9 mediated gene corrections. Using this approach, we successfully created Crispr/Cas9 gene corrected mutants for line i0195 and i0197. Most of our subsequent analyses focused on i0195, as it had a severe phenotype in the patient. These lines were characterized as described (PCR, Western, immunostaining, in vitro differentiation, and corrected DNA sequences were confirmed by sequencing). All lines were positive for pluripotency markers: Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, but when differentiated, these markers were lost as a function of time. Concomitantly, markers of differentiation were up-regulated. The lines appeared to be normal in terms of function and differentiation potential, and these lines were used in the experiments described under aim 3 as planned. However, after the completion of this project and after the end of the funding period, exonic sequencing reactions were performed because of more recent reports stating that Crispr/Cas9 mediated gene corrections could lead to unanticipated off target effects. These sequencing reactions were performed in addition to those performed earlier during the course of the study looking at sites that may have had off-site target effects as predicted by the software available from MIT for Crispr/Cas9 primer designs. The sequencing led to an identification of an ~300 bp deletion (off-target effect) that partially affected a coding sequence of a gene implicated in apoptosis. We believe this mutation was generated during the construction of this line. We have therefore gone back to some of the original selected i0195 clones to identify sub clones that lacked this deletion. Because of this unexpected finding (and one that was not identified from the initial characterizations), we felt is necessary to re-confirm some of our findings. The mutation is NOT in a gene region that should affect cell differentiation; however, it may have affected some of our results related to apoptosis/cell death. For this reason, we delayed submission of a third manuscript until we could confirm the results from this clone. For Aim 3, we differentiated the diseased and normal hiPSC lines into endothelial cells (using a modified protocol from what we originally proposed), vascular smooth muscle cells (Paraxial and lateral plate mesoderm, and neuroectodermal origin), fibroblasts and other cells present in the 3 germ layers. We also differentiated the hiPSC lines to mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs); however, we found that these cells did not fully recapitulate the normal phenotypes of MSCs, derived directly from patients. Given that the basic properties of these cells differed from what was anticipated, we de-emphasized this one aspect of the grant and focused primarily on fibroblasts and vSMCs. The in vitro differentiation capacities of the various hiPSC lines did NOT differ significantly among the lines There were some minor differences in the timing and efficacy of differentiation; however, this appeared to be more a property of hiPSC variability than anything directly related to the COL3A1 mutations. In fact, some of the Crispr/Cas9 corrected lines had more problems with differentiation than either the normal or mutant parental lines. Upon differentiation, we learned that endothelial cells (ECs) produce very limited amounts of collagen relative to either the vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs) or the fibroblasts (FBs). Cell death (apoptosis) and viability (MTT assays, as well as neutral Red assays) were NOT affected by the presence of COL3A1 mutations in any of the fibroblasts or vSMCs (all 3 lineages) analyzed. When we examined collagen fibril formation using a hyperplasia model of fibrosis, we observed differences in collagen fibril thickness, deposition and quantity (using scanning electron microscopy as well as by Western and other assays). These differences were most readily observed when ascorbic acid was added to the culture medium to improve cross-linking of the fibrils. Unexpectedly, the addition of TGFb1, which increased fibrosis in the hyperplasia model, did not lead to any major changes in cell viability or apoptosis. After addition of a number of other TGFb1 inhibitors and performance of dose response curve analyses, we ultimately concluded that TGFb1 (or b3) are not actively involved in the signaling mechanisms that exacerbate the pathophysiology of vEDS. Based on these results, we began to create 3D micro tissue models to examine the effects of stress and strain on the strength/stiffness and function of these constructs. For these experiments, which were not proposed in the original application, we used human collagen, fibrin and other substrates to create the micro tissues. This model was used to better model the disease process and to develop a system that can be used to monitor drug interventions. During the course of these studies, we could not identify any major cell autonomous event that may contribute to the progression of vEDS - save one. Very specifically, we identified changes in the gene expression and presence of integrins on the vSMCs and fibroblasts from mutant hiPSCs. These differences were not observed in the Crispr/Cas9 corrected clones, which has led us to postulate that an innate problem of vEDS is associated with the connections between cells and the ECM that cause integrin defects in connection. We are now following up these results to identify how changes in integrins may be responsible for the localized aneurisms and dissections using the 3D micro tissue models. Finally, we also used microRNA based techniques to try to knockdown the defective gene transcripts in these lines; however, this methodology proved to be ineffective. Although it was not part of the original grant, this approach seemed likely to lead to some potential clinical applications, which were ultimately abandoned.

17100214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100214.value: The major findings of this research project include: 1) Generation and characterization of human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) lines from normal and diseased patients with vascular Ehlers-Dalos Syndrome (vEDS). 2) Generation and characterization of Crispr/Cas9 edited and gene corrected mutations from the hiPSCs derived from these patients. Although the gene corrections were verified by sequencing, subsequent publications indicated that the frequency of off-target effects by Crispr/Cas9 gene corrections was higher than originally postulated. From subsequent exonic sequencing, we determined that the i0195 line contained a deletion (unexpected) that may have adversely affected result outcomes. The identification of other gene edited lines without the COL3A1 mutation and which lack other gene mutations/deletions was initiated at the end of this project to reconfirm the results and ensure that our findings were not due to this unexpected mutation. 3) The major sources for collagen 3, type A1 (COL3A1) were found to be from fibroblasts and from vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs). Cell types, like endothelial cells, produced very little COL3A1. 4) The COL3A1 mutant versus control hiPSC derived progeny did not show significant differences in the spontaneous rate of apoptosis, viability or general functional properties. 5) Unexpectedly, we found cell intrinsic differences associated with the presence of integrin molecules (in quantity and types) on fibroblasts and vSMCs, suggesting that defects in the extracellular matrix (ECM) composition caused by COL3A1 mutations lead to cellular modifications that likely contribute to the disease process. 6) TGF-beta could induce a hyperplasia model that improved collagen deposition; however, the fibrillar collagen structures did not differ very much between controls. Ascorbic acid was required for improved collagen production and deposition, but it did not have major differences between normal and mutant lines. 7) Based on scanning electron microscopy, we determined that defects in the structure of fibrillar collagen was preferentially affected by COL3A1 mutations that caused premature termination. For point mutations, the structures only showed trends in defects. It was unclear why the latter was found, but since the mutation is a dominant negative, the fibrillar collagen deposited on the cell plates may have been representative of mostly normal collagen fibrils. 8) Collagen RNA and proteins levels differed significantly between one mutant and normal hiPSCs. Of greatest significance was the finding that COL3A1 mutations could elicit changes in cellular integrin production and distribution in fibroblasts and vSMCs, suggesting that altered ECM contributed to cellular defects in adhesion and junctional protein interactions.

17100214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100214.value: Using the hiPSC lines that we have developed, we have begun a cooperative research program with a laboratory at Johns Hopkins University, USA to 1) Develop a new microtissue-based test-bed for assessing the role of mechanics on the structure and function of human cells and tissues. 2) Integrate the mechanical testing and dynamic stimulation into a single, conveniently used platform for efficient study and screening of small tissue constructs. 3) Develop predictive models of functionality and mechanics based on precisely defined, heterotypic iPSC- derived constructs that are fully of human origin. 4) Advance the engineering of heterotypic tissues possessing the full array of biomechanical attributes and signaling typical of native vessels. 5) Improve in vitro pharmacological and small molecule testing approaches for bioengineered tissues and mechanically-compromised diseases. These studies are being performed with funding that has been obtained in the U.S.A. and a collaborative group has developed to foster improved studies of vEDS with the goal of improving our general understanding of disease progression and ultimately in identifying possible treatments to improve the outcomes of patients with this disease.

17100214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100214.value: Researchers at The University of Hong Kong have developed new human model systems (induced pluripotent stem cell lines) that can be utilized to study the basic biology of vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome. Together with gene corrected control lines, these researchers have confirmed that mutations in the gene, COL3A1, adversely affect fibrillar collagen synthesis and deposition, and have confirmed that the major source of this extracellular matrix component is fibroblasts and vascular smooth muscle cells. The model also led to the novel finding that these gene mutations lead to changes in the proteins responsible for the attachments of cells to the extracellular matrix. These protein changes likely affect tissue strength and structural integrity, a finding that is now being exploited to model the disease process using three-dimensional tissue constructs.

17100314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100314.value: In Hong Kong, 71% of older adults have or require prostheses for the replacement of missing teeth. Such replacement is considered important by patients to improve aesthetics, function and quality of life. Tooth replacement is therefore a significant issue in Hong Kong and while dental implants and conventional bridges have been used to replace missing teeth, dental implants are too expensive for many and conventional dental bridges are destructive to supporting tooth tissue. Resin-bonded bridges (RBBs) are a conservative and cost effective replacement option that involves minimal tooth preparation, leaving the majority of the tooth intact. They are secured in place with an adhesive cement, which is bonded to the outer enamel layer. Clinical audit of these prostheses at the University of Hong Kong shows two-unit RBBs to have some of the highest success rates in the dental literature for the replacement of missing premolar and incisor teeth. However, for the replacement of molar teeth, two-unit RBBs are not performed, as established protocol and recognised texts contraindicate their use due to concerns with tipping or drifting of supporting teeth. Replacement of a single missing molar tooth can be with a three-unit, fixed-fixed (single-piece casting) or three-unit, fixed-movable (two-part casting). However, the fixed-fixed option has a higher debond failure rate than two-unit RBBs and therefore, at this centre, a modified, 3-unit fixed-movable design is used. This two-part casting allows for minor, independent movements of the supporting teeth and thereby aims to reduce stresses between them and, similarly, reduce de-bonding forces. This has the potential for greater longevity and easier long-term maintenance as if the major part of the bridge debonds it can be recemented. The aim of this unique study is to compare 2-unit and 3-unit RBBs for the replacement of single missing molar tooth in a randomized clinical trial. These two designs will be clinically evaluated every 6 months to observe the outcome measures. The primary outcome will examine the success of the dental prostheses with respects to the need of any clinical intervention to repair or remediate the RBB or supporting tooth. Minor outcome measures will examine fatigue or damage to the prosthesis, changes in bone support, pulpal or periodontal health or tooth mobility. Patient satisfaction and quality of life evaluation of the dental prostheses will also be examined. Will 2-unit RBBs offer patients a simpler, cheaper, and successful option over current designs? This has not been previously reported.

17100314.label: Realisation of objectives
17100314.value: This project has been suitably registered - https://clinicaltrials.gov/ NCT02239718. It has met and exceeded many of the required objectives. In particular we recruited 78 patients which was more than the 60 planned. Also these were obtained all from one centre in HK. We placed a total of 92 dental bridges which was similarly more than planned. Patients have been followed up for 36 months and will continue to be followed up for longer term data presentation. We have presented these findings at a 6 different regional and international dental research conferences at the International Association of Dental Research conferences. In Total 6 different abstracts presenting the different data outcomes and at different time periods have been disseminated. Currently a final research publication is being completed for submission to a top 10 dental journal. This publication has now only had sufficient longevity of data to make it suitable for publication. It is not usual to publish clinical trials below 3 years of data. No difference between the two test groups were observed for the primary and secondary outcomes at any of the time intervals that they were reviewed at. The simpler design of the 2-unit RBB is as successful at the traditional 3-unit design. Longer term data collection will be followed up This will become the standard in treatment for replacing missing molars 8-10 mm in length in the future.

17100314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100314.value: This highly significant research is the first of its kind to challenge the dogmatic belief that two-unit cantilever bridges cannot be used to replace missing posterior teeth. This study adopted the use of resin-bonded bridges comparing two designs, one three-unit fixed movable and the other two-unit cantilever for the replacement of missing molars 8-10 mm in length span. 78 patients were treated between the two groups which is above the number of 60 set as a target. In total 92 prostheses were provided between the two groups. Clinical outcomes determined that there was no significant difference in the success, retention and surfival rates between these two treatments over the course of the different evaluation periods from 6, 12, 24 and 36 months. The two-unit RBBs did not move or tip and did not experience any difference in mobility compared to the thee-unit designs. Patients differentiated no difference in their satisfaction (14-item questionnaire) or in oral health quality of life (OHIP-49) This study demonstrated that two-unit RBBs are a successful treatment option over the short term of this evaluation period and not different to the more traditional three-unit design. The impact of this is that the two-unit design will be easier and simpler for dentists to prepare and cement. For the patient it will have a lower treatment cost and be easier to clean. This will mean it is a simpler, easier, faster, cheaper and better treatment option for patients who want to have missing teeth replaced.

17100314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100314.value: Longer term these two cohorts will be followed up to determine if there are any differences between in the long-term. The next target will be 5 years and ultimately 10 years. Possible further research will be undertaken, to consider alternative tooth preparation designs for two-unit Cantilever RBBs examining how to do less tooth preparation.

17100314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100314.value: This project has successfully shown that in the short-term (up to 3-years), there is no difference in the clinical success and clinical outcomes of the 2-unit or 3-unit resin-bonded bridges. Both treatments were perceived to be similar to patients based on their satisfaction and with regards to the impact on their quality of life. Given the lack of difference in the two treatment outcomes we can now offer this treatment option to patients that means they are easier and simpler for dentists to prepare and fit and for patients the treatment will be more cost-effective and easier to clean.

17100414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100414.value: Background: Problem-based learning (PBL) is a recognised instructional method and, to a lesser extent, approach to curriculum design in higher education that aligns university learning experiences with the real life professional work students undertake on graduation. PBL is seen as mirroring and supporting both clinical reasoning and scientific research processes with recent syntheses of meta-analyses of studies establishing that PBL programs are consequential to student learning across disciplinary knowledge, skills and attitudes. PBL remains current and is adapting to 21st Century, net-gen learners through the introduction of educational technologies. Applications include enhancing rich PBL problems/cases in virtual and blended spaces and developing multimedia for self-directed learning. PBL researchers in higher education see an imperative to move beyond research designs using survey-based perception studies towards research studies addressing questions such as ‘how’ PBL is consequential to inquiry-based learning as it unfolds over time. Research into PBL and educational technologies, however, remains limited in scope and scale. The application of an Interactional Ethnography (IE) will address both issues. Materials and Methods: Three foundational undergraduate PBL healthcare programmes form a case study design addressing: 1. How and when are educational technologies used in and across PBL learning contexts? 2. What do the multiple members of the PBL learning community count as evidence of using educational technologies in learning within and across curriculum contexts, specifically from PBL tutorials to case-based clinical discussions? 3. How are these members’ beliefs and practices of using educational technologies situated in relation to past and current educational theories? Data collection will be across learning events and contexts (from junior PBL tutorials and self-directed learning to senior case-based discussions); the various participants involved (undergraduate students and facilitators); and across time (2 years). Purposeful sampling across three curricula will include consenting participants from PBL (Yr1-2) and clinical (Yr 3-5) groups (~180 students; 36 facilitators). IE analysis of the protected, searchable data-base of recordings will examine how new technologies may affect PBL tutorials and case-based clinical reasoning processes. Significance: The novel methodological application of IE will contribute to educational theories of situated learning in an information-rich age. It will address the practical issue of direct evidence of student learning with: a) an evidence base further examining “inside” the PBL process; and b) the impact of educational technologies on PBL curriculum design and enactment across curricula. It will provide clear guidance to students and facilitators on best practices in technology-enabled PBL. 背景：問題為本學習(PBL) 是一種被認可的教學方式， 而且在較小程度上，是在高等教育課程設計中所採取的一種方式。PBL把大學生的學習經驗配對到大學生畢業後在現實生活中從事的專業工作。 問題為本學習被視為可反映與支援臨床推斷與科學研究過程，原因是最近綜合各研究的整合分析，証明問題為本學習課程是因應學生學習跨學科的知識、 技巧、及態度而產生的。 問題為本學習與時並進，引入教育科技以融入廿一世紀， 迎合N世代學生。 教育科技的應用包括於虛擬與混合空間 (virtual and blended spaces) 增加問題為本學習中豐富的問題 / 病例與發展專為自我導向學習而設的多媒體資源。 在高等教育中研究問題為本學習的研究者認為，當務之急是要從基於調查的認知研究提升至解決一些問題，如問題為本學習將「如何」因應探究式學習(inquiry-based learning) 隨着時間發展而生? 然而，有關問題為本學習與教育科技的研究，在范圍及規模方面仍然很有限， 利用互動俗民誌則可解決這兩個問題。 材料及方法： 此硏究採用一個案例研究設計,案例由三個問題為本學習的基礎本科課程所組成, 目的在解決下列問題： • 教育科技是如何的和是在甚麽時候用在不同的問題為本學習環境裏? • 問題為本學習社群中的成員，認為要有甚麽證據，在單一或跨越課程領域內，或更具體地，由問題為本學習導至病例為本臨床討論，才足以証明教育科技對學習的影响，? • 怎樣把這些成員使用教育科技的信念與方式連繫到過去與現在的教育理論? 數據收集將橫跨學習活動與領域 (由低年級的問題為本學習導修班與自我導向學習至高年級的病例為本臨床討論) ， 涉及各種研究參加者 (本科生們與引導老師們) ，以及跨越時間 (兩年期間) 。 立意抽樣將橫跨三個課程包括同意參加研究的問題為本學習組 (一至二年級) 與臨床組 (三至五年級) 的參加者(約一百八十名學生名及三十六位引導老師)。 我們利用互動俗民誌來分析位於受保護並可檢索的數據庫中的錄音， 詳細分析新科技如何影響問題為本學習導修班與病例為本臨床推斷的過程。 重要性：互動俗民誌嶄新的應用方法將於這個資訊發達的年代， 為情境學習教育理論作出貢獻。 互動俗民誌將從以下兩方面解決有關直接證明學生學習的實際問題： (一) 進一步研究問題為本學習過程的實證基礎與 (二) 教育科技對跨課程的問題為本學習課程設計與制定的影響。 互動俗民誌將為學生與引導老師對科技輔助式問題為本學習最好的做法作出明確的指導。

17100414.label: Realisation of objectives
17100414.value: Objective 1) To investigate the use of educational technologies in PBL for situated, contextual learning in undergraduate clinical programs. This has been fully achieved with publications not only systematically mapping the technologies currently employed (Jin & Bridges, 2014) but also identifying the processes involved as the adoption of new technologies is reshaping learning processes in PBL curricula in health professions education (Hmelo-Silver, Bridges & McKeown, 2019). Objective 2) To document how such technologies can enhance deep learning and student engagement across formal and informal contexts and over time. This has been fully achieved through our building of an extensive archive of video recordings and related artefacts of PBL student learning in the health sciences. Video recordings across the three clinical programs have traced students over 2-4 years of their clinical programmes. The process of video archive building and the Interactional Ethnographic approach to interdisciplinary analysis has been reported widely and attracted international attention. Objective 3) To trace the consequential nature of the PBL knowledge construction process in the early years of the curriculum for case-based, clinical reasoning in later years of the curriculum. This has been conducted to the satisfaction of the grant but more work is being undertaken with the successful international recruitment of a Postdoctoral Fellow to conduct further analysis. Tracing the communicative processes across clinical tutorials revealed that the interactive and collaborative dialogues among the participants across contexts supported the development of clinical reasoning over a three-year period. Analysis of student discourse from earlier years in Dentistry showed that clinical knowledge discussed was consequential to building clinical reasoning in later years, leading to providing appropriate justification for diagnosis and recommendations for patient care in the final year of the program (Bridges, Botelho, Chian, 2019). Objective 4) To address the need to establish valid, systematic approaches to the collection of ‘direct evidence’ of student learning. The Interactional Ethnographic approach has provided a systematic framework for the collection and analysis of classroom videos and student-produced artefacts as a forms of ‘direct evidence’ of student learning (see Green & Bridges, 2018). Objective 5) To build a new theoretical framework for technologically enhanced PBL. Given their shared interest in the complexities of situated learning in inquiry-based designs, the project has also formed a key intersection between the field of the Learning Sciences and Interactional Ethnography (see Green & Bridges, 2018). The tracing of the unfolding knowledge co-construction processes across technology-rich PBL has illustrated how these processes are interactionally accomplished in and across intertextually tied events where devised, generated, accessed, curated and appropriated digital texts are connected in dialogic webs of meaning. Drawing upon the concepts of multimodality and intertextuality from literacy studies, we have proposed the concept of dialogic intervisualizing to theorize the new text-discourse relations evident in this study (Bridges et al, under review).

17100414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100414.value: Technology-enriched PBL has been creating new virtual and blended learning spaces across health professions education (Jin & Bridges, 2014). This Interactional Ethnography (IE) has moved the field beyond the predominant focus on survey-based perception studies to investigate the situated nature of learning. By examining learning processes in-situ through systematic collection and analysis of tutorial videos and associated artefacts, this IE study has addressed the issue of how educational technologies are consequential to inquiry-based learning processes, such as problem-based learning (PBL) as they unfold within and across learning events and contexts. Methodologically, the study has built one of the most extensive archives of video recordings and related artefacts of PBL student learning in undergraduate health professions education. Theoretically, the study has become central to the intersection of the fields of Interactional Ethnography and the Learning Sciences with arising publications re-examining the epistemological foundations of PBL and the role of multimodal texts, visualisations, and discourse in a technology-rich era of fluid modernity. Implications for practice have been evident disseminations across the professions in a Masterclass for PBL facilitators in Hong Kong. The original taxonomy of PBL facilitator goals and strategies (Hmelo-Silver & Barrows, 2006) has been updated to include project findings on technology-supported PBL facilitation when infusing technologies within the traditional, small‐group, face‐to‐face process of inquiry into the PBL cycle (Hmelo-Silver, Bridges & McKeown, 2019).

17100414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100414.value: The detailed ethnographic archive is a rich resource for ongoing analysis. PI Bridges with external advisor Green were successful in securing a Postdoctoral Fellowship post at The University of Hong Kong. The successful PDF (Dr Chian, University of California) took up post in 2018 and is undertaking ongoing analysis of the video records and archives. The PI Bridges and PDF Chian have secured funding for 4 scholarships under the “Laidlaw Undergraduates Research and Leadership Program” on the topic, “Transitions into professional practice”. The four scholars are being recruited from the health professions and teacher education to learn qualitative research methods and undertake interviews in 2019.

17100414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100414.value: This research closely studied how educational technologies enabled and enhanced the PBL curriculum designs and facilitation experiences of undergraduate students and tutors across three undergraduate health professions programmes (Medicine, Dentistry, Speech and Hearing). The integration of various educational technologies in different, problem-based learning contexts was documented longitudinally through collection of video recordings, learning artefacts and interviews over the course of three academic years. The video and audio recordings and project artefacts were systematically recorded and securely archived for discourse-based analyses. Key findings included identifying: new forms of technology-enhanced PBL designs; new student learning practices in accessing, curating and creating digital texts for deep approaches to learning; and new facilitation strategies to enhance students’ multimodal practices in inquiry-based learning. The study has, therefore, contributed new understandings as to the nuanced practices of effective technology-enhanced PBL knowledge construction processes in supporting clinical reasoning processes in health sciences education.

17100514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100514.value: The essential requirement of dentists is that they possess excellent hand-eye co-ordination skills necessary to carry out dental procedures in an efficient and accurate manner. This in itself produces an interesting conundrum for dental educationalists, as unlike other training courses, an appropriate practical skill level of a student must be achieved prior to graduation. Students start dental school with a variety of abilities of skill level, and it is the requirement of dental teachers to ensure every student reaches the necessary level of competence, ideally in the most efficient way. The majority of skill acquisition is carried out using phantom head simulators made of a dummy head with a set of plastic teeth, allowing the student to practice procedures in an ergonomic way similar to a ‘real’ dental setting. Disadvantages of such traditional methods involve the unrealistic nature of plastic teeth compared with natural teeth, the inability of the teacher to identify exactly when procedural errors have been made and restrictions in hours of equipment use. Dental virtual reality simulators have been used since the early 90’s. These are computerized simulators with inbuilt programmes, allowing dental students to carry out dental procedures manually, in their own time and can repeatedly carry out the same task. Such simulators allow dental supervisors to identify when mistakes have been made rather than assessing a final procedure, something very important in the process of motor skill learning. Studies have shown such simulators can be superior to traditional methods of teaching & learning in improving the efficiency of acquiring motor skills. The development of dental haptic simulators in the early 2000’s has been able to build on the success of dental simulators. Haptic simulators are virtual reality simulators with the added aspect of touch sensory feedback. This allows the dental student to sense the difference between decay and sound tooth for example when carrying out a preparation. Limited research has been carried out in medicine, especially laparoscopic surgery, and it has been shown that haptic training is a valuable training tool, resulting in improved results when compared to traditional methods. This series of studies plans to further research into haptic training in dentistry. Several dental schools have commenced using haptic simulators, but currently there is little or no evidence of their effectiveness in dental education, how they should be used or when in the dental curriculum they can be most effective. 在牙科學上，一個必備的要求：就是具備優越的眼手調節能力，以便精準地在程序上進行操作。學生必須具備一定的實踐能力方能畢業，而如何讓學子們擁有這樣的技長，是一個牙科教學上與眾不同的有趣難題。以最有效的方式讓原本技能參差不齊的學子，達到一定的水平是牙科學教師們的責任。通過由模擬人和塑膠牙齒組成的模擬幻像，學子得以掌握主要的操作技能並且能在有利、仿真度高工作環境下進行練習。這傳統教學方式的短處包括：仿真齒和人齒質地上的差距、教師們無法識別操作上的錯誤確切是在哪時候造成和模擬操作上的時間限制。 從上世紀90年代，牙科學的虛擬實境就開始被採用了。這電腦化的模擬系統讓牙科學子得以在閒餘時間，重複、動手進行牙醫學上單一的操作。這樣的模擬偏重在非最終的成果，使導師們知道：錯誤是大致哪一時段造成的。這是一個運動技能學習的重點。有研究顯示：模擬操作比傳統教學更能讓學子掌握動手技巧。觸覺模擬在這世紀初的發展延續了牙科模擬的成就，在虛擬實境的基礎上加上了觸覺模擬。這幫助學子在操作上進一步辨別蛀牙和健康牙齒。目前為止，在醫學上，尤以腹腔鏡的研究是有限的，與此同時，有報導顯示觸覺（虛擬）訓練是一個有價值的培訓器材。有了它，相比傳統教學，學子技能掌握更顯著。 這一系列的研究將著重要於牙醫學觸覺模擬上的訓練。迄今，已有數間牙科學院啟用觸覺模擬系統，但是這系統對牙科教學成效，何時以及如何將它派上用場的研究依就罕見或缺乏。

17100514.label: Realisation of objectives
17100514.value: Dental curricula need to ensure every student reaches the necessary level of clinical competence, ideally in the most efficient way. Traditionally, dental skill acquisition has mostly been acquired on ‘dummy’ phantom heads with a set of plastic teeth, allowing ergonomic practice similar to a ‘real’ dental setting. New virtual reality (VR) and 3D haptic simulators have been introduced to maximize psychomotor skill development. This GRF aimed to provide an evidence-base to advise on the ongoing implementation of 3D VR haptics in dental curricula. The cross-disciplinary team drew upon separate but complementary areas of research and pedagogic expertise to achieve transdisciplinary understandings as to how dental novices learn in 3D haptic environments and how this information can inform undergraduate curriculum design. A detailed literature review and international scoping survey of curriculum approaches to psychomotor skill development in dentistry determined that a very large variation currently exists worldwide with respect to the incorporation of virtual reality simulation into dental curricula and future planning to use haptic simulation. Virtual reality simulators are recognized as being useful to track an individual’s progress in skill development as well as aid the self-directed learning aspect of skill acquisition. Studies were conducted to identify the neurophysiological markers of psychomotor efficiency of simulated clinical dental performances and examine differences in neurophysiological markers of efficiency on 3D VR dental haptic simulators using EEG and functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) a non-invasive, non-ionizing optical neuroimaging measuring brain activation (cerebral cortex) as well as the Movement Specific Reinvestment Questionnaire (MSRS) to determine the propensity for an individual to reinvest in relation to movement. Finally, a learning analytics study of the virtual reality simulator hard drive data explored training effectiveness and approaches to skill development using VR haptic simulations. a) Assessment of residual attentional capacity differences between novices and experts. Having skilled and lesser-skilled dental practitioners’ complete representative clinical tasks affords the measurement of mechanisms that might mediate skilled performance (Ericcson, 2003). Specifically, with regard to the attentional demands of clinical tasks, electroencephalography (EEG) power spectral analysis of the higher frequency alpha bandwidth can provide insight (Smith et al., 1999). Alpha power in the region of the cerebral cortex associated with attentionally demanding verbal-analytical processing (left temporal region or T3) differentiates skilled from lesser-skilled rifle shooters (Haufler et al., 2000), and implies that skilled performers have higher residual attentional capacity. Interesting, alpha power in the region associated with visual-spatial processing (right temporal region or T4) did not discern skill level (Haufler et al., 2000). We recruited 17 dentists enrolled in postgraduate dental training programmes (skilled) and 18 first-year dental students (less-skilled) to complete a non-clinical and a clinical (amalgam removal) task on Simodont™ haptic virtual reality simulator. EEG recordings were taken of the T3 and T4 regions of the cerebral cortex and high frequency alpha power (10-12Hz) was analysed. Poor quality recordings were taken from 5 postgraduates and 6 undergraduates resulting in a sample size of 12 in each group. In the non-clinical task, no significant differences were found in high frequency alpha power at the T3 region (U = 62.00, z -.58, p = .56) or the T4 region (t(22) = -.99, p = .34). In the clinical task, high frequency alpha power was significant different at the T4 region (t(13.39) = -2.33, p = .04, d = .95) and approached significance at the T3 region with a moderate to large effect size (t(22) = -1.92, p = .07, d = .78). In both cases, alpha power tended to be higher for the more skilled dental practitioners than the lesser skilled dental students, which reflects more efficient cognitive processing (e.g., Haufler et al., 2000; Kerick et al., 2001). b) EEG study of novice versus expert performance and movement specific reinvestment. The analysis of differences between novices and skilled performers can provide construct validity for instruments in addition to providing insight into the particular characteristics of expertise. Thirty-five individuals took part in the study, comprising 18 ‘novice’ first-year dental students and 17 ‘experienced’ dentists. The novices had not started practical preclinical skills learning and were recruited from the dental student population of the University of Hong Kong. The experienced dentists were recruited from a local dental hospital and had on average 4.6 years of work experience. Participants completed a non-clinical (‘Doughnut’) and a clinical (‘Tooth’) task on the simulator. Results from this study showed a significant performance difference between the clinical and non-clinical tasks, with the experienced group demonstrating significantly better performance of the clinical task (MANOVA, p<0.05) and of the ‘container component’ of the non-clinical task (Mann Whitney-U p<0.05). Although a similar amount of tooth tissue was preserved by novice and experienced participants, experienced participants removed twice as much of the filling. The clear differentiation between more experienced dentists and novices suggests that the simulated tooth task may provide an effective representation of a clinical procedure. No differences in neural communication between the T3-Fz and T4-Fz regions of the brain were evident between the novice and experienced groups, or in relation to movement specific reinvestment. As the propensity for movement specific reinvestment increased, there was a significant reduction in performance, however, in two components of the non-clinical task. There were no such effects for the clinical task. c) fNIRS analysis of working memory and reinvestment. As noted in the annual progress report, this was a deviation from the original plan due to encouraging results utilizing the MSRS questionnaire amongst dental students. We used fNIRS to assess oxygen demands in 24 undergraduate dental students during 2 dental tasks (clinical, nonclinical) on a VR haptic simulator and the Movement-Specific Reinvestment Scale questionnaire to assess the students’ propensity to reinvest. Students with a high propensity for movement-specific reinvestment displayed significantly greater oxyhemoglobin demands in an area associated with working memory during the nonclinical task (Spearman correlation, rs=.49, P=.03). This small study presents neurological evidence suggesting that a higher propensity for conscious control of movements during dental procedures is associated with greater blood oxyhemoglobin demands in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), an area associated with working memory activity. d) Longitudinal study of student performance on dental VR simulators. The studies of dental students and their learning with haptic VR simulators indicated the importance of task complexity and verified the ability of haptic VR simulators to track individual psychomotor skill improvements over time. A study of the longitudinal tracking of student performance during simulated tasks examined their potential association with an objective assessment. Psychomotor skill testing using a VR haptic simulator was carried out four times over a fifteen-month period on a cohort of dental undergraduate students. The four VR test results were correlated with an operative dentistry course test conducted at the end of the course, i.e. second year, first semester. Over the period of the entire study (15 months), there was a significant improvement in the mean score from four of the haptic VR psychomotor skill tests (Repeated measures ANOVA, p<0.05) indicating that a dental haptic VR simulator has the ability to detect psychomotor skill changes in dental students. Class practical test results (pass/fail) did not significantly associate with VR simulator test scores at any of the four time points. Results from this longitudinal study over a fifteen-month period.

17100514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100514.value: The findings of the novice-expert EEG study suggested that skilled performers had greater residual attentional capacity at their disposal, than their more novice counterparts. Dental training and practice may reduce both the verbal-analytic and visual-spatial processing attentional demands associated with completing representative clinical tasks. In addition to demonstrating the ability of the Simodont to differentiate between experts and novices in terms of performance, the EEG study identified the potential for reinvestment to affect performance. The functional Near Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) study (Perry et al 2017) aimed to determine the potential relationship between the propensity to reinvest and blood flow to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortices of the brain indicated differences in patterns of oxygenated blood flow between individuals with high and low propensities to reinvest. A secondary aim was to determine the propensity to reinvest and performance during 2 dental tasks carried out using haptic VR simulators. Students with a high propensity for movement-specific reinvestment displayed significantly greater oxyhemoglobin demands in an area associated with working memory during the nonclinical task. This small-scale study suggests that neurophysiological differences are evident between high and low reinvesters during a dental VR task in terms of oxyhemoglobin demands in an area associated with working memory. For the longitudinal learning analytics study of hard drive data, over the 15 month period, there was a significant improvement in the mean score from four of the haptic VR psychomotor skill tests; however, class practical test results (pass/fail) did not significantly associate with VR simulator test scores at any of the four time points. Overall, the outcomes of this GRF study provided some early information showing differing trends in relation to skill acquisition and development from a novice to an experienced professional. The use of virtual reality simulation may provide learners with a different pathway of skill acquisition that is less reliant on ‘following rules’ and being bounded to achieve ‘perfection’, but rather allow learners to learn by making mistakes that have no consequence and provide a more ‘stress free’ learning environment.

17100514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100514.value: Our findings suggest that neurological differences between high and low reinvesters do potentially exist in the working memory region during dental tasks, but the DLPFC is used for many other brain processes and, as with many brain imaging techniques, it is difficult to localize the exact regions of the brain that are responding. Additionally, our sample size was small, and it was impossible to quantify. Further studies with larger sample sizes and providing additional quantification of each participant’s exact amount of prior experience with each dental task would provide invaluable evidence concerning the neurological and psychological processes underpinning dental procedures performed on a haptic VR simulator. As time for psychomotor skill training in health care becomes even more challenged and an increasingly more complex range of surgical skills is required in dentistry, it is likely that screening of not only innate technical abilities but also personality traits will increase. This study indicates the potential of MSRS as a useful additional screening tool to potentially allow the identification of individuals who may struggle to achieve predefined psychomotor skill levels in the allotted curriculum time, allowing individualized training pathways to be put in place earlier in the curriculum for such students. Overall, further work is needed to expand the research undertaken in this study to better understand how to create an ‘ideal’ learning environment for acquiring the psychomotor skills needed by a dentist.

17100514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100514.value: Traditionally, dental students commence clinical psychomotor training by learning on a mannikin or ‘phantom’ head which replicates a set of human teeth. New haptic virtual reality (VR) simulation technologies allow real-time tactile feedback on 3D simulated clinical tasks; aid the self-directed learning aspect of skill acquisition; and track and provide feedback on an individual’s skill development. However, there is a limited evidence-base for optimal psychomotor skill acquisition by dental students using VR haptic simulators. This study aimed to investigate learning processes and their implications for undergraduate curriculum design. Neural (brain) activity studies of students and practicing dentists using electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) noted some variations in brain activity amongst students and trained dentists depending on the set task. The use of virtual reality simulation may provide learners with a different pathway of skill acquisition that is less reliant on ‘following rules’ and being bounded to achieve ‘perfection’, but rather allow learners to learn by making mistakes that have no consequence and provide a more ‘stress free’ learning environment. Further work is needed to expand this research to better understand how to create an ‘ideal’ learning environment for acquiring the psychomotor skills needed by a dentist.

17100614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100614.value: Major liver resection that involves removal of up to two thirds of the liver for hepatocellular carcinoma is risky due to the chance of small future liver remnant leading to postoperative liver failure. As a result, any clinical measure that could augment the size of the future liver remnant could potentially improve the safety profile of major hepatectomy in this group of patients. Portal vein embolization (PVE) that involves embolizing the tumor-bearing liver segments has been found to be an effective method to induce compensatory hypertrophy of the contralateral lobe of liver. Previous studies have shown that PVE could decrease the incidence of postoperative morbidity and the risk of hepatic failure after major hepatectomy. However, the benefit of PVE is less than satisfactory in patients with chronic liver diseases due to the impaired regeneration ability of the underlying hepatocytes and the presence of arteriovenous shunting within the liver. To overcome the latter problem, sequential transarterial chemoembolization (i.e. delivery of chemotherapeutic agent followed by gel foam embolization of the right hepatic artery in patients contemplating for right hepatectomy) prior to right portal vein embolization has been proposed in recent years. Another potential benefit of TACE is to prohibit tumor growth during the period when the contralateral liver undergoes hypertrophy. Although recent retrospective studies have shown some promising results, there is yet clinical data derived from randomized trial that shows the superiority of TACE + PVE over PVE alone in terms of the degree of compensatory hypertrophy and enhancement of opportunity to proceed to major hepatectomy. The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of sequential TACE + PVE in comparison with PVE alone before major hepatectomy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. 主要涉及到三分之二的肝癌肝切除的肝切除是危險的偶然的小未來殘肝導致術後肝功能衰竭. 其結果是，任何臨床的措施，可能增強的未來的殘肝大小可以潛在地提高安全設定檔在這組患者的主要肝切除。門靜脈栓塞 （PVE），涉及到荷瘤肝段栓塞術已被認定為有效方法，以引起對側肝葉代償性肥大。以前的研究表明 PVE 可降低術後併發症的發生率和肝衰竭的風險，主要的肝切除術後。然而，PVE 的好處是由於底層的肝細胞受損的再生能力和在肝臟內的動靜脈瘺的存在的慢性肝臟疾病患者不令人滿意。為了克服這一問題，序貫化療栓塞 （即交付緊接著凝膠泡沫栓塞術的病人考慮為右半肝切除的肝右動脈化療劑). 在門靜脈右支近年來提出了栓塞治療。肝動脈化療栓塞的另一個潛在好處是禁止期間當側肝經歷肥厚的腫瘤生長。雖然最近的回顧性研究 顯示一些可喜的成果，還有來自隨機試驗表明肝動脈化療栓塞 + PVE 的優越性在 PVE 獨自在多大程度的代償性肥大與增強的機會繼續肝大部切除的臨床資料。這項研究的目的是評估效果的順序肝動脈化療栓塞 + PVE 獨自在肝細胞癌患者肝大部切除前相比

17100614.label: Realisation of objectives
17100614.value: Major liver resection that involves removal of up to two thirds of the liver for hepatocellular carcinoma is risky due to the chance of small future liver remnant leading to postoperative liver failure. As a result, any clinical measure that could augment the size of the future liver remnant could potentially improve the safety profile of major hepatectomy in this group of patients. Portal vein embolization (PVE) that involves embolizing the tumor-bearing liver segments has been found to be an effective method to induce compensatory hypertrophy of the contralateral lobe of liver. Previous studies have shown that PVE could decrease the incidence of postoperative morbidity and the risk of hepatic failure after major hepatectomy. However, the benefit of PVE is less than satisfactory in patients with chronic liver diseases due to the impaired regeneration ability of the underlying hepatocytes and the presence of arteriovenous shunting within the liver. To overcome the latter problem, sequential transarterial chemoembolization (i.e. delivery of chemotherapeutic agent followed by gel foam embolization of the right hepatic artery in patients contemplating for right hepatectomy) prior to right portal vein embolization has been proposed in recent years. Another potential benefit of TACE is to prohibit tumor growth during the period when the contralateral liver undergoes hypertrophy. Although recent retrospective studies have shown some promising results, there is yet clinical data derived from randomized trial that shows the superiority of TACE + PVE over PVE alone in terms of the degree of compensatory hypertrophy and enhancement of opportunity to proceed to major hepatectomy. The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of sequential TACE + PVE in comparison with PVE alone before major hepatectomy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. The study was commenced on 1.9.2014 and the initial estimated sample size was 84 patients in total i.e. 43 patients in each arm. Due to the decline in hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma in Hong Kong in recent years owing to the improved vaccination rate against hepatitis B and the recent introduction of alternative popularised approach i.e. ALPPS to augment future liver remnant before hepatectomy, there has been difficulty in the recruitment of patients and the rate of recruitment was somewhat slower than expected. In the end, a total of 24 patients have been recruited at the time of writing and an interim analysis was performed. Despite the small size, we were still able to conduct the required level of data analysis in order to evaluate the primary endpoint. Nonetheless, the study is still ongoing and we are planning to continue until the target sample size is met.

17100614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100614.value: 13 patients were randomised to the PVE group and 11 patients were randomised to the TACE + PVE group. The median age was 61 years old (48-74) and hepatitis B was the predominant aetiology for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in both groups (84.6% vs 72.7%, p=0.142). There was no significant difference in terms of liver status (cirrhosis: 69.2% vs 72.7%, p=0.376), tumor size (7.5 vs. 6.0cm, p=0.931), frequency of microvascular invasion (38.5% vs. 36.4%, p=1.000)) and macroscopic vascular invasion (23.1% vs 9.1%, p=0.596) between the two groups. The degree of future liver remnant hypertrophy was also comparable between the two groups. The percentage of absolute volume gain for PVE and TACE + PVE were 44.1% and 36.3% respectively (p=0.172); and the gain in FLR/estimated total liver volume (FLR/ESLV%) was 15.7% and 11.0% respectively (p=0.333). The drop-out rate after PVE and TACE + PVE were 23.1% and 18.2% (p=1.000). Nonetheless, a significantly higher proportion of patients (p=0.03) in the TACE+PVE group underwent extended right hepatectomy (36.4% vs. 0%) while more patients underwent right trisectionectomy in the PVE alone group (7.7% vs. 0%). The 1-, 3- and 4-year disease-free survival rates for PVE were 70%, 45% and 45% while the corresponding rates for TACE + PVE group were 75%, 62.5% and 62.5% respectively (p=0.549). The 1-, 3- and 4-year overall survival rates for PVE were 80%, 70% and 56% and the corresponding rates for TACE + PVE group were 100%, 71.4% and 71.4% respectively (p=0.549). In summary, there was no significant difference in drop-out rate and oncological outcome between PVE alone and sequential TACE + PVE. Routine addition of TACE to PVE is therefore not recommended.

17100614.value: Our plan is to continue the study until the target size is met. If the study outcome remains the same as the interim analysis, the need to add one dose of TACE before PVE will no longer be required.

17100614.value: For the first time in the literature, our study showed that there was no significant impact on adding TACE to PVE with regard to the degree of augmenting the future liver remnant and the oncological outcome after liver resection.

17100714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100714.value: Cartilage injuries are very common and the majority requires surgical management. However, existing surgical treatments have significant limitations. Tissue engineering offers great hope in cartilage repair but none has so far stood the test of time. In particular, lack of a stable osteochondral interface in the bioengineered construct remains a major problem, among others. Engineering osteochondral interfaces has received increasing attention recently. Different fabrication technologies, biomaterials and cells have been employed, but the results are far from being able to achieve the ultimate goal of simulating the structural zonal organization and functional properties of native osteochondral interface. Challenges including identifying the optimal combination of cells and scaffolds and stimulating interface maturation remain to be tackled. Funded by a previous GRF grant, we are the first to bioengineer a tri-layered osteochondral construct with an intact calcified cartilage interface using bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (MSC). The interface structurally simulates their native counterparts in many ways. We have obtained exciting in vivo data in rabbits with zonal organization, tidemark regeneration, quality hyaline cartilage, good bony integration, and close-to-normal matrix composition in 4 weeks’ time. Smooth articular surface, persistent zonal organization, tidemark regeneration and quality hyaline cartilage were found at 6 months post-operation. Our most recent data at 1 year demonstrated significant advantages of the tri-layered construct over other control groups in terms of excellent cartilage regeneration without degenerative changes such as thinning of hyaline cartilage and advanced calcification front. Several critical questions have to be addressed before we can translate this technology to clinical applications. First, species variation in MSC performance is large. Therefore, human-specific protocols for differentiation, co-culture and phenotype maintenance will be established in fabricating the tri-layered osteochondral construct with calcified cartilage interface. Second, the interface formed in vitro is usually immature. Therefore, strategies promoting interface maturation and stabilization such as compression loading in bioreactors and supplementation of biological factors will be developed. Third, to provide important clinical insight of translating this technology in cartilage repair, a large animal model with comparable defect size is required. Specifically, we shall evaluate the fate and efficacy of the human MSC-based construct in a minipig cartilage repair model under immunosuppression. This study develops human MSC-based osteochondral construct with stable interface and evaluates its efficacy in a large animal model.
