17100914.label: Realisation of objectives
17100914.value: Lupus nephritis is a common and severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and is an important cause of both acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease. Anti-dsDNA antibody production is a cardinal feature of lupus nephritis, the level of which often correlates with disease activity. Although evidence suggest that anti-dsDNA antibodies contribute to the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis, the mechanism through which they bind to resident renal cells to exert their pathologic effect remains to be fully elucidated. The tubulo-interstitium constitutes approximately 90% of the kidney volume and proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC) are the predominant cells in this compartment. Although immune deposits are predominantly deposited in the glomerulus, up to 70% of lupus nephritis patients also exhibit immune complex deposits along the tubular basement membrane. Ku70 and Ku80 are proteins that are predominantly located in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells, and play critical roles in DNA double strand break recognition and repair, and apoptosis. Although Ku70 and Ku80 expression outside of the nucleus has been reported, little known of their functions. This study investigated (a) the role of Ku70 and Ku80 in the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis, (b) whether serum levels of Ku70 and Ku80 may serve as markers of disease activity and (c) renal expression of Ku70 and Ku80 in patients and mice with active disease. We employed a combination of animal and in vitro studies and staining of clinical specimens. We have completed Objectives 2, 4 and 5, and Objectives 1 and 3 are 80-90% completed. We envisage we will complete Objectives 1 and 3 within 6 months and data will be analyzed for manuscript submission. The delay in completing these Objectives was due to problems encountered in the generation of stable clones with genetic deletion of Ku70 and Ku80, possibly an indication of their essential role in DNA double strand break recognition and repair. In this regard, we have used PTEC with transient knockdown of Ku70 and Ku80 expression. In our in vitro studies using PTEC, we isolated proteins from the plasma membrane, cytosolic and nuclear fractions. Human polyclonal anti-dsDNA antibodies were isolated from patients with active lupus nephritis using affinity chromatography and were used to investigate their cross-reactivity to plasma membrane, cytosolic and nuclear proteins. LC-MS/MS identified Ku70 as a cross-reactive antigen on the plasma membrane of PTEC that mediated anti-dsDNA antibody binding. After binding, anti-dsDNA antibodies were internalized and translocated to the cell membrane within 30 min, mediated in part through Ku80. This was associated with increased secretion of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic mediators such as IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and TGF-beta1, increased ERK, JNK, p38 MAPK, PI3K and PKC signaling and upregulation of Ku70, Ku80, fibronectin and laminin expression. Gene silencing of Ku70 or prior incubation of PTEC with anti-Ku70 antibody attenuated anti-dsDNA antibody binding and downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes in PTEC. Furthermore, gene silencing of Ku70 had no effect on Ku80 expression, whereas gene silencing of Ku80 expression resulted in a concomitant reduction in Ku70 expression. We have previously demonstrated that TGF-beta1, MCP-1, IL-6 and IL-8 could induce matrix protein synthesis in PTEC. Incubation of Ku70-deficient PTEC with the aforementioned pro-fibrotic mediators significantly decreased fibronectin and laminin expression when compared to control cells. Given that tubulo-interstitial fibronectin deposition is an early event in kidney fibrosis and fibronectin accumulation serves as a scaffold for the deposition of other matrix proteins, identifying mechanisms that induce fibronectin synthesis is essential before devising novel therapeutic strategies. We have demonstrated that increased Ku70 and Ku80 expression is associated with increased fibronectin expression in PTEC. Ku70 and Ku80 expression in PTEC was expressed predominantly in the monomeric form. Archived renal biopsy specimens obtained from Class III or IV ± V lupus nephritis patients were retrieved to determine Ku70 and Ku80 expression in the kidney. Archived renal specimens from patients with non-lupus renal diseases such as IgA nephropathy, membranous glomerulonephritis, minimal change disease and tubulo-interstitial nephritis, and normal kidney tissue obtained from patients who underwent nephrectomy served as controls. In normal kidney tissue, Ku70 and Ku80 expression were absent in the glomerulus and weakly expressed in the tubulo-interstitium. In lupus nephritis patients, Ku70 expression was marginally increased in areas of glomerulosclerosis, and markedly increased in highly proliferative proximal tubules especially along the apical aspect of the tubules, in the cell nuclei, and in tubulo-interstitial areas where prominent immune cell infiltration was observed. Ku80 was localized solely to the nuclei of PTEC, suggesting that Ku70 and Ku80 exist as heterodimers that contribute to DNA double strand break recognition and repair, whereas Ku70 may have a role that is independent of DNA repair. Increased renal expression of Ku70 and Ku80 was associated with disease activity and anti-dsDNA antibody level in lupus nephritis patients. Intra-renal Ku70 and Ku80 expression in patients with non-lupus renal diseases was also increased but to a lesser extent suggesting that altered Ku70 and Ku80 expression may play a role in chronic kidney disease although further studies are warranted to confirm this. Serum levels of Ku70 and Ku80 were comparable between patients with lupus nephritis and control groups. Animal studies allow researchers to determine longitudinal expression of target proteins and their association with disease activity. We demonstrated that Ku70 and Ku80 were weakly expressed in PTEC in non-autoimmune BALB/c mice and their expression did not differ with increasing age. In NZB/W F1 mice, an experimental model of lupus nephritis, Ku70 and Ku80 expression was increased in PTEC before the development of nephritis, and their expression increased with increasing severity of disease and was predominantly observed in atrophic tubules. Tubulo-interstitial Ku70 and Ku80 expression correlated with proteinuria, and serum creatinine and anti-dsDNA antibody levels. Taken together, we have identified Ku70 as cross-reactive antigens that mediates anti-dsDNA antibody binding to the cell surface of PTEC, and Ku80 as a cytoplasmic protein that may translocate anti-dsDNA antibodies from the cytosol to the nucleus to mediate downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes.

17100914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100914.value: Lupus nephritis is a common cause of acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease. Anti-dsDNA antibody production is a cardinal feature of lupus nephritis and they bind to resident renal cells to exert downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes. We and others have identified cross-reactive cell surface antigens that mediate anti-dsDNA antibody binding in human mesangial cells, but how anti-dsDNA antibodies bind to PTEC has not been determined. In this study, we demonstrated that anti-dsDNA antibodies from patients with active lupus nephritis bound to a 70 kDa PTEC plasma membrane protein that was identified as Ku70 by LC-MS/MS. The binding was not influenced by exogenous DNA, histones or nucleosomes suggesting that anti-dsDNA antibody binding was direct and independent of chromatin material. Anti-dsDNA antibody binding to Ku70 was validated by Ku70 gene silencing and prior incubation of cells with anti-Ku70 blocking antibody. Following their binding to Ku70, anti-dsDNA antibodies were rapidly internalized and translocated to the nuclei, mediated in part through binding to Ku80. Anti-dsDNA antibodies increased gene and protein expression of Ku70 and Ku80 in PTEC and this was accompanied by increased secretion of IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and TGF-beta1, and matrix protein expression (fibronectin and laminin). Ku70 or Ku80 knockdown decreased anti-dsDNA antibody mediated secretion of cytokines and growth factors, and matrix protein expression in PTEC. Renal specimens from patients and mice with active lupus nephritis showed increased Ku70 and Ku80 expression in PTEC with distinct localization. Whereas Ku70 was observed in the nuclei of PTEC, and also along the apical aspect and cytoplasm of PTEC, Ku80 was localized solely in the nuclei of PTEC, suggesting that Ku70 and Ku80 exist as heterodimers that contribute to DNA double strand break recognition and repair, whereas Ku70 may also have a role that is independent of DNA repair. Increased renal expression of Ku70 and Ku80 was associated with disease activity, proteinuria and serum creatinine and anti-dsDNA antibody levels in lupus nephritis. Taken together, our findings suggests that immune-mediated injury in the tubulo-interstitium in lupus nephritis, may be attributed at least in part, to increased expression of Ku70 and Ku80 and their interaction with anti-dsDNA antibodies. Part of our findings was accepted for two poster presentation at the ISN World Congress of Nephrology in 2017 and 2019, and accepted for oral presentation at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2018, the top ranked international nephrology conference. A manuscript is currently under preparation.

17100914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100914.value: Based on our in vitro findings that gene silencing of Ku70 and Ku80 is accompanied by downregulation of matrix protein expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors in PTEC, we will undertake preliminary studies to investigate the role of Ku70 and Ku80 in chronic kidney disease. If preliminary data are encouraging, we will apply for funding support from RGC General Research Fund or the Food and Health Bureau to further elucidate the role of Ku70 and Ku70 in experimental models of chronic kidney disease.

17100914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100914.value: Lupus nephritis is an important cause of acute kidney injury and chronic kidney failure in Asia. Anti-dsDNA antibody production is a hallmark of lupus nephritis but how they bind to resident renal cells to induce kidney injury remains to be fully elucidated. The tubulo-interstitium comprises 90% of the total volume of the kidney and proximal renal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC) are the predominant cell type. The amount of tubulo-interstitial injury strongly correlates with poor prognosis. In this study, we identified Ku70 as the cross-reactive antigen that mediates anti-dsDNA antibody binding to PTEC and following binding, anti-dsDNA antibodies are rapidly internalized and translocated to the cell nuclei where they exerted downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes such as increased secretion of cytokines and growth factors, and expression of extracellular matrix proteins. Suppressing Ku70 synthesis reduced anti-dsDNA antibody binding and subsequent downstream inflammatory and inflammatory processes. Kidney specimens from patients and mice with active lupus nephritis showed increased expression of Ku70 and Ku80 in PTEC compared to normal kidney specimens. Our data show that Ku70 mediates anti-dsDNA antibody binding to PTEC, and Ku70 may play a role in mediating inflammatory and fibrotic processes in tubulo-interstitial injury in lupus nephritis.

17101014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101014.value: Cells are constantly under stress from dynamic intrinsic and extrinsic changes, and numerous pathways are call upon to deal with unfavorable outcomes. Secreted proteins are produced in the endoplasmic reticulums (ER). Cells have evolved means of sensing perturbations in protein folding load with specific ER membrane sensors. In vitro studies have shown that a cell will die under a “lethal” level of ER-stress, activating apoptosis; whereas a cell under “sub-lethal” levels of ER-stress activate signals that help cells to alleviate stress and the cell survives. Studies of in vivo responses are limited and how cells behave under different developmental and environmental contexts is poorly understood. In our studies of mouse models for metaphyseal chondrodysplasia type Schmid (MCDS), we showed mutations in collagen X affect protein folding in the ER, activating ER-stress in hypertrophic chondrocytes of the growth plate. However, the disease is not due to cell death but rather survival that leads to an altered cellular differentiation. How hypertrophic chondrocytes avoided apoptosis from a seemingly “high” dose of ER-stress is not clear. As the growth plate cartilage is avascular, we studied interplay between ER and hypoxic stress signals as a survival strategy. Indeed, we showed an intrinsic relationship where ER-stress activates hypoxic signals such as maintenance of HIF1α and Hif2α proteins. We further showed that this is associated with ATF4 via activation of the PERK sensor. Importantly, from transcriptome and proteome analyses of the growth plate, we identified a significant up regulation of FGF21 expression, and metabolic changes link to potential changes in mitochondrial function. We hypothesize a shift towards glycolysis for ATP production similar to the Warburg effect for cell survival. In the current proposal, we aim to study the role of FGF21 and HIF proteins in the energy management of hypertrophic chondrocytes under ER stress in mice. We will also use a 3D cell culture system to study the relationship between intrinsic and extrinsic factors in hypertrophic chondrocytes differentiated from wild type (wt) and MCDS mouse embryonic stem cells with defined genetic modification of FGF21 and HIF proteins. This represents a systematic study of cellular outcomes from inactivation or overexpression of these factors with varying exogenous input of Glucose, FGF21 and oxygen levels. This proposal will provide new molecular insights for a relationship between ER and mitochondrial function, in the balancing of metabolic needs for cell fate determination in developmental processes or diseases where ER-stress has a role.

17101414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101414.value: Ovarian cancer is one of the most lethal gynecological malignacies in Western countries as well as in Hong Kong. Most patients are diagnosed at the advanced stage with frequent metastasis develops, resulting in overall poor prognosis. It preferentially metastasizes within the peritoneal cavity with omentum being the major metastasis site. The precise mechanisms underlying the tumorigenesis and the unique metastasis pattern of ovarian cancer are still poorly defined. A recent study revealed adipokines secreted by omental adipocytes including interleukin-8 (IL-8) promote ovarian cancer metastasis, suggesting the importance of tumor microenvironment on ovarian cancer. Altered glucose metabolism is a new hallmark for cancer. High lactate production and low glucose oxidation, regardless of the oxygen supply, known as the Warburg effect, are commonly found in cancers. Such metabolic switch is governed by gate-keeping enzymes pyruvate dehydrogenase kinases (PDKs) which negatively phosphorylate pyruvate dehydroagenase (PDH), leading to the conversion of pyruvate to lactate in the cytoplasm instead of further oxidation in the mitochondria. PDK1 controls the metabolic switch, leading to malignant phenotypes in different human cancers, yet the mechanisms remain elusive. To date, little is known about altered glucose metabolism in ovarian cancer. Moreover, PDK1 in ovarian cancer remains to be explored. Our pilot study showed PDK1 was up-regulated in ovarian cancer cell lines and significantly higher PDK1 expression was found in metastatic foci in patient samples. Knockdown of PDK1 in ovarian cancer cells decreased lactate level, inhibited cell migration and invasion accompanied by alternation of genes related to metastasis. Moreover, we found that PDK1 expression and lactate level were regulated by IL-8 and microRNA-128, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between tumor microenvironment, altered cell metabolism, tumorigenesis and metastasis in ovarian cancer. We hypothesize that PDK1, which can be regulated by IL-8 and miR-128, plays a critical role in ovarian cancer tumorigenesis and metastasis through metabolic switch and pathways related to homing, migration and invasion. We propose to (1) study the clinical significance of PDK1 in ovarian cancer; (2) examine the effects of PDK1 and DCA, a PDK inhibitor, in ovarian cancer metabolic switch, tumorigenesis and metastasis in vitro and in vivo; (3) delineate the molecular pathways in mediating the above effects; (4) identify the mechanisms governing PDK1 deregulation in ovarian cancer. Our findings will yield novel mechanistic insights into ovarian tumorigenesis and metastasis and help to identify useful prognostic markers and develop new strategies and effective therapies for ovarian cancer. 無論是在西方國家還是香港，卵巢癌都是導致女性死於癌症的重要原因之一。大多數卵巢癌在診斷時已屬晚期，並常伴有癌細胞轉移，導致總體預後較差。卵巢癌傾向於腹腔轉移，其中大網膜是主要的轉移部位。然而卵巢癌發生的確切原理以及其獨特的轉移方式還不甚清晰。最近的一項研究顯示大網膜中的脂肪細胞所分泌的脂肪細胞因子，包括白介素8（IL-8）在內，能夠促進卵巢癌的轉移，這說明了腫瘤微環境在卵巢癌中所起到的重要作用。糖代謝的改變是癌症的一個新標誌。在癌症中常見一種叫做“瓦柏格效應”的現象，即不管在有氧還是無氧的條件下，細胞都可以產生大量的乳酸，而葡萄糖的氧化卻很少。這種代謝轉變由類似門衛的酶——丙酮酸脫氫酶激酶（PDKs）控制。PDKs抑制酮酸脫氫酶(PDH)的磷酸化，致使丙酮酸在細胞質中轉變為乳酸，而不是在線粒體中作進一步的氧化。PDK1控制這種代謝轉變，導致人類不同腫瘤的惡性表型，但其中的機制還不清楚。時至今日，關於卵巢癌中糖代謝的改變知之甚少。此外，PDK1在卵巢癌中的作用還有待探索。我們的初步研究顯示PDK1水平在卵巢癌細胞系中升高，並且在病人轉移灶的樣本中檢測出較高水平的PDK1。抑制卵巢癌細胞的PDK1水平能夠降低乳酸的生產水平，抑制細胞的遷移性和侵襲性，並且改變與轉移相關的基因。與此同時，我們發現IL-8和微RNA(miR)-128可以調節PDK1的表達和乳酸的水平。這表明了腫瘤微環境，細胞代謝的改變，腫瘤的發生及轉移在卵巢癌中的潛在關聯。我們做出了這樣的假設，即受IL-8和 miR-128調節的PDK1能通過改變細胞代謝和與黏附性、遷移性、侵襲性相關的通路，從而在卵巢癌的發生和轉移中起到重要的作用。我們提議：（1）研究PDK1在卵巢癌中的臨床意義；（2）通過體外和體內研究來檢測PDK1和DCA（一種PDK抑制劑）在卵巢癌代謝改變、腫瘤發生和轉移中的作用；（3）探索調節上述作用的信號通路；（4）確立卵巢癌中控制PDK1異常活動的機制。我們的研究將為卵巢癌的發生和轉移機制提供新穎而深入的見解，並有助於確立有效的預後指標和研發更新更有效的治療策略。

17101414.label: Realisation of objectives
17101414.value: For objective 1, we evaluated protein expression of PDK1 in 130 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue samples by immunohistochemistry. PDK1 protein was primarily localized in the cytoplasm. PDK1 staining was moderate to strong in ovarian cancers, in contrast to the barely detectable staining in benign cystadenomas. We also detected significantly higher PDK1 mRNA level in ovarian cancers when compared with their corresponding nontumor counterparts from 20 paired clinical samples of ovarian tumors by qPCR. Moreover, statistically higher PDK1 immunoreactivity was found in metastatic foci than their corresponding primary carcinomas. High PDK1 immunoreactivity was significantly associated with resistance to chemotherapy, shorter overall and disease-free survival. By multivariate analysis, PDK1, disease stage, grade and chemosensitivity were significant independent predictors of overall survival. Furthermore, we found protein expression of PDK1 was up-regulated in ovarian cancer cell lines compared with normal ovarian epithelium cell lines. For Objective 2, we first examined cell metabolic effects of PDK1 on ovarian cancer. For transient knockdown, siRNA specifically targeting PDK1 was introduced into SKOV-3 and A2780CP cells. For stable knockdown, cells were transfected with a set of shRNA constructs against human PDK1 or control pRS vector. The media from cultured cells were used for measuring lactate level using the Lactate Colorimetric Assay Kit. We found that PDK1-transient (SKOV-3) and stable (A2780CP) silenced cells have a significantly reduced lactate level as compared to control cells accompany with reduced phosphorylation of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1-alpha subunit (PDHE1α). Then adhesion of ovarian cancer cells to fibronectin and mesothelial cells was assessed by cell adhesion assay. Transient knockdown of PDK1 in SKOV-3 cells significantly impeded cells adhere to fibronectin and mesothelial cells. Wound healing assay revealed a slower migration rate in A2780CP and ES-2 cells upon shPDK1 knockdown. Both cell migration and invasion rates were decreased in transient (SKOV-3 and A2780CP cells) and stable (A2780CP and ES-2) silencing of PDK1 compared to the control cells. We also investigated the effects of dichloroacetate (DCA), a PDK inhibitor, in A2780CP and ES2 cells. DCA, a pyruvate analog, binds to the N-terminal of PDK, leading to PDK inhibition. To determine if DCA can mimic the effects of PDK1 silencing in ovarian cancer cells, A2780CP and ES2 cells were treated with various concentration of DCA (0, 0.5, 1 and 5 mM) for 24 hours. DCA decreased p-PDHE1 expression in a dose dependent manner, suggesting that DCA could inhibit PDHK, thus blocking PDH phosphorylation. DCA also retarded migration and invasion ability of A2780CP and ES2 cells dose-dependently. We further determined the effect of PDK1 on ovarian cancer cell growth. PDK1-depleted A2780CP and ES2 cells did not alter anchorage-dependent growth as evaluated by focus formation assay. Yet smaller and less colonies were formed in PDK1-depleted A2780CP cells in soft agar, suggesting PDK1 can induce anchorage-independent growth. Next, we studied PDK1 depletion on in vivo tumor growth and dissemination. shPDK1 ES-2 and control cells were inoculated subcutaneous (s.c.) or intraperitoneal (i.p.) to nude mice. PDK1 knockdown revealed a significant reduction of tumor growth. Control mice displayed extensive abdominal dissemination predominantly at the mesentery, whereas only focal nodules were found at mesentery of mice with PDK1 depleted cells. For Objective 3, we examined the downstream targets that mediate PDK1 adhesion, migration and invasion effects. When disseminated primary ovarian cancer cells home to the omentum or peritoneum, they first form interaction with mesothelial cells through integrin receptors. After that, ovarian cancer cells adhere, migrate and invade through the extracellular matrix (ECM) in the submesothelial basement membrane. Thus, urokinase plasminogen activator (u-PA) and VEGF, critical components for ECM remodeling, may play crucial roles in ovarian cancer metastasis. Remarkably, siPDK1 in SKOV-3 and shPDK1 in A2780CP cells attenuated α5 integrin and β1 integrin protein expression. We also found uPA and VEGF expression was downregulated. To further examine the effects and downstream targets of PDK1 in ovarian cancer, OVCAR-3 cells were stably transfected with DDK-tagged PDK1 plasmid or control empty vector. We found that ectopic expression of PDK1 significantly enhanced cells adhere to fibronectin and mesothelial cells, cell migration and invasion abilities, as well as induction of α5 integrin, β1 integrin and uPA protein expression. For Objective 4, we identified the mechanisms governing PDK1 deregulation in ovarian cancer. We found that conditioned medium from ovarian cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs-CM) attenuated PDK1 expression in SKOV-3 and ES-2 cells. Given that interleukin-8 (IL-8) was upregulated in CAFs derived from ovarian cancers, we further discovered that CAFs-CM induced PDK1 expression was blocked by neutralizing IL-8 and CXCR1 antibodies. We also detected up-regulation of PDK1 in IL-8 treated SKOV-3 cells.

17101414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101414.value: Major findings included: 1) PDK1 was highly expressed in both ovarian cancer clinical samples and cell lines. Evaluated PDK1 expression was significantly associated with metastasis of ovarian cancers, reduced chemosensitivity, and poor overall and disease-free survival. PDK1 was an independent prognostic factor. 2) Silencing of PDK1 retarded lactate production, ovarian cancer cell adhesion to fibronectin and mesothelial cells, cell migration and invasion, and anchourage-independent growth, along with reduced p-PDHE1, α5β1 integrin, uPA and VEGF expression. DCA, a PDK inhibitor, also reduced p-PDHE1 expression and inhibited lactate production, and cell migration and invasion. Conversely, PDK1 overexpression induced lactate level, ovarian cancer cell adhesion, migration and invasion, which was accompanied by an increase in p-PDHE1, α5β1 integrin, uPA and VEGF expression. PDK1 depletion also hindered tumor growth and dissemination in nude mice. 3) We further showed PDK1-mediated cell adhesion involved its regulation of α5β1 integrin and PDK1-mediated cell migration and invasion probably via its regulation of uPA and VEGF. 4) PDK1 was up-regulated by treatment with conditioned medium from ovarian cancer-associated fibroblasts, probably through interleukin-8 and its receptor CXCR1. Research outcome: 1. This work was presented as a poster presentation in EACR-AACR-SIC Special Conference on Anticancer Drug Action and Drug Resistance at Florence, Italy in 2015. 2. A manuscript based on the present findings titled ‘PDK1 induced by IL-8 derived from CAFs promotes ovarian cancer cell metastasis via upregulation of α5β1 integrin/uPA/VEGF expression and correlates with poor prognosis in patients’ is attached with this report, which will be submitted in the coming month. 3. A Mphil student has been trained and graduated.

17101414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101414.value: 1) Our present finding identified PDK1 could up-regulate VEGF expression. Bevacizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody to VEGF that block its binding to its receptors, is the only FDA approved anti-angiogenic agent for the treatment of ovarian cancer. However, modest response with resistance limits its clinical efficacy. The present link between PDK1 and VEGF suggested that dual targeting of PDK1 (such as by DCA) and VEGF on ovarian or other cancers as alternative therapeutic approaches can be evaluated in future studies. 2) Our immunohistochemistry data showed high PDK1 immunoreactivity was significantly associated with resistance to chemotherapy. Chemoresistance is a major hurdle in successful ovarian cancer treatment. Our preliminary data demonstrated that DCA could sensitized A2780CP cells to cisplatin treatment. DCA has been used to treat mitochondrial diseases with low toxicity profile and in a small clinical trial in patients with glioblastoma. We are currently working on how PDK1 regulates chemoresistance, which could provide novel insights into ovarian cancer chemoresistance. Such preclinical results can potentially translate to selective ovarian cancer treatment for women with PDK1 expressing ovarian cancers.

17101414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101414.value: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignacies due to its lack of symptoms until widespread metastases develop. Thus, identifying novel prognostic and therapeutic targets can improve survival. In this study, we examined PDK1, a gate-keeping enzyme of the Warburg effect, and showed PDK1 was up-regulated in ovarian cancer clinical samples and cell lines. Higher PDK1 expression was associated with metastasis of ovarian cancers, reduced chemosensitivity and a poorer prognosis. PDK1 deletion in ovarian cancer cells decreased lactate level, inhibited cell adhesion, migration and invasion, and anchourage-independent growth, accompanied by reduced p-PDHE1, α5β1 integrin, uPA and VEGF expression. DCA, a PDK inhibitor, also displayed similar effects. Conversely, PDK1 overexpression showed opposite effects. Moreover, we found that PDK1 can be up-regulated by conditioned medium from ovarian cancer-associated fibroblasts through IL8/CXCR1, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between tumor microenvironment, altered cell metabolism, tumorigenesis and metastasis in ovarian cancer. This is the first report demonstrating the association between PDK1 and survival in ovarian cancer patients, indicating PDK1 to be a useful prognostic marker. Results of the project also implicate the potential use of the PDK inhibitor, such as DCA, for targeting the cancer-specific altered metabolic preference in ovarian cancer.

17102014.label: Realisation of objectives
17102014.value: 1. Elucidate how Tspyl2 alters the level of H3K27Me3 and possibly other histone marks Based on the expression of TSPYL2 in the developing and adult brain and its interaction with diverse histone modifiers and readers, we examined the effect of Tspyl2 loss-of-function on several histone marks associated with transcriptional activities. Intriguingly, we discovered a specific increase in the level of H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) in the mutant hippocampus. H3K27me3 is a key repressive histone mark which plays an important role during brain development, neuron specification and function. The H3K27 methylation mark is set up by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). Mammalian PRC2 consists of four core components: Enhancer of zeste (EZH), Embryonic ectoderm development (EED), Suppressor of zeste 12 homolog (SUZ12) and RbAp46/48. The presence of other components are context-dependent. To test whether TSPYL2 directly affects the methylation of H3K27, we performed affinity pull down using bacterial recombinant GST-tagged TSPYL2 with HEK293 nuclear extract. We detected EZH2. By contrast, only weak signals of the H3K27 demethylases UTX and JMJD3 were detected even when they were overexpressed individually. To test if the interaction between TSPYL2 and EZH2 was direct or indirect, we separated components of the PRC2 core complex consisting of EZH2, EED, SUZ12, RbAp48 and AEBP, and probed with recombinant GST or GST-TSPYL2. GST-TSPYL2 specifically bound EZH2, as confirmed by western blot using antibodies to EZH2 to probe the enzyme complex in parallel. To identify the H3K27me3 marked genes in neurons, we employed DIV14 primary hippocampal neurons for ChIP-seq in order to minimize heterogeneity in cell types and experience-dependent variations in gene expression. The purity of neurons as determined by NeuN and DAPI staining was 95 - 97% throughout the 14 days culture period. We also clarified that EZH2 was expressed in primary hippocampal neurons at DIV14 by western blotting and by co-immunostaining with the neuronal marker Neu N. For ChIP-seq, the specificity of H3K27me3 antibodies used was confirmed using a peptide array. We performed ChIP-seq in biological duplicates. To ensure sufficient sequencing depth, ~50 million non-duplicated reads were mapped for each sample. We did not detect any obvious changes in the genomic localization of H3K27me3 marks in neurons isolated from Tspyl2 mutant embryos. To confirm that TSPYL2 is not generally required for the recruitment to or maintenance of EZH2 at specific target sites, we further performed ChIP-seq using ChIP-validated EZH2 antibodies with one pair of samples. We collected more than 43 million reads for each sample and identified no redistribution of EZH2 genomic binding sites. The data validate that TSPYL2 is not important for the recruitment or maintenance of EZH2 at genomic target sites. 2. Demonstrate the importance of Tspyl2 in establishing the epigenetic landscape By k-mean clustering, we divided all RefSeq genes into four clusters from high to low modification levels based on H3K27me3 occupancy ± 5 kb of transcription start sites (TSS). Metagene analysis showed that there is an increase in the level of H3K27me3 only in cluster 1 genes in mutant neurons. In agreement with the literature, these genes include known H3K27me3 marked genes in embryonic stem cells which are suppressed. Cluster 2 genes have a much lower level of H3K27me3. Ontology analysis (DAVID Gene Ontology Bioinformatics Resources) shows that they are enriched in processes important for multicellular organism development, including positive regulation of neuron differentiation, in comparison to 9069 cluster 3 genes which are enriched in diverse pathways including G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathway, sensory perception of smell and immune responses. Cluster 4 genes are unmarked. There were no major changes in the level of H3K27me3 in cluster 2-3 genes. (We also performed ChIP-seq in biological replicates for H3K4me3 before and after addition of KCl and detected no major changes). 3. Elucidate the role of Tspyl2 in precise gene expression As H3K27me3 is associated with transcription repression which can be inherited during cell division, in mutant neurons there should be unchanged or reduced expression of cluster 1 genes. We randomly tested several genes in cluster 1. As predicted, their expressions were low in both wild-type and mutant neurons with high threshold cycles by RT-qPCR analysis. Nevertheless, we could detect a further reduction in the expression of a few of them in mutant samples, for example Gbx2 and Prss16, suggesting subtle changes in gene expression during development. We further quantitated the expression of cluster 2 neuronal genes and found reduced expression in mutant neurons in all 7 neuronal genes being tested, with 5 genes showing statistical significant differences. These include Acvrl1 (WT: n = 6; Mut: n = 5, P = 0.0243), Bdnf transcript variant 1, the longest transcript and therefore used for clustering (WT: n = 5; Mut: n = 5, P = 0.0324), Egr3 (WT: n = 7; Mut: n = 11, P = 0.0234), Grin2c (WT: n =7; Mut: n = 11, P = 0.0061) and Igf1 (WT: n = 7; Mut: n = 11, P = 0.0299). To test whether there is dynamic deposition of the H3K27me3 mark in synaptic genes, we applied GSK126, a specific inhibitor of EZH2, before we collected samples at DIV14. In both wild-type and mutant neurons, GSK126 caused a significant increase in the expression of Egr3 (WT: n =8, P = 0.0387; Mut: n = 12, P = 0.0429) and Grin2c (WT: n = 8, P = 0.0181; Mut: n = 12, P = 0.0147). Interestingly, Bdnf was significantly upregulated by GSK126 in mutants only (n = 12, P = 0.0053). Conversely, pre-treatment with GSKJ4, a selective inhibitor of JMJD3 and UTX, significantly reduced the expression the Egr3 (WT: n = 9, P = 0.0095; Mut: n = 10, P = 0.0001), Grin2c (WT: n = 9, P = 0.0227; Mut: n = 10, P = 0.0670) in both genotypes. Finally, we determined whether TSPYL2 and EZH2 co-existed in target promoters. Since we could not identify TSPYL2 antibodies suitable for ChIP after an extensive search, we resolved to transfect HA-TSPYL2 into Be(2)-C human neuroblastoma cells. Cells were transfected with HA-TSPYL2 or the vector pcDNA3.1 and subject to ChIP with HA and EZH2 antibodies in parallel. We detected increased binding of TSPYL2 to promoters of GBX2, PRSS16, BDNF and GRIN2A in three independent transfections. EZH2 bound equally to these regions in vector and HA-TSPYL2 transfected cells in two independent experiments. The results revealed the binding of both TSPYL2 and EZH2 to the promoters of GBX2, PRSS16, BDNF and GRIN2A in this cellular context. The data provide insight into how TSPYL2 fine tunes the expression of multiple genes and contribute to neurodevelopmental syndromes in humans.

17102014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102014.value: 1. TSPYL2 interacts with EZH2 and reduces the activity of the EZH2 enzyme complex in vitro. 2. TSPYL2 is recruited to the promoter of a subset of EZH2 target genes through interaction with EZH2. 3a. Tspyl2 knockout results in an increased level of H3K27me3 and reduced expression of some 'development genes' marked by H3K27me3 (eg. Gbx2 and Prss16) in hippocampal neurons. 3b. EZH2 is expressed in primary neurons. Furthermore, TSPYL2 and EZH2 dynamically regulate the expression of the important synaptic genes including Bdnf, Egr3 and Grin2c in primary hippocampal neurons. In summary, this investigation reveals a previously unrecognized role of TSPYL2 in regulating the expression of EZH2 target genes in hippocampal neurons. Through H3K27me3 ChIP-seq, we have indirectly identified a specific subset of EZH2 target genes which are also regulated by TSPYL2. We found that TSPYL2 interacts with EZH2 but did not affect its genomic distribution. In hippocampal neurons, some of the H3K27me3 marked genes, including Bdnf, Egr3 and Grin2c, are dynamically regulated by EZH2 and TSPYL2. Since Tspyl2 loss-of-function caused reduced expression of these marked genes, TSPYL2 normally enhances the expression of these genes in differentiated neurons. Building on the existing knowledge on the importance of these genes in long term potential and fear-associated memory, our data provide the molecular link between regulation of gene expression byTSPYL2 in neurons to the behavioural outcome.

17102014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102014.value: Multiple in vitro studies have shown that TSPYL2 is a potential tumour suppressor. Our database analysis shows that lower expression of TSPYL2 is correlated with poor outcome in neuroblastoma. As EZH2 plays a role in the development of a variety of cancer types, currently we are investigating whether TSPYL2 has a role in controlling gene expression through EZH2 in in neuroblastoma cell lines. Furthermore, we have established overseas collaborations and submitted joint grant applications on the role of TSPYL2 as a tumour suppressor with Dr. Laura Zanni, now in Istituto di Genetica Molecolare, Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (IGM-CNR), Pavia, Italy

17102014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102014.value: The genetic control of behaviour is complex. TSPYL2 is a protein found in the brain. Our previous study using a mutant mouse model shows that TSPYL2 regulates the expression of Grin2a and Grin2b genes. These two genes are important in processes such as learning and memory. Here our work reveals other genes regulated by TSPYL2 in neurons. TSPYL2 interacts with EZH2, a key enzyme for epigenetic regulation of gene expression through histone methylation. Furthermore, TSPYL2 and EZH2 dynamically regulate the expression of specific genes in neurons which include Bdnf, Egr3 and Grin2c. The importance of these genes in neuron function and behavioural control is well established. In summary, our work identifies how TSPYL2 acts as a novel player in the epigenetic control of gene expression in neurons, and how it might contribute to behaviour control and neurodevelopmental syndromes.

17102314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102314.value: Anticoagulant drugs are used to prevent blood clots, which may cause stroke in individuals with atrial fibrillation (the most common type of heart arrhythmia) or following major joint replacement surgery. Traditionally, vitamin K antagonists (e.g. warfarin) have been the only oral anticoagulant medication. However, these have disadvantages including food/drug interactions, and the need for strict blood monitoring to detect excessive bleeding risk. Antiplatelet medications (e.g. aspirin and/or clopidogrel) are used where warfarin is not suitable. Following claims of advantages to existing therapies, new oral anticoagulant drugs (NOACs; dabigatran, rivaroxaban and apixaban) were approved for clinical use. Of these, dabigatran was first to become available, with a steadily increasing volume of use since its registration in Hong Kong in 2008. Important knowledge gaps associated with the use of dabigatran however, warrants further exploration. Dabigatran, at its highest commercial dose is superior to warfarin in preventing stroke in patients with AF, however, significantly more cases of stomach discomfort (dyspepsia) and gastrointestinal bleeding in the randomised clinical trial (RCT) setting were reported. This conflicts with data generated from an observational study reporting no significantly increased bleeding risk compared to warfarin in the real-life setting. The risk of bleeding with anticoagulation medications are well known, however could be better characterised for Asian patients, who are known to be at higher risk for peptic ulcer disease and bleeds. It is important to identify risk factors for bleeding, as, unlike warfarin, there are no effective antidotes for NOACS. Dosing with NOACs and co-administration with other drugs require further research. It is recommended that dabigatran is avoided/dose adjusted based on renal function, concomitant interacting drugs, and in high-risk patients. In real-life practice, there is no data to inform on the impact of varying doses on corresponding effectiveness and adverse events. A Hong Kong-wide cohort study is proposed to review oral anticoagulant usage and compare dabigatran to warfarin and dual-antiplatelet therapy in patients with AF from January 2010–December 2014. Pilot data indicate that there were more than 80,000 patients with AF within the study period. Multiple clinical outcomes will be explored including adverse events (GI events [ulcer and bleeds], bleeds and death from any cause), and clinical effectiveness, including stroke/systemic clot prevention. Exploration of prescribing patterns will enhance current understanding of the clinical impact of dosing and drug interactions. Risk factors for NOAC associated bleeding can be further characterised, informing on safe medication practice globally. 摘要 抗凝血藥能夠防止血液凝固，進而為心房顫動（最常見的心律不齊）患者或剛做過全關節置換手術的病人預防腦血管栓塞（中風）。一直以來，維他命K拮抗劑 （例如華法林warfarin）是抗凝血藥物的唯一選擇。不過，華法林有諸多缺點，它不但與許多食物和藥物都會發生交互作用，而且需要定期驗血以監察出血風險。若病人不適宜使用華法林，可服用抗血小板藥物（例如亞士匹靈aspirin，氯吡多clopidogrel，或兩者合併使用）取而代之。最近，被視為比傳統抗凝血藥更具優勢的新一代口服抗凝血藥（新口服抗凝血藥；包括達比加群dabigatran、利伐沙班rivaroxaban及阿哌沙班apixaban）獲准在臨床上使用。其中達比加群是首個獲批核使用的新口服抗凝血藥。自2008年在香港註冊以來，達比加群在香港的使用量穩步增加。 然而，達比加群的使用是值得探討的議題。雖然隨機對照試驗 (Randomized Controlled Trials) 的結果顯示，心房顫動患者服用最高商品劑量的達比加群比服用華法林能夠更有效地預防中風，但是前者服用後出現消化不良或胃腸道出血的人數卻較華法林多。與其相悖的是，另一項在現實生活中進行的觀測性研究卻發現達比加群的出血風險與華法林相若。儘管口服抗凝血藥存在出血風險眾所周知，但是對於較易患上消化性潰瘍及出血的亞洲人來說，口服抗凝血藥於他們身上的出血風險仍需進一步剖析。再者，新口服抗凝血藥不像華法林般擁有特效解毒劑，因此找到出血的風險因素尤其重要。 新口服抗凝血藥的劑量和它與其他藥物同時服用的情況，都需要更深入的研究。有建議指出，對於腎臟功能不全、同時服用與新口服抗凝血藥有交互作用的藥物或高風險的病人，服用達比加群時需要調整劑量，必要時應避免使用此類藥物。然而在臨床實踐中，目前還未有數據能夠闡明不同劑量的新口服抗凝血藥對其有效性和安全性的影響。 本研究是一項全港性的群組研究計劃。研究旨在分析2010年1月至2014年12月期間，新口服抗凝血藥在心房顫動患者中的使用情況，並將達比加群與華法林和雙抗血小板藥物進行比較。初步數據顯示，研究期間全港有超過80,000個心房顫動患者。多種不良反應（包括胃腸道事件（潰瘍和出血）、出血及任何原因導致的死亡）和臨床療效（包括預防中風或全身性血管栓塞）都在本研究探究範圍之內。透過分析新口服抗凝血藥的用藥狀況，本研究能使人們進一步認識藥物的使用劑量及藥物間交互作用對臨床的影響。而藉著剖析與新口服抗凝血藥相關的出血風險因素，本研究將為新口服抗凝血藥的處方安全提供重要資料，以供國際參考。

17102314.label: Realisation of objectives
17102314.value: With respect to the above mentioned objectives, they are realized in the following ways: 1. The initial study period was dedicated to data identification, retrieval, and cleaning. Subsequently, data analyses on the local prevalence of AF; prescribing trend of new oral anticoagulants (NOACs), warfarin and antiplatelet therapy among patients with AF; treatment duration, dosing and frequency; were performed. Characteristics of patients with AF, including co-morbidities and concurrent drug use, and its association with outcomes such as gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) were assessed (i.e. Objective 1). We also assessed the risk factor for GIB in patients on dabigatran. The work has led to publications in respected peer-reviewed journals (Gastroenterology [impact factor=18.1] and Heart Rhythm [impact factor=4.39]). 2. Further analysis was conducted to compare warfarin to aspirin and/or clopidogrel with respect to a range of clinical outcomes, such as ischemic stroke/systemic embolism, intracranial hemorrhage, GIB, and all-cause mortality (i.e. Objective 2). Absolute rates for each outcome were determined in all treatment groups. The results of the analysis are published in Heart Rhythm (impact factor= 4.39). Other outcomes of interest: hospital admissions and length of hospital stay were also assessed and the manuscript is under review by the Journal of the American College of Cardiology. Finally, additional studies were conducted to simultaneously compare the use of dabigatran, warfarin, and dual antiplatelet therapy with respect to their effectiveness and safety in patients with AF. The findings are expected to be published in an international peer-reviewed journal.

17102314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102314.value: We conducted a population-based study to investigate the risk factors for bleeding with dabigatran. The results showed that the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in dabigatran users increased among patients 75 years old or older (incidence rate ratio [IRR]=2.47; 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.66-3.68), patients with a history of peptic ulcers or GIB (IRR=2.31; 95%CI=1.54-3.46), and patients who used aspirin (IRR=1.52; 95%CI= 1.03-2.24). Concomitant use of gastroprotective agent was associated with a reduced risk of GIB (IRR=0.52; 95%CI=0.35-0.77). Subcategory analysis showed that use of proton-pump inhibitors (IRR=0.53; 95%CI=0.31-0.91) or histamine type-2 receptor antagonists (IRR=0.61; 95%CI=0.40-0.94) were associated with lower risk of GIB. The work has led to publication in a peer-reviewed journal (Gastroenterology, impact factor=18.1; Part C, paper 1: Chan EW et al. 2015). The research study revealed a large proportion of undertreated patients with AF in Hong Kong. We found that among the new patients with AF, 85% possessed several risk factors of ischemic stroke (e.g. aged≥75 years, congestive heart failure, or diabetes, etc.) and were categorized as high-risk patients in need of anticoagulation (OAC). However, it was found that only 23% of the high-risk patients received OACs (warfarin or new oral anticoagulants [NOACs]). The remaining 61% received antiplatelet drugs alone (aspirin and/or clopidogrel), and 16% received no antithrombotic therapy. Dabigatran was the most commonly used NOACs (85%). The most common dosage of dabigatran was 110 mg bid (75%), followed by 150 mg bid (13%), and 75 mg bid (9%). The results are published in a respected journal in the field of cardiology (Heart Rhythm, impact factor=4.39; Part C, paper 2: Chan EW et al. 2016). Further analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between anticoagulant use and hospital admissions. The manuscript is currently under review by the Journal of the American College of Cardiology (Part C, paper 3: Lau WCY et al. 2016). Finally, we compared dabigatran, warfarin, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for a range of clinical outcomes in the real-life practice. The manuscript is completed and will be submitted to an international peer-reviewed journal (Part C, paper 4: Lau WCY et al. 2016).

17102314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102314.value: The current work was the first territory-wide study that examined the pharmacoepidemiology of the use of NOACs, warfarin, and dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with AF in Hong Kong. A variety of further studies can be conducted in the respective area, such as exploring the underlying reasons why anticoagulants are largely underused in Hong Kong; the exact mechanism of how gastroprotective agents prevent GIB in patients taking dabigatran; underlying ethnic differences in the clearance and bleeding risk of dabigatran; and risk-benefits of dabigatran by quantifying the risk of thromboembolism versus the benefit of bleeding. This study also serves as the basis for future prospective randomized clinical trial to consolidate the evidence observed in this project, such as the effect of gastroprotective agents on reducing the risk of GIB in patients using dabigatran.

17102314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102314.value: Arial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia that increases the risk of stroke by 5-fold. Oral anticoagulants (OACs) are indicated for preventing stroke in patients with AF; however, evidence concerning the local use of OACs was unclear and had not been explored in a population-wide perspective. The current work was the first territory-wide study to examine the use of OACs in Hong Kong. We found that an unexpectedly large proportion of high-risk patients (>75%) did not receive OACs. While aspirin and/or clopidogrel were more commonly prescribed, their uses were associated with a two-fold increased risk of stroke when compared to OAC, reflecting the urgent need to improve the management of patients with AF. Our findings also suggested that acid-suppressing drugs could prevent bleeding with OAC. With the current wide usage of acid-suppressing drugs and their ease of use, a large group of patients are anticipated to benefit from the implementation of our research findings into clinical practice. The findings of our research are published in respected peer-reviewed journals, of which the readership is broad and international. We expect that the findings will influence clinical practice to improve patient management in stroke prevention in Hong Kong and aboard.

17102814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102814.value: The 2008 global financial crisis has had far-reaching impacts on the global economy. Turmoil in the banking sector led to downturns in stock markets, bankruptcies, housing repossessions and rises in unemployment worldwide. There have been numerous discussions about how best to spur economic recovery, but what impact has the recession had on health? What is the human cost of the economic downturn and subsequent austerity measures? Hong Kong’s economy was hit hard by the 2008 ‘financial tsunami’. It experienced four consecutive quarters of economic contraction between the last quarter of 2008 and the third quarter of 2009. Hong Kong’s unemployment rate also rose substantially, from 3.4% in August 2008 to a high of 5.4% in May-July 2009. The Hang Seng Index reached a historic high (31,897) in October 2007 but then fell dramatically to 10,676 in October 2008. The economic impact of the financial crisis is obvious, but what impact has it had on the Hong Kong people’s mental health in the face of economic hardship? There is a clear need for systematic investigations into the impact of the 2008 economic crisis in Hong Kong and whether social policies such as active labour market programs may have mitigated some of the crisis’ adverse effect on mental health in different countries globally. Our aim in the project is to investigate the impact of the 2008 recession on suicide in Hong Kong in comparison to Taiwan and South Korea, the socio-demographic groups / areas worst affected, any difference between this recession and the previous recession in 1997 and whether, globally, certain countries’ social policies have mitigated some of the negative effects. We have also proposed to investigate the effect of employment / income statuses and their changes on individuals’ mental health in the Hong Kong population. Our findings will have important implications and a potential long-term impact on policy. If we can better understand the negative effect of the recession on suicide, policy measures can be put in place to protect the most vulnerable in future economic downturns. Many parts of the world are still struggling with the ongoing recession, and economic instability and even stagnation could return to Hong Kong in the near future. If some countries have avoided a rise in suicides despite the significant economic downturn, then there is a clear need to implement similar policy initiatives to protect the health of populations during the ongoing and future recessions. 2008年的全球金融危機對全球經濟有深遠的影響。危機從銀行業開始，之後導致股市下跌、企業破產、房屋貸款違約致被回收，以及全球性的失業率上升。關於如何刺激經濟復甦，已有許多討論，但是經濟危機對健康的影響較少被關切：經濟蕭條和之後的緊縮政策，究竟對人口健康甚至生命有何影響？ 香港經濟也深受2008年「金融海嘯」的影響。在2008年最後一季，到2009第三季之間，香港經歷了接連四季的經濟衰退。香港失業率也顯著上升，從2008年8月的3.4%，增加到2009年5-7月的5.4%。恆生指數在2007年10月到達歷史高點（31,897點），但在一年後的2008年10月下跌到10,676點。金融危機的經濟影響顯著，但困難的經濟環境對香港人口的精神健康有何影響？ 因此，我們認為有必要針對2008年經濟危機對香港的影響，以及是否社會政策，例如就業扶助，是否在不同國家能夠減少經濟危機對精神健康的不良影響，進行系統性的研究。 此研究的目標，在於分析2008年經濟蕭條對香港自殺率的影響，並和鄰近經濟體（台灣和韓國）比較。我們也試圖找出受影響最深的人口族群、研究和上次1997年金融危機的不同處，以及是否某些國家的社會政策，有助減少經濟蕭條的負面影響。我們也將研究就業/所得，及其改變，對人們精神健康的效應。 我們的研究成果對於政策的擬定將有重要的意涵，以及潛在性的長遠影響。如果我們能夠更深入地了解經濟危機對自殺率的負面效應，那麼我們就能擬定政策來保護弱勢族群，免受未來經濟衰退的影響。目前，世界上的許多地區，仍然受困於當前的經濟蕭條，而經濟不穩定，甚至不景氣，也可能隨時重臨香港。如果某些國家在蕭條當中自殺率仍不見上升，那麼我們應該採用類似的策略，以保護人口的健康，免受當前與未來經濟蕭條的影響。

17102814.label: Realisation of objectives
17102814.value: We have examined the suicide situation in the two major financial crisis in Asia 1997 and 2008 for Hong Kong, Taiwan and South Korea. The impact of 2008 was not as serious as in 1997 for Hong Kong and Taiwan, whereas a significant increase was found in South Korea for both periods. Also, the impact is also age-gender dependent. For Hong Kong women was more severely affected in 2008 than their men counterparts and it can be explained by the increase in the women participating rate in the last decade. The older adults in South Korea has experienced largest increase during the period. The differential impact on age-gender has provided more information to develop more focused measures to mitigate the impact of the financial crisis. Financial expansion rather than contraction to responding to the financial crisis in Asia might be preferred as the Government's welfare support is relatively less generous in comparing to the west. By injecting additional resources to maintain the financial and economic activities of the society might be able to benefit the whole society to get through the financial storm. We have experienced some delay in the project as the original PI (shusen Chang) left HKU and join the National University of Taiwan in the middle of project. Thank you for the extension being granted such that we are still able to complete the project. The results would be helpful to prepare Hong Kong and other developed high income Asian countries to prepare for any financial crisis in the future. Hopefully the submitted paper will be found acceptable and appear soon,

17102814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102814.value: The 1997 and 2008 global financial crisis has had far-reaching impacts on the Asian and global economy, respectively. Turmoil in the finance and banking sector led to downturns in stock markets, bankruptcies, housing repossessions and rises in unemployment worldwide. There have been numerous discussions about how best to spur economic recovery, but what impact has the recession had on health? What is the human cost of the economic downturn and subsequent austerity measures? Have we learnt from the 1997 one such the impact of the 2008 have been mitigated. We have illustrated these by examining the suicide rates in Hong Kong, Taiwan and South Korea which are the developed high income places and the societies have been undergoing rapid changes. The ability to compare the impact of two major financial crises provides a new insight into the relation between suicide and economy crisis for three high-income and rapidly changing societies. Our findings show that regarding to the economy downturn and the suicide rate, in Hong Kong women had experienced larger negative impact in 2008 recession compared to year 1997 which might be due to the increasing number of women in the workforces and subsequently been subject to more stress than a housewife. On the positive side, Hong Kong male population has been benefited from the experience of the 1997 crisis such that the impact of 2008 one was less severe than the last one. This trend is also valid for the female population of Taiwan and female and male populations in South Korea. For the older adults, it seems the effect is more prominent among older adults in South Korea. The beginning and the duration of the impact of the economy recession is different for Hong Kong, Taiwan, and South Korea. Hong Kong is the last region among these three regions that was affected by the 1997 economy crisis, and South Korea is the last region during the recession in 2008. South Korea hits for a longer period by the financial crises in 1997 and 2008. The impact of economy downturn has been mitigated, nevertheless, it is important to examine the social support structure in time of crisis and how the population can get through without much tragedies. The welfare system should be improved especially during the time of crisis to provide buffer to protect those vulnerable groups in the time of financial crisis.

17102814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102814.value: Our aim of the project is to investigate the difference in impact of the 1997 and 2008 recession on suicides in Hong Kong in comparison to Taiwan and South Korea, the socio-demographic groups / areas worst affected, any difference between this recession and the previous recession in 1997 and whether, globally, certain countries’ social policies have mitigated some of the negative effects. It seems there is much heterogeneity of impact of the financial crisis on suicide deaths in these three places. This needs to be studied carefully in the local context in order to come up with effective mitigation measures. There are also much room for improvement in the data collection as we have spent considerable time in collecting the information for the project.

17102814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102814.value: It seems Hong Kong and Taiwan has learnt from the painful experience in 1997 such that the impact of the 2008 one is limited, whereas South Korea had experienced another significant increase of number of suicides in 2008. There is much heterogeneity in its impact of the financial crisis on suicide deaths in these three places. There are specific sex/age groups appeared to be more vulnerable to certain socioeconomic factors than other groups. It is important to make preparation for facing the challenge arising from economic crisis. It is important to examine the social support structure in time of crisis and how the population can get through without much tragedies. The welfare system should be improved especially during the time of crisis to provide buffer to protect those vulnerable groups in the time of financial crisis. Financial expansion rather than contraction to responding to the financial crisis in Asia might be preferred as the Government's welfare support is relatively less generous in comparing to the west. By injecting additional resources to maintain the financial and economic activities of the society might be able to benefit the whole society to get through the financial storm.

17102914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102914.value: 內耳發育需要早期細胞特化分化,感知及非感知器官結構部件形態形成這兩者的緊密協調，令細胞可以在正確位置發育成特定細胞種類。感覺毛細胞及它們相連的支持細胞對於內耳的聽覺功能及平衡功能起決定作用。這些細胞作為機械應力感受器可以偵測聲音（耳蝸毛細胞），重力以及加速度 （前庭毛細胞），並將這些信息通過感受神經元傳達至中樞神經系統。這些感知器官由耳表皮前體細胞發育而來，然後發展成內耳六個感知器官內的毛細胞和支持細胞，以及連接毛細胞的神經元。早於內耳整體結構的出現，前體細胞在聽囊的空間位置已經決定了感知及非感知器官在內耳中的正確形成位置。而這些前體細胞的位置可以通過檢測一些對於細胞特化及分化有調節作用的轉錄因子的表達而確定。部分或整體缺失這些前體細胞，或者打亂它們的空間分佈形態，都可導致內耳功能被破壞。透過對Sox2等位突變小鼠模型 Lcc (Lcc/Lcc, 全聾) 以及 Ysb （Ysb/Ysb， 嚴重聽力喪失）的研究，我們發現Sox2對於聽力和平衡都有着重要作用。其中，Lcc/Lcc小鼠喪失了6個感知器官，既沒有毛細胞也沒有支持細胞，而Ysb/Ysb小鼠中，僅感知表皮組織不能正確形成。這些小鼠模型表明嚴重缺失(Lcc/Lcc)或部分缺失(Ysb/Ysb) Sox2可導致內耳發育不良的表型，而我們的研究揭示了對於前感知和感知器官的發育，Sox2有着劑量依賴性的特性。 為了進一步揭示感知器官發育的分子機理，我們分析了Sox2等位突變小鼠模型的全球基因表達譜。從中，我們發現BMP/TGFβ是其中一個受到嚴重影響的信號通路。而為了研究BMP/TGFβ信號通路在內耳發育中的作用，我們特異性在聽囊內滅活了這條通路。BMP/TGFβ的缺失導致嚴重的內耳異常，包括前庭半規管的缺失以及耳蝸退化。在突變內耳中，我們發現擴張的前感知組織，進而導致多餘的感知器官,毛細胞和支持細胞的出現。這些研究成果使我們做出以下推測: Sox2和BMP/TGFβ信號通路在內耳發育過程中相互拮抗而調節,從而使感知及非感知細胞得以在正確的位置上發育成器官，而這個拮抗調節過程是在轉錄及轉錄後水平上受到調控的。 在這項研究中，我們將充分利用發育遺傳學，基因組學技術，細胞生物學以及生物化學來證實我們的推測，深入探討Sox2和BMP/TGFβ信號通路之間相互作用的分子機理，從而理解內耳發育過程中感知及非感知器官形成的機理。現有數據表明，每800個新生兒中就有一個聽力受損，而超過60%的70歲以上老人飽受聽力退化之苦，其主要病因都是由於內耳毛細胞的永久殞壞。我們的研究將充分闡明內耳中感知及非感知細胞的發育是如何受到轉錄及轉錄後調控的，從而為臨床上耳再生療法及修復療法提供重要有效的試驗理論基礎。

17102914.label: Realisation of objectives
17102914.value: Development of the inner ear requires coordination of induction and specification of 6 sensory organs comprising: three sensory cell types, hair cells (HCs), supporting cells (SCs), and sensory neurons that contribute to the spiral ganglion (SGNs), derived from a common progenitor early in otic development, and non-sensory cells, all properly located. The dorsal otocyst contributes the vestibule, the ventral portion, the cochlear. Domains within the otic vesicle (OV) mark future compartments, prior to the emergence of different cell types. Hypomorphic mutants, Sox2Ysb/Ysb and Sox2Lcc/Lcc, Sox2EGFP/Lc identified SOX2 as the master regulator of otic prosensory development. Inactivating Smad4, the transducer of BMP/TGFβ signaling, in the E8.5 OV, causes enhanced prosensory development and ectopic HCs/SCs in the in non-sensory cochlear wall of Smad4cKO/cKO mutants. Bulk transcriptome analyses of Sox2EGFP/Lcc E9.5 otic vesicles revealed significant differential expression changes (DEGs) in regulators of BMP/TGFβ pathway including genes encoding E3 ubiquitin ligases that regulate ubiquitination/deubiquitination (e.g. Usp9x) of SMAD4. We hypothesized that disruption of SOX2 or SMAD4 impacts on the balance of sensory versus non-sensory cell identity. We aimed to test if SOX2 and SMAD4 function antagonistically and whether Sox2 controls ubiquitination of SMAD4. Objective 1: Genetic definition of relationship between Sox2 and Smad4 Using Pax2Cre to generate otic-specific loss of BMP transducers, Smad1 and Smad5, we tested for genetic interaction with Sox2. Expression of prosensory markers (SOX2, P27KIP1) or non-sensory marker, GATA2, were unchanged is otic-specific Smad1;Smad5 mutants, different from Pax2Cre;Smad4cKO/cKO. The impact of SMAD4 otic deficiency should be a consequence of loss of both BMP and TGFβ signaling. We tested whether reducing SOX2 dosage by removing one Sox2 allele, could modify Sox2EGFP/+;Smad4cKO/cKO mutant phenotype but the inner ear phenotype of E14.5 Smad4cKO/cKO was unaffected. We then asked whether SOX2 protein levels and allelic dosage are correlated. Quantitation of SOX2 protein level in Sox2EGFP/+, Sox2Lcc/Lcc, Sox2EGFP/Lcc and Pax2Cre;Sox2EGFP/cKO E9.5 OVs revealed similar SOX2 expression in Sox2EGFP/+ and Sox2+/+OV, implicating feedback autoregulation, where SOX2 protein negatively regulates transactivation of Sox2 to maintain levels. The expanded SOX2EGFP domain in Sox2EGFP/Lcc E14.5 cochleae compared to Sox2EGFP/+ and enhanced LacZ expression in Sox2βgeo/Lcc dermal papillae compared to Sox2βgeo/+ is consistent. This finding explains why Sox2 heterozygosity did not modify the phenotype. Since Sox2 is absolutely required for prosensory development, testing for interaction between Sox2 and Smad4 genetically is not feasible. Objectives 2 & 3: Impact of reduced SOX2 levels on BMP/TGFβ signaling We measured the activity of BMP signaling in E10.5 and E9.5 otocysts by immunostaining of pSMAD1/5 and application of proximity ligation assay (PLA) which detects SMAD4-pSMAD1/5 complexes. No differences in frequency of positive signals in Sox2EGFP/Lcc and Sox2EGFP/+ otocysts were found by PLA. In wild-type, immunostaining revealed a gradient of pSMAD1/5 staining in the OV (dorsal, high; ventral, low), consistent with an opposing pattern of BMP activity to SOX2. Staining intensity for the pSMAD1/5 positive domain was unaffected in Sox2EGFP/Lcc. Usp9x, a SMAD4 deubiquitinase, was identified from bulk RNAseq as a potential SOX2 target. USP9X is expressed in E9.5 OV but conditional otic knock-out mutants of Usp9x did not impact on inner ear development. The potential role of ubiquitinylation of SMAD4 in inner ear development cannot be excluded because of likely redundancy in ubiquitinases. Testing for redundancy requires generating compound knockouts of different ubiquitinases. Unfortunately, we did not have sufficient resources to test this possibility. Objective 4: Molecular insights into Smad4 control of otic cell fate Bulk RNA sequencing cannot distinguish between genuine changes in gene transcription, from those attributable to changed cell identity and populations. We sequenced 135 single cells from Pax2Cre;Smad4cKO/cKO;Rosa26tdTomato/+ and Pax2Cre;Smad4cKO/+;Rosa26tdTomato/+ E9.5 OVs. were identified. Expression of Id1, Id3 (BMP target genes), were reduced in mutant cells and these cells clustered separately from controls in tSNE plots. Significantly mutant cells not wild-type, expressed Lfng (SOX2 target and regulator), a neurogenesis promoter, and Sox2. Neurog1 and Neurod1, specific neurosensory and neuroblast markers respectively, were turned on in Smad4cKO/cKO cells. These data suggest non-sensory identity switched to a neurosensory/prosensory one. This could explain the ectopic HCs and SCs in Smad4cKO/cKO and are consistent with a suppressive activity of Smad4 on neurogenesis. Cell fate changes and upregulation of BMP/TGFβ targets in Sox2 mutant cochleae To address whether Sox2 deficiency causes a change in cell fate, we lineage traced the fate of Sox2 descendant cells in Sox2CreERT2/Lcc;Rosa26tdTomato/+ and Sox2CreERT2/Ysb;Rosa26tdTomato/+ compared with Sox2CreERT2/+;Rosa26tdTomato/+ controls after Cre activation at E12.5. In wild-type, at E14.5, most of the E12.5 tdTomato+ Sox2 descendant cells in the cochlea contributed to the prosensory domain and the greater epithelial ridge (GER). This population was mutually exclusive to the non-sensory domain marked by GATA2 in the lesser epithelial ridge (LER). In Sox2CreERT2/Ysb;Rosa26tdTomato/+ and Sox2CreERT2/Lcc;Rosa26tdTomato/+ ears, expression of the GATA2+ domain was expanded and partially overlapped with the Sox2 descendant domain. Significantly the size of the P27KIP1+ prosensory domain was reduced or disappeared. The data suggest reduced SOX2 in otic progenitors causes a change from prosensory to nonsensory fate. Since Gata2 is a known direct target of SMAD4, this result is consistent with an upregulation of SMAD4 activity in Sox2 mutant OV. We followed fate of Sox2 mutant descendants to E17.5 following Cre activation at E12.5. In control, tdTomato+ Sox2 descendant cells contributed to HCs (MYO6A+), SCs (SOX2+), Reissner’s membrane (SLC26A7+), interdental cells (NR2F1+). Mutant cells expressing tdTomato+GATA2+ were present in the E17.5 Sox2CreERT2/Lcc;Rosa26tdTomato/+ truncated cochlea. Reissner’s membrane and interdental cells were intact, but HCs and SCs were missing, and the entire cochlea duct was tdTomato+. The data is consistent with the essential role for Sox2 in specifying HCs and SCs but not Reissner’s membrane, interdental cells and the conversion of mutant cells to a nonsensory identity. Increased apoptosis adjacent to the Sox2-descendant domain in E11.5 and E12.5 cells marked by Cre activity at E9.5, suggest SOX2 cells provide extrinsic factors for non-sensory cells survival. Single cell transcriptomics reveal SOX2 deficiency causes changed cell identity It was important to distinguish between altered cell fate impacting on cell population composition versus individual cells’ transcriptional activity. We sequenced 316 Sox2EGFP/Lcc and Sox2EGFP/+ E9.5 OV single cells. Wild-type and mutant cells clustered as distinct populations. Sox2EGFP/+ cells were either neuroblast-like (Neurod1+Isl1+) or progenitor-like (Pax2+Lfng+). By contrast a small proportion of Sox2EGFP/Lcc cells were neuroblast-like, the majority were of mixed/hybrid identity, expressing both neuronal and progenitor markers such as Isl1, Oc90+,Neurod1+. Factors important for neuroblast/neuronal identity (Neurog1, Ntf3, Bdnf, Fgf3, Fgf8, Isl1) were downregulated in mutant cells. Instead mutant cells expressed non-sensory genes Lmx1a, Gbx2, Tbx1, Wnt6. Comparison between mutant vs wild-type progenitor-like cells confirmed the hybrid prosensory/sensory/ non-sensory character of the mutant cells which displayed upregulated expression of dorsal OV related genes (e.g. Msx1, Tbx1, Lmx1a, Gbx2, Nr2f1). Concomitantly mutant cells expressed higher levels of neuronal genes such as Neurod1. Therefore loss of Sox2 leads a changed cell identity to a “confused” hybrid state. Our study implicates SMAD4 in inhibiting prosensory and neurosensory cell fate, which is opposite to SOX2 action. The upregulation of Sox2 and prosensory and neurosensory genes in Smad4 mutant cells and vice versa in Sox2 mutants is consistent with antagonistic regulation of common pathways. The critical role of SOX2 in maintaining cell identity is likely achieved by a combination of transactivation of prosensory genes and repression of non-sensory genes. Repressing mechanisms could include antagonizing SMAD4 control of non-sensory cell identity.

17102914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102914.value: How relative proportions of sensory versus non-sensory cells in the developing otocyst is controlled is poorly understood. We tested the hypothesis that SOX2 and SMAD4 antagonise each other to achieve balanced numbers of sensory and non-sensory cell fate/cell. 1. Comparison of SOX2 protein levels in Sox2EGFP/+ OV, with wild-type, provided evidence for an autoregulatory mechanism in which levels of SOX2 protein are maintained at wild type levels, even with only 1 functional allele. 2. Deficiency for SOX2 causes cell fate changes and upregulation of BMP/TGFβ targets in Sox2 mutant cochleae. By a combination of lineage tracing and marker analyses, we found reduced SOX2 in otic progenitors causes a shift in otic cell fate from prosensory to nonsensory, judged by ectopic expression of GATA2. Since Gata2 is a known direct target of SMAD4, this result is consistent with upregulated SMAD4 activity in Sox2 mutant cells. SOX2 cells were found to provide extrinsic factors for non-sensory cells survival. 3. Single cell transcriptomics revealed SOX2 deficiency causes changed cell identity We sequenced Sox2EGFP/Lcc and Sox2EGFP/+ E9.5 OV single cells. Wild-type and mutant cells clustered as distinct populations. Sox2EGFP/+ cells were either neuroblast-like or progenitor-like. By contrast fewer Sox2EGFP/Lcc cells were neuroblast-like, the majority were of mixed/hybrid identity, expressing both neuronal and progenitor markers. Comparison between mutant vs wild-type progenitor-like cells confirmed the “confused” hybrid prosensory/sensory/non-sensory character of the mutant cells, which displayed upregulated expression of dorsal OV related genes (e.g. Msx1, Tbx1, Lmx1a, Gbx2, Nr2f1). Concomitantly mutant cells expressed reduced levels of neuronal genes such as Neurod1 while its regulator Neurog1 was unchanged. Implications: SOX2 may cooperate with NEUROG1 to control neuroblast differentiation. SOX2 may control specification of neuronal and prosensory lineages by repressing expression of nonsensory and dorsal OV genes 4. Single cell transcriptome analyses of OV-specific Smad4 mutants revealed an opposite impact compared to Sox2 OV-specific knock-outs. We found Smad4 mutant OV cells expressed markers for neuroblasts and sensory neurogenic genes such as Lfng, Neurod1, Neurog1. Summary: Our study implicates SMAD4 in inhibiting prosensory and neurosensory cell fate, opposite to SOX2 action. Upregulation of Sox2 and prosensory and neurosensory genes in Smad4 mutant cells and vice versa, in Sox2 mutants, is consistent with antagonistic regulation of common pathways. The critical role of SOX2 in maintaining cell identity is likely achieved by a combination of transactivation of prosensory genes, repression of non-sensory genes, including antagonizing SMAD4 control of non-sensory cell identity.

17102914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102914.value: Our results show that SOX2 is a pivotal factor for lineage decision making and maintenance of prosensory cells by both cell autonomous and non-cell autonomous mechanisms. Our work also provides evidence for opposing controls of otic cell identity mediated by SOX2 and SMAD4. The single cell transcriptome data we have derived for otic cells from wild-type, Sox2 and Smad4 mutants are a rich resource for identifying molecular signatures of the constituent cells in the OV, target genes of SOX2, SMAD4 and for building gene regulatory networks (GRN) controlling cell identity in the otic vesicle. Further development of the work are: clarification of the molecular nature of SOX2 and SMAD4 interaction; acquiring knowledge of the epigenetic changes involved. Integration of the data will be invaluable for insights into the GRN controlling otic cell fate, for the discovery of deafness genes and understanding the underlying molecular pathogenesis. Future work should include identification of epigenetic controls, using the mouse models for drug testing and/or gene therapy.

17102914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102914.value: Development of the inner ear requires coordinated induction and specification of 6 sensory organs that are essential for hearing and balance function, all in the correct location and including the specific cell types comprising hair cells (HCs), supporting cells (SCs), and sensory neurons. Perturbing balanced production of prosensory and nonsensory cells in the inner ear, no matter how small, leads to hearing loss. However, how the balance between prosensory and nonsensory is controlled is poorly understood. In this project we discovered that two master regulators, SOX2 and SMAD4 work by opposing mechanisms to ensure the proper specification of sensory and non-sensory precursors in the early stages of inner ear development. The discoveries are based on tracking the fate of mutant otic cells and by comparing and analyzing gene expression signatures of mutant and normal single cells in mice. One child out of 800 is born with hearing impairment and 60% of people over 70yrs suffer some hearing loss, caused by the loss of hair cells in the inner ear. Our data and discoveries are valuable for identifying deafness genes for molecular diagnosis, for understanding underlying mechanisms of hearing loss with applications for future development of therapeutic approaches for restoring hearing.
