17103214.value: 自2013年春天以來的H7N9禽流感病毒感染人是1997年以來最嚴重的流感病毒跨種感染，清楚瞭解病毒跨種感染和傳播的機制非常重要。病毒跨物種傳播受到多種因素的制約，包括受體結合的特異性，病毒的複制和宿主的先天免疫限制。序列分析發現H7N9病毒的血凝素（ HA）包含Q226L的突變可能賦予病毒壹定程度的結合人類型唾液酸受體的能力，然而，該Q226L突變已在禽H9N2病毒普遍存在，但許多年以來，H9N2 只發生非常少的人類感染，所以分析其他病毒因素在2013 H7N9禽流感病毒的感染人過程中的能力非常必要。 流感病毒通過病毒聚合酶複合體 （PB1，PB2 和PA亞基）在細胞核中轉錄和複製病毒基因組。病毒聚合酶複合體在細胞的這應能力是病毒複制和跨物種傳播的關鍵。對H7N9病毒的PB2基因的分析發現，大約94.7% 的H7N9病毒株至少帶有壹種已知的PB2基因這應性標記，如E627K，D701N 或Q591K，這是壹個不尋常的特點，更值得注意的是其中有部分的H7N9病毒還帶有新的標記， K526R。我們的研究還發現發現近80%來自印度尼西亞的H5N1病毒和幾乎所有1970年後的季節性H3N2A亞型流感病毒的PB2基因都帶有K526R。因此，除了E27K，D01N，590S / 591R和591K， 526R可能是禽流感病毒向哺乳動物這應另壹個標記，本研究將系統深入分析流感病毒PB2-K526R在哺乳動物細胞繁殖的適應性功能的分子基礎。

17103214.label: Realisation of objectives
17103214.value: While many subtypes of influenza A virus are present in nature, host restriction limits influenza virus cross species transmission and replication. To overcome host barriers, viruses must gain the ability to bind cell receptors, adapt to use host machinery for genome transcription and replication and avoid restriction by elements of the host innate immune system during virus infection. Although receptor specificity is critical for efficient transmission in a specific host, replication is equally essential for host adaptation. The influenza virus replication complex is composed of three polymerase subunits (PB1, PB2 and PA) plus NP. Characterization of host adaptation markers among human isolates is important for recognizing avian influenza A viruses with high potential for cross-species transmission. Adaptation of avian influenza A virus polymerases in mammals has been extensively studied and the most well-characterized adaptation markers are located in the PB2 polymerase subunit, which is involved in transcription and replication of viral RNA in infected cells. This study focused on the characterization of host adaptive strategies of avian influenza virus through the study of H7N9 and other influenza viruses which have infected humans. All proposed objectives have been achieved and are summarized as follows: 1. Influenza virus infection involves receptor binding, endocytosis of the viral genome, nuclear import of the viral genome, transcription and replication in the nucleus, nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, packaging and budding stages. Upon entry of host cells, gaining the ability to transcribe and replicate the viral genomes is essential to achieve infection. In addition to attaining) host-specific receptor binding through changes to viral hemagglutinin, host adaptation mutations in the basic polymerase subunit PB2 are critical for avian influenza viruses to gain the ability to infect and replicate in mammalian cells. Previous reports have described the host adaptive mutations PB2-E627K, PB2-D701N and PB2-Q591K among different influenza virus subtypes. This study identified a novel adaptive mutation, K526R, in H7N9 virus, and further revealed that this mutation is closely associated with human H5N1 virus infections in Indonesia. More importantly, it was found that H3N2 gained the PB2-K526R mutation immediately after the 1968 pandemic and that this mutation synergistically enhances virus replication together with PB2-E627K. Since the 2013 H7N9 outbreak, human infections have continued to occur and increasing numbers of isolates carrying dual PB2-E627K-K526R or single PB2-K526R mutations were identified each year since, suggesting that PB2-K526R plays an important role in human H7N9 virus infections. PB2-K526R is a novel adaptive mutation that we have detected in the genomes of both avian and seasonal influenza viruses. Our data show that H7N9 is an unusual virus which utilizes multiple adaptive strategies to cross the host barrier and infect humans. 2. To understand the role of K526R in influenza virus replication, we have systematically analyzed the functions of K526R alongside those of other adaptive mutations and found that K526R can function alone in some influenza viruses, such as H7N9 and H5N1 (Indonesia lineage), work together with E627K and/or D701N adaptive mutations to augment virus replication and transcription in the H3N2 virus and avian influenza viruses, respectively, but that it has little effect when combined with Q591K. This study provided new insight into a collaborative mechanism whereby different adaptive mutations in the PB2 protein synergize to promote virus replication in mammalian cells. 3. Influenza virus transcribes and replicates the viral genome in the nucleus. We have analyzed the functional coordination of PB2 proteins derived from PB2 genes carrying host adaptive mutations with other functional viral proteins, including the polymerase subunits PA & PB1, nucleoprotein (NP) and viral nuclear export protein (NEP). We found that acquisition of K526R is necessary for optimization of the interaction between PB2 and NEP and to achieve RNP polymerase fitness during virus replication. Our finding clearly indicated that the addition of K526R to E627K in PB2 was essential to compensate for the introduction of an avian PB1 to the H3N2 virus in 1968, providing seasonal H3N2 virus with the fitness required for efficient circulation in humans. 4. The function of the influenza virus polymerase complex (RNP) is closely associated with NEP, with expression of NEP being regulated by splicing of NS mRNA, which generates NS1 and NEP mRNAs. Investigating the regulation of NEP expression and virus replication in the H7N9 virus, this study identified a novel substitution, G540A, in the NS segment of H7N9 and found that this substitution is situated within the motif of a formerly uncharacterized splicing enhancer which acts on the viral genome. The NS-G540A substitution modulates splicing efficiency of NS1 and NEP mRNA through interaction with the host factor SF2. We found that the H9N2 virus acquired this mutation through an evolutionary process, prior to the reassortment event that generated the H7N9 virus, which inherited the NS-G540A segment. Our findings indicate that NS-G540A primes H7N9 virus with the ability to replicate in humans without affecting its fitness in the avian host. This part of the study provides evidence to show that, in addition to PB2, the NS segment also plays an important role in host adaption to enhance H7N9 virus replication in mammalian cells. 5. Although the E627K host adaptation substitution in the PB2 protein was identified in 1992, the molecular mechanisms associated with PB2 adaptations remain largely unknown. Previous work on the function of PB2 adaptive mutations has mainly focused on the effect of the mutations on the enhancement of viral polymerase activity in mammalian cells. Other studies have attempted to investigate whether adaptive mutations in PB2 may facilitate evasion of host restriction of virus replication. However, no definitive conclusions have been reached on the molecular mechanisms set in action by PB2 host adaptations. Because influenza virus replication progresses in multiple stages and the virus relies on host machinery for nucleocytoplasmic ( trafficking to complete the replication cycle, we hypothesized that PB2 adaptive strategies may involve vRNA trafficking following genome replication in the nucleus. To understand the molecular basis of PB2 host adaptive strategies in mammalian cells, we analyzed viral vRNA trafficking in infected mammalian cells and found that intracellular trafficking of vRNA lacking any PB2 adaptive mutation is inhibited and virus replication correspondingly compromised in mammalian cells. Our study characterized a novel mechanism by which mammalian cells limit avian influenza virus replication by interrupting the normal trafficking process of vRNA after nuclear export. Further, we discovered that influenza virus carrying any currently known adaptive mutation in PB2 is not interrupted by this host restriction process. Finally, this study found that host restriction of avian influenza virus in mammalian cells involves a non-canonical autophagy process leading to degradation of vRNA, and that acquisition of adaptive mutations in the PB2 allows viruses to evade this restriction. In conclusion, this project analyzed PB2-associated host adaptive strategies for replication in mammalian cells and identified a novel mutation, K526R, in H7N9, H5N1 and seasonal H3N2 viruses. We characterized the function of K526R in virus replication and the interaction of PB2 with other polymerase subunits and NEP, identifying a unique host adaptive mutation (NS-G540A) which regulates NS1/NEP expression to promote virus replication in mammalian cells, and also revealed a previously uncharacterized mechanism by which the host limits virus replication through interruption of the vRNA trafficking process, with only viruses possessing host adaptive mutations in the PB2 evading this restriction.

17103214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103214.value: Pandemic influenza is caused by cross species transmission of zoonotic influenza A viruses from birds or swine. Influenza viruses encounter host barriers during virus entry, transcription and replication in the nucleus, nuclear and cytoplasmic trafficking, and assembly and budding. One of the most important influenza A virus host adaptions is the acquisition of mutations in the PB2 gene. Despite several adaptive mutations in the PB2 being described, details of the molecular basis of their effects remain elusive. Several subtypes of avian influenza virus have caused human infections since 1997. The persistent emergence of human cases of avian H7N9 virus infection since 2013 has triggered speculation that this virus may be unusually able to cause cross species infection in humans. This study investigated these H7N9 virus properties: 1. We identified a novel host adaptive mutation, K526R, in the PB2 of some H7N9 viruses and revealed that this mutation is also present in a lineage of H5N1 viruses in which no PB2 adaptive mutation has been found before. More significantly, we found that K526R was acquired by the H3N2 virus soon after the 1968 pandemic, which may partly explain the optimal circulation ability of H3N2 in humans since then (Research output: Peer-reviewed publications 1 & 4). 2. Functions of PB2-K526R in H7N9 and H3N2 viruses were characterized in in vitro and in vivo experiments. We revealed a mechanism by which the K526R mutation in PB2 enhances interaction between polymerase complexes and NEP in H7N9 virus, promoting replication in mammalian cells, and further optimized polymerase activity during the formation of pandemic H3N2 virus. Most significantly, this study revealed a hitherto uncharacterized mechanism by which mammalian cells limit avian influenza by interrupting vRNA trafficking during virus replication. Influenza viruses can evade this restriction using multiple adaptive strategies incorporating mutations in the PB2. Some of these findings have been published (Research output: Peer-reviewed publications 1 & 3) or presented at an international conference (Research output: Conference 1). A manuscript on PB2-associated host adaptation and vRNA trafficking is under preparation and will be published soon. 3. During influenza virus replication, viral NEP is closely associated with PB2 and other polymerase subunits. This study identified a novel G540A substitution in the NS segment which modulates NS1/NEP expression and further characterized the molecular process by which NS-G540A substitution primes H7N9 and other avian influenza viruses for human infection (Research output: Peer-reviewed publication 2 and Conference 2).

17103214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103214.value: Cross species transmission of avian influenza A virus is restricted by host barriers which may include receptor specificity, replication-limiting mechanisms and host innate immunity. If direct cross species transmission of virus from avian species to humans can occur, it seems reasonable to suggest that certain host-specific adaptations must pre-exist in some avian influenza viruses, and that these adaptations do not impair virus replication fitness in avian species, ensuring virus prevalence. It is postulated that host adaption is a progressive process and may begin prior to human infection. For those avian viruses with a pre-existing adaptation promoting replication ability, any further adaptation during replication within a mammalian host may transform the virus into a fully human virus. This study found that H7N9 viruses utilize multiple adaptive strategies in the PB2 and NS segments that prime the virus for human infection. It is necessary to characterize the pandemic potential of H7N9 and other viruses which have been generated with the same internal genome segments. Further studies should aim to characterize the specific functions of PB2-K526R and NS-G540A in the host adaptation of avian influenza H7N9, H5N1 and H3N2 viruses.

17103214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103214.value: Pandemic influenza is unpredictable and has occurred four times during the past 100 years. Although host barriers limit cross species transmission of animal influenza viruses to humans, human infections with H5 and H7 subtype avian influenza viruses have been observed sporadically since 1997, with H7N9 viruses causing the most human cases of cross species infection since 2013. There are concerns that some of these avian influenza viruses may gain the ability to transmit efficiently in humans or reassort with other human viruses, forming a pandemic virus. What make this virus so unusual compared to other avian influenza viruses? What are the molecular determinants which are critical for avian influenza viruses to jump species to humans? We have identified and characterized mutations in the viral polymerase PB2 and non-structural (NS) genome segments which prime for and enhance virus replication in mammalian cells. Our findings suggest that not all avian influenza viruses can infect humans, but that H5 (since 2003) and H7 (since 2013) subtype viruses have gained adaptive functions which allow them to replicate in mammalian cells without affecting their fitness for circulation in avian species. Further adaptation of these viruses in human cells could generate a new pandemic strain.

17103514.label: Realisation of objectives
17103514.value: The overall objective of the proposed study is to determine the functional role of the newly identified PD-1 isoform, Δ42PD-1, in modulating host immunity. Based on our preliminary results, we hypothesize that Δ42PD-1 engages its receptor TLR4 expressed mainly on dendritic cells to play an important immune regulatory role in modulating innate and adaptive immunity. To test this hypothesis, we propose a well-focused study with two specific objectives: (1) To understand the role of the Δ42PD-1/TLR4 pathway in innate immune responses; and (2) To determine the function of the Δ42PD-1/TLR4 pathway in modulating adaptive immune responses. To address the specific aim one, we produced the soluble Δ42PD-1fc protein (sΔ42PD-1) to stimulate various types of immune cells. We found that sΔ42PD-1fc primarily induce robust cytokine production in dendritic cells via interaction with TLR4 receptor and downstream pathways. Moreover, we demonstrated that sΔ42PD-1 but not sPD-1 was able to induce inflammatory cytokines in a humanized mouse model. sΔ42PD-1+T cells exhibited reduced function in terms of cytokine production. Importantly, using two in-house Δ42PD-1-specific monoclonal antibodies, we found that Δ42PD1+Vδ2 T cells were increased in early HIV-1 infected patients, which were correlated with immune activation. Δ42PD1 was induced in vitro upon HIV-1 infection and was accompanied by high co-expression of gut-homing receptors CCR9/CD103. Gut-homing of HIV-induced Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells into small intestines after adoptive transfer led to inflammatory pathology and tissue damage in humanized mice. Inhibition of the Δ42PD1–TLR4 axis successfully reduced the cytokine effect induced by Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells and mucosal pathological effects. This finding has implicated that Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells might play a role in immune activation soon after HIV-1 primary infection and may serve as a target for the investigation of disease with mucosal inflammation. We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective 1 by defining a critical role of the Δ42PD-1/TLR4 pathway in innate immune responses. To address the specific aim two, we compared sPD1-p24fc, msΔIgVPD-1-p24fc and sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccines. We found that sΔ42PD1-p24fc induced slightly or much stronger antigen-specific T cells immune responses compared with sPD1-p24fc or msΔIgVPD-1-p24fc, respectively. Interestingly, while sPD-1-mediated intracellular processing of HIV-1 p24 in dendritic cells (DCs) for antigen cross-presentation, sΔ42PD1 did not seem to engage the same route. Instead, we found that sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccine could recruit relatively more DCs into spleen and induce better DC activation, maturation and antigen presentation by interacting with TLR4 than other vaccines, which determine the levels of T cell adaptive immunity observed. sPD1-p24fc vaccine preferentially promoted CD8+ conventional DCs (cDCs) maturation, whilst sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccine activated monocyte-derived DCs to induce stronger CD4+ and CD8+ T cells proliferation and cytokine release. Therefore, sΔ42PD1-based vaccine likely engages distinct mechanism underlying vaccine-induced potent T cell responses. More importantly, we tested vaccine efficacy in a viral challenge model using chimeric EcoHIV in immune competent mice. Although vaccine-induced potent T cell responses controlled viral replication but could not eliminate infected cells completely. We then found that EcoHIV-infected myeloid derived immune suppressive cells were highly resistant to antigen-specific T cells. We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective 2 by defining a critical role of the Δ42PD-1/TLR4 pathway in adaptive immune responses. In summary, we have revealed a role of the newly identified PD-1 isoform, Δ42PD-1, in modulating host innate and adaptive immunity. We have worked hard on the proposed study with one high impact SCI publication (Nature Microbiology), which acknowledged this grant support. Another paper is now in preparation. We were able to overcome the technical difficulties especially on efficacy experiments by establishing both humanized and EcoHIV mouse models. During the study, we have trained a Ph.D. student at HKU.

17103514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103514.value: In this study, we uncovered the role of Δ42PD-1 in HIV-induced gut-homing Vδ2 T cells that may contribute to innate immune activation and intestinal pathogenesis during acute HIV-1 infection. Specifically, gut-homing γδ T cells displayed significantly upregulated Δ42PD1 expression in acute (~20%) HIV-1 patients compared to chronic HIV-1 patients (~11%) and healthy controls (~2%). Moreover, the frequency of Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells correlates positively with plasma levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and fatty-acid-binding protein before detectable lipopolysaccharide in acute patients. The expression of Δ42PD1 can be induced by in vitro HIV-1 infection and is accompanied by high co-expression of gut-homing receptors CCR9/CD103, which mediated migration of HIV-infected Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells into small intestinal and cause inflammatory damage there after adoptive transfer. In addition, blockade of Δ42PD1 significantly reduced the cytokine effects induced by Δ42PD1+Vδ2 cells in vitro, as well as the mucosal pathological effect in humanized mice. The results of this study have been published in Nature Microbiology in 2017. To determine the role of Δ42PD1 in modulating adaptive immune response, we compared the immunogenicity, possible mechanism and efficacy of sPD1-p24fc, msΔIgVPD-1-p24fc and sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccines. As mentioned above, we found that sΔ42PD1-based vaccine likely engages distinct mechanism underlying vaccine-induced potent T cell responses. More importantly, we found similar to sPD1-p24fc, sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccine showed significant protection against EcoHIV infection in immune competent mice. sΔ42PD1-p24fc could significantly decrease the proviral load in splenocytes for 100 fold compared with controls. Furthermore, sΔ42PD1-p24fc vaccine resulted in higher number of multiple DC subsets accumulating in spleen and enhanced maturation of conventional CD8+ and Mo-DCs compared with control vaccines. The results of this study will be submitted for publication soon.

17103514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103514.value: Based on the findings generated in this study, we are now seeking for research funding to study a promising anti-Δ42PD1 monoclonal antibody in animal and human study. The key discovery made by us is to blockage Δ42PD-1 in HIV-induce acute innate immunity, which may slow or control disease development. After four years of study, we demonstrated not only the role of novel Δ42PD1/TLR4 axis in acute HIV infection, but also anti-Δ42PD1 can attenuate HIV-induced mucosal damage. It warrants to further study the capacity of anti-Δ42PD1 antibody in HIV functional cure. With this critical discovery in the world, the ultimate goal of future proposal is to bring this promising anti-Δ42PD1 antibody into human trials, phase I as the first step and phase II/III as the second step. The new discovery will be useful not only for controlling HIV disease progression but also provide a potential alternative therapy for other human diseases. As such, it warrants examining the role of the Δ 42PD1–TLR4 axis in other setting, such as tumor pathogenesis, autoimmune disease and bacterial infection in future studies.

17103514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103514.value: Programmed death-1 (PD-1) is a protein, which is well known being able to inhibit T cell function during tumor development. The role of its isoform namely Δ42PD-1 remains incompletely investigated. In this study, therefore, we aimed to define the biological function of Δ42PD-1 in regulating innate and adaptive host immune responses. We found that Δ42PD-1 is actually a functional protein that regulates innate responses essential for immune activation. Specifically, the over-expression of Δ42PD-1 on gut-homing γδ T cells in HIV infection contributes to rapid innate inflammatory responses leading to significant intestinal mucosal damages in humanized mouse model, which is associated with innate signaling via Toll-like receptor 4. Since the damage took place earlier than bacterial translocation, we revealed a previously unrecognized mechanism underlying HIV-induced acute mucosal pathology. Furthermore, we investigated Δ42PD-1-based vaccine for induction of antigen-specific T cells. We found that Δ42PD-1-based vaccine functions differently from PD-1-based vaccine by engaging different subsets of dendritic cells for antigen presentation. Lastly, we determine the in vivo efficacy of Δ42PD-1-based vaccine in treating EcoHIV infection in mice with intact immune system. By conducting these studies, we have revealed the function of the Δ42PD-1/TLR4 axis in shaping both innate and adaptive immune responses.

17103614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103614.value: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and its complications are becoming a major global health burden. Defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) in pancreatic β-cells is a key feature of T2DM, and contributes to the development of hyperglycemia. Although chronic metabolic stress (eg. obesity or nutrient overload) has been shown to impair β-cell function, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. A thorough understanding of the pathogenesis of β-cell failure will help to develop more therapeutic strategies against diabetes by relieving metabolic stress in β-cells. The tumor suppressor p53 is stabilized and becomes transcriptionally active in response to genotoxic stress, thereby controlling cell cycle. Apart from these established roles, p53 has recently been shown to contribute to the development of metabolic disorders such as insulin resistance and premature aging. Recently, we showed that p53 is stabilized and activated in β-cells of obese mice with β-cell dysfunction, which is accompanied with an elevation of mouse double minute 2 (MDM2), a principle negative regulator of p53. Treatment with the MDM2 inhibitor Nutlin-3a, which stabilizes and activates p53 by disrupting the interaction between MDM2 and p53, causes defective GSIS, leading to glucose intolerance in mice. Such a defect is perhaps due to aberrant tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and diminished ATP production in mitochondria. Consistently, genetic deletion of MDM2 in β-cells results in an uncontrolled activation of p53, leading to defective GSIS and glucose intolerance. Based on these results, we proposed that a tight control of the MDM2-p53 axis is important for maintaining β-cell function. Chronic metabolic stress activates p53, leading to aberrant mitochondrial functions, thereby resulting in β-cell dysfunction and T2DM. In this project, we will test whether inactivation of p53 in β-cells can alleviate obesity- and Nutlin-3a-induced deleterious effects on β-cell function, and prove the concept that chronic activation of p53 by deleting its negative regulator MDM2 leads to the onset of T2DM. In addition, we will investigate how the interplay between p53 and MDM2 fine-tune GSIS by modulating TCA cycle and ATP production. The results will provide new insight into the fundamental mechanisms of β-cell function and regulation of insulin secretion, and to shed new light on the pathogenesis of glucose dysregulation in diabetes. The unique mouse model established in this study will serve as a useful tool to identify and validate novel drug targets for the development of therapeutics to combat diabetes, a major chronic disease affecting nearly one million people in Hong Kong. 近年來，2型糖尿病及其相關拼發症已成為全球健康的重大負擔。胰島β細胞葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌功能受損是糖尿病的一個重要特徵，直接導致機體血糖升高。盡管慢性代謝應激（例如營養過剩、肥胖或衰老）已被證實可以損害β細胞功能，其中的潛在機制仍未闡明。因此，深入理解β細胞功能受損的發病機理，將有助於建立以減輕β細胞代謝應激為靶點的糖尿病治療新策略。 MDM2的抑制劑Nutlin-3a通過阻斷MDM2和p53之間的相互作用激活p53，Nutlin-3a導致小鼠葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌功能受損和葡萄糖耐量異常。Nutlin-3a導致胰島三羧酸循環功能障礙，影響線粒體ATP合成，最終導致葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌功能受損。與之相一致的是，在β細胞中敲除MDM2基因會導致小鼠葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌功能受損和葡萄糖耐量異常。基於這些結果，我們認為MDM2-p53是調節β細胞代謝過程的一個關鍵信號通路。 慢性代謝應激會穩定並激活p53，引起線粒體功能異常，並最終導致β細胞功能受損和糖尿病。在該項目中，我們將會探究在β細胞中p53的失活是否可以減輕或預防由高脂飲食或Nutlin-3a誘導的β細胞功能損傷，明確通過敲除p53上游負調節因子MDM2引起的p53調節異常或慢性激活是否可能導致糖尿病的發生。這些結果將有望為探尋β細胞功能和胰島素分泌的調節機制提供新的見解，為研究糖尿病發生過程中葡萄糖調節異常的發病機制提供新的線索。本研究中建立的獨特的小鼠模型，還將作為研發糖尿病治療藥物過程中鑒定和驗證新型藥物靶點的有效工具，而糖尿病這一重要的慢性疾病在香港影響了近一百萬人的生命健康。

17103614.label: Realisation of objectives
17103614.value: All the proposed objectives were well-performed as originally our plan. Please find the detailed findings in the following section. Objective 1: To examine how the interplay between MDM2 and p53 regulates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and β-cell mass. Work done: In the mid-term report, we have demonstrated that β-MDM2KO mice exhibited leads an elevated p53 activity and defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) in both in vivo and ex vivo system. In this report, we mainly focus to determine whether p53 activation in β-cells is responsible for the MDM2 null phenotypes, First, we injected β-MDM2 KO mice with adeno-associated virus (AAV) encoding dominant-negative mutant of p53 (DN-p53) (in which arginine-172 of p53 was mutated to histidine [p53R172H]) with FLAG-epitope driven by mouse insulin promoter. The p53R172H mutant is known to inactivate wild-type p53 by blocking the interaction between p53 and its target genes. In addition, the efficiency of our AAV system was previously validated. Protein level of p53 was induced by ~2 folds relative to its endogenous levels in islets of mice infected with AAV encoding FLAG-tagged DN-p53, which was accompanied with a reduction of MDM2 protein level. In addition, expression of exogenous DN-p53 was confirmed by immunohistochemical staining of the pancreatic tissues using an anti-FLAG antibody. AAV-mediated inactivation of p53 partially reversed glucose intolerance and defective GSIS in β-MDM2 KO mice. In vitro, inhibition of p53 either by adenovirus-mediated overexpression of DN-p53 or treatment with the p53 inhibitor pifithrin-α (PFHα) reversed defective GSIS in MDM2 deficient islets. Second, to further confirm whether p53 activation is responsible for glucose intolerance and defective GSIS in β-MDM2 KO mice, we generated β-cell-specific MDM2-p53 double KO (DKO) mice by crossing β-MDM2 KO mice with p53floxed/floxed mice. Activation of p53 by deletion of MDM2 was abolished in islets of DKO mice when compared to those from β-MDM2 KO mice. Glucose intolerance and defective GSIS in β-MDM2 KO mice were partly corrected by concomitant genetic deletion of p53, whereas insulin sensitivity was comparable among the three groups . Ex vivo static GSIS assay revealed that GSIS in islets isolated from DKO mice was normal when compared to WT controls. The above experiments clearly demonstrate that inactivation of p53 can rescue the defective GSIS in β-MDM2KO mice. Objective 2: To elucidate how MDM2-p53 axis couples mitochondria function to insulin secretion in β-cells. Work done: In the last report, we demonstrated that MDM2 deficiency impairs TCA cycle in pancreatic beta cells, as evidenced by reduced mitochondrial respiration and NADPH, ATP production. In this report, we have further confirmed that activation of p53 by the MDM2 inhibitor nutlin-3a or adenoviral-mediated overexpression also impairs TCA cycle, which in turn impairs GSIS. On the other hand, reductions in ATP level and calcium influx in response to glucose stimulation in MDM2-null islets were reversed by inhibition of p53 using PFHα or by concomitant genetic deletion of p53. We have found that OAA level was dramatically reduced in islets and β with activation p53 or genetic deletion of MDM2. Likewise, mRNA and protein expression of mitochondrial enzymes pyruvate carboxylase (which promotes OAA production in TCA cycle) was reduced in MDM2 null islets but not MDM2-p53 DKO islet. Other the other hand, other mitochondrial enzymes such as malic enzyme 1, 2 and 3 were not altered by the MDM2-p53 axis. Likewise, adenovirus-mediated overexpression of p53 inhibited mitochondrial respiration, expression of pyruvate carboxylase and OAA production in MIN6 beta cell line. In addition, we have demonstrated that activity of p53 is elevated in db/db diabetic islets, accompanied with reduced expression of pyruvate carboxylase and OAA production. Importantly, treatment with PFHα restored GSIS, OAA production and pyruvate carboxylase. The above data suggest that dysregulated MDM2-p53 axis causes mitochondrial dysfunction, leading to defective GSIS in type 2 diabetes. Objective 3: To delineate whether MDM2-p53 axis controls glucose-stimulated insulin secretion via regulation of TCA cycle-associated enzyme pyruvate carboxylase Work done: In the last report, we showed that replenishment of pyruvate carboxylase is able to rescue the defective GSIS, reduced OAA and ATP production in MDM2 null islets. In this report, we demonstrated that genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of p53 can reverse the reduction of pyruvate carboxylase in pancreatic islets of MDM2 knockout mice. To test whether p53 directly regulates expression of pyruvate carboxylase, we employed adenoviral system to overexpress p53 in MIN6 pancreatic β cells. This analysis demonstrated that p53 suppressed both protein and mRNA levels of pyruvate carboxylase. We cloned the putative p53 response element (RE) between -6810 and -6781 bp in the promoter region of the pyruvate carboxylase gene in the luciferase reporter. Adenoviral-mediated overexpression of p53 dramatically suppressed the promoter activity of pyruvate carboxylase in β cells. To further confirm that p53 regulates PC promoter activity via the p53 RE, we created two mutant constructs in which the p53 RE were mutated to non-functional one. Luciferase assay indicated that the suppressive effect of p53 on promoter activity of pyruvate carboxylase was lost in the mutants, suggesting the p53 RE are crucial for p53 action. On the other hand, glucose upregulated the promoter activity of pyruvate carboxylase in pancreatic beta cells, and such upregulation was counteracted by p53. Of note, overexpression of p53 did not suppress the promoter activity of pyruvate carboxylase in human embryonic kidney cells, suggesting that other co-factor(s) in pancreatic beta cell is crucial for the p53 action. Lastly, we showed that p53 directly bound to the p53 RE of pyruvate carboxylase using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay. Taken together, our work indicated that p53 down-regulates pyruvate carboxylase expression by directly binding with the p53 RE in the pyruvate carboxylase gene, resulting in transcriptional repression.

17103614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103614.value: Major research findings: Dysfunction of pancreatic β cells, exemplified by impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), is a hallmark of type 2 diabetes and a therapeutic target for several anti-diabetic drugs. Mitochondria couple glucose-sensing to insulin secretion by generating various metabolite signals to modulate the insulin exocytotic machinery. Defect in mitochondrial function impairs this metabolic coupling, leading to impaired GSIS in type 2 diabetes. However, the molecular pathways integrating mitochondrial metabolites with insulin secretion in physiological and pathophysiological conditions remain poorly unknown. In this prject, we uncovered an unexpected role of the MDM2-p53 axis, a key player in regulating cell growth and tumorigenesis, in coupling mitochondrial metabolism to insulin secretion by fine-tuning the mitochondrial enzyme pyruvate carboxylase (PC) in β cells. The major findings presented in this GRF project are summarized below: 1. In type 2 diabetes mouse model, impaired GSIS and glucose intolerance is associated with increased expression of both p53 and MDM2, diminished level of PC and its metabolite oxaloacetate (OAA) in pancreatic islets compared to the healthy mice. 2. Pancreatic β cell-selective deletion or pharmacological inhibition of MDM2 (an endogenous inhibitor of p53) leads to exacerbated p53 activation, diminished expression of PC and OAA, thus impairing both first- and second-phases GSIS and ensuing glucose intolerance in mice. The impairment in GSIS in MDM2-deficient islets can be reversed by either pharmacological or genetic inhibition of p53, or replenishment with PC or its metabolites OAA. 3. p53 directly represses the expression of PC by binding to the canonical p53 responsive element at the promoter region of the PC gene, leading to impaired mitochondrial respiration and metabolite production in tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, which results in diminished calcium influx and insulin secretion. 4. The aberrant MDM2-p53-PC axis in diabetic islets is a key mediator of dysregulated mitochondrial metabolism and defective GSIS. Inactivation of p53 by genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition with pifithrin-α is sufficient to reverse these defects by restoring PC expression and mitochondrial functions in diabetic islets. Our results identify the MDM2-p53-PC axis as a novel pathway which tightly controls metabolic coupling in mitochondria to insulin secretion in β cells. Furthermore, our study raises the possibility that the modulation of MDM2-p53-PC axis may represent a promising strategy for diabetes therapy. The findings have been published in Nature Communications (2016 Jun 6;7:11740. doi: 10.1038/ncomms11740) and presented in several local and international conferences (Please refer the detail in Part C)

17103614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103614.value: p53 is induced in pancreatic beta cells in response to different metabolic stress such as lipotoxicity and inflammation in type 2 diabetes, however whether this p53 activation is mediated via MDM2 is unknown. In addition, whether beta cell selective inactivation of p53 can protect the mice from type 2 diabetes is also unknown. In the future, we can employ the unique research tools developed in this GRF project (such as beta cell specific MDM2 KO mice, p53 KO and MDM2-p53 double KO mice as well adenoviral gene transfer system) to further delineate the interplay between MDM2-p53 in the pathogenesis of beta cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes.

17103614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103614.value: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) is a highly dynamic and regulated process involving multiple steps including glucose uptake, glycolysis and subsequent mitochondrial TCA metabolism in pancreatic β-cells. Mitochondria act as energy sensors that connects glucose metabolism to insulin secretion by producing numerous small metabolites, which in turn trigger and potentiate insulin secretion. In this project, we have demonstrated mitochondrial function is impaired in diabetic islets. In particular, we recently identified the novel role of MDM2-p53-pyruvate carboxylase signaling axis in regulation of GSIS. Activation of p53 by either genetic or pharmacological inhibition of its upstream negative regulator MDM2 induces impairment of first-phase and second-phase GSIS, leading to glucose intolerance in mouse models. Mechanistically, activation of p53 impairs mitochondrial oxidation and pyruvate metabolism in pancreatic β-cells by repressing transcription of pyruvate carboxylase, but has little effect on glycolysis. Reduced expression of pyruvate carboxylase leads to decreased production of oxaloacetate in the TCA cycle, thereby diminishing the coupling factors for GSIS. On the contrary, inhibition of p53 alleviates defective GSIS in diabetic islets. Our data collectively suggest that targeting the MDM2-p53-pyruvate carboxylase signaling axis may represent a new therapeutic approach to improve GSIS in diabetes.

17103614.value: This is an international project involves The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University (China), Capital Medical University (China), University of Southern Denmark (Denmark) and Mayo Clinic (USA). Through this project, we establish collocation among the aforementioned institute. Dr. Xiaomo Li from Fudan University (co-first author of the journal article published in Nature Communications) have worked on this project in HKU from 2014-2015, when she investigated how MDM2-p53 axis controls glucose stimulated insulin secretion. In addition, by collaborating with Dr. Yasuhiro Ikeda in Mayo Clinic, we have generated a novel adeno-associated gene transfer system to selectively inactivate p53 in pancreatic beta cells, thereby alleviating beta cell dysfunction. In this project, we closely worked with Dr Philip Hallenborg (Co-I) to dissect how the MDM2-p53 regulates TCA cycle and expression of pyruvate carboxylase. Apart from this GRF project, we are now collaborating to investigate how the MDM2-p53 axis regulate adipose tissue dynamics. This project has been presented in The 3rd Helmholtz-Nature Medicine Diabetes Conference (2016) by PI and awarded with best abstract award.

17103814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103814.value: MicroRNA (miRNA)-based therapy is increasingly regarded as a novel and promising approach in cancer therapy. Emerging evidence supports that miRNAs regulate the sensitivity of cancer to chemotherapeutic drugs. We have recently succeeded in establishing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cell line models of acquired chemoresistance, and found that these 5-fluorouracil resistant (FR) cell lines showed significant reduction in the expression of a novel microRNA, miR-338-5p. Our preliminary data showed that re-expression of miR-338-5p in chemoresistant ESCC cells restored chemosensitivity, thus suggesting that miR-338-5p has a role in modulating chemoresistance. An integrative study combining cDNA microarray, SILAC-based proteomics, and in silico analysis was conducted to identify biologically relevant genes upregulated in the FR cells that are targeted by this particular microRNA. Id1 (inhibitor of differentiation and DNA binding) was the only gene identified in the overlap between the upregulated genes in the FR cells by genome-wide profiling and the potential miR-338-5p targets predicted by computational software. Id1 is a marker for unfavorable prognosis in ESCC and is therefore an important therapeutic target. However, the mechanism causing frequent upregulation of Id1 in cancer is as yet unknown. Data from our pilot study suggest that this may be attributed to miR-338-5p dysregulation since we found low expression of miR-338-5p in ESCC clinical samples and cell lines, and forced or tetracycline-inducible (Tet-On) expression of miR-338-5p in ESCC cells resulted in repressed Id1 expression. More importantly, re-expression of Id1 in miR-338-5p-overexpressing ESCC cells abrogated the effects of miR-338-5p and reversed chemosensitivity. Taken together, we have obtained compelling evidence suggesting that miR-338-5p can modulate the chemosensitivity of ESCC cells by regulating Id1. In the proposed study, we plan to explore the clinical significance of miR-338-5p in ESCC, and determine the effects of miR-338-5p overexpression and knockdown on chemoresistance. The mechanisms that regulate miR-338-5p will be investigated. Deciphering the role of miR-338-5p in inhibiting Id1, and its functions in suppressing chemoresistance has great mechanistic and functional significance in the study of microRNA function in cancer development and progression. In vitro and in vivo experiments will be performed to confirm that Id1 is a direct target of miR-338-5p, and that Id1 mediates the function of miR-338-5p in regulating chemosensitivity. The efficacy of systemically delivered miR-338-5p in suppressing tumor chemoresistance in animal models will be studied to provide valuable preclinical data that may translate into novel therapy for esophageal cancer.

17103814.label: Realisation of objectives
17103814.value: Objective 1: To study the expression pattern and clinicopathological significance of miR-338-5p in esophageal cancer. The expression pattern and clinicopathological significance of miR-338-5p in primary tumors of patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) were studied by in situ hybridization using archival issue microarrays (TMAs) containing 96 ESCC samples with clinical follow-up data. Our results indicated that miR-338-5p were localized in both the cytoplasm and nucleus of ESCC cancer cells, and that low expression of miR-338-5p was correlated with tumor invasion (T stage) and lymph node metastasis (N stage). Since we postulated that miR-338-5p is a tumor suppressor miRNA, we also used real time PCR to compare the expression level of miR-338-5p in paired ESCC tumors and adjacent non-neoplastic esophagus tissues. We found that miR-338-5p was significantly downregulated in ESCC tumors compared with the non-neoplastic esophageal tissues. We also analyzed miR-338-5p expression in cancers of the gastrointestinal tract using public sources including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database and GEO datasets. The expression level of miR-338-5p in the TCGA esophageal carcinoma (ESCA) data cohort was significantly lower than that in non-tumor tissues. Notably, the ESCA patients with high miR-338-5p expression in their tumors had longer overall survival time. In the GEO datasets, lower expression of miR-338-5p was also found in other gastrointestinal cancers including gastric, colon and rectal cancers. These results suggest that miR-338-5p also has tumor suppressor function in other gastrointestinal cancers. In view of increasing reports suggesting that circulating miRNAs may be ideal tools for monitoring cancer progression, we went a step further and determined whether serum miR-338-5p level may serve as a non-invasive biomarker for ESCC. We analyzed the expression level of miR-338-5p in admission/pretreatment serum samples of 104 ESCC patients who underwent neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (with 5-FU and cisplatin) followed by esophagectomy. Serum samples of 50 healthy individuals were included for comparison. We found that the average expression level of serum miR-338-5p in patients with ESCC was significantly lower than that in healthy controls, and that patients with high serum miR-338-5p expression had significantly better survival rates (median survival = 58.00 months) than those with low miR-338-5p expression (median survival = 21.57 months). Importantly, the expression level of miR-338-5p in pretreatment serum was inversely correlated with post-therapy pathologic ypT-stage, ypM-stage, overall pathologic stage (ypTNM), and histologic grade. Furthermore, high serum miR-338-5p expression was associated with lower percentage of residual viable cells in the primary tumor collected during surgery, and with complete response to therapy, which indicated that higher pretreatment serum miR-338-5p level could predict a better response to chemoradiotherapy. Objective 2: To study the suppressive effects of miR-338-5p and the mediating role of Id1 on 5-FU resistance. Dual luciferase reporter assay was first performed to confirm that miR-338-5p targets and suppresses Id1 by binding to its 3'UTR. Pairs of ESCC tumor and non-neoplastic tissues were analyzed for miR-338-5p and Id1 protein expression. A significant inverse correlation was found between these two parameters, which provided evidence that Id1 was negatively regulated by miR-338-5p. We then made use of 5-FU-resistant (FR) ESCC cell lines to determine whether miR-338-5p plays a role in 5-FU chemoresistance, and whether Id1 mediates this function. Our results showed that miR-338-5p was downregulated while Id1 was upregulated in the FR cells, compared with their parental ESCC cell lines. Stable miR-338-5p overexpression decreased Id1 protein level and the viability of the FR cells in 5-FU-containing culture medium, as well as increased their sensitivity to 5-FU-induced apoptosis. These effects were abolished by ectopic overexpression of Id1 in the FR cells. Conversely, knockdown of miR-338-5p in ESCC cell lines led to increased Id1 protein expression, increased cell viability as well as resistance to 5-FU-induced apoptosis, and that these effects were reversed after Id1 knockdown. Tumor xenograft experiment was performed to determine if miR-338-5p overexpression in ESCC cells could render them more sensitive to 5-FU treatment in vivo. Comparison of tumor size showed that miR-338-5p overexpression in KYSE150FR cells could significantly increase the sensitivity of the tumors to 5-FU therapy, and since concomitant overexpression of Id1 significantly restored the 5-FU resistance, these data showed that miR-338-5p can modulate 5-FU chemoresistance in vivo by downregulating Id1. Several studies including our own demonstrated that overexpression of Id1 is correlated with tumor invasion and metastasis in different cancer types including ESCC. Since our data showed that miR-338-5p could suppress Id1, we further speculated that miR-338-5p may play a role in regulating invasion and migration of ESCC cells. The results of transwell cell invasion and wound healing assays demonstrated that forced expression of miR-338-5p significantly inhibited the invasion and migration activity of ESCC cells in vitro, while re-overexpression of Id1 attenuated these effects. Conversely, silencing miR-338-5p increased the abilities of ESCC cells to migrate and invade, and the effects were ameliorated by Id1 knockdown. These findings suggest that, in addition to modulating chemoresistance, miR-338-5p also has metastasis-inhibiting functions which are mediated by downregulating Id1. Objective 3: To investigate the epigenetic mechanisms of miR-338-5p dysregulation in esophageal cancer. miRStart was used to predict the Transcription Start Sites (TSS) of primary miR-338 (i.e. pri-miR-338), and position 79102680 (2931 bases upstream of pri-miR-338) was identified to be a putative TSS. Using the University of California Santa Cruz Genome Browser (https://genome.ucsc.edu/), we identified two CpG islands (chr17:79102749-79102970 and chr17:79109699-79109911) near this putative TSS of pri-miR-338, and several methylation sites were identified RRBS and methylation 450K Bead Array. Methylation specific PCR showed that one of the CpG islands was unmethylated in an immortalized normal human esophageal epithelial cell line but methylated in parental ESCC cell lines and their FR sublines. Treatment with 5-Aza-CdR restored miR-338-5p expression and reduced Id1 level in ESCC cells. Sequenom Mass ARRAY DNA methylation analysis was also performed for 26 CpG units to assess the methylation ratios. The results showed that the average methylation ratios of the CpG units in two normal esophageal epithelial cell lines (which had high miR-338-5p expression) were 0.22 and 0.17 respectively. In contrast, the CpG units were strongly methylated in ESCC cell lines which had low miR-338-5p expression, with methylation ratios averaging 0.91, 0.90 and 0.72 for 3 different ESCC cell lines. However, there was no significant increase in methylation in the FR sublines, which suggests that epigenetic mechanisms other than DNA methylation may be involved in downregulation of miR-338-5p in ESCC cells during acquisition of 5-FU chemoresistance. The putative promoter of miR-338-5p was cloned into pGL3 vector. Dual-luciferase reporter assay was performed by co-transfecting the construct encompassing the putative promoter with Renilla luciferase reporter vector into ESCC cells. However, our data did not show obvious change in luciferase activity in the cells transfected with putative promoter-expressing construct, compared with the empty vector. Even though we were unable to confirm conclusively that the region upstream of the predicted miR-338-5p TSS was indeed a functional promoter region (therefore objective not 100% achieved), our data nevertheless showed that CpG hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism responsible for miR-338-5p silencing in ESCC, and suggests that the methylation status of an accurately mapped miR-338-5p promoter could serve as a potential molecular marker for ESCC.

17103814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103814.value: (i) MicroRNAs modulate chemoresistance in ESCC through different targets and signaling pathways: miR-338-5p was identified to be a novel modulator of 5-FU chemoresistance in ESCC. Our in vitro data showed that miR-338-5p modulated 5-FU chemoresistance by targeting and inhibiting Id1, which is frequently overexpressed in ESCC. Id1 promoted 5-FU chemoresistance by inducing E2F1 and thereby upregulating thymidylate synthase expression. Id1 also increased IGF2 secretion and subsequent autocrine activation of PI3K/AKT pathway in ESCC cells. Through this mechanism, miR-377 expression in ESCC cells was downregulated. We found that ectopic overexpression of miR-377 had chemosensitizing effect on ESCC cells by targeting CD133 and suppressing cancer stemness. The profiles of miRNAs changed during acquired 5-FU chemoresistance. By profiling differentially expressed miRNAs in a 5-FU-resistant ESCC cell line established in our laboratory and performing functional studies, we identified and experimentally validated miR-29c to be another miRNA with chemosensitizing function in ESCC cells. This function was attributed to its ability to target FBXO31, which is an upstream regulator of the p38 pathway. Our in vivo experiments showed that restoring the expression level of or systemically delivering the relevant miRNAs are potentially useful strategies to overcome chemoresistance. (ii) miR-338-5p, miR-377 and miR-29c are downregulated in ESCC: miR-338-5p, miR-377 and miR-29c expressions were all aberrantly downregulated in the primary tumors of patients with ESCC, compared with paired normal esophageal tissue, whereas their targets, namely Id1, CD133 and FBXO31, respectively, were overexpressed in ESCC tumors. An inverse correlation was found between the miRNAs and their respective targets in clinical samples. Extensive DNA hypermethylation was detected in CpG units within a putative promoter region of miR-338-5p in ESCC cell lines relative to normal esophageal epithelial cell lines. This mechanism is likely to be a key mechanism responsible for dysregulated miRNA expressions in ESCC. (iii) Serum miRNA expression levels in patients have diagnostic and prognostic significance: Non-invasive biomarkers that can facilitate early diagnosis and predict treatment response are instrumental in optimizing therapy and improving the outcome for patients. Our data showed that the expression levels of miR-338-5p, miR-377 and miR-29c in the admission/pre-therapy serum samples of patients with ESCC all had diagnostic significance, and that high expression of these miRNAs could predict favorable response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Some of the results were published in various peer-reviewed journals (see Part C #1-6). Data on miR-338-5p have been submitted to Cancer Science and is currently under revision (Part C #7).

17103814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103814.value: Besides playing a role in modulating 5-FU chemoresistance, we found that forced expression of miR-338-5p in ESCC cells significantly suppressed cell migration and invasion, suggesting that this miRNA has anti-metastatic functions. However, rescue of Id1 expression failed to fully restore these properties, suggesting that other target gene(s) and signaling pathways are involved in mediating the anti-metastatic function of miR-338-5p. Further analysis showed that miR-338-5p inhibited the expression of PAK4 (p21-activated protein kinase 4), which was one of the potential targets of miR-338-5p as predicted by computational microRNA target prediction tools. Moreover, higher PAK4 expression was detected in the metastatic cancer cells compared with the parental cells. We therefore hypothesize that PAK4 may be a novel direct target of miR-338-5p and that it may mediate the function of miR-338-5p in suppressing cancer invasion and metastasis. We therefore extended our study to investigate the role and mechanism of miR-338-5p in progression of ESCC, and the therapeutic potential of systemically administered miR-338-5p in suppressing tumor metastasis in animal models in order to obtain preclinical data that may translate into novel therapy for esophageal cancer. This project was awarded a RGC GRF grant of $1,166,553 in 2017.

17103814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103814.value: 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin are commonly used chemotherapeutic agents in the treatment of esophageal cancer, but development of chemoresistance frequently occurs and the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. Our results showed for the first time that miR-338-5p was underexpressed in esophageal cancer cell lines with acquired 5-FU chemoresistance, and that this microRNA could modulate 5-FU chemoresistance. We found that forced overexpression of miR-338-5p suppressed Id1, and restored the sensitivity of esophageal cancer cells to 5-FU treatment both in vitro and in vivo. miR-338-5p also had metastasis-related functions in esophageal cancer. We also found that miR-338-5p was significantly downregulated in tumor tissue and serum samples of patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Notably, low serum miR-338-5p expression level was associated with poorer survival and poor response to 5-FU/cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy given before surgery. Besides miR-338-5p, we found that miR-377 and miR-29c were also downregulated in the tumor and serum samples of patients with ESCC, and that their chemosensitizing functions were mediated by different targets and signaling pathways. In summary, microRNAs play important roles in modulating chemoresistance in esophageal cancer and are potentially useful non-invasive prognostic and predictive biomarkers.

17104314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104314.value: Personalized medicine involves the use of an individual's genetic profile to guide treatment decisions: it helps determine the optimal drug and dosage and prevent adverse drug reactions (ADR). By September 2013, more than 100 drugs were advised to include pharmacogenomic information in their label, including those known to be associated with severe ADR, such as carbamazepine, phenytoin, and abacavir. Clinical application of pharmacogenomic findings holds great promise. Anti-thyroid drugs (ATD; such as carbimazole and propylthiouracil) have been prescribed in the clinical management of hyperthyroidism for more than 50 years. They are generally quite effective although associated with rare but severe ADR such as agranulocytosis. Agranulocytosis is a condition defined by decreased absolute neutrophil count that can lead to life-threatening and fetal infection. Nonetheless little is known about ATD-induced agranulocytosis, and its pharmacogenomic biomarkers have not been identified. The objective of the current study is to identify the pharmacogenomic biomarkers of ATD-induced agranulocytosis and investigate the effect of genetic variants on candidate gene expression. A genome-wide association study will be performed in 47 patients with carbimazole-induced agranulocytosis and 750 healthy controls. To validate the findings, SNPs with false-positive report probability <0.5 will be replicated in an additional 9 patients with carbimazole-induced agranulocytosis (cases) and 135 unaffected patients prescribed carbimazole (super controls). Given that genetic variants are known to exert a strong effect for severe ADR, our study will have >80% power to detect the susceptibility loci with OR≥4. To identify the casual variants, DNA from 56 (47+9) cases and 56 age- and sex-matched super controls will be used for re-sequencing. The 2-Mb candidate region (1-Mb upstream and downstream of the most associated SNP) will be re-sequenced. Single nucleotide variants will be called using the existing in-house pipeline in the Linux cluster. Association will be carried out using single SNP association and burden test. Moreover, the relationship between gene expression and genotype in the candidate region will also be assessed using expression quantitative trait loci analysis, with the RNA extracted from patients' peripheral blood mononuclear cells and polymorphonuclear neutrophil. Our study will identify potentially clinically useful pharmacogenomic biomarkers for ATD-induced agranulocytosis, reveal the role of genetic variants in ATD-induced agranulocytosis, identify the susceptibility genes, and improve our limited understanding in ATD-induced agranulocytosis and the genetic architecture of drug induced ADR. 個性化治療涉及以個人基因圖譜協助決定治療的方向：它能夠幫助確定最佳的藥物和劑量，並防止藥物不良反應（ADR）。直到2013年9月，藥物基因組學的資訊已出現在超過100種藥物的藥物標籤上，當中包括那些已知與嚴重不良反應相關，如卡馬西平，苯妥英和阿巴卡韋。因此，藥物基因組學研究對臨床應用帶來了巨大的希望。 抗甲狀腺藥（ATD;如甲亢平及丙硫氧嘧啶）已在甲亢的臨床應用了超過50年。它們一般都是相當有效的，但有機會引致罕見但嚴重的ADR，如粒細胞缺乏症。粒細胞缺乏症是因為中性粒細胞數量下降而引起，可能危及生命及導致嚴重感染。儘管如此，醫學界對由ATD引起的粒細胞缺乏症所知甚少。此研究項目目的是找尋ATD引起的粒細胞缺乏症的藥物基因組學標誌物和調查遺傳變異體如何影響候選基因的表達。 全基因組關聯研究將在47個由甲亢平誘發的粒細胞缺乏症病人和750名健康對照進行。為了驗證結果， FDR少於0.5的SNP將會在額外的9病人及135名健康對照進行複驗研究。眾所周知，遺傳變異對ADR有著很強的影響力，對於影響力大的易感基因位點(e.g. OR≥4)，我們的研究將有大過80％的統計力。 要確定致病位點，我們會在56病例和56個對照的易感基因位點上進行重測序及統計研究。此外，我們會利用患者的外周血單核細胞和中性粒細胞中提取的RNA進行表達數量性狀基因座的分析評估。 我們的研究將確定有潛在臨床應用價值的藥物基因組生物標誌物，揭示遺傳變異對ATD引起粒細胞缺乏症的影響，確定易感基因，並提高我們對ATD引起粒細胞缺乏症的有限認識和藥物引起的不良反應的遺傳結構。

17104314.label: Realisation of objectives
17104314.value: We have completed both objectives 1 and 2. For objective 1, we conducted two studies. - First, we conducted a population-based case-control study was conducted using the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System, a database managed by the Hong Kong Hospital Authority. Patients with drug-induced agranulocytosis from 1 January 2004 to 31 December 2013 were identified. World Health Organization causality assessment was used to evaluate the possible drug aetiology of each case. Odd ratios (ORs) of the drug exposure were calculated using exact conditional logistic regression. A total of 155 cases of drug-induced agranulocytosis were identified. Mean age was 51.4 years, and 95 cases were female. Incidence rate was estimated to be 2.2 cases per million person-years, and the all-cause mortality of patients with drug-induced agranulocytosis was 3.9%. Among the cases, the most common associated drug groups were antithyroid drugs (41.9%), antimicrobials (20%), anticonvulsants (10.3%), and antipsychotics (6.5%). Carbimazole had the highest risk of agranulocytosis (adjusted OR 416.7, 95% confidence interval (CI) 51.5-3372.9) with an incidence of 9.2 (95%CI 6.9-12.1) per 10 000 users and 3.6 (95%CI 2.7-4.8) per 10 000 user-years. Other drugs with significant risk included cephalosporins, clozapine, penicillins, phenytoin, and propyl thiouracil. Antithyroid drugs were the most common implicated drug class, and carbimazole had the highest risk of agranulocytosis. 17104314.value: Anti-thyroid drug (ATD) is a drug for treating hyperthyroidism. ATD is widely used and considered effective, but it is associated with a rare but severe side effect, agranulocytosis (low white blood cell count). It is believed that ATD-induced agranulocytosis has a genetic basis, but the genetic marker of this condition was unidentified. In this study, we identified the clinically useful genetic marker (HLA‐B*38:02:01) of ATD-induced granulocytosis. 17104514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104514.value: Modulating of cytoplasmic calcium (Ca2+) concentration through the activation of intracellular Ca2+ release channels elicits signal that control numerous cellular processes. The characterization of the regulation of these intracellular Ca2+ release channels is therefore the elementary to understand the generation and modulation of intracellular Ca2+ signaling events. In human, three Ca2+ mobilizing messengers have been identified. The inositol trisphosphate (InsP3) and cyclic ADP-ribose (cADPR) have been demonstrated to mobilize Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) by activating the InsP3 receptor (InsP3R) and ryanodine receptor (RyR), respectively, whereas the nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP) mobilizes Ca2+ from the endosome and lysosome. However, the receptor responsible for NAADP activation was mystery until recently that several research groups have proposed a novel lysosomal cation channel, two-pore channel 2 (TPC2), is the putative candidate for NAADP. Although the intracellular localization of TPC2 hindered the electrophysiological study by conventional patch-clamp technique, the biophysical properties of TPC2 have been investigated by incorporating the purified protein into planar lipid bilayer or by targeting the channel proteins to plasma membrane. However, these techniques require tedious experimental procedures or genetic modification and therefore the channel properties recorded by these techniques might not totally reflect their physiological properties as they are in the native environment. Furthermore, recent articles challenged that the activation of TPC2 channel is mediated by phosphoinositide urging the development of novel methodology for characterizing the TPC2 channel. In this regard, we employed human TPC2 retrovirus to transduce a cell line that lacking both endogenous InsP3R and RyR (DT40TKO). In combination with the nuclear membrane electrophysiology, we developed a cell model that enabled us to rigorously investigate the biophysical properties of the TPC2 channel with minimal manipulations. Using this newly developed approach, we successfully detected NAADP-activated TPC2 single channel currents in the isolated nuclei from TPC2 virus transduced DT40TKO cells. In this study, we aim to address the most elemental question that whether the TPC2 is a NAADP-mediated Ca2+ channel. If so, the conductive properties and the ligands regulations of the TPC2 channels will also be investigated. Furthermore, we will investigate the effects of phosphorylation on TPC2 channel activities as we have identified putative PKA and Akt phosphorylation sites in the human TPC2 protein. Elucidation of the biophysical properties of the TPC2 channels and its regulation by phosphorylation will provide information for the physiological regulations of the lysosomal Ca2+ release and its role in lysosome functions. 許多的細胞功能都是通過調控胞質鈣離子（Ca2+）濃度來調控的，而激活細胞Ca2+ 的釋出是影響胞質Ca2+ 濃度的主要因素。因此，定義細胞Ca2+ 通道的電生理特性是研究鈣離子信號的根本。現時，已鑑定的細胞內Ca2+ 激動劑有三種。它們分別是能激活三磷酸肌醇受體（IP3R）的三磷酸肌醇（IP3）和蘭尼鹼受體（RyR）的環腺苷二磷酸核糖（cADPR），以及能釋出內吞體和溶酶體Ca2+ 的菸酸腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸（NAADP）。然而，我們一直都未能確定誰是NAADP的受體，直到近年，幾個研究組同時提出位於溶酶體的雙孔通道2 （TPC2）就是NAADP受體。雖然TPC2位處細胞內，其位置阻礙了以傳統膜片鉗電生理研究其通道特性，科研界仍然以平面脂雙層技術或轉基因技術把TPC2表達在細胞膜上去探討它 的通道電生理特。然而，這些技術需要繁瑣的分離程序或遺傳基因修飾，因此， 這它們所記錄到的TPC2離子通道特性可能不完全反映其在細胞環境的生理特性。在這種情況下，我們採用了逆轉錄病毒轉導，把人類TPC2 蛋白表達於DT40TKO 細胞。此細胞是現存唯一不具內源性InsP3R和RyR的細胞株，在TPC2逆轉錄病毒轉染後，TPC2是 就是唯一的細胞內Ca2+ 釋出通道了（hTPC2-DT40TKO)！我們將hTPC2-DT40TKO與核膜膜片鉗結合， 開發了一個全新的TPC2細胞模型，此模型使我們能更有效率地研究TPC2通道的電生理特性。以此新細膜模型，我們於hTPCDT40TKO的細胞核成功地檢測到NAADP能激活TPC2單個通道電流。 此研究我們旨在探討一些關於TPC2的最基本問題：（1）TPC2是不是NAADP介導的鈣離子通道；（2）如果是的話， 我們會深入探討TPC2通道的離子導電特性和它的配位體調控。除此以外，在蛋白序列分析中，我們發現了TPC2蛋白的PKA和Akt的磷酸化位點，我們將會對研究磷酸化對TPC2單通道電流有什麼影響。通過對TPC2鈣離子的電生理特性的研究及磷酸化對其單通道電流的調控會為我們提供TPC2 Ca2+通道在溶酶體上所起的生理作用。

17104514.label: Realisation of objectives
17104514.value: i. To characterize the activation of TPC2 single channel by NAADP using nuclear membrane electrophysiology Ca2+ imaging techniques have revealed that NAADP mobilizes lysosomal Ca2+ via the activation of TPC2 channels. However the direct evidence showing NAADP can activate TPC channel in native membrane is uncertain. To test if NAADP can directly activate hTPC2 natively, we generated a stable human TPC2 expressing DT40TKO cell line by retroviral infection (DT40TKO-hTPC2) and performed nuclear membrane electrophysiology on the DT40TKO-hTPC2 in the “on-nucleus” configuration. In the presence of symmetrical KCl solutions (K+ as the charge carrier) with 10 nM NAADP in the pipet solution, single-channel currents were detected in ~30% of the nuclear patches (n = 412 patches). Under the activation of 10 nM NAADP, hTPC2 single-channel currents with a channel open probability (Po) of 0.39 0.07 (Fig. 1b; n = 3) were detected from nuclei isolated from DT40TKO-hTPC2 cells. This NAADP-activated single-channel current was not observed when we patched the DT40TKO-EGFP nuclei or when we omitted the NAADP in the pipet solution. An amplitude histogram revealed that the detected hTPC2 channels had current amplitudes of about 220 pS which is similar to those obtained from the planar lipid bilayer study. Our results show for the first time that NAADP activated the hTPC2 channels expressed in the native nuclear membrane of DT40TKO-hTPC2 cells. In addition to that, the nuclear membrane electrophysiology is an alternative approach suitable for single-channel recording of NAADP-activated hTPC2 channels. We have completed the proposed specific Aim 1 stated in our original proposal by developing an new approach to study TPC2 single channel in physiological membrane and demonstrated that NAADP is a physiological agonist for TPC2 channel. ii. To characterize the permeation properties of the TPC2 channel As demonstrated in the reconstituted planar lipid bilayer, hTPC2 forms a large conductance, cation-selective channel permeable to monovalent and divalent ions, similar to other intracellular Ca2+ release channels. We performed analogous experiments by nuclear membrane patch to investigate whether the conductance and permeation properties observed by nuclear membrane patch resemble those observed in the planar lipid bilayer experiments. Current/voltage (I/V) relationships were determined using 2 µM Ca2+ in the pipette solution, with symmetrical K+ or Cs+ as the permeant ion (140 mM pipette:bath). The I/V relationships were generated using K+ or Cs+ as charged carrier (140 mM pipette:bath) with membrane potential stepping from -60 mV to +60 mV in 20-mV increments. From these experiments, the detected hTPC2 channels, in both symmetric K+ and Cs+, exhibited an ohmic I/V relationship with no discernible voltage dependence. The slope conductance of K+ as the charge carrier was 208.4 20.7 pS, which resembles those reported in the lipid bilayer. In comparison, the slope conductance of using Cs+ as charged carrier was 77.5 13.6 pS indicating TPC2 is more permeable to K+ than the Cs+. The conductance and permeation properties of the hTPC2 channel recorded from the nuclear membrane are similar to those reported in previous studies with the lipid bilayer or hTPC2 retargeting to the plasma membrane. iii. To characterize the regulation of the TPC2 channel by different ligands NAADP dose-dependently regulates lysosomal Ca2+ release and two distinct NAADP binding sites have been proposed. To investigate this NAADP dependence, we performed nuclear membrane patches on DT40TKO-hTPC2 nuclei and included different concentrations of NAADP in the pipette solution. No TPC2 channel activity was detected when NAADP was omitted from the pipette solution or when 1 µM Ned-19, a NAADP antagonist, was included in the pipette solution with 100 nM NAADP. With the presence of NAADP in the pipette solution, hTPC2 single channel Po increased dose-dependently from 0.08 0.03 (1 nM NAADP) to 0.39 0.07 (10 nM NAADP) and reached a maximum Po of 0.63 0.06 (100 nM). The detected hTPC2 single-channel Po started to decrease when the NAADP concentration was further increased. Human TPC2 Po was 0.21 0.03 when 1 µM NAADP was included in the pipette solution, whereas Po decreased further to 0.07 0.03 when 10 µM NAADP was added to the pipette solution. To gain mechanistic insights into the effects of NAADP on hTPC2 channel Po, we performed dwell-time analysis on the recorded hTPC2 currents. In sub-micromolar concentrations, NAADP increased hTPC2 Po by increasing the channel open time, whereas the channel closed time remain unaltered (Fig. 3c). Conversely, micromolar concentrations of NAADP inhibited hTPC2 channel activity by decreasing the channel open time. Our results show that the unique and characterized bell-shaped NAADP dependence of hTPC2 channel activity is preserved when the channel is expressed on the nuclear membrane. The bell-shape NAADP dependence was not observed in the lipid bilayer experiment or retargeting TPC2 on the plasma membrane. In addition, our results demonstrated NAADP affects hTPC2 channel Po by regulating the stability of the channel’s open state. iv. To characterize the regulation of TPC2 channel by phosphorylation Apart from regulation by physiological ligands and Ca2+, the channel activity of InsP3Rs and RyRs are modulated by different protein kinases. We analysed the TPC2 protein sequences and found a putative protein kinase A (PKA) phosphorylation site at position 666 in human, which is conserved in several other mammals. We investigated the influence of PKA phosphorylation on hTPC2 channel activity using DT40TKO stable cell lines expressing either phosphomimetic (S666E) or unphosphorylatable (S666A) mutants. We observed TPC2 channel Po was significantly increased in the phosphomimetic S666E mutant cell line (Po = 0.80 ± 0.09; n = 3) compared to wild-type hTPC2-expressing cells (Po = 0.63 ± 0.06; n = 3; p = 0.0151), suggesting that PKA phosphorylation of hTPC2 augments its activity; in contrast, the unphosphorylatable S666A mutation decreased channel activity (Po = 0.33 ± 0.01 vs 0.63 ± 0.06 in wild-type, p = 0.0062). To further validate PKA phosphorylation enhances TPC2 channel activity, we patched DT40TKO-hTPC2 nuclei with the addition of PKA catalytic subunit in the pipette solution. With the presence of PKA catalytic subunit and 10 nM NAADP in the pipet, hTPC2 channel Po was increased significantly as compared to those in the absence of PKA (Po: 0.55 ± 0.04 vs 0.39 ± 0.04, p = 0.0412). Conversely, channel Po in DT40TKO-hTPC2-S666A did not affected by PKA phosphorylation (Po: 0.11 ± 0.01 vs 0.09 ± 0.01, p = 0.410) but lower than those in wild-type DT40TKO (Po: 0.09 ± 0.01 vs 0.39 ± 0.04, p = 0.002). These data suggest PKA phosphorylation of hTPC2 results in significantly increased Po, whereas dephosphorylation decreases Po. Although we have made some progress on characterizing the regulation and permeation of TPC2 channel in native membrane, many of its properties are still waiting for us to elucidate such as its regulation by membrane lipid (PIP2) and its Na+ permeability. The major hurdle of this project is that PI switched institutions from HKU to HKBU. One of the major equipment required by this project (a fluorescent microscope procured by PI’s GRF grants) was withheld by HKU. This significantly affected PI’s research output. Luckily, with the support from HKBU, PI built a new patch-clamp setup in HKBU and PI will continue to complete this project.

17104514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104514.value: 6.1 Major findings and research outcome (400 words) The major finding of this research project is that we have developed a novel method to investigating and characterizing the regulations of intracellular TPC2 channel using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology technique. We are the first group using the nuclear membrane electrophysiological approach to demonstrate that the single channel activity of TPC2 can be regulated by protein kinase A phosphorylation (Lee et al, 2016, Sci. Rep.) We have constructed a stable human TPC2-expressing DT40TKO cell line that lacks endogenous InsP3R and RyR (DT40TKO-hTPC2). The immunostaining revealed hTPC2 expression on the nuclear envelope. Intracellular dialysis of NAADP into Fura-2-loaded DT40TKO-hTPC2 cells elicited cytosolic Ca2+ transients, suggesting that hTPC2 was functionally active. Using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology on the T40TKO-hTPC2 line, we detected a ~220 pS single-channel current activated by NAADP with K+ as the permeant ion. The detected single-channel recordings displayed a linear current-voltage relationship, were sensitive to Ned-19 (known antagonist for TPC2) inhibition, were biphasically regulated by NAADP concentration, and regulated by PKA phosphorylation. In summary, we developed a cell model for the characterization of the TPC2 channel and the nuclear membrane patch-clamp technique provided an alternative approach to rigorously investigate the electrophysiological properties of TPC2 with minimal manipulation. We have trained a PhD student, Lee Shuk Kwan, during the course of the research project and published our cell model and research findings in Scientific Reports (Lee et al, 2016, Sci. Rep). With this new technique, we are now moving on to the investigation of the role of TPC2 channel in some particular pathophysiological conditions. One of our primarily target is to elucidate the role of TPC2 in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease. We have secured a funding support from the Health and Medical Research Fund (HMRF 15163421) from the Food and Health Bureau for initiating an in vitro study of using traditional Chinese Medicine to target lysosomal TPC2 as a treatment strategy for AD. In addition, we have established collaboration with a group in Shanghai, China. Using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology technique to found the InsP3R interacts with SEC5 protein and modulates innate immunity against the C. albicans infection (manuscript is accepted by BMC Biology; Impactor factor: 6.779). Another review article on Ca2+ signaling in Alzheimer’s disease and therapies was submitted to BBA Molecular Cell Research (IF: 4.521).

17104514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104514.value: The TPC2-mediated Ca2+ release plays significant roles in cytoplasmic Ca2+ homeostasis and participates in normal physiological processes as well as in pathophysiological conditions. Because of the intracellular localization of the TPC2 (in the lysosomal membrane), it is always difficult to elucidate the regulation and electrophysiological properties of TPC2 using traditional patch-clamp electrophysiology. By applying the nuclear membrane electrophysiology in DT40 cells lacking endogenous InsP3R and RyR (DT40-TKO), we overexpressed human TPC2 channel in the nuclear membrane of the DT40-TKO cells. We have partially characterized the permeation properties and ligand regulation of TPC2 and found that the TPC2 is an NAADP-activated, PKA-regulation cation permeable ion channel involved in lysosomal Ca2+ release. The lysosomal Ca2+ content is important for the normal functions of lysosome, particularly it plays essential role in the autophagy-lysosomal pathway, a cellular degradative pathway for cell survival. Therefore, knowing the physiological and pathophysiological roles of the lysosomal TPC2 channel and identification of novel compounds that can intervent TPC2 functions are of interest in the lysosome research filed. We are now studying the roles of TPC2 in the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis and identifying new molecules to regulate the functions of TPC2 as a therapeutic target for AD treatment.

Using nuclear membrane electrophysiology, we detected a ~220 pS single-channel current activated by NAADP with K+ as the permeant ion. The detected single-channel recordings displayed a linear current-voltage relationship, were sensitive to Ned-19 inhibition, were biphasically regulated by NAADP concentration, and regulated by PKA phosphorylation.
