17106614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106614.value: 黴菌毒素是菌絲狀真菌的次級代謝物, 其毒性非常高, 主要由鐮胞菌屬、麴黴屬和青黴菌屬產生, 它們在致癌、抑制免疫系統和導致生長遲緩方面引起各方關注。全球估計約 25%穀物 受天然黴菌毒素污染,其程度對公共衛生構成一定的風險。生活在發展中國家的人民暴露於 黴菌毒素含量水平較高的環境,因此急性中毒個案並不罕見;而發達國家的人民則恆常接觸 中度水平的黴菌毒素。進食受污染的食物是接觸黴菌毒素的主要途徑,腸道是受毒性影響的首個目標器官。腸上皮屏障的完整性限制外來抗原和病原體入侵, 這對腸道健康和保護其下面的組織是至關重要的。腸道表面覆蓋有由杯狀細胞分泌的粘液, 它充當保護屏障的作用， 防止細菌易位。實驗性動物和農場動物在攝取鐮胞菌屬毒素後,無論感染屬於實驗室條件或天然情況, 黏膜更容易受感染, 其原因可能是粘蛋白動力學和微生物種群的改變, 然而，無論是體外或體內研究都没有提供證據。因此，本研究的長遠目標是闡明調節鐮胞菌屬毒素引起的粘蛋白的生物合成和/或分泌的分子機制，並評估和驗證新的方法來逆轉這種狀況。本研究假定鐮胞菌屬毒素通過有關粘蛋白生物合成的細胞信號途徑影響小腸上皮細胞 (Intestinal epithelial cells, IEC)粘蛋白的生物合成和/或分泌。這個假設是基於以下意見。首先，我們的初步數據顯示幾種鐮胞菌屬毒素能不同的調節幾種分泌性黏蛋白。其次，一些研究已經表明細胞信號途徑，如蛋白激酶C (protein kinase C, PKC)，表皮生長因子受體（epidermal growth factor receptor, EGFR)，Ras/ Raf，促分裂原活化蛋白激酶 (mitogen-activated protein kinase, MEK) 和絲裂原活化蛋白激酶(mitogen-activated protein kinases，MAPKs) 可在不同的細胞中的粘蛋白的調製發揮一定的作用。根據這些意見，本方案的實驗重點是調節有關黏蛋白生物合成和/或分泌的細胞信號途徑。研究中將評估的黴菌毒素包括伏馬鐮孢毒素(fumonisin B1)、玉米黴菌毒素(zearalenone)、去氧雪腐鐮刀菌烯醇(deoxynivalenol) 和雪腐鐮刀菌烯醇(nivalenol)。自然界中不會單一地出現某一種毒素, 人和動物通常暴露於黴菌毒素的混合物中。本實驗室的初步研究和積累在文獻中的證據表明益生菌能有利地調節黏蛋白生物合成和分泌以及腸道菌群的組成。因此，我們將進一步以體內的方法評估這些細菌對保護以及防止鐮胞菌屬毒素在腸道所產生的不良影響的能力。過往實驗成功證明益生菌能有效將這些毒素的不良影響逆轉, 本研究會參考此結果, 透過一群有毒素暴露高風險的農場動物進行飲食介入的試驗。有關黴菌毒素毒性和食物污染物的控制的研究領域正在擴展致全球, 而這項研究所獲得的綜合數據,可為飼料業和食品工業提供一個極佳益生菌發酵和非發酵產品研發及應用機會。

17106614.label: Realisation of objectives
17106614.value: Experiments were performed to test predictions of our hypothesis that the modulation of mucin biosynthesis and secretion following exposure to Fusarium toxins is associated with several signaling pathways associated with mucins synthesis. These studies provided mechanistic understanding of intervention studies with probiotics (Specific Aim 2). Deoxynivalenol (DON) and zearalenone (ZEA) are the two mycotoxins studied. They are produced by members of the genus Fusarium and are of concern because of their frequent occurrence in agricultural staples such as wheat, corn, barley and oats. Concentrations chosen for DON and ZEA for the measurement of mucin synthesis and secretion were based on our previous experiments in Caco-2 cells, in which their impacts on mucus secretion were investigated (Wan et al. 2014). Selected levels of respective mycotoxins reflect concentrations expected to be encountered in the gastrointestinal tract of animals or human tissues following consumption of food or feed contaminated with 2–4 mg/kg of body weight of these mycotoxins. Previous studies conducted by our laboratory indicate the modulation of biosynthesis of secretory mucin (MUC5AC and MUC5B) following exposure to individual and mixture of DON and ZEA in the Caco-2 cell line. It was shown that DON or ZEA up-regulate MUC5AC and MUC5B mRNA expression level while combination of DON and ZEA down-regulate MUC5AC and MUC5B mRNA expression level (Wan et al. 2014). The Caco-2 cell line was opted in our study because it exhibits structural and functional features similar to intestinal epithelial cells. It was first shown that DON an/or ZEA decreased total mucin-like glycoprotein expression in most of the incubation time points. When we looked at the mRNA expression of secretory mucin MUC5AC and MUC5B, DON and ZEA alone or in combination generally regulated mRNA MUC5AC and MUC5B expression level in Caco-2 cells (Fig. 7). Up-regulation of MUC5AC and MUC5B expression level was more profound at 15 min than at 2 hr incubation in DON and/or ZEA. This may be explained, at least partly, by activation mechanism of cellular signaling pathway MAPK, there have been studies demonstrated that MAPK pathway is activated obviously and rapidly by external stimuli (Song et al. 2002). This study also explored the interactive effects of DON and ZEA. Upon 2 µM DON exposure at 2, 4, 6, 12 and 24 hr incubation, MUC5AC mRNA was generally up-regulated. However, in DON/ZEA mixture, MUC5AC mRNA expression was inhibited which suggests an antagonism interaction between DON and ZEA. The results generated suggested that the DON and ZEA modulate mucin synthesis and secretion in enterocytes, which may thereby influence pathogen translocation from the gastrointestinal tract. As a result, we later evaluated the effect of DON on bacterial translocation an aim which was not included in the original proposal submitted to The GRF. Probiotic bacteria, particularly those belonging to the genera of Lactobacillus beneficially modulate the mucus barrier and improve symptoms of inflammatory bowel diseases in association with down-regulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Sahar et al., 2010). Accordingly, in this study, it was hypothesized that probiotic bacteria, in particular Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG), could modulate the mucus barrier and inflammation. This may provide an approach to manage the adverse effects induced by Fusarium toxins. An exposure regimen was designed to simulate human exposure, and included LGG to either prevent or treat mice exposed to a mixture of DON and ZEA. Male pathogen-free Balb/c mice, 5 weeks old, weighing 18-20g were obtained from the Laboratory Animal Unit, University of Hong Kong. Mice were fed initially with the standard control diet and water was available ad libitum. After 1 week of acclimation, Balb/c mice (6 weeks old, 20-22g) were randomly assigned to control and treatment groups (n=6/group). In order to estimate food consumption and water intake, animals were housed individually per cage and were provided the appropriate diets and water ad libitum. Food consumption was measured on a daily basis by calculating the difference of the food supplied and that remaining (food container and in bedding), and thus the amounts of ingested Fusarium toxins were calculated. Food conversion ratio was calculated as the total feed intake divided by the total weight gain of the animal. The animal protocol was approved by the Committee on the Use of Live Animals in Teaching and Research (CULATR) at the University of Hong Kong (Number 2820-12) and the Department of Health of HKSAR Government. After one week of acclimation, mice were randomly assigned to six groups (six animals per group) for the eight weeks of feeding trial. Groups included control (fed AIN-93G diet; group = C), mycomix (fed diet containing 12μg of DON/g and 0.5μg of ZEA/g; group =M), LGG (fed diet containing 1x108CFU/g; group = L), pair-fed control (fed daily the mean food intake of toxin group as measured on the previous day; group = PF) and two groups with both probiotic and mycomix (described below). As DON may cause a reduction of food consumption, the pair-fed control group was included in the study design to exclude a possible indirect effect of reduced feed intake from the direct action of DON on growth and immunological parameters (Rotter et al. 1995). For the probiotic intervention component, two different protocols that varied the time-point of oral administration of LGG were studied to determine whether LGG could prevent and/or treat unwanted effects induced by Fusarium toxins. In the treatment arm of the study, mice were first exposed to mycomix diet for four weeks and both mycomix and LGG diet for the next four weeks (group = ML). For the prevention protocol, mice fed with LGG diet for first four weeks and both mycomix and LGG diet for the next four weeks (group = LM). Chronic ingestion of DON/ZEA mix regulated goblet cell mucus secretion in cooperation with intestinal trefoil factors, accompanied by a moderate increase in plasma D-lactate level. Plasma IL8/CXCL8 and serum immunoglobulin (Ig)A, IgM and IgG levels were also differentially regulated. The results showed that LGG partially prevented or treated the unwanted adverse effects of DON/ZEA in mice by regulation of goblet cell mucus secretion, improvement of plasma D-lactate, IL-8/CXCL8 and serum Ig levels. Results from specific aim I encouraged us to further investigate the effects of low and relevant concentrations of DON on intestinal susceptibility to pathogen infection. In the present study, semi-confluent Caco-2 cells were exposed to DON followed by enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC) infection. The effects of DON and EIEC contamination on mucin, cytokines and related signal transduction pathway were examined as part of the local immune system. Caco-2 cells were able to generate a rapid immune response against DON without or with post-challenge with EIEC. Secretory MUC5AC and membrane-bound MUC17 may play an important role in attaching and invasion of EIEC and thus protect intestinal cells from EIEC infection. Cells were able to express and produce important mediators of inflammation such as cytokines and other signal molecules like toll-like receptors (TLRs) that are important for host defence and bacterial recognition. The inflammatory stimulation might be a consequence of nuclear factor κ-light chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) activation. These data indicate that DON may confer various immunomodulatory effects on IECs, which might therefore modify the susceptibility of human to diseases.

17106614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106614.value: In the present study, we aimed to understand the underlying molecular mechanisms regarding the impact of Fusarim toxins on intestinal immunity. To address this a semi-confluent Caco-2 cells were exposed to the Fusarium toxin deoxynivalenol (DON) followed by enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC) infection. The effects of DON and EIEC contamination on mucin, cytokines and related signal transduction pathway were examined as part of the local immune system (Manuscript submitted to Tox letter). Caco-2 cells were able to generate a rapid immune response against DON without or with post-challenge with EIEC. Secretory MUC5AC and membrane-bound MUC17 may play an important role in attaching and invasion of EIEC and thus protect intestinal cells from EIEC infection. Cells were able to express and produce important mediators of inflammation such as cytokines and other signal molecules like toll-like receptors (TLRs) that are important for host defence and bacterial recognition. The inflammatory stimulation might be a consequence of nuclear factor κ-light chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) activation. These data indicate that DON may confer various immunomodulatory effects on IECs, which might therefore modify the susceptibility of human to diseases. Furthermore, we investigated the potential of the probiotic strain Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) on modulating the toxicity of two Fusarium toxin Don and Zearalenone (ZEA) Our study showed that LGG partially prevented or treated the unwanted adverse effects of DON/ZEA in mice as shown by regulation of goblet cell mucus secretion, improvement of plasma D-lactate, IL-8/CXCL8 and serum Ig levels as important markers for intestinal permeability and inflammation status (Wan et al., 2016). Individual toxins were not investigated here; antagonistic, additive, or synergistic effects of the combination of two toxins are possible, and LGG modulation may have a different effect depending on mixture ratios and of mixtures compared to individual toxins.

17106614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106614.value: Further studies using molecular approaches, such as high throughput mRNA sequencing and proteomics, will be useful to elucidate the mechanistic pathways involved in understanding the dynamic interplay that occurs between mycotoxins, probiotic bacteria and IECs. Further experimental validation of probiotic efficacy in promoting intestinal epithelial defences could support public health approaches to improve gut health in mycotoxin exposed individuals.

17106614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106614.value: Deoxynivalenol (DON) and zearalenone (ZEA) are mycotoxins produced by Fusarium species, which naturally co-occur in foods/feeds.The gastrointestinal tract represents the first barrier against dietary xenobiotics. The present study aimed to investigate the effects and underlying molecular mechanisms responsible for modulation of mucin synthesis and secretion induced by these toxins. Moreover, ability of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) to improve intestinal barrier functions and ameliorate inflammation in mice fed diets containing DON/ZEA mix. An exposure regimen that simulated human exposure experience was designed. Chronic ingestion of DON/ZEA mix regulated intestinal mucus secretion and several markers of intestinal immune system. The results showed that LGG partially prevented or treated the unwanted adverse effects of DON/ZEA in mice . This offers a potential dietary intervention strategy against intestinal exposure to mycotoxins.

17107214.label: Realisation of objectives
17107214.value: After receiving the grant, our team (PI and Co-Is) immediately started working together efficiently on the project. Overall, this RCT was carried out as planned, following the methodological designs. All the milestones and study objectives were successfully achieved. RAs (dental hygienists) and a PhD student were first recruited and trained. Some logistic preparations were completed. Invitations were then sent to secondary schools. A total of 484 adolescents were recruited from 12 participating schools. Randomization was done at school basis (i.e. cluster randomization) to avoid possible intervention contamination. There were 156, 169 and 159 participants assigned to Groups I to III respectively. At baseline and after 6, 12, and 24 months, questionnaires were administered to collect information on socio-demographic factors, oral health self-efficacy, and oral health behaviors. Silness & Löe Plaque index and the International Caries Detection and Assessment System (ICDAS) were employed to record participants’ oral hygiene and caries status, respectively. Within 6 weeks after baseline data collection, Group I-III received their respective interventions, i.e. conventional health education (CE), motivation interviewing (MI) by face-to-face individual counseling, and online group MI. Data were entered and intention-to-treat analysis was performed. Mixed-effects logistic regression and generalized linear mixed model were constructed to adjust for confounding factors and address the clustering effect (by “school”). The data collected at 4 time points (baseline and after 6, 12, and 24 months)allowed us to evaluate and compare the short-, mid-, and long-term effectiveness of the 3 interventions (CE, face-to-face individual MI, and online group MI) in changing adolescents' oral health-related self-efficacy and behaviors and protecting their oral health. The project period was originally proposed as 30 months. The participant recruitment and baseline work however took slightly longer than what we expected. Since some schools had pre-scheduled events/activities in the suggested period, our baseline work in these schools were postponed to later dates in order to avoid clash and minimize the disturbance of the school operation. We reported this to RGC and a 6-month project extension was approved. The trial was then completed within a 36-month study period.

17107214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17107214.value: The findings of this trial showed some significant differences among Group I (CE), Group II (face-to-face individual MI) and Group III (online group MI) in their changes of oral health behaviors, oral hygiene status and oral health. After 6 months, significant improvement in snacking and toothbrushing behavior in Group II and oral hygiene status in Group III were observed, compared with Group I (all p<0.05). After 12 months, compared with Group I, there was significantly better toothbrushing behavior in Group II and significantly better oral hygiene status and smaller total caries increment in both Group II and Group III (all p<0.05). After 24 months, 437 (90.3%) participants were followed up. Bivariate analysis showed that significantly lower plaque score was found in Group II (p=0.009) and Group III (p=0.040) compared with Group I [means(SD): 1.00(0.52), 0.84(0.50), and 0.87(0.53) for Groups I to III respectively]. No significant difference was detected between Group II and Group III (p>0.05). Significantly smaller increment of cavitated surfaces (△DICDAS3-6MFS) was found in Group III, compared with Group I [mean(SD):0.58(1.55) vs. 0.85(1.54); p=0.043]. However, Group II did not differ from the other two groups (both p>0.05). Significantly smaller mean increment of total carious surfaces (△DICDAS1-6MFS) was detected in Group II [1.57(4.25); p=0.008] and Group III [1.13(3.20); p=0.020], compared with Group I [2.37 (3.93)], while Group II did not significantly differ from Group III (p>0.05). In terms of self-efficacy and behaviors, no significant difference was found in both intervention groups, compared with Group I (all p>0.05). Multivariate analysis showed no significant difference in self-efficacy, behaviors, plaque score and caries status among the three groups after 24 months (all p>0.05). Findings of this RCT supported that 1. Both face-to-face individual MI and online group MI outperformed CE in improving adolescents’ oral health, as evidenced by the greater improvement in some health behaviors, oral hygiene and caries status. 2. While 6- and 12-month findings of this trial supported the superiority of MI in both modes in changing a whole range of behavioral and clinical outcomes, evidence on its 24-month effect on clinical outcomes was less robust. This suggests a need for follow-up counselling session to reinforce the positive changes. 3. At all time points (6-, 12- & 24-months), the effectiveness of online group was similar to that of face-to-face individual MI, if not higher. With its other advantages (access, efficiency & anonymity), online group MI is a viable alternative for promoting positive behavioral changes in the young generation.

17107214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17107214.value: This study provided evidence on the effectiveness of two modes of motivational interviewing (face-to-face individual MI and online group MI) in changing adolescents' oral health related behaviors and protecting their oral health. Further study can be conducted in the following areas: 1. To test the effectiveness of MI in eliciting other positive oral health behaviors of adolescents, such as smoking cessation, regular flossing, regular dental visit 2. To evaluate the acceptance and effectiveness of alternative modes of MI (telephone, mails, online chatting, group counseling) in promoting oral health of other age groups, especially the hard-to-reach communities for health promotion 3. To analyze the process of the counseling and identify possible effect moderators and mediators in dental MI counseling 4. To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of MI interventions (in various modes) for improving oral health

17107214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17107214.value: Empowering people to adopt healthy living is an important and difficult task. Adolescents is a group that is know to be particularly resistant to advice giving and they often do not put health as one of their priorities. This 24-month research trial among 484 adolescents from 12 local secondary schools showed that, by respecting their autonomy and eliciting their own perspectives/reasons/ arguments, motivational interviewing (MI) helps adolescents to find their motivation/solutions to change their behaviors and improve their oral health. As the very first of this kind, the trial showed that online group MI was equally effective as face-to-face individual MI, if not more effective. Given its other advantages (access, efficiency & anonymity), online group MI is a viable alternative for health intervention for this group. This is particularly relevant since Internet communication is becoming part of the lifestyle of the young generation.

17107314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107314.value: 圍產期膽道閉鎖（Perinatal Biliary Atresia, PBA）是一種罕見的嚴重疾病， 以在生後最初幾個星期漸進性的纖維硬化和肝外膽道系統的炎性閉塞為特徵。 手術是唯一的治療方法， 但治療結果較差。 PBA呈現單純性（非綜合徵）並散發性發病。 PBA的相關病理理論提出， 在圍產期未知的環境因素施加於遺傳易感個體的免疫系統而引發無法控制的免疫反應， 導致肝纖維化和肝外膽汁導管閉鎖。 患者的“遺傳”易感性是至關重要的。 散發的罕見疾病是由要么從頭突變（非遺傳）或隱性遺傳性的破壞DNA/突變基因的編碼序列（Coding Sequence, CDS）， 從而解釋PBA的散發性和罕見性。 過對24個散發性PBA患者肝組織DNA的全外顯子組測序（Whole Exome Sequencing, WES）， 我們發現並確認48例，獨特的、破壞性的突變（包括肝臟組織和外周血液中）。 這些突變是分佈在27個基因（包括同一基因不同位點的反複變異）， 參肝臟發育， 免疫調控， 或者纖毛性疾病。 變異是遺傳的， 往往為複合雜合遺傳或者潛在的雙基因遺傳。 候選突變基因和疾病的關聯可能只能通過在獨立樣本中識別新的和重複的突變來鑑別。 這需要對相對大樣本患者的篩選。 鑑於我們已獲得的有疾病相關潛力和意義的數據， 同時因為結果復制對於了解病人的突變譜及闡釋基因在疾病的影響具有愈來重要的意義， 我們現在建議在604例PBA患者（迄今最大的PBA樣本）中篩查新發現的BA-候選基因。 該提案的成功將有助於解決我們的核心問題： 是否通過WES得出的突變基因參與PBA的發病？ 如果是， 我們將提供PBA的遺傳基準， 對病人和醫療工作產生的巨大而重要的影響， 包括能提供基因檢測而對早期或產前診斷預防措施， 提供懷孕的風險規避措施。 相關的知識將有助於了解疾病發病機理， 最終制定相關治療措施。 這個提案在中國尤其相關， 其PBA發生率是在世界範圍內最高的一個， 而PBA仍然是最嚴重的兒童肝臟疾病之一。

17108314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108314.value: 大多數腫瘤細胞的基因遺傳並不穩定。儘管基因組不穩定可以加速腫瘤細胞的增殖與惡化，但與此同時這種“機會屬性”也會令它們面對特定的靶向藥物時，更容易被選擇性殺死，其背後的原理就是“協同致死”。在眾多卓有成效，利用協同致死原理的治療方案中，使用PARP抑製劑來治療BRCA相關癌症的方案，強有力地揭示了研究DNA損傷信號傳導及修復的迫切重要性，也為利用研究DNA損傷修復從而開發人類基因組不穩定性相關疾病的治療方案，提供了可行性示範。 我們的研究目的是探索理解細胞如何保護基因組的完整性。基於對細胞如何檢測及應答基因損傷，和DNA損傷信號如何誘導細胞檢驗點控制和DNA損傷修復方面的興趣，我們最近發現並報導了在DNA雙鏈損傷中起到負調控信號作用的Ring Finger 蛋白RNF169。正是由於DNA損傷應答與腫瘤發生之間已經建立起的聯繫，RNF169的發現為我們提供了難得的機會來研究RNF169異常可能會怎樣導致人類腫瘤的發生。 為了進一步了解RNF169的異常表達是如何干擾基因組的完整性，我們分析了RNF169的相互作用圖譜，以期發現RNF169是如何被調控。 DYKR1A激酶正是一種我們發現參與RNF169相互作用的蛋白。如同RNF169一樣，DYRK1A聚集於DNA雙鏈損傷部位，然後抑制乳腺癌宮頸癌易感基因產物BRCA1在DNA雙鏈損傷部位的聚集。這正說明RNF169－DYRK1A複合體在BRCA1依賴的腫瘤抑制功能中可能起到相當重要的作用。 本次申請中，我們計劃研究RNF169如何參與細胞中的基因損傷應答；RNF169的異常表達是如何影響細胞對化療的敏感性；以及RNF169的功能異常對基因組不穩定性和腫瘤發生的影響。我們還會研究RNF169和DYRK1A作為負調控因子在DNA雙鏈損傷信號傳導和修復中的功能聯繫；和分析由於負調控導致的BRCA1和其他DNA損傷應答蛋白（如在DNA修復，細胞週期檢驗點控制和轉錄調控中起作用的DNA損傷應答蛋白）在DNA損傷部位的聚集減少所導致的可能後果。 通過完成這項工作計劃，我們將會闡明RNF169基因異常如何影響基因組的不穩定性和人類癌症的發生；推動對於細胞中基因損傷應答基本原理的理解；以及為發展制定基因組不穩定相關人類疾病的診斷治療方案提供知識基礎。

17108314.label: Realisation of objectives
17108314.value: We have successfully completed the project, and have published the research findings in two research papers. An L, Dong C, Li J, Chen J, Yuan J, Huang J, Chan KM, Yu CH, Huen MS. RNF169 limits 53BP1 deposition at DSBs to stimulate single-strand annealing repair. PNAS 2018; 115(35): E8266-E8295. An L, Jiang Y, Ng HH, Man EP, Chen J, Khoo US, Gong Q, Huen MS. Dual-utility NLS drives RNF169-dependent DNA damage responses. PNAS 2017; 114(4): E2872-E2881. Briefly, we have delineated how RNF169 restrains DNA damage responses by limiting 53BP1 occupancy on the damaged chromatin, and how this in turns regulates choice of DNA double-strand break repair pathways. We also identified the ubiquitin specific protease USP7 as an RNF169 regulator, and showed in breast cancer specimens that the two proteins exhibit a positive correlation in their expression pattern. Furthermore, we have consolidated the RNF169-DYRK1A interaction, and are currently writing up a manuscript to describe how DYRK1A coordinates DNA repair with gene transcription activities.

17108314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108314.value: We are currently extending our work to more in-depth study how DNA double-strand breaks are repaired on the active chromatin. Recent evidence highlights a transcription-coupled DNA repair pathway to ensure that gene transcription can be temporary halted, and that failing to couple gene transcription and DNA repair can have devastation consequences on genome stability. We are therefore taking a lead to further dissect the molecular determinants that drive this transcription-coupled NA repair process.

17108314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108314.value: Swift activation of DNA repair is key to genome integrity protection. Exactly how cells have evolved to activate DNA repair in the right time at the right place remains obscure. In this study we have identified the Ring Finger protein RNF169 as a molecular rheostat that fine-tunes the output of DNA damage signals, and plays a role in DNA repair pathway choice. Deficiency of RNF169 compromises genome stability, and may contribute to human cancers. Our work therefore provides the molecular bases to examine how RNF169 dysregulation may fuel human tumourigenesis.

17108514.label: Project Objectives
17108514.value: To determine the relationship between CMM metrics and brain cytoarchitecture after ischemic stroke. Rationale: In order to draw inferences from CMM metrics, it is imperative to investigate the longitudinal change thereof along the course of ischemic infarction. We will therefore perform a cross-sectional stroke patient study. Structural MRI will be performed to corroborate the longitudinal changes in CMM metrics. Impact: Potential biophysical interpretation of CMM will help elucidate the mechanism that is associated with recovery of motor function after stroke. To investigate the association between CMM metrics and spontaneous and rehabilitation-induced motor recovery after stroke. Rationale: Since the potential of motor function recovery is believed to be associated with stroke-related microstructural changes, we hypothesize that CMM will provide prognostic indicators of motor recovery and possibly rehabilitation outcome. We will determine the association between CMM metrics measured during acute stroke and spontaneous and rehabilitation-induced recovery of stroke patients. Impact: The ability to determine a patient’s motor recovery using CMM will potentially help tailor rehabilitative interventions.

17108514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108514.value: 第一次中風後，大約有三分之一的中風患者忍受持續性運動障礙。旨在提高患者的自主管理日常活動的能力的康復干預措施是促進運動功能恢復的關鍵。關於具體的康復方案的設計決策是由病人的潛在運動恢復等因素的臨床評估管轄。Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) 是一種有前途的磁共振成像方法，用於量化中風對大腦的顯微結構的損傷與中風患者最終的恢復功能。對於慢性中風，幾個DTI的研究表明，非理想的運動功能恢復與DTI的參數有相關聯。不過，相應的DTI結果尚未可靠的證實在急性中風。由於延遲中風後的復康往往會導致更糟的運動功能，提高神經影像學技術在中風急性期評估恢復的潛力是有迫切的需要。 我們開發了一種磁共振成像方法叫做cerebral microenvironment modeling (CMM) 。我們相信，我們的新技術將大大提高中風對腦組織的檢查。在這項研究中，我們的中心假設是從我們的CMM將提供有效的中風腦損傷的標記，而且它可能是一個運動功能恢復的可靠的預後指標。這一假設將通過以下的目標進行測試：（1）確定CMM的參數和缺血性中風後的腦細胞結構之間的關係。（2）調查中風後的CMM的參數和運動功能恢復之間的關聯。 成功完成這項項目將提供中風恢復期的靈敏的影像學標誌。

17108514.label: Realisation of objectives
17108514.value: We have successfully performed all the objectives. We were able to recruit a total of 37 patients. Of these, we have lost some due to attrition: n=25 (less than a week after stroke), n=18 (one month after stroke), n=14 (three months after stroke), and n=11 (six months after stroke). It is to our utmost frustration that we did not find any statistical significance for neither objectives regardless of the biophysical models that were investigated (CMM or NODDI). In an effort to investigate the elusive biomarker(s) for prognostication of motor recovery after stroke, we reanalyzed all our data by using a more holistic approach to characterize the brain. Numerous studies have demonstrated that it is the specific brain network (i.e. the connections amongst specific brain regions) that ischemic infarct disrupts, rather than infarct size, that is attributable to neurological sequelae, thus suggesting the notion that the relationship between brain changes and functional impairment and recovery should be studied from the perspective of the brain as a network, rather than local regional changes (which was the original objectives of this proposal). We therefore used the diffusion MRI data to estimate the anatomical connections between all the 90 brain regions in the automated anatomical labeling atlas. Apart from examining individual connections in the structural brain networks, any changes in the topology and local characteristics of the entire networks can also be studied in the context of functional deficits and recovery. This could be made possible by a method known as brain connectivity analysis. In normal brain, the topology of brain network was found to be characterized by high local clustering (the number of connections between nearest neighbors of a brain region with respect to all possible connections; it represents the efficiency of local information transfer) and short paths (the smallest number of connections that have to be traversed to get from one brain region to another; it is related to global information transfer) using network analysis. Such topology, known as ‘small-world’ topology, permits economical information exchange that is essential for maintaining normal brain physiology. Previous studies have shown that the information exchange between neighboring brain regions became less efficient (i.e. decreased local clustering), and there was a shift from small-world to random motor network (i.e. a topology with low local clustering and shorter paths) for stroke patients with good clinical recovery. With brain connectivity analysis, we aimed to investigate the relation between stroke recovery (defined as the difference in upper extremity Fugl-Meyer motor scale and Barthel index between 6 months versus less than a week after stroke) and the structural brain network at baseline. Although we have observed some longitudinal changes in the structural brain network, none of which are related to motor recovery. On the other hand, we have observed significant associations between motor recovery and baseline local structural brain network of the ipsilesional superior frontal gyrus and caudate, and between functional recovery and baseline local structural brain network of ipsilesional amygdala, cuneus and supramarginal gyrus, and contralesional superior frontal gyrus. Significant association of the global brain network at baseline and a month after stroke with motor recovery were also found. Altogether, we have successfully demonstrated that the global and local structural brain networks measured at less than a week after stroke onset are related to the brain functional recovery measured at 6 months after stroke for patients with first acute stroke in the motor system. Our results indicate that the baseline residual structural brain network may be relevant to the prediction of the functional outcome of patients with first acute ischemic stroke in the motor system.

17108514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108514.value: Although we did not find any statistical significance for neither objectives regardless of the biophysical models that were investigated (CMM or NODDI), we have successfully demonstrated that the global and local structural brain networks measured at less than a week after stroke onset are related to the brain functional recovery measured at 6 months after stroke for patients with first acute stroke in the motor system. Our results likely indicate that the baseline residual structural brain network may be relevant to the prediction of the functional outcome of patients with first acute ischemic stroke in the motor system. This work has been submitted and is currently under review in Scientific Reports (see manuscript in the Part C1). As was alluded in previous report, we have also stumbled on the implication on cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) on brain changes. In particular, previous studies have shown that different types of SVD lesion (there are four major types, namely cerebral microbleed, lacunar infarct, white matter hyperintensity, visible perivascular space) disrupt structural brain network individually. Because these types of lesions often coexist and that there was a lack of investigation on the collective effect of these lesions on the structural brain network, we investigated the thereof in 95 patients with first transient ischemic attack (TIA) or ischemic stroke, 59 and 36 of whom with and without SVD lesions, respectively. We used the previously published total SVD score to account for the collective effect of these SVD lesions (or the total SVD burden). Our results showed that the global efficiency and characteristic path length of the structural brain network are respectively lower and higher due to SVD. Lower nodal efficiency is also found in the insular, precuneus, supplementary motor area, paracentral lobule, putamen and hippocampus. The total SVD score is correlated with global network measures, the local clustering coefficient and nodal efficiency of hippocampus, and the nodal efficiency of paracentral lobule. We have successfully demonstrated that the disruption of global and local structural brain networks are associated with the increase in the overall SVD severity or burden of patients with TIA or first-time stroke.

17108514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108514.value: Considering that there are two types of connections that make up a brain network, namely structural (SC) and functional connectivities (FC). Future development of this research should include the investigation of the association between motor recovery and functional brain network. In so doing, one could thus investigate the spatiotemporal relationship between neurological diseases and behavioral deficit as well as functional recovery more systematically. Another avenue that is worth pursuing is that mass-univariate approaches have been widely used for investigating the relationship between imaging biomarker and patient outcome at the group level. Prognostication of individual patients can be made possible by using multivariate methods, which likely have greater statistical power and are less prone to outliers, to combine observations across the whole brain and from different modalities. We strongly believe that such prediction model will potentially benefit clinicians for tailoring timely rehabilitative strategies.

17108514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108514.value: Since rehabilitation has a strong bearing on the recovery of stroke patients, better neuroimaging techniques for evaluating the potential for recovery during the acute stages of stroke would potentially be valuable for the planning of appropriate and timely rehabilitative intervention. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been indispensable in numerous diagnosis of neurological diseases and disorders. Particularly, diffusion MRI has been very sensitive to brain changes due to stroke. Nevertheless, the diffusion MRI biomarker for the prognostication of the outcome of stroke patient remains elusive. The overall goal of this research is thus to find the said biomarker. That our original hypothesis that biomarker akin to tissue microstructural properties could be the potential prognsotic indicator was rejected by our results has us led to explore alternative approach that exploits the fact that the brain is a network of interconnected brain regions. Thanks to the brain connectivity analysis, which permits the characterization of the brain at the global and local scales, we have successfully demonstrated that the structural brain networks at less than a week after stroke may be relevant to the prediction of the motor recovery of patients with first-time acute ischemic stroke.

17108614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108614.value: Hepatitis B virus infection remains an important clinical issue among patients on renal replacement therapy. Seroprotection rate as defined by an anti-HBs (hepatitis B surface antibody) titre ≥10 IU/L after intramuscular hepatitis B vaccination (HBVv) remains poor in this cohort. Factors associated with inadequate anti-HBs response include older age, diabetes mellitus and concomitant immunosuppression. Various methods including intradermal vaccination, high dose intramuscular vaccination and adjuvant vaccines were attempted with variable response. Apart from adopting the aforementioned techniques, imiquimod, a synthetic Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) agonist useful for the treatment of DNA virus infection, has been shown to improve vaccine immunogenicity against influenza virus in both human and mouse models, and also against other infections including human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus and malaria. Imiquimod induces cytokine production through the activation of TLR7 and nuclear factor-kappa B. We aim to enroll 120 adult subjects on renal replacement therapy in this prospective double blind randomized placebo controlled trial over a period of 2 years. All recruited subjects have to be HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen), anti-HBs, anti-HBc (hepatitis B core antibody) and anti-HIV (HIV antibody) negative. The safety, immunogenicity and clinical efficacy of the intradermal HBVv with topical imiquimod ointment pretreatment will be compared with topical placebo aqueous cream pretreatment, and conventional intramuscular HBVv. Enrolled patients will be randomized into 3 groups after written informed consent: Group 1: four reduced doses of 10μg intradermal HBVv with topical imiquimod ointment pretreatment; Group 2: four reduced doses of 10μg intradermal HBVv with topical placebo aqueous cream pretreatment; Group 3: four high doses of 40μg intramuscular HBVv with topical placebo aqueous cream pretreatment. All intradermal vaccines will be given via a microneedle syringe and the vaccination schedule will be at 0, 1, 3 and 6 months. Patients and investigators will be blinded to the type of topical treatment applied. Anti-HBs titre will be measured at baseline, before each vaccination, and at 12 and 18 months after the first dose of vaccination. The primary end point is the seroprotection rate of the HBVv at 12 months after the first dose of vaccination. The secondary end points are the seroprotection rate of HBVv and the geometric mean titre (GMT) fold increase of the anti-HBs at 1, 3, 6, 12 (GMT only) and 18 months after the first dose of vaccination. 17108614.label: Realisation of objectives
17108614.value: A total of 116 patients on dialysis were screened, of which 94 patients underwent randomisation. 92 patients completed the study. One patient from each of the IMQ_ID and the AQ_IM succumbed before 52 weeks after the first vaccination. Both patients succumbed from community acquired pneumonia which were not related to the HBVv. Thirty-two patients were randomized to the IMQ_ID group, and 31 patients were randomized to AQ_ID and AQ_IM respectively. Overall, 28.7% and 71.3% of the patients were on HD and CAPD respectively. Fifty-four patients (57.4%) received previous HBVv with no response. The median age was 60.5 [Interquartile range (IQR) 53.5-67.5] years and 59.5% of the patients were male. Past medical history, cause of renal failure and baseline laboratory findings were well matched among the three groups. Safety No serious adverse events related to vaccination were reported. Incidence of local or systemic adverse events was infrequent and self-limiting. Although grade 1 pain, swelling, induration and hyperpigmentation were more commonly found in IMQ_ID and the AQ_ID groups, there were no statistically significant differences among the three groups. None of the subjects had visible vaccine leakage from the injection site. Primary and secondary outcome measure The primary outcome by intention to treat of seroprotection rate was significantly higher at week 52 for the treatment group (IMQ_ID) with 96.9% seroprotection rate, comparing to 74.2% and 48.4% for the AQ_ID and AQ_IM groups respectively (p<0.001). The GMC was also significantly higher at week 52 for the IMQ_ID group of 1135 mIU/mL (95% CI 579.4-2218.2 mIU/mL), comparing to 86.9 mIU/mL (95% CI 18.5-409.3 mIU/mL) and 7.2 mIU/mL (2.0-26.5mIU/mL) for the AQ_ID and AQ_IM groups respectively (p<0.001) (Table 3 and Figure 3). The seroprotection rate and GMC measured at all five time points were significantly higher for the IMQ_ID group (p<0.001). The seroprotection rate remained at 96.9% with a very high GMC 631 mIU/mL (95% CI 312.6-1273.5 mIU/mL) at 78 weeks. Subgroup analysis of the 54 initial non-responders (all previously received a 4-dose regimen of Engerix-B 20μg) demonstrated a similar pattern. The seroprotection rate and GMC measured at all five time points were significantly higher for the IMQ_ID group (p<0.01 and p<0.001 respectively). The peak GMC of the non-responders IMQ_ID group at 52 weeks and 78 weeks was even higher when compared to the IMQ_ID group as a whole [1721.9 (95% CI 826-3581) mIU/mL and 984 (95% CI 533.3-1811.3) mIU/mL vs. 1135 (95% CI 579.4-2218.2) mIU/mL and 631 (95% CI 312.6-1273.5) mIU/mL]. Univariate analysis demonstrated that IMQ_ID vaccination was associated with higher seroprotection rate whereas higher neutrophil count was associated with lower seroprotection rate at 52 week. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that IMQ_ID vaccination [Odds ratio (OR) 3.70 (95% CI 1.16-11.81; p=0.027)] was independently associated with higher seroprotection rate at 52 weeks. With regard to the safety and practical concern of topical application of TLR7 agonist and intradermal injection of the aluminium hydroxide containing Sci-B-Vac™, results from this study demonstrated clearly such strategy is safe. Although the local side effects of grade 1 swelling, induration and pigmentation were more common via the intradermal route, such local side effects were self-limiting and showed no significant difference among the three groups. The results were comparable to the dermatological local side effects found in a recent report on intradermal HBVv in dialysis patients.14 Systemic side effects were infrequent in all three groups. The limitations of this study are that the long-term immunological data beyond 2 years after vaccination was not available. Clinical trial with larger sample size will be necessary to better assess the safety profile and clinical efficacy in the prevention of hepatitis B infection. The effect of TLR7 agonist in single S-antigen containing HBVv has yet to be tested. Accelerated regimen with fewer doses and dosage could be explored. Other poor HBVv or non-responders due to disease entities including post-transplant, immunosuppressed and HIV should also be studied. Hepatitis B specific T cell response should also be analysed in future study, and lastly, we believe this strategy is well suited for other vaccines such as influenza and zoster in this and similar high-risk populations.

17108614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108614.value: Background & Aims Patients on dialysis are hyporesponsive to the current hepatitis B virus vaccines (HBVv). We conducted a phase 2 trial examining four-doses of intradermal HBVv with topical TLR7 agonist imiquimod pretreatment in dialysis patients. Methods In this double blind, randomized-controlled trial, we enrolled and prospectively followed adult patients on either haemodialysis or continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis between January 2016 and September 2018. Eligible patients were randomly allocated (1:1:1) into one treatment: topical imiquimod-cream followed by intradermal HBVv (IMQ_ID), and two control groups: topical aqueous-cream (placebo) followed by intradermal HBVv (AQ_ID) and topical aqueous-cream followed by intramuscular HBVv (AQ_IM). The primary end-point was the seroprotection rate (anti-HBs ≥10mIU/mL) at 52 weeks after the first dose of HBVv. Results Ninety-four patients on dialysis were enrolled, among which 57.4% were non-responders. The primary outcome of seroprotection rate was significantly better at week 52 for the treatment group (IMQ_ID) with 96.9% seroprotection rate, comparing compared to 74.2% and 48.4% for the AQ_ID and AQ_IM groups, respectively (p<0.001). The GMC was also significantly higher at week 52 for the IMQ_ID group of 1135 mIU/mL (95% CI, 579.4-2218.2 mIU/mL), compared to 86.9 mIU/mL (95% CI, 18.5-409.3 mIU/mL) and 7.2 mIU/mL (2.0-26.5mIU/mL) for the AQ_ID and AQ_IM groups, respectively (p<0.001). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that IMQ_ID vaccination [OR, 3.70 (95% CI, 1.16-11.81; p=0.027) was the only factor independently associated with higher seroprotection rate at 52 weeks. Adverse reaction was infrequent. Conclusion Pretreatment with topical TLR7 agonist imiquimod before intradermal HBVv was safe with favorable seroprotection and as such potentially improved prevention against HBV infection for dialysis patients.

17108614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108614.value: Pretreatment with topical TLR7 agonist imiquimod before intradermal HBVv is safe with favorable and prolonged seroprotection. We are following-up the recruited patients for a longer-period up to 5 years post vaccination and study their antibody response. In view of the relatively small sample size, we also plan to perform a much larger size study. This strategy will improve prevention against HBV infection for dialysis patients and have the potential to change the current vaccination policy in immunocompromised hosts and poor responders.

17108614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108614.value: Background and context Hepatitis B infection remains an important clinical issue among patients on dialysis and is associated with high risk of complication including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma and mortality. Nevertheless, patients on dialysis have poor response to the current hepatitis B virus vaccines. New findings In this phase 2 double-blind randomized controlled trial with 94 patients (57.4% non-responders) on dialysis, the seroprotection rate (96.6%) and antibody titre (1135 mIU/mL) at week 52 in the group who received intradermal hepatitis B vaccination with topical imiquimod pretreatment were significantly higher than the controls (intramuscular and intradermal hepatitis B vaccination only). This trend was maintained from week 4 to week 78 after vaccination. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that intradermal hepatitis B vaccination with topical imiquimod pretreatment was the only factor independently associated with higher seroprotection rate at week 52. Limitations Relatively small sample size and longer follow-up needed. Impact Pretreatment with topical imiquimod before intradermal hepatitis B vaccination is safe with favorable and prolonged seroprotection. This strategy will improve prevention against hepatitis B infection for dialysis patients and have the potential to change the current vaccination policy in immunocompromised hosts and poor responders.

17109114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109114.value: 先天免疫是人體對付入侵的病源微生物及其他危險信號的第一道防線。最新發現的cGAMP第二信使及其受體蛋白STING是微生物DNA 或人體本身受損的DNA所觸發的 先天免疫的重要組成部分，其激活可導致干擾素的大量產生。人類的cGAMP含有特殊的2’-3’和2’-5’混合磷酸二酯鍵。既然有負責合成人類cGAMP的cGAMP合酶cGAS，人體細胞中必然也應存在分解cGAMP的磷酸二酯酶。我們已發現一種新的冠狀病毒蛋白可能具有分解cGAMP的能力，隨之又發現另一種人體CNP 蛋白可能有cGAMP磷酸二酯酶的活性。本項目主要研究CNP 的生物化學及生物學特性。首先，我們將確定具備cGAMP 水解活性的人類磷酸二酯酶。其次，我們將確定此類酶的催化產物及酶學特性。再次，我們將深入研究此類酶在病毒與人體的相互作用過程中的生物學意義，特別是對人體識別病毒DNA以及人體對抗病毒感染的實際影響。本項研究不僅解答了DNA 所誘導的先天免疫中的一個重要問題，而且對新型抗病毒藥物、免疫調節藥物及疫苗的研制也有啟迪作用。

17109114.label: Realisation of objectives
17109114.value: All three parts of our project as stated in our original proposal have been executed fully. All proposed experiments have been done and many additional studies have also been conducted. A human PDE for cGAMP named ENPP1 has been published (Li L, Yin Q, Kuss P, Maliga Z, Millán JL, Wu H, Mitchison TJ. Hydrolysis of 2'3'-cGAMP by ENPP1 and design of nonhydrolyzable analogs. Nat Chem Biol 2014;10:1043-1048) immediately before the start of our project. However, the in vitro and in vivo PDE activity of either or CNP could not be detected by us or by other groups due to technical difficulty. The best result that we obtained is the activity of a novel viral protein that decreases cGAMP levels in cultured cells as measured by mass spectrometry. We suspected that it could be an enzyme that acts on the G(2'-5')A dinucleotide. Further investigations are underway and we are trying really hard to complete this study and publish a decent paper. At the end of our project, the search for human PDE still goes on. To overcome the difficulties in cGAMP detection, we have recently used commercial ELISA kits to measure intracellular cGAMP. To overcome the difficulties in purifying functional recombinant PDE from mammalian cells, we have tried to make use of a good anti-CNP antibody to immunoprecipitate the protein from cultured cells where CNP was shown to be active. We need more time to complete our ongoing studies. As stated in our original proposal, “If no candidate PDEs are identified in Sections 1.1 and 1.2 or if others have published the cGAMP-hydrolyzing PDEs before the completion of our study, we will focus on any novel cGAMP-binding proteins identified in Section 1.2”. We therefore activated our contingency plan. We focused on a new transcript isoform of STING named STING-β that binds cGAMP and modified our Specific Aims 2 and 3 to characterize it fully. In addition, a transcript isoform of IFI16 designated IFI16-β that cooperates with cGAS-cGAMP-STING in DNA sensing was also identified and characterized. In 2018, we published two original research articles on STING-β and IFI16-β. These are major achievements of our project. In our Specific Aim 1, global analysis of cGAMP-binding proteins revealed one new transcript isoform of STING. This isoform STING-β was found to bind with cGAMP tightly. In light of this, in our Specific Aim 2, functional characterization of STING-β was performed. Particularly, STING-β was shown to compete with STING-α for binding with cGAMP. In addition, STING-β also associated with other sensors including IFI16-β, which is also novel. IFI16-β was identified initially through its association with STING-β. In our Specific Aim 3, the biological significance of STING-β in DNA sensing and viral infection were defined. STING-β functions as a dominant negative version that suppresses DNA sensing and viral induction of innate antiviral response. A paper summarizing our findings was published in Nucleic Acids Research (Wang et al., 2018a). In addition to this, we also made an effort to characterize the function of IFI16-β in the inhibition of AIM2 inflammasome activation. Our findings on IFI16-β were published in EMBO Reports (Wang et al., 2018b) and featured in the October issue of the journal. Both studies are the direct results of this RGC-GRF project.

17109114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109114.value: 1. We identified and characterized a novel transcript isoform of human STING designated STING-β that dominantly inhibits innate nucleic acid sensing. STING is a core adaptor in innate nucleic acid sensing in mammalian cells, on which different sensing pathways converge to induce type I interferon (IFN) production. Particularly, STING is activated by 2',3'-cGAMP, a cyclic dinucleotide containing mixed phosphodiester linkages and produced by cytoplasmic DNA sensor cGAS. The STING-β isoform that we identified has no transmembrane domains. It was widely expressed at low levels in various human tissues. Induction of STING-β by RNA and DNA viruses correlated inversely with IFN-β production. The expression of STING-β declined in patients with lupus, in which type I IFNs are commonly overproduced. STING-β suppressed the induction of IFNs, IFN-stimulated genes and other cytokines by various immunostimulatory agents including cyclic dinucleotides, DNA, RNA and viruses, whereas depletion of STING-β showed the opposite effect. STING-β interacted with STING-α and antagonized its antiviral function. STING-β also interacted with TBK1 and prevented it from binding with STING-α, TRIF or other transducers. In addition, STING-β bound to 2',3'-cGAMP and impeded its binding with and activation of STING-α, leading to suppression of IFN-β production. Taken together, STING-β sequesters 2',3'-cGAMP second messenger and other transducer molecules to inhibit innate nucleic acid sensing dominantly. Our findings reveal another new level of regulation in cGAMP-dependent signalling and have important implications in the study of not only innate antiviral immunity but also autoimmune diseases (Wang et al., 2018a). 2. We identified and characterized a novel transcript isoform of human IFI16 named IFI16-β which interacts with STING-β. IFI16-β was isolated through its association with STING-β. IFI16-β also has a domain architecture similar to that of mouse p202. Mouse p202 is a disease locus for lupus and a dominant-negative inhibitor of AIM2 inflammasome activation. A human homolog of p202 has not been identified so far. Like p202, human IFI16-β contains two HIN domains, but lacks the pyrin domain. IFI16-β is ubiquitously expressed in various human tissues and cells. Its mRNA levels are also elevated in leukocytes of patients with lupus, virus-infected cells and cells treated with IFN-β or phorbol ester. IFI16-β co-localizes with AIM2 in the cytoplasm, whereas IFI16-α is predominantly found in the nucleus. IFI16-β interacts with AIM2 to impede the formation of a functional AIM2-ASC complex. In addition, IFI16-β sequesters cytoplasmic dsDNA and renders it unavailable for AIM2 sensing. Enforced expression of IFI16-β inhibits the activation of AIM2 inflammasome, whereas knockdown of IFI16-β augments interleukin 1β secretion triggered by dsDNA but not dsRNA. Thus, cytoplasm-localized IFI16-β is functionally equivalent to mouse p202 that exerts an inhibitory effect on AIM2 inflammasome. Our findings revealed a functional homolog of mouse p202 in human which dominantly inhibits AIM2 inflammasome and also modulates cGAMP-dependent signaling for innate DNA sensing. Our study is relevant to the study of viral DNA sensing and autoimmunity (Wang et al., 2018b).

17109114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17109114.value: Two original research articles were published in Nucleic Acids Research and EMBO Reports. Both studies are derived directly from this project and most experiments were done as planned in our original proposal, although significantly more results are required for publication in these two journals that are among the best in the world. Therefore many more experiments were actually done and many more results were presented. We are proud that we can still conduct top-notch basic research in Hong Kong that have the potential to create significant impact in the field. Our future studies will continue to focus on cellular and viral PDEs that act on cGAMP or its degradation product such as G(2-5)pA dinucleotide. Developing cGAMP and other cyclic dinucleotides into antivirals, vaccine adjuvants and immuno-modulatory agents is another direction we might explore, although my main interest is still in basic research on cGAMP signaling. In particular, there are more interesting cGAMP-binding proteins that we can further study. With plenty of interesting leads generated in this project, we are highly confident that we can make other important conceptual contributions to the field, as long as we can get new funding. However, my funding on innate immunity projects will soon come to a major gap. Lack of stability and sustainability is the nature of research funding in Hong Kong, which we have to face and tackle. In order to support my group, I just have to work harder to obtain new funding from RGC or other sources so that our research on innate immunity will not be interrupted in the next few years.

17109114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109114.value: Innate immunity is our body’s first-line defense against invading viruses and other pathogens. cGAMP is one of the small signaling molecules that mammals including human use to activate innate immunity. The goal of our project is to identify the enzymes and other proteins that bind with cGAMP to control the signaling process in the activation of innate immunity. Two interesting proteins involved in the cGAMP signaling process were identified in our study. The first is another version of the STING protein bound and activated by cGAMP. This protein called STING-β can bind to cGAMP and then block its binding with other proteins, thereby shutting down the signaling process. The second known as IFI16-β is a protein that also binds to STING-β and works together with it to control the activation of innate immunity. We found that IFI16-β can bind with and inhibits a similar protein of the same group named AIM2, which mediates the formation of a protein machinery required for inflammation, another form of host response to viral infection. Defining the function of these two proteins involved in cGAMP signaling not only generates new knowledge in immunology but also reveals new targets and strategies for the control of viral infection.

17110414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110414.value: The primary goal of this project is to develop a safe and effective topical siRNA formulation to the airway for the treatment of influenza viral infections. The efficacy of traditional antiviral drugs is declining, partly due to the emergence of new strains. This is a particular problem for the treatment of influenza as these viruses evolve rapidly. A new effective therapy against influenza is highly sought-after. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) is a promising antiviral agent. Specially designed siRNA can mediate specific viral gene silencing, hence inhibits viral replication through RNA interference (RNAi). However various pulmonary obstacles and intracellular barriers for siRNA transport challenge this novel therapeutic molecule. The success of siRNA therapeutics relies on the development of an optimized formulation that is suitable and safe for human use. A series of amphipathic peptides which contain pH responsive 2,3-diaminoproprionic acid groups (LADap) have been shown by our group to deliver siRNA effectively to mediate specific gene silencing in various mammalian cell lines and primary cells. They have low to negligible toxicity and are able to form non-covalent complexes with siRNA. The major attractive property of these peptides is their ability to respond to pH change; inside the acidic endosomal compartments, the peptides change their structural conformation in response to the drop in pH, release the siRNA and destabilize the endosomal membranes. Consequently, the siRNA is able to escape from the degradative endosomal pathway, and the transfection efficiency is greatly enhanced. Our preliminary data demonstrate that by using LADap peptides to deliver siRNA targeting viral nucleocapsid protein (NP), over 10,000-fold reduction of virus titres was observed in vitro after viral infection, compared with the control. Further investigation is necessary to develop these promising peptide-based siRNA delivery systems into pharmaceutical formulations for clinical use. In this project, three major aims are proposed: (i) to optimize the in vitro efficacy of siRNA delivered by LADap peptides against influenza infection, using primarily, but not exclusively, human influenza A/PR/8/34 (H1N1) virus as model; (ii) to develop an effective peptide-based siRNA formulation in dry powder form for intranasal or inhalation route of administration; (iii) to evaluate the in vivo antiviral efficacy and safety of these formulations. The outcome of this project will have a profound impact on influenza research by providing an understanding of how delivery barriers to siRNA therapeutics can be overcome, making the clinical application of siRNA for influenza and other respiratory diseases possible and practical. 本項目主要的研究目的，在於研製一種安全和有效的小幹擾RNA（siRNA）製劑，用於治療流感病毒的感染。由於流感病毒變異非常迅速，新的病毒株不斷出現，導致傳統抗病毒藥物的臨床治療效果不斷地降低，這迫切需求一種新而有效的抗流感治療藥物。小干擾RNA是一有潛力的抗病毒物質。經過專門設計的小干擾RNA，能夠通過RNA干擾（RNAi）， 介導病毒基因的沉默，從而抑制病毒的複製。然而，由於小幹擾RNA是一種帶負電的生物分子，其應用於臨床治療流感，仍然存在許多遞送上的障礙，如肺部和細胞內的屏障。小幹擾RNA臨床上的成功應用，有賴於研製出安全和適合人類使用的製劑。 本研究組利用一系列含有pH響應性2,3-二氨基丙酸基團的兩親多肽（LADap）作為小幹擾RNA的遞送載體。研究發現這些多肽能夠在哺乳動物細胞系和原代細胞中，介導基因沉默效應。LADap多肽能夠跟小干擾RNA形成非共價聚合物，同時具有低毒的特點。此外，LADap多肽最重要的特性，在於它們能夠對環境的pH值產生應答。在細胞胞內體（endosome）的酸性環境下，隨著pH值的降低，多肽的構象隨之發生變化，導致小幹擾RNA從多肽複合物中釋放出來，多肽進一步影響胞內體膜的穩定性，導致小幹擾RNA從胞內體中逃逸出來，避免了其在胞內體發生降解，從而大大提高了遞送的效率。我們前期的研究結果證明，利用LADap多肽，有效地遞送抑制流感病毒核衣殼蛋白（nucleocapsid protein） 的小幹擾RNA進入細胞，病毒在體外感染的細胞內的複製降低了超過10,0000倍。 本項目有三個主要的研究目標：（i） 利用人甲型流感病毒株A/PR/8/34(H1N1)作為模型，優化由LADap多肽介導的小幹擾RNA體外抑制流感病毒感染的效果；（ii）研制出一種能夠經鼻或呼入給藥的多肽-小幹擾RNA 乾粉吸入劑；（iii）評價該製劑在體內的安全性和抗病毒功效。本項目的研究有助於進一步了解如何克服小干擾RNA的遞送障礙，使小幹擾RNA可以用於治療流感或其它呼吸道疾病，上述研究將會對流感領域的研究產生深遠的影響。

17110414.label: Realisation of objectives
17110414.value: 1. The efficacy of pH-responsive peptides in delivering siRNA targeting nucleocapsid protein (NP) of influenza virus was examined. siRNAs targeting the conserved sequence of viral NP were employed. A549 (adenocarcinomic human alveolar epithelial cells) and MDCK (Madin-Darby Canine Kidney cells) were transfected with peptide/siRNA complexes, followed by influenza virus A (H1N1) infection. Standard plaque assays was carried out to quantify the virus titer of samples after siRNA treatment. siRNA targeting NP-574, NP-1494 and NP-1496, which have been previously demonstrated to inhibit the replication of H1N1 influenza A virus were employed. Transfection of peptide/antiviral siRNA complexes resulted in significant reduction of virus titer in cultured MDCK and A549 cells, confirming the prophylaxis effect of pH-responsive peptides in delivering antiviral siRNA. The viral inhibition effect of the peptide/siRNA complexes in A549 cells was more remarkable than MDCK cells. Peptide/siRNA complexes may adopt distinct intracellular trafficking pathways in these two cell lines, thus the difference in siRNA transfection efficiency and virus inhibition effect. Overall, the result indicated that the antiviral effect was attributed to specific gene silencing effect of NP instead of non-specific innate immune response as the viral inhibition effect was not observed in negative control siRNA samples. 2. Spray dried and spray freeze dried powder formulations containing antiviral siRNA and pH-responsive peptides were prepared and their antiviral activity against influenza virus A (H1N1) infection was evaluated. Standard plaque assays was carried out to quantify the virus titer of mammalian cell samples after they were treated with the antiviral siRNA powder formulations. Inhalable dry powder formulations of peptide/siRNA complexes can be successfully produced by spray drying and spray freeze drying without compromising their physical integrity and biological activity. The transfection efficiency of LADap(Me)6-L1 peptides /siRNA powders was retained in the presence of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), making it a promising vector for pulmonary siRNA delivery. The antiviral activity of peptide/siRNA complexes was also preserved after drying. Inhalable spray dried powders containing LADap(Me)6-L1 and siRNA is a potential formulation for the prophylaxis and treatment of influenza in the future, and such delivery system could be adopted to deliver different siRNA sequences for the treatment of other respiratory diseases. 3. To evaluate the antiviral efficacy and safety of the formulations in animal models, the siRNA formulations were administered to animal through intratracheal route. Unfortunately, it was found that the peptides/siRNA formulation caused local inflammatory response in the lung following intratracheal administration, making it unsuitable for the subsequent in vivo antiviral study. Therefore, an alternative protocol was adopted, by using naked siRNA formulation. To evaluate the efficacy of the siRNA in vivo, three doses of siRNA (40ug each in 25ul of normal saline) were given to each of the mice, on the day before infection and after infection (two doses). The siRNA was administered intratracheally. On the day of infection, mice were inoculated with H1N1/PR8 viruses through intranasal instillation. Treatments included placebo and siRNA targeting nucleocapsid protein (NP-1496 siRNA). A reduction in number of plaques was observed on Day 2 post infection in mice treated with NP1496 siRNA. However, this reduction was not statistically significant from the control group. Furthermore, the dry powder formulations of naked siRNA was also developed using spray drying and spray freeze drying technologies. The dry powder formulations were inhalable with good aerosol performance, and the siRNA remained physically intact and biologically active after formulation.

17110414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17110414.value: 1. We demonstrated that the pH-responsive LADap(Me)6-L1 peptides can deliver siRNA targeting a highly conserved sequence of the influenza viral gene into mammalian cells and substantially inhibit the production of virus in the transfected cells after pathogen infection. (Liang et al 2015 Molecular Pharmaceutics) 2. Inhalable dry powder formulations of peptide/siRNA complexes can be successfully produced by spray drying without compromising their physical integrity and biological activity. The transfection efficiency of LADap(Me)6-L1 peptide spray-dried powders was retained in the presence of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, making it a promising vector for pulmonary siRNA delivery. (Liang et al 2015 Molecular Pharmaceutics) 3. The in vivo study using LADap peptides system for pulmonary delivery was not satisfactory due to local inflammatory response. As a result, we modified the system to use naked siRNA. We demonstrated that siRNA (at 2% w/w) in its naked form could be formulated into inhalable dry powders using spray drying and spray freeze drying. No inhaled siRNA powder formulation (containing delivery vector) with siRNA load above 2% w/w has been reported in the past. The integrity of siRNA was successfully retained. (Chow et al 2017 International Journal of Pharmaceutics; Liang et al 2018 Asian Journal of Pharmaceutical Science) 4. We explored the effect of pulmonary delivery of siRNA targeting the nucleocapsid protein (NP1496 siRNA) of influenza virus on H1N1 infected mice. The siRNA was administered as a prophylaxis treatment or as a daily treatment. Under the current experiment protocols, the siRNA has no improvements on either the survival rates or the body weight of infected mice, regardless of the dosage regimen. However, there was a reduction in number of plaques was observed on Day 2 post infection in mice treated with NP1496 siRNA. However this reduction was not statistically significant with the other treatment groups. (Chow's PhD thesis)

17110414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17110414.value: The objectives of future study include further increasing the siRNA concentration in the formulation (to reduce powder dose required to achieve therapeutic dose), and evaluating the long-term stability of the dry powder formulations in terms of both the siRNA integrity and the aerosolization performance. The aerosolization performance of the siRNA powders will also be assessed with different inhalers and in different dispersion flow rates. Based on the physical robustness of siRNA demonstrated in the current study, it is also worth to explore the feasibility of spray drying siRNA under even more extreme conditions to allow higher flexibility in particle engineering. The in vivo influenza model for evaluating the efficacy of siRNA needs to be further optimised. With a higher dose of siRNA administered to the animals, it is anticipated that the antiviral effect will be more pronounced.

17110414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17110414.value: In this study, we demonstrated that the pH responsive peptide LADap(Me)6-L1 was able to deliver siRNA targeting the highly conserved sequence of influenza viral gene into mammalian cells and significantly reduced the virus titer. Inhalable dry powder formulations of peptide/siRNA complexes were successfully produced by spray drying and spray freeze drying without compromising their physical integrity and the biological activity was preserved after drying. Overall, inhalable siRNA dry powder formulation with good aerosol performance was developed with a potential for the prophylaxis and treatment of influenza, as well as other respiratory infections.

17111414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111414.value: 人類大約有高達70%的妊娠未能發育至生產，其中30%-75%與胚胎著床有關。早期流產率因隨著胚胎著床延遲而增加。胚胎著床期間，囊胚的滋養外胚層貼附於子宮內膜上皮并繼續分化最終形成胎盤。胚胎著床異常可導致胎兒發育障礙、流產、先兆子癇、滋養細胞增生及分化異常等胎盤相關性疾病。因醫學倫理爭議與實際操作困難，人類胚胎或胎盤組織往往難以獲取以供研究胚胎著床及滋養層分化的分子機制，於是探索妊娠滋養細胞相關性疾病的發病機理也顯得困難重重。因此，構建新型的體外模型用於研究人類胚胎著床過程便尤為重要。 目前廣泛使用的人類胚胎著床體外模型大多採用絨毛膜癌源性的滋養細胞系或從妊娠早期胎盤中分離而來的原代滋養細胞。但是，滋養細胞系為腫瘤細胞，而原代滋養細胞增生能力較弱。近期研究發現，人類胚胎幹細胞培養在含有BMP4 （骨成型蛋白4）但無FGF2（成纖維細胞生長因子2）的小鼠胚胎成纖維細胞條件培養基中可迅速轉變為KRT7+細胞，這些分化后的細胞可表達包括HLA-G在內的多種滋養細胞特異性蛋白，并產生hCG（人絨毛膜促性腺激素）、孕酮、胎盤生長因子及胎盤催乳素等。 經過進一步探索，我們用這些由人類胚胎幹細胞分化而來的滋養細胞形成滋養細胞球（人胚胎替代物），用於胚胎著床的相關研究。我們將人類胚狀體置入相同的分化液中培養，分化出的滋養細胞可形成與胚胎大小類似的滋養細胞球，更有一些滋養細胞球經過2-3天分化后可形成囊胚腔樣的腔體。免疫組織化學染色證實了多種滋養細胞標記物的表達。共培養的相關實驗也證實這些滋養細胞球可粘附於子宮內膜上皮細胞并在分化3日后侵入子宮內膜間質。 我們旨在進一步探索人類胚胎幹細胞分化為滋養細胞的實驗條件，并在體外條件下探索這種滋養細胞是否可以用於研究胚胎滋養層粘附及分化的相關分子機制。我們認為，這將成為研究胚胎著床、滋養細胞侵襲及分化新方法。本研究也將為探索滋養細胞形成和分化對其粘附能力的影響提供新思路，同時，這種體外分化滋養細胞可用於構建新的胚胎著床模型。

17111414.label: Realisation of objectives
17111414.value: Objective 1: Molecular characterization of differentiation protocol for the formation of trophoblastic cells (100% complete) Aim 1 – To compare the expressions of the trophoblastic markers of the various differentiating cells. We studied different differentiating protocol and medium (e.g. MEF/CM with HES/SR or HES/BSA medium) on trophoblastic cell differentiation and different trophoblastic markers were used. It was found that the original BAP medium gave the best differentiation result. This protocol also successfully been used to differentiate another commonly used hESC line, H9 (Yue, PhD Thesis). Aim 2 – Transcriptional profiling of human ES cell-derived trophoblastic cells, choriocarcinoma cell lines, human embryonic trophectoderm and primary human trophoblast. Next generation RNA sequencing was used to generate the transcriptomes of BAP-EB during differentiation. Gene Ontology term and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis indicated Hippo signaling was induced at all time point of BAP-EB differentiation (Lee et al., in preparation). Aim 3 – To study the effect of differentiation medium withdrawal on the formation of trophoblastic cells. We modified the original 96h differentiation protocol and determine which time period is critical for successful trophoblastic cell differentiation. It was found that the first 24 h of BAP treatment was sufficient for BAP-EB formation. Objective 2: Functional characterization of the human ES cell-derived trophoblastic cells (100% completed) Aim 1 – To investigate the attachment potential of the differentiating trophoblastic cells. BAP-EB derived from hESCs (VAL3 and H9) were collected at 24, 48, 72 and 96h, and the attachment rate on receptive and non-receptive endometrial cell lines were studies. It was found that 72h differentiation gave the best attachment potential in receptive endometrial cells (Yue, PhD Thesis). Aim 2 – To study the invasion potential of the trophoblastic cells in vitro. The invasion ability of BAP-EB in 2D/3D culture model was studied using Matrigel-coated transwell assay. Although similar levels of gene expression of trophoblastic markers were found, higher level of trophectoderm marker like CDX2 and ELF5 were confirmed in 3D BAP-EB model. However, no difference of ELF5 methylation status was found between two groups. It was found that BAP-EB invaded through epithelial (Ishikawa) and primary endometrial stromal cells (Lee et al., 2015). Objective 3: Explore the use of human ES cell-derived trophoblastic cells to study the mechanism of trophoblastic differentiation and spheroids attachments (100% completed) Aim 1 – To delineate the changes p63 expression in regulating the differentiation process. Results from recent literature suggested the gap junction molecule Connex 43 (Cx43) plays important role on stem cells interaction and regulate differentiation process. We therefore studied Cx43 and demonstrated that knockdown Cx43 in VAL3 enhanced the attachment rate, hCG secretion and cell invasion of the derived trophoblastic cells (Peng et al., 2019). Aim 2 – To study the changes in the Wnt-signaling pathway during spheroid attachment. RNA-seq results from Objective 1 (aim 2) suggest the YAP and Hippo, but not Wnt-signaling pathway as proposed play important role on trophoblastic cell differentiation. We confirmed this by using YAP inhibitor verteporfin (VP) that suppress differentiation of BAP-EB in vitro (unpublished). Aim 3 – To study the role of autocrine and paracrine signals in the decidual-trophoblast microenvironment. Instead of performing the effect of cytokines on trophoblast cells invasion to human endometrial stromal cells, we studied the attachment rate of BAP-EB on receptive (hCG+7) and pre-receptive (hCG+2) primary endometrial epithelial cells (EECs) isolated from patients, and demonstrated that the BAP-EB could be used as a predictive tool for endometrium receptivity. Results from this part of the study lay the foundation for 2 successful external grant applications (see below).

17111414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111414.value: The pregnancy rate of IVF treatment remains low mainly due to implantation failure. Currently, there is no reliable tool to assess the implantation potential of the endometrium. The molecular, biochemical and biological results obtained in this study suggested that BAP-EB can potentially be used as an embryo surrogate to study early implantation process and predict pregnancy outcome in IVF. The development of predictive model can relieve the burden of both the clinicians and the patients in deciding whether to pursue for IVF treatment. In addition, the ethical constraints by using donated human embryos for studying early human implantation can be minimized.

17111414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111414.value: This study established an optimal protocol to derive trophoblastic cells called BAP-EB from human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). The BAP-EB spheroids (blastocyst surrogates) have gene signature resemble to the outer cells of human embryo. Importantly, BAP-EB selectively attached to receptive endometrial cells but not non-receptive endometrial cells or non-endometrial epithelial cells, suggesting with the patient endometrial biopsy taken at the time of embryo transfer, the BAP-EB could be used to predict pregnancy outcome in subsequent transfer cycle. Further validation with larger number of clinical samples should be performed to evaluate the applicability of the model on pregnancy prediction.
