17111614.label: Realisation of objectives
17111614.value: In this proposal, we have investigated the role of cancer associated fibroblast (CAF)-derived HGF in the regulation of liver T-ICs (Objective 1), to elucidate the molecular mechanisms involved in this process (Objective 2), and evaluate the clinical significance of CAF derived-HGF in human HCC (Objective 3). Objective 1: a) Isolation, Characterization and clinical significance of CAFs in HCC To further understand the functional roles of CAFs in HCC, we isolated CAFs from fresh HCC clinical samples. We minced HCC tissues into small pieces and cultured them in vitro, and the culture medium was replenished once every two days. After 2-3 weeks of incubation, CAFs that had attached to the culture plate would start to grow out; other cell types would become unattached and would be removed through washing. We then characterized and confirmed the 'fibroblast' identity of the CAFs isolated from the HCC specimens. We found that majority of the CAFs that were established displayed positive expression of markers of activated fibroblasts including α-SMA and FAP by flow cytometry analysis. Free of contamination of endothelial cells, HCC cells, and other epithelial cells within the isolated CAF populations was confirmed, as evidenced by ~1% expression of these markers. This result was further confirmed by imunofluorescence (IF) staining. Based on these results, all the CAFs isolated using this method had a fibroblastic phenotype without contamination of other cell types. b) CM from CAFs regulates liver T-ICs and this effect is further promoted by the stimulation of HCC cells To determine whether CAFs play a role in regulating tumorigenicity in HCC, we subcutaneously injected HCC cells derived from PDTX#1 and PDTX#5 into NOD/SCID mice alone or together with their corresponding CAFs at a ratio of 1:1 or 1:3, or with the conditioned medium (CM) of CAFs. Compared to the HCC cells injected alone, all of the groups injected with CAFs or with the CM of CAFs showed a greater tumorigenic potential. We found that HCC cells injected with CAFs or with the CM of CAFs had a similar capacity for enhanced tumorigenicity. These data suggest that CAFs likely perform their regulatory role in cancer mainly through paracrine signaling. Therefore, we collected CM from CAFs for subsequent in vitro experiments to examine the functional role of the CAFs in regulating the properties of liver T-ICs. Upon incubation of CM of CAFs, HCC cells including Bel-7402 and Huh7 showed enhanced liver T-IC properties including self-renewal, tumorigenicity, drug resistance, and expression of liver T-IC markers. To further confirm the role of CAFs in maintaining self-renewal, we used a pluripotent mouse embryonic stem cell line (mESCs). Under feeder-free conditions, mESCs are maintained as a self-renewing and pluripotent population in the presence of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) in the culture medium. Upon LIF withdrawal, mESCs undergo spontaneous differentiation and this effect was reversed in the presence of CM from CAFs. This result further supports the role of CM of CAF in regulation of self-renewal. To examine whether HCC cells educate CAFs to further enhance their potential to regulate liver T-ICs, we incubated CAFs with CM collected from Huh7 cells. We found that the CM of educated CAFs (st-CAFs) had a greater ability to promote the self-renewal of HCC cells when compared to CM from CAFs without education. This result demonstrated that CAFs could promote liver T-IC properties and, in turn, HCC cells also could educate CAFs to further increase their potential. Objective 2: To identify the key secretory protein in CAF CM that mediates the self-renewal-promoting effect on HCC cells, we compared the cytokine profiles of the CM from Huh7 cells, CAFs, and Huh7-stimulated CAFs by cytokine array. We found that HGF was the most potent cytokine in stimulating spheroid formation of HCC cells. Using ELISA assay, we found that both CAFs secreted HGF and that this effect was further enhanced by stimulation with Huh7, confirming the results of the cytokine array profiling. Interestingly, we found that all of the HCC cell lines examined produced no or negligible levels of HGF, while all of the CAFs produced a significant amount of HGF, which suggests that CAFs in the tumor stroma are a major source of HGF. To investigate the functional role of CAF-derived HGF in regulating T-ICs, we evaluated the self-renewal ability of T-ICs in vitro by administering recombinant HGF at a level comparable to that secreted by CAFs (2 ng/ml and 10 ng/ml). At this dosage, we found that HGF resulted in increased c-Met phosphorylation at tyrosine residues 1234 and 1235 in Huh7 and Bel-7402 cells and promoted the spheroid formation ability of both cell lines. In addition, recombinant HGF showed enhanced chemoresistance, invasiveness, tumorigenicity and expression of liver T-IC markers. On the contrary, opposite effects on T-IC properties was observed when HCC cells were treated with HGF-neutralizing antibody (HGF Ab) or the c-Met kinase inhibitor PHA-665752. By cDNA microarray, we identified FOS-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) to be downstream effector of HGF-mediated T-IC function. Furthermore, we found a positive correlation between the expression of HGF and FOSL1 mRNA in HCC clinical samples (R=0.5303, p<0.0001, Pearson correlation). Further analysis showed that HGF induces Erk1/2 phosphorylation and subsequent upregulation of FRA1, which leads to the direct transcriptional activation of FOSL1 in HCC cells to form an auto-feedback loop. To evaluate examine the downstream genes under regulating of FRA1, we have performed the RNA sequencing analysis to compare the profiles between FRA1 knockdown and the vector control cells. By qPCR analysis, we found that HEY1, an important downstream effector in the Notch signaling pathway, was the only gene that was consistently down-regulated in both FRA1 knockdown clones. By ChIP assay, we consistently found binding between FRA1 and the HEY1 promoter in HCC cells. Further functional analysis showed that HEY1 is the downstream effector of FRA1. There is a stepwise increase in the expression of α-SMA, FRA1, T-IC markers, and secretory HGF during fibrosis-dependent hepatocarcinogenesis In conclusion, CAF regulates T-IC plasticity in HCC through cMet/FRA/HEY1 signaling. Objective 3: We have evaluated their clinical significance by analyzing the α-SMA expression in 47 HCC patients using IHC staining. Patients whose tumors had α-SMA over-expression had significantly shorter disease-free survival rates (p=0.04, log-rank test). In HCC clinical samples showing a positive correlation between the mRNA expression of HGF and the CAF marker ACTA2 (in our HCC clinical samples (R=0.7995, p<0.0001, Pearson correlation). Clinically, FRA1 was frequently detected in HCC as compared to non-tumor tissue. High FRA1 expression also correlated with reduced disease-free (p=0.01) and overall survival (p=0.029) (log-rank test). Lastly, we retrospectively analyzed the HEY1 expression in 79 HCC patients by qPCR. Patients whose tumors had high HEY1 expression was associated with microsatellite formation (p=0.044), direct liver invasion (p=0.007) and shorter overall and disease-free survival rates than those with low HEY1 expression (p=0.008 and p=0.028, respectively, log-rank test). Cancer-associated fibroblasts regulate tumor initiating cell plasticity in hepatocellular carcinoma through c-Met/FRA1/HEY1 signaling. Cell Reports 2016; 15:1175-89. All proposed objectives have been achieved. Work for the project was primarily carried out by one PhD student Dr. Eunice Yuen-Ting LAU under the supervision of Dr. Terence Lee (PI).

17111614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111614.value: Like normal stem cells, cancer stem cells (T-ICs) are regulated extrinsically within the tumor micro-environment. Because HCC mostly develops in the context of cirrhosis with an enrichment of activated fibroblasts, we hypothesized that CAFs would regulate liver T-ICs. We found overexpression of α-SMA(+) CAFs was correlated with poor clinical outcome (p=0.04, log-rank test). By functional analysis, we found that CAF regulates liver T-IC via paracrine manner. Conditioned medium (CM) of CAF was found to regulate the function of liver T-ICs including tumorigencity, self-renewal, drug resistance, invasiveness and expression of liver T-IC markers. By cytokine array, HGF was identified to be the crucial secretory factor in CM of CAF, mediating various T-IC functions, which was confirmed by administration of recombinant HGF as well as the neutralizing antibody of HGF and c-MET inhibitor. Mechanistically, CAF-derived HGF regulates liver T-ICs via regulating FRA1 protein through post-translational modification by Erk1/2 phosphorylation upon C-MET phosphorylation. Further functional analysis identified HEY1, a crucial component in Notch signaling pathway, as a novel direct downstream effector of FRA1-mediated T-IC phenotype. Because most HCC cases develop in a severe fibrotic or cirrhotic background that is enriched in activated fibroblasts, it would be interesting to investigate whether HGF-dependent FRA1 activation is associated with fibrosis-dependent HCC development. To evaluate the significance of HGF-mediated FRA1 activation in the regulation of liver T-ICs in fibrosis-dependent hepatocarcinogenesis, we employed a STAMTM non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) HCC mouse model, in which HCC develops from liver with fibrosis. We found that HGF-induced FRA1 activation was accompanied with the increase in liver T-IC markers, which was associated with the fibrosis-dependent development of HCC. In conclusion, this study provides a mechanistic insight of how CAF affects tumor behavior of HCC patients. Most importantly, we have opened a novel therapeutic avenue by targeting the CAF-derived HGF-mediated c-Met/FRA1/HEY1 cascade for the treatment of HCC. The data generated in this proposal has been deposited to a publicly available database: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), NCBI Database Deposit / Contribution - GSE67927 and GSE68005) (2016) – pertaining to profiling data described in the paper referenced in this completion report.

17111614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111614.value: Thus far, the role of cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in cancer remains controversial. In HCC, the role of CAFs is particularly important as HCC mostly develops in the context of cirrhosis with an enrichment of activated fibroblasts. Having said that, the potential role and its underlying mechanism of CAFs in HCC remains unknown. In this study, we found that CAF regulates live T-ICs through secretion of HGF. Upon further analysis, we found that CAF-derived HGC regulates liver T-ICs through c-Met/FRA1/HEY1 cascade. This study provides a better understanding of how liver T-ICs are regulated in the tumor microenvironment and reveal a potential target that could be used for the development of more effective therapeutic strategies in HCC. Recently, the therapeutic role of c-MET inhibitor was being evaluated in various clinical trials. This study provides an insight for this treatment strategy by stratifying patients based on c-Met activation status as well as the abundance of CAFs for personalized medicine in the hope of increasing the efficacy of this treatment. This is a project that continues on the interesting leads identified from the current funded project.

17111614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111614.value: Liver cancer (HCC) is the fifth most common cancer worldwide. More than 80% of HCC cases develop within the context of cirrhosis, which is always accompanied by an enrichment of activated fibroblasts due to chronic inflammation. Despite increasing evidence revealing the supportive function of CAFs in HCC, the molecular mechanism of how these cells affect tumor behavior remains unknown. Recently, cancer stem cells (T-ICs) is regarded as the root of tumor relapse and therapeutic resistance. Thus, targeting these cells may be a novel therapeutic strategy against HCC. In the current proposal, findings presented in this study not only provide evidence to show the clinical relevance of CAFs in HCC but also demonstrated its pivotal role and mechanistic action in regulation of liver T-ICs. Specifically, CAFs, major cellular constituents of stroma, played a crucial role in regulation of liver T-ICs through HGF mediated c-Met/FRA1/HEY1 cascade. Targeting this signaling pathway may be a promising approach for cancer treatment.

17111714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111714.value: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play key roles in innate immune recognition of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) of invading microbes. Among the ten TLR family members identified in humans, TLR10 remains an orphan receptor without known agonist or function. Recent studies have reported genetic polymorphisms of TLR10 in humans in association with diverse diseases, including inflammatory and respiratory diseases, but the mechanisms remain obscure. Lately, we revealed that influenza virus infection increased TLR10 expression and demonstrated novel findings showing an involvement of TLR10 in innate immune sensing of viral infection leading to cytokine and interferon (IFN) induction, suggesting a role of TLR10 as a new innate immune sensor. However, the two key questions regarding this orphan receptor remain unanswered. (1) Ligand for TLR10 sensing during viral infection has not been confirmed and (2) function of TLR10 in host response following viral infection remains unknown. In this study, we aim to identify the ligand, and determine the biological function of this receptor in viral infection. This study will open a new area in innate immunity and provide fundamentally important information in understanding virus-host interactions. 在微生物入侵機體而引起的機體固有免疫反應過程中，Toll樣受體對病原體相關分子模式的識別發揮了重要的作用。在已被鑒別的10個人體Toll樣受體家族成員中，Toll樣受體10仍然是功能、配體都尚不清楚的孤兒受體。最近的研究指出，人體的Toll樣受體10其基因多態性與各種疾病如免疫系統和呼吸系統的疾病相關，但是具體機制仍然不清楚。 近來，我們的研究揭示了流感病毒感染能夠增加Toll樣受體10的表達，同時也首次展現了Toll樣受體10在固有免疫應答中識別病毒並介導細胞因子和干擾素的表達，提出了Toll樣受體10作為固有免疫反應感受器的角色。然而，關於Toll樣受體10仍然有2個關鍵問題有待解決：1，在病毒感染中，Toll樣受體10的配體還不確定，2，病毒感染後宿主所作出的免疫反應中Toll樣受體10的功能仍然未知。在本研究中，我們旨在鑒別Toll樣受體10 的配體，並且確定其在病毒感染中的功能。本研究將為固有免疫開闢一個新的領域，並且在理解病毒與宿主的相互作用方面提供重要的信息。

17111714.label: Realisation of objectives
17111714.value: Achievements in Objective 1: We provided different lines of evidences and successfully identified that dsRNA is the ligand of TLR10. We also demonstrated that TLR10 is predominantly localized and binds dsRNA intracellularly in endosomes. Sub-cellular localization of TLR10: Confocal microscopy was used to define the sub-cellular localization of TLR10. TLR10 was detected on cell surface but was expressed more abundant intracellularly. Markers of intracellular organelles were used to investigate co-localization of TLR10 in different cellular compartments. TLR10 was predominately expressed in endosomes, with the highest expression detected in RAB11A+ recycling endosomes and RAB5+ early endosomes. TLR10 can also be found in endoplasmic reticulum and RAB7+ late endosomes and low expression in Golgi apparatus. dsRNA is a ligand for TLR10 sensing and signaling: High TLR10 expression in early endosomes of resting cells suggested that TLR10 might be a nucleic acid sensing receptor (Itoh et al., 2011 PLoS One, 6(12), e28500; Qi et al. 2012 J Biol Chem, 287(39), 32617-29). To study TLR10-specific biological function, we generated TLR10 overexpressed (OE) and knock-down (KD) cells and compared that with the wildtype (WT) THP-1 cells. Viral RNA isolated from influenza A viruses or the dsRNA analog, poly(I:C) was used to stimulate these three types of cells both at cell surface or transfected intracellularly. Relative to induction of interferon (IFN)-b in WT cells, a significantly higher level of induction occurred in TLR10 KD cells while overexpression of TLR10 reduced IFN response upon intracellular stimulation. Both influenza viral RNAs and dsRNA analog exert a similar effect in IFN expression, and thus dsRNA analog was used to mimic viral products generated during infection for subsequent experiments. In contrast to transfected RNAs, naked RNAs induced only very weak IFNb expression in WT cells and TLR10 OE or KD cells showed no difference relative to WT cells. Binding of dsRNA to TLR10 requires acidic pH: TLR10 was readily pulled down in vitro using biotinylated dsRNA as bait at pH 5.5. Addition of unlabeled dsRNA markedly decreased amount of TLR10 pulled-down, suggesting that TLR10 specifically bound dsRNA. At pH 7.4, physiological pH and of cell culture and cell surface, TLR10 pull-down was not detectable. This is consistent with hypothesis that binding of dsRNA to TLR10 occurring in acidic compartments such as the endosomes and not at cell surface. Intracellular interactions between TLR10 and dsRNA confirmed by fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay: To determine if TLR10 and dsRNA are sufficiently close for molecular interaction to occur, a FRET assay was performed. An increased intensity of FITC fluorescence was observed after photobleaching of rhodamine-labelled dsRNA (FRET efficiency = 50.4% ± 12.7%), indicating close proximity of TLR10 and dsRNA and further supporting that there is a direct binding of dsRNA to TLR10 in endosomes. Achievements in Objective 2: We suggested for the first time that TLR10 is a novel nucleotide sensing receptor. Recognition of dsRNA by TLR10 activates recruitment of MyD88 for signal transduction and suppression of IRF7 dependent type I IFN production. Pathway analysis demonstrated that TLR10 regulates key molecules in multiple signaling mechanisms, including inflammasome, IFN and TLR pathways. We originally planned to generate TLR10 knock-out (KO) cells using CRISPR technology. Cells were transfected with 2 plasmids encoding Cas9 protein and expressing sgRNA targeting either the 3’ or 5’ end of TLR10 exon. Transfected cells were selected with puromycin and clonal lines obtained by limiting dilution. 2 of 36 resistant clones were found promising initially by Western Blotting. Cells were expanded and genomic DNA underwent PCR with TLR10 primers, and sent for sequencing. One clone was found to have a non-sense mutation, and the other with a 3.2kb major deletion in exon. These clones were further expanded but they are either found to be positive for TLR10 by both Western blotting in later passage or were not be able to grow and died. The procedures have been repeated for at least 3 times but similar phenomenon observed and we are unable to obtain clone of TLR10 KO cells. Therefore TLR10 KD and/or OE cells were employed in subsequent experiments. MyD88 is recruited to TLR10 upon dsRNA stimulation: On transfection with RNAs, co-localization of MyD88 with TLR10 was observed as early as 5 min post stimulation. Recruitment of MyD88 by TLR10 upon viral RNA or dsRNA stimulation was further confirmed by immunoprecipitation, and MyD88 can also be pulled down by TLR10 in the co-ip experiments. TLR10 regulates dsRNA-mediated IFN responses via IRF7: IRF phosphorylation was examined following transfection of dsRNA into WT and TLR10 OE cells. Phosphorylation of IRF7 stably increased in response to dsRNA challenge in WT cells, while it was markedly reduced in OE cells. Expression of soluble luciferase in reporter THP-1 cells under the control of IRF-inducible promoter allows quantification of induction of IFN responses through detecting the level of luciferase activity. TLR10 siRNAs were introduced to reporter cells to compare luciferase activities with non-targeting control siRNA transfected cells, in response to dsRNA stimulation. A significant increase in luciferase activity was seen in TLR10 siRNA transfected reporter cells vs control siRNA transfected cells, indicating that IRF dependent IFN response would be augmented in TLR10 deficient environment upon dsRNA stimulation. Regulatory role of TLR10 in inflammasome: Pathway analysis revealed that TLR10 is involved in regulation of inflammasome pathway. Expression of IL-1b and EIF2AK2, also known as PKR in the inflammasome mechanism was induced in WT cells in response to dsRNA stimulation. Such inductions were significantly suppressed and upregulated in TLR10 OE and KD cells respectively. It is known that maturation of IL-1b is promoted from activation of inflammasomes, while pattern recognition receptors could act as inflammasome sensors. Whilst PKR broadly affects inflammasome activation via physical interaction with multiple inflammasome components, it is worth noting that PKR, as an IFN-induced dsRNA-dependent protein kinase, its induction is correlated to the expression of IFN. Therefore, whether expression of PKR and IFN are both regulated by TLR10 would deserve investigation. TLR10 regulates IFN signaling via TLR3 expression: Array data also revealed that IFN and TLR signaling are regulated by TLR10. Expression of IFNb was significantly upregulated (>100 folds) in WT cells upon dsRNA stimulation. Its expression significantly suppressed and upregulated in OE and KD cells respectively. Whilst, a significant induction of TLR3 (>10 folds) was observed in WT cells in response to stimulation at 6h post challenge, there was no significant differential expression at 1h and 3h post challenge time. TLR3 induction was markedly reduced in OE cells at 6h post challenge. Data was confirmed by qPCR. A panel of other TLR members (TLR 1-9) was also included for comparison. Expression of TLR1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9 did not altered to stimulation and were not affected by OE or KD of TLR10. Although array data, did not show up TLR7 and 8, qPCR data demonstrated that expression of TLR7 and 8 was marginally increased (> 1.5 folds) in WT cells, whilst no significantly altered in their expression with TLR10 OE or KD. TLR3 is a key pattern recognition receptor in response to dsRNA stimulation. Upon ligand recognition, TLR3 induces IRF3 activation and downstream type I IFN production. Data here suggested that TLR10 regulates TLR3 expression and may modulate TLR3 signaling and its downstream IFN production proposing possible crosstalk between TLR10 and TLR3 in regulation of IFN signaling.

17111714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111714.value: In this study, we demonstrated for the first time that TLR10 - a TLR member, though has been identified since 2001, remained as an orphan receptor in the family, without well-established ligands and functions identified so far - is a novel nucleotide sensing receptor. We provided different lines of evidences to demonstrate that dsRNA is in fact a true ligand for TLR10 sensing and signaling, and thereby identifying a previously unrecognized role of TLR10 in regulating IFN signaling. To date, only nucleic acid sensing TLRs have been reported to be located in early or late endosomes in resting cells. The expression and localization of TLR10 in RAB5+ early and RAB7+ late endosomes of resting cells in concordance with the nucleic acid sensing nature of TLR10. Co-localization study of the spatial association of TLR10 with dsRNA showed that, after ligand transfection, fluorophore-labelled dsRNA co-localized with TLR10 in endosomes. We also revealed that TLR10 physically binds dsRNA, such binding is favorable at a pH condition similar to that within endosomes. The intracellular interaction between TLR10 and dsRNA was further confirmed by FRET assay. We also worked out a novel signaling pathway of TLR10. We showed that recognition of dsRNA by TLR10 activates recruitment of MyD88 for signal transduction and suppression of IRF-7 dependent type I IFN production. Result from pathway analysis also revealed that TLR10 regulates inflammasome, IFN and other TLR signalings, provides mechanistic insight explaining the role of TLR10 in regulating host innate immune mechanism. The discovery of ligand for TLR10 is a major step in the understanding of the biological function of this hitherto orphan receptor. In addition, this study also provides important information in the understanding of TLR10 signaling and function. Modulation of TLR10 signaling may provide a unique option to fine-tune fundamental physiological pathways involved in pathological conditions such as infectious diseases, autoimmune diseases and cancers. Data arising from this study are ready for submission and manuscript is now in preparation to submit to scientific journal eLife.

17111714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111714.value: Involvement of TLR10 in cytokine response could be largely dependent on TLR10 signaling solely or in combination with one or more signaling of other pattern recognition receptors, especially in the scenario of pathogen infections, microbial components could be pathogen associated molecular patterns to trigger a diverse array of pattern recognition receptors, thus the complicated crosstalk between TLR10 and other pattern recognition receptors would be an important area for future study. Here, we have identified the ligand of TLR10, such discovery is a major step in understanding of the biological function of this receptor. As there are increasing evidences suggesting the involvement of TLR10 in different disease pathogenesis, our study here revealed dsRNA is ligand of TLR10, proposed its signaling and novel functions of TLR10 in regulating IFN signaling would bring indispensable importance to further investigate the role of TLR10 in different diseases. Furthermore, it will also be important to apply our in vitro data to test in vivo. As TLR10 is a pseudo-gene in mice, using a human TLR10 knockin mouse model to investigate the biological relevance of this receptor in disease pathogenesis will be our next step to go.

17111714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111714.value: Toll-like receptor (TLR)-10 remains an orphan receptor without well characterized ligands or functions. Here we reveal that TLR10 is predominantly localized to endosomes and binds dsRNA in vitro at endosomal pH, suggesting that dsRNA is a ligand of TLR10. Recognition of dsRNA by TLR10 activates recruitment of myeloid differentiation primary response gene 88 (MyD88) for signal transduction and suppression of interferon regulatory factor (IRF)-7 dependent type I IFN production. Pathway analysis further revealed that TLR10 involves in the regulation of inflammasome mechanism and expression of other TLRs which may modulate IFN response. Our results suggest for the first time that TLR10 is a novel nucleotide sensing receptor and proposing a potential crosstalk between TLR10 and TLR3 in the regulation of IFN signaling. As there are increasing evidences suggesting the involvement of TLR10 in different disease pathogenesis, this study brings indispensable importance, not only to the understanding in basic immunobiology of this receptor but also have great significance in further investigation on the role and functional relevance of TLR10 in different diseases.

17111814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111814.value: Penicillium marneffei infection is a form of endemic mycosis indigenous to Southeast Asia. Majority of the cases occur in patients with acquired immunodeficiency disorder (AIDS), and less commonly in individuals with secondary immunodeficiencies. Remarkably, some patients suffering from pencilliosis but without HIV infection or apparent immunodeficiency are reported, but why they are susceptible to P. marneffei is uncertain. Host defense mechanisms against this fatal opportunistic infection are not well understood, and such knowledge is important in identifying immunologic factors that influence the susceptibility to penicilliosis, which will guide the investigations of affected individuals for underlying immunodeficiencies. We previously investigated 4 HIV-negative children with penicilliosis and concomitant chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. One patient had hyper-IgE syndrome caused by STAT3 defect, while 3 patients had gain-of-phosphorylation STAT1 mutations. The hallmark of both hyper-IgE syndrome and gain-of-phosphorylation STAT1 disorder is defective Th17 response towards fungal pathogens, thus suggesting the importance of Th17 immunity against P. marneffei. To date, mechanisms involved in generating Th17 immunity towards P. marneffei have not been studied. Inflammasomes are a group of multimeric protein complexes which sense and respond to a diverse range of pathogens and endogenous danger signals. Inflammasome activation triggers proteolysis of caspase-1, leading to maturation and secretion of IL1-beta and IL18. Recent data suggested an essential role of NLRP3 inflammasome in host defense against Candida albicans by driving protective Th1 and Th17 cellular response. In the present study, we intend to test the hypothesis that NLRP3 inflammasome activation is important in mediating innate and protective Th1/Th17 cellular response to P. marneffei. Specific aims are: 1. To characterize the pro-inflammatory and T-helper cytokine response towards P. marneffei conidia and yeast in human macrophages and dendritic cells. 2. To demonstrate that IL1-beta and IL18 response is dependent on NLRP3 and caspase-1 activation. 3. To identify the pattern recognition receptors which lead to caspase-1 activation, and the involvement of Syk kinase signaling pathway in the induction of IL1-beta response. 4. To evaluate the importance of NLRP3 and caspase-1 in the induction of Th1 and Th17 adaptive immune response towards P. marneffei by means of in vivo infection model using wild-type and NLRP3- and caspase-1 knockout mice. This study is expected to significantly enhance our understanding of host defense mechanisms against P. marneffei. The resulting knowledge can assist clinicians in formulating a diagnostic approach to investigate genetic immune defects in patients with penicilliosis, and improve the treatment outcome for this fatal infection. 馬爾尼菲青霉菌感染是東南亞獨有的地方性真菌病。此病是一種 機會感染性的傳染病，主要發生於感染愛滋病（HIV）病毒或繼 發性免疫缺陷病的患者。馬爾尼菲青霉菌具高致命性，並因環球 人口流動的增長，馬爾尼菲青霉病已突破地方病的區域界限向非 疫區擴散，成為威脅世界多國的傳染病。需流意的是有部分患者 並沒有HIV病毒感染或其他繼發性免疫缺陷，醫學界對這些人士 患上馬爾尼菲青霉病的原因還未完全了解。人類抵禦馬爾尼菲青 霉菌的免疫機制所知甚少，而現時亦未有方針指引應如何對特發 性馬爾尼菲青霉病的患者進行相關的免疫學檢查以找出隱藏的免 疫缺陷。 本研究團隊較早前對四位感染馬爾尼菲青霉菌伴慢性黏膜皮膚念 珠菌病的兒童進行詳細的免疫分析，發現他們都患有原發性免疫 缺陷病。其中一位患有高免疫球蛋白E病，並找到STAT3基因變 異。另外三位病童則找到STAT1基因變異，令STAT1蛋白磷酸化 功能亢進。這兩種原發性免疫缺陷病的相同之處是導致抗真菌感 染的Th17免疫應答嚴重缺乏，反映出Th17於對抗馬爾尼菲青霉菌 的重要性。但是，至今並未有研究闡述馬爾尼菲青霉菌啟動Th17 免疫應答的機制。 炎性小體是細胞內的一組多蛋白复合体，是宿主先天免疫系统的 重要部分。炎性小體能感應外界的危險訊號，激活半胱天冬酶-1 (caspase-1)，令白介素-1β 和白介素-18 等促炎性因子得以成熟並 於細胞內釋放出來。研究指出NLRP3炎性小體能誘導Th1及Th17 免疫應答，於對抗念珠菌有重要的保護作用。本計劃旨於研究 NLRP3炎性小體對馬爾尼菲青霉菌的鑒別及免疫應答的作用。本 研究將界定人類巨噬細胞對馬爾尼菲青霉菌孢子和酵母細胞的炎 性因子反應，及展示由馬爾尼菲青霉菌所激發的IL-1β是基於 NLRP3及caspase-1的活化而產生。本研究並將介定馬爾尼菲青霉 菌的模式識別受體 (pattern recognition receptor) 及其相關的信號通 路，尤其是Syk kinase對激活NLRP3炎性小體及IL-1β的作用。最 後，本研究將以活體馬爾尼菲青霉菌血行感染模型，比較野生型 、NLRP3及caspase-1基因剔除小鼠對馬爾尼菲青霉菌所產生的 Th1和Th17的免疫反應、病灶之形成和死亡率，從而證明NLRP3 炎性小體在宿主對抗馬爾尼菲青霉菌的重要性。 本研究計劃對了解抗衡馬爾尼菲青霉菌的免疫機制提供新的理論 依據。研究結果將有助醫療人員對特發性馬爾尼菲青霉病的患者 進行更全面的免疫功能檢測，或能帶來更有效的治療以提高治癒 率。

17111814.label: Realisation of objectives
17111814.value: Objective 1 To examine the different IL-1beta responses to Talaromyces marneffei (TM) yeast and conidia, freshly isolated human PBMCs were co-cultured with live TM yeasts or conidia for varied incubation time at 0.5 MOI. TM yeasts induced a high level of IL-1beta production as early as 8 hr post infection, and it almost peaked at 18 hr and remained steady thereafter till day 5 post infection. TNF-alpha production was detectable earlier at 4 hr post infection, and similarly peaked at 18 hr but showed a slight falling trend up to day 5 post infection. In contrast, IL-1beta was undetectable even on day 5 after infection with TM conidia, whereas TNF-alpha production increased dramatically after 2 days of infection. The lack of IL-1beta response to TM conidia was not altered by treatment with heat or paraformaldehyde . In contrast, both yeast and pseudohyphal forms of C. albicans were capable of inducing IL-1beta production in human PBMCs, and similarly, heat or paraformaldehyde treatment had no effect on IL-1beta response elicited by C. albicans. Since IFN-gamma and IL-17A are important in the host defense against fungal infection, we sought to examine the induction of Th1 and Th17 immune responses by TM yeast. Human PBMCs were co-cultured with TM yeasts for 18 hr, 3 days and 5 days respectively. We found that both IFN-gamma and IL-17A were detectable in culture supernatant on day 3 and day 5 post infection. Meanwhile, high levels of IL-6, MCP-1, IL-8 could be detectable, while IL-18 and IL-10 production was minimal, and IFN-gamma was absent throughout the 5 days of co-culture. Objective 2 To study the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome by TM yeasts, we evaluated NLRP3 expression, ASC oligomerization (“speck” formation) and caspase-1 activity in monocytes co-cultured TM yeasts. Immunoblotting showed that NLRP3 protein was markedly upregulated by TM yeasts compared to unstimulated groups. Moreover, TM by itself induced very few ASC specks, while LPS priming significantly enhanced the assembly of ASC specks induced by TM yeasts. Paralleling the observation from ASC speck assembly, TM yeast induced active caspase-1 in pyroptotic monocytes but was significantly enhanced by LPS priming. To further verify our hypothesis that IL-1beta response to TM yeasts was dependent on caspase-1 activation, we pre-treated monocytes with caspase-1 inhibitor prior to co-culture with TM. IL-1beta production was almost completely abolished in Z-YVAD-treated groups, whereas it had no obvious effect on TNF-alpha production. It is known that NLRP3 inflammasome activation is dependent K+ efflux. We sought to study the effect of K+ efflux inhibition on NLRP3 inflammasome activation by TM yeasts. Monocytes pre-treated with KCl (40mM) to block K+ efflux had impaired IL-1beta release in response to TM yeasts, while IL-1beta response to LPS was unaffected. Furthermore, K+ efflux blockade had no effect on TNF-alpha production in monocytes co-cultured with TM yeasts. These findings indicated that IL-1beta response to TM yeasts was dependent on NLRP3 inflammasome and caspase-1 activation in human monocytes. Objective 3 To elucidate the involvement of PRRs for IL-1beta response to TM yeasts, human monocytes were stimulated with heat-killed TM yeasts in the presence or absence of specific blocking antibodies to TLR2 and dectin-1. Dectin-1 blockade resulted in a marked reduction of IL-1beta and TNF-alpha production. However, TLR2 blockade had no effect on IL-1beta and TNF-alpha production in monocytes. The reduction of IL-1beta production in monocytes after dectin-1 blockade suggested that dectin-1 binding and its downstream signaling is important for triggering IL-1beta response towards TM. To study the role of Dectin-1/Syk pathway in the induction of IL-1beta response to TM, we analyzed Syk phosphorylation and IL-1beta production in the presence or absence of Syk inhibitor (R406) in monocytes co-cultured with TM yeasts. As expected, TM yeasts induced higher level of syk phosphorylation compared to unstimulated groups. Furthermore, syk inhibition by R406 blocked the production of intracellular pro-IL-1beta and mature IL-1beta as well as TNF-alpha, in response to TM yeasts in a dose-dependent manner. These data indicate that dectin-1/syk signaling pathway plays a critical role in initiating IL-1beta response to TM. Objective 4 To investigate the role of inflammasome in the activation of Th17 immune response against TM yeasts, human PBMCs were co-cultured with TM yeasts for 5 days in the presence of caspase-1 inhibitor Z-YVAD. Blocking of caspase-1 activation substantially dampened IL-17A release in response to TM yeasts. Next, we determined the percentage of IFN-gamma and IL-17A producing CD4+ T-cells upon co-culture TM yeasts with monocytes in the presence of Z-YVAD. Z-YVAD treatment significantly reduced the percentage of IL-17A producing T cells, whereas it could not affect intracellular IFN-gamma production on day 7 after fungal stimulation. Our data suggest that the inflammasome activation promotes T. marneffei yeasts-induced Th17 rather than Th1 immune response. We further investigated the induction of IL-1beta response to T. marneffei yeasts in NLRP3 knockout (KO) and caspase-1 KO mice. Murine bone marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) from WT, Nlrp3 KO, and Caspase-1 KO C57BL/6 mice were stimulated with heat-killed TM yeasts (1 MOI), LPS (100ng/ml), LPS plus TM yeasts for 18hrs, or LPS plus nigericin as a positive control. IL-1beta production was significantly lower in BMDCs from Nlrp3 KO and caspase-1 KO mice, with the lowest seen in Nlrp3 KO mice. The same pattern was seen in BMDCs stimulated with LPS and nigericin, the canonical activation of NLRP3 inflammasome. By confocal microscopy, we showed that ASC speck formation was absent in TM-infected BMDCs from Nlrp3 KO and Caspase-1 KO mice. Splenocytes isolated from Nlrp3 KO and caspase-1 KO mice showed significantly impaired IFN-gamma production. Upon co-culture with TM yeasts up to 6 days, IFN-gamma production in splenocytes became evident as early as 18 hours from WT mice and peaked on day 4. The profile of IFN-gamma production in splenocytes from Nlrp3 KO and Caspase-1 KO mice closely paralleled with one another; both were evident only on day 3, and peaked on day 5, and remained significantly lower than splenocytes from WT mice. IL-17 production from splenocytes from WT mice began to rise on day 2, peaked on day 4 and levelled off thereafter. IL-17 production from TM-infected splenocytes from Nrlp3 KO and Caspase-1 KO mice began to rise on day 3 and continued to show a rising trend, albeit at a significantly lower level then WT splenocytes up to day 6. Finally, we asked the question whether NLRP3 inflammasome activation confers protective immune defense against TM. WT, Nlrp3 KO and Caspase-1 KO mice (n=9 for each strain) were infected with live TM yeasts (5x10^5 CFU) by intravenous injection, and the mice were monitored for body weight changes and survival. Nlrp3 KO, but not Caspase-1 KO mice, showed significantly weight loss starting from day 15 post-infection, and all died by day 23. Interestingly, the body weight changes and survival of Caspase-1 KO mice were comparable with WT mice. These results suggested that other caspases, in addition to caspase-1 downstream to NLRP3 inflammasome activation might be crucial in protective immune response against T. marneffei. Further investigations will provide more insights to the mechanistic pathway by which NLRP3 inflammasome eliminates and protects the host from TM.

17111814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111814.value: Our results showed that the yeast, but not conidia, form of T. marneffei potently induced IL-1beta production in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). TM yeasts stimulated NLRP3 expression, caspase-1 activation and ASC speck formation in human monocytes infected wtih TM. IL-1beta response is dependent on caspase-1 activation, as caspase-1 inhibitor (Z-YVAD) attenuated IL-1beta production in TM-infected monocytes. LPS priming was required for IL-1beta response to T.marneffei yeasts in monocyte-derived macrophages and dendritic cells, whereas LPS priming was dispensable for IL-1beta production in PBMCs and monocytes. We further investigated the signaling pathway of IL-1beta response in human monocytes. T. marneffei yeasts induced IL-1beta response via dectin-1/syk pathway as the first signal of inflammasome activation, and LPS priming remarkably promoted ASC speck assembly and caspase-1 activation. Syk inhibition resulted in marked reduction of IL-1beta and TNF-alpha response in monocytes infected wtih TM. The activation of inflammasome by T. marneffei yeasts initiated Th1 and Th17 immune response, and caspase-1 blockade impaired the Th17 cell differentiation. Finally, by using Nlrp3 KO and caspase-1 KO mice, we showed that deficiency of NLRP3 or caspase-1 compromised IFN-gamma and IL-17 production in splenocytes infected with TM. Impaired survival was observed in Nlrp3 KO mice, suggesting that Th1 and Th17 immune response mediated by NLRP3 confers protective immunity against TM. To our knowledge, this is the first study investigating the role of inflammasome in innate immunity against TM, and the mechanism by which T. marneffei induces NLRP3 inflammasome activation and Th17 immune response.

17111814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111814.value: Findings of this study advanced our understanding of host defense mechanisms against T. marneffei. While majority of patients suffering from disseminated T. marneffei infection are HIV-positive, those who are HIV-negative and without secondary immunodeficiencies could have undiagnosed primary immunodeficiencies and the etiology is yet to be unravelled. Our findings point to the crucial role of NLRP3-mediated innate immunity in bridging to adaptive Th1 and Th17 response, and evaluation of this signaling pathway should be incorporated into a diagnostics pipeline to investigate genetic immune defects in patients with talaromycosis. The study of cellular response towards T. marneffei may provide breakthroughs for the discovery of genetic immune defects in patients with talaromycosis which is not otherwise explained. To further address this, we have initiated collaborations with infectious disease physicians in Northen Thailand, where T. marneffei is highly endemic, to discover cellular defects and genetic lesions in HIV-negative children suffering from talaromycosis. Our findings also led to the question that whether patients receiving IL-1 blockade could have increased susceptibility to talaromycosis, which is a potential hazard for patients in Southeast Asia. Using the existing murine models, we will test effect of IL1-receptor blockade (by canakinumab) and anti-IL1 (anakinra) on susceptibility to T. marneffei in vivo.

17111814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111814.value: Penicillium marneffei is a pathogenic fungus endemic in Southeast Asia. It is the third most common systemic opportunistic infection in AIDS, ranking just after Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia and tuberculosis. The susceptibility to penicilliosis in HIV-infected individuals highlights the importance of T-cell immune response against T. marneffei. However, little is known about the induction of adaptive immune response and the functional importance of various T-cell subsets contributing to its clearance. Our results showed that T. marneffei potently induced IL-1beta production in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells in a caspase-1 dependent manner. IL-1beta response was mediated via dectin-1/syk pathway as the first signal of inflammasome activation, and LPS priming remarkably promoted ASC speck assembly and caspase-1 activation. The activation of inflammasome by T. marneffei yeasts initiated Th1 and Th17 immune response which was dependent on caspase-1. Survival of Nlrp3 KO mice, in which Th1 and Th17 immunity were impaired, was significantly lower compared with wild-type mice. Our studies demonstrate for the first time the mechanism by which T. marneffei induces NLRP3 inflammasome activation and Th17 immune response. Our findings led to the understanding of the importance of NLRP3 inflammasome that bridges innate and adaptive Th1 and Th17 immunity, hence protection against P. marneffei.

17112014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112014.value: Recently, our laboratory has provided evidences that secretin (SCT) is a novel element in the osmoregulatory pathway. SCT functions at multiple levels to directly stimulate water intake in the central nervous system, and it is released from the posterior pituitary into circulation under osmotic stress to stimulate water reabsorption in the kidney. It is interesting to note first of all that SCT and its receptor (SCTR) are colocalized with a key osmo-sensitive transactivator, nuclear factor of activated T-cells 5 (NFAT5), in the osmoregulatory centers in the brain and the kidney, and also that SCT and SCTR genes are activated upon hyperosmolality. However, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying the induction of SCT and SCTR gene expression in response to changes in plasma osmolality have not yet been clarified. Detailed DNA sequence analysis of the promoter regions of SCT and SCTR genes reveals the presence of multiple NFAT5 binding sites, we therefore hypothesize that NFAT5 is responsible for modulating SCT and SCTR expression in different osmotic environments. In our preliminary studies, consistent with this hypothesis, we found that hypertonic treatment stimulates the promoter activities of both SCT and SCTR in a mouse collecting duct cell, M1. Overexpression and silencing of NFAT5 further confirm that NFAT5 is responsible for the up-regulation of SCTR gene under hypertonic condition. In in vivo situation, osmotic stress upregulates both SCT and SCTR genes in kidney cortex and medulla of wild-type mice, but not in NFAT5+/- animals. The first two objectives of the present study aims to confirm the role of NFAT5 in modulating SCT and SCTR gene expression upon changes in plasma osmolality. In kidney, NFAT5 is a key factor in cell protection under high extracellular osmolality created for water reabsorption. Our preliminary data indicate that the SCT/SCTR axis is potentially involved in this protective mechanism. In fact, we have previously shown that SCTR knock-out mice exhibit higher kidney/body weight ratio with morphological abnormalities in renal cortex and medulla. The third objective of this study is to investigate the functions of SCT/SCTR in the protective mechanisms against extracellular hypertonicity. In summary, the proposed study should provide comprehensive information on how NFAT5 regulate SCT/SCTR expression under different osmotic environment and interrelationship between SCT and NFAT5 in the osmoprotective mechanisms in the kidney. 近期，我們證明了胰泌素（SCT）是滲透調節通路裡面的一個新的因數。在中樞神經系統中，胰泌素從多個層次刺激水分吸收。在滲透脅迫的條件下，胰泌素從垂體後葉釋放到循環系統裡，進一步促進腎臟的水分重吸收。我們發現，在腎臟和大腦的滲透調節中心，胰泌素和胰泌素受體（SCTR）共同被一個名為，活化T細胞核因子5（NFAT5）的轉錄啟動因數調節。NFAT5是一個對滲透壓敏感的轉錄啟動因數。但是，血漿滲透壓的變化對胰泌素和胰泌素受體的轉錄啟動的具體機理還沒有被研究。根據基因測序，在胰泌素和胰泌素受體的啟動子位點中，有多個NFAT5結合位點。因此，我們推斷，在滲透壓變化的情況下，NFAT5可以調控胰泌素和胰泌素受體的表達。我們的初步研究也符合這個推論。在小鼠的腎集合管細胞M1中，高離子濃度處理能啟動胰泌素和胰泌素受體的轉錄活性。對NFAT5的過量表達和基因靜默的研究亦證實了NFAT5是高離子濃度能增加胰泌素受體的表達的重要一環。在活體條件下，滲透脅迫能增加小鼠的腎皮質和腎髓質中胰泌素和胰泌素受體的轉錄。但是在NFAT5+/-的小鼠體內無法觀察到此現象。此研究的前兩個目的就是確認，在血漿滲透壓變化時，NFAT5如何對胰泌素和胰泌素受體表達的調節作用。在腎臟中，為了促進水分重吸收而提高細胞外滲透壓時，NFAT5在細胞保護過程中起到關鍵的作用。我們的初步研究指出，在這個細胞保護過程中，胰泌素/胰泌素受體軸起了潛在作用。事實上，我們已經證明了胰泌素受體基因敲除鼠表現出更高的腎臟/體重比例，以及形態上不正常的腎皮質和腎髓質。因此,本研究的第三個目的就是研究在細胞外高離子濃度的條件下，胰泌素和胰泌素受體在細胞保護過程所起的作用。總的來說，本研究能夠對不同滲透壓條件下NFAT5對胰泌素和胰泌素受體表達的調節，和胰泌素與NFAT5在細胞滲透保護機制中的相互作用提供全面的資訊。

17112014.label: Realisation of objectives
17112014.value: Objective 1: NFAT5 is an osmo-indicible transactivator regulating osmotic tolerance genes which mostly contain at least one osmotic response element (ORE) consensus. Previously our laboratory have found potential ORE sequences in the 5’ flanking region of SCT and SCTR gene and a change in the sensitivity of different regions of kidney to hyperosmolality as reflected in NFAT5, SCT and SCTR gene expression. Hereby we hypothesized that NFAT5 modulates SCT/SCTR expression when body cells under osmotic stress. We first proved that both NFAT5 and SCTR expression were significantly increased after mouse M1 and mIMCD3 cells treated with graded concentration of NaCl. Moreover, the endogenous cAMP responses to SCT were much stronger in the hypertonic condition. These data clearly showed hypertonicity can up-regulate both SCTR and NFAT5 expression in kidney collecting duct cells. By in silico analysis, six potential OREs were identified in the 5’flanking region of SCTR gene. We used several 5’ and 3’ deletion constructs with luciferase as reporter genes for transient transfection into M1 and mIMCD3 cells to locate the responsible regulating regions for SCTR expression in kidney collecting duct cells. In both cell lines, constructs with promoter fragments -867/-228, -665/-228, -556/-228 and -367/-288 were found to have a higher luciferase activities than the others. In contrast, the constructs containing sequences between the TSS and the start codon (-288 to +1) displayed lower promoter activities. These demonstrated that the core promoter region of SCTR is located at a position ranging from -367 to -228. Of note, only this region was able to respond to hypertonic stimulation, which further indicated that the OREs located within this region is related to the up-regulation of SCTR expression during osmotic stress. We further explored the functional relationship amongst NFAT5, SCTR and hypertonicity by performing NFAT5 overexpression and siRNA silencing studies. Under isotonic conditions, NFAT5 dose-dependently reduced SCTR promoter activity in M1 cells. In hypertonic medium, overexpression of NFAT5 significantly increased SCTR promoter activities in both cell lines. These results indicated that SCTR exerts different degrees of basal expression regulation in M1 and mIMCD3 cells. Next, the treatment of NFAT5 siRNA significantly reduced NFAT5 transcript level in both M1 and mICMD3 cells compared with control siRNA. Additionally, transfection of siNFAT5 lowered NFAT5 protein level in both cell lines but not in siRNA control. Co-transfecting NFAT5 siRNA with the SCTR promoter construct abolished hypertonicity-stimulated SCTR promoter activities. Taken together, these data strongly suggested NFAT5 is the key mediator in hypertonic-induced expression of SCTR in kidney cells. Nevertheless, positive signals were found in samples with primers specifically amplified the -367/-228 region treated with NFAT5 antibody, indicating the binding of NFAT5 with mouse SCTR promoter. Meanwhile, increased tonicity also prompted NFAT5 binding to promoter region. Moreoever we found the position of -268 reduced the basal promoter activities and significant repression to the hypertonic-induced promoter activity, indicating that this position is a functional motif mediating hypertonic-induced SCTR gene expression. Objective 2: We identified that both NFAT5 and SCTR proteins were localized in the kidney cortex and medulla regions by immunohistochemistry staining, suggesting that they are highly co-expressed in majority of tubules. Next we found that NFAT5, SCT and SCTR gene expression in kidney cortex and medulla regions were all up-regulated in WT mice after acute and chronic salt loadings while the increase of NFAT5 and SCTR transcript levels in medulla were much lower than those in cortex. Noteworthy, the up-regulation of NFAT5 and SCTR were more pronounced in medulla after chronic hypertonic treatment. However, all these effects were absent in NFAT5+/- mice, with NFAT5 and SCTR expression levels undergoing no significant changes following either acute or chronic salt loading. Our data therefore suggested a change in the sensitivity of different regions of the kidney to hyperosmolality, as reflected in the differences in the expression of NFAT5 and SCTR gene. Objective 3: Previously our laboratory have found that SCTR-/- mice exhibited abnormalities in the renal cortex and medulla, characterized by increased mesangial area, enlarged urinary space and frequent tubular dilation and hypertrophy in collecting tubules of the medullary region, indicating the presence of inflammatory responses in SCTR-/- mice kidneys. In addition, we proved that SCT/SCTR regulates trafficking and expression of aquaporin 2 (AQP2) in renal principal cells against osmotic challenges, demonstrating a possible role for SCT in regulating sodium reabsorption and protecting renal cells from inflammatory damage due to osmotic stress. Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid produced in adrenal zona glomerulosa (ZG) and regulates renal sodium channel (ENaCs) to enhance sodium retention in kidney. Since SCT/SCTR has already proven with a close involvement in body fluid homeostasis and together with the data above about SCT functions in sodium retention, we therefore studied the function of SCT in regulating sodium retention through aldosterone under salt restriction condition. As cholesterol uptake into adrenal cortex is the first step in aldosterone biosynthesis, we therefore performed oil-red-O staining to investigate the effect of SCT/SCTR on cholesterol uptake. We firstly found that the cholesteryl ester accumulation was remarkedly increased in the adrenal cortex of WT mice, but not in SCTR-/- mice. While the basal level of plasma HDL cholesterol in SCTR-/- mice was slightly but significantly increased compared to WT mice. Next, we examined the transcript level of SCARBI in adrenal cortex after low-sodium diet treatment as HDL-cholesterol is the main source of cholesterol for steroidogenesis through SCARBI. Scarb1 was significantly stimulated in WT low-sodium diet group, but not in SCTR-/- mice. This indicated that SCT/SCTR is involved in cholesteryl ester accumulation in adrenal gland through regulation on selective HDL-cholesterol pathway mediated by SCARBI. Since SCTR modulates ANGII-induced aldosterone biosynthesis, we explored its role in ANGII-mediated ENaC regulation. Significantly higher baselines of ENaC-α, β and γ transcripts were observed in renal cortex of SCTR-/- mice after low-sodium diet treatment. SCTR-/- mice also showed increased cortical ENaC-α in response to sodium restriction. Meanwhile, very similar patterns of transcript changes were observed in renal medulla. Cortical ENaC-α protein in WT mice was elevated due to low-sodium diet, but not in SCTR-/- mice, while ENaC-γ expression was unchanged in both genotypes regardless of dietary sodium content. Since ENaC-α protein expression is selectively induced by aldosterone, the unchanged ENaC-α in SCTR-/- mice is likely a result of disrupted aldosterone biosynthesis. Lastly, we investigated the impact of SCTR on the sensitivity of ENaCs to aldosterone by IP-injection of amiloride in WT and SCTR-/- under basal or low Na+ diet conditions. Amiloride is a common medication for blocking ENaC to inhibit sodium reabsorption in kidney tubules. In WT/low-sodium group, amiloride only exhibited a slight effect on urine osmolality, however, SCTR-/-/basal group showed a decreasing trend in urine osmolality immediately after amiloride injection but without compensatory increase at 24 hours. For SCTR-/-/low Na+ group, a much more pronounced drop in urine osmolality was observed in the first 3 hours, but the level was unable to go back to the pretreatment level at 24 h. These data collectively suggested the absence of SCTR results in less sensitive amiloride/aldosterone ENaCs and disrupted aldosterone biosynthesis, which in turn showed that SCT/SCTR has an important role in regulating sodium reabsorption and further protecting the renal cells from inflammatory damage due to osmotic stress.

17112014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112014.value: With the support from this grant, we worked on the functional relationship of NFAT5, SCT and SCTR expression in kidney during osmotic stress. First, we showed the up-regulation of SCTR and NFAT5 expression in kidney collecting duct cells under hyperosmolality, indicating that these two genes are highly responsive to hypertonicity in kidney tubule cells. Next, we identified six potential ORE in the 5’ flanking region of SCTR gene, where the position ranging from -367 to -228 is identified as the core promoter region of SCTR gene. Interestingly, only this region is able to respond to hypertonic stimulation, revealing that the OREs located within this region is related to the up-regulation of SCTR expression during osmotic stress. The position of -268 in SCTR promoter was found to be significant repressed hypertonic-induced promoter activity, therefore indicating this position is a functional motif mediating hypertonic-induced SCTR gene expression. On the other hand, we also looked into the functional relationship amongst NFAT5, SCTR and hypertonicity in kidney cells. By performing NFAT5 overexpression and siRNA silencing studies, NFAT5 was found to be dose-dependently reduced SCTR promoter activity in kidney cells under isotonic conditions. While overexpression of NFAT5 significantly increased SCTR promoter activities in cells under hypertonic conditions. In addition, co-transfecting NFAT5 siRNA with SCTR promoter construct abolished hypertonicity-stimulated SCTR promoter activities. These data clearly showed that NFAT5 is the key mediator in hypertonic-induced expression of SCTR in kidney collecting duct cells. These data has been published in Biochimica et Biophysica Acta 2015. Second, we also worked on the functional role of SCT/SCTR axis in renal cell protection against osmotic stress. We demonstrated that SCT/SCTR axis is involved in cholesteryl ester accumulation in adrenal gland through regulation on selective HDL-cholesterol pathway mediated by Scarb1. In addition, we investigated the impact of SCTR on the sensitivity of ENaCs to aldosterone by IP-injection of amiloride in WT and SCTR-/- under basal or low Na+ diet conditions. For SCTR-/-/low Na+ group, a much more pronounced drop in urine osmolality was observed in the first 3 hours, but the level was unable to go back to the pretreatment level at 24 h. These data collectively suggested the absence of SCTR results in less sensitive amiloride/aldosterone ENaCs and disrupted aldosterone biosynthesis, more importantly showing that SCT/SCTR has an important role in regulating sodium reabsorption and further protecting the renal cells from inflammatory damage due to osmotic stress.

17112014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112014.value: Our data showed SCTR promoter activity and gene expression are responsive to hypertonicity in kidney collecting duct cells. It is interesting to see the possible role of SCTR in protecting kidney tubule cells from osmotic injuries and renal failure. We next demonstrated NFAT5 functions as an activator binding to SCTR promoter region and increased occupancy of SCTR promoter with NFAT5 by hypertonicity, indicating that the increased binding of NFAT5 with SCTR promoter is the mechanism of elevated SCT expression in response to hypertonicity stimulation. Meanwhile, we discovered the SCT/SCTR axis is involved in aldosterone secretion and important to kidney morphological integrity, further stating the importance of SCT/SCTR in protecting kidney cells from long term osmotic stress. However, the molecular mechanism of this axis in avoiding deleterious osmotic injuries and protecting kidney cells from renal failure is still not clear. We will continue looking into the functional relationship of SCTR with other osmo-tolerance genes in kidney cells. Nevertheless, as salt conservation in kidney is tightly related to blood pressure, while our recent data showed SCT as an important modulator in cardiopulmonary system through renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, the possible action of SCT/SCTR in anti-hypertension could be deeply investigated.

17112014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112014.value: In mammal kidney, medulla is always in hypertonic condition due to the urinary concentrating function, therefore those kidney cells have a well-adopted protective mechanism to avoid deleterious osmotic injuries and renal failure. Our findings showed that NFAT5, an osmo-indicible transactivator, can bind to SCTR promoter and mediate SCTR expression in kidney collecting duct cells under hypertonic conditions. This data provides us insight into the protective mechanism of kidney tubules cells against hypertonicity and a comprehensive information on how NFAT5 regulates SCTR expression in different osmotic environments. Nevertheless, our work is crucial to the area of water/salt homeostasis research and is important for understanding the actions of SCT/SCTR in protecting kidney functions. In global, approximately 10% of the population is affected by kidney failure, this project implicates the future investigation in how SCT protect kidney cells from severe damage in clinical prospective.

17112914.label: Realisation of objectives
17112914.value: The funded project has addressed the hypothesis stated in Objectives 1, 2 and 3, leading to the conclusion that (1) hypoxia facilitates the production of cyclic inosine monophosphate (cIMP) by activated soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC): based on findings of experiments measuring isometric tension (in an organ chamber set-up) and release of cyclic nucleotides (with high performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) in porcine coronary and rat mesenteric and pulmonary arteries exposed to hypoxia and in the absence or presence of pharmacological agents to activate and inhibit sGC; (2) an altered form of sGC appears not required for the preferential production of cIMP during hypoxia: based on the findings that hypoxic vasoconstriction mediated by sGC activation can occur in the presence and absence of NO (which differentiates between heme-dependent and –deficient forms of sGC) but requires the presence of magnesium divalent ions (Mg2+); and (3) hypoxic vasoconstriction requiring biased activation of sGC producing cIMP depends mainly on calcium entry through voltage-dependent calcium channels- with L-type channels being the predominant ones involved in contraction in porcine coronary arteries and T-type channels being the major ones for rat arteries [Rho-kinase activation also contributes to hypoxic vasoconstriction in porcine but not in rat arteries]. Since the findings from the experiments (for “Objective 3”) indicate that hypoxia facilitates calcium entry but not calcium-release from sarcoplasmic reticulum (the initial hypothesis for “Objective 4”) for contraction, instead of examining the role of cyclic adenosine diphosphate-ribose (cADPR) in hypoxic vasoconstriction (the initial proposal), experiments were designed to examine the signals responsible for the biased activation of sGC. The results identify the important role of NAD(P)H:quinone acceptor oxidoreductase-1 [NQO1; also known as complex I of the mitochondrial respiratory chain] in the signaling pathway.

17112914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112914.value: (1) Hypoxia causes augmentation of porcine coronary arteries through biased activation of sGC with the production of cIMP instead of the canonical cGMP [reported in the publication in 2015 in J Cardiovasc Pharmacol] (2) Biased activation of sGC producing cIMP not only mediates hypoxic vasoconstriction but also augmentation of contractions to thymoquinone, in porcine coronary arteries as well as in rat arteries (aortae, mesenteric and pulmonary arteries); the findings illustrate the importance of quinone moiety for the biased activation of sGC, and the involvement of calcium entry for the contraction [reported in oral and poster presentations at ASCEPT/BPS Joint Meeting 2015 and EB2016, respectively, and in the publication in 2016 in J Pharmacol Exp Ther] (3) Contractions to hypoxia and thymoquinone are mediated by cIMP in both porcine coronary and rat arteries; in the former they are attributed to activation of Rho-kinase and L-type calcium channels, while in the latter calcium entry through T-type calcium channels appear to play an important role [reported in oral presentations at MOVD2016, and in the publication in 2017 in Acta Pharm Sin B] (4) Both hypoxic vasoconstriction and thymoquine-induced augmentation of contractions requires the presence of Mg2+ as cofactor for sGC. As well, vasodilator action of sGC depending on cGMP production also requires the presence of Mg2+; the findings thus suggest that hypoxia and thymoquinone do not affect the preference of sGC for divalent ion to shift the enzyme in producing cIMP [reported in poster and oral presentations at EB2016 and IUPHAR2017 meetings, respectively] (5) Biased activation of sGC leading to hypoxic vasoconstriction and thymoquinone-induced augmentation of contractions depends on activation of NQO1; and activation of NQO1 by β-lapachone augments contraction in rat aortae and mesenteric arteries through sGC activation and dependent on presence of ITP and cIMP [reported in oral presentation at MOVD2016, and in the publication in 2018 in Naunyn Schmiedebergs Arch Pharmacol]

17112914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112914.value: The present study demonstrates the biased activity of sGC in mediating hypoxic vasoconstriction; therefore, further studies to examine the conditions which facilitate the biased activation of sGC would provide scientific background for preventing and/or alleviating the vascular complications, especially associated with obstructive sleep apnea. Moreover, since sGC, upon activation by NO, can produce cIMP for vasoconstrictor effect, identification of the conditions favouring the biased activity of sGC would prevent unexpected outcomes with clinically-used nitrates (e.g. nitroglycerol and isosorbide dinitrate). In addition, further experiments should be conducted to consolidate the signaling pathways downstream of cIMP responsible for its vasoconstrictor effect. One of the approach is to develop cell-permeable cIMP for functional and cellular experiments. As such, a collaboration with synthetic chemists (from Department of Chemistry of University of Hong Kong) have been established to pursue this objective. In view of the involvement of NQO1 in the biased activation of sGC, studies should be performed to characterize the physiological role of this enzyme, not only in the vascular system but in the whole body, in order to determine whether or not NQO1 inhibitors may have a therapeutic potential against vasoconstriction associated with cIMP production.

17112914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112914.value: The present research project analyzed the mechanisms underlying the vasoconstrictor responses during hypoxia, with the aim to identify the cellular target(s) for which novel strategies may be developed to prevent coronary hypoxic vasospasm in a patient population at risk, in particular cardiac patients suffering from sleep apnea. The findings demonstrated that hypoxic vasoconstriction occurs following the activation of the enzyme soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC) in the vascular smooth muscle cells. While this enzyme under normal conditions produce a vasodilator signal [cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)], under hypoxia it shifts to produce a vasoconstrictor signal cyclic inosine monophosphate (cIMP). A major determinant for the biased activation of sGC involves the activation of NAD(P)H:quinone acceptor oxidoreductase-1 (NQO1); thus pharmacological agents leading to activation of NQO1, including the natural product thymoquinone which has been used traditionally for the management of cardiovascular diseases, also cause augmentation of contractions in blood vessels with the production of cIMP. In conclusion, the findings of the project advance the knowledge on the signaling pathways involved in hypoxic vasoconstriction, leading to the identification of NQO1 as a potential cellular target for the management of the condition, as well to the awareness of a possible detrimental vasoconstrictor effect of thymoquinone.

17113114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113114.value: All human mouths are colonized by microbes, yet certain microbes can become problematic. For example, in gum disease cases, anaerobic periodontopathogenic bacteria invade the gingival tissues and initiate ailments such as periodontitis. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) and nucleotide oligomerization domain receptors (NLRs) are pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) located on and in human cells, respectively. The former are type I trans-membrane proteins that recognize structurally conserved molecules such as those derived from microbes (microbe-associated molecular patterns, MAMPs), and the latter are cytoplasmic proteins that can also recognize MAMPs. Our research group has previously reported a specific PRR expression that appeared to be upregulated in the residential cells in periodontitis tissue. In addition, hypoxic cellular responses, observable as an accumulation of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), were evident in gum disease cases and could be stimulated by bacterial products. We therefore hypothesize that the PRRs of periodontal lining cells function as important innate defense receptors/sensors against microbial challenges, and that the hypoxia preconditioning of periodontal lining cells could serve as protection by modulating or orchestrating local tissue responses to create a tissue environment that facilitates inflammatory periodontal defense. The proposed project will investigate the biology of periodontal lining cells and their TLRs and NLRs in oxygen tension, mimicking early anaerobic periodontal infection. The aims of the project will be to examine host-bacteria interactions at the tooth-gum junction by i) refining PRR profiles in periodontal lining cells in health or disease; ii) determining how the expression of periodontal lining cell PRRs is influenced by various oxygen or HIF-1α levels in vitro; and iii) investigating the periodontal cellular outcomes following hypoxia and MAMP recognition, particularly the initiation of inflammation mediation via cytokines production/regulation, epithelial proliferation and barrier disruption, fibroblasts apoptosis and extra-cellular matrix remodeling. Periodontal lining cell reactions are widely observed in periodontitis and signify gum inflammation. The proposed project will attempt to decipher the biology and role of gingival lining cells in their innate defense against gram-negative anaerobic periodontal infection. 人類口腔中有大量微生物寄居，其中某些微生物可導致問題。譬如，在牙周疾病中，厭氧牙周致病菌侵入牙齦組織並引發牙周炎。Toll样受體(TLR)和NOD受體(NLR)都屬微生物分子模式(MAMP)識別受體(PRR)，分別位於宿主的細胞表面和細胞漿内。前者是I型跨膜蛋白，可識别結構保守的分子，後者是胞漿蛋白，也可職別MAMP。本課題組曾報道過一特異性的PRR在牙周炎組織襯細胞中的表達上調。此外，在牙周疾病中，可能為細菌產物的刺激所致，我們可觀察到缺氧誘導因子1α (HIF-1α) 上調。因此，我們假定牙周袋壁襯細胞的PPR在對抗微生物挑戰中是作為先天免疫防禦中的受體或感應因子。牙周袋壁細胞缺氧預適應可調節，統籌局部組織反應尤其炎症性的牙周防禦。本計劃將通過模擬早期的低氧牙周感染來探討在缺氧情況下牙周袋壁細胞的生物學特性及其TLR和NLR的變化，並從以下幾個方面來研究在齒齦結合處宿主和細菌間的相互作用：1）更深入檢測PRR在健康或炎症的牙周袋壁襯細胞中的表達；2）體外探究不同的氧氣濃度或者HIF-1α水平如何影響到牙周袋壁細胞的PRR；3）研究在缺氧和MAMP識別之後牙周袋壁細胞的反應，尤其是通過以下方法來啟動炎症的調控：細胞激素的產生或調節，上皮的增生和細胞屏障的瓦解，成纖維細胞的凋亡和細胞外基質的重塑。牙周袋壁細胞的反應在牙周炎中非常常見，同時也反映了牙齦炎症的存在。此次的研究計劃將試圖揭示牙周袋壁襯細胞在針對由革蘭氏陰性厭氧菌引發的牙周感染的先天防禦中的生物學特性和作用。

17113114.label: Realisation of objectives
17113114.value: Objectives 1-4 had been realized. In the early experiments, the characterization of TLRs, NLRs and HIF-1α peptides and signals in healthy and diseased periodontal lining cells were carried out. In brief, TLR-1, -2, -4, -5, and -6 are expressed in periodontal epithelium and periodontal fibroblasts and so as major NLRs. Follow up experiments showed expression of HIF-1α peptides are tightly controlled while noncanonical NF-κB pathway appeared to be involved. Autophagy in HGFs was found to be hypoxia-related while in HGKs autophagy remained unchanged in a normoxic or hypoxic environment with or without LPS. Autophagy apparently appeared to be a connective tissue cellular reaction that takes place in chronic periodontitis while hypoxic state may be of the mechanisms inducing such biological function independent on bacteria LPS or DAMP recognition. Upregulated autophagy is at least partly associated with type I collagen synthesis enhancement in HGFs, under hypoxic condition.

17113114.value: Human mouths are colonized by microbes, yet certain microbes can become problematic. For example, in gum disease cases, anaerobic periodontopathogenic bacteria invade the gingival tissues and initiate ailments such as periodontitis. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) and nucleotide oligomerization domain receptors (NLRs) are pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) located on and in human cells, respectively. In addition, hypoxic cellular responses, observable as an accumulation of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), were evident in gum disease cases and could be stimulated by bacterial products. From this GRF supported project, we confirmed that the PRRs of periodontal lining cells function as important innate defense receptors/sensors against microbial challenges, and that the hypoxia preconditioning of periodontal lining cells could serve as protection by modulating or orchestrating local tissue responses to create a tissue environment that facilitates inflammatory periodontal defense. In particular, TLRs 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are upregulated. We also investigated the influence of hypoxic environment towards the periodontal residential cells function and confirmed that despite epithelial cells appeared minimally affected, periodontal fibroblasts expressed autophagy reactions and down regulation of collagen metabolism indicative of initiation of periodontal supporting tissue destruction. 17113114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113114.value: The GRF supported study provided opportunities for further understanding concerning MAMPs, PRRs, tissue hypoxia and periodontal residential cells autophagy and innate periodontal defense/destruction initiation. We are able to identify the key cells involved, the corresponding biological/pathological processes and certain intracellular signaling pathway that may lead to periodontal destruction. Further experiments/planning is underway along such directions to decipher the biology and role of gingival lining cells in their innate defense against gram-negative anaerobic periodontal infection.

17113114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113114.value: Gum diseases occur when there is imbalance between oral anaerobic bacteria and human host defense. This GRF supported study identified/reconfirmed the importance of certain host cell surface factors in recognizing and calling on the defense against gum bacteria. We also identified gum collagen forming cells are vulnerable to bacterial insult and low oxygen environments. The latter triggered autolysis of the cells involved. Perhaps attempt to control the bacteria induce changes in the gum cells involved may help dentists in controlling and preventing periodontitis in the future.
