17113314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113314.value: Tubal ectopic pregnancy occurs in 1.5–2% of all pregnancies and is the major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality in the first trimester of pregnancy. The cause of tubal ectopic pregnancy is not entirely clear. Impaired embryo-tubal transport and infection leading to the development of inflammatory conditions are the major risk factors of the disease. Adrenomedullin is a peptide hormone abundantly expressed in the human oviduct. Its expression peaks at the early luteal phase when the developing embryo is being transported through the oviduct. We found that adrenomedullin increased the beating of the oviductal cilia, which is an important mechanism for transporting embryo within the oviduct. Our work demonstrated oviductal tissue from women with tubal ectopic pregnancy had reduced adrenomedullin production and oviductal cilia beating, suggesting that these women might have impaired adrenomedullin-mediated embryo transport that could cause retention of embryo in the oviduct. Embryo implantation in the uterus involves inflammatory events. Adrenomedullin has well-known anti-inflammatory action. Thus, the reduced adrenomedullin in tubal ectopic pregnancy may contribute to its pathogenesis by rendering the oviduct more susceptible to inflammatory response, which then favors embryo implantation in the oviduct. Indeed, we found higher expression of pro-inflammatory molecules in the human oviducts from tubal ectopic pregnancy. This project studies the role of adrenomedullin and its interaction with inflammatory mediators in the pathogenesis of tubal ectopic pregnancy. Our hypothesis is that reduction in oviductal adrenomedullin production increases susceptibility of the oviduct to inflammatory response, which promotes tubal implantation. Some women are inherently producing less adrenomedullin due to certain DNA sequence variation known as single nucleotide polymorphism in the adrenomedullin gene. We further propose that women carrying such variation would be more susceptible to development of tubal ectopic pregnancy. This is the first study aiming at linking up a genetic susceptibility to tubal ectopic pregnancy with inflammatory activities and embryo implantation in the human oviduct. The results could be applied clinically to identify the at-risk population so as to facilitate early diagnosis, hence reducing morbidity and mortality. The results would give a comprehensive understanding on the pathogenesis of tubal ectopic pregnancy. As pelvic infection is thought to account for the majority of tubal subfertility cases, the results obtained will also lay the foundation of future intervention studies exploring for the possibility of using adrenomedullin supplementation concurrent with fertility treatment in patients with tubal factor subfertility. 本項目旨在研究腎上腺髓質素及其與炎症介質的相互作用於輸卵管異位妊娠的發病機制的作用。我們假定腎上腺髓質素在輸卵管的表達降低, 會增加輸卵管易受炎症反應，促使胚胎在輸卵管植入。有些婦女如帶有先天的腎上腺髓質素的基因變異而令其表達降低, 可能會促使其更容易發生輸卵管異位妊娠。 此研究旨在探討腎上腺髓質素與輸卵管異位妊娠的遺傳易感性及輸卵管炎症活動和胚胎著床的關係。 結果可能在臨床上適用於識別的高危人群，以便及早診斷，並有助我們更全面了解輸卵管異位妊娠的發病機制。研究結果也將為未來探索臨床使用腎上腺髓質素於治療輸卵管因由的不孕症提供基礎。

17113314.label: Realisation of objectives
17113314.value: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when an embryo implants outside of the uterus, the majority (>97%) of which occur in the oviducts, known as tubal ectopic pregnancy (TEP). The exact mechanism leading to TEP remains unknown and there are no suitable animal models because TEP is rare in animals. However, defective cilia beating/muscular contraction for embryo transport and pro-inflammatory phenotype in the oviduct is suggested to be the major risk factors for TEP. Adrenomedullin (ADM) is a peptide hormone abundantly expressed in the human oviduct. Interestingly, significantly reduced ADM expression has been demonstrated in the oviductal tissues of TEP patients when compared with control. We have also demonstrated the association of a single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNP; rs4910118) in the ADM gene with reduced plasma ADM level in the Hong Kong Chinese population. Therefore, in the first part of this study, we hypothesize that the reduction in ADM expression in TEP could have a genetic origin, and women with SNP(s) associated with reduced ADM production would be more susceptible to development of TEP. Previous studies have shown that ciliary beating and muscle contraction in the oviduct can be stimulated by ADM, therefore, the ADM reduction in TEP patients has suggested to impair oviduct transport of embryos, leading to embryo retention within the oviduct. However, as the retention of blastocysts in the oviduct does not result in TEP in mice, there may be other concomitant alterations induced by ADM reduction in the oviducts to permit embryo implantation. Implantation is widely accepted to be associated with local inflammatory event. In addition to be a modulator of ciliary/muscle cell function, ADM is a well-known anti-inflammatory regulator. Therefore, in the second part of this study, we hypothesized that reduced ADM expression in the oviduct triggers excessive inflammation, consequently induced a susceptible tubal epithelium for embryo implantation. Objective 1: To study the effect of SNP on ADM production and to correlate the occurrence of the SNP with susceptibility to tubal ectopic pregnancy We studied the association of the SNP rs4910118, as well as three other tag SNPs of the ADM gene, namely rs11042725, rs3814700 and rs34354539, with the occurrence of TEP. The SNP rs4910118 was previously found by our group to be associated with reduced plasma ADM level in Southern Chinese population. We obtained blood from 144 women with history of TEP and another 510 control women with known history of previous intrauterine pregnancy and without history of TEP. DNA was isolated and genotyped using the MassARRAY system (Sequenom, San Diego, CA, USA) with the iPLEX assay in the Centre for Genomic Sciences, University of Hong Kong. However, rs4910118, as well as the other three SNPs analysed, did not have significant correlation with the TEP phenotype compared to controls. Objective 2: To determine the role of ADM on the inflammatory condition of oviduct We compared the oviductal ADM expression from salpingitis/TEP with normal non-pregnant oviductal tissues. ADM expression is predominately localized in the apical region of tubal epithelium. In line with our previous study, a significant reduction of ADM expression was observed in tubal epithelium from TEP. Since this observed down-regulation of ADM maybe the cause or effect of TEP, therefore, we next determined whether the same phenomenon occurs in salpingitis, a well-known predisposing state of TEP. Interestingly, similar observation of reduced ADM expression was demonstrated in salpingitis when compared to the control, indicating that oviductal ADM insufficiency may contribute to the pathophysiology of TEP. Although macrophages account for the predominant leukocyte population (~50%) in the oviducts of TEP, there are lack of studies on the distribution and phenotypic characterization of macrophages within the human oviducts. To achieve this, flow cytometry analysis was applied to evaluate the percentage of macrophages within the oviductal leukocyte population. In control oviductal samples, CD68+ macrophages accounted for very small percentage (3.57%±0.89%). In sharp contrast, the proportions of CD68+ macrophages were significantly increased in TEP (33.77%±5.55%) and salpingitis groups (15.92%± 4.9%). The results were supported by the IHC staining using anti-CD68 antibody. The phenotypes of the isolated oviductal macrophages from TEP and salpingitis groups were further characterized by RT-qPCR. While the isolated oviductal macrophages showed high expression of M1 macrophages marker, no M2 macrophage marker expressions can be detected. Similar observations can be obtained using immunofluorescent staining. ADM receptors compose of 2 transmembrane components, namely the CRLR and RAMP. By using immunofluorescent staining, ADM receptor components, including CRLR and RAMP2, were identified on the oviductal macrophages of TEP/salpingitis. To confirm the anti-inflammatory activities of ADM on macrophages, the cytokine/chemokine secretome of the oviductal macrophages (TEP/salpingitis) with or without ADM treatment were analysed using antibody array and ELISA. Our results showed that ADM administration significantly suppressed the pro-inflammatory IL-6 and IL-8 production by oviductal macrophages of both TEP and salpingitis. To confirm our observations in primary oviductal macrophages, we further determined the IL-6 and IL-8 secretion by LPS-activated M1 macrophages derived from blood monocytes or THP-1-derived macrophages after ADM treatments. LPS triggers an active pro-inflammatory response in both macrophage subsets. These stimulatory activities of LPS can be attenuated by ADM administration. In addition, the inhibitory effect of ADM can be abolished after siRNA-based CRLR suppression, indicating the importance of ADM receptor specificity on ADM action. Objective 3: To study the role of pro-inflammatory cytokines on tubal ectopic pregnancy using a trophoblastic spheroid-OE-E6/E7 cell co-culture model In order to demonstrate the role of oviductal macrophages from TEP/salpingitis in inducing the implantation, OE-E6/E7 cells were cocultured with the spent medium of the isolated oviductal macrophages. Our results showed that the secretome of oviductal macrophages from both salpingitis and TEP significantly enhanced the expression of implantation-associated factors and the blastocyst surrogates attachment of OE-E6/E7 cells. These data clearly demonstrated the important role of oviductal macrophages in increasing the susceptibility of tubal epithelium for embryo implantation. Implantation is widely accepted to be associated with local inflammatory event in the endometrium that are required for establishment of a receptive endometrium and embryo adhesion. In order to confirm the critical role of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages in enhancing oviductal receptivity, we repeated the study using the spent medium of LPS-activated GM-CSF-polarized M1 macrophages. Similar stimulatory effects on implantation-associated factors expression and blastocyst surrogates attachment of OE-E6/E7 cells can be observed. The reduction in oviductal anti-inflammatory ADM expression in TEP/salpingitis may enhance the inflammatory response of the pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages within the oviduct, and thereby promotes tubal implantation. To examine this hypothesis, the spent medium of purified oviductal (TEP and salpingitis)/LPS-activated M1 macrophages with or without ADM treatment were collected. Their activities on stimulating oviductal receptivity of OE-E6/E7 cells were then analysed. In line with our hypothesis, the inclusion of ADM significantly suppressed the stimulatory effects of oviductal macrophages and LPS-activated M1 macrophages on implantation-associated factors expression and blastocyst surrogates attachment in an IL-6/IL-8 dependent manner.

17113314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113314.value: This project studied the regulatory role of ADM on the inflammatory environment in human oviductal tissue and its relationship with tubal ectopic pregnancy. In particular, we determine whether the ADM-mediated changes in pro-inflammatory cytokines environment within the oviduct can affect embryo implantation. This is the first study on determining the roles of oviductal macrophages and cytokine environment that favors tubal ectopic pregnancy in humans. The results give a comprehensive understanding on the pathogenesis of tubal ectopic pregnancy mediated by inflammation. As pelvic inflammatory disease and salpingitis are thought to account for the majority of cases of TEP, results from this study lay the foundation of future intervention studies exploring for the possibility of using ADM supplementation concurrent with fertility treatment in patients with tubal factor subfertility.

17113314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113314.value: This project studied the regulatory role of ADM on the inflammatory environment in human oviductal tissue and its relationship with tubal ectopic pregnancy. In particular, we determined whether the reduction in ADM-mediated changes in the macrophages (a special type of white blood cells that mediates inflammatory responses) and their secreted products in the oviduct that may favour implantation of the embryo in the oviduct, leading to tubal ectopic pregnancy. This is the first reported study on this topic. Our results gave a comprehensive understanding of how ADM modulates the inflammatory processes and reduce the likelihood of inflammation-enhanced attachment of embryo to the oviductal wall. This shed light on the mechanism whereby reduced ADM expression secondary to inflammatory condition in the oviduct may predispose to tubal ectopic pregnancy. Our findings will pave the way for further studies on the application of ADM as a preventive treatment for the occurrence of tubal ectopic pregnancy in women with history of pelvic infection.

17113514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113514.value: Major structural, functional and metabolic changes in human cardiomyocyte (CM) phenotypes occur during perinatal development, accompanied by hypertrophic growth, in response to complex combinations of neurohumoral and metabolic stimuli in an electromechanically dynamic 3D tissue environment. The individual signals and mechanisms responsible for these phenotypic changes have proved difficult to study, because standard in vitro culture systems do not adequately recapitulate the natural human cardiac niche. Human pluripotent stem cells and cardiomyogenic progenitors represent an unlimited ex vivo source of human CMs; although early cardiac differentiation events can now be reasonably captured in vitro, most stem cell-derived CMs reported to date are heterogeneous with very immature cardiac phenotypes. To overcome this major roadblock and develop a physiological adult-like in vitro heart surrogate for improved tissue and disease modeling, cardiotoxicity and drug discovery applications, we propose to employ hierarchical next-generation engineered human (h) ventricular (V) tissue constructs composed of purified efficiently-produced human embryonic stem cell (hESC)-derived VCMs, pioneered and developed by our team. These include state-of-the-art high-throughput human ventricular cardiac microtissues (hvCMTs) and tissue strips (hvCTSs). Specifically, we will test the central hypothesis that a multiplexed temporal variation of developmentally relevant metabolic, neurohumoral and biomimetic cues can trigger conserved molecular and signaling events in 3D engineered cardiac models that more completely recapitulate the micro-environmental niches of the native human ventricular myocardium. Our central hypothesis is that significant synergisms among electrophysiological, metabolic and neurohumoral strategies to promote maturation can be optimized in hvCMTs for enhanced electro-mechanical functions. To this end, experiments are proposed to systematically develop an enhanced ontogenically inspired, stage-specific combinatorial approach for driving maturation by employing a combination of metabolic, neurohumoral, and pharmacological stimuli paired with electro-mechanical conditioning using high-content hvCMTs. Taken collectively, our combinatorial approach will identify cues and growth pathways essential for human cardiac development and unravel mechanisms critical to the formation of 3D structures that better accurately mimic “human” myocardium. 人心肌細胞表型的主要結構，功能和代謝的變化發生在圍生期發育且通過在有機械電生理動態的三維組織環境中復雜神經介質和代謝刺激的組合而進行著增生性生長。因為標準的體外培養系統不能充分模擬自然中人心臟生長微環境，造成上述表型變化的獨特信號和機制已被證實難以研究。人多功能幹細胞和心肌祖細胞是無限體外人心肌細胞的來源。雖然早期的心肌分化已經可以在體外被合理地模擬，迄今報導的大部分乾細胞分化的心肌細胞是有不成熟心肌細胞表型且異種的。為了克服這個主要的難點和研發體外成熟的心臟代替物以便改善其在組織和疾病模擬，心臟毒理和新藥研發中的應用，我們計劃使用新一代分層級的由我研究組率先研發的方法有效分化並純化而來的人胚胎幹細胞分化的心室細胞（hESC-VCMs）所構成的人心室工程組織。這包括頂尖的高通量人心室微組織（hvCMTs）和組織條（hvCTSs）。具體而言，我們將會驗證在更完整地模擬了人心室肌生長微環境的心臟三維工程模型中，與發育相關的代謝，神經介質和仿生信號的複合時間變化可以觸發保守的分子和信號傳導事件這個核心假設。我們的核心假設是電生理，代謝和神經介質策略的顯著協同促進的心肌細胞成熟可以在hvCMTs中被優化以便增強心肌細胞機電功能。為了這個目的，我們計劃在高含量hvCMTs中通過代謝，神經介質和藥物刺激的組合配以機電刺激來系統地研發一個增強的，符合個體發育且階段特異的組合方法以促進細胞成熟。總體而言，我們的組合方法將會發現人心臟發育所必要的線索和生長通路並且闡明對於更精確地模擬人心肌的三維結構形成的關鍵機制。

17113514.label: Realisation of objectives
17113514.value: We have successfully carried out Objectives 1 and 2 outlined in the original proposal. The extent to which these objectives have been achieved are stated below: As outlined in Objective 1 of the original proposal, we have studied the effect of various metabolic, neurohumoral and pharmacological biomimetics on maturation of hESC-VCMs assembled as hvCMTs. Our first step in developing a 3-stage combinatorial protocol was to examine the effect of different biomimetic stimuli from different stages individually to dissect out the effect of different stimuli on global maturation. These conditions and stimuli were chosen based on our previous data obtained from single hESC-VCM, in which these stimuli applied individually have been shown to show evidence of enhanced maturation based on positive effects on electrophysiology, calcium handling and gene expression. For Stage 1, the Priming stage, we have tested the effect of various prenatal biomimetics outlined in the original proposal in the hvCMT system. These biomimetics include hypoxia (5%O2), triiodothyronine (T3), the histone deacetylase inhibitor valproic acid. For Stage 2, loading, we have investigate the role of biomimetics that mimc postnatal changes of fetal heart development, in particular mechanical and metabolic loading including the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor alpha (PPAR alpha) agonists and oleic acid which promote the development of fatty acid beta oxidation. For Stage 3, adrenergic agonists were applied to mimic neuronal effects on maturation during pre-and post natal periods. In our experiments with hvCMT, these stimuli were first screened for positive effects based on an enhancement of contractile force. Only those conditions that gave rise to an increase in contractile force were further investigated in Objective 2 using the hvCTS system. Based on the above, we have successfully identified biomimetics in both Stage 1 and Stage 2 that can increase contractile force. These stimuli include hypoxia, T3 and oleic acid and PPAR alpha and mechanical stimulation. Objective 2 was carried out by testing the stimuli and conditions identified in objective 1 in the hvCTS system both individually and in combination. With the hvCTS system, we have tested the effect of hypoxia, T3, PPAR alpha/oleic acid firstly on contractile force. Only those stimuli confirmed to have effect on contractile force in the hvCTS system were further studied, both individually and in combination. The electrophysiological properties of hvCTS cultured in these conditions were investigated using the optical mapping system to investigate the changes in parameters such as conduction velocity. Calcium handling properties were also assessed with optical mapping. Gene expression were also studied and changes in expression of key genes for calcium handling, electrophysiology and other cardiac genes were also identified.

17113514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113514.value: We have studied the effect of various metabolic, neurohumoral and pharmacological biomimetics on maturation of hESC-VCMs assembled as hvCMTs. We have identified 2 biomimetic stimuli for Stage 1, Priming stage of the promaturation protocol. Specifically, the effect of hypoxia (5%O2) on contractile force in hvCMT was investigated as guided by our previous finding in single hESC-VCMs showing an increase in sarcKATP current. Our results showed that hvCMT cultured under hypoxic condition showed increased contractile force when compared to normoxic control. While expression of HIF1 alpha was not significantly altered, expression of genes downlstream of HIF1 alpha including SERCA2a and GLUT1 were found to have increased, suggesting an increase in HIF1 alpha activity in hypoxia. However, when we extend this study to the hvCTS system, we did not observe an increase in contractile force. We have also investigated the effect of T3 in hvCMT. T3 treatment for 4 days increases contractile force in hvCMT. T3 treated hvCMT also showed higher resistance to hypoxia/ischemia when pretreated with the mitochondrial KATP opener diazoxide suggesting an increase in the expression of mitochondrial KATP which confers protection from ischemia. (Results published in Keung et al, Sci Rep 2016). T3 treatment also showed an increase in contractile force in hvCTS. In both systems, T3 caused an increase in expression of key calcium handling genes including ryanodine receptor 2 and L-type calcium channel. For Stage 2, loading, we have determined that chronic electrical conditioning at 1 Hz, which induced contraction in hvCMT resulted in a significant increase in force of contraction in both system. Oleic acid supplement in hvCMT has also been shown to increase contractile force. In hvCTS, both electrical conditioning and oleic acid/PPAR alpha agonist caused an increase in contractile force. Expression of key fatty acid oxidation genes including medium chain acyl CoA dehydrogenase, 3 keto CoA thiolase and enoyl CoA hydratase were all upregulated after oleic acid treatment suggesting maturation of the metabolic pathway in hvCTS after oleic acid/PPAR alpha treatment. A manuscript is now in the preparation for publication (see Part C for citation). For Stage 3, wiring, we investigated the effect of isoproterenol, a beta adrenergic agonist on the effect of contractile force in both hvCMT and hvCTS, However, we failed to observe any changes in contractile force in both systems. As the next step in developing a combinatorial treatment protocol for maturation, we have investigated the effect of combined T3/EC (priming+loading) in hvCTS. We observed that while T3/EC applied individually increased contractile force, the combined T3/EC exerted a synergistic effect which further increased the contractile force. Moreover, T3/EC treatment showed improved structure with elongated CMs and organized myofibril as revealed by transmission electron microscope. Gene expression analysis also showed an increase in expression of key calcium handling genes including phospholamban. Optical mapping of calcium transient also revealed a decrease in upstroke time and decay time in hvCTS that underwent combined T3/EC treatment. The finding from this combinatorial treatment of T3 and EC (priming+loading) are now in preparation for publication (see Part C for citation). In sum, we have identified T3 and electrical conditioning as the most effective stimuli representing the Priming and Loading stage respectively. Treatment with T3/EC in combination causes promotes functional maturation of hESC-VCMs.

17113514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113514.value: We have identified T3 and EC treatment as effective promaturation stimuli for hESC-VCMs. Studying the gene expression profile of hvCTS in different conditions reveal the increased expression of key calcium handling proteins. To further investigate the role of T3 and EC and dissect out the mechanism by which these two stimuli exert their promaturational effect. We propose to investigate the global transcriptomic difference of hvCTS under different conditions using RNA sequencing to identify key genes responsible for these promaturational effects. The understanding of promaturational effects of these stimuli will help extend the use of this promaturational protocol for developing mature and phenotypically relevant hESC and hiPSC –VCMs based engineered tissue models accurate disease modeling and drug screening.

17113514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113514.value: We have developed a simple protocol for producing human stem cell derived heart cells that resembles mature adult human heart cells. This involved assembling human stem cell-derived heart cells into artificial tissues and treating these tissues with the hormone T3 and electrical stimulation. The resultant tissues are functionally more akin to adult human heart cells and can be utilized for screening of new drugs as well as providing an accurate model for different heart diseases when used with induced pluripotent stem cells derived heart cells.

17113914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113914.value: A leading cause of blindness worldwide is degeneration of retinal photoreceptor cells. The two large classes of such disorders are retinitis pigmentosa (RP), which affects hundreds of thousands around the world, and age-related macular degeneration (AMD), which affects millions. The causes of both disorders are diverse, but the initial lesion in both cases is to the retinal photoreceptor cells, leaving a retina – either the entire tissue or specific regions of it – unable to detect light. Cone photoreceptors are responsible for daytime and color vision, whereas rod photoreceptors provide for night vision. Therefore, cone dysfunction is particularly debilitating for patients, yet it appears to be secondary to rod death. However, the mechanism of cone cell death is still uncertain. In this proposal, we try to explore a new strategy to prevent a substantial number of cones from the secondary loss in human RP. Previous studies in animal models suggest that collapse of the outer nuclear layer during rod degeneration may cause changes that specifically make the cones vulnerable over time. In this case, preservation of rods may be sufficient to prevent secondary cone death. The main hypothesis of this proposal is that ectopic expression of melanopsin photopigment in rods, which do not normally express melanopsin -- will make the rods resistant to neurodegeneration in RP, thereby preventing secondary cone loss. The melanopsin photopigment is normally present in a very small group of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) in humans and other mammals. Interestingly, recent reports have revealed that melanopsin-expressing RGCs are specifically resistant to neurodegeneration and are selectively spared in several models of retinal diseases compared to conventional RGCs that do not normally express melanopsin. These new findings indicate that melanopsin-containing RGCs may be intrinsically protected from pathological situations by expressing melanopsin, suggesting that melanopsin itself might be a very promising candidate for providing neuroprotection. The proposed strategy is to genetically modify rods in a mouse model of RP, by inserting into them genes coding for the light-sensitive protein melanopsin, using either in vivo electroporation or an adeno-associated viral (AAV) vector. We will examine cellular and functional preservation of cones and investigate the unique neuroprotective mechanisms that may preserve the newly melanopsin-transduced rods. If rods can be modified by the melanopsin treatment that slows the rate of disease progression and thereby delays the onset of vision loss, the impact on human health will be substantial. 視網膜感光細胞的變性是世界範圍內導致失明的首要病因。視網膜色素變性（RP）和年齡相關性黃斑變性（AMD）是兩類最重要的視網膜變性的疾病，困擾世界各地成千上萬的病人。儘管這兩種疾病的起因不同，但都造成視網膜感光細胞死亡。感光細胞中的視錐細胞負責白天顏色視覺，而視桿細胞提供夜視覺。因此，視錐細胞功能對我們視覺至關重要。但是，在視網膜色素變性中，視桿細胞的死亡也會造成視錐細胞的繼發性死亡。然而，視錐細胞死亡的機制至今仍然不清楚。在這個研究方案中，我們將探索一種新的治療策略，來防止視網膜色素變性中大量視錐細胞的繼發性死亡。 以前的動物模型研究表明，視桿細胞死亡引起視網膜外核層的崩潰從而造成對視錐細胞的傷害。我們因此推測如果保護了視桿細胞就可以防止視錐細胞的繼發性死亡。最近的報告顯示，在不同的視網膜疾病中，表達黑視素蛋白的神經節細胞要比不表達黑視素蛋白的神經節細胞更容易活下來。這些新的研究結果表明，黑視素蛋白本身可能具有特殊的神經保護功能。我們此研究方案的主要假設是：如果在視桿細胞上異位表達黑視素蛋白， 可增強視桿細胞抵禦變性能力，那么就可進一步防止視錐細胞的繼發性死亡。 我們的研究策略是用在體電穿孔或腺伴隨病毒在RP的小鼠模型中的視桿細胞上異位表達黑視素蛋白。我們將檢測視錐細胞的功能，以及其獨特的神經保護機制。如果我們這種治療可以減緩疾病進展的速率，從而延緩視力喪失，那麼對人體健康的影響將是巨大的。

17113914.label: Realisation of objectives
17113914.value: The main hypothesis of this proposal was that ectopic expression of melanopsin photopigment in rods, which do not normally express melanopsin -- will make the rods resistant to neurodegeneration, thereby preventing secondary cone loss in RP. To test our hypothesis, we initially over-expressed melanopsin protein in the rod photoreceptors of the rd10 mouse model of RP by using AAV-mOpn4 driven by a rod-specific promoter, bovine rhodopsin promoter (Rho). The rd10 mice were aged to P26, P30 and P50 after AAV injection. After immunocytochemistry and confocal microscopy, we found that melanopsin protein was widely expressed in rod photoreceptor cells of the rd10 mouse retina, indicating the specific-expression of melanopsin protein in the rod photoreceptor cells. We observed that the thickness of the ONL (outer nuclear layer), where the cell bodies of rod photoreceptors are located, is much thicker in melanopsin-transduced rd10 retinas than that of the control rd10 retinas, indicating that the ectopic expression of melanopsin protein preserves rod photoreceptor cells. We then studied whether the preservation of rods in rd10 retinas would prevent cone photoreceptor degeneration. Interestingly, we found that cone cell morphology was well preserved in melanopsin-transduced rd10 retinas, suggesting that the preservation of rod photoreceptors slows down cone degeneration. To evaluate the function of these preserved photoreceptors in melanopsin-transduced rd10 retinas, we performed electroretinograms (ERGs) and optokinetic tracking in these mice. We observed markedly increased amplitudes of scotopic a and b-waves in melanopsin-transduced rd10 retinas compared with rd10 controls. Similarly, photopic ERG a and b-waves amplitudes were significantly larger in melanopsin-transduced rd10 mice than rd10 controls. Our data demonstrate a significant preservation of photoreceptor function with melanopsin treatment. In addition, we evaluated spatial visual performance in rd10 animals treated with melanopsin. To do so, we measured mouse optomotor responses to moving gratings of different spatial frequencies. Photopic visual acuity was significantly better in melanopsin-treated rd10 mice than in rd10 controls, which was consistent with ERG results in melanopsin-treated rd10 mice, indicating improved visual performance after melanopsin treatment. Moreover, we investigated the mechanisms underlying the preservation of rod photoreceptors following melanopsin treatment. Rd10 retinas exhibit calcium (Ca2+) accumulation in the early stages of the degenerative process. We performed the analysis of intracellular Ca2+ in photoreceptor cells using the imaging fluorescent calcium-indicator Fluo-4 AM and flow cytometry. We found that the percentages of photoreceptor cells with elevated Ca2+ from melanopsin-transduced rd10 mouse retinas decreased as compared with the corresponding rd10 controls. In addition, we got similar results from the analysis of intracellular Ca2+ levels in photoreceptors by Fluo-4 AM in living retinal slices. Our data show a deduction in intracellular Ca2+ levels in photoreceptor cells of rd10 mouse retinas following melanopsin treatment. We measured the protein expression levels of calpains, a group of Ca2+-activated proteases, caspase-3 and ceruloplasmin using ELISA. We observed an decrease in these proteins in rd10 retinas following melanopsin treatment. In addition, we evaluated expression levels of the pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 family and pro-survival members of the Bcl-2 family using ELISA. We found downregulation of the pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 family Bax, Bak, and Bok, and upregulation of the pro-survival members of the Bcl-2 family Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL in melanopsin-treated rd10 retinas.

17113914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113914.value: Major findings: 1. Over expression of melanopsin protein in rod photoreceptor cells preserved rod photoreceptor cells in rd10 mouse model of human RP; 2. The preservation of rod photoreceptors prevents secondary cone photoreceptors degeneration; 3. Melanopsin treatment preserved the function of photoreceptors in the rd10 retina; 4. Melanopsin treatment improves visual performance in rd10 mice; 5. Melanopsin treatment reduced the percentages of photoreceptor cells with elevated calcium (Ca2+) in photoreceptor cells of the rd10 retina, whereas control rd10 retinas exhibit Ca2+ accumulation; 6. Melanopsin treatment downregulated the pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 family Bax, Bak and Bok, and upregulated the pro-survival members of the Bcl-2 family Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL; 7. Melanopsin protein might be capable of triggering the mobilization of intracellular Ca2+ and driving Ca2+ outflow, leading to a deduction in intracellular Ca2+ levels in rod photoreceptors; 8. Melanopsin treatment might open up an alternative therapeutic treatment to prevent a substantial number of photoreceptors from degeneration and achieve long-term effective neuroprotection in currently untreatable human RP patients.

17113914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113914.value: Our data show that ectopic expression of melanopsin in rods makes the rods resistant to neurodegeneration and prevent rod degeneration and secondary cone degeneration in RP animal model. It will be interesting to further the unique neuroprotective mechanisms of melanopsin treatment and explore whether melanopsin maintain regulated levels of intracellular Ca2+ via the opening of voltage-gated calcium channel. Moreover, our study has provided the initial proof-of-principle that melanopsin treatment slows the rate of disease progression and delays the onset of vision loss in RP animal models. We have established a close collaboration with other PIs and examined the preclinical efficacy and function of ectopic expression of photopigment melanopsin in the macaque eyes. Our animal works have provided an essential first step towards moving the optogenetic approach nearer to clinic application by providing evidence that it is safe and effective in an animal that has a similar genetic mutation and comparable vision loss to those in human RP. We have received a human ethics approval to conduct clinical trials on human RP patients in mainland China, using an adeno-associated virus vector carrying human melanopsin. We plan to initially validate the therapeutic efficacy, efficiency, safety and toxicology of the optogenetic approach in legally blind RP patients with no light perception vision and determine whether the optogenetic approach is safe in humans before it could be used to treat the disease in human patients.

17113914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113914.value: Melanopsin is a light sensitive G-protein coupled receptor, which is normally present in 1-2% of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) in mammals. These ganglion cells are capable of autonomous phototransduction. In this study, we investigated whether ectopic expression of melanopsin photopigment in rods, which do not normally express melanopsin, could make the rods resistant to neurodegeneration in RP and preserve vision loss in RP. Indeed, our data showed that ectopic expression of melanopsin in rods prevented rod degeneration and secondary cone degeneration and vision loss in a RP animal model. Moreover, we investigated the unique neuroprotective mechanisms underlying the preservation of rod photoreceptors following melanopsin treatment and founded that melanopsin protein triggered the mobilization of intracellular Ca2+ and driven Ca2+ outflow, leading to a deduction in intracellular Ca2+ levels in photoreceptors. Meanwhile, melanopsin treatment downregulated the pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 family and upregulated the pro-survival members of the Bcl-2 family. Our study provided the initial proof-of-principle that melanopsin treatment might provide an alternative therapeutic approach to prevent photoreceptors from degeneration and achieve long-term effective neuroprotection in human RP.

17114114.label: Realisation of objectives
17114114.value: The overall objective of this grant proposal is to investigate the mechanism of a soluble ∆42PD1-based vaccine in amplifying antiviral CD8+ T-cell immunity. With our key emphasis on the induction of HIV-specific CD8 T cells, we propose a focused research program with three specific aims: 1) To determine the antigen presenting cells that take up ∆42PD1-fusion DNA vaccine antigen in situ using flow cytometry and immuno-histochemistry staining. 2) To determine the effect of ∆42PD1-based vaccine on dendritic cells (DCs) maturation and polarization using in vitro culture assay and in vivo study. 3) To determine the role of different APCs in ∆42PD1-based vaccine enhanced CD8 T cell immunity by evaluating proliferation and cytokine production of ovalbumin-specific transgenic T cells. To achieve these goals, we hypothesized that vaccine involving different DC subsets might result in distinct anti-HIV immune responses. To test this hypothesis, we have conducted proposed and additional experiments based on three specific aims. We not only compared ∆42PD1-fusion DNA vaccine and control non-DC targeting vaccine, but also investigated the differences between ∆42PD1 and PD1 in various models. We further investigated the efficacy and correlation of protection by the ∆42PD1 and PD1 vaccine-induced T cell immunity against EcoHIV in mice. First, we constructed the DC-targeting vaccines that conjugated with a luciferase reporter gene to investigate the kinetics of antigen expression in vivo after DNA vaccination. We found no significant differences between ∆42PD1 and PD1 DC-targeting strategies and controls in term of timing and duration of gene expression at the sites of vaccination. Therefore, these two DC-targeting proteins did not affect the level of protein expression in vivo. Moreover, we found significantly increased cell number of myeloid cells on the site of injection, indicating enhanced APCs recruitment during vaccination. We were not able to detect antigen-uptake dendritic cells at the sites of vaccination or lymph tissue probably due to their rapid homing to lymph node and/or antigen digestion after antigen-uptake. We also attempted to conduct immunohistochemical staining of DC subsets with similar results. We, however, found that whilst both of these two DC-targeting proteins bind to myeloid cells at the sites of vaccination, as well as conventional DCs (cDC) and monocytes derived DCs (Mo-DC) in LNs and spleens effectively, there was twofold higher binding efficiency of spleen Mo-DCs by s∆42PD1 compared to sPD1. This finding suggests likely more important role of Mo-DC in antigen-uptake during ∆42PD1-based vaccination. We, therefore, addressed 100% of this project objective. Second, we compared two DC-targeting proteins and control protein in modulating DCs maturation and polarization using invitro culture assay and in murine models. We found that both PD1 and ∆42PD-1 protein enhanced MHCII and CD86 expression on cDCs, but only ∆42PD1 protein enhanced MHCII and CD86 expression on Mo-DCs. In contrast, PD1-based vaccine preferentially activated CD8+ cDC, suggesting that s∆42PD1 and PD1 protein likely enhance T cell immunity through promoting Mo-DCs and CD8+ cDC maturation, respectively. We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective. Third, in order to confirm the role of APCs in ∆42PD1-based vaccine enhanced CD8 T cell immunity, we constructed PD1- and ∆42PD1-based vaccines that express OVA protein. After coculturing with DCs isolated from PD1- and ∆42PD1-based vaccines vaccinated mice, we examined cell proliferation of ovalbumin-specific transgenic T cells and cytokine production in the culture. We found that whilst both ∆42PD1- and PD1-based vaccine engaged antigen-cross presentation, ∆42PD1 enhanced the antigen-cross presentation and CD8 T cells priming compared to PD1 protein. Moreover, ∆42PD1 activated DCs have higher capacity in boosting p24 specific T cell proliferation and TNF and IL-2 cytokine release. In the EcoHIV/mice model, PD1-based vaccine, however, conferred better protection against viral infection in mice. Further study revealed that EcoHIV infected monocytic cells to escape vaccine-induced protection. We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective as well. This finding has important implication for AIDS immunotherapy. In summary, we have worked very hard on the proposed study with two international conference presentations, two papers are in preparation acknowledging this grant support. We revealed not only a promising vaccine strategy but also some mechanisms underlying the vaccine efficacy. This study also resulted in graduation of one Ph.D. student at HKU.

17114114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114114.value: PD1- and Δ42PD1-based DNA vaccines enhance HIV antigen-specific CTL with significantly improved quantity and quality, which confer significant protection against deadly vaccinia viral challenges and antigen-expressing malignant cancer called mesothelioma in mouse models, respectively. In this study, we focus on the mechanism investigation of the ∆42PD-1 and PD1-based vaccine in amplifying antiviral CD8+ T-cell immunity in murine model. Specifically, we discovered that ∆42PD1- and PD1-based vaccination potentiated CD8+ T cell responses by enhancing antigen binding and uptake in DCs and DCs activation in the lymphoid tissues. When compared with PD1-mediated DC targeting, which has advantage in engaging CD8+ DCs, ∆42PD-1 enhanced antigen binding and up-take by Mo-DCs, and maturation and accumulation of Mo-DCs in spleen. Subsequently, we found that both ∆42PD-1 and PD-1-based vaccine engaged antigen-cross presentation in a CD4-independent way, but ∆42PD1- stimulated DCs primed stronger CD8+ T cells response compared to PD1 protein, and have higher capacity in boosting p24 specific T cell proliferation and TNF-alpha and IL-2 cytokine release. This finding indicated that ∆42PD1 and PD1-based vaccine engage different DC subsets, and might have important implication for AIDS immunotherapy considering the CD4 loss after HIV infection (Paper in preparation). The high frequency of durable and protective GAG-specific CD8+ T cell immunity induced by PD1 and ∆42PD1-based vaccination suggested that these kinds of vaccines could potentially be used against HIV-1 and other pathogens. To determine the efficacy of CD8+ T-cell immunity elicited by ∆42PD1 and PD1-based vaccine, we demonstrated that antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell correlates with the elimination of EcoHIV that expresses HIV Gag P24 antigen in immunocompetent BALB/c mice. Moreover, PD1-based vaccine conferred better protection against EcoHIV infection in mice compared to ∆42PD1, although ∆42PD1 enhanced antigen-cross presentation, and induced stronger CD8+ T cells proliferation and cytokine release. Further study suggested that virus infect monocytic cells to escape vaccine induced CD8+ T-cell immunity. Our data suggest that vaccine involving CD8+ DC and Mo-DC subsets not only result in distinct anti-HIV immune responses, but also might have impact in the efficacy in eliminating viral infection. We show that vaccine targeting at CD8+ DC might have advantage in inducing T cell immunity for viral elimination compared to Mo-DCs. The results of this study have been presented in two conferences, and two related papers are in preparation. Overall, our discoveries provide new insights into quantitative and qualitative characteristics of ∆42PD1 and PD1-vaccine-elicited functional CD8+ T cells.

17114114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114114.value: We are now seeking for research funding to study the promising PD1-vaccine in humans. The key discovery made by us is to enhance effective T cell immunity for viral elimination by delivering HIV antigen via PD1 to CD8+ DC subsets effectively. After three years of study, we demonstrated that this PD1-based vaccine strategy has resulted in high levels of qualitatively enhanced HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, which confer better protection in mice against viral infection. The study also revealed underlying mechanisms of this new discovery, which have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens. With this critical discovery, the ultimate goal of future proposal is to bring this promising PD1-based vaccine into human trials. Once the new vaccine works in human with reliable safety profiles during phase I, it will warrant for further phase II/III human studies. The new discovery will be useful not only for preventing HIV infection but also for immunotherapy of treating 36.9 million of infected people because a high frequency of HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells is important for both suppressing viral replication and clearing persistent infection (so-called HIV latency). Our findings also have important implication for future vaccine design.

17114114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114114.value: AIDS has been one of the deadliest human diseases, which has killed over 35.4 million people since 1981. After over 30 years of efforts, effective vaccine and therapeutic cure are still unavailable. For both preventive vaccine and vaccine-based therapeutic cure, it is necessary to induce high levels of broadly reactive neutralizing antibodies and cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes (CTL). Programmed death-1 (PD1)- and a novel PD1 isoform (Δ42PD1)-based DNA vaccines enhance HIV antigen-specific CTL with significantly improved quantity and quality, which confer significant protection against deadly vaccinia viral challenges and cure of an antigen-expressing malignant cancer called mesothelioma in mouse models. In this study, the discovery made by us is the mechanisms of potentiating functional CD8+ T cells in quantitative and qualitative ways by two promising PD1 and sΔ42PD1-based vaccine. we demonstrated that virus may target myeloid cells to escape vaccine-mediated protection. vaccine involving different DC subsets might result in distinct anti-HIV immune responses and protection, which may have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens.

17114514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114514.value: 水稻不僅是重要的糧食作物也是單子葉模式植物之一。作為一種冷敏感作物，水稻在其生長期常受到突發的亞適宜低溫影響。大量水稻蛋白組學的研究表明，葉綠體是受到低溫脅迫影響的主要細胞器。葉綠體不但是光合作用的場所，光合作用效率則是決定作物產量的關鍵因素，而且葉綠體也為人類健康提供豐富的植物化學成分。水稻基因組資訊學科技的最新進展，使得科研人員可以從分子水準解讀維持葉綠體發育和功能的關鍵因素。 定量分析突變體中葉綠體蛋白組水準變化的技術，已被用來探討擬南芥和水稻葉綠體發育的分子機制。本實驗室通過圖位克隆的方法，鑒定出一個核基因編碼的葉綠體J-like蛋白（OsV5a），其在植物中高度保守。低溫敏感型黃轉綠突變體v5a幼苗在低溫條件下（<24°C）葉色呈明顯黃色，葉綠體發育異常，在較高溫條件下，突變體幼苗葉片接近正常綠色，生長正常。OsV5a在雙子葉植物中的同源蛋白CPP1剛被報導是一種依賴光調控的酶（POR）的分子伴侶，並在葉綠素生物合成途徑中發揮重要作用。CPP1在擬南芥中是單拷貝的，其純合突變體導致胚致死。另一方面，由於水稻中存在另一個CPP1同源蛋白OsV5b，因此OsV5a在低溫葉綠體發育過程中可能發揮著特別的適應調控作用。 本課題旨在闡明水稻中OsV5a和OsV5b可能的亞細胞功能。其與POR相關的可能高度保守的生化活性分析將通過蛋白質互作實驗和分子伴侶活性分析測定。通過分析v5a突變體，我們將研究OsV5a/b與POR的功能聯繫以及與低溫下葉綠素合成的關係。通過定量蛋白組學的方法，尋找相關蛋白表達的變化，分析控制v5a溫度敏感表型的分子機制。這些資訊將進一步反映OsV5a在調控低溫葉綠體發育機制中的作用。為了深層次探討OsV5a的分子功能，我們將篩選及鑒定與OsV5互作的新蛋白（不僅限於PORs）。本研究將以OsV5a和OsV5b為例，為單子葉植物基因重複和適應性進化提供依據。研究OsV5a對低溫條件下正常葉綠體功能的調控，將為水稻和其他禾本科作物通過雜交育種和遺傳改造提高產量提供新思路。

17114514.label: Realisation of objectives
17114514.value: Objective 1 OsV5A and OsV5B are highly conserved homologs of the dicot CPP1 which was previously demonstrated to interact with PORs and maintain their stability. In rice, there are two isoforms of POR, namely, OsPORA and OsPORB. We focused the following investigations on OsPORB because it was the only POR isoform detected in light-grown seedlings (our experimental system). POR is an enzyme essential for chlorophyll biosynthesis in all plants. Both OsV5A and OsV5B were shown to interact physically with OsPORB using yeast 2-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays. The BiFC analysis was done by expressing the full coding sequences in combination as enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (EYFP)-N and EYFP-C fusion proteins in rice protoplasts following polyethylene glycol (PEG)-mediated transformation. The different transformed protoplasts exhibited strong EYFP fluorescence inside chloroplasts, demonstrating that the OsV5A-OsPORB interaction and OsV5A-OsPORB interaction occur inside chloroplasts which are likely to be their functional location. The in vitro capacities of OsV5A and OsV5B to alleviate hydrogen peroxide-induced aggregation of OsPORB were further demonstrated. These results indicate that OsV5A and OsV5B have chaperone activities on OsPORB and could stabilize OsPORB protein against oxidative stress. Objective 2 The complementation of osv5a mutation by constitutive over-expression of OsV5B indicated that the two homologs share redundant functions in rice. The abundances of OsV5A and OsV5B were then examined in rice seedlings at 3-leaf stage by immunoblot analysis. OsV5A- and OsV5B-specific antibodies were designed based on the unique regions in the respective sequences. Western blot experiments were done using 3-leaf stage seedlings (whole plant, 3rd and 4th leaves) of wild type and osv5a mutant. At this stage, the 4th leaf was still concealed in the shoot by the 3rd leaf sheath. The osv5a mutant shows chlorotic phenotype when grown at 22 ºC but remains green at 28 ºC. Our results illustrated that OsV5A accumulates mainly at an early stage (4th leaf) while OsV5B accumulation occurred shortly afterwards and maintained over an extended period during seedling development. In addition, OsV5B accumulation was apparently delayed in osv5a seedlings at 22 ºC in comparison to 28 ºC. When kept at 22 ºC until the 5-leaf stage, the osv5a mutant seedlings showed considerable increase in green pigmentation while the more mature 3rd and 4th showed substantial chlorophyll content together with high abundances of OsV5B. Given that OsV5A/B interact with OsPORB with chaperone activities, the accumulation of OsPORB was examined in total protein samples prepared from the rice seedlings by immunoblot analysis. Substantial reduction of OsPORB abundance was observed in osv5a seedlings at 22 ºC, consistent with the chlorosis phenotype and the lack of detectable OsV5A and OsV5B accumulation. Similarly, OsPORB was absent or barely detectable in the 3rd and 4th leaves of the mutant seedlings at this temperature. However, appreciable levels of OsPORB were observed the 3rd and 4th leaves when the mutant seedlings were grown to 5-leaf stage at 22 ºC. Hence, OsPORB abundances correlate well with the abundances of OsV5A and OsV5B abundances in the rice seedlings. These results further supported the roles OsV5A and OsV5B in regulating the abundances of OsPORB, which in turns would affect chlorophyll production and photosynthetic performance. Objective 3 We have tried two quantitative proteomics approaches, namely iTRAQ labeling and label-free SWATH, to investigate the proteome of osv5a mutant in our study. Following in-depth analysis, we decided to focus on the SWATH proteomics dataset which contains substantially more useful information than the iTRAQ data in terms of the number of differentially regulated proteins that are statistically significant. The SWATH proteomics platform was recently implemented in our lab (Zhu et al. J Proteome Res 2016, 15, 3528-3539). In this project, the concealed 4th leaf of 3-leaf seedlings was used as the tissues for comparative and quantitative proteomics analysis of WT and osv5a mutant. OsV5A showed strongest abundance in the concealed 4th leaf as revealed by our published paper (Liu et al. 2016) for this project. The SWATH data showed that a total of 442 proteins are differentially regulated (fold change > 1.2 or <0.8, p value <0.05) in the osv5a mutant, among them 289 are up-regulated and 153 are down-regulated. The vast majority of these proteins are functionally categorized by Mapman Bin in different metabolic processes or specific metabolic pathways. The proteome data suggested that in the osv5a mutant, protein translational activities were increased in cytoplasm but decreased in chloroplasts, while photosynthetic activities are suppressed, carbohydrate energy metabolism is activated (glycolysis, TCA cycle, mitochondrial electron transport chain), and amino acid (arginine, leucine, lysine) biosynthesis in chloroplasts are up-regulated. Following the identification of V5-interacting proteins (Objective 4), we further analyzed the SWATH proteomics dataset showing reduced abundances of these proteins (LIL3 and GGR) in the osv5a mutant. Objective 4 Initially we tried to use AtCPP1-HA (Arabidopsis ortholog of OsV5) and OsV5A-HA transgenic rice lines for identification of OsV5A-interacting proteins in vivo. However, the osv5a mutant phenotype could not be complemented by either AtCCP1-HA or OsV5-HA, suggesting that the epitope-tagged proteins were not functional in planta. As it would take considerable time to generate new transgenic rice plants, we have adopted an alternative approach to identify potential interacting proteins of OsV5A. We performed yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) screening of a commercially available Arabidopsis cDNA library (derived from different tissues) using AtCPP1 as a bait. Following several rounds of screening and selection, we obtained four positive AtCPP1-interacting clones. The full-length coding regions were isolated and confirmed to be AtCPP1 interactors by Y2H. In addition, bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assays were performed by Nicotiana benthamiana infiltration. It was demonstrated that the four candidates interact with AtCPP1 in chloroplasts. Three of the Arabidopsis proteins were found to have close homologs in rice. The corresponding rice homologs were isolated and were found to interact with both OsV5A and OsV5B using Y2H and BiFC assays. Subsequently, we decided to focus on one of the interactor: Light-harvesting-like protein (LIL3) for further characterization. Literature searches revealed that LIL3 forms a large protein complex with several terpenoid and tetrapyrrole biosynthesis enzymes in thylakoid membranes of Arabidopsis and rice. These enzymes include POR, chlorophyll synthase (CHLG), geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase (GGPPS), and geranylgeranyl reductase (GGR). Interestingly, LIL3 was recently shown to regulate the abundances of POR and GGR. This has prompted us to examine their interactions with OsV5A and OsV5B. Using Y2H and BiFC assays, we demonstrated that both OsV5A and OsV5B interact with GGR, but not CHLG or GGPPS. Western experiments further demonstrated that LIL3 and GGR abundances were reduced in the concealed 4th leaf of osv5a seedlings (3-leaf stage) where OsV5A is absent and OsV5B levels are minimal. These results strongly indicated that OsV5A and OsV5B are part of the thylakoid protein complex and regulate the abundance of GGR and LIL3, in addition to PORB (as revealed by our tasks for Objectives 1 and 2). These findings were further corroborated by our SWATH proteomics data (Objective 3) showing the reduced abundance of GGR and LIL3 in osv5a mutant seedlings compared to wild-type plants.

17114514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114514.value: In Objectives 1 and 2, we have successfully demonstrated the differential roles of OsV5A and OsV5B in regulating the abundances of OsPORB which is an essential enzyme for chlorophyll biosynthesis. OsV5A accumulates mainly functions at an early stage in concealed leaves while OsV5B functions over an extended period during seedling development. This is distinct from Arabidopsis which contains only one ortholog for this chaperone protein (AtCPP1). We further demonstrated the in vitro chaperone activities of OsV5A and OsV5B on OsPORB during oxidative stress. These tasks were mainly conducted by Dr Li Qingzhu who completed her PhD study in January 2016. During the early stage of this study, Dr Li isolated and characterized several rice chlorotic mutants. She also presented a poster at the Plant Biology 2015 conference on the ylc2 mutant. With the participation of Mr Yang Feng (a current PhD student), the above results were published in in Plant and Cell Physiology 57(11):2392-2402 (2016). A poster on OsV5A/OsV5B was also presented at the Plant Genomics and Gene Editing Congress: ASIA (2017). In Objective 3, we have determined the major proteome changes in the osv5a mutant including up-regulation of protein translational activities in cytoplasm, carbohydrate energy metabolism, and amino acid biosynthesis. On the other hand, protein translation and photosynthetic activities are down-regulated in the mutant. In Objective 4, we have successfully identified and characterized two novel interactors of OsV5A/OsV5B: LIL3 and GGR. Hence, OsV5A and OsV5B are likely components of a previously described protein complex in thylakoid membrane consisting of several enzymes in terpenoid and tetrapyrrole biosynthesis. Like OsPORB, LIL3 and GGR3 abundances are regulated by OsV5A/OsV5B in rice seedlings. All the tasks in Objectives 3 and 4 were performed by student Yang Feng. He is now preparing a manuscript covering the results in these two objectives. He is expected to submit his thesis (all the work is supported by this funding) in August, 2018.

17114514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114514.value: Given the conserved chaperone function of OsV5/AtCPP1 on POR in rice and Arabidopsis, we speculate that AtCPP1 may also regulate LIL3 and GGR in Arabidopsis like OsV5A/OsV5B in rice. Mr Yang Feng has confirmed the AtCPP1+GGR1 and AtCCP1+LIL3 physical interactions by Y2H and BiFC assays. He is now finishing up western experiments to analyze LIL3 and GGR1 abundances in an AtCCP1 RNAi mutant provided by the Korean group who published the AtCCP1 paper. He is also trying to determine whether OsV5A/B is located in the same protein complex (as published recently) by blue native PAGE, followed by western analysis. Hopefully these results can be included in the manuscript which is now under preparation. These findings may provide evidences for the existence of a V5/CPP1 protein complex with terpenoid and tetrapyroole enzymes in flowering plants.

17114514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114514.value: Photosynthesis performance, a key factor affecting crop yield, is largely dependent on the functional maintenance of chloroplasts. A nuclear-encoded chloroplast J-like protein (OsV5a) highly conserved in plants was previously identified in our laboratory by map-based cloning using rice mutants. This study revealed that OsV5A and its closely homolog OsV5B showed differential roles in regulating the abundance of a key enzyme (POR) for the production of chlorophyll which is essential for photosynthesis. OsV5A functions during very early seedling stages, followed by OsV5B throughout later growth stages. OsV5A is particularly important at lower temperatures as seedling development is slowed down and accumulation of OsV5B is delayed. We also analyzed the osv5a mutant using quantitative proteomics, revealing major alterations in protein synthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and photosynthesis. Furthermore, two novel interacting proteins of OsV5A/OsV5B were identified (LIL3 and GGR). Like POR, their abundances in rice are also dependent on OsV5A/OsV5B. Further understanding of OsV5A/OsV5B-dependent mechanism for proper chloroplast functions may provide insights for yield improvement in rice and other cereals through cross breeding or genetic manipulation. This project has allowed the training of two PhD students. It also resulted in one publication, two poster presentations, and one manuscript under preparation.

17114614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114614.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is one of the most common autoimmune diseases, affecting around 1% of the population with high morbidity and increased mortality. Although the etiology of RA is still not clear, extensive investigations have suggested that dysregulated B cell activation and antibody production contribute to RA pathogenesis. Numerous studies have been performed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying conventional B cells (B2 cells)-mediated immune responses under autoimmune conditions. However, the functional implication of B1 cells in the development of RA is currently unknown. B1 cells are distinct from conventional B2 cells by their unique developmental origin, cell surface markers, anatomical localizations and functions. Apart from their well recognized function as first line immune response against infections, B1 cells have been increasingly appreciated for their involvement in autoimmune pathogenesis. Recent studies have found aberrant migration of B1 cells into the kidney in lupus mice and significant infiltration of B1 cells in the pancreas during the initiation of insulitis in nonobese diabetic mice. However, it is largely unclear whether B1 cells are involved in the pathogenesis of autoimmune arthritis. In our pilot studies, we detected the evident migration of peritoneal B1 cells to the inflamed joint tissue in mice with collage-induced arthritis (CIA), a widely used model for human RA. We also confirmed the presence of infiltrated B1 cells in the synovium by immunofluorescent microscopy. Moreover, adoptive transfer of B1 cells significantly increased the severity of disease symptoms and joint damage in CIA mice. Thus, these findings provide a strong baseline for testing our research hypothesis that B1 cells may play a role in the pathogenesis of autoimmune arthritis. In this project, we will investigate how B1 cell activation, migration and function are dysregulated during CIA development. Furthermore, we will determine the effect of B1 cell depletion on the disease progression in CIA mice. Our expected findings will provide further insight in understanding the pathogenesis of autoimmune arthritis and may facilitate the development of targeting B1 cells as a new therapy for treating patients with RA, a cripple disease with high social relevance in Hong Kong and mainland China. 类风湿性关节炎(Rheumatoid arthritis, RA)是最常见的自身免疫性疾病之一，其发病率约为1%，具有较高的致畸性和死亡率。虽然RA的发病机制仍然未完全阐明，但许多研究表明B细胞的异常激活以及自身抗体的产生与RA的发病相关。早前关于RA的发病机制的研究多侧重于传统B细胞(Conventional B2细胞)介导的免疫反应，而B1细胞在RA发病过程的功能不明。 B1细胞有别于传统B2细胞，它们具有独特的发育起源、细胞表面标志、解剖学分布及功能。一直以来，B1细胞在感染中发挥重要作用，但近年来越来越多的研究表明B1细胞参与了自身免疫性疾病的发病。在系统性红斑狼疮小鼠模型的肾脏和糖尿病NOD小鼠的胰腺中都发现了大量 B1细胞的浸润。然而，B1细胞是否参与了自身免疫性关节炎的发病尚不清楚。 我们初步研究发现，在胶原诱导性关节炎 (collagen-induced arthritis, CIA) 小鼠模型中，腹腔B1细胞可迁移至炎症肿胀的关节。尤其过继输入B1细胞可显著加重关节炎症状和组织损伤加重。以上结果表明B1细胞参与了自身免疫性关节炎的发病。 本课题将研究B1细胞在CIA模型中的活化、迁移和功能异常与关节发病和破坏的关系。其次，我们将会清除腹腔B1细胞后观察对CIA小鼠发病进程的影响。研究结果将有助于阐明B1细胞在自身免疫性关节炎的发病机制，为建立以B1细胞作为靶向的免疫治疗RA提供新的线索

17114614.label: Realisation of objectives
17114614.value: 1. The dysregulations of B1a cell migration and function in autoimmune arthritis (1) We have observed markedly reduced B1a cells in the peritoneal cavity (PC) which was correlated with significantly increased numbers of B1a cells in the spleen, inguinal lymph nodes and joint tissue during development of collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) in mice, indicating the increased migration of B1a cells from peritoneal cavity to other organs and tissues. We also detected the presence of infiltrated B1a cells in the joint tissue of CIA mice by immunofluorescence microscopy. (2) To investigate whether the increased number of B1a cells was due to proliferative expansion, CFSE was injected into the PC of collagen II (CII)-immunized mice. The proliferative rate of B1a cells was determined by measuring the diluted CFSE fluorescence intensity with flow cytometry. Remarkably, the proliferative rate of B1a cells was rapidly increased during CIA progression, suggesting that B1a cells underwent proliferative expansion in the peritoneum during the development of CIA. (3) To further determine the mechanisms underlying the increased migration of B1a cells in the joint tissues, we detected significantly upregulated CXCR5 expression on B1a cells and increased CXCL13 expression in joint tissue of CIA mice. These results suggested a possible role of CXCL13-CXCR5 axis in the migration of B1a cells to the inflamed joint tissue. (4) To characterize the phenotypic features of B cells in the inflamed joint of CIA mice, we detected significant Receptor Activator of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Ligand (RANKL) expression on synovial B cells, with a 7-fold higher frequency of RANKL-expressing CD19+CD43+ B1 than that of CD19+CD43+ B2 cells. These results demonstrated that B1a cells were the major RANKL-expressing cell subset among synovial B cells in the joint tissue of CIA mice. 2. The molecular signals that regulate B1a cell survival and function (1) To determine the inflammatory cytokines involved in inducing RANKL expression on B1a cells in the joint, we detected increased IL-1β and IL-6 in both mRNA and protein levels in the synovium of CIA mice compared with DBA controls. Moreover, treatment with IL-1β and IL-6 significantly increased both the percentage and total number of RANKL+ B1a cells in vitro, suggesting the critical role of proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6 in the induction of RANKL expression on B1a cells in the inflamed joint. (2) Next, we found that IL-1β- and IL-6-stimulated B1a cells markedly promoted osteoclast differentiation and maturation when compared with freshly isolated B1a cells. Consistently, CIA mice transferred with B1a cells exhibited significantly increased numbers of osteoclasts in the joint tissue with exacerbated bone erosion. In contrast, CIA mice with B1a depletion displayed substantially decreased numbers of osteoclasts in joint tissue with ameliorated bone erosion when compared with PBS-treated mice. These results indicated that synovial RANKL-expressing B1a cells could promote osteoclastogenesis both in vitro and in vivo. 3. The role of B1a cells in the development of autoimmune arthritis (1) By transferring sorting-purified peritoneal CD19+CD11b+CD5+ B1a cells into CIA mice, we observed exacerbated arthritis development with an earlier disease onset and higher clinical scores of arthritis symptoms in these mice when compared to PBS-treated CIA mice. Further assessment of synovial hyperplasia, cartilage damage and bone erosion in joint tissue revealed that B1a-transferred CIA mice exhibited more pronounced joint damage with significantly higher histopathological scores when compared with PBS-treated CIA controls. (2) To further determine whether peritoneal B1a cell depletion may ameliorate the development of CIA, we performed intraperitoneal Milli-Q water injection for B1a cell depletion and observed significantly lower incidence of arthritic development and clinical scores of disease severity in B1a-depleted CIA mice than PBS-injected CIA controls. Importantly, B1a cell depletion attenuated the joint pathology with decreased synovial hyperplasia and bone damage in CIA mice. Together, these results demonstrated a pathogenic role of B1a cells in the development of CIA.

17114614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114614.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is one of the most common autoimmune diseases, causing joint pain, stiffness, swelling and decreased movement of the joints. Osteoclasts are multinucleated cells of hematopoietic origin and are the primary bone resorbing cells. Early studies have characterized a contribution of conventional B cells to the development of autoimmune disorders, but it remains largely unclear whether and how B1a cells, a subset of B cells, are involved in the pathogenesis of autoimmune arthritis. Using a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, we demonstrated that B1a cells play a pathogenic role in the disease progression by expressing Receptor Activator of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Ligand（RANKL） which promotes the expansion of osteoclasts from bone marrow cells. These findings reveal a previously unknown role of B1a cells in regulating osteoclast differentiation and exacerbating autoimmune arthritis, which contributes to a fuller understanding of the physiological role of B cells in autoimmune arthritis and may facilitate the future design of alternative therapeutic strategies for the treatment of patients with RA and other autoimmune diseases.

17114814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114814.value: 為對標靶治療在臨床上有特殊反應病者作基因鑑定是一種在臨床治療上有希望的新興方法。這個方法已經成功地加速了個人化治療在多種癌症上的發展,以及基因生物反應標記的確認。我們運用了全外顯子組基因測序，已經成功確定了頭頸癌（HNC）患者若擁有腫瘤性MAPK1 E322K突變必會對厄洛替尼（一種在臨床上安全的EGFR酪氨酸激酶抑製劑）有着非凡的臨床完全緩解的治療反應。這項發現揭示了MAPK1 E322K突變在驅動頭頸癌對EGFR酪氨酸激酶抑製劑敏感性的一個潛在機制。 泛腫瘤基因組全面檢測分析顯示這種MAPK1突變乃是出現在頭頸癌、子宮頸癌和在亞洲中幾種普遍癌症的主要基因突變熱點。與此同時, 這種分析亦在頭頸癌中發現了其他在這MAPK1突變附近的常見突變熱點。細胞研究結果顯示MAPK1（E322K）突變在推動 MAPK高水平活化和頭頸癌的細胞生長有着強大的生物活力；這些結果確定了MAPK1 (E322K）為一個啟動頭頸癌的驅動基因突變。另外, 亦有研究指出，MAPK1基因擴增也是驅動頭頸癌增長的潛在動力。值得注恴的是，我們在細胞內訊息傳遞的進一步研究顯示該MAPK1 (E322K)突變熱點擁有在頭頸癌細胞模型內有着推動EGFR活化的能力。我們這項研究首次展示了一種MAPK1突變在頭頸癌中引致表皮生長因子受體過度活化的新的機制。 這些臨床和臨床前研究結果引領我們作出以下推測:MAPK1染色體異常可直接驅動頭頸癌的發生;另外,並可引起激活MAPK1的突變能導致EGFR的過度活化通過在頭頸癌細胞中未定義的機制（S）的狀態，從而令EGFR更易被厄洛替尼抑制。為此, 我們建議以下研究計劃：1）比較MAPK1的基因組譜; 2）相關MAPK1突變對頭頸癌的生長和擴散;和3）闡明厄洛替尼的敏感性的機制。這項研究不僅定義了MAPK1基因突變在頭頸癌病變上的作用和對厄洛替尼的敏感的機制，提供個人化的治療頭頸癌的基礎。

17114814.label: Realisation of objectives
17114814.value: All objectives 1,2 &3 have been completed for this project. Results from these studies have led to two original scientific manuscripts, which have been submitted, as well as 4 conference abstracts, which have been published. As a summary of the project completion, we have found that Asian HNSCC carried a relatively higher rate of MAPK1 somatic mutations as compared to the TCGA-HNSCC from the US patients (~5.7% rate in Hong Kong HNSCC vs 1.8% in US-HNSCC). This part was performed by next-generation sequencing and with comparison with the US HNSCC TCGA dataset. This findings indicate a likely ethnic enrichment of MAPK1 somatic mutations. We identified no germline mutation of MAPK1 in our Asian HNSCC patients. Importantly, there is a potential difference in mutational pattern between Hong Kong HNSCC vs US-HNSCC, as US-HNSCC showed a rather uniform mutation pattern with mutation at MAPK1 p.E322 position, whereas in Hong Kong HNSCC, a wide spectrum of MAPK1 mutations are found, including MAPK1 p.D321N, p.R135K. For functional studies, we subsequently showed that MAPK1 gene amplification and MAPK1 p.D321N are driver mutations, driving growth of HNSCC cells, while MAPK1 p.R135K is not a driver for growth. Yet, all these events drive upregulation and activation of p-EGFR in vitro and in vivo. In addition, we found by 3D modeling that these Hong Kong-related, or potentially Asian-related HNSCC MAPK1 mutations are located in the same functional KIM domain in the X-ray crystallograph structure of MPAK1 protein, indicative of functional relatedness. Lastly, for the drug sensitivity study, we performed in vivo studies showing that MAPK1 p.E322K, p.D321N were able to confer significant erlotinib-sensitivity in vivo (P<0.05), with remarkable suppression of p-EGFR as well, consistent with the marked growth inhibition noted in these mutant models. Whereas, the MAPK1 p.R135K conferred moderate erlotinib-sensitivity (P=0.06, trend) with suppression of p-EGFR upon erlotinib treatment. On top of these completion of the project plan, we were further able to discover by bioinformatics approach unique signaling and immunological features of MAPK-mutant HNSCC tumors by data-mining of the transcription profiles of the US TCGA-HNSCC tumors (N=510). We discovered that MAPK-mutant HNSCC tumors have important features that are distinct from other mutant HNSCC tumors, using the TCGA dataset. Briefly, MAPK-mutant HNSCC tumors can have potentially exhibit ERRB3-suppressive effects. The ERBB3-suppressive effects are contributed directly by the ERK (MAPK) activity in mutant cells only. Furthermore, MAPK-mutant HNSCC tumors have the ability to induce cytolytic immunological signatures in situ. Functionally, we successfully showed that MAPK-mutant HNSCC tumors could induce massive recruitment of CD8+T cells in immunocompetent mouse models of HNSCC. This massive CD8+T cell infiltration was accompanied by massive tumor cell apoptosis in vivo as well. Therefore, we believe that MAPK mutations may have the potential to be further developed as genomic biomarkers informing CD8+T cell infiltrations in HNSCC settings. Lastly but not least, we have successfully demonstrated the potential prognostic value of MAPK mutations for HNSCC in 2 patient cohorts. As a summary, we have taken next-generation sequencing approach, in vitro functional, in vivo functional, in vivo (immunocompetent mouse models), bioinformatics analyses of human HNSCC tumors from the TCGA HNSCC dataset to show the functional importance as well as the clinical importance of MAPK mutations in HNSCC development and drug sensitivity. We have identified prognostification values of MAPK mutations in HNSCC.

17114814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114814.value: The major findings have been put together in 2 major manuscripts under review currently. As summary, we found that MAPK1 mutations occur at a higher rate in Asian head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) in Hong Kong vs the US-TCGA HNSCC, and there exist novel mutations in recurrent HNSCC as well. Furthermore, these novel mutations of MAPK1 (D321N and R135K) demonstrated in vivo erlotinib-sensitivity from cell models generated in our lab. Moreover, D321N is a driver mutation for growth causing increases in p-EGFR in isogenic background, while R135K is not a driver for growth, but causing moderate increase in p-EGFR in our cell models. Lastly, we also identify novel signaling (p-ErbB3) specifically altered by MAPK1 mutation in patient tumors as well as in isogenic mouse models in vivo (by immunohistochemistry). Interesting, guided by our in vivo findings, and findings from bioinformatics along reveal also immunological effects of MAPK1 mutations, we have also achieved on top of what we proposed, and identified novel immunogenic features of MAPK1 mutations in mouse models, showing increases in immune infiltrates. Importantly, we also found that MAPK mutations have positive prognostic values in 2 cohorts of head and neck cancer. These findings have been put together into 2 manuscripts under submission/review currently.

17114814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114814.value: There is a potential to further develop MAPK1 mutations into therapeutic targets to guide precision treatment of HNSCC patients with EGFR inhibitor. We would like to try applying for an ITF grant to see if analytic tools can potentially be developed, if possible.

17114814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114814.value: Nature: The nature of the current study is translational, and we aimed to examine the biological activity and drug sensitivity nature and mechanisms of MAPK1 mutations in head and neck cancer. The study was based on our previous clinical finding in the US that a patient completely responded to erlotinib was found to carry MAPK1 p.E322K mutation. Significance: Our finding showed that mutations of MAPK1 p.E322K, p.D321N, and p.R135K all could increased p-EGFR expressions in head and neck cancer cells and mouse models. Importantly, this new mutation MAPK1 p.D321N is also sensitizing head and neck tumors in mice towards erlotinib with marked inhibition of p-EGFR. This mutation is a driver mutation for growth in head and neck cancer. Another mutation, is MAPK1 p.R135K , which showed partial response to erlotinib, and marked inhibition of p-EGFR was also observed in vivo. Additional findings include suppression of growth signals in HNSCC and induction of transcriptional profile related to immunological stimulation by MAPK mutations in HNSCC patients and HNSCC tumors in vivo. We also demonstrated prognostic value of MAPK mutations for HNSCC in 2 cohorts. Value: Findings can be translated into precision medicine clinical trials for erlotinib coupled with MAPK1 mutations, and also for prognostic biomarker development for head and neck cancer.
