17115114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115114.value: 我們以前的功能互補的方法和隨後的cDNA微陣列分析，已經確定了血清澱粉樣蛋白A1（SAA1）是鼻咽癌（NPC）候選抑癌基因。雖然SAA是眾所周知的一種急性期蛋白，它是在肝臟中產生響應於一些刺激，我們先前的研究已經發現了它在鼻咽上皮的表達，有助於新的腫瘤抑制和抗血管生成作用。我們清楚地表明，SAA1蛋白質可以直接用作內源性血管生成抑製劑與增粘堵活動。 SAA1有五個多態等位基因編碼而它們的基因產物相差幾個氨基酸。只有三個SAA1亞型（SAA1.1，1.3和1.5），會在香港鼻咽癌患者和健康的人表達。有趣的是，該變體SAA1.5已經失去了這種新穎的抗血管生成作用。純合子SAA1.5/1.5基因型在鼻咽癌患者的頻率不相稱表明這SAA1基因型可能是一個隱性的易感基因，這有助於增加鼻咽癌風險。我們的初步結果表明，SAA1染色在轉移性鼻咽癌組織中的損失與腫瘤進展相關。然而，這三個SAA1變種的功能作用在NPC轉移尚未研究。我們首先要檢查的SAA1空細胞系中的這三個SAA1亞型的重組是否會影響這些細胞系的轉移潛能。其轉移潛能將通過體內肺轉移模型中考慮。在血管內皮細胞中，我們已經證明，這兩個官能SAA1.1和1.3的異構體可通過直接阻斷整合素V3 與黏著斑激酶（FAK）信號通路抑制粘著斑的裝配。細胞與基質粘附性的用於播散的腫瘤細胞在體內肺轉移模型是關鍵步驟之一。我們要調查SAA1.1和1.3異構體是否可通過拮抗整合素與FAK信號，而抑制鼻咽癌細胞的粘附。我們還計劃使用實驗動物模型，來比較表達三種SAA1亞型鼻咽癌細胞株在體內滲出的作用。作為一種替代戰略，我們也計劃使用質譜儀來識別其他負責對抗鼻咽癌細胞黏附和轉移的SAA1結合夥伴。最後，我們將總結體內滲出化驗結果是否與體外細胞粘附和體內轉移是否有關，以及是否與整合素FAK信號軸起著的核心作用是否有這些相關。此外，整合素FAK信號傳導途徑在鼻咽癌進展的重要性將通過此提議的研究受到牽連。雖然整合素是公知的癌症相關蛋白，其對NPC進展尚未測試。整合素FAK的結果有可能為治療鼻咽癌轉移的治療應用的拮抗劑和粘著斑激酶抑製劑。SAA蛋白也表達在各種組織中的正常上皮細胞，所以SAA1和其基因型可能參與上皮起源的其它類型癌症的腫瘤發展。兩者合計，SAA1多態性與鼻咽癌進展這一提議的研究將在不久的將來開拓不同的研究領域。

17115114.label: Realisation of objectives
17115114.value: Objective 1: We have shown that by using the gain- and loss-of function approaches in various NPC cell lines, the focal adhesion mediated by integrins alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5 and focal adhesion kinase (FAK) could be suppressed by overexpressing SAA1.1 and 1.3 in NPC cell lines with down-regulated SAA1 expression. The integrin alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5-FAK-mediated focal adhesion and their activities were studied by both immune-fluorescent staining. NPC cells expressing SAA1.5 had no significant effect on the focal adhesion. The gene silencing of the physiological SAA1.3 levels had reverted this anti-focal adhesion phenotype. In addition, the natural ligand of integrin alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5 could revert the anti-focal adhesion phenotypes mediated by the functional SAA1. In order to ascertain the functional role of the secreted SAA1 protein on focal adhesion, the three recombinant SAA1 variant proteins were produced, and cell treated with SAA1.1 and 1.3 proteins could significantly inhibit the NPC cell adhesion. Taken together of our previous study that SAA1.1 and 1.3 could effectively bind with the integrin alphaVbeta3, we clearly showed that the gene products of SAA1.1 and 1.3 are able to block the NPC cell focal adhesion mediated by alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5, whereas SAA1.5 is a defective protein to act against the focal adhesion. Thus, 100 % of this objective was achieved. Objective 2: The tail vein metastatic assay was performed for NPC cells. The results showed that after 2 months of injection, the SAA1-expressing cells could reduce the metastatic tumors when compared with the vector-alone control. This reduction of metastatic tumor number seems to be associated with the integrin alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5-FAK activities. Thus, 100 % of this objective was achieved. Objective 3: After restoration of the three SAA1 isoforms in NPC cells, the in vivo lung extravasation assay was performed. Various time point from 1 hours to 7 days were tested for the extravasation ability of the NPC cells. We found that NPC cells began to leave the blood vessels to the parenchyma of the lungs at 6 hours onwards. Twenty four hour was chosen for the analysis. NPC cells-expressing the functional SAA1.1 and 1.3 could consistently reduce the numbers of perfusion-resistant cells and knockdown of one SAA1 functional isoform could revert this phenotype. Hence, the expression of the functional SAA1 isoform is strongly associated with the suppression of extravasation of NPC cells. As can be seen, 100 % of this objective was achieved. Objective 4: This is a backup plan. Although we have shown that the two functional SAA proteins could suppression the NPC cell progression via the suppression of the integrin-FAK pathway, the proteomic analysis was performed by mass spectrometry. The binding partners of the SAA1.1 protein were enriched by co-immunoprecipitation and fractionation according to their sizes. Interestingly, putative binding proteins were identified, including various septin isoforms, collagen alpha-6(VI) chain, FRAS1-related extracellular matrix protein 3, inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 2, UDP-glucose:glycoprotein glucosyltransferase 2, etc. All these candidates have been reported to be associated with tumor development, it will be interestingly to pursue for future studies. 100 % of this objective was achieved.

17115114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115114.value: From the gain- and -loss-of-function analyses of SAA1, we found that the two functional SAA1 isoforms (SAA1.1 & 1.3) can suppress tumor invasion by antagonizing the integrin-focal adhesion kinase (FAK) pathway in NPC tumor cells. The focal adhesion assay was performed, and both the SAA1.5-expressing cells and the vector-alone control were able to adhere to the bottom matrix in the first few hours after seeding, whereas there was only minimal attachment observed in the SAA1.1- and SAA1.3-expressing cells, and the reduced cell-matrix adhesion is associated with the decreased in cell viability. The natural ligand of integrins alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5(vectronectin) could revert the anti-invasive activities of the functional SAA1. The extravasation to the parenchyma of the lungs were significantly suppressed in NPC cells-expressing the functional SAA1.1 and 1.3 genes, but cells expressing-SAA1.5 had no significant effect. Knockdown of the functional SAA1 with physiological level could induce the NPC cells to disseminate to the lung. This observation of inhibition of tumor cell extravasation might be associated with the findings of the lung metastasis of the functional SAA1. Our previous study had shown that the SAA1.1 and 1.3 proteins are effective to directly inactivate the alphaVbeta3 protein, taken together, the current results suggest that these two functional SAA1 can suppress the extravasation of NPC cells by blocking the alphaVbeta3-induced focal adhesion. The major results of this project has generated two conferences papers in two international cancer conferences (see Part C9 below), and a manuscript has been prepared and will be submitted (see Part C8 below, the full version of this manuscript is attached).

17115114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115114.value: As the current results indicate that the functional SAA1 isoforms are associated with the suppression of NPC tumor progression, and alphaVbeta3-FAK pathway is involved. These findings suggest that the alphaVbeta3-FAK signaling pathway a potential drug target for treating the NPC patients with advanced diseases, and agents against this pathway should be tested for NPC tumor progression and preclinical analysis should be pursued for investigating the efficacy and safety of these agents. On the other hand, the SAA1 polymorphisms as well as the protein components of the alphaVbeta3-FAK pathway might be useful as biomarkers to identify the advanced cases of NPC. Moreover, as SAA1 is reported to function as a cytokine, the cytokines and growth factors induced by SAA1 could be useful for identification of more biomarkers related to NPC progression and metastasis. We should investigate the possibility of using these SAA1-related circulating protein as cancer biomarkers.

17115114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115114.value: In summary, the findings of the current project suggest that the functional SAA1 isoforms are able to suppress the NPC tumor cells to adhere to and infiltrate the blood vessels to enter the secondary tumor site. These SAA1 proteins can actually interrupt the cell adhesion to suppress the subsequent tumor invasion. These results suggest that the integrin alphaVbeta3 and focal adhesion signaling pathway is associated with NPC progressing to the advanced stages, suppression of this particular cancer pathway could be useful to restrict the migration of the NPC cells to other nearby tissues and distant organs. As distant metastasis is still the major reason of NPC treatment failure in the clinics, this study has opened a new drug target for the control of NPC progression. Furthermore, the genetic variation of SAA1 is likely to be co-related with the cell-matrix adhesion and the invasiveness properties of the NPC tumors. As can be seen, this unique features of SAA1 gene might provide an opportunity to be used as a prognostic biomarker for the advanced diseases.

17115214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115214.value: The basement membrane (BM) protein nidogen 2 (NID2) is an essential component of the protein network responsible for structural integrity. It is involved in cell adhesion and migration. It has a known role in developmental diseases such as osteoarthritis and cancer. NID2 is an important extracellular matrix (ECM) secretory protein that plays an important functional role in invasive metastatic tumors. It also has potential diagnostic value as both a serum biomarker hallmarking aggressive tumors with a poor prognosis and as a methylation marker associated with early disease in a number of cancers. Tissue-specific NID2 expression is reported. Up to now, reports of NID2 are confined to bladder, lung, prostate, liver, colon, stomach, ovarian, breast, and thyroid tumors. We propose to study this important gene associated with metastatic tumors in the context of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), which are both cancers of special interest among the Chinese population, which have not yet been studied. Our interest in this gene stemmed from earlier findings. We find that NID2 is down-regulated in both ESCC and NPC. Its expression is regulated by hypermethylation. Our preliminary data show that when the gene is over-expressed, there is decreased cell migration, invasion, and angiogenesis. We demonstrated that NID2 co-immunoprecipitates with EGFR and the αV/α4/α5 integrins. Therefore, we expect NID2 to play an important role in tumor cell migration, invasion, and angiogenesis and to contribute to ESCC and NPC metastasis. We now propose functional and mechanistic NID2 studies to further define its role in tumor cell migration, invasion, metastasis, and angiogenesis in two cancers of local interest in Hong Kong. We also aim to determine its potential as a promising serum biomarker for metastatic tumors and as a methylation marker for diagnosing early cancer. The proposed studies are expected to elucidate the role of NID2 in cell signaling, cancer development and metastasis, and address its future clinical utility as a biomarker and its potential as a candidate for targeted therapy. 基底膜(BM)巢蛋白(NID2)是決定結構整體性蛋白質網絡中不可缺少的成分。該蛋白的功能涉及到細胞的粘附和遷移。 它的功能在和發育異常相關的疾病中，譬如骨關節炎和癌症，已經被廣泛地研究和了解。NID2是一種重要的細胞外基質(ECM)分泌蛋白，它在腫瘤的侵襲和轉移過程中具有重要的功能。該蛋白還可以作為惡性腫瘤預後不良的血清標記物以及許多癌症早期疾病的甲基化標記物，具有潛在的診斷價值。 有研究表明NID2在組織中有特異性表達。至今關於NID2的報道僅限於膀胱癌，肺癌，前列腺癌，肝癌，結腸癌，胃癌，卵巢癌和甲狀腺癌。我們提出在食道癌(ESCC)和鼻咽癌(NPC)中研究該蛋白在惡性腫瘤轉移中的作用。 這兩種癌症在中國人群中具有較高的研究價值，並且該蛋白從未在以上兩種癌症中被深入地研究過。我們研究巢蛋白的興趣源自較早前的發現。我們發現NID2在食道癌和鼻咽癌中表達下調。NID2基因的表達通過甲基化調控。初步數據表明當該基因被過表達時，細胞的遷移，侵襲以及血管生成都有所降低。我們的研究表明NID2可以和表皮生長因子受體(EGFR)以及V/4/5整聯蛋白免疫共沉澱。因此，我們預測NID2在腫瘤細胞的遷移，侵襲和血管生成中具有重要的功能，從而導致食道癌和鼻咽癌惡性轉移。 食道癌和鼻咽癌在香港人群中有著重大的研究意義，為了進一步確定NID2在這兩種癌症腫瘤細胞遷移，侵襲和血管生成中的作用，現在我們提出了對於NID2功能和機理的研究。同時，我們也致力於明確NID2作為轉移癌血清標記物和癌症早期診斷的甲基化標記物的潛在診斷價值。這項研究有希望闡明NID2在細胞信號傳導，腫瘤發生發展以及轉移過程中的作用，同時強調了巢蛋白作為生物標記物的臨床意義和作為靶向治療靶點的潛力。

17115214.label: Realisation of objectives
17115214.value: Aim 1: Elucidating the function of NID2 We have successfully established NID2 expression constructs and have used them to overexpress NID2 in selected NPC and ESCC cell lines. These NID2-expressing cell lines were then utilized for various functional assays and mechanistic studies in NPC and ESCC. Specifically, we found that NID2 suppresses colony formation ability in both 2D and 3D culture, suppresses wound healing ability and impedes cell migration and invasion. In the in vivo study, we have made use of an intrasplenic metastasis assay to investigate the role of NID2 in regulating cancer metastasis. From the study, we found that NID2 can significantly inhibit liver metastasis of the luciferase-labelled NPC HONE1 cells. Owing to the intrinsic limitation of the cell line metastatic ability, we failed to perform the same metastasis assay using ESCC KYSE30 cells. However, effort has been made to establish the assay in other alternative ESCC cell lines, such as KYSE150, that has higher metastatic ability in vivo. Using the pCEP-Pu-NID2 contructs, we have also successfully purified recombinant NID2 proteins using a mammalian expression system. The purified recombinant NID2 was then utilized in our subsequent ELISA study. Aim 2: Mechanistic studies of NID2 Using both the phosphorylation array and Western blot, we revealed that upon NID2 re-expression, the integrin and EGFR signaling pathways were negatively regulated. Specifically, we found reduced phosphorylation level at various sites of several key signaling molecules, including EGFR (Y992, Y1068, Y1086, Y1148, Y1173), Akt (T308, S473), FAK (Y397, Y925) and PLCγ (Y783). Since these two pathways were known to regulate cancer metastasis in both NPC and ESCC, the current findings are coherent with the observation of potent inhibition effect of NID2 on in vivo metastasis. We also proposed to investigate the role of NID2 in regulating angiogenesis signaling pathways. Upon screening of the expression levels of several angiogenesis-related cytokines using q-PCR and performing in vitro angiogenesis assay with NID2-expressing NPC and ESCC cells, we did not find any significant differences between the vector-alone control group and NID2-expressing group. Hence, the metastasis inhibition effect of NID2 appears to be independent of the regulation of angiogenesis. In the quest to identify what are the proteinase(s) responsible for NID2 degradation, we used zymography with collagen or gelatin as substrates. However, we did not see any significant difference in the collagen or gelatin degradation activities by the corresponding MMPs, when vector-alone or NID2-expressing conditioned media was utilized in the zymography. Aim 3: Evaluating the clinical utility of NID2 as a diagnostic biomarker We have confirmed that the NID2 promoter is hypermethylated in both NPC and ESCC, using the methylation-specific high resolution melting (MS-HRM) assay. We also explored the potential of NID2 hypermethylation detection as a diagnostic biomarker for NPC, using patient plasma. Due to the rather low level of circulating cell-free plasma DNA from the tumor source, only very low frequency of methylated NID2 was detected in the plasma (<10%). On the other hand, we performed the ELISA screening of serum NID2 levels using an in-house established NID2 ELISA, using the recombinant NID2 proteins as internal standards. NPC and ESCC patients’ sera were screened. As no significant differences in serum NID2 level was observed for NPC patients, we did not go further with our analysis. In contrast, for the 101 ESCC patients’ sera screened, the mean serum NID2 level was significantly elevated among the patients, when compared to the 50 healthy control sera. We then performed subsequent analysis to investigate the potential of using NID2 as diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in ESCC. Based on the receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curve, we found that NID2 is a potential diagnostic biomarker, especially when it can also distinguish the early stage patients from the healthy controls. Using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier curve analyses, we revealed that NID2 is a significant independent prognostic factor for predicting overall survival of ESCC patients. We have achieved to a substantial extent all of the project objectives and our research findings serve to enhance our knowledge on the role of NID2 involvement in cancer metastasis and offer novel insight into its potential to be developed as useful diagnostic and prognostic biomarker.

17115214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115214.value: The NID2 protein is a key constituent of the basement membrane that stabilizes the macromolecule networks in the extracellular matrix (ECM). Hence, absence of this protein may have catastrophic consequence such as increased invasiveness and metastatic ability of the cancer cells. Although promoter hypermethylation of NID2 has also been reported in several other cancers, little is known about its functional roles and mechanisms, especially in NPC and ESCC. Both genome-wide methylation profiling and gene-specific methylation-sensitive high-resolution melting (MS-HRM) assays revealed the hypermethylation status of the NID2 promoter in NPC and ESCC biopsies and cell lines. In this project, the functional roles of NID2 in the pathogenesis of NPC and ESCC were scrutinized. NID2 was found to be down-regulated in the clinical samples and cell lines of both NPC and ESCC. In order to characterize the roles of NID2 in NPC and ESCC, the lentiviral transduction system was used to re-express NID2 in NPC and ESCC cells, for use in the subsequent in vitro and in vivo functional analyses. Re-expression of NID2 was shown to suppress the clonogenic survival of NPC and ESCC cells. Besides, the wound healing, migration and invasion abilities of NPC and ESCC cells were also impeded upon the re-expression of NID2. More importantly, using the in vivo metastasis assay, it was shown that re-expression of NID2 in the HONE1-Luc cells significantly inhibits liver metastasis. The mechanistic studies of signaling pathways also confirm that re-expression of NID2 in the NPC and ESCC cells suppresses the integrin/FAK/PLCγ and EGFR/Akt pathways, both of which are known to regulate cancer metastasis. A research article reporting on these findings was published in Oncotarget in 2016. Our ELISA screening of serum NID2 level in ESCC patients also revealed the potential usefulness of detecting elevated serum NID2 level as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. Another research article reporting elevated serum NID2 level in ESCC has been published in Cancer Biomarkers in 2017.

17115214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115214.value: Further study will be needed in order to fully delineate the mechanism behind the cause of reduced phosphorylation, whether it merely involves direct binding between the NID2 protein with the EGFR or integrins, or via other signaling molecules. This would require delicate scrutinization at various levels of the signaling cascade, which can potentially be done by blocking either pathway at various upstream and downstream levels, and screening for the effect of NID2 on the signaling pathway regulation. Further study can also be done to study the degradation of NID2, in terms of the mechanism, abundance, cellular localization and functional roles of various cleaved or degraded NID2 fragments. This would require generation of fragment-specific antibodies to aid in the analysis, as well as generation of expression constructs carrying specific fragments of NID2 with different functional domains. In order to reach translational use, the role of NID2 as a biomarker for ESCC will need further validation in a larger sample cohort, as well as having the comprehensive clinical information to rule out all possible confounding

17115214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115214.value: Nidogen-2 (NID2) is a ubiquitous protein that plays an important role in maintaining the integrity of cellular extracellular matrix and basement membrane. The extracellular matrix and basement membrane serves as a critical barrier to the spread of cancer, a process called metastasis. We hypothesized that the loss of this crucial protein in the NPC and ESCC patients could have catastrophic effect and, hence, we initiated a detailed investigation to scrutinize the role of NID2 in the pathogenesis of NPC and ESCC. Using both a cell line model (in vitro) and mouse model (in vivo), we confirmed the role of NID2 in acting as a suppressor of tumorigenic and metastatic properties. With better understanding of the role of NID2, our findings offer useful insight in the tumor and metastatic development of NPC and ESCC and could aid in improving the therapeutic strategy. Besides, we also explored the use of detecting this protein in serum specimens, and utilizing it as a marker to indicate presence of ESCC (as a diagnostic marker) or to predict the overall survival of an existing ESCC patient (as a prognostic marker). This could serve to improve the therapeutic strategy and outcome of the patients.

17115614.label: Realisation of objectives
17115614.value: Orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) has been regarded as the promising treatment for long-term the patients with early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Because of the severe shortage of grafts from brain-death donors and the importance of timely operation on recipients, living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) offers the unique opportunity of early transplantation with theoretically unlimited source of liver grafts. Since the first successful adult to adult LDLT in Hong Kong in 1994, this surgical innovation has been well established locally and relieved the organ donor shortage. However, a liver graft from a living donor is frequently small-for-size for the recipient. The small-for-size liver graft injury is commonly presented at the early phase after liver transplantation. A series of inflammatory cascades triggered in small-for-size liver grafts may not only regulate graft injury during the early phase after transplantation, but also promote late phase tumor recurrence and even induce chemoresistance. The development of chemoresistance became the main restriction to limit the efficiency of chemotherapy, which is the most important adjuvant treatment for the tumor recurrence after transplantation. Therefore, it is worthwhile to study the impact of acute phase liver graft injury on the induction of late phase chemoresistance after liver transplantation. Understanding the molecular signaling pathway regulating chemoresistance after liver transplantation will be crucial to develop the novel therapy for the improvement of chemosensitization. In this GRF project, we have successfully achieved following research objectives: 1. We have demonstrated the impact of acute phase liver graft injury on the induction of late phase chemoresistance after transplantation for liver cancer both in clinical series as well in animal models. We have addressed the role of inflammatory chemokine-CXCL10 on acute phase graft injury induced chemoresistance in a series of in vitro functional experiments and animal models, and further validated in clinical series. 2. We have elucidated the molecular mechanism of CXCL10 regulating chemoresistance, including the cross-talks among inflammatory networking, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and drug resistance in vitro and in vivo. The findings on mechanistic actions have been further validated in clinical studies. 3. Originally, we have designed a rat liver transplantation model for developing chemoresistance after liver transplantation. However, the rat liver transplantation model for liver cancer have not been built up within the grant duration due to the following difficulties: a. Insufficient budget (total amount of grant is around 73M) and consistent increasing price of reagents for the experiments of Aim 1 & 2. b. Breeding problem of inbred Buffalo Rats for the model – not enough birth of male pubs and high incidence of abnormal liver anatomy, which could not be used for liver transplantation. Solution: We have explored the treatment using CXCL10 neutralizing antibody in a mouse model with liver cancer and hepatic ischemia reperfusion injury plus major hepatectomy. That model has been well-recognized as the ideal model for small liver remnant injury and cancer recurrence (Ling CC, J hepatology 2014, Li et al, J Hepatology 2016). It that model, we have demonstrated the efficacy of the treatment using CXCL10 neutralizing antibody on the improvement of chemosensitivity (Geng et al, Oncotarget 2015). Therefore, although we could not build up the rat liver transplantation model using Buffalo Rat due to short of budget and breeding difficulty, we have developed the treatment in a mouse model.

17115614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115614.value: Representing the efforts for basic, translational and clinical research, we have identified that an inflammatory chemokine CXCL10 plays important roles in liver cancer recurrence and chemosresistance after liver transplantation both in human liver transplantation as well as in animal models. We have further explored the underlying molecular mechanisms as well as developed the potential therapeutic strategy targeting at CXCL10 to improve the sensitivity of chemotherapy in liver cancer animal models. CXCL10 and cisplatin resistance: In orthotopic rat liver transplantation model, CXCL10 was over-expressed in small-for-size liver graft, in which lots of chemoresistance related genes were confirmed to be up-regulated. This finding was further validated in clinical samples. Circulating CXCL10 was significantly elevated in the HCC patients with small-for-size liver graft and the patients with higher CXCL10 had more tumor recurrence after liver transplantation. The proliferation of HCC cells under cisplatin was significantly increased by recombinant CXCL10 protein or over-expression of CXCL10. Moreover, over-expression of CXCL10 could promote tumor growth in ectopic or orthotopic nude mice liver cancer model under cisplatin treatment. Furthermore, application of neutralizing CXCL10 antibody could sensitize cisplatin treatment in HCC cells or orthotopic nude mice liver cancer model. The details of the results may refer to the published paper in Oncotarget (Geng, et al). CXCL10 and graft injury/cancer recurrence: The positive correlation was found among tumor recurrence, circulating Tregs and liver graft injury after liver transplantation for HCC patients. Using hepatic IR injury model in CXCL10 knockout mice, we demonstrated that the knockout of CXCL10 decreased hepatic recruitment of CXCR3+ Tregs and late phase tumor recurrence after hepatic IR injury. The details of the results may refer to the published paper in Journal of Hepatology (Li, et al). The mechanism of inflammatory response on tumor recurrence and potential treatments: A series of functional experiments have been conducted to explore the mechanism of inflammatory response on tumor microenvironment, which further promote tumor recurrence. The potential treatments have been also explored in animal models. The details of the results may refer to the published papers in Oncotarget (Qi et al), Theranostics (Guerra et al), Oncology Letter (Li et al) and Liver transplantation (Man).

17115614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115614.value: Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism of acute phase liver graft injury on tumor recurrence and chemoresistance after transplantation will lay the foundation for the further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent tumor recurrence and increase the chemosensitivities. It will also open a new window for the Research & Development for local and overseas pharmaceutical companies. Therefore, there will be potential commercial benefit for local R&D industries. We are currently developing the new treatments to attenuate liver graft injury at early phase and prevent tumor recurrence and chemoresistance at late phase after LDLT.

17115614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115614.value: Orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) has been regarded as the only promising treatment for the patients with early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, cancer recurrence is the major obstacle of patient’s long-term survival. Chemotherapy is the main option for cancer recurrence after liver transplantation. However, the acute phase liver graft injury may not only induce primary graft non-function, but also result in tumor recurrence and chemoresistance after transplantation. In current study, we aimed to tackle the basic issues of molecular mechanism for chemoresistance after liver transplantation through integrating clinical, translational and basic research. We have identified that an inflammatory chemokine CXCL10 plays important roles in liver cancer recurrence and chemosresistance after liver transplantation both in human liver transplantation as well as in animal models. We have further explored the underlying molecular mechanisms as well as developed the potential therapeutic strategy targeting at CXCL10 to improve the sensitivity of chemotherapy in liver cancer animal models.

17116014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116014.value: Oral diseases remain the most common health problems of childhood. Children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) have poorer oral health compared to children unaffected by developmental disabilities. Poor oral health results in pain, reduced oral function (such as eating and communication problems), and places an additional burden on their general health status, development and well-being. Furthermore, management of oral diseases among children with ASD is complex owing to cooperation issues and underlying medical conditions. That is why typically oral diseases among children with ASD remains untreated, and they suffer. Oral diseases are largely preventable and appropriate oral hygiene is ‘the mainstay’ to attain oral health. Developing oral self-care skills, namely tooth-brushing, is crucial to preventing oral diseases and is an important life skill that promotes independent personal care. The use of visual pedagogy and social story-telling is a well-established teaching method to train children with ASD to perform important tasks for daily life and promotes independence. We developed a tooth-brushing visual pedagogy intervention in collaboration with local organisations servicing pre-school children with ASD that is evidence-based with standards and recommendation for pre-school and at-home tooth-brushing programmes. We have been working with Special Child Care Centers (SCCC) in Hong Kong over the past decade to improve the oral health of pre-school children, and following a recent population-based oral health survey we have focused our attention on the needs of children with ASD. In collaboration with SCCC, medics, educational pscyhologists and the dental team we plan to conduct a randomized clinical trial to test our tooth-brushing visual pedagogy in enabling pre-school children with ASD to perform the task of tooth-brushing and to improve their oral health. The ability to perform the task of tooth-brushing and improvements in clinical oral status (oral hygiene and gingival health) will be determined among those who receive the tooth-brushing visual pedagogy intervention compared to those of the control group who receive standardized oral hygiene instruction. The outcome of this clinical trial will have translational research implications and inform practices in SCCC in Hong Kong and beyond. We have been working with Special Child Care Centers (SCCC) in Hong Kong over the past decade to improve the oral health of pre-school children, and following a recent population-based oral health survey we have focused our attention on the needs of children with ASD. In collaboration with SCCC, medics, educational pscyhologists and the dental team we plan to conduct a randomized clinical trial to test our tooth-brushing visual pedagogy in enabling pre-school children with ASD to perform the task of toothbrushing and to improve their oral health. The ability to perform the task of toothbrushing and improvements in clinical oral status (oral hygiene and gingival health) will be determined among those who receive the tooth-brushing visual pedagogy intervention compared to those of the control group who receive standardized oral hygiene instruction. The outcome of this clinical trial will have translational research implications and inform practices in SCCC in Hong Kong and beyond.

Likewise the mean change (∆) in ‘% of sites with visible dental plaque’ was significantly larger among the TBVP group than among the conventional oral hygiene group at 3-month (p<0.001) and at 6-month (p<0.001). 17116014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116014.value: Null hypothesis 1 was rejected. The brushing visual pedagogy / social story-telling intervention (test intervention) was more effective in controlling dental plaque than conventional oral hygiene instruction alone (control intervention). This was evident in terms of (i) dental plaque index scores at the end of the trial, and ii) percentage of tooth surfaces with visible dental plaque at the end of the trial. Among the test group dental plaque index scores reduced by approximately a third and ‘% of sites with visible plaque’ reduced by approximately a quarter. In contrast in the control group no significant differences in dental plaque index scores occurred and there was minimal changes in the ‘% of sites with visible plaque’ Null hypothesis 2 was rejected. The brushing visual pedagogy / social story-telling intervention (test intervention) was more effective in improving gingival health than conventional oral hygiene instruction alone (control intervention). This was evident in terms of i) gingival index scores at the end of the trial, and ii) ‘% of sites with gingivitis’ at the end of the trial. Among the test group gingival index scores reduced by approximately a third and ‘% of sites with gingivitis’ reduced by approximately a quarter. In contrast in the control group no significant difference in gingival index scores nor in the % of sites with gingivitis occurred. Null hypothesis 3 was rejected. The brushing visual pedagogy / social story-telling intervention (test intervention) was more effective in enabling performance of the task of tooth-brushing than conventional oral hygiene instruction alone (control intervention). This was evident in terms of i) number of tooth-brushing steps overall (13-steps) that were performed at the end of the trial, ii) ‘number of effective’ tooth-brushing steps (specific to oral hygiene) that were performed at the end of the trial, and iii) higher ratings of tooth-brushing performance as rated by independent observers. Baseline dental plaque level was associated with dental plaque level at the end of the trial. Baseline gingival health level was associated with gingival health at the end of the trial. Performance of tooth-brushing at the end of trial was associated with baseline level of performance in tooth brushing, developmental profile (cognitive function, social skills and reading skills), age of child and parental education levels.

17116014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116014.value: Findings from this clinical trial were that the visual pedagogy (social story) was more effective than conventional oral hygiene instruction in teaching children with autism spectrum disorder how to perform the task of tooth brushing, at improving dental plaque levels and at improving gingival health. Of note however the pre-intervention (baseline) levels of tooth-brushing performance, dental plaque levels, levels of gingival inflammation and the development profile of the children were key predictors of the improvements that occurred. Thus it would be useful to consider the effectiveness of the visual pedagogy (social story) compared to conventional oral hygiene instruction among groups with similar levels of development and similar levels of hygiene and disease to support or refute the claim of the greater effectiveness of the visual pedagogy (social story) intervention in all circumstances.

17116014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116014.value: The use of visual pedagogy (social story) was found to be more effective in teaching children with autism spectrum disorder how to perform the task of tooth brushing compared to the conventional approach of providing oral hygiene instruction. Furthermore the visual pedagogy was effective in reducing dental plaque levels. Improvements in dental plaque index scores of around a third were observed, and the percentage of tooth surfaces with visible dental plaque reduced by approximately a quarter. In addition, the visual pedagogy was found to be effective in reducing gingival inflammation (gum disease). Improvements in gingival plaque index scores of around a third were observed and the percentage of sites with gingivitis reduced by approximately a quarter. In contrast, following the use of conventional oral hygiene instruction no significant improvements in dental plaque levels nor in gingival health were observed. The findings from this clinical trail has implications for incorporating the visual pedagogy (social story) as a method of learning for children with autism spectrum disorder to learn how to perform tooth brushing effectively, and to improve dental plaque control and their gingival health.

17116414.label: Realisation of objectives
17116414.value: We have achieved realization of all objectives. The realization is detailed as follows under each of the objectives (1-4): (1) By examining the genomic and transcriptomic dysregulation of solid cancers and using HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a model, RSK2 was found to be dysregulated through two different mechanisms at the DNA and mRNA levels. RSK2 is the RSK isoform dominantly expressed in the liver and was frequently upregulated in several human cancers including HCC. Upregulation of RSK2 in HBV-associated HCCs was associated with more aggressive tumor behavior. (2) Novel recurrent somatic mutations of RPS6KA3 (7/111, 6.3%) were identified in a cohort of HBV-associated HCCs. All RPS6KA3 mutations were somatic and affected by various mutation types including non-synonymous (3/7=42.9%), non-sense (2/7=28.6%), INDEL (1/7=14.3%) and splicing-related (1/7=14.3%). RPS6KA3 encodes RSK2 (p90-ribosomal S6 kinase 2), an ERK1/2 downstream target with two kinase domains. Most of the mutations affected either one of these kinase domains. RPS6KA3 was found to be recurrently mutated. Interestingly, RPS6KA3 mutations had low co-occurrence with known HCC driver mutations (CTNNB1, AXIN1, ARID1A, and TSC1/2). Upon clinicopathological correlation, RPS6KA3 mutation was significantly associated with venous invasion, and tended to be associated with larger tumor size and advanced tumor stage. (3) Restoration of RSK2 expression in Hep3B also significantly reduced c-Raf-MEK-ERK signaling through a SOS1/2-dependent mechanism. Further transcriptomic analysis suggested RSK2 mutation-mediated upregulation of MAPK signaling and revealed upregulated expression of key enzymes in driving the cholesterol biosynthesis, supporting the cellular functions and signaling in HCC. These previously unrecognized findings signify RSK2 mutation may reflect cellular dependency on MAPK signaling and underlying metabolic reprogramming in HCC. (4) Using stable knockdown approach, we have shown that stable shRSK2 knockdown suppressed the tumorigenicity and metastatic abilities in animal models. To functionally characterize RPS6KA3, an RPS6KA3 rescue model was established in Hep3B cells, which carry a naturally-occurring exon10 truncation at RPS6KA3 with no RSK2 protein expression. Restoration of RSK2 expression in Hep3B significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and incidence of xenograft tumors.

17116414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116414.value: RPS6KA3 encodes RSK2 (p90-ribosomal S6 kinase 2), a direct ERK1/2 downstream target with two kinase domains. Through relaying the growth signal from ERK1/2, RSK2 has long been recognized to be playing an important role in supporting cell proliferation under normal physiological condition and is found to be upregulated in human cancer cells. On the other hand, loss-of-function mutation of RSK2 has been suggested to be the underlying cause of Coffin-Lowy Syndrome, a X-linked hereditary disease leading to severe brain and skeletal defects in predominantly male patients. By examining the genomic and the transcriptomic dysregulation of solid cancers and using HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a model, RSK2 was found to be dysregulated through these two different mechanisms at the DNA and mRNA levels. RSK2 is the dominantly expressed RSK isoform in the liver, and was frequently (44/105, 42%) upregulated in HCCs. The upregulation was associated with more aggressive tumor behavior. Stable shRSK2 knockdown suppressed the tumorigenicity and metastatic abilities in animal models. Surprisingly, novel recurrent somatic mutations of RPS6KA3 (7/111, 6.3%) were identified in HBV-associated HCCs. All RPS6KA3 mutations were somatic and affected by various mutation types including non-synonymous (3/7=42.9%), non-sense (2/7=28.6%), INDEL (1/7=14.3%) and splicing-related (1/7=14.3%). RPS6KA3 encodes RSK2 (p90-ribosomal S6 kinase 2), an ERK1/2 downstream target with two kinase domains. Most of the mutations affected either one of these kinase domains. RPS6KA3 was found to be recurrently mutated. Interestingly, RPS6KA3 mutations had low co-occurrence with known HCC driver mutations (CTNNB1, AXIN1, ARID1A and TSC1/2). Upon clinicopathological correlation, RPS6KA3 mutation was significantly associated with venous invasion and tended to be associated with larger tumor size and advanced tumor stage. To functionally characterize RPS6KA3, a RPS6KA3 rescue model was established in Hep3B cells, which intrinsically carry an exon10 truncation at RPS6KA3 with no RSK2 protein expression. Restoration of RSK2 expression in Hep3B significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration and incidence of xenograft tumors, underlying a reduction in c-Raf-MEK-ERK signaling through a SOS1/2-dependent mechanism. Further transcriptomic analysis suggested that RSK2 mutation-mediated upregulation of MAPK signaling supports the upregulation of the expression of key enzymes in driving the cholesterol biosynthesis pathways in supporting the cellular functions and signaling in HCC. This previously unrecognized findings signify RSK2 mutation may reflect cellular dependency on MAPK signaling and underlying metabolic reprogramming in HCC.

17116414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116414.value: In this study, we systematically demonstrated that RSK2 was dysregulated in human HCCs through two different mechanisms. On one hand RSK2 expression was found to be upregulated in human HCCs and carry out traditional RSK2-mediated oncogenic functions as in other cancers. On the other hand, herein, we have provided new evidence that RSK2 could also be dysregulated through inactivation loss-of-function mutations in HCC. RSK2 mutation has significant clinical relevance and likely plays an important role in supporting the MAPK activation, which may be critical in supporting cholesterol synthesis, a critical metabolic process required for HCC development. Further investigation of the relationship between RSK2 and cholesterol synthesis pathway will discover novel translational application.

17116914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116914.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is attributed to a failure of neural crest cells (ENCCs) to form enteric ganglia in the hindgut. Development of the enteric nervous system (ENS) relies on a precise regulation of the neuronal and glial differentiation of ENCCs. Defects in these processes may lead to premature differentiation, resulting in intestinal aganglionosis as seen in HSCR. Hedgehog (Hh) signaling and Sox10 have been implicated in ENS development and HSCR pathogenesis. In addition, Sox10 is linked with two key Hh signaling pathway components, Suppressor of Fused (Sufu) and GLI-Kruppel family member 3 (Gli3), in the regulation of lineage specification of various stem cells. Sox10 repression of Sufu is essential for directing neural stem cells to the glial lineage, while Gli3 is a modifier of Sox10 in the specification of NCC into melanoblasts. Whether these molecules interact and work coordinately to regulate the specification of ENCCs into the glial lineage is unknown. We previously reported that aberrant Hh signaling confers higher risk to HSCR, and that abnormal glial differentiation is a novel disease mechanism. By exome sequencing analysis of our HSCR patients, GLI2/3 and SOX10 were found mutated in some isolated-HSCR patients. Our unpublished results indicate that, in mice, when Hh pathway was constitutively activated through targeted ablation of Sufu, the ratio of Gli2 activator (Gli2A) to Gli3 repressor (Gli3R) was increased in ENCCs, which showed premature gliogenesis of ENCCs accompanied by elevated Sox10 expression. These observations raise an intriguing possibility that Hh signaling induces glial differentiation of ENCCs through suppressing Sufu, Gli3R and/or up-regulating Gli2, thereby promoting Sox10 expression. We hypothesize that aberrant Hh signaling interrupts the coordinated actions of Sufu, Gli and Sox10 in the glial specification of ENCCs, leading to HSCR. In this application, we propose to determine how perturbed Hh signaling causes ENS defects by 1) studying how Sufu mediates glial differentiation of ENCCs; 2) testing if Gli2A and Gli3R regulate gliogenesis of ENCCs; 3) defining the involvement of Gli2A and Gli3R in Sufu-mediated gliogenesis; 4) elucidating if glial differentiation of ENCCs requires the cooperative interaction between Gli and Sox10. In recent years, many genes associated with glial development have been implicated in HSCR and various neurodevelopmental diseases. Our observations suggest that Hh pathway is a key regulator of glial development, representing a potential therapeutic target for these diseases. Our proposed studies should gain biological insights in glial specification, with the long-term goal of improving their treatment. 先天性巨結腸病是由於神經嵴細胞異常，導致腸道缺乏神經細胞 。在腸神經系統的發育過程中， 神經嵴細胞會分化成神經元和神經膠質細胞。神經細胞分化過程必需精確地調控，如分化失衡，會導致先天性巨結腸病。Hedgehog（HH）信號和SOX10對在腸神經系統的發育和先天性巨結腸病有緊密的關係。其中，SOX10與兩個HH信號的關鍵成員互相合作並規範各個幹細胞的分化，它們分別稱為SUFU和 GLI3抑制蛋白。SOX10 壓制SUFU的表達，從而誘導神經幹細胞分化成神經膠質細胞。而在神經嵴細胞分化成為黑色素細胞的過程中，GLI3是SOX10的改性劑。現時，我們仍未能全面了解這些分子是怎樣互相協調工作，從而規範腸神經嵴細胞分化成為神經膠質細胞 。 我們曾經報導過異常HH信號會引致不正常神經膠質細胞發育，從而增加患上先天性巨結腸病的風險。我們分析病人的基因組，發現 GLI2/3和SOX10的基因有遺傳變異。 在小鼠中，我們當通過刪除SUFU，從而增加GLI2 活化蛋白（Gli2A）對Gli3抑制蛋白（Gli3R）的比值，並激活腸神經嵴細胞的HH信號。初步的研究結果顯示，這會增加SOX10表達，並引致膠質神經細胞過早發育。這些數據引出一個有趣的可能性：HH信號通過抑制SUFU，上調GLI2A和GLI3R的比值， 促進SOX10表達，從而誘導腸神經嵴細胞分化成神經膠質細胞。我們假設異常HH信號會引致SUFU，GLI和SOX10分子失衡，並影響神經嵴細胞分化，導致先天性巨結腸病。在這個提案中，我們建議進一步研究異常HH信號是怎樣破壞腸神經系統的正常發育。包括1）研究SUFU如何介導腸神經嵴細胞分化成神經膠質細胞; 2）GLI2A和GLI3R對此過程的作用; 3）定義GLI2A， GLI3R和SUFU的合作關係; 4）確定在腸神經膠質細胞發育中， GLI和SOX10 的互動關係。近年來，先天性巨結腸病和各種神經疾病都與神經膠質細胞發育有關。跟據我們的觀察，HH是膠質細胞發育的一個關鍵信號，可能是治療這些疾病的靶點。我們所提出的研究有助了解神經膠質細胞發育，並以提升治療方法為長期目標。

17116914.label: Realisation of objectives
17116914.value: Aberrant glial differentiation of neural crest cells (NCCs) represents a possible cause of Hirschsprung (HSCR), but the gene machinery involved remains unclear. In this project, we have identified several mutations in GLI1-3 in HSCR patients that all lead to increased GLI transcriptional activity on Sox10 expression. We then used various mutant mouse lines to specifically knock out the key hedgehog (Hh) pathway genes (e.g. Sufu, Gli2) or constitutively express repressor form of Gli to suppress Hh singling to show that Sufu-Gli expression is dynamically regulated during NCC differentiation and correlates with the segregation into neurons and glia. Importantly, we also used Sox10 mutant mice to further establish a regulatory loop between Sufu-Gli and Sox10 to control neuronal versus glial lineage differentiation and migration of NCCs. In our mouse mutants, we demonstrated that aberrantly high Gli activity caused by loss of Sufu disturbs the reciprocal balance of Sufu-Gli and Sox10, resulting in disrupted enteric NCC chain migration, defective axonal fasciculation and intestinal hypoganglionosis. In summary, we identified some novel GLI mutations in HSCR patients, and showed that perturbed Sufu-Gli-Sox10 regulatory nexus contributes to HSCR pathogenesis in mouse and human. We have fully addressed the objectives of this project.

17116914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116914.value: A genetic screen has been conducted to identify disease-causing DNA changes and experimental mouse models were established to investigate the mechanisms underlying and how these DNA changes cause Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease. With the mouse models, the study identified that specific DNA changes in GLI1, GLI2 or GLI3 genes (genes that work coordinately to control the formation of the nerve cells in bowel) disrupt the formation of the nerve cells and their subsequent gut colonisation, resulting in absence of nerve cells at the distal end of the colon as seen in HSCR patients. The novel finding provides important breakthrough for understanding the pathology of this genetic disease.

17117014.label: Realisation of objectives
17117014.value: 1) To isolate and functional characterize CD71(+) subpopulation cells in cervical cancer cell line and primary cervical cancer: A) Investigation of the subpopulation of cervical cancer cell lines by flow cytometry B) Investigation of the proliferation rate of the CD71(+) cells by XTT assay: D) Study of the in vivo tumorigenicity of CD71(+) cells by NOD/SCID mice injection E) Investigation of the self-renewal and tumorigenic ability of CD71(+) cells by serial transplantation F) Investigation of the cell response to radiation of CD71(+) cells by clonogenic assay G) Identification of potential signaling pathways in CD71(+) cells contributing radio-resistance To investigate the percentage of CD71 subpopulation cells in cervical cancer cell lines and primary cervical cancer cells, cells were stained with FITC-CD71 conjugated antibody. We have performed flow cytometry analysis on cervical epithelial cells, HPV-negative cervical cancer cells, HPV-positive cervical cancer cells and tumor tissue-derived primary cervical cancer cells. We found that the percentage of CD71(+) population was high in HPV-positive cervical cancer cell lines (93.5%-96.7%). Moderate to high percentage of CD71(+) population was found in tumor-derived primary cervical cancer cells (19.8%-82.3%) and low percentage of CD71(+) population was detected in HPV-negative cervical cancer (6.5%). The CD71(+) and CD71(-) populations were isolated in tumor-derived primary cervical cancer cells, HPV-negative cervical cancer cells (C33A) and HPV-positive cervical cancer cells (ME180). The purity of isolated CD71(+) and CD71(-) populations were confirmed by flow cytometry after cell sorting. However, the sorted cells from primary cervical cancer cells did not growth well after cell sorting. We then performed functional assays in the sorted CD71(+) and CD71(-) populations from cervical cancer cell lines. XTT assay, soft agar assay and mice injection assay were performed to examine the cell proliferation rate and tumorigenicity of the CD71(+) and CD71(-) populations isolated from C33A and ME180 cells. We found that the cell proliferation rate and tumorigenicity were enhanced in CD71(+) population as compared with CD71(-) population. Furthermore, spheroid formation assay and serial transplantation were performed to evaluate the self-renewal ability of the isolated CD71(+) and CD71(-) cells. We found that CD71(+) cells had a higher ability in forming spheroids while CD71(-) cells could not form spheroid under the same condition. Clonogenic assay was also performed to investigate the cell response to radiation. We also found that the survival rate of CD71(+) cells was higher than CD71(-) cells after irradiation treatment. Quantitative real-time PCR with Human DNA damage-induced array was performed to compare the expression of DNA damage related genes in CD71(-) and CD71(+) cells. However, no significant difference was found. 2) To elucidate the roles of HPV-E6 and CD71(+) in cervical cancer: A) Ectopic expression of HPV-E6 protein in HPV-negative cervical cancer cell lines and normal cervical cell To investigate the significance of HPV-E6 protein in cervical cancer cells, HPV-negative cell line C33A was stably transfected with HPV16 or HPV18 E6 proteins. C33A cells overexpressing HPV16E6 or HPV18E6 were established. We found that HPV-E6 protein (both HPV16 and HPV18) enriched CD71(+) population in all established stable clones. The transforming ability of HPV-E6 stable clones and control clone were examined by soft agar assay and mice injection assay. We found that the in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity were enhanced in HPV-E6 C33A stable clones. Since the CD71(+) population was enriched in HPV-E6 stable clones, we attempted to test whether silencing of CD71 expression in HPV-E6 stable clones could reverse the transforming ability induced by HPV-E6 protein. We found that siRNA could reduce the expression of CD71 in HPV-E6 stable clone. Silencing of CD71 in HPV-E6 stable clone suppressed the in vitro tumorigenicity. These data indicated that HPV-E6 protein enriches CD71(+) population and enhances both in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity while suppression of CD71 expression in HPV-E6 stable clone can reverse the transforming ability. 3) To examine the effects on the blockade of CD71 in targeting CD71(+) cells in cervical cancer A) Establishment of CD71-silenced cervical cancer cells B) Study of the significance of CD71 in maintaining CSCs characteristics in cervical cancer cells C) Study of the role of CD71 in cell proliferation in CD71-silenced cervical cancer cells D) Study on the effect of CD71 in cell cycle in CD71-silenced cervical cancer cells E) Investigation of the oncogenic role of CD71-silenced cervical cancer cells To examine the effect on CD71 in cervical cancer cells, we attempted to establish CD71 knockout clones using CRISPR/Cas9 editing system. However, from the isolated clones after Cas9 and gRNA transfection, only heterozygous clones (wild type and allele with indels) were established. None of the clone was pure homozygous (all alleles with indels). We therefore performed siRNA knockdown of CD71 in cervical cancer cells to examine the effects on the blockade of CD71. Functional studies were performed after confirming the suppression of CD71 expression with real time quantitative PCR and western blot. We found that cell proliferation, self-renewal ability and in vitro tumorigenicity were inhibited in CD71-silenced cells. These data suggested that silencing of CD71 could suppress the oncogenic function of CD71 in cervical cancer cells.

17117014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117014.value: Clinical significance of CD71 in cervial cancer We identified CD71(+) sub-population possessed stem cell-like characteristics and was associated with HPV-E6 expression in cervical cancer cells. Abundant CD71(+) population was detected in HPV-positive cervical cancer cell lines. Ectopic expression of HPV-E6 protein in HPV-negative cervical cancer cells (C33A) enriched CD71(+) population. These findings suggest that HPV-E6 enriches CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells. Oncogenic roles of CD71 in cervical cancer We studied the functional significance of CD71 with CD71(-) and CD71(+) populations. Functional assays were performed. CD71 was found to promote cell proliferation, self-renewal, clonogenic survival, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity of cervical cancer cells. Conversely, we applied siRNA to knockdown the expression of CD71 in HPV-positive cervical cancer cells. We found that suppression of endogenous CD71 expression in HPV-positive cervical cancer cell line sensitized cells in response to radiation and inhibited cell proliferation, self-renewal ability, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity. These data suggested the important role of CD71 in the maintenance of cancer stem-like cells properties and radio-resistance of cervical cancer. Role of HPV-E6 enriched CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells To study the association of HPV-E6 and CD71, we evaluated the size of CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cell lines. We observed high percentage of CD71(+) population was detected in HPV-positive cells while only small amount of CD71(+) cells were detected in HPV-negative cells. Ectopic expression of HPV-E6 protein enriched the CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells. The in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity were enhanced in HPV-E6 C33A stable clones. These observations explained in part the oncogenic role of HPV viral protein in cervical cancer and the involvement of CD71 in promoting tumorigenesis. Effects on silencing of CD71 in HPV-E6 stably transfected cervical cancer cells To determine the oncogenic properties exerted by HPV-E6 could be suppressed via targeting CD71, siRNAs specific for CD71 were applied to knockdown the expression of CD71 in the HPV-E6 stable clone. Silencing of CD71 suppressed cell proliferation, anchorage-independent cell growth and clonogenic survival. Collectively, our data suggested that the important role of CD71(+) population in contributing cell proliferation, in vitro tumorigenicity and the resistance in response to irradiation in HPV-E6 expressing cells. Research outcome All the results have been gathered and will be included in the manuscript. The manuscript is in preparation and will be submitted to an internationally recognized journal such as British Journal of Cancer.

17117014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117014.value: The novel findings of our study identify the association of HPV-E6 protein and CD71 in the contribution of cervical carcinogenesis. Our data demonstrated that the enrichment of CD71(+) population by HPV-E6 protein is responsible for the oncogenic phenotypes of cervical cancer cells. Further investigation on the clinical significance of CD71 in cervical cancer is needed. In addition, we found that CD71(+) population was more tumorigenic while knockdown of CD71 expression in cervical cancer cells inhibited the oncogenic phenotype of the cells. Therefore, suppression of CD71 may be useful in suppressing tumor growth in cervical cancer and may serve as a therapeutic target for cancer treatment. Given that using single cell surface marker may not be ideal in targeting cancer stem-like cells population, future studies on the characterization of CD71 together with other potential cancer-related cell surface markers will be necessary to improve the efficiency in targeting sub-population cells resided in cervical cancer.

17117014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117014.value: In this study, we isolated and characterized CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells. We confirmed that the enrichment of CD71(+) population is connected to the expression of viral oncoprotein (HPV-E6) expression. Our work on studying the association of HPV-E6 and CD71 (+) population is original. This is the first report to show the significance of HPV viral protein in the enrichment of CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells which may be responsible for the tumorigenicity and radio-resistance. We also found that the isolated CD71(+) population in cervical cancer cells exhibited cancer stem-like cells properties which enhanced cell proliferation, self-renewal ability, cell migration, radio-resistance and tumorigenicity. Furthermore, suppression of CD71 expression in HPV-E6-expressing cells could reverse the tumorigenic phenotypes of cervical cancer cells. The findings in this study provided new insight on the use of cell surface marker for isolation of cancer stem-like cells in cervical cancer.

17117514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117514.value: Homologous recombination (HR) usually occurs in late S and G2 phase when an undamaged sister chromatid is available as the template to precisely repair DNA lesions including DNA double strand breaks (DSBs), DNA interstrand crosslinks (ICLs) and other types of damage encountered during DNA replication. HR is also required for the proper segregation of homologous chromosomes during the first meiotic division. HR frequently involves the formation and resolution of four-way DNA intermediate referred to as the Holliday junction (HJ). Holliday junction intermediates have to be resolved for the subsequent chromosome segregation after the broken DNA has been re-synthesized. Despite extensive study, the machinery and mechanisms used to resolve Holliday junction structures in eukaryotes have remained poorly understood. Only recently three structure-specific endonucleases including GEN1, SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 have been implicated in resolution of Holliday junction intermediates in human cells. Multi-domain containing scaffold protein SLX4 (also known as BTBD12) has been shown to interact with a group of proteins including SLX1, MUS81-EME1 and XPF-ERCC1 and coordinates these endonucleases for the resolution of HJs or ICLs structures. SLX4 has also been reported to bind to telometric protein TRF2, mismatch repair proteins MSH2-MSH3 complex, the protein kinase Plk1 and a previously uncharacterized protein C20orf94. Furthermore, SLX4 contains tandem UBZ domains that have been demonstrated to be critical for SLX4 to localize to sites of DNA damage. Interestingly, mutations in SLX4 have recently been identified in patients with a new subtype of Fanconi anemia (Fanconi anemia-p), hence SLX4 has been renamed as FANCP. Although considerable progress has been made in understanding how SLX4-coordinated protein complex functions to preserve genome integrity, the precise mechanism by which SLX4 complex resolves the HJs at the molecular level has yet to emerge. In this proposal we will develop a new structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of SLX4 complex including the following aims: (1) To characterize molecular interaction of SLX4 with SLX1; (2) To elucidate the molecular mechanism of interaction between SLX1-SLX4 complex and DNA substrate; (3) To determine crystal structure of SLX4 tandem UBZ domains in complex with Lys63-linked diubiquitin. The results from our proposed studies should define the molecular basis of SLX1-SLX4 complex formation, provide molecular insights into substrate recognition and catalysis by this complex, and further reveal the molecular basis of K63-linked polyubiquitination as a regulatory signal to modulate SLX4 complex localization. The completed study will enhance our understanding of DNA interstrand crosslink repair pathway. DNA損傷修復是維持基因組穩定的重要機制。DNA損傷如未能及時修復可能導致病變如腫瘤，神經退化，衰老和其他遺傳綜合症。了解DNA損傷修復機制在預防及治療腫瘤等疾病有重要醫學意義。 同源重組（HR）通常發生在細胞週期的S晚期和G2期，此期間同源的姐妹染色單體可被作為模板來精確地修復DNA損傷，如DNA雙鏈斷裂（DSB），DNA鏈間交聯（ICL）等。另外，HR還需要在第一次減數分裂期間分離同源染色體。HR是解開同源重組的重要修復中間產物稱為DNA Holliday 交叉的主要機制。儘管在過去幾十年中進行了廣泛的研究，在真核生物中用於解開Holliday 交叉的蛋白復合物和相關的機制仍然知之甚少。只是在最近3個結構特異性內切核酸酶，包括GEN1，SLX1-SLX4和MUS81-EME1才被發現涉及到在人類細胞同源重組過程中切開Holliday 交叉結構。 SLX4（也稱為BTBD12）含多個結構域，能同多個蛋白包括SLX1（也稱為GIYD2）, MUS81-EME1和XPF-ERCC1 相互作用，並協調這些核酸內切酶切開Holliday 交叉或DNA鏈間交聯結構。 SLX4還被報導結合telometric蛋白TRF2，錯配修復蛋白MSH2-MSH3複合物，蛋白激酶Plk1的和以前未表徵的蛋白C20orf94。此外，SLX4蛋白中的串聯UBZ4結構域已被證明在SLX4招募到到DNA損傷位點過程起關鍵性的作用。有趣的是，在範可尼貧血（Fanconi貧血症-P）患者發現SLX4突變，因此SLX4已被命名為FANCP。雖然最近在SLX4如何協調其蛋白複合物的功能方面已經取得了相當大的進展，但精確的分子機制還不清楚。 鑑於此我們希望在項目支持期間完成以下目標：（1）利用結構生物學手段去表徵SLX4與SLX1的分子間相互作用机制; （2）確定SLX4串聯UBZ結構域如何精确识别泛素化修饰。從我們提議的研究結果應該確SLX4-SLX1複合物形成的分子基礎，進而提供SLX4-SLX1底物識別和催化機制，並進一步揭示多泛素化調節SLX4複雜定位的分子基礎。完成此項研究將提高我們對DNA Holliday 交叉，及間交聯修復途徑的理解。考慮到DNA的交聯劑和電離輻射廣泛應用於腫瘤化療和放療，我們所提出的研究可對腫瘤治療的設計提供重要見解。

17117814.label: Project Objectives
17117814.value: Assess the natural history of Modic changes and risk factors affecting their progression, extent and conversion between types (Years 1-3). We will conduct a 5-year prospective follow-up study since baseline assessment of T1- and T2-weighted MRIs of 100 subjects with Modic changes to determine environmental and lifestyle factors as well as imaging parameters that may prognosticate the progression, extent and conversion of Modic changes as well as their clinical profile. This will represent the largest and longest study to date in the assessment of Modic changes determinants, particularly in Chinese. Assess the presence and extent of endplate breaks, and clinical relevance (Years 1-3). It remains unclear which Modic types present with increased disc degeneration and pain. Studies have noted that nerve fiber density increases in the presence of endplate breaks, which may affect the disc and pain profile. We will conduct ultrashort-time-to-echo (UTE) assessment of the lumbar spine to assess the presence, extent and morphology of cartilaginous endplate breaks in 100 subjects with Modic changes. Levels with no Modic changes and Modic types will be assessed. Clinical profile of each subject will be assessed and correlated with Modic types with and without the presence of endplate defects. Since endplate defects may have a 3D morphology, we aim to perform 3D MRI to further delineate the extent of endplate involvement and surface changes, their relationship with disc degeneration, and their clinically relevance. Assess early developments of Modic changes on T1-rho MRI and their clinical relevance (Years 1-3). Traditional T1- and T2-weighted MRI are not sensitive enough to detect early stages of Modic changes. Therefore, we will conduct T1-rho MRI of the lumbar spine in 100 subjects with different types of Modic changes and compare them to traditional T1- and T2-weighted MRI to detect subtle changes in the subchondral bone and endplate regions. Levels of no known Modic changes on traditional imaging will also be compared to known levels of Modic changes. We will further utilize a historical control group of 100 subjects with no known Modic changes on T1- and T2-weighted MRI but with T1-rho imaging for comparison. In addition, T1-rho will also be utilized to quantitatively assess the proteoglycan content of the disc in relation to Modic changes, and determine their impact. Assess perfusion/diffusion of the subchondral bone/endplate and the disc (Year 3). The disc is avascular, relying on transport of nutrition and metabolites from the subchondral bone and endplate regions. Disruption of perfusion of materials from these regions has been noted to be related to the pathogenesis of disc degeneration. Utilizing dynamic-contrast enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), we aim to perform, in age/sex/BMI/presence of endplate breaks-matched subjects, perfusion studies of the subchondral bone and endplate regions in 20 subjects with known Modic changes (n=10 Type 1, n=10 Type 2) and in 10 subjects with no known Modic changes matched from the Cohort study. T1-rho and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) studies will also be performed to assess the integrity and diffusion of the adjacent disc to Modic and non-Modic changes. The clinical profile in relation to the aforementioned will also be addressed.

17117814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117814.value: Low back pain (LBP) is the world's most disabling condition. Intervertebral disc degeneration commonly occurs in the lumbar spine and is a LBP risk factor. However, overall disc degeneration is not always synonymous with LBP, but severity of such degeneration and “Modic changes” may be more impacting. Modic changes are subchondral bone and endplate changes. These are phenotypes that are important pain generators and “highly associated” with disc degeneration and its severity. Modic changes present as altered signal changes on conventional T1- and T2-weighted MRI, and have been traditionally characterized into 3 main types: fibrovascularization with edema and increased inflammatory production (Type 1), fatty infiltration (Type 2), and sclerotic changes (Type 3). Although once believed that Type 1 Modic changes are highly associated with LBP, evidence suggest that is not always the case and that Type 2 changes may also be symptomatic. Higher nerve density is noted near endplate breaks. Risk factors related to the progression, extent, and conversion of Modic changes as well endplate breaks are speculative, in particular in Chinese. As such, additional imaging is necessary to assess endplate integrity in relation to the Modic phenotype and its clinical relevance. Furthermore, imaging to assess "early" development of Modic changes to better understand its clinical profile and impact has not been previously addressed. Of note, the endplate is the main regulator for disc nutrition and integral in the common pathway of disc degeneration. Lumbar diffusion studies have noted altered diffusion in degenerated discs and in the setting of endplate irregularities/changes, but remain unclear in the setting of subchondral changes. Based on the investigators’ population-based Cohort study, this proposal will address in the largest study to date in subjects with lumbar Modic changes: 1) a “long-term” prospective study assessing risk factors related to the progression, extent and conversion of Modic changes; 2) UTE and 3D MRI to assess the presence, extent and morphology of endplate breaks in relation to Modic type, disc degeneration, and clinical profile; 3) T1-rho to detect early developments of Modic changes and their clinical implications; and 4) DCE-MRI and DTI to assess the perfusion and diffusion, respectively, of the subchondral bone/endplate and disc in relation to levels with and without Modic changes/types as well as endplate breaks. 17117814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117814.value: Based on the studies published, we have very importantly refined the phenotyping of Modic changes based on morphologies assessed on MRI. This sectioning my location helps better classification of abnormalities when studying clinical back pain and is an important biomarker for association studies. We also determined the relationship of disc calcification with UTE sign on MRI. This is an important early sign to highlight the likelihood of a disc becoming degenerated. The calcification increases stiffness of the disc and is a unique change that cannot be seen on plain radiographs or conventional MRI. Finally, we have determined the clinical implications of this imaging phenotype as it has been shown to be strongly associated with degenerative spine changes, chronic low back pain and disability indices. This UTE assessment of the discs serves as an important parameter to identify early disc degeneration and also correlates strongly with clinical severity of back pain.

17117814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117814.value: Based on our previous work, we need further studies to understand the etiology of Modic changes better. Currently we are running two studies, one basic science and one clinical RCT to determine the impact of Modic changes in patients with back pain. For the basic science study, we are performing finite element modeling to determine the relationship of disc calcification and stiffness with the onset and location of Modic changes. For the clinical RCT, we are studying the utility of zoledronic acid to minimize back pain related to Modic changes and also to see if these findings will be altered with drug treatment.

17117814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117814.value: Modic changes is an important imaging finding that correlates with back pain and disability. Our work has refined the understanding and description of this imaging finding and also determined its clinical significance. We found associations with disc stiffness and calcification which are early changes of disc degeneration. We also observed that these changes are associated with worse back pain and disability. Our new definition of a UTE sign on MRIs provide an early biomarker for disc degeneration.

17117914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117914.value: Fifty to one hundred million people are infected with dengue virus every year resulting in over 25,000 deaths (predominantly children under the age of 14), underscoring our need to better understand its mechanism of pathogenesis. Infection with one serotype confers immunity against the particular serotype while increasing incidence of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) during subsequent infections by other serotypes. DENV is transmitted by mosquito bites, principally of Aedes aegypti and is endemic to over 100 countries around the world, predominantly affecting Southeast Asian countries. The predominant species of mosquito in Hong Kong is Aedes albopictus which is capable of transmitting the disease as exemplified by the incidence of local cases in Hong Kong that have drawn attention to dengue propagation to non endemic regions. The Hong Kong government has launched a campaign with advertisement in public places and residential buildings to spread awareness and caution against the spread of JEV and dengue. There are currently no vaccines available against dengue. A molecular understanding of host cellular factors involved in dengue infection is crucial not only to provide novel insights into pathways hijacked by flaviviruses, but also for development of effective antimicrobials and therapeutic strategies against the pathogen. Identification of host factors that can be targeted for developing novel anti-viral compounds has the additional benefit of avoiding potential resistance acquired in viruses by mutation and selection. The complexity of the assembly and release of dengue virus provides a potentially rich source of host targets for interference. The modus operandi of propagation of Dengue virus (DENV) , West Nile (WNV) and other members of the family appears to be extensive remodeling of the ER to facilitate virus replication, trafficking, assembly and egress. However, we have been severely limited in our understanding of the role of fundamental biological pathways typically hijacked by flaviviruses. 17117914.label: Realisation of objectives
17117914.value: Specific objective 1: To establish a biochemical assay to monitor intracellular trafficking, assembly and release of dengue virus. We completed this section and provided a summary in the previous progress report. We successfully established a biochemical assay to analyze secretion of dengue E-protein, and used this strategy to identify host factors that are important in intracellular dengue virus trafficking. In addition, by using a ubiquitin derived activity based probe that is resistant to hydrolysis by cellular deubiquitylases, we identified proteins that were specifically ubiquitylated upon dengue virus infection versus mock (control). The bands were systematically analyzed by mass spectrometry. Lipid droplet associated proteins, including Aup1 (as described in Aim 2) were categorically identified as the most prominent hits that were differentially modified by ubiquitin using our assay system. In contrast to the other hits, Aup1, which is typically monoUbiquitin modified, was found in the deubiquitylated form upon infection. Amongst the hits that were identified with the activity-based probe, several deubiquitylases (DUBs) were identified in our mass spectrometry dataset. We characterized one of these DUBs, Usp12, in greater detail, which turned out to play a significant role in stabilizing receptors at the cell surface of immune cells. We further analyzed its mechanistic function in T-lymphocytes (where it is expressed to significant levels). Data obtained for this section was accepted for publication in PNAS (Jahan et al, 2016). Specific objective 2: To analyze the role of lipid droplets in dengue virus infection. We analyzed the interactome of Aup1 in mock and dengue infected cells to chart out the pathways that are activated under conditions of infection, using a proximity based labeling assay. We generated a BirA fused construct of Aup1 that was reintroduced into cells lacking Aup1. These cells were either mock infected or challenged with dengue virus and all Aup1 interactors (isolated through biotin modification) were identified using mass spectrometry and further validated by immunoblotting. Aup1 was found to interact predominantly with the lipid droplet and ER machinery under normal physiology, but shifted to interacting with the autophagy machinery upon dengue infection. Loss of Aup1 inhibited virus-induced lipophagy that is crucial for sustaining virus replication. Our results indicate that consumption of lipid droplets through autophagy is essential for generating fatty acids that are necessary for dengue replication. We generated several mutants of Aup1, which could not trigger virus-mediated autophagy and were also deficient in dengue virus production. Data obtained through identification and characterization of Aup1 in the context of lipophagy in dengue virus infection had been submitted for peer-reviewed publication in Cell Host and Microbe and is now accepted. Specific objective 3: To analyse domains of Aup1 that are important for association with dengue NS-proteins. Using the variants of Aup1 containing mutations in its different domains, we determined that dengue NS4A specifically interacts with Aup1. In addition we identified that the ubiquitylated version of Aup1 does not interact with dengue NS4A; however, once deubiquitylated, the NS4A-Aup1 interaction results in activation of the acyltransferase enzymatic activity of Aup1. This presumably enables the formation of viral replication compartments through supplying the appropriate lipid components, while facilitating replication through the β-oxidation of fatty acids that are formed upon lipophagy. Results obtained from this section have also been accepted in Cell Host and Microbe. A review summarizing these data and the involvement of lipid droplets in flavivirus infections have been accepted in Frontiers in Microbiology, with a second one in process in Frontiers in Immunology. All the stated objectives have been achieved as planned, except generation of a knock-out mouse as this is being conducted in our collaborator's laboratory. All of the data generated in this proposal have now been accepted into two manuscripts in PNAS and Cell Host and Microbe. In addition a summary of research findings has been accepted in an invited review in Frontiers of Microbiology, and a second one that is being reviewed in Frontiers in Immunology.
