17117914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117914.value: Specific objective 1: To establish a biochemical assay to monitor intracellular trafficking, assembly and release of dengue virus. This aim has been successfully completed. We established a biochemical assay to analyze secretion of dengue E-protein, and used this strategy to identify host factors that are important in intracellular dengue virus trafficking. A modified E-protein was created for transducing into cells that could be analyzed for its trafficking characteristics through pulse-chase assays. In addition, by using a ubiquitin derived activity based probe that is resistant to hydrolysis by cellular deubiquitylases, we identified proteins that are modified upon dengue virus infection versus mock (control). Amongst the hits that were identified with the activity-based probe, several deubiquitylases (DUBs) were identified in our mass spectrometry dataset. We characterized one of these DUBs, Usp12, in greater detail, which turned out to play a significant role in stabilizing receptors at the cell surface of immune cells. We further analyzed its mechanistic function in T-lymphocytes (where it is expressed to significant levels). Data obtained for this section was accepted for publication in PNAS (Jahan et al, 2016). Specific objective 2: To analyze the role of lipid droplets in dengue virus infection. We have successfully completed this aim. We analyzed the interactome of Aup1 in mock and dengue infected cells to chart out the pathways that are activated under conditions of infection, using a proximity based labeling assay. Aup1 was found to interact predominantly with the lipid droplet and ER machinery under normal physiology, but shifted to interacting with the autophagy machinery upon dengue infection. We created Aup1 knock-out cells using CRISPR/Cas9. Loss of Aup1 inhibited virus-induced lipophagy that is crucial for sustaining virus replication. Our results indicate that consumption of lipid droplets through autophagy is essential for generating fatty acids that are necessary for dengue replication. Data obtained through identification and characterization of Aup1 in the context of lipophagy in dengue virus infection had been submitted for peer-reviewed publication in Cell Host and Microbe and is now accepted. Specific objective 3: To analyse domains of Aup1 that are important for association with dengue NS-proteins. Using the variants of Aup1 containing mutations in its different domains, we determined that dengue NS4A specifically interacts with Aup1. In addition we identified that the ubiquitylated version of Aup1 does not interact with dengue NS4A; however, once deubiquitylated, the NS4A-Aup1 interaction results in activation of the acyltransferase enzymatic activity of Aup1. Results obtained from this section have also been accepted in Cell Host and Microbe. A review summarizing these data and the involvement of lipid droplets in flavivirus infections have been accepted in Frontiers in Microbiology, with a second one in process in Frontiers in Immunology. Results obtained from this proposal have been presented at various international conferences.

17117914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117914.value: In this proposal we investigated the role of host lipid metabolism in dengue virus infection, which we have alread extended to other flaviviruses to test whether this is a universal phenomenon. We have started unravelling the involvement of lipid utilization in virus infections, especially how cholesterol homeostasis is perturbed. Apart from providing important insights into cholesterol metabolism, this has significant therapeutic potential, because of the availability of small molecule inhibitors that are already available for targeting this pathway without causing toxicity in the host.

17117914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117914.value: Through this proposal we identified a crucial link between dengue virus mediated utilization of host lipid metabolic pathways for facilitating virus replication. We determined that upon infection, DENV nonstructural proteins interact with Aup1, which is a lipid droplet associated protein. This interaction results in activation of the acyltransferase function of Aup1, and a subsequent "switching on" of the autophagy pathway to generate fatty acids necessary for energy production. Loss of Aup1 or expression of mutant variants in cells that do not associate with DENV NS-proteins become resistant to dengue production. This appears to be largely due to the inability of dengue virus particles to co-opt the lipophagy pathway in the absence of Aup1. This finding is particularly significant in terms of defining perturbations in host metabolic network upon virus infections, but perhaps more importantly, in emphasizing the possibility of pharmacological interventions by repurposing available drugs such as statins that are in clinical use. Data generated in the course of this project resulted in three manuscripts that have been accepted for publication, including one which was published in PNAS in 2016, one accepted in Frontiers in Microbiology (2017) and another in Cell Host and Microbe (2017). In addition, a second invited review has been submitted in Frontiers in Immunology.

17118014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118014.value: Next-generation sequencing technologies are revolutionizing our understanding of the evolution of floral morphology by enabling the identification of the diversity of genes involved and their complex interactions. The proposed research focuses on the Annonaceae, which as a family of early-divergent angiosperms is of particular importance in providing insights into the early evolutionary diversification of floral morphology. The perianth in Annonaceae flowers consists of differentiated sepals and petals, often with morphologically distinct inner and outer petals; the petals are hypothesised to be of bracteal origin, and hence the organ distinctions in the Annonaceae presumably evolved independently of those in eudicots, in which petals are generally derived from stamens. The proposed research aims to identify candidate genes responsible for variation in floral morphologies in selected Annonaceae species using quantitative transcriptome analysis. We will then evaluate the spatial and temporal patterns of gene expression across the floral meristem and their functions during floral development. The research will test hypotheses that changes in the expression or function of genes controlling floral development are responsible for phenotypic differences observed in different species. The morphological differentiation of distinct perianth whorls is likely to represent a key evolutionary innovation, enabling the formation of highly complex pollination chambers that are of functional significance in effecting pollination. The research interface between evolutionary and developmental biology (‘evo-devo’) has attracted considerable attention due to our increasing understanding of phylogenetic relationships and the functional role of gene expression during development. The current proposal incorporates research into floral phenology, pollination ecology and plant breeding systems, thereby achieving an integrative ‘eco-evo-devo’ approach. The proposed research will detect candidate genes involved in perianth differentiation of exemplar Annonaceae, address gene orthologies against publicly available genomes, and start to understand gene function through gene expression analysis. We have the following specific objectives: (1) to identify candidate genes for selected genera that exhibit different degrees of perianth differentiation (Anaxagorea, Friesodielsia, Goniothalamus and Uvaria); (2) to investigate whether the petal loss in Dasymaschalon is due to changes in the timing or spatial location of gene expression and to understand the origin and homology of remaining petals; (3) to test the hypothesis that the sepaloid outer petals in Meiogyne bidwillii are the result of a homeotic transformation from the ancestral petaloid condition; and (4) to evaluate the functional significance of morphological changes in the flower by comparative studies of the floral phenology, pollination ecology and breeding systems of studied species. 新一代測序技術通過鑑定遗传多样性及其複雜的相互作用革新了我們對花卉形態進化的理解。本研究計畫的目標類群為番荔枝科，屬於基部被子植物，故有助了解花卉形態的早期演化 。 番荔枝科花的花被由不同形態的萼片和內、外花瓣組成，其形態分化有別於真雙子葉植物的花器官分化，因此被推测為趨同進化的產物。 本研究計畫將針對選定的番荔枝科品種以轉錄組數據分析來分離與鑑定影響番荔枝科花形態變化的候選基因，並分析該候選基因的功能與時空方式表達。本研究計畫將假設檢驗問題中由相關候選基因的表達和功能的不同導致在選定品種中的表型差異。 花萼和花冠的形態差異及由內外花瓣形成的花授粉室可能是進化中關鍵的創新， 此形態變化有助於花的授粉過程。本研究計畫在已知的系統關係、繁育系統，傳粉生態，生殖構件與基因表達功能的基礎知識上融合了進化和發育生物學以達對課題全面和深入的了解。 本研究計畫將分離和鑑定選定的番荔枝科品種中有關花被形態分化的候選基因，透過差異基因表達和BLAST同源分析尋找相關的同源基因和其功能。

17118314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118314.value: 在神經系統的發育過程中，於特定部位產生數量合適並功能特異的神經元對於大腦功能起著至關重要的作用。早期發育過程中，多重信號通路的共同調控著神經前體細胞的增殖和分化。尤其對於中樞神經系統來說，Sonic hedgehog (Shh)信號確定了神經前體細胞族群和它們的細胞命運。這裡我們提出Suppressor of fused (Sufu) 在調節Shh信號和其他信號通路從而維持神經前體細胞中扮演著重要角色。 Sufu基因編碼了一個可與Gli蛋白互相作用同時負調控Shh信號通路的細胞內蛋白。另一方面，我們和其他研究者發現了Sufu蛋白也與β-catenin 及GSK3β有著相互作用，進而調控Wnt/β-catenin信號的響應。目前還不明確Sufu如何在活體內協調多重信號因數間的特異相互作用從而控制神經前體細胞的增殖和分化。 我們採用後腦神經發生在轉錄層面的控制為模型，也說明了Gli2/3在控制神經元命運的關鍵性轉錄調控因數。為了研究Sufu在控制神經前體細胞的模式建成、增殖及分化中的作用，我們構建了特異性Sufu基因敲除小鼠(Sufu-Cr4)。初步分析表明Sufu-Cr4突變體增大神經前體細胞區域及異常的細胞週期過程。此外，通過遺傳學手段，我們發現在複合突變體中，敲除Gli2和β-catenin基因可以部分緩解Sufu-Cr4突變體的神經前體細胞表型。我們的結果指出通過共同調節Shh/Gli和Wnt/β-catenin信號通路，Sufu以一個區域特定性的方式控制著神經前體細胞的增殖和分化。 我們現階段的假設是：在神經前體細胞中，Sufu抑制Gli2和β-catenin但促進GSK3β的功能。本專案的目標是發掘Sufu在調節多種信號通路因數從而控制後腦神經前體細胞中的角色。使用遺傳學和分子生物學方法，我們將破譯在維持神經前體細胞中Sufu調控的基因作用的層級關係。

17118314.label: Realisation of objectives
17118314.value: Objective 1. To investigate the interactions of Sufu with Gli2 and Gli3 in regulating domain-specific neural progenitor proliferation and differentiation In this study, we investigated the neural progenitor phenotypes of the SufuCr4 mutants and found that Sufu is required to control the dorsoventral patterning of progenitor domains in hindbrain r4. As a major phenotype of the SufuCr4 mutant was an enlarged r4 with increased number of Sox2+ progenitors, we investigated the regulation of cell proliferation. We carried out a series of BrdU labelling experiments over the time course of neural progenitor proliferation from E9.5 to E12.5, and performed an in-depth in vivo cell cycle progression analysis together with mathematical modelling. We found that deletion of Sufu did not cause a faster cell cycle progression. On the contrary, a mild increase of cell cycle duration was observed in every domain examined (14 hr to 15 hr). There was also a notable lengthening of S phase duration in Sufu mutant brain compared to control (5.5 hr to 7 hr). Furthermore, by 24h long pulse BrdU incorporation assay and co-immunostaining of BrdU and Ki67, we found that in the SufuCr4 mutant the dorsal cells displayed significantly reduced cell cycle exit as compared to control. By gene expression analysis, we found that a panel of cell cycle regulator genes including Ccnd2, Ccna2, Ccnb2, Ccne2, N-myc, Chk1, Hes1, p21 were up-regulated, suggesting altered cell cycle kinetics and neurogenesis in the Sufu mutant brain. To examine whether Sufu could regulate the mode of divisions, a pair cell assay platform was adopted using single cells dissociated from the r4 brain. Our results showed that in the absence of Sufu, symmetrical neural progenitor divisions were enhanced and neuronal cell divisions were reduced. The expression of proneural genes such as Mash1 were delayed in Sufu mutant. These results were further confirmed using Sufu knockout P19 embryonal carcinoma cell lines. To address whether alteration of Gli expressions could account for the phenotype of SufuCr4 mutants, we examined the phenotypes of Gli2 and Gli3 mutants. While Gli3d699 ⁄ d699 mutant r4 was unaffected, removal of Sufu in the Gli3d699 ⁄ d699 background could partially restore the expansion of Nkx6.1+, Pax6+ domains, suggesting that the expansion of Nkx6.1+ domain was due to dys-regulation of Gli3 repressors. Analysis of SufuCr4;Gli2-/- double mutants showed that removal of Gli2 could alleviate the phenotype of SufuCr4 mutants, as demonstrated by the reduction of Nkx2.2 and Nkx6.1 progenitors and recovery of Tuj1+ differentiated neurons. Therefore, the phenotype observed in Sufu mutants has reflected a combinatorial requirement of Gli2 and Gli3 during r4 neural patterning. Here we have completed the study described in Objective 1. Objective 2. To investigate the role of β-catenin in the function of Sufu in hindbrain neural progenitor patterning, proliferation and differentiation To study the role of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in the functioning of Sufu, we investigated conditional knock-out mutant of β-catenin. We found an expansion of Tuj1+ population at the expense of Sox2+ neural progenitors in β-cateninCr4 mutant embryos. Although the expression of progenitor patterning genes including Nkx2.2, Nkx6.1, Pax6 and Pax7 appeared unaffected in the mutants, the neural progenitors were disorganized along the ventricular layer. As loss of Sufu in the SufuCr4 mutant would lead to an increase in the protein amount and nuclear localization of active β-catenin, we tested whether ectopic activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling also contributed to the r4 phenotype of SufuCr4 mutant. By analysis of SufuCr4;β-cateninCr4 compound mutant, we found that Sox2+ neural progenitors were reduced in number and formed abnormal clusters similar to those seen in β-cateninCr4. Cell cycle analysis showed partial recovery of proliferation and cell cycle exit defects in the compound mutants. Interestingly, concomitant deletion of β-catenin in SufuCr4 mutant resulted in a more ventralized r4 than those found in the Sufu or β-catenin single mutants, as revealed by the reduction of the ventral Nkx2.2+ and Nkx6.1+ domains. To mimic the nuclear accumulation of β-catenin observed in Sufu mutants, we used a gain-of-function approach and generated a conditional mutant with stabilization of β-catenin in r4 (β-cateninCr4-Ex3). The β-cateninCr4-Ex3 mutant displayed an expansion of neuroepithelium similar to SufuCr4, Sox2+ progenitors were expanded, neuronal differentiation was inhibited. Furthermore, SufuCr4;β-cateninCr4-Ex3 compound mutants displayed exercebated cell cycle exit defects. Interestingly, progenitor patterning genes Nkx2.2, Pax6 were not expressed in β-cateninCr4-Ex3 mutant r4, while Nkx6.1 and Pax7 remained, and the dorsal Msx1 domain expanded ventrally. These data suggested that a proper level of β-catenin was required for progenitor domain patterning and maintenance in the hindbrain. Taken together, our results indicated that β-catenin level is critical for the establishment of neural progenitor domains in r4 and a convergent regulation of neural progenitor cell cycle exit by β-catenin and Sufu are required along the dorsoventral domains in hindbrain r4. Here we have completed the study described in Objective 2. Objective 3. To investigate the role of Sufu in the crosstalk of multiple signaling factors and elucidate the hierarchy of Sufu-mediated genetic interactions in hindbrain neural progenitor maintenance In this part of the study, we aim to elucidate how Sufu, a negative regulator of mammalian hedgehog signaling, cross-talk with other signaling factors in the maintenance of neural progenitor domains in r4. Based on results obtained in Objectives 1 & 2, we concluded that the regulation of Sufu, and β-catenin in specific context, mainly converged on the control of Gli factors. Therefore, we investigated the modulation of Gli factors by analysis of Spop (Speckle-type poz protein), an adapter protein required for E3 ubiquitin complex that is responsible for the degradation of Gli2 and Gli3, using the Spop mouse mutant. Our phenotype analysis of conditional Spop mutant showed that r4Cre;Sufuf ⁄ f;Spopf ⁄ f mutant r4 was further expanded along the dorsoventral domains, with a significant expansion of Sox2+ progenitor population, while Tuj1+ differentiated cells were much reduced when compared to control and SufuCr4 brains. Severe patterning defects were also observed, both Nkx2.2 and Nkx6.1 domains were dramatically expanded, along with a reduction of Pax6 and Pax7 domains, indicating a severe ventralization phenotype when both Sufu and Spop were removed. Moreover, cell proliferation and cell cycle exit were further exacerbated in the dorsal Pax6+ cells of the r4Cre;Sufuf ⁄ f;Spopf ⁄ f mutants. By in situ hybridization we examined the expression patterns of Gli1/2/3 in SufuCr4 and r4Cre;Sufuf ⁄ f;Spopf ⁄ f mutant r4. Interestingly, although Gli1/2 could be detected in the ventral midline of the hindbrain region at early stages (4-5 somites), they were not found in the ventral hindbrain from 7-8 somites onwards in normal and mutant hindbrains. We found that Gli1, the direct transcriptional target of Hedgehog signaling, was dramatically up-regulated from E10.5 in the intermediate to dorsal regions of both SufuCr4 and r4Cre;Sufuf ⁄ f;Spopf ⁄ f mutant r4. The expression of Gli2 and Gli3 were dorsally shifted and absent in ventral region in both single and compound mutant r4. The shift of Gli expressions were consistent with the patterning marker expression changes in Sufu and Spop mutant brains. As r4Cre;Spopf ⁄ f embryos showed no apparent phenotype compared to normal embryos, we conclude that Sufu and Spop genetically interact to define neural progenitor proliferation in developing r4 by controlling the availability of Gli factors. Here we have completed the study in Objective 3.

We showed that Sufu mutant progenitors had prolonged cell cycle length and S phase duration. Moreover, Sufu mutation promoted symmetric proliferative divisions of neural progenitors. In Sufu mutants, neural progenitors prolonged their progenitor state, with a concomitant delay in cell cycle exit and commitment to neural differentiation. We further confirmed this result in Sufu knockout mutant P19 embryonic carcinoma cell lines, in which compromised neuronal specification was observed when compared to control. We have reported these findings in the manuscript by Pan et al. (see Part C). 2. The phenotype in neural progenitor maintenance varied in Sufu mutant r4 at different dorsal-ventral domains and we investigated the roles of Gli factors in mediating the domain specific neurogenesis phenotypes. We demonstrated the expression of Gli factors during early hindbrain development. By compound mutant analyses we showed that conditional removal of Gli2 or forced expression of Gli3 repressors could counteract Sufu mutant r4 progenitor patterning and maintenance phenotypes. Moreover, removal of Spop, a positive regulator of Gli degradation, could exacerbate the phenotype in Sufu mutant r4. Our study revealed that the neural progenitor domain specific phenotype of Sufu mutants at different DV level of r4 were dependent on the availability of Gli activators and repressors during r4 neurogenesis. We have reported these findings in the manuscript by Pan et al. (see Part C). 3. We have investigated the crosstalk between Sufu/Shh signaling and β-catenin/Wnt signaling during hindbrain neurogenesis. Using both loss-of-function and gain-of-function mouse models of β-catenin, and in combination with Sufu and Gli2/3 mutant studies, we showed that Sufu and β-catenin displayed specific as well as coordinated functions in hindbrain neurogenesis. Stabilization of β-catenin caused increased Sox2+ neural progenitor proliferation and decreased cell cycle exit, similar to Sufu mutants. However, suppression of Pax6 and Neurogenins, the major neurogenic factors during brain development, were observed in β-catenin mutants but not in Sufu mutants. These results suggest that β-catenin has independent functions in regulating proliferation and differentiation of hindbrain neural progenitors. We presented these findings in the ISSCR2016 conference.

17118314.value: 1. In our analysis of the gain-of-function and loss-of-function β-catenin mutants, we have discovered that β-catenin has distinctive functions in hindbrain neurogenesis along the entire dorsoventral domains. We also observed specific regulation of the Pax6 gene by β-catenin. The functions of β-catenin and Wnt signaling in hindbrain neurogenesis require further investigations. 2. While this study focused on hindbrain rhombomere 4 as a defined system to investigate the the regulatory roles of Sufu, Spop, β-catenin and Gli factors, the functional roles of these signaling factors in other regions of the hindbrain require further investigations. 3. With the advancement in single cell technologies, query into the single cell transcriptome and epigenome of neural differentiation processes with normal and aberrant Hh signaling pathways will shed light on our understanding of molecular signaling pathways in neurogenesis. 17118314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118314.value: Proper formation of a functional brain requires coordinated progenitor proliferation and cell fate specification that contribute to the final numbers of neurons with different subtypes. In this study, by genetics, cellular and molecular analyses, we demonstrated that Suppressor of fused (Sufu) and Gli signaling regulate neural progenitor patterning and proliferation in mouse hindbrain rhombomere 4. We performed in vivo cell cycle kinetics analysis and showed that Sufu controls cell cycle progression and cell cycle exit in a neural domain specific manner. Moreover, progenitor proliferation and cell cycle exit could be restored by genetic ablation of Gli2; or be exacerbated by knock-out of Spop, which encoded an adaptor protein of the E3 ubiquitin complex required for Gli turnover. By compound mutant analysis, we demonstrated the intricate interactions between β-catenin and Sufu mediated signaling in the control of hindbrain neural progenitor maintenance, novel functions of β-catenin in hindbrain patterning gene expressions were identified. Collectively, our data highlighted the importance of Sufu-Gli signaling axis in defining regional cell proliferation regulations in mouse hindbrain development. As mutations in SUFU are associated with human patients with cerebellum defects, this study has contributed to our understanding of the human disease mechanisms.

17118514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118514.value: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease but its underlying mechanisms are unclear yet. Current therapies have no expected achievement so far. Thus, development of new molecular targets are timely important for MS treatment. Experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) is a laboratory-induced animal model mediated by antigen-specific CD4+ T lymphocytes, which is a reliable and well-established animal model for MS study. The EAE pathological processes include T lymphocytes infiltration, brain-blood barrier (BBB) disruption and demyelination. In the process, T lymphocytes infiltration and migration from peripheral blood into central nerve system (CNS) is the early and critical step, but the mechanisms of T cells infiltration into the CNS remain to be addressed. T lymphocytes migration is closely related with brain vascular endothelial cells in microenvironment. As a major trans-membrane protein, caveolin-1 (cav-1) is abundantly expressed in endothelial cells. Previous reports showed that expression and phosphorylation of cav-1 were increased in the spinal cord of EAE animal model and phosphorylated cav-1 affected cell shape and leukocytes migration. Therefore, cav-1 could be a potential signaling molecule contributing to leukocytes infiltration across the BBB in EAE. Subsequently we conducted pilot studies to explore the roles of cav-1 in the EAE animal model. Our preliminary data showed that cav-1 deficiency mice had less disease symptoms and incidence rates, less demyelination in spinal cord and less T lymphocytes infiltrated into the CNS than wild type mice in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG35-55)-induced active EAE model. In this proposal,accordingly, we hypothesize that cav-1 could play an important role in T lymphocytes infiltration into the CNS, leading demyelination and cell death in MS pathology. We will conduct a series of experiments coached by three specific objectives: (1) To test the hypothesis that cav-1 deficiency could reduce disease incidence, symptom severity and demyelination through limiting CNS-directed pathogenic CD4+ T lymphocyte infiltration into the CNS in MOG35-55 induced active EAE mice model in vivo; (2) To investigate whether endothelial cav-1 contributes to the CNS-directed pathogenic CD4+ T cells trans-endothelial migration into the CNS during EAE pathological process; (3) To investigate the roles of cav-1 in CD4+ T lymphocyte for its trans-endothelial migration during EAE. With the related expertises in the research team and preliminary data in pilot study, we expect to verify the hypothesis. Eventually we will advance current knowledge about pathological mechanisms of MS and caveolin-1 could be a novel molecular target for drug discovery in multiple sclerosis treatment. 多發性硬化症是自身免疫性疾病，其發病機製不清，臨床治療效果不理想。實驗性自身免疫性腦髓鞘炎是多發性硬化症的實驗動物模型，是由T淋巴細胞透過血腦屏障介導形成的。其病理過程包括T淋巴細胞浸潤、血腦屏障損害、脫髓鞘病變為特徵。其中T淋巴細胞由外周血進入中樞神經系統是關鍵的病理環節。 血管內皮細胞及其微環境是實驗性自身免疫性腦髓鞘炎病變過程中T淋巴細胞浸潤的重要影響因素，小凹蛋白在內皮細胞高表達是重要的膜轉運蛋白，研究表明實驗性自身免疫性腦髓鞘炎病變過程中脊髓中小凹蛋白表達增加，且小凹蛋白磷酸化增強，影響白細胞遷移，該蛋白在疾病過程中可能有重要影響，有待深入研究，為此我們開展了初步實驗，結果表明：(1) 小凹蛋白基因敲除鼠的發病率和症狀嚴重程度明顯減輕；(2) 其臨床症狀的減輕與脫髓鞘程度輕微有關；(3) 小凹蛋白基因敲除鼠顯示有比較少的T淋巴細胞進入中樞神經系統。因此我們假設小凹蛋白可能是治療多發性硬化症的重要生物靶標，本課題針對小凹蛋白為中心環節設計了一系列實驗證明小凹蛋白在T淋巴細胞透過血腦屏障跨膜轉運及在多發性硬化症發病中的作用，本研究將為多發性硬化治療提供新的思路。

17118514.label: Realisation of objectives
17118514.value: Based on the main objectives of the project, we conducted a series of in vivo and in vitro experiments to demonstrate the role of caveolin-1 in the pathogenesis of EAE and in regulating immune cells trafficking into the CNS tissues during neuroinflammation. We have reached all of the goals in the original proposal. The research work mainly fulfills three objectives previously claimed in this project including (1) the roles of cav-1 during EAE pathogenesis; (2) the effects of endothelial cav-1 on T lymphocytes extravasations into the CNS during the process of active EAE; and (3) the functions of cav-1 on regulating T lymphocytes during EAE pathogenesis and trans-endothelial migration (TEM). Major discoveries of the project are summarized as below: Objective 1: To test the hypothesis that cav-1 deficiency attenuated EAE induced disease incidences, neurological deficit symptoms, oligodendrocyte death and demyelination through affecting T lymphocytes extravasation into the CNS In the EAE pathogenesis, the expression of caveolin-1 in serum and spinal cord tissues were dramatically increased, whose maximum level was coincident with the EAE severity in wild-type mice. In agreement with this, caveolin-1 KO mice were largely protected from active EAE induction with the alleviated EAE incidence, the delayed onset and the reduced severity of neurological deficit symptoms, the reduced oligodendrocyte death, demyelination and microglial activation in the white matter of spinal cord and cerebellum. Thus, those discoveries suggest that caveolin-1 contributes to the EAE pathogenesis. Objective 2: To test the hypothesis that endothelial cav-1 contributes to the process of active EAE by affecting T lymphocytes extravasations into the CNS We found that the effects of caveolin-1 deficiency was not due to the down-regulation of immune cells activation in the peripheral lymphoid tissues but related to the limited primed pathological immune cells diapedesis into the CNS lesions. By IHC staining and flow cytometry, we verified that Caveolin-1 KO mice had less frequencies of encephalitogenic T cells, specifically antigen specific TH1 and TH17 effector cells in the CNS white matter parenchyma, which was highly coincidence with the EAE resistance observed. In the CNS tissues, caveolin-1 was predominantly localized on the CNS vascular endothelium and its expression was increased on CNS derived microvessels after actively immunization, suggesting the effects of the endothelial caveolin-1 on T lymphocytes extravasations into the CNS during EAE pathology. Therefore, caveolin-1 play essential roles in the events of the formations of EAE lesions, including inflammatory infiltration, demyelination and glial cell activations during EAE. Then, we established ex vivo co-culture system and demonstrated that losses of caveolin-1 on endothelial cells partially compromised the transmigration of encephalitogenic T cells, specially polarized TH1 and TH17 cells in vitro. Taken together, we conclude that endothelial caveolin-1 could be essential for the recruitment of encephalitogenic CD4 + T cells, specifically TH1 and TH17 cells, into the CNS parenchyma. Objective 3: To investigate the function of cav-1 in T lymphocytes during EAE pathogenesis and trans-endothelial migration (TEM) We further investigated the molecular basis of endothelial caveolin-1 in regulating lymphocytes trans-migration. We found a sharply increase in the expressions of adhesion molecules ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 at the site of inflammatory sites within EAE lesions in the white matter of spinal cord and cerebellum of the WT mice. Consistently, caveolin-1 knockout mice had significantly reduced expressions of adhesion molecule ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 within CNS lesions. In vitro knockdown of caveolin-1 on endothelial cells also impaired the up-regulation of ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expressions, indicating that the caveolin-1 presented on endothelial cells was essential for the inflammatory induced up-regulations of ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expressions, a prerequisite of immune cells trafficking. Furthermore, we found that emodin, natural anthraquinone compound actively modulated caveolin-1 expressions with CNS lesions after EAE induction. The underlying mechanisms of emodin could be related to alleviate EAE development with attenuation of inflammatory responses both at the periphery and CNS tissues. In conclusion, we demonstrate that caveolin-1 deficiency could lead to EAE resistance via limiting encephalitogenic T cells trafficking into the CNS by modulating adhesion molecules ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. This study highlights a critical role of caveolin-1 in CNS-directed lymphocyte diapedesis and may implicate it as a potential molecular and therapeutic target in neuroinflammatory diseases.

17118514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118514.value: We have made following progress and had the major discoveries in the project: (1) Caveolin-1 deficiency attenuates EAE disease incidences, neurological deficit symptoms, oligodendrocyte death and demyelination through affecting T lymphocytes extravasation into the CNS; (2) Endothelial caveolin-1 contributes to the process of active EAE by affecting T lymphocytes extravasations into the CNS; (3) Caveolin-1 plays critical role in encephalitogenic lymphocyte trafficking into CNS by targeting ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. The study brings novel insight into understanding the mechanisms of caveolin-1 in modulating lymphocyte trafficking during EAE/MS pathology. More importantly, targeting caveolin-1 could be a potential molecular and therapeutic target in neuroinflammatory diseases, which could be a new area for drug discovery. Particularly, emodin, a natural compound from TCM, showed beneficial disease outcomes for EAE partially though down-regulating caveolin-1 expression in the CNS lesion, which provides a new cue of how synergistic actions of emodin are necessary for the treatment of those highly complicated autoimmune disorders such as EAE and MS.

17118514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118514.value: Current and merging therapeutic approaches for multiple sclerosis (MS) treatment are not satisfactory. Developing new molecular targets for drug discovery is critical and timely important. Our research proposed a novel mechanism of T lymphocytes infiltration from periphery into CNS and found that a membrane protein named caveolin-1 could be an attractive therapeutic target to reduce inflammatory mediators and attenuate the pathological process of CNS autoimmunity, demyelination and even oligodendrocyte death in MS. Our study greatly advances current knowledge about the pathological basis of MS. Moreover, we bring new insights on two new research directions: [1] studying endothelial caveolin-1 as therapeutic target for drug discovery to attenuating immune cell infiltration into the CNS for MS treatment; [2] conducting clinical trials on MS human subjects with potentials to develop novel MS diagnostic methods by collaborating with neurologists.

17118514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118514.value: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease. The hallmark feature of neuroinflammatory diseases is the massive infiltrations of encephalitogenic leukocytes into the CNS parenchyma, a process that remains largely unclear. Current therapies have no expected achievement so far. Thus, development of new molecular target is timely important for MS treatment. T lymphocytes migration in EAE is closely related with endothelial cells at the microenvironment. Caveolin-1 (cav-1) is one of major trans-membrane protein which abundantly expressed in endothelial cells. Our study demonstrates the critical contribution of caveolin-1 to encephalomyelitis pathogenesis and CNS-directed lymphocyte trafficking by modulation of adhesion molecules ICAM-1 and VCAM-1, highlighting the pathological involvement of caveolin-1inneuroinflammatory diseases. The discovery also indicates that caveolin-1 serves as an active modulator of CNS directed lymphocyte trafficking and could be a therapeutic target for neuroinflammatory diseases, such as multiple sclerosis.

17118914.label: Realisation of objectives
17118914.value: For objective one, we have shown that small clones of FLT3-ITD existed before azacitidine treatment and became significant upon azacitidine failure. This was shown by the following findings: 1. Serial molecular evaluation showed increased frequency of FLT3-ITD in patients failing treatment with hypomethylating agents (HMA). A database of 288 patients with MDS over 15 years were studied. Clinicopathologic features, treatment and outcome were reviewed. 80 patients with MDS developed secondary AML. By conventional PCR, FLT3-ITD was present in 8 patients at the diagnosis of MDS=8 (2.8%) and 16 patients with with secondary AML=16 (20% of sAML). 6 patients had prior HMA use. In non-HMA group (N=43), 8 patients had FLT3-ITD and MDS and sAML stage. In HMA group (N=26), no patients had FLT3-ITD at MDS stage and 8 patients “acquired” FLT3-ITD at sAML stage. HMA use significantly associated with FLT3-ITD “acquisition” (P=0.021). 2. Clonospecific FLT3-PCR showed the presence of small clone of FLT3-ITD present at MDS stage may have emerged during HMA failure. By comparing the FLT3 ITD sequences with the wild type FLT3, clonal-specific PCR primers were designed which one of the each primer set (either forward or reverse primer) spanned the ITD region and WT sequence.4 patients showing azacitidine failure and FLT3-ITD at AML stage were evaluated. These patients were FLT3-WT by conventional PCR at MDS stage. Clonospecific PCR showed the presence of FLT3-ITD at the MDS stage in these patients. This implied that patients in patients with MDS small clones harboring FLT3-ITD, emergence of selection of FLT3-ITD+ clones may occur during HMA treated and lead to treatment resistance and disease progression to AML. 3.The use of FLT3 inhibitor (sorafenib) with azacitidine induced responses in patients failing treatment. The combination of sorafenib with azacitidine was shown to be synergistic in vitro in FLT3-ITD+ AML cell lines. That was also confirmed in a xenograft model. Clinically the combination of sorafenib and azacitidine improved responses and survivals in patients in patients with MDS failing HMA and harbouring FLT3-ITD. This work was published as “Gill H, Man CH, Ip AH, Choi WW, Chow HC, Kwong YL, Leung AY. Azacitidine as post-remission consolidation for sorafenib-induced remission of Fms-like tyrosine kinase-3 internal tandem duplication positive acute myeloid leukemia. Haematologica 2015; 100(7): e250-3.” [2017 Impact factor:9.09] For objective number two, an in-vitro model of azacitidine-resistent MDS was developed. P39 cell line (in-vitro model of myelodysplastic syndrome) treated continuously with escalating doses of azacitidine starting at 1nM and P39 resistant to azacitidine was generated with an IC50 of 10 times more than azacitidine sensitive P39 . Azacitidine resistant P39 (AZA-R) and azacitidine sensitive P39 (AZA-S) were both FLT3-WT. This showed that FLT3-ITD was not an acquired mutation in an in-vitro model of azacitidine resistant MDS. We were unable to demonstrate differences in leukemia-initiating activity using this model.

17118914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118914.value: In short, our project demonstrated that the presence of a mutation called FLT3-ITD in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) as a cause of failure of standard frontline treatment with the hypomethylating agent azacitidine. 17119514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119514.value: Hirschsprung’s (HSCR) disease is a congenital disorder of the colon in which certain nerve cells are absent due to incomplete colonization of bowel with enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), causing functional intestinal obstruction. Phenotypic severity is classified according to the length of the aganglionic segment. RET/GDNF signaling is crucial for ENCC development and RET is the most predominant susceptibility gene for HSCR. Genetic variant/mutations in coding (CD) and non-coding (NCD) regions of RET are respectively associated with the severe (total colonic aganglionosis, TCA) and mild (short segment, S-HSCR) forms of HSCR. In addition, many of these genetic lesions directly lead to reduced or defective RET/GDNF signaling, suggesting that these variant/mutations may impair NCC development. However, whether these RET CD and NCD variant/mutations affect a particular NCC developmental process (proliferation, migration, differentiation); and to what extent does RET mutational profile of the patient affect NCC development and the disease severity, have yet to be fully understood. We have established and characterized two induced pluripotent stem cell (HSCR-iPSC) lines from patients who presented with S-HSCR and TCA, respectively harboring RET NCD and CD variant/mutations. NCCs derived from the HSCR-iPSC line carrying RET NCD showed defects in migration and neuronal differentiation, accompanied by a differentiation bias towards the glial lineage. Importantly, the expression of genes involved in migration, neuronal and glial differentiation was dysregulated, and RET expression was reduced. In addition, early NCC development defects and impaired RET expression were observed in another iPSC line from a TCA HSCR patient carrying RET CD mutation. These observations prompted us to hypothesize that RET CD and NCD variant/mutations may cause NCC-specific defects in a cell-autonomous manner, contributing to disease severity. In this project, we propose to (i) study if RET CD mutations impair NCC development using isogenic human embryonic stem cell (ESC) lines that carry HSCR relevant RET CD mutations; (ii) establish the causal link between the impaired RET/GDNF signalling and NCC defects using HSCR-iPSC and hESC; and (iii) demonstrate the relevance of a RET CD mutation on NCC defects by generating a "disease corrected" HSCR-iPSC using CRISPR genome-editing platform. In summary, the data from this study will address how RET mutations affect human NCC development. This proof-of-concept study will provide a foundation for using stem cell-based model to unveil the genetic basis of HSCR, with a long-term goal of hastening the clinical application of hESC/iPSC in reconstructive medicine. 先天性巨結腸病（HSCR）是一種先天性疾病。由於腸神經嵴細胞不能完全定植結腸，導致腸道缺乏神經細胞， 引起功能性的腸梗阻。 嚴重程度是根據無神經節段的長短分類。 RET/ GDNF信號是腸神經嵴細胞發育的關鍵，其中，RET 是致病的最主要基因。 RET遺傳基因突變可發生在編碼（CD）或非編碼（NCD）區域。編碼區的突變／變異會引致結腸完全缺乏神經細胞（TCA），情況一般十分嚴重。如在非編碼區，病程會比較輕微，只有短段的腸道沒有神經細胞（S-HSCR）。此外，這些基因突變／變異都會直接影響RET/ GDNF信號， 損害神經嵴細胞的發育。不過， 我們對這些RET CD和NCD的基因變異是怎樣影響神經嵴細胞的增殖，遷移，分化 ; 以及病程， 還沒有充分的了解。 我們已從兩個分別帶有RET NCD和CD 基因變異／突變的S-HSCR和TCA患者中提取細胞，並建立誘導性幹細胞（HSCR-IPSC）。同時，我們發現從帶有NCD基因變異的HSCR-iPSC 分化出來的神經嵴細胞都有遷移和分化缺陷，它們大都只能分化成神經膠質細胞。重要的是，與神經元和神經膠質細胞分化相關基因的表達都失調，而RET的表達也減少。此外，從觀察另一個帶有RET CD 基因變異的iPSC，我們發現 RET無法正常表達，而神經嵴細胞的早期發育也受損 。這些數據顯示， RET CD和NCD變異/突變是導致神經嵴細胞發育缺陷，直接影響病程。在這個項目中，我們建議（一）利用人類胚胎幹細胞（ESC）來研究與HSCR相關的RET CD基因突變，並了解它們是如何影響神經嵴細胞的發育； （二）利用現有的HSCR-iPSC，建立 RET/ GDNF信號與神經嵴細胞的發育的關係；及（三）使用CRISPR基因組編輯平台，為HSCR-iPSC 作出“疾病糾正”，從且證明RET CD變異和神經嵴細胞發育缺陷的相關性。綜上所述，本研究將討論 RET基因突變是如何影響人類神經嵴細胞發育。這項概念驗證，能為將來利用幹細胞疾病模型來了解先天性巨結腸病相關基因突變的研究奠定基礎，也加速人類胚胎幹細胞/ iPSC臨床應用的長遠發展。

17119514.label: Realisation of objectives
17119514.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is caused by the failure of enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs) to fully colonize the bowel, thus leading to bowel obstruction and megacolon. Heterozygous mutations in the coding region of the RET gene account for the severe form of HSCR (total colonic aganglionosis, TCA). However, 80% of HSCR patients have short segment HSCR (S-HSCR), whose genetic etiology remains unclear. In this project, we have established a new strategy for the functional identification of novel mutation(s) in HSCR disease. We have generated three HSCR-iPSC lines (from 1 TCA-HSCR patient with a RET G731del mutation and 2 S-HSCR patients without a RET mutation) and two RET isogenic mutant iPSC lines (RET+/- and RET-/-) were established to generate disease-relevant ENCCs. The migration and differentiation capacities of the iPSC-derived ENCCs were analyzed with various in vitro differentiation and migration assays. We further identified disease-associated mutation(s) by combining genetic and transcriptomic data obtained from patient blood and iPSC-derived ENCCs, respectively. Subsequently, the mutations in HSCR-iPSCs were corrected with CRISPR/Cas9 to directly demonstrate the impact of the mutations in ENCC development. In brief, ENCCs derived from all diseased iPSC lines exhibited defects in migration and neuronal lineage differentiation. RET mutations were functionally associated with cellular phenotypes of ENCCs in vitro. Our integration study by combing the genetic and transcriptomic data, we identified a novel mutation in Vinculin (VCL M209L) associated with S-HSCR. Correcting the RET G731del and VCL M209L mutations in HSCR-iPSCs restored the ENCC functions. In summary, we identified VCL as a novel HSCR gene. Importantly, our results also illustrate the value of human iPSCs for defining mutations that functionally contribute to a complex disease.

17119514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119514.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease (congenital megacolon) is a birth defect affecting the motility of the bowel. These babies suffer from severe constipation and intestinal obstruction because the nerve cells which co-ordinate bowel movements are absent. It is a global problem but is particularly prevalent in Asia, affecting 1 in 3,000 babies. It is known that DNA changes disrupting the function of RET gene cause a severe form of HSCR disease (total colonic aganglionosis). However, 80% of HSCR patients have short-segment HSCR disease (S-HSCR), which has not been associated with genetic factors. In this project, we created a stem cell-based disease model of HSCR for discovery of novel DNA changes that contribute to disease phenotypes. With the stem cell-based disease model of HSCR and the next-generation sequencing technologies, the study identified that specific DNA changes in RET and Vinculin (VCL) genes disrupt the migration and differentiation of neural stem cells of the bowel, leading to malformation of enteric nervous system as seen in HSCR patients. The newly developed stem cell-based disease model provides a powerful platform for studying the heterogeneous phenotypes of the diseases and that represents an important step toward personalised treatment.

17119814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119814.value: DNA origami is the self-assembly of carefully designed DNA sequence into two and three dimensional shapes at the nanoscale. Since the first DNA origami report in 2006, the cross-disciplinary field of “structural DNA nanotechnology” has blossomed with potential applications in molecular diagnostics, drug delivery, self-assembly and nanorobotics. The central question facing the field is how best to integrate the structural features of DNA origami with modular functional features such as those for molecular recognition, computation and self-replication. Here, we propose to interface DNA origami with DNA aptamers (a type of DNA evolved to recognize proteins for diagnostics/therapeutics applications) to seamlessly integrate structure and recognition as an enabling technology for molecular diagnostics. The principal investigator and one of the co-investigators in this grant have a track record and expertise in DNA aptamers used for molecular recognition of proteins for diagnostics or therapeutics applications. In particular, they recently published (Proc Natl Acad Sci USA) the structure for a new aptamer-target pair for malaria diagnosis that is ideal as a proof-of-principle system for this proposed integration of DNA origami and DNA aptamers. A further co-investigator brings expertise in bionanotechnology and DNA origami with a strong record in macromolecular self-assembly and nanodevices at one of the strongest centres in Asia for such work at RIKEN, Japan. We synergise this expertise to address modular aptamer-origami integration with four objectives. In objective I, we will integrate two different malaria DNA aptamers which we previously developed (one which detects lactate dehydrogenase for general Plasmodium detection, and a second which detects histidine rich protein II for specific Plasmodium falciparum detection) into a rectangular DNA origami scaffold in parallel and confirm self-assembly of the DNA nanoarchitecture using atomic force microscopy (AFM). In objective II, we will investigate the ability of this system to specifically and differentially detect single molecules of lactate dehydrogenase and histidine-rich protein II using AFM. In objective III, we incorporate gold nanoparticles and enzymatic assays into the modular system to develop approaches amenable to point-of-care diagnostics without requiring AFM. In objective IV, we will use the aptamer-target recognition event as a hinge on a DNA origami nanobox to release a DNA barcode diagnostic payload as a new highly innovative signal amplification approach. Taken together, this work will act as a proof-of-principle for modular aptamer integration into DNA origami with significant implications for DNA origami-mediated molecular diagnostics. DNA折紙術（DNA Origami）是在納米尺度下把精密設計的DNA序列組裝在二維和三維形狀上的自組裝技術。自DNA折紙術在2006年被第一次報道后，名為“結構性DNA納米技術”（Structural DNA nanotechnology）的交叉學科領域在分子診斷，藥物運輸，自組裝和納米機器人等潛在應用技術上得到了蓬勃的發展。如何最好地整合DNA折紙中的結構特性和諸如分子識別，計算，與自組裝等的模塊化功能特性成為了此領域的核心問題。在此，我們提出利用DNA適體（一種具有識別蛋白功能并應用于診斷/治療技術的DNA）無縫整合DNA折紙的結構和其識別功能從而作為一種分子診斷的使能技術。本申請的主要研究員和其中之一的合作研究員在以DNA適體和蛋白的分子識別作為診斷和治療應用上擁有豐富的專業技術和研究記錄。特別是，他們最近于Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 上發表了一個可應用在瘧疾診斷上的新型適體-靶標結構，此項研究可以作為一個理想的理論基礎系統以驗證整合DNA折紙與DNA適體的可行性。另外一個合作研究員具有豐富的生物納米技術和DNA折紙術的專業知識，並且在此領域具有相當科研實力的日本RIKEN研究所進行了大量的大分子自組裝和納米器械的研發工作。因此，我們將協同各方面的專業技術去研發模塊化適體DNA折紙術，并為本研究設立四個目標。目標一，將整合我們早期研發的兩個不同的瘧疾DNA適體(其一能識別乳酸脫氫酶以檢測普遍性的瘧原蟲， 其二能識別富組氨酸蛋白II以檢測特異性的惡性瘧原蟲)並行于一個四方形DNA折紙骨架，且利用共聚焦顯微鏡確認其納米架構的自組情況。目標二，將使用共聚焦顯微鏡研究這個系統在特異性識別和區分單個乳酸脫氫酶和富組氨酸蛋白II分子的能力。目標三，將整合金納米粒子技術和酶學測定法于一個模塊系統中以研發不需要使用共聚焦顯微鏡的即時檢測診斷。目標四，將利用適體-靶標識別作為DNA折紙納米盒子的一條鉸鏈，控制DNA條碼釋放并以此作為一種新型的高創新性信號放大方法。由此，這項研究對DNA折紙術介導的分子診斷應用起到重要的啟示作用，并會成為整合模塊化適體于DNA折紙在分子診斷應用中的一項原理驗證工作。

17119814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119814.value: DNA can be folded into larger nanostructures termed DNA origami which can be used in diagnostics and therapeutics applications. Before this grant, it was difficult to functionalise DNA origami with modules that enable a response to the environment, for example to a particular molecule. We have integrated sensing DNA molecules termed DNA aptamers onto the DNA origami and shown that this mechanism can be effective in diagnosis of malaria. In this grant we showed several different mechanisms using nanoboxes, nanotweezers and nanotetrahedrons on gold sensing surfaces of possible approaches for entirely new ways to diagnose a particular disease. Nanoboxes appeared excellent for carrying large cargos but may be slow for molecular release, implying a good fit for therapeutics rather than diagnostics. Nanotweezers were fast but there were some issues with sensitivity – this approach could be good for diagnosis of high abundance molecules. Nanotetrahedrons are excellent for new approaches which might be amenable to point of care or electrochemical device interfacing. There is wide-ranging impact of this work in new approaches to sense molecules and diagnose disease.

17120514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120514.value: Today haloacetates (HA) can be found widely distributed in our environment due to our indiscriminate use of disinfection processes. Many of these HA are toxic and mutagenic and affected our health invariably. A bacterium, Burkholderia caribensis MBA4, produces an enzyme, dehalogenase, which removes the halogen from haloacids, and rendered the HA degradable. Earlier works involved the purification and characterisation of the dehalogenase; cloning and characterisation of the gene and identification of associated HA-transporters that facilitate growth and HA-degradation. The HA-degrading activity of the bacterium is inducible. Molecular biology approach has ratified the binding of regulatory protein upstream of the dehalogenase gene in un-induced condition. This suggested a negative-regulatory mechanism. A transposon was introduced into MBA4 and an insertion-library was screened for clones that produced dehalogenase in medium without HA. It was assumed that a repressor-inactivated mutant would produce dehalogenase in the absence of HA. While mutants defective in various functions have been ubiquitously identified no repressor mutant was acquired. A preliminary transcriptome analysis shows that other than the dehalogenase and associated permeases, expressions of the ribosomal proteins and many others were up- or down- regulated. It is obvious that many genetic interactions are involved. The transcriptome analyses are unlikely to identify, unequivocally, the major determinants. It would be ideal to determine the effect of each of the genes on the growth of the bacterium on HA. With more than eight thousand genes in MBA4, it sounds impractical to disrupt each gene separately and determine their contribution. Nonetheless, a recently developed phenotype sequencing method makes this approach possible. In this proposal I would like to determine the significance of each of the genes in MBA4 in degradation of HA. A transposon-insertion library will be generated and the integration sites determined quantitatively by sequencing. Cells from the library will grow in medium containing HA for a fixed number of generation and the integration sites determined again quantitatively. Disruptants with a defective gene that disturbed the utilisation of HA will have a slower growth and their proportion in the population will decrease with respect to time. By means of determining the abundance of each of the insertion mutant in the two samples, it will be able to determine the importance, and thus fitness, of each of the disrupted gene in degradation of HA. With this single gene fitness data it will then be feasible to determine the genetic interactions in the future. 今天鹵代乙酸酯(HA)之所以廣泛地存在我們的環境裡，是由於 我們濫用消毒程序。這許多HA都是有毒的，致突變的，及影 響我們健康的。細菌卡瑞苯西思伯克霍爾德氏菌菌株MBA4 可以生產一種脫鹵酶，從而幫助降解鹵酸。早期的研究均涉 及脫鹵酶的純化和鑑定; 基因的鑑定與克隆及尋找相關的轉 運蛋白，用以促進細菌的生長和它的降解功能。這細菌 的HA降解活性是誘導型的。調節蛋白在非誘導條件下已 被分子生物學方法確定為能與脫鹵酶基因的上游結合。這 指出了一個負調控機制。利用轉座子誘變及在插入庫中篩選， 能在沒有HA的情況下而能生產脫鹵酶的菌株都被挑選出來。 據推斷，這些菌株都理應含有阻遏滅活的突變。然而各種 突變體都有，只是沒有抓到阻遏突變體。初步轉錄組分析 指出，除了脫鹵酶和相關的轉運蛋白外，核糖體蛋白和許 多其他的表達均有上調或下調的情況。很明顯地，這裡存 在許多遺傳相互作用的參與。轉錄組分析是不可能識別到 主要的決定因素的。最理想的作法是確定每個基因對細菌 生長在HA的影響。對擁有超過八千個基因的MBA4， 要分別擾亂每個基因，並確定他們的貢獻，這聽起來很像 不切實際。然而，最近開發的表型測序方法，使這種模式 成為有可能。在這個方案裡，我想鑒定每個MBA4的基因 對它的HA降解能力的重要性。轉座子插入庫裡的各個整 合位點將進行測序和定量測定。庫中的菌株將培養在含有 HA的基中，生長固定數目的世代後，再次確定它們的整合 位點的定量。若缺陷的基因干擾菌株使用HA的速率，它們 的增長將會有所放緩和在總數的比例將會隨時間減少。通過 測定每個插入突變體在兩個樣本中的豐富度，將可以决定 每個基因對HA的降解的重要性和適存度。有了這個單一 基因適存度的數據，將可以促進未來遺傳相互作用研究的 可行性。

17120814.label: Realisation of objectives
17120814.value: 1. To define the functional domains and their respective key signaling pathways of LMP1 involved in generation of invadopodia. Invadopodia are actin-rich membrane protrusions commonly observed in invading cancer cells to facilitate its invasive activity and metastasize to distant organ sites. Invadopodia can secret abundant matrix metalloproteinases to facilitate an invading cell to digest the extracellular matrix to facilitate invasion of cancer cells. We demonstrated that the EBV-encoded LMP1 could induce invadopodia formation in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and NPC cells which have lost their EBV. Local invasion and distant metastasis is common in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. NPC is almost 100 % associated with EBV infection. The LMP1 is a latent EBV gene commonly expressed in NPC particularly at its early stage of pathogenesis. To investigate if LMP1 could induce invadopodia formation to facilitate NPC invasion, we first transfected LMP1 into several immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial (NP) cell lines including NP361, NP460, NP550 and NP69, and performed invadopodia assays in the LMP1-transfected NP cell lines. The ability of LMP1 to induce invadopodia was examined in both transient and stable transfected immortalized NP cells as well as in our recently established NPC 43 cells which have lost their EBV episomes upon prolonged propagation. To assay for the ability of LMP1 to induce invapodia in immortalized NP cells as well as EBV-ve NPC 43 cells, the cells were transfected with LMP1and seeded onto FITC-conjugated gelatin coated coverslip for 3, 6 and 9 hrs, then fixed and stained with Alexa555-conjugated phalloidin to visualize the invadopodia as actin- rich dots. The number of invadopodia was counted and the area of digested gelatin were measured using ImageJ softaware analysis. Live cell imaging of the invadopodia action induced by LMP1 to degrade the FITC-labelled gelatin were also established. We observed that LMP1 expression increased the percentage of cells forming invadopodia and gelatin degradation by 2 to 8 folds compared control cells. Stable expression of LMP1 in NP460 and NP550, asa well as EBV-ve NPC cells, enhanced both the invadopodia formation and matrix degradation. We further defined that The C-terminal activation regions (CTAR) of LMP1 is involved in the activation of invadopodia formation LMP1. We then examined the signaling pathways involved by examining various signaling pathways using specific inhibitors of signaling pathways and the use of LMP1 mutants. Furthermore, the use of wild type and mutant LMP1 expression vectors reveald that the C-terminal activation regions (CTAR1 and CTAR2) are involved in the activation of invadopodia formation. The mutant LMP1s (with defective CTAR1 and/or CTAR2 cytoplasmic domain lost their ability to activate invadopodia. The CTAR1 and CTAR2 to activate MAPK has been well-documented. Inhibition of MAPK signaling effectively inhibited invadopodia formation induced by LMP1. Activation of Cdc42 through the CTAR 1 and 2 is involved in LMP-mediated invadopodia through pull down assay. All these results have been described in the Ph.D thesis of Mr. Wilson Tang, who has just completed and passed his Ph.D viva examination in June 2019. 2. To define the role of podoplanin in LMP1-induced invadopodia. To understand the functional relationship between podoplanin and LMP1 in the induction of invadopodia formation, we first examined whether LMP1 could regulate the expression of podoplanin in different NPC and NP cell lines. We found that LMP1 could elevate the expression of podoplanin in HONE1 (a NPC cell line), and in NP361 and NP69 cells (two immortalized NP cell lines). In the cell lines which have high expression of podoplanin, we are now conducting experiments to knock down the podoplanin (using pLKO-shPodoplanin) and to assess its inhibitory effect to the LMP1-mediated invadopodia formation. Our previous publication has shown that podoplanin are recruited to the F-actin rim of the invadopodia to promote their stability and consequent matrix degradation. In this study, we examined recruitment/localization of podoplanin are being observed by transfecting GFP-tagged podoplanin in LMP1-expressing cell lines. Using time- lapse confocal imaging and kymographic analysis, live cell imaging of the podoplanin organization in the LMP1-induced invadopodia was performed to determine the localization of podoplanin in invadopodia. However, our results showed that podoplanin is more associated with the formation of filipodia and migration of cells but not specifically localized to invadopodia and invasion. 3. To define the involvement of LMP1 activation of PKC-EZRIN-podoplanin pathways in stabilization and function of invadopodia We previously proposed that LMP1 can activate phosphorylation of EZRIN through PKC activation and promote invasiveness via actin cytoskeleton remodulation (Kodos et al., 2009). However, further experiments showed that the podoplanin is inconsistently expressed in LMP-expressing NPC cells. We switched our research emphasis to examine the other signaling pathways involve din activation of invadopodia in NPC cells, in particular the signaling pathways involved in synergistic action of TNF-alpha and LMP1 in NPC cells. We observed that synergistic actions of TNF-alpha and LMP1 in stabilization and degradative action of invadopodia in NPC cells. We then defined the signaling pathway involved in the synergistic activation of TNFalpha and LMP1 in invadopodia formation. Activation of Src, cortactin, ERK and ROS signaling pathways was identified in TNFalpha treated NPC cells. The Src signaing is the major driver of invadopododia formation by TNFalpha. TNFalpha treated LMP1-expressing NPC cells strongly induced invadopodia formation through the synergistic action of LMP1-induced cdc42. The invadopodia induced also have high mobility in addition to degradative activity. Furthermore, we observed high content of TNF-alpha in the supernatant of macrophages which could be a potential source of TNFalpha in NPC. Incubation of supernatant from activated macrophage culture strongly induced invadopodia formation in NPC cells which could be effectively neutralized by anti-TNFalpha antibody. This observation has been written up for submission for publication. We further found out that the activated macrophages could secrete high level of TNFalpha to activate invadopodia formation and activities. 4. To examine the correlation of LMP1, activated EZRIN and podoplanin expression in clinical NPC specimens. We have performed immunohistochemical staining of podoplanin in NPC tissues. Interestingly, the expression of podoplanin is mainly observed at the invasive front of the NPC tissues. However, we were not able to identify a close association between EZRIN/Podoplanin expression to survival and staging in NPC. We have also examined the LMP1 expression with other invasion markers and observed a high expression of SNAIL which correlate with LMP1 expression and prognosis of NPC patient (Results published in Zhang et al., Oncogene 2019). Interestingly, we observed a strong association of LMP1 wih SNAIL expression which is relating to the alteration of mTORC2 activation. There are multiple reports on alteration of metabolism and invadopododia. Our preliminary results also confirmed that in NPC. We have expanded the study to cover the ability LMP1 to induce invadopodia and invasion through altered metabolism and identified the involvement of mTORC2 activation, SNAIL and altered expression profile of metabolic enzymes in NPC using tissue microarray of NPC. In a recently published collaboration manuscript, we observed a relationsip between EBV encoded microRNA in activation of metabolism and invasion.

17120814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120814.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is an invasive carcinoma. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is closely associated with EBV infection and multiple signaling process activated by LMP1 are involved (Research output 1; manuscript published in Oncogene 2019). Invadopodia is a specialized cellular structures developed to facilitate cell invasion (Research output 2; Manuscript submitted to Acta Materialia: invited for revision). It is commonly present in invasive and metastatic cancer cells. In this study, we have demonstrated that the EBV-encoded LMP1 is capable to induce invadopodia formation whih is a effective cellular process to degrade extracellular matrix. Induction of invadopodia formation is strongly associated with invasive properties of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells. We further defined that the CTAR1 and CTAR2 regions of LMP1 could activate Cdc42 which is a major component in invadopodia (Research output 3; Manuscript in preparation). The CTAR1 and CTAR2 are the key domains for multiple signaling pathways of LMP1 including NF-kB and MAPK. Invadopodia induction by LMP1 could be effectively inhibited by inhibitors of NF-kB and MAPK (Research output 1 & 2). Furthermore, the invadopodia activity is strongly enhanced by the treatment of TNFalpha which is a common cytokines released by activated macrophages present in NPC. The TNFalpha and LMP1 has synergistic action in invadopodia formation and activation. TNFalpha is a common cytokine released by activated macrophages present in NPC. Inhibition of the synergistic action of TNF alpha and LMP1 could be effective to suppress metastasis of NPC. We also make the novel discovery that LMP1 could activate SNAIL to induce invasion of NPC cells. In patients, expression of LMP1 and its downstream events including mTORC2, SNAIL and other metabolic enzymes are involved in the invasive properties of NPC cells (Research output 1). Several key players in the activation of invadopodia in NPC were identified in NPC specimens. Understanding of the association of EBV infection, action of LMP1 and its interaction with inflammatory cytokines may provide novel targets for therapeutic intervention to prevent disease progress in NPC.

17120814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120814.value: The signaling pathways of LMP1 induction of invadopodia in NPC was defined. Its synergistic action with TNF alpha was identified. Several key players involved in invadopodia formation in NPC were identified. The effects of targeting these invasive markers and signaling pathway may provide an effective way to prevent the metastatic process in NPC.

17120814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120814.value: We have identified the involvement of LMP1 and its synergistic action with TNF alpha to induce invadopodia in NPC cells. Some of the key players and signaling pathways were identified which provide novel target for therapeutic intervention to prevent NPC metastasis. TNF alpha is commonly secreted by infiltrated stromal cells notably activated macrophages. The findings of this study also suggested the importance of tumor microenvironment in modification of tumor cell behavior including invasive properties. The tumor microenvironment may represent effective therapeutic target to prevent NPC invasion and metastasis to improve survival of NPC patients.

17121014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121014.value: Heart failure (HF) has become increasingly prevalent due to the aging population and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and in Hong Kong. Among those HF patients, half of them suffer from HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and the remaining half have HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Despite the difference in the ejection fraction (EF), both types of HF are associated with similar and high morbidity and mortality. In randomized clinical trials, pharmacological therapies, such as ß-blocker and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockers which are effective for HFrEF have no or limited therapeutic efficacy in patients with HFpEF. As a result, there is an emerging need to develop novel therapy specifically targeted to this subgroup of HF patients. HFpEF is more likely to occur in older, female and obese patients, and is frequently associated with hypertensive left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). Indeed, the most common pathophysiological hallmarks of HFpEF are highlighted by impaired left ventricular (LV) relaxation and increased diastolic stiffness associated with maladaptive LVH and myocardial fibrosis. Activation of RAAS and sympathetic nervous system (SNS) are known to play an important role in the development and sustainability of an increased blood pressure (BP). Moreover, both of them can also contribute to the occurrence of HFpEF. Shortening of LV diastolic filling period with SNS activation exerts a detrimental effect in HFpEF. On the other hand, peripheral vasoconstriction and sodium/water retention related to RAAS activation increase LV end-diastolic pressure and afterload. Nevertheless, these neurohormonal activations in HFpEF appear to be more variable than in HFrEF, and might contribute to suboptimal therapeutic effects of ß-blocker and RAAS blockers. Recently, much attention has focused on the role of a autonomic imbalance in refractory hypertension and HF. Increased peripheral sensory afferent signaling, eg from kidney and splanchnic organs can directly influence central sympathetic outflow to perpetuate the global sympathetic overdrive in HFpEF, and regional norepinephrine (NE) spillover as well as adrenaline secretion from adrenal medulla are major contributors to the total excess in sympathetic drive. On the other hand, the enhanced efferent sympathetic signaling to the kidney during HF can lead to decreased renal blood flow and activation of the RAAS. It is possible that a novel therapeutic approach that modulates these different peripheral SNS imbalance may improve symptoms and/or clinical outcome in HPpEF. Here, we hypothesize that direct modulation of SNS innervation of the kidney, splanchnic organs and adrenal gland using spinal cord stimulation (SCS) at the lower thoracic level via the innervation at the celiac, superior and inferior mesenteric ganglion can decrease BP and attenuate HFpEF in a clinically relevant large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy with induced by angiotensin-II infusion and DOCA. Specifically, the long-term safety and efficacy, as well as the mechanisms of action of SCS on BP reduction and attenuation of maladaptive LV remodeling and diastolic dysfunction associated with hypertensive cardiomyopathy will be investigated. The results of this study should provide important insight into the development of a novel non-pharmacological therapy with spinal cord stimulation for the treatment of HFpEF induced by hypertensive cardiomyopathy.

17121014.label: Realisation of objectives
17121014.value: To address Objective 1 and 2, we first established a large animal model of hypertensive heart disease induced by angiotensin-II infusion and DOCA treatment. We induced sustained elevated blood pressure (BP) in 8 adult pigs using a combination of intravenous angiotensin II (Ang II, 0.025mg/hr) infusion using an osmotic infusion pump and subcutaneous implantation of deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) pellets (100mg/kg) for 10 weeks. Another 6 animals were served as control. Serial blood sampling at multiple regions (aorta, coronary sinus, renal and splanchnic circulation), and echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic measurements were performed to assess regional of SNS activation, and left ventricular (LV) performance, respectively were performed at baseline, 10 and 20 weeks in 6 control and 8 hypertensive animals. At 20 weeks, there were significantly increased in systolic, diastolic and mean BPs, increased LV filling pressure, and impaired LV diastolic function with preserved LV systolic function associated with LV hypertrophy in the hypertension group as compared to control. Moreover, significantly increased systematic, and regional norepinephrine venoarterial gradient over the myocardium, kidneys and splanchnic organs after induction of hypertension compared to their baseline. While there are significantly increase in sympathetic nerve as detected by tyrosin hydroxylase staining over the kidneys and splanchnic organs, only significantly raised in tissue norepinephrine was observed in the spleen. In conclusion, a large animal model of sustained hypertension with pathophysiological phenotypes of HFpEF induced by a combination of low dose Ang-II and DOAC administration, there was significant regional heterogeneity of SNS activations in which prominent splenic sympathetic activation could be observed. Next, we investigated whether lower spinal cord stimulation (SCS) can reduce BP and improve cardiac performance in this large animal model of HFpEF. Unfortunately, lower SCS treatment does not reduce systemic and LV BP in this large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy. Therefore, SCS treatment had no effect of LV contractile function but also did not improve LV diastolic function in hypertensive cardiomyopathy. There were no significant differences in +dP/dt, -dP/dt, ESPVR and EDPVR between the two groups at different phases. In the SCS group, SCS treatment had no effect of LV ejection fraction and dimension but also did not reduce LV mass index and wall thickness in hypertensive cardiomyopathy. There were no significant differences in LV ejection fraction, LV dimension, LV mass index and LV wall thickness between the two groups at different phases. Finally, there were no difference in the systemic and regional differences in norepinephrine levels and venoarterial gradient in the SCS groups versus control. In conclusion, our results failed to demonstrate any significant therapeutic effects of lower thoracic SCS for BP reduction and LV diastolic dysfunction in large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy. The negative results of this study might be related to the lack of direct effects of SCS on splanchnic autonomic innervation or due to the differences on the spinal cord innervation in pig versus human, and thus the level of stimulation tested in this study had no effect on splanchnic innervation.

17121014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121014.value: In conclusion, in porcine model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension, spinal cord stimulation was not effective to decrease blood pressure and improves left ventricular diastolic function. Our findings suggest that spinal cord stimulation is not a potential novel non-pharmacological approach for treatment of hypertensive cardiomyopathy. Based on these findings, we have presented one abstract in major international cardiology congress and the full publication is now under preparation.

17121014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121014.value: Based on the findings of this pre-clinical study in large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy, future clinical studies should be performed to investigate on other novel treatment approach, such as direct splanchnic modulation for treatment of patients with hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension. Indeed, we have started to discuss with the industries for potential collaboration for the development of novel catheter for splanchnic denervation as therapeutic approach for hypertensive cardiomyopathy.

17121014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121014.value: In a clinical relevant large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension, our findings suggest that splanchnic sympathetic innervation is a potential target for novel non-pharmacological for treatment of hypertensive cardiomyopathy. However, our results failed to show the benefit of spinal cord stimulation as effective therapy for treatment of patients with hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension, and thus other therapeutic approach, such as direct splanchnic nerve modulation should be further investigated .

17121414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121414.value: The interaction between transcription factor (TF) and its DNA binding site (BS) is central to gene regulation. The interaction in the core promoter region is responsible for basal transcription of the target gene, whereas interaction in the distal region controls the temporal and spatial expression of the gene. Mutations in the transcription factor binding sites will disrupt these interactions, which cause many diseases such as the blood disorder thalassemia. Currently, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified tens of thousands of Genetic Variants (GVs) associated with human diseases. To our surprise, many of these loci are located in non-coding regions, sometimes far away from a protein-coding gene. For example, recent GWAS studies (including a lung cancer study done by us) found a 63 kbp region that harbors TERT and CLPTM1L genes and their regulatory regions is highly associated with over a dozen cancers. Detecting TFs that bind to these regions is not only important for the understanding of the mechanisms of cancer pathogenesis but also for potential therapeutic treatments. We have developed analysis pipelines to annotate and prioritize putative functional GVs, based on information from predicted TF-BS interactions, Linkage disequilibrium, epigenetics and chromatin interaction. In this study, we propose the novel concept of “allelic-specific co-expression analysis” that takes into account allelic differences of each individual when inferring the co-expression relationship between TF and its target gene. We hypothesize that this concept will help us identify TF-BS interactions more accurately and improve our GV annotation pipeline and detection of upstream regulators. In this proposal, we will (1) test our hypothesis using recent cancer genomic data, (2) develop a novel computational pipeline to predict accurately the transcription factors that interact with regulatory GVs, and (3) predict regulators of the TERT-CLPTM1L region for lung cancer and validate our predictions with experiments. The study will develop a novel framework that uses an allelic-specific co-expression method to infer regulators and prioritize GWAS GVs, especially those in enhancer and promoter regions. The framework will be more accurate than the existing methods and can be widely used in other genetic studies. It will be used to unravel the molecular determinants of the TERT-CLPTM1L region in lung cancer that can also be used to provide clues for the causes of other cancers. The discovered upstream regulators on this region can be therapeutic targets for future drug development. 轉錄因子（TF）和它的DNA結合位點（BS）之間的相互作用是基因調控的關鍵。在核心啟動子區的相互作用控制靶基因的基礎轉錄，而在遠端區域的交互控制靶基因表達的時空次序。在轉錄因子的突變位點的結合會破壞這些相互作用，從而引起多種疾病，如血液病地中海貧血症。目前，全基因組關聯研究（GWAS）已經確定了數以萬計的與人類疾病相關聯的DNA變異。令我們吃驚的是，許多變異位於非編碼區，有時離蛋白質編碼區很遠。這些變異很多是與基因調控相關的。例如，最近的全基因組關聯研究（包括我們做了肺癌研究）發現一個含TERT和CLPTM1L基因的63 kbp區域與超過十幾種癌症有關。檢測結合於這些區域的TF不僅可以幫助我們了解癌症的發病機制，也可以開發潛在的治療途徑。我們前期已經開發了一些生物信息學軟件來註釋這些非編碼區的功能。在此，我們提出一個“等位基因特異的共表達分析”的新概念來推斷的TF及其靶基因的共表達關係。我們假設，這一概念將有助於我們更準確地識別TF-BS的互動，提高我們對DNA​​突變的功能標註。通過這個項目，我們將（1）使用最近癌症基因組數據來測試我們的新概念，（2）根據這一概念，開發一種新的計算方法來精確預測TF與DNA變異區的相互作用，（3 ）實驗驗證在肺癌中調控TERT-CLPTM1L區的關鍵TF，並用實驗結果驗證我們新方法的可靠性。該框架會比現有的方法更準確並可廣泛用於其他遺傳病研究。它將被用於解開TERT-CLPTM1L區域與肺癌及其他癌症相關聯／致病的成因。這些關鍵TF也可成為未來藥物開發的靶標。

17121414.label: Realisation of objectives
17121414.value: We developed computational frameworks for • identifying regulatory genetic variants which contain transcription factor binding sites (Li et al. Predicting regulatory variants with composite statistic, 2016) • identifying regulatory genetic variants within significant genomic regions from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) (Li et al. GWASdb 2: an update database for human genetic variants identified by genome-wide association studies, 2015) • integrating regulatory genetic variants with transcriptic, epigenomic and other omics data to derive gene regulatory networks (Wang et al, ChIP-Array 2: Integrating mulitple omics data to contruct gene regulatory networks, 2015) • linking regulatory genetic variants to disease by considering tissue or cell-type specific epigenomic data (Li et al. CEPIP: contect-dependent epigenomic weighting for prioritization of regualtory variants and disease-associated genes, 2017) The methodologies were applied in studies which demonstrated • the importance of the trancription factor FOXM1 as a regulator of cell cycle progression and a protector against oxidative stress in human embryonic stem cells (Kwok et al. The forkhrsf box transcription factor FOXM1 is required for the maintenance of cell proliferation and protection against oxidative stress in human embryonic stem cells, 2016) • the importance of microRNA-200c in cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation (Poon et al. Integrated transcriptomic and regulatory network analyses idnetify microRNA-200c as a novel repressor of human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation, 2018) • GWAS results predict the success of the development of new drugs (Nelson et al. The support of human genetic evidence for approved drug indications, 2015) Dr. Junwen Wang, the original principal investigator of the project, left the University of Hong Kong in 2016. He continued to be on the project team, but the role of principal investigator was transferred to Prof. Pak Sham
