17121414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121414.value: • Development of computational frameworks for studying gene regulation and its role in embryonic development and disease states. These methods have been implemented in a number of computer software freely available to the research community - ChIP-ARRAY2, GWASdb2 and CEPIP. • Application of these methods in studies which uncovered important roles for FOXM1 and microRNA-200c in normal development, and showed that GWAS data can be used to predict whether a new drug is likely to be effective in treating a particular condition.

17121414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121414.value: We are engaged in further method development: • a mathematical model of the relationship between gene expression on the whole-genome scale is regulated by groups of transcription factors. This work forms part of a PhD thesis which has been submitted • a model based on the disruption of typologically-active domains to predict the damaging effects of structural variations in the genome, and its relevance to cancer. The work forms part of a PhD thesis which will be submitted this year.

17121414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121414.value: The normal development and functioning of the human body depends on appropriate control of the activities of the approximately 20,000 genes in various cells and at various times. Mal-function of the normal control mechanisms can lead to congenital defects or disease. We have developed sophistical mathematical models, which combine different types of genomic data generated by modern molecular technologies, to understand the mechanims that control activity of genes. We have implemented these models in a number of freely available computer programs, and used these to identify important molecules in embryonic development. We also showed that large-scale genetic data can be used to predict which drugs will be effective in the treatment of a particular disease.

17121714.value: 肥胖是一個世界性的公共衛生問題和心腦血管疾病高患病率的一大主因。體內循環中的脂類物質以及促炎症分子的水平和表達上調增高與肥胖密切相關, 是兩個主要的心血管危險因素。血管周圍的脂肪組織分泌多種活性物質來發揮調節血流量和血管緊張度的作用。由於距離很近，血管周圍的脂肪組織功能障礙更容易引起血管功能異常。在肥胖的人群或动物模型中，具有促炎作用的脂籠蛋白-2在血浆中的含量显著升高。有报道指脂籠蛋白-2在高血脂，高血压，冠狀動脈疾病的病理发展过程中扮演重要作用。缺乏這種蛋白質可保護小鼠對抗肥胖或脂肪酸誘導的血管功能障礙。脂籠蛋白-2在正常的血管幾乎檢測不到，但可以大量積累在動脈粥樣硬化斑塊和受傷的動脈內膜。最近我們發現人類和小鼠脂籠蛋白-2可被聚胺化，而脫聚胺化穩定該蛋白並促進其在組織中的積累，例如血管。脂肪組織是主要的脂籠蛋白-2脫胺化部位。游離脂肪酸或飲食性肥胖都可以促進脂籠蛋白-2脫胺化，隨後導致血管功能障礙。這些數據共同表明，活化的脂籠蛋白-2是肥胖脂肪組織引起的血管功能異常的關鍵機制。因而此提案的目的是解剖脂籠蛋白-2脫胺化的分子途徑和機制，並闡明脂籠蛋白-2轉譯後修飾的病理生理和臨床意義。研究結果將揭示脂籠蛋白-2的激活/失活機制，以預防心血管疾病的發生發展過程中的不必要的促炎功能。

17121814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121814.value: Inorganic polyphosphate (poly-P) is a simple molecule with a complex range of biological functions. It is fundamentally important to all cellular life forms. In bacteria, poly-P helps cells survive in hostile conditions, e.g. during desiccation, nutritional starvation, or when being ‘attacked’ with antibiotic agents. Furthermore, poly-P also plays a pivotal role in the ability of pathogenic (disease-causing) bacteria to cause persistent or ‘virulent’ infections. However, the precise molecular mechanisms remain obscure. Polyphosphate hydrolase proteins (PPX-GppA family), are responsible for the hydrolysis of poly-P molecules in most bacteria. General consensus is that bacterial PPX-GppA proteins also have the universal ability to hydrolyze guanosine pentaphosphate (pppGpp) intracellular signaling molecules, which are also known as ‘magic spot’ alarmones. These molecules play various key roles in bacterial survival and adaptation. The general paradigm is that pppGpp molecules inhibit the poly-P degrading activities of all PPX-GppA proteins. Thus PPX-GppA proteins are posited to act as ‘gatekeepers’ between two vitally-important cellular pathways. However, our preliminary results show that this general paradigm is not universally true, and must be critically re-evaluated. In this proposal, we will establish structure-function relationships to clarify the biological roles of bacterial PPX-GppA proteins across bacteria. This will be done using a focused combination of biochemical, genetic, bioinformatic and structural biology approaches. Our specific objectives: 1) Characterize the biochemical activities of a small, but carefully-selected set of PPX-GppA proteins from diverse bacterial species. 2) Identify conserved amino acid residues and structural domains that play key catalytic or regulatory roles. 3) Use genetic and targeted molecular diagnostic approaches to establish the functions of PPX-GppA proteins within three important bacterial pathogens: Vibrio cholerae (cholera), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (pneumonia, tissue infections) and Porphyromonas gingivalis (periodontal disease). Our results will significantly improve our fundamental understanding of how bacteria survive and adapt to hostile environments. This will be of critical importance for a more holistic knowledge of how medically-important pathogens cause persistent biofilm infections; which are often highly resistant to traditional therapies. The data generated here will also rationalize the selection of proteins implicated in the polyphosphate and stringent response pathways as targets for the development of novel anti-infective agents. Furthermore, our findings will also be directly relevant to many other areas of applied and environmental microbiology, such as waste-water phosphate removal, bioremediation, oceanic phosphate cycle modeling and microbial biotechnology. 無機聚合磷酸（poly-P）是一種具有多种複雜生物作用的簡單分子。它對一切細胞形式的生命體具有重要意義。在細菌體內，聚合磷酸協助其應對不利環境（如乾燥，營養缺乏，受抗生素“攻擊”等）。其次，聚合磷酸對致病（引發病症）細菌的耐受能力及“毒性”有關鍵的作用。但是，兩者之間的確切的相互作用機理尚不明確。 在大多數細菌體內，無機聚合磷酸水解蛋白（PPX-GppA家族蛋白）負責聚合磷酸的水解過程。廣泛認為，PPX-GppA家族蛋白通常具有分解五磷酸腺苷（pppGpp）的能力，而五磷酸腺苷是一種被稱為“神奇點”的細胞內信號分子。這種信號分子對細菌的存活能力和適應性具有多種關鍵作用。一般通用模式認為，五磷酸腺苷能抑制PPX-GppA家族蛋白并降低其降解聚合磷酸的活性。因此, PPX-GppA家族蛋白在兩種至關重要的細胞代謝模式中被授予“把關”的地位。然而，我們的初步結果顯示這種通用的模式並不完全正確而且需要謹慎地重新評估。 在本項目中，我們将建立構效關係模型去了解不同細菌體內的PPX-GppA家族蛋白的生物作用。我們將集中使用生物化學，基因學，生物信息學以及結構生物學方法。 具體實驗目的： 1）判定一系列來自不同細菌種類但經過審慎選擇的PPX-GppA家族小分子蛋白。2）找出對蛋白活性具有關鍵催化作用和調控作用的保守性氨基酸殘基和結構域。3）利用基因及有目標分子診斷方法確立來自三種PPX-GppA家族蛋白的功能：霍亂弧菌（霍亂），假銅綠單胞菌（能引起肺炎，組織感染）和牙龈卟啉菌（牙周病菌）。 此研究之結果將極大地提高我們對細菌的生存方式和如何適應不利環境的基礎認識。這對於瞭解一些對傳統治療手段有高度抗性的致病菌如何形成頑固性生物膜感染的認識上具有高度的重要性。此項研究所得的數據亦有助於合理篩選處針對聚合磷酸和應激反應途徑中的蛋白作為新型抗感染藥物試劑研發的對象。此外，我們的研究與應用及環境微生物學的許多領域直接相關，譬如去除廢水中磷酸，生物修復，海洋磷酸循環模型和微生物生物技術領域。

17121914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121914.value: Scientists worry that we are either entering into, or in the midst of, a mass species extinction due to the rapidly changing environmental conditions caused by human activities. Our planet is warming up at an unprecedented rate that most species have not experienced in their evolutionary history, and hence may have limited capacity to adapt to. In particular, many tropical species are already living close to their physiological limits and they are predicted to be the initial victims of such climate warming. A substantial amount of research has studied the thermal tolerance of species in order to predict their fate (e.g. shift in distribution or extinction) under climate warming. Most studies assume that adaptive genetic change will not have the time to act to combat these threats, and so populations mostly lack resilience to such rapid climate warming. Some scientists, however, argue that phenotypic plasticity through behavioural responses has largely been overlooked as an adaptive strategy, and that fast behavioural responses to environmental change may allow additional time for adaptive genetic changes to arise. Increasing evidence also suggests that sexual selection may facilitate adaptation of populations by accelerating genetic change if it acts in the same direction as viability selection. To predict species' resilience under climate warming, therefore, requires an integrated approach, taking into account both behavioural responses and changes in selection pressures. Marine snails in the genus Echinolittorina are suitable candidates for modeling species' responses to climate warming using such an approach. These snails live in the extreme physical environment of the high rocky intertidal zone; living at the limits of their physiological tolerances in tropical regions; exhibit various behavioural responses to tolerate heat stress; and show strong sexual selection. Variation in intensity of behavioural responses related to heat tolerance (e.g. hiding in crevices, aggregation and aestivating) will be investigated in situ on shores of different thermal regimes in three common Echinolittorina species. Changes in direction and intensity of selection pressures (i.e. sexual and viability selection) of the three species will be determined by investigating how temperature influences their mating preferences (via mucus trail following and copulation duration) and fitness costs of sexually selected traits of the snails. The overall prediction of population resilience of the three species to climate warming can, therefore, be derived based on their behavioural responses and the direction and intensity of different selection pressures on these snails in a thermally variable environment. 由於人類活動造成環境急劇變化，科學家們擔心我們正步入，又或已處於一個大規模物種滅絕的世代之中。 我們的地球正以一個前所未有的速度暖化，而這個暖化速度是大多數物種難以適應的，因為在牠們的進化史裡面並沒有經歷過這種情況。 由於許多熱帶物種本身已居住在靠近他們生理極限的環境，這些物種預計將會成為氣候暖化的最先受害者。至今已有大量研究透過了解物種的耐熱程度，從而預測牠們在氣候暖化中的命運（如分佈的轉移或絕種的可能性）。這些研究一般認為多數物種缺乏抵禦氣候暖化的能力，因為牠們不會有足夠的時間演化出抵禦機制。 另一些科學家則認為，很多研究都忽略了物種有能力快速地改變牠們的行為模式去應付氣候暖化，從而允許更多的時間來產生適應性的遺傳變化。 另外，越來越多的證據顯示：如果性擇與天擇的方向是一致的，性擇就會加快遺傳變化，從而促進種群的適應能力。 因此，要能夠預測物種在氣候暖化的適應能力需採取一個綜合的方法，就是同時考慮到物種在應對暖化的行為反應及選擇(性擇與天擇)壓力的變化。屬名Echinolittorina的海螺是利用這種綜合方法去模擬物種面對氣候的反應的合適人選。這些海螺具備合適的條件，包括: （一）牠們住在極端物理環境，即岩岸的較高位置; （二）牠們在熱帶地區的生活環境已迫近他們的生理極限; （三）牠們有不同的耐熱行為和顯示出強勁的性擇。 我們會實地研究三種常見的Echinolittorina在不同受熱程度的海岸發生的耐熱行為變化（如隱藏在縫隙中、聚集和夏眠）。 同時我們亦會透過調查溫度對這些海螺擇偶偏好(即透過跟隨黏液的軌跡和交配時間的長度)的影響，以及牠們所喜好的伴侶的特徵會否影響生存能力，以了解選擇(性擇與天擇)壓力的方向與強度。通過研究這三種海螺在不同受熱環境的行為反應及選擇(性擇與天擇)壓力的方向和強度的變化，我們就能夠具體地預測牠們適應氣候暖化的能力。

17121914.label: Realisation of objectives
17121914.value: Objective 1: To investigate the thermally-induced changes in behavioural responses and selection pressures of littorinids (100% achieved) This objective has been achieved by utilizing a number of sites in Cape d’ Aguilar Marine Reserve that represented a natural thermal gradient (from non-stressful to highly stressful) to study a variety of behavioural responses and selection pressures under different thermal regimes in two high shore littorinids (Echinolittorina malaccana and E. radiata) and a mid shore littorinid (E. vidua). Apart from the thermal regimes, a range of other physical (e.g. rock colour, refuge availability) and biological (e.g. grazer density, food availability etc.) parameters were also assessed at these study sites to construct an overall stress profile across the sites. These profiles showed that the sites could be aligned to form a stress gradient based on environmental characters relevant to thermal stress. These sites were subsequently able to be used for further investigations. To examine the behavioural responses and various fitness-associated activities across the established thermal/stress gradient, we first conducted 24-hour surveys to assess the general behavioural patterns of these species and to estimate the allocation of their activity budgets to various fitness-associated activities in the three littorinids. These surveys were conducted during different seasons and over different days and showed that the snails have clearly defined behavioural patterns; moving at certain times of the tidal cycle (when awash in summer, when they mate; and being inactive whilst emersed). After knowing that these snails exhibited reproductive behaviours only during awash periods and performed various thermoregulatory behaviours during emersion periods, snapshot surveys (with E. vidua excluded due to its very low abundance; which resulted in insufficient animals to achieve realistic sample sizes) were then conducted to investigate these behaviours as well as sexual selection pressure across the thermal gradient (i.e. on the shores with different thermal regimes). These were all able to be carried out successfully for Echinolittorina malacanna and E. radiata which occurred in high abundance at all sites and results indicated that there was no difference in mate choice (size etc) of either species between the different sites. Although E. vidua were not sampled to investigate sexual selection during the time-specific surveys, due to their low abundance on the shores, we do not feel that the overall achievement of this objective was undermined given that we have obtained results from the other two species. Objective 2: To elucidate the role of sexual selection in modulating adaptation to a warming climate (100% achieved) This objective has been achieved by investigating whether large/small snails were more/less tolerant to thermal stress based on Arrhenius breakpoint temperatures (ABTs, the temperature at which the heart starts to malfunction and the heart rate drops rapidly), and whether snails’ size-based mate choice would be altered under different temperature regimes. These experiments were all carried out in controlled laboratory experiments and showed that these snails have exceedingly high ABTs but show no variation with site or between sexes (although there was a difference between species). Fecundity of females of various sizes and females exposed to various thermal regimes from different sites was also measured (in terms of eggs released per female) in the SWIMS aquarium to assess the reproductive benefits associated with males choosing large/small females under various thermal conditions. Such investigations have allowed us to determine whether natural selection acted in the same direction as sexual selection and, hence, whether sexual selection would modulate adaptations in littorinids under climate warming. We initially planned to investigate mate choice under various thermal conditions in the laboratory by holding snails with different thermal histories (i.e. from shores with different thermal regimes) at different temperatures, but this experiment was not successful. As already mentioned in the previous report, the three Echinolittorina species appeared stressed and mostly aggregated within the glass experimental chambers and did not mate, which is a different response found in previous studies with other littorinid genera (e.g. Littorina and Littoraria). From the study of sexual selection among the study sites in the natural habitats from Objective 1, there was no indication of any effect of thermal history on mate choice in the field. We, therefore, conclude that the thermal effect on mate choice is likely irrelevant and hence terminated further mating experiments in the laboratory. Alternatively, we decided to examine the mechanisms of mate choice in situ. Our findings in the surveys to achieve Objective 1 showed that these snails mated only when awash by the rising tides and they formed hundreds of mating pairs on the shore during this period, especially for the two high-shore littorinids. Mating activities at such high intensity allowed us to sample mating pairs and their adjacent non-mating individuals to measure mate choice. Given the high numbers of individuals mating at any given awash phase on the rising time we could also use these assessments to determine the scale (i.e. distance) over which choice was being made by the individuals, and test theories of spatial scale in determining mate choice. As our major focus of this study is the strength of sexual selection (which has already been achieved in Objective 1) instead of its underlying mechanism, we used only E. malaccana for this additional experiment. Given the high intensity of mating activity this work was also used to develop appropriate methods (using the Scale of Choice Effect) for assessing mate choice (in E. malaccana and E. radiata) on the shore. Objective 3: To predict the resilience of littorinids under rapid climate warming (100% achieved) This objective has been achieved by measuring the thermal safety margin (TSM) and thermal performance curves (TPCs) of the three littorinids, in addition to the natural and sexual selection pressures investigated in the previous two objectives. TSM measures how close a species is living to its thermal limits, and thus serves as a sensitivity estimate to further increases in environmental temperatures (i.e. the wider the TSM, the less sensitive and hence less vulnerable to warming scenarios). TPCs measure the relative performance of a species under various temperatures, and thus allow the examination of the optimal temperature range and how the species’ living environment deviates from the optimal conditions. Both concepts have been widely applied as crucial indicators of species sensitivity and vulnerability in studies forecasting species’ response to warming scenarios. Maximum body temperatures obtained from thermal imaging in the field and lethal thermal limits obtained from previous studies were used to calculate the TSM. Locomotor performance (i.e. change in movement speed with temperature; a proxy of foraging) and oxygen consumption (a proxy of metabolism) were two performance metrics (one behavioural one physiological) used in the three littorinids. By considering changes in physiological/behavioural responses and selection pressures in a holistic manner under different thermal regimes, we were able to elucidate the resilience of the tropical littorinids to climate warming.

17121914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121914.value: All three species partitioned their activities across the tidal cycle, foraging and mating intensively during thermally-benign periods (rising tides) and exhibiting stress mitigating (e.g. thermoregulatory) behaviours during stressful periods (low tides). Thermoregulatory behaviours can be summarized as fight and flight reponses (Ng et al. 2017; fight: modifying their environment by shell posturing behaviours; flight: retreating to refuges). These behaviours were effective stress-mitigating strategies, reducing body temperatures of the high shore species by 4.4℃ (average) and up to 10.3℃ with respect to the environment. These behaviours intensified with the thermal gradient (i.e. hotter sites = higher intensity of these behaviours) and with daily weather conditions (hotter days = higher intensity of these behaviours), showing plasticity in the snails’ behaviours according to their thermal conditions. Positive sexual selection on both female (males prefer large females) and male size (large males were more successful in mating competitions) was recorded in E. malaccana (Ng et al. 2019). No clear pattern of changing mating intensities, sexual selection pressure and female fecundity was observed across the thermal gradient, suggesting that priori exposure to various thermal regimes did not contribute significantly to variation in mating patterns (Ng et al. 2016). Exposure to various thermal regimes did not affect the benefits associated with males choosing large females. Physiological tolerance of snails did not vary with size or sex, suggesting that climate warming may not select for snail size. Sexual selection, therefore, has a limited role in modulating adaptation to climate warming. There was no clear difference in TSM between littorinids living at different shore heights, but a decoupling of behavioural and physiological TPCs with decreasing shore height (SLY Lau, unpublished data), suggesting high shore species lower metabolism during emersion to conserve energy; contradicting the paradigm that high shore species are most vulnerable to warming scenarios. This study also advanced two research areas: firstly, using a novel method developed by our team (Fernandez-Mireman et al., 2017) our experiments on sexual selection in E. malaccana demonstrated that littorinids exercised their mate choice within a very short distance (within 10cm, Estevez et al., 2018), representing one of the first times that spatial scale of mate choice was assessed in invertebrates; secondly, by using standardized methods to study sexual selection patterns across marine gastropods, we were able to generalize that sexual selection did not play a key role in shaping size in marine gastropods, contradicting the conventional paradigm (Ng et al., 2016).

17121914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121914.value: Mobile animals are not prisoners to climate warming and behavioural adaptations are vital to survival in extreme environments. Littorinid snails rapidly detect and respond behaviourally according to the dynamic intertidal environment. Further understanding such small-scale (i.e. day-to-day, site-to-site) decision making (i.e. when to do what) is important to determine key questions of what triggers certain physiological/behavioural responses; the associated costs of such responses; and how adaptive such responses are in the long term. Such decisions may provide a key to understanding the evolutionary importance of such tradeoffs in responses used. As behaviour is tidally-driven, there is a clear segregation of littorinid active/inactive phases which has led to a unique decoupling of behavioural and physiological performances (TPCs). Investigating how these TPCs change with thermal stress will provide insights on how such traits are shaped through time. Finally, integration of these physiological and behavioural responses with more detailed ‘omics techniques to establish physiological pathways being utilized and their associated metabolic costs will allow the development of predictive models to highlight threshold energetic and thermal climate conditions for species in extreme environments. This integration of ecological/physiological and ‘omics techniques can help elucidate the adaptive capacity of species towards future changing climates.

17121914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121914.value: Climate warming is the most alarming global threat and scientists have been attempting to predict how species’ will perform to warming scenarios. In this context, current theories predict that species living in the tropics and in extreme environments are the most sensitive to climate warming. Most studies address species’ physiological tolerances and often neglect mitigating behavioural responses and how these affect sexual or natural selection. Using snails living in the physically stressful high zone of tropical rocky shores, this study used a holistic approach to assess multiple aspects of their ecology (e.g. behavioural patterns, thermal tolerance, fecundity etc.) and the interplay of natural and sexual selection (thermal tolerance, relative performance and mate selection) in the context of climate warming. Effects of thermal stress were investigated at different scales (shore heights across sites with different thermal environments for three species) and on both physiological, behavioural and mate choice responses of these species. In general, snails were able to show behavioural and physiological responses which were site and time dependent to ensure their survival; and thermal stress did not affect their reproductive performance. These high shore tropical species therefore, have evolved a high level of resilience towards climate warming, challenging conventional theories.

17122014.label: Realisation of objectives
17122014.value: Objective 1: Peritoneal metastasis is an important factor affecting the prognosis of patients with ovarian cancer. The attachment of ascitic ovarian tumor sphere forming cells to the peritoneal mesothelium is a key and pivotal step to the onset of the metastatic spread. This tumor cell lodgment requires the presence of specialized adhesion molecules capable of binding under shear stress, but not static, conditions. Thus, it is important to develop 3D tumor model that recapitulates shear-induced changes and, consequently, natural tumor progression in real time. Here, we developed a clinically relevant 3D model generated under controlled physiological shear stress conditions, which could serve as a precise experimental model to study molecular mechanisms involved in ovarian tumor progression. Using this 3D-microfluidic platform and flow cytometry, we identified sLex glycoprotein as a ligand that played potential roles during rolling and firm adhesion events in the metastatic cascade. Glycosyltransferases/glycosidases in glycosylation machinery involved in the synthesis of sLex such as a1,4-galactosyltransferase 1, a2,3-sialytransferase 3, and a1,3-fucosyltransferase 5 (FUT5) were significantly increased in highly metastatic (M-) compared to non-metastatic (NM)-CSCs. While the sLex glycan displayed canonical biochemical features such as sialofucosylation and nonsulfation, our data also unveiled novel features of sLex different from other sLex ligands (2, 3). Knocking down FUT5, a key enzyme in the synthesis of sLex, suppressed adhesion of M-CSCs and metastatic spread in mice. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: We show for the first time that M-CSCs and NM-CSCs differed in their adhesion efficiency to the peritoneal mesothelium under physiological flow conditions. M-CSCs, as compared to NM-CSCs, exhibited slower rolling velocity, with an average rolling velocity of 56.7±0.4 um/s (at least 2-fold less than required for NM-CSCs), higher tethering frequency (1.8-fold at 0.05 dynes/cm2), and bound more firmly to the peritoneal mesothelium. The maximum adhesion percentage was found at 0.04 to 0.07 dynes/cm2, which matches with ascitic shear stress. In addition to E-selectin, we showed that P-selectin expressed by the peritoneal mesothelium also played an important role in this interaction. P-selectin had a greater strength than E-selectin in adhesion. Treatment with anti-E-, P- or L-selectin increased the rolling velocities of M-CSCs when compared with that of isotype control (24.8% increase by anti-E-selectin, 63.3% increase by anti-P-selectin, and 22.5% increase by anti-L-selectin in median rolling velocities). Notably, blockade of P-selectin almost completely abrogated (~88%) tumor-mesothelial adhesion, whereas inhibition of E-selectin or L-selectin had partial effects (48% by anti-E-selectin; 28% by anti-L-selectin). Consistently, significant adherence to P-selectin-Fc (59%), but not E-selectin- or L-selectin-Fc, was observed with M-CSCs. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: We show for the first time that the sLex-P-selectin interaction activates P-cadherin, but not other cadherins or b1 integrin, for the firm adhesion to the peritoneal mesothelium. Moreover, this adhesion activates specific downstream signaling paths to confer metastatic success. We found that P-cadherin could activate the accumulation of p120 catenin in the cytoplasm and the subsequent tumor cell migration and invasion. The use of P-cadherin siRNA or neutralizing antibody to inhibit P-cadherin expression and function resulted in diminished p120 catenin activation, confirming that the effect was P-cadherin specific. Moreover, we showed an essential role for insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) as a novel sLex-bearing ligand in the peritoneal milieu, which in turn activated mesothelial cells. P-cadherin was associated with complex formation with IGF-1R, which could induce the ligand-independent activation of IGF-1R. Inhibition of IGF-1R expression or its activity significantly inhibited the P-cadherin-dependent p120ctn activation. Furthermore, we uncovered a new link of microRNA-199a-3p, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt, and multidrug transporter activation in shear stress-induced CSC enrichment. Percentage achieved: 100% These findings not only reveal a novel class of sLex ligand but also unveil a previously unrecognized role for P-selectin in mediating tumor-mesothelial adhesive interactions under shear stress, which provide new perspectives on shear stress-based biology in the peritoneum, and that its targeting may represent a potential therapeutic advantage for metastatic ovarian cancer. 17122014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122014.value: Objective 1: We have developed a customizable microfluidic platform to overcome the technical limitations of the conventional approaches and to recapitulate peritoneal dissemination in dynamic flow. Using this microfluidic platform, we have uncovered a novel sLex-bearing P-selectin ligand in ovarian cancer cells, which is distinct from those previously defined P-selectin ligands. Very little is known about the selectin ligands on ovarian carcinoma cells. The sLex-bearing glycan present on M-CSCs binds P-selectin in a rigid fucosylation-dependent and relatively loose sialyation-dependent manner, instead of a simple sLex structure that relies equally on fucose and sialic acid moieties. Such biochemistry is of biological significance, as fucosylation has been shown with increased affinity and bind selectin more efficiently. Whereas sulfation is a common feature of P-selectin ligands, our results suggest that the sLex-bearing glycan on M-CSCs does not require sulfation for its binding to P-selectin. There is evidence that sulfated polysaccharides of P-selectin ligands tend to be more resilient to stress which is required for binding under high shear conditions. Publications: Journal articles: #1, #3 Conference proceeding: #6-8 Objective 2: We show for the first time that CSCs were effectively captured to HPMCs at 0.03-0.15 dynes/cm2 (a physiologically relevant range of shear stress of the ascites) with maximal activity at a shear stress of 0.05 dynes/cm2, consistent with a catch bond that requires a clear threshold shear to initiate rolling. Strikingly, both the kinetic and mechanical properties that govern tumor-mesothelial interaction were significantly different between the two CSCs populations. Compared with NM-CSC, M-CSCs had a higher tethering frequency and lower rolling velocity on HPMCs, resulting in a higher percentage of firm adhesion of M-CSCs to HPMCs. Mechanistically, this interaction is mediated by P-selectin expressed by the peritoneal mesothelium. Tumor xenograft models and clinical samples corroborate the relevance of these findings. Publications: Journal articles: #1 Conference proceeding: #6-8 Objective 3: On exploring how the sLex-P-selectin interaction mediates firm adhesion, we show that this is through a critical member, P-cadherin. Moreover, we show that sLex-P-selectin can transduce an outside-in p120 catenin metastatic signaling cascade through the crosstalk of IGF-1R and P-cadherin. This may provide an attractive mechanism whereby sLex-P-selectin can affect tumor progression in ovarian cancer and may explain the highly aggressive behavior of ovarian tumors expressing these two molecules. Furthermore, we uncovered a new link of microRNA-199a-3p, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt, and multidrug transporter activation in shear stress-induced CSC enrichment. These findings not only shed new light on the significance of hydrodynamics in cancer progression, but also emphasize the need of a flow-informed framework in the development of therapeutics. Publication: Journal article: #2, #4 Conference proceeding: #5 Taken together, our data strongly support the important role for a sLex-P-selectin cascade in ovarian cancer metastasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for targeting the sLex-P-selectin cascade or its associated signaling in the treatment of metastatic ovarian cancer.

17122014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122014.value: We reveal the novel identification of sLex-P-selectin cascade on tumor-mesothelial adhesion under ascitic fluid shear flow that has a pivotal role in the metastatic progression of ovarian cancer. This reveals a new direction for understanding the oncogenic role of sLex-P-selectin in ovarian cancer metastasis and implicate that sLex-P-selectin could be a promising therapeutic target. Our findings underscore a critical role for FUT5 during the development and maintenance of the metastasis. While most of the glycosyltransferases genes involved in sLex synthesis are constitutively expressed to produce sLex direct precursor, FUT5 catalyzing the last and rate-limiting step of sLex synthesis by adding fucose to the precursor are normally switched off. We are actively pursuing in this direction to document such effect using more extensive in vitro, in vivo, and clinicopathological studies. Given that glycans can be rationally selected based on the targeted glycosyltransferase, it is of great interest to identify the key enzyme in this process. Peritoneal metastasis has also been detected in patients with breast, gastric, and colon cancer. To expand our understanding of the sLex-P-selectin cascade, we plan to examine if this sLex-P-selectin cascade is also seen in other tumor types in which peritoneal metastasis is an important pathological process. We will also examine the level and effect of sLex-P-selectin interaction in healthy donors or non-cancerous patients. These findings should highlight the functional importance of sLex-P-selectin in impacting malignant cell behavior and implies important clinical implications.

17122014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122014.value: One of the greatest unmet needs compromising the successful treatment of cancer is metastasis. A critical, rate-limiting step of metastasis is the ability of tumor cells to colonize specific target organs, which involves specific cell-cell recognition. Moreover, tumor cell lodgement requires binding under shear stress, but not static, conditions. Therefore, unraveling the intricate details of this particular adhesion is of obvious importance. Several of our new findings of this project indicate that the sLex-P-selectin cascade is a pivotal regulator of tumor-mesothelium interaction under ascitic fluid shear flow and that it could be a promising target. (i) We show for the first time a preferential binding of the metastatic populations of cancer stem/tumor-initiating cells than the non-metastatic populations of cancer stem/tumor-initiating cells to the peritoneal mesothelium. (ii) We also present evidence that this interaction is mediated by a sLex-P-selectin cascade. (iii) We uncover a new uncommon non-sulfated sLex epitope serves as a distinct P-selectin binding determinant. These results reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic roles of a sLex-P-selectin cascade and highlight its importance as a viable therapeutic target. Targeting sLex-P-selectin may thus be a useful approach to decrease metastatic colonization, the most distressing complication for ovarian cancer.

17122214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122214.value: Hepatocellullar Carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies in the world. Prognosis of HCC is extremely poor due to the lack of promising curative therapy. Although liver is a metabolic organ, knowledge regarding the metabolic alterations in HCC is scarce. Better understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms and the metabolic machineries in HCC is warranted for new therapeutic intervention. Uncontrollable growth in HCC is accompanied with a rapid increase of oxygen (O2) consumption, leading to hypoxia in regions of the tumor bulk. Cancer cells adapt to hypoxia mainly through transcription factor, hypoxia-inducible factor-1 (HIF-1), which acts as a master regulator to optimize mitochondrial respiration to maximize cancer growth. HIF-1 directly activates genes that promote glycolysis and many of which have been shown to be implicated in cancers. Our preliminary data demonstrated that a mitochondrial protein, NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 alpha subcomplex, 4-like 2 (NDUFA4L2), was drastically induced by hypoxia and was significantly up-regulated in human HCC. Pharmacologic inhibition or genetic knockdown of HIF-1 suppressed hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 expression. NDUFA4L2 is located in complex I of the electron transport chain where most of the reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the cells are generated. Interestingly, knockdown of NDUFA4L2 in HCC cells promoted intracellular ROS accumulation and suppressed HCC cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo. Based on these data, we hypothesize that HIF-1 confers growth advantage to HCC cells by transcriptionally activating NDUFA4L2. NDUFA4L2, through attenuating mitochondrial activity to reduce ROS production, promotes HCC survival and growth. In this proposal, we will first investigate the clinical and prognostic significance of NDUFA4L2 overexpression in HCC with an expanded sample cohort. Second, we will delineate the regulatory pathway that drives NDUFA4L2 overexpression in HCC cell lines and HCC clinical samples. Third, we will comprehensively study the metabolic functions of the HIF-1/NDUFA4L2 pathway in HCC. Fourth, as this metabolic alteration is driven by HIF-1, we will examine the suppressive effect of HIF inhibitor in HCC progression in vitro and in vivo. In sum, our study will be the first to provide clinical evidence about the deregulation of NDUFA4L2 in HCC and the oncogenic roles of NDUFA4L2 in vivo. Our study will also provide invaluable insights about the metabolic machineries and the adaptive mechanisms of HCC cells. 17122214.label: Realisation of objectives
17122214.value: All the objectives of the proposal have been addressed and hypothesis has been proven with data. Objective 1: Clinical relevance of NDUFA4L2 expression in human HCC To better understand the hypoxia-adaptation system in HCC, we performed transcriptome sequencing to compare the gene expression profiles of a HCC cell line, MHCC97L, that were exposed to normoxia (20% O2) and hypoxia (0.1% and 1% O2). Intriguingly, when we interrogated the expression of genes that are involved in the mitochondrial complex I, only the subunit NDUFA4L2 was distinctly and dramatically up-regulated in hypoxia (both 0.1% and 1% O2) while all the other subunits remained unaffected or down-regulated. We further examined the transcriptome sequencing data on 16 primary HCCs and their corresponding non-tumorous (NT) livers and found that NDUFA4L2 was substantially over-expressed in HCC tissues. Moreover, over-expression of NDUFA4L2 mRNA was validated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in a separate, larger cohort of 100 pairs of HCC samples. Furthermore, over-expression of NDUFA4L2 in HCC tumors was significantly associated with aggressive pathological features including presence of tumor microsatellite formation and absence of tumor encapsulation. More importantly, over-expression of NDUFA4L2 tended to be associated with poorer overall survival of HCC patients. TCGA database which includes transcriptome sequencing data of 49 pairs of HCC and NT liver tissues from an independent cohort echoed with our in-house data. Objective 2: Regulation of NDUFA4L2 in human HCC To investigate whether NDUFA4L2 expression was mediated by HIFs under hypoxia, we generated HCC cells, MHCC97L, that stably expressed short hairpin RNA (shRNA) against HIF-1α (-shHIF-1α) or HIF-2α (-shHIF-2α). The hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 expression was markedly abolished when HIF-1α, but not HIF-2α was knocked down. We further established HIF-1α knockout cells by Transcription Activator-like Effector Nuclease (TALEN) approach and found that hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 expression was drastically abrogated. Digoxin inhibited HIF-1 protein synthesis and profoundly inhibited hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 expression in a dose dependent manner. In addition, by in silico analysis, we identified two potential hypoxia response elements (HREs) containing the core HIF binding sequence motif 5’-RCGTG-3’ at the promoter of NDUFA4L2. ChIP assay in cell lines of different origins, MHCC97L and HeLa cells, indicated that DNA was enriched when HIF-1α antibody was used, as compared to the IgG control. Objective 3: Functional implications of HIF-1/NDUFA4L2 pathway in HCC To investigate the functions of hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 in mitochondria in vitro, we generated NDUFA4L2 loss-of-function and gain-of-function HCC cell models. For NDUFA4L2 loss-of-function HCC cell model, shRNA against NDUFA4L2 (shL2) or non-target control (NTC) was stably expressed in MHCC97L cells by lenti-viral transfection approach. For NDUFA4L2 gain-of-function HCC cell model, NDUFA4L2 and empty vector (EV) were stably expressed in another HCC cell line which expressed a lower level of NDUFA4L2, PLC/PRF/5 (PLC). As NDUFA4L2 is located in the first complex of the ETC, we asked if NDUFA4L2 would affect the mitochondrial activity by staining the cells with a probe, JC-1, which accumulates in active mitochondria to indicate mitochondrial potential. We showed that the mitochondrial membrane potential was decreased in hypoxia but was elevated when NDUFA4L2 was knocked down. Mitochondrial mass was increased in NDUFA4L2 knockdown cells as indicated by the nonyl acridine orange (NAO) staining. Consistently, we found that oxygen consumption in the mitochondria was significantly elevated when NDUFA4L2 was knocked down under hypoxia. HIF-1α knockout mirrored the effect of NDUFA4L2 knockdown in oxygen consumption, further supporting the regulatory role of HIF-1α on NDUFA4L2. Hypoxia triggers an imbalanced electron flow through the ETC leading to generation of ROS in the mitochondria. Hence, we evaluated the intracellular ROS level by the general ROS indicator, chloromethyl-2’,7’-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (CM-H2DCFDA) and mitochondrial ROS indicator, MitoSOXTM. ROS level was elevated when cells were exposed to hypoxia and was further induced when NDUFA4L2 was knocked down especially under hypoxic condition. Reversely, a significant reduction of ROS was found in NDUFA4L2 overexpressing HCC cells. To demonstrate the roles of ROS in HCC cells, we employed two antioxidants, N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) and L-ascorbic acid. ROS induced by NDUFA4L2 knockdown was rescued dose dependently by both antioxidants. To further demonstrate the regulation of HIF-1α on NDUFA4L2 in ROS scavenging, we re-expressed NDUFA4L2 in HIF-1α knockdown PLC cells. ROS was dramatically induced in HIF-1α knockdown cells under hypoxia and was significantly rescued upon re-expression of NDUFA4L2. Excessive accumulation of ROS can cause cell senescence and apoptosis, eventually leading to cell death. We therefore evaluated apoptosis by annexin V-propidium iodide (PI) staining in MHCC97L-NTC and -shL2 cells. MHCC97L-NTC cells showed higher annexin V and PI staining under hypoxic than normoxic condition, while knockdown of NDUFA4L2 further increased apoptosis, which could be rescued by extracellular glutathione ethyl ester (GSH-EE), a modified and more permeable form of glutathione, an antioxidant that counteracts mitochondrial ROS. Consistently, both the cell counting and 5-bromo-2’-deoxyuridine (BrdU) assays showed that cell proliferation was substantially reduced when NDUFA4L2 was knocked down especially under hypoxic condition. More interestingly, cell proliferation was restored by NAC in the NDUFA4L2 knockdown HCC cells, suggesting that impairment of cell proliferation was associated with ROS. All these data converged to show that NDUFA4L2 was responsible to reduce ROS under hypoxia, thereby maintaining cell survival and promoting cell proliferation. To demonstrate the functions of NDUFA4L2 in tumor growth in vivo, we orthotopically injected the luciferase-labeled MHCC97L-NTC and -shL2 cells into nude mice. MHCC97L-NTC tumors grew substantially larger than the MHCC97L-shL2 tumors. We further dissociated the tumors and measured the ROS level of the tumors derived from MHCC97L-NTC and -shL2 cell lines. Consistent with our in vitro data, knockdown of NDUFA4L2 elevated ROS in vivo. Moreover, knockdown of NDUFA4L2 markedly repressed growth of metastatic lesions in the lungs of the tumor-bearing mice as indicated by Xenogen imaging (4 out of 6 in MHCC97L-NTC and 1 out of 6 in -shL2 group). Objective 4: Effect of pharmacologic inhibition of HIF-1/NDUFA4L2 pathway in HCC growth We found that hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 tightly regulated REDOX homeostasis and survival in HCC cells, and HIF-1α is the central regulator of NDUFA4L2. We therefore reasoned that HIF inhibitor could repress the tumors that express high levels of NDUFA4L2 by damaging HCC cells through elevating ROS. We evaluated the ROS levels of MHCC97L-NTC and -shL2 cells treated with a HIF inhibitor, digoxin, under hypoxic condition. We observed that digoxin was more efficient in elevating the ROS level in MHCC97L-NTC cells than -shL2 cells. Next we evaluated the effect of digoxin in vivo. We performed orthotopic implantation of the luciferase-labeled MHCC97L-NTC and -shL2 cells in nude mice. One week after implantation, mice were administered with 1.2 mg/kg/day digoxin or vehicle control (saline) through intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection for 21 days. Digoxin markedly repressed growth of tumors with a more prominent effect on the MHCC97L-NTC group as compared to MHCC97L-shL2 group. Similarly, digoxin decreased the growth of subcutaneous tumors derived from MHCC97L-EV cells more significantly as compared to MHCC97L-shHIF-1α cells. Meanwhile, body weights of the animals were not affected by digoxin. These results suggested that HIF inhibitor block HCC progression at least partially through HIF-1α/NDUFA4L2.

17122214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122214.value: Liver is well characterized as a major metabolic organ; however, the metabolic machineries driving hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression remains poorly understood. Oxygen (O2) deprivation, hypoxia, is frequently found in regions of tumors with insufficient blood supply. Hypoxia stabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) which transcriptionally activates genes that utilize glycolysis over oxidative phosphorylation for ATP production. This metabolic switch reduces mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production that would otherwise occur due to electron imbalance through the electron transport chain (ETC) in hypoxic condition. In our transcriptome sequencing analysis, among all the mitochondrial subunits in the complex I of the ETC, only NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 alpha subcomplex 4-like 2 gene (NDUFA4L2) was distinctly and significantly induced by hypoxia and over-expressed in human HCC. We further provided evidence that NDUFA4L2 was indispensable for HCC survival for its ability to reduce ROS under hypoxia. Our findings are important for the following reasons: 1. Our study provided the first clinical data regarding the expression of NDUFAL2 in human cancers including HCC. We showed that overexpression of NDUFA4L2 in human HCC was correlated with aggressive HCC clinicopathological parameters including absence of tumor encapsulation, formation of tumor microsatellite, and poorer overall survival. 2. Our study confirmed that NDUFA4L2 was positively regulated by HIF-1α in human HCC. ChIP assay confirmed the binding of HIF-1α with hypoxia response elements (HREs) in NDUFA4L2 promoter and expression study showed that hypoxia-induced NDUFA4L2 was abolished in HIF-1α knockdown or knockout HCC cells. 3. Functionally, we showed that inactivation of HIF-1α/NDUFA4L2 increased the mitochondrial activity that coupled with higher intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ROS-induced apoptosis in HCC cells. 4. By orthotopic liver implantation model, we provided the first in vivo evidence supporting that the oncogenic roles of NDUFA4L2 in cancer development. 5. Therapeutically, we found that HIF inhibitors, digoxin and Sorafenib, profoundly inhibited the growth of HCC that expressed high levels of NDUFA4L2. Taken together, our study has substantially enriched our knowledge on the advantageous metabolic machinery utilized by HCC cells. Particularly, this machinery is governed by HIF-1α/ NDUFA4L2 to reduce intracellular oxidative stress for HCC survival. Targeting HIF-1α/NDUFA4L2 pathway by HIF inhibitors represent a new therapeutic strategy for HCC.

17122214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122214.value: Our work has revealed that NDUFA4L2 might be a good prognostic indicator for hypoxic tumors and aggressive HCC. Our data also suggested that NDUFA4L2 is also important to metabolism of other cancer types and could be used as a prognostic marker for other cancers. Since HIF-1 is difficult to be detected in human samples due to its highly unstable nature, we will further examine whether NDUFA4L2 could be accurately reflecting the level of HIF-1 using mouse tumors. Also, our study revealed that HIF inhibitors might be effective in HCC treatment. We will further evaluate whether HIF inhibitors could be used in combination with other FDA-approved therapies for HCC treatment.

17122214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122214.value: Hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, causes high level of oxidative stress due to unbalanced electron flow in the electron transport chain. To survive hypoxia, HIF-1 activates NDUFA4L2 to decelerate electron flow to alleviate oxidative stress production in cancer cells. NDUFAL2 promotes cancer cell survival and acts as a good prognostic marker for hypoxic and aggressive liver cancer. Targeting HIF-1/NDUFA4L2 by HIF inhibitor also efficiently inhibited liver cancer in preclinical mouse models.

17122914.label: Realisation of objectives
17122914.value: 1. Sample selection Stage I - Development of the RDS for the southern Chinese The samples were randomly selected from the archives of the Prince Philip Dental Hospital (PPDH), Hong Kong. The PPDH is the only dental hospital in Hong Kong and serves as the teaching hospital affiliated with the Faculty of Dentistry at the University of Hong Kong. The subjects were selected from the most recent patient list (within five years) provided by the PPDH using a systematic random sampling method. Starting with the highest patient code number (the most recently registered patient), this patient and then every other patient sequentially was selected until the desired sample size is obtained. The patient’s records were examined for the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The dental panoramic tomograph (DPT) that was taken previously for diagnostic purposes were re-used in this study. Participants’ DPTs and their age information were retrospectively analysed. In order to cover the developmental stages of all the permanent teeth, patients aged from 3 to 22 years (3 years ≤ age group 1 < 4 years,…, 22 years ≤ age group 20 < 23 years; 20 age groups in total) were selected. For each age group, 100 females and 100 males were recruited, resulting a total of 4000 subjects for use in establishing the RDS. Stage II - Validation of the RDS for the southern Chinese The southern Chinese RDS established in Stage I was first validated internally using a sample of DPTs collected in PPDH, Hong Kong. The southern Chinese RDS established in Stage I was then validated externally using a sample of southern Chinese from outside Hong Kong. This sample was randomly selected from a dental hospital in Guangzhou, one of the largest cities in south China. The most recent patients in the age range from 3 to 22 years (25 subjects in each age/gender group, 1000 subjects in total) were selected from the archives of the dental hospital using the same systematic random sampling method described in Stage I. Stage III - Application of the southern Chinese RDS to a northern Chinese population The applicability of the southern Chinese RDS to northern Chinese individuals was tested using a randomly selected sample from the archives of dental hospitals in northern China. The most recent patients in the age range from 3 to 22 years (25 subjects in each age/gender group, 1000 subjects in total) were selected from the archives of the dental hospitals using the same sampling method described in Stage I. 2. Data collection, processing and analysis Participants’ DPTs and their personal information related to age (date of birth and date when the DPT was taken) and ethnicity were collected from the existing records by a research assistant using the same protocol. The DPT were assigned a code, scanned at a resolution of 300 dpi in grey-scale format, and stored as a JPEG image with dimensions of 2440 x 1280 pixels (Epson scanner 1000XL, Epson Inc, USA). The age and ethnicity data were stored separately from the DPT data. The digitised DPTs and the participants’ ages and ethnic information collected from China were brought to the Hong Kong centre for scoring and analysis. Two trained and calibrated examiners evaluated the DPTs. Ten percent of the DPTs were randomly selected using the random numbers generated electronically, and the tooth developmental stages were re-evaluated to test the inter-examiner and intra-examiner reliabilities. The age of attainment was calculated for each tooth development stage using STATA software (STATA version 11.0, STATA Corp). The estimated dental age (DA) was calculated for each subject and compared with the chronological age (CA, gold standard) within each age/gender group.

17122914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122914.value: Stage I - Development of the RDS for the southern Chinese The RDS was established and published using the DPTs collected in PPDH, Hong Kong. The Kappa values of the intra- and inter-examiner repeatabilities for assessing tooth developmental stages were 0.85, 0.85 and 0.83 respectively, indicating that the observed scores were “almost perfect” (Paper No. 1). Stage II - Validation of the RDS for the southern Chinese For the internal validation, the calculated age differences (CA-DA) were 0.05 years (2.6 weeks) for males and 0.03 (1.6 weeks) years for females. The difference in ages between the CA and the DA were not statistically significantly different (p > 0.05). Bland and Altman plots demonstrate that 94% of males and 91% of females were estimated within a range of 2 standard deviations from the mean, which was between 1.83 years and -1.73 years for males and between 1.77 years and -1.71 years for females (Paper No. 1). For the external validation, the mean estimated age differences (DA - CA) were 0.06 years (3.12 weeks) for males and 0.04 (2.08 weeks) years for females. The difference in ages between the CA and the DA were not statistically significantly different (p>0.05). Bland and Altman plots demonstrates that most of the subjects were estimated within a range of 2 standard deviations from the mean, which was between 1.95 years and -1.84 years for males and between 1.86 years and -1.78 years for females (Conference Abstract No. 1). Stage III - Application of the southern Chinese RDS to a northern Chinese population Using data pooled across age groups, Bland-Altman plot showed that the differences between CA and DA were randomly distributed around the mean difference of -0.06 years (SD 0.78 years) in females and -0.10 years (SD 0.70 years) in males. Approximately 95% of the discrepancies between CA and DA were expected to lie within -1.58 years to 1.47 years for females and -1.48 years to 1.28 years for males. For both sexes, most of the discrepancies were within 1 year and more than half were within 0.5 years. Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient was 0.989 for females (95% CI 0.986 - 0.991) and 0.989 for males (95% CI 0.986 - 0.992), both of which were very close to the perfect concordance. The intraclass correlation coefficient values were 0.99 for both sexes, suggesting excellent reliability of the method (Paper No. 2 and Conference Abstract No. 2).

17122914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122914.value: Future studies could be designed to gather specific detailed information and other potential factors for dental age assessment. Malocclusion and dental anomalies should also be taken into consideration in future studies. Future studies establishing reference dataset for northern/southern Chinese based on other methods such as the Nolla’s method, modified Demirjian’s method, and the Cameriere’s method are warranted. Other investigations, especially examinations of applicability of the reference dataset on other ethnic groups could also be conducted to further expand our knowledge of dental age assessment.

17122914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122914.value: Dental development can be used to estimate a person’s chronological age. Dental age is defined as the age estimated by comparing the dental development status of an individual with that of published dental development surveys. It is gender- and ethnicity-specific. Dental age assessment is important because the demand in medico-legal issues is increasing when birth data are missing or undocumented. However, it is methodologically difficult to establish an ethnicity-specific norm of dental age for every ethnic groups. The RDS for the southern Chinese established in this study is a first for Hong Kong to contribute to the international population database of the Dental Age Research London Information Group. This study has proved that the established RDS can be used in Chinese, who constitute nearly one-fifth of the world’s population, for clinical applications and further compare investigations.

17122914.value: Dr Wong led a team of PhD and undergraduate students in the Faculty of Dentistry, The University of Hong Kong to conduct a series of knowledge exchange (KE) programmes to apply dental age assessment to address the social issue of unregistered births in the region. Dr Wong’s team brought dental age assessment and oral health education programmes to two villages in Chennai, India and orphanages in Mainland China. Their public awareness campaigns on importance of birth registration have reached 500 families. Oral health information and oral health education was provided to 300 less privileged children. About 250 undocumented children in rural welfare homes had their ages estimated through their efforts and got their age certificates. The team also wanted to train the trainers in order to sustain the project efforts. They provided training in dental age assessment to about 300 dentists and forensic practitioners in India and Hong Kong. In addition, the team has established a charity, the D.O.B. (Date of Birth) Foundation (www.dob-foundation.org), the first of its kind in the world, to promote accurate birth records. The team has obtained the following awards: 1. Knowledge Exchange Excellence Award 2015, The University of Hong Kong for "Dental Development: An Aid to Give Identities and to Inform General Health". 2. Faculty Knowledge Exchange Award 2015, Faculty of Dentistry, The University of Hong Kong for "Dental Development: An Aid to Give Identities and to Inform General Health". 3. Stephen H Y Wei Award in Paediatric Dentistry 2016 for "Dental Outreach Project - To Special-Need Groups in Nanning & Liuzhou Guangxi, Mainland China".

17123514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123514.value: Tumor-initiating cells (TIC) are dynamic cancer cell subsets that display enhanced tumor functions and resilience to treatment but the mechanism of TIC induction or maintenance in lung cancer is not fully understood. In this study, we show the calcium pathway transcription factor NFATc2 is a novel regulator of lung TIC phenotypes, including tumorspheres, cell motility, tumorigenesis, as well as in vitro and in vivo responses to chemotherapy and targeted therapy. In human lung cancers, high NFATc2 expression predicted poor tumor differentiation, adverse recurrence-free and cancer-specific overall survivals. Mechanistic investigations identified NFATc2 response elements in the 3’ enhancer region of SOX2, and NFATc2/SOX2 coupling upregulates ALDH1A1 by binding to its 5’ enhancer. Through this axis, oxidative stress induced by cancer drug treatment is attenuated, leading to increased resistance in a mutation-independent manner. Targeting this axis provides a novel approach for the long-term treatment of lung cancer through TIC elimination. These findings are published in eLIFE (DOI: 10.7554/eLife.26733.001)

17123514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123514.value: Downstream targets of NFATc2 would be explored using RNA-seq. Several candidates have been found and preliminary studies showed promising results. The data have been incorporated into an application for the HMRF research grant exercise.

17123514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123514.value: Research has shown lung cancers cells in the same tumor display differences. One aggressive cell type called tumor initiating cells (TIC) behave like stem cells and can renew themselves or mature into different cell types. They are thought to help cancers grow and spread, and even promote resistance to treatments. Using human lung cancer cell lines and animal models, we showed that lung TIC had higher levels of a protein called NFATc2. Tumors with higher NFATc2 levels were more aggressive. When NFATc2 was removed from cells, they formed smaller tumors and were more sensitive to drug treatment compared to those retaining NFATc2. NFATc2 helps to increase the levels of SOX2, and together, they stimulate the production of another protein, ALDH, and assist TIC to survive otherwise fatal challenges due to acidosis that result from high metabolic activities within cancer cells. These series of events help to maintain and propagate TIC. These findings improve the understanding of mechanisms regulating TICs in lung cancer, and will help scientists tackle new questions about how this cancer progresses and resists therapy. In the longer-term, combining classic cancer treatments with new therapeutic strategies targeting NFATc2, treatments for lung cancer patients could be made more effective.

17123814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123814.value: 糖尿病黃斑水腫（DME）是導致糖尿病患者喪失視力的一個重要原因。正如它的名字所指出，DME影響負責中央視力的黃斑區（視網膜中心） 。DME的患者的中央視力和日常活動會受到很大影響，如駕駛，閱讀， 配藥以取得正確劑量的藥物，甚至認人也可能會受到影響。 在常規臨床評估檢查中，除了視力檢查及臨床眼部檢查外，黃斑部的光學相干斷層掃描（OCT）已經成為檢查中不可缺少的部分。OCT掃描能顯示黃斑區（視網膜中心）的橫切面，詳細顯示視網膜內的變化，並且可以量化黃斑的厚度。這有助於診斷，協助監測進展情況，並指導適當的治療予DME患者。它是完全非入侵性的，因此是日常檢查理想的工具。 通常，在黃斑中心的總視網膜厚度（CRT）已被用作疾病監測和預測結果的參數。因為視網膜一共有10層以上，有時DME可能引起節段性變化，而不是擴散的病狀，尤其是在早期階段。因此，使用CRT去判斷視力可能並不適用於所有的患者。更多的證據都傾向使用OCT掃描進行視網膜外層的節段性分析，以作為更準確的參數，判斷視力受到的影嚮是否與各種黃斑疾病有關，包括糖尿病性黃斑水腫。例如，在DME患者中，用視網膜（相當於感光細胞層）的最外層的標誌距離去判斷與視力的關係，比CRT來得更好。 從我們的DME患者中，我們得到78個試驗性橫切面數據，顯示在外層視網膜層的新參數比CRT與視力有較高的相關性。我們量度視網膜色素上皮細胞（RPE）和外界膜（ELM）之間的距離。這是之前沒有被研究過的，此數值亦代表感光體本身的完整長度，此長度亦反映感光體的完整性及功能。我們已經證明，此數值與視力的相關性比在其他文獻中公佈的任何參數更高，意味它與視力有更大的相關性， 因而引導更準確的預測結果，以及更準確的治療。 因此，我們想擴大研究規模，在以上建議、有2個相距6個月時間測量點的前瞻性隊列研究納入更多患有DME的研究對象 。有望可以更深入研究這新參數在OCT的角色，以及研究它在根據視力變化預測視力結果的可能性，決定病人是否需要治療。這有助研究OCT造影技術未來為DME患者 的應用方向，以及預測視力結果，並且可促進對疾病演進過程的認識，更能引導更準確的預後預測。

17123814.label: Realisation of objectives
17123814.value: In the current project, we aimed to utilize the various outer retinal landmarks for visual correlation in subjects with diabetic macular edema at two separate visits 6 months apart. We have successfully recruited enough subjects (312 in total) during the study period, and have performed the required assessments on each of them at the two visits. We have demonstrated that the outer retinal landmarks, i.e. central retinal thickness (CRT), external limiting to retinal pigment epithelial distance (ELM-RPE), ellipsoid zone to retinal pigment epithelium distance (EZ-RPE), correlated with visual acuity. We have shown that best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at the final visit correlated with baseline BCVA and EZ-RPE. The successful demonstration of such a significant relationship between baseline EZ-RPE and final visual acuity at 6 months was a prove of the realization of the objectives (objectives 1, 2, & 3) as set out in this project. Although in our pilot data, ELM-RPE had more significant correlation with BCVA, and the original aim of the project was to explore whether ELM-RPE could be used to correlate visual acuity. However, the pilot study we performed and those in the literature were all cross-sectional observational studies with only a single assessment. The current project was the first to use such retinal parameters to correlate visual progress. Hence, there was a fundamental difference in the study design and direct comparison may not be entirely appropriate. We believe results from this project carries a higher impact as the study was better designed with a larger sample size and two assessments spaced out by 6 months. We believe this would represent a more accurate measure of the values of outer retinal landmarks in correlation with vision and visual progression in DME. We have also correlated the need for treatment with these features at baseline. However, we failed to demonstrate any significant correlation between the need to undergo treatment with outer retinal landmarks at baseline. This may be due to the relative short follow up period (i.e. 6 months), may not be enough to show significant progression, hence only a small proportion of subjects required treatment (14.1% received anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections and 24.4% received laser treatment). We are in the process of continuing observation among these subjects beyond the study period, in hope to see if longer follow ups can produce results with higher significance. We hope this would translate into pilot data for future studies along the same theme.

17123814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123814.value: Consecutive subjects with diabetic macular edema (DME) from the diabetic retinopathy screening program at the Department of Ophthalmology, Queen Mary Hospital were recruited. A total of 312 subjects were recruited for the study during the approved period (1-1-2015 to 31-12-2016). The mean age was 65.8 years, and among these, 148 were male (47.4%). At baseline, the mean best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 0.34 0.28 logMAR units (Snellen equivalent 20/44), the mean central retinal thickness (CRT) was 361.3 106.0m, mean distance between the ELM and RPE (ELM-RPE) was 84.0 12.9m, and mean distance between the EZ and the RPE (EZ-RPE) was 55.9 9.9m. A total of 14.1% of subjects required injection of anti-vascular endothelial growth factors and 24.4% required laser treatment during the study period. Multivariate linear regression showed that the final BCVA was significantly associated with baseline BCVA and baseline EZ-RPE. However, it failed to show any significant correlation between baseline OCT features with the need for treatment. The successful demonstration of the correlation of baseline BCVA and EZ-RPE with final visit BCVA was a major finding in our project as this implied that baseline OCT feature (i.e. EZ-RPE) can be used to predict visual acuity at 6 months, regardless of whether treatment was delivered or not. By multivariate linear regression analysis, every 10 µm increase in baseline EZ-RPE was significantly associated with 0.04 logMAR units decrease in BCVA at 6 months (P = 0.024). This relationship has not been shown in the literature. This will add additional implications for performing OCT for patients having DME, as the features on OCT may have prognostic implications other than showing the status of the macular at the particular visit. This will lay foundation for prospective cohort studies with longer follow up period to further investigate the relationship between the need for treatment and the baseline OCT features. Although we failed to demonstrate any significant correlation in this regard in the current project, larger scale studies may be able to demonstrate such a relationship.

17123814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123814.value: As mentioned in the earlier sections, the pilot data which formed the foundation of the current project pointed towards a good correlation between the distance from the external limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium (ELM-RPE) with visual acuity. In the current project, this relationship was not as apparent. However, we successfully found that the distance between the ellipsoid zone to retinal pigment epithelium (EZ-RPE) had a better correlation than the ELM-RPE. Despite this, we failed to show any significant relationship between any of these outer retinal parameters with the need for treatment. As pointed out earlier, as the observation period was only 6 months (due to various limitations when designing the study), clinical progression in DME may not have time to mature. Future plans to carry on the observation until a longer period (i.e. up to 12 month and beyond) are being implemented in hope to identify significant correlation between baseline OCT features and the need for treatment.

17123814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123814.value: Structural changes in the outer retinal layers on optical coherence tomography (OCT) correlates well with vision in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME). However, in real life, due to various reasons, OCT scans are not done every visit for all patients. If these changes can be used to predict clinical progress or need for treatment, there will be additional implications for performing an OCT scan in patients with DME. In the current study, subjects were followed up for 6 months, and clinical progress in terms of visual acuity changes and need for treatment were being correlated with the OCT parameters at baseline. It was found that the distance between the ellipsoid zone to the retinal pigment epithelium on OCT at baseline had a significant relationship with the visual acuity at 6 months. This means that be examining the OCT at baseline, the visual outcome at 6 months could be predicted. This was an important finding as it adds as indication for patients with DME to receive OCT scans every visit, such that it could be used to predict clinical outcome later.

17123914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123914.value: 失聪是一种相对普遍的人类感觉缺失。约800个新生儿中就有1个患有严重的永久性听力损伤。虽然已经有与失聪相关基因的报道，但是仍有许多与人类失聪有关的基因还有待被发现。 Cdo（与细胞黏着分子相关的down-regulated by oncogenes）与 Boc（Brother of Cdo）是两个Hh通路的新受体。在Cdo上的突变会造成前脑无裂畸形，即人类中一种以前脑中线缺陷为特征的先天性异常，这种缺陷明显与Shh信号通路的活性减弱相关。Cdo与Boc是Hh通路最终的目的基因也是通路反馈网络的一部分。Cdo与Boc通过成为Ptch1与Gas1的共受体或者通过调控Gli转录因子，来增强Shh信号。Gli抑制因子和活化因子的平衡对于调控内耳发育过程中Shh信号有着重要作用。 Cdo或Boc基因敲除小鼠会完全失去听力。但是Cdo与Boc在内耳发育过程中的作用还不为人所知。我们的预实验结果率先表明了Cdo 和Boc在内耳上表达。我们发现在E16.5，Cdo与Boc表达在小鼠内耳听毛细胞两侧的非感觉区域。在Cdo与Boc突变小鼠的内耳发育过程中，前感觉特化时伴有细胞增殖减少、过早退出细胞周期的现象以及异位的听毛细胞。基于我们的初步观察，我们推测Cdo与Boc在介导Hh应答的内耳发育过程中非常重要，同时Cdo与Boc调控了感觉前体细胞的特化和听毛细胞的分化。 在这个课题中，我们有以下几个目标：1）描述Cdo-/-, Boc-/-, Cdo-/-; Boc-/-突变小鼠的内耳表型，并通过分析Smo突变将其表型与Hh通路特定的表型区分开来；2）研究Cdo，Boc和Gas1这些Hh通路共受体在内耳发育过程中的作用；3）研究Cdo和FGF通路在柱状细胞特化和分化过程中的相互作用。本项目中，我们拟利用此基因敲除小鼠模型进行遗传学，细胞和分子研究来分析Cdo与Boc突变中细胞特化、增殖和听毛细胞分化过程，阐明其在听囊形成和限制内耳感觉神经区域中的全新作用。本研究将会增进人们对Cdo与Boc在哺乳动物内耳发育过程中的功能的了解，同时也会加深人们对Cdo与Boc在Hh通路中对内耳感觉前体细胞特化的功能的认识。我们的研究结果不仅将揭示一个全新的调控听觉与失聪的分子遗传学通路，加深对耳朵感觉神经元分子发育机制的理解，还将为听毛细胞再生和失聪条件下神经元再连接的临床应用提供理论基础。

To investigate the interactions between Cdo and FGF signaling pathway in pillar cell specification and differentiation Objective 1: To characterize the inner ear phenotypes of Cdo-/-, Boc-/-, Cdo-/-;Boc-/- mutants and to differentiate Hh pathway-specific phenotypes by comparison with Smo mutant analysis Using the Cdo and Boc mutant mice and by genetic analyses, We have shown the developmental defects of cochlear hair cells and supporting cells in Organ of Corti in Cdo and Boc mutant mice. We have shown that Cdo and Boc restrict prosensory domain within Organ of Corti by inhibiting Atoh1 from hair cells induction and differentiation. In Cdo and Boc mutants, the inner ear phenotypes are similar to Smo mutant mice. We have fully achieved Objective 1. Objective 2: To investigate the role of Cdo, Boc and Gas1 co-receptors in the modulation of Hh signaling function in inner ear development We have examined the combinatorial effect of Cdo, Boc and Gas1 co-receptors on the proliferation and hair cell differentiation in modulating Hh signaling in inner ear. We have shown that the overlapping roles of Cdo, Boc and Gas1 in promoting Hh signaling in cochlea. We have made use of Cdo, Boc and Gas1 mutant mice to show that Cdo, Boc and Gas1 are important for the development of hair cell number in the cochlea. We have used Cdo and Boc mutant mouse line. In combination with Gas1 null mutants, we have shown that Cdo and Boc are specifically required for proliferation and hair cell differentiation in cochlea. In addition, based on Cdo;Boc compound mutant studies, we have found that both Cdo and Boc shared redundant roles in the growth and hair cell differentiation of the cochlea. We have fully achieved Objective 2. Objective 3: To investigate the interactions between Cdo and FGF signaling pathway in pillar cell specification and differentiation Cdo, Fgf8 and Fgfr3 work synergistically for pillar cell specification. We have shown that Cdo is involved in regulating pillar cell through FGF signaling. We identified Fgf8 and Fgfr3 genes regulated by Cdo in inner ear development and have validated regulation by molecular and biochemical methods. By genetic, molecular, biochemical and cellular assays we could link Cdo gene into FGF regulatory pathways. We observed that Cdo expression overlaps with Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in pillar cells. We found that there was down-regulation of Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in Cdo-/- mutants. Cdo, Fgf8 and Fgfr3 work synergistically for pillar cell specification. We have shown that Cdo is involved in regulating pillar cell through FGF signaling. Fgf8 acts as an important molecule in mediating the pillar cells formation was examined in Cdo-/- cochlea at early stage E14.5. We found that Fgf8 mRNA expression was abolished in Cdo-/- cochlea by in situ hybridization. We also detected the reduced of Fgf signaling receptors Fgfr3 and Fgf20 that known to be important for pillar cell specification in the Organ of Corti of Cdo-/- mutants. Cdo may be independent of Shh pathway in specifying pillar cell.

17123914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123914.value: We have fully addressed all the objectives. Objective 1 and 2 have been reported in the progress report before. Objective 1. To characterize the inner ear phenotypes of Cdo-/-, Boc-/-, Cdo-/-;Boc-/-mutants; and to differentiate Hh pathway–specific phenotypes by comparison with Smo mutant analysis. Objective 2. To investigate the role of Cdo, Boc and Gas1 co-receptors in the modulation of Hh signaling function in inner ear development Objective 3. To investigate the interactions between Cdo and FGF signaling pathway in pillar cell specification and differentiation 3.1 We have shown that the genetic relationship between Cdo, Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in controlling pillar cell specification. Our data demonstrated that Cdo is specifically expressed in pillar cells in the Organ of Corti at E16.5. This points to a Cdo specific function, which may be independent of Shh pathway in specifying pillar cell. We observed that Cdo expression overlaps with Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in pillar cells. Similar to Cdo-/- mutants, Fgf8-/- and Fgfr3-/- mutants also lack pillar cells. We found that there was down-regulation of Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in Cdo-/- mutants and showed that Cdo, Fgf8 and Fgfr3 work synergistically for pillar cell specification. We generated Cdo+/-;Fgf8+/-, Cdo+/-;Fgfr3+/- and Cdo+/-;Fgf8+/-;Fgfr3+/- compound mutants to show the impact of reducing Cdo, Fgf8 or Fgfr3 on pillar cell development and analyzed the change in pillar cell development using for immunostaining using P75Ntr to mark pillar cells and Myo7A to mark hair cells at E16.5. 3.2 To assess the function of Cdo and Fgf signaling in specifying pillar cell development by gain of-function approach We have shown that the overexpression of Fgf8 and Fgfr3 in cochlea explants at E13.5 leads to ectopic pillar cells. We have also shown that Cdo act in the same or parallel pathway with FGF signaling in pillar cells specification. We used the gain-of-function approach to ectopically expressed Cdo, Boc, Fgf8 and Fgfr3, individually or in combination, are sufficient to induce pillar cells formation. We have isolated and cultured cochlea explants from E13.5 embryos and electroporated Cdo, Boc, Fgf8 and Fgfr3 into the cochlea explants. The electroporated cochlea explants were processed for immunostaining using P75Ntr to mark pillar cells and Myo7A to mark hair cells. We tested the overexpression of Fgf8 and Fgfr3 for compensating the loss of Cdo/Boc function in pillar cells specifications in the Cdo-/- cochlea explants. (Wong et al. 2018a, 2018b Developmental Biology, under review)

17123914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123914.value: Understanding the molecular pathogenesis of Cdo and Boc in underlying the human congenital hearing loss In this study, we have discovered that Cdo and Boc are working in Hh signaling in inner ear development and Cdo/Boc are responsible for mediating the pillar cells and hair cell development. However, how Hh components cooperate in cell type specification and differentiation is unclear. How Cdo/Boc cooperatively function in controlling hair cell and pillar cell specification and the molecular mechanisms controlling these developmental processes will be further investigated. Understanding the role of Cdo by identifying cross talk with FGF signaling in inner ear development Cdo may play a role in Pillar cell specification in Hh-independent function. However, how Cdo/Boc regulates FGF signal transduction will also be an important issue for further study. The molecular mechanisms underlying the functions of Cdo and Boc in the sensory development in cochlea will be further investigated. Aid in strategic development of therapeutic interventions for hearing loss This project will lead to not only novel findings of Cdo and Boc function in Hh signaling pathway in regulating cell fate determination and differentiation in cochlea, but also form the basis for developing future therapeutic strategies to reprogram dysfunctional or degenerating sensory tissues for restoring hearing function.

17123914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123914.value: This project focused on uncovering genetic relationships and signalling pathways in inner ear development. We used a combination of mouse models, cell and cochlea explant culture to dissect the genetic and molecular control of inner ear development. It enabled us to gain knowledge of how genes act in a regulatory network to control the induction and development of sensory organs in inner ear. We have uncovered a pathway by which Cdo/Boc coreceptors in Hh signalling control the establishment of the complex sensory pattern of the inner ear. Mutations in human CDO and BOC cause the congenital hearing defects. Sensorineural deafness is characteristic for hearing disorders and we have provided new insights into the functions of Cdo and Boc in normal inner ear development. We have discovered that Cdo and Boc are essential for maintaining the sensory hair cells and pillar cells within the cochlea, providing new insight into the underlying causes for the hearing defects in human congential deafness. Congenital deafness occurs in one in 800 live births and hearing loss affects one in three elderly people. The new insights into the causes of human deafness provided by this study may lead to the development of therapies for hearing loss.
