17124314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124314.value: 該項目將開發一種新的擴散磁共振波譜（Diffusion MRS）的方法來探討早期椎間盤退變（IVDD）。 IVDD是腰椎相關腰腿痛的主要原因，廣泛流行的一種疾病，導致巨大的社會負擔。雖然IVDD是一個緩慢的過程，臨床診斷IVDD目前主要只在後期的和不可逆的階段進行。因此，有迫切的臨床需求，開發，以便及早發現IVDD新的成像策略。在正常盤，一個組織良好的膠原蛋白網絡中交織著的前列腺素，固定的聚醣。當ECM緩慢降解，這些大分子的片段，然後分離，成為移動。隨著時間的推移，這些大分子片段漏出盤，導致PG減少。最終，滲透壓下降，吸水率的減少，從而導致光盤脫水，形態學變化和受損的生物力學特性。磁共振（MR）為IVDD評估最全面的非侵入性的方式。目前，所有可用的MR檢測的方法是細胞外基質降解發病後大幅發展的病理生理變化。雖然IVDD是一個緩慢的過程，幾乎可以肯定的發展了幾十年，臨床診斷IVDD目前主要只在後期的和不可逆的階段進行。因此，有迫切的臨床需求，開發，以便及早發現IVDD新的成像策略。此外，新的IVDD的治療，現在的發展，將需要鑑定IVDD在分子和微觀層面來評估臨床前和臨床療效的提高了成像的方法。 我們假設擴散MRS可以靈敏地檢測PG和膠原擴散的增加，探討檢測早期椎間盤退變IVDD。 為了測試我們的假說，此研究項目將系統地研究擴散法來檢測，並在IVDD初期表徵ECM降解的能力。為了測試我們的假說，此建議的研究項目將系統地研究了擴散杜法來檢測，並在IVDD初期表徵ECM降解的能力。使用我們7T核磁共振成像掃描儀，我們將首先實現和優化擴散MRS測量。最後，我們將探討採用3T臨床MRI掃描儀在人體內椎間盤擴散MRS的可行性。這種新的无创性磁共振方法的發展將為臨床前和臨床IVDD的研究提供了一個獨特和敏感的成像技術 。我們的結果將有助於早期檢測和臨床IVDD，選IVDD療法的評估，並增加对IVDD在分子和微觀結構方面的基础理解。

17124314.label: Realisation of objectives
17124314.value: The three project objectives have been mostly achieved. #1. Implement and optimize the diffusion MRS acquisition and analysis protocol for accurate and reproducible ECM macromolecular diffusivity measurements in intervertebral discs on a 7T preclinical scanner. This objective #1 has been fully achieved, resulting publications in premium journals of MRI research (i.e., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine, NMR in Biomedicine) and presentations at leading MRI research conference (i.e., International Society of Magnetic Resonance in Medicine, namely, ISMRM). #2. Compare the diffusion MRS method with T1ρ and CEST methods at 7T, and determine whether monitoring ECM integrity by diffusion MRS provides earlier and more sensitive IVDD detection than is possible with these alternative approaches. This objective #2 has been 90% completed. Experimental data have been fully corrected, and results are presently being analysed in details and considered for publication. #3. Finally, as an exploratory objective, we will implement the diffusion MRS protocol on a 3T clinical scanner and examine the feasibility of detecting macromolecular diffusion changes in human intervertebral discs. This exploratory objective #3 has been 65% achieved. The DW MRS sequence protocol has been fully implemented on the 3T Philips scanner available at our institution. We have performed data acquisition in human subjects, and successfully obtained DW MRS spectra at various disc locations. However, the final results are not sufficiently reliable to be conclusive. The reason was the insufficient signal SNR and variations. It is possible to increase SNR by going for better MRI hardware upgrade (namely better spine RF coils) or study at high field human MRI scanners (namely 7T). However, doing so is not feasible in HK due to lack of funding to purchase hardware upgrade to existing 7T scanner or the absence of 7T human MRI scanner. Nevertheless, we are presently collaborating with other research groups at UCSF and NYU (where high performance 7T human MRI scanners are available) to pursue this research direction. In addition, the PhD student train in this project (Dr. Anna Wang) is also presently pursuing this spectroscopy direction at John Hopkins University.

17124314.value: Yes! With advances in MRI hardware and diffusion methodology, diffusion MRS of non-water molecules is expected to provide increasingly valuable and biologically specific information on tissue microstructures and physiology, complementing the traditional diffusion MRI of small and ubiquitous water molecules. The publications so far resulting from this project have been well cited by peers in the international MRI community.

17124314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124314.value: This project developed a new diffusion magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) method to detect extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation during the early stage of intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). IVDD is a leading cause of lumbar spine-related low back pain, a disease of wide prevalence that causes enormous societal burdens. In this project, we have developed and demonstrated that diffusion MRS provides a new method to characterize the ECM degradation processes directly and sensitively. Macromolecule ADCs offer a potentially more sensitive and earlier marker for ECM degradation than the proteoglycan content and T2, and water MR properties during early IVDD. Such diffusion MRI approach offers new ways to directly monitor ECM integrity and degradation processes in vivo at molecular and microstructural levels in both preclinical and clinical settings.

17124514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124514.value: Abstract Traumatic injury in peripheral nervous system (PNS) usually results in nerve tissue loss and creates gap that prevents nerve regeneration. Bridging the gap is one of the most important steps for repairing the damaged PNS tissues for axonal regeneration. Although the autograft is considered as the best material for bridging larger nerve defect gaps, the shortage of donor graft and the potential loss of additional motor and sensory function at the donor site limit its use. Allograft and xenograft are also used to substitute autograft nerve. However, their use is limited by immunological rejection. Due to the lack and limitation of nerve grafts, it is urgent to find substitutions to bridge the gap in nerve tissue for the repair of PNS injuries. Therefore, the purpose of this project is to develop a nerve conduit, a bioactive guidance scaffold, to facilitate axonal regeneration following severe PNS injury with larger nerve defects. The conduit is constructed by a self-assembling nanofiber hydrogel enhanced with electrospun nanofibers serving as conduit sheath. We hypothesize that the nerve conduit can guide regenerating axon linear growth across the site of lesion, sequentially improving regeneration rate and functional recovery. Experiments in the study will determine whether the nerve conduit along can provide benefit effect for axonal regeneration and whether neurotrophic factor with gradient concentration in the nanofibrous conduit can further enhance axonal regeneration. Our study addresses an alternative and important approach for nerve repair after traumatic injury. Findings from the study will enhance our understanding for the mechanisms of axonal regeneration. Any improvement in terms of axonal regeneration will be significant for a potential clinical application for nerve tissue loss due to traumatic injury. 周圍神經系統（PNS）的創傷性損傷通常導致神經組織的損失和產生間隙，影响神經的再生。修復受損的PNS組織是軸突再生的最重要的步驟之一。雖然PNS移植被認為是最好的，較大的神經缺損很难找到供體和額外的運動。即使有，感覺功能的損失限制了它的使用。同種異體PNS移植和異種移植也可用來代替自體移植的神經。然而，它們的使用由于免疫排斥反應而受限制。由於缺乏供神經移植的PNS，迫切需要尋找可用于外周神经再生的替代物做搭桥，以使周围神经得以再生。 因此，這個項目的目的是開發一種神經導管及生物活性導向支架，以方便軸突再生。該導管是由一種自組裝納米纖維凝膠加強與作為導管鞘納米纖維構成。我們推測，神經導管能夠引導再生軸突線性增長橫跨病變的部位，依次提高再生率和功能恢復。在研究中的實驗將確定神經導管是否沿可提供好處的效果為軸突再生和是否與在納米纖維導管梯度濃度的神經營養因子可以進一步增強軸突再生。 我們的研究涉及外傷後神經修復的替代和重要途徑。從研究的結果將提高我們理解神經軸突再生的機制。任何改善軸突再生方面將是一個潛在的臨床應用神經組織損失顯著因外傷。

17124514.label: Realisation of objectives
17124514.value: Both objectives stated in the application were achieved. In the current study, we designed two self-assembling nanofiber hydrogels (SAPs) by appending RADA 16-I with epitopes: IKVAV and RGD, which had different net charges and amphiphilic properties at neutral pH. These hydrogels solidify upon administration to biological tissues due to changes in pH and can be combined to increase bioactivity. We thus achieved our first objective, to develop a true 3 dimensional bioactive nanofibrous conduit. Our second objective involved testing the effects of the developed hydrogel on neuronal regeneration after peripheral nerve injury. We achieved this by injecting the RADA 16-Mix hydrogel into the transected rat sciatic nerve gap and effect on axonal regeneration was examined and compared with the traditional RADA16-I hydrogel.

17124514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124514.value: In the current study, we have made two designer self-assembling nanofiber hydrogels (SAPs) by appending RADA 16-I with epitopes: IKVAV and RGD, which had different net charges and amphiphilic properties at neutral pH. The self-assembly of the designer nanofiber hydrogels is intensively investigated as a function of pH, canion type, and assembly time. Our study indicated that both electrostatic and hydrophilic/hydrophobic interactions of the motifs exhibited influences on the self-assembly, consequentially affecting the fiber morphologies and rheological properties. Moreover, our study documented that NaOH induced a quicker assembly/reassembly of the designer nanofiber hydrogels than Tris because of its strong ionic strength as well as the possibility that Na+ helped the peptides to adopt transitional expanded α-helical conformation in order to induce better interaction sites for self-assembly as compared with Tris. Therefore, our study gained insight into comprehensive information on the self-assembling mechanism as references for developing RADA 16-I-based functional SAPs. In vitro study showed that the new SAPs (mixture of two designer SAPs defined as RADA 16-Mix hydrogel) provide better 3D environment for cultured cell survival than the traditional RADA 16. In order to facilitate the transplantation of SAPs hydrogels, a conduit was fabricated by electrospinning poly-L-(lactic acid) onto a rotating metallic rod attached to a rotating mandrel, generating a PLLA conduit with an inner diameter of 1mm with a wall thickness of 150µm. To determine the viability of using the newly developed hydrogel, we transplanted the RADA 16-Mix hydrogel-loaded PLLA conduit into transected rat sciatic nerve gaps and effect on axonal regeneration was examined and compared with the traditional RADA16-I hydrogel. The regenerated nerves were found to grow along the walls of the large cavities formed in the graft of RADA16-I hydrogel, while the nerves grew into the RADA 16-Mix hydrogel toward distal position. RADA 16-Mix hydrogel induced more axons regeneration and Schwann cells immigration than RADA16-I hydrogel, resulting in better functional recovery as determined by the gait-stance duration percentage and the formation of new neuromuscular junction structures.

17124514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124514.value: Due to their consistency and lack of a fluid-gel state, composite hydrogels are more directly applicable to injuries in the CNS, such as traumatic brain injury, stroke or spinal cord injury, than for the direct treatment of nerve gaps in the peripheral nervous system. Embedding the hydrogels within a suitable conduit overcomes this physical limitation in the PNS. Our results indicated that the functional SAP RADA16-Mix nanofibrous hydrogel provided a better environment for peripheral nerve regeneration than RADA16-I hydrogel and could be potentially used in peripheral nerve injury repair. Furthermore, the transplanted system may be seeded with cells to enhance growth factor synthesis and further encourage regeneration. The hydrogel mix alone may be suitable for enhancing regeneration after traumatic injuries in the central nervous system, but robust animal studies would be required to assess this.

17124514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124514.value: Injuries to the nervous system are particularly debilitating due to the reduced regeneration capacity of neurons. Some injuries can cause damage to nerve tracts that takes months or years to regenerate, while injuries that cause nerve gaps can very rarely be overcome. Nanomaterials represent an engaging opportunity to develop strategies for nerve regeneration. In the present study, we designed a bioactive conduit loaded with a mixed hydrogel and evaluated its effect in promoting the recovery of peripheral nerve injury using an animal model. The improved hydrogel and the unmodified version were transplanted to bridge a gap in the rat sciatic nerve, and the morphology of the nerves and more importantly, the functional recovery were assessed comparatively. The axonal regeneration target muscular re-innervation and motor functional recovery were thoroughly assessed and found to have improved after RADA16-Mix treatment. The improved hydrogel combined with conduit show promise in the treatment of severe peripheral nerve injuries. Our study addresses an alternative and important approach for nerve repair after traumatic injury.

17124614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124614.value: We have conducted a series studies in type 1 diabetic rat models of myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury and find that cardiac FoxO1 is activated in the diabetic rats that was accompanied with exacerbated post-ischemic myocardial infarction. Further, we confirmed that inhibition of FoxO1 can protect the diabetic hearts against myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury in rats. We find that treatment that can enhance adiponectin can attenuate FoxO1-mediated exacerbation of myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury in diabetic hearts in vivo, and additional study is on the way to further explore the potential interplay between adiponectin and foxO1 in this pathology. Increase of cardiac Foxo1 may be major a mechanism that rendered diabetic hearts to loss responsiveness to postconditioning cardioprotection (J Diabetes Res. 2016;2016:9213034). FoxO1 in mediating PDK4 expression and subsequent PDH inactivation in the heart and also activation of cardiac apoptosis may represent major mechanisms whereby inhibition of FOXO1 improves cardiac function in early stage of diabetic cardiomyopathy in Type 1 diabetic rats and may provide a promising therapeutic target to treat the disease. We further extended the study to show that treatments (such as pterostilbene) that can stimulate AMPK, a metabolic regulator, may suppressing cardiac oxidative stress and apoptosis to attenuates diabetic myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (Cellular Physiol Bioch 2018) via the AMPK/Nrf2/HO-1 Pathway (Cardiovasc Drugs Ther. 2018). Given that diabetes-induced liver pathological changes and dysfunction in metabolism may have impact on myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, we extended the study to look at Foxo1 inhibition on diabetic induced liver dysfunction and related finding has been published (J Diabetes Res, 2018) which may lead to new directions of research.

17124614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124614.value: Based on the findings from the current study, we are now planning to extend the research to combine cardiac and vascular mechanisms (in relation to Foxo1) in conditioning cardioprotection in collaboration with colleagues from USA and we have jointly published (Cardiovasc Res. 2018 Jun 21. doi: 10.1093/cvr/cvy157).

17124614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124614.value: We have found that excessive Foxo1 activation (especially in diabetic status) plays an important role in exacerbating myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury in animal models of diabetes. The increase in cardiac Foxo1 activation also makes the diabetic heart not responsive to cardioprotective interventions (such as postconditioning cardioprotection) that would otherwise be effective in non-diabetic subjects. Treatment that can enhance adiponectin can attenuate FoxO1-mediated exacerbation of myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury in diabetic hearts and also let the diabetic heart regain responsiveness to conditioning cardioprotection. Current research outcome includes the publication of three original research articles and seven conference abstracts presentation/publications that will eventually lead to full length publication. The above research findings should facilitate the development of new therapeutics in combating diabetic heart ischemic injury.

17124714.label: Realisation of objectives
17124714.value: With the support of this GRF grant, we have comprehensively investigated the physiological roles of adiponectin in cold stress-induced browning and thermogenesis of white adipose tissues and underlying mechanisms involved, as summarized below. In objective-1, We have interrogated the roles of adiponectin in adaptive thermogenesis by comparing energy expenditure, oxygen consumption, rectal temperature between adiponectin knockout (ADNKO) mice and wild-type (WT) littermates under three temperature conditions (thermoneutral (30°C), subthermoneutral (23°C) and cold (4°C)), followed by a series of ex vivo and in vitro studies for tissue morphology and gene expression profiles in adipose tissues. We found that there was no obvious difference in energy expenditure, oxygen consumption and thermogenic gene expressions between WT and ADNKO mice under thermoneutral or subthermoneutral conditions. However, cold-induced adaptive thermogenesis in subcutaneous fat of ADNKO mice was markedly impaired, as demonstrated the loss of multilocular structure and expression of thermogenic gene expression. By contrast, cold-induced activation of classical brown adipose tissues (BAT) was not altered in ADNKO mice, suggesting that adiponectin plays an indispensable role in cold-induced browning of subcutaneous fat. To interrogate the role of the adiponectin in theβ3 agonist CL16243-induced energy expenditure and body weight loss, we treated 12-week-old male ADNKO mice and WT littermates with CL316243 or vehicle control using ALZET mini-osmotic for 2 weeks. Our result showed that adiponectin deficiency has no obvious effect on CL16243-induced browning of subcutaneous white adipose tissues (sWAT) or activation of interscapular brown adipose tissues. We further confirmed the above findings using metabolic cage analysis and measurement of local body temperature with Thermo-camera, showing that cold exposure-induced oxygen consumption and temperature in inguinal regions were reduced by ADNKO mice compared to WT littermates. In objective-2: We comprehensively investigated the molecular events by which adiponectin is selectively recruited to sWAT upon cold challenge, leading to increased accumulation of alternatively-activated M2 macrophages. Using cell fractional analysis and immunocytochemistry, we found that cold-induced adiponectin accumulation mainly colocalized with M2 macrophages, although its mRNA is predominantly expressed in mature adipocytes. Our gene profiling analysis showed that cold exposure specifically increased the expression of T-cadherin (a membrane-anchored adiponectin binding partner) in M2 macrophages, but had no influence on expression of the other two adiponectin receptors (AdipoR1 & AdipoR2). By intravenous injection of red dye-labelled recombinant full-length adiponectin into mice followed by tissue distribution analysis, we found that adiponectin was selectively sequestrated into subcutaneous WAT by binding to T-cadherin in response to cold exposure. Our in vitro studies also found that adiponectin bound to the surface of M2 macrophages, whereas such a binding was weakened by siRNA-mediated downregulation of T-cadherin, but not AdipoR1 and AdipoR2. Furthermore, by infusion of fluorescent dye-labelled monocytes into ADNKO and WT mice, followed by in situ labeling and flow cytometry analysis, we found that adiponectin was obligatory cold-induced proliferation of M2 macrophages (as determined by flow cytometry analysis for BrdU+CD206+ cells or CD206+ and Ki67+ cells). in sWAT via an Akt-dependent mechanism, but had little effect on M1-to-M2 polarization or infiltration of circulating monocytes into sWAT. Furthermore, cold exposure-induced browning and thermogenesis (determined by UCP1 expression, ex vivo measurement of oxygen consumption, and real-time PCR analysis for thermogenic markers), sequestration of adiponectin and proliferation of M2 in scWAT were markedly attenuated in T-cadherin KO mice as compared to WT controls, supporting the key role of T-cadherin in mediating cold-induced browning of scWAT by sequestrating adiponectin into M2 macrophages for stimulating cell proliferation. In objective-3: To determine whether adiponectin-induced browning of sWAT is mediated by M2 macrophages or attributed to the direct effect of adiponectin on differentiation of bipotent adipocyte progenitor cells, we depleted adipose-resident macrophages in mice by treatment with clodronate-containing liposomes (which can selectively deplete tissue macrophages and circulating monocytes) followed by chronic administration of recombinant adiponectin with osmotic pumps to evaluate its effects on browning and thermogenesis in sWAT. Our results showed that adiponectin-induced browning and thermogenesis of sWAT were largely abrogated by depletion of M2 macrophages. Our in vitro studies showed that treatment of adipocytes differentiated from stromal vascular fraction (SVFs) of sWAT with recombinant adiponectin had little effect on induction of UCP1. In contrast, the conditioned medium M2 macrophages can induce the thermogenic programs of adipocytes differentiated from SVFs of sWAT, and such an effect was augmented by pretreatment of adipocytes with recombinant adiponectin. However, our real-time PCR and immunoassays showed that M2 macrophages expressed very low amount of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) with no obvious release of catecholamine in the conditioned medium. Furthermore, treatment of M2 macrophages with the tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor α-methyl-p-tyrosine did not affect the stimulatory effects of the conditioned medium on UCP1 expression and thermogenesis of white adipocytes, suggesting that TH-driven catecholamine production is not a major contributor to cold-induced browning of white adipocytes. By using a series of fractionation analysis, we narrowed down a protein factor released from M2 macrophages is responsible for M2 macrophages-induced browning and thermogenesis. We also conducted a comprehensive flow cytometry analysis for SVFs of sWAT from ADNKO mice and WT mice under thermoneutral and cold conditions for the abundance of different immune cells, type-2 cytokines and adipocyte progenitor cells. Our results showed that adiponectin deficiency had no effects on abundance of ILC2 cells or eosinophils, or their derived type-2 cytokines, whereas cold-induced proliferation of PDGFα+ bipotent progenitor cells and their commitment to beige-lineage cells were compromised in ADNKO mice. Additionally, we discovered that Adipocyte-fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP), another major adipokine secreted from adipocytes, participated in cold-induced activation of classical brown adipose tissues (BAT), but not sWAT. A-FABP KO mice were more susceptible to diet-induced obesity due to impaired thermogenesis of BAT, despite that they are metabolically healthy.

17124714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124714.value: Brown/beige adipocytes have recently attracted great attention due to their anti-obese/anti-diabetic properties. However, little is known about how beige adipocytes, which are scattered in white adipose tissues (WAT) in quiescent states, are activated. This study allowed to uncover adipocyte-secreted adiponectin as a key mediator of cold exposure-induced beiging (browning) and thermogenesis in WAT by facilitating the crosstalk between adipocytes and adipose-resident macrophages, as summarized below: 1. Chronic cold exposure led to a marked induction of adiponectin in mature adipocytes of WAT, which in turn binds to the cell surface of adipose-resident M2 macrophages through T-cadherin, but not AdipoR1 and AdipoR2; 2. Cold exposure-induced beiging and thermogenesis in subcutaneous WAT, as determined by UCP1 expression, formation of multilocular cells and oxygen consumption, were abrogated in adiponectin knockout (ADNKO) mice, accompanied with reduction in cold-induced proliferation and accumulation of M2 macrophages. 3. Replenishment with recombinant full-length adiponectin reversed the defective cold-induced browning and thermogenesis of WAT, whereas such a browning effect of recombinant adiponectin was largely abrogated by pharmacological ablation of adipose-resident macrophages. 4. Mechanistically, adiponectin promotes the proliferation of M2 macrophages by activation of the protein kinase Akt, which in turn sends the signals for browning of white adipocytes. However, an unknown protein factor(s), but not catecholamine, are the major M2 macrophages-released factors for browning of WAT. 5. Adiponectin is not required for activation of classical brown adipocytes in interscapular BAT, which was mainly controlled by sympathetic nerve system. The work was published in Cell Metabolism (See section C-8 item-1). Additionally, this grant also contributed to our discovery of A-FABP, another major adipokine secreted from adipocytes into bloodstream (identified by our group (Xu A, Clinical Chemistry, 2006), as a potent activator of brown adipocytes by inducing the expression of type-II iodothyronine deiodinase in BAT via inhibition of the nuclear receptor liver X receptor-α, thereby leading to the conversion of thyroid hormone from its inactive form T4 to active T3, as well as by facilitating the transport of WAT-released free fatty acids into BAT as an energy substrates for mitochondrial oxidation (published in Nature Communication, section C-8 item-2). Furthermore, we have also uncovered adiponectin as an obligatory downstream target of the anti-diabetic hormone FGF21 in conferring its insulin-sensitizing and anti-atherosclerotic effects in obese mice (See section C-8 item-3). Our animal-based been confirmed in several clinical trials, showing that therapeutic administration of FGF21 leads to a marked elevation of circulating adiponectin in obese patients with type-2 diabetes.

17124714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124714.value: Identification of adiponectin as a novel factor for promoting the browning and thermogenesis of WAT open a new field for further investigation of this major adipocyte-secreted adipokine with multiple protective effects against obesity-induced cardiometabolic disorders. We plan to apply for additional RGC grants or other funding schemes to investigate whether the therapeutic benefits of adiponectin on glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity are dependent on its browning effects by performing adipose transplantation experiments, and will interrogate the clinical relevance of our animal studies in Chinese. Furthermore, we are actively seeking industrial collaborations to use the platforms and animal models established in this study to screen for lead compounds and to develop drugs with anti-obese potentials, using adiponectin as a biomarker and readout. Additionally, we will perform omics-based analysis to identify the nature of M2 macrophages-secreted protein factors which can promote the browning of white adipocytes, which will extend our ongoing study on adipose remodeling.

17124714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124714.value: In mammals, there are three types of fat cells (adipocytes) with different colors: white adipocytes which store extra energy as lipid droplets, brown adipocytes and beige adipocytes, both of which dissipate energy into heat by mitochondrial uncoupling process. A large body of evidence suggests that conversion of white into brown/beige adipocytes not only helps our body to defend cold environment by generating heat, but also has additional benefits for alleviation of obesity and diabetes. However, it remains unclear about how cold exposure induces the conversion of white adipocytes into beige/brown adipocytes in the body. Here, we identified fat cells-secreted adiponectin, an adipokine with anti-diabetic and anti-inflammatory properties, as an important player in “browning” of white adipocytes in response to cold environment. Furthermore, we have uncovered proliferation of anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages as a novel mechanism by which adiponectin induces browning and adaptive thermogenesis in white adipose tissues. The findings not only deepen our understanding of how human bodies adapt to cold environment by generating heat, but also provide knowledge base for development of adiponectin analogs for treatment of obesity and diabetes.

17124814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124814.value: 肝細胞性肝癌（HCC）多見於東南亞地區，更是香港的第二大致死性疾病。由於HCC具有高復發，高轉移特性，其預後較差。因此找到確實有效的靶基因對抗這類高侵襲性的疾病非常必要。 肝癌缺失基因1（DLC1）是一種首先在HCC中分離的抑癌基因，但一系列新的研究發現DLC1的抑癌作用並不侷限於肝臟，在多個癌症模型中DLC1均起到有效抑癌細胞生長及轉移。動物實驗已證實DLC1在抑制腫瘤生長，轉移及血管新生中發揮作用。DLC1是一種Rho GTP酶激活蛋白，它具有的Rho GTP酶活性是其抑制腫瘤發生和轉移的關鍵。因此厘清DLC1的Rho GTP酶活性和其在癌細胞中的表現之間的關係十分重要。我們已經報道了protein kinase A（PKA）通過上調DLC1絲氨酸－549磷酸化水平促進其二聚體化進而加強其RhoGAP酶及抑制肝細胞生長和轉移(Ko et al., Nature Commun 2013)。 DLC1絲氨酸－549缺失體（S549D）具有更強的抑癌作用。我們近來運用比較蛋白質組學技術發現在S549D穩定表達的細胞株中半乳糖凝集素1（galectin-1）表達被抑制。這提示galectin-1在肝癌的發生發展中起關鍵作用。而在S549D中引入galectin-1又增強了細胞的生長和侵襲性。我們推測DLC1絲氨酸－549的磷酸化可能通過抑制galectin-1的表達而達到其抑制腫瘤生長和轉移的作用。因此我們將選用在體和離體功能實驗研究galectin-1的表達而達到其抑制腫瘤生長和轉移的作用，從分子水平分析其機制，並評價其臨床意義。據我們所知，這是首個在HCC研究活化的DLC1對galectin-1表現影響的課題，這將幫助我們重新認識肝癌及為治療提供新的靶點。

17124814.label: Realisation of objectives
17124814.value: 1. To characterize the functional effect of galectin-1 in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis using both in vitro and in vivo functional assays The functions of Gal-1 was investigated by transient/stable overexpression and knockdown approach in different cell lines, namely, non-metastatic and metastatic HCC cell lines as well as immortalized normal liver cell line. Some of these parental cell lines were stably labeled with luciferase which enables in vivo bioluminescence imaging when injected into animal. The stable clones of Gal-1 were subjected to different in vitro functional assays and animal models. Apart from cellular functions, secretory Gal-1 was studied. The levels of secretory Gal-1 in the conditioned medium of stable clones were analyzed by ELISA. The expression level agreed with the cellular expression of Gal-1 in these stable clones. Functionally, the activity of Gal-1 in the conditioned medium was neutralized by anti-Gal-1 antibody. In addition, recombinant Gal-1 was applied to cells and the properties of cells were examined. The results obtained were in line with our hypothesis that Gal-1 exerts oncogenic effect in driving HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasiveness, tumorigenesis and metastasis. The study on this objective was successfully accomplished. 2. To delineate the molecular mechanism underlying the functional roles of galectin-1 in HCC Based on our background study, Gal-1 was identified as a downstream effect of DLC1 tumor suppressor. We originally proposed to study how DLC1 regulates Gal-1. The inconsistent causal effect between DLC1 and Gal-1 detected in various HCC cell line model prompted us to investigate other potential upstream regulator of Gal-1. Using in silico analysis, miR-22 was found to be potential candidate as regulator of Gal-1. The casual association between miR-22 and Gal-1 was detected in various HCC cell lines using transient and stable expression approach. Expression of miR-22 was found to downregulate Gal-1 not only its level but the promoting activity in HCC cells. Conversely, knockdown of miR-22 upregulated Gal-1 expression and potentiates the aggressive properties of cells. In HCC clinical tissues, a significant negative association between miR-22 and Gal-1 was found. Analysis of miR-22 in a cohort of HCC tissues revealed downregulation of miR-22 in HCC. Apart from miR-22, we also found that hypoxic conditions could elevate expression of Gal-1 in HCC cells and tumors formed in mice. Functions of miR-22 were also investigated using mimic and inhibitor of miR-22 as treatment for HCC cells. Functional characterization well demonstrated the inhibitory activity of miR-22 in HCC cells. At the end, the study on this objective was successfully completed 3. To evaluate the clinical relevance and prognostic significance of galectin-1 in clinical HCC samples The expression of Gal-1 in a cohort of HCC clinical samples was analyzed by quantitative PCR and immunohistochemistry. RNA samples and tissue microarray of HCC tissues were provided by our collaborator. Serum of HCC patients and control subjects were provided by the Department of Medicine and Department of Surgery, The University of Hong Kong. Gal-1 level in serum of individuals was analyzed by ELISA. These analyses consistently showed upregulation of Gal-1 in tumorours samples when compared to non-tumorous counterparts. Statistical analysis was performed to evaluate the potential correlation between Gal-1 expression and clinicopathological features and survival rates of patients. These analyses showed that Gal-1 mRNA, protein and serum level was upregulated. Overexpression of Gal-1 was significantly correlated with tumor aggressive features and poorer survival rate. The study on this objective was successfully completed.

17124814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124814.value: Gal-1 promotes oncogenic properties of HCC cells Gal-1 knockdown cells were shown to display reduced ability to grow on soft agar, migrate and invade. Subcutaneous injection mouse model showed reduced tumorigenicity when Gal-1 was reduced in these cells, with tumor weight and length also significantly reduced when excised. In an orthotopic liver implantation experiment, delayed liver tumor formation and distant metastasis to lungs were observed in Gal-1 knockdown group when compared to non-target control group. Conversely, overexpression of Gal-1 enhanced HCC cell aggressiveness. miR-22 suppresses Gal-1 expression and its effect in HCC In silico analysis identified miR-22 as a potential regulator of Gal-1. Transient introduction or inhibition of miR-22 resulted in the decrease or enhanced expression of Gal-1 in cells. The activity of luciferase reporter carrying Gal-1 3’UTR/miR-22 seed sequence was reduced when coexpressed with miR-22 mimic. A significant negative correlation between Gal-1 and miR-22 expression was observed in HCC clinical tissues. miR-22 was evidently underexpressed in 49.4% of the HCC cases examined. Functionally, when miR-22 was stably expressed in cells, Gal-1 expression was reduced and the ability of cells to form colonies, migrate and invade was also diminished. By contrast, reduction of miR-22 increased Gal-1 expression and resulted in an increase in the aggressiveness of cells. However, such increase was abolished when cells were treated with Gal-1 inhibitor, OTX008. Clinical significance of overexpression of Gal-1 In 45% (36/97) of HCC clinical samples, qPCR analysis revealed Gal-1 overexpression in tumorous tissues. Consistently, immunohistochemical staining revealed 64.9% of the samples expressed Gal-1 at higher levels compared to the non-tumorous counterparts. Furthermore, Gal-1 overexpression was significantly correlated with the absence of tumor encapsulation, the presence of microsatellites and poorer disease free survival. Level of Gal-1 in serum of 177 HCC patients was analyzed. A significant increase in Gal-1 level in patents with HBV when compared to control subjects was detected. Hypoxia upregulates Gal-1 expression and potentiates its oncogenic effect When HCC cells were treated with cobalt II chloride or placed in hypoxic chamber, upregulation of cellular and secretory Gal-1 when compared to control cells was detected. IHC staining of Gal-1 in HCC cell derived tumor revealed that in the areas of hypoxia, as indicated by the positive staining of Pimonidazole, Gal-1 was also clearly more highly expressed. The effect of hypoxia inducible Gal-1 expression further enhanced the oncogenic effect of Gal-1 in the migration and invasiveness of HCC cells.

17124814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124814.value: HCC is a typical hypervascular tumor. However, abnormal architecture of newly developed blood vessels and inefficient oxygen delivery has made tumors associated with regions subjected to hypoxia. In fact, intratumoral hypoxia is associated with promoted angiogenesis, metastasis and enhanced resistance to radiotherapy and chemotherapy of tumor cells. Hypoxia induced elevation of Gal-1 and the upregulation of Gal-1 in a broad spectrum of human cancers prompt us to explore the therapeutic effect in targeting Gal-1. Treatment with HCC cells with inhibitor of Gal-1, OTX008 suppressed HCC cell growth and motility. In mice subcutaneously injected with metastatic HCC cells, intraperitoneal of OTX008 was shown to effectively delay tumor formation. We also found OTX008 significantly sensitized tumor cells to sorafenib in animal model. The resulting tumors formed in mice administered with OTX008 and sorafenib were significantly smaller than those formed in mice received with sorafenib alone. For further development of this study, the proof of concept about targeting Gal-1 expression with or without sorafenib or other inhibitors for liver cancer treatment under hypoxia will be performed in animal model subjected to hepatic artery ligation, a technique to obstruct the blood flow into the liver and hence mimicking hypoxic condition.

17124814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124814.value: Liver cancer is a prevalent malignancy in Hong Kong. High incidence and death rate have led to the attention of major public health problem. Understanding the way how liver cancer is developed deserves careful investigation. In this study, we have provided the evidence that galectin-1 (Gal-1) is highly expressed in liver cancer tissues when compared to non-tumorous liver tissues. Overexpression of Gal-1 is significantly correlated with aggressive tumor behavior and poorer survival rate. Besides, we have provided a vigorous demonstration of the functional activities of Gal-1 in liver cancer and delineated the molecular pathway leading to the elevated level of Gal-1 in cancerous tissues. Based on expression and functional role of Gal-1, we attempted to reveal the therapeutic efficacy of inhibiting Gal-1 using pre-clinical model. Our findings have provided profound implications in the therapeutics for liver cancer and suggested the potential of Gal-1 as a potential therapeutic and diagnostic marker for liver cancer.

17125114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125114.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by production of autoantibodies and multiple organ damages, which mainly affects women of child-bearing age. Genetic factors play important roles in the disease. Identifying the genetic factors predisposing people to SLE holds much promise for a better understanding of the disease, identification of new drug targets, and personalized treatment. Genome–wide association study (GWAS) conducted by us on Hong Kong cases and controls has identified ETS1, WDFY4, and ELF1 as associated with the disease. Subsequently, meta-analysis of the two GWAS on Chinese populations from Hong Kong and Anhui led to the identification of CDKN1B, TET3, CD80, DRAM1, ARID5B and 11q23.3 as associated with the disease in Asians. Despite all these advances, many questions remain about the genetic factors for this disease. An important issue is to further increase power of the discovery stage as the two GWAS on Chinese populations were based on relatively small samples. Not having data from European populations also prevented us from comparing the genetic factors involved in the two major ethnicities using first-hand data. In this study, a meta-analysis will be conducted on the three existing GWAS datasets from Hong Kong, Anhui and UK, with the latter a novel cohort provided by Tim Vyse from King’s College, London (KCL). With the newly added large dataset from KCL, this study promises to identify novel susceptibility genes and loci for SLE by meta-analysis and replication using additional independent cohorts. This is the very first meta-analysis on lupus genetics involving two major ethnicities. The findings will allow us to have a better understanding of the disease and the common and different genetic factors involved in the two major populations. Subphenotype stratification and functional studies will help us better predict clinical manifestations using genetic information and understand the biological pathways involved in the disease processes. 系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）是一種自身免疫性疾病，患者會產生自身抗體，對自身各個器官造成損害，多發于女性，特別是育齡婦女。目前研究認為，遺傳因素起著重要的作用，因此，識別新的系統性紅斑狼瘡易感基因能幫助我們更好地認識疾病的發病機制，確定新的藥物靶標，實現個性化的治療。之前，我們運用全基因組關聯研究（GWAS），發現基因ETS1，WDFY4和ELF1在香港人群中顯著地和系統性紅斑狼瘡相關。隨後，通過META分析，我們進一步發現新的基因CDKN1B，TET3，CD80，DRAM1，ARID5B和11q23.3在亞洲人群中與該疾病具有相關性。 儘管近幾年來，在識別該病的易感基因方面取得了很大的進展，但是目前的發現仍不足以完全解釋所有遺傳因素的作用，還有許多的易感基因沒有被挖掘，而這在很大程度上受限於研究樣本的規模。之前基於中國人群的樣本量相對較小，且只能代表亞洲人群的病例。而缺乏來自歐洲的相關研究數據，使得我們無法比較該病在兩個主要人種中的差異。 在這項新的研究中，我們獲得了來自英國Tim Vyse （King’s College）的相關研究數據，使得我們能夠運用薈萃分析的方法和獨立樣本的驗證（Replication），在香港，安徽和歐洲人群中，發現新的紅斑狼瘡易感基因。本次研究首次結合亞洲和歐洲的相關研究數據進行分析，不僅能讓我們更好地了解這種疾病普遍存在的發病機制，而且能發現該病在兩大群體间的不同遺傳因素。而隨後的亞表型分析和相關基因功能的研究，不僅有助于我們更好地運用遺傳信息診斷疾病發生，并且能让我们更好地了解疾病發生的病理途徑。

17125114.label: Realisation of objectives
17125114.value: First, I would thank the panel for awarding the grant to us, to allow us to carry out the good work we are doing. The first objective of the project is "To identify novel susceptibility genes for SLE through meta-analysis of three GWAS datasets from Hong Kong, mainland China and UK and replication in additional independent cohorts". This was exactly what we did, which was clearly documented in our publication in Nature Genetics in 2016 (48(8):940-946) titled: Genome-wide association meta-analysis in Chinese and European individuals identifies ten new loci associated with systemic lupus erythematosus." In this study we identified 10 novel loci associated with SLE in both East Asians and European populations. Following up this study, and making use of the data from different cohorts and independent replications, we have identified additional new loci for this prototype autoimmune disease. These pieces of work were published in Ann Rheum Dis. 2018 Jul;77(7):1078-1084, Ann Rheum Dis. 2016 May;75(5):891-8, Arthritis Res Ther. 2018 May 3;20(1):92. and Arthritis Res Ther. 2015 Mar 20;17:67. The second objective for this project is "To evaluate the similarities and differences between the genetic factors involved in Europeans and Asians". In our publication of Morris et al, we systematically compared the signals in genetic loci associated with SLE in the two major ethnicity. While most of the loci are shared between East Asians and Europeans, we did report a number of loci with clear differences in susceptibility, which is not explained by allele frequencies and study power. More importantly, we have shown that East Asians have higher genetic risk scores overall, even among the healthy individuals, partially explains the higher disease prevalence of SLE in Asians and more severe clinical manifestations than in Europeans. The third objective of the project is "To explore the biological functions of the identified genetic variants through both bioinformatics analysis and functional characterizations". In our recent work published in Ann Rheum Dis. 2018 Jul;77(7):1078-1084， we analyzed correlations between histone markers and susceptibility loci. For example, we clearly shows one of the susceptibility locus we identified is correlated with enhancer and promoter markers in B cells, but not in T cells and monocytes. We also showed that highly significant enrichment of protein interaction between SLE susceptibility genes and known targets for widely used SLE drugs. We systematically analyzed the correlations between susceptibility genes and gene expression profile and methylation profiles in T cells, B cells and PBMC. These two studies are summarized in two manuscripts under review. It can be seen that we have successfully completed this project, fulfilling our promises in the three objectives. More importantly, the data we have generated will be further explored, analyzed and interpreted in the future in the context of new knowledge, new databases, and to help us further understand the mechanisms of the disease. Thus, in a way, they are small steps in our effort to better understand the disease from the genetic perspective and under the context of other data.

17125114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125114.value: In genetic research, each project is a stepping stone for the next step of the research effort. The data we keep collecting will be analyzed together with the data we collected before to build up the power for novel discoveries. In addition, there is also a rapid development in genomic biology and accumulation of knowledge of genomic elements and activities. Thus, the interpretation and understanding of the data generated in this project will continue to evolve with our knowledge in genome biology. We will continue to revisit and reanalyze the data we have collected to have better understanding of the mechanisms of associations and to identify biomarkers and novel drug targets for this prototype autoimmune diseases.

17125114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125114.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a disease for which the immune system fails to distinguish self and non-self tissues and produces autoantibodies that attack self-tissues. It is a disease mainly affects women of child-bearing age, and Asians have more SLE than Europeans. SLE is a disease that affects 1 in a thousand people and genetics play very important role in the disease. The purpose of this study is to look for the genetic variants in human genome that predispose people to this disease. Making use of DNA samples collected locally both from SLE patients and healthy controls, and collaborating with research scientists from the mainland and abroad, we have examined the genetic variants genome-wide and identified a number of genetic variants that have much higher frequency in cases than in controls. We also revealed that Asians have higher genetic risk scores than European individuals, which partially explains why Asians have more SLE. Elucidating the genetic variants predispose people to SLE will help us better understand the mechanisms of the disease and to find biomarkers for the diagnosis, treatment of the disease and to identify novel drug targets for SLE.

17125214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125214.value: The Forkhead box transcription factor FOXM1 is ubiquitously expressed in proliferating cells and its levels up-regulated in various cancers. Depletion of FOXM1 in normal and cancer cells suppresses cell proliferation. Moreover, FOXM1 has been shown to play important roles in cancer cell migration/invasion and “epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)”, a regulatory event tightly related to the invasiveness of cancer cells. The critical requirement of FOXM1 in maintaining cancer cell proliferation and migration/invasion has led to its increasing recognition as diagnostic marker and target for developing anti-cancer drugs. To further understand how FOXM1 exerts its multiple roles in cancer cells, we designed a screen for FOXM1-interacting proteins to identify partnering factors that function with FOXM1. Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) Pathway Substrate 8 (EPS8), also ubiquitously expressed in proliferating cells, emerged as a specific interactor of FOXM1. Levels of EPS8 are up-regulated in various cancers and EPS8 is known to regulate Rac-mediated actin remodeling at the cell cortex. Our recent demonstration that EPS8 became nuclear localized when CRM1/exportin 1-dependent nuclear export was inhibited by Leptomycin B, and the identification of a functional nuclear export sequence (NES) in EPS8, strongly support a novel nuclear function of EPS8. Indeed, suppression of EPS8 expression by RNA interference led to decreased expression of FOXM1 and its downstream target Cyclin B1, supporting functional cooperativity between EPS8 and FOXM1. We hypothesize that EPS8 is a critical partnering factor required for FOXM1 to promote cancer cell proliferation and migration/invasion. In this proposal, we will investigate how EPS8 depletion would affect cancer cell proliferation, migration/invasion and EMT, and whether the effects are FOXM1-dependent. Constitutively nuclear EPS8 (gain-of-function or dominant negative) mutants will be designed to test for perturbations of cell proliferation and migration/invasion, and the expression of FOXM1 and FOXM1 target genes. A structure-function analysis will also be performed to define the critical domain(s)/amino acid(s) required for mediating interaction between EPS8 and FOXM1, and the functional effects of EPS8. EPS8L2 (for EPS8-Like2) has been recently shown to display overlapping expression pattern and functional properties as EPS8. We will test for interaction of EPS8L2 with FOXM1 and similarly analyze its nuclear function. Together, the proposed analyses will provide novel insight into the nuclear role of EPS8/EPS8L2 and its crosstalk with FOXM1 in the regulation of cancer cell proliferation, migration/invasion and EMT, which is of major biological interest and a prerequisite for devising future strategies for suppressing cancer cell proliferation and migration/invasion.

17125214.label: Realisation of objectives
17125214.value: Objective 1 (Achieved) Using both cervical and ovarian cancer cell lines as model, we demonstrated functional involvement of EPS8 in the regulation of cell proliferation and chemoresistance by FOXM1. For regulation of cell proliferation, we successfully showed that EPS8 depletion using shRNAs in cervical cancer cells suppressed FOXM1 and FOXM1-target gene expression, leading to a concomitant slowdown in cell proliferation through the G2/M phase of the cell cycle. In particular, we selected HeLa cells overexpressing EPS8-targeting shRNA (with GFP coexpression) and synchronized them at the G1/S boundary by double thymidine block, followed by drug release and monitoring of cell cycle progression using PI/DNA analysis (of gated GFP-expressing cells). Interestingly, EPS8-deficient cells showed a delay in re-entering G1 phase while their rate of transition into G2 phase did not show discernible difference. Importantly, ChIP analysis revealed direct recruitment of both EPS8 and FOXM1 to the promoter of known FOXM1 target genes CCNB1 and CDC25B, supporting a partnering role of EPS8 with FOXM1 in the regulation of mitotic genes. Since studies reported in 2015 (Nature 527: 472-476; 525-530) have convincingly shown that EMT contributes to chemoresistance but not metastasis in vivo, we shifted our attention to study the involvement of EPS8 in chemoresistance instead of migration/invasion in cancer cells. To this end, we employed human ovarian cancer cells (mainly ES2) as model for studying the role of EPS8 in cisplatin resistance. We used EPS8-targeting shRNAs and the specific small molecular inhibitor (against DNA binding) of FOXM1 FDI-6 for suppressing EPS8 and FOXM1 activity, respectively. Suppressing EPS8 or FOXM1 individually was enough to decrease cisplatin chemoresistance (based on IC50 analysis), whereas co-suppression of both led to further suppression of chemoresistance with XTT-based cell viability assay and cell death monitored by caspase 3 and PARP-1 cleavage as readout. Importantly, EPS8 and FOXM1 were shown to stimulate the expression of one another at both transcript (based on qPCR analysis) and protein level (analyzed by immunoblotting). Depletion of EPS8 led to suppression of expression of the known FOXM1 target EXO1, which plays a role in homologous recombination-based DNA repair. Co-depletion of both EPS8 and FOXM1 further suppressed EXO1 expression. Objective 2 (Achieved) We used both yeast two-hybrid and immunoprecipitation analyses to study the interaction between EPS8 and FOXM1. Deletion analysis led us to define the domains with EPS8 necessary for interaction with FOXM1. Interestingly, the SH3 domain believed to serve a role in EPS8 dimerization was not required for interaction with FOXM1. EGFP-EPS8 fusion constructs coupled with site-directed mutagenesis defined a functional nuclear export sequence (NES) at amino acids 265 to 288. Subcellular localization of the fusion proteins was assayed by fluorescence microscopy after transient transfection into HEK293T cells. In 2013, Cunningham et al. reported in a quantitative proteomic study of EPS8 phosphorylation and phosphorylation-dependent protein binding that multiple tyrosine residues within EPS8 are differentially phosphorylated upon stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinases. Many of the tyrosine residues were found to bind proteins involved in nucleocytoplasmic shuttling. Therefore, we individually mutated these tyrosines (in particular Y485 and Y525) into phosphomimetic (Y to E) and non-phosphorylatable (Y to F) mutants in the EGFP-EPS8 backbone and assayed for any effect on nuclear translocation. No significant effect was observed but it remains to be tested whether mutation of multiple sites would lead to enhanced nuclear entry. On the other hand, Logue et al (2015) recently reported multiple MAPK phosphorylation sites (S624 and T628) within EPS8 that appeared to be required for regulation of subcellular localization of the protein. It would be worth testing whether these sites are critical for regulation of EPS8 nuclear translocation. In summary, we have shown that EPS8 is regulated by nuclear export as inhibition of exportin-mediated nuclear export by LMB treatment led to dramatic nuclear accumulation of EPS8. A functional NES was found by EGFP-tagging and site-directed mutagenesis. Although the mechanism underlying the regulated nuclear import of EPS8 remains to be clarified, our findings that EPS8 could enter the nucleus at G2/M phase and interacted with FOXM1 in vitro are supportive of EPS8 playing a critical partnering with FOXM1 in gene regulation (see also Objective 1 for evidence that they played cooperative role in the regulation of mitotic targets). Objective 3 (Achieved) We studied the expression of all three EPS8-related family members (EPS8L1, EPS8L2 and EPS8L3) in both cervical and ovarian cancer cells by both qPCR and bioinformatic analyses. Only EPS8L2 was expressed in high levels, suggestive of its involvement in the regulation of cell proliferation and chemoresistance, similar to EPS8. We also demonstrated that EPS8L2 was regulated by nuclear export as LMB treatment enhanced nuclear entry of EPS8L2 and sequence analysis revealed a leucine-rich NES-like sequence within EPS8L2. Unfortunately, repeated attempts failed to detect interaction of EPS8L2 with FOXM1 in yeast two-hybrid and immunoprecipitation assays, arguing against a partnering role of EPS8L2 with FOXM1, similar to EPS8. With limited resource and manpower (MPhil student recruited could only finish the chemoresistance study of EPS8 in ovarian cancer cells), we could not further study the effect of EPS8L2 depletion in cancer cell proliferation and chemoresistance.

17125214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125214.value: FOXM1, named Molecule of the Year in 2010, is a well-known cancer target of diagnostic and therapeutic importance. Its levels were upregulated in cancer cells and previously FOXM1 promoter activity was shown to be stimulated by EPS8, which was also upregulated in multiple cancers. However, interplay of FOXM1 and EPS8 in the regulation cancer cell proliferation and chemoresistance remains unclear. This grant provides the resource to characterize the interaction of EPS8 with FOXM1 and to study how EPS8 as partnering factor with FOXM1 mediates the regulation of cancer cell proliferation and chemoresistance. We made the novel findings that FOXM1 and EPS8 interacted in vitro and they showed colocalization in the nucleus at the G2/M phase of the cell cycle. Interestingly, we showed that EPS8, known to interact with the EGF receptor, could be translocated into the nucleus when exportin-mediated nuclear export was inhibited by LMB treatment. We further defined a functional NES within EPS8 by EGFP-tagging and site-directed mutagenesis. Both EPS8 and FOXM1 were shown to associate with the promoter of known FOXM1 targets CCNB1 and CDC25B by chromatin immunoprecipitation assay and depletion of EPS8 led to delay of transition through the G2/M phase of the cell cycle, consistent with EPS8 playing a partnering role with FOXM1 in the regulation of cell proliferation. These findings were reported in an international conference (see Part C for poster) and recently documented in an article that is under peer review at Frontiers in Oncology (see Part C). We also provided evidence to show that EPS8 was required for cancer cells to confer chemoresistance to cisplatin. Interstingly, FOXM1 and EPS8 cross-regulated one another transcriptionally and they could both stimulate expression of EXO1, previously known to be a important component in the homologous recombination-mediated repair pathway. These findings were generated by a MPhil student who graduated in early 2018 (see Part C). This project provides an invaluable training experience for the MPhil candidate, who was hired as Research Scientist R&D at DiagCor Bioscience Inc Ltd.

17125214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125214.value: We made the novel finding that EPS8 partners with FOXM1 to regulate mitotic genes. To have a better understanding of the genome-wide co-regulation of target genes by the two proteins, ChIP-seq analysis would need to be conducted using specific EPS8 antibody and bioinformatic analysis performed to identify EPS8 targets followed by the comparison of this dataset against that of FOXM1. This proposed analysis will reveal putative targets for future cancer diagnosis and development of cancer therapeutics. How the nuclear localization of EPS8 is regulated remains unclear. It would be worthwhile to conduct further site-directed mutagenesis of the various tyrosine and serine/threonine residues believed to play regulatory role to study their relevance in the regulation of EPS8 nuclear entry. Although EPS8L2 was not shown to interact with FOXM1 in our study as predicted, it would still be worthwhile to study the effect of depletion of EPS8L2 in the regulation of cancer cell properties. In summary, our findings lay the foundation for further study of the interplay of FOXM1 and EPS8 and or EPS8L2 in the regulation of cancer cell proliferation and chemoresistance. These novel findings will provide the groundwork for future application of research funds to continue the worthwhile research.

17125214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125214.value: Sustaining proliferative signaling is an notable hallmark of cancer cells that proliferate uncontrollably. Both FOXM1 and EPS8 are known to be activated by mitogenic signaling and their levels upregulated in cancer. Here, we provided the first evidence to support protein-protein interaction between FOXM1 and EPS8. FOXM1 and EPS8 were shown to interact in vitro and to colocalize in the nucleus at the G2/M phase of the cell cycle. Indeed, inhibition of exportin-mediated nuclear export using LMB induced dramatic nuclear entry of EPS8 and a functional nuclear export sequence was defined by EGFP-tagging and site-directed mutagenesis. Importantly, downregulation of EPS8 by RNA interference led to downregulation of expression of FOXM1 and the FOXM1-target CCNB1, and slowed down G2/M transition. Chromatin immunoprecipitation analysis indicated recruitment of EPS8 to the promoters of CCNB1and CDC25B, supporting a novel partnering role of EPS8 with FOXM1 in the regulation of cancer cell proliferation. Moreover, EPS8 was shown to play a critical role together with FOXM1 in the regulation of chemoresistance in ovarian cancer cells. In summary, our findings provide novel insight into the crosstalk between FOXM1 and EPS8. Perturbation of this novel interaction should shed new light into the future development of cancer therapeutics.

17125414.label: Realisation of objectives
17125414.value: The trial was completed but was terminated for futility in the planned interim analysis according to the recommendation from Independent Data Monitoring Committee. Overall, the trial result fails to meet the primary endpoint.--the addition of capecitabine and oxaliplatin to sorafenib did not result in significant improvement in time-to-progression (TTP) and overall survival (OS). The trial was conducted at three participating hospitals—Queen Mary Hospital, Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital and Tuen Mun Hospital in Hong Kong between 1 Apr 2015 and 30 Apr 2017. At the time of interim analysis, 66 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were recruited in which 50 were randomized to receive treatment. Twenty five and 25 patients were randomized to receive SECOX and sorafenib respectively. Four patients withdrew from the study after randomization, three of whom were randomized to receive SECOX. The median duration of follow-up was 7.8 months. Median TTP was 3.2 months for SECOX compared to 2.8 months for single agent sorafenib. The hazard ratio for TTP was 0.91 (95% CI 0.49-1.70; two-sided p=0.77; predetermined futility boundary HR ≥ 0.86). Median OS was 7.1 months for SECOX compared to 12.5 months (95% CI 7.2-15.4 months) for sorafenib (p=0.29). Regarding the best tumour response rate, two patients (9.1%) vs zero patients(0%) achieved partial response in SECOX arm and single agent sorafenib arm, respectively. Concerning the safety of the treatment regimens in both arms, incidence of treatment-related adverse events (AEs) was common in both SECOX and sorafenib arms (63.6% and 70.8% respectively, p=0.75. There was no statistically significant difference between these two arms. The most common Grade 3-4 AE was ALP increase (13.6%) for SECOX arm and hand-foot skin reaction for single agent sorafenib arm (25.0%). In the exploratory biomarker analysis, both serial alpha-fetal protein changes and the intensity of β-catenin expression in the biopsied liver samples at the baseline did not predict response nor survival benefits for the enrolled patients in both arms Last but not least, the Quality of Life(QOL) assessment by serial QOL questionnaire measurements between patients on SECOX regimen and patients on single agent sorafenib did not demonstrate any significant differences between these two arms.

17125414.value: Between 1 Apr 2015 and 30 Apr 2017, 66 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were recruited in which 50 were randomized to receive treatment. Twenty five and 25 patients were randomized to receive SECOX and sorafenib, respectively. Four patients withdrew from the study after randomization, three of whom were randomized to receive SECOX. The median age was 64 years and majority of the patients were male (n=33; 71.7%). Forty patients (87.0%) were hepatitis B carrier, and 42 patients (91.3%) had Child-Pugh A liver function. Thirty patients (65.2%) had received prior treatment for HCC. The median duration of follow-up was 7.8 months (range 0.3-25.8 months). As at the time of analysis, one patient in the SECOX arm is still receiving treatment. Median time-to-progression (TTP) was 3.2 months (95% CI 1.7-5.8 months) for SECOX compared to 2.8 months for sorafenib (95% CI 1.8-4.0 months). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 3.1 months (95% CI 1.6-5.8 months) for SECOX compared to 2.7 months for sorafenib (95% CI 1.8-4.0 months). The hazard ratio (HR) for TTP was 0.91 (95% CI 0.49-1.70; two-sided p=0.77; predetermined futility boundary HR ≥ 0.86). Median OS was 7.1 months (95% CI 3.0-15.3 months) for SECOX compared to 12.5 months (95% CI 7.2-15.4 months) for sorafenib (p=0.29). Regarding the best tumour response rate, two patients (9.1%) vs zero patients (0%) achieved partial response in SECOX arm and single agent sorafenib arm, respectively. The clinical benefit rate (defined as the proportion of patients achieving a response or stable disease) was 36.4% for the SECOX arm and 20.8% for the sorafenib arm (p=0.50). Incidence of treatment-related adverse events (AEs) was common in both SECOX and sorafenib arms (63.6% and 70.8% respectively, p=0.75). The most common AEs of the SECOX arm were hypertension (22.7%), thrombocytopenia (22.7%), rash (22.7%), ALP increase (18.2%) and hand-foot skin reaction (18.2%). The most common AEs of the sorafenib arm were hand-foot skin reaction (37.5%), thrombocytopenia (20.8%) and rash (20.8%). The most common grade 3-4 trAE was ALP increase (13.6%) for SECOX arm and hand-foot skin reaction for sorafenib arm (25.0%). In the exploratory biomarker analysis, both serial alpha-fetal protein changes and the intensity of β-catenin expression in the biopsied liver samples at the baseline did not predict response nor survival benefits for the enrolled patients in both arms The addition of capecitabine and oxaliplatin to sorafenib did not result in significant improvement in time-to-progression and overall survival.

17125414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125414.value: Overall, this randomized phase II trial result failed to meet the primary endpoint and was terminated for futility in the interim analysis. Although the addition of capecitabine and oxaliplatin to sorafenib (SECOX) resulted in higher tumour response rate and disease stabilisation, it unfortunately did not translate into any significant improvement in time-to-progression and overall survival. Moreover, the SECOX treatment resulted in treatment related adverse events in over half of the enrolled patients. Therefore, the SECOX treatment should not be recommended for further development in future clinical trials in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma patients. This is in fact a second failed clinical trial in the literature in adding chemotherapy to sorafenib to improve the outcomes of the advanced hepatocellular cancer patients. Our findings serve to imply that the combination of chemotherapy and sorafenib may not be a promising systemic therapy option for future treatment of advanced HCC patients.

17125414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125414.value: Liver cancer is the second most common cause of cancer-related death in Asia-Pacific region. Sorafenib is the standard of treatment in advanced liver cancer patients but with poor survival outcome. Our previous phase II trial had shown that the combination of sorafenib together with oxaliplatin and capecitabine (SECOX) had promising activity and safety in Asian advanced liver cancer patients. Recently, we had completed a randomized phase II trial to compare the efficacy and tolerability of SECOX regimen with sorafenib alone as the first-line treatment of advanced liver cancer patients. The trial was unfortunately terminated for futility in the planned interim analysis according to the recommendation from Independent Data Monitoring Committee. Overall, the trial result failed to meet the primary endpoint.--the addition of capecitabine and oxaliplatin to sorafenib did not result in significant improvement in patient’s survival. Moreover, the SECOX treatment resulted in treatment related side effects in the majority of the enrolled patients. Therefore, SECOX treatment should not be recommended for further development in future clinical trials in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma population. Our current findings imply the notion that the combination of chemotherapy and sorafenib is not a promising systemic therapy approach for treatment of advanced HCC patients.

17125814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125814.value: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the most prevalent neurological disorders, affecting the daily living conditions and functions of significant numbers of the elderly worldwide. In general, AD clinical trials are expensive and difficult, as they typically collect longitudinal measurements to identify treatment effects and thus often require larger sample size, longer follow-up, and more examinations than other trials. In the era of personalized medicine, subgroup analysis becomes increasingly important. Patients with similar disease diagnosis and histology may respond differently to the same treatment. Hence, it is critical to identify the right treatment for the right patient subpopulation. To improve efficiency and flexibility in the conduct and analysis of clinical trials, we propose two new statistical methods. First, we will develop a Bayesian hierarchical modeling and dose-finding method for AD treatment, which will be generally suitable for other therapeutic areas as long as the disease is chronic and the outcome is measured repeatedly over time. Second, we will propose a Bayesian subgroup analysis approach with shrinkage estimation. In the Bayesian framework, the prior information and the strength of the observed data are naturally integrated for better decision making. To facilitate the routine use and broad application of our proposed methods, we will develop user-friendly software for free downloading. 阿茲海默症(老年癡呆症)是最常見的神經系統疾病之一。全球有 相当數量的老人都遭受此病的困擾，主要體現在他們的日常生 活能力受到了严重的影響。總體來說，針對阿茲海默症的臨床 試驗需要較高的成本並具有顯著的困難性。這是因為其往往需 要通過收集縱向測量數據來鑒別治療的效果，從而導致該試驗 比其他病症的試驗通常需要更大的試驗人群、更長的後續跟進 时间以及更多的測驗次數。在個體化醫學的時代，亞組或子群 分析逐漸展現出其前所未有的重要性。具有類似疾病診斷和組 織學的病人可能對相同的治療有不同的反應。因此，如何正確 地鑒別出相應患者子群的正確治療方案是至關重要的。為了提 高臨床試驗操作及分析的效率和靈活性，我們提出兩個新的統 計模型。首先，我們針對阿茲海默症的臨床試驗構造一個貝葉 斯分層模型和劑量探索方法。該模型和方法同樣也適用於其他 治療領域，只要其對應的是慢性疾病且其治療結果需要對病人 跟進并且多次測量。其次，我們提出收縮估計的貝葉斯亞組分 析模型。在貝葉斯统计框架下，先驗信息以及觀測数据能夠自 然地整合以此來作出更好的决策。為了使我們提出的方法得到 廣泛的應用，我們將会開發相應的电脑軟件, 以供免費下載。

17125814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125814.value: As human life expectancy continues to increase, Alzheimer's disease (AD) is becoming commonplace in aging populations worldwide. Patients with this progressive neurodegenerative disorder of the brain often suffer from memory and cognitive deterioration. The number of AD patients is rising fast, and costs and burden of related health care are soaring. Among potential AD treatments, symptomatic agents are expected to improve cognition and function over a short period of time, while disease-modifying agents can alter the course of the disease and slow down the rate of disease progression. However, no disease-modifying agent currently exists for AD patients. New drugs are urgently needed to help these patients. Our research helps improve the design of AD clinical trials and expedite the development of AD drugs.

17126014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126014.value: With more than half of the world’s population living in cities, we need better understanding of how the health and well-being of these more than three billion urban dwellers is shaped by their urban environment. Although living in cities offers most a better life, the benefits of urbanization are not equally distributed. Recent reports by the World Health Organization (WHO) reveal that pronounced health inequalities continue to persist in cities all over the world. Here the WHO definition of health represent “a state of complete, physical, mental and social well being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. This definition implies that to be healthy is not only to be free of disease but also the ability to make a living, to live in decent conditions, to have access to basic services, to engage in social relationships and to fell able affect one’s own circumstances. While Hong Kong is known for effective delivery of health care, health inequalities continue to be an important and unexplored public health issue. Being relatively economically unequal and extremely dense, Hong Kong’s proximity of rich and poor constitutes an unusual socio- spatial configuration that may bear important lessons for tackling health inequalities in other cities. this project will focus on the relationship between social and physical environments and small geographic areas, “neighborhoods”. The research question is, do the social and physical characteristics of an individual’s neighborhood affect their health outcomes? Health outcomes in this case refer to expressions of cumulative individual disadvantage, such as all-cause premature mortality, child mortality, mortality due to infectious diseases, non- communicable diseases and injuries, some major morbidity relating to the Global Disease Burden classification. Additionally, we will seek to assess whether the geographic location of public interventions such as, public housing park, medical and health facilities (e,g clinics) ameliorate potential negative impacts of lower quality urban environments. The research questions will be answered with advanced techniques of spatial analysis spatial econometrics. We will combine micro data on vital events and morbidity with Census, Hospital Authority and other sources of geospatial data. The results of the analysis will reveal a deeper understanding of how neighborhood characteristics can impact various health outcomes, which in turn can be used to develop and improve evidence based policy interventions. The results would be found relevant locally and internationally as well with many cities in this region have been undergoing similar changes as in Hong Kong,

17126614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126614.value: Mobilization of intracellular Ca2+ stores is involved in almost every aspect of many cellular processes. Cyclic adenosine diphosphoribose (cADPR) is an endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing nucleotide present in many cell types and different species, from plants to animals. cADPR is formed by ADP-ribosyl cyclases from nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD). It has been shown that many extracellular stimuli can induce cADPR production that leads to Ca2+ release or influx, establishing cADPR as a second messenger. Although evidence indicates that cADPR elicits Ca2+ release via ryanodine receptors (RyRs), the molecular mechanisms regarding the cADPR-induced Ca2+ release remain unknown. We hypothesize that novel signaling proteins are required for or can modify the ability of cADPR to induce Ca2+ release. We recently synthesized a fluorescent caged cADPR analogue, coumarin caged isopropylidene protected cIDPRE (Co-i-cIDPRE), and found that it is a potent and controllable cell permeant cADPR analogue. We subsequently performed targeted RNAi screening of 22 known RyRs associated proteins on uncaged Co-i-cIDPRE induced Ca2+ increase in human Jurkat cells. Knockdown of several genes, e.g. CHERP, Calcium homoeostasis modulator 1 (CALHM1), and Homer 1, markedly inhibited uncaged Co-i-cIDPRE induced Ca2+ increase. Yet, the precise roles of these hits in cADPR-Ca2+ signaling remain elusive. Moreover, it is quite possible that other proteins not included in our initial RNAi screening are also involved in cADPR-Ca2+ signaling. Therefore, we chemically synthesized a novel photoaffinity labeling cADPR analogue, PAL-cIDPRE, and found that it is a cell permeant cADPR agonist. In this proposal, we will apply PAL-cIDPRE to (1) dissect the roles and mechanisms of the hits from the RNAi screening, e.g. CHERP, Calsequestrin, and Homer1, in cADPR-mediated Ca2+ mobilization; and (2) identify novel cADPR binding proteins by combining approaches of photoaffinity protein-ligand labeling and mass spectrometric analyses.
