17126614.label: Realisation of objectives
17126614.value: Objective 1. To identify novel cADPR binding proteins by combining approaches of photoaffinity protein-ligand labeling and mass spectrometry analysis. Cyclic adenosine diphosphoribose (cADPR)-mediated Ca2+ signaling pathway is involved in a wide variety of cellular processes. Many extracellular stimuli have been shown to induce cADPR production that leads to calcium release or influx, establishing cADPR as a second messenger. CD38 is the dominant enzyme for synthesizing cADPR in mammalian systems and CD38 knockout mice show a number of physiological defects. Although the physiological importance of cADPR has been well documented, the molecular mechanism mediating the cADPR signaling remains elusive. It has been shown that cADPR targets ryanodine receptors (RyRs) on the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in many cell types, yet cADPR does not directly act on the receptor. It is possible that cADPR binds to an accessory protein in the channel complex. We hypothesize that novel signaling proteins are required for or can modify the ability of cADPR to induce Ca2+ release via RyRs. We designed and synthesized PAL-cIDPRE, a photoaffinity labeling cADPR analogue, and biotin carrying a corresponding clickable terminal of an azide group. We found that PAL-cIDPRE is a cell permeant cADPR agonist and can trigger Ca2+ releases via RyRs. Subsequently, we incubated PAL-cIDPRE with Jurkat cell crude extracts in the presence or absence of cIDPRE, followed by UV irradiation and click reaction, to produce the protein(s)-cIDPRE-biotin complex. Afterwards, the cIDPRE-bound proteins were purified by streptavidin-coupled Dynabeads® and analyzed by mass spectrometry analyses. One of bands, which was competed off by cIDPRE pre-incubation, turned out to be GAPDH by mass spec analyses and western blot analyses. We further found that cADPR specifically bound to the recombinant GAPDH proteins by the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. We then performed the molecule docking and molecular dynamic simulations to predict the binding sites in GAPDH for cADPR based on the crystal structures of GAPDH and cADPR, and found that Arg234 and His179 in GAPDH could be potential binding sites for cADPR. As expected, the SPR assay showed that GAPDHHis179Ala or GAPDHArg234Ala mutant proteins had significant lower binding affinity to cADPR than the wildtype GAPDH. Whereas His179Ala or Arg234Ala mutation in GAPDH did not affect the binding affinity between NAD+ and GAPDH. Thus, these data indicate that His179 and Arg234 in GAPDH are specific for its binding with cADPR, not NAD+. We also found that cADPR did not change GAPDH’s oxidative phosphorylation activity, and GAPDH failed to catalyze or degrade cADPR into ADPR or any other compounds. Therefore, we reason that cADPR might bind to GAPDH to trigger Ca2+ release from ER. As expected, GAPDH knockdown markedly inhibited NPE-cADPR or PAL-cIDPRE induced cytosolic Ca2+ increase in Jurkat cells, RyR3-expressing HKE293 cells, or human coronary artery smooth muscle (HCVSM) cells. On the other hand, GAPDH knockdown did not affect ATP, or histamine, or ionomycin, or thapsigargin induced Ca2+ increases in Jurkat cells, suggesting that GAPDH is not involved in IP3-mediated Ca2+ mobilization, and the ER Ca2+ pool is not affected by GAPDH depletion. In addition, GAPDH knockdown had little effects on store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE). Taken together, these data suggest that GAPDH is specifically involved in cADPR-mediated cytosolic Ca2+ mobilization. In addition, we found that cADPR treatment transiently but markedly increased the interaction between RyRs and GAPDH as shown by the Co-IP experiments. Furthermore, we treated Jurkat cells with saponin to partially permeabilize cell membrane, which enables the cytosolic GAPDH to leak out of the cells but spare the organelle or membrane associated one. Strikingly, we found that addition of cADPR to the permeabilized cells transiently induced the co-localization of GAPDH with RyRs by immunostaining analyses with antibodies against GAPDH and anti-RyRs, respectively. Pre-incubating the antibodies with respective peptides abolished the positive staining pattern in Jurkat cells, and ADPR, a metabolite of cADPR or NAD+, or NAD+ itself, failed to induce the localization of GAPDH with RyRs in saponin-treated Jurkat cells. Furthermore, super-resolution imaging analyses confirmed that GAPDH was transiently co-localized with RyRs in saponin-treated Jurkat cells upon cADPR treatment. Collectively, these data indicate that cADPR treatment transiently increases the interaction between GAPDH and RyRs in vivo. We also mapped the regions in RyRs or GAPDH for the interaction in vitro and found that the cADPR treatment increased the binding affinity between the catalytic domain of GAPDH and the central domain of RyRs. In summary, our data clearly indicate that GAPDH is the long-sought-after cADPR binding protein and is required for cADPR-mediated Ca2+ mobilization from ER via RyRs. Above findings have been published in Zhang et al., J Am Chem. Soc., 2017 Thus, we have successfully completed the objective 1.

17126614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126614.value: GAPDH plays essential roles in many important cellular events. The conformational changes of GAPDH and its trans-localization to ER upon cADPR binding, reported by us, should add another layer of regulation on GAPDH. Yet, the molecular details on how cADPR binds with GAPDH to trigger Ca2+ release from ER via RyRs remain elusive. Therefore, we are currently structurally and mechanistically studying the role of GAPDH in cADPR-mediated Ca2+ signaling. Based on the simulated cADPR-GAPDH complex structure, we performed structure-based drug screening and identified a number of small chemicals with high docking scores to the cADPR’s binding pocket in GAPDH. Therefore, we will further pharmacologically characterize these chemicals, and also chemically synthesize and characterize other small chemicals to modulate cADPR-mediated Ca2+ signaling. In summary, we aims to further dissect the role an mechanism of GAPDH in cADPR-mediated Ca2+ signaling in detail by combining approaches of organic chemistry synthesis, structural biology, and molecular and biochemical characterization. Our ultimate goal is to build a comprehensive cADPR-Ca2+ signaling network. Given the essential role of cADPR, RyRs, and GAPDH in a wide variety of cellular processes, the success of our study will be both scientifically significant and clinically relevant.

17126614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126614.value: Cyclic adenosine diphosphoribose (cADPR), an endogenous nucleotide derived from NAD, mobilizes Ca2+ release from ER via ryanodine receptors (RyRs), yet the bridging protein(s) between cADPR and RyRs remain(s) unknown. Here we synthesized a novel photoaffinity labeling cADPR agonist, PAL-cIDPRE, and subsequently applied it to purify its binding proteins in human Jurkat T cells. We identified glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) as one of cADPR binding protein(s), characterized the binding affinity between cADPR and GAPDH in vitro by SPR assay, and mapped the cADPR’s binding sites in GAPDH. We further demonstrated that cADPR induces the transient interaction between GAPDH and RyRs in vivo, and GAPDH knockdown abolished cADPR-induced Ca2+ release. On the other hand, GAPDH did not catalyze cADPR into any other known or novel compound(s). In summary, our data clearly indicate that GAPDH is the long-sought-after cADPR binding protein and is required for cADPR-mediated Ca2+ mobilization from ER via RyRs.

17126714.label: Realisation of objectives
17126714.value: 1. Determine the execution time of Bre1 in cohesion during the cell cycle: To determine the cell-cycle stages at which Bre1 is important for sister chromatid cohesion, we exploited the Auxin-Inducible Degron (domain for inducing degradation) (AID) system to conditionally control the expression of Bre1 at specific cell-cycle stages and examined the cohesion phenotype in G2/M-arrested cells. We constructed an AID*−9Myc tag of Bre1 at the endogenous locus and expressed F-box Transport Inhibitor Response 1 (TIR1) from rice Oryza sativa in a strain containing the GFP–LacI:LacO system for cohesion assay. Auxin binds to AID* and OsTIR1, which targets AID*−9Myc-tagged Bre1 for polyubiquitination and proteasome-mediated degradation. We degraded Bre1 at specific cell-cycle stages. Once the arrest in G1, S or G2/M was achieved by α-F, HU or Noc, respectively, with or without auxin induction, the medium was washed and released into the next cell cycle. Cohesion phenotype in G2/M-arrested cells was assessed. Degradation of Bre1 in G1 only or in G1 and S phases showed similar proportions of cohesion defects (20.7% and 17.1%, respectively), which were comparable to the proportion of cells in which Bre1 was degraded in all cell-cycle stages (19.2%), suggesting that Bre1’s role in G1 phase contributes to sister chromatid cohesion. To our surprise, degradation of Bre1 in S phase only or in S and G2/M phases resulted in fewer cells with cohesion defects (12.4% and 10.2%, respectively), but still significantly more defective cells compared to control. The occurrence rate of the cohesion defect caused by degradation of Bre1 in G1 and S phases (17.1%) was significantly higher than that in cells in which Bre1 is degraded in S only (12.4%). Degradation of Bre1 in G2/M phase only resulted in an occurrence rate for cohesion defects similar to that in the the negative control, implying that Bre1 is not required in G2/M phase for cohesion. These findings demonstrated that Bre1’s role in sister chromatid cohesion is most prominent in G1 phase, but also in S phase, but Bre1 is not required in G2/M phase. 2 Elucidate the molecular function of Bre1 in sister chromatid cohesion: Our Bre1 degron mutant experiment suggested that Bre1 is important in G1 and S phases, and may be involved in cohesin loading in G1 or sister chromatid cohesion establishment in S phase. The enrichment of Scc1 at early origins or on chromatin was not affected by BRE1. Next, we elucidated that the association of Ctf4, Ctf18 and Eco1 with chromatin and at early origins in S phase was significantly reduced in bre1Δ cells compared to WT. Our results suggest that Bre1 facilitates the localization of these cohesion establishment factors to the chromatin, and specifically to the early origins. We hypothesized that Bre1 may signal to replication factors upstream of Ctf4 and Ctf18 to affect their localizations. ChIP-qPCR and chromatin spreads showed the occupancy of Psf2, Polα and Mcm10 at early replication origins and on chromatin in bre1Δ cells in S phase was significantly reduced. Bre1 plays a role in regulating the localization of an upstream replication factor, Mcm10, which is important for replication initiation at origins, replication fork progression, and recruitment of replication-coupled cohesion establishment factors. 3. Decipher the biochemical action of Bre1 in sister chromatid cohesion: Ctf18 and Eco1 are both required for the acetylation of Smc3 during S phase to generate a stably chromosome-bound cohesin pool for enduring sister chromatid cohesion. In the absence of Bre1, Smc3 acetylation was significantly diminished, whereas the protein levels of Smc3 in WT and bre1Δ cells were similar. E3 ubiquitin ligase Bre1 is known to function with E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Rad6 to monoubiquitinate histone H2B at K123 (H2Bub1) through the conserved RING domain of Bre1. We performed the cohesion assay in G2/M-arrested cells by adding nocodazole for 3 hr. The cohesion defect in rad6Δ (19.6% ), bre1-RINGΔ (18.0%), which lacks E3 activity and cannot ubiquitinate H2B, and htb1-K123R htb2Δ (17.9%) occured at frequencies comparable to that in bre1Δ in nocodazole (18.8%). These results suggest that Rad6 and Bre1-catalyzed H2Bub1 accounts for Bre1’s function in sister chromatid cohesion. By contrast, deletion of the other known substrate of Bre1, swd2Δ (5.6%), showed only a WT level of cohesion defect.

17126714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126714.value: Bre1, a conserved E3 ubiquitin ligase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, together with its interacting partner Lge1, are responsible for histone H2B monoubiquitination, which regulates transcription, DNA replication, and DNA damage response and repair, ensuring the structural integrity of the genome. Deletion of BRE1 or LGE1also results in whole chromosome instability. We discovered a novel role for Bre1, Lge1 and H2Bub1 in chromosome segregation and sister chromatid cohesion. Bre1’s function in G1 and S phases contributes to cohesion establishment, but it is not required for cohesion maintenance in G2 phase. Bre1 is dispensable for the loading of cohesin complex to chromatin in G1, but regulates the localization of replication factor Mcm10 and cohesion establishment factors Ctf4, Ctf18 and Eco1 to early replication origins in G1 and S phases, and promotes cohesin subunit Smc3 acetylation for cohesion stabilization. H2Bub1 epigenetically marks the origins, potentially signaling the coupling of DNA replication and cohesion establishment.

17126714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126714.value: In the future it will be worthwhile to investigate whether genetic mutations that prevent sister chromatids adhering to each other is a major cause of the chromosome abnormalities seen in cancer cells. This knowledge may be useful for diagnosing cancers. Drugs that prevent the activity of Bre1 and other proteins involved in holding together sister chromatids could also be developed as potential cancer treatments that kill cancer cells by causing instability in their number of chromosomes.

17126714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126714.value: Most of the DNA in a cell is stored in structures called chromosomes. During every cell cycle, each cell needs to replicate its chromosomes, hold the two chromosome copies (also known as “sister chromatids”) together before cell division, and distribute them equally to the two new cells. Each step must be executed accurately otherwise the new cells will have extra or missing chromosomes – a condition that is seen in many cancer cells and that can cause embryos to die. Since these processes are so essential to life, they are highly similar in a range of species, from single-celled organisms such as yeast to multicellular organisms like humans. However, it was not clear when and how sister chromatids first join together, or how this process is linked to DNA replication. The DNA in the sister chromatids is wrapped around proteins called histones to form a structure known as chromatin. An enzyme called Bre1 plays roles in gene transcription and DNA replication and repair by adding ubiquitin molecules to a histone called H2B. By using genetic, molecular and cell biological approaches to study baker and brewer yeast cells, Zhang et al. show that the activity of Bre1 helps to hold sister chromatids together. Specifically, Bre1 recruits proteins to the chromatin before and during DNA replication, which help to initiate replication and to establish cohesion between the sister chromatids. The ubiquitin molecule attached to H2B by Bre1 is also essential for establishing cohesion, acting as a mark that helps to link the two processes.

17126814.label: Realisation of objectives
17126814.value: This project aimed to elucidate changes in fibronectin expression and functional consequence in tubulo-interstitial injury in lupus nephritis. We have completed Objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4. The remaining experiments for Objective 5 will be completed within the next 3-4 months. Objectives 1-3: The production of anti-dsDNA antibodies is a cardinal feature of lupus nephritis and they have been reported to contribute to pathogenesis. Their role in kidney fibrosis remains to be fully elucidated. Anti-dsDNA antibodies were isolated from 11 patients with active lupus nephritis using sequential DNA-cellulose and Protein A-Sepharose affinity chromatography. When compared to Control IgG, anti-dsDNA antibodies increased both soluble and extracellular fibronectin expression in human proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC). A subset of anti-dsDNA antibodies also induced fibronectin fragmentation in PTEC, denoted by the presence of low molecular weight fibronectin (~45 kDa) and this was accompanied by a concomitant increase in matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2) and MMP-9 activity, whereas anti-dsDNA antibodies had no effect on TIMP-1 or TIMP-2 activity. This would suggest a possible disparity between MMP and TIMP activities and subsequent synthesis and degradation/fragmentation of matrix proteins. Anti-dsDNA antibody-mediated induction of fibronectin was through activation of MAPK, mTOR and PI3K signaling pathways, and increased secretion of TGF-beta1, TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-8 and MCP-1. The assembly of fibronectin in the extracellular milieu is dependent on the activation and polymerization of soluble fibronectin monomers and their interaction with cell surface integrins. Incubation of PTEC with soluble fibronectin increased TGF-beta secretion and collagen I expression, suggesting that soluble fibronectin, in addition to increasing extracellular fibronectin accumulation, may also directly amplify fibrotic processes within the tubulo-interstitium. Anti-dsDNA antibodies also induced senescence-associated beta-galactosidase in PTEC, a marker of early aging, an observation not noted in PTEC incubated with Control IgG. Aging PTEC possessed increased inflammatory and fibrotic properties under physiological conditions as demonstrated by increased secretion of IL-6, IL-8 and MCP-1 and expression of matrix proteins such as fibronectin, laminin and collagen I, and these injurious processes were exacerbated in the presence of anti-dsDNA antibodies. Multiple isoforms of fibronectin can be produced as a result of alternative splicing and post-translational modifications. These splicing sites include extra domain A (EDA) and extra domain B (EDB). Under physiological conditions, EDA and EDB fibronectin were not expressed in PTEC. Incubation of cells, especially aging PTEC, with anti-dsDNA antibodies induced EDA, but not EDB expression, mediated in part through mTOR and PI3K phosphorylation and increased secretion of TGF-beta1, IL-1beta and TNF-alpha. Increased EDA fibronectin expression was accompanied by decreased E-cadherin expression, a marker of epithelial integrity. To assess the functional role of EDA fibronectin in the PTEC, EDA+ and EDA- peptides were generated. EDA+ but not EDA- peptide, induced native fibronectin expression in a dose dependent manner. This was accompanied by increased SNAIL, ZEB2, collagen I and laminin expression (markers of EMT and fibrosis), and decreased E-cadherin expression. Using immunohistochemistry, native fibronectin, collagen I and laminin were predominantly expressed in the extracellular matrix. Increased matrix protein expression by EDA+ peptide was mediated through upregulation of mTOR and PI3K phosphorylation. EDA+ peptide also increased IL-6, IL-8 and MCP-1 secretion through ERK, p38 MAPK and PI3K phosphorylation. Furthermore, EDA+ peptide increased alpha5beta1 expression and induced actin polymerization in PTEC but had no apparent effect on cell proliferation. Objective 4: We investigated EDA fibronectin expression in the kidney. In renal specimens from patients with biopsy-proven Class III/IV +/- V lupus nephritis, EDA fibronectin was noted in the tubulo-interstitium, especially in proximal tubules showing atrophy, whereas EDA fibronectin was absent in normal kidney specimens. Since it is not feasible to collect serial renal biopsies from patients to assess EDA fibronectin expression with disease progression, we utilized the NZBWF1 mouse, an established murine model of lupus nephritis. In NZBWF1 mice, EDA fibronectin was present in glomeruli in proliferative lupus nephritis and in the tubulo-interstitium when tubulo-interstitial injury denoted by influx of infiltrating cells and tubular atrophy, were apparent. A proportion of infiltrating immune cells also expressed EDA fibronectin. Tubulo-interstitial EDA fibronectin increased with progressive renal failure and its expression correlated with proteinuria and the extent of kidney fibrosis. Objective 5: Plasma fibronectin level was increased in patients with active lupus nephritis compared to healthy subjects. We are currently optimizing our ‘in-house’ ELISA for EDA fibronectin and measurements and analysis of data will be conducted in the coming few months.

17126814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126814.value: In this study, we have uncovered a role of soluble fibronectin in the amplification of fibrogenesis in PTEC. We have also identified a role of EDA fibronectin in kidney inflammation and fibrosis in lupus nephritis, and its contribution to epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) transition in PTEC, a process that precedes tissue fibrosis and endows epithelial cells with invasive and fibrotic properties. Using a combination of biochemical and molecular biology techniques, we demonstrated that anti-dsDNA antibodies but not Control IgG increased soluble and insoluble native fibronectin expression in a time-dependent manner in PTEC, which was mediated through increased phosphorylation of MAPK, PKC and PI3K signaling pathways and anti-dsDNA antibody induction of TGF-beta1, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and TNF-alpha secretion. Whereas insoluble fibronectin was predominantly deposited in the extracellular matrix, soluble fibronectin amplified tubular cell fibrogenesis through increased TGF-beta1 secretion and collagen I synthesis. Anti-dsDNA antibodies also induced EDA but not EDB fibronectin expression and this was mediated in part through increased TGF-beta1, IL-1beta and TNF-alpha secretion, and activation of mTOR and PI3K signaling pathways. These findings were more prominent in aging PTEC or cells undergoing early senescence. To elucidate the role of EDA fibronectin in PTEC, recombinant EDA- and EDA+ peptides were generated. EDA+ but not EDA- peptide, increased IL-6, IL-8 and MCP-1 secretion and native fibronectin, collagen and laminin expression and induced SNAIL- and ZEB2- repression of E-cadherin expression in PTEC. In renal biopsies from patients with biopsy-proven Class III/IV +/- V lupus nephritis, EDA fibronectin was markedly increased in the tubulo-interstitium especially in proximal tubules showing atrophy and areas showing influx of immune cells, whereas EDA+ fibronectin was absent in normal kidney specimens. Similar results were observed in lupus-prone mice and the expression of EDA fibronectin and extent of kidney fibrosis correlated with renal failure. Our data highlight a pathogenic role of EDA fibronectin in tubulo-interstitial injury in lupus nephritis, and its induction in the kidney may be attributed to anti-dsDNA antibody binding to PTEC. This study resulted in one original article published in the Journal of Autoimmunity, and another manuscript is currently under preparation. Part of the data has been included in four invited review articles. Part of this study has also been presented at the 12th International Congress on SLE & 7th Asian congress on Autoimmunity in Melbourne in 2017.

17126814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126814.value: In this study, we demonstrated that EDA fibronectin, a glycoprotein that is not normally present in healthy adult tissue, is expressed in the tubulo-interstitium of patients with biopsy-proven severe proliferative lupus nephritis. EDA fibronectin was also present in renal specimens from patients with non-lupus renal diseases such as IgA nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy, suggesting that its induction is not specific to lupus nephritis. We have conducted some preliminary studies and have observed increased EDA fibronectin in a murine model of non-lupus tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. The degree of tubulo-interstitial damage is strongly associated with less favorable long-term renal prognosis in renal patients. There is currently no treatment for kidney fibrosis. Insight into the underlying mechanisms that mediates kidney fibrosis is essential for the design of novel treatment. To further develop this research, we plan to investigate the role of EDA fibronectin in PTEC and interstitial fibroblasts in murine models of chronic kidney disease using EDA fibronectin wildtype and knockout mice. We have submitted our research proposal for funding support to the RGC GRF 2019/20 application round, and the outcome is pending.

17126814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126814.value: Lupus nephritis is a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus, a debilitating autoimmune disease prevalent in this locality that predominantly affects females of child-bearing age. Lupus nephritis is characterized by the production of anti-dsDNA antibodies and immune-mediated kidney injury. If inadequately controlled, chronic inflammation will lead to kidney fibrosis where viable tissue is replaced by scar tissue leading to a loss of kidney function. How kidney fibrosis is initiated remains to be fully defined. Fibronectin is a large multi-functional protein that is absent from the tubulo-interstitium of healthy kidneys. Multiply forms of fibronectin are expressed during disease such as extra domain A (EDA) fibronectin. EDA fibronectin is present in the tubulo-interstitium in patients and mice with active lupus nephritis, and the extent of EDA fibronectin accumulation correlated with the severity of kidney impairment. Anti-dsDNA antibodies induced EDA fibronectin expression in proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC, the predominant cell type in the tubulo-interstitium) through activation of the mTOR and PI3K signaling pathways. EDA fibronectin contributed to kidney injury by endowing PTEC with more invasive, inflammatory and fibrotic properties. Our data provide insight into the pathogenic role EDA fibronectin in lupus nephritis.

17126914.value: 大塊組織的移植成活依賴於移植後立即獲得宿主的血液供應。牙髓組織被包裹在牙本質中央,僅有根尖孔供用血液。我們的研究表明，即使預先血管化的牙髓組織植入根管內,組織的上部也會發生缺氧性壞死。促進預先預血管化牙髓在根尖孔與宿主血管形成迅速、直接的血管連接可能解決組織上部的缺氧。我們的初步研究表明，根尖周幹細胞在缺氧狀態下,顯著上調促血管生成因數如:HIF, VEGF和EphrinB2的表達。調控這些因數的表達有助於血管新生和血管連接。 本課題將研究EphrinB2過表達根尖周幹細胞促進血管內皮細胞形成血管網的能力。研究 EphrinB2/EphB4調控根尖周幹細胞與血管內皮細胞的相互作用,對新形成血管網的影響。通過動物體內研究，探討預先血管化的初級血管網與宿主血管的吻合，已及EphrinB2過表達對其促進作用。本研究將EphrinB2過表達根尖周幹細胞預先血管化, 體外和體內實驗結果，將揭示EphrinB2在牙髓血管再生和血管吻合中的作用。

17126914.label: Realisation of objectives
17126914.value: 1. The objectives 1 and 2 have been fully achieved with in vitro studies. We found that coculture of HUVECs and SCAPs on Matrigel accelerated the formation of blood vessel-like structures, and Western blot confirmed that ephrinB2 phosphorylation was initiated at 0.5 hours of coculture and peaked at 1 hour. The delayed interaction of SCAPs with HUVECs could stabilize these structures. The addition of ephrinB2 into the coculture of SCAPs and HUVECs could preserve vascularlike structures for a longer duration. Hence, it can be inferred that ephrinB2/EphB4 signaling plays a crucial role in angiogenic processes during coculture of SCAPs with HUVECs, by recruiting SCAPs as pericyte-like cells in the stabilization of vascularlike structures (J Endod. 2016 ;42(9):1362-70). Further, we studied the angiogenic ability of HUVECs cocultured with ephrin-B2-SCAPs or GFP-SCAPs under normoxia and hypoxia. It was found that HUVECs cocultured with ephrin-B2-SCAPs had formed extensive vascular-like structures. HUVECs cocultured with ephrin-B2-SCAPs under hypoxia formed vascular-like structures earlier than GFP-SCAPs. We further measured VEGF gene and protein expression in ephrin-B2-SCAPs and GFP-SCAPs under hypoxia. It was found that Ephrin-B2-SCAPs upregulated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) secretion under hypoxia (Oral Diseases Manuscript ID ODI-09-18-OM-6581.R1). 2. The objective 3 has been completed. It was found that Matrigel-encapsulating HUVECs with or without ephrin-B2-SCAPs or GFP-SCAPs were transplanted into a subcutaneous region of SCID mice. After 1 week, gel plugs were removed by surgery. Gel plugs of the control group without cells were translucent white. There was a very small red region in gel plugs of the GFP-SCAP group. Furthermore, ephrin-B2-SCAPs formed more red blood vessels than GFP-SCAPs. Compared with GFP-SCAPs cocultured with HUVECs, more blood vessels were seen in the gel plugs of ephrin-B2-SCAPs cocultured with HUVECs, and the gel plugs were full of dark red blood vessels. H&E staining and immunohistochemistry for CD31 were performed to detect tissue profiles. The number of blood vessels was lower in GFP-SCAP and ephrin-B2-SCAP groups compared with co-transplanted groups. The diameter of blood vessels formed in the ephrin-B2-SCAP coculture group was significantly larger than that in the GFP-SCAP coculture group. Compared with the GFP-SCAP group, ephrin-B2-SCAPs formed more blood vessels. Human CD31, which is a marker of ECs, was clearly stained in HUVEC-containing vessels. These data indicated that the morphology of the newly formed blood vessels was influenced by ephrin-B2 expression. Furthermore, the majority of blood vessel lumens were perfused with red blood cells, indicating that the blood vessels are functional (Oral Diseases Manuscript ID ODI-09-18-OM-6581.R1). 3. The objective 4 has been fully completed. We are now analysing the in vivo sample further by immunohistochemistry methods, such as α-SMA, SM22α. We also applied in vitro 3D fibrin culture model to cocultue HUVECs and DPSCs, and found that DPSCs were capable of inducing vascular morphogenesis by ECs in fibrin matrix, blockade of EphrinB2/EphB4 interaction significantly reduced expressions of α-SMA, calponin and PDGFRβ, which indicates that the capacity of DPSCs to differentiate into mural cells may be dependent on EphrinB2/EphB4 signaling. The expression of laminin, a major molecular component of ECM, vascular maturation predominantly through interacting with adhesive integrin receptors expressed on ECs was remarkably diminished once EphrinB2/EphB4 signaling was inhibited. Collectively, our results provide molecular insights that show EphrinB2/EphB4 being a key player regulating the capacity of DPSCs to induce ECs capillary morphogenesis. Specifically, DPSCs formed mural cell association with ECs and secreted VEGF to promote angiogenesis (Oral Diseases Manuscript ID ODI-09-18-OM-6581.R1; Journal of Dental Research Manuscript ID JDR-18-1059).

17126914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126914.value: EphrinB2/EphB4 signaling regulates dental stem cells (SCAPs and DPSCs) in inducing ECs angiogenesis and stabilizing the newly formed vessel-like structures. Overexpression of EphrinB2 in SCAPs increased blood vessel formation and accelerated the interconnection with host blood circulation. Therefore, the role of EphrinB2 signaling in promoting earlier establishment of functional blood vessels can significantly support the survival and integration with host tissues. Regulation of EphrinB2 signaling via drug delivery could be an effective way for promoting new tissue regeneration and treatment of ischemia diseases.

17126914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126914.value: Enhancing new blood vessel formation is the key for new tissue formation or recovery of ischemic tissues or organs. Our studies revealed that EphrinB2/EphB4 signaling critically regulates the interactions between dental stem cells and endothelial cells in blood vessel-like structure formation. Specifically, much faster blood vessel formation and quick connection with the host blood circulation have been achieved via manipulating EphrinB2 expression. These findings will not only expand our understanding of the in vivo dynamic interplay between DPSCs and ECs but also aid in engineering functional vasculatures that could in turn facilitate dental pulp tissue regeneration.

17127014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127014.value: Hematopoiesis refers to a multistep process that continuously produces a variety of blood cells, including erythroid, lymphoid, myeloid, NK, and dendritic cells in response to infection and homeostasis requirements. It estimated that a healthy adult needs to produce about 500 billion new blood cells daily to maintain steady state cell number in the peripheral circulation. This process is under tight regulation, and deregulation of which leads to blood diseases, such as leukemia and anemia. Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer. ALL can be broadly classified into B-ALL and T-ALL according to its origin, i.e. B-ALL from bone marrow primed toward B lineage and T-ALL from thymus primed toward T lineage. Transcriptional factor Ikaros is a master regulator of hematopoiesis with crucial role in lymphoid development and maturation. Inactivation of Ikaros by recurrent deletion and mutation has been implicated with the pathogenesis of human ALL with poor outcome. Patients identified carrying deletion of Ikaros are at high risk of relapse, necessitating an alternative intensive treatment. In murine model, deletion of Ikaros in thymus almost always leads to T-ALL. Our recent work by integrative genomic profiling has characterized the mechanism underpinning the leukemic transformation mediated by Ikaros depletion. In thymocytes, Ikaros’ function is dependent on the interaction with ATPase Mi-2beta-containing Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase (Mi-2beta/NuRD) complex. During thymopoiesis, Ikaros directs Mi-2beta/NuRD to lymphoid loci by the DNA binding specificity of Ikaros, and regulates lymphoid gene expression. When Ikaros depleted, the local activity of Mi-2beta/NuRD is dramatically increased along with redistribution of Mi-2beta/NuRD to the permissive chromatin of other poised genes. Many of these poised genes are involved in metabolism and cell growth, activation of which drives the aberrant proliferation of thymocytes. Intriguingly, mice double deficient in both Mi-2beta and Ikaros survived past 6 months and were disease free, whereas mice with only Ikaros depletion rapidly developed T cell leukemia. It is postulated that double knockout of both Ikaros and Mi-2beta can partially reverse the aberrant gene expression caused by the knockout of Ikaros only. We will verify this in this study. Ikaros is not working alone. Actually, there are many other proteins cooperatively acting in concert to regulate T cell development and leukemogenesis. We’ll characterize how Ikaros orchestrates this process and identify the common downstream gene targets mediating leukemogenesis. Characterization of the convergent downstream effectors will lead to novel targets for diagnosis and therapeutic intervention against leukemia. 因应于感染和内环境稳定的要求, 造血干细胞连续生产各种种类的血细胞，包括红细胞，淋巴细胞，粒细胞，NK细胞和树突细胞。据估计一个健康的成年人需要 日产约5千亿新的血细胞，以维持稳定的外周循环细胞数。这个过程是在严格的监管下进行的，放松管制 会导致血液病，如白血病和贫血。 急性淋巴细胞白血病（ALL）是最常见的儿童癌症。根据其来源可以 大致可分为B-ALL和T-ALL。转录因子Ikaros基因在淋巴发育和成熟中起着至关重要的作用 。 Ikaros基因经常性的缺失和失活 突变导致白血病, 并与疾病预后不良直接相关。 患者携带缺失的Ikaros基因是复发的高危人群，因此需要 另一种强化治疗。 在小鼠模型中，胸腺缺失Ikaros基因几乎 总是导致T细胞白血病。 我们最近的工作经由综合基因组分析揭示了由Ikaros基因缺失介导白血病转化的机制。在胸腺细胞，Ikaros基因的功能是依赖于与含有ATP酶活性的Mi-2beta 核小体重塑和去乙酰化酶（MI-2beta/ NURD）复合体的相互作用。在胸腺细胞发育中，Ikaros蛋白确定了Mi-2beta/ NURD的DNA结合 特异性，并调节淋巴细胞基因的表达。有趣的是，同时缺乏MI- 2beta和Ikaros基因的小鼠在存活的6个月中，并无白血病，而仅缺失Ikaros基因的小鼠迅速发展成T细胞白血病。据推测，同时缺乏MI- 2beta和Ikaros基因可部分逆转仅Ikaros基因缺失所造成的异常基因表达 。我们将在本研究中验证这一点。 在调节T细胞发育和白血病的过程中, Ikaros基因需要与许多其它蛋白共同作用。我们将研究Ikaros基因如何编排控制这个过程，并确定共同的下游靶基因 ,及它们如何影响白血病的产生, 这将提供诊断和治疗白血病的新靶标。

17127014.label: Realisation of objectives
17127014.value: Ikaros is a transcriptional factor (TF), whose activity is regulated by forming complex with chromatin remodeler (CR, also called chromatin regulator) Mi-2beta. Focusing on Ikaros in leukemogenesis, we have collaborated with a lab from Harvard University with a paper published on Nature Immunology (Joshi I, Yoshida T, Jena N, Qi X, Zhang J, Van Etten RA, Georgopoulos K (2014) Ikaros Mutation Confers Integrin-Dependent Survival Of Pre-B Cells and Progression To Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia. Nature Immunology 15(3):294-304). We also further explored the interaction data between Ikaros and Mi-2beta in another papers of ours (Zhang J*, Jackson Af, Naito T, Liu F, Dosei M, Seavitt J, Liu F, Dose M, Kashiwagi M, Yoshida T, Gounari F, Petrie H, Georgopoulos K. (2012) Harnessing of the Nucleosome Remodeling Deacetylase complex controls lymphocyte development and prevents leukemogenesis. Nature Immunology 13, 86-94). We hypothesized that there is a general paradigm of gene regulation, in which the activity of TF is regulated by forming complex with its CR partner. Alterations of the interaction between TF and its CR partner mediate dysregulated development and tumorigenesis. Within this study, we designed a strategy to prove our hypothesis. We identified and validated these TF-CR chromatin remodeling complex, and addressed our proposed aims (aim 1, the mode of action of the chromatin remodeling complex; aim 2 genetic network orchestrated by master regulators mediating tumorigenesis, e.g., leukemogenesis). This GRF project is to focus on Chromatin Remodelers (CR, also called Chromatin Regulator) forming complex with TF, and their mode of action in tumorigenesis, e.g. leukemogenesis. CRs are important components of epigenetics. Many CRs can function as Master Regulators (MR) mediating development and tumorigenesis, e.g., Mi-2beta, an important CR, is involved in leukemogenesis by interacting with TF Ikaros, another MR identified before by us. In this study, we designed a framework to identify the general mode of action for CRs to function as master regulator by interacting with TF. We conducted differential connection analysis to explore the functional interaction between CRs and TFs as well as the implications in transcriptional dysregulation during tumorigenesis. Finally, we experimentally verified the top-ranked driver CRs and modulation pairs of CR-TF interaction. This study has been published by us (Ru B, Sun J, Kang Q, Tong Y, Zhang J*. (2018) A framework for identifying dysregulated chromatin regulators as master regulators in human cancer. Bioinformatics. 2018 Oct 25. doi: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty836. [Epub ahead of print]. ). We have also designed a strategy to identify and prioritize master regulators in cancer. A Master Regulator (MR) is a gene that locates at the hub of a regulatory network and controls a large number of target genes (collectively termed as its regulon). MRs are highly connected and have been demonstrated to be involved in lineage specification during development. Traditionally, it mainly refers to transcription factors, which typically regulate gene transcription by acting on the cis-regulatory elements of their targets, including promoters and enhancers. Recently, the concept has been expanded to include chromatin regulators (see our paper: Ru B, Sun J, Tong Y, Wong CN, Chandra A, Tang ATS, Chow LKY, Wun WL, Levitskaya Z, Zhang J*. (2017) CR2Cancer: a database for chromatin regulators in human cancer. Nucleic Acids Research. 46(D1):D918-D924) and miRNAs (see our paper: Tong Y, Ru B, Zhang J*. (2018) miRNACancerMAP: an integrative web server inferring miRNA regulation network for cancer. Bioinformatics. 2018 Sep 15;34(18):3211-3213), which can also affect intracellular functions via transcriptional regulation of mRNA transcripts. Many studies have revealed that various genetic alterations in upstream pathways would converge to a small number of deregulated MRs, initiating and maintaining tumor cell state and identity. Therefore, identification of aberrant MRs in a specific context can provide new insights for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutics. One feature of MRs is that small variations in the expression level of MRs may result in greater changes in their target genes’ expression. Therefore, it is always challenging to identify the influential MRs directly by themselves since MRs are usually not the most differentially expressed genes during a phenotype transition. An alternative strategy was proposed that the activity of a MR can be represented by the expression of its regulon. With the rapid development of high-throughput sequencing techniques, construction of regulons benefits from gene regulatory network reconstruction based on large-scale gene expression profiles. We designed a strategy based on reverse engineering to successfully identify the master regulators involved in tumorigenesis. This study has been published by us (Ru B, Tong Y, Zhang J*. (2018) MR4Cancer: a web server prioritizing master regulators for cancer. Bioinformatics. 2018 Jul 23. doi: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty658. [Epub ahead of print]). We have also catalogued all CRs critical for tumorigenesis (Ru B, Sun J, Tong Y, Wong CN, Chandra A, Tang ATS, Chow LKY, Wun WL, Levitskaya Z, Zhang J*. (2017) CR2Cancer: a database for chromatin regulators in human cancer. Nucleic Acids Research. 46(D1):D918-D924). In aim 3, we tested various therapeutic approaches to treat leukemia mediated by Ikaros inactivation, such as applying HDAC inhibitor to inhibit HDACs (part of NuRD) activity, restoring Ikaros function, and inhibiting downstream convergent targets via shRNA. However, these strategies had limited effect. For example, to restore Ikaros activity/function, it is critical to understand how Ikaros activity is regulated. Toward this direction, we figured out some fundamental rules about Ikaros gene regulation with collaboration with the lab from Harvard University (Yoshida T, Landhuis E, Dose M, Hazan I, Zhang J, Naito T, Jackson AF, Wu J, Perroti EA, Kaufmann C, Gounari F, Morgan BA, Georgopoulos K (2013) Transcriptional regulation of the Ikzf1 locus. Blood. 122(18):3149-59). From this study, we identified a T cell-specific enhancer, named Enhancer-H, critical for Ikaros gene expression, but the detailed information about this enhancer is still lacking. In this project, we have designed a strategy, which led to full characterization of the T-cell specific Ikaros (encoded by gene Ikzf1) enhancer. First we employed CRISPR/Cas9 to insert two loxP sites into the Ikzf1 locus along with selection markers to swap out Enhancer H. Single cell-clones with the two Ikzf1 alleles swapped by the two selection markers can be obtained with drug selection. Subsequently, Enhancer H variants with point mutations were introduced into genome mediated by Cre-Lox recombination, and selected by Thymidine Kinase/ Ganciclovir system. This application of double genome-editing has proved to be very efficient and flexible, solving the issues and limitations with single CRISPR/Cas9 system. With this efficient approach, we identified the minimum cis-acting elements on Enhancer H critical for Ikzf1 T cell-specific expression, which was further verified by murine primary T cells and in vitro T-cell differentiation from embryonic stem cells. Furthermore, the study identified Oct2 and Gata3 as the cognate trans-acting factors associating with Enhancer H to regulate Ikzf1 expression. The screening method described here can be applied into functional interrogation of genomic non-coding elements in general. The results described above have been reported by our paper, “Dissection T cell-specific enhancer of Ikaros by CRISPR/Cas9 and Cre-Lox mediated in situ mutagenesis”, currently under review.

17127014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127014.value: Our characterization of the underlying mechanism how Ikaros mutation mediating leukemia is essential for therapeutic development in next step. We have generalized the mode of action between TF Ikaros-and CR mi2-beta to a general paradigm. 17127014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127014.value: It is increasingly recognized that epigenetics plays a critical role in pathogenesis of many diseases as well as genetics. Chromatin remodeler is an important class of epigenetics, serving as the bridge by which environment and lifestyle exert its effect on the cellular machinery at the molecular level. The fascinating part is how the interplay between genetics (like transcriptional factor, TF) and epigenetics (like chromatin remodeler, CR) defines cell differentiation, lineage specification, organ development, and its implications in pathogenesis, such as tumorigenesis. We have identified the general mode of action for CRs to function as master regulator by interacting with TF to affect tumorigenesis. Our characterization of the underlying mechanism how Ikaros mutation mediating leukemia is essential for therapeutic development in next step. Our characterization of the gene regulatory network of Ikaros paves the way to restore Ikaros activity/function.

17127714.label: Project Objectives
17127714.value: To investigate if the N9 NA gene confers better infectivity and/or transmissibility over the N7 and N3 in the genetic context of a human H7N9 virus. The H7N9 has caused hundreds of human cases while H7N7 and H7N3 viruses co-circulating in poultry are not known to cause human infections. Laboratory ferret experiments demonstrated that H7N7 was shed from the nasal route at lower titers and transmitted at delayed and less efficient patterns than the human H7N9 viruses. This may be partially attributed to the different NA subtypes. To examine if the deletion in the NA stalk region of the human H7N9 and Ck/WZ-like H7N7 contributes to the ability of the virus to replicate and transmit across species. One of the most notable signatures observed in the NA genes of the related H7N7 and H7N9 is the amino acid deletions at the stalk region (Δ69-73 for N9 and Δ53-72 for N7). As NA stalk deletions have been repeatedly associated with the adaptation of avian influenza viruses in a new host, we seek to test if such changes will alter the NA activity and the virus replication and transmissibility. To investigate if the internal gene constellation derived from the enzootic Asian H9N2 virus is a determinant for the better replication and transmission of the H7N9 and H7N7 strains in ferrets. The most significant change in the H7N9 and related H7N7 viruses from the duck gene pool viruses was the acquisition of the internal gene complex from the H9N2 viruses enzootic in China. We will test if incorporating this complex would contribute to viral replication and transmission and also if it leads to replication in the upper respiratory tract and transmission through the nasal route. To investigate if the H7N9 HA lineage is responsible for the viral infectivity and transmissibility in mammals. We will test HA genes from different H7 virus strains and see how they contribute to the virus infection and transmissions. Potential substitutions related to the increased virus infectivity or transmissibility may be identified.

17127714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127714.value: In February to March of this year, an avian-origin influenza A(H7N9) virus was initially transmitted to humans and subsequently caused repeated, sporadic human infections. Genetic analyses revealed that the H7N9 viruses had some mammalian virus signatures and evidence of limited human-to-human transmission in a few family clusters. This suggests that this H7N9 lineage has human pandemic potential and highlights that China is still one of the major influenza epicenters. Our active surveillance revealed that chickens (Ck) at live-poultry markets (LPM) in the outbreak regions were the source of human infections. The H7N9 viruses mainly replicated at the upper respiratory tract of birds, and direct exposure of humans to affected poultry was the major interspecies transmission route. Our active surveillance also revealed that an H7N7 virus (Ck/WZ-like), with all gene segments except for neuraminidase (NA) highly related to those of the H7N9 lineage, was circulating in parallel in the outbreak region. However, no human infections with H7N7 have been identified. Infectivity and transmission studies in ferrets showed that both avian and human H7N9 viruses replicated productively in the upper and lower respiratory tract, but the human viruses transmitted more effectively. Ck/WZ-like H7N7 viruses replicated and transmitted more poorly than the H7N9 viruses while related duck H7N7 isolates with gene pool-like internal genes could not transmit between ferrets at all. The exact determinants and mechanisms responsible for the differential infectivity and transmissibility of the H7 viruses to humans are not clear. We hypothesize that the genetic differences between the groups of viruses caused these differences. Here we propose to use the ferret model and a set of reverse genetically reconstructed viruses to investigate the molecular basis that may underlie the observed range of behaviors of avian H7 viruses in mammals. Our proposal aims to examine the steps that led to the H7N9 related viruses becoming infectious to humans and to understand the related molecular changes or gene constellations that contributed to this. The information generated in this proposal will provide insights into the pathway leading to the emergence of the human H7N9 isolates and the genetic determinants of the infectivity, pathogenicity and transmissibility of H7N9 related viruses. Such knowledge will be crucial for a better understanding of the threats from these viruses and preparedness for future influenza pandemics. 自2013年2月份以來，一種新型的禽源H7N9甲型流感病毒已經引起了數百宗人類感染個案。遺傳分析結果表明這種病毒已經具備了一些可能較爲適應哺乳動物的突變，在個別家庭聚集性病例中，也出現了有限的人傳人證據。因此，該病毒可能具有引起流感大流行的潛力，中國也仍然是主要的流感形成中心。 我們通過流感病毒監測發現活禽市場的雞是疫情爆發區人感染的最主要來源。H7N9病毒主要在家禽上呼吸道中複制，並通過直接暴露跨物種傳播給人。另外我們還發現了一種Ck/WZ樣H7N7病毒，除了NA基因之外，其他七條基因片段都與H7N9高度相關。這兩種H7病毒共存于華東的爆發區，但目前沒有人類感染該H7N7的報道。 在動物模型的感染與傳播實驗中，我們發現人和禽的H7N9病毒都能夠有效地在雪貂的上下呼吸道中進行複制，但人的分離株傳播性較好。Ck/WZ樣H7N7病毒雖可在雪貂中感染與傳播，但其複制及傳播性都比H7N9病毒弱。來自于鴨子的典型基因庫樣H7N7病毒則完全不能在雪貂間進行傳播。 不同H7亞型流感病毒株對人類表現出不同的感染與傳播能力，這種差異的機制目前尚不清楚。我們認爲不同H7病毒間的遺傳差異，可能是其主要的決定因素。在本研究中，我們擬使用雪貂作爲動物模型，通過反向遺傳學構建一系列的重組病毒，用于研究禽H7病毒對哺乳動物感染與傳播能力的分子機制。我們將系統研究H7N9及其相關的病毒是如何逐步獲得感染人類的能力，以及其相關的基因構成和分子突變。 本研究將爲深入了解人類H7N9病毒産生的途徑、以及H7N9相關病毒感染性、致病性、傳播性的遺傳決定簇提供重要的信息。這將有助于我們更好理解病毒的危險性，並爲以後的病毒大流行做好准備。

17127714.label: Realisation of objectives
17127714.value: < Objective 1 > To investigate the mammalian infectivity and transmissibility of different NA subtypes in the genetic context of the human H7N9 virus, the NA gene of a prototype H7N9 virus (A/Anhui/1/2013, AH1) were replaced respectively by those from three co-circulating H7 viruses, A/Chicken/Wenzhou/610/2013 (CK/WZ610, H7N7), A/Duck/Wenzhou/771/2013 (Dk/WZ771, H7N3) and A/Duck/Wenzhou/47/2013 (Dk/WZ47, H7N7). A total of four reverse-genetically reconstructed (RG) viruses were tested in A549 cells (adenocarcinomic human alveolar basal epithelial cells) at different temperatures and in a ferret model. NA activity was also measured for each virus. It was found that replacement with the N7 gene from CK/WZ610 or Dk/WZ47 significantly reduced the virus replication in A549 cells both at 33℃ and 37℃, but this was much more prominent at 33℃ and for replacement with N7 gene from CK/WZ610. Replacement with the N3 gene from Dk/WZ771 only limitedly reduced virus replication when compared with the prototype H7N9. Assays on the NA activities indicated that both N7 NAs shown lower Vmax and higher Km than the N3 and N9 NAs, implying that the N7 might have a higher affinity but a slower reactivity to the substrates. In ferrets inoculated with the RG viruses, replacement of the NA genes in the AH1 gene backbone did not significantly change the virus replication and shedding titer from the nasal route. Although RG virus with the N7 NA genes from Dk/WZ47 showed a slight delay in the onset of virus shed by the physical contact and airborne exposed ferrets, both H7 viruses seroconverted all ferrets in the transmission study. In general, the virus transmissibility was not significantly reduced if the NA gene of AH1 was replaced by the chicken or duck N7 or the duck N3 viruses. < Objective 2 > To examine if deletions in the NA stalk region would alter the NA activity and the virus replication and transmissibility across species, four pairs of RG viruses with full-length NA segments or deletions at the NA stalk were reconstructed. Specifically, QISNT at position 69-73 for the N9 and INQNNTTVVENTYVNNTTII at position 53-72 for the N7 were inserted back to the NA genes of the AH1 (N9) and CK/WZ610 (N7) viruses, or deleted correspondingly from the wild type DK/WZ47 (N7) and A/Shanghai/05/2013 (SH5, H7N9) viruses with full-length NAs. Infections in A549 cells found that deletion at the NA stalk of wildtype SH5 virus significantly reduced the H7N9 virus replication at both 33℃ or 37℃, while insertion at the NA stalk to the wildtype AH1 virus reduced the virus growth. Therefore, the naturally selected wildtype H7N9 viruses, either with or without the NA deletion, replicate at higher efficiency than their counterparts. Dk/WZ47 (H7N7) virus, either with or without the NA deletion, did not replicate in A549 cells at 33℃, implying that this duck virus may not have good replication at the lower temperature that normally occurs in the upper respiratory tract of human being. Wildtype Dk/WZ47 without deletion replicated better than that with deletion at 37℃. Comparatively, after introduction of the deleted amino acids back to the CK/WZ610 virus, it showed slightly but not significantly better replication both at 33℃ and 37℃. Therefore, N7 NA gene without deletion seemed to have conferred better replication to the two H7N7 virus tested in the human alveolar basal epithelial cells. < Objective 3 > To investigate the role of H9N2-like internal genes in the genetic context of human H7N9, the internal genes of Dk/WZ47 (which are derived from the Eurasian avian influenza gene pool) were replaced with those from the AH1 and vice versa to observe whether the H9N2-origin internal genes (of AH1) are a prerequisite for viral replication and transmission in ferrets. A total of ten RG viruses were reconstructed and tested in A549 cells and ferrets. Briefly, replacement of the whole AH1 internal gene cassette or the RNP complex (i.e. the PB2, PB2, PA and NP genes) with those from the DK/WZ47 dramatically reduced the virus replication in A549 cells at both 33℃ and 37℃, while acquisition of the AH1 internal gene cassette or RNA complex significantly enhanced the virus growth of DK/WZ47 virus. Obviously, the H9N2-like internal gene cassette, especially the H9N2-like RNP gene complex, is essential for the virus replication of H7N9 virus. On the contrary, replacement of either M or NS gene from DK/WZ47 to AH1 significantly reduced the virus replication at 37℃, but there was no viral replication for viruses with the backbone from DK/WZ47 at 33℃. Replacement of the AH1 virus with the M or NS gene from the DK/WZ47 virus enhanced the virus replication in A549 cells at 33℃, but did not changed the virus growth at 37℃. It seemed that the M and NS genes from DK/WZ47 conferred better virus replication to both AH1 (H7N9) or DK/WZ47 (H7N7) viruses at certain temperatures. In ferrets, prototype AH1 can efficiently be transmitted to both the physical contacts and some of the airborne exposed ferrets, but replacement of its internal genes, or the RNP complex, with the genepool-like internal genes from DK/WZ47 drastically hampered this transmissibility. Further investigation showed that either 627K or 701N substitutions on the PB2 gene could improve the virus replication in mammalian cells and pathogenicity in mice. Dual substitutions could readily occur during transmission of the virus among ferrets via direct physical contact, and these mutations conferred higher polymerase activity and improved viral replication in mammalian cells, and enhanced virulence in mice (Zhu et al, Sci Rep 2015). < Objective 4 > To investigate if HA gene is responsible for the H7N9 infectivity and transmissibility in mammals, we have tested ten different H7 strains and found that wildtype SH5 and Dk/WZ47 were not able to airborne transmitted but most H7N9 could. Replacement of the AH1 HA gene with that from Dk/WZ47 indicated that HA play a key role in maintaining the virus replication in A549 cells and transmission among ferrets. To examine the phenotypic difference conferred by the H7 HA genes, we have identified a series of amino acid substitutions in the H7 HA genes that may be associated with virus adaption in chickens or humans. These include T173M, D183S, I188V, G195V, Q235L, K321R, T410N, N455D and A541V. Preliminary data indicated that RG virus with a single point mutation of D455N in the HA gene of AH1 had increased acid stability and reduced virus replication in A549 cells. Antigenic epitopes were also identified in the HA gene using a panel of monoclonal antibodies and ferret antisera. Further investigation is warranted to explore the differential function of each residue in HA gene.

rows: To investigate if the N9 NA gene confers better infectivity and/or transmissibility over the N7 and N3 in the genetic context of a human H7N9 virus. The H7N9 has caused hundreds of human cases while H7N7 and H7N3 viruses co-circulating in poultry are not known to cause human infections. Laboratory ferret experiments demonstrated that H7N7 was shed from the nasal route at lower titers and transmitted at delayed and less efficient patterns than the human H7N9 viruses. This may be partially attributed to the different NA subtypes.

To examine if the deletion in the NA stalk region of the human H7N9 and Ck/WZ-like H7N7 contributes to the ability of the virus to replicate and transmit across species. One of the most notable signatures observed in the NA genes of the related H7N7 and H7N9 is the amino acid deletions at the stalk region (Δ69-73 for N9 and Δ53-72 for N7). As NA stalk deletions have been repeatedly associated with the adaptation of avian influenza viruses in a new host, we seek to test if such changes will alter the NA activity and the virus replication and transmissibility.

To investigate if the internal gene constellation derived from the enzootic Asian H9N2 virus is a determinant for the better replication and transmission of the H7N9 and H7N7 strains in ferrets. The most significant change in the H7N9 and related H7N7 viruses from the duck gene pool viruses was the acquisition of the internal gene complex from the H9N2 viruses enzootic in China. We will test if incorporating this complex would contribute to viral replication and transmission and also if it leads to replication in the upper respiratory tract and transmission through the nasal route.

To investigate if the H7N9 HA lineage is responsible for the viral infectivity and transmissibility in mammals. We will test HA genes from different H7 virus strains and see how they contribute to the virus infection and transmissions. Potential substitutions related to the increased virus infectivity or transmissibility may be identified.

17127714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127714.value: We have identified the viral gene segments and some residues that may contribute to the emergence of H7N9 infections in humans and the enhanced mammalian infectivity, pathogenicity and interspecies transmissibility of the avian H7 viruses. Further investigation will be more focused on how these genes or residues would interact with the host factors and immune responses to lead to the overall pathogenesis.

17127714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127714.value: The avian-origin influenza A(H7N9) virus that emerged in 2013 poses a continuous threat to agriculture and public health. To understand the mechanisms how an avian H7 virus from the Eurasian gene pool may evolve to become human infectious, we choose duck and chicken viruses that were genetically closely related to the human H7N9 virus for the research. We replaced different gene segments of the prototype human H7N9 virus with the duck or chicken virus genes, and we found that internal gene cassettes, especially the RNA polymerase complex, significantly contributed to the virus replication and transmission abilities in the mammalian models. HA gene also serves as an important determinant for the H7N9 infection and transmission in mammals. Replacement of NA genes with other subtypes may not significantly hamper the virus virulence, implying that other NA subtypes can confer similar threat posed by H7N9 in mammals, especially when they acquire the other genes from the H7N9 viruses. Close monitoring of these viruses was warranted to provide early warnings of disease emergence. Information generated by this study provides insights into mechanisms that can lead to the interspecies transmissions of an avian influenza virus with a human infectivity and transmissibility.

17200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200114.value: The shape and roughness of soil particles can have a significant effect on soil behaviour. This project aims at defining new quantifiers for the morphology of soil particles and mapping the change in morphology during loading events. The research is based on laboratory soil particle testing and advanced particle image analysis. High resolution particle image analysis and optical microscopy with interferometry are combined with advanced fractal and Fourier analysis to define the new quantifiers to describe the morphology of soil particles. The changes in these quantifiers are tracked during loading and new mathematical expressions derived to describe these changes. A successful outcome is ensured by a unique collaboration gathering complementary expertise in experimental micro-mechanics, particle image analysis physics and numerical analysis. The outcome of this research will provide information to numerical modellers, paving the way for a new class of numerical models that integrate change in particle morphology during loading.

17200114.label: Realisation of objectives
17200114.value: 1. Define new tangible quantifiers for soil particle shape and roughness The particle shape was examined using the Qicpic apparatus where basic parameters, such as size, sphericity, aspect ratio, convexity, elongation could be obtained based on 2-D images. Particle shape was then described using the Fourier descriptors where the large scale morphology was successfully characterized. The finer scale surface features of soil particles, such as roughness or texture which is in between of particle shape and roughness were firstly investigated using the high resolution interferometer where a 3D surface morphology could be obtained. A new method was developed in which a 3D characterization was made with the aid of power spectral density of the (Yang and Baudet, 2016; Yang et al., 2016). Fractal analysis was carried out for the characterization. It was found that the sand roughness could be adequately characterized by the power spectral density and the fractal dimension. This method provides an alternative to the separation procedure (that comes with the interferometer) which gives rises to uncertainties but is frequently used in previous studies in the literature. The influence of the size of field of view on the surface roughness quantifiers of natural sand particles was investigated. It was found that the surface roughness by both power spectrum density method and the motif extraction method is scale dependent. The relationship between particle size and the surface roughness of Leighton Buzzard sand indicates that the finer the particles the rougher the surfaces. The few studies on measurements and quantification of surface texture are limited to sand sized particles, such as in the paper above. To date, the surface texture of sand has been successfully obtained by using a high-resolution optical microscope for a given measurement area that is small and comparable to the sand particle size. However, for larger particles, such as gravel, the larger surface area may create difficulties, where the surface texture could be influenced by other factors such as the mineral composition and scale-dependent fabric. Yang et al. (2019) attempted to address this challenge by proposing a method to measure and quantify the surface texture of gravel which explicitly takes into account the different texture scales. Using crushed granite, the surface texture was measured at different scales with a 3D laser scanner (at millimeter scale) and a high-resolution optical microscope equipped with interferometry (at micrometer scale). The novel method defined and quantifies the surface texture of gravel with the aid of the power spectral density function (PSD) and a fractal method. It was found that the fractal dimension at the two different scales do not coincide, which might be interpreted as two different self-affine patterns of the surface (Yao et al., 2018a, 2018b). 2. Map changes in these new quantifiers during loading events. Single particle compression tests were carried out to induce changes in the surface morphology. Special attention was paid to the experiments and the procedure used showed success to track the changes on consistent measuring area. The quantifiers defined in the above were found to map the changes successfully. It was found that the asperities of Leighton Buzzard sand (LBS) deformed plastically even at small loads. By comparing the surfaces of the particle before and after tests, the changes of surface roughness during loading could be investigated. All the surface roughness quantifiers showed similar decreasing trends with increasing normal loading. The experimental results reveal that the flattening of the asperities smoothens the surfaces at lower loading level, while the plastic deformation of the bulk could either smoothen or roughen the surfaces at higher loading level. The evolution of surface roughness of sand particles varies with each other, therefore the Weibull function was used to fit the cumulative distributions of the surface roughness of thirty particles at different normal loadings. The surface roughness is found to decrease with increasing normal loading after which it becomes constant (Yao et al., 2019). 3. Derive simple mathematical expressions to describe particle shape and roughness and their evolution during loading. Part of this objective (descriptions of particle shape and roughness) was achieved in the objective 1. The derivation of simple mathematical expressions to describe the evolution of these quantities depends in the essence on the contact situations about which a literature review has been performed and described in Yang et al. (2016). Deriving the expressions is still underway and will be facilitated with more coming experimental results. The experimental results of the single particle compression tests revealed that both the asperities and the bulk of sand particles could deform plastically under compression. Surface roughness of sand particles decreases firstly with increasing normal loading because of the flattening of the asperities. However, the effect of the plastic deformation of the bulk on the change of surface roughness varies among the tested particles that it could either smoothen or roughen the surfaces. In order to investigate the evolution of the surface roughness during loading, the Weibull function was adopted to represent the cumulative distributions of surface roughness of all the tested particles at different loadings. When the load was less than 20N, the surface roughness of the particles decreases dramatically with the increasing normal loading and then becomes constant.

17200114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200114.value: Yang and Baudet (2016): A new method was proposed which characterizes roughness with the aid of the power spectrum of the whole surface profile of sand particles. Results from natural sand (Leighton Buzzard sand) tested using an optical interferometer revealed that the sand roughness could be characterized by the power spectrum and the fractal dimension calculated from a cut-off length scale that was inferred from surface area estimation. Yang et al. (2016): A new method is proposed, which applies the power spectral density, used in tribology, to optical interferometry measurements of soil grain surfaces. The method was adapted to characterize the roughness of soil grains separately from their shape. The surface roughness can be characterized by a roughness value and a fractal dimension, determined based on geometrical properties of the surface (triangular-prism method) or its stochastic formation process (power spectral density). Yao et al. (2018a): RMSf of sand particles with different particle sizes increases with the size of field of view and then converges at larger sizes. Surfaces of medium sized (1.18-2.36 mm) particles are the smoothest. Surface roughness of one particle varies at different measurement points, with no correlation between the mean value of RMSf and the number of points. Yao et al. (2018b): The Weibull function was used to fit the cumulative distribution of RMSf and its suitability in modelling the distributions is presented. The correlation between particle size and two parameters (shape parameter and scale parameter) of the function were investigated. Yang et al. (2019): This paper proposes a method to measure and quantify the surface texture of gravel which explicitly takes into account the different texture scales. Most of the research on the previous papers is on sand. The novel method defines and quantifies the surface texture of gravel with the aid of the power spectral density function and a fractal method. Yao et al. (2019): The plastic deformation of sand particles under normal loading was studied with a custom-made particle compression apparatus and the optical interferometer. It was found that the plastic deformation of the asperities at low loadings could decrease the surface roughness, while the plastic deformation of the bulk at high loadings could either roughen or smooth the surfaces (under preparation). The methods devised above where extend to investigate particle coatings (Saulick et al, 2018, Liu et al., 2019) and particle morphology evolution in landslides (Lu et al., 2018, Li et al., 2019).

17200114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200114.value: During the course of the project, the methods developed to measure particle surface roughness and texture were used to address other research questions, namely (1) to quantify the particle morphology evolution in debris flows (Lu et al., 2018, Li et al., 2019) and (2) to quantify the investigate the characteristics of particles coatings by means of surface roughness (Saulick et al, 2018, Liu et al., 2019). There is ongoing research on both the particle morphology evolution and particle coatings that make use of the methods developed by this GRF project. Finally, and as an outcome of Yao’s papers, because of the plastic deformation of both asperities and the bulk during compression, the classical elastic Hertz theory may not be appropriate to model the contact behaviour of sand particles. A new elastic-plastic contact model could be proposed which could be used in the DEM simulation.

17200114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200114.value: We have developed new methods to quantify the particle shape and roughness of soil particles. We have investigated how these factors change when soil particles are loaded by, for example, an engineering structure. We have successfully applied these new methods to quantify how particle shape and roughness change on various settings, from landslides to new granular materials for construction purposes. This project has laid the foundations to address future research questions where the processes at soil particle scale are important.

17200214.value: 未知(超)圖上的無識匹配算法

17200214.label: Project Objectives

rows: To develop novel techniques for improving the performance ratio for the problem on unweighted graphs, and consider high-probability statements.
