17204014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204014.value: Numerous physical phenomena and engineering processes—such as those found in chemical reactors, compartmental networks, gene regulation, drug delivery or congestion control—have the characteristic that their inputs, internal states, and outputs are inherently non-negative. These systems, commonly referred to as positive systems, have been intensively studied in recent years as more of their salient features have been unraveled. While positive systems have many truly remarkable properties, they have also presented significant technical difficulties when synthesizing controllers and filters. Existing linear theories are handicapped by their inflexibility in handling systems that are defined on cones, rendering most design methods not directly applicable to positive systems. Conventional control design approaches for positive systems are often ad hoc or have significantly reduced performance. Indeed, one significant drawback of standard performance-based control designs is that they do not naturally apply to gain-based control specifically for positive systems. This difficulty stems from traditional design methods having been developed based on the quadratic Lyapunov function framework, which becomes unsuitable for inputs and outputs that are only integrable/summable and not square-integrable/square-summable. In this project, we will tackle performance-based control synthesis problems targeted to positive systems. Several classes of positive systems such as those with time-varying delays and nonlinear characteristics will be studied. By employing a linear Lyapunov framework, fundamental results on the stability and input-output characteristics of positive systems will be developed. To reduce the cost of realization, the design methodologies will focus on fixed-order synthesis which may be structured for implementation needs, such as admitting a decentralized form or inheriting the positivity behavior in reduced modeling or filter design. Analysis will be carried out on the system gains for various input-output signal spaces so as to provide the corresponding equivalent analytical characterizations on the system performances. Using the latest theoretical tools, computational algorithms in the form of linear or semi-definite programming will be constructed for solving the design problems. One of the key objectives of the project is also to generalize the gain-constrained synthesis to cone-preserving systems. The proposed work will not only reduce the undesirable conservatism in current system analysis and compensator synthesis, but also considerably narrow the gaps between theories and applications, and offer higher performance in control system implementations.

17204014.label: Realisation of objectives
17204014.value: All the objectives have been achieved. The details are listed below. Work has been carried out to develop stability and synthesis results for systems with positivity structures. These include systems with positive state components (positive systems and Boolean control networks) and complex networks with positive edge dynamics. The focus has been to establish stability conditions for synthesis such as controller design, model reduction, and multi-agent consensus. Control and gain performances based on the L1-norm, L-inf-norm, l1-norm, H-inf norm and guarantee cost have been examined. Moreover, computational algorithms based on linear or semi-definite programming have been constructed for numerical verification of stability, performance, as well as various synthesis specifications. For positive linear systems, the static output-feedback stabilization with optimal L1-gain has been studied. A static output-feedback controller such that the closed-loop system is positive, asymptotically stable and the L1-gain from the exogenous input to the regulated output is minimized. The results can be extended to solve the L1-optimal controller synthesis problem. For continuous-time positive linear systems of fractional order with delays, the stability and L-inf-gain analysis problem for continuous-time positive fractional-order delay systems with non-commensurate orders between zero and one has been investigated. A necessary and sufficient condition has been given to characterize the positivity of continuous-time fractional-order systems with bounded time-varying delays. It has been established that the asymptotic stability of positive fractional-order systems is not sensitive to the magnitude of delays. Moreover, it has been shown that the L-inf-gain of a positive fractional-order system is independent of the magnitude of delays. Important generalization of results on positive linear systems has been studied for systems with cone-invariant property. The decay rate constrained stability analysis for cone-invariant linear delay systems has been carried out. Under mild assumptions on the growth rate of a non-decreasing positive function, an explicit condition is given to ensure that a cone-preserving linear system with unbounded time-varying delays is asymptotically stable with a given decay rate. As typical cases, necessary and sufficient conditions are given to characterize the decay rate when the delay is restricted by a linear, sublinear or logarithmic growth rate. During the course of the project, the input-output gain analysis for dynamic systems defined on cones has been analysed. For such monotone systems, their input–output gain induced by the so-called cone linear absolute norm has been characterized. It is further shown that for a linear time-invariant system represented by a convolution operator that maps one proper cone to another in the L1 space, its operator norm is governed by the static gain of the system. As a byproduct, the spectral radius of a cone-preserving convolution operator turns out to be the same as that of the static gain matrix. Moreover, dual results based on the cone max norm are obtained. As the L2 -gain of positive systems is fully determined by the static gain matrix, and hence the linear matrix inequality characterizing their H-inf performance admits a diagonal Lyapunov matrix variable. This property has been shown to be true for systems with input, state and output defined on general cones. Although it is known that the L2-gain is no longer governed by the static gain matrix for systems defined on general proper cones, this property is still valid when the cone in the state space is symmetric, and the cones in the input and output spaces are self-dual. Another line of development towards nonlinear positive systems has been devoted towards positive systems with T-S fuzzy description. The design problem of ℓ1-induced controller has been carried out with the use of linear co-positive Lyapunov function. A novel performance characterization is first established to guarantee the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system with ℓ1-induced performance. Iterative convex optimization approaches are used to solve the design conditions. The α-exponential stability analysis and ℓ1 controller synthesis of positive Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy discrete-time systems with time-varying delays have been tackled. A sufficient condition of α-exponential stability for autonomous positive fuzzy systems is first established by constructing a new Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional which is followed by a control scheme subject to an ℓ1-gain constraint. Boolean control networks (BCNs) form a special type of positive systems. For general BCNs, the weighted ℓ1-gain analysis and ℓ1 model reduction problem have been proposed and investigated via semi-tensor product method. The input energy and output energy are described by pseudo-Boolean functions, based on which the definition of the weighted ℓ1-gain is introduced. A sufficient condition is established to ensure that a Boolean control network is not only internally asymptotically stable, but also has an ℓ1-gain performance. By virtue of the properties of semi-tensor product, the ℓ1 model reduction problem of a Boolean control network is defined and converted to the ℓ1-gain problem of another Boolean control network with more nodes. Concerning the reachability and controllability criteria of BCNs, several improved criteria based on the Warshall algorithm have been obtained. The proposed method has lower computational complexity compared with existing methods, and thus facilitates the reachability and controllability analysis for BCNs. For BCNs under different time-triggering scenarios, the project has investigated their stability and guaranteed cost performance. The time triggering is generated by mode-dependent average dwell-time switching signals. A sufficient condition is derived to ensure that the considered network is globally stable under a designed average dwell-time switching signal. For BCNs with stochastic delays randomly attaining finite values (modeled by Markov chains), some stochastic stability results are obtained based on stability results of positive systems. Subsequently, the stabilization of Boolean networks with stochastic delays is investigated, and an equivalent condition for the existence of feedback controllers is provided. Finally, further extension of the application of positive systems theory developed has been considered for the positive edge-consensus problem via output feedback protocols for undirected networks and directed networks whose edge dynamics are defined on nonnegative spaces. Two observer-type positive edge-consensus protocols have been introduced, and sufficient conditions of positive consensus for uncertain positive systems are proposed without utilizing the information of algebraic connectivity. Furthermore, necessary and/or sufficient conditions of positive consensus for the nominal systems have also been derived.

17204014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204014.value: For the stability and stabilization of positive linear systems using output feedback, a controller design method to ensure L1-optimality for the closed-loop system has been obtained [1]. The stability of positive fractional-order systems with time-varying delays has been characterized with a necessary and sufficient condition. The insensitivity of the time delays applies to both the asymptotic stability and the L-inf-gain [3]. For linear systems defined on cones, input-output gain induced by cone linear absolute norm has been characterized in terms of generalized inequalities. It is further shown that for a linear time-invariant system represented by a convolution operator that maps one proper cone to another in the L1 space, its operator norm is governed by the static gain of the system [6]. Some extensions on the Bounded Real Lemma for positive systems have been obtained. The property that the L2-gain characterized by the static gain matrix being related to the H-inf performance with a diagonal Lyapunov matrix variable has been shown to be valid when the cone in the state space is symmetric, and the cones in the input and output spaces are self-dual [7]. For discrete-time linear cone-invariant delay systems, the decay rate constrained stability condition has been explicitly derived [8]. The controller synthesis of positive Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy systems under the l1 performance has been solved with fuzzy controllers which can be obtained through iterative convex optimization approaches [4]. When the system has time-varying delays, the discrete-time alpha-exponential stability condition has been established and controller with l1-gain has been designed [5]. The idea of positivity has been used to solve the edge-consensus problem via output feedback for undirected or directed networks with nonnegative edges. Two observer-type positive edge-consensus protocols have been for positive consensus of uncertain positive systems without utilizing the information of algebraic connectivity [12]. The l1-gain of Boolean control networks has been established for the first time based on the concept of weighted l1-gain. The result has been employed to establish the first model reduction method for such networks based on input-output performance [2]. Improved reachability and controllability criteria have been obtained by resorting to the semi-tensor product technique and the Warshall algorithm [9]. Time-triggered Boolean networks have been studied with their stability and guaranteed cost performance characterized [10]. Furthermore, the stability and stabilization of Boolean networks with stochastic delays have been studied using positive systems theory [11].

17204014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204014.value: Amongst the many potential applications and extensions of the results developed in the project, there are two areas where the results can be further developed: (a) Due to the recent interest in periodic piecewise linear systems, polynomial-type Lyapunov functions can be used to establish stability conditions for periodic piecewise positive linear systems. By increasing the number of partitions when constructing the Lyapunov function, improved exponential stability conditions can be obtained which may be able to approach the exact condition in the limit. (b) For time-delay cone-preserving systems, an interesting theoretical problem is to study the existence of positive definite solutions for the algebraic Riccati inequality. It is also of interest to see if the idea can be used to generalize the characterization of structured singular values for positive uncertain systems to more general cone-preserving systems. (c) The problem of consensus for multi-agent systems with positive agents can be further studied as current research results have mainly been focused on single-input systems. Multi-input positive multi-agent systems need to be solved without sign-definite gain requirements. The non-fragile and robust cases can also be investigated.

These so-called positive systems have been intensively studied in recent years due to their salient features such as monotonicity of the system state and the insensitivity of time delays. While positive systems have many truly remarkable properties, they have also presented significant technical difficulties during control synthesis. In this project, we have tackled L1 and L-inf-gain control synthesis problems targeted to positive systems. Several classes of positive systems such as those with time-varying delays and Takagi-Sugeno description have been studied. Important properties of positive systems have been generalized to cone-invariant systems. The consensus problem of multi-agent systems with positive edge dynamics has been solved. The asymptotic and exponential stability of these systems have been characterized. The stability, controllability, and model reduction problems of Boolean control networks have also been investigated. All the stability characterizations and synthesis algorithms have been constructed in numerical tractable form for computation. The results have laid down the foundation for researchers and academics working in the positive systems area.

17204114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204114.value: Many environmental and industrial flow processes involves transport of fine particles heavier than the carrier fluid. Common examples include dust storms, aerosol sprays, biomedical droplets generated by sneezing, sediments in rivers, volcano eruptions, particle-laden jets and plumes. It is important to predict the settling paths and velocities of these fine heavy particles in fluid flows for environmental assessment or engineering design. In most cases, the fluid flows are turbulent or contain coherent flow perturbations in the form of periodic oscillations in flow speeds (e.g., tidal estuaries), organized eddies (in heat exchangers) or large-scale vortices (in jet flows or flows behind obstacles). There have been many past studies on the effect of turbulence on particle settling velocities but most of them were limited to near-isotropic turbulence with zero mean flow and measurements of particle settling alone without concurrent measurements of the fluid flow fields around the settling particles. A number of theories have been postulated for the mechanisms of turbulence actions to modify the particle settling velocity from the still-water value but there were few physical experiments to evidently observe and verify these theories. The few experiments were mostly limited to large settling particles of the millimeter or larger scales. The proposed project aims to fill the research gaps by applying an advanced two-camera particle-image velocimetry (PIV) technique to make simultaneous measurements of the velocity fields of the particle phase and fluid phase in a time-resolved manner. The flow will be illuminated by a laser sheet whereby images of scattered light from the particles recorded by a high-speed camera will be analyzed to obtain the instantaneous particle velocities. At the same time, micrometer-sized fluorescent seeding particles will be used to show the fluid motions and compute the water velocities from the images of the fluorescence signals captured by another high-speed camera. This two-phase measurement will reveal the dynamic interaction between the settling particles and the fluid flow around the particles. The focus of study is on fine particles of sub-millimeter sizes (which are more relevant to many environmental and engineering processes) and on particles settling in a turbulent flow steam (with non-zero mean flow). In addition to obtain engineering information of the settling velocities of sub-millimeter sized particles in different turbulent flow streams, the project will explore the roles of isotropic turbulence and organized flow perturbations in the flow stream in affecting the settling paths and velocities of the particles. 許多環境和工業的流動過程涉及細小的重粒子在流體中傳輸；常見的例子有沙塵暴，噴霧劑，打噴嚏産生的生理飛沫，河流沉積物，火山噴發，攜帶粒子的射流和羽流等。預測這些細小的重粒子在流體中的運行軌跡和速度在環境評估和工程設計中具有重要作用。在大多數情況下，粒子所在的流場是湍流或包含流體協同作用的擾動，如流速的周期震蕩（河口潮汐），有組織的漩渦（在熱交換器中），或大尺度的渦流（在射流或障礙物後流場）。關於湍流對粒子的沉降速度的影響已有很多研究，但是大多局限於各向同性且平均流速為零的湍流和僅對粒子沉降本身的測量，併沒有對粒子周圍的流體流速進行同步測量。許多理論都假定一些湍流機製來對粒子在靜水中的沉降速度進行修正，但是有很少實驗來提供確切的實驗觀測和驗證這些理論。已有的少許實驗大多局限於毫米或更大尺度的粒子。 本建議項目旨在通過應用先進的雙攝像機激光粒子成像測速（PIV）技術，對粒子和流體兩相的流場進行同步的實時測量，以填補研究空白。激光片光源將被用來照亮流場；一個高速像機將記録下粒子散射的激光，併通過圖像分析得到粒子的瞬時速度。與此同時，微米級的熒光粒子將被用來顯示液相流體的流動，另一個高速攝像機將捕捉到熒光信號以計算水流速度。此兩項的測量數據將揭示沉降粒子和周圍流場的動態相互所用。本研究的重點放在亞毫米大小的粒子（更多見於許多環境和工程過程中）和非零平均流速的湍流流動中的粒子沉降。除了獲得亞毫米級粒子在不同湍流條件下的沉降速度的工程信息，該項目將探尋各向同性湍流和有組織流場擾動對粒子在沉降過程中軌跡和速度的作用。

17204114.label: Realisation of objectives
17204114.value: The project aims at an experimental investigation of the settling behavior of sub-millimeter sized solid particles in a turbulent water flow. The turbulent flow cases studied cover near-isotopic grid-generated turbulence, and flow streams with random turbulence or organized flow perturbations. Most of the project objectives have been accomplished through extensive laboratory experiments carried out in the Croucher Laboratory of Environmental Hydraulics at HKU. The main experimental tool of the investigation is the two-camera particle-image velocimetry (PIV) technique which enables simultaneous time-resolved velocity measurements of the particle phase and fluid phase in the flow problem. Year 1 of the project was mainly devoted to the setting up of this PIV system whose success lies in an effective optical separation of the two phases and synchronization of flow images captured by the two high-speed cameras. Experiments were made on an otherwise stagnant water body with grid-generated turbulence to which a small amount of solid particles of mean diameter about 0.2 mm and relative density 2.5 were dropped from an hourglass. Movement of the solid particles was estimated from their scattered light images using the particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) technique in which the particle velocities were found by tracking the particle locations between two successive images in the Lagrangian frame. In the same time, the turbulent fluid motion was obtained by PIV with fluorescent seeding particles added to the water. The use of two light signals, namely scattered laser light and fluorescent light, was expected to achieve effective optical separation of the two phases in the flow by applying optical filters of different wavelengths to the two cameras. Within the time over which the heavy particles fall through the imaging area, particle streak lines were obtained at different locations at different times, together with the instantaneous turbulent water velocity fields. In this complex laboratory and equipment setup, we encountered a number of experimental difficulties such as the heavy particles falling out the PIV/PTV measuring plane and the weak signal of micron-sized fluorescent flow feeding particles. The initial progress was slower than planned due to these experimental difficulties and the departure of an experienced RA in Year 0.5. Later experiments were mainly carried out by an M.Phil. student who required substantial training. At the end of Year 1, we succeeded to find partial solutions for the experimental problems but the experiments were then suspended for another 3 months due to the repair of one PIV camera. Despites the slow pace of project commencement, we were able to present some preliminary results in a conference [C1, see Part C]. In addition, during the planning phase of the project, we applied our idea of two-phase PIV measurement technique to the related problem of settling of solid particles carried in jet turbulence. This helped preparation of the final version of a journal article [J3] in which the PIV measurement data were used to validate numerical flow simulations and to study the relationship between particle clustering and intensities of turbulence. In Year 2, we conducted detailed experiments in the water tank in which ambient turbulence was produced by a pair of turbulence grids oscillating in the sideway directions. The amplitude of oscillation was set to a constant value but the frequency was varied to different values so as to provide different levels and scales of turbulence. We made an improvement in the measurement technique by using fluorescent glass spheres as the settling solid particles and seeding the water flow with neutrally buoyant fine polyamide particles. This helped to boost the light signals of the small number of heavy particles in a falling experiment where a portion of particles tend to move out of the laser sheet illumination plane while falling in turbulence. An in-house process was devised to fabricate these fluorescent heavy particles from spherical glass particles by adding fluorescent dye in a resin base, following by grinding and sieving the dried base. The in-house particles were found to work satisfactorily and we used them in the oscillating grid experiments to study the effect of turbulence characteristic of particle settling in near homogeneous turbulence [J2]. The experimental data suggested some apparent clear effects of grid turbulence on the particle settling behavior but large variations in the values of particle settling velocity were observed. For the second objective of particle settling in a turbulent flow stream, experiments were carried during Years 2-3 in a 0.4-m wide laboratory flume in which turbulence was produced in the channel flow using a of turbulence grid and floor roughness elements. The in-house made heavy fluorescent particles were dropped at different downstream locations from the grid and using a grid from different sizes. In this way, particles falling in flow streams of different turbulence characteristics could be studied with our two-camera PIV technique. Similar to the experiments in the water tank, we encountered the problem of heavy particles moving out the vertical laser sheet illumination plane upon falling through the water depth. In Year 3, two more sensitive high-speed cameras were used to solve this problem. The purchase of one camera used the project funding. We observed that the settling velocities are affected by a number of turbulence parameters in the open-channel flow. The large and small turbulent length scales were found to affect particle settling via different mechanisms [J1]. For the third objective regarding organized eddies in a flow stream, a vibrating shutter unit was designed and built in the laboratory flume in Year 2. The unit had the same width of 0.4 m as the flume and had a height 0.5 m. There were 11 blades of width 45 mm each and they could be set to vibrate at an adjustable frequency up to 2 Hz and an adjustable amplitude up to 50 mm peak-to-peak. Starting from Year 2.5, experiments of heavy particles falling in an open channel flow with organized eddies generated by the vibrating shutters were carried out. The settling velocity of the particles were found to change with the vibration frequency and amplitude of the shutters [C2, C3]. Through the project, it is found that ambient turbulence generally has weak effects on the settling of sub-millimeter sized heavy particles. This may be due to the small particle response time so that very high level of turbulence with a small Kolmogorov time scale is needed to match the particle response time. It appears that other mechanisms such as large vertical structures in turbulence can affect the particle settling behavior in addition to the Stokes number which is the ratio between particle response time and Kolmogorov time scale. The experiments were difficult to control both in terms of particle falling and turbulence generation. Large variations in particle settling velocities and turbulence characteristics existed among different test runs but statistically stable results could still be found.

17204114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204114.value: The project provides valuable experimental observations on the settling behavior of sub-millimeter sized heavy particles falling in turbulent waters, including grid-generated turbulence and flow stream with random turbulence or organized flow perturbations. In the near-zero mean flow turbulence generated by a pair of oscillating grids, the heavy particles are found to fall with slightly reduced settling velocities in most cases. When the turbulence level increases, the variations of settling velocity exhibit increased variations among test runs. Presence of falling particles is found to introduce additional turbulence in surrounding water when the ambient turbulence is weak. At one particular grid oscillation frequency, the heavy particles evidently fall with a settling velocity faster than the still-water value. This case of grid-generated turbulence exhibits a number of particular characteristics distinct from other cases, such as peak horizontal turbulent velocities and lower TKE dissipation rate. Large-scale vortex arrays seem to appear at some instants during which the particles tend to fall with accelerated speeds along pathways between vortices, suggesting the fast tracking mechanism. Findings are reported in conferences [C1, C4] and journal article [J2]. Turbulence grids are installed in a laboratory flume to generate near-homogeneous turbulence in an open channel flow. The PIV/PTV data suggest that the large and small turbulent length scales in the open channel flow affect particle settling via different mechanisms. Scaling laws are suggested for the settling velocity changes using turbulent velocity and vorticity in the flow. Results and findings are published in journal article [J1]. A vibrating shutter device is built to produce organized eddies in an open channel flow. Experiments suggest that the average particle settling velocity is reduced with presence of organized eddies. While the vertical turbulent velocities in the flow stream increases with the shutter vibration frequency, it appears that turbulence structures, such as circulations induced by large-scale vortices, govern the settling behavior of the heavy particles as they fall through the turbulent water column. Preliminary results are reported in conferences [C2, C3] and a journal article will be prepared to report the detailed results. The in-house fabrication process of fluorescent solid heavy particles provides an economical and effective approach to two-phase flow studies, particularly in large scale flow experiments [J2]. During the planning phase of the project, the proposed two-phase PIV technique was applied to the problem of particle settling in jet turbulence. This helped preparation of the final version of journal article [J3].

17204114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204114.value: The project reveals that the interaction between flow turbulence and sub-millimeter sized heavy particles is more complicated than expected. In grid turbulence, a large increase in settling velocity is reported in many investigations for Stokes number near unity. The fast particle response time of the present small-sized solid particles leads to a much lower Stokes number unless in very high level of turbulence. Nevertheless, evident increase in particle falling velocity is observed in one case of gird turbulence where particular turbulence characteristics are found. This suggests that in addition to fine-scale turbulence, large-scale eddies in the flow turbulence also affect particle settling via separate mechanisms. In an open channel flow with weak grid turbulence, results also suggest different actions on particle settling from turbulent eddies of different scales. The detail interaction mechanisms between heavy particles and different length scales of turbulence are yet to be explored in future studies, preferably using heavy particles of a range of sizes and densities. The project team will continue to carry out more experiments to fully understand the particle-turbulence interaction problem. Attempts will also be made to investigate the problem with large-eddy simulations.

17204114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204114.value: Particle laden flows are found in many natural and engineering processes. Suspended particles, sedimentation and turbidity are the dominating pollutant factors in water bodies. This project studies the settling behavior of sub-millimeter sized heavy particles in water with various levels and characteristics of turbulence. The problem is typical of sand grains carried in water flows but the exact effect of flow turbulence on particle settling remains unknown. Numerous laboratory experiments are performed for solid particles falling in turbulent waters, including grid-generated turbulence and open channel flow with random turbulence or organized flow perturbations. An advanced two-camera particle image velocimetry (PIV) technique measures simultaneously the instantaneous velocities of the falling solid particles and the turbulent fluid motions around them. Phase separation of the two camera images is achieved by fluorescence tagging to the solid heavy particles. The experimental results show that the small-sized solid particles of diameter around 0.2 mm generally experience a slight reduction in their average settling velocity in an otherwise-stagnant water with ambient turbulence. In a flow stream with turbulence, evident increase in particle settling velocity is observed and this appears to be associated with the presence of large-scale flow eddies and their interaction with the falling particles.

17204614.label: Project Objectives
17204614.value: Devise a unified theory of robust link pricing (RLP) principles: Link price is a general measure of congestion at a link for enabling distributed congestion control. In Internet congestion control, AQM corresponds to a realization of link pricing mechanisms. We will devise a set of RLP principles that ensures prompt response against network congestion. At the same time, the RLP principles should help decouple the performance of AQM and the parameter configurations, and minimize the manual configurations needed. The RLP principles will have general applicability in guiding the design of AQM and other distributed congestion control mechanisms. Propose a new family of RLP-based AQM: By employing the findings and theoretical results derived from RLP, we will design a new family of AQM, called AQM-RLP, which implements the RLP principles. The properties of RLP principles are expected to be inherited by AQM-RLP. This greatly simplifies the parameter-tuning process in AQM, and provides the incentive for the wide deployment of AQM, which we believe is the key to solving the bufferbloat problem. We will demonstrate the performance of the novel AQM-RLP schemes (throughput, fairness, stability, responsiveness, and queue length dynamics) by computer simulations.

17204614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204614.value: The Internet is playing an increasingly important role in enabling real-time communication for people in geographically distributed locations. Presently, Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is the most popular transport layer protocol for point-to-point, connection-oriented, in-order, reliable data transfer in the Internet. It transports over 90% of data traffic in the Internet. To support the mix of diverse Internet applications, it is highly desirable to keep the Internet operating at the optimal operational region of high throughput and low delay. Unfortunately, the current congestion control mechanisms in the Internet are inadequate because 1) without buffer management at the router, TCP tends to fill the large router buffers with traffic, leading to high delivery delay, known as “bufferbloat”, and 2) while active queue management (AQM) has been proposed for managing a router buffer, its parameter configuration is very sophisticated, and the performance of AQM deteriorates severely when parameters are not properly tuned. Consequently, AQM is often disabled in daily operations of the Internet. In this project, we propose to devise a unified theory of robust link pricing (RLP) principles. Link price is a general measure of congestion at a link for enabling distributed congestion control. In Internet congestion control, AQM corresponds to a realization of link pricing mechanisms. We will devise a set of general link pricing principles to decouple the performance of AQM and parameter configurations, and to minimize the needs of manual configurations. The link pricing principles will have general applicability in guiding the design of AQM and other distributed congestion control mechanisms. By employing the findings and theoretical results derived from RLP, we will design a new family of AQM, known as AQM-RLP, which implements the RLP principles. This greatly simplifies the parameter-tuning process in AQM, providing the incentive for the wide deployment of AQM, which we believe is the key to solving the bufferbloat problem. To evaluate the performance of AQM-RLP, we will implement and evaluate a prototype communication system utilizing the proposed AQM-RLP in a network testbed. We expect this project to impact the design and development of the next-generation congestion control mechanisms, particularly in providing integral solutions to bufferbloat in the heterogeneous network environment. The basic science developed in this project will be important contributions to the research community, while the knowledge and experience gained in the testbed deployment will be invaluable to industry. 近年來，互聯網上的數據流量爆炸性地增長。互聯網在使分隔各地的人們能夠實時交流扮演著日漸重要的角色。目前，傳輸控制協議（Transmission Control Protocol，簡稱 TCP）是最流行的提供點到點，面向連接的，有序的，可靠的互聯網數據傳輸的傳輸層協議。它負責傳輸超過 90% 的互聯網數據流量。為了支持各種各樣的互聯網應用程序，我們必需使互聯網保持在高吞吐量和低延遲的最佳區域中運行。不幸的是，現有的互聯網擁塞控制機制存在不足之處，原因如下：（1）沒有路由器的緩衝管理，TCP 趨向於用數據流量填滿巨大的路由器緩衝區，從而導致高傳送延遲，這被稱為過度緩衝（bufferbloat）；（2）雖然主動隊列管理（AQM）算法已經被提出來管理路由器的緩衝區，它的參數配置是非常複雜的，而且當參數調整不正確時，AQM 的性能會嚴重惡化。因此，AQM 在互聯網的日常運行中往往被棄用。 在這個項目中，我們提出建立一個由穩健鏈接定價（Robust Link Pricing，簡稱 RLP）原則組成的統一理論。鏈接價格是為實現分佈式擁塞控制而採用的對鏈接擁塞程度的基本衡量。在互聯網的擁塞控制中，AQM 相當於鏈接定價機制的一個實現。我們會建立一套通用的鏈接定價原則來使得 AQM 的性能不受參數配置的影響，並最大限度地減少手動配置的需求。鏈接定價原則將普遍適用於指導 AQM 和其他分佈式擁塞控制機制的設計。通過採用從 RLP 得出的發現和理論結果，我們將設計一系列新的應用了 RLP 原則的 AQM 算法，稱之為 AQM-RLP。這大大簡化了 AQM 的參數調整過程，並為 AQM 的廣泛使用提供了動力，我們認為這是解決過度緩衝問題的關鍵。為了評估 AQM-RLP 的性能，我們將在網絡測試平台上實現和評價一個應用了所提出的 AQM-RLP 算法的原型通信系統。 我們希望這個項目對下一代的擁塞控制機制的設計和開發產生影響，特別是能夠提供對異構網絡環境中的過度緩衝問題的整體解決方案。在本項目裡開發出的基礎科學將對學術界產生重要貢獻，而在測試平台的建設中獲得的知識和經驗對於工業界也是非常寶貴的。

17204614.label: Realisation of objectives
17204614.value: The Internet is playing an increasingly important role in enabling real-time communication for people in geographically distributed locations. Presently, Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is the most popular transport layer protocol for point-to-point, connection-oriented, in-order, reliable data transfer in the Internet. It transports over 90% of data traffic in the Internet. To support the mix of diverse Internet applications, it is highly desirable to keep the Internet operating at the optimal operational region of high throughput and low delay. Unfortunately, the current congestion control mechanisms in the Internet are inadequate because 1) without buffer management at the router, TCP tends to fill the large router buffers with traffic, leading to high delivery delay, known as "bufferbloat", and 2) while active queue management (AQM) has been proposed for managing a router buffer, its parameter configuration is very sophisticated, and the performance of AQM deteriorates severely when parameters are not properly tuned. Consequently, AQM is often disabled in daily operations of the Internet. To overcome this problem, under Objective 1 of our project, we have developed a unified theoretical framework based on the concept of link price, which is a general measure of congestion at a link for enabling distributed congestion control. AQM corresponds to a realization of a link pricing mechanism. Recently, Controlled Delay (CoDel) has been proposed as an AQM algorithm to address this problem by setting a limit (i.e., a target delay) on the queueing delay. However, such a target delay is fixed, and CoDel is thus unable to adapt to changes in the network environment. Building on this theoretical framework, under Objective 2 of our project, in our papers published in IEEE Systems Journal [1] and IEEE ICCS 2016 [2], we proposed a framework to adaptively control the target delay with changing network conditions, so as to overcome bufferbloat. Specifically, we first proposed a framework to adaptively and stably control queueing delay based on network conditions, so as to combat bufferbloat. We employed controlled delay (CoDel), a recently proposed AQM, in our framework. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that has developed an analytical model for the CoDel system and derived necessary and sufficient conditions for its stability. Based on the stability analysis, we proposed adaptive CoDel with interval tuning (ACoDel-IT) and adaptive CoDel with target and interval tuning (ACoDel-TIT) algorithms, to improve the system stability and performance by automatic parameter tuning. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that ACoDel-IT and ACoDel-TIT effectively stabilize queueing delay, whereas ACoDel-TIT further improves link utilization and reduces packet drops, compared to other representative AQM algorithms. Adaptive CoDel is designed based on network models with a single bottleneck link, rendering their performance and stability unclear in multi-bottleneck networks. In our INFOCOM 2018 paper [3], we proposed a general theoretical framework to combat bufferbloat in multi-bottleneck networks. We first conducted an equilibrium analysis for a general multi-bottleneck TCP/AQM system and developed an algorithm to compute the equilibrium point. We then decomposed the system into single-bottleneck subsystems and derived sufficient conditions for the local asymptotic stability of the subsystems. Using the proposed framework, we presented a case study to analyze the stability of CoDel in multi-bottleneck networks and devised Self-tuning CoDel to improve the system stability and performance. Extensive simulation results show that Self-tuning CoDel effectively stabilizes queueing delay in multi-bottleneck scenarios, and thus contributes to combating bufferbloat. References: [1] Jiancheng Ye and Ka-Cheong Leung, "Adaptive and Stable Delay Control for Combating Bufferbloat: Theory and Algorithms," IEEE Systems Journal, Vol. 14, No. 1, pp. 1285-1296, March 2020. [2] Jiancheng Ye, Ka-Cheong Leung, and Victor O. K. Li, "Optimal Delay Control for Combating Bufferbloat in the Internet,'' Proceedings of the 15th IEEE International Conference on Communication Systems (IEEE ICCS 2016), Shenzhen, China, 14-16 December 2016. [3] Jiancheng Ye, Ka-Cheong Leung, Victor O. K. Li, and Steven H. Low, "Combating Bufferbloat in Multi-Bottleneck Networks: Equilibrium, Stability, and Algorithms,'' Proceedings of the 37th IEEE International Conference on Computer Communications (IEEE INFOCOM 2018), Honolulu, HI, U.S.A., 15-19 April 2018.

17204614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204614.value: In this project, we have developed a theoretical framework and proposed algorithms for combating bufferbloat in general multi-bottleneck networks. We have analyzed the equilibrium of a general multi-bottleneck TCP/AQM system and provided the sufficient conditions for the uniqueness of an equilibrium point in the system. We have then conducted stability study for the system by decomposing it into single-bottleneck subsystems and deriving the sufficient. conditions for the local asymptotic stability of the subsystems. Based on the equilibrium and stability studies, we have proposed an algorithm for computing the equilibrium point. We have further presented a case study to analyze the stability of multi-bottleneck TCP/CoDel system and proposed Self-tuning CoDel to improve the system stability. For future research, one can utilize the framework to analyze the stability of Cisco’s Proportional Integral controller Enhanced (PIE) algorithm in multi-bottleneck networks. This involves a study on the packet dropping probability function of PIE. Moreover, one can study the interactions among different AQM algorithms employed by different bottleneck links.

The need for transferring huge amount of data and the limited capacity of the Internet calls for the most efficient usage of network capacity. At the same time, the Internet is playing an increasingly important role in enabling real-time communication for people in geographically distributed locations, via network applications like IP telephony and video conferencing. This imposes stringent constraints on delivery delay. Presently, Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is the most popular network control mechanism for data transfer in the Internet. It transports over 90% of data traffic in the Internet. To support the mix of diverse Internet applications, it is necessary to keep the Internet operating at high capacity and low delay. This project has developed the theoretical framework and the network control mechanisms based on such framework to ensure the timely delivery of messages in the Internet to support diverse applications.

17204914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204914.value: Phosphorus (P) is one of valuable natural resources that have the largest risk of scarcity. Recovery of P from various sources that are originally regarded as wastes such as domestic wastewater becomes essential to future food security. Phosphorus removal in wastewater treatment also is needed for water pollution control purposes. Conventionally, P removal from wastewater is achieved through excessive sludge discharge, which not only results in a large amount of waste sludge but also affects the biological treatment process. Extraction of P from the waste sludge is both difficult and costly. It is therefore desirable and more cost-effective to recover P from wastewwter during the treatment phase without excessive sludge discharge. In the proposed project, a new biological process with ferric iron (Fe) dosing will be developed for simultaneous wastewater treatment and P recovery. The novel process features a combination of an aerobic phase and an acidogenic anaerobic phase. Dosing of ferric iron in the aerobic bioreactor leads to P precipitation or adsorption and hence ensures the P removal from wastewater. The P-rich sludge will be circulated through an anaerobic bioreactor for P extraction from the solid phase. Under an acidogenic condition in the anaerobic reactor, ferric iron is to be reduced to the more soluble ferrous iron, which releases phosphates into the supernatant for P recovery. Since the biomass sludge is then returned to the aerobic reactor, P is recovered without the need of sludge discharge from the treatment system. In the proposed study, a membrane bioreactor (MBR) will be used as the aerobic reactor to meet stringent effluent discharge or reuse standards. The MBR together with iron dosing makes use of the Fe–P chemistry and membrane filtration for P retention. The fundamentals about Fe and P interactions and Fe-facilitated P transformation under aerobic and anaerobic (acidogenic) conditions will be investigated. Batch tests and advanced analytical techniques (e.g. ICP-AES, XRD and EXAFS) will be utilized for the fundamental study. For the MBR-based system, the treatment capacity, effluent quality, P recovery efficiency, chemical and organic dosages, and the membrane fouling rate will be determined. The biological systems and the chemical dosing scheme will be optimized for wastewater treatment and cost-effective P recovery. The experiments will be conducted on the treatment of domestic sewage to demonstrate the feasibility, cost-effectiveness, operational convenience and long-term stability of the novel process. 大量的含磷廢水排入地表水體，引起嚴重的水體富營養化。同時，磷是一重要的化肥元素，是一種不可再生且極度匱乏的重要資源。在廢水處理中實現磷回收，不僅可控制水體富營養化，還對未來食品安全具有重要意義。然而，通過排放富磷的污泥而達成的傳統除磷工藝不僅產生大量剩餘污泥，還會影響廢水生物處理的效率。從污泥廢渣中回收磷的難度極大並且成本很高。因此，在廢水處理階段回收磷的工藝不僅極具效益還能減少剩餘污泥的產生。在本項目中，一種新型的通過鐵強化混凝的生物處理工藝將被開發，以實現廢水處理與磷回收的同步運行。該工藝結合了好氧和厭氧酸化生物處理技術。首先在好氧反應器中投加三價鐵形成非溶解性磷酸鹽沉澱物，從而將磷從廢水中去除。然後，將富磷污泥排至厭氧酸化反應器，在厭氧酸化條件下，三價鐵會被生物還原至可溶性二價鐵從而將磷酸鹽從沉澱物中釋放至上清液實現回收。最後，將除磷後的活性污泥回流至好氧反應器，從而無需排放剩餘污泥。 本項目中，膜生物反應器將被應用於好氧生物處理中以達到嚴格的廢水排放或再生回用標準。通過鐵強化混凝的膜生物反應器利用Fe–P化學反應機理和膜過濾技術實現磷的去除。應用批量實驗和高級分析技術（如ICP-AES、XRD和EXAFS）研究在好氧和厭氧酸化條件下鐵和磷的相互作用及其化學轉化。分析膜生物反應系統的處理負荷、出水水質、磷回收效率、化合物投加劑量和膜污染等問題。優化生物處理系統和化學藥劑投加以滿足廢水處理要求同時提高磷回收效率。實驗將通過處理生活污水來驗證新工藝的可行性、成本效益、運行控制及其長期穩定性。

17204914.label: Realisation of objectives
17204914.value: 1. All research objectives have been well achieved. A novel integration of the MBR with the sludge fermentation was developed for effective P removal and recovery during municipal wastewater treatment. The process makes use of an aerobic MBR tank with Fe-dosing to achieve enhanced P removal and side-stream acidogenic co-fermentation to extract P from the MBR sludge for recovery. Unlike chemical acidification, biological acidogenesis can lower the sludge pH for P extraction without deactivating the biomass. Dissimilatory iron reduction during the anaerobic sludge fermentation led to P release into the liquid phase of the sludge. In addition, food waste was added for co-fermentation and sludge acidogenesis. After P release and recovery, the activated sludge was returned to the aerobic MBR tank for the purpose of biological wastewater treatment. 2. Long-term experimental study was conducted, the performance of the new process for P removal and recovery was evaluated, and P and Fe transformation during the process was investigated and modelled. Mass balance modelling was performed on the transformation of P and Fe throughout the chemical precipitation and MBR treatment, acidogenic fermentation and recovery process to optimize the important influencing factors and reveal their interactive relationship. The membrane fouling problem was evaluated under different Fe dosage conditions, and the membrane fouling (TMP) monitoring results indicated a negative relationship between the Fe dosage and membrane fouling. High-throughput sequencing was applied to analyse the microbial communities in the integrated system, and important functional bacteria were identified for nitrification, denitrification, acidogenic fermentation and dissimilatory iron reduction through the different components of the system. 3. The quantitative P and Fe speciation in aerobic MBR and anaerobic fermenters was investigated by using X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy at both Fe and P K-edges. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a powerful technology for determination of chemical speciation and relative species fractions in a complicated mixture. XAS has been extensively used to characterize or identify the structural details of trace elements in environmental samples and to quantify mineral composition in sludge. For the present research and development, the Fe and P species and their relative abundances were determined at different stages of wastewater treatment and sludge processing. The findings regarding the transitions of Fe and P in the sludge under different conditions can provide new insights into the pathways and controlling factors for effective P removal and recovery in the chemical-biological wastewater treatment system. 4. The major pathways for P removal and recovery via Fe-dosing MBR and side-stream acidogenic fermentation are revealed. In the aerobic MBR, P in wastewater was removed by precipitation into ferric phosphate and by adsorption onto ferrihydrite. For a long SRT in the MBR, a certain portion of ferrihydrite was transformed into goethite. In the anaerobic fermenter for P release, waste organics were converted into VFAs via hydrolysis and acidogenesis to lower the solution pH. Meanwhile, organics acted as electron donors to induce microbial iron reduction. As observed in this study, ferric phosphate and ferric (oxy-)hydroxide were reduced to ferrous phosphate and ferrous hydroxide, respectively. At a lower pH, ferrous compounds dissolved, releasing soluble ferrous iron and orthophosphate into the supernatant. In summary, pH decrease and microbial iron reduction are the two critical conditions that control the dissolution of Fe-P complex and the resulting P release for recovery. Both conditions can be effectively enhanced with the addition of food waste for sludge fermentation. Eventually, with a simple pH adjustment to 8, orthophosphate and ferrous iron in the supernatant readily re-precipitated to form solid precipitates, consisting mainly of vivianite, for recovery as a raw material for P-fertilizers.

17204914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204914.value: • A novel process for enhanced P removal and recovery in municipal wastewater treatment was developed, which included chemical-enhanced (iron) phosphorus removal (CPR), an aerobic MBR and side-stream acidogenic sludge fermentation. The sludge from the MBR was circulated through the side-stream fermenters for Fe and P dissolution and extraction. By co-fermentation with a model food waste (2 g COD/L) for 2 d, the MBR sludge underwent acidogenesis and dissimilatory iron reduction. About 44.4% of P and 45.9% of Fe were then released from the sludge into the supernatant (Li and Li, BT 2017; Lin et al., CEJ 2017; Li et al., WR 2018). • A phosphorus removal efficiency of 98.1%, an overall N removal of over 91% and a 96% COD removal was stably achieved in the MBR system with side-stream co-fermentation and denitrification. Mass balance was well established to help understand the P flow and transformation through the different stages of the process and to evaluate the influences of various factors on the overall P removal and recovery results (Li et al., WR 2018; Lin and Li, Chem 2018; Li et al., BT 2018). • An overall P recovery of 62.1% from the wastewater can be achieved in the form of vivianite, and the inorganic build-up problem in the MBR can be alleviated. Compared to chemical acidification for P extraction from sludge, co-fermentation allows effective P recovery without using strong acids. Also, acidogenesis does not inactivate biomass, so the fermented sludge is returned to the MBR to maintain its long SRT (Li and Li 2017, Li et al., WR 2018; Lin et al., CEJ 2018; Li et al., BT 2018). • Microbial community analysis showed that Comamonadaceae was the dominant denitrifier for denitrification. In the anaerobic fermenter, the genus Prevotella was identified, which was apparently responsible for acidogenic fermentation, and the family Clostridiaceae was enriched, playing an important role in dissimilatory iron reduction (Lin et al., JCP 2018; Li et al., BT 2018). • According to the XANES analysis, the major pathways for P removal and recovery via Fe-dosing MBR and side-stream acidogenic fermentation are revealed. Eventually, with a simple pH adjustment to 8, orthophosphate and ferrous iron in the supernatant readily reprecipitated to form solid precipitates, consisting mainly of vivianite, for recovery as a raw material for P-fertilizers (Li et al., WR 2018; Li et al., ES&T 2018).

17204914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204914.value: • The system configuration is still a remaining and important issue for the combination of chemical P removal (CPR) and MBR for both wastewater treatment and P recovery. In most previous studies, Fe-coagulant was dosed into the MBR to enhance P removal. However, the continuous addition of Fe in the MBR not only results in the accumulation of inorganic solids in the activated sludge suspension. Alternatively, Fe-based CPR may be conducted separately before the MBR step, and the Fe-based primary sludge is fermented for P release and recovery. However, these two CPR-MBR configurations, which have different Fe dosing modes, have not been compared or evaluated. The comparison of P recovery from different CPR-MBR configurations should be conducted to further improvement of new P removal and recovery technology. • The aging phenomena of ferric compounds in MBR sludge was identified during long-term operation. The reactivity of ferric compounds was significantly influenced by the Fe aging process. The Fe and P interaction was important to P recovery by the APR process. However, the kinetics and mechanism of Fe-aging process has not been reported before. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct further investigation on iron-aging process and its relevance with P recovery.

17204914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204914.value: A new P removal and recovery process with an integration of the Fe-dosing, a membrane bioreactor (MBR) and side-stream acidogenic co-fermentation has been developed for wastewater treatment. The innovations and new findings of the research work include that: (i) acidogenic co-fermentation was applied for the first time to recover P from the sludge of the MBR, (ii) XAS analysis was utilized to identify the Fe and P species and their transformation dynamics in the aerobic MBR and anaerobic fermentation system, (iii) the major pathways of P removal and recovery were revealed, and the enhancement of microbial iron reduction by acidogenic co-fermentation was reported. The research findings provide important insights into the dynamic change of Fe-P species through the chemical and biological processes under the alternative aerobic and anaerobic conditions. With the utilization of Fe respiration and transition in the biological system, the novel process enables efficient and environmentally-friendly P recovery from municipal wastewater without the secondary pollution problem.

17205014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205014.value: Previous work has shown that ventilation can reduce exposure to airborne infectious agents in a building, and mitigate epidemics of infectious diseases transmitted through the airborne route. A significant knowledge gap, however, persists with respect to the impact of ventilation at the community level on infectious diseases transmitted through multiple routes. In a large city, people of different occupations constantly move from one building to another. People are also frequently in close contact at any location. We shall first develop a novel dual contact network model (i.e. both airborne and close contacts) for estimating the probability and duration of any two individuals meeting (subject to airborne transmission) AND in close contact (subject to droplet or surface transmission) in each indoor environment in a large city. Our improved airborne contact network model will be established from an existing model by using the available statistical sub-population data, the number of each indoor space type (locations), and the probability of people visiting different locations. An empirical close contact model will be developed to estimate the proportion of close contact in each location type based on data in literature and our own studies. Our dual contact network model will then be integrated with an existing epidemiological Susceptible, Exposed, Infectious and Recovered (SEIR) model for influenza. We will combine a revised Wells-Riley model for the airborne route and an exponential dose response model for the contact and droplet routes. The partial airborne transmission will be studied using two approaches. The first approach is to simply assume a specified contribution ratio of airborne transmission, while the second approach is to develop a more detailed multi-route model, by considering detailed transmission process of droplets and droplet nuclei via air, surfaces and direct deposition. The novelty of this proposal is in the use of a contact network model that distinguishes indoor environments, is unique relative to other network models that do not consider the physical dimensions (e.g. ventilation) of the environment and in incorporation of mechanistic exposure/transmission processes into an epidemic model. Our proposed approach links the individual contact and exposure at indoor environment level to the disease transmission at the entire city level, enabling the study of effectiveness of ventilation in a city. This project will provide an understanding of the ventilation effectiveness for multi-route transmission of influenza. Our results can lead to the formulation of improved ventilation guidelines for inclusion in future infection control guidelines. 研究表明建築通風能夠有效減少空氣懸浮傳染物暴露，從而控制建築內以空氣傳播為主的疾病爆發。但是，有關建築通風對於多途徑傳播疾病在社區尺度的作用的知識，則一直缺乏。 在城市裡，不同職業的人們一直在不同建築間，和同一建築內不同房間之間走動。在一個房間內人們常常由於生活和工作需要而緊密接觸。我們計劃首先開發嶄新的雙接觸社交網絡模型（可用於空氣和緊密接觸傳播），計算一個大城市內任何兩個人在任何一個室內聚會（用於空氣傳播）和緊密接觸（用於緊密接觸傳播）的概率和時間。我們的緊密接觸社交網絡模型將基於我們已有模型，加以改進，考慮不同人群，不同室內環境種類地點和人們進出不同室內環境概率。基於此，一個緊密接觸經驗模型也將得以開發。 我們將這個雙接觸社交網絡模型與現有流感SEIR模型串聯，並將一個用於空氣傳播疾病的Wells-Riley模型改進，並和用於緊密接觸和飛沫傳播的劑量反應模型相併聯。我們將採用兩種方法研究部分空氣傳播，即簡單假定空氣傳播貢獻率和開發一個多途徑疾病傳播模型（包括空氣傳播，緊密接觸和表面傳播）。 本課題的創新點在於開發雙接觸社交網絡模型以區分不同室內環境，和將劑量和感染過程的原理加入傳染病模型。現有的社交網絡模型並不考慮物理特性（比如通風）。我們建議的研究將連接室內環境的個人接觸和暴露與整個城市的疾病傳播，從而使得我們能夠研究建築通風對於多途徑傳播疾病在社區尺度的作用。 本課題將改善我們對於建築通風對於多途徑傳播疾病的理解。課題結果可用於將來疾病控制指南。

17205014.label: Realisation of objectives
17205014.value: We set up two objectives in this project. The first is to develop a new approach for studying the relative effectiveness of engineering methods with a focus on building ventilation. The second is to determine conditions at which ventilation becomes an effective control; and determine conditions under which ventilation is valuable in a large city such as Hong Kong by using the model. To achieve the first objective, we first developed an mathematical model that can estimate the probability and duration of any two of the 7 million people in Hong Kong meeting together (airborne contact) or in close contact (droplet contact) in any of the approximately 3 million indoor environments (locations). This is referred to as the dual contact and the separation of close-contact from airborne-contact is a novelty. The basis of our model is to simulate the location visiting behaviors of individuals of different occupations. In the existing model, we consider 8 population groups (home stayers, office workers, classroom attendees, food service workers, shop workers, drivers, public space workers and others), and 7 location groups (home, office, classroom, restaurant, shop, transport vehicles, and other public locations). We assume that each population group has the same location visiting schedule, and each location group has the same occupant density, ventilation rate distribution etc. Location-visiting probabilities of individuals in each population group are assumed to follow normal distribution. One novelty is that we reasonably assume that individuals only choose from a collection of their favorite locations such as favorite shops, restaurants etc. This reduces significantly the size of the interaction matrix of individuals and locationsOne advantage of our new airborne contact model is the statistics of individuals is known for each location. We further assume that the number of close contact of any individual in a location is related to the number of individuals in the location with the relationship determined using the existing data. It is a pity that due to the reduced budget, the planned small-scale study in a hospital ward for verifying or developing such a relationship was not carried out, though luckily a related surface touch behavior study in a student office was carried out in a subsequent CFD project. The developed dual contact model was successfully integrated with both a new and simple dynamic model for partial airborne transmission and a detailed multi-route model as planned. The general sub-models/parameters for all routes include the size distribution and number of the initial respiratory droplets, the initial concentration of the infectious influenza A viruses, calculation of the equilibrium respiratory droplet (droplet nuclei) size, and virus inactivation rate in air. Specific sub-models for the airborne route include the room air concentration of droplet nuclei including removal of ventilation, inactivation and settling. Those for short-range airborne, direct inhalation and large droplet deposition include idealized respiratory jet or puff model, statistical models of expiratory puff for different encounter angles, individual heights and gestures. The sub-model estimating the dose via surface contact transmission, represents the process by which virus on surfaces is transferred to the facial mucous membranes of the individual via contamination of his/her hand, which can be calculated if the following parameters are known, i.e. frequency of hand touching on mucous membranes, area of mucous membranes, hand area, contact area of hand to mucous membranes, transmission rate from hand to mucous membranes, from hand to hand, from surface to hand, frequency of touching a surface, area of contaminated surface, virus death rate on surface, virus death on hand, etc. . One novelty here is the short-range airborne route. The mechanisms for the long- and short-range airborne transmissions are different; hence the effectiveness of alternative control methods is also different. For the short-range airborne route, traditional methods such as ventilation dilution are least effective, but there may be a role for personalized ventilation. It is a pity that the international project EMIT 2013 did not produce expected useful data for evaluating our developed model. However, we had opportunity to analyze the unexpected MERS outbreak in South Korea during the project period. We also applied our newly developed to re-analyze the largest hospital SARS outbreak in Hong Kong in term of the roles of the fomite route, which we analyzed for the airborne route alone back in 2005. To achieve the second objective, we analyzed different combinations of intervention methods. Ventilation is found to be an effective intervention, particularly when transmission rate is high. Increasing ventilation in critical locations is important. Our results of increasing ventilation rate policies suggest that it is essential to find the high infection risk location groups to apply targeted control strategies. Homes are found to be the most important locations to control the infection of the whole community. Classrooms and offices, on the other hand, play a role as connecting small hubs (homes) with medium and large size hubs in the network. Interestingly, our results show that building ventilation can have significant effects in airborne transmission-dominated conditions. Moreover, even when the airborne route only contributes 20% to the total infection risk, increasing the ventilation rate has a strong influence on transmission dynamics, and it also can achieve control effects similar to those of wearing masks for patients, isolation and vaccination. Our multi-route model allows us to explore the roles of different routes in a specific outbreak. We reexamined the roles of the fomite transmission route in the largest SARS hospital outbreak in Hong Kong in 2003.We also took the opportunity to use our developed model and analyze the transmission routes of MERS-CoV in the first nosocomial outbreak in the Republic of Korea in May 2015. Our work was published in 6 peer-reviewed journal papers, including two in Indoor Air, three in Plos One and 1 in Science of the Total Environment.

17205014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205014.value: Our major research outcome is a multi-route model for a large city. Using our developed model and we performed analyses of disease spread at both city and building level. At the city level, ventilation is found to be an effective intervention, particularly when transmission rate is high. Increasing ventilation in critical locations is important. Our results of increasing ventilation rate policies suggest that it is essential to find the high infection risk location groups to apply targeted control strategies. Homes are found to be the most important locations to control the infection of the whole community. Classrooms and offices, on the other hand, play a role as connecting small hubs (homes) with medium and large size hubs in the network. Interestingly, our results show that building ventilation can have significant effects in airborne transmission-dominated conditions. Moreover, even when the airborne route only contributes 20% to the total infection risk, increasing the ventilation rate has a strong influence on transmission dynamics, and it also can achieve control effects similar to those of wearing masks for patients, isolation and vaccination. Thus, we conclude that increasing building ventilation such as by natural ventilation in locations such as classrooms, offices and homes is relatively an effective strategy in a large city. In exploring the roles of different routes in two specific outbreaks, i.e. SARS and MERS, we were also able to make conclusions on the most probable routes, which shed light on the effective intervention control. In reexamining the roles of the fomite transmission route in the largest SARS hospital outbreak in Hong Kong in 2003, our new results revealed that SARS-CoVs were most likely to spread in combined long-range airborne and fomite routes, and the fomite route has played a non-negligible role in transmission. We also took the opportunity to use our developed model and analyze the transmission routes of MERS-CoV in the first nosocomial outbreak in the Republic of Korea in May 2015. We found that in case that the index patient was a super-spreader, MERS-CoV was most likely to spread via the long-range airborne route. However, it is also possible that the index patient shed an average viral load comparable to those reported in the literature, and in that case, transmission via combined long-range airborne and close contact routes are also possible.

17205014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205014.value: The project has resulted a new and useful mechanisms-based approach for analyzing disease spread, i.e. a multi-route model at a city level, which is useful for offering input to infection control policy. However, many input parameters are needed, and the accuracy of the prediction relies on the accuracy of these input parameters. We identified the major deficiencies, e.g. understanding the microbe transfer during surface touch, inactivation of viruses during the evaporation process as well as the poor understanding of the close contact route. We have already secured further funding to study the microbe transfer due to surface touch, focus on the mechanisms of the fomite route as well as a new surface touch network, which are in their completion phase, and we have also successfully secured a major CRF funding to further develop the approach and understanding inactivation of infectious respiratory viruses in collaboration with other disciplines. However, the need for developing further understanding on the so-called close contact route is urgent as influenza is now suspected to be transmitted mainly in the close contact route. Many media can be involved, such as large droplet, fine droplet nuclei, skins and fomites.

17205014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205014.value: Previous work has shown that ventilation can reduce exposure to airborne infectious agents in a building, and mitigate epidemics of infectious diseases transmitted through the airborne route. In this project, our new results using two new multi-route models at city level show that building ventilation can have significant effects in airborne transmission-dominated conditions. Moreover, even when the airborne route only contributes 20% to the total infection risk, increasing the ventilation rate still has a strong influence on transmission dynamics, and it also can achieve control effects similar to those of wearing masks for patients, isolation and vaccination. Thus, we conclude that increasing building ventilation such as by natural ventilation in locations such as classrooms, offices and homes is relatively an effective strategy in a large city. We also found that in the largest SARS hospital outbreak in Hong Kong in 2003, and the first nosocomial outbreak in the Republic of Korea in May 2015, the fomite and close contact routes might have played non-negligible roles respectively. All these findings are useful for developing evidence-based infection policies for major respiratory infectious diseases.

17205114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205114.value: Although the genetic causes and pathogenesis of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) are rather well understood, current treatments for this disease are still challenged by the fact that CML cells can be resistant to most leading drugs aiming to limit their growth or trigger their apoptosis. As such, finding new ways to induce death of CML cells will likely be one of the keys in the development of interventions for this disorder in the future. Interestingly, our preliminary studies have suggested that surrounding hydrostatic pressure alone might be able to slow the population growth of CML cells as well as trigger their cytoskeletal rearrangement. Despite these initial findings, however, whether (and how if indeed) pressure can be used as a cue to regulate the behavior/fate of these cancer cells remains largely unclear. This question is of great importance not only for finding new ways to treat/contain chronic myeloid leukemia but also for our understanding of how this disease progresses and interacts with other disorders in vivo, given that conditions like hypertension and inflammation can easily put blood cells into an environment with elevated pressure. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address this unsettled issue. Specifically, precisely controlled pressures, within the physiological range, will be applied on CML cells while their biological response will be systematically investigated. Hopefully, a mapping between the characteristics (magnitude, duration and frequency) of the pressure stimuli and quantities of central interest, such as the degree of DNA/mitochondria damage and the portion of cells arrested in different cell cycle stages or undergoing apoptosis, can be established. In addition, cytoskeletal rearrangement and the resulting bleb formation of pressurized CML cells will also be carefully monitored and analyzed in conjunction with simultaneous theoretical modeling, taking into account realistic features that were neglected in previous studies. If successful, results from this project will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that physiologically relevant changes in the surrounding hydrostatic pressure will affect the biological and mechanical behavior of chronic myeloid leukemia cells, and hence greatly enhance our understanding of this disease as well as provide valuable information for the development of new interventions. In addition, predictions and data to be generated in this study will also shed light on how cytoskeletal remodeling and cell blebbing, two processes of great importance, actually take place and interact with each other. 虽然慢性骨髓性白血病（CML）的遗传原因和发病机理已经知道，对于这种疾病的治疗目前仍然受限于这种白血病细胞能够对几乎所有旨在限制它们的生长或引起其凋亡的药物都产生抗药性的事实。因此，寻找新的方法来诱导慢性髓性白血病细胞的死亡将是未来对抗这种疾病的关键之一。 我们的初步研究表明，周围静水压力的变化就能够延缓慢性髓性白血病细胞的增长以及引发其内部细胞骨架的重组。但是，是否真的可以通过对环境压力的控制来调节这些癌症细胞的行为及命运在很大程度上仍然不清楚。因为象高血压以及组织发炎一类的病症炎可以很容易的将血液细胞的胞外压力， 所以这个问题不仅对于寻找新的方法来治疗慢性骨髓性白血病非常的重要，同时它也可以帮助我们理解人体内不同的疾病是如何相互影响的。在这个项目中，我们计划进行实验和模拟相结合研究来找出这个问题的答案。具体来说，在生理范围内的压力变化将会被精确的施加到慢性髓性白血病细胞上，然后这些细胞的生物响应将会被系统地观测及记录。我们希望，一个关于压力特性（幅值，持续时间和频率）同细胞周期停滞，线粒体损伤的程度以及凋亡的定量关系可以被确立。此外，压力引起的细胞骨架重组和细胞膜微泡的形成也将被仔细监测，并与同时进行的理论模拟相结合进行分析。 如获成功，这个项目的结果将清楚地证实或反驳我们的主要假设，即环境水压的变化会影响慢性髓性白血病细胞的生物和力学性能，从而大大提升了我们对这个疾病的认识，并提供对未来治疗方按重要的信息。此外，在本研究中产生的预测和数据也将阐明细胞骨架重组和细胞出泡这两个非常重要的过程是如何发生并相互影响的。

17205114.label: Realisation of objectives
17205114.value: 1. We have developed methods to introduce precise changes in the hydrostatic or osmotic pressure, within the physiological range, to CML cells as well as systematically observe their response to such pressure stimuli. 2. The rearrangement of cytoskeletal F-actin/microtubule and subsequent blebbing in CML cells, triggered by variations in the surrounding pressure, were quantitatively monitored and analyzed. 3. A boundary integral method-based computational model was developed to describe the blebbing process of cells. Here realistic features such as the bilayer-cortex adhesion and 3D nature of the problem have all been taken into account.

17205114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205114.value: 1. Methods to introduce precise changes in the surrounding pressure of cells have been developed. It was found that active ion transport across the membrane of CML cells could be triggered by a sudden change in the extracellular hydrostatic or osmotic pressure, leading to slow variations in the cell size. Furthermore, when subjected to the same pressure stimuli, cancer cells appeared to undergo larger volumetric changes and have a higher death rate compared to their normal counterparts. We showed that such distinct response is largely caused by the overexpression of aquaporin-4 in tumor cells, with knockout of this water channel protein resulting in a markedly reduced change in the cellular volume. (refer to item 8-1 and 8-2 in Part C). 2. We showed that the spatial distribution of F-actin and microtubule, two major components of the cytoskeleton, in pressurized CML cells become more inhomogeneous as the surrounding pressure increases. In addition, it was also observed that more blebs were formed on cells under higher hydrostatic pressure. Finally, the growth dynamics of cellular blebs was carefully recorded (item 9-2 and 10-1 in Part C). 3. From our boundary integral method-based blebbing model, it was shown that, for a given differential pressure across the cell membrane, the size of the weakened cortex must be over a critical value for blebbing to occur and the steady-state volume of a bleb is proportional to its initial growth rate, all in good agreement with recent experiments. The predicted shape evolution of blebs also matches well with our observations. Finally, a blebbing map, summarizing the essential physics involved, was obtained which exhibits three distinct regimes: no bleb formation corresponding to a low intracellular pressure or a small weakened cortex region; bleb formed with a fixed width when the disrupted cortex zone is very large; and a growing bleb resulted from progressive membrane-cortex detachment under intermediate weakened cortex size. (item 8-8 and 9-2 in Part C) .

17205114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205114.value: 1. Our finding that cancer cells are more susceptible to changes in the surrounding pressure may lead to new strategies in achieving selective killing of tumor cells which could have great clinical implications. 2. The model developed could be extended to examine other interesting problems like the blebbing-assisted migration and homeostasis regulation of cells. Studies along these lines are underway.

17205114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205114.value: We have developed novel methods to introduce precise changes in the hydrostatic or osmotic pressure, within the physiological range, to CML cells. Using these setups, it was found that the spatial distribution of cytoskeletal components in pressurized cells become more inhomogeneous which eventually leads to cellular blebbing. In addition, when subjected to the same pressure stimuli, cancer cells appeared to undergo larger volumetric changes and have a higher death rate compared to their normal counterparts. Findings from this study will enhance our understanding of this disease and could provide valuable information for the development of new interventions.
