17205314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205314.value: Pollutant plume dispersion in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) is usually calculated by the Gaussian model. The dispersion coefficients are empirical functions of atmospheric stabilities based on flat and open terrain by neglecting ground elevation and surface features such as topography and urban areas. Practically, plume meandering is simply handled by trajectory adjustment according to topographic contours so the commonly observed flow separation and re-attachment are omitted at all. Buildings are roughness elements that increase the aerodynamic resistance, influencing both the flows and turbulence structure in the urban boundary layer (UBL). Their effects on plume dispersion, however, are not accounted for in the dispersion coefficients nowadays. Although Gaussian models are cost-effective, ignoring the plume meandering and dispersion modification often overlooks the tight coupling between ABL dynamics and transport processes, resulting in uncertain UBL air quality estimates for urban inhabitants. To bridge the aforementioned knowledge gap, this project is conceived to elucidate the plume meandering over idealized topography and the dispersion modification over hypothetical urban morphology. The pollutant transport between natural terrain and built environment, i.e. changes in surface roughness, will be examined in details to characterize the plume dispersion for buildings in mountainous landscape. As a pilot attempt, a complementary approach, consisting of physical (water channel experiments) and mathematical (large-eddy simulation, LES) modeling, will be sought to address the core scientific question: “How topographic configuration and urban morphology collectively affect the dynamics and plume dispersion in the stratified flows over urban areas”. Utilizing a more affordable single-layer model of open-channel flows, a large-scale sensitivity test will be performed to create a systematic database expressing the interaction among ABL/UBL structure, turbulent transport and plume dispersion in response to topographic and urbanization effects in stratified flows. In particular, deriving from classic theoretical hydrodynamics, hydraulic jump could occur over changes in topography and/or surface features, resulting in tremendous energy dissipation. It is thus hypothesized that substantial turbulence is produced locally, leading to a new conceptual model for flows and transport processes in stable UBL stratification. This project will enrich our fundamental understanding of transport processes in stratified flows over topography and urban areas. Moreover, it will parameterize the dispersion coefficients for rough terrain and dense cities to improve the next-generation Gaussian model. Finally, by unveiling the flow instability and the unconventional turbulence production mechanism in stratified UBL, the scientific community will be aroused by the importance of natural topography to pollutant removal from urban areas. 大氣邊界層中污染物煙羽擴散通常利用高斯模型計算出來，擴散系數大都是基於平坦地勢和穩定大氣的經驗函數而往往忽略地面高度和地表特徵例如地形和城市地區。應用上，煙羽蜿蜒只根據地形輪廓調整軌跡而省略所有日常觀察到的流體分離和再附著。建築物增加了空氣阻力從而影響城市邊界層湍流結構，但它們對煙羽擴散的效果就暫時沒有計算到擴散系數中。雖然高斯模型的性價比高，不考慮更改了的煙羽蜿蜒和污染物擴散往往輕視了大氣力學和輸送過程之間的耦合，最後導致不準確的城市邊界層空氣質量估量。 為了解答上述的知識差距，我們構想了這個項目旨在闡明煙羽在理想化地形上的蜿蜒和污染物在假想城市形態上的擴散變化。大氣污染物在自然地形和環境建設之間的輸送，即每當有地表粗糙度變化涉及當中，將會詳細審查從而刻畫煙羽擴散在山地建築物中的輸送細節。作為指引試點，我們將會設計一個包括物理（水糟實驗）和數學（大渦模擬）模型的互補方式以尋求解決最核心的科學問題:”地形結構和城市形態如何共同地影響污染物煙羽在城市分層流中的擴散” 。利用較實惠的單層明槽水力学模型，大規模的試驗將會進行以創建一個數據庫從而描繪城市邊界層結構、湍流輸送和煙羽擴散在城市分層流中的互動。特別是，從理論流體力學推導，在地形和地表變化之間有可能發生水躍，從而導致巨大的能量耗散，繼而大幅產生湍流，我們因此假設一個創新的概念模型希望有助解釋城市分層流中的輸送過程。 這個項目將充實我們對地形和城市地區分層流輸送過程的基本認識，此外，它將有助優化擴散系數在崎嶇地形和稠密市區應用中的參數化，提高下一代高斯模型的可靠程度。最後，揭開了流場不穩定性和非傳統的分層流湍流產生機制，科學界將會對自然地形在城市地區污染物移除中的重要性引起關注。

17205314.label: Realisation of objectives
17205314.value: Objective #1. Investigate the effects of aerodynamic resistance on plume dispersion over topography and urban areas. Mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments were used concurrently to investigate how topography and urban areas affect the aerodynamic resistance together with the plume dispersion over the turbulent boundary layer (TBL) aloft. The Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) turbulence model and the large-eddy simulation (LES) were employed as the mathematical models. The RANS model offered quick results of the flow statistics that paved the basis. Moreover, it helped configure the LES sensitivity tests (domain size and range of surface roughness, etc.) in a systematic manner. Finite volume method (FVM) was used to discretize the computational domain while the implicit Euler method was used in the time integration. The Smagorinsky model was used to model the subgrid-scale (SGS) motions. In the laboratory experiments, reduced-scaled physical models were tested in our wind tunnel (6,000-mm long x 550-mm wide x 550-mm high with wind speeds up to 15 m/sec). Constant-temperature (CT) hot-wire anemometry (HWA) was used to sample the flows in high frequency (2,000 Hz) and water vapor was used as the tracer for dispersion (safe and environmentally friendly). Because of the detailed spatio-temporal flows, the LES results were employed to look into the fundamental mechanism and the turbulent transport processes. Roughness elements of Idealized shape (ribs in cross flows and bricks), urban morphology (real urban models fabricated by 3D-printing) and vegetation (plastic tree models) were adopted. The roughness elements were tested by both LES and wind tunnel experiments for complementary solution. In the idealized configuration of roughness elements, it was found that the aerodynamic resistance, which was measured by the drag coefficient in this project, is small when the roughness elements are close to each other. Increasing the separation increases the aerodynamic resistance that arrives a peak then decreases thereafter. As such, it was found that the aerodynamic resistance is dominated by form drag (impingement on windward walls of roughness elements) while the shear drag is negligible in most applications. This finding was helpful to interpret the aerodynamic resistance over real urban morphology such that high building density does not necessarily imply high aerodynamic resistance but diversified buildings with wide spectra of building height/shape variability. It was confirmed by the mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments as well. Plume dispersion is governed by turbulence which is mainly driven by surface roughness. Hence, the extent of plume dispersion, which is measured by the vertical dispersion coefficient, is enhanced with increasing drag coefficient. Objective #2. Examine the ABL/UBL structure over different surface features and the associated transport processes in thermal stratification. The sensitivity tests conducted above archived extensive datasets that were used to examine the structure of atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) and urban boundary layer (UBL) over different (rough) surfaces. Generally, the conventional logarithmic law of the wall (log-law) is applicable to both smooth and rough surfaces. Modification is needed when the conventional log-law is applied to rough surfaces (shift downward). Instead of the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, it was found that there exists the roughness sublayer (RSL) below the inertial sublayer (ISL), which, however, has been overlooked in many studies of atmospheric transport processes. Different from the ISL, the RSL is affected by individual roughness elements (e.g. buildings) in which the velocity gradient is less than that in the ISL. Hence, RSL transport is stronger than its ISL counterpart. It is thus expected that the flows and the concentrations of atmospheric constituents are more uniform at the building-roof level (urban canopy). Based on the dimensionless wind speed gradient, we derived the analytical solution to the wind-speed profile of RSL and ISL from first principles. The new analytical wind-speed profile comprises the characteristics in both RSL and ISL (unified formulation) that was verified by the wind-tunnel data over different roughness elements (Objective #1). There is a constant term, the RSL constant, whose values are different for urban areas (~ 2.6) and vegetation canopy (> 3.0). Additional work will be conducted in the future to improve our understanding in that regard. Nonetheless, the analytical solution helped elucidate the RSL and ISL transport processes that has been extended to describe the mechanism in terms of turbulent length scales. Preliminarily, it was found that the RSL turbulent length scales increase faster than the conventional log-law that in turn enhance the transport processes over rougher surfaces (urban areas). Objective #3. Elucidate the coupling among topography, urban morphology and thermal stratification in order to refine the UBL plume dispersion parameterizations. The findings in Objective #2 help enrich our fundamental understanding of the transport processes over rough surfaces with application to urban areas, forest canopies and topography. In this connection, analytical studies were carried out to derive the plume dispersion parameterizations in terms of other environmental variables such as wind speeds and aerodynamic resistance. In our previous studies, we had found that the street-level ventilation is proportional to the square root of the drag coefficient over urban areas. In this project, as a continuation of our existing effort, we used the drag coefficient to parameterize the (vertical) dispersion coefficient over rough surfaces. In addition to the downwind distance, it was found that the vertical dispersion coefficient is proportional to fourth root of drag coefficient. The newly proposed parameterization can be nondimensionalized using the TBL thickness to characterize the length scale. It was verified by wind tunnel measurements, RANS and LES of a range of length scales. Favorable agreement has been obtained. The major benefit of the newly proposed parameterization of dispersion coefficient is simplification such that the infinite combinations of building shape, orientation and blockage, etc., are handled by the drag coefficient only. Hence, the ability of ventilation and pollutant removal of certain urban areas can be estimate quickly by the drag coefficient. Practically, the drag coefficient is usually measured in development projects (wind engineering and structural safety) so the financial implication extending to ventilation and pollutant removal is minimal. The newly proposed parameterization is thus a cost-effective solution for the environmental assessment of urban areas.

17205314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205314.value: Apart from the advancement in laboratory instrumentation and mathematical modeling techniques, the major finding of this project is related to the fundamental understanding of how morphology affects turbulence and the pollutant plume dispersion over urban areas. Our systemic sensitivity tests, both LES and wind tunnel experiments, showed that the aerodynamic resistance of urban areas is dominated by the form drag while the shear drag is negligible. Under this circumstance, buildings in dense cities do not necessarily imply elevated aerodynamic resistance. Indeed, building clusters with diversified height, shape and orientation, etc., increase the aerodynamic resistance because of the large amount of flow impingement. Apart from practical significance, this finding supports the use of surface-level Reynolds stress to determine the drag over urban areas that is useful in laboratory experiments. Another major finding is the analytical solution to the wind profiles that is a unified formulation connecting the RSL and ISL, i.e. the interface in-between does not affect the mathematical model. The major contribution of the analytical solution is an in-depth understanding of the TBL structure (more uniform wind profiles in the RSL compared with those in the ISL) and the turbulent length scale (increasing faster in the RSL than the ISL). The urban climate community used to neglect the RSL or extrapolate the ISL theory to RSL transport processes. Whereas, the results obtained in this project showed that, though it is thin, the RSL differs from that of ISL. Because of the different structure, the RSL has a characteristic transport processes that cannot be explained by its ISL counterpart. We found that the RSL turbulent length scale (i.e. eddy size) increases with the wall-normal distance faster than does ISL. As such, rough surfaces, which usually have thicker RSLs, possess enhanced transport processes. Computers are fast but are too expensive to resolve all the flow details around individual buildings together with the UBLs. We derived analytically, as an extension of our previous parameterization of street-level ventilation, the formulation to the plume dispersion over urban areas. Instead of the complicated buildings details, we use the dimensionless variable, drag coefficient, to unprecedentedly parameterize the plume dispersion over urban areas. The analytical solution agrees well with wind tunnel measurements and mathematical modeling results (at different length scales). As drag is commonly measured in development projects, it can be easily extended to evaluate the environmental impact of (new) urban areas in the design stage.

17205314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205314.value: The findings from this project unprecedentedly proposed the use of drag coefficient to parameterize the dispersion coefficient over urban areas. So far, the results obtained are favorable. Whereas, more tests should be conducted to verify the newly proposed parameterization. More cities of diversified urban morphology should be employed to evaluate the accuracy of the parameterization. While the current solution approach should be continued, it would be excellent extending the verification to field campaigns because too many processes of microphysics are not yet included in mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments. We hypothesize that the enhanced transport processes over rougher urban areas are attributed to the RSLs, which, however, are often overlooked. While the velocity scale in the RSL is about constant, the turbulent length scale increases in the wall-normal distance faster than that in the ISL. Rougher urban areas come with thicker RSLs. It in turn elongates the turbulent length scales and enhances the transport processes (by larger eddies). Another stage of analytical studies should be conducted to verify our hypothesize. The next course of action is thus to examine how RSL turbulent length scales change with the drag coefficient of urban areas and their implication to plume dispersion.

17205314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205314.value: Extensive mathematical modeling (large-eddy simulation; LES) and laboratory measurements (wind tunnel experiments) were performed to elucidate the pollutant dispersion in the turbulent boundary layer (TBL) over urban areas. Apart from idealized roughness elements (ribs and bricks), real urban morphology was fabricated by 3D-printing and tested. It was found that the drag coefficient is an indicator of the street-level ventilation and pollutant dispersion. Diversified building height, orientation and shape, etc., promote drag coefficient so are favorable to ventilation and pollutant dispersion. There exists a thin roughness sublayer (RSL) below the conventional inertial sublayer (ISL) that possesses a more uniform wind speed together with stronger mixing and transport. The RSL length scale increases faster than does ISL. Urban areas come with RSLs that partly explains the enhanced transport processes. The plume dispersion coefficient is parameterized in terms of the drag coefficient that serves as a quick estimate to pollutant distribution over urban areas. The newly proposed parameterization agrees well with the results of mathematical modeling and wind tunnel experiments of different scales. It can be used to evaluate the environmental performance of development projects and urban design in a cost-effective manner. Field measurements would be needed to further improve the parameterization.

17205414.label: Project Objectives
17205414.value: To introduce novel solar cells with broad applications. In principle, the new PV architecture can be applied to any existing semiconductor PV materials, inorganic and organic. In addition, there exist more flexibility in device design and operation. For example, we can adjust the induced electric field in the semiconductor by simply changing the ferroelectric thickness or the electrode spacing. Moreover, unlike traditional p-n junction solar cells, the new device requires no heavy doping that results in strong Auger recombination. To attain simple and inexpensive processing steps for producing solar cells. Much less inexpensive processing steps can be applied to the new-concept cells, compared to traditional crystalline Si-based solar cells. Although both anode and cathode were digitized on the same side of the prototype cell and they had to be close to each other to match the diffusion length (sub-millimeter in existing best PV materials), they could be on different sides of the cell as well. To achieve high-performance solar cells. In a traditional p-n junction solar cell, only carriers generated within the diffusion length near the depletion region can be collected and utilized for energy conversion. In our new devices, since the external electric field can span the whole region of the absorber layer, all the carriers generated can be possibly separated and collected. Also, compared to traditional ferroelectric photovoltaics, our new devices have better light absorption and carrier transport.

17205414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205414.value: 光伏是一種通過光伏效應將太陽能直接轉換為電能的技術。由於太陽能是最豐富的能量來源，它注定會在我們的未來能源版圖中佔有重要的一席之地。和其它的從太陽能轉化為電能的途徑相比，光伏具有較高的整體轉換效率，並且是唯一的可用任何有光的地方的技術。為了增加太陽能發電在我們能源版圖中的市場份額，很有必要探索性價比優異的太陽能電池。光伏器件的發展通常在於優化電荷載流子的三個方面：產生、分離和傳導。特別是如何實現電荷載流子的分離通常決定了器件的基本結構。傳統的太陽能電池本質上來講是基於pn節（或者電子供體/電子受體節）的，是利用pn節界面處的內建電場來實現電荷分離。但是，基於節的結構只是實現太陽能電池功能的一種方式。另外，由於晶格失配、摻雜以及能帶匹配等原因，這種基於節的結構會限制器件製備的材料選擇。同時，由於在傳統太陽能電池中需要重摻雜， 這會導致俄歇複合。因此，在器件設計方面，很值得探索其它的可能性。 在此我們展示一種新型光伏器件：鐵電場效應太陽能電池。該器件同時利用鐵電材料和半導體材料的優良性能。和傳統太陽能電池一樣，該新器件也用半導體材料來吸收陽光，因為半導體材料具有適合吸收太陽光的能量帶隙和良好的載流子傳輸性能。除此之外，鐵電材料表面的固定極化電荷也被用來提供一個外加電場在半導體層上，從而加強半導體內的電荷分離。但是和傳統的鐵電太陽能電池不同，我們新器件中的鐵電層不會用來吸光，因為其能量帶隙太大而不適合吸陽光。因此，我們的新器件可以克服上面提到的傳統光伏器件的缺點，從而有希望實現更高的能量轉換效率（從載流子的產生、分離和傳輸的角度來看）。該新概念在太陽能電池的製備方面也提供了很大的靈活性，在實現高性能、廉價的太陽能電池方面具有很好的前景。 關鍵詞: 太陽能電池; 鐵電材料; 場效應; 電荷分離; 太陽能。

17205614.label: Project Objectives
17205614.value: to map the project-based organisations (PBOs) into social networks by introducing a novel social network analysis (SNA) approach; to ascertain the empirical impacts of building information modeling (BIM) on the social networks.

to ascertain the empirical impacts of building information modeling (BIM) on the social networks.

17205614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205614.value: 建築信息模型（BIM）已經成為近幾年建築業最熱門的流行語之一。很多與BIM相關的國際研討會在全球各地召開；軟件開發商們積極開發他們的BIM產品；各國政府也在大力普及BIM以推進建築業革新。與此同時，建築企業們受到了這股BIM浪潮的鼓舞，也正在嘗試和接納BIM。 BIM是貫穿建築設計、工程施工和運營管理等全生命周期的一種集合信息數據並促進信息傳遞交流的數字化表達方式。它不僅是一種實現虛擬設計和施工的技術工具，同時也被視為一種項目管理的輔助平臺，以幫助解決項目執行中許多長期存在的問題，比如人機料脫節、工序安排不夠連續和溝通效率不夠高等。 BIM甚至被贊譽為帶動整個建築業產業轉型和升級的革命性技術 。然而，在迄今為止大量的BIM研究中，很少有研究真正深入探討BIM在實踐中是怎樣影響項目團隊的組織行為（這裏的項目團隊特指基於項目的組織[PBO]）。 該研究旨在通過社會網絡的方法探討BIM這種技術創新是如何影響PBO的組織行為，診斷組織執行中的效率問題繼而創造更大的項目價值。本研究的理論基礎是將項目的組織（PBO）本身看做一個社會網絡。可以預見，BIM的使用將會促進組織溝通，鼓勵團隊協作，從而提高項目表現。該研究有兩個相關聯的研究目標：（1）通過社會網絡分析（SNA）的方法將項目的組織行為描述成一系列具有時間跨度的社會網絡（圖表達和數學表達兩種方式）；（2）解讀BIM的使用對上述社會網絡的影響。本研究將會使用案例分析的方法來實現這些研究目標，而香港房屋委員會（HKHA）作為在大型公共房屋項目中推廣BIM使用的倡導者，將會為該研究提供很大的支持。 該研究項目的成果將會豐富關於BIM等技術創新對於PBO組織行為影響的研究文獻，並且將加深BIM等技術創新如何影響PBO組織行為的理解（從溝通模式、組織流程和組織管理等角度）。同時，該研究將會幫助PBO內的利益相關者了解BIM的不同使用模式對項目執行的影響，從而使他們能夠診斷組織執行中的效率問題繼而為社會創造更大的價值。從長遠來看，該研究將會有助於BIM在建築業行業內更合理地使用與實施。

17205614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205614.value: This research confirms that the fit between formal and informal institutions is positively correlated with project performance. A central corollary is that a higher metric of formal or informal networks need not, in itself, result in better project performance; of equal (if not greater) importance is the extent of fit between the two. These results have both theoretical and practical significance. Research that has traditionally focused on rigid, hierarchical formal institutions in project management can now be redirected toward pursuing a new angle: the interplay between formal and informal institutions. Project managers can use this research to guide periodic and systematic diagnoses of their project networks with the aim of continually improving project performance. By using the metrics available through SNA to quantify and visualize network interplay, project management—especially as regards diagnosis and subsequent intervention—can wield a powerful tool for improving project management practices. A critical review of existing studies shows that they mainly concern ‘tracking’ and ‘generation of an ‘as-built’ model’ at construction stage, while wider applications of bridging BIM and building (BBB) at other stages are yet to be considered. The major technologies explored were laser scanning, RFID, camera, GIS, GPS, and AR. To date, software, databases, and data exchange protocols have been paid scant attention in BBB studies. Collaboration of various technologies could integrate building information models and physical building processes for better project management performance. Auto-ID, including RFID, was applied to bridging the physical and the cyber of construction projects with BIM. Smart construction objects with the properties of awareness, communicativeness, and autonomy were also developed to link BIM and IoT for more efficient and effective construction logistics and supply chain management, safety management, and procedure guiding.

17205614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205614.value: Scholars should consider incorporating the relational factors derivable from big data (e.g., timesheets, records) instead of relying solely on curated small-data samples, make stronger connection between the graphical and mathematical representations of SNA and their practical implications for organizational studies, and collect data on the evolution of formal and informal networks to investigate their changing with the progress of BIM implementation. Future research is recommended into theorizing bridging BIM and building (BBB) by linking it to the general theories of information management and the characteristics of construction projects and project-based organizations. Researchers are also recommended to further explore the practical uses of BBB technologies that can make BIM a more useful decision-support system. Besides, research on the localization of BIM, the implementation of BIM to the projects’ whole life-cycle instead of just construction stage, and the integration of heterogeneous data into BIM models for better project performance are also encouraged.

17205614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205614.value: The topic of this research project is an emerging technology called building information modeling (BIM), which is being more and more widely used in construction project management. This research project aims to map and understand the impacts of BIM on the organization and performance of project teams in terms of the way they communicate, the processes they work, and the manners they govern. The significance and value of this research project are threefold. Firstly, the research project provided a method to understand how different BIM implementation modes affect the functioning of project teams. Secondly, the research findings guides project managers to diagnose the project teams’ efficacy and make better decisions to enhance the performance of the project teams. Finally, the research outputs point out a way to enrich the information of BIM by bridging BIM and other technologies such as RFID that can capture real-life location and condition data in construction project management.

17205714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205714.value: The International Osteoporosis Foundation estimates that more than 8.9 million elderly patients suffer from osteoporotic fractures each year, and that by 2050 rates for some fracture types will rise by 300% due to ageing demographics worldwide [1]. While injection of bone cement can be an effective treatment for osteoporotic fractures, several problems with this method remain. Bone cement leakage into surrounding tissue can lead to dangerous complications such as spinal stenosis and pulmonary emboli and conventional biologically inert bone cement requires long periods of time for osteointegration to occur. Our research team has devoted significant attention to innovative bioactive bone cements, which harbor osteoinductive elements such as strontium in order to accelerate the rate of bone regrowth after cement injection [2]. However, clinical concerns over leakage risks have slowed the large-scale adoption of bioactive bone cement. Additionally, leakage risks have held back the development of new preventative treatments employing bone cement injection in order to reduce the likelihood of fractures in patients with osteoporotic bones. In response, our team of clinicians, bioengineers and biomaterial experts is developing a novel leak-free cement injection system, potentially opening the doors to wider adoption of both bioactive cement and preventative bone cement injection. Our system features a thermosensitive balloon, synthesized using innovative upper critical solution temperature (UCST) polymer, that acts as a “smart barrier” to prevent the flow of cement into surrounding tissue, and then dissolves due to heat released by the bone cement once it has hardened. The aim of the current study is to: • Synthesize a UCST thermo sensitive polymer with melting temperature of 65C (matched to the heat of polymerization of bone cement) • Final design of the injection system and finite element/computational fluid dynamics analysis of design under typical clinical conditions • In-vitro experiments to finalize and validate the system Following this study, we intend to pursue pre-clinical research employing animal models to evaluate the system during treatment under osteoporotic conditions. We strongly believe in the potential positive impact of this research on the health of millions of elderly in Hong Kong and worldwide who presently suffer from painful and debilitating osteoporotic fractures. 17205714.label: Realisation of objectives
17205714.value: In this project, we have planed our study and conducted following experiments and tests to realise our objectives. In Synthesis of a biomaterial, a novel nanocomposite hydrogel (NC gel) was successfully prepared by in situ free-radical photo-polymerization of the acrylic acid derivatives. The novel polymer, composed of Laponite XLG clay attractive fracture strain up to 4000% and good compression strength and the obtained hydrogel has good biocompatibility and high viscosity before photo-polymerization, which means this kind of hydrogel is a very suitable bioink candidate of the layer-by-layer bioprinting method for the fabrication of stratified tissues. In the implant design study, we have developed the anti-cutting device which the axial migration was explored using a novel fracture mechanics model based on the Griffith Criterion and material compaction. Three tip designs were considered based on typical 5 mm locking screws: flat and conical tip designs, as well as a novel polymer tip. Crack formation and friction were found to be negligible mechanisms of energy absorption; material compaction was the dominant mechanism under axial loading, regardless of tip design. The medical implant designed to maximize the cross- sectional area of compacted material – such as the elastomeric tip – may be useful in reducing excessive implant migration under axial loads in elderly trabecular bone. In the biomechanical study, a novel computational model of implant migration in trabecular bone was developed using smoothed-particle hydrodynamics (SPH). Further more, biomechanical testing using six human cadaveric specimens from the proximal femurs of female donors conducted. SPH models were constructed based on microCT scans of the specimens prior to penetration and the experiments were repeated in silico. The concordance correlation coefficient between experimental and simulated pairs was found 0.888, with a 95% CI of 0.8832–0.8926. This is the first known study to show that simulations based on SPH can produce accurate predictions of trabecular bone penetration that are useful for characterizing implant performance for elderly bone.

17205714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205714.value: In this project, Firstly, a novel nanocomposite hydrogel (NC gel) was successfully prepared by in situ free-radical photo-polymerization of the acrylic acid derivatives. We found the NC hydrogels composed of Laponite XLG clay attractive fracture strain up to 4000% and good compression strength. The strong hydrogen bonds between 4-Acryloylmorpholine polymer and clay are suggested to account for the good mechanical properties. More interestingly, the obtained hydrogel has good biocompatibility and high viscosity before photo-polymerization, which means this kind of hydrogel is a very suitable bioink candidate of the layer-by-layer bioprinting method for the fabrication of stratified tissues. In the second study, the effect of implant tip design on axial migration was explored using a novel fracture mechanics model based on the Griffith Criterion and material compaction. Three tip designs were considered based on typical 5 mm locking screws: flat and conical tip designs, as well as a novel polymer tip. Tip designs were inserted into polyurethane foam (0.16 g/cc) to a depth of 10 mm at a rate of 2 mm/min. At maximum depth, polymer tips required the greatest force for axial migration (248.24 N, 95% CI: 238.1–258.4 N), followed by conical tips (143.46 N, 95% CI: 142.1–144.9 N), and flat tips (113.88 N, 95% CI: 112.2– 115.5 N). Crack formation and friction were found to be negligible mechanisms of energy absorption; material compaction was the dominant mechanism under axial loading, regardless of tip design. Compacted material cross-sectional area was a strong determinant of force (Pearson Coefficient=0.902, p<0.001). Implant tips designed to maximize the cross-sectional area of compacted material – such as the elastomeric tip – may be useful in reducing excessive implant migration under axial loads in trabecular bone. In our 3rd study, a novel computational model of implant migration in trabecular bone was developed using smoothed-particle hydrodynamics (SPH). Six human cadaveric specimens from the proximal femurs of female donors (age 75-90) measuring 10Å~10Å~20 mm were penetrated under axial loading to a depth of 10 mm with 5 mm diameter cylindrical indenters bearing either flat or sharp/conical tip designs. SPH models were constructed based on microCT scans of the specimens prior to penetration and the experiments were repeated in silico. Peak forces varied between 92.0–365.0 N in the experiments, and 115.5–352.2 N in the SPH simulations. The concordance correlation coefficient between experimental and simulated pairs was 0.888, with a 95% CI of 0.8832–0.8926, a Pearson ρ (precision) value of 0.9396, and a bias correction factor Cb (accuracy) value of 0.945. Patterns of bone compaction were qualitatively similar. This is the first known study to show that simulations based on SPH can produce accurate predictions of trabecular bone penetration that are useful for characterizing implant performance under high-strain loading conditions.

17205714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205714.value: Insights from these basic research studies, the future projects that will be applied to the design of an initial pair of novel implants for femoral and humeral fractures with polymer (polycarbonate urethane elastomer) tip designs. Pilot studies showed the superiority of these implants in resisting migration in porous bone. These prototype implants will futher be biomechanically tested according to ISO standard methods from the literature, and a pilot biocompatibility study of in rat femurs was performed. Safety and efficacy of the implants will be further suitably demonstrated to anticipate ready approval of such devices, or improved future designs based on similar principles, in the major regulatory jurisdictions (e.g. US FDA, CE, CFDA).

17205814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205814.value: RDF知識庫中空間語義之高效管理

17205814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205814.value: The Resource Description Framework (RDF) data model is a standard for expressing information that does not conform to a crisp schema. In the past decade, there have been many efforts by researchers and companies on the effective storage and efficient search of information knowledge bases in the form of RDF triples. The RDF data model has recently been extended to support representation and querying of spatial information (i.e., locations and geometries), which is associated with RDF entities. On the other hand, there are limited efforts toward extending RDF stores to efficiently support spatial queries, such as range selections (e.g., find entities near a given location) and spatial joins (e.g., find pairs of entities whose locations are close to each other). Given the fact that a large percentage of entities in most RDF knowledge bases carry spatial semantics, there is a need for spatially extended RDF stores that handle spatial data effectively. In this project, we will study in detail the spatial extensibility of state-of-the-art RDF stores. Specifically, we will investigate spatial indexing and data encoding techniques for RDF entities, which facilitate the efficient evaluation of queries with spatial components. Besides, we plan to develop advanced query selectivity estimation statistics, which consider spatial correlations that exist in the RDF data. A query optimizer, which will consider spatial along with non-spatial selectivity estimation statistics toward identifying a good evaluation plan for any given query, will be developed. Finally, we will consider other issues, such as the maintenance of the data encoding and statistics after dynamic data updates, and system extensions toward handling spatio-temporal data semantics and processing of spatial aggregate queries. A successful completion of the project will result in an extendable RDF store that handles and queries spatial information efficiently. This is an important advancement to the state-of-the-art, since (i) spatial data and queries are ubiquitous and (ii) their handling in current RDF storage systems is inadequate. 資源描述框架（英文resource description framework，縮寫為RDF）數據模型是一組技術標準，用以表達那些難以經由模式（schema）來表達的信息。在過去的十年中，研究者和企業關注RDF三元組形式的信息知識庫，在有效存儲和高效搜索方面做了大量的工作。最近，RDF數據模型經已被擴展，用以支持對RDF實體的空間信息（如位置、幾何形狀等等）的表示和查詢。然而在另一方面，對於如何擴展RDF存儲使之有效支持空間查詢——諸如範圍選擇（例如尋找指定位置附近的實體）以及空間連接（如找出所有位置接近的實體對），這樣的工作目前還鮮有討論。事實上，大多數RDF知識庫中的大部份實體都載有空間語義，鑑於此，我們需要有空間上擴展了的RDF存儲來高效地處理空間數據。 在本項目中，我們將具體研究當前最新RDF存儲的空間可擴展性。特別地，我們將研究RDF實體的空間索引和數據編碼技術，這些技術能夠為響應附有空間成分的查詢帶來便利。同時，我們計劃開發高級的查詢選擇度評估統計量，這樣的統計量應是考慮到了存在於RDF數據中的空間相關性。我們將開發一個查詢優化器，這個優化器將會考慮空間的以及非空間的選擇度評估統計量，為任意給定的查詢製定出好的執行規劃。最後，我們還將考慮其他問題，例如，在數據動態更新時數據編碼和統計量的維護問題、系統針對時空數據語義的擴展問題、處理空間聚合查詢的問題，等等。本項目的順利完成將會帶來一個能夠高效處理及查詢空間信息的可擴展的RDF存儲，這將是對當前系統的重要發展，因為（1）空間數據和查詢是普遍存在的，且（2）當前的RDF存儲系統對於它們的處理還很不充分。

17206114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206114.value: Conducting polymers and nano-structured materials such as nanoporous noble metals, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and carbon aerogels are exciting, new types of actuator materials which can flex or stretch upon receiving an electrical signal. Compared with conventional actuating materials such as piezo-ceramics and electroactive polymers which may require kilo-volts for actuation, these materials only require a few volts to produce comparable or even larger actuation strains. However, these materials are expensive and some of them also exhibit very slow strain response with low energy efficiency. Recently, the PI’s group discovered a new type of nano-porous oxide-on-metal composite materials which also exhibit reversible dimensional changes upon excitation by electrical voltages of a few to tens of volts. Strong electrostatic (Coulombic) interactions within the nano-porous structure are believed to be a reason for the observed actuation behaviour. Compared to the other low-voltage actuation materials, our materials are much cheaper and easy to fabricate, and yet can produce very rapid strain responses, and are capable of actuating in both liquid electrolyte and air environments. If properly developed further, this group of materials should greatly increase the choice of low-voltage actuation materials for micro-robotic or similar applications. In this project, we propose to conduct systematic work to understand the underlying mechanisms as well as the key factors for the actuation behaviour of our new materials, with a view to optimize their performance. First, theoretical modeling at both the atomic and the continuum levels will be carried out to understand the actuation mechanisms in both liquid electrolytes and in air. Systematic experimentation will be conducted to provide data for the theoretical work, and this includes measurement of the actuation performance and reliability of the materials by nano-mechanical characterization techniques. Also, the key factors influencing the strain amplitude, including the thicknesses of the oxide actuating layer and the substrate, the type and structure of the nanoporous oxide in the actuating layer, and, in the case of actuation in liquid environments, the type and concentration of the liquid electrolyte, will be systematically explored. We will also attempt to combine our materials with other nanomaterials, such as carbon nanotubes, atomic gold layers, or nanoporous metals, to form composite material systems to see if the actuation strain amplitude can be further improved. Finally, an undergraduate student will be involved in the design and fabrication of prototypic micro-robotic systems using these new actuating materials, as part of his/her experiential learning. 導電聚合物和多種類型的納米材料，例如納米多孔貴金屬、碳納米管、碳氣凝膠等，是新型的電致動材料。在循環電壓的激勵下，這些材料具有延長或收縮的性質。傳統的電致動材料，例如壓電陶瓷、電活性聚合物等，需要上千伏的電壓來實現電致動，而納米結構的材料只需要幾伏電壓就可以達到與前者相當或者更大的應變。但是，這些新型納米材料受限於昂貴的價格、電致動響應時間長、低能量效率等。近期，PI課題組發現了一種新型的納米多孔氧化物/金屬複合電致動材料。在幾伏到幾十伏循環電壓的激勵下，該材料的尺寸呈現可恢復性變化。聚集在納米結構表面的電荷所形成的靜電庫倫力是導致這種電致動的原因。與其它的低電壓電致動材料相比，我們發現的這種材料具有廉價、製備方法簡單、電致動響應時間很短等優點，更重要的是它既可以像其它低電壓電致動材料一樣在電解質溶液環境下實現電致動，又可以在空氣環境下實現。我們相信經過進一步的深入研究，這一類型的複合材料將會成為未來低電壓電致動材料的有力候選者，應用在微米級機器人或其他類似的領域。 在本項目中，我們建議對這種納米多孔氧化物/金屬複合電致動材料進行系統的研究，其中包括電致動的機理、影響電致動的主要因素等，從而優化該材料的電致動性能。首先，從原子層次到連續介質層次，對該材料在電解質和空氣中的電致動機理，進行理論建模和數值計算。系統的實驗研究將為理論計算提供必要支持，其中包括利用納米力學表證技術對電致動進行測量以及材料的可靠性研究等。其次，研究影響應變幅度的主要因素，包括納米氧化物層和金屬襯底層的厚度、氧化物層的納米結構和孔有序性、電解質的類型和濃度等。另外，我們將嘗試把該納米材料與其它納米材料進行複合，例如碳納米管、原子級厚度的貴金屬鍍層、或納米多孔金屬等，研究能否進一步提高原有材料的電致動性質。 最後，一名本科生也會參與到這項研究，即利用電致動材料設計和製備最初類型的微機器系統，這將成為該學生實驗學習的一部分。

17206114.label: Realisation of objectives
17206114.value: As per Objective 1, three types of novel oxide/metal actuating materials were developed. These include: (i) nickel nanohoneycombs and nano-fibril forests [papers 3, 4], (ii) Au-film actuators with nanotextured surfaces [paper 2], and (iii) nickel hydroxide-on-nickel actuators [papers 6, 7]. We first synthesized nickel nanohoneycombs by using a dual-template method, to result in a bi-layered cantilever structure comprising a nanohoneycomb layer of Ni backed by a solid layer of the same metal [paper 3]. Reversible bending of the cantilever upon cyclic potential triggering in an alkaline hydroxide electrolyte was observed and characterized. Electrical impedance spectroscopy measurements suggest the actuation mechanism is mainly due to a pseudocapacitive behaviour by means of reversible faradic redox reactions involving the conversion between Ni(II) and Ni(III). Furthermore, by performing anodization on purity-containing aluminium substrates, we have produced a special type of nanohoneycomb template structure which contains sub-channels bridging the main honeycomb channels. By performing electrodeposition of Ni into such a template structure, we managed to produce a peculiar 3D nano-network structure that consists of nano-fibrils connected up by side branches [paper 4]. Such a structure was found to exhibit ultra-fast electrochemical actuation response in hydroxide environments, due to the same redox reactions involving Ni(II) and Ni(III) as described above. The strain response time was on the order of 0.1 second, which is two orders of magnitude faster than existing metallic actuators. Such an ultra-fast response is due to the enhanced ion flow in the peculiar network structure. We also synthesized and studied another actuating material system comprising a gold-film with nanotextured surface [paper 2]. Using electroless gold plating onto a substrate of porous anodized aluminum oxide (AAO), a thin film of gold with a high density of short gold nanofibres on its surface was made. Bending actuation of this structure was observed in air, when such a film was electrically charged by an ion generator. Our experiments showed that the free end of an 8 mm film could be displaced by more than 1.6 mm. In contrast with other types of thin-film artificial muscle materials, the present Au-film did not require any electrolyte to function. The work on nickel nanohoneycombs and nano-fibril forests indicates a significant electrochemical actuation effect due to the redox conversion between Ni(II) and Ni(III). This has led us to focus on the third material system, namely, nickel hydroxide-on-nickel actuators, where the actuation arises from the redox conversion between nickel hydroxide (Ni(OH)2) and oxyhydroxide (NiOOH) [paper 6]. Of the three material systems developed, this material system has the best actuating performance, namely, actuating stress of ~20MPa, actuating strain rate of ~1%/s and highest actuating strain of around 0.6%. In addition to electrochemical actuation due to the redox conversion, we also discovered that the same material system can also actuate under the stimulus of visible light illumination of much less than 1 sun, due to a light-triggered water loss mechanism [paper 7]. The nickel hydroxide-on-nickel material system has the best potential to be further exploited as a novel actuating material for real applications. As per Objective 2, the actuating behaviours of all three materials developed were characterized, and the results have been reported in the corresponding publications. In particular, the light-triggered mechanism of nickel hydroxide/oxyhydroxide allows the material to lift up weights that are >2000 times its own weight, as characterized by nano-tensile experimentation in a nano-tensile tester [paper 7]. Long-term durability tests of 5000 cycles of this material also revealed no observable degradation of the actuation behaviour and the material itself [paper 7]. In addition, the electrochemical actuation mechanism of nickel nanohoneycomb/nano-fibril forests, and that of the nickel hydroxide/oxyhydroxide were well characterized by techniques including cyclic voltammetry, electrical impendence measurement, X-ray diffraction, high-resolution electron microscopy, and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Similarly, the light actuation mechanism of nickel hydroxide/oxyhydroxide was also characterized by these techniques, as well as quartz crystal microbalance. These techniques enabled the mechanisms described above to be established for each material system. As per Objective 3, we employed a multi-scale, multi-field simulation approach to model the electrochemical actuation behavior of the Ni nanohoneycomb mentioned above [paper 5]. In this approach, molecular dynamics simulations with reactive force-field potentials and a modified charge-equilibrium (QEq) method were used to calculate the surface stress built up in Ni(100) surface in contact with water electrolyte due to a voltage applied across the interface, as a result of capacitive charging of the double layer in the contacting electrolyte as well as redox reaction of the Ni surface. The calculated surface stress is then used as input in a meso-scale finite-element (FE) model to compute the actuating stress set up in a single hexagonal unit cell of the Ni nanohoneycomb structure. The single-unit actuating stress is eventually used in a continuum FE model at a larger scale, to calculate the bending of an entire bilayered cantilever which replicates experimental conditions. The actuation deflection of the bilayered nanohoneycomb nickel is predicted to be 41.4 microns at 0.43 V vs the point of zero charge (PZC), which corresponds to ~0.48 V vs saturated calomel electrode (SCE), and this is in excellent agreement with the experimental value of 45-62 microns at a similar voltage vs SCE. This is the first successful attempt to simulate the electrochemical actuation of a real-sized, nano-porous metallic structure in an electrolytic environment. In addition, the pore growth process in nanohyneycomb structure formation during anodization was modeled as a high electric-field driven process [paper 1]. A two-dimensional model for the pore growth matches well with experimental observations. As per Objective 4, we have used the best material developed, namely, the nickel hydroxide/oxyhydroxide system, to design and fabricate prototypic micro-robotic devices. Devices including walking-bot, mini-robotic arm and bio-mimicked “sensitive plant” with rapid leaf movements have been realized [paper 7].

17206114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206114.value: In this project, three types of novel oxide/metal actuators were developed: 1) Ni nanohoneycomb actuators - We synthesized metallic nickel nanohoneycombs by using a dual-template method, to result in a bi-layered cantilever structure comprising a nanohoneycomb layer of Ni backed by a solid layer of the same metal. Reversible bending of the cantilever upon cyclic potential triggering in an alkaline hydroxide electrolyte was observed and characterized [Papers 1, 3]. Furthermore, by performing anodization on purity-containing aluminium substrates, we produced a special type of nanohoneycomb template structure which contains sub-channels bridging the main honeycomb channels, and electrodeposition of Ni into such a template structure yielded a peculiar 3D nano-network structure of Ni. Such a structure was found to exhibit ultra-fast electrochemical actuation response in hydroxide environments [Paper 4]. In terms of modelling, we have employed a multi-scale, multi-field simulation approach to model the electrochemical actuation behavior of the Ni nanohoneycombs. The actuation deflection of the bilayered nanohoneycomb nickel is predicted to be in excellent agreement with the experiments [Paper 5]. 2) Gold-film actuators with nanotextured surfaces – using electroless gold plating onto substrates of porous anodized aluminum oxide (AAO), thin films of gold with a high density of short gold nanofibres were fabricated. Bending actuation of such a structure was observed in air when electrically charged by an ion generator [Paper 2]. 3) Nickel hydroxide-on-Ni actuators – we discovered a remarkable electrochemical actuation effect of Ni(OH)2/NiOOH in alkaline environment, under low voltages of less than 1 volt, due to a redox reaction accompanied by volume changes. By masked electrodeposition, actuators of various shapes and actuation performance were also demonstrated. The required electrolyte can be packaged with the actuating material to achieve a stand-alone actuating device [Paper 6]. In addition, we further demonstrate that the same material system can actuate by illumination of visible light of low intensities, due to the rapid and reversible intercalating water molecules into the material when triggered by light. By electroplating the active material on selected areas of the substrate, hinged actuators that can lift objects ~100 times of the weight of the actuating material were achieved. Other examples showing the potential use in robotic devices were demonstrated, including sunlight-induced actuation, bio-mimicked “sensitive plant” with rapid leaf movement, and light powered walking-bot. This work was published in Science Robotics, a sister journal of Science, in their special issue on “new materials, actuators, and fabrication schemes” [Paper 7].

17206114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206114.value: Materials capable of actuating intrinsically under different stimuli in a self-contained way are highly desirable for future generation micro-robots, for which traditional prime movers such as gears, pulleys, belts, or hydraulic or pneumatic systems would become too bulky to use. In fact, “new materials and fabrication schemes” have been identified as the first of ten grand challenges of robotics [Yang et al., Science Robotics 3, eaar7650 (2018)]. Out of the three types of new actuating material systems developed in this project, we find the electrochemical and light-driven actuation behaviour of the nickel hydroxide system most promising for further development. Through proper engineering, ultra-large device strains can be achieved with also high load-bearing capacities. Scientifically, this topic involves the interdisciplinary marriage of mechanics and chemistry, or “chemomechanics”. The next stage of development involves applications as well as basic science exploration. We anticipate both patents and high-impact publications as results.

17206114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206114.value: Futuristic robots may be expected to be powered by new smart materials capable of actuating in a self-contained way under different stimuli. In this project, three types of novel actuating material systems were developed, namely, nickel nanohoneycombs, gold films with nanotextured surfaces, and nickel hydroxide-on-nickel actuators. These materials are capable of undergoing significant shape or volume changes when stimulated by electrical or light signals. In cases when a liquid electrolytic is needed for the actuation, the constraint can be alleviated by designing an assembly system in which the required electrolyte is packaged, so that the entire assembly can actuate in a dry environment. In each of the materials developed, the actuation mechanism was identified by experimental characterization or multi-scale, multi-physics materials modelling. The results were published in top journals. Out of the three materials developed, the nickel hydroxide-on-nickel system has the best potential for further development in terms of applications.

17206514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206514.value: The rapid decline in the accident rate on Hong Kong construction sites stopped in 2005 and has plateaued ever since at a level of around 50 accidents per 1000 workers per annum. Such a rate is unacceptable. The industry has been grappling with the reasons for this plateau effect; there has been no shortage of site safety initiatives but it appears that the effectiveness of the initiatives is reducing. Thus, the question addressed by this research is why has safety performance plateaued and what can be done to promote a new, sustained decline in accident rates? Previously, Rowlinson et al. (2009) benchmarked performance of local contractors and concluded the majority of contractors could be classed as immature organisations in that their focus in safety management was on compliance rather than continuous improvement that was emphasised by top performing contractors. So, how can top performers kickstart further improvement? During a study of construction workers health many workers were found to have high blood pressure, high BMI and high levels of blood sugar and cholesterol. The average age of the sample was 45 years and key trades averaged 55 years. Workers generally had a low level of literacy and difficulty answering what were relatively simple questions. Two studies of safety climate highlighted the linking pin role played by subcontractors’ safety supervisors in translating the conflicting demands of production and safety to the workers. The issue of dynamic risk assessments appeared as an important communication mechanism in safety awareness. In preparing this proposal a workshop was conducted to explore the reasons why, despite a well-planned and monitored safety management system, accidents still happened on sites run by a major Hong Kong contractor. Key issues emerging were the risk-taking propensity of Hong Kong workers, the pace of construction, the payment systems (piece rate as opposed to a daily wage), subcontracting and culture (workforce risk-taking propensity and the cultural gap between managers, supervisors, and the workforce. Tangible change has taken place in procedures and systems in place on Hong Kong construction sites but intangible changes in safety climate and cultural values have not changed. This research explores the impact of safety climate, risk-taking propensity and cultural dissonance on the effective working of safety management systems in Hong Kong’s construction industry. The results have the potential to kickstart a downward trend in accident rates and enhance workers’ lifestyles and Hong Kong’s reputation. 原本快速下降的香港建築地盘事故率曲線在2005年嘎然而止，事故率曲線更加趨於平緩並在每年每千人55次安全事故的水平停滯不降。建築行業已經因為這一平台效應苦苦尋找各種原因。事實上，建築地盘並不缺乏安全創新，然而這些安全創新的效應在逐步減少。因此，本次研究將就安全改進措施的平台效應進行深入研究，並且探尋新的改善機制所需的新動力以及探討足以讓安全事故率持續下降的機制。 Rowlinson et al. (2009) 衡量了本地承建商的具體表現並且得出結論， 他認為行業的大多數可以被劃分為不成熟的組織，進而這些組織只是被動的關注安全管理措施而並非像極少數表現優異的承包商那樣持續改善組織管理水平。 在另一項建築地盘工人健康的研究調查中發現， 許多建築地盘工人遭受著高血壓，高血脂，高血糖症狀的困擾。該研究調查的主體為平均年齡為45歲的扎铁工和平均年齡為55歲的模板工人。究對象的教育程度非常低甚至不能用讀寫的形式回答一些簡單的問題。另外兩項關於安全氣候的研究指出了分包商的安全監督員在面對生產和安全相衝突的時候的重要作用。另外，動態的風險評估是一種非常重要的溝通機制。 研究還以研討會的形式探尋當前香港建築承包商為何在一個規劃完善並監督有力的安全管理機制下他們的建築地盘仍然時有安全事故發生。研討會指出這與工人的風險偏好，施工節奏與速度，付款機制（生產承包薪酬制度與工作日薪酬制度比較），工程分判以及項目經理與安全督察員的文化差異有很大關係。 在香港的建築工地可以很明顯的看到一些程序上和系統上的顯著地變化， 然而一些與安全氣候和文化價值觀的隱性因素卻沒有得到重視。本次研究將主要探索香港建造業在安全氣候，風險偏好以及文化差異方面對安全管理體系的實施效果的影響。

17206514.label: Realisation of objectives
17206514.value: Summary of Findings The 360° assessment of contractors' staff revealed a disconnect between worker and management perceptions of safety management; engagement of the workforce by management was not taking place. The assessment of the client HQ revealed significant differences in safety climate between management staff, safety advisors, professional/technical staff and administrative staff; there was no consistent organisational culture across the entreprise. The 360° assessment led to the questioning of the effectiveness of voluntary OHSW initiatives by both workers and management. Rule breaking was observed to be an everyday occurrence on the part of the workforce. The proximal cause of this was the lack of engagement of workers by management. However, through discussion and observation it was concluded that the distal causes were institutional and stemmed from cultural dissonance, power distance and pragmatism. This institutional problem surfaced as a lack of visibly felt leadership and became the focus of safety management initiatives at MTR, Work undertaken Studies accomplished are listed detailed below: Survey of major client's project and headquarters based staff, 1099 respondents, including questionnaire survey and written observations; Survey of client, contractor and subcontractor staff with 901 respondents, including questionnaire survey and verbal observations; Detailed interviews with construction management staff and workers on six sites, 42 face to face respondents and 285 questionnaire responses. Additional research undertaken that was not in the original proposal: A self report survey of alcohol consumption on a range of the client’s sites, 1203 responses; Analysis of accident records from a major client and a major contractor for the past five years – to date 75 records have been analysed out of 600 and when a larger sample size has been analysed a journal paper will be written and GRF funding will be acknowledged. Outcomes The outcome of these investigations has enabled the confirmation of: A mismatch of perceptions in terms of management and workers as to the nature of safety climate on site and the expectations of both parties; A mismatch in terms of observed action and espoused values of management that has given the perception of a lack of visibly felt safety leadership. Through a series of workshops on sites it has been determined that major issues exist and some of these, which have led to problems, are: Pace of work and the willingness of management and supervisors to turn a blind eye to unsafe behaviours; A proliferation of different rules, procedures and standards applied by different contractors, supervisors and client on the same site; A weakness in engaging the workforce in discussion and decision-making on safety procedures and work progress; The inadequacy and ineffectiveness of current safety training initiatives, particularly voluntary schemes; Weaknesses in feeding back the learnings from near miss incidents to management and workforce. The workforce was observed to be multicultural in that there are many workers from Nepal, Pakistan, Mainland China and local Hong Kong origins working together on Hong Kong construction sites. There is a substantial proportion of expatriate management staff from Europe, Australia and Southeast Asia and this is a problem in terms of communication, engagement and the display of visibly felt safety leadership. The latter is exacerbated by the fact that management staff tend to focus on their own specific competence and work tasks and do not display a general concern for the workforce and safety procedures whilst conducting their tasks around site. Indeed, the worker is rarely, if ever, engaged in discussions about work or other issues such as welfare, health and safety. This is an industry wide issue that can be addressed by bringing about a change in safety values and hence safety climate. Certain key trades were found to display poor safety culture and these included steelfixers, formworkers and general labourers. The former two trades wield a high degree of influence and power on site due to the current labour shortage and their consequent ability to command high wage rates. They are also homogeneous groups that have a strong sense of their own group identity and create serious management and supervisory problems on site. They tend to display the traits of eastern pragmatism in that they do not believe that rules are inviolable and they adapt working practices to their own priorities and management’s tight project deadlines. There was a degree of scepticism on the part of management in terms of the feedback from worker surveys. Although accepting that the climate survey had clearly identified workgroups that were not safety conscious management was unwilling to accept their complaints, observations and suggestions. This defensive attitude is natural but is one that needs to be addressed by the industry if improvement is to take place. The analysis of the accident reports indicated that the feedback from the site survey matched with the reports from the accidents whereby risk-taking was a common contributing cause of accidents for general labourers, riggers, steelbenders, carpenters and tunnel workers. Furthermore, feedback from an alcohol use survey also pinpointed steelfixers, formworkers and tunnel workers as being amongst those most at risk from alcohol consumption issues. However, an associated finding is that accident causality models used in Hong Kong are too simplistic and the data collected for accident analysis reflects this in that no distal causes are recorded and considered. Issues in conducting research Although the work has continued at a pace and has been successful in identifying key issues the work has been painstakingly labour intensive. Many of the workers, from whatever ethnic background, are poorly educated and only partly literate. Hence, the surveys had to be conducted on a face-to-face basis in many instances and researchers had to be recruited with the a range of language skills to communicate effectively with the work force. In addition, gaining the trust and cooperation of head office and site management staff was a challenging task as the research has been conducted in a period when the industry has been under intense scrutiny due to time and cost overruns. Thus, the PI is exceedingly grateful to his research team for their resilience and unflagging resolve to complete this research successfully. Conclusions Risk taking propensity is undoubtedly an issue in the Hong Kong construction industry. However, contrary to popular belief, this propensity is present in management and supervisory staff as well as frontline workers . The final period of this research project focussed on unraveling the complex set of relationships that exist on site and developing an understanding of how and why risk-taking comes about and is tolerated. This was followed by an exploration of measures that can be implemented in an attempt to help reduce this propensity. This reflective period led to the paper on Institutional environment and institutional logics and the paper on voluntary OHS initiatives, highlighting the ineffectiveness of these measures (the latter paper has been revised and resubmitted for re-review to "Safety Science") The paper on transformational leadership was developed during the site based studies of six sites where the instrument developed to measure safety climate was applied to management, supervisors, subcontractors and contractors' own staff on these sites. Parts of this work were published in conferences in Colombo and Puerto Rico in 2016 and the alcohol survey was published the following year in Colombo.

17206514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206514.value: Overview A key issue not being adequately addressed in the Hong Kong construction industry is worker engagement by management and supervisors. This issue came over very strongly in the major site survey and also on the six sites that were surveyed in detail. Risk taking propensity is undoubtedly an issue in the Hong Kong construction industry. However, contrary to popular belief, this propensity is present in management and supervisory staff as well as frontline workers . Key findings Management of safety interventions needs to be redirected from promoting safety alone to addressing the institutional issues that impede improvement. These inhibitors surface in the entire organization and are driven in part by the organisations societal context. A need to engage the multiple levels of actors both on and off site to stimulate an improvement in safety culture has emerged from this research. The results suggest that future safety climate interventions will be more effective if supervisors exhibit transformational leadership, encourage construction personnel to voice safety concerns without fear of retaliation, and repeatedly remind all employees about good safety practices on the job. In short, the workforce must be engaged by management and supervisors. The major weaknesses in safety climate surfaced in the following indicators: work procedures for safety, safety compliance, work pressure over safety priority, safety cooperation and involvement, safety communication and appreciation of risk. Conflicting safety rules and inadequate training were commonly identified issues by the workforce. Our results results showed that 17% of workers drink excessively, and 28% drink in a harmful way. The consequences of these figures are obvious in the same way that the consequences of drink driving are inevitable; more accidents and incidents will take place. Mechanics, welders, shot firers and miners were found to be high risk groups, as were certain ethnic groups. The safety climate instrument was presented to the cooperating client along with statistical analysis software to be used as an ongoing, annual survey in order to monitor change and improvement. This is now being implemented at two levels: at individual site level to pinpoint areas that need management and supervisory attention; at corporate level to feedback information to senior management in order to set stretch safety targets and to devise new safety initiatives that are targeted at identified weaknesses.

17206514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206514.value: There is still scope to publish at least two more journal papers based on this research, one being an overview of the whole range of OHSW issues and the other focussing on the different nature of risk taking propensity in Hong Kong compared with Malaysia. This is a comparative study that arose through liaison with a PhD graduate now working in Malaysia and the data for this study (not included in the original proposal) are currently being analysed by an existing part time PhD student. The data from the client accident records (sample of 750 out of 7497 recorded accidents) were used by a BSc student to produce a dissertation on falls from height and are still being analysed for other accident types. Again, this was not part of the original proposal but when the data became available the research team took the opportunity to use this for further, complementary research and the GRF will be acknowledged when these papers are published and presented. PI has just received joint funding with UCL, through the HKU-UCL Strategic Partnership Fund, to conduct a comparative study of Hong Kong and UK OHSW environments based on this research.

17206514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206514.value: Construction is a dirty, demanding and dangerous job. The accident rate in the construction industry is unacceptably high. This research has investigated the problems that exist in the management of occupational health, safety and welfare in the construction industry. Among the issues that emerged is the lack of engagement of front line workers by management and supervisors. Workers are not asked to participate in discussion about working methods and safety practices. They are told what to do and often believe that there are safer and quicker methods of working that they could use but are not allowed to do so. A major change of attitude by employers is needed to improve this situation. Furthermore, there is a mismatch of safety cultures within major client organisations that hampers an integrated approach to safety management. Poorly devised, often voluntary, safety initiatives are a reflection of this mismatch and are ineffective and divert attention from the major issues. The institutional drivers for change are weak and focus on legislation and punishment rather than systematic, well thought out and integrated safety initiatives. There is an urgent need for improvement in worker engagement by management and supervisors to drive a radical improvement in safety climate on site.

17206714.label: Project Objectives
17206714.value: The main project purpose is to reveal the key mechanisms of initiating the speciation of lead in glass-ceramic matrices. By sintering lead compounds with different precursors under various thermal conditions, the incorporation and recrystallization of lead species in glass-ceramic matrices will be clearly identified by X-ray diffraction, electron diffraction, and electron microscopy results. The evolutionary processes of different lead hosting phases and their configuration features will be precisely delineated across different composition, temperature, and time ranges. Our expertise in quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis (Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through internal standards) will then report the quantities of lead hosting phases in products through high resolution X-ray diffraction data. An amorphous content quantification protocol employing a commonly available calcium fluoride internal standard will be also conducted to assist in the development of a reliable quantification method for the amorphous content. Crystalline characteristics (lattice parameters, cation distribution, crystal size, etc.) of lead hosting phases generated from the glass-ceramic matrix will be also obtained by Rietveld analysis to evaluate the quality of the metal stabilization. The effects of precursor composition and thermal conditions will also be systematically evaluated by monitoring the responses of crystal characteristics to provide direct evidence of the changes in the metal coordination structures. The lead stabilization effects in different aqueous environments will be examined by leaching experiments at constant pH (ranging from 2-12), and surface-sensitive characterization tools, e.g., X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and atomic force microscopy (AFM), will be used to elucidate the metal leaching behavior on product surfaces. These results can assist in the product design for either reduced (for metal stabilization) or enhanced (for metal recovery) metal leachability. Based on the mechanistic understanding of lead incorporation into glass-ceramics, the influences of operational parameters, such as sample preparation and compositional design, will be delineated to provide an effective control on the reactive metallic lead crystallization and viscous sintering processes. Such understanding is crucial to determining the nano- and micro-structural features in final products and is also a necessity for developing safe and reliable metal stabilization and recovery strategies.

17206714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206714.value: Lead (Pb) is an important and widely used industrial material, due to its versatile physical and chemical characteristics. However, Pb-containing waste causes significant environmental concern owing to its toxic and non-biodegradable nature. The use of well-stabilized forms of lead in industrial products can prevent the loss of this metal, which would both maintain product functionality and minimize toxic waste generation. The form of the metal in the waste matrix also highly influences the recovery potential and process design. A glass-ceramic matrix has amorphous (glass) and crystalline (ceramic) phases coexisting in a system and is commonly encountered in natural and engineered materials. The understanding and control of metal speciation mechanisms in glass-ceramic matrices are crucial to the effective stabilization of metals in industrial products and to their recovery from waste streams. Potential applications of the speciation mechanisms include the safe incorporation of waste sludge/ash into the fabrication of eco-ceramics, the recovery of metals from waste electrical and electronic equipment parts, new thermal treatment methods for metal-contaminated soils at temperatures much lower than that of vitrification, and the development of new multiple-metal loaded catalysts or composite materials with different combinations of oxide matrices. Most metal speciation studies of solids focus on the reaction mechanisms in either crystalline phases or glass form, but recent reports have suggested a new strategy of synergistically using glass-ceramic matrices to create different metal hosting sites and stabilization mechanisms in the system. This project aims to identify and control the key mechanisms of incorporating and extracting lead by glass-ceramic matrix. The generated lead-bearing phases will be systematically quantified to obtain the optimized incorporation and extraction processing parameters. Experimental activities will start by calcining the lead compounds with the most commonly available silicon-, aluminum-, iron-, and titanium-based oxide precursors for glass-ceramic products. The high resolution X-ray diffraction technique will then be performed on the calcined samples, and a state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification will be implemented to quantify different lead phases and their crystalline parameters. By identifying the lead incorporation features and evaluating the metal leachability of product phases, the hosting characteristics of lead by different glass-ceramic matrices will be further examined. Finally, the reactive crystallization and viscous sintering behavior of glass-ceramic products under a variety of thermal conditions will allow the design of a variety of nano- and micro-structural features to facilitate reliable stabilization and efficient recovery strategies for minimizing the lead hazard. 廣泛存在工業製程中的鉛可以不同的物化型式造成對環境污染的威脅. 然而適當控制鉛的礦物相可充份利用其功能特性, 亦可減低其環境危害風險. 本研究期利用鉛於玻璃陶瓷基質中的不同賦存性質, 以達到有效控制其金屬穩定性與增加其回收性的目地. 此關鍵技術的應用可於無害化金屬污泥與灰等廢棄物質, 以其機理創造出環保安全的產品達到維繫降低環境污染並創造價值的目地. 對於金屬賦存機制的研究, 本計劃將聯合以玻璃陶與瓷基的複合基質手段來達到鉛離子賦存機制的調控. 實驗工作的內容將包含利用矽, 鋁, 鐵, 鈦等氧化物的基底系統以進行鉛離子的結合機制研究. 高質量之X光繞射技術與資料將輔助晶體結構的解析工作. 配合本工作團隊歷年來累積之世界頂尖X光繞射定量相分析技術, 鉛離子於各晶體結構與玻璃基質的賦存量將被精確的報導與調控. 希望藉由一系列的實驗與最佳化設計, 本計劃將可發展出多種微米與納米結構材料以有效穩定鉛的化性與實踐資源回收的目地.

17206714.label: Realisation of objectives
17206714.value: The understanding and control of metal speciation mechanisms in the glass-ceramic matrix are crucial to effectively stabilize metals in the products and to remove pollutants in the waste streams. We have confirmed the benefits of using the glass-ceramic matrix to create different metal hosting sites and stabilization mechanisms. In this project work, we sintered lead and the other metal oxides with different ceramic precursors under the thermal conditions of producing glass-ceramics. The incorporation and recrystallization of lead and the other metal species in these products were already identified by X-ray diffraction, electron diffraction, and electron microscopy techniques. The protocols of quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis (Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through internal standards) were successfully established to report the quantities of hosting phases for different metals in products. Crystalline characteristics in samples are monitored for the glass-ceramic matrix via Rietveld analysis. The effects of precursor composition and thermal conditions were observed through the metal stabilization results. Such results also provide a good opportunity to discuss with the observed crystal characteristics and to explore the particular product functional mechanisms. In the process of pursuing safe and reliable products, the leaching experiments were used to observe the stabilization effects of lead and the other metals in the products. In this study, the constant pH leaching experiment protocol was developed to more meaningfully compare the metal leachability. The surface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy were also employed to observe the changes of product surfaces to explain the metal leaching behavior. The findings contributing to the optimized design for metal stabilization or metal recovery were discussed according to the used processing parameters. Overall, the mechanisms triggering evolutionary processes of different metal hosting phases and their configuration features have found across different composition, temperature, and time ranges. These incorporation mechanisms were found to be largely controlled by the processing parameters in sample preparation and compositional design. The nano- and micro-structural features in final products were also observed by electronic microscopes. The stabilized metals in these glass-ceramic matrices are proven to be beneficial in many applications, such as for stabilization purposes, environmental treatment uses, and electrochemical functions. The promising findings from these reactive crystallization and sintering processes can further facilitate different product designs in the environmental industries.
