17206714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206714.value: This project has generated substantial details in explaining how different types of metal oxides systems can be generated to host lead and hazardous metals, together with their reliable product applications. For example, a promising strategy for the detoxification and immobilization of metals can be achieved with the glass-ceramic matrix. Using Rietveld quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis, the crystal phase contents and the metal distribution in the final products can be identified. The leaching performance of the stabilized products needs to be evaluated in a prolonged acid-leaching test to distinguish the superiority of the stabilized products in the glass-ceramic matrix. It is promising to see a range of affordable additives can reliably immobilize the hazardous metals in the glass-ceramic matrix for safe disposal. PbO was used to simulate the lead-laden sludge fired with gamma-Al2O3 by Pb/Al molar ratios of 1/2 and 1/12 at 600-1000 C for 0.25-10 h. The sintered products were identified and quantified using Rietveld refinement analysis of X-ray diffraction data from the products generated under different conditions. The results indicated that the different crystallochemical incorporations of hazardous lead occurred through the formation of PbAl2O4 and PbAl12O19 in systems with Pb/Al ratios of 1/2 and 1/12, respectively. Our incorporation experiment also shows that introduction of CaCO3 facilitated the breakage of strongly connected bonds between O-Si-O and Pb-O, which were firmly linked in the glass network. The X-ray diffraction results demonstrate that 30 wt % CaCO3 loading effectively facilitated the transformation of Pb in the glass phase to the stable PbFe12O19 phase. We have also developed a hydrometallurgical process to recover submicron lead oxide (PbO) particles from the waste lead paste. The final product was identified as orthorhombic beta-PbO, with an average size of about 200 nm. Heat treating at 550C for 3 h with the PVP/Pb(CH3COO)2 precursor at a molar ratio of 2.0, was identified as the critical procedure for forming pure submicron beta-PbO via the thermal decomposition of lead acetate to reach the lead recovery goal.

17206714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206714.value: The leachability data indicated that the incorporation of lead into PbAl12O19 crystal is a preferred stabilization mechanism in aluminate-ceramics. Although a leaching test demonstrated the superiority of Pb9Al8O21, PbAl2O4, and PbAl12O19 over PbO in resisting acidic attack, PbAl12O19 is still considered to be the ideal structure for hosting lead. This finding is crucial for product design, and the technique on how to produce this preferred phase in the industrial-scale operation may need further development. Also, this study demonstrates an alternative method of regenerating ultrafine PbO particles from the spent lead paste with high electrochemical performance, but further incorporation of this waste-derived material reliably and consistently into the actual energy-storage products may warrant a further investigation.

17206714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206714.value: Lead and other heavy metals are widely used in industry and consumer products. However, after their service period, the disposal of them causes significant environmental concern owing to its toxic and non-biodegradable nature. The use of well-stabilized forms of metals in industrial products can prevent the loss of this metal and minimize toxic waste generation. A glass-ceramic matrix has amorphous (glass) and crystalline (ceramic) phases coexisting in a system and is commonly encountered in natural and engineered materials. The understanding and control of metal speciation mechanisms in glass-ceramic matrices are crucial to the effective stabilization of metals in industrial products and their recovery from waste streams. This study generated substantial details in explaining how different types of glass-ceramic matrices can be generated to host lead and the other hazardous metals, together with their reliable product applications. For example, lead-laden waste can be fired with alumina precursor to form stable lead-containing structures. Moreover, the recovery of lead from spent lead paste to generate ultrafine PbO particles with a high electrochemical performance was successfully demonstrated. Other environmental treatments and energy applications relevant to the environmental materials techniques used in this study were also reported.

17206914.value: 市场作价中定价与库存的协调问题研究

17206914.label: Project Objectives

17206914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206914.value: Market makers assume the role of counterparty in the financial transactions with their clients. They sell to the clients at a higher ask price and buy from the clients at a lower bid price, and hence benefit from selling high and buying low. However, the market makers have the obligation to trade with the clients at the quoted bid/ask prices. Therefore, when the buying and selling orders from the clients are not balanced, they have to hold positions in the financial products they are responsible for. These positions could be undesirable because their market values fluctuate over time. The market makers should adjust the inventory positions to a more advantageous level so as to reduce the inventory risk or to improve the profit brought by the positions. This adjustment could be achieved by both quoting bid/ask prices favoring trade orders in one direction and actively trading with other market makers. This project studies how a market maker should simultaneously optimize the bid/ask prices and the active trades with other market makers. We consider dynamic programming formulations where the market maker could manage a single financial product or multiple products. Three models are proposed to reflect different risk attitudes of the market maker, namely, when he or she is risk neutral, has an exponential utility function, or optimizes a tradeoff between the expectation and variance of the profit. An extension is also considered to capture that the decisions of the market maker may have an impact on the market values of the financial products. One focus of this project is to characterize the optimal inventory policy for each of these models, i.e., how to actively trade with other market makers, and to explore how the optimal bid/ask prices and spreads depend on the inventory positions and the market prices. These structural properties will provide valuable managerial insights for market makers. We will also analyze the benefits of jointly optimizing the inventory and pricing decisions, which answers when the market makers should consider both inventory-dependent pricing and active trading with other market makers. Based on the structural properties of the optimal inventory and pricing policy, we aim to construct efficient algorithms to compute the optimal decisions numerically. Close-to-optimal approximation algorithms will also be developed for problems with multiple financial products so as to obtain practical solutions in daily operations. 市场作价者，即做市商，在与他们的客户交易时充当交易对手。他们以较高的卖出价将金融产品出售给客户，并以较低的买入价向客户购买这些产品，因高价卖出、低价买入而获利。然而，一旦做市商向客户提供了买入卖出价，他们就有义务按报价与客户交易。因此，当做市商收到的买单和卖单不能彼此抵消的时候，他们必将持有一定数量的金融产品。由于产品的价格随时间波动，这些仓位可能对做市商不利。做市商需要将仓位调整到更有利的水平，从而降低风险或增加因持仓而带来的利润。调整仓位的手段包括通过报价来吸引更多的买单或卖单，以及主动与其他做市商进行交易。 该项目旨在研究做市商应如何同时优化对客户的报价以及与其他做市商的交易量。我们就做市商可以管理单个或多个金融产品的情况，用动态规划进行建模。采用风险中性、指数效用函数、及期望方差间的权衡三种模型，来反映做市商不同的风险态度。并考虑做市商的决定可能对金融产品的市场价值产生影响。 该项目的重点之一是刻画上述模型的最优库存策略，即如何与其他做市商进行主动交易，并探讨如何根据仓位和市价来优化买入卖出价及其价差。这些结构性的理论结果将为做市商提供重要的管理启示。我们还将分析联合优化定价与库存策略所带来的益处，从而了解在什么情况下做市商应该同时考虑基于仓位的定价和与其他做市商的主动交易。 通过对最优库存和定价策略的结构性分析，我们将设计高效的算法来计算最优决策。并就多个金融产品的问题，开发接近最优的近似算法，以获得在日常运营中切实可行的方案。

17206914.label: Realisation of objectives
17206914.value: This project has led to 2 papers published in Production and Operations Management (Lu et al. 2018 and Hu et al. 2019), 4 presentations in international conferences, and 1 seminar talk at the University of Science and Technology of China. Furthermore, we are preparing the following working paper, which will be soon submitted for peer review at Production and Operations Management: Simchi-Levi, D. and M. Song. 2019. Coordinated pricing and inventory decisions in market-making. Working paper. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: 1. Formulation: This problem considers a market maker who quotes a pair of bid and ask prices for each of the financial products s/he is responsible for. If a client would like to buy the financial product at the ask price or sell at the bid price, the market maker has the obligation to serve as the counterparty in this transaction. Through this process, the market maker gains the bid/ask spread, i.e., the difference between the bid and ask prices s/he quotes. As the buying and selling orders from clients may not be balanced, the market maker may need to carry positions of the financial product, which can result in either profit or loss as the market price of the financial product fluctuates. It has been observed that market makers actively trade with each other so as to adjust their positions to more desirable levels at the cost of paying the bid/ask spreads to other market makers. The research question is which bid and ask prices the market maker should quote (pricing decision) and how many units of the products s/he should actively sell to or buy from other market maker (inventory decision). In this project, we propose a dynamic programming model over a finite planning horizon to optimize these decisions. For the risk-neutral model, the objective is to maximize the expected total profit of the market maker during the given planning horizon, including the spread gain from trading with clients, the spread loss from trading with other market makers, and the profit or loss from market price changes. Two risk-averse models, i.e., the exponential utility model and the mean-variance model, are also proposed to capture the fact that the decision maker could be risk-averse. The exponential utility model assumes that the decision maker has an exponential utility function and targets to maximize the expected total utility throughout the planning horizon. The mean-variance model then considers the case that the decision maker cares about a linear trade-off between the expectation and variance of the profit in each period. For both risk-averse models, the objective functions ensure that we can obtain the corresponding Bellman equations so as to solve the dynamic programs recursively. In practice, a market maker may manage multiple financial products. The price movements of these products can be correlated. The clients’ decisions on whether to trade one product may depend on the prices of other products. The multi-product models are constructed to capture these considerations. We also study the single-product models, which yield sharper results on the structural properties of the optimal policy. 2. Optimal Policy: For ease of analysis, the bid and ask prices quoted in each period are equivalently translated to the decisions on the expected amount of buying and selling orders (demand and supply) from clients. We first identify the conditions under which the Bellman equation for each period solves a convex optimization problem. The objective function can then be separated into two terms. One only depends on the inventory decision. The other depends on the inventory decision only through the inventory position after actively trading with other market makers. Utilizing this property, we show that there exists a well-structured optimal inventory policy, which is elaborated in Section 6.1. We further identify conditions under which the inventory policy is symmetric with respect to 0. How the inventory policy changes with respect to various model inputs, such as the spread quoted by other market makers, the market price, and the risk-aversion parameter, are also studied both analytically and numerically. The analysis of the optimal pricing policy mainly focuses on how the optimal expected demand and supply from clients change with respect to the inventory position after actively trading with other market makers. Given the optimal inventory policy and the specific forms of how the quoted bid/ask prices determine the expected supply and demand, these results immediately yield how the optimal prices and spread depend on the initial inventory level. For the risk-neutral and mean-variance models, we use the concavity and separablity of the objective function to characterize the pricing policy. For the exponential utility model, the analysis is conducted based on the concavity, log-supermoduarity, and log-submodularity of the objective function. Numerical studies are used to shed lights on how the optimal pricing policy changes with respected to other model inputs. 3. Solution Algorithm: A computationally tractable algorithm is proposed to solve the dynamic programming models based on the structural property of the optimal inventory policy. For each period, this algorithm can avoid solving the Bellman equation for each initial inventory position and hence reduces the number of dimensions for the dynamic programs. We also analyze the conditions under which the state space can be reduced, which further improves the efficiency of the algorithm. The symmetric and monotonic properties of the optimal policies are applied to speed up the algorithm as well. Extensive numerical studies have been conducted to show that the proposed algorithm is capable of solving practical-scale problems efficiently. Furthermore, we propose heuristic algorithms by approximating the value functions (see Lu et al. 2018) and applying decision rules to the pricing decisions (see an earlier version of Hu et al. 2019). They obtain policies that are more insightful and hence easier to be implemented in practice. Extensive numerical experiments have been conducted to validate their efficiency and effectiveness. 4. Extension with Market Impact: This extension considers the case that the inventory and pricing decisions of the market maker may have impact on the future price movements of the financial products. For this purpose, we propose dynamic programming models where the unit profit/loss of carrying inventory from one period to the next and the market price in the next period both depend on the inventory and pricing decisions of the current period. The analysis of the optimal policy focuses on identifying the conditions under which the optimal policy shares the same structure as the counterpart without considering market impact. The solution algorithms are also extended so that they can be applied to the models with market impact.

17206914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206914.value: This project has generated 2 papers published in Production and Operations Management, 4 conference presentations, and 1 seminar talk. One working paper will be soon submitted for publication. The major findings of the project are summarized as follows: - Optimal Inventory Policy (see Simchi-Levi and Song 2019). Under general conditions, we can show that the following inventory policy is optimal: (i) For any period, given the mid prices and the market spreads of all the financial products, there exists a simply connected no-trade region, which, for each product, is defined by an interval bounded by two threshold functions, such that it is optimal not to actively trade with other market makers if the inventory position of the products falls in this region. (ii) If the inventory position of the products is not in the no-trade region, then only two types of inventory adjustment can be optimal. One is to increase the inventory of a product by actively trading with other market makers until it hits the lower threshold function of this product on the boundary of the no-trade region. The other is to decrease the inventory of a product by actively trading with other market makers until it hits the upper threshold function of this product on the boundary of the no-trade region. We have also identified conditions under which the no-trade region is symmetric with respect to the origin, independent of the mid prices and spreads, and monotonic with respect to the mid prices, spreads, and risk-aversion parameters, respectively. - Optimal Pricing Policy (see Simchi-Levi and Song 2019). For the risk-neutral and mean-variance models, under mild conditions, we can show that the optimal expected supply (resp., demand) decreases (resp., increases) in the inventory level after actively trading with other market makers. Furthermore, the expected inventory level after trading with both clients and other market makers increases in the inventory level after trading with other market makers. For the exponential utility model, we have identified conditions under which the above pricing policy remains optimal. Under more general conditions, it is proved that either the optimal expected supply is lower or the optimal expected demand is higher when we have higher inventory level after trading with other market markers. - Solution Algorithms (see Simchi-Levi and Song 2019, Lu et al. 2018, and Hu et al. 2019) We have developed efficient exact algorithms and strongly performing heuristics for the dynamic programs.

17206914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206914.value: As our problem determines the amount of each financial product to buy from or sell to other market makers, we can obtain a multi-period portfolio optimization model with transaction costs by removing the pricing decisions and ignoring the profits generated by market making in the objective function. In this case, we can incorporate more sophisticated risk measures to better model the trade-off between risk and return. Robust optimization techniques can also be applied to resolve the ambiguity in the distribution of future prices. Furthermore, we note that the proposed model in principle treats the market prices of the financial products as exogenous variables. It has been observed that a few large players dominate the market for certain financial products. To study the optimal decisions of the dominant players, it should be more appropriate to endogenize the market prices. In particular, we can consider a market mechanism that determines the future prices based on the current decisions of the dominant players and the responses from their clients. This study can lead to important insights on market price evolvement, which we leave for future research.

17206914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206914.value: Market makers quote bid and ask prices for the financial products they are responsible for. Given these prices, they have the obligation to sell to (resp., buy from) their clients at the ask (resp., bid) price as long as the clients would like to trade. Since the buying and selling orders from the clients may not be balanced, market makers often need to hold positions of the financial products, which are subject to market value fluctuations. In order to reduce the inventory risk or to improve the profit brought by the positions, they could adjust the inventory positions by both quoting bid/ask prices favoring trade orders in one direction and actively trading with other market makers. This project studies how to optimally make these pricing and trading decisions simultaneously. Dynamic programming models considering different risk attitudes are proposed for this problem in both single- and multi-product settings. We characterize the corresponding optimal policies to deliver managerial insights for industrial practitioners. Numerical algorithms are developed to compute numerical solutions efficiently. An extension is also studied for the case that the decisions of a market maker can have an impact on the future price movements of the financial products.

17207114.value: 近年來，醫用納米機器人的研究在新型的醫療保健應用中發揮著重要的作用。當機器人達到納米尺度時，機器人系統和顯影劑變得很小。早期的檢測方法，無創成像，追踪在身體裡面的納米尺度的物體變得非常重要，特別是藥物傳輸和醫用納米機器人。由於外加磁場的作用，納米機器人將會與外加磁場的梯度方向相反。因此，納米機器人的全波特性和場檢測在追踪和控制納米機器人非常重要。 因為皮膚組織可以近似看作分層的環境，非均勻的最有效的模型之一是局部平面分層介質模型。然而，訪問納米尺度物體包含多尺度和大尺度問題同時存在與在正逆計算中。目前分層介質格林函數的積分方程的效率仍然存在問題。 在過去的十年裡，針對實際問題的全波積分方程的快速求解器得到了很好的發展，電磁逆散射應用到很多領域，例如：遙感，醫療成像，地球物理問題。然而，求解三維醫用納米機器人的仿真問題，以下的困難必須解決：1）效率地求解分層介質格林函數的矢量積分方程的 2）在反演方法中用分層介質格林函數替換自由空間或者半空間格林函數 3）優化掃描頻率納米尺度物體的分辨率。 因此，我们需要研究 1）有效的預條件系統针对分析分層介質中的金屬和介質體 2）微和納米尺度場特徵的精確工具，求解多尺度和大尺度問題的分層介質格林函數的求解器 3）納米尺度的電磁逆散射。需要仔細的選擇和優化非線性反演方法，以獲得掃描頻率範圍和高分辨率圖像。 由於本方法的一般性，綜合正逆散射的物理現象，醫學應用中的分層介質中高​​精度納米尺度的計算，它不同與以前的方法。我們的長期目標是發展一種針對電磁與生物醫學共同的快速有效的數值求解器。

17207114.label: Realisation of objectives
17207114.value: For Deliver No. 2, to develop a Calderon preconditioner for the analysis of electromagnetic scattering with a layered medium, first a Calderón preconditioner is developed for the analysis of electromagnetic scattering of perfect electrically conducting (PEC) objects embedded in a layered medium. The electric field integral equation (EFIE) is formulated with the kernel of layered medium Green’s function to account for the effects from the multilayered background. The Calderón projector is derived based on the general source-field relationship and the extinction theorem for inhomogeneous environment in electromagnetic theory. The Calderón identities can be naturally deduced based on this projector, which is then leveraged to precondition the EFIE with layered kernel. An alternative implementation is then proposed to make the implementation of the preconditioner as efficient as the one in free space. Different numerical examples are designed to show the performance of the preconditioner, where the objects are located in different positions with respect to the layered medium, or different types of excitation are adopted. It is shown that the proposed effective and robust preconditioner makes the EFIE system converge rapidly in all cases, independent of the discretization density. Then we studied Calderón preconditioners for analyzing electromagnetic scattering by penetrable objects in a layered medium. To account for the scattering effects of the multilayered background, the layered medium Green’s function is adopted in the Poggio–Miller–Chang–Harrington–Wu–Tsai (PMCHWT) method. However, similar to the free-space case, the spectrum of the resulting equation is undesirable. This leads to a slow convergence of an iterative solver, especially when the geometry is densely meshed. To improve the convergence, a highly effective preconditioner is proposed. Different from its free-space counterpart, the preconditioning operator is constructed based on the Calderón identities for inhomogeneous medium. To reduce the relatively high construction cost of the preconditioning operator, several alternative simplified schemes are proposed and analyzed. Finally, the performances of different preconditioners are examined and compared carefully. It is shown that the convergence of the PMCHWT system in a layered medium can be significantly improved by using the proposed Calderón preconditioners. For Deliver No. 1 and No. 3, to study and improve the accuracy of the integral equation solver with layered medium Green’s function,and to study the nonlinear inversion algorithms for electromagnetic imaging for medical nanobots inside human body, a new hierarchical algorithm based on surface equivalence principle is proposed. The equivalent sources residing on relaxed spherical equivalence surfaces are computed by closed-form integral operators rather than numerical approximations. Consequently, a hierarchical algorithm based on oct-tree is straightforward to implement. Numerical examples validate the accuracy and capability of the proposed algorithm. Consequently this approxch is applied in the inverse process in sensing of random discrete medium embedded with irregular shape of scatterers, which is a similar senario to the layered human body. Radiative Transfer (RT) theoretical modeling is applied through the Hierarchical Equivalent Source Algorithm (HESA) to compute scattered fields based on hierarchically structured equivalence sources residing within relaxed spherical equivalence surfaces. The 3D scatterer model used in HESA can be created using a 3D modeling software. After the 3D scatterer model is divided into smaller groups and each group is enclosed with a spherical equivalence surface, the scattered fields can be computed by equivalence source residing on smooth spherical equivalence surface through integral formulations. By incorporating HESA method into the current RT theoretical modeling, this can provide the improved theoretical model the capability to compute scattering of irregular or non-basic shape of scatterers embedded within the medium. The simulated scattering coefficient and extinction coefficient results from the newly implemented HESA based theoretical model were compared with those of current RT theoretical model and it was found that both results agreed with each other. The new model is then ready to be applied to simulate backscattering from a layer of medium for further theoretical analysis. The mixed-form fast multipole algorithm (MF-FMA) with feasible error controllability is further studied through high-order multipole rotation that can make the translation matrices very sparse. The saving of both storage and CPU time makes it attainable to increase the number of harmonics in the middle frequency regime, thus shifting up the transition region of MF-FMA. Consequently, the broadband accuracy of the MF-FMA can be improved significantly. To further enhance the nonlinear simulatiom capability of integral equations, we developed the PMCHWT based Second-harmonic (SH) generation simulation method, which is tremendously important for nonlinear sensing, microscopy and communication system. By using the resultant method, we were able to harness plasmonic hybridization mechanism together with a special selection rule governing the SH radiation to achieve the high-intensity and tunable-direction emission by a metallic particle-in-cavity nanoantenna (PIC-NA). The nanoantenna is modelled with a first-principle, self-consistent boundary element method, which considers the depletion of pump waves. Then a study of the right-hand side effect for an iterative solver is further persued. The right-hand side determines whether a mode can be excited under certain excitation. Based on the matrix equation system A· x = b, different formulations are discussed including the electric field integral equation (EFIE), Calder´on preconditioned EFIE with electroquasi-static problems, and the magnetic integral equation (MFIE) with magneto-quasi-static problems. Our detailed spectral analysis shows the importance of the weighted right-hand side effect in both the convergence and accuracy of iterative system.

17207114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207114.value: In this project, the following novel computational electromagnetic algorithms are developed: Calderón preconditioners for analyzing electromagnetic scattering by both PEC and penetrable objects in a layered medium are studied and developed. The layered medium Green’s function is adopted in the Poggio–Miller–Chang–Harrington–Wu–Tsai (PMCHWT) method to account for the scattering effects of the multilayered background. To avoid the slow convergence of an iterative solver, a highly effective preconditioner is proposed. To reduce the relatively high construction cost of the preconditioning operator, several alternative simplified schemes are proposed and analyzed. It is shown that the convergence of the resultant PMCHWT system in a layered medium can be significantly improved by using the proposed Calderón preconditioners. Then to improve the accuracy of the needed integral equation and handle the nonlinearity, a new hierarchical algorithm based on surface equivalence principle is proposed. The equivalent sources residing on relaxed spherical equivalence surfaces are computed by closed-form integral operators rather than numerical approximations. Consequently, a hierarchical algorithm based on oct-tree is straightforward to implement. Numerical examples validate the accuracy and capability of the proposed algorithm. It is further dintegrated with the radiative transfer (RT) theoretical modeling method to handle the inverse process in sensing of random discrete medium embedded with irregular shape of scatterers, which is a similar senario to the layered human body. It makes it convenient to simulate the backscattering from a layer of medium. Relevant nonlinear integral equation method, MF-FMA with the high-order multipole rotations, and iterative process in integral equations are also studied for the objectives. The above mentioned new methods have been developed, presented, and published.

17207114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207114.value: Because nanobots are of known shape and basic features to the detection, prior knowledge could be used to provide initiations in the algorithms. Also because they could be active radiator, its location could be found through phase detections. Therefore a new set of methods could be developed for certain specific objects. This could be an interesting point to be developed in the future.

17207114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207114.value: The early detection, noninvasive imaging, and tracking of these nanometer-sized objects inside human body become increasingly important, especially for drug delivery and medical nanobots. Full-wave characterization of the burried objects in layered medium and field detection are critical to applications and very challenging in practice. The efficiency of the integral-equation-based solver with layered medium Green’s function is still in question. In this work, we developed the first Calderón preconditioner to analyze the electromagnetic scattering of conducting and dielectric objects embedded in a layered medium. The solver with layered-medium Green’s function is carefully studied to solve the multiscale and large-scale problems. Different accelerated forward and nonlinear inversion algorithms are carefully selected and optimized to optimize both convergence and accuracy. Several new algorithms have been developed and published for the methoed objectives. It is our long term goal to develop fast and efficient numerical solvers for applied electromagnetics in various areas.

17207214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207214.value: This project will develop a probabilistic cell transmission model (PCTM) for modeling network traffic propagation and determining the mean and variance of traffic travel time under the uncertainties of the fundamental diagram (FD) parameters. The traffic propagation will be modeled over the proposed space-time expanded cell network. The mean and variance of traffic travel time over the network will be determined using the probabilistic dynamic programming technique. The properties and accuracy of the PCTM will be analyzed theoretically and numerically. An empirical study will be carried out to calibrate and validate the PCTM. Based upon the PCTM, this project will develop a path-based variational inequality (VI) model for formulating a simultaneous route and departure time choice problem. The VI model will be formulated based on the reliability-based extension of the ideal dynamic user optimal principle, which specifies that the criterion for travelers to select their route and departure time is the effective generalized travel cost. The effective generalized travel cost will be defined based on the mean variance approach. The properties of the VI model will be examined. A hybridized solution method will be proposed to solve the model. The hybridized solution method will consist of the extragradient method, a proposed adaptive cell length strategy, and the column generation technique. The extragradient method will make use of the decomposition property of the constraint set, and will be convergent if the travel cost functions are pseudomonotone and Lipschitz continuous. The Lipschitz constant of the travel cost functions will not need to be known in advance. The adaptive cell length strategy will allow longer cell lengths to be used in earlier iterations to speed up the computation, and shorter cell lengths to be used in later iterations to achieve the required accuracy. The column generation technique will be used to generate paths if necessary. Computational experiments will be performed to illustrate the convergence and efficiency of the solution method and the importance of capturing the uncertainties of the FD parameters in the VI model for traffic control and transportation planning.

17207214.label: Realisation of objectives
17207214.value: To propose and examine a stochastic traffic flow model, a deterministic version of the proposed traffic flow model was first developed [J5]. The traffic flow model was developed based on link-based traffic flow model rather than the cell transmission model (CTM) as the recent literature has pointed out that the link-based version is more computationally efficient. The solution properties of the proposed traffic flow model, including existence and well-posedness, were examined. The computation efficiency of the traffic flow model was analyzed using various networks and random demand levels [J5]. The analysis helped the PI to develop the stochastic version of the traffic flow model. Then a stochastic version was developed based on Monte Carlo simulation technique and a modified sampling technique [J6, C2]. The Monte Carlo technique was used because it can deal with general fundamental diagrams. The computation efficiency of this stochastic version was examined by integrating it into an SRD model [J6, C2]. The proposed stochastic traffic flow model is actually better than the PCTM originally proposed by the project (and stated in objective (1)) in terms of computational efficiency and the ability to capture general fundamental diagrams. To achieve objective (2), various deterministic versions of simultaneous route and departure time choice (SRD) problems were formulated as differential variational inequalities and variational inequalities [J3-J4], and systems of nonlinear equations [J1-J2, C1]. Although these formulations are shown to be equivalent mathematically, they lead to different solution approaches to solving these SRD problems, which is the third objective of this project. The properties of these SRD problems, including solution existence, the monotonicity of cost function, etc. were analyzed [J1-J4]. The resultant formulations and analysis helped the PI to develop an SRD model that captures the proposed stochastic traffic flow model. Eventually, the variational inequality formulation was used to develop the SRD model that encapsulates the stochastic traffic flow model [J6, C2]. The SRD model was analyzed and different paradoxical phenomena were demonstrated using numerical examples [J6, C2]. To achieve objective (3), two main solution approaches were proposed to solve various SRD problems. The first approach is to formulate the SRD models directly using the techniques developed for differential variational inequalities, variational inequalities, and fixed point problems [J3-J4] such as the route swapping algorithm and extragradient method. The second approach is to solve an SRD problem by decomposing it into a master problem and the route choice subproblem [J1-J2, C1]. The master problem is solved by the backtracking inexact Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (BFGS) method. The subproblem is solved by the extragradient method or the self-regulated averaging method. The convergence conditions of the two main solution approaches were examined and discussed [J1-J4, C1]. The performance of the computational techniques in terms of efficiency and accuracy were compared with the existing solution methods [J1-J4, C1]. Finally, based on the results of the comparison, route swapping algorithm and extragradient method were selected and extended to solve the SRD model that encapsulates the proposed stochastic traffic flow model [J6, C2]. The convergence and efficiency of the solution methods were demonstrated [J6, C2].

17207214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207214.value: The research outcomes (in forms of the modeling framework, submodels, solution method, and properties of studied problems) and major findings were published in six journal papers [J1-J6] and were presented in two international conferences [C1-C2]. Three of the journal papers was published in a prestigious transportation journal – Transportation Research Part B. The other journal papers were published in Science Citation Index journals. The following summarizes the major findings of the journal papers. Regarding problem properties and insights, [J6] presented three interesting paradoxical phenomena that can occur in degradable road networks through different specific examples: (1) the addition of a link may result in an increase in total system travel cost (TSTC), (2) an improvement of road outflow capacity may result in an increase in TSTC, and (3) an increase of network degradation may result in an increase in TSTC. Moreover, the first two paradoxes may not be observed when queue spillback is ignored. These examples demonstrated that physical queue and network degradation must be taken into consideration in any policies aimed towards the reduction in TSTC. [J2] showed that the generalized route travel cost function can be nonmonotone, even if the route travel time function is monotone. This implies that the mapping function of the VI problem for an SRD problem can be non-monotone, and that the convergence requirement of many existing solution algorithms for the SRD problems which are formulated as VI problems in general networks cannot be met. Regarding solution methods, there are five main findings: 1. [J6] showed that a larger sample size can improve the accuracy of the proposed solution algorithm for solving the SRD model with the stochastic traffic flow model as a submodel at the expense of computational time. 2. [J6] demonstrated that our proposed variable sample size scheme can obtain solutions with the same quality much quicker than the fixed sample size scheme and that the variable sample size scheme can obtain a better solution for a given computational time. 3. [J2] showed that the extragradient method for the dynamic user optimal (DUO) route choice subproblem with perfectly elastic demand can converge much more quickly than that for the DUO-SRD subproblem with perfectly elastic demand. 4. [J1] confirmed that not all existing solution methods can solve the SRD problem under stochastic DUO. 5. [J3] showed a clear trade-off between the generality of theoretical convergence and the computational efficiency of the algorithms. In particular, the projection method, despite its restrictive convergence condition, tends to yield a faster convergence rate than the self-adaptive projection algorithm, and the proximal point method and provide solutions with higher quality.

17207214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207214.value: In this research, the traffic assignment models were mainly developed based on the classical or stochastic DUO principle, where the main factor that affects route choice is expected travel time. In reality, a driver may consider other factors such as variation in travel time, travel time reliability, distance and the number of signalized junctions when making route choice decisions. The route choice principle in these models can be replaced with more sophisticated and realistic principles without encountering fundamental difficulties. This generalization is left to future studies. This research opens up various new future research directions including dynamic network design, traffic control, and pricing that considers stochastic traffic flow models. The proposed SRD model can be incorporated into bilevel optimization models for network design, traffic control, and pricing.

17207214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207214.value: An SRD model can be used to determine traffic flow pattern in network design, road pricing, and traffic control. To improve model realism and the accuracy of the modeling results for the preceding transportation applications, it is necessary to capture the uncertainties of the fundamental diagram parameters and queue spillback in the SRD model. This project aimed to propose an SRD model to capture the uncertainties of the fundamental diagram parameters and queue spillback. A stochastic traffic flow model was developed and incorporated into the variational inequality formulation. The properties of the SRD model were examined. Various solution methods were proposed. Numerical studies were carried out to analyze the efficiency and convergence of the solution methods and the properties of the model and the submodel. Numerical results showed that constructing a new road, enhancing link outflow capacity, or reducing outflow capacity degradation can lead to poor network performance and it is important to consider both network degradation and queue spillback when making transportation policies aimed at improving network performance. This project also opens up novel research directions for network design, pricing, and traffic control.

17207314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207314.value: Common devices used in distributed energy resource (DER) systems, which include photovoltaic arrays, thermoelectric generators, fuel cells, and battery storage etc., provide unstable DC voltages that are relatively low level as compared to the required voltage level of power grids. To achieve grid connection, high-voltage-gain DC-DC converters are used to perform the required voltage step-up conversions and voltage regulations to achieve an appropriate and stable DC voltage. In the case of battery storage, high-voltage-gain DC-DC converters allowing bidirectional power processing is required. The use of conventional converters for performing high-voltage-gain step-up conversion typically suffers from high duty ratio and voltage stress, which lead to low power efficiency. Many solutions have been proposed to improve this. Among them, the non-isolated DC-DC converters are regarded as a more attractive solution for their low cost and high efficiency. In particular, the switched-capacitor (SC)-based boost converter is thought to be a promising candidate for the application. This converter is achieved through the integration of an extra circuit to a high-efficiency step-up SC converter. Such a solution catering for grid connection is still seldom explored and needs to be investigated. Additionally, with multiple DER units each requiring one DC-DC converter, it is interesting to see if the concept of a multiport converter which concurrently performs the voltage conversion of multiple DER units is applicable here. This would reduce the number of converters required for the same application, thereby saving space and cost. Moreover, with their integrative nature, the multiport SC-based converter is expected to be more efficient than the single-port solution. Investigation is required to verify this. In practice, the idea of multi-port SC-based high-voltage-gain bidirectional converters can be achieved by using capacitors of the SC converter as “energy banks” to hold the intermittent energy between power supply and demand differences. DER units can be connected to the ‘energy bank’ via simple auxiliary circuits to achieve the multi-port configuration. Thorough investigation is required to achieve this. New control schemes must be developed to facilitate these operations. With the growing adoption of renewable energy, millions of high-voltage-gain converters would be required. Investigation into such kinds of converters would be useful. Success of this project will lead to greater interests in and wider use of the SC-based converters. The outcomes will be an enrichment of the theory of power electronics (new SC-based high-voltage-gain converters, multiport converter theory, and their control), and practical results verifying its potential for applications. 分佈式能源系統中，常用的分佈式能源設備的輸出電壓，如太陽能板，熱電發生器，燃料電池，以及儲能電池等，相對於電網電壓比較低。因此，如果要把這些設備并上電網，需要大變比變換器。 然而，對於儲能電池，需要具有雙向能量流動的高變比變換器。 傳統的變換器，在進行大變比電壓變換時，不但變換器工作的占空比非常大，而且開關器件的耐壓很高，這會導致變換器的效率特別低。很多的方案被提出以解決這個問題。其中，一個很有吸引力的方法是採用非隔離的直流變換器，因為這種變換器的效率高，價格低。特別的， 基於開關電容的boost變換器被認為是一種很有優勢的解決方案。這種變換器通過集成了高效率變換器與額外電路來實現。這種應用于並網的解決方案目前仍然很少被研究。 另外，對於多個新能源單元，每個單元都需要一個變換器。這種情況下，採用同時擁有多個輸入并同時能夠進行電壓變化的變換器，能夠減少變換器的數量，進而減少空間和花費。由於變換器具有的可集成性，多輸入變換器將會比單輸入變換器更高效。需要更多的研究來驗證這個想法。 實際中，基於開關電容變換器的多輸入高變比變換器，可以通過應用開關電容變換器的電容做為‘能量銀行’來吸收變換器輸入端電壓與輸出端目標電壓的電壓差。多個分佈式能源將通過簡單地輔助電路連接至此‘能量銀行’之中，從而實現多輸入功能。新的控制方案將會被研究從而實現這些功能。 隨著新能源的廣泛使用，將會需要大量的高變比變換器。因此，對於此類變換器的研究將會有廣泛應用空間。此項目的成功將會帶來很大的經濟效益，并能夠促成基於開關電容變換器的更廣泛使用。此項目將會豐富電力電子理論（新的基於開關電容的高變比變換器，多輸入變換器理論及其控制），並且實際研究結果將會驗證他的潛在應用價值。

17207314.label: Realisation of objectives
17207314.value: With regards to Objectives 1, 2, 3, and 5, we have been working and have successfully developed a new kind of bidirectional high-voltage-gain switched-capacitor step-up DC–DC converters. These converters are of high efficiency, easy to control, and are with low output voltage ripple of less than 1%. The required controller is an open loop one and very simple to implement. While the proposed converters are open-loop controlled, their voltage regulation is relatively well kept at less than 5% between full load and no load. These converters can be applied in power electronic interfaces connecting distributed energy resources to the grid. They are especially useful for high-temperature application since they do not possess magnetic component, which dramatically degrades the converters’ performance at high temperature. The proposed converters are also capable of delivering bidirectional power, which is a key requirement for the applications with battery storage. A prototype of 9-time SC converter at 20 V input voltage, 100 W output, 75 kHz, has been built and tested. Experiment results show that the maximum efficiency of the 9-time SC converter is over 98% without driver’s loss and the efficiency over the entire load range between 25 W and 100 W is over 95.5% including the driver’s loss. Additionally, in order to increase the voltage conversion ratio, power rating, and also power density of the high-voltage-gain switched-capacitor converters mentioned above, further work on converting the switched-capacitor converter into a compact modular form has been explored. We are glad to report that we successfully developed a switched-capacitor DC/DC converter with exponential voltage gain, high efficiency, light weight, and bidirectional power flow. With an output voltage that is 2N (N is the cell number) times the low-side voltage, the proposed converter has a considerably low component count and suffers from the lowest overall capacitor voltage stress as compared with other existing switched-capacitor converters. Besides, the proposed converter adopts a modular structure and simple control scheme, which enables it to be easily extended, through a repeated cascade of the same module, to achieve a higher voltage conversion. Moreover, since the load is charged via two complementary paths in an interleaved operation, the output voltage ripple is small, which is beneficial for high efficiency. A 8 times-gain prototype at 5 V input and 70 W output power have been constructed and tested. The achievable efficiency is up to 95.78% (including the driver’s loss). Moreover, in order to expand the flexibility of the conversion ratio in case of varying input voltage and load requirements in distributed energy resources application, the modular converter work mentioned above can be extended into a type of modular-cell-based morphing switched-capacitor (SC) converter for application as a front-end converter of the two-stage converter. The conversion ratio of this converter is flexible and can be freely extended by increasing more SC modules. The varying conversion ratio is achieved through the morphing of the converter’s structure corresponding to the amplitude of the input voltage. This converter is light and compact, and is highly efficient over a very wide range of input voltage and load conditions. Experimental results show that the efficiency of a single SC module is higher than 98%. This work is a useful part of achieving objective 3 and 4 as a multi-port SC converter with bi-directional conversion capability. Furthermore, as power efficiency is of prime importance in any power converters including the switched-capacitor converters that are mentioned here, an important aspect of the work which we have been working on is to develop a proper theoretical framework for helping us in designing and optimizing such converters. With regards to this, we have developed a new method of designing and optimizing switched-capacitor power converters design using a type of energy-flow-path analysis. While many analytical methods of establishing accurate models of the switched-capacitor (SC) converters have been developed and could be found in the literature, they are either applicable only to simple low-order SC converters or can provide only a general efficiency calculation of SC converters. They do not provide clear analytical solutions that can be used for the optimal design of a complex (high-order) SC converters. For complex SC converters like those mentioned in our work, a constituent capacitor may have a profound effect upon the converter’s efficiency depending on the configuration of the switches and the arrangement of the energy flow paths. In our work, the relationship of capacitors on the efficiency of complex SC converters is derived and investigated using the principle of energy-flow-path analysis. This allows the design of complex SC converter to be performed in terms of optimizing its power efficiency. The results of both calculation and experimental works show that the approach is valid and effective. In addition, to deal with extremely high conversion needs with low-cost, circuit simplicity and high efficiency, we have developed an extremely high-ratio step-up nonisolated dc/dc converter, in the form of a harmonics-boosted resonant converter. This proposed converter consists of a high-frequency dc/ac inverter stage that is followed by a passive ac/dc rectifier stage connected in cascade. Conventionally, such a dc/ac inverter is designed to output a pure sinusoidal ac voltage with an amplitude several times the amplitude of the input voltage. However, for the proposed converter, the harmonics-boosted inverter stage is designed to contain selected voltage harmonics that significantly boost the amplitude of its output voltage. This greatly increases the overall gain of the converter. The adopted ac/dc stage is a diode-capacitor rectifier, which is of high efficiency and easily extendable to increase the voltage gain. Importantly, the proposed converter involves only one active switch. With only one active switch, the driver’s loss is minimized and the converter’s control is simplified. Zero-voltage switching is applied to reduce the switching loss, which also allows the converter to operate efficiently at high frequency, and thus can be designed for high power density. The optimal design of the two converter stages and their combined voltage gain is investigated and reported. Besides, a design guideline of the proposed converter is provided. We developed a prototype of a 57-time harmonics-boosted resonant converter with 3.3 V input voltage, 500 kHz switching frequency, and 21 W output power with an achieved converter’s efficiency as high as 88.6%. With regards to objectives 3 to 5, we have also developed a multiphase-interleaved non-isolated high-step-up DC/DC resonant converter for high-current applications with wide load range. The converter consists of an inverter stage with multiple resonant inverters in parallel interleaving operation that is cascaded to a common diode-capacitor rectifier stage. The topology of the inverter stage is a variation of class E inverter, which is designed for voltage boosting and is insensitive to load change. The rectifier stage comprises multiple pairs (correlated to the number of inverters in parallel) of diodes in parallel and a small output capacitor, which makes it simple and low cost. Together, the voltage gain variance of the converter can be confined in a small value and zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) operation can be maintained over a wide load range. A prototype of the proposed converter with input voltage of 23.6 V, rated output voltage of 190 V, and rated output power of 80 W at 486 kHz has been constructed to verify the performance of the proposed converter. The converter is controlled by a frequency controller.

17207314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207314.value: A new kind of bidirectional high-voltage-gain switched-capacitor step-up DC–DC converters. These converters are of high efficiency, easy to control, and are with low output voltage ripple of less than 1%. The achievable voltage regulation is relatively well kept at less than 5% between full load and no load. They are capable of delivering bidirectional power, which is a key requirement for the applications with battery storage. Publications related to this work are "Family of Cascaded High-Voltage-Gain Bidirectional Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Converters," IEEE ECCE, 2015 and "Cascaded high-voltage-gain bidirectional switched-capacitor DC-DC converters for distributed energy resources applications,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, 2017. We successfully developed a switched-capacitor DC/DC converter with exponential voltage gain, high efficiency, light weight, and bidirectional power flow. The proposed converter may adopt a modular structure and simple control scheme, which enables it to be easily extended, through a repeated cascade of the same module, to achieve a higher voltage conversion. Publications related to this work are "Compact Modular Switched-Capacitor DC/DC converter with Exponential Voltage Gain," IEEE APEC, 2016 and "Morphing Switched-Capacitor Step-Down DC–DC Converters with Variable Conversion Ratio," IEEE APEC, 2016, and “Morphing switched-capacitor converters with variable conversion ratio,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, 2016. Furthermore, we developed a new method of designing and optimizing switched-capacitor power converters design using a type of energy-flow-path analysis. Our approach allows the design of complex SC converter to be performed in terms of optimizing its power efficiency. Publication related to this work is "Optimal design of complex switched-capacitor converters via energy-flow-path analysis,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, 2017. An extremely high-ratio step-up nonisolated dc/dc converter, in the form of a harmonics-boosted resonant converter has been proposed. For the proposed converter, the harmonics-boosted inverter stage is designed to contain selected voltage harmonics that significantly boost the amplitude of its output voltage. This the overall achievable gain of this converter is extremely high. Publication related to this work is "Nonisolated harmonics-boosted resonant DC/DC converter with high-step-up gain,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, 2018. A multiphase-interleaved non-isolated high-step-up DC/DC resonant converter for high-current applications with wide load range is developed. The converter is designed for voltage boosting and is insensitive to load change and operates at high power. It is applicable to multi-port SC based bidirectional power conversions. Publication related to this work is under 2nd review "Multiphase-Interleaved High-Step-Up DC/DC Resonant Converter For Wide Load Range", IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics.

17207314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207314.value: (1) For applications such as PV grid-connected system, wide input voltage range operation is required for the front-end DC/DC converter. High-frequency resonant converter suitable for wide load operation has been investigated in this work. However, high-frequency resonant converter suitable for wide input voltage range operation has not yet been proposed. Reconfigurable high-frequency resonant converter may be a potential solution for the wide input voltage range application. (2) For interleaved high step-up DC/DC resonant converter, the number of inductors is increased with increasing number of phases. To further increase the power density of the converter while maintain the high efficiency, it is worthwhile to reduce the volume of the magnetic cores of these inductors without increasing switching frequency. Utilizing the flux cancellation magnetic integration technique is a potential solution to reduce the volume of multiple magnetic cores in multiphase. (3) For the existing analysis of high-frequency resonant converter, the mathematical model of the converter is constructed by fundamental approximation. However, this model is not accurate, especially for harmonics-boosted converter case, as only fundamental component is considered in this model. Thus, more accurate models that consider high order harmonic components should be investigated for the design of the high-frequency resonant converter.

17207514.label: Project Objectives
17207514.value: To develop multilayer-structured rejection layers for organic micropollutant removal. With each layer designed to remove targeted class(es) of contaminants, the resulting membrane will have potential to reject a wide range of organic micropollutants. Multilayer-structured films and membranes will be synthesized in the proposed project and their layer structure characterized. The novel multilayer-structured approach for controlling micropollutants removal represents a paradigm shift from conventional RO and NF membrane design. Upon successful implementation, the project will result in a new generation of high-performance membranes optimized for water reclamation. To characterize through experimentation the interaction between organic micropollutants and their transport through multilayer-structured rejection layers. Detailed characterization will be performed to investigate the major mechanisms involved in solute transport in membranes. In addition, filtration tests will be performed to verify membrane separation performance. The fundamental insights gained will lead to a set of guiding principles for the design of future generations of membranes for water reclamation. The results from the project will be disseminated in the form of publications, seminars, and a publicly available database. To develop a theoretical framework and a set of design criteria for multilayer-structured membranes. Organic micropollutant rejection, water permeability and salt rejection will be modeled, and criteria for developing multilayer-structured membranes with optimal separation properties will be established. The model will be verified by experimental separation performance data and will be used to improve the design and synthesis of multilayer-structured membranes.

17207514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207514.value: Water scarcity is an increasingly serious global issue due to rapid urbanization, population growth, and climate change. Only 20-30% of Hong Kong’s water supply is from local catchment, and the rest must be imported. Water reclamation is a logical way of providing additional clean water for non-potable uses by treating municipal wastewater with a reverse osmosis (RO) or nanofiltration (NF) membrane process. However, conventional RO and NF membranes have been shown to have low rejection rates against a number of organic micropollutants, such as some endocrine disrupting compounds and pharmaceutically active compounds. The presence of these organic compounds in reclaimed water is a potential risk to human health. In this proposal, we envisage a novel multilayer-structured membrane with a rejection layer comprising multiple sub-layers. Our primary hypothesis is that a thin (sub-)layer having low affinity with a targeted organic compound can significantly enhance the rejection of the compound. The physiochemical properties of each layer can be tailored to enhance the rejection of specific class(es) of organic micropollutants. When assembled together, the layers complement each other in the resulting membrane to safeguard against a wide range of targeted organic micropollutants. Whereas the conventional RO and NF membranes are optimized on the basis of water permeability and salt rejection, the proposed multilayer approach allows each layer to be separately controlled and optimized to reject targeted organic contaminants. The project will systematically test the primary hypothesis through a set of specific tasks including: (i) analytical methods development, (ii) preparation of multilayer-structured rejection layers, (iii) characterization of the interaction between organic micropollutants and multilayer-structured rejection layers, (iv) evaluation of membrane separation performance (particularly rejection of organic micropollutants), and (v) modeling the separation properties of multilayer-structured rejection layers. The proposal introduces a new paradigm for membrane architecture, developing novel multilayer-structured membranes that are optimized for organic micropollutant rejection. Upon successful completion of the project, novel high-performance membranes with enhanced micropollutant removal will be developed. Fundamental insights into the transport of organic micropollutants in membranes will be gained. The project will also lead to the establishment of a theoretical framework and a set of design criteria for multilayer-structured membranes. It has the potential to change the way membrane-based water reclamation is performed, and thus lead to improved sustainability of water supply in water-stressed megacities such as Hong Kong. 快速的城市化，人口增長，和全球氣候變化讓水資源匱乏問題變得日益嚴重。香港只有20-30%的水供來自本地集水區，其餘需從東江引水。基於反滲透膜和納濾膜的污水回用技術可以有效的提供新的非飲用水源。然而，傳統的反滲透膜和納濾膜對部份有機微污染物（例如一些內分泌干擾物和藥物）的處理效率低下，因而帶來隱含的健康風險。 本項目致力於一種新型多鍍層複合膜的設計和開發。此結構中，每一單層針對某一類特定的目標污染物，通過該層物理化學性質的調節對其處理效率最優化。將若干單層有機組合在一起的複合膜將因而對各類目標污染物達到高效截留。與傳統的僅基於水通量和截鹽率的反滲透膜和納濾膜設計理念不同，本項目提出了著重於有機微污染物截留率最優化的理念。 本項目的主體工作包括：（1）分析方法的建立，（2）複合鍍層的製備，（3）對有機微污染物和複合鍍層間的相互作用的表徵，（4）多鍍層複合膜分離性質的測試，以及（5）對多鍍層複合膜分離性質的擬合。 本項目提出了多鍍層複合膜的新理念。進一步的研究將為此類膜提供完善的理論體系和設計原則。項目的成功將帶引新型的高效污水回用膜技術開發。這將為香港創造長遠的可持續的水供。

17207514.label: Realisation of objectives
17207514.value: The first objective of this project is to develop multilayer-structured membrane rejection layers for the removal of organic micropollutants. Various surface coating methods and interfacial technologies such as self-polymerization, in-situ growth of nanoparticles, and interfacial metal-organic complexing, were used to create the multilayer structures. These additional layers were introduced onto the surface of existing membranes to enhance their rejection of organic micropollutants. A mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating technique was used to form a hydrophilic coating layer on the polyamide layer to improve membrane rejection of hydrophobic compounds, e.g., endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs), an important class of organic micropollutants with significant environmental and health concerns. Moreover, different nanoparticles such as silver and palladium nanoparticles (i.e., AgNPs and PdNPs, respectively) were incorporated on the PDA layer through in-situ growth methods to functionalize the membranes. The AgNPs-PDA-polyamide multilayer membrane showed significantly enhanced selectivity to water permeance and against EDCs transport, leading to the much greater rejection of EDCs with mild water permeability loss compared to traditional polyamide membranes. In addition, a rapid, green, and cost-effective assembly of tannic acid-iron (TA-Fe) complexes was used to form a thin layer on polyamide layer to enhance membrane rejection of both hydrophobic EDCs and hydrophilic antibiotics. The second objective is to characterize the interaction and transportation of organic micropollutants with and through multilayer-structured rejection layers. A sorption behavior analysis of hydrophobic EDC into polyamide layer and PDA-polydopamine multilayer revealed that reduced EDC sorption after PDA coating led to less transmission (and thus improved rejection). Compared to single polyamide layer, AgNPs-PDA-polyamide multilayer presented more hydrophilic and more negatively charged surface simultaneously, which could enhance membrane rejection of both hydrophobic compounds and negatively charged solutes. For all the compounds no matter charge and hydrophobicity, size exclusion is a key mechanism governing their transportation and rejection. Neutral and hydrophilic molecular probes were used to characterize the effect of size exclusion of membranes. Both AgNPs-PDA-polyamide and TA-Fe-polyamide multilayer-structured membrane showed enhanced effect of size exclusion compared to the plain polyamide membrane on the basis of the molecular probes characterization. The third objective is to develop a theoretical framework and a set of design criteria for multilayer-structured membranes. A resistance-in-series model was developed in this project to model the transportation of water, organic micropollutants, and salt through multilayer-structured rejection layers. The model can be expressed by followed equations: 1/Aoverall = 1/A1 + 1/A2 + … + 1/An and 1/Boverall = 1/B1 + 1/B2 + … + 1/Bn where Aoverall and Boverall represent the water permeability and solute permeability (e.g., organic micropollutant or salt) of the multilayer-structured membrane, respectively. 1/ Aoverall and 1/Boverall can be simplified as the membrane resistance to water and solute, respectively. A1, A2,…An and B1, B2,…Bn mean water permeability and solute permeability of each individual layer, respectively. This model was successfully applied to analyze the separation performance of AgNPs-PDA-polyamide membrane. The AgNPs-PDA layer showed high water permeability and low organic micropollutants permeability, thus improved membrane rejection of the pollutants without sacrificing water permeability.

17207514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207514.value: 1. A hydrophilic polydopamine (PDA) coating layer could enhance the rejection of hydrophobic endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) by the resulting PDA-polyamide multilayer membrane. The presence of PDA layer prevented unfavorable hydrophobic interaction between the EDCs and membrane, thus reduced the transmission of EDCs across the membrane (i.e., increased rejection). Meanwhile, a thin PDA coating layer could increase membrane water flux, reduce reverse solute diffusion, and improve membrane antifouling performance simultaneously in forward osmosis. These findings provide a promising strategy of introducing additional layers to create multilayer-structured membrane for the enhancement of membrane separation performance. Related publications in Section C: 2, 11 2. A silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) incorporated PDA coating layer could significantly enhance membrane selectivity to water permeance and against EDCs transport. The AgNPs-PDA-polyamide multilayer membrane showed greatly improved rejection of EDCs with only slightly decreased water permeability compared to the traditional polyamide membrane. The enhancement could be attributed to the combined effects of increased hydrophilicity and size exclusion. A resistance-in-series model analysis revealed that the AgNPs-PDA layer presented one order of magnitude higher selectivity than polyamide layer, promoting the AgNPs-PDA-polyamide membrane to have higher selectivity against EDCs transport. AgNPs-PDA layer also could improve membrane anti-microbial performance to safeguard membrane life and water safety. Besides AgNPs, other nanoparticles or novel materials with specific functions such as palladium nanoparticles (PdNPs) and metal organic framework could also be imbedded into the multilayer structure to functionalize membrane (e.g., catalytic membrane using PdNPs for water decontamination). The results confirm the feasibility and validity of tailoring membrane structure and chemistry using nanotechnologies to improve membrane performance including organic micropollutants removal and antifouling. Related publications in Section C: 1, 3, 5, 8, 13 3. Tannic acid-iron (TA-Fe) coordination complexes could be a rapid, green, and cost effective coating chemistry to create multilayer-structured membranes. These membranes showed high rejection of organic micropollutants including EDCs and antibiotics. A quartz crystal microbalance characterization confirmed that the TA-Fe layer could be formed within 2 minutes. Such a rapid coating duration means greatly shortened manufacturing time and saved operational cost for practical applications. The TA-Fe-polyamide membrane gave 4-5 times lower permeability of EDCs and 1 order of magnitude lower permeability of antibiotics compared to the single polyamide membrane. The significant enhancement of the rejection could be related to the enhanced effect of size exclusion. Related publications in Section C: 6

17207514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207514.value:  It is recommended to further explore novel materials such as zwitterionic polymers, carbon-based materials, covalent organic frameworks, and biomimetic aquaporin for multilayer-structured membrane fabrication used for wastewater reclamation. These materials are promising alternatives for membrane separation because of their high water permeability, high salts rejection, and superior antifouling performance.  Development of more effective non-polyamide based membranes. A subsequent work using tannic acid-iron thin layer as a rejection layer confirmed the possibility of using non-polyamide based membrane for the rejection of organic micropollutants. Other materials such as graphene can be further explored as the selective barrier of a membrane.  Membranes with high selectivity is needed, no matter for seawater desalination or wastewater treatment. A well-designed membrane shall be highly permeable to water and highly resistant to solutes. Thus, they can achieve the goal of producing large amount of water with high quality.  It is also worthwhile to develop more energy-saving membranes. As current nanofiltration and reverse osmosis membranes generally need external hydraulic pressure to drive the process, their applications may be restricted in emergency situations (e.g., natural disasters) and poor places without sufficient electricity supply. Low-energy multilayer-structured membranes such as gravity-driven nanofibrous membrane may be more useful in such situations.

17207514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207514.value: Water scarcity is serious global issue. This grand challenge of the century can be addressed by water reuse using reverse osmosis (RO) technology. However, conventional RO membranes have been shown to have low rejection rates against a number of toxic organic micropollutants that present potent risks to human health. In this project, we have developed novel multilayer-structured membranes to achieve enhanced removal of harmful micropollutants. In our novel design, each sub-layer of a multilayer-structured membrane is optimized to cater for specific types of micropollutants. For example, we demonstrated the use of a hydrophilic polydopamine coating layer to minimize the sorption of hydrophobic endocrine disrupting compounds and therefore enhances their rejection by the coated membrane. Effective post-functionalization and alternative coating strategies have been developed to achieve orders of magnitude increase in selectivity, which safeguards against potable water reuse. Our work establishes a new paradigm for membrane architecture design. The project also led to a theoretical framework for design and optimization of membranes for water reuse applications. It has the potential to change the current practice of water reuse and significantly improve the sustainability of water supply in Hong Kong and worldwide.

17207714.label: Project Objectives
17207714.value: High-throughput multiplexed bioassays become increasingly imperative as biomedicine is evolving into an arena of solving “big-data” problems, e.g. the “-omics” approaches and single-cell analysis. Among different assay technologies, microfluidics is gaining sizeable popularity because of its cost-effective implementation. Two key features are essential for realizing high-throughput microfluidic assays: (i) flexible encoding – establishing a highly scalable “barcode” library which is versatile for a wide range of bioassay applications; (ii) High-throughput decoding – “barcode” read-out of each coded microparticle in high-speed microfluidic flow. Impressive innovations have been made for scaling the encoding capacity > 1,000,000 elements. However, efficient barcode read-out is very often restricted by an unspoken speed limitation of the image sensors – the workhorse of numerous microfluidic devices used for decoding. Practical decoding throughput is thus typically limited to ~ 100–1,000 codes/s, beyond which both detection sensitivity and pixel resolution are compromised. In this project, we aim to address the above-said two issues by exploiting an entirely new strategy for high-throughput multiplexed bioassays, imaging flow refractometry. This technique includes a new-generation of our recent work on time-stretch imaging called multiple-angle time-stretch (MATS) imaging, which achieves interferometry-free quantitative phase imaging simultaneously with qualitative bright-field imaging, for ultrahigh-speed microparticle decoding at a rate of ~10,000-100,000 codes/s – orders-of-magnitude faster than the existing decoding technologies. In view of the compatibility between this ultrafast imaging technique and the growing interest in droplet microfluidics, the proposed imaging flow refractometry will be developed with a new encoding scheme based on the physical properties of the droplet-emulsion templates – resulting in a highly-scalable droplet library (100 –1,000,000 unique codes). As the same droplet emulsion can compartmentalize for the target biomolecules/cells, the proposed MATS imaging flow refractometry could be a compelling alternative for practical microfluidic high-throughput screening. Specifically, we aim to:  Develop the multiple-angle time-stretch (MATS) microscope Built upon our recent work on ultrafast optical time-stretch imaging, a new-generation prototype, coined multiple-angle time-stretch (MATS) imaging, will be developed. In contrast to its earlier generation, MATS imaging has a unique feature of delivering both high-contrast qualitative phase-gradient imaging and quantitative phase-contrast imaging simultaneously in single-shot at line-scan rate of >10MHz. To demonstrate this unique potential in practical use, the MATS prototype will have two major advancements over the earlier generation of time-stretch imaging: (i) superior temporal imaging stability due to its interferometry-free operation – particularly benefits robust ultrafast decoding of the proposed droplet library and cellular imaging in the same assay platform. (ii) An order-of-magnitude higher group velocity dispersion (GVD) for time-stretch – essential for realizing practical real-time ultrafast back-end data processing.  Develop a MATS-compatible droplet library based on image-based refractometric-encoding We will develop a droplet microfluidic platform generating “barcoded” droplet emulsion templates with a new encoding scheme – image-based refractometric-encoding. The encoding scheme exploits the combinations of different physical properties of the droplet emulsions (e.g. refractive index, geometry), that constitute the unique barcodes which can be decoded with MATS imaging at ultrahigh speed. This scheme does not suffer from the spectral overlap limitation in the spectroscopic encoding scheme that restricts the coding capacity (~100-1,000). It also does not require the relatively complex and costly lithographic process involved in the graphical encoding scheme albeit its high coding capacity (>1,000,000). As the droplet’s properties can be flexibly fine-tuned with high precision and stability by the well-established low-cost microfluidic droplet technology, we will exploit and characterize different viable droplet emulsion templates (based on single or double emulsions) which could create a highly scalable coded-droplet library for multiplexed assays (100-1,000,000 codes).  Establish the MATS-based imaging flow refractometer for ultrafast barcoded microparticle read-out We will develop a MATS-based imaging flow refractometer as an ultrafast droplet microfluidic decoder, which performs quantitative imaging, thus decoding of the proposed encoded-droplet emulsions in microfluidic flow at a throughput of 10,000-100,000 droplets/s (codes/s). To demonstrate the feasibility of real-time high-speed readout, we will also integrate the system with parallel signal processing using field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Through the proof-of-principle assay experiments and concomitant system characterization (e.g. decoding throughput/accuracy), we will explore the potential applications of this technology, particularly in high-throughput multiplexed single-cell analysis, in collaboration with Faculty of Medicine at HKU.
