17207714.value: 持續發展的生物科學使得人們越來越多的對單細胞分析產生了濃厚的興趣，從而使得相關研究迫切的需要與此相應的高通量多重生物檢測技術。在眾多檢測技術中，微流體學技術因其性價比高而被廣泛采用。為實現高通量多重生物檢測，基於微流體學的檢測技術應滿足以下兩點：（1）靈活的編碼能力，即建立一個高拓展性的信息條碼數據庫，用以鑒別數量巨大的裝載不同目標生物分子或細胞的微粒（量級為1,000到1,000,000以上），這對於生物檢測具有廣泛的應用價值。然而，目前主流的生物編碼技術，即光譜檢測法，受制於其有限的檢測容量（約100到1,000量級）。新湧現的圖像編碼技術，可以達到多於1,000,000量級的檢測能力，然而其編碼程序復雜且昂貴。（2）高通量的解碼能力，即對編好的生物條碼通過微流體的高速流動來進行快速的生物信息解讀。在人們花費大量精力用於提高生物編碼能力的同時，與之匹配的信息解碼能力也至關重要，然而目前形式卻不容樂觀。其主要原因在於大多數的解碼手段長期依賴於傳統的圖像傳感器，因而在熟知的成像速度與靈敏度以及成像速度和分辨率的博弈之間進行艱難的權衡。為保證合理的檢測靈敏度以及解碼分辨率，現有的生物解碼率通常限制在約100到1,000碼每秒。 為解決上述問題，我們研發了一種新型生物檢測平臺-流體成像折射測定計。其技術是由我們新一代的時域展寬成像術，即多角度時域展寬（英文簡稱MATS），衍生而來，通過低成本的微液滴流體編碼方案實現高拓展性的生物編碼能力，並進行超快速的生物檢測解碼。我們近期關於時域展寬成像的工作實現了創紀錄的百萬幀每秒超快速靈敏成像。因此，我們開發出MATS成像技術，在無光學相干的條件下，可以超快速的同時定性定量的對微粒進行流體成像，並達到約100,000碼每秒的超快解碼率，這比現有的同類技術高出幾個數量級。該解碼方案可以自然而然的兼容於微液滴流體技術（一項快速發展的低成本高效率高通量的篩選技術）。為此，我們還將建立一個基於液滴乳液屬性的，與MATS成像系統相配合的高拓展性信息條碼數據庫（約100到1,000,000碼），用以區分不同的目標生物分子或細胞。對於實現高通量的微粒篩選，我們所研發的流體成像折射測定計，將來可以廣泛的應用於生物醫學領域。由於高通量多重細胞檢測在生命科學研究及藥物篩選中具有極其重要的作用，我們將在此雛形基礎上不斷探索該技術的應用潛力。

17207714.label: Realisation of objectives
17207714.value: We have developed high-speed multiple-angle time-stretch (MATS) microscopy platform that both high-contrast qualitative phase-gradient imaging and quantitative phase-contrast imaging simultaneously in single-shot at line-scan rate of >10MHz without the need for interferometry, and at a line scan rate typically between 10-12 MHz (Objectives 1-3). We have developed a droplet microfluidic platform generating “barcoded” droplet emulsion templates with a new encoding scheme. Combined with MATS microscopy, we demonstrated that the system could extract quantitative phase profiles of microparticles (droplets, cells etc.) with high spatial resolution (~1um) and high phase (i.e. refractive index read-out) accuracy (down to ~mrad level) and stability (Objective 4). We successfully applied MATS microscopy for high-throughput multiplexed single-cell analysis, in collaboration with Faculty of Medicine at HKU. Notably, we tested the system for a number of biomedical applications (at a high-throughput of >10,000 cells/sec) and enabled new label-free single-cell analysis approaches, such as studying the hypertrophy of chondrocytes in all label-free manner; classification of leukaemic cell lines in PBMCs; multi-class classification of multiple leukaemic cell lines; as well as label-free single-cell study of cell-cycle (Objective 5).

17207714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207714.value: The project has partially and fully supported over 15 peer-reviewed publications (including Nature publishing's Scientific Reports, Optica, Biomedical Optics Express, Lab on a Chip etc.), as well as over 30 international conference publications all related to high-speed and high-resolution spectrally-encoded imaging and illumination based technologies. 2 US patent applications related to methods for high-resolution MATS imaging, as well as the barcoding concept. Specifically, we in this project have developed the MATS prototype that has two major advancements over the earlier generation of time-stretch imaging: (i) superior temporal imaging stability due to its interferometry-free operation – favouring ultrafast decoding of the proposed droplet library and cellular imaging in the same assay platform. (ii) An order-of-magnitude higher GVD for optical time-stretch (~2ns/nm) – essential for realizing practical real-time ultrafast back-end data processing (~10GB/s throughput). We have developed a droplet microfluidic platform generating “barcoded” droplet emulsion templates based on optical phase/refractive index encoding scheme. And we combined such system with MATS for optical phase/barcode read out at high phase accuracy - down to milli-radian precision. We have integrated the system with parallel signal processing using field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Custom logic has been implemented on the FPGA to automatically detect and segment cells from the digitized data stream in real time, at a processing throughput equivalent to > 10,000 cell/s. This segmentation step is critical in maximizing the efficiency of the downstream data storage subsystem. The system has also been extended to other applications, such as ultrafast optical coherence tomography, ultrafast spectroscopy/spectral analysis. Most significantly, We have employed the MATS system to enable a new paradigm of label-free single-cell analysis approaches, such as (1) studying the hypertrophy of chondrocytes in all label-free manner ; classification of leukaemic cell lines in PBMCs; multi-class classification of multiple leukaemic cell lines; as well as label-free single-cell study of cell-cycle. In general, we demonstrated that such label-free single-cell analysis tool provides unprecedented statistical and discrimination power for revealing cellular heterogeneity down in single-cell precision.

17207714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207714.value: MATS microscopy together with droplet-based barcoding technique could further be combined with state-of-the-art microfluidic cell sorter. This could present an integrated approach for single-cell analysis, from imaging to down-stream molecular analysis (e.g. single-cell RNA sequencing). We in the future will plan to conceptualise and implement possible cell sorting approach which could be compatible with our imaging technique. In addition, we will explore the data analytical approaches, especially deep learning, for "big-data" management and analysis of single-cell images generated from our technology.

17207714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207714.value: We have developed an new optical imaging technique that could formulate new strategies for high-throughput multiplexed bioassays, imaging flow refractometry - which essentially quantifies physical properties of microparticles (e.g. droplets, cells). This technique includes a new-generation of our recent work on time-stretch imaging called multiple-angle time-stretch (MATS) imaging, which achieves interferometry-free quantitative phase imaging for ultrahigh-speed microparticle decoding and label-free single-cell quantitative imaging at a rate of ~10,000-100,000 particles/s (cells/s) – orders-of-magnitude faster than the existing technologies. This technological platform represents an alternative for realizing for practical high-throughput screening used in a wide range of applications in biomedicine and life science research where high-throughput multiplexed cellular bioassays are critical.

17207914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207914.value: 胶体体是一种壳体由紧密排列的胶体颗粒组成的微胶囊，有望在活性物质的包覆与释放方面发挥重要作用， 从而应用于生物医学，食品工业， 材料，药学，农业以及化妆品等行业。然而，目前已有的胶体体的功能化结果并不尽人意，其根源在于传统制造方法在设计与制作胶体体微结构、性质、功能和释放特征方面的缺陷。 我们计划发展一种普适、高效的方法来精确制造尺寸均一结构稳定的胶体体，使其对目标物质同时兼备高效包覆与根据环境温度智能可控释放的性能。技术的关键在于以微流控双重乳液模板取代传统制造方法中的单乳液模板，以不依赖于壳解体的释放代替传统释放机制。此技术将采用玻璃毛细管微流控装置生产所需的双重乳液，利用微流体装置所具有的精确操纵微量流体的特性，对其形成的双重乳液模板和胶体体进行精准的控制。在释放机制方面，我们将一种具有可逆吸附与解吸性质的嵌段共聚物溶解在核心及胶体体壳体的内表面，当外部环境温度发生改变，嵌段共聚物将会吸附或解吸于壳体表面的孔隙，从而阻塞或开启释放核心物质的通道。我们旨在明确这项技术在精准控制热响应释放靶向物质，操控双重乳液液滴、胶体体及其壳体形态的潜力，确定相关工艺参数、胶体体结构及其释放性能间的关系。 我们首先以水相为核体，开发该项智能胶体体的制作方法。 这个项目的成功将会革新胶体体微胶囊的制造方法，实现对胶体体制作的精确控制，促进高效封装与控制释放，生产出更为优质的胶体体。项目过程中的发现将有助于推动胶体体形态结构及释放性能的设计与定制，以满足不同类型的应用需求。同时，此项目得到的创新型胶体体，作为胶体体的未来发展趋势，将对食品、药学、化妆品、材料以及生物医学等多种领域中的高效封装、输送和释放产生非凡影响。

17207914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207914.value: Colloidosomes are microcapsules whose shells consist of densely-packed colloidal particles. They are very promising candidates for encapsulation and release of various active materials of technological importance in biomedicine, food industry, materials, pharmaceutics, agriculture, and cosmetics. However, the functional outcomes of existing colloidosomes have not been satisfactory because of the inadequacies of conventional fabrication approaches in engineering their microstructures, properties, functionalities, and release profiles. A general and effective approach has been developed in this project for precisely fabricating uniform and stable colloidosomes with effective encapsulation and release of encapsulated materials on demand. Conventional single emulsion templates and shell-deformation-dependent release strategy were replaced by microfluidic double emulsion templates and release strategy involving no shell-deformation, respectively. A microfluidic device was used to generate required double emulsions, which exploits the microfluidics-offered capability of precisely handling small fluid volume and thus allows an accurate control over the formation of both double emulsions and colloidosomes. The approach relies on the reversible adsorption or desorption of a block copolymer, dissolved in the core, on the inner surface of the colloidosome shell in response to a temperature change, to block or unblock the pores in the shell for switching off or on the release.

17208214.label: Project Objectives
17208214.value: A new growth-based method that iteratively adjusts the positions and orientations of packing objects concurrently to achieve tight packing. For its efficient implementation, we propose a new approximate representation of a generalized Voronoi diagram of arbitrary 3D objects. A new method based on force simulation for tight packing of 3D objects. Here, inspired by the interaction energy of molecular particles, we propose a novel energy minimization framework for efficient packing. Study on an effective stochastic optimization scheme that is based on simulated annealing and works in coupling with our continuous optimization methods to further improve packing results.

17208214.value: 本项目拟提出有效的方法解决不规则几何物体的填装问题（packing problem），特别是三维不规则几何体。填装问题是多个研究领域中的基础问题，如运筹学、计算机科学、工业工程学和材料科学等。在几何建模和计算机图形学领域，填装方法的研究也具有广泛的应用，如布料填装、马赛克图案设计、蓝噪声采样、网格生成、纹理合成，以及针对三维打印的模型结构优化问题等。 以往已经有大量的工作研究填装问题，但是往往因为效率不高或者适用条件约束限制了其应用范围。大部分现有方法在考虑二维和三维填装问题时总是假设物体的形状比较简单（如球体或者超椭球），并约束物体在填装过程中不能旋转或者只能在有限的几个角度旋转。然而在材料科学中模拟一般粒子的填装以及优化三维打印模型的布局时，有效的填装算法应该允许物体在三维空间内自由旋转。因此，目前我们还缺乏一种方法能有效地解决大规模三维不规则物体的填装问题。 在本项目中我们主要研究三维不规则物体的填装问题。填装问题有本质上的困难，因为即使是求解大小不等的圆在正方形区域内的填装问题也是NP-困难的。因此，我们将重点研究有效的近似方法。从计算方法的角度来看，填装问题的求解包含两种不同特性：一是局部的连续优化，即调整物体和邻近物体的相对位置关系；二是整体的组合优化，如求解所有物体的整体最优布局。我们将结合连续优化和组合优化方法，提出一种新的三维填装问题的有效解决方法。 对于填装问题中的连续优化，我们将充分利用物体旋转和平移自由度，探索两种不同的新方法。第一种方法是基于一般化Voronoi图的增长模型。每一个物体都有一个包围它的Voronoi区域。在迭代过程中，我们通过匹配物体形状和它的Voronoi区域的形状来决定物体的平移和旋转量。由于物体是在各自独立的Voronoi区域之内进行变换，所以可以保证物体之间不会产生相互重叠。同时，我们也提出了针对该问题的新的一般化Voronoi图的表示和快速计算方法。在第二种针对三维填装问题的连续优化方法中，我们借鉴了分子动力学中描述分子之间作用力的范德华力场模型。根据此模型，两个物体在相距较远的情况下会相互吸引，这种吸引力会促使它们聚拢在一起。然而当它们距离较近时，会产生巨大的排斥力，这种排斥力又会阻止它们相互重叠。我们定义一个物体间相互作用能量，它是物体间范德华力场势能和重力势能之和。通过最小化这个能量函数，并且施加约束保证物体被包含在容器之内，我们可以找到一个紧致的填装结果。 连续优化方法在搜索最优解时容易陷入局部极小，从而导致这样一种情况：物体不能继续移动，但是它们之间仍有很大的空隙。针对这个问题，我们结合调整物体整体布局的组合优化方法。我们将会探究一些有效的随机组合优化方法，用以避免上述的局部最优问题，从而进一步提高最终填装结果的质量。此外，我们还会研究优化方法的并行化实现，以降低计算成本。目前的初步实验结果显示，我们提出的方法相比以前的方法更加有效，也验证了我们方法的可行性

17208214.value: The first objective has been achieved 100 percent in three cases: 2D, on a surface and in 3D. Two papers have been published. The second objective has been tested in 2D and 3D. 17208414.label: Project Objectives
17208414.value: To design a high-performance WET system The proposed WET leverages the time-sensitivity of a linear frequency shifting device to differentiate the spatial depth-induced delay. Spatial (depth)-to-wavelength conversion is essential to WET, consisting of two-stage four-wave mixing (FWM). In this stage of the project, we will design the spatial resolution, wavelength conversion bandwidth, conversion efficiency, etc. features of the WET system for implementation and optimization in the later stages of the research. To implement and characterize a WET prototype A WET prototype will be implemented and its performance thoroughly characterized in a number of respects, including spatial resolution, wavelength conversion bandwidth and conversion efficiency in its wideband mechanism. Higher wavelength conversion efficiency and wider conversion bandwidth by fiber optical parametric amplifier (OPA) will also be explored. This stage of the research provides a platform for obtaining 2D/3D images in the last phase of the research. To optimize the WET system with respect to the detection scheme and obtain 2D/3D images We will explore two different kinds of detection schemes; namely, conventional CCD array and ultrafast parametric spectro-temporal analyzer (PASTA). The thorough study of the WET system’s performance and its application in imaging layer structures in the first and second phases of the proposed project will lay the foundation for its use in capturing 2D/3D images (e.g. the anterior segment of a fish eye) towards the end of the research process.

17208414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208414.value: Growing demand for healthcare solutions has necessitated substantial advancements in biophotonics over the past decade. Various imaging techniques such as X-ray radiography, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), ultrasound imaging and optical coherence tomography (OCT) have proven to be promising in their respective applications. In particular, OCT complements other imaging techniques by providing non-invasive cross-sectional imaging of internal structures in biological tissues by measuring their optical reflections. The expertise acquired in telecommunications and in development of photonic components offers a powerful knowledge base for addressing the stringent requirements of biophotonic applications, especially in optical imaging technology. The proposed wavelength-encoded tomography (WET) is an entirely new optical imaging modality that captures tomographic (i.e. layered) images in a non-invasive manner, and enables ultrafast axial-scan (A-scan) rate with high resolution and sensitivity. Unlike the conventional OCT system, in which speed is limited by mechanical scanning of the imaging (time-domain) and computationally demanding signal processing in reconstructing the image (Fourier-domain), the WET system realizes single-shot imaging for its inherent all-optical signal processing. It offers a tremendous improvement in A-scan rate; in principle, hundreds of megahertz or even gigahertz rate. In the proposed project, we will implement the WET system and investigate its operating performance, including the spatial resolution, wavelength conversion bandwidth, conversion efficiency, detection sensitivity, imaging frame rate and synchronization. These analyses will not only provide overall guidelines for the design of the WET system, but also contribute to its image output in two implementations; namely, charged-coupled device (CCD) array and ultrafast parametric spectro-temporal analyzer (PASTA). The proposed project thus constitutes advancement in next-generation optical imaging modality in the context of ultrafast frame rate, and will contribute to future research on the improvement and optimization of new optical imaging technology. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry. 近十年來，人類對生命科學和醫療保健解決方案的需求的不斷增長，對大幅度提升各種生物光子學應用的發展提出了迫切要求。目前，各種各樣的成像技術已經在各自領域裡被廣泛認可，比如Ｘ射線影像術，核磁共振成像（MRI），計算機斷層掃描（CT），超聲波成像以及光學相干斷層掃描（OCT）。從電信系統及其發達的光電子器件的研究中獲得的專業知識為解決這些生物光子學應用的需求提供了豐富的知識基礎，特別是對光學成像技術的研究方面。光學相干斷層掃描通過探測生物組織的反射光，可以對其內部結構進行非入侵的橫斷層面成像，進而成為了其它成像技術的補充。 我們提出一種全新的光學成像模式——波長編碼斷層掃描，它通過非入侵的方式獲得斷層圖像，並使超快幀頻下實現高分辨率和高靈敏度成為可能。傳統的光學相干斷層掃描系統的幀頻受時域成像的機械掃描速度和頻域成像中重構圖像時所需的信號處理時間的限制，然而波長編碼斷層掃描系統是基於它固有的全光信號處理能力，實現了單次激發成像。它從原理上極大程度地改善了成像幀頻——高達兆赫茲甚至千兆赫茲。在這個項目中，除了實現波長編碼斷層掃描，我們還將研究它的工作性能，包括幀頻與波長范圍間的權衡，以及影響空間分辨率ˎ探測靈敏度ˎ轉換效率和功率校準的因素。這些研究不僅為波長編碼斷層掃描系統的設計提供整體指導方針，而且通過兩種實現方式有助於其圖像輸出，也就是傳統的電荷耦合器件（CCD）陳列和超快參量時域頻譜分析儀（ PASTA）。 因此，本項目預研了下一代精確光學成像模式——原理上高達兆赫茲甚至千兆赫茲的超快幀頻，它將引領未來對新型光學成像技術研究的改進和優化。這個項目中所研究的豐富知識將會對研究領域以及工業界作出突出的貢獻。

17208414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208414.value: In this project, we proposed and demonstrated an entirely new optical imaging modality, wavelength-encoded tomography (WET), that captures tomographic (i.e. layered) images in a non-invasive manner, and enables ultrafast (hundreds of megahertz or even gigahertz) axial-scan (A-scan) rate with high resolution and sensitivity. First, we demonstrated WET by leveraging the time-sensitivity of a linear frequency shifting device to differentiate the spatial depth-induced delay through two-stage four-wave mixing (FWM). We specified the spatial resolution, wavelength conversion bandwidth, conversion efficiency, etc. features of the WET system. Second, we implemented a WET prototype and its performance thoroughly characterized in a number of respects, including spatial resolution, wavelength conversion bandwidth and conversion efficiency in its wideband mechanism. Higher wavelength conversion efficiency and wider conversion bandwidth by fiber optical parametric amplifier (OPA) has also been explored. Finally, we explored WET system’s performance and its application in imaging layer structures. With these efforts, this project thus constitutes advancement in next-generation optical imaging modality in the context of ultrafast frame rate, and will contribute to future research on the improvement and optimization of new optical imaging technology. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry.

17208514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208514.value: 尋根究底：基於多項式的非線性電路設計

17208514.label: Project Objectives
17208514.value: To promulgate the framework of polynomial-based nonlinear EDA ---- an initial class of analog EDA problems transformable into polynomial problems will be showcased. On-going research efforts and innovative analytical techniques are keeping the list of amenable topics ever-expanding. To cope with modern variation-aware chip design ---- perturbation of polynomial roots subject to noisy polynomial coefficients, arising from uncertainties in analog device parameters, will be studied in terms of the matrix Jacobians and interval arithmetic. To optimize and speed up the Macaulay-matrix-based polynomial solver ---- sequential version of the solver has been implemented whose speed is already orders faster than conventional symbolic routines. Further optimization and parallelization of the in-house solver will be carried out to achieve even higher accuracy and faster runtime. A way forward is to make the solver publicly available to facilitate analog circuit design. Benchmarking by industry examples will be done to verify applicability of all developed algorithms. Long-Term Impact: The long-term impact of this project is ensured by the growing importance, alongside with emerging difficulties, in designing analog circuit blocks under the intensifying nonlinearities and process uncertainties. The success of the above goals and their streamlined integration will lead to an advanced analog design toolkit permitting speedy transient and steady-state circuit simulations, as well as robust designs accounting for fabrication and device uncertainties. This project can also provide students and research assistants with the necessary knowledge to contribute to the EDA industry and academia. The educational content of the project will be merged into postgraduate courses at HKU to provide an interdisciplinary training in circuit modeling, nonlinear theory and numerical algorithms.

17208514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208514.value: 從字面和實際上，這個專案試圖解決非線性電子設計自動化（EDA）中``根’’的問題。具體而言，求解多項式方程組的根是大量類比（非線性）電路合成和分析問題，包括元件參數的選擇和直流工作點的評估等中的核心任務。求解多項式系統的主流方法包括計算代數的Gröbner基和分支定界方法，然而，它們的指數複雜性使它們一般對實際問題計算過慢。更通用的牛頓法對初始條件非常敏感，同時既不能保證收斂性也不保證全域最優解。最近一個重大突破是將矩陣線性代數與（非線性）多元多項式方程組聯繫起來。這是通過Macaulay矩陣的設置和使用來實現的，它的零空間就對應多項式的根。所有有限解集都可以用這種方法很快找到，也可以容易從中選擇最優解。由於它的非符號性質和容易的數值實現，係數不確定性和/或靈敏度的影響可以也容易考慮進來，從而使得這種方法非常適合於感知變化的混合信號晶片設計。 本專案有兩層主題：拓展基於多項式的類比電路EDA的應用範圍和優化數值多項式求根方法。為了實現這一點，我們提出了三個主要目標： 1．提供一個基於對多項式的表示和求解的統一框架來處理一系列類比電路EDA問題。 2. 將工藝和參數的可變性引入該多項式框架來確保類比晶片設計的魯棒性。 3. 利用矩陣結構和平行計算來加快基於Macaulay的多項式求解。 該專案的成果，無疑將為多項式表達和求解在非線性類比電路方面的應用, 提供一個革新的視角。應用實例的積累將激發EDA社群的創新熱情,引入更多多項式的問題，這反過來將促使研究者開發更快的求解方法。通過用Matlab /Octave等流行語言程式設計並將代碼公開，晶片設計人員可以很容易將多項式求解器嵌入到他們自己的EDA流程，從而縮短設計週期和上市時間。由專案產生的理論研究和實際工作會激勵研究者和應用者，並幫助培養學生和工作人員在EDA領域做出貢獻。

17208514.label: Realisation of objectives
17208514.value: In the following, we present the realization of project objectives in a coherent summary (where the corresponding objectives are mentioned in appropriate places). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Many circuits and systems in the scope of electronic design automation (EDA) are often sufficiently approximated by sets of multivariate polynomials. The roots (or solutions) of these systems of polynomial equations can then be given specific physical interpretations like the equilibrium points of the dynamical system or the poles of this system. In some cases, this is the only information one has upon which a model of these circuits and systems can be constructed. For example, the periodic steady state (PSS) of an autonomous or periodically excited system is closely tied to the poles of the system model. In • K. Batselier and N. Wong, “Inverse multivariate polynomial root-finding: numerical implementations of the affine and projective Buchberger-Moller algorithm, Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics,” vol. 320, pp. 15-- 29, Aug. 2017. we have developed and implemented pioneering and novel algorithms to construct these multivariate polynomial models solely from information of the equilibrium points and poles and applied them to several cases (e.g. the Vanderpol oscillator, Lotka-Volterra and Fitzhug-Nagumo systems) to demonstrate the effectiveness of polynomial-based modeling, without the need of initial guesses, for solving the PSS of oscillator dynamics commonly found in mixed-model chips. This is a problem which used to be difficult using harmonic balance or Newton shooting methods, both being sensitive to the quality of initial guesses. (-->Objective #1 fully accomplished.) We then extended these algorithms with the ability for the user to fix the degrees of the polynomials to arbitrary values by adding additional "roots at infinity": • K. Batselier and N. Wong, “Computing the state difference equations for discrete overdetermined linear mD systems,” Automatica, vol. 64, pp. 254--261, Feb 2016. This extension provides more flexibility to the user by allowing him/her to design the polynomial approximation much more accurately, and readily incorporates polynomial bounds of uncertainties within the modeling framework. (-->Objective #2 fully accomplished.) Nonetheless, the above works are still based on conventional matrix algebra and operations. It quickly became apparent though that an explicit construction of the Macaulay matrix in these applications limits the applicability of the algorithms as the dimensions of this matrix grow exponentially with the degree. This is the so-called curse of dimensionality. Over the past decade, research on tensor decompositions in order to lift this curse has picked up considerate momentum and various algorithms were developed to compute these decompositions with convincing successful applications. In short, tensors are generalizations of vectors and matrices to higher orders. Our group turned to tensor research with the goal to represent the Macaulay matrix in the polynomial root-finding solver by a tensor decomposition, thus lifting its inherent curse of dimensionality. Subsequently, our team set forth to exploit the intimate connection between tensors and homogeneous multivariate polynomials. When applying the most-common tensor decomposition, the canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD), to the Macaulay matrix we stumbled into the problem of the tensor rank. Indeed, the tensor rank is crucial to be able to represent the Macaulay matrix and the corresponding polynomials accurately, yet finding the tensor rank is an NP-hard problem. In order to tackle this problem, we developed a constructive algorithm to compute a CPD-like tensor decomposition, called the TTr1SVD, where each rank-1 term is orthogonal to all the others: • K. Batselier, H. Liu and N. Wong, “A constructive algorithm for decomposing a tensor into a finite sum of orthonormal rank-1 terms,” SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications, vol. 36, no. 3, pp. 1315-1337, Sep 2015. An additional benefit of the TTr1SVD is that the tensor rank of this decomposition is computed by the algorithm and one therefore obtains, without any additional cost, an exact representation of the given tensor. The orthogonality of these rank-1 terms are very promising as this would allow us to define tensors that are orthogonal to a given tensor, which is a generalization of the concept of a nullspace for matrices to tensors. For the Macaulay matrix, these rank-1 nullspace tensors are then connected to the roots of the corresponding polynomial system. (-->Objective #3 fully accomplished) The intimate connection between multivariate polynomials and tensors was further exploited in speeding up the simulation of circuits and systems in • H. Liu, L. Daniel and N. Wong, “Model reduction and simulation of nonlinear circuits via tensor decomposition,” IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems, vol. 34, no. 7, pp. 1059-1069, Jul 2015. • J. Deng, H. Liu, K. Batselier, Y. K. Kwok and N. Wong, “STORM: a nonlinear model order reduction method via symmetric tensor decomposition,” in Proc. Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASPDAC), Jan 2016, pp. 557--562. • H. Liu, X. Xiong, K. Batselier, L. Jiang, L. Daniel and N. Wong, “STAVES: speedy tensor-aided Volterra-based electronic simulator,” in Prof. Intl. Conf. on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD), Nov 2015, pp. 583--588. • K. Batselier, Q. Chen and N. Wong, “An adaptive dynamical low-rank tensor approximation scheme for fast circuit simulation,” in Proc. Intl. Conf. on ASIC (ASICON), Nov 2015, pp. 1-- 4. In these publications the representation of multivariate polynomials as tensors together with the application of our developed TTr1SVD decomposition are used to lift the curse of dimensionality of describing higher order polynomials. In addition, by allowing the tensor rank to be smaller than its canonical value one can further reduce the storage complexity of the tensor, thereby speeding up the simulation significantly by orders. Working codes of the above works have all been released to the public domain allowing free access and modifications by EDA researchers and practitioners. (-->Objective #4 fully accomplished.)

17208514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208514.value: As depicted in the previous section, namely, “Realisation of objectives”, the first major outcome is the significant enhancement of the Macaulay matrix machinery to allow a novel and non-trivial two-way application. That is, besides the traditional use in solving for roots of polynomial equations, we further utilize the Macaulay framework to solve the *inverse* problem of setting up a polynomial system given the set of roots/system poles. This enables us to reverse-engineer a circuit nonlinear state-space model when its behavior is known from external measurement or numerical simulation. Then, our team has drawn the important connection between polynomials and tensors, and discovered that multivariate polynomials are naturally cast into a formalism of tensor mode products. Our team then generated a series of tensor publications featuring various efficient tensor decompositions, and applied them to a multitude of electronic design automation (EDA) problems with immense success. In fact, the PI’s team is among the first to promulgate the use of tensor arithmetic in EDA, which opens up a new direction and room for exciting research and practical investigations.

17208514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208514.value: The research outcome of this project had directly inspired its next two GRF proposals featuring the highly beneficial use of tenors in different EDA areas, which were also granted thanks to the RGC panel and recognition from reviewers. As noted in the previous section, it is recognized that an intimate link exists between polynomial systems and tensor mode product formulation. The results of this project have largely inspired the PI’s team to dig deeper into tensors and their utilization in EDA problems, finally giving rise to the recent keynote paper: Z. Zhang, K. Batselier, H. Liu, L. Daniel and N. Wong, "Tensor computation: a new framework for high-dimensional problems in EDA," (Keynote Paper) IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems, vol. 36, no. 4, pp. 521--536, Apr 2017. Subsequently, our on-going goal and course of action is to draw further connections between tensors and EDA problems. The power of tensors for lifting the curse of dimensionality in emerging large-scale EDA problems is definitely a sustainable and rewarding research topic for now and the foreseeable future.

17208514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208514.value: First, besides the standard use of Macaulay matrix in solving for roots of polynomial equations, we further developed and utilized the Macaulay framework to tackle the inverse problem of deriving a polynomial system given the set of roots/system poles. This allows the reverse-engineering of a compact polynomial-based circuit state space model when prior knowledge of the external behavior is known from measurement or numerical simulation. Then, our team has drawn the key connection between polynomials and tensors, and discovered that multivariate polynomials are naturally cast into a formalism of tensor mode products. Our team then generated a series of tensor publications featuring various efficient tensor decompositions (including generic and symmetric tensors), and applied them to a multitude of electronic design automation (EDA) problems with immense success, practically lifting the curse of dimensionality previously faced by these problems. In fact, the PI’s team is among the first to promulgate the use of tensor arithmetic in EDA (cf. our IEEE Keynote Paper on Tensor-based EDA mentioned in the previous section), which opens up a whole new direction and room for exciting research and practical investigations.

17208614.label: Project Objectives
17208614.value: To establish the fundamental relationships between traffic quantities for the development of a dynamic continuum model. To formulate a sustainable land use and transportation (SLUT) model in a systematic and consistent manner for the planning of an urban city. To set up effective and efficient solution procedures to solve the SLUT model. To develop a bi-level programming procedure for a sustainable land use and transportation optimization (SLUTO) framework for urban design problems.
rows: To establish the fundamental relationships between traffic quantities for the development of a dynamic continuum model.
To formulate a sustainable land use and transportation (SLUT) model in a systematic and consistent manner for the planning of an urban city.
To set up effective and efficient solution procedures to solve the SLUT model.
To develop a bi-level programming procedure for a sustainable land use and transportation optimization (SLUTO) framework for urban design problems.

17208614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208614.value: Land use and transportation, and their interactions, are essential elements of a sustainable development plan for an urban city. Using a continuum modeling approach, we will develop a sustainable land use and transportation (SLUT) model in which land use attributes and travel demands are continuously distributed across a city that has several highly compact central business districts. In this SLUT model, the users’ location choices depend on the land use availability, rent, accessibility, and environmental conditions. The city’s dense transportation network is approximated as a continuum. Travelers are free to choose their routes through this two-dimensional continuum space in a predictive dynamic user-optimal manner such that the actual travel costs experienced on any used routes are equal and minimal for any users traveling between any origin-destination pair who are leaving their origin at any instant; further, the actual travel costs that they would have experienced on any unused routes are greater than or equal to the minimum actual travel cost on the used routes. All of the traffic quantities, including density, flow, and speed, are time-dependent. Locally, we will build macroscopic fundamental diagrams using data from the Hong Kong networks, and then establish the effects of topological characteristics on the macroscopic relationships. Globally, in the two-dimensional city domain, the spatio-temporal traffic movement pattern is governed by the spatially variable macroscopic fundamental diagrams, the conservation law, and appropriate initial and boundary conditions. All of the model specifications will be translated into a set of partial differential equations with appropriate boundary conditions, based on the continuous variables defined in the problem. The SLUT model will be solved with efficient numerical solvers. We will conduct a sensitivity analysis of the solution to obtain the derivative information of the continuous variables; the results will be used to establish a bi-level programming framework for sustainable urban design problems. In this sustainable land use and transportation optimization framework, the objective functions are the total travel and environmental costs, subject to the development, budgetary, and other socio-economic constraints that govern the social aspects of sustainable development, such as equity issues. The control variables are land use development in the long term and road pricing scheme in the short term. 土地利用、交通以及兩者的交互作用是城市可持續發展規劃中的重要元素。通過一個連續模型的建模方法，我們可以根據用地特徵和交通需求為一個擁有高度密集商業中心的城市建立一個可持續用地和交通（SLUT）模型。在這個SLUT模型中，使用者位置的選擇取決於土地的可利用性、地租、可達性以及環境條件，而城市的密集交通網絡則被假計為一個連續流。使用者能夠隨意以一個動態和可預測的方式在這個二維連續空間內選擇路線。而對於每位使用者來說，無論他們在何時於任何起始點離開，每條路線的實際通行費用都是最小並且是相同的。相比之下，其他路線的實際通行費用會相等或高於他們選擇的路線。所有交通的特徵值，包括密度、流量、速度都是與時間有關的。我們將會利用香港道路網路的資料建立宏觀的基本圖，並且探索佈局（拓撲）特徵對宏觀關係的影響。對於一般情況，由於時間與空間的交通移動模式在二維城市領域中是受空間變化的宏觀基本圖、守恆定律以及合適的初始和邊界條件控制的，所以基於問題中定義的連續變數，所有模型的設定將會以一組帶有合適邊界條件的偏導數式來描述。SLUT模型會用高效的數學辦法來解決。我們會採用靈敏度分析的方法以獲得連續變數的導數資訊。而該結論將會被應用于建立一個可持續城市設計的雙層程式設計框架。在這個可持續用地和交通優化的框架中，目標函數是總通行和環境消費。而這個函數則由發展、預算和其他決定著可持續發展的社會性內容的社會經濟條件，例如公正問題所制約的。控制變數為長期用地發展和短期土地價格計畫。

17208614.label: Realisation of objectives
17208614.value: To achieve Objective (1), Hong Kong traffic data were collected to derive the fundamental relationships between traffic quantities. The data were obtained from two major sources: a stationary source, namely fixed detectors providing traffic count data, and a mobile source, namely probe vehicles supplying Global Positioning System (GPS) data. The stationary source provided high-resolution data with limited spatial coverage; the mobile source offered greater spatial coverage but a lower sampling rate. We integrated the data from these stationary and mobile sources using a linear data projection method to reveal the traffic conditions in the street systems under consideration. This enabled us to establish the fundamental relationships between traffic quantities, including speed, flow, and density. These relationships are the building blocks of continuum models. However, systematic biases were discovered in the estimation procedure. Effective methods were developed to reduce these biases to improve the reliability of the estimated model parameters and their standard errors. To address the variability of network topology between districts of an urban city, the effects of street patterns on these parameters were also established, enabling the representation of topological effects on traffic movements by continuum modeling. To achieve Objective (2), we formulated sustainable land use and transportation (SLUT) models for the planning of urban cities. We first enhanced the continuum modeling technique by interfacing with a discrete road network, incorporating elastic demand, and considering departure time choice. Both predictive and reactive user equilibrium principles were investigated. In the reactive model, users were assumed to make route choices based on instantaneous traffic conditions, whereas the predictive model assumed that users made route choice decisions according to actual traffic costs. Two SLUT models were considered. The first model established a procedure for estimating the total greenhouse emissions due to traffic movements arising from different land use patterns in an urban city, which provided a useful tool for addressing the problem of climate change. The second SLUT model took account of the dispersion of air pollutants due to meteorological conditions in the land use and transportation problem, which aided evaluation of the long-term air quality conditions in different parts of the city. This model offered a useful means of representing residents’ choice of housing locations, in addition to the conventional attributes of accessibility and rent. To achieve Objective (3), effective and efficient procedures were developed to solve the SLUT models. These continuum models comprised several major building blocks: a macroscopic fundamental diagram that described the relationship between traffic quantities, a conservation law governing the conservation of traffic in the system, an Eikonal equation representing the route choice strategy, and an advection-diffusion equation governing the dispersion of air pollutants. Conventional continuum models assume isotropic conditions, in which traffic speed is independent of movement directions. In reality, traffic speed is anisotropic, due to the different topological settings of street networks. We developed a self-adaptive method of successive averages to handle this anisotropic problem. The conservation equation and advection-diffusion equation were both solved using an efficient weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme, whereas the Eikonal equation was solved by the fast sweeping method. The stability of the time incremental steps was maintained using the total variation diminishing (TVD) Runge-Kutta method. Both rectangular grid and unstructured grid schemes were derived to solve problems for cities with regular boundary conditions and complicated boundary conditions, respectively. These solution algorithms were effective and efficient in solving the SLUT models developed in the study. To achieve Objective (4), we formulated a bi-level optimization of land use and transportation infrastructure for the planning and design of urban cities. We used housing allocation as a control variable in the upper-level sub-program, and the lower-level sub-program was the developed SLUT model. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to derive the gradient of the objective function (total greenhouse emissions) with respect to the control variable (housing allocation pattern), based on which the Frank-Wolfe algorithm was established to solve the bi-level program. This procedure helped to identify an optimal land use development pattern that minimized the total greenhouse gas emissions resulting from traffic movements in polycentric cities.

17208614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208614.value: The fundamental relationships between traffic quantities were studied based on GPS data in Hong Kong [J7]. To take advantage of both stationary and mobile sources of data, scaling factors were constructed to estimate the area-wide traffic quantities in selected areas of Hong Kong [J13]. To remove biases discovered in the expected values and standard errors, comprehensive procedures were established for both linear modeling [J1, J6, C6] and nonlinear modeling [J15, J17, C9]. Dr. Wai Wong, a PhD student under the supervision of Professor S. C. Wong, received the HKSTS Outstanding Dissertation Paper Award cum Gordon Newell Memorial Prize in 2018, based on the work in [J17]. Based on information on street patterns [J3], the effects of topological characteristics on the developed macroscopic speed-flow relationships were studied [J5, C3]. The continuum modeling technique was enhanced in several dimensions by interfacing with discrete road networks [J4, C7], incorporating elastic demand [J12], and simultaneously considering departure time and route choice [J14, C8]. Two dynamic continuum user equilibrium models were explored: predictive user equilibrium [J10, J14, C2, C8] and reactive user equilibrium [J12, C11]. We first developed a SLUT model to estimate total carbon dioxide emissions in an urban city [J18, C1, C5]. For housing choice problems, we considered a utility function comprising three choice attributes, namely accessibility (or travel cost), rent, and environmental conditions (or air quality), in the second SLUT model [J9, J16, C10, C11]. The conventional approach to solving continuum models is the finite element method [J4, C7, C9]. However, for the dynamic models developed in this study, the finite difference scheme was more promising [J8]. To address anisotropic conditions, a self-adaptive method of successive averages was developed [J2]. To effectively solve the conservation equations coupled with the Eikonal equation, we established an integrated numerical scheme consisting of a high-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory method and a fast sweeping method, together with a high-order TVD Runge-Kutta method [J10, J12, J14, C2, C8]. To simultaneously consider departure time and route choice, the model was formulated as a variational inequality problem solved by the projection method [J14]. The high-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory method was also adopted to solve the advection-diffusion equation [J16, C10, C11]. Several urban design problems were considered, including reliability-based analysis [C4], tolling structure in a linear continuum city [J11], and housing allocation problems [C1, C5]. To reduce greenhouse gas emissions, we formulated the problem as a bi-level program to determine the optimal housing allocation in an urban city [J18].

17208614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208614.value: Conventional continuum models often assume that the parameters of the macroscopic relationships between traffic quantities are deterministic. In reality, however, this is often not the case due to the stochastic variability of endogenous user characteristics and exogenous environmental factors. Therefore, we anticipate that the parameters of the macroscopic relationships that govern local travel cost will follow certain probabilistic distributions in representing these stochastic variability effects, thus influencing the route choice patterns in the dynamic user equilibrium model. This will result in a set of stochastic partial differential equations for the continuum modeling of traffic or pedestrian movements. Traditional methods of solving these kinds of stochastic problems are based on Monte Carlo simulation and polynomial chaos expansion, neither of which is an efficient means of solving high-dimensional problems. However, the identification of intrinsic low-dimensional structures in these high-dimensional stochastic partial differential equations will enable the development of reduced-order models and better formulations for efficient numerical schemes. The development of dynamic-stochastic user equilibrium models will greatly enhance the applicability of these methods to real-world problems. A research proposal based on the findings of this project has been submitted to the Research Grants Council’s General Research Fund in the 2019-2020 exercise.

17208614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208614.value: Land use and transportation, and the interactions between them, are essential elements of a sustainable development plan for an urban city. Using a continuum modeling approach, we have developed sustainable land use and transportation (SLUT) models in which land use attributes and travel demands are continuously distributed across a city with one or more highly compact central business districts. In these SLUT models, the users’ location choices depend on accessibility, rent, and environmental conditions. The city’s dense transportation network is approximated as a continuum. Travelers are free to choose their routes through this two-dimensional continuum space in a dynamic user-optimal manner. Locally, we constructed macroscopic fundamental diagrams using data from Hong Kong road networks, and then established the effects of topological characteristics on the macroscopic relationships identified. Globally, in the two-dimensional city domain, the spatio-temporal patterns of traffic movement were shown to be governed by spatially variable macroscopic fundamental diagrams, the conservation law, and appropriate initial and boundary conditions. The SLUT models were solved using efficient numerical solvers. We established a bi-level programming framework for sustainable urban design problems. The study provides a promising methodology for the conceptual planning of an urban city.

17209014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209014.value: In the recent two decades, producer services in China have been growing rapidly as a direct consequence of deepened market reforms, state policy support, and accelerated globalization. These activities are found to be highly concentrated in a few major cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. On the other hand, since the late 2000s, China’s urban development is undergoing a new phase of transition in which the development of high speed rail (HSR) is significantly reshaping the economic space. It is observed in the West that the advancement of transportation and telecommunication technologies is leading to a process of decentralization, although central cities remain important to harbor producer services. China is building the world’s largest HSR network to improve inter-city accessibility. Many Chinese municipal governments have reformulated urban development strategy to make use of this new way of transportation to develop producer services and central business districts (CBDs) to enhance their competitiveness in the era of globalization. However, although it is widely recognized that positive relationship exists between transportation infrastructure development and economic growth, it remains unclear about the spatial impacts of HSR development due to the debatable findings in the existing literature. Relatively less is known about how the operation of HSR has affected the spatial development of producer services in China. What kinds of cities are winners and what kinds of cities are losers? Some of the cities may overestimate the effects of HSR. Their CBDs may be over-done, leading to a waste of resources. This proposed research will investigate the process and pattern of China’s producer service development since 2008 when HSR was introduced. It will conduct systematic quantitative and qualitative analyses to examine the relationship between the operation of HSR and the spatial development of producer services, and analyze the location and operation strategies of producer services in a new context of urban development. This proposed project will advance theoretical enquiry in the existing literature and benefit decision-making on China’s urban planning and economic and urban development. Moreover, producer services are one of the main pillars of Hong Kong’s economy, and the city is developing HSR which will connect the country’s network and will be opened in 2016. This proposed research will be of direct relevance to decision-making on Hong Kong’s economic and urban development, helping identify its potential partners and competitors in producer service development through HSR connections.

17209014.label: Realisation of objectives
17209014.value: (1) Identify the process and pattern of producer service development in the Chinese urban system since 2008 (100%). Firm-level data have been collected and analyses have been carried out to better understand the spatial distribution of producer services at different scales. Apart from identifying the location pattern of producer services, we have compared manufacturing and producer services to reveal the spatial linkages between these two industries. This has contributed to the existing debate on the evolving manufacturing-services relationship. Moreover, given the regional-oriented characteristics of producer services, we have identified the range of hinterland of major producer service concentrations in China. Two papers have been published in SSCI journals. (2) Investigate the relationship between HSR development and the change in producer service distribution (100%). As the major effect of HSR lies in its capability to improve inter-city accessibility, we used the increase in market potential due to the reduction of travel time to measure the impact of HSR development. To separate the impact of HSR from other inter-city travel mode, an online survey in 14 selected Chinese cities (including representative cities of different size and in different regions) and a site survey in Guangzhou on the travel behaviors of the passengers have been conducted. Quantitative analyses have been undertaken to reveal the relationship between HSR development and the change in the spatial economy of the Chinese urban system from the service perspective. One manuscript has been submitted and under review by Urban Studies, top journal in our field. (3) Analyze the location considerations and operation strategies of producer services in the context of HSR development (100%). Based on a thorough search and review of the existing literature, the theories and explanations on producer service location have been critically evaluated and major factors affecting the uneven growth of producer services have been identified. Field trips and interviews with producer service providers have been conducted to understand their location considerations in the cities where they are located and how HSR development has affected their economic performance.

17209014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209014.value: (1) The distribution of producer service development in the urban system and its spatial relationship with manufacturing activities A comparison was made between the locations of producer services and manufacturing at the city as well as the county levels. Our findings suggest that manufacturing and producer services are less likely to co-locate despite their close input-output linkage because of the distinctive process of rural industrialization has not reduced the importance of large cities and city centers in producer service development. This is different from the general expectation that manufacturing and producer services have incentives to locate close to each other where manufacturing is still an important component of the national economy in the developing countries. We have published one paper in Habitat International, key journal in our field. (2) Regional effects of producer services on manufacturing productivity in China Given that producer services are tradable and essential for improving manufacturing productivity and efficiency, we explore the interactions and connections between manufacturing and producer services at the regional level in China. We identify the range or hinterland that producer services can possess to benefit manufacturing firm operation. Our findings indicate that the effects of producer services on manufacturing productivity are not limited to local firms but are regional oriented. A paper has been published in Applied Geography, key journal in our field. (3) Impacts of high-speed rail on the spatial economy of the Chinese urban system from the service perspective As an efficient long-distance transport system, HSR development and its consequence on the spatial restructuring of regions has received considerable attention. We have conducted a study to examine the impacts of HSR construction on the spatial economy of the Chinese urban system, with a special focus on the spatial change in service development. Our findings suggest that the construction boom of HSR in China leads to a direct and considerable growth in service demand and effectively reduces the disparity among cities with access to the HSR network. By stimulating the growth of new service centers and improving the accessibility of cities near the core metropolises, HSR in China improves the polycentricity of the urban system and a “divergent convergence” pattern in major mega-city regions. The paper submitted to Urban Studies, top journal in our field, has been attached in the report.

17209014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209014.value: The following two issues warrant further examination : (1) In our project, we analyze the impact of HSR operation on service development at a broader urban system level without probing into the changes within cities. Existing literature suggests that the HSR terminal led to significant increases in commercial, business, tourist, and other service sectors, which had provided a boost for the local economy, leading to urban sprawl and the transformation of the urban economy. Therefore, more detailed case studies should be conducted to better understand the intra-urban location dynamic of producer services resulting from the construction of HSR. (2) Impact of HSR on Hong Kong-PRD economic integration. Producer services are one of the main pillars of Hong Kong’s economy, and the city has developed HSR services which connect the country’s network. Since the 2000s, the industrial linkages between Hong Kong and the PRD has evolved from manufacturing-services to services-services connection as a result of the rapid growth of producer services in China. How will the improvement of inter-city mobility strengthen the linkages of producer services between Hong Kong and the PRD? This is an issue important for Hong Kong’s future economic and urban development.

17209014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209014.value: After the commencement of HSR in 2008, the expanding HSR network has significantly rearranged the economic space in China. Given the vital importance of producer services in facilitating economic growth, how HSR development has reshaped the distribution of producer services becomes an important issue for scholarly enquiry. Producer services tend to concentrate in certain metropolitan centers where favorable economic and technological infrastructure is available and where the benefits of agglomeration are found. They may also disperse when transportation and telecommunication advancement enables them to enjoy lower wages and rent and a better living environment in locations outside existing metropolitan centers. China is building the world’s largest HSR network. Improvement in accessibility can provide new development opportunities for the peripheral regions, but can further enhance the attractiveness of central regions as well. Many local governments have reformulated urban strategies to make use of HSR to develop producer services and central business districts (CBDs). Some cities may overestimate the effects of HSR. Their CBDs may be over-done, leading to a waste of resources. Our research has advanced the theoretical enquiry for HSR on urban system development and can help to guide urban planning and economic and urban development of Chinese cities.

17209214.label: Project Objectives

rows: Develop methods for unsupervised short-term monitoring of human-induced land cover changes using RADARSAT-2 PolSAR images.

17209214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209214.value: 非法土地利用是當今中國在快速發展中所面臨的一大問題。該問題已經導致耕地數量的銳减，幷且嚴重威脅到城市的可持續發展。及時獲取土地開發活動的信息對于監測非法建設用地至關重要。由于土地開發常常伴隨著劇烈的土地覆蓋變化，因此短期監測開發活動所引起的土地覆蓋變化對于早期發現和整治非法土地利用至關重要。光學遙感由于受天氣條件及日光的限制，常常在獲取多雲多雨地區的土地覆蓋信息時遇到困難。衛星極化合成孔徑雷達遙感由于不受天氣和日光的限制，幷且在土地覆蓋分類中優于傳統的單極化雷達影像，因此非常適用于短周期監測土地覆蓋變化。 分類後比較法常用于遙感影像的變化檢測。該方法不僅能檢測到變化區域，同時還可以確定變化的類別。然而，分類後比較法受分類精度的限制。目前大多數衛星極化雷達系統只能獲取單波段的極化雷達影像，幷且極化雷達影像具有很强的斑點噪聲。由于受到光譜信息的限制及斑點噪聲的影響，極化雷達影像的分類精度都比較低。因此，當應用于極化雷達影像時，分類後比較法可能會産生較差的結果。此外，目前大多數的分類方法爲監督分類方法。這類方法依賴于從圖像中選取的訓練樣本。訓練樣本通常是通過野外實地觀測選取的。短周期土地覆蓋變化監測勢必要求頻繁的野外實地調查，從而花費大量的時間，人力及物力。另外，短周期監測開發活動引起的土地覆蓋變化可能會受到植被季節性生長的影響。季節性的自然植被及農作物的生長會導致大量的土地覆蓋變化。這些變化很容易與土地開發活動引起的變化相混淆，從而會對監測土地開發活動産生誤差。 本研究的目的爲探索從RADARSAT-2極化雷達影像中自動提取開發活動引起的土地覆蓋變化的新方法。研究將集成自動變化檢測算法，分類後比較法，及面向對象的圖像分析方法從極化雷達影像中提取出土地覆蓋變化。通過减少雷達斑點噪聲及分類精度對變化檢測的影響，該集成方法將大大提過土地覆蓋變化檢測的精度。本研究還將探討基于决策樹規則的非監督分類方法用于極化雷達影像的分類。按照預先定義的决策樹結構進行層次的非監督分類，該分類方法可用于不同時間獲取的極化雷達影像的土地覆蓋分類幷且不需要任何訓練樣本。此外，本研究還會探索自動區分開發活動引起的土地覆蓋變化和季節性植被生長所引起的土地覆蓋變化的新方法。該方法將利用從極化雷達影像中所提取的干涉信息及多時相土地覆蓋分類信息鑒別開發活動所引起的土地覆蓋變化。

17209214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209214.value: a) Investigation of the effects of PolSAR frequency variation on land cover classification A comparison was made between an L-band PALSAR PolSAR image and a C-band RADARSAT-2 PolSAR image for land cover classification. The comparison showed that C-band image performed better than L-band image in identifying water, bare land, vegetation, and built-up areas. After that, polarimetric decomposition theorems were used to analyze the mechanisms how the PolSAR frequency variation affects the land cover classification. The analyses indicated that L- and C-band images produced different classification results because the frequency variation affected the differences in scattering mechanisms between different land cover categories. C-band image created more substantial differences in volume scattering between water and bare land, volume scattering between bare land and crops, and dihedral scattering between built-up areas and forests than L-band image. C-band image was better because of its higher sensitivity to surface roughness and smaller penetration power than L-band image. As land development mainly involves changes from vegetation to bare land and those from bare land to built-up areas, our investigations indicate that C-band RADARSAT-2 PolSAR images are suitable for the monitoring of land developments. We have written a paper for submission to international journal which is attached in this report. b) A crop phenology knowledge-based approach for detecting monthly construction land expansion We developed an innovative crop phenology knowledge-based approach to detect monthly construction land expansion by using consecutive polarimetric SAR imagery to remove errors introduced by seasonal crop growth. Using crop phenology knowledge as a basis, a knowledge-based system is built to automatically determine when seasonal crop growth yields considerable errors. A comparison was made between the proposed approach and the traditional approach for the monthly monitoring of construction land expansion. We found that seasonal paddy growth created many errors by using the traditional approach. Compared with the traditional approach, the proposed approach reduced errors by up to 87.33% with an average overall error rate of only 0.24%. The results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms the traditional approach in monitoring monthly construction land expansion and suppressing the disturbance from seasonal crop growth. The integration of this crop phenology knowledge-based approach with the method that we proposed for automatic PolSAR image classification will achieve a fully automatic monitoring of construction land expansion. We have published one paper in ISPRS, which is the best journal in remote sensing. The paper has been attached in this report.

17209214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209214.value: Further studies will be carried out to integrate optical and SAR remote sensing data for the detection of construction land expansion. Optical images produce higher accuracies for land cover classification than SAR data, while SAR data achieve shorter detection interval than optical images. Moreover, SAR and optical remote sensing data are sensitive to different properties of ground targets; thus, they provide complementary information to each other. Therefore, the combination of SAR and optical remote sensing data has a great potential to significantly improve accuracies for the short-term monitoring of construction land expansion. With the fieldwork data that we have collected, we will further examine the use of deep-learning for unsupervised change detection.

17209214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209214.value: The ruthless unauthorized land developments have caused many social and environmental problems in many developing countries, such as arable land loss, urban sprawl, and ecological degradation. Traditional optical remote sensing is limited by weather conditions; thus, it experiences difficulties in preventing unauthorized land use. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which is nearly weather independent, is promising for timely monitoring of land developments. However, land cover classification using SAR images is based on the manual selection of training samples, which requires SAR professionals and field investigations that consume a considerable labor and money. Moreover, seasonal crop growth causes land cover changes that are hardly distinguishable from land developments by using SAR images. By addressing these issues, this study develops new methods for the monitoring of land developments using SAR images. The methods allow for the automatic extraction of land cover information from SAR images and are capable of utilizing crop phenology knowledge to automatically remove errors induced by seasonal crop growth. As a result, the proposed methods can achieve a fully automatic monitoring of land developments using SAR images. This study is significant to the prevention of unauthorized land use, especially in the perpetually cloud-covered equatorial and tropical regions.

17209614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209614.value: High strength steel structures have been increasingly used in structural and architectural applications. Their superior mechanical properties allow the use of slender sections, and hence design of creative and aesthetic structures. Furthermore, cold-formed steel structural members are formed at room temperature, and the effect of cold-working will enhance the yield stress of the material. The amount of constructional material needed can be reduced due to high strength material. The high strength of steel material and cold-forming sections due to cold-working will lead to cost saving and environment friendly in construction industry. However, there is no design rule for cold-formed high strength steel structural members with nominal yield stress greater than 700 MPa. Research on high strength steel material is also limited up to date, which restricted the use of such material in construction. Columns and beams are the important and essential structural elements. Furthermore, tubular sections having aesthetic and structural advantages are frequently used by engineers and architects. However, research on cold-formed high strength steel tubular columns and beams is rarely found in literatures. Design rules of steel columns and beams are available in the American Specification (AISC, 2010), Australian Standard (AS, 1998), Australian/New Zealand Standard (AS/NZS, 2005), North American Specification (AISI, 2012) and European Code (EC3, 2006), but these design rules do not cover high strength steel material with yield stress higher than 700 MPa. Therefore, there is a need to investigate the structural behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel structural members. The objectives of this research project are to provide member strengths of cold-formed high strength steel tubular columns and beams with nominal yield stress up to 1100 MPa. Therefore, design recommendations for cold-formed high strength steel tubular columns and beams will be proposed. 17209714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209714.value: There exist trillions of digital photos in the world because of the prevalence of digital cameras and mobile phones. More and more images are captured using imaging devices with low-end lenses and optics, such as those found in mobile phones, and with shooting conditions where lighting and exposure are less than perfect. Manually adjusting a photo to improve its quality or adding artistic effects is often tedious and labor-intensive. The sheer volume of photos demands low-cost automatic or semi-automatic photo editing and enhancement tools. Image editing and enhancement are important research topics in computational photography and image-based graphics. Nevertheless, photo adjustment is a highly empirical and perceptual process. Photographer and artists decide photo adjustment operations according to high-level image semantics, such as the types of objects (such as faces and cars) and surfaces (such as terrain and building surfaces) present in the image. Nevertheless, most existing techniques are still based on low-level image feature statistics. Therefore, we propose semantics-aware techniques to overcome this limitation. Semantics-aware techniques perform photo adjustment or transformation according to the semantics of the input photo, much like what artists and photographers do. Thus they have the potential to achieve significantly better results much closer to those manually produced by human experts. In this project, we plan to focus on semantics-aware color and tone style editing, color theme enhancement and photo stylization and abstraction. The outcomes of our proposed research will significantly advance the state of the art in digital photo editing and enhancement. The proposed research on semantics-aware RGB-D image and video abstraction and enhancement will inspire much future work and steer more researchers' attention towards this direction. We also plan to improve computer vision algorithms related to image semantic analysis, and make them more suitable for computational photography. Thus, the proposed project has an interdisciplinary nature, and will advance the state of the art on certain computer vision research topics as well. The proposed research has important practical values. If our project is successful, publications resulting from our work will have influence on future versions of industrial photo editing software, such as Adobe Photoshop and Google Picasa. 因為數碼相機和手機的流行，目前世界上存在以萬億計的數碼照片。越來越多的圖像被（比如那些配置在手機上的）低端透鏡和光學成像器件所捕獲，或是在照明和曝光不盡如人意的條件下拍攝的。手動調節照片來提高它們的質量或添加藝術效果往往是一項非常乏味和耗力的工作。目前照片的數量要求低成本的自動或半自動的照片編輯與增強工具。 圖像編輯與增強在計算攝影學和基於圖像的圖形學中是重要的研究課題。雖然如此，但是照片調整是一個非常憑經驗和感知的過程。攝影師和藝術家根據高層次的圖像語義決定照片調整所需要的操作。這些語義包括圖像中的物體（如人臉和汽車）和表面（如地面和建築物的表面）的類型。大多數現有技術仍然是基於低級別的圖像特徵的統計特性。因此，我們提出感知語義的技術來克服這種局限性。感知語義的技術根據輸入圖像的語義調整或變換照片，就像藝術家和攝影師所做的。因此，這類技術有潛力實現與人類專家的手工製作更接近的結果。在擬建項目中，我們計劃專注於感知語義的色彩與明暗的編輯，以及照片的抽象與風格化。 我們的研究成果將推進數碼照片編輯與增強的技術現狀。在基於語義識別的RGB-D圖像的抽象與增強方面的研究會激發後續工作，把更多的研究人員的注意力引向該方向。我們還計劃改進相關的計算機視覺算法，使它們更適用于計算攝影。因此，擬建項目有跨學科的性質，可能推進部分計算機視覺研究方向。如果我們的項目獲得成功，發表的論文還會影響工業界的照片編輯軟件的未來版本。

17209714.label: Realisation of objectives
17209714.value: During this project, we have investigated and completed the four objectives. 1) As the outcome of the first objective, we introduce the first automatic photo and video enhancement framework based on deep neural networks and fully convolutional semantic features. A variety of normal and artistic photo enhancement styles can be achieved in our framework by training a distinct model for each enhancement style. We cast exemplar-based photo enhancement as a regression problem, and use a deep neural network to represent the highly nonlinear and spatially varying color mapping between input and enhanced images. Unlike existing work that integrates hand-crafted features, our solution is a large-scale deep network. It consists of fully convolutional networks (FCNs) for automatic feature extraction and fully connected neural layers for adjustment prediction. The fully connected neural layers predict color transforms according to contexts and pixel features. Feature design is a key issue that can significantly affect the effectiveness of machine learning techniques. To make sure the predicted color transforms respond to complex color and semantic information, our deep network makes use of fully convolutional networks to extract global and contextual semantic features for every superpixel in the input image. The global feature of a superpixel is the globally pooled deep CNN feature. And the pixel feature is simply the pixel color at the centroid of the superpixel. The contextual feature of a superpixel consists of three components. The first two components are deep CNN features extracted over two differently sized receptive fields centered at the centroid of the superpixel. The third component is a set of concatenated color histograms computed over a 3x3 grid also centered at the centroid of the superpixel. To make our deep network trained on image exemplars perform video enhancement, we represent the video with temporal superpixels (TSPs). To reuse our trained deep network for predicting per-TSP color transforms, we project a TSP onto video frames to obtain a sequence of temporally adjacent superpixels. We then predict color transforms associated with those superpixels and aggregate them to obtain the per-TSP color transform. Our experiments demonstrate that our trained deep neural networks successfully capture sophisticated photographic styles. In particular and unlike previous techniques, it can model local adjustments that depend on image semantics. We have shown that this yields results that are qualitatively and quantitatively better than previous work. 2) As the outcome of the second objective, we introduce ColorSketch, an interactive sketching system that automatically resolves stylization issues related to painting colors, brush layouts and region filling styles given user-provided sparse pencil strokes. Our system lets the user have complete control over pencil strokes, including their location, shape, drawing order and the level of abstraction. While the user is drawing, our system analyzes the existing sketch layout and automatically generates color brushed regions that are compatible with existing pencil sketches. Given an input photo, producing a color sketch using our system consists of two stages, an offline automatic preprocessing stage, and an online drawing stage carried out through the sketching interface. In the offline stage, our system performs automatic image understanding to determine object contours and occlusion boundaries, which are taken as “visual guides”. Our system automatically generates these guides in the form of thin strokes. We have designed a novel deep network to detect contours and occlusion boundaries. The proposed network architecture integrates state-of-the-art techniques, such as top–down refinement, multiscale feature fusion, dilated convolution, and residual learning. During the online stage, the user draws sparse pencil strokes to delineate the shape of objects. To facilitate contour sketching, our interface dynamically displays a stroke automatically extracted during the preprocessing stage as a suggestion near the stroke being drawn by the user. The user can choose to accept the stroke, or ignore it and continue to draw. Whenever the user finishes a new pencil stroke or revises an existing stroke, the system automatically updates the final sketching result by adjusting and rendering color regions. We have tested our interface in a user study. Comparisons between sketches produced with and without our system indicate that users, especially novice ones, can generate much better color sketches more efficiently with our system than using traditional manual tools. 3) As the outcome of the third objective, we introduce a data-driven context-aware grayscale image colorization framework based on deep convolutional neural networks. It consists of three main phases: an initial colorization model, a boundary-guided conditional random field (CRF), and a color transform convolutional neural network (CNN). The initial colorization model formulates colorization as a pixel-wise labeling problem. It divides the color space into discrete bins, and the target grayscale image is fed to a classification-oriented CNN model, which generates a probability distribution over these discrete color bins for each pixel. Dilated convolutions are adopted to capture contexts. For the boundary-guided CRF, we calculate the unary term of CRF on the basis of the predicted probability distribution. When calculating the pairwise affinity of CRF, we involve boundary cues obtained with an off-the-shelf boundary detector from the input grayscale image. With such a boundary-guided CRF, we aim to improve the spatial coherence of the initial labeling result. Subsequently, to infer final continuous color values, we further adopt another CNN to learn a transformation from discrete color bins to final color values. This second CNN takes into account color correlation and contrast among image regions. Comparison between colorization results with and without CNN-based color transform shows that CNN-based color transform makes our final colorization more natural and realistic. Extensive experimental results, including a user study, demonstrate that our proposed method significantly improve colorization quality in comparison to existing leading methods. 4) As the outcome of the fourth objective, we generalize our color sketch generation and grayscale image colorization techniques in 2)-3) to RGB-D images. To achieve this goal, we have developed a deep learning based semantic image segmentation algorithm for RGB-D images. With the help of the depth channel, segmentation on RGB-D images can reach higher accuracy than that on RGB images. More accurate object contours extracted from RGB-D segmentation results have been incorporated into our color sketch generation and grayscale image colorization techniques to improve the quality of their results as both techniques make use of object contours or region boundaries. While we develop our semantic image segmentation algorithm, we also i) develop a novel Long Short-Term Memorized Context Fusion (LSTM-CF) Model that captures and fuses contextual information from multiple channels of RGB and depth channels, and ii) incorporate this model into deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for end-to-end training. Specifically, contexts in RGB and depth channels are, respectively, captured by stacking several convolutional layers and a long short-term memory layer; the memory layer encodes both short-range and long-range spatial dependencies in an image along the vertical direction. Another long short-term memorized fusion layer is set up to integrate the contexts along the vertical direction from different channels, and perform bi-directional propagation of the fused vertical contexts along the horizontal direction to obtain true 2D global contexts. At last, the fused contextual representation is concatenated with the convolutional features extracted from the RGB channels in order to improve the accuracy of fine-scale semantic labeling.

17209714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209714.value: 1) The first research output in Part C introduces the first automatic photo adjustment framework based on deep neural networks. A variety of photo enhancement styles can be achieved by training a distinct neural network model for each enhancement style. This framework adopts informative yet discriminative image feature descriptors at the pixel, contextual, and global levels. 2) The second research output in Part C presents a drawing assistant for generating color sketches from photos. To preserve artistic freedom and expressiveness, the proposed system gives users full control over pencil strokes, while automatically augmenting pencil sketches using color mapping, brush stroke rendering, and blank area creation. 3) The third research output in Part C introduces a novel deep learning architecture for stylistic image enhancement. It consists of fully convolutional networks and fully connected neural layers. Fully convolutional networks extract global features and contextual features. This output also demonstrates that deep neural networks trained with image exemplars can be used to enhance videos as well. 4) The fourth research output in Part C decomposes single image super-resolution into deterministic component reconstruction, stochastic component hallucination, and local statistical rectification. A generalized gradient loss and an orientation loss are introduced for the deterministic component. Novel loss functions based on local Gramm matrices and local correlation matrices are also adopted for local statistical rectification. 5) The fifth research output in Part C presents a fully convolutional generative adversarial network for semantic image inpainting. The proposed network discards fully connected layers for better maintaining the original spatial information in the input image. A novel context-aware loss function for quality improvement is also introduced. 6) The sixth research output in Part C introduces a novel fully automatic grayscale image colorization pipeline which involves an initial colorization model, a boundary-guided CRF (conditional random field) and a CNN-based color transform. Two novel automatic evaluation schemes for assessing colorization quality in terms of spatial coherence and localization are also proposed. 7) The seventh research output (conference paper) in Part C introduces a novel deep learning architecture for RGB-D image semantic segmentation. This architecture jointly optimizes LSTM layers and convolutional layers for better performance. Context modeling and fusion are incorporated into this architecture to enhance the discriminative power of feature representation. Object contours extracted from RGB-D image segmentation results have been incorporated into our color sketch generation and grayscale image colorization techniques to improve the quality of their results.

Nevertheless, image enhancement is a highly empirical and perceptual process. Photographer decide photo adjustment operations according to high-level image semantics, such as the types of objects (such as faces and cars) and surfaces (such as terrain and building surfaces) present in the image. This imposes significant challenges as most existing techniques are based on low-level image feature statistics. Our proposed semantics-aware techniques try to perform image enhancement or transformation according to the semantics of the input photo, much like what photographers would do.
