17209914.value: To study the correlations of different populations and identify those keystone populations based on next generation sequencing of 16S/18S rRNA gene of AS collected over a long period. The AS from a Hong Kong large-scale secondary municipal wastewater treatment plant (Shatin sewage treatment work, treating 250, 000 m3 sewage per day) has been sampled monthly in the past 7 years and the corresponding data of operational conditions and influent/effluent characteristics had been obtained from Hong Kong Drainage Service Department. The samples will be used for DNA extraction, PCR amplification, and then sequencing of 16S/18S rRNA genes. The network analysis will be conducted to identify the keystone populations based on sequencing data of these time-series samples. To validate the identified keystone populations in a macro scale. AS will be collected from multiple secondary municipal WWTPs of different treatment capacities and different processes at Hong Kong and some cities in mainland China. A keystone population will be considered as being validated at a macro scale if it is still an important hub in the network established based on the data of these WWTPs, especially those hubs identified in both temporal series network and spatial series network. To investigate the keystone populations and their co-occurrence patterns in single flocs (micro scale) of AS. Single flocs (from 100 to 300 micrometer in diameter) from WWTPs will be isolated by serial dilution and confirmed by microscopic examination, and then be investigated for their microbial communities by next generation sequencing of the 16S/18S rRNA genes.

17209914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209914.value: As the most commonly used biological wastewater treatment process worldwide, activated sludge (AS) has been applied to remove oxygen-demanding organics and nutrients from wastewater for exactly 100 years since 1913. AS is a unique artificial microbial ecosystem with high diversity and high biomass concentration. Our knowledge is quite limited due to the low-throughput methods, considering the high microbial diversity of activated sludge. In recent years, our understanding of microbial diversity in activated sludge has been advanced considerably by applying high-throughput profiling of taxonomic markers (such as 16S rRNA gene) using next generation sequencing (NGS). However, not much effort has been made to investigate the inter-species interactions based on the high-resolution picture of microbial diversity. Correlation-based network analysis has been extensively applied in a broad range of fields with great success in exploring the interactions between individual populations in complex microbial systems, like soil. In this project, we will apply high-throughput next generation sequencing of 16S/18S rRNA gene and correlation-based network analysis, 1) to study the correlations of different microbial populations and identify those keystone populations/species in activated sludge collected over a long period (more than 7 years); 2) to validate the identified keystone populations at a macro scale by investigating secondary wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) of different influent characteristics, different treatment processes and different geographical areas; 3) to investigate the keystone populations and their co-occurrence patterns within single flocs which are at a micro scale; and 4) to further examine the roles of the keystone populations using laboratory reactors of different designs and under different operational conditions. The identification of the keystone populations will increase our knowledge of activated sludge and help us figure out some engineering measures to enhance the operation efficiency and stability of AS treatment systems. 作为最常用的生物废水处理工艺，100年来活性污泥已被广泛用于从废水中除有机物和氮磷污染物。活性污泥是一个人工微生物生态系统，具有高度的多样性和密集的生物量。我们以往的关于活性污泥的知识是相当匮乏的，主要是由于研究方法的限制。近年来，利用新一代测序技术对标志性基因（如16S rRNA基因）进行大量测序已经大大推进了我们对活性污泥中的微生物多样性的认识。然而，目前仍然缺乏对微生物物种之间的相互作用的探讨。而基于大数据的网络分析已经在不同领域得到广泛应用，在探索人群中各个体之间的相互关系以及复杂的微生物系统（如土壤）中的种间作用方面取得显著的成功。 在这个项目中，我们将采用高通量16S/18S rRNA基因测序和相关的网络分析技术，1）利用长期采样数据研究不同微生物种群的相互关系，并确定关键种群; 2）通过调查具有不同进水特性、不同的处理流程和不同地区的二级污水处理厂，在宏观尺度验证所确定的关键种群; 3）研究活性污泥中的单个生物絮体，以确定在微观尺度内的种群相互作用模式。对关键种群的确定将会提高我们对活性污泥的认识，有助于找出了一些工程措施，以提升污水生物处理系统的运行效率和稳定性。

Please refer to the abstract "Bacterial diversity and assembling patterns are related to the spatial scales. However, the micro-scale microbial ecology has been poorly investigated yet. With several superiorities and as a significant artificial community type, the biofloc in activated sludge is a good candidate for the micro-scale microbial ecology. In this study, we profiled the bacterial communities in single flocs of activated sludge collected from two sewage treatment plants by sequencing bacterial V3 region of 16S rRNA gene at a sequencing depth of 6,000. The results indicated that the single flocs were of high alpha diversities (above 1,000 species-level OTUs), and suggested that the bacteria in flocs were distributed as the ‘island-distribution’ pattern. Via analyzing beta diversity, it should be a large step on testing the unfitness of bacterial cosmopolitan hypothesis to small spatial-scale bacterial communities, since deep sequencing was applied on tiny communities. More importantly, based on community structure the flocs could be clustered into different phases, which may suggest the different developing stages or independent assemblage patterns of individual flocs. A large proportion of OTUs display statistically strong co-occurrence associations, implying the comprehensive microbial interactions in micro-scale. Taxa found as network hubs were affiliated with Mycobacterium and Anaerolinaceae, indicating their potential significant roles in bioflocs. Overall, the heterogeneous but patterned bacterial communities among flocs indicated that the bioflocs could be a fine paradigm for studies on micro-scale biodiversity and bacterial assembling pattern."

17209914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209914.value: As the increasing throughput of sequencing platforms and decreasing of sequencing prices, next generation sequencing is becoming more important in detangling the microbial composition, interaction and activity. In this study, activated sludge (AS) samples were collected and sent to perform 16S rRNA gene amplicon, metagenomics and metatranscriptomics sequencing with NGS platforms. This thesis aimed to: (1) study microbial community dynamics using large-scale 16S rRNA gene with different timescales, i.e. monthly samples over five years for one wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) , biweekly samples of two WWTPs over 12 months and daily samples over 13 months at one WWTP; (2) develop an absolute quantification method at cell level for metagenomics and metatranscriptomics data, and then apply the method to study the activities of taxa and functional genes in foaming AS; (3) establish a reference gene catalog for AS from globally collected 226 deeply sequenced metagenomics data sets. The five years 16S rRNA gene in Shatin WWTP revealed high diversity and abundance variations of bulking and foaming bacteria (BFB). The dynamics of BFB and their correlated bacteria and environmental parameters were investigated. Moreover, BFB could be well predicted by environmental interaction network (EIN) module. Two WWTPs with significantly different influent composition and operational conditions were compared to temporal microbial community dynamics. The communities were discovered to be major governed by influent composition and operational conditions and temperature drove the temporal dynamics in each plant. Temporal microbial community studies have broadened our knowledge of the dynamics and correlations among microbes in both natural and artificial engineering systems. Using activated sludge as a model system, we utilized the intensive longitudinal sampling method to identify overlooked diversity and the hidden dynamics of microbes, detect cross-associations among microbes after detrending, and reveal the central microbial dynamics during sludge bulking and foaming. We discovered that the accumulative alpha diversity in activated sludge sampled daily over 392 days could be as high as 14 000 OTUs, and that the bacterial community dynamics followed a gradual succession, drifting away from the initial observed day and displaying a significant time-dependent trend. Cross-associations among bacteria were modulated autocorrelation in microbial time series. Moreover, clusters of bacteria displaying rapid turnover were discovered during the beginning, ongoing, and fading of sludge bulking and foaming, and their physicochemical parameters are resolved. These identified groups of bacteria and their related environmental factors could potentially supply clues to form hypotheses for treating operational problems, such as sludge bulking and foaming.

17209914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209914.value: With correlation-based network analysis, the microbial association network was generated and their non-random modularity features were revealed. However, the correlation should be carefully interpreted as correlation was not necessarily indicated of association, not mention of causation. Causation identification of microbial interactions should be further considered. As the emergent and mature of third generation sequencing platforms like PacBio and MinION, researchers should try to utilize their advantage in yielding longer sequences such as in study full-length 16S in a high throughput way or using the new platform to obtain better assembly results. As the continue decreasing of sequencing price, it would be much more easy to sequence more AS in the future, the metagenomic-wide association study (MWAS) should be taken into consideration for its power in identifying of the core functional bacteria associated with a disease or abnormal phenomenon, such as sludge bulking and foaming. Currently still litter studies used metatranscriptomics or metaproteomics to identify the highly expressed genes or proteins in AS system under different environmental conditions. The further study about the transcriptome or proteomes may give more interesting information for better management of AS process.

17209914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209914.value: Activated sludge is the major biological wastewater treatment process over 100 years. There are thousands of species of bacteria, fungi, and other microorganisms in the flocs of activated sludge. Some of these species are key populations for functions of activated sludge and performance of wastewater treatment reactors. To design and understand the reactors in a better way, it is very important to study these key populations. In this project, next-generation sequencing has been applied to investigate the major/key populations in activated sludge. The results showed that the activated sludge has very high bacterial diversity, and the number of bacterial species could be more than 30, 000. There are specific bacterial populations at different seasons in the wastewater treatment plants, for example, bulking/foaming bacteria. The dynamics of these populations are significantly affected by the operational parameters, like hydraulic retention time, temperature, salinity, etc. and also the chemical parameters of the influent, for example, chemical oxygen demand, ammonia-nitrogen, etc. These results provide us new insights into the microbial ecology of activated sludge and improve our understanding of the complicated microbial interactions in the activated sludge. The knowledge generated in this project will help our engineering practice of biological wastewater treatment.

17210014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210014.value: Microwave oscillators are ubiquitous components within present and future information and communication technology, and the envisaged devices have disparate applications within wireless telecommunications, vehicle radars, inter-chip connections and radio links, hard disk drive read heads, and microwave sensors. Further applications being developed in the sector of information and communication technology will require even larger amount of low cost, low power memory and communication protocols, but limits to the scaling of conventional microwave signal generators and detectors is becoming evident. Spintronic nano-oscillators are remarkably tunable (0.1 – 200 GHz), nano-scopic, and rapidly swept microwave oscillators, with strong potential for use in mobile telephony, vehicle radar, and inter-chip communication. This project addresses the key issues of miniaturization, output power output, efficiency and sensitivity of microwave devices. By introducing novel concepts (e.g. nano-droplets, active feedback, phase-locking circuit), recent scientific breakthroughs and fundamental knowledge made by the project team will be turned into prototypes that can be validated against customer need. Our project will study devices that incorporate magnetic nano-droplets with large amplitude magnetization precession, and incorporate magnetic tunnel junction structures to maximize the power from the devices. Final electronic circuits will be taped-out utilizing the devices to the fullest and their performance will be simulated using a developed Graphic Processing Unit (GPU) accelerated platform. The devices, circuits, simulation software and experimental fabrication tools will form the basis for the industrial partners exploitation plans. Our project aims to investigate the latest spintronic more-than-Moore approaches to provide microwave devices well beyond current-state-of-the-art in terms of miniaturization, frequency range, modulation rates, and sensitivity. Our focus will be on the utilization of novel spintronics for broadband microwave applications, which is important for both fundamental scientific research and practical applications. It is expected to generate many new insights, phenomena, and opportunity for wireless industry over the coming years. The PI and co-I have pioneered the magnetic droplet and its microwave oscillator and have strong links to the industry that seek to commercialize this nascent technology. Through our efforts and activities, we strive to put Hong Kong in an internationally leading position in high frequency spintronics devices and circuits. 微波振蕩器是現在和將來信息通訊技術的不可或缺的元件。微波振蕩器的主要應用包括無線通訊、車輛雷達通訊、芯片內部通訊、磁盤讀出頭、微波輻射檢測器等。目前通訊行業亟需低造價、低能耗並且可以微縮化的微波振蕩器，但已有的微波振蕩器由於受限于現有技術而很難進一步微縮化。在此項目里，我們將主要致力於研究一種新型的微波振蕩器--自旋電子微波振蕩器。這種振蕩器具備以下傳統微波產生器不具備的優勢：寬頻（1MHz-200GHz），快速響應（頻率切換時間<0.1ns），造價低（尺寸<100nm)以及可以微縮化。 具體來說，此項目將利用基礎科學研究最新的突破即磁孤子模式的發現來實現增大自旋電子微波振蕩器的輸出功率，並且通過相位鎖定電路設計來實現進一步增大微波輸出功率的目的。我們將研發一套基於圖形處理器的並行化模擬平台，實現自旋電子學器件的基礎性能和相關電路設計的全面仿真。

Our major findings include: 1, we set up a multiscale multiphysics simulation platform for simulating micromagnetic problems and STT in Spin Valves, MTJs, and STNOs. 17300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300014.value: The sodium ion battery is considered to be a better alternative than lithium ion battery in terms of availability, safety, and costs, for electric vehicles and large scale electricity storage. It is under active intense international investigations to reach performance and maturity similar to that of the lithium ion battery. An experimental program of materials syntheses, materials characterizations, and electrochemical measurements are proposed here to develop composite materials for electrode of sodium ion batteries. The emphasis will be on control of structure and dimensions of the composite structure at several length scales and to understand the impact of different electrochemical and physical processes in each length scale for each component. Synthetic strategies are conceived to fabricate composite materials with control of molecular structure, nanostructure, and the aggregate architecture of the components. The negative electrode which has fewer materials options will be the focus of investigation. Rate, capacity, cycle life of the synthesized materials will be tested by advanced electrochemical techniques. It is promising to apply these approaches to sodium ion batteries which have different electrochemistry and materials requirements compared to lithium ion batteries. Correlating performance to structure of the composite, detailed materials characterizations will be performance and include electron microscopy, x-ray diffraction, microscopic elemental analyses, surface area and porosity measurements. Relation of structure to performance will be further studied by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy to decouple faradaic versus non-faradaic processes and how they are affected by geometry of each component of the composite. The syntheses produced are based on previous experience developed for related materials including titanium dioxide, platinum carbon, antimony doped tin oxide, core-shell carbons with hierarchical porosity, lithium titatnates, and their composites. Similar materials characterizations and electrochemical studies have been performed with a multiple length scale approach to lithium ion batteries and fuel cells. It is promising to apply these approaches to sodium ion batteries which have different electrochemistry and materials requirements. 鈉離子電池可適用性高、安全性能好、成本低廉。這些特點優於鋰離子電池，有望在電動汽車和大規模儲能等領域得到廣泛應用。鈉離子電池研究成為國際的研究熱點，以期達到與鋰離子電池相似的性能和成熟度。本實驗項目主要針對材料種類選擇性較少的鈉離子電池負極，旨在開發適用於鈉離子電池的複合負極材料，實驗涵蓋了材料合成、材料表征、電化學性能檢測與表征等內容。本項目的研究目的在於可控合成不同尺度的金屬/金屬氧化物/碳複合負極材料，並闡明不同電化學/物理過程在不同尺度下對各組成的影響。通過所提出的合成路線制備出具有一定分子組成、納米結構和它們的綜合結構，並采用先進的電化學檢測技術考察復合材料的容量、循環性能和功率性能。鈉離子電池的電化學過程及電極材料要求與鋰離子電池不同，本項目將采用電子顯微鏡、X-射線衍射、元素分析、比表面積和孔結構分析等檢測手段考察材料結構與電化學性能的關系，並通過電化學阻抗譜進一步區分法拉第與非法拉第電極過程，探討複合材料各組成的結構與形貌影響其性能的作用機制。本項目的合成路線是基於過去相關工作提出的，如二氧化鈦、鉑/碳複合材料、銻摻雜二氧化錫、層次孔結構碳、鈦酸鋰及其相關複合材料等；本項目的材料表征和電化學檢測方法也被用於過去相關研究，如鋰離子電池和燃料電池。

17300014.label: Realisation of objectives
17300014.value: Template-less synthesis of Sodium titanates with tunable composition and structure: Extensive trials were carried out to develop a solid state scalable synthesis of sodium titanates with control of nanostructures for high performance in batteries. We achieved an energy efficient solid state synthesis, via the addition of Vulcan carbon, to mass-produce uniform, single crystalline 1D metal oxide nanorods with tunable composition. Neither surfactant nor template is used. The carbon added in the solid-state reaction provides alternative energy saving routes for the metal oxide formation due to the extra local heat generation, CO2/CO release from carbon oxidation. To demonstrate the methodology, a series of single-crystalline Na2Ti3O7/Na2Ti6O13 nanorods with tunable composition are synthesized and applied in sodium ion batteries. The local heat generated from carbon allows formation of Na2Ti3O7 at 450 °C, a much lower annealing temperature than conventional solid state method of 750- 1000 °C. By control of carbon content, CO2/CO release from carbon oxidation provides an alternative low temperature route to transform Na2Ti3O7 into Na2Ti6O13. Material Properties Optimisation for Battery Performance: Materials composition and structure can be optimized for performance in terms of capacity and stability. The high theoretical capacity of Na2Ti3O7 and the low volume expansion of Na2Ti6O13 upon charge/discharge are synergistically exploited to achieve high electrochemical performance and stability. This synthesis method opens up a scalable, energy-saving route to mass-produce uniform 1D nanostructured electrode materials and fine-tune the composition and morphology according to performance demands. Hierarchical Porous Carbon Composites: In addition to development of scalable synthesis for titanates, hierarchical porous carbons are synthesized and successfully applied to disperse active components of titanates for electrochemical applications. Nitrogen doping of carbon has also increased activity and durability. Another solid-state synthesis of titanates has been developed to hybridize titanate and titanium dioxide (B) for synergistic properties in terms of capacity and durability. The materials has been successfully applied for lithium ion anode. The same principle can be applied to sodium titanate for sodium batteries. Electrochemical Performance of Electrodes in Metal Ion Batteries: The titanates and hierarchical carbon composites have been successfully applied to several battery technologies. In addition to sodium ion battery, the developed materials have been applied to lithium ion, lithium-oxygen batteries. The research has led to increase understanding of materials properties to electrochemical performance.

17300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300014.value: An energy-efficient solid-state synthesis via the addition of carbon has been developed to mass-produce uniform, single crystalline, one-dimensional metal oxide nanorods with tunable composition according to performance demands. A series of single crystalline Na2Ti3O7/Na2Ti6O13 nanorods with tunable composition are synthesized and applied in sodium-ion batteries. The high theoretical capacity of Na2Ti3O7 and low volume expansion of Na2Ti6O13 upon charge−discharge are synergistically exploited to achieve high electrochemical performance and stability. We achieve the first synthesis of TiO2(B)/Li4Ti5O12 nanocomposite by interfacing high energy (020) planes of TiO2(B) nanofibers and Li4Ti5O12 with a small lattice mismatch. The TiO2(B)/Li4Ti5O12 nanocomposite features a significantly mitigated initial capacity loss, stable cycling, and enhanced rate performance. This can be mainly attributed to the synergistic effect of the composition and structure resulting in reduced and stabilized SEI formation.

17300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300014.value: Our 2016 publication on synthesis of sodium titanates has been cited 13 times by other research groups. There is good potential for further development and collaborative with other researchers. Success of the research has led to further development in related batteries technology such as sodium-oxygen battery. A collaborative research on sodium-oxygen battery has started in 2018 with a NSFC-RGC grant "Construction of a Long Cycle-life Na-O2 Battery and Study of its Reaction Mechanism" awarded in 2017.

17300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300014.value: The sodium ion battery is considered to be a better alternative than lithium ion battery in terms of availability, safety, and costs, for electric vehicles and large scale electricity storage. Our research consists of materials syntheses, materials characterizations, and electrochemical measurements. Our achievements in scalable synthesis of sodium titanates and composite materials have contributed to the development of electrodes for sodium ion batteries. The synthesis has control of structure and dimensions of the composite structure at several length scales. The titanates and hierarchical mesoporous carbon materials developed in this research are also applied to other advanced technologies of lithium ion, lithium-oxygen, and sodium-oxygen batteries. The research also led to fundamental understanding of structure-electrochemical performance relationship linking electrochemical and physical processes to different length scales. The development of sodium ion batteries will enable better sustainability in the landscape of energy technologies.

17300414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300414.value: Metals are important constituents in biological cells, engineered nanomaterials, and environmental particles. Quantitative determination of the metal contents in the discrete particles is necessary for the characterization of the particles and for the understanding of their interactions with the environment and living organisms. The average metal contents of the particles are typically determined by acid digestion of the bulk sample followed by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Single-particle ICP-MS has attracted strong interest in recent years as an alternative analytical method of particles. Publications on the method have increased exponentially since 2007. Single-particle ICP-MS measures the ICP-MS intensity of individual particles. The method is attractive because relatively small sample size is required. Only a few hundred sample particles are needed for quantitative analysis, a thousand times less than the conventional digestion method. The method also requires little or no sample preparation. In addition, the distributions of metal contents and particle size are determined, which are important characteristics of the particles. The strong research interest in single-particle ICP-MS acknowledges the analytical potentials and the challenges of the method. Calibration of the single-particle ICP-MS intensity is probably the most challenging. Calibration methods using continuous flow of standard solutions, standard particles, and standard solution droplets have been proposed. Despite the claim of successful calibration using continuous flow of standard solution, the published data show negative errors of 15 – 20% in particle diameter and 50% or more in particle mass. The dynamic range of single-particle ICP-MS is also limited. The detection limit of gold nanoparticles is approximately 20 nm. The upper limit of the linear calibration curve is approximately 100 nm for gold nanoparticles because larger particles are not completely vaporized in the ICP. We propose fundamental studies of the processes of desolvation, particle vaporization, and analyte atom diffusion and ionization. We plan to investigate the processes using standard particles of wide range of particle size and properties. The single-particle ICP-MS intensity will be measured under wide range of ICP operating conditions. We will refine our computer model of the processes using the experimental intensity. We will use the computer model to estimate the correction factor to improve the accuracy of the calibration method of continuous flow of standard solution. The fundamental studies will provide valuable information for the optimization the ICP operating conditions. We will also investigate methods to improve the sensitivity and the linear dynamic range based on the studies. 金屬是生物細胞、工程納米材料、和環境顆粒的重要成份。定量測定這些離散顆粒的金屬含量是檢定這些顆粒的特徵和認識它們與環境和活生物體的相互作用的重要手段。測定顆粒的平均金屬含量的常用方法是使用電感耦合等離子體-質譜法（ICP-MS）去量度經酸消化、含有大量顆粒的樣品。近幾年來，另一種備受關注的顆粒分析方法是單顆粒-ICP-MS（SP-ICP-MS）。自2007年以來，SP-ICP-MS的科學論文數量以幾何級數增加。SP-ICP-MS量度單個顆粒的ICP-MS訊號強度。該方法的強項之一是樣本量較小。定量分析只需幾百個顆粒，比傳統的酸消化方法少一千倍以上。該方法也祗需簡單的、甚或無需樣品製備。此外，該方法可提供顆粒的一些重要特徵，如金屬含量和粒徑的分佈。 近年對SP-ICP-MS研究的強烈興趣標示著該方法的潛質和挑戰。SP-ICP-MS訊號強度的校準方法可能是最具挑戰性的課題。文獻上的校準方法包括標準溶液連續進樣法、標準顆粒法、和標準溶液液滴法。標準溶液連續進樣法據稱是成功的校準方法。但文獻上的資料顯示，這方法所測得的顆粒直徑有15－20％的負誤差、顆粒質量的負誤差為50％或以上。SP-ICP-MS的動態範圍也比較窄。納米金顆粒的檢測極限約為20納米。而線性校準曲線的上限約為100納米，因為較大的納米金顆粒不能在ICP中完全汽化。 我們提出對顆粒在ICP中的脫溶劑、顆粒汽化、和被分析物的原子擴散和離子化的過程的基礎研究。我們計劃採用各種不同大小和性質的標準粒子，有系統地測定這些顆粒在不同的ICP操作條件下的SP-ICP-MS訊號強度。這些數據將用於改進我們的電腦模型。我們將使用這計算機模型來推算標準溶液連續進樣法的校正因子，以改善這方法的準確性。該基礎研究也將會提供優化ICP運作參數的有用的資料。基於以上的研究，我們將進一步研發提高SP-ICP-MS靈敏度和線性動態範圍的方法。

17300414.label: Realisation of objectives
17300414.value: 1. We have performed fundamental studies of the signal production processes of single particles in the ICP. The experiments include systematic investigation of the effects of ionization potential of an element and boiling point of its oxide on the sensitivity of ICP-MS over a range of ICP sampling depth. A large number (16) of elements, representing a wide range of ionization and oxide boiling point, were used in the studies. The investigation provides significant insight on the combined effects of ionization of an analyte and vaporization of its oxide on the optimal ICP-MS operating conditions for single-particle ICP-MS measurement. The findings have been incorporated into our computer model of particle vaporization and analyte ion formation. 2. We have also investigated the mechanisms for the non-linearity of the calibration curves of single-particle ICP-MS intensity measurement. We have previously shown that incomplete particle vaporization is a major factor for the non-linear calibration curves. In this project, we have further shown that ion plumes of large number density causes non-linear response in the ICP-MS detector because of the existence of more than one ion within the dead time of the detector. Poisson statistics was used to model the ion-overlapping effects. The investigation has revealed one of the fundamental limitations of single-particle ICP-MS measurement. We have also investigated the feasibility of calibration of single-particle ICP-MS measurement using standard solutions and have proposed the criteria of accurate calibration using standard solutions. Empirical correlation factors for solution calibration were determined. The factors have also been compared to the theoretical calculation. 3. We have investigated methods to improve of the analytical performance of single-particle ICP-MS based on the findings of the fundamental studies in (1) and (2) above. A computer model was built to assist the optimization process. We have also investigated several methods to improve the detection limits of single-particle ICP-MS. Particles that are below the typical detection limits can be detected readily and the size of the particles can be determined accurately. We have also applied single-particle ICP-MS to single-cell analysis. We have developed a correlation method of single-cell ICP-MS intensity of cellular elements and cell size for the investigation of the relation of cell size and cellular response to external stresses. The method provides new insight on cell heterogeneity in response to external stress, namely heavy metal toxicity.

17300414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300414.value: We are the first research group to propose and establish that the dead time of ICP-MS detector contributes to non-linear single-particle ICP-MS calibration curves. The finding is significant for accurate quantitative measurement single particles. We have further developed criteria for accurate solution calibration of single-particle ICP-MS and proposed an empirical correlation factor for solution calibration based on our experimental work and theoretical calculation. [J. Anal. At. Spectrom., 2015, 30, 1245–1254. The article is one of the most accessed articles in JAAS 2015, with 18 citations as recorded by CrossRef and RSC Journals.] We have investigated and delineated the combined effects of oxide boiling points and ionization potential of the analyte on the sensitivity of single-particle ICP-MS measurements. The fundamental investigation is the base for the understanding of the signal-production processes of single-particle ICP-MS. We have also proposed strategy for the optimization of the ICP-MS operating parameters, especially the ICP sampling depth, for single-particle ICP-MS measurement based on the two properties of the analyte. [J. Anal. At. Spectrom., 2015, 30, 2066–2073. The article is one of the “Hot articles in JAAS 2015”, with 4 citations as recorded by CrossRef and RSC Journals.] We have developed several methods to improve the detection limits of single-particle ICP-MS. Particles that are below the typical detection limits can be detected readily and the size of the particles can be determined accurately. The particle size distributions can also be determined, provided that the number density of the sample particles is known. The methods is being refined for applications in various sample matrix. We have also developed a novel correlation method to study cellular responses to external stress. The effects of cell size on cellular responses to Cr(VI) toxicity is determined quantitatively using a novel correlation method. Heterogeneous cellular responses were determined quantitatively. Cell heterogeneity is an important properties of biological cells. The classical approach of cell digestion and measurement of the average cell properties does not provide information on cell heterogeneity. The novel method is a powerful tool for unambiguous identification and quantitative characterization heterogeneous cellular responses. [J. Anal. At. Spectrom., 2017, 32, 807–815]

17300414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300414.value: The fundamental studies and the novel methods for accurate quantitative single-particle ICP-MS are the base for the application of the technique to the analysis of a wide range of samples of discrete particles. The method will be especially important in the measurement of the cellular contents of individual biological cells. We have already published several articles on single-cell ICP-MS and will further develop the technique for various biological applications, such as environmental stresses on biological cells. We have developed tools for fundamental investigation of single-particle ICP-MS. One of the novel techniques is double-slit ICP-AES. We are currently using the technique for the investigation particle vaporization and analyte diffusion loss in the ICP.

17300414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300414.value: We have performed fundamental studies of single-particle ICP-MS, such as the combined effects of oxide boiling points and ionization potential of the target elements on the sensitivity of the technique. The findings have been applied to the optimization of operating parameters of the technique. We have also built a computer model for fundamental investigation of particle-plasma interactions and optimization of the ICP-MS operating parameters. We have characterized the instrumentation of single-particle ICP-MS. We find that detector dead time of the ICP-MS is an important factor contributing to the commonly observed non-linear calibration curves of single-particle ICP-MS. We have also investigated the feasibility of calibration using standard solutions. The method can potentially eliminate the need of calibration particles which are not readily available and can be very expensive. We have also developed methods to improve of the detection limits of single-particle ICP-MS based on the findings of the fundamental studies and the computer model. We have applied the single-particle ICP-MS to single-cell analysis. The method provides new insight on heterogeneous cellular responses to external stress. Cell heterogeneity is an important characteristics of biological systems and applications.

17300614.label: Realisation of objectives
17300614.value: We have completed the project and achieved all the objectives listed above. 9 papers have been published in peer-reviewed journals: 3 in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2 in Chem. Sci., 1 in Chem. Commun., 2 in Chem. Asian J. and 1 in Israel Journal of Chemistry. 6 presentations were delivered in international conferences. All these contributions have acknowledged the support from this RGC grant. The important findings are summarized below: [1] Objectives 1 and 2. We prepared a series of palladium(II) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes which are stable in the presence of biological thiols. A representative complex, [Pd(C^N^N)(N,N’-nBu2-NHC)](CF3SO3) (Pd1d, HC^N^N = 6-phenyl-2,2’-bipyridine, N,N’-nBu2-NHC = N,N’-di-n-butylimidazolium), displays potent cytotoxicity toward cancer cells (IC50 = 0.09–0.5 μM) but is less cytotoxic toward normal human fibroblast cell line (CCD-19Lu, IC50 = 11.8 μM). In vivo anti-cancer studies revealed that Pd1d significantly inhibited tumor growth in nude mice model. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 11935–11939]. [2] Objectives 1 and 2. Taking a multi-faceted approach employing two clickable photoaffinity probes, we reported the identification of multiple molecular targets for water-soluble, anti-cancer active pincer gold(III) NHC complexes. These complexes display potent and selective cytotoxicity against cultured cancer cells and in vivo anti-tumor activities in mice bearing xenografts of human cervical and lung cancers. Our experiments revealed the specific engagement of the gold(III) complexes with multiple cellular targets, including HSP60, vimentin, nucleophosmin, and YB-1, accompanied by expected downstream mechanisms of action. Additionally, Pt(II) and Pd(II) analogues can also bind the cellular proteins targeted by the gold(III) complexes, uncovering a distinct pincer cyclometalated metal–NHC scaffold in the design of anti-cancer metal medicines with multiple molecular targets. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 3892–3896] [3] Objectives 1, 2, and 4. We have prepared two classes of cationic palladium(II) acetylide complexes containing pincer-type ligands. Replacing 2,2’:6’,2’’-terpyridine with the strongly σ-donating C^N^C ligand with two N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) units results in the Pd(II) acetylide complexes displaying phosphorescence and stronger intermolecular interactions in the solid state. X-ray crystal structures of [Pd(terpy)(C≡CPh)]PF6 and [Pd(C^N^C)(C≡CPh)]PF6 reveal that the complex cations are arranged in a one-dimensional stacking structure with Pd⋅⋅⋅Pd contacts with distance ranging from 3.292 to 3.349 Å. Some of the Pd-NHC complexes exhibit photo-cytotoxicity under cellular conditions. [Chem. Asian J. 2017, 12, 145–158] [4] Objective 2. Two palladium(II) complexes (Pd1, Pd2) supported by tetradentate cyclometalating ligand have been prepared. Pd1 exhibits unprecedented dual phosphorescence properties. Extensive spectroscopic studies show that the relative intensities of the two emission bands of Pd1 are dependent on the excitation wavelength. It is proposed that there are two excited state minima of the low energy triplet excited state of Pd1. Variation of the twisting angle between the pendent p-(t-butyl)phenyl group and the coordination plane C^N^N^C-Pd leadd to two excited decay pathways. Ultra-fast femto-second time-resolved fluorescence measurement and DFT calculations have been conducted to obtain a comprehensive understanding of the dual-phosphorescence origin. A paper is in preparation. [Dr. Li Kai as co-worker, unpublished result] [5] Objective 2, 5. We reported a series of Au(I) and Au(III) complexes bearing heterocyclic arylacetylide ligands with narrow band-gap. The luminescence of both series are derived from an intraligand transition localized on the arylacetylide ligand (ππ*(C≡CR)) but Au(I) complexes displayed prompt fluorescence (emission lifetime = 2.7–12.0 ns) while Au(III) complexes showed mainly phosphorescence (emission lifetime = 104–205 μs). DFT/TDDFT calculations revealed that the energy gap between the singlet and triplet excited states (ΔEST) with effective spin-orbit coupling (SOC) for Au(I) systems is much larger than that for the Au(III) counterparts, thus resulting in the poor ISC efficiency for the former. [Chem. Sci. 2017, 8, 2352–2364] [6] Objective 3. Gold complexes are generally known to undergo ligand exchange or redox reactions with thiols and hence are potentially useful agents that could target thiol-containing enzymes but not DNA. Recent studies have shown that deubiquitinases (DUBs), key enzymes regulating proteasome-related protein homeostasis, are potential anti-cancer targets of both gold(I) and gold(III) complexes. In this regard, we have published a review article to discuss the current status of gold complexes as DUB inhibitors. In particular, auranofin and cyclometalated gold(III) complexes containing dithiocarbamate ligands (e.g., [(AuIII(C^N)(DEDT)]+, HC^N = 2-phenylpyridine, DEDT = diethyldithiocarbamate) are highlighted as examples of DUB inhibitors. [Israel Journal of Chemistry, 2016, 56, 825–833] [7] Objective 3. We prepared Pt(II) NHC complexes which selectively probe mismatched DNA. In the presence of mismatch DNA, the low-energy orange emission of the Pt(II) NHC complexes will turn-off due to de-aggregation process and a relative high-energy blue-green emission will turn-on as a result of interacting with mismatch pocket. As different kinds of DNA mismatch show varying degrees of stability, the extent of aggregation or de-aggregation of these Pt (II) NHC complexes would vary upon their bindings with different DNA mismatches, thus resulting in a new label-free luminescence method for DNA mismatch screening. [Mr. Zhang Ming as co-worker, unpublished result] [8] Objective 4. We prepared an amphiphilic gold(III) complex AM-Au which is soluble in water and displays phosphorescence with quantum yield and lifetime of 4.5% and 117 μs, respectively. AM-Au forms micelle (ca. 100 nm) and short nano-rods in water. AM-Au was used as photodynamic therapy agent for in vitro photodynamic therapy treatment. ESR measurements evidenced that singlet oxygen (1O2) is generated in AM-Au aqueous solution through photoinduced energy transfer from excited gold(III) complex to oxygen. [Chem. Commun. 2016, 52, 13273–13276] [9] Objective 4. We prepared pincer Pd(II)–isocyanide complexes that display intermolecular interactions and emissive 3MMLCT excited states in aggregation state(s) at room temperature. The intermolecular Pd(II)-Pd(II) and ligand-ligand interactions drive these complexes to undergo supramolecular polymerization in a living manner. Comprehensive spectroscopic studies revealed a pathway with a kinetic trap that can be modulated by changing the counter-anion and metal atom. DFT/TDDFT calculations lend support to the MMLCT absorption and emission of these pincer Pd(II)-isocyanide aggregates. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3089–3093] [10] Objective 5. We designed and synthesized a series of charge–neutral Au(III) complexes comprising dicarbanionic C–deprotonated cyclometalating biphenyl and bidentate ancillary ligand [Au(C^C)(O^X)]. These complexes are emissive with quantum yield reaching 18 % in solution and 35% in thin-film. Their luminescence originates from the 3IL states of the cyclometalated C^C or the ancillary O^X ligands, and the emission color can be switched from blue green (λem ~ 466 nm) to orange (λem ~ 585 nm). OLEDs devices fabricated with these gold(III) complexes exhibit maximum EQE of 6.71%. The shortest Au(III)―Au(III) contact with intermetal distance of 3.408 Å was revealed X-ray diffraction crystallography. [Chem. Asian J. 2017, 12, 2104–2120] [11] Objective 5. We reported a series of phosphorescent palladium(II) complexes supported by tetradentate [N^C^C^N] and [O^N^C^N] ligand systems. These complexes display sky blue to red phosphorescence with emission quantum yields and emission lifetimes up to 0.64 and 272 μs. The Pd(II) complexes are efficient catalysts for visible light-driven, reductive C–C bond formation from unactivated alkyl bromides, and photosensitizers for [2 + 2] cycloaddition of styrenes. Both green and sky blue OLEDs have been fabricated with these Pd(II) complexes as emitters with maximum EQE of up to 16.5%. By utilizing these Pd(II) complexes as sensitizers, green and yellow phosphor-sensitized fluorescent-OLEDs having high EQE (up to 14.3%) and long operation lifetimes have been realized. [Chem. Sci. 2016, 7, 6083–6098]

17300614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300614.value: The results of this project have revealed the great potential of luminescent Au(III) and Pd(II) complexes as new classes of functional materials with applications in various areas. The rich photophysical properties of Au(III) and Pd(II) complexes demonstrated in our works strongly suggest that these complexes may exhibit properties comparable to those of Pt(II) and Ir(III) complexes by the use of suitably designed ligand(s). With the insight gained from these studies, we will continue to expand the structural diversity of luminescent Au(III) and Pd(II) complexes, and endow these complexes with new functionalities by appropriately modifying the ligand framework. Besides, the long-lived, emissive excited states of Au(III) and Pd(II) complexes would render these complexes to be excellent photocatalysts for visible light driven organic transformations, and luminescent sensors for bio-molecules with high sensitivity. We conceive that luminescent Au(III) and Pd(II) complexes have a large room for exploration and enormous potential to be developed into useful molecular materials having practical applications.

17300614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300614.value: Luminescent metal compounds have well been documented to display impactful applications in diverse areas including OLEDs, luminescent bio-sensing and photocatalysis. At present, the majority of the studies in this field are focused on luminescent iridium, platinum and ruthenium complexes. This research project focused on new classes of luminescent gold and palladium compounds having high stability especially in biological medium, dual emissive behavior and investigation on their applications. Through this project, we have obtained new design principle for luminescent metal compounds having very long-lived emissive excited states with lifetimes over 100 μs in solutions under ambient condition, and demonstrated their application in bio-medicines. The use of multi-dentate C-donor ligand scaffold with high structural rigidity is the key to achieve long-lived emissive excited state and high stability. These findings have been reported in leading international chemistry journals and disseminated in academic conferences. The accomplishments achieved in this project would provide new rationale and research direction in the Photophysics and Photochemistry of Coordination Compounds, and also contribute to Hong Kong as the world-leading research center in luminescent metal compounds.

17300814.label: Project Objectives
17300814.value: To study why some pulsars can emit photons with energy higher than 10GeV and exhibit non-exponential cut-off spectrum, which seem to conflict with current understanding of outer gap model. To study the structure of pulsar magnetosphere in order to explain what are the conditions to produce gamma-ray pulses align with the radio pulses and to produce gamma-ray pulse ahead of the radio pulse. We will also carry out data analysis in X-rays and gamma-rays to find the differences between the canonical pulsars and millisecond pulsars. To study why some young pulsars cannot be detected in GeV gamma-rays. If the conditions are found what are the population ratio between soft gamma-ray pulsars and gamma-ray pulsars?

17300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300814.value: Pulsars are strongly magnetized and rapidly spinning neutron stars. Nearly 2,000 radio pulsars are found in the Milky Way and nearly 10% of them are detected in high energy bands including X-rays and gamma-rays. Two major classes of gamma-ray pulsars, i.e. canonical gamma-ray pulsars and millisecond gamma-ray pulsars, are found. The former class of pulsars has typical magnetic field ~ 10^12 Gauss, spin period ~ 0.1 second and age younger than million years old, and the latter class has weaker magnetic field ~ 10^8 Gauss, faster spin period ~ 0.001 second but much older >10^8 years. Despite these distinctive differences their gamma-ray emission features are quite similar. It is generally believed that the high energy photons from these two classes of pulsars are emitted by relativistic electrons/positrons, which are accelerated in the pulsar magnetosphere through the electric field along the magnetic field lines. It turns out that the potential drop and current intensity in the magnetosphere of these two classes of pulsars are very similar. The global properties of these two classes of pulsars are so much different, somehow these differences should affect their emission properties. The data of the gamma-ray satellite “Fermi” is publicly available, we can analyse the observed data to identify any differences between these classes of gamma-ray pulsars. In addition Fermi satellite has also found many interesting features among gamma-ray pulsars. These features include (1)photons with energy >10GeV are found in many pulsars, which are very difficult to be explained in terms of conventional curvature radiation process, (2)only one canonical pulsar is found gamma-ray pulsation align with radio but several millisecond pulsars have this property despite the fact that the population of gamma-ray millisecond pulsars is only 1/3 of canonical gamma-ray pulsars, (3)the gamma-ray pulse of some pulsars appears before the radio pulse, which imposes challenge for many theoretical models, (4)despite the great sensitivity of the Fermi satellite, it cannot detect gamma-ray emissions from quite a large number of young pulsars with age similar to the Crab and Vela pulsar. In this project we will focus on studying the acceleration mechanisms and various of radiation processes inside the pulsar magnetosphere. We will also compare the model results with the observed data. 脈衝星是強烈磁化和飛速旋轉的中子星。近 2,000 射電脈衝星的發現在銀河系中，近 10%的他們都在高能量包括 x 射線和伽瑪射線中檢測到。兩個主要類別的伽瑪射線脈衝星，即典型的伽瑪射線脈衝星和毫秒伽瑪射線脈衝星被發現。典型脈衝星的磁場 ~ 10^12 高斯,旋轉期間 ~ 0.1秒和年輕。後一類有較弱的磁場 ~ 10 ^8 高斯，更快地旋轉 ~ 0.001 秒但老得多 > 10^8 年。儘管有這些獨特的差異其伽瑪射線發射功能是相當相似。一般認為從這兩個類的脈衝星的高能量光子由相對論性電子/正電子發出的。原來電壓和電流強度在兩個主要類別的伽瑪射線脈衝星是非常相似。這兩個類的脈衝星的脈衝星磁層全域屬性有許多不同，這些差異應以某種方式影響他們發射性能。伽瑪射線衛星"費米"的資料是公開的我們可以分析觀測的資料來標識這些類的伽瑪射線脈衝星之間的任何差異。此外費米衛星還發現了許多γ 射線脈衝星的有趣功能。包括 (1) 發現在很多脈衝星光子的能量 > 10GeV 這是很難用常規的曲率輻射過程來解釋,(2) 只有一個典型脈衝星發現伽瑪射線脈動對齊無線電脈動，但多個毫秒脈衝星具有這個屬性，但是伽瑪射線毫秒脈衝星數量上只有典型伽瑪射線脈衝星的1/3，(3) 有些脈衝星的伽瑪射線脈衝出現在無線電脈衝之前，這現象挑戰許多理論模型，(4)儘管費米衛星的高度敏感性但大批年輕的脈衝星卻沒有發現伽瑪射線。在這個專案中我們將會專注研究脈衝星的加速機制和各類脈衝星磁層內的輻射過程。我們也將比較模型計算結果與實測資料。

17300814.label: Realisation of objectives
17300814.value: We have studied the objectives as follow: Objective 1: We first analyzes the data from the Fermi satellite, in particular the Vela and Geminga pulsar in great detail because these two pulsars are the second and third most luminous gamma-ray pulsars (the Crab pulsar is the most luminous one but we believe that the gamma-ray emission is not directly coming from the outer magnetosphere accelerator instead high energy emission are produced by secondary pairs outside the accelerator.). According to our model the gamma-ray emission of these two pulsars should be emitted by the primary charged particles inside the accelerator. We mainly focus on two special aspects. First we analyze the phase resolved spectrum in a smallest allowed phase bin, we find that even in the smallest bin size most of these phase resolved spectrum cannot be described by simple exponential spectrum. In other words the spatial superposition of many simple exponential spectrum could not be the reason of forming the non-exponential phase average spectrum (cf. the M.Phil thesis of Miss Chai). Secondly we analyze the very high energy component of the Vela pulsar we find that the highest energy of the photon emitted from this pulsar can be up to 90 GeV, which any simple curvature radiation model can not explain. We propose that the acceleration region in the pulsar magnetosphere should not be a stationary situation. One can imagine that the electric field inside the accelerator becomes strong enough it accelerates charged particles to relativistic speed and radiate very high energy photons. Part of these photons can be converted into pairs. The separation of opposite charged particles can screen out the electric field or shut-down the accelerator. Therefore the accelerator should be always on-and-off or fluctuating in time. Such dynamical situation cannot make the potential drop of the accelerator as constant. The potential and current of the accelerator should be also fluctuating. Therefore we propose a non-stationary model to explain why the high energy spectrum should not be simple exponential and photons>10GeV can be emitted. The actual situation of the accelerator is not a steady state. In fact it can be described by a distribution of states, i.e. the potential drop and current can be described by a power law distribution. We have used this model to fit all known gamma-ray pulsars with reasonable agreement. This objective is covered in pub. 1, 8 and the M.Phil. thesis of Miss Chai. Objective 2: This objective related to comparing the model calculation and the observed X-ray and gamma-ray data. In addition to canonical pulsars we would like to extend the model calculations to millisecond pulsars which has magnetic field 4 order of magnitude weaker than the canonical pulsars but the spin period is about 100-1000 shorter. We first analyze the X-ray and Gamma-ray data from some specific millisecond pulsars including PSR J1023 and PSR J2129, as well as some candidates of millisecond pulsar in the Fermi Unidentified Object list. Then we compare our model spectrum with the observed multi-wavelength spectrum. We find that for millisecond pulsars in the binary systems X-rays are emitted from shock region whereas the gamma-rays are still emitted from the pulsar magnetosphere. These studies are published in pub. 2, 3, 6 and 7. We also carry out detail study for young canonical pulsar, e.g. PSR J2021, which is a radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar and the fourth most luminous gamma-ray pulsar. In particular this pulsar has a very special property, namely, its spectral properties exhibits sudden change after glitch (glitch is a phenomenon for pulsar, which show some pulsars their rotation period can suddenly increase.) We argue that the glitch can change the angle between the rotation axis and the magnetic axis (inclination angle). We calculate the structure of the magnetospheric accelerator for different inclination angle. We can explain the observed spectral property changes if the inclination angle has been changed by 5 degrees. This value is consistent with the jump in the change of spin-down rate. If the spin-down rate results from magnetic dipole radiation then the change in spin-down rate may result from the change in the inclination angle. Our findings are published in pub. 5 and 9. There are two classes of gamma-ray pulsars, i.e. radio quiet and radio loud. If their gamma-rays are both emitted from the outer gap why one is radio loud but other is radio quiet. We first carry out the statistical analysis for various of spectral properties, e.g. spectral curvature, flux ratio between X-ray and gamma-ray, photon index, cut-off energy, variability, pulse width, age, period, magnetic field etc. We find that the most significant differences are their distribution in spectral curvature and magnetic field strength at the light cylinder. We are able to model these differences by outer gap accelerator model and taking into account the viewing angle effect. this is reported in pub. 11. Finally we compare two very young pulsar emission efficiency and their spectrum. One is the Crab pulsar in our own galaxy and another one with almost the same age but located outside Milky Way in LMC. The one in LMC shows much stronger gamma-ray luminosity than the Crab pulsar. We explain the differences by modeling the LMC pulsar with small inclination angle and large viewing angle. Our model has successfully explained the differences between these two Crab-like pulsars (cf. pub. 10). Objective 3: There is a small class of young pulsars which can only be detected in soft gamma-ray energy band GeV. We believe that there is no reason to believe that they have different acceleration and emission processes. We propose that perhaps it is the geometric effect to cause this difference. We first consider that their radio intensity it turns out that they are either radio quiet or radio weak. We speculate the radio signal is suppressed by electron/positron plasma near the neutron star surface. If this is true then there must be some way to produce copious amount of pairs near the surface. We propose that if the gamma-ray beam is propagating very near the neutron surface where the magnetic field is extremely strong then the magnetic pair creation can convert the GeV-photons into pairs and they re-radiate in softer gamma-ray energy range. This model is able to explain the X-ray and soft gamma-ray observed spectrum for all known soft gamma-ray pulsars. In addition in the non-stationary model if the power law distribution is very steep then it means the accelerator will spend most of their time in low states where the electric field/potential is weak and hence it is very difficult to emit GeV photons. Therefore the geometric effect and outer gap fluctuation process may be the crucial reasons to suppress the GeV gamma-ray emission. Our findings report in pub. 4 and 8. In addition in our statistical analysis of all Fermi gamma-ray pulsars we also conclude that those spectral differences can be partially due to the geometric effect. This finding in pub. 11 is consistent with assumption in pub. 4.

17300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300814.value: In midterm report we have already summarized our findings up to 2015 (pub. 1-7). In this final report we cover our major findings (pub. 7-11) from 2016-2017 as follow: In Pub. (8) we develop a non-stationary outermagnetospheric gap model to describe the high energy emission from pulsars. Basically we argue that the actual accelerator in the pulsar magnetosphere should be in a dynamical situation or time dependent state. The observed spectrum is a time average result. We assume a power law distribution of accelerator state, we calculate the spectrum of the individual state and once the power index is given then the contribution of each state to the overall spectrum is known. We have applied this model to explain the observed spectrum of all known pulsars. This model can explain why the high energy component of the pulsar spectrum is not simple exponential form. It is because the observed spectrum is a superposition of many simple exponential spectra for different state. In addition for some large power index the cut-off energy can be much less than GeV which results in GeV deficit pulsars,which is another way other than magnetic pair creation process (cf. Pub. 4) to explain the weak GeV-emission pulsars. This finding cover objective 1,2 and 3. In pub. 9, we studied how the magnetic axis change can change the accelerator properties and hence affect the phase resolved spectrum and overall radiation power. We analyse the Fermi satellite data of PSR J2021 and find that the radiation properties is changed after glitch. We argue that the glitch can change the mangetic axis very slightly about 5 degree but this is large enough to cause the overall radiation power change by 20% and the phase resolved spectrum. This is related to objective 2. In pub. 10, we explain why the Crab-like pulsar in LMC is much more powerful than the Crab pulsar in our galaxy. This can be explained due to the inclination angle difference between these two similar age pulsars. The inclination angle can affect the structure of pulsar magnetosphere significantly. This relates to objective 3. In pub. 11, we compare the properties of radio-quiet and radio-loud gamma-ray pulsars, we find that their spectral curvature index, F_g/F_x ratio and B_lc are significantly different. We can explain these differences by using the outergap model and the viewing geometry. This relates to objective 2 and 3.

17300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300814.value: We have developed a non-stationary model to explain why the high energy component beyond the cut-off energy will not behave as a simple exponential as predicted by simple curvature radiation model. It is because the observations do not have enough time resolution to identify the spectrum in short period of time. The reported observed spectrum is actually a time average spectrum over a time scale bigger than several weeks to months, which is much larger than the fluctuation time scale of the accelerator. The non-stationary model suggests that the accelerator potential and current can be in many different states and correspond to different spectrum. Consequently the observed spectrum is the average spectrum over all these different states. However we find that some pulsars, e.g. Crab, Vela and Geminga, they can emit some photons with energy higher than any possible states if the emission is curvature radiation. For example the Crab is detected with photon energies >100GeV. We speculate that inverse Compton process with either IR and radio in the ambient may explain this problem. We can study this possibility in next GRF project.

17300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300814.value: In this project we have studied some key problems of high energy emission from pulsars. We believe that the actual accelerator in the pulsar magnetosphere is not a steady state situation instead it is a dynamical accelerator, which can be described in terms of a distribution of non-stationary states. In each state the spectrum can be described by a power law with a simple exponential spectrum. However the observational spectrum is a time average over many states, consequently a non-exponential high energy tail beyond several GeV is formed. We calculate gamma-ray spectrum from canonical pulsars and millisecond pulsars and find that they are very similar. The geometric effect, i.e. inclination angle and viewing actually pay very important role in the observed spectrum. The Crab-like pulsar in LMC is more powerful than the Crab pulsar could be due to these effect. In addition pulsar glitch can also change the inclination suddenly and hence result in sudden spectral change. This suggestion has been used to explain the suddent spectral change of the glitching pulsar PSR J2021.

17301214.label: Project Objectives
17301214.value: To propose a structural firm value model for two correlated firms in an incomplete information market. To obtain the conditional distribution of default times and firm asset values and show the existence of the default intensity. To develop theory for the analytic solution of the default correlation structure in a reduced-form model transformed from a structural firm value model. To extend the theory to the case of more than two correlated firms and apply it to solve the counterparty risk problem. To apply the developed results, simulation methods and numerical implementations, to solve the problem of pricing credit derivatives in the proposed structural firm value model under the assumption of incomplete market information.

17301214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301214.value: Modeling credit risk has long been an important research issue for both researchers and practitioners. In particular, since the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers in 2008, credit risk modeling has received much more attention. In this project, we shall investigate the relations between different models, in particular, the relationship between reduced-form models and structural models in an incomplete information market. The major difficulty comes from the fact that default events are not independent but they are correlated. We shall focus on the correlation structure of two firms with the model transformed from a structural model to a reduced-form model due to incomplete information. Analytic solutions and numerical implementations will also be developed for our proposed models. Extension of the results to the case of more than two firms will be addressed, and this is useful for studying the counterparty risk problem. We expect our results obtained in this project will contribute to a better understanding of default risk contagion and also the selection of appropriate credit risk models. As a consequence, we can gain a new perspective for pricing and hedging default risk in an incomplete information market. 信用風險的建模一直是研究者和從業員的一個重要的研究課題。特別是，由於雷曼兄弟在2008年破產，信用風險模型獲得了更多的關注。在這個項目中，我們將探討不同模型之間的關係，特別是信息不完全的市場中，簡化模型和結構模型的關係。研究的主要困難來自一個事實，即違約事件不是獨立的，而是相關的。我們著眼於兩家公司由於信息不完全，從結構模型轉化成簡化模型的關聯結構。解析解和數值實現也將基於我們所提出的模型開發出來。我們把模型擴展到多家公司的情況，這將用於研究第三方交易風險問題。我們期待我們的研究結果將有助於研究者們更好地了解違約風險的傳染性和選擇適當的信用風險模型。從而，我們會對在不完全信息的市場下，違約風險的定價和對沖問題有一個新的認識。

17301214.label: Realisation of objectives
17301214.value: The proposed objectives of this project are generally achieved. The research results obtained from the project have been reported in [1-9] and a number of them have been published in top international journals such as Automatica, Quantitative Finance, and Journal of Economic Dynamics & Control, etc. In this project, we proposed a structural asset value model for two correlated firms using a two-dimensional Brownian motion under the situation of incomplete information [2]. The information set available to the market participants is assumed to include the default time of each firm and the periodic asset value reports. The original structural model was first transformed to a reduced-form model, and then the conditional distribution of the default time together with the asset value of each name were obtained analytically. The existence of the intensity processes of default times was proved and the explicit form of the intensity process was also obtained. Possible extension into three names case by considering a special correlation structure was illustrated. As the structural model can be transformed to a reduced-form model, we then studied a reduced-form intensity-based credit risk model with a hidden Markov process [4]. We proposed a novel filtering method to extract the underlying state given the observation processes. The method could be applied to a broad range of problems. Based on this model, the joint distribution of multiple default times was derived without imposing any stringent assumptions on the form of default intensities. Closed-form formulas for the distribution of default times were also obtained. The formulas could be applied to a number of practical financial problems and we demonstrated an application to pricing credit derivatives by numerical simulations. We then further investigated the reduced-form intensity-based model where the default intensities are determined by the hidden economic states governing by a Markov chain, as well as the past defaults [9]. An Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm was proposed to estimate the model parameters with an application to pricing credit default swap (CDS). Using real-world default data, we conducted numerical experiments to compare the results under our models with real recession periods in US. The results show that our model is able to capture the hidden features and simulate credit default risks which are important in risk management. A general framework was proposed for modeling default risk where default processes for all the entities (multiple firms) are governed by interacting default probabilities [5]. A general formula was obtained for the joint distribution of two important random variables featuring the severity of a crisis: duration of a crisis and severity of the defaults. These two quantities are useful risk measures in a default cycle. A new Markovian infectious two-sector model was proposed. It allows the causality of defaults of two sectors in both directions and therefore enriches the dynamics of the dependent default risk. Recovery rate is another important and interesting issue in risk management. The difference between economic default date and recorded default date was studied [1]. We developed reduced-form models for characterizing the economic and obtained recorded default times and their probability distributions. Numerical experiments with empirical data were given to demonstrate the results and provide a new perspective for economic and recorded defaults which has a significant impact on the estimation of recovery rate. We also investigated and solved two other related problems: optimal portfolio selection problems with a risk constraint and long-term memory of economic conditions, and optimal market making problems under information asymmetry. We solved an optimal portfolio selection problem in the presence of the Maximum Value-at-Risk (MVaR) with the price dynamics of the multiple risky assets governed by a hidden Markov process [3]. The problem was successfully reduced to a Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation using the separation principle. We developed a numerical algorithm to solve the HJB equation efficiently. We then studied an optimal portfolio selection problem under a high-order hidden Markov-modulated autoregressive (HO-HMMAR) model [6]. Numerical experiments were conducted to demonstrate that the model can effectively incorporate the long-term memory of hidden economic states in modeling price dynamics, and therefore producing better forecasting results and performance in portfolio strategies. Another high-order interactive hidden Markov model (HOIHMM) was developed [7]. It can incorporate both the feedback effects of observable states on hidden states and their mutual long-term dependence. An efficient heuristic algorithm was proposed to estimate the hidden states of the chain and the model parameters. Demonstrated by using real-world default data, the proposed model can effectively identify the high risk periods. An optimal market making problem under information asymmetry was studied [8]. An event-triggered regime-switching jump-diffusion model was introduced with a view to incorporating the impact of asymmetric information on optimal trading decisions. The modeling structure is novel in the sense that it can disentangle the behavior of three different types of traders, namely uninformed, partially informed and informed traders.

17301214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301214.value: The research results of this project have been reported in 9 papers. A number of the papers [1-9] have been published in top international journals. Two Ph.D. students and one M. Phil. student were also trained. We successfully proposed a structural firm value model for two correlated firms. The existence of the intensity processes of default times was proved and the explicit form of the intensity process was also obtained with possible extension to the case of three names. A better understanding between structural models and reduced-form models is achieved. A novel filtering method for extracting hidden state was developed for the reduced-form intensity-based models. The model can be applied to a broad range of problems. In particular, we obtained closed-from formulas for the distributions of default times. The models and methods can be efficiently applied to a number of practical financial problems such as hedging and pricing credit derivatives of multiple firms [2,4,5,9]. Other interesting models and results were also developed for the recovery rate problems, optimal portfolio selection problems with a risk constraint and optimal market making problems under information asymmetry [1,3,6-8].

17301214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301214.value: The models and methods developed in this project can be further extended from the applications in pricing credit derivatives to portfolio management and trading strategy with default risk. Another potential direction is to consider data-driven models in our proposed problems by employing data assimilation methods. We plan to prepare a research grant proposal for the mentioned research directions.

17301214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301214.value: Pricing and hedging financial products in the presence of default risk are important topics in financial markets. Therefore, advanced quantitative models and efficient numerical methods are required for the valuations of such products. In this project, new and general model frameworks with mathematical theory were proposed and established for studying the default process of correlated firms. We provided closed-form formulas and efficient algorithms for solving the models numerically, and thus the computational time can be saved significantly. Since our model and approach are quite general, they can be applied not only to hedging and pricing credit derivatives but also other practical valuation problems in finance.

17301314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301314.value: Alkaloids are nitrogen-containing natural products, many of which are biologically and pharmacologically active. The synthesis of these types of compounds require reaction tools that are able to incorporate the nitrogen residue efficiently and with the correct stereochemistry. We have discovered an intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of substituted pyrroles that are able to construct the tricyclic nitrogen-bridged carbon framework efficiently, and in an asymmetric manner. This reaction tool would enable the synthesis of complex polycyclic alkaloids. This project aims to study the scope of the intramolecular pyrrole (4+3) cycloaddition, and to demonstrate its utility as a key step in the asymmetric total synthesis of a complex alkaloid, himandrine. Thus far, only one total synthesis of this hexacyclic alkaloid bearing 10 stereocenters has been reported. The completion of the total synthesis of this significant molecule would be a feat that demonstrates the power of this epoxy enolsilane cycloaddition methodology. 生物碱是一类含氮的天然產物， 其中許多具有生物醫藥活性。 合成這類化合物通常需要應用一些能高效引入含氮基團的反應， 同時需要構建正確的立體化學。 我們初步的研究表明取代的吡咯分子内（4+3）環加成反應可以 高效地、不對稱地構建含有氮橋的三環結構。這一反應將成爲 複雜的多環生物碱的合成中十分有用的工具。 本課题的研究目的主要是研究吡咯分子内（4+3）環加成反應的 底物普適性及其應用於複雜生物碱Himandrine的不對稱全合成中 的關鍵步骤。Himandrine是含有l0個手性中心的六環生物碱， 到目前爲止只有一例全合成報道。因而完成這分子的全合成將有 力表明環氧烯醇硅醚的環加成反應在複雜分子全合成中所 具有的廣闊應用前景。

17301314.label: Realisation of objectives
17301314.value: All the objectives have been visited and completed. Objective 1: A total of 13 pyrrole-tethered epoxy enolsilanes have been synthesized. The substrates vary in the protecting group on the pyrrole nucleus, variations in substitution on the 2- and 4-positions on the pyrrole, and the substituents at the epoxy enolsilane. Objective 2: All of the synthesized pyrrole substrates have been subjected to (4+3) cycloaddition. The reaction proceeded in moderate to excellent yields, and generally with good diastereoselectivity. The cycloaddition has also been demonstrated to be able to afford optically pure cycloadducts. All of the variations incorporated into the substrates are tolerated. All of the major cycloadducts were found to be endo, except the 3-substituted pyrrole underwent cycloaddition predominantly in the exo mode. Some intramolecular cycloaddition results will be combined with previous cycloaddition results to be published together in a full paper in the Journal of Organic Chemistry; the manuscript is under preparation. Objective 3: An enantiomerically enriched substrate that yielded three rings of the core of himandrine was synthesized, in 7 steps. The intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition proceeded successfully to generate the exo cycloadduct as the major diastereomer, and in good ee. Objective 4 Using the exo-cycloadduct obtained, we have subjected this cycloadduct to an additional 11 transformations to successfully synthesize the core of the natural product, himandrine, bearing rings B, C, D, E, F. Many functional groups proved to be tolerated. This pyrrole cycloaddition methodology and partial synthesis were combined for greater impact, and published in the journal Angewandte Chemie International Edition in 2018.

17301314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301314.value: 1. Pyrroles undergo the (4+3) cycloaddition in the intramolecular sense only, not intermolecular. This was a difficult cycloaddition, because pyrroles are more aromatic and they undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction only. However, we have shown that the intramolecular cycloaddition with epoxy enolsilanes as the dienophile was effective, surprisingly with a variety of protecting groups on the pyrrole of a variety of electron demands, from as electron-rich groups as methyl to as electron poor protecting groups as nosyl. This is signficant, given that pyrroles are much less competent dienes for cycloaddition than furans. Moreover, this is the first intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition with pyrroles that generate a fused nortropane skeleton. It is also significant that the cycloadducts are obtained with excellent ee, retained from the epoxide. All the pyrroles were effective in the intramolecular cycloaddition which proceeded in good to excellent yields and high endo selectivity. The intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of pyrroles reliably generate fused tropane derivatives. 2. All pyrroles underwent endo (4+3) cycloaddition except the 3-substituted pyrroles, which were predominantly exo. This result allowed us to choose the correct epoxide stereochemistry to generate the correct stereochemistry of the nitrogen bridge. 3. A complex subunit of the himandrine was synthesized asymmetrically. A 3-substituted pyrrole substrate was assembled in 7 steps. Importantly, an asymmetric epoxidation was used to set up the key directing element in this cycloaddition. Under the optimized conditions, cycloaddition proceeded to provide the desired enantiomerically enriched exo cycloadduct. This cycloadduct was further subjected to additional reactions to fashion the final two rings, to afford the BCDEF pentacyclic subunit of himandrine, which was also common to all of the Type II galbulimima alkaloids, as a proof-of-concept synthesis for this intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of pyrroles. These results were published in the journal Angewandte Chemie in 2018.

17301314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301314.value: As the proof-of-concept synthesis for the application of the intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of pyrroles with epoxy enolsilanes to a subunit of the natural product has been completed, a full synthesis incorporating the final ring A, can now be attempted. The total synthesis of himandrine is now being pursued in our group, using the strategy already developed. Himandrine has anti-spasmodic and antihypertensive activities, and this synthesis may be able to generate analogues for bioactivity testing. Based on the success of this reaction, additional dienophiles, such as aziridinyl enolsilanes, can also be tried in this reaction, as other aromatic dienophiles such as thiophenes as well.

17301314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301314.value: Tropanes are important subunits of over 20 drugs in clinical use. The (4+3) cycloaddition of pyrroles should generate nortropinones directly but due to the aromaticity of pyrroles, they are not reactive and competent dienes. However, our studies showed that the intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition of pyrroles with epoxy enolsilanes as dienophiles proceed effectively and are able to generate fused nortropane framework. This is the first such intramolecular cycloaddition with pyrroles. It is also able to provide the cycloadducts in enantiomerically enriched forms. To demonstrate the utility of this reaction, it has been used as a key step in the synthesis of the pentacyclic core of himandrine, a natural product with anti-hypertensive and anti-spasmodic activities. The subunit has been synthesized successfully and in optically enriched form. These results lay the ground work for the total synthesis of this bioactive natural product.
