17301814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301814.value: The major concern of this proposal is the problem of computing the capacity of a finite-state channel, which is a fundamental problem in information theory and has been open for decades. Equipped with the ideas and techniques from some recent work by the information theory community, we propose to tackle this important yet challenging problem. As elaborated in the proposal, our two recent results, "the analyticity result" and "the limit theorem result", are of vital importance to our approaches. Roughly speaking, "the analyticity result" confirms that the mutual information rate of our channel is an analytic function, which, as elaborated in the proposal, opens the door to a vast collection of derivative-based numerical methods. On the other hand, "the limit theorem result" confirms that the mutual information rate, which is extremely difficult to compute otherwise, can be "well-approximated" using Monte Carlo simulations, and it further suggests that its derivatives can be effectively simulated as well. In this proposal, we plan to conduct in-depth investigations of modifications/adaptations an extensive collection of numerical methods for the computation of the capacity of finite-state channels, including "expectation-maximization method", "stochastic approximation method", "Newton-based method", "convex programming method" and their numerous variants. A deluge of theoretical problems (on the functional behavior of the mutual information rate of our finite-state channel) naturally arise when implementing and analyzing the above-mentioned numerical methods, including differentiability/asymptotics/concavity of the mutual information rate, the location of the capacity achieving distribution and accurate approximation of the mutual information rate and its derivatives. Not only can the solutions to these problem advance our understanding of the convergence behavior of the proposed algorithms, they are also of great theoretical significance and interest in their own right. Our preliminary investigations reveal that our approaches to the fundamental problem of channel capacity computation are promising. Indeed, we have recently designed a stochastic approximation algorithm, which is the first algorithm with proven convergence and convergence rate for some practical finite-state channels. If the project is carried out successfully, we will have effective algorithms that compute the capacity of a wide range of practical finite-state channels with proven convergence rate and thus completely solve this long open problem, and we will also gain in-depth understanding of the behavior of the mutual information rate of finite-state channels as a function of the input and channel parameters, such as differentiability, asymptotics and concavity. 本提案的主要問題是計算一個有限狀態通道的容量。這是資訊理論中的一個基本問題，幾十年後還是沒有解決。 最近資訊理論研究的進展給了我們很多的有用的工具和思想， 並且似乎這些新的思想和工具對本提案會有很大的幫助。詳細來講，我們 我們兩個最近的結果“解析性結果”和“極限定理的結果“，是至關重要的方法，粗略地說，在”解析性結果“中，我們證明通道的互資訊率是一個解析函數。另一方面，“極限定理的結果”確認該互資訊率可使用蒙特卡羅模擬。 在此提案中，我們計畫進行深入調查的計算一個有限狀態通道的容量的問題。我們要調查的方法包括“期望最大化法”，“隨機逼近法“，”牛頓型法“，”凸規劃法“和其眾多的變種。我們所提出的演算法有在重大的理論意義和實用價值。事實上，我們最近設計了一個隨機逼近演算法，這是第一個實用的收斂演算法. 如果項目成功實施，我們將有一個有效的算法可以廣泛應用來計算的有限狀態通道的容量.

17301814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301814.value: One of the major findings in this project is a randomized algorithm for a broad class of finite-state channels, which proves to be convergent and feature an expilicit convergence rate (Reference 1). The algorithm and the ideas and techiniques have been used in some subsequent work dealing with input-constrained/continuous-output channels (see References 2, 3 and 4). Another major finding is an extension (see Reference 5) of the influential I-MMSE relatioship by Guo, Verdu and Shamai to the feedback/memory case, which promises uses in communications scearios where feedback/memory/interference might be present.

17301814.value: We are looking to extend the results from this project to continuous-time settings, for which there is a resurge of interests lately.

17301814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301814.value: Discrete-time finite-state channels are a broad class of channels which have attracted plenty of interest in information theory; prominent examples of such channels include partial response channels, Gilbert-Elliott channels and noisy input-restricted channels, which are widely used in a variety of real-life applications, such as magnetic and optical recording, and communications over channels with inter-symbol interference. The computation of the capacity of a finite-state channel is notoriously difficult and has been open for decades. For a discrete memoryless channel with a discrete memoryless source at its input, the classical Blahut-Arimoto algorithm can effectively compute the channel capacity, however, for almost all nontrivial finite-state channels, little is known about the channel capacity other than some bounds, which are numerically computed using Monte Carlo approaches. This project is meant to conduct a thorough information-theoretic analysis of such channels and propose methodology for computation of the capacity of finite-state channels. The project has been successfully carried out and all the proposed objectives have been successfully realized. In particuar, we have proposed an algorithm that proves to be effective for computing the capacity of a broad class of finite-state channels, which is the first algorithm with proven convergence rate.

17302214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302214.value: Organic compounds of high degree of complexity are now known to be widespread in the Universe, ranging from objects in our Solar System to distant galaxies. Through the techniques of millimeter-wave spectroscopy, over 170 molecules have been identified from their rotational transitions. Space infrared spectroscopy has detected the stretching and bending modes of compounds with aromatic and aliphatic structures. Analyses of samples of meteorites, comets, asteroids, and interplanetary dust also revealed a rich content of organic substances, some of which could be of extra-solar origin. A number of unexplained astronomical phenomena (diffuse interstellar bands, 217.5 nm feature, extended red emission, 21-micron feature, etc.) are also likely to originate from organic carriers. The understanding of the origin, evolution, chemical composition and structure, and distribution of organic matter in space is a topic of high current interest in astronomy. From spectroscopic studies of the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars, we have learned that these stars are major sources of organic molecules and solids. By performing spectroscopic studies of objects in successive stages of evolution, we have found evidence for molecular synthesis from acetylene to benzene to aromatic compounds. In this study, we propose to continue our observation and analysis of spectral behaviour of stars in the last hundred thousand years of evolution using a variety of observational techniques. These observations will be complemented by computer quantum chemistry calculations to determine the chemical structure of the organic compounds. These works will allow us to construct and test chemical and physical theories leading to the synthesis of organic compounds. 極複雜的有機物質遍佈整個宇宙，由太陽系中的天體直到遙遠的星系。透過毫米波光譜學的技術，科學家憑旋轉躍遷辨認出超過170種份子。此外，太空紅外光譜儀曾偵測到同時帶有脂肪族及芳香族結構的化合物所發出的伸縮和彎曲譜線。隕石、彗星、小行星，和行星際塵埃的樣本分析亦顯示當中含有豐富的有機物質，有些甚至可能源自太陽系之外。一些未能解釋的天文現象，包括散射星際物質光譜帶、217.5納米特徵、延伸紅光譜線、及21-微米特徵等，都似乎源自有機物質。太空中有機物質的來源、演化、化學成份和結構，及它們的分佈已成為天文界當今的熱門話題。 從已演化恆星周圍包層的光譜研究，我們得知這些恆星就是有機份子和固體粒子的主要來源。而不同演化階段的天體光譜研究，又証明了從乙炔到苯繼而到芳香族的份子合成過程。是項研究讓我們得以繼續對經歷了數十萬年演化過程的恆星進行各種觀測及分析，再配合電腦的糧子化學計算，從而確定當中有機化合物的化學結構。好讓我們構思和測試出有機化合物合成過程的化學和物理學原理。

17302214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302214.value: We have proposed that the unidentified infrared emission features through throughout the universe is due to complex organic compounds, specifically mixed aromatic aliphatic organic nanoparticles. This proposal, first published by us in Nature in 2011, is followed up by further observations and quantum chemical calculations. Our results have attracted worldwide attention, as they have significant implications on the origin of organics in the solar system and on the origin of life on Earth. Interest from the international community is evidenced by the fact that the PI delivered 20 invited talks at international conferences and in colloquia given at international institutions in 2017 (http://www.scifac.hku.hk/kwok/colloquia_lectures.html). A major part of the research progress has been on the quantum chemistry calculations of the vibrational spectra of complex organics, which has never previously been attempted. We have also been able to relate the carriers of astronomical unidentified infrared emission bands to organics in the solar system, as well as possible carriers of other unexplained astronomical spectral phenomena such as the 21 micron emission, extended red emission, 220 nm band, etc. Our observations of molecular species in the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars have supported our premise that evolved stars are major sources of molecules and solids in the Galaxy, and is the source of abiotic synthesis of organics.

17302414.label: Realisation of objectives
17302414.value: Computational studies have been carried out to study the electronic structure and the origin of the low-energy excited states for a series of platinum complexes. In particular, geometry optimizations using density functional theory (DFT) have been performed on the ground-state structures of these platinum complexes and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations on the optimized ground-state structures have been performed to study the factors which govern the ordering of the singlet and triplet excited states. In addition, the low-lying triplet excited states have been optimized with the unrestricted DFT formalism and TDDFT calculations on the optimized low-lying triplet excited states have been carried out to compute the singlet–singlet and singlet–triplet transitions for the study of the radiative decay rate constants, in order to investigate the factors controlling the radiative process of the platinum complexes, and to understand the differences in the radiative decay rate constants among the complexes with different pincer and ancillary ligands. Furthermore, in order to explore the potential energy profiles for the deactivation process from the lowest-lying triplet excited state via the triplet metal-centered (3MC) state, which is crucial to the nonradiative decay, the 3MC state and the transition state between the lowest-lying triplet excited state and the 3MC state have been optimized on the potential energy surface. Moreover, the effect of the substituents attached to the ligands on the energy of the 3MC state has been explored, and the results provide an in-depth understanding of the effect of the ligands on their different photophysical behaviors as well as crucial information for the future design of platinum(II) complexes in various applications. To ultimately obtain a detailed picture of the deactivation process, the minimum energy crossing points (MECPs) between the 3MC and the ground state surfaces have been located for the investigation of the feasibility of the regeneration of the ground state from the 3MC state. To study the effect of metal centers on the radiative and nonradiative processes, density functional theory density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations have also been performed on a series of square planar gold(III) alkynyl complexes for comparison study. A comparison of the processes between the platinum(II) and gold(III) complexes have been made. It has been found that the electronic properties of the metal center could have a significant impact on the radiative and non-radiative processes. Please note that due to the departure of Dr. W.H. Lam in September 2015, there was a change of PI from Dr. W. H. Lam to Prof. V.W.W. Yam with Dr. Lam as a Co-I, approved by the RGC. The conference expenditure was not used as a result of Dr. Lam’s departure.

17302414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302414.value: Computational study using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) has been performed on platinum complexes with two classes of dianionic pincer ligands, 2,6-diphenylpyridine (C^N^C system) and 2,6-bis(1H-1,2,4-triazol-5-yl)pyridine (N^N^N systems, to gain more insight into the radiative and nonradiative decay processes that are critical to their luminescence properties. Several factors were found to be critical to the radiative process of the platinum pincer complexes, that is, the contribution of the platinum d orbital character to the electronic configuration of both the singlet excited states and the lowest-lying triplet excited state, the oscillator strengths of the singlet excited states, and the energy separation between the lowest-lying triplet excited state and the singlet excited states. Larger platinum d orbital character in singlet excited states and the lowest-lying triplet excited state, higher oscillator strengths in the singlet excited states and a smaller energy difference between the singlet excited states and the lowest-lying triplet excited state would lead to a larger radiative decay rate constant and enhance the radiative decay process. Meanwhile, the luminescence properties of the platinum complexes being studied also depend on their nonradiative deactivation pathways via the 3MC state. The nonradiative deactivation pathway would be energetically more favorable with a smaller energy separation between the lowest-lying triplet excited state and the 3MC state, a smaller barrier height for the conversion from the lowest-lying triplet excited state to the 3MC state, and a lower-lying crossing point between the 3MC and the ground state surfaces, with respect to the 3MC state. Moreover, it was observed that the large structural distortion of the lowest-lying triplet excited state from the corresponding ground state would lead to a thermally accessible crossing point between the lowest-lying triplet excited state and the ground state surfaces for nonradiative deactivation. Apart from the platinum complexes with di-anionic C^N^C and N^N^N ligands mentioned above, DFT and TDDFT calculations have also been performed on a new series of luminescent platinum complexes with mono-anionic N^C^N ligand to provide additional insights on the nature of their photophysical properties, in order to obtain correlation between calculations and experiments for the study of excited state processes of the platinum complexes. The computational results obtained with the hybrid Perdew, Burke, and Ernzerhof (PBE0) functional are in good agreement with the experimental results obtained from the photophysical measurements such as electronic absorption and emission spectroscopy. For instance, the optimized ground-state geometry shows good agreement with the experimental X-ray crystal structure, the TDDFT results further support the assignment of the electronic absorption spectra, and the calculated emission energies fairly agree with the experimental values. (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2017, 139, 10750-10761). In addition to platinum complexes, DFT and TDDFT calculations have also been carried out on a series of square planar gold(III) alkynyl complexes to investigate their radiative and nonradiative decay processes, so that a comparison of the processes between the platinum and gold(III) complexes could be made. It has been found that, the cyclometalated gold(III) complexes possess a larger radiative decay rate constant compared to the complex with pure nitrogen-donor pincer ligands. Furthermore, it has been shown that the position of the carbon rings in the pincer ligand has a small effect on the energy of the emissive state. Nevertheless, by shifting the lateral phenyl ring to the central position, the nonradiative deactivation process becomes energetically less favorable (Inorg. Chem. 2015, 54, 3624-3630).

17302414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302414.value: The present work provides a detailed picture of both the radiative and nonradiative decay processes via the 3MC state, and an in-depth understanding on the effect of the di-anionic pincer ligands on the different photophysical behaviors among the platinum complexes and gold(III) alkynyl complexes. These results are crucial to the future design of platinum and gold(III) complexes for sensing, photonic and other applications. In the future, more computational studies are needed to be carried out on the platinum and gold(III) complexes with other tridentate pincer ligands to provide guidance for the design of luminescent complexes with specific applications.

17302414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302414.value: Computational study based on density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) has been carried out on a series of platinum complexes with tridentate pincer ligands to investigate the radiative and nonradiative decay processes that are critical to their luminescence properties. The factors that control the radiative decay process have been investigated and the potential energy profiles for the nonradiative deactivation process from the emissive state via the metal-centered excited states of the platinum complexes have been explored. Such computational studies have also been carried out on gold(III) alkynyl complexes for comparison with the platinum complexes. This work does not only provide a better understanding on the electronic structures, photophysical properties, radiative and nonradiative processes of selected platinum and gold(III) complexes, but also provides guidance for the design of luminescent complexes with various applications in the future. The outcome of this work has contributed to the publication of high-impact international SCI journal articles and training of a PhD student.

17302514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302514.value: In 1839, Dirichlet proved a formula, known as Dirichlet's class number formula today, that expresses the class number in terms of the value of Dirichlet L-functions at the point 1. Afterwards there are many studies on this value. Around fifteen years ago, Montgomery and Vaughan proposed some conjectures, on which Granville and Soundararajan made a notable advance. The Dirichlet L-functions constitute a special (or classical) class in the framework of GL(N) automorphic L-functions -- the L-functions attached to GL(N) automorphic forms. Thus it is of fundamental importance to extend the investigation to other L-functions. There are works by Cogdell and Michel, the PI and his collaborators, Lamzouri, etc, but still a lot of cases and problems remain uncultivated. In this project, we shall carry out a statistical study of the values of automorphic L-functions in some families at the point 1. Analogous conjectures of Montgomery and Vaughan will be formulated and investigated in the context of generic automorphic L-functions. To facilitate the project work, we shall develop a new auxiliary tool, called the Elliott-Montgomery-Vaughan (EMV) large sieve inequality, for GL(N) automorphic forms. A prototype of large sieve inequalities was devised by Linnik in the last century to study the least quadratic non-residue problem. The variant of EMV will be applied to tackle (part of) the conjecture of Montgomery and Vaughan. In addition, for GL(2) automorphic forms, EMV has another application, which shows its independent interest, on the sign problem of their Fourier coefficients. In this project, we shall study the GL(N) case. 1839年，Dirchlet 證明了一個公式，今天我們被它稱為 Dirichlet 類數公式。這公式以 Dirchlet L-函數在點1之值來表示類數，此後有許多相關研究。約15年前， Montgomery 和 Vaughan 提出了一些猜想，在此方面 Granville 和 Soundararajan 取得了顯著的進展。 在 GL(N) 自守 L-函數（即連接到 GL(N）自守形式的 L-函數）框架下，Dirichlet L-函數只是一個特殊（或古典）的部族。因此，將 Granville 和 Soundararajan 的研究伸延至其他 L-函數是至關重要的。有這方面，現有 Cogdell 和 Michel ，首席研究員和他的合作者，Lamzouri 等等的著作，但還是有不少情況和問題仍然是未開墾的。在這個項目中，我們將進行某些族中自守 L-函數在點1之值的統計研究，並提出及了解類似 Montgomery 和 Vaughan 的猜想。 為了這個項目工作，我們要開展一個對於 GL(N) 自守形式的新輔助工具，叫做 Elliott-Montgomery-Vaughan（EMV）大篩不等式。 這大篩不等式的原型是在上世紀 Linnik 研究最少的二次非剩餘問題所創立的。EMV 的變體被應用來處理（部分）Montgomery 和 Vaughan 的猜想。此外， EMV 在 GL(2) 自守形式的傅立葉係數的正負值問題上，有另一個有趣的應用。在這個項目中，我們將研究GL(N) 的情況。

17302514.value: Objective 1: We extended successfully the Elliott-Montgomery-Vaughan large sieve inequality in the GL(2) case to GL(N). Objective 2: We carried out an investigation of asymptotic formulas for moments. Objective 3: We studied lower and upper bounds in order to understand the size of exceptional forms. Objective 4: We approach the problem by considering the density. Objective 5: A graduate student is recruited but he may finally work on another topic.

17302514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302514.value: An Elliott-Montgomery-Vaughan large sieve inequality is derived for the GL(N) case, and the result is of the same strength as the GL(2) case, cf. Output 4. Asymptotic formulas for moments are obtained, which generalized the GL(2) case in a quite satisfactory way, cf. Output 2. Lower and upper bounds are derived, cf. Output 2. We show that the zero density of forms such that the real part of their Fourier coefficients over a certain sector of primes are of a specific pattern of signs, cf. Output 4. In addition Outputs 1 and 3 are partly consequences of the research activities for this project.

17302514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302514.value: It would be interesting to consider automorphic forms for other groups, such as GSp, other than the general linear group. For this it is necessary to understand the known trace formulas in the literature and identify, if any, the right formula to work out.

17302514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302514.value: We have successful extended the study of some interesting problems on GL(2) objects to GL(n) objects for n bigger than 2. This is not a routine generalization since the higher rank case (i.e. n larger than 2) is more complicated and many things are not well-understood.

17302714.value: 钼和钨簇合物的斑岩成矿流体的实验和计算研究 鉬和鎢簇合物的斑岩成礦流體的實驗和計算研究

17302714.label: Project Objectives
17302714.value: To examine the composition, molecular structure and thermodynamic properties of mono- and polynuclear molybdate clusters and the affinity of transition metals for molybdate species. The goal of this effort is to identify the range of molybdate clusters present in complex multi-component electrolyte solutions because molybdate speciation is strongly influenced by the type and level of cation present in natural aqueous fluids. Ion cluster studies will be undertaken using FT-ICR mass spectrometry and density functional theory calculations with the aim to 1) probe the stoichiometries and abundances of molybdate clusters and their corresponding molecular structures and energetic properties, 2) using ESI mass spectrometry and theoretical calculations to examine the affinity of transition metal ions, such as copper, nickel, cobalt and gold for molybdate clusters and 3) to compare trends in the predicted stepwise energy profile of molybdate clustering, metalation and solvation reactions with variations in measured ion signal intensities. The objective of task2 is to apply ion resonance mass spectrometry and quantum chemical calculations to characterize the molecular compositions, geometries, solvation behaviour and thermodynamic properties of tungstate clusters. These FT-ICR mass spectrometric studies will be performed using a modified ESI source designed to facilitate higher ion throughput. From such mass spectrometric and molecular simulation studies we hope to gain a deeper understanding of 1) the range of tungstate clusters, water-free and microsolvated, present in water vapor, 2) the nature of the solvation shell surrounding tungstate clusters and the influence that microsolvation has on the stability of individual tungstate species, 3) the affinity of transition metal cations to tungstate clusters, specifically, the structure of metalated tungstates and their thermodynamic properties both at ambient and elevated temperatures.

17302714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302714.value: 大約 2.0×10^9 立方公里的水存在與地殼中，這比世界上所有湖泊和河流中的水的總體級還要多2500倍。大量的水由於浮力上昇，穿過地殼時會引起高溫水岩反應；這類反應對地殼中的金屬的流動，揮發分離和再分佈有重要影響。在水岩反應的熱液持續上升解壓相分離的過程中，一個高密度的液相和一個低密度氣相會同時形成；這兩者俱有不同的氫鍵特徵和理化性質。此類低密度的氣相，是化學和地熱工程領域的研究重點；尤其是在地球化學方面，此低密度氣相對水熱反應中金屬的形態和移動有重要的意義。舉例來說，地震時岩石裂解，富金屬脈在熱力反應中成型，這與礦床的形成緊密有關。當前我們對於金屬的水汽反應的理解，多是通過對金屬的分離和分解進行的實驗研究，但對於金屬在同類條件下的分子級結構和穩定性卻知之甚少。因此，不論是在實驗還是理論方面，我們對於氣相金屬在分子水平上的地球化學反應都需要進一步的研究。 金屬酸鹽是一類重要的地化物質，並且俱有複雜的特性和高親水性（水溶性）。 從成礦的角度講，由於越來越多的光譜數據證明金屬酸鹽尤其是鉬（Mo）酸鹽和鎢（W）酸鹽是高度穩定的，這種穩定性對於地殼中鉬和鎢的流動性俱有很大的影響。當前儘有少量針對氣相的鉬酸鹽和鎢酸鹽的實驗和理論研究，而絕大多數的實驗研究儘關注與較高密度的堆積狀液相的金屬酸鹽的形成，而非針對水蒸氣作為輸送載體對金屬酸鹽的影響。我們的研究小組的主攻方向以及本實驗方案的重點則是通過利用傅里葉變換離子迴旋共振質譜（FT-ICR/MS）和量子化學的方法來研究氣相的鉬酸鹽和鎢酸鹽的結構和穩定性。

17302714.label: Realisation of objectives
17302714.value: Objective1: We recruited two PhD students (Tony, Zhang Yimeng, completion date Dec210; M. Taczkowska, PhD completion date Jan2015) who are conducting their thesis research under HKU-17302714. As noted previously, it is a challenge to identify good experimental PhD. candidates who are willing to work at the interface between chemistry and the Earth sciences; M. Taczkowska, Y. Zhang and I have conducted a series of FTMS experiments looking at the stability and the distribution of POM clusters, in particular those containing Mo. These FTMS Studies have been undertaken to probe the molecular scale speciation of Mo oxide clusters present in aqueous solution and water vapor. These experimental studies have been complimented with a wide range of quantum chemical calculations, in particular, DFT studies of structures and thermodynamic properties; three manuscripts have evolved from this work, one has recently been published as a Review paper by the PI, ie K.H. Lemke and T.M Seward (2018) “Molecular clusters and solvation in volcanic and hydrothermal vapors. Reviews in Mineralogy and Geochemistry, 84, 57, and two more are currently in their final stage of preparation. Objective2: This portion of HKU 17302714 deals with the speciation of tungstate clusters using FTMS and ab initio tools; experimental studies undertaken under objective2 dovetail directly with those undertaken under objective1, and focused on the molecular scale speciation of polytungstate clusters, both in the gas-phase and microsolvated; the later part is directly related to the speciation of W in low density ore fluids, and the role that water vapor would play in facilitating transport and redeposition of W; one manuscripts has evolved from this work (K.H. Lemke and T.M Seward (2018), and one more is currently in its final stage of preparation. We anticipate that these new data will guide other experimentalist and interested theoreticians to more closely examine the interactions between these metal clusters and solvating water molecules.

17302714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302714.value: Objective1: objective 1 focuses on the molecular scale characterization of molybdate clusters, their thermodynamic properties and the affinity of water molecules to interact with specific sites on these cluster services. An important conclusion that we have drawn from our FT mass spectrometric studies, is that ESI source conditions play a very important role in generating POM clusters, in other words, we have had to carefully explore the effects of ESI cone potential and capillary temperature on the stability of molybdate clusters, including ESI source effects on the POM water solvation shell. These FT-MS have shown for the first time that a wide range of molybdate clusters with up to 11 [MoO4] units exist in the gas-phase with varying degrees of water molecules attached; we have also for the first time identified, using both FT-MS and density functional tools, highly stable magic-number type clusters with 6 [MoO4] units, that are both sodiated and water solvated when electrosprayed from NaCl bearing stock solutions. Using a new set of molecular simulation tools, i.e. artificial bee colony algorithms and M06 type DFT tools, we have also been able to determine the structure of these molecular species. In general, these FT-MS and quantum chemical results appear to indicate that sodium-molybdate clusters containing hydrogen bonding water molecules on their surfaces would be stable in Mo-enriched hydrothermal and volcanic vapors, with important implications for molybdenum speciation and transport in the Earth’s crust. Objective2: building on our results from objective1, we have been able to identify a broad range of tungstate clusters using ESI FT-MS and molecular simulation tools; results from these experiments differ significantly from those FT-MS experiments in which we explored the molecular speciation of molybdate clusters: first, electrospray ionization of tungstate stock solutions generates a wide(r) range of clusters with up to 20 [WO4] units, singly, doubly and triply-charged; secondly, even under the harshest ESI conditions we were unable to “remove” all water molecules from these clusters, in other words, water appears to have a strong propensity to attach to most tungstate clusters, whereas molybdate clusters of the same size range do not appear to retain water molecules on their surfaces. We have complimented these FT-MS studies with DFT structure optimizations and energy calculations with the goal to identify global minimal structures for each cluster size, and each microsolvated tungstate cluster. Finally, results from ESI FT-MS experiments in which we ESI’ed along the tungstate/molybdate binary, demonstrate that polymerization extends to clusters with up to 4 metalate centers only, with 1-5 water molecules in each ion mass spectra; it is worth noting here that these type of FT-MS experiments are generally quite challenging because the ion intensities in these systems tend to be at ~ 10% relative to those commonly encountered in ESI FT-MS studies, and thus a considerable amount of time (months!) have been spent in our laboratory fine-tuning ion signals for tungstate/molybdate clusters.

17302714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302714.value: Results from our mass spectrometric and quantum chemical studies conducted under HKU-17302714 have important implications for our understanding of tungsten and molybdenum speciation in volcanic and hydrothermal vapors. A natural extension of this kind of FT-MS work is to mass-isolate Wo- and W- bearing clusters using OPO/OPA and free electron lasers for IRMPD type studies. Our in-house mass spectrometer has been coupled to an OPO/OPA IR laser system that can generate wave-tunable IR radiation in the 2800-4000 cm-1 wave number range. Several major challenges, however, still exist with these kind of OPO/OPA experiments, in particular, the relatively low laser power in the lower wave number range; this problem can now be overcome by using new free electron lasers such as such at FELIX, NL, that allow to measure IRMPD spectra down to the 300 cm-1 wave-number range with sufficient laser power even at 200-300 cm-1. We have over the last two years initiated two new RGC-funded research projects that make use of our of OPO/OPA and now also include beam time using FELIX type laser systems. Important metal-vapor clusters currently under investigation using OPO/OPA and FELIX facilities include, for example, mono- and polynuclear clusters generated from electrosprayed aqueous AuCl3 and CeCl3 systems, and these IRMPD studies can now be elegantly complimented with DFT, MP2 or even high level CCSD(T) frequency calculations using harmonic and VPT2 anharmonic approaches. These two newly funded RGC grants that have been developed directly from HKU-17302714 and are HKU-17330216 ($816,340) and HKU-173007118 ($505,298); we will be submitting an additional request for RGC-funding this coming fall 2019 focusing on probing metal clusters, with a particular relevance to ore vapors, using FT-MS, IRMPD and ab initio tools.

17302714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302714.value: Both tungsten and molybdenum occur ubiquitously throughout the earth’s crust, there are still large uncertainties with respect to their speciation in aqueous fluids, and even greater uncertainties with respect to they are vapor-phase distribution, structure and stability. The experimental and theoretical studies that we have undertaken as part of this project aim at characterizing the structure and stability of tungstate and molybdate clusters, and also center on identifying water solvated at tungstate/molybdate species that are likely to exist in naturally occurring volcanic and hydrothermal gases. In brief, our experiments indicate that gases and volcanic vapors containing W and Mo would contain characteristic distributions of tungstate and molybdate clusters, both water-free and microsolvated, in other words, each PT point along the vapor saturation curve would be characterized by a family of molecular clusters rather than a single species. Interestingly, at higher temperatures and water pressures, i.e. at 500 K and Psat > ~20 bars, our quantum chemical calculations appear to indicate that a stable network of surface water molecules would fully encapsulate tungstate and molybdate clusters. Further, we have also identified a group of highly stable magic-number type clusters in the sodium tungstate system that appear as characteristic discontinuities in the stepwise binding energy profiles, and would therefore be more likely to exist in natural ore vapor systems. In conclusion, these FT-MS and DFT results have important implications for the physical geochemistry of tungstate and molybdate species, because they exhibit a strong propensity for clustering and microsolvation in the gas-phase, in preparation for vapor transport and aggregation of W and Mo towards ore deposits.

17303014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303014.value: Thermochronology refers to determining or constraining the thermal history of a specific rock, mineral, or geologic unit using various dating techniques. Previously, the dating techniques have limits of minerals used and high closing temperatures (>90°C)/long history of thermal events. Luminescence and electron spin resonance (ESR) are two methods that have been used in low temperature thermochronology. Both methods share similar mechanisms and use quartz for measurements. This project will study the methodological aspects of thermochronology using ESR and Luminescence signals. The key problems are to determine the thermal kinetics involved in the trapped charges, and accurately measuring the parameters of the ESR and luminescence signals. The Tibetan plateau is the one of the most rapidly uplifting in recent earth history. The south-east part of the plateau provides ideal sites for the studies. Results from our initial pilot study indicate that luminescence is a promising method for fast and recent cooling/heating events. Uplift of the plateau has affected global climates and is a key factor in understanding global changes in recent geological history. This project will provide a direct measurement of uplift rates of the plateau. 热年代学是采用年代学方法测量矿物，岩石或某地质单元的热历史。以往的测年方法局限于高封闭温度，既长时间的热历史。释光和电子自旋共振（ESR）两种测年方法适用于低封闭温度的物质，而且测量的原理和材料（石英）相同。本计划研究这两种热年代学的实验方法。将集中研究石英释光和ESR信号的热力学特征。 青藏高原是地球上近来隆升最快的区域。其东南部为低温热年代学提供了理想的研究对象。初步研究表明，释光热年代学是研究低温热事件的一种可行且具有潜力方法。青藏高原的隆升是近代全球变化的重要特征，且与全球气候变化密切相关。本研究将直接测量高原的隆升速度。

17303014.label: Realisation of objectives
17303014.value: 1. To develop methods of thermochronology using ESR and luminescence signals from quartz New methodology of luminescence and ESR thermometers were developed. Quartz and feldspar were the minerals being investigated. For luminescence signals, thermoluminescence (TL) signals were studied. It is found that Isothermal thermoluminescence (ITL) and TL signals from quartz can be used as geothermal meters (1). A single aliquot regenerative dose protocol has been applied for ITL De determination (SAR-ITL). In the SAR- ITL protocol, the preheat condition was a cutheat to 10C higher than measurement temperature. The test dose was approximate to the expected De, and a 450 C heat was given at end of each cycle to minimize signal build-up. Based on signals strength and dose recovery test, temperatures of 235 and 255 C were selected for the ITL De measurement. A multiple aliquots regenerative protocol has been applied for TL De determination (MAR-TL). The preheat procedure was a cutheat of 235 C and a second glow TL of 175 Gy was used for normalization. The sensitivity change of first heating to 450 C was negligible, supported by comparison between additive and regenerative dose growth curves. Based on the natural TL signal and preheat condition studies, De values at temperatures of 250~330 C were used for thermochronological study. Luminescence signals from K- feldspar were studied. The signals from K-feldspar have provided multiple thermometers for thermo- chronological study (7). Protocols of multiple aliquot (MA) additive-dose (A) and regenerative-dose (R) have been applied and tested for equivalent dose (De) determinations using TL and ITL signals (MAA-TL, MAR-TL, MAA-ITL and MAR-ITL). Single aliquot regenerative-dose (SAR) protocol was only applied for De determination using ITL signals (SAR-ITL). A 50–60°C translation of heating temperature was necessary for the ITL De values to agree with TL De values. Based on the experimental results and merits-drawbacks comparison of the five tested protocols, the MAR-TL and SAR- ITL are favorable because of their efficiency and accuracy in De determinations. ESR signals from quartz grains were used for comparison studies with samples from sedimentary basins. It is found that the ESR and luminescence signals can reveal the thermal history of the samples in similar ways, though they have different closing temperatures and sensitive ranges of cooling rates. These two protocols were further applied to the samples from the Nujiang River valley and both explicitly demonstrated the thermal history of the samples. They are suitable for K-feldspar thermochronology study.. 2. To study trap parameters of the luminescence and ESR signals so that quantitative results can be obtained. We have studied the characteristics of trap parameters that luminescence signals used for thermochronological studies. It is found that quartz and K-feldspar TL and ITL signals can provide multiple measures for a rock sample with the same thermal history in geo-thermochronological studies. With different signals, they have different thermal stability and closing temperatures. They have the capacity to measure the thermal history of the samples with a closing temperature as low as 40 C. They can be applied to reveal the cooling history happened in recent half of million years. 3. To estimate the cooling rates of samples from sections in south-east Tibetan plateau, and their implications for the incision rates, and uplift and denudation history The protocols developed in this study were applied to rock samples collected at different elevations from Nujiang River (also called Salween River) valley slope. The results clearly demonstrate the differences in the thermal histories between the analyzed samples. It is revealed that the Nujiang River was cut through the rocks in a rapid and accelerated process. It happened as young as the last 100 thousand years. Particularly, the cooling/denudation rate is tremendously fast during last 30 thousand years. We have applied the luminescence protocols and ESR protocol to samples from borehole of Fergusons Hill, Otway Basin, Australia for comparisons. The samples were stored over the last few million years at stable thermal steady state conditions, thus providing a natural annealing experiment. TL signals from separated quartz were studied as geothermometers with a newly developed measurement protocol (1). The results have demonstrated that the apparent TL ages reflected the thermal history of the samples. At least four thermometers can be obtained from one set of TL data of a sample. Which have different ‘closing’ temperatures (53~85°C), but the same thermal history. The thermal gradient in Otway Basin can be perfectly predicted from the TL results.

17303014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303014.value: Several thermal meters can be used from different luminescence and ESR signals from either quartz and/or K-feldspar minerals from one rock sample. These signals have different closing temperatures and applied ages/cooling rates, because of different trap parameters associated with the signals. The closing temperatures of luminescence signals are in range of 50-80C. It can be as low as 40C with particular cases. Such low temperatures cannot be achieved with other radiometric methods. They are particularly suitable for rapid cooling/denudateion during the most recent earth history. The results/ages of luminescence thermometers can be influenced by several environmental factors, because of low closing temperatures. They include: recent thermal events, signal saturation, change in dose rate, fluctuations of ambient temperature, and changes in environmental dose rate. The thermometers should be tested with stable thermal conditions before applying to complicated geological systems. A closed stable sedimentary basin may be used for testing. The Nujiang River valley was cut through the rocks by the river in a rapid and accelerated process. It happened as young as the last 100 thousand years. Particularly, the cooling/denudation rate is tremendously fast during last 30 thousand years. Such a rapid and recent process is a result of both fast uplifting of Tibetan plateau and large amount of water in the river. Glaciers formed during the last glacial maximum may also play a role in the process.

17303014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303014.value: It would be very useful to test the protocols and methodologies to some rocks with knowing thermal history. In particular, applying to samples from boreholes in stable sedimentary basins would further prove the parameters of traps used in the thermometers. The protocols developed in this study can be applied to the areas in Tibetan plateau. It would be faviour to be used in the Three River Region adjacent to Nujiang River, so that the cooling/denudation history of the region can be revealed.

17303014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303014.value: Methodology and protocols were developed for studying the uplifting/cutting rate in the most recent history of the Earth. It is found that the methods can be applied to the evolution of geomorphology in the recent 500 thousand years, which cannot be achieved by other radiometric methods. We have applied to samples from Nujiang River valley. Results revealed that the uplifting of Tibetan plateau/cutting by the river could happen as young as 30 thousand years, associated with glacial formed during the last cool phase of the Earth climate.

17303114.label: Project Objectives
17303114.value: Aim 1: To identify enzymes that ‘erase’ lysine crotonylation ‘marks’ on histones. To understand functional roles of histone crotonylation, it is critical to identify its regulating enzymes. Here we aim to profile histone deacetylases in human cells. We will first focus on a newly discovered crotonylation ‘mark’ on histone H3 lysine-4 (H3K4Cr). In preliminary studies, we developed a photo-cross-linkable peptide probe to capture proteins that recognize H3K4Cr. When coupled with our published chemical proteomics approach(15-17), we identified 3 protein candidates that preferentially bind to H3K4Cr. In ongoing work, we have found that one of the candidates, Sirt3, can efficiently remove crotonyl group from H3K4Cr peptide. We will examine if the other two candidates also have decrotonylase activity. In addition, to minimize the potential bias that may arise from the substrate sequence preference of decrotonylases, we will identify decrotonylases using peptide probes based on other histone crotonylation sites, such as crotonylated histone H2B at lysine-5 (H2BK5Cr) and H4 at lysine-8 (H4K8Cr). Aim 2: To analyze how histone crotonylation is regulated by histone decrotonylases. We will combine biochemical, structural, cell biology and proteomics approaches to characterize the identified histone decrotonylases in vitro and in cells. Specifically, this Aim includes the following three sub-Aims: (a) To characterize enzymatic properties of histone decrotonylases. We will examine the enzyme activity and kinetics of the identified decrotonylases toward a variety of synthetic crotonylated peptides and histones extracted from cells. (b) To reveal the structural basis for histone decrotonylases. In ongoing works, we have solved the crystal structure of human Sirt3 in complex with an H3K4Cr peptide. We will study the effect of the key residues within the binding site on substrate recognition and enzyme activity. In addition, we will examine the mechanism of Sirt3-catalyzed decrotonylation by trapping the reaction intermediates in crystal structures. (c) To identify endogenous substrates of histone decrotonylases. In ongoing work, we have found that Sirt3 can catalyze histone decrotonylation in cells. We will combine gene knockdown techniques (e.g., RNAi) and proteomics approaches to identify histone crotonylation sites targeted by specific histone decrotonylases.

17303114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303114.value: In the nuclei of all eukaryotic cells, genomic DNA is highly compacted into chromatin by wrapping around ‘spools’, which are comprised of histone proteins. Diverse posttranslational modifications (e.g., acetylation, methylation and phosphorylation) of histones are known to regulate a variety of fundamental cellular processes, such as gene transcription, DNA replication and DNA damage repair. As a result, errors in cellular control of these histone PTMs are often associated with human diseases such as cancer. Therefore, it is important to understand how a histone PTM is regulated in cells. Lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a covalent modification at lysine side chains by a crotonyl group, is a newly discovered histone PTM. Kcr has been found to specifically localize at active gene promoters and potential enhancers in mammalian cell genomes. However, enzymes that regulate the addition and removal of Kcr are unknown, which has hindered further investigation of its cellular mechanisms and functions. To fill this knowledge gap, the proposed research aims at developing chemical proteomics approaches to profile histone decrotonylases (i.e., enzymes that catalyze removal of crotonyl groups from histone lysine residues) in human cells and combining biochemical, structural and proteomics methods to characterize how histone Kcr is regulated by these enzymes in vitro and in cells. The completion of these studies will open new opportunities for further investigation of cellular mechanisms and functions of histone Kcr and provide critical information to help dissect its regulatory networks in chromatin biology.

17303114.label: Realisation of objectives
17303114.value: Objective 1: To identify enzymes that ‘erase’ lysine crotonylation ‘marks’ on histones. In our preliminary study, we used our previously developed chemical proteomics approach to comprehensively profile histone decrotonylases at whole cell proteome level and identified Sirt3 poses decrotonylase activity toward a histone H3K4cr peptide in vitro. In this project, to identify enzymes that 'eraser' other Kcr marks, we design and synthesized photoaffinity probes derived from H3K9cr and H3K27cr peptides. Similar strategies were applied to profile potential 'erasers' of these two Kcr marks. The enriched proteins were examined by LC-MS/MS. The identified proteins were analyzed and varified for the interaction with Kcr marks. To facilitate the identification and characterization of histone PTMs-mediated protein-protein interactions, we developed a new lysine-based photo-reactive amino acid, termed photo-lysine. We demonstrate that photo-lysine, which is readily incorporated into proteins by native mammalian translation machinery, can be used to capture and identify proteins that recognize lysine PTMs, including ‘readers’ and ‘erasers’ of histone modifications. Based on these results, we further developed crotonyl photo-lysine (photo-Kcr) in collaboration with Chen Lab in PKU and adopted the amber suppression-mediated unnatural amino acid incorporation to site-specifically incorporate into multiple histone lysine sites. We demonstrated that the photo-Kcr can be site-specifically incoporated into GFP and multiple histone lysine sites. Using a histone H3 protein carrying a photo-Kcr at Lys79 site, we also demonstrated that the known eraser (i.e., Sirt3) can remove the crotonylation mark. More importantly, we showed that Sirt3 can be captured by this photo-Kcr containing histone H3. This results demonstrated the ability of photo-Kcr to identified unknown Kcr 'erasers' in situ. Objective 2: To analyze how histone crotonylation is regulated by histone decrotonylases. In our preliminary study, we identified Sirt3 as a decrotonylase in vitro. The co-crystal structure of Sirt3 in complex with a H3K4cr peptide was also obained, revealing a unique pi-pi stacking interaction between the carbon-carbon double bond of crotonyl group and the phenyl ring of Sirt3 Phe180 residue. In this project, we first sought out to determine if the decrotonylation activity of Sirt3 follows its deacetylation activity. To this end, the enzymatic reactions were monitored by LC-MS and the presumed decrotonylation product (i.e., O-Cr-ADPR) could be detected. At the same time, samples without adding the co-factor NAD or using a catalytically inactive Sirt3 H248Y mutant were also prepared and analyzed. The results indicated that Sirt3 catalyzes the hydrolysis of crotonyl group by following a similar mechanism as its deacetylation. To test the site selectivity of the Sirt3-catalyzed decrotonylation, we synthesized other crotonylated histone peptides, including H3K9cr, H3K27cr, H2AK36cr, H2BK5cr, and H4K8cr to see if Sirt3 can remove the crotonylation marks. LC-MS analyses indicated that Sirt3 posed certain site selectivity when removes Kcr marks. To further examine the importance of this conserved phenylalanine, Phe180 of Sirt3 was mutated to a leucine residue (F180L) to remove an aromatic ring as a pi donor but retain similar hydrophobicity. The kinetic studies on Sirt3 F180L mutant showed 40-fold lower catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km=21 s^−1 M^−1) for the hydrolysis of the H3K4Cr peptide compared with wild-type Sirt3, while the deacetylation activity only had a two-fold decrease, demonstrating a critical role of the phenylalanine-mediated pi-pi interaction in the decrotonylation activity of the enzyme. Inspired by the fact that the phenylalanine residue is conserved in Sirt1, Sirt2 and Sirt3 ,we next sought to investigat the decrotonylation activity of Sirt1 and Sirt2, which also showed high binding affinity with H3K4Cr probe in our proteomics experiments. We performed ITC experiment to detect the direct binding affinity of Sirt1 and Sirt2 toward H3K4Cr peptides. The data showed that, while Sirt2 weakly bound to H3K4Cr peptide, the binding affinity of Sirt1 towards H3K4Cr was undetectable. However, by LC-MS-based enzymatic assay, we found that Sirt1 and Sirt2 could also catalyze the hydrolysis of the H3K4Cr peptide, although they were relatively weaker binder towards substrate. Sirt5 and Sirt6, which lack the phenylalanine residue, failed to catalyze the removal of Kcr marks. To examine whether Sirt1-Sirt3 regulate histone lysine crotonylation in living cells, we knockdown Sirt1-3 in HeLa cells using siRNA. We found that only Sirt3 knockdown cause dramatic increase of crotonylation level, and this increase seemed only happen on histone proteins while not on other proteins. Although Sirt1 and Sirt2 can decrotonylate histone peptides and proteins in vitro, their knockdowns by siRNA failed to cause an appreciable increase in crotonylation levels for both the global histone and the two tested Kcr, H3K4cr and H3K27cr. In contrast, Sirt3 knockdown caused accumulation of both global histone crotonylation and the H3K4Cr mark, suggesting Sirt3 may act as main decrotonylase in cells. More importantly, chromatin precipitation (ChIP) coupled with quantitative PCR (qPCR) experiments showed that Sirt3 knockdown resulted in significant increases in Kcr levels of five of the seven known Sirt3 target genes analyzed, indicating that Sirt3 may directly regulate crotonylation dynamics at the genomic loci where it binds. In addition, mRNA levels of the three candidate genes with increased Kcr levels, Ptk2, Tshz3, and Wapal, were also significantly upregulated upon Sirt3 knockdown, suggesting that Sirt3 might relieve a repressive effect on these target genes through ‘erasing’ histone Kcr ‘marks’.

17303114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303114.value: To understand the biological consequence of a histone posttranslational modification (PTM), it is required to identify the regulating-enzymes that catalyze the addition and removal of this modification. Histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is a newly identified histone PTM whose regulatory mechanisms and biological functions remain largely unclear. To fill this knowledge gap, in our preliminary study, we identified Sirt3, a well-known deacetylase, as a decrotonylase in vitro. The crystal structure of Sirt3 in complex with a H3K4cr peptide was also resolved to show that the carbon-carbon double bond of crotonyl group forms a pi-pi interaction with the phenyl ring of Sirt3 Phe180. In this project, we demonstrated that the Sirt3 catalyzes the hydrolysis of crotonyl group by following a similar mechanism as its deacetylation. Sirt3 posed varied decrotonylation activity toward histone Kcr peptides other than H3K4cr, suggesting that Sirt3 showed certain site selectivity when removes Kcr marks. Kinetic study revealed that the activity of Sirt3 to remove acetyl groups from lysine residues are 5-8 times higher than that for the removal of crotonyl groups. A F180L mutation, which maintains the size and hydrophobicity of the residue but eliminates the pi system, reduced the decrotonylase activity of about 40-fold compared with the wild-type Sirt3, while the deacetylase activity showed only a two-fold decrease, indicating the importance of the pi-pi interaction for the decrotonylase activity of Sirt3. We further demonstrated that that endogenous Sirt3 can function as an ‘eraser’ enzyme to regulate histone crotonylation dynamics in cells. Through the decrotnylase activity, Sirt3 might relieve a repressive effect on its target genes (Bao et al. Elife. 2014,3. DOI: 10.7554/eLife.02999). To facilitate the identification of histone PTMs-meidated protein-protein interactions in live cells, we developed a lysine-based photo-reactive amino acid, photo-Lys, which can be incorporated into proteins by native translation machinary (Yang et al., Nat Chem Biol. 2016, 12, 70-72). In collaboration with Chen Lab in PKU, we further developed crotonylated photo-Lys (photo-Kcr) and used amber suppression-mediated unnatural amino acid incorporation to site-specifically incorporate into multiple histone lysine sites. Photo-cross-linking experiment using a photo-Kcr containing H3 at K79 position robustly captured endogenous Sirt3 from cell lysates, demonstrating its potential to identify unknown Kcr 'eraser' in situ (Xie et al. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2017, 139, 6522-6525).

17303114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303114.value: In our current study, we comprehensively profiled the enzymes that remove histone Kcr marks. Together with the identification of Kcr 'erasers', we further identified proteins that tightly and specifically recognize these histone marks that are not likely to catalyze the removal of the Kcr marks, suggesting these proteins could be potential effector proteins ('readers') that bind to the Kcr to signal the downstream cellular events. These 'reader' candidate will be further characterized. In our current study, we characterized the decrotonylase activity of Sirt3 and discovered that Sirt3 can participate in the regulation of gene expression through its decrotonylase activity in cells. It is interesting to further determine the functions of histone Kcr in gene regulation in different model systems (e.g., stem cells), and how the levels of histone Kcr marks are controlled by the regulating enzymes to realize its functions in gene regulation. The above questions will be explored in our further studies. In fact, we have already applied for fundings (as PI and Co-I) to support our continuous studies, including Regulation and Function of Novel Histone Modifications (CRF C7029-15G), Chemical Biology Approach to Molecular Medicine (AoE/P-705/16), Chemical Tools for Identification and Interrogation of ‘Readers’ of Histone Crotonylation (GRF 17126618).

17303114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303114.value: The eukaryotic DNA is compacted into cell nuclei by wrapping around histone proteins. Besides serving as the structural scaffold for DNA packing, histone proteins play essential roles in a variety of fundamental cellular events, such as gene expression, DNA replication and damage repair. Posttranslational modifications (PTMs) of histones is one of the mechanisms that underlie the regulation of these above-mentioned processes. Histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is one of the newly identified PTMs, whose regulatory mechanisms and biological functions remain poorly understood. In this project, we use multidisciplinary approaches to identify the enzymes that remove the Kcr marks, characterize how and how active the enzymes remove the Kcr marks, and investigate the biological functions/consequences of the removal of the Kcr marks by the enzymes. Our results greatly advance our knowledge on histone Kcr and its regulating enzymes. Moreover, the information may help the development of potential therapeutic strategies for the treatment of human diseases associated with the abnormalities in the regulation of histone Kcr.

17303414.label: Project Objectives
17303414.value: Star Formation I: Studies of star formation in NGC 1275 is complicated by the presence of a foreground infalling galaxy known as the HVS. We plan to make a complete catalog and study the physical properties of all the star clusters towards NGC 1275 and the HVS from archival data taken with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST). We have shown that the bluer star clusters belonging to the HVS can be separated out from those belonging to NGC 1275 based on their projected locations against bright HII regions in the HVS as well as their different overall colour distributions. By separating out the star clusters belonging to NGC 1275, we plan to study the recent star-formation history in this galaxy. We also plan to study the recent star-formation history in the HVS. Star Formation II: To better understand the physical properties of the bluer star clusters, we plan to conduct spectroscopy of selected clusters. Star Formation III: We plan to make an [OIII] image of the optical emission-line nebula associated with NGC 1275 to pinpoint regions of recent/ongoing star formation, and to compare the relationship between these regions and molecular hydrogen gas as traced in CO.

17303614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303614.value: The Eocene-Oligocene Transition (EOT) around 33.7 million years ago (Ma) represents one of the best examples to study how natural climate change occurred in Earth’s history. During the EOT, the Earth entered from a greenhouse world, essentially ice-free, to an icehouse world that we humans live in today. With greenhouse gases anticipated to approach the Eocene level rapidly due to human activities, how the Earth’ climate, as well as the ocean chemistry and marine ecosystem, will respond to the greenhouse gas forcing, is thus a critical scientific question and has important societal values. Although the Eocene climate may not be an exact analog, studies of greenhouse warmer climates and how the transition from warm to glacial climates occurred, will definitely provide useful information for us humans to get prepared for future climate change. Our understanding of the EOT has indeed improved in the recent years due to intensive internationally-collaborated studies. Terrestrial and sea surface temperatures (SST) cooled substantially, especially at high latitudes, and Antarctica started to be glaciated. Atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) level dropped roughly in-phase. However, some outstanding issues still exist. Spatial coverage of the dataset is very limited and the chain of climatic events across the EOT remains largely unspecified. The recent Integrated Ocean Drilling Program Expedition 342 discovered a highly expanded EOT section, which, for the first time, provides the opportunity to further address the existing scientific issues. Taking advantage of being a shipboard scientist in this expedition, the PI proposes to reconstruct detailed SST and CO2 changes across the EOT. Detailed SST and CO2 records during the EOT between 36 and 32 Ma, aiming at orbital resolution of 5-10 kyr (thousand years), will be generated from Site U1411. Lower-resolution SST and CO2 records between 40 and 20 Ma, at ~50 kyr resolution, will be generated from Site U1404. Quantitative SST changes will be reconstructed using the primary proxy, alkenone unsaturation index (UK’37), with the supplement of the tetraether index (TEX86). CO2 reconstructions will be based on the standard alkenone compound-specific carbon isotope technique. Key issues we hope to address include: How warm it was during the late Eocene and how much of cooling occurred at this mid-latitude ocean? Can we resolve orbital changes in SST and CO2 changes across the critical EOT? Did CO2 levels indeed change in-phase with SST? The preliminary work shows great promise that major objectives can be successfully achieved. 精細重建始新世/漸新世氣候轉型期的海溫和大氣CO2變化 約33.7百萬年前的始新世/漸新世氣候轉型期是研究地球歷史時期的自然氣候變化的一個重要時期。在此轉型期，地球從基本上無冰的溫室氣體氣候進入到我們人類生活的冰室氣候。由於人類活動的影響，大氣溫室氣體濃度將很快達到始新世的水平，研究地球氣候，海洋化學及海洋生態系統怎樣對此響應是一個非常關鍵的科學問題並具有重要的社會價值。儘管始新世氣候系統不能作為將來氣候變化的直接類比，研究溫室暖期氣候及向冰期氣候的轉變將有助於我們人類為將來的氣候變化做出應對。 由於近年來大量的國際合作研究，我們對始新世/漸新世氣候轉型期的認識的確有了很大提高。我們已大概知道在轉型期，陸地和海表降溫明顯，特別在高緯度區域，冰蓋在南極洲開始形成，大氣CO2大致同時降低。然而，一些科學問題仍然存在，已有的記錄空間覆蓋不夠，在轉型期的氣候事件的反應鏈也大都不能確定。最近的國際海洋鑽探計劃（IODP）342航次在西北大西洋發現了高沉積速率的始新世/漸新世轉型期的沉積樣品。此沉積樣品第一次為研究解決現存的科學問題提供了可能性。 作為一員342航次的船上科學家，申請人想利用此機會提出精細重建始新世/漸新世氣候轉型期的海溫和大氣CO2變化。將從鑽孔1411柱重建32-36百萬年間，5-10千年分辨率的海表溫度和大氣CO2變化，並從1404柱重建20-40百萬年間，100千年較低分辨率的溫度和CO2記錄。定量的海表溫度變化將主要由生物標志物長鏈烯酮來實現，並輔以TEX86。大氣CO2的重建將基於標準的長鏈烯酮單分子碳同位素技術。我們希望此項目能回答以下關鍵問題：晚始新世時地球氣候有多暖和？中緯度海洋的降溫幅度有多大？我們能否重建轉型期時在軌道尺度上的海表溫度和大氣CO2的變化？大氣CO2變化是否和溫度變化同步？我們的初步工作顯示這些基本目標應該可以達到。

17303614.label: Realisation of objectives
17303614.value: For this project, we have performed various analyses on ~800 samples requested from IODP and achieved all the project objectives. Specifically, we have performed alkenone analyses on samples from IODP Site 1411 and 1404 to reconstruct sea surface temperature (SST) and atmospheric CO2 changes for this critical climatic interval, thus achieving the Objectives 1 and 2. Further, with data generated, we could assess how SST changed associated with atmospheric CO2, thus achieving Objective 3, and better define the latitudinal SST pattern across the Eocene-Oligocene Transition, thus achieving Objective 4. We have also trained postgraduate students in the field of paleoceanography/paleoclimatology, and one PhD student graduated during the project interval, who was mainly supported by this project.

17303614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303614.value: 1. Sea surface temperature changes in the mid-latitude North Atlantic largely followed global climatic changes between 43 and 18 million years ago. 2. One exception occurred at the Eocene-Oligocene Transition when sea surface temperature did not cool immediately associated with the Antarctic glaciation, displaying a transient hemispheric temperature asymmetry, which perhaps indicates the onset of early Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. 3. Detailed sea surface temperature record across the Eocene-Oligocene Transition suggests orbital modulation of temperature changes. 4. Atmospheric CO2 drop across the Eocene-Oligocene Transition was indeed in-phase or slightly lead temperature changes. 5. The group of tetraethers compounds (glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers or GDGT) have great potential to be used to reconstruct early Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Major findings 1 & 2 has been published in Nature Geoscience, and the rest of major findings are being written up, aiming at high impact journals. Another paper, partially supported by this project, has been published in Science Advances (See Part C).

17303614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303614.value: One of the big surprises from this project is that the originally proposed GDGT-based TEX86 cannot be used as a temperature proxy. Along with consistently "abnormal" values from other GDGT-based indices, this may reflect archaea community changes which is ultimately associated with ocean water column structure changes. Therefore, these GDGT indices, instead of being used for temperature reconstruction, have great potential to trace past water masses/ocean circulation changes. Inspired by this new finding, we have proposed to use GDGT indices to trace ocean water column structure changes during another warm period, the Middle Miocene Climatic Optimum between 14 and 17 million years ago, which has been funded by RGC in 2018/2019 round. For the critical Eocene-Oligocene Transition, with the new data generated from this project that now well constrains detailed structure of temperature changes in Northern Hemisphere, it is time to generate a comparable high-resolution temperature record from Southern Hemisphere, in order to better define the hemispheric temperature asymmetry, especially for the time interval right before the transition. This could be developed as a future proposal/project.

17303714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303714.value: In some materials, electron’s spin (or more generally pseudo-spin) is locked to its momentum, and energy bands near the Fermi surface are strongly coupled. In these materials, electrons can be described properly by the Dirac equation, a relativistic quantum description for spin 1/2 particles, and therefore called Dirac fermions. The transport of Dirac fermions is distinct from conventional electron gases in many aspects. For example, the spin-momentum locking gives rise to a nontrivial Berry phase, which can drastically modulate the transport, leading to the absence of backscattering, weak anti-localization, and absence of Anderson localization. The project is to theoretically explore the transport of Dirac fermions and its applications to electronic transport of emergent materials, such as graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides, silicene, topological band, Kondo, and crystalline insulators. One of well known Dirac systems is graphene (Nobel Prize of Physics in 2010), which is described as four cones of 2D massless Dirac fermions, located at two inequivalent corners of Brillouin zone (known as valleys). The topological insulators, which are currently under extensive investigations, have single-valley surface states that can be regarded as one quarter of graphene. Recently, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides became experimentally accessible, they looks like massive graphene but with opposite Zeeman splitting for valence bands at different valleys. More recently, the topological Kondo and crystalline insulators have been experimentally confirmed. Many predicted Dirac systems are yet to be realized in transport setups, such as Weyl semimetals and silicene. In these materials, transport is subject to electron scattering, quantum interference, interactions, and dimension, bringing a lot of theoretical interest in the quantum diffusive transport of Dirac fermions under impurities and interactions. The project will formulate the electronic transport in these emergent materials as the transport of Dirac fermions, focusing on the topics such as: the roles of electron-electron interaction and impurity in the quantum correction and fluctuation of conductivity, intervalley and intravalley scattering in multi-valley massive Dirac systems, the quantum transport of quasiparticles in topological Kondo and crystalline insulators. The study will be applied to the experiments of relevant materials and facilitate collaboration with experimental activities. 在一些材料中，電子的自旋（或者是類似自旋的自由度）和它們的動量鎖定，並且費米面附近的能帶強耦合在一起。在這些材料中，電子可以用狄拉克方程等效描述。狄拉克方程是狹義相對論量子力學對自旋1/2粒子的描述。因此，我們稱這些材料中的準粒子為狄拉克費米子。在許多方面，狄拉克費米子的輸運和一般電子有所不同。比如，自旋動量鎖定會產生一個非平庸的Berry相位，從而改變輸運性質，導致沒有背散射，弱反局域化和安德森局域化的消失。本研究計劃是為了理論研究狄拉克費米子的輸運并將其應用于新型材料中，如單層石墨烯，過渡金屬氧化物，單層硅，拓撲能帶絕緣體，拓撲近藤絕緣體，拓撲晶態絕緣體等。 一個眾所周知的狄拉克系統是單層石墨烯（2010年諾貝爾物理學獎），它可以被描述為四個二維無質量的狄拉克費米子構成的狄拉克錐，分佈于布里淵區兩個不等價的角落（或稱為能谷）。目前被广泛研究的拓撲絕緣體的表面态可以被看成四分之一個石墨烯。最近，實驗上實現了單層過渡金屬硫族化合物，它們的能帶看著如同有質量的石墨烯，且在不同的能谷的價帶具有自旋相反的賽曼劈裂。更近一段時間，拓撲近藤絕緣體和拓撲晶態絕緣體也被實驗所實現。許多被理論預言的狄拉克系統也有待實驗實現，比如Weyl半金屬或者單層硅。在這些材料中，電輸運受制于量子干涉，相互作用和維度的影響，引發了許多興趣來理論研究狄拉克費米子在雜質散射和相互作用下的量子輸運。 本計劃將會著眼于表征這些新型材料中的狄拉克粒子的電輸運，集中研究比如：電子相互作用和雜質散射在電導的修正和關聯中的作用；有質量多能谷狄拉克系統中的谷內和谷間散射；拓撲近藤絕緣體和拓撲晶態絕緣體的準粒子輸運。本研究將被應用于相關材料以於促進相關實驗的發展。

17303714.label: Realisation of objectives
17303714.value: The project was aimed to formulate the electronic transport in the emergent materials such as the 2D materials and topological materials. Three objectives are (1) To explore the transport properties of Dirac fermions in emergent materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides and silicene, topological band, Kondo, and crystalline insulators, focusing on the conductivity corrections from the quantum interference and electron-electron interaction, the magnetic field and temperature dependence, impurities of different symmetries and acting ranges. (2) To distinguish the material-dependent transport properties between these emergent Dirac systems, such as differences in dimension, mass, and lattice symmetry. (3) To describe and predict new phenomena in transport experiments. Over the past few years PI and his collaborators have studied the quantum transport in the two-dimensionla materials and topological materials. We developed theory of quantum transport and obtained a useful formula for magnetoconductivity, and collaborated with experimental groups to understand the observed phenomena in transport. We have published 8 papers relevant to the present project, including 1 in Physical Review Letters, 3 in Physical Review B, 2 in Nature Communications, 1 in New Journal of Physics, and 1 in Chinese Physics B. All the three objectives have been fully achieved. In the following, PI summarize the main achievements of the present project. Weak antilocalization and localization in disordered and interacting Weyl semimetals [Phys. Rev. B 92, 035203 (2015)] Using the Feynman diagram techniques, we derive the finite-temperature conductivity and magnetoconductivity formulas from the quantum interference and electron-electron interaction, for a three-dimensional disorderedWeyl semimetal. For a single valley of Weyl fermions, we find that the magnetoconductivity is negative and proportional to the square root of magnetic field at low temperatures, as a result of the weak antilocalization. By including the contributions from the weak antilocalization, Berry curvature correction, and Lorentz force, we compare the calculated magnetoconductivity with a recent experiment. The weak antilocalization always dominates the magnetoconductivity near zero field, thus gives one of the transport signatures for Weyl semimetals. In the presence of strong intervalley scattering and correlations, we expect a crossover from the weak antilocalization to weak localization. In addition, we find that the interplay of electron-electron interaction and disorder scattering always dominates the conductivity at low temperatures and leads to a tendency to localization. Finally, we present a systematic comparison of the transport properties of single-valley Weyl fermions, 2D massless Dirac fermions, and 3D conventional electrons. High-field magnetoconductivity of topological semimetals with short-range potential [Phys. Rev. B 92, 045203] Weyl semimetals are three-dimensional topological states of matter, in a sense that they host paired monopoles and antimonopoles of Berry curvature in momentum space, leading to the chiral anomaly. The chiral anomaly has long been believed to give a positive magnetoconductivity or negative magnetoresistivity in strong and parallel fields. However, several recent experiments on both Weyl and Dirac topological semimetals show a negative magnetoconductivity in high fields. Here, we study the magnetoconductivity of Weyl and Dirac semimetals in the presence of short-range scattering potentials. In a strong magnetic field applied along the direction that connects two Weyl nodes, we find that the conductivity along the field direction is determined by the Fermi velocity, instead of by the Landau degeneracy. We identify three scenarios in which the high-field magnetoconductivity is negative. Our findings show that the high-field positive magnetoconductivity may not be a compelling signature of the chiral anomaly and will be helpful for interpreting the inconsistency in the recent experiments and earlier theories. Detecting monopole charge in Weyl semimetals via quantum interference transport [Phys. Rev. B 93, 161110(R)(2016)] Topological Weyl semimetals can host Weyl nodes with monopole charges in momentum space. How to detect the signature of the monopole charges in quantum transport remains a challenging topic. Here, we reveal the connection between the parity of monopole charge in topological semimetals and the quantum interference corrections to the conductivity. We show that the parity of monopole charge determines the sign of the quantum interference correction, with odd and even parity yielding the weak antilocalization and weak localization effects, respectively. This is attributed to the Berry phase difference between time-reversed trajectories circulating the Fermi sphere that encloses the monopole charges. From standard Feynman diagram calculations, we further show that the weak-field magnetoconductivity at low temperatures is proportional to + √B in double-Weyl semimetals and − √B in single-Weyl semimetals, respectively, which could be verified experimentally Anomalous Phase Shift of Quantum Oscillations in 3D Topological Semimetals (Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 077201(2016)) Berry phase physics is closely related to a number of topological states of matter. Recently discovered topological semimetals are believed to host a nontrivial π Berry phase to induce a phase shift of 1=8 in the quantum oscillation (þ for hole and − for electron carriers). We theoretically study the Shubnikov–de Haas oscillation of Weyl and Dirac semimetals, taking into account their topological nature and inter-Landau band scattering. For a Weyl semimetal with broken time-reversal symmetry, the phase shift is found to change nonmonotonically and go beyond known values of 1/8 and 5/8, as a function of the Fermi energy. For a Dirac semimetal or paramagnetic Weyl semimetal, time-reversal symmetry leads to a discrete phase shift of 1/8 or 5/8. Different from the previous works, we find that the topological band inversion can lead to beating patterns in the absence of Zeeman splitting. We also find the resistivity peaks should be assigned integers in the Landau index plot. Our findings may account for recent experiments in Cd2As3 and should be helpful for exploring the Berry phase in various 3D systems. Negative magnetoresistance in Dirac semimetal Cd3As2 [Nat. Communi. 7, 10301 (2016)] A large negative magnetoresistance (NMR) is anticipated in topological semimetals in parallel magnetic fields, demonstrating the chiral anomaly, a long-sought high-energy-physics effect, in solid-state systems. Recent experiments reveal that the Dirac semimetal Cd3As2 has the record-high mobility and positive linear magnetoresistance in perpendicular magnetic fields. However, the NMR has not yet been unveiled. Here we report the observation of NMR in Cd3As2 microribbons in parallel magnetic fields up to 66% at 50 K and visible at room temperatures. The NMR is sensitive to the angle between magnetic and electrical fields, robust against temperature and dependent on the carrier density. The large NMR results from low carrier densities in our Cd3As2 samples, ranging from 3.0 1017 cm 3 at 300 K to 2.2 1016 cm 3 below 50 K. We therefore attribute the observed NMR to the chiral anomaly. In perpendicular magnetic fields, a positive linear magnetoresistance up to 1,670% at 14 Tand 2 K is also observed.
