17402814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17402814.value: The benefits of writing practice on reading development have been consistently reported; nevertheless, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Recent research in my lab showed that Chinese character acquisition is characterized by an inverted-U shape pattern in visual processing: an increase in holistic processing in beginning readers without much writing experience, followed by a decrease in holistic processing after the acquisition of writing skills. This observation is consistent with the literature on face and object recognition: visual discrimination training increases holistic processing of the stimuli. In addition, our research showed that subsequent writing practice enhances analytic processing, which may further facilitate reading. Consistent with this finding, artists with face drawing experience show reduced holistic processing in face perception as compared with non-drawers. In computer vision research, the fusion of component-based (analytic) and holistic approaches yields the best face recognition performance. All these findings suggest that writing/drawing experience may enhance analytic processing ability, and the ability to engage both holistic and analytic processing may be essential for mastering visual recognition. In this proposed project we first test this hypothesis through examining how face drawing experience influences face perception and whether it can enhance face recognition ability particularly in tasks that require engagement of local/analytic processing, such as judging whether two face images taken under different conditions are of the same person. We also examine whether face artists show more analytic eye movement patterns in face recognition than non-drawers to understand whether they differ in information extraction from stimuli, and what information is important for expert face processing. We then investigate whether explicit instructions on constituent structure recognition have similar effects to writing/drawing by training non-Chinese speaking children to read Chinese characters, and non-drawers to recognize unfamiliar faces. These examinations have very important real-life applications such as security surveillance and improving computers’ and humans’ face/character recognition performance. In addition, we aim to examine the brain mechanism underlying face drawing and Chinese character writing expertise through EEG experiments. The engagement of analytic processing may be related to how the two hemispheres are recruited, since hemispheric asymmetry in the perception of local/global features has been consistently observed. This examination will also help us understand how brain regions are recruited for supporting different cognitive processes. This research will contribute to our understanding of the cognitive and brain mechanism underlying visual expertise acquisition. It has important educational implications for how to facilitate visual expertise acquisition and promotes understanding of learning disabilities. 書寫練習對閱讀發展的幫助已被廣泛報導，但其詳細的作用機制仍未知。近年來我們的研究發現中文字的視覺認知發展承現Ｕ字形：一開始無書寫練習之前是透過整體處理，之後透過書寫練習可發展分析處理能力。這個發現與在臉孔以及物體識別的發現相似。另外，我們的研究發現分析處理能力也可進一步增進閱讀能力。其他相似的研究也發現有繪畫臉孔經驗的藝術家比一般人有更好的分析處理能力。在電腦視覺研究中發現，表現最好的臉孔辨別程式通常會結合分析與整理處理的訊息。 這些研究結果顯示，書寫/繪圖的經驗可能可以提高分析處理能力， 而有同時從事整體和分析處理的能力是掌握專業視覺識別必不可少的。 在此提出的研究項目中，我們首先通過研究繪圖經驗如何影響面孔識別以及是否能增進面孔識別能力（尤其在一些需要同時做整體與分析處理的任務中，像是判定在不同情況下兩個臉圖像是否是同一人的 ）來檢驗這一個假設。 我們還檢驗臉孔繪畫的藝術家是否比一般人在識別人臉時表現出更多分析性的眼球運動，以了解他們是否有不同信息提取方式，和什麼樣的信息對專業臉孔識別是重要的。然後，我們研究是否在培訓非華語學生讀中文字上，明確教導他們中文字的組成結構與透過寫作/繪圖訓練有類似的效果 。這些研究具有十分重要的現實生活中的應用，如安全監控設備和改善電腦對人臉/文字識別的性能。 此外，我們也會透過腦電圖實驗來了解繪畫與中文字書寫專業能力的大腦機制。 分析處理能力可能涉及到兩個大腦半球如何相互合作，因為研究發現大腦兩半球在局部/全局知覺處理上有不對稱性。這種研究也將幫助我們了解不同的大腦區域如何分工處理不同的認知過程。 這項研究將有助於我們對視覺專業辨識與其底層認知和腦機制的理解。其也有重要的教育意義以及能增進我們對學習障礙的理解。

17402814.label: Realisation of objectives
17402814.value: Objective 1: To examine how face drawing experience influences face perception and whether it can enhance face recognition ability through behavioral experiments. We conducted two experiments to address this objective. In the first experiment, we examined whether face drawing artists and novices/non-drawers differ in holistic face processing as measured in the composite paradigm, left side bias in face perception, and face matching performance. We found that artists outperformed novices in face matching, and had reduced holistic face processing and left side bias in face perception as compared with novices. In addition, participants’ drawing rating was positively correlated with face matching performance and negatively correlated with the left side bias effect, suggesting that these effects were related to their drawing expertise. This result was consistent with our hypothesis that face-drawing experience enhances engagement of local attention. In the second experiment, we examined whether face drawing experts and novices differed in face recognition and face matching performance, and holistic face processing as measured by the part-whole paradigm. We replicated the finding that face artists outperformed novices in face matching performance. However, they did not perform better than novices in face recognition, and did not differ from novices in holistic face processing as measured in the part-whole paradigm. This result suggested that face artists’ advantage in face processing may be limited to tasks similar to their drawing experience such as face matching or the composite paradigm. Objective 2: To understand face drawing experts’ eye movements in face recognition, as compared with ordinary observers’, with Hidden Markov Models We conducted two experiments to address this objective. In the first experiment, we examined how global and local attention priming using hierarchical patterns could influence participants’ eye movement patterns in face recognition. Through Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models (EMHMM) approach, we found that local attention priming significantly increased the similarity of participants’ eye movements to an eyes-focused eye movement pattern, whereas global attention priming did not modulate participants’ eye movement patterns. In addition, participants had better recognition performance after local priming than global priming, suggesting an advantage of eyes-focused patterns in face recognition. These results were consistent with our hypothesis that eyes-focused eye movement patterns are associated with the engagement of local attention/featural-based processing, which may consequently enhance participants’ face recognition performance. In the second experiment, we examined whether face artists and novices differed in eye movement patterns during face matching, face recognition, and the part-whole face judgment task, and whether their eye movement patterns were related to performance. We found that face artists adopted a more eyes-focused eye movement pattern and outperformed novices in simultaneous face matching, and participants’ drawing rating was correlated with both eye movement pattern and performance. In contrast, face artists and novices did not differ in either eye movement pattern or performance in face recognition or the part-whole task. Interestingly, in both face matching and face recognition, we observed an inverted-U shaped relationship between eye movement pattern and performance, where the best performance was observed for eye movement patterns that were in between eyes-focused and nose-focused strategies. These results suggest that the optimal face processing performance involves a combination of local and global information processing; however the expertise in such combination of information processing may be task-specific. Objective 3: To examine neural correlates and temporal dynamics of face drawing/character writing experts’ perception of faces/characters through EEG/ERP examinations To address objective 3, we conducted an EEG study to examine the neural correlates of the modulation of different learning methods on artificial character recognition. We trained participants to recognize and read artificial characters through either whole-word approach, grapheme-to-phoneme approach, or whole-word approach with writing practice. Interestingly, we found a significant moderation effect of learning method on the relationship between holistic processing and N170 amplitude in the right hemisphere: a positive correlation was observed when learning to recognize artificial characters using the whole-word approach, whereas a negative correlation was observed when the grapheme-to-phoneme mapping approach was used. This result was consistent with our previous computational modeling study, which showed that holistic processing is positively correlated with right hemisphere lateralization when the recognition task depends on configural information (i.e., exact distances between components/features), and negatively correlated with right hemisphere lateralization when the recognition relies on featural information. Thus, our results suggest that whether the learning method for visual object recognition emphasizes on configural or featural information processing modulates how visual objects are perceived and processed during learning. It also suggested that writing practice may not be necessary for developing decreased holistic processing and increased right hemisphere lateralization observed in Chinese expert character processing, as the grapheme-to-phoneme mapping approach led to similar effects. Objective 4: To investigate whether writing/drawing practice is necessary for visual expertise acquisition and whether similar facilitation effects in visual recognition can be obtained through explicit recognition practice on the constituent structures We conducted two studies to address objective 4. In the first study, we examined the effects of writing/copying training and component reconstruction training on Chinese character recognition. We recruited non-Chinese speaking students as the participants, and found that while both types of training increased holistic character processing for beginners, only component reconstruction training significantly enhanced orthographic awareness. This result suggested that increased holistic processing may be the behavioral marker for an early stage of learning to read Chinese characters regardless of learning experience. This finding was consistent with our previous finding that suggested an inverted-U shape curve of holistic processing in learning to read Chinese characters: an increase in holistic processing initially, followed by a decrease in holistic processing due to writing experience. However, we suspect that our training session may not be long enough to allow us to see the effect of reduced holistic processing due to writing experience at a later stage. In the second study, we recruited adult participants and examined whether a short one-hour drawing training could enhance their face recognition performance or change their eye movement patterns. The results showed that short-term drawing training was not sufficient to induce either eye movement pattern or performance differences in face recognition.

17402814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17402814.value: Here we found that in both face recognition memory and simultaneous face matching tasks, the best performance was observed when participants’ eye movement patterns involved a mixture of eyes-focused and nose-focused strategies (e.g., Chuk, et al., 2017; Chan et al., 2018). This result suggests that a combination of local and global information processing is optimal in visual object recognition. We also found that face drawing experience may be particularly relevant to the enhancement of local information processing of faces, as demonstrated in face drawing artists’ reduced holistic face processing, reduced left side bias/right hemisphere lateralization in face perception (Conference [1]), and a more eyes-focused eye movement pattern in simultaneous face matching (using EMHMM; Conference [14]) as compared with novices. However, face drawing artists’ advantage in face processing was only found in the simultaneous face matching task, but not in the face recognition tasks. Together these results suggest that face drawing artists may have a better ability to engage local face processing in addition to global face processing in face perception; however, this ability may be limited to tasks similar to their face drawing experiences, such as in simultaneous face matching. To understand whether drawing/writing experience is necessary for participants to develop better local processing skills in the recognition of visual stimuli, we conducted two training studies. In an ERP study of artificial character learning, we found that learning method significantly modulated the relationship between holistic processing and N170 amplitude in the right hemisphere: a positive correlation was observed when learning to recognize artificial characters using a whole-character approach, whereas a negative correlation was observed when a component-mapping approach was used (Conference [16]). This finding is consistent with our previous modeling studies, suggesting that whether the learning method for visual object recognition emphasizes on configural or featural information processing modulates how visual objects are perceived and processed. In another study where we trained non-Chinese-speaking students to read Chinese characters, we found that both writing/copying training and component reconstruction training increased holistic character processing for beginners; however, only component reconstruction training significantly enhanced orthographic awareness (Conference [10], [15]). Together these results suggested that there may be an initial increase in holistic processing in the acquisition of visual object recognition to develop global configural processing skills, and training methods that facilitate local information processing such as drawing/writing and component mapping may help develop local analytic processing skills at a later stage.

17402814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17402814.value: Our results suggested that a combination of local and global information processing may be optimal for face recognition and face matching. However, expertise in such combination may be task-specific. Face artists’ advantage in face matching suggested the possibility of developing such expertise through face drawing practice. In contrast to face matching, it has been suggested that due to our abundant experience, adult face recognition may have reached a capacity limit and thus may have limited flexibility for improvement. Future work may examine whether it is possible to enhance adult face recognition by training participants to adopt the optimal eye movement patterns that lead to the best recognition performance. In the study with non-Chinese speaking children, we observed an increase in holistic character processing regardless of the learning methods. This is in contrast to other studies with adult participants, which typically showed that writing or component processing experiences are associated with reduced holistic processing. Future work may investigate whether the benefit of writing or component processing training would emerge at a later stage in children through longitudinal studies of how different learning methods modulate developmental changes of holistic processing and related perceptual effects.

17402814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17402814.value: Here we show that the optimal eye movement strategies for recalling previously learned faces and matching face identities involve a combination of global and local face processing through looking at the face center/nose and the eyes respectively. Face drawing training is particularly related to the enhancement of local face processing. However, this benefit may require long-term practice. Also, it is limited to face processing tasks similar to drawing experience such as matching face identities, and does not transfer well to other face recognition tasks such as recalling previously learned faces. Similar to the effect of drawing training on face processing, writing practice also facilitates local component processing of Chinese characters or novel characters. However, drawing or writing practice is not the only way to enhance local processing of visual stimuli. Training involving local component processing seems to have similar effects. These learning methods that can potentially enhance local processing of visual stimuli seem to play an important role during learning to recognition a visual stimulus type (such as faces or words), particularly at a later learning stage after the knowledge about the global configuration of the stimuli is acquired.

17403014.value: 睡眠貧乏困擾不少人。缺乏睡眠或睡眠質素不佳對情緒、工作及學業表現均有負面影響，但睡眠與主要性格特質和人與人之間變數的關係卻有待研究。在這項計劃裡，我們提出一個想法，把性格特質中的情緒穩定、正面世界觀、寛恕態度與睡眠質素連繫起來。雖然現時有一些相關數據與我們這個新想法吻合，但它們之間的因果關係尚待發掘。所以，我們會利用一個現存的數據庫進行研究，再把這項計劃得出的新數據加到裡面，來回答以下問題。 1) 若然對世界有負面的看法，會否令我們對一些曾經傷害我們的人，衍生出怨恨和不寛恕? 抑或不寛恕令我們陷入與人磨擦的惡性循環中，令我們確信這個社會是一個危險和不好的地方? 2) 如果我們不能寛恕，這會否干擾我們的睡眠? 抑或睡眠問題會令寛恕變得困難? 3) 優質的睡眠會否令我們有一個更正面的人生展望? 抑或一個正面的人生展望，讓我們內心有平安，所以有一個無憂慮的睡眠? 4) 情緒穩定是一個構成正面世界觀、寛恕態度和良好睡眠質素的原因嗎? 抑或情緒穩定是它們造成的長遠結果? 5) 以上的因果關係是否在各性別和年齡群體均存在? 6) 如果抑鬱經常出現在悲觀或睡眠貧乏的人身上，那麼抑鬱會否以上一些因果關係的解釋? 我們將會用數年時間來追蹤研究對象的情緒穩定、世界觀、寛恕態度和睡眠質素，並運用結構方程模型去分辨這四種特徵之間可能存在的因果關係。 這項研究有長遠的實用涵義。例如，若欠佳的睡眠質素是造成不寛恕，負面的世界觀和情緒不穩定的重要原因，那麼改善睡眠便可以作為預防方法。而另一方面，若結果顯示負面的世界觀是影響這些特徵的根本原因, 我們可以致力幫助人們改善這項認知功能。所以，這個研究的發現可以幫助為有需要者設計和提供最適合的治療和訓練方案。

17403014.label: Realisation of objectives
17403014.value: All three objectives were achieved successfully. Objective #1: To establish associations among emotional stability, positive worldview, forgivingness, and sleep quality We have shown interesting (and also anticipated) correlation among our research variables. For example, an optimistic worldview is associated with sleep quality while social cynicism is negatively associated with optimism; emotional stability is associated with forgivingness and an optimistic worldview; people who sleep well are also more forgiving, higher on emotional stability, and lower on social cynicism; and optimism is associated with forgivingness. Further details of the associations among our study variables can be found in Table 2 of attachment 1 (Lau*, Hui, Lam, & Cheung, 2017) and Table 2 of attachment 2 (Lau*, Hui, Lam, Cheung & Cheung, under review), as well as in this link (https://goo.gl/ueCjLy). Using a large dataset, we established associations among emotional stability, positive worldview, forgivingness, and sleep quality. Objective #2: To identify the directions of causality among emotional stability, positive worldview, forgivingness, and sleep quality We have determined, through the use of cross-lagged analyses, the presence or absence of directional relationships among the research variables. For instance, we found forgivingness a robust predictor of emotional stability across three waves of survey, suggesting that forgivingness may reduce neuroticism with lasting effects. As one forgives more readily, resentment and right to retaliate are abandoned. With less motivation to harm and more motivation to act favorably to the offender, forgivingness may also strengthen agreeableness, albeit marginally, as supported by our cross-lagged analysis across all three waves of data. Inclination to forgive others might have promoted better moods over the course of six years in the current study. Despite cross-sectional correlations, our longitudinal data did not support directional relationships between forgivingness and sleep quality across waves, once auto-regressions were taken into account. Therefore, our analyses of this longitudinal dataset enable us to differentiate cross-sectional versus directional relationships, and such distinction is pivotal in understanding the complex associations among the study variables, with important implications. Objective #3: To explore possible mediators and moderators of the relationships among emotional stability, positive worldview, forgivingness, and sleep quality Regarding Objective #3, we explored several mediating relationships. For example, using three waves of data, we tested a path model of forgivingness being predicted by three antecedents (namely emotional stability, sleep quality, and social cynicism), mediated by depressive mood, anxiety, and stress. Besides finding a direct effect of emotional stability on forgivingness, we also found an emotional stability → depressive mood link, as well as a depressive mood → forgivingness link. In another series of cross-lagged analyses, we tested several models in which emotional stability, sleep quality, mood symptoms (depressive mood, anxiety, and stress), and forgivingness were posited as antecedents, mediators, and outcomes. Age, gender, and education were used as covariates throughout. We found forgivingness predicting subsequent level of anxiety, which further predicted emotional stability. Anxiety partially mediated the effect of forgivingness on emotional stability. Another series of cross-lagged analyses over three waves of data revealed an anxiety → emotional stability → sleep quality link. In terms of moderators, we found that sleep quality affects mood symptoms and optimism differently for different circadian preferences. Poor sleep results in depressive mood and thus pessimism in non-morning persons only. In contrast, the effects of optimism on sleep quality were invariant of circadian preference. We shall continue to look for other theoretically meaningful mediators and moderators of the directional relationships we have uncovered thus far. As a whole, all three objectives were realized by application of cross-sectional, cross-lagged, and path analyses on our longitudinal dataset successfully collected through the support of this project grant. In addition to replicating some correlations between our study variables, we established some new cross-sectional relationships, identified some directional relationships and refuted some that have been (inaccurately) assumed in the literature with cross-sectional data. The dataset also allows us to continue to explore mediators and moderators of the hypothesized directional relationships.

17403014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17403014.value: In the original proposal, we stated six pairs of hypotheses for testing. We are listing them below, as well as the findings and research outcome pertaining to those hypotheses. H1a: Forgivingness would improve sleep quality. H1b: Good sleep quality would enhance forgivingness. There is no causal relationship between forgivingness and sleep quality within the timeframe we studied, despite the existence of cross-sectional correlations. This suggested the presence of some common external factors that influence both forgivingness and sleep quality (Lau, Hui, Lam, & Cheung, 2016). H2a: Being emotionally stable would help quality of sleep. H2b: Having good sleep quality would improve emotional stability. Emotional stability predicts prospectively sleep quality both one year and four years later; sleep quality predicts emotional stability prospectively four years later but not one year later. H3a: People high on emotional stability would develop a positive worldview. H3b: People with a positive worldview would become more emotionally stable, There is some evidence that emotional stability predicts higher optimism one year later and lower social cynicism four years later. However, positive worldview does not seem to have a reliable effect on emotional stability. H4a: People high on emotional stability would become more forgiving. H4b: People who are forgiving would become more emotionally stable. Forgivingness strengthens emotional stability but not the other way round. In addition, we found that forgivingness predicts agreeableness and negative moods measured 2-3 years later. We also found a weak causal link from conscientiousness to forgivingness (Lau, Hui, Lam, Cheung, & Cheung, under review). H5a: People with a positive worldview would have better quality of sleep. H5b: People who have good sleep quality would develop a positive worldview. Social cynics have poor sleep quality. However, this negative social worldview are not causally linked to poor sleep quality (Lau, Kung, Hui, Lam, Lam, Cheung, & Cheung, 2017). Cross-lagged analyses showed a bidirectional effect between optimism and sleep quality. Moreover, path analyses demonstrated that anxiety and stress symptoms partially mediated the influence of optimism on sleep quality, while depressive mood partially mediated the influence of sleep quality on optimism (Hui, Lau, Lam, & Cheung, 2015; Lau, Hui, Lam, & Cheung, 2017). H6a: People with a positive worldview would become more forgiving. H6b: People who are forgiving would develop a positive worldview. Pessimistic attributional style was found to be both an antecedent and outcome of unforgivingness, which also fueled subsequent social cynicism (Lau, Cheung, Kung, Lam, Hui, & Cheung, submitted).

17403014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17403014.value: With respect to sleep quality, so far we have investigated how this relatively transient factor may or may not affect people’s forgivingness, emotional stability, and worldview. This opens an avenue of research on how the trajectory of change in sleep quality over time (rather than the sleep quality at a particular time point) might affect a wider array of human functioning, from physical health, neurocognitive affective functions, social relationships, to personality formation and character development. We are currently preparing a GRF proposal in this direction of investigation, examining the key variables of sleep and some flourishing outcomes measured both by a longitudinal survey as well as in-lab objective tests. We believe that this will make an important contribution to the literature, as to date, the only sleep trajectory study focused only on sleep duration. The inclusion of objective data in a new wave of data collection being proposed is expected to enhance this already-rare Chinese longitudinal dataset of psychosocial variables and wellbeing outcomes. We intend to write another manuscript on the personality factors as antecedents and consequences of sleep quality (findings of H2 and H3).

17403014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17403014.value: This research project utilized survey data collected repeatedly from a large Chinese sample, to understand if a personality trait of emotional stability, a positive worldview comprising of optimism and low social cynicism, a forgiving attitude, and good sleep quality are related to each other. With a longitudinal design enabling cross-lagged modelling, we can draw inferences about directionality of relationships more confidently than were a simple cross-sectional survey conducted. From the research, it is quite clear that: - A negative outlook about the world breeds bitterness and unforgivingness towards people who have harmed us. At the same time, the unwillingness to forgive entraps us in a vicious cycle of interpersonal conflicts, thus reinforcing in us that the social world is indeed a dangerous place. - Being unforgiving and having sleep disturbance are related to each other, and are probably the result of some common causes yet unknown. - Sleeping well results in a more optimistic outlook in life. Likewise, being optimistic helps one’s sleep. - A person’s forgiving attitude builds emotional stability, which would in turn help sleep. These findings are useful for practitioners assisting clients to improve their sleep, to have a more positive outlook of the world around them, and to flourish psychologically and socially.

17403514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17403514.value: 自知副本： 探究古畫副本的創造性

17403514.label: Project Objectives
17403514.value: To determine a historic account of the copy and the original in the history of Chinese ink painting. Although this project is not intended as a comprehensive history, it will provide close examinations of how imitative acts were assessed and valued from the sixteenth century to the early twentieth century. To examine the idea of copying as a self-knowing act. By looking at repetitions, revisions and citations, I will provide an analysis of how these three modes differed, and how they were used by artists to make copies that expressed ideas or themes such as wit, nostalgia, filial piety, ideals of erasure, and the passage of time. This approach will also sharpen terminologies such as understanding original in terms of inventiveness (creativity) or as a singular starting point (origin). To investigate four important cultural contexts that influenced the use of copying as an inventive act. I have identified four interlinked contexts in which ideas of the original were exploited or challenged. Each case study will provide historical specificity to these four contexts: the rise of the art market, large-scale production, new technology and mass production, and the collection of and writing about Chinese art on the global stage. To include intercultural discussions and how notions of cultural authenticity impacted ideas of copies and originals. This objective will result in placing unlikely types of ink paintings side by side (Ming handscroll next to export watercolors) thus breaking away from the conventions of ink painting as a literati mode made by a socially exclusive group of artists. To determine any social, political, and technological patterns in the four case studies. While the copying of paintings has continued throughout history, the case studies will attempt to pinpoint any common factors when questions of copies were being asked and explored. By looking at pre-1950s Chinese art, this project will provide a historical study that will be relevant to current discussions on contemporary Chinese art where copying are deliberate acts that often form social and political critiques. It will provide a foundation in understanding how strategies such as irony or cynicism were (similar to ideas of wit or nostalgia in the past) employed to speak on the theme of originality.

17403514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17403514.value: Historically, a common view in Chinese art was that the transmission of style is achieved through repeated copying of masters until the student is able to transcend the model. According to the system developed to assess the ability of an artist, to be imitative rather than transcendental was to be skilled yet without talent. Copying, however, was not only instructional, it also cultivated a lineage of artists and a legacy of brush mode which, to this day, uphold the tradition of Chinese ink painting. Under what circumstances can imitative acts be considered more than an expression of skill, and even inventive? In the proposed study, I will examine cases, where artists produced self-knowing forms of copy by using different modes of replication, revision and citation to provoke the audience to respond to their performance of copying as an inventive act. In such instances, there are always at least two embedded narratives – one that references the original, and the other of the conceit. My interest lies in unpacking how the different narratives interact, what new relationships are formed, and what happens when two different moments in time are collapsed together, and when a copied painting no longer acts as a stand-alone art object, destabilized from a fixed point in history. This new book project comprises four in-depth studies. The historical specificity of each will enrich the analysis of what constituted a copy at different times. I begin with the sixteenth century when a growing art market saw artists revised famous paintings as a form of pictorial wit that challenged the commodification of art. I end with one of the first modern revisions of ink into oil when a Japanese artist reworked a famous Yuan dynasty ink painting, thus bringing two different pictorial systems and cultural contexts into play. In between, I will also investigate how earlier cross-cultural borrowings, and the challenge of reproduction technologies also impacted the role of the copy. My findings, when published, will greatly advance our understanding of how painters would copy for reasons that goes far beyond a need for training, or to cultivate a lineage. My research will show how copied artworks interacted with histories of technology, the market place, the writing of history, and new mediums. It will add significant complexity to issues of copying, and perhaps more tellingly, the role of the original in Chinese art history. 在中國古畫史上，所以一般認為款式傳輸是通過著名藝術家的重複複製實現，直到學生能超越的典範。這也確定的系統，評估一個藝術家的技巧。而且熟練筆法還培養了傳統的風格，到今天堅持中國水墨畫的歷史。 在什麼情況下模仿的行為可以被認為是多技能的表達，甚至是有創造性？ 我 的研究是從這焦點來挑戰一些傳統副本的想法。我所說的“自知仿像”是當畫家故意使用原件和副本之間的關係來提供了一個對圖像製作的探索分析。由於複製品具有其自身別於原件的歷史意義， 我會檢正本和副本之間不同的關係 （例如如何原始是定在某一時刻而副本是沒有定時的關係），不同的複製，修改和引用的方式，以及如何複製性能作為一個創造性形式。最終, 我的調查提供了思考中國藝術史的圖像文化的一種方式。

17403614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17403614.value: Improving supply- and demand-side energy management is important to reducing carbon-emissions. Much has been achieved on the supply-side by integrating cleaner energy or improving energy efficiency. On the demand-side, studies show that providing simple aggregate consumption feedback via energy monitors to electricity consumers can achieve energy savings between 5-20%. However, previous studies on direct energy feedback have been criticized. First, possible variations in local climate and cultures have often been overlooked. Second, the impact of the energy consumption behavior (ECB) change has not been sustained over the long term. Third, many studies have suffered from small data samples and poor experimental control. Fourth, Smart-Energy-Management-Systems (SEMS) have been experimented with in some Western countries, but the opportunity to use social media with Smart Energy Management Technologies (SEMT) to empower citizens for ECBs has not been explored comprehensively or with high methodological rigor. Technological Empowerment (TE) can be achieved by the provision of useful EC information at the household-level to enable users to effectively adapt their lifestyles and form a social identity to actively reduce energy consumption. This study investigates whether TE facilitated by SEMT/SEMS can produce better and more long-term change of ECBs. This project adopts an interdisciplinary model hypothesizing that ECBs are linked to (i) TE (ii) human cognition (including: values-beliefs-norms; knowledge, behavioral intention; technology use gratifications). A large-scale field experiment will be conducted to study the effects of these factors on ECBs in 400 households in HK for 12 months. The field experiment is divided into two parts: (i) quantitative analysis of EC via SEMS and quantitative survey discharge, and (ii) qualitative analysis of the participating households. The SEMS installed in participating households will monitor EC and provide different levels of TE, including: (a) information distribution, (b) information sharing and (c) information co-creation and empowerment. Pre- and post-experimental surveys will be administered to assess the behavioral change. Focus group interviews will be undertaken to understand how SEMT in SEMS facilitate ECB change. The significance is threefold. First, the TE project will go beyond simple information feedback and links TE with ECB change and human cognition. It informs researchers and policy-makers of the role of technological interventions in empowering citizens in ECB changes. Second, it generates an integrated and sophisticated interdisciplinary methodology that combines social-science and engineering perspectives in energy and ECB research. Third, this pioneering study will provide a new TE paradigm for understanding and changing ECB in a Chinese context. 改善能源供應和需求管理對減少碳排放非常重要。過去多透過採用清潔能源和提高能源效率控制能源供應。能源需求管理方面，研究顯示，通過節能顯示器所提供的簡單反饋可節約能源百分之五到二十左右。然而，過去，有關能源直接回饋的研究受到批評。第一，當地氣候和文化的因素往往被忽略了。第二，能源消費行為（ECB）是否出現長期變化仍未有可靠論證。第三，過去許多研究所採用的數據樣本非常有限，缺乏嚴謹實驗對照。第四，智能能源管理系統（SEMS）雖已在一些西方國家推行，但仍沒在社交網絡獲嚴謹實驗驗證，和獲廣泛採用，以推動公民改變ECB。技術赋能（TE）可以透過向家庭提供有用信息， 使用戶能夠有效地改變他們的生活模式，提高社會認同，積極節能。本研究旨在探討是否TE通過SEMS可以產生更好，更長遠的ECB 改變 。

17403914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17403914.value: Being highly prevalent, breast cancer, creates a massive health and social burden and is widely considered to generate significant psychosocial distress. For most women this distress is widely believed to peak during BC diagnosis and treatment, and thus is transient, or spontaneously remits during the first year following diagnosis. However our previous studies demonstrated that most affected women in fact experience little distress, but one-in-seven experience substantially-elevated distress persisting for many years. Identifying such women vulnerable to poor psychological adjustment and developing effective preventive interventions is an important goal. However, factors differentiating distress trajectories in response to cancer diagnosis remain obscure. Prior work suggests selective information-processing bias may critically modulate adjustment to cancer diagnosis. Two forms of bias in particular, attention bias and interpretation bias, are postulated to be important in differentiating emotionally vulnerable and non-vulnerable individuals both through determining initial response to adverse events, and modifying subsequent adaptation and hence recovery. This study proposes to test four main questions: (1)are there differences in the way women with persistent high distress vs. those with low distress following BC diagnosis attend to negatively-valenced stimuli when primed with cancer context vs. a non-primed condition? (2) are there differences in the way these two groups of women attend to cancer-related stimuli? (3) are there differences in the way such women attend to negatively-valenced or cancer-related stimuli when these are presented very briefly vs. for prolonged duration? And; (4) are there differences in the way such women interpret ambiguous cues. An experimental paradigm is adopted to test the proposed questions. To compare between women with persistent distress and those with low distress in response to BC diagnosis, we will draw 166 participants (83 women identified with low-stable distress and 83 with persistent distress) for the proposed study from our existing study of psychological distress trajectories following BC diagnosis. Eligible women will be invited via phone by the research assistant to visit our laboratory for one two-hour session to complete the computerized experimental task and a questionnaire measuring concurrent distress, on a one-on-one basis. A dot-probe task, the technique commonly used to assess attention bias, and an ambiguous cues paradigm for tests of bias in interpretation will be used. Our research team members have substantive experience in all aspects of this study. The experimental design enables clear tests of these hypotheses that will inform therapeutic interventions for women who are at risk for persistent distress. 乳癌高發，造成嚴重的健康和社會負擔，也引起顯著的社交及心理困擾。對於大部分的女性，這種困擾在乳癌診斷和治療期間達到最高，而在診斷後的一年內會緩慢降低。根據我們已有的研究結果，大部分患乳癌女性經歷較少困擾，但每七人中有一人的困擾會明確提高及其困擾會持續多年。 要有效預防婦女因患乳癌以導致長期心理困擾，我們需要識別高危的婦女。但是，影響癌病診斷導致困擾發展軌跡的因素至今並不明確。研究顯示選擇性信息處理偏誤對於適應癌症診斷的適應有關鍵的調節作用。特別是兩種偏誤，注意力偏誤和解釋偏誤，被普遍認為可以區別情感易受影響和情感堅韌的人。 本研究致力於四個主要問題：（1）乳癌診斷後持續困擾的女性和低困擾女性在注意有癌病背景刺激因素和無關刺激的時候分別有什麼區別？（2）這兩組女性在注意癌病相關的信息時有什麼區別？（3）這兩組女性在面對負面信息或者癌病相關刺激時，刺激較長時間和短時間有什麼區別？（4）這兩組女性在解釋兩可信息時，有什麼區別？ 我們設計了實驗來檢驗這些問題。為了比較對於乳癌診斷有持續困擾的女性和低困擾女性，從我們已經進行的關於乳癌診斷後困擾軌跡的研究中選取166名參與者（83名為穩定低困擾女性，其他83名為有持續困擾的女性）。符合要求的女性會接到研究助理的電話邀請，到訪我們的實驗室進行兩小時的項目，包括完成一個電腦實驗和一份測量同時間困擾的問卷。点探测范式常用於評估認知偏差，兩可線索解釋範式用於檢測解釋偏差。 這項實驗的設計可以清楚的檢驗這些假說，進而有助於為持續困擾的女性提供干預。

17403914.label: Realisation of objectives
17403914.value: To achieve the above four objectives, we adopted an experimental paradigm approach. To compare women with breast cancer experiencing persistent distress and those with low/transient distress, we used the sample from a previous longitudinal study of psychological distress trajectories following breast cancer diagnosis. We identified two groups of patients having either persistent distress (persistent high levels of anxiety or depression) or low-stable/transient distress. A total of 83 subjects who had persistent distress in the previous study were re-contacted and invited to participate in the current study, of whom 67/83(81%) agreed to participate. Also from that study a similar number of patients with low-stable/transient distress were randomly selected to join the present study, with 73/83(88%) patients agreeing to participate. Women invited but refusing to participate did not differ by demographic or clinical characteristics. The main reason for refusal was lack of time. A total of 140 patients gave informed consent and participated in the present study. About three years had elapsed between the original and current studies, with 1.9 years(SD 1.17) on average having elapsed since the last assessment of the original study. Eligible participants were contacted via phone by the research assistant who explained the study purpose and nature of participation, emphasizing confidentiality and anonymity. Those agreeing to participate attended an individual 90-minute assessment session. Both the dot-probe task and ambiguous cues task were programmed using e-prime, using a 2.20 GHz notebook computer with a 15-inch color display. Each participant sat 50 cm in front of the computer display and instructed on the two dot-probe tasks, the ambiguous cues task, and questionnaire. Each dot-probe task had 8 practice trials and 64 test trials, totaling 72 trials. Participants then completed the ambiguous cue task, followed by a self-report questionnaire. To achieve objective 1 and part of objective 3, a modified dot-probe task involving visually-presented verbal stimuli was used. Dot-probe tasks use pairs of stimuli, one negative/positive valence and one neutral, presented briefly on each trial, followed by a probe stimulus (dot) in the location of one of the paired stimuli immediately on termination of each stimulus pair. Here, participants were asked to respond to the probe as quickly as possible. We used verbal (word) rather than image-based stimuli, as they have comparable effect potency and ambiguity is easily controlled. Negative two-character Chinese compound words were used as negative-valence stimuli; positive two-character Chinese compound words are used as positive-valence stimuli; neutral two-character Chinese compound words are used as control stimuli. Sixty-four neutral, 32 negative, and 32 positive two-character Chinese compound words were used in the dot-probe test(29). The chosen sets of words have been repeatedly validated and used locally to study the role of attention bias in relation to anxiety and depression. To test if attention bias occurs globally or only in cancer-related contexts, a priming condition was incorporated in the dot-probe task. The priming involved subliminal presentation (~ 20 ms duration) of the Chinese text “breast cancer” for half of the trials (target prime) and a subliminal presentation of a neutral Chinese text (“sky”) for the other half of the trials (neutral prime). To test selective attention style, we manipulated exposure duration to the stimulus words. Hence, each trial began with the display of a white fixation cross in the middle of a black screen for 500ms. Then the prime condition was presented for 20 ms, followed by a pattern mask for 500ms, and then a pair of words was presented (e.g. a negative word paired with a neutral word). Word pairs were presented for either 500 ms (i.e. to assess initial orienting) or 1250 ms (i.e. to assess maintenance of attention). The 500 ms exposure has been shown to be effective for capturing the initial attention shift. Immediately after termination of each word pair stimulus presentation, the probe (a small black dot) appears at the location of one of the words, requiring a rapid key-press response from the participant. Attention to negative-valence stimuli is indicated by faster response times to probes replacing negative-valence words than to those replacing neutral words.Response latency scores (recorded reaction times) for dot detection were used to calculate attention bias scores, using the following formula: Bias index=[(TRPL-TLRL)=(TLPR–TRPR)]/2, where T=target stimulus, P=probe location, R=right side, L=left side. Positive bias index indicates an attentional tendency towards the target stimulus, whereas a negative bias index indicates an attentional tendency away from the target stimulus. Reaction time data with errors and outliers of <200 ms or >3000 ms, or those more than three standard deviation above each participant’s mean reaction time were excluded from trials. A similar modified dot-probe task was used to assess attentional bias for cancer-related information (Objective 2 and part of objective 3). Cancer-related words replaced negative words as cancer-related threat stimuli. Cancer-related words including “arm lymphedema”, “cancer treatment”, “treatment side-effects” were used as threat stimuli; neutral or positive words matched in length were used as control stimuli. Following pilot testing on breast cancer patients and healthy women 64 neutral, 32 negative cancer-related, and 32 positive two-character Chinese compound words were used in the dot-probe test. Since cancer-related information was used as threat stimuli, a priming condition was unnecessary in this second dot-probe task, but in all other respects the procedure was identical to that described above. Based on previous studies using ambiguous cues paradigms to test interpretation bias, a 30-word list was created to assess interpretation bias for somatic or illness-related information (Objective 4).In this task, we used 15 ambiguous Chinese words which have both neutral and illness-related interpretations (e.g. 岩 (phonetically similar to “cancer” in Chinese), 讀 (phonetically similar to “toxic”), 雨 (phonetically similar to “breast”) and 15 unambiguous words (e.g. 天 (sky), 杯 (cup)). These 30 words were randomly presented. Participants were told that this was a word-association exercise and wrote down the first word entering their mind after each cue word was read aloud. Responses were then independently coded by the second and third authors blinded to both participants’ distress status and cue word sequence. Participants received one “point” for every somatic or illness-related interpretation, with higher summed point scores suggesting greater interpretation bias for cancer-related information. In addition to the experimental tasks, participants completed the HADS to measure psychological distress. Data analysis: To test if attentional bias differentiated participants with persistent distress and low distress, a mixed, repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed with group (persistent distress vs. low distress) as a between-subject variable and priming condition (cancer vs. neutral), stimuli (negative vs. neutral), and exposure duration (500 vs. 1250 ms) as within-subjects variables. Independent sample t-test analysis was used to assess group differences in interpretation bias scores. Using the above approach, all project objectives had been achieved.

17403914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17403914.value: To examine the role of information processing bias in persistent distress, participants experiencing persistent high distress in both the original study and who continued to report high HADS scores (HADS scores =>8) in the present study (i.e. 31 participants reporting high anxiety and 30 reporting high depression scores) comprised the persistent distress group. Attentional bias for negative-valences stimuli (Objective 1 and 3) When we examined persistent anxiety status, repeated ANOVA analysis showed no significant main effect for group F(1,138)=0.15, p = 0.70. There was a significant 4-way interaction of group x prime x stimulus word x duration F(1,138)=4.13, p=0.044, eta2= 0.03. Post-hoc student t-test analyses showed women reporting persistent anxiety had a significant bias away (mean=-22.98, SD 49.03, t=-3.47, p=0.001) from negative-valence stimuli under the neutral prime in the supraliminal (1250 ms) condition. Similar findings were observed for women reporting persistent depression. There was no significant main effect for group F(1,138)=0.35, p=0.55, but there was, again, a significant 4-way interaction of group x prime x stimulus word x duration F(1,138)=7.38, p =0.007, eta2= 0.05. Post-hoc t-test analyses showed women reporting persistent depression showed a significant bias away (mean=-19.26, SD 54.21, t=-2.72, p=0.008) from negative-valenced stimuli under neutral primes in the supraliminal (1250 ms) condition. Attention bias in cancer-related information (Objective 2 and 3) For women reporting persistent anxiety, there was a marginal main effect for anxiety group status, F(1,138)=3.07, p=0.08 and a significant 3-way interaction of group x word stimulus x duration, F(1,138)=5.59, p=0.019, eta2= 0.04. Post-hoc analysis revealed that these women also showed a significant bias away (mean=-17.84, SD 43.39, t=-2.90, p=0.006) from cancer-related information in the supraliminal condition. For women reporting persistent depression, the analysis showed a significant main effect for depression group status, F(1,138)=7.75, p=0.006, and a significant 3-way interaction of group x word stimulus x duration, F(1,138)=4.58, p=0.034, eta2=0.03. Post-hoc analysis revealed that women reporting persistent depression showed a significant bias away (mean=-17.16, SD 53.15, t=-2.74, p=0.009) from cancer-related information in the supraliminal condition. Interpretation bias (Objective 4) For anxiety, interpretation bias scores showed a borderline result between groups on (mean 6.01, SD 2.38 for low anxiety vs. mean 7.19, SD 3.20 for persistent anxiety, t = -1.89, p=0.065). Correlation indicated significant positive association between interpretation bias and anxiety (r=0.20, p=0.019). For depression, there was no significant difference between groups (mean 6.12, SD 2.53 for low depression vs. mean 6.85, SD 2.89 for persistent depression, t=-1.27, n.s.).

17403914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17403914.value: The present study showed women treated for breast cancer who report persistent distress show responses potentially consistent with avoidance strategies to cope with threat stimuli, possibly including symptoms. Avoidant or disengagement coping can impair adaptation. Future studies should test whether tailored interventions like attention bias modification promoting active goal-focused attention search can shift disengagement coping to engagement coping and if this benefits women at risk of persistent distress. Moreover, women with persistent anxiety may have a tendency to negatively interpret ambiguous information, perhaps leading to illness preoccupation. Cognitive behaviour therapy strategies focusing on identifying and challenging these women’s negative interpretations of cancer-related information may help to manage anxiety symptoms. Hence, future research should test if attentional bias modification and cognitive behaviour therapy intervention help to reduce attention bias and interpretation bias, respectively. Furthermore, the present study lacked a healthy control group for comparison purposes.We therefore cannot determine if these study findings are specific to women with breast cancer. To build on the present study, we are currently recruiting a group of healthy women to participate in a similar study. This will enable us to compare between the breast cancer group with the healthy control group.

17403914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17403914.value: This study tested if bias in attention to and interpretation of cancer-related stimuli differentiates women with persistent psychological distress from those with low/transient distress following breast cancer. 140 women classified in a prior longitudinal study as having low(n=73) or persistent high(n=67) distress completed two experimental tasks assessing attention bias and an ambiguous cues task assessing interpretation bias towards cancer-related vs. neutral information. Persistent distress and low distress groups did not differ in attentional bias toward negative-stimuli or cancer-related information. However, women in the persistent distress group showing avoidance toward negative-stimuli or cancer-related information under supraliminal conditions. There was a borderline difference in interpretation bias scores between low anxiety and chronic anxiety groups. In summary, women with persistent distress may adopt avoidance strategies to cope with breast cancer. Women reporting persistent anxiety may also have a tendency to negatively interpret ambiguous information, leading to illness preoccupation. These findings offer critical insight for clinicians to develop tailored interventions to help women with persistent psychological distress.

17404314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17404314.value: Hong Kong has launched three IT in Education Strategies since 1998, underpinned by the perceived importance of preparing citizens with 21st century skills such as problem solving, information literacy and collaboration (Dede 2010) and the role that Information and Communication Technology (ICT) can play in supporting the necessary pedagogical transformations. However, evaluation studies show that pedagogical change through ICT adoption in Hong Kong has been slow (Yuen et al. 2010). Recent education literature reveals that changes initiated internally top-down or externally (Kezar 2001) often suffer from lack of ownership from frontline teachers. The past decades have witnessed different models of change ranging from bottom-up, to top-down to various combinations of bottom-up and top-down initiatives. Hargreaves and Shirley (2009) report on an emerging model of change that focuses on supporting bottom-up innovations that align with system level policy directions through various strategic mechanisms. This alignment can aid with the biggest challenge faced by pedagogical innovations: their sustainability and scalability (Kampylis et al. 2013). In 2010, the HKSAR Government launched an e-Learning Pilot Scheme involving 21 projects in 61 schools to stimulate and support transformative uses of ICT for teaching and learning in schools and to identify effective models to sustain and scale them. This pilot scheme broadly followed the Hargreaves and Shirley (ibid.) model. On the other hand, innovations often fail to survive when the conditions that led to their emergence are withdrawn, such as at the completion of a pilot program. The aim of this proposal is to study how the system and school level factors and their interactions may affect the further development and sustainability of the e-Learning innovations after the Pilot Scheme comes to an end. The research design is underpinned by an ecosystem model of change in which the sustainability of the new species (innovation) depends on the mutual adaptation between the new species and the environmental conditions (Law, Yuen and Fox, 2011). The proposed two-year study will use comparative, embedded case study methodology to investigate how the e-Learning innovations change and further develop after the Pilot Scheme ends (i.e., from 2014 to 2016). Both quantitative and qualitative data will be collected to find out (1) the overall status and impact of e-Learning implementation as reported by a representative sample of stakeholders, (2) whether and how the sampled e-Learning innovations further evolve and develop, and (3) the interdependencies and interactions that contribute to changes within the sampled schools. 自1998年以來香港推出的三個把資訊科技融入教育的策略文件都是建基於ICT在培養21世紀能力，如解難、信息素養和協作能力及促進教學範式轉變的重要角色。然而評價研究 發現， 香港在通過ICT達致的教學變革一直很緩慢。 最近的教育文獻揭示了來自內部或外部自上而下啟動的變化往往因缺乏來自一線教師的認同受到負面影響（Kezar, 2001）。在過去的數十年裡見證了不同類型的教育變革，包括自下而上、自上而下、以至各種自下而上和自上而下之舉措的各種組合。Hargreaves & Shirley (2009)提出了一個新的變革模式，其重點是通過各種機制支持與制度層面戰略政策方向一致的、自下而上的創新項目。這種一致性可以幫助解決教學創新所面臨的最大挑戰：其可持續性和可擴展性（Kampylis et al.，2013年）。在2010年，香港特區政府推出了電子學習試驗計劃，以鼓勵和支持信息通信技術在學校的教與學的創新性應用，並找出有效的模式，以維持和擴展它們。最後試驗計劃挑選了21個項目，共61所學校參與。這項試驗計劃大體沿襲了Hargreaves & Shirley (2009) 的模型。可是另一方面， 創新往往就在導致他們出現的條件被撤銷時銷亡。 這研究項目的目的是為了研究系統和學校層面的因素及其相互作用如何在電子學習試驗計劃結束後影響e-Learning的進一步創新和可持續的發展。研究設計以生態系統模型為基礎，其中創新的可持續性取決於新物種和環境條件之間的相互適應（Law, Yuen and Fox, 2011） 。 建議的研究項目為期兩年，採用比較，嵌入式案例研究方法，以探討電子學習創新在試驗計劃結束後兩年內（即2014年至2016年）如何進一步發展。研究將收集定量和定性的數據，以了解（1）從一些利益相關者的代表性樣本取得有關電子學習的總體實現狀況和影響，（2）樣本中的電子學習創新是否能進一步演變和發展，和（3）樣本學校的相互作用和相互依存如何影電子學習的持續發展。

17404314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17404314.value: The following key findings from this project helped to further refine this model (the item number refers to the publications listed in Part C): 1. The innovations followed diverse trajectories after the funding period ended. Some totally dissipated after two years. The architecture for learning (AfL for short, comprising the ICT infrastructures, organizational structures, routines, interactions and support mechanisms) at the network and school levels play a key role in the divergence observed (items 1,6, 7) 2. The AfL in the pilot project networks and schools changed throughout the five years. The more interactions there are among teachers and between teachers and the school leadership around the goals and implementation strategies leading to decision making in support of the innovation, the greater advances in the transformational aspects of the e-learning implementation was observed (items 2, 4, 7). 3. Teachers who have more opportunities to engage in co-planning lessons with peers and contributing to the design of the e-learning tools and their usage are more able to improve in their technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPCK) for implementing e-learning that foster students’ 21st century skills. An AfL that fosters peer learning within and across schools contribute greatly to teachers’ learning. Teachers’ actual classroom implementation of e-learning also depends on whether the infrastructure, technical support and school routines (such as timetabling) and other organizations factors were able to be modified to align with the changes in pedagogical practice (items 3, 5, 6, 7). 4. Nearly all of networks that were established to bid for funding and to implement the e-learning pilot network projects were dissolved after the funding period ended. This turned out to impact strongly the (un)sustainability of the innovation in the project schools, particularly those that were not taking a leadership role in coordinating the project. Only one of the networks were sustained, and that project in fact further prospered. This network is unique in that it existed for more than 10 years to pursue a common goal among the schools. The e-learning pilot was used as a lever to further enhance what the network wanted to achieve. This demonstrated the resilience and important of networks in sustaining and scaling innovations. (items 4, 6, 7) 5. The findings from this project provides the basis for further developing design principles for scaling pedagogical innovations using technology (items 6, 7)

17404314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17404314.value: Given the findings from the project, we have been designing more specific design principles for Design-Based Implementation Research (DBIR). Specifically, we have designed a multilevel multiscale design framework for scalable innovation at network, school and teacher levels. As described under section 11 below, we have been awarded a project titled “The title of the project is “Multilevel Leadership Network for Self-Directed Learning Innovation to Advance STEM Development” designed on the basis of these principles. The project was launched in August 2017, and preliminary data shows overall great advances in the teachers’ TPCK as well as the pedagogical practices observed. Specifically, we see a much stronger shift towards giving opportunities to students to engage in collaborative inquiry. Also our efforts to help schools build interdisciplinary project teams with teachers from different subject areas have resulted in some outstanding examples of within school collaboration. We are now in the process of analysing the data to develop a better understanding of the architecture for learning in the different schools to write up case studies and cross-school analysis.

17404314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17404314.value: Technology-Enhanced Pedagogical Innovations (TEPIs) are considered important to foster the development of 21st century skills in students. This project studies the conditions for TEPIs to achieve significant, sustainable and scalable changes in pedagogical practice in classrooms. The project finds that the implementation of the e-learning innovations, or TEPIs, is an evolutionary process, during which both the quality of teachers’ and leadership learning play an important role. The learning experiences and outcomes of teachers and school leadership depends on the “architecture for learning” (organizational structures, routines, interactions and support mechanisms) available to then at the school and network level. The core principle is to support actors at different levels—teachers, school middle managers such as panel heads, and senior school leaders such as principals and vice principals—to connect (1) horizontally so that they can engage in peer learning and inquiry to refine their core knowledge, skills, and practices for the core business of the individuals concerned, and (2) vertically to adapt school level conditions such as school routines, curriculum and assessment practices to align with the pedagogical changes at the classroom level. These findings provide the basis for the design of TEPI innovation networks that are effective, sustainable and scalable.

17404414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17404414.value: For most of the world’s population, having to communicate in spoken and/or written form in two or more languages in different contexts on a daily basis is a way of life. The questions of how different language and writing systems can be processed effortlessly by multilingual speakers and how the characteristics of these systems may interact with one another in their representation at the brain level have fascinated psycholinguists and cognitive neuroscientists in recent decades. Previous research examining the effects of the similarity between an individual’s native language (L1) and a second language (L2) on L2 literacy learning, and the neural representations of visual word form and orthography-phonology conversion of different orthographic systems has observed inconsistent findings. This might be due to the fact that comparisons of L1 effects on the processing of different L2s were made between different L2 learner groups, where L2 proficiency was not well controlled for either within or between L2 participant groups. Moreover, most previous studies were limited in the sense that the languages under investigation were restricted to scripts belonging to the same writing system, i.e. alphabetic. The present study aims to fill this gap and circumvent the confounding factors through studying trilingual speakers who live in Hong Kong with different L1s, including Indo-European languages with alphabetic scripts, Japanese with syllabic Kana and logographic Kanji, and Korean with alphabetic Hangul, who are L2 learners of Chinese and English. Chinese and English differ drastically not only in their grammatical systems, but also in their written forms and relationships between orthographic and phonological units. As such, different degrees of similarity between L1 and L2 in these participants will allow us to examine the relevant issues systematically and comprehensively, while contrasts between L2s can be made within individuals. Both behavioral measure of response latency and event-related potential (ERP) will be employed. ERP, with exquisite temporal resolution, can reflect neural activities of online processing at the orthographic, phonological, or semantic levels. Various tasks designed to respectively highlight the processing at each of these levels will be administered. An innovative method of ERP data analysis, i.e. mixed effect modeling, will be applied to assess the effects of L1 backgrounds and different psycholinguistic variables on L2 visual word processing. The results of the study will have important theoretical implications in multilingual research and pedagogical significance in L2 teaching and learning.

17404414.label: Realisation of objectives
17404414.value: A. Study design for achieving project objectives Objective 1: This study aims to examine the role of L1-L2 similarity in L2 visual word processing with event-related potential (ERP). Comparisons on form similarity at the script-level (letter strings or block characters) and orthography-phonology mapping (alphabetic, syllabic or logographic systems) are achieved in three trilingual groups with Indo-European languages, Japanese, or Korean as L1, and both Chinese and English as L2s. These languages are chosen because they represent major writing systems of the world. The four orthographic systems, i.e. Roman alphabets/English, Hangul, Kanji, Chinese, constitute significant contrasts in visual complexity and overall shape of orthographic units. For the former, we draw heavily on Chang, Plaut, and Perfetti (2016), which puts forth a set of objective measures that together quantify the visual complexity of an orthography. According to their metric system applied to 131 orthographies, the overall visual complexity scores of the four writing systems in question cover almost the entire spectrum. In short, Hangul is more similar to English in complexity, while Kanji is more similar to Chinese. With respect to the overall shape of lexical/morphemic units, Japanese Kanji has more or less the same characteristics as Chinese characters and Korean Hangul can be said to resemble Chinese characters in overall shape and internal structure. The various target languages also encompass different orthography-phonology mappings – alphabetic and phonemic for English and Korean hangul, syllabic for Japanese katakana and hiragana, and morphosyllabic/logographic for Chinese and Japanese kanji. These trilingual groups with comparable non-native language proficiency allow us to examine the research question through comparing their neural responses with those of native Chinese and English control groups, respectively. The fully crossed factors of scripts, writing systems, and language proficiency thus enable us to examine how language distance between L1 and L2 affects L2 lexical processing at the orthographic, phonological and semantic levels. Multilingual studies with language users of typologically different languages are especially valuable because they allow for uniform comparisons of effects coming from various sources. We want to highlight that despite the previous revision of project objectives to remove the Korean group in light of significant budget reduction, we eventually managed to include L1 Korean participants. Objective 2: Besides the distinctive language backgrounds of our participant groups, another important design feature of the present study is the employment of a non-factorial design with a large number of written word stimuli in Chinese and English representing different orthography-phonology mappings. With a non-factorial design, our data analyses adopt linear mixed-effects modelling (LMEM). A number of publications has discussed its advantages over repeated measures ANOVA of behavioural data and ERPs. LMEM assesses effects of ﬁxed factors and those of random factors of subject and item that are un-correlated with the independent variables. It is superior to traditional analyses in dealing with unbalanced data, missing values, and non-sphericity, common problems in ERP studies. Objective 3: Three ERP tasks focusing on different levels of analysis to highlight the processing of each lexical constituent have been carried out in Chinese and English, respectively, to compare how tasks affect visual word processing. More specifically, they include a Repetition Detection task assessing visual/orthographic processing, a Semantic Categorization task revealing semantic access, and Delayed Naming of words demonstrating processes of sublexical and lexical phonology. B. Data collected and progress on data analysis In terms of data collected, we have administered the three ERP tasks described above on five groups of participants (i) 22 native Mandarin speakers and readers of the simplified Chinese script, (ii) 22 native English speakers, (iii) 18 native Japanese speakers, (iv) 22 native Korean speakers, and (v) 15 native speakers of European languages with Roman alphabets other than English. Participants in groups (iii) – (v) learned Chinese and English as non-native languages. A language background questionnaire and reading screening tests were developed for selecting trilingual participants with adequate reading proficiencies in Chinese and English. The questionnaire gathered information on the trilingual participants’ ages-of-acquisition of Chinese and English and the extent of non-native language use in different settings of their daily living, including home, work/school, social interaction and recreational activities. The information is taken into consideration when performing LMEM. While the experimental tasks are common in the literature, our study (with a non-factorial design and use of LMEM for data analyses) differs from many previous studies particularly in Chinese visual word processing. Hence, our data analysis first focused on the L1 Chinese group in semantic categorization and delayed naming. Subsequently, we analysed delayed naming of the Korean participants in Chinese and English, in comparison with L1 Chinese and English speakers, respectively. More recently, we have been focusing on the issue of lateralization of an early ERP component (i.e. N170) reflecting expertise to print, across L1 Chinese, L1 Korean and L1 Japanese participants during repetition detection of Chinese characters. The comparison with the most exciting findings thus far comes from the analyses of picture trials (in the final block of the repetition detection tasks) across the four speaker groups – Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean. Details of results are provided in 6.1. There is a good deal of data analyses that remains to be conducted, including data in the delayed naming and semantic categorization tasks of the L1 Japanese group, semantic categorization task of the L1 Korean group. Data from participants of the European group of any tasks have not begun. Reasons for this relatively slow progress are given below. C. Challenges encountered and possible solutions The biggest challenge of our project is a significant budget cut of 32%, compared with the requested amount of HKD$918,917. That has drastically reduced the manpower required to accomplish the goals of our project efficiently, given its scale. Early on, we decided that our resources would focus on recruitment of participants and data collection. To that end, we reached the target simple size for the Chinese, English, and Korean groups. It was much more difficult to find L1 Japanese and European participants satisfying our criteria in the university, and many of the participants in these two groups were recruited in the community through various channels. The reduced budget allowed us to support a research assistant for two years. Given the advanced data analytic skills required, extensive training had to be provided before the RA could conduct processing of EEG data and LMEM relatively independently. While we have collected a vast amount of very rich data, EEG data pre-processing was time consuming and data analyses using LMEM have taken much longer than expected given the complexity of modelling. A portion of the budget contributed to support a post-doc fellow who spent 50% of her time on data analysis for this project. Unfortunately, she had to resign early this year (2018) due to personal reasons. We intend to continue analysing the data, despite without any research assistant. One strategy might be to recruit RPG students with an interest in the topic, who will take advantage of the available data as a first step in their investigation.

17404414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17404414.value: This project has so far resulted in two paper publications in major international peer-reviewed journals, including Journal of Neurolinguistics (Impact actor: 1.547) and Cognition (IF: 3.354), one manuscript under review, and one manuscript in preparation, as well as five presentations in international conferences, including Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society, Annual Meeting of the Academy of Aphasia, International Conference on the Processing of East Asian languages, and Conference of Association for Reading and Writing in Asia (see Part C). Major findings by manuscript: 1. ERP correlates of concreteness effects on single Chinese characters of nouns, verbs and adjectives in semantic categorization (Law, Yum, & Cheung, 2017) – The results showed that concreteness modulated N400 amplitudes elicited by monomorphemic nouns and verbs in posterior regions, similar to previous studies examining compound words. Concreteness continued to modulate neural response to verbs in the same pattern as in the N400 during 500-1000 ms. 2. Impact of characteristics of L1 literacy experience on picture processing (Yum & Law, 2018) – This study examined whether the characteristics of one’s native writing system, with respect to visual complexity and overall shape of orthographic unit, would influence the processing of pictured objects embedded among English or Chinese word trials. The results did not show lateralization of N170 or N400 in either language block. The Japanese and Korean groups differed from each other in both language blocks and both ERP components. The Korean group differed from L1 Chinese in both N170 and N400, but was similar to L1 English in both ERP components. However, the Japanese participants were similar to both native Chinese and English speakers when processing picture stimuli. Finally, both trilingual groups exhibited more negative N400 to pictures presented among English words than Chinese characters. 3. Dissociation between effects of age-of-acquisition and lexical frequency in delayed character naming of L1 Chinese speakers (Yum & Law, 2nd revision) – Single-trial ERP analyses were conducted to contrast the interactions of frequency and AoA effects with phonological regularity, while controlling for the other factor. The interaction of frequency and regularity was found in Chinese for the first time in the N400 and LPC time windows but not at early components. The interaction of AoA and regularity at the N400 favoured the semantic hypothesis over the arbitrary mapping hypothesis. Results showed dissociable effects of frequency and AoA at the N400 and LPC, suggesting effects at phonological and semantic-level processing.

17404414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17404414.value: The methodology of the current investigation, including features of a non-factorial design with a large number of stimuli to ensure ecological validity, a neuroimaging technique with exquisite temporal resolution to reflect neural activities of online processing at the orthographic, phonological, or semantic levels, within-subject comparisons between critical language conditions, and an application of linear mixed-effects modelling particularly suitable for ERP studies, has demonstrated its unique advantages to address the research questions. We will likely employ the same design in future language processing studies, albeit its high demand for resources. For further improvement, as pointed out by a reviewer of one of the publications (Yum & Law, 2018), two of the non-native speaker groups, Korean and Japanese, are not well-matched in age, due to difficulties in recruiting trilingual speakers with Chinese and English proficiency levels that met our criteria. The imbalance in age naturally leads to different amounts of experience in non-native languages, which may possibly have unknown influence on observations of the experimental tasks. This should preferably be avoided in future investigation, perhaps through collaborating with language centres in the university for recruitment of potential participants, to ensure comparability across speaker groups.

17404414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17404414.value: The questions of how different language and writing systems can be processed effortlessly by multilingual speakers and how the characteristics of these systems may interact with one another in their representation at the brain level have fascinated psycholinguists and cognitive neuroscientists in recent decades. Previous research has focused exclusively on readers of alphabetic scripts and yielded inconsistent findings. The present study fills this gap and circumvent the confounding factors through studying trilingual speakers who live in Hong Kong with different L1s, including Indo-European languages with Roman alphabet, Japanese, and Korean, who are non-native learners of Chinese and English. Different degrees of similarity between L1 and L2 in these participants allow us to examine the relevant issues systematically and comprehensively, while contrasts between L2s can be made within individuals. Various tasks designed to respectively highlight the processing at the orthographic, phonological, or semantic levels are administered. An innovative method of event-related potential (ERP) data analysis, i.e. mixed-effects modelling, is applied to assess the effects of L1 backgrounds and different psycholinguistic variables on L2 visual word processing. The results of the study will make important theoretical contribution to multilingual research and have pedagogical significance in L2 teaching and learning.

17405014.label: Project Objectives
17405014.value: To establish the paradigm of the Chinese cybertext by conceptualizing various modalities of experimental Chinese poetry as a dynamic spectrum: the printed book, the digital hypertext and the interactive installation.
