17406514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17406514.value: “Productive ageing” was introduced as a concept and practice in several developed societies to counter the dominant perception that older people are dependents of society rather than economically productive members. It has been adopted as a policy initiative to advocate for elderly-friendly employment policies and practices. Productive ageing differs from other related concepts (e.g. “successful ageing”), as it focuses on older individuals’ production of goods and services – paid and unpaid work. Most often, these contributions occur through volunteering, caregiving, working, and life-long learning roles. Older people who engage in productive ageing roles interact with society and generate products and services that create economic value, thereby serving as more than mere dependents of their communities. While there is strong evidence to support the benefits of productive ageing engagement for older adults, we know little about how or why older people allocate their time between different activities (family, social, productive), and most research on productive ageing is static. However, productive engagement is a dynamic process, waxing and waning in response to the nature of family and social role obligations and circumstances. Most studies focus on just one or two active commitments (e.g., volunteering or working), ignoring the reality that individuals engage in multiple roles and activities in their lives. Older adults’ decision-making and selection processes in terms of their level of commitment to competing roles (e.g., productive roles, family roles, and other social roles) remain unclear. Based on psychological and economic theories, a person’s expected longevity is an important factor influencing time commitment in various roles; however, no previous studies have attempted to investigate whether expected longevity mediates productive role engagement. Before we can maximize the untapped human capital within this age group, we need to understand how older people invest their time in various dynamically changing roles. The proposed study aims to investigate (1) variations of productive ageing in older persons of different age, gender, socioeconomic status and health conditions; (2) the effect of expected longevity on engagement in productive roles in relation to other roles and activities; and (3) the goodness of fit of a theoretically driven explanatory model with the effects of age and health mediated by expected longevity and other role engagement in predicting productive role engagement among elderly in Hong Kong.

17406514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17406514.value: We interviewed 369 community-dwelling older persons in Hong Kong for their health and perceived life expectancy, followed by a 7-day ecological momentary assessment to record their family, social, and productive activities. Participants (age 75 ± 8.3 years; 80% women) reported a perceived life expectancy of 10 ± 6.4 years. Majority (57.4%) reported engaging in productive activities over 7 days. Shorter perceived life expectancy correlated negatively with productive engagement and positively with immediate family engagement. Our results failed to reject the hypothesis that an individual’s expected longevity mediates the effect of age and health condition on the person’s engagement in different roles including both the productive and family/social roles. We also found that compared with health, age had a greater effect on perceived life expectancy (standardized coefficient -0.616) and that expected life longevity had a stronger effect on productive role engagement than cognitive ability and economic status. The model showed excellent goodness-of-fit: Chi-square 25.29 (df = 19; p = 0.15); CFI 0.984; RMSEA 0.032; SRMR 0.048. Our study sample differs from those in earlier studies from other economically developed societies as we had a large percentage of our sample with no formal education (31%) or only primary school education (33%). Empirical evidence suggests that human capital, typically measured by education attainment, promotes active civic participation and volunteering. However, even with such low education achievement, elders in our sample were very active in productive activities. The figures are comparable or even slightly higher than our western counterparts which have much higher education achievement. In our regression analysis, we found no association between education and productive aging engagement. Our findings seem to suggest that among older persons, either human capital has limited effect on productive aging engagement or education attainment is not a good proxy for human capital among older people. We found that health, measured objectively by the number of diseases, had no directly effect on productive aging engagement, but had an indirectly effect through perceived life expectancy. Among individual factors such as cognitive ability and economic status, perceived life expectancy had the strongest effect on explaining older people’s preference for immediate family role versus productive role. Worse health may affect productive ageing via a subjective path of lower perceived life expectancy and an objective path of higher physical constraints. Perceived life expectancy is potentially modifiable and effort to promote healthy aging will likely have indirectly effect on productive aging.

17406514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17406514.value: Findings of this study point to several research directions. First, we found an indirect association between health and productive aging engagement, mediated by the perceived life expectancy. Perceived life expectancy is potentially a modifiable factor. This point to a potential pathway connecting healthy aging and productive aging. Further research is needed understand such pathway and how intervention on promoting healthy aging may have an indirect effect on productive aging. We found that education attainment may not be a good proxy for human capital among older people. Early research showed that human capital is a significant predictor for productive aging engagement and civic engagement among older people. More research is need to understand how to better measure different from of capitals, including human capital and social capital) among older people and their association with productive aging and other civic engagement among older people. This study focused on individual factors affecting productive aging engagement. Although our variables explained a large variance of productive aging engagement, we still need to have better understanding on how institutional factors, such as labor policy and human resources practice, may affect productive engagement among older people.

17406514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17406514.value: Productive aging refers to older people participating in activities that generate economic values. Most often, these contributions occur through volunteering, caregiving, working, and life-long learning roles. Earlier studies found positive effects of productive aging engagement on health and mental health. Despite known benefits of productive aging, it is unclear what predicts time allocation in productive activities among older people. Most research did not consider multiple role engagement and time investment. Theoretically, perceived life expectancy may mediate the effects of age and health to predict productive engagement. We interviewed 369 community-dwelling older persons in Hong Kong for their health and perceived life expectancy and collected their activity patterns over 7 days. They reported an average perceived life expectancy of 10 years. Majority of them engaged in productive aging activities during these 7 days. We found that age and health affected perceived life expectancy which affected how older persons allocated their time between immediate family role and productive aging role. Shorter perceived life expectancy correlated negatively with productive engagement and positively with immediate family engagement. Perceived longevity has a stronger effect on productive aging engagement than other individual factors, such as cognitive ability and income status.

17407014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17407014.value: 近現代日本的性別，身體文化，禮儀，健康

17407014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17407014.value: This historical and ethnographic study examines female Japanese body cultures and its transformations from the late 19th to the first decade of the 21st century to understand the complex interactions between gendered notions of propriety, physical acts, and diverse health practices and beliefs in the construction of an idealize national female identity. In this inquiry, body culture refers to the physical ideals, techniques, practices and acts and its cultural contexts that shape these interpretations. The body is akin to a cultural artifact, where its physical actions are molded and informed by socio-cultural and historical factors and conditions. In the latter half of the 20th century, a young Japanese woman may hesitate to sit down on the sidewalk for reasons of propriety and health. For women of her generation, sitting on the ground was considered “inappropriate,” but the physical act was also viewed as detrimental to her health because her “waist” (lower torso) would be chilled by the direct contact to the cold ground, possibly leading to infertility. In this example, the questions to pose are numerous: Why (and since when) was sitting on the ground inappropriate for women and not men? And why were ideas of “chilling” one’s body, based on traditional Chinese and Japanese medical thought, selectively entrenched in the discussion of women’s health in the 20th century? Did health concerns inform gendered physical manners of propriety, or vice versa? Despite the apparent dominance of conventional medicine in contemporary Japan, how do we understand the historical and cultural interplay between these physical acts of propriety, gender, and health? The research objective is to analyze the body as a depository of rituals and disciplined acts, shaped by and embodying historically and culturally specific ideals to better understand the physicality of propriety, gender, and health in the making of a national identity as a “Japanese” woman. 這是一個結合歷史和人種學的研究, 探討19世紀末到21世紀間 日本女性身體文化的轉變, 以理解這個時期有關禮儀､身體行為､與衛生習慣中的性別觀念､以及這些觀念與理想的民族女性身分間的互動關係。。所謂身體文化， 指理想身體､身體技術，､動作與行為，以及解釋這些行為的文化背景。身體類似文化産品，社會文化與歷史因素影響了它所有的行為與動作。。在20世紀後期，年輕的日本女子不會隨便為了健康原因坐在路邊，因為對這代婦女而言， 這樣做是不禮貎的。同時這樣做也被認為是不衛生的， 因為坐在冷冰冰的地方會傷害她的下半身， 甚至讓她不育。 。這個例子反映了很多問題： 為什麼（以及從甚麼時代開始）坐在地上不適合女性，而不是男性？為什麼基於傳統中國與日本醫學思想的 ＂受寒＂觀念， 在２０世紀只注焦在女性身體健康？到底是健康議題影響著動作與禮儀， 仰或是後者影響著前者？雖然當代日本社會十分重視傳統醫學, 我們仍不容易充分掌握禮儀､性別､與健康這些觀念中的歷史與文化因素。本研究把身體看成是體現歷史與文化理想的一個 ＂器＂， 這些理想塑造了身體的禮儀和訓誡行為。研究的目的在分析這些行為以便更清楚地了解禮儀､性別､與健康這些概念如何建構＂日本女人＂ 的這個民族身分。

17407214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17407214.value: The English rule of law is central to the history of colonial Hong Kong. Traditional colonial histories conceptualized it as a civilizing mission to the colonized. Today, the rule of law is widely acknowledged in Hong Kong as a core value contributing to the city’s continued growth and prosperity. Current textbooks on Hong Kong’s legal system describe this famed rule of law and its ingredients, e.g., judicial autonomy and equality before the law, as intrinsic to the common-law system Hong Kong inherited. However, this widely held assumption among both legal professionals and the general public has been subjected to surprisingly little scrutiny. Few have asked how and when the rule of law evolved into its current shape, and even fewer have questioned whether and to what extent the rule of law today bears any relation to that practiced in the colonial past. The proposed study will constitute a historical study involving the Geographic Information System (GIS) and a book-length project considering how the rule of law was understood, discoursed, practiced and experienced in Hong Kong from 1900 to 1941 in a broader historical context connecting colonial Hong Kong, mainland China and the operations of the British Far East. Interdisciplinary in nature, drawing on expertise in law, history and geography, the study will construct a long-overdue empirical legal history of Hong Kong and add to emerging scholarship in the global and comparative study of law and colonialism. Its results will enrich the academic discourse on the relationship between the rule of law and post-colonial governance in present-day Hong Kong. The study’s significance lies in the richness of the unexplored archived historical and spatial data of which it will make use. These data promise to inform us of how the understanding, discourse, practice and experience of the rule of law were contingent upon the political, economic, social and ideological developments occurring outside the realm of legal doctrine. The working hypothesis is that 1900s-1940s Hong Kong conformed to a pragmatic rule of law that was a much watered-down version of the English idealized notion. Another hypothesis is that the grassroots Chinese population did not treat this pragmatic rule of law as an important enabler of prosperity and stability in their daily lives; rather, the avoidance of contact with it may have bettered their economic and social well-being. The anticipated outcome of this study includes international refereed journal articles, an online GIS dataset and a book manuscript. 英式法治過去一向被有關香港近代史的主要論著認為是重要的殖民遺產。至今普遍香港社會大眾亦認同英式法治乃香港多年來發展和成功的核心因素。今天的法律課本仍會說司法獨立和法律面前人人平等是香港實施的英式法治的本質。很少人會嘗試質疑大家今天享受和重視的法治和在殖民時代香港的法治本質是否一樣。如果不是，原因何在？近年很多論著都挑戰前英國殖民地法治上的正義性，包括印度，澳洲和美洲等。而香港殖民地法治的修正歷史，仍有待開展。 本研究旨在透過收集1900-1941年香港的歷史檔案資料，去了解20世紀初香港的法治情況，特別是有關司法獨立和法律面前人人平等的原則是如何在當時表述和執行，以及一般市民如何感受和認知當時的法治。本研究會採用跨學科的研究方法，使用法學，歷史學和地理學的方法去分析資料，試圖追蹤20世紀初香港的法治在時間和空間上如何因英帝國在遠東的形勢和中國的政治環境而變遷。 本研究的重要性在於其檔案資料之豐富，和空間數據之運用。本研究的結果相信可以使我們更了解英式法治的表述和執行是如何可以因應政治，經濟，社會和意識形態而改變。本研究認為，透過分析檔案資料，我們會知道在1900-1941年間，法治並不披香港一般市民認為是香港賴以成功的核心價值。反而，對老百姓來說，避開法治才是生存之道。因為當時在香港實施的法治和英式法治聲稱的理想差距太遠。

17407214.label: Realisation of objectives
17407214.value: Objective (1) The project aims at challenging the prevailing narrative that English rule of law, which offers values that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today such as freedom of expression and judicial independence, is the most important legacy of British rule in Hong Kong, a legacy that is very often used to distinguish the legal and societal development of Hong Kong from that of mainland China. Drawing on unexplored archival materials this study successfully challenges such widely accepted narrative and reconstructs it. The study results show that the aforementioned conventional narrative does not stand up to the scrutiny of archival study. During the study, unexplored archival sources were found in Hong Kong Public Records Office, Special Collections of HKU Library, and The National Archives at Kew, the U.K. Information and documents for comparative purposes were also found from archives at Shanghai, Beijing, Singapore and Taipei. Archival materials discovered include correspondences of colonial office, foreign office, parliamentary documents, newspaper reports, historical laws and regulations, Hong Kong Hansard, Hong Kong Government Gazette, etc. Given the time constraint, the study focuses on high-profile cases where freedom of expression was suppressed and judicial independence denied to substantiate our arguments. By revealing how the press were continually and systematically monitored, pervasively censored, and regularly prosecuted and convicted and how students participating in peaceful assembly were arrested and prosecuted through the collaborative efforts of executive actions, legislative provisions and judicial decisions, the study shows that such purported safeguards of English law as equality before the law, freedom of expression and judicial autonomy to have remained subordinate to sovereignty, state power and geopolitics during at least the first one hundred years of Hong Kong’s colonial period (1850s -1940s). The project exceeds the historical period covered in the proposal by studying archival materials dated back from 1850s in order to get a coherent picture. Any discussion of the rule of law in Hong Kong needs to be situated in an informed understanding of this history. We further hypothesize that the rule of law that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today is more a ‘legacy’ of the decolonisation process that began in the 1980s, as colonialism erected a kinder façade in the decolonisation stage. Such hypothesis will be verified by PI’s another funded GRF project as a continuation of this completed project. We believe that the project objective of constructing a new narrative on colonial justice system and rule of law in Hong Kong during the early 20th century has been met. Objective (2) Prior to this research, the historical directories and maps were archived in print and scattered across the Special Collections of the University of Hong Kong Library, the Hong Kong Public Records Offices and the National Archives at Kew. Because there was no base map available to geocode the historical directories, the researchers built the road network from scratch. A common challenge in base map development centers on data quality (e.g. postal addresses without no street number). Another challenge in geocoding historical data is to reconcile temporal inconsistencies in the database as the street geometry, name and number often change (e.g. Praya was renamed Des Veoux Road;). In this study, a street was updated by cross-referencing from the data sources as well as auxiliary data (e.g. Google Maps and archived photographs). Using the detailed road network, historical directories were geocoded throughout 1900-1941. Not only the spatial locations were mapped precisely at the street level, the attributes for each business entity, including the Chinese and English company name and business description were entered. For analytical purposes, the researchers also added values to the historical directories by assigning business affiliation (e.g. engineers), generic categories (e.g. professionals) and functional units (e.g. economical). However, the mix of Chinese and English in the directory, the heterogeneous content and unstructured formatting yielded modest success in Optical Character Recognition. Eventually, a manual data entry approach to compile the directories in spreadsheets was adopted and internally cross-referenced multiple times to ensure data quality. In this research, considerable effort has been devoted to conducting quality assurance on the base maps and geocoded directories. Hence, this research developed a historical GIS database of HK Island consisting of detailed road network over time as well as a series of point layers representing the archived business directories during 1900-1941. The GIS database can benefit future researchers in, for example, Hong Kong history, colonial urban history, business and legal history of early 20th century Asia as the historical base maps are suitable for geocoding other datasets. The consolidated and value-added business directories also provide a unique lens to understand the legal and urban landscape during the colonial period. Although Kowloon Peninsula and the New Territories were not included in the final study due to the difficulty in finding an appropriate map with suitable scale and street details, it does not affect our study as there is no legal business located in Kowloon and the New Territories during the period under study. We believe that the objective of this study in developing a digital GIS database of historical information on the legal and urban development has largely been achieved. This important research infrastructure in the form of a unique historical GIS database about urban Hong Kong is now archived at HKU Library and will be made available online for researchers’ free access in due course when online user interface is built by the HKU Library. Objective (3) A key to understand a place is to explore the geographies of population, physical environments, socioeconomic entities and their interaction over time and space. This project explored their spatiotemporal relationships of generic business categories within legal, social, economic and political functional units over time using both parametric and non-parametric methods. First, the spatial distribution of the geocoded businesses was analyzed using mean center and standard deviational ellipse, which indicates the directional distribution and the overall compactness of a set of point locations over time. Besides the descriptive spatial statistics, this study derived the kernel density estimation (KDE) for each functional unit to quantify their spatial density within a kernel. In this study, with reference to PI’s previous findings on lawyering in Republican Beijing during the period from the 1910s to 1930s, the spatial density (i.e. KDE) of lawyers representing the legal functional unit is the dependent variable whereas the KDE of other functional units are independent variables. The parametric analysis adopted a two-step approach, first using exploratory regression then Ordinary Least Square regression, to explore and validate the multivariate relationships. A major challenge of spatiotemporal analysis was to the uncertainties of the geocoded directories and their error propagation due to, for instance, change of street names. After cross-referencing with other historical records, this study updated the street names and assumed the same distribution of street numbers along the corresponding segments for geocoding purposes. This may affect the reliability of subsequent spatial analysis and introduce uncertainties to the interpretation of results. Nevertheless, this study achieved its objective by demonstrating the use of non-parametric spatial data mining to cross-examine the multivariate relationships and analyzing the spatial patterns of legal changes and their underlying factors in Hong Kong (1900-1941), with reference to PI’s previous findings on Republican Beijing.

17407214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17407214.value: The project revises the prevailing narratives that English rule of law, which offers values that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today such as freedom of expression and judicial independence, is the most important legacy of British rule in Hong Kong. The research outcome shows that such purported safeguards of English law as equality before the law, freedom of expression and judicial autonomy to have remained subordinate to sovereignty, state power and geopolitics during most of Hong Kong’s colonial era. Any discussion of the rule of law in Hong Kong needs to be situated in an informed understanding of this history. (Ng 2016 and Ng 2017 in Part C) Through building an unprecedented historical GIS database of Hong Kong Island from 1900-1941, we found a close significant spatial correlation between legal firms and commercial establishments such as shipping firms and banks, and social clubs in Hong Kong. Commercial firm (COM) was the only category that consistently reported by both regression and local entropy map to have significant correlations with lawyers (LAW) during the 1900-1930 period. As an infant capitalistic market economy, the intimate spatial associations between COM and LAW brought together the catalysts needed to bridge the capital providers and consumers in a financial system. The growing importance of legal services was affirmed by the dominant array of economic functional units to be correlated with lawyers in 1930. This finding supports the previous postulation that legal practitioners were more keen on engaging the commercial firms operated mostly by Europeans than representing the general public - the majority Chinese population, a trend that was also found in Republican China of the same period (Ng et al. 2016 in Part C). These relationships were consistently supported by the regression analysis and the local entropy map. It was also interesting to observe significant relationships between LAW and some social units like social clubs in 1910 and 1930. These findings resonate with some narratives that clubs and associations were important venues for European businessmen and elites to socialize formally and informally for business or pleasure. (Chow et al. 2018 in Part C)

17407214.value: From the research outcomes of this project, we further hypothesize that the rule of law that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today is more a ‘legacy’ of the decolonisation process that began in the 1980s, as colonialism erected a kinder façade in the decolonisation stage. Such hypothesis will be tested by PI’s another funded GRF project as a continuation of this completed project to study the history of rule of law in colonial Hong Kong through the lens of media censorship practiced by Hong Kong colonial government from the 1850s to 1980s.

17407214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17407214.value: This inter-disciplinary research project studied the legal history of Hong Kong (1900s - 1940s) through examining unexplored archival materials and a historical geographic information system (GIS) database built from scratch. It revises conventional perception that English rule of law, which offers values that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today such as freedom of expression and judicial independence, is the most important legacy of British rule in Hong Kong. The research outcome shows that such purported safeguards of English law as equality before the law, freedom of expression and judicial autonomy to have remained subordinate to sovereignty, state power and geopolitics during most of Hong Kong’s colonial era. Any discussion of the rule of law in Hong Kong needs to be situated in an informed understanding of this history. Through building an unprecedented historical GIS database of Hong Kong Island from 1900-1941, we found a close significant spatial correlation between legal firms and commercial establishments such as shipping firms, banks, and social clubs in Hong Kong. This finding supports the postulation that legal practitioners were more keen on engaging the commercial firms operated mostly by Europeans than representing the general public. Another significant contribution of this project is the unique historical GIS database of urban Hong Kong based upon archived business directories built by the project team. The database, now archived by HKU Library, can benefit future researchers in, for example, Hong Kong history, colonial urban history, business and legal history of early 20th century Asia as the historical base maps are suitable for geocoding other datasets.

17407414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17407414.value: 提升年青人的金融素養

17407414.label: Project Objectives
17407414.value: To characterise financial literacy among young people. To identify theory-grounded and evidence-based pedagogical principles to enhance financial literacy in schools. To critically examine the nature of domain-specific “learning-to-learn” effects.
rows: To characterise financial literacy among young people.
To identify theory-grounded and evidence-based pedagogical principles to enhance financial literacy in schools.
To critically examine the nature of domain-specific “learning-to-learn” effects.

17407414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17407414.value: Aside from being pertinent to the financial stability and development of economies, financial literacy is regarded as an essential life skill for young people that enables them to participate in modern society. National surveys, however, have consistently revealed that young people have amongst the lowest levels of financial literacy. Increasingly more economies, including Hong Kong, are recognising the importance of financial literacy and are developing financial education programmes for schoolchildren. To formulate a successful economy-wide policy on financial education for young people, it is important to develop a deeper understanding of whether financial education in schools is effective and study how it works in the classroom, which is currently not well understood. Although many studies have evaluated the efficacy of financial education programmes, few have critically examined what actually happens in the classroom, which is vital to the development of financial literacy. In particular, there has been no systematic investigation of how teachers handle financial education content in such a way that it enhances students’ financial literacy. The proposed project will aim to fill this research gap. By drawing upon the classroom teaching and learning data collected in our previous project on financial literacy (funded by the Hong Kong Research Grants Council), we plan to identify pedagogical principles that are critical to the development of financial literacy, and to validate, modify and/or refine these principles through design experimentation. We want to find out what is needed for success; specifically, what aspects of teaching and learning in the classroom are critical not only for better learning, but also for better continued learning in the context of financial literacy. To identify those theoretically grounded, evidence-based pedagogical principles, the proposed study will be carried out in two stages. Stage One: We will identify the pedagogical principles by conducting secondary analysis of existing data from our previous project in two steps. First, pronounced differences between classes in terms of student learning outcomes will be identified. Second, the variation theory of learning will be used as the analytical framework for relating variations in what the students learned to variations in the conditions of learning, in the sense of how the object of learning (financial literacy in this case) was dealt with in different classes. Stage Two: We will collect new evidence about the efficacy of these pedagogical principles through experimentation. The principles will be validated, modified and/or refined after each cycle of design experimentation. 金融素養除了與金融穩定性和經濟發展息息相關之外， 更被視為現代社會的年青人不可或缺的基本生活技能。然而，調查顯示年青人的金融素養水平一直是社會上最低的一群。越來越多的經濟體系(包括香港)都意識到金融素養的重要性，並正積極推動學校的理財教育。 要制定政策有效地幫助年青人提升金融素養，我們首先要深入了解學校如何推行理財教育及檢視其有效性，目前我們在這方面的研究仍有不足。雖然很多研究對一些理財教育項目的有效性作出評估，但是很少研究對理財教育課堂上的學與教進行仔細分析。值得留意的是，我們一直沒有進行有系統性的研究去調查教師如何處理理財教育課程的內容，以有效提升學生的金融素養。 這項目旨在填補這一研究缺口。我們計劃利用我們之前由香港研究資助局資助的項目所收集得來的理財教育課堂上的學與教資料，找出一些對提升金融素養最為重要的教學原則，並透過「設計實驗」去驗證、修改和/或優化這些原則。我們希望能夠找到達至成功學習的關鍵; 並找到哪些教學原則對提升金融素養最為有效，不僅為學習金融知識，更重要的是幫助年青人學會學習。 為了找出及驗證這些建基於理論和實證的有效教學原則，這研究項目將分兩個階段進行。 第一階段：我們將對之前的研究項目所收集得來的學與教資料進行深入分析，從而找出上文所提及的教學原則。我們首先識別在學習成果方面有明顯差異的班別。之後，我們運用「變易理論」去分析不同的學習條件如何導致學生有不同的學習成果，重點分析在不同的課堂上老師如何處理理財教育課程的內容，以提升學生的金融素養。 第二階段：我們將透過「設計實驗」檢視這些教學原則的有效性。這些原則將在「設計實驗」的過程中將被驗證、修改和/或優化。

17407414.label: Realisation of objectives
17407414.value: All the three objectives of the project have been fully achieved. Objective 1: To characterise financial literacy among young people Financial literacy is characterised as “the capability to make use of the core economic concepts learned, to make well-reasoned financial decisions in novel situations through focusing on, or taking into account, intertwined critical aspects of the financial situation” (Pang, 2010, p.662). Unlike the practical and piecemeal approach frequently adopted to equip people with the knowledge necessary to manage their financial assets, the study proposes a conceptual approach, in the sense that “by helping students develop a good grasp of certain core economic concepts related to critical aspects that they need to take into account when dealing with financial matters, they will have a better chance of understanding financial phenomena and thus make more effective financial decisions” (Pang, 2010, p.662). This study shows that the conceptual approach to developing generative learning in the domain of financial literacy, which is grounded in the two pedagogical principles derived from the variation theory, is effective to empowering students to see the financial world in a new light, i.e. from an undifferentiated world to a more differentiated one. The systematic use of the pattern of ‘contrast-fusion-generalization’ to deal with the individual core economic concepts can help students lay a solid conceptual foundation for developing generative learning. Furthermore, with the use of the meta-level pattern of ‘contrast-fusion-generalization’ through complex everyday financial situations which transcend the specific concepts, students can make effective use of the core economic concepts learned and transform them organically into one’s analytical framework. This enables students to discern the critical aspects of novel financial situations and have a greater likelihood of making well-reasoned and sound financial decisions. Objective 2: To identify theory-grounded and evidence-based pedagogical principles to enhance financial literacy in schools Based on our analysis of the previous study, two pedagogical principles, which are critical to developing students’ generative learning in the domain of financial literacy, were identified. The first one is the systematic use of variation in the critical aspects of the core economic concepts, through carefully designed tasks, examples and so on. In the course of analysing the enacted object of learning of the target group and that of the comparison group, the patterns of variation and invariance enacted were found to be quite different. For the target group, the teachers juxtaposed systems of examples and tasks to introduce systematic variation in the dimensions of variation which correspond to the critical aspects of the core concepts, while other critical aspects were kept invariant. With the use of the pattern of ‘contrast’, the teachers successfully directed students’ focal awareness to each of the critical aspects of individual concept separately, before employing the pattern of ‘fusion’ to bring the various critical aspects of the concept back together. Afterwards, the pattern of ‘generalization’ was used to help students generalize the concept from one instance or context to another. The pattern of ‘contrast-fusion-generalization’ created by the teachers can support students’ learning of the core economic concepts by helping the learners first discern each of the critical aspects and subsequently see the inter-relationships between the various critical aspects of the economic concept in question. The second pedagogical principle was the use of some complex everyday financial situations which transcend the specific concepts. The provision of capstone, ill-defined problems offers a chance for the learners to fuse and synthesize the various core economic concepts learned to develop an analytical framework or ‘lens’ which can assist them to discover the critical aspects in the new contexts and handle the novel problems or situations from the perspective of the economics discipline. In some instances, the core concepts may contest with each other and point to different critical aspects of the novel problems or situations to be dealt with and the students need to thoughtfully apply and integrate the various concepts learned. This pattern of variation and invariance can be seen as a kind of ‘meta-fusion’, in the sense that it fuses the various inter-related economic concepts learned to form the analytical framework. At the same time, the introduction of variation in the financial situations as found in the different novel tasks was to help students generalize the analytical framework to different contexts, which belongs to a kind of ‘meta-generalization’. In the course of doing so, the students need to contrast the different novel situations to identify their critical differences and thus the corresponding critical aspects, which can be seen as a kind of ‘meta-contrast’. This meta-level pattern of ‘contrast-fusion-generalization’ seems to be conducive to the development of generative learning. Objective 3. To critically examine the nature of domain-specific "learning-to-learn" effects The mechanism of enhancing generative learning resembles the experience of a person who learns how to make use of her new pair of glasses with progressive lens. In the process of an eye examination, the optician would firstly put one kind of lens (i.e. a core concept), say for her shortsightedness (with varying degrees) whilst keeping other lens invariant. Next, another kind of lens (i.e. another core concept), say for her long-sightedness (with varying degrees) would be added. Subsequently, another kind of lens (i.e. another core concept), say for her astigmatism (with varying degrees) would also be added. The process continues until all the required lens needed to provide the person with good eyesight (i.e. a powerful way of seeing the phenomenon in question) are included. The different kinds of lens are similar to the different core economic concepts in nature, which need to be contrasted, fused and generalized so that the learners can be empowered to discern and attend to the critical aspects of novel situations and develop a more powerful way of seeing and acting. However, although the progressive lens are very powerful, a person may not be able to effectively use the new glasses to see the world better when they are first worn because one may not be familiar with how to use them. She needs to come across various learning instances or situations, through which she can learn when and how to use the different parts of the progressive lens tactfully, say during driving, working with a computer or reading a book. ‘Generative learning’ takes place through a learner’s lived experience with different novel situations. Within these situations, she develops a better understanding of the salient features of the powerful progressive lens itself as well as enhancing her capability to discern the critical aspects of the novel situations that she encounters. Hopefully, one day it becomes a reflexive action for her to make effective use of the progressive lens to see the ever-changing world more powerfully. This supports the notion of educative experience advocated by Dewey (1972), in which one’s new experience of exploring a novel ill-defined financial situation is a continuity of one’s experience of exploring an earlier ill-defined situation, which has a similar goal or purpose. Simultaneously, one’s new experience with a novel financial situation also brings in variation to one’s earlier experience, which helps to open up the learner’s mind to new possibilities. In the end, this kind of educative experience enhances the capability of the learners to discern the critical aspects of novel situations, and ultimately fosters the development of generative learning.

17407414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17407414.value: Based on our analysis, two pedagogical principles derived from the variation theory of learning, which are critical to developing students’ generative learning in the domain of financial literacy, were identified. The first pedagogical principle is the systematic use of the pattern of variation and invariance in the critical aspects of the core economic concepts, through carefully designed tasks, examples and so on when dealing with the individual core economic concepts identified. This can help students lay a solid conceptual foundation for developing generative learning. The pattern of ‘contrast-fusion-generalization’ created by the teachers can support students’ learning of the core economic concepts by helping the learners first discern each of the critical aspects and subsequently see the inter-relationships between the various critical aspects of the economic concept in question. The second pedagogical principle is the systematic use of the ‘meta-level’ pattern of variation and invariance through complex everyday financial situations which transcend the specific concepts. This can help students make effective use of the core economic concepts learned and transform them organically into one’s analytical framework to identify the critical aspects of novel financial situations. Each of the economic concepts serves as a kind of ‘lens’, which helps challenge some specific ‘natural attitudes’ of the learners and focus on certain critical aspects of the situation. Furthermore, the integration and synthesis of the individual core concepts further helps the learners see the intricacies and dynamics between different critical aspects of the novel financial situation and conceptualise it in a more sophisticated way. The more opportunities the learners take to make use of the analytical framework to deal with ill-defined financial situations or problems, the more opportunities the learners create to develop a deeper understanding of the various core concepts, and ultimately sharpen the analytical framework. In the end, this kind of educative experience (Dewey, 1972) enhances the capability of the learners to discern the critical aspects of novel situations, and ultimately fosters the development of generative learning. This study shows that the conceptual approach grounded in the two pedagogical principles derived from the variation theory is effective to empowering students to see the financial world in a new light, i.e. from an undifferentiated world to a more differentiated one. This enables students to discern and focus upon the critical aspects of novel financial situations that they may not have discerned before and have a greater likelihood of making well-reasoned and sound financial decisions.

17407414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17407414.value: The research project will generate further impact to the Hong Kong society by putting forward a knowledge exchange project application with Quality Education Fund of the Hong Kong Education Bureau in the near future. The overarching aim of the proposed project is to develop the financial literacy of young students who come from underpriviledged families in Hong Kong through the organisation of appropriate financial education courses whose design is based on the pedagogical principles identified and validated in the current research project.

17407414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17407414.value: Two pedagogical principles are found to be critical to developing students’ generative learning in the domain of financial literacy. The first pedagogical principle is the systematic use of the pattern of variation and invariance in the critical aspects of the core economic concepts identified, through carefully designed tasks, examples and so on. This can help students lay a solid conceptual foundation for developing their ‘learning to learn’ capability in a domain-specific manner. The second principle is the systematic use of the meta-level pattern of variation and invariance through complex everyday financial situations which transcend the specific concepts. Within these situations, students can make effective use of the core economic concepts learned and transform them organically into one’s analytical framework. This enables students to discern the critical aspects of novel financial situations and have a greater likelihood of making well-reasoned and sound financial decisions. One of the most important functions of learning in school is to enable students to be better learners in the future, seeing the world and handling novel situations more powerfully. This study shows that the conceptual approach grounded in these two pedagogical principles is effective to empowering students to see the financial world in a new light.

17407714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17407714.value: 墨家學說與中國哲學的起源

17407714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17407714.value: This project will investigate the central role the Mohists played in the rise of philosophical discourse in China's Warring States period (5th century BCE to 221 BCE). Its motivating hypothesis is that by the last century of this period a philosophical discourse had arisen that had been provoked by the Mohists and derived some of its most fundamental and distinctive features from them. The Mohists were a philosophical and social movement that began in the 5th century BCE and remained active through the Warring States period. They seem to have been the first Chinese philosophers to develop extended written arguments in favour of their views, to recognise a need to respond to objections, and to develop philosophical accounts of the basis of their arguments. One could say that they were the first to engage in a particular sort of philosophy. Previous work by the investigator concludes that they did not do so in response to an existing philosophical discourse. That conclusion raises three questions that this project will try to answer. First, what led the Mohists to place such weight on argumentation? Second, to what extent is it because of their work that later philosophers such as Mencius and Xunzi began engaging in similar philosophical activities? And third, granted that it was significantly because of their work, how if at all was the resulting philosophical discourse shaped by Mohist arguments and by Mohist accounts of argumentation? This project will attempt to answer these questions with an account of the rise of philosophical discourse in early China. Texts from the last century of the Warring States period attest to the existence of a discourse in which philosophers addressed one another, rather than just the court, their own followers, or a general literate public. In doing so, they adopted Mohist ideas about language and argumentation, Mohist argumentative strategies, and even certain Mohist moral values. For example, the project will argue that the tendency to discuss reasoning and argumentation in terms of such concepts as shi-fei 是非 (this/not-this), bian 辯 (distinctions), and fa 法 (models, standards), and the tendency to defend moral and political claims with pragmatic or consequentialist arguments, reflect not ahistorical cultural or linguistic dispositions but rather the specific influence of the Mohists. Further, the project will argue that this was not because of the Mohists' direct influence on particular later philosophers, but that their influence was mediated by the philosophical discourse they helped provoke. 本計劃研究墨家學說於中國戰國時期(公元前五世紀至公元前二二一年)哲學話語開展中扮演的角色。本計劃由一個假說推動,此即戰國時期最後一世紀的話語及其一些基本特徵是由墨家學說引發而起。 墨家學派是一個始於公元前五世紀的哲學及社會運動,並持續至戰國時期的終結。墨家學說似乎是中國哲學上最先以論證作為論述方式以支持自家觀點的學派。此學說承認了反駁異議的需要,並哲學地解釋了他們論證的基礎。我們甚至可說此是整個哲學史上最先從事論證分析的學派。 以前的研究認為墨家學說關於論證的分析是獨立於當時的哲學話語,故此本計劃會嘗試回答以下三個問題:一,什麼因素令墨家學說如此重視論證?二,此學說那程度上影響了後來的孟子和荀子而使得他們皆關心論證?三,假定墨家學說的確有顯著影響,墨家學說中的論證及其關於論證的解釋如何塑造了之後的哲學話語? 本計劃藉解釋當時哲學話語的起源以回答上述三個問題。戰國時期最後一世紀的文本證實了當時哲學話語中,各學派不僅處理君臣,識字的民眾和自家學派當中的觀點,更有處理別家學派的觀點。這現象顯示其他學派接受了墨家學說關於語言和論證的觀念,並接受了他們的論證技巧,甚至道德價值觀。舉例而言,往後學說傾向以「是非」、「辯」和「法」等概念提出理由和論證,亦傾向以實用和後果論式的論證支持道德和政治上的主張,本計劃將論證這些傾向反映了他們皆受到墨家學說的影響,而非一個獨立於歴史的文化或語言傾向。本計劃會進一步論證墨家學說並非直接地影響了一些特定的學說,墨家學說的影響是藉由他們所激發而起的整個哲學話語而傳遞。

17407914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17407914.value: Locomotion is a basic sensory-motor task that utilizes a variety of visual and nonvisual sources of information. An important visual source of information is optic flow - the pattern of visual motion produced when moving through an environment. During walking, information about self-motion is also provided by vestibular, proprioceptive, and motor cues. A previous GRF-funded project investigated how optic flow is used to predict one’s path of movement, and how visual and nonvisual information are used to guide walking to a goal. This project will investigate how information about self-motion is integrated over time for spatial updating and visual-motor calibration. Spatial updating is the ability to perceive the changing position of one’s self relative to objects and landmarks while moving through an environment. Previous studies of spatial updating have focused on ability to navigate without vision, or the ability to integrate optic flow and nonvisual information to perceive distance traveled. This project will test the relative contributions of visual and nonvisual information to spatial updating, for both direction and distance components of self-motion. Control of locomotion involves anticipating one's future course of movement to make online correlations, while spatial updating involves tracking the consequences of past actions. These tasks might therefore integrate information about self-motion in different ways. This project will test spatial updating in various conditions that have previously been used to investigate perception of instantaneous self-motion and use of visual information for online control of locomotion. Use of optic flow for spatial updating can then be directly compared to use of optic flow for these other tasks. Visual feedback about self-motion is important for maintaining calibration of visual-motor systems. This project will also investigate this process. The proposed studies will test how visual-motor adaptation can be modulated, and whether errors in spatial updating can drive visual-motor adaptation. 移動是一種基本的感知任務，完成該任務需使用各種視覺及非視覺的信息源。其中一種重要的信息源是光流（optic flow），即人在某一環境中行走時所產生的視覺特征。同時，在行走過程中，前庭系統，本體感覺以及運動線索也可以提供關於本體移動的信息。 之前本人所申請的一項GRF基金項目被用於研究如何使用光流來預測個人的運動軌跡，以及視覺信息和非視覺信息是如何被用於導引被試走向一個特定目標的任務。本項目將用於研究與自身運動相關的信息是如何隨著時間變化而整合，以用於空間信息更新和視覺-運動校正。 空間信息更新是指在特定空間中行走時，個人知覺自身相對於物體和地標的位置變換的能力。之前關於空間信息更新的研究關註於在沒有視覺信息的情況下的導航能力，及光流信息和非視覺信息如何被整合用於知覺之前移動的距離。本計劃將檢測視覺及非視覺信息對於空間信息更新的相對貢獻，這裏的空間信息更新包括對自身運動方向和距離的更新。 移動控制涉及到如何預測個體之後的運動過程，並以此進行即時的調整；同時空間信息更新涉及如何追蹤之前各種動作的結果。因此這兩種任務可能通過不同的方式整合了自身運動的信息。本計劃將研究不同條件下的空間信息更新，這些條件之前都被用來研究對瞬間的自身運動的知覺以及個體如何使用視覺信息來即時控制自身的移動。個人在完成空間信息更新時對光流信息的使用可以與其在上述這些任務中對光流信息的使用做比較。 對自身運動的視覺信息反饋對於維持視覺-運動系統的校正是非常重要的。本計劃也將研究這一過程。這些計劃中的研究將用於探測視覺-運動適應是如何被調整的，以及空間信息更新中的錯誤能否引起視覺-運動適應。

17407914.label: Realisation of objectives
17407914.value: The research we conducted was related to the general problem of using vision to navigate and learn spatial layout, but diverged considerably from the original plan. In response to some practical difficulties, our initial studies investigated related questions using methods that did not require extensive physical movement in VR. The directions of research further diverged as we responded to interesting findings from initial studies, and the research interests of the PhD students being trained. The mid-term report describes three completed studies on visual and nonvisual contributions to spatial perception (objective 1), visual-motor adaptation and transfer (objective 4), and visual perception of self-motion from optic flow. We have since continued the adaptation research, and performed new studies of visual and nonvisual influences on spatial learning. We did not address objectives 2 and 3 from the original research plan. The study on flow parsing during walking (VSS, 2016a) investigates a question closely related to objective 1. The results provide evidence that visual and nonvisual information are integrated in a similar way for perception of external space (motion of an object relative to the environment) and for control of walking direction. We developed a novel method and analysis to compare performance in the two tasks, which could potentially be applied in other contexts. A manuscript reporting this research is in late stage of preparation. The study on center bias in perception of heading from optic flow (VSS, 2016b) does not directly address the proposed objectives, but is related in that it investigated integration of visual and nonvisual cues for perception of self-motion. In this case, the hypothesized nonvisual influence is a Bayesian prior. The results from three experiments yielded interpretable results, consistent with a Bayesian model, and a manuscript is in preparation. For the research on visual-motor adaptation, we came up with a novel method to distinguish different possible types of adaptation and their time courses. This was not part of the proposed studies, but we thought that it was an interesting research direction, and was less constrained by equipment and space. Initial results were reported at VSS in 2017, and were the basis for an MPhil thesis. An interesting finding emerged from follow-up studies: different patterns of generalization for fast/transient and slow/gradual adaptation. These new findings were presented at the Society for Neuroscience meeting in 2018, and we submitted a manuscript to the Journal of Neurophysiology in 2019. The manuscript was rejected, but the reviewer comments were generally favorable, and we believe that a revised manuscript will be publishable in another journal. New research led by my PhD students has studied learning spatial layout on a larger scale (a cognitive map) from simulated self-motion through a virtual environment. I originally planned to investigate the influence of self-motion cues on space perception at a smaller scale, but we ran into difficulty implementing the planned studies, and the students developed some good ideas for alternative research directions. One current study tests for the influence of non-spatial properties on the judgments of spatial layout learned from navigation. Inspired by neurophysiological evidence that space and events are jointly encoded, my PhD student hypothesized that judgments about the layout of a learned environment could be influenced by cues that are unrelated to space and self-motion. We developed a novel method using virtual reality to test this possibility, and found evidence that non-spatial similarity of the experience at locations can bias perception of spatial distance. Results have been presented at the Society of Neuroscience (2019), and will be the basis for her PhD thesis, and an eventual publication. Another current study tests whether learning a spatial layout by navigating in a virtual environment can be facilitated by providing spatial information in the format of a top-down map. This was inspired by recent theories and evidence suggesting that spatial knowledge of allocentric relationships may not be encoded in a map-like manner. We conducted three experiments using a novel paradigm and found surprisingly little influence of map viewing. Results were reported at VSS in 2019, and a manuscript is in preparation. Although the studies conducted for this project have resulted in multiple conference presentations, they have not yet been published in academic journals. One reason for the delay in publishing this work is that I have still been completing manuscripts from previous GRF projects. We recently published a paper reporting research from my 2012-14 GRF project on visual control of grasping (Chen & Saunders, 2018), and a paper reporting research from my 2013-15 GRF project on integration of 3D cues (Chen & Saunders, 2019). Another manuscript currently under review reports research that follows up my 2011-2013 GRF project. In addition, the PhD students involved with the project have been completing their theses, both due this year. During the next year, completing manuscripts from this project will be prioritized.

17407914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17407914.value: The studies conducted for this project have been presented at academic conferences, and have been the basis for a MPhil thesis and two expected PhD theses. We believe that we have obtained enough interpretable results for 3-4 publications in good academic journals. Some notable findings: Visual and nonvisual cues to self-motion are used in a consistent way for the tasks of controlling self-motion and perceiving of the movement of objects relative to an environment. Distinguishing visual motion due to moving objects and self-motion (flow parsing) could potentially be based solely on optic flow. However, we found that nonvisual information available during walking also influenced perception of object motion, and there were correlated effects on the two tasks. This suggests that a common internal representation of self-motion, which integrates visual and nonvisual cues, is used for both visually-guided navigation and spatial updating. Center biases in judgments of heading direction from optic flow vary with the quality of optic flow information in the manner that is consistent with a Bayesian model. Although center bias has been reported in many studies of heading perception, it had not been systematically investigated in any previous studies. A Bayesian explanation is that optic flow information is combined with a prior expectation of motion in a forward direction. We measured reliability and center biases in heading judgments and found that they co-varied in the expected way. Visual-motor adaptation occurs at multiple sites that differ in temporal dynamics. We tested transfer of adaptation across conditions that differed in functional task, motor actions, or both. We also used a novel method of measuring the temporal dynamics of adaptation and transfer. We observed both motor-specific and generalized transfer of adaptation, but the motor-specific adaptation was slower and gradual while the general adaptation was faster and transient. Simultaneous adaptation at multiple sites with different time courses might explain some conflicting findings in previous studies. Non-spatial similarity can affect judgments about spatial layout of environments learned through navigation. Neurophysiological evidence suggests that such interactions could occur, but there have been few attempts to test this prediction behaviorally in humans. We developed a paradigm to experimentally test for non-spatial influences on spatial judgments, and observed some detectable effects.

17407914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17407914.value: One priority for follow-up is simply to publish the main findings. There are also a number of promising directions for further research. The novel method and analysis developed for our flow parsing study could be applied to investigate the roles of vision and nonvisual cues in spatial updating. The main innovation was testing for correlated trial-to-trial variations in performance of two simultaneous tasks. This could similarly be used to test for interdependence between locomotion control and spatial updating. We also developed an innovative method for our adaptation studies that allows sensitive measurement of the time course of adaptation and transfer. This could be applied in other domains, or used to study implicit and explicit visual-motor learning. We now have a portable VR system that makes it more feasible to test walking in VR in a larger space. This was an obstacle to performing some of the proposed studies, which remain interesting and worth pursuing. Our study of the influence of map viewing on spatial learning from navigation has potential for further research. Manipulating map information provides a way to investigate how allocentric is integrated with egocentric information acquired during navigation.

17407914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17407914.value: The research used virtual reality to investigate how we use visual and nonvisual information to perceive our movement and the spatial layout of an environment. We tested how visual and nonvisual cues during walking contribute to two tasks: steering toward a target and distinguishing the visual motion caused by moving objects and our own movement. Results suggest that a common integrated percept of self-motion is used for both tasks. We investigated systematic biases in perception of heading direction from visual motion. Results were consistent with a Bayesian model that integrates visual information with a prior expectation of forward movement. Visual-motor adaptation occurs when we experience conflicting sensory information. We tested how adaptation generalizes across locomotion and pointing tasks. Results suggest that adaptation can occur at multiple sites, and that motor-specific adaptation is slower and more gradual that generalized adaptation. We investigated our ability to learn the layout of an environment though navigation. One study found that non-spatial similarity could affect spatial judgments, consistent with common neural mechanisms for space and events. Another study found that viewing a top-down map did not facilitate spatial learning, consistent with theories that spatial knowledge is not encoded in a map-like manner.

17408514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17408514.value: Research on developmental dyslexia has strongly demonstrated that deficits in processing speech sounds and phonology are closely related to reading disorders. Studies in Chinese have by and large obtained consistent findings, but also found ample evidence for poor morphological and orthographic awareness skills that may be specific to the Chinese orthography. Given the multiple predictors of poor reading, subtyping had been proposed, and led to the conclusion that there is weak evidence for phonological dyslexia, and as many as 7 subtypes can be found in Chinese. Sub typing shows that characteristics of dyslexia may vary across different languages. However, it is argued that it provides little insight to understanding core deficits of dyslexia and its heterogeneous nature. An alternative view relevant to developmental dyslexia is the lexical quality hypothesis (Perfetti & Hart 2002; Perfetti 2007). Dyslexic individuals may have weaker representations or lack of tight integration the three lexical constituents (orthography, phonology at the word and sub-word levels, and lexico-semantic) that consequently lead to poor reading. This framework does not focus on classifying particular subtypes of dyslexia per-se, but attempts to explain reading difficulties for each individual based on underlying deficits of the core constituents used during the typical reading process, and may more sufficiently capture the heterogeneous characteristics of deficits. The proposed project aims to take Perfetti’s approach to understand reading difficulties. Eighty primary grade four poor readers (dyslexics and dyslexics co-morbid with specific language impairment) and eighty chronologically age-matched typically developing control readers will participate in a series of behavioural tasks to assess their speed of processing, phonological, orthographic and morphological awareness skills. Electrophysiological measures will also be taken to investigate the children’s neurological pattern as they are engaged on tasks require orthographic, phonological and morphological processing. Using multiple single-case design the profile of performance on the behavioural and event-related potential (ERP) measures will be investigated to identify common patterns of atypical processing of the core lexical constituents across the poor readers, and correlate ERP indices of orthographic, phonological and semantic processing to the observed atypical behavioural profile. Two fundamental questions will be addressed from this work; (1) given the heterogeneous pattern manifested in children with reading difficulties, are there indeed different subtypes of developmental dyslexia in Chinese, and (2) can electrophysiological techniques capture the nature of reading difficulties in terms of atypical processing/and or integration of particular lexical constituents as proposed by the lexical quality hypothesis.

17408514.label: Realisation of objectives
17408514.value: The project has successfully disambiguated whether children with SLI and developmental dyslexia show a profile different from those with dyslexia only, established the relative dominance of certain profiles of deficits in performance in children with developmental dyslexia in Chinese, and determined the nature of abnormal lexical constituents and/or integration processing that contributes to difficulties in reading.

17408514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17408514.value: The outcomes of this project provide valuable data on various accounts of dyslexia largely based on research in alphabetic scripts, highlight the need to understand the heterogeneity of the deficits among dyslexics, and determine the potential of using ERPs to understanding the etiology of developmental dyslexia within a language-specific context. Our findings show that dyslexics in Chinese show several atypical neural activation during language processing. The first differences emerged at P100 component whereby a greater positivity was evoked for objects than characters for readers with dyslexia only. Normal readers develop sensitivity to well-formedness of object, whereby real-objects elicited a greater negativity than non-objects at N170, but not in dyslexic readers. At N400, dyslexic readers showed a frontal shift of sensitivity, whereby non-characters evoked a greater negativity than real-character, despite the similar effort required in both groups. When assessing ability to read aloud characters, children with dyslexia found it more difficult to read irregular characters. At the neural level, regular characters elicited greater positive P200 in both groups, but regularity effect at the N170 was only seen in controls, suggesting that children with dyslexia have reduced sensitivity to the extraction of phonological information from the orthographic forms. Stepwise regression analysis show that oral language ability, phonological awareness and sensitivity to regularity at the N170 predicted children’s reading ability. At the level of morphological processing, different topography and congruency pattern were observed in dyslexic and control group. At N400, both greater overall activation and orthographic similarity effect were observed in dyslexic group, and left lateralization pattern observed in control was absent in dyslexic group. P200 and N400 components measuring morphological sensitivity of semantic congruency and orthographic similarity contributed significant variance in predicting reading ability. The Time-frequency analyses showed that incongruent word pairs elicited greater theta power than congruent ones in the anterior sites for the control group, and absent in dyslexic readers despite eliciting larger theta power over the whole scalp. Taken together, the findings show that dyslexics in Chinese show atypical neural activation, particularly during phonological and morphological processing. More neural effort is needed to suppress the activation of unrelated word meanings that share similar sounds and words that look visually similar. Importantly, we also found that brain sensitivity to sub lexical phonology and morphology is associated and predicts reading skill, and that children with reading difficulties have a weak integration among word form, meaning access and the working memory

17408514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17408514.value: Developmental dyslexia is a major learning disability specifically related to reading. Much more effects are needed to understand its nature and to devise effective intervention programs. Given that our neural findings suggest weak phonological and morphological awareness in children with reading difficulties, developing effect intervention programs that aim to help children's identify, analyze and manipulate the structure of the phonology and morphemes. Furthermore analyses on the brain oscillations using time-frequency analysis at the theta frequency suggest a weak integration among orthographic form, lexical semantic functional networks and working memory in children with reading difficulties. Further work may look into other frequency bands such as the delta and alpha frequency, as well as the coupling of theta and gamma frequency that has been known to reflect cortical communication between local and distant regions of the brain in an ordered way. This would provide further evidence for our observations of weak integration in the language processing neural networks. The following articles are in the works aiming for publication: - Lau, D.K.Y., Law, S.P., & Su, I.F. “ERP markers of good and poor readers in Chinese.” - Su, I.F. & Petrova A. “Atypical theta activation in dyslexic during morphological processing.”

17408514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17408514.value: The outcomes of this project provide valuable cross-linguistic data that shed light on current accounts of developmental dyslexia largely based on research in alphabetic scripts, highlight the need to address and understand the heterogeneity of the deficits among developmental dyslexics, and determine the potential of using ERPs as a sensitive measure to understanding the etiology of developmental dyslexia within a language-specific context. Our findings show that dyslexics in Chinese show atypical neural activation during phonological and morphological processing. More neural effort is needed to suppress activation of unrelated word meanings that share similar sounds and words that look visually similar. Importantly, we also found that brain sensitivity to sub lexical phonology and morphology is associated with reading skill, and that there is a weak integration amongst word form, meaning access and the working memory.

17408714.label: Project Objectives
17408714.value: To understand the impact of mainlandization on the cultural identity politics of Hong Kong films in relation to the local, national, regional culture through a mix-methodology of industrial analysis coupled with content-textual-contextual analysis. To answer the question: what are the struggles and dilemmas filmmakers face in the choice between mainlandization and localization of film production and film content? To do micro-level qualitative research on different SAR New Wave film in comparison with Hong Kong New Wave/Second Wave films, focusing on their production-innovation networks, creative content development and collective innovation processes. These profiles will allow us to evaluate the sustainability of their industry and labor practices. Most research on film and creative industries in Hong Kong were based on macro-level policy analysis, which did not consider innovation capabilities, networks and institutional support for the industry. We fill this gap by providing thorough understanding of the dynamics of collective innovation (in contrast to individual creativity) in the film industry. We will do qualitative research that systematically interviews insiders, conducts focus group discussions and does participatory observation, because long-term and effective policy on creativity and creative talent cannot be created based on cursory information from surveys and fore de-contextualized opinions of foreign experts.

17408714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17408714.value: Deng’s “[neo]liberalization and reform” since the early 1980s attracted Hong Kong manufacturing north to mainland China. Hong Kong film production followed suit in the 2000s. A decade into this mainlandization process, the debate on whether Hong Kong film production has mainlandized is settled. We define “mainlandization” as a survival tactic to save what is left of the Hong Kong film industry after its long decline since the early 1990s. This tactic involves increasing co-productions between Hong Kong and mainland filmmakers, targeting the Chinese market. Today cross-border film co-production has become the dominant mode of Hong Kong film production—a shift from “made in Hong Kong” to “made by Hong Kong.” (Berger and Lester, 1997) The new question today, beyond whether to mainlandize or not, is how Hong Kong filmmakers can continue to make Hong Kong-style films with focus on local culture and sensitivities in the present condition of mainlandization and neoliberalization. We have coined the term “Hong Kong SAR New Wave” (SAR meaning Special Administrative Region) to name the collective effort of local filmmakers who are keeping this “minor mode of production” surviving and kicking (Szeto and Chen,2011, 2012, 2013) This new research investigates (1) to what extent is the trend of mainlandization a new opportunity for the revival of the Hong Kong film industry? (2) What are the impacts of mainlandization on the creativity of the industry and the creative cultural content of Hong Kong films? In other words, do Hong Kong films become more creative or vise versa in the process of mainlandization? How does mainlandization impact the cultural content and politics of Hong Kong films in relation to the local? We analyze the relation between macro-dynamics of the glocalization of neoliberalism and the micro-politics of local cultural responses, with particular focus on the different strategies of survival and creativity the Hong Kong SAR New Wave filmmakers demonstrate, in comparison with the strategies of the established Hong Kong New Wave/Second Wave. By studying the two scales of analysis relationally, we see how the material condition of Hong Kong cultural production is being shaped by both global neoliberal political-economy and specific translocal cultural conditions, and how their impact on the industry is articulated in film content. Integrating micro-level qualitative research and textual analysis we show how this is done in a collective innovation process, involving creative labor and production-innovation networks of Hong Kong-based film companies in the local, China, Asia, global contexts. 自80年代初鄧小平的新自由主義改革開放吸引了香港製造業北上 以來，香港電影製作也在2000年代隨著北上。這十年來香港電影 業是否正在「大陸化」的辯論已塵埃落定。我們定義「大陸化」 為一種生存策略，目的是挽救自90年代以來長期衰退的香港電影 業。這種策略包括大量增加中港合拍電影的比例，以瞄準中國市 場。今天，中港合拍片已成為香港電影製作模式的主流，而香港 電影也已經從「香港製造」轉為「港人製作」的生產模式了 （Berger和Lester，1997年）。新的問題是，香港電影人怎麼能 在「新自由主義化」與「大陸化」的壓力底下繼續拍有香港特色 的電影、保留對當地文化的敏感度，與貼近香港現狀。，我們以 「香港特區新浪潮」去命名在這情況下，依然保持以「小規模的 生產方式」拍富有香港特色的本地製作的一群香港電影人（司徒 和陳，2011年，2012年，2013 ）。 這項新的研究試圖了解（1）這「大陸化」趨勢有多大程度是香 港電影業復興的新契機？（2）對香港電影行業的創造力和創意 文化內涵又有多大的影響？換句話說，香港電影因「大陸化」而 變得更有創意了，還是反之亦然？「大陸化」又如何影響著香港 電影的文化和政治內涵？ 我們分析「香港特區新浪潮」電影人相對於香港新浪潮/第二浪 潮的電影前輩，在全球「新自由主義」在地的宏觀動力與本土文 化的微觀政治之間，有何不同的生存和創作策略？通過研究分析 全球化與在地跨境兩個不同尺度的文化政治之間的關係，我們可 以看到全球「新自由主義」的政治經濟與具體跨境與本土的文化 條件，怎樣互動而塑造出香港文化生產的物質條件，以及影響著 行業的運作與電影的文化內容。我們會以這種分析再結合微觀的 質性研究與文本分析，結合我我們對「香港特區新浪潮」文化內 涵跟以前怎樣不一樣的了解，去立體地勾畫出他們面對本地、中 國、亞洲、全球環境衝擊的集體創新過程與方法。

17408814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17408814.value: The Witwatersrand Gold Rush of 1886 led to the establishment of Johannesburg and set in motion a series of large-scale alterations to the geology, hydrology, and ecology of the region. Gold mining across an 80-km strip traversing the heart of Johannesburg and its neighboring municipalities became a conduit for regional infrastructure and shaped the contested social landscape of the region. With soaring gold prices, the gold mining belt is currently going through another iteration of environmental change as mining companies are now scavenging for remnant gold in historic tailings—or mine dumps. This flurry of gold recovery is reshaping the topography of the city, and releasing potential land for future urban development literally in the center of the city, and removing physical barriers between the rich north and poor south. However, the environmental consequences of unchecked mining for over a century are now coming into effect. Acid Mine Drainage (AMD)—polluted water with high acidic levels and heavy metals—is now threatening to decant at an unprecedented scale, endangering the freshwater resources and ecological viability of two major continental watersheds. This project moves beyond simplistic descriptions of singular aspects of this complex city and seeks to document the past and current mining landscapes through a series of visual narratives to compose an atlas for the region. The atlas analyzes the ecological, political, and economic forces of the Johannesburg region through “Operative Maps”, “Spatial Narratives”, and “Time Charts”. Information is collected through extensive fieldwork, interviews, and archival research. The intertwined relationship between constructed ground and the natural landscape demonstrated in Johannesburg resists singular perspectives and demands complexity. This work acknowledges the non-linear logics and hypercomplexities of the region and seeks to represent relationships, operations, and change. Ultimately, this project aims to provide an alternative perspective on environmental change in Johannesburg by giving voice to previously invisible actors. 約翰內斯堡是在1886年的淘金熱成立，並同時開始一系列地質，水文和生態上的巨大改變。跨越80公里的金礦帶穿越約翰內斯堡及其周邊城市的中心，成為區域性基礎設施的管道並塑造了該地區多爭議的社會景觀。近年飛漲的黃金價格又使得這個景觀再度經歷劇變，金礦工業回收一個世紀前所形成的廢棄土壤。這個回收熱潮塑造城市的地形，並在城市的中心釋放有發展潛能的土地，並除去南北貧富之間的障礙。然而一個多世紀的環境變化所造成的後果正慢慢的浮現，酸性礦山廢水（ AMD）－即具有高度酸性和重金屬汙染的水，正威脅以前所未有的規模溢出，危及非洲大陸兩個重要流域的淡水資源和生態。 該項目透過一系列的大型繪圖和視覺敘事手段超越了過於簡化單一的說明策略來描述這個複雜的城市。寰分析了約翰內斯堡地區的生態，政治和經濟，以“操作地圖” ， “空間敘事” ，和“時間圖表” 的圖繪方式分析約翰內斯堡地區的生態，政治和經濟。資料是通過廣泛的實地調查，訪談和文獻研究收集。
