17409214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17409214.value: Speech sound disorder (SSD) is a prevalent childhood communication disorder and forms a significant caseload of speech-and-language-therapy services in Hong Kong (To, Law & Cheung, 2012). SSD in preschool children can be persistent and may lead to long-term literacy difficulties. Emerging evidence indicates possible speech processing deficits that underlie SSD and later reading disorder. At the other end of the spectrum, a sizable subgroup of children originally demonstrates speech problems outgrow their speech errors without clinical attention and follow the typical growth trajectory in later years. Previous studies using simple correlation and the logistic regression have successfully identified risk factors that are significantly associated with the occurrence of SSD. However, these studies did not include time aspect and did not address the speech processing problems which can explicate different presentations of SSD, i.e., transient and persisting SSDs. Given the large variability in the growth trajectory of speech development and its disorder, previous studies may not provide much strong evidence on prognosis. This current study will employ a research technique of the survival analysis with the use of Cox's regression model to investigate the evolution of speech sound development along with children’s speech processing ability in those with SSD. The statistical analysis method is particularly for longitudinal designs and has taken into account the major problem of subject drop due to lost to follow up. We recruit Cantonese-speaking preschoolers who demonstrate the concern of speech problems without other known developmental problems in Hong Kong. To achieve adequate statistical power for analysis, 76 preschoolers with SSD aged at 5 years old will be recruited at the baseline using a validated parental questionnaire. Children who fit the inclusion criteria will be reassessed at a 6-month interval for a period of 2 years or until they master their sound inventory. Besides the child-related and family risk factors, the child’s speech processing ability will also be investigated in the present study. At the theoretical level, the findings result from the present study on the speech processing ability may dissect possible points of processing constraint in children with persisting SSD. At a clinical level, such a predictive model can contribute towards the evidence for speech-language therapists (SLTs) to better predict outcomes and estimate prognosis for children with SSD, and to decide on the appropriate treatment options. This will eventually lead to improved clinical estimation of prognosis SSD and better allocation of resources to early intervention provision. 構音障礙是現時一種非常普遍地兒童溝通障礙。在相關言語治療案例中佔有極為重要的比重。對於學前兒童，構音障礙是可持續的，並可導致長期的讀寫困難。近來有研究顯示某些語音處理上的不足可能是構音障礙的緣因，後期變成閱讀障礙。另一方面，在沒有臨床干預的情況下，原本有構音障礙的一大批兒童在成長過程中會逐漸減少至無語音上的錯誤，並於後期呈現正常的成長軌跡。 以前的研究通過簡單的相關系數分析和邏輯回歸成功的找出了與構音障礙的誘發因素。然而，這些研究並未考量時間因素，亦未強調語音處理的問題，而這些問題可解釋不同構音障礙，即短暫性和持久性構音障礙。鑒於成長過程中構音發展及相關障礙有巨大可變性，過去研究未能提供一個強而有力對預後的依據。本研究將採用活存分析手段結合Cox回歸模型來探究構音障礙兒童在語音處理能力方面的發展變化。統計分析方法特別使用縱向研究並已考慮參與者因跟進不到而終止研究等主要問題。 本研究選取以廣東話為母語，已出現語音問題關注但未有其他發展問題的香港學前兒童作為參與者。通過有效的家長問卷，共招募76名五歲構音障礙兒童，以取得足夠的統計功效。符合上述要求的兒童於每六個月會進行一次測試，為期兩年的時間或直至已掌握所有發音。除兒童及家庭相關的影響因素之外，此研究中亦會探究兒童的語音處理能力。 理論上，此研究結果可詳細分析持久性構音兒童所遇到的潛在處理障礙。臨床上，此預測模型為言語治療師作出更好的估計並預後結果，及安排恰當治療提供了依據。最終，這將提升言語障礙的臨床預後水平並更好地分配早期干預治療的相關資源。

17409214.label: Realisation of objectives
17409214.value: In general, the study was completed with the objectives achieved. The major challenge was to recruit sufficient participants who demonstrated 53 children with suspected speech sound disorders and at the age of 5 years old or other even though the scale of the screening exercise was expanded to a 890 children. We therefore adopted a set of more lenient inclusionary criteria by accepting younger children at or older than the age of three. Finally a total of 82 children who showed (1) an incomplete phonemic inventory with ≥ 5 errors in the Hong Kong Cantonese Articulation Test at the initial assessment, (2) a mean Intelligibility in Context – Traditional Chinese (ICS-TC) lower than the suggested cut-off of 4.29 (Ng et al., 2014), (3) at the age between 3 and 6 years old, have not started speech therapy at the initial assessment, (4) no significant deficits in structures or function of the speech or hearing mechanisms, cognitive deficits or psychosocial dysfunction, and (5) with the parents’ consent. These children were followed up in a six month interval until they showed demonstrated the completion of their phonemic inventory or normalized or the end of the study whenever earlier. In the final stage, 891 children were recruited and 845 participated in the initial assessment. Based on the above initial participant recruitment criteria, 82 children were followed up in the second stage. In order to reduce the attrition rate, children received a compensation fees of HK$200 for each of the follow-up assessment. In the third stage, 75 were followed up and at the last stage, 65 children were remained. In the initial assessment, children were assessed using HKCAT, the Hong Kong Cantonese Receptive Vocabulary Test, Oral Mechanism Examination. Demographic data were collected using a questionnaire. In each of the follow-up assessment, children’s speech performance was evaluated using the standardized speech sound assessment and the language assessment. 17 cases were censored, either lost to follow-up or with the completion of the phonemic inventory.

17409214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17409214.value: In the study, 845 children participated in the initial assessment. A large amount of data was collected, including children’s actual speech sound abilities and parents’ perception regarding the child’s speech intelligibility (ICS-TC). The data generated have been used to further validate the ICS-TC. The results were written up into a manuscript which was under-reviewed in the journal called Language, Speech and Hearing Services at School (LSHSS) after the first revision. In order to examine whether and when speech normalization (event) is likely to occur, the Hazard function h(t), that is, the probability of speech normalization at time t given no completion of phonemic inventory until time t was computed. Results showed that the probability of speech normalization (hazard) of the children increases with time. Before 40 months, a small increase in normalization rate and followed by an accelerated rate between 40 and 60 months. An exponential acceleration of rate from 60 to 80 months was observed. In other words, speech normalization happened but prolonged. In order examine what predicts the occurrence (risk factors), a Cox regression analysis was conducted aiming to model the effect of covariates (risk factors) on the hazard rate (with the baseline hazard rate unspecified). For the risk factors, we focus on the demographic background & child’s developmental history other than speech production. Initial selection of variables to be put in the Cox model is based on the Wald’s test which included only those variables for which the associated χ2 with test statistic having a p-value < 0.15 which reducing the potential risk factors from 25 to 4. The general results were as followed. For sex, Exp(β) = 5.684. The expected hazard (of speech normalization) is 5.684 times higher in girls as compared to boys, holding Temperament-Perceptual sensitivity scores constant, implying that girls are 5.684 times more likely to normalize. For Temperament-Perceptual sensitivity scores, Exp(β)= 1.848, meaning that there is an 84.8% increase in the expected hazard (of speech normalization) relative to a one SD increase in Temperament-Perceptual sensitivity, holding sex constant. In other words, children with 1 SD higher in the Perceptual sensitivity scale are 1.85 times more likely to normalize. The main results will be written up for dissemination in the Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research (JSHLR). We target at JSHLR where the main audience is clinician researchers. We would like to introduce this novel analysis method to the field of Speech-Language Pathology.

17409214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17409214.value: The current study showed that normalization happens in most of the children but some children did not show normalization even by the end of the study. We suspected some of the children with persistent problem may suffer from Childhood Apraxia of Speech which is often resistant to change. The speculation has led to a new project on examining the nature of the CAS which was supported by GRF 2018/2019 (ref: 17614717).

17409214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17409214.value: Speech sound disorder (SSD) is a prevalent childhood communication disorder and forms a significant caseload of speech-and-language-therapy services in Hong Kong. SSD in preschool children can be persistent and may lead to long-term literacy difficulties. At the other end of the spectrum, a sizable subgroup of children originally demonstrates speech problems outgrow their errors without clinical attention and follow the typical growth trajectory in later years. In the current study, we made use of a new statistical method known as survival analysis to enable us to predict if children, showing a slower start in speech sound ability but without any other developmental disorders will catch up later. We found that most children with an initial delay of speech sound production skills still showed speech normalization but the normalization process was protracted and takes about 80 months. Boys appeared to be more likely to show a longer normalization process. In addition, children’s perceptual sensitivity in the temperament scale is more predictive than a number of children’s language proficiency and family characteristics such as parental education level.

17409714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17409714.value: Myanmar’s largest city and commercial capital Yangon is the site of extraordinary and ongoing economic, demographic, and physical transformations; its leaders, planners, and communities are challenged to accommodate these changes fairly and efficiently while preserving Yangon’s unique heritage and urban character. The proposed project explores an element of this character that, although vital, is under-studied and without advocates: the network of parks, gardens, grounds, and greenways that constitute the city’s terrestrial landscape ecology. The goal of this research is to understand the historical relationship between nature and the city in Yangon, and to document the ecosystem services—the benefits to environment, culture, and economy—supplied by these landscape systems within the unexplored context of urban tropical Asia. The project is composed of three specific but interrelated explorations of landscape in Yangon. The first investigates the transformation of a tropical environment into an urban landscape through the construction and maintenance of a primate city from its colonial origins to the present. The second surveys the network of green spaces in the city, planned and unplanned, old and new, to understand and describe how they contribute to the vital urban ecology of Yangon. The third synthesizes the empirical and historical observations using the heuristic methods of landscape architecture and urban design to assess and speculate on the future of this rapidly changing urban landscape. These explorations will build on a discourse in urban ecologies that, while vast, has rarely examined cities in tropical climates. A study of the evolution of Yangon’s landscapes will create new knowledge of the complex relationships between structures of power and economy, social welfare, and the tropical environment. As both cultural artefact and living material, landscape as a medium and ecology as a lens promise to complicate postmodern notions of the construct of urban space and environmentalism. The functional description of Yangon’s landscapes, which borrows empirical methods and conceptual models from ecological science and landscape analysis, will observe and evaluate these parks, grounds, gardens, and greenways as an interdependent, layered urban ecology. Ultimately, given the precarious condition of Yangon, the project seeks to deliver applied research and actionable knowledge on the subject of the city’s rich landscape ecologies. Important lessons drawn from this exploration will also position Yangon as a case study in urban landscape ecology, challenging and extending dominant planning and management practices in the tropical and subtropical regions. 作为缅甸最大的城市和商业首都，仰光的经济、人口和城市正产生着飞速的发展和转型。如何在保留仰光的独特传统和城市特色的同时，公平而有效的适应这些变化，是仰光的领导者、规划者和社区民众当前所面临的巨大挑战。本课题针对城市特色中非常重要却常被忽视的要素：构成城市陆地景观生态的公园、花园、绿地、绿道网络系统。研究目的在于了解仰光的自然和城市之间的历史关系并记录生态系统所提供的服务——由亚洲热带城市的不发达地区景观系统所提供的——对于环境、文化和经济的贡献。 本研究由三个既独立又互相联系的探索组成。第一，调查研究从殖民地起源到现在，仰光从热带丛林到由人类建设和管理的城市景观之转变。第二，全面审视仰光的绿地空间网络，包括规划内和规划外，新与旧，理解描述它们如何对仰光的城市生态所做之重要贡献。第三，综合经验和历史观察，采用景观和城市设计的启发式方法 ， 评估和预测这个瞬息万变的城市未来之生态景观。 当前城市生态研究热门且范围广阔，而热带气候下的城市案例却十分鲜见。本课题对于仰光景观生态演变的研究，将带来对于动力和经济、社会福利和热带环境之间复杂关系认知的新知识。景观即是一种文化产品又为一种生活资料，课题将其作为媒介，从生态学的视角，实现了城市空间建设和环境保护后现代观的复杂性。从生态学和景观分析中借鉴了实证研究和概念模型的景观功能性分析，将对仰光的公园、绿地、花园和绿道作为相互依存的不同城市生态层面展开观察和评估。 最终，鉴于仰光景观生态的危机状态，本研究旨在为仰光的丰富城市生态景观提供应用性研究和可操作知识，而这一探索中得出的重要经验也将其定位为，一个处于热带与亚热带地区面对不断扩展的规划与管理实践挑战的城市景观生态学研究案例。

17409714.label: Realisation of objectives
17409714.value: As briefed in previous project reports, the originally defined seven objectives have been structured as three related research projects onto which I have mapped the stated objectives. The first of these projects involved a study of the historical evolution of Yangon’s planned landscapes in the context of colonial city-building and the reimaging of that heritage in the post-colonial and contemporary periods. This project largely utilized archival research and field-work and was underway already as part of the background research for the original GRF proposal. The primary goal of this part of the project was to meet objectives [1], [1.1], and [1.2]. These goals were achieved and this early work solidified relationships that would lead to greater access for the later goals and formed the basis for informal advisory roles and involvement with local community and government groups. The findings of this research was presented at multiple international conferences. However, I regret not seeking wider audience or higher-value forms impact such as journal articles for this body of research. I believe (as stated in my goals) that this level of output depends on a continuous assessment of both colonial and post-colonial archival material. The dynamic political environment of Myanmar has little affected my work, except for the ability to gain access to local archives from the 1960’s to the 1990’s. I have each year made written request for this access and/or sought partnerships with local academics. I have not yet been successful, but am convinced that I will be eventually, and will be ready to conclude this part of the work when I am. A second research project was ill-defined in the original GRF but became relevant as I carried out initial field work related to the first and third objectives. When complete, it will substantially address objective [2],[3], and [3.1]. A full survey of the colonial city’s street trees was substantially completed in Fall 2016 with follow-up and corrective work done in Summer 2017. This work has led to collaborative work with the local NGO the Yangon Heritage Trust, but has not yet been completed for publication in the targeted journal largely because a statistical evaluation of the dataset has not yet been completed. This is a clear under-achievement and I plan to remedy this by partnering with a R.A. or co-author that can assist with a statistical analysis that can be incorporated into the written piece. The third project dealt with the typological description and assessment of the current situations of the particular urban ecologies of Yangon. It is less focused on archival research, and is more focused on mapping, geo-spatial analysis and interviews. This research activity involves the creation of 8 large-scale urban transects of about 5 sq.km each. These transects combine observational methodologies and geospatial analysis to create a mapping of patches and land-cover attributes. These have been using high-resolution aerials and low-resolution landsat multispectral data. Analysis of these mappings, combined with on-site verification, hope to reveal a typological study of the urban/ecological fabric in the city, directly relating to objectives [2] and [2.1]. Mapping, and fieldwork, and data-collection for this activity was completed in early 2017 and initial results were presented in a May 2017 conference. Completion of this work is still outstanding.

17409714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17409714.value: As contemporary post-colonial research illustrates, the urban public realm in colonial cities is both the manifestation of power systems and symbols, but also the site and means for its resistance and re-appropriation. This research provided a further case-study in this body of work, but challenged the traditional passivity attributed to these actually living, dynamic systems that are the physical medium of urban systems. In conference presentations I showed the ways in which natural systems—the mud just below the surface, and the jungle potentiate in every aerial root and errant weed—were variously co-opted or resisted in fluid and improvisational ways. While some of the research focused on the ‘monumental’ parks of the inner city, we also found that extensive areas of recent urban expansion have exacerbated the potential for natural systems and endemic ecologies to trigger conflicts between society, community, and government. A survey of street trees in the formerly colonial downtown revealed an urban forest in transition and at risk of degrading social, ecological and economic value. With preliminary findings, I argued in conferences, in community workshops and with local NGO’s that street trees are a fundamental but element of Yangon’s urban heritage. I showed that urban areas seeing the greatest amount of economic development targeting the growing business and tourism sectors often correlated to the lowest measures of species diversity, coverage, and other ecological and cultural services. Low-performing street tree zones could be attributed to uniformed but well-meaning decisions within public works departments, whereas high-performing street tree-zones could be attributed to absence of municipal activities and strong community organization and cultural practices resulting in the maintenance and preservation of tree stock. Both suggest a capacity for municipal training and community education and agency in protecting the urban forest in the future. The most recent work presented in conferences, but yet to be developed further, finds that the field of landscape architecture has much to learn from the adaptive urban landscapes encountered in Yangon. As the field becomes more dominant in global practice, its theoretical origins and base of experience are still limited to western centers of knowledge and temperate climates. I have also argued that landscape architect practitioners, educators, and scholars have an obligation to engage in these at-risk sites with the aim of arming communities with the design and planning knowledge to increase their capacity for building healthy and resilient settlements in the future.

17409714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17409714.value: This research is part of my larger interest in the role of landscape systems in large-scale urban development. The first priority for this research project is to finalize the outputs that are still outstanding, including the papers intended for the second and third ‘projects’ described above. Outside of the research scoped by this GRF, there are two clear avenues for further research. Both expansions of the current research involve expertise beyond my own, so I would need to seek wider partnership with other scholars and researchers. The first expansion involves and expanded street tree survey reaching a much larger portion of the urban metropolitan area. This would involve significant funding and utilize very different survey methodologies than the current study, focusing much more on the ecological value of the urban forest and utilizing appropriate sampling methods. Various private entities have expressed interest in partial funding, but I have not pursued it further. A second expansion area would see much greater focus on remotely sensed map-analysis of the region. Some methods, which have been developed in this study at the scale of the ‘transect’ could be scaled and the on-site interviews and observations would prove useful to initially ground-truth—or ‘tune’—any new dataset.

17409714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17409714.value: This research project looked at the green spaces of Yangon, Myanmar in order to understand how these natural systems played a role in the development of the city. The research showed how nature was not just a site for the urban evolution that saw a precolonial outpost become colonial capital and then a base for a military dictatorship, but an active participant in the struggles for making the city both historically and today. In a city defining itself as a tourism hub and central market for a newly-opening economy, this research argued for an expanded definition of urban “heritage” so central to these narratives of progress. We showed how street trees and other largely invisible or underappreciated green landscapes were actually critical in grounding social and community identity, and provided economic and ecological value—aspects that were not adequately taken account of in the city’s models for protecting its physical and cultural heritage. Finally, this research documented for a global audience of landscape architects the ways in which the people of Yangon have understood and adapted to their environment—one in which unpredictability and risk exist in ways we do not see in the cities in which we live and work.

17410914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17410914.value: In Asia, Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia are unique in adopting common law while most countries like China, Japan and South Korea implement civil law. This research undertakes a comparative study of the values of law students in these three Asian common law jurisdictions. This topic is significant because lawyers play an important role in the administration of justice and information about their values can help us in assessing the quality of justice and legal systems involved. Moreover, a study of law students’ values can help us predict their future behaviors and ethical decision-making in legal practice. However, there has been a paucity of research into the values of lawyers or law students in the common law world, particularly those jurisdictions in Asia. This project attempts to answer four research questions. Firstly, what values are empirically important in determining the behaviors and ethical decision-making of law students in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia? Secondly, whether there is a common core of values shared by law students in these three Asian common law jurisdictions? Thirdly, whether there are differences in value orientations of law students in these three places? Finally, whether there is a gender difference in the value hierarchies of law students in these Asian common law jurisdictions? These research questions are answered by conducting questionnaire surveys and semi-structured interviews with law students in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia respectively. This project will build on previous studies undertaken by one of the researchers in Australia and an ongoing study undertaken by three of the researchers in the Greater China Region. It will adapt the survey questionnaire used in the Australian studies to extend the analysis of law students’ values in the context of these three common law jurisdictions. In this way, this study will advance the boundary of current research on values of lawyers and law students from the Western common law world to its Asian counterpart. 在大部份亞洲國家如中國、日本和南韓都實施大陸法；但是，香港、新加坡及馬來西亞卻使用普通法。因此，本研究項目將對這三個亞洲普通法區的法學生之價值觀進行比較研究。律師在司法制度中扮演重要的角色，瞭解他們的價值觀將有助研究有關地區的法律制度之質素；此外，研究法學生的價值觀將有助預測他們未來執業時的行為及道德標準。然而，在普通法區，特別是亞洲的普通法區，卻缺乏這類對律師或法學生價值觀的研究。 本項目集中於四道研究問題：第一，哪些價值對香港、新加坡和馬來西亞法學生的行為及道德倫理影響最大？第二，這三個亞洲普通法區的法學生有沒有共同的核心價值？第三，這三個地方的法學生的價值取向有没有相異之處？最後，這些亞洲普通法區的法學生的價值有否受性別差異的影響？ 本項目的研究方法包括問卷調查及與香港、新加坡和馬來西亞法學生進行半結構式訪談。這項目是建基於本研究團隊一位澳洲教授之前對當地學生所進行的研究，以及三位本團隊成員正在大中華地區進行的類似研究；本項目以澳洲採用過的問卷內容為藍本，並將律師和法律系學生價值取向這研究範疇，由西方普通法區延伸至亞洲普通法區。

17410914.label: Realisation of objectives
17410914.value: Objective One (identification and comparison of the values that are characteristic of law students in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore); secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore). Objective Two (assessment of the significance of values in the decision-making process of law students in the three Asian common law jurisdictions): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore); secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore). Objective Three (investigation of the effect of class and gender on the value orientations of law students in the three Asian common law jurisdictions): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore); secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the impact of class and gender on value hierarchies of law students. Objective Four (evaluation of the impact of law school education on the value orientation of law students in the three Asian common law jurisdictions): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore); secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the legal education development of Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore. Objective Five (investigation of the contextual factors, both external and internal to law schools in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore, that impact the values of their students): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore) ; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore); and thirdly by literature review undertaken on the impact of Islamic culture, particularly religious influence, on the value development of law students in Malaysia. Objective Six (identification and development of strategies that can help both the governments and law schools in the three Asian common law jurisdictions to reform their curricula on value development of their law students): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 35 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong), Malaysia (International Islamic University of Malaysia) and Singapore (National University of Singapore); secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 269 law students in Malaysia (two law schools including International Islamic University of Malaysia and Malaya University) and 412 law students in Singapore (the law school of National University of Singapore); and thirdly, by literature review on the ethics education of law school focusing on clinical legal education and legal ethics teaching.

17410914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17410914.value: Major Findings and Research outcome (please refer to items 1 and 2 in Section 8, and items 5 and 9 in Section 9 of the Research Output in Part C) 1. Overall, law students in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia have developed ethical values similar to common law students in other Western common law jurisdictions like Australia. 2. There is a common pattern of feminization of law students in the three Asian common law jurisdictions, namely, there are more female than male law students in all three jurisdictions. 3. Some correlations exist between gender and ethical values of law students in Hong Kong. Female law students are more motivated by the value of ‘business efficacy’ than their male counterparts. They are also more motivated by the values of ‘access to legal justice’ and ‘civic duty’ than their male counterparts. 4. Students in all three Asian jurisdictions developed similarly strong professional values like ‘obedience to the law’, which reflect the success of common law education in all three jurisdictions in cultivating professional values. 5. In future, law schools in all three Asian common law jurisdictions should expand their legal clinics programmes to inculcate upon their students the value of ‘access to legal justice’. 6. Law schools in the three Asian common law jurisdictions should strengthen the ethical values of law students by developing their “personal conscience“, “ethics of duty”, and “ethics of aspiration”. They should also cultivate such virtues like honesty, perspective, and fairness among their students to help them encounter ethical dilemmas. 7. The law students in Singapore have stronger pro bono culture. In contrast, law students in Hong Kong and Malaysia share a weak pro bono culture. 8. A new generation of law students has emerged in the three Asian common law jurisdictions who cherish work-life balance. They rate personal values of “family loyalty” and “family members’ well-being” higher than professional values like “obedience to the law firm partner/supervisor”, “professional ambition” and “loyalty to the firm”.

17410914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17410914.value: As we have studied the ethical values of law students in the three Asian jurisdictions, we plan to expand our research to countries in other parts of the world, in particular Belt and Road countries like Myanmar, Indonesia and Israel. On basis of the findings of this project, Dr Wu (PI) applied for another GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in four Asian civil law countries (China, Japan, Vietnam and South Korea) in 2014 and was awarded a sum of HK$798,480 (Project No.17601815) in 2015. Subsequently, Dr Wu (PI) applied for two more GRF grants to study the ethical values of law students in four fastest growing Asian countries (China, India, Philippines and Thailand) and four emerging and transitional economies (China, Russia, South Africa and Kazakhstan) in 2016 and 2017 respectively. He was awarded a sum of HK$844,880 in 2017 (project No. 17602717) and another sum of HK$918,160 (Project No. 17601018) in 2018 respectively. In 2018, Dr Wu (PI) has also applied for another GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in four Belt and Road countries (China, Myanmar, Israel and Indonesia).

17410914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17410914.value: This project investigates empirically the ethical values of law students in three Asian common law jurisdictions. It found that law students in these three jurisdictions have developed ethical values similar to those in other common law countries like Australia. This study also recommends law schools in the three Asian common law jurisdictions to cultivate such virtues like honesty, perspective, and fairness among their students in future. This project is significant as it has enhanced our understanding of the ethical values of law students in Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia. It is also invaluable in developing a new field of academic inquiry by leading to three research projects on the ethical values of law students in Asian civil law countries like Japan, South Korea and Vietnam; Asian fastest growing countries like India, Philippines and Thailand; and transitional and emerging economics like Russia, Kazakhstan and South Africa. Overall, this project is a pioneering study of the ethical values of Asian common law students. It has made an important contribution to the academic discourse on the ethical values of law students and Asian legal education.

17411214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17411214.value: 亚洲普通法体系中的宪法对话

17411214.label: Project Objectives
17411214.value: Challenge the conventional wisdom that a constitutional dialogue between legislators and judges can only take place in jurisdictions where the bills of rights expressly include structural devices whereby the legislature’s right to disagree with the local court’s conception of rights, in the course of ordinary politics, is preserved. Fill the gap in the academic literature by analysing three common law systems in Asia, i.e. Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia, since current discourse focussed only on common law systems in the West. Illustrate and explain how domestic courts in common law Asia have engaged or can engage in “dialogic” review via the application of dialogic doctrines. Reconceive prior case-law using the dialogic doctrinal tools I propose.

17411214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17411214.value: In the last decade, “dialogue” has become a common place metaphor in constitutional discourse. This term was popularised by Peter Hogg and Allison Bushell when they argued how Canadian judges are engaged in a collaborative conversation with the legislature over the optimum level of human rights protection within the constitutional state. The metaphor has however travelled across the oceans and has since entered the legal vernacular of other common law systems that have also adopted bills of rights that include various creative structural mechanisms that expressly confer upon the national courts the right to apply fundamental human rights norms, while preserving the legislature’s right to disagree with those views in the course of ordinary politics. One must however note at the outset that while dialogic review is most commonly discussed in these common law systems where weak-form review was first conceived, the existence of these structural mechanisms is not a prerequisite for a dialogic approach to constitutional discourse to occur. The spacious text in most bills of rights permits divergence on a litany of issues and provides a framework for the political communities to disagree and struggle over the document’s meaning. Where the judiciary facilitates but does not foreclose the constitutional debate for the electorate and its representatives, the processes of constitutional interpretation become more dynamic and a dialogue between the judicial and political branches of government on constitutional meaning can ensure. Notably too, discussions on dialogic review have primarily focussed on common law constitutional system in the West. This project will thus seek to fill the lacuna in the literature by analysing these common law systems in Asia i.e. Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia. In particular, these three jurisdictions are former British colonies that continue to observe common law norms and traditions; their respective judiciaries are generally empowered under their written constitutions to invalidate legislation for perceived rights-violations and their respective constitutions also do not include any structural devices that enable the legislatures to reserve a judicial decision they disagree with, except via a constitutional amendment. I will argue that in these three common law Asian constitutional systems, even though the respective constitutions do not provide for structural devices that enable the legislatures to reverse or avoid a judicial decision they disagree with, the courts in question can still apply judicial techniques that foster a debate with the political branches of government on constitutional values. 在过去的十年间，“对话” (dialogue) 已经成为一个在宪法话语中常见的比喻。这个术语是通过 Peter Hogg 和 Allison Bushell 这两位学者的使用而普及起来的。他们在论证加拿大法官就如何在宪政国家中为人权提供最佳的保护与立法机关进行沟通合作时，使用了这个比喻。这个比喻后来被引进不同已制定人权法案普通法体系成为当地的术语。这些普通法体系的人权法案均规定了不同具有创新性的机制；这些机制一方面明确地授权本地法院适用关于基本人权的规则，另一方面又保护立法机关在普通的政治议题上对上述法院关于基本人权的意见提出异议的权利。 然而，必须注意的是，虽然对话式的审查模式是在最先实行较宽松司法审查机制的普通法体系中成为讨论对象的，但是这种机制的存在并非对话式宪制发生之前提。大部分人权法案均使用了含义模糊的用语，这些用语不仅使得人们产生不同的意见，更为各政治团体提供一个平台，让它们就文本的理解提出异议和展开辩论。如果法院推动（而非妨碍）选民及由其选出的代表开展宪制辩论，那么宪法解释的过程将更为多变，而且法院与政府中的立法及行政机关之间的对话亦将获得保障。 同样值得注意是，关于对话式审查模式的讨论目前主要集中于在西方的普通法宪制体系。本研究课题旨在填补现有文献在亚洲普通法体系（即香港、新加坡和马来西亚）研究方面的这个空缺。其中，本研究课题将就以下三个方面展开讨论：第一，这三个法域均为继续实行普通法规则和传统的前英国殖民地；第二，它们的法院根据其成文宪法均一般有权促使被认为侵犯法律人权的法律归于无效；第三，它们的宪法亦没有规定任何让立法机关通过除修改宪法以外的其他方式推翻一个其不同意的法院判决之结构性工具。 笔者将会论证，在上述三个普通法亚洲宪制体系中，即使相关的宪法并没有规定让立法机关推翻或者取消其不同意的法院判决之结构性工具，但法院仍然可以通过使用一些司法技巧，促使立法和行政机关与其就宪法价值展开辩论。

17411314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17411314.value: During the transitional period in late Qing and early Republic of China, Nanshe (The South Society,南社) with members over a thousand dispersing from north to south, had played an important role in various aspects of China. Established in 1909, Nanshe advocated its mission on political revolution and cultural reservation, and consequently drew great attention of modern intellectuals and politicians. However, among previous research on Nanshe, most of them focused on its activities and renowned members of the Jiangnan area where the society originally set up. Indeed, important figures such as Liu Yazi (柳亞子), Chen Qubing (陳去病) and Huang Binhong (黃賓虹), not only involved actively in the operation and gatherings of Nanshe, but also made achievements in modern literature and art. Yet from regional perspectives, Guangdong members of Nanshe had simultaneously contributed a lot, while their accomplishments had been underestimated and little attention was paid in previous studies. In view of the importance of the Guangdong members, this research will concentrate on the organization of Cantonese branch of Nanshe, its active members’ roles within the context of conflicts of Chinese tradition and modernity, and also their remarkable contribution to political, literary and academic development of southern China including Hong Kong. Strictly speaking, the Guangdong branch was rarely comprehensively discussed before. In fact Cantonese members (with amount of 172 and ranked the third among all members from different provinces) had played crucial roles in establishing a sub-society and even illustrated another undeniable trend for Nanshe after 1920s. The composition and operation of the branch, its cultural identity and members’ literary achievements will firstly be scrutinized. In addition, the significant role of the branch in Chinese modernity will be overall reviewed and re-appraised. Secondly, Cantonese members engaged actively in literary and cultural reformation of modern China. Apart from some pioneers who introduced and promoted “new” literary genres like Su Manshu (蘇曼殊), the majority chose to persist traditional writing, which very likely revealed the paradox of east and west cultures in modern China. In this sense, further exploration would be pursued. Thirdly, representative Cantonese members such as Su Manshu, Cai Shao(蔡守)，Deng Erya(鄧爾雅), Huang Jie(黃節), Pan Feisheng(潘飛聲), Wang Jingwei(汪精衞)，Gu Zhi(古直) etc will be further investigated. Their contributions in political, social, cultural, literary and even academic aspects would be deeply examined, that might eventually provide examples for a better understanding of the significance of the branch and Cantonese members within Nanshe during the time of Chinese modernization. 南社成立於1909年，是清末民初提倡社會改革、文學革新的一個重要文學社團。南社發展迅速，社員過千、遍佈大江南北，而且很多都是身居各行各業的顯要人物，對清末民國的社會、文化、文學、藝術，以至政治各領域均有重大的影響和貢獻。過去對於南社的研究，大多集中於南社在北方的重要活動和一些著名成員如柳亞子、陳去病、黃賓虹、蘇曼殊、李叔同等人身上，事實上，南社的分社如湖南湘集、廣東粵社及它們的成員，同樣對當時中國社會有重大貢獻，影響深遠，可惜並未得到應有的重視和深入的學術討論。本計劃便是以南社的廣東支社及其成員為研究對象，詳細檢視廣東南社在中國現代化進程中起着的作用和意義。 南社廣東支社有172位成員，是南社的第三大分會。它的組成和演變，各會員的背景和他們在不同崗位上的成就，特別是他們對傳統與現代，中西文化、文學的取捨與抉擇，以及傳承發揚嶺南文化等問題，本計劃將有細致的稽考和討論，借以說明南社分會的地域性功能，並進一步宏觀地認知南社作為一個全國性社團的整體意義，藉此填補過去研究的不足。 宏觀的考察之外，計劃也會對廣東支社的一些重要成員作開拓性的探討，如它的核心社員蔡哲夫、鄧爾雅、蘇曼殊；學者兼作家黃節、古直、潘飛聲、黃仲琴；政界人物汪精衞、沈鈞儒；書畫家談月色、尹爟、姚禮修等。上述成員，當中只有少數曾被學者作過研究，然而也不是從南社成員的角度把他們放到廣東支社，以至整個南社中去檢視他們的功績和作用。因此，較全面地分析這些廣東支社成員的業績，他們的社會文化角色，肯定是南社研究和現代史研究不可或缺的論述議題。 簡言之，通過對廣東支社宏觀的考察及其重要成員的論述，本計劃期望能對廣東支社的來龍去脈、地域性功能，它在整個南社社團內起到的角色作用，以及它對中國現代化進程的貢獻等，有更透徹的認知和客觀的評價。

17411314.label: Realisation of objectives
17411314.value: In the past three years, extensive collection of relevant materials and in-depth investigation have been done in order to address the objectives and questions suggested in the project. The close relationship between Nanshe and its Cantonese branch (Objective 1) has been assured through the study of the intimate connection of the two leading representatives Liu Yazhi(柳亞子), one of the founders of the association and Cai Shou (蔡守), the leader of the Branch. Their friendship could be verified by their retrieved letters(original copies) and poems to each other showing their close communication. In addition, the members of the Branch had frequently participated in the activities organized by Nanshe proper and they always contributed various kinds of writings to be published on Nanshe’s core bulletin 《南社叢刻》. (Draft paper〈蔡守柳亞子交游研究：以南社與廣東分社為中心〉referred.) The Cantonese Branch established in March 1917 with its first meeting in Guangzhou. Later in 1920s, some active members moved to Hong Kong and around late 1923, the Branch had merged into Hunan Branch (南社湘集) and continued its activities. According to documentary records and previous research findings, the Branch has 213 members. Most of them were literati or scholars. They joined the Branch due to their admiration of Nanshe advocates and their common interests of writing literary works as well as making friends for broadening their horizon. (objective 2) It could be easily observed that regular gentle gatherings of Nanshe proper and branches in which one person writing a poem and one or more other people replying it by using the same rhyme sequence had been taken place periodically and the Cantonese members joined in with great enthusiasm. This kind of gatherings was inherited from traditional culture of intellectuals that was regarded as an effective way of consolidating the members and enhancing the social status of the association. In parallel of supporting the Nanshe proper, the Cantonese members had played a significant role in the literary, academic, educational and other aspects of South China Provinces and colonial Hong Kong. They had a strong sense of mission to preserve and carry forward of the quintessence of Chinese culture. (objective 3) Instead of promoting vernacular literature or overthrowing the classical works, Cantonese members devoted to write traditional form of poetry and study Confucian Classics in new perspectives for cultural preservation and reformation. It was their choice that supposed to be an effective way in pursuit of Chinese modernization. Their cultural identity was clear and firm but seemed to be semi-conservative and this was also the main reason for the uprising conflicts between those revolutionary members and some of Cantonese members in the 1920s. (objective 4) Comparing with Nanshe proper, the size of member population of Cantonese Branch was small but there were significant figures in it. Some were renowned writers like Su Manshu(蘇曼殊), Cai Shou(蔡守), Pan Feisheng(潘飛聲), Wang Jingwei(汪精衞),; distinguished professors and scholars like Deng Erya(鄧爾雅), Yi Ru(易孺), Huang Jie(黃節),，Gu Zhi(古直), Huang Zhongqin(黃仲琴), Chen Zhu(陳柱); and eminent artists like Cai Shou, Tan Yuese(談月色), Deng Erya, Yi Ru etc. They had published a lot of literary works, artistic creations(painting, calligraphy and seal cutting) and academic outputs at their time. In order to have a sharp understanding and accurate evaluation of Cantonese members’ achievements in different aspects and cultural reformation, the remarkable works of individual representative members have been scrutinized. The following draft scripts were in-depth studies of some prominent members: 〈論蔡哲夫及其《寒瓊遺稿》〉 〈論黃仲琴及其詩作特色〉 〈易大厂及其文學成就〉 〈「憂樂莫忘文正語，安危終眷杜陵心」──潘飛聲的詩文論略〉 〈現代化語境下的文化承傳──論易大厂的藝術活動與詞學〉 〈蔡哲夫、談月色、鄧爾雅書畫藝術及交誼〉 〈南社廣東成員題寫晚明張二喬的詩畫〉 〈論南社學者古直的古典詩學研究〉 〈新舊批評觀念的交鋒：黃節與朱自清的樂府「清商三調」討論〉 〈馮自由、鄒魯及陸丹林的歷史學撰述〉 Through the micro-study of above-mentioned figures and their interaction with Nanshe members or other intellectuals, their role of cultural inheritance and the composite accomplishment of the Branch had been expounded and known well. (objective 5) Being the members of a regional Branch of Nanshe, most of the Cantonese members were growing up or living in South China provinces and Hong Kong, the impact of Cantonese local culture on their writings and research works could be easily identified by analyzing the subject-matters, the allusions and expressions of their texts. Geographical scenery, social issues, historical characters and cultural relics were extensively appeared in the poems, paintings and their research topics. The most typical example was the late Ming female figure Zhang Erqiao(張二喬), who was an ideal image of faithfulness and fidelity, had been always praised in members’ poems and even portrayed by Tan Yuese in her painting. The rationale of recalling local historical figures or things has implied that Cantonese members were passionate about their home place and people, and they had also expressed an urge for reference and learning in their texts. (objective 6) The key members Cai Shou, Tan Yuese and Deng Erya had moved to Hong Kong one after the other in early 1920 and resided at the colony for a long period. Hong Kong was considered to be a place of refuge for them, and the colonial culture has more or less influenced their living and works. They remained active in Hong Kong literary circle, participating in gentle gatherings and writing presented poems. Their texts did assimilate colonial objects into the contents and it have probably enriched the subject-matters of their creative writings. However, it should be realized that though Hong Kong elements or things had been absorbed, they were simply presented as an emblem of the members’ feelings for being the transient guests in the city. (objective 7)With attentive reading of the texts, it could be ascertained that the young colonial culture and its Chinese-western nature might not easily override the Chinese traditional values of Cantonese members (孫瑩瑩 〈南社廣東詩人之香港詩歌：以鄧爾雅、蔡哲夫為中心〉referred). In short, all the objectives of the project have been achieved with exhaustive materials and substantial arguments. And the literary and cultural significance of Cantonese Branch of Nanshe in modern context could be comprehensively realized.

17411314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17411314.value: 1. Rare materials retrieved: (1) The hand-writing of the letters of Liu Yazhi and Cai Zhuo; (2) The copy of hand-writing of Nanshe Sihua 南社詩話 by Wang Jingwei; (3) Original painting portrait of Zhang(張二喬) by Tan Yuese. Three types of rare materials of Cantonese members have been retrieved in the course of conducting the project. They are firstly discovered and regarded precious not only of their artistic values but also their documentary importance for clarifying some issues in Nanshe studies. Making use of these first-hand materials, three papers titled〈蔡守柳亞子交游研究：以南社與廣東分社為中心〉、〈“曼昭”便是汪精衛，而非李曼昭──《南社詩話》手稿全篇出版敘言〉、〈南社廣東成員題寫晚明張二喬的詩畫〉have been drafted for the verification of the close relationship between Liu Yazhi (Nanshe proper)and Cai Shou(Cantonese Branch), the authorship of Nanshe Sihua, and the cultural inheritance of Cantonese members. In fact, the materials are rare and valuable, they are worthy to be published for sharing. 2. Findings on Cantonese Branch of Nanshe (1) Semi-conservative cultural identity of Cantonese Branch It has been realized that Cantonese members inclined to advocate traditional cultural inheritance and promote classical forms of writing. They were considered to be conservative in modern context. But as the project observed, Cantonese members were not simply inheriting traditional legacy without any queries or reforms. On the contrary, they had injected new subject-matters in their poetry writings and employed modified methods in academic studies. The following draft papers might clarify the actual cultural identity of Cantonese members:〈現代化語境下的文化承傳──論易大厂的藝術活動與詞學〉、〈論南社學者古直的古典詩學研究〉、〈新舊批評觀念的交鋒：黃節與朱自清的樂府「清商三調」討論〉〈馮自由、鄒魯及陸丹林的歷史學撰述〉。 (2) Remarkable achievements of Cantonese members There were prominent figures in Cantonese Branch and they all have had remarkable achievements in literary, fine arts and academic areas at their time. Most of their writings or academic outputs had not been widely known or well received, but in the project representative members were scrutinized and their contributions have likely been explored. Belowwere draft papers prepared: 〈南社廣東成員著述要目〉 〈論黃仲琴及其詩作特色〉 〈易大厂及其文學成就〉 〈「憂樂莫忘文正語，安危終眷杜陵心」──潘飛聲的詩文論略〉 〈蔡哲夫、談月色、鄧爾雅書畫藝術及交誼〉 These scripts did reflect some Cantonese members’ professional skills and their accomplishment. Their names and remarkable performance should be recognized and recorded in the history of modern China.

17411314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17411314.value: 1. More representative Cantonese members could be studied in detail and their first-hand materials should be exhaustively retrieved for the refinement of the project. 2. Individual representative member of the Branch could be separately developed as a case study project whose life and thought, contribution and achievement, could be fully recognized. 3. The nature and implication of Nanshe sub-societies organized in different geographic areas of China could be treated as related projects for a comprehensive understanding of the significance and importance of Nanshe in the late Qing and the Republican China. Therefore, Nanshe’s institutional significance would be further explored from regional perspective of investigation, and this approach might in long-term inspire the coming research on Chinese literary societies.

17411314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17411314.value: The project was the first and an in-depth study of the Cantonese branch of literary association Nanshe in the late Qing and Republican China. Nanshe was a revolutionary party, advocating for political reform, promoting traditional forms of writings and encouraging cultural inheritance. The Cantonese Branch was established in Guangzhou which played an important role by extending Nanshe impact in South China provinces including colonial Hong Kong. Based on exhaustive materials and first-hand resources, the project has verified the composition, activities and operation of the branch, its semi-conservative cultural identity and its close connection with Nanshe proper. In addition, representative members like Su Manshu(蘇曼殊), Cai Shou(蔡守), Pan Feisheng(潘飛聲), Wang Jingwei(汪精衞), Deng Erya(鄧爾雅), Yi Ru(易孺), Huang Jie(黃節), Gu Zhi(古直), Tan Yuese(談月色) etc, their achievements in literary, artistic and academic aspects have been illustrated. The exposition of these figures might truly reflect the accomplishment of individual member and in fact, also demonstrate the composite strength of the Branch. The project was comprehensive and innovative, a valuable research of Nanshe studies.

17411414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17411414.value: With the introduction of e-learning, a number of learning management systems (LMSs) have been launched in Hong Kong schools. Due to a lack of comprehensive investigation, however, little knowledge exists about student acceptance and continuance of LMS usage. Therefore, the aim of this research is to establish theoretical models with a focus on learning and student development to explain and predict student LMS acceptance and continuance of usage. Technology acceptance studies, an important research area in business information systems, examine the individual and the choices an individual makes to accept or reject a particular technology. A review of such studies undertaken in educational settings reveals that a number of well-researched contributing factors and models have been examined. However, although educational environments share some characteristics of business organizations, the influence of technology change (particularly in schools) does not appear to be well-captured by research. This study argues that students’ conceptions of learning and learning styles are critical to their interactions in learning environments, including their use of LMS products. It will investigate students’ LMS usage in the school curriculum and trace the associated changes in beliefs, attitudes, conceptions of learning, learning styles, information literacy, intention, LMS usage behavior and LMS satisfaction. A panel longitudinal study with cross-sectional age groups will be conducted, with the primary goal of characterizing changes in students’ responses over time. The study will involve 630 Secondary 1 students and 630 Secondary 2 students from 21 sample schools. The students will undertake two computer-based information literacy performance tests and respond to three self-reported online surveys at different stages of the study. The impact of individual characteristics, contextual factors and social influence on students’ performance in information literacy skills, perceptions, beliefs, intention, and LMS usage behavior will be explored. The findings will offer a better understanding of student acceptance and continuance of LMS usage, and help to establish a theoretical framework for these behaviors with a focus on learning. The results will also provide teachers, practitioners and policy-makers with well-researched guidelines to plan and improve e-learning implementation. 通過引入電子學習，學習管理系統已經應用在一些香港的學校中。由於缺乏全面的調查，有關學生在學習管理系統的採納和延續使用的資訊是比較少的。因此，本研究的目的是建立有關學習和發展的理論模型，來解釋和預測學生對學習管理系統的採納和延續使用行為。在教育環境中進行的一些有關科技採納的研究指出，尤其在學校裡科技變革的影響似乎並沒有很好地被反映出來。這項研究認為，學生們的學習概念和學習風格對他們在學習環境中的互動至為關鍵。是次研究是縱向性的。研究將會調查學生在學校課程中使用學習管理系統的情況，和追蹤他們在信念，態度，學習概念，學習方式，資訊素養，意向，學習管理系統的使用行為和對學習管理系統滿意度的轉變。這項研究將涉及來自21間學校的630位中一和630位中二學生。學生們將透過利用電腦進行兩次資訊素養測試，並在研究計劃過程中的三個不同階段填寫網上問卷。研究將會探討學生們的個人特徵，環境因素等等所帶來的衝擊。研究結果將會讓我們更好地了解學生對學習管理系統的採納和延續使用情況，並幫助建立理論框架。其結果也將為教師和政策制定者等等提供良好的指導規劃，從而提高電子學習的實施力度。

17411414.label: Realisation of objectives
17411414.value: We have achieved all three objectives. A number of research instruments have been established and validated covering the following 10 aspects. (1) Student Characteristics: Age, Gender, Academic ability, Socioeconomic status (2) Contextual Factors: School and teacher practices in using LMS, Curriculum, Technical support, Home access, System design and functionalities, Online learning strategies (3) Social Influence: Subjective norm, Teacher conception of e-learning, Teacher influence and support, Parental influence and support, Peers’ engagement with LMS (4) Information Literacy (IL) Skills: 7 information literacy skills: Define, Access, Manage, Integrate, Communicate, Create, Evaluate (5) Conceptions of Learning (COL): 6 student conceptions of learning: Understanding, Personal change, Social competence, Continuous, Gaining information, Duty (6) Learning Styles: 4 factors for student learning preferences: Visual, Aural, Read/write, and Kinesthetic (7) Beliefs about LMS: Perceived usefulness; Perceived ease of use; Enjoyment; ICT self-efficacy (8) Usage Intention: Degree to which a student intends to accept the LMS (9) Usage Behavior of LMS: Frequency and purpose of using LMS; Usage in school as well as outside school; Types of learning activities related to school curriculum (10) Satisfaction with LMS: 4 factors: Learner interface, Learning community, Content, and Personalization Three online survey questionnaires were developed, and a 3-wave panel longitudinal data of Secondary 1 and 2 students were collected from 25 schools (N=1,182). The research team have commenced to investigate students’ learning management system usage, trace the change of students’ perceptions, beliefs, information literacy skills, satisfaction, intention, and usage behavior, examine the effect of student characteristics, contextual factors and social influence, and formulate/test theoretical models to explain and predict student acceptance and continuance of LMS. Since this is a very rich dataset, the development of new models is an ongoing exploration.

17411414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17411414.value: The results of the proposed two-stage model show that although perceived ease of use is not significantly related to the intention to use an LMS at the initial use stage, its relationships with the intention to use an LMS and satisfaction with an LMS use become stronger in later use stages. In contrast, though perceived usefulness has the strongest relationship with intention and satisfaction, these relationships become weaker over time. In addition to user beliefs, students’ LMS use is also significantly related to satisfaction. The results also support the effect of satisfaction in predicting LMS continuance intention. [paper published in Computers and Education] This study aims to model and explain individual variations in acceptance and continuance of LMS using latent growth modeling within the structural equation modeling, which provides a holistic understanding of how belief and use of LMS change over time. Findings demonstrate significant relationships between belief, use, and satisfaction in dynamic changes, particularly the initial level of belief and rate of change in LMS use were found to be strong and positive predictors of students’ learning and system satisfaction of LMS. [paper under review by British Journal of Educational Technology] An integrated model was proposed to explore teenagers’ LMS acceptance and continuance. The results of structural equation modelling supported the hypothesized model. Multi-group SEM was used to test whether the paths in the hypothesized model varied across teenagers with different immigrant backgrounds. The results showed that cultural divides existed in the relations of the proposed model across different groups. [paper under review by Educational Technology Research and Development] The objective of this study is two-fold: first, to examine students’ belief and attitude change in junior secondary students’ LMS use over time; second, to explore the effect of antecedent variables on the model which include conceptions of learning and demographics. An extended two-stage model of cognition change for LMS continuance, which includes perceived ease of use and antecedents, has been established and confirmed. [paper under preparation and will be submitted to Computers in Human Behavior] This study unpacked students’ learning development patterns by integrating the modified Conceptions of Learning Inventory and VARK learning styles inventory through latent profile analysis. LDP’s effect on students’ LMS use was explored. Six LDP were identified and students with different LDP differed in their LMS use. [paper under preparation and will be submitted to New Media and Society]

17411814.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17411814.value: Dr Lu, Jie Dr Zhang, Dong

17411814.label: Project Objectives
17411814.value: To establish a new framework for studying the Internet’s democratizing role in nondemocratic societies such as China. To test how the competing online framing of (anti)corruption news interactively affects political trust in authoritarian regimes such as China. 17411814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17411814.value: Our aim is to contribute to the long-standing debate over how the Internet affects the survival of authoritarian regimes. The extant literature disagrees on the Internet’s political impacts and falls short in explaining how it affects political attitudes, particularly trust in an authoritarian government. Political trust is one of the most important determinants of stability for any regime, and the media exerts a strong influence on such trust in most countries. It plays an essential role in propagandizing state policies and controlling ideology in authoritarian societies such as China. However, scholars report inconsistent findings on media consumption and political support in China, and most focus on traditional media and the frequency of media exposure rather than news content. Particularly lacking is research on the framing effect, which can lead to different positions on an issue. Therefore, little is known about how the Internet, a popular new media platform especially effective in alternative framing, affects political trust. To fill this gap, our proposed research will explore how different online framings of (anti)corruption news affect different categories of political trust in China. Doing so will also allow us to engage with two additional strands of the literature: the very serious problem of corruption in contemporary China and the Internet's impact on the country’s democratic prospects. We will establish a new theoretical framework borrowing ideas from public opinion studies in democracies, and look at the Internet in China as a “quasi-competitive information context.” Of concern will be how different information sources (e.g., official versus unofficial), framing, and receiver attributes interactively influence political trust in this context. Further, how do the special features of the sources and framing styles that are affected, or even produced, by the quasi-competitive context affect receivers’ acceptance of messages and ultimately their political trust? Equipped with this theoretical framework, we will investigate how the Chinese government’s anticorruption propaganda and netizens’ alternative messages interactively and competitively influence public trust. We hypothesize that one-sided exposure to government propaganda may boost public support, whereas netizens’ criticisms can dilute it to various degrees, depending on framing and audience attributes. We will combine in-depth qualitative studies, content analyses, and survey experiments to test our hypotheses. Our findings will illuminate the democratizing effects of the Internet, helping us to determine whether the Internet reinforces (dis)trust in government or alters citizens’ attitude toward it and whether the state can maintain public trust by controlling online information. 本研究旨在为“互联网如何影响威权政权存亡”这一长期争议贡献新的观点。现有文献对于互联网的政治影响存有不同见解，并且缺少关于互联网对政治态度，特别是人们对独裁政府信任度影响方面的研究。政治信任度是影响政权稳定的最重要的决定因素之一。在大多数国家，媒体对政治信任度发挥着举足轻重的作用。尤其是在例如中国这样的威权社会，媒体在宣传国家政策，控制意识形态上都扮演着关键的角色。然而，学者们对中国的传媒消费和政治支持的发现各异，其中大部分学者把研究重点放在传统媒体和媒体曝光率上而非关注报道的内容。特别是对框架效应(framing effect)研究的不足造成我们还不能充分了解互联网对政治信任的影响。框架效应可以造成人们对同一问题持不同立场。而互联网这个流行的、新兴的媒体平台尤其擅长从不同角度描述一件事物(alternative framing)。为了弥补这一不足，我们提出的研究将会深入探讨不同的关于（反）腐败的网络新闻编构如何影响中国不同类别的政治信任度。这项研究同时有利于丰富另外两方面的研究文献：一类是中国严重的贪腐问题，另一类是互联网对国家的民主前景影响。 我们借助一些对民主国家公众舆论研究的思想来建立一个新的理论框架，将中国的互联网视作“半竞争(quasi-competitive)的信息环境”。我们将重点关注在这一背景下，不同信息的来源（例如官方的相对于非官方的）、不同框架和接收者特征如何相互影响政治信任度。具体来说，“半竞争的信息环境”会影响甚至制造信息的来源和框架方式。那么，这些来源和框架方式的特点又会如何影响接受者对信息的吸纳并最终影响到他们的政治信任？基于这个理论框架，我们将研究中国政府打击腐败的宣传和网民们提供的不同信息如何在互动和竞争中影响公众的信任。我们的理论假说是单方面的政府的宣传工作会提高公众支持度，然而网民的批评会随议题框架和受众特点的变化在不同程度上消弱大家对政府的支持。 我们将会结合深度的定性研究、内容分析和问卷实验来检验我们的假设。我们的发现将有利于揭示互联网的民主化效应，并以此帮助我们明确互联网到底是增强人们对政府（不）信任还是改变公众对政府的态度，以及国家能否通过操控网上的信息来维护人民对它的信任。

17411814.label: Realisation of objectives
17411814.value: 1. The first objective is achieved. To realize this objective, we reviewed existing literature and studied the information environment characteristics of China and other authoritarian countries. We have developed the new concept of “quasi-competitive information context” to describe the information environment like China and a new framework of information flow in this context. We name this framework “information compensation”, which consists of “external-oriented information compensation” and “internal-oriented information compensation”. We have used this framework in our latest research, which is presented in international conference. We will get the papers published to further publicize our analytical framework. 2. The second objective is achieved. We have conducted text analysis of big data of online comments to understand the major alternative framing of (anti)corruption news and people’s understanding of official news. We have also conducted online survey experiments to test how different quality of different framing influenced people’s trust in the information. 3. The third objective is achieved. We conducted experiments, text analysis of online comments, and field interviews to learn about government’s control on people’s opinion formation and information pursuit. 4. The fourth objective is achieved. We have lodged public support in China to three different layers based on previous research on government support. In particular, we look at public support to the central government, the top leaders, and anticorruption institutions. We conducted sentiment analysis of the online comments to analyze people’s political trust. In general, all the proposed research objectives have been achieved. Some research with these objectives have been published or presented in international conferences. We hope with more publicity, our new framework and methods can be widely recognized and used by other scholars.

To examine whether different framings of anticorruption propaganda can effectively boost different categories of political trust in the Information Age.

17411814.label: Major findings and research outcome
17411814.value: We carry out three trends of research. The first trend of research on anticorruption campaign itself generates two research articles. “Weapons of the powerful: Authoritarian elite competition and politicized anticorruption in China”, is published in Comparative Political Studies, a leading journal in political science. By studying the changing intensity of news reports of anticorruption campaigns, along with other measures, we find that corruption investigation in China is most intense during power transitions, especially when the predecessors and the successors are in fierce power competition. Anticorruption is an important way to consolidate power for politicians. The second article is “Eating, Drinking, and Power Signaling in Institutionalized Authoritarianism,” published in Journal of Contemporary China, a top journal in area studies. Using local party mouthpieces’ reports of Xi’s antiwaste reports, we find that the antiwaste campaign is a way for Xi to signal his power. Local governments by echoing to his call of antiwaste showed their loyalty to Xi and therefore exhibit Xi’s informal power network in the party and army. The second trend of research studies social reactions to the campaign resulting in two articles. “Big Tigers, Big Data” is published in Public Administration Review, the No.1 journal in Public Administration. By conducting text analysis of a big data of online comments of the anticorruption, we find fighting high rank officials intensively, can help boost political trust in the top leaders and the central government. However, trust in institutions, such as the anticorruption agencies and laws did not increase much. The second article, “Information Compensation and Political Rumors in an Authoritarian Country” is presented in the 6th Asian Polmeth in Japan. We find that months before the government formally announced the downfall of several national leaders, the public had correctly speculated the central government’s decision based on the clues of formal news reports. We define this phenomenon as “internal-oriented information compensation in a quasi-competitive information environment”, which helps government to prepare for public opinions, but also fostered political cynicism of the public. The third trend of research testing our hypotheses resulting in a working paper not publicized yet. The survey experiment is politically sensitive to conduct, which took us time. However, we have obtained the results, which are generally consistent with our theory: When official news and online rumors compete, people trust higher quality rumors more, a special feature of quasi-competitive information environment.

17411814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17411814.value: Findings of this research project have a large potential for further development of research. One implication from our current findings is the intention of anticorruption campaigns and their possible influence on public opinions, such as political support of government. If anticorruption is largely politicized for purging political enemies, how much do the Chinese public perceive so and how much anticorruption campaigns can help boost political support as the government attempts? We have already developed this idea into a new research proposal applying for GRF. The other important implication lies in our theoretical framework of “quasi-competitive information environment” and “information compensation”. We plan to design a series of new research using this framework to further understand the Chinese information market. Finally, the PI has planned to write a book about the politics of anticorruption in China based on the findings of this research project and her other related research. Tentative research has been conducted.

17411814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17411814.value: The whole process of writing research proposal, applying for GRF, and generating research output has greatly benefited the PI and her coauthors. The comments from GRF reviewers and journal reviewers have been helpful in guiding the research team to refine research questions, theoretical frameworks, and arguments, and research designs. The research outputs generated from this project so far have been well received by the field. Several papers have been widely read, downloaded, and cited, with positive comments. The findings have contributed to existing knowledge about Chinese elite politics, information politics, and anticorruption work. The process of conducting this project has also inspired the research team for several new ideas for future research. Team members became more experienced researchers in the procedure and RPg students are trained in the process. Larger research networks are developed for the project. The datasets built will also benefit future research. New methods developed by the team have also inspired other scholars. We appreciate RGC and HKU’s support of the research.

17500014.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17500014.value: Mrs Lowry, Michelle Rene Mr Webb, David M. Dr Zhu, Wenjie

17500014.label: Project Objectives
17500014.value: Examine the influence of company control profiles on board of director compositions. Determine implications for related studies. Extend related research. Inform stock exchanges and regulators.
rows: Examine the influence of company control profiles on board of director compositions.

17500014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500014.value: Extensive prior research examines how board of director characteristics influence company characteristics, for example, how board size and member social connections relate to company performance (e.g., Chen 2008, Geletkanycz and Boyd 2011, Larcker et al. 2013). A pervasive design challenge in this literature is how to control for “endogenous influences” on both company and board characteristics so that the effects of board characteristics on company characteristics can be isolated (Brown et al. 2011). This study proposes to examine an even more fundamental endogeneity of the influence company control preferences on board characteristics. Specifically, we will consider how company ownership structures and controlling interests influence board compositions in relation to two regulatory changes in board membership requirements in Hong Kong. To our knowledge, this study is among the first to specifically focus on endogenous influences of company ownership profiles on board composition and resulting implications for company-board relations. Whereas Clune et al. (2013) provide qualitative evidence of CEO influence on director nominations, Fracassi and Tate (2012) find firms with more powerful CEOs to select directors with closer ties, Wintoki et al. (2012) adopt a dynamic panel GMM estimator to address endogeneity, and Guest (2008) offers U.K. evidence regarding determinants of board size and composition, little direct empirical evidence exists regarding how company ownership structures and controlling interests influence board compositions and memberships. Hong Kong offers a propitious setting in which to isolate and document the endogenous influences of company ownership profiles on board compositions for several reasons. First, Hong Kong’s stock market is large (with 1,538 listed companies at 31-Dec-2012 and 891 at 31-Dec-2004) with a bifurcated distribution of directors serving on multiple (few) boards at large- (small-) capitalisation firms (details below), thus facilitating the identification of preference patterns. Second, Hong Kong offers a diverse cross-section of control, including sizable proportions of listed companies closely held either by families or government entities that may prefer to perpetuate control. Third, and importantly, changes in Hong Kong listing rules effective October 2004 (year-end 2012) required three (one-third) independent non-executive directors (INEDs), which provide two precisely defined natural experiments for examining how company control preferences influence board member selections (HKSE). Thus, this study will utilize Hong Kong’s corporate control diversity, numerous board cross-memberships, and two regulatory changes to document the influences of company control preferences on board member selections and company-board relations, with attendant implications for corporate governance research, practice and regulation. 之前的大量研究检查了董事会的特性如何影响公司的特性，比如说，董事会的规模和董事们的社会关系与公司表现的相关度 (e.g., Chen 2008, Geletkanycz and Boyd 2011, Larcker et al. 2013)。在这类文献中，一个广泛存在的研究难题，来自于如何辨认其他目前尚不可知的“内生性影响因子”，从而使之前的研究结论更确信 (Brown et al. 2011)。本文提出一个更本质的关于“内生性影响因子”的研究方向：公司管理层对控制权的需求，会反过来影响董事会的特性。具体来说，我们利用了香港最近几年内连续两次董事会规则变更的契机，来研究公司所有权结构和控制权对董事会构成的影响。 据我们所知，本次研究属于最新的专注于论证董事会内生性影响因子的课题。在此之前，Clune et al. (2013) 提供了公司首席执行官(CEO)对董事会提名影响的定性证据；Fracassi and Tate (2012) 的结论是越强大的CEO会选择越有亲近关系的董事； Wintoki et al (2012) 采用了动态GMM经济模型测量方法来处理内生性难题；Guest (2008)提供了来自英国的证据，以此说明是什么决定了董事会的规模和构成。尽管如此，目前的研究几乎无法提供来自实证方面的直接证据：有没有数据可以证明，公司所有权结构和控制权需求会影响到董事会本身的构成，而不是之前普遍认为的相反的关系？ 香港提供了一个非常难得的机会来实证以上的猜想，原因有三：1，香港的股市总量非常大，2014年底港交所共有上市公司891所，至2012年底共有1538所；关于董事席位在大/小公司分布的数据非常有信息量，从而能够帮助我们更好的检测其中的规律。2，香港的许多上市公司能够体现出很多种跨行业的具有特异性的控制主体特性，比方说由家族控制，或者由政府控制，从而为本次研究提供了充分的关于公司控制权的信息量。3，一个很重要的机构背景是，港交所从2004十月开始实行三位独立董事规则，又接着从2012年底改为1/3独立董事规则。两次上市规则的改变非常巧妙地提供了来自公司外部的强制执行的近似自然实验，从而为本次研究提供了独一无二的实施条件。因此，我们将利用香港资本市场特有的公司控制模式，董事会的数据信息，以及两次规则改变的契机，来取得关于公司控制权和董事会选择内生性的一些新结论。这些结论将为企业治理的学术研究，从业，和立法提供有力的佐证。

17500214.label: Project Objectives
17500214.value: One major objective of this project is to develop a conceptual framework with the institution-based view as its theoretical underpinning to examine the choices of market entry mode of foreign affiliates of multinational corporations in different regions within host countries. The second major objective is to examine the independent and relative effects of the level of development of subnational economic, political and social institutions on the choice of ownership structure of foreign affiliates in different sub-national regions. The third major objective is to examine in which regions within a host country multinational corporations are more likely to choose acquisition rather than greenfield investment mode of foreign market entry. The forth major objective is to examine in which regions within a host country multinational corporations are more likely to have the governance choice of expatriate management rather than local management. The fifth objective is to provide implications for theoretical development, international managers, and policy makers.
