17500214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500214.value: This project draws on the institution-based view to explore the influences of the level of the development of subnational institutions on the choices of foreign market entry mode of multinational corporations (MNCs) in subnational regions within a host country. Previous research, drawing on the transaction costs economics, suggests that MNCs choose the entry mode that minimizes the transaction costs (Anderson and Gatignon, 1986). Other studies, based on Dunning’s (1980, 1988) framework, reveal that the ownership advantages of a firm, the location advantages of a market, and the internalization advantages of integrating transactions within the firm are the key determinants of that choice (Hill et al., 1990). The basic premise of these perspectives is that MNCs desire to minimize transaction costs, increase resource access opportunities, and secure greater control over the operation of their affiliates. A more recent line of research, drawing on the neo-institutional perspective, suggests that the entry mode choice reflects the desire of MNCs to exchange ownership for legitimacy in host countries (Chan, et al., 2006; Lu, 2002). While these studies stress the importance of the host-country institutional environment, the institutional environments vary across regions within a host country because of the differences in the institutional development of subnational institutions which consist of economic, political and social institutions (Chan et al., 2010), finding that these subnational institutions jointly explain the variation in foreign affiliate performance. However, little is known about the independent, relative effects of the three aspects of subnational institutions on the foreign market entry mode choice of MNCs in different regions within a country. The three research questions are (1) what the independent, relative influences do the levels of the development of subnational economic, political and social institutions have on the choice of ownership structure of foreign affiliates; (2) what the influences do the levels of the development of subnational economic, political and social institutions have on the choice between acquisition and greenfield investment mode of entry; and (3) what the influences do the levels of the development of subnational economic, political and social institutions have on the governance choice between expatriate and local management. The project intends to develop a measurement of the development of subnational economic, political and social institutions. The project will provide implications for theoretical development and policy makers; and implications for managers who have to deal with institutional uncertainties in different regions within a country. 基於制度基礎觀，本研究探究在東道國內各個區域不同制度發展水平對於跨國企業市場進入模式選擇的影響。基於交易成本理論的研究指出跨國企業偏向選取可以實現交易成本最小化的市場進入模式(Anderson and Gatignon, 1986; Hennart, 1988)。 而其他基於Dunning理論框架（1980, 1988）的研究強調企業的所有權優勢，市場的區位優勢，以及整合交易的內部化優勢是決定進入模式選擇的關鍵要素（Hill et al., 1990; Luo, 2001）。這些理論視角的基本假設強調跨國企業希望最小化交易成本，增加獲取資源的機會，以及確保對於海外子公司運作的控制。而最近基於新制度理論視角的研究指出市場進入模式的選擇也反映了跨國企業希望通過所有權交換獲取在東道國市場上的合法性（Chan, et al., 2006; Lu, 2002）。儘管這些研究強調了海外子公司嵌入的東道國國家制度環境的重要性，但是在東道國國內各個區域的制度環境也存在顯著的不同，體現在區域制度發展水平的不同（Chan et al., 2010）。因此本研究針對東道國國內制度環境不同的重要性，檢驗區域制度是如何影響跨國企業在東道國國內不同區域的市場進入模式選擇的。 本研究的三個主要研究問題包括（1）區域制度對於海外子公司所有權結構選擇有哪些影響；（2）不同區域經濟，政治和社會制度的發展水平分別對海外子公司所有權結構選擇的影響；（3）不同區域經濟，政治和社會制度的發展水平分別對併購和綠地投資兩種市場進入模式選擇的影響。本研究還會開發對於區域經濟，政治和社會制度發展水平的測量。本研究的研究結果會為理論發展以及政策制定者提供重要借鑒意義；也會為跨國企業的決策者提供一定的管理啟示因為他們要面對發達國家以及/或發展中國家的不同區域制度。

17500314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500314.value: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX) was enacted with the intention of restoring investor confidence through the implementation of rules and regulations emphasizing accountability, transparency and reliability in corporate disclosures. Some recent empirical studies examine the effectiveness of SOX in reducing agency cost and improving overall corporate governance, but mostly focus on its impact on executive pay (Carter et al. 2009; Cohen et al. 2011; Chen et al. 2013). This research project provides a comprehensive analysis of the economic consequences of the new internal control reporting (ICR) requirements imposed by Sections 302 and 404 of SOX, which impose affirmative duties on managers and auditors to evaluate and attest to the effectiveness of internal controls and disclose any control weaknesses. The proposed model emphasizes not only the strategic interaction between internal control and external audit in detecting accounting manipulation, but also the multiple roles of accounting information in financial reporting that induce diverging reporting incentives. I use this model to explore the broader relationships between internal control and other corporate governance mechanisms on motivating managerial effort and restricting misreporting behavior, and investigate how these relationships vary with regulations under Sections 302 and 404 of SOX. I will make predictions regarding the effects on a firm’s choices of compensation policy and internal control quality as well as on its external auditor’s choice of audit quality; all these elements being important determinants of the accuracy of the firm’s accounting information. I hope that this project will contribute to the ongoing debate regarding the costs and benefits of making SOX internal control quality disclosures, and provide guidance for future empirical research on corporate governance. 2002年頒布的薩班斯 - 奧克斯利法案（SOX）旨在實施強調問責制、透明性和可靠性的公司披露相關的制度准則以重建投資者信心。近年來一些實証研究探討了薩班斯法案在降低代理成本和提高整體公司治理上的成效，但它們大都聚焦其對高管薪酬的影響（Carter等 2009; Cohen等 2011; Chen等 2013）。薩班斯法案的302章和404章對內部控制報告（ICR）提出了新的要求，規定了作為管理層和外部審計師 對公司內部控制的有效性進行評估、驗証並披露控制薄弱環節的肯定職責 。本項目旨在對薩班斯法案302章和404章有關內部控制報告的新規定會導致的經濟結果進行全面分析。本項目採用的數學模型不僅強調了內部控制和外部審計在檢測會計操縱中的戰略互動，還強調了會計信息在財務報告中導致分歧的報告動機的多重角色。此數學模型將用來探索內部控制和其他公司治理機制在激勵管理層努力作為和限制會計操縱行為上更深層次的關系，並研究這些關系如何隨薩班斯法案302章和404章的規定而變化。公司高管薪酬制度、內部控制質量以及外部審計質量都是公司會計信息准確性的重要決定因素，本項目將就新法案對這些因素的影響作出預測。我希望這個項目能對有關薩班斯內控質量披露的成本和收益的持續爭論做出貢獻，並就未來有關公司治理的實証研究提供理論上的指導。

17500314.label: Realisation of objectives
17500314.value: The objectives of this study are 100% achieved. A theory paper titled “The Effects of Internal Control Reporting Regulation on Control Quality, Compensation and Audit Effort” has been written and presented internally at HKU accounting research workshop on October 16, 2015 and externally at the 12th Workshop on Accounting and Economics on June 23-24, 2016, in Tilburg, Netherlands. The latter is a highly reputable international accounting workshop mainly for scholars working in analytical research in the fields of accounting and economics. I received many constructive comments and suggestions to improve the paper from the workshop participants, and have revised the paper by incorporating these comments and suggestions. In November 2016, I submitted the revised paper to The Accounting Review, one of the top peer-reviewed international journals in accounting with an acceptance rate of less than 10%. On March 7, 2017, I received the decision letter and two review reports from The Accounting Review, inviting for revision and resubmission to The Accounting Review. The two reviews were very thorough that consist of 8 pages in total and ask for a major revision. After going through a substantial revision of the paper that addresses the comments and incorporates the suggestions from the editor and the two reviewers, I resubmitted the paper to The Accounting Review on November 28, 2017. On April 16, 2018, I received the final decision letter from The Accounting Review. While one of the two reviewers liked the paper and suggested some constructive comments on further improving the writing of the paper, the other reviewer insisted that the contribution of the paper is not substantial for publication in The Accounting Review. Unfortunately, the editor agreed and decided to reject the paper. Since the editor and the reviewer with a negative view did not deny the importance of the research questions nor showed any serious concerns about any of the assumptions or results in the paper, I believe that the rejection decision was mostly based on personal preference. Incorporating the suggestions from the more positive reviewer and having the help from a professional copy editor to improve the readability of the paper, I have recently resubmitted the paper to The Review of Accounting Studies, which is considered one of the A- journals in accounting.

17500314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500314.value: The results obtained in the paper titled “The Effects of Internal Control Reporting Regulation on Control Quality, Compensation and Audit Effort” are summarized as follows: ABSTRACT: New internal control reporting (ICR) requirements under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX) imposed affirmative duties on managers and auditors to evaluate and attest to the effectiveness of internal controls. This paper studies the role of ICR regulation in alleviating accounting manipulation. My basic model with one firm emphasizes the strategic interaction between internal control and external audit in its detection, as well as the stewardship and valuation roles of accounting information in financial reporting. I investigate whether and why ICR requirements under SOX can enhance incentives for internal control quality and audit effort, and make predictions regarding their effects on audit failure rate, manager’s expected compensation, audit fee and current owner’s expected payoff. An extension to a multi-firm setting suggests that ICR regulation can improve social welfare in the presence of an endogenous norm of internal control quality.

17500314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500314.value: Investor confidence in reporting firms’ financial statements was severely shaken by a series of high-profile corporate and accounting scandals at the turn of the 21st century, including the infamous Enron scandal. Charged with investigating its accounting practices, a special committee of Enron’s board of directors identified the failure of internal controls as a key reason for its collapse. In the wake of Enron, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX) was enacted with the intention of restoring investor confidence through the implementation of rules and regulations emphasizing accountability, transparency and reliability in corporate disclosures. Inter alia, SOX Sections 302 and 404 imposed new internal control reporting (ICR) requirements on reporting companies and their auditors to ensure the accuracy of information provided to investors. In coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) created detailed guidance for ICR requirements in the form of auditing standards. The implementation of these new requirements has given rise to ongoing debate about whether their costs outweigh their benefits, and why they ought to be mandatory. The purpose of this paper is to formulate a theoretical model to address these concerns.

17500414.value: 行政總裁抵押個人持股之經濟後果

17500414.label: Project Objectives
17500414.value: To study market reaction to stock price when a firm first discloses that its shares are pledged by insiders. Findings will indicate whether the market reacts negatively to such disclosure. To examine the performance of firms in which insiders have pledged shares. The project will look at one-year stock returns and earnings changes after pledging. To provide empirical evidence of the relationship between shares pledged and risk-taking behavior. The project will examine whether managers engage in more or less risk-taking projects and stock return volatility when insiders pledge their own shareholdings.

17500414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500414.value: Equity compensation, such as stock options and restricted stock, comprises a significant portion of U.S. executives’ total compensation. After a long period of employment, an executive may have accumulated considerable wealth through his or her shareholding in the firm, and may pledge these shares as collateral for a loan. Pledging allows the title to remain with the pledger, but the pledged shares may be subject to sale if necessary to settle the loan (Larcker and Tayan 2010). Since 2006, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has required all firms to disclose any pledged executive shares in proxy statements, but to date very little research has been done to understand investors’ perception of such disclosures and how pledging affects the decisions and risks of a firm. This proposal attempts to provide empirical evidence for the effect of pledged executive shares by investigating the economic consequences for firms. Specifically, I will examine 1) market reaction to stock price when a firm first discloses via proxy statement the existence of pledged executive shares, 2) the change in long-term firm performance after pledging, and 3) the subsequent effect on risk-taking behavior. The findings of this proposal will have implications for both academic research and policy-makers. First, we will gain an understanding of whether the investors view the pledging of shares by executives as poor corporate governance, and thus whether they believe the board of a firm and the SEC should restrict the practice. Second, I will provide empirical evidence to show whether firms engage in risk-taking behavior when executives have pledged their shares as collateral, with implications for the question of how equity compensation affects the risks of firms. 權益薪酬，如股票期權和限制性股票，在美國已佔經理總薪酬 的主要部分。 經過長時間就業，經理已積累自己的財富在公司 的股票。因此，經理可以以自己的股票作為貸款的抵押。 抵押股票的股份所有權仍屬於經理，一旦不能償還貸款便須出 售股票以作還款(Larcker和Tayan2010)。 2006年，美國證券交易委員會要求所有企業披露是否有任何 經理抵押自己的股份。但到目前為止這話題只有很少的研究。 這提案試圖提供證據在抵押股份的影響。我們將考察市場對 抵押股份在股票價格反應，對長期公司業績的影響，以及經理 會否進行投資冒險行為。

17500414.label: Realisation of objectives
17500414.value: All the three objectives have been achieved. First, we looked at the market reaction around the proxy statement release date when a firm first discloses that its shares are pledged by insiders. We do not find negative change in stock price. One possible reason is there is too much new information contained in the proxy statement. (Other possible reasons are discussed in Section 6.1) Therefore, we may need to change our research design for H1. Specifically we plan to identify those firms with high pledged ratio and examine whether the stock price reaction is larger for these firms. We will also run a time-series analysis to look at whether there is a difference in stock price reaction around the proxy statement date of the pledged firms. Second, we included earnings quality to measure firm performance in objective 2. The reason is on the one hand, managers may have incentive to manage earnings to improve performance of the firms after shares are pledged. On the other hand, managers may want to disclose better earnings quality to signal the firm performance. Preliminary findings are discussed in section 6.1. Third, we looked at the risk-taking behavior of the pledged firms. Results are discussed in section 6.1.

17500414.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500414.value: 1. We did not find any market reaction to the disclosure by the firm with the shares pledged by the insiders. There are two possible reasons. One is the investors do not pay attention to such disclosure. The second is probably there is a delay between the disclosure and the pledging event happened and the market already reacted to the event before the disclosure. 2. We find that the earnings quality and firm performance improves for firms with shares pledged. Specifically, the earnings becomes more persistent, the accruals are lower, and profitability increases. This is consistent with the argument that stock price of the firm is undervalued and insiders therefore have taken advantage of the insider information to pledge the shares. 3. We find that firms with shares pledged become less risk-taking. The result is consistent with the notion that executives become more risk-adverse to avoid any downside risk by cutting risky projects.

17500414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500414.value: We find economically significant results in the project, especially objectives 2 and 3. But we need to further polish the empirical analyses to make the project publishable. Specifically, we will partition the sample into firms with relatively high pledged ratio and with low pledged ratio and re-examine the three objectives to see whether this will drive different results between the two groups. We will also investigate whether the results will be different between the top executives (CEO and CFO) who pledge their shares and the largest shareholders who pledge their shares. We will also look at whether there is a shift in the investment mix of the firms after having shares pledged.

17500414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500414.value: Equity compensation, such as stock options and restricted stock, comprises a significant portion of U.S. executives’ total compensation. After a long period of employment, an executive may have accumulated considerable wealth through his or her shareholding in the firm, and may pledge these shares as collateral for a loan. Pledging allows the title to remain with the pledger, but the pledged shares may be subject to sale if necessary to settle the loan (Larcker and Tayan 2010). In this project we find that the market does not react to the first disclosure of such pledging. However, the earnings quality improves. Specifically, earnings become more persistent, accruals are lower, and profitability increases. In addition, we find that managers of pledged firms become less risk-taking, indicating that they become more risk-adverse to avoid any downside risk by cutting risky projects.

17500514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500514.value: 網上拍賣市場中用戶反饋的時序效應：用戶研究和貝葉斯更新模型

17500514.label: Project Objectives
17500514.value: To validate the order effect of feedback on both transaction price premiums and buyers’ trust toward sellers in online auction markets. To propose and evaluate the use of a Bayesian updating model in predicting transaction price premiums in online auction markets.
rows: To validate the order effect of feedback on both transaction price premiums and buyers’ trust toward sellers in online auction markets.
To propose and evaluate the use of a Bayesian updating model in predicting transaction price premiums in online auction markets.

17500514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500514.value: Online auction markets process a large number of transactions every day. The transaction data in these markets are useful for understanding the buyers and sellers who engage in those transactions. Previous research has shown that sellers with different reputation levels, as shown by the ratings and comments left in online feedback systems, enjoy different levels of price premiums in their transactions. Feedback scores and feedback texts have been shown to correlate with buyers’ level of trust in a seller and the price premium that buyers are willing to pay (Ba and Pavlou 2002; Pavlou and Dimoka 2006). However, these models do not consider the order effect, that is, recently posted feedback potentially being considered more important by buyers than that posted longer ago.The proposed study will address this shortcoming in the literature by testing the order effect and proposing a Bayesian updating model to represent the interactions between buyers and sellers in online auction markets, taking the order effect into consideration. The proposed model takes the profile of a targeted seller as input to compute that seller’s reputation and predicts the price premium of his or her items. To validate the order effect and evaluate the proposed model, a lab experiment will be conducted and real-life transaction data will be collected from the eBay online auction market. The contribution of this research will be twofold. First, we will demonstrate the order effect in the feedback mechanism on price premiums. Second, we will develop a model that better predicts the price premiums in online auction markets relative to existing models. The proposed model will be useful in fostering our understanding of these increasingly important markets. 網上拍賣市場的交易量十分龐大，這些交易數據可供更好地了解買賣雙方的交易行為。已有研究指出，通過交易的反饋評價系統，由評分和評論顯示出不同信譽水平的賣家可以在交易過程中享受不同的溢價水平。反饋的評分和文字與買家對賣家的信任及溢價支付意願呈現相關關係(Ba & Pavlou, 2002; Pavlou & Dimoka, 2006)。但現有研究模型並未考慮反饋的時序效應，即用戶可能認為近期發布的評論比較長時間前的評論更加重要。本研究將先驗證時序效應，再運用貝葉斯更新模型來呈現考慮時序效應的拍賣雙方互動，以填補現有文獻的這一空白。本模型以目標賣家的資料作為輸入，進而計算其信譽並預測產品的溢價。為了驗證時序效應和本文提出的模型，我們將從eBay拍賣市場中收集真實的交易數據及進行用戶研究實驗。本研究將於網上拍賣領域體現出雙重貢獻。首先，我們可以驗證拍賣反饋評價系統中針對溢價的時序效應；其次，本文提出的模型與現有模型相比，可更好地預測網上拍賣的溢價水平，並使我們進一步了解愈顯重要的網上拍賣市場。

A Bayesian updating model was proposed to predict transaction price premiums in online auction markets. The model was evaluated using field data collected from eBay and analysis results showed that the model performed better than benchmark models.

17500514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500514.value: This study proposed and tested the time order effect in online auction markets and proposed a Bayesian Updating Model to represent the interactions between the buyers and sellers in such markets, taking the time order effect into consideration. The proposed model takes the feedback profile of a targeted seller as input to compute the seller’s reputation and predict the price premium of an item of the seller. In order to validate the time order effect and evaluate the proposed model, a user experiment was conducted and real-life transaction data were collected from the eBay online auction market. In our evaluation, the time order effect is confirmed, and the proposed model outperforms the benchmark models, which are based on feedback rating history or feedback comments, reaching a higher average adjusted R-squared. We also find that the feedback text comments explain more variance of price premium than the ratings since the comments offer relatively more detailed information of the seller. The contribution of this research is twofold. First, we verify the time order effect in the feedback mechanism on price premiums. Second, we propose a model that provides a better prediction of price premium in online auction markets than existing models. The study advances our understanding of the feedback mechanism in online auction markets.

17500514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500514.value: Text comments are categorized manually in this study. It is tedious to read and categorize text comments due to the high volume. Therefore, it is worthwhile to design a machine learning algorithm to categorize the text comments automatically. Furthermore, there are other factors that may affect buyers’ perception of the importance of feedbacks, such as the web site’s display. It would be interesting to study how various factors affect buyers’ trust and price premiums.

17500514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500514.value: In online auction markets, buyers rely on the feedback profile of a seller to estimate whether the seller will ensure the quality of the transaction. Previous research has shown that the feedback profile of a seller has an impact of the price premium that the seller receives. In previous studies, feedbacks posted at different times were considered equally. We propose that feedbacks posted at different time may have different value in building the buyer's trust in the seller. We validate this effect in our study through a user experiment. In addition, we propose a mathematical model, called the Bayesian Updating Model, that incorporates this time order effect, and empirical data show that the proposed model performed better than existing model in the prediction of price premium.

17500614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500614.value: 中产阶级的政治经济学

17500614.label: Project Objectives
17500614.value: We plan to empirically document the phenomenon of middle class activism in developing and emerging countries in the past decades, both anecdotally and systematically. We plan to build and characterize non-monotone equilibria in a global game model with a continuum of citizens. We plan to provide a relatively general methodology to study the the properties of non-monotone equilibria, including equilibrium existence, multiplicity and stability. We plan to study the interaction between model uncertainty and payoff uncertainty in the global game framework. The literature has been advanced by incorporating each feature separately. This project investigates the interplay of the two mechanisms and study its resulting effects in coordination games. We also plan to analyze the dynamic aspect of the game and investigate the conditions for an initial protest to beget the so-called "snow balling effect" that induces more citizens to participate in the later stages. To address this question, we need to enrich our baseline model and accommodate a richer set-up to allow for dynamic choices.

17500614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500614.value: The authors empirically test three key mechanisms of their theory: • First, they show that the poorer are the respondents to the World Values Survey, the more likely they are to be politically pessimistic. This result is robust to various definitions of pessimism. • Second, the data reveal that people who hold more pessimistic views about real changes in politics are less likely to participate in mass political action. More than a fifth of respondents in the least pessimistic group claim that they have ever participated in demonstrations against governments; while fewer than one in ten of the most pessimistic group report this. • Third, the evidence indicates that poor people do not have sufficient knowledge about their actual status in society and tend to believe that they are closer to the median than they actually are. As a result, the poor wrongly believe that many more people would be as pessimistic as they are, which further prevents them from taking action.

17500614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500614.value: It is a longstanding puzzle that the middle classes rather than the poor typically cause political ferment and spearhead mass movements against the status quo in modern societies. After all, in most circumstances, it is the poor who should be more dissatisfied with the current regime – and their opportunity costs of taking action are lower than those of the middle classes. In general, the new study shows, the political aspirations and involvement of individuals are directly influenced by their experiences and economic status in society. The authors first confirm empirically the puzzling phenomena of the activism of the middle classes and the passivity of the poor. They analyse political participation data from the third, fourth and fifth waves of the World Values Survey, which cover 78 countries from 1994 to 2007. The data suggest that the lower and upper classes are indeed significantly less likely to participate in demonstrations against governments than those in the middle social strata. While the established view rationalises this phenomenon with education, the new study demonstrates that it is far from the complete story: once the authors tease out the effects of education empirically, the political aspirations of individuals are still significantly correlated with their economic status. The new theory that these researchers propose shows that the economic circumstances or experiences of individuals in society may shape their attitudes towards the prospect of social movements. Downtrodden individuals are pessimistic and reluctant: based on their own circumstances, they perceive the current regime as bad, rationally infer that all governments are bad and therefore believe mass movements are futile.

17500714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500714.value: 分析师团队的使用（ Thurm 2005）在上升，与经纪公司指派小组采取如多段大公司工作，或采取紧急任务，例如预测财务危机公司（布朗和2009年于贡） 。经纪公司也争取在个人和团队的水平，机构投资者的排名。当分析师移动到新的经纪公司，他们的预测性能变化较少，当他们移动作为一个团队，（ Groysberg2006） 。这些证据显示了分析师团队绩效的具体因素的存在。 此前有研究发现，多种因素会影响分析师的表现，虽然他们的研究结果可能无法概括分析团队的预测性能，因为它们不区分那些球队取得由个别分析师的预测。更重要的是，团队的预测源于自由互动和开放的讨论，而不是个别分析师的信念的数学聚集。 在建议的研究中，我们将调查的分析师团队的预测性能，特别是是否以团队为基础的预测精度由团队结构的特点决定的。答案将是有益的投资者利用分析师的预测，特别是那些由分析师团队发出，形成自己的交易策略。此外，我们的研究结果可以提供有关如何有效地组织各个人才进入团队从业有意义的证据。对于如何执行任务的相互依赖专业团体可以从团队合作中受益有限的证据。虽然现有文献研究个人如何的技能和能力能够影响团队绩效（西和1997年艾伦，威廉姆斯和1998年O'Reilly出版） ，并分析影响因素的个人专长（米哈伊尔等，1997 ; 1999年克莱门特，雅各等人1999年，赫斯特等人，2004 ） ，所缺少的是分析师队伍的组成如何影响团队绩效。这项研究构成了试图填补这一空白。

17500714.label: Realisation of objectives
17500714.value: In this study, we investigate how an important group dynamic – group task cohesion that is determined by directors’ social similarity – affects outside directors’ reports that the CEO influences their beliefs. The level of CEO influence is a key element of board independence. Specifically, we hypothesize the following relationships. First, as the degree of social similarity between an outside director and other directors increases, the more task cohesion this outside director experiences in her board. In turn, the degree of task cohesion (the commitment to work together to achieve group goals) increases the extent to which outside directors make efforts to obtain, and ultimately receive, information from the firm and CEO. Second, information sharing leads to greater independence from the CEO. Additional analyses show that the relationship between information sharing and CEO’s influence is especially pronounced when the CEO allows for cognitive conflicts, i.e., when board processes encourage the expression of these viewpoints and constructive criticism thereof (Forbes & Milliken, 1999). Examining these research questions allows for a richer understanding of the processes through which outside directors provide better monitoring of management; an understanding of processes may lead to suggestions for improving board practices. Process research of this nature also informs the long-standing debate about whether regulators should dictate the composition of corporate boards given that input-based attributes (i.e., the external, observable attributes of individual directors such as demographic characteristics, education level, and professional background) may have less effect on group decisions than process factors (i.e., the factors concerning board’s communications, interactions, and dynamics). While corporate boards in America now are dominated by outside directors, there still is debate about whether this has led to effective governance (Romano, 2005). Further, other countries’ regulators currently are debating whether to follow the United States in increasing the required percentage of outside directors (Chu, 2013). Also, under the auspices of enhancing social diversity, regulatory pressure in the United States and elsewhere recently has focused on pushing corporate boards to add more female and minority directors (Aguilar, 2010; Ahern & Dittmar, 2012). Our findings related to the processes through which outside directors provide monitoring of management may also be relevant to this issue – both from the perspective that input measures may not be predictive of monitoring and from the perspective that social similarity could, at least under certain circumstances, lead to more effective monitoring than social diversity.

17500714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500714.value: Corporate boards in America are dominated currently by outside directors because of the belief that they are more effective at monitoring management. There continues to be debate, however, concerning whether regulators should dictate board composition using input-based attributes of directors such as outside status. Opponents contend that board independence is best established through applying voluntary best practices to board processes. In this research, we study board processes and examine how group task cohesion that is determined by directors’ social similarity affects outside directors’ reports that the CEO influences their beliefs, a key element of director independence. We propose that the degree of social similarity (similarity as to backgrounds) between outside directors and other directors is positively related to the degree of commitment directors have toward the board’s tasks. We show that this task commitment (cohesion) has a positive effect on directors’ efforts to obtain and receive information from the firm and CEO. Additional analyses show that the effect of information sharing on the level of CEO influence of outside directors depends on the presence of cognitive conflict – constructive discussion among directors regarding differing viewpoints – between the outside directors and the inside directors. We test our hypotheses using a survey, which was developed based on in-depth field interviews, and the archival data on directors’ attributes as well as firm-level outcomes. Results support the hypotheses, and have implications for regulators and boards.

17500714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500714.value: There are a number of interesting implications of and future research questions related to our research. First, since social similarity also can create social cohesion, which can create detrimental effects on board performance, is cognitive conflict alone enough to stop these effects? Instead, perhaps there is something about the Chinese setting such as a cultural norm emphasizing collective behavior that also must be in place for social cohesion either to stay in check or to not seep into the group decision-making process. Indeed, scholars currently are debating whether the independent (outside) director model used by the U.S. and being pushed in China will work there (Clarke, 2006; Shen & Jia, 2005). Second, we find that cognitive conflict is not associated with social similarity, task cohesion, or social cohesion, contrary to some of the previous literature’s conjectures. Future research could examine the conditions under which this occurs, given that governance scholars advocate this combination of factors for effective monitoring. Third, future research also could explore the determinants of cognitive conflict per se, especially those related to the CEO given the recent literature on how the CEO’s personality and background affect corporate policies (e.g., Bamber, Jiang, & Wang 2010; Dikolli, Mayew, & Steffen, 2012; Dyreng, Hanlon, and Maydew, 2010; Hribar & Yang, 2011).

17500714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500714.value: Using a survey of 59 Chinese outside directors and archival data on the directors and the firms on whose boards they sit, this study provides evidence on how board processes affect directors’ self-reported invulnerability from influence by the CEO, a key element of board independence. Specifically, we find that task cohesion created by social similarity among board members leads to greater information sharing among outside directors and corporate executives. Further, when the CEO allows for cognitive conflict in the boardroom, information sharing is negatively related to directors’ reports of how influenced they are by the CEO. When the CEO does not allow for cognitive conflict, information sharing has no relation to this influence measure. Moreover, the influence measure is positively related to abnormal accruals and CEO compensation, and negatively related to CEO turnover. These findings indicate that self-reported CEO influence can be a valid measure of director independence. Finally, and of most significance, this measure is significantly related to these outcomes that reflect effective board monitoring when the traditional measure of independence (proportion of outside directors) is included in analyses, and the traditional measure itself is not related to these outcomes.

17501014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501014.value: We document the central role of collateral in the pricing of tri-party repos. Markets are competitive for repos with safe collaterals, but are severely segmented for repos with risky collaterals such as equities and low-grade corporate bonds. Fund families are the sole contributors of the segmentation, and collateral concentration is the main determinant in the substantial variation in repo pricing, both across and within segments. The segmented structure points to Fidelity as a systemically important player and the markets potential fragility. Facing market segmentation, dealers optimize financing cost by allocating their collateral across fund families.

17501014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501014.value: In the future, we would like to collect more recent data, and investigate how the recent policy changes affect the tri-party repo market.

17501014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501014.value: Taking advantage of a unique data set of repo transactions between U.S. money market funds and dealer banks, we examine the trading and the pricing in the tri-party repo market. For repos backed by safe collateral assets, such as Treasury and investment-grade corporate bonds, the market is competitive and the repo prices are uniform, within each asset class. However, for repos backed by risky collateral assets, such as equities and high-yield corporate bonds, the market is highly segmented and the repo prices vary substantially, both across segments and within segments. The segmentation is shaped by fund families who self-select different collateral risk, through requirements on the collateral concentration levels. Fund families in the high risk segment ask for higher haircuts and spreads, resulting a strongly positive relationship between repo prices and collateral concentration across segments. Within segments, haircuts are mainly determined by collateral concentration and counter-party; spreads are mainly determined by maturity and counter-party. Facing a highly segmented market, dealers behave rationally to minimize their cost of financing by allocating their collaterals across different fund families.

17501314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501314.value: 提供物超所值的大型基建項目―構建政府公營部門的用戶端功能

17501314.label: Project Objectives
17501314.value: Explore what the most appropriate role for public sector clients in large infrastructure asset acquisition projects is. Establish what ‘mix’ of project-related capabilities public sector clients require to ensure the effective and efficient definition and delivery of different types of major projects. Develop a set of managerial principles that can support public sector clients in deciding on the most appropriate level and mix of capabilities for managing the projects they sponsor.
rows: Explore what the most appropriate role for public sector clients in large infrastructure asset acquisition projects is.
Establish what ‘mix’ of project-related capabilities public sector clients require to ensure the effective and efficient definition and delivery of different types of major projects.
Develop a set of managerial principles that can support public sector clients in deciding on the most appropriate level and mix of capabilities for managing the projects they sponsor.

17501314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501314.value: Governments are charged with delivering services of various kinds to the citizens whose taxes support them, and also hold a brief for ensuring sustained economic growth. In order to meet these obligations they acquire infrastructure assets as varied as transportation infrastructure, large information systems, hospitals, and defence systems etc. Driven by a range of issues, such as urbanisation, sustainability, an ageing existing infrastructure, and the rising expectations of the citizens, many countries are now on the verge of massive investments in social and economic infrastructure. Hong Kong is no exception with an estimated future yearly spending of HK$70billion on public capital projects. This research project examines the role of the specific public sector bodies that are charged with the acquisition of these infrastructure assets. In particular, it investigates what the most appropriate role for public sector organisations as clients for infrastructure asset acquisition projects is; and seeks to establish what ‘mix’ of capabilities they require to ensure the effective definition and delivery of their projects. The research need is qualified on the basis of three observations. First, cost and time overruns have become close to inherent features on large infrastructure projects. Second, public sector clients are increasingly being asked to do more for less, i.e. produce more public value with fewer resources. Third, the pressures on resources in combination with changes in the organisation of the public sector at large have led to the outsourcing of client capabilities, in order to achieve slimmer client organisations. There is a growing body of evidence that points towards that the process of capability outsourcing has gone too far and that many clients now have too little capability to manage their projects. The research takes as its point of departure that public sector clients need the capability to manage the projects that they promote. The focus is on establishing what mix of capabilities large clients require to ensure the effective definition and delivery of the projects in which they invest. The findings promise to support clients in establishing organisational structures and procedures based on a suitable mix of capabilities necessary to realise their objectives. They also promise to contribute to the academic literatures on organisational capabilities, procurement and project management.

17501314.label: Realisation of objectives
17501314.value: At the time of writing the research proposal (2012-2013) there was a construction boom and much enthusiasm towards large scale investment in public infrastructure in Hong Kong. The ‘Hong Kong 10 Major Infrastructure Projects’ were already in progress, and the estimated further yearly spending on capital projects was estimated at around $70 billion. There was also talk of further investments in the form of an investment programme for large hospitals, further investment in public housing and an expansion of MTR and lightrail networks. Hence, at the time there was seemingly an abundance of empirical opportunities. However, as described in the mid-term progress report things changed. By the time the project was supposed to start (early 2015) the political situation was markedly different. There was increased public and political scrutiny of projects (something that is carrying on to this day), which in turn led to projects being delayed or at times frozen. Many large projects experienced significant opposition and were subjected to relentless negative press. There were at the time, and continue to be, high level accusations of mismanagement of public funds resulting in the resignations of senior level managers and decision makers. The corollary of all this was significant reluctance among public sector clients to engage with the research team. Informal discussions were not a problem, but it was clear that they did not want to be associated with research targeting their in-house competence and ability to manage their projects (note: access for other types of research such as improving site safety and developing technologies was never a problem). Much time was spent on negotiating access to a variety of public sector clients, e.g. the development Bureau and the Hospital Authority, but these efforts proved fruitless. The above scenario forced us to adapt and seek empirical opportunities elsewhere. We pursued two different strategies: i) we approached colleagues at Chalmers University of Technology, Sweden where the PI had formally worked (and is as of 2016 a visiting professor). Sweden has a much more open and accessible public sector than Hong Kong, which frequently engages with research. Academics, therefore, enjoy good access to empirical data. Two streams of research were developed. The first targeted a long-term development project in the City of Gothenburg and the other a strategic initiative driven by the Swedish ‘Real Estate organization of County Councils’ in an attempt to strengthen and centralise their construction expertise in the health care sector. These two streams gave us access to the qualitative data we needed to fulfil the research objectives; However, ii) we thought that it is important to also pursue the research in Hong Kong despite not being able to secure access to the kinds of public sector clients that we targeted. Given the differences between public and private sectors in terms of ultimate business objectives (growth and profit) we decided to approach a non-for-profit organisation, the Hong Kong Jockey Club (HKJC). The response was positive, but due to internal changes in the organisation and a very stringent approval process it took over a year from initial agreement (spring 2016) to when the empirical part of the research could actually start. As a result we have not officially published anything from this research yet. But we have written internal reports and the PhD student working with the data has extended his candidature and is due to submit in March 2018. We have also established contact with, and conducted a pilot study at, the Tianjin Rail Transit Group, but this work should be considered as informing rather than contributing to the research project reported on here. Achieving objectives: 1. Explore what the most appropriate role for public sector clients in large infrastructure asset acquisition projects is. 2. Establish what ‘mix’ of project-related capabilities public sector clients require to ensure the effective and efficient definition and delivery of different types of major projects. 3. Develop a set of managerial principles that can support public sector clients in deciding on the most appropriate level and mix of capabilities for managing the projects they sponsor. Given the difficulties of attaining empirical access, attention was initially given to objectives 1 and 2. Early work focused on developing a conceptual framework for owner project capabilities. This framework is published in the International Journal of Project Management (2016) and has of December 2017 garnered 12 citations in the WoS. We have subsequently developed this framework by providing more detail and depth to the various sub-themes, putting much emphasis on capability identification. The work has been published in four conference papers. These are mainly theoretical, but build on insights gained from the ongoing empirical work. They address objectives 1 and 2 by illuminating the different types of capabilities needed and how their presence, together with how they are combined, dictates the role that the client can take on the project. To further strengthen our theoretical positioning we have also undertaken a systematic literature review initially covering some 6000 articles in order to establish an in-depth understanding of how our underpinning theoretical framework, dynamic capabilities, can be operationalised in the project-based domain. The resulting paper is currently under review. Subsequent work has focused on objective 3 with a particular emphasis on how the appropriate level and mix of capabilities can be developed, i.e. moving from capability identification to capability development. The slight change in terminology from the original objective is worth noting. It became apparent as research progressed that solely focusing on managerial principals for deciding on the level and mix of capabilities misses out the very important issue of how these capabilities once identified could be acquired, developed and refined. Our work here has centred on case study work in HKJC, the City of Gothenburg and the Real Estate organization of County Councils, Sweden. Work with the HKJC focused on how the organisation over the past seven years has developed their governance capabilities; work with the City of Gothenburg targeted how 28 municipal organisations in collaboration have developed joint capabilities in the form of ‘shared construction guidelines’; and the collaboration with the Swedish health care clients focused on how they were working to strengthen their strategic capabilities. Research outputs here include a journal paper submitted to Public Management Review + a conference paper (both detailing the work in the City of Gothenburg), a paper under preparation based on the first phase of the work the Swedish Counties, two conference papers on commercial capabilities for conferences in the summer (under review), a report to the HKJC (not public) and a PhD thesis (based mainly on the work with the HKJC) to be submitted no later than 30 March 2018.

17501314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501314.value: The research outcomes to date consist of: - One published journal paper and two journal papers currently under review. The two targeted journals International Journal of Project Management and Public Management Review are both in the first quartile of their respective categories in WoS. Furthermore, one journal paper is at the final stages of preparation and will be submitted to the Project Management Journal (current impact factor 2.7). - Five conference papers have been presented in what could be considered as the leading conferences within the broader construction management domain. A further two conference papers are currently under review. - An internal report to the Hong Kong Jockey Club. - A PhD thesis which will be submitted no later than March 2018. The main contribution can be summarized as follows: From an academic perspective we contribute to theoretical development by showing how organisational capabilities can be applied to project-base organising. Our specific contributions are threefold. Firstly, we show how the theoretical constructs that stem out of research on private sector firms can be applied on public sector organisations. Secondly, we provide one of the first attempts at applying project capabilities to the client organisation, rather than the supply-side. Thirdly, we respond to current calls for empirically based research on project capabilities and provide evidence from three case studies of how client organisations can develop dynamic capabilities through a combination of short and long-term mechanisms. The practical contribution lies foremost in the identification of a broad set of client capabilities the client organisation needs to have either in-house or tied semi-permanently to the organisation. We also highlight the important role of learning, on and between projects, as a fundamental cornerstone of capability development. A further contribution, directly linked to learning, concerns capability acquisition and how easily, or not, capabilities can be acquired externally. Here our findings point to the need of finding a balance between explorative and exploitative measures, or put somewhat differently between introducing disruptive changes or refining and developing already existing routines and processes. This is by no means trivial. In terms of teaching, the PI is currently supervising two PhD students at HKU and is the co-supervisor of a PhD student at Chalmers University of Technology, all researching on the topic. The research findings in general, and the important role of the client and how its performance can be improved in particular, is taught in two MSc courses and one BSc course.

17501314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501314.value: We are currently developing the research in three main areas. i) Client governance capability development – working with the Hong Kong Jockey Club to explore how capabilities can be developed through various learning mechanisms. Ongoing case study, part of which is PhD research. ii) Building commercial capabilities for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) – studying how a large client organisation, Tianjin Rail Transit Group, is organising themselves to be able to promote PPPs. This is a PhD project. A pilot study has been undertaken and a longitudinal case study based on participative observation will commence in March 2018. The project is of interest as PPPs are becoming increasingly common in China and in the Belt and Road initiative. iii) Strategic capability development – we are working with the Centre for Healthcare Architecture, Sweden, in studying an attempt at homogenising and centralising client capabilities in health care facility acquisition across 18 out of 24 counties in Sweden. Part 1: a large scale survey is completed, Part 2: selected case studies will commence in April 2018.

17501314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501314.value: This research project has its origins in two observations. First, cost and time overruns have become close to inherent features on public sector infrastructure projects, such as new schools, hospitals, roads and rail. Second, the public sector organisations responsible for initiating and realising these projects, for example Government bureaus, departments and authorities, have increasingly been asked to do more for less in terms of producing more public value at the same time as their internal resources have been reduced in order to achieve slimmer organisations. The research has sought to study how these public sector client organisations can change and develop in order to ensure the effective definition and delivery of the projects they promote. Findings show the areas in which the client organisation needs to have in-house capabilities in order to effectively relate to the project suppliers, and illustrate how these capabilities, through a variety of actions, can be developed over time.

17501614.value: 借券市場的避險和投機需求與選擇權賣權交易的交互影響研究

17501614.label: Project Objectives
17501614.value: To investigate how the option market and the equity lending market interact with each other. To use the 2008 Short-sale Ban to tease out the influence of speculation demand in the equity lending market on the put options volume. To provide reconciling evidence on how put options volume is related to short sale constraints. To explore how cross-sectional variations of option moneyness and leverage affect the results.
rows: To investigate how the option market and the equity lending market interact with each other.
To use the 2008 Short-sale Ban to tease out the influence of speculation demand in the equity lending market on the put options volume.
To provide reconciling evidence on how put options volume is related to short sale constraints.
To explore how cross-sectional variations of option moneyness and leverage affect the results.

17501614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501614.value: Previous studies offer mixed evidence on the relationship between the options market and the equity lending market. On the one hand, bearish options and short sales are viewed as substitutes as investors can capitalize on negative information by buying put options or short selling. On the other hand, bearish options and short sales are viewed as “complements” in the sense that option market makers need to hedge their short positions in put options by short selling the underlying stocks. These confounding arguments in two streams of literature might result from a lack of detailed data. Moreover, without disentangling the speculation demand of informed traders and hedging demand from option makers in the equity lending market, it is not clear how short sales constraints are related to the trading costs and volume in the options market. In this study, we propose a comprehensive framework to shed light on this debate. We make contributions to both options and short selling literatures by asking the two following questions. First, how are short-sale constraints related to option trading in general? More specifically, when the trading costs of capitalizing on private negative information becomes more expensive in the equity lending market, will informed traders turn to the options market? If so, short sales and put options are substitutes, and we should observe a positive relation between short selling costs and put options trading volume and bid-ask spreads. Second, does this positive relationship between short sales constraints and put options activities disappear or reverse when the demand of equity lending is solely driven by the put option market makers? We utilize the 2008 Short Sale Ban to tease out the speculation demand in the lending market, as only the options market makers are allowed to short for the stocks on the ban list during that period. By synthesizing the two channels in a panel regression framework, we will be able to reconcile the ostensibly conflicting findings on the interaction of the two markets. 文獻對於期權市場和借券市場之間的交互影響一直都沒有決定性的證據。一方面來說，投資者可以通過買入賣權或是放空獲利，因此賣權和借券可以被視為替代品，。另一方面，由於選擇權造市者需要透過放空來避險選擇權賣權的空頭部位，賣權和借券因此又被視為具有某種互補性。在缺乏借券市場詳細數據，以及未同時考慮投機需求及造勢者避險需求的雙重影響下，過去的研究往往偏執於其中一種論述。 本研究試圖提出一個全面性的框架，來闡明兩個市場間的互動關係。首先，我們研究放空限制對於賣權交易的影響。具體來說，我們研究當放空變得更加昂貴時，擁有訊息的知情交易者是否會轉向賣權市場交易？如果真是如此，我們應該會觀察到借券成本和賣權交易量與價格呈正向關係。其次，當借券需求只來自於賣權造市者時，我們是否觀察到賣權交易量會隨著借券成本上揚而下挫?為此，我們借用了2008年放空禁止令的時空背景，因為在這段時間內，在放空禁止令所規範的股票，只有賣權造市者可以放空。因此借券市場上的需求，只單純來自於賣權造市者避險需求。透過區別借券市場的避險與投機需求，以及結合2008放空禁止令，本研究可以揉合過去文獻上關於這兩個市場，在相互影響上的矛盾結論。

17501614.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501614.value: We find that put options trading volume and bid-ask spreads both increase with equity lending fees. However, we also find that put options trading volume decreases with lending fees for banned stocks during the 2008 Short-Sale Ban period, when only options market makers could short. By separating the speculative demand of short sellers from the hedging demand of options market makers in the lending market, our results provide a thorough analysis of the interaction between the options market and the equity lending market. We also shed light on the substitutability/complementarity between put options volume and short interest shown in the literature.

17501614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501614.value: The project could be extended to using the detailed options trading data provided by International Security Exchange (ISE). The options volume of ISE are signed, meaning that we could differentiate buy or sell volume. This would help to refine our tests in this paper.

17501614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501614.value: Our article adds to the literature on the interaction between short selling and put options trading by disentangling the speculative demand of short sellers from the hedging demand of options market makers in the equity lending market. By separating two types of demand in the short-selling market, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between the two markets.

17501714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501714.value: 變革型和交易型領導方式，特別的就業安排，及員工的情緒和行為

17501714.label: Project Objectives
17501714.value: To propose and test a theoretical model which integrates i-deal research with leadership research (this objective is not addressed in any previous or my own studies). To extend the predominant self-focused perspective to an examination of employee perceptions of both their own i-deals and those of their coworkers (all previous studies have examined either, but not both, perspectives, and studies which address perceptions of coworkers’ i-deals are far fewer than those that address employee perceptions of their own i-deals). To examine both the positive and negative emotional consequences of i-deals, which will, in turn, help to clarify the benefits and costs of using i-deals in the workplace (this objective is not addressed in any previous or my own studies). To investigate emotions as mediators of i-deals’ effects on job behavior, as mixed findings have been observed concerning these effects (this objective is not addressed in any previous or my own studies, although some prior studies (including mine) have shown that i-deals are directly related to job behaviors).

17501714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501714.value: 近年，研究人員和從業者留意到給予員工特別的就業安排(簡稱I-安排)可以提升他們的忠誠度及工作績效。特別的就業安排是針對個人的喜好和員工個人的需求的。例子包括特別的培訓機會，彈性工作時間，遠程辦公的機會，度身訂做的補償方案等等。 這個研究項目的目的是提出並測試一個新的理論模型來填補文獻中四個重要的空缺。其他研究人員或我以往的研究調查亦還未有填補這四個缺口。 第一，儘管監事和經理通常負責談判給與員工的I-安排，I-安排的研究和領導的研究現在仍然是獨立進行的。這兩個學術範圍流需要整合，因為I-安排可能是領導者有效地激勵員工的工具。這個缺口促使我去研究變革型和交易型領導方式行和I-安排的關係，以及哪一種領導方式會更有效地發揮I-安排的功用。 第二，許多研究迄今著重於員工自己的I-安排。然而，社會學家强調，人類習慣從社會環境中尋找線索來分析及了解這個世界。因此，要更完整地評估I-安排的影響，學者不單要研究員工本身，還要擴展到員工怎樣看他們的同事的角度。這個缺口促使我去研究員工自己的I-安排和觀察同事的I-安排的影響。 第三，很少學者研究在工作場所運用I-安排的壞處。雖然員工很樂意收到I-安排，他們也可能會為工作場所資源的競爭而感到更大的工作壓力。此外，一些研究人員指出，使用I-安排可能會增加運營成本和製造不公平的氣氛。這個缺口促使我去研究I-安排對於員工好壞情緒的影響。透過這些角度，我便可以解釋在工場運用I-安排的正負影響。 第四，在這方面的研究主要側重於I-安排對員工行為的影響，而且到目前為止還未有一個明確的結論。然而，其中一個可以更清楚了I-安排對員工的行為的影響，是先去了解員工對I-安排的即時情緒反應。很多跨學科累積的證據表明，員工的情緒親密地影響他們的工作行為。這個缺口促使我去研究I-安排怎樣影響情緒，以及這些情緒怎樣影響員工正職以外的行為，包括公民行為和負面的工作行為。這兩種行為都跟情緒有密切的關係。 總括而言，解決上述四大缺口將能夠幫助研究人員更了解領導者如何才能有效地使用I-安排以提高組織的工作效率以及因為運用I-安排而帶來的好處及壞處。 這項研究也有實踐價值的。 I-安排是昂貴的安排，因為他們需要運用公司額外的資源。如果公司對I-安排的影響不理解，而最終影響到員工的士氣及情緒(和行為)，那I-安排的代價就更大了。例如，如果在工作場所使用的I-安排顯著增加了員工之間的妒忌，那麼I-安排所帶來的好處可能還不及抵消它帶來的壞處。

17501714.label: Realisation of objectives
17501714.value: Through longitudinal data collections, I was able to gather a sample that reported their i-deal experiences and to relate those i-deal experiences to work outcomes. In this model, leadership was found to be significant predictors of i-deal experiences, which in turn affected multiple attitudinal and behavioral variables. Overall, the first objective, which was to integrate the leadership and i-deal research, was attained. In my investigation, I examined both employees’ receipt of i-deals and their witnessing of coworkers’ i-deals. I found that these two types of i-deal experiences tended to be positively correlated, suggesting that they go hand in hand in organizations that offer i-deals. Thus, the second objective was attained as well; I have found evidence that employees do formulate perceptions of coworkers’ i-deals, in addition to their own ideals. I also examined whether receiving and witnessing i-deals would affect both positive voice (e.g., making constructive suggestions) and negative voice (e.g., voicing criticisms). I observed that receiving i-deals indeed indirectly enhanced positive voice (via gratitude), whereas witnessing coworkers’ i-deals indirectly enhanced negative voice (via envy). Thus, the third objective was attained. My study showed that i-deals could result in both positive and negative outcomes. Finally, I showed that emotions (gratitude, envy) were the major reasons why i-deals can create both positive and negative outcomes. Employees who were grateful for their i-deals spoke up with more constructive suggestions, whereas employees who were disgruntled as a result of witnessing others’ i-deals tended to criticize and complain more in the workplace. Thus, the fourth objective was accomplished as well; I showed that emotions were important lynchpins that explained why i-deals could affect a variety of work outcomes.

17501714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501714.value: Two manuscripts arose from this project. First, I tried to examine the four aforementioned objectives in a single study. I collected data from 207 employees at four points in time over a one-year period. The proposed model, which collectively tested the four study objectives, received empirical support. Specifically, transformational and transactional leadership were found to predict employees’ receipt of i-deals, which in turn predicted their gratitude and positive voice. However, employees’ receipt of i-deals was also found to positively affect witnessing coworkers’ i-deals, which in turn predicted their envy and negative voice. A moderator was also identified. The relationship between receiving and witnessing i-deals was stronger when transactional leadership was higher. These findings offer empirical support for the proposed leadership-event-emotion-behavior framework, which in turn helps researchers integrate the research on leadership and i-deals. This manuscript is currently under first review at Journal of Vocational Behavior, a recognized journal on the faculty’s journal list. Prior to this submission, the manuscript was previously under second review at Journal of Management Studies (another recognized journal on the faculty’s journal list). Another manuscript that arose from this project was one that examined how being envied in the workplace would affect employees’ ethical judgment. I used the survey space to collect several additional variables and created this manuscript, which is currently under second review at Human Relations, a recognized journal on the faculty’s journal list. It is also one of the FT-50 journals. The grant was also used to help gather data to test another research idea about i-deals. That project created a conference paper that addressed the benefits and downsides of offering i-deals in the workplace. This paper showed to researchers that i-deals can have both positive and negative outcomes, in addition to the ones examined in my original project. The details of the conference paper can be found in Part C.

17501714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501714.value: As this study represents the first to integrate the research on leadership and i-deal experiences, future studies can consider how leaders can effectively use i-deals without drawing the negative emotional problems and without creating negative job behavior. Future research can also identify other types of emotions, now that I have shown that discrete emotions can help explain the psychological processes that link i-deals to outcomes. Other types of leadership styles, in addition to transformational and leadership (e.g., authentic leadership, ethical leadership, paternalistic leadership) can be considered too, as I have uncovered that i-deals are important leadership tools for motivation.

17501714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501714.value: To promote employee motivation and productivity, organizations often need to carefully consider what to offer employees to induce effort and loyalty. One possible approach is to offer special employment arrangements (called i-deals) to high-potential employees. This study showed that transformational and transactional leaders are more likely to grant i-deals to employees. This finding illustrates the importance of making the best use of workplace resources to craft i-deals that satisfy employees’ individual needs, because in the eyes of their followers, leaders who grant i-deals are likely to be seen as transformational or transactional or both. However, this study also highlights a key management dilemma involving i-deals that deserves more managerial attention. Although followers report greater gratitude and positive voice when they receive i-deals, the perceptions of their own i-deals may also inevitably color their perception of their coworkers’ i-deals. That is, the more i-deals an employee receives, the more likely he or she will believe that others receive the same i-deals. This is problematic because this study has shown that this process is related to the envy of coworkers, which in turn relates to defensive voice, which can stifle positive organizational changes, and to destructive voice, which can harm organizational morale and the reputation of the company. Therefore, the findings of this study illustrate that managers should not blindly increase the use of i-deals in the workplace, as this could inadvertently encourage envy in the workplace and burden the organization in the long run.

17501814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501814.value: In a democracy, where elections are the means by which governments are held accountable, the mass media play a role in disciplining politicians via dissemination of information to voters. The economic literature has well recorded the effect of mass media in promoting good government. However, in a weak democracy or autocratic institution, the monitoring and disciplining functions of the media may be missing. In fact, the persuasion effect of the media may even be dangerous because of bias and capture resulting from government control. In such a situation, officers are not held to account by either their superiors or the public, and this can lead to welfare loss or efficiency loss. This may be the case in China today, presenting a real threat to continued economic growth and improvements in social welfare. In view of this threat, the proposed project will examine the role of the media in monitoring and disciplining politicians and in cracking down on corruption in China. We will address two issues in our research. First, we investigate whether the traditional media, namely newspapers, are manipulated by heads of local government in order to promote their own careers or the ranking of their political cliques.A byproduct of our research on this issue will be the development of a new method to identify political cliques. We will use newspaper content analysis to capture the occasions at which any two politicians both appear and construct indices to show the closeness of their connection. We will then be able to identify those politicians who are highly likely to belong to the same political cliques. Second, we examine the effect of media on disciplining corrupt officers. By investigating around 500 corruption cases, we will be able to ascertain whether there is an effect of the media on the penalties imposed upon corrupt officers. Besides the traditional media, we also study the effect of a new media: microblogs. The salient difference between the new media and traditional media lies in the degree of political control imposed upon them. While Chinese newspapers are strictly controlled by the government, microblogs are difficult to censor and are thus comparatively free and independent. We will therefore investigate whether microblogs have greater effects than newspapers when it comes to disciplining corrupt officers. In addition,we will investigate whether the emergence of Sina Weibo, the most popular microblog, has enhanced the disciplining effect of newspapers.

17501914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501914.value: Foreign direct investment (FDI) is one of the most important aspects of globalization and is among the fastest growing economic activities around the world. Many countries compete fiercely to attract FDI because it is perceived to be economically beneficial, particularly in the transfer of managerial knowledge, skills and advanced technology to local firms. From 1991 to 2002, developing countries made over 1500 regulatory changes favorable to FDI (UNCTAD, 2003). The economic wisdom of these policies depends on whether, common perceptions aside, inward FDI in fact benefits a host country’s economy and generates positive spillovers to domestic firms. The aim of this project is to adopt a new approach to investigate this issue. In both policy debate and academic research, there exist two opposing views with regard to FDI spillovers. The positive view argues that domestic firms can benefit from the demonstration effect of foreign multinationals, unintentional technology leakage, and labor turnover from foreign firms to domestic firms. The negative view casts doubt on the existence of any positive spillover from FDI, even arguing that the effects of FDI are negative because domestic firms face tougher market competition. The evidence found in existing empirical studies is mixed, leaving the debate over FDI spillovers unresolved. This project will make a significant contribution to the literature on FDI spillovers as it is distinguishable from existing studies in a number of important ways. First, it focuses on China, offering valuable insights into FDI spillover in the world’s largest developing country which attracts the most FDI among developing countries. Second, it focuses on Sino-foreign joint ventures (JVs), a popular mode of FDI in China (and the dominant mode prior to 1999) and one which the Chinese government encourages in the belief that it facilitates technology transfer. This is an unexplored area which we are able to tackle through the construction of a unique database which allows us to examine how domestic parent firms directly benefit from JVs. Third, we will adopt various methods to conduct rigorous empirical analysis, ensuring that our findings are convincing and robust. While this research is mainly empirical, we will also conduct a theoretical analysis based on the key empirical findings, which will be of direct application to discussions on FDI policies in China and other developing countries. 对外直接投资是经济全球化最直接的体现，也是近年来国家与国家之间最活跃的经济活动之一。经济学的观点一般认为，外商直接投资可以促进当地经济发展。对于发展中国家而言，学习外国企业优秀的管理和技术尤其重要，因此各国通过各种优惠政策去吸引外资。据联合国贸发会议（2003）数据显示，从1991年至2002年，发展中国家共出台1500多项法令法规吸引外资。 但是外商直接投资是否能对当地企业发挥促进作用，根本还在于当地企业能否最大效用的利用外资，并吸收跨国企业带来的先进管理经验和技术。本项目旨在研究本地企业的吸收能力。 外商投资对于当地经济发展一直被认为存在正反两方面的作用：一方面，当地企业可以通过向跨国企业学习新的管理经验和技术来提高效率，另一方面，外商直接投资也可能对当地资本产生挤出效应。本课题旨在通过大样本的数据分析，全面评价外商投资这两方面的综合作用。 此项目将有助于完善对外直接投资方面的文献。第一，此项目将主要研究中国公司，因此可以更好的帮助我们了解外商直接投资在全球最大的发展中国家到底发挥什么样的作用。第二，此项目将主要研究在中国新成立的中外合资公司，检验中国母公司是否可以从这些合资公司中受益。

17501914.label: Realisation of objectives
17501914.value: We have written one paper on JV partner selection (objective 1), and one paper on spillovers (objective 2). However, to increase the significance of the research output, we decided to put them together in one output. In order to conduct a research to achieve the first two objectives, we need to build a rich database which consists of three data sets: (i) the Above-scale Industrial Firms Panel (ASIFP), (ii) the Name List of Foreign and Domestic Joint Ventures in China (Name List), and (iii) the Patent Database maintained by the China’s State Intellectual Property Office (SIPO). The ASIFP contains financial data of large manufacturing firms in China. The Name List data is the key for us to identify which Chinese firm is the parent company of a joint venture. The Patent Database enable us to see Chinese firms’ innovation activities. Based on this database, we first run a regression with the dependent variable being the dummy variable which takes value 1 if a Chinese firm is selected as a JV partner in year t, and zero otherwise. The independent variables (factors that may affect the choice of the firm being the JV partner) include a variety of firm characteristics including productivity, sales, employment size, innovation, profitability, government subsidy, export status, foreign ownership, etc. The regression results will inform us what factor are important for JV partner selection. This is for objective one. Then, based on the same database, we run a regression with the dependent variable being the performance of all Chinese companies. The performance variables include productivity, innovation, and others. For the independent variables, the key one is a dummy variable which takes value 1 if the Chinese firm has a JV, and zero otherwise. This is to identify whether the performance of the Chinese JV partner is better than others due to the formation of JVs. This analysis is for objective two. In addition, we do more analysis than our original plan for objective two. In particular, we also examine how formation of JVs affect the performance of the JV themselves and the other Chinese firms. Therefore, we are able to identify three effects of JVs in China (while in the proposal we only thought of one effect): the effects on JVs, the effects on the Chinese partner companies of the JVs, and other Chinese firms. The findings therefore are much richer and complete. Then we move on to identify the mechanism of the three effects, or spillovers: to achieve objective three. We do that by first constructing the degree of JV presence in each industry. There are two channels that generate spillovers to the Chinese firms (the partners and others): the negative competition effect and the positive technology learning or leakage. We are able to empirically estimate the importance of each of these channels. We have also done some work on constructing a theoretical model to help explain and understand the empirical findings, especially the JV partner selection, but it turns out this part is not so easy and we are not able to get very successful results. However, we have written articles which help policy discussions, in particularly related to the recent trade war between the US and China. Our research catches a lot of media attention. Objective 4 is partly achieved.
