17501914.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501914.value: In this study, we employ a novel administrative dataset accounting for all joint ventures in China from 1998–2007. We first explore the characteristics that determine which Chinese firms are most likely to be selected as IJV partners. We find that the Chinese firms most likely to be chosen as partners in IJVs are larger, more productive, and engage in more innovation/patenting – perhaps unsurprising, but these large, productive firms on the frontiers of innovation will be the firms that possess the absorptive capacity to benefit from the intergenerational technology transfer effect hypothesized earlier. We next examine the evidence for the channels of technology transfer outlined above, finding strong support for each. Controlling for other firm characteristics, joint ventures tend to be more productive (by about 30%, as measured by total factor productivity), have higher sales, and engage in more patenting relative to other, non-joint venture Chinese firms, evidence consistent with the beneficial transfer of technology. As evidence for the intergenerational transfer of technology, a similar effect is apparent for Chinese joint venture partners, though this effect is much more muted than that for the joint ventures, as the partners tend to be only around 5% more productive than other Chinese firms. While foreign investors have a strong incentive to transfer technology directly to their joint ventures, no such incentive exists with regard to their Chinese partners, and yet foreign partners are able to indirectly benefit from the technology conferred on their joint venture offshoots. We also find that when joint venture firms (or the domestic partners) account for a larger share of the market in a particular industry, other Chinese firms see substantial gains in their own productivity – on average, when the share of industry sales by joint ventures increases by 10 percentage points, other firms in that industry are 10 percent more productive, while for the effect arising from domestic partners, a 10 percentage point increase in IJV partners’ share of industry sales yields around a 4.5 percent increase in other firms’ productivity. When we delineate this effect by the origin of the foreign investor – Hong Kong/Macau/Taiwan versus Japan versus the United States – we find that U.S. joint ventures account for the bulk of these externalities.

17501914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501914.value: The literature on multinationals has expended significant effort in quantifying the effects of FDI; however, the specific role of joint ventures has remained underexplored. At a broad level, our results serve to inform our understanding of effective foreign investment policy. As China has liberalized its foreign investment environment, encouraging the establishment of WFOEs and opening more sectors to foreign entry, the ensuing reduction in the utilization of joint ventures promises to impact the way in which knowledge is transmitted between firms. While channels for learning and technology transfer might arise from WFOEs, the fact that domestic firms play no direct role in this type of investment shuts down the potential international technology transfer effects revealed in joint venture firms and the intergenerational effects accruing to partner firms. Additionally, WFOEs are likely to be better equipped to safeguard their intellectual property and proprietary technologies from being disseminated to domestic firms, dampening the innovation externalities that we find evidence for, while potentially sapping market share from domestic competitors. Future work might consider the effects of the various modes of foreign investment jointly, particularly in light of the explosion of WFOEs in China in recent years.

17501914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501914.value: International joint ventures are unique in the manner with which they allow domestic and foreign firms to interact. China’s government mandates that foreign investors in particular industries form joint ventures with a domestic Chinese partner, with the tacit purpose of encouraging the transfer of advanced technology from the foreign investor to the domestic operation. In this project we consider the incentives underlying international joint venture formation, and explore the extent to which they encourage international technology transfer, finding empirical evidence for the existence of multiple channels through which this transfer takes place. The topic and findings of this research provide very important elements to the current debate of the possible trade war between the US and China. We employing a novel administrative dataset accounting for all joint ventures in China from 1998–2007 in this research. We find that the Chinese firms most likely to be chosen as partners in IJVs are larger, more productive, and engage in more innovation. We also find that joint ventures tend to be more productive, have higher sales, and engage in more patenting relative to other, non-joint venture Chinese firms, evidence consistent with the beneficial transfer of technology.

17502014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502014.value: 在線業務對不斷保持在搜索引擎結果首頁的排名的追求導致了搜索引擎優化（SEO）的興起。通過投資於搜索引擎優化，賣家可能會受益於他們的網站知名度的提高，同時買家也可以從能夠更輕鬆地找到所需的產品中受益。雖然搜索引擎也旨在服務信息搜尋者和信息提供者，但賣家的搜索引擎優化可能使得這兩者越來越難使用同一個平台找到彼此。由於搜索引擎的收入受瀏覽量和付費廣告影響，搜索引擎優化可能最終排擠信息搜尋者和信息提供者，降低了付費列表的價值和傷害搜索引擎的業務。 我們的研究旨在解決三個問題： 1）在何種程度上搜索引擎優化影響搜索引擎的收入？ 2）在什麼情況下搜索引擎優化投資傷害或提高搜索引擎用戶的整體福利？ 3）監管機構應該如何平衡有關各方的利益？ 這項研究的結果將不僅提供最佳的搜索引擎優化的干預策略，更重要的是，我們還將就監管機構在改善互聯網搜索生態系統的所有參與者的福利提供政策指引和管理準則。

17502114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17502114.value: 中美贸易对美国政治有影响吗？

17502114.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17502114.value: Dr Che, Yi Prof Lu, Yi Prof SCHOTT, PETER K.

17502114.label: Project Objectives
17502114.value: To investigate whether Chinese imports affect the outcomes of various levels of U.S. election To examine whether Chinese imports impact on the voting behavior of the elected legislators
rows: To investigate whether Chinese imports affect the outcomes of various levels of U.S. election
To examine whether Chinese imports impact on the voting behavior of the elected legislators

17502114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502114.value: United States and China are the world’s two largest economies with increasing bilateral trade and investment. China’s trade with the United States, however, is rather unbalanced. For example, in 2012, China was the largest importing country of the United States (with the import value of USD 425.6 billion) and its second largest exporting country (with the export value of USD 110.6 billion). The large U.S. trade deficits against China have made Chinese imports a contentious issue in various levels of elections in the United States (congressional, senatorial, gubernatorial and presidential). It is both interesting and important to investigate whether Chinese imports influence American politics. The proposed research is to address this question by examining whether Chinese imports affect the outcomes of various levels of U.S. elections, and whether the Chinese imports actually influence the voting behavior of elected legislators. The proposed research will contribute to the economics literature by elucidating the intertwined nature of international trade and domestic politics. It will also have important implications for the future of Sino-U.S. trade and the extent of world economic integration. 本研究项目旨在分析中美贸易对美国政治的可能影响。 具体包括： 从中国进口多的美国地区会否更可能选出民主党的议员？ 代表这些美国地区的议员会否更可能否决促进贸易的议案？

17502114.label: Realisation of objectives
17502114.value: Globalization, the latest wave of which was unleashed by China's joining the World Trade Organization in 2001, has received a rude awakening in the latest votes in the United Kingdom in its break from the European Union and the success of Donald Trump in the 2016 U.S. presidential elections. There is increasing evidence suggesting that imports from China, despite all the benefits associated with them, cast various adverse effects on U.S. society; for example, a surge in the manufacturing unemployment (e.g., Autor et al., 2013; Acemoglu et al.,2016; Pierce and Schott, 2016) and deterioration in public health (e.g., Autor et al., 2016; McManus and Schaur, 2016; Pierce and Schott, 2016). This project takes the view that the adverse effects of Chinese imports competition on U.S. manufacturing employment is expected to impact on Americans’ voting preferences, election outcomes, and the legislative activities of U.S. legislators, all of which are also amplified by bias in media reporting of China (or media slant against China). The first part of our project examines the relationship between increased import competition from China and voting in elections for the U.S. House of Representatives using difference-in-differences empirical strategy (objective #1 of the project). We show that U.S. counties with greater exposure to permanent normal trading relations (PNTR)'s trade liberalization exhibit relative increases in the share of votes cast for Democrats and the probability that a Democrat represents the county from 2000 to 2010, as well as increases in voter turnout. Moving a county from the 25th to the 75th percentile in terms of exposure to the change in U.S. trade policy is associated with a 1.3 to 1.4 percentage point increase in the share of votes cast for Democrats, representing a 2.6 to 3.6 percent increase relative to the across-county average share of votes for Democrats in the 2000 Congressional election, the closest Congressional election to the change in U.S. trade policy. Coefficient estimates from similar specifications indicate that the probability of a switch in representation for a county from a Republican to a Democrat Representative increases by 3 to 4 percentage points. Additional evidence on voter turnout and on voting for other offices (such as presidential and gubernatorial elections) provides further support for a role for PNTR in U.S. election outcomes. The second part of our analysis examines Representatives' votes on legislation during the 1990s and 2000s using a regression discontinuity identification strategy that compares the voting of Democrats and Republicans who win office by small margins (which is objective #2 of the project). The analysis indicates that Democrats during this period are more likely to take positions that restrict trade and that offer economic assistance that may benefit those adversely affected by import competition, providing a rationale for the change in voting documented in the first part of the analysis. We find that the tendency for Democrats to support such legislation is stronger after implementation of PNTR. Together, the results in the first and second parts of the project suggest that voters who perceive themselves as being disadvantaged by trade are more likely to vote for politicians that might restrict imports or be in favor of redistributing gains from winners to losers. Given the important role played by media in reporting the adverse effect of Chinese imports competition on U.S, manufacturing unemployment and its equally (if not more) important role in influencing the U.S. elections, we decide to expand the scope of the project by investigating how exposure to Chinese imports influences newspaper (negative) attitudes toward China, and (if the answer to the first question is affirmative) whether the media slant against China in turn influences U.S. election results. We focus on a set of 147 U.S. local daily newspapers over 1998-2012, whose readership suffers varying impacts of Chinese imports competition. We measure a newspaper’s slant against China by the proportion of articles devoted to negative issues about China in the newspaper’s total articles on China, and use three different ways of classifying articles as reporting negative issues about China. We adopt two approaches to identify the impact of Chinese imports competition on media slant against China: instrumental variable approach of Autor et al. (2013) and the difference-in-difference method of Pierce and Schott (2016a). We find that newspapers with circulation in counties that face greater exposure to Chinese imports report more negative news about China, which is consistent with some of the negative impacts of Chinese imports on the American society documented in the literature, such as rising unemployment and mortality (e.g., Autor et. al., 2013; McManus and Schaur, 2016; Pierce and Schott, 2016a). We further find that media slant against China is associated with increased voting shares for Democrats in House and Senate elections. That is to say, the media slant has lent support for Democrats, who traditionally are champions for the poor and critical of globalization, implying a limit of globalization if redistribution mechanisms are not put in place to help the victims of globalization.

17502114.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502114.value: This project first examines the effect of increased import competition from China on U.S. political outcomes. We find that U.S. counties more exposed to increased competition from China experience relative increases in the share of votes cast for Democrats in Congressional elections, along with increases in the probability that a Democrat represents a county and the probability of a county switching from a Republican to a Democrat Representative. The results are also economically significant – we find that moving a county from the 25th to the 75th percentile of exposure to PNTR increases the Democrat vote share in Congressional elections by 1.4 percentage points, or a 3.6 percent increase relative to the average share of votes won by Democrats in the 2000 Congressional election. Moreover, we find that increased import competition is associated with higher voter turnout and a higher share of votes cast for Democrats in gubernatorial and Presidential elections. The second half of our analysis investigates potential links between these voting outcomes and the legislative votes of members of Congress. We find that Democrats during the period we examine are more likely to support policies that limit import competition and that provide economic assistance that may benefit workers adversely affected by trade competition, providing an explanation for the voting behavior documented in the first part of our project. Our results suggest that voters who perceive themselves as being disadvantaged by trade are more likely to vote for politicians that might restrict imports or promote economic assistance. Anecdotal evidence suggests that U.S. media has played an amplifying and important role in reporting the loss of U.S. manufacturing jobs, leading to media slant against China, which subsequently impacts on the U.S. election outcomes. Using a data set of 147 U.S. local newspapers over 1998-2012, indeed we find that newspapers whose circulating counties face greater exposure to Chinese imports report more negative news about China. Furthermore, we study the effect of media slant against China on election outcomes between 2000 and 2012 at the county level, and find that in the House and Senate elections media slant is associated with increased voting shares for Democrats. As Democrats traditionally are champions for the poor and critical of globalization, our results imply a limit of globalization if redistribution mechanisms are not put in place to address the victims of globalization.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502114.value: This project examines the impact of trade liberalization on U.S. political elections. We find that U.S. counties subject to greater competition from China via a change in U.S. trade policy exhibit relative increases in turnout, the share of votes cast for Democrats and the probability that the county is represented by a Democrat. Next, we show that these changes are consistent with Democrats in office during the period examined being more likely to support legislation limiting import competition or favoring economic assistance. We also find substantial exposure to imports from China is associated with a deteriorating image of China in the U.S. media: newspapers whose circulation counties face greater exposure to Chinese imports report more negative news about China. Furthermore, the media slant is associated with increased voting shares for Democrats in U.S. House and Senate elections between 2000 and 2012.

17502214.label: Realisation of objectives
17502214.value: We have completed the project with the realization of the stated objectives. Overall, we have completed a working paper with solid results. We have presented this paper at 2017 International Conference in Accounting, Finance, Economics and Law at Taiwan (Apr 2017), and submitted this paper to Management Science for publication currently. In addition, we are presenting our paper at Hong Kong Baptist University on September 12 2018, and have scheduled the presentations at National Chengchi University (October 1 2018) and National Taiwan University (Sept 20 2018). We believe the objectives are fully completed as follows: 1. Regarding the objective 1, we do show that the adoption of international financial reporting standards (IFRS) significantly affects the product invention awards (a measure for innovation). The results are robust in terms of cross-sectional variations and the several alternative research designs. 2. For the objective 2, since the international financial reporting standards have changed the way to treat R&D, our results suggest that the effect of the IFRS adoption on innovation can be associated with the relevance of IFRS that include how R&D is treated. We also included R&D in the regressions to test how R&D, after considering the IFRS adoption, affects product invention. 3. We have also achieved Objective 3 because we do show that IFRS affects the real operation of companies (product designs and development). We further show two mechanisms by which IFRS has impacts on international product development: attracting international institutional investors and attracting foreign private acquirers. In conclusion, with our paper, we have fully achieved the project objectives.

17502214.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502214.value: The project examines how the convergence of accounting standards internationally affects firms’ attention to, and effort on, global recognition in product markets. Using a difference-in-differences analysis, we find that winning the prestigious iF design awards, our proxy for a firm’s achievement in developing globally recognized products, is positively related to the mandatory adoption of IFRS in 2005. We also find that such a relation is stronger for firms in common-law countries or in countries with a good audit environment. We further examine channels through which the IFRS mandate changes firms’ incentive to pursue iF design awards. We find that, after IFRS adoption, firms attract more international institutional investors and foreign acquirers who use winning iF design awards as a global relative performance measure to evaluate managers. Overall, this study highlights the real effect of the IFRS mandate on the product market space and innovation.

17502214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502214.value: First, we would like to discuss the impact of the study. We contribute to the literature in two ways. (1) this study adds to the literature on capital market regulations and financial reporting standards using a novel dataset of product development. The effect of regulations on real economies has been debated for a long time (Bushee and Leuz 2005; Leuz and Wysocki 2016; Ball 2016). We tackle this issue by examining a critical economic growth engine, product development, in a global setting. Thus, our study sheds light on this line of literature from a new perspective and answers the call by Leuz and Wysocki (2016) for research exploring the real effects of regulation mandates globally. (2) our evidence suggests that the international convergence of financial reporting can lead to convergence in corporate operations. In particular, we show that the convergence of accounting standards can have a profound impact on globalization of product development, which is measured by the iF award, an international prize for excellent product inventions. This extends the research on accounting standard convergence (e.g., De George et al. 2015). Second, for the future development of the research, we hope that we can publish this project’s work on one of international journals (currently the paper is under review at Management Science). We also intend to extend our research to China’s setting, which can be more relevant to our community.

17502214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502214.value: In this project, we show that the adoption of international financial reporting standards, which are regarded as better accounting standards improving financial reporting quality and transparency, positively affect product inventions and designs. We also show that one of the underlying mechanisms is that international financial reporting standards attract sophisticated international investors so that the companies implementing these standards are better monitored and motivated for product development. Our findings have significant implications to regulators and investors. For regulators who intend to promote innovation, improving financial reporting can be one of the ways to facilitate innovation. For investors who search for investment opportunities in firms with long-term competitiveness, focusing on firms in high quality financial reporting environments can be the first step to find out candidate companies with innovative product designs.

17502514.label: Project Objectives
17502514.value: We aim to construct an extensive international panel data, containing firm level information such as stock return and other key accounting variables. We will also collect country's systematic risk factors (MKT, SMB, HML, MOM, IVOL, INV, etc.) and country risk profile including financial risk, political risk, and economic risk. This data should also include country characteristics in many dimensions, such as intellectual property protection, shareholder protection, limits-to-arbitrage, and growth opportunities. We then conduct comprehensive portfolio analysis and predictive regressions to discover whether the R&D intensity can predict returns in an international stage. We then construct alternative measures of R&D intensity to confirm the economic and statistical significance of R&D return predictability around the world. Based on our hypothesis, we will also examine whether R&D intensity can predict firm productivity, profitability, and return volatility and performance volatility. We study whether such an effect is intervened by country-specific characteristics such as shareholder production, infrastructure, intellectual property protection, risk preference, information environment, tax policy, and government policies. We also study the intermediary role of country risk profiles including financial risk, political risk, and economic risk.

17502514.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502514.value: 1. Using an unbalanced comprehensive panel of public firms listed in 21 countries with stock returns from 1981 July to 2012 June in the Datastream and Worldscope databases, we find that R&D-intensive firms are associated with higher subsequent stock returns. 2. This relationship is robust in equally-weighted and value-weighted portfolio analyses and predictive regressions, and different proxies of R&D intensive measures. 3. We conduct cross sectional regressions to find out that R&D investments are associated with higher market-to-book ratio, higher future profitability, and higher future return volatility; all these results collectively support that R&D investments are closely related to growth options. 4. We construct three sets of country-level proxies for dispersion in growth option value, limits-to-arbitrage, and sentiments, respectively, to test rational and behavior explanations. 5. We also construct four measures to quantify the R&D effect for each country in a month: top-minus-bottom R&D spreads (both equal- and value-weighted) and the slopes on R&D intensity from cross-sectional regressions (both equal- and value-weighted). 6. We regress these R&D effect measures on these country-specific variables and find that R&D spreads and slopes can be significantly explained by growth option proxies but not by the proxies for limits-to-arbitrage or sentiments. These results indicate that, in markets with higher value to growth options, stock returns are more sensitive to R&D activities as these markets more likely recognize the value of growth options driven by R&D investments. Thus, our country-level analyses also support that the R&D effect could be attributed to risk premiums rather than market frictions or behavioral bias.

17502514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502514.value: 1. As intangible investment, R&D intensity is associated with future stock returns. We may compare the tangible investment--return and intangible investment--return relationships. How are they related to each other in an international setting? 2. RD effect is hard to explain by the current international asset factor models. We may explore whether a global RD factor can be useful in pricing stock returns in each country over the world. 3. We may consider comparing the return predictive power between the innovation input RD, and the innovation output patents around the world. This requires the collection of international patents data and merge with our current data. 4. Our result that RD strongly predict returns in an international setting has strong implications for global investors. Combined with other findings from empirical studies on global investment, such as value premium, investment effect, momentum and reversal, investors may be able to develop more profitable trading strategies.

17502514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502514.value: 1. Firms spending more on research and development have higher future stock returns. This is not only true in U.S., but also prevails in other international financial markets. 2. Investors can follow conventional approach to build portfolio in many ways based on this finding to achieve superior performance in stock market. 3. This phenomenon can be more pronounced in some countries than others, for example, those which have better growth prospectives, or where the stock market is more efficient in processing information. 4. Investors can take the differences in this RD effect across countries in the portfolio construction. They can further employ strategies to change the weights of their capitals to invest more in countries with more information efficiency and growth opportunities every period to further outperform the benchmark.

17502614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502614.value: Research on organizational ambidexterity continues to receive increasing attention and has been extended to services research. More firms across service industries (e.g., retail banks, department stores, airlines, and restaurants) are exploring a service‒sales ambidextrous strategy, by redesigning the responsibilities of their service employees to include the dual goals of providing excellent services while achieving increased sales targets, as a way to maximize the profit potential inherent within customer-employee interactions. Such a strategy is supposed to increase employee productivity and improve their service and selling skills through cross- and up-selling. Customers also are expected to be more satisfied and loyal because of receiving more comprehensive and one-stop services. However, successful implementation of this dual service‒sales strategy may be difficult and tension may be created because the two goals of service versus sales reflect distinct organizational philosophies and compete for limited employee resources. It also may cause adverse experiences such as increased job stress and waiting time for employees and customers, respectively, which will ultimately result in deterioration in both service and sales levels. These opposing views on the strategy also are evidenced in the mixed performance results revealed across academic studies and business presses and reports. Recent studies may have improved our understanding of how to engage and facilitate employees to take on dual service‒sales assignments, but they fail to account for employees’ experience let alone customers’ experience when employees take on the challenges of simultaneously achieving the dual goals. They also lack a coherent conceptualization embracing the interactions between employees and their customers. Therefore, the proposed research aims to examine the respective experiences of employees and customers (benefits and costs that they perceived) arising from employees adopting dual service‒sales roles, and how they influence employee job satisfaction, customer satisfaction, and employee job performance in terms of achieving service, sales, and efficiency goals. We will also identify specific firms’ supports and customer-employee relationship characteristics that can increase the benefits and/or reduce the costs associated with a dual service‒sales strategy. Findings of this research will help address the controversies surrounding the effectiveness and performance effects of a service‒sales ambidextrous strategy and contribute to inform both service researchers and managers about how to design a performance-enhancing strategy by building up the positive experience (or benefits) and addressing the negative experience (or costs and concerns) perceived by employees and customers, respectively.

17502714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502714.value: Research and development (R&D) is the major driving force behind technology improvement at the country/industry level, and enhances individual firm performance in the modern economy. Many countries invest heavily in R&D to develop new products or improve productivity or quality of existing products. In Germany, for example, 66.0% of firms in the manufacturing industries reported to invest in R&D according to the Mannheim Innovation Panel (MIP), with 58.7% of firms reporting product innovation and 31.5% reporting process innovation from 1993 to 2008. In 1999, R&D accounted for 2.84% of Germany’s GDP. Technology spillover, as one type of externality, is another important source of technology improvement. If a firm develops a technology innovation, other firms may benefit from it through various channels such as imitation, patent disclosure, and informal acquisition of the new innovation knowledge. The presence of technology spillover has a significant impact on firms’ R&D decisions, with firms considering the effects of such spillover when they choose their R&D investment. In this case, the R&D decisions of individual firms, although optimal at the individual firm level, usually lead to under-investment in R&D. Some government policies (e.g, lump-sum R&D subsidies and R&D tax incentives) are necessary to solve this externality problem. Information on the existence and size of such spillover is essential for the proper implementation of such policies. The goals of the proposed project are to study firms’ R&D-innovation process, detect the innovation spillover among firms, and investigate firms’ dynamic R&D demand in the presence of technology spillover using a novel dataset MIP. The MIP is collected by the Centre for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Germany. It surveys firms’ R&D activities and innovation outcomes yearly. It contains information on R&D expenditure and its direct R&D outcomes – product innovation and process innovation – as well as the usual data on revenue, input expenditure, and other firm characteristics. Using this dataset, we will construct and estimate a dynamic structural model of endogenous firm R&D demand in the presence of technology spillover. This model will allow us to achieve the aforementioned goals. This work will extend the current literature to allow for continuous R&D choice and technology spillover among firms. Our structural model can also be applied to evaluation of the effects of different innovation-stimulating policies, such as lump-sum R&D subsidies and R&D investment tax incentives. 研究与开发在现代经济下是推动国家和产业技术进步的源动力，同时也是提升企业竞争力的核心因素。许多国家投资大量的研发以开发新产品，提高生产效率，或改进现有产品的质量。以德国为例，据Mannheim Innovation Panel （MIP）统计，在1993到2008年期间66.0%的企业宣称进行过研发投入，其中58.7%的企业获得了产品创新，31.5%的企业获得了流程创新。在1999年，德国研发投入占其国内生产总值的2.84%。 技术溢出作为一种外部性，是技术进步的又一源泉。如果一个企业获得了一项技术创新，其它企业可能以不同的方式从中获益，例如模仿，专利技术披露，以及以非正式的方式获取的新技术知识。技术溢出效应的存在会极大的影响企业的研发决策，因为企业在做研发决策时会考虑其从其他企业的创新中获益的可能性，同时也会考虑其它企业也会从其创新中获益。一个直接的结果就是，在有技术溢出效应的前提下，虽然每个企业的研发决策对其自身都是最优决策，但对社会来说并非最优--往往导致研发投入偏低。在这种情况下，政府有必要利用相关的政策（例如，一次性研发补贴或研发税收激励）来解决技术溢出带来的外部性问题。对技术溢出存在性的确认以及外部性大小的度量是正确选择和实施这些政策的关键。 这个研究项目主要有三个目的：（1）研究企业的创新过程，（2）确认并度量技术溢出效应的大小，（3）模型化企业在面临技术溢出效应时的动态研发投入决策。这个项目主要使用德国欧洲经济研究中心（ZEW）收集整理的一个非常独特的数据MIP。这个数据库对企业的研发投入和创新的结果进行年度问卷调查。它涵盖的信息不仅包括了研发投入，还包括了其导致的直接创新结果—产品创新和流程创新—以及其他变量例如销售收入、投入品支出、以及其他企业特征变量。利用这个数据，我们建立并估计一个在技术溢出效应下企业的动态研发投资决策模型。这个模型能有效实现以上三个研究目标。这项工作在两个方面拓展了现有文献，其一是估计了动态条件下企业的研发投资量，其二是允许动态条件下的技术溢出效应。这个动态结构模型可以用来评估和筛选多种研发激励政策，例如一次性政府研发补贴和研发税收激励等。

17502714.label: Realisation of objectives
17502714.value: We developed a dynamic R&D investment model and estimate it using data from two electronics industries in Taiwan, in order to evaluate the long-term gains from R&D. We find that long-term private gains from R&D is large (Objective 1). We tested the possibility for cross-firm spillover using many different ways, using both the Taiwan data and the original German data, and found no evidence of significant spillover across firms (Objective 2). Based on the dynamic structural model, we estimated individual firms' dynamic R&D investment decisions. We find that firms do take into account the long-term payoff to optimize their R&D investment. However, they need to overcome short-term costs of R&D, which may create a burden to their short-term balance sheet (Objective 3 and 4). Given our dynamic R&D investment model, we can directly apply the dynamic estimation results to evaluate the impact of a variety of different R&D incentive policies on firm and industry growth (Objective 5). We also find that inventory and demand shocks play an important role in determining firm investment and turnover (Objective 5). We completely achieved the first 4 objectives, and about 95% of Objective 5 (policy evaluation), which we are currently working on using Taiwanese R&D tax credit policy as an experiment. The (first) paper will be ready for submission after the final step is done. These results are summarized in two papers. 1. "The Long-Run Payoff to R&D Investment in the Electronics Industry in Taiwan" by Bee Yan Aw, Yi Lee, Mark J. Roberts, and Hongsong Zhang, working paper, 2017. 2. "Productivity or Unexpected Demand Shocks: What Determines Firms' Investment and Exit Decisions?" by Pradeep Kumar and Hongsong Zhang, International Economic Review, accepted 2018.

17502714.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502714.value: In the first paper, "The Long-Run Payoff to R&D Investment in the Electronics Industry in Taiwan", we made the following major findings: (1) R&D investment affects the future path of firm productivity, short-run profits, and long-run value. The elasticity of revenue productivity with respect to R&D spending varies between 0.08 and 0.10 across firms in the two Taiwanese electronics industries. These productivity gains persist over time with an elasticity between 0.40 and 0.50. The expected long-run return to R&D is measured as the impact of R&D expenditure on the expected future value of the firm. The elasticity of firm value with respect to R&D spending varies between 0.03 and 0.10, implying very substantial returns to R&D investment among the leading firms in these industries. (2) A variety of tests found very weak productivity spillovers in both the Taiwanese electronics industries and German firm-level data. (3) Firm R&D investment largely depends on firm capital size and current productivity, which determines the long-run payoff of R&D investment. However, the R&D investment costs are large too, and they need to be paid in the short run. (4) These analysis implies that R&D subsidies may be effective to help firms overcome the short-term investment costs. In the second paper, "Productivity or Unexpected Demand Shocks: What Determines Firms' Investment and Exit Decisions?", the main findings are as follows: We investigate the roles played by unexpected demand shocks, besides productivity, on firms' capital investment and exit decisions. We propose a practical approach to recovering unexpected firm-level demand shocks using inventory data. The recognition of demand shocks and inventory also improves the productivity estimation. The empirical results indicate that while productivity and demand shocks are both significant factors determining firm behavior, the former is more important for investment decision and the latter is more salient for firm exit. These findings confirm that unexpected demand shocks, besides persistent productivity, are necessary factors when analyzing capital investment and firm exit decisions.

17502714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502714.value: The research project opens up a variety of potential projects for future consideration. First, the dynamic R&D investment model can be used to evaluate a variety of different R&D subsidy policies, which has both academic and policy implication. Second, although we did a variety of tests we find very weak productivity spillover across firms. This generates future projects to investigate why and under what circumstances the R&D and productivity spillover is significant. Finally, our study on the impact of unexpected demand shocks and productivity firm investment and turnover implies that the unexpected demand shocks play important roles in determining firm activity. We plan to further explore its impact on firm performance in a follow-up project.

17502714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502714.value: Research and development (R&D) is the engine of growth for both micro firms and the aggregate economy in modern economy. As a result, it is important to understand how heterogeneous firms make their R&D decisions in a world with productivity uncertainty. This project aims at understanding the how firms make their dynamic R&D decisions and its impact on firms' growth and turnover in the long run. Our model allows us to empirically quantify the impacts of R&D on productivity and long-run profits, and to evaluate the importance of various factors determining R&D demand and firm growth. This framework can be applied to evaluate the impact of a variety of R&D incentive policies. Also, our study of the role of productivity and unexpected demand shocks broadens our understanding of how firms grow and die. We find that while both productivity and unexpected demand shocks are both significant factors determining firm behavior, the former is more important for investment decision and the latter is more salient for firm exit. These findings have significant policy implication on how to promote firm growth. Moreover, this paper also provides a practical approach of measuring the demand uncertainty faced by firms based on inventory volatility.

17503014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503014.value: In recent years, customer participation (CP) has rapidly become one of the most revered management practices. A 2010 article in Business Week states that CP is “the second largest innovation trend happening today, right behind sustainability.” This belief is echoed by the IBM Global CEO 2011 survey, in which most CEOs indicate that “the most successful organizations are those that co-create products and services with consumers and integrate customers into the core processes”. CP has also received tremendous attention from the academic community. It is argued that CP improves knowledge exchange, product quality, and new product development performance. As CP may well be the next frontier in creating competitive advantage, it seems clear that firms should proactively incorporate the voice of customers and collaborate with them to create values. Despite the enthusiasm for CP in both industry and academic circles, its true value in new product development (NPD) warrants further investigation. It is well-known that the NPD process is fraught with potential conflict, and managing this inter-functional conflict is a highly complex endeavor. The involvement of external customers who have different mental models and behavioral habits can further exacerbate this problem. Given the ubiquity of conflict in the NPD process, it is surprising that no study so far has investigated the relationship between CP and potential conflict in the NPD context. The absence of investigation is of major concern because such conflict can adversely impact NDP output and impair firm performance. To address these research gaps, we incorporate conflict management theory into NPD research and examine the interplay among CP, conflict, and NPD performance, with a dyadic sample of high-tech firms and their major customers in China. Specifically, we examine the following questions: (1) How does CP affect conflict in the NPD process? (2) How does the nature of the new product, e.g., degree of market and technology newness, moderate the effect of CP on conflict? (3) What is the underlying process through which conflict affects NPD performance in customer co-development projects? (4) What mechanisms mitigate the potential negative effects of conflict on NDP performance in customer co-development projects? By addressing these research questions, our study will not only enrich the CP literature by uncovering both the bright and dark side of CP in NPD, but also provide important implications for high-tech companies, including Hong Kong firms, in terms of understanding how to collaborate with customers to develop superior new products in China. 在近年来，客户参与迅速成为最受关注的管理实践。商业周刊的一篇文章指出，客户参与是“今天仅位于可持续性之后的伟大创新。”IBM 2011年全球CEO的调研报告同样指出，“最成功之企业是那些与顾客共创产品及服务并整合客户进入核心过程之企业。” 客户参与在学术界也倍受关注。有学者认为客户参与能增强知识交换，产品质量，及新产品开发绩效。客户参与可能成为下一个创造竞争优势的前沿，故公司需要积极主动地与客户合作以创造价值。 尽管客户参与受到学术界与业界的一致认可，它对新产品开发的真正价值还有待考量。众所周知，新产品开发充满了跨部门冲突，而且冲突管理极其复杂。因为客户有不同的思维模式和行为习惯，引入他们会让冲突问题更加复杂。尽管此冲突会负面影响新产品开发成果及企业绩效，现在文献缺乏对客户参与和冲突在新产品开发过程中的研究。 为解决这些问题，我们引入冲突管理理论来研究客户参与，冲突，及新产品开发绩效之间的关系。 此研究将基于高科技公司于其主要客户之间的双边数据。研究问题如下： （1） 客户参与如何影响新产品开发过程中的冲突？ （2） 新产品的特性（例如市场新颖度和技术新颖度）如何调节客户参与对冲突的影响？ （3） 在客户共同开发项目中，冲突对新产品开发绩效的影响机制是什么？ （4） 在客户共同开发项目中，什么机制能减少冲突对新产品开发绩效的负面作用？ 本项目的研究结果将揭示客户参与之正面与负面的影响；这不仅会丰富客户参与的文献，还会对高科技公司（包括香港公司）掌握如何与客户共同开发卓越新产品提供重要的指导。

(3) To uncover the process through which conflict may hinder NPD performance through resource commitment and compromise in customer co-development projects
(4) To examine what mechanisms can help firms mitigate the negative effect of conflict in in customer co-development projects

(5) To provide implications for high-tech companies, including Hong Kong firms, in terms of understanding how to collaborate with their customers to develop superior new products in the Chinese emerging market

17503014.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503014.value: Major findings: 1) Customer participation (CP) have two distinct facets, which affect conflict differently. Customer participation as the information provider (CPI) mitigates conflict, whereas customer participation as the codeveloper (CPC) increases it. 2) The nature of new products act as important moderator. Market newness attenuates the role of CPI in mitigating conflict and reduces the positive effect of CPC on conflict; in contrast, technology newness increases the influence of CPC on conflict. 3) Conflict hinders NPD performance through reducing resource commitment and increasing compromise in customer co-development projects. 4) Both formal (e.g., coordination) and informal (e.g., relational ties) mechanisms can mitigate the negative effect of conflict by moderating its impact on resource commitment and comprise. 5) Legal inadequacy negatively relates to customer participation, whereas dysfunctional competition positively affects customer participation. Further, the negative effect of legal inadequacy on customer participation is more salient for local firms than foreign firms, and the positive effect of dysfunctional competition is weaker when the focal firm has longer exchange experience. Outcome: two working papers under review at peer-reviewed journals 1) “How Does Customer Participation Hurt New Product Development Performance? Customer Role, Product Newness, and Conflict”, under 1st round of R&R at Journal of Business Research. 2) “Institutional Forces and Customer Participation in New Product Development: A Yin-Yang Perspective,” under 2nd round of R&R at Industrial Marketing Management. Two papers published in peer-reviewed journals. 1) Lu JJ, KZ Zhou, Y Wang (2016), “Exploitation and Exploration in International Joint Ventures: Moderating Effects of Partner Control Imbalance and Product Similarity?” Journal of International Marketing, 24(4): 20-38. 2) Zhou KZ, GY Gao, and H Zhao (2017), “State Ownership and Product Innovation in China: An Integrated View of Institutional and Efficiency Logics,” Administrative Science Quarterly, 62(2): 375–404.

17503014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503014.value: One potential way is to study how the role of customer participation varies in different institutional settings. We could develop a model to examine, for example, how economic development and guanxi importance moderate the impacts of customer participation on conflict and NPD performance.

17503014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503014.value: This project advances a framework to study the effects of customer participation of high-tech firms in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) Institutional characteristics– legal inadequacy and dysfunctional competition – differentially influence customer participation in firms’ NPD process in China. 2) If customers participate as information provider, it helps reduce customer-developer conflict; in contrast, if customers participate as the codevloper, it will increase customer-developer conflict. 3) The effect of CP as information provider is less salient when market newness of the product is higher; the effect of CP as co-developer is more salient if technology newness of the product is higher. 4) Conflict can reduce resource commitment and increase compromise in customer co-development projects, which in turn hurt NPD performance. 5) Firms should use formal coordination and informal relational ties to reduce the negative effect of conflict on NPD performance. The findings of this project not only enrich our understanding of the roles of customer participation in China, but also provide important managerial implications for companies to understand the differential aspects of CP and match them with different types of product newness to reduce the potential conflict and enhance NPD performance.

17503314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503314.value: 在当今充斥社交网络， 网上社区，和用户原创内容的年代， 公司放开了其创新的流程，在产品设计中融入了来自开放人群（包括消费者，设计人员，工程师，科学家，营销人员，研发人员，等等）的创造力。这个项目研究的产品共创模型（PCCR），代表一个新的用线上平台和大众共同开发产品的行业，并展示了众包这个新商业模式在新产品开发（NPD）方面的巨大潜力。 与内部开发新产品不同，这个开放式的创新将大众作为创造力，智慧和人力资源的源泉。 本提议研究项目对于这个有待开发的新兴学术领域有着显著的贡献。我们先描述PCCR模型的理论框架，着重于两个方面：最初概念和最终产品。我们通过区分产品概念的新颖度，用户价值和可行性来探求不同的质量范畴。 我们研究这些质量特性对最初概念成功通过筛选和研发阶段的影响力。接着，我们连接产品概念与最终产品，提出产品概念的质量对最终产品绩效的影响。 不仅于此，我们调查大众的专长在各个产品开发接段的作用， 以来探求价值是如何共创的。具体地，我们检验大众在技术（非技术）产品研发阶段的含有技术（非技术）专长的投入如何提高产品的质量和销售业绩。最后，我们建议调查如何识别提供最多价值的产品概念提供者和开发者，并且假定这两组大众不会有太大的重合。 我们挑选了一个现实世界的PCCR案例模型来实现我们的研究框架：出现于最近的学术研究中Quiky.com。我们详述了我们收集的历史数据，并且建议用在人力资源众筹平台上消费者评分来扩充数据。这种平台是线上商业研究用来挖掘智力资源的最新发展。 从管理的角度来说，这个研究推荐众包作为一个有效的NPD过程，并且为PCCR决策，如概念筛选，产品选择等提供指导，以取得最好的产品市场业绩。在研究中提取的研发过程的独有信息能更好地帮助描述如何通过PCCR共创价值。对于大众个体的研究为如何鉴别和挖掘大众中最具生产力和利润创造力群体的潜力提供借鉴。

17503314.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503314.value: Soliciting novel ideas from the crowd is a paradigm shift for innovation that gains increasing attention from researchers and practitioners. However, studies examining the relationship between the novelty of crowdsourced ideas and firms' idea adoption decisions are surprisingly rare. This research adopts the path-of-least-resistance (POLR) theory as a new theoretical angle to examine the role of idea feasibility as a key heuristic cue mediating the effect of idea novelty on adoption decisions. We further explore factors that may amplify or mitigate this mediation. Using data collected from a laboratory experiment and a firm-sponsored crowdsourcing community, we reveal that firms tend to follow the POLR by using idea feasibility as meta-information to evaluate novel ideas in their idea adoption decisions. However, this tendency depends on external stimuli and constraints, such that the mediation of idea feasibility exists only when idea favorability from the crowd is low or when an ideator's prior ideation participation is high. Our supplementary study further offers preliminary insights on the extension of our proposed effects to the ultimate success of adopted ideas. These findings illuminate a better understanding of firms' idea adoption decisions and suggest ways to manage idea crowdsourcing effectively for new product/service development and improvements.

17503314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503314.value: Our study has some limitations. First, we only focus on firm-sponsored idea crowdsourcing platforms that are open and without financial incentives. However, the idea selection and adoption processes might differ across different crowdsourcing approaches (e.g., one-time crowdsourcing contests or platforms that are organized by intermediaries with restricted access to ideas and comments), which are thus worth exploring. Second, as firms seldom disclose actual decision makers (i.e., who and how to make final idea adoption decisions) and their internal idea selection mechanisms (if any) in those firm-sponsored idea crowdsourcing communities, we are unable to shed insights on this regard.

17503314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503314.value: Findings of this study have several practical implications. First, our research helps illuminate a better understanding of firms' bias in their idea filtering processes and tendency to take the POLR, that is choosing less novel ideas, which they might have been unaware of. Second, more favorable comments from the crowd can push firms off the POLR.Third, firms need to be aware of potential challenges in developing idea crowdsourcing platforms.

18200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18200114.value: Cointegration is an econometric concept that describes the common equilibria in an economic series through linear transformation. The founder of this concept was awarded a Nobel Prize in Economics in 2003. Recent studies are focused on non-linear cointegration models. Threshold and regime-switching cointegration models are two important empirically testable models that are used in practice. However, their uses in stochastic optimal control problems in finance are not considered in this work. The possible financial problems to which this concept can be applied include but are not limited to portfolio selection, asset-liability management, consumption investment, and hedging. This study develops a general framework for dealing with stochastic optimal control problems when the multivariate stochastic processes exhibit non-linear cointegration in the form of thresholding or regime switching. The techniques involved are backward stochastic differential equations, the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman framework, partial differential equations, and Brownian occupation times. The theoretical results are empirically tested against real financial data. 在2003年諾貝爾經濟學獎得主因 “協整性” 這個經濟學概念而得獎。而它能通過線性變換去描述經濟學中的經濟均衡或市場均衡。此專案主要結合協整性於兩個重要的投資組合模型裡---臨界及體制轉換模型。應用協整性臨界模型和協整性體制轉換模型這兩個非線性協整模型於投資組合選擇、資產負債管理、消費投資和對沖是本專案的主要內容。並且會利用倒向隨機微分方程(BSDE)、漢密爾頓 - 雅可比 - 貝爾曼 (HJB) 框架和偏微分方程找出此非線性協整模型之問題的解。理論結果將會用財務數據實證驗証。

18200114.label: Major findings and research outcome
18200114.value: When the price process of risky assets or the related stochastic differential equations (SDE) are cointegrated, an explicit solution is hardly made for the optimal trading strategy. The difficulty seems on the stochastic parameter(s) in the price process/SDE. The traditional methods cannot be applied directly. This project does not only deal with cointegrated SDE but also threshold or regime-switching features. A lot of time were spent on the modelings and verification. Surprisingly, closed-form solutions are still obtained for many practical situations, including the consideration of portfolio management ([1], [3], [5], [6], [7], [9], [10], [12] ), the situations of pre-commitment ([1], [3], [10]) and time-consistent strategies ([4], [5],[6], [7], [9], [10]), and game ([2]). The application covers high-dimensional portfolio ([3]), interest rates ([4]), longevity securities ([2]), insurance risk ([1]), bond pricing ([4]), stocking pricing ([8]), subsistence consumption ([12]) and commodity ([10]). However, the cointegrated asset prices require additional conditions to ensure a stable (non-blow-up) the trading strategy. The stability is important for the verification theorem if the optimisation is based on the HJB framework. In [2], [5], [6] and [9] we discuss the verification theorems under different situations in detail. Besides, we investigate the statistical arbitrage opportunity under regime-switching setting in [10]. It concludes that regime-switching reduces statistical arbitrage opportunity significantly.

18200114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18200114.value: There are several future developments from this project. 1. Although a lot theoretical background and economic implication of the strategy are developed in this project under a constant cointegration matrix or regime oriented conintegration matrix, it remains unclear about the stochastic modeling for the process of cointegration matrix. 2. Although this project considers a market constraint on position limit, the other market constraint such as no-shorting, and transaction cost will be considered in the future research agenda. These are promising theoretical extensions. 3. AI techniques are recent hot topics. It would be interesting to investigate the combination of theoretical trading strategy and some ad hoc rule in industry by using AI techniques.

18200114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18200114.value: One of the longstanding problem in finance is optimal investment. However, under uncertain returns of stocks, chaotic structure of financial market data and sudden changing in market situations, investment decision becomes very difficult and non-robustness. This project addresses the issue that price processes are cointegrated (a kind of price structure) in a regime-switching or thresholding market situations (a kind of sudden changing market conditions). It develops several practical solutions to improve investment outcomes by taking into account of the chaotic market situations.The framework is justified mathematically, tested empirically and implemented efficiently. The project also addresses the potential use of the mathematical formulas in a big data environment. In addition to the aforementioned advantages of the mathematical and statistical approaches, this project also offers reasonable conditions under which the investment strategy can be implemented stably. The conditions provide insight into the favourable market regime and the investment horizon.

18400114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18400114.value: Leung Ping-kwan (Ye Si) is one of the most prominent and widely read Hong Kong modernist poets, novelists and critics. However, comparatively few in-depth studies have been conducted on the works of Leung as a modernist writer. I interviewed Leung in 2009, and when Leung was asked whether he would consider himself a modernist, his answer was yes. Despite his self-perception as a modernist, however, only a few scholarly works focus on the direct relationship between Leung’s works and modernism. Instead, Leung’s works are always discussed from various perspectives, such as from the perspectives of ordinary life/things, urbanisation, postcolonialism, magical realism, travelogue and Chinese lyrical tradition. This project will use the main corpus of Leung’s works as examples to demonstrate how he brings these apparently disparate but actually connected topics under the umbrella of Hong Kong modernism and helps to enrich the meaning of the literary movement. More specifically, this study will focus on three distinctive features of Hong Kong modernism which are observed in Leung’s works, namely, its relation to the ordinary, postcolonialism and Chinese literary tradition. Food, ordinary people and objects as well as our daily living space in Hong Kong are some of Leung’s favourite topics. Elements of postcolonialism and Chinese literary tradition are also frequently found in his work. Although studies on these three characteristics are not lacking, these characteristics are seldom discussed alongside Leung’s commitment to modernism. On the other hand, recent research suggests that Western modernism tends to depict ordinary life. The connections of Western modernism with postcolonialism and literary traditions have been widely discussed for decades. In comparison, relatively few studies have focused on Hong Kong modernism and its relationship with such concepts. This project strives to bridge this research gap by actively examining their precise relationships in the context of Hong Kong modernism. Leung once questioned the suitability and feasibility of adopting Western postcolonial theories to explain the colonial situation in Hong Kong. I will take Leung’s scepticism as far as possible as a strategy to study Hong Kong modernism. Thus, Western modernist theories serve only as a theoretical backdrop for this study. I believe that a systematic study of the literary works of Leung will help us to understand not only the distinctive features of his works, but also the precise uniqueness of Hong Kong modernism. 梁秉鈞（也斯）是香港其中一位最重要的現代主義詩人、小說家及評論家，他的作品備受廣泛的關注；然而，對其現代主義作品進行詳細及深入分析的評論卻相對不多。我在2009年曾經訪問梁秉鈞，其中一個問題是：他認為自己是現代主義者嗎？梁的答案是肯定的。雖然梁秉鈞認為自己是現代主義者，但有關梁跟現代主義的研究並不多，我們較多看到的是其他各種各樣的研究方向，例如： 梁秉鈞的作品跟城市化、殖民/後殖民主義、魔幻現實主義、遊記體、抒情傳統及日常生活或日常事物等關係。這個研究計劃會以梁秉鈞的主要作品為例，說明梁把以上這些看似無關連但實際上關係千絲萬縷的話題同時放在他的作品中，直接豐富了香港現代主義的內容。 為了達到上述的目的，這項研究會集中分析在梁秉鈞作品所包含的三個香港現代主義重要面向，它們包括：香港現代主義跟日常生活、殖民主義及中國文學傳統的關係。食物、普通人及物，還有就是香港日常的生活空間等都是梁秉鈞喜歡的話題。同樣地，後殖民主義和文學傳統等元素亦經常出現在梁的作品中。雖然對於這些題材的討論大不乏人，但把這些話題納入現代主義的討論中卻較少見。 事實上，最近有不少研究顯示西方現代主義作品傾向描述日常生活。同樣地，西方現代主義和後殖民主義及文學傳統的關連在過去一段日子亦受到廣泛的討論。相比之下，香港現代主義跟這些概念之間的討論絕無僅有，這個研究計劃旨在補充這個漏洞，積極探討這些話題與香港現代主義之間的關係。 梁秉鈞曾質疑引用西方的殖民/後殖民理論來說明香港殖民狀況的適當性及可行性。我會將梁的懷疑論視為一種策略，用來探討香港現代主義，因此在整個研究的過程中西方現代主義理論只是被看作一種理論背景、一個參照點。我相信對梁秉鈞的文學作品進行有系統的研究不單會幫助我們理解其作品的特色，更可以讓我們明白香港現代主義獨特的地方。

18400114.label: Realisation of objectives
18400114.value: The project’s objectives stated below have been achieved, as demonstrated by my research outputs (please refer to Part C). To achieve this end, I have divided my study into five stages. In the first stage, I have examined the topic of modernisms in Hong Kong in the context of Western modernisms and Chinese modernism of the 1940s, with special references to Leung Ping-kwan, and other two Hong Kong modernist writers Liu Yichang and Ma Lang. The relationships among modernisms, the traditional, the ordinary, the colonial situations, and translation stood out as crucially important as a result. I have studied these issues in detail during the research period. I have examined the relationship between Hong Kong modernism and the Chinese literary traditions in the second stage. By doing this, the Chinese lyrical tradition and the yongwu tradition (tradition about objects) embodied in Leung’s work have been studied in the context of Hong Kong modernism. Leung Ping-kwan embedded and innovated ideas of the lyrical, as well as things or objects (wu), in his literary work which can be generally divided into four types: the lyrical novel, lyrical poetry, yongwu poems, and yongwu novels. So far as the Chinese lyrical tradition is concerned, it is interesting to note that Leung Ping-kwan started rejuvenating the tradition in the form of the novel instead of in poetry. Nonetheless, he did not consider his experiments successful and had to admit that poetry was a better form to present the lyrical. It was probably no coincidence that Leung ‘rewrote’ and rejuvenated nine Shijing poems of the same names, entitled “Shijing Exercise,” in his later years. The rejuvenation of the yongwu tradition is complicated since the definition of things and the relationship between human beings and things has been changing dramatically in recent years. Leung started writing yongwu poems (poems on objects) instead of novels as early as the 1970s and he intended to reinvigorate this sub-genre of the Chinese literary tradition. At some point, Leung’s yongwu poems were mainly referred to as food poetry. His inclusion of the “Liaozhai poetry” series in his book entitled East West Matters definitely helps us reconsider various issues, for example, the changing relationship between human beings and things, including food, sub-humans, animals, and so on, not to mention the fact that another topic in modernisms–primitivism–emerges in Leung’s works as a result. And due to the limitations of the poetic form, the changing roles played by things (in this case, food) and human beings cannot be effectively reflected by food poetry. Nor can the changing relationship between things and human beings in the modern world be presented clearly in Leung’s “Liaozhai poetry” series. He eventually achieved his goal through depicting food and things in such novels as Shimen the Dragon-keeper and Postcolonial Affairs of Food and the Heart, which I consider to be yongwu novels. The subtle connection between ordinary and Hong Kong modernism as manifested in Leung Ping-kwan’s works have been studied in the third stage. So far as the concept of the ordinary is concerned, perhaps the major difference between Leung and his Western counterparts is that there is no such thing as ordinary ‘ordinary’ in Hong Kong, which means he took nothing for granted. If the ordinary generally refers to things that we take for granted, Leung proposed that the colonial situation in Hong Kong suggests otherwise. Thus, Leung had to invent the ordinary, which resulted in depicting different daily things such as home, food, medicine, clothes, and so on, in his literary works. For example, Leung could not find a homely home in Hong Kong, but managed to invent an ordinary place out of the extraordinary: he found home away from home. Similarly, to what extent the axiom ‘you are what you eat’ may help forge a Hong Kong residents’ identity? The poet believed that, despite changes in food’s appearance, its essence could be discovered or recollected in different places. Clothes used to help people develop a stable identity, whereas modern fashion provides the tools for people to construct multiple identities or to hide their identities. In his poetry series Clothink Leung used the character of Alice from Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland as a reference point. He suggests that Alice can remain unchanged despite their change in appearance. Healthcare is also considered a part of our everyday life. Nonetheless, if the kind of disease—especially mental disease—was evoked by colonialism, the disease itself would become something ordinary, while medical treatment would be considered something extraordinary. Leung’s “Paper Cut-outs” and “An Acrobat’s Story” are novels that provoke deep thoughts in this regard. Perhaps the relationship between colonial/postcolonial studies and Leung’s modernism is the most complicated of all, and is manifested in two sub-genres, namely travelogues and magical realist novels, which have been discussed during the fourth stage of study. The travelogue is often seen as a form of cultural imperialism employed exclusively by colonizers. Recent attempt to study alternative travelogues suggests both the need to study ‘countertravel writing’ and to explore the complexity of the literary form. It is believed that by offering an opportunity to reflect on the possibility of writing travelogues from the perspective of the colonized shows how the genre can be understood in a sense that is not informed by imperialist ideology, if not one that subverts it. Leung’s travelogues, however, further distinguish themselves from those of the colonized and the colonizer in terms of perspective. Since he did not believe in a single perspective, he thought neither traditional travelogues nor ‘counter-travel writing’ could help to develop multiple perspectives. Thus, Leung tried to develop multiple perspectives in his travelogues. In a similar manner, many Western studies suggest that magical realism is a means of challenging colonialism. According to these studies, magical realism has numerous variants because of its controversial, complicated origins and its international nature. A close study of Leung’s two magical realist novels, Shimen and Paper Cut-outs, will reveal that although the author stated that his works were influenced by Latin American magical realism, the kind of magical realism found in his novels is definitely different from that of Latin America. Leung’s adaptation of magical realism in his writings of the 1970s raises numerous questions that undoubtedly contribute to our understanding of one other aspect of Hong Kong modernism. For instance, to what extent are Leung’s magical realist novels different from their Latin American counterparts? What are the reasons for the differences? One possible answer to these questions is again related to Leung’s preference for multiple perspectives. In the last stage of my study, I have summarized the modernist features embodied in Leung’s works by means of examining his translations. In collaboration with Osing, Leung translated his forty poems into English. Examining the differences between the original and the translated versions helps to manifest the major characteristics of Leung’s modernist work, namely celebrating multiple perspectives and inclusiveness. With a closer look at all these , these two features are in fact embodied in all the topics discussed in this project, though most of the time the reader may be distracted by various elements presented in Leung’s work.

Based on the research findings, a road map for future studies has been created.

18400114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18400114.value: I will continue working on several problems that are directly downstream of my current research. These all relate to Hong Kong literature and culture, including (1) the development of conceptions of the Hong Kong lyrical tradition; (2) the uniqueness of Hong Kong travelogue; and (3) the reception of magical realism in Hong Kong literature. All these areas are natural outgrowths of my current GRF project, which have not received enough attention before. As far as the study of conceptions of the Chinese lyrical tradition is concerned, there are two main issues that need to be addressed. First, critics always focus on the relationship between elite culture and the Chinese lyrical tradition. The close relationship among popular culture, cultural identity formation, and the Chinese lyrical tradition suggested by Chen Shih-hsiang has mostly neglected. Second, critics showed least interest in developing conceptions of a Hong Kong lyrical tradition. I suggest that a study of the conceptions of a Hong Kong lyrical tradition can help fill the research gaps. I have already included these issues in my new GRF application (2018/2019). Other research areas that may consider developing external grant proposals are Hong Kong travelogue and magical realist writing.

18400114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18400114.value: Given the relatively few studies that have been conducted on the relationship between Leung Ping-kwan and Hong Kong modernism, it is my goal that the issues — The relationships among modernisms, the traditional, the ordinary, the colonial situations, and translation — covered in my project will help re-orient Leung’s position in Hong Kong modernist literature and subsequently reposition Hong Kong modernism in the study of modernisms. As the project unfolds, we see how Leung, in order to understand his past, paid special attention to Chinese literary traditions. In order to forge his identity, he attempted to depict and invent ordinary things. The colonial condition in Hong Kong naturally drew Leung's interest to magical realist writing and ‘counter-travel writing,’ which were mostly created by other colonized writers. Nevertheless, it is obvious that Leung’s modernist features are different from those of the colonizer or the colonized. He found Hongkongers’ identities as fragmented instead of being unified. However, Leung believed that Hongkongers could develop and discover a unified self somewhere and sometime. This belief contributed to the development of Leung’s modernist features—celebrating multiple perspectives and inclusiveness—which are also the uniqueness of Hong Kong modernism.

18400914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18400914.value: This proposed study will examine the development of Cantonese narrative in ethnic minority children of Hong Kong with special focus on three sub-groups, namely, Indian, Pakistani, and Nepalese, who are commonly called South Asians (SA hereafter). Despite public concerns and the recent efforts of the Hong Kong government to help these children develop their language proficiency in Chinese, their oral narrative in Cantonese, which is an important component for success in school, has not been duly examined and documented. The absence of such research evidence could hinder the development of an effective Chinese-language education program for ethnic minority children. According to Bruner (1991), a narrative is a main mode of human thought in which human actions and intentions are interpreted and organized with internal consistency and social value. A narrative is an important tool for socialization (Miller, Wiley, Fung, & Liang, 1997) and the transmission of cultural knowledge (Campbell, 1988). The development of narrative begins from the personal narratives of children with support from adults (McCabe & Peterson 2004). In addition to social interactions with adults, language and cognition are major determinants of the narrative development in children; with language and cognition, children organize and refer to events that are understood as socially meaningful (Nelson, 1996; Bohanek, Fivush, & Duke, 2006). After initial explorations of personal narratives, children can advance to the development of decontextualized speech, which is the ability to speak about and understand events in the past or in the future and a major precursor to literacy development (Tabors et al., 2001; Whitehurst & Lonigan, 1998). To examine the development of Cantonese narrative in SA children in Hong Kong, this project will adopt a cross-sectional correlational design in which children's narratives will be collected at two different time points with 10 months interval. Three groups of primary school SA children in grades 1, 3, and 5 (each with 30 children) will be examined. Age-matched native Cantonese children from the same school will be tested as controls. Two elicitation tasks, personal experience sharing and picture-story retelling, will be used to collect narrative samples. Standardized oral Cantonese and Chinese assessment tools will be adopted to investigate their contributions to narrative development.

18400914.label: Realisation of objectives
18400914.value: This project investigated the development of oral Cantonese narrative in three sub-groups of ethnic minority children in Hong Kong, namely, Indian, Pakistani, and Nepalese, commonly known as South Asians (SA hereafter). Ninety SA children, from age 7 to age 14 were examined, with another sixty age-matched native Cantonese children tested as controls. HKCOLAS, a standardized oral Cantonese test, a narrative elicitation task and a Chinese reading test were administered twice to each participant with a 10-month interval in between. Due to the big variations in these children's oral Cantonese, comparisons between age groups did not yield any meaningful results. Instead, regression analyses were conducted with data collected in the first year as predictors of their narrative performance in the second year. Contrary to the impression that written Chinese is the sole barrier of these SA children in their schooling, the results show that most of these South Asian children performed poorly in their spoken Cantonese. Of all the linguistic variables examined, their vocabulary is the weakest and showed little growth during the period of investigation. SA children made some progress in their Cantonese grammar, which is also believed to be the contributing factor to their gain in the story-retelling task in the second year. With these results, the four objectives of the project were fully achieved and the major findings are highlighted as below. Objective 1 - To compare the L2 narrative development of school-age SA children with that of age-matched native Cantonese controls; By using the sub-test of HKCOLAS, a picture-story retelling task, the narrative performance of SA children from age 7 to age 14 was examined. According to the norm data of HKCOLAS, most SA children's performance was 2 SD below their age-matched peers while the controls, as expected performed within the normal range. Objective 2 - To examine whether uneven profiles exist in the Cantonese narrative development of SA children at micro- and macro-structure levels According to the results of the narrative task, most SA children produced barely acceptable stories. At macro level fewer attempts and actions were mentioned. At micro level, simple declarative sentences, mixed with sentence fragments, were produced. It is such a 'flat' profile, that the term 'uneven profile' is barely applicable. The most unexpected finding is that while they made some good progress in grammar, their oral vocabulary is much weaker and did not show any significant gain in 10 months. This uneven growth at the micro-level is quite different from what had been reported in the second language learning literature, that vocabulary grows before grammar. Future investigation may include receptive vocabulary test as the expressive vocabulary test used in this study could be too challenging and cannot reflect SA children's minute gain in word learning within one year. Objective 3 - To examine the role of written Chinese proficiency in the development of Cantonese narrative in SA children A Chinese reading test was used to access SA children's written Chinese proficiency. SA children were asked to perform a read-aloud task in which written characters of the test items used in the oral vocabulary test that they received earlier were used as stimuli. Results from regression analyses showed that their performance in reading Chinese in the first year did not predict their oral narrative scores in the second year. Further analyses showed that many SA children cannot name the objects but they can read the constituent characters, such 'car; in 'car park', and 'sky' in 'sky bridge'. This is another interesting finding that have not been reported in the literature. Objective 4 - To examine the role of L2 vocabulary and grammar in the development of Cantonese narrative in SA children Only SA children's receptive grammar of Oral Cantonese in the first year can predict the narrative score in the second year, with an R square of 0.136. However, some non-significant growth in vocabulary is also observed.
