18400914.label: Major findings and research outcome
18400914.value: This project examined the development of Cantonese narrative skills of in school-age children with south Asia background. Ninety SA children, from age 7 to age 14 SA were tested with a standardized oral Cantonese test and a self-developed narrative elicitation task. Their growth in oral Cantonese was measured at two time points, with a 10- month interval in between. Sixty age-matched children who spoke Cantonese as their first language were also tested as controls. The overall results showed that these SA children performed poorly in all language tasks and most of their scores were two years below their age-expectation levels. While they did show some progress in the test of receptive Cantonese grammar, there was no significant gain in their expressive vocabulary. They also did better when they were asked again to retell a story in the second year of the study. Regression analyses showed that their receptive grammar in the first year is a significant but weak predictor of their storytelling scores in the second year (R square = 0.14). Of the various linguistic components that were measured by the story-retelling task, SA children performed better in introducing referents and they did poorer in using connectives for encoding causality and temporality between events. Comparing the linguistic requirements of these two components, the challenge that SA children faced was a combination of syntactic and discourse-related matters. Besides, SA Children who were born in Hong Kong performed better than those who arrived at age 7 and older but the performance of those who came to Hong Kong before age 6 was not much inferior to the local-born group. An analysis of their language use in different domains revealed that children who used Cantonese outside classroom and across domains have better vocabulary, grammar and produced better stories. These findings suggested that when planning for the teaching and learning of Chinese to these SA children, in addition to the complex linguistic features of written Chinese, the role of oral Cantonese skills, in particular, as realized in their ‘integrative’ motivation, should not be overlooked.

18400914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18400914.value: Results from the survey of language use in SA children revealed that there was not a single language that can connect their life experience across domains. This is an aspect that should receive more attention when formulating educational programs for ethnic minority students.

18400914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18400914.value: This project investigated the development of oral Cantonese narrative in three sub-groups of ethnic minority children in Hong Kong, namely, Indian, Pakistani, and Nepalese, who are commonly called South Asians (SA hereafter). Ninety SA children, from age 7 to age 14 were examined with another sixty age-matched native Cantonese children were tested as controls. HKCOLAS, a standardized oral Cantonese test and a narrative elicitation task were administered. Contrary to the general impression that written Chinese is the major barrier of these SA children in their schooling, the results show that most of these South Asian primary students performed poorly in their spoken Cantonese. They could conduct daily conversations with classmates and friends to express their basic needs of life but they cannot appropriate words and sentence patterns to express their experiences or paraphrasing that have been said, in particular, a lack of background information and clear causal relations of events. These shortcomings in narrative ability have greatly affected their classroom learning where Cantonese is a medium of instruction. Their deficit in oral Cantonese should be addressed before remedial program of the written language is provided.

18401314.label: Project Objectives
18401314.value: to identify the profile of the working poor and examine the main mechanisms underlying in-work poverty in Hong Kong; to evaluate the impact of three existing measures (disregarding earnings in CSSA, statutory minimum wage, and the Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme) on the risk of in-work poverty in Hong Kong using static micro-simulation modeling; to evaluate all these proposed policy options such as income tax credit, child benefit and child care, low income family subsidy for working families with children, through static micro-simulation modeling; to estimate the financial sustainability of the existing anti-poverty measures and the proposed measures in the coming three decades using micro-simulation modeling; to evaluate the recommended measures or designs by taking into account the results obtained from achieving the above objectives, as well as by considering social (public acceptance to policy change), economic, and political circumstances of Hong Kong; and to recommend the most appropriate policy options by taking into account the results obtained from achieving all of the above objectives, and to propose a detailed redesign of the scheme and an appropriate implementation strategy.

18401314.label: Realisation of objectives
18401314.value: To achieve the objectives of this study, we conducted a household survey during the period between March 2015 and May 2016. The sampling frame used in this study was the list of household addresses (n=8,000) we purchased used for the General Household Survey conducted by the Department of Census and Statistics of the Hong Kong SAR Government. A two-stage stratified sampling design was used in this study to select our potential participants. In the first stage, a random sample of quarters was selected from a frame of quarter which were stratified by geographic area and the type of quarter. In the second stage, one working member of selected households with at least one working was randomly chosen using the last birthday method and invited to participate in the study. Using this sampling frame, we invited 5,681 households to participate in this study and 3,816 of them were successfully interviewed in face-to-face format at their household, yielding a response rate of 62.8 per cent. In these 3,816 households, there were 8,403 of them aged between 18 and 64. Among these 8,403 adults, 5,643 worked at least one week in the past year but most of them (4,950) worked full-year in the previous year. Survey content in individual, employment-related and household levels included: (a) individual variables: sex, age, educational attainment, marital status, place of birth, ethnicity, and health (self-rated health, presence of medical conditions, self-reported disability); (b) household level variables: household composition (2 adults without dependents i.e., children or retired older adults; single without dependents, single parents, 2 adults with one dependent, 2 adults with 2 dependents, 2 adults with more than 2 dependents; others), household labor intensity (the ratio of working to non-working household members of working age): 1; less than 0.5; ≥ 0.5 and <1), and number of earners (1 earner vs. 2 or more earners); (c) employment related variables: current details and history of economic activity and employment status (i.e., type of industry and occupation); hourly pay, low earning from main employment (< 66% of median earning); having secondary employment; other sources of income (family transfer and welfare in cash), employed vs. self-employed, size of workplace (1-5 persons, 6-10 persons, and more than 10 persons); type of contract (temporary or permanent); and weekly working time. Other assessment included (a) amount of income in the following sources: jobs, transfers from family members or friends, welfare (CSSA, other cash-transfer programs, in-kind programs such as public rental housing, food bank, education, and medical services), retirement schemes, rental income, investment and other income; (b) amount of expenditure in the following items: rental fees, mortgage payments, management fees for properties, rates and government fees for properties, utilities, food, traveling, contribution to retirement schemes, educational expenses, salaries for domestic helpers, gifts of money to relatives or friends, medical expenditures, medical insurance fees, taxes, daily necessities, clothing, entertainment, and personal services; (c) amount of financial assets (including self-occupied premises or debts). We used unfolding brackets to obtain the data on income and asset because it has been proven to overcome these potential problem areas and is adopted in large-scale national longitudinal studies of older Americans (Hill, 1999); (d) household income will be calculated based on personal income to be obtained and it is assumed to be equally shared among all individuals within a household. Secondly, we evaluated and compared the four existing measures, namely disregarding earnings in Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme, statutory minimum wage, the Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme, and public rental housing in their effectiveness and efficacy in in-work poverty reduction using a micro-simulation model we developed specifically for this project. Data obtained in the household survey mentioned above was used in this micro-simulation analysis. First, we estimated the percentage of households with workers receiving welfare benefits and the average level of benefits they received as a percentage of the poverty threshold. Then, program efficacy was assessed by calculating inclusion error (i.e. the percentage of families with workers who were not income poor but receiving welfare benefits) and the percentage of welfare expenditure spent on reducing the poverty gap while scheme effectiveness was measured by program coverage (i.e. to what extent the benefits reached poor families with workers), the percentage of the working poor could escape from poverty, and the share of poor households with workers receiving the benefits brought above the poverty threshold. We also estimated the change in poverty rate and poverty gap before and after the welfare intervention of each measure as well as the combined effect of all these four measures. The poverty rate is defined as the percentage of poor workers in the population of workers and poverty gap is the distance between household income and poverty line or the money needed to raise all families with workers out of poverty by number of household members. Poor families were identified using the official poverty threshold of Hong Kong in 2016, with square root formula household adjustment method. Thirdly, we designed four policy options including raising minimum wage substantially, introducing income tax credit, launching universal child benefit, and providing adequate and accessible free child care for this project and we also examined the Low-Income Working Family Allowance Scheme (renamed as Working Family Allowance in 2018) which the Government implemented in May 2016. Similar to what we did to the existing measures mentioned above, we evaluated these five measures in terms of their efficacy and effectiveness. First, we calculated the percentage of households with workers receiving those benefits and the average level of benefits they received as a percentage of the poverty threshold. Then, program efficacy was assessed by calculating inclusion error and the percentage of benefits used to reduce the poverty gap. Lastly, scheme effectiveness was measured by program coverage, the percentage of the working poor as well as the poor households with workers were brought above the poverty line. We also calculated change in poverty rate and poverty gap before and after the implementation of each measure. Fourthly, we developed a dynamic micro-simulation model to project the expenditure of the three existing cash benefits, namely disregarding earnings in Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme, the Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme and Working Family Allowance as well as two proposed cash benefits including income tax credit and child benefit. The model began the simulation period with data obtained in the survey conducted in 2015/2016 and the final output file was the detailed information for each household for each year from 2017 to 2048, on income and financial assets. In this simulation, we computed the complete chronological sequences from each household in turn and the model is a discrete time model in which status changes were computed annually. The sequence of each cycle was as follow: 1) mortality; 2) fertility; 3) new immigrant added to the household; 4) marital status, 5) living arrangement; 6) economic activity; 7) income and assets; and 8) welfare participation. Lastly, we interviewed a number of policy makers, social workers, tax payers, and working poor themselves to evaluate the acceptability of these measures we examined. Then we conducted a phone survey of 834 Hong Kong adults to evaluate the public attitude to introducing income tax credit and child benefit as policy options used to alleviate working poor.

18401314.label: Major findings and research outcome
18401314.value: We have found that low-paid work and the absence of a second earner living in household are the two main mechanisms that lead to in-work poverty in Hong Kong (Cheung and Chou, 2016). This findings are robust because we have found similar results when we defined poverty using material deprivation (Cheung, Chan and Chou, 2018a) instead of income-based threshold (Cheung and Chou, 2016). However, we have found that the estimates of working poverty range from 1.56% to 24.47% depends on age criteria, weeks and hours worked used to define workers, whether the income had been adjusted to full-time and full-year equivalent as well as the poverty unit (Cheung, Chan and Chou, 2018b). We evaluated four existing measures, including disregarding earnings in Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA) Scheme, statutory minimum wage, and the Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme on their effectiveness and efficacy on working poor alleviation in Hong Kong. Our findings indicate that the efficacy of all three measures are low due to high inclusion error and the minimum wage was the highest in terms of effectiveness among three measures due to its high benefit amount (Cheung, Chan and Chou, 2018c). The results of our simulation show that the universal income tax credit and child benefit have lower exclusion error and could substantially reduce in-work poverty over the means-tested Working Family Allowance Scheme (Cheung, Chan and Chou, 2018d). Moreover, our findings also indicate that the flat-rate child benefits have higher adequacy than slide scales in income tax credit. We conclude that universal benefits with flat rate is a better policy option than the ones with slide scale in alleviation of working poor. As expected, according to the results of our dynamic micro-simulation modelling, the projected expenditure for income tax credit and child benefit was much greater than for existing means-tested benefits, namely CSSA, the Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme and Working Family Allowance. However, due to the low fertility rate and projected reduced labour force in the coming decades, we have found that the income tax credit and child benefits are financially sustainable in the coming decades in term of expected GDP growth (Cheung, Chan and Chou, 2018d). Compared with universal child benefit, the income tax credit receives stronger support from the public based on the public opinion phone survey we conducted (Cheung and Chou, 2018d). The findings may be due to the popular work ethic in Hong Kong.

18401314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18401314.value: Hong Kong Government implemented the means-tested Working Family Allowance Scheme (formerly called the Low-income Working Family Allowance Scheme) in 2016 when our survey was almost completed. Therefore, we are not able to capture the impact of this measure on working poor. Due to the low take-up rate of this scheme, the Government implemented a number of improvement measures (e.g. extending the scheme to cover singletons, introducing a tier with the income limit pitch at 70% of the median monthly household income, adding a new tier of 168 hours a month for the working hour requirement, allowing household members to aggregate working hours, and increasing all rates of allowance) in 1 April 2018. It is timely to examine the impact of these changes to the take-up rate of this scheme and evaluate its efficacy and effectiveness. Moreover, it is also important to investigate how to further improve its efficacy and effectiveness by manipulating these parameters related to the eligibility criteria and the amount of benefits. Future study should be conducted to investigate the impact of these changes in take-up rates of this scheme, too.

18401314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18401314.value: Although in-work poverty is a pressing issue in Hong Kong, our knowledge about the major drives for the working poor and the efficacy, effectiveness as well as financial sustainability of used to reduce in-work poverty remains inadequate. To fill this important research gap, the objectives of this study are to identify the major explanation for in-work poverty in Hong Kong, to evaluate the efficacy and effectiveness of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA) scheme, Work Incentive Transport Subsidy Scheme, and statutory minimum wage on reducing working poor, and to evaluate the efficacy, effectiveness and financial sustainability of three proposed measures including income tax credit, child benefit and one newly introduced policy, namely Working Family Allowance. We conducted a survey of 3,816 households which were randomly selected and detailed data on 8,403 workers at individual, employment-related and household levels were collected through face-to-face interviews. We found that low-earning work and the absence of a second earner living in household are the two major drivers for in-work poverty. Moreover, the efficacy of CSSA is the highest and the effectiveness of the statutory minimum wage is the greatest among the three schemes we evaluated. Policy implications and recommendations were drawn from these results.

18401514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18401514.value: 自2001年英語科教師語文能力評核成立以來的十年：我們能否斷定教師英語標準有所提高？

18401514.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18401514.value: Dr Drave, Neil Dr Falvey, Peter Dr Lockwood, Jane Prof Mak Chan, Barley Shuk-yin Dr Urmston, Alan

18401514.label: Project Objectives
18401514.value: To investigate, quantitatively, perceptions of whether English teachers’ English language standards have improved since the introduction of the LPATE in 2000 To investigate, qualitatively, the perceptions of English panel chairs of the effects of the LPATE policy
rows: To investigate, quantitatively, perceptions of whether English teachers’ English language standards have improved since the introduction of the LPATE in 2000
To investigate, qualitatively, the perceptions of English panel chairs of the effects of the LPATE policy

18401514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18401514.value: The proposed impact study will investigate perceptions of changes in Hong Kong English language teachers’ English language proficiency, given that over a decade has elapsed since the minimum language standards Language Proficiency Assessment for Teachers (English) [LPATE] was introduced in 2000. Given that if a teacher is to deliver a second language via a ‘communicative curriculum’, a teacher’s language proficiency – the ability to function in the second language – is the cornerstone on which the pedagogy rests (Medgyes, 1999). The study will comprise three elements. The first, main element involves two strands. The first strand is a quantitative survey of key stakeholders – school principals; English language department panel heads; teacher educators; long-serving LPATE chief examiners; EDB Classroom Language Assessment examiners; and overseas immersion providers – who will complete a survey contrasting their attitudes towards the language proficiency of English language teachers before the introduction of the LPATE and their more current experiences. The second strand will consist of qualitative semi-structured interviews with a smaller number of key respondents. The data from the first strand will be analysed before the qualitative interviews take place – allowing for key elements of the survey to be mined more deeply with interview participants. The second, main element will involve an analysis of LPATE data from the Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority over the years in order to determine the extent to which levels of proficiency among English language teachers may have changed. The third element will involve an analysis of the impact of LPATE on issues not directly connected to teacher language proficiency. For example, the LPATE has been designed as an instrument for assessing teachers’ language ability. Nonetheless, as reported in language attitude research studies, it inevitably reflects a view of language and the status and positioning of English in Hong Kong. Such information could assist policy makers in future as could information about the need to raise the bar on language proficiency standards for some categories of teachers e.g. heads of departments. The first two elements outlined above, will, it is anticipated, combine to provide a platform upon which to investigate key stakeholders’ views of English language teachers’ English language proficiency both as a post hoc reference point and for future reference. The third element will also attempt to gauge the impact of the introduction of the LPATE on issues not directly connected to the assessment of the language proficiency of teachers. 自2000年至今，英語科教師語文能力評核（以下簡稱“能力評核”）最低語言標準推行已有十年（參見Falvey & Coniam, 2002），因而本項影響研究旨在探究對香港英語科教師語言水準變化所持的看法。該研究的重要性不言而喻，如果教師是在“交際課程”中使用第二語言，教師的語言水準，即使用第二語言進行交際的能力，就成為教學法本身的立足基礎（Medgyes, 1999）。 首先應當指出，無論直接比較有多麼重要，對2000年教師語文能力標準和現今的教師語文能力標準進行直接比較是近乎不可能的。因而，我們關注的是相對間接的比較證據，闡述如下。 本項研究由三個部分組成。第一部分包含量化調查及質化訪談。量化調查主要在主要利害關係者中進行，即：校長、英語科主任、教師培訓師、長期從事能力評核的首席考官、教育局課堂語文評核考官、政府督學及管理人員、海外浸入式專案提供者，當然還包括教師他們自己。這些利害關係者們將獲邀完成一項調查，就能力評核實施前及現在的英語科教師語文水準進行比較。質化訪談主要是對部分重要的受訪者進行半結構式的訪談。定量調查的資料分析將在質化訪談前進行。這樣做主要是為了量化調查的關鍵發現可在受訪者訪談時進一步挖掘。應當指出，該部分並非“釣魚行為”。該部分非常重要，一方面，探究“（語文能力）基準”的需求在多大程度上受到相關專業人士的認同；另一方面，基於利害關係者的意識及看法，探究能力評核啟動至今究竟產生了哪些影響。 第二部分主要對香港考試及評核局提供的13年以來的能力評核資料進行分析，進而判定英語科教師語文水準的變化程度。這將有可能進一步探究起初未能通過能力評核及在哪項測試中未能通過的受試者人數、再次參加能力評核及是否通過的受試者人數以及對整體專案有用的相關統計資料。 第三部分將對能力評核所產生的影響進行分析，儘管這些影響與教師語文水準並無直接關聯，然而這些影響自身非常重要。例如，能力評核已被設計為評估教師語言能力的工具。然而，正如語言態度相關研究表明，能力評估已不可避免的反映了對待語言的看法（即：英語）以及英語在香港的狀況及定位（參見，例如：Appel & Muysken, 1987; Garrett 2010; Garrett, et al. 2005）。相關資訊，例如校長、科主任及教師對英語在香港定位的看法——英語過去作為第二語言的許可權已轉變為外語（Lee & Falvey, forthcoming）以及提高某類教師（例如科主任）的語言能力標準門檻的需求，都能在未來對政策制定者們提供幫助。同樣重要的是要確定能力評核最初開發者的出發點是否被利害關係者們所認同，最初能力評核開發者認為，能力評核英語口語的標準要求不應參照英語本族語者來制定，而應參照受過良好教育的香港英語使用者來制定——這些人的口語在世界各地都可以交流。 綜上所述，本項研究前兩個部分將相互結合，共同探究利害關係者們對英語科教師語文水準所持的看法，從而對過去進行總結，為將來提供參考。第三部分則嘗試探究啟用能力評核對教師語文水準評估所產生間接影響的相關議題。

18401514.label: Realisation of objectives
18401514.value: With the completion of both the quantitative and qualitative studies, the two objectives of the whole research projects were achieved. This section was divided into two subsections, respectively elaborated on how each research objective was addressed. Objective 1: Regarding the first objective, the questionnaire data were collected from principals, English language panel chairs and English language teachers, across different primary schools and secondary schools in Hong Kong. 236 complete responses were collected. The data analysis shows that the questionnaire was reliable and well-constructed; the teacher-to-panel chair-to-principal ratio in the sample is not too far off the actual ratio in Hong Kong schools. The questionnaire data demonstrate a feeling of approval for the LPATE, its assessment levels and its assessment criteria. There was an agreement over the following perspectives: English language standards are acceptable; a minimum standard is necessary; content teachers should face minimum standards; and panel heads should achieve a Level 4. The responses on the attitude items were very supportive of the HKSAR government’s decision to go ahead with the language benchmarking/LPATE initiative almost two decades ago. Participants’ attitudes towards the LPATE were affected by a range of factors, including: levels of schools (primary or secondary), ability band (Band 1, 2 or 3 schools), teaching experience, number of times the LPATE was taken and highest scores attained. Participants were more likely to agree that the LPATE had positive impact and necessary when they had taken the LPATE more than one time, when they had longer teaching experience, and when they had obtained a higher mark in the LPATE. To sum up, the quantitative data analysis developed an understanding of how participants perceived the impact of the LPATE and factors affecting their perceptions. Objective 2 Regarding the second objective, interview data were collected from school principals, English panel chairs and experienced English teachers. Altogether 24 interviews were conducted, with four interviews from principals/vice-principals, 15 interviews from English panel chairs, four interviews from local English teachers and one from a NET teacher. The qualitative data collected rich responses and drew a clear connection between the LPATE and English language teaching as a profession. The LPATE was considered to have had an impact on teachers’ language proficiency, language knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge. As the current study took a retrospective perspective, it developed an understanding of the different impacts of the LPATE when it was first introduced and in the current era. The study also identified different degrees of relevancy of the LPATE in the context of both English panel chairs and English language teachers. Apart from its positive impacts, the study also identified the negative impacts of the LPATE. The negative impacts included: the LPATE raised the issue of distrust; and the LPATE not being relevant in the current time. The quality of the LPATE itself was also criticized. On the whole, the second objective was achieved through providing insights into how the LPATE impact the language teaching profession and English teacher language standards in Hong Kong.

18401514.label: Major findings and research outcome
18401514.value: The quantitative data show that there was agreement over the following perspectives: that English language standards are acceptable; that a minimum standard is necessary; that content teachers should face minimum standards; and that panel heads should achieve Level 4. Participants’ attitudes towards the LPATE were affected by: level of school, ability band, teaching experience, number of times LPATE had been taken and highest scores attained. Participants were more likely to agree that the LPATE had a positive impact and was necessary when they had taken the LPATE more than once; when they had longer teaching experience; and when had obtained a higher mark in the LPATE. The introduction of the LPATE brought home the message that English language teaching is a profession that requires language proficiency, subject-matter knowledge and pedagogical skills. Participants believed that English language teachers needed to have sufficient language proficiency and that the LPATE, to an extent, guaranteed English language teacher standards. There were variations in the views regarding whether English language teachers and panel chairs need to take the LPATE. As most English language teachers now become qualified through taking relevant degree courses, the LPATE is considered to be a good indicator but not a compulsory requirement in language teacher recruitment. In this regard, the LPATE was considered to be more relevant to potential panel chairs. The LPATE ensures that heads of department are capable, reliable and professional – so that they can be a role model to lead the department. From a retrospective perspective, the changes caused by the LPATE were generally positive. There has been an improvement in the English language standards, language knowledge and pedagogical skills of English teachers generally. One obvious change is that English teachers are now better trained – a positive response to the HKSAR Government’s initiative to introduce the LPATE. However, the LPATE has been considered to have become somewhat less relevant, as most English teachers are better trained and consequently exempt. The introduction of the LPATE also gave rise to some challenges: test quality, and the issue of trust and distrust. To sum up, the current study supports the contention that the LPATE has generally had a positive impact on English language teacher standards and reinforces the notion that English language teaching is a profession.

18401514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18401514.value: The first issue worth further researching and considering is that how the LPATE can be improved in its quality and focus, to make it more beneficial to the development of language teacher professionalism in Hong Kong. The second aspect for potential research is to study subject teachers’ perceptions of language standards in EMI schools, to explore their perceptions of language standards and how language standards of subject teachers in EMI schools can be ensured.

18401514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18401514.value: The current research project contributes to the understanding of the impact of a language proficiency assessment for English teachers (i.e. the LPATE test) on English teachers’ language standards. The findings support the notion that English teachers’ language proficiency is important for English language teaching. The LPATE guaranteed English language teacher standards by keeping unqualified teachers away from teaching. More importantly, the LPATE raised teachers’ awareness of the notion that not everyone who speaks good English can become an English teacher; rather, English language teaching is a profession that requires language proficiency, subject-matter knowledge and pedagogical skills. The LPATE is also considered to make sure English panel chairs have sufficient language proficiency and expertise to lead the panel. The impact of the LPATE has nonetheless changed over time. Whereas the LPATE played an important role in guaranteeing teachers’ language standards a decade ago, it now plays a somewhat less important role as most English language teachers become qualified through taking degree courses. Hence, it is worth studying how the LPATE can be improved in its quality and focus, to make it more beneficial to the development of language teacher professionalism in Hong Kong.

18402014.label: Project Objectives
18402014.value: 追尋香港兒童雜誌出版的源頭，探討上海、香港及東南亞兒童雜誌的發展與聯繫，肯定香港兒童雜誌五十年代以還在出版史的意義和地位。 以兒童為研究主體，發掘他們的眼光、聲音、經驗，藉以探討兒童成長期中的生存環境與情感世界，重新確立兒童的主體性與能動性。 將兒童或童年經驗納入歷史的大景觀，檢視兒童與社會文化的互動關係。 分析兒童雜誌的編寫取向，以至社會所持的兒童及童年概念，透過訪談，讓過往的小讀者回憶當日境況，探討兒童雜誌對小讀者人生價值取向的啟發與影響。

18402014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18402014.value: 上海，是兒童雜誌的發祥地，在清末即有《蒙學報》和《童子世界》的創辦。後因中日戰爭與四十年代末的政局鉅變，上海的出版事業經歷曲折，而香港則憑藉政治、地理及先進的印刷技術等優勢，取代而為造貨出版，以及內地轉運，並向海外發展的基地。五十年代初，《世界兒童》、《小朋友》及《兒童樂園》在香港出版，並先後湧入南洋各地。 本計劃從兒童視點切入，以上述三本兒童雜誌為研究對象，藉著原始材料的研究，期以深入探討以下幾項：一、從中國大陸、香港及東南亞的政治社會背景、出版、刊物編寫路向等角度切入，彰顯香港五十年代後兒童雜誌的印刷與出版地位，釐清其流通與版圖發展。二、借助成人所創作的兒童作品，探討作品及兒童雜誌中所表現的兒童本位，期以考察成人所理解的兒童及童年，以及當時社會文化對兒童觀念的生成。三、通過爬梳雜誌中所記載的兒童創作，重新發現過往被忽略的兒童聲音和經驗，藉以把他們回歸於歷史架構之中，展示一幅豐富而立體的兒童畫卷。

18402014.label: Realisation of objectives
18402014.value: 本人細讀《世界兒童》、《兒童樂園》及《小朋友》三份兒童雜誌的原始資料後分類建檔，並透過文本細讀，從內容、表達兩者探討他們的作品，以了解：一、雜誌的編寫取向，從而勾勒其發展面貌，追尋香港兒童雜誌出版的源頭與軌跡；二、把兒童作品納入歷史的大景觀中分析，檢視他們與歷史、文化的互動關係，了解兒童讀者的生存環境與情感世界，突顯他們的主體性與能動性。 三份兒童雜誌中，以《世界兒童》與《小朋友》的兒童聲音最為豐富，無論是南洋兒童，抑或香港讀者，都在雜誌中表達了自己的聲音，其中有嚴肅的話題，也有充滿童趣的言論。此外，從已有文獻及相關人物的訪談，追認了兩本兒童雜誌的編者：其一、曾為《兒童樂園》創刊團隊之一的張一渠，他是上海「兒童書局」的創辦人，對上海與香港兒童出版業的努力與貢獻不容忽視；其二，匿名編輯《小朋友》的鷗外鷗，他的詩論與詩教是兒童雜誌中最具文學性的。 在是次的研究計劃中，本人借助口述史的研究方法，與三本雜誌的參與者深入訪談，以補足文獻無法提供的史料，並探討兒童雜誌對讀者的啟發與影響。早在2006年，本人已與《兒童樂園》的張浚華、羅冠樵及李成法作多次非正式訪談。到了2010年，本人遠赴三藩市與新加坡，與三本雜誌的相關人士進行了一連串訪談。不過，雜誌創刊於上世紀五十年代，而訪談人物如閻起白、陳濯生、王建武、戚鈞傑及奚會暲都是八、九十歲的老人，訪談所得資料各有說法，難以就有限文獻印證。以陳濯生所憶，《兒童樂園》參與《今日美國》的徵稿，在獲選後得一年份資助為例，在翻查《今日美國》後，仍未能找到相關徵稿資訊。 此外，主編《小朋友》的鷗外鷗於1995年在美病逝，亦無從訪談。本人嘗試再次訪問與鷗外鷗稔熟的黃慶雲，期以補遺鷗外鷗主編《小朋友》時的相關資料，惜黃慶雲年近百歲，身體欠佳，再無法訪談。至於《世界兒童》的訪談工作，本人曾幾度訪問藏書家、《世界兒童》前員工楊善才，但他在1950年代中期才加入世界出版社，並主職行銷業務，對創刊及編務了解不多。再者，本人亦訪問了《世界兒童》的當年讀者，今知名馬華兒童文學家年紅、梁志慶及愛薇，其中以愛薇較多地談及投稿《世界兒童》的經歷。馬漢，當年《世界兒童》的讀者，常投稿雜誌，也在計劃訪問前去世。 本計劃所列的四個研究目標，前三項的目標已達成，而第四項的訪問亦有進行，但限於客觀條件，部份當事人或在計劃訪談前經已離世，或因年事已高，未便訪談。不過，本人幸得楊善才多次捐贈兒童雜誌，並獲周星衢基金會安排，旁聽星洲出版人的訪談，都有利計劃的進行。就蒐集的資料，本人參加了四次研討會，就與會者的交流再行修訂原稿，共撰寫四篇論文，其中一篇已刊於〈《文學山水——第五屆世界華文旅遊文學國際學術研討會文集》（2017），其他三篇亦已物色期刊予以投稿。此外，獲是次研究資助前，本人已就《小朋友》進行先導計劃，論文〈一道流動的風景：《小朋友》的承傳與流播〉刊於《文化生態之旅——第四屆世界華文旅遊文學國際學術研討會文集》。

18402014.label: Major findings and research outcome
18402014.value: 本計劃以《世界兒童》、《兒童樂園》及《小朋友》為探討對象，就他們在出版發展、社會現狀、歷史文化、兒童文學、兒童教育等相關課題上，有以下成果： 1. 追尋了三份雜誌的出版歷程，以勾勒他們在上海、香港及東南亞兒童雜誌的出版發展與聯繫，肯定他們在兒童出版史上的意義和地位。 2. 追尋了三份兒童雜誌的主編誰屬，並透過編者、作者及兒童讀者的作品，了解他們的編輯和創作的方向。 3. 發掘《世界兒童》與《小朋友》的兒童聲音，尋繹他們與編者的交流與互動，以至對社會、歷史及文化的反響，一方面探討雜誌對他們的啟發與影響，另一方面則了解兒童作為雜誌持份者的主體性與能動性，為雜誌提供編輯的寶貴意見。 4. 藉著兒童的視覺與聲音考察原始文本，打破學界過往視兒童為「受」者的偏見，重新審視在兒童、兒童文學及兒童雜誌方面的研究。此外，刷新學界對兒童與童年的既有概念，使在社會、文化、歷史、文學、創作及教育等方面，得到更確切的理解、演繹及詮釋。

18402014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18402014.value: 三本兒童雜誌歷史悠久，內容豐富，除本計劃的研究目標外，有待發掘的空間仍多，而兒童圖畫書（picture book）是最值得開拓的。華文兒童書刊起步較遲，多取經外國經典，今從事圖畫書研究者，都以台灣為華文譯介圖畫書的始祖，但《兒童樂園》早在1960年代已是推介圖畫書的先鋒，尤以張浚華的貢獻最大。2011年，本人就她譯介的兒童圖畫書發表論文，但當中仍待鈎沉者眾。朝著這個方向探索，華文世界譯介圖畫書的發展史將要重寫。

18402014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18402014.value: 本計劃以《世界兒童》、《兒童樂園》及《小朋友》為研究對象，探討他們的發展與其在出版史上的地位。此外，以兒童為主體，發掘他們的聲音，藉以探討成長中兒童的生存環境與情感世界；再把兒童納入歷史的大觀景，檢視他們與成人、歷史文化的互動關係，為兒童史補白。最後，本計劃藉著訪談，追尋刊物的出版過程，以及編者與讀者之間的交流，探索兒童雜誌對小讀者價值取向的啟發與影響，為早期香港兒童雜誌史、香港兒童文學史補白。

18402514.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18402514.value: 『既非移民, 亦非公民』: 香港少數族裔學生在跨國族環境中的公民價值觀建立

18402514.label: Project Objectives
18402514.value: Assess the citizenship values of a sample of ethnic minority students in Hong Kong, compare them with a sample of Chinese students drawn from ICCS 2009 and relate the results to Hong Kong’s civic regime as referred to in Objective 1.
rows: Assess the citizenship values of a sample of ethnic minority students in Hong Kong, compare them with a sample of Chinese students drawn from ICCS 2009 and relate the results to Hong Kong’s civic regime as referred to in Objective 1.

18402514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18402514.value: This proposal focuses on “the limits of citizenship” (Soysal, 1994) in a transnational context. It draws on research developed from the “new institutionalism” by adopting a theoretical framework that views institutions as major influences on attitudes. Social identity theory is also be used to acknowledge the agency of individuals in responding to the institutional contexts in which they are embedded. The focus of the research is Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students where previously the emphasis has been on micro issues of educational provision. The current proposal seeks to locate ethnic minority students in a broader macro social and institutional context. It will assess students’ responses to that context in terms of their attitudes to citizenship as well as their social identities. This is a trajectory approach: from macro to micro, from structure to agency. It seeks to understand how ethnic minority students are influenced by and in turn influence the environment in which they live and how this dialectic may influence their life chances. Since 1 July 1997, the macro context in Hong Kong has been dominated by the development of closer ties between the city and the political and economic infrastructure of China. All former British subjects of Chinese descent in Hong Kong automatically became Chinese citizens (White, 1987). Current new arrivals from China intending to take up residence in Hong Kong are referred to as “immigrants.” Yet at the time of the handover, there were other than people of Chinese descent in Hong Kong and their status was left to the British to determine (Sui & Ku, 2009). These non-Chinese groups remain invisible – neither citizens nor immigrants. Institutional theory has argued that such a context must influence the attitudes of non-citizens in much the same way as political culture exerts influences through processes of political socialization (Weldon, 2006). The institutional contexts influencing ethnic minority students and their responses to them are the subject of this proposal. With a mixed methods design, this research will use document analysis, interviews and surveys to study ethnic minority students’ attitudes to citizenship. It will first identify and analyze the key institutions influencing citizenship formation. A survey of ethnic minority students’ citizenship attitudes will show how students respond within this context. Finally, interviews will be conducted with students to obtain an understanding of how their social identity responds to this context and whether it reinforces or resists the institutional arrangements for citizenship. 本計劃旨在將Soysal 1994年的「公民身份的限制」(the limits of citizenship) 論說置於一個跨國族環境進行研究；同時取材新制度論(new institutionalism)之理論框架，認為各項社會制度對個人態度取向極具影響。社會身份認同亦是另一採用之論述：個別主體有能力去回應其置身之制度環境。本計劃研究對象為香港少數族裔學生，過往其他研究多集中於他們身上的微觀事務如教育機會提供；而本計劃則探討其他宏觀層面譬如社會及制度環境，以學生公民身份態度和社會身份認同為他們對社會制度環境回應之測量。透過從微觀層面到宏觀層面、並由社會架構到主體動力的軌跡追尋；以了解少數族裔學生受週遭環境的影響，而隨他們之反應又如何塑造環境，並探求這種互動將如何影響他們的生涯機遇。自1997年7月1日起香港的宏觀環境即主要受制於其作為一個城市與中國政治經濟架構之緊密關係所牽引；所有前英屬華裔居民於當天即自動歸屬作中國公民 (White 1987)，目前從中國內地新遷入香港的居民皆被視為「移民」。然而主權移交時在港的非華裔居民之身份歸屬則由英國方面決定 (Sui & Ku 2009)，這些非華裔族群一直彷如被視而不見－ 既非移民, 亦非公民。制度論者認為身處於這般環境下，非公民的公民態度所受之影響將一如政治文化於政治社教化過程之影響 (Weldon 2006)。故此社會制度環境對少數族裔學生之影響並他們對社會制度之反應是本研究之主旨。透過文獻分析、訪談、調查等不同方法去研究少數族裔學生的公民身份態度。研究將先找出和分析對公民身份構成具影響之主要社會制度，並對少數族裔學生進行調查他們的公民身份態度，從中展現出他們對制度環境的回應。及後會透過訪談他們以求了其社會身份認同如何對應此間制度環境，究竟是在強化抑或抗衡現時對其公民身份的各種制度安排。

18402514.label: Realisation of objectives
18402514.value: 1. Explain the change to Objective 2: Objective 2 was revised in response to the budget cut. We have therefore relied on existing data in the ICCS 2009 data base. Such data provides a baseline measure for comparison with the civic values of ethnic minority students. 2. Objective 1 Identify and analyze the main elements of Hong Kong's civic regime as represented in the macro social and institutional environment and assess their potential to influence the civic life of citizens and non-citizens. Hong Kong’s civic regime is dominated by bureaucratic structures from multiple government agencies: Immigration, Education, Social Welfare, Security and Constitutional Affairs are chief among these. Immigration/Constitutional Affairs Ethnic minorities can be designated a “permanent resident” but usually not as “ Chinese citizen”. Chinese citizenship was automatically bestowed on all Chinese people after 1997 but not on ethnic minorities. They were not offered British citizenship, even though prior to 1997 they had been British subjects. As a result they had to revert to the citizenship of their historic families, even if they had been in Hong Kong for generations. Education While schools are open to ethnic minorities, including the children of asylum seekers, research is clear that schooling processes do not always meet the ends of ethnic minority students. Language issues are central with many ethnic minority students having to sit through lessons in a language they do not understand. The alternative is for ethnic minority students to be clustered together in schools where there are very few Chinese students. Neither of these solutions is satisfactory and in many cases is oppressive. Social Welfare Many, although by no means all, ethnic minorities live on the poverty line. Pakistani families are amongst the poorest groups in the community therefore they need to interact extensively with the Social Welfare Bureau. This is also true for asylum seekers, whose lives are dominated by social welfare handouts for which there are many bureaucratic barriers. These agencies act together to influence the lives of a large majority of ethnic minorities in Hong Kong. At the same time processes of institutional racism in the community, limited labour market opportunities (largely because of language), limited access to higher education and government discourses focusing on integration and the need to speak Cantonese also pressurise many ethnic minorities who have chosen to make their lives in Hong Kong. Thus the civic regime consists of both formal and informal strands that interact on a daily basis to influence the lives of Hong Kong’s ethnic minorities. Objective 2 Assess the citizenship values of a sample of ethnic minority students in Hong Kong, compare them with those of a sample of Chinese students and relate the results to Hong Kong’s civic regime as referred to in Objective 1. Work has been done and continued as part of a PhD student’s project that involves a survey of ethnic minority students citizenship values with a particular emphasis on the use of digital technology as a form of civic participation. This focus has been adopted in the light of Hong Kong’s recent civic disturbances where a great deal of civic action was related to the use of social media. It is also related to a great deal of work that has been done in the United States on the use of social media as a new form of democratic participation. Objective 3 Explore the social identities of a sample of ethnic minority students to understand how their group membership and personal identity have responded to Hong Kong's civic regime and influenced attitudes to citizenship This objective called to our attention to the inappropriateness of referring to “ethnic minorities” as though they were a homogeneous group. They are not. This was clearly revealed to us as we interviewed young ethnic minorities and found some similarities across different national groups but found more differences. Thus we focused our research not so much on a generic category of citizen but on sub-groups: Filipino, Pakistani, Indian, Nepalese. These sub-groupings are reflected in our publications. We found young Filipinos to be resilient, caring little about their national citizenship but eager to be considered as “Hong Kong people”. Pakistani youth, on the other hand, had a much stronger connection to their national citizenship linked to their religion and heritage (even if they had been born in Hong Kong). Indian youth did not regard their national citizenship as overly important, underwent many changes in Hong Kong and were critical of their heritage nation. Work on Nepalese youth is continuing. Apart from the Pakistani students, citizenship was not a strong factor in the way these young people saw their lives; but their identity as “Hongkongers” was. This attachment was not to China (we explicitly explored this issue), it was to the city of Hong Kong. In addition, it was a largely instrumental attachment: Hong Kong was seen as a good place to make a living, to succeed and to make a career. Given that Pakistani youth stood out in this group, a PhD student is now exploring in greater depth related acculturation issues. His thesis will be submitted by the end of 2019 and will provide considerable insights to the Pakistani case. Objective 4 Draw conclusions about the relationship between different levels of the environment influencing ethnic minority students in Hong Kong and assess the implications for policy making and theory building. Neo-institutional theory often seems to suggest that institutions exert their effect in such a way that human agency is not always possible. This study suggested otherwise. Deprived of local citizenship in Hong Kong and forced to rely on what might be called ‘family’ or ‘heritage’ citizenship, all of our interviewees showed how they navigated this process with some ease. Citizenship was merely a passport to most of these young people. Identify, on the other hand, was where they lived, who they talked with and what they could achieve. Yet a number of issues within this framework require comment. Racism Many, although by no means all, of our interviewees had experienced racism in Hong Kong. It may have been incidental (muttered comments as a group of Chinese people walked by) or explicit (name calling in public). Yet what became clear was that those who could speak Cantonese were much less likely to experience any racism at all. The salience of language, therefore is important and needs to be seen not so much as a technical requirement (as indicated by government discourse) but as a key to social interaction and indeed cohesion. There is also a link (as yet unexplored in the literature) between language and labour market entry. Theoretically, more work is needed on these links especially taking into consideration the cultural context and the way multiculturalism is viewed in Asian contexts. Access to higher education While participation statistics are clear on lack of access we heard many stories about how the groups we talked to gained access (often connected with second language proficiency) as well as the importance of such education to social mobility for these students. This is an important area for future research.

18402514.label: Major findings and research outcome
18402514.value: ‘Family’ or ‘heritage’ citizenship, as required by Hong Kong is not important for many ethnic minority groups, but this statement cannot be generalized. For Pakistani youth, their heritage citizenship is much more important, especially linked to religion. This is an important finding – nuanced research in this area requires a focus on sub-groups of ethnic minorities rather than random groups of ethnic minorities. For example, Filipinos who can speak Cantonese have a different view of their identities as those who do not. Thus this project has shown that overgeneralization needs to be avoided because there is an individuality about ethnic minorities that makes such generalization highly questionable. Identity in this project is a much more salient social construct that citizenship. For the most part the latter is viewed instrumentally – it is basically a passport. Rights, values, attachment, belonging are associated with identity. Many of our participants could distinguish between attachment to Hong Kong, attachment to China and attachment to their heritage countries. For the most part, their identities were constructed by their attachment to Hong Kong, even though for Pakistani youth there was a strong pull from their heritage citizenship. For all of them, ‘Hong Kong was a good place to live’ even for the Pakistani students. Theoretically, this project has suggested that traditional labels of disadvantage cannot be applied to Hong Kong’s ethnic minorities. There are significant differences between groups (Indian youth come largely from middle class families while Pakistani youth come from families that on average are below the poverty level). This has often meant that Indian youth have been educated in private schools while Pakistani youth have had to endure Chinese speaking schools. Filipino youth have taken advantage of local education but in English language schools. These diverse experiences create different environments and influences that affect young people in different ways. It is the diversity of experiences that is highlighted in our outcomes which means we need to consider individual experience. Methodologically, the project has shown the need to explore not just ‘themes’ as they emerge from the data. In addition, the exceptions to the themes also need to be identified. Thematic analysis can be overly reductionist. We found that going back to consider individuals who do not fit this analysis can expand meaning in the data. The work of Sara Lightfoot Lawrence and Elliot Eisner have helped us consider data in more holistic ways.

18402514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18402514.value: The work of our PhD students pursuing two different strands of this research is instructive for important follow up work. 1. Comparative Relationships between Civic Identity, Citizenship Engagement and Online Participation of Hong Kong Ethnic Minority Students (this project was reported under Objective 2 above). This project involved 5 schools and 748 students. Preliminary results suggest that ethnic minority students score higher on measures of online participation than local students.Yet this participation seems to be limited to their own cultural group. Local students score higher on actual civic engagement and see this as part of their ability to influence civic change. This suggests that ethnic minority students are not engaging in the broader community perhaps because they have little concern for it. This issue is being followed up with focus group interviews. 2.Acculturation among Pakistani Students in Hong Kong This project has completed data collection and is being written up. It has the potential to provide insights into the way Pakistani families nurture their children and perhaps indicate if this is linked to the strong attachments many Pakistani youth feel for their heritage. Preliminary results suggest that acculturation theory as currently understood may not account for the dynamics of local Pakistani families.

18402514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18402514.value: Hong Kong’s ethnic minorities are a little recognized group in a dominate Chinese society. Yet “ethnic minorities” is better seen as a census label rather than a social group. Our project has identified the distinctiveness of different subgroups of ethnic minorities in Hong Kong, their strong attachment to the city and its values and a common regard for Hong Kong as a good place to live. This does not mean that ethnic minorities have no regard for their heritage or family backgrounds and cultures. For some, such as Pakistanis, this is stronger than for others. Overall, however, ethnic minorities see themselves as part of Hong Kong and value the opportunities it provides. At the same time a key finding shows that Hong Kong society has a responsibility to address issues such as institutional racism, low levels of access to high education and to the labour market. Our study showed that strong and resilient ethnic minority youth were often able to overcome these barriers, but this was not always the case. Language is a key issue in this regard and without downplaying the significance of heritage languages, the importance of language proficiency in the local language cannot be over-estimated.

18403314.label: Project Objectives
18403314.value: To investigate the distribution patterns of leadership practices in curricular and instructional decision-making processes that occur in Hong Kong primary schools and curriculum teams, and to examine how such patterns affect the team performance; To empirically investigate the mediating effects of socio-cultural artifacts that facilitate and/or constrain leadership practices among teachers in curriculum teams; and To provide an empirical foundation for the development of a theoretical model of distributed leadership practices in Hong Kong primary schools that will contribute to the international studies and to the development of curriculum leadership practices in schools.

To provide an empirical foundation for the development of a theoretical model of distributed leadership practices in Hong Kong primary schools that will contribute to the international studies and to the development of curriculum leadership practices in schools.

18403314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18403314.value: 香港小學課程小組作為分散課程領導機制的研究 這個兩年研究計畫應用混合的研究方法探討香港小學老師課程領導的現狀。這個研究的構想是源自當代世界課程理論對學校課程發展的研究，是研究老師課程領導的發展模式的一個組成部分。在這個領域的核心學者包括史必霖（Spillane），李活（Leithwood），葛隆(Gronn),和 何立希（Harris）都認為，分散課程領導是過去十五年，世界教育改革的重要現象，並指出有效的學校分散課程領導模組還沒有驗證和建立。 在九十年代推行校本管理之後， 亞洲有越來越多的教育家支持學校分散領導的實踐。這種改革現象也在香港出現。 這反映了國際上公認的一種看法，認為有效持久的學校改革必須在老師當中廣泛推行課程領導。 本研究計畫建基於香港學者在這方面的實證研究，他們指出，老師課程領導一般在課程發展小組出現。他們的研究進一步指出，在小組裡的文化因素和社群環境都直接或間接影響老師課程領導的散播和出現。本研究計畫將集中探究老師課程領導在香港小學課程發展小組的散播和出現模式。同時還將探討文化因素和社群環境如何控制和調適分散課程領導在課程發展小組的散播和出現。 在第一年，每個小學裡的中文，英文和數學課的課程小組都要填寫問卷，以找出每個學校和小組的領導模式，和不同的模式如何影響小組表現。第二年的研究将抽出六個代表不同分散課程領導模式的課程小組，進行深度的調查。主要的研究方法包括開會錄影，小組訪談，追蹤觀察等。每組開會的談話都進行話語分析，找出課程領導的散播和出現的特點。量和質的數據和資料會用來建立學校和課程發展小組的分散課程領導理論 （Distributed Curriculum Leadership）和實踐的基礎。

18403314.label: Realisation of objectives
18403314.value: Objective 1: The survey data has shown various patterns of distribution in terms of leadership practices among the schools in the investigation. The relationship between patterns and team performance has been established in the survey as well; Objective 2: Field studies were conducted in 3 schools. The preliminary findings are established. Yet, a paper on the basis of the field studies is still to be finalized; Objective 3: The publication of the book in 2017 by London Routledge is well received. It has shown directions and patterns of curriculum leadership practices that HK can contribute to international discussions about the topic.

18403314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18403314.value: The research project has based on an international concern about decentralization of curriculum decision making and leadership practices in Western contexts. The findings point to the emergence of various distribution patterns among primary schools in HK. These patterns have implications on professional development of teachers and the ethos of the school. Though distribution among teachers is expected, it is inconclusive to claim that one pattern of distribution is necessarily preferred than the other. Various patterns of distribution have their functions in various stages of school development and school management teams must be constantly monitoring the professional development of the schools and plan accordingly. The publications do contribute to international scholarship in the discussion of leadership practices and school improvement.

18403414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18403414.value: 粵劇創意之本質：藝術家、鑑賞家和初學者的視角及其相互關係

18403414.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18403414.value: Prof Leong, Samuel Prof Yu, Siu Wah

18403414.label: Project Objectives
18403414.value: To examine and identify musical creativity in selected repertoires of Cantonese opera performed by eminent artists in the 20th century; To investigate and identify the socio-cultural factors affecting the changes in perception of artistic creativity; and To investigate the possible different perceptions and expectations among professional Cantonese opera artists, connoisseurs and beginners regarding artistic creativity in Cantonese opera.
rows: To examine and identify musical creativity in selected repertoires of Cantonese opera performed by eminent artists in the 20th century;
To investigate and identify the socio-cultural factors affecting the changes in perception of artistic creativity; and
To investigate the possible different perceptions and expectations among professional Cantonese opera artists, connoisseurs and beginners regarding artistic creativity in Cantonese opera.

18403414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18403414.value: Traditionally, Cantonese opera artists strived to develop individual unique artistic style. Since the mid-20th Century, various artists have successfully established their own personal style recognized by the audience. Nowadays there is anecdotal evidence that some practicing artists are hesitant in developing their own style but are imitating the performance styles of established virtuosi. In what ways the artists’ conceptions of creativity have changed over time and why today’s audience seem to have accepted or even come to appreciate this shift have not been investigated. While creativity is regarded as one of the most important generic competences in the West, the notion of creativity in relation to oriental traditional arts, such as Cantonese opera has been a neglected research area. This proposed research project will be significant in addressing three critical issues that impact on the future development of Cantonese opera: (1) the nature of creativity demonstrated by eminent artists in the 20th century; (2) the extent to which the conceptions of creativity in Cantonese opera have changed from the perspectives of practicing artists and learners; (3) how artistic creativity can be re-valued by the profession and audience. The study will be undertaken in three phases. Phase 1 involves a musical analysis of selected audio-video recordings by different artists with a focus of similarity and differences in personal interpretation. Through an ethnographic study at two local Cantonese opera institutions, Phase 2 aims to investigate how the socio-cultural contexts in Hong Kong affect the development of Cantonese opera. Through observation of classes and interviews with stakeholders, an updated understanding can be obtained. Phase 3 aims to solicit the perspectives of current practicing artists, connoisseurs and beginners on their views of creativity in Cantonese opera. A mixed method with both qualitative and quantitative tools will be employed, including a questionnaire survey of the groups, and in-depth interviews with voluntary respondents. This study will document and provide evidence to account for the development of artistic creativity in Cantonese opera. It will reveal the particular characteristics of creativity in the genre and the extent to which conceptions of creativity held by both artists and patrons are influenced by socio-cultural contexts. The findings will enrich the current understanding of Chinese creativity as applied to Cantonese opera, and serve as a useful reference for developing and implementing programmes for general education and training of future artists, as well as stimulating current artists in the pursuit of creativity. 傳統上，香港粵劇藝術家致力發展個人獨特的藝術風格。自20世紀中期，多位粵劇名伶成功建立了個人風格，受到觀眾的認同。今天，部份藝術家似乎不在意發展自己的風格，卻透過錄音和錄影模仿以往名伶的演出，期望觀眾的認同。藝術家對創意的觀念似乎隨時間而變化，今天的觀眾似乎已經接受甚或體會到這種轉變，然而並沒有學者研究這個現象。創意在西方是一個最受重視的共通能力，但是在東方傳統藝術中，包括粵劇，創意是一個被忽視的研究領域。 本研究項目將著力解決三個關鍵問題，期望對粵劇未來發展有正面的影響：（1）調查和分析由20世紀名伶所展示的藝術創意; （2）面對粵劇的創意觀念，藝術家和學生的視角如何改變？; （3）粵劇藝術的創意如何可以被專業演員和觀眾重新估值？這項研究將開展三個階段。第一階段分析由不同名伶演出的錄製音樂，分析集中在個別名伶詮釋的相似和差異。第二階段利用民族志方法觀察兩間粵劇教育機構並訪談持份者，研究社會文化背景如何影響香港的粵劇的發展。第三階段的目標是調查專業藝術家、鑑賞家和初學者對粵劇創意的觀點。研究方法混合定性和定量工具，包括問卷調查和深入與志願受訪者訪談。 本研究將記錄並提供證據來解釋粵劇創意的發展。它將揭示粵劇創意的具體特點，和在何種程度上藝術家和觀眾的創意觀念受到社會文化背景所影響。研究結果將豐富目前中國人對粵劇創意的理解，並有助制定和實施一個有效的通識教育課程供未來的藝術家參考，以及刺激當代藝術家以追求藝術創意。

18403414.label: Realisation of objectives
18403414.value: For Objective 1, a music analysis of 6 excerpts sung by 3 artists were implemented, with a thorough literature review on theories of creativity as well as historical and socio-cultural contexts of Cantonese opera in Hong Kong during early 20th Century. Musical creativity of those selected artists was discussed in the contexts of Hong Kong with theoretical framework on creativity. For Objective 2, a total of 14 Cantonese opera artists (including singers and accompanists) were interviewed in a semi-structured format. The interview questions aim to investigate their experience about creativity and personal innovations during learning process and professional practices, their understanding about Cantonese opera artists’ imitation and learning, and their opinion towards improving the current status of Cantonese opera. The interview questions were derived from literature, with a focus on imitation, adaption, and self-recognition, and how personal style can be recognized by the peers and the audience. For Objective 3, a questionnaire survey was implemented. Three groups of respondents were categorized, namely, artists, connoisseurs, and beginners. Artists refer to those professional actors and actresses as well as music accompanists who were performing for their living. Connoisseurs refer to experienced audiences who are knowledgeable frequent attendants of Cantonese opera performances. They were recruited from fans clubs of Cantonese opera. Beginners refer to those university students who have taken a course of Cantonese opera as General Education. They are the future audiences if they find Cantonese opera creative and interesting. Based on literature, a questionnaire was designed with 20 semantic-differential-scale questions in six categories: 1. Value: The value system of the respondents towards creativity in Cantonese opera performances 2. Possibility: Respondents’ belief on the possibility of developing personal styles by current artists 3. Audience expectation: Whether the audience expect the artists to develop their personal style 4. Perception towards current artists: How the respondents perceive the current artists in develop their personal style 5. Artist-audience interaction: Perception of how audience perceive artists’ development of personal style 6. Environment: Whether the environment facilitate the development of personal style Before formal implementation, the questionnaire was piloted by 5 university students, 2 connoisseurs, and 1 artist to see if they could understand the questions. Minor revision of wording of the questionnaire was done. As a result, a total of 33 artists, 166 Connoisseurs, and 331 beginners responded to the questionnaire. An internal reliability test was implemented to check the reliability of the designed questionnaire. One-way ANOVA was used to measure if there are significant differences among the perceptions of the three groups of respondents.

18403414.label: Major findings and research outcome
18403414.value: The first part of this study suggests that creation of personal styles in Cantonese operatic singing depends on different factors including the social environment, motivation of artists, and their knowledge and skills in Cantonese operatic singing, as well as the extent to which artists can develop their artistry by demonstrating originality and appropriateness in order to deviate from both tradition and current trends. The second study aims to investigate the reason of hindering artists’ establishment of personal style through 14 semi-structured interviews. A 3-stage model of developing personal style as musical creativity is proposed: Stage 1: Imitation as prerequisite Stage 2: Adaption and self-recognition Stage 3: Popularity and sustainability of a new personal style There are several socio-cultural factors which have been changing since the 1930s, which have hindered the development of personal style. These include: 1. Cantonese opera is not a main-stream art form and entertainment; 2. Long term co-operation between artists and musicians is missing; 3. Modern artists are more utilitarian with a short-sighted perspective; 4. Musical creativity is not the focus of the artists; rather, they would focus on the staging, special effects and costumes etc. 5. Audiences have lowered their expectations while most of them are in lack of knowledge about Cantonese opera; and 6. The conservatory has become the main venue of nurturing professional artists; graduates are benchmarked rather than nurtured according to their individuality. The third part of the study was a questionnaire survey. Major findings include: 1. All respondents support the notion of developing creativity of Cantonese opera in general; 2. All respondents believe that artists are possible and capable to develop their own personal style 3. All respondents tend to agree that the audience would support artists to develop their personal style 4. All respondents tend to agree that the current artists are not developing their personal style. 5. Among the 3 groups, the artist group possess a significantly lower perception than the other groups Respondents tend to agree that artists should not follow audience’s expectation 6. All respondents agreed that the current environment of Cantonese opera could hardly facilitate the development of personal style

18403414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18403414.value: This study has reflected that education of audience should be valued and developed. First, professional artists tend to follow the expectation of audiences when they make artistic decisions in their performances. For instance, some artists focus on imitating previous eminent artists without considering developing their own style. The current audiences tend to satisfy with those artists who can successfully imitate their previous idols. This can be a vicious cycle which spoils the audiences. On the other hand, novice audiences tend to appreciate creative performances with new elements. How to balance between those experienced and novice audiences is another crucial research question. The findings of this study will be disseminated to the field of Cantonese opera in Hong Kong. Stakeholders including professional artists, teachers, students, promoters, administrators, experienced and novice audiences will be invited to attend a seminar for a discussion on the findings and how their different roles could contribute to the development of personal styles. Apart from publishing journal articles, findings of this study will also be presented in other channels such as newspapers and media on internet.

18403414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18403414.value: The nature of this study is firstly to investigate how eminent artists of Cantonese opera in Hong Kong have developed their personal creativity, and how musical creativity in Cantonese operatic singing can be analysed and demonstrated. Further, the study proposed a 3-stage model in developing a personal style, and examined how the changing socio-cultural contexts have impacted on the development of personal styles. Finally, a comparison of perceptions of developing personal styles of professional artists, experience audiences and novice audiences was done in order to examine if there are different view of these groups. This study has shown that some eminent artists have successfully founded their own personal style due to their effort and determination to do so, with a lifelong pursuance plus their domain knowledge and skills in Cantonese opera. The competitive environment was also a critical factor leading to their success. They did not follow the audiences’ expectation, but raise the enjoyment of the performance, which had won their support. Experienced artists reflected that it is rare to see such artists at present; most of them tend not to determine for developing their own style. Young audiences should be taught in expecting a creative personal style.

18403614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18403614.value: 學前教育是香港教育制度的重要組成部分，其幼教老師是高品質和發展適宜兒童早期教育計劃的重要組成部分。改革方案於2000年（陳 & 陳，2003）強調，必須在各級教育提升的專業能力。一個關注的焦點是多元文化，特別是有關香港的教育系統，直到2008年種族歧視條例往往忽視少數族裔誰只佔2％的整體學生人數的焦點。來自不同種族背景的，如印度，印尼，尼泊爾，巴基斯坦，菲律賓和泰國的學生，面臨著許多挑戰，包括低學業成就，學習中國作為一門外語，家庭收入低，社會適應問題的困難，以及缺乏社會支持（莊，2005;色調，2011;色相和肯尼迪2012年肯尼迪和色相，2011）。在兒童早期教育的多元文化行為，已自20世紀90年代中期在許多西方國家討論在美國（Rhedding - 瓊斯，2010）和21世紀初（克拉克，2000;精梳機，2003年）教師在教育學生在多元文化教室之能力是必不可少的這些兒童的成功。 從指定的少數族裔學生在香港40所幼兒園幼兒教師將參加本次研究。定量和定性分析的混合方法將被採用。定量分析將基於三個自我報告的問卷。教師信念與行為的調查將被用於評估有關的文化和包容幼兒教育工作者的教學信念和實踐。這份問卷是根據2009年的指導方針由國家協會幼兒的教育（NAEYC）在美國出版的發展適宜性實踐（DAP）。我以前對幼兒教師在香港（梁，2012）的研究考察的具體類型由本問卷評估，教學信念和實踐。一個有趣的發現是廣泛的響應與文化多樣性的項目。本項目不相關的衡量與家庭，文化和包容的信仰和習俗等物品。這一發現表明，香港幼兒教師的意識，在課堂上與文化多樣性問題相當大的變化。根據NAEYC指引，DAP是另一個問卷，翻譯和驗證我之前的研究。最後，多元文化教學規模驗證的Spanierman等。 （2011）將被用來評估教師的觀點和行為，與在課堂上多文化問題。定性分析將作為基於課堂觀察，學校的文件，以及半結構式訪談，調查課堂教學與教師和學生的學習經驗，並研究在整個學校中的經歷不同的案例研究。 繼近期的政策指引和以往的研究，本研究將探討以下內容：多元文化主義（1）幼兒教師多文化概念是DAP的一部分，（2）學校對打造多文化敏感的環境需要的影響，以及（3 ）教師專業發展需要，以促進多元文化的學習環境。結果應該能夠提供政府的政策制定者的一些指引，校長和教育機構在他們的努力，以促進幼兒教育多元文化的做法。

18403614.label: Realisation of objectives
18403614.value: In the attempt of achieving the research objectives, collection of quantitative and qualitative data of preschool teachers’ view were made. The main focus of the research activities is to deploy the survey instruments to measure teachers’ and students’ constructs of cultural responsiveness, teaching belief and practice of inclusion education. By conducting quantitative data-collection from 347 teachers in 22 kindergartens, it gave us feedback on the effectiveness of promoting cultural responsiveness, the importance and difficulties encountered for teaching practices for a culturally diverse classroom. By using the 16 items of Multicultural Teaching Competency Scale (MTCS) survey, an average score is calculated for each kindergarten. Invitations for in-depth interviews were sent to 5 schools with the highest score (indicating the awareness of cultural responsiveness is high) and 5 schools with the lowest score. In result, 17 preschool teachers from 4 schools were invited for semi-structured interviews in 2015. The 16 items of MTCS were applied to explore preschool teachers’ constructs of cultural responsiveness and multiculturalism (Objective 1). For the Teacher Beliefs and Practices Survey (TBPS), a validated Hong Kong version of TBPS is adopted to examine new concept of teaching beliefs and practices for a culturally diverse classroom (Leung, 2012) (Objective 2). The 30-item Instructional Activities Scale (IAS), from the same validated Hong Kong version, was also applied (Leung, 2012). Both were used to examine the teachers’ self-reported frequency of appropriate and inappropriate practices in classroom. The survey was conducted between January 2015 and October 2015. Invitation of survey participation was sent out to 40 kindergartens. Samples were recruited on a voluntary basis and consent from the participants were collected. As at October 2015, 22 target kindergartens had participated in the project. It contributes a total number of 347 teachers participated in the survey to investigate their perceptions of multicultural teaching competence and beliefs (Objective 1 & 2). A summary of the school participation in survey study is shown below: Among 347 participants, 5 are male preschool teachers and 342 female teachers. For their teaching experience, around 200 teachers have more than 10 years of teaching experience and 100 teachers have less than 3 years. More than 90% of the participants are Chinese and have obtained their teacher’s certificates. About the education level of these 347 teachers, around 50% of them have a higher diploma degree and another 50% have a bachelor’s degree or higher education level. But it is disappointed to find that more than 80% of the participants did not receive any training for inclusive teaching in classroom. In-depth interviews were also conducted. By using the 16 items of MTCS survey, an average score is calculated for each kindergarten. 5 schools with the highest scores and 5 schools with the lowest are selected to conduct in-depth interview with teachers. 35 preschool teachers from 8 schools were interviewed individually about their views of multicultural responsive classroom and their beliefs and practices on teaching ethnic minority students as at 31st December, 2016. 2 schools have rejected our invitation for the in-depth interview and analysis is carried out in early 2016 in order to understand any school differences and professional needs for teachers on promoting inclusive learning environments (Objective 3 and 4). Mean responses, standard deviations, and inter-items correlation were examined to understand teachers’ perceptions of multicultural teaching competence, beliefs and practices. In the data collection process, the major difficulty we encountered is that more time is required for collecting qualitative research as the school teachers are fully-occupied most of the time. It is difficult to invite them for the interviews, hence we have applied for an project extension which enabled us to complete planned qualitative data-collection. No further deviation is made from the original research plan.

18403614.label: Major findings and research outcome
18403614.value: (Leung & Hue, in press) An article of the confirmatory factor analysis on the MTCS model is currently under review. A tripartite model of the MTCS assessing skills, knowledge and relationships, was found to be well suited to our sample of Hong Kong teachers. The development of a Hong Kong version of the MTCS provides contextual and cultural insights for the region’s teacher-education institutes into the development of effective multicultural-training programs for in-service and pre-service teachers. (Leung, in press) Structural equation modeling of MTCS was used to test the hypothesized conceptual model in which teachers’ multicultural sensitivity predicted their use of DAP in the classroom. Results showed that the dual factors of the MTCS, namely teachers’ knowledge and relationship/harmony, were significant predictors of DAP. Some interesting findings were also revealed in the model, such as: promoting cultural diversity is based on Multicultural Teaching Knowledge; teachers may require community resources in teaching diverse cultural classes. Such multicultural teaching knowledge appears to help to develop teachers’ developmentally appropriate beliefs on teaching, and to discourage the formation of developmentally inappropriate practices in teaching. Multicultural teaching knowledge can enhance developmentally appropriate teaching beliefs and practices, and reduce developmentally inappropriate practices. It is highly recommended that multicultural education be embedded in early childhood education programs for both in-service and pre-service teachers. (Hue, 2017) In examining teachers’ talk about the cultural responsiveness, two challenges for the ethnic minority education have been identified: balancing of unity and diversity, and the negligence of involvement of mainstream schools. First, the teachers’ construct of cultural responsiveness is closely linked to the pre-determined goals of ‘cultural integration’ and ‘cultural harmony’ held by individual teachers and schools. It is a challenge for teachers, school managers and policy makers to promote cultural responsiveness as a dynamic process of balancing unity and diversity. Second, the teachers’ constructs of cultural responsiveness is totally set for the ethnic minority groups of students and how they can be integrated into mainstream schools and society. To tackle these challenges, there is a need to broaden our discussion of ethnic minority education, from ‘designated’ or ‘segregated’ schools to mainstream schools, and to examine in depth the concept of educational purpose and the cultural knowledge of ethnicity related to the schooling of these students and school practitioners’ understanding of rationales of ethnic minority education, such as ‘cultural responsiveness’, ‘cultural integration’ and ‘social justice’.

18403614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18403614.value: Future research should also focus on environmental influences on multicultural teaching, such as school bureaucracy. It is suggested that researchers further study teachers’ attitudes toward multicultural education in terms of teaching beliefs and more general attitudes by using tests that assess implicit attitudes, including the implicit association test, evaluative and semantic priming tasks, the Extrinsic Affective Simon Task, Go/No-Go Association Task, and the Affect Misattribution Procedure. Though these tests vary in administration and content, they are based on the shared assumption that the tests allow investigators to capture attitudes that individuals are unwilling to report. There is also a need for further investigation of teaching beliefs and practices in a multicultural education environment. One multicultural education concern, namely school bureaucracy, has not been considered in the present study, but may have a large effect on teachers’ beliefs and practices in the classroom. One line of research could investigate teachers’ macroperspective awareness of issues in schools that affect the experiences of culturally diverse students (Marshall, 1996).

18403614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18403614.value: Hong Kong is widely recognized as an international and ethnically diverse city, but just around 8% of the population is made up of ethnic minorities. Many of these students come from disadvantaged socioeconomic backgrounds, and often experience difficulties in learning , along with various adaptation problems. Hong Kong schools are concerned about how diverse learning needs of ethnic minority students could be better fulfilled. This composition flows into schools where teachers in selected schools need to cater for a diverse school population. This research examines multiculturalism in schools and cultural responsiveness of teachers, in terms of their practices and constructs of assessment classroom environments. Using both quantitative and qualitative data: surveys and interviews collected from local school teachers in Hong Kong. The culturally responsive method to assessment described in this research foregrounds considerations of cultural influence in teachers’ beliefs regarding assessment. Multicultural teaching knowledge can improve developmentally appropriate teaching beliefs and practices, and reduce inappropriate practices. It is highly recommended that multicultural education be embedded in early childhood education programs for both in-service and pre-service teachers. The insights of this research will help teachers, school managers, and policy makers to foster teachers’ multicultural-teaching competency and create supportive multicultural classroom environments.
