18406214.label: Major findings and research outcome
18406214.value: Key research findings This research examined the general tendency of 15,000 Hong Kong youth towards school and civic engagement, and more particularly the tendency of those with different religious affiliations. The application of the three frameworks was supported by the findings. Consistent with the spiritual health framework, our findings show that youth with a religious faith rated happier and more balanced in maintaining relationships with oneself, others, nature and the higher order than those without such an affiliation. Religious youth also reported more positive engagement outcomes than their non-religious counterparts in being appreciative of parental support, teachers’ care and peer support rendered to their school life and work harder. Likewise, they also responded higher in mastering civic knowledge, respecting the rule of law, and actively involved in community and political activities. Overall, religious affiliation is a key factor promoting school/academic engagement and civic engagement among both mainstream and non-mainstream youth. Indeed, our findings confirm a significant and positive direct effect of school engagement on civic engagement, and demonstrate a stronger indirect effect on civic engagement, with civic-related self-belief as a crucial mediator of school engagement on civic behaviours. Significant student group differences were noted. NCS indicated the highest level of satisfaction with school, family and friends. They reported a better spiritual health than the other student groups. Both the CIS and CBS reported the lowest level of civic engagement but indicated the highest desire to pursue a degree in postsecondary. HK mainstream students gave the lowest scores to the areas of life satisfaction, spiritual health, school engagement and societal engagement. Overall, boys, specially the non-religious mainstream boys, are of greater risk and with negative subjective life outcomes. Research outcome We generated a data-set of over 15,000 samples. PI-Yuen has delivered 5 international conference presentations; one international keynote speech; one school development seminar; 1 press release and 1 knowledge transfer research dissemination seminar with the research team; and 1 public speech at the ETV Online RTHK. The findings have helped the research team in generating 5 peer-refereed articles (2 published, 1 forthcoming and 2 under review); one book of 84,000 words (in Chinese)(expected 2019 by Breakthrough Ltd); one book contract from Routledge (London) and 3 short articles. Also, there are 3 articles targeting SSCI journals under preparation. PI-Yuen has authored and launched another GRF project (GRF Ref. No. 18606717); submitted a Knowledge Transfer Grant proposal. PI-Yuen is currently supervising 2 doctoral students on the related field.

18406214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18406214.value: Spiritual health appears to be a core element in positive student development academically and socially. It deserves more attention in the school curriculum. Increase students’ pro-school behaviours, attitudes and efforts will be instrumental and beneficial for their school-related endeavours. Implications for teacher development Our findings challenge teachers’ commonsensical notions. Educating the mainstream poor is as important as immigrant and minority students. Teachers’ understanding of student diversity needs to be expanded and their awareness of a range of oppressions in their daily teaching should be raised. This is to call for the rejection of the one-size-fit-all approach and to offer differentiated support measures for different student groups. Future studies should advance understanding of the nature of the correlation among religious affiliation, school and civic engagement of young people by providing longitudinal and qualitative data to further unfold the trends and characteristics of student engagement. The role of civic related self-belief needs to be further understood. The study revealed the importance of virtual civic engagement, especially to more passive Asian youth. New strategies and methodologies should be explored in future studies to accurately represent the current state of civic engagement of Asian-Pacific youth.

18406214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18406214.value: The rationale and significance of the study is rooted in the belief that education should be for the public good. Hence, nurturing the well-being and the positive engagement among the young people from diverse social and cultural backgrounds is key for building an equitable and sustainable society. This empirical study was framed within the international literature of spiritual health and civic engagement to examine the critical factor of religious affiliation in the civic engagement of the disadvantaged student groups. The sample size (over 15,000) was large and the integrated instrument was credible. Our study offers a systematic investigation into and a deep understanding of the civic participation of the mainstream, Chinese immigrant and ethnic minority young people in Hong Kong secondary schools. The comparison is also significant in strengthening the contemporary findings of how religious affiliation affects civic participation. Given the unique contextual situation of Hong Kong, our findings provide new insights into how students view their school lives, the learning environment, and interactions with the community. The asserted significant direct effects of school engagement on civic engagement provide sufficient evidence with regard to the effectiveness of student engagement within school and society to affect policy change.

21200414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200414.value: 基於熒光和電化學方法的常規醫療診斷儀器通常由分立元件組成，這使得它們速度慢，體積大，且價格昂貴。在本項目中，我們計劃對可實現先進醫療診斷儀器的光子、電子和微加工的原理展開研究。為了驗證我們的科學理論，將對一種新型的雙熒光電化學傳感微系統進行設計、原型製作，並通過實驗驗證。在該研究中，有兩個主要的創新點。首先，微系統的高集成度可使單一設備同時支持熒光、電化學和電化學發光檢測。

21200414.label: Realisation of objectives
21200414.value: To address the 1st objective (to 100% completion), we have investigated both fluorescence and electrochemical sensing techniques, through the study, formulation and design of advanced prototypes based on novel architectures. Overall, this project led to the publication of 7 journal papers and 3 conference papers. To overcome the technological limitations of conventional devices, such as bulkiness and high complexity (which leads to high-cost), we have focused on microelectronics and microsystem techniques and architectures that enable highly-integrated, small size, low power, and low cost devices. We have investigated time-resolved fluorescence sensors, as this technique is in many cases more suitable for observing the dynamics of a bio/chemical process and is more immune to the adverse effects of autofluorescence, for example from biological samples. We have studied techniques such as time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) [J1] (Part C) and explored the feasibility of its complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) implementation. We have studied various CMOS architectures for TCSPC in terms of chip-area/hardware requirement, speed of operation, temporal resolution, and power consumption. It was found that the CMOS technology is a highly suitable technology for two reasons: i) high-speed capability translates directly to high temporal resolution, and ii) high level of integration enables a large number of channels/components to be integrated on the same chip, which significantly lower power consumption [J2][C1]. For signal transduction from the analyte to a physical signal (such as light and electrical current), we have investigate molecular probe sensors [J3]. In terms of electrochemical/chemical sensors, we have made significant improvements in sensitivity through the design and fabrication of nanostructured sensing surfaces [J4-J6][C2-3]. We have performed two investigations, each with different nanostructures and materials. The first investigation has focused on the technique for fabricating nanostructured Schottky diodes with a large surface area [J4-5]. The technique is based on hydrothermal synthesis, where the crystallographic phase and surface morphology of the sensing film can be controlled during fabrication and post-fabrication annealing temperature. Material properties are analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Diode I-V characteristics and barrier height, which corresponds to the sensor diode device turn-on voltage, have been measured and analyzed. Unlike conventional diode implementations, the fabricated Schottky diode exhibits a barrier height that ranges from 1.10 to 1.19 eV, due to the formation of different crystallographic phases and surface morphologies of the TiO2 nanostructures. Large surface area and low turn-on voltage holds great potential for high-sensitivity, low-power chemical sensing applications. The device physics has been investigated in detail to gain fundamental understanding of device operation [J6]. To probe chemical sensing from a materials perspective, the second investigation has focused on creating devices that can operate at very lower power consumption. We have devised a method for modulating the barrier height of RF sputtered ZnO nanoclustered Schottky diodes and annealing conditions [J7]. By controlling the ZnO growth deposition parameters, different device I-V characteristics have been achieved and analyzed. Results indicate that the ZnO nanostructured Schottky diode exhibit a low turn-on voltage, thus is suitable for the realization of low-power sensor. To address the 2nd objective (to 100% completion), during this reporting period, we have investigated sensor interface circuits, in particular for readout of optical and image data (which can form the backend of, for example, a fluorescence sensor). These circuits and systems must take into consideration the shot noise characteristics of the photonic input. Rather than improving a conventional CMOS architecture, we have explored computational sensor architectures [J2]. In terms of technological challenges to be overcome, currently, optical encoding is implemented using components that are typically not integrated on the image sensor chip. This results in camera systems with large physical sizes, performance compromises, and implementation challenges, particularly in applications where size and power are constrained. In this project, we have designed, simulated, and fabricated a CMOS pixel sensor array with bidirectional multi-level spatial coded exposure encoding capability for computational imaging. Based on a capacitive transimpedance amplifier (CTIA) core, the proposed pixel architecture achieves bidirectional multi-level optical encoding, and is compatible with monolithic CMOS implementation. Designed and laid out in a standard 0.13-μm CMOS process, the pixel occupies an area of 13.8 μm × 13.8 μm with a fill factor of 30%. The journal paper [J2] was jointly authored with our collaborator at the University of British Columbia. Overall, project objectives were completed. Results achieved thus far are promising and is expected to contribute to the advancement of highly-sensitive, low-power, and small-sized fluorescence and chemical sensors for a variety of diagnostics applications.

21200414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200414.value: In the project, we have devised several advanced techniques (and developed several prototypes) for fluorescence and electrochemical analysis. These devices have a substantially cost and size advantage over existing components. From the initial evaluation, some of these devices show that they have performance and cost advantages that rival their conventional counterparts. Further development of the research will be carried out in two paths: 1) From the research front, focus will be placed on the continuation of expanding the capabilities of the developed platform. For example, the use of nanomaterials and nanoparticles will be used to enhance the selectivity of these devices to various analytes. 2) In view of the commercial potential of the developed technology, we are actively soliciting partner from the industries to work toward commercializing components, based on our filed patent, for the medical diagnostics market.

21200414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200414.value: Demand for accurate, rapid, and low-cost medical diagnostics has been ever rising due to the global aging population. Medical diagnostics based on the detection of biomolecules has wide applications from viral and pathogenic screening to genetic and cancer studies. Fluorescence and electrochemical methods are commonly used in biomolecule detection. Conventionally, fluorescence and electrochemical detections are performed by the bench-top fluorimeter and potentiostat, respectively. Both instruments typically consist of discrete components, making them bulky and expensive. Due to the sequential nature of the instrument, the throughput is generally low. This project investigated the design of advance prototypes, and their experimental validation, of fluorescence and electrochemical sensory microsystem. Advance in these detection strategies enables reduced sample volume, simplifies instrumental procedures, and enables new capabilities such as improves reliability and accuracy. In the microsystem, a CMOS sensor array serves as the sensory and computational core. The research findings open doors to highly-integrated, low-power sensory platform will enable novel implementation of disposable, wearable, and implantable biosensors that not only address key unmet needs in ubiquitous medical diagnostics, but can also be used as vehicles for the more general applications in the biological sciences.

21200714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200714.value: One of the key techniques that have evolved into the next generation (e.g., LTE) broadband wireless standards is the multiple antenna technique. The multiple antenna technique has already become part of our daily lives, which can be clearly shown by the high LTE-smart phone possession rate in Hong Kong. Today, there is gradual movement to further increase the number of antennas to tens or potentially hundreds. These systems are often dubbed as massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Promising theoretical results have been shown improved network capacity is possible. However, despite the theoretical success, many challenges have to be addressed, before any of the promised gain could be harnessed. At the very front of them are questions related to channel training overhead for large-dimensional channel estimation. Usable channel estimates at the transmitter and receiver are critical to facilitate advanced MIMO precoding techniques, such as beamforming and spatial-multiplexing. However, as the number of antennas increases substantially, the training overhead could overwhelm the channel resources allocated for data communications, resulting in significant decrease in data rates. Most massive MIMO research, however, circumvents this difficulty by focusing on the single antenna user. Hence, to provide spatial-multiplexing gain in the network, a large number of simultaneous users are always required, where the scenario does not extend to emerging multi-tiered small cell (e.g., picocell/femtocell) networks. Furthermore, restricting the receiver to single antenna precludes substantial spatial-multiplexing gain that large-scale antennas can provide. Thus, there is great interest in increasing the number of antennas both at the transmitter and receiver to leverage massive spatial-multiplexing gain. However, the achievable spatial-multiplexing gain is obviously reliant on the quality of the channel estimate. The goal of the project is to provide new approaches that greatly scale the large-dimensional channel training and channel estimation for massive MIMO spatial multiplexing systems. The approaches are constrained to only require a fixed training overhead, while still improving the quality of channel estimation. The novelty of the project lies in introducing new training signal adaptation schemes that leverage feedback information, and the optimal channel resource allocation that maximizes the system performance. The result is an upgraded channel training and channel estimation framework that greatly scales the system performance with the increased number of antennas. Such a framework can serve as a baseline for developing advanced massive MIMO systems, which could potentially revolutionize current cellular deployments by providing high throughput user access in various wireless applications.

21200714.label: Realisation of objectives
21200714.value: Conventional massive MIMO systems will have tens or hundreds of antennas where each antenna element is fed by its own dedicated RF chain. However, this system with such hundreds of RF chains is very costly and substantially energy inefficient, lacking its practicality. Instead, we started by looking at hybrid massive MIMO architecture, where the large antenna arrays are driven by a small number of RF chains. This architecture is of practical interest. To address Objectives 1, 2, and 3, we extended a general spatial modulation technique to the hybrid massive MIMO spatial-multiplexing system and conducted achievable throughput analysis. The transmitter is adapted to the channel state information (CSI) estimated at the received by using a feedback sent from the receiver to the transmitter (Objective 1). Conventionally, the achievable throughput analysis of spatial modulation for the spatial multiplexing systems has not been available in the literature. We undertook this analysis and derived the achievable throughput results in closed-form expressions. Moreover, tight upper and lower bounds of the achievable throughput were also provided (Objective 2). Based on the latter analysis, the feedback information is chosen to maximize the achievable throughput expression (Objective 3). Numerical simulations were conducted to show the tightness of the analysis. It was found that the investigated hybrid spatial-multiplexing can achieve similar performance as the conventional massive MIMO system, however, with far lower number of RF chains. To further realize Objectives 1, 3, and 4, we also devised iterative training signal adaptation technique that leads to robust precoder and combiner designs. The underlying idea is to optimize the training signal subspace and power allocation to maximize the achievable throughput of the network. We leveraged sophisticated source separation techniques to iteratively refine the signals (Objectives 1 and 3). In the considered design, the large array is modeled as a highly directional linear array, creating spatially correlated MIMO channels. Through the iterative adaptation, the subspace of the training signal was adjusted to be closely aligned with the correlated channel direction (Objective 4). A difference of rate and channel gain metric was proposed to formulate a quasi-water filling power optimization problem under the per-user power constraint. The formulated problem is convex and the power allocation values can analytically be obtained by solving the KKT conditions (Objective 3). The overall achievable throughput enhancement of the designed signal adaptation and power allocation techniques have been demonstrated as compared to other existing channel training and precoder coordination techniques.

21200714.label: Major findings and research outcome
21200714.value: The goal of the research is to exploit all the available side information to provide advanced channel adaptation techniques for hybrid massive MIMO spatial multiplexing systems. The underlying idea is to employ channel feedback and forward-backward adaptations to iteratively refine the training signal and optimize the power allocation to improve the throughput performance. We proposed the spatial modulation technique for the hybrid massive MIMO spatial multiplexing systems that deploy uplink feedback to adaptively design the transmit precoder. The feedback is optimized by maximizing the achievable throughput expression that is obtained by analyzing the proposed spatial modulation system. The latter proposed framework and the system concept have resulted in one journal publication in IEEE Transactions on Communications [Part C, 8, publication No. 1]. We also proposed a training signal adaption technique that iteratively refines the signal subspace and the power allocation that is adapted to spatially correlated MIMO channel subspaces. This work has been accepted for the publication in IEEE Journals of Selected Areas in Communications [Part C, 8, publication No. 2] and will be published soon. The developed framework could serve as a baseline for developing advanced massive MIMO systems. Moreover, the adoption and adaptation of the devised scheme to various different massive MIMO scenarios and 5G applications will potentially enhance current cellular deployments.

21200714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200714.value: The proposed method has a great potential to be extended to millimeter wave MIMO systems. Unlike the sub-6GHz massive MIMO, the millimeter wave MIMO channel exhibits substantial sparsity. The adoption of the proposed closed-loop channel sounding technique to the sparse millimeter wave MIMO channel is a very interesting research direction.

21200714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200714.value: The outcome of the project is a unified approach resulting in new solutions to the hybrid massive MIMO channel adaptive spatial multiplexing that exploits the feedback, forward-backward iteration, spatial correlations, and optimal subspace matching and power allocation. These contributions will upgrade the state-of-the-art massive MIMO systems, by providing a framework extracting high quality CSI and precoder/combiner, which could potentially be employed in current cellular deployments. These results will be of great interest to wireless communication community in both academia and industry. The hope is that by providing an enhanced signaling framework with tractable analysis, the adoption and adaptation of the proposed scheme to various different massive MIMO scenarios, e.g., single-user point-to-point channel, multiuser interference channels, multicell multiuser cooperative networks, multi-tiered small cell networks, will be as easy as choosing appropriate system paramters. Although we focus solely on the wireless communications in this proposal, we anticipate the developed scheme will also be applicable to other signal processing areas that concern the training and tracking vary large numbers of random objects under the noisy observations, such as radars, computer visions, economics, etc.

21201214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201214.value: 黑炭顆粒物是化石燃料和生物燃料燃燒所產生的排放物的主要成分。它能夠改變地球輻射平衡，影響氣候和大氣能見度。在香港和中國南方城市，黑炭通常與夏季季風聯繫在一起共同影響區域氣候。黑炭也是柴油機尾氣的其中一種成分，並且可以與類似多環芳烴這樣的有毒物質結合，能夠對人體產生多種不良影響。大氣中的黑炭很容易受到影響產生物理尺寸和化學特性的變化，從而改變其在肺部中的沉積位置和對太陽輻射的吸收能力。儘管過去已經有對黑炭基於實驗室和模型的研究，但是針對黑炭的實際研究是很少的，尤其是在城市環境中。這方面數據的缺失會大大地阻礙對黑炭在當地空氣治理，區域和全球範圍的氣候強迫及人體健康這三方面的評估。 本項目的目標是：(1). 研究城市環境中黑炭尺寸分佈在近源和混合層中隨時間變化的演變過程并分析影響黑炭變化的因素；(2).確定城市環境中混合或包裹在初級和完全混合型氣溶膠上的黑炭的化學特性；(3).研究顆粒物表面的致癌物質多環芳烴的變化模式，以及其對黑炭混合狀態的影響；(4).研究煤煙粒子塗層的化學性質對初級和完全混合型溶膠的光吸收特性的影響。

21201214.label: Realisation of objectives
21201214.value: The proposed study was carried out at a roadside site in comparison with a background site, representing fresh traffic-driven and aged ambient environments, respectively. The objectives set for the study was achieved in a combination of online and offline measurements to investigate the “roadside-to-ambient” evolution of particle physicochemical and optical properties in typical urban atmospheres of Hong Kong. In brief, 5-min particle size distribution (18.1 to 532.5 nm) was continuously monitored using a Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer (DMA 3082 in tandem with CPC 3775, TSI Inc., USA) to reveal PM state during this aging process, including condensation and coagulation. Then, the diurnal profiles of online data carried over 24 hours, included real-time measurements of black carbon (BC), particle-bound polyaromatic hydrocarbons (p-PAHs) and their interaction on PM optical properties was analyzed in-line in real-time. This approach, identified the varying specific trends BC and p-PAHs at roadside and background sites during sampling periods. In addition, 24-hour filter sampling was carried out to collect PM2.5 particles and analyze their chemical properties. Further, a thermodenuder (TD) was employed in determining the role of a controlled temperature (in the range 50 – 200oC) in the interaction of semi-volatile (SVOCs) components with particles, may provide some insights on investigate the impact of soot particle (BC) coating on the light absorption properties of fresh, mixed and aged aerosols. Firstly, this project presents the total particle number (PN) concentration and size distributions (ranging from 18.5 nm to 532.5 nm) in the two different environments represented by the roadside (LCK) and ambient (KLT) sites, respectively. The roadside PN levels were clearly higher than those of the ambient PN for most of the time, as is also shown in the comparison of average particle size distributions. The mode of roadside particles was between 30 and 40 nm, similar to the sizes of particles from typical diesel emissions (<50 nm), indicating the freshly emitted roadside particles. The mode of ambient particles was at larger sizes around 50-70 nm inside the Aitken mode (30-130 nm), likely due to particle growth through condensation of and coagulation between nucleation mode particles during the atmospheric aging processes from roadside to the ambient atmosphere. There were three distinct peaks of PN concentration for both roadside and ambient aerosols. The morning peak of roadside PN concentration is attributed to the presence of nucleation mode particles at 30 nm, reflecting the abundant freshly emitted particles with heavy traffic loadings and including the accumulation of ultrafine particles and the formation of new particles from vehicle emissions. The evening peak was also influenced by traffic, but with wider size distribution (25-40 nm) than that in morning peak, which likely resulted from condensational growth of aged particles. With reduction of nucleation mode particles, roadside particles displayed peaks at larger sizes (40-80 nm) during noon-afternoon periods. We attributed this phenomenon to new particle formation via chemical and photo-chemical reactions, first by nucleation and then by accumulation of particles transported from heavy-duty traffic areas. The peak of ambient particle number concentration also occurred at noon with enhanced photochemical production of new particles. Secondly, the Aethalometer was programmed to automatically record BC concentrations in μg·m-3 at 5-min intervals over the sampling period in each location and a photoelectric aerosol sensor (PAS 2000, Echo-chem) was operated as an indicator of the p-PAHs. Both low BC and p-PAHs concentrations were observed in ambient site, while much higher and variable BC and p-PAHs ranges occurred in the roadside atmosphere. We classified the diurnal measurements into four periods (0:00-06:00, 06:00-12:00, 12:00-18:00 and 18:00-24:00) based on time series of PM number size distributions to illustrate the contribution of the sources and aging impacts on particles. There is a poor correlation between BC and p-PAHs in ambient particles (R=0.18) during 0:00-06:00, suggesting that less BC emissions with fewer traffic flow would supply less surface for p-PAHs absorption. On the other hand, much higher and more constant correlation coefficients were observed for the other time periods (06:00-12:00, 12:00-18:00 and 18:00-24:00), suggesting that the relationships between ambient BC and p-PAHs. In roadside particles, the regressions between BC and p-PAHs are significantly different during sampling periods, with an R of 0.75, 0.83, 0.01 and 0.83 at 0:00-06:00, 06:00-12:00, 12:00-18:00 and 18:00-24:00, respectively. These results indicate that local traffic significantly drives the variation of these ratios, as demonstrated in the periods of 06:00-12:00 and 18:00-24:00. Additionally, high regression slopes (Slope (06:00−12:00) =31.9) and (Slope (18:00-24:00) =40.7) suggests that high fresh roadside BC concentrations were emitted with p-PAHs coating during rush hour traffic at near-traffic site. However, the poorest relationship was observed between (R=0.01, P=0.56) and the lowest slope values (2.8) during 12:00 -18:00 suggests the presence of considerable scattering materials coated on fresh roadside BC particles, such as SOA, NH4+, and NO3-. Moreover, the variation in the p-PAHs concentrations were opposite to the nss-SO42-/EC trend. This is likely a result of nss-SO42- coated on particle surface would significantly suppress the underlying p-PAHs detection. Lastly, the light absorption coefficient (babs) was calculated from the seven wavelengths (i.e., 370, 470, 520, 590, 660, 880, and 950 nm) Aethalometer measurements taken by the AE42 and AE33. The absorption at 880 nm is assumed to be only BC absorption, while absorption at the lower wavelength (370 nm) is attributed to both BC and BrC. Therefore, the corrected babs at 880 nm refers to babs-BC, while the babs-BrC is obtained from babs at 370 and 880 nm wavelengths. The wider range of babs-BC,880nm value observed in roadside particles than those in ambient particles, reflects that babs-BC,880nm values were more sensitive to traffic density. In roadside particles, the two peaks of babs-BrC,370nm occurred at 12:00 and 18:00 with descending values of babs-BC,880nm. These results suggest the importance that the increasing UV-absorbing materials of p-PAHs, would heavily affect the detection of BC absorbing properties in roadside particles. For this approach, the role of temperature can influence the presence of semi-volatile species in the BC mixing. Thus, the filter-based light absorption enhancement of BC (Eabs- degree-wavelength) as well as the remaining aerosol compositions were investigated to indicate remaining percentage (RP) for aerosol passing through TD at certain temperature. Parallel light absorption measurement by AE33 showed that E_(abs-fb)^ generally increased from 1.02 (Eabs-50 degree-880nm) to 1.20 (Eabs-200 degree-660nm) with heating temperature from 50 to 200 degree. While as TD was heated at 280 degree, Eabs increased sharply to ~1.64 (Eabs-280 degree-660nm), representing the mixture of BC. As discussed above, RP of organics and nitrate decreased very little from 200 to 280 degree, whereas sulfate and ammonium showed a remarkable decrease, indicating a significant impact of ammonium sulfate on light absorption enhancement, due to their lensing effect by coatings. In addition, possible artificial coating by organic aerosol (OA) might induce light absorption enhancement of BC. However, according to our observation, organics have less impact on Eabs since organics varied slightly for heated aerosol from 200 to 280 degree, whereas Eabs-fb increased sharply from 1.16 (Eabs-200 degree-880nm) to 1.63 (Eabs-280 degree-880nm). Moreover, a decrease of ~41% in babs was observed at 660-950 nm after heating at 280 degree compared to ~ 39% at 370-470 nm, indicating the existence of a stronger absorption of low volatile organics which were still present after 280 degree heating.

21201214.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201214.value: From the studies of PM size distribution, and chemical and optical properties in PM2.5 at a typical urban roadside and urban ambient site in Hong Kong during cool weather periods. Both roadside and ambient PM shared similar PN profiles during daytime with typical peaks during traffic rush hours and noon time photochemical period while the two distributions have different mode diameters, reflecting that atmospheric processes (e.g., condensation and coagulation) play important roles in the change in particle size distribution with ages. The similar and high portions of SIA (sum of nss-SO42-, NO3- and NH4+) and SOC (secondary organic carbon) in PM2.5 were found between ambient and roadside particles, suggesting the secondary aerosol formation occurs quickly in urban areas. The nss-SO42-/EC and NO3-/EC show different trends at the two different sites that reflect their different origins. These accomplished results were transformed into couple of publications. Subsequently, in the PM optical properties studies, BC shows more evident relationship with p-PAHs in roadside particles than those in ambient particles, indicating that traffic sources were main contributors to light absorbing particles. High levels of typical absorbing materials (BC and p-PAHs) were observed at roadside. Aging of ambient BC particles by coating with secondary aerosol appears to result in a decrease in ambient p-PAH/BC ratios at noon-afternoon time period and may prolong the lifetime of PAHs in the atmosphere. The discussions between BC and p-PAHs were also published in the articles. In the BC mixing studies, the concentrations of semi-volatile materials were noted varied with increase in the temperature of TD. It is in good agreement with the reduced mass concentrations of SIA with increase in the temperature. It concludes that ammonium sulfate have an obviously impact on light absorption enhancement of BC (Eabs,) in relation to their lensing effect by coatings. However, based on our observation, organics don’t have notable impact on Eabs, since organics varied little for heated aerosol from 200 to 280 C, whereas Eabs increased sharply from 1.16 (Eabs-200 degree-880nm) to 1.63 (Eabs-280 degree-880nm). Moreover, OA was usually recognized to have stronger absorption at short wavelength, so it’s reasonable to observe a positive bias at short wavelength. Therefore, it’s hard to claim OA has such impact on light absorption enhancement at long wavelength here determined from Aethalometer measurement. The comparisons between SIA and OA impacts on Eabs was adequately discussed in the attached research publication.

21201214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201214.value: In this project, the in-depth analysis on the evolution of BC characteristics in urban environments and the factors that influence them in near-source and well mixed air over diurnal and seasonal time scales were investigated. However, there exists very few real-world investigations and experiments on the topics of BC coatings and how it impacts the optical and chemical nature of these particles and their dynamic formation processes. In the absence of such knowledge it remains a challenge to assess their impact on local air quality, regional and global climate forcing and on human health. Thus, in future works, controlled parametric investigation by thermally removing semi-volatile particle coating will also be applied for direct comparative study on the physicochemical nature of BC aerosol coating. Further, p-PAHs as an indicator of primary BrC shows more evident relationship with BC in two sites. However, linking other light absorbing organic carbon (BrC) materials with BC of different characteristics and sources is not well understood. Thus, we will vary different experimental conditions to understand the evolution of ambient BrC through chamber study and their impact on BC coatings.

21201214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201214.value: Black carbon (BC) particles are major components of emissions from fossil fuel combustion and biomass burning. It is a strong light absorbing material in the atmosphere, changing earth’s radiative balance and affecting the climate and visibility. Large fleets of diesel vehicles locally in Hong Kong contribute to 50% of total mileage and produce BC in highly packed urban environment with large population exposed to the roadside pollutants. BC has been often mixed with other toxic constituents, such as particle-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (p-PAHs), and associated with various adverse health effects. This study aimed at investigating the PM size distribution in Hong Kong from near-source to well mixed air over diurnal time scales. The BC alongside the PM chemical components and p-PAHs were generally noted in high quantities during 9 AM to 9 PM at roadside compared to background site. In addition, the optical characteristics of BC mixing and coating was better investigated in fresh, mixed and aged aerosols in urban environment. Finally, controlled parametric investigation by thermally removing semi-volatile particle coating will also be applied for direct comparative study on the physicochemical nature of BC coating.

21201314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201314.value: Pollen tube is the passageway to deliver the sperm cells from pollen grain to ovule. Mechanical characterization of pollen tube is extremely significant for the understanding of plant growth and plant fertilization. Nowadays, many techniques have been proposed to address this issue. However, these methods can only measure the upper surface of pollen tube, since few technology can overturn or rotate the sample flexibly under microscopy. These data were not adequate to elucidate the natural growth of pollen tube with 3D morphology clearly. Furthermore, owing to the technique limitation, rare quantitative results were reported about the mechanical anisotropy of the cellulose microfibrils distribution within cell wall, which have been thought to play an important role in determination of pollen tube’s diameter. Therefore, the approach for mechanical characterization of pollen tube from full orientation (360’ panorama) with high spatial resolution is essentially required. Nanorobot is able to manipulate the small object precisely at nanometer scale, which provides an effective solution for the pollen tube overturning/rotating under microscopy. This project aims to pollen tube mechanical characterization from full orientation by developing a high-flexible nanorobot platform. First, a rotation alignment station will be developed based on nanorobot, which can alignment the pollen tube to the rotation center and rotate it about 360 degree freely inside an environmental scanning electron microscopy (ESEM). Second, a closed-loop control system for the alignment station will be developed to realize the high-speed manipulation and high-accuracy positioning. Third, a high-precise nano characterization system will be designed for pollen tube by integrating a nano-indentor and a nanorobot arm. Forth, the mechanical property of pollen tube will be characterized from full orientation based on the above systems. Finally, PI expects to build an improved physical model for pollen tube and elucidate the role of mechanical principles in plant growth. This proposal will provide a novel strategy to investigate pollen tube’s mechanical properties from full orientation based on nanorobot technique. The results will lead to an in-depth understanding of the correlation between the cell wall mechanical property and cell growth. Furthermore, this platform will enhance the observation ability of SEM greatly, which will be able to image the sample from 360’ panorama rather than from only one direction. This platform can also be used to test the anisotropy performance of other micro/nano material from full orientation, especially for 1-D material, such as nanotube and nanowire. 花粉管是連接花粉粒和胚珠的通道，其機械特性研究對於理解植物生長和植物受精有著重要意義。該專案通過開發高柔性納米機器人平臺，旨在從全角度研究花粉管的機械特性。研究基於納米機器人的旋轉對中裝置，實現對花粉管在電子顯微鏡下的360度自由旋轉。開發閉環的控制系統，實現對樣品的高速操作和高精確度定位。最終實現對花粉管的機械特性測量，闡明其在植物生長中的作用機理。

21201314.label: Realisation of objectives
21201314.value: Objective 1: To realize the flexible manipulation and rotation of pollen tube inside ESEM chamber by designing a rotation alignment station. We designed a nanorobotic system with 7 degrees of freedom containing two units, which can work independently with three DOFs x-y-z and y-z-theat, respectively. This system has a miniature size (about 140mm x 50mm x 50mm) and is able to be installed inside the ESEM chamber easily. We also developed a master-slave control system for the nano robot, to allow users to manipulate the micro/nano samples inside the ESEM chamber by computer remotely. With this developed system, we are able to manipulate and characterize the nanomaterial with high accuracy not only for the pollen tube, but also for other cells and micro/nano materials. The relevant results have been published in [4][7][10][11]. Objective 2: To automate the alignment process by developing a closed-loop control system to improve the operation accuracy and working efficiency. We developed a vision-based system to realize the closed-loop control of the robotics. Here, ESEM real-time image is captured automatically with 24 f/s by a video capture card. Then, the sample is identified based on template matching and feature recognition. The position of the sample at different time was calculated automatically via OpenCV programming. After obtaining the position, the distance information was sent to the manipulator controller as a control signal. Thereby, the sample can be moved to the rotation center automatically. In addition, we also developed a dialog-based human-machine interface based on VC++ programming. This interface integrates the above functions together, including imaging processing, position calculation and motor movement, by which the alignment process can be realized only by clicking a few buttons. The relevant results have been published in [2][6][9]. Objective 3: To characterize the local mechanical property of pollen tube at nanometer scale by designing a high-precise nano characterization system. We applied our developed system to study the mechanical properties of the biology cells, and several results have been achieved: In [8], an integrated system, named dynamic force characterization microscopy (DFCM), is proposed to investigate the detachment process of the single yeast cell. In this process, the detachment force is measured by the laser displacement sensor dynamically. All the while, the shape changing of the sample is observed by ESEM at nanometer resolution. The experimental results verify that DFCM integrates the accurate force measurement ability of AFM, the real-time high-resolution imaging ability of SEM and the flexible manipulation ability of robot. It provides a novel approach for the dynamic force characterization at small scale, which will greatly benefit the in-depth understating of the dynamic detachment process and the characterization of material’s mechanical property. In [3][6], we propose a vision-based nano robotic system and then realizes automatic non-embedded cell cutting with this system. First, the nano robotic system is developed and integrated with a nanoknife inside an environmental scanning electron microscopy (ESEM). Then, the positions of the nanoknife and the single cell are recognized, and the distance between them is calculated dynamically based on image processing. To guarantee the positioning accuracy and the working efficiency, we propose a distance-regulated speed adapting strategy, in which the moving speed is adjusted intelligently based on the distance between the nanoknife and the target cell. The results indicate that the automatic non-embedded cutting is able to be achieved within 1-2 mins with low invasion benefiting from the high precise nanorobot system and the sharp edge of nanoknife. This research paves a way for the high-throughput cell cutting at cell’s natural condition, which is expected to make significant impact on the biology studies, especially for the in-situ analysis at cellular and subcellular scale, such as cell interaction investigation, neural signal transduction and low invasive cell surgery. In conference [2], we developed a MEMS based for sensor and employed to characterize the mechanical property of pollen tube. We found that the largest force 120 nN is four times larger than the smallest value 26 nN when bending the pollen tube from different directions. Objective 4: To investigate the mechanical property of pollen tube from full orientation via the high-flexible robot platform, which will be integrated by the rotation alignment station and the nano characterization system. Then, to elucidate the mechanical principles in pollen tube growth based on the experimental data. Mechanical properties, such as flexural rigidity and elastic modulus, are important factors deciding how pollen tubes penetrate and navigate inside flowers’ styles and finally into ovules. As the ratio of pollen tubes’ length to diameter can be far more than several thousand, bending pollen tubes is an effective method to measure their mechanical properties. However, current techniques, such as microfluidic system, can only bend pollen tubes from one fixed direction. With regard to pollen tubes’ irregular shapes and ununiform properties, properties achieved from pollen tubes’ one direction cannot reflect properties of other directions. Herein, we use our rotary nanorobotic system to rotate the pollen tubes and measured its mechanical property from multi-direction, instead of one fixed direction. We found that the flexural rigidity of pollen tubes varies as much as fifteen times at different directions. During pollen tubes’ penetration inside carpels, pollen tubes need to change their penetration direction to fit into external environment. For example, when pollen tubes start to enter into the micropyle and embryo sac, the growth direction of pollen tubes need to change about 120°. To keep the turning area stable, the outer edge of the turning area should be more rigid than other areas. The measured results by our method can help explain how pollen tubes control their penetration, growth and shapes within a flower’s carpel, which gives new opportunities for the in-depth understanding of the mechanism of pollen-tube guidance inside pistil. The relevant results have been published in [1].

21201414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201414.value: The research objective of this project is to construct a statistical methodology for designing and analyzing computer experiments using interpolating polynomials. Multivariate polynomial metamodels are increasingly being used in computer experiments due to the development of polynomial chaos expansions and sparse grid interpolation for uncertainty quantification, and the popularity of response surface methodology and regression for model building. For deterministic computer codes (those that yield fixed outputs/ responses for fixed inputs), interpolating polynomial metamodels should be used instead of noninterpolating ones for logical consistency and prediction accuracy. However, methods proposed in the literature for constructing interpolating polynomial metamodels only provide point predictions. There is no known method that can provide probabilistic statements about interpolation errors, which is crucial for assessing the impact of potential interpolation errors on decision-making. Furthermore, in the uncertainty quantification of engineering models, grid designs or sparse grids are used to construct interpolating polynomials, resulting in highly inflexible designs with large number of runs for moderate to high dimension problems. These designs are also nonadaptive, i.e., they do not use information in the data at hand to determine the best location for the next design points. Consequently, they can be inefficient. This research will develop a stochastic interpolating polynomial (SIP) that seeks to overcome the problems discussed above. A Bayesian approach will be taken in which interpolation uncertainty is quantified probabilistically through the posterior distribution of the output. The proposed model will allow assessment of the effect of interpolation uncertainty on estimation of quantities of interest, optimization, and decision-making based on metamodel predictions. Statistical methods for designing experiments to construct the SIP will be developed. Algorithms for generating designs that optimize several posterior measures of uncertainty about the true output will be proposed. It is expected that these designs can be of almost any size and can adapt to the peculiarities of the function being modeled. Finally, this research will apply the SIP to four important classes of engineering problems. The basic SIP model will be extended to model experiments with multiple levels of fidelity and functional outputs. Applications of the SIP to optimization and robust parameter design (RPD) will also be considered. This project will provide novel, flexible, and powerful statistical methods for polynomial interpolation. The proposed methods will be important contributions to the engineering community due to the widespread acceptance and use of polynomial metamodels for uncertainty quantification in the community. 本项目研究目的是利用插值多项式来建立用于设计和分析计算机试验的统计方法。 随着多项式混沌展开和稀疏网格插值方法在不确定性量化中的发展，响应面法和回归方法在建模中的流行，多元多项式元模型在计算机试验中正被越来越多地使用。在确定性的计算机代码（对于固定的输入会产生固定的输出或者响应）中，应该采用插值多项式元模型替换非插值多项式元模型，以达到逻辑上的一致性和预测的准确性。但是现有的文献中提出的建立插值多项式元模型的方法仅提供了点预测。同时没有任何已知的方法可以对插值误差进行概率上的阐述，而这一过程对评估潜在的插值误差给决策制定带来的影响十分重要。进一步地，在工程模型的不确定性量化中，网格设计或者稀疏网格方法被用来建立插值多项式，但是这些方法经常产生十分不灵活的设计以及针对中高维问题的大量试验。这些设计也是非适应的设计，即不利用手头的数据中的信息来确定下一次设计点的最佳位置。因此，这些设计方法是效率低下的。 本研究将会提出随机插值多项式(SIP: Stochastic Interpolating Polynomial)的方法，来解决上文讨论的问题。采用贝叶斯方法，通过输出的后验分布来实现对插值不确定性进行概率上的量化。本文提出的模型可以基于元模型的预测，评估插值的不确定性给一些感兴趣的量，优化和决策制定带来的影响。同时将会研究建立SIP的设计实验的统计方法。并提出可以生成设计的算法，以优化关于真实输出不确定性的一些后续措施。可以预料这些设计方法几乎可以是任何大小尺寸并可以适应被建模函数的特性。 最终，本研究将SIP应用到四种重要类别的工程问题中。同时将基本的SIP模型扩展到有着多层次保真度和功能输出的模型实验。并将会考虑SIP在优化和稳健参数设计(RPD: Robust Parameter Design)中的应用 本次项目提出了创新，灵活并强有力的统计方法，来实现多项式插值。随着社会中对多项式元模型不确定性量化的广泛接受和使用，上述提出的方法将会对工程领域做出重要的贡献。

21201414.value: Objective 1 has been achieved with the publication of Article#1 and Article#2. In Article#1, an early version of SIP based on Bayesian regression with orthonormal polynomials is proposed. In Article#2, a Bayesian model for polynomial interpolation with orthonormal polynomials, called the SIP, is proposed. The model interpolates the experiment data in deterministic computer experiments and gives prediction intervals that quantify interpolation uncertainty. The SIP is found to have a significant advantage over the traditional Gaussian process (GP) model, i.e., computational ease in obtaining the functional ANOVA and variance decompositions. As follow-up work to SIP, the PI also worked on construction of monotonic and other shape constrained metamodels for computer experiments. As shape constrained problems cannot be handled well with the standard stationary GP model, the PI developed more suitable methods for those problems. Work in this area resulted in the publication of Article#4, Article #8, and Article #10. Article#4 and Article #8 provide methods for constructing monotonic metamodels. 21201414.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201414.value: In this project, statistical methodologies for designing and analyzing computer experiments using interpolating polynomials were developed. Multivariate orthogonal polynomial metamodels are useful in computer experiments due to their readily computable functional ANOVA decomposition and interpretability. For deterministic simulators, interpolating polynomials should be used instead of noninterpolating ones for logical consistency and prediction accuracy. To predict at unobserved input points, the standard interpolating polynomial metamodel gives point predictions but not prediction intervals or measures of prediction uncertainty. While error bounds are available in the mathematics literature, they depend on the unknown function being interpolated, and are therefore, not useful in practice. Moreover, due to the lack of random error in the data, the use of standard regression methods to fit a polynomial metamodel and obtain point and interval predictions lacks statistical validity. However, probabilistic statements about interpolation errors are crucial for assessing the impact of these errors on decision-making. This project develops a stochastic interpolating polynomial model based on a rigorous Bayesian framework. The model interpolates the experiment data almost surely and provides prediction intervals for unobserved input sites. In addition, an adaptive scheme for adding design points based on the predictive distribution at unobserved sites can be used, which yields a more accurate model than fixed designs. The proposed model or its variants are applied to global sensitivity analysis, multiobjective optimization, and robust parameter design. It is demonstrated that they yield analytical formulas for point and interval estimates of the functional ANOVA components, and variances of the functional ANOVA components. In contrast, computing the functional ANOVA components of the standard stationary Gaussian process (GP) model for deterministic computer experiments involves the computation of multidimensional integrals. Apart from some special cases, these multidimensional integrals cannot be computed analytically and thus, a numerical method or Monte Carlo simulation must be used, which is a tedious process subject to nonnegligible numerical errors. This project also makes important contributions to the development of monotonic and other shape constrained metamodels, which are problems that cannot be dealt with effectively by standard GP models since it is only possible to constrain their predictions on a finite point set. Monotonic Bernstein polynomial and B-spline models are developed for monotonic simulators, and a boundary constrained GP model is developed for incorporating boundary information. Finally, the project develops methodologies for integrated parameter and tolerance design with time consuming simulators, which is an important engineering problem.

21201414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201414.value: There are many areas with potential for further development. The first is computationally efficient methods to fit the stochastic interpolating polynomial when the number of data points is large and/or the dimension of the input space is high. These “big data” problems are increasingly important as computer models are becoming more complex, which causes the number of inputs to be large, and computing power is becoming cheaply available, which allows more simulation data to be obtained. The curse of dimensionality problem can be mitigated by selecting only the variables or functional bases with largest effects to be included in the model, and large datasets can be handled with the use of piecewise polynomial bases like B-spline bases that have compact support since they yield sparse coefficient matrices. More research is needed in the choice of design points for fitting the stochastic interpolating polynomial. Conditions for verifying the optimality of the design need to be establish, which may lead to new interesting mathematical theory. Finally, it is of interest to try the stochastic interpolating polynomial model, monotonic models based on Bernstein and B-spline bases, and boundary constrained model developed in this project on more time-consuming computer simulation problems encountered in practice.

21201414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201414.value: In this project, statistical methodologies for designing computer simulation experiments and analyzing data from the experiments using interpolating polynomials were developed. Multivariate orthogonal polynomial models are computationally efficient and interpretable tools for analysis of simulation data. However, existing versions of these models cannot provide a probabilistic measure of prediction uncertainty, which are crucial for assessing the impact of prediction errors on decision-making. This project develops a stochastic interpolating polynomial model based on a rigorous Bayesian approach that provides prediction intervals for unobserved input sites. The proposed model is applied to general statistical engineering problems in computer simulations like global sensitivity analysis, multiobjective optimization, and robust parameter design. It is demonstrated that they allow these problems to be solved analytically, which is a significant advantage over standard stationary Gaussian process (GP) models that requires the computation of multidimensional integrals. This project also makes important contributions to the development of monotonic and other shape constrained models that cannot be dealt with effectively by standard GP models. Monotonic and boundary constrained models are developed. Finally, the project also develops methodologies for optimizing parameters and tolerances of an engineering design based on computer simulations, which is an important engineering problem.

21201514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201514.value: Having the potential for low-cost and high-efficiency, organic photovoltaic (OPV) cells have attracted lots of attention during the last decade. Although OPV has already achieved power conversion efficiency (PCE) comparable to that of the amorphous-silicon (a-Si) based PV, challenges still remain on transferring the laboratory to manufacturing processes and further improving the device efficiency. For the later, understanding the loss mechanism in OPV is of the utmost importance for developing more efficient materials and device architectures. In OPVs, the electronic properties at the donor-acceptor interface play a significant role in determining the device efficiency. It is recently proposed that charge-transfer (CT) states at the organic heterojunctions are necessary and intermediate steps for charge dissociation. Depending on the energy profile of the CT states, the excitons will either be recombined or dissociated into free charges. However, correlation between the energy profile of CT states and the charge dissociation rate in PV devices has never been reported. The challenges mainly due to the lack of standard experimental approach to probe the energy profile of such low-density CT states, and the technique to pinpoint the states those are responsible for efficient charge dissociation. In this proposed research, we are aiming at determining the role of charge-transfer states on charge dissociation in organic photovoltaic materials. We will develop a new approach by combing the charge-modulated electroabsorption spectroscopy (CMEAS) and photothermal deflection spectroscopy (PDS) to probes the CT states in OPV devices. We will then correlate the spectroscopy results with the charge dissociation results on a series of OPV materials. Our objectives are to: 1) Develop a methodology to investigate the CT states in organic heterojunction devices; 2) Establish a correlation between the energy profile of CT states and the charge dissociation efficiency in devices; 3) Establish a correlation between material properties and CT states in different organic heterojunctions; 4) Explore the theoretical model of charge dissociation in OPVs. The success of this project would not only bring insight into developing more efficient photovoltaic devices, but more fundamentally the charge transfer process in organic electronic materials. 基于低成本，高效率等优点，在过去十年里，有机太阳能电池（OPV）倍受关注。虽然OPV的光电转换效率已可与非晶硅基PV媲美，但实现产业化及进一步提高效率依然是OPV面临的最大挑战。就后者而言，了解OPV能量损失的机理是提高器件效率的关键。 在OPVs中，给受体界面的电学性质，对器件效率的影响发挥着重要的作用。最近，有研究指出，在有机异质结界面产生的电荷转移（CT）态是电荷分离必经的中间态。根据对CT态能级分布的研究，在界面形成的激子，既可发生复合亦可分离形成自由电荷。然而，目前针对PV器件中CT态能级分布与电荷分离速率之间关系的研究尚未出现。其中，最主要的挑战是缺少用于检测低密度CT态能级分布的标准实验手段，以及准确描述CT态是引起电荷有效分离关键的技术。 本项目将针对有机光伏材料中电荷转移（CT）态对电荷分离的影响展开研究。通过结合电场调制吸收谱（CMEAS）和光热偏转光谱（PDS），开发一种新的实验手段，用于探测研究OPV器件中的CT态。本项目的目标旨在：1）开发一种研究有机异质节器件中CT态的方法；2）建立电荷分离效率与CT态能级分布之间的关系；3）建立不同有机异质节中CT态与材料性质之间的关系；4）创建OPVs中电荷分离的理论模型。 本项目的成功，不仅能为开发更高效率的光伏器件提供技术指导，而且能从本质上了解有机光电材料电荷转移过程。

21201514.label: Realisation of objectives
21201514.value: O1: To develop experimental approach to investigate the CT states in organic heterojunction devices. (100% achieved) We had successfully developed two highly sensitive techniques to probe the charge transfer (CT) states at organic heterojunction devices. One of them was a highly sensitive quantum efficiency measurement setup, which we achieved a sensitivity down to 10-5%. This is among the lowest reported in literature. Such high sensitivity was achieved by a combination of high power light source, lock-in technique, and optical and electrical filtering components. Those are purchased by the funding from the proposed project. Another experimental setup we had developed was the charge modulated electroabsorption spectroscopy (CMEAS). This technique provides a very high sensitive measure of optical changes in the presence of charge-transfer states that cannot be measured by typical UV-vis technique. CMEAS technique was developed in combination of electrical and optical modulation techniques and components, those were supported by this proposed project. Details of the application of the two techniques have been published in Tsang et al., J. Phys. Chem. C 2016, 120, 14059−14068. O2: To perform an ensemble of experiments on different donor-acceptor material systems, and to establish a correlation between the energy profile of CT states and the charge dissociation in OPV materials (100% achieved) We had performed measurement on more than ten commonly used organic donor-acceptor materials and successfully correlated the energy profile of CT states with the exciton dissociation efficiency. Briefly, we found that the CT states energy was correlated to the energy level arrangement between the donor and acceptor materials. Larger the CT energy facilitates larger open-circuit voltage in corresponding photovoltaic devices. However, the large CT energy would reduce the charge dissociation efficiency. The knowledge and technique acquired from this study had been applied in various materials systems and successfully published in several peer reviewed journals. A detailed study on the energy profile of CT states can be found in Tsang et al., J. Phys. Chem. C. 120, 14059 (2016). O3: To establish a correlation between material properties and CT states for future development of efficient PV materials. (100% achieved) Using the two techniques developed in this project, we had successfully probed the CT states in more than ten different organic heterojunctions. More importantly, we had found different physical properties (polarizability and delocalization) in various heterojunctions responsible for exciton dissociation in organic solar cells. Particularly, by probing the frequency response of the CT states by CMEAS in different materials systems, we found that the CT states in more efficient heterojunction systems were able to catch up the high frequency modulation. On the other hand, the CMEAS signal diminished in less efficient system at high frequency regime. This new finding provides a deeper insight into the charge/exciton dissociation mechanism in CT states. Details of the findings can be found in our publication in Tsang et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 8 (33), 21798, (2016), and ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 10, 7256−7262 (2018). O4: To explore the theoretical model to describe the charge dissociation in OPV with the consideration of CT states. (100% achieved) By using CMEAS, we observed that the polarizability of excitonic states of donor materials can be significantly increased by blending with n-type acceptors, which is different from previous opinion that Frenkel excitons are the same in pristine donor and in D/A blend systems. This highly polarized exciton is easier to dissociate and contribute to free charge carriers according to the Onsager model. In addition, by comparing several organic semiconductor systems, we find that the dielectric effect of organic semiconductor films is directly determined by the polarizability of excitons rather than that of the interfacial CT states. Our finding reveals an important role of the polarizability of excitons in photoinduced charge separation process. It suggests possible approaches for designing D/A systems for improving the excitonic polarization and more effective carrier dissociation. Details of the findings can be found in our publication in Tsang et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 10, 7256−7262 (2018).

21201514.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201514.value: In this project, we have successfully developed two highly sensitive techniques (quantum efficiency spectroscopy and charge modulated electroabsorption spectroscopy Ref.[7]. We find that the energy level alignment between the organic donor and acceptor materials in a bulk heterojunction plays a key role in determining the charge transfer (CT) state energy and corresponding dissociation efficiency. Ref[1,4,6,7] More importantly, for the first time, we find out that the different polarizability and delocalization of the CT states by CMEAS which has direct correlation with the exciton dissociation at the organic heterojunction.Ref[8,9]. In addition, by comparing the exciton polarization in pristine polymers and blend heterojunctions, we find that the previous Frenkel type model in describing the excitation species in blended system is questionable. Ref[10] On the other hand, by comparing several organic semiconductor systems, we find that the dielectric effect of organic semiconductor films is directly determined by the polarizability of excitons rather than that of the interfacial CT states that has been widely proposed in literature.

21201514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201514.value: The developed research and findings in this project can potential applied to the recent newly developed high efficiency organic solar cell with small energy loss. Although high efficiency over 14% has been reported, it is still unclear how observed small energy offset between the donor-acceptor can facilitate efficient charge dissociation. It is proposed that using CMEAS and highly sensitive EQE, which can both extract the energy profile and dynamic of the CT state would potential bring insight into the unsolved working principle of this newly developed materials system.

21201514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201514.value: This UGC funded project facilitates the development of unique sensitive characterization techniques to unlock the working principle of organic solar cells. The developed techniques allow the access of the key physical process of charge separation at the organic electron donating and accepting materials interface, which cannot be achieved by conventional techniques. Through this project, the team has discovered that there is significant modification of the materials, namely the exciton polarizability, once the donor and acceptor materials bring into contact. This discovery provides valuable insight in explaining several key unsolved issues regarding the working principle of recently developed high efficiency organic solar cells.

21201714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201714.value: With millions of users worldwide, cloud providers deploy geo-distributed datacenters to support Internet-scale services. Wide area networks (WANs) are the critical underpinning of such an infrastructure. Architecturally, a provider operates two WANs: a user-facing WAN that connects users with datacenters, and a backbone WAN that provides connectivity among datacenters. As cloud services proliferate, how to manage and orchestrate the sheer amount of traffic flowing across datacenter WANs becomes a pressing yet challenging issue. The main thesis of this proposal is to explore elasticity as a new degree of freedom for traffic management in datacenter WANs. Specifically, for the user-facing WAN, traffic management needs to route user requests to datacenters for processing. The common approach is to consider geographical diversity of energy prices, and balance the tradeoff between user latency and energy cost. We propose to consider another kind of datacenter workloads, batch jobs, and their inherent elasticity. By reducing capacity for batch jobs we can make room at cost efficient locations for request routing to provide more cost saving. We will further consider elasticity of interactive requests, by allowing partial execution to trade small response quality degradation for reduced energy use given the concave quality–processing time curve. For the backbone WAN, traffic management needs to make routing decisions, i.e. traffic engineering. We will explore the elasticity of bulky replication traffic for rate control as a new control knob. Since the provider owns the applications and servers in addition to routers, it can adjust flow sending rate according to the network state for improved performance. Our objective is to systematically investigate and prototype novel traffic management solutions with elasticity taken into account. We will develop optimization frameworks to capture essential tradeoffs in each scenario and maximize efficiency. For practicality, we will draw upon the recent advancement in the alternating direction method of multipliers to devise novel distributed optimization algorithms. These algorithms are massively parallelizable to solve cloud-scale problems with millions of variables efficiently. We will use both testbed implementation with software prototypes and simulations with empirical traces for realistic performance evaluation. The research results can be readily adopted by industry for managing their user-facing and backbone networks with salient cost saving and performance improvement. The results will also appeal to a wide audience in optimization and networking communities, and may even be applicable to large-scale convex optimization problems with big data in machine learning, data mining, and other domains. 為了服務遍佈全球數百萬用戶，雲服務運營商部署了地域分佈式的數據中心。廣域網（WAN）則是其中一個關鍵基礎。在結構上，運營商經營兩個廣域網：一個面向用戶的廣域網，連接用戶與數據中心；另一個廣域骨幹網，提供數據中心之間的連接。隨著雲服務的激增，如何管理和協調廣域網巨大的流量量成為一個緊迫而具有挑戰性的問題。 該方案的主要論點是，探索流量彈性作為一個新的自由度在數據中心流量管理的應用。具體而言，對於面向用戶的廣域網，流量管理需要路由用戶請求到數據中心進行處理。常見的方法是考慮能源價格的地域多樣性，並平衡用戶等待時間和能源成本。我們建議考慮另一種工作負載－－批作業，以及其固有的彈性。通過減少對批處理作業能力，我們可以騰出空間在成本高效的地點請求路由，節約更多的成本。我們會進一步考慮交互請求的彈性，允許部分執行請求以減少能源使用。對於骨幹廣域網，流量管理需要做出路由決策，即流量工程。我們將探索龐大的數據備份流量中的彈性。由於運營商完全控制著應用程序，服務器，和路由器，它可以根據網絡狀態自由調節流量的發送速率來提升性能。 我們的目標是系統地研究和實現這些創新的流量管理解決方案。我們將開發優化問題框架，以捕捉每個中必不可少的權衡，最大限度地提高效率。處於實用性的考慮，我們將利用最近的ADMM算法，發展新的分佈式優化算法。這些算法可以大規模並行化計算以解決多達幾百萬變量級別的問題。我們將用原型實現和模擬實驗來真實評估我們的算法。我們的研究結果可以很容易地被工業界採用，為其面向用戶廣域網和骨幹廣域網絡提供顯著的成本節約和性能改進。我們相信這些結果也將在優化和網絡等領域吸引廣大同行關注。我們的算法甚至可以適用於在機器學習大數據，數據挖掘，和其他領域的大型凸優化問題。

21201714.label: Realisation of objectives
21201714.value: 1. We have developed a general optimization framework for traffic management problems in geo-distributed data centers, based on distributed ADMM. We have extended the framework with joint rate control and routing, and developed novel distributed ADMM algorithms as well as its convergence proof. We have published a journal paper that summarizes the main results at IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems in 2017. This corresponds to objectives 1, 2, and 4. 2. We have explored the elasticity of both batch and interactive workloads in data centers to reduce the energy cost of data centers, and extended the optimization framework developed above to solve the new problem. The results are published at the top conference in energy area, ACM SIGCOMM International Conference on Future Energy Systems (ACM e-Energy) in 2014. In addition, we have also explored the elasticity of workloads for water saving in geo-distributed data centers. The results are published in IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing in 2018. This corresponds to objectives 3 and 1. 3. Summarizing the work described above, the PI believes all objectives have been achieved within the project duration.

21201714.value: 1. We have developed a general optimization framework for traffic management problems in geo-distributed data centers, based on ADMM. We have developed novel distributed ADMM algorithms as well as its convergence proof. We have published a journal paper at IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems in 2017. 2. We have explored the elasticity of workloads in data centers to reduce the energy cost of data centers, and published a paper in ACM SIGCOMM International Conference on Future Energy Systems (ACM e-Energy) 2014. 21201714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201714.value: The optimization framework and the distributed ADMM algorithms developed in this project has many potential applications in computer networking. So long as the problem can be casted into our formulation, the algorithms can be applied to solve it in a distributed fashion with fast convergence. This can also lead to efficient distributed protocol design. In addition, many machine learning training problems are inherently optimization problems in nature, and our algorithms may be applied to develop new distributed training methods.

21201714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201714.value: This project focuses on traffic management in data centers. The topic is timely and important because data centers are the backbone infrastructure that empower almost all of the big data, mobile, and machine learning workloads that our life now relies on. Networking is a critical component in data centers as it moves data across the wide-area transoceanic links which are extremely expensive. We explore the elasticity of some common datacenter workloads, such as interactive queries and batch processing, to facilitate the wide-area traffic management. We took a principled approach and developed a mathematical optimization framework to model the problems. We proposed novel distributed algorithms to solve these problems based on a technique called ADMM, alternating direction method of multipliers. Our results have potential to be applied in various traffic management in real-world data centers.

21201914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201914.value: 該研究項目擬開發新的快速和強大密集的通信算法。密集對應的估計是計算機視覺很基本的任務，並發現廣泛應用在諸如立體匹配，光流估計，視頻跟踪，視覺識別，以及攝像機標定的許多任務。然而，傳統的通信算法不健壯照明，攝像機和曝光的變化。他們的表現是低點閉塞和低紋理區域，計算複雜度高。 我們建議，調查內容大致如下方向的密集通信問題： 線性時間光照不變性密集對應的估計。 我們建議開發高效密集的相應算法魯棒性，既局部和全局光照仿射交流。要研究制定仿射的計算變換中間人每兩個本地補丁圖片作為圖像去噪問題解決了，可以有效地利用圖像技術過濾。轉換後的圖像亮度值可以為密集的對應估計相似度現有措施一體化。 閉塞感知密集對應的估計。 我們建議開發新的高效率和強大的邊緣感知的圖像的技術，並在建議對應的算法來處理阻塞過濾整合他們。從參考圖片中的樹狀結構將是農業和提取的用於過濾的指導。所得過濾器會自動邊緣識別，並能有效地降低周圍閉塞不正確的對應關係估計。 茂密的通信算法的項目定量評估。 一些基準測試與測量任不同的有源傳感器或合成為此獲得地面實況對應的運動具備的，已經開發了如立體匹配和光流估計特定的計算機視覺任務。擬議密集的通信算法將定量評價論文的標準。但是內容，每一個這些標準都有其自身的局限性。我們建議制定一般對應估計的新標杆。它可以種地績效評估和自動參數選擇由 - 其他研究人員開發密集的通信算法。 一些在這個建議的初步研究結果發表在IEEE會議計算機視覺和模式識別（CVPR）2009年，2010年，2012年和2013年，計算機視覺（ECCV）歐洲會議2012年在IEEE交易模式分析程序與機器智能（TPAMI）2009和2013年。
