21401214.label: Major findings and research outcome
21401214.value: The current project successfully demonstrated that narratives can vividly model health threats in a connected manner and is more effective than the conventional didactic approach in enhancing high-risk groups’ threat perceptions. When controlling all the covariates, narrative PSA produced significant greater perception of severity and susceptibility than the didactic and control conditions. Such effects were further moderated by an individual’s health literacy. Individuals with lower health literacy benefitted more from the narrative messages while individuals with higher health literacy find the narrative and didactic messages equally effective. However, narrative PSA and didactic PSA are equally effective in influencing perceptions of efficacy beliefs and behavioral intention. The study also followed up the participants in their actual uptake behavior three months after the experiment. There was no significant difference across three experimental conditions in terms of either self-vaccination or influencing vulnerable others. In other words, the narrative approach, by modelling series of negative events in influenza contamination, was more effective in enhancing threat perceptions about influenza than the didactic presentation of influenza-related information. On the other hand, the narrative approach did not appear superior to the didactic approach in changing efficacy beliefs, probably because our storyline emphasized the interrelated negative events and was too subtle in presenting the efficacy particularly response efficacy of vaccination. Indeed, it has always been difficult to portray the response efficacy in vaccination advocacy. Unlike other health behaviors that can produce highly visible outcomes (e.g., physical exercises), the effectiveness of vaccination is invisible. In the case of seasonal influenza, people usually cannot recognize the mutation nature of influenza virus and further perceive vaccine as “not very effective’ because they need to take a new shot every year. This insignificant effect on efficacy perceptions to some extent contributed to the lack of evidence in enhancing behavioral intent and actual uptake, given that health behavior theories widely consider efficacy as a predictor to behavior enactment. Another possible explanation is that the sample size is not enough to capture the persuasive effect. Previous meta-analyses have revealed a relatively small effect size for the impact of narrative persuasion, and vary by health issues (Shen, Sheer, & Li, 2015). In the current study, the effect size of narratives on threat perceptions also appeared to be relatively small, which similarly suggested a possibility of lack of statistical power.

21401214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21401214.value: Albeit its effectiveness in enhancing high-risk groups’ threat perceptions, the current project failed to provide an effective template for developing effective storylines for emphasizing efficacy and behavioral enactment in the context of influenza vaccination promotion. Future research should focus on the message design dedicated to efficacy-enhancing strategies, in particularly for health protection behaviors like vaccination which do not have explicit health outcomes when in effect. Positive events need to be depicted in reasonable and explicit manners to achieve better persuasive effects. Future study should continue to look at the role of health literacy and health knowledge with more sophisticated research design because the current investigation clearly pointed out some unsolved issues in understanding the mechanisms of narratives. Beside trait factors, situational factors in message processing also deserve attention. Future research should go beyond the simple conceptualization of message enjoyment to look at deeper media psychological constructs such as transportation and identification in local contexts.

21401214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21401214.value: Story is the basic unit for people to understand, memorize and use information. In the context of health communication, scholars argue that storytelling, or in a more academic definition – narratives, is capable of influencing people health beliefs, opinions, and behaviors. The current study focused on the power of narratives in changing beliefs and behaviors about influenza vaccination, which has long been a critical problem in Hong Kong’s public health arena. The study introduced narratives as a useful tool to promote influenza vaccination and tried to demonstrate its applicability in the context of Hong Kong by comparing its effects against a commonly-used information-based method as well as a no-message condition. The study successfully demonstrated the persuasive capacity of narratives by producing culturally grounded stories on influenza prevention and vaccination promotion. It empirically showed that narratives can vividly model health threats in stories that are easy to understand, and therefore is more effective in influencing high-risk groups particularly groups with limited health literacy.

21401414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21401414.value: 影像是一種主導的展示方式。IMAX及3D電影院的大屏幕上不能夠完全展示文學作品所表達的內容。在電影上，語言被局限於字幕及片尾；在廣告上，文字以口號及標誌的形式展示。通過擴展已在數碼文獻及rectilinear CAVE 沉浸式領域中廣泛的研究，本項目擬在 360度的曲面閱讀環境中填補這文化上的隔閡。 與此同時，觀眾不只是以英語作為母語。經常有部份觀眾的語言能力不足。在這之後，他們需要翻譯。簡而言之，雖然大部份國際的觀眾懂多於一種語言，但他們偏向使用自己的母語來理解文字。 在香港城市大學創意媒體學院8樓，有一個360度影院（由Jeffrey Shaw教授開發）。該影院利用5個3D（stereoscopic）投影機及環迴立體聲，在一個直徑十米、約兩個人高的柱面屏幕上建立了一個互動沉浸式的環境。這不是一本書，不是一幅卷軸，也不是一個CAVE；但它的展示系統有著強大的能力，讓作家有新的表達模式，讀者亦能與文字進行互動。 本研究探索曲面互動3D空間裝置的可行性，為創意寫作及閱讀提供一個雙語的文化環境。

21401414.label: Realisation of objectives
21401414.value: 1. Our research team successfully adapted the animation text engine (developed under MILK start-up grant) for bilingual Cantonese and English display. What we learned was that the constraints of the 360 grant environment defined a tightly formulated path. Numerous text activities and special effects proved to be untenable given the master computer and subsidiary computer relation, which recompiled and redistributed the source Unity code in order to perform geometry correction and edge-blending. This necessary interception between the core server and the multiple projection setup resulted in numerous bugs which deflected capacity to implement complex effects. In order to evade this tight set of constraints, a multiple screen image sequence with transparency was attempted. This led to an effective display but an inefficient file size with extreme latency in distributing to the clients (each of which feed a separate projector). So in order to compensate, the organic solution was to use the affordances and constraints of the system: one path was to create custom textures wrapped around custom geometry; for this we chose to emulate boulders-rock-stones which are the orginary point for all language, — the result was etched stones and steles of ancient times mobilised in a multimedia immersive theatre. The other path was to implement a total separation between surface text effects created in After Effects and the 3D world. This proved to be both an advance and an impediment: the process bifurcated, work doubled, but the visual impact allowed for an animation text engine combining Cantonese and English into a single display. The separation between text and rendered models enabled tactile and handheld interactivity. The game controller button process was implemented to allow transitions between scenes. In addition to dynamic video behind text, we added dynamic 3D rendered worlds, complete with 3D geometry mapped/wrapped text. This process worked well in both 2D and with active 3D stereoscopic projection. With the addition of audio, 3D audio-reactive letterforms were created from the texture-wrapped boulders. The core idea of voxel morphs was implemented by animating transforms between radicals of Chinese characters, using the English as subtext to drive tangential meanings. Proofs of each these processes are documented in video form on the project website at http://curved.glia.ca 2. In early 2015, I invited the local Hong Kong poets, Ng Mei Kwan (Chinese community coordinator, poet) and Collier Nogues ( English community coordinator, poet). Their presence enabled the team to develop a process that enables literary authors to create and deploy literary language-art within the 360 Gallery or other immersive cinemas. Documentation of this process is online along with some of the comment based conversations among the team, and the texts developed and translated. Where the research project encountered difficulties was in developing tools to give authors independent access to develop 360 literary art autonomously. The density of code required to develop authentically different structures independently (without the assistance of a programmer) was beyond the capacity of our poet collaborators. Yet with the assistance of our talented programmer, working together in the 360, we rapidly prototyped numerous experiments, deploying bilingual text into stereoscopic 3D environments. 3. This team-engaged process led to (what we feel) is precedent-setting multimedia language-art work (made with the custom software developed to enable its deployment) for an immersive 3D stereoscopic 360-degree space. This work combined dual language distributed networks of text styled in numerous ways over particle systems of boulders texture-wrapped in text-etched. We distributed that work by: i. 21401414.label: Major findings and research outcome
21401414.value: At the wider sociocultural level relating to parallel cultures and languages, the research ( understood from the feedback of numerous viewers and the 82 students who filled the post-exhibit questionnaire ) revealed that the usage of simultaneous bilingual Chinese and English typographic explorations within the immersive cinema allows for a new form of reading. One where a tension bifurcates yet ultimately consolidates upon the primary language. Each viewer can choose to read a single path, while others operate in a kind of binoculars rivalry oscillating between the two languages and the multimedia layers in order to arrive at a radically transformed mode of reading that encapsulates the entire body of the viewer. Literature in immersive environments operates in a liminal zone between cinema, screen, game, and printed material. Our exploration of the technology clearly demonstrated that at the current evolutionary stage of 3D immersive cinematic experiences, it is impractical and implausible to expect an ordinary literary practitioner to have the technical capacities necessary to adopt their artistic creation for this very technical cinematic environment without a small dedicated team and a set of techniques (some of which our research provides). One of the core key research outcomes is to reinforce awareness that immersive cinema literature experiences require teamwork in the same way that cinematic processes such as making a film require teams.

21401414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21401414.value: This process has implications for the future of language education, media arts, literary practice, film credits, and gaming VR. The capacity to simultaneously witness reconfigurations of two or more languages on a large immersive screen controlled by the viewer suggest a variety of future paths. The pedagogical impact of such technology could be vast allowing for nuanced control of a lot of linguistic data. On another level the artistic potentials of this technology allow for a rich wider engaged experience more appropriate to the network multimedia preferences of digital natives. In short the research generates a clear prototype for the bilingual delivery of literature to large groups of viewers whose language capacity is split for overlaps across primary languages.

21401414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21401414.value: The CURVED research explores the future of reading where large 3D screens wrap around the viewer, where words mutate and fly, where words and texts combine with video, sounds and interactivity. Specifically it creates cinematic experiences that involve reading poetry made for bilingual audiences: both languages are displayed at once in an immersive 360 cylinder screen-gallery using 5 synchronised projectors and active 3D shutter glasses. Interactivity control of the reading occurs using a simple game controller. Reading for the 21st century emerges: active engaged interactive audio-visual. The implications of the research extend into both education (language learning) and arts (VR documentaries, fiction and the future of literature).

21402414.label: Major findings and research outcome

21402414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21402414.value: This projects examines Japan's foreign intelligence system. It focuses, in particular, on the agencies comprising the country's intelligence community and the methods they have adopted to gather information on economic, political and military developments abroad. This project is the first study to examine comprehensively Japanese foreign intelligence activities across the economic, political and military domains. An exploration of this hitherto neglected topic provides a guide to understanding the country's broader security policy changes over the past two decades, as well as national perceptions of its place within the Asia-Pacific region.

21402514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21402514.value: 此研究針對廣東話單字詞產生的認知機制。廣東話是華南的主要方言。此研究包括四個採用圖詞干擾命名範式的實驗，以研究音段(次音節與音節單位)與超音段(聲調)訊息在廣東話單字詞產生中的加工過程。在每個圖詞干擾命名的實驗中，廣東話被試需要對每幅單獨呈現的圖片作出即時命名並要忽略伴隨圖片的聽覺干擾字詞。圖片與干擾字詞會同時或依次呈現。此研究的結果有兩個重要的理論貢獻，一者關於現時主要從非聲調語發展出的語言產生理論的普世性，二者關於使用聲調語中的特殊性。應用方面，此研究的結果將對改善聲調語使用者的發音，以及對聲調語的教學提供重要啟示。

21402514.label: Realisation of objectives
21402514.value: The three project objectives listed above have been achieved within the proposed time frame. Four experiments were conducted to investigate how Cantonese speakers retrieve phonological information in spoken word production by using the classical picture-word interference task. In addition, the results of the proposed experiments have provided pilot data for follow up experiments on related issues about the mechanisms of Chinese spoken word production. Details are discussed in the following. Objective 1: Participants’ picture naming responses were faster, relative to an unrelated condition, when the target and distractor shared the same syllable (with or without the same lexical tone). The priming effect became weaker when the target and distractor shared only the same sub-syllabic components (e.g., rhyme, syllable body, or onset consonant + coda). These results indicated that syllables and sub-syllabic constituents are legitimate phonological processing units in Cantonese speech production. The size of priming observed was largest in the syllable related condition, followed by syllable body related condition, rhyme related condition, and then onset+coda related condition. In addition, the present project provided data showing that the effect of syllable priming occurred earlier than that of sub-syllabic priming, indicating that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic specification in Cantonese phonological encoding. In Cantonese spoken word production, the entire atonal syllable (syllable without the tone specified) is retrieved first followed by a serial encoding process (from left to right) of its sub-syllabic components. Objective 2: Null effects were observed when the target and distractor shared only the same lexical tone. However, the effect of tone was shown together with other segmental components. For instance, the priming effect of the syllable+tone related condition was significantly larger than that of the syllable (without the same tone) alone related condition. This non-additive pattern indicated that 1) tone has a role to play in Cantonese phonological encoding, and 2) there is interactivity between syllable retrieval and tonal processing. There is no clear evidence from this project indicating that tone is processed interactively with sub-syllabic components in Cantonese speech production. Objective 3: The present project provided data showing an earlier effect of syllable priming than sub-syllabic priming, indicating that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic encoding in Cantonese speech production. In addition, a significant interaction between syllable relatedness and tonal relatedness was found at early SOAs (-150 ms and 0 ms) but not in the late SOA (150 ms), indicating that lexical tones are processed interactively with syllable retrieval at the early stage of phonological encoding, followed by sub-syllabic specification.

21402514.label: Major findings and research outcome
21402514.value: Major findings of the research endeavors supported by the current project are highlighted in the following. 1) Syllables and sub-syllabic components both are legitimate phonological units in Cantonese spoken word production, consistent with the previous studies conducted by PI (Wong 2010, Wong & Chen, 2008, 2009, 2015). 2) The effects of syllable priming observed were generally larger and appeared earlier than that of sub-syllabic priming, suggesting that the syllable unit has a superior role to play than its sub-syllabic constituents, and that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic encoding in Chinese spoken word production (relevant findings have been reported in Wang, Wong et al., 2017, and Wong et al., under review, as listed in Part C). This finding is novel and important. Given many existing prominent models of speech production assume that phonemes are the basic and primary phonological processing units (Dell, 1986; Levelt et al., 1999; Rapp & Goldrick, 2000), findings from the current project do not support this assumption. Instead, the current findings are consistent with the view that the primary phonological unit is language-specific. In Chinese speech production, the primary (first retrievable) phonological unit is atonal syllable but not phoneme (Wang, Wong et al., 2017, Wong et at., under review). 3) Robust priming effects were observed when both the syllable unit and the tone of the target word were primed together. Encoding of the syllable units in Cantonese word production works in a serial right-ward manner with the first syllable+tone unit encoded first followed by the second syllable+tone unit. Encoding of the first syllable unit occurs at approximately 44-ms prior to the encoding of the second syllable unit (see Wong et al., 2016 listed in Part C). 4) By using the same picture-work interference task with concurrent EEG signal recording, efforts have been made to locate the time course of phonological encoding relative to semantic processing in Chinese spoken word production. Robust and very early semantic effects have been observed, whereas the phonological effects appeared relatively weak and late (see Wong et al., 2017, as listed in Part C). This finding is in general consistent with the view that semantic processing begins earlier than phonological encoding in spoken word production.

21402514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21402514.value: Findings of the current project have laid an important ground for further development of the research on language production. It has been shown that the picture-word interference task is a useful task to reveal the phonological encoding processes in speech production. More importantly, it has provided pilot data showing that this overt picture naming task can possibly be combined with concurrent EEG signal recording. With its exceptionally high temporal resolution, the EEG data can reflect the fine-grained temporal dynamics of the mechanisms underlying speech production. This research idea has been further developed into two GRF proposals, one was awarded in the 2015-16 exercise (CityU 11673316), and one was submitted in the 2017-18 exercise (results pending). The current project has shown some interesting results which are probably language-specific. For instance, the robust and early effect of the syllable unit in phonological encoding is probably specific to the Chinese language. However, the underlying neural mechanism sub-serving this potential cross-language difference is still a largely open issue. Future studies can be conducted to investigate the roles of syllable and sub-syllabic units in phonological planning across substantially different languages (e.g., Chinese, English, and Japanese) by combining an overt speech production task with concurrent EEG recording.

21402514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21402514.value: This project aims at investigating how Chinese speakers retrieve phonological information in spoken word production by using an experimental approach. The current findings indicate that syllables, sub-syllabic components, and lexical tones are all legitimate phonological processing units in Chinese speech production. Specifically, the effects of syllable have been found to be stronger and earlier than that of sub-syllabic units, indicating that the entire syllable is retrieved first prior to its sub-syllabic constituents. The effect of tone was shown only upon the condition where the segmental syllable of the target word has also been primed. These findings are not consistent with the long-held assumption in the language production literature that phonemes are the primary phonological units in phonological planning. In contrast, the present findings are consistent with the view that syllables are the primary phonological units in Chinese and that the nature of the primary phonological unit in speech production is language-specific. Theoretically, findings of the current project offered important insights to the on-going debate in the psycho-linguistic literature regarding the language-universal versus language-specific aspects of the language production processes. Practically, the current findings highlight the importance of the syllable units in the teaching and learning of the Chinese spoken languages.

21402714.value: 中國農村愛滋病患者的抗逆力和抑鬱症狀的縱向分析

21402714.label: Project Objectives
21402714.value: Based on the ecological model (Figure 1), we will begin with the traditional approach at the individual level, and go on to expand to the spouse level, and then to the family level. We will examine i) whether baseline (T1) resilience at the individual level is associated with low levels of PLHIV DS at T1 and the one-year follow-up (T2) (Hypothesis 1a); ii) whether T1 spouse resilience adds independent variance over and above individual factors in predicting low levels of PLHIV DS at T1 and T2 (Hypothesis 1b); iii) whether T1 family resilience is associated with low levels of PLHIV DS at T1 and T2, after controlling for the individual and spouse characteristics (Hypothesis 1c); iv) whether T1 spouse and family resilience have effects on T2 PLHIV DS through the effect of enhancing PLHIV resilience from T1 to T2 (indirect effect, Hypothesis 1d, Figure 2); and v) whether these associations between T1 resilience at different levels and T2 PLHIV DS are stronger when PLHIV experience high levels of stress at T1 (moderation, Hypothesis 1e, Figure 3). By using data of the dyadic sample, we will i) examine the congruence in DS within couples, both concurrently and over time (Hypothesis 2a, Figure 4); ii) investigate the conditions under which PLHIV and their spouses’ DS (concurrent and over time) are most strongly related by testing the moderating effects of resilience at different levels (i.e., PLHIV, spouse, or family resilience is weak, Hypothesis 2b, Figure 4); and iii) investigate the conditions under which PLHIV and their spouses’ DS (concurrent and over time) are most strongly related by testing the moderating effects of stress experienced by either PLHIV or their spouses (i.e., PLHIV or spouse stress is high, Hypothesis 2c, Figure 4).

21402714.label: Realisation of objectives
21402714.value: In this project, we recruited 252 HIV serodiscordant couples (exceeding the planned number of 198 couples) to participate in two waves of the two-year longitudinal survey. Most of these participants were middle-aged, with relatively low educational level and long-term marriage. We have achieved our first objective to examine the influence of resilience at different levels (individual, spouse and family) on PLHIV DS based on the ecological model by testing all the hypotheses. The results showed that resilience was associated with lower level of PLHIV DS. T1 spouse resilience added independent variance over or above individual factors in predicting PLHIV DS at T2. Family resilience was significantly associated with lower level of PLHIV DS after controlling for the individual and spouse characteristics. The indirect effect of T1 spouse resilience and family resilience to predict T2 PLHIV DS via enhancing PLHIV resilience was not significant. Stress experience of PLHIV did not moderate the association between resilience (PLHIV resilience, spouse resilience, or family resilience) and PLHIV DS. We have achieved our second objective with the dyadic sample, using Actor-Partner Interdependence Model (APIM). We examined all the hypotheses and found that DS was congruent within couples, which means DS of PLHIV and spouses were positively associated with each other. PLHIV resilience, spouse resilience or family resilience did not moderate the association between PLHIV DS and spouse DS. Spouse stress significantly moderated the concurrent association between PLHIV DS and spouse DS. To be specific, when HIV-negative spouses experienced higher level of stress, the congruence between PLHIV DS and spouse DS was stronger; when HIV-negative spouses experienced lower level of stress, the association of DS within the couple was not significant. In addition, we had further analyses with the APIM using the dyadic sample of couples affected by HIV. Our findings showed that the couples showed significant association in their distress levels. PLHIV’ stigma had significant actor and partner effects on distress within the dyad, and so did spouse’s perceived discrimination and exclusion. Moreover, the dyad showed significant congruence in their mental health (measured by the mental health component of a quality of life scale). PLHIV’s AIDS belief and spouse’s AIDS belief both showed actor and partner effects on mental health of the couples.

21402714.label: Major findings and research outcome
21402714.value: By examining the protective effect of resilience on PLHIV DS, we found that PLHIV resilience had concurrent association with PLHIV DS. PLHIV and spouses demonstrated concurrent DS congruence within the couple, which means PLHIV DS was significantly associated with spouses DS concurrently. The concurrent congruence of DS was moderated by spouse stress. In spouses experiencing higher level of stress, the association between PLHIV DS and spouses DS was particularly stronger. The couples affected by HIV showed interdependence in their distress, with PLHIV’s stigma and spouses’ perceived discrimination and exclusion showing significant actor and partner effects to predict distress within the dyad. In addition, the HIV couples demonstrated congruence in mental health, with both partners’ AIDS beliefs contributing with actor effects and partner effects to predict mental health of the couples.

21402714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21402714.value: Guided by the ecological model, this study identified the contextual protective factors for DS of PLHIV and spouses. It highlights that individual resilience protected PLHIV from DS and maintain their well-being, consistent with our previous findings. To step forward in health psychology research under the resilience framework, we need further investigations of cross-level interplays among variables at various levels (e.g., personal, couple, family). Our consistent findings on the dyadic model showed the congruence of DS, distress, and mental health within the couples, and PLHIV and spouses’ variables had significant actor and partner effects to predict these outcomes. In addition to strong theoretical contribution to health psychology which often neglects the mutual influences between the couples, our results on dyadic interdependence call for future intervention programs to target the couple as a unit rather than solely the patient or spouse.

21402714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21402714.value: Given the limited longitudinal research on development of DS and well-being in patients and spouses affected by HIV, this project conducted a two-wave survey to examine the interconnected well-being within HIV discordant couples and how social surroundings could make a difference. Our results highlight the congruence of DS, distress, and well-being of couples affected by HIV. This project made a significant contribution to the field as most of the health psychology studies neglect the dyadic interdependence within the couples affected by chronic diseases. Our findings also provide empirical insights for future intervention programs to improve the well-being of PLHIV and spouses by strengthening the couple as a unit instead of treating patient or spouse independently.

To investigate the neighborhood effects at DCCA level on child academic performance and non-cognitive social skills, with particular attention to the effects of neighborhood socio-economic characteristics and local residents’ attitudes toward Chinese immigrants within neighborhoods. To investigate the impacts of education-oriented parental practices on child academic performance and non-cognitive social skills. 21402914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21402914.value: Public tension surrounding the consequences of Chinese immigration into Hong Kong has drawn the attention of researchers and policy makers. In particular, the less-well-off profiles of Chinese immigrant families caused public worries about burdens to government welfare expenditure, over-occupancy of public medical and educational resources, and rising inequality, especially for immigrant-concentrated areas such as North, Yuen Long, and Tuen Mun. At the same time, researchers also paid much attention to studying the integration of Chinese immigrants and their offspring. In determining the integration of immigrants’ children, educational outcomes and non-cognitive skills are two complementary and important factors. While there is a large body of literature focusing on educational outcomes, the research has not been done with population-based survey data on children of Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong. Besides, insufficient attention has been paid to non-cognitive skills that not only are crucial for child learning but also have long term influence on adult socio-economic success. This proposed study aims to fill in the gaps by simultaneously examining academic performance and non-cognitive social skills of Chinese immigrants’ children in Hong Kong using data from 2011 Population Census and the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics (HKPSSD). The distinct feature of the proposed study is its multi-level analysis. It investigates the impacts of neighborhood socio-economic characteristics and neighborhood local residents’ attitudes towards Chinese immigrants at DCCA level, parental education-oriented practices at family level, and development related factors at child level. Empirical results of the study will enable us to gain an empirical understanding of the well-being of Chinese immigrants’ offspring in Hong Kong, and to identify mechanisms and factors at individual, household, and neighborhood levels, which could facilitate the successful integration of children of Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong. 研究者和政策制定者都非常關注中國內地移民遷入到香港後所引起的公共（資源）緊張。具體而言，內地移民家庭較差的社會經濟狀況使得公眾擔憂政府福利開銷的負擔、公共醫療和教育資源的過度佔用，以及不平等的上升——尤其是在北區、元朗和屯門等移民聚居區。同時，研究者也對內地移民及其孩子的融入做了很多研究。 對於移民孩子的融入，教育獲得以及非認知能力是互補的兩個重要決定因素。雖然有大量文獻關注教育獲得，但卻還沒有利用大樣本調查(population-based survey)資料來研究在港的內地移民孩子。此外，對於非認知能力的研究也很少。非認知能力不僅對於孩子的學習很重要，而且還會對其成年以後的社會經濟成就有著長期的影響。此項研究旨在填補這些研究空隙，運用2011年人口普查和香港社會動態追蹤調查的資料，同時考察在港內地移民孩子的學業表現和非認知能力。 此項研究的一個特別之處在於其多層次分析。它在地方選區（DCCA ）層面上考察社區的社會經濟特徵的影響和社區本地居民對於內地移民的態度，在家庭層面上考察父母的教育行為的作用，以及在孩子層面上考察與成長相關因素對學業表現和非認知能力的影響。 此項研究的實證結果會讓我們獲得關於在港內地移民孩子的福祉（well-being）的實證認識，以及找出個人層面、家庭層面和社區層面上能夠促進在港內地移民孩子成功融入的因素。

21402914.label: Realisation of objectives
21402914.value: The project objectives have been achieved. 1. The spatial distribution and residential concentration of Chinese immigrants (and their families) in Hong Kong has been documented. The PI (and her collaborator) also examined the relationship between residential concentration of Chinese immigrants and neighborhood socio-economic status (SES) at DCCA (District Council Constituency Areas) level, using micro-level sample data of 2011 population census. The analysis is included in one of the reported working papers. 2. The PI (and her collaborator) used HKPSSD data and compared children of Chinese immigrants to children of Hong Kong locals in academic performance (Chinese, Mathematics, and English) and non-cognitive social skills. The analysis is included in one of the reported working papers. 3. The PI (and her collaborator) studied the effect of neighborhood SES on child academic performance and non-cognitive social skills and found no significant net impact of neighborhood SES after controlling for family (parental practices), school, and individual characteristics. The results are included in one of the reported working papers. The PI (and her collaborators) also examined Hong Kong residents’ attitudes toward Chinese immigrants and presented preliminary results in an overseas academic conference. 4. The PI (and her collaborator) investigated the impacts of education-oriented parental practices on child academic performance and non-cognitive social skills. The analysis is included in one of the reported working papers. 5. The PI (and her collaborator) also examined whether the impacts of parental practices vary by neighborhood SES and found no significant interactive effects.

21402914.label: Major findings and research outcome
21402914.value: 1. Chines immigrants (and their families) concentrate on neighborhoods with lower SES. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zeng and Zhang in Part C. 2. Children of Chinese immigrants do not perform as well as children of Hong Kong locals in Chinese, Mathematics, and English, mainly due to differences between the two groups in family SES (as measured by family income, house ownership, and parental education). Once family SES is controlled, there is no significant difference between the two groups. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zhang, Nie, and Xu in Part C. 3. Children of Chinese immigrants do not differ significantly from children of locals in non-cognitive social skills. They have better non-cognitive social skills once measures of parental practices, family SES, and school characteristics are controlled. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zhang, Nie, and Xu in Part C. 4. There is no significant net impact of neighborhood SES on academic performance or non-cognitive social skills, after controlling for family (parental practices), school, and individual characteristics. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zhang, Nie, and Xu in Part C. 5. Parental practices have positive and significant impacts on child academic performance and non-cognitive social skills. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zhang, Nie, and Xu in Part C. 6. Family SES and school characteristics also have significant impacts on academic performance and non-cognitive social skills (i.e., positive effect of family SES on Chinese and English performance and non-cognitive social skills, and positive effect of English school on English performance and non-cognitive skills). Please refer to the reported working paper of Zhang, Nie, and Xu in Part C. 7. The PI (and her collaborator) also compared Chinese immigrants to Hong Kong locals with regard to life satisfaction. Please refer to the reported working paper of Zeng and Zhang in Part C. 8. The PI (and her collaborators) also examined determinants of attitudes toward Chinese immigrants, and found that localism identity, perceived threats of losing Hong Kong self-governance, and perceptions of lack of opportunity explain the formation of native attitudes towards new immigrants and mainlanders. In the context of tense Hong Kong-mainland relations, opposition to new immigrants and mainlanders seems to be an expression of setting up the boundaries between Hong Kong and the mainland to construct localism identity. The results were presented in an overseas academic performance (Please refer to Part C).

21402914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21402914.value: Empirical data generated from this project can be further used to address relevant research topics in migration study, such as how schooling systems (i.e., public vs. private/international) affect educational attainment of immigrant children (or children of immigrants), how religious affiliation of secondary schools affect adult socio-economic outcomes, and etc.

21402914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21402914.value: Chinese immigrants and their families have been documented as a less-well-off group in Hong Kong. The academic performance and non-cognitive skills are two complementary and important factors in determining the integration of Chinese immigrants' children and their likelihood of achieving upward mobility in Hong Kong. This project used 2011 population census and a population-based survey , the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics (HKPSSD), to simultaneously examine academic performance and non-cognitive social skills of Chinese immigrants' children. The results showed that family background, school characteristics, and parental practices have significant impacts on academic performance and non-cognitive social skills. And in particular, the poorer academic performance of Chinese immigrants' children is mainly resulted from their poorer family background. The project enabled us to identify the main mechanisms and factors at individual, family, school, and neighborhood levels that could facilitate a better integration of children of Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong.

21403014.label: Project Objectives
21403014.value: To identify and document 30 to 50 important socially engaged art projects in China since 1989. To design and build an online database that facilitates research on these projects. To analyze these projects in order to answer a set of theoretical questions: How do Chinese artists negotiate with the state and the market? How do they conjure publics and counterpublics? How are notions like collaboration and antagonism activated in the Chinese context? What can socially engaged art teach us about cultural activism and civil participation in China? To produce a book-length manuscript for publication. To explore the possibility of organizing an exhibition on Chinese socially engaged art in public museums.

21403014.label: Realisation of objectives
21403014.value: All objectives have been achieved. An open online database (seachina.net) with over 7,000 images and 300 videos of key socially engaged art projects by Chinese artists has been built. (The online database presents twenty projects and several of these projects, such as "Keepers of Waters," "Everyone's East Lake," and "Nanting Research," are umbrella projects, meaning that they contain multiple individual projects.) An open online course (MOOC) has been created and launched, reaching over 2,000 learners from China, US, UK and many other countries, greatly enhancing public awareness of Chinese socially engaged art. A book-length manuscript has been completed and will be submitted to a publisher. It includes fifteen case studies and five analytical essays. One exhibition of the archive has been realised at a university gallery in the US.

21403014.label: Major findings and research outcome
21403014.value: Major findings: The socially engaged art projects we have documented in this research project occurred in many different parts of China and took many different forms, but they shared a common set of values: they all addressed real and pressing social issues, and aimed to effect social change. They all moved away from the idea of artist-as-genius and celebrated collaboration and participation. The main issues addressed by these socially engaged art projects include: our relationship to land, water, and other beings; social justice, for migrant workers, and for queer citizens; the preservation of history and collective memory; and the rebuilding of social life in local communities. The forms of socially engaged art created by Chinese artists range from knowledge production to antagonistic action. They materialize as visual archives, pedagogical workshops, awareness-raising campaigns, and critical performances. Because social movements are almost non-existent in China, Chinese artists cannot embed socially engaged art inside social movements. Having no movement infrastructure to rely on, they have to create something akin to mini-movements on their own. Research outcome: An open online database (seachina.net) with over 7,000 images and 300 videos of key social of key socially engaged art projects by Chinese artists has been built. An open online course (MOOC) has been created and launched, reaching over 2,000 learners from China, US, UK and many other countries, greatly enhancing public awareness of Chinese socially engaged art. A book-length manuscript has been completed. It includes fifteen case studies and five analytical essays. One exhibition has been staged of the archive at a university gallery in the US.

21403014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21403014.value: Socially engaged art continues to develop in China. We will monitor the field and conduct further research in a few years.

21403014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21403014.value: This research project documents key socially engaged art practices in Mainland China from 1989 to 2016. It articulates the strategies that Chinese artists have developed to address pressing social issues ranging from environmental protection to social justice. It presents a comprehensive study of an important field of Chinese contemporary art.

21500214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21500214.value: 外部薪酬差距和企业政策

21500214.label: Project Objectives
21500214.value: Though lots of effort has been focused on the association between executive compensation and corporate policies, there is limited evidence of how implicit external incentive contracts affect various firm policies. This study will thus add to the literature by providing more empirical evidence. We will use a GMM-IV approach to investigate the relation between industry tournament incentives and a firm’s financial disclosure policy. Specifically, we will examine whether external promotion-based incentives induce managers to manipulate earnings through different ways. Furthermore, we will study the influence of external tournament incentives on a firm’s acquisition decision. Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) decision is among the largest investment decisions a company makes. We argue that higher external tournament incentives increase a firm’s likelihood of engaging in acquisitions, and also affect the deal performance. After we conduct all empirical tests and find relevant results, we will discuss the implications and write at least one working paper suitable for publication in a top finance journal.

21500214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500214.value: Several recent studies have found that implicit executive incentive contracts can influence firm policies significantly. For example, Coles, Li, and Wang (2013) show that pay gap among CEOs in the same industry can serve as a tournament incentive and motivate managers to work better and take more risk. In this project, we will examine the influence of such industry tournament incentives on corporate financial disclosure and acquisition policies. When CEOs in the same industry are paid differently, they will have incentive to compete for the position with the highest pay. We hypothesize that CEOs with stronger external tournament incentives are more likely to engage in earnings management activities, so as to boost their reputation in the labor market and enhance their upward mobility. On the other hand, if managers manipulate earnings too aggressively and trigger fraud charges, they will suffer substantial reputation loss in the labor market. Therefore, we conjecture that CEOs with stronger external tournament incentives are more likely to manage earnings within the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) framework but less likely to experience financial restatements. Regarding a firm’s acquisition policy, we hypothesize that CEOs facing stronger external tournament incentives are more likely to engage in acquisitions, since doing so can increase their monetary rewards as well as their visibility in the labor market. However, it is not clear how external tournament incentives affect acquisition performance. If CEOs are concerned about reputation loss resulting from making bad deals, tournament incentives may motivate managers to make better acquisitions. However, some theoretical studies also argue that compensation disparity may induce lower paid CEOs to undertake value-destroying acquisitions by overpaying the target. Therefore, this is an important empirical question to be answered. To test all of these hypotheses, we will follow Coles, Li, and Wang (2013) to construct three industry tournament incentive measures. We will also adopt a GMM-IV approach to address the endogeneity concern. Preliminary results show that firms have higher abnormal accruals when their CEOs have stronger industry tournament incentives, which is consistent with our conjecture. This study can help further our understanding of the impact of such implicit incentive contracts on firm policies, and contribute to the literature on both finance and accounting. 最近的研究表明，隐性的经理人激励合同可以显著影响企业政策。例如，Coles, Li, and Wang (2013) 发现，同一产业里的CEO薪酬差距可作为锦标赛式激励来推动管理层更好地工作及承担更多风险。在这个项目，我们将研究锦标赛式外部激励对企业的财务披露及收购政策的影响。 当同一产业里的CEO们薪酬不同时，他们会努力去争夺最高薪酬的位置。我们推测，具有较强外部激励的CEO们更有可能通过盈余管理来提高他们在经理人劳动市场中的声誉。但同时，为了避免可能的财务重述带来的负面影响，他们会遵循一般公认会计准则（GAAP），而不会过于激进地操纵盈余而引来欺诈指控。对于公司的收购政策，我们推测，有较强外部激励的CEO更有可能从事收购，以此来增加自己的薪酬及在劳动市场上的知名度。至于外部激励对并购收益的影响，我们没有明确的预期。一方面，外部激励可以使CEO们更加关注自己的声誉，从而促使他们做出更好的收购决定。然而，一些理论研究却认为，薪酬差距可能导致低收入的CEO盲目地进行价值损害型并购。 为了回答这些实证问题，我们沿用Coles, Li, and Wang (2013)的方法来衡量CEO所面对的外部激励， 并采用GMM-IV的方法来解决内生性问题。初步结果与我们的推测相一致。当公司的CEO面对较高的产业外部奖励时，他们的异常应计通常较高。我们希望通过这项研究来更好的认识这类隐性激励合同对公司政策的影响。

21500214.label: Realisation of objectives
21500214.value: We started the project by further reviewing the literature on the relation between executive compensation and corporate policies. We then collect data from multiple sources for empirical analysis. In particular, we start with all publicly traded U.S. firms covered by the ExecuComp database and use the CEO compensation information in each year to construct labor market incentive measures. We obtain firm characteristics from COMPUSTAT, stock price and return information from CRSP, analyst earnings forecasts from I/B/E/S, and other CEO characteristics from ExecuComp. In addition, we collect firm’s financial restatements from the U.S. General Accounting Office. We then examine our hypothesis using the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimations with instrumental variables (IV). We find results highly consistent with the predictions of our hypothesis. Specifically, we find that our measures of managerial labor market incentives are significantly and positively related to a firm’s probability of meeting or narrowly beating analyst forecasts. We also find that firms run by CEOs with stronger labor market incentives are associated with larger income-increasing abnormal accruals. The CEO’s labor market incentives are also positively related to measures of real earnings management, but the relations are insignificant. Finally, we find that managers display restraint in their strategic distortion of firms’ financial information in that the probability of a firm committing financial fraud or accounting irregularities is significantly lower when the firm’s CEO faces larger potential rewards for upward career movements. In further analyses, we study how a CEO’s benchmark-beating behavior affects her future compensation and mobility in the managerial labor market. We find that a greater frequency of meeting or narrowly beating analyst forecasts leads to higher CEO compensation and more mobility in the labor market. We do not find evidence that corporate boards or the managerial labor market takes into account the CEO’s labor market incentives and discounts the CEO’s track record of benchmark beating. After examining the impact on financial disclosure, we then examined how external tournament incentives affect a firm's acquisition decision. However, we do not find evidence that higher tournament incentives affects a firm's acquisition decisions. After all of these empirical tests, we wrote a paper. We presented our work in various institutions, including Australian National University, Chinese University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong and Clemson University. We also presented the paper at the 26th Annual Conference on Financial Economics and Accounting in US. After obtaining many valuable comments and suggestions from seminar participants and conference discussant, we made some revisions. We expect to have this paper published in a high quality accounting journal. So overall, we have achieved all major objectives of this project.

21500214.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500214.value: We find that chief executive offers (CEOs) facing greater labor market incentives are more likely to engage in strategic financial disclosure choices to inflate their firms’ reported performance and to meet or narrowly beat earnings benchmarks, thereby enhancing their reputation and upward mobility in the labor market. At the same time, these CEOs are more careful not to trigger financial fraud and restatements, which will severely damage their reputation and undermine their future career prospects. We wrote a paper based on our findings. We presented our work in several institutions and a high-quality international conference. We kept revising our paper based on valuable feedback from other scholars. Now the paper is under review in a top accounting journal.

21500214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500214.value: We expect to publish this paper in a high quality journal. After that, we will explore whether external labor market incentives have any impact on firms' other policies.

21500214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500214.value: In this project, we examined how labor market incentives, as measured by the compensation gap between a firm’s chief executive offer (CEO) and the highest paid CEO in industry peer firms, affect the CEO's financial disclosure decisions. We find that such compensation gap affects CEOs' incentives to inflate their firms’ reported performance. Our study provides evidence on how CEOs use publicly available compensation information of other firms to decide their own firm's disclosure policy. It improves our understanding of the impact of external labor market on corporate executives.

21500314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500314.value: Over the last few decades, globalization has been an economic force in importation that firms cannot avoid. In particular, it has significantly increased competitive pressure by facilitating the penetration of foreign rivals into local markets. While many studies have investigated the effect of import penetration on domestic performance, only recently has its effect on the corporate policies of domestic firms received attention from researchers. However, to fully understand the effect of import penetration on the domestic economy, firms linked economically to those firms that are directly affected should also be considered. This project aims to investigate how a negative shock to a customer’s competitive environment, represented by an increase in import penetration, affects supplier firms, specifically their performance and leverage choices. While several recent studies have established the interdependence between customer and supplier, it not evident how an exogenous shock to a customer’s competitive environment propagates along the supply chain, as a customer would optimally choose whether to transfer the negative shock to its suppliers. Existing studies do not clearly predict whether suppliers would be negatively affected by intensified competition in their customers’ industry, even if customers choose to transfer the negative shock to their performance. Additionally, this project will address a related research question: whether the influence of customer shock varies in magnitude according to the nature of the customer-supplier relationship and the supplier’s market structure. Both the intensity of customer-supplier relations and supplier market structure determine the bargaining power of a customer over its suppliers. At the same time, the importance of a particular supplier-customer relationship to a customer would affect how much the customer cares about the particular supplier. Both the customer’s bargaining power and the customer’s concern for the supplier should affect the magnitude of the customer shock effect on suppliers. 在過去的幾十年裏，全球化帶來的進口增長一直是企業必須面對的問題。全球化使外國競爭者更易地滲透到當地市場，從而顯著增加國內產業所對面的競爭壓力。雖然有許多研究探討了進口滲透對國內產業業績的影響，其對公司政策的影響直到最近才受到關註。為了充分了解進口滲透對國內經濟的影響，我們還需要研究那些受沖擊產業的關聯企業。 該項目旨在研究客戶產業的競爭沖擊對其供應商的影響。我們用進口滲透率來衡量客戶產業所面臨的競爭環境，並研究其如何影響供應企業的業績和融資政策。雖然最近的幾項研究都確認了供應鏈企業間的相互依存關系，但是客戶企業的競爭環境沖擊如何影響供應商卻並不明確。一個原因是客戶可以選擇是否將負面沖擊轉嫁給供應商。如果客戶選擇轉嫁，那供應商又會受到怎樣的影響？現有的研究也沒有明確的預測。另外，因為供應商關系的緊密程度及供應產業的市場結構都會影響客戶的議價能力及客戶對一特定供應商的關註程度，這一項目還會研究這兩者對沖擊程度的影響。

21500314.label: Realisation of objectives
21500314.value: The paper shows that the import competition affects not only the industry that is directly affected by the competition, but also the upstream industries. Thus, the paper achieves the first objective of understanding the broad economic effect on domestic firms. The paper also shows that negative shock of downstream industry propagate along the supply chain and indicates that customer shock is transferred to alter performance of economically linked firms (suppliers), which achieves the second and third objectives. The paper's main finding is the increased downstream import competition leads upstream firms to choose lower financial leverage, which achieves the fourth objective. Finally, the paper shows that the effect on suppliers' leverage is stronger when the customer-supplier relationships are likely to be stronger (valuable to suppliers), which address the fifth objective.

21500314.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500314.value: This paper studies the spillover effect of import competition in downstream industries on upstream capital structure. we use tariff data for the US manufacturing sector during the period 1989 to 2005. We first identify the largest tariff reduction for each industry, focusing on cuts larger than four times the industry average during our sample period. We then use input-output tables to identify customer–supplier industry pairs. Using a sample of industry pairs that operate in different four-digit NAICS industries, we find that suppliers whose main customers experience a large tariff reduction lower their leverage by about 5% of their assets. We show that firms lower their leverage more when the customer–supplier relationship is more valuable to the firms and when firms are more vulnerable to the downstream shock. Finally, firms adjust their leverage mainly by issuing more equity.

21500314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500314.value: This paper is also related to the literature on the interaction between product market competition and capital structure. Most of these studies have focused on shocks that directly affect domestic competition. This study suggests that investigating firms’ strategic responses to changes in their product market environment that are caused by foreign competition shocks could be fruitful research in future studies.

21500314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500314.value: The globalization of economic activities in the past few decades has changed the competitive configuration of industries and generated vigorous debate about trade openness among policymakers. It is well acknowledged that globalization exposes firms to greater international competition and has a profound impact on firm performance. However, there is very limited empirical evidence in the international business literature on how trade liberalization affects firm policies through product market interactions. Prior research shows that the level of domestic competition in a firm’s customer or supplier industries are important to firms’ capital structure decisions. Given the significantly increased trade liberalization in the past few decades, we argue that it is important to investigate the impact of international competition on firm’s financial policies. In this paper, we examine how changes in import competition arising from tariff reductions in downstream industries spill over to upstream capital structure. We find that upstream firms choose significantly lower leverage after downstream industries experience large tariff reductions. This effect is magnified when the customer–supplier relationship is more valuable to the firm and when firms are more vulnerable to downstream shock. Firms lower their leverage mainly by issuing more equity.

21500614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500614.value: While help and advice were traditionally sought from experts and professionals, an increasing number of people have begun taking advantage of question-and-answer (Q&A) websites where they can ask questions and others can answer them (Harper et al. 2009). According to a survey commissioned by Yahoo! (2006), one third of online adults have used a Q&A website, and over half of these individuals state that information from a Q&A website has affected a decision that they have made. A more recent report revealed that adults seeking legal advice consider Q&A websites as the most useful online tool (American Bar Association 2011). Q&A websites can facilitate knowledge discovery and delivery if the answers help readers to address people's problems. Despite the growing body of literature that has examined the helpfulness of online consumer reviews, relatively little is known about what makes a helpful answer on Q&A websites. We identify two types of source expertise – professional expertise and experience-based expertise – and argue that they are positively associated with answer helpfulness. In addition to source expertise, we hypothesize an inverted U-shaped relationship between the amount of information in an answer and its helpfulness. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, we further predict that both types of source expertise moderate the nonlinear impact of information amount. To test these hypotheses, we will collect a unique data set from one of the leading Q&A websites, WebMD Answers. This paper will contribute to the studies on information amount and source characteristics, and our findings may provide significant practical implication for managers of knowledge sharing platforms. 根據一項來自雅虎的調查顯示，有1/3成年網民使用問答網站，並且其中有一半的人認為來自問答網站的信息影響了他們的決策。雖然很多的文獻已經檢驗了在線消費者評論的有用性，很少有人知道是什麼讓一個問答網站的回答有用。我們識別出了兩種類型的來源知識，並認為他們與回答的有用性正相關。同時也假設了信息量和其有用性的倒U型關係 。這篇文章將會為關於信息量和來源特徵的研究做出貢獻，並且有著重要的實踐意義。

21500614.label: Realisation of objectives
21500614.value: 1. To revisit the effects of source characteristics and the effects of content characteristics on information helpfulness. >> We found that the fit between an answer’s abstract level and disease chronicity is positively related to the perceived helpfulness of the answer. We also found that the match in language styles between an answer and all the answers to questions on the same disease topic is positively related to the perceived helpfulness of the answer. 2. To examine whether the effects of source characteristics and the effects of content characteristics on information helpfulness depend on the nature of user-generated content websites (e.g., review websites and Q&A websites). >> We focused on Q&A website. We found that the “fit” concept are important in both different user-generated content websites. 3. To increase the awareness of the importance of information helpfulness >> The PI has presented this study in the seminar at two universities (City University of Hong Kong and National Sun Yat-sen University). >> The PI has discussed the findings in many courses at City University of Hong Kong. 4. To identify more practical implications of information helpfulness >> We have demonstrated the utility of matching characteristic of content with its context: the same content may be perceived as more or less diagnostic, depending on the specific context factors that may influence readers’ mental representations and expectations. Thus, previous findings that content should be written in a certain way to be helpful might need to be qualified. In a medical setting, our findings suggest that an answer to a question would be evaluated more favorably if its abstract level matches the temporal distance of the disease topic (for example, writing an abstract answer to a question about a chronic disease). As a result, content contributors should keep the chronicity of diseases in mind as they determine the “right” abstractness of their answers. In addition, most Q&A communities have diverse interest groups, with each group preferring a specific language style for sharing information and knowledge. Contributors may benefit from writing in a language style consistent with the style typically adopted by a particular interest group. Overall, contributors striving to provide more helpful content should be aware of the context surrounding the crafted content. Furthermore, the findings have indirect implications for the design of UGC platforms. One of the critical success factors for a UGC platform is content. If readers perceive content from a UGC platform to be useful for their decision-making, they will “stick” to this platform longer. Our findings provide useful guidelines for designing better medical Q&A communities. In particular, these communities may be better off establishing strategies concerning how contributors should prepare their answers for different types of diseases. The value of an answer could be greatly enhanced when it matches a reader’s mental representation. That is, when answering questions related to acute diseases, contributors should be encouraged to rely on more concrete words and examples. In contrast, when answering questions related to chronic diseases, contributors should be recommended to make use of more abstract concepts and logical interpretations. Therefore, medical Q&A communities should design guidelines not only targeted toward the content or context of answers, but also toward their fit with each other.

21500614.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500614.value: First, this study proposes a fit perspective – user-generated content is perceived to be more diagnostic when its characteristics (for example, abstractness and language styles) are congruent with their respective contextual factors. Previous studies on antecedents of information diagnosticity have focused primarily on the independent effects of content and context factors, suggesting that content needs to be crafted in a certain way or be perceived in a certain context to be considered diagnostic. To the best of our knowledge, no research has examined the role of C-C fit in UGC. A variety of contextual factors can influence the mental representations and expectations of users as they read and make sense of a piece of UGC. Therefore, a better fit of content with its context can lead readers to perceive the content as more diagnostic. Our findings highlight the importance of taking this more nuanced perspective in studying perceived value of UGC, and this approach opens up exciting new avenues for future research in this area. Second, we explore the role of distinct types of C-C fit in UGC. When the fit perspective is adopted in other areas of information systems literature such as task-technology, it is defined as a match or congruence without making further distinctions. Extending concepts from person-environment fit literature, we classify C-C fit into complementary fit and supplementary fit. Complementary fit occurs when content characteristics provide what readers want, and supplementary fit occurs when characteristics of a piece of content are similar as those of content at a collective level. To the best of our knowledge, this paper represents the first attempt to introduce the concepts of complementary vs. supplementary fit in information systems literature. This research also empirically demonstrates that both types of fit contribute to the perceived value of UGC. Third, the majority of research to date on antecedents of information diagnosticity focuses on what is being communicated (e.g., ratings and review content in the online reviews setting). However, emerging literature has started to explore how content is being communicated, such as two-sidedness and emotional factors. This paper extends this line of research by exploring the role of two “how” factors – abstractness of content words and language style of function words. Both of these factors have received little attention to date. Thus, this paper has deepened our understanding of how the diagnosticity of information is shaped by the way it is presented and conveyed.

21500614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500614.value: First, our theoretical rationale suggests that both complementary and supplementary types of C-C fit can contribute to perceived diagnosticity of UGC and we propose two hypotheses regarding the roles of fit in construal levels and language styles. However, we acknowledge that the fit in construal levels may not be the only type of complementary fit and similarly in language styles may not be the sole type of supplementary fit. Second, although this research provides empirical evidence for the effect of C-C fit in terms of construal levels and language styles, it would be valuable for further investigation to explore the underlying mechanism of such effects. In particular, it has been demonstrated that as consumers read and make sense of certain content, their mental representations and expectations play a critical role in their diagnosticity evaluation of the content. Third, this research focused on one dimension of psychological distance (that is temporal distance). In order to fully understand the role of psychological distance, future studies should explore the effects of its other dimensions.

21500614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500614.value: Given the popularity and prevalence of user-generated content (UGC), it is increasingly important to understand what constitutes diagnostic content in UGC. While prior research has revealed content and context characteristics as important determinants, we propose a content-context (C-C) fit perspective emphasizing that certain content needs to be congruent with its context in order to speak the “right” language. In addition, two types of C-C fit involving different types of words are recognized and differentiated. Specifically, drawing on construal-level theory and language style matching literature, we present a theoretical framework in which greater complementary fit regarding the use of content words (such as nouns) or greater supplementary fit regarding the use of function words (such as pronouns) can lead to more diagnostic content. To test this framework, we advance a set of fit-related hypotheses in the setting of medical question-and-answer (Q&A) communities and test them using a unique data set from WebMD Answers. The findings demonstrate the importance of incorporating the C-C fit perspective into research examining the perceived value of UGC. The results deepen current understanding of the fit concept (e.g., complementary fit and supplementary fit) as well as its application in the medical setting.

21500714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21500714.value: 在科技驅動下，物理空間上分散的虛擬團隊已經成為壹種至關重要的組織形式，用以在全球範圍內規劃工作。盡管虛擬團隊能帶來潛在利益，許多虛擬團隊的員工卻傳達了諸如通信人格解體，沖突，孤立感以及缺乏共享知識等負面體驗。上述負面體驗可能會對虛擬團隊員工的工作績效帶來消極影響。鑒於虛擬團隊在商業領域的普及，如何應對這些挑戰從而提高虛擬團隊員工的工作績效，對學術界和產業界來說都極具價值。 概括來說，研究人員從兩個視角調查了為何有些員工在虛擬協作中比別人工作能力更強。鄰近度視角檢驗了客觀距離（如，空間，時間以及文化差距）如何影響虛擬團隊員工的心理狀態（如，與同事的分離和疏遠）以及他們面臨的關於知識的挑戰（如，知識獲取，處理和應用）。網絡視角探索了電子連接如何用在線網絡將物理上分散的人們聯合起來。在線網絡的構成被認為可以抵消客觀距離的影響。兩個獨立研究方向的存在使得虛擬工作領域的研究成果分散而且模棱兩可。分裂的研究和理論更是限制了我們對虛擬團隊中個人行為和集體動態的理解。 為了解決這個問題，本項目將整合鄰近度和網絡視角並開發壹個全面的理論模型，用以解釋虛擬團隊中員工的工作績效。具體來說，這個項目旨在解決虛擬團隊員工在執行任務時面對的兩大挑戰：（1）虛擬團隊員工如何有效地克服空間，時間以及文化差距並完成工作任務， （2）員工如何管理他們的在線網絡關系以最大化虛擬協作帶來的利益。 為了測試理論模型，我們實施了壹系列的問卷調查。此外，為了進壹步驗證我們的實證結果從而系統地提出關於虛擬團隊中的實際距離和在線網絡關系的不同緯度的理論機制，我們執行了多案例研究。為達上述目標，我已經與全球五大公司達成了安全合作意向，這些公司運營中的虛擬團隊遍布世界各國。我聯系了幾個目標公司的高管，他們已經確認將會為網絡分析提供虛擬團隊名單以及每個員工的位置信息。此外，為了克服自我報告的績效指標中的偏差，我還將同時利用監管對員工工作表現的評級。這項研究的結果對學術界和產業界都具有重要意義。對學術界來說，這項研究將創造新的知識，並豐富對於物理距離和在線連接的共同作用的理解，這些都是虛擬團隊成功的基礎。對產業界來說，如果有公司希望在虛擬工作中設計虛擬團隊並部署信息通信技術以預警團隊動態，該研究將提供深刻見解和說明性的指導方針。

21500714.label: Realisation of objectives
21500714.value: The main purpose of this project was to address two major challenges faced by virtual workers in performing their tasks: (1) how virtual workers effectively overcome spatial, temporal, and cultural distances to accomplish their job tasks better and (2) how they manage their online network ties to maximize the benefits provided by virtual collaboration. Drawing on construal level theory, the PI developed a model to explain how different dimensions of objective distance (spatial, temporal, and cultural) influence a virtual worker’s psycho-logical distance to other virtual team (VT) members and how this distance influences an individual's job performance in the context of virtual collaboration. To achieve the objectives of this project the PI carried out the following research activities: (1) The PI elaborated on research constructs and improved the proposed research model (2) The PI collected empirical data from 163 virtual workers of three multinational companies (3) The PI tested the proposed model using the collected data (4) The PI examines how online networks of virtual workers offset the influence of the objective distance on psychological distance (5) The PI explored how technological characteristics enable the formation of online network and influence a virtual worker's job satisfaction (6) The PI wrote the several research papers related to the research objectives. Specifically, the proposed research model was tested with the collaboration of three multinational companies operating VTs across countries around the world. Executives of the target companies provided support for this research. With this support, the PI selected VTs where members worked separated by space (e.g., in different cities or countries), time (e.g., different time zones), or were of nationalities (to reflect cultural distance), thus meeting conventional definitions of a VT and providing variation across all dimensions of objective distance. Empirical data was collected by a series of surveys from 163 virtual workers employed across the VTs. The measurement model was assessed by examining its convergent and discriminant validity. To assess convergent validity, the composite reliability (CR) of each multi-item construct was examined. To assess discriminant validity, the PI examined the values for average variance extracted (AVE). For satisfactory discriminant validity, the AVE from a construct should be greater than the variance shared between the construct and other constructs in the model. For each construct, the square root of the average variance extracted should exceed the construct’s correlation with every other construct. The results indicates that the AVE for each construct is larger than the correlation of that construct with all the other constructs in the both models, thus ensuring discriminant validity of the constructs Given the structure of the model, the statistical analysis is expected to employ hierarchical linear regression to take into account the different impacts of different sets of independent variables. In particular, the PI entered the interaction terms of different dimensions of objective distance into the model and regress it to psychological distance in order to verify their non-additive effects. The results indicate that organizational tenure has a negative influence on psychological distance. The results also show that spatial distance significantly positively influences psychological distance, whereas temporal and cultural distances have no significant influence on psychological distance. Interaction terms between different dimensions of object distance were entered as independent variables into the regression model. The results show that significant interaction effects exist between spatial and cultural distance; spatial and temporal distance; and spatial, temporal, and cultural distance, which account for 12% of the variance of psychological distance. The results showed that psychological distance was the main determinant of job performance and that the different dimensions of objective distance increased psychological distance in a nonlinear fashion. The results also showed that interaction effects exist between each dimension of objective distance. That is, the different objective distances increased the psychological distance in a non-additive way. The PI argue that neither cultural nor temporal distance by themselves increased psychological distance but cultural and temporal distance interacted with spatial distance to produce greater psychological distance than did the simple combination of the two dimensions of the objective distance. By providing a consistent and solid foundation for diagnosis and assessment of psychological distance, this study contributes to VT literature. The findings of this research significantly shift academic and practical attention from objective distance toward subjective distance. A more nuanced understanding of how psychological distance is formed by the different dimensions of objective distance and how psychological distance influences job performance is of academic value. The overarching practical implication of this study is that virtual workers’ psychological distance should be carefully monitored and managed to improve their job performance. The measurement this study developed for objective and psychological distance helps VT managers predict more precisely potential challenges a virtual worker may experience. Given that each VT member has varying degrees of objective distance, VT managers need to pay greater attention to those who have high degrees of distance in its two or more sub-dimensions. VT managers should also carefully monitor virtual workers’ psychological distance at the team level when the team is highly dispersed. Furthermore, the findings of this study imply that VT members’ psychological distance can be mitigated by altering virtual workers’ perceptions of responsiveness, subjective proximity, and accessibility. Technological affordances that can promote emotional and social interaction (e.g., interactivity support, self-presentation, identity expression) may help to mitigate psychological distance.
