22400914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22400914.value: This study reassesses the effects of the Ming-Qing Transition (1619-1740) on the original Ming (1368-1644) institutions of local governance, as well as on the course of Chinese socioeconomic development in the light of the evolving text of the Great Qing Code, before its consolidation in 1740, and of the casebooks from the late Ming and early Qing periods. Through a detailed comparison of the Great Ming Code with various early versions of the Great Qing Code from the first century of the Qing rule (1644-1911), this study argues that the Manchu imposed a series of subtle yet striking transformations on the Ming legal foundation to serve their administrative interests and specific intellectual concerns, and, therefore, that the established opinion that the Qing institution adopted its Ming predecessor in its entirety should be seriously reconsidered. Moreover, by investigating the works of documented legal cases from the two epochs in question, the study attempts to identify the socioeconomic changes—if not the disastrous effects—brought about by the establishment of the Qing rule in different regions of China Proper from the perspective of local societies. In addition, because two key posts of the provincial judiciary, namely the Regional Inspector and Prefectural Judge, were both abolished in the 1660s, the study also investigates how the quality of justice at the local level was influenced by the absence of these professional and independent judges from the records of the early Qing courts. Through a deeper understanding of the differences in legal institutions and modes of social control between the late Ming and early Qing regimes, and by building an electronic database from the Historical Geographical Information System (GIS) comprising all available court cases during the Ming-Qing Transition, the study aims to throw light on social and legal studies in traditional China, on concepts for the management of similar institutional changes in contemporary China, and on research into the problems of social control. 本研究以《大清律例》在1740年定型前之發展修改情況，以及明末清初的判牘為主要資料，重新審視明清易代（1619年-1740年）對明人原有地方行政制度及社會經濟發展歷程的影響：滿族統治者為自身的利益與知性的關懷，對晚明的法制進行了一系列雖不顯眼卻意義深遠的修改，而前人以為清人只全盤照搬明代法制的成說，實有修正的必要；透過比較明末與清初相似的案例，並將有關案例輸入歷史地理訊息系統作分析，可望將易代的變化更清晰地呈現出來。

22400914.label: Realisation of objectives
22400914.value: To realize the objective of building a Historical GIS of casebooks from the Ming-Qing Transition, the Principal Investigator (PI) and his assistants have analyzed several representative casebooks from the late Ming and early Qing periods. These casebooks also represent the major sources for their respective researches which is now in the final stages of creating interfaces to facilitate the use of the spatial and jurisprudential information they contain. It is anticipated that further funding and the provision of suitable scholarly talent will create a more comprehensive system for all the casebooks in question. The dataset will be uploaded into the “History in Data” Database system hosted by university library of the Hong Kong Baptist University (https://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/history/index.php?lang=en) during the next academic year to ensure that information from these casebooks can be accessed by both academic and public users with basic GIS knowledge. The other qualitative research objectives of the project have all been satisfactorily achieved. The Principal Investigator has published more than a dozen journal articles and conference papers, in addition to a full-length book which is currently under review for publication, addressing most of the issues raised in the original application. Firstly, the institutional and socioeconomic changes that took place during the Ming-Qing Transition are directly discussed in the light of legal materials from the codes and casebooks by a seminal paper on toilets and night soil management during the Ming-Qing Transition. Utilizing these new sources, this study describes an overlooked aspect of social history as well as the changes in morality and the concerns of “public” and city management in South China during the 17th century. Another paper which argues the authorship and publication of a late Ming Fujianese casebook, the Xinqi santi wenfa shenyu, describes the folk culture and socioeconomic changes of coastal Fujian on the eve of dynastic change. Moreover, the PI has produced several further papers exposing the situation of Chinese society during the Ming-Qing transition. These include a paper that employs casebook materials to discuss how the original nature, as a godown, of the Portuguese settlement of Macau in the late Ming differed from the well-known semi-colonial system of the Qing period; a paper that studies gender issues during late Ming China through the lens of legal materials; and another paper on the authorship and publication of the late Ming casebook Zheyu xinyu. Secondly, the objective of studying the discontinued elements of the Ming legal system by the interruption of Qing rule has been realized by the book manuscript “Justice in Print” (under review for publishing by a renowned university press). This monograph emphasizes the abolishment of some key posts, such as Regional Inspectors and Prefectural Judges in the early Qing which created a very different provincial judiciary from the original form it took during the Ming. Moreover, to inquire into some unexplored aspects of the original Ming judicial system, the PI has written two papers discussing the establishment of sub-statutes systems since the mid-Ming which mended the shortcomings of the unalterable Great Ming Code along with a paper concentrating on the effect of public opinion on the judicial decisions of the local courts as seen in the late Ming casebooks. Thirdly, to demonstrate the unique characteristics and specific concerns of the Qing rulers as to the legal system, the PI continued his discussion in a new paper on judicial tortures during the late Ming China in an earlier GRF project and researched many relevant reforms of the Qing government in regards to judicial fact-finding methods. As greater restriction had been added to the application of judicial torture over time, during the latter half of the Qing period, it was very risky for frontline officials to employ torture formally in their judicial duties, otherwise they might face serious consequences to their own position and even risk their lives. This more restricted use of torture, however, did not necessarily lead to better quality justice, since the judges categorized all problematic cases as dubious ones and refused to commit themselves to finding facts for judgement, so that many accused were imprisoned for decades without a sentence and many of them died in prison before learning of a concrete result. The most significant findings of this paper relating to torture including the identification of some internal development trends of the Chinese legal system, and the discovery that even without the pressure of legal reform imposed by foreign powers during the late Qing, the abolishment of judicial torture should be seen as inevitable as the Qing court had already discovered that torture created more practical political and judicial problems than they could have solved. Therefore, it is sensible to review other magnets of criticisms of Traditional legal system during the Late Qing Reform to ascertain if any of them had experienced similar internal development trends as the judicial torture. On this basis we are able to re-evaluate the Western impact on Chinese laws at the beginning of 20th century. Finally, the objective to investigate the effects of institutional changes and economic recession on local society is mainly dealt with by a paper that discusses the suppression of popular religions and Catholicism from 17th to early 19th centuries. The PI puts forward the significant differences between the Ming Court and the succeeding Qing regime towards this foreign religion. Indeed, the research findings of this paper and some related studies in progress could certainly provide insights to the effectiveness and limitations of similar efforts to control personal faith of both domestic and foreign origins by governments of China today.

22400914.label: Major findings and research outcome
22400914.value: The current project reveals that judicial cases are important sources for the investigation of Chinese local societies and institutions past and present. As seen in the Macau paper, the late Ming casebooks reveal the godown nature and dominate role of the “interpreter” in the Portuguese settlement of Macau in its initial stage during the late Ming so that the early Qing concessions to the Portuguese settlers for more autonomy rights could be identified. The casebooks show the Chinese toilet and faeces management situation during the late Ming and early Qing in the Jiangnan regions, which was a significant research gap in Chinese social history. The Catholic paper that is based on unexposed legal materials demonstrates that the Qing rulers did impose far harsher measures to suppress Catholicism as a heresy, while the Ming emperors had shown more tolerance to this alien cult. In the field of legal history, the judges’ rulings in the judicial disputes vividly expose much social information, especially regarding the lower strata of society with is not found in other sources. The addition of early Qing cases and elements of the Great Qing Code provides unique insights into some of the subtle changes which occurred during dynastic change such as the situation whereby judges and legislators unintentionally exposed some of the new concerns of the Manchu rulers which made the Qing judiciary markedly different from its late Ming predecessor, as shown in our monograph on the prefectural judge and related provincial judicial posts from the late Ming period. It was discovered that the professionalism and judicial independence created by the uniqueness of those post abolished at the beginning of the Qing regime had a detrimental effect on Chinese legal development as the Manchu rulers prioritized cutting personnel costs and emphasized efficiency in closing cases in favour of the prefect realization of justice. Moreover, the paper on the impact of public opinion towards judicial judgement also demonstrates that the judicial case reports can provide abundant information no found elsewhere on the interactions between the judge and the public during the hearing process under the open system of the traditional Chinese court. Furthermore, the torture paper exposed subtle yet important changes over the original Ming system as seen in the revisions of different versions of the Great Qing Code. Without the Ming rulers’ burden of ancestral rules, the new dynasty could change the Ming system and introduce new rules comparatively freely.

22400914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22400914.value: There are three possible directions of further research development inspired by the current project. The first is to complete a comprehensive electronic database of judicial cases from the late Ming and early Qing periods. The second is a more comprehensive investigation to the legal developments of the Qing regime. Even though it would not be possible to handle all of the issues within the limited time frame of the current project, the methodologies and source materials employed by the Qing torture paper could be utilized and applied to inquire into related legal issues such as the extremely cruel punishments and prison management of the period. The last direction is a new GRF project “Faithfully Outlawed? The Struggles of Chinese Catholics during the mid-Qing persecution of Christianity (1721-1860) in light of judicial records from the Xingke tiben” which would be developed from the current project’s methodology which studies religious history through legal materials. Following the discoveries of the PI’s paper on the High Qing persecution of Catholicism and other popular religions, the new study would inquire further into the legal and social development of Chinese society during the mid-Qing by investigating the archival materials that are mostly unavailable from earlier eras.

22400914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22400914.value: This project investigated Chinese judicial cases and different codes from the 17th to 18th centuries for two reasons. Firstly, it used legal materials to study socioeconomic history. These judicial materials reveal some unexplored corners of the Chinese society, such as the public toilet and homosexual activities in different parts of late Ming and early Qing China. The legal materials also give new insights in studying Catholicism and other popular religions in late imperials China, as they provide exclusive information from the persecutor’s side. Secondly, the study employed authentic records of judicial disputes to evaluate the changes of judicial system during the Ming-Qing Transition. The provincial judiciary of the Qing was markedly different from that of the Ming as the new Manchu rulers abolished several key posts such as prefectural judges and regional inspectors. Moreover, by looking closely to the tracks of development of legal apparatus related to judicial torture during the Qing period, the Manchu rulers’ assiduous efforts to keep traditional Chinese judicial means under better control can be observed. Another contribution of the project has been building a framework for an electronic database of the casebooks from Ming-Qing China (1368-1911).

22401414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22401414.value: 受到文化消費及文化資本等理論的啟發，是項研究從藝術經濟學、文化研究及藝術社會學與人類學的角度，視藝術市場為文化資料積累以進行考察（Bourdieu: 1984, 1993; Throsby: 1994, 1995, 1999, 200）。研究員將發掘有關觀眾的藝術經驗及其知識、社會地位、文化志趣等，並將之置於高端銷售、奢侈品消費及藝術收藏等社會脈絡，試圖發掘本地藝術生產的發展趨勢。計劃並引用文化消費及文化資本等理論，探討藝術巿場如何影響文化消費以至本港的文化發展。是項計劃是首次以本地藝術生態為中心的研究，其旨在討論全球藝術銷售網絡的流通，以歸納出拍賣行等機構如何影響文化資本的累積。研究也將涉及藝術巿場全球化的討論，即從資產流動的軌跡整理出文化消費的動態，藉以從文化消費的供求關係，申述文化演化的關鍵。

22401414.label: Realisation of objectives
22401414.value: Consumption, in the context of cultural developments in Hong Kong has been subject to a wide variety of speculation, expectation and, more, assumption. The assumptions have increasingly opened up a fracture between what is believed and what is assumptions about the ecology of the creative industries, art markets, buyers and, crucially, the audiences. Through all the data and research collected for this project, the single standout feature is that of the audience. The audience’s central role affects and effects the very ecology as the pivot point which activates spaces, defines cultural aesthetic and sustains growth. This research has begun to address some of the assumptions that have surfaced through unpacking how the ecology feeds, thrives and sustains in the layers of the environment. As stated previously, Hong Kong presents a unique market environment. It is, to all intents and purposes, an upside down model evolving from the secondary art markets. Historically, market emergence stems from either a state sponsorship of art or a collector’s patronage of art, and relies on established infrastructure; education, art schools, galleries, museums and cultural fascination. In Hong Kong this model is distinct in its differences. Rather we have experienced the emergence of sales before solid infrastructure, presenting an upside-down scenario. However, in identifying the current position in both the public and the private sectors, role of the art markets and its ecosystem, this research has revealed a pivotal role of the secondary markets in the promotion of arts and culture. Substantial quantitative data has been gathered from the sales of the two international heavyweight auction houses Christies and Sotheby’s. This data has been gathered from auction house sale data and cross compared against the markets in New York and London, further cross-referenced with economic fluctuations and gold prices. The data has indicated the continuing fiscal rise of the secondary markets. Of the key findings is the use of terms. For example, in the global market reports, New York remains the leading art market by sales, followed by London and then China. Yet the use of the term China is utterly misleading. Firstly, because for Hong Kong has independent sales and offices, but more fundamentally because China trades in a different currency with vastly different trade rules; such as monetary restrictions and non-taxable status of luxury goods in Hong Kong. To further confound, the global figures are not geographically defined offering a possible skewed interpretation. This project’s data has offered a geographical delineation. [Fig 1] Categories of sales are also subtlety different. However, finding like for like has become a pathway to audience differences. The extensive data gathered in this research has further delineated the categories of the art market. This is of key importance to understanding the market consumption. It is a common assumption that the art markets are selling art, but clearly this broad and generic term ‘art’ need considerable clarification. The most visible of the art markets are the high-end prestige sales. These are all but out of reach for the majority, inaccessible to most collectors and often national collections. It is, however, this small and exclusive portion that is the fodder of the media. However, none of the international salesrooms sell exclusively high end fine art. In the period of research, the categories of the sales shows an interesting yet complex dynamic range of objects and artefacts. Further suggesting that the market share is not exclusively visual art. In the private galleries market, the number of establishments has risen by almost 20%. Despite the growth in the presence, less than 10% would fall into the A list gallery, defined simply in terms of their international profile. However, of similar market size are galleries catering for Hong Kong artists and art spaces and NGO providers. Suggesting that while the numbers increase, the market shares remain the same. This would indicate that the appetite for the art is increasing but not necessarily developing. Of consideration here is the interplay between the private and public sector. As a city with scant public-sector presence currently, and few aesthetic markers in the visual arts, this has taken the private sector into unfamiliar territory as social educators regularly showing important works and substantially aiding creative development. This finding would seem to be further supported by the visitor numbers published by the public sector institutions. Despite an increasing number, the Hong Kong Museum of Art (HKMA) annual visitor number is still below one million. While showing apparent growth, the numbers are not close to comparable with other institutions in major cities; The National Gallery, London - 5.9 million; Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney - 1.5 million; The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York - 7 million. Rather, the annual visitor number compares in international terms, to a reasonably successful exhibition. Or put another way just over 50 days of Art Basel! Of course this simplistic comparison does not allow for evaluations of collections or visiting experiences. However, visitor numbers have become a consolation prize, suggesting a number is equitable to experience or interaction of the audience or successful engagement. They do not, and Hong Kong is woefully behind international progress on audience studies. The statistics do though reinforce the current consumption of the visual arts as primarily based in the private sector. Even bearing in mind the constraints of renovation and construction and any number of ‘pop up’ exhibitions, the fundamental need to have a concrete tangible space is paramount. The ritual of the site, space and experience is creating a distinct fracture in the future of audience practices and the future of the aesthetic experiences. This combination of circumstances has pushed the impact of the private sector further into the psyche and the foundations of audience. Reinforced by regular and privileged mini moments of significant art that increase the aesthetic markers and the one to one experiences of great art. Combining the sector numbers would offer a suggestion that there is a growing demand for visual art and it would seem logical to assume that there are an equally large number of visitors who have participated in arts and cultural activities. However, this is not a complete picture. A UK study on the impact of admission fees concluded that admission fees are immaterial to visitors. Rather, factors of time and interest were more pivotal to visiting an art museum. Of specific interest to this research context, is that of the repeat visitor. The study found that attendance increases were often due to the same audiences visiting more frequently – NOT necessarily from engaging new audiences. Suggesting that it is not the total visitor number that should be considered but rather the unique visitor who is important to sustainable development. This evaluation of consumption is supported in the Hong Kong contest by the research and data of this project and suggests that market dominance has been the catalyst for the growing ecology of art and public engagement. The art market has breathed life into the creative industries, building foundations of knowledge and education for audiences and provided the emerging production of art on an international stage.

22401414.value: There have been a 4 major outputs that have come directly from this project. The series of events; In the Age of Art: Consumption to Production began with; 1. In the Age of Art: Consumption to Production – Environment, Gentrification and Art Basel #1 –Research Film Production. Andrew Hevia, Fullbright Research Scholar. This was a collaborative documentary about the social ecology of Art Basel on the community, shot and produced by the PI’s Fulbright research scholar Andrew Hevia, an Oscar award winning producer (moonlight 2016). 22401414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22401414.value: The investigations into the historical exhibition of art in Hong Kong have led directly to further research and funding applications. This specific archival research, revealed a much larger and unexplored field of visual art study. The projects discoveries uncovered a significant history of the visual ethnography of Hong Kong which appears to have begun in the mid 19th Century. Constructed from the visual ephemera of the late 19th to mid 20th Centuries. This distinctly constructed ethnography offer significant insight into the histories and foundations of audience evolution and development. Of considerable interested is the constructed ideal of Hong Kong visual culture. In the late 19th Century this construction was through the export of the image and today we are encountering the import of the cultural industries through the art markets. This continuation effectively further dictating taste through contemporary art, Hong Kong playing host to the image and ideas of visual art for a trans-global audience. Following initial discoveries as a part of this project, a seed fund of $50,000 was awarded through the Robert Ho Foundation 'Through our Eyes' project 2017. This development is now the subject of a GRF funding application 2017.

22401414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22401414.value: Money is traditionally a dirty word in Art. Sale prices, rising values, market inflation and blockbusting sales are (apparently) at a discord with the process of aesthetics, creative sustainability and simple enjoyment. But this is not the case in Hong Kong where market dominance has been the catalyst for the growing ecology of art. This research has shown that it has rather facilitated the early exchanges of capital culture and begun the process of sustainable development through general interest, public awareness and, crucially, increased audiences. Here the secondary commercial markets have created a unique and prestigious environment in which art ecology has the opportunity to grow. From the public viewing of da Vinci’s masterpiece Salvator Mundi; to a shopping mall full of Monets’s, access to international aesthetic markers is coming from the distinct parent of commercial market place. The public sector, despite the progress underway in the expansion of HKMA and M+, are still somewhat behind. And now Art Basel has upped the ante further with queues of people waiting for tickets and over 70,000 visitors. In Hong Kong the money of the art market has breathed life into the creative industries and the emerging Hong Kong production of art.

To explain how we can use this framework for making progress in other areas of philosophical and more general interest (e.g., ethics, philosophy of science). 23400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23400014.value: Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that tackles questions involving the most fundamental components of reality. But how do we answer such questions? What is the best method for undergoing metaphysical inquiry? Recently, metaphysicians have become increasingly attracted to the idea that metaphysical problems can be approached by means of truthmaker theory, which engages metaphysical questions by asking what needs to exist in reality in order to make our beliefs true. This approach to metaphysics begins with the idea that what is true depends upon what exists in the world. When some belief is true, we explain its truth by way of investigating what does or doesn’t exist. For example, consider the “counterfactual” claim that if I were to place a glass of water in my freezer, it would eventually turn to ice. This is something that we believe to be true. But what makes it true? Its truth is not some primitive, inexplicable fact. Truthmaker theorists approach this question by asking what our world needs to be like in order for this counterfactual to be true. Does the world contain laws of nature that govern the behavior of chemical substances? Does the water possess certain kinds of properties that interact with the laws of nature to make the belief true? Many metaphysicians nowadays share the perspective that we can make progress on these questions by employing the tools of truthmaker theory. So what are these tools of truthmaker theory? Unfortunately, while interest in truthmaking has skyrocketed over the last decade, there remain few systematic treatments of what truthmaker theory is, and how philosophers should best practice it. My ambition in this project is to bring some much needed cohesion to truthmaker theory. Accordingly, my project is divided into two major components. The first is methodological. Far too little attention has been given to the method of truthmaker theory, and many of its critics believe that it is plagued by numerous unwarranted assumptions. To date, there exists only one systematic and sympathetic presentation of what truthmaker theory is, and many are unconvinced by it. My aim is to offer a different account which isn’t front-loaded with the many controversial assumptions that accompany other views. In the second, constructive, part of the project, I put my framework to work, showing how it can offer compelling answers to many metaphysical questions involving the nature of properties, time, numbers, moral values, and others. 形上學（Metaphysics）是哲學的一個分支，主要處理與真實最基本的構成部份有關的問題。可是我們要如何解答這類問題呢？而進行形上學探究的最好方法又是甚麼呢？ 近年來，致真論（Truthmaker Theory）作為處理形上學問題的方法，引來愈來愈多形上學家的關注。致真論的進路，是從「有甚麼東西需要真實存在才會使得我們的信念為真」這個問題入手，去試圖解答各種形上學的議題。這個形上學進路的出發點，在於我們有甚麼真理取決於世界上有甚麼東西存在。當一個信念為真，我們就以研究甚麼東西存在或不存在的方法，去解釋這個信念何以為真。 比如說，我們考慮一個虛擬事實（counterfactual）的宣稱：如果我把一杯水放到冰箱裡，它最後就會變成冰。我們相信這個宣稱為真。可是它之所以為真是如何奠定的呢？這個宣稱的真，並非初基的（primitive）、不可解釋的事實。而致真論者解答這個問題的進路，就是去問：這個世界上到底需要甚麼東西存在，才會使得這個虛擬事實的宣稱為真呢？這個世界是不是有一些自然法則，支配著化學物質的行為呢？是不是水本身擁有一些性質，而這些性質又與自然法則發生互動，使得上面的宣稱為真呢？現時，很多形上學家都認同一個觀點：有了致真論的工具，我們就能在解答形上學問題上面有所進展。 然而，這些致真論的工具到底是甚麼呢？很不幸，即使在過去十年，形上學家對致真論的興趣急升，可是對於甚麼是致真論的這個問題本身，系統性的處理很少，而且對於哲學家該怎樣運用致真論的研究也不多。我進行這個計劃的願景，就是為致真論提供一個極其需要的統合處理。因此，我的計劃分成兩大部份。第一部份是方法論。對於致真論方法的研究一直很少受到關注，而且很多致真論的批評者都認為它有太多缺乏根據的假設。到目前為止，學界中對於甚麼是致真論這個問題，只有一個有系統的、站在贊同立場的闡述，而且很多哲學家也不被說服。我的目標是提出一個不同於其他看法的理論，不會一開始就預定了很多備受爭議的假設。而計劃的第二部份是建設性的工作。我會把我的理論框架加以應用，去證明致真論如何在各種形上學問題上，都能提供令人信服的解答。這些問題包括了性質的本質、時間、數字本身、道德價值等等。

23400314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23400314.value: As genetic research aimed at extending our life expectancy and at reducing the side-effects of ageing advances, new fundamental philosophical issues arise: is it rational to invest resources in these life-extending technologies? What kind of biomedical research with such aims should be permitted? What are the limits of our personal identity? On the one hand, several scientists and bioethicists have welcomed the prospect of extending the lengths of our lives and the possibility of manipulating our biological nature in order to lessen (or, ideally, eliminate) the impairing effects of old age. On the other hand, other thinkers have raised a series of objections not only to the future employment of techniques that manipulate our genes, but also to the overall desirability of any life-extending enhancement. One family of these objections is based on the alleged negative consequences that such technologies would have for our personal identity, that is, for the continuity of what makes one person the same over time. More specifically, Mary’s rational justification for being self-concerned about extending the length of her life essentially includes her belief that it will be her who will benefit from such additional years. Critics also argue that if we increase significantly the life span of ‘normal’ individuals, then the relation of personal identity cannot hold between the various stages of the life of the biological organism involved. In recent years, debates on personal identity and on what matters for survival have flourished and questioned some of the assumptions discussed in the mentioned criticisms. For example, Eric Olson has argued in favor of the essential role played by the continuity of the same organism in the re-identification of the same person over time. In addition, Derek Parfit has criticized the requirement that what matters in survival is the relation of personal identity, undermining the previous reasoning against life-extension. My research stems from the need to update the current debate on life-extending technologies with the most recent research on the self and personal identity. This connection, in turn, may provide new insights on our conception of what constitutes a person, in particular, in relation to scenarios in which our ‘normal’ temporal margins are severally challenged. In addition, the exploration of such issues can have consequences in further advancing also the traditional religious debate on the rationality and desirability of immortality by introducing new elements of evaluation (i.e. the desirability of earthly immortality). 基因研究致力延長我們的壽命，亦減少年邁帶來的負面影響。然而，這種研究亦使新的根本哲學問題出現：投放資源在這些生命科技上，合理嗎？以延長壽命、抑制衰老為目標的生物醫學研究之中，哪些是應被容許的？我們的個人同一性有甚麼限制？一方面，有些科學家和生物倫理學家樂見我們有望延長人類的壽命，也樂見我們可以操控自身的生物結構，從而減少（甚至希望消除）身體老化帶來的勞損。另一方面，其他思想家提出一系列的反駁。這針對的問題不止是基因研究應不應繼續下去，還包括人工延長壽命這一套究竟是好是壞。其中一類反駁的立論根據是這樣的：基因科技會削弱我們的個人同一性，也就是說會降低同一個人之所以在時間上繼續為同一個人的延續性。更確切地說，某甲之所以關心延長她自己的壽命，其理由之一是她相信多出了那部份的壽命是令她「自己」受惠的。然而，反對者辯說：如果某正常個體的壽命增長太多，會擾亂本應只是同一個體生命中的不同階段，令其無法建立起個體同一性。近年來，關係到個人同一性、以及生命中最有價值是甚麼的辯論越來越多，亦有質疑上述批評背後的預設。例如，Eric Olson認為我們之所以能鑑定某個人經歷長時間仍保持為同一個人，關鍵是因為作為一個生物本身有其延續性，而非那人心理上的延續性。還有，Derek Parfit批評個人同一性的要求，認為生存中要緊的並不是維繫個人同一性。這就動搖了上述反對人工延長壽命的論證。本研究的緣起是有見於當下的生命科技辯論有必要深化，原因是要考慮到關於自我及個人同一性的最新研究。加上這層考慮，能使我們對「甚麼是人」的問題有嶄新的思考。尤其是在我們「正常」的壽命上限面臨重大變革的時候。另外，探究這些議題亦可為傳統宗教中關於追求不朽是否合理、是否可欲等問題加入新的討論元素（此處指在世不朽之問題）。

23400314.label: Realisation of objectives
23400314.value: Realisation of objectives: 1. To advance the debate on the ethics and desirability of human enhancements, in particular those enhancements aimed at extending our life span and at reducing the effects of ageing. This topic is discussed in chapter 7 of my forthcoming book and in a paper to be submitted soon. In particular, I discuss Parfit's claim that identity is not what matters in survival. In the book chapter I also draw several connections between soul-, narrative-, physical-, psychological-based theories of personal identity and several proposed futuristic life-extending enhancements, such as cryonics and mental uploading. Claims regarding the desirability of such technologies are then evaluated. For instance, holding a psychological theory of personal identity which includes the claim that psychological connections must be realised by their 'normal' causal chain (e.g. brain continuity), implies that one may find reasons to opt for cryonics instead of mental uploading—or to promote research in cryonics instead of mental uploading (and IA). 2.To improve on the current debate on the nature of the self and personal identity by taking into account how these theories deal with issues related to immortality and survival. This topic is discussed in various chapters of my forthcoming book and in the paper published in the prestigious journal 'Philosophical Studies' (see list of publications). I discuss Bernard Williams' theory of personal identity in the forthcoming paper in the Archiv für Geschichte der Philosophie. I discuss one the definition of a religious belief in the paper published in the Neue Zeitschrift für Systematische Theologie und Religionsphilosophie. More specifically, in the papers I discuss, among other things, some conceptual issues arising from a contemporary theory of our nature called 'animalism', how religious beliefs are individuated, and several thought-experiments related to our survival and reduplication in the context of B. Williams' early criticism of psychology-based theories of personal identity. The book introduces most of the current theories of the nature of the self and of our diachronic persistence through time. 3.To clarify the technical distinctions between different kinds of life-extending technologies (genetic, pharmacological, and so on) and their connection with specific ethical and moral concerns. This topic is discussed in various chapters of my forthcoming book (in particular chapter 7 and 8). I further discuss these issues in a paper to be submitted soon. More specifically, I claim that there is a set of life-extending technologies and considerations regarding personal identity and what matters in survival may help distinguish which of these existing technologies are rational to further pursue, privately or as publicly funded research projects. In addition, considerations regarding personal identity and what matters in survival may help us discern which forms of life-extending should be developed in the future. Certain lines of research may be irrational qua researches on life-extension, given our best theory of what matters in survival. The life-extending technologies under consideration here are not yet developed or are in their infancy (i.e. cryonics). Life-extending technologies may offer a) in case they do not yet exist (i.e. mental uploading), hypothetical thought-experiment to test our theories of personal identity and of what matters in survival; b) in case such life-extending technologies exist or are to a certain extend available, they can provide a series of test-cases to rethink some of the key concepts used in the debate. For instance, there are technologies that can keep alive the body of a patient for a certain amount of time even after cortical death. These technologies may offer us an occasion to rethink what matters in survival. Among the distinctions drawn in my book, I distinguish between ‘strong lifespan extensions’ and ‘weak lifespan extensions’. The former are the results of technologies that increase both average and maximum lifespan, while the latter are the result of an incremental surge in life expectancy obtained through improvements in the treatment and prevention of disease. Along with these two types of lifespan extensions, we can also include ‘deep lifespan extensions’, the ultimate aim of which is the elimination or interruption of the process of ageing—‘deep’ extension in the sense of, in principle, endless. Life extending technologies can then be classified as those technologies aimed at producing one or more of the previous kinds of extensions. 4.To carefully examine those arguments against and in favour of human enhancements based on philosophical theories of personal identity. This topic is discussed in chapter 7 of my forthcoming book and in a paper to be submitted soon. Among the arguments evaluated in this regard is Walter Glannon's claim that, since psychological connections would necessarily deteriorate over an extensive length of time, certain life-extending technologies may not be rational to pursue or, at least, an actual subject may not find it rational for her to engage in such technologies given the diminished psychological connections between her now another entity, vaguely physically related to her but significantly different from a psychological point of view. This claim is criticised by applying a narrative approach to personal identity. Among the other things, I object to Glannon's claim that, if his point were true, we may not find it rational for infants or adolescent to improve, even significantly some of their psychological features. 5.To assess the rationality and/or desirability of immortality, and its connections with traditional religious beliefs in different traditions (reincarnation, Karma, resurrection). This topic is discussed in various chapters of my forthcoming book (chapter 2 for Buddhism, chapter 7 for what matters in survival, chapter 1 and 8 for various religious perspectives, chapter 3 and 8 for Confucian relational views of the self). For instance, in the chapter on Buddhist theories of no-self, I discuss various attempts to reconcile the idea that there isn't any continuous self through time with the idea of reincarnation. The Christian doctrine of resurrection is discussed in relation to various accounts of the nature of the soul in various chapters of my book (in particular, 1 and 8). 6.To produce and submit a number of articles to various philosophical journals (both general philosophy journals, such as Mind, Philosophical Quarterly, Philosophical Studies, and more specialized journals, such as Bioethics and Journal of Medical Ethics). See the list of accepted papers and the book contract. The book manuscript is due on the 1st of July. At the moment (29/4) the book is 90% finished: I just need to write the introduction and edit it for internal consistency.

23400314.label: Major findings and research outcome
23400314.value: Papers Accepted The Early Reception of Bernard Williams’ Reduplication Argument (1956-62), Archiv für Geschichte der Philosophie (forthcoming). (Journal rated A in the old philosophy journal list) The reduplication argument advanced by Bernard Williams in 1956 has greatly stimulated the contemporary debate on personal identity. The argument relies on a famous thought experiment that, although not new in the history of philosophy, has engaged some of the most influential philosophers on the topic, among the others, Derek Parfit and John Perry. In this paper I discuss the early reception of Williams' reduplication argument and clarify some of its main points. The Definition of Religion, Super-empirical Realities, and Mathematics, Neue Zeitschrift für Systematische Theologie und Religionsphilosophie (2016). (Journal rated A in the old philosophy journal list) Providing a precise definition of “religion”—or an analysis in terms of sufficient and necessary conditions of the concept of religion—has proven to be a difficult task, more so in light of the diverse types of practices considered religious by scholars. Here, I discuss Kevin Schilbrack’s recent definition of “religion”, elaborate it and raise several objections, one of which is based on a specific theory in philosophy of mathematics: mathematical realism. My main conclusion is that also Schilbrack's definition is not satisfying and the definition of what counts as a religious belief is still highly controversial. Andrea Sauchelli (forthcoming). The Animal, the Corpse, and the Remnant-Person. Philosophical Studies:1-14. (Journal rated A* in the new journal list) I argue that a form of animalism that does not include the belief that ‘human animal’ is a substance-sortal has a dialectical advantage over other versions of animalism. The main reason for this advantage is that Phase Animalism, the version of animalism described here, has the theoretical resources to provide convincing descriptions of the outcomes of scenarios problematic for other forms of animalism. Although Phase Animalism rejects the claim that ‘human animal’ is a substance-sortal, it is still appealing to those who believe that our nature is continuous or of a similar kind to that of other physical entities. Book Contracts I signed a contract with Routledge for the book ‘Personal Identity and Applied Ethics’. Manuscript due date: July 2016. This book proposes a systematic discussion of various theories of our nature and of personal identity. For more details, please see the book proposal and the details specified in the book contract. Visiting Scholar Oxford Uehiro Centre for Applied Ethics, University of Oxford (Sep-Oct 2015) Papers Submitted The Will to Make-Believe Work in progress Life-extending Technologies and Narrative Identity

23400314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23400314.value: I originally planned to work on several papers aimed at clarifying the connections between personal identity and applied ethics, but I realised that this objective can be achieved more effectively by writing an introductory book on the topic. Such a book-project developed in time and I signed a contract with Routledge. Since the book offers a variety of ways in which the contemporary debate can be developed—directions which have not been thoroughly explored in the current literature—I am planning on developing some of these lines. For instance, I am interested in developing the role of relational accounts of personal identity and of our own nature and their relation to narrative views of the self. In turn, this is of relevance for various debates in practical ethics (again, abortion, life-extending technologies, survival, etc.). I am also developing a course tentatively called 'Creation Ethics' as an extension of certain remarks I suggested in chapter 8 of my book.

23400314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23400314.value: The central aim of my project has been that of providing a systematic treatment of the relationship between our nature—what we are, in the most general sense—, our personal identity through time, and several debates in practical ethics (life-extending technologies, abortion, survival, etc.). By 'what we are' is here meant what you and I essentially are, the kind of entities we are (e.g. human organisms, soul-body compounds, psychological entities, embodied brains, etc.). These theories influence (even simply as implicit beliefs) our decisions regarding the rationality of certain practical issues at the beginning and end of life. A clear example is the debate on the morality of abortion: we find in the relevant literature formulations such as 'the foetus is one of us', 'the human being begins at conception', or 'the foetus is not a person'. However, it is not clear what key terms like 'human being', 'person', 'being one of us' stand for. By providing an answer to the question 'what are we?' we also have the theoretical means to address questions such as 'when did we begin?' and, in turn, to evaluate claims that having an abortion is similar to killing 'one like us'.

23500014.label: Project Objectives
23500014.value: To develop a theoretic framework to describe the relationship between communicators, source heterogeneity, source credibility, and message persuasiveness. To enrich our knowledge regarding the communication process by studying the role of communicators' relation. To demonstrate the impact of the communicators' relation on source heterogeneity, source credibility, and message persuasiveness via three studies. Specifically, a mediation model is expected to explain the impact of the communicators' relation on message persuasiveness. To propose a boundary condition to moderate the impact of source heterogeneity on credibility. One possible moderator could be the required topic knowledge. When the topic requires advanced knowledge and expertise, communicators with similar background may provide stronger evidence to validate the message. In this case, source homogeneity, rather than heterogeneity, may enhance source credibility.

23500014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23500014.value: Individual decision is often influenced by friends. For example, consumers may decide to read an online article or watch a Youtube video because their friends recommend or endorse the content on Facebook. Prior research has studied the influence of communication source from an individual level perspective (e.g., close friend vs. seldom contact acquaintance; Brown and Reingen 1987; Rogers 1983) and an aggregate level perspective (e.g., average product rating; Chevalier and Mayzlin 2006 ) and suggested that messages transmitted from close friends or from a larger size of people are more influential, however little is known about the impact of relation between recommenders (or communicators) on message persuasiveness. For example, if both Tom and Mary are my friends and they simultaneously share the same article from a local newspaper with me, will my decision to read the article be affected by how I perceive the relation between Tom and Mary? This research aims to address a communication situation like this. That is, how do consumers respond in a multiple senders communication context? Will the message be more persuasive and effective when communicators are friends or non-friends? We suggest that relation between communicators can affect message persuasiveness. According to the model of communication (Berlo 1960), when a communication source is more credible, the message is more persuasive. Based on this model, we suggest that a collective source credibility is a function of communicators' relation. Specifically, when communicators have weak relations, perceived source credibility will be higher because the two sources are perceived as more heterogeneous and independent. the perception of source heterogeneity is likely to be higher. When information is transmitted from a diverse source, it may be perceived as more credible and therefore be more persuasive. We propose three lab studies to test the proposed mechanism. Study 1 aims to show the basic communicators' relation effect on message persuasiveness. Study 2 examines the underlying mechanism by measuring perceived source credibility and perceived source heterogeneity. In the last study, we plan to provide a boundary condition by investigating a situation when high source heterogeneity would lead to lower credibility. These findings are expected to contribute to marketing practitioners in developing a more effective social media strategy by presenting a convincing set of information endorsers. We also aim to contribute to the literature of WOM communication and persuasion by investigating the role of communicators' relation in a multiple senders communication context. 本研究探討口碑行銷中,訊息傳遞者之間的關係如何影響訊息接受者的訊息接收. 我們預期, 當訊息傳遞者之間的關係較為疏遠時(例如非朋友關係) 而不是緊密時 (例如朋友關係), 訊息更具有說服力, 理由是訊息接受者所接受的訊息可信度會比較高.

24100014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100014.value: 目的：此課題的目的是提高難溶，滲透性差藥物分子的口服生物利用度。這些藥物通常都是BCS IV類的藥物，而它們佔世衛組織基本藥物目錄還不到10％。 背景：口服藥物必須在胃腸道溶解方可吸收。因此，溶解和滲透性是口服生物利用度的主要因素。 BCS IV類的藥物通常難以開發，因為其溶解和滲透性都是吸收的限制因素。 無定形固體分散技術(ASD）是一項最先進多功能技術。它通過達到短暫的過飽和度來提高其溶解度。它可被應用于具有不同特性的藥物，也可以來提高劑量，此外, 這項技術也易於製備。最重要的是它能增加溶解度但不會影響滲透性。然而，它在BCS IV類藥物的應用卻很少。 假設：通過藥用輔料來抑制藥物外排可以改善外排限制性藥物的透過性，但此方法應用很少。ASD通常側重於將飽和度最大化。但對飽和度與藥物轉運的關係到現仍然不清楚。我們將會研究這些因素會如何改善藥物的轉運和生物利用度。我們推測，過飽和度和“外排抑制”的表面活性劑都能顯著改善BCS IV類外排限制性藥物的轉運。因此，ASD則可以通過控制這兩個因素來對BCS IV類藥物進行優化。 建議的工作：沙奎那韋和速尿將被用作BCS IV的模型藥物。為了將我們的理念應用到中醫中，我們也研究了丹參酮IIA。這些都是難溶，生物利用度低的外排底物。我們會（目標1）研究過飽和度對於藥物運輸的影響。通過研究在Caco-2細胞不同飽和度的滲透性/藥物轉運，我們將確定過飽和度是如何影響沉澱和藥物轉運的。我們也會（目標2）了解“外排抑制”表面活性劑對於藥物運輸的影響。通過使用Caco-2細胞和統計設計，我們將確定表面活性劑以及其和其他組分之間相互作用對于藥物轉運的影響。最後，我們將（目標3）製備ASD並且在體外和體內進行評價。通過使用不同攪拌速度下的溶解滲透模型來研究其對過飽和，沉澱和藥物運輸的影響。我們的統計設計將有助於確定不同配方變量以及相互作用對于過飽和度，藥物轉運，和在體內表現的影響。模型的預測性將通過比較體外和體內數據來確定。 意義：我們不會因為生物利用度低而去放棄那些安全，高效率和靶向性的藥物。我們的方法將作為一種篩選工具，為藥物難題提供科學依據。而且將被應用於醫藥研發。我們的體外模型會解釋配方變量是怎樣與生物系統相互作用從而提高生物利用度的。我們的模型改進后將會預測藥物傳遞系統在體內的表現，省去了實驗;這將降低成本和縮短週期。我們的技術可能復活一些“死”分子。它也可能會解決中醫藥傳遞的問題。此研究在當前以及未來都具有很大的潛力。

24100014.label: Realisation of objectives
24100014.value: Basically, both committed objectives have been 100% completed. As stated in the mid-term report, in order to make the study more impactful, we decided to change the model compound from furosemide to paclitaxel. Paclitaxel is a widely used anti-cancer drug. However, oral formulations of this drug are not currently available due to the extremely challenging biopharmaceutical properties of paclitaxel, namely poor drug solubility and efflux by p-glycoproteins (pgp) substrate, which result in very poor oral bioavailability. As a result, there is a pressing need to devise effective formulations to overcome the delivery challenges. Objective 1: A. Preparation of amorphous solid dispersions: Originally, we proposed to apply a solvent shift method to induce supersaturation and use polymers to sustain it. However, the solvent shift transiently generated an extremely high level of supersaturation, which could not be maintained by a wide range of polymers. In other words, immediate drug precipitation was observed during the solvent shift process. As a result, we adopted an alternative approach to circumvent this hurdle. We prepared amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel by using a rotary evaporator. Briefly, paclitaxel:polymer=25:75 or 50:50 w/w was dissolved in a volatile organic solvent which was subsequently removed using a rotary evaporator under vacuum. The resulted powder was collected, milled and analyzed by using a DSC to confirm the amorphous nature of the drug. We have screened three polymers with different chemistry, HPMC AS, HPMC E3 and PVP K30, to prepare amorphous solid dispersions by using this method. B. Solubility assessment of the amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel: Our ultimate goal is to design a system that can simultaneously over the solubility and permeability challenges. Before assessing the permeability enhancement of the amorphous solid dispersions, we assessed the solubility improvement of paclitaxel by using these delivery systems. Accurately weighed powder of amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel was added to Hank’s balance salt solution (HBSS) with shaking and samples were taken after 1 hour and analyzed by using a UPLC. Basically, we found that amorphous solid dispersions prepared with different polymers yielded different solubility and our results provided clear scientific rationale for formulation development. C. Selection of a cell model for studying drug absorption: We selected MDCK II as a cell mode to study drug absorption as this model is commonly employed to study oral drug delivery. MDCK-MDR1 was also employed to study the impact of pgp in limiting drug uptake. D. Cytotoxicity of the amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel: We intended to assess the permeability enhancing effect in a cell model. In order not to complicate the interpretation of the data due to cytotoxicity of the prepared amorphous solid dispersions, a MTT cytotoxicity study was conducted. It is obvious that both pure polymers and amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel did not cause any cellular damage relative to the control (no drug treatment) after 3.5-hour incubation. As a result, in the following cellular uptake study, the improved uptake is not attributable to the cytotoxicity of our samples. E. Determine the maximum permeability achieved by solubility enhancement and Determine the optimum supersaturation level to maximize the drug transport: We employed rhodamine 123, a pgp substrate with fluorescent properties, to elucidate the pgp inhibitory effects of paclitaxel at supersaturated levels provided by amorphous solid dispersions. Both rhodamine 123 and paclitaxel are pgp substrates and they competitively bind to the same target. In other words, an increased solubility of paclitaxel enhances the cellular uptake of rhodamine 123. We monitored the cellular uptake of rhodamine 123 in the presence of paclitaxel at different levels of supersaturation provided by amorphous solid dispersions. F. Determine how a hydrophilic polymer affects the precipitation and drug transport: In order to elucidate how a hydrophilic polymer impacts drug precipitation which in turn influences cellular uptake, we employed amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel by using three different polymers, HPMC AS, HPMC E3 and PVP K30, in this study. A precipitation study was conducted on these three amorphous solid dispersions and they were also employed in a cellular uptake study. We also studied the effect of polymer concentration on drug precipitation and cellular uptake. Amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel:polymer=1:1 and 1:3 were prepared and the drug precipitation and cellular uptake was conducted. Objective 2: This experiment was completed smoothly as planned. In this study, we intended to demonstrate the pgp inhibitory activity of polymeric surfactant, PEG-b-PCL and show its capability to improve the cellular uptake of paclitaxel in MDCK-MDR1. We have selected PEG-b-PCL (570:750), a pgp inhibitor, and PEG-b-PCL (5k:10k), a non-pgp inhibitor, in the current study. A. Cytotoxicity of different polymeric surfactants: The first criterion is that the selected surfactant(s) is not cytotoxic. We have conducted a screening of surfactants by using a MTT or trypan blue cytotoxicity assay. Unfortunately, a number of well-known pgp inhibitory surfactants such as Tween 80, Solutol HS15, etc. are cytotoxic and therefore they cannot be used in our study. As a result, based on our preliminary data, PEG-b-PCL was selected for future studies. B. Preparation and characterization of blank and paclitaxel-loaded micelles: Blank and paclitaxel-loaded micelles were prepared by a previously established anti-solvent method. The particles of the micelles were characterized by DLS and their morphology was assessed by TEM. Drug loading encapsulation and drug release were also examined. C. Cytotoxicity of paclitaxel-loaded PEG-b-PCL micelles: Similar to Objective 1 for amorphous solid dispersions, to eliminate the complication of misinterpretation of the uptake data due to cytotoxicity, we assessed the cytotoxicity of paclitaxel-loaded PEG-b-PCL micelles. The cytotoxicity of PEG-b-PCL micelles in MDCK II and MDCK-MDR1 was assessed by a SRB assay for 3.5 hours. Basically, both block copolymers were non-toxic (> 85% viability) up to 500 μM. D. In vitro Rhodamine-123 (R-123) and Coumarin-6 uptake study: To demonstrate the pgp-inhibitory activity of the polymers, cellular uptake of Rhodamine-123, a pgp substrate, was assessed in MDCK II and MDCK-MDR1 in the presence of PEG-b-PCL (570:750) and PEG-b-PCL (5k:10k) at different concentrations. It is expected that pgp inhibition by PEG-b-PCL (570:750) will lead improved cellular uptake of R-123. Improved cellular uptake of R-123 in the presence of PEG-b-PCL (5k:10k) or in MDCK II may be related to other non-pgp membrane enhancing effect. E. In vitro paclitaxel uptake study: As a proof-of-concept, to demonstrate the capability of PEG-b-PCl micelles to improve the permeability of a real problematic drug, cellular uptake of paclitaxel from the two drug-loaded PEG-b-PCL micelles was assessed in MDCK II and MDCK-MDR1 at different drug concentration.

24100014.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100014.value: Objective 1: The amorphous solid dispersions of paclitaxel prepared appear to be non-cytotoxic (close to 100% viability) and all the polymers chosen increased the drug solubility by 12-22x. Paclitaxel-loaded dispersions enhanced the cellular uptake of rhodamine 123, a pgp substrate, in MDCK-MDR1. However, the maximum level of rhodamine 123 uptake never reached a plateau at 20x supersaturation. However, the 20x supersaturation was the highest concentration we could achieve and therefore, we might not able to achieve complete pgp inhibition by increasing the solubility of paclitaxel with amorphous solid dispersions. Cellular uptake of paclitaxel from the dispersion of HPMCAS was significantly better than other amorphous solid dispersions. Drug:polymer ratio has minimal influence on drug precipitation. Interestingly, higher polymer concentrations yielded better cellular uptake. Or data clearly indicated that formulation selection purely based on precipitation does not necessarily predict the absorption behavior of amorphous solid dispersions. Objective 2: Among different potential pgp inhibiting surfactants under investigation, only PEG-b-PCL appears to be safe (>80% viability). As a result, this polymeric surfactant was selected for our study. PEG-b-PCL (750:570) and PEG-b-PCL (5k:10k) enhanced the solubility of paclitaxel by approximately 1,500x and 5,600x compared to the solubility of the free drug. PEG-b-PCL (750:570) increased both P-gp and non P-gp substrate cellular uptake and increased the apparent permeability coefficient of a P-gp substrate. Our results clearly demonstrate the potential applications of polymeric surfactants in overcoming the solubility of permeability challenges of oral drug delivery simultaneously, which is the ultimate goal of this funded project. We have exceeded our committed objectives by conducting a preliminary animal study. PEG-b-PCL micelles efficiently enhanced the oral bioavailability of paclitaxel in rats. In line with the cell-based assay in Objective 2, PEG-b-PCL (750:570) provided a better oral bioavailability compared with PEG-b-PCL (5k:10k), indicating that both solubility enhancement and pgp inhibition play a pivotal role in improving the oral bioavailability of paclitaxel. Furthermore, we also exceeded our objectives by assessing the impact of the route of administration in improving bioavailbility of problematic molecules. We applied sublingual delivery to overcome the metabolism/pgp issies of drugs by employing ropinirole as a model drug. Th sublingual route improved the oral bioavailability substantially and the results were published in Colloids Surf B Biointerfaces. 2018 Mar 1;163:9-18. It would be interesting to combine the findings in Objective 1 and 2 and the sublingual route to overcome the current challenges of oral drug delivery.

24100014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100014.value: 1. An extensive animal study: The current study mainly focused on in vitro cellular study. Although we also did experiment in animals and the data appear to be encouraging, our in vivo data are quite preliminary. As a result, a more extensive animal study is required to validate our in vitro findings for proof-of-concept. 2. A combinational strategy to maximize bioavailability: In the current study, we studied the impact of amorphous solid dispersion and polymeric micelles independently. It would be interesting to combine the two techniques to determine whether any synergistic improvement in cellular uptake/oral bioavailability can be achieved. 3. The impact of polymer block length: In Objective 2, as a starting point, we only assessed the impact of polymeric surfactant , PEG-b-PCL, with two extreme block length. We intend to systematically to assess the influence of polymer block length on pgp inhibition and permeability improvement. This will provide s strong scientific rationale for future formulation development. 4. Extend our strategy to other model poorly soluble and permeable drugs: In the current study, we only employed paclitaxel as a model compound. In order to generalize our concept, it would be necessary to apply out technology to other poorly soluble and permeable drugs for proof-of-concept.

24100014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100014.value: The oral drug delivery is the most preferred route of drug administration and it is well accepted by patients. Poor drug solubility and permeability are the two major challenges in oral drug delivery which precludes development some of drug molelcules into oral dosage forms. We cannot afford to lose safe, highly efficacious and targeted drugs because of their poor biopharmaceutic properties. As the starting point of a sustained effort to develop delivery solutions, our work will immediately serve as a screening tool and provide scientific justifications to guide development strategies for challenging drug molecules. This will be widely applied to Pharmaceutical R&D to improve efficiency. Our in vitro models will help us to understand how different formulation variables interact with the biological system to impact ioavailability, which is critical but currently missing in drug delivery research. After further refinement, our models will predict the in vivo performance of drug delivery systems without running animal or human studies; this will reduce cost and shorten development timelines. Our technology potentially resurrects “dead” molecules to treat various diseases. It will also shed light on overcoming delivery challenges of TCM. Obviously, this has unlimited potential at the present time and in the future.

24100114.label: Realisation of objectives
24100114.value: Objective 1 : We successfully recruited 27 each of age-sex-education matched young treatment-naïve BPII, UD and HC. All imaging protocols, serum collection and behavioural data collection were completed and analysed in these subjects. Integrity of a priori white matter tracts and energy metabolism of major affective neural circuits were determined by means of diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and MRS. DTI was successfully completed for all subjects. MRS on 4 metabolites expressed as ratios over creatine – (i) Glx (Glutamate [Glu] + Glutamine [Gln]), (ii) Glu (iii) N-acetylaspartate (NAA), (iv) myo-inositol (mI) in three regions of interest (ROIs) – (i)bilateral supragenual cingulate cortex (sgACC), (ii) bilateral pregenual cingulate cortex (pgACC), (iii), left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) was completed for all but one UD subject. Choline and Gln were excluded from analysis due to overlapping signals with creatine and pixel-wise variance exceeding acceptable limits (20% SD) respectively. Excessive pixel-wise variance was also found in sgACC for 1 BPII subject, which was also excluded from analysis. Serum levels of lipid hydroperoxide (LPH) and 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) were examined as concurrent peripheral measures of lipid peroxidation. In total, serum samples for 81 subjects were collected and stored, but only that for 73 subjects were analysed. Laboratory error made it impossible for analysis of samples of 8 (5 BPII, 2 UD, 1 HC) subjects to proceed as of the date of completion report. We are now just able to properly process the samples again for analysis to complete soon. Of the analyzed samples, 4-HNE was not detected for 37 subjects (10 BPII, 14 UD, 13 HC) in two assaying attempts using two different analysis kits. Possible reasons include low HNE concentrations falling beneath detection thresholds and prolonged storage, albeit the latter is less unlikely given older samples were not more likely to have non-detectable readings. Since causes for non-detection cannot be determined conclusively, the 37 undetected values were treated as missing in our analysis. Analysis regarding 4-HNE should be interpreted with caution owing to small sample count. Objective 2: Across the whole sample, interactions were first examined within outcome pairs - DTI x serum measures and MRS x serum measures. Since no between-group differences in energy metabolites were obtained from relevant ROIs on MRS, DTI x MRS correlational analysis did not proceed. Interactions were then examined amongst the two patient groups, with variables differentiating BPII from UD in univariate analysis being entered into a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) after dimensional reduction using principal component analysis (PCA) to account for multicollinearity. Univariate analysis was performed on the following variables: -Socio-demographic: age, sex, education, marital status, monthly income, employment -Clinical: Specifiers (rapid cycling, atypical, melancholic, mixed), lifetime number of affective episodes, lifetime duration of depressive episodes, duration of current depressive episode, number of anxiety, psychotic, obsessive compulsive and somatoform comorbidities, Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale, Young Mania Rating Scale, Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, Global Assessment of Functioning, Short-form 36 health survey -Family history: bipolarity and depression -Intelligence test: three-subtest Short Form of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale-III -Neuropsychological assessment: Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, Trail-making test A and B, Stroop Colour and Word Test, Verbal fluency and Wechsler Memory scale -All the aforementioned MRS, DTI and serum measures Variables entered into PCA and LDA: 1.Rapid cycling specifier 2.Lifetime number of affective episodes 3.Family history of bipolarity 4.Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) 5.Trail making test - Task A (TMT-A) 6.Parietal part of right superior longitudinal fasciculus AD (rSLF-parietal AD) 7.Temporal part of right superior longitudinal fasciculus AD (rSLF-temporal AD) Delay in project completion and measures taken to overcome problems- Recruitment was difficult as many patients have received medications, or would soon need to receive treatment given clinical need, by the time they first presented to the clinic for booking. We have expended tremendous effort in facilitating all study procedures to complete before first clinic appointment, to promote the study amongst clinic staff and also address logistical issues with them. Further delay has incurred from unforeseen administrative hurdles on the occasion of internal policy changes in the department of Radiology, leading to withholding of MRI scanning for some months. With efforts in inter-departmental liaison, MRI scanning was resumed with administrative measures taken to address the previous policy issues.

24100114.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100114.value: 6.1 Major findings and research outcome Demographics: Twenty-seven each of BPII depressed, UD and HC subjects were recruited. Subjects had a mean age of 23.68 (SD 3.76). 68% were female, and 74% had tertiary education. No significant differences in age [F(2,78)=1.11, p=.33], sex (p=.44), or education (p=.28) were found. Objective 1: DTI: Repeated measures ANOVA of grouping x bilateral-combined WM measures showed no significant interactions in FA, RD and AD. Unilateral tract analysis using one-way ANOVA found significantly lower AD in rSLF-parietal (t= 2.8, p=.007) and rSLF-temporal (t = 3.5, p=.001) in UD compared to BPII, suggesting greater structural connectivity loss in UD. No difference was observed between BPII and HC. MRS: One-way ANOVA test for grouping x concentrations of four metabolites in three ROIs found significant difference in Glu/Cr in sgACC [BPII (x̄ = 1.67), UD (x̄ = 1.66) and HC (x̄ = 1.56)] [F(2, 76) = 3.36, p=.04], although pair-wise differences were not detected in Tukey HSD post-hoc. Serum: Repeated-measures ANOVA found significant main effect for measurement type (LPH or 4-HNE) [F(1, 33) = 21.83, p<.001] but not diagnosis [F(2, 33) = 2.19, p=.13]. Interaction between measurement type and diagnostic grouping was insignificant [F(2, 33) = 2.08, p=.14]. Effect of grouping on LPH was insignificant [F(2,69) = 0.36, p=.70] on one-way ANOVA. Objective 2: Serum x DTI measures: LPH positively correlated with left SLF-parietal RD (N=72, p=.04, r = 0.24), consistent with the link between lipid peroxidation and structural connectivity loss. Conflicting findings were found for 4-HNE - its negative correlations with right anterior thalamic radiation RD (N=36, p=.02, r = -0.38) , rSLF-temporal AD (N=36, p=.02, r = -0.38), and positive correlation with FA at forceps minor (N=36, p=.03, r = 0.53). Serum x MRS: Multiple regressions found no significant relationships. PCA + LDA: Two principal components (PC), with strongest loadings on right-sided structural integrity and episodic recurrence respectively, were included in the LDA, wherein a cut-off of 0.725 best predicted BPII grouping amongst patients. Linear discriminant function = 0.89 PC1 + 0.26 PC2 PC1: 0.38 YMRS +0.31 rapid cycling specifier +0.31 lifetime number of affective episodes +0.33 family history of bipolarity -0.28 TMT-A +0.47 rSLF-parietal AD +0.51 rSLF-temporal AD PC2: -0.26 YMRS +0.53 rapid cycling specifier +0.48 lifetime number of affective episodes +0.23 family history of bipolarity -0.27 TMT-A -0.44 rSLF-parietal AD -0.32 rSLF-temporal AD

24100114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100114.value: This is the first imaging study of treatment-naïve bipolar II depressed (or any bipolar disorder) patients. Our finding of intact structural connectivity and energy metabolism in Bipolar II challenged existing understanding of the associations of these processes with bipolarity. Manuscripts are in preparation. Our findings were presented at 4 international conferences. In preparation of analysis, collaborators in Utrecht University and University of Ottawa were consulted. We are beginning to solicit collaborative opportunities with overseas institutions in proceeding to larger BPII cohorts. The MRS apparatus at study planning could not measure concentrations of Glutathione – which is implicated in energy metabolism and oxidative stress. We have, in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University, installed the HERMES sequence in our MRI. This allows us to quickly estimate brain glutamate, GABA, NAA as well as glutathione concentrations. The trends of between-group differences and correlations in energy metabolites and serum measures suggested the need for larger sample sizes to more effectively control type II bias. Longitudinal studies would be required to ascertain whether abnormalities of brain energy metabolism may emerge later in the illness course of Bipolar II disorder, as well as the prognostic significance of increased structural connectivity loss found in the unipolar depressed subjects.

24100114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100114.value: Increased brain structural connectivity loss in bipolar depressed compared to unipolar depressed (UD) and healthy controls (HC) has been observed, but could have been confounded by medication use and high illness chronicity of extant samples. In this study, we measured DTI, H1-MRS and serum measures of lipid peroxidation (LPH and 4-HNE) in 27 each of young, treatment-naïve bipolar II depressed (BPII) and UD, with age-sex-education matched HC. Increased structural connectivity loss was not found in BPII, but was found in right SLF of UD compared to BPII and HC. There was significant between-group difference in sgACC Glu/Cr but post-hoc analysis found no significant pairwise differences. LPH significantly correlated with parietal left SLF RD but its clinical significance is unclear. Correlation of 4-HNE with structural connectivity may be attributed to insufficient sample size. Multivariate analysis suggested that intact right-sided structural connectivity and high episodic recurrence predicted BPII grouping amongst patients. In summary, this study found no significant disruptions in energy metabolism and lipid peroxidation in young treatment-naïve BPII. Longitudinal studies would be needed to ascertain whether brain metabolism and structural connectivity abnormalities may emerge later in illness course of BPII, and the prognostic significance of increased structural connectivity loss in UD.

24100314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100314.value: 此研究計劃的目標是探討巨噬細胞從致病促炎性M1型轉變為抗發炎M2型之極化作用的分子機制，以及研究巨噬細胞的極化作用抑制神經炎症的過程。 神經炎症是在中樞神經系統（CNS）中一個複雜的病理過程。此病症對於各地的社會和經濟有著相當大的影響。神經炎症可引發許多神經退化性疾病，例如多發性硬化症（MS）和腦退化症（AD）。直到目前，醫學界還沒有具效用的預防和治療方法用於神經炎症。針對研究預防和治療方法，重點在於理解體內的神經炎症調控，當中巨噬細胞的極化作用扮演著非常重要的角色。 兩個主要使巨噬細胞活化的路徑分別為 M1 和 M2。M1路徑是由促炎性細胞因子IFN- 和細菌產物如脂多糖所介導的。M1巨噬細胞能產生活性氧（ROS）和一氧化氮（NO），以消除細胞內的病原體，並有效地刺激適應性免疫反應。M1 巨噬細胞所分泌的炎症有效介質 （例如 ROS/ NO，TNF腫瘤壞死因子） 會使神經組織受到重大損害。相反，M2巨噬細胞是由調節性細胞因子IL-4和IL-13所誘導，它會抑制適應性免疫反應，並製造一種能夠重塑和修復組織的蛋白質（如精氨酸，Ym-1）。 我們曾經在微膠細胞中，發現microRNA-124在抗發炎M2型之極化作用中扮演著相當重要的角色。當患有多發性硬化症的小鼠於注射miR-124後，我們發現在小鼠的中樞神經系統內的微膠細胞和周邊系統內的巨噬細胞均轉變為抗發炎M2型，從而抑制小鼠的神經炎症，最後小鼠能夠完全康復。在研究巨噬細胞內的miR-124作用機制中，我們發現miR-124能抑制轉錄因子CEBPα的表達，巨噬細胞從而轉變為抗發炎M2型。最後，我們發現IL-4 於抗發炎M2型的巨噬細胞中能夠刺激REST/ CREB 的路徑，從而增加CEBPβ的表達，亦同時抑制CEBPα。 基於這些發現，我們假設miR-124藉著通過改變兩種形式的轉錄因子CEBP（CEBPα和CEBPβ）的表達水平，令巨噬細胞極化朝向M2，使神經炎症得以調節。 此專題研究能找出顯示巨噬細胞極化的轉錄和表觀遺傳水平的新分子機制，對於日後研究抑制神經炎症和治療神經退化性疾病，例如﹕多發性硬化症（MS）或腦退化症（AD），有莫大的幫助。

24100314.label: Realisation of objectives
24100314.value: In our study, we successfully addressed all three planned specific aims. Although results of our study did not fully support our initial hypothesis, we made significant progress in achieving all goals using alternative approaches. In Aim 1, we found that CEBPβ but not CEBPα mediated both M1 and M2 modes of macrophages activation depending on the presence of other co-factors. We established that cAMP pathway upregulated both miR-124 and CEBPβ to mediate M2 activation. In this case, ERK served as co-factor for CEBPβ that was required for M2 activation. The results of this study were published in international peer-reviewed journal Frontiers in Immunology (IF=6.4; see Research Output#1, section 8 for details). Another co-factor that was found to be important for modulation of CEBPβ in M1 macrophages is Egr2 transcriptional co-activator, which was critical for macrophage polarization towards M1 and M2. These results are currently under review in Frontiers in Immunology (see Research Output#4, section 8 for details). Thus, the Aim 1 was completely accomplished with two research outputs. In Aim 2 we fully characterized new factor that induced expression of miR-124 in macrophages and deactivated them by downregulation activation markers MHC class II and CD45. We found that miR-124 itself in complex with high-density lipoproteins (HDLs) mediated this process. We established that miR-124-HDL complexes had the ability to bind to the surface of macrophages and microglia and become internalized. In the cytoplasm of microglia/macrophages, miR-124 deactivated these cells affecting CEBPα-PU.1 pathway. Similar to miR-124, other neuronal microRNA miR-9 also contributed to macrophages deactivation by targeting NFκB. We found that miR-124 and miR-9 were constantly produced by electrically-active neurons, while HDLs were produced by glia to make complexes with miR-124 and miR-9 in extracellular space. Please refer to our Research Output#5 (section 8), which s currently in the revision stage in Journal of Neuroscience Research. Thus, the Aim 2 was fully accomplished with one research output being in the revision stage in the international peer-reviewed journal. In Aim 3, we found that complexes of miR-124 with liposomes or with HDL were too large to efficiently penetrate into CNS (not published). Therefore we used an alternative approach to find a small molecule to affect upstream pathways to upregulate miR-124 in the CNS instead of its delivery. To do so, we utilized FDA-approved drug Forskolin that induced miR-124 via a cAMP pathway leading to M2 polarization in the CNS and complete recovery from experimental autoimmune encephalitis (a mouse model of multiple sclerosis). These results were also published in Frontiers of Immunology as a part of the Research Output#1. Thus, Aim3 was accomplished in one research output, which is shared with the same output for Aim 1. Thus, all three aims were successfully accomplished to 100% with three research outputs. Two other research outputs (e.g. methodological study and the review) were also published and described in the next section 6.1.
