24100314.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100314.value: Major findings are fully described in Part C (sections 8-11) as a research outputs 1. “Cyclic AMP Pathway Suppress Autoimmune Neuroinflammation by Inhibiting Functions of Encephalitogenic CD4 T Cells and Enhancing M2 Macrophage Polarization at the Site of Inflammation” (Research Output#1, section 8). 2. “Early growth response gene-2 is required for M1 and M2 macrophage activation and plasticity by modulation of the transcription factor CEBPβ” (Research Output#4, section 8). 3. “Neuronal Extracellular MicroRNAs miR-124 and miR-9 Mediate Cell-Cell Communication between Neurons and Microglia” (Research Output#5, section 8). 4-5. New pilot (e.g. platelet-derived factors in M2 polarization) and methodological (microglia/macrophages analysis in the central nervous system) findings were published as a Research Output#2 (review paper) and Research Output#3 (research protocol), respectively (see section 8). These pilot findings were also reported on the international conference (see section 9). Two PhD. students that were working on this grant (see sections 10-11) are co-authors in three the grant-related publications (Research outputs#1, 3, 4 shown in section 8).

24100314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100314.value: In addition to execution of our aims, we made several pilot discoveries, which will be further investigated in new projects. First, we found that components of plasma (including factors secreted by platelets) provide strong M2 stimulus. Second, we found that CEBPα transcriptional factor does not promote M1 polarization as we hypothesized, but rather serve as an M2 inhibitor. This fact could be very important for regulation of allergic inflammation where the dysregulated M2 mode of macrophage activation in lungs contribute to allergy and asthma. This will be further investigated in the future using mouse model OVA-induced allergic lung inflammation as we did earlier in our previous study (Veremeyko et al, Plos One, 2013).

24100314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100314.value: The goal of this project was to investigate molecular mechanisms of innate immune cell activation from pathogenic pro-inflammatory M1 towards anti-inflammatory M2 mode and implication of this process for suppression of inflammation in the brain and spinal cord Brain inflammation is a complex pathological process in the central nervous system (CNS) with a high social and economic impact worldwide. Currently, there is no effective therapy for prevention and treatment of CNS inflammation that accompanies neurodegenerative diseases such as multiple sclerosis (MS) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). To focus on disease prevention and treatment, it is important to understand key events in the regulation of CNS inflammation such as activation of innate immune cells. We found that specific molecule microRNA-124 downmodulate CNS inflammation by promoting a protective M2 mode of activation of innate immune cells. We established particular mechanisms how this molecule mediates communication between neurons and immune cells in the normal brain and how to induce expression of microRNA-124 during CNS inflammation using known food supplement Forskolin. The results from this study are important for fundamental science and for translational biomedicine to prevent and treat pathological conditions such as AD and MS.

24100414.label: Project Objectives
24100414.value: Objective #1 Examine physiological endoplasmic reticulum stress during pronephros formation. We will access physiological ER stress during pronephros development by examining, 1) whether Xbp1 mRNA cytoplasmic splicing is increased, 2) whether inhibition of UPR affects pronephros formation, 3) whether knockdown of Bip disrupts the UPR in Xenopus embryos, 4) whether Xbp1 binds to Bip promoter directly, and if so, whether such binding is increased along the developmental process, 5) whether Xbp1 is required for pronephros formation. Objective #2 Investigate molecular mechanisms as to how Bip regulates pronephros formation. We will examine whether Lhx1 and Wt1, which are regulated by RA signaling and serve as two master genes regulating pronephros development, can rescue the phenotype of pronehros inhibition induced by knockdown of Bip. Objective #3 Identify downstream target genes regulated by Bip during pronephros formation. The animal caps dissected either from control embryos, embryos injected with Bip antisense morpholino nucleotide (bipMO) or from Bip-knockout embryos will treated with activin and atRA for induction of pronephros in vitro. The gene expression profiles of these tissues will be analyzed with Affymetrix DNA microarray.

24100414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100414.value: 生理狀態下內質網應激反應Xbp1-Bip信號通路在原腎發育過中功能的相關研究 脊椎動物的腎臟是一個用於調節身體內環境平衡的複雜 器官，其功能是主要包括過濾血液中的有毒物質、維持離子和水平衡、調節激素的釋放等。與腎臟和泌尿系統相關的先天性發育異常大約占所有胎兒期發育異常的20-30％。高等脊椎動物腎臟發育包括三個連續的過程，即前腎、中腎和後腎。在這三個發育過程中，後期的腎臟發育過程總是起始於前體結構，並進一步發育成更加復雜的形式。在胚胎發育過程中前腎由複雜的基因調控網絡誘導而成，但具體的調控過程還存在有很多認知盲點。內質網應激通常是指在內質網中未折疊蛋白或不正確折疊蛋白的大量積纍的情況。為了應對內質網應激，細胞激活未折疊蛋白反應(unfolded protein response, UPR)，並通過激活IRE1α-XBP1的信號通路調控基因表達，恢復內質網的動態平衡 。在此信號通路激活狀態下，核酸內切酶IRE1α在細胞質中誘導XBP1 mRNA剪接， 從而產生活化狀態XBP1，並調控下游包括 BIP等基因的表達。Bip可以與IRE1α結合，並抑製IRE1α對低水平內質網應激的反應。雖然 IRE1α、XBP1和BIP 的相關研究受到了特別的關註，但他們在胚胎發育過程中的作用在很大程度上還是未知。我們的前期研究發現，IRE1α、Xbp1和Bip在胚胎中都特異地錶達於原腎。我們因此將正常胚胎發育過程中與 內質網應激相關基因的激活和錶達定義為生理狀態下的內質網應激。此外, 我們還發現在胚胎發育過程中，XBP1調控Bip表達，敲低Bip 抑製前腎的形成。同時敲低Bip也會抑製視黃酸信號通路。我們推測生理狀態下XBP1-BIP信號通路是前腎發育所必須的，敲低Bip蛋白會干擾UPR反應，並導緻視黃酸信號轉導的異常， 從而抑製原腎的形成。我們將通過以下幾點來驗證我們的假説：1) 研究XBP1-BIP信號通路在前腎形成過程中的功能; 2) 研究BIP調控前腎的形成分子機製; 3) 分離和研究Bip在形成原腎過程中調控的下游靶基因。通過這些研究，我們可以理順Bip在原腎的形成過程中的作用並確定其作用的分子機製，這將進一步豐富我們對調控前腎形成信號網絡的理解，並擴大我們對生理狀態內質網應激反應作用在胚胎發育過程中的認知。我們的研究也將為腎臟發育 異常所造成的慢性腎臟疾病的治療提供一定的借鑒作用。

24100414.label: Realisation of objectives
24100414.value: The primary goal of this proposal is to delineate the function of Xbp-Hspa5 signaling axis during embryonic development. Both Xbp1 and Hspa5 have been implicated in ER stress. During the progress of our project, the genome editing tool CRISPR/Cas9 was proved effective for gene disruption. Our group made important contribution to the first publication that demonstrates CRIPSR/Cas9-mediated genome editing in Xenopus embryos. Moreover, we established a CRISPR/Cas9 mediated gene knockin platform in this funding period. We also utilized the CRISPR/Cas9 to disrupt and Hspa5, and now we obtained the F1 frogs harbouring mutations. Our knockout frog lines set up a base to study the function of Hspa5 with the genetic approaches. Overexpression of Xbp1 increases the expression of mesoderm marker genes such as bra and fgf8. We examined the interaction between the Xbp1 and Hspa5. The spatial expression of Xbp1 and Hspa5 are largely overlapped in Xenopus embryos, e.g., both of them are expressed in pronephros. Furthermore, we found that overexpression of Xbp1 enhances the expression of Hspa5. We used morpholino antisense oligonucleotides (MO) to knockdown endogenous Hspa5 in Xenopus embryos. Knockdown of Hspa5 can increase the expression of unspliced Xbp1. Global knockdown of Hspa5 caused severe gastrulation defect, showing open blastopore and inhibition of convergent extension. Indeed, the Hspa5MO reduced the expression of pronephros marker genes lhx1, atp1b1, smp30, nephrin, and pax2 in both embryos and the induced pronephros tissue. These results indicate that Hsap5a is required for pronephros formation. Loss of Hspa5 function increased cell apoptosis and decreased cell proliferation. We utilized Hspa5 MO to knockdown endogenous Hspa5 expression. Knockdown Hspa5 inhibits pronephros formation. We next examined whether impaired pronephros formation is due to increased cell apoptosis or decreased cell proliferation. To test these possibilities, we examined cell apoptosis by whole mount TUNEL and cell proliferation by immunostaining for the phosphorylated histone H3 (PH3) in Hspa5 morphants. One of the ventral-vegetal blastomeres of eight-cell stage embryos which will give rise to pronephros was injected with Hspa5MO. The TUNEL assays were performed to examine cell apoptosis at stage 32. At the Hspa5MO-injected side, a higher level of TUNEL positive cells was observed compared to the uninjected side. In addition, immunostaining to detect the PH3 was performed to examine cell proliferation. The PH3-positive cells were visualized at a lower density within the ,pronephros region at the injected side compared to those at the uninjected side. These data suggest that loss of Hspa5 led to pronephros malformation possibly due to increased cell apoptosis and decreased cell proliferation at cellular level. Hspa5 is required for the transduction of retinoic acid (RA) signalling. The expression of genes involved in RA signalling transduction and atRA metabolism, including RARα, RXRβ, RXRγ, Raldh1, Raldh2, Raldh3, and Cyp26A1 in Hspa5-depleted HEK293T cells, remains normal. However, the retinoic acid receptor, endogenous RARα protein level is reduced upon knockdown of Hspa5. Thus, our data suggest that Hspa5 regulates retinoic acid signalling, at least in part, by mediating the expression level of RARα. We will test whether depletion of Hspa5 will enhance the protein degradation of RARα. We investigated the effects of Hspa5 on FGF signalling, which is required for pronephros specification. We suggest that Hspa5 and the retinoic acid signaling axis is required for FGF8 secretion. Generation of Hspa5 knockout X. tropicalis line. Hspa5 is essential for early embryonic development. We expected and indeed encountered some difficulties in generating the Hspa5 knockout out X. tropicalis line. At first round, we disrupted Hspa5 gene in X. tropicalis with TALEN. However, the heterozygous F1 frogs that we obtained all harbor a trinucleotide deletion right after the ATG site. We expected that such mutations would not affect Hspa5 function. So we decided to utilize the CRISPR/Cas9 to disrupt X. tropicalis in the second round. Two sgRNAs were designed to target the front region of the Hspa5 gene. We have obtained the heterozygous Hspa5 KO X. tropicalis line. This Hspa5 KO line harbors a seven bp-deletion, which cause an early stop of Hspa5a open reading frame. However, the homozygous mutant embryos look normal. The expression of marker genes, including xbra and sox17, are not changed compared to those in wild type embryos. Analyzing the genotype of Hspa5 KO, we found a putative open reading frame (ORF) after the stop codon. This ORF encodes a predicted protein that is equivalent to amino acid 138 to 655 of Hspa5. These data suggest this truncated Hspa5 (138-655) fragment is essential for Hspa5 function. We will disrupt the allele of truncated Hspa5 by using CRISPR/Cas9. We will also test whether the mRNA of truncated Hspa5 can rescue the pronephros phenotype caused by Hspa5 MO. Alternatively, the mild phenotype in the Hspa5 KO X. tropicalis can be explained that the disruption of Hspa5 induces genetic compensation response that can compensate for the loss of Hspa5. We plan to perform RNA-seq to identify the gene that may contribute to the genetic compensation response. Compare the gene expression profiles between the Hspa5 morphants and wild type embryos. We carried out microarray assay to compare gene expression profiles between Hspa5MO injected embryos and control MO injected embryos. We collected the injected embryos at stage 11.5, 15, and 32 for Affymetrix DNA microarray assay, and the microarray data was analyzed with Partek software. We selected genes with the absolute fold change over 2 at each comparison. The selected genes were analyzed with Gene Ontology (GO). Of those, at the biological process level, 21% of counts are in the GO term of growth, 16% are involved both in GO term of immune system process and biological adhesion, 12% are involved both in response to stimulus and developmental process. At molecular function level, 18% of counts are involved in the electron carrier activity, 17% of counts are related with the enzyme regulator activity, and 15% are associated with structural molecule activity, molecular transducer activity, and transcription regulator activity. At last, 14% of counts are involved in the GO term of transporter activity. We validate the selected genes by Real-Time PCR, including solute carrier family 2 member 12 (slc2a12), Down syndrome critical region gene 1 (dscr1), and solute carrier family 38, member 8, (slc38a8). Their expression was all decreased in Hspa5MO morphants at stage 11.5. In line with microarray data, real-time PCR indicated that cyclin A1 and cyclin B5 also were decreased in Hspa5 morphants at stage 15. The expression of rxr-γ, retinol dehydrogenase 8 (rdh8), fatty acid binding protein 2 (fabp2) was decreased in Hspa5MO morphants when compared those in control stage 32 embryos. We further examined the expression pattern of the selected genes by whole mount in situ hybridization. Slc9a3r1 was expressed in the pronephros, liver and ear vesicle at stage 28 and stage 30 and only in pronephros at the stages 40. Slc2a12 was expressed in the somite at stage 28. At stage 40, its expression remains in the somite and notochord. We found that rxr-γ, retinal G protein coupled receptor, retinol-binding protein 2, rdh7, rdh8 are all decreased in HspaMO injected group. These genes have all been implicated in RA signaling. Our microarray assay is in line with our finding that RA signaling was inhibited in Hspa5MO injected embryos.

24100414.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100414.value: 1) We have established gene disruption approaches such as TALEN and CRISPR in my laboratory, and generate Xenopus Hspa5 knockout line. We now obtained the Hspa5+/- frogs harbouring seven-nucleotide deletion. The Hspa5-/- embryos show the same morphology as the wild type embryos. The possible reasons were discussed in 5.3. This frog line is valuable to study the essential element of Hspa5 protein, to study the nonsense mRNA decay and afterward genetic compensation response. We will perform RNA-Seq to identify the potential genes that can cause genetic compensation. 2) Both Xbp1 and Hsap5a are expressed pronephros, and their expression patterns are largely overlapped. Indeed, overexpression of Xbp1 can induce up-regulation of Hspa5 in Xenopus embryos. 3) Knockdown of Hspa5 strongly inhibits the expression of pronephros specification. 4) Hspa5 is required for the transduction of retinoic acid (RA) signaling. Pronephros tissue is induced in vitro by treating animal caps with all-trans retinoic acid (atRA) and activin. Depletion of Hspa5 in animal caps, however, blocked the induction of pronephros as well as reduced the expression of RA-responsive genes, suggesting that knockdown of Hspa5 attenuated RA signalling. Knockdown of Hspa5 in animal caps resulted in decreased expression of lhx1, a transcription factor directly regulated by RA signalling and essential for pronephros specification. Co-injection of Hspa5MO with lhx1mRNA partially rescues the phenotype induced by Hspa5MO. These results suggest that the RA-lhx1 signalling cascade is involved in Hspa5MO induced pronephros malformation. 5) Hspa5 regulates retinoic acid receptor, RAR expression level in SH-SY5Y cells. Knockdown of Hspa5 does not affect the transcription of genes involved in RA signalling transduction and atRA metabolism including RARα, RXRβ, RXRγ, Raldh1, Raldh2, and Raldh3; but reduce the protein level of RARα. Thus, our data suggest that Hspa5 regulates RA signalling, at least in part, by mediating the expression level of RARα. 6) Hspa5 promotes Fgf8 secretion, which is essential for pronephros. 7) Xbp1 and P85α can physically interact each in Xenopus embryos. Co-injection of Xbp1 and P85α promotes the expression of fgf8 when compared to the single injection of Xbp1. 8) Generate gene expression profile regulated by using Affymetrix DNA microarray. Through analysing the expression profile, we identified genes regulated by Hspa5, including Slc9a3r1 and Slc2a12. Components in RA signalling cascade such as rxr-γ and rdh8 was inhibited in Hspa5MO injected embryos.

24100414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100414.value: We have obtained F1 Hspa5+/-frogs harbouring seven-nucleotide deletion, resulting in a truncated Hspa5. The truncated Hspa5 contains the essential fragment for Hspa5 function. We intend to test whether the Hspa5 essential fragment can rescue the phenotype induced by Hspa5MO. We next want to collect the Hspa5-/- embryos, and use RNA-seq to identify the gene mediated by Hspa5. We found that depletion of human HSPA5 induces down-regulation of RARα at the protein level in cultured SH-SY5Y cells. The underlying mechanism remains unknown. We plan to investigate whether knockdown of HSPA5 will affect other retinoic acid receptors and whether knockdown of HSPA5 will affect the ubiquitination of RARα.

24100414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100414.value: Congenital kidney malformations are the leading cause of chronic renal failure in children, which consists of about 20 to 30 percent of all anomalies identified in the prenatal period. Therefore, studying the molecular mechanism of kidney development and establishing methodology for induction of kidney in vitro will bring great benefit to public health. We used Xenopus embryos to elucidate the interaction between the Xbp1-Hspa5 signaling involved in ER stress and RA signaling pathway, and studied how the interactions govern the formation of the functional nephron. Our studies provide more insights into the regulatory networks in pronephros formation, further our understanding on the physiological roles of ER stress during early embryonic development, and provide scientific evidence for a better understanding of developmental defects that lead to clinically significant malformations.

24200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200114.value: Perishable products such as meat, fruit, dairy products, frozen foods, and pharmaceuticals are ubiquitous and play an indispensable role in our society. However, control and optimization of perishable inventory systems is very hard due to their finite-lifetime nature. Indeed, the optimal control policy for perishable inventory systems is very complicated; and the computation of the optimal policy using dynamic programs suffers from the well-known “curse of dimensionality” and is intractable even with a relatively short product lifetime. Thus, researchers have turned to seek simple heuristic policies since 1970s. However, almost all the heuristic policies developed thus far have been focused on the case with independent and identically distributed demand processes. Such demand processes cannot capture demand seasonality or demand correlation (e.g., demand forecast, advance demand information), both of which are commonly observed in business practices. Furthermore, none of the existing heuristic policies reported in the literature has a provably performance guarantee; and without worst-case performance guarantees, the policies could perform, in theory, arbitrarily badly. In this project, we aim to develop easy-to-compute and near-optimal approximation algorithms with worst-case performance guarantees for several classes of perishable inventory systems with non-stationary and arbitrarily correlated demand processes. Similar approximation algorithms have been developed recently for non-perishable inventory systems. In our preliminary study, we have developed two approximation algorithms for a basic perishable inventory system with zero order leadtime. Both algorithms have provably worst-case performance guarantees; and numerical study shows that both of them perform consistently close to optimal. In this project, we propose to develop approximation algorithms for more general perishable inventory systems, including perishable inventory systems with positive leadtime, capacitated perishable inventory systems, perishable inventory systems with setup cost, and multi-echelon perishable inventory systems. If successful, the research output of this project will not only significantly contribute to the research literature on perishable inventory management, but will also have a broad impact on researchers and practitioners in perishable product industries/organizations. 易腐产品（如：肉类、水果、奶制品、冷冻食品和药品）无处不在，并且在我们的社会中发挥着不可或缺的作用。然而，由于生命周期有限，易腐产品库存系统的控制和优化非常困难。的确，易腐产品库存系统的最优控制策略非常复杂；并且由于遭遇了著名的“维数灾难”，基于动态规划的最优控制策略在计算上对于产品寿命相对较短的问题也是非常的困难。因此，研究人员早在20世纪70年代以来就开始寻求简单的启发式策略。然而，几乎所有的已知启发式策略都专注于独立同分布的需求过程。这样的需求过程无法描述需求的季节性和相关性（如：需求预测、提前需求信息），而这两者在商业实践中都非常普遍。此外，相较于最优控制策略，目前所有文献中的启发式策略都不存在可证明的绩效担保。由于没有最坏情形下的绩效担保，在理论上讲，这些启发式策略的绩效在某些情形下可能会非常的差。在这一项目中，我们的目标是针对几类在非平稳和具有相关性的需求过程下的易腐库存系统开发易于计算、接近最优且具有最坏情形下绩效担保的近似算法。近年来，类似的近似算法已经在非易腐库存系统下被开发出来了。在初步研究中，我们已经对一类简单的不存在订货提前期的易腐库存系统开发出了两个近似算法。这两个算法都具有可证明的最坏情形下的绩效担保；并且数值算例表明它们的绩效一致地接近最优。在这一项目中，我们计划对几类更一般的易腐产品库存系统开发近似算法，包括：订货提前期为正的易腐产品库存系统、带有订货量约束的易腐产品库存系统、带有固定订货成本的易腐产品库存系统、以及多层级的易腐产品库存系统。如果获得成功，这一项目的研究成果将会对易腐产品库存管理领域的学术研究做出显著贡献，并且会对易腐产品行业的研究和管理人员产生广泛的影响。

24200114.label: Realisation of objectives
24200114.value: First, we develop an easy-to-compute approximation algorithm, referred to as proportional-balancing (PB) policy, for perishable inventory systems with finite ordering capacities. We prove that when the demand process is associated, the PB policy admits a theoretical worst-case performance guarantee less than 3. We show that the associated demand process includes independent and many commonly used positively correlated demand processes as special cases. We also conduct an extensive numerical study to test the numerical performance of our proposed PB policy and find that it performs consistently very well and near-optimal under various parameter settings. The first objective of this project has been successfully realized. Second, we develop an easy-to-compute approximation algorithm, also referred to as proportional-balancing (PB) policy, for perishable inventory systems with positive lead times and with or without finite capacities. We prove that when the demand process is associated, the PB policy admits a theoretical worst-case performance guarantee less than 3 for most practical scenarios. We also conduct an extensive numerical study to test the numerical performance of our proposed PB policy and find that it performs consistently very well and near-optimal under various parameter settings. The second objective of this project has also been successfully realized. Finally, the third objective of this project was unfortunately given up. The reason is as follows. Building on our algorithm and results developed for capacitated perishable inventory systems, my collaborators developed an approximation algorithm for perishable inventory systems with setup costs and published the paper in April 2016. The full citation of this paper is as follows: Zhang, H., C. Shi, X. Chao. 2016. Technical Note – Approximation Algorithms for Perishable Inventory Systems with Setup Costs, Operations Research, 64(2): 432-440. Considering that this paper has already achieved the third objective of this project, we finally had to give it up.

24200114.label: Major findings and research outcome
24200114.value: We develop an easy-to-compute approximation algorithm, referred to as proportional-balancing (PB) policy, for perishable inventory systems with finite capacities and positive lead times. We prove that when the demand process is associated, the PB policy admits a theoretical worst-case performance guarantee less than 3 for the capacitated systems with zero lead times and for most practical systems with positive lead times. We also conduct an extensive numerical study to test the numerical performance of our proposed PB policy and find that it performs consistently very well and near-optimal under various parameter settings. The research findings have been published in the journal Management Science.

24200114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24200114.value: Managing perishable inventory systems is important while challenging in both practice and academia. In this project, we apply the idea of cost balancing to develop an approximation algorithm for perishable inventory systems with finite ordering capacities and positive lead times. This algorithm admits a theoretical worst-case performance guarantee less than 3 for most practical scenarios and numerically performs consistently very well and near-optimal under various parameter settings. The progress we have made is encouraging but it is just a start. We believe that there are many other interesting and important perishable inventory systems, for which the development of such near-optimal approximation algorithms is desirable and worthwhile. For example, it is worthwhile to develop near-optimal approximation algorithms for more complex perishable inventory systems, such as systems with lost sales and positive lead times, systems with multiple echelons, systems with multiple demand classes. We leave the algorithmic designs for these systems as future research.

24200114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24200114.value: Perishable products such as meat, fruit, dairy products, frozen foods, and pharmaceuticals are ubiquitous and play an indispensable role in our society. However, control and optimization of perishable inventory systems is very hard due to their finite-lifetime nature. Researchers have turned to seek simple heuristic policies since 1970s. However, almost all the heuristic policies developed thus far have been focused on the case with independent and identically distributed demand processes, ignoring the demand seasonality and demand correlation (two commonly observed demand patterns in practices). Furthermore, none of the existing heuristic policies has provably performance guarantee against the optimal policy. In this project, we develop easy-to-compute approximation algorithms with worst-case performance guarantees for perishable inventory systems with finite ordering capacities and positive lead times, under very general demand processes. Our extensive numerical study shows that our proposed algorithms perform consistently very well and near-optimal under various parameter settings. The research findings of this project will not only significantly contribute to the research literature on perishable inventory management, but will also have a broad impact on researchers and practitioners in perishable product industries/organizations.

24200214.label: Project Objectives
24200214.value: To give Markov and semimartingale characterizations of time-inhomogeneous Markov semimartingales, which are obtained by additive subordination of time-homogeneous Markov semimartingales, and study equivalent measure changes for these processes. This lays down the theoretical foundation for their applications in finance. To develop empirically realistic and tractable models using additive subordination in a variety of financial markets. In particular, we shall consider the following applications. (1) Develop a new electricity spot price model which can capture seasonal spikes and is tractable for pricing electricity derivatives. In practice the extremely volatile electricity price presents a big challenge to the finance and the power industry. We expect our model will help financial institutions and power companies improve their valuation and risk management decisions related to electricity with computational efficiency. (2) Develop an empirically realistic and analytically tractable cross commodity model for pricing crack spread options. Crack spread is the price difference between the oil output (heating oil or gasoline) and the crude oil. In practice crack spread options are important for refinery firms to manage their risks. We expect our model to calibrate well to the volatility surface for both the crude oil and its output, thus allowing consistent pricing in single commodity and cross commodity options. (3) Improve the Levy subordinate models developed in the literature for modeling in credit, equity and interest rate markets by using additive subordination instead of Levy subordination. We expect these additive subordinate models to achieve excellent calibration results. To calibrate these models from market data and empirically validate them.

24200214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200214.value: A fundamental task in financial engineering is to develop empirically realistic as well as tractable derivative models. For tractability reasons many standard models are assumed to have time-homogeneous local characteristics (i.e. drift, diffusion coefficient, jump measure), These models are undesirable from the empirical standpoint in many applications, as they cannot capture time dependent behavior such as seasonal spikes observed in electricity spot prices, and may not achieve satisfactory results in calibrating the term structure of interests (e.g. implied volatilities). While the modeling toolbox of financial engineers already contains a large number of tractable time-homogeneous Markov semimartingales, the number of tractable time inhomogeneous Markov semimartingales which capture empirical features is substantially smaller. The aim of this proposal is to study the theory and applications of a technique called additive subordination for modeling time dependency in financial engineering. We start with a time-homogeneous Markov semimartingale X, and time change it by an independent additive subordinator T (this procedure is called additive subordination). By appropriately choosing X and T we obtain a large family of tractable time-inhomogeneous Markov semimartigales with rich and desirable time dependent structure in the local characteristics. We shall give Markov and semimartingale characterization for such processes and study equivalent measure changes for them. This lays down the theoretical foundation for their applications in finance. Using the additive subordination technique, we shall construct new financial models for a wide range of applications in various markets including commodity (energy, agricultural products and metals), electricity, credit, equity and interest rates, and develop analytical and computational methods for pricing derivatives under these models. We shall calibrate our models to market data and empirically validate them. 建立現實且容易處理的衍生品模型是金融工程一項基本的任務。爲了便於計算，很多標准的模型都假設其局部特徵（即漂移，擴散，跳躍）是不依賴于時間的。在很多應用中，這些模型不符合實證的要求，比如他們不能刻畫電价中帶周期性的尖點，以及不能擬合關心變量（例如隱含波動率）所呈現的期限結構。 雖然金融工程師的工具中已經包含了很多不依賴時間的馬氏半鞅過程用於建模，對時間依賴且容易處理的馬氏半鞅模型還非常少。在本提案中，我們的目標是研究可加時間變換（一種對時間依賴性建模的方法）的理論及應用。我們從一個不依賴于時間的馬氏半鞅X出發，對它用一個獨立的可加隨機時間T進行時間變換 （這種方法稱爲可加時間變換）。通過恰當的選取X和T， 我們得到了大量的容易處理的對時間依賴的馬氏半鞅過程。它們的局部特徵具有豐富的時間依賴性結構，可以滿足各種應用的需要。我們將給出這些模型的馬氏性以及半鞅性的刻畫，並研究它們的等價測度變換。這些結果將為它們在金融中的應用提供理論基礎。利用可加時間變換，我們將開發新的模型應用於不同金融市場中，包括商品（即能源，農產品，金屬），電力，信用，股票和利率，以及為這些模型發展解析和計算的方法用於衍生品定價。我們將用市場數據來校正我們的模型並通過實證分析來驗證他們。

24200214.label: Realisation of objectives
24200214.value: All the four objectives have been achieved. For Objective 1, we proved that for time-inhomogeneous Markov semimatingales obtained from additive subordination of time-homogeneous Markov semimartingales, they are again semimartingales and we derived an explicit formula for their generator. We also developed conditions for equivalent measure changes. For Objective 2, we applied additive subordination to construct new models for electricity prices, the prices of crude oil and its output, and VIX (a popular volatility index). We also compare additive subordinate models to Levy subordinate models. For Objective 3, we developed an analytical approach based on eigenfunction expansions and a computational method based on characteristics functions and Laplace transform. For Objective 4, we calibrated all the models that we developed and analyzed their empirical performance to validate them.

24200214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24200214.value: The current project focuses on univariate additive subordination (i.e., using one additive subordinator) for modeling one asset or one financial variable. A potential direction for future research is to generalize the current modeling framework by using a separate additive subordinator for each process to construct multivariate subordinate models for several assets or financial variables. These models hold the promise of capturing time dependence in each asset/variable's behavior as well as in their dependence structure while being tractable.

24200214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24200214.value: Financial institutions employ mathematical models for their derivatives business. Typically a model is needed to calibrate observed market prices and then applied to pricing tasks. Due to the complex behavior of asset prices, to achieve a good fit to market data requires models with time dependence. However, existing time-dependent models are often quite intractable, making them unfavorable in practice. This project proposes and studies a new technique, called additive subordination, for constructing tractable time-dependent models. We developed the theory for this technique and explored various applications in the project. The conclusion is that additive subordination can be applied to developing empirically realistic and tractable models in different financial sectors, and these models can be computed fast, enabling real-time pricing decisions. The research results equip financial practitioners with a new useful tool for their derivatives business.

24200314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200314.value: In dynamic decision making problems, a policy is typically evaluated by the expected net present value or expected utility from the corresponding uncertain cash flow. While these approaches are intuitive and computationally appealing, they neglect the target attainment, i.e., the ability to achieve profit targets. Indeed, the target attainment is a common concern in real practice, and it also has a strong normative basis. In this project, we aim to propose a target-based criterion to efficiently evaluate the prospect of an uncertain profit flow in achieving profit targets over time. By optimizing the target-based criterion, we can find the optimal policy which leads to the lowest shortfall risk with respect to the profit targets. In our pilot research, we constructed the target-based criterion using an axiomatic approach, such that the criterion has salient properties like attainment content and starvation aversion. In this project, in order to calculate the value of the target-based criterion efficiently and illustrate the insights on its connection with the classical expected utility criterion, we plan to focus on the class of criteria that can be constructed from a general utility function. By arbitrarily approximating the underlying utility function with a piecewise linear function, the complexity of evaluating the target-based criterion could be significantly reduced. In addition, we will also take into account the distributional ambiguity in the dynamic decision making framework and capture the correlation between uncertainties in different periods. In order to reduce the complexity in the optimization procedure, we intend to avoid the second and higher moment information of the uncertainties. Instead, we hope to exploit the linear structure, and retain as much information as possible. Finally, we will provide an efficient algorithm to solve the proposed dynamic decision making problem, which is under a target-based criterion and with distributional ambiguity. The key idea is to use a decision rule to approximate the profit flow’s dependency on uncertain factors by an explicit function, such as a linear function. In our preliminary results, under the target-based criterion constructed from piecewise linear function and specific distributional ambiguity information, the whole problem can be reformulated in a linear structure and hence it is easy to solve. After theoretical studies, we will apply the framework on real problems such as the multi-products and multi-periods inventory control problem, and the multi-periods project selection problem. 在动态决策问题中，评价一个策略通常是通过比较它所带来的现金流所对应的净现值或者期望效用。这样的评价方针很直观，并且在某种程度上是易于操作的。然而，它并没有把收益目标考虑进来，也就是说，它并不能反映能否达到预设收益目标的能力。实际上，收益目标是现实操作中一个常见的考虑，同时它也有着很强的规范基础。在本项目中，我们希望可以提出一个基于目标的衡量标准，从而可以有效的衡量一个不确定现金流最终能否达到收益目标的风险。通过最优化此基于目标的衡量标准，我们可以找到最优策略，也就是把达到利益目标的风险降到最低的策略。在我们前期的研究中，我们通过公理化的手段建立起一个具体的基于目标的衡量标准，它有着很好的性质，例如凸性等。在本项目中，由于我们既希望可以有效迅速的计算此基于目标的衡量标准，也希望可以刻画出它与经典期望效用函数之间的联系，因此，我们将会把注意力集中在能够从普通的效用函数引申出来的衡量标准。通过对原有效用函数用分段线性函数来任意逼近，我们可以极大的降低计算此衡量标准的复杂性。此外，我们也会把鲁棒性考虑到此多阶段决策过程中来，并把每个阶段之间不确定性的交互作用也包括在内。出于降低优化过程中的计算复杂度的需求，我们计划避免使用不确定因素的二阶或更高阶的信息。我们希望通过充分的利用线性结构，同时尽可能多的刻画随机信息。最后，我们会提供一个有效的算法来解决提出来的动态规划问题。解决的关键思路是利用决策规则，并采用近似算法。在前期研究中，我们研究了利用分段线性效用函数构造的基于目标的衡量标准，以及一个特殊的分布性息；在这种情况下，整个问题可以被转变成线性结构从而易于解决。在理论研究之后，我们会把这个框架应用到实际问题中，例如多产品多阶段的库存管理问题，以及多阶段的项目选择问题等。

24200314.label: Realisation of objectives
24200314.value: 1. The first objective is achieved. In particular, we developed a target-oriented decision-making framework using axiomatic approach. While our proposed decision-making framework itself does not respect the time-consistency, we resolve the time-consistency issue by enforcing a pre-determined policy. The details can be seen in our Research Output No. 3, a journal paper with the title of “On Dynamic Decision Making to Meet Consumption Targets”. 2. The second objective is achieved. We have characterized the distributional ambiguity information for uncertain factors using a rather general information set, which is both general enough to cover a wide range of examples and computationally tractable in optimization. Moreover, we propose to use a linear-factor-based method to describe the correlation between different uncertain factors. The details can be seen in our Research Output No. 2, a journal paper with the title of “Managing Underperformance Risk in Project Portfolio Selection”. We remark that while this approach is used for static decision-making problem in this paper, as a fundamental method, it can be also applied in dynamic decision-making problem. 3. The third objective is achieved. More specifically, the new problem can be solved via a series classical dynamic programming problem. Therefore, we have developed an algorithm, where each iteration is to call Bellman’s Equation to solve a classical dynamic recursion, to solve the new target-oriented dynamic decision-making problem. The details can be seen in our Research Output No. 3, a journal paper with the title of “On Dynamic Decision Making to Meet Consumption Targets”. 4. The fourth objective is achieved. We have three applications: 1) on shortest path problem (Research Output No. 1), 2) on project portfolio selection problem (Research Output No. 2).

24200314.label: Major findings and research outcome
24200314.value: By conducting this project, we have two streams of findings. In the first stream, we propose an appropriate target-oriented dynamic decision decision-making framework, which can incorporate the impact of targets and preserve computational tractability. We also propose an algorithm to solve such proposed dynamic decision-making problem. In particular, we decompose it to a series of classical dynamic programming problem, such that the optimal policies can be solved via a number of Bellman’s equation. This result can be seen in our Research Output No. 3. We apply this theoretical result on two important operations management problems, which include project portfolio selection problem (our Research Output No. 2) and the multi-period inventory control problem (our Research Output No. 3). In both applications, the efficiency of the solution provided by our proposed method is demonstrated by computational studies. In the second stream, we develop appropriate distributional robust information set to characterize the uncertainties, such that it can address both the issue of distributional ambiguity and that of computational burden. The method we propose is rather general as it includes several classical methods in literature as special cases. We apply it to two discrete optimization problems, which are shortest path problem (our Research Output No. 1) and project portfolio optimization problem (our Research Output No. 2). In both applications, we show the efficiency of computation and effectiveness of the solution.

24200314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24200314.value: In the future, there are two potential directions for further development. The first one is to investigate some other important applications. As we have accomplished interesting and important methodologies, whose effectiveness has been demonstrated already in a few existing applications, we can continue to explore applications on other important problems. The second potential direction is on the theoretical side, and to investigate how to further improve the computational efficiency. Right now we solve the problem via a series of classical dynamic programming, which by itself is not always computationally tractable when the size is large. Therefore, we can consider to employ or develop certain heuristics to solve the problem more efficiently.

24200314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24200314.value: We consider the decision making problem under uncertainty. While classical researches focus on expected cost, we incorporate the practical concern of many decision makers, which is to what extend can we achieve some pre-specified targets. We build a mathematical model to incorporate the consideration of targets. We then develop effective optimization method to solve this mathematical model, such that we can obtain the exact optimal solution which could be considered to be able to achieve the targets better than other solutions. We then apply our method on several important practical problems in operations management, such as the inventory control problem. The application shows that the solutions from our model can perform relatively better than other models in terms achieving targets.

24200414.label: Project Objectives
24200414.value: The overall objective of this project is to understand the sources of instability in the non-carbon-based electrodes and reveal electrode properties that govern the reaction stability and reaction kinetics of nonaqueous oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER). A stable, active and high-energy electrode design based on fundamental insights developed in this project will be fabricated, fully-characterized and developed into a nonaqueous lithium-oxygen battery prototype. The technical objectives that lead to our overall goal are follows: We will design, fabricate and characterize model electrodes of select early transition metal carbides and nitrides (TMC/TMN) (i.e., MeX, where Me = Ti, Cr, Mo and X = C, N) with particle size around 50 – 100 nanometer and specific surface area around 20 – 50 meter square per gram. We will characterize their phase purity, crystallinity, particle size, morphology, surface adsorbed species and surface chemical states. We will investigate the influence of surface chemistry on the cycling stability and reaction kinetics of the TMC/TMN electrodes. We will compare and correlate the type/amount of surface adsorbed species of the as-prepared TMC/TMN electrodes to their cycling stability and reaction kinetics. Further, we will examine the role of surface chemistry via systematically tuning the surface species of the TMC/TMN electrodes using heat treatments under different gas environments such as forming gas, methane and synthetic air. We will monitor the formation/oxidation and overall growth of lithium peroxide, carbonates and carboxylates byproducts as a function of battery depth of discharge/charge and cycle number. With controlled surface chemistry, we will examine the influence of bulk nonmetal atom (C, N, e.g., Ti / TiC / TiN) and metal host (e.g., TiC / Cr3C2 / Mo2C) on the cycling stability and ORR/OER kinetics of the TMC/TMN electrodes. We will correlate the electron-accepting ability of the transition metal to its reaction stability; and correlate their oxygen binding energy (or its heat of formation of low order oxide) to their nonaqueous ORR/OER activities. We will design and fabricate high-surface-area and porous oxygen-electrodes based on the optimized carbide/nitride chemistry identified in this project. Specifically, we plan to carburize/nitridize metal-containing precursors on high-surface-area supports as well as apply surface carbide/nitride coatings on porous carbon materials. We will perform full chemical and electrochemical characterizations to examine their reaction reversibility, cycling stability, round-trip efficiency and gravimetric energy density at single cell level, aiming to demonstrate enhanced cycle life (150-200 cycles with more than 80 % capacity retention) and round-trip efficiency (> 75 %).

24200414.label: Realisation of objectives
24200414.value: 1. Overall: We have fully achieved all the objectives listed in this project. We revealed the source of instability of the sources of instability in the noncarbon-based electrodes and showed that the bonding nature between metal and non-metal elements is the key to govern the reaction stability and reaction kinetics of nonaqueous oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Applying the fundamental understanding obtained in this project, we successfully improve the efficiency and stability of rechargeable lithium-oxygen batteries. 2. We designed, fabricated and characterized model electrodes of select early transition metal carbides, nitrides and oxides (i.e., MeX, where Me = Ti, V, Cr, Mo, W and X = C, N, O) by first making the slurry of nanoparticles with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder onto a stainless steel mesh with a loading of about 0.6 – 1.0 mg/cm2. We characterized their phases, crystallinity, morphology and surface chemistry via X-ray diffraction spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The average specific surface area of these particles was 30 meter square per gram. 3. We revealed the influence of surface chemistry on the cycling stability and reaction kinetics of the selected electrodes. We found that the weaker the bonding between the transition metal and the non-metal of the compounds, the higher the catalytic activity (higher reaction kinetics) and the higher the surface reactivity (low cycling stability). We compared the correlation between the type/amount of surface absorbed species of the electrode (as prepared and treated) to the electrode kinetics and stability. Our results indicated that annealing is an effective way of improving the activity by removing the surface adsorbed carbonates. 4. We examined the influence of bulknonmetal atom on kinetics and stability. We revealed that bonding nature between metal and non-metal elements is the key to govern the reaction stability and reaction kinetics. In the carbide series (TiC, VC, Cr3C2, Mo2C, WC), we showed that TiC and Mo2C have the highest catalytic activity among the five materials for both ORR and OER process. In the titanium series (TiC, TiN, TiO2), TiC is most active among the three materials for both ORR and OER. In the chromium series (Cr3C2, CrN, Cr2O3), Cr3C2 is most active among the three materials for both ORR and OER. These results showed the metal carbide exhibits the highest activity among carbide, nitride and oxide, suggesting that the weaker the metal/nonmetal bonding, the higher the activity. However, carbide exhibits larger amount of surface absorbed species with lower stability. 5. We designed and fabricated high-surface-area and porous oxygen-electrodes using multi-component transition metal oxides and examine the role of each metal in influencing the reaction activities. We performed full chemical and electrochemical characterizations of the catalyst electrodes and examined their reaction reversibility, cycling stability, round-trip efficiency and gravimetric energy density at single cell level. We successfully demonstrated enhanced cycle life and round-trip efficiency of rechargeable Li-O2 batteries with the catalysts developed in this project. More importantly, the fundamental catalyst design principle developed in this project will guide the future design of catalyst to further improve the Li-O2 battery performance.

24200414.label: Major findings and research outcome
24200414.value: We revealed that the large overpotential needed for oxygen evolution reaction OER in Li-O2 batteries can be significantly improved by metal-based catalysts in both liquid and solid electrolytes (Part C, No. 1, JPCC 2016). We found that non-metal element and the surface adsorbed species of the metal-based non-carbon-based catalysts play a critical role on the reaction stability and reaction kinetics. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed that carbide/nitride based catalyst exhibit more surface carbonate than that of oxides. Our results showed that carbide based electrode exhibit higher catalytic activity (revealed by cyclic voltammogram) but higher surface reactivity (XPS), which highlights the trade-off between battery efficiency and cycling stability. We employed online electrochemical mass spectrometry to understand the gas evolution during charging of the Li-O2 cells with and without metal carbides and nitrides. We found that the charge reaction OER of Li-O2 batteries is not stable and generates carbonate-based by-products and parasitic gases including H2, CO and CO2 (Part C, No. 2, JACS 2016). The origins responsible for the side reactions are associated the generation of reactive intermediates including lithium deficient Li2-xO2, which then reacted with carbon electrodes and glyme electrolyte (Part C, No. 2, JACS 2016). Our results showed that the use of carbon-free metal carbide reduces the parasitic gas evolution and the surface adsorbed carbon-containing species on the electrode could be responsible for the minor CO2 evolution on charging of the Li-O2 batteries. In addition to the solid catalyst, we further show that the use of soluble catalyst LiBr could help to improve reaction kinetics and reaction stability Li-O2 batteries (Part C, No. 2, JACS 2016). This was inspired by the synergetic effects we discovered between LiI and sulfur redox chemistry (Part C, No. 4, AEM 2016). Furthermore, we develop a new technique operando UV-Vis spectroscopy (Part C, No. 4, JPCL 2016) aiming to understand the reaction mechanism during oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) during the Li-O2 battery operation. Our results indicated that the use of catalyst can reduce the generation of singlet O2, which is a reactive intermediate species generated during operation of Li-O2 batteries. These findings suggest that by-passing the formation of reactive intermediates is a promising future direction to enable a stable and efficient Li-O2 batteries.

24200414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24200414.value: We have shown that employing carbide/nitride based catalyst as well as soluble catalyst is an effective way to improve the battery efficiency and improve the stability of the Li-O2 batteries. Future direction in applying catalyst for both discharge and charge reactions to by-pass side reactions and protect electrode/electrolyte materials is critical in order to further improve the battery performance. Important course of actions includes identifying stable electrolyte that is chemical resistant to LiO2, Li2O2 and singlet O2; decoupling the electrode materials from direct oxygen reduction reaction and oxygen evolution reactions; investigating the stability of solid-state electrolyte toward the Li-O2 reaction species (e.g. LiO2, Li2O2 and singlet O2); developing polymer-sealed solid state electrolyte membrane to block oxygen cross-over to the anode, and developing alternative anode to replace lithium metal anode.

24200414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24200414.value: Developing high-energy and efficient energy storage is critical to bridge the gap between intermittent renewable energy such as solar and wind powers to the user demands. The development of lithium-oxygen batteries is important as it promises three to five times energy density that of the conventional lithium-ion batteries. However, lithium-oxygen technology is still far away from practical application where fundamental and mechanistic research developments are urgently needed. Through this project, we developed metal carbides/nitrides and soluble catalysts to improve the energy efficiency and reaction stability of the lithium-oxygen batteries. We developed multiple online spectroscopy techniques to monitor the battery reactions during it’s operation, from which we identified fundamental origins responsible for parasitic processes in the Li-O2 batteries with and without metal carbides/nitrides electrodes. This project resolves various key scientific open questions and yields several new directions to further improve lithium-oxygen batteries. These fundamental understanding and technological development are important and applicable to other high-energy metal air batteries.

24200514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200514.value: 規範台外金融衍生品的交易是全球監管機構反思2008年金融危機後的重要舉措。其主旨是通過設立中央清算機構和推行實時保證金交易制度來集總管理整個市場的對手信用風險。在各種標的資產中，市值最大的台外市場是以利率為標的的衍生品。利率衍生品的保證金交易涉及兩類資產，一類是標的利率，一類是作為抵押品的高質債券。聯合建立這兩類資產收益曲線的無套利期限結構模型是本研究課題的第一個主題。與此同時，保證金交易的實時性要求所設計的定價模型能夠快速校準市場息動。圍繞漸進解析方法研究掉期期權產品的精確定價公式是本課題的第二個主題。台外利率衍生品有線性產品（如利率遠期和利率掉期）和非線性產品（如利率期權和掉期期權）之分，後者相對前者更為複雜。本課題所研究的期限模型和解析方法將針對後者， 以期能夠用低維度的隨機因子來實時校準利率掉期期權的隱含波動性，尤其是在掉期期限，行權價位，和行權時限這三個維度上的結構。本課題的成功實施一方面能夠對用漸進解析方法研究多資產收益期限結構的定價問題做出一定貢獻，另一方面也能夠為相關金融機構提供有實用價值的定價模型和有實際操作性的校準方法。

24200514.label: Realisation of objectives
24200514.value: 1. The PI constructed a new family of multi-curve term structure model which model the joint risk neutral dynamics of OIS discount curve and LIBOR forward curve. The new model can be degenerated to the simple classic Hull-White model as a simple special case. The "rich" version of the model features multi-factor stochastic volatility and multi-factor yield curve drivers. It is designed to fit the swaption implied volatility cube and to incorporate the two-curve modeling paradigm. The model exhibits non-Gaussian forward swap rates whose distributions are parameterized across the dimensions of the volatility cube: underlying tenor, option strike and option expiration. Objective 1 is thus successfully achieved. 2. To facilitate rapid model calibration, the PI established suitable asymptotic expressions for the bond prices. Furthermore, the PI derived an effective SABR dynamics for each forward swap rate. Finally, the PI used the mean field approximation to match the effective SABR parameters corresponding to each swaption to the market levels. Through these newly developed mathematical treatments, the PI successfully addressed the Objective 2.

24200514.label: Major findings and research outcome
24200514.value: 1. Research outcomes of this project are as follows: a) One journal paper is accepted by "Management Science" in which financial support from this project is acknowledged. MS is a flagship journal in the broad area of operation research and management science. . b) One journal paper is submitted to "Mathematical Finance". The current status is R&R. MF is a flagship journal in the area of financial engineering and quantitative finance . c) 4 presentations were delivered at the most internationally recognized conferences in the area of Financial Engineering. These include 2 top ones in Financial Engineering in USA and 2 main stream regional ones in Europe and Asia. d) 2 Ph.D and 2 Mphill students are successfully trained, besides engaging a dozen of undergraduates along the process. All postgraduate students's research are strongly motivated during the process when the PI's conducting research for this project. e) The PI developed an new graduate course on Interest Rate Term Structure Modeling at his host university, based on the research content through the project. A good portion of the class are undergraduates. f) Collaboration: the PI has established co-authorship with 2 US universities and 1 US Bank, all based in New York. --Baruch College, Department of Mathematics; --Bank of New York Mellon, Division of Market Risk. --Columbia University, Business School, Department of Decision, Risk and Operations. 2. Our major findings are summarized as below: The findings are reflected in the novelties of our model. There are three folds. a) First and foremost, we took the more classical short rate approach, rather than the HJM approach, and justified that short rate approach is more economical in the dual curve context. b) The second novelty is that we are able to capture the swaption cube, which contains one more dimension than the typical implied volatility surface seen in stocks, commodities, etc. The key findings here is the use of multiple factor of stochastic volatility to allow the variation of vol term structure. c) The third one is the novel model calibration method. We formulate the model calibration problem as an novel optimization problem which maps market parameters of the SABR model directly to the optimal model parameters. This approach differs significantly from traditional approach where optimal model parameters are calibrated to prices. All these results are summarized in the Research output 8 (1-2) in Part C, presented and well received in Research output 9 (1-4) .

24300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24300014.value: Nanoparticles are under intense investigation as drug delivery vehicles for the treatment and diagnosis of diseases. Successful translation of nanoparticle-based vehicles from laboratory to clinic is rare, because understanding in the nature of interactions between nanoparticles and the living system remains cursory. Many previous studies elucidated how nanoparticle size dictates their ability to enter cells, but did not delineate the effects of other physicochemical parameters, such as surface charge and shape. For the selected few that probed other parameters, conclusions drawn are often inconsistent from report to report and do not reach a universal consensus. Furthermore, most findings are rather phenomenological and seldom dissect the biological mechanisms for their cellular uptake as well as intracellular events subsequent to cellular entry. In this proposal, we seek to explore how nanoparticles interact with the living system. Specifically, we will investigate the effects of nanoparticle shape, although one can envision the adoption of a similar approach to unraveling the effects of other unexplored parameters. Project success can be realized by the accomplishment of the following milestones. We will first prepare a library of anisotropic nanoparticles (e.g., rods, discs, prisms) that are amenable to the covalent attachment of biomolecules (e.g., oligonucleotides, peptides) to their surface. Such nanoparticles will have near-constant properties such that the only parameter under investigation is shape. Next, we will evaluate the ability of these biomolecule-coated anisotropic nanoparticles to enter cells as a function of nanoparticle geometry (e.g., aspect ratio), and further deduce the specific pathways and proteins involved in the cellular uptake of anisotropic nanoparticles and their intracellular trafficking. Ultimately, we seek to investigate whether results derived from the proposed cell-based studies can be faithfully translated to animals. Using mouse models, we will examine whether the efficiency of delivery of the same biomolecule-coated, anisotropic nanoparticles to a certain cell type in vivo (e.g., hepatocytes of the liver) is consistent with the structure-function relationships established for the same cell type in vitro (e.g., hepatocyte cell line). We will further probe whether the effects of shape at the cellular level contribute to changes in pharmacokinetics and distribution of nanoparticles at the organ and tissue levels. Results from the proposed investigations are not only of interest to a broad scientific audience spanning nanomaterials and cell biology, but also technologically relevant as they inform materials design rules for developing more potent nanoparticle-based therapeutic, diagnostic, or imaging agents that can potentially improve human health. 有關納米顆粒作為藥物載體用於各種疾病的治療和診斷的研究當下正熱，但是以納米顆粒為基礎的載體還沒真正從實驗室走向臨床試驗。究其原因，科研人員並不充分掌握納米顆粒和生物體系之間的相互作用。前人的研究工作主要解釋納米顆粒的大小如何支配納米顆粒進入細胞的能力，但是並沒有探明其他物理化學性質對於細胞攝取的影響，比如表面電荷和形狀。從目前有限的嘗試探究納米顆粒其他性質的文獻來看，得出的結論並不一致，學術界并沒有對此問題達成共識。而且，大多數研究成果僅局限於現象觀察，絕少剖析對於細胞攝取納米顆粒的生物機理及隨後的細胞內運輸。 在本提案中，我們旨在探索納米顆粒和生物體系之間的相互作用。具體來說，我們先調查納米顆粒的形狀的影響。在預見的將來，我們會採取類近的手段，探究其它物理化學性質的影響。本提案的成功，將取決於以下里程碑能否實現。首先，我們會合成一系列非球狀的納米顆粒（如棒狀、圓盤形、角柱等），並利用共價鍵把生物分子（如寡核苷酸、多肽）修飾它們的表面。這些納米顆粒的物理化學性質基本一致，確保我們唯一研究的物理化學性質就是形狀。 接著，我們將評估幾何特徵（比如長徑比）如何影響這些經生物分子修飾的非球形納米顆粒進入細胞的能力，並進一步推斷細胞攝取及運輸過程中所涉及到的內吞作用和相對應的蛋白。 最後，我們將探討提案中細胞實驗的結果能否成功在動物實現。透過小鼠動物模型，我們將驗證此等經生物分子修飾的非球形納米顆粒分別在體內、體外相同的細胞類型中得到同樣的結構和功能關係，例如體內肝實質細胞和體外肝細胞系。此外，我們將探究不同形狀的納米顆粒在細胞層面的影響能否影響其在器官和組織層面上的藥物動力學和生物分佈。 本提案的研究成果不僅能夠引起納米材料和細胞生物學界的廣泛興趣，而且與技術工業界息息相關。成功的實驗結果將揭示若干材料設計規則，有助於發展更有效的以納米顆粒為基礎的藥物、診斷劑或影像劑，改善人類健康。

24300014.label: Realisation of objectives
24300014.value: Objective 1: We have fully achieved our stated objectives. In our first publication (Yang H et al, Small, 2016), we have synthesized and characterized a collection of DNA-coated gold nanorods of defined aspect ratios (ARs), from 1 (nanosphere) and 2 (short nanorod) to 4 and 7 (longer nanorods). These DNA-coated nanostructures can effectively target Class A scavenger receptors on the surface of C166 endothelial cells. As their untargeted nanoparticles, we have synthesized and characterized poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-coated gold nanorods of the same aspect ratios (ARs). Both DNA and PEG-coated nanorods of all ARs are stable in serum-containing medium for 24 h. In our second publication (Ho LWC et al, ACS Nano, 2017), we have prepared densely PEGylated gold nanoparticles that bear alkyl chains of varying carbon chain lengths (n) and loading densities (termed “alkyl-PEG-AuNPs”). On chain length, these alkyl groups include hexyl (n = 6), dodecyl (n = 12), and octadecyl (n = 18). We have also included methoxy as a control functional group against alkyl groups. On loading density, the alkyl groups occupy from 1% to 100% of the PEG shell for all three chain lengths considered. As an alkyl loading higher than 10% led to agglomeration of nanoparticles, and in the spirit of decoupling the effects of hydrophobicity and alkylation, we have capped the maximal alkyl loading density at 4% for our cell-based studies. In serum-containing medium, alkyl-PEG-AuNPs touch one another without irreversible aggregation. In our third publication (Yang H et al, Nanoscale, 2018), we have synthesized and characterized a collection of PEG-coated gold nanoparticles of four defined sizes, including 3 nm, 6 nm, 13 nm, and 20 nm. Attachment of fluorophores to the PEG shell, for tracking their localization inside the cell by confocal microscopy, did not affect their colloidal stability and their cellular uptake. For our compression studies, some of the PEG-coated nanoparticles will be embedded inside a porous hydrogel for compression for 140 min. These particles of all sizes are stable in serum-containing medium for 140 min, and their introduction to the gel does not change the stress-strain relationship of the hydrogel. Objective 2: We have fully achieved our stated objectives. In our first publication (Yang H et al, Small, 2016), we have observed contrasting dependencies of cellular uptake on AR when the gold nanorods display targeting or non-targeting biomolecules. For the non-targeted (or PEG-coated) nanorods, cellular uptake monotonically decreases with AR. For targeted (or DNA-coated) nanorods, however, we observed an optimal AR that maximizes cellular entry. That is, short nanorods (AR = 2) enter C166 cells more than nanospheres (AR = 1) and long nanorods (AR = 4 or 7). Due to their higher cellular uptake, short DNA-coated nanorods traffic to the late endosomes sooner than DNA-coated nanorods of other ARs, but eventually all DNA-coated nanorods accumulate in the late endosomes. Interestingly, DNA-coated nanorods of all ARs did not progress to the lysosomes. In our second publication (Ho LWC et al, ACS Nano, 2017), we have shown that, provided a modest alkyl mass percentage of 0.2% (2 orders of magnitude lower than that of conventional lipid-based NPs) in their PEG shells, dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 12) and octadecyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 18) can enter Kera-308 cells 30-fold more than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs (no alkyl groups) and hexyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 6) after 24 h of incubation. Such strong dependence on n is valid for all serum concentrations considered (even under serum-free conditions). Most alkyl-PEG-AuNPs adopt the “endo-lysosomal” route of trafficking, independent of ∼15% of them accumulate in the cytosol. Regardless of intracellular location, alkyl-PEG-AuNPs predominantly appear as individual entities after 24 h of incubation. In our third publication (Yang H et al, Nanoscale, 2018), we have shown that the uptake of PEG-coated nanoparticles smaller than 25 nm by compressed C2C12 myoblasts is up to 5-fold higher than that by uncompressed cells. The optimal compressive stress for maximizing the cellular uptake of sub-25 nm NPs monotonically increases with nanoparticle size. We have also observed an effect of extracellular compression on the intracellular localization of nanoparticles. Notably, for all sizes considered, the nanoparticles more readily reside in the late endosomes or lysosomes of compressed cells than uncompressed cells. Objective 3: We have fully achieved our stated objectives. In our first publication (Yang H et al, Small, 2016), we have provided, to our knowledge, the first experimental evidence of how targeted nanorods by TEM imaging: Long DNA nanorods align to the cell membrane in a near-parallel manner followed by rotating by ~90° to enter the cell. For all ARs considered, the DNA-targeted nanorods adopt the caveolae-mediated pathway to enter C166 endothelial cells, and can also bind to Class A scavenger receptors. In our second publication (Ho LWC et al, ACS Nano, 2017), we have shown that alkyl-PEG-AuNPs can rapidly enter Kera-308 skin keratinocytes via the filipodia-mediated pathway, engaging the tips of membrane protrusions and accumulating within interdigital folds. On the contrary, they do not adopt the conventional pathways of entry, such as clathrin-mediated endocytosis, caveolae-mediated endocytosis, and dynamin-mediated endocytosis. In our third publication (Yang H et al, Nanoscale, 2018), we have demonstrated the effect of extracellular compression on the mechanism of cellular uptake sub-25 nm PEG-coated gold nanoparticles by C2C12 myoblasts. With and without compression, the nanoparticles of all sizes enter C2C12 cells via energy-dependent uptake. Interestingly, the nanoparticles enter compressed cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis as the major pathway. Objective 4: We have partially achieved our stated objectives. My research group spent considerable time on publishing the above three papers (all in decent journals with an impact factor higher than 7) based on cell-based experiments. Toward the completion stage of the ECS project, I made an intellectual judgment to allot less time for the animal-based studies for the three different types of nanoparticles discussed above (i.e., DNA-coated gold nanorods, alkyl-terminated PEG-coated gold nanospheres, and PEG-coated nanoparticles). Below, we will explain our progress made toward understanding the in vivo behavior of PEG-coated nanorods and alkyl-terminated PEG-coated nanoparticles till this point. After systemically injecting PEG-coated gold nanoparticles of various aspect ratios, we sacrificed the animals after 24 hours and collected their major organs for ICP measurements. AuNPs, regardless of aspect ratio, mainly accumulate in the liver and spleen. For other organs such as kidney, the accumulation ratio is below 1%. Nanorods with a smaller AR show higher accumulation in liver and spleen, especially for AR=2. Clearance of long nanorods (AR=4 and AR=7) is faster than that of short nanorods (AR=2). We also systemically injected alkyl-PEG-AuNPs into BALB/c mice. 24 hours post-injection, the nanoparticles mainly accumulate in the liver, spleen, and kidney. Other organs show insignificant accumulation [<0.2% of the injected dose (ID)]. Addition of 0.5 mol% dodecyl groups to the PEGylated NPs results in ~1.5-fold more NP accumulation in the liver than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs. Addition of 0.5 mol% dodecyl groups to the PEGylated NPs results in ~1.5-fold more NP accumulation in the liver than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs. Notably, addition of 4 mol% dodecyl groups on the PEGylated NPs drastically changes the biodistribution of NPs. 50% ID of dodecyl4%-PEG-AuNPs accumulated in the spleen, ~2-fold higher than that of dodecyl0.5%-PEG-AuNPs or methoxy-PEG-AuNPs. The liver and spleen together sequestered up to 90% ID of dodecyl4%-PEG-AuNPs.

24300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
24300014.value: Effect of nanoparticle geometry and receptor targeting (Yang H, Small, 2016; ASME NEMB Conference 2016 and MRS Fall Meeting 2016 with acknowledgment of RGC funding): When coated with poly(ethylene glycol) strands, cellular uptake of untargeted nanoparticles monotonically decreases with aspect ratio (AR). When nanoparticles are functionalized with DNA oligonucleotides to target Class A scavenger receptors expressed by C166 cells, cellular uptake is maximized at a particular AR. Shorter nanorods (AR = 2) enter C166 cells more than nanospheres (AR = 1) and longer nanorods (AR = 4 or 7). Long targeted nanorods align to the cell membrane before rotating by 90° to enter the cell. Upon cellular entry, targeted nanorods of all ARs predominantly traffic to the late endosome without progressing to the lysosome. Effect of alkyl chain length (n) and alkyl loading density (Ho et al, ACS Nano, 2017; SBE ICBE Conference 2018 with acknowledgment of RGC funding): Provided a modest alkyl mass percentage of 0.2% (two orders of magnitude lower than that of conventional lipid-based NPs) in their PEG shells, dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 12) and octadecyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 18) can enter Kera-308 cells 30-fold more than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs (no alkyl groups) and hexyl-PEG-AuNPs (n = 6) after 24 h of incubation. Alkyl-PEG-AuNPs rapidly enter Kera-308 cells via the filipodia-mediated pathway, engaging the tips of membrane protrusions and accumulating within interdigital folds. Most alkyl-PEG-AuNPs adopt the “endo-lysosomal” route of trafficking, but ∼15% of them accumulate in the cytosol. Effect of compressive strain and nanoparticle size (Yang H, Nanoscale, 2018; ASME NEMB Meeting 2018 with acknowledgment of RGC funding): Uptake of PEG-coated gold nanoparticles smaller than 25 nm by compressed C2C12 myoblasts is up to 5-fold higher than that by uncompressed cells. The optimal compressive stress for maximizing the cellular uptake of sub-25 nm nanoparticles monotonically increases with nanoparticle size. With and without compression, the Au-PEG NPs enter C2C12 cells via energy-dependent uptake; they also enter compressed cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis as the major pathway. Upon cellular entry, the nanoparticles more readily reside in the late endosomes or lysosomes of compressed cells than uncompressed cells.

24300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24300014.value: Our data on the optimal aspect ratio of gold nanorods for cellular uptake inspire us to develop contrast agents for label-free contrast agents for dark-field microscopy. We will attempt cell imaging without the attachment of fluorophores that may add colloidal stability to nanoparticles and influence their cellular uptake. We will explore their application as NIR-absorbing agents for photothermal therapy. Our data on the optimal alkyl chain length and loading density for effective cellular uptake of nanoparticles by skin keratinocytes motivate us to develop new alkyl-containing nanoparticle-based carriers of drug molecules or genes for topical application. We will explore their permeation through the skin epidermis with diseased mouse models, such as dermatitis and psoriasis. Our data on the optimal nanoparticle size and compressive stress for effective cellular uptake of nanoparticles by mouse myoblasts prompt us to investigate the relationship between intracellular trafficking and cellular biomechanics. We also aspire to develop other compressive-inspired approaches to delivering nanoparticles to other cell types that constantly experience extracellular compression under physiological conditions, such as osteocytes and chondrocytes.

24300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24300014.value: In this ECS proposal, we have performed detailed investigations into the effects of different nanoparticle design parameters (e.g., size, geometry, type of biomolecules attached, and functional groups) on the cellular uptake of nanoparticles as well as the of their movement to different organelles inside the cell. The mechanistic insights derived from this work inform important materials design rules for building bionanomaterials that can effectively enter mammalian cells and target specific organelles. These data will benefit the design of nanoparticle-based biomedical products such as drug carriers, imaging agents, and molecular diagnostic tools. The results will also appeal to the academia and industry from the diverse communities of nanotechnology, pharmacology, and cell biology.
