24300814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24300814.value: 摘要 這個項目的目的是利用密度泛函理論的方法，通過共摻雜和應變，來控制拓撲絕緣體（TI）中磁性摻雜。 摻雜和缺陷控制在半導體器件中至關重要。在磁性半導體器件中，通過摻入磁性雜質來獲得磁矩是可能的。因為磁學性質和電子性質在這類器件中相互作用的廣闊前景，磁性摻雜吸引了大量研究興趣。TI，作為唯一一種實現了量子反常霍爾效應的材料，在磁性半導體中的重要性非常突出。然而，由於雜質和取代元素之間的尺寸不匹配，或者由於雜質元素的低磁矩，TI磁性摻雜和磁性的控制是非常困難的。雜質和晶格之間復雜的軌道耦合使這個問題極具挑戰性。 因此，TI中，磁性摻雜和磁性的控制策略的研究還非常少見。 密度泛函理論（DFT）由於能夠準確計算摻雜和缺陷的性質，因而是一種有效的研究方法。通過DFT研究，我們曾經提出了許多新策略，來控制諸如磷化鎵，氧化鋅，矽，銅鋅錫硒等半導體雜質和缺陷的濃度以及類型。在這個項目中，我們計劃，（1）研究TI材料（Bi2Se3）中磁性摻雜的尺寸效應; （2）施加外部應變來控制磁性摻雜濃度和調整它們的磁性，特別是研究應變將如何控制自旋有序性，磁有序性，軌道有序性，以及它們之間的相互作用，並且探索共摻雜元素對的可能性。 我們的研究結果將有助於提升對於應變控制下，磁摻雜和磁學性質的基礎科學研究。對於TI，我們希望我們的研究結果能夠提高磁性摻雜濃度，並且進一步提升量子反常霍爾效應。這些結果將直接影響到TI與量子反常霍爾效應的領域。磁性摻雜和磁性控制的總體策略將有助於提高磁存儲設備和其他自旋電子學器件的效率。這些器件都已經或者將要在我們的日常生活中扮演重要的角色。

24300814.label: Realisation of objectives
24300814.value: Firstly, we have carried out a systematic investigation on 4f transition metal doped Bi2Se3. We predicted that Eu and Sm are promising to introduce stable long-range ferromagnetic states in Bi2Se3. And further, codoping method with group VII codopants was proposed to maintain a semiconducting electronic structure. These important results offer a step in facilitating the realization of QAHE in TI systems. Continuously, we also systematically investigated the 4d transition metal doped Bi2Se3. We found out that the absence of QAHE in such cases results from the AFM ordering as well as gapless character induced by 4d dopants, explaining why 4d transition metal may not lead to insulating long range magnetic ordering. Moreover, during the process of the investigations aforementioned, we reexamined the cases of 3d transition metal doping in TI, and found the key mechanism of the only working example of carrier-free long-range magnetism, experimentally observed in group-V tellurides quintuple layers. We discovered that the lone pair state of Bi or Sb is the key component that mediates the long range ferromagnetic coupling. To our surprise, the dopant Cr has a strong magnetic coupling with its seventh nearest neighbor, which is the ground state for two atom doping case. We called it as stepping stone mechanism, which provided an important guideline for further discoveries of new dilute magnetic semiconductors. To further study the codoping effect on long range magnetism, we found that stepping stone mechanism does not only belongs to TI materials. In the semiconductor LiZnAs, we discovered that a long-range magnetic ordering appears when Mn and an acceptor are codoped in it, which can be regarded as an approach of precise control of the magnetic order in future spintronics. Those works aforementioned open up the door of further investigations on other novel magnetic phenomena in varieties of materials. Recently, we collaborated with other experimental groups, studied the electronic structure and quantum oscillation properties in the semimetal ScSb, and studied the magnetism mechanism as well as gating properties in a novel 2D magnetic metal Fe3GeTe2. Note that in the nature paper, we discovered a room temperature ferromagnetism in 2D material system and attracted a lot of research attentions. Therefore, we firmly believe that our research objectives are all well achieved. Based on the research, new physical mechanism of stepping stone was discovered. New codoping and strain doping strategies have been proposed, and room temperature 2D magnetic materials have been discovered.

24300814.label: Major findings and research outcome
24300814.value: Firstly, we have carried out a systematic investigation on 4f transition metal doped Bi2Se3. We predicted that Eu and Sm are promising to introduce stable long-range ferromagnetic states in Bi2Se3. And further, codoping method with group VII elements was proposed to maintain a semiconducting electronic structure. These important results, which offer a step in facilitating the realization of QAHE in TI systems, are published on Physical Review B. And we presented this work on the 2017 APS March Meeting. Codoping strategy is a generally effective method for tuning material properties, including the magnetic properties in TI that we concentrated on. Therefore, we also published an invited review paper of the codoping method in semiconductors on Frontier of Physics. Continuously, we also systematically investigated the 4d transition metal doped Bi2Se3. We found out that the absence of QAHE in such cases results from the AFM ordering as well as gapless character induced by 4d dopants, explaining the puzzle of why 4d transition metal can not be doped to induce carrier free long range magnetism in Bi2Se3. These important results have been published on Physical Review B. Moreover, during the process of the investigations aforementioned, we reexamined the cases of 3d transition metal doping in TI, and found the key mechanism of the only working example of carrier-free long-range magnetism, experimentally observed in group-V tellurides quintuple layers. This long range magnetic interaction is due to the lone pair state of Bi or Sb. We called it as stepping stone mechanism, which provided important guideline for further discoveries of new dilute magnetic semiconductors. This important work has been published on Chinese Physics Letters as an express letter. We also found that such mechanism not only belongs to TI materials. In the semiconductor LiZnAs, we discovered that a long-range magnetic ordering appears when Mn and an acceptor are codoped in it, which can be regarded as an approach of precise control of the magnetic order in future spintronics. This work has been preprinted on arxiv, and submitted to Physical review letters, still under review.And we presented this work on the 2017 CPS Fall Meeting and the 2018 APS March Meeting. Those works aforementioned open up the door of further investigations on other novel magnetic phenomena in varieties of materials. Recently, we collaborated with other experimental groups, studied the electronic structure and quantum oscillation properties in the semimetal ScSb, and studied the magnetism mechanism as well as gating properties in a novel 2D magnetic metal Fe3GeTe2. This two works have been published on Physical Review B and Nature, respectively. Note that in the nature paper, room temperature ferromangetism was first time reported in 2D materials. We presented this Nature work on the 2018 CPS Fall Meeting.

24300814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24300814.value: The most important discovery of this project is the general long range magnetic ordering mechanism which is independent of band topology. This model is named as stepping stone model. We offered a Hubbard electron hopping model to explain this model. Still, the realization of the long range carrier free magnetic ordering is challenging. Currently, Cr doped (SbBi)2Te3 is the only working system. Inspired by the so called "stepping stone" mechanism, we are currently searching for new material systems with strong long range magnetic couplings and have some preliminary results already. Therefore, it's possible to go further along this direction to eventually solve the most challenging problem in condense matter physics, which is to realize diluted magnetism in semiconductors that may lead to revolutionary spintronic devices.

24300814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24300814.value: Our key discoveries including a systematic study of transition metal and rare earth metal doped topological insulator systems. We proposed various codoping strategies to neutralize the carrier, maintain the band topology, and achieve strong magnetism. We also explained why 4D metals are not good candidates for Bi2Se3. Also, during our investigation of long range vs. short range magnetic coupling, we discovered that key physical mechanism, "stepping stone mechanism", that lead to the realization of the very long range magnetic coupling in Cr doped Bi2Te3. Inspired by this mechanism, we further proposed codoping strategy to tune the long range and short range magnetic coupling, which is very important in the engineering of magnetic devices. Also, based on our mechanism and studies, we discovered the room temperature ferromagnetism and the gating behavior in 2D materials, which was published in Nature one month ago.

24400114.label: Project Objectives
24400114.value: To promote the use of bamboo as an environmentally sustainable, economical construction material, suitable both for Hong Kong and for broader areas with easy access to bamboo. To advocate and explore the use of real-time physics engines in architectural design, allowing earlier feedback on the physical performance of structures, resulting in more economically and ecologically viable structures. To expand the geometric repertoire of bending-active shell structures by using virtual simulation environments for the geometric definition, rather than the highly restrictive physical models used in the 1970s. To test the construction of light-weight, bending-active, bamboo shells through prototyping. To revitalise the pressured Cantonese Scaffolding Industry's role by offering it new construction methods and structural designs where bamboo is part of the final architecture; thus giving this traditional craftsmanship the opportunity to safeguard its sustainable future.

24400114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24400114.value: This project investigates how available construction systems for Bamboo Scaffolding building in Hong Kong can be expanded with methods for the architectural design and construction of bending-active, bamboo shell structures. It brings together research from three significant, yet separated fields: bamboo architecture; bending-active shell structures; and architectural design through live physics engines for interactive simulation, optimisation and form-finding. These are combined in a project that will result in the development of construction methods for light-weight, environmentally friendly, large span shell structures, which will be tested through a full-scale built prototype. Bamboo is a widely available, environmentally friendly material that is currently only used in Cantonese construction industries for temporary scaffolding. This project begins by mapping out alternative applications of bamboo as an architectural construction material in various cultures globally. A comparative analysis of preservation methods, construction detailing and building regulations will sketch a comprehensive application framework. Combined with the study of built architecture precedents, this will reveal empirically proven ways to technically expand currently available Cantonese bamboo construction methods. In parallel, research will be undertaken in the recent advent of various computational design tools that allow real-time feedback and physical performance evaluation of designed structures through live physics engines. Similar to analogue material computation methods used to find ideal geometries by pioneers, such as Antoni Gaudí or Frei Otto, these tools apply real-world, macroscopic properties to virtual particle systems. In real-time, rather than over the span of months, structurally optimised forms and equilibrium surfaces can be derived from these digital setups. These surfaces can then automatically be translated into construction documentation for realising economically, ecologically and structurally optimised, light-weight structures that require minimum amounts of material for maximum spans. Bending-active grid shells form a sub-group within this research, which consists of shell made from a spatially curved framework of rods and rigid joints. Although small-scale tests with grid shells from bamboo have taken place in the past, and large grid shells from wood or paper tubes have been built, no large scale applications in bamboo have been realised. This project’s final design research component consists of the construction of various small and one large-scale prototype for bending-active bamboo shells. Ultimately, this project aims to promote ecologically sustainable construction methods for large structural spans, and to expose ways for traditional Cantonese Bamboo Scaffolding to productively adapt and evolve for the 21st century architecture and construction industry. 這個研究主要探討在如何從香港常見的竹棚衍生成彎曲活動結構。希望藉著新的建築設計及建造方法去擴大竹在建造薄殼結構的可能性。 我們的研究可分為三個不同領域: 竹造建築，彎曲活動結構，及通过实时的物理模擬軟件來優化建筑設計，我們將會集合三方面研究所得, 設計新的建造方法， 然後建造一個原型進行測試。 竹在香港被廣泛應用為臨時結構，它環保， 材料供應充足，這促使竹棚成為香港建造業的特色之一。這研究首先由在東西方文化中找尋一些特別的竹結構開始。我們會比較它們的保存方法，參考其建築細節和法則，然後繪製一個更實用的竹建築手冊。加上對竹建筑先例的研究，保留傳統竹棚建造方法，這將會促進廣東現時竹建造業的發展。 近年有不少模擬物料物理特質的軟件面世，運用這些軟件，我們可以得到物料的即時反饋及對設計的結構評估。建築師Antoni Gaudí, Frei Otto 及他的 Institute for Lightweight Structures都是以模擬材料物理來尋找理想的幾何型狀的先驅。運用相同的原理， 那些軟件把真實世界裡的物理特性以電腦中的粒子系統模擬出來， 令原本需時幾個月的計算大大縮短，我們甚至可即時得到最理想的結構形狀。使我們可以輕易地設計出一個合符經濟, 環保, 結構等各方面原則的竹建築, 以更少的材料便可以建成更闊的跨距。 研究裡再設小組專責研究彎曲活動薄殼結構。它由直桿(竹) 型成的曲面網狀以及接駁零件組成。雖然曾有人以竹作小型薄殼結構測試， 或者以木及紙管建造大型薄殼結構，但至今仍沒有以竹來作大型薄殼結構。這個計劃最後會包括以竹製造各種小型及一個大型的彎曲活動薄殼結構。 這計劃的最大目的是宣傳可持續建築，尤其是建造大跨度的結構上，同時發展傳統竹棚手藝，使之能在現化建築設計及建造上與時並進。

24400114.label: Major findings and research outcome
24400114.value: The major research finding is the discovery of a new method for the construction of bamboo bending-active gridshell structures that suits traditional Hong Kong Cantonese Scaffolding methods. The major research outcome is the design and construction of the ‘ZCB Bamboo Pavilion’ as a proof of concept of this method. Up until now, gridshells were usually built following the ‘flatbed’ method. ‘Flatbed’ structures employ initially flat, prefabricated, regular grids with no shear rigidity, and elastically deform and brace those into place. This mode of working does not work well with bamboo due to the material’s irregularities, nor does it fit well with Cantonese Scaffolding techniques that build structures one stick at a time. The project devised the alternative ‘lay-up’ method for bamboo bending-active structures. The ‘lay-up’ method additively bends and joins individual members into a final shape onsite. The challenge and innovation of this method lies in the design data development, management and translation for construction. New construction implementation protocols were set up to handle tolerances from material and installation without losing overall project rigour and holistic control. Because of this design control system, the geometrically complex structures could be straightforwardly materialised, which in turn substantially expands the design solution space available to bamboo architecture and traditional Cantonese Craftsmanship. Several journal and conference articles were written to discuss these methods in detail. Also, a series of international exhibitions and public talks presented these findings. The ‘ZCB Bamboo Pavilion’ received 16 international design and research awards, highlighting its importance and impact (see Part C).

24400114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24400114.value: The research findings provide valuable fundamental research data for bending-active bamboo structures in architecture. The project’s scientific process can be logically continued by working towards more widespread implementation and the transition of gained knowledge into practice. This will be the topic of a follow-up GRF grant application, where the focus will be on the development of ‘Guidelines of Best Practice’ and a ‘Taxonomy Overview’. These two documents will facilitate access to the building typology form designers and architects, and will proved the required knowledge to coordinate implementation with Cantonese Scaffolding builders. Following this, future grant applications can address policy matters in detail, focussing on the hiatus in the building ordinance to allow for the application of these structures. In parallel, the research findings can be inferred to other building contexts and materials. Bamboo grows in the most rapidly developing parts of the world. With minor adjustments to the idiosyncrasies of local building contexts, the methods should allow for straightforward local implementation. Alternative materials could also be introduced. The parameter-driven setup of the structures suggests that large parts of the method could be reused when material input parameters are changed.

24400114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24400114.value: This research project expands the types of construction systems for Bamboo Scaffolding building in Hong Kong by introducing novel methods for the architectural design and construction of bending-active, bamboo shell structures. Bending-active shells are amongst the most material-efficient, hyper-light-weight structures. They rely for strength and construction implementation on the overall geometrical double curvature and elastic bending properties of their components. Their nonstandard geometries provide unique spatial design opportunities, and their material efficiency results in a reduced need for natural resources. Bamboo is a material of high environmental and socio-cultural importance. It is one of the fastest growing, widely available, low-cost, carbon-sequestering natural resources suitable for direct implementation in construction. It has globally been part of vernacular construction for centuries, but is bamboo is hardly incorporated as a viable structural material in today’s construction. The significance and value of this research lies in the expansion of the design solution space of bamboo structures with contemporary answers, tested through built large-scale structures as proof of concept. The project positively impacts both the built environment as well as the locally significant but dwindling building traditions and cultural craftsmanship.

24400614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24400614.value: After three decades of massive internal migration in post-reform China, an increasing number of second-generation migrant youth, children of migrant workers who were either born in or brought to their parents’ adopted cities and have spent most of their childhood there, are entering adulthood and becoming a key source of urban China’s labor pool. However, the rural-urban dividing hukou (household registration) system still prevents them from translating their urban residence into formal urban citizenship in their adopted cities. Despite their increasing weight upon China’s future sociopolitical landscapes, second-generation migrant youth remain largely hidden from both empirical and analytical view. This proposed project looks beyond the well-studied realm of first-generation migrant workers to explore how economic boundaries are transgressed, sociopolitical hierarchies redrawn, and cultural meanings re-defined among their children. Taking Shanghai as a case study, my research seeks to understand how state policies of urbanization, local economic restructuring under global market forces, and the political rhetoric of social harmony translate into the life chances of second-generation migrant youth. From January 2015 to December 2016, this project will examine the aspirations, experiences, and perspectives of second-generation migrant youth who finished vocational schooling and started working in Shanghai. Through participant observation, semi-structured interviews, panel discussions, and surveys, this project pays particular attention to three significant but unexplored aspects of migrant youth adulthood: working experience, love life, and recreational consumption. By doing so, it provides new and critical insight into how institutional barriers based on the hukou system and widespread sociocultural discriminations against migrancy and rurality in urban China have shaped migrant youth’s employment opportunities, marriage prospects, and social lives. This project investigates the governing techniques that serve the state agenda of population control, economic development, and social stability by preserving existing socioeconomic hierarchies in Chinese cities like Shanghai as well as the everyday practices and subjective experiences of migrant youth in response to such top-down reproduction schemes. By providing insight into the constant tensions and negotiations between state policies, market forces, and individual agencies amid China’s rapid urbanization and economic restructuring, my research contributes to the scholarship of citizenship, social reproduction, intergenerational mobility, social class formation, and youth culture in a late-socialist context.

24400614.label: Realisation of objectives
24400614.value: The PI successfully completed the objectives. 1) Through participant observation and open-ended interviews between 2015 and 2017 with key informants that the PI has known since 2008, the PI gained longitudinal, ethnographic data of their trajectories from middle-school to the first few years in the job market and their experiences during the process. By doing so, the PI generated ethnographic data to complete a book manuscript, which is currently under review by Stanford University Press. The book manuscript illuminates on the impacts of the hereditary hukou status upon second-generation migrant youth and the nature of urban citizenship and governance in post-reform China. 2) Through questionnaire surveys with sixty pairs of parents and their children who grew up and attended vocational schools in Shanghai, the PI compiled a data-set that provides both quantitative and qualitative information for analysis on social mobility and inter-generational differences with regards to educational achievement, working experience, dating practices, and marriage preferences. 3) Through six focus group discussions in Shanghai, the PI probed into the experiences and subjectivity of Shanghai vocational graduates (including both second-generation migrant youth and Shanghai local youth) during their school-to-work transition and how they experience and talk about the role of hukou in their job searches, dating practices, and future development. 4) The PI also gained insights of migrant youth culture by hanging out during fieldwork with some of the key informants, attending two of their weddings, and studying their social media usage and postings. 5) The PI has been working closely with a local NGO that provides educational services to migrant children in Shanghai. The PI uses research expertise and findings to give suggestions on program development, help train social workers, and serve as a mentor to some of the migrant students and social workers. 6) Due to the changing political environment and tightened media control in mainland China, the PI experienced delay in terms of carrying out survey studies in Shanghai so that the PI had to extend the project duration. Nevertheless, the PI managed to outsource the survey to a local scholar in Shanghai who has much more institutional support and local access. To ensure research quality, the PI went to Shanghai twice to train in person the student assistants who helped conduct the survey and closely monitored the process through regular communication with the local research team and double-check each questionnaire input. 7) Although the political atmosphere and media control in mainland China are getting worse, the PI has been disseminating not only in international conferences but also through workshops, public talks and social media in mainland China her research findings and critique of China's hukou and education systems, esp. the recent population control policies in megacities like Shanghai and Beijing after the 2014 hukou reform. The PI also did an interview with a prominent Chinese journal to discuss the difficulties facing second-generation migrant youth to make policy recommendations and raise public awareness. 8) Due to the heavy teaching load in the academic year of 2016-2017 (2 undergraduate courses plus 1 directed reading course for postgraduate students per semester) and administrative duties in a small department with only a few full-time teaching faculty), the PI was unable to utilize fully the survey data collected in the late spring of 2017 in Shanghai to develop or revise papers as much as the PI would like to. But the PI will continue to work on the conference papers for future publication.

24400614.label: Major findings and research outcome
24400614.value: Ethnographic data from field work and survey data generated in Shanghai do suggest that China's hukou barriers continue to circumvent second-generation migrant youth's life chances, especially during their school-to-work transition and when they are set up their own families and have children. The local-nonlocal distinction maintained by the hukou system remains tangible at their major life stages and exercise as invisible borderwork within national boundaries. The effects of hukou are, nevertheless, much less pronounced in their sociocultural lives. Migrant youth themselves tend to dismiss or underestimate the importance of hukou distinction in daily practices, including dating practices. They do not fully identify themselves as Shanghainese even though they grew up in Shanghai or were born in Shanghai. Their ambiguous sense of belonging and fluid, deterritorialized identity are double-edged. As Shanghai's economy keeps growing, these second-generation migrant youth share optimism to various extents and strive to make best out of their circumscribed situations. Little evidence suggests class consciousness or the potential of class formation in the Marxist sense among these youth in Shanghai. Political initiatives to push for policy change and social equality are largely absent among them. 1. The PI has published 2 sole-authored English-written articles that are enriched by newly collected data from this project in renowned international peer-reviewed journals in 2017. 2. The PI completed one book manuscript on migrant youth in Shanghai to illuminate on the politics of urban citizenship and governance in post-reform China. The manuscript is currently under review by Stanford University Press. Hopefully the PI will get two anonymous reviewers' feedback by April 2018 to revise the manuscript accordingly for publication by 2019. 3. The PI has presented sole-authored 7 papers in major referred international conferences on different aspects of this project between 2015 and July 2017. One of the conference papers, entitled "Learning Not to Labor" has been revised and submitted for review. The PI has been developing the other conference papers for publication in peer-reviewed journals. 4. The PI organized a workshop in Shanghai on "Cultural Anthropological Take on Migrant Youth in Urban China" in December 2016. In addition to the PI, four invited Chinese scholars discussed their latest research on migrant children and youth issues and exchanged ideas. Prof. Sun Bin from University of Virginia served as discussant and a dozen graduate students of sociology from East China University of Science and Technology attended the workshop. 5. The PI gave 2 public talks on migrant youth issues in top Chinese universities. The PI also did one interview with a major Chinese media Caixin in March 2018 to raise public awareness of hukou discrimination against migrant youth and how such hukou discrimination affects their life chances. Please refer to the publication record in Part C for details.

24400614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24400614.value: 1) The PI has been developing the conference papers for publication in international peer-reviewed journals. 2) The data-set built on the questionnaire survey offers sixty pairs of parent-child profiles and sheds light on inter-generational changes and/or continuities in terms of educational achievement, working experience, consumer behaviors, and social values. There is possibility in developing a larger collaborative project with sociologists on intergenerational mobility and social change through the lens of migrant families by conducting a large-scale survey and involving both qualitative and quantitative research methods for data analysis. 3) During fieldwork, the PI observed a new form of housing arrangement adopted by low-income migrant families in Shanghai. The PI presented a conference paper entitled "Snail House: Bulldozer Urbanism and Container Livelihood in Shanghai" in the end of 2017 based on field data. The PI will also join a conference panel on demolition in urban China if it is accepted by the American Anthropological Association in 2018 after peer-review. The recent demolition of migrant enclaves and forced relocation of migrants in Beijing and other major cities invites more empirical and analytical studies. The PI may develop a collaborative project with urban anthropologists to compare different housing strategies among different social groups across regions in the future.

24400614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24400614.value: An increasing number of second-generation migrant youth, who were either born in or brought to their parents’ adopted cities and have spent most of their childhood there, are entering adulthood and becoming a key source of urban China’s labor pool. However, they remain largely hidden from both empirical and analytical view despite their increasing weight upon China’s future sociopolitical landscapes. This project is the first qualitative study of second-generation migrant youth as they join the labor force in Shanghai. Through participant observation, semi-structured interviews, panel discussions, and surveys, it studies migrant youth’s aspirations, experiences, and perspectives as they finished vocational schooling and started working in Shanghai. This project focuses on three significant but unexplored aspects of migrant youth's adulthood: working experience, marriage prospects, and recreational consumption. Takes Shanghai as a case study, this study reveals how China's hereditary household registration (hukou) system, which ties individual eligibility to social welfares with one's registered hukou place rather than residential place, affects second-generation migrant youth’s experiences and subjectivities. The findings provide new and critical insights to the scholarship of citizenship, social reproduction, intergenerational mobility, class formation, and youth culture as China continues its socialist market economic reforms.

24400714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24400714.value: This project investigates how teachers use language to mediate junior secondary science learning in English. It uses tools from systemic functional linguistics (SFL) to explicate classroom sequences where the teacher is moving students from their ‘commonsense’ understanding towards the school science. It has long been recognized that learning science is dependent upon an academic language use which can be difficult even for those studying through their first language. English for school science has been studied in English-language contexts such as the UK and Australia from the point of view of science educators and of educational linguists. Contexts where English is a foreign language, such as Hong Kong, have been less studied, yet their students’ linguistic difficulties are often even greater. This study intends to videotape two sequences of the junior secondary science curriculum as taught by three teachers, each from a different school. Further data will be gathered through interviews with teachers and students, and from student questionnaires. The sequences will be analyzed at a macro level using a framework from science education to establish the stages involved in the movement between commonsense knowledge and school science understandings. This analysis will be combined with interview and questionnaire data to identify and explore areas of learning and of difficulty in the sequences. The sequences will be further analyzed for use of language which SFL has identified as facilitating the development of understanding. Tools from SFL will also explicate strategies discussed in science education. The analysis will reveal, for example, the language used by teachers to move from the specific example to the general rule, to lead students through logical reasoning and co-construct knowledge, and to move between the dense nominal groups (noun phrases) of science knowledge and the linked clauses of everyday language. This work has practical and also academic significance. On a practical level, knowledge of the language used at particular points of tension and of learning can inform teacher education. In academic terms, the research adds an understanding of language use in foreign-language English to the body of knowledge on first language English and English as a second language. Furthermore, analysis combining the science education framework and strategies with tools from SFL adds to the understanding of both fields, and provides a detailed example of how each can extend the range and investigatory powers of the other.

24400714.label: Realisation of objectives
24400714.value: The project objectives have been realised through collection and analysis of data, plus consideration of previous research. Data collection Data were collected which would allow the researchers to examine the teachers’ classroom language (objectives 1-4), and also enable the identification of student difficulties (objective 4). Data collection was as follows (‘how objectives have been achieved’). The data were collected from the secondary one EMI science classes of three schools, with one secondary two class from an additional school as pilot and as backup. Two topics per school were observed using the same topics in each school, except where variations in the syllabus or teacher’s schedule made differences unavoidable. Seventeen lessons of 40-80 minutes each were videorecorded and transcribed, and materials used were collected. Questionnaires were administered to the students, with questions on, for example, what they found most difficult about the lesson; these issues were further probed in interviews with subgroups of students. The interviews with students were carried out in Cantonese; the questionnaire for students was bilingual in Chinese and English, and contained both open and closed questions. Pre- and post-lesson interviews with the teachers were semi-structured; questions focused on sources of difficulty, effects of teaching through L2 English and attainment or otherwise of their objectives. In addition, the relevant textbook materials were analysed for purpose, content, genre and language, and compared with the teachers’ purposes. Data collection (‘to what extent project objectives have been achieved’) The data collected matched the expectations as laid out in the project proposal, and were sufficient to address the objectives as intended. Since the analysis of lessons and materials is in-depth, manual, and therefore necessarily time-consuming, the number of lessons that can be analysed is limited. Therefore, and as usual with this type of research, caution needs to be exercised when making any claims for the representative nature of the data. Data analysis Teaching purposes (objective 1) were identified using the Mortimer and Scott (2003) framework as described in the project proposal plus understandings of discourse purpose from the genre work within systemic functional linguistics, also as stated in the proposal. Tools from systemic functional linguistics, particularly genre analysis and also nominal group analysis, were used to analyse • Language resources not/used by the teacher (objective 1) • The movement between everyday and scientific understanding (objective 2) • The use of dialogue in order to construct and co-construct school science (objective 3) For objective 4, areas of difficulty in the lessons were first identified from a) explicit comments by the teacher and/or students either in the lesson itself or in the questionnaires or interviews, and/or b) difficulty implied from student answers in the lesson. The episodes containing these difficulties were then analysed for: • Focus (Content and teaching purpose), Approach and Action (Patterns of discourse and Teacher interventions), following Mortimer and Scott (2003). • These concepts were further operationalized through a consideration of o SFL understandings of genre (purpose, staging, linguistic features) o The realization in language of register differences (everyday-scientific), e.g. through nominalisations and embedding in nominal groups (Halliday & Matthiessen, 2013, p. 492) o Use of L1, and how that interacted with other areas, particularly register The analysis enabled the realization of the objectives 1-4 (‘how’). Data analysis (‘To what extent’) The analytic tools from SFL were particularly effective in revealing the movement between everyday and scientific understanding (objective 2) where this occurred (and see Findings in 6.1 below). Similarly, SFL genre analysis was effective in capturing the difference between more and less successful language resources used by teachers to co-construct school science in dialogue with students (objectives 3 and 4). All of these examples also relate to objective 1 (language resources). Objective 5, comparison with previous research into classroom discourse and secondary science. (‘How project objectives have been achieved’) Previous work consulted included Hong Kong-based studies of EMI science classes (e.g. Lin and Wu 2015; Lo 2015; Ng 2007), work on bilingual education more widely (e.g. Bruna, Vann and Perales Escudero 2007; Llinares, Morton and Whittaker 2012; Mohan and Slater 2006). Once it became clear that ‘language resources’ (the focus of the objectives) included use of L1 Cantonese, then the body of work considering translanguaging in bilingual education, and also use of mother tongue in ELT more generally, was also consulted (e.g. Garcia and Wei 2014; Gierlinger 2015; Hall and Cook 2012; Lin and Lo 2017). Objective 5 (‘To what extent project objectives have been achieved’) A wide range of relevant research was involved, sufficient to realise the objective. References Bruna, K. R., R. Vann and M. 24400714.label: Major findings and research outcome
24400714.value: Major findings include: a. Explanation causes most difficulty for co-construction. When attempting to co-construct the scientific explanation, teachers often either ask questions at genre level or within the transitivity structure (at word level). The first is too demanding for most students, and the second can result in superficial engagement. (The midway option would be to scaffold students in the stages of the explanation.) Reported on in Maxwell-Reid (2015) (Part C). b. Coursebooks can lead teachers into genre confusion and unnecessary difficulty for students. For example, a teacher may wish to explain the workings of a device, but the coursebook provides a procedure (how to set up the device) and a description, but not an explanation. The teacher ends up switching back and forth between the various genres, rather than working through the explanation systematically. Maxwell-Reid and Lau (under review) (Part C) details this confusion and difficulty for a lesson on the motor-generator. c. Teacher modelling of the relationship between everyday and scientific knowledge. Some sequences reveal greater facility than others, with teachers building up technicality through increasing use of nominal group expansion, moving up and down the cine of technicality to clarify the meaning, and the construction of meaning, to students. At times this is very skillfully done; at other times less so. Reported on in Maxwell-Reid (accepted), and Maxwell-Reid and Lau (under review) (Part C). d. Teachers make very varied use of L1 Cantonese. More positive uses include the teacher’s translation of a word that is causing difficulty, or the checking of student understanding with a request that they translate a word. Such uses could support the development of the students’ scientific knowledge in English. More questionable uses saw the whole message delivered in Cantonese. In these cases, the scientific knowledge was not always modelled in English. Furthermore, the relationship of the technical with the everyday knowledge was not always highlighted. Reported on in Maxwell-Reid (accepted). e. Even where teachers modelled the build up of technicality, they did not generally provide students with opportunities to make this knowledge and language their own through practice (Maxwell-Reid accepted). f. Teachers and students explicitly focus on vocabulary as a source of difficulty, and are less aware of other difficulties that emerged (Maxwell-Reid accepted).

24400714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24400714.value: There are several potential areas for development. The area that currently interests me the most is the difference between the language demands of studying secondary science through English and the secondary English syllabus. The findings from the project (e.g. the build up of technicality) reveal some quite specific and demanding language requirements that are not found explicitly in the English syllabus. My plan for my next GRF proposal is a comparative review of secondary science materials and secondary English materials. This review would use similar tools from systemic functional linguistics as used in this ECS project, for example analyzing for genre and for nominal group expansion. My hypothesis is that students are facing greater linguistic challenges in their science classes than in their English classes. If this was found to be the case, it would suggest a need to revise the English syllabus and/or materials used.

24400714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24400714.value: This research project investigated the classroom discourse of English Medium of Instruction (EMI) junior secondary science. It is of value because of its focus, its methodology and its findings. More secondary schools are now using EMI for junior science, and concern has been expressed at the challenges involved. This research benefits from dual perspectives on these challenges. On the one hand it uses a framework from science education to analyse the content, purpose and interactions of the lessons. On the other hand tools from systemic functional linguistics (SFL) are able to detail the language used to carry out these teaching purposes. The findings from this combined approach are of significance in both research and practical terms, and contribute to the current disciplinary conversation on how best to integrate content and language learning (CLIL). For example, developments in our understanding of how the mother tongue is used in EMI classes (see 6.1) were described by a reviewer of Maxwell-Reid (accepted) as “exceedingly interesting and important”; these developments have implications for educational policy. The detailed descriptions of, for example, the build up of technicality and of co-constructed explanations, also provide respectively positive and negative models for use in EMI teacher education.

24400814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24400814.value: The issue of disability is a global one. It is estimated that one billion people in the world have disabilities and 80% of them live in low to middle income countries. ‘Tackling disability’ is a strategy to ensure the enforcement of human rights and eradicate extreme poverty among those so afflicted. The overall project objective is to close the global knowledge gap of people with disabilities in the field of education, focusing on access. It is aimed that the accumulated knowledge can stimulate the global discussion on the Post 2015 agenda and improve the methodological framework of global initiatives such as Out-Of-School-Children (OOSC). The knowledge gap exists due to mainly a lack of data. The UN’s Washington City Group on Disability Statistics developed a recommended set of disability questions based on the criteria seen in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health, but their recommendations are yet to be mainstreamed. The preparation analysis for this project identified that there are nine national sampling surveys that have been conducted in the last decade which used the recommended set of disability questions. This project uses these data sets to fill the major knowledge gap by quantifying the proportions of, and developing complex profiles of OOSC with disabilities, and conducting econometric analyses on the determinants of schooling, as well as return of education among children with disabilities, drawing on established templates for this kind of study. The resolution of the High-Level Meeting of the United Nations General Assembly on Disability on September 23rd in 2013 states that improvement of disability data analysis and monitoring is key for the realization of the rights of people with disabilities. Academic and development communities need to meet the demand for internationally comparable data and statistics. This project is the first attempt to carry out an international comparison on the educational situation of children with disabilities using global standards in measuring disabilities. The generated knowledge will not only improve scholarly understanding of the education for children with disabilities but also provide recommendations and critical reflections to improve existing global efforts to achieve Education for All goals. The findings will be shared with international organizations such as UNICEF, UNESCO and the World Bank, and national stakeholders of the studied countries to improve the understanding of the situation of children with disabilities and to perfect education policy for them. 殘疾問題是全球性的。據估計，在全球有十億殘疾人士，而當中80％生活在中低收入國家。「殘疾應對」是一種確保人權執法和杜絕極端貧困的必要策略。此項目的整體目標是要去除在教育領域上對殘疾人士的全球性知識差距。此項目亦有助積累知識以刺激對後2015年議程的全球性討論，並改善如Out-Of -School-Children（OOSC）的方法框架。 知識差距存在的原因主要是缺乏數據。聯合國駐華盛頓市殘疾統計小組開發並推薦一系列建基於功能，殘疾和健康問題的國際分類標準的問卷，但尚未成為主流。在過去十年間，有九個全國性抽樣調查使用了此問卷。本項目將採用這些數據，通過量化殘疾人士比例、建設OOSC複雜的數據庫、對學校教育的判定因素及教育對殘疾兒童的回報進行計量性分析， 建立相關研究的模板以填補重大的知識差距。 在2013年9月23日的聯合國關於殘疾與發展問題的大會高級別會議的決議指出，提高殘疾數據的分析和監測是實現殘疾人權利是關鍵。學術和發展中國家需要研發一套可供國際比較的數據和統計數據。本項目是第一個以國際標準衡量殘疾兒童的教育狀況的比較研究。此項目不僅會提高了學術層面對殘疾兒童的教育理解，同時也會批判及建議改善目前狀況，致力協助全球達成「全民教育」目標。研究結果將與國際組織，如聯合國兒童基金會、聯合國教科文組織和世界銀行，以及被研究國家的利益相關者共享，以提高對殘疾兒童情況的了解和完善為他們策劃的教育政策。

24400814.label: Major findings and research outcome
24400814.value: The paper aims to reduce the global knowledge gap pertaining to the impact of disability on school attendance, using cross-nationally comparable and nationally representative data from 18 surveys in 15 countries that are selected among 2,500 surveys and censuses.T hese selected surveys administered the Washington Group Short Set (WGSS) of disability-screening questions, covering five functional domains of seeing, hearing, mobility, self-care, and remembering, and collected information on educational status. Using both descriptive and econometric approaches, the paper finds that (i) the average disability gap in school attendance stands at 30% in primary and secondary schools in 15 countries; (ii) more than 85% of disabled primary-age children who are out of school have never attended school; (iii) the average marginal effect of disability on primary and secondary school attendance is negative and significant (-30%), and (iv) countries that have reached close to universal primary education report high ratios of disabled to non-disabled out-of-school children indicating that general education policies to improve access do not effectively mainstream disabled children in education, and (v) disabled children confront the same difficulties in participating in education, regardless of their individual and socio-economic characteristics.

24401014.label: Project Objectives
24401014.value: To provide detailed, cogent, and historically-grounded analyses and interpretations of Prokofiev’s last four operas. To demonstrate links between Prokofiev’s opera and with their immediate Stalinist contexts, including related practices in Soviet novel, theatre, and film. To outline the core elements of Prokofiev’s operatic style and its later development, and assess of the composer’s aesthetic position in terms of his relationship to the common-practice tradition and to modernism. To assess a comprehensive amount of relevant sources, including the original manuscripts of the operas, other primary sources documents, and recent work in related disciplines. To combine methodologies and synthesise my findings, thereby shedding light on the operas from different angles. To build on and contribute to music analytical work on Prokofiev’s music, and to develop new techniques that take the specifics of operatic styles, forms, and drama into account.

24401014.label: Realisation of objectives
24401014.value: By travelling to archives in Moscow, St. Petersburg, and New York, I was able to collect the last of the primary source materials that I needed to complete the research for the monograph. These include, for example, the manuscript score for Prokofiev's opera Betrothal in a Monastery, with the composer's revisions for production in 1943. This is an important discovery which will enhance my discussion of the opera considerably, and essentially solve a mystery about this aspect of the work's genesis. Other finds include official documents revealing the views of members of the arts administration about another opera, Semyon Kotko, as well as manuscript scores of other works from Prokofiev's Soviet period. The evidence of these sources will add to the arguments I have developed about Prokofiev's interactions with Soviet culture and with the regime's demands as revealed through his late operas. Many of the points I make draw on recent scholarship in the field of Soviet history. I also demonstrate how Prokofiev's operas relate to literature, the theatre, and the cinema in both their creation and reception. Much of the discussion in the book involves accounting for Prokofiev's stylistic tendencies in opera and providing a critical assessment of how these are manifested in different ways in the four operas. Overall my goal has been to weave together the cultural and historical background of these works with an original account of their unique characteristics, and I believe this has been achieved satisfactorily.

24401014.label: Major findings and research outcome
24401014.value: I have submitted the entire manuscript to Cambridge University Press in December 2016. My major findings include new readings of the operas' genres and stylistic features; new discoveries about their genesis, including revisions and the all-important exchanges between the composer and representatives of the administration which had an influence on their final versions; and new insights into the ways in which the operas related to their historical contexts. Along the way I enrich my discussion with references to recent work in other fields.

24401014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24401014.value: Since Prokofiev has been excluded from the scholarly canon for so long, there is more work to be done on his Soviet period, and on his earlier career as well. Additionally, further studies of other Soviet operas would be welcome, and this is something I may wish to pursue in the future. At present, my research involves several smaller projects on Prokofiev's instrumental works from earlier and later periods.

24401014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24401014.value: This is the first in-depth study of Sergey Prokofiev's last four operas, which he composed after returning to the Soviet Union in 1936. In four chapters - one on each of the operas - I examine the unique features of each work and make original observations about their form, style, etc., as well as the messages or meanings that they contain, while at the same time I demonstrate the ways in which the various historical and cultural contexts that surrounded them (pre-war to post-war, novel to film) related to their significance, their purpose, and their function in Stalinist society.

24401314.label: Realisation of objectives
24401314.value: The three objectives were fully realized by carrying out 7 experiments. Objective 1, 2, and 3 was addressed by experiment 1-4, 5 and 6, and 1-7, respectively. Experiment 1 (Xiao et al., under review) investigated the Inferior Frontal Cortex, (IFC) and Superior Temporal Cortex (STC) network in detecting changes of feature conjunction in the auditory modality with event-related optical signal (EROS). A feature conjunction rule “the higher the frequency of a tone, the stronger the intensity” established by standards was violated by deviants of 12 deviance levels. When deviants were preceded by a short train of standards, early IFC, STC, and late IFC EROS mismatch responses were found for the larger deviants but not for the smaller deviants and demonstrated linear relationships with the deviance levels. When deviants were preceded by a longer train of standards, the STC but not the early or late IFC EROS mismatch responses were elicited by all the deviants without modulation by deviance levels. Experiment 2 (Xiao et al., 2018) investigated whether the human brain could extract patterns with different levels of abstractness from the auditory events. Tone triplets with varying pitch (first-order property) served as the auditory events. The pitch intervals (interval 1 and interval 2) between the tones in a triplet and the ratio of intervals 1 and 2 were considered second- and third-order properties, respectively. Both second- and third-order properties of the standards were kept constant in the mixed patterns block, while only the third-order property was kept constant in the ratio pattern block. Four sets of tone triplets violating the interval and ratio patterns with different deviance levels were presented as deviants in both blocks, and subtracted with physically identical stimuli in a control block to isolate the mismatch negativity (MMNs). Interval and ratio pattern deviants elicited MMNs in the mixed patterns block while only ratio pattern deviants elicited MMNs in the ratio pattern block. Larger MMNs were elicited by large deviants as compared to small deviants. Experiment 3 (Tse et al., in submission; Zhao K. Y. PhD thesis) investigated whether the human brain could extract the regularity underlying the presentation of emotion and consonant vowels (CV) of speech stimuli, and how the autism-related low empathizing and high systemizing cognitive styles (indexed by a high discrepancy or D-score) modulate this process. Empathizing and systemizing which specify how a cognitive system handles others’ emotions and tackles regularities. Mismatch brain responses elicited by emotion (angry and happy) and non-emotion (speech and pitch) deviants were compared between the high and low D-score groups. The low D-score group showed emotion related lateralized mismatch response to emotion deviants, a physical change related centralized mismatch response to the pitch deviant, while no mismatch response was found for the speech deviant. The high D-score group showed centralized, but not lateralized, mismatch responses to all four deviants. Model fitting analysis showed that individual differences in the mismatch responses model with D-score as predictor best explained the deviants, but not for models with either empathizing or systemizing, or both as the predictors. The second part of this experiment further investigated how variations in the regularity structure of the sequence modulated mismatch responses for angry versus speech deviants in the two D-score groups. With reduced variation, the low D-score group showed a shift of the mismatch responses from a lateralized to a centralized distribution for the angry deviants and recovered the centralized mismatch responses to the speech deviant. The high D-score group consistently revealed a centralized mismatch response for both angry and speech deviants independent of the variation levels. Experiment 4 (Tse et al., 2018) examined the causal functional connectivity of the frontal and temporal cortices. Current theories postulate that before the STC detects a change, the IFC engages in stimulus analysis, which is particularly critical for ambiguous deviations (e.g., deviant preceded by a short train of standards). These theories rest on the assumption that IFC and STC are functionally connected, which has only been supported by correlational brain imaging studies. We examined this functional connectivity assumption by applying Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) to disrupt IFC function, while measuring the later STC mismatch response with EROS. Due to its optical nature, EROS is inert to the electromagnetic energy produced by TMS. Specifically, the STC mismatch response at 120-180ms elicited by a deviant preceded by a short standard train when IFC TMS was applied at 80ms was compared with the STC mismatch responses in temporal control (TMS with 200ms delay), spatial control (sham TMS at vertex), auditory control (TMS pulse noise only), and cognitive control (deviant preceded by a long standard train) conditions. The STC mismatch response to deviants preceded by the short train was abolished by TMS of the IFC at 80 ms, while the STC responses remained intact in all other control conditions. Experiment 5 (in preparation for journal submission) studied the frontal-occipital network in pre-attentive detection of physical versus abstract pattern changes in the visual modality. In the physical change condition, bar arrays with constant orientation were presented as the standards while bar arrays with a different orientation were presented as the deviants. In the abstract change condition, the orientation of the standard bar arrays changed from one standard to another standard with +32.7 degrees. The deviant bar arrays were bar arrays reversing the standard rotation pattern (-32.7 x 2 degrees). The results showed EROS mismatch response in the occipital but not in the frontal cortex for the oddball condition. However, for the rotating oddball condition, a frontal–occipital–frontal mismatch response pattern was found. Experiment 6 (Zeng Q. H. PhD thesis; in preparation for journal submission) examined whether the violation of abstract regularity in the form of cultural pictures can be detected in the visual modality. The cultural information was presented in stimuli consisting of one Eastern or Western picture. The visual MMNs (vMMNs) elicited by Eastern and Western deviants between the Hong Kong Chinese, Mainland Chinese, and Westerners with high and low racial essentialism were compared. Racial essentialism is a measure of sensitivity to racial differences. The results demonstrated differences in vMMNs to the Eastern and Western deviants were observed in the 3 samples and modulated by racial essentialism. Experiment 7 (Wang et al., under review) investigated if other types of mismatch signals, the feedback-related negativity (FRN) and mid-frontal theta and beta oscillations, would respond differently during the outcome evaluations of conformity decisions, which were consistent with self vs. others’ opinions. Participants first performed a perceptual judgment task, then saw the majority opinion prior to submitting their final decision, and subsequently learned whether their final decision was correct. With incongruent initial self and others’ opinions, the incorrect feedback to a non-conform (no-change) final decision elicited larger FRN while the incorrect feedback to a conform (change) decision elicited larger theta power, compared to their respective correct decisions. In addition, beta power was larger in the correct than incorrect conform decision. FRN and theta power, but not beta power, were associated with subsequent conformity behavior. The FRN and theta signals therefore demonstrated differential sensitivity to the source of information that drove a conformity decision. These results suggest the prediction violation mechanism also takes place in decision making.

24401314.label: Major findings and research outcome
24401314.value: Experiment 1, 2, and 3 demonstrated that human brain can detect violations of abstract regularities established by physical features, feature conjunctions, emotions, and speeches in the auditory modality. Experiment 1 (Xiao et al., under review) demonstrated a predictive role of the IFC in the abstract change detection when insufficient rule-conforming information could be extracted from the preceding standards and is consistent with the predictive violation account of pre-attentive change detection. Experiment 2 (Xiao et al., 2018, published in Psychophysiology) suggests that the change detection system is sensitive to the violation of both second- and third-order abstract patterns. In addition to regularities in the abstract properties of auditory events, regularities in the relationships between abstract properties can also be extracted. Experiment 3 (Tse et al., in submission; Zhao K. Y. PhD thesis) showed that the pre-attentive detection system is sensitive to higher level properties (e.g., emotion and speech) composed of lower level physical features and the mismatch responses are modulated by the general tendency of the cognitive system in processing information. Experiment 4 (Tse et al., 2018, published in Neuroimage) further demonstrated a causal functional connection between IFC and STC with an innovative combination of brain stimulation and imaging technique. Experiment 5 and 6 demonstrated our brain can detect both physical and abstract changes in the visual modality. Experiment 5 (Shum et al., in preparation) demonstrated the frontal cortex involvement in abstract pattern changes in the visual modality. Combined with the findings in the auditory modality above, a general frontal-sensory-frontal brain network in detecting changes in the visual and auditory modalities is proposed. Experiment 6 (Zeng Q. H. PhD thesis; Zeng et al., in preparation) demonstrates spontaneous categorization of the cultural symbols into the respective cultures. It also highlights the importance of long-term experience in pre-attentive change detection process and the importance of psychological essentialism in the social perception from a cognitive neuroscience perspective. Experiment 7 (Wang et al., under review) suggests the prediction violation mechanism can also take place in decision making. This project demonstrated mismatch responses to abstract changes in both the auditory and visual modalities. More importantly, this project established a general frontal-sensory cortex network in pre-attentive change detection in different sensory modalities. The frontal-temporal-frontal and frontal-occipital-frontal networks in pre-attentive abstract change detections of auditory and visual stimuli are consistent with the predictive coding framework which assumes both top-down and bottom-up mechanisms in the change detection processes.

24401314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24401314.value: The current project has established the spatiotemporal dynamics of the frontal-sensory network in the pre-attentive detection of both physical and abstract changes. In addition, the current project demonstrated a new methodology for examining the causal functional connectivity of a brain network in studying human cognition by the concurrent application of TMS and EROS. A new research area can focus on how to apply this method in understanding human cognition from the network perspective. The spatiotemporal dynamics of the frontal-sensory-frontal network are consistent with the predictive coding hypothesis. The predictive nature of the frontal cortex suggested by this hypothesis is regarded as the fundamental principle in human cognition. Further studies can focus on the prediction related functional role of the frontal cortex in the backward and forward circuits. The findings of the current project demonstrated individual differences in the sensitivities of the pre-attentive change detection system. In addition, as the passive oddball paradigm used in pre-attentive change detection does not require participant to engage in an active task, the mismatch brain response elicited in pre-attentive change detection can potentially be used as biomarker in some clinical populations.

24401314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24401314.value: The human brain is capable of monitoring signals in the environment (e.g., traffic noise) and making predictions of future events without focus of attention. When this automatic system detects a salient change out of expectation (e.g., screech of car tires), the brain will orient attention to the change, and carry out remedial action if required (e.g., jump out of the way). This pre-attentive change detection process reflects a predictive nature of human brain which is a fundamental principle in human cognition. The findings from this project demonstrated that the human brain is not only sensitive to simple physical changes in the environment, but also to complicated abstract changes, such as emotional speech and cultural information. A general frontal-sensory-frontal brain network supporting a predictive mechanism was shown in both the auditory and visual modalities. The sensitivity of the change detection system is modulated by the general processing style of the individuals. These findings allow us to understand human cognition from the predictive brain perspective and suggest the possibility in using the mismatch brain signals elicited in pre-attentive change detection as biomarkers for individual differences.

24401814.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24401814.value: 邁向成功老齡化之路：人生歷程、世代差異、以及當地情境

24401814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24401814.value: Promoting successful aging is a priority for China, which has the largest elderly population in the world. The proposed study aims to assess multidimensional aspects of successful aging of Chinese older adults and to identify factors related to successful aging by using a life-course ecological model. Three years of funding are requested to address four specific aims: (1) To assess and compare multidimensional aspects of successful aging of Chinese older adults across various subgroups (e.g. gender, rural/urban residence, and cohort); (2) To determine life-course factors and local contextual factors associated with successful aging; (3) To investigate how the effects of these factors interact with gender, rural/urban residence, and cohort membership; and (4) To identify implications for policy-makers and social service professionals tasked with designing and implementing policies and programs that promote successful aging in China. To address these goals, a cross-sectional survey will be conducted of 1,800 Chinese older adults (age 60 and over) living in 40 neighborhoods in central coastal Shanghai and the southwestern province of Guangxi. Data will be obtained through face-to-face interviews based on a structured questionnaire. The questionnaire will assess retrospective life-history information, which is rarely available in existing public datasets on older Chinese persons, as well as multidimensional aspects of successful aging (including physical health status, mental health status, and social engagement), socio-demographic information, and local neighborhood contextual information. This systematic examination of multidimensional aspects of successful aging of Chinese older adults will add substantially to existing evidence from western countries and will enable future cross-national comparisons. In addition, by using a life-course ecological model to study successful aging, we will expand successful aging research beyond the current focus on micro-level, individual contemporary characteristics and attainments to early-life/later-life and micro-macro linkages in aging well. An enhanced understanding of the major factors involved in successful aging could enable the development of interventions and policies that promote aging successfully in China. 促進老年人的成功老齡化對於中國這樣一個擁有世界上最多老年人口的國家而言是一個緊要的議題。本研究致力於考量中國老年人成功老齡化的多維度指標以及運用人生歷程的生態學模型來鑒別影響成功老齡化的因素。此項為期三年的研究將完成四個具體的研究目的：（1）考量和比較不同組別（男女、城鄉、和世代）老年人的成功老齡化的多維度指標；（2）鑒別影響成功老齡化的人生歷程和當地情境因素；（3）探索這些因素如何與性別、城鄉、和世代差異相互作用；（4）為設計和推動促進中國老年人成功老齡化的政策和服務提供建議。 此項研究計畫將在上海和廣西兩地收集1800個老年人的資料。資料的收集將採用面對面的問卷調查。問卷將包括個人背景資訊、健康資訊、社會交往資訊、人生歷程資訊、以及居住社區的情境資訊。 此項系統的研究中國老年人的成功老齡化的项目將補充現有的以西方國家為主的成功老齡化研究，並為將來的跨文化比較提供文獻。除此之外，運用聯繫早期人生經歷和老年生活，聯合微觀和宏觀層面的人生歷程的生態學模型來研究成功老齡化，將拓展現有的以個人微觀層面為主的研究。這項研究將提高我們對影響成功老齡化的因素的認識，以此將有助於發展有效的促進成功老齡化的政策和服務。

24500214.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24500214.value: 消费者基于团购的购买与推荐行为研究

24500214.label: Project Objectives
24500214.value: To empirically investigate the effects of the group buying features of the social coupon website. We aim to develop three hypotheses about how the group buying features affect consumer behavior and whether the current change of de-emphasizing the features is beneficial to the company or not. The three hypothesis include 1) Based on theoretical predictions, group buying features will stimulate deal referrals; 2) The design of tipping point will facilitate deal sales; 3) The information of prior purchases will increase purchase likelihood through the mechanism of herding rather than social learning. To carry out the analysis, we will develop a procedure for cleaning and analyzing Groupon’s clickstream data. We aim to generate three sets of data to store the behavior, deal and consumer information, respectively. To develop an empirical analysis for examining the behavior of newly registered customers on social coupon website under two customer acquisition strategies. The two strategies are 1) at the macro level, initiating a national advertising campaign; 2) at the micro level, encouraging existing customers to refer new customers by double the reward. We aim to quantify the different effects of the two strategies on consumer behavior and investigate moderators to those effects. To develop a structural model to study consumers’ sequential choices of products from different categories when uncertainty prevails and information is costly. We aim to apply the model to the social coupon context and estimate the individual “reservation value for deals” based on the search theory, taking into account the effects of deal characteristics, social influence and individual demographic information. To conduct policy simulations based on the model and parameter estimates to offer insights into customer segmentation and promotion strategies that will allow firms to offer social coupons more effectively.

24500214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500214.value: Social coupons that combine the features of daily deals and group buying have become an important marketing strategy (Kumar & Rajan, 2012). By 2011, over 50 million Americans had signed up with social coupon vendors such as Groupon and LivingSocial, and the annual revenue of the social coupon sector had reached $1 billion (Washington Post, 2011). With over 80 social coupon websites operating in Hong Kong, the industry is estimated to generate revenues of $60-70 million each year (Li, 2012). To the best of our knowledge, this study will be the first to empirically investigate social coupon-related consumer behavior based on detailed consumer-level data. We will consider two questions: (1) how consumers choose deals to purchase and (2) how consumers recommend deals to others. The purchase of daily deals involves making sequential decisions on different product categories, an aspect that has not yet been examined in the marketing literature. We aim to build a structural model based on the search theory (McCall, 1970), and to derive an optimal decision process using the “reservation value for deals” construct to explain the deal purchase behavior of consumers. This “reservation value” will be identified and estimated based on the information of received deals and purchasing histories. Second, we will seek to understand the social aspect of coupon purchasing. Social coupon vendors use the special mechanism of the “assurance contract” (Brubaker, 1975) to motivate consumers to act as sales agents and thereby ensure that their purchased deals are eligible for redemption (Jing & Xie, 2011). However, consumers risk their reputations if the deals they refer are not widely considered good. This study will empirically address whether and how this arrangement affects consumer deal recommendation behavior. To answer these questions, we have obtained access to a large proprietary dataset that features the complete clicking paths within a browser session of over 186,000 consumers in the U.S. who logged on to the Groupon website between January and March 2011. This study will contribute to the online marketing literature in general and to the social coupon industry in particular, especially for regions such as Hong Kong that are experiencing rapid Internet business growth. Our empirical analysis will help firms better understand consumer purchases and social coupon referrals. This knowledge will assist companies to develop more effective online social communication practices and better targeted couponing strategies.

24500214.label: Realisation of objectives
24500214.value: The project was completed and all objectives have been accomplished.In Hu and Winer (2017), we studied the group buying feature of social coupons. It was the first study to empirically investigate social coupon-related consumer behavior based on detailed consumer-level data. Their findings are as follows: (1) contrary to their theoretical predictions, group buying does not stimulate referrals, no matter whether the deal is tipped (enough people have purchased the deal before it kicks in) or not; however, (2) the information from the deal that is tipped increases deal purchase probability by removing a consumer’s uncertainty about whether the deal will eventually tip and it accelerates deal purchase speed; and (3) the information from prior purchases affects an individual’s purchase decision through the mechanism of herding rather than social learning. These findings together suggest that the group buying features of social coupons change consumer behavior and affect sales. This study also provides an example of using web analytics tools to augment clickstream data and consolidate information from other sources. Hu, Zhao and King (working paper) proposed a recommendation system for sequential decision-making scenarios in which choices are time sensitive (will expire in a short time) and made sequentially available and the quality of future choices is uncertain, for example, recommendations on daily deal websites. The proposed recommendation system is grounded in the search literature of Economics and we develop a new machine learning algorithm to solve the search model. In particular, we leverage the means of Semi-parametric Gaussian copula (SGC) to generate a complex joint distribution among variables including individual characteristics, choice features, sequential temporal factor and purchase decisions. Recommendations are made based on the purchase likelihood of each available deal on a specific day for an individual calculated by the conditional posterior of the joint distribution. The authors apply the model to a proprietary dataset from Groupon customers' clickstream data and demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed approach by comparing it to other traditional or sequential based recommendation algorithms, including collaborative filtering methods and multi-armed bandit models. The system facilitates companies' efforts to target the right customers with the right product at the right time. In Hu, Dang and Chintagunta (working paper), we study purchase behavior of daily deals with individual clickstream data on browsing sessions of consumers who newly subscribe to Groupon between January and March 2011. The data reveal two patterns. First, the probability of a consumer clicking on a merchant in the emailed newsletter declines over time which appears to be consistent with consumer ``fatigue". Second, the probability that the consumer makes a purchase conditional on clicking increases over time, which seems contrary to the notion of ``fatigue". To reconcile the two observations, in this paper we propose a model that rationalizes these patterns and then provide insights for companies in the daily deal industry. When consumers first subscribe to a daily deal site, they are unlikely to be fully informed about the quality of the deals offered on the site. The daily newsletter provides price and some limited information about that day's featured deals. To learn more about quality, consumers need to click on the newsletter, go to the deal's website and invest time and effort to learn about quality. Such a search for information is costly and only provides a noisy signal of quality to consumers. Further, consumers do not know the future deals they may receive. Given the uncertainty about quality and the cost of searching, consumers are more likely to search early on (i.e., click on the newsletter). As they learn about deal quality, they need to search less; resulting in clicks declining over time. As learning accumulates, consumers are better at recognizing deals of higher quality to click on and they are more likely to click in order to purchase rather than to learn about quality. This results in an increase in the conditional probability of purchasing. We formulate a dynamic model of search and Dirichlet learning based on the above characterization of consumer behavior. We show that the model is able to replicate the patterns in the data. Next, we estimate the parameters of the model and provide managerial insights to daily deal websites based on our findings and policy simulations.

24500214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24500214.value: In China, there are similar websites as Groupon, such as Meituan. One possible extension is to compare the consumer behavior under the similar business model in different cultures. To explore this direction, we first need to collect individual level behavior data from the Chinese websites. Then we can apply the models we developed in this project to the data and compare the differences.

24500214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24500214.value: Groupon pioneered a new business model which combines the features of daily deals and group buying. This so-called social coupon and daily deal industry has experienced explosive growth in recent years. Consumers exhibit unique behavior patterns in such context. The series of research in this project help the websites as well as retailers using the website to better understand their customers. The project also demonstrate the great value of clickstream data in the combination of advanced business analytics tools and economic models to facilitate marketing activities.
