24500314.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24500314.value: 服务系统中的渐近机制:一个经验分析框架及一个理论问题

24500314.label: Project Objectives
24500314.value: Develop a statistical model to test the goodness-of-fit of universal approximation with data Develop a framework to identify operational regimes in data, which will be a bridge connecting existing theory with practice Determine staffing levels for time-varying systems, so that performance measures such as the proportion of customers who have to wait upon arrival can be stabilized
rows: Develop a statistical model to test the goodness-of-fit of universal approximation with data
Develop a framework to identify operational regimes in data, which will be a bridge connecting existing theory with practice

24500314.label: Realisation of objectives
24500314.value: All the three objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. In paper #1 (see Section 8 of the report), we build a unified framework to establishing diffusion approximations for critically-loaded service systems with impatient customers. We provide a general approach to incorporating different customer patience-time distributions and apply it to several systems that have different number of servers. In paper #2, we develop new universal approximations that are universal in both operational regimes and patience-time distributions. The general patience-time distributions in the model allow us to fit performance measures of many service systems. As discussed in the paper (see the figures there), we figure out that the third moment of the service time distribution is the determining factor on the goodness of fit of the universal approximations for performance measures of service systems. In this way, Objective 1 is addressed. Though not reported in Paper #1, we identify service systems that are critically loaded, collect the corresponding datasets, and fit the data with our Theorem 1. That verifies our Theorem 1 in practice (though it is universal in the number of servers, our Theorem 1 holds only in critically loaded systems). In paper #3, we collect data from a call center and identify its operational regime (efficiency-driven regime). In this setting, identifying the overloaded operational regime is a key factor, and that regime plays an essential role for the success of that paper. Together with some interesting observations of customer behaviours, we build theory to manage delay announcements in call centers. The theory is motivated by data from real systems and is then applied to make staffing decisions for those service systems, hence it has strong connection to practice. These ensure that Objective 2 is successfully addressed. Though not reported in the paper, Theorem 1 in paper #1 can also be applied to time-varying settings. In Paper #2, we consider transit performance measures of service systems as well and propose the corresponding universal approximations. Our numerical analyses give us strong confidence to claim that universal approximations are very accurate for approximating those transit performance measures. The capacity-design (corresponding to staffing) problems are also addressed in that paper, both statically and dynamically. One of the conclusions is that universal approximations are indeed accurate and helpful for making capacity decisions. Because the results are applicable to different operational regimes, they are insensitive to the change of arrival rates, and the related capacity decisions can be used to manage time-varying systems. As a result, Objective 3 is successfully addressed.

24500314.label: Major findings and research outcome
24500314.value: This project has contributed significantly to both theory and applications. We advance the theory of universal approximations to incorporate various patience-time distributions. Together with the universality in operational regimes, the newly developed universality in patience-time distributions ensure that the universal approximations can be applied to more general service systems and fit data from service systems better. The development of the new universal approximations and detailed investigations figure out the essential factor that determines the goodness of fit of the universal approximations to performance measures of service systems. We also solve the capacity design problem, both statically and dynamically, and establish the related universal results. Because the results are applicable to different operational regimes, they are insensitive to the change of arrival rates, and the related capacity decisions can be used to manage time-varying systems. These findings are reported in Operations Research (paper #2). Though universal approximations are useful for many systems, it is also important to identify the operational regimes. In an earlier work, we build a unified framework to establishing diffusion approximations for critically-loaded service systems with impatient customers. That general approach is independent of both the number of servers and customer patience-time distributions. We apply the approach to establishing approximations for performance measures in three systems. Though not reported in the paper, Theorem 1 there can be applied also to time-varying settings, and fits data quite well. Identifying systems that are critically loaded is the key step in validating the theoretical results in practice. These are reported in Mathematics of Operations Research (paper #1). By identifying operational regimes in another call center, we solve a problem involving capacity design (staffing) decision. When under-staffing happens, and queues are invisible and significant in service systems, it makes sense and is hence prevalent to provide customers with delay information. Such information could provide a relatively simple and inexpensive means for improving customer experience and controlling delay. However, such information has no noticeable impact in short-wait conditions. As a result, we need to identify service systems that are overloaded. For an overloaded (efficiency-driven regime) system, with the observation from its data that delay-time-related information has a noticeable impact on phone-customers (delay announcements can abruptly increase the likelihood to abandon), we propose decisions on the timing the announcements and the staffing levels. These findings are reported in Operations Research (paper #3).

24500314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24500314.value: For large-scale service systems, asymptotical analyses provide useful tools to gain managerial insights. When applying those managerial insights to service systems in practice, one needs to identify the operational regimes. In this project we develop new universal approximations (that can be used to fit data directly) and figure out the essential factor that determines the goodness of fit of those universal approximations to performance measures of service systems. Then a natural question to ask next would be that when the universal approximations do not approximate well, can we develop better approximations? We also identify the operational regimes in some service systems and solve the emerging operational questions. In this project, the service systems have only one server pool. It thus would be an interesting question to identify operational regimes in service systems with more complex structures. For example, if a service system has multiple server pools and customers may return for service after completing the current service, then how to identify the operational regimes from data of that system? This problem would be complicated because identifying whether a customer is a new one or a returning one is already not easy.

24500314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24500314.value: Applying asymptotic analyses to manage service systems require identifying the relationship between demand and supply (the relationships are called operational regimes). However, identifying the operational regimes is generally not easy in practice. In this project we develop new approximation results which are universal in operational regimes and patience-time distributions. Those approximations can fit performance measures of service systems well and can be applied without most of the assumptions required for the traditional asymptotical analyses. We figure out the essential factor that determines the goodness-of-fit of the universal approximations with performance measures of service systems. Because the results are applicable to different operational regimes, they are insensitive to the change of arrival rates, and the related capacity decisions can be used to manage time-varying systems. We also identify the operational regimes in some service systems and discover interesting research problems. For example, in one application, we identify an overloaded system and determine the timing of delay announcements which is meaningful only in overloaded systems. The findings of this project make significant contribution to both the theory and practice of service systems.

25100014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100014.value: 細菌耐藥性是個日益嚴重的全球問題,特別是高致命性社區型耐甲氧西林金黃色葡萄球菌（CA-MRSA）。通過靶向毒素的轉出體系即酚可溶性調控轉運蛋白（PMT）來減少CA-MRSA的重要毒力因子，有望成為抗菌感染新方法。 PMT是一種與膜結合的ATP結合盒（ABC）轉運蛋白，具有兩個獨立的膜部分和兩個單獨的ATP酶。這兩個ATP酶位於所述膜的胞質面的外周，通過結合併水解三磷酸腺苷（ATP）釋能來排出毒素。金黃色葡萄球菌的PMT是高度保守的，它主要負責所有酚可溶性調控蛋白（PSM）的轉出。 PSM是常見的細胞溶解性的肽類毒素，是導致金黃色葡萄球菌感染的關鍵因素。更重要的是，在沒有PMT的作用下，PSM衍生不僅會降低感染機遇還會導致大量細菌產生缺陷。幾種黃酮類化合物已顯示出抑制金黃色葡萄球菌感染所產生的人血紅細胞溶血。然而，目前沒有使用的小分子上的Pmt抑制的報導。基於我們早前在腫瘤化療耐藥性的工作，發現了作用於ABC轉運蛋白，包括P-糖蛋白，多藥耐藥相關蛋白與乳腺癌耐藥蛋白的新型抑製劑，我們提出通過專門設計作用於PMT的結合位點的二價配體來實現PMT的抑制。本研究的目的是設計並合成含黃酮類新型雙價配體，並考察它們的PMT的抑制活性，選擇性，效力和安全性。選取有希望的化合物來進行PMT抑制機理研究。並與目前使用的抗生素進行聯用，以發掘潛在的協同作用。本研究能讓我們基本理解PMT作用的機制，並研發出可以治療CA-MRSA感染的潛在藥物。

25100014.label: Realisation of objectives
25100014.value: Community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) is a dangerous human pathogen that causes a series of diseases ranging from mild skin infections to fatal blood infections. It was recently demonstrated that phenol-soluble modulins (PSMs), a family of cytolytic peptide toxins, were major contributors to infection of highly virulent CA-MRSA strains. Attenuating CA-MRSA virulence by using small molecules rather than killing the bacteria is a promising strategy to treat bacterial infections as this strategy applies less selection pressure for development of antibiotic resistance than traditional strategies, which aim for killing the bacteria. Four different PSMα peptides (PSMα1-4), two different PSMβ peptides (PSMβ1-2) and one δ-toxin were produced by CA-MRSA. All PSMs were formylated at the N-terminal methionine residue. Multiple key roles were played by the PSMs in staphylococcal pathogenesis; (1) they lyse human red and white blood cells efficiently, in particular PSMα3; (2) they contribute to biofilm structuring, detachment, and systemic dissemination of biofilm-associated infection; (3) they promote inflammatory responses by activating the formyl peptide receptor 2; (4) they show antimicrobial function toward other strains, such as Streptococcus pyogenes. Thus, selective lowering of PSMs may offer a promising way to attenuate CA-MRSA virulence. Flavonoids are naturally occurring polyphenolic compounds in fruits and vegetables. They have a general structure of a benzopyran ring. They constitute a normal component of human diets with an average of 200 mg consumed daily in the Western diet. They are known to exhibit a number of beneficial properties for human health including anti-inflammatory, antiviral and anticancer properties. More specifically, they do show various effects on S. aureus virulence, such as flavone, apigenin, quercetin, luteolin, chrysin, epicatechin gallate and licochalcone A significantly decreased hemolysis of human red blood cells by S. aureus. We have previously synthesized a novel series of about 20 bivalent flavonoid dimers. In the present study, we reported the discovery of flavonoid dimers as potent anti-virulence agents against CA-MRSA by lowering the level of PSMs. The cytotoxicity of flavonoid dimers towards murine fibroblast cells L929, S. aureus and E. coli strains were also determined. It was found that all flavonoid dimers 8 to 14 were nontoxic to these cell lines even at 100 µM, suggesting that these compounds did not have any killing effect on these cell lines. Moreover, the cell growth of S. aureus USA300#757 indicated that there was no effect for all flavonoid dimers 8 to 14 at 10 µM. Among all the flavonoid dimers tested for hemolysis assay, flavonoid dimer 9c showed significant anti-hemolytic activity at 10 µM by attenuating about 80% hemolysis. Interestingly, this series of flavonoid dimers 9a-9e clearly showed a linker length dependency on attenuating hemolysis by S. aureus USA300#757. For flavonoid dimers with shorter (n < 8) or longer (n > 8) linker length than flavonoid dimer 9c, they are less effective than flavonoid dimer 9c at the same concentration. Introduction of hydroxyl groups at position C5 and C7 of flavone ring (flavonoid dimer 8c) reduced anti-hemolytic activity by attenuating only 20% hemolysis, suggesting the presence of a hydrophobic binding pocket. Unexpectedly, these compounds did not show clearly dose-dependent attenuation on the rat blood hemolysis by S. aureus USA300 strain #757 at higher concentration of flavonoid dimers presumably due to their poorer aqueous solubility. Next, another clinical S. aureus USA300 ATCC#1717 strain was tested at a lower concentration of flavonoid dimers. Flavonoid dimers 9a, 9c, 9d and 9e all showed clearly dose-dependent attenuation of hemolysis by S. aureus ATCC#1717. These compounds at 1 µM significantly attenuated the hemolysis activity of S. aureus ATCC#1717 by 60% to 90%. The effective concentration that can attenuate hemolysis by 50% (EC50) was determined as 0.44, 1.24, 0.39 and 0.22 µM for 9a, 9c, 9d and 9e respectively, which are about 150- to 650-fold more potent than the monomeric flavonoid 1. No effect was observed on the rat blood hemolysis at a compound concentration below 0.04 µM. We reason that flavonoid dimers exerted anti-hemolytic activities by lowering PSMs level. To prove that, we investigated the cell growth of S. aureus ATCC#1717 in the presence of flavonoid dimer 9c. It was clearly demonstrated that a significant delay in the cell growth was observed in the presence of 10 µM flavonoid dimer 9c after 13-hour incubation. The effect of growth delay was dose-dependent with the concentration of flavonoid dimer 9c. Next, we analysed secreted protein profiles, particularly PSMα1-4, in the culture media of S. aureus USA300 ATCC#1717 in the presence of different concentrations of flavonoid dimers 9d and 9e using Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography (UPLC) and tandem mass spectrometry analysis. It was clearly shown that the presence of flavonoid dimer 9d in the culture media of S. aureus ATCC#1717 reduced the percentages of PSMs in a dose-dependent manner, with the amounts of PSMα1 and PSMα4 reduced to 39% and 36%, respectively, at the highest concentration (3 µM) tested. Similarly and even more effectively, the presence of 3 µM flavonoid dimer 9e further reduced the percentages of PSMα1 and PSMα4 to approximately 25%. The reduction of PSMα1 and PSMα4 in the culture media of S. aureus by flavonoid dimer 9e also showed dose-dependency. It was also worthy to note that PSMα2 and PSMα3 were not detected in the culture media. However, the qRT-PCR analysis indicated that these bivalent flavonoid dimers did not attenuate the level of expressed PSM genes. Unexpectedly, combinations of the active compounds with currently used β-lactam antibiotics exhibited no synergism with Fractional Inhibitory Concentration Index greater than 0.5. Thus all objectives have been realized. Taken together, these data demonstrated that our synthesized flavonoid dimers showed a promising protective effect against rat blood hemolysis caused by S. aureus USA300; such protective effect is most likely mediated through lowering the extracellular level of PSMs, which may, in turn, lead to accumulation of PSMs inside the S. aureus cells and hence growth defects. The EC50s of these effective compounds were as low as sub-micromolar range and could be considered as potential novel antivirulence agents for the treatment of infections by MRSA in the future.

It was clearly demonstrated that a significant delay in the cell growth was observed in the presence of 10 µM flavonoid dimer 9c after 13 hour incubation. The effect of growth delay was dose-dependent with the concentration of flavonoid dimer 9c. 25100014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100014.value: Taken together, our data demonstrated that several flavonoid dimers at optimal linker lengths showed promising protective effect against rat blood hemolysis caused by S. aureus USA300 by lowering extracellular PSMs level; such protective effect seems to be mediated through attenuating the PSMs level, but not downregulating the level of PSMs genes, which may, in turn, lead to accumulation of PSMs inside the S. aureus cells and hence growth defects. The EC50s of these effective compounds were as low as the submicromolar range. Further animal experiments should be pursued in order to confirm the in vitro results. Moreover, studies of the molecular mechanism of how flavonoid dimers reduce the PSMs level are worthy for further investigation.

25100014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100014.value: Community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) is a dangerous human pathogen that causes a series of diseases ranging from mild skin infections to fatal blood infections. It was recently demonstrated that phenol-soluble modulins (PSMs), a family of cytolytic peptide toxins, were major contributors to infection of highly virulent CA-MRSA strains as PSMs were secreted at relatively higher concentration compared with others MRSA strains. In this project, screening of synthesized bivalent flavonoid dimers demonstrated that some of these compounds are potent anti-virulence agents against CA-MRSA with an effective concentration that can attenuate rat blood hemolysis assay by 50% (EC50) at 0.22 to 1.24 µM, which are about 150- to 650-fold more potent than monomeric flavonoid. UPLC/MS analysis of the secreted toxin profiles in the culture media of CA-MRSA in the presence of flavonoid dimers suggested that flavonoid dimers attenuate CA-MRSA virulence by lowering the extracellular level of phenol-soluble modulins, exhibiting novel anti-virulence potential. This will open up a new approach to treat bacterial infection of CA-MRSA.

25100114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100114.value: Influenza epidemics and pandemics have had a huge impact in the past and continue to pose a serious threat for the years ahead. Influenza viruses evolve rapidly and spread among human and other species including birds, swine and equine. Vaccination is an effective control measure, and the virus components in the vaccine are updated annually. Vaccination policies and coverage vary across countries. However, it is unclear whether the differences in vaccination policies have caused any large-scale spatio-temporal patterns of influenza transmission. In the United States and Canada, influenza vaccination is free and is recommended to healthy individuals, and vaccination coverage in the general population (VCG) has reached 40% and 30%, respectively. The coverage in school-aged children has reached 50% in the US which is higher than that in the rest of the world. For example, it is well below 15% in Europe and Hong Kong, where influenza vaccination is not recommended to healthy individuals and is not free. Weekly laboratory-confirmations of samples from 138 countries are freely accessible via the World Health Organization (WHO) Influenza Surveillance Network (FluNet), which consist of influenza types A and B, subtypes A/H3N2/68 (variants of the 1968 pandemic strain), A/H1N1/77 (variants of the 1957 pandemic strains) and A/H1N1/09 (the 2009 pandemic strain). Rich patterns of the emergence, displacement, co-existence and competition among different types and subtypes are vividly exhibited in these data. Several descriptive studies have been conducted by others for the period 1997 to 2008. Mechanistic modeling studies were only conducted for a few countries and for a short period. Large-scale mechanistic modeling across countries has not yet been attempted. The impact of the vaccination on the patterns of influenza spreading in these data has not been studied, to our knowledge. Our preliminary analysis indeed suggests a possible correlation. More specifically, we found that the A/H1N1/09 strain skipped the 2011/12 flu season in Europe and Eastern Asia, with an evidently low annual total compared to that of the previous and following flu seasons, whereas it showed consistently mild epidemics in Northern America. 25100114.label: Realisation of objectives
25100114.value: We achieved the project objectives through extensive data-analyses and mathematical modelling approaches. We published our findings in 12 journal papers (with influenza or vaccination in the title) and three manuscripts are ready for submission. One PhD and two MPhil students were supervised. The findings of this project is also reflected in their thesis. In He et al (Sci Report 2015), we studied the global spatio-temporal patterns of influenza dynamics. This was achieved by analysing and modelling weekly laboratory confirmed cases of influenza A and B from 138 countries between January 2006 and January 2015. The data were obtained from FluNet, the surveillance network compiled by the World Health Organization. We reported a pattern of skip-and-resurgence behavior between the years 2011 and 2013 for influenza H1N1pdm, the strain responsible for the 2009 pandemic, in Europe and Eastern Asia. In particular, the expected H1N1pdm epidemic outbreak in 2011/12 failed to occur (or “skipped”) in many countries across the globe, although an outbreak occurred in the following year. We also reported a pattern of well-synchronized wave of H1N1pdm in early 2011 in the Northern Hemisphere countries, and a pattern of replacement of strain H1N1pre by H1N1pdm between the 2009 and 2012 influenza seasons. Using both a statistical and a mechanistic mathematical model, and through fitting the data of 108 countries, we discussed the mechanisms that are likely to generate these events taking into account the role of multi-strain dynamics. We argued that a basic understanding of these patterns has important public health implications and scientific significance. We are the first to report such an evident skip-and-resurgence behavior of an influenza strain in a large-scale geography. Thus our work caught some media attention (such as Asia Research News magazine 2016 page 52) In He et al (Sci Report 2015), we fitted a mathematical model to aggregated influenza A cases (by combining H1N1pdm and H3N2) in top ten countries in term of reported influenza cases. We found that the duration of immunity (due to either infection or vaccination) is most likely around 2 years (this is true in 7 out of the top 10 countries), or have a wide confidence interval from 2 to 4 years (China and Norway), or around 4 years (e.g. UK). Our mathematical modelling and data-fitting work is more advanced (trustworthy) than previous works, because we managed to fit one model to data from TEN countries simultaneously. Most of previous works are focused on one country. Thus we concluded that the skip of H1N1pdm is most likely a result of low susceptibility to H1N1pdm and interference between H1N1pdm and H3N2. The resurgence of H1Npdm in the following year is a result of replenishment of susceptible of H1N1pdm due to waning-of-immunity of H1N1pdm. In Ho et al (JTB 2019), we developed 2 models (for 1 & 3 influenza strains) to describe the 2017/18 influenza epidemics in Hong Kong. We found that at least 72% of Hong Kong population had to be vaccinated to prevent seasonal epidemics in Hong Kong. We also found that increase in one influenza subtype vaccine efficacy may lead an increase in infections caused by another subtype. In Chiu (IJID 2018), we found that A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 have shown annual and biannual periodicities in Hong Kong. We found that A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 have shown annual and triannual periodicities in the North Temperate Zone. We reported anti-phase patterns between influenza A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 in Hong Kong and the North Temperate Zone. In Lin (PhD Thesis, 2019), with reported cases of Influenza A/H1N1 and A/H3N2 from January 2010 and July 2017 from World Health Organization, we explored and verified the anti-phase temporal pattern of these two subtypes both in Hong Kong and North Temperate Zone, which indicates a high prevalence of A/H1N1 coincides with a low prevalence of A/H3N2 and vice versa. By constructing a statistical metric, i.e., weekly case ratio of influenza B over influenza A, we showed a strong positive correlation with the activity of B/Victoria in China, abnormality of extremely high ratio accompanied by unusual low vaccine effective in the United States, as well as revealed the global pattern of influenza activity by computing the statistical correlation of the ratios between countries and regions. We report that the weekly ratio of influenza B over A in both state-level and country level showed a peak in 2015 and the VE is low in 2015 than other years. We argue that these two events could have some associations. Statistically speaking, the probability that these two events occur in the same year (out of eight years) is 1 out of 8. This is equivalent to toss two fair dices (assume eight sides for each) and obtain the same side for both. Although this is not statistically significant (1/8), this finding deserves further investigation. He et al. (2015) argued that the difference in vaccination coverage could possibly cause some large-scale patterns, e.g. a skip-and-resurgence of influenza A/H1N1 in mainland China, HK and some European countries. The abnormality in weekly ratio of B over A in 2014/2015 season could be related to the competition between influenza A and B. When the VE is low, the competition of being infected by A or B for the susceptible pool becomes strong. Therefore, the time delay between influenza A and B epidemics is enlarged. Thus, low VE (or low vaccination coverage) favors the "antiphase pattern" between influenza A and B. One of other reasons could be the emergence of a novel strain or clade of influenza B, which was very transmissible and virulent in 2015 (See Bedford and Neher (2016)). With the methodology developed (on the large-scale effect of vaccination for a vaccine-preventable diseases) in this project, the research team won the award for Outstanding Research Articles in Biosurveillance (second place) by the international society for disease surveillance for the paper "Modelling the Large-scale Yellow Fever Outbreak in Luanda, Angola, and the Impact of Vaccination. PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 12(1): e0006158." On Dissemination of the research finding in this project. The PI has conveyed the finding to public health officers of Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevetion (SZCDC). To suppor this, the SZCDC provide a testimony "Professor He and his team have collaborated closely with our Center in recent years. He has conducted research on influenza in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, modeling of varicella infectious diseases in Shenzhen, and Guillain-Barre syndrome in Hong Kong, providing a solid theoretical basis for prevention and control of infectious diseases in the city. Among them, the 'Synchronous Study of Influenza Epidemic Situations in Shenzhen and Hong Kong' conducted a comparative analysis of the influenza epidemic situation in Shenzhen and Hong Kong in 2006-2017. It was found that the A/H3N2 epidemic in Hong Kong was serious in 2015 and was mild in Shenzhen; In Shenzhen, influenza B is more servere than in Hong Kong, most likely due to the younger population in Shenzhen. The vaccine is not completely compatible with Yamagata lineage, suggesting that the city should try to use the four-valent flu vaccine. At the same time, the study also provided a theoretical basis for the early prediction of influenza epidemics in the city."

25100114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100114.value: Occasionally, the WHO recommended influenza vaccine misses the target strain and shows a low efficacy against a strain among the three targeted strains. Further studies should take advantage of these chances to study the large-scale impact of mismatched vaccine in those countries with high vaccination coverage (e.g US and Canada). Some metrics may be developed to reveal these hidden impacts. For example, the 2015 vaccine mis-match, we found that the influenza B weekly cases over influenza A weekly cases show abnormally high value. So far, this finding is not statistically significant due to the relatively short (eight years) of data. I expected when a few more years of data come in, we may claim this is a significant effect.

25100114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100114.value: Influenza poses a serious threat to global public health. In this project, we reported interesting interference phenomena among influenza strains and vaccination. We analyzed influenza weekly reported cases from 138 countries and regions combined by the World Health Organization. We found that high vaccination coverage in the United States and Canada most likely prevented a skip-and-resurgence phenomenon in 2011-2013 which occurred in a large portion of Europe and Asia where vaccination coverage is generally low. We found that influenza A/H1N1pdm (together with influenza B) and A/H3N2 show anti-phase patterns in the north temperate zone and Hong Kong. Thus when one strain causes a severe epidemics, cases of the other strain will be rare. Waning of influenza A due to either infection or immunization is most likely short around two years in the post-pandemic era (2010-2015).

25100614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100614.value: Myopia (shortsightedness) is a multifactorial condition which is resulted when an eye has grown too long for its focus. It is regards as the most common refractive error which often occurs at an early age and it usually progress over the years. The prevalence of myopia is alarmingly high and is up to 90% in some Asian countries. Both the prevalence and severity of myopia are growing worldwide. High myopia can lead to many sight-threatening ocular complications. In fact, myopic retinal degeneration is one of the leading causes of blindness in Hong Kong. As the myopic population continues to rise, it is feared that the number of visual impairments will escalate drastically. Despite that a large number of clinical and animal studies were conducted in the past, evidence–based methods for prevention or arrest of this disorder remain hampered by the lack of clear knowledge of the pathogenesis of myopia. Proteomic approach provides molecular “snap-shots” in which thousands of cellular proteins can be profiled, catalogued and compared efficiently. Modern advances in proteomic methods have enhanced our knowledge in many diseases for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. By comparing changes between normal and myopic tissues, key biochemical pathways in myopia may be revealed. In addition, protein phosphorylation is currently regarded as one of the most important post-translational modifications found in eukaryotes. It is a key mechanism of cellular signaling pathways and has been implicated in the development of a number of human diseases. However, there is still no published data on the possible protein modifications involved in myopia. Vitreous is known to be significantly altered during the myopic eye growth. Recent breakthrough in Liquid Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (LCMS)-based profiling technique streamline with the tremendous development in bioinformatics tools offer sensitive and comprehensive analysis at high throughput which is nearly impossible 5 years ago. We aim to provide the first protein profiling of chick vitreous during the normal emmetropization. Applying isobaric labeled and novel label-free proteomic approach, we also aim to investigate the differential protein expressions as well as the phosphorproteomics in vitreous in response to the myopic growth and during recovery. More tissue specific data will provide a clearer picture about biochemical pathways that regulate the elongation of eyeball. This proposed pioneer proteomic work using the well-established chick model will shed important light on the mechanism of eye growth as well as open up new molecular targets for drug treatment for myopia.

25100614.value: The two objectives proposed for the study have been successfully achieved (100%). The key research questions are: 1. Whether more sensitive gel-free proteomics technique can be modified and adopted in studying of the proteome of very diluted vitreous in a small chick eye 2. Whether proteins expressions and temporal changes can be identified and detected in normal growing chick vitreous 3. Whether differentially expressed proteins can be found in the compensated myopic vitreous using the classic chick model

25100614.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100614.value: We have published at least 5 conference abstracts and 5 journal publications with the support of the funding. In addition, training for one PhD student and two undergraduate students has been supported by the grant. Using the established novel proteomic platform, I have secured one GRF grant and two collaborative grants. Key findings: - We have successful developed a Lens-induced myopia chick model for the study of vitreous proteomics. Experimental procedures from biometric measurement, protein sample extraction, labeled and SWATH mass spectrometric settings to bioinformatic analysis for studying the vitreous proteome were successfully optimized for the first time in myopia research. - A custom-made T-PER buffered protocol for SWATH MS detection was successfully used for high-throughput identification of chick vitreous proteome: more than 1000 proteins could be identified from only 1-2ug of vitreous sample from a single eye. We have established and published online the 1st comprehensive chick vitreous ion-library on public data repository. - using -10D LIM chick myopia model, a number of statistically significant regulated proteins were successfully identified and quantified in progressing myopia. Using a new cloud-based bioinformatic software, our data supported oxidative stress and lipid metabolism which linked to previously known TGF-beta signal as key pathways involved in the elongation of the posterior eye.

25100614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100614.value: This study is the first to analyze the chick vitreous proteome under normal conditions and in induced eye growth. A number of novel proteins were confirmed to be significantly regulated and expressed in the myopic eyes. These proteins can be served as potential myopia markers in ocular development. This study has provided new insights in the mechanisms leading to myopia. Our next step aims to look for potential molecules which could modulate the expression of these candidates in order to develop new drug candidates for myopia control.

25100614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100614.value: Recent data predicted that the number of myopes worldwide will grow towards a staggering 5 billion by 2050 with the majority of myopes living in Asian cities. It remains unknown that how the myopia mechanism works exactly on the eye. During myopia progression, the eyeball elongates so that the image will not be able to be focused on the retina properly. Vitreous Chamber Depth (VCD) is the main contributor to the increased eye axial length during myopia progression. This elongation is also seen during the emmetropization of the eye during normal growth, which could serve as a link in the identification of the myopia progression mechanism. Chick vitreous at selected time points were collected during the emmetropization period as well as during the myopia growth. Using a cutting edge SWATH-based label free proteomic approach, our group has successfully profile and established a chick vitreous proteome. Surprisingly, the protein compositions in vitreous were far more complicated than it was expected. Among more than 1000 soluble proteins we could identified, novel proteins and their functions involved in myopia were found, for the first time in this study.

25100714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100714.value: Adult neurogenesis is a life-long process which occurs at two regions in the central nervous system: the dentate gyrus (DG) of hippocampus and the subventricular zone along the later ventricles. New DG neurons are continuously generated and functionally incorporated into the existing hippocampal neural circuitry. While hippocampus is known for its importance in memory formation and affective behaviors, the new neurons are suggested to play critical roles in these functions. Contextual fear conditioning, in which an individual learns to associate a neutral environment (context) with a fearful emotional experience, is dependent on the hippocampal neurogenesis. Animals could not demonstrate the association when neurogenesis is suppressed. Interestingly, recent studies showed that the new neurons are also necessary for the extinction of the contextual fear memory. Extinction is a form of learning which allows the subject to adapt to the changing environment. The involvement of neurogenesis in extinction suggests a new function of the new neurons which is related conditioning. Although the behavioral outcomes of memory formation and extinction are different, neurogenesis may be a key neural substrate for both processes.Compared to memory formation, studies which investigate the relationship between neurogenesis and extinction is still scarce. In addition, since most of the extinction protocols involve conditioning before extinction, the complexity of study design leads to ambiguous, contradictory results. In contrast to contextual fear conditioning, the extinction process of innate fear stimulus does not require a conditioning process, which allows a direct demonstration of the extinction process. In the current proposal, we aim at determining whether neurogenesis is involved in the extinction process, and whether fearful stimulus regulates neurogenesis. Repeated exposure of an innate phobogenic stimulus (trimethylthiazoline, a synthetic fox feces odor) will be applied on rats. The rats will display freezing behavior as the innate fearful response. The necessity of neurogenesis for extinction will be determined by suppressing neurogenesis in the hippocampus, followed by the assessment of duration of freezing behavior. To investigate the neurological mechanism, assessment of hippocampal neurogenesis in terms of cell proliferation, survival and differentiation of new neurons will be carried out, and the molecular regulation of the above processes (with focus of the stress hormone corticosterone) will be assayed. By utilizing the phobia model, this study will provide novel knowledge on the roles of neurogenesis, which will shed light not only on the physiology of fear extinction but also suggest a novel role of hippocampal neurogenesis. 成年神經元新生是發生在兩個腦區域 (海馬齒狀回和腦室下區)的一個終身過程 ，新生的神經元不斷產生和結合到現有的神經迴路。海馬在記憶形成和情感行為中擔當關鍵的角色 ，而新的神經元亦於這些功能中發揮重要作用。 塲景性恐懼條件化指一個人或個體把一個中立的環境聯想至恐懼的情感，而這種學習是依賴於海馬神經元新生的。若神經元新生被抑制，實驗動物將不能展示此關聯。有趣的是，最近的研究表明，消退塲景性恐懼也需要神經元新生。從相反角度而言，消退塲景性恐懼也是學習的一種形式，它允許個體用以適應不斷變化的環境。新生神經元在消退恐懼的參與表明了有關新神經元的一個新發現。 雖然記憶的形成和消亡的結果迴然不同， 神經元新生卻可能同時是兩者的一個關鍵。與記憶形成的研究相比下，探討恐懼消退與新神經元之間關係的研究仍是稀缺的。再者，由於多數的恐懼消退實驗包含了條件化學習，研究設計的複雜性導致不明確的、矛盾的結果。 與此相反，以情境恐懼制約的，先天恐懼的滅絕過程不需要條件化學習，它允許直接演視恐懼消退。 在此研究計劃中，我們的目標是確定神經元新生是否參與先天恐懼的滅絕，和先天恐懼的刺激會否影響神經元新生。在動物實驗中，大鼠將會重複接受一種引致先天恐懼的化合物(trimethylthiazoline，狐狸的糞便臭味)，大鼠會由於先天恐懼反應而顯示呆立不動(凍結)的行為 。神經元新生在消退恐懼的必要性將會透過 抑制實驗測定，同時亦會評估凍結行為的持續時間。為了研究先天恐懼的刺激會否影響神經元新生，海馬的細胞增殖、存活和分化方面將被評估，並且在上述過程的分子調控 過程（與壓力荷爾蒙皮質酮的關係）將被檢測。通過利用此恐懼症 模型，本研究將提供有關新神經元功能的知識，並 揭示恐懼滅絕的神經機制。

25100714.label: Realisation of objectives
25100714.value: The project, which tested the hypothesis that neurogenesis is involved in the behavioral modification after repeated exposures to phobogenic stimuli, has been completed. The following outline describes how the objectives have been archived. For objective 1: To determine whether repeated exposures to innate fearful stimulus would bring behavioral modification (extinction) and changes in neurogenesis. Methods: Young adult Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to two groups (n = 6 per group): (1) TMT (Trimethylthiazoline) group: rats were placed in a non-restraining cylinder and exposed to 300nM TMT or (2) Control group: rats were placed in an identical situation as TMT group but exposed to vehicle (propylene glycol). Innate fearful response was indicated by the time of freezing displayed by the animals in a 10 minutes exposure session. The whole experiment lasted for 14 days and the exposure sessions were carried out on alternate days. Freezing behaviors were assessed on the first day and the last day of exposure. The animals were subsequently sacrificed for assessment of neurogenesis in the hippocampus. Results: On the first day of exposure, the duration of freezing time displayed by the TMT group was significantly higher than the control group, which was in line with the expectation that fearful behavior is induced by exposure to TMT. After repeated exposure to TMT, however, the TMT group didn’t differ significantly from the control group in freezing behavior. Assessment of neurogenesis by bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU, a cell proliferative marker) and doublecortin (DCX, a cellular marker of immature, new neurons) immunostaining indicated a significant increase in hippocampal neurogenesis in TMT group. Conclusion: Repeated exposure to TMT, an innate phobogenic stimulus, would tend to reduce fear response (extinction) and promote hippocampal neurogenesis. For objective 2: To determine whether blocking neurogenesis would suppress extinction. Methods: Rats were randomly assigned to three groups: (1) TMT group, (2) Control group or (3) TMT+MAM (methylazoxemethanol acetate) group, which received daily intraperitoneal injection of MAM (10mg/kg) to suppress neurogenesis and exposure to TMT as group (1). The experiment lasted for 14 days and the time of freezing was assessed in the last exposure session. Results: No significant difference was found between TMT and Control groups in the time of freezing at the last session. However, significant difference was found between Control and TMT+MAM groups, in which the later group shows longer duration of freezing. Conclusion: Blocking neurogenesis by MAM would abolish the effect of repeated phobogenic stimulus exposures found in TMT group. For objective 3: To determine whether pharmacological treatment, which was shown to increase neurogenesis, would facilitates the extinction effect of repeated fear exposures Methods: Fluoxetine (Fx), a serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) and antidepressant, was proven to increase neurogenesis. We use fluoxetine as the pharmacological treatment to promote neurogenesis. SD rats were divided randomly into (1) TMT group or (2) TMT+Fx group, which received daily intraperitoneal injection of Fx (10mg/kg) and repeated exposures to TMT. The time of freezing in the last exposure session was assessed. Results: The time of freezing displayed by the TMT+Fx group was significantly lower than the TMT group. Conclusion: Pharmacological treatment which increased neurogenesis facilitates the reduction in time of freezing after repeated exposures to phobogenic stimulus. The finding supports the usage of SSRIs facilitate exposure therapy, including specific phobia. For objective 4: To determine whether repeated TMT exposures would affect new neurons’ survival, and whether the new cells are responsive to the stimulus. Methods: Rats were divided into TMT or Control groups as described in objective 1 and received repeated exposures to TMT or vehicles for 14 days. Before the first exposure session, BrdU was intraperitoneally injected to label cells which were proliferative at the beginning of experiment. Rats were sacrificed after 14 days and then brains were harvested for brdU and c-fos immunostaining. Before sacrifice, animals were exposed to TMT to activate neurons which are responsive to TMT. Result: Though the average number of BrdU-positive cells in the hippocampus of TMT group animals was higher than that of the control group, no significant difference was found. Co-immunostaining of brdU and c-fos (an immediate early gene product which indirectly indicates activity of neurons) indicated that co-localization of BrdU and c-fos could be found. In other words, the new born neurons (with BrdU staining) are activated (with c-fos expression) by TMT before the rats were sacrificed. Conclusion: Repeated exposures to phobogenic stimulus might not promote the survival of new born neurons. The new born cells in the hippocampus were found to be responsive to TMT. For objective 5: To determine whether corticosterone, a stress hormone, is involved in the molecular regulation of neurogenesis by innate fear exposure Methods: SD rats were assigned to (1) TMT group or (2) TMT+RU486 (an antagonist of glucocorticoid receptor) group, which received intraperitoneal injection of RU486 30 minutes before each exposure session. After exposures for 14 days, animals were sacrificed and their brains were harvested for brdU staining. Serum was collected from the experiment in objective 1 and the level of corticosterone were determined by enzyme-link immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Another experiment divided aniamls into (1) control group and (2) high dose, exogenous corticosterone injection (40mg/kg) was conducted. Neurogenesis and emotional behaviors were assessed after 14 days’ treatment. Results: The serum level of corticosterone was significantly higher in the TMT group than the control group, which indicated that exposures to TMT would activate the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. The number of BrdU-positive cells in the hippocampus of TMT+RU486 group was significantly lower than the TMT group. Exogenous, high dose treatment with corticosterone was shown to significantly suppress neurogenesis and induced emotional disturbances. Conclusion: Corticosterone, a stress hormone, is likely involved in the regulation of neurogenesis by phobogenic stimulation. This was supported by the increase in serum corticosterone level after repeated phobogenic stimulus exposures, and the number of proliferative cells in TMT-exposed animals was significantly lower when the receptors of corticosterone were blocked by antagonist. In situation with high dose corticosterone (hypercortisolemia), in contrast, there was a suppression of neurogenesis and induction of emotional disturbance. These indicated that corticosterone may have dose-dependent effect on neurogenesis and behaviors.

25100714.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100714.value: The major findings are: (1). with an animal model of repeated exposures to phobogenic stimulus (specific phobia), we demonstrated that repeated exposures to TMT would reduce the innate fearful response. This finding provides supports, based on laboratory animal study, for the current practice of exposures therapy in the treatment of human specific phobia. The possible translation of laboratory results from animal studies to clinical application was discussed in publication 1 (Cheung et al.). (2). Neurogenesis is probably involved in the behavioral modification, which is supported by the following observations: i. repeated TMT exposures increased neurogenesis; ii. when neurogenesis was blocked, the behavioral modification was abolished and iii. increasing neurogenesis, by pharmacological means, would enhance the reduction of fearful responses in exposure therapy. These findings suggest that neurogenesis may be an underlying mechanism which mediate the reduction of fearful stimulus, and thus may be a potential target for future development of treatment for specific phobia. As we found that inhalation of specific odor molecules would alter neurogenesis, we have extended our study to search for other compounds which has potential effects on neurogenesis and emotional behaviors, which is discussed in publication 4 (3) Corticosterone, a stress hormone, may be a mediator of the augmented neurogenesis induced by repeated TMT exposures. Based on this finding, we have extended our study to investigate the effect of supraphysiological dose of corticosterone treatment on neurogenesis and emotional behaviors related to anxiety, and the results are published in publications 3 and 4. The project has resulted in 5 peer-reviewed journal papers and 1 conference abstract which is accepted for publication in a special issue of Simulation in Healthcare. One journal paper ‘Potential involvement of neurogenesis in behavioral habituation after repeated exposure to an innate stimulus’ is pending for submission to a special issue of Frontiers in Neuroscience by invitation.

25100714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100714.value: The current study indicates that repeated exposures to an innate fearful stimulus increases neurogenesis. However, the current study design could not differentiate whether TMT increase neurogenesis as an odor molecule or as a phobogenic stimulus. To solve this question, future studies may test the effect of repeated TMT exposures on neurogenesis in a species which does not display fearful response to TMT, and test the effect of repeated exposures to other phobogenic stimuli (e.g. natural cat odor collected by collar) on neurogenesis of rat. The results would further confirm whether the current animal model would be a valid one to simulate exposure therapy in human. On the other hand, as the current study shows that treatment with SSRI, which increase neurogenesis would enhance the behavioral modification of repeated exposures to feared stimulus. It would be worthwhile, therefore, to investigate if other pro-neurogenic treatments would also enhance the reduction in fearful responses. The result would be translated to clinical application of possible new treatment regime for specific phobia, for instance, concomitant treatment of pro-neurogenic treatment (e.g. wolfberry polysaccharide) and exposure therapy.

25100714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100714.value: Specific phobia is a long lasting, unreasonable fear to particular objects or situations. The intense anxiety makes the sufferers avoid the object or situation, and may interfere with the individual’s daily functioning. There are different options for the treatment of specific phobia, while exposure therapy (repeated exposures to the feared object/situation) is a common one. To explore the underlying mechanism of exposure therapy, the current study examines the neurobiological changes after repeated exposures to trimethylthiazoline (TMT, a component of fox feces which could induce innate fearful response on rodents). After repeated exposures for 7 sessions, the fearful response was reduced. The exposures increases the production of new cells (including neurons and supporting cells) in the hippocampal region of the brain, and the new cells may be essential for the behavioral change. Corticosterone, a stress hormone, may mediate the production of new neurons. These results suggest that there is a neurobiological basis of exposure therapy, and the production of new neurons may be a key player. Thus treatment methods known to promote production of new neurons may augment the efficacy of exposure therapy, and future exploration of the biological mechanisms underlying different treatments may provide further evidence to support clinical practice.

25101014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25101014.value: Time-based walk tests are simple, inexpensive and safe field tests that provide information on functional exercise capacity of individuals. Distance covered in a set time period in the walk tests, such as in a period of 2 minutes (2MWT) or 6 minutes (6MWT), give valuable information on the functional exercise performance of individuals and monitoring treatment effectiveness of different patient groups. There are concerns that individuals with poor muscle strength, decreased exercise tolerance and reduced attention span may find it very difficult to complete the 6MWT. Therefore, the 2MWT may be more feasible for these client groups. Very limited research findings are available for this walk test especially for paediatric population groups. No norm has yet been published for this walk test at present. In addition, no psychometric properties of the 2MWT have been thoroughly evaluated. This lack of research evidence greatly impacts on the decision making on client management in paediatric rehabilitation. The main objectives of the present study are (1) to examine the test-retest, intra-rater and inter-rater reliability of 2MWT on a convenience sample of 55 typically developing (TD) children (Phase I); (2) to establish normative values of 2MWT on a convenience sample of 600 TD children in Hong Kong (Phase II); (3) to examine feasibility, known groups validity (construct validity) and minimal clinically important difference of the 2MWT on a convenience sample of 50 children with neuromuscular disorders (Phase III); and (4) to recommend testing guidelines on the 2MWT for children under 12 years of age. Study children, all aged between 6 and 12 years, will be asked to walk on an indoor quiet corridor of 30 metre in length with a self-selected pace without jogging or running for 2 minutes. The distance covered in the walk test will be measured with a distance-measuring wheel by an assessor walking behind the children. Three trials of the walk test will be performed in each testing. In Phase I, children will be assessed on 3 occasions by 2 assessors. In Phases II and III, children will be assessed on 1 and 2 occasions respectively by 1 assessor. The results will provide research evidence on the clinimetric properties of the 2MWT to clinicians for both clinical and research purposes. The normative values collected in the present study will be the first worldwide norms on the 2MWT. Testing protocols of the 2MWT will be recommended.

25101014.label: Realisation of objectives
25101014.value: Objective 1- at the end of the study, 61 children were recruited and completed to examine the reliability of the 2MWT. The walk test has been shown to have an excellent intra- and inter-rater reliability. This objective was fully fulfilled. Objective 2- at the end of the study, 716 healthy children aged 6 to 12 years of age were completed to establish the first worldwide norms for the 2MWT. This objective was fully fulfilled. Objective 3- at the end of the study, 46 children with neuromuscular disabilities were completed to establish the known group validity of the 2MWT and MCID was established for children with neuromuscular disorders who walked independently and walked with walking aids. 50 children with neuromuscular disorders were targeted in the proposal. 47 children were recruited due to the stringent criterion that children were able to follow simple instructions and commands, hence, children with moderate and severe cognitive impairment as well as behavioural problems were excluded. In addition, there was a very poor recruitment from 2 of the largest special schools for children with physical disabilities under the same NGO, where only 1 child was recruited without any obvious reason for the poor recruitment. For the 47 recruited children, one child with Duchene Muscular Dystrophy was able to complete only one of the 3 trials of 2MWT and his data was discarded for statistical analyses. Despite the small shortfall of recruitment, significant differences were found in the performance of the 2MWT between the children with neuromuscular disorders and their healthy counterparts. The 2MWT was also able to differentiate those children with neuromuscular disorders, who walked independently and with walking aids. Hence, this objective was fully fulfilled at the end of the study. Objective 4- a testing protocol of the 2MWT for children have been proposed and published by the PI in a peer-reviewed journal in 2014, just before the commencement of this study (Pin TW. Psychometric properties of 2-minute walk test: a systematic review. March 2014. Arch Phy Med Rehabil. 2014;95, 1759-1775.). This testing protocol was tested in the present study and published in another peer-reviewed journal in 2017 (Pin TW and Choi, HL. Psychometric properties and normative values of 2-minute walk test in children between 6 and 12 years of age. Disabil & Rehabil 2017. http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/09638288.2017.1294208). 25200014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200014.value: Most System on Chips (SoCs) are created from a combination of legacy Register Transfer Level (RTL) blocks, Intellectual Properties (IPs), newly developed RTL and C/SystemC descriptions synthesized using behavioral synthesis (also called High-Level Synthesis). This re-use of existing legacy code allows design teams to focus only on the new features that need to be implemented, thus reducing time to market considerably. The International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS) suggest that by 2020 a 10x productivity increase for designing complex SoCs is needed [1]. Two main factors are predicted to help achieving this goal. The first is the re-use of components. ITRS estimates that around 90% of the SoCs will be composed of re-used components. Secondly, the use of new design methodologies to raise the level of abstraction i.e. High-Level Synthesis (HLS). C-Based design has many advantages compared to traditional RTL design. The increase in design productivity, which allows design teams to meet the increasingly stringent time-to-market requirements, the ability to create smaller designs compared to hand-coded RTL due to its ability to maximize resource sharing [2] and the possibility of generating a set of different micro-architectures with different area vs. performance trade-offs without having to modify the original behavioral description, also called Design Space Exploration (DSE). In traditional RTL design it is virtually impossible to do DSE as it would involve having to re-write the RTL description completely in order to create the new micro-architecture. Moreover it is common practice not to modify any hardware (HW) block that has been fully verified, even if a more efficient architecture could be achieved in subsequent designs, due to the cost of having to re-verify the new implementation. The main goal of this proposal is 3-fold: The first is to investigate practical methods to abstract synthesizable RTL descriptions into synthesizable ANSI-C or SystemC optimized for HLS design space exploration. This involves identifying structures in the RTL that can be converted into high level language constructs that when explored have the strongest impact on the final micro-architecture (e.g. loops, arrays and functions). The second goal is to evaluate and develop methods to verify that the original RTL description and the newly generated C/SystemC are equivalent and lastly to investigate DSE methods which can find the best area vs. performance trade-off curve (Pareto-optimal curve) in the smallest possible time, also looking into computational methods to speed the exploration up (e.g.multi-thread computing, General-Purpose Graphics Processing Unit(GPGPU)). 大多數片上系統（SoC）設計是由以下方式綜合開發而成的：傳統的寄存器傳輸級（RTL）模塊組合，知識產權核（IP），新發展的寄存器傳輸級設計，以及由行為綜合（也稱高級綜合）合成的C或SystemC語言設計。重複使用現有的設計能夠讓開發小組更集中注意力在需要實現的新設計上，從而大大地減少上市的時間。國際半導體技術發展藍圖（ITRS）表示，到2020年為止，複雜的片上系統開發生產力需要有10倍的增長來滿足需求。他們預測主要有兩個因素會幫助實現這一目標。第一個就是元件的重複使用。ITRS估計大約有90%的片上系統是由重複使用的元件組成的。第二個是利用新的設計方法來提高抽象層，例如高級綜合（HLS）。 相比于傳統的RTL設計，以C語言為基礎的開發有許多優點：提高了設計生產力，這使得開發小組滿足更迫切的上市時機的要求；能夠開發出更小面積的設計，相比純人工編程的RTL設計，這是資源共享最大化的結果；進行設計空間探索（DSE），即生成一系列不同面積對比性能權衡的微結構，而且不需要改變原行為描述。 在傳統的RTL開發中，設計空間探索是不可能實現的，因為這必須要完全地重寫原RTL代碼來構造一個新的微結構。此外，一般情況下食不會修改任何已經驗證過的硬件（HW）模塊，即使一個更有效的結構能夠在隨後的設計中實現，這是因為必須為新的設計實現進行重新驗證的花費。 這份計劃書的主要目的是三方面的。首先是研究一個切實可行的方法來提取可綜合化的RTL描述并轉變成ANSI-C或SystemC語言，然後由高級綜合的設計空間探索進行優化。這個目的包括了識別能從RTL語言轉換到高級語言的部分，並且這部分在探索中對最後微結構影響最大（例如，循環體，數組以及函數結構）。第二個是評估和研究方法去驗證原RTL描述與新生成的C或SystemC語言是等效的。最後則是研究設計空間探索的方法，從而在最短的時間內找到最好的大小對比性能的權衡曲線（Pareto最優曲線），同時考慮計算方法來加快探索速度（例如，多線程計算，通用圖像處理器（GPGPU）等）。

25200114.label: Project Objectives
25200114.value: To develop a cost-effective process flow to sandwich a few-layer graphene at the metal/dielectric interface. We expect that a few-layer graphene can effectively block the migration of metallic species into the dielectric under the normal electrical/thermal stressing conditions occurring in an integrated circuit (150 º C and 0.5 MV/cm). To fabricate an ECM memory structure with the insertion of a graphene nanopore between the metal and dielectric, and investigate the effects of graphene nanopore size and distribution on the performance (power consumption, retention, endurance, variation, and switching time) of ECM memory. We expect to fabricate an ECM cell with effective electrode size down to 5 nm with the use of a graphene nanopore interfacial layer. To study the fundamental limits of a minimum Cu source that ensures the stable resistance switching in an ECM cell. We will use graphene nanopores and ultra-thin Cu electrodes to confine the Cu source in the structure of ECM cells.

25200114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200114.value: The understanding of metal/dielectric interfaces remains an important topic in the field of nano-electronics and beyond. The intrinsic complexity of the metal/dielectric interface is caused by inter-diffusion, and is further complicated by the electrical/thermal stressing that usually occurs in electronic devices. The migration of metallic species into the dielectric can adversely affect the reliability of the insulating dielectric, and can also form an electrochemical metallization (ECM) memory by growing/dissolving metal filaments in the dielectric. An ECM cell consists of a metal/dielectric/metal structure, in which the ON/OFF resistance states are controlled by the growth/dissolution of nanoscale metal filaments in the dielectric. ECM cells have been demonstrated with high performance down to the size of 20 nm. However, the continuous downward scaling of ECM cell is currently hindered by the process complexity of ultra-small and high-aspect-ratio contact plug/via. To enable an ECM cell to scale down below 10 nm, we propose the use of a graphene nanopore structure and a low-ion-mobility dielectric to localize the formation/rupture of the metal filaments. The geometric “pore” size of the hexagonal lattice in graphene is only 0.064 nm (less than the radius of a Cu atom (0.14 nm)), leading to a high impermeability level of graphene against atom and ion migration. The graphene nanopore only allows metallic species to pass through the sub-nanoscale holes. In the low-ion-mobility dielectric, ion transport becomes a rate-limiting factor. The shape and diameter of the metal filaments can be controlled with the appropriate combinations of ion migration, oxidation/reduction rates, and compliance current. We will firstly insert a graphene barrier at the metal/dielectric interface to completely impede the migration of metallic species into the dielectric. We will use a few-layer graphene to avoid the migration of metallic species through the intrinsic defects in a monolayer graphene. Electrical and elemental characterizations will be conducted to analyze the migration at different electrical/thermal stressing conditions. Secondly, we will prepare graphene nanopores through either electron-beam drilling or ultraviolet treatment, and sandwich them at the metal/dielectric interface to localize the source for the formation/rupture of metal filaments in the ECM cell. The effective size of the active electrode is confined to sub-nanoscale holes. Our objective is to scale down the effective electrode size to below 10 nm. Finally, we will use an ultra-thin Cu electrode to limit the Cu source, and investigate the minimum Cu source that ensures the stable resistance switching of an ECM. 對金屬/介質界面之間的理解是納米電子學及其相關領域的一個重要話題，金屬/介質界面之間的互相擴散以及存在於電子器件中的熱或者電應力使得該界面非常復雜。金屬在介質中的擴散會導致介質可靠性的降低，也會通過在介質中形成或者斷裂金屬絲來構造電化學金屬化存儲器。目前最小的電化學金屬化存儲器為20納米，為了持續縮小其到10納米以下，我們提出使用石墨烯納米孔結構和低離子遷移率的介質來形成存儲器。

25200614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200614.value: Long bus queues have been observed at busy multi-berth bus stops in many cities in the world. These bus queues are formed due to: the mutual blockage between those buses that are dwelling simultaneously in different berths of the stop; chaotic bus entry/exit maneuvers at the stop; and influences of nearby mixed traffic and signalized intersections. This state of affairs degrades the overall performance of bus systems, and thus discourages travelers from using public transit. Even worse, the bus queues might create bottlenecks for adjacent car traffic. The matter can be remedied by efficiently designing and managing congested bus stops. To this end, we propose to formulate analytical models for estimating bus discharge capacities and bus delays at stops under three operating scenarios: i) where bus operations at the stop are isolated from the influence of nearby signalized intersections and other (e.g. car) traffic; ii) where bus operations at the stop are affected by a nearby signalized intersection located either upstream or downstream of the stop; and iii) where bus entry/exit maneuvers at the stop interact with other traffic in an adjacent mixed-traffic lane. For the last scenario, the impact of the stop will be assessed for both bus and car traffic. The models will be developed using the Markovian properties embedded in the stochastic bus queueing process at a stop, and other techniques in queueing theory; and for wide ranges of operating conditions, including bus arrival rate, distribution of bus dwell time, bus drivers’ behavior, traffic state in the adjacent road section, and traffic signal timing at neighboring intersections. These models will be further enhanced to explore bus-stop operating strategies and real-time control schemes that can reduce bus queueing and delays. The results will be used to formulate guidelines to assist practitioners in choosing better designs, management policies, and control strategies for mitigating bus-stop congestion. The models will be applied to examine real cases of congested bus stops in Hong Kong and other cities. Possible remedies for the case studies will be proposed and examined. 在许多城市中，公交车往往在繁忙的多泊位站台前排成长队。公交车排队的主要原因是：1）停靠于不同泊位的公交车相互之间发生阻挡；2）公交车进出站所造成的混乱；3）站台附近其他车流与信号交叉口的影响。这种排队现象严重影响了公交系统的服务水平，从而降低了公交对于出行者的吸引力。更为严重的是，公交站台排队往往形成交通瓶颈，从而影响到其他车辆的行驶。 为解决这一问题，需要更有效地设计与管理繁忙公交站台。为此目的，本研究项目将研发用以计算公交站台的公交车通行能力和排队延误的理论模型。理论模型将讨论以下三种情形：1）孤立站台，即站台附近的公交车行为不受信号交叉口和其他车流的影响；2）受到邻近信号交叉口影响的公交站台；3）公交车进出站行为受到其他车流影响的站台。对于第三种情形，模型将同时评估站台对于公交车和其他车流的影响。模型的建立将基于公交车的随机排队过程中隐含的马尔可夫过程。该模型可用于研究一般情形下多种系统运行参数（包括公交车到达流量、停靠时间分布、司机行为、附近交通流状态、交通信号参数等）对于公交站台排队的影响。基于这一理论模型，我们将进一步研究公交站台运营管理策略（包括实时控制策略）对于减小公交排队延误的作用。理论模型与管理策略的研究结果将为繁忙公交站台的设计与管理提供指导。最后，模型将被应用于研究香港与其他城市的多泊位繁忙公交站台，并提出缓解公交车站台拥堵的方案。

25200614.label: Realisation of objectives
25200614.value: Regarding Objective 1. We have conducted several fruitful research tasks, some of which are moderately deviated from the original proposal. We believe these moderate deviations are necessary since the real research work and achievements cannot perfectly match the original proposal due to the uncertainty and exploratory nature of research work in general. The tasks completed in this project are detailed as follows: - On bus stop queueing. We have completed and nearly completed three papers and one master thesis regarding: i) bus discharge capacities and delays for isolated stops with various queue disciplines, berth numbers, etc.; ii) analytical approximation of bus discharge capacities of stops near signalized intersections; iii) efficient methods for allocating berths to various bus lines in a multi-berth stop; and iv) operations of congested multi-berth stops where buses need to merge into the general traffic at the stop exit. Note that these four research tasks are closely related to Objective 1 stated in the original proposal. Among the three papers, one is under review by a top journal in Transportation Engineering; one was presented at an international conference and a revised version is ready for submission to a top journal; and the last one is almost ready for submission to another top journal. The master thesis is also ready to be converted to a journal submission but due to the limited time we have not yet done so. - In addition, we also investigated the vessel (specifically, oil tanker) queues at busy ports. Although not stated in the original proposal, this queueing system is similar to multi-berth bus stops and can be studied using a similar approach. The findings are however very different. Another paper on this topic was presented at an international conference and is ready to be submitted to a journal. - We also investigated vehicle queues formed at drop-off areas of large transportation terminals (e.g. rail stations and airports). The system also shares some similarities with the bus stop queueing system. Another paper is near completion. Regarding Objective 2. - On bus stop queueing and bunching, the PI has supervised three master theses on: i) operations of congested multi-berth stops where buses need to merge into the general traffic at the stop exit (note that this is also related to Objective 1); ii) adaptive bus control considering random passenger arrivals; and iii) adaptive bus control considering random passenger arrivals and bus-departure-based boarding policy. These works are closely aligned with Objective 2; i.e., they investigated control methods and strategies for mitigating bus queueing or bunching, which are built upon the novel sensoring or connected vehicle technology. The first master thesis will be converted to a journal submission; and the latter two will be combined to be part of another journal submission under preparation. - In addition, we also investigated how to better control passenger queues when they board large airplanes. Basically, how various boarding policies perform, and what is the optimal boarding policy for various airplane sizes and layouts. This may not be using advanced technologies, but it still belongs to the board area of congestion-mitigation strategies for transportation queueing systems (note the similarity between passenger queues for airplane boarding and the bus queues at busy stops). A paper is also under preparation. Regarding Objective 3. We have explored the real-world cases of Cross-Harbour Tunnel bus stops (both southbound and northbound). These two bus stops are among the busiest in Hong Kong. In particular, the northbound stop is a near-side stop where buses have to merge into the general traffic at the stop exit; thus it combines the features of a busy multi-berth stop near signalized intersection and a merge to the general traffic. During the course of project, the PI supervised 10 undergraduate student Final Year Projects (some of those students were also hired as undergraduate student helpers) studying different aspects of the stops (data collection and analysis, driver behaviour analysis, simulation, congestion mitigation strategies, etc.) With their help, the graduate students and research staff obtained good quality data for calibrating simulation models and testing various strategies. We now have much better understandings of the queue mechanism and the causes of congestion at those stops, and will complete 1-2 papers on these real case studies in the near future. Regarding Objective 4. Guidelines for advising the practice of design, management, and control of busy stops were summarized in the aforementioned papers and theses. Examples of these guidelines include: i) allowing overtaking almost always yields higher capacity; ii) that a far-side stop has a smaller capacity than a near-side one given all the other conditions equal; iii) that far-side stops placed immediately downstream of an intersection is a very bad design from the perspective of bus capacity; iv) that simply allocating bus lines to berths by keeping the so-called “load factor” equal among the berths would yield nearly the lowest bus delay; and v) that the previous uniform-passenger-arrival based control would be ineffective and even invalid when the passenger arrivals are random.

25200614.label: Major findings and research outcome
25200614.value: Major findings: - Allowing overtaking generally increases capacity; allowing overtaking for exiting buses is more efficient than for entering buses. Allowing overtaking for exiting buses is always better than the no-overtaking rule (this is at odds with a previous study). - The capacity loss due to the nearby signal drops rapidly as the distance between signal and stop grows. Our models can be used to determine the appropriate distance between the intersection and the stop. - Practitioners may consider decreasing the signal cycle length while keeping the green ratio unchanged. This would increase a near- or far-side stop’s capacity without affecting the general traffic by much. - A near-side stop always produces a higher capacity than a far-side one, should other conditions be the same. But the advantage of near-side stops diminishes as the distance between signal and stop increases. - Allowing overtaking still results in higher capacity than the no-overtaking rule for stops near signals. But the benefit decreases as the distance between stop and signal increases. - . For multi-berth stops with no-overtaking rule, evenly distributing bus lines to berths with equal “load factor” (which is defined as the bus arrival rate divided by the the service rate), i.e., the “naïve policy”, yields an acceptable heuristic, with an optimality gap less than 10% for most cases. The policy is much more efficient than the methods proposed in the literature. However, for other queueing rules, the gap will be larger. - We proposed a new randomized searching algorithm for better allocating bus lines to berths, which yields better allocations and still more efficient than existing algorithms. - Under random passenger arrivals, longer slacks are needed to regulate the bus headways and avoid bunching. - Control applied when bus is ready to go (after loading and unloading passengers) performs slightly better than control applied upon bus arrivals to stops. - For vessel queues, serial bottlenecks exist regarding both the number of berths and the nagivation channel capacity. Using a buffer to increase the nagivation channel capacity would be a good strategy. - For taxi queues in one-lane drop-off area, we propose multiple strategies to improve the lane’s discharge capacity. - For flight boarding policy, “back-to-front” can sometimes be near optimal (which is very different from previous studies). Research outcomes include five papers (and a few more in preparation), three master theses (all attached in Part C), and one ongoing PhD thesis (expected in 2019).

25200614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25200614.value: - Complete the ongoing papers and manage to publish them on suitable journals. - Continue to examine bus queueing operations at the stop level and the corridor level when passenger queueing and boarding process are incorporated into the models. We discovered an unexpected effect that can significantly influence the bus-stop capacity and bus queueing. We intend to study the joint effect of bus queueing and bus bunching in this respect. - Complete the real-world case studies on Cross-Harbour-Tunnel bus stops and other special, complicated bus stops. Our focus will be on: i) the stop designs; ii) driver behaviour and its impact; and iii) control strategies. - Study unconventional stop designs, e.g. a large stop consisting of pairs of berths back-to-back. - Examine how signal control can be integrated to improve bus operations reliability and reduce bus queueing. We will further examine connected buses and their control strategies for improving the capacity, reliability, efficiency, and safety of bus operations. - Extend our present studies on vessel queues at ports, vehicle queues in drop-off lanes, passenger boarding queues for flights, etc. We will apply for new proposals regarding some of the above topics.

25200614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25200614.value: We examined how buses form queues at congested bus stops, especially how the bus and passenger delays are related to the design of the stop, bus operations, driver behavior, and surrounding traffic infrastructure (e.g. traffic signals) and vehicle traffic. We obtain findings that can guide the practice regarding design, management, and control of bus stops and bus operations at stops. We also investigated real bus stop cases such as the Cross-Harbour-Tunnel bus stops and how to mitigate congestion at those stops. In addition, we also examined similar queues in transportation sector, including: queues of taxis and vehicles that drop off passengers at airports or large rail terminals, queues of vessels at busy ports, and queues of passengers boarding a flight. Useful practical guidelines on improving the efficiency and reducing the queueing delays have been obtained.

25200714.label: Project Objectives
25200714.value: Development of mathematical traffic models to adequately capture the time and space dynamics of realistic vehicular traffic and communication capability in urban environments, so that network connectivity and various communication performances can be readily computed given the vehicular velocity statistics. Design of information aggregation and dissemination techniques based on the velocity dynamic for efficient delivery of connectivity and various performance profiles to vehicles for real-time VANET optimization. Design of cross-layer communication protocols that exploit the dynamics and future predicted evolution of connectivity and communication capabilities to provide energy-efficient high-data-rate communications for enabling real-time applications in VANETs. Development of a realistic VANET simulation platform and collection of real-world traffic data to facilitate the validation and evaluation of the developed design methodologies, communication algorithms and networking functions.
