25200714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200714.value: 發展中國家不斷增長的汽車數量無疑會帶來更嚴重的交通擠塞、空氣污染和能源損耗、以至交通意外和傷亡。車載通信網絡，作為智能運輸系統中負責無線通信的重要一員，在改善交通安全和效率，及減低交通擠塞和汽車排放上，將扮演著一個重要的角色。在這項目中，我們會勾劃如何利用經驗性的汽車速度數據來開發更真實的交通及通信連接度模型，以優化城市環境中的車載網絡設計。 車載通信網絡中最具挑戰性的是難以預測的車輛移動以致不斷改變的網絡拓撲。但是，我們卻缺乏對車輛移動與通信連接度之間的互動的根本理解。因此，普遍的通信協定設計都是啟發式的，難以克服移動環境中的無線電條件。本計劃最主要的目標是要建立一個全新的車載通信網絡設計與優化框架。初部重點是透過開發數學交通模型研究城市中車輛移動與通信性能的關連，然後跟據不同地點的網絡連接度更有效地設計跨網絡層面的通訊演算法和網絡功能。最終目的是優化車載通信網絡以達致能運行實時應用的省能的、高數據量的傳送。 跟據項目負責人對車載網絡、無線通信演算法、及無線內嵌式系統的研究的經驗，我們打算透過開發理論模型及設計方案以建立研究下一代車載通信協定和功能的理論性框架。本研究結果將會打開跨學科研究的機會以實現未來的巨大車載通信平台，改善高密度城市的交通安全和效率，以及為不斷增加的移動設備和越來越複雜的通信要求提供無處不在的通信連接。

25200714.label: Realisation of objectives
25200714.value: With regard to Objective 1 (development of mathematical traffic models), we have developed the 802.11p broadcasting and unicasting models based on Markov chain and interference models to characterize the communication performance of 802.11p Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) under heterogeneous urban traffic with signal control [1 – 3]. The broadcasting model [1] can be easily incorporated into the stochastic traffic models so that we can readily predict the network performance (e.g., throughput and delay) at different locations on the road according to the given vehicular velocity statistics. Such model was further extended to characterize unicast performance with the exponential backoff and re-transmission mechanism in the MAC layer with a two-dimensional Markov chain model [2, 3]. Specifically, we found that the impact of the contention window size in the MAC protocol on transmission delay is significantly different in the broadcast and unicast modes, which provides insights into our study of cross-layer optimization of the protocol in Objective 3. With regard to Objective 2 (design of efficient information aggregation and dissemination techniques), we have surveyed inter-flow network coding (XNC) in [4] that considers encoding packets from different flows in a wireless network with either reliable or lossy links. The results can be applied to data encoding and dissemination in a VANET for optimization and various application services. The use of fountain code (rateless code) for sensor data dissemination in urban area with obstacles and buildings was studied in [5]. Machine learning methods were applied to better characterize different driving behaviors and patterns to optimize the data dissemination [6]. In addition, we have investigated a sub-class of network coding in VANET called index coding based on the mobility patterns of vehicles for efficient dissemination of 3D point cloud road map data from LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) for autonomous navigation [7]. The purpose is to minimize the overall number of transmissions for disseminating traffic and road information from road-side units (RSUs) to vehicles in the network based on the availability of side information. Such technique can be applied to practical transportation problems, for example, the toll gate selection problem for improving server utilization and reducing vehicle waiting time as studied in [8]. It also leads to interesting RSU deployment problem in VANETs for balancing the load of various road-side fog nodes [9]. Moreover, software-defined networking technology can be applied to VANETs for better quality of service (QoS) guarantee and facilitating various network optimization and functionalities. In [10], we proposed a two-layer hierarchical architecture called software-defined vehicular ad-hoc networks (SDVN) with road-side units in the lower layer controlling vehicles passing by and a super controller in the top layer controlling the road-side units. For the design of cross-layer communication protocols in Objective 3, we have considered in [3] the cross-layer optimization of 802.11p through power control (PHY layer) and contention window adjustment (MAC layer). The optimal transmission range and contention window size at different locations are derived based on the spatio-temporal velocity profile and are made known to entering vehicles. These aid the vehicles to configure their transmission power and rate accordingly upon entering a road segment. We have evaluated the proposed system in terms of the network delay and throughput performance, and our results indicate that delay was improved by about 53% on average for homogeneous traffic and 45% on average for heterogeneous traffic. In the network layer, we have proposed a solution called store-carry-cooperative forward (SCCF) routing with information epidemics control in [11]. It aims to solve long delivery delay problem and information epidemic problem for opportunistic networks like VANETs where the lack of infrastructure, high mobility, unstable link connectivity, fading, and obstacle-constrained environments are the major concerns on the data delivery performance. To provide energy-efficient high-data-rate communications in VANETs with respect to Objective 3, the feasibility of harnessing wireless interference in a VANET through physical-layer network coding (PNC) or other related interference management and mitigation techniques was studied [12, 13]. Specifically, we evaluated the performance degradation in PNC due to Doppler shift (or rapid vehicle movements), and we proved that PNC works in highly-mobile environments like VANETs in principle. With the introduction of advanced carrier frequency offset (CFO) compensation methods and signal detection techniques based on joint channel estimation and signal detection with expectation maximization (EM) and belief propagation (BP) in time-frequency-selective channels [13, 14] respectively, the data rate performance can be further boosted. In addition, a more comprehensive version of channel-coded PNC with joint signal detection and channel decoding for addressing the CFO problem in OFDM modulated PNC was studied in [15]. These can adequately address the problem of short contact time in VANETs and significantly improve the transmission data rate for real-time applications. Overall, we conclude that the three objectives stated in the research proposal were adequately addressed throughout these three years. For sure, the research outcome of this project will foster new research directions for further studies in VANETs in the near future. Publications [1] H. J. Qiu, I. W.-H. Ho, C. K. Tse, Y. 25200714.label: Major findings and research outcome
25200714.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1. We have developed the 802.11p broadcasting and unicasting models based on Markov chain and interference models to characterize the communication performance of 802.11p Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) under heterogeneous urban traffic with signal control [1 – 3] 2. We have investigated network coding techniques (e.g., inter-flow network coding, fountain code, index coding, etc.), RSU deployment schemes, and software-defined networking for efficient data dissemination in VANETs [4 – 10] 3. We have proposed cross-layer optimization algorithms based on the 802.11p broadcasting and unicasting models, as well as a network layer solution based on store-carry-cooperative forward routing with information epidemics control [3, 11] 4. We have explored the feasibility of physical-layer network coding (PNC) in VANETs, and proposed joint channel estimation and signal decoding schemes for tackling the time-frequency-selective channel in highly-mobile vehicular networks [12 – 15] Overall, the major findings and research outcome were published in six journal papers and nine conference papers.

25200714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25200714.value: The mathematical traffic and protocol models can be easily extended to more complicated road topologies by superimposing multiple road segments. Further protocol parameters in different network layers (e.g., carrier-sensing threshold, transmission rate, etc.) can also be optimized under the proposed modeling framework. The data dissemination problem via index coding studied can be further extended to a city-wide urban scenario through the investigation of empirical mobility traces. It can also be integrated with various fog computing techniques to better manage the resources (e.g., transmission bandwidth, computational resources, etc.) at fog nodes (e.g., road-side units, base stations). For dissemination of 3D point cloud road map data for autonomous navigation, the processing of 3D point cloud data (e.g., source coding, hashing) should also be further considered to better address the bandwidth and delay requirements for autonomous driving services. For PNC in VANETs, it can be further extended to support non-orthogonal multiple access in a dense vehicular network (e.g., at busy road junctions) via incorporating respective multi-user detection and PHY and MAC layer bridging techniques. Finally, the practical performance of the proposed schemes and algorithms should be verified through real-world V2X experiments with software-defined radio platforms, which is within our future research agenda.

25200714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25200714.value: In this research project, we have developed the methodologies to characterize the performance of vehicular communication protocols in highly-dynamic vehicular networks. This also provides the ground for various network optimizations at different network layers. In addition, various techniques were proposed to facilitate the data dissemination in vehicle networks based on the mobility patterns of vehicles, and we have proposed advanced methods to harness wireless interference in vehicular networks for real-time applications. The developed models and design methodologies are expected to lay the theoretical framework for the investigation of next generation vehicular communication protocols and networking functions. The research outcome will also open up inter-disciplinary research opportunities for realizing a giant vehicular communication platform in the future that enhances safety and efficiency of transport systems in highly congested cities, and provides ubiquitous communication connectivity to an increasing and diverse number of devices and complex user requirements.

25200914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200914.value: In recent years, due to the increased global travels and globalization, the speed of spread of communicable diseases has been increased. Recent reports of human-human transmission of the virulent H7N9 strain of influenza led to tremendous public concern. While keeping the public informed is an effective way to prevent the potentially-disastrous large-scale outbreaks, faster, more accurate, and more reliable biosensors would allow earlier detection of pathogens and facilitate the management of communicable diseases. A key component of a reliable biosensor is the detection technique. Over the past two decades, a lot of research effort has been devoted to develop a variety of approaches. Among them, plasmonic based sensing techniques have emerged as a practical approach with high detection sensitivity. Plasmonics refers to the oscillation of free electrons in metals such as gold and silver. In resonant condition, collective oscillation of charge carriers produces strong absorbance and scattering of light, which is very sensitive to the surrounding environment. Biomolecular interactions with such substrates can be detected and monitored by observing the changes in their optical properties (absorbance and scattering of light). However, the detection sensitivity achieved with these methods remains unsatisfactory for some applications, such as DNA or virus detections. The cost for producing disposable gold and silver substrates is also high that makes the biosensor less common in the community. To address these issues, in this proposal, a new plasmonic material will be synthesized and employed. We propose a copper-based semiconductor nanocrystal structure in which the resonant condition is supported by another regime (oscillation of free holes). Studies have shown that the optical properties of these nanocrystals are also very sensitive to the surrounding medium, as well as to the concentration of free holes. By taking the advantages of this “additional” effect, a new sensing mechanism is proposed to enhance the detection sensitivity. As the new material is copper-based, which is an abundant element, the production cost can be drastically reduced. The proposed new sensing mechanism will be verified theoretically and experimentally. Ultimately a portable prototype will be developed and tested with standard biomolecular samples. The outcomes of this project will benefit public health through the development of new biosensor technology, will advance fundamental science through improved understanding of these new materials, and will benefit society through the training of students in the important and expanding fields of bio-nanotechnology, materials chemistry, and nanophotonics. 近年來，隨著經濟貿易全球化進程的發展，人員流動加劇，傳染病傳播速度也越來越快，波及範圍也越來越廣。近期“人傳人”H7N9型致命禽流感的報導引起社會的強烈關注。及時確診和報告新增病例能有效預防疾病的大規模爆發。因此，研發快速準確可靠的生物傳感器，早期檢測診斷出病原體，對疾病的預防與控制有著重大意義。 生物傳感器的可靠性很大部分決定於它的檢測技術。在過去的二十年中，對新型檢測技術的開發已經有了許多進展。在眾多的技術手段中，基於表面等離子效應的檢測技術以其獨特的高靈敏度使它成為最具開發潛力的檢測手段。表面等離子效應實質是金屬（金、銀）表面的自由電子共振產生的現象。在共振條件下，載流子的集體振盪對光產生強烈的吸收和散射，並且這個現像對周圍環境的變化非常敏感。因此加入具有這種特性的材料，生物分子之間的相互作用就能夠通過載流子對光效應（散射和吸收）的變化檢測和觀測。然而，在檢測像DNA和病毒這些應用中，表面等離子共振檢測技術的靈敏度卻有待改進。而且製作金銀基底的表面等離子共振檢測生物傳感器價格比較昂貴使得它的普及也受到局限。 因此，本項目的目的就是要降低表面等離子共振檢測生物傳感器的造價。為此我們將合成一種新型的能產生表面等離子共振的材料。它是一種以銅為基底的半導體納米晶體，而它的等離子效應不同於金銀，而是由空穴提供的。許多研究表明，這類晶體的光學特性對周圍介質和空穴數量都非常敏感。由於這個“附加”特性，一種新的傳感機制可能被應用於增加靈敏度。此外，由於銅元素非常豐富，所以這種以銅為基底的新型傳感器造價將會大大降低。而它的新型傳感機制也將會在理論和實驗中被印證。最終，這種生物傳感器的簡易模型將會被用於開發和測試生物分子樣品。 本項目的研究將產生如下積極意義：通過研發新型生物傳感器將有利於公共衛生事業的發展；通過提高對新材料的認識將促進基礎科學的進步； 通過培養新一代人掌握生物納米技術、材料化學科學和納米光學技術等前沿學科將推動整個社會的發展。

25200914.label: Realisation of objectives
25200914.value: Objective 1, 2 and 3 have been achieved by developing a millifluidic approach for synthesizing copper based nanocrystals (Cu2- xE) with different shapes and sizes using a homemade device. Conventionally, shape control of nanocrystals was accomplished using a surfactant-controlled approach, where directional growth is facilitated by selective passivation of a particular facet of the nanocrystals using surfactants. We demonstrate a “surfactant-free” approach where different sizes and shapes (i.e. spherical, triangular prism and rod) of plasmonic copper sulfide (Cu2-xS) nanocrystals can be fabricated by adjusting the flow rate and precursor concentrations. As millifluidic systems enable precise control of reaction temperatures, mixing processes, reaction times, and precursors’ stoichiometries, they serve as excellent incubation environments for controllable growth of particles. Transmission electron microscope (TEM), fast fourier transmission (FFT) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) techniques were used to characterize the as-synthesized nanocrystals and revealed that structures ranging from copper-deficient covellite (CuS), spionkopite (Cu1.39S), roxbyite (Cu1.75S), to copper-rich djurleite (Cu1.94S). The localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) peak of the nanocrystals can be tuned from 1115 to 1644nm by simply varying the Cu:S molar ratio and flow rate settings of the millifluidic device. In this work, we found that on-chip fabrication could provide a more precise control of the reaction time. This is a crucial parameter in obtaining the desired sizes of nanocrystals as the reaction can be quenched desirably after propagating through a certain length of channel. More interestingly, in our continuous flow regime, the system was open and no specific “de-gassing” progress and high temperature were required. To fabricate the millifluidic chip, a 3D printer from PP3DP was applied to print the mould of 3D channels followed by pouring pre-mixed polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) into the mold. The PDMS was then cured at 65 °C for 4 hours. Finally, the PDMS was carefully bonded to a glass slide and connected with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tubes. This homemade device consists of four ports (two precursor inlets, an ethanol inlet and an outlet for collection) and housing five different sections. Then copper (I) chloride was dissolved in oleylamine and sulfur source was dissolved in oleic acid. Both of them were heated at 120 °C with stirring. By using a syringe pump, the precursor solutions were simultaneously injected into the millifluidic chip which was placed on a pre-heated hot plate at 120°C. The winding path was designed for precursors mixing and initializing the nucleation process. It was followed by the growth of Cu2-xS along the channel and the nanocrystals were subsequently quenched at the final stage by ethanol. The purified nanocrystals were redispersed in chloroform. This approach is more environmental friendly because less toxic chemicals such as oleic acid and oleylamine were used in the synthesis. Another direct aqueous phase synthesis of Cu2-xS nanocrystals was also developed to address Objective 1, 2 and 3. By using low-molecular-weight poly-ethylenimine (PEI) as the reducing and capping agent, other than the size, the shape of Cu2-xS nanocrystals can also be controlled with lengths from 6.5 nm to 46.5 nm and the aspect ratio from 2.2 to 7.5 by adjusting the concentration of PEI. The LSPR (plasmonic) peak of Cu2-xS exhibits a red-shift (from 1145 nm to 1369 nm) when the length increases from 6.5 nm to 44.5nm due to the variation of free hole. Finely control the size and morphology of Cu2-xS nanostructures is of great importance in specific applications. Various reports have described the methods for synthesizing a variety of Cu2-xS nanoparticles. For example, Cu2-xS nanoparticles were synthesized by injecting sulfur precursors into Cu-O organic solution at 210-220℃ with strict oxygen free environment. To obtain rod-shaped Cu2-xS nanocrystals, one research group replaced Cd element on cadmium sulfide nanorods with Cu element through cation exchange method. To synthesize copper sulfide nanorods, very toxic chemicals such as trioctylphosphine oxide (TOPO) and octadecene (ODE) should be used as with surface ligands with accurate temperature control in reactions. As mentioned above, our group has reported a non-aqueous millifluidic approach for fabricating a variety of Cu2-xS nanostructures by adjusting the concentration of precursors and flow rates to reduce the environmental impact. It can be observed that varying the size and shape of nanoparticles is relatively easy to achieve in organic phase synthesis. In organic phase synthesis, the use of high temperature and highly concentrated surfactants solution, and the large variety of surfactants, that can passivate specific crystal faces, can facilitate anisotropic growth of nanocrystals, resulting in complex nanostructures. However, the use organic solvent and high concentration of organic ligands are not very environmental friendly. In our developed protocol, Cu2-xS nanocrystals were synthesized by employing low-molecular-weight branched PEI as reducing and capping agent. Copper chloride and sodium sulfide were employed as copper source and sulfur source, respectively. The nucleation and growth processes were proceeded at 85℃, followed by incubation in an ice bath. Typically, PEI solution was prepared in a required concentration, copper chloride powders were dissolved in PEI aqueous solution under stirring. The solution was blue color. Freshly prepared sodium sulfide solution was then added dropwise until the color turned red-brown. The mixture was then sonicated for 10 minutes and subsequently incubated in 85℃ water baths for another 10 minutes. The color of solution changed from red-brown to dark-green, indicating the formation of Cu2-xS nanocrystals. The samples were centrifuged with acetone and dialyzes with double distilled water. This approach is more “green” because only some metal salts, low-MW PEI and low temperature were used. To achieve Objective 4, a plasmonic quenching effect was demonstrated by the use of o-phenylendiamine (OPD). OPD is a compound which emitted yellow fluorescence (568 nm) when it was oxidized (electrons donator) by the Cu₂-xS nanocrystals (electrons acceptor). As the concentration of OPD increased, more Cu₂-xS nanocrystals were quenched and the fluorescence was enhanced, therefore the plasmonic quenching effect could be observed. It was shown that the LSPR of Cu₂-xS nanocrystals was quenched effectively as the ratio of Cu₂-xS nanocrystals to OPD increased from 0.003 to 600. Besides, the fluorescence was enhanced from 0.2 × 10³ to 1.1 × 10⁶ by distinct morphologies and compositions of Cu₂-xS nanocrystals. All Cu₂-xS nanocrystals / OPD samples showed that the enhancement was optimized when the ratio reached 0.3. The results showed a satisfying signal-to-noise ratio and sensing capability, revealing the potential for the future development of the Cu₂-xS based nanosensor.

25200914.label: Major findings and research outcome
25200914.value: Major Fundings: 1. A millifluidic approach was developed for synthesizing copper based nanocrystals (Cu2- xE) with different shapes and sizes using a homemade device. We demonstrated a “surfactant-free” approach where different sizes and shapes (i.e. spherical, triangular prism and rod) of plasmonic copper sulfide (Cu2-xS) nanocrystals can be fabricated by adjusting the flow rate and precursor concentrations, instead of using very toxic surfactants in the traditional synthesis (Research 1, 2 and 3 in Part C). 2. A direct aqueous phase synthesis of Cu2-xS was also developed to synthesize Cu2- xS with different shapes, sizes and high monodispersity. The use of low-molecular-weight poly-ethylenimine (PEI) as the reducing and capping agent allows us to control the morphology by varying the concentration. This approach is more environmental friendly because only metal salts, low-MW PEI and low temperature were used. (Manuscript in preparation) 3. A plasmonic quenching effect was demonstrated by the use of o-phenylendiamine (OPD). We found that a small variation of carrier density will lead to a significant shift in the LSPR peak. Therefore, the sensitivity enhancement was optimized when the ratio of Cu₂-xS nanocrystals / OPD reached 0.3. (Ref: Master of Philology thesis of Cheung Tai-Lok, student of PI)

25200914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25200914.value: Potential for Further Development: The synthesis, LSPR properties and sensing capability of copper based nanocrystals have been comprehensively studied in this project. As we found that a small variation of carrier density will lead to a significant shift in the LSPR peak, one of the future research directions could be a design and fabrication of plasmonic hetero-nanostructures. By using the interaction between two different plasmonic regimes (i.e. electrons and holes), the number of free hole carriers can be manipulated by growing hetero-nanostructures with metallic nanoparticles. When an electron rich moiety contacts with the sensing substrate, the vacancies in the sensing substrate will be filled by electrons from the donor moiety, decreasing the number of free holes in the semiconductor and creating an additional red shift and damping of the LSPR peak. Through this mechanism, the detection sensitivity can be potentially enhanced.

25200914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25200914.value: In this project, the researchers have developed a high sensitivity sensing technique based on nanotechnology. The technique can be applied in creating a range of test kits for public health. For example, the developed sensing substrates can be modified with bio-molecules that can be specified to particular biomarkers in our body. When the biomarkers are in contact with the sensing substrate, it will change the properties of nanoparticles and the signal can be detected by a simple color analyzer. A rapid assay can then be developed and incorporated with portable devices. The technology developed in this project will be suitable for both point of care and biomedical applications.

25201114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201114.value: Developing biorefinery techniques to convert biomass into sustainable fuels is an environmentally progressive way in mitigating global climate changes. The technology has recently shown to be applicable in converting high recalcitrant feedstock into bioethanol; and can be useful in supporting the treatment of municipal solid waste in large cities, i.e., Hong Kong. The urban-generated wood product waste has not been widely investigated as other lignocellulosic biomass feedstock, but has great economic and environmental potentials: the collection and transportation networks of the feedstock are well-established in the cities, and more supporting facilities are available. The challenges of using municipal solid waste for bioethanol production are of the inconsistent qualities of the feedstock. Municipal wood product waste is composed of different wood species and various types of functional polymers (i.e., formaldehyde-based resin, and polyvinyl-acetate resin), which are used in the coatings or adhesives for wood processing. The polymers may change the physicochemical characteristics of the lignocellulosic structure during thermochemical pretreatment and affect the performances of hydrolysis and fermentation. They may also result in higher amount or different types of pretreatment by-products (i.e., free formaldehyde), which may reduce the efficiency of the biorefinery and/or become a potential source of wastewater. In this study, a series of experimental and modeling works are proposed to clarify the hypotheses and to overcome the stated challenges. Synthetic wood flour-polymer mixtures and wood product waste generated from different wood-plastic products (i.e., plywood and fiberboard) will be pretreated by using the state-of-the-art pretreatment processes (i.e., SPORL) in bench-reactors. The effects of the wood-processing functional polymers to the surface properties of the lignocellulosic structure will be analyzed by monitoring the changes of roughness (using atomic force microscopy), water retention time, chemical composition, and cellulose accessibility to cellulase, and compare with the substrate enzymatic digestibilities. The inhibiting effects of the pretreatment by-products to enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation will be tested on a commercial cellulase cocktail (i.e., CTec2) and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The reaction kinetics and inhibiting coefficients will be measured and used to develop new biological model. A two-stage biological process, which has never been used in biorefinery studies, will be applied to simultaneously remove the inhibitors and enrich the yeast for high solid saccharification and fermentation. The finding of this study can benefit higher education by extending the existing pretreatment severity model to predict delignification and generation of the inhibitors; and to clarify the mechanisms of growth inhibition. 研發新的生物煉製技術將生物質轉化為可持續燃料是延緩全球氣候暖化的一大課題。應用這項生物技術不僅可以將高頑抗的生物質轉化為生物燃料，亦可減少城市（如香港）固體廢棄物的負擔。此外，相較於森林或農業廢棄物，城市木材廢棄物蘊藏著巨大的經濟和環境潛力: 城市廢棄物的收集和運輸網路多已完備，且城市中有完善的配套設施（如電力與污染處理），可符合生物煉製在經濟與環境上的需求。 轉化城市固體廢棄物最大的挑戰主要來自這些原料成分的不一致性。城市木材廢棄物由不同種類的木材品種組成。這些木材多含有不同種功能的高分子聚合物（如酚醛樹脂或聚醋酸乙烯樹脂）這些聚合物在木材加工過程中被用作塗料和膠黏劑，且在預處理過程中可能會改變木質纖維素的結構，進而影響後續水解和發酵的效果。另外也可能在預處理過程中產生更多副產物（如游離甲醛），這些副產物不僅會降低生物煉製技術的效率，亦可能成為城市廢水的潛在來源。 本研究設計了一系列的實驗以論證上述假設、克服相關問題、並配合文獻資料建立理論根基。將不同木粉-聚合物混合物的木塑產品（如膠合板和纖維板）和木材產品廢棄物，經預處理後對各種功能性高分子聚合物與木質纖維素材料表面性能的影響進行探討。採用的材料表徵方法包括表面粗糙度（以原子力顯微鏡測定）水分保留度、化學成分、酶的可及性和底物的轉化率等。針對商用酵素水解和釀酒酵母的發酵效率表徵預處理副產物對酶水解和發酵的抑製作用。測定反應動力學常數和抑制常數以建立生物模型。此外，本研究將採一新生物過程對高固同步糖化發酵進行測試。運用建立的預處理模型預測木素去除和副產物的產生，闡明抑制物產生的機理作為未來教學、研究與產業化的基礎。

25201114.label: Realisation of objectives
25201114.value: The research progresses follow well with the set targets as in the proposed research plans and are summarized as follows: Task 1 – Feedstock and Substrate Analysis (accomplished) In order to better understand the current situation of woody product wastes in Hong Kong we selected and analyzed the characteristics of five major woody products wastes (e.g., formwork and wooden pallet) collected by the recycler. The chemical and physical characteristics of different wood wastes were analyzed to assess their chemical compositions, the energy and trace metal contents, and compared with coal. The experiment results showed that all the collected woody product wastes contain only small amount of artificial adhesives, resins, preservatives, paints, and heavy metals. The impacts of the contaminants are less significant than expected. With the information of the physical and chemical composition analysis, the environmental impacts of using recycled wood wastes for wood pellets biofuel was assessed by conducting a lifecycle assessment. It was demonstrated that the caloric values of the wood wastes samples were only slightly lower than the reference coal, and have much lower ash contents. The overall concentrations of heavy metals in the wood samples were acceptable, meeting the standards setup by different countries. More details please refer to publication 8-4, Part C. Task 2 – Pretreatment (accomplished) Enzymatic saccharification of cellulose is the primary step for bioconversion of lignocellulosic biomass, and pretreatment is a mandatory process to destruct the cell wall structure to allow the cellulases access the target substrates. A series of pretreatment was conducted by using a 4-L stainless steel rotary-type electric heating digester (KRK 2611, Tokyo, Japan). In each batch, a total of 500 g wood chips were pretreated under three designed conditions, i.e., (1) dilute acid (DA) treatment; (2) sulfite pretreatment process with 10% (w/w) bisulfite and 1.2% (v/w) sulfuric acid; and (3) sulfite process with 20% (w/w) bisulfite and 1.9% (v/w) sulfuric acid. The temperature profile and cooking time of the processes were fixed at 165°C and 75 minutes. Hydrolysis experiments were conducted to evaluate the performances of the processes. DA process showed significantly lower digestibility of the substrates (SED) than other substrates, as expected. However, the SED of SP20 substrate was lower than the SP10. Hydrolysis was inhibited by higher degree of sulfonation, whereas conventional wisdoms believed that higher sulfonation is always a favorable strategy for saccharification. This often-misinterpreted phenomenon has been dealt with in our study through a hypothesis that the lignosulfonates can randomly adsorbed on the binding domain and the catalytic domain of the cellulase. More detailed discussion to elucidate the duel mechanisms of lignosulfonate to enzymatic hydrolysis has been included in publication 8-6. Task 3 – Wastewater Analysis (accomplished) Based on the finding of Research Task 2, a new biorefinery technique (i.e., the whole slurry biomass saccharification process) was tested in our pretreatment broth to recover the pretreatment liquor. In this exercise pretreatment spent liquor that was originally considered a wastewater become a new resource to the biorefinery. In the whole slurry saccharification process, the pretreated substrate is hydrolyzed together with the spent liquor without washing to completely use of the sugars for high product yield and reduces water consumption. In order to investigate the impacts of pretreatment by-products to the process, the importance of the interactions between the cellulases and pretreatment products have been re-emphasized. A comprehensive literature review was conducted together with the instrumental analysis of the pretreatment spent liquor. The nonproductive binding has been concerned in nearly all the newly developed biomass pretreatment methods. Various chemical, biochemical and genetic tools have been employed for stabilizing or even activating cellulase in presence of lignin. We reviewed the most recent research progress on the fundamental mechanisms correlating the cellulase-lignin interactions with the status and structures properties of lignin; the synergistic action of cellulases; and the rapidly developed stabilization strategies as presented in publications 8-2&3. Task 4 – Kinetic Analysis of Inhibited Biological System (accomplished) Kinetic analysis will focus on establishing the growth/decay activities of the microorganisms and inhibiting coefficients of different components, such as furfural, organic acid, and lignin-derived products to enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. A series of SSF were performed in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks using an incubator. The whole slurry substrate or washed substrate was added to the flasks. The pH of the medium was adjusted to pH 5.5 by addition of solid calcium hydroxide. The experiments were started by adding 15 filter paper unit (FPU)/g glucan cellulases (CTec2) and prehydrolyzed at 50 °C. The temperature was then reduced and inoculated with 5 g/L activated dry yeast while the shaker speed was reduced to 130 rpm. Fed-batch SSF experiments were started with an initial 15% (w/w, washed substrate) or 22% (w/w, the whole slurry substrate) solid content. Another 8% (w/w) portions was added at 12 h, giving a final concentration of dissolved matters at 23% (w/w, washed substrate) and 30% (w/w, the whole slurry substrate), respectively. The combination of high solid concentration and high temperature pose synergistic adverse effects on microbial growth and ethanol production. A lag phase of cell growth and glucose consumption was observed at the presence of furfural concentration of 0.34 g/L. The details of the study was published in publication 8-6. Task 5– Model Development of the Biological Process (accomplished) This kinetic model describes the complexity of enzymatic hydrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass and fermentation of the released sugars. The pretreated solid substrate and pretreatment liquor were mixed and added to the SSF system. The solid substrate mainly involved cellulose and non-soluble lignin, in which the cellulose is hydrolyzed by enzyme complex and simple glucose is released and dissolved in the solution. The kinetic of fermentation involves sugar consumptions, cell growth, ethanol production and metabolism of inhibitors and the inhibitors (i.e. furfural, HMF, and aromatic compounds) hinder the fermentation reactions. The results obtained in Tasks 1-5 were used to construct and validate the kinetic model. The structure of the substrate is assumed to be uniform and the hydrolyzability of the amorphous and crystalline zone of cellulose are the same. The kinetic model was coded, simulated and solved by using a numeric computing program Matlab R2013a (MathWorks). The dynamic functions were solved using the ‘ODE45’ function to simultaneously estimate the kinetic model parameters. More details of the model have been presented in the PhD candidate’s confirmation exam and will be published in peer-reviewed journal. Task 6 Biorector Setup (accomplished) A lab-scale bioreactor have been set up and run for experimental test in our laboratory. The bioreactor system includes a stirred tank for enzymatic hydrolysis lignocellulosic substrate and a stirred tank of fermenter with temperature and pH control. Substrate was pre-hydrolyzed at 50°C for a designed period of time and then the reducing sugar containing supernatant was transferred to the fermenter with the yeast inoculation for fermentation. The temperature of fermentation was 35°C. A pH probe was positioned on the side of the fermenter to ensure the optimal pH for yeast growth and fermentation (pH =5.5). Aliquot samples of 1 mL were taken at designed time intervals from the side hole of the reactor for further analysis. More details of the process design conditions have been published in publication 8-5.

25201114.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201114.value: An innovative urban biorefinery system was investigated to convert solid wastes derived lignocellulosic biomass (i.e., woody products and yard wastes) into bioethanol. Five types of woody biomass derived from construction and demolition activities and municipal solid wastes were collected and analyzed to evaluate the feasibility for bioconversion in Hong Kong (Hossain et al., 2016). No toxicity, heavy metals, or significant contamination was detected in the samples after two-stage acid hydrolysis and thermochemical digestion, implying the suitability of the feedstock to be used in the urban biorefinery. Monterey pine was selected throughout our studies due to its high lignin content and large production rate in Hong Kong and nearby regions. A whole slurry simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF) process was established to completely utilize the fermentable sugars from sulfite pretreated substrates. The pretreatment by-products did not cause significant impacts to enzymatic hydrolysis in comparison with other processes (Liu et al., 2016), but can influence the yield and kinetics of fermentation (Dong et al., 2018b). The results of control experiments showed that carbohydrate based pretreatment by-products (i.e., furfural and hydroxymethylfurfural) were not the major factors inhibiting the fermentation process. The fermenting microorganism suffered from heat stress associated with aromatics and/or other components in the hydrolysate. The non-isothermal conditions designed for high hydrolysis efficiency is less feasible in the whole slurry system. A new temperature profile was introduced along with the whole slurry SSF process to maximize the energy yield (Dong et al., 2018a). Energy analysis showed that the benefits of high ethanol titer created after temperature profiling can increase by 43.5-234.7%, which overcame the energy loss due to cooling and re-heating. The water consumption was 25.8-51.2% lower than the other similar processes. The experimental results and mathematic model was then served as an fundamental to calculate the carbon sequestration potentials of urban greening management (Chan et al., in review) and the overall agricultural residues in Mekong River basin after energy harvesting (Ko et al., 2017). The research outputs of this study have created new scientific insights, positive impacts, and collaboration from the lab to a region, and then to the world.

25201114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25201114.value: This study elucidated the inhibiting effects of aromatic by-products to yeast fermentation in whole slurry SSF process. A series of lab-experiments, analytical appraoch, and new dynamic model were developed and conducted. The inhibiting effects were quantified kinetically and demonstrated to be more sensitive at 35°C rather than at 28°C even with a commercially engineered strain to function at 45°C. Enzyme-substrate interactions showed that the efficiency of enzymatic hydrolysis was not affected under the new temperature profile. Extreme low water consumption and high conversion rate/yield of the feedstock resulted in at least 50% higher energy yield than the other state-of-the-art processes. Pretreatment is the bottleneck of the overall bioconversion process. The fermentation broth contains large amount of sulfur based by-products, such as sulfate and lignosulfonates, which are with environmental/health risk if disposed of in the landfills. The environmental footprint of the biorefinery process can be further reduced when the pretreatment by-products can be recovered, regenerated, or valorized. Our further research will be on exploring new solvent systems to assist cell decomposition and developing innovative consolidated hydrolysis/fermentation bioprocess to enhance the biological activities. These new practices shall further reduce sulfite and cellulase consumption toward a more environmental-friendly and economical application.

25201114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201114.value: This project aims to develop a low environmental impact bioconversion process to valorize woody product waste. Lignocellulosic chemistry was incorporated into environmental research and engineering practices to mitigate the solid waste problems in Hong Kong. Our team investigated the decomposition mechanisms of plant cell wall micro-structure under thermochemical conditions. We also constructed a dynamic model to simulate and optimize the energy/water balance during the process. The merits of the new technique include high product yield and reaction rates. In line with the theory developed in this project, the research works have resulted in a few related publications, collaborations, and applications. The outcome of the findings supported five peer-reviewed publications, five conference papers, and one PhD student.

25201214.label: Project Objectives
25201214.value: To modify the pile group and piled raft analysis tool, previously developed by the PI, to model nonhomogeneous soil conditions. The finite element method will be formulated to extract the soil flexibility matrix in these soil conditions. The tool is also capable of modelling the flexural behaviour of the pile cap, and allows incorporation of the condensed stiffness matrix of the superstructure, resulting in a holistic analysis tool for the foundation and superstructure. To collate geotechnical information obtained from the site exploration of construction projects in Hong Kong, and to perform statistical analyses that will reveal the spatial correlation structure of the properties of marine clay deposits and saprolitic soils in Hong Kong. To perform systematic analyses on the implications of the spatial correlation of soil properties on pile group performance indicators, including differential settlements, distortions and tilting, and to develop design charts that will serve as decision-making tools for practitioners.

25201214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201214.value: Over the past few decades, a number of analysis methods have been developed to model pile group behaviour. Despite their relative strengths and limitations, similar results are generally obtained as long as appropriate input parameters are used. In fact, the major challenge in pile design and analysis is usually not the choice of analysis methods or programs, but the choice of input parameters considering the variability of soil properties under actual site conditions. The risks of foundation underperformance due to such variability are also poorly recognised. A survey conducted in the United Kingdom stated that more than 40% of geotechnical problems encountered during construction were due to these uncertainties in soil profiles and soil properties, while only 5% were caused by the detailed designs. Therefore, there is a need to investigate the spatial variability and correlation structures of soil properties, and how these features affect the performance and reliability of pile group designs. Statistical studies of the spatial correlation of soil properties require a large amount of geotechnical information, and the lack of data is a major obstacle to these studies. The proposed project will harness the vast resource of geotechnical information that has been archived in the Civil Engineering Library maintained by the Hong Kong Government. Comprehensive statistical analyses will be conducted on the geotechnical information obtained from ground investigation of previous projects in Hong Kong, in order to reveal the spatial correlation features of soil properties, with the emphasis placed on local saprolitic soils and marine clay deposits. While the results will be immediately applicable to future projects in Hong Kong, they will also shed lights onto the spatial structure of similar soil types and geologic settings in other parts of the world. In addition, a pile group analysis tool, previously developed by the Principal Investigator, will be extended to model spatially-variable soil properties, by incorporating an efficient, streamlined finite element code to extract the soil flexibility matrix under nonhomogeneous soil conditions. The modified analysis tool will be used to investigate the implications of soil spatial variability on the risks of differential settlements, tilting and distortion of the foundation. The pile group analysis tool also allows coupling of the superstructure stiffness, resulting in holistic simulation of both superstructure and foundation behaviour. Based on these analyses, design charts will be produced to illustrate the relationships between spatial correlation and variability of soil properties and the reliability of foundation performance. 在過去數十年間，大量有關群樁地基分析方法的研究論著相繼出現。儘管各種方法之間各存在相對的優勢和局限，但基於相同的輸入參數下，不同分析方法往往可以得到相類似的結果。實際上，樁基礎設計和分析的最大挑戰往往並非如何選擇最合適的分析軟件，而是如何確保輸入的參數能夠充份反映現場地質條件下的土壤變化情況。這種由土壤特質的空間變異性所導致的地基問題並未得到充份的研究和重視。早前一項英國的調查指出，超過40% 的岩土工程事故是在施工過程中由於土層分佈和土壤特性的不確定性引起的。相比之下，只有5% 的岩土事故是由於詳細設計的缺失而產生。因此，研究土壤特性的空間變異性和結構相關性，及其對群樁地基設計和可靠度影響的重要性顯而易見。 利用統計學對土壤的空間變異性/相關性的研究需要運用大量岩土工程磡探資料，但數據匱乏成為這類研究在世界各地的一個主要障礙。因此，本項目將利用香港土木工程圖書館中儲存的大量岩土工程資料，以揭示本港土壤的空間相關性特質。本研究項目將針對香港常見的風化土和海成粘土，其研究結果不僅可應用於香港未來的岩土工程項目，也可為世界各地的類似土壤類型和地質環境提供參考。另外，本項目將基於研究團隊先前開發的群樁分析軟件進行多項擴展，包括加入有限元分析法以探討土壤空間變異性對地基不均勻沉降、傾斜和結構扭曲風險的潛在影響。此地基分析軟件更可結合上層建築的結構剛度，用以模擬上層建築和地基結構的整體強度及穩定性。藉由上述的研究成果，研究團隊將製作一系列設計圖表用以闡明土壤的空間變異性與地基穩定之間的關係，為工程業界的地基分析與設計作出貢獻。

25201214.label: Realisation of objectives
25201214.value: The main objective of this research is to quantify the risk to piled foundations (pile groups and piled rafts) due to spatial variability of soil properties. On top of that, this research aims to manage and reduce the risk through soil sampling and field monitoring. The research project has addressed those objectives. The specific works that correspond to the research objectives are listed as follows: 1) An efficient numerical program code has been developed to incorporate three-dimensional finite element approach, streamlined to obtain the flexibility matrices for modelling of pile-soil-pile interaction effects. This is then coupled with the beam elements for pile elements, and the plate elements for pile caps or rafts. This further allows coupling of superstructure stiffening effects through matrix condensation approach. The result is a program for efficient and holistic analyses of the superstructure with its pile group foundation, taking into consideration the heterogeneous or spatially correlated soil properties. 2) Large amounts of local soil and rock data have been collected from the Civil Engineering Library maintained by the Hong Kong government. In particular, the commonly encountered soil types, including residual soils such as completely decomposed granite/tuff and marine deposits have been studied systematically, through a newly proposed rigorous geostatistical approach, to define the spatial correlation features. These include the scale of fluctuations along various directions, and the rotation of principal axes for the scale of fluctuations. The linkage between these spatial variability features and the site geology has been discussed, to provide guidance to researchers and practitioners regarding the determination of site-specific spatial correlation parameters. 3) A matrix version of eigen-decomposition of random field has been proposed, which preserves the characteristics of continuous Karhunen Love (KL) expansion but is more versatile, meaning the eigenvectors and eigenvalues can be obtained easily for arbitrary spatial autocorrelations. The matrix decomposition method can incorporate the effect of soil samples by decomposing the conditional autocorrelation matrix, which KL expansion cannot achieve currently. Based on the matrix decomposition, an efficient random field simulation scheme is proposed, namely Latin Hypercube Sampling with Dependence (LHSD), which is a stratified simulation scheme that preserves the spatial autocorrelation characteristics. LHSD can be readily applied to types of random fields commonly encountered in geotechnical engineering (normal, lognormal, cross-correlated, conditional). LHSD is combined with Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE), a type of surrogate model, to analyse the failure probability of footings and piled foundations. 4) Design charts for footing and pile group displacement under elastic soil, Tresca soil and Coulomb soil are established, using LHSD-PCE analysis combined with unconditional and conditional random fields. The design charts have been normalized such that they can be applied to a wide variety of foundation size, loading, as well as mean and variance of soil properties. This enables the practitioners to perform parametric studies by adjusting the design parameters. Using these design charts, the reliability of footing and pile group foundations can be efficiently assessed without conducting random field modelling which can be time consuming and technically challenging for some practitioners. 5) The response function (RF) methodology has been established and applied to shallow and deep foundation analyses, which can be used to evaluate the mean, variance and covariance of the responses subjected to a wide range of spatial autocorrelations of soil properties. An estimation scheme for RF is proposed to evaluate the RF values at chosen spatial frequencies, followed by interpolation between the frequencies. The simulation scheme can be readily applied for 1D, 2D and 3D random fields, which are particularly important for pile groups (which cannot be approximated as 2D problems). The RF approach matches the result of Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) most accurately in the footing displacement problem, when the soil property has relatively low variance. Meanwhile, RF can successfully identify the worst-case spatial autocorrelation for the differential settlement in the pile group study. In all the applications, the computational effort of RF is significantly lower than that of conventional MCS, since separate sets of analyses for different autocorrelation structures are not required. In other words, this is a very efficient approach for probabilistic evaluation of performance indicators such as differential settlements of pile groups and piled rafts.

25201214.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201214.value: This research project proposes the 3D autocovariance model in Liu and Leung (2018) and its application to characterise the spatial variability of SPT-N values and undrained shear strengths using in situ soil test data. The Gaussian autocorrelation model is adopted and the model is implemented using the restricted maximum likelihood method under the framework by Liu et al. (2017), ensuring the stationarity of the residuals, and the determination of an optimal trend structure through rigorous geostatistical techniques. Through application of the approach to two sites in Hong Kong, and the spatial correlation features are found to be potentially related to the local geological settings. For example, the major principal directions of 3D spatial correlation are found to coincide with the major joint set directions in a number of cases (Liu and Leung, 2018). These results supplement the physical tests in revealing the characteristics of variations within the subsurface domain. The approach is also shown to produce more accurate predictions of soil properties than the traditional site characterisation practice, through the additional consideration of spatial variations of residuals. Under the proposed approach, uncertainty in the soil properties may be quantified and represented by the predication variance estimates, which can be useful input for probabilistic analyses of geotechnical performance. These estimates may also be considered in the derivation of cost-effective soil sampling strategies at project sites where pre-existing information is available. This research also leads to the development LHSD-PCE approach, which is capable of achieving similar accuracy compared with raw Monte Carlo simulations, but with much smaller numbers (around 10%) of model simulations (Lo and Leung 2017). The method is used to conduct probabilistic analyses of large pile groups and piled rafts founded on soils with spatially correlated properties varying in three dimensions, and validated through favorable comparisons with real settlement measurements at two piled raft projects in Europe (Leung and Lo 2018). The probabilistic approach also reveals potentials of foundation tiling, that cannot be captured by conventional deterministic analyses. In addition, various patterns of soil variability are investigated systematically. For example, 3× 3 and 5× 5 pile group analyses showed that the critical scenarios for differential settlements involve the horizontal autocovariance distance being comparable to the foundation dimensions. The investigation also leads to the development of a series of design charts and practical guidelines, which allow researchers and practitioners to quickly estimate the uncertainty of foundation performance without performing the probabilistic analyses.

25201214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25201214.value: This project develops the framework for probabilistic analyses of large pile groups and piled rafts, mainly incorporating the spatial variability of geotechnical properties, such as soil stiffness and shear strength parameters. One potential area of further work would involve incorporation of uncertainty associated with the superstructure, including material properties, connection between structural members and load distributions, all of which can lead to variability in foundation performance such as total and differential settlements and tiling. Another area of further research could involve incorporation of Bayesian learning approach, or machine learning or other data analytics methods, to analyze the measurement data (such as settlements) obtained during the earlier stages of the construction, to refine the estimates of spatial variability features. These refined estimates can then be used to update and refine the foundation and structural response for subsequent construction stages. This would be particular pertinent to high-rise buildings with potentially 100 storeys or more, as early warnings of possible underperformance can be obtained through rational probabilistic estimates of the likely future response. This has been made possible by the efficient reliability analysis approach resulting from this project, and a research proposal is being developed to explore these areas.

25201214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201214.value: Foundation designs by deterministic analyses constitute the predominant approach in the current geotechnical practice, as there is a common perception that conservatism is always achieved by adopting ‘moderately conservative’, deterministic parameters. However, neglecting spatial variability of soil properties may lead to oversight of certain failure modes, such as foundation tilting or underestimation of settlements. In this project, a numerical program was developed for efficient probabilistic assessments of foundation response, which take into consideration the spatial variability of soil properties, and their interactions with foundation piles and the superstructure in a holistic manner. The findings have been presented in design charts that illustrate the risks regarding differential settlements and distortions of building foundations arising from such geotechnical variability. Site-specific characterisation of geotechnical properties requires proper understanding on the spatial variability features of soil properties. This project harnessed the rich resource of geotechnical information available in Hong Kong, and developed an integrated geostatistical tool to analyse site-specific variability features in subsurface strata and soil properties. It was found that these features are often closely related to the geological settings of the site. Together with the abovementioned design charts, these tools facilitate efficient assessments of foundation reliability.

25201314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201314.value: Recently, there is an increasing demand for high performance hydrogen gas sensors due to the rapid developments in hydrogen fuel cell technology. Existing hydrogen sensors have some disadvantages such as complex fabrication procedures, poor selectivity and repeatability, long response/recovery time, high production cost, the need for heating of the sensor head and the requirement for complicated optical detection system. These sensors are inapplicable to a broad range of system demanding high mechanical durability and large-area coverage such as wrapping over hydrogen pipelines. Hence, a novel flexible hydrogen sensor based on organic thin-film transistor (OTFT) is proposed. OTFT-based gas sensors can offer advantages such as low-cost and simple processing and fabrication, room-temperature operation, multiparameter response, flexibility, lightweight, large-area sensing, easily integrated into an electronic circuit and tailored chemical selectivity. The sensing performance of an organic sensor depends largely on the properties of the insulator, the organic layer, and the interfaces. However, the performances of organic TFT-based sensors are not yet ideal. There are still several features such as operating voltage, sensitivity, stability, reliability, and reproducibility that needed to be improved in order to satisfy numerous requirements in applications. Hence, the main aim of this project is to investigate the preparation methods and optimize processing conditions for the insulator, organic thin film, electrodes and encapsulation layer of the device so that a sensitive, selective, stable, bendable, and low-power OTFT-based hydrogen sensor can be produced. Our approach is to (i) use new hafnium-based oxide insulators with high dielectric constant (high-k) inside the OTFT sensors, with a view to greatly reducing their operating voltage and power consumption, (ii) passivate the surface of the high-k dielectrics by low-temperature ultraviolet (UV) ozone annealing technique, fluorine plasma treatment and UV assisted chlorination technique to achieve smoother and passivated surface and hence facilitate growth of organic thin film with good structural ordering, less grain boundaries and structural defects for improving stability, sensitivity and response time, (iii) prepare stable organic thin films including pentacene, copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) and C60:LiF nanocomposites with large grains by optimization of the growth conditions, (iv) use catalytic metal Pt as the source-drain electrodes for achieving high H2 selectivity, and (v) use suitable gate electrode materials e.g. Al or chlorinated indium tin oxide (Cl-ITO) for flexible plastic substrate and bendable parylene polymer thin-film encapsulation for enhancing long-term stability of the sensors. 最近，由於氫燃料電池技術的迅速發展，對於高性能的氫氣傳感器的需求日益增加。現有的氫傳感器具有一些缺點，如複雜的製造過程，選擇性和重複性差，響應/恢復時間長，生產成本高，傳感器頭需要加熱和要求複雜的光學檢測系統。這些傳感器不適用於範圍廣泛，要求機械耐久性高和覆蓋面積大的系統諸如包裹在氫氣管線。 因此，提出了一種基於有機薄膜晶體管（OTFT）的新型柔性氫傳感器。OTFT基氣體傳感器可以提供優點，如低成本和簡單的處理和加工，室溫操作，多響應參數，柔韌性，輕量，大面積傳感，很容易集成到一個電子電路和定制化學選擇性。有機傳感器的感測性能很大程度上取決於絕緣體，有機層和接口的屬性。然而，有機TFT型傳感器的性能還不理想。還有幾個特性，如工作電壓，靈敏度，穩定性，可靠性和可重複性是需要加以改進，以便滿足大量在應用上的要求。因此，該項目的主要目的是為絕緣體，有機薄膜，電極和器件的包封層研究製備方法和優化加工條件，使得敏感的，選擇性的，穩定的，可彎曲的，並且低功耗OTFT基於氫氣傳感器可以生產。我們的方法是（ⅰ）使用新的具有高介電常數（高k）的鉿基氧化物絕緣體於OTFT傳感器內，以大大降低其操作電壓和功耗，（ⅱ）使用低溫紫外線（UV）臭氧退火技術，氟等離子處理和UV輔助氯化技術鈍化高k電介質的表面，以實現更平滑和鈍化表面，從而促進具有良好的有序結構，晶界和結構缺陷少的有機薄膜生長，提高穩定性，靈敏度和響應時間，（ⅲ）優化生長條件以製備穩定的晶粒大的有機薄膜，包括並五苯，銅酞菁（CuPc ）和C60 ：氟化鋰納米複合材料，（ⅳ）用催化金屬Pt作為源極-漏極電極，用於實現高H 2選擇性，（v）使用合適的柵電極材料如鋁或氯化銦錫氧化物（Cl - ITO）為柔性塑料基板和可彎曲的聚對二甲苯聚合物薄膜封裝，以提高傳感器的長期穩定性。

25201314.label: Realisation of objectives
25201314.value: 1) Hydrogen gas sensors based on organic thin-film transistor (OTFT) with high-dielectric-constant (high-k) Al2O3, HfLaO and NdTaNO as gate insulator films have been developed. The dynamic behavior and working principle of these novel H2 sensors have been studied in detail. 2) The as-deposited gate insulators in organic TFT devices have been undergone annealing in N2 at low temperature (200 oC) to improve the quality of the gate insulators. In situ nitrogen doping during sputtering of NdTaO have been employed to passivate the gate insulator for growing organic thin film with suitable morphology for high-performance sensors. The catalytic-electrode thickness as an important factor affecting the sensor performance has been investigated systematically. Organic TFTs with source/drain electrodes using different metals and fabricated methods have also been fabricated and compared. 3) High-quality pentacene organic semiconductor has been prepared by sublimation process and used as the active layer in the organic hydrogen sensors. A H2 sensor based on a TFT with oxide semiconductor InGaZnO (IGZO) as channel material have been fabricated and compared with its counterpart based on pentacene. 4) Low-temperature ultra-violet assisted chlorination technique has been used to prepare chlorinated indium tin oxide (Cl-ITO) gate electrode for OTFT. OTFT devices employing different gate electrode materials (e.g. Al, Ti, ITO and Cl-ITO) and substrates (e.g. glass and flexible vacuum tape) have been fabricated and characterized. The flexibility of the OTFT has also been demonstrated. 5) Parylene polymer deposited by vapor deposition has been used as an encapsulation layer for the organic TFT devices.

25201314.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201314.value: Four top-tier journals and 4 international conference papers have been published. Working principle of hydrogen sensor based on OTFT was developed. When exposed to hydrogen with various concentrations, the sensor exhibits a clear change in drain current due to three reasons: (1) work-function change of the source electrode induced by hydrogen absorption; (2) reduced carrier mobility; and (3) increased source/drain (S/D) series resistance both caused by the H2-induced expansion of the S/D electrodes. The OTFT sensor can give rapid, reversible and concentration-dependent response upon introduction and removal of hydrogen with concentration ranging from 200 to 17 000 ppm without the need of heating [C9.1, C8.1]. Surface morphology, restrained lattice expansion (clamping effect) and processing-induced stress of the palladium electrodes can affect the sensing characteristics of OTFT. The sensitivity of the H2 sensor first increases with the catalytic-electrode thickness due to weaker clamping effect on the electrode expansion but then decreases as the electrode thickness further increases because of larger stress generated at the Pd/pentacene interface [C8.2]. The S/D electrode material (Ni, Pt and Pd) and deposition method (electron-beam evaporation and sputtering) can also influence the OTFT performance. The drain current and carrier mobility of the OTFTs with sputtered S/D electrodes show the following trend: Pd > Pt > Ni, while their threshold voltage |VT| exhibit the opposite tendency: Pd < Pt < Ni. OTFTs with sputtered S/D electrodes have much better electrical characteristics than their counterparts with evaporated S/D electrodes, especially for metals with high melting point [C8.4]. The IGZO TFT sensor with Pd S/D electrodes as sensing medium has an opposite response compared to its counterpart based on pentacene TFT upon exposure to hydrogen. The hydrogen dipole layer produces an electric field that can help the flow of electrons from the source electrode to the IGZO channel, but oppose the flow of holes from the source electrode to the pentacene channel [C8.3]. Surface chlorination treatment on ITO gate electrode is a simple, low cost, low-temperature and effective way to enhance the OTFT performance. OTFT with chlorine pretreatment of ITO has higher mobility, larger drain current, smaller sub-threshold slope, and larger on/off ration than the non-chlorinated sample. A low-voltage H2 sensor based on pentacene OTFT fabricated on flexible vacuum tape was realized. The OTFT can respond to hydrogen and function properly even on a curved surface [C9.2-4].

25201314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201314.value: Hydrogen is a very important gas because it has numerous useful applications and is an indispensable raw material in many industries. However, hydrogen is a very dangerous gas. It can cause serious explosion if a spark is present and also weaken metals internally, causing serious engineering problems. Hence, there is an increasing demand for high-performance hydrogen sensors for leakage detection and continuous gas monitoring. Existing H2 sensors have some drawbacks such as poor selectivity and repeatability, high production cost, long response/recovery time, the need for heating the sensor head and the requirement for sophisticated optical detection system. Moreover, these sensors are not suitable for a broad range of system requiring high mechanical durability and large-area coverage such as wrapping over hydrogen pipelines. Because of these limitations, a novel flexible hydrogen sensor based on organic thin-film transistor (OTFT) has been proposed. Organic TFT-based hydrogen sensors can offer many advantages such as low cost, room-temperature operation, simple fabrication and operation processes, multiparameter response, flexibility, lightweight, large-area sensing and easy integration with electronic circuits. The low-voltage, sensitive, selective, stable and flexible OTFT-based hydrogen sensors produced in this research project are very useful in many industrial applications.

25201514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201514.value: Containerization and information technology have substantially improved the efficiency of inland logistics and intermodal transportation systems and consequently intensified competition among gateway seaports. Major port cities have made huge investment in port accessibility through physical infrastructure upgrade and policy innovations. Such investments may impose externality on the others in the intermodal transportation system. Appropriate level of coordination among port and inland governments might be desired. Another major issue in the port industry is the gradual commercialization and privatization of seaports. Thus, in determining the level of accessibility, the concerns of those privatized ports may be quite different from those controlled by local governments. This study investigates, in the context of accessibility investment and port competition, the incentives to coordinate among competing ports and inland and welfare implications of various forms of coordination. A theoretical model is built to study the interaction among port and inland regions facing with improved accessibility, analyze regional governments’ incentives to coordinate in making accessibility investment and look for welfare implications. The role of port ownership structure in the aforementioned issues will also be discussed. An empirical study based on port accessibility improvement projects will be conducted to check the consistency between our theoretical predictions and real life observations. 集裝箱和資訊技術的運用大大改進了內陸物流和多式聯運系統的效率，並且因此加大了門戶港口之間的競爭。通過基礎設施升級和政策創新，許多港口(包括空港)城市在港口可達性方面投入巨大。這些投入會對多式聯運系統中的其他地區帶來外部效應。因此，港口和內陸地區政府間的適度合作是必要的。另一個港口業的重要問題是港口的逐漸商業化和私有化趨勢。 所以，在做出可達性程度的決策時，私有港口所關心的問題可能與地方政府控制的港口很不同。本項目重點研究在可達性投資和港口競爭的環境下，相互競爭的港口和內陸之間合作的動機以及各種合作形式對社會福利的影響。通過建立理論模型，我們將研究港口之間以及港口與內陸地區之間複雜的相互作用，分析政府間協作改善港口可達性的動機，探討各種形式的合作對社會福利的影響， 並討論港口所有權結構的影響。基於對現實中港口可達性投入專案的研究，我們還將通過實證分析檢驗理論預測與實際觀察的一致性。

25201514.label: Realisation of objectives
25201514.value: Objectives 3 and 4 are fully achieved. Following the original setting given in the research proposal, we started with modifying the conventional linear city model to incorporate two gateway seaports with their respective captive markets (port regions) and a common inland region for which the seaports compete in prices (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016). With this model, we analyzed the interaction between competing port regions and the inland region, as well as their local governments’ incentives to collaborate in port accessibility investment. In particular, we (i) derived equilibrium price and investment decisions, (ii) analyzed the impacts of accessibility investment on the rival ports’ competition, equilibrium prices and each region’s welfare, (iii) compared accessibility investment incentives under four different inter-regional coalition structures, (iv) assessed local governments’ preference over different coalitions and stability of these coalitions, and finally (v) discussed the role of port ownership, private vs. public, on all the abovementioned analysis. Based on the above analysis, we then drew policy implications in terms of desired type of inter-regional coordination, what the local government may need to do to achieve the highest level of coordination and how port privatization may affect coordination. Objective 3 is achieved by points (i) and (ii). Objective 4 is achieved by points (iii), (iv) and (v) and the discussion on policy implications. Later on, we aware that shipping lines’ practice of calling ports in sequence may also affect port competition and coordination, as the delay could pass on from one port-of-call to the next port-of-call. This “knock on” effect would affect the shipping lines’ usage of gateway ports, which in turn will affect the port pricing as well as investment in port facility accessible by shipping lines. In order to have a more comprehensive understanding on our research question from another perspective, we built another theoretical model to analyze the port charges and infrastructure investments while taking into account the “knock on” effect (Jiang, Wan and Zhang, 2017). In particular, we analyzed three scenarios of ports’ objective function: global welfare maximization, coordinated profit-maximization and independent profit-maximization. In each scenario, we derived equilibrium port charges and infrastructure investment rules. Then, we compared these rules across the three scenarios. We also compared how shipping lines’ modes of competition (Cournot vs. Stackelberg) lead to different outcomes. This part of the research adds new insights related to objectives 3 and 4. For example, we found that when the shipping lines’ “knock on” effect is strong, an increase in shipping lines’ operation in one port will cause a reduction in operation in the other port and the ports may charge too little and invest too little from the social welfare point of view. The first theoretical model mentioned above relates to the achievement of Objective 1, but to obtain tractable results, simplification on the structure of hinterland access system is made in this model. Thus, to fully achieve Objective 1, we then proposed a general (full-fledged) theoretical framework which combines various key modeling aspects in the literature (Wan, Zhang and Li, 2018) by extending (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016) and some of our previous studies. In the general framework, in addition to the captive local markets (regions) and inland market (region), we incorporated different hinterland access systems, including corridors linking port and inland regions (inter-region corridors), transport system connecting the port to its captive market (e.g. intra-region roads) and transport system within the inland (e.g. inland roads). We (i) compared results of models which capture some but not all aspects of our framework, (ii) identified the missing pieces in the theoretical literature and future research opportunities, and (iii) discussed how different modes of port competition (price vs. quantity) could lead to differentiated impacts of accessibility investment. Objective 2 has been well-achieved as well. In terms of contribution to the theoretical literature about infrastructure competition, the two models mentioned above and the general theoretical framework all contribute in different aspects. Based on these models and corresponding analysis, we published three journal papers, one in Transportation Research Part B and two in Maritime Policy and Management. The empirical part of the research does not exactly follow the strategy described in the proposal. As mentioned in the previous progress reports, after lots of effort to collect data, we find it impossible to conduct a large-scale empirical study as we planned, because information about hinterland accessibility investment projects is very fragmented and incomplete. Many key information, such as the investment amount and cooperative arrangement between governments and other investors, is unclear. However, we do find another way to contribute to the empirical literature. First, we conducted a thorough literature survey on related empirical studies, pointed out questions that have not been investigated in the empirical literature, proposed an econometric specification that may be used to investigate these questions, and most importantly identified the challenges and data difficulty which have to be addressed to make large-scale empirical studies possible. All of the above points are included in Wan, Zhang and Li (2018). Second, due to the difficulty in conducting an empirical analysis incorporating a large variety of ports and hinterland systems, we decided to scale down the empirical study by focusing on the port of Ningbo in China and its influence and investment in various dry ports located in the inland regions of China. Thus, the empirical strategy has been adjusted by focusing more on how the cooperation between seaports and inland, reliance on seaport-inland rail linkage, and level of competition affects productivity. This study leads to another paper (Chang, Yang and Wan, 2018) which has been submitted to Transport Policy and is now under the second round review. This study also contributes to objectives 3 and 4 by providing policy implication on seaport’s investment in the inland infrastructure and the impact of such investment on inland terminal’s productivity.

25201514.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201514.value: When ports are publicly owned (local welfare maximizers), a port’s investment in accessibility to its captive market makes it more aggressive (Wan, Zhang and Li, 2018) and negatively affects its competitors, leading to higher level of competition. Therefore, competing ports may have incentives to invest less. However, such investment benefits inland region due to reduced port charges (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016). When ports are privately owned (profit maximizers) and the captive market is large, the above no longer holds. Rather, investing in the accessibility to the captive market makes a port less aggressive (Wan, Zhang and Li, 2018) and imposes positive effect on its competitors, alleviating price competition and leading to incentives to invest more (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016). Investing in the transport system of the inland region raises the competition between port regions, but the port regions’ local welfare may increase if ports are private and have large captive markets (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016). There is a conflict of interest between the port regions and the inland in terms of investment cooperation. Although cooperation among all the regions generates the highest total welfare, it is difficult to achieve. When ports are public, due to the sizable investment required by port-inland cooperation, the port regions prefer not allying with the inland, unless receiving sufficient compensation from the inland. With private ports and large captive markets, however, the port regions gain from coordinating with the inland while the inland loses, so it is essential for port regions to compensate the inland if cooperation is desired (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016). With the presence of strong knock-on effects due to shipping lines’ sequential port-calling (Jiang, Wan and Zhang, 2017) or large captive markets (Wan, Basso and Zhang, 2016), cooperation between the private ports (or port regions) may generate higher port charges but it also leads to higher level of investment than the non-cooperative case. Empirically, Chang, Yang and Wan (2018) find that port’s heavy investment in the inland associates with low inland terminal productivity unless the inland has sufficient shipping demand. This finding is consistent to our theoretical prediction.

25201514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25201514.value: Wan, Zhang and Li (2018) provide a comprehensive discussion on the avenues of future development for this line of research. Here list a few important directions. The most straightforward follow-up study is to complete the picture of the impacts of accessibility investment by fully understanding the roles of each individual components of the full-fledged general framework, including different types of land-side access systems, the captive markets and the modes of competition. Another extension is to combine the landside accessibility issue from shippers’ point of view and the seaside accessibility issue from shipping lines’ point of view. In this way, one can study how seaside and landside investment can be interrelated and together how these two types of infrastructures jointly influence port competition and social welfare. This can be achieved by adding Jiang, Wan and Zhang (2017)’s modeling features into Wan, Basso and Zhang (2016)’s linear city model. Empirically, more attention can be paid on testing theoretical predictions with real life data. To make any large-scale empirical test possible, future research should start with developing strategies to deal with several difficulties, such as quantifying accessibility of complex land transportation system, identification of captive and inland markets, etc.

25201514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201514.value: Due to the intensified competition, many gateway seaports have invested heavily in local or inland transportation infrastructures to improve their reach to shippers. Some ports cooperate with the inland or other port regions in such investment projects. This research project studies seaport and inland regions’ incentives to coordinate in accessibility investment, analyzes the regional welfare and port competition impacts of such investment and inter-regional coordination, and provides an analytical framework that incorporates different hinterland access systems. Our study reveals the complexity of the issue. It suggests that policy makers and industry players should consider several factors when making investment and cooperation decisions, including the ownership of seaports, the relative size of the port’s captive local market and contestable inland market, and the type of access system to be invested. This research is particularly important to Hong Kong, because substantial investment in inland terminals by major seaports in mainland China, the construction of major transportation infrastructure such as Hong Kong-Macau-Zhuhai Bridge, and inter-regional cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative, could all change the landscape of port competition and affect Hong Kong’s competitiveness in port-related business.
