25201614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201614.value: 香港是一個位於亞熱帶地區的現代化都市，然而在過去幾十年中，香港氣溫持續上升。而人為熱排放是造成香港熱島效應的主要原因之一。本研究的目標旨在建立一種適用於複雜城市地表環境的人為熱估算方法，該方法將應用於中國環境與災害監測預報小衛星數據，從而估算整個香港的人為熱分佈。

25201614.label: Realisation of objectives
25201614.value: During the project period, the project team has accomplished the following objectives: The project team has developed a novel algorithm to estimate anthropogenic heat fluxes by decomposing image pixels into fractions of impervious surfaces and vegetation, then estimating the total heat flux for the mixed pixel. Anthropogenic heat is the heat flux generated by human activities and is a major contributor to the formation of urban heat island. In a city such as Hong Kong, obtaining pure pixels from medium- or coarse-resolution remote sensing images is challenging. Considering the completely different thermal properties of vegetation and impervious surfaces, the new method separates the mixed pixels of vegetation and impervious surface to estimate the heat fluxes over urban areas. The Chinese small satellite HJ1B images with a spatial resolution of 30 and 300 m for visible and thermal wavebands respectively, and the temporal resolution of four days were used for the heat flux modeling. The urban surface temperature is an important parameter for urban heat flux estimation. While the effects of urban geometry on surface temperature retrieval is a challenge, this study has initiated a set of innovative strategies to map the historical thermal-built environment of a compact city, with a spatiotemporal approach to analyze the relationships between building structures and urban heat islands, with a view to developing a sustainable protocol for future urban planning. The 3D building datasets representing the building morphology and sets of urban morphological data derived from building datasets were reconstructed. This study has also developed an improved urban emissivity model based on sky view factor (IUEM-SVF) from urban morphological data to consider all radiance contributions leaving the urban canopy, including (i) emission by all facets within an instantaneous field of view (IFOV); (ii) reflection by all facets of emission from surrounding facets; and (iii) propagation of emitted and reflected radiation with multiple reflections (scattering) within a complex 3D array of urban objects. The effective emissivity derived from IUEM-SVF was evaluated with a microscale radiative transfer and energy balance model: Temperatures of Urban Facets in 3-D (TUF-3D). IUEM-SVF performs well when urban facets have uniform emissivity and temperature, e.g., root mean square deviations (RMSD) are less than 0.005 when material emissivity is larger than 0.80 (ɛ ⩾ 0.80). Effective emissivity derived from IUEM-SVF was used to retrieve urban surface temperature from a nighttime ASTER thermal infrared image. Promising results were achieved in comparison with standard LST products retrieved with the Temperature and Emissivity Separation (TES) algorithm. IUEM-SVF shows promise as a means to improve the accuracy of urban surface temperature retrieval. Additionally, the geometric effects on the application of split-window algorithm over urban areas were also studied and results showed that the geometry effect will be removed and mis-deemed as atmospheric effect when the split-window algorithm without geometry effect is applied in urban areas. The split-window algorithm with the geometry effect can be used to distinguish between geometry and atmospheric effect in further study. As the accurate LST product is a key element in modeling anthropogenic heat flux, this part of study shows a new research method for deriving LST images at promising accuracy. How the geometric effects on urban surface temperature retrieval affect the urban sensible heat flux estimation was studied in this project. Two different land surface temperatures (with considering geometry effect and without considering geometry effect) were derived to estimate sensible heat flux over urban areas using remotely sensed land surface temperature. Results showed that the surface temperatures with considering geometry effect could bring up to 18.0% difference in the estimated sensible heat flux over built-up areas. The sensible heat fluxes derived from surface temperature with considering geometry effect are lower than those without considering geometry effect, particularly over built-up areas (e.g., the mean value is 44.3 W/m2). The sensible heat fluxes over built-up areas are higher than those over flat impervious surfaces. In addition to the anthropogenic heat emission over urban areas, dense buildings cause higher displacement heights and roughness lengths than flat surfaces, thus aerodynamic resistances for heat are lower over built-up areas; this makes sensible heat dissipation into atmosphere easier over built-up areas than over flat surfaces. Wind ventilation in an urban environment is important for heat dissipation. Accurate mapping of wind ventilation in an urban environment is challenging when large spatial coverage is required. This study has developed a GIS-based model for estimating the frontal area index (FAI) of buildings, infrastructure and trees using very high resolution airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data, which can also be used to investigate the “wall effect” caused by high-rise buildings at a finer spatial scale along the coasts in the Kowloon Peninsula of Hong Kong. New algorithms have been created by improving previous algorithms utilizing airborne LiDAR data in raster unit, as well as considering the backward flow coefficient between windward and leeward buildings. Vehicular traffic is an important heat source of anthropogenic heat flux especially it is a key element in LUCY model. It is crucial to map and monitor the spatio-temporal heat patterns of vehicular traffic in a city. Data observed from traffic counting stations are readily available for mapping the traffic-related heat across the stations. However, macroscopic models utilizing traffic counting data to estimate dynamic directional vehicular flows are rarely established. Our work has proposed a simple and robust cell-transmission-model to simulate all possible cell-based origin-destination trajectories of vehicular flows over time, based on the traffic counting stations. And these results were cross-compared as part of LUCY model with the results from remote sensing imagery. However, the project team has attempted to access and model the dynamic population data as a part of LUCY in this project, but due to the limitation of the data accessibility in Hong Kong, we could not model this part in the LUCY. Thermal data from helicopter-borne thermal camera were acquired in collaboration with the Hong Kong Government Flying Service, the Hong Kong Observatory and the project team. The very high spatial resolution data have been used to improve the algorithms for deriving the land surface temperature over urban areas in accurate manner. Days and nights surveys on four days i.e. 16 Jul 2015; 11 Sep 2015; 16 Dec 2015; 24 Oct 2017 were conducted.

25201614.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201614.value: A novel algorithm to estimate anthropogenic heat fluxes by decomposing image pixels into fractions of impervious surfaces and vegetation, and by estimating the total heat flux for the mixed pixel were developed; and the anthropogenic heat fluxes in different seasons were estimated. Results showed that anthropogenic heat fluxes in Hong Kong are correlated to the building density and the building height and the commercial areas emit the largest anthropogenic heat fluxes compared with other land-use types. An improved urban emissivity model based on sky view factor (IUEM-SVF) was developed to consider all radiance contributions leaving the urban canopy which has not been considered in the literature. This model tackled the issues of cavity effects caused by urban geometry. IUEM-SVF shows promise as a means to improve the accuracy of urban surface temperature retrieval, which is a key component in urban heat energy balance modeling. The temperature difference between with and without the geometry effect can reach 2 K in built-up areas. A comparison was also conducted between LST retrieved by split-window algorithm with and without geometry effect. Results showed that the LST retrieved by split-window algorithm without geometry effect has generally higher value than the one with the geometry effect. The geometry effect will be misdeemed as atmospheric effect when the split-window algorithm without geometry effect is applied in urban areas. Three major data sources for urban heat energy balance modeling were reconstructed, including 1) the annually averaged Land Surface Temperature (LST) for determining the relative temperature across a compact city; 2) 3D building datasets for representing the building morphology; and 3) sets of urban morphological data derived from building datasets for analyzing the thermal spatial patterns and energy balancing. The surface temperatures with considering geometry effect could bring up to 18.0% difference in the estimated sensible heat flux over built-up areas. The sensible heat fluxes derived from surface temperature with considering geometry effect were lower than those without considering geometry effect, particularly over built-up areas. We adapted the LUCY model to estimate the anthropogenic heat fluxes from vehicles based on the traffic counting stations. Result showed that the heat patterns have notable daily and weekly periodical circulation/pattern, and volumes of heat vary significantly in different grid cells. The findings suggested that vehicular flows in some places are the dominating influential factor that make the UHI phenomenon more remarkable.

25201614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25201614.value: This study has developed several novel algorithms for estimating land surface temperature as well as anthropogenic heat flux accurately. The urban geometric and 3D data developed in this study can also be used to calculate and estimate the “complete urban surface temperature”. The “complete urban surface temperature” is an important variable in urban climate research. A research study is proposed and will be carried out by the research team in the near future. We carried out field experiments by thermal camera on helicopter on 16 Jul 2015, 11 Sep 2015, 16 Dec 2015, 24 Oct 2017. These data have been used to improve and validate the urban surface temperature retrieval and then to estimate the sensible heat fluxes over the heterogeneous surface of urban areas. The thermal data obtained in field experiments can provide the thermal information of wall facet, street and rooftop of buildings. This can be used to calculate the heat fluxes from all components in urban space and study the heat dissipation over urban areas. Future work can track the UHI evolution using the developed object-oriented dynamic model and simulate the urban dynamics with multi-disciplinary knowledge, and analyze their spatiotemporal correlations systematically to explore and understand potential factors.

25201614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201614.value: Urban Heat Island (UHI) is caused by the urbanization and industrialization of human civilization (Oke, 1982; Lo and Quattrochi, 2003; Grimmond, 2007; Rizwan et al., 2008; Tomlinson et al., 2011). Different from the natural vegetated areas, heat fluxes generated by anthropogenic activities, including space heating and cooling, industrial plants, vehicle exhausts, and human metabolism, which is known as anthropogenic heat, intensify the urban heat island (Kłysik, 1996; Ichinose et al., 1999; Shahmohamadi et al., 2011; Lindberg et al., 2013). Thus, study of anthropogenic heat fluxes over urban areas is very important and is a key for UHI and urban energy consumption research. This study estimates the anthropogenic heat fluxes over Hong Kong using geospatial technologies, and the anthropogenic heat patterns as well as their season variations are analyzed. This can help strengthen our understanding of UHI in Hong Kong.

25201814.value: 節理岩體中波傳播與動態響應和損傷的相互作用

25201814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201814.value: Rock is different from other engineering materials by the existence of a great number of discontinuities. They are usually termed as rock joints. Rock joints are usually in parallel form as joint sets. They are key elements of rock, and control mechanical and seismic properties of rock masses. Rock is often suffered from dynamic loading such as blast, impact and earthquakes. The dynamic loading propagates in rock in the form of stress wave. When a wave propagates through a jointed rock mass, rock and joints will deform, damage or even fail. Dynamic response of rock and joints is more complicated, compared with static one. Meanwhile, dynamic response of rock masses will also affect wave propagation and attenuation. Wave attenuation is attributed to three mechanisms including wave reflection and transmission at discontinuous joints, dynamic damage of material, and dynamic damage and response of joints. It is of great scientific interests and engineering significance to study this interactive process of wave propagation and dynamic damage and response in jointed rock masses. Dynamic damage of rock material and its effects on wave propagation, and wave reflection and transmission across rock joints have been investigated by previous studies. However, there are still some remaining problems to be solved, including dynamic mechanical properties of rock joints, dynamic damage of rock joints and its effects on wave propagation, and wave propagation and attenuation in jointed rock masses considering all three attenuation mechanisms. The proposed study aims at solving those remaining problems. Combined theoretical analysis, numerical modeling and experimental testing will be conducted. Theoretical solutions will be incorporated into numerical program, and experimental measurements will act as references to calibrate numerical modeling. The outcomes would provide understanding of the physical mechanisms lying behind wave attenuation in rock masses, dynamic behavior of joints and the whole interactive process of wave propagation and dynamic response in jointed rock masses. The expected research findings could be significant for rock mechanics and engineering, underground excavation, protective engineering, earthquakes and mechanics, and hence for the society at large. 岩石區別于其他工程材料的一個特征就是，岩石中存在大量的非連續面。這些非連續面通常為節理。岩石節理通常彼此平行，形成一個節理組。它們是岩體的關鍵結構單元，并控制著岩體的力學與動力特性。岩體經常遭受動荷載，比如爆炸、衝擊、地震。這些動荷載在岩石中以應力波的形式傳播。當一個波通過節理岩體時，岩石和節理會變形、損傷甚至破壞。與靜力響應相比，岩體的動力響應更加複雜。同時，岩體的動力響應會影響波傳播與衰減。波衰減是由於三個機制造成的，包括非連續節理處的透反射、材料的動態損傷、以及節理動態損傷與響應。針對節理岩體中波傳播與動態反應和損傷的相互作用過程的研究，具有重要的科學意義與工程價值。 之前的研究致力於解決岩石材料的動態損傷及其對波傳播的影響，和岩石節理處的透反射。然而，目前還有一些未解決的問題，包括：岩石節理的動態力學行為、岩石節理的動態損傷以及其對波傳播的影響、考慮所有三個損傷機制的波傳播與衰減。本課題致力於解決這些未知的問題。採用的研究手段包括理論分析、數值模擬和室內實驗。理論解析解會被嵌入到數值計算程序中。實驗測試結果用來標定數值模擬。 本課題的成果有助於理解節理岩體中波衰減、節理的動態行為、以及節理岩體中波傳播和動態響應的整個作用過程。相關成果對岩石力學與工程、地下開挖、防護工程、地震工程與力學等領域有著重要的價值。因而，對大眾以及社會有益。

25300114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300114.value: 細胞變形能力的化學和生物學影響與人類血液學疾病甚至癌症有著極其重要的關係. 血紅細胞正是依靠其強大變形能力通過微血管, 它是決定血液粘度的關鍵因素, 與血管疾病緊密相關. 因此, 紅細胞變形性能在紅細胞相關疾病的檢測中有重要的參考價值. 現有的細胞變形檢測方法主要基於高精度光學技術, 價格昂貴, 並只局限於光學純化樣本. 聚焦激光誘導的局部高熱能極易損傷靶細胞, 因此光鑷技術不能通過激光束本身來捕獲細胞. 相比之下, 聲學檢測設置更為簡單, 價錢便宜, 其最大的優點就是聲能對生物樣本的損傷極微. 本課題就將研發新型非侵入型聲學技術用於檢測細胞變形能力: 1. 研發不同種類的聲學器件和單波束聲鑷; 2. 量度該器件的基本特性與聲力大小; 3. 推導公式計算器件聲力; 4. 利用有限元分析模擬聲學器件的性能表現, 為物理模型與實驗結果提供確認參照; 5. 器件微束探測細胞變形能力, 將利用紅細胞作為靶細胞進行探測研究; 6. 最後從醫學與生物學角度分析細胞變形性能.

25300114.label: Realisation of objectives
25300114.value: The first objective has been achieved. Various types of single beam acoustic tweezers, including single-element with different configurations (e.g., aperture design, f-number, frequency, etc.) and array, have been developed using lithium niobate (LN) single crystal and lead zironate titanate (PZT) ceramics. The frequency was mainly from 20 to 100 MHz. For acoustic tweezing application, the f-number of acoustic devices should be small (≤1). To study the device performance as a function of f-number, the acoustic stacks of devices were press-focused into a spherical shape using a steel ball bearing of different radii (focal lengths). The lowest f-number was 0.6 that approaches a physical limit of the device. The basic performance of the single beam acoustic tweezers was evaluated in distilled water by a conventional pulse-echo response measurement. From the measurement, the frequency, bandwidth, and sensitivity of the acoustic tweezers were obtained. The measured results show good agreement with the simulated ones. Besides, to optimize the device performance for further characterizations and applications, the basic performance of devices was evaluated under different damping conditions. It is shown that the device performance (i.e. bandwidth) varies much under different damping conditions. In general, heavier damping is recommended to use with higher-frequency (>20 MHz) acoustic devices so that the echo shape can be optimized. The second objective has been achieved. The acoustic (mechanical) properties of single beam acoustic tweezers with the frequencies of <60 MHz have been evaluated using a commercial hydrophone. The performance is comparable to the results reported in literature although the single beam acoustic tweezers are with a press-focused curvature. Besides the acoustic pressure, the acoustic output profile of acoustic tweezers has also been evaluated using the commercial hydrophone and the single-beam Heterodyne laser interferometer. The results have been compared. It was found that the measurements using the laser interferometer were very time consuming, i.e. few hours for performing one measurement. As the measurement time was long, the stability of data was very poor. On the other hand, the output profile of acoustic tweezers was much better with using the hydrophone for measurement. Nevertheless, it was found that the results could vary against the aperture size of hydrophone. Thus, the spatial averaging effects of the hydrophone in the field characterizations have also been investigated. The third objective has been mostly achieved. The experimental setup for evaluating the performance of single beam acoustic tweezers in micro-particle trapping and deformation has been built. All the single beam acoustic tweezers, except the array (because of lacking of appropriate equipment to drive the array), have shown the capability of cell trapping, manipulation, and deformation. The individual red blood cell could be deformed by acoustically manipulating a polystyrene microsphere attached on the cell (the indirect approach). The other breakthrough is that the red blood cells could also be deformed successfully without the involvement of the polystyrene microspheres (the direct approach). In the direct approach, the cells were deformed directly by the radiation force generated from the acoustic tweezer. The deformation behavior of cells was studied against the ambient temperature, the driving voltage and the corresponding calibrated pressure. Nevertheless, the correlation varied from cells to cells even using the same tweezer, which may be attributed to the variations of nature of blood collected. Since there are many factors affected the cell properties, much more samples should be taken for interpretation with the statistical analysis.

25300114.label: Major findings and research outcome
25300114.value: Single beam acoustic tweezers with various configurations have been successfully developed, including the circular (No. 1, 3, 5 in Part C8), ring (No. 6 in Part C8), and complicated (No. 8 in Part C8) types. Some of them are major breakthroughs in the research field of single beam acoustic tweezer. A single beam acoustic tweezer was developed to be capable of manipulating an individual micrometer scale non-spherical cell at Rayleigh regime and even a single millimeter scale organism at Mie regime, and imaging tissue as well (No. 1 in Part C8). This work brought out possibilities that a single acoustic device is capable of performing non-invasive multi-functions simultaneously for biomedical and biophysical applications. Besides, the other single beam acoustic tweezer was developed to act like an ordinary tweezers, which was able to manipulate the targeted micro-particle precisely and selectively from a mixture of particles with different sizes (No. 5 in Part C8). This work produced new fundamental insights into the performance enhancement of the existing acoustic manipulation techniques. With the ring configuration, the single beam acoustic tweezer was shown to be capable of levitating and manipulating a micro-particle on the substrates made of materials with different acoustic impedances (No. 6 in Part C8). This work revealed that the structural design of the acoustic stack could be an effective approach to produce the desired ultrasonic field distributions for specific applications. The acoustic tweezing performance of micro-particles including cells could also be enhanced by designing the novel structure of piezoelectric component (No. 8 in Part C8). The work gave an idea to further enhance the performance of single beam acoustic tweezers for multi-functional applications. As the hydrophone is the main approach to characterize the axial and lateral pressure distributions of acoustic tweezers, the spatial averaging effects of the hydrophone in the field characterizations have been investigated (No. 4 in Part C8). It was found that the spatial averaging effects can only be neglected under the specific conditions that are related to the configurations of focused transducer, which can be a useful guide when using the hydrophone to characterize the acoustic tweezers.

25300114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300114.value: The success of the research has revealed the great potential of single beam acoustic tweezers, and brought out many possibilities of using acoustic tweezers for biomedical applications. Previously, high-frequency transducers with a press-focused circular aperture were the common design of single beam acoustic tweezers. The research showed that the desired ultrasonic field distributions of acoustic tweezers could be achieved via the structural design of the acoustic stack. More effort will be spent on this topic for high-impact journal publication and grant application. The cells were deformed successfully by the acoustic microbeam, which is an interesting and significant work. As the statistical analysis has not been completed yet, more work will be performed to study the cell deformation behavior. Patents and grants will be applied when the correlation between the cell deformability and the calibrated force of acoustic tweezers is obtained. Besides, other cells will be chosen as targets to evaluate the validity of the approach. In the present method, only the axial acoustic properties have been involved to calibrate the radiation force generated from the acoustic tweezers. Nevertheless, in practical use, the streaming effect and the lateral acoustic properties should also be considered to optimize the force calibration method.

25300114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300114.value: The physical deformability of biological cells is highly related to a number of human diseases from cancer to hematology, so the development of cell deformation characterization tools is crucial. The state-of-the-art tools are based on high-resolution optical technology, which are costly and invasive to cells. The research proposed a novel non-invasive acoustic technology for cell deformation characterization. Using an acoustic microbeam produced by the specific acoustic devices, the biological cells can be trapped, manipulated, and even physically deformed without any adverse effect. With the known mechanical output generated by the acoustic devices, the cell deformation could be quantified. In this research, various types of specific acoustic devices have been developed. Both electrical and acoustic properties of those devices have been measured. It was found that the acoustic microbeam could deform the red blood cell successfully. The cell deformation behavior was studied as functions of the ambient temperature and acoustic pressure. The research has high value and importance for biomedical and biophysical research, which revealed that the acoustic devices are capable of manipulating and deforming the cells effectively. Besides, it also proved that the acoustic devices can do similar work as the optical devices, but in a non-invasive and low-cost manner.

25300214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300214.value: 蛋白B23/核仁磷酸蛋白/核基質蛋白(B23) 被認為對細胞生長相關功能(如rRNA的合成) 起主要作用。這點已經在它與細胞的刺激生長和誘導雕亡的聯系上表現出來。作為壹種多功能核仁磷酸蛋白，它對核糖體的產生起著關鍵作用。在B23的C端有多種氨基酸序列，這對核仁定位非常重要，同時它也可以導致不同的類型的基因混亂。例如，表達致瘤的融合蛋白，導致C端區域移碼的基因突變。 因此，理清B23的細胞功能是從分子機理上了解和解開潛在癌癥隱藏之謎的重要關鍵。我們相信，rRNA和B23之間的關系是壹個關鍵的主導因素。 鑭系金屬離子克服了現有典型商業有機生物標記的缺點，已經成為壹種有吸引力的替代品。它們的招牌光學特性，如特異的發射性、大的斯托克斯位移、尖的指紋發射峰和長的發射壽命(~毫秒)等使之成為生物標記和著色的引人註目的特性。因此，我們的目標就是開發壹種新型的將鑭系金屬離子和B23結合在壹起的配合物, 通過標記和抑制B23蛋白質這兩種功能來解決上述問題。我們的研究團隊在鑭系化學和體內生物應用方面已經有了紮實的研究背景，從我們之前所發文獻已經能夠足已證明。 我們已經開展了以下四項基礎理論實驗：1)合成了三種銪金屬修飾的對B23有特異性結合的多肽，證明它們在結合B23蛋白之後其發射信號顯著增強。這表明發光體、蛋白質以及鑭系金屬離子之間發生了能量轉移的變化，研究這種變化將會非常有趣。2)分子對接理論研究，B23蛋白和我們的目標配合物之間產生了強烈的反應能（>-10kCal/mol）。3)重要的前期活體海拉細胞成像研究,已經顯現出與預期壹致的特異性核靶向定位和結合。4）MTT比色法實驗，顯示出癌細胞和正常細胞間明顯不同的細胞毒性，與預期相符合。 基於鑭系金屬的特殊性能，以及我們的初步研究發現，我們有信心建立壹個普遍適用的多光子激發的鑭系元素生物配合物，通過簡單的化學連接及合成方法，實現靶向結合B23蛋白質。同時，我們也相信，這些生物配合物也可作為抗癌藥物。

25300214.label: Realisation of objectives
25300214.value: In our proposal we have stated four objectives- So far in this completion report we have been able to achieve three out of our four stated objectives, So far we have achieved our first objective in which we have developed a chemical ligation system that is water soluble for potential imaging. We have also achieved our second objective in which we have found some potential two photon chromophores- in this work, we carefully designed and screened a lot of potential chromophores that can be used as optical probes to be used as dyes in the trafficking of the nucleophosmin binding and mechanism. Some of these synthetic route has been published in international journals. Two photon probe systems are crucial as it can improve the properties for utilization of two photon confocal microscopy, which can promote longer time imaging due to reduced phototoxcity. In this aspect we only achieved 80% of our goal as the GM value is still low and not desirable. In our third objective, we wanted to analyze and select one of the best peptide to bind to B23 protein to inhibit the activity. So in order to investigate the interaction between our designed probes and B23, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations have been done to check and compare the binding of each systems. The surface of B23 is mostly charged amino acid residues. hence, with the modification of the peptides and the ligands, the binding energy of the peptides and protein increases with increasing charged groups of the ligands. The calculated MMPBSA took the order of P1 > P3 > P2 > P4 for the cyclic peptide. With the addition of EUL and ELO, the order was EuL-P1 > EuL-P2. However, the order of the MMPBSA reverse its order when CPP group (-R8) and NLS group (-RrRK) were introduced to the systems. The binding energy were relatively stronger than other peptides probably due to the highly charged CPP and NLS groups. From the purification of the B23 protein, we were able to perform binding studies to show that for both our peptide conjugates, there was some indication of responsive inhibition. Finally, to conclude, we have encountered some problems in the cell and nucleus penetration. Therefore, the last objective concerning cellular studies is still incomplete. In this direction and part of our future work, we have made a variant of the B23 peptide that includes cell penetrating and nucleus targeting vectors, in which we will later on evaluate the performance of these new delivery systems by analyzing the structure-biological activity relationship) hence working towards our fourth stated objective.

25300214.label: Major findings and research outcome
25300214.value: The purpose of the studies is to discover the best peptide to bind to B23 protein to inhibit the activity. To investigate the interaction between our designed probes and B23, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations have been done to check and compare the binding in each system. Form our docking studies we found that he surface of B23 is mostly charged amino acid residues. hence, with the modification of the peptides and the ligands, the binding energy of the peptides and protein increases with increasing charged groups of the ligands. Here we can design our probe to favour these interactions. We also have been able to show that our compounds have some binding interaction with the B23 protein. This has been done by using SDS PAGE analysis of B23 recombinant proteins produced by the His-tagged purification system. ) Western blot analysis of the purified B23 protein. From our results we observed that EuP2 and Pra-R8-NLS-B23 can interact with B23, the mobility of B23-associated complexes is shifted (higher molecular weight after binding with the probe) when these two probes were added. Finally during our synthetic development of our b23 probes, we have also established synthetic methodologies and screened a lot of potential chromophores that can be used as optical probes to be used as dyes in the trafficking of the nucleophosmin binding and mechanism. Some of these synthetic route has been published in international journals.

25300214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300214.value: We would ultimately like to analyze the inhibition of the cell proliferation cycle in the nucleolus stages in some common cell lines, comparing cancel and normal cells. In our future work we would like to complete our final objective and show some cellular images of the b23 inhibition in the nucleophosmin, hence we like to solve the cell penetration issue, for example by incorporating sequences of NLS (PKKKRKV and RRRRRRRR (R8)) that are known to assist cellular entry. Finally, we also like to develop a few more chromophores that can be used as two photon probes with better GM values. One of these chormohphores are still currently ongoing work.

25300214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300214.value: Nucleophosmin (NPM) also known as NPM1 or B23, is an ubiquitous protein that is highly expressed in various solid tumor cells and is involved in various cellular processes, including the regulation of protein and nucleic acid as a molecular chaperone, biosynthesis of ribosomes, regulation of gene transcriptional, inhibition of apoptosis, maintenance of genomic stability, and regulation of cell cycle. Therefore it is considered as a promising target for the treatment of both haematologic and solid malignancies. From literature there have been studies of numerous different types of targeting molecules that may suppress different functions of the protein and interfere with its subcellular localization or cause inhibition to the cells mitotic cycle. However, a lot of these compounds are still ineffective and there are limited studies on their mechanistic activity and their toxicity. We hope to use our peptide targets and small conjugate probes to provide a new strategy for studying, trafficking and targeting the nucleophosmin protein. We believe that there is still a lot of scope and development in this area.

25300414.label: Project Objectives
25300414.value: Develop the theory of asymptotically periodic systems: derive the conditions such that the long-term behaviours of an asymptotically periodic system (such as global attractivity, global convergence and uniform persistence) can be reflected by its limiting system. Derive a system of delay impulsive differential equations (Model 1) to investigate the effect of impulsive larviciding on mosquito population; define the reproduction number of mosquitoes; qualitatively analyze the model's long-term dynamics. Formulate an impulsive system of reaction-diffusion equations (Model 2) to describe the mosquito population when spermless mosquitoes are released as a control measure; derive the basic reproduction number and determine the model's global dynamics by using the reproduction number as a bifurcation parameter. Develop a system of delay impulsive differential equations (Model 3) for malaria transmission to investigate the effect of the release of genetically modified mosquitoes on combating disease; define the basic reproduction number and investigate the global dynamics of Model 3. Parameterize the models with data chosen from the literature, experiments and surveillance; evaluate the cost-effectiveness of different control measures for containing the mosquito population and disease transmission; highlight the most efficient control measures to public health agencies and policy-makers.

25300414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300414.value: Differential equations with impulses arise when describing many evolving processes that are subject to abrupt changes, such as shocks, harvesting, and natural disasters. These phenomena involve short-term perturbations from continuous and smooth dynamics, whose duration is negligible compared to other time scales. When modelling such perturbations, it is natural to assume these perturbations act instantaneously or in the form of impulses. Consequently, impulsive differential equations are used to model impulsive problems in physics, population dynamics, ecology, biotechnology, industrial robotics, pharmacokinetics, optimal control, and so on. Some control effects with fixed moment impulses are eventually periodic, that is, the coefficients subject to control have periodic functions as limits. In this case we call the models asymptotically periodic systems, with periodic systems as their limiting systems. We conjecture that the long-term behaviors of solutions for an asymptotically periodic system can be reflected by those of its limiting periodic system. An important aspect of this proposal is to put this idea onto a rigorous footing. The results will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of control strategies and design optimal integrated control measures in biological sciences, such as impulsive vaccination, biological resource management with impulsive releasing and harvesting, drug treatment for diseases and so on. In this project we will take malaria control problem as an example. As a widely prevalent mosquito-borne disease in tropical and subtropical areas, malaria poses great threats to public health and the economy. Since no efficient vaccine is widely available currently, the key to malaria prevention is to target mosquitoes, which can transmit the disease between humans. Three malaria control models are formulated to describe three different control measures, the impulsive release of larvicides, spermless male mosquitoes, and genetically modified mosquitoes that cannot transmit malaria through their bites. These models will be analyzed in the light of the developed theory, and conditions that ensure success of a mosquito control program will be found. By parameterizing the models and analyzing parameters' sensitivity, the effectiveness of each strategy will be evaluated and an optimal control strategy will be determined. These models can serve as baseline models for evaluating integrated vector management which shares a high priority to combat malaria suggested by The World Health Organization (WHO) and The Roll Back Malaria (RBM).

25300414.label: Realisation of objectives
25300414.value: Various biological models, by extending those in the proposal and listed in the objectives 2, 3 and 4, have been formulated in the project to describe the population dynamics evolution from many different topics which highlight different factor impacting the population growth. For example, the age-dependent birth, death rates, the competition within and between different age groups, the increased death rate or decreased growth rate in size driven by the competition, the model with periodic coefficients to describe the continuous and smooth changes of the environmental conditions, the asymptotically periodic systems. The project led to 13 publications in such high impact scientific journals such as SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, Journal of Differential Equations, Journal of Nonlinear Science, Chaos. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations in these papers are strongly related to objectives 1 and 5. We have considered two possible factors induced by competition with specific biological species: increased density-dependent death rate or decreased density-dependent growth rate in size. (1) Using an age structured system incorporating competition among both larvae and adults, we derive a system of distributed delay equations for the numbers of larvae and adults. The system is neither cooperative nor reducible to a single equation for either variable. Positivity, boundedness and uniform strong persistence are established. Linear stability analysis of equilibria is difficult due to the strong coupling, but results are proved for small delays using monotone systems theory and exponential ordering. For small delay we prove a theorem on generic convergence to equilibria, which does not directly follow from standard theory but can be proved indirectly using comparison arguments. Finally, we consider an extension to two-strain competition and prove theorems on the linear stability of the boundary equilibria. (2) We derive a stage-structured model for an insect population in which a larva matures on reaching a certain size, and in which there is intra-specific competition among larvae which hinders their development thereby prolonging the larval phase. The model, a system of delay differential equations for the total numbers of adults and larvae, assumes two forms. One of these is a system with a variable state-dependent time delay determined by a threshold condition, the other has constant and distributed delays, a size-like independent variable and no threshold condition. We prove theorems on boundedness and on the linear stability of equilibria. Models with periodic coefficients are substantially studied. When the individual growth is dependent on seasonal factors, such as temperature, which is the case for many species including mosquitoes and ticks, the model formulation is challenging and needs careful mathematical justification. We successfully formulate models, with the aid of biological and mathematical reasoning, and propose a synthetic approach for the model formulation and model analysis. The theoretical analysis involves new ideas of introducing two functional spaces and showing the identity of spectral radius for the periodic solution semi-flow induced operators on two different functional spaces. The theoretical results are applied to host-parasite transmission and tick growth. Further applications to disease transmission and pest control are illustrated. By observing that the total population follows a single Fisher-KPP equation. Then the total population density approximates a traveling wave solution. We consider the Fisher-KPP equation in a wave-like shifting environment for which the wave profile of the environment is given by a monotonically decreasing function changing signs (shifting from favorable to unfavorable environment). This type of equation arises naturally from the consideration of pathogen spread in a classical SIS epidemiological model of a host population where the disease impact on host mobility and mortality is negligible. We conclude that there are three different ranges of the disease transmission rate where the disease spread has distinguished spatiotemporal patterns: extinction; spread in pace with the host invasion; spread not in a wave format and slower than the host invasion. We calculate the disease propagation speed when disease does spread. Our analysis for a related elliptic operator provides closed form expressions for two generalized eigenvalues in an unbounded domain. The obtained closed forms yield unsolvability of the related elliptic equation in the critical case, which relates to the open problem proposed by H. Berestycki and L. Rossi. We propose a mathematical model, of four coupled delay differential equations, for control of the Asian longhorned beetle (pest to plants) by one of its natural predators, the cylindrical bark beetle or another predator with similar characteristics. It is a predator prey interaction at the larval rather than adult level which creates interesting modelling challenges. A pest such as Asian longhorned beetle will destroy its habitat and must continually find new host trees. Even though our model does not have explicit spatial dependence, we may use it to make some inferences about the likely spatial spread of an infestation. Some further applications includes the Lyme disease transmission and Zika transmission. The PI would like to highlight that we formulate the first Zika model incorpoting both the sexual transmission and host-vector transmission routes to estimate the impact of sexual transmission mode on the disease transmission, which illustrates that the contribution is around 3%. This study brought much media report. The disease transmission in contact networks are also investigated with the support from the project. 25300414.label: Major findings and research outcome
25300414.value: The work, published in Theoretical Biology and Medical Modelling, applies the idea of the project to investigate the impact of host community diversity on the disease transmission. It is shown that the climate warming can amplify the disease risk and slightly change the seasonality of disease risk. Both the dilution effect and amplification effect are observed by feeding the model with different possible alternative hosts. The result has important impact on disease control through revising the intermediate host community. Serious studies published in SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics, Journal of Differential Equations, Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, formulate different models to investigate the effect of heterogeneity on the population dynamics, with the focus on various aspects, such as competition in different age groups, the spatial environmental factors, the seasonality driven by climate. The work in Scientific Reports formulates and studies the first Zika model with the incorporation of sexual transmission. The model provides a very reasonable fit of the ZIKV data in Brazil, Colombia, and El Salvador. Based on the estimated parameter values, the median and confidence interval of the distribution of the basic reproduction numbers. It estimates the percentage of contribution by sexual transmission in disease transmission is 3.044%. The epidemiological interpretation is interpreted as follows: Though sexual transmission alone is unlikely to initiate or sustain an outbreak, it increases the risk of infection and epidemic size and prolongs the outbreak. In order to prevent and control the transmission of ZIKV, it must be treated as not only a mosquito-borne disease but also a sexually transmitted disease. Finally, an important contribution of this project is to propose various mathematical techniques to theoretically analyze the resultant models. The project develops some new ideas on model formulation and novel techniques on analyzing the model from dynamical system point of view. For example, the paper published in Journal of Nonlinear Science formulate a biological model through rigorous mathematical arguments, and illustrate that there should be a new term incorporated. Moreover, to analyze the model with periodic coefficient, two different functional spaces should be introduced and the spectral radius of the periodic semi-flow in two different spaces are shown to be the same.

25300414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300414.value: A summarizing report is ongoing to present the results of this project from various points of view: theoretical proofs and real world applications to the biological systems. Furthermore, during working on the project, some new applications of the results in the projects are found. For example, the results are applicable to evaluate the effect of air pollution on respiratory infection transmission. To do that, models can be formulated with the Air Quality Index (AQI)-dependent transmission probability and the AQI-informed behavior changes. In real situations, smog and haze weather, on one hand, affects the infectivity of the disease and consequently influences the transmission probability. As such, the transmission probability is a function of the AQI. However, the AQI is strongly dependent on the heating system for many cities, in particular, in mainland China. Take Xian, Shaanxi province, as an example, the winter heating system works during November 15th of a year and the March 15th of the subsequent year. This heating system triggers a natural impulsively controlled system. We are hoping to work on the application of the results in this project to the AQI studies and the effect of AQI on diseases.

25300414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300414.value: This project deals with systems subject to impulses when describing many evolving processes that are subject to abrupt changes, such as shocks, harvesting, and natural disasters. In particular, we focus on the population size changes in terms of time flying. Here the population size has a general meaning, for example, the cities population number/density, the diseased cases during an epidemic outbreak and so on. Since some control effects with fixed moment impulses are eventually periodic, that is, the coefficients subject to control have periodic functions as limits. The project make use of this observation by developing and applying the mathematical theories for systems with periodic coefficients. Furthermore, the project formulates many new model types, in the form of ordinary differential equations and reaction diffusion systems, as well as differential equations with time delay. These modeling ideas are applicable to other research fields, such as the environmental science, where some abrupt changes lead to an impulsive systems.

25401214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25401214.value: This proposed study will be the first to empirically investigate self-deception as an interpersonal strategy to better deceive others. The study of self-deception comprises two approaches. The intrapersonal or trait approach regards self-deception as a stable trait representing an overly positive self-concept, which can be and has been empirically investigated using self-report questionnaires. The interpersonal approach treats self-deception as an ongoing behavior that is executed to better deceive others; this involves the self-deceiver storing truthful information in the unconscious, but presenting false information both to others and to the self. Because the self-deceiver cannot access the truth in the unconscious, he or she can deceive others without leaking out such cues as facial and eye muscle contractions, voice volume and pitch, and other observable physiological changes that indicate deception. Because of the involvement of the unconscious to which researchers can not access, the interpersonal self-deception has remained as a theory that has not been empirically investigated. The proposed study will empirically investigate interpersonal self-deception by taking a novel theoretical and methodological approach. Because self-deception is used to avoid detection, it must respond to social conditions that register the probabilities of deception detection so that individuals should self-deceive when they sense high rather than low probabilities of detection. The social status of the deceived, relative to that of the deceiver, represents such a detection-registering condition that should affect the likelihood of self-deception. Including social status in an investigation should also facilitate separating self-deceptive and deceptive motivations. Methodologically, a dual-retrieval memory method is proposed to bypass the impossibility of accessing the unconscious. In the first retrieval conducted in front of the deceived, the deceiver should fail to retrieve encoded information because of the motivation to deceive. In the second retrieval, following the successful deception, the deceiver retrieves the true or full amount of information to benefit the self. The difference between the two retrievals in a self-serving direction helps to verify self-deception. This is the first study to contribute to both theory and methodology, elucidating self-deception as an interpersonal strategy to better deceive others of high social status. Practically, knowledge gained from this study should help to manage the deception and self-deception that are ubiquitous to hierarchical human social relationships. 自欺通常被看作是個人欺騙自己的行為，不涉及他人。然而，有理論認為，自欺的人讓自己相信了錯誤資訊，失去了真實資訊，這是不利於自己生存發展的；自欺對個體的真正貢獻在於它能夠使個體更好地騙過他人，從而獲得利益。因為人們在欺騙他人時通常會因驚慌、心虛、害怕而漏出馬腳，如果個體連自己都欺騙了，就可以很淡定地向別人傳遞錯誤資訊且不被察覺。本研究希望用一系列實驗來檢驗上述理論，探討自欺是否是一種有助於人際間欺騙的策略。 本研究將於理論層面擴充對人際間自欺的探討，並嘗試用新的方法來證明自欺策略的存在。在理論上，由於自欺是為了更好地欺騙他人，那麼在欺騙不容易成功的情況下，人們更有可能啟動自欺策略來幫助欺騙他人。欺騙是否容易成功取決於欺騙被探測到的概率，這概率與具體的欺騙情境和對方的探測能力有關。本研究推測如果對方的地位比欺騙者高，相比于對方地位低的情況，欺騙更難成功，因為地位高的個體更善於洞察來自低地位個體的欺騙。在對方地位高的情境下，為了成功欺騙，自欺策略更容易被啟動。在方法上，本研究將採用兩次記憶的程式，證實個體在欺騙他人時自己的記憶也發生改變，也就是出現了自欺。當第一次記憶時，在個體需要向對方隱瞞資訊的情境下，個體的記憶變差，無法提取出真實資訊，這種記憶失敗有助於隱瞞行為；當第二次記憶時，在欺騙物件不再存在的情境下，個體可以重新提取出之前無法回憶起的資訊。兩次記憶的差異說明個體通過記憶變差來瞞騙他人，從而證明人們會用自欺來幫助成功欺騙。 本研究將在理論和方法上突破以往對自欺的探討，通過創設不同欺騙探測概率的情境，驗證人際間自欺的存在及其功能。研究結果將有助於人們更好地理解欺騙及自欺的課題，以及不同地位的人之間的欺騙和防範欺騙的行為。

25401214.label: Realisation of objectives
25401214.value: All research objectives have been realized. The first objective is to advance the theory and methodology of interpersonal self-deception by conducting an empirical investigation of self-deception for the first time in the literature. I have advanced the theory of self-deception by identifying circumstances where interpersonal self-deception is likely to occur. Self-deception is the result of an “arms race” between deception and the detection of deception. Self-deceivers store truthful information in the unconscious, whereas they present false information to others as well as to their conscious self. Because self-deceivers cannot access the truth in their unconscious, they can genuinely communicate the false information without leaking cues for detection. Those cues include unnatural facial expression, slight movement of body or hand, and change of voice pitch, all of which may reveal the ongoing deception. Because self-deception is evolved to countermine detection of deception, it should be sensitive to situations registering different probabilities of detection with individuals being more likely to self-deceive when sensing a higher chance of detection. Social status registers different probabilities of detection. The second objective is therefore to examine the function of social status in inducing self-deception. A high-status detector or deceived target may register high probability of deception detection, because high-status individuals have been adaptive to detect deception more than low-status ones in the human evolutionary history. Compared to low-status counterparts, high-status individuals are less likely to deceive but are more likely to detect deception because they have more honest means (through force or by changing the rules) to acquire resources and have more resources to lose in a deceptive ploy. Moreover, high-status individuals have the power to punish. Therefore, individuals are likely to self-deceive for escaping detection and subsequent punishment if their status are lower than that of the deceived. In a series of experiments, I manipulated status among participants. In a pair of participants who played out a deceiver and the deceived, the high-status participant (by experimental manipulation that was randomly assigned) had the power to evaluate the work of the counterparty, whereas the low-status party (again by randomly assigned manipulation) had to submit his/her work to the high-status party for evaluation. The power of evaluating others and the inferiority of being evaluated has been shown to generate perceptions of a status-based hierarchy. The manipulation of status enabled an empirical verification of self-deception compared to deception under different conditions registering high versus low probability of deception detection. Through these experiments, I have advanced the methodology of self-deception, realizing the third objective of introducing and developing a dual memory paradigm that bypasses the impossibility of the unconscious in falsifying self-deception. The dual memory paradigm offers a self-deceiver two chances to retrieve (or distort) encoded information. The first retrieval occurs in the presence of the deceived and during an ongoing deception, whereas the second retrieval occurs in the absence of the deceived after a successful deception. Self-deception occurs in the first retrieval when the deceiver fails to retrieve or distorts encoded information due to the motivation to deceive and to escape detection. In the second retrieval, the deceiver may recall the truthful information that was once withheld from the conscious mind to serve self-interest and achieve fitness gains. In the experiments, participants were motivated to conceal the truthful information of “committing misconduct” from the deceived. Apart from what they told the deceived, the participants were asked to indicate what they actually remembered. Admitting misconduct, or offering truthful information, or detection of deception would result in deduction of monetary reward to the participants. They freely decided whether to deceive or not. Under the motivation of deception, had a participant forgotten his or her “misconduct” and honestly told the deceived that he or she had done nothing wrong, self-deception is therefore verified through this dual retrieval process. The forth objective is to separate out deception from self-deception by applying physiological tests, e.g., galvanic skin conductance and heartbeat. I realized this objective by measuring physiological responses of heartbeat, respiration, pulse, and skin conductance while participants were interacting with the deceived target. Sometimes deceivers may feel nervous and stressful while deceiving others and their blood pressure will increase due to peripheral vasoconstriction. As a compensation for the increased blood pressure, the heart rate and pulse rate decrease to maintain the homeostasis of blood pressure. Moreover, in contrast to common misconception that lying results in rapid breathing rhythm and increasing heart rate, deception was empirically demonstrated to decrease respiration, slow down cardiac rhythm, and constrict finger blood vessels. The decreased respiration, heart rate, and pulse rate are caused by a disturbed function of the autonomic nervous system induced by increased cognitive loads during deception. By contrast, skin conductance response increased during both deception and self-deception, because it indicated both conscious and unconscious awareness of truth information that contradicts false information presented to others. By observing changes of the above-mentioned physiological indicators, we can distinguish between deception and self-deception.

25401214.label: Major findings and research outcome
25401214.value: The purpose of this study is to empirically investigate interpersonal self-deception played out between low-status individuals as deceivers and high-status individuals as detectors. Self-deception was conceptualized to occur in contexts where detection of deception is high and subsequent punishment for deception is severe (Lu, in press). High-status individuals have more direct means including physical coercion to acquire resources than do low-status individuals, who are likely to realize self-interest by hiding resources or concealing truthful information. A dual-retrieval memory system was employed to operationalize self-deception, allowing individuals to retrieve truthful information twice – once under the motivation to deceive and once after deception is complete. Self-deception is demonstrated if in the first retrieval individuals distort memory by forgetting the truthful information and honestly offer false information. In the second retrieval where the motivation to deceive disappears, truthful information that once has been withheld from the self and others will then be retrieved to benefit the self. Major findings show that the low-status individuals recalled less truthful information in the first retrieval when they were motivated to deceive the high-status counterparty and they recalled more truthful information in the second retrieval after the deception had been completed, whereas high-status individuals retrieved a similar amount of truthful information during and after deception (Lu, 2016). Results of physiological responses help verify deception and self-deception (Lu, in preparation). Heart rate (HR), respiration, finger pulse, and skin conductance responses (SCR) were measured during deception. These physiological indicators have been extensively used in studies of detection of deception. While deceiving others, a blatant deceiver keeps both truthful and false information in the consciousness but presents only the false information to others, whereas a self-deceiver or an honest person keeps only one type of information in the consciousness (the self-deceiver keeps the falsehood and the honest one keeps the truth). The increased cognitive load of the deceiver causes a disturbed function of the autonomic nervous system and physiological rigid in the person, resulting in a decrease of heart rate variability, pulse rate and respiratory rhythm. Consistent with previous studies, results of this project showed that heartbeat, respiration, and pulse all decreased for the deceivers compared to the self-deceivers and truth-tellers. SCR increased during deception regardless of whether deceivers were aware of the deception or not. Consistent with previous studies, we found that SCR in the deception and self-deception condition were higher than that in the honesty condition.

25401214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25401214.value: Theoretically, future studies can explore other conditions that induce self-deception. Findings of this project showed that low-status individuals may self-deceptively lie to high-status individuals, in order to escape detection and subsequent punishment. Other social situations such as lying to a group of people (e.g., lying in a political rally) who exert deception detection pressure as multiple detectors or lying in a moralistically charged situation (e.g., lying under oath) that induce additional detection pressure are also worth investigation. Methodologically, researchers can further examine other physiological and neurological responses when individuals are self-deceiving versus intentionally deceiving. According to previous studies, blood pressure increases and temperature of facial skin around the eyes increases when individuals intentionally deceive others. These physiological responses are caused by lying-induced stress and nervousness. Because self-deception incurs no stress on the deceiver, blood pressure and facial skin temperature should not differ from when the individual who is telling the truth. In addition, neurological responses measured by Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can be applied to detect deception. Future studies can employ these technologies to investigate self-deception.

25401214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25401214.value: Self-deception has evolved in humans and many other animals under pressure of deception detection. Thus, people self-deceive when they are afraid of being caught blatant deceiving. This project investigated whether people self-deceived by temporarily forgetting truthful information when self-servingly motivated to conceal such information from others, what social situations were likely to induce self-deception compared to deception, and how people’s physiological responses changed during deception and self-deception. I found that low-status individuals (by experimental manipulation) were more likely to self-deceive while lying to a high-status person than the other way around. This is because a high-status person has more power over a low-status person in detection of deception and implementation of punishment. I also found that, when deceiving, a person’s heartbeat, respiration, and pulse all decreased, but, when self-deceiving, these physiological responses remained unchanged. This is because an increased cognitive load of deceiving causes a disturbed function of the autonomic nervous system and physiological rigidity in the deceiver. A self-deceiver does not experience the increased cognitive load because the self-deceiver employs temporary memory loss or distortion to conveniently forget the truthful information and honestly conveys false information to the deceived.

25401414.label: Realisation of objectives
25401414.value: Four objectives of this project have been achieved. The study identified the differences in the prevalence of wanted and unwanted exposure to online pornography (Objective 1). In particular, both types of exposure increased linearly across early adolescence (Objective 2). Wanted exposure to online pornography gradually increased over time; while unwanted exposure to online pornography increased more rapidly as adolescents aged. Consistent with the literature, both types of exposure were associated with individual (e.g., gender, religious belief) and family factors (i.e., family functioning) (Objective 3). Male adolescents reported significantly higher levels of exposure to online pornography than their female counterparts. Adolescents with religious beliefs reported lower levels of wanted and unwanted exposure to online pornography than their counterparts with no religious beliefs. Family functioning was associated with a lower level of exposure to online pornography. Adolescents with higher levels of family mutuality and better communication with family members displayed lower levels of both types of exposure to online pornography. The impacts of both types of exposure on psychosocial have been supported in the cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses (Objective 4). Early exposure to online pornography was negatively related to adolescent developmental outcomes. This association was more salient in wanted exposure to online pornography. This project provides a better understanding on the influence of different types of exposure to online pornography on adolescent developmental outcomes during early adolescence. Helping adolescents to handle online pornography can be facilitated by creating an open and warm communication with trusted adults concerning topics about sex or sexuality. This project highlights the importance to differentiate the nature of exposure to online pornography and how these differences may have implications on adolescent development.

25401414.label: Major findings and research outcome
25401414.value: Major findings In this project, a total of 1,401 secondary school students were invited to participate in a three-year longitudinal study. This project has revealed the prevalence of online pornography differs by the nature exposure among early adolescents. More specifically, older adolescents, especially males, were likely to be exposed to pornography than their young female counterparts. Also, adolescents having a dating relationship reported higher levels of unwanted and wanted exposure to online pornography than their counterparts who had no dating relationship. Apart from the demographic characteristics, this project explored how contextual factors were associated with different online activities. Social support was linked with frequent internet use. In particular, perceived support from friends was significantly related to computer-mediated communication and the use of social network sites. Family functioning and positive youth development have been associated with lower exposure to online pornography, less likely to be involved in problem behaviors and better academic performance. Also, groups with different profiles for online activities were found. Lastly, the temporal relationships between exposure to online pornography and psychological well-being were explored in this project. Early exposure to online pornography was related to later depressive symptoms. It is noteworthy that this longitudinal effect was only found in wanted exposure, but not in unwanted exposure, to online pornography. Furthermore, life satisfaction appears to be a predictor, rather the outcome, of this behavior. These findings highlight the importance to study the long-term effects of exposure to online pornography during adolescence. This project contributes to a deeper understanding of the impacts of exposure to online pornography. Research outcome Based on the data of this project, four manuscripts have been published; two are still under review (see Part C). Also, the PI presented the findings in an international conference (oral presentation).

25401414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25401414.value: This project provides insights to the literature by differentiating the nature of exposure to online pornography and assessing its impacts during early adolescence. It highlights the dynamic relations between exposure to online pornography and adolescent developmental outcomes over time. Future research could extend the project by exploring the long-term impact of exposure to online pornography using a longer length of time (i.e., from early to late adolescence). This would enable us to have a better understanding of the relationships between exposure to online pornography and adolescent outcomes.

25401414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25401414.value: Nowadays, the internet becomes an essential part of our daily lives. With 24/7 access, adolescents can search for online sexual and related health information anonymously with minimal restrictions. Adolescents are likely to use the internet to satisfy their sexual interests and pursuits, especially when they enter the puberty. There is an increasing concern regarding the impacts of online pornography on adolescents. This project assessed the factors and consequences of exposure to online pornography during early adolescence. The findings of the project have shown that exposure to online pornography is associated with individual and social factors. In particular, the impacts of online pornography differ by the nature of exposure (unwanted and wanted). This project underlines the importance of considering the long-term relationships and factors related to this behavior. Given the popularity of the internet, this project provides insights on promoting internet literacy among adolescents.

25401614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25401614.value: The proposed research will evaluate, using empirical methods, the extent to which the statutory derivative action has promoted the right of shareholders to sue in the courts of Hong Kong. The derivative action is a legal remedy that allows a shareholder to enforce the rights of the company. The action is pertinent when a company, after suffering injury typically from the misconduct of its members or directors, cannot obtain relief because the organs that make the corporate decisions refuse to take protective actions. In such a situation the derivative action entitles a willing shareholder to defend the rights of the company by starting litigation on behalf and for the interest of the company. To this extent, the derivative action fosters shareholder protection and good corporate governance. Two types of derivative action are currently allowed in Hong Kong, namely the statutory derivative action (SDA) and the common law derivative action (CDA). The SDA was created in 2005 in order to correct the shortcomings of the long-standing CDA and, consequently, make it easier for shareholders to file a derivative action. However, to what extent the SDA’s more advantageous rules have effectively improved the right of shareholders to sue in the practice of enforcement has not been evident. There has been no study in Hong Kong evaluating systematically the extent and characteristics of the enforcement of the SDA. The proposed research will fill this gap. The operation of the SDA in court will be described and compared with that of the CDA. Unlike any other prior study of the derivative action in Hong Kong, this research will generate results using empirical methods. Measures of legal costs, discovery of evidence, defendants, cause of action and leave of court will be used, as will be a unique database (built in our preliminary research) containing ninety-two cases of both SDAs and CDAs. Data are extracted from the identified cases and categorized systematically. Both descriptive and inferential statistics will be produced. Non-parametric tests, especially the Chi-square test, will be utilized to make diverse comparisons between the groups of cases (SDA cases, pre-2005 CDA cases and post-2005 CDA cases). The findings will tell us more about the extent to which the SDA has delivered increased shareholder protection in Hong Kong. They will also inform the discussion of law reform in relation to the SDA and CDA. The need for reform has been strongly emphasized in the literature.

25401614.label: Realisation of objectives
25401614.value: Limitations of the Research The PI believes that the project objectives have been met. There have been limitations, however, that prevented a more productive implementation of this project. The process of reading and categorizing the content of Statutory Derivative action (SDA) cases and Common Law Derivative Action (CDA) cases proved very difficult and time-consuming. The information publicly available was seldom found clearly presented and complete. These elements added an extra burden to the already complex content of the cases. The most severe limitation found was the unavailability of public data on case outcomes. Whereas case facts and other case characteristics could be identified from diverse court documents, data on the win or lose outcome in litigation proved elusive. For example, in relation to the SDA cases we were able to collect systematically and without major problems the outcomes from the leave of court applications. In a high percentage of those cases in which the plaintiff was granted leave of court, however, it was unclear whether or not the plaintiff brought subsequently the substantive action. If the plaintiff did, whether such litigation was won, lost or settled could not be observed. In only four cases we succeeded in obtaining the final judgments for the SDA substantive litigation (in all of them the plaintiffs lost the case). In relation to the CDA, we found that out of the 19 cases in our database for the 2005-2014 period (excluding foreign-company CDAs), five cases were rejected, one case was won by the plaintiff, and one case was settled. In the other 12 cases the action is currently been administered at different stages of proceedings or has been settled, yet this is very difficult to observe or verify. Out of the 28 CDA cases identified during the 1995-2004 period, data on litigation outcomes was also incomplete enough to preclude the making of any reasonable group comparison. As the result of this data problem, the project could not make systematic (inferential statistics) comparisons between CDA and SDA cases, but deployed instead descriptive statistics. For example, a correlation between litigation occurrence rates and litigation outcomes could not be tested systematically. Findings from this research showed that the number of derivative actions almost doubled after the implementation of the SDA in 2005 (1995-2004 = 29; 2005-2014 = 53). Before the 2005 Reform plaintiffs started 2.9 DAs annually (29/10); after the 2005 Reform this number grew up to 5.3 (53/10). It is unclear, however, whether this higher incidence of DAs during the 2005-2014 period resulted also in more successful outcomes for plaintiffs relative to the 1995-2004 period. Such a question could not be addressed due to data limitations. This example illustrates well how the scope of the inferences that can be drawn from our research was constrained by data-availability problems. We attempted different avenues to find more data on case outcomes. For each SDA, that was granted leave of court by the courts and CDA (2005-2014) we identified the plaintiff’s law firm and contacted the solicitors using a brief survey. Yet nearly all solicitors who responded to our call told us that due to client confidentiality they could not share this information with us. We also visited the Hong Kong courts, without success. Ways out of the data-availability problem were found. Data from the outcomes of leave of court applications in SDA cases proved easier to obtain, more complete and faster to process. For this reason, like other studies of this type made in China, Australia or New Zealand found in the literature, the project output focused on this group of SDA applications, complemented with available data from CDAs as well as firm data collected from the Companies Registry. Since most of the firms involved in DA cases were private firms, firm data was also of limited access.

25401614.label: Major findings and research outcome
25401614.value: It was investigated how shareholders have exercised their choice between the SDA and CDA during the 2005-2014 period. It was found that the SDA did prevail over the CDA to become the preferred choice among those members that exercised the right to sue derivatively. But this outcome occurred gradually through a transitional period. Although the CDA was chosen more often than the SDA in the first five years of implementation (2005-09), this trend reverted sharply in the following five years (2010-14). With the SDA becoming the choice of preference, it was investigated to what extent the SDA increased the ability of shareholders to sue derivatively during the period 2005-2014. Results showed that leave of court applications were granted in 90 percent of the cases during the period 2005-09, whereas cost indemnity orders in relation to the leave of court proceedings were granted at a moderate rate during 2005-2014. This evidence is consistent with the SDA having strengthened the ability of members to bring derivative actions. However, the problem of funding seems to have stubbornly persisted in relation to the applications for indemnity covering the costs to be incurred by the plaintiff in the SDA substantive litigation: the courts disapproved all such applications. In relation to the outcomes from SDA substantive litigation, the view was confirmed that during the period 2005-14 the greater access or ability to sue derivatively need not, and indeed did not, entail more successful outcomes in SDA litigation. The plaintiffs lost their derivative action case in all four final judgments in our dataset. Our findings have also shown that important challenges remain ahead, with policy implications. The evidence produced in this article calls for the merits of preserving the CDA in Hong Kong to be re-assessed. That the SDA has failed to resolve the long-standing problem of funding of derivative litigation is a worrisome effect to the extent that litigation costs are a key factor influencing the exercise of the right to sue. Since no SDA litigation case was found where the plaintiff won the case, it is difficult to see how the SDA can deliver on its core functions in terms of compensating harm and deterring misconduct. In the absence of a more effective regime of derivative action litigation, attention must be drawn to other complementary tools for the protection of minority shareholders.

25401614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25401614.value: The lack of publicly available data did not allow us to focus on litigation outcomes such as win/lose in final DA judgments. However, there is room to shift focus towards evaluating the shareholders’ right to sue. More particularly, from our hand-collected data the set of conflicts that gave rise to a party entering a derivative action (either a CDA or SDA) can be well identified for all DAs. Further research can describe/categorize the set of conflicts that triggered derivative actions in Hong Kong, and analyse to what extent this set of conflicts has or not widened since the creation of the SDA. A finding showing that the set of conflicts has widened (for example, due to the removal of the legal requirement of ‘control’ in the SDA or a wider definition of the relevant conduct ‘misconduct’) would be indicative of increased protection, for the right to sue has been utilized in more diverse situations. The weakness of this analysis is the impossibility of connecting the resulting increased access to sue with litigation outcomes.

25401614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25401614.value: Since 2005 two types of derivative actions have coexisted in Hong Kong, the CDA and SDA. This setting created room for an investigation into how shareholders exercised their choice of derivative action during this period, and into whether the creation of the SDA in 2005 has resulted in increased shareholder protection. It was found that during the 2005-2014 period the SDA became the most preferred remedy, a trend that, if consolidated, will challenge the utility of preserving the CDA in Hong Kong. Even so, the SDA performed below expectations. It failed to resolve the problem of funding which seriously discourages derivative action litigation. Moreover, not a single case was observed where the plaintiff ended up winning the SDA litigation and obtaining court relief. This litigation outcome casts serious doubt whether the SDA has thus far met its core functions in regards to compensating corporate harm and deterring future misconduct. In the absence of a more effective regime of derivative action litigation, attention must be drawn to other complementary tools for the protection of minority shareholders.
