26300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26300014.value: New materials with peculiar properties are revolutionizing technology. The discovery of a high-temperature superconductor, a graphene, or a topological insulator, for example, inspires not only the physical science, but also extensive applications in cutting-edge technology. The exotic phenomena in those materials stem from subtle control of electrons with the intrinsic electro-magnetic field and symmetry arising from the crystal structure. Synthesizing such materials often requires extremely clean preparation to minimize defects. Recently, ultracold atoms have revolutionized the synthesis and characterization of new quantum materials. Ultraocold atoms, laser-cooled and trapped in a so-called optical lattice, mimic the subtle behavior of electrons in solid-state materials, for example simulating the Hubbard model describing the quantum behavior of two fundamental classes of particles, bosons and fermions. Over the past few years, several breakthroughs came when novel manipulations of atoms using non-standard optical lattices or artificial gauge fields were demonstrated, and such as when a single atom trapped in a lattice was directly detected with single-site resolution. Despite their great success, fermions mimicking electrons have not been implemented in a novel optical lattice under the single-atom microscope due to the intrinsic difficulties associated with the electronic structure of the atom. In this work, we propose to construct an apparatus producing ultracold ytterbium atoms and to develop a fermionic single-atom microscopy with the non-standard optical lattice. The ytterbium atom has rich atomic structure and novel optical transitions. These properties make it suitable for developing fermionic single-atom microscopy and after combining it with a novel optical lattice. We propose to examine several long-standing many-body physics problems related to magnetism and the flat band where the energy of particles is degenerate. Our objective is to investigate possible localized states like a quasi-supersolid phase in the flat band where the particle energy is dispersionless. We will also investigate ferromagnetism in the ytterbium atomic gas with high spin symmetry (so-called SU(N) symmetry). The high spin plays an important role in a gas of ytterbium atoms in contrast to the solid-state where the spin fluctuation effect is suppressed for high spins. Our new approach will dramatically advance designing and characterizing new quantum materials with ultracold atoms. 具有特殊屬性的新奇材料如高溫超導體，石墨烯，拓撲絕緣體的發掘為科學技術帶來了革命性的改變，這些材料不僅僅促進了物理科學的發展，更是廣泛大量的應用在了各種前沿科學技術中。利用材料本身固有的電磁場和來源於晶格結構的對稱性，電子的行為可以被精細控制進而使材料展現出各種奇特的現象。但是，為了最大程度減少材料中的缺陷，材料的合成往往對製備過程的潔淨度有著極其嚴苛的要求。 近年來，超冷原子技術的出現使得合成和表徵新型量子材料有了革命性的進步。經過激光冷卻與囚禁，最終被裝載在光學晶格中的超冷原子可以很好的模擬真實固體材料中電子的各種行為，例如模擬哈巴德(Hubbard)模型中描述的兩種基本粒子——玻色子與費米子的量子行為。 在過去的幾年裡，非標準光學晶格的出現，人造規範場技術的成熟，以及直接觀測被囚禁在單個光學晶格格點中的單個原子技術的出現，更使得該領域有了突破性的進展。但是，儘管如此，受限於的電子結構本身特性，在新型光學晶格里通過單格點分辨率顯微鏡觀察費米子模擬電子行為尚未實現。 在該研究計劃中，我們計劃搭建一套超冷鐿原子製備系統並非製造非標準光學晶格以及單原子費米子顯微鏡系統。鐿原子本身有著豐富的原子結構和奇特的光學躍遷過程，結合新型光學晶格技術，這些特性使得其成為發展單原子費米子顯微鏡系統的良好選擇。 我們的計劃致力於研究與磁學和能量簡併的平帶中粒子行為相關的一些由來已久的多體物理問題。我們將探索可能的局域態行為，例如粒子能量沒有色散的平帶中的準超固體相，以及高自旋對稱性(也稱為SU(N)對稱性)的鐿原子氣體中的鐵磁相。相比在固體材料中由於自旋漲落效應而被抑制的高自旋對稱性行為，在超冷鐿原子氣體中，高自旋對稱性將扮演十分重要的角色。我們的研究將有力的推動超冷原子技術在新型量子材料設計與表徵領域的應用。

26300014.label: Realisation of objectives
26300014.value: (Objective 1) We figured out the recipe to produce a tunable zigzag and sawtooth lattice which contains a flat band structure using a tunable superlattice technique. At the same time, we devised alternative method to create effective zigzag lattice in a synthetic dimension using spin-orbit coupling in a Raman-dressed lattice. References: T. Zhang et al., Scientific Reports 5, 16044 (2015) B. Song et al., Science Advances 4, eaao4748 (2018) (Objective 2) We demonstrate the engineered flatter band structure using strong spin-orbit coupling in 1D and 2D optical lattices. References: B. Song et al., Science Advances 4, eaao4748 (2018) B. Song et al., Nature Physics 15 911-916 (2019) (Objective 3) The high-resolution optical imaging has been setup and demonstrated in a ytterbium quantum gas apparatus. References: PhD Thesis, Yueyang Zhou, HKUST 2018 PhD Thesis, Bo Song, HKUST 2019 (Objective 4,5 and 6) We have substantially achieved Objectives 4,5 and 6. For Objectives 4 and 5, we demonstrated how the collective property depends on the spin multiplicity (i.e. SU(N) symmetry) by measuring the collective oscillations including dipole, breathing and quadrupole modes. The measured collective oscillation frequencies indirectly reflect the thermodynamic properties of the SU(N) Fermi gas, and therefore this measurement would lead to the investigation of spin susceptibility in the system. To enhance the interaction effect, we implement quasi-2D geometry and increase the interaction energy induced by confinement. The collective-mode measurement allows us to reveal SU(N) characteristics, and can be applicable to investigate the magnetism in Fermi gases in general. For Objective 6, we already have demonstrated the way to create a zigzag optical lattice. Reference: Chengdong He et al. Collective excitations in two-dimensional SU(N) Fermi gases with tunable spin Under Review, arXiv:1905.10815 (2019) T. Zhang et al., Scientific Reports 5, 16044 (2015) Reason for under-achievements and outline attempts: The remaining challenge for Objectives 4-6 is the experimental tuning of the atom-atom interaction towards strongly interacting regime. To achieve this, we will prepare a mixture of 1S0-3P0 states and utilize the inter-orbital Feshbach resonance. However, the construction of the Clock laser that is necessary to address the 3P0 state has been delayed due to the technical noises that limit the laser linewidth. In the recent work [C.He et al. arXiv:1905.10815 (2019)], however, we partially control the interaction parameter in 2D. Attempts to overcome problems: Building a clock laser system : Currently, we are building up the clock laser system, and will utilize the orbital Feshbach resonance to control atom-atom interactions. Currently, we have been attempting to reduce the noise of the system by (1) isolating the laser system from noisy floor, (2) increasing the feedback bandwidth and (3) stabilizing the laser frequency with respect to the stable optical cavity. It is expected that the clock laser system will be ready within a few months. On the measurement side, we expect to successfully investigate magnetic properties of the SU(N) Fermi gas based on the technique developed in the work [C.He et al. arXiv:1905.10815 (2019)]. In this regards, we expect to fully achieve the objectives within one year.

26300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
26300014.value: (1) Observation of nodal-line semimetal with ultracold fermions in an optical lattice For a long time, it has been an open challenge in ultracold atom experiments to realize and observe 3D topological matters. While numerous schemes have been proposed, the experimental complexity and the characterization of the 3D band structure acted as a barrier against experimental groups achieving this outstanding goal. Our group for the first time realized and observed the 3D topological band with ultracold atoms. In our work, we realized a 3D topological semimetal with nodal lines by an innovative approach to implement 2D SO coupling in an optical lattice together with a 1D linear SO coupling, and develop a fundamentally new technique to successfully observe the topology of the 3D semimetal [References: B. Song et al., Nature Physics 15 911-916 (2019) ] (2) Realization of symmetry-protected topological phase for ultracold atoms We proposed a novel topological phase (known as a symmetry-protected topological phase) and experimentally observed such topological phases with ultracold fermions for the first time. Our work highlights the remarkable potential of realizing and exploring new topological states with ultracold atoms and beyond natural conditions. [References: Song et al., Science Advances 4, eaao4748 (2018)] (3) First realization of spin-orbit-coupled two-electron atoms Spin-orbit (SO) coupling, linking the particle’s spin to momentum, is the essential ingredient to realize novel quantum phenomena. Until 2016, however, SO coupling has been realized only for Alkali fermionic 40K and 6Li atoms in 2012 (also for bosonic 87Rb atoms in 2011), but the Raman transition that locks momentum to the atomic spin inevitably causes spontaneous heating. This heating has limited the ability to observe interacting many-body phenomena in a fermionic atomic system that necessitates long time scales. In 2016, we broke through this barrier by implementing SO coupling in a Fermi gas of 173Yb atoms using a narrow optical transition. This work has opened new possibilities to explore SO coupling physics with ultracold two-electron fermions, and has inspired a variety of theoretical and experimental works. [References: Song et al., Phys. Rev. A Rapid Communications 94, 061604(R) (2016)]

26300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26300014.value: As an immediate follow-up development, we plan to improve the clock laser system and realize a two-orbital Fermi gas toward the strongly interacting regime. This will allow us to control atom-atom interactions, and our collective-mode measurement can be used to investigate the magnetic property in the system. We are in the process of isolating the clock laser system from the mechanical and sound noises. In parallel, we will experimentally explore the interacting fermionic system with tunable interactions, and check if the system is favourable toward a fermionic superfluid state.

26300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26300014.value: Quantum-enabled technology is expected to change the world in terms of how intractable problems can be efficiently solved with quantum computing. The project is about building synthetic quantum matter with ultracold atoms, prepared near the absolute zero temperature, and investigating novel physical properties of complex material. For the purpose, we constructed an apparatus, so-called an atomic quantum simulator, in which ultracold atoms can be arranged inside crystalline lattice structure mimicking the electron behaviour in solids. In the project, we investigated unconventional quantum systems, a Fermi gas with SU(N) symmetry and fermions in topological bands. This project is forward-looking and exploratory work, but we have demonstrated a proto-type quantum-enabled device, which will be applicable in interdisciplinary fields including computational material science, information technology and quantum technology.

26400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26400014.value: The experiences we have in our early years form a crucial foundation for our identity and preferences as adults. At a young age, children largely rely on information provided by others to understand the world in which they live. Children are active in their efforts to learn from and socialize with the people around them, judging their reliability based on a variety of cues. In the following study, using rigorous empirical methods, we propose to examine the potential impact of one cue in particular – social group membership – on children’s learning and socializing preferences. Specifically, we investigate whether, by the time they are in pre-primary school, Hong Kong Chinese children are able to identify with their own ethnic group (Chinese), as well as distinguish it from two other ethnic groups commonly seen in Hong Kong (White and Southeast Asian). We also propose to examine whether children attend to ethnic group differences when making decisions about whom to trust when learning (e.g., learning the functions of unfamiliar objects) and when socializing (e.g., sharing secrets with others). Finally, we examine several factors that may influence children’s awareness of social group membership as well as the degree to which they prefer members of their own group for learning and socializing: place of residence (ethnically heterogeneous areas vs. ethnically homogenous areas), type of school (enrollment in an international or English Schools Foundation kindergarten vs. in a local Chinese kindergarten), and the presence or absence of Southeast Asian domestic workers in the home. We intend to collect our data from children enrolled in kindergartens, and will also collect demographic information from their parents and from government census data. The focus on children in Hong Kong will allow us to gain an understanding of how different kinds of social experiences, at home and at school, may influence children’s perceptions of themselves and of others. This study builds on previous scholarly work on early childhood development and education as well as on social cognitive development, much of which is based on research in Western cultures. By expanding into a non-Western cultural context, we expect our findings to offer insight into the potential universal impact of social group membership on preferences in learning and socializing. 幼兒時的經驗往往成為成年人身份與喜好的重要基礎。在這項研究計劃裡，我們將探討社會群組如何影響香港學前兒童的學習和社交偏好。具體而言，我們將調查香港的小朋友: 1) 是否能夠區分自己的族群（中國人）和其他族群（西方白人及東南亞人）的不同; 2) 在做出有關學習及社交的決定時，是否會考慮到自己的社會群組; 3) 在認知及喜歡其所屬社會群組上，是否會受到周圍環境（居住地，學校類型，與外籍傭人的接觸）的影響。我們打算進行問卷調查並參考政府普查數據，透過實驗來探討香港幼兒在不同的社會經驗下對自己以及他人的了解的影響。這項研究建立在過去幼兒發展、學前教育、以及社會認知發展等領域的研究成果; 這些成果的研究對象通常是在西方文化成長的幼兒。因此，我們希望這項研究計畫能夠增加對東方文化的幼兒的了解，深入探討社會群組在不同文化中是否對幼兒有相似的影響。

26400014.label: Realisation of objectives
26400014.value: All objectives have been realized. In total, I have recruited 224 Hong Kong Chinese pre-primary school children across five kindergartens and one playgroup center, collecting demographic information from the children's schools/playgroup center and from their primary caregivers to assess (among other factors) whether the family had domestic workers living at home. The information we have obtained from the experiments with the children (e.g., their learning and socializing preferences), from the parental surveys (e.g., the presence of domestic workers at home, ethnic composition of child's residential area), and from the schools (e.g., whether the school is local or international, number of Chinese and non-Chinese teachers among staff) have allowed us to address our three project objectives. More specifically, our experimental study with the children addressed project objectives 1 and 2, while responses from the caregivers and schools addressed project objective 3. Further information is provided in Section 6.1: Major findings and research outcome.

26400014.label: Major findings and research outcome
26400014.value: As we had originally proposed, we ran two experiments with our participants. The first experiment involved two computerized tasks that required children to differentiate between ethnically ambiguous faces that appeared either friendly or threatening. The second experiment required children to choose between ethnic ingroup and outgroup members when deciding from whom to learn and with whom to socialize. Both experiments allowed us to address the first two objectives. First, we have determined that Hong Kong Chinese pre-primary school children are sensitive to social group membership. They can differentiate between their ethnic ingroup (Chinese) and two different ethnic outgroups (White, Southeast Asian), and are capable of identifying with their own ethnic group. Second, we have also been able to quantify the extent to which children attend to ethnic group membership information when making decisions regarding whom to trust for learning and with whom to socialize. Specifically, children show a robust preference for their ethnic group members when deciding whom to trust for learning the functions of novel objects and whom to trust when sharing information and engaging in social activities. Finally, through questionnaires completed by the children's caregivers and through checks with the children's schools, we have been able to quantify the extent the following external factors are related to Hong Kong Chinese children’s awareness of ethnic group membership and the strength of their preferences for learning and socializing: a) place of residence; b) type of school; and c) presence of domestic workers in the home. While place of residence (given that the vast majority of children already live in areas that are predominantly Chinese) had limited impact on children's preferences, whether they attended an international or local kindergarten and whether they were being raised with a domestic worker at home did have impact on the degree to which they preferred their own ethnic group members. Of the two latter factors, type of school had the larger impact for learning and socializing preferences, although presence of a domestic worker at home influenced children's implicit ingroup preferences when they were comparing members of their ethnic group against members of the Southeast Asian outgroup. Our findings from the study have been presented at multiple international conferences and one research workshop, and are also under review as two separate publications. Please see Part C for further details.

26400014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26400014.value: The present study investigated the sensitivity to social group information and social group preferences in Chinese pre-primary school children, who are members of the dominant ethnic group in Hong Kong. Our findings indicate that children demonstrate sensitivity to and robust preferences for their ethnic ingroup. However, given the differences in social status among the different ethnic groups in Hong Kong, we would like to further examine the extent to which children in Hong Kong weigh social status information alongside ethnic group information. We would also like to examine whether children from ethnic minorities in Hong Kong demonstrate similar levels of sensitivity to and preference for their ingroup, and to compare their responses more systematically with their Chinese peers. We are currently applying for funding from the Research Grants Council to continue our investigation on how children from different ethnic groups in Hong Kong consider and use social group information at a young age.

26400014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26400014.value: We examined whether ethnic Chinese pre-primary school children who were raised in Hong Kong were sensitive to social group membership information, differentiating between members of their own ethnic group (Chinese) and members of two other ethnic groups (White, Southeast Asian). We also examined whether children demonstrated a preference for their ethnic ingroup members, and whether this preference affected from whom they decided to learn and with whom they decided to socialize. Our study findings indicated that children were aware of social group membership differences at a young age, and also showed a preference for ethnic ingroup members when making learning and socializing decisions. However, unlike their same-aged peers from other cultures, Hong Kong Chinese children did not perceive ethnic outgroup members to be more threatening than ingroup members, suggesting that the strength of their preferences may vary depending on the measures used. Children’s ingroup preferences were also affected by the specific outgroup ethnicity, the type of schools they attended, and the presence (or lack thereof) of a domestic worker at home. Our study is one of the first to examine how early-life experiences can influence Hong Kong Chinese children’s willingness to interact with individuals from different backgrounds.

26400114.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26400114.value: 蘇聯和美國在社會主義時期中國動畫電影產業中的角色

26400114.label: Project Objectives
26400114.value: To examine Sino-Soviet interactions in animated filmmaking in socialist China To explore the role of the U.S. in animated filmmaking in socialist China
rows: To examine Sino-Soviet interactions in animated filmmaking in socialist China
To explore the role of the U.S. in animated filmmaking in socialist China

26400114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26400114.value: This project aims to analyze the roles of the Soviet Union and the U.S. in animated filmmaking in socialist China between the 1940s and 1970s. As the major two superpowers during the cold war era, the Soviet Union and the U.S. exerted tremendous impact upon young socialist China. Numerous studies have addressed China's interactions with these two superpowers in terms of politics and diplomatic relations. However, their interactions in filmmaking, especially animated filmmaking, remain understudied. Animated film mainly targeted children and was often dismissed as a minor genre in socialist China. A close examination of these animated films will challenge and even subvert our traditional knowlege of the cold war era. The Soviet Union and the U.S. form an interesting contrast in terms of their animated interactions with socialist China. The Sino-Soviet encounter took place mainly in the materialist sphere—the advancement of animation technology and the emulation of the Soviet style. At the representational level, the Soviet Union was absent—no animated film produced in socialist China features the Soviet Union. However, in the case of the U.S. the opposite is true. At the very time when China cut off its ties with the U.S. due to cold war ideology, this enemy country took hold in the national imagination—many animated films produced in socialist China featured the U.S. The two kinds of transnational flows of culture were further complicated by the dynamic encounter between the Walt Disney Company and the world of Soviet animation. In addition, children, as the audience in socio-historical reality and as fictional figures on film, played a vital role in these cultural imaginaries, contacts, and entanglements. Tracking these multi-directional movements of culture at socio-historical and representational levels, the proposed project will offer insightful analyses that will cast new light on our conventional understanding of the socialist era. This proposed new project differs from the PI’s doctoral dissertation. The PI’s dissertation focuses on East Asia, while this proposed new project extends to the West. The PI’s dissertation discusses the transnational flows of culture between China and Japan as well as the roles of Taiwan and ethnic minorities in animated filmmaking between the 1940s and 1970s. This proposed new project voyages out of East Asia to explore the roles of the Soviet Union and the U.S. in animated filmmaking in socialist China. It will serve as a crucial building block for the PI’s first book on Chinese animation. 此項目旨在分析社會主義時期時，蘇聯和美國在中國動畫電影產業中的角色。作為冷戰時期的兩個超級大國，蘇聯和美國對社會主義中國產生了極大的影響。許多研究都分析了在政治和外交方面，中國和這兩個超級大國之間的關聯。然而，它們之間在電影文化產業，特別是動畫電影產業方面的關係，還沒有太多深入的研究。在社會主義中國，動畫電影主要以兒童為觀眾，因而常常被誤認為是一種次要的藝術形式，不足以進行嚴肅的研究。然而，通過仔細地發掘研究，這些被忽略了的動畫電影往往能挑戰、甚至是顛覆我們對冷戰時期長期以來固有的印象和認識。 在和中國動畫電影的互動關係中，蘇聯和美國形成了極有意思的對比。中蘇之間的交流主要體現在物質層面上：對蘇聯動畫技術以及動畫外在客觀藝術形式的學習和模仿。在藝術再現和題材方面，蘇聯幾乎是不在場的：幾乎沒有一部中國動畫是以蘇聯為題材的。美國的情形正好相反。在冷戰意識形態的影響下，中國切斷了和美國的一切交往。 在那個年代，美國是資本主義的象征，其在中國的痕跡幾乎被抹殺得一乾二淨。然而，當在物質層面上美國的蹤跡無處可尋時，社會主義中國對它的藝術想像卻 愈加強烈，出現了大批以美國為題材的動畫電影。值得一提的是，中國和這兩個超級大國之間的關係並不是平行、互不相關的。美國迪斯尼和蘇聯動畫之間的交錯使得中國和這兩個超級大國之間的關係變得更加錯綜複雜。此項目將會從社會歷史和藝術再現及題材兩方面，追蹤這些多方位的文化流動和關聯，以此重新認識社會主義時期中國的文化。 該項目是全新的，有別於作者的博士論文。作者的博士論文涵蓋社會主義時期的中國動畫，但探討的對象是東亞，而該新項目擴展到西方。作者的博士論文研究的是在四十年代和七十年代之間，中國和日本動畫之間的姻緣關係，以及臺灣和少數民族在中國動畫形成中的角色。該新項目走出亞洲，研究在動畫文化產業方面，社會主義中國和蘇聯以及美國兩個超級大國之間錯綜複雜的關係。它將成為作者第一本專著裏的一個重要組成部分。

26400114.label: Realisation of objectives
26400114.value: The two objectives have been realized. I have addressed the two objectives in Chapter 3 of my first monograph, Animated Encounters: Transnational Movements of Chinese Animation, 1940s-1970s, published by the University of Hawaii Press in February 2019. https://uhpress.hawaii.edu/title/animated-encounters-transnational-movements-of-chinese-animation-1940s-1970s/ For Objective 1, I discussed how the rise of the National Style (such as ink-painting animation) in Chinese animated filmmaking in the late 1950s and early 1960s took place in relation to the Soviet Union. The deteriorating Sino-Soviet relationship towards the late 1950s triggered the rise of cultural nationalism and the National Style in China. In addition, I analyzed the Black Crow incident regarding the alleged Soviet influence in Chinese animation in the late 1950s. For Objective 2, I discussed how the U.S. was imagined and represented in Chinese animation in the late 1950s and early 1950s at a time when the US presence was erased in everyday life and in live-action films. It generated an "international style" by portraying the U.S. as subject matter with a more de-sinicized animation style such as cartoon and caricature (not ink-painting, papercutting...characteristic of China). The late 1950s and early 1960s were often regarded as the golden age of the National Style (ink-painting, papercutting, paperfolding animation). I demonstrate that it was also the golden age of the International Style (in relation to the US). I therefore reframe the late 1950s and early 1960s as the era of the Inter/National Style, effectively challenging the pure national style/identity argument prominent in Chinese animation studies.

26400114.label: Major findings and research outcome
26400114.value: The major findings of this project is that Chinese animated films were not made in the vacuum of an isolated national space. Rather, it was always situated in an international context in relation to the Soviet Union and the US in the 1950s and 1960s, thus challenging the stereotype of the socialist years as a closed system due to Cold War ideology. The major research outcome of this project is the publication of my first monograph in English: Animated Encounters: Transnational Movements of Chinese Animation, 1940s-1970s, published by the University of Hawaii Press in February 2019. I located my analysis of Chinese animation in relation to the Soviet Union and the U.S. in the 1950s and early 1960s.

26400114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26400114.value: I am now working on two articles or book chapters derived from this project. One on the "International Style" animated films featuring the U.S. I've completed a preliminary draft. One on the failed Sino-Soviet co-production of an animated feature film titled Nezha Conquers the Dragon King. When I started this project in Hong Kong several years ago, it was very difficult for me to hire a Russian RA. During my stay at Harvard-Yenching in 2018, I was lucky enough to locate two Russian RAs there. They will complete their research and collect Russian materials for me in the summer of 2019. I will then start to write.

26400114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26400114.value: Classical Chinese animation made during the socialist years has long been regarded as stubbornly national by using traditional Chinese arts, literature, and culture. This project challenges this view by demonstrating the international dimensions of classical Chinese animated filmmaking. It analyzes the Soviet Style adopted and later abandoned in Chinese animated filmmaking in the 1950s; it also analyzes the "international motif" animated films featuring the U.S. with a more international or even modernist style made in the late 1950s and early 1960s. The late 1950s and early 1960s, often regarded as the golden age of the Chinese "national style," was redefined as the era of the "inter/national style." Foregrounding the internationality of Chinese animated filmmaking, this project subverts the stereotype of this era as a closed system due to Cold War isolationism.

26500014.value: 創業型企業董事會對創新的影響

26500014.label: Project Objectives
26500014.value: To identify the impact of power and status discrepancies on venture innovation. To offer a methodology for building board histories of ventures by integrating information from multiple databases.
rows: To identify the impact of power and status discrepancies on venture innovation.
To offer a methodology for building board histories of ventures by integrating information from multiple databases.

26500014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500014.value: ABSTRACT Despite the critical importance of innovation to entrepreneurial firms and the potentially large impact of boards of director in such ventures, there is little scholarly understanding of how venture boards influence innovation. The vast body of literature on boards of directors remains dominantly framed by the agency theory. However, an agency-theoretic approach to boards does not illuminate well the organizational forms (such as ventures) where there is a considerable alignment between the management and the firm. Since the main focus of agency-theoretic research is on minimizing the downsides created by principal-agent misalignment, there is little attention to how boards may assist in creating the upside value through innovation. Boards research using the resource dependence theory suggests that boards can provide useful resources for innovation, but this work does not examine how such director help may be potentially hindered by directors’ dynamics within the board, and empirically focuses on resource acquisition or firm performance rather than innovation. The research proposed here seeks to address this gap by examining the influence of boards of directors in creating value for a firm through innovation. More specifically, it focuses on how intra-board dynamics generated by power-status discrepancy, goal dissimilarity, and role experience affect a firm's product innovation, especially in ventures where the principal-agent problem is not a primary concern. The empirical context is the medical devices sector in the US where innovation is critical. This research has potentially many contributions. To research on entrepreneurial process, this research adds by clarifying the role of boards of directors in innovation, while also identifying a novel methodology to build histories of boards of directors in ventures. To resource dependence theory, this research contributes by highlighting the importance of intra-board dynamics, and not just individual director characteristics, in resource provisioning. To agency theory, this research contributes by underscoring that principal-agent alignment is not enough for value creation. Instead, such alignment needs to be complemented by an appropriate board configuration that takes into account directors’ power, status, goals, and role experience. 創業型企業董事會對創新的影響 儘管創新對創業型企業極為重要，並且董事會在這樣的企業中可能發揮著巨大的影響，可是董事會如何影響企業創新的相關學術研究，則甚為缺乏。大部份對董事會的學術研究文獻中，都以代理理論為框架。然而，代理理論未必適用於這種組織形式（如創業型企業），因為這類企業和管理層之間的利益有相當的一致性。由於代理理論研究的重點是盡量減少委託代理偏差所產生的負面影響，從而很少關注董事會如何透過創新幫助企業提升價值。依據資源依賴理論，有研究提出董事會可以為創新提供有效資源，但這類研究並沒有考慮如此獲得的資源可能受制於董事之間的互動，而且這類研究主要集中在資源獲取和企業績效的關係，而不是和創新的關係。 這裡提出的研究旨在填補以上空白，探查董事會在創新過程中，如何以其影響力為企業創造價值。更具體地說，本研究集中在董事會內的互動如何在權力與地位的差異，目標差異性，以及角色經驗的基礎上形成，從而影響企業的產品創新，特別是集中在董事會內的互動在委託代理問題不是首要問題的創業型企業中的影響。本研究以美國醫療器械行業作為實證研究的範圍，因為創新對該行業至為關鍵。 本研究有許多潛在的貢獻。對創業過程的研究，本研究能理清董事會在企業創新中的作用，同時也確定了一種嶄新的方法來為創業型企業建立董事會的歷史。對於資源依賴理論，這項研究能突顯董事會內的互動對資源供給的影響，而不僅僅是個別董事的影響。對於代理理論，本研究強調，委託代理一致性並不足以為企業創造價值。委託代理一致性要配以恰當的董事會架構，並需考慮到董事的權力，地位，目標和角色經驗。

26500014.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500014.value: This is the first paper on new ventures to empirically explore the impact of board of directors. It examines the consequences of different types of directors in new ventures - VC-directors, CVC-directors and founder-directors - on a wide range of outcomes that are related to new venture growth and development. 26500114.label: Project Objectives
26500114.value: Understand how problem familiarity, example familiarity, and problem-example relevance affect participants’ strategy in crowd-based contests. Understand how participants’ strategy affects design outcomes in crowd-based contests. Understand drivers of online banner ad performance.
rows: Understand how problem familiarity, example familiarity, and problem-example relevance affect participants’ strategy in crowd-based contests.
Understand how participants’ strategy affects design outcomes in crowd-based contests.
Understand drivers of online banner ad performance.

26500114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500114.value: This study focuses on the use of crowd-based design contests to acquire online banner ad designs. Firms spend a significant amount of money on online advertising, yet the typical return on their ad spending is relatively low. A key objective in this study is to examine how participants' familiarity with domains of ad design problems and client-provided examples, and relevance of examples to problems jointly affect participants' strategy and resulting design outcomes during ad design contests. Crowd-based design contests allow a large and diverse group of individuals to participate, and participants' familiarity with a particular design problem's domain is likely to be heterogeneous. Furthermore, clients often provide examples of designs that they like in design projects. Depending on the participants' familiarity with the examples' domain and the relevance of the examples to the design problems, these examples can affect participants' exploration of the design solutions space and their design submissions. What is even more critical is that these factors – problem familiarity, example familiarity, and problem-example relevance – could jointly affect designers' strategy and the attributes of their submissions during the contests. For example, the impact of problem familiarity on participants’ strategy could depend on their familiarity with client-provided examples and the relevance of the examples to the design problem. Investigating such joint effects is important and necessary as they reflect the dynamics in crowd-based contests. In addition, I want to understand how attributes of the resulting ad designs relate to ad performance. For instance, how does distinctiveness and attractiveness of the ad design affect performance such as click-through rate, consumers’ attitude towards the ad, and ad recall and recognition? I plan to conduct a randomized online design contest experiment, where I would recruit participants with diverse experience in graphic designing, and randomly assign design examples to them. Participants would be asked to submit ad designs based on certain stated criteria. I would then evaluate the attributes and performance of submitted designs. Apart from the theoretical contributions of understanding the joint effects of problem familiarity, example familiarity, and problem-example relevance, findings from this study can provide valuable implications to various groups of practitioners. Graphic designers should find the strategic implications from this study complementary to their technical knowledge. Firms and advertising agencies should be interested in knowing how to identify and acquire ad designs with better performance. 本研究聚焦于利用基于大众的设计竞赛来获得在线横幅广告的设计方案。尽管公司经常花费巨额资金于在线广告，但回报甚微。本文的一个核心目标是研究参与者对与广告设计问题相关领域知识的熟悉程度，对客户提供的示例的熟悉程度，及示例与问题的相关程度如何共同影响参与者在竞赛过程中的策略以及最终的设计结果。基于大众的设计竞赛能够吸引庞大且背景多样化的参赛群体，同时参赛者对某一个设计问题相关领域知识的熟悉程度也很有可能呈现出异质性。另外，在设计过程中客户也常会提供一些他们偏好的示例。由于参赛者对相关领域知识的熟悉度以及所提供示例与设计问题相关度的不同，这些示例也会不同地影响参赛者对可能解决方案的探索策略以及提交的最终方案。更为关键的是，这些因素 — 问题熟悉度，示例熟悉度，及问题示例相关度 — 可能会联合地影响参赛者的策略和最终提交的方案。比如，问题熟悉度对参赛者策略的影响可能会随着他们对客户提供的示例的熟悉度以及示例与问题的相关度不同而不同。研究这样的联合影响方式是重要且必要的，因为它能够反映出基于大众的设计比赛中的动态变化。此外，我也想了解最终得到的广告设计的属性如何影响这个广告的表现。比如，广告的独特性及吸引力如何影响它的点击率，以及消费者对这个广告的态度，回想和识别？我计划进行一个随机分配的网上设计竞赛实验。我将招募有多样化平面设计经验的参与者，然后随机分配给他们设计示例。参与者会被要求基于一些事先说明的标准来提交作品。事后我会评估这些作品的属性以及表现。除了在理解问题熟悉度，示例熟悉度，及问题-示例相关度的联合影响方式上做出理论贡献外，这个研究的结果也能够为不同的从业者提供宝贵的指导意见。平面设计者可以从中找到与他们专业知识相互补充的策略方面的指导。公司和广告代理机构也能够知道如何识别和获取表现更佳的广告设计方案。

26500114.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500114.value: The results in "Confirmation Bias in Adoption of Seeker Exemplars in Crowdsourcing Ideation Contests" show the solution examples that seekers provide in contests shape how contest participants generate ideas and solutions. While these examples could help participants to understand what the seekers are looking for in the solutions, they could also constraint the search and solution space due to the effect of confirmation bias. For example, when problem-related examples are provided, participants could shortlist and submit fewer ideas during idea generation. However, when unrelated examples are provided, the size of the search space and the number of ideas selected are lower. Hence, when seekers are using crowdsourcing contests to solicit ideas, they have to be mindful of the impacts of the solution examples that they provide. In the other paper, "Adopting Seekers’ Solution Exemplars in Ideation Contests: Antecedents and Consequences", I show that participants could improve the performance of their ideas when they incorporate seeker examples in their ideas; however, this impact is stronger for participants with lower domain experience for the problem in hand. Note: In Part C, I stated "No" for "Acknowledged the support of RGC" for the output "Confirmation Bias in Adoption of Seeker Exemplars in Crowdsourcing Ideation Contests". This is because during the review stages of this paper at MIS Quarterly and Academy of Management Annual Meeting, it was required to exclude the funding information for the purpose of blind review. I will acknowledge the support of RGC when it is appropriate to do so.

26500114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26500114.value: One of the two papers from this research project, "Adopting Seekers’ Solution Exemplars in Ideation Contests: Antecedents and Consequences", has been accepted at Information Systems Research. The other paper, "Confirmation Bias in Adoption of Seeker Exemplars in Crowdsourcing Ideation Contests", is currently being revised for a second round submission at MIS Quarterly and will also be presented at the Academy of Management Annual Meeting in August 2019. From the feedback of the respective reviews, there are a few potential areas of further development. First, there is a need to conduct deeper examinations of the ideation process during contests, and not simply looking at the ideation outcomes (e.g., quantity and quality of ideas). Doing so can increase our understanding of what participants do and suggest possible mechanisms to enhance the idea generation progress. Second, because the range of crowdsourcing contests is relatively broad (covering design contests, R&D problems, coding, etc.), it is also necessary to both (i) develop an overarching theory is is relevant in different types of contests and (ii) identify unique considerations and factors in the respective types of contests, so as to advance the literature in this topic.

26500114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500114.value: This research project shows that, although participants in crowdsourcing contests can generate good ideas to address problems, their contest behaviorsand strategies are affected by information such as solution examples that seekers provide. Hence, in order for us to tap into the wisdom of the crowd, we need to be aware of certain cognitive biases that could influence participants and how to strategically manage the contests so as to get the best outcomes from the contests.

26500514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500514.value: In recent years, we have witnessed a rapid growth of online labor marketplaces (e.g. oDesk, Elance, Guru, Freelancer, vWorker), which allow millions of freelancers to get hired and perform jobs online. The economic impact regarding employment created and revenue generated is significant and growing fast, but little is known about the consequences of such IT-enabled labor platforms on the distribution of the market outcomes between the two genders-a major topic in labor economics that has been studied extensively in traditional labor markets. This research aims to fill this gap by analyzing a comprehensive proprietary dataset from a leading online marketplace. Specifically, this research will examine the gender inequality in terms of the likelihood of getting hired and the earned wage rates, with special attention paid to the role of occupational segregation and online reputation. First, employers are likely to hold stereotypical beliefs about male and female workers when making their hiring decisions, especially for jobs perceived as masculine or feminine. Does hiring discrimination still exist online? To what extent can hiring discrimination explain the observed (if any) occupational gender segregation? What is the effect of platform-specific experience on moderating the hiring discrimination? Second, female workers in general receive less pay than their male counterparts with identical qualifications, which can be caused by their lower pay expectations, reluctance to ask for pay raises, or the cultural devaluation of female-dominated occupations. Is there a gender wage gap in online marketplaces? How much does between-occupation differentials contribute to the pay gap? Will the platform-specific experience narrow or widen the gender wage gap? This research can provide insights into the influence of IT on labor market outcomes on male and female workers by delving below the surface and exploring the gender inequality at the category level and across different experience levels. On the theoretical level, this study will advance our understanding of the mechanisms that drive gender inequality and occupational segregation. Also, it will contribute to the literature on the role of online reputation in reducing information asymmetry and redistributing the economic benefits among participants. Findings from this study will have practical implications to online employers and workers, designers of online marketplaces, and policy makers. 近年来，我们见证了网上劳动力市场（比如oDesk，Elance，Guru，Freelancer，vWorker）的快速增长。这让数以百万计的自由职业者可以通过在网上工作得到报酬。虽然这些市场在创造就业和产生收入所带来的经济影响非常大而且增长迅速，但我们对这种信息科技驱动的劳动力平台在两性之间的利益分配方面却知之甚少。性别差异是传统劳动力市场上被广泛研究的主要话题。这篇研究旨在通过分析从一个网上劳动力市场获得的数据集来填补这一空白。 具体来讲，本研究将会探讨不同性别在被雇佣概率和所赚薪水上的差异，并特别注意职业性别隔离和在线信誉在这其中所起的作用。首先，雇主在做雇佣决定时可能会对不同性别的工作者持有模式化的信念，尤其是在那些被认为是更适合于男性或者更适合于女性的职业上。那么，雇佣歧视在网上劳动力市场也存在吗？雇佣歧视在何种程度上可以解释观察到的（如果有的话）职业性别隔离？特定平台上的经验是否可以减少雇佣歧视呢？第二，女性工作者一般比同等能力的男性工作者获得的薪水低。原因可能是她们对薪酬的期望比较低，也有可能是因为她们不愿意要求加薪，或者传统观念上对女性主导工作的贬视。那么，在网上劳动力市场上两性之间是否还存在薪酬差距呢？这差距有多少可以归因于行业之间的差距？特定平台上的经验是会缩小还是加大性别薪酬差距呢？ 本研究探索网上劳动力市场中不同类别、不同经验水平上的性别不平等状况，希望借此来在信息科技对劳动力市场的影响方面提供一些有意义的见解。在理论方面，这篇研究将推动我们对隐藏在性别不平等和职业性别隔离后的机制的理解。此外，它还能对探索在线信誉在降低信息不对称方面和重新分配参与者的经济利益方面所产生的作用有所贡献。这项研究的结果将会对网上雇佣者、劳动者、在线市场的设计者、以及政策制定者有实际的影响。

26500514.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500514.value: Using a novel proprietary dataset from a leading online labor platform, we investigate the impact of gender-based stereotypes on hiring outcomes. After accounting for endogeneity via a holistic set of job and worker controls, a matched sample approach, and a quasi-experimental technique, we find evidence of a positive hiring bias in favor of female workers. An experiment was used to uncover the underlying gender-specific traits that could influence hiring outcomes. We find that the observed hiring bias diminishes as employers gain more hiring experience on the platform. In addition, the female hiring bias appears to stem solely from the consideration of applicants from developing countries, and not those from developed countries. Sub-analyses show that women are preferred in feminine-typed occupations while men do not enjoy higher hiring likelihoods in masculine-typed occupations. We also find that female employers are more susceptible to the female hiring bias compared to male employers. Our findings provide key insights for several groups of stakeholders including policymakers, platform owners, hiring managers, and workers. Managerial and practical implications are discussed.

26500514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26500514.value: Future efforts can be made to cross-validate our findings in other online labor marketplaces and strengthen the external validity of our study. Real experiments (e.g., by manipulating the gender information of job applicants) can also be conducted to further validate our results. We also make a few suggestions to platform owners. For example, platforms can make use of avatars and screen names that do not reveal workers’ demographic characteristics to minimize the hiring biases. Moreover, platforms should continue to provide detailed information that are indicative of applicants’ work quality, so that hiring decisions can be made based on merit and not on biases. Future studies can be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed strategies.

26500514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500514.value: The exponential growth of this nascent online phenomenon holds important social and economic implications, as the hiring decisions made on these online platforms implicate the incomes of millions of workers worldwide. Despite this importance, limited effort has been devoted to understanding whether potential hiring biases exist in online labor platforms and how they may affect hiring outcomes. Using a novel proprietary dataset from a leading online labor platform, we investigate the impact of gender-based stereotypes on hiring outcomes. By conducting a set of rigorous empirical tests, we find evidence of a positive hiring bias in favor of female workers. We also find that the observed hiring bias diminishes as employers gain more hiring experience on the platform. In addition, the female hiring bias appears to stem solely from the consideration of applicants from developing countries, and not those from developed countries. Sub-analyses show that women are preferred in feminine-typed occupations while men do not enjoy higher hiring likelihoods in masculine-typed occupations. We also find that female employers are more susceptible to the female hiring bias compared to male employers. Our findings provide key insights for several groups of stakeholders including policymakers, platform owners, hiring managers, and workers.

27100314.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27100314.value: 上皮间质转化（epithelial mesenchymal transition，EMT）是上皮细胞通过失去细胞间的粘附，重塑肌球蛋白以及粘着斑复合体转化成间质细胞的过程。EMT是至关的重要生物学过程，与胚胎发育中组织器官的发生，及肿瘤细胞的转移密切相关。神经嵴（neural crest， NC）是研究基因调控EMT过程的最具特征和常见的实验模型之一。神经嵴细胞(neural crest cell, NCCs)起源于背侧神经管的神经上皮细胞，经过EMT过程与神经上皮细胞分离，这一过程称之为分层，向外周迁移，分化为头面骨骼以及外周神经系统等。基因调控EMT是NC迁移以及分层的关键因素，基因突变将会导致先天性疾病。最近研究中发现一些转录因子在NC基因调控中扮演重要角色，但其具体作用机制不明。 体神经嵴细胞在胚胎发育特定的时间启动分层，一些转录因子的联合作用发挥主要的调控作用，包括Snail2，Fox3和一些Sox家族成员（如Sox9，Sox10）。我们前期鸡胚电穿孔研究中发现NC分层发生需Sox9的磷酸化，磷酸化Sox9可启动NC分层，但仅限于背侧NC起源区；而 Sox9与Snail2的协同作用可诱导全神经管部位NC启动分层，同时Fox3调控细胞间粘附分子的表达。这一结果显示Sox9磷酸化可独立控制NC分层的发生，然而Sox9磷酸化如何诱导NC细胞获得迁移能力仍未知。我们最近发现磷酸化的Sox9而非Sox9S64A,S181A(非磷酸化形式)和Sox10可诱导表达Rho GTP酶激活蛋白DLC1(Deleted in liver cancer1)。Nedd9((neural precursor cell expressed, developmentally downregulated)是细胞内骨架蛋白，是Cas家族成员，我们的研究亦发现磷酸化和非磷酸化Sox9均可诱导表达Nedd9，此外Sox9依赖Nedd9控制NC的分层的发生，这一过程可能通过调控细胞迁移因子Rho GTP酶活性完成。重要的是过表达DLC1抑制RhoA的活性，促进NC分层；Sox9+Nedd9-MO仍能诱导DLC1异位表达，但没有减少具有活性的的RhoA-GTP表达量，亦发现内源性DLC1蛋白与Nedd9可相互作用。基于以上研究，我们推测：DLC1依赖Nedd9，通过控制Rho GTP酶活性调节磷酸化的Sox9活性诱导NC的分层和迁移。 在这项研究中，我们拟进一步探索DLC1调控NC分层和迁移的机制。研究目的：（1）阐明DLC1在NC分层和迁移中的作用模式；（2）探讨Nedd9调控DLC1活性的机制；（3）通过研究DLC1与磷酸化的Sox9产生的效应分子的相互作用，阐明NC分层和迁移的机制。 本项目研究成果会从新的角度阐明Sox9磷酸化诱导NC迁移的机制；正确认识NC EMT分子机制，为认知及研究先天发育缺陷性疾病提供理论线索。

27100314.label: Realisation of objectives
27100314.value: Objective 1: To define the mode of action of DLC1 in neural crest (NC) delamination and migration 1.1 – To define the role of functional domains of DLC1 in NC delamination by in ovo electroporation. In ovo electroporation analysis showed that overexpression of a dominant-negative version of DLC1 (DN-DLC1), comprising of an amino-terminal region of DLC1 without the RhoGAP and START domains, resulted in inhibition of neural crest delamination. This construct exhibited an increased level of RHOA-GTP through dominant-negative inhibition of the endogenous RhoGAP activity of DLC1 using RHOA activation assay and fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based biosensor for RHOA. We speculated that DN-DLC1 functions by sequestrating co-factors away from the endogenous DLC1 protein, resulting in disruption of its polarized localization and RhoGAP activity. To further map the minimal region(s) of DN-DLC1 required for its inhibitory action, we generated two V5-tagged mutant constructs comprising of DLC1-SAM domain alone and DLC1-SAM with FAT (focal adhesion targeting) region (DN-DLC1 320), which has been shown to carry co-factor binding residues essential for focal adhesion localization and regulating RhoGAP activity. The results showed that overexpression of DN-DLC1-320 but not the SAM domain alone was able to inhibit NC delamination as shown by reduced expression of SOX10 on the transfected side. Thus, we revealed that the FAT region confers the inhibitory action of DN-DLC1 on NC motility. 1.2 – To examine the role of DLC1 in the regulation of RHO activity in the context of NC delamination and migration. The establishment of RHOA-FRET biosensor platform allows us to examine endogenous RHOA activity at the single cell level and also the dynamics of active RHOA distribution in time-lapse imaging of neural crest explant culture. We first examined the endogenous RHOA activity in delaminating and migrating NCCs in developing chick embryos. FRET imaging and measurement of the FRET index between the back and front of NCCs revealed high RHOA activity in the cytoplasm of the cell rear relative to low or fluctuating RHOA activity in membrane protrusions at the leading front of delaminating/early- and late-migrating NCCs. In contrast, moderate level of RHOA activity was detected and uniformly distributed throughout neuroepithelial cells in the neural tube. These results indicate that NCCs exhibit differential RHOA activity in subcellular localization as they undergo directional delamination and migration. Since DLC1 is a RhoGAP protein which inhibits RHOA activity, we then examined whether DLC1 is expressed in a complementary manner to RHOA in emigrating NCCs. Immunofluorescence analysis of neural tube explants showed that DLC1 exhibited asymmetric localization in the cytoplasm at the front of emigrating and migrating NCCs. Thus, polarized DLC1 expression displays a negative correlation with high RHOA activity at the cell back. These findings raise the possibility that DLC1 could involve in establishing polarized RHOA activity in delaminating NCCs. To address this issue, we overexpressed FRET biosensor together with full-length DLC1 cDNA into the caudal hemineural tube of stage 10-11 chick embryos. At 24 h post-transfection, analysis of FRET signals on embryonic sections showed that RHOA activity was reduced or barely detectable in DLC1 overexpressing NCCs, which exhibited lack of front-back polarity axis. Moreover, dorsal neuroepithelial cells overexpressing DLC1 were observed delaminating not only from the basal surface where laminin was lost but also infiltrated into the neural tube lumen through disruption of apical N-Cadherin expression, indicating that overexpression of DLC1 disrupted apical-basal polarity of dorsal neural tube. In contrast, overexpression of DN-DLC1 resulted in a marked elevation of RHOA activity, which was evently distributed throughout the cytoplasm of delaminating NCCs without distinct subcellular localization and cells appeared round in shape. The majority of NCCs expressing DN-DLC1 remained in the neuroepithelium without disrupting apical-basal polarity and the amount of early migratory NCCs was reduced on the transfected side. A similar phenomenon was observed in embryos treated with DLC1 morpholino (MO). These results demonstrate functional requirements for DLC1 in the establishment of NC polarity and delamination. Altogether, these in vivo studies indicate that appropriate level of DLC1 activity is required for the spatial restriction of RHOA activity, the establishment of NC polarity and directional delamination of NCCs. 1.3 – To determine the role of DLC1 in NC migratory behavior using live imaging This issue was already addressed and reported in the mid-term report. The results from this in vitro studies also lead to the same conclusion as in vivo that the appropriate level of DLC1 expression and its asymmetric localisation are crucial for NCCs to migrate in a directional manner. Objective 2 – To investigate how the activity of DLC1 is regulated by NEDD9. Our previous data reported in the mid-term showed that NEDD9 can associate with DLC1 and is required for the asymmetric localization of DLC1 in the cytosol of emigrating NCCs. Similarly, the polarized distribution of NEDD9 in the cytoplasm at the cell front was disrupted in DN-DLC1 expressing cells. These data suggest that DLC1 and NEDD9 depend on each other for their asymmetric localization in the cytoplasm to establish differential RHOA activity along the front-back axis. Co-immunoprecipitation was performed to map the domain(s) of DLC1 essential for partnering with NEDD9. Consistent with the previous results in 1.1 in which overexpression of DN-DLC1 (320) reduced NC delamination, DN-DLC1 (320) but not the SAM domain alone was able to associate with NEDD9. These results suggest that NEDD9 and possibly other interacting factors could be sequestered from their interaction with endogenous DLC1 through binding to the FAT domain of DN-DLC1, rendering DLC1 incapable for spatial restriction of RHOA activity. If that was the case, polarized RHOA activity could be restored by NEDD9 overexpression. Indeed, the differential distribution of RHOA activity between the back and front of DN-DLC1+NEDD9 expressing cells was restored with FRET index comparable to the control. Collectively, these data show that interaction of DLC1 with NEDD9 is essential for the spatial restriction of RHOA activity at the back of the cell and the lead edge that is prerequisite for the establishment of a front-rear polarity axis and directional delamination and migration of trunk NCCs. Objective 3: To investigate how DLC1 is integrated with the downstream transcriptional events of the phosphorylated form of SOX9 to promote NC delamination and migration. Our attempt in using SV40- or CMV-driven DLC1 expression construct to restore or alleviate defects of NC delamination induced by SOX9S64A,S181A was not successful as the levels of ectopic DLC1 expression and activity were too low as shown by Western blotting and FRET analysis respectively. We took an alternative approach by titrating the amount of pCIG-DLC1 expression vector to co-express with SOX9S64A,S181A but the majority of cells transfected with the lowest concentration of pCIG-DLC1 (0.5 ug/ul) still infiltrated into the neural tube lumen. We speculated that overexpression of DLC1 overrides the effects of SOX9S64A,S181A. We, therefore, pursed another direction to examine whether DLC1 and NEDD9 genes expression are subjected to the transcriptional regulation by SOX9 and/or SOX10. Functional and epistasis analysis showed that SOX9 and SOX10 regulate NEDD9 and DLC1 expression to govern NC directional delamination and migration respectively.

27100314.label: Major findings and research outcome
27100314.value: In this study, using FRET-based biosensor analysis for RHOA in chick embryos and live-cell imaging vitro, we show that high RHOA in the cytoplasm defines the prospective rear of delaminating and migratory trunk NCCs while fluctuating RHOA activity in the membrane protrusion at the cell front. This differential RHOA activity is regulated by asymmetric localization of the RhoGAP DLC1 in the cytoplasm at the cell front. Gain- and loss-of-function studies reveal that appropriate level of DLC1 activity is essential for the establishment of NC polarity through spatial restriction of RHOA activity at the back, which is prerequisite for directional delamination and migration. Importantly, this differential distribution of DLC1 depends on its binding partner, NEDD9 and their association is required for the establishment of polarized rather the total level of RHOA activity. Last, DLC1 and NEDD9 genes are subjected to transcriptional regulation by NC specifiers SOX10 and SOX9 respectively. Together, these results reveal a SOX9/SOX10-NEDD9/DLC1-RHOA regulatory axis to orient trunk NCCs in the direction of movement. The work was published in Nature Communications on 31 Oct 2017 (Part C, Section 8).

27100314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27100314.value: In addition to trunk NCCs, we also investigated the role of DLC1 in avian cranial NC development. We found that DLC1 expression is initiated following neural plate border regulator PAX7 but prior to NC specifiers. In addition, DLC1 exhibits dual nuclear and cytoplasmic localization in cranial NC progenitors. Strikingly, both gain- and loss-of-function studies of the DLC1 result in switching of cell fate from NC to neural lineage independent of its RhoGAP activity, indicating that proper levels of DLC1 expression are crucial in the consolidation of NC identity. Consistent with the spatial-temporal order of DLC expression, PAX7 regulates DLC1 expression and their interaction is required for PAX7 occupancy to the enhancers of NC specifiers. Nuclear DLC1 further recruits TCEB1, which is essential for DNA binding of elongating RNA polymerase II to maintain transcription of NC specifiers. In vivo biosensor analysis demonstrate that cytoplasmic DLC1 recruits STRAP to stabilize SNAIL2 protein through inhibition of GSK3 activity, allowing NC EMT. Our results unravel a RhoGAP-independent role of DLC1 by recruiting distinct subcellular complexes in governing NCC fate determination and EMT onset, suggesting a new perspective on the cellular functions of RhoGAP proteins. This work has recently been submitted to Nature Communications for review.

27100314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27100314.value: Directed cell migration is fundamental to our life, from organ formation to tissue repair. How such directed migration is established and controlled remain controversial. We study this important issue in embryonic trunk neural crest cells which are highly migratory and essential for peripheral nervous system development. Consequently, abnormal neural crest cell migration could lead to various human diseases. In this study, we found that a tumor metastasis suppressor, DLC1 (Deleted in Liver Cancer 1), is asymmetrically localized in the cytoplasm of the migratory neural crest cell front that restricts active RHOA at the cell rear to determine directed neural crest motility. Importantly, the association of DLC1 with NEDD9 is critical for its asymmetric localization and differential RHOA activity. Expression of DLC1 and NEDD9 are regulated by SOXE transcription factors which specify neural crest identity. In summary, our studies have unraveled an unexpected role of an inhibitor of tumor metastasis DLC1 in governing neural crest motility, as well as a novel SOXE-DLC1/NEDD9-RHOA regulatory axis to orient trunk neural crest cells in the direction of movement. Thus, we identified DLC1 as a potential causative gene for defective neural crest cell migration underlying various developmental abnormalities in humans.

27100414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27100414.value: Surgical extraction of wisdom teeth is a common dental procedure. Patients receiving this procedure are predominantly young and healthy adults who are socially active. They will experience side effects after the procedure such as pain, swelling and limited mouth opening for 5 to 7 days. Although these side effects are often temporary, they can significantly affect the patient’s quality of life and work. Ketamine has been used as an anaesthetic drug for over three decades. It interacts with a number of receptor systems in the body and exhibits several clinical effects such as anaesthesia, pain relief and positive effects on depressive mood. However, the clinical use of ketamine has become limited because it may cause altered consciousness and hallucinations. Recently, ketamine was shown to be able to influence the inflammatory response and limit the exacerbation of systemic inflammation without affecting the local healing processes. Although a number of studies demonstrated that administration of single sub-anaesthetic low dose ketamine before and / or during surgery could reduce the biological inflammatory markers IL-6 and TNF-α, the correlation between this finding and the clinical outcomes such as post-operative pain and swelling has not been established. The aim of this study is to conduct a double blind randomised clinical trial to compare the post-operative pain and recovery outcomes in patients after surgical removal of wisdom teeth under general anaesthesia with or without receiving a single low dose of ketamine before surgery. The magnitude of the effect will be compared with a positive control group (dexamethasone, a steroid with anti-inflammatory activity) and placebo group with injection of saline. The amount of post-operative facial swelling will be measured using a three dimensional laser surface scanning technique. Other post-operative outcomes and complications such as time to first painkiller request, total painkiller consumption, infection rate, adverse effects and patient satisfaction will also be compared. Patients will be followed up after surgery for up to 3 months. We will assess if ketamine is effective for reducing post-operative pain and facial swelling, which will improve the quality of life of the patients and reduce the consumption of painkillers. The findings may also improve our understanding about the relationship between inflammation and post-operative pain in a surgical setting.

27100614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27100614.value: 在香港，越來越多兒童患有動作協調能力喪失症，因此，兒科復康服務的對象亦由嚴重動作障礙(如大腦痲痺)兒童，變成輕微動作障礙(如發展性協調障礙)兒童，為切合新的需要，便要制訂一些以證據為本的復康策略。患有發展性協調障礙的兒童，他們的動作功能有明顯的缺陷，最值得關注的是他們的平衡能力較弱，這可導致他們容易跌倒及影響肌能發展。現時，復康訓練的重點在於使用功能性運動來誘發患有發展性協調障礙兒童的中樞神經系統的可塑性，從而提升平衡表現，卻忽略了治療神經肌肉障礙對功能方面的影響。最近，我們的研究團隊發現患有發展性協調障礙兒童的平衡能力較弱，這可能是因為他們的膕繩肌肌肉發力較慢，但現時治療這一神經肌肉障礙的方法尚未有定論。根據一些神經肌肉的機理，肌肉力量訓練能有效提升成年人的肌肉發力速度及平衡能力。在這個研究中，我們會針對患有發展性協調障礙兒童的中樞及周邊神經系統障礙作治療。所以，我們會使用功能性運動配合肌肉力量訓練。我們預計，如果患有發展性協調障礙兒童的中樞及周邊神經系統障礙得到治療，他們的平衡策略及功能將得到最大的改善。如果這個推論成立的話，研究結果將會顯示接受功能性運動配合肌肉力量訓練的兒童，他們的平衡能力及功能，比只接受功能性運動的兒童為佳。研究目標：比較(1)功能性運動配合肌肉力量訓練、(2)功能性運動訓練及(3)沒有訓練，對患有發展性協調障礙兒童的平衡策略及功能的影響。設計：一個隨機對照試驗。參與者：87位患有發展性協調障礙的兒童。訓練：為期12週的功能性運動配合肌肉力量訓練或功能性運動訓練。主要結果測量方法：感覺整合測試 - 站立平衡策略得分及平衡能力總分；動作能力協調測驗 - 運動障礙總分及平衡得分；肌力檢測 - 下肢肌肉力量及發力的時間。預期結果及臨床的重要性：接受功能性運動配合肌肉力量訓練的兒童，他們的平衡能力最佳。如果研究結果理想，這個訓練計劃可以用於臨床實踐中，這有著正面的社會經濟價值，例如可以縮短治療時間及減少醫療開支。

27100614.label: Realisation of objectives
27100614.value: The project was completed successfully. The following summary describes how and to what extent the project objective was achieved. Objective: This study compared the effectiveness of (1) power training with functional movement training (FMPT), (2) functional movement training (FMT) alone, and (3) no intervention to improve the balance strategies and balance abilities of children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Methods: This study conducted a randomized, single-blinded, parallel group–controlled trial. A total of 178 children with DCD were recruited and screened for eligibility; of these children, 161 (age = 6–10 years) qualified and were randomly assigned to the FMPT group (n = 53), FMT group (n = 55), or control group (n = 53). The two intervention groups underwent 1-hour FMPT or FMT sessions twice a week for 3 consecutive months. The control group underwent no training during the study period. Measurements were taken before (baseline) and immediately after (posttest) the intervention period and 3 months after its completion (follow-up test). The primary outcomes were the composite equilibrium score (ES), condition-specific strategy score (SS), and overall SS on the sensory organization test (SOT), as measured using a computerized dynamic posturography machine. Secondary outcomes included the Movement Assessment Battery for Children (MABC) total impairment score (TIS) and balance subscore, and lower limb muscle (hip flexors and extensors, knee flexors and extensors, and ankle dorsiflexors and plantarflexors) isometric peak force as well as the time taken to reach the peak force. In addition, the expectation regarding treatment credibility was measured posttest using a questionnaire (maximum score = 10). The intention-to-treat assumption was made to handle missing data. Mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance followed by post hoc tests conducted as appropriate were employed to analyze the data. Results: Forty-two children in the FMPT group (mean age = 7.8 years; 28 boys and 14 girls), 47 children in the FMT group (mean age = 7.9 years; 33 boys and 14 girls), and 41 children in the control group (mean age = 7.5 years; 28 boys and 13 girls) completed the intervention and posttest. The attendance rates of the FMPT and FMT interventions were 83% and 79%, respectively. The FMPT (p < 0.001) and FMT (p = 0.004) groups exhibited greater improvements in balance performance (SOT ES) at posttest than did the control group. The balance strategies adopted in a sensory challenge environment (SOT condition 6 SS) by the FMPT participants demonstrated greater improvements from baseline to posttest than did those adopted by the FMT participants (p = 0.008) and controls (p = 0.005). In the follow-up test, the FMPT participants exhibited a significant improvement in SOT condition 6 SS (p < 0.001). The between-group differences were 8.34 points (p = 0.001) between the FMPT and FMT groups and 10.03 points (p < 0.001) between the FMPT and control groups. The FMPT group exhibited greater improvements from baseline to posttest in knee extensor isometric peak force (p = 0.001) and time to peak force in the knee flexors (p = 0.016) than did the other two groups. The FMT participants achieved favorable results for functional balance (MABC balance subscore) than did the control group at posttest (p < 0.001). The improvement demonstrated by the FMT participants relative to the controls was maintained until the follow-up test (p = 0.019). No significant within- or between-group changes were noted in any other outcomes, including SOT condition 1 to 5 SS and overall SS, MABC TIS, hip and ankle muscle isometric peak force, time taken to reach peak force, knee extensor time to peak force, and knee flexor peak force (p > 0.05). The treatment credibility scores were 8.29 and 8.25 for the FMPT and FMT groups, respectively. No major adverse events were reported. Conclusions: The FMPT program was more effective than the conventional FMT program for enhancing balance strategies in a sensory challenge environment and the knee neuromuscular performance of children with DCD, whereas the FMT program improved the functional balance performance of such children.

27100614.label: Major findings and research outcome
27100614.value: Major findings: (1) A 3-month course of FMPT appears to be a safe and effective stand-alone intervention for improving standing balance strategies (in a sensory challenge environment) and knee neuromuscular performance in children with DCD. (2) Conventional FMT could be effective in enhancing functional balance performance in such children. (3) Neither FMPT nor FMT was effective in improving balance strategies (when standing in less challenging sensory environments), overall motor proficiency, or hip and ankle neuromuscular performance in children with DCD. (Please refer to the “realization of objectives” section for a detailed description of the results.) Research outcome: This project has yielded the publication of seven papers in high-impact peer-reviewed journals. In addition, the research findings have been presented at four conferences (international and local), and nine abstracts have been published. The Ph.D. student who was supported financially to conduct this project has received two research awards, and the principal investigator has received one knowledge-exchange grant based on the project findings. (Please refer to the “research output” and “other impact” sections.)

27100614.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27100614.value: Studying the underlying physiological mechanisms associated with FMPT is critical before further examining its clinical efficacy — we intend to investigate how electromyographic leg muscle activity affects dynamic balance performance in children with DCD in a sensory challenge environment. A postgraduate research student is currently investigating the association between leg muscle activation timing and dynamic balance control after FMPT in children with DCD. Moreover, the application of FMPT or FMT could be further examined. Our recent study demonstrated that the underlying causes of impaired balance control—specifically, limits of stability (LOS)—in children with DCD include suboptimal volitional control of the center of gravity (COG) and reduced knee muscle force production speed. FMPT can accelerate knee muscle force production but cannot improve COG control. Hence, Tai Chi (which is known to improve COG control) alongside FMPT may be a useful training strategy for increasing LOS in children with DCD. A grant proposal to test this hypothesis is being prepared. In addition, further research could investigate the effectiveness of FMPT among other pediatric populations (e.g., children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or autism spectrum disorder).

27100614.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27100614.value: This study examined whether muscle strengthening alongside functional movement training was superior to functional movement training alone or no training for improving leg muscle performance, body balance, and associated movement patterns in children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD). This investigation is critical because children with DCD exhibit balance difficulties that may predispose them to falls and injuries in daily life; functional movement training alongside muscle strengthening may be a useful rehabilitation strategy for such children. A total of 161 elementary school–aged children with DCD were randomly allocated to a muscle strengthening plus functional movement training group, functional movement training group, or control group. The two intervention groups received functional movement training alongside muscle strengthening training twice a week over a 3-month period. Body balance and its associated movement strategies and leg muscle performance were measured before and after the training period and 3 months after its completion. The results revealed that muscle strengthening alongside functional movement training was more effective than functional movement training alone in terms of enhancing balance movement patterns (especially in a sensory challenge environment) and knee muscle performance in children with DCD, whereas functional movement training alone improved balance performance during functional activities in such children.

27100814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27100814.value: Introduction: In recent years, there has been a notable surge in the reporting of enteroviral infection-induced hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD), causing increased concern for public health. The disease is mainly caused by two common viruses, CoxsackievirusA16 (CA16) and Enterovirus71 (EV71). Currently there are no effective vaccinations or antiviral drugs to treat CA16 and EV71, and they are controlled only through public health interventions such as social distancing and school closure. Understanding their transmission dynamics among the general population is of critical importance to maintain surveillance and preparedness for HFMD, considering the potential serious consequences. Only a few studies to date have explicitly investigated the epidemiological dynamics of these two enteroviruses in the general population and in school or preschool settings. Reported outbreaks in recent years have occurred mainly in child care institutions. The proposed study aims to clarify the transmission dynamics of the causative viruses, link the contact pattern of children to epidemiological patterns of HFMD in Hong Kong, and identify an optimal control strategy in these settings. Methods: We will construct compartmental susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered models to analyze the transmission dynamics of CA16 and EV71 in the community, with explicit household and school structures. The proposed model will describe the transmission dynamics of CA16 and EV71, equipped with age-specific transmission parameters, age-specific contact patterns and seasonal forcing in the transmission rate. The effectiveness of interventions such as school closure and social distancing will be comparatively assessed through simulation. Possible outcome: Our proposed study will elucidate the fundamental aspects of the transmission dynamics of CA16 and EV71 particularly in day-care centers, preschools and schools. The major driving force behind epidemics and the key epidemiological components for regulating HFMD transmission will be identified to help design effective countermeasures. The parameterized model will be used to identify the number of infections averted under various intervention measures at different timings, permitting us to assess the effectiveness of school and preschool closure, reduced contact between classes, and other measures such as increased frequency of hand-washing. Qualitative findings will also offer important public health implications for the control of other childhood diseases that are transmitted through similar routes. Relevance and significance: The epidemiological dynamics of HFMD in children are largely unknown. Improved understanding of disease transmission dynamics based on firm scientific evidence would stimulate new ideas concerning the design and implementation of control strategies for enteroviruses and other childhood diseases mainly transmitted through direct contact. 介紹：近年，腸病毒引致的手足口病通報個案有着顯著的增長，引起公共衞生部門方面的關注。這種疾病主要由柯薩奇病毒A16型及腸病毒71型這兩種病毒引起。現時，沒有特效藥物治療手足口病。因此，控制疫情主要是透過公共衛生干預措施，如社交隔離或學校停課。明白手足口病在人羣中的傳播途徑和潛在的嚴重後果，對維持疫情監察和作出防疫準備十分重要。到目前為止，只有少數研究能明確地指出這兩種病毒在大眾人口中，學校或幼兒園的流行傳播動態。 在近年的報告中，手足口病主要在學前機構中爆發。本研究的目的是釐清引起手足口病的傳播動態，找出香港兒童的接觸模式跟流行病情的關係，及在學前機構中的最佳防控策略。 方法：我們將會建立「易感-暴露-感染-復原」倉室模型來分析手足口病在社區的傳播動態，尤其考慮到學校和家居。這個模型將加入年齡別的參數和接觸模式，和影響傳播速度的氣候性壓力。我們將會透過模擬分析來評估學校停課或社交隔離等防疫干預措施對控制疫情的效果。 預期結果：我們建議的研究將會解釋手足口病特別在日間托兒所、幼兒園及學校的主要傳播動態。我們會找出手足口病爆發背後的主導原因和控制手足口病傳播的主要流行病學元素，藉以設計有效的對應措施。這參數化模型將被用作識別不同預防措施在不同時間中防止感染疫症的數目。這讓我們評估學校及幼兒園停課，減少班房與班房間的接觸，增加洗手次數等措施的防疫效用。質性方面的研究結果也將對控制其他有類似傳播途徑的兒童病症提供重要的公共衛生意義。 相關性及重要性：目前對兒童手足口病的傳染病動態的了解是未明的。根據明確的科學證據而加強對疾病傳播動態的認識，將會啓發對腸病毒及其他透過直接接觸傳播的兒童疾病，在防控措施上的設計和實行。

27100814.label: Realisation of objectives
27100814.value: Objective 1. This objective was met by the data collection and analysis of detailed HFMD outbreak data from 24 kindergartens, 3 primary and 8 secondary schools, with a total of 1981 participants including 309 diagnosed HFMD cases. In particular, we collected information on the time of symptom onset, sick absence of HFMD cases and household HFMD infections. Our data showed that there were very few infections in schools which were preceded by HFMD cases from households (<4%), among which it is expected only some of them were within-household transmission. Hence the outbreaks were mainly driven by within-school transmission. We also constructed a mathematical transmission model to describe the outbreaks in schools. Based on the epidemiological parameters of HFMD from the literature, the collected data and analysis of the mathematical model, it was found that the time from symptom onset to taking sick absence has a key role in limiting transmission. Objective 2. This objective was met by fitting the above mathematical models to the school outbreak data, followed by simulation studies. The range of transmissibility from different schools were estimated which was then fed into simulations under scenarios of different control measures with different assume efficacy. The number of HFMD infections avoided was simulated by comparing the expected number of infections under the scenario with the considered interventions versus that from the baseline scenario. We identified the most effective strategy which maximized the number of HFMD infections avoided. All simulations were carried out within plausible ranges of parameters for the interventions.
