27100814.label: Major findings and research outcome
27100814.value: We report the following major findings and research outcomes: 1. We estimated that the median incubation period was 6.8 (95% CI 5.8-8.1), with 27% of the incubation period longer than 10 days. This suggested that intensive school-based control strategy should be extended in the order of 2 weeks. To our knowledge, this is the first study to provide empirical evidence on the incubation period of HFMD (Koh et al. 2016 Pediatr Infect Dis J). 2. Less than 4% of the HFMD cases reported in schools had prior exposure to household HFMD cases in the previous 2 weeks. This indicated a very limited impact of household infections on the school-based control strategy. 3. Based on a mathematical transmission model, we estimated that the reproductive number (R0) for HFMD ranged from 1.7-11.7 in different schools (median = 4.6). The result is consistent with a previous study in Hong Kong using other analytic method (Ma et al. 2011 Pediatr Infect Dis J). 4. We estimated that the mean time from symptom onset to sick absence is 1.25 days (range: 0-9 days). The mathematical model incorporated the process where HFMD cases take sick absence from schools, and found that R0 highly depends on how fast HFMD cases took sick leave from schools. 5. We simulated the impact of reducing the duration from symptom onset to sick absence, closing schools when reaching a certain threshold of HFMD cases and improving hygiene. School closure is most effective but will lead to substantial burden of childcare for the parents, especially the median incubation period of HFMD is around one week and hence the closure period can be up to two or more weeks. 6. In schools with lower transmissibility, further reduction of the time from symptom onset to taking sick leave is effective in reducing potential HFMD cases. Improving hygiene can also be effective theoretically but given that most schools have already good hygiene practice in place, it is unclear whether within-school transmissibility can be further reduced significantly. In schools with higher transmissibility, improving hygiene is less effective. Reducing the average time from symptom onset to taking sick leave to an average of 0.5 days is likely to be effective to reduce HFMD infections. This is more likely to be achieved during a period with high HFMD activity in the community.

27100814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27100814.value: Potential further research includes theoretical development of statistical inference based on the distribution of symptom onset over weekdays, and its potential implications in the control of transmission are being investigated. School is a special setting where there is a natural interrupt of contacts between students during weekends. Control measures taking into consideration of this particular schedule is under-investigated in the literature. The optimization of school-based interventions will be examined. The results may also have implication in the control of infectious diseases at workplace. Besides publication in academic journals, the results will be disseminated to the participating schools. Recommendation will be given in a practical manner.

27100814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27100814.value: There have been limited studies on the control of hand, foot and mouth disease in a school setting. This research project aimed to develop evidence-based recommendations for the control of hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) in a school setting. We recruited kindergartens, primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong to participate in the study, where detailed epidemiological information were collected from the HFMD outbreaks. We found that household HFMD cases had a limited impact on the transmission in schools. Based on a mathematical model informed by the data collected, HFMD was found to have high transmissibility even good hygiene practice has already in place. We also carried out simulations to assess the impact of different control strategies. Given the current good hygiene practice in most schools, reducing the time from symptom onsets to taking sick absence from schools is likely to reduce the size of the outbreaks. While maintaining hygiene is an important measure, further improving hygiene may have relatively limited impact on transmission. School closure remains to be the most effective intervention, however the implications on childcare by working parents should also be considered.

27101214.label: Realisation of objectives
27101214.value: We investigated the clinical relevance, prognostic significance, functional role, and mechanism of action of miR-1246 in CD133+ liver cancer stem cell (CSC)-driven hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We showed human miR-1246 to promote cancer stemness, including self-renewal, drug resistance, tumorigencitiy and metastasis by activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway through suppressing the expression of AXIN2 and GSK3β, two key players of the β-catenin destruction complex. Clinically, high endogenous and circulating miR-1246 was identified in HCC clinical tissue and serum samples and correlated with a worse prognosis. Further functional analysis identified Oct4 to be the direct upstream regulator of miR-1246, which cooperatively drive β-catenin activation in liver CSCs. In sum, we uncovered the non-canonical regulation of Wnt/β-catenin in liver CSCs by the Oct4/miR-1246 signaling axis, and also provide a novel diagnostic marker as well as target for therapeutic intervention for HCC. Specifically, we report: 1. Wnt/β-catenin signaling is preferentially activated in CD133+ liver cancer stem cells. 2. miR-1246 is preferentially overexpressed in CD133+ liver cancer stem cells and targets two key players of the β-catenin degradation complex to regulate Wnt signaling in HCC. 3. miR-1246 enhances cancer and stem cell-like properties in HCC in vitro. 4. miR-1246 augments tumor-initiating and metastatic potential in vivo. 5. miR-1246 regulates cancer stemness and the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in HCC by targeting AXIN2 and GSK3β of the β-catenin degradation complex. 6. Endogenous and secretory miR-1246 overexpression is tightly associated with adverse HCC survival. 7. Oct4 activates miR-1246 expression through miR-1246 promoter binding and cooperatively drive β-catenin activation in HCC. Please kindly refer to our publication for further details: Chai S, Ng KY, Tong M, Lau EY, Lee TK Chan KW, Yuan YF, Cheung TT, Cheung ST, Wang XQ, Wong N, Lo CM, Man K, Guan XY, Ma S. Octamer 4/microRNA-1246 signaling axis drives Wnt/β-catenin activation in liver cancer stem cells. Hepatology 2016; 64: 2062-76. All proposed objectives have been achieved. Work for the project was primarily carried out by a then PhD candidate Ms. Stella CHAI under the supervision of Dr. Stephanie Ma (PI). Stella has now successfully obtained her PhD degree at HKU. Her thesis entitled ‘The regulatory roles of miR-142-3p and miR-1246 in CD133+ liver cancer stem cells driven hepatocellular carcinoma’ was rated the top grade – ‘outstanding’ (top 5%) by the thesis examining committee.

27101214.label: Major findings and research outcome
27101214.value: We report that a human miRNA, miR-1246, activates the β-catenin pathway by suppressing the expression of AXIN2 and GSK3β, two members of the β-catenin destruction complex, thus leading to nuclear accumulation and activation of β-catenin and, consequently, promoting cancer and stem-cell-like phenotypes in CD133+ liver CSCs. Clinically, endogenous and secretory miR-1246 is closely associated with adverse patient survival and likely to represent a novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for HCC. miR-1246 overexpression in HCC is driven by direct promoter binding of another important self-renewal molecule, Oct4, which is also commonly overexpressed in CD133+ liver CSCs. Together, the Oct4/miR-1246 signaling axis drives Wnt/β-catenin activation in this subset of HCC cells. Importantly, miR-1246 overexpression events are inversely correlated with the presence of β-catenin mutations in exon 3 and represent mutually exclusive events in liver CSCs and HCC. Collectively, we demonstrate that Oct4/miR-1246 overexpression substantially activates and sustains Wnt signaling in CD133+ liver CSCs and HCC by simultaneously suppressing multiple Wnt inhibitors of the β-catenin destruction complex (AXIN2 and GSK3β), providing a new layer of molecular mechanism by which the Wnt-mediated stem cell-like properties of HCC cells are developed and a novel mechanism by which Oct4 and Wnt/β-catenin self-renewal pathways are linked by miR-1246.

27101214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27101214.value: We are currently exploring on the possibility of using circulating miR-1246 as a diagnostic and or prognostic biomarker for HCC. This is a project that continues on the interesting leads identified from the current funded project.

27101214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27101214.value: Findings from our work provide evidence to show the clinical relevance and functional significance of both endogenous and secretory miR-1246 in maintenance of cancer stemness in HCC via modulating Wnt/β-catenin self-renewal signaling. We believe that miR-1246 can be used as a novel biomarker for the better detection or as a predictor of treatment response in HCC.

Such notions must be theoretically sound, and allow us to approximately maximize social welfare or revenue. Welfare Maximization: Design poly-time, privacy-preserving, and truthful mechanisms that approximately maximize welfare for matching markets, combinatorial auctions, etc. Design poly-time, privacy-preserving mechanisms in Fisher markets that compute approximate market equilibria. Design a reduction that converts any approximation algorithm for welfare maximization into a privacy-preserving, truthful mechanism in the Bayesian setting. Revenue Maximization: Design poly-time, privacy-preserving mechanisms that approximately maximize revenue for multi-item auctions, combinatorial auctions, etc. Develop a privacy-preserving reduction from revenue to welfare maximization. General Framework: Develop a general framework of designing (potentially super-poly-time) privacy-preserving mechanisms with respect to our notions. This involves characterizing for which problems privacy-preserving mechanisms exist, and introducing general techniques for designing such mechanisms. Empirical Evaluation: Implement our mechanisms and test them on both simulated data and real data of ad auctions. The goal is to understand the trade-off between protecting agents' privacy and maximizing welfare or revenue.

27200214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200214.value: This project studies how to protect agents' privacy in economic markets. Designing computationally efficient mechanisms for allocating resources to self-motivated agents, with the aim of maximizing social welfare or revenue, is a fundamental problem at the interface between Economics and Computer Science. Traditionally, the agents are assumed to only care about the utility derived from the allocation and payments of the mechanism, and many previous mechanisms, such as the second price auction, violate the agents' privacy. Recently, protecting the agents' privacy has received growing interest. This project aims to lay out the theoretical foundation of designing privacy-preserving mechanisms in economic markets by contributing in the following perspectives. 1. We will identify notions of privacy that are tailored for economic markets so that we can design privacy-preserving mechanisms that approximately maximize social welfare or revenue, getting around known obstacles encountered when applying previous notions such as differential privacy. 2. We will introduce new techniques for designing privacy-preserving mechanisms for some important economic markets, including matching markets, multi-item auctions, combinatorial auctions, and Fisher markets. Further, we seek to develop a general framework for designing such mechanisms for a large family of economic markets. 3. The propose research will advance our understanding on how protecting agents' privacy may affect the social welfare and revenue of real-life auctions. We plan to implement our privacy-preserving mechanisms on both simulated data and real data from ad auctions of Google and Microsoft Bing. Through this study, we hope to provide a reference point for companies such as Microsoft and Google on whether and how to revise the privacy policy of their online services. 我们从保护用户隐私的角度重新审视计算博弈论中的市场机制设计问题，如搜索引擎上的广告拍卖机制等。传统机制设计常假设用户只关心机制结果的效用，而忽略了用户隐私的保护。近年来用户隐私的保护越来越受到重视。我们的目标是为市场机制设计中的隐私保护提供以下两方面的理论基础：(1) 找到适合市场机制设计的隐私标准，解决差分隐私等标准无法运用到市场机制上的问题，(2) 对于常见的市场提出保护用户隐私的机制设计手段。

27200214.label: Realisation of objectives
27200214.value: We have accomplished all objectives stated in the project through a series of publications. In terms of modeling, we have characterized the sufficient and necessary conditions under which privacy-preserving algorithms exist for a large family of packing problems, which essentially capture all resource allocation problems in economic markets. Our algorithms can be used for both welfare maximization and revenue maximization and are obtained in a unified framework. Empirical evaluations have been done by UG students as part of the education plan.

27200214.label: Major findings and research outcome
27200214.value: - We characterized the sufficient and necessary conditions under which jointly differentially private algorithms can achieve an approximately optimal solution for a large family of packing problems that capture the problems we proposed to study in this project. - Through implementations of our algorithm and the previous ones and empirical evaluations, we found that all existing algorithms, including ours, are too slow to be run on real-life large-scale data. In particular, these algorithms generally have a running time that depends cubically on the size of the dataset, while the modern standard of efficient algorithms is (near-)linear time. - We proposed a fast algorithm that can be run on large-scale data, whose running time is linear in the size of the dataset. However, it requires stronger conditions to work compared with the previous one. - The results are published in a refereed conference paper titled "near optimal jointly private packing algorithms via dual multiplicative weight update" in SODA 2018, the No. 1 conference on algorithms. - There are a couple of other related refereed conference papers funded by this project.

27200214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27200214.value: - A natural question is whether there exists an algorithm that gets the better of the two previous algorithms we proposed. That is, its running time shall have only a linear dependence on the size of the dataset as in our 2nd algorithm, and it achieves an approximately optimal solution with the optimal conditions characterized by our 1st algorithm. Such an algorithm will be much more practical than all previous jointly differentially private algorithms.

27200214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27200214.value: Through this project, we significantly extended our knowledge of private mechanisms for economic markets, in particular, with respect to the notion of joint differential privacy. We now understand exactly under what sufficient and necessary conditions one can hope to achieve both good privacy and good economic efficiency and/or revenue. The next step, which is beyond the scope of this project, is to make such privacy-preserving mechanisms for economic markets more practical. In particular, we shall explore the possibility of linear-time mechanisms for this problem

27200414.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27200414.value: 後工業化城市的社區規劃與能源效率：以深圳和香港為例

27200414.label: Project Objectives
27200414.value: To construct a large cross-sectional dataset that links neighbourhood design portfolio, housing, vehicle ownership to household energy uses in Shenzhen and Hong Kong; To formulate a theoretical framework to integrate the two main sources of household direct energy consumption, and relate them to the neighbourhood design in China’s urban context, through the influence on urban households’ lifestyles; To empirically examine the impacts of neighborhood design on a household’s energy consumption and carbon emissions, through the use of instrumental variables (IV) approach and Structural Equation Models (SEM); To compare and contrast the cases in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, and recommend neighborhood land use planing and design guidelines for low carbon development in Chinese cities.

To formulate a theoretical framework to integrate the two main sources of household direct energy consumption, and relate them to the neighbourhood design in China’s urban context, through the influence on urban households’ lifestyles;

To empirically examine the impacts of neighborhood design on a household’s energy consumption and carbon emissions, through the use of instrumental variables (IV) approach and Structural Equation Models (SEM);
To compare and contrast the cases in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, and recommend neighborhood land use planing and design guidelines for low carbon development in Chinese cities.

27200414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200414.value: 在能源和氣候變化的挑戰面前，后工业化城市时代的中国城市如何实现低碳发展是一个值得探索的课题。本研究旨在進一步理解城市形態和社区规划對於减少居民能效的潛力，並回答在後工業時代的中國城鎮，社区规划和设计如何通过改变居民家庭的生活方式，影響家庭的直接能源消耗和碳排放量。本研究在建築環境，出行行為和家庭能源消費之間的定量關係研究将提供一种新的视角。该方法将居住选择和出行行为的动态关系作为生活方式的组合，並澄清城市形態和社区规划设计在影响与能源消耗和碳排放相关的生活方式选择方面的作用。在研究中，我們也提出了利用工具變量（IV）方法和結構方程模型（SEM），来解决“自我選擇”問題。通过香港與深圳之間的比較研究，本研究也将提出在社区层面通过土地利用總體規劃和社区設計准则来实现溫室氣體減排的政策建議。

27200414.label: Realisation of objectives
27200414.value: All the four research objectives are fully realized through the following research activities. Objectives (1) and (2) are met in the following ways. The cross-sectional dataset that links neighbourhood design portfolio, housing, vehicle ownership to household energy uses in Shenzhen and Hong Kong was assembled. We collected valid data from around 500 households in Hong Kong through household questionnaire survey, which covers questions from basic demographic, socio-economic information, housing and vehicle ownership, weekly travel summary and in-home energy use, to a series of attitudinal questions. Attributes of neighbourhood design characteristics were also extracted from field survey and GIS file, and matched to the household data file. In Shenzhen, after three field trips by the PI for preparing the data collection and research collaboration, the household questionnaire survey was conducted by our research collaborator at Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School. The survey covers around 1000 residents in four typical neighbourhood types in Shenzhen: superblocks, mid- and high-rise apartments (enclave), urban village, as well as residential neighbourhood attached to an industrial park. The PI and the research team also explored the use of urban big data in the data collection stage, including the measurement of neighbourhood design by location-based social media data, remotely sensed satellite imagery, and usage pattern of shared bicycles. A journal paper concerning the data quality issues in the big data age was completed and published by ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (cited by 40+). Analyses were carried out to assess the impacts of neighbourhood design on household activity pattern and energy consumption. Based on existing theories, literature review and the general context of Chinese cities, the theoretical and analytical frameworks were proposed for this study. The model for urban household’s energy consumption and carbon emission, has an ownership component and a usage component. The ownership component includes residential choice and vehicle ownership portfolio. This ownership component is medium to long-term decision the households make, therefore has a “lock-in” effect on energy use and carbon emission. The usage component is conditioned on the ownership component, and focuses on personal travel and in-home use. The role of lifestyle is yet to be included in this theoretical model anticipating theory-building results from the qualitative analysis. Objectives (3) and (4) are met in the following ways. Three journal papers were completed to address these two objectives. Two papers, published in Science of the Total Environment and Journal of Urban Planning and Development (accepted) respectively, seek to identify and examine the impacts of neighbourhood land use planning and design, on individual activity pattern, energy consumption and the resulting urban heat island effect. The paper in Science of the Total Environment (cited by 14), links the urban land use composition and configuration to potential heat source and sink. It identifies, at the macro level, the strong and weak heat sources according to the natural and socioeconomic factors influencing land surface temperature, including population density, electricity consumption, normalized difference built-up index, and elevation; and evaluates, at the micro scale, the heterogeneous effects of land use pattern (percent, density, and shape complexity of patches, edge density) on the thermal environment. A conference presentation was also made to an international audience in 2015 on some preliminary findings. The paper accepted for publication in Journal of Urban Planning and Development, focuses on one of the emerging low-carbon transport mode in Urban China, shared bicycle system, compares the daily usage patterns in the city centre and a suburban district of Shenzhen, and attributes the differences in usage pattern to neighbourhood land use and transport planning, in particular the job-housing balance and provision of public facilities. The last paper, submitted to Urban Studies (under review), compares and contrasts the cases in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, using the household questionnaire survey results, and aims to provide appropriate suggestions for improving neighbourhood land use planning and design towards low carbon development in Chinese cities. All these papers have adopted rigorous quantitative methods to quantify and evaluate the findings, for example, through the use of instrumental variables (IV) approach and structural equation models (SEM), and semiparametric geographically weighted regression (SGWR) models. All these three empirical papers have come up with insightful and non-trivial findings. First, the transportation sector is playing an increasing role in achieving low carbon development in Chinese cities. The emergence of the shared bicycle systems, along with the continuous development of public transit networks in Chinese cities, makes it possible for the behavioural changes on the consumption side to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions. Though, it does not lead to a significant mode shift and changes in household lifestyle naturally simply with the supply of these new low-carbon transport modes. The role of land use planning and neighbourhood design, in promoting the use of low-carbon transport mode, is yet to be examined. Second, the empirical data in Shenzhen suggests that the overall usage intensity and peak-hour use in the suburban district (Longgang) are much lower than those in the city centre (Luohu). In the city centre, shared bicycles are used for not only short-distance trips, but also complementary tool for vehicle transit facilities; While in the suburban district the shared bicycle serves only as a mode to access to other public transit. The job-housing imbalance and lack in urban infrastructure have been the primary reason for the inefficient use of shared bicycles in the suburban district. Therefore, there is an essential need to examine the local land use mix, polycentric urban development structure, and integration with existing and planned public transit network in planning and managing the shared bicycle system. Furthermore, the behavioural changes towards sustainable urban mobility and low carbon development can only be achieved by integrating transportation and land use planning, neighbourhood design, through the influence on urban household’s lifestyle. Third, with regards to the role of land use planning on energy consumption and resulting urban heat island issue, land use composition has exhibited significant effects on thermal environment, while the patch shape of green space and water body, as well as the spatial configuration of interactions between high density residential area and green space also exert important impacts. Consequently, it is essential to design and transform the urban landscape in specific ways based on the heterogeneous effects of land use pattern on the thermal environment to mitigate the urban heat island issue. Fourth, by comparing and contrasting the cases in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, the study has demonstrated how to improve neighborhood land use planning and design towards low carbon development. The findings and the methodology have policy implications. The study has also encountered some difficulties. The manuscript review process of the last paper takes a long time as we aim at publishing our last paper at the top international journal in urban studies. We are hopeful that our fourth journal paper can get published eventually.

27200414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27200414.value: There is still scope to complete and publish at least one more journal paper based on this research. The methodology and the data collection approach adopted in this study can be used to examine the impacts of neighbourhood planning and design, not only on energy consumption and carbon emissions, but also on air pollution exposure related to household activity pattern and the resulting health effects. However, given the significant seasonal variations and complicated mental health issues related to air pollution, it is important to conduct repeated questionnaire surveys to identify the causal relationships. This was not part of the original proposal but when the data became available for the PI to take the opportunity to use this for further research, the GRF will be acknowledged when the paper is published and presented.

27200414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27200414.value: Achieving low carbon urban development in Chinese cities requires a combination of approaches. This research takes a step further by seeking to understand the potential of alternative urban form and neighbourhood design in relation to energy efficiency, and to answer the question of how neighbourhood planning and design affect energy consumption and carbon emissions, through the influence on urban household’s lifestyle in post-industrial Chinese cities. The emergence of the shared bicycle systems, along with the continuous development of public transit networks in Chinese cities, makes it possible for the behavioural changes on the consumption side to reduce energy consumption. Though, empirical data in Shenzhen suggests that the job-housing imbalance and lack in urban infrastructure have been the primary reason for the inefficient use of shared bicycles in the suburban district. Therefore, it is essential to examine the local land use mix, polycentric urban development structure, and integration with existing and planned public transit network. Using household questionnaire survey data from both Hong Kong and Shenzhen, this study has confirmed the role of urban form and neighbourhood design in influencing household behaviour and demonstrated how to improve neighbourhood land use planning and design towards low carbon development in Chinese cities.

27200514.value: 软件产品线（ SPL ）是一个系列软件产品共用一套共同的特点，其中每个产品可能会引入一定程度的变异。国家的最先进的产品线开发，包括前进， FeatureHouse工具，使用基于代码生成的元编程方法。也就是说，有一些工具/ （间位）是用来描述SPL和需要特定的产品时，该工具会生成目标语言（如Java或C + + ）代码的语言。不幸的是，这种元编程开发声压级的方法有重要的缺陷，包括缺乏独立的编译和模块类型检查的。单独编制的缺乏阻止的经营模式，公司将出售SPL模块的二进制文件给客户。对于公司来说，这是一个有吸引力的商业模式，因为它允许客户构建定制化的产品，没有给这些客户访问源代码（以及该公司的知识产权） 。模块化类型检查的缺乏使得开发过程更加复杂和脆弱。例如，在错误报告而言，只能报告类型错误已经生成一个具体的产品之后。此外，这些误差将不会，而是在所生成的代码来报告返回到显影剂在​​他写的代码表示。这显然是不能令人满意的。 我们的项目旨在通过建立代数解决的元编程方法的弊端：一种新的编程语言，用于开发声压级。代数并不需要的元编程方法。相反，它需要一个编程方法，为地方创造声压级的机制被直接集成在语言的语义。写在代数结果的程序完全支持模块类型检查和独立的汇编。为了实现这一目标，代数都会有提供内建支持对象代数的新的语言结构。对象代数是最近的发展在面向对象的编程，可以用来开发高度模块化的程序。代数的编程语言将是第一个编程语言提供对象代数的原生支持，允许：高度模块化的程序和声压级1 ）方便的开发;使用对象代数课程2 ）高效的编译。在项目结束时，我们想到的是，先进设备，最先进的产品线开发将同时被显著从业务的角度更具吸引力显着更有效的实现了从开发人员的生产力观点。

27200514.label: Realisation of objectives
27200514.value: My group conducted a number of projects directly related to this project. We published 8 papers related to this project. Out of those, 1 paper was awarded the best paper award (Modularity 2016). I highlight the various research tracks next - Language Support for Object Algebras (Objective 1): On this track we have 5 publications (OOPSLA 2015, Haskell 2015, Modularity 2016, ICFP 2016, GPCE 2016). The OOPSLA work focused on creating language extensions in Java to better support Object Algebras. The Modularity work studied a novel technique which can complement Object Algebras in Object-Oriented Languages. The Haskell 2015 work is exploratory work on novel modularization techniques, which generalize Object Algebras. That work was conducted in Haskell, which is a state-of- the-art programming language suitable for this kind of exploration. The ICFP paper does some foundational work on the semantics and type systems of languages that can support Object Algebras natively. Finally the GPCE paper provides additional language extensions for Java to support Object Algebras and other modularisation constructs. - Study of compilation schemes for ALGEBRA (Objective 2): On this track we have 1 publication (APLAS 2015). The APLAS work has focused on studying better compilation schemes for functional programs in the JVM. Since we want to develop a language with support for Object Algebras on top of the JVM, it is quite important that we develop good compilation schemes, and since Object Algebras are very functional in style, we must tackle some difficult challenges of compiling functional programs on the JVM. - Development of case studies and evaluation of the approach (Objective 3): On this track we have 2 publications (ECOOP 2017 and SLE 2017). In both works we employed JVM modularisation frameworks developed by us to modularize the interpreters on the famous "Types and Programming Languages" book. Our results show that the frameworks are successful in modularising and reusing code across the interpreters.

27200514.label: Major findings and research outcome
27200514.value: In this project we produced 8 research publications, all published at international conferences in Programming Languages. Out those 3 publications were at top conferences (ICFP, OOPSLA and ECOOP), while all the others were at very good and reputable PL conferences. Additionally all papers come with open source artefacts available online on github/bitbucket. 27200514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27200514.value: The project has focused mostly on lightweight language support for Object Algebras, by extending Java/Scala with annotations to support Object Algebras. A more foundational approach will be to develop a language from scratch with build-in support for Object Algebras.

27200514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27200514.value: This project showed that it is possible to build modularization frameworks on top of existing languages that support modular type-checking and separate compilation. The prior state-of-the-art was mostly based on syntactic approaches to develop software-product lines, which did not have modular type-checking and separate compilation. Since those two properties are very important and desirable in software engineering, our project has shown that we do not need to forfeit them to get modularity.

27200614.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27200614.value: 基於生物學指導的軌跡優化技術的人體動作合成技術研究

27200614.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200614.value: Synthesizing realistic human movement from compact user specifications is a fundamental problem in computer animation. For example, given a humanoid character, generate a walking animation simply from a target velocity and direction, or choreograph a complex dance from a few key-poses. An effective motion synthesis algorithm would greatly simplify the animation creation process as well as find applications related fields such as robotics and human movement science. In robotics, the generated motion trajectories can be an essential element of the robot's control strategy. In movement science, a biologically-plausible motion synthesis algorithm can be used to gain insight into how properties of the body (e.g., a weakened muscle or a broken leg) affect movement. We formulate motion synthesis as a trajectory optimization problem, where motion trajectories over time are optimized to satisfy user specifications. The problem is highly underconstrained, as specifications such as target velocity or sparse poses alone cannot fully describe the movement of a humanoid model. Consequently, additional assumptions about the solution space --- for example, motions are constrained by Newton's laws --- must be incorporated to make the problem tractable. While there has been a long history of work on the topic, incorporating physical constraints has been insufficient to ensure solutions that correspond to realistic human movements can be found. The goal of this research is to show that an algorithm for high quality 3D human motion synthesis can be created by incorporating biologically-motivated constraints into the problem formulation. In particular, we propose to incorporate biomechanical constraints by actuating humanoid models using muscles that generate forces respecting human anatomy and physiology, and neurological priors by biasing muscle activation signals to ones that are likely for natural human movement. We will demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm both by evaluating our results against human data, as well as by creating complex animations such as dances and martial arts from compact user inputs. We expect the outcome of the proposed project to be a general human motion synthesis system that can significantly improve state-of-the-art in authoring character animation. In addition, by taking a biologically-motivated approach, the method can potentially be used to investigate scientific hypotheses of human movement. 在計算機動畫領域，借助簡單的用戶設置來合成真實的人體動作是一個重要的方向。例如，通過簡單給定運動方向和速度來產生人物角色的行走動畫，或者利用人物的關鍵姿態來編排出複雜的舞蹈動作。一個有效的運動合成算法應該在較大程度上簡化動畫製作的過程，同時也能夠在相關領域得到很好的應用，如機器人技術和人體運動學等領域。在機器人技術中，運動軌跡合成是機器人控制策略中重要的環節，而在人體運動學領域，基於生物學的動作合成算法可被用來研究人體特定部位（如虛弱的肌肉或受傷的腿部）對相關人體動作所產生的影響。 動作合成可被視為一種軌跡優化問題，使運動隨時間推移所產生的軌跡符合用戶設置的約束條件。然而軌跡優化仍然是一個還未得到較好解決的問題，因為無論是目標速度還是少量的關鍵姿態都不能完整的描述人體模型的動作特點。因此需要在解空間中引入額外的假設來使得這個問題更加容易處理，比如引入牛頓定律來控制運動。雖然長久以來在這個問題上有著大量的工作，然而僅僅利用物理約束本身並不能夠產生真實的人體動作。 本課題的任務為，通過在問題建模中引入生物學約束的思路來提出能夠產生高質量3D人體動作的算法。具體而言，本課題擬引入生物機械學約束來進行動作合成，通過模擬反映人體解剖和生理的肌肉模型來驅動人體模型，並引入神經學先驗知識使得肌肉模型的啟動能夠反映正常的人體動作特點。本課題將通過將所提出的模型與實際人體數據作比較，以及通過簡便的用戶操作而製作的如舞蹈、武術等複雜的人體動畫來展示本課題算法的可用性。本課題的研究成果為採用前沿動畫製作技術的通用人體動作合成系統。此外，通過引入生物學指導的方法，本課題成果還可被用於研究關於人體運動學的科學理論。

27300014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300014.value: Catenanes are molecules comprised of mechanically interlocked macrocycles that are linked to each other by their relative spatial arrangement instead of chemical bonds. Due to their complex topology and distinct mechanical properties, catenanes and related interlocked architectures not only represent a synthetic challenge but are also promising candidates as basic core units of molecular machines and novel functional materials. Although advancement in molecular recognition has led to templating strategies that boost the efficiency of catenane synthesis, specific structural requirements of the precursors and reaction conditions, as well as the common use of just a single pre-organization handle in an assembly event have limited the vast majority of the assembled catenanes to be relatively simple with only two to three interlocked macrocycles. Strategies for the synthesis of high-order catenanes with more than three interlocked rings are underdeveloped and examples of such catenanes are extremely rare. Therefore, a logical, general and efficient strategy to assemble these complex molecules with more interlocked rings is necessary, if we are to realize their potential as molecular machines and smart materials. In this proposal, we will explore a new templating strategy that exploits the concurrent use of orthogonal supramolecular interactions as preorganization handles in the self-assembly of [oligo]catenanes. Simple cyclic and acyclic building blocks engineered with two orthogonal recognition motifs capable of engaging in coordination bonds, donor-acceptor, hydrophobic and charge-dipole interactions will be synthesized, followed by a study of the macrocyclization and self-assembly of these building blocks into [oligo]catenanes. Both kinetic and thermodynamic approaches of the ring-closing reactions will be explored. A range of physical techniques such as NMR, LC/LCMS, and UV-Vis will be used to characterize and study the dynamic, potential guest binding and switching properties of the assembled interlocked architectures. Results from this work should provide not only insights of the mechanism of the fundamental assembly process of complex natural systems, but also pave the way to new functional materials with unprecedented mechanical properties originating from the interlocked units. 如鎖鏈一樣，索烴是一類由若干大環互相聯鎖所構成的分子。因為這些大環是由空間上的契合而非共價鍵所連繫，所以環與環之間能自由地相對轉動。索烴這種特殊的機械特性以及複雜的空間結構，不單能促進合成方法的發展，還使它們具有成為分子機器和新型材料的潛質。儘管由分子識別所發展的模板合成策略能有效提高索烴的合成效率，但在前體的特殊結構要求、環合反應條件以及預組裝策略等限制下，已有的大部分索烴只含有兩至三個環。到目前為止，用於組裝多於三個環的高價索烴的方法仍未得到有效發展，相應的索烴也十分罕見。因此，如果要預見這類高價索烴在複雜的分子機器和微型材料上巨大的應用前景，開發一種高效並具有普遍性的多環預組裝策略也就顯得十分重要。 此計劃目的在於開發一種能有效地組裝高價索烴的新型預組裝策略。研究目標包括：合成能通過金屬‒配體、芳香受體‒供體、憎水性、離子‒偶極等多於一項的非共價作用而互相識別的組件，通過這些組件的環合反應進行高價索烴的預組裝，以及對所合成的高價索烴進行結構表徵、動態特性及主客化學的研究。

27300014.label: Realisation of objectives
27300014.value: All the projects objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, "to design and synthesize new molecular building blocks for catenane assembly with two or more preorganization units", at least 60 new linear and macrocyclic building blocks that are derived from common preorganization units such as phenanthroline, pyridyldiamine, pyridine, dioxynaphthalene, naphthalenediimide, biphenylene, hexane-1,6-diamine, 4,4'-bipyridinium, azobenzene... etc. have been successfully synthesized and thoroughly characterized. The complementary building blocks that bind to these newly designed and synthesized building blocks such as cucurbit[6]uril, cucurbit[8]uril, and dinaphthol-38-crown-10 for engaging in metal-ligand coordination, ion-dipole interactions, hydrophobic interactions and donor-acceptor interactions have also been prepared. These building blocks are functionalized with amine, aldehyde, azide, aminoalkyne, aminoazide, alkene, bromo, alcohol, phenol, aminothiol, benzothiazole, and many other functional groups for investigating different types of bond forming reactions (e.g. azide-alkyne cycloaddition, nucleophilic substitution, alkene metathesis, reductive amination, imine or ester exchange) macrocyclization reaction in [n]catenane formation. By analysing the [n]catenane formation efficiency and compatibility of various preorganization and macrocyclization reaction, a good understanding on the general principles of building block design related to the basic structural parameters such as the type of preorganization unit, functional group for bond forming reaction, linkers for building block flexibility and solubility has been achieved. Synthetic strategies to obtain these building blocks in significant quantity from commercially available starting materials with good synthesis efficiency have also been developed. For objective 2 "to establish a strategy for the self-assembly of [oligo]catenanes by exploiting the complementarity and orthogonality of the recognition motifs and bond forming reactions", two bond forming reactions - imine formation and cucurbit[6]uril-mediated azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CBAAC), have been identified as the efficient macrocyclization reaction that are compatible with a wide variety of preorganizing units for [n]catenane synthesis. For synthesis in organic medium, imine formation is found to be compatible with preorganization interactions such as copper-phenanthroline coordination and donor-acceptor interactions; for CBAAC, it is compatible with an acidic or neutral aqueous environment and can function well with building blocks that can engage in copper-phenanthroline coordination and hydrophobic interactions. Several series of [n]catenanes of various structures, including a notable branched [6]catenane, a pair of radial [5]catenane isomers, a linear [4]catenanes, and around 20 examples of other [5]-, [4]- and [3]catenanes have been successfully synthesized and characterized by a range of physical methods including 1D 1H and 13C NMR, 2D COSY, NOESY, and DOSY NMR, LCMS, HR-ESI-MS, MS-MS, MS-MS-MS, UV-Vis, IR and fluorescence spectroscopies. In addition, structural factors of the building blocks that dictate the macrocyclization pathway of a copper templated bis(phenanthroline) precursors for the successful interlocking of the macroccycles have been elucidated. It was found that the length, rigidity and chirality of the building block will affect the way how the macrocycles are formed and give either the mechanically bonded catenanes or the twisted molecular figure-eight. Strategies to chemically modify the building blocks to encourage mechanical interlocking were therefore developed and a rare linear [4]catenane was obtained. Detailed insights on building blocks design were also realized from unsuccessful formation of multi-ring [n]catenanes. In one example, a subtle, inobvious cooperative binding between CB[6] and cyclodextrins on a phenylene-containing building block was discovered that inhibited the simultaneous interlocked of a phenanthroline macrocycle in the presence of beta-cyclodextrin. The building blocks were re-designed to overcome this unexpected cooperative binding between the macrocycles. An unexpected kinetic effect involved in the binding of two aromatic building blocks to a cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) was discovered. Although simple donor-acceptor building blocks derived from 4,4'-bipyridinium and 2,6-dioxynaphthalene can successfully form a ternary complex inside the CB[8]cavity, further attachment of linkers with terminal functional groups for macrocyclization and [n]catenane formation from a similar ternary complex resulted in the unsuccessful inclusion of both building blocks in CB[8]. Careful modification on the linker length on the building blocks revealed an unexpected kinetic effect that is not known in host-guest binding involving CB[8]. New strategies will needed to be developed if CB[8] is to be used for [n]catenane synthesis. For objective 3 "to isolate, characterize, and study the dynamic properties and potential guest binding ability of the assembled [oligo]catenanes", all the synthesized [n]catenanes have been purified from preparative reverse-phase HPLC and their structure characterized. For those [n]catenane containing a copper template, the copper ion was also removed by treatment with cyanide and the structures and dynamics of the copper-containing and copper-free [n]catenanes were studied by variable temperature NMR. For those [n]catenanes obtained via CBAAC, the ammonium ions were also neutralized by treatment of a base which removed the strong CB[6]-ammonium interactions to render the interlocked CB[6] mobile, and the dynamic properties were studied by VT NMR and also MS and tandem MS. For example, the [5]catenane isomers featuring an isomeric sequence of the interlocked macrocycles were found to displayed different macrocycle dynamics and shuttling as revealed by VT NMR and MS studies. In addition, the potential guest binding behaviour of the [n]catenanes derived from gamma-cyclodextrin was also tested against a wide range of potential guest including dopamine, adrenaline, menadione, tocapherol and other aromatic molecules. Interesting guest binding-induced macrocycle shuttling has been discovered.

27300014.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300014.value: A new strategy for efficient [n]catenane synthesis by cucurbit[6]uril-mediated azide-alkyne cycloaddition has been developed. A series of new hetero[6]- and [5]catenanes from the orthogonal preorganization of building blocks of different nature have been successfully synthesized and characterized. These [n]catenanes from this project are among the most complex [n]catenanes that have been prepared to date. A clear understanding on the compatibility and complementarity of various preorganizing interactions, bond forming reactions and reaction conditions has been achieved for the efficient, high-yielding synthesis of high-order [n]catenane. A pair of [5]catenane sequence isomers featuring four of two different types of macrocycles being mechanically interlocked in different sequences have also been obtained using our new strategy. This pair of isomers represent one first example of the realization of isomerism due to mechanical bond and allows for the investigation of the different properties of molecular link isomers. The [5]catenanes also showed an unprecedented, pH-responsive macrocycle dynamics that is dependent on the sequence of the interlocked macrocycles, which will be implicated in the future design of complex, multi-component molecular machines of the next generation for advance functions. In addition, a basic understanding on the structural features such as length, rigidity and chirality of a building block that control the macrocyclization pathway of a preorganized building block complex for the successful formation of the mechanical bond has been achieved. The findings from these projects have been published in 6 international, peer-reviewed journals. The results have also been presented in 7 international conferences, in which one is an invited oral presentation that resulted in the award of the Asian Core Program Lectureship Award in 2018. One graduated MPhil student, and two PhD students (one to submit the thesis by Dec 2019 and one is continuing in his second year) have been trained on this project.

27300014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300014.value: By considering that only a very tiny fraction of the theoretically unlimited numbers of molecular links and knots has been realized, the strategies developed for efficiently complex [n]catenanes in this work will be an important foundation for the further development of the many different molecular links and knots that are not yet realized. One example is the molecular Whitehead link which can be accessed by interlocking a molecular figure-eight with a macrocycle by employing our understanding on the factors that governed the macrocyclization reaction on preorganized building blocks that we discovered. The compatibility and complementarity of the preorganization interactions, bond forming reactions and reaction conditions can also be further applied to access molecular links of even higher complexity, i.e. [poly]catenane and for the efficient synthesis of different catenane precursors for incorporation of the mechanical bond into materials e.g. polymers. The realization of isomeric sequences of mechanically interlocked macrocycles as a pair of [5]catenane isomers is one first example of isomerism of mechanically bonded compounds. The new chemical properties from this isomers due to mechanical bonds will have a large potential for further exploration in both basic and applied research, just as the different kinds of isomerism of chemically bonded compounds.

27300014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300014.value: New strategies have been developed to successfully realize complex, multi-component molecular links featuring mechanical interlocking of discrete macrocyclic units at the molecular level. By bringing together newly designed building blocks through the use of intermolecular interactions of different nature and formation of new macrocycles from these basic units, multi-component catenanes featuring various number of mechanically interlocked macrocycles akin to links at the molecular scale of unprecedented complexity have been synthesized and characterized. Some of the synthesized catenanes are examples of the most structurally complex interlocked molecules to date. Isomerism, a fundamental concept in chemistry, has also been realized for the first time for chemical entities that are linked via mechanical bond, which will open up an entire new area in chemistry where isomerisms of compounds that are chemically bonded are traditionally concerned. The new molecular link design and synthetic strategies developed in this work will also be implicated in the future design of advance molecular machines that exploit the unique features and properties of mechanical bonds.

27300114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300114.value: Terrestrial vertebrate fossils, including dinosaurs, pterosaurs, crocodilians, turtles and fish have been discovered from the 9000 meter thick Gyeongsang Supergroup in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. Although most fossils are yet to be well studied, and only few of the fossil occurrences have been published in western journals, the Gyeongsang Supergroup has great potential for substantially increasing our knowledge of Cretaceous terrestrial ecosystems and paleogeography in East Asia. In addition to the body fossils, abundant and well-preserved dinosaur, bird and pterosaur tracks are found from these formations. Well-preserved and extensive vertebrate ichnofaunas from the Gyeongsang Supergroup represent the largest concentration of Cretaceous vertebrate track sites reported from the Asian continent. Furthermore, the stratigraphic frequency of track-bearing levels is greater than that reported for any other region in Asia, and the diversity and abundance of named bird tracks is greater than for any other region. From the abundant fossils and tracks from the Gyeongsang Supergroup it is clear that highly diverse vertebrate communities existed during the Early Cretaceous in the Korean Peninsula. Determining the age and duration of the Gyeongsang Supergroup using abundant interbedded volcanic rocks is critical to understanding several fundamental questions: 1) When did Gyeongsang fauna first appear? 2) Were the Gyeongsang fauna and the Jehol Biota contemporaneous? 3) Is there evidence for diachroneity of first appearances of fauna between Gyeongsang and NE China? 4) Did frequent volcanic eruptions impact the Gyeongsang ecosystem? Reliable radioisotopic age determinations for these fossil-bearing formations will allow us to address all of these questions and test our biogeographic hypothesis for the distribution of Mesozoic terrestrial fossils in Asia. 自上個世紀以來，科學家在朝鮮半島南端的慶山超群裡發現了大量的脊椎動物化石，出土的化石包含了龜、鱷魚和種類繁多的恐龍，這些發現提供了研究中生代生物演化和生態系的重要線索，可惜至今這套地層的具體年代仍有爭議。本研究旨在建立慶山超群高精確年代，我們期望藉由詳細的地層對比、精準的實驗室工作，能夠瞭解朝鮮半島中生代的盆地演化，同時，也能夠對慶山動物群和中國遼西著名的熱河生物群進行年代對比，瞭解兩者之間的演化和遷徙關係。

27300114.label: Realisation of objectives
27300114.value: Objective 1: To determine robust ages for the Cretaceous fossils from the southern part of the Korean Peninsula, we collected two well-known tuffs from the middle and the upper part of the Gyeongsang Supergroup, one rhyolite from the uppermost Gyeongsang Supergroup and one tuffaceous sandstone right above the pterosaur tracks from the Uhangri Formation. After mineral separations, fresh sanidines and groundmass from tuffs and rhyolites were analysed at Ar/Ar lab in Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory of Columbia University, while detrital zircons from tuffaceous sandstone were analysed using LA-ICP-MS facilities at the Institute of Geology and Geophysics (IGG), Chinese Academy of Sciences. The age results from most samples are reasonable and allowed to establish chronological control for the fossil-bearing beds. Objective 2: The Ar/Ar age of one rhyolite from the uppermost Gyeongsang Supergroup and the U/Pb detrital zircon age for tuffaceous sandstone right above the pterosaur tracks from the Uhangri Formation do not fit the proposed stratigraphic model. The widely accepted stratigraphic model for the Gyeongsang Supergroup needs to be revised. Furthermore, our age data for the famous Kusandong Tuff from different localities indicated that the previously lateral correlation might be wrong. The 1-5 meter thick Kusandong Tuff from the middle of the Hayang Group is a crystal-rich rhyodacitic tuff. Because of the ~200 km lateral exposure and unique lithology, this tuff has been used as a key bed for stratigraphic correlation in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. However, our age data from ~200 zircons from this sample suggested that this "tuff" has been reworked and the lateral correlation for this "tuff" remains controversial. Our study indicated the development of Cretaceous sedimentary basins in the southern part of the Koran Peninsula is more complicated than previously thought. This research therefore demonstrated that the previously established stratigraphic column for the Gyeongsang Supergroup requires modification. Further geological, radioisotopic and sedimentary studies of these strata can help clarify stratigraphy and chronology of the fossils within. Objective 3: This study enabled to constrain Cretaceous non-marine correlation across East Asia. We compared the ages for several terrestrial strata in eastern China, north China and South Korea and proposed new development model for the tectonic history in late Mesozoic. Our study provided detailed surface evidence for Paleo-Pacific subduction and associated effects. Furthermore, our geochronologic and geochemical data from different localities helped to reconstruct sedimentological and tectonic history in vicinity of the Sulu Orogenic Belt. Objective 4: This project also allowed to test biogeographic hypothesis for the distribution of Mesozoic terrestrial fossils in Asia. Our study indicated that the fossils from the Gyeongsang Supergroup are younger than the fossils of famous Jehol Biota. The Gyeongsang Supergroup were not deposited contemporaneously with the classic Jehol strata in NE China and the Gyeongsang fauna is distinct from the Jehol animals. Our research demonstrated that the widely accepted hypothesis of the Jehol radiation and migration should be reappraised.

27300114.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300114.value: We investigated geological and geochronological background for the 9000 meter thick fossil-rich Gyeongsang Supergroup in the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. Based on fossil assemblages, previous studies proposed that the Jehol Biota progressively expanded from the classic Jehol area, with younger representatives covering progressively larger geographic ranges. Fossils collected from the Gyeongsang Supergroup in South Korea are generally classified as the third phase of the Jehol Biota. During the field work, PI Chang and Co-I Lee observed the body fossils, dinosaur and bird tracks from these strata. The morphology of these fossils are distinct from the Jehol animals (Chang et al., 2015, AOGS abstract). Our U/Pb and Ar/Ar age data for different part of the Gyeongsang Supergroup also suggested that Gyeongsang fauna appear after ~100 Ma (Chang et al, 2016, AGU abstract). For example, our 40Ar/39Ar data for the famous Kusandong Tuff indicated that the middle part of the Gyeongsang Supergroup is ~78-82 Ma. Therefore the Gyeongsang fauna and the Jehol Biota were not contemporaneous. Our research further indicated that the previously established stratigraphic column for the Jehol fossil-bearing formations requires modification and the hypothesis for Cretaceous animal migrations needs to be reappraised (Chang et al, 2017, Palaeo^3). In addition to biogeographic interpretations, our study proposed a revised tectonic history of East Asia using detrital zircon age data from Cretaceous sedimentary basins along with previously published geochronologic data to reconstruct sedimentological and tectonic history (Wang et al, 2016, Tectonophysics; Wang et al., Geoscience Frontiers, in press).

27300114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300114.value: Although it sounds crazy, I propose to investigate Cretaceous fossil-bearing formations in North Korea. Our recent and previous geochronological studies for classic fossil outcrops in NE China and South Korea suggested that the migration routes for Cretaceous fauna are more complicated than previously thought and serval hypotheses related to biogeography in East Asia need to be reappraised. Reliable age data and stratigraphic correlations from the fossil-bearing formations in North Korea will allow to understand exactly how the animals exchanged during Cretaceous. This further study needs to be done once the door of North Korea opens.

27300114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300114.value: Abundant Cretaceous fossils and dinosaurs footprints from the southern part of the Korean Peninsula are well-preserved. Discoveries from this area have great potential for substantially increasing our knowledge of Cretaceous terrestrial ecosystems and paleogeography in East Asia. In this study, we investigated the fossil-bearing formations and aimed to reconstruct ancient sedimentary environments. Our study indicated that animals from this area thrived during middle-late Cretaceous and they did not co-exist with the famous feathered dinosaurs of the Jehol Biota from NE China. Our research also refined tectonic model for East Asia. This project provided fundamental implications for the understanding of biological evolution and the geological circumstances that influenced major episodes of diversification in Earth history.

27300214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300214.value: This project studies Donaldson-Thomas theory and stability conditions. Donaldson-Thomas (DT) theory was introduced by Donaldson and Thomas in the late 90s as an analogue of Donaldson theory on four manifolds and Casson-Floer theory on three manifolds. The Donaldson-Thomas invariants count holomorphic vector bundles on Calabi-Yau (CY) threefolds. They are important deformation invariants of CY threefolds. Moreover, they are the mathematical counterpart of Bogomol'nyi–Prasad–Sommerfield (BPS) numbers in string theory counting certain energy minimizing supersymmetric states. In the last two decades, there have been many exciting progresses in DT theory due to the influence of mirror symmetry. Mirror symmetry is a deep equivalence between the geometries of a mirror pair of CY threefolds predicted by string theory. The homological mirror symmetry conjecture of Kontsevich predicts that the complex geometry of a CY threefold and the symplectic geometry of its mirror partner have the equivalent algebraic strucures called Calabi-Yau 3D categories. Out of these categories, one can produce numbers counting certain objects. These numbers are the DT invariants. On the complex geometry side, the DT invariants count holomorphic vector bundles and on the symplectic geometry side they count Lagrangian submanifolds. After the landmark works of Joyce-Song and Kontsevich-Soibelman, DT theory finds more and more applications outside geometry, for example, in low dimensional topology and representation theory. In this project, the PI aims to study stability conditions in DT theory. The stability conditions are some extra parameters that DT invariants depend on. The change of DT invariants with respect to variation of stability conditions is controlled by the beautiful and mysterious Wall Crossing formulae. Surprisingly, these formulae show up in many apparently unrelated mathematical subjects. Bridgeland has setup a foundation for the theory of stability conditions on triangulated categories. The main objective of this project is to study the connections between Bridgeland’s stability conditions and the problem of existence of critical metrics in differential geometry. This can be viewed as an extension of the classical correspondence between algebraic geometry and Yang-Mills theory proved by Donaldson and Uhlenbeck-Yau. It will be a crucial step for understanding the geometry of CY threefolds and the mirror symmetry conjecture. Donaldson-Thomas理論作為四維流形上Donaldson理論以及三維流形上Casson-Floer理論的高維推廣，由Donaldson和Thomas在90年代末引入。其主要研究研究對象是關於複三維Calabi-Yau流形上的全純向量叢的計數幾何。Donaldson-Thomas不變量是超弦理論中BPS不變量的數學形式。在過去的二十年，Donaldson-Thomas的研究對數學和理論物理的很多領域都產生了深遠的影響。其中具有代表性的是Joyce和Song，以及Kontsevich和Soibelman關於motivic Donaldson-Thomas理論的開創性工作。 在該項目中，申請人將重點研究穩定性條件和三維Calabi-Yau流形上向量叢的幾何之間的聯繫。在一個方面，我們將研究Donaldson-Thomas不變量的模性質和穩定性條件之間的關係。另一個方面，我們將研究Bridgeland穩定性條件在緊致Calabi-Yau流形上的存在性問題和向量叢上的廣義Bogomolov-Gieseker不等式之間的聯繫。

27300214.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300214.value: Toric case: We have proved the global existence of algebraic Chern-Simons functional for bounded family of stable sheaves on toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. The result has been published on Pacific Math Journal 277-1 (2015), 119–147. Non-toric case: We have investigated the case when the Calabi-Yau 3-fold is the formal neighbourhood of a contractible rational curves. In this case, we find some surprising link between the study the Donaldson-Thomas invariants and the wall crossing formula and the study of the non commutative algebra and cluster category. The results can be summarised as follows: 1. For simple flopping contraction, we use the wall-crossing formula to show that the genus 0 Gopakumar-Vafa invariants can be reconstructed from the non commutative deformation algebra of the structure sheaf of the contractible curve. We also prove that the dimension of this algebra is the euler number of the dg-endomorphism algebra of a matrix factorisation. 2. The non-toric contraction is usually much more complicated than the toric ones. However, one can always deform a non-toric contraction to a "collection" of toric contractions. Using this idea we show that the non commutative deformation algebra for the non-toric contraction indeed deforms to semi-simple algebras. This is a nice application of DT theory to the study of non commutative deformation. 3. We study the conjecture of Donovan and Wemyss, which states that the non commutative deformation algebra of a contractible curve determines the underlying singularity. We prove that the deformation algebra admits a natural Z/2 graded A-infinity enhancement. Together with this enhancement, the deformation algebra indeed determines the singularity. 4. We have generalised some idea in Donaldson-Thomas theory to the non commutative context. The major results are a non commutative version of Mather-Yau theorem and a non commutative version of Saito's theorem. Work 1,2 are published in a joint work with Yukinobu Toda on International Mathematics Research Notices no. 10 (2018), 3173-3198. Work 3 is published on Mathematische Zeitschrift (2018): 431-443. Work 4 are in the preprints joint with Gui-song Zhou Non-commutative Mather-Yau theorem and its applications to Calabi-Yau algebras and homological minimal model program arXiv:1803.06128 Quasi-homogeneity of superpotentials arXiv:1808.03754 Both have been submitted.

27300214.value: The study of noncommutative deformations of rational curves has now became a very hot topic. The ideas from DT theory play important roles in this subject. We have been actively working on this subject.

27300214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300214.value: Our research links two different subjects in pure math: geometry and algebra, and leads to solution to open problems in the fields.

27300314.label: Project Objectives
27300314.value: The first goal is to understand the connection between vanishing of central L-values and modularity of local polynomial functions. This should be established through the known connection between vanishing of central L-values and vanishing of certain modular forms. The second goal is to establish a criterion to determine the modularity of these local polynomial functions on a case-by-case basis. The proposed criterion involves counting the number of circles of a certain type containing certain rational points. This would establish a computer algorithm to determine whether a central L-value will vanish or not. Using the established criterion from the second goal, establish a new criterion for determining when a number is congruent (when it is the area of a right triangle, all of whose sides are rational). Search for special infinite families where the above criteria (in the second and third objectives) may be determined explicitly (not case-by-case), hence establishing non-vanishing results overall.

The second goal is to establish a criterion to determine the modularity of these local polynomial functions on a case-by-case basis. The proposed criterion involves counting the number of circles of a certain type containing certain rational points. This would establish a computer algorithm to determine whether a central L-value will vanish or not.
Using the established criterion from the second goal, establish a new criterion for determining when a number is congruent (when it is the area of a right triangle, all of whose sides are rational).
Search for special infinite families where the above criteria (in the second and third objectives) may be determined explicitly (not case-by-case), hence establishing non-vanishing results overall.

27300314.label: Realisation of objectives
27300314.value: The first main project objectives have been achieved and a preprint with three co-authors has been uploaded to arvix and submitted for publication. There was need to construct a theta lift in the intermediary steps, and one of the co-authors was added for his expertise on this subject. The main resolution of the first objective is as follows: the vanishing of central L-values of the D-th quadratic twist of a given elliptic curve is equivalent to modularity of a certain "locally-constant part" of a modular object known as a locally harmonic Maass form. The second goal was achieved by taking the limit of these locally-constant parts towards the cusps of the given group upon which the locally harmonic Maass form is invariant. This in turn leads to a connection between the vanishing of the central L-value and comparison of the evaluation at two cusps. This was implemented on a laptop using a simple algorithm, and many cases were computed explicitly within a few hours; the resulting data obtained is available on the arxiv preprint. This was implemented for the special case of determining congruent numbers, and furthermore was used to also establish a criterion for checking whether a given integer may be written as the sum of two rational cubes (there are some technical restrictions which arise due to the construction, so these questions are only resolved for certain arithmetic progressions). This established the third goal. For the fourth goal, a certain parity condition was observed via the data for checking the non-vanishing at the p-th quadratic twist for the congruent number elliptic curve. There are some other cases where the same type of phenomenon was observed, and it would be interesting for future researchers to investigate whether this type of parity condition arises in a more general setting. Indeed, although the parity condition was not proven in the arxiv paper, after reading a preliminary version of the paper Dr. Volker Genz has announced a proof of the parity condition for the special case of the congruent number curve that was observed in the paper; the proof appears to be too technical to generalize, as it involves an understanding of the specific structure of the modular surface and showing that a certain intersection number is odd, but there are future directions where this research may have impact.

27300314.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300314.value: The main results are new criteria for vanishing of central L-values of D-th quadratic twists. The new condition is used for some combinatorial problems in order to establish a new criteria for determining the resolution of the congruent number problem and whether a given integer is the sum of two rational cubes. Along the way, there were related side-results involving the investigation of modular local polynomials (published in Math. Res. Lett.), p-adic properties of half-integral weight modular forms (published in Res. Number Theory), studies of meromorphic modular forms (A series of papers with Kathrin Bringmann in J. Math. Pures Appl., Res. Math. Sci., and Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg), as well as applications to divisors of modular forms (published in Adv. Math.).

27300314.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300314.value: There are two main directions that future research and developments in the area may take that come out of the primary research in this project. The first is a parity condition that was observed from the data that implies non-vanishing of quadratic twists. Volker Genz has announced a proof of the specific case observed in the paper, and there may be additional cases for which non-vanishing may be shown with this method. A search for a pattern of this type of behavior and a more general proof might lead to an interesting non-vanishing result. The second potential follow-up direction might be in looking for other combinatorial questions which can be addressed with this method.

27300314.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300314.value: A rational number is a number of the form a/b where a and b are integers (counting numbers). A new criterion is developed for finding whether a given integer n can be written as the sum of two rational cubes (that is, whether n=x^3 +y^3 is solvable with x and y rational numbers). A similar condition is obtained for determining if there exists a right triangle whose area is a given positive integer and all three of whose sides is rational. These are traditionally difficult questions and there have been alternative criteria determined within the last 30 years. Here similar conditions are found, which involve a simple sum that can easily be computed via a computer. The new conditions also have a geometric interpretation in terms of intersections of circles and lines and are connected to a deep mathematical object known as an L-function and another newer object known as a locally harmonic Maass form. The main goal of this research was to establish a connection between these two areas (namely, L-functions and locally harmonic Maass forms) and observe the consequences of this connection on certain classical counting problems such as those given above.
