27300514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300514.value: Recent significant changes in streamflow and the growing need for integrated basin management call for a better understanding of spatial drought patterns in the Pearl River basin and their long-term variability. However, instrumental records in the Pearl River basin are sparse, and most were not available until the 1950s. Such short and sparse instrumental data limit our ability to fully characterize regional drought variability, making it hard to assess the causes of observed variability and trends. Tree-rings are a valuable source for understanding large-scale drought variability over the past few centuries to millennia. Tree-rings are widely distributed across the Pearl River basin, yet they have not been employed to study long-term drought variability over the region. In this project we will employ tree-rings to investigate spatial drought patterns in the Pearl River basin and their multi-century variability. Specifically, we will develop a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Pearl River basin to reconstruct regional droughts five hundred years or more into the past. With the reconstruction we will assess current variability and trends with regard to natural fluctuations during the past five centuries, and will discern whether recent droughts are consequences of global warming or just inevitable natural swings of dry-wet periods. We will assess the linkages between regional droughts and large-scale climate modes such as the Asian monsoon and the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), so as to reveal the response of regional droughts to radiative and internal climate forcing. Our project will be the first integrated research that aims at investigating spatial drought patterns in the Pearl River basin and climate forcings that drive their multi-century variability. Through the development of a large-scale, multi-species tree ring network, we will be able to provide the much-needed long-term perspective necessary to detect and attribute recent drought and streamflow variability in the basin. Our results will allow the characterization of the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of drought anomalies, and will provide a testing and validation target for improving climate models. More broadly, our results will help policy makers and the general public understand long-term changes of basinwide droughts and streamflow, and will help plan for sustainable water resource management, mitigate impacts of floods and droughts, and reduce conflicts among stakeholders. 近年來珠江徑流發生了顯著變化，對流域進行綜合管理的需求亦日益增長。理解流域範圍內幹旱發生的空間特征及其長期變化規律迫在眉睫。然而，珠江流域內氣候觀測資料稀少，並且大部分在二十世紀五十年代後才開始。如此短且稀少的觀測資料使我們無法全面理解流域幹濕長期變化特征及其驅動因素。 樹木年輪是理解歷史時期大範圍幹濕變化的重要手段。樹輪在珠江流域分布廣泛，但目前還沒有被很好地用以研究該地區幹旱長期變化。此項目將利用樹木年輪研究珠江流域內幹旱發生的空間特征以及過去幾百年來的變化規律及其驅動因素。具體來講，我們將建立一個大範圍，多樹種的年輪網絡，並在此基礎上重建流域內過去五百年來幹旱變化歷史。在樹輪重建資料的基礎上，我們將評估近期流域內氣候、水文變化是否超出歷史範圍，是否為全球變暖的區域響應。進而我們將研究區域幹濕變化與亞洲季風和厄爾尼諾是否存在關聯，進而揭示區域幹濕變化對氣候變化外部及內部驅動因子的響應方式。 此項目為首次對珠江流域幹旱空間變化的長期特征及其驅動因素進行集成研究。通過建立大範圍，多樹種的年輪網絡，我們將能夠提供評估流域近期氣候及水文變化所需的長期背景資料。該項目研究結果將定量揭示流域內幹濕變化的典型時間尺度，持續時間及其強度特征，為利用氣候模型預測未來變化提供關鍵信息。另外，研究結果亦將幫助政策制定者及公眾更好的認識珠江流域幹旱和徑流長期變化特征，並有助於流域水資源可持續管理、減輕洪澇災害的影響，以及協調不同利益群體間的矛盾。

27300514.label: Realisation of objectives
27300514.value: We have achieved the five objectives outlined in the proposal of the project. Specifically: 5.3.1. Develop a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Pearl River basin for spatio-temporal drought reconstruction. During the past four years we have conducted four field trips in order to collect tree-ring samples for the development of a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Pearl River basin and neighboring areas. We have newly collected samples from seven sites in Yunnan province, three sites in Guangxi province and eight sites in Guangdong province. Together with previous collection of eleven sites in Yunnan and three sites in Guangxi, we have built a tree-ring network totaling 32 sites, with 18 (14) sites in the west (east) part of the Pearl River basin, respectively. The tree species sampled include: Abies georgei, Fokienia hodginsii, Picea likiangensis, Pinus fenzeliana, Pinus massoniana, Pinus yunnanensis, Pinus kwangtungensis, Tsuga chinensis. All the eight species have been identified to develop clear annual ring patterns and are suitable for dendrochronological studies in the region. All the samples were properly prepared and cross-dated with conventional dendrochronological techniques. Ring-widths were measured to 0.001 mm precision using a Velmex measuring system. The raw series were conservatively standardized in order to remove biological growth trends that are unrelated to climate. The standardized series were merged to develop robust mean chronology for each sampling site, which was retained for subsequent spatio-temporal drought reconstruction. The statistics indicate that most of the tree-ring chronologies cover the past 300-500 years, with the longest covering the past 800 years. These data provide a solid basis for the study of long-term climate change in the region. 5.3.2. Employ this tree-ring network to reconstruct spatial drought patterns over the Pearl River basin and their five hundred years variability. All the tree-ring data were synthesized to reconstruct long-term drought variability in the study area. Before performing the reconstruction, we identified with instrumental data that there are two dominant drought patterns in the Pearl River basin, with one centering in the west and another in the east part of the basin. Therefore, we aimed to use tree-rings to reconstruct long-term drought in the west and east basin separately. We employed linear principal components (PC) regression for the spatio-temporal drought reconstructions, and skills of the regression models were quantified with a suite of statistics for both the calibration and verification periods. For the west basin, we developed a five‐century drought reconstruction, which revealed dramatic change in regional drought and its coherent relationship with the Tibetan Plateau (TP) surface temperature at multi-decadal time scales. For the east basin, we conducted a three‐century drought reconstruction only due to the limits of tree-ring data in the region. Nonetheless, the reconstruction revealed severe droughts and marked multi-decadal variations over the past three centuries that were absent in the instrumental era. 5.3.3. Examine recent droughts with a five-century perspective, and identify the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of drought variability in the basin. The tree-ring reconstructions enabled the examination of recent drought status with a multi-century perspective for both west and east part of the Pearl River basin. During the research we statistically characterized the occurrence of extreme dry and wet periods and identified the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of droughts in the two parts of the basin. We assessed whether the observed trends and variability are unprecedented when compared with previous variations during the past few centuries, and determined whether there has been a response of regional droughts to global warming. The results and findings helped understand long-term variability of regional droughts at both time and frequency domain. 5.3.4. Assess the linkages between regional droughts and large-scale climate modes such as the Asian monsoon and the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and reveal the response of regional droughts to radiative and internal climate forcing. On the basis of the reconstructions, we investigated the linkages of drought variability in the Pearl River basin with large-scale climate modes. For the west basin, the five‐century drought reconstruction revealed dramatic change in regional drought and its coherent relationship with the Tibetan Plateau (TP) surface temperature at multi-decadal time scales, with increased moisture coincident with periods of high temperature. The coherent warm-wet relationship identified in our study implies a generally wetter condition on the southeastern TP under future warming, which is a manifestation of its response to anthropogenic radiative forcing. For the east basin, the three‐century drought reconstruction revealed severe droughts and marked multi-decadal variations over the past three centuries that were absent in the instrumental era. Further analysis showed that the drought extremes and variations were closely related to the East Asian monsoon strength and were also remotely modulated the ENSO events. Therefore, our assessment of the linkages between regional droughts and large-scale climate modes revealed the response of regional droughts to both internal and external climate forcing. 5.3.5. Determine the implications of our drought reconstruction for sustainable water resource management in the Pearl River basin. Our multi-century drought reconstructions provided strong justifications for sustainable water resource management in the Pearl River basin. For the west basin, the five‐century drought reconstruction revealed dramatic change in regional drought and its coherent relationship with the Tibetan Plateau (TP) surface temperature at multi-decadal time scales. The findings suggest that the southeastern TP will get wetter under global warming, which implies an increase in headwater flow for the west tributary of the Pearl River. Meanwhile, frequent and severe droughts and marked multi-decadal variations occurred in the east basin, which implies great challenges exist for sustainable water resource management now and in the future. Moreover, our assessment of the linkages between regional droughts and large-scale climate modes revealed the response of regional droughts to both internal and external climate forcing, an outcome that will lead to the development of improved climate models for better drought and streamflow forecasting in the Pearl River basin.

27300514.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300514.value: Under the generous support of the ECS grant, we built the first large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Pearl River basin, which was employed for conducting regional spatio-temporal drought reconstructions. Two dominant drought patterns were identified and reconstructed for the west and east part of the basin, respectively. For the west basin, we developed a five‐century drought reconstruction that revealed dramatic change in regional drought and its coherent relationship with the TP surface temperature at multi-decadal time scales, with increased moisture coincident with periods of high temperature. The coherent warm-wet relationship identified in our study suggests a generally wetter condition on the southeastern TP under future warming, which implies a moisture increase in the headwater area of the west tributary of the Pearl River. This work was published in Climate Dynamics (2017). For the east basin, we conducted a three‐century drought reconstruction only due to the limits of tree-ring data in the region. Nonetheless, the reconstruction revealed severe droughts and marked multi-decadal variations over the past three centuries that were absent in the instrumental era. Further analysis showed that the drought extremes and variations were closely related to the East Asian monsoon strength and were also remotely modulated the ENSO events. These results were reported in Mr. Li Teng’s PhD thesis and will be submitted for journal publication in summer 2019. Our assessment of the linkages between regional droughts and large-scale climate modes revealed the response of regional droughts to both internal (i.e., ENSO and AMO) and external (i.e., GHGs and volcanic eruptions) climate forcing in the Pearl River basin. The AMO and GHG forcing is more evident in the west, whereas ENSO and the volcanic forcing is stronger in the east part of the basin. These findings were detailed in Climate Dynamics (2017, 2018) and Mr. Li Teng’s PhD thesis. In addition to drought reconstructions, we found that many of the tree-rings in the area are actually temperature sensitive. Therefore, we have used some of the tree-ring data for temperature reconstructions, including a three-century winter temperature change on the southeastern TP published in Climate Dynamics (2017) and a 564-year annual minimum temperature change on the eastern Tibetan Plateau published in Global and Planetary Change (2017). Moreover, in order to facilitate further work that seeks to compare river flow anomalies in southern and northern China, we have reconstructed the Yellow River flow for the past 1200 years using tree-rings, which enabled an assessment of natural flow variability and the detection of human contributions to recent flow reductions. This work was published in Geophysical Research Letters (2019) and was highlighted by AGU in its publication Eos.

27300514.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300514.value: The tree-ring network developed through this project provides a solid basis for the study of long-term climate change in the Pearl River basin. We will continue to update the network by sampling more tree species and new sites in the next 2-3 years. The updated network will be used to extend our drought reconstruction for the past eight hundred years or so, which will help better understand recent droughts with a long-term perspective and identify the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of drought occurrence in the basin. In particular, we will use the updated tree-ring network to reconstruct long-term Pearl River flow for the past five to eight centuries, which will enable a comparison of river flow and water resource anomalies in southern and northern China and an assessment of the response of river flow to various climate forcing. We plan to apply for a new grant to support this work in the next round of RGC grant application.

27300514.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300514.value: Recent significant changes in rainfall and streamflow in the Pearl River basin call for a better understanding of regional droughts and their long-term variability. In this project, we built the first large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Pearl River basin and employed it to reconstruct regional drought patterns and their multi-century variability. The reconstructions enabled the examination of recent drought status with a multi-century perspective, and revealed the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of droughts in both west and east part of the Pearl River basin. The reconstructions also revealed the robust response of regional droughts to both internal and external climate forcing. Overall, our project is the first integrated research that investigated spatio-temporal drought patterns in the Pearl River basin, which provided the much-needed long-term perspective necessary to detect and attribute recent drought and streamflow anomalies in the basin. Our results should help policy makers and the general public understand long-term changes of basinwide droughts and streamflow, and will help plan for sustainable water resource management, mitigate impacts of floods and droughts, and reduce conflicts among stakeholders.

27400014.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27400014.value: 近代時期的詩歌，修辭及異論

27400014.label: Project Objectives
27400014.value: To delineate the predominating conceits of discursive agency, or the causal capacity of words, during the late mediaeval and early modern periods in Western Europe and England. To argue for, and illustrate, the transformation of several concepts of language central to Renaissance literary culture — ‘communication,’ ‘persuasion,’ and ‘expression.’ To proffer a novel theory of literary censorship based on discursive rivalry — the idea that social institutions such as religion and law might be competitors in the same language ‘business’ as literature, often reliant upon the same kinds of verbal resources to persuade. To provide new insight into the concept of heresy by bringing to light and engaging with arguments for its suppression in sixteenth-century versions of the Index librorum prohibitorum. Because no funds were given for conference travel and my proposed general expenses budget was cut by 81%, which leaves little opportunity for travel essential to my proposed outputs, my new fifth objective is to complete a book manuscript.

27400014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400014.value: As the tragic hero of Christopher Marlowe’s Tamburlaine the Great (1587) conquers the East like a juggernaut, he delivers magniloquent speeches that create a larger-than-life persona and reflect a mightier-than-the-gods attitude. After his promise of such spectacular martial deeds as could “chase the stars from heaven,” one admiring listener responds: “You see, my lord, what working words he hath.” My book project investigates how words were thought to work upon minds from the late mediaeval to the early modern period. To map the causal power imputed to speech over this time span, it is necessary to call upon a great multitude of verbal artifacts, both popular and learned. The observations that undergird my arguments are therefore drawn from a swath of Renaissance literary culture, including Tyndale’s Bible, Shakespeare’s plays, and Milton’s poetry, as well as diverse genres that are contiguous to the canon, such as treatises on witchcraft, pharmacopoeias, and proverbs. I will concentrate on those moments that reveal significant assumptions about the essential functions of language-use — moments that demonstrate the emergence of three key discursive concepts as we recognize them today: ‘communication,’ ‘persuasion,’ and ‘expression.’ I argue that each of these ideas changes greatly during the Renaissance, and each can play a large role in our understanding of the period. A good ingress to recuperating beliefs about discursive agency can be found in the conceits of those who found words especially formidable: poets and censors. Consequently, another major source of evidence that I propose to examine is rationales for the suppression of heterodox speech in censorship decrees. I observe that, during this epoch, poets and censors not only share a model of how language operates, but also are engaged in a high-stakes competition over verbal resources — the fabulation of poetry and the figuration of rhetoric. These means were deemed valuable since they were supposed to be especially effective in creating and altering the criteria of belief. The overarching purpose of this project, therefore, is to explain the nature of the Renaissance rivalry between institutional authorities and literary authors, and to expound the devices by which texts attempt to control other texts — to the end of winning the hearts and minds of readers. The project will involve the PI in extensive library and archive work in several languages, with the ambition of producing a monograph that will make a substantial and original contribution to the scholarship of Renaissance studies. 當克裏斯托弗•馬洛筆下的悲劇英雄帖木兒大帝 （原書出版於1587年）像萬能的神靈般征服東方時，他發表的演說言辭極為誇張，渲染壹種英雄式的，甚至超越眾神的傳奇色彩。當他允諾 “把星星從天堂驅趕出去”的壯舉時，聽眾中壹名崇拜者稱贊道：“尊敬的閣下，看他那言辭多麽富有力量！”本人申請的項目將研究從中世紀末到近代人們對於語詞如何作用於心靈的看法。 為了達到此研究目的，本人需要調查大量通俗及經典文本。其中包括多部文藝復興時期的經典作品，如廷代爾的聖經，莎士比亞的戲劇和彌爾頓的詩歌；以及其他各種與這些經典緊密相連的文本，如論述巫術，藥典及諺語的文章。本人將重點分析那些表現語言使用功能的論述。這些功能，按當今學者的共識，可分為“交流”，“說服”以及“表達”三方面。而這三項功能的起源都可追溯至上述文本。在這壹時期對於每項功能的論述前後發生很大的變化，這些論述深刻的影響我們對於整個文藝復興時期的理解。 為了深入了解圍繞“話語能動性”(discursive agency)的各種論述，壹個好的切入點是詩人和審查者—他們都對語言的巨大效力深信不疑。正基於此，審查法令中對於壓制異論的論述也是本項目主要的研究資料。在研究過程中，本人發現此時期的詩人和審查者不僅對於語言運作的機制持相同觀點，而且在搶占話語資源的風險戰中，他們都極盡能事使用各種策略（例如：詩歌中的虛假編造，各種繁復的修辭技巧）。他們對這些策略的使用，正表明人們相信話語的效力—它們能夠建立並改變信仰的標準。而本書將重點研究權威機構和作家之間的這種對手關系，並且展示他們為了實現最終目的，即贏得讀者的親睞，而在文本中运用的各種技巧。 此研究項目需要申請人使用大量圖書館和檔案資源（涉及多種語言）。該項目預期成果為學術專著壹本。本人期待該專著將為文藝復興研究做出紮實的原創性貢獻。

27400014.label: Realisation of objectives
27400014.value: In the course of working on a theory of literary censorship, my objectives shifted to an investigation of a different, but related target, namely obscenity. I devised a novel theory of literary obscenity by looking at historical developments in both law and literature—from classical antiquity to early modernity to more more modern instances. That theory and investigation can be found in “Obscenity and Marginality,” Law and Humanities 11:1 (2017): 7-23. In addition, I followed the question of taboo topics into a more contemporary forum by looking at the use and abuse of names in the rhetoric of U.S. presidential nominees. See “The Function of Names in U.S. Presidential Debates: Some Recent Powerplays,” Performance Research 22:5 (2017): 94-105. I acknowledged ECS support for both of these publications. I have completed a substantial portion of the original fifth objective, which included three conference papers. “The Bounds of Renaissance Prose Satire” Renaissance Society of America March 2017 Chicago, Illinois “The Art of Arts: Transcendental Dialectic in Early Modernity” American Comparative Literature Association March 2016 Cambridge, Massachusetts “Obscenity and Marginality: The Problem of the Complicit Censor” Interdisciplinary Colloquium on Legal Marginalia April 2015 The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong “Lyric Licence in Early Modern Spain” (paper accepted) Renaissance Society of America March 2015 Berlin, Germany In addition, I published two articles in international refereed journals (see above). The objectives for 5.2 should be tweaked as follows: 1- To delineate a predominating conceit of discursive agency, or the causal capacity of words, by looking at how obscenity was thought to affect readers’ minds during early modern and modern periods in Anglophone law and literature. 2- To argue for, and illustrate, how tropes and figures about names serve to communicate U.S. presidential identities during debates. 3- To proffer a novel theory of obscenity and therefore of certain literary censorship based on a philological investigation of the idea of the ‘margin.’ 4- To provide new insight into the concept of obscenity by bringing to light and engaging with arguments for its suppression in long-neglected early modern legal cases. 5- To publish two articles in internationally peer-reviewed journals.

27400014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27400014.value: The significance of the obscenity project: One of the neglected origins of the word 'margin' is scar. The dictates of taboo and law form a protective boundary, a scar or margin, over the wound of obscenity, so we are not in touch with what is ever raw—so that we are hidden from our embodied natures. The law stamps out indecorums that threaten to ‘scandalize and debase human nature’, that make salient our inexorably fleshly facets. A requisite of one kind legal power is the cultivation of a subject with an elevated self-image—a supra-bestial mindset—and therefore higher behavioral expectations. This is why one prominent juristic explanation of obscenity’s harm sounds sweeping and fundamental: subverting morality in general, slackening society’s ‘moral fiber’, ‘poison[ing] the springs and principles of manners’. These proscriptions encourage us to carry on with a dignified bearing; or, from a different angle, they demand that we regard the body, the skânos or portable tent, as a holy tabernacle that houses a lofty spirit. The Significance of the Use of Names Article: I examine how US presidential candidates have increasingly deployed names to create a powerful ethos for themselves while characterizing their opponent tendentiously. I explore selected rhetorical strategies in debate performances, momentous oratory in which a presidential identity is staged. In particular, I look to recurrent figures in service of typing the adversary and augmenting the self. The essay concludes with a reflection on how candidates’ name-based shaming of voters has shaped the past two US elections.

27400214.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400214.value: This project creates an inventory and archive of outdoor stairs located primarily in the Central and Western District, HK Island. A significant and often historic part of the urban fabric, staircases evidence a unique stair culture which is increasingly threatened by careless maintenance practices and construction projects. The aim of the project is to research the history of HK stairs, to document their present state through contemporary archival photography, architectural drawings, and a physical and social inventory, and to theorize the research through scholarly publications and conference presentations. The project will begin by examining archival and government records in combination with basic site investigations to determine a list of historically significant stairs which will structure the framework for the documentation and stair inventory content management system prototype. This system will be a repository for the data collected throughout the project. Local models for the system include the HK slopes database and the Old and Valuable Tree list, but our system will be based on open source principles with a goal to use it as a model for a more complete inventory of HK stairs. The second part of the project will include detailed data collection and measurements to facilitate drawings and the physical and social inventory. This part of the project will also involve collaboration with a photography course at the Savannah Collage of Art and Design, a crowdsourced effort to collect stair photos and stories, and Google Streetview to capture stair routes, 90% of which are not currently available on Google Maps. The third part of the project will organize and synthesize the data into five types of output: a website, a coffee-table type book, a public exhibition, an academic symposium, and a journal paper. Ultimately, this work seeks to raise public awareness about the value of stairs to HK's history, its everyday life, and its continuance as a liveable city. As key components of a rich, walkable pedestrian environment which occupies steep topography, the physical and social life of stairways needs to be documented, recorded and celebrated, both to increase the likelihood of their protection, and to contribute to a broader historical archive of the continuing development of the city. The HK Stair Archive is an opportunity to capture a typology of infrastructure which has never been systematically or thoroughly researched in Hong Kong, despite their ubiquitous presence and absolute necessity in the efficient navigation of the city. 這個計劃是創建一個目錄清單，主要記錄香港島中西區的戶外樓梯。作為城市脈絡中的重要的歷史部分，梯級構成的獨特樓梯文化，卻被粗心的維修方法和建設項目所威脅。本計劃的目的是研究香港樓梯的歷史，透過現代保存攝影 (archival photography)、建築圖則以及實體和社會詳細目錄，記錄它們的現狀，同時透過學術出版和會議演說，嘗試把樓梯文化理論化。 本計劃將首先盤點現有的文獻和政府檔案，及基本的實地考察，以列出具有歷史意義的樓梯，并以它們為研究框架，建立文檔和樓梯的庫存內容管理系統原型。這個系統將儲存本計劃的所有資料。本地的系統範例包括“斜坡資訊系統”及 “古樹名木冊”，不過我們的系統將會是開源的（open source），以成為一個更完善的香港樓梯資料庫。 計劃的第二部分將包括詳細資料收集和測量，以協助建立建築圖則以及實體和社會詳細目錄。這個計劃部分將包括：與薩凡納藝術設計學院協辦的攝影課程，透過眾包（crowdsourcing）去收集樓梯的相片及相關故事；在谷歌街景服務去獲取樓梯路線，因為九成的樓梯路線不在現在的谷歌地圖上。 項目的第三部分將會把資料整理和總結成五個研究成果：一個網站，一本放置咖啡桌上的書（coffee-table type book），一個公共展覽，一場學術研討會，及一份期刊論文。 最後，本計劃希望引起公眾關注樓梯在香港歷史、日常生活以及使香港成為宜居城市的價值。作為建構於陡峭地形豐富的步行環境的關鍵，樓梯中的實體及社會面貌值得記錄和讚頌，以增加保育樓梯的可能性和成為城市的持續發展的歷史記錄。基礎建設隨處可見，而“香港樓梯資料庫”將是全港罕有關於香港基礎建設的深入研究，去記錄基建的基本形體（typology of infrastructure）。

27400214.label: Realisation of objectives
27400214.value: Project objectives have been achieved to about 95%. See the previous two reports for details of research activities and aspects of objectives achieved. In addition, since the last report in March 2017, the following has been achieved: 1) The exhibition, “always at the edge of things and between places” was held for three weeks as Connecting Space Hong Kong with the support of the UGC, PolyU, the HKADC and ZHdK. The intent of the exhibition was to provoke the general public, as well as the art and design community, to reflect upon: 1) the role of stairs in creating and preserving a walkable, livable city with a vibrant arts and cultural life; and 2) potential futures for Hong Kong’s vernacular, cultural landscape. The project achieved these objectives by inviting the public to participate not only as viewers, but also as catalysts and contributors. The result was the activation of the HKSA through innovative time-based, socio-cultural works that built history while also envisioning the future of Hong Kong’s urban landscape. The exhibition and events, including tours, workshops and discussion panels, directly reached almost 1000 people and was covered by several local media outlets, including an online video feature by Apple Daily. The work continues to draw public and media interest, with students, professionals and media continuing to contact Melissa for interviews and for her expertise and perspective on HK Stair Culture and several of the artworks commissioned for the show being re-presented in other venues or presented as part of the participant's research and production outcomes/writing/lectures. Regarding the artists and local arts development, the exhibition brought together a somewhat unique mix of people, including visual and multimedia artists, architects, landscape architects and urban designs, politicians and policy makers, students of all ages, academics, and the general public. This intermixing of what is research, what is art, what is advocacy, what is play, and what is heritage and preservation (amongst other topics touched upon in the works and in the events) broadened the perspective of all the parties, creating an exciting transdiciplinary collaborative environment. Please see stairculture.com/archive/ and https://www.facebook.com/alwaysathedge for more information on the events of the show and the exhibition catalog for information on the artworks and artists included in the exhibition. 2) Outstanding items including the submission of the book proposal and academic article for review, and the ongoing work of updating the online map, as well as placing the physical artifacts in a physical archive. These have been delayed due to the PI taking on other projects and public outreach activities for the HKSA (including tours and lectures) as well as teaching commitments. In addition, the work to complete these is taking longer than expected, partially due to the decision to include the work of the exhibition in the publication, as well as several collaborators moving overseas (and the PI no longer having support staff after Dec 2017). However the framework is now set up, the PI continues to be contacted with issues regarding stairs by local and international students, professional and the general public and the work has led to other projects locally (such as Magic Lanes) and internationally ( such as the UTS visiting fellowship, which applied similar methodologies to the Sydney context in preparation for a comparative study which employs ideas of topographic urbanism developed in the HKSA project.

27400214.label: Major findings and research outcome
27400214.value: - Mapping and documentation of over 3000 stairs through QGIS, organized into 12 types and accessible online; - 1:100 Architectural drawing sets of 8 historic stairs and 15 archival photographic sets, both to HABS standards; - Public exhibitions, lectures, publications etc (see Part C); - Primary uses of stairs include walking, sitting, chatting and smoking. Additional uses include gathering spaces for events and activities like watching movies, organized exercise, hanging and drying of clothes and traditional foods, and hawking, among others. - Found there are no universal standards for design, construction and maintenance that apply to stairs as a class of infrastructure within Hong Kong. Responsibility is divided amongst as many as eleven different government departments. This makes enforcing unified standards and an accounting system for all the stairs extraordinarily difficult. A primary recommendation would be to expand the existing Slope Information System (SIS) to include information about stairs or to create a separate system along that model. An example of this would be stair records of the Seattle Department of Transportation Capital Projects and Roadway Structures (CPRS) Division, which is responsible for overseeing the city’s roadway structures, including bridges, retaining walls, public stairways. They have hard copy and digital records on each of the city’s 650 stairways. - A significant number of stairs do not meet international code for accessibility, primarily because HK’s standard handrail/guardrail is not compliant (if a stair has a handrail at all). A primary recommendation would be to include a compliant handrail in HK standard details and to require all exterior stairs to have at least one handrail, as well as other accessibility features for the visually impaired. - Pound Lane, a stari which was an early focus of the PI's work in 2011-2013, has ben given a Grade 2 by the AMO in 2018.

27400214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27400214.value: Due to the nature of the topic, the PI is still involved in many aspects of HKSA related work. For example, the website continues to be developed through gathering further details and photos of stairs through the Stair Quest app and through more traditional means. The project has led to work on advisory boards, such as at Magic Lanes, which has already led to two book chapters and a URF funded project to renovate the Lane (with CUHK and Caritas). Stairs in HK are still under threat, even just this week the Highways Department damaged Shing Wong Street (which is under review for heritage grading), leading to an outcry by the local concern group (https://www.hongkongfp.com/2018/12/18/workers-tidy-ugly-yellow-non-slip-paint-historic-sheung-wan-steps-amid-outcry/), who has now asked the PI to give a workshop on the importance of stairs on how to document and assess local needs for accessibility improvements so as to make changes that respect the local community and heritage. Both an academic article and an edited volume of the work/book proposal are in production, with submittals planned for the first quarter of 2019.

27400214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27400214.value: The Hong Kong Stair Archive is a collaborative pilot project to document outdoor stairs, initially a selection located primarily in the Central and Western District. It is part of Stair Culture, an internationally unique long term research and curatorial project undertaken in collaboration with artists, designers, students, curators, and cultural and educational institutions to investigate the way stairs define the character of the urban environment. As part of the everyday landscape of mountainous HK, outdoor stairways play a critical role in creating a permeable and accessible public realm. Embedded in hillsides, stacked on sidewalks or replacing streets and alleys altogether, these ubiquitous stairs and the complex wayfinding they enable are a reflection of a diverse city in continual flux. Considered utilitarian uphill access routes, the majority of HK stairs are built and maintained with function and frugality in mind. Although some number among the city’s oldest remaining built insertions, consolidated documentation is limited to the few declared a Monument or given a Built Heritage Grade. However, there are thousands whose transitioning role is an indicator of wider cultural landscape change. An awareness of this Stair Culture can condition types of intervention that respect and improve the existing fabric of the city.

27400414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400414.value: 摘要 背景 根據資料顯示，不孕問題影響8-15%正值生育年齡的夫婦。在香港，試管嬰兒是一種不孕夫婦常採用的治療方法。這種治療不但需時長、痛苦和有損害性，而且只有約20－25%接受療程的婦女能成功懷孕。婦女在過程中經常出現焦慮和情緒低落，有關方面制訂了干預方案以減低她們所承受的不安。傳統的輔導需要親身接觸，這既高成本，而服務使用者也很難在忙碌的生活中抽時間安排。有學者研究發現，自我管理形式的介入，對正在接受試管嬰兒治療的婦女在減低不安情緒方面有正面的成效，這正好避免了以上的困難。 目的與方法 這項研究將會測試自我管理形式的介入對正在積極接受試管嬰兒治療的婦女在改善精神健康方面的成效。研究的目標如下： • 為正在積極接受試管嬰兒治療的婦女制訂一套自我管理形式的心理干預方案 • 探究心理干預方案中有關不同元素的成效，評估針對靈性和行為的元素的不同組合 • 為加強對試管嬰兒治療的心理支援作出貢獻，並減低正在積極進行試管嬰兒治療的婦女的不安 這項介入方案改編自綜合身心靈介入治療。綜合身心靈介入治療曾對接受第一次療程前的婦女進行測驗。從這介入治療中，心靈和行為的要素將會被採用，並改編為一套自我管理的套件。研究顯示，婦女在接受了胚胎移植後，和等候進行驗孕測試的兩星期間格外有壓力。因此，套件的運作會集中在這段時間等候結果中的婦女。這是一個三組隨機抽樣對照的設計，而抽查樣本數量為192人。兩次測量都會採用已被驗證對中國人口有效的量表。 重要性 這研究針對現有不孕輔導的缺陷：1. 需要最低的面對面接觸，因此成本會較低；2. 針對在積極治療期間突發性的壓力；3. 比較只有靈性介入元素，和結合靈性和行為元素的介入方案，以了解綜合身心靈介入治療的機制。如這自我管理式的介入有正面的成效，將有利於擴大輔導服務至其他類別的服務使用者。這能在不加重成本壓力下，讓之前未能接觸輔導服務的人得到更有效的支援。

27400414.label: Realisation of objectives
27400414.value: Objective 1 has been fully realised with the development of a self-help booklet informed by the integrative body-mind-spirit (I-BMS) intervention, which has been administered to 357 women during IVF treatment. The aim of the booklet was to help lessen anxiety and enhance holistic well-being during the period before pregnancy test, which is widely regarded as the most stressful of treatment stages. In line with the concept of interconnectedness of the mind, body, and spirit, the booklet incorporates both spiritual and mind-body components. Respectively, these components are presented in the form of tales and proverbial stories sharing the common motif of acceptance and self-affirmation intended to induce spiritual reflection and mobilize acceptance coping strategies, as well as instructions for behvioural exercises like acupressure, swinging movements, breathing exercises and clapping Qignog. Women were advised to spend at least 15 minutes on each module daily during the two-week waiting period. Objective 2 has been fully realised with the execution of a three-arm randomized-controlled trial that compares the effectiveness of 1) an intervention with spiritual and behavioural components, 2) an intervention with spiritual components only, and 3) a control condition with informational reading materials on IVF treatment. The purpose of introducing two intervention arms is to test whether effectiveness differs when the behavioural and spiritual components are administered in combination versus when the spiritual component is administered alone. Our assumption was that differential effects would reflect the extent to which individual components influences well-being, and provide valuable data for future adaptations of the self-help contents. Level of anxiety was our primary outcome of interest. To a lesser extent, effects of the intervention were also explored in relation to dispositional gratitude, bodily distress, holistic well-being, infertility-related stress and quality of life, as well as perceived importance of childbearing. Participants were asked to complete a gratitude journal daily after completing the prescribed exercises. Journal completion serves as a proxy measure of exercise completion, an instrument with which to record daily levels of psychosocial functioning and clinical symptom, as well as a medium for personal reflection as they narrate their daily experience. We hypothesized women who received the spiritual-behavioural booklet would exhibit lower levels of anxiety together with improvement in secondary outcomes compared to women who received the spiritual intervention alone or an informational booklet on IVF. We also expect greater reduction in distress over time in the spiritual-behavioural intervention group than in either the spiritual group or control group. Our hypotheses were not supported by the present findings. Data show the benefits brought about by a self-help booklet with spiritual and behavioural exercises do not exceed those brought about by other interventions. Also, results give no indication of any improvement in primary or secondary outcomes over time, and the extent of change does not differ between groups. In other words, our results appear to suggest that effectiveness does not differ whether spiritual and behavioural components are administered in combination or in isolation. With regards to objective 3, comments gathered from participants' gratitude journal show thy find the booklet useful in helping them think positively and distracting them from negative thoughts. Through reading spiritual and proverbial stories, participants were encouraged to re-evaluate the meaning of infertility in relation to their life and they reported gaining solace from realizing they are not alone in this journey. In particular, many participants felt they were more able to appreciate the impermanence of things in life and the importance of treasuring what they own instead of agonizing over what is beyond their control. In brief, the booklet may have given them timely prompts for reappraisal and spiritual reflections. While the present findings do not reveal significant reduction in anxiety or improvement in psychological well-being during the intervention period, we suggest incorporating materials to stimulate spiritual reflections may effectively increase positive affect and improve emotional well-being. This provides a viable target for future research on psychosocial interventions for this population. The present findings should be interpreted in light of several methodological constraints. For example, the present sample consists only of women actively seeking treatment at a local fertility clinic, resulting in a sample of participants who are more well off and possibly more in need of psychosocial support to begin with. The latter is supported by observations on the state-trait anxiety inventory indicating high levels of state and trait anxiety even before the start of the intervention period. This limits the generalizability of the findings to other subgroups of infertile women. Although this study finds little convincing evidence for the self-help booklet to effectively reduce anxiety during the IVF waiting period, further research is needed with more generalizable samples and more meticulous strategies for participant recruitment and retention. The present findings should also be interpreted in relation to existing psychosocial support services for IVF receivers in Hong Kong. The self-help booklet provides a less intrusive alternative to existing services and targets specifically the two-week IVF waiting period as the period of intervention, which is often considered the most of distressing of treatment stages. Based on the present findings, we suggest the self-help booklet may be administered as an adjunct to other support services like counselling or group-based therapies. We also speculate the two-week wait may not be the best period during which to intervene. This is in line with most group interventions taking place few weeks before the start of treatment or during active treatment periods.

rows: A self-help booklet was developed for women undergoing IVF treatment. The intervention consists of a) a spiritual component in the form of affirmation-acceptance stories and messages created by the research team based on the spiritual themes prescribed by the I-BMS model; and b) a body-mind component with instructions for a series of body-centered exercises, such as acupressure, simple qigong , and breathing exercises. Women were advised to complete the prescribed exercises each day during the 14-day waiting period and then detail their reflections and clinical symptoms in a gratitude journal.

The relative effectiveness of the spiritual and behavioural components were assessed with a three-arm randomized-controlled trial. Findings reveal the spiritual-behavioural self-help booklet is no more effective than either spiritual materials or IVF-related informational materials alone. Also, neither of the three intervention leads to improvement in psychosocial well-being during the waiting period. This leads us to speculate the waiting period is itself naturally stress-inducing and that it is best to intervene before the start of or during active IVF treatment.

This study addresses limitations of existing psychosocial support services for IVF patients by developing an intervention that requires minimal facilitation and therefore one more cost-efficient and addresses acute stress during the active treatment period (Details can be referred at Section 11 on project impact). Although the self-administered booklet did not reduce women's distress during the waiting period, it may well serve as an adjunct to other forms of support such as counselling and multi-session group programs. Future studies may consider delivering interventions before the start of the IVF treatment or in parallel to treatment to allow sufficient time for women's coping repertoire to build up prior to the waiting period.

27400414.label: Major findings and research outcome
27400414.value: We randomized and analyzed data from a total of 356 women. Response rate for the study was 44%. All analyses were performed by the intention-to-treat principle, which means data from all randomized participants were entered into analysis, irrespective of any protocol deviation or subsequent drop-out. From Time 1 (i.e. the day of embryo transfer ) to Time 2 (i.e. the fourteenth day of the waiting period), paired samples t-test revealed significant elevations of state anxiety, bodily irritability and spiritual disorientation in the spiritual-behavioural and spiritual groups. No such changes were observed in the control group. Further, ANCOVA revealed no significant time x group interaction [Fs(2, 349)<2.61, p>.075], suggesting the extent of change between Time 1 and Time 2 did not differ between groups. The present findings revealed two major observations: 1) women experienced significant levels of anxiety both before and after the intervention and 2) neither of the three conditions is more effective than another in reducing anxiety and improving psychosocial outcomes in women during the IVF waiting period. Contrary to our hypotheses, women in the spiritual-behavioural and spiritual conditions showed elevated levels of bodily irritability and spiritual disorientation during the Time 1-Time 2 period, with effect sizes ranging from small to medium. Based on the present findings, we suggest the self-help booklet be used as an adjunct to other forms of support services because of the ease of administering, rather than an intervention to be administered alone. Also we speculate the two-week waiting period may not be the best time to intervene, and that some form of facilitation may be necessary to initiate positive changes. The present findings should be interpreted in light of several methodological caveats, such as the low response rate and high attrition rate. Future studies would benefit from more elaborate recruitment strategies as well as strategies to maximize participant retention. Further, because only a small proportion of participants returned the gratitude journal, we cannot determine participants' level of adherence to the intervention exercises, and it may have been poor adherence that attenuated the intervention effects. In short, the present study did introduce a feasible and cost-efficient addition to existing psychosocial services, although further studies are needed to clarify the benefits of such an intervention and identify factors conducive of its beneficial effects, for example, whether its effects are more pronounced when administered alongside weekly coaching sessions delivered by social workers.

27400414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27400414.value: This study agrees with previous studies in finding the IVF waiting period to be a particularly stressful period for women receiving treatment, and thus advocates for continual psychosocial support for this population. The present study shows it is feasible to incorporate spiritual contents in interventions for infertile individuals. Further, this study revealed the importance of timing of intervention, such that beneficial effects may be more pronounced were the intervention administered in parallel with active treatment. Although the data did not reveal major findings in favour of the intervention on a population level, women's feedback in the gratitude journal show the proverbial stories successfully communicated key spiritual themes (e.g. acceptance and surrendering control) and these did facilitate emotional well-benig in times of difficulty. Future studies could further examine the utility of self-help tools in IVF treatment by comparing a condition with a group-based program combined with self-help materials against a condition with group-based program alone. Such findings would not only test the rigour of such combined intervention for clinical use, but also establish the effectiveness and feasibility of self-help materials as adjunct treatment. These studies could also investigate impact on psychosocial well-being with and without professional coaching or facilitation to complement self-help materials.

27400414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27400414.value: The two-week waiting period in IVF treatment is considered by many to be a very distressing stage, often accompanied by such psychological symptoms as anxiety, depression and stress. These psychological detriments can be dealt with by formal counselling services and group interventions with differing focus on the mind and body. However, most patients do not see themselves as distressed enough to warrant counselling services and group sessions often require extra commitment from already distressed individuals. We therefore set out to test whether a self-help booklet informed by the integrative body-mind-spirit model can effectively reduce anxiety and improve well-being for women waiting for pregnancy test results during IVF treatment. This booklet is easy to administer and requires little facilitation, making it a handy instrument that can be more broadly utilized by women with differing care needs. Through testing the effectiveness of this self-help intervention with a rigorous scientific method, however, the findings show that it is not more effective than a currently utilized care condition. The development of the booklet may be used as an adjunct to existing psychosocial services and may serve as a handy source of support for women who prefer to opt out of formal support services.

27400714.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27400714.value: 金屬微觀結構模型的認識 - 高中化學學習進展

27400714.label: Project Objectives
27400714.value: To identify and describe students’ progression in learning different models of the nanoscale structure of metals throughout their Grade 10-12 (equivalent to 16-18 year olds) chemistry studies. To understand how students deploy different models of the nanoscale structure of metals in explaining different physical and chemical properties of metals throughout the course of their chemistry studies.
rows: To identify and describe students’ progression in learning different models of the nanoscale structure of metals throughout their Grade 10-12 (equivalent to 16-18 year olds) chemistry studies.

To understand how students deploy different models of the nanoscale structure of metals in explaining different physical and chemical properties of metals throughout the course of their chemistry studies.

27400714.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400714.value: Chemistry can be regarded as the study of the relationships between the nano-structures of substances and their properties. In the senior secondary science curricula of many countries, there are three scientific models of the nanoscale structure of metals, each with a different level of sophistication. Learning of these models is not straightforward. Learning of the more advanced models requires an understanding of the simpler one. Students are expected to use different models flexibly to explain properties of metals (e.g., malleability, heat and electrical conductivity), and to learn other chemical concepts throughout their chemistry studies. Investigating students’ understanding of chemical concepts is a key research area in chemistry education. Many research studies on students’ learning of chemistry are cross-sectional. This project is longitudinal and will be able to track students’ development. It aims to investigate (i) how students develop an understanding of the three models of the nano-structure of metals based on their prior knowledge and (ii) how they draw on their understanding of those models in learning other chemical concepts such as chemical reactions, electrochemistry and crystal structures. Students’ learning of different models of metals is investigated because such learning is representative of the nature of chemistry understanding, namely, the study of structure/property relationships, and the progressive study of chemical concepts based on a flexible use of different scientific models. This study adopts qualitative methodology. Data will be drawn from in-depth interviews with 18 students taking senior secondary school chemistry (Grades 10-12) in Hong Kong. To generate insights from the widest variety of students’ understanding, students will be drawn from three secondary schools with diverse levels of academic achievement. Each student will be interviewed on eight occasions over a three-year period. Data from these 144 interviews will reveal students’ knowledge prior to learning the different models of metals, how they utilize that prior knowledge in learning these models, and how they use these models in learning other concepts. The study will advance our understanding of students’ cognitive structures and the cognitive resources they use in learning. There is extensive research on the progression of junior secondary (Grades 7-9) students’ learning of “matter as particles”. But the learning progression of chemical models in senior secondary chemistry remains an unexplored area. The findings on students’ learning progression, how some students succeed and others struggle will inform chemistry curriculum development, teaching, and assessment, which are key to enhancing students’ participation in STEM education.

27400714.label: Realisation of objectives
27400714.value: I have collected all the data collection (144 individual interviews over 2.5 years, with each interview lasted for 20-45 minutes) as planned. The data were all transcribed and analyzed, which enabled me to answer questions in relation to the two objectives.

27400714.label: Major findings and research outcome
27400714.value: This project proposed that there are three submicroscopic structural models of metals at the school level science/ chemistry. They are (1) Simple particle model, (2) Atomic model, and (3) Free electron model. Based on these models, this study embarked on identifying how students reasoned chemical reactions with these models. It was found that students' reasoning of chemical reactions can be conceptualized as using two models: (a) Particle model of reactions - reactions are regarded as spatial rearrangement of simple particles. This model is commonly likened to rearrangement of Lego blocks. (b) Atomic model reactions - reactions involve specific particles such as ions, atoms, molecules and electrons. The Lego analogy breaks down in this model because particles would change, say, from ions to molecules or from atoms to ions (cw. individual Lego blocks remained unchanged in spatial rearrangement). Some students were adept at representing chemical reactions as the particle model – to the extent that they adopted this model for redox reactions, which should be represented more usefully by the atomic model. Also, this project conceptualized variations within individual students as they represented the same reaction in different occasions (after they were taught acid/base reactions, electrochemistry, and at the end of their secondary schooling respectively). Instead of treating their models as misconceptions or failure to learn, their preference for the particle model could be regarded as resources for the teaching of the atomic model. Additionally, findings from this project suggested that although the particle model looks simpler than the atomic model, it can help to support the learning of some advanced chemical concepts such as energetics and collision theory. Therefore, it is postulated that students who reason using the particle model are able to demonstrate some advanced ideas about chemical reactions. The conceptualisation of reactions in terms of the atomic model and the particle model allows a flexible understanding of students’ learning. The study offers insights for curriculum planners and teachers into the potential of these two models to help students understand chemical reactions.

27400714.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27400714.value: The two models should inform curriculum development in Junior Science and senior secondary school chemistry,

27400714.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27400714.value: Curriculum developers around the world, including those in HK, did not have a clear view of how to develop students' understanding of structural models of matters and models of reactions in their STEM curriculum at the secondary school levels. This project identified (1) three submicroscopic structural models of metals, and (2) two major models of chemical reactions that were adopted in school chemistry. They are of different levels of sophistication. Results of this study can inform school science curriculums that can better support students' learning progressively.

27400814.value: 投機都市主義：殖民地香港的現代主義規劃與房屋建造，1912-1939

27400814.label: Project Objectives
27400814.value: To reposition the interwar period as a significant moment where emergent ideas of planning, housing and urban reform were debated and implemented in Hong Kong. To illustrate the multifarious networks that connected Hong Kong with other regions, and by doing so challenge the previous “diffusionist,” “derivative” models of urban development and longstanding conceptions of “centers” and “peripheries.” To address the significance of property relations facilitated by colonial capitalism and to provide a more nuanced understanding of the relations between the government and the “governed” under colonial rule. To enable more critical revaluations of urban development and governance in the post-WWII period. To make the case that historical research is an essential component for pedagogies of planning and policy practices.

27400814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400814.value: The proposed research traces the history of modernist planning and speculative housing practices in colonial Hong Kong between 1912 and 1939. It aims to explore three central but under-examined aspects of colonial urban development in the period: the advent of modernist planning practices that were closely entwined with early segregation policies in Hong Kong and other British colonies; the adaptation of official narratives by local developers in large-scale housing projects; and the emergence of a distinct urban milieu in which a growing number of the propertied class sought to claim a stake in the evolving colonial society amidst ongoing modernization and economic growth. Although the focus of this research is on Hong Kong, it adopts a transnational approach in its analysis, attending particularly to the exchange of new knowledge in planning, housing and urban reform across national boundaries during the interwar years. The research consists of three main parts. It will begin by historicizing Hong Kong’s early segregation policies and contextualizing them within those of other British colonies. This includes examining the adaptation of the garden city concept in planning practices and the widespread debate over its role in colonial urban management. The second part will trace the development of three speculative housing projects initiated between 1912 and mid-1930s; Kowloon Bay, which was conceived as an exclusive residential district for the Chinese middle class; Kowloon Tong, which was originally proposed as a Portuguese enclave but was later opened up to Chinese investors; and Kadoorie Estate, the only surviving early “garden suburb” that retained its original form and purpose. The final section will examine competing narratives of development by different constituencies. These include colonial-era opinion pieces in local newspapers and magazines, through which writers of different social positions expressed their views on issues of housing and modernization. The ultimate goal of this project is to identify the interwar years as a significant historical moment in which a particular mode of speculative development and urban “governmentality” became consolidated in Hong Kong. A careful study of the transnational flow of knowledge and its uneven translation into specific projects will offer critical insights on how conceptions of race, class and property ownership became key elements in the shaping of the urban milieu and emergent sense of identity. It will also show how discourses and policies established in the colonial past have remained powerful frameworks for urban change in the post-colonial present. Does teacher-supported group work effect greater academic and attitudinal change in science than self-directed group work?
In what respects is peer interaction influenced by teacher participation in small group discussions?

27400914.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27400914.value: Investigations into the concept of cooperation in the classroom and the ideology behind collaborative group work began in the late 20th century, primarily in social psychological research. Although general conclusions have been drawn about the positive implications of peer collaboration in Western classrooms (e.g. Blatchford, Baines, Rubie-Davies, Bassett, & Chowne, 2006; Johnson & Johnson, 1985, 1999), little attention has been paid to the pedagogical differences between group work and traditional whole-class teaching in Hong Kong (Education Bureau, 2008; Galton & Pell, 2010). To fill this research gap, the proposed study will develop a teaching intervention in the context of the Hong Kong secondary science curriculum to investigate students’ joint construction of conceptual knowledge through a combination of collaborative group work strategies. Building upon Piaget’s (1932) theory of constructivism with regard to children’s cognitive development, the proposed intervention will take the form of a series of 16 lessons that contextualise a set of science questions through group work activities, including peer-critiquing tasks and debates, in the junior secondary integrated science curriculum. It will thus enable teachers to play a crucial role in encouraging their students to evaluate alternative conceptions and common-sense beliefs about science. At the same time, it will also allow students to establish a set of regulations for expressing their opinions during collaborative tasks, thereby facilitating the development of peer interaction. In its entirety, the intervention will place emphasis both on enhancing student engagement, particularly in relation to the co-construction of conceptual knowledge, and the importance of teacher guidance. Methodologically, the proposed study will be guided by a conceptual framework that is underpinned by the work of Vygotsky (1978) and divided into three inter-related domains: ‘whole-class teaching’, ‘self-directed student group work’ and ‘teacher-supported group work’. Informed by a quasi-experimental research design, the study will adopt a mixed-methods approach to examine the relationship between different types of pedagogy and students’ academic and attitudinal changes in science learning. Samples of students’ written responses, showing how they work collaboratively to draw inferences or produce alternative arguments in science discourse, will be collected through tasks involving predictions of experimental outcomes. After these data are collected, semi-structured interviews will be conducted to investigate how peer collaboration can be used to help students to overcome scientific misconceptions. The results of the proposed study have potential implications for other contexts in which social interaction supports cognitive development in science. 摘要 關於合作學習和小組協作概念的研究始於二十世紀後期，主要為社會心理學研究。雖然它們的正面影響在西方教育已被肯定（貝恩斯，布拉奇福德＆卡尼克，2003；約翰遜＆約翰遜，1985，1999），但香港在研究小組協作和傳統教學方面卻常被忽視（教育局，2008； 高爾頓＆佩爾，2010）。為填補這方面的知識，本計劃以小組協作的策略教授香港初中科學科，以窺探學生共建知識的過程。 建基於皮亞傑（1932）在兒童認知發展的建構主義上，本研究以一連十六課，在初中綜合科學課程中，將一系列的科學問題置入分組活動，包括朋輩互評及辯論，讓教師在鼓勵學生評價錯誤概念和科學常識中飾演不可或缺的角色。同時，學生亦能在協作活動中發展規範去表達他們的意見，從而促使朋輩交流。總括來說，這個教學研究不但令學生在共建知識中更投入，也強調教師指導的重要性。 這個研究的結構依靠維谷斯基（1978)的概念，分成三個相關的領域：「傳統教學」、「學生自主小組學習」和「教師支援小組學習」。本研究採用準實驗性研究設計，以混合研究方法去檢視不同的教育學對學生學術成績及態度轉變的關係。在這研究中，學生的書面回應會被收集，樣本能顯示他們合作推論或提出不同論據的過程。半結構式訪問探討朋輩合作如何能幫助學生消除科學的誤解。總體來說，研究結果對互動學習幫助科學認知發展有潛在的影響。

27400914.label: Realisation of objectives
27400914.value: Objective 1 [i.e. How does collaborative group work affect student learning in junior secondary science in Hong Kong?]: As noted in the mid-term report, this objective had been met by the data collection of the current research project through pre- and post-diagnostic tests, written responses to adapted TIMSS questions and audio-recordings of group discussions and individual presentations. The results indicate that group work incorporating effective strategies distinguishes itself from self-directed group work in the case of Hong Kong students’ science learning. . The better learning results of the group work students can be ascribed to the effective group strategies that were applied exclusively to that group in the current project. Currently, the research findings have led to two conference papers presented in the ‘NARST 2015’ and ‘BERA Annual Conference 2015’ and a journal publication in the ‘International Journal of Science Education’. Objective 2 [i.e. Does teacher-supported group work effect greater academic and attitudinal change in science than self-directed group work?]: This objective is also fully achieved. To meet this objective, teacher trainings had been conducted in the project and the research findings suggest that teacher-supported group work had greater effects than self-directed group work on both students’ academic and attitudinal performances. In particular, the teaching intervention in the current project that compared students’ learning results under three different pedagogies, i.e. conventional whole-class teaching, self-directed group work, and group work with teacher support, found the latter approach to exert the most positive effects on students’ motivation, expressiveness and problem-solving ability in science. Data analysis related to this objective has been completed, contributing to a completed manuscript which is currently under major revisions (‘International Journal of Science and Mathematics Education’) and a conference paper presented in ‘The International Academic Research Conference’ at the University of London. Objective 3 [i.e. In what respects is peer interaction influenced by teacher participation in small group discussions?]: This objective was fully completed by the end of the project. To achieve the objective, the current project investigated the audio-recordings of group discussions in small-group activities. The findings suggest that effective group work strategies, namely, pre-class team-building amongst students, emphasis on teachers’ role as facilitators and classroom-contextualised tasks, contribute to greater student accomplishment and satisfaction with shared cognitive activities. It is thus recommended that more resources be allocated to introducing these strategies in secondary science education to increase Hong Kong students’ engagement in group-based interactions rather than sustaining the tradition of teacher-centred, examination-driven lessons. Analyses of the above results have led to a draft manuscript under publication consideration and one conference paper presented in the ‘2016 International Symposium on Education and Psychology’.

27400914.label: Major findings and research outcome
27400914.value: With regard to the research findings and outcome, we report: 1. The teachers in the current project concentrated on their facilitator role in group activities by engaging with the students only to keep them on the right track and to encourage interactions. Such minimal intervention enables students to be the primary and active participants in constructing shared cognition, a process considered to be essential for effective group learning (Barron, 2003; Hatano & Inagaki, 1991; Roschelle, 1992). In the current study, the students with teacher guidance proved more capable of considering multiple perspectives, which rendered richer argumentation and evoked greater creativity (Van den Bossche, Gijselaers, Segers, & Kirschner, 2006), as later confirmed by their teachers in the interviews. Moreover, the classroom practices in the group with teacher support were contextualised for group tasks, specifically the provision of briefing and debriefing sessions. These short preparations and evaluations before and after classroom undertakings increased the students’ sense of shared commitment in problem-solving (Barron, 2000, Van den Bossche et al., 2006) during the process of mutual cognition, thereby rendering them more sensitive to recognising scientific knowledge and more evidence-oriented in forming their arguments while answering the TIMSS questions. 2. By acquiring communication skills and building mutual trust and respect before working in teams, the group with teacher guidance established “team psychological safety” (Edmondson, 1999), which reduced their concerns about “being seen as incompetent” (p. 355) and assured them that speaking up would be valued rather than cause embarrassment. Such preparation also explains why the students were more illustrative when attempting the adapted TIMSS questions, and more upfront in seeking clarification from others in the audiotaped group discussions. 3. Both the students and teachers were receptive to the motivating learning atmosphere and outcomes brought about by group work. Students from the experimental groups found that cooperative learning assisted them not only in comprehending scientific concepts, but also in overcoming some of the typical barriers to leaning in the local educational environment, such as the prevalence of passive rote learning. The students with teacher support in group work, in particular, felt more at ease about proposing and sharing their ideas after relational training. This attitudinal change, together with evidenced increase in students’ conceptual knowledge, reassures that the group work design is applicable in Hong Kong schools and more beneficial to students than the customary whole-class teaching approach that has gone unquestioned for decades.

27400914.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27400914.value: Potential further development of the research is taking place in a number of confirmed and proposed activities. 1) A new GRF project, based on the results of the current study, was submitted to the RGC in the title of ‘Drawing and talking science with the aid of collaborative mind mapping in Hong Kong primary schools’. The corresponding ethical approval has been obtained and a pilot study has already been implemented in a few local schools in Hong Kong. 2) Future writing and further research related to the teachers’ role in group work are expected, which will explore the theoretical as well as the applied implications in effective group work under teacher guidance. Moreover, the concept of teachers’ pedagogic efficacy will also be scrutinized in future research projects.

27400914.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27400914.value: The research project was motivated by the negative relationship between Hong Kong students’ outstanding performance and declining interest in secondary science subjects. A teaching intervention that compared local students’ learning results under three different pedagogies, i.e. conventional whole-class teaching, self-directed group work, and group work with teacher support, found the latter approach to exert the most positive effects on students’ motivation and academic performances in science. Analyses of the pre- and post-diagnostic assessments, audio-taped discussions and interviews with the student and teacher participants revealed that group work with effective strategies not only raised test scores, but also enhanced students’ science learning experience. The findings suggest that effective group learning strategies and teacher support in group work are contributory factors to superior student accomplishments and higher satisfaction levels accruing from shared cognitive activities.
