28402014.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28402014.value: 網絡欺凌是一個重要的公共健康議題及研究項目。根據不少西方國家的研究顯示，網絡欺凌的受害者可能出現一系列負面心理問題，例如抑鬱、憤怒、憂傷、自殺傾向、孤單等。 現有的文獻大都集中於揭示網絡欺凌的成因、其負面影響及比較網絡欺凌跟傳統學校欺凌的分別，卻忽略了網上旁觀者對網絡欺凌帶來的影響。根據以往對傳統學校欺凌的認知，旁觀者的反應可分為三種：支持欺凌、反對欺凌及置身事外。他們的反應足以增加或減少傳統學校欺凌的發生。由於網絡欺凌比傳統學校欺凌牽涉更多旁觀者，按此推論，網上旁觀者於網絡欺凌中扮演的角色尤為重要。然而我們對此卻所知甚少。雖然西方國家已有不少與網絡欺凌相關的研究，但以香港青少年作為研究對象的文獻卻相當缺乏。因此，本研究將探討網絡欺凌與香港青少年的關係。 本研究將分為三個部份。 第一部份將對一些經常上網、曾參與網絡欺凌的青少年進行訪談，以了解他們欺凌別人的動機及作為網絡欺凌旁觀者的心態。第二部份將對一批青少年作出縱貫研究。透過問卷調查，深入探討網絡欺凌的成因、網絡欺凌旁觀者的想法及網絡欺凌受害者的心理狀態。第三部份將虛擬一些網絡欺凌的處境，並測試青少年對網絡欺凌的取態及看法。 本研究將以嶄新的角度及多種研究方法去了解網絡欺凌者、網絡欺凌受害者及網上旁觀者的社會心理發展狀況。研究成果有望能於將來用以制定預防或應付網絡欺凌的方法或教育方案，從而減低網絡欺凌對香港青少年所帶來的影。

28402014.label: Realisation of objectives
28402014.value: The four objectives for this project were satisfactorily achieved. To address objectives one to three, interviews were conducted to examine participants’ beliefs and understanding of cyberbullying. These data informed the design of the questionnaires and experiments. A longitudinal study was conducted with over 1000 secondary school and college students from seven local secondary schools and five universities who completed two waves of data collection (7-months apart). To address objective four, an experiment tested how cyber-bystanders’ responses affected beliefs about helping cyber-victims. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of an anti-cyberbullying intervention was tested. This effort fulfilled the intended long term, overall impact of the project: to increase students’ awareness of cyberbullying and changing their attitudes toward it. For objective #1, the relations among cyberbullying, cyber-victimization, conventional school bullying and victimization were examined. The results showed that bullying and victimization were strongly correlated in both the conventional and online contexts. Therefore, in both contexts, students who experienced bullying were also likely to experience victimization. Bullying and victimization behavior across the two contexts also overlapped moderately. To examine age differences, participants were then divided into three groups (1. lower secondary school, Form 1 to 3, i.e., Grade 7 to 9; 2. upper secondary school (Form 4 to 6, i.e., Grade 10-12); and 3. college students). Bullying and victimization in conventional and online contexts were the most strongly associated among the college students compared to the other two age groups. Similarly, the four types of bullying and victimization in conventional and online contexts were the most strongly intercorrelated among the college student group, followed by upper secondary school and lower secondary school students. Because the association between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying among college students was particularly high (r > .80). This pattern was repeated in a separate dataset with than 300 college students. The results showed that cyber-victimization explained the variance in cyberbullying among college students (See Part C). For objectives #2 & 3, the longitudinal dataset provided the opportunity to examine stability of cyberbullying, cyber-victimization and online bystanders’ behavior over time and the psychological constructs that may predict these behaviors. In addition, a separate dataset was collected to investigate how morality and personal values were related to adolescents’ cyberbullying. By subtracting Time 1 involvement from Time 2, about 30% of secondary school and 40% college students showed no changes in their cyber-victimization and cyberbullying behavior over time. However, about 12% of the secondary school and 8%of the college students showed a substantial increase in cyber-victimization over time whereas, about 6% of both secondary school and college students had a substantial increase in cyberbullying over time. The increment in both cyber-victimization and cyberbullying peaked with early adolescents under 13 years old (i.e., lower secondary school). This finding implies that schools could consider educating adolescents in upper primary or lower secondary school settings to prevent cyberbullying or cyber-victimization. Online bystanders could either reinforce cyber-bullies by leaving comments online that encourage or praise the cyber-bullies or defend the cyber-victims by leaving comments that asked others to stop attacking the cyber-victims. By subtracting Time 1 cyber-bystander behaviors from Time 2, our longitudinal data showed that more than half of secondary school and college students demonstrated no changes in reinforcing cyber-bullies’ behavior over time, while 5% of secondary school and 6% of college students showed a substantial increase in reinforcing cyber-bullies’ behavior; about one-third of secondary and college students showed no changes in defending cyber-victims over time, while about 6% of secondary school and 10% of college students had a significant increase in defending cyber-victims behavior over time. Generally, there was a slight, but insignificant decline in both reinforcing cyber-bullies or defending cyber-victims behavior over time, although early adolescents (12 years old; i.e., mostly Form 1 students) showed slight increase in reinforcing cyber-bullies behavior over time; while college students (18 years old; mostly freshmen) demonstrated slight increase in defending cyber-victims behavior over time. Below is a summary of the different psychological constructs that are related to cyberbullying, cyber-victimization, and online bystanders’ behavior. First, we examined how adolescents’ personal values that include cognitive representations of ideals, such as security and justice, and their moral disengagement that reflects their justification of transgression as something morally acceptable, were predictive of cyberbullying behavior. In a separate dataset, we found that individuals’ self-transcendence was negatively associated with cyberbullying, whereas moral disengagement positively explained cyberbullying, and moral disengagement mediated the relation between self-transcendence and cyberbullying (See Part C). In terms of predictors of cyberbullying over time, in our longitudinal dataset, we also found that awareness of cyberbullying; and positive attitudes towards cyberbullying (i.e. endorsing cyberbullying) negatively and positively predicted cyberbullying, respectively. Based on these results, a short intervention study was designed (see Part C). Results showed that participants who received the intervention experienced an increase in their awareness and had more negative attitudes toward cyberbullying and an increased awareness that cyberbullying is unacceptable behavior, than did the control group. The results also showed that cyber-victimization negatively predicted adolescents’ self-esteem over time and those who were high in conventional victimization and depression were more likely to experience cyber-victimization over time. Finally, Adolescents’ positive attitudes towards cyberbullying positively predicted reinforcing cyber-bullies behavior over time, and there was a trend that social competence positively predicted defending cyber-victims behavior over time. To address Objective #4, an experiment was conducted (see Part C). We set up a hypothetical simulated social networking site to test how cyber-bystanders’ responses might affect participants’ perceived control and normative beliefs. A 4 cyberbully-victim group (pure cyberbullies, non-involved, pure cyberbullied victims, and cyberbullied-victims) X 2 condition (reinforcing cyber-bullies vs. defending cyber-victims) experimental design was employed. 203 Hong Kong Chinese secondary school and university students were randomly assigned into one of two conditions. Results showed that participants’ involvement in cyberbullying was significantly related to their control beliefs about bully and victim assisting behaviors, while exposure to the two offend vs. defend comments conditions was related to both their control and normative beliefs. In general, the defend condition promoted higher control beliefs to help the victims and promoted higher normative beliefs to help the victims. Regardless of their past involvement in cyberbullying and exposure to offend vs. defend conditions, both cyber-bullies and cyber-victims were more inclined to demonstrate normative beliefs to help victims than to assist bullies. These results have implications for examining environmental influences in predicting bystander behaviors in cyberbullying contexts, and for creating a positive environment to motivate adolescents to become “upstanders” in educational programs to combat cyberbullying.

28402014.label: Major findings and research outcome
28402014.value: This project yielded a number of important findings, leading to several journal publications and conference papers. Major findings and research outcomes are summarized below. First, we found that cyber-victimization positively explained cyberbullying, while friendship closeness and security moderated the relation between cyberbullying victimization and perpetration for female students. Specifically, friendship closeness buffered the relation between cyberbullying victimization and perpetration while friendship security enhanced the relation. (*Leung, Wong, & Farver, 2017, see Part C, section 8). We found that self transcendence, or the motivation to promote the well-being of others negatively explained cyberbullying; while moral disengagement and cognitions that justify transgression as something morally acceptable, positively explained cyberbullying. Moral disengagement also partially mediated the relation between self-transcendence and cyberbullying. (*Leung et al., submitted, see Part C, section 8; *Leung & Lo, 2018, see Part C, section 9). In addition, empathy predicted cyberbullying, and positive attitudes toward cyberbullying positively explained cyberbullying. Finally, the experience of merely witnessing cyberbullying positively explained cyberbullying. (*Leung, 2018, see Part C, section 9). Second, we found that cyber-victimization positively predicted depression among both college and secondary school student samples (*Leung, 2016, 2017, See Part C, section 9). Moreover, merely witnessing cyberbullying and self -esteem positively explained depression (*Leung, 2017, see Part C, section 9). Third, we designed an intervention to change students’ attitudes about cyberbullying behavior and increase their awareness of cyberbullying. Participants were assigned to an experimental or control group. The experimental group participated in a 1-hour intervention where they were presented with a simulated Facebook page showing the helpless feelings of cyber-victims, they watched video clips of the consequences of cyberbullying, and they engaged in small group discussions and a self-reflection writing task. Results showed that participants who received the intervention experienced an increase in their awareness and had more negative attitudes toward cyberbullying (i.e., the perception that cyberbullying is unacceptable behavior) than did the control group. In addition, those who reported being highly engaged in the intervention maintained the positive effects at the 8-week follow-up. (*Leung, Fung, & Farver, 2017, see Part C, section 8). Finally, we developed a hypothetical simulated social networking site. Results showed that participants’ perceived control and normative beliefs about assisting the victims were affected by the simulated cyber-bystanders’ comments that reinforced cyber-bullies or defended cyber-victims, and their past involvement as cyber-bullies/victims. (*Leung, Wong, & Farver, 2018, see Part C, section 8).

28402014.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28402014.value: Findings and outcomes of this project provide the basis to develop further research on cyberbullying. Future studies and educational programmes should further investigate the relations among self-transcendence, empathy, awareness of cyberbullying, attitudes towards cyberbullying and cyberbullying to prevent cyberbullying. This project found that participants’ perceived control and normative beliefs were influenced by the simulated cyber-bystanders’ comments in the experimental setting, and attitudes towards cyberbullying predicted the likelihood of reinforcing cyber-bullies behavior over time. These results support the importance of further investigating cyber-bystanders. Studies in conventional bullying settings show that individuals who witness bullying or are “bystanders” to these situations, can play crucial roles in accelerating or reducing bullying by intervening in a negative (joining the bully) or positive (acting to stop the event) way. Relatively little is known about the bystander phenomenon in an online context, and how to promote helping behavior among cyber-bystanders. Building on the effective 1-hour short intervention programme, future research can investigate how a short intervention can be effective to influence bystanders’ inclination to intervene. Some of these research ideas were developed into grant proposals, and a GRF project on cyber-bystanders’ helping behavior was funded in the 2017-18 exercise.

28402014.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28402014.value: Cyberbullying is a serious concern among internet users worldwide. Adolescents’ experiences of cyber-victimization is associated with negative psychological outcomes that include depression and low self-esteem. Yet, large scale studies on cyberbullying based on Hong Kong Chinese students are currently scarce. This project examined cyberbullying, cyber-victimization, and cyber-bystander behaviour among Hong Kong secondary and college students using interviews, questionnaires, and an experimental design. The results of this project showed that cyber-victimization was associated with individuals’ negative psychological adjustment and that past experiences of cyber-victimization, individuals’ self-transcendence and moral disengagement also explained their likelihood of cyberbullying their peers, and comments made by cyber-bystanders who witnessed bullying behavior affected students’ beliefs about their likelihood of helping the cyber-victims. The results enrich our understanding of cyberbullying behavior among Hong Kong Chinese students and can inform future educational and intervention programmes for anti-cyberbullying education. Based on findings of this project, promoting self-transcendence, empathy, awareness of cyberbullying, and attitudes towards cyberbullying should be emphasized among youth in school settings. Moreover, the project highlights the importance of examining the important role of cyber-bystanders can play in promoting reducing and ultimately preventing cyberbullying.

28402114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28402114.value: 過去幾年內地地方政府大力推進各項金融開放措施。在地方當局及官員的支持下，各地主要城市都先後成立了金融服務辦公室。除了促進當地金融發展及為所在的金融機構爭取更大的市場利益外，他們亦主動提出種種國家金融開放的舉措。近年來廣受關注的例子包括在深圳為中小型企業及高新科技企業專門成立的中小板及創業板、在北京及各地為非上市公司股份交易而設的新三板，以及天津在濱海新區展開的金融創新實驗。自二千年起，上海亦銳意成為中國的國際金融中心，先後提出了成立國際版、自由貿易區及發展全國衍生工具交易市場等種種建議。 然而，地方政府的角色及策略仍未被中國研究及國際政治經濟學的專家有系統地探討。前者往往着眼於地方及中央政府在財政，稅收以及貿易投資開放等議題上的博弈；後者則從國家層面上出發，忽視了對了解中國政治經濟，及國家與全球資本市場融合接軌至為重要的地方政治互動。 因此這研究項目主要有兩大目標。首先透過全面有系統地對國內地方政府的金融開放政策倡議及措施進行梳理及分類，再對相關策略及政策制定過程，決策的種種因素進行深入分析及探討。通過研究地方政府的行為及其與金融業界及中央各部委在政策過程中的互動，是次研究將對了解中國政治經濟，特別是對外經濟金融開放的走向，提出新的分析角度；亦為香港金融業界及政府政策制定提供相關的參考依據據及建議。

28402114.label: Realisation of objectives
28402114.value: All objectives have been realized. To attain Objective 1, the PI and Research Assistant had conducted an exhaustive search of publicly available documentary sources in Chinese and English that would illuminate the extent of local states’ activism and their initiatives in pursing financial opening. A major finding of the research activity is that while there have been many bottom-up initiatives throughout China, only a handful of local states matter and have successfully advanced their initiatives into the national policymaking process. These, perhaps unsurprisingly, include Shanghai, Hong Kong as well as minor financial hubs like Shenzhen and Tianjin. Importance of these few financial hubs provides a more focused empirical scope and focus essential to carrying out research tasks associated with other project objectives. In relation to Objective 2,the PI has teased out analytically the motivations of local authorities in their financial opening pursuits. Whereas the literature has rightly pointed to the importance of material and political concerns to local authorities, this project distinguishes two determinants-- distributional implications and policy risks-- that influence the local states’ preference toward particular liberalizing pursuits. In connection with Objective 3, these two factors are also found to condition the preference of financial industry interests and central bureaucratic actors, shaping their alignments as pro-opening and dissenting parties as liberalizing agendas enter the policymaking process. For Objectives 3 and 4, the PI has carried out in-depth comparative analyses of several liberalizing episodes China has embarked on since the 2000s, including the evolution of outbound equity investment regime, attempts to internationalize domestic equity market by way of listing of foreign firms, and development of offshore renminbi center in Hong Kong critical to renminbi internationalization. The PI has theorized a coalition politics model to understand the changing trajectory underlying these three financial opening episodes (sometimes showing policy stasis and reversal from opening, for example) and assess how local authorities have interacted with financial industry and bureaucratic constituents. Empirical analyses and the framework are published in a book (Routledge 2018) that synthesizes the insights of various streams of literature on China’s decision making and political economy, and were presented in several international conferences attended by China specialists, economists, and political economy researchers. Last and in relation to Hong Kong’s positioning in and policy responses to China’s financial opening, the PI has developed a Hong Kong-focused journal manuscript toward the project’s concluding phase (accepted by Asian Survey in 2018) and disseminated the analysis and policy recommendations to audiences in Hong Kong SAR 20th anniversary symposium at Stanford University, UC Berkeley and UC Angeles in November 2017 that were well-attended by local research communities, Chinese and Hong Kong government representatives and general public. The PI also intends to summarize and translate part of the monograph to Chinese for publications in local media outlets in Hong Kong.

28402114.label: Major findings and research outcome
28402114.value: The project has generated important findings that refine the literature of China’s and international political economy regarding the agency and roles of subnational authorities in China’s financial opening. Foremost, the project demonstrates the relevance of local governments of financial centers (including onshore and offshore hubs) in the course f capital market opening. Motivated by both material concerns such as local competitiveness vis-a-viz their local peers and political agendas to boost the locality’s political economic standings, local authorities have played parts in agenda formation, deliberation and implementation of liberalizing initiatives. To account for the interplays between local authorities with financial industry interests and bureaucratic agencies of the central government, the project advances a coalition politics model to analyze and evaluate the strategies of these policy actors, and conceives financial opening as a process driven the interplays by the pro-opening coalitions and dissenting parties. Whereas local authorities are instrumental to advance the liberalizing agendas they desire, more than often they have acted in concert with financiers (such as banks, securities brokerages and bourses) and pro-opening central government agencies as coalitions. The local and financial industry constituents have employed several strategies in advancing their agendas: shaping Beijing’s policy agendas and framing liberalizing initiatives in ways that would appeal to and obtain support from bureaucratic entities during policy formation and deliberation, as well as seeking political support from top decision elites by way of their political connections. The pro-opening coalition have also engaged in political maneuvering that would allay resistance to its liberalizing pursuits, through for example, making concession with dissenting parties over implementation specifics that would help maintain political and technical consensus during policy deliberation and implementation. This, however, does not always succeed. Dissenting parties deterred by adverse distributional and policy risk implications underlying the opening initiatives might turn down the concessionary offers, resulting in policy trends other than opening. Although these findings inevitably present a more complex picture of how and why China’s financial opening unfolds, they enrich the understanding of the political mechanisms of China’s capital de-control and the associated roles of public authorities (at local and central levels) in the process, and will be important to the research and policymaking communities in Hong Kong and beyond in fathoming China’s policy tendencies and outlook. The general public and investors would also benefit from realizing the importance of political drivers in shaping the liberalizing trajectories of China.

28402114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28402114.value: In addition to understanding how local authorities have played part in driving China’s financial opening, this project has shed light on the diversity of political interests in the underlying policymaking process. Notably it reveals the rising but oft-underappreciated importance of non-bank financial institutions (e.g. securities firms, stock exchanges) in the mainland financial system, as well as the multiplicity of bureaucratic interests within the central financial bureaucracy. These findings have inspired me to pursue two other projects with respective focuses on political strategies employed by China’s central bank in pursuing renminbi internationalization, and the interplays among central-level regulators in shaping the adoption of global rules in the post-subprime crisis context. These two smaller projects have matured and developed into papers for presentation in international conferences (e.g. International Studies Association Annual Convention), and for peer reviews in refereed journal outlets since 2017. The PI may also develop collaborative projects with other international political economy specialists investigating in more details the political trajectories of China’s financial opening (and the use of liberalizing initiatives for nationalist ends) in the future.

28402114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28402114.value: As China presses on financial reforms and flexes its financial power abroad, understanding the domestic political dynamics of financial opening becomes an imperative to both market practitioners and policymakers offshore. Existing studies by political scientists and China specialists, however, have mostly concentrated on central-level policy actors, and do not sufficiently consider the importance of local authorities of China’s financial centers in the course of China’s financial opening. Through in-depth comparative case studies of several liberalizing episodes Beijing has pursued since the mid-2000s, this study opens the domestic “black box” by illuminating how local governments have been instrumental to the making of capital markets liberalization. The local authorities have shaped the central policymaking agendas, allied with financial industry interests and central bureaucratic actors, and engaged in political bargaining. These political maneuvering has promoted and helped catalyze the easing of outbound equity investment regime for mainland investors, and development of the world’s first offshore renminbi center in Hong Kong in the last decade. The study also sheds lights on the indispensable position of Hong Kong as an offshore financial hub pivotal to China’s pursuit of financial globalization by way of the city’s market openness and political leverage to onshore policy actors.

28402214.value: To great extent that the project objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, it was achieved in the first year with help of RA. A lot of related reference materials and catalogs had been produced including "Critical Writings on The Story of Shrimp-ball in 1940s", "Lists of Critical Writings of Dialect Literature in DLM" and "Chronicle of Works of Huang Gu-liu". There are 2 papers produced: "Confrontation of Spoken and Written Languages: A Critical Account of Dialect Literature Movement in Post-war Hong Kong" and "In Context of Post-war Hong Kong: Dialect Literature Movement and Production of The Story of Shrimp-ball". They realize the other 3 objectives. The first paper evaluates the contributions of DLM in both theories and literary works in macroscopic perspective. This realize the second objective. The paper investigate DLM in an innovative perspective: interaction and struggle between spoken and written languages. Starting from late Qing period, unification of spoken (yan) and written (wen) languages has been the goal of intellectuals. In 1920s, vernacular of northern population was developed as Bei Hua Wen, actually can be regarded as a writing system. However, this modern written Chinese was soon challenged by leftists. They claimed that Bei Hua Wen was product by elite and neglected vocal languages of mass public. In the background of Sino-Japanese war and civil war, dialects became more and more important. In late 1940s, there was another critical stage of modern China. Leftists fled to Hong Kong and initiate Dialect Literature Movement (DLM). By inheriting theories and goal of revolutionary literature in 1930s, they explored how dialects in Southern China, mainly Cantonese, can become resources in the process of “popularization in arts and literature”. Although all leftists target at “popularization in arts and literature”, their views regarding how to use dialects are very different. According to their arguments, they can be divided into two groups: The compromised leftists regarded dialects as supplementary elements in creative works while the radical leftists advocated purely usage of dialects for sake of illiterate mass. By investigating three representative writers: Fu Gong-wang, Huang Gu-liu and Chen Can-yun, we can discover that how political beliefs and cultural background affects their choices in writing. It is clear that tension between spoken and written languages is still unneglectable in late 1940s. The imagination and experience in DLM is valuable resources for us to develop written forms of dialects. On the other hand, equilibrium of both form of languages is prerequisite in producing written styles of literary works. Taking the novel "The Story of Shrimp-ball" as a case study, the second paper review DLM in microscopic vision. This paper argues that the representative novel of the movement demonstrated uniqueness of Hong Kong and tension between revolution and entertainment among leftists writers and editors. Before the formal start of civil war, struggle between Kuomintang and Communist Party was began in Hong Kong when leftists came to the city for preparation of ideological propaganda. In 1947, more leftist fled to Hong Kong and initiate a series of cultural and literary activities. Dialect Literature Movement (DLM) was the most representative one. The involved leftists aimed at continuing “Popularization of Arts and Literature” in Hong Kong. Although workers and farmers in Guangdong were their imaginary readers and audience, they could not neglect local citizens who were their actual readers and audience. In order to maintain survival of cultural business and to explore writing resource, leftist editors and writers had to consider the need of citizens whose interests were very different from general mass in rural mainland. The Story of Shrimp-ball, the famous novel written by Huang Gu-liu, was regarded as most successful works produced in DLM. However, this paper points out that the writing strategy and production process of the novel demonstrated server tension between revolution and entertainment. From the viewpoints of orthodoxic leftists, the plot of The Story of Shrimp-ball is too dramatic and could not reach the goal of Popularization. The unique context of commercial urban Hong Kong, although provided freedom for leftists in a certain extent, but also constrained their considerations which put themselves into inevitable dilemma. For objective 4, both papers mentioned above discuss the role of DLM in context of revolutionary literature: how leftists inherited theories and principles from important leftist thinkers and writers, how they developed such theories and principles in unique context of Hong Kong, how aesthetic of revolutionary literature clashed with local industry of popular literature, what are inspirations and shortcomings of theories and works of DLM as leftist literature movement, etc. The PI is terribly sorry that the 2 papers mentioned above have just finished written before submission of final report. This is because of unexpected difficulty in finding most suitable perspectives of analysis and explanation. It was not until late June in 2017, when it was the end of research period, PI was satisfied with her explanation framework of DLM. In addition, there were many other research duties that have been conducted by PI including application of other research funding in 2016. The PI also organized a academic workshop which brought critical benefit for the research project in 2017. Despite the difficulties, both papers are under review by academic journals and hopefully will be revised and published in near future. The PI will inform RGC as soon as possible through university RDO.

28402214.label: Major findings and research outcome
28402214.value: Two papers are produced: "Confrontation of Spoken and Written Languages: A Critical Account of Dialect Literature Movement in Post-war Hong Kong" and "In Context of Post-war Hong Kong: Dialect Literature Movement and Production of The Story of Shrimp-ball". The major findings are as follow: 1. The leftists found themselves in inevitable dilemma when they try to balance revolution and entertainment. The unique context of colonial and commercial urban Hong Kong provided freedom for leftists in a certain extent but also constrained their strategies. 2. According to their views in dialect literature, leftists can be divided into 2 groups: compromised leftists regarded dialects as supplementary elements in creative works while the radical leftists advocated purely usage of dialects for sake of illiterate mass. 3. After nearly 20 years of modern Chinese writing (Bei Hua Wen) was establishment as common writing system, tension between spoken (yan) and written (wen) languages is still very strong in late 1940s. Unification of both forms of languages remains a difficult task in modern China. The imagination and experience in DLM is valuable resources for us to develop written forms of dialects. On the other hand, equilibrium of both form of languages is prerequisite in producing written styles of literary works. 4. Different from consensus in academia, leftists in DLM did not neglect Hong Kong and its citizens - the reality they confronted. In the contrary, it was common for them to discuss how to meet interests of local citizens and what is the relationship of city life and revolutionary literature production. 5. Different from consensus in academia, "The Story of Shrimp-ball" is representative as literary production in DLM not because of using Cantonese, but demonstrates tension between revolution and entertainment. The novel was popular among young citizens in 1940s, however, the plot is too dramatic and could not reach the goal of Popularization in the viewpoints of orthodoxic leftists.

28402214.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28402214.value: The analysis framework, "interaction between spoken and written languages", developed in this research project will become references for other related research in future. This framework helps to put research of "written Cantonese" in extensive historical and cultural context. The PI is considering methodologies and content of her next monograph which will involve analysis framework and research outputs of the project. To serve this purpose, PI will investigate related research outputs regarding "spoken and written languages in modern China".

28402214.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28402214.value: The research points out that Hong Kong is unique in political, historical and cultural context. On the one hand, she provided relatively freedom to leftist who fled southwards in civil war and could initiate literature and cultural activities in the city. As a region in South China, Hong Kong inherited tradition of written Cantonese which stimulated imagination of leftists about dialect literature which had been advocated by their forerunners in mainland since 1930s. On the other hand, Hong Kong has already been a commercial city in post-war period. When leftists writers and editors tried to impose ideological propaganda and literature movement in Hong Kong, they had to consider interests of local citizens whose background was completely different from workers and farmers in rural mainland. The leftists found that they were in the dilemma between revolution and entertainment. They have to reconsider their literature theories and revise their writing strategies. It is obvious that Hong Kong is not only a neutral place that receive political struggle passively, she interacted with the era with her uniqueness.

28402814.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28402814.value: One of the most difficult tasks facing policymakers today is how to embed meaningful changes in the technical core of schooling – learning and teaching. Schools are increasingly expected to orchestrate improvement efforts from within, rather than simply adopting pre-packaged change programs. School-based research is often promoted as a solution for schools that intend to initiate, construct and design improvement in line with their own contextual needs. The job of making this work falls squarely on shoulders of school leaders. For school-based research initiatives to work, leaders must take responsibility for promotion, coordination, resource acquisition and allocation, and teacher motivation and engagement. Little research has been conducted in this area in the Asia-Pacific Region. This study aims to build an in-depth understanding of the leadership strategies and practices associated with the successful promotion and implementation of school-based research in Shanghai. More specifically, the study aims to identify and analyze the key roles of school leaders in leading school-based research to improve student learning. The study is located in Shanghai because school-based research as a change strategy has been promoted and mobilized at a large scale, a scenario that is rarely seen in other settings. Six high schools will be selected to participate in the study. Data will be drawn from principals and vice principals, key mid-level leaders, teachers and students. Data will be collected to gain a better understanding of how school leaders perceive school-based research, what strategies they adopt to engage teachers in research projects, how they embed research findings in school practices and how teachers and students perceive and enact the research process and outcomes. This study will contribute to the sparse knowledge base in these two areas: strategies and practices for promoting school-based research, and school leadership in China. The research findings will have substantial implications for schools around the world, and for Hong Kong in particular. 如何將變革切實落實到學校教育的最核心 – 學與教的這個層面，歷來是各國的政策制定者最感棘手的難題之一。近年來的政策取向是鼓勵學校量身定制自己的改進方案，而不是一味地從外面照搬現成的變革措施。基於學校的需求設計、制定和規劃改進方案，通常要借助的手段之一是校本研究。引領和實施校本研究的工作通常又落在學校領導者的肩上。校本研究若要在一間學校順利實施，需要學校領導大量的溝通、協調、爭取及分配資源，以及用多種方式激勵教師的參與。然而，有關校本研究在東亞地區的開展鮮有相關的研究。 這項研究聚焦於中國上海，旨在探討在推廣和實施校本科研方面上海的成功經驗及具體的領導措施。本研究的重點是瞭解學校領導在引領校本研究促進學生學習方面採取哪些措施以及擔任什麼角色。選擇上海主要是因為上海在推廣和實施校本研究方面的力度和廣度。在上海基本上每一所學校都有各種級別的校本研究課題，這一點在世界範圍來說非常的罕見。 研究將在六所上海的中學開展，在每一間學校訪談學校校長、副校長、相關的中層領導和教師。該研究將補充和充實至少兩個領域的知識基礎： 引領校本研究的策略與具體實踐，以及中國大陸的學校領導。在推進和開展校本科研方面,上海的成功經驗以及存在問題相信會對香港及國際其他地區有借鑒意義。

28402814.label: Realisation of objectives
28402814.value: The objectives have been achieved with the competition of these research activities: Objective 1: A series of literature reviews have been conducted to depict the landscapes of the state-of-condition of the school leadership in general and school leadership for promoting school-based learning in particular. These include the literature review of school leadership published both in English and in Chinese between 1998 and 2016 and the review of successful school leadership literature published in Chinese between 2000 and 2014. These reviews help to map out the knowledge base about school leadership in China and indicate the necessity for further empirical understandings of in-depth leadership practices of Chinese school leaders. Objective 2: On the basis of the literature reviews, the project has successfully collected empirical data from six high schools in Shanghai as planned. During the data collection stage, the researcher interviewed school principals, vice principals, key middle-level leaders (usually school research coordinators and subject leaders) and teachers of different development stages. The data helped to gain a better understanding of how school leaders perceived school-based research, the strategies they adopted to engage teachers in research projects and how they embedded their research findings in school practices. Objective 3: The study identified some common strategies adopted by school leaders. For example, most school leaders tended to rely on expert teachers (backbone or gugan teachers) to play a leading role in school-based research. School leaders also tended to redesign the school evaluation policies to prioritize school-based research. However, the study also discovered some divergent patterns of leadership practices in different schools. For example, some school leaders integrated school-based research with the direction setting of the schools while in other schools, school-based research only involved individual rather than the majority of teachers. Thus the study identified some organizational and personal factors that shaped the way school leaders organized, coordinated and implemented school-based research and how leadership practices influenced the way teachers perceived and participated in school-based research. Objective 4: Some characteristics of the socio-political and educational system have been identified to both facilitate and inhibit the promotion and implementation of school-based research. For example, the local government invested a lot of resources encouraging schools to apply for different levels of research funds. The collectivist culture in China also facilitated the collaboration among teachers and the establishment of mentorship between experienced and younger teachers. Each coin has two sides. These facilitating factors can simultaneously inhabit the promotion and implementation of school-based research. For example, the number of research grants each school won tended to be a major criterion to assess the quality of school-based research. Schools thus used all means to push up the number while in some cases the large number of research projects did not necessarily lead to successful teacher learning and school improvement. Objective 5: The researcher has synthesized a set of propositions about successful leadership strategies in two levels. One is the common successful strategies adopted by school-level research coordinators, that is, the middle level leaders who are directly responsible for school-based research. Another is the general successful leadership practices enacted by Chinese principals. The syntheses at these two levels have been published in the form of journal papers and book chapters. Thus, the proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. In the process of completing the research project, new research areas have been identified and these research opportunities have led to a successful funded GRF project.

28402814.label: Major findings and research outcome
28402814.value: There was in general a thin knowledge base of school leadership in China. Few empirical studies have been conducted to provide updated understandings about how school leaders in China lead teacher learning and school improvement (Output #2 and #4). For example, one of the literature reviews the PI and Co-I conducted identified that between 1998 and 2016 altogether 87 journal papers and book chapters about school leadership in China were published in the English language (Output #4, the co-authored academic book). Thus, there is a need to explore the emerging leadership practices in the changing context of China. Leading school-based research is one of such practices. It is particularly important as there is no other site that promotes school-based research to the scale as observed in China. Over the decades, government in Shanghai has funded large numbers of school-initiated research projects. Many schools have created a new mid-level leadership post – Research Coordinator – to help provide support and incentives that foster research and its take-up in practice. We have compared and contrasted the role perception and enactment of Research Coordinators across our case schools (Output #3) and found that a Research Coordinator in the context of Shanghai seemed to have to take up three different types of roles – as an administrator, as a research expert and as a professional teacher. The study also identified some common conditions that helped to successfully promote and implement school-based research. The important conditions include a high degree of coherence between policy and implementation, a collaborative learning culture, a strong connection between research and instructional improvement, and school leadership enabling and supporting the learning of teachers and their own learning. Promoting school-based research was often seen by school leaders as an effective means to develop teachers and build a teacher learning culture. The study found that school leaders in Shanghai consciously made connections and conditions within and across three different cultural conditions to build the positive learning culture: structures, values and relationships (Output # 1). Many of the strategies were culturally and contextually sensitive. The case studies contributed to the depiction of a collective portrait of school leadership in China (Output # 5). The portrait includes the major expectations of school leaders, the repertoire of leadership skills shared by Chinese school principals and sociocultural factors that shape school principalship in China. Thus, a number of important insights on the major common features of Chinese principals have been initially explored and summarized.

28402814.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28402814.value: 1. The project focused on leadership within schools (e.g., school principals, vice principals and middle-level leaders). We have found that school leaders closely work together with some cross-school leaders (e.g., jiaoyanyuan, special-class teachers and subject leaders) to promote school-based research and teacher learning. It is thus worthwhile to further explore the role played by these cross-school leaders. A new GRF project entitled Promoting teacher learning and improving instruction: What is the role of cross-school instructional leadership has been proposed and successfully funded. 2. The project has provided some initial understandings about the relationships between leadership practices in promoting school-based research and teacher classroom practices. More studies need to be conducted that explicitly explore the links between them. 3. The project unveiled many context-specific leadership and teacher learning practices adopted in Shanghai. These practices can be further compared with those adopted in Hong Kong and contribute to the knowledge base of educational practices in high performing societies.

28402814.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28402814.value: This research studied the leadership strategies and practices associated with the successful promotion and implementation of school-based research in Shanghai. We thought this important because most of what we know about school leadership comes from western countries such as the US. Many of the newly-emerging leadership strategies in China were rarely known to the outsiders. Given that Shanghai is now a yardstick for educational success due to its achievement in international comparisons, this study helped to unravel the codes of educational processes in Shanghai and to draw lessons from its experience. We collected data through interviewing school principals, vice principals, middle leaders and teachers in each of the six case schools and then transcribed and analyzed data. This allowed us to build some initial understandings of school leadership in China in general and school leadership strategies for promoting and implementing school-based research in particular. The study also captured the dynamics between school-based research, some unique organizational settings in Chinese schools (e.g., jiaoyanzu as a peer-learning unit) and the societal cultural values that promote collectivism and harmonious relationships. These findings have substantial implications for schools in other settings.

28403414.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28403414.value: 青少年的其中一個特質就是衝動和愛冒險。這些特質往往會令他們作出一些錯誤的決定（例如加入黑社會）和進行一些高風險行為（如吸毒），並為他們未來的人生帶來極嚴重的後果。本計劃以心理生理及腦神經研究方法，探討青少年的情緒反應如何影響他們的自我控制和決策能力。在過往的文獻中，大腦負責情緒管理的杏仁核和負責抑制衝動行為的前額葉皮層對青少年的自我控制和決策能力有密切的關係。我們假設正面和負面的情緒對青少年和成年人的自我控制和決策能力有不一樣的影響。本實驗將使用情緒引發的方法去改變參與者的情感狀態，並使用Go-NOGO任務和簡單的賭博遊戲以比較青少年和成年人的腦部有關決策能力的活動是如何受不同情緒的影響。我們亦會以皮膚電反應（SCR）和心臟速率（HR）等的心理生理測量，以量化參與者的情緒變化。我們的研究結果將提供一個以腦神經科學為基礎，對青少年的情感狀態如何影響他們的自我控制和決策能力作更深入了解。

28403414.label: Realisation of objectives
28403414.value: In this project, we aimed to examine the interplay between emotion and impulsive decision/behavior of adolescents using behavioral, psychophysiology and neuroimaging methodologies. In brief, we conducted two sets of experiment (i.e. lab experiment with newly developed behavioral tasks and psychophysiology measurements and fMRI experiment with the same set of behavioral tasks) with over 120 adolescent adult participants. More details are discussed in the following paragraphs. To address the first objective, we have developed two new behavioral tasks, a modified Go-NoGo task and a moral dilemma task and translated the impulsivity scale, UPPS-P into a Chinese version. The modified Go-NoGo task aims to examine the interplay between working memory and inhibitory control in adolescent and adults. We examined the correlation between the impulsivity trait of adolescents (i.e. characterized with the Chinese version of UPPS-S) and their inhibition control ability. In line of the literature, there is no significant correlation between the self-report measure of impulsivity and the behavioral results obtained from behavioral measurements even we examined the correlation between the inhibition control and working memory separately (i.e. Accuracy and False Alarm rate of the NoGo trial in the Go-NoGo task). We concluded that self-reported measure of impulsivity may not be a reliable measurement in predicting the impulsive behavior of adolescents. Instead of prescribing impulsivity trait questionnaire, we suggested to characterize the impulsivity and risk-seeking behavior of individual adolescents with a 10-15mins behavioral task on executive functions (e.g. stop-signal response task, go-nogo task, or loss aversion task). On the other hand, we found differences between adolescent and adult participants in their behavioral response to the moral dilemma task. The moral dilemma task was designed to examine the interplay between the emotion and cognition system. The dual-process theory (Greene, Nystrom, Engell, Darley, & Cohen, 2004; Greene, Sommerville, Nystrom, Darley, & Cohen, 2001) suggests that the emotion and cognition systems have competing roles in moral judgment. Previous studies show that brain areas associated with emotion and social cognition are more active whereas areas related to working memory are less active during personal moral dilemmas as compared to impersonal moral or non-moral dilemmas (Greene et al., 2001, 2004; Greene & Haidt, 2002). Another theory of moral judgment is the social intuitionist model (SIM) (Haidt, 2001), which says that moral judgment is much like aesthetic judgment. Slow, effortful moral reasoning comes after a moral judgment is made to provide arguments that support the already-made judgment caused by quick, effortless moral intuitions. Our behavioral data suggested that, without any training in answering the dilemma questions, adolescent but adult participants responded to the dilemma questions in a way consistent with SIM. Also, adolescent participants are more willing to reflect on their already-made judgement with the new information provided. To address the second objective, we monitored the physiological response of participants with Electroencephalography (EEG), Electromyography (EMG), Electrocardiography (ECG) and galvanic skin response (GSR) and altered their emotional state with different kind of music. 50 individuals participated in the experiment under four different affective states as determined by Self-Assessment Manikin Rating Scale (SAM) (i.e. high arousal and high valence, high arousal and low valence, low arousal and high valence and low arousal and low valence). Based on participants’ SAM response, we successfully introduced different affective states to the participants. We hypothesized that the different affective states can be differentiated with the psychophysiological measurements. Therefore, we compared the signal features across different measurements and adopted a support vector machine (SVM) approach to classify affective states based on the physiological measurements. Our findings demonstrated that ECG and GSR are the most reliable predictors of affective states. Besides, we also investigated the feasibility of using short-term frontal EEG as a means to evaluate the dynamic changes of mental executive function. Frontal EEG signals were recorded from twenty healthy subjects performing four cognitive and motor tasks, including arithmetic operation, finger tapping, mental rotation and lexical decision task. Our findings revealed that theta activity is the common EEG feature that increases with difficulty across four tasks. Meanwhile, with a short-time analysis window, the level of mental executive function could be classified from EEG features with 65%±75% accuracy across participants using a SVM model. These findings suggest that frontal EEG could be used for evaluating the dynamic changes of mental executive function. To address the third objective, we recruited 3 groups of participants: 1) adolescent (age 13-14), 2) late adolescent (age 16-17) and adult (age 19 or above) and examined their cortical response to risky decision, dilemma decision, inhibition control and executive control using BOLD fMRI. In addition to the Go-NoGo and moral dilemma paradigm, participants also completed the loss aversion task, counting Stroop task, task switching and resting state. With the focus of the interplay between affective states and decision making, we prioritize the analysis on the moral dilemma task and the resting state BOLD data. In particular, we examined how the brain regions associated with executive function interact with the medial prefrontal cortex which has been showed to play a key role in integrating emotional and somatic signals in moral decisions in adolescents. Our findings showed that adolescents activated a similar neural network during dilemma question (d1) and control question (c1) conditions, except for the relatively greater activation identified in the posterior cingulate (PC)/precuneus during d1. In addition, the medial prefrontal gyrus (MPFG) (BA 9/10), anterior cingulate (AC) (BA 24) and precuneus/posterior cingulate gyrus (BA 7/31) were significantly more active in the dilemma feedback (d2) than in the control feedback (c2) conditions. The MPFG was found to have greater activities for personal moral judgment in Greene et al.’s studies (2001, 2004) whereas the AC also exhibited increased activity during personal moral judgment (Greene et al., 2004). In overall, the PC/precuneus were more activated in the moral dilemma conditions than in the control conditions. Similar observation was reported in the previous studies (Greene et al., 2001, 2004; Pujol et al., 2008). In addition, the medial prefrontal cortex and PC are parts of the default mode network (DMN). The functional connectivity of DMN has been showed to change with age in previous studies. Our findings illustrated that the functional connectivity within posterior DMN, particularly the atrophy-corrected interhemispheric functional connectivity strength correlated with age of the participants significantly. In overall, our findings shed light on the neural mechanism that correlated with the difference between the decision making behaviors of adolescents and adults. Young people, compared to adults, are more likely in engaging the dopaminergic system and affective network in the decision process. Therefore, their decision making seems to be more intuitive and less calculated. This is in line with the existing literature that adolescence is characterized by risky decision making due to the still-maturing prefrontal cortex.

International psychogeriatrics, 29(5), 805-814. Besides, we have presented our findings in 5 international conferences and published the abstracts on the conference proceeding (see Part C for details). We are now preparing the two manuscripts that will report the psychophysiological data and fMRI data on the interplay between emotion and decision making in adolescents and adults. In particular, we found that adolescents activated a similar neural network during dilemma question (d1) and control question (c1) conditions, except for the relatively greater activation identified in the posterior cingulate (PC)/precuneus during d1. 28403414.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28403414.value: We propose to conduct a larger scale cross-section study on the individual differences of impulsivity across adolescent and adult population. In our existing data, we observed a considerable individual difference in the behavioral, psychophysiology and neural response to the decision making tasks. Understanding the factors (e.g. education, family background, social economic status, genetics and life style) that may contribute to the individual differences will give us a more comprehensive picture and predictive power on the risk-seeking behavior of an individual. Besides, we propose to monitor the physiological response of the participants with wireless wearable sensors which can enable us to monitor the dynamic changes of the physiology when an individual is engaged in real-life decision making. A continuous monitoring can provide enormous data for us to characterize the impulsivity control and decision behavior across real-life settings. In particular, teachers are eager to understand the causes and factors that affect the decision and behavior of their students. Using wearable sensors at a classroom setting will provide an objective measurement of student behaviors and heighten the awareness of teachers and students on how to regulate their impulsive behaviors.

28403414.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28403414.value: Young people, compared to adults, may be more morally idealistic. Their decision making seems to be more intuitive and less calculated. However, adolescence is also characterized by risky decision making. Our findings provided biological evidence on the difference of brain mechanism involved in decision making in adolescents and adults. As adolescents are more likely to engage the brain region involved in emotion processing in their decision making, emotion plays a significant role in their decision making. Our study further illustrated the importance in understanding the biological basis of behavior. In particular, parents, teachers and the society should consider the developmental and biological changes in adolescents and provide appropriate support for our younger generation. On the other hand, we suggest that further study should be conducted to understand the individual difference of impulsivity control across adolescents and adults. Although we found that adolescents are in general more impulsive and susceptible to the influence of emotion in their decision making, a considerable individual difference is observed across participants. The factors that may cause such individual differences should be studied in the future study.

28403514.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28403514.value: Hong Kong is an ageing society in which an intergenerational conflict over welfare resources between the older and younger people is argued to be ongoing. For a long time, sociopolitical analysts have been concerned about horizontal equity and intergenerational fairness. Individuals in childhood and old age (especially after retirement) receive most financial and other forms of help from the government. Nevertheless, limited research is available on the public expenditure on the elderly and children in the Hong Kong context. In this proposed study, we aim to tackle this important issue by using a mixed method to analyze the public spending on the elderly and children. To determine whether the elderly receive public welfares at the expense of children, this study formulates these four objectives: (1) to examine the trends in the public expenditure on cash and in-kind benefits to the elderly and children in the past three decades; 2) to assess whether the older adults have received public welfares at the expense of the younger generation in the past three decades; 3) to project the public expenditure on cash and in-kind benefits to the elderly and children for the next three decades by means of macro- and micro-simulation modeling; and 4) to evaluate whether the intergenerational conflict over public resources would continue or emerge in the next three decades. In addition, we seek to develop a feasible policy model to address the intergenerational conflict. The proposed project would be managed by a team of multidisciplinary experts on social policy, public finance, and redistributive politics through the use of different research methods. When completed, the proposed study would be the first to offer insights into whether and to what extent an intergenerational conflict exists in the Hong Kong context. On the basis of the findings of this proposed study, policy implications would be made to resolve the issues regarding the financial sustainability and legitimacy of age-related public expenditure. 作為一個老齡化的社會，年青人和老年人對福利資源的需求及可能的代際衝突是值得關注的。許多觀察者關心代際公平和社會的橫向公平。一般來說，兒童和老年人（特別是退休後的老年人）獲得較多的財政資助。不過，政府的財政資源是有限的。因此，政府需要在資源需求和滿足方面進行有效的平衡。 本研究中，我們試圖用一個混和的研究方法來分析香港政府在老年人和兒童的公共支出。為了瞭解此代際衝突，我們有四項研究目標。一是瞭解過去三十年香港政府在老年人和兒童的公共支出；二是研究老年人獲取財政資源是否以犧牲年輕人的福利為代價？三是基於模擬建模研究未來三十年香港政府在老年人和兒童上的公共支出；四是評估在未來三十年代際衝突是否發生、是否持續？ 本項研究將由一個跨學科的團隊來執行。團隊的成員有社會政策、公共財政和分配政治的研究經歷。這是首個系統性研究香港公共資源配置中的代際衝突的研究專案。基於此研究，我們也會提出相關的政策建議供政府參考。

28404114.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28404114.value: Difficulties with arithmetic in the early years of schooling are obstacles to achieving competence in more advanced mathematics in the later years and even to gaining societal and occupational opportunities far into adulthood (Every Child a Chance Trust, 2009). Recent analyses of population-based longitudinal data sets have demonstrated that early number and arithmetic competence has a greater predictive power of school achievement (Duncan et al., 2007) and adulthood earnings (Crawford & Cribb, 2013) than early reading competence. However, knowledge on the sources that contribute to individual differences in learning arithmetic, compared with learning to read, is considerably limited. This condition is especially true in the context of Chinese societies because only a few studies have examined the numerical and arithmetic development and learning of Chinese children. In this study, we propose to follow up 300 Chinese young children in Hong Kong throughout their preschool years and examine their numerical and arithmetic development. The study aims to develop and test a model in which children’s number competence serves as a stepping stone from early fundamental cognitive skills to later development of competence in different domains of arithmetic. The study will contribute to the scientific literature by delineating the specificity of cognitive and numerical processes in learning various aspects of arithmetic. The findings are likewise expected to inform early childhood education by suggesting specific cognitive and numerical skills that are important for preventing children’s difficulties with arithmetic and improving their arithmetic competence. 兒童在幼稚園和學校中若是出現算術學習方面的問題，將會對他們以後的數學學習造成極大的困擾，甚至會給他們成年以後的職業和生活帶來負面影響。最近，學者們對數個大型追蹤資料庫的科學分析發現，幼兒對數字的理解和算術能力比閱讀能力更能夠預測他們在中小學時的學業成就和成年以後的社經地位。然而，在過去的幾十年裏，儘管學者們對兒童閱讀能力的發展有了比較深入的瞭解，但對算術能力的發展及其影響因素卻知之甚少。這一狀況在華人社會中尤為明顯，因為很少有研究關注華人兒童算術能力的發展。我們的這項研究計畫擬在香港跟蹤數百名華人兒童，縱貫整個幼稚園階段，探討華人兒童對數字的理解能力和算術能力是如何發展的。我們的目標是建立一個兒童算術學習的理論；在此理論中，我們認為，兒童對數字的理解能力在不同形式的算術學習中均發揮著橋樑作用，然而這一橋樑的發展卻基於更為基礎的認知能力，這些認知能力可能包括兒童更早些時候就已經掌握的對數量、空間和語言的理解能力。這項研究計畫的科學價值在於幫助我們理解不同形式的算術學習中隱藏的認知機制和數字表徵機制。我們的研究發現對幼兒數學教育亦有啟發意義，比如若想預防兒童在算術方面的學習問題，以後的數學教育應注重培養兒童哪些基礎認知能力和數字理解能力。

28404114.label: Realisation of objectives
28404114.value: All the project objectives have been fully achieved. We analyzed the data of the project to address the four project objectives and summarized our findings as follows: 1) For Objective 1, quantitative skills was found to be associated with children's levels but not growth of arithmetic competencies across the three domains. Children with higher subtizing (quantitative) skills had higher levels of arithmetic competencies. 2) For Objective 2, spatial skills significantly predicted children's levels and growth of arithmetic competencies across the three domains. Children with higher spatial skills not only had higher levels of arithmetic competencies but also had faster rates of growth in these competencies. 3) For Objective 3, the results showed that oral language skills predicted children's performance in arithmetic word problems and written language skills predicted their performance in written arithmetic. In contrast to our hypothesis, however, written language skills also predicted children's performance in nonsymbolic arithmetic. 4) For Objective 4, we found that the relations from quantitative, spatial, and linguistic skills to arithmetic competencies were mediated by children's number competencies. Overall, all the four objectives of this project have been fully addressed, although a few results were not consistent with our original hypotheses.

That is, children with higher subtizing (quantitative) skills had higher levels of arithmetic competencies. Spatial skills significantly predicted children's levels and growth of arithmetic competencies across the three domains. Children with higher spatial skills not only had higher levels of arithmetic competencies but also had faster rates of growth in these competencies. The results also showed that oral language skills predicted children's performance in arithmetic word problems and written language skills predicted their performance in written and nonsymbolic arithmetic. Finally, we found that the relations from quantitative, spatial, and linguistic skills to arithmetic competencies were mediated by children's number competencies. Research outcome: (1) Based on this project, we have produced six papers, among which five have been published in high-impact international journals (e.g., Learning and Instruction, Contemporary Educational Psychology, and Early Childhood Research Quarterly) and one is now under revision and resubmission to Journal of Educational Psychology. Moreover, I received the 2018 Research Output Prize from the University of Hong Kong for the paper that was based on this project and published in Learning and Instruction. Finally, based on this project, one graduate student, Qi Huang, was successful in developing her thesis work and publishing her findings in British Journal of Educational Psychology. (2) Based on this project, two poster presentations and one oral presentation were given at three recognized international conferences (e.g., SRCD, EARLI, and ICP). (3) The research team is planning to present the final research findings of the completed project at one or two more international conferences and is preparing at least two more manuscripts for considering to be published in high-impact international journals.

28404114.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28404114.value: A new GRF project (No. 17603817) that is an extension of this completed research project was also funded by the RGC and began on January 1, 2018. Based on the findings of this completed research project, the three-year new GRF project is going to further explore the role of spatial skills in arithmetic development and develop an intervention program to enhance young Chinese children's spatial and arithmetic skills. The new project will be completed at the end of 2020.

28404114.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28404114.value: Achieving arithmetic competence at an early age provides the basis for learning more advanced mathematics later. Over the past decades, a growing body of knowledge has been accumulated on the sources of individual differences in arithmetic learning. Most prior work, however, has been based on cross-sectional or short-term longitudinal samples and has rarely considered multiple domains of arithmetic. The aim of the present study is to examine to what extent a wide range of general cognitive and quantity-number skills contribute to young Chinese children's multiple domains of arithmetic competencies, including nonsymbolic, verbal, and written arithmetic. The proposed study carried important theoretical and applied implications. The study developed and tested a fine-grained model linking different types of cognitive skills to different types of arithmetic outcomes. Arithmetic competence is not necessarily uniform across all arithmetic domains; thus, focusing on various aspects of arithmetic competencies helped identify the potential precursors of symbolic and non-symbolic arithmetic competence. The finding provided information for researchers and practitioners on the key elements that effective prevention and intervention early childhood programs should target among young Chinese children who have not yet entered primary school.
